title: Tatum Paxley Defends WWE Signing Athletes Without Indie Experience
raw_title: Tatum Paxley Defends WWE Signing Athletes Without Indie Experience
summary_src: Tatum Paxley knows there are wrestling fans who aren’t exactly thrilled about WWE signing athletes who never spent years grinding on the independent scene. But if anyone expects that criticism to bother her, Paxley says they’re wasting their time.
body: 蝶 Connect with us on Bluesky → Tatum Paxley knows there are wrestling fans who aren’t exactly thrilled about WWE signing athletes who never spent years grinding on the independent scene. But if anyone expects that criticism to bother her, Paxley says they’re wasting their time. Speaking to Complex Graps , Paxley was asked about her unusual path into WWE. She didn’t arrive after years of wrestling on the indies or even as someone who had spent her entire life dreaming about becoming a wrestler, instead coming from a competitive powerlifting background. That’s become increasingly common in NXT, where WWE has recruited athletes from a variety of sports and trained them from scratch. It has also led to criticism from some fans who believe those recruits haven’t “paid their dues” in the same way wrestlers who spent years on the independent circuit did. Paxley understands that conversation exists, but she doesn’t walk around feeling like she has something to prove because of it. She believes anyone who doesn’t genuinely fall in love with professional wrestling probably isn’t going to make it very far anyway. “Yeah. I wouldn’t say I have a chip on my shoulder. I understand why people—I don’t understand why they have it out for me, you know? Because, to me, you really only get far if you have a genuine love for the business, you know? Because you can tell if somebody’s not happy here, you know? And if you’re not happy here, then, you know, you’re welcome to go elsewhere.” As far as Paxley is concerned, the success of WWE’s athlete recruits speaks for itself. She believes the people who stick around and start succeeding are doing so because they’ve developed a real passion for wrestling, regardless of what brought them through the door in the first place. “So, when you see, you know, these Superstars getting the success that they’re getting, it’s because they found the love for the business. And I think if you love something, you want to share that love with other people.” And when it comes to fans who are still angry that people like her didn’t come through the indies, Paxley isn’t losing any sleep over it. She’s happy with where she is and loves what she’s doing, which is ultimately all she cares about. “So, I mean, people, you know, can get mad. It doesn’t really bother me that much. I’m happy. I love what I do, and that’s all that matters.” Paxley isn’t arguing that everyone has to take the same road into wrestling. Her point is that how someone gets through the door matters a lot less than whether they actually fall in love with the business once they’re there. There have been many incidents when a match finish has not gone to plan, leading to some unexpected moments. Something similar happened during an episode of WWE RAW in 2012. A Divas battle royal was held to determine the number one contender for the Divas Championship, held by Layla. Eva Torres was supposed to win the match, but a botched ending saw Kaitlyn win the battle royal. During a recent appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet , Kaitlyn detailed what happened and the aftermath of the situation. She revealed how she was supposed to last till the end, but Eve would eliminate her. However, the ending didn't go as planned. Kaitlyn was supposed to clothesline Eve and send her over the top rope. But the plan was for Eve to hang on and eliminate her opponent. However, things didn't go to plan. Kaitlyn said this left everyone surprised, and the referee was asked to raise her hand. However, the former WWE Divas Champion was left fearing the botch could get her fired. Kaitlyn said when she headed backstage, she saw Eve was upset, but Vince was laughing. Kaitlyn joined WWE in 2010 and started her run on NXT. Her early run on the brand saw her be a part of an infamous match. She faced fellow NXT talent Maxine, and both of them had their respective mentors in their corner. Kaitlyn was mentored by Vickie Guerrero, and Maxine had Alicia Fox accompany her. The match was widely panned by the fans and saw many botches with a clear lack of chemistry between the two stars. During the contest, Michael Cole repeatedly criticized the match on commentary and even took a phone call on air. Speaking on INSIGHT about the segment, Kaitlyn said both she and her opponent were not experienced but said Michael Cole took things really far with his actions . Shawn Spears recently returned to action during NXT house shows, and his recent outing saw him compete in an eight-man tag team match in a live event. He teamed up with Shiloh Hill, Tavon Heights, and Tony D'Angelo to beat Birthright in the main event. The show was held in Kitchener, Ontario. Spears was released in 2019 and joined AEW in the same year. Spears was part of MJF's The Pinnacle faction and feuded with some top names. He eventually left the promotion in 2023. Shawn Spears' last televised match in WWE came on the July 21 episode of NXT. He faced The Culling's Niko Vance and won the match after a disqualification. Ex-WWE star gets major honor Discuss Now Former WWE star Tanea Brooks has been given another major platform in her ongoing battle against ALS. On October 15, patient advocacy organization I AM ALS announced that Brooks had been named the first Honorary Member of its Board of Directors, according to a press release from PR Newswire . Tanea Brooks' ring name is Rebel. This comes after she joined the group as an ambassador in June, following her terminal diagnosis in May. In her new leadership role, Rebel will continue leveraging her wrestling platform to drive public awareness, fight for treatment accessibility, and push for a cure. The ex-WWE star emphasizes that this remains a priority in her journey and commitment to fight the good fight alongside the organization. I AM ALS CEO Andrea Goodman praised Brooks for transforming a devastating personal experience into immediate, impactful action that has inspired others to get involved. Rebel's time in WWE was brief, and she was not signed to a contract. She teamed up with Amber Nova in a tag team match against Io Shirai (now Iyo Sky) and Kairi Sane during an NXT television taping, and that was her only match there. This was during the time Triple H was in charge of the developmental brand. The wrestling community has come together to raise funds through AEW's Rebel Heart merchandise line, which benefits I AM ALS and Team Gleason, an organization founded by former NFL star Steve Gleason, who was also diagnosed with ALS. After her stint in WWE, she joined AEW in a backstage role as the hair-and-makeup stylist. Then she appeared on screen as Britt Baker's assistant and began wrestling, too. AEW dedicated the September 9 edition of AEW Dynamite in Rebel's honor. The show, which took place at Akins Ford Arena in Athens, Georgia, opened with Britt Baker hosting The Waiting Room alongside Rebel, commending her co-host's strength and resilience. AEW also presented a tribute video celebrating Rebel's career and honoring her work in the fight against ALS.

title: Cook County sheriff's officer sues WWE, wrestler over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
raw_title: Cook County sheriff's officer sues WWE, wrestler over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
body: CHICAGO - A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE, wrestler Montez Ford and an event production company, alleging he was subjected to unwanted sexualized contact while working security at a live wrestling event. Noel Lucas filed the lawsuit Wednesday in Cook County Circuit Court. The complaint says he was working an off-duty security job at WWE Monday Night Raw on July 6 at Allstate Arena in Rosemont. According to the lawsuit, Lucas was seated at his assigned post outside the ring when Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, approached him, straddled him and began moving his hips in a sexually suggestive way. Lucas’ attorneys say he was not told he would be part of the performance and did not consent. Live announcers on the Netflix broadcast allegedly mocked Lucas in real time, telling viewers, "That guy clearly hates fun," and comparing him to Paul Blart, the fictional security guard from "Paul Blart: Mall Cop." "Mr. Lucas was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE’s entertainment," attorney Whitney Barr said in a statement. The incident aired live on Netflix. The lawsuit says WWE later shared video of it on TikTok and Instagram, where it received more than 300,000 views. Ford also shared footage, according to the lawsuit. The complaint says Lucas, who has roughly 24 years of law enforcement experience, was later mocked at work, while his children were ridiculed at school because of the videos. The complaint includes 14 counts, including battery, assault, intentional infliction of emotional distress and claims under Illinois’ Gender Violence Act and Right of Publicity Act. "Entertainment is not a defense to unwanted sexual contact," Barr said. "We intend to hold WWE and those responsible accountable for what happened to Mr. Lucas and for the harm caused by the subsequent publication of the footage." FOX Chicago has reached out to WWE for comment, but the company had not responded as of publication. title: WWE Stands By Crown Jewel Plans Despite Saudi Conflict

body: Frazer Harrison/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover After some uncertainty thanks to the ongoing armed conflict in Saudi Arabia, WWE made clear on Monday that they were still planning on holding Crown Jewel in Riyadh next month. It's a decision that has raised eyebrows, and one that Dave Meltzer believes may have been made thanks to some outside pressure. On Monday's "Wrestling Observer Radio," Meltzer and co-host Garrett Gonzalez were discussing a tweet sent by Saudi's General Entertainment Authority director Turki Al-Sheikh , which was seemingly directed just at Canelo Alvarez coming to the country for a boxing match, but one Meltzer thinks was directed towards WWE as well. "In WWE, when that tweet came out, they knew it was a message for them too," Meltzer said. "I mean...it's a real tough thing. And this is obviously going to be Ari Emanuel's decision. This is way over Nick Khan's head...I'm sure it won't be without Nick Khan's input. But that's...it's a really tough decision, because they shouldn't go. We all know that. It's too dangerous." Meltzer pointed out that the United States State Department and Travel Advisory had also advised against anyone traveling to Saudi Arabia for the time. Even still, Meltzer believes that the money WWE is being paid and Al-Sheikh's desire for them to put on the show would ultimately be prioritized over anything else, pointing out that WWE's parent company, TKO, was beholden to Al-Sheikh due to his funding of TKO's Zuffa Boxing . As a result, Meltzer thinks WWE will exhaust any option to get there, even if many people within the company are against the idea. "If there is anyway they can go, they're going to go," Meltzer said. "And it's going to be very interesting because the families of the talents, I'm sure, are not going to be happy. The talent probably isn't going to be happy. The backstage people, I know, aren't happy." If you use any of the quotes in this article, please credit "Wrestling Observer Radio" and provide a h/t to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription

title: WWE's Montez Ford Sued for Alleged Lap Dance on Security Guard
raw_title: WWE star Montez Ford sued over alleged ‘sexualized lap dance’ on Illinois security guard during live broadcast
body: An Illinois security guard alleged that WWE star Montez Ford performed a “sexualized lap dance” on him during a live Netflix broadcast of “Monday Night Raw.” Noel Lucas accused Ford, whose real name is Kenneth Crawford, and the WWE of assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and other claims, according to the lawsuit filed on Wednesday, which was obtained by Post Wrestling and confirmed by The Post. Lucas alleged the incident unfolded as Ford and his Street Profits tag team partner, Angelo Dawkins , made their entrance before their televised match at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Ill. on July 6. Lucas, an officer with the Cook County Sheriff’s Department who was working off-duty security at the event, claimed Ford approached him without warning or consent and began dancing in a “sexually provocative” manner. “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance,’” the lawsuit, filed in the Circuit Court of Cook County, stated. Lucas alleges Ford moved increasingly closer to Lucas as the dance continued and that his “left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff’s leg.” The lawsuit alleges 14 counts, including violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Ford is seen intently thrusting his hips and dancing over Lucas, who appears uncomfortable and initially looks away before eventually cracking a smile, according to fan footage. The July 6 episode of “Raw” drew an estimated 12,500 fans at Allstate Arena and recorded 2.5 million global views on Netflix over seven days, according to Wrestlenomics data reported by “Wrestling Inc.” The episode currently available on Netflix appears to cut away early during the Street Profits’ entrance, leaving out the interaction described in the lawsuit. Lucas claimed footage of the encounter spread across social media, drawing hundreds of thousands of views, including on WWE’s and Ford’s own accounts. The alleged fallout continued the following day when Lucas returned to his full-time job at a courthouse. “Members of the public recognized him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements” allegedly performed during the broadcast, the lawsuit stated. Lucas also claimed his children were “mocked and ridiculed” at school over the footage. The lawsuit alleges Lucas has suffered “humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress” and continues to be affected because the video remains available online. He also accuses WWE and Ford of using his image for commercial purposes without authorization, citing the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas is seeking unspecified monetary damages, punitive damages, legal fees and a court order barring the defendants from using his identity. Lucas also supervises security gua
summary: An off-duty Cook County sheriff's officer working security at the July 6 Monday Night Raw in Rosemont, Illinois has filed suit against WWE performer Montez Ford and the company. Noel Lucas claims Ford approached him without consent during the Street Profits entrance on the live Netflix broadcast and performed an unwanted sexually provocative dance that included repeated hip thrusting, gyrating and inner-thigh contact. The lawsuit accuses Ford, whose real name is Kenneth Crawford, and WWE of assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress.

title: Will Riyadh Airport Attacks Force a Change? — WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel: Will Riyadh Airport Attacks Force a Change?
body: WWE Crown Jewel remains scheduled for Riyadh on November 7, but a series of attacks on the Saudi capital’s King Khalid International Airport has raised serious questions about whether the event will go ahead as planned. WWE has not announced a cancellation or a change of location, although recent reports suggest the situation is being discussed internally. The attacks have intensified concerns just weeks before WWE is due to stage one of its major international premium live events in Saudi Arabia. With the airport struck repeatedly and new threats issued against the country’s aviation infrastructure, the question is no longer simply whether Crown Jewel will proceed, but whether WWE can safely maintain its plans. WWE and Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority announced on September 1 that Crown Jewel would take place at Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD on Saturday, November 7. The event is expected to feature champion-versus-champion matches in both the men’s and women’s divisions. WWE’s official announcement continues to list Riyadh as the host city. As of October 12, however, neither WWE nor its parent company, TKO Group Holdings, has publicly announced a change to the date or venue. That means Crown Jewel remains on the calendar, even as the security situation creates uncertainty around the event. The distinction matters. Reports of internal concern do not amount to an official postponement, and there is no confirmed replacement venue or revised date at this stage. The immediate concern is the repeated targeting of King Khalid International Airport. Saudi authorities reported that an attack on October 10 killed at least 12 people and injured hundreds. A further strike on Sunday, October 11, killed one person and injured 11 others, according to reporting published by Al Jazeera on Monday. Airport operations were disrupted as authorities assessed damage and safety conditions. The Iran-backed Houthi group in Yemen has claimed responsibility for earlier attacks and issued a new warning against using Saudi airports and airspace, according to Wrestling Observer reporting. The warning adds another layer of concern for an international event that would require wrestlers, staff, production crews and travelling fans to reach Riyadh. The airport attacks do not establish that the Crown Jewel venue itself has been targeted. However, the safety of travel routes and the ability to move international personnel into the country are significant considerations for WWE and its partners. A recent report of Wrestling Observer by Dave Meltzer, described Crown Jewel as being in jeopardy amid the escalating situation. Meltzer also suggested that a contingency plan would need to be available if WWE could not hold the event in Riyadh as scheduled. That does not confirm WWE has decided to move the show, nor does it establish that a backup location has been selected. title: New WrestleMania 42 Rumor May Point To a Major Heel Turn From a Top Star
raw_title: New WrestleMania 42 Rumor May Point To a Major Heel Turn From a Top Star
body: While we are still six months from the 2027 edition of the "showcase of the immortals," the WWE has long tried to plan its top matches for the event well in advance. That tradition returned to being the norm once company legend Triple H officially took over the creative direction a few years ago. While injuries and fan reactions can always change plans, now would be a good time to start plotting out a rough draft for the Night 1 and Night 2 headliners for the first WrestleMania ever on foreign soil. According to Wrestle Votes, WWE decision-makers already have two specific matches in mind. In a new report from the industry insider , Oba Femi vs. Roman Reigns is still penciled in as one of the main events. That claim would align with reports in recent months that the brand was eyeing a showdown between its biggest and hottest stars. However, the other match may be a letdown for fans, and that allegedly will be a rematch between Cody Rhodes and CM Punk . Finding out that WWE is thinking about going back to the Rhodes and Punk well will probably get a sigh from a good number of fans. While the build-up to their match at SummerSlam was solid, the bout itself underwhelmed. Especially when compared to the other headliner of the two-night event, Reigns vs. Seth Rollins. Yes, both men are two of the most popular stars on the roster, but why would the company want to rehash a rivalry that did not deliver epic moments? Well, that may be because they are planning something major to come before or during the rematch. It is possible that WWE is considering a heel turn for either man. For a few months, the company has been trying to tell a story of Rhodes tapping into a darker side because being a true blue hero is not working for him anymore. It makes sense if this is all a build to his long-rumored turn before or at WrestleMania 42. Punk can sometimes act like a heel and still get cheers from fans. Turning him would be trickier, but it is not impossible. Furthermore, there may be a belief that a heel version of Punk can be extremely helpful in lifting up younger stars they are trying to turn into main event players. title: Drew McIntyre Calls CM Punk a Piece of Crap
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Blasts Former WWE Champion: 'I Can't Stand Him'
body: McIntyre has been absent from WWE programming since losing to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 weekend six months ago. The 41-year-old took time off to film The Last Druid (a historical action movie starring Russell Crowe) and Highlander (a fantasy action film also starring Crowe and Henry Cavill). While there's no clear timeline on McIntyre's return to the squared circle, he certainly appears ready to rekindle a feud with another former WWE Champion. "He's a piece of crap. I avoid him whenever I can avoid him," McIntyre said. "I can tell everybody, he's a genuine piece of crap. I can't stand him. I got writers telling me, 'You're working with that guy' and I'm like, 'Alright, I can't stand him but I know he's very good at his job.' I can't stand him. "You put us together, it's magic for the audience but also, we have to be professional and not pound each other because if we pound each other's heads, I would murder him. Did you see him in UFC? It would look like that if it got real in there." McIntyre and Punk had a lengthy 10-month feud in 2024, starting after the latter tore his triceps in the men's Royal Rumble Match. Following McIntyre's successful World Heavyweight Championship defense against Seth Rollins at WrestleMania 40, Punk viciously attacked his rival. Damian Priest then showed up to cash in his Money in the Bank contract, easily defeating McIntyre to become the new champion. Punk and McIntyre concluded their program at the Bad Blood 2024 pay-per-view, with the former emerging victorious. McIntyre is a four-time world champion in WWE (one World Heavyweight title and three WWE Championships). Punk is an eight-time world champion in WWE, with three of those reigns occurring over the last 14 months. Sami Zayn, who ended Punk's last WWE Championship reign, is the current title holder. Roman Reigns has held the World Heavyweight title since WrestleMania 42, defeating Punk in the main event. GET WRESTLING NEWS Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via E-mail More share options Share on Pinterest Share on Flipboard Share on Reddit Share on WhatsApp 190 Views 0 Shares By Juan Paolo David Updated Oct 15, 2026 at 10:02pm Getty INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 06: Carmelo Hayes attends Netflix's Debut of WWE Monday Night Raw at Intuit Dome on January 06, 2025 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for Netflix) Following Money in the Bank last Saturday, WWE is now building toward its next Premium Live Event. Crown Jewel is the subject of the latest WWE rumors due to the United States’ travel advisory. The latest rumors roundup also features the original winners of the Money in the Bank ladder matches, an update on Carmelo Hayes and more. Play Original MITB Winners Penta and Tiffany Stratton won this year’s Money in the Bank ladder matches. They now have an opportunity to cash in their contract anytime, anywhere for one year. According to False Finish , the original winners for the MITB briefcases this year were Bron Breakker and Roxanne Perez. However, WWE pivoted away from Breakker and Perez. It’s unclear why the company made the decision, but Penta gained momentum after his excellent match against Roman Reigns. Stratton, on the other hand, has a ready-made storyline with Chelsea Green. Self Made Pro reported that Stratton could turn heel on Green. Play Crown Jewel Update Due to a recent attack at the King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, the United States government issued a travel advisory. It puts WWE’s Crown Jewel event in jeopardy, though the company continues to promote the PLE. There are growing concerns about holding the event there, but as of this writing, it’s still good to go. According to PW Insider , WWE is in regular talks with the Saudi Arabian government and authorities regarding the situation. They are even waiting for clearance from a private security company. Play On the other hand, Saudi Arabian outlet Ejal reported that the Kingdom’s General Entertainment Authority is considering canceling the rest of the Riyadh Season, which includes Crown Jewel. On Monday’s episode of WWE Raw, Carmelo Hayes joined 946 in a shocking turn of events. Hayes attacked Solo Sikoa with a crowbar as he was about to finish Royce Keys with the Samoan Spike. Hayes has been absent from television, and there were speculations that he could be getting released. According to PW Insider , there was no talk of Hayes leaving the company. He has always been planned to join Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price and Jaida Parker. title: Maria Kanellis Leaves Door Open For WWE Return
raw_title: Ex-WWE Star Isn’t Ruling Out a Wrestling Comeback Seven Years After the Last Match
body: Maria Kanellis last competed in WWE on the July 1, 2019, episode of RAW. She teamed up with her husband, Mike Bennett, losing to Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch in a mixed tag team match. She and Bennett left the promotion the following year and signed with AEW in 2022. While her husband is still signed to the promotion and working in ROH, she announced her exit in January 2025. "I don't know. In wrestling, you never know. I haven't closed the door, but it's not always up to the person." "Wrestling probably not, unless it's like the Royal Rumble or another Evolution pay-per-view or something like that. But consistently wrestling? Probably not. I think it's so much fun, and those girls took care of me so well the last time I was there, so that's great. I got to look awesome in the ring, much better than I am. It was so much fun. But wrestling consistently, probably not. When I got into wrestling, it wasn't for wrestling," the former WWE star said. Maria Kanellis said she was initially interested in working as a backstage interviewer in WWE before growing interested in an on-screen manager role. "I'm sure you remember this, but Jonathan Coachman and The Rock used to have the banter backstage, and I really wanted to be an interviewer. I loved it. I loved the banter. I loved the way of moving the conversation from one topic to the other. I loved that Jonathan Coachman could do one little thing, and it meant everything in the interview. So that's what I wanted to do, and then somehow I ended up wrestling. But the interviewing part, the managing part, all of that, I really love," the former WWE star said. The post Ex-WWE Star Isn't Ruling Out a Wrestling Comeback Seven Years After the Last Match appeared first on Wrestlezone .
summary: Maria Kanellis last wrestled in WWE on the July 1 2019 episode of Raw in a mixed tag team match alongside husband Mike Bennett against Seth Rollins and Becky Lynch. The couple departed WWE the next year before signing with AEW in 2022 where Bennett remains active in ROH while she exited the company in January 2025. Kanellis stated she has not fully closed the door on wrestling but is unlikely to compete consistently again although she would consider appearances like the Royal Rumble or an Evolution pay-per-view.

title: Austin Creed Names Key New Day Match Before Kofi's WrestleMania Push
raw_title: Austin Creed Feels Most Important Match That New Day Had As A Team Was Securing Kofi's WWE Title Match At WrestleMania 35
body: Austin Creed discusses the past and looks ahead to the future. As of this writing, it is coming up on a full month since The New Level (Kofi & Austin Creed) arrived at All Elite Wrestling. Alongside Swerve Strickland, they are in the midst of a reign as the AEW World Trios Champions. A new interview with Creed and Kofi was conducted by Cameron Hawkins of Uncrowned. Looking back on their time as The New Day with Big E, Creed feels the most important match they had was in the lead-up to WrestleMania 35 when they secured Kofi’s shot at the WWE Championship. “I think with my definition (of important),” he says, “the most important match that we’ve had as a team was when me and (Big) E won that match to get Kofi a title shot.” As for the present, Creed talked about venturing into All Elite Wrestling. “(Swerve Strickland) goes, ‘Look, if we jump in this trios, you get a chance to wrestle, what, six, seven other tag teams right from the jump at Wembley,” says Creed. “So logically, well, of course we want to put hands on everybody as quick as we can, and now by winning those titles, we beat a bunch of other very credible, very good tag teams that AEW has to offer, and so it’s about making sure that we are getting the reps with all of these people on the roster, and having the most dangerous man in all of AEW at our side while we’re doing that, with Prince Nana as well.” On October 17th at AEW WrestleDream, Creed, Kofi, and Strickland will defend the Trios Titles against Hangman Adam Page, Bandido, and Brody King in a two-out-of-three falls match.

Now competing in AEW as The New Level with Kofi, Creed discussed how teaming with Swerve Strickland allowed them immediate access to multiple top tag teams. The trio are currently reigning as AEW World Trios Champions after defeating several credible opponents.

title: Sheriff's Officer Sues WWE and Montez Ford
raw_title: Cook County Sherriff’s Officer Files Lawsuit Against WWE & Montez Ford
body: A Cook County Sheriff’s officer named Noel Lucas filed a lawsuit on October 14th in the Circuit Court of Cook County against WWE and Montez Ford, real name Kenneth Crawford. WWE’s subsidiary, Event Services, LLC, is also included in the suit. Lucas was working as an off-duty security guard for a July 2026 edition of Monday Night Raw in Rosemont, Illinois. Crawford is from the city of Chicago. Lucas is suing because Crawford performed a ‘lap dance’ on him during Netflix’s live broadcast of Raw, and WWE then pushed the clip out onto their social media pages. Lucas alleges 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. POST Wrestling reached out to WWE for a statement, but as of this writing, they have not responded. The site notes that the interaction between Crawford and Lucas is no longer on the July 6th Raw on Netflix feed. Lucas states that Crawford danced toward him without consent. He added that because of the attention it got, he became publicly recognizable. He said the next day, people saw him and started mocking him by imitating what Crawford had done. Lucas added that his children have been ‘mocked and ridiculed’ at school because of what happened. He said he’s suffered humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress. He brought up that WWE and Crawford used his image for commercial purposes, which he alleges violates the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas’ attorney, Whitney Barr, issued the following statement to POST: “Like so many law enforcement officers, Mr. Lucas works a second job in order to better provide for his children.” “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized ‘lap dance.'” It continues, “[Crawford] moved his body increasingly closer to [Lucas]; continued the lap dance. [Crawford’s] left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff’s leg.” Lucas is asking the court to award him an unspecified amount of monetary damages, punitive damages, his legal costs, and to order that WWE and Crawford can’t use his identity.
summary: Cook County Sheriff's officer Noel Lucas filed a lawsuit October 14 in Cook County Circuit Court against WWE, its subsidiary Event Services LLC, and Montez Ford over an unwanted lap dance performed during the July 6 Monday Night Raw broadcast in Rosemont, Illinois. Lucas claims the incident, which aired live on Netflix and was shared on WWE social media, led to public mockery, recognition on the street, and ridicule of his children at school. The suit alleges 14 counts including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act.

title: On the Record: Roman Reigns Explains Why He No Longer Works WWE Live Events
raw_title: Roman Reigns Explains Why He No Longer Works WWE Live Events
body: In the past few years, Roman Reigns has become more of a star attraction for WWE. He doesn’t wrestle as often as he used to, but his involvement still brings a lot of eyeballs to the product. During his early days in WWE, Reigns was consistently featured on WWE programming, including its live events. With Reigns now working a part-time schedule with WWE, he rarely works on such events anymore. Also read: Roman Reigns On Whether Being Called ‘Overrated’ By Conrad Thompson Bothers Him Reigns explained that WWE’s current business model is television rights, so it doesn’t make sense for him to work house shows for a smaller audience. “Now with my schedule, people will pick on it but they don’t remember from 2012 to 2018 when I was doing 150-200 shows a year, every single year, just working my a** off but staying in the lab, continually getting the reps, conquering my 10,000 hours, putting my time in, that’s where I learned how to do everything, and we’re trying to get that back,” Reigns said. “I think we’re trying to run more live events and they are good, but we’re just at a business model where TV rights are TV rights and there’s just so much money on the line that we’ve got to that point where it’s just like it doesn’t make sense for me to do live events anymore. What if I got hurt? There’s so much money that’s riding on Mondays and Fridays and our PLEs now that I can’t just go out there and wrestle for 4,000-5,000 only, just for those eyes only. Now, I’ve got to conserve it.”

title: Drew McIntyre Prioritizes Acting While Staying Ring-Ready
raw_title: Former WWE Champion Says He’s Ready To Wrestle but Is Focused on ‘Hollywood Drew’
body: During a new interview with OutKick Dropkick , the former WWE World Heavyweight Champion made it clear that he's mainly concentrated on his acting gigs. In case WWE calls him for his return, though, he's keeping himself physically ready. "I'm as big as I've ever been. I'm 285, right? And I'm 10 pounds bigger than I was for 'Agent of Shadows.' I'm in the best shape of my life," McIntyre said when asked about his return to a WWE ring. "I posted myself running the ropes the other day, keeping myself in ring shape. I'm always ready to go. I think it got like over 8 million views, just bouncing off the ropes a few times, across my social media platforms. But right now, I'm focused on Hollywood Drew. So, we'll see. We will see." Amidst his hiatus from WWE TV, McIntyre took on roles in The Last Druid and Highlander , action movies in which he starred alongside Academy Award-winning actor Russell Crowe. A press release also revealed him as a voice actor in Disney's upcoming fantasy film Hexed , starring Hailee Steinfeld. Next week, fans will see him in a new ReelShort microdrama, titled Agent of Shadows , too. The timeframe for McIntyre's long-awaited return to a WWE ring is unclear. WrestleVotes on Fightful Select recently reported that WWE officials have discussed the possibility of him landing on the WWE Raw brand whenever he does make it. His last WWE appearances saw him feuding with The Bloodline's Jacob Fatu on SmackDown in the lead-up to WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas. McIntyre is currently focused on his Hollywood career, which includes starring roles in The Last Druid and Highlander alongside Russell Crowe, a voice part in Disney's Hexed with Hailee Steinfeld, and an upcoming appearance in the ReelShort microdrama Agent of Shadows. The timing of his WWE comeback remains unknown after officials reportedly discussed bringing him back during his hiatus.

In an exclusive interview shared with Heavy , Diamond Dallas Page explained his new role with NXT and the vital techniques he plans to teach the talent. Trick Williams is not the only former NXT Champion Diamond Dallas Page has trained. Page shared that he has known Bron Breakker since he was in college and has a good relationship with his father and uncle, Rick and Scott Steiner. “I’ve been working with Bron Breakker since he was in college, because I’m buddies with the Steiners,” Page told Gambling.com . body: superstar Roman Reigns revealed which pro wrestlers he has on his own personal Mount Rushmore list. The Mount Rushmore list has been an ongoing debate within the pro wrestling community. Pro wrestling has a very rich history. Given the success of companies outside of WWE, there are several wrestlers who can make strong arguments. As a result, many fans and wrestlers themselves have their own criteria that they prioritize most. Reigns is no different, as he shared the metric he strongly considers when putting together a Mount Rushmore list. That metric is money that the talent drew during their career, particularly when they were top stars in the industry. revealed which WWE legends he has on his personal Mount Rushmore list. 'The Tribal Chief' took into account the money each star drew, as well as their popularity. "Only one metric matters, the money. It's show business. The first day I went around the ring, my dad told me, 'Don't ever be confused, this ring is only about money. It's a business. Don't treat it any other way,'" Reigns told Club Shay Shay . "I would probably have to say Hulk [Hogan], Steve [Austin], Dwayne [ The Rock ], and John [Cena]. I mean, you could definitely throw some other guys in there for sure, but we only got so many slots. And those guys, when it came to the money and shifting the business, and changing the view of it, the optics of it, they all had their way of doing that, and they were all critical." He added: "We wouldn't be here today without those four for sure." Reigns also revealed that he considers Hulk Hogan to be the greatest of all time. During his appearance on Club Shay Shay , host Shannon Sharpe asked Reigns who he considers to the greatest of all time. Like the Mount Rushmore debate, the GOAT conversation has become an ongoing debate among fans. Although Reigns noted that while his cousin, The Rock, makes a strong argument, Hogan revolutionized the industry. "Dwayne, I really respect how he did it. It was just lightning in a bottle. You never seen it like that. Nobody picked it up so quickly and at such a jump," he said. "Early on, Rock trying to figure out that character to boom, superstardom in a matter of 18 months and then was able to just go like, 'I don't need the machine anymore.' So in a way, there's a GOAT factor to that." "Hulk had a crazy amount of merch. Every little thing you could think of. Hulk took us from a carnival to a global product, you know what I mean? So that's a tough one." The post WWE Superstar Roman Reigns Reveals His Mount Rushmore appeared first on HEAVY .

The pair were invited to appear as extra talent on the Sept. 28 card and took a leap of faith, unsure how — or even if — they’d be included. “We waited all day to be told what we were going to do,” Ali said. “After the security guards got picked, we were picked as fans, still not knowing what we were going to do. They finally told us and we were like ‘Wow, hopefully this goes through,’ and it did! It was a lot of fun.” But after they arrived at the Fiserv Forum, they found themselves in the center of the action. Ali and Blackrose were incorporated into a throwdown between the Bloodline faction (Jacob Fatu and the Usos) and the heel stable the 946 (Royce Keys, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price). Tensions couldn’t have been higher between the rival groups, and their six-way brawl escaped the confines of the ring. After Bloodline’s Jimmy Uso jumped from the barricade, the 946’s Price grabbed him and hurled him into the audience, straight into Ali. Blackrose, who narrowly avoided being toppled by Uso, opted for a more direct altercation. He confronted Nima and, despite his best efforts, went down after a swift hit to the jaw. The segment ended shortly after with the two factions taking their feud backstage. The Alamo City wrestlers’ appearance was brief, but it gave them a chance to perform at one of professional wrestling’s highest-profile events. Like their Greyhound bus journey to last month’s Raw, Blackrose and Ali’s wrestling careers began in San Antonio. Both are graduates of the Hybrid School of Wrestling, where they train under the guidance of head coaches Sho Funaki, a WWE legend, and independent wrestler Chris Marval. San Antonio-born Blackrose got the wrestling bug early. He attended his first WWE show at the age of 9 and saw legendary El Paso-born wrestler Eddie Guerrero in action three weeks before his untimely death. “Years later, I attended a [River City Wrestling] show, and that’s when I discovered independent wrestling,” Blackrose said. “I asked RCW promoter Brandon Oliver about joining the business, and he gave me the information for Hybrid, where I’ve trained since 2019. title: Kaitlyn Rules Out In-Ring Return
raw_title: Former WWE champion definitively rules out return and confirms retirement: ‘I don’t have this burning desire’
body: Former WWE Divas Champion Kaitlyn, aka Celeste Bonin, has shared a major update on her wrestling career. A part of the WWE roster from 2010 to 2014, Kaitlyn was known for her powerhouse move set and impressive physique. A former WWE Divas Champion, Kaitlyn parted ways with WWE in 2014 and wrestled for a few years in the indies. She later returned for a brief run in 2018. However, her second run did not last long, and she was eliminated in the Mae Young Classic 2018 Second Round by Michin, aka Mia Yim. Recently, speaking to Chris Van Vliet, Bonin opened up about her wrestling future and completely ruled out the chances of an in-ring return . "I hope no one hates me for this, but I don't really want to get back in the ring. I respect wrestling a lot, and I find it very entertaining. "I love the artistry of it. I don't think I could ever have the appreciation that I have now if I had never been a professional wrestler. Because there are so many aspects to the performance," said Kaitlyn. "There's so many things to think about. The psychology of the match, connecting with people, telling a story with your face and your body, protecting your face and your body, protecting the person that you're in the ring with, helping them perform to their best," she further added. The 40-year-old currently works as a model and has no "burning desire," for a wrestling return. "Knowing where the cameras are, knowing how much time you have, being able to change it up if the people in the audience aren't buying it, if they don't care about it, so there's so much to it. "It's such a beautiful art form, so I will always love it and deeply respect it. I don't really watch it, but occasionally I will if there's someone that I'm still friends with or that I love. Occasionally I'll watch a match, but I don't know. I don't think I am gonna get back in the ring because I don't have this burning desire to do that." She last wrestled in 2019 at the GWA 3rd Annual Toy Drive and is vividly remembered for her feud against AJ Lee in WWE.

Get NFL Alerts Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share via E-mail More share options Share on Pinterest Share on Flipboard Share on Reddit Share on WhatsApp 0 Shares By Jalyn Smoot Updated Oct 15, 2026 at 3:01pm Getty MEXICO CITY, MEXICO - SEPTEMBER 14: Roman Reigns makes his entrance during Monday Night RAW at Arena Ciudad de Mexico on September 14, 2026 in Mexico City, Mexico. (Photo by Meg Oliphant/WWE via Getty Images) Roman Reigns is one of the most heralded WWE superstars in history. A former Royal Rumble winner, WrestleMania main eventer, and multi-time World Champion, there are few things Reigns has not accomplished in the squared circle. Although he descends from a lineage of wrestling legends , Reigns initially did not intend to pursue wrestling. In an interview with Pro Football Hall of Famer Shannon Sharpe, Reigns explained how his leukemia diagnosis spurred his career pivot from football to WWE . Play Reigns (real name Joe Anoa’i) played defensive tackle at Georgia Tech for four seasons from 2003 to 2006. During his senior season, the standout defensive tackle earned First Team All-ACC honors. He was also named Lifter of the Year in 2006, an award he shared with Detroit Lions legend and Georgia Tech alum Calvin Johnson . Shortly after college, Reigns signed with the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent, and believed he would carve out a lengthy NFL career. However, a leukemia diagnosis all but dashed his football dream. Reigns recalled that lab work revealed he had “way more” white blood cells than usual, putting his budding NFL career in jeopardy. “I think I had about 70,000 white blood cells . Typically, you’re somewhere between 5,000 and 10,000 if anything is running normally.” He added, “Back then, there was nobody like me. There was nobody that had come out at 21 years old, collegiate athlete with leukemia. So, I thought it was pretty much a sports death sentence. There was a gonna be a giant asterisk attached to my name. Nobody was gonna [sign] me.” Reigns said of his leukemia diagnosis: “ That was the day that changed my life .” Reigns briefly signed with the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2007, when his leukemia was in remission, but was cut during training camp. The reigning World Heavyweight Champion retired from football in 2008 after his lone season in the CFL. Although he didn’t have the NFL career he envisioned, Reigns is grateful that he ultimately pursued pro wrestling. When asked if he would have pursued a WWE or Hollywood career if his NFL career wasn’t cut short, Reigns said, “Naw, I don’t think so. That was my grand story. title: Did Street Fighter Actor And WWE Wrestler Cody Rhodes Accidentally Let Slip He’s In The X-Men Reboot?
raw_title: Did Street Fighter Actor And WWE Wrestler Cody Rhodes Accidentally Let Slip He’s In The X-Men Reboot?
body: We already know a handful of the actors who will be joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe when Marvel finally fully reboots the X-Men in 2028 . Sadie Sink has already made her debut as Jean Grey in Spider-Man: Brand New Day , and others set to join the mutant crew in the new film include Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbot as Professor X, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost. Adam Driver will round out the cast as villain Mr. Sinister, but there are plenty of other X-Men who aren’t accounted for. Enter Cody Rhodes, a WWE wrestler turned actor who is playing Guile in the new Street Fighter movie that’s out tonight. With his new movie in theaters, he and the rest of the cast have been on a promotional tour, and in a new interview with Nerdist , Rhodes may have accidentally let it slip that he’s in the X-Men movie. At the 1:29 mark, Rhodes is talking about his various nerd interests, and says what sure sounds like “I’m in X-Men .” . His co-star, anti-woke personality Andrew Schulz , reacts immediately, saying “Wait, you are?”, and then, as Rhodes carries on as if all is normal, says he thought Rhodes had just “made an announcement” of some kind. If Rhodes realized what he’d said, he maintained a great poker face and managed to carry on the interview without missing a beat. Now, fans are speculating about who Rhodes could be playing in the movie. There’s no shortage of big buff mutants in the X-Men universe, so could he be Colossus, Cable, Havok, Iceman, or someone less obvious and prominent? If he’s locked down the role, maybe an official announcement is imminent. For now, the MCU is focused pretty squarely on December’s Avengers: Doomsday , though VisionQuest premiered this week on Disney+ and is pretty good so far. body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 16, 2026, 5:37 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. An off-duty security guard has filed a lawsuit against both parties for the unwilling part he played during a Street Profits entrance earlier this year, with emotional distress listed among the many counts being brought against the defendants. Details about the lawsuit have been shared by POST Wrestling . The plaintiff, Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas, was working his second job as a security guard during an episode of Raw this past July, which aired live on Netflix. Lucas was one of the many people working security who spend the majority of the show sitting just inside the barrier with their back to the ring. The clip that aired live and was subsequently shared on social media, including by Ford himself, shows the WWE Superstar approaching Lucas and then dancing in front of him for an extended period. Ford gyrates and thrusts his hips towards Lucas in a moment the plaintiff's attorney claims was unplanned and describes as a "lap dance". The suit also claims Ford's leg repeatedly rubbed against Lucas's. The lawsuit includes 14 counts being brought against Ford and WWE, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Lucas also claims that since his face is visible in the clip, meaning that he can be easily identified, WWE has violated the Illinois Right of Publicity Act by using his likeness for commercial purposes without permission. Lucas claims that, when he returned to his day job at the courthouse the day after appearing on Raw, he was recognized by multiple members of the public, some of whom ridiculed him by mimicking the movements Ford had performed in front of him on the show the night before. Months later, Lucas notes that the humiliation and embarrassment brought on by the segment in which he was an unwilling participant persists. body: Is "The Mad Dragon" on his way to AEW? After weeks of reports and speculation about Ilja Dragunov 's much-awaited AEW debut, it now seems that the time has finally come. Dragunov parted ways with WWE a couple of months ago when he decided to not renew his contract. Soon after rejecting a contract extension, Dragunov immediately became a free agent upon its expiry. Rumors soon emerged about him signing an AEW deal and joining the promotion. While fans waited weeks for signs of his arrival, AEW decided to keep silent. Now, after months of speculation, AEW has finally dropped Dragunov's first television tease . On the recent Oct. 14, 2026, episode of AEW Dynamite and Collision, before AEW WrestleDream 2026, a mysterious vignette aired. Running for about 25 seconds, the vignette features multiple shots of a metronome as well as a person conducting music with their hands. The video package also shows a person walking down a set of steps and running across a training ring. The video teased the arrival of a new AEW star. While it did not confirm or specify Ilja Dragunov's name, fans were certain of his arrival on the internet. Once the signing is made official, Dragunov will join The New Level and Motor City Machine Guns as former WWE talents joining AEW in the last few months. Dragunov is a former WWE United States Champion, NXT Champion, and NXT UK Champion. He was with WWE since 2019 before not renewing his contract in 2026. The 33-year-old's last match dates back to the 2026 Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal before WWE WrestleMania 42.

title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement
raw_title: Adam Copeland, Edge in WWE, Announces His Retirement Plans
body: Copeland announced Wednesday on AEW Dynamite that 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling. The 52-year-old made the announcement after defeating Josh Alexander to qualify for the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, where the AEW World Championship will be at stake. Copeland acknowledged that he is "aging out" and isn't the wrestler whose face is on posters on teenagers' walls anymore. He then made it clear that becoming AEW World Champion is one of the goals he wants to accomplish before walking away. Copeland is one of the greatest wrestlers of all time and one of my personal favorites, so I wish him nothing but the best. His comments about aging out of the business are true, but this time there is something satisfying about it. Copeland gets to decide when it's time. That wasn't the case in 2011, when Edge was forced to retire because of his neck. His return at the 2020 Royal Rumble was something most fans never expected to see. Now, assuming he wrestles into 2027, Copeland will have effectively gotten a seven-year second act to a career that once ended far too soon. I'd love to see Edge wrestle one more WWE match before it's over. At the same time, I don't feel like I need it. His WWE return already gave us more than we ever thought we'd get after 2011. Everything since 2020 has been bonus time. Now Copeland gets something even better: the chance to finish on his own terms. title: Zelina Vega Reveals Cody Rhodes Extended Her SmackDown Match

body: D.S. Shin of Ring The Belle conducted an extensive interview with former WWE talent Xelina, a.k.a. Zelina Vega. One of the stories she shared centered around the Women’s United States Title match that she had against Giulia on an August 2025 episode of SmackDown. Xelina mentioned that she views Giulia as her wrestling soulmate. She shared that their match time was initially based on how long John Cena and Cody Rhodes would go in the opening segment. Xelina went to speak to Rhodes about it, and he ended up saving 10 minutes of time for the U.S. Title match. Xelina remembers seeing a plan that she and Green pitched together be brought up by Brian ‘Road Dogg’ James on WWE: Unreal on Netflix. You would win it back, but have Zoey come in, beat the everliving sh*t out of me. Make it disgusting. Make it really bad so that people will feel for me. I will get that kind of sympathy back and then you guys are sitting up there, the big heels, you got your title back, and it’s great. You guys are sitting up there. Now I have something to chase. Give me something to chase. I needed — as a babyface specifically — I needed to have that kind of push from the audience again. She loved the idea and she’s like, ‘Let’s do it,’ like whatever, and so we pitched it together, then they pitched it in the meeting and then that’s how it happened, but, I already went in kind of knowing I was gonna win it and then I was gonna lose it the very next week, or at least that’s what it was supposed to be. Did not happen that way… What’s funny is, on (WWE: Unreal), you see Road Dogg saying, ‘Oh, I think we should switch it back to Chelsea.’ He was trying to pitch what we came up with. He got so much heat for that, but he was just trying to pitch what her and I came together on. It looked completely different and obviously Hunter had different ideas. Zoey Stark was supposed to interfere during the rematch by attacking Xelina severely to generate sympathy for her as a babyface. Xelina said the goal was to position Green and her group as strong heels with the title while giving Xelina a clear storyline to chase.

She explained that she entered knowing she would win the championship only to drop it shortly after as part of the booked sequence. Xelina saw Brian 'Road Dogg' James present a similar concept on WWE: Unreal on Netflix, which originated from the pitch she and Green submitted together.

Xelina had requested the chance to demonstrate the title's importance to her so that losing it would create stronger emotional impact. As a result of the change, Xelina had limited title defenses and Chelsea Green was left without a clear direction in the storyline.

title: Shotzi Blackheart Withdraws From CMLL Tour
raw_title: Former WWE Star Shotzi Blackheart Withdraws From CMLL Tour Following Family Tragedy
body: WWE/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It's been a week of change for Shotzi Blackheart's career, as she's made the move from MLW to TNA after appearing on the latter's TV tapings on Tuesday. Unfortunately, it has also been a trying week for Blackheart in her personal life, one that will be affecting a booking she had next week. Taking to X on Wednesday morning, Blackheart revealed that her brother, Dean, had passed away last Sunday night. Blackheart further stated that now that her booking obligations for this week had been fulfilled, she would be taking time off to be with family and "honor my brother's memory," announcing that she would be pulling out of the CMLL Women's Gran Prix as a result. "It was a huge honor to be selected for the CMLL Grand Prix, and I don't take that opportunity lightly," Blackheart said. "Thank you to everyone at CMLL and the fans for understanding how hard all this is for me." It was just seven months ago that Blackheart's brother was in the news after the former MLW Women's Featherweight Champion revealed that he had gone missing in California after stumbling away from a car accident. He was found shortly after and hospitalized . Blackheart has credited her brother with helping her become a wrestling fan as a child, as she would watch matches and play wrestling video games with him. It's the second family loss Blackheart has suffered in the last five years, having lost her father in 2021 . At the moment, it is unclear who will replace Blackheart in CMLL Gran Prix next week. It will be the second time CMLL has had to make a change to the lineup after Lady Frost was removed from the match and replaced by Masha Slamovich last week after Frost departed MLW. Wrestling Inc. would like to offer its condolences to Blackheart during this difficult time.
summary: Shotzi Blackheart has pulled out of the CMLL Women's Gran Prix next week to mourn the death of her brother Dean, who passed away last Sunday. The former WWE performer had just switched from MLW to TNA after appearing on their TV tapings earlier this week and fulfilled her current obligations before stepping away to be with family. She expressed gratitude to CMLL for understanding during this difficult time.

title: Lola Vice Recalls Scary Ladder Fall At MITB
raw_title: Lola Vice Comments On Ladder Incident At WWE Money In The Bank: “It Hurt A Lot & Was Very Scary”
body: One of the marquee bouts at the 2026 WWE Money in the Bank Premium Live Event was the women’s Money in the Bank Ladder match. Among the participants were Lola Vice and WWE Women’s United States Champion Jacy Jayne. There was a point in the bout when the two talents were trading blows on the same side of a ladder. Vice put Jayne in a chokehold, and then they fell onto a ladder that was propped up by the middle ring rope and the ladder they were standing on. Vice and Jayne bounced off the ladder, but it shifted and then sent them both out of the ring and onto the floor. Vice commented on the incident during her appearance on WWE Ahora (translation by Fightful’s Luis Pulido ). “I had Jacy (Jayne) in a choke and when I put her to sleep, she fell back and I fell with her. I thought that was the end of it, but suddenly the ladder went backwards, and literally, it got us out of the ring. Because of that, I didn’t win Money in the Bank. It hurt a lot and was very scary, but looking back, thank God it came out like this because it could have been very ugly. I think an injury in a Ladder match would have been rough. They are not for everyone, but thank God I’m strong and I was able to do it.” If the quote in this article is used, please credit WWE Ahora with an H/T to Fightful’s Luis Pulido for the transcription.
summary: During the women's Money in the Bank ladder match at the 2025 premium live event, Lola Vice and Jacy Jayne fell from a ladder that shifted unexpectedly after Vice applied a chokehold. The incident sent both competitors out of the ring to the floor, preventing Vice from winning the briefcase. Vice later described the moment as painful and frightening but expressed relief that neither wrestler was injured in what could have been a serious accident.

title: Cody Rhodes Says Ari Emanuel Didn't Know Him Before WrestleMania 40
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Claims TKO CEO Ari Emanuel Didn’t Know Who He Was Until WWE WrestleMania 40
body: Among the cast members of the Street Fighter movie are WWE’s Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns. They’ve been touring with fellow cast members for a media run, and one of the outlets they spoke to was the New York Times . Rhodes told the outlet that TKO CEO Ari Emanuel was unaware of who he was until WrestleMania 40 in 2024, where Rhodes headlined nights one and two. A month after WrestleMania 40, Rhodes signed with W.M.E. (Williams Morris Endeavor), which is the talent and media agency that Emanuel is the Executive Chairman of. In 2023, a deal made W.W.E. part of a new company, TKO Group Holdings, led by the Hollywood power broker Ari Emanuel. After a high-profile match in Philadelphia in 2024, Rhodes signed with WME, the talent agency Emanuel helped found, which also represents Johnson and Cena. Rhodes said Emanuel did not know who the wrestler was before that night, but WME set up the meeting at Legendary and Rhodes was cast in “Street Fighter.” Rhodes said he wanted to “do right” by Emanuel and Khan, a former television agent at Creative Artists Agency, a rival of WME. “They’ve told the town, ‘You’re a serious person,’ and that’s really helpful,” Rhodes said. A TKO spokeswoman declined to make Emanuel available for comment. Rhodes is a three-time Undisputed WWE Champion. His latest reign came to an end in June 2026 when he dropped the belt to Sami Zayn.
summary: Cody Rhodes revealed that TKO CEO Ari Emanuel was unaware of who he was until Rhodes headlined WrestleMania 40 in 2024. A month after the event Rhodes signed with WME, the agency Emanuel serves as Executive Chairman of, which helped lead to his casting in the upcoming Street Fighter movie alongside Roman Reigns. Rhodes noted he wanted to do right by both Emanuel and his former CAA agent Ari Greenwald, crediting them for establishing him as a serious talent in Hollywood.

title: Roman Reigns Says Wrestling Is His Craft
raw_title: Roman Reigns: Wrestling Is My Craft, I Own That Shit - Fightful | WWE News, AEW News, Pro Wrestling Backstage News
body: The upcoming ‘Street Fighter’ film features a big cast that includes egos from the world of wrestling and from Hollywood. According to most accounts, it sounds like the cast had a blast during the film’s shoot in Australia. Speaking with Sam Roberts for a new interview , Reigns said that he wasn’t running around the set acting like he was Noah Centineo. But in wrestling, a bunch of people walk around acting like their on Roman’s level. “There’s a great camaraderie in wrestling. I mean, being one of the boys, I can’t even explain it because I’m in the small fraternity, I’m in that 1%. Honestly, that should just be for us. But, the difference is I wasn’t running around thinking I’m Noah [Centineo], you know what I mean? There’s plenty of dudes in the locker room that are running around thinking they’re Roman Reigns, thinking they’re of my level. It’s crazy. It’s just ridiculous. Look in the mirror and look at all your stuff, everything that comes with your life. Look at your bank account, all the stuff. We’re not the same. I didn’t run around thinking I’m Noah [Centineo] or Andrew [Koji]. No, I’m here to work with them, compliment them, make the very best combination or collaboration to create the best film. There’s no confusion here, we all understand who we are and what we’re trying to do and we all came together that way in a perfect way. But in wrestling, it just can’t be had that way.” Despite coming from a football background, Reigns isn’t vibing with the teamwork aspect of wrestling. He insists that he owns “that shit”. “Look, I come from football, so I’m always going to look at a teamwork aspect but wrestling is different. That’s my craft, I own that shit. That is mine, you know what I mean? Like mine. I don’t give a shit about any of them, it’s mine.” Sam Roberts proceeded by asking Reigns when he adopted this mindset. “Probably when I was born, but it doesn’t click until — honestly, before COVID hit and I left, I had dog food all on me, it was just one of those situations where I just wasn’t creatively — I just wasn’t in line. I didn’t like what I was doing. I didn’t like the way I was portrayed. It was just time to take complete ownership and the proof is in the pudding.” Elsewhere in the interview, Roman Reigns talked about the importance of analytics in wrestling. title: Bully Ray Questions WWE Booking Of Chelsea Green's Raw Loss
raw_title: Bully Ray Is Baffled By WWE's Decision To Have Current World Champion Lose On Raw
body: Bryan Steffy/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover It was a rare appearance for WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green this past Monday on "Raw," and not one she'll want to remember, as she not only lost to Roxanne Perez, but was beaten up by Perez, Liv Morgan, and Raquel Rodriguez in the post-match . While all of this was done to build to Green vs. Morgan at Crown Jewel , Bully Ray was left cold to it, questioning co-host Dave LaGreca on "Busted Open Radio" about why Green had to be the one who lost this match. "Can you help me make sense of it?" Bully said. "I'm legitimately asking you this question. This is not for radio entertainment. I don't know why they brought Chelsea over last night. I don't know why Chelsea had to lose in the middle to Roxanne last night." While LaGreca presented plenty of arguments, and did note that Green's loss wasn't a clean loss, Bully still wasn't buying it. "For the most part, I got that there was a pretty definitive victory for Roxanne, and then the beat down afterwards," Bully said. "I just didn't know why they had to beat Chelsea Green last night. It just seems like every time there's a step forward for Chelsea Green, there's some kind of a step back. And then Chelsea finds a way to step forward again." Bully then argued that Green should've gone over, and if the idea was for WWE to keep Perez strong, they should've had her win the Women's Money in the Bank match days before . Furthermore, Bully was bothered by WWE presenting Green as a serious wrestler, only for her to come up short at her best. "They went out of their way last night to have Chelsea Green really wrestle a match, didn't they, to show her wrestling ability, which we see a lot more of Chelsea's entertainment side then we see her wrestling side, right?" Bully said. "Well, in Chelsea bringing her best wrestling game to the table last night, in a wrestling match, not climbing a ladder, in a wrestling match, she lost." body: 00:30 Featured Video CARMELO JOINS 946 😱 Previous Next WWE/WWE via Getty Images Top WWE Moments That Could Be Horror Movies Erik Beaston Oct 15, 2026 October ushers in the Halloween season, when horror movie fans embrace all things haunting, macabre and terrifying. It also offers wrestling fans a chance to revisit WWE's long history of incorporating horror into its programming—with varying degrees of success. In celebration of all things that go bump in the night, make the hairs on your arms stand up and send shivers down your spine, relive these moments from the last four decades of WWE television—each worthy of a horror movie in its own right. Imagine if the giant snake in Anaconda had feasted on Jennifer Lopez's character, or the titular serpent had gotten the best of Jessica Rothe's character in Beware Boiúna . That was the situation in 1991, when Jake "The Snake" Roberts produced a live cobra and taunted "Macho Man" Randy Savage as the reptile bit into the Hall of Famer's biceps. Miss Elizabeth and fans in attendance and watching at home looked on in horror, fearing for the former WWE champion's safety. Savage would recover and get revenge on Roberts, but the attack remains unsettling to watch today—especially for viewers afraid of snakes. He didn't carry red balloons or ask young fans in the front row if they could float too, but the original incarnation of Doink the Clown was evil nonetheless. Taking great delight in tormenting fans and wrestlers alike, the evil jester would chuckle one moment, then stare menacingly into the camera the next, his expression suddenly turning deadly serious. It wasn't one particular moment that made the original Doink terrifying—it was the entire experience. He laughed and joked like an innocent circus clown but behaved like a vile, deceitful horror villain. Much of that could be credited to Matt Borne and his understanding of how to bring Doink to life. His performance gave the character a sinister depth and helped establish a legacy that endures today. As long as you stop watching before his ill-fated babyface turn. Still, Doink evoked Tim Curry's portrayal of Pennywise in 1990's It . Beneath the seemingly harmless clown exterior lurked a sinister edge—a reminder that appearances could be deceiving. In the spring of 2019, Bray Wyatt was badly in need of a reboot—and he delivered, introducing the wrestling world to the Firefly Fun House. Channeling Mr. Rogers, he greeted the audience with enthusiasm, but a dark, sinister edge lurked beneath his cheerful demeanor. Each week, fans ventured further down the rabbit hole until Wyatt introduced one of WWE's most terrifying characters: The Fiend. Wyatt's alter ego was the stuff of nightmares. Former WWE star Xelina has opened up about her run as Women’s United States Champion, revealing that she wanted to take the championship beyond WWE and establish it as a true workhorse title. During an interview with D.S. Shin of Ring The Belle , she reflected on what she hoped to accomplish and why she wished WWE’s creative direction had allowed her more freedom. Xelina became the second holder of the Women’s United States Championship and held the title for 63 days. However, her reign featured just one successful title defense before she lost the championship to Giulia. Speaking about her championship run, Xelina said she wanted to defend the belt in different promotions rather than keep it confined to WWE programming. “I wish that he (Triple H) would have loved it on me enough to let me defend it the way I wanted to defend it,” Xelina said. She then explained the bigger ambition behind her idea, naming two promotions where she hoped to bring the championship. “But it’s fine, because I wanted to go and bring it to AAA and f*cking STARDOM. Let me bring it to different places and really make this the workhorse title if that’s what we were gonna do.” The comments suggest Xelina wanted the championship to become a regular feature across multiple wrestling promotions, giving it a more active presence through frequent defenses. Her proposed approach would have taken the title beyond WWE’s own shows and introduced it to audiences elsewhere. The Women’s United States Championship was Xelina’s first singles title in WWE. She had previously won the Women’s Tag Team Championship, but her singles reign offered a unique opportunity to establish herself as a champion. Her remarks also reflect a broader frustration with the creative freedom she believes was limited during her WWE tenure. In the same interview, she discussed wanting more room to express her personality through promos and pursue matches she felt suited her abilities. For Xelina, the title could have been more than another championship to hold — she wanted it to be defended regularly and travel with her. Her vision for a workhorse belt never fully materialized during her reign, but she has now made clear what she hoped it could become. raw_title: Who Is Necro Butcher? Hardcore Wrestling Legend Signs WWE Deal at 53
body: Butcher announced Tuesday that he signed what he described as a "basic legends deal" with WWE. PWInsider subsequently confirmed with WWE sources that the deal is "100% accurate" and reported that WWE President Nick Khan spearheaded the agreement. The signing is unusual because Butcher built his reputation almost entirely outside wrestling's biggest companies. For WWE fans who only became familiar with him this year through Dark Side of the Ring , here's what to know about one of independent wrestling's most notorious performers. Necro Butcher's real name is Dylan Keith Summers. Born July 13, 1973, in West Virginia, Summers made his professional wrestling debut in 1998 and eventually became known for an exceptionally violent style of wrestling. His matches frequently included the weapons and violence associated with "deathmatch" wrestling, but Butcher also worked with some of the biggest names to emerge from the 2000s independent scene. His list of opponents included Bryan Danielson, Kevin Steen, Eddie Kingston, Chris Hero, Claudio Castagnoli and Samoa Joe. Butcher even reached Hollywood. He appeared in the acclaimed 2008 film The Wrestler , starring Mickey Rourke. If there is one match that defines Butcher's career, it's his 2005 encounter with Samoa Joe. The two met at IWA Mid-South's Something to Prove at the former ECW Arena in Philadelphia. The match developed a reputation over the next two decades for its brutality, including a memorable moment in which Joe kicked Butcher off the arena bleachers and onto the concrete floor. More than 20 years later, that match put Butcher back into the wrestling conversation. VICE's Dark Side of the Ring dedicated an episode of its seventh season to the story behind Samoa Joe vs. Necro Butcher. The episode explored not only the match but Butcher's life, career and the circumstances that brought the two wrestlers together. VICE later released the full episode on YouTube in July, where it has since generated more than 700,000 views. The timing is noteworthy. Butcher went from being the subject of a nationally televised wrestling documentary in 2026 to signing a WWE Legends deal months later. While neither WWE nor Butcher has publicly said Dark Side of the Ring led to the agreement, the episode undoubtedly brought renewed attention to his career and likely helped put him back on the radar. A WWE Legends deal generally allows WWE to license a wrestler's name and likeness for merchandise, video games and other projects, while also opening the door for appearances. It will be interesting to see whether that eventually includes an on-screen WWE appearance for Butcher. Given the unusual nature of the signing and the renewed attention surrounding his career, a future WWE Hall of Fame induction no longer feels completely out of the question, either. title: Dave Meltzer Explains Short Vaquer Title Run

body: WWE Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover At WWE Money in the Bank , Liv Morgan defeated Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch to become the Women's World Champion for the fourth time . She landed the Ob-LIV-ion on Vaquer after Vaquer sent Lynch through a table with a running knee to regain the title. title: Kofi and Austin Creed chase tag team greatness in AEW
raw_title: The New Day is gone, but the brotherhood lives on: Kofi and Austin Creed on finding a New Level in AEW
body: But while the location may change, and the names might be tweaked, and the music may get a new mix, the brothers who make up AEW's New Level have come this far together, and that reliance on one another has them looking at a run as pro-wrestling's definitive tag-team. "I'm funny with the word legacy, because honestly, I don't care if people remember me or not," Kofi, sans his former Kingston surname, explains ahead of Saturday's AEW WrestleDream 2026 pay-per-view , with a giant mural of Falor from "The NeverEnding Story" painted on the wall behind him. The man who won virtually every title during his WWE tenure, including becoming the company's second Black and first African-born WWE Champion ever, doesn't live in the past. He's always looking at what he can do, right now, to make people feel something in the moment. "The reason that we do community service, the reason that we help people, it's not for us. Like, I'm not doing it so that you remember me. I want everybody to have the greatest experience when I interact with them. And whether you remember me or not, is not important." There are too many moments in the group's career to count, but outside of KofiMania's climax , it's hard to think of a more electric, more feel-good moment than A$AP Ferg's "New Level" blaring through Wembley Stadium's speakers this past August at All In , the graphics that were once pink unicorns giving way to fire-breathing dragons on a wireframe grid, and Kofi and Austin Creed emerging to flank Swerve Strickland to challenge for the AEW Trios Championship. "I believe in myself and I believe in [Kofi]," Creed chimes in, leaning back on his "Rocky"-inspired roots for the next chapter of his career. "So regardless of where we are, we're going to be able to adapt. We're going to be able to create change. We are always going to be able to create success. So I don't necessarily think that we focus on legacy, because we're focused on the now. Like, what can we do now?" That "now" came about as quickly as possible under AEW's roof, with the pair capturing the trios titles alongside Strickland that night in the inaugural "Trios Roulette Royale." Now they're set to defend them against the former champions — "Hangman" Adam Page, Brody King and Bandido — at WrestleDream in a two-out-of-three falls match. But between bursting onto the new scene and giving the former champs their rematch, The New Level had to address the question that was top of everyone's minds: Did they have what it takes to hang with the no-frills, no-fear athletes of All Elite Wrestling? Their answer came right away, in a week-one title defense against The Rascalz, the free-spirited cruiserweight crew known for their quick tags, intricate team maneuvers and outlandish out-of-the-ring dives. We'd know right away if Creed and Kofi were up to snuff. Ospreay learned who would join him, “Speedball” Mike Bailey and Joe in the final five spots of Clockwork Carnage.
