Borden debuted in October 2025 and is one year into his wrestling career. With assistance from Darby Allin, he advanced to AEW's main roster.

During an episode of AEW Close-Up, Borden described leaving his previous life behind. He explained that he could not manage both his company responsibilities and wrestling training, which required 80 to 90 hours per week.
Borden chose to walk away from the company to focus entirely on wrestling. He has expressed that he is glad he made that decision.
At AEW All Out 2026, Borden suffered a serious concussion during a tag team match with Darby Allin against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight. The match had to be stopped as a result.
Borden has since recovered fully from the concussion. There is currently no information available on his return to the ring.

title: Mike Bailey Hesitant Joining AEW Faction
raw_title: Mike Bailey Was Hesitant To Join Another Group In AEW, Says It Was Interesting To Be A Lone Wolf
body: Bailey surprised fans by joining the group on the September 23 episode of AEW Dynamite. Whether it be luck or a wave of momentum, ‘Speedball’ hasn’t lost a match since making that decision. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Mike Bailey admitted that he was hesitant to join another group/team. “There was some hesitation in joining a group once again. I think AEW has a lot of factions and it is interesting to be a lone wolf, but obviously, I think those groups tend to to drag each other up, which is great. However, the last team I was in did not end very well. So having been hurt in the past, there was some hesitation, but when I talked about it with Will and saw the other members that were in it—I think Andrade is absolutely a top star in AEW right now. There is no doubt about it. He is doing his best work and it’s amazing to watch him being a part of the United Empire.” Bailey went on to say that Will Ospreay help him get to the next level. “Will Ospreay, I was thinking back when it was brought up to his match with Kenny Omega at All In, which I was completely blown away watching, thinking not only this is the best pro wrestling that we have ever seen, this is some of greatest stuff in history that I am seeing being written before my eyes, but also thinking this is exactly where I believe I belong. I want to prove that, and I want to get there, and I know that I can reach that level, and who better to take me there than Will Ospreay.” Fans can check out Fightful’s full interview with Mike Bailey in the video linked at the top of this article. Also, head over to our YouTube channel to catch up on more of our recent interviews.
summary: Mike Bailey revealed he had reservations about joining another group in AEW after a previous team ended poorly for him. The Speedball ultimately decided to align with Will Ospreay and the United Empire on the September 23 episode of Dynamite, citing Ospreay's influence and the presence of top star Andrade as key factors. Bailey has remained undefeated since the move and praised Ospreay's match against Kenny Omega at All In as historic.

title: AEW World Title To Be Defended In Clockwork Carnage Match At WrestleDream 2026
raw_title: AEW World Title To Be Defended In Clockwork Carnage Match At WrestleDream 2026
body: It was announced during the October 3 episode of "AEW Collision" that at WrestleDream, the AEW World Championship will defended in the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The match was actually trialed at Pro Wrestling EVE's "EVE 155: Global Thunder Queens Attack" event on October 2, with Ospreay booking the match himself and getting the seal of approval from Tony Khan to bring the stipulation to AEW. The match works in two stages. A total of eight AEW stars will take part with two men starting the bout. After three minutes, another performer will enter until all eight men have entered, but if someone is pinned or forced to submit but the final man enters the match, they officially eliminated. Once the last entrant is in, the second stage of the match begins as the remaining participants compete in a 15 minute Iron Man Match where every fall counts. At the end of the 15 minutes, the man with the most falls will be victorious and leave WrestleDream as the AEW World Champion. However, there is no guarantee that Ospreay will even be in the match as he will be making his second defense of the AEW World Championship this Tuesday at AEW Grand Slam France. Ospreay will go one-on-one with Kazuchika Okada with the title on the line, where the winner will move on to WrestleDream and attempt to defend the title in the new stipulation match. As for who the challengers will be, the first qualifying match for Clockwork Carnage will also take place in Paris as Samoa Joe will take on Jack Perry. The rest of the field will be revealed in the lead up to the big event on October 17.
summary: It was revealed during the October 3 episode of AEW Collision that at WrestleDream, the AEW World Championship will defended in the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The match was actually trialed at Pro Wrestling EVE's EVE 155: Global Thunder Queens Attack event on October 2.

llm.headline: AEW World Title Set For Clockwork Carnage At WrestleDream
llm.summary: The AEW World Championship will be defended in the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream 2026. The unique stipulation features eight competitors entering over three-minute intervals, with eliminations via pinfall or submission only counting after all have entered, followed by a 15-minute Iron Man period where every fall counts toward the final score. The concept was first trialed at a Pro Wrestling EVE event and received approval from Tony Khan after being devised by Will Ospreay, who defends the title against Kazuchika Okada at AEW Grand Slam France this week.

llm_long: The AEW World Championship match at WrestleDream will be contested under a new stipulation called Clockwork Carnage. The format was first tested at an independent event the day before it was announced on AEW Collision.

Eight competitors will participate in the match. It begins with two wrestlers, followed by an additional entrant every three minutes until all eight have entered. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated.

After the last participant enters, the match transitions into a 15-minute Iron Man format. All remaining wrestlers compete, with every pinfall or submission counting toward the total. The wrestler with the most falls at the end of the time limit wins the AEW World Championship.

The reigning champion will first defend the title in a singles match on Tuesday at AEW Grand Slam France against Kazuchika Okada. The winner of that bout will proceed to defend the championship in the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream.
Qualifying for the multi-man match begins in Paris with a bout between Samoa Joe and Jack Perry. Additional participants will be determined in the weeks leading up to the October 17 event.

title: Tony Khan Updates Jamie Hayter Injury Status
raw_title: Tony Khan Announces Jamie Hayter Is Injured, Hopes She'll Be Back In 'A Couple Of Weeks'
body: Following the three-hour broadcast of AEW Dynamite/Collision , All Elite Wrestling President Tony Khan went live on X. He broke the news that one-half of the AEW Women’s World Tag Team Champions, Jamie Hayter, is injured. Khan is hopeful that she’ll be back in the mix in a couple of weeks. “I was hoping The Brawling Birds would be able to defend the Tag Team Championship but Jamie Hayter — from that Chicago Street Fight — is still out injured. Hopefully Jamie Hayter will be back in a couple of weeks. But that was a major injury.” The Brawling Birds (Alex Windsor & Jamie Hayter) were in a backstage segment on the 10/14 Dynamite/Collision alongside fellow United Empire members ‘Speedball’ Mike Bailey, AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo, and AEW World Champion Will Ospreay. Hayter was last in action at All Out , where she and Windsor bested Divine Dominion (Lena Kross & Megan Bayne) in a Chicago Street Fight to retain the AEW Women’s World Tag Team Titles. The next pay-per-view for AEW is WrestleDream on October 17th. If the quote in this article is used, please credit Fightful for the transcription.

Hayter and Alex Windsor, known as The Brawling Birds, are the reigning AEW Women's World Tag Team Champions. Khan expressed hope that the British star will return to action within a couple of weeks.

title: Cornette defends Caster over TNA firing
raw_title: Jim Cornette says Max Caster didn’t deserve to be fired, blames TNA for Riyadh joke
body: Link AEW’s Twitter Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Former AEW star Max Caster made his TNA debut at Sunday’s Bound for Glory pay-per-view. His entrance rap included a line about recent bombings in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Less than 24 hours later, TNA cut ties with Caster for “making light of violent attacks.” Max then issued a statement on the matter where he ultimately said, “I can’t apologize for anyone being offended, but it’s not my intention to make people upset.” “When I turned on the Twitter machine and saw the news, I was like, what the fuck did he say? And then I listened to the clip. And after I listened to the clip, I was like, what the fuck did he say? I know the one thing that was probably problematic, but having said that, there wasn’t really a reason to fire the guy because who was producing him?” In a hypothetical scenario where Cornette was the producer, it would be part of his job to make sure he knows what Max plans on saying in his rap. “Max does have a history of being edgy . So, hear the promo. If I would have heard that, I would have said, take out Riyadh. People got killed, blah, blah, blah. Put something else in. And there’s nothing else that’s an issue. He didn’t say ‘fuck.’ He didn’t violate any broadcast standards. And then we’d go over their match, and their finish, and the blah, blah, blah. And if he really said, ‘Oh god, no. I gotta say this. My career depends on me getting out this greatest line that I’ve ever come up with.’ Then because I’m just the producer, I’m not the boss, I’m going to go to ‘insert name here,’ depending on whoever the boss is on scene of whatever production this is in this fictitious world, and say, Max wants to say this, this, and this. Yay or nay? And then let him plead his case or whatever, if it’s that big a deal. And most of the time it’s not.” Unless Caster went rogue and intentionally lied to TNA ahead of time about his rap, Cornette doesn’t understand how this happens when producers are there in part to make sure it doesn’t happen. “When people are mad about something and TNA hears about it, I wouldn’t have called Max Caster. I would have said, who fucking produced this shit? …Who didn’t ask him what he was gonna say? Who produced the thing? Did [Max] not tell him? If he told him one thing and did another, well then all the heat’s on Max. But for trivial bullshit like this that could have been easily addressed before it became an issue, I don’t understand how this happens.” Cornette’s line of reasoning sure makes sense to me. TNA did admit “the responsibility is ours” in their official statement, but those words seem pretty empty when Caster is the one taking the fall. summary: Jim Cornette believes Max Caster should not have been released by TNA after his Bound for Glory rap referenced recent bombings in Riyadh. Cornette argued that a producer should have reviewed the material in advance given Caster's history of edgy content and would have instructed him to remove the problematic line about the attacks that killed people. Caster made his TNA debut at the pay-per-view and later issued a statement saying he did not intend to upset anyone.

body: TNA has announced an International Championship match and more for next week’s episode of TNA Impact. It was announced on Thursday night’s episode of Impact that Mustafa Ali will get a rematch against Jason Hotch for the TNA International Championship in a Two Out of Three Falls match. In addition, a #1 contenders match for the TNA X-Division Championship will take place as Rich Swann, KC Navarro, Cedric Alexander, and Fabian Aichner will compete. And finally, Avery Styles will face off against Joe Alonzo. You can see the updated lineup below for next week’s episode of TNA Impact, which airs Thursday night on AMC, AMC+, and TNA+: * TNA International Championship Two Of Three Falls Match: Jason Hotch vs. Mustafa Ali. * TNA X-Division Championship #1 Contender’s Match: Rich Swann vs. K.C. Navarro vs. Cedric Alexander vs. Fabian Aichner * Avery Styles vs. Joe Alonzo

title: End of an Era: Former TNA and WWE star announces retirement from in-ring competition
raw_title: Former TNA and WWE star announces retirement from in-ring competition
body: In a post on his Facebook account , former TNA and WWE star Zach Gowen announced that he has retired from in-ring competition. This comes after the former WWE and TNA talent shared a picture of his experience working production at Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Northern Rising event on October 3. Following his WWE run in 2003-2004, Gowen competed in limited pro wrestling dates with TNA and independent promotions until 2013, and returned to the ring in May 2025 with AEW, facing Ricochet at that year’s Beach Break Dynamite in a match he calls “the best moment of my career,” noting that he wrestled in front of his wife, kids, and parents that night. His last match took place at the August 7 MLP tapings in Windsor, Ontario, Canada with a victory over Michael Allen Richard Clark. First promo pic and last promo pic! My in-ring career has come to an end. Thank you to every promoter who gave me an opportunity to wrestle. I’ve had the privilege of performing for every major company over the past 24 years. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid. All I ever wanted to be was a professional wrestler and I accomplished that solely because you accepted me not as a sideshow act but as a legitimate pro wrestler. I’m deeply grateful. The best moment of my career was wrestling for AEW in front of my wife, kids, and parents. That was the cherry on top after burning my career to the ground as a result of my crippling drug addiction then having the opportunity to not only rebuild my life but my passion then sharing that with the world while enjoying every second of it. My victories are not the result of my talents but ultimately the result of God working through others allowing them to pour into and invest in me. I am the luckiest guy in the world.
summary: Former TNA and WWE star Zach Gowen revealed that he has retired from in-ring competition. This comes after the former WWE and TNA talent shared a picture of his experience working production at Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Northern Rising event on October 3.

title: Ben Bishop Yet To Sign With TNA
raw_title: Backstage Update On TNA Status Of Ben Bishop Following Bound For Glory Debut
body: TNA Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover There were many names that took part in TNA's Call Your Shot battle royal this past Sunday at Bound for Glory, but none perhaps bigger than Ben Bishop. The 6 '10 Rhode Islander was the second to last entrant in the match, and though he failed to eliminate anyone, he made enough of an impression that some wondered whether he could be part of the TNA roster full-time. As it turns out, it hasn't happened just yet. Fightful Select reports that Bishop hasn't signed a contract with TNA, although those within the company felt he made a good impression. Bishop commented on the report on X, joking that this was why TNA hadn't allowed him into the building at Dothan, Alabama, where TNA held its TV tapings this week. It had previously been reported that Bishop has been a talent that TNA's had their eye on for some time, though attempts to hire him previously were seemingly thwarted by former TNA booker Tommy Dreamer, as the ECW veteran and "Busted Open Radio" co-host was said to not be a fan of videos Bishop had posted on social media regarding certain character ideas. While Dreamer admitted he told Bishop that he thought the videos were preventing him from being hired, he seemingly denied having anything to do with TNA not hiring Bishop, stating he liked him and that Bishop failing to sign on with TNA was more to do with a poor tryout from years earlier. Bishop has kept busy while waiting for an opportunity elsewhere, wrestling multiple times a month on the independent circuit, and even made an appearance in MLW's Battle Riot match that was taped back in January. Bishop also has several appearances for AEW under his belt, having competed in "AEW Dark" matches in both 2021 and 2022. His most high profile AEW match would occur in 2024, when he was defeated by Roderick Strong on an episode of "AEW Rampage."

body: Sacrifice 2022 Date: March 5, 2022 Location: Paristown Hall, Louisville, Kentucky Commentators: Tom Hannifan, Matthew Rehwoldt So this might be interesting as I was in the arena for the show. Granted I didn’t actually see much of it as the venue is NOT well designed for wrestling and if you’re not on the floor, good luck seeing anything. Instead I was up in the balcony, where I might have been able to see about a third of the ring due to a couch, a barricade and a kid who would not sit down all night long. The main event here is Moose defending the World Title against Heath, just in case you were wondering how bad things had gotten around this point. Let’s get to it. Frost snapmares her down to start and a frustrated Shaw is sent outside. That’s fine with Frost, who plants her on the floor as well but an anklescissors is broken up inside. Shaw’s running elbow gets two and she faceplants Frost to keep her in trouble. A Vader Bomb gets two more on Frost, who certainly has the fans’ support. Frost is right back up to send her into the corner for a handspring Cannonball, only to get caught on top. The hanging DDT plants Frost again but she’s able to block a belly to back superplex. Instead Shaw is elbowed down and a moonsault gives Frost the pin at 6:03. Rating : C. The match was hardly memorable but it wasn’t supposed to be. This was about getting a match in front of the fans and the big spot for the finish made it that much better. Shaw always felt like she was going to be a big deal in TNA but it never quite got there. Frost wasn’t much of a star either, but you could easily see the athleticism and that was enough to catch your attention. Honor No More (Matt Taven/Mike Bennett) have Maria, who joins commentary, with them. The idea is that Honor No More was a group of former ROH wrestlers who had shown up here and tried to take over, with hit and miss success. Bennett headlocks Swann to start but gets dropkicked into the corner for his efforts. Taven comes in to take over on Swann but it’s off to Mack just as fast. Mack gets in a knockdown of his own until the villains send him outside. The brawl heads to the floor, with Mack getting back inside for the big running flip dive. Back in and a DDT gets two on Mack and it’s time to beat him down in the corner. An assisted backbreaker gets two and a jumping enziguri connects for the same. Mack punches his way out of trouble though and it’s back to Swann. An assisted bulldog gets two on Taven with Bennett making the save. Mack Stuns Taven and Swann is back up, only to get caught in the corner. The Backpack Stunner is broken up though and Swann sunset flips Bennett for the pin at 7:44. Rating : C+. This was a pretty standard tag match and it was nice to see Swann and Mack working together well. They could have been a nice team if they were given a chance but that only went so far. llm_long: Tasha Steelz retained the Knockouts Championship in her match at Sacrifice. The event took place on March 5, 2022 at Paristown Hall in Louisville, Kentucky.

In an opening match, Tasha Steelz faced an opponent who started with a snapmare and sent her outside the ring. The opponent followed up by planting her on the floor, but the action returned inside where an ankle scissors was broken.

The opponent landed a running elbow and a faceplant to maintain control before hitting a Vader Bomb for a near fall. Steelz responded with a handspring cannonball in the corner but was caught on the top rope.

A hanging DDT connected for the opponent, who then attempted a belly to back superplex. Steelz blocked the move, elbowed her down, and hit a moonsault to score the pinfall in six minutes and three seconds.

The issue arose from a line in Caster's pre-match rap that referenced the recent deadly airport attacks in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Less than a day after the show, TNA announced it would no longer work with him amid significant backlash over the remark.

The offending line has since been removed from all official recordings of the TNA event. Caster took to social media to issue an apology to those offended, beginning with TNA president Carlos Silva. He stated that he spoke with Silva in person, who remained generous and professional despite the situation, and that he understood the decision to protect the company because he had gone too far.
Caster added that he wanted to apologize to everyone in the TNA office and to anyone who had vouched for him to secure the appearance, saying he felt he let those people down.

title: TNA Partners With LaMelo Ball's LaFrance Brand

Off the court, the California-born guard is equally as flashy. After the historic win, Slater said he was "grateful" for the support he's received along the way to achieving his dream of becoming a World Champion. "I'm a big believer in manifestation and self-confidence and all of that jazz . I always saw myself with something like this," Slater said while holding the TNA World Championship. Slater is now the youngest X-Division Champion and World Champion in TNA history. Slater is expected to appear on the next episode of TNA iMPACT! on Tuesday, Oct. 13, following his historic performance. title: Max Caster done with TNA Wrestling after referencing attacks in Riyadh
raw_title: Max Caster done with TNA Wrestling after referencing attacks in Riyadh
body: Max Caster is done with TNA Wrestling following a line in his rap at Sunday’s Bound for Glory event. Caster made his promotional debut on Sunday and, during his rap on the way to the ring, stated, “I’m gonna drop bombs, you don’t even have to fly to Riyadh”, referencing the attacks in Saudi Arabia, which included twelve people being killed over the weekend. The company issued an apology on Sunday, adding that Caster will no longer be wrestling for TNA: During Sunday’s Bound For Glory pay-per-view, insensitive comments were made by Max Caster referencing attacks in Riyadh that killed and injured many people. Making light of violent attacks is wrong. This should never have made it into the show, and that responsibility is ours. Our thoughts are with the victims, their families, and everyone affected. We sincerely apologize. We have removed the segment from replays and our social channels and are taking steps to ensure something like this never happens again. Caster had just become a free agent after wrestling for AEW since 2020. Moose issued an open challenge last Thursday on Impact, which was answered by Caster the following day on social media. The line drew criticism immediately, and the False Finish outlet reported that TNA would no longer be working with Caster.

The promotion issued a public apology, removed the segment from all replays and social media, and confirmed Caster will no longer work with the company. Caster had recently become a free agent after leaving AEW.

title: Shotzi Blackheart's MLW Contract Expires

body: Blackheart showing up in TNA had many wondering about her status with MLW, leading to an earlier Fightful report which clarified that her most recent MLW contract had been for six months, expiring on October 5. Blackheart was said to still be on good terms with MLW and had "committed" to dates working for the promotion in 2027, though it would seem her contract with TNA would prevent that. Those close to the situation indicated MLW was at least aware of the possibility Blackheart could be moving on, as they are said to have "contingencies" in case it happened. Despite Blackheart losing the Featherweight Championship to Masha Slamovich last month , the change has not yet ad on TV, suggesting Blackheart is still scheduled to appear on upcoming episodes of "MLW Fusion." Blackheart will be able to keep some dates outside of TNA, as she is still currently scheduled to appear on "Chris Jericho's Rock N' Wrestling Rager at Sea" cruise next month, hosted by her old nemesis Chris Jericho . Though this will be her first stint in TNA as a contracted wrestler, Blackheart wrestled twice on "Impact" in 2018, losing a singles match with Allie before teaming with Tessa Blanchard in a losing effort against Allie and Kiera Hogan. She would later also work two TNA spot shows in 2019, including a singles match against Madison Rayne.

title: Indi Hartwell and Shayna Baszler win big on TNA Bound For Glory
raw_title: Indi Hartwell and Shayna Baszler win big on TNA Bound For Glory
body: TNA Wrestling’s “Bound For Glory,” the company’s biggest annual pay-per-view of the year, delivered multiple title wins and historic moments for out LGBTQ performers on Sunday. Indi Hartwell , one year after her unsuccessful challenge for the TNA Knockouts World championship at the same event, defeated Xia Brookside to win the top women’s prize in the company. The win makes Hartwell the first out LGBTQ wrestler to ever hold the TNA Knockouts World championship in the nearly 20-year history of the title. “It’s crazy what can change in a year,” Hartwell said in a video posted to TNA Wrestling’s social media accounts. “This year, I finally turned the toy belt into the real thing.” TNA star Indi Hartwell announces engagement to her soon-to-be wife Indi Hartwell wrote that ‘It’s giving forever’ to caption a photo of herself wearing an engagement ring from her fiancee. Hartwell’s reference to “the toy belt” harkens back to her fandom of TNA’s women’s division growing up in Melbourne, Australia. Photos of an adolescent Hartwell showing off a collection of toy pro wrestling belts, including an old version of the TNA Knockouts World title, were used in the lead-up to Sunday’s event as part of the story of her journey back to title contention. Knowing her TNA fandom previous to entering pro wrestling, it made sense that TNA Hall of Famer and five-time TNA Knockouts World champion Mickie James was the special referee for her title match. “I used to watch her have crazy matches and now she’s out there reffing me,” Hartwell said fighting back tears. “She was there for me to win my first title here in TNA. I’m just so grateful for all the hiccups, the roller coaster, all the times I failed because, I mean, it all led to this.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by TNA Wrestling (@tnawrestling) Joining Hartwell in the championship winner’s circle was the debuting Shayna Baszler . The former NXT Women’s and WWE Women’s Tag Team champion marked her entrance into the company by reuniting with Zoey Serrano and defeating Allie and Kiera Hogan for the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team titles. Naming themselves The Apex, Baszler and Serrano downed the champions in only the third TNA Knockouts World Tag Team title match to feature multiple out LGBTQ participants. Former WWE star returns home and immediately wins gold Indi Hartwell returned to her home country to defeat Aysha and win the Renegades Of Wrestling Women’s title. Both Hartwell and Baszler add their name to the TNA record books alongside Hogan, “Speedball” Mike Bailey and Steph De Lander as the only out LGBTQ pro wrestlers to hold TNA gold. They are joined by former TNA Knockouts World champion Winter, who came out publicly after her time with the company. Outsports congratulates Hartwell and Baszler on their accomplishments and for continuing to show that Courage is Contagious. But his arrival quickly turned to dust following a rap lyric gone bad. Caster’s character is built around a rap that disses his opponents as he walks to the ring. His personality and charisma helped his team, Anthony Bowens, rise to AEW Tag Team Champions as The Acclaimed. But at times, his lyrics toed the line, if not crossed it altogether. Many of his songs went viral, including ones that referenced troubled WWE chairman Vince McMahon . But in 2021, he was reportedly suspended for lyrics about Simone Biles and the Duke lacrosse case. AEW let both Caster and Bowens leave the company as their momentum stalled amid a number of new arrivals. Unfortunately for Caster and TNA, he went too far once again on his first night in the company. Debuting on the pay-per-view event, Caster taunted Moose with the line, “I drop bombs, you don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” It was a reference to missile attacks that have killed at least 14 people in the Saudi Arabian capital. The day after, TNA released a statement saying it had removed the video from all replays and social channels and that Caster would no longer work with the company. On Tuesday, Max Caster issued his own statement. He posted a video on his social media page apologizing for the lyrics and thanking TNA for the opportunity to perform. “I wanna say thank you to Carlos Silva. I talked to him in person. title: Deonna Purrazzo Credits TNA Run For Building Her Confidence
raw_title: Deonna Purrazzo: ‘My Time In TNA Gave Me The Confidence To Know I Could Lead A Division And Do It Without Compromising Who I Am And What I Stood For’
body: Deonna Purrazzo says her time in TNA Wrestling shaped her the most as a performer. While Deonna Purrazzo is currently signed to AEW/ROH, she’s worked for many other wrestling promotions in the past, such as WWE, Lucha Libre AAA, TNA Wrestling, and more. While speaking with The Ledgera magazine , Purrazzo was asked which period of her career shaped the performer that fans see today. Purrazzo said it was her TNA run, and provided the following explanation: “My time in TNA/IMPACT shaped me the most. In April/May 2020, I didn’t even know if I wanted to continue to wrestle so when TNA called, I was hesitant. From the moment I walked in the doors on my first day, I felt like I was home. Besides winning 5 World Championships, main eventing countless PPVs and TV shows, for the first time in my career, I had a team of people who wanted to see me succeed and were willing to work alongside me to see me do so. My time in TNA gave me the confidence to know I could lead a division AND do it without compromising who I am and what I stood for.” Purrazzo worked for TNA from 2014-2017 and then 2020-2023. During her tenure, she would capture the Knockouts World Title three times and have a Knockouts World Tag Team Title reign with Chelsea Green. Elsewhere in the interview, Purrazzo talked about what a potential match with Athena would mean for her. Fans can read her full comments here .

After joining in 2020 at a time when she considered leaving the business, she found a supportive environment that helped her win five world titles, main event multiple shows and lead a division while staying true to herself. The Virginia native previously worked for TNA from 2014-2017 before returning for a second stint that lasted until 2023.

title: Max Caster Apologizes For Controversial TNA Debut Rap
raw_title: "I Understand Why He Did": Max Caster Breaks Silence Addressing Controversial TNA Exit
body: Caster made his TNA debut on October 11, answering Moose's open challenge at Bound for Glory. Although he ultimately lost the match, his pre-match rap overshadowed his performance after he referenced the recent deadly attacks in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia . "I drop bombs. You don't even have to fly to Riyadh," Caster said during his entrance. Speaking in an Instagram video on October 13, Caster addressed TNA president Carlos Silva and others involved in bringing him to the promotion. "I want to say thank you to Carlos Silva. I talked to him in person. He was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened. And I understand why he did what he did. It's his show. He's got to protect TNA, and I went too far for him. So I want to apologize to him and everybody else in the office. I want to apologize to anyone who vouched for me to get that spot. I feel like I let those people down." The former AEW World Tag Team Champion also thanked Moose for sharing the ring with him and expressed regret over how his TNA debut ended. "Thank you to Moose for sharing your platform with me, and I wish things didn't turn out the way they did. But I'm proud of that match, and I'm sorry for how things have ended up." He then explained that his raps are intended to entertain, although he stopped short of apologizing simply because people were offended. "I just want everybody to know that when I do these raps, it's never to offend people. It's only to entertain. So, in my mind, it's entertainment value first, and then, if you're offended by it, that's your right. So I can't apologize for anyone being offended, but just know that it's not my intention to make people upset." "The Best Wrestler Alive" then acknowledged that the reaction had made the segment widely discussed, but accepted the consequences. He also admitted feeling embarrassed that his TNA run ended after just one match, adding that he would accept the situation and move forward. "If it gets a reaction, I think I did my job. It was a very relevant part of the show and highly talked about, so I feel good about that. But the consequences of everything, I'm accepting that. And then, to anybody who is asking if I'm good, I'm good. I'm just embarrassed about how all this happened. You don't want it to be one match and then that's it, you get fired. But again, that's the reality of the situation. I'm accepting it, and that's life. And in life, sometimes you gotta man up and just accept it and move on. So whatever's next, I don't know, but we'll see. Thank you to everybody who's reaching out and supporting." TNA issued a statement on October 12 condemning the remarks and apologizing to those affected by the attacks. The company also confirmed that Caster would no longer wrestle for the promotion and that the segment had been removed from replays and social media. body: Wrestler Max Caster said he holds no ill will against TNA Wrestling after the promotion fired him for using a controversial rap lyric during its Bound for Glory pay-per-view over the weekend. Caster, 37, is known for dissing his opponents via rap as he walks to the ring. His match with Quinn Ojinnaka , better known as Moose, on Saturday, October 10, was no different. This time, however, he appeared to make light of the ongoing missile attacks in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, rapping, “I drop bombs, you don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” TNA dropped him on Monday, October 12. Caster released a statement in response the next day. “I wanna say thank you to [TNA President] Carlos Silva ,” he said in a video shared via X. “I talked to him in person. He was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened. And I understand why he did what he did. It’s his show. He’s got to protect TNA, and I went too far for him. So, I want to apologize to him and everybody else in the office. I want to apologize to anyone who vouched for me to get that spot. I feel like I let those people down.” Caster continued, “For anybody who’s offended, I just want everybody to know that when I do these raps, it’s never to offend people. It’s only to entertain. So, in my mind, it’s entertainment value first. And then if you’re offended by it, that’s your right. So I can’t apologize for anyone being offended, but just know that it’s not my intention to make people upset. If it gets a reaction, I think I did my job.” He added that he has accepted “the consequences of everything.” “To anybody who is asking if I’m good, I’m good,” Caster insisted. “I’m just embarrassed how all this happened. You don’t want it to be one match, and then that’s it, you get fired. But again, that’s the reality of the situation. I’m accepting it, and that’s life. And in life, sometimes you’ve got to man up and just accept it and move on.” TNA also released a statement on Monday when it announced that it had fired Caster. “During Sunday’s Bound For Glory pay-per-view, insensitive comments were made by Max Caster referencing attacks in Riyadh that killed and injured many people,” the statement read. “Making light of violent attacks is wrong. This should never have made it into the show, and that responsibility is ours. Our thoughts are with the victims, their families and everyone affected. We sincerely apologize.” The statement continued, “We have removed the segment from replays and our social channels and are taking steps to ensure something like this never happens again. body: "Impact" aired live from the Boeing Center at Tech Port in San Antonio, Texas, where the show's average viewership remained the same as the previous week at 207,000 viewers , according to " Wrestlenomics ." The number is about the same as the month-long average, which is at 208,000. The key demographic ratings for the show, though, saw a slight fall as it reduced from 0.04 for the previous week's show, to 0.03 for the September 24 show. Since the start of August, viewership for the Thursday night show has stayed between 184,000 and 232,000 viewers, with the highs coming on the September 10 and August 6 episodes. body: TNA Wrestling Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Amazing Red has spoken about his emotions after winning the X-Division Championship at TNA's Bound For Glory. Red had a dream day at Bound for Glory, where he was not only inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame but also won the X-Division Championship . The 44-year-old star was inducted into the Hall of Fame before the show, where he announced that he would be part of the seven-way scramble for the X-Division title. Later that night, he won the championship, and Red then took to social media to speak about the memorable day he had. "This whole day has been a blessing. This whole day, I cannot put into words, I could never put into words, but one word if I can use it right now, it's been amazing," he began. "What a ride, like from the first day I've been here to right now, I feel like everything has just been full circle, and how good does this feel, like you guys don't know how good this feels. For someone like me, the last couple of years, taking loss after loss after loss, and everything is just feeling negative around me, and then the last year, everything just switched." Red spoke about how he has always been closely associated with the X-Division and that winning the title once again was a full-circle moment for him. "To be very humble here, man, when you think of Amazing Red, you think of the X-Division. I think that was what was coded over my style, was the X-Division. That's what I kind of wanted even before X-Division started, and then X-Division was here, I felt right at home," he added. "This [X-Division title] felt so good. So dear to my heart and so winning right now everything is just, again, a full-circle moment." Red's win marked his fourth X-Division Championship, with his last reign coming in 2010 and lasting just two days.

body: Leon Slater was on commentary for the bout ahead of his World title challenge this weekend at Bound for Glory. The Hardys were challenging the Nemeths in a rematch of Lockdown in August , where the TNA World Champion and his brother dethroned the five-time World Tag Team Champions in a Steel Cage match. title: Max Caster Releases Apology After Getting Fired By TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Max Caster Releases Apology After Getting Fired By TNA Wrestling
body: Max Caster’s time as a wrestler for TNA Wrestling barely lasted 24 hours before an insensitive remark made on television got him fired. On Sunday, C aster made his debut during TNA’s Bound For Glory pay-per-view event. He cut a promo at the entrance ramp to make fun of TNA star Moose. Known for rapping about his opponents as he approaches them in the ring, he stunned the crowd by referencing the ongoing Middle East conflict with the line “I drop bombs, you don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” Platinum Max Caster has arrived to the Impact Zone. #TNABoundForGlory pic.twitter.com/DPv6Uxid9K This morning, Caster took to X and offered an apology and thanked TNA for the opportunity to appear on the show. “I wanna say thank you to Carlos Silva. I talked to him in person. He was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened. And I understand why he did what he did. It’s his show. He’s got to protect TNA, and I went too far for him. So, I want to apologize to him and everybody else in the office. I want to apologize to anyone who vouched for me to get that spot. I feel like I let those people down,” Caster said. “For anybody who’s offended, I just want everybody to know that when I do these raps, it’s never to offend people. It’s only to entertain. So, in my mind, it’s entertainment value first. And then if you’re offended by it, that’s your right. So I can’t apologize for anyone being offended, but just know that it’s not my intention to make people upset. If it gets a reaction, I think I did my job.” Caster rose to prominence during his run with All Elite Wrestling from 2020 to 2026. During his time with the company, he would win the AEW World Tag Team Championship with Anthony Bowens and later won the World Trips Championship with Bowens and wrestling legend Billy Gunn . But even during his AEW run, he had a knack for getting into trouble with some of his insensitive raps. He made fun of topics such as Simone Biles ’ mental health issues, COVID-19 testing and even the infamous Duke lacrosse case. Some fans (including his bosses) found it highly offensive, while others found it hilarious and have encouraged him. Whether or not Caster “crossed the line” is subjective, but he might find it hard to get work in one of the larger wrestling promotions for a while. "So this is my first year in it, and I've basically won everything else in MLW. I think I'm going to take this Opera Cup home." The MLW Opera Cup is a signature tournament in MLW every year. The winner of the tournament wins the Opera Cup, which is an old prize utilized by Stu Hart in his Stampede Wrestling promotion. It's the oldest recognized trophy in pro wrestling today and as Riddle said, is one of the only things he hasn't won in MLW. Riddle kicks off his tournament on Thursday's edition of MLW Fusion. His opening round match is against Mark Coffey. Prior to the match, Riddle talked exclusively with The TakeDown on SI about the tournament, MLW, life on the indies, WWE, and so much more. "My match against Mark Coffey is this Thursday on MLW Fusion on Tubi , so go check that out if you haven't yet," Riddle said. "It should be good. It's nice to be somewhere where you saw where it started and you see where it's going. I think the sky's the limit (for MLW). The roster is getting more experienced, more grizzled ... and things are clicking." Prior to joining WWE in 2018 as part of the NXT brand, Riddle made his name in MLW. He's a former MLW World Champion and his time in that company helped him achieve the notoriety needed to eventually make it to WWE. From 2018 to 2023, Riddle was a fixture of NXT programming. He debuted for NXT at the TakeOver Brooklyn event in 2018 and then worked with all of the top guys on the roster, including Adam Cole, Keith Lee, and a host of other talents. Riddle was released from his WWE contract in 2023, but immediately went back to his roots. MLW and the indies. Business is good. "I stay busy, I get to meet a lot of fans, and I enjoy myself all the time," Riddle said. "With the holidays coming up, I've been working double time because there aren't as many bookings during Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year's. So, I'm just trying to get in as much work as possible. "I know I get a lot of flak online. The first year I got released, I did a kid's birthday party in California, and people were giving me crap. I'm like, 'hey, they paid me.' They were stoked to have me perform. That's it. I was happy. I flew in same day, flew out, and I think the night before, I won the cruiserweight title in AAA. So I enjoy myself." Riddle is doing strong business on the independents right now, but the stories from the road add to his enjoyment of the craft. Riddle recently wrestled in a torrential rainstorm for an indie. He wouldn't necessarily want to do it again, but he made the most of it. It's the perfect story to showcase the mindset of independent pro wrestlers in 2026. Hurricane rains? No problem. "I knew it was raining and I knew it was going to be bad," Riddle said. body: Shotzi Blackheart’s run with Major League Wrestling has come to an end, and Sean Ross Sapp has learned that her deal expired October 5. title: Tessa Blanchard Reportedly Joining MLW With CMLL's Approval
raw_title: Tessa Blanchard Reportedly Joining MLW With CMLL's Approval
body: On Thursday morning, The Wrestling Observer's Dave Meltzer posted "Tessa Blanchard headed to MLW. All worked out with CMLL" to X (formerly known as Twitter). The day before, CMLL announced that Blanchard will make her MLW debut on November 7 at Saturday Night Super Fight. Blanchard originally announced she was signed to MLW on September 1 . A few days later, CMLL said that Blanchard wasn't signed to MLW, just that she was scheduled for a match. She was removed from the September 12 MLW show . On Wednesday, CMLL announced the participants for the Grand Prix de Amazonas. Blanchard will represent CMLL alongside La Jarochita and Thunder Rosa. MLW will be represented by Blackheart and Slamovich. Alice Crowley will represent MLP while Megan Bayne, Queen Aminata, and Harley Cameron will represent AEW. The show is on October 23.

title: Former AEW Star Lady Frost Finishes up With MLW — Report
raw_title: Former AEW Star Lady Frost Finishes up With MLW — Report
body: Frost joined MLW earlier this year following the expiration of her AEW contract and becoming a free agent. She quickly reached an agreement with the promotion after MLW expressed interest in signing her. The "Ice Cold Killer" made her MLW debut at Blood & Thunder in April, where she competed in a Triple-Threat match against Scarlett Bordeaux and Shotzi. She went on to become a regular presence in the promotion's women's division. Frost's final MLW match took place at the Fightland taping on September 12. She faced Masha Slamovich in what was Slamovich's MLW debut, with Frost ultimately suffering a defeat. According to Fightful Select , Lady Frost has "finished up" with MLW. The report did not provide additional details about the circumstances surrounding her departure. Frost signed with MLW in April shortly after her AEW contract expired. Fightful previously reported that MLW immediately pursued her after she entered free agency. Her AEW contract expired on April 1, 2026. Frost had been with AEW since 2023 and last wrestled for the company on the January 10 episode of AEW Collision, where she lost to Mina Shirakawa. Frost's run with MLW included appearances at several events throughout the year. She also worked matches outside the promotion, including dates with CMLL. title: MLW star Donovan Dijak hopes to tag with former partner who left for WWE after lengthy title reign
raw_title: MLW star Donovan Dijak hopes to tag with former partner who left for WWE after lengthy title reign
body: You are using an outdated browser. Please upgrade your browser to improve your experience. Oct 8, 2026 | 8:16 AM Donovan Dijak and Bishop Dyer had a lengthy reign as Major League Wrestling (MLW) tag team champions, sharing it with Josh Bishop as well under the Freebird Rule which allowed any members of the trio to hold and defend the belts. The group, collectively known as The Skyscrapers , had the titles for 317 days. As Dyer left MLW for WWE, Dijak and Bishop held the titles until losing the belts on a summer episode of “Fusion” to The Good Brothers. With Dyer now in WWE and a former WWE United States champion almost immediately upon his return there, Dijak looked back on his reign with the competitor fondly. He told OutKick Dropkick he wants to team up with Dyer again somewhere down the line. “I love everything that I was able to do with Bishop Dyer, now Baron Corbin , and tag teaming with him was unbelievable levels of fun,” he said. “We got to do it in Mexico. We got to do it in Australia. We got to do it all over the United States, which was great for me, especially from a guy like him at his level. He didn’t take like a ton of indie dates. He was doing sort of limited appearances, but I was a part of a ton of that. So, to be able to have that experience with him, and I worked with him in WWE before, I just can’t wait to tag with him again. “I don’t know when and where it’s going to happen. I hope that it does happen because that’s like kind of how pro wrestling works. You never know when your last time tagging with someone or your last time wrestling someone is going to be. Every time you work with someone, your brain always goes, oh man, I can’t wait to do that again, and where are we going to do it and stuff like that. And then sometimes it’s just like, oh, they’re retired, I guess it’s never happening again or, in some like horrible cases, sometimes, the person you’re working with unfortunately passes away or something, which, sadly, happened to me way too many times in the world of professional wrestling, and that hits on an entirely different level in terms of I’m never going to be able to see that person again. But sometimes you leave a locker room and you’re like, I’ll see these guys all, and then you never see them for another year or two.” Dijak and Dyer had multiple title defenses during their reign. They defeated Averno and Euforia at CMLL Viernes Espectacular and they beat The Good Brothers earlier this year after winning the belts at last year’s Summer of the Beasts against Magnus and Rugido. “There’s so many of those experiences. I just hope that he and I get to tag together again because we had an incredible run in MLW,” he told OutKick Dropkick. “We were the MLW tag team champions, and he’s just a good friend. We still talk all the time. I hope it happens again.” Now, Dijak and is partnered with Bishop as The Skyscrapers continue to forge their own path in MLW. title: MLW star Donovan Dijak Discusses tag team wrestling being a 'lost art,' partnering with Josh Bishop and growth
raw_title: MLW star Donovan Dijak talks tag team wrestling being a 'lost art,' partnering with Josh Bishop and growth
body: 0 Donovan Dijak reveals why The Skyscrapers are banking on Killer Kross and Matt Riddle failing to coexist in their massive MLW tag team clash. It has been more than two years since Donovan Dijak joined Major League Wrestling (MLW) and just as he was in WWE NXT, he continued to be a force to be reckoned with. The average pro wrestling might feast their eyes on the 6-foot-7, 270-pound Massachusetts native and believe he should be a singles competitor in the ring. However, Dijak has torn it up in MLW as part of The Skyscrapers tag team with Bishop Dyer and now Josh Bishop. Dijak and Bishop are set to have a massive tag team match against MLW world heavyweight champion Killer Kross and Matt Riddle. Kross and Riddle have had their differences in the past. Kross won the title in a Battle Riot earlier this year. Riddle had done the same in 2025. A win for Dijak and Bishop might catapult each of them into a shot at the world title down the line. "I'm banking on them not being able to coexist," Dijak told OutKick Dropkick. "Hopefully me and Josh can coexist. I know there's some volatility there. But he (Bishop) has all the potential in the world. He's just an incredible dude. Big, strong, exactly what you want in a tag team partner, especially in a tag team called The Skyscrapers. I'm very excited for his future. "I'm very excited to help mold his future and give him the path and the avenue and the direction and the instruction that is necessary for success at the level against guys like Killer Kross, against guys like Matt Riddle, who I've been wrestling for years and years and years, both of them. So, I'm super excited to get back in the ring with those guys and to be in the ring with Josh as well because he's just an unbelievable competitor." Dijak said he was a big fan of tag team wrestling as well as singles wrestling. He teamed with Mace in WWE and wrestler Mikey Webb. He also credited Tommaso Ciampa with helping him learn the psychology of a tag team match. Dijak held the MLW tag team titles with both Dyer and Bishop for nearly a year before dropping it to The Good Brothers – Karl Anderson and Doc Gallows . Pro wrestling fans have expressed some dismay about tag team wrestling over the years. OutKick Dropkick asked Dijak whether the style was a "lost art" in the sport. "Absolutely. There's so many points and purposes around tag team wrestling that I think kind of get lost in today's sort of system of professional wrestling. And I understand why, right? Because my perspective — and I teach a lot of this," Dijak said, pointing to his work at the New England Pro Wrestling Academy in Massachusetts and the course he offers online at Dijakwrestling.com. "A big piece of tag team psychology that kind of gets lost is how different and unique of a platform it is as opposed to a singles match or singles wrestling. title: AJ Styles Reveals Reason He Rejected Bullet Club Leadership
raw_title: WWE's AJ Styles Explains Why He Didn't Want To Be The 'Leader' Of Bullet Club In NJPW
body: "Our whole thing was, at least the way I presented it to the world, was we don't follow anybody, and so therefore that means you don't follow me. I'm not your leader, I'm just part of this group because we don't follow anybody, and that was a way for me to make sure that everybody stays important. It wasn't just one guy, like we as a group were a big deal, I didn't want it to be about AJ Styles, I didn't want it to be about [Doc] Gallows and [Karl] Anderson, I wanted it to be about all of us together, and I thought that's what made it special." Styles rounded off by saying that you could tell that everyone in Bullet Club was enjoying themselves and having a good time, which in turn made the group more popular in Japan because when people see their attitudes and think it's cool and want to either be a part of it, or support it. Bullet Club was quietly disbanded at the beginning of 2026, with the remaining members either leaving NJPW, or joining the new Unbound Co. stable led by Yota Tsuji. Please credit "What Do You Wanna Talk About?" when using quotes from this article, and give a H/T to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.
summary: AJ Styles explained that he positioned Bullet Club as a group where no one followed a single leader so every member would remain equally important. He emphasized that the faction's appeal came from everyone working together rather than focusing on individual stars like himself, Karl Anderson or Doc Gallows. Styles added that the group's visible enjoyment of their time together helped boost their popularity with Japanese audiences before the stable's quiet disbandment in early 2026.

He emphasized that the faction's appeal came from everyone working together rather than focusing on individual stars like himself, Karl Anderson or Doc Gallows. llm.quote: We don't follow anybody, and so therefore that means you don't follow me. I'm not your leader, I'm just part of this group because we don't follow anybody.

llm_long: AJ Styles explained his decision to turn down the leadership role in Bullet Club. He presented the group as one that does not follow any single person, including himself, to ensure that every member remained equally important.
Styles emphasized that the faction was not built around one individual. He wanted the focus to stay on the collective rather than on himself or specific members like Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson.

According to Styles, this approach helped make the group special by keeping all participants on the same level. The shared dynamic reinforced the idea that Bullet Club operated as a unified entity without a central leader.

Styles noted that the enjoyment and positive attitudes among the members were evident. This energy contributed to the group's popularity in Japan, as audiences responded favorably to their fun and cool demeanor.
Bullet Club was quietly disbanded at the beginning of 2026. The remaining members either departed NJPW or joined the new Unbound Co. stable led by Yota Tsuji.

title: Taichi Challenges Gabe Kidd For IWGP Global Title
raw_title: Taichi Challenging Gabe Kidd For IWGP Global Heavyweight Title At NJPW Power Struggle
body: The IWGP Global Heavyweight Championship was up for grabs at New Japan Pro-Wrestling’s King of Pro-Wrestling show on October 12th . Gabe Kidd put the belt on the line against Shota Umino. Kidd is in the midst of his second reign with the belt, and the match against Umino was his second defense. During the backend of the bout, Kidd hit a clothesline on Umino. He got a two-count and then transitioned into the Brutalizer submission, which was used by the late Benjamin Satterley, a.k.a. PAC , who was part of the Death Riders in AEW alongside Kidd. Kidd would later go on to defeat Umino to retain the title. Post-match, he asked who was going to step up to him next, and out came Taichi. Taichi staked his claim to a title match, and Kidd set the date for Power Struggle on November 3rd.
summary: Gabe Kidd retained the IWGP Global Heavyweight Championship against Shota Umino in the second defense of his current reign at NJPW King of Pro-Wrestling on October 12. Kidd finished the match with his Brutalizer submission hold after a clothesline sequence. Following the victory, Taichi confronted him and earned a title shot scheduled for NJPW Power Struggle on November 3.

Following the match, Kidd called for the next challenger. Taichi then entered the ring and declared his intention to face him for the title.
Kidd accepted the challenge and scheduled the title match for the Power Struggle event on November 3.

title: Yota Tsuji Retains IWGP Title, Omega Issues Challenge
raw_title: Yota Tsuji Retains at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling, Receives Challenge from Kenny Omega
body: Yota Tsuji Retains at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling, Receives Challenge from Kenny Omega 4 days ago Photo Credit: New Japan Pro Wrestling Photo Credit: New Japan Pro Wrestling A large crowd was drawn to NJPW King of Pro Wrestling for the hotly anticipated match between the reigning IWGP Heavyweight Champion, Yota Tsuji, and the G1 Climax winner, Ryohei Oiwa. Tsuji managed to overcome his tenacious challenger, only to be met with another huge obstacle in the form of Kenny Omega. The NJPW King of Pro Wrestling main event was a bout befitting the occasion. For over 35 minutes, Tsuji and Oiwa battled for the right to be called IWGP Heavyweight Champion. After managing to withstand Oiwa’s headlocks, Tsuji finished the bout with a Fire Blaster, finally able to keep the G1 winner down for the three-count. Receiving loud reactions in the arena and impassioned praise online, Tsuji could not bask in the confetti for too long. A video played on the arena’s big screen, with Tsuji being addressed by a former world champion, Kenny Omega. What's happening? @kennyomegamanx has issued a challenge to Yota Tsuji?? #njkopw pic.twitter.com/udjEHlWRah Taking offence to Tsuji passing up this year’s Forbidden Door event, and looking to test the current strength of NJPW against that of the 2010s peak, Omega has challenged Tsuji to a match. Tsuji was then met in the ring by Oleg Boltin, one of the men that had defeated Tsuji during the G1 Climax. While the Kazakh was making his title intentions clear, Omega appeared out of nowhere and attacked the champion, making sure that his message was delivered as effectively as possible. 視聴＆登録⏩「NJPW WORLD」で検索📱 #njpwworld #njkopw pic.twitter.com/NoDUgiTzmL Speaking backstage, Omega has called his shot, demanding a three-way between himself, Tsuji and Boltin at Power Struggle on November 3rd. Omega noted that should he get the winning fall, he will challenge for the IWGP Heavyweight Title at Wrestle Kingdom.
summary: Yota Tsuji defeated Ryohei Oiwa in a 35-minute main event to retain the IWGP Heavyweight Championship at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling. Immediately after the victory, Kenny Omega appeared via video package to challenge Tsuji, citing the champion's absence from this year's Forbidden Door and seeking to compare current NJPW strength against its peak in the 2010s.

title: Kenny Omega Attacks Yota Tsuji At NJPW King Of Pro-Wrestling
raw_title: Kenny Omega Appears At NJPW King Of Pro-Wrestling, Lays Out Yota Tsuji
body: Kenny Omega makes a surprise appearance at NJPW King of Pro-Wrestling. Yota Tsuji retained the IWGP Heavyweight Title at NJPW King of Pro-Wrestling, defeating Ryohei Oiwa in the main event. Tsuji addressed the crowd following the victory when the lights went down and Kenny Omega appeared via video. Omega addressed Tsuji not appearing at Forbidden Door, noting that the I in IWGP stands for International, but Tsuji was unwilling to travel. Omega said that if Tsuji wouldn’t come to him, he’d be willing to fight him on his terms. Tsuji said that if Omega wants to face him, he has to come to Japan. Boltin Oleg came out to confront Tsuji, but Omega attacked him from behind. He then laid out Tsuji with a V-Trigger and One Winged Angel. Omega said he would talk to NJPW President Hirsohi Tanahashi about a match with Tsuji. What's happening? @kennyomegamanx has issued a challenge to Yota Tsuji?? #njkopw pic.twitter.com/udjEHlWRah

title: Omega, Moxley Matches Set For NJPW Power Struggle
raw_title: Kenny Omega & Jon Moxley Matches Announced For NJPW Power Struggle
body: Etsuo Hara/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Following an action packed NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026 even t on October 12, an event that saw Kenny Omega return to New Japan Pro Wrestling and Jon Moxley announce his intentions of returning in the near future, the first set of matches of NJPW Power Struggle on November 3 have been announced, and both Omega and Moxley will be in action. Omega closed out King of Pro Wrestling by attacking IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji, and the man who declared his intention of being the next champion, Boltin Oleg. Omega wanted to teach Tsuji a lesson for not being an international fighting champion, but wanted to earn his title shot in the right way. This has led to a three-way match being signed for Power Struggle in Hiroshima between Omega, Tsuji, and Oleg, where if Omega scores the winning fall, he will become the number one contender to Tsuji's title and challenge him at NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 at the Tokyo Dome on January 4. While all that happened at the end of the show, the start of the show saw Moxley announce that he would be answering Shingo Takagi's open challenge for a match, but stated that he wouldn't be coming alone after Takagi beat Moxley's fellow Death Rider, Claudio Castagnoli, in September . Joining Moxley for a special tag team match will Wheeler Yuta, with the Death Riders taking on the Unbound Co. duo of Takagi and Jeff Cobb. Omega and Moxley aren't the only AEW stars traveling to Hiroshima, and in Moxley's case, he will have more than just Wheeler Yuta by his side representing the Death Riders. On the same card, Gabe Kidd will make another defense of the IWGP Global Heavyweight Championship as he goes one-on-one with Taichi, with Taichi making it clear that if he wins, Kidd will never be allowed back in NJPW ever again. Rounding out the AEW involvement in Power Struggle will be an IWGP Tag Team Championship match between the champions Yuto-Ice and OSKAR, better known as The Knockout Brothers, taking on Callum Newman and the current AEW World Champion Will Ospreay. Newman and Ospreay almost came to blows at the end of King of Pro Wrestling, but will have to get on the same page if they want to bring gold back to the United Empire. Yota Tsuji vs Boltin Oleg vs Kenny Omega- non title but high stakes! Callum Newman & Will Ospreay vs KOB for the IWGP Tag titles?! Jon Moxley returns! https://t.co/YG7PpIIW14 #njpst #njpw pic.twitter.com/1oxdvZWTZ3
summary: Following the NJPW King of Pro Wrestling event, Kenny Omega attacked IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji and Boltin Oleg. This has resulted in a three-way match at Power Struggle on November 3 in Hiroshima where a victory for Omega earns him a title shot against Tsuji at Wrestle Kingdom 21. Jon Moxley also answered Shingo Takagi's open challenge for the same show after Takagi defeated Claudio Castagnoli.

Omega attacked IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji after the main event and also targeted Boltin Oleg. This has resulted in a three-way match between Omega, Tsuji and Oleg, with the winner of the fall earning a title shot at Wrestle Kingdom 21 on January 4.
Moxley responded to an open challenge from Shingo Takagi at the start of the King of Pro Wrestling show. He will team with Wheeler Yuta to face Takagi and Jeff Cobb in a tag team match.

title: Kenny Omega and Jon Moxley Set for NJPW Returns
raw_title: AEW's Kenny Omega & Jon Moxley Set For NJPW In-Ring Returns
body: Etsuo Hara/Getty Images Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover New Japan Pro Wrestling held its annual King of Pro Wrestling event on October 12 at Ryogoku Sumo Hall in Tokyo, and the in-ring returns of both Kenny Omega and Jon Moxley are on the horizon in NJPW. In the night's opening contest, Shingo Takagi and Daiki Nagai defeated Hirooki Goto and Tatsuya Matsumoto, with Takagi picking up the win by hitting his own version of a Death Rider on Matsumoto. After the match, a video message from Moxley was played on the big screen in the arena, declaring that he would be returning to NJPW after Takagi had issued another open challenge to anyone in AEW. Takagi recently defeated Moxley's fellow Death Rider, Claudio Castagnoli, at NJPW Destruction in Kobe 2026 , and Moxley will likely not be coming alone when he makes his first appearance in NJPW in nearly three years in the coming months. 視聴＆登録⏩「NJPW WORLD」で検索📱 #njpwworld #njkopw pic.twitter.com/kZ8lM0Iwgj Later in the show, Yota Tsuji defended the IWGP Heavyweight Championship against the winner of the G1 Climax, Ryohei Oiwa. After that match, another video was played on the big screen, this time from Omega who ran down Tsuji for not technically being a "world" champion since he didn't want to appear at AEW x NJPW Forbidden Door earlier this year before calling him out for a match. Before Tsuji had time to think about the challenge, he was confronted by Boltin Oleg, but just as those two men faced off, Omega rushed the ring and laid out both Tsuji and Oleg. 視聴＆登録⏩「NJPW WORLD」で検索📱 #njpwworld #njkopw pic.twitter.com/NoDUgiTzmL Omega then offered a different challenge, a three-way match between himself, Tsuji, and Oleg before the end of the year. The main stipulation of the match being that if Omega wins the match, he will then be the number one contender to the IWGP Heavyweight Championship, with that match most likely taking place at NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 at the Tokyo Dome on January 4.

title: On the Record: MJF Challenges NJPW Star, Says He'll Put 'Actual' AEW World Title On The Line
raw_title: MJF Challenges NJPW Star, Says He'll Put 'Actual' AEW World Title On The Line
body: On the opening night of the Road to King of Pro Wrestling tour in Korakuen Hall, a video message sent by Maxwell Jacob Friedman played on the big screen, where he called out the winner of this year's G1 Climax tournament, Ryohei Oiwa. In his message, MJF called NJPW second rate and made fun of the company for losing all of its top stars in recent years. However, he did note that Oiwa is one of the best that NJPW currently has to offer, and by beating him, he will be one step closer to locking the Forbidden Door forever and proving why he's been right all along about NJPW as a company. MJF even sweetened the deal for Oiwa by stating that he would put his beloved "Triple B" on the line, claiming that he is still the real AEW World Champion and the belt that Will Ospreay currently holds is a phony title. The "Salt of the Earth" rounded off by throwing down the gauntlet and asking Oiwa who the real master of the Headlock is, because in MJF's mind, it's him, and he will prove that by beating "The Grip" with a Headlock Takeover. This rivalry between MJF and Oiwa actually started on social media following Oiwa's victory in the G1 Climax final back in August. Oiwa's win over Yuya Uemura was critically acclaimed by everyone apart from the "current" AEW World Champion, who baited "The Grip" into an exchange on X (formerly known as Twitter) that led to both men claiming that they will fight each other in whichever company allows them to. MJF won't be at the forefront of Oiwa's mind, at least in the immediate future, as he will be challenging Yota Tsuji for the IWGP Heavyweight Championship on October 17 at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026.

The challenge stems from a social media exchange that began after Oiwa's G1 Climax victory in August.

title: On the Record: Dave Meltzer Says This AEW Star Was Responsible For Relationship With NJPW
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Says This AEW Star Was Responsible For Relationship With NJPW
body: Netflix Add Wrestling Inc. on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover AEW and New Japan Pro Wrestling have had a strong working relationship for over five years at the time of writing, to the point where the AEW x NJPW Forbidden Door pay-per-view has become a staple of the wrestling calendar and has been held in the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom. However, things didn't start out that way. Initially, there was no relationship between the two companies as NJPW management wasn't happy with The Elite leaving in 2019, as well as former NJPW President Harold Meij not seeing any upside in working with AEW since the company was already partnered with CMLL and ROH. However, according to Dave Meltzer on " Wrestling Observer Radio ," one man was pivotal to the AEW and NJPW relationship becoming a reality, and that man was Jon Moxley. "Jon's the one responsible for the New Japan and AEW relationship back during the pandemic," Meltzer said. "Jon had the [IWGP] US title and he was an AEW guy...there was no relationship at all. it opened up the relationship. That's when KENTA came to AEW and it opened the door. They basically built a relationship after that point." Moxley actually won the IWGP United States Championship in his debut match for NJPW , a match that took place less than two weeks after his AEW debut. However, while he was initially stripped of the title due to travel complications that forced him out of a title defense in October 2019, he wasn't stripped of the title when he won it back in January 2020 and couldn't make it back over to Japan throughout that year due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Chris Jericho also competed in NJPW as the AEW World Champion no less, though that would be Jericho's final official match for NJPW and hasn't returned to the company since. Please credit "Wrestling Observer Radio" when using quotes from this article, and give a H/T to Wrestling Inc. for the transcription.

The relationship did not exist at first. New Japan Pro Wrestling management was unhappy with The Elite's departure in 2019, and the company's former president saw no benefit in partnering with AEW because of existing ties with CMLL and ROH.

According to Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio, Jon Moxley played a key role in establishing the connection between the two promotions. Moxley held the IWGP United States Championship while signed to AEW at a time when no formal relationship existed between the companies.

Meltzer stated that Moxley's possession of the title during the pandemic period opened the door for cooperation. This led to KENTA appearing in AEW and the two promotions building an ongoing relationship afterward.

Moxley captured the IWGP United States Championship in his first match with New Japan Pro Wrestling, which occurred shortly after his AEW debut. He was stripped of the title once due to travel issues preventing a defense but regained it in January 2020 and retained it despite being unable to travel to Japan during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Chris Jericho also appeared in New Japan Pro Wrestling while holding the AEW World Championship. That appearance marked his last official match for the Japanese promotion.

title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar looks unrecognizable at Minnesota Hall of Fame event
raw_title: WWE legend Brock Lesnar looks unrecognizable at Minnesota Hall of Fame event
body: On Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026, WWE legend Brock Lesnar was inducted into the University of Minnesota's M Club Hall of Fame following his professional wrestling retirement at SummerSlam . The "Beast Incarnate" was one of 10 inductees into the Hall of Fame. He wore glasses and a suit to the induction event, a far cry from his MMA gloves and shorts from his WWE days. Fellow former WWE Superstar and Lesnar's college roommate, Shelton Benjamin, was at the festivities to celebrate his friend. He posed for a picture with the "Beast" and his family. Born in South Dakota, Lesnar attended Bismarck State College before transferring to the University of Minnesota on a wrestling scholarship. He was a decorated wrestler, winning the 2000 NCAA Division I heavyweight championship a year after finishing as the runner-up. Lesnar went 106-5 in his collegiate career. After his collegiate amateur wrestling days, Lesnar transitioned to professional wrestling. He joined WWE's former developmental program, Ohio Valley Wrestling (OVW), in 2000. In March 2002, he made his main roster debut. Almost immediately, the "Beast Incarnate" was treated as the "Next Big Thing" and won a world championship five months into his main roster career. He beat The Rock at SummerSlam 2002 to win his first of 10 world championships. He left WWE in 2004, wrestling in other promotions like New Japan Pro-Wrestling (NJPW) before trying his hand at professional football and MMA. Lesnar became a decorated UFC fighter before rejoining WWE in 2012. His return marked a shift in his persona. Lesnar began infusing more MMA moves in his arsenal and wearing MMA gloves to the ring. Lesnar retired from WWE at SummerSlam 2026 after losing to Oba Femi in a "Hell in a Cell" match. Their feud had been going on for months, and the "Ruler" finally slayed the "Beast Incarnate" for the final time at SummerSlam.
