title: End of an Era: 5 Ways Adam Copeland Can Retire From AEW
raw_title: 5 Ways Adam Copeland Can Retire From AEW
summary_src: Adam Copeland shocked the AEW universe by revealing that 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling.
body: This Wednesday, AEW held a three-hour Dynamite+Collision special , the go-home show for tomorrow night's WrestleDream 2026 pay-per-view. Adam Copeland competed on the show, facing Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage Qualifying Match. After his victory, Cope made two shocking revelations: his tag partner, Christian Cage, was severely hurt in their 3-way ladder match at All Out, and 2027 will be his last year in wrestling. Adam Copeland revealed that his decision stemmed from Cage's injury and the fact that he's getting older. He also noted that he now has to go all in for the AEW World Championship. With that in mind, here are five ways the Jacksonville-based promotion can book Cope's retirement match. By winning his Clockwork Carnage qualifier, Adam Copeland has joined seven other challengers for Will Ospreay's AEW World Title. The eight participants are Ospreay, Cope, Darby Allin, Konosuke Takeshita, Samoa Joe, Ricochet, Kazuchika Okada, and Mike Bailey, who will battle for the championship at WrestleDream this Saturday. It seems unlikely the Aerial Assassin will lose his title at this event Adam Copeland's desire to win the AEW World Title before retiring almost certainly means the promotion will put the belt on him. We just don't know when. The pro-wrestling world is structured to create tomorrow's stars, and right now the company's next big star, likely to become its flag bearer, is none other than Kyle Fletcher . In early 2027, Tony Khan could put the World Title on Adam Copeland, who would then serve as a fighting champion. During this time, the Rated-R Superstar would face many challengers and defeat them all except his final opponent, Kyle Fletcher. Many would argue that the Protostar is a mirror image of a young Cope (fka Edge), which makes narrative sense. This could be a true passing-of-the-torch moment if booked right. Adam Copeland's retirement run will be one to watch, and he will most likely compete against everyone on the roster he wants to lock up with. That said, choosing the right superstar as the Rated-R Superstar's final opponent becomes increasingly important. Interestingly, AEW could go the John Cena route and let the locker room fight for the chance. A month before Cope's final match at Worlds End 2027 or Dynamite: New Year's Smash, Tony Khan and Cope could announce a Rated-R Invitational tournament. The tournament would feature superstars such as Kenny Omega , MJF, Darby Allin, Will Ospreay, Swerve Strickland, Hangman Page, Kyle Fletcher, and Konosuke Takeshita. Cope could tell a compelling story with each of these stars, making the match one to watch, even beyond the Canadian legend's final. The legendary tag team of Adam Copeland and Christian Cage finally reunited earlier this year and even went on an impressive 125-day run with the titles before losing them to the Young Bucks at All Out 2026 in a chaotic 3-way ladder match. Unfortunately, Cage suffered multiple injuries in the bout and has been out of action since.
summary: This Wednesday, AEW held a three-hour Dynamite+Collision special , the go-home show for tomorrow night's WrestleDream 2026 pay-per-view. His decision stemmed from Cage's injury setback and how he's getting older, Adam Copeland disclosed.

title: On the Record: John Cena Opens Up On Why Staying in WWE Longer Would Have Been Unfair to His Wife
raw_title: John Cena Reveals Why Staying in WWE Longer Would Have Been Unfair to His Wife
summary_src: John Cena may miss wrestling every single day, but he has a pretty personal reason for refusing to push his body beyond its expiration date. During his appearance on TODAY’s Making Space with Hoda Kotb, Cena opened up about knowing when it was time to end his in-ring career.
body: During his appearance on TODAY’s Making Space with Hoda Kotb , Cena opened up about knowing when it was time to end his in-ring career. Hoda Kotb asked how he could be so certain when plenty of people were still telling him he had more left in the tank. Cena explained that the answer came down to the amount of preparation and recovery required to continue performing at WWE’s level. At 49, Cena said he knew he could technically keep wrestling, but doing so would demand more and more of him physically and personally. “Simply because of the preparation and recovery it takes to participate at that level and speed. And I’m not near as fast as, like, younger, more athletically refined, elite-level performers. It wasn’t like I, I’m, I’m at peace with what I had to do and have a lot of gratitude for being able to do it for 23 years. That’s amazing. The normal lifespan is way less than that.” Cena said the numbers ultimately made the decision for him. He had already enjoyed a wrestling career far longer than most, and continuing would have meant putting even more of his life into staying physically capable of performing. “So I’ve already kind of beat the system by not only making it, but by having a nice long tenure. The data was the closure for me. Like, I’m just, I just can’t keep up, and I can’t, I could continue to do this. It’s already very consuming. It will be exponentially more consuming.” That led Cena into the bigger reason why walking away made sense. WWE was once the center of his entire life, but that changed as he got older and his relationship with wife Shay Shariatzadeh became his priority. “So when I was 20, WWE was it. When I was 30, WWE was also it. Started to fragment as I turned 40. I have love and partnership in my life, and that’s like, that’s the bull’s-eye. So, hey, is taking all this time and putting it away from the bull’s-eye really walking the talk about saying I want to try to be a good husband and a good partner? Not really.” Cena then explained that the issue went beyond simply spending too much time away from home. He also had to think about what another serious wrestling injury could mean for his wife later in their lives. “And physically, am I being fair to my partner by, hey, I’m gonna put my health at risk so people, when I’m 52, can cheer as they might bring me out on a stretcher, but then I put an unnecessary burden on you if I make it to 80? You know what I’m saying? So I guess my priorities shifted.” Even after laying out all of those reasons, Cena made it clear that retirement did not happen because his love for wrestling disappeared. “Yeah, clear. But I still, I love it and I miss it every day.” Cena spent more than two decades putting WWE ahead of nearly everything else, but his explanation makes it clear that retirement became less about whether he could squeeze out another match and more about what that match might cost him years later. title: "I didn't want to go back"
raw_title: "I didn't want to go back" - Female star rejected WWE's offer
summary_src: WWE has given stars opportunities on multiple occasions, and a female star recently revealed that the company offered her a contract for a second run, but she rejected it.
body: From 2010 to 2014, Kaitlyn , aka Celeste Bonin, was a notable name in WWE's Divas division. She had a lengthy feud with AJ Lee and captured the Divas Championship before she left the industry to focus on other aspects of her life, personally and professionally. Later, she returned to the industry for a very short stint. On INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet , the former WWE Divas Champion explained how she returned to the company for Mae Young Classic. Kaitlyn revealed that WWE offered her a contract after her second-round match with Mia Yim in the tournament. However, the 40-year-old star had conversations about changing her name for a potential second run, which didn't happen. Furthermore, Kaitlyn's heart wasn't in it, as she didn't resonate with the name, which is why she rejected the offer. She also gave a few more reasons behind her decision. In 2019, Kaitlyn had her last match. She recently addressed the possibility of a return, saying she might never wrestle again . The former Divas Champion is still friends with AJ Lee and Big E , but has made up her mind when it comes to in-ring competition. title: WWE Eyes Reigns vs Femi For WrestleMania 43 Main Event
raw_title: Backstage Report On WWE's Early Plans For WrestleMania 43 Card
summary_src: WrestleMania 43 will be held in Saudi Arabia next year, and WWE appears to have begun planning the show, including a potential main event.
body: Next year's WrestleMania will be held in Saudi Arabia, and according to " Fightful Select ," WWE has earmarked a clash between WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns and 2026 King of the Ring winner Oba Femi for the show. The report added that some sources they spoke to believe that the match could main event the show. As expected, former world champions Cody Rhodes and CM Punk will play important roles at the show, according to the report. A source also suggested that the two could face off again in a rematch of their SummerSlam match . Rhea Ripley — currently out with an injury — is also expected to play a part in it. Reports from earlier in the year had claimed that the Saudi Arabia organizers want to see The Rock at the event, who last wrestled in WWE back in 2024 at WrestleMania 40. WWE is keen to host the show in Saudi Arabia , marking the first time its biggest PLE will take place in the country, despite the ongoing conflict involving the Houthis. Reports have highlighted WWE's firm stance on holding both WrestleMania, which is still several months away, and Crown Jewel, scheduled for November, in Saudi Arabia. At the time of publication, WWE has yet to announce a date for WrestleMania 43, which is reportedly not a priority for the promotion at the moment.
summary: WWE has preliminary plans for WrestleMania 43 in Saudi Arabia that include a potential world title match between Roman Reigns and Oba Femi, with some believing it could headline the show. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk are both expected to feature prominently, possibly in a rematch from SummerSlam. Rhea Ripley is also slated for a role upon her return from injury, while The Rock has been requested by Saudi organizers.

title: Swerve Strickland Pitched Trio Opportunity To New Level
raw_title: AEW's New Level Detail How Swerve Strickland Pitched Them On Forming A Trio
summary_src: The New Level have settled into AEW almost seamlessly thanks to Swerve Strickland, who reportedly pitched the idea of the three men being a trio.
body: "[Strickland] goes, 'Look, if we jump in this trios [situation], you get a chance to wrestle, what, six, seven other tag teams right from the jump at Wembley. So logically, well, of course we want to put hands on everybody as quick as we can. And now by winning those titles, we beat a bunch of other very credible, very good tag-teams that AEW has to offer. And so it's about making sure that we are getting the reps with all of these people on the roster, and having the most dangerous man in all of AEW at our side while we're doing that, with Prince Nana as well." Whether Strickland and The New Level remain as AEW World Trios Champions after this weekend is a different story. They put their belts on the line this Saturday at AEW WrestleDream 2026 against Hangman Page and Brodido in a Two-out-of-Three Falls match, marking the first time that stipulation has ever been implemented into a trios match in AEW history. The champions did defeat the challengers last month at AEW All Out 2026, but they will need to reach a new level in itself to remain as champions this weekend.
summary: Swerve Strickland convinced AEW's New Level to form a trio by highlighting the chance to immediately face six or seven top tag teams at Wembley. The strategy allowed them to gain valuable in-ring reps against credible opponents while having Strickland as the most dangerous man in the company alongside Prince Nana. As current AEW World Trios Champions, they defend against Hangman Page and The Acclaimed this Saturday at WrestleDream 2026 in the first-ever two-out-of-three-falls trios match in company history.

title: On the Record: John Cena Opens Up On What WWE Fans Chanting “You Suck” Taught Him About His Critics
raw_title: John Cena Reveals What WWE Fans Chanting “You Suck” Taught Him About His Critics
summary_src: John Cena spent years walking into WWE arenas where half the crowd treated him like Superman and the other half couldn’t wait to tell him he sucked. It turns out those hostile reactions taught him a lesson he still carries with him today.
body: Cena explained that he had already experienced hostile crowds long before he became WWE’s top star. In fact, he believes wrestling in front of tiny audiences prepared him even better than being booed by thousands of people. “Having the anonymity to be in a crowd of 10,000 yelling, ‘You suck,’ when you know you’re, you can’t be noticed, that, that doesn’t take a lot of courage. When you’re at, um, Saint Teresa’s Gym and you’re in a crowd of 10 and you’re one of those 10 who stand up and say, ‘Prototype, you suck,’ and I can look you in the eye and be like, ‘What?’ That takes courage and bravery.” Cena said he dealt with that kind of direct reaction while wrestling as The Prototype in Ultimate Pro Wrestling and later during his developmental run in Ohio Valley Wrestling. “And I dealt, I got to deal with that wrestling in the LA for Ultimate Pro and I got to deal with that wrestling for, uh, Ohio Valley Wrestling.” Those early experiences helped Cena understand what professional wrestling really was and gave him an important lesson before he was ever standing in packed WWE arenas. “So I guess, I guess I just kinda, again, good teachers around me to tell me, like, this is the business, you know, and, um, and what a great lesson to learn of, like, you can’t please everybody.” Cena then connected those divided WWE reactions to the rebellious personality he had as a kid. He recalled wearing clothes that made him stand out when he was younger and said he could have changed himself then just as easily as he could have changed his WWE character later. “And I think the reason I was so polarizing is just like at 12 years old wearing those MC Hammer pants. When I could have easily took them off, that’d been an easy route. Or I could have remained myself.” That same mentality became a major part of how Cena approached his WWE character. Instead of trying to eliminate the boos by becoming whatever critics wanted him to be, Cena said he stayed committed to a character that reflected his actual values. “I was very authentic to character, and character mirrored a lot of the things that I value in real life. And either you’re watching that channel or you’re not. You know what I’m saying? And that’s, you know, we all have our favorite things to do and things we also criticize, and I’m, I am who I am.” Cena said trying to create a version of himself capable of winning everybody over would have been impossible anyway. “I’m not trying to amalgamate to get to, to, to spread this impossible blanket that includes everybody. I can’t please everybody.” His message to the fans who supported him, and especially those who didn’t, was simple. Cena spent years hearing “Let’s Go Cena” and “Cena Sucks” battle each other inside the same building, but he never saw winning every critic over as the endgame. He learned early that some people were never going to ride with him, so his answer was to stay himself and make sure they had plenty to react to anyway. H Jenkins H Jenkins has bee

title: WWE Stars Hesitant to Face Oba Femi

body: Femi is hot on the heels of a win over Bronson Reed at Money in the Bank last weekend, which follows in the footsteps of two major wins over Brock Lesnar, becoming the 2026 King of the Ring, and consistent on-screen talk of being the future of the industry - all as many fans predict the Ruler will end up facing Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Title at WrestleMania 43 next year. Speaking on the latest Self Made Sessions , Ibou of Self Made Pro said that "a lot" of wrestlers have been "hesitant" to work with Oba Femi. This isn't anything personal against Oba, but more that, given how protected and strongly positioned Femi is, a match or rivalry might not be the most productive thing for a talent, as it's likely to simply end with Oba beating them and that talent dropping down the card. It was also noted that there is somewhat of a similar feeling from talent when it comes to potentially working with Gunther , as the Ring General is another star who's heavily protected. For those working against Oba Femi and Gunther, some have the feeling that they "don't get a lot out" of those matches. As for their current plans, Oba Femi recently shut down Paul Heyman's advances on this week's Raw, while Gunther is on a collision course with Finn Balor over on SmackDown right now.

body: Bron Breakker and Austin Theory won the tag team titles from The Street Profits on the July 6 episode of RAW, thanks to Maxxine Dupri . The Alpha Queen hit a low blow to Angelo Dawkins, helping Theory and Breakker win. WWE receives plenty of criticism for how they book the tag team division. It rarely receives the same importance as the singles division and is often overlooked. The Vision's current reign as the World Tag Team Champions is a good reason why the criticism is valid. Breakker and Theory have been champions for over a hundred days now, but they have yet to defend the titles on television. The Vision regularly appears on WWE TV, but not to represent the tag team division. The heel group is more focused on its members' individual feuds. Recently, The Vision was involved in a feud with Oba Femi . First, Bron Breakker feuded with The Ruler, leading to a match at Sunday Night's Main Event. However, the bout did not produce a clear winner due to Bronson Reed attacking Femi. Reed then began feuding with Femi. At WWE Money in the Bank, The Ruler defeated the Australian powerhouse despite The Vision trying to help Reed. The lack of title defenses could eventually force Adam Pearce to take action. The RAW General Manager has a responsibility to keep the tag team division moving, and it would be difficult to justify The Vision holding the championships indefinitely without putting them on the line. Adam Pearce could confront The Vision and remind them they have a responsibility to defend the World Tag Team Titles as the reigning champions. The heel faction's members aren't known to be team players, so they might not take the RAW General Manager seriously. However, Pearce could make it clear that there would be consequences if they refuse to cooperate. Such a decision would give the tag team division an opportunity to move forward. WWE could use this situation to make the World Tag Team Championship feel important again. If Adam Pearce believes the champions are neglecting the titles, he could be forced to take action. That said, this scenario is only based on speculation, and nothing has been confirmed.

title: WWE superstars AJ Styles and Nattie bring smiles to Perth Children’s Hospital ahead of weekend — Telethon 2026
raw_title: Telethon 2026: WWE superstars AJ Styles and Nattie bring smiles to Perth Children’s Hospital ahead of weekend
body: Styles and fellow global wrestling heavyweight Natalya made a surprise heart-warming visit at Perth Children’s Hospital yesterday, sharing hugs and snapping selfies with patients — and WWE devotees — ahead of the Telethon weekend. For 13-year-old patient Blade Dyson, meeting his WWE idol was an unforgettable moment. “I have been waiting for hours to meet him, as soon as Mum told me I couldn’t believe it,” he said, shaking in disbelief. “I’m so starstruck right now, he (AJ Styles) is like my hero. I love wrestling so this has just been the best day ever.” Five-year-old Elijah Green was equally captivated as the stars walked into his ward. “Dad loves AJ and I do, too,” he said. “It’s cool that he is here.” For the two-time WWE world champion, meeting patients at PCH put everything into perspective before the frantic fundraising frenzy kicks off on the weekend. “I think that it’s great being able to be a superstar in wrestling, but it’s even better when you’re able to share special moments with kids who really sometimes need to, you know, get a smile on their face,” Styles, 49, said. “It’s the best, I love being able to be a star in wrestling, but it’s even better when you’re able to make kids smile. It marks his first time visiting Perth’s iconic charity marathon and the father of four immediately felt the cause’s magnitude. “I don’t know much about Telethon, but From what I’m seeing, it’s a pretty big deal. So I’m expecting something big,” Styles said. “I think the opportunity to just obviously meet the kids and then meet other celebrities that are able to do this as well is what I’m looking forward to most. Third-generation wrestler and former SmackDown women’s champion Natalya — affectionately known as Nattie — was equally moved by the warm WA welcome a decade after last visiting Perth. “And almost all the kids that we’ve met today, they are big fans of WWE, so it’s even more rewarding to know that they know who we are and they’re excited that we came. title: Major League Wrestling Lands Amazon Deal, MLW Fusion Now Available On Prime Video
raw_title: Major League Wrestling Lands Amazon Deal, MLW Fusion Now Available On Prime Video
body: Share on Twitter --> Major League Wrestling has landed on Amazon Prime Video. On Tuesday, the promotion issued a press release to officially announce that their weekly show MLW Fusion is coming to Amazon Prime Video. This is in addition to its other current weekly home, Tubi, with replays also available on YouTube, VEEPS and NJPW WORLD. Check out the complete announcement with all of the details below. Full seasons and individual episodes now available to purchase, bringing MLW’s hard-hitting flagship series to another major platform CHARLESTON, S.C. – Oct. 13, 2026 — Major League Wrestling (MLW) today announced that MLW Fusion is now available on Amazon Prime Video, expanding the league’s reach and giving fans another way to experience and collect its championship fights, epic rivalries and hard-hitting action. Fans can purchase full seasons for $26.99 or individual episodes for $1.99. Explore MLW Fusion on Prime Video here . The launch of MLW Fusion on Amazon Prime Video further expands MLW’s distribution across leading streaming platforms, bringing the league’s flagship series to a broader audience and strengthening its global media footprint. “MLW belongs on the biggest platforms, and Amazon Prime Video is another significant step in that direction,” said MLW Founder and CEO Court Bauer. “We’re making it easier for fans to discover and experience Fusion, follow the rivalries and revisit the fights that get everyone talking. This gives our fans another way to watch and opens the door for a new audience to experience MLW.” MLW Fusion premieres Thursdays at 8 PM ET, streaming free on Tubi , with replays available on YouTube, VEEPS and NJPW WORLD. title: Former WWE, MLW wrestler reportedly signs with TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Former WWE, MLW wrestler reportedly signs with TNA Wrestling
body: Shotzi Blackheart has officially signed with TNA Wrestling, according to Fightful Select. Shotzi appeared at the promotion’s television tapings on Tuesday, October 13 at the Dothan Civic Center in Dothan, Alabama. Shortly after her appearance, reports surfaced that her contract with MLW had expired on October 5. Her final match with MLW took place at the company’s September 12 taping in Charleston, South Carolina, where she dropped the MLW Women’s World Championship to Masha Slamovich. Shotzi posted to social media earlier in the day on Wednesday that her brother Dean passed away on Sunday night. She said that while she was able to fulfill her commitments this week with her family’s support, she is withdrawing from her scheduled CMLL tour next week to be with her family. Shotzi had been scheduled to compete in the 2026 International Women’s Grand Prix on October 23 at Arena Mexico. Shotzi made her MLW debut at Summer of the Beasts on June 26, 2025. That appearance came shortly after her departure from WWE when her contract expired, ending a six-year run with the company. Since leaving WWE, Shotzi has also wrestled for GCW, House of Glory, World Series Wrestling in Australia, PROGRESS, and several CMLL shows in Mexico in April. title: Match Made: Shotzi Retains as Kross vs. Bishop Gets Last Man Standing — MLW Fusion 217
raw_title: MLW Fusion 217: Shotzi Retains as Kross vs. Bishop Gets Last Man Standing
body: PHILADELPHIA — Shotzi survives Rina to retain the MLW Women’s World Championship , Matt Riddle advances in the Opera Cup, and Killer Kross vs. Josh Bishop gains a Last Man Standing stipulation in a pivotal edition of MLW Fusion 217 from the 2300 Arena. The episode builds toward Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7 with a major world-title announcement, trouble within The Skyscrapers and an attack that derails CJ Gallows’ planned singles debut. ZAMAYA and Okumura also pick up victories, while Yota Tsuji closes the broadcast with a message for Chicago. Kross arrives with Scarlett and acknowledges both sides of his rivalry with Bishop: he won their earlier singles meeting, but Bishop pinned him when they met again in tag team competition. “But one thing I’m not going to do is hold great talent back,” Kross says. The conversation takes a turn when Dijak interrupts. The Skyscrapers member argues that the victory belonged to the team and that, as its self-proclaimed captain, he should receive the championship opportunity. “He’ll talk when I say he can talk, and right now it’s my time to talk, and I deserve that championship shot,” Dijak says as Bishop watches him. Kross calls attention to the dynamic between the partners and urges Bishop to speak for himself. Despite Dijak’s demands, the champion offers Bishop another shot at the MLW World Heavyweight Championship. Tiara James makes her return with a dismissive assessment of Philadelphia and its support for ZAMAYA. Calling herself top tier, James challenges the undefeated powerhouse and mocks the idea that ZAMAYA could become a bigger star. The confrontation lasts far longer than the match. ZAMAYA storms into the ring, and once the contest officially begins, she hits a Death Valley Driver to put James away almost immediately. Result: ZAMAYA defeats Tiara James following a Death Valley Driver. The win keeps ZAMAYA unbeaten in MLW. Later in the episode, an ominous message warns that her success has attracted attention, introducing another potential obstacle in her path without identifying a confirmed opponent. body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » Former WWE Star Signs With TNA Wrestling — Report Shotzi Blackheart has reportedly secured her next wrestling destination following her recent departure from MLW, appearing at TNA Wrestling’s television tapings in Alabama this week. However, the career development comes during a difficult period for the former WWE star, who has also announced a change to her upcoming schedule following a family tragedy. According to Fightful Select , Blackheart has signed a deal with TNA after appearing at the Dothan Civic Center in Dothan, Alabama, on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Her MLW contract reportedly expired on Oct. 5, opening the door for the move. Blackheart is no stranger to TNA, having competed for the promotion in 2019 when it operated under the IMPACT Wrestling name. She also built experience across several independent promotions after her WWE contract expired, ending a six-year run with the company. Her most recent MLW run began in June 2025, and she previously held the MLW Women’s World Featherweight Championship before losing the title to Masha Slamovich at a September taping. While Blackheart’s next professional chapter appears to be taking shape, she has also shared heartbreaking news with fans. On Wednesday, she revealed that her brother, Dean, had passed away on Sunday night. Blackheart announced she would withdraw from the CMLL Women’s Grand Prix, which is scheduled for Oct. 23 at Arena México, so she could spend time with her family and honor her brother’s memory. “It was a huge honor to be selected for the CMLL Grand Prix, and I don’t take that opportunity lightly,” Blackheart wrote. “Thank you to everyone at CMLL and the fans for understanding how hard all this is for me.” Blackheart has previously credited her brother with helping spark an interest in wrestling during childhood, making the loss particularly personal. raw_title: Drew McIntyre Reveals Foot Issues Were Causing Major Balance Problems in WWE
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has been wrestling for 26 years, but somehow he says his body feels better now than it has in more than a decade.
body: “I mean, I think 26 years of wrestling has probably, you know, done a little damage, but incredibly, I feel amazing. The past year-plus, I started working with a new trainer, and he was born with brittle bone disease. Basically grew up in a body cast, was told, ‘This is kind of going to be your life.’ And he wanted to be a bodybuilder, loved Schwarzenegger. Like so many of us as kids, young men, just idolized Arnold. He was like, ‘I’m going to be like Arnold.’” McIntyre explained that Black spent years learning how to strengthen his own body and eventually started passing some of those techniques along to him. That’s led to Drew doing a ton of preventative work that he simply wasn’t thinking about earlier in his career. “And he started reading books about how to strengthen your bones, strengthen your tendons, learned a lot of tricks. And inevitably — I mean, he’s the angriest, littlest man I’ve ever met in my life. Tall as he is wide, but he’s jacked out of his mind. He could have walked on the outside of his feet, but he’s built up his body where he gets around great. He trains like crazy.” That work has apparently paid off in a big way. McIntyre is currently sitting at 285 pounds, the heaviest he’s ever been, but says he physically feels better than he has in around 12 years. The biggest surprise for Drew was discovering just how much of his problem started with his feet. He’d noticed himself feeling strangely off-balance both in everyday life and inside the ring, something his wife apparently had plenty of fun roasting him about. “They’re very, very important. My feet were — I roll them out. You really don’t think about it. I didn’t realize how bad they were either. Like, I felt off-balance at times in real life, in the ring. My wife says, ‘You’re the most unathletic professional athlete in the world. You go inside a wrestling ring and it’s like magic. Then you walk around, you’re falling over and stuff.’” Once Drew started working on his feet, things began changing. His routine now includes rolling them out along with toe raises and calf raises, all with the goal of giving him a stronger base. “And I was like, ‘Yeah, I always feel off-balance at times.’ And he told me it starts from the ground up, and we’ve got to start rolling those feet out, start doing toe raises, calf raises — just start building from the ground up.” McIntyre really noticed the difference when he recently stepped back into a wrestling ring and filmed a clip of himself running the ropes. While barefoot in the ring beforehand, he suddenly realized just how much sturdier he felt — and naturally found a way to turn that into a joke about his WWE push. “As I say, it’s been over a year now. And when I was in a ring recently, I posted a little clip online just bouncing off the ropes. I think about over nine million views, probably. People want me back. title: Adam Copeland Sets 2027 Retirement, Eyes AEW World Title

body: Copeland announced that 2027 marks his final year as a wrestler on Wednesday's edition of AEW Dynamite while also confirming that he's looking to capture the AEW World Title. "I'm aging out, and that's okay," Copeland said (0:20 mark). "It happens to everybody. But because of that, I just want to let you all know that 2027 will be my last year in professional wrestling." But all of that being said, that is why I have to go for the AEW Championship." Copeland also revealed that tag-team partner Christian Cage suffered a collapsed lung and three broken ribs after he was thrown into a ladder at AEW All Out on Sept. 26. Copeland's 2027 retirement will mark the end of a legendary professional wrestling career that began in 1992, as he started by competing in singles and tag team competitions with several independent promotions. He finally made his televised debut with the WWF, which was later renamed to WWE, in 1998 as Edge. During his WWE career, he won 31 total titles. This included 11 world championships. Copeland also had memorable feuds with rivals such as John Cena, Jeff Hardy, Matt Hardy and The Undertaker. Copeland eventually returned to WWE from 2020-23 before making his AEW debut in Oct. 2023. He quickly established himself as a threat upon joining AEW, winning the TNT Championship by defeating Cage at Worlds End in Dec. 2023. It represented the first of two TNT Championship reigns by Copeland. Copeland and Cage ultimately joined forces, capturing the AEW World Tag Team Championship at Double or Nothing on May 24. The 52-year-old will be stepping away from wrestling at the end of 2027, but will attempt to secure the title before doing so.
summary: On AEW Dynamite, Adam Copeland declared that 2027 will be his final year in professional wrestling. He explained that he wants to capture the AEW World Championship before retiring due to his age. Copeland also updated fans on tag team partner Christian Cage, who sustained a collapsed lung and three broken ribs from a ladder spot at All Out.

title: Sheamus Recalls Nervous WWE ECW Debut
raw_title: Sheamus Looks Back On WWE Debut, Says He Never Had A 'Great Story' In The Company
summary_src: "The Celtic Warrior" Sheamus opens up about his main roster WWE debut and the years of storylines, or lack thereof, that followed.
body: For former WWE Champion Sheamus, his main roster journey traces back to that now-defunct brand, with his official debut pitting him in a match against Oliver John on the June 30, 2009 edition of "ECW." "The Celtic Warrior" ultimately walked away with a win, but not without a sense of nervousness behind it. In his early years with WWE, Sheamus noted that he got "extremely" nervous out of fear of making mistakes. Fortunately, he spent time in WWE's developmental system and competed in dark matches to make him more comfortable, and in turn, prepare him for his eventual ascent. Sheamus defeated John in quick fashion on "ECW," courtesy of a Brogue Kick and a backbreaker. Less than six months later, he bested the company's top star, John Cena, to become the WWE Champion. Multiple current and former WWE stars have gone on record citing Sheamus as the hardest in-ring hitter they've ever encountered . Sheamus himself confirmed that he never stopped them from dishing the physicality right back to him, however. In fact, he encouraged it, both for the sake of his opponent and the audience watching along. "People love to see a fight," Sheamus said. "They want to see a person give something, a character, wrestler, whatever it is you want to call it, they want to see something different. An internal hunger and fight in them. I prided myself in getting that out of them. That was my forte. Would I have loved a lot more storylines and stuff like that? Of course, I would have. I never really got a really great story that I could sink my teeth into." The multi-time world champion departed from WWE after reportedly turning down a restructured contract extension offer. He officially hit the free agency market earlier this month.

The Celtic Warrior admitted feeling extremely nervous early in his WWE run and credited time in developmental plus dark matches for helping him gain confidence before winning the WWE Championship from John Cena less than six months later. He also discussed his reputation as one of the hardest hitters in the business and how he always encouraged opponents to return the physicality because fans want to see a real fight.

title: WWE Creative Frustrated With Gunther's Booking
raw_title: Details On Creative Frustration Regarding GUNTHER's Current WWE Booking
summary_src: Questions have reportedly been raised among WWE's creative personnel about GUNTHER's current booking on SmackDown.
body: Some have argued that GUNTHER's booking has been underwhelming since he retired several WWE legends, and a new report by " Wrestlevotes on Fightful Select " has revealed that some members of the company's creative team are unhappy with it. The outlet has claimed that the people that they spoke to backstage in WWE are frustrated with how GUNTHER has been booked in recent times on "WWE SmackDown." The report added that its sources were unsure how GUNTHER could be used to build on the momentum he gained after retiring the likes of John Cena and AJ Styles. Questions have also been raised about whether WWE had a clear plan for him after his retirement match against Cena. A source that the outlet spoke to was unsure about the direction for his character on the blue brand. The former WWE World Heavyweight Champion has remained in and around the world title picture, even taking out current Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn on the October 2 edition of "SmackDown." Curiously, he has also been feuding with Danhausen, an unusual pairing given that Danhausen is a comedy character while GUNTHER has a more serious gimmick. On last week's " SmackDown ," GUNTHER attacked Danhausen before the bell rang to signal the start of their match, but Finn Balor came to Danhausen's rescue, who is another star currently feuding with GUNTHER.

title: WWE and Montez Ford Sued by Security Guard
raw_title: WWE & Montez Ford Reportedly Being Sued By Security Guard
summary_src: WWE & Montez Ford (Kenneth Crawford) are reportedly being sued by a security guard that was working at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois.
body: According to POST Wrestling , Lucas filed a lawsuit in the Circuit Court of Cook County. The suit alleges 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, along with violating the Illinois Gender Violence Act. POST also notes that Event Services, LLC, a WWE subsidiary is also named in the lawsuit. Since the clip of the interaction between Crawford and Lucas is widely available online, Lucas alleges that both he and his kids have been "mocked and ridiculed". Due to these actions, Lucas believes he has "suffered humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress". Because his face is easily seen in the clip, Lucas also claims his image has been used for commercial purposes and therefore violates the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. The clip is not currently on the Netflix replay as the show cuts to commercial. Lucas maintains that a WWE employee had him seated against the ringside barricade, positioning him in Street Profits path. The filing states that "Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized 'lap dance.'" As Crawford moved closer to Lucas, the suit alleges that his "left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff's leg." A case management hearing is scheduled for December 10. Lucas is seeking punitive damages along with unspecified monetary damages, and coverage of his legal costs. He also wants an order that WWE and Crawford cannot use his identity.
summary: A security guard named Lucas has filed a 14-count lawsuit in Cook County Circuit Court against Montez Ford, WWE and its subsidiary Event Services LLC. The suit alleges assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act and Right of Publicity Act after Ford performed a sexually provocative dance in front of him at ringside. Lucas claims the widely circulated clip has caused him and his children to be mocked, resulting in humiliation, embarrassment and emotional distress.

title: Bully Ray Praises Je'Von Evans' Intense Ambulance Return
raw_title: Bully Ray Talks Je'Von Evans Spot That Stood Out To Him In WWE MITB Men's Ladder Match
summary_src: Bully Ray highlighted a spot that made Je'Von Evans stand out in the men's WWE Money in the Bank ladder match, and it wasn't his ambulance bump.
body: Evans competed in the men's Money in the Bank match alongside eventual winner Penta , CM Punk, Trick Williams, Bron Breakker, and Kevin Owens. During the match, Evans was wheeled away but returned to the ring in an ambulance and got his revenge on Breakker by landing punches, which greatly impressed Ray. "There was a moment in time in that match that meant more to me, for Je'Von Evans and his future, than that spot. When he pulls up to the ring, and Bron Breakker looks inside the driver's side, and Je'Von opens that door with such force, Bron Breakker goes flying, did you see Je'Von Evans when he jumped out of that ambulance and started beating the sh*t out of Bron Breakker?" asked Ray on " Busted Open ." "There was so much intent behind those fists flying. We talk about the art of the run-in, or we talk about, you know, making everything mean something. I felt Je'Von Evans in that moment, more than I felt him in the entire match." "A babyface can only rely on his fists. That's all a babyface needs at the end of the day is his fists. And the way Je'Von's fists were flying made me believe in him more than any other spot in that match. And that's why less is more," he added. The Hall of Famer praised Evans for looking determined and making his punches seem convincing. Evans' night ended on a brutal note, as Breakker threw him from the top of the ladder onto the ambulance just minutes after he landed multiple punches on him. Breakker continued the assault on the following episode of "WWE Raw," spearing an already injured Evans.
summary: Bully Ray highlighted a specific moment from the men's Money in the Bank ladder match that stood out more than Je'Von Evans' other spots. After being wheeled away, Evans returned in an ambulance, forcefully opened the door to knock Bron Breakker down, and unloaded with purposeful punches that Ray felt conveyed real intent and made him believe in Evans as a babyface. The WWE Hall of Famer emphasized that the convincing fist strikes and determination shown were more impactful than any other part of the match, proving less is more.

title: Roman Reigns regrets 'Sufferin Succotash' promo
raw_title: Roman Reigns wishes he’d said ‘Nah’ to that ‘Sufferin’ Succotash’ promo
summary_src: As the three former members of The Shield began their runs as singles stars, Seth Rollins and Jon Moxley/Dean Ambrose seemed to be favored by many wrestling fans because of their time on the independents, and because they were CM Punk’s first choices for the group.
body: There was much more skepticism of Roman Reigns, and it wasn’t long until that turned into hostility. A key moment that led to the outright rejection of Reigns happened in early 2015, when he interrupted Rollins on SmackDown and said ( emphasis mine): “… look at you, you’re just so full of yourself now. Actually, you’re full of something else. You are a sniveling little suck up sellout full of sufferin’ succotash, son ! Yeah, yeah, yeah, I know, that was not easy to say!” Talking about that stretch of his career on Club Shay Shay earlier this week, Roman told Shannon Sharpe: The example that came to mind for the Big Dog-turned-Tribal Chief? He was fuzzy on the dates, but… you guessed it… ”This was like 14 years ago, and they’ll still quote me for saying ‘sufferin succotash.’ This was so long ago. It was 12 years ago, you know? ”I mean, I’ve delivered unbelievable work since then, but still, I’ll be tied to that. There wasn’t that many, but there’s probably two or three promos or scenarios, segments or, you know, finishes of a match or something like that that I would probably go back and develop the balls to be like, ‘Nah, not today, brother,’” That’s a sentiment our own Geno Mrosko expressed on the moment’s third anniversary : Watching it back now, it’s still mind blowing that he was given such horrific copy to recite from a script that should have been burned before it ever reached his fingertips. It is, however, worth watching because I’ll be damned if it doesn’t show just how much Roman Reigns has grown as a performer. I’m not saying he could make that copy work today — I don’t even think John Cena at his cheesiest could make that work — but he’s far more comfortable in his own skin, the kind of change you hardly notice because it’s drawn out over time. And that was back when The Bloodline was just a glimmer in Reigns’ eye! For me, while I’m sure it wasn’t fun for him, I’m glad we had that awkward stretch of Roman’s WWE career. It informs his current character so much, adding layers we wouldn’t have if The OTC had arrived fully formed before our eyes. What’s your current take on WWE Creative/Vince McMahon giving their hand-picked next big thing a Sylvester J. Pussycat line? Could, should, or would Roman have said no? The famous one-legged star shared the ring with Hulk Hogan, Brock Lesnar, and McMahon, but his best moment came in AEW. Cena doesn’t have much stroke in WWE, so he is excited about WrestleMania 43 making his London wish more viable. The WWE star weaves work and shoot into an interesting answer about his unresolved storyline with Dwayne Johnson. The fex-WWE CEO has completed his ‘accelerated rehab program’ for driving 100 mph into the back of another moving car. Be respectful in your interactions with contributors and fellow fans. Reigns noted that despite strong work since then the line from over a decade ago continues to be quoted and tied to him.

During the segment Reigns delivered the line "you are a sniveling little suck up sellout full of sufferin’ succotash, son" before adding "Yeah, yeah, yeah, I know, that was not easy to say." Appearing on Club Shay Shay earlier this week Reigns discussed that stretch of his career with Shannon Sharpe.

Reigns noted the line is still quoted years later saying "This was like 14 years ago, and they’ll still quote me for saying ‘sufferin succotash.’" He expressed some uncertainty about the exact timing adding "This was so long ago. It was 12 years ago, you know?"

He identified a small number of segments he would approach differently today explaining "There wasn’t that many, but there’s probably two or three promos or scenarios, segments or, you know, finishes of a match or something like that that I would probably go back and develop the balls to be like, ‘Nah, not today, brother.’"

title: AEW Honors PAC in Full Gear Artwork
raw_title: AEW pays tribute to PAC in updated graphic for Full Gear pay-per-view
summary_src: AEW is honoring the late Benjamin Satterley ‘PAC’ in its artwork for next month’s Full Gear pay-per-view.
body: AEW is honoring the late Benjamin Satterley, ‘PAC’, in its artwork for next month’s Full Gear pay-per-view. Full Gear became a term in relation to PAC’s appearance at the inaugural AEW press conference in January 2019 to confront Hangman Page in his trunks. The term was used on an edition of ‘Being the Elite’ and led to the name being adopted for the promotion’s annual pay-per-view in November. AEW has updated the logo for this year’s event, scheduled for November 14 in Arizona. The logo features two black arrows coming out of the logo, a ‘Black Arrow Warning’ sign with a sketch of PAC performing the maneuver, and an image of Pac’s chair and towel, which have become a staple of the Death Riders’ entrances. The performer died suddenly on September 27, one day after competing at the All Out show in Illinois.
summary: AEW has updated the Full Gear pay-per-view logo to pay tribute to the late PAC. The new graphic incorporates imagery tied to his Black Arrow move, signature chair and towel from Death Riders entrances, and references his role in originating the Full Gear name at the company's 2019 launch press conference. PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, passed away on September 27 shortly after wrestling at All Out.

title: Trey Miguel earns TNA title shot at Destination X
raw_title: TNA Destination X main event set for November 15
summary_src: The main event for TNA Destination X was confirmed after Thursday Night Impact.
body: The main event for TNA Destination X was confirmed after Thursday Night Impact. Trey Miguel became the #1 contender for the TNA World Championship by defeating Moose, Elijah, Ricky Sosa, and Jason Hotch in a ladder match. The match headlined Thursday’s edition of Impact taped earlier this week in Dothan, Alabama. It sets up Leon Slater’s defense of the championship on November 15 at the Destination X show in Edmonton, Alberta. Elijah was on his way to grabbing the contract when former champion Nic Nemeth interfered and dropped Elijah with a superkick. Miguel got rid of Nemeth by using the Lightning Spiral and climbed the ladder to secure the contract. Miguel is a former two-time X Division champion and held the International and tag team belts in TNA.
summary: Trey Miguel won a five-man ladder match on Thursday's Impact to become the number one contender for the TNA World Championship. He defeated Moose, Elijah, Ricky Sosa and Jason Hotch in the bout taped in Dothan, Alabama. Miguel will challenge Leon Slater for the title on November 15 at Destination X in Edmonton, Alberta.

llm_long: Trey Miguel earned a shot at the TNA World Championship by winning a five-way ladder match on Thursday's episode of Impact. The bout featured Moose, Elijah, Ricky Sosa, Jason Hotch and Miguel competing for the number one contendership. Miguel secured the contract after former champion Nic Nemeth interfered to stop Elijah from grabbing it.

Miguel then took out Nemeth with the Lightning Spiral before climbing the ladder to retrieve the contract. The match headlined the post-Bound For Glory edition of Impact that was taped earlier this week in Dothan, Alabama. During the contest, new International Champion Jason Hotch was climbing when former champion Mustafa Ali interfered, leading to the pair brawling backstage.

Leon Slater, who defeated Nic Nemeth for the title at Bound For Glory, will defend against Miguel at Destination X on November 15 in Edmonton, Alberta. The event will take place at the Edmonton Expo Arena and air live on TNA+.

title: Netflix Ousts Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria
raw_title: Netflix’s chief content officer Bela Bejaria gone from streaming service
summary_src: Bajaria helped oversee Netflix’s programming strategy with a $20 billion budget and was pivotal in WWE coming to Netflix in 2025.
body: Netflix’s chief content officer Bela Bajaria is out as the streamer made a bold decision to let the executive go. Bajaria helped oversee Netflix’s programming strategy with a $20 billion budget and was pivotal in WWE coming to Netflix in 2025. When the deal was announced in early 2024, Bajaria was quoted , “(WWE) has been very under-distributed outside the US. I think there’s really great opportunity to still grow it outside the U.S.” The exit comes one day after Netflix cut approximately 1,000 jobs with an underperforming stock and stalled engagement on the platform. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos acknowledged the disappointing performance in a recent chat, saying the service was “Not growing as fast as I want us to.” Former Fox and Disney executive Peter Rice will replace Bajaria.
summary: Netflix has parted ways with its chief content officer Bela Bajaria, who played a key role in securing the WWE programming deal set to begin in 2025. The move follows the streaming service cutting around 1,000 jobs amid disappointing stock performance and slowing subscriber engagement. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos admitted the platform is not expanding at the desired pace, with former Fox and Disney executive Peter Rice stepping in as her replacement.

body: PAC helped inspire the name of AEW Full Gear — and the logo for this year’s edition has been updated to pay tribute to him. The new Full Gear logo includes multiple nods to PAC . A “Black Arrow Warning” sign has been added to the Arizona desert backdrop, and a pair of black arrows are now part of one of the Full Gear cogs. PAC’s Death Riders chair and his towel have also been included. Full Gear has been one of AEW’s pay-per-views since the promotion’s inaugural year of 2019. The name derives from PAC showing up in full wrestling gear at AEW’s February 2019 launch rally in Jacksonville. While pretty much everyone else was dressed formally in business attire, PAC, without a shirt on, confronted Hangman Page while wearing wrestling trunks and boots. That became a bit on Being the Elite during PAC and Page’s feud. At Full Gear 2019, Page defeated PAC in a singles match. The 2025 edition of Full Gear saw PAC defeat Darby Allin. AEW, and the entire wrestling world, has been in mourning since PAC unexpectedly passed away at 40 years old on September 27. His cause of death is still pending additional testing after an initial autopsy was performed. Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona is hosting Full Gear 2026 on Saturday, November 14. The PPV is already less than a month away, and the build will pick up after WrestleDream concludes this weekend. WWE has confirmed that Ricky Saints will get his AAA Cruiserweight Championship shot against Rey Fenix on tonight’s SmackDown episode from Sacramento, California. The two have been feuding for a while — and Saints earned another shot at the Cruiserweight title by pinning Fenix in a six-man tag bout two weeks ago. Saints teamed with The War Raiders to defeat Fenix & Fraxiom on the October 2 SmackDown episode. After making a blind tag, Saints took advantage of the fact that Fenix did not know that he was the legal man, hitting Roshambo for the victory. In an online exclusive segment last Friday, Saints called out Fenix for this title match . Saints is looking for a different result this time after coming up short when he challenged Fenix for the title last month. WWE has established that, while the Cruiserweight Championship is primarily a Lucha Libre AAA title, it can be defended across all of the company’s brands. Fenix has been champion since late May. body: It sounds like Steven Borden is continuing to progress well following the scary injury he suffered at AEW All Out 2026. Along with that, the report notes that Penelope Ford was backstage at the show as well. Ford has been sidelined since late February due to an ankle injury. Borden’s injury occurred on September 26 while teaming with Darby Allin against Kevin Knight & Kyle Fletcher at All Out. After Borden hit his head during a double coast-to-coast spot, Knight & Fletcher won the number one contender’s match by referee stoppage. This Saturday’s WrestleDream pay-per-view will see Knight & Fletcher challenge The Young Bucks for the AEW Tag Team titles. It remains to be seen when Borden will be back in the ring. He had to pull out of an indie booking for Defy Wrestling on October 1 due to the injury. Debunking speculation that their deals could be coming up soon, it was reported last month that Ford and her husband Kip Sabian both have years remaining on their AEW contracts. Ford was teaming with Megan Bayne prior to her injury. Bayne has since formed a team with Lena Kross. Psicosis received the 2026 Lucha Libre Award at the Cauliflower Alley Club reunion and attended the event in person with Mysterio present while using a cane for mobility. The development follows a recent report that Tony Khan helped secure a WWE Legends contract for Necro Butcher.

llm_long: WWE has agreed to cover the cost of hip replacement surgery for lucha libre legend Psicosis. Rey Mysterio was the one who proposed the idea to the promotion.
Psicosis received the 2026 Lucha Libre Award at the Cauliflower Alley Club reunion. He attended the event in person and was joined by Mysterio for the celebration.
At the time of the ceremony, Psicosis was using a cane to help with his mobility.

The development follows a recent report that a different individual was responsible for death match legend Necro Butcher receiving a WWE Legends contract even though he had never worked for the company.

title: JBL Named President of Tragos/Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame
raw_title: JBL Named President of Tragos/Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame
summary_src: John Bradshaw Layfield is taking on a major new role in professional wrestling, while Gerry Brisco is stepping away from the position he has held for more than two decades.
body: The National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum announced that Brisco is stepping down as president of the George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame board of directors and moving into an advisory role. Layfield will replace him as president effective immediately. Brisco has served as president since the Hall of Fame was established in 1999 and helped guide its growth into one of the most respected institutions honoring professional wrestling history. Brisco said he feels comfortable handing things over to JBL and believes the Hall of Fame will continue moving in the right direction. “I’m happy to be leaving the board in the capable hands of JBL, and I am confident that he and his support team will ensure that the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame continues to grow and remain the best.” Brisco brings plenty of history to the role he is leaving behind. He won multiple championships during his career in the NWA and WWE and has been inducted into several halls of fame, including the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame itself. Layfield also has a long connection to the organization. He received the Lou Thesz Award from the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame in 2012 after a career that included three WWE Tag Team Championship reigns alongside Ron Simmons. “I’m honored that Mr. Brisco has chosen me to help continue the incredible success he has worked so hard to achieve.” He also made it clear that he and the team already have plans to expand the Hall of Fame’s reach. “The team and I look forward to growing the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame and moving forward in building the Global Hall of Fame brand.” That Global Hall of Fame brand is tied to the newly created Global Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame, LLC, which is expected to work closely with the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame. The new organization was created to expand opportunities involving the Hall of Fame, the Dan Gable Museum, professional wrestlers and the wrestling business as a whole. Layfield addressed any concern that the new organization could change how the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame operates for fans or inductees. He added that more information is coming and believes the arrangement will benefit both groups. “The GPW Hall of Fame will not affect fans or the enshrinement of members of the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame.” “We will announce more details in the future, but we view this as a win-win situation for both the GPW Hall of Fame and the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame.” Brisco helped lead the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame for more than 25 years, and now JBL is being handed the keys as the organization looks toward its next phase. With Brisco remaining involved in an advisory capacity and Layfield already talking expansion, this is less of a clean break and more of a major changing of the guard. title: Why John Cena Tries to Follow So Many People on Twitter
raw_title: Why John Cena Tries to Follow So Many People on Twitter
summary_src: John Cena doesn’t just want millions of people following him on social media — he wants to follow millions of them right back. In fact, the WWE legend says the only thing stopping him from following way more people on X is the platform itself.
body: Speaking to BuzzFeed UK , Cena was asked about the massive number of accounts he follows. He explained that the whole thing actually started while he was in Kensington filming Fast 9 , when he noticed how obsessed people had become with bragging about their follower counts. “They cut me off. I want to follow everybody. You used to only be able to — before it transformed names into X — follow a thousand people a day. And I actually started doing that here in Kensington. I was shooting Fast 9, and I’m like, ‘You know what? People are bragging about their followers. I get that — like, so many people are paying attention to me.’” Cena had already taken a completely different approach with Instagram. He deliberately follows nobody there because his account is basically a collection of unexplained images, and he doesn’t want who he follows influencing how people interpret whatever he posts. But when it came to Twitter, now X, Cena decided to go completely in the opposite direction. Instead of bragging about how many people wanted to hear from him, he liked the idea of bragging about how many people were willing to let him listen. “Because I didn’t follow anybody on Instagram and I was following a bunch of folks on Twitter, I’m like, ‘No. Follow everybody.’ Like, I want to brag about the people who allow me in their conversation.” There’s also a practical reason behind it. Cena follows all kinds of different people because he wants to see opinions and conversations that might be completely different from his own. “It can be a pretty gamey environment. And I follow a wide range of folks because if I want to learn and if I want to see how people think, you’ve got to be open to listening to their conversation.” “Now with X, you can only follow, like, eight people a day. That’s why I’m stuck at a million. I wish I was at, like, 12 million right now. Every day you get on there and chip away and chip away, and hopefully that number will go up. But, like, I’m still working.” Cena also knows that getting a random follow from John Cena can be a pretty cool moment for somebody. If clicking one button can make a fan smile or give them something to brag about, he figures there’s no reason not to do it. “There’s a lot of nuance there. People want to be heard. If they’ve got a message to send, they’ve got a voice that they believe in. A follow from me — it feels good, it makes them smile.” For Cena, it’s a ridiculously easy way to give a little something back to people who have spent years supporting him. It doesn’t cost him anything, but he knows that tiny notification could mean a lot more to the person receiving it. Cena’s social-media strategy might look completely random from the outside, but there’s clearly a method behind it. While Instagram is deliberately kept disconnected and mysterious, X is basically the opposite — Cena wants to hear from as many people as the platform will allow. title: Injury Update: Mercedes Martinez Undergoes ACL Surgery After GoFundMe Covers Procedure in Full
raw_title: Mercedes Martinez Undergoes ACL Surgery After GoFundMe Covers Procedure in Full
summary_src: Mercedes Martinez has officially undergone the ACL surgery she needed after turning to the wrestling community for financial help. The veteran wrestler had launched a GoFundMe after tearing the ACL in her right knee during her August 15 match against Allie Katch.

Martinez previously explained that she did not have health insurance and would have to pay for the surgery herself before doctors would schedule the procedure. Now that surgery is done. In a new video posted to Twitter, Martinez gave fans an update from the early stages of recovery and revealed that the GoFundMe covered the operation in full. Martinez said she was already moving into the next phase of recovery, which includes removing the dressing, cleaning the incision and starting rehab exercises from home. “Today we are taking the dressing off and cleaning up the incision and starting our first rehab session. Basically, it’s at home. Just me doing my own exercises is at home for today and taking the pain meds if we need them.” She also said she has barely been using pain medication and prefers to avoid it unless she absolutely needs it. “But me, I don’t take pain meds. Doctor says with me not taking my pain meds means I’m way ahead of the game, which just means I have a high tolerance of pain. And I prefer to do this as much as possible without any meds. And just if I need them, I’ll take them. If not, I can deal with it.” Martinez then showed fans part of the immediate post-surgery process, explaining that the larger bandage had been removed and she was preparing to clean the area, put on a smaller dressing and get back into her brace. “We took the big bandage off. Right now it’s now the gauze. We gotta clean this up. I’m gonna clean all this up and then put the big brace back on. Our big trusty brace right here. I’ll put that back on once I clean this out and put a different bandage on, smaller one, so we can start icing it.” The biggest news came when Martinez confirmed that the fundraiser had accomplished exactly what she needed it to do. “I just wanted to do a quick shout out and just say thank you all for the GoFundMe. The GoFundMe paid for the surgery in full. Thank you, thank you, thank you. That is a blessing for me where it’s one less stress and now it’s just dealing with the expenses of the recovery.” Martinez had previously said the surgery could not be scheduled until it was paid for because she was considered a self-pay patient. The GoFundMe changed that situation, allowing her to move forward with the procedure and begin the long road back. She said the next concern is covering the costs that come with rehabilitation and recovery. “I have done an Amazon ACL recovery wish list for some of the things that I’m figuring out now what I need to help get this recovery faster and heal faster. title: Injury Update: Kendal Grey Makes In-Ring Return After Injury at NXT Live Event

summary_src: Kendal Grey is officially back in the ring. After spending weeks on the sidelines and recently confirming that she’d finally been medically cleared, the NXT star returned to action at WWE’s October 15 live event in Kitchener and immediately picked up a win.
body: Grey faced Karmen Petrovic in her first match back and defeated her, putting an end to an absence that stretched back to August 30. More importantly, the match confirmed that Grey isn’t just cleared to compete anymore — she’s officially back in business. It’s a pretty big turnaround from where Grey was just a few days ago. On October 11, she was still teasing fans about her absence with a beach photo drop on Instagram and a caption that made it clear she hadn’t disappeared from anyone’s radar. That changed in Kitchener. Grey didn’t just step back between the ropes for the first time in more than a month — she walked away with a victory over Petrovic and made it clear her time on the sidelines is over. Her return also comes at an interesting point in the Women’s Championship picture. Sinclair is currently scheduled to challenge Jordan for the title at Halloween Havoc on October 31 after NXT General Manager Robert Stone lifted her suspension and granted her the match. Grey has already made it clear that she wants to reclaim the championship she lost while sidelined. With Sinclair getting her opportunity first and Grey now officially wrestling again, the title picture could get complicated pretty quickly depending on what happens at Halloween Havoc. For now, the biggest news is that Grey’s comeback has gone from a medical clearance to an actual in-ring return. After weeks of recovery, she wasted no time getting back in the win column. title: WWE Had Nothing to Do With Max Caster’s Firing After TNA Bound for Glory
raw_title: WWE Had Nothing to Do With Max Caster’s Firing After TNA Bound for Glory
summary_src: WWE is apparently making one thing very clear about Max Caster’s TNA exit — don’t blame them. Despite WWE and TNA’s working relationship, people within WWE insist they had absolutely nothing to do with Caster getting dropped after his controversial Bound For Glory rap.
body: That shuts down any idea that WWE stepped in behind the scenes and pressured its partner promotion to do something about Caster. Based on the report, TNA made the call on its own before the situation even reached most of WWE’s decision-makers. The controversy started at Bound For Glory, where Caster made his TNA debut against Moose. As usual, he performed an entrance rap before the match, but a line referencing Riyadh quickly became the bigger story coming out of his appearance . Caster’s run didn’t survive the fallout. We had also previously reported that TNA President Carlos Silva made the decision to cut ties with him , ending Caster’s stint with the company after just one match. Caster wasn’t believed to have a long-term contract either. He was working under a per-appearance arrangement, which made it much easier for TNA to simply end the relationship once the controversy erupted. Another major detail was that TNA didn’t know what Caster was going to say beforehand. He had creative control over his entrance rap, and the Riyadh line was neither scripted nor approved by the company. TNA ultimately removed Caster-related content and issued a public apology before cutting ties with him altogether . Some people within AEW felt TNA should have anticipated the possibility of Caster pushing things too far considering controversial freestyle raps have always been part of his act. With WWE and TNA working together, it was always possible that questions would come up about whether WWE had any influence over how the situation was handled. This report paints a much simpler picture — TNA had apparently already made its move before most important people in WWE even knew there was a controversy. summary: That shuts down any idea that WWE stepped in behind the scenes and pressured its partner promotion to do something about Caster. Based on the report, TNA made the call on its own before the situation even reached most of WWE’s decision-makers.

title: Key Executive Who Helped Put Together WWE’s Netflix Deal Leaving Streaming Giant
raw_title: Key Executive Who Helped Put Together WWE’s Netflix Deal Leaving Streaming Giant
summary_src: WWE’s relationship with Netflix just got a pretty interesting shakeup behind the scenes. One of the executives who helped bring WWE to the streaming giant is leaving, and the man replacing her happens to be very familiar with WWE himself.
body: Netflix chief content officer Bela Bajaria is leaving the company after holding the position since 2023. Bajaria was instrumental in the negotiations that helped land WWE on Netflix , making her departure especially notable just a couple of years after WWE made its massive move to the platform. Her exit comes during a bigger shakeup at Netflix. The company is laying off around six percent of its workforce amid stock declines and concerns over stagnant business without signs of substantial growth. But here’s where things get interesting for WWE. Former Disney and Fox executive Peter Rice is taking Bajaria’s position, and Rice isn’t exactly a stranger to the wrestling business. Rice was one of the major players behind SmackDown moving to Fox. Back in 2018, when he was Chairman and CEO of Fox Networks Group, he was directly involved in trying to land WWE as soon as NBCUniversal’s exclusive negotiating window ended. The morning after that window expired on May 16, 2018, Rice hosted a meeting on the 44th floor of Fox’s Manhattan headquarters. Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Stephanie McMahon, Rupert Murdoch, Eric Shanks and Larry Jones were all involved, with Fox making a serious pitch to WWE. There’s another reason this situation is worth watching. Raw and WWE’s premium live events have been doing good numbers on Netflix, even if they may not have reached some of the expectations people had when the deal was first announced. Netflix’s behavior since landing WWE has also raised questions about how much weekly sports programming it actually wants. The company has shown more interest in major events than adding a bunch of regular weekly sports properties, and it didn’t outbid ESPN when the U.S. rights to WWE’s premium live events became available. None of that means WWE is suddenly in trouble at Netflix, and there’s no indication right now that Rice plans to change anything involving the company. But the executive who helped bring WWE to Netflix walking out while one of the people who helped bring SmackDown to Fox walks in certainly gives WWE another situation to keep an eye on. title: There Is Only One Way Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton Can End Their Feud in WWE

body: The latest chapter of this rivalry began when Randy Orton returned at SummerSlam and hit Cody Rhodes with an RKO, preventing him from defeating CM Punk for the Undisputed WWE Championship. Orton later made it clear that he wanted to stop his former friend from winning another championship, giving The American Nightmare another reason to go after him. Since then, the two WWE Superstars have struggled to keep their emotions under control. Their showdown at Sunday Night's Main Event ended with The Viper bagging the W after playing mind games with Cody Rhodes. Rhodes’ hesitation when Orton appeared vulnerable also showed that their complicated history could still affect him inside the ring. And that is why the unforgiving structure of Hell in a Cell makes so much sense. The so-called devil’s playground will keep both men inside, making it harder for either superstar to escape when the action gets brutal. It would also allow WWE to pursue a different angle in the rivalry, with Rhodes forced to show how far he is willing to go to finally defeat his former mentor. The match should also come with one clear stipulation: the rivalry ends when the bell rings, regardless of who wins. That would give the result real meaning and prevent WWE from dragging the conflict into another premium live event.
summary: The latest chapter of this rivalry began when Randy Orton made a comeback at SummerSlam and hit Cody Rhodes with an RKO. Orton later made it clear that he wanted to stop his former friend from winning another championship, giving The American Nightmare another reason to go after him.

title: Chicago-area officer sues WWE, Montez Ford over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
raw_title: Chicago-area officer sues WWE, Montez Ford over alleged unwanted lap dance during Raw
body: A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE over an alleged incident during a live broadcast. CHICAGO - A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE, wrestler Montez Ford and an event production company, alleging he was subjected to unwanted sexualized contact while working security at a live wrestling event. Noel Lucas filed the lawsuit Wednesday in Cook County Circuit Court. The complaint says he was working an off-duty security job at WWE Monday Night Raw on July 6 at Allstate Arena in Rosemont. According to the lawsuit, Lucas was seated at his assigned post outside the ring when Ford, whose legal name is Kenneth Crawford, approached him, straddled him and began moving his hips in a sexually suggestive way. Lucas’ attorneys say he was not told he would be part of the performance and did not consent. Live announcers on the Netflix broadcast allegedly mocked Lucas in real time, telling viewers, "That guy clearly hates fun," and comparing him to Paul Blart, the fictional security guard from "Paul Blart: Mall Cop." "Mr. Lucas was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE’s entertainment," attorney Whitney Barr said in a statement. The incident aired live on Netflix. The lawsuit says WWE later shared video of it on TikTok and Instagram, where it received more than 300,000 views. Ford also shared footage, according to the lawsuit. The complaint includes 14 counts, including battery, assault, intentional infliction of emotional distress and claims under Illinois’ Gender Violence Act and Right of Publicity Act. "Entertainment is not a defense to unwanted sexual contact," Barr said. "We intend to hold WWE and those responsible accountable for what happened to Mr. Lucas and for the harm caused by the subsequent publication of the footage." The Source: The information in this story came from Chicago-based law firm Caffarelli & Martin Ltd. and Cook County court documents.
summary: The latest: a Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE over an alleged incident during a live broadcast. CHICAGO - A Cook County sheriff’s officer is suing WWE, wrestler Montez Ford and an event production company.

title: On the Record: Ex-WWE Referee Opens Up On How Valuable The Miz Truly is
raw_title: Ex-WWE Referee Reveals How Valuable The Miz Truly is
body: The former WWE referee was with the company when Miz first debuted. It is well-documented that the two-time WWE champion was not very popular in the locker room. Miz came from the world of reality TV, so he was already labeled an outsider before he debuted. He has opened up about being kicked out of the locker room for months before The Undertaker allowed him return. Despite his rocky start, Miz turned things around and has since become one of the longest-tenured superstars on the roster. Miz, 46, has main evented WrestleMania opposite John Cena and had memorable feuds with the likes of Daniel Bryan. He has also transitioned into film and television, while returning to his reality TV roots. Former WWE referee Jimmy Korderas says The Miz ‘s versatility as a performer makes him a valuable asset to the company. “People concentrate on the in-ring stuff and the moves, it’s not about the moves, it’s how you engage your audience and get them invested in you. Miz was able to, whether he was a babyface or a heel, because he was a babyface a few times, but his main deal is being a heel, that’s where he really excels. That’s his strength. That’s where I think people buy him more as a heel,” Korderas exclusively told Heavy Sports via T he Game Plan . “You need a guy to plug in anywhere. In a spot where you need comedy, he’s there because he can do it. You need a guy who can help get someone over, a young talent over, he’s the guy to put him in there with, because it’s still to this day, for a young talent, a big deal to beat The Miz.” The former WWE referee pointed to Miz’s track record and praised him for excelling wherever he is needed. “Eventually we saw it in The Miz. At first, he did generate a lot of heat from the locker room, and I hate to say it, it was pretty much deserved, because he did alienate some people in the wrong way. But he stayed the course, he learned, he developed. And he became not only a good hand, but one of the best ever utility players in wrestling, ever,” Korderas exclusively told Heavy Sports via The Game Plan .
