body: To work for the majors in North America is to c hase job security in an industry with almost none . At the very top, there are guaranteed contracts, reduced schedules, generous travel and accommodation offerings and a wealth of opportunities to earn money outside of wrestling to improve your negotiations to simply stay in it. In an era where television rights deals have replaced house show, merchandise and pay-per-view numbers as primary revenue drivers, wrestlers have theoretically never had less individual value, but the motivation to get to the very top is made clear by the cushy lives of those that occupy the best spots. The slope is slippery, and never is that clearer than when a wrestler has lost their spot before audiences have gotten used to them even getting it. Season Two's finale on August 31st 2010 very briefly profiled the women that would be competing the first all-female edition of the show, and very literally standing out amongst the newest chasing pack was new rookie "diva" Lindsay Kay Hayward. Known previously as "Isis The Amazon", she'd worked around 20 matches over two years en route to the market leader, so it wasn't as if the company were just taking a total punt on somebody with physical gifts. Nor would that be a new phenomenon for pro wrestling anyway - plenty of behemoths broke in simply because other wrestlers were taken with their size upon spotting them out and about somewhere or other. It was effectively "airport test" stuff, and the rebranded Aloisia had passed with flying colours just by standing there in the line-up . Why, then, was she nowhere to be found when the show started for real a week later? In storylines, her "pro" Vickie Guerrero had fired her due to supposed unhappiness with her efforts, but the reality was far harsher.

title: Samoa Joe rejects fear-based locker room leadership

body: Joe helped change what professional wrestling looked like in the 2000s alongside contemporaries like AJ Styles, Bryan Danielson and CM Punk. They helped revolutionize an independent wrestling movement, blending different elements into a hard-hitting style and proving you didn't need a bodybuilder physique to become a star. The former AEW world champion previously told CBS Sports that his current contract will "most likely" end in his retirement. He's already established an acting career, portraying Sweet Tooth in the television adaptation of "Twisted Metal" and lending his voice to various projects across film and video games. But before he walks away from wrestling, Joe wants to give back to the industry that has given him so much. Professional wrestling isn't particularly forgiving. The hours are brutal, the money isn't always good and backstage politics can be more exhausting than the matches. Joe doesn't have many horror stories to share. He's worked for practically every major wrestling promotion of the last 20 years, winning championships in TNA, WWE and AEW. He's chasing major accomplishments right up until the finish line. On Saturday, he and multiple wrestlers from different generations challenge AEW world champion Will Ospreay in a Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. "No great man is led by fear; usually they're led by people that they respect, find knowledgeable and give a shit about their opinion," Joe said. "You must first establish a basic respect and rapport with people. If they choose to respect and like you, and you find yourself in that position, then so be it. "But I think the idea of this physically domineering presence who will bury your career if you don't adhere to the unwritten book of laws is a ridiculous ideology. I've never come across it, and I've never felt pressured by that. I think it's a weird fallacy. I think a lot of people respect The Undertaker because they respect The Undertaker as a person, not out of career fear." "I think the adaptability and coordination are way better than they probably have been in years," Joe explained. "You get a lot of people who have more of a natural aptitude, but maybe less physical potential. I think that's kind of the best way to put it... I think the technicality probably is a lot higher than it's been." "Finding more ways to connect what they do with the crowd. That comes with time," Joe said. "I think any young generation suffers from that. I don't think it's particularly unique to any particular young generation. It's probably one of the biggest things: as time goes on, you become more confident, calmer, and more poised in the presence of a large crowd. You begin to interact with them on a different level; you begin to read them and understand their vibe and how to get them going at a different level." raw_title: Exclusive: Kevin Knight names AEW’s most underrated men and women wrestlers
body: Former AEW TNT and Trios Champion, Kevin Knight, is currently one of the most talked-about names in the pro-wrestling industry. Just days before his scheduled WrestleDream tag team championship match against The Young Bucks, Knight sat down for an exclusive interview with ClutchPoints. "Oof, that's a great question 'cause there are a lot of people. I'ma start on the women's side. The women are so talented, like, so talented. I really like Red Velvet and her energy that she brings. Her and Zayda Steel. I think Zayda Steel is a great prospect. She's doing her thing. She has great charisma, great energy, and I feel like when the time comes, she's gonna shine. "The roster is vast, and she's still very new, you know, learning her chops and everything, but once she's ready, both of them, Red Velvet and Zayda Steel, I think they'll shine on television," Knight added. He further shared the MXM Collection as the underrated duo of the men's division. "As for the men's side, there are so many. Me personally, I'm a big fan of MXM Collection. I feel like they bring a different energy to the AEW locker room. Very entertaining, very fashionable, very different, and I think they will shine. I think they do shine each and every time they're on TV, so I think with more opportunities, they're gonna make the most of it." Red Velvet was last seen on AEW during the Jun. 17, 2026 edition of Collision. However, she continues to actively wrestle on ROH. Quite new to AEW, Zayda Steel last wrestled Thekla on AEW Collision back in Sept. 2026, and her latest match dates back to the Sept. 28, 2026 edition of ROH. Mansoor and Mason Madden last teamed up with Johnny TV on the Sept. 28, 2026 edition of ROH as MXM TV. "For me personally, it's Arena Coliseo. Everybody talks about Arena Mexico in Mexico, but what's really popping is Arena Coliseo, in Mexico City. It's like a little smaller, a little bit more grungier. But just the energy in that stadium is so peak; it's so top tier, you have no other option but to show out each and every time. So I love Arena Coliseo, out in Mexico City. The energy is unmatched, unmatched," he shared. Knight had teamed up with "Speedball" Mike Bailey during his match in Mexico City's Arena Coliseo. However, that tag team, JetSpeed, is now over, and Knight now finds himself in a new alliance with Kyle Fletcher. Discussing the differences between the two teams, Knight claimed that his tag teams have always been with people with whom he won't hang out in real life. "It's funny because all of my tag team partners have been people that in my normal life, in my regular life, I would not hang out with them or, like, spend extra time with them or anything like that. But once we get into the ring, that bond is 100% there, whether that's with Kushida, Speedball, or Fletcher. "It's‌ still a little early with Fletcher. We've been tagging for what? About two months, you know, on and off. But we definitely have a great chemistry that's grown on camera," he added

title: On the Record: AEW Rumor Opens Up On Who Was Originally Set for Clockwork Carnage Instead of Adam Copeland
raw_title: AEW Rumor Reveals Who Was Originally Set for Clockwork Carnage Instead of Adam Copeland
body: The Observer also noted that Christian Cage was seriously injured at the same show. With Cage sidelined, the tag team of Copeland and Christian is being put on hold, and the report said it made sense to move Copeland into the Clockwork Carnage match. White teamed with The Bang Bang Gang in a three-team match against the Death Riders and The Dogs on the All Out Tailgate Brawl pre-show. Tony Schiavone announced on the October 3 episode of AEW Collision that White would be out for a month or two. The nature of the injury has not been made public. Copeland addressed his partner’s condition after beating Josh Alexander in a Clockwork Carnage qualifying match on Wednesday’s edition of AEW Dynamite. He told the crowd, “What we didn’t know is that he ended up breaking three ribs. One rib broken in three places.” He also said of Cage, “Yet, at the end, he was standing on top of those ladders reaching for our tag-team championships.” Clockwork Carnage is a new match type for AEW. Two wrestlers start, and another enters every three minutes until all eight have entered. Anyone pinned or forced to submit before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last man enters, the match becomes a 15-minute Iron Man match, and whoever has the most falls when time expires leaves with the AEW World Championship. Champion Will Ospreay defends the title against Samoa Joe, “Speedball” Mike Bailey, Copeland, Konosuke Takeshita, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet and Darby Allin. Copeland, Takeshita, Okada, Ricochet and Allin all earned their places with wins on Dynamite. For White, the timing is unfortunate. He was in line for a spot in a world title match on a major show, and a one- to two-month absence means he will likely miss most of the fall. When he returns, AEW will need to find something comparable for him, especially since the report indicates he was part of the plans at the top of the card.

title: Max Caster Fired By TNA Over Riyadh Rap
raw_title: Max Caster Fired By TNA After Controversial Riyadh Rap At Bound For Glory
body: On October 11, Caster made a surprise appearance at TNA Wrestling's "Bound For Glory" event, answering a open challenge from former champion Moose. It wasn't long before the debuting talent took the microphone to deliver a scorchingly hot introduction: " I drop bombs. You don't even have to fly to Riyadh (Saudi Arabia)" For those who missed it in the world news, that city's international airport has recently been the target of several enemy missile attacks. Shortly after the conclusion of the event, TNA President Carlos Silva released the following statement on Twitter/X: Kind of a "raw" deal for someone making his company debut, don't you think? When it comes to wrestling, firing people up with controversial remarks isn't exactly the newest thing under the sun. For years, some of the industry's biggest names have routinely crossed the line of good taste, all to provoke a reaction from the viewing audience. In 1997, Booker T of WCW (World Championship Wrestling) infamously remarked, " Hulk Hogan, we coming for you (n-word expletive)!" During WWE's "Attitude Era", D-Generation X frequently told viewers to do something that you might do to a lollipop. And in a now-legendary rant delivered in 2011, CM Punk had this to say: " I'd like to think that maybe this company will be better after Vince McMahon's dead ". Yet except for actions taken as part of on-screen storylines, the performers involved have not been subject to any real-world repercussions. That's because scandal is part of the game; to quote Eric Bischoff, "controversy creates cash". Speaking of which, Caster has an interesting assemblage of characters in his corner right now. Coming to the defense of the embattled wrestler is no less than the "Louisville Slugger" himself; Mr. James E. Cornette. Never one to be at a loss for words, Cornette didn't hold back when offering his opinion on the current situation. " Max does have a history of being edgy. So, hear the promo. And there's nothing else that's an issue. He didn't say (blank). He didn't violate any broadcast standards. Who produced the thing? If he told him one thing and did another, well then all the heat's on Max. But for trivial BS like this that could have been easily addressed before it became an issue, I don't understand how this happens. " The legendary manager and promoter makes a solid point here. TNA President Carlos Silva and other upper management should've have known the score; if they didn't want to use the "bleep button", then perhaps they shouldn't have given Caster a live microphone. One day after Caster's abrupt release, the rising star made his first public statement about the situation, according to Sportskeeda . " I want to say thank you to Carlos Silva. I talked to him in person. He was very generous, very professional, even after all this stuff happened. And I understand why he did what he did. It's his show. He's got to protect TNA. And I went too far for him. So I want to apologize to him and everybody else in
summary: Max Caster made a surprise debut at TNA's Bound For Glory on October 11 by answering Moose's open challenge and delivered a controversial rap referencing recent missile attacks on Riyadh's airport. TNA President Carlos Silva quickly issued a statement announcing Caster's termination from the company following the segment. The incident has sparked discussion about boundary-pushing promos in wrestling, similar to past examples from stars like Booker T, D-Generation X and CM Punk.

title: TNA Pulled Moose vs Max Caster Match After Saudi Rap
raw_title: TNA Reportedly Wanted Former WWE Star Sheamus To Debut At Bound For Glory
body: Never one to be coy for his daring promos in the form of raps, the former World Tag Team and Trios Champion tried his luck again in a new setting; however, his line of, "This the firing squad, I drop bombs, you don't even have to fly to Riyadh," sent the promotion in a tizzy since its promotional partner WWE remains set on traveling to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in three weeks for its Crown Jewel PLE, despite recent airstrikes at the King Khalid International Airport. Unhappy with the unscripted and unapproved line, TNA executives made the decision to pull any and all mentions of Moose and Caster's match off its official social media platforms and YouTube. Soon after the event, Caster released a statement across his social media platforms, issuing apologies to TNA, its president Carlos Silva (who he said was very generous and professional even after the fact), his opponent Moose, and to the general public for his wrongdoings.
summary: Max Caster delivered an unapproved rap line referencing Saudi Arabia during a TNA segment, angering executives because of the promotion's partnership with WWE ahead of the Crown Jewel event in Riyadh. The company quickly removed all mentions of the Moose versus Caster match from its social media and YouTube channels. Caster later issued a public apology to TNA, president Carlos Silva, Moose and fans.

body: According to Fightful Select , former WWE United States Champion Ilja Dragunov has officially put pen to paper with All Elite Wrestling after sorting out his visa situation . The outlet also confirmed that the mysterious vignette aired on Wednesday's special episode of "AEW Collision" belongs to Dragunov. The 22-second footage showed a sharply dressed man walking around a nighttime location as classical music played and a metronome ticked back and forth. Dragunov departed WWE over the summer after opting not to renew his contract. It is unknown if his subsequent AEW debut will take place at this weekend's WrestleDream pay-per-view or elsewhere. Another name linked to AEW recently is former WWE Women's Tag Team Champion Kairi Sane, who exited the company in the midst of a mass talent release in April 2026. Sane and AEW officials reportedly have engaged in discussions about potentially bringing "The Pirate Princess" aboard there next, but as of this week, Fightful Select has indicated that no deal has been reached. Sane has history with the reigning AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Mone, having wrestled each other in WWE and New Japan Pro-Wrestling. At WrestleDream, Mone will defend the AEW Women's Title against "The Toxic Spider" Thekla, another former opponent of Sane's. title: Roman Reigns Discusses Acting Transition on SiriusXM
raw_title: ROMAN REIGNS AND MORE TALK 'STREET FIGHTER' ON SIRIUSXM SPECIAL
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game ROMAN REIGNS AND MORE TALK 'STREET FIGHTER' ON SIRIUSXM SPECIAL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 07:30:00 SiriusXM issued the following: SiriusXM Front Row special w/ Roman Reigns and the Cast of "Street Fighter" The cast of the upcoming “Street Fighter” movie recently joined Sam Roberts for a special SiriusXM Front Row event on the WWE Radio channel, where stars 50 Cent, Roman Reigns, Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, and Callina Liang discussed their experiences filming the movie, behind-the-scenes moments, and the camaraderie among the cast. Roman Reigns spoke about making the transition from WWE to acting, and the difference in dynamics between being on a movie set and working with actors, versus working/competing in the world of pro wrestling. Noah Centineo talks about Marky Mark and Jake Paul being inspirations he drew from for his character in the film, Ken Masters. The cast also shares fun behind-the-scenes stories about 50 Cent buying out Luna Park for the entire cast and crew to build camaraderie, and more. Sam Roberts: How do you wrap your head around commanding that attention when you’re shooting scenes, it’s a movie, it’s not like getting into a wrestling ring and feeling 20,000 people around you. And, number two, making it different than Roman Reigns. Akuma is very different, even in the way you use your body, very different than what Roman Reigns does. Roman Reigns: The main parallel for me, especially in this movie, my main contributions were in the third act. So it’s in the main event of the movie is what I was telling myself. And that’s what I practice, is main event performance. That’s my bag. That’s what I do when it’s my time to go out there and wrestle. So I just try to keep that type of weight on it. The stakes are as high as can be so you need to be able to come in and match what everybody’s done. … These guys know what they’re doing. I'm not a real actor. I go out and I wrestle. It really helped me to see what they have done and the way they led the film. It set the tone for what needed to be matched. It wasn't easy, but there were a bunch of things I was able to rely on from wrestling to help me take this on. Sam Roberts: You've also evolved your performance as a wrestler, I think, further than a lot of traditional wrestlers and WWE Superstars do, in terms of the stories that you actively tell with your face. Bringing the audience on that ride, is that something that translates into film? Is that something you bring over here and maybe then bring something from here back to how Roman Reigns is portrayed? title: End of an Era: Samoa Joe Wants to “Sprinkle a Little Bit Back” Before Retirement
raw_title: Samoa Joe Wants to “Sprinkle a Little Bit Back” Before Retirement
summary_src: Samoa Joe knows the clock is ticking on his wrestling career, and he’s already thinking about what he wants to leave behind before he finally calls it quits.
body: While speaking with CBS Sports , Joe reflected on the final stage of his career and made it clear that his focus is shifting toward giving something back to the wrestling business that gave him so much over nearly three decades. Joe explained that his career has taken him all over the world, introduced him to countless people and given him experiences he never expected when he first broke into professional wrestling. “Really, it was this grand adventure that I got to meet a ton of cool people and go to a ton of cool places and learn to love the world, which is a rare opportunity.” Joe said traveling for wrestling also gave him a different perspective on the world and the people in it. “If anybody ever gets to literally travel the world and understand that, it’s a beautiful place. There are a lot of places that have a lot of love for you, as long as you have the best intentions.” That is a big reason why Joe doesn’t seem interested in spending the final chapter of his career chasing recognition or acting like the business still owes him something. Instead, he’s thinking about how he can give some of that experience back before he’s done. Joe summed up his mindset with one line that says a lot about where his head is at right now. “I like to sprinkle a little bit back before I’m done and hopefully leave the pro wrestling industry a much better place than I found it.” Samoa Joe still has plenty left to do inside the ring, but it’s obvious he’s already thinking beyond wins, losses and championships. Before the curtain comes down, he wants to make sure he leaves something behind for the people who come next. What do you think about Samoa Joe wanting to give back to wrestling before retirement? Do you think his influence on younger talent could end up being just as important as his in-ring career? Let us know what you think. title: WWE questions Sami Zayn’s actions following recent altercation
raw_title: WWE questions Sami Zayn’s actions following recent altercation
summary_src: Sami Zayn is currently in his second reign as the Undisputed WWE Champion. This has made him the target for many superstars on the SmackDown roster, including Kevin Owens.
body: WWE began its Road to Survivor Series: WarGames 2026 live event series on Thursday, October 15, with a house show at Canada Life Centre in Winnipeg, Manitoba. The event featured some blockbuster matches, including Sami Zayn defending his title against his former friend Kevin Owens. Sami managed to retain the gold. However, his actions before the bell have raised questions within WWE. Owens was holding a mic and started by saying he wanted to kick Zayn’s a**. But then he cut himself off, stepped in, and condescendingly fixed the champion's s hair while saying, “Now you look good." That immediately p*ssed Sami Zayn off. He got visibly angry and moved toward Owens, but a referee stepped in to stop the confrontation from getting physical. The incident reportedly prompted WWE officials to ask Zayn why he was upset, suggesting Owens had only been trying to help. That said, with the first episode of Friday Night SmackDown after Money in the Bank a few hours away, it will be interesting if the feud between the former friends continues. Sami Zayn is set to go one-on-one against Roman Reigns in a Champion vs. Champion match for the Men's Crown Jewel Championship. The bout is scheduled for Saturday, November 7, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Last Saturday at Money in the Bank, the OTC successfully defended his World Heavyweight Championship against LA Knight. He now looks towards locking horns with his former Bloodline member, Sami, with the Men's Crown Jewel Championship on the line. Sami Zayn joined Roman Reigns and The Bloodline in 2022, earning the honorary title of Honorary Uce. He became close to the family, especially Jey Uso. However, Roman’s manipulation and constant disrespect troubled him. Sami finally turned against the OTC at the 2023 Royal Rumble, refusing to attack Kevin Owens. Hoping to end Roman Reigns' dominant reign, Sami challenged Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Championship at Elimination Chamber 2023. Sadly, he was unable to end the champion's dominant reign. With the duo set to go one-on-one again, it will be interesting to see if Zayn will secure a victory over Roman Reigns.

title: Match Made: 4 Reasons why CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes at WrestleMania 43 would be a bad idea
raw_title: 4 Reasons why CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes at WrestleMania 43 would be a bad idea
summary_src: CM Punk vs. Cody Rhodes is reportedly one of the matches being considered for WrestleMania 43.
body: However, while this match may sound exciting on paper, it might be a bad idea to book it for WrestleMania 43 for these four reasons. CM Punk and Cody Rhodes have already faced each other in a high-profile singles match at SummerSlam 2026. A rematch at WrestleMania 43 would therefore revisit a matchup WWE has already presented on a major stage. The two stars could still cross paths again in the future. However, WWE would benefit from giving them different opponents for now, allowing both men to develop new rivalries before revisiting their previous encounter. Both CM Punk and Cody Rhodes already had prominent roles at WrestleMania 42. The Second City Saint main-evented the second night against Roman Reigns , while The American Nightmare headlined the first night against Randy Orton. Rhodes retained the Undisputed WWE Championship, while Reigns defeated Punk to win the World Heavyweight Championship. Much of Cody Rhodes ' recent WWE run has revolved around the Undisputed WWE Championship. His pursuit of the title and subsequent reign have been central to his character since returning to the company. The American Nightmare has already achieved his goal of becoming the face of WWE, and another title-focused WrestleMania program may not be the most interesting next step. Rhodes does not necessarily need to remain in the world-title picture to stay relevant. WWE could use the coming months to establish a fresh direction for him, giving another star the chance to enter the championship scene. CM Punk remains one of WWE's most established performers, but WrestleMania 43 could provide an opportunity to elevate a younger star by having him defeat The Second City Saint on the grandest stage. Bron Breakker is one potential opponent. The Dog of WWE challenged Punk for the World Heavyweight Championship on the January 5, 2026 episode of RAW after pinning him during the Men's WarGames Match. Breakker pushed the champion to his limit, but Punk ultimately retained after countering a Spear attempt and connecting with the Go to Sleep. Breakker has the physical ability and intensity to headline major events, and another match against Punk would give WWE a chance to revisit their earlier encounter with higher stakes. If Punk holds a world championship again by WrestleMania season, the former NXT Champion could challenge him for the title and finally score a decisive victory. That would give Breakker a significant career milestone while allowing Punk to help establish another leading star.

title: John Cena Explains Benefits of WWE's PG Era
raw_title: John Cena Weighs In On WWE’s Move to PG, How It Helped Them Globally
body: Cena reflected on the move to PG in his appearance on What Now? With Trevor Noah. You can see the highlights below: “I think it’s — it was billed as real. It rebranded itself, and when you rebrand it takes 10, 15 years to get over. We got over, and I was happy to be involved in a lot of that rebranding process.” “Well, here’s the good thing about PG: you can ship it anywhere. A lot of countries won’t take PG-13 or MA content. If they know it’s PG, now we can go global. That takes time. But after like 15 years of doing that, everybody’s like, ‘Yeah, I watch the wrestling.’ And I will say the success of content creators. So you know, 2008, people started posting on social media, the advent of Instagram and the success of YouTube. “It used to be like, you were in movies or you were in television, you were an actor. You played pure sport, you were an athlete. Wrestlers were none of that, they’re just carnies. Like, we used to be just carny folk. And then everybody started making content, and there became multiple lanes to success. Multiple lanes to relevancy, to resource. So it’s like, ‘Oh man, these people have a voice, and they have influence.’ WWE was on the cusp of all that, and our social accounts are off the charts. Our audience is super engaging. You can’t ignore the math. You can’t ignore the data. It also became okay to be in the crowd for a wrestling match. It used to be a thing of, ‘I’ve seen it, but I don’t watch that stuff.’ And now it’s like, ‘I’m going.’”
summary: John Cena discussed WWE's shift to a PG rating during an appearance on What Now? With Trevor Noah. He noted the rebranding process took over a decade to gain acceptance and enabled the company to distribute content worldwide since many countries reject PG-13 or MA material. Cena also highlighted how the rise of social media and content creation around 2008 helped elevate wrestlers beyond their previous carny image, leading to massive audience engagement and influence for WWE.

llm_long: John Cena discussed the advantages of WWE's shift to a PG rating during an appearance on What Now? With Trevor Noah. He noted that the product was initially presented as authentic and required 10 to 15 years to gain acceptance after rebranding, adding that he was pleased to participate in much of that process.

Cena highlighted that PG content can be distributed worldwide because many countries reject PG-13 or MA material, enabling WWE to expand globally over time. After approximately 15 years of this approach, audiences broadly accepted wrestling, with Cena pointing to the rise of content creators as a key factor.

He explained that in 2008, the growth of social media, Instagram, and YouTube created new pathways to success, moving wrestlers beyond their previous image as mere carnival performers. Wrestlers gained recognition as having voices and influence, similar to actors and athletes, which opened multiple avenues for relevance and resources.

Cena stated that WWE was at the forefront of these changes, resulting in exceptionally strong social media accounts and highly engaged audiences that cannot be overlooked based on the data. He observed that attending live wrestling events has become socially acceptable, shifting from past attitudes where people admitted seeing it but denied following it to openly declaring their attendance.

title: AEW Collision Draws 372K Viewers on October 10

summary_src: Viewership for "AEW Collision Grand Slam: France" on October 10 was down slightly in viewership compared to the previous week's episode.
body: According to Wrestlenomics , the October 10 edition of "Collision" drew 372,000 average viewers, down 10 percent from the previous week's 415,000 viewers . The episode was also down in the rating for the ever-important ages 18-49 demographic, earning a 0.04 for the week, down 50 percent compared to the previous episode's 0.08 rating. Viewership was up two percent compared to the trailing four weeks average of 365,000 viewers, however. Compared to this time last year, "Collision's" average viewership, 394,000 at this point of the month, is up 53 percent compared to the October 2025 average of 257,000 viewers. The main event of "Collision Grand Slam: France" saw the Young Bucks successfully defend their AEW World Tag Team Championships against The Dogs' David Finlay and Clark Connors. After Matt and Nick Jackson's victory, they were taken out by their WrestleDream opponents, the Don Callis Family's Kevin Knight and Kyle Fletcher. Elsewhere on the show, Andrade El Idolo defended his AEW National Championship against Michael Oku, and Swerve Strickland defeated Carlie Bravo. The episode also saw a Clockwork Carnage match qualifier ahead of WrestleDream , with "Speedball" Mike Bailey earning his way into the match with a victory over Lee Moriarty.

title: William Regal Urges Aggressive Pins and Kickouts
raw_title: William Regal Advises Wrestlers To 'Kick Out Like Your Life And Career Depend On It'
summary_src: William Regal offers advice to wrestlers regarding pins and kickouts. Over the course of his career, William Regal worked with countless talents in WWE and WCW. While he retired from in-ring competition back in 2013, Regal still remains active in the business.
body: William Regal shares advice to wrestlers regarding pins and kickouts. Over the course of his career, William Regal worked with countless talents in WWE and WCW. While he retired from in-ring competition back in 2013, Regal still remains active in the business. He’s currently working as the Vice President of Global Talent Development in WWE after returning to the company back in 2023. On social media , Regal recently shared advice with current wrestlers. He asked them to make every pin and kick out “like your life and career depend on it.” “I work for WWE but watch a lot of wrestling worldwide. This goes for all wrestlers in all companies. I have worked in Wrestling for 42 years. An observation. We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts ( even comedy bouts). If you don’t win you would make less money in the story we’re telling. Every TV bout , if there’s a pin, the cameras focus in. Please pin and kick out like your life and career depend on it. In story, it does. I’ve also been a part of knowing most talent since the 2000’s in many companies. As time goes by younger talent copy their favourite of film. I recently watch AJ Styles v Amazing Red from the early 2000’s. I see how many people copied them. What I saw was every pin was aggressively applied and shoulders covered and stacked. Every kick out they kicked out like their life depended on it. Something has been lost in the last 20 + years. Let’s not insult the intelligence of our audience who are giving us their precious time. In a fight scene in a movie ( which is what wrestling is) we know the punches don’t really hit but if we saw that we would eventually stop watching it. Your audience and fans deserve better. If you can’t be uncomfortable for a few seconds being stacked up in a pin, maybe this isn’t for you.” I work for WWE but watch a lot of wrestling worldwide. This goes for all wrestlers in all companies. I have worked in Wrestling for 42 years. An observation. We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts ( even comedy bouts). If you don’t win you would make less money in…
summary: William Regal, WWE Vice President of Global Talent Development, advised wrestlers across all promotions to treat every pin and kickout with maximum intensity as if their life and career depend on it. The 42-year veteran emphasized that in the story being told, wrestlers are trained fighters whose instincts and financial outcomes hinge on these moments, with cameras capturing every detail on TV. He noted that younger performers often emulate past matches like early 2000s AJ Styles versus Amazing Red, where pins were applied with strong shoulder coverage.

llm_long: All Elite Wrestling has updated the poster for its Full Gear 2026 event as a tribute to the late PAC, whose real name was Benjamin Satterly. The updated poster includes a Black Arrow Warning sign featuring a sketch of PAC performing the move, along with his signature chair and towel.

Black arrows have been added to the Full Gear cog and the Arizona desert backdrop on the poster. PAC inspired the Full Gear name after showing up in his wrestling trunks and boots at AEW’s February 2019 launch rally in Jacksonville to confront Hangman Adam Page while others wore business attire.

The incident was later used as a segment on Being the Elite during PAC and Page’s feud. At the inaugural Full Gear event in November 2019, Page defeated PAC in a singles match. PAC defeated Darby Allin at the 2025 edition of Full Gear.

PAC died suddenly on September 27 at the age of 40, one day after competing at All Out in Illinois, with his cause of death still pending additional testing after an initial autopsy. AEW’s next pay-per-view, WrestleDream, is set for October 17, after which the Full Gear 2026 build will intensify.

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game WWE, MONTEZ FORD SUED OVER WWE RAW 'LAPDANCE' By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 08:45:00 ???????? pic.twitter.com/T6pdOoR20q PostWrestling.com in Canada reported yesterday that Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas is suing WWE, Montez Ford of the Street Profits tag team and WWE subsidiary Event Services, LLC, over an alleged unwanted sexualized dance during the 7/6 episode of WWE Monday Night Raw, which was broadcast from the Chicago area at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. Lucas was working off-duty security when, according to the lawsuit, Ford approached him during the Street Profits’ entrance and performed a sexually suggestive dance (embedded above) involving hip thrusts and gyrating without his consent. Lucas alleges that footage of the incident spread widely across social media, including on WWE’s and Ford’s accounts, making him recognizable to the public. He also alleges that his children were ridiculed at school because of the video, causing him significant humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress. The lawsuit includes 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act, and unlawful use of his image under the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas is seeking monetary and punitive damages, legal costs, and an order preventing WWE and Ford from using his identity. Neither WWE nor Ford have responded to the lawsuit as of yesterday. body: WrestleDream will set out to launch a new concept with the hope that the stipulation and eight of its top performers will be a recipe for pay-per-view success. The Clockwork Carnage, an idea of Will Ospreay’s tried out by EVE, is the foundational selling point of Saturday’s pay-per-view. Ospreay will defend the title over a thirty-three-minute layout against Kazuchika Okada, Konosuke Takeshita, Samoa Joe, Speedball Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Darby Allin, and Adam Copeland. The first fifteen minutes are treated like a Casino Gauntlet where new entrants arrive every three minutes with the possibility of eliminations during the period. Once the fifteen minutes are up, a second 15:00 period begins, and it becomes an Iron Survival or Scramble match where the most falls win during the allotted time. The match quality is less a concern than its marketability as the crux of a $39.99 pay-per-view. They are returning to pay-per-view three weeks after All Out and with a truncated time to promote after the tragedy of Pac’s death and dedicating its September 30 episode to Ben Satterley. The week after was Grand Slam France, which was its own mini-PPV on its own and the eight participants for the main event for WrestleDream weren’t known until the closing moments of Wednesday’s “go home” program. It’s similar for the next pay-per-view cycle as Blood & Guts on November 4 will serve as its own major show, ten days before Full Gear. Unlike many AEW events over the past year, there is no WWE or NXT competition or a battle in the Orlando market as All Out had in Chicago. On Friday, the WrestleTix figure has topped 6,000 tickets distributed to the Addition Financial Arena in Orlando. Its last pay-per-view in the venue was Worlds End, finishing at 6,651 in December 2024, a number within shooting distance by showtime. Boeing Center at Tech Port is the venue for the show. ROHFinalBattle will be in San Antonio on 12/4!” Khan tweeted . “After a tremendous #ROHDBD ppv, I can’t wait for Final Battle!” Athena, Bandido, Mistico, Mascara Dorada, Lee Moriarty, and Deonna Purrazzo are featured on the poster for the show. They all currently hold gold in ROH, with Athena and Bandido being the women’s and men’s World Champions. Final Battle has been an ROH end-of-year tradition for more than two decades. The 2025 edition took place in Columbus, Ohio and was headlined by Athena defeating Persephone to retain the ROH Women’s World Championship. Athena’s title reign began at Final Battle 2022. If she’s able to defeat whoever her 2026 challenger ends up being, she will reach four years as champion. At Death Before Dishonor this August, Athena and Bandido made respective defenses against Hazuki and Nick Wayne. title: William Regal urges wrestlers to pin and kick out harder
raw_title: William Regal offers advice to wrestlers: ‘Your audience and fans deserve better’
summary_src: On social media today, WWE employee William Regal sent out a message pointing out one thing he would like to see today’s wrestlers improve on. Regal advised wrestlers, no matter where they’re working around the globe, to pin and kick out as if their lives depended on it.
body: On social media today, WWE employee William Regal sent out a message pointing out one thing he would like to see today’s wrestlers improve on. Regal advised wrestlers, no matter where they’re working around the globe, to pin and kick out as if their lives depended on it. Wrestling matches should resemble fight scenes, and Regal thinks the audience deserves better than some of the pins and kickouts he’s been seeing. Regal recently rewatched an AJ Styles vs. Amazing Red match from the 2000s where “every pin was aggressively applied and shoulders covered and stacked.” That art has largely been lost over the past couple of decades, Regal believes. The 58-year-old Regal has made similar posts in the past, particularly in regards to wrestler safety. His quality of life is still affected to this day due to the damage he took in his own in-ring career, and Regal has advised talent against doing “stupid” moves where they land on their heads. Regal also praised Roman Reigns last month for the “masterful” job he did in his match against Penta on WWE Raw. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: WWE's William Regal posted on social media urging wrestlers worldwide to treat every pin and kickout with maximum intensity as if their lives depended on it. He compared matches to fight scenes and said audiences deserve better than what many are currently delivering. Regal cited a rewatched 2000s bout between AJ Styles and Amazing Red where every pin was applied aggressively with full shoulder coverage as an example of the lost art.

title: On the Record: William Regal Warns Wrestlers They’re Risking Fans’ Trust by Making Matches Look Less Believable
raw_title: William Regal Warns Wrestlers They’re Risking Fans’ Trust by Making Matches Look Less Believable
summary_src: William Regal thinks wrestling has a credibility problem, and this time his concern is not about ratings, booking, or which company is winning the weekly argument. He is talking about the audience itself, and he believes wrestlers are giving fans too many reasons to stop buying into what they see.
body: “I work for WWE but watch a lot of wrestling worldwide. This goes for all wrestlers in all companies. I have worked in Wrestling for 42 years. An observation.” Regal’s biggest issue is the way wrestlers handle pins and kickouts. In his view, if the audience is supposed to believe these performers are trained fighters, then every cover should look like somebody is desperately trying to win, and every kickout should look like somebody is desperately trying to survive. “We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts (even comedy bouts). If you don’t win you would make less money in the story we’re telling. Every TV bout, if there’s a pin, the cameras focus in. Please pin and kick out like your life and career depend on it. In story, it does.” “I recently watch AJ Styles v Amazing Red from the early 2000’s. I see how many people copied them. What I saw was every pin was aggressively applied and shoulders covered and stacked. Every kick out they kicked out like their life depended on it.” “Something has been lost in the last 20 + years. Let’s not insult the intelligence of our audience who are giving us their precious time.” “In a fight scene in a movie (which is what wrestling is) we know the punches don’t really hit but if we saw that we would eventually stop watching it.” That is where Regal’s message got even more direct. In his mind, fans are already giving wrestlers something valuable every time they tune in: their time. He does not think performers should repay that by getting lazy with the details that are supposed to make the whole thing work. Regal then finished with a line that was basically a challenge to anybody who does not want to put in the effort to make those moments look convincing. “If you can’t be uncomfortable for a few seconds being stacked up in a pin, maybe this isn’t for you.” Regal’s message was not complicated. Fans know what wrestling is, but they still want to believe while they are watching it. If the wrestlers stop making the little things look important, Regal thinks the audience will eventually stop treating the big things like they matter too. What do you think about William Regal warning wrestlers not to insult the audience’s intelligence? Do you think modern wrestling has gotten too loose with the small details that keep fans invested? Leave your feedback below. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: The latest: an observation. Regal’s biggest issue is the way wrestlers handle pins and kickouts. If the wrestlers stop making the little things look important, Regal thinks the audience will eventually stop treating the big things like they matter too.

title: On the Record: Will Ospreay Responds to Constant Questions About Leaving AEW for WWE
raw_title: Will Ospreay Responds to Constant Questions About Leaving AEW for WWE
summary_src: Will Ospreay keeps getting asked the same question about WWE, and at this point, he knows it’s just part of being one of wrestling’s biggest names. But if fans are waiting for him to start teasing some big jump away from AEW, they’re probably not going to get much from him right now. Speaking to ...
body: Speaking to Brandon Kravitz , Ospreay was directly asked whether he’s getting tired of constantly hearing questions about WWE and the possibility that he’ll eventually leave AEW. Ospreay isn’t losing sleep over it because he understands those questions simply come with the territory. “Uh, it’s — I just, I know it’s a part of the gig. Like, people always ask, and, like, I can only give my opinion. I don’t really care about it.” That doesn’t mean Ospreay is secretly sitting around thinking about his next move either. As far as he’s concerned, his attention is on AEW and what he can accomplish with the company he’s already working for. “Like, it’s just — I’d rather focus on AEW, and I’d rather focus on, like, what we’re able to do here.” Ospreay then made it pretty clear why he’s so invested in AEW. He believes the company is actively changing professional wrestling, and he’s proud of what it puts in front of fans. “And, like, what I believe AEW is, is changing the face of professional wrestling. And I love what we present. I love what we do. I love our wrestling. I love everything that, like, we’re all about.” And when it comes to worrying about what WWE or anybody else is doing, Ospreay doesn’t sound particularly interested. His answer couldn’t have been much clearer about where his priorities are right now. “So, like, I couldn’t really care less about any other promotion.” The conversation then shifted to the never-ending comparison between wrestling companies and whether that constant AEW-versus-WWE debate actually hurts the business. Ospreay didn’t blame fans for doing it or turn the question into another promotional war, instead treating it as something wrestlers simply have to deal with. “It’s just part of the game, boss. Like, you just got to learn to take it.” H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Speaks On Rumors He’s Joining the MCU After Marvel Meeting
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Addresses Rumors He’s Joining the MCU After Marvel Meeting
summary_src: Cody Rhodes knows people want answers about that mysterious Marvel meeting, but he’s not giving them anything. In fact, the former Undisputed WWE Champion says people have been throwing potential characters at him all day, and he’s refusing to confirm whether any of those guesses are even close.
body: “You know, there’s one guy in particular who was sitting next to me on this couch pretty much all day who is teasing things that aren’t real — and if they were real, I wouldn’t say anything — and guessing characters that are great, great characters.” That’s about as much as Cody was willing to give away. Even if somebody happened to correctly guess what was discussed during the meeting, he made it pretty clear he wouldn’t be the guy confirming it. Marvel isn’t exactly unfamiliar territory for Cody either. He explained that his connection to those characters goes all the way back to childhood, when trading cards and the animated series basically became his Marvel education. “Because I grew up — I mean, I learned every Marvel character you could from the trading cards, and then, of course, I had the animated series, and we have it again now.” For all the speculation surrounding the meeting, Cody pointed out that he hasn’t actually said much about what happened behind those doors. All he’s publicly acknowledged is that he visited the Marvel offices, met with people there and took a photo afterwards. “It’s been heavily discussed, but I never discuss it. That’s the beauty. I’ve said nothing other than that was just a photo at a wonderful office after a wonderful meeting with wonderful people.” “Yeah, it is, really. And also the whole history — if they had said to you, ‘Hey, this character,’ something like that, and you go in there, there’s a whole library. You could take 30 minutes and go, ‘Got it. Know it.’ You know?” That doesn’t mean Cody just confirmed Marvel offered him a role, and he was careful to frame the whole thing as a hypothetical. Still, he clearly knows exactly how much attention that meeting has received, and he’s having no problem keeping everyone guessing. body: While we are still six months from the 2027 edition of the "showcase of the immortals," the WWE has long tried to plan its top matches for the event well in advance. That tradition returned to being the norm once company legend Triple H officially took over the creative direction a few years ago. In a new report from the industry insider , Oba Femi vs. Roman Reigns is still penciled in as one of the main events. That claim would align with reports in recent months that the brand was eyeing a showdown between its biggest and hottest stars. However, the other match may be a letdown for fans, and that allegedly will be a rematch between Cody Rhodes and CM Punk . Finding out that WWE is thinking about going back to the Rhodes and Punk well will probably get a sigh from a good number of fans. While the build-up to their match at SummerSlam was solid, the bout itself underwhelmed. Especially when compared to the other headliner of the two-night event, Reigns vs. Seth Rollins. Yes, both men are two of the most popular stars on the roster, but why would the company want to rehash a rivalry that did not deliver epic moments? Well, that may be because they are planning something major to come before or during the rematch. It is possible that WWE is considering a heel turn for either man. For a few months, the company has been trying to tell a story of Rhodes tapping into a darker side because being a true blue hero is not working for him anymore. It makes sense if this is all a build to his long-rumored turn before or at WrestleMania 43. Punk can sometimes act like a heel and still get cheers from fans. Turning him would be trickier, but it is not impossible. Furthermore, there may be a belief that a heel version of Punk can be extremely helpful in lifting up younger stars they are trying to turn into main event players. title: TNA World Champion Could Soon Jump Ship to WWE: Report

body: Slater, 22, became the youngest World Champion in TNA history at Bound For Glory. The high-flyer defeated Nic Nemeth on Oct. 11 at Bound For Glory to secure his first World Championship. He is now the youngest wrestler to hold World Championship gold in TNA, WWE or AEW . Play After the historic win, Leon Slater said he was “grateful” for the support he’s received along the way to achieving his dream of becoming a World Champion. “I’m a big believer in manifestation and self-confidence and all of that jazz . I always saw myself with something like this,” Slater said while holding the TNA World Championship. “People have asked me if I’m nervous or if I’m worried. I say no. I feel like everything is happening how it’s supposed to. “ I’m just so grateful. I’m grateful for the people God put me around ,” he continued. “Grateful for the environment God put me in.” Before their main event match at Bound For Glory, Nic Nemeth heaped praise on Slater, describing him as a rising star. “We’ve already seen Leon Slater go over a couple times and look like a million freaking bucks , as he should because he is,” Nemeth told Casino.org . Nemeth hinted that Slater’s stardom may cause him to ascend beyond TNA . “ I would like to keep him with us , but he’s someone who’s already walked in there and already kind of looked like a star.” The TNA World Champion has already appeared on WWE programming multiple times. In December, Slater teamed with Je’Von Evans in a tag team match against Dragon Lee and AJ Styles during the John Cena Farewell Tour. Play Less than a week later, Slater competed in an Iron Survivor match on Dec. 6 on NXT. Slater, the youngest X-Division Champion in TNA history, also challenged Oba Femi for the NXT Championship in January. His most recent WWE appearance was on January 16, when he accepted Carmelo Hayes’ United States Championship Open Challenge. Boasting an impressive resume at just 22 years old, Nemeth believes the sky is the limit for Slater. “He’s a kid and he’s got plenty of growth to go,” Nemeth told Casino.org . “But man, he doesn’t need any more reps to be good . He’s already got it figured out.” When asked if Leon Slater was the complete package, Nemeth said, “Dude, he really is. Like, there’s so many kids out there that can do some gymnastics, and I’m like, man, that’s incredible. This guy backs it up. Like, he’s got the charisma, he can talk. I’ve watched him go from good at talking to great at talking just on TNA, to where he comes out, he’s so comfortable. I’m like, damn it, he’s good to go .” PWIE reported that the belief in WWE is that his deal is up at the end of the year. body: Femi beat Lesnar inside Hell in a Cell in the main event of SummerSlam Night One on Aug. first in Minneapolis. The former NXT Champion knocked a chair out of Lesnar's hand and hit Fall From Grace for the win. Afterward, Lesnar hugged Femi, raised the Ruler's arm, and called him "the future of WWE." Heyman was at ringside with Lesnar that night, not Femi. Lesnar spent most of his WWE career with Heyman as his advocate. After the match, Femi said, "The future is now, and the future is me." Femi described the night in his own words before Heyman arrived. The Nigerian star said The Vision told him to expect a series of tsunamis in New Orleans, but he found clear skies. Femi also warned that anyone who steps to him will kneel, pointing to Reed and Bron Breakker. Heyman built his career around the idea of the Paul Heyman Guy. Lesnar and Reigns both spent years with Heyman doing much of the talking, and the advocate served as Reigns' special counsel during The Bloodline era. Heyman also managed CM Punk during Punk's 434-day WWE Championship reign. The advocate left The Vision on July 13, a week after Maxxine Dupri joined the group. Heyman had been aligned with Breakker and Reed before that exit. Both men are now Femi's rivals. On the Oct. fifth Raw, Reed attacked Penta after a win by Penta and Je'Von Evans over Breakker and Austin Theory. Femi ran in to make the save and warned Reed ahead of their Money in the Bank match. The Vision went after Penta, Evans, and Trick Williams again on the Oct. ninth SmackDown. Fans chanted for Femi on that SmackDown, but the Ruler did not appear. Breakker speared Evans on the Oct. 12 Raw, the same night Femi turned down Heyman. The Vision targeted Evans on Oct. 9 and again on Oct. 12. Femi has beaten Lesnar at SummerSlam and Reed at Money in the Bank. Reigns holds the World Heavyweight Championship on Raw, and Penta has the men's Money in the Bank contract. The Tribal Chief faces Sami Zayn at Crown Jewel on Nov. seventh. Lesnar called Femi the future after SummerSlam, and Femi's results since August have matched those words. Femi's next opponent has not been announced. Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 28 in Houston is Raw's next premium live event after Crown Jewel. The next step should be a world title match, and it should come soon. Reigns is busy with Crown Jewel and WarGames, but Femi is the most logical challenger left on Raw. The future Lesnar talked about at SummerSlam should arrive before WrestleMania 43. The post Oba Femi Was Right To Turn Down Paul Heyman: 5 Reasons Why appeared first on Stadium Rant .
summary: Oba Femi defeated Brock Lesnar in a Hell in a Cell match at SummerSlam Night One, earning praise from Lesnar who called him the future of WWE. Femi later turned down an approach from Paul Heyman, who had previously served as advocate for Lesnar, Roman Reigns and CM Punk. Heyman had been aligned with Femi's current rivals Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed before departing The Vision in July.

title: Four Top Challengers for Liv Morgan's Title Reign
raw_title: Liv Morgan's Next Challengers: Four Best Opponents For Her Women's World Championship Reign
body: Stephanie Vaquer has held the Women's World Championship twice. The Chilean star won the vacant title by beating IYO SKY at Wrestlepalooza on Sept. 20, 2025, and lost it to Morgan at WrestleMania 42. Vaquer won it back in her home country on Sept. 12, and the second reign lasted 28 days before Morgan pinned her in New Orleans. Vaquer suffered an ankle injury in the Money in the Bank triple threat. The former champion was on crutches on the Oct. 12 Raw, telling Lynch she would be fine in "a few days." WWE has not announced a timeline for her return. Vaquer also missed more than three months after WrestleMania 42 before returning on the Aug. 3 Raw. Lynch has been chasing Morgan since returning on the Aug. 3 Raw, calling the champion's reign the worst of all time. Lynch, as special guest referee on Sept. 12, stopped her count at two after Morgan hit Oblivion, and Vaquer won the title. The No. 1 contender's match between Lynch and Morgan on the Oct. 5 Raw ended without a winner after Vaquer attacked both women. Roxanne Perez has worked closely with Morgan and Raquel Rodriguez on Raw. On the Oct. 5 Raw, Perez and Rodriguez beat Lola Vice and Sol Ruca. A week later, Perez pinned WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green with Pop Rox in a non-title match after Morgan and Rodriguez distracted the champion. Perez also competed in the women's Money in the Bank ladder match in New Orleans. Tiffany Stratton won the briefcase. Perez is a former NXT Women's Champion. Earlier in 2026, Perez and Morgan challenged Ripley and SKY for the Women's Tag Team Championship at Saturday Night's Main Event. SKY lost to Morgan for the Women's World Championship on Night 1 of SummerSlam on Aug. 1. The Genius of the Sky reached that match by winning the 2026 Queen of the Ring tournament. SKY also held the Women's World Championship in 2025, beating Ripley on the March 3 Raw before losing it to Naomi's Money in the Bank cash-in at Evolution. SKY was off WWE television after the Aug. 10 Raw, and the former champion said she had been on vacation in Japan. At a Sept. 9 live event in Quito, Ecuador, SKY lost a fatal four-way for the Women's Intercontinental Championship. Rodriguez retained the title. What's your take? The Man has been chasing the champion since August, and their last one-on-one match ended without a winner. A Morgan win settles the feud and makes the fourth reign look stronger heading into the end of 2026. Lynch can move on without the title picture hanging over her. Vaquer should be the one who takes the title. Morgan has beaten the Chilean star at WrestleMania and in New Orleans, and the next meeting should go Vaquer's way. The injury gives Vaquer time to heal while Morgan handles Lynch. A December title win would make the former champion the top star of the Raw women's division. Perez and SK

body: We’ve asked ChatGPT to predict all of the winners, title changes, and shocks for AEW WrestleDream 2026, providing an insight into what the events of the show may look like. As ever with AI, professional wrestling predictions can be a little weird. This will mark a turning point for Ciampa, as AI predicts that this loss will send him over the edge, trashing the ringside area in a rage post-match. Baker will hit Persephone with the TBS Championship, allowing Aminata to roll-up Hyan to steal the victory and escape with her first AEW title. This will lead to the eventual break-up of Baker & Persephone as a duo. Chris Jericho & Nick Wayne and 1-1 in their series heading into WrestleDream, and after cheating and shenanigans it will be the young and rising Wayne who stands tall, per AI. The interesting part comes post-match, when the veteran Jericho offers a handshake and respect to his opponent, only for Wayne to hit a vicious low blow, reminiscent of Jericho’s kick to Shawn Michaels all the way back at WrestleMania 19. In a hard-hitting slugfest, AI predicts that Jon Moxley will bounce back from recent defeats to continue his dominant Continental Championship reign, which has been ongoing since Worlds End last year, to beat Mark Davis. The feud between Adam Page & Swerve Strickland has ignited once again, and it will be central to this AEW World Trios Championship match. Following a chaotic 2-out-of-3-falls matchup, it will be Page beating Strickland to win the match for his team. The Young Bucks picked up the AEW World Tag Team Championships as recently at All Out, it will be a surprise upset that hands The Don Callis Family pairing of Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight the gold, per AI’s predictions. Mercedes Mone is one of the surefire favorites heading into WrestleDream, but that hasn’t stopped AI from making a wild prediction. Mone won the AEW Women’s World Title at All In, with this being her first PPV title defense since then… but AI thinks she will lose. With the help of Skye Blue & Julia Hart, Thekla is predicted to cheat her way to winning the championship, leading to a Mone babyface turn in the aftermath. This is wildly unlikely, especially since Thekla has become so popular since her title loss back at Redemption , and is more likely the one to turn babyface. Will Ospreay will defend his AEW World Title in AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, battling Konosuke Takeshita, Darby Allin, Samoa Joe, Mike Bailey, Kazuchika Okada, Ricochet and Adam Copeland, the latter of whom recently announced that he will retire next year. AI predicts that Ospreay will win, but it will be at the final second. Heading into the last minute of the match, Copeland is predicted to have the points advantage, only for Ospreay to pick up two quick falls right at the final gasp to stand tall and win the match.

title: Is there any chance Will Ospreay loses in Clockwork Carnage? — Big Vinny V
raw_title: Big Vinny V: Is there any chance Will Ospreay loses in Clockwork Carnage?
summary_src: AEW is trying a wacky new match at WrestleDream called Clockwork Carnage.
body: We’re not going to get into the rules of the match right now. (If you want to, you can find all 72 words of them here .) For today, let’s simply rank the seven challengers, from least likely to walk out of WrestleDream as champion to most. That means starting at the bottom with Ospreay’s United Empire stablemate. After losing the AEW World Trios Championship in April (along with Kevin Knight and Mistico), Bailey spent most of the summer trying and failing to win various championships. He lost five title matches since then, with losses to Darby Allin, Knight, Mark Davis, and Kyle Fletcher in the process. He also lost a title eliminator match to Jon Moxley. After all that failure, he’d make for a very weak champion right now. Ricochet has been on his own losing streak of late. Before beating Ace Austin in a Clockwork Carnage qualifier, he had not won a singles match since defeating Chris Jericho at Dynasty in April. He and the Demand were AEW World Trios Champions at one point this summer, but Ricochet still feels cold going into WrestleDream, and AEW doesn’t often put belts on wrestlers without heating them up first. Make no mistake, Takeshita will likely be AEW World Champion someday. He might even be the man to beat Ospreay down the road. But having been absent from AEW for most of the fall, he has very little momentum going into Clockwork Carnage. Whenever Takeshita wins the world championship, it needs to be a high-profile pay-per-view main event with a long buildup to grow anticipation. WrestleDream is not that. Besides, Takeshita still has unfinished business with his former Don Callis Family stablemates Kyle Fletcher and Kazuchika Okada. Allin is also a former AEW World Champion, with a very short but very memorable reign earlier this year. That reign started with a shocking win over MJF on Dynamite. His second reign could start with another shocker at WrestleDream. Copeland announced on Dynamite last night that 2027 would be the last year of his career, and he was still targeting the world championship. Copeland has won unexpected world championships before on Money in the Bank cash-ins and in Elimination Chambers. A win in Clockwork Carnage would be appropriate for the man once known as the Ultimate Opportunist. Okada is one of the most decorated wrestlers in the history of … well, the world, but especially in AEW, having spent over 1,000 days as either AEW Continental Champion or AEW International Champion; he still holds the latter title. AEW likes to promote him as the world’s best tournament wrestler, and Clockwork Carnage could be described as a tournament of sorts. A win here would leave him with a bevy of top-level ready-made challengers, including Fletcher, Takeshita, and of course Ospreay himself. Make no mistake, the smart money is still on Ospreay. But if you must bet elsewhere, Okada seems like the best available option.

title: On the Record: Roman Reigns Opens Up On the Insane Amount of Food He Eats to Stay WWE Ready
raw_title: Roman Reigns Reveals the Insane Amount of Food He Eats to Stay WWE Ready
summary_src: Roman Reigns doesn’t get much time to take his foot off the gas when it comes to staying in WWE shape, and his daily diet shows just how strict things get when he is preparing for a major event. During Men’s Health’s “Gym & Fridge” series, Reigns opened up his refrigerators and broke down what ...
body: During Men’s Health’s “Gym & Fridge” series , Reigns opened up his refrigerators and broke down what he actually eats when he is locked into his training routine. Roman explained that most of his prepared meals follow the same basic formula, with a vegetable, a carbohydrate and a protein making up the bulk of what he eats. That can mean a lot of chicken, ground beef and other simple proteins. Reigns admitted the meals can become pretty boring when he is eating that way for long stretches. “Well, when I’m locked in for a big event, we’re always going to be in meal prep. So as you can see, we have a vast selection of meal prep. That makes it a lot easier for me. Typically, it’ll be a vegetable, a carb, and a protein. A lot of times, it’s boring and you’re just switching between different types of chicken, you know, some kind of a beef, a ground beef.” Roman said steak sometimes gets worked into the rotation, but the closer he gets to a deadline, the simpler his food becomes. “We had steak in before, but it just gets a little easier to eat once we get closer to the deadline.” The former Undisputed WWE Champion also admitted that sauces are basically his survival mechanism when he is eating bland meal-prep food over and over again. “That’s how you get by this whole, you know, process of eating the most bland food in the world is you find the most bland condiments in the world with no calories and you just slather it all over that stuff and then you eat it.” Reigns specifically gave sugar-free ketchup some love before mentioning Melinda’s sauce, joking that the company could send him a check. The bigger problem for Roman is that there really isn’t much of an offseason. When asked how often he meal preps, Reigns explained that WWE’s schedule keeps him in that mode for most of the year. “I mean, with the WWE schedule being year round, it kind of just never stops, you know? I do have gaps here and there, but for the most part, we’re pretty locked in year round.” His daily routine gets even more intense when he is fully preparing for a major WWE event. Roman said the day starts with fasted cardio before he moves into breakfast, which is one of his favorite meals. Reigns said he will sometimes mix collagen or protein powder into the oatmeal before immediately getting back into his prepared meals for the rest of the day. “Usually we’ll put a little bit of collagen or protein powder in there to flavor it up a little bit. And then we’re just like right to these meals.” “Four whole meals including that breakfast. Three being from the meal prep and then two protein shakes. One being after the workout and then one after PM cardio.” “So five meals with two shakes. Excuse me. Six meals with two shakes. Sorry.” That means Roman can be putting away six meals and two protein shakes during a serious training period, but none of it sounds like the kind of eating spree most people would enjoy. It is tightly controlled food designed to keep him ready for the ring. Reigns
summary: Per Ringside News: reigns opened up his refrigerators and broke down what he actually eats when he is locked into his training routine. Most of his prepared meals follow the same basic formula, with a vegetable, a carbohydrate and a protein making up the bulk of what he eats, Roman explained.

Fellow WWE Superstar and current WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns also appears as Akuma, and former New Japan Pro-Wrestling IWGP World Champion Hirooki Goto plays E. Honda. During an interview with Brandon Davis, Cody Rhodes was asked which current WWE Superstars he believes would fare well in a real-life World Warrior tournament. At first, he agreed with Brandon that Dominik Mysterio, son of WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio, would put up a good showing as a sneaky fighter. Then, Cody touted Jacob Fatu, a relative of Roman Reigns, as a solid Blanka-type force. He also said that Chad Gable, the current WWE Intercontinental Champion, would fare well in the tournament as a genuine Olympic-level wrestler. “You got some parallels with a Blanka and a Jacob Fatu. Just a madness,” he said before adding, “World Warrior Tournament at WWE? Chad Gable. A shooter’s shooter, Chad Gable.” I'm Robert DeFelice. I spent years covering pro-wrestling industry for outlets such as Fightful. After years in wrestling journalism, I’ve transitioned to video games, another passion of mine. The show also featured two title matches, five qualifiers for Clockwork Carnage, Jon Moxley eating a pin, Julia Hart spitting black mist, a massive brawl to close the night, and more from Wolstein Center in Cleveland, OH. There are three moments I want to touch on before getting to the matches. Copeland announced that 2027 will be his final year as a professional wrestler. That news came as a huge surprise. Cope delivered the scoop in a post-match promo after winning his Clockwork Carnage qualifier. This was prompted by another bit of news that Christian Cage suffered broken ribs and a collapsed lung in the ladder match at All Out. Copeland assessed his own status to see the finish line coming, and he wants the world championship. True surprises in AEW don’t happen that often. This was so far out of left field that I don’t think anyone saw it coming. It will be interesting to see what cool stuff AEW has in store for Cope over the coming year. Let’s enjoy the ride. And, best of health to Christian in his recovery. title: Guidelines for Guest Posts on Wrestling Websites

body: That distinction matters in wrestling, where readers know the difference between an informed piece and copy that has been dropped onto a site simply to carry a link. A post about the business of independent wrestling might fit a publication that covers sports media or event promotion. A generic article with no connection to wrestling, entertainment or the site's readership is much harder to justify. Before arranging a placement, look at the website as a reader would. Is it publishing current material? Does it have a clear subject and a consistent editorial voice? Are its recent stories relevant to the audience you hope to reach? A site that has a wrestling section but rarely updates it may not be as useful as a smaller publication with an active readership and a clear focus. Check the quality of the articles around the proposed placement, too. A page surrounded by unrelated posts or a long list of paid-looking contributions can make even a well-written article feel out of place. Ask what the editor expects, whether the article will be reviewed, and whether it will remain published. Those details affect the reader's experience as much as the link itself. There are different ways to handle outreach and publishing. FATJOE is positioned as a managed service, while iCopify operates as a marketplace where users can select publishing websites themselves. The comparison of FATJOE and iCopify is useful for understanding that difference before deciding which process suits a campaign. A managed service may appeal to a buyer who wants more of the process handled for them. A marketplace can offer more direct choice, but that choice also means doing the evaluation: reviewing available sites, checking their subject matter and deciding whether the proposed placement is appropriate. Neither approach removes the need to read the final article carefully or consider how it will look to the site's audience. For a wrestling-related campaign, make a short list of acceptable publications before ordering anything. Set practical standards for relevance, quality and audience. If the goal is to introduce a new training school, for example, a local sports or community publication may be more relevant than a broad marketing site. If the article concerns wrestling collectibles, an entertainment or hobby publication could make more sense. The strongest guest articles answer a question or provide context that the host site's audience can use. A piece about how smaller promotions build a live-event audience could cover venue selection, local promotion and the challenge of creating repeat attendance. An article about wrestling media might explain how a promotion can share timely information without overwhelming fans with promotional posts. That is different from writing several paragraphs around a link. The link should lead to something that adds useful context, and the sentence containing it should read naturally. title: Austin Creed Hints at New Gaming YouTube Channel
raw_title: Austin Creed teases new video game channel following AEW arrival
summary_src: Austin Creed isn’t able to host UpUpDownDown anymore, but he might have another video game-related project in the works. The former Xavier Woods was the face of WWE’s UpUpDownDown gaming channel on YouTube, reaching 2.43 million subscribers before Creed departed the company this May.
body: Austin Creed isn’t able to host UpUpDownDown anymore, but he might have another video game-related project in the works. Creed, Tyler Breeze, Adam Cole, and Claudio Castagnoli, who are all video game fans, have called their streaming group “Da Party.” Three of them are now signed to AEW, and the other (Breeze) is a free agent . Creed teased the idea of reuniting their group and hinted that a new YouTube channel is already being worked on. “I will say that you are correct, none of the Da Party members are currently signed with WWE,” Creed said. “And that would lead me to believe that there is at least the chance that something will happen. The chance of something to be created is available. I will not confirm or deny if anyone has been filming anything or if anyone has been creating assets for a new YouTube channel — I will not confirm or deny that. I will not.” Since arriving in AEW , Creed has enjoyed forming bonds with the wrestlers he’s meeting for the first time. Having a good rapport with the locker room is part of why UpUpDownDown worked. Creed wants that same dynamic to exist if he were to start a similar project within AEW. “I would hope that maybe there’d be a chance to do something with video games. I don’t know. I cannot say. But that rapport with the locker room is first and foremost the most important thing,” he said. “So before I even think about setting up a camera and getting people to play games and stuff, I want that rapport first.” WWE owns the rights to the UpUpDownDown name and channel, so Creed would need to come up with a new name if he does launch another project.
