body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email October 12, 2026 – WWE today announced the addition of three events across Australia and New Zealand this December which will see WWE Superstars visit Melbourne on Wednesday, December 9 , Brisbane on Tuesday, December 15 , and Auckland on Thursday, December 17. The upcoming events will mark WWE’s first return to Brisbane, Australia, in 7 years and the first return to Auckland, New Zealand, in 10 years. Tickets will go on sale Thursday, October 15 at 2pm local time.Fans interested in an exclusive presale opportunity beginning on Wednesday, October 14 at 1pm local time can register now by visiting https://www.wwe.com/live-tour-december . Fans in Melbourne will see their favorite WWE Superstars in action including CM Punk , “The American Nightmare” Cody Rhodes , Randy Orton , Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn , United States Champion Trick Williams , WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green , Charlotte Flair , GUNTHER , Jade Cargill and many more. Brisbane and Auckland will see the arrival of WWE Superstars including Seth Rollins , Becky Lynch , Oba Femi , World Tag Team Champions The Vision, The Bloodline, Women's World Champion Liv Morgan , LA Knight , Je’Von Evans and many more*. As previously announced, Perth’s RAC Arena will play host to three events this December including SmackDown on Friday, December 11 , Wrestlepalooza: Perth on Saturday, December 12 , and Raw on Monday, December 14. Tickets available now from www.ticketek.com.au . Fans attending WWE's live dates across Australia and New Zealand can elevate their event experience with a range of VIP packages, offering premium seating and once-in-a-lifetime opportunities to get closer to WWE Superstars. From first-row seats and ringside access to exclusive WWE Superstar autograph signings, exclusive inside-the-barricade experiences to pose ringside with a WWE Championship title belt alongside Superstars, plus WWE merchandise, a commemorative 3D event poster, priority check-in, express venue entry, and early merchandise access. With a range of packages available, fans can choose the experience that brings them closest to the action and their favorite Superstars. For additional information on package types, please visit superfan.live/wwe .

body: It's three hours of AEW action tonight, as AEW Dynamite & Collision comes your way with a live 3-hour special at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on TBS and HBO Max from the Wolstein Center in Cleveland, Ohio! It’s the final stop before AEW WrestleDream on Saturday in Orlando, Florida, but there’s still much to be decided tonight when five Clockwork Carnage qualifiers, including a pair of title matches, will determine who joins AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and “Speedball” Mike Bailey of United Empire, as well as Samoa Joe, in the 8-man field. Speaking of Ospreay and Joe, they’ll be on opposite sides of a star-studded tag team match that is just one of four multi-person matches with WrestleDream opponents facing off tonight. After Tommaso Ciampa attacked Andrade on Collision to make his AEW National Title aspirations clear, Andrade and Ospreay challenged Ciampa to find a partner, so he’s bringing Joe to the fight. AEW champions who are part of the Clockwork Carnage qualifiers were required to put their titles on the line, so as mentioned above, we’ll see a pair of championship tilts among the five matches. TNT Champion Darby Allin defends against CMLL World Heavyweight Champion Hechicero, and AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada risks his title against Myron Reed. Plus, Adam Copeland takes on Josh Alexander, Brian Cage meets Konosuke Takeshita, and Ricochet faces Ace Austin in the remaining Clockwork Carnage qualifiers. AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Moné joins Divine Dominion to fight Triangle of Madness days before facing Thekla at WrestleDream, and the Death Riders face the Don Callis Family in trios action with Mark Davis set to challenge AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley on Saturday in Orlando. Plus, TBS Champion Persephone and Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. battle Dani Luna and Hyan! Check out everything you need to know for this LIVE 3-HOUR SPECIAL! Two current champions face two challengers tonight before their respective matches at WrestleDream. After Andrade retained the AEW National Championship against Michael Oku on Collision, Ciampa made his next title quest painfully clear. He shook Andrade's hand and planted a kiss on his cheek, then ambushed him with a knee to the head and a draping DDT on the National Title. Andrade and Ospreay responded by challenging Ciampa and any partner to a fight, so Ciampa is bringing Samoa Joe, who is already set to meet Ospreay, Speedball Bailey and five other wrestlers in Clockwork Carnage after beating "Jungle" Jack Perry in Paris. The champions have revenge on their mind, so will they get it heading into WrestleDream, or will the challengers take the momentum into their championship challenges in Orlando? Thekla beat Willow Nightingale last month at All Out to get her shot at Moné and the AEW Women’s Championship at WrestleDream. body: We were back in Paris for the Collision half of Grand Slam: France from Adidas Arena on TNT and HBO MAX! It was another perfect atmosphere for the best professional wrestling in the world thanks to a molten-hot Paris crowd! And they got to see a pair of championship tilts and another qualifier for Clockwork Carnage, which is now just one week away at AEW WrestleDream in Orlando on October 17! The night started with a rivalry that may never end between The Conglomeration and Death Riders in a Mixed Fight in Paris! Willow Nightingale returned to action for the first time since AEW All Out to join Orange Cassidy, Kyle O’Reilly and Roderick Strong, but they fell to Claudio Castagnoli, Marina Shafir, Wheeler Yuta and Daniel Garcia in a chaotic brawl! In the main event, the Young Bucks avenged a previous loss to The Dogs to retain their AEW World Tag Team Championship. However, it was the Bucks’ challengers at WrestleDream, “The Protostar” Kyle Fletcher and “The Jet” Kevin Knight, who stood tall holding the titles after laying out Matt and Nick Jackson to close out the night in Paris! The other championship bout saw Andrade El Ídolo turn away Michael Oku to retain his AEW National Championship before he was confronted and laid out by Tommaso Ciampa, who made his next title quest painfully clear! Plus, “Speedball” Mike Bailey beat ROH Pure Champion Lee Moriarty to join AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and Samoa Joe in Clockwork Carnage. Wrathlander won a 3-Way over Sisters of Sin and Divine Dominion to become #1 contenders to The Brawling Birds AEW Women’s World Tag Team Championship. All that and more closed out a tremendous debut week in Paris for AEW! O'Reilly came in and locked Yuta in a guillotine while the rest of the teams continued battling outside. Shafir broke it up, grabbing O'Reilly from behind and trapping him in a straight ankle lock, but O'Reilly escaped into a cross armbreaker of his own! What a tremendous exchange of mat wrestling between the two! The pair came face to face, with O'Reilly pulling back on a kick, only for Shafir to fake him out and land one of her own right to his face. As O'Reilly went after her, Garcia knocked him out of the ring, but Willow shoved Garcia into Shafir, sending her into the corner. Willow chopped Shafir across the chest and hoisted her up, but Shafir slipped free, and the two traded brutal open-hand chops. Shafir rebounded off the ropes with a German suplex, then went for a PK, but Willow ducked and rolled her up for a two-count. Willow followed with a pair of chops and a feint before body-slamming Shafir to the mat, pausing to pose for the crowd — only for Castagnoli to sneak up behind her. Willow beat her chest and dared him to bring it, but Strong blocked Castagnoli’s pump kick attempt and joined Willow in for a double-team of chops on Castagnoli. raw_title: AEW Grand Slam: France Collision Preview – Young Bucks Put Up AEW World Tag Team Titles Against The Dogs, Andrade El Ídolo Defends National Title, Mixed Fight in Paris, More - AEW
body: The Collision edition of AEW Grand Slam: France hits your screens tonight at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on TNT and HBO Max, closing out AEW's debut week in Paris from Adidas Arena. Tensions are on the rise with AEW WrestleDream just one week away, and seven matches highlight tonight’s card, including two championship matches, a massive Mixed Fight in Paris, and a Clockwork Carnage Qualifier. AEW World Tag Team Champions Young Bucks defend against The Dogs, with the winners set to face Don Callis Family's Kyle Fletcher and "The Jet" Kevin Knight at WrestleDream. The Dogs beat the Bucks back at Summer Blockbuster, but can they do it again tonight to snatch the gold? AEW National Champion Andrade El Ídolo enters the sixth defense of his title against UK standout Michael Oku. And after AEW Grand Slam: France Dynamite saw AEW World Champion Will Ospreay beat AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada to retain his title and Samoa Joe become the first man to qualify for Clockwork Carnage by beating Jack Perry, United Empire's "Speedball" Mike Bailey takes on ROH Pure Champion Lee Moriarty in the second Clockwork Carnage qualifier. Check out everything you need to know for Grand Slam: France Collision in Paris! Matt and Nick Jackson became the first-ever four-time AEW World Tag Team Champions at AEW All Out when they climbed the ladder and pulled down the titles in a chaotic 3-Way Ladder Match against Christian Cage and Adam Copeland and FTR. Now, they face a team that has already beaten them, The Dogs, who defeated the Bucks at Summer Blockbuster back in June. Connors and Finlay have a chance once again to claim gold, and the winners of this match will face Don Callis Family's Kyle Fletcher and "The Jet" Kevin Knight at WrestleDream. Do the Young Bucks start their fourth reign with a successful defense, or do The Dogs make good on their earlier win and pull it off again to become AEW World Tag Team Champions? The Conglomeration and Death Riders came face-to-face on Collision last Saturday between each team’s respective trios victory. There is no shortage of history between the two sides, and they’ll get to add to that tonight in a unique Mixed Fight in Paris. Will The Conglomeration, looking to get back on the path to backpacks full of gold, send a message to the Death Riders with a big win, or will the Death Riders continue to handle their business against most anyone who steps in their way? AEW National Champion Andrade El Ídolo has proven to be a fighting champion by taking on all comers. His sixth challenger is British star Michael Oku, who gave Kazuchika Okada a run for his money and the AEW Unified Championship on Collision last September and is looking to take his career to a new level with an AEW championship of his own. title: Legal Watch: WWE Espn Lawsuit Update

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game WWE ESPN LAWSUIT UPDATE By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-12 14:00:00 United States District Court of ConnecticutJudge Sarah F. Russell ruled on 10/6 that WWE, ESPN, etc. will have until 10/16 to respond to Michael Diesa and Rebella Toback's motion objecting to ESPN and BAMTech, LLC being added as defendants in the lawsuit alleging that WWE misled customers about how to watch its major PPV/PLE events after it moved them to the ESPN Unlimited streaming platform as of WrestlePalooza 2025. Judge Russell also ruled the Court will hold off on ruling whether the case should be moved to arbitration until Diesa and Toback's objection is ruled on. Obviously, access depended on behind-the-scenes agreements between Disney (ESPN’s parent company) and individual TV providers. At the time, some services (Verizon Fios, DirecTV, Spectrum, and Hulu + Live TV) allowed customers to log into the ESPN app and watch the events. Others (such as Cox, Xfinity and YouTube TV at the time) did not at the time of launch, forcing customers to pay extra. The lawsuit has been seeking, "An award of actual, compensatory, and/or consequential damages, alternatively, an award of nominal damages (if and as necessary), an award of statutory damages (if and as permitted by law), an award of punitive damages (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(a) and/or as otherwise permitted by law, an award of reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses incurred in connection with this action (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(d) and/or as otherwise permitted by law, an award of the costs of this action (pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. §42-110g(d) and/or as otherwise permitted by law), any injunctive relief necessary to preclude WWE from (a) continuing to violate CUTPA, (b) conspiring with ESPN to violate CUTPA, and/or (c) aiding and/or abetting ESPN in its violation(s) of CUTPA; and/or any other legal or equitable relief as the Court deems appropriate." title: Legal Watch: Wwe, Montez Ford Sued Over WWE Raw 'lapdance'
raw_title: WWE, MONTEZ FORD SUED OVER WWE RAW 'LAPDANCE' - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game WWE, MONTEZ FORD SUED OVER WWE RAW 'LAPDANCE' By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 08:45:00 ???????? pic.twitter.com/T6pdOoR20q PostWrestling.com in Canada reported yesterday that Cook County Sheriff’s officer Noel Lucas is suing WWE, Montez Ford of the Street Profits tag team and WWE subsidiary Event Services, LLC, over an alleged unwanted sexualized dance during the 7/6 episode of WWE Monday Night Raw, which was broadcast from the Chicago area at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. Lucas was working off-duty security when, according to the lawsuit, Ford approached him during the Street Profits’ entrance and performed a sexually suggestive dance (embedded above) involving hip thrusts and gyrating without his consent. Lucas alleges that footage of the incident spread widely across social media, including on WWE’s and Ford’s accounts, making him recognizable to the public. He also alleges that when he returned to his full-time courthouse job the next day, people recognized and mocked him by imitating the dance. He also alleges that his children were ridiculed at school because of the video, causing him significant humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress. The lawsuit includes 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act, and unlawful use of his image under the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. Lucas is seeking monetary and punitive damages, legal costs, and an order preventing WWE and Ford from using his identity. Neither WWE nor Ford have responded to the lawsuit as of yesterday. llm_long: Cappuccino Jones and Santi Rivera have left WWE's ID program. Their departures add to a series of exits from the developmental initiative.
Cappuccino Jones previously held the WWE ID Men's Championship. He carried the title for 234 days between August 2025 and March 2026.
Jones currently reigns as the Reality of Wrestling Texas Champion. He has not yet made a public statement regarding his exit from the program.
Santi Rivera, aged 24, began his wrestling career in 2021. He has appeared for promotions including Create A Pro, Beyond Wrestling, and Reality of Wrestling.
Rivera also has not publicly commented on his departure from WWE ID. Additional talents such as Laynie Luck, Sam Holloway, and Marcus Mathers have previously left the program.

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game ROMAN REIGNS AND MORE TALK 'STREET FIGHTER' ON SIRIUSXM SPECIAL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-16 07:30:00 SiriusXM issued the following: SiriusXM Front Row special w/ Roman Reigns and the Cast of "Street Fighter" The cast of the upcoming “Street Fighter” movie recently joined Sam Roberts for a special SiriusXM Front Row event on the WWE Radio channel, where stars 50 Cent, Roman Reigns, Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji, and Callina Liang discussed their experiences filming the movie, behind-the-scenes moments, and the camaraderie among the cast. Roman Reigns spoke about making the transition from WWE to acting, and the difference in dynamics between being on a movie set and working with actors, versus working/competing in the world of pro wrestling. Noah Centineo talks about Marky Mark and Jake Paul being inspirations he drew from for his character in the film, Ken Masters. The cast also shares fun behind-the-scenes stories about 50 Cent buying out Luna Park for the entire cast and crew to build camaraderie, and more. Sam Roberts: How do you wrap your head around commanding that attention when you’re shooting scenes, it’s a movie, it’s not like getting into a wrestling ring and feeling 20,000 people around you. And, number two, making it different than Roman Reigns. Akuma is very different, even in the way you use your body, very different than what Roman Reigns does. Roman Reigns: The main parallel for me, especially in this movie, my main contributions were in the third act. So it’s in the main event of the movie is what I was telling myself. And that’s what I practice, is main event performance. That’s my bag. That’s what I do when it’s my time to go out there and wrestle. So I just try to keep that type of weight on it. The stakes are as high as can be so you need to be able to come in and match what everybody’s done. … These guys know what they’re doing. I'm not a real actor. I go out and I wrestle. It really helped me to see what they have done and the way they led the film. It set the tone for what needed to be matched. It wasn't easy, but there were a bunch of things I was able to rely on from wrestling to help me take this on. Sam Roberts: You've also evolved your performance as a wrestler, I think, further than a lot of traditional wrestlers and WWE Superstars do, in terms of the stories that you actively tell with your face. title: NXT Halloween Havoc championship matches take shape for 2026
raw_title: NXT Halloween Havoc championship matches take shape for 2026 - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game NXT Halloween Havoc championship matches take shape for 2026 By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-16 10:04:00 Halloween Havoc takes shape after NXT’s masked surprise Halloween Havoc returns on October 31, and WWE NXT has begun shaping its championship card. Kelani Jordan will defend the NXT Women's Championship against Wren Sinclair, while Grayson Waller is guaranteed a title defense against an opponent yet to be decided. Both developments came out of the October 6 episode, giving the Halloween show two stories to follow. This marks Halloween Havoc's first Halloween-night edition. The announcements also raise a question for viewers following wrestling on their phones: will either match appear in a sportsbook? Fans checking an android app for possible markets still need an actual event listing before treating mobile betting as an option. For now, the confirmed news concerns the matches, not any published Halloween Havoc odds. The temptation is to call one wrestler the favorite after watching those results. Yet NXT is scripted entertainment, not an unscripted sporting contest; storyline direction matters more than conventional form statistics. Predictions can be part of the conversation without becoming genuine sportsbook odds. Unlike boxing or mixed martial arts, wrestling has a planned finish, which is why some bookmakers leave WWE off their betting menus entirely. title: What Wrestling Sites Should Know — Guest Posting With Your Own Article

body: That distinction matters in wrestling, where readers know the difference between an informed piece and copy that has been dropped onto a site simply to carry a link. A post about the business of independent wrestling might fit a publication that covers sports media or event promotion. A generic article with no connection to wrestling, entertainment or the site's readership is much harder to justify. Before arranging a placement, look at the website as a reader would. Is it publishing current material? Does it have a clear subject and a consistent editorial voice? Are its recent stories relevant to the audience you hope to reach? A site that has a wrestling section but rarely updates it may not be as useful as a smaller publication with an active readership and a clear focus. Check the quality of the articles around the proposed placement, too. A page surrounded by unrelated posts or a long list of paid-looking contributions can make even a well-written article feel out of place. Ask what the editor expects, whether the article will be reviewed, and whether it will remain published. Those details affect the reader's experience as much as the link itself. There are different ways to handle outreach and publishing. FATJOE is positioned as a managed service, while iCopify operates as a marketplace where users can select publishing websites themselves. The comparison of FATJOE and iCopify is useful for understanding that difference before deciding which process suits a campaign. A managed service may appeal to a buyer who wants more of the process handled for them. A marketplace can offer more direct choice, but that choice also means doing the evaluation: reviewing available sites, checking their subject matter and deciding whether the proposed placement is appropriate. Neither approach removes the need to read the final article carefully or consider how it will look to the site's audience. For a wrestling-related campaign, make a short list of acceptable publications before ordering anything. Set practical standards for relevance, quality and audience. If the goal is to introduce a new training school, for example, a local sports or community publication may be more relevant than a broad marketing site. If the article concerns wrestling collectibles, an entertainment or hobby publication could make more sense. The strongest guest articles answer a question or provide context that the host site's audience can use. A piece about how smaller promotions build a live-event audience could cover venue selection, local promotion and the challenge of creating repeat attendance. An article about wrestling media might explain how a promotion can share timely information without overwhelming fans with promotional posts. That is different from writing several paragraphs around a link. The link should lead to something that adds useful context, and the sentence containing it should read naturally. title: Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling
raw_title: Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling - PWInsider
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game Why So Many Former NFL Players Go into Wrestling By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-14 10:05:00 Former NFL players have long made the transition to professional wrestling. The two sports share similar physical attributes, skills, and culture, making the crossover a more natural progression for players looking to make the change. Active recruitment of NFL players by promoters has also provided a pathway and encouraged players to take the leap. There are other factors at play here too. NFL careers can be notoriously short; therefore, the chance to become a professional wrestler and pursue another potentially lucrative path is an attractive proposition for many, especially for fringe players and free agents. Some players just want to remain in the spotlight a little bit longer and extend their careers for longer than would ever be possible in football. American football and professional wrestling may look like very different sports, but there’s a surprising number of skills that both disciplines share. Strength and power are the most obvious. Football players use it for blocking, tackling, and breaking tackles, while wrestlers rely on it for takedowns, throws, lifts, and control. Linemen in particular have multiple crossover skills. Their speedy reactions and upper-body coordination, plus experience of fighting for hand position, are similar to wrestlers fighting to establish grips and create openings. A lineman exploding off the line and a wrestler shooting for a takedown also require similar abilities. Staying upright is important in both sports, despite opponents desperately trying to take you down. That’s why agility, footwork, balance, and body control are key skills in wrestling and football. The similarity between tackling and takedowns needs no explanation. There are plenty of NFL players who didn't go on to become full-time wrestlers but made notable WWE appearances, including Lawrence Taylor, four-time Super Bowl champion Rob Gronkowski , and William "The Refrigerator" Perry. But some of the most successful wrestling stars to have ever entered the squared circle are former football players. Sonnenberg is regarded as the first prominent professional football player from the major era to successfully make the leap. He played in the National Football League (NFL) from 1923 until 1930, winning the 1928 NFL championship with the Providence Steam Rollers. Sonnenberg’s wrestling career proved even more successful. Not only did he revolutionise the sport by introducing the "flying tackle" , but he won the National Wrestling Association (NWA) World Heavyweight Championship in 1929 and held the title for two years. In 1939, Sonnenberg became the American Wrestling Association champion after defeating and unmasking Marvin Westenberg (“The Shadow”). title: Meltzer: Saudi Government Pressuring WWE Over Crown Jewel
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Believes WWE Crown Jewel Decision Comes Down To Saudi Arabian Government
summary_src: Dave Meltzer has broken down the situation regarding WWE Crown Jewel, and believes the Saudi government have the final say on if the event takes place.
body: Meltzer mentioned the recent post on X (formerly known as Twitter) by Al-Sheikh that read "Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends," was a post that has put pressure on TKO to not cancel Crown Jewel, or any of the boxing and MMA events that are on the horizon. Al-Sheikh did announce that the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament has been moved from October to December, and events like the Red Sea International Film Festival, the FIFAe Finals, The Joy Awards, and the Soundstorm EDM festival have all been postponed. However, because WWE Superstars are independent contractors in name only, they wouldn't have a choice about going. Many people in the company, particularly the non-wrestlers, aren't thrilled about going over , and as for the wrestlers, it is largely expected everyone travels over to Riyadh to avoid pressure from above. These backups might need to be put into play due to the high risk of terrorist attacks in Saudi Arabia, with entertainment venues, hotels and locations where U.S. citizens gather, and places visited by U.S citizens and other foreigners all be at risk of being potential targets. Transportation hubs such as airports are also targets, as proven by the recent bombing at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Meltzer stated that the the Iran-backed Houthi have threatened to attack Saudi Arabia again, and even if missile strikes are intercepted, falling debris could also be a risk to citizens in certain areas. With all that said, the amount of money at stake is too much to risk according to Meltzer. While WWE will not lose any money on their current deal by postponing an event due to their current deal with the Saudi's, the long-term relationship between the two parties could be hindered when it comes to negotiating a new deal when the current one expires in 2028. Al-Sheikh is also the sole investor in Zuffa Boxing, another TKO entity, and much like WWE's deal, a pull out wouldn't be the end of the world at this time but it could hamper the relationship between TKO and the Saudi government in the future.
summary: Dave Meltzer reported that Turki Al-Sheikh's recent social media post has increased pressure on TKO Group to proceed with Crown Jewel in Riyadh despite regional instability. Several major Saudi entertainment events have been postponed or rescheduled following the recent airport bombing and heightened terrorist threats targeting foreigners and public venues. WWE talent classified as independent contractors would have little say in attending the show, though many non-wrestling staff members are reportedly unhappy about the trip.

title: AEW's Pac Died From Bronchial Asthma
raw_title: Late AEW Star Pac's Cause Of Death Reportedly Revealed
summary_src: The cause of death for late AEW star Pac, real name Benjamin Satterley, was reportedly revealed.
body: The outlet, citing a spokesperson from the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office, reported that Satterley, age 40, died of bronchial asthma. Officials, who found Satterley dead when they arrived on scene, noted at the time that while his death did not appear suspicious , he was found with saliva on the front of his shirt. Reports indicated undisclosed medication was found in the vehicle. Satterley was headed to O'Hare Airport and had stopped at a CAVA restaurant on the way. That's where he was discovered slumped over in the vehicle by witnesses, who alerted authorities. Officials arrived on scene and pronounced the star dead around 4 p.m. AEW revealed his passing later that night via social media. Pac competed the night before his death at All Out, where he faced off against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship. At the end of the night, Satterley appeared once again on the show, coming to the aid of Death Riders leader Jon Moxley in his match against AEW World Champion Will Ospreay. In the days following his passing, AEW held an emotional tribute show in his honor , where the Death Riders, including Moxley, Marina Shafir, Claudio Castagnoli, Wheeler Yuta, Daniel Garcia, and even Bryan Danielson, all competed in matches to honor their friend. Various WWE stars who knew Satterley as Neville during his time in WWE, including in "WWE NXT," also shared their memories of the star in an emotional tribute video posted to the company's YouTube channel.
summary: Pac, whose real name was Benjamin Satterley, was 40 when he passed away. The Cook County Medical Examiner's Office determined the cause to be bronchial asthma after he was found unresponsive in his vehicle outside a Chicago-area CAVA restaurant while en route to O'Hare Airport. The night before, he had wrestled Andrade El Idolo for the AEW Continental Championship at All Out and later aided Jon Moxley in the main event; AEW paid tribute with an emotional show featuring the Death Riders stable in the following days.

title: Sheamus Books Fan Convention On AEW Full Gear Date
raw_title: Report On S. Farrelly (FKA Sheamus) Booking Convention On Same Day As AEW Full Gear
summary_src: A new report revealed more on former WWE star Sheamus, now going by S. Farrelly, booking a convention date the same day as AEW Full Gear.
body: Farrelly was announced for The Big Event EXS, a wrestling fan convention at the Suffolk Credit Union Arena in Brentwood, New York, on November 17. The star recorded a video, posted to the convention's Facebook page , confirming he'd be in attendance to sign autographs and take photos with fans. The date, notably, lines up with AEW Full Gear. As of this writing, Farrelly has not been teased for any upcoming AEW event, including AEW WrestleDream on Saturday. Alongside the news of Farrelly's free agency, Fightful Select also reported there are many within AEW, both from a talent standpoint, as well as executives, who would like to see the former "Celtic Warrior" in the company. As of the report on October 2, no discussions had been had between the sides. TNA reportedly wanted the star at Bound for Glory 2026 , but the appearance was never locked on, or even considered, on Farrelly's side. Max Caster ended up filling the spot the company reportedly wanted for Sheamus, in a match against Moose.
summary: Stephen Farrelly, formerly known as Sheamus, has been announced for The Big Event EXS fan convention at Suffolk Credit Union Arena in Brentwood, New York on November 17. That date coincides with AEW's Full Gear pay-per-view. Multiple people within AEW are interested in bringing in the free agent, though no talks have taken place between the sides as of early October.

While some of us aren't betting against Jericho, given the star's history, 75 percent of us are predicting that Wayne will win the match, and the feud. We're hoping that Wayne is set for a bit of a push here, as Jericho does not need yet another victory over a young talent. Wayne's only recent victory in AEW, other than his "Grand Slam France" win, was against Komander back at the beginning of September. He also competed in the AEW All In London Casino Gauntlet match , where he had an impressive showing, but also took the pin, so he needs to stack some more wins. A WrestleDream, and feud-ending, victory over a veteran like Jericho would be big for him. Actually getting an apology segment from Jericho to Wayne would also be big, but we're not holding our breath on that one. While it's oftentimes difficult to bet against Jericho in this latter portion of his career, 75 percent of us are holding out hope, and predicting a Wayne victory. Like a coiled spring, Ciampa had been held down in WWE for years, and now he seems content to put on a true spectacle on his way to looking up at the lights. Ninety-two percent of the Wrestling Inc. Staff believe it to be so. How you know? Well, Andrade is just simply on a tear as National Champion. His catchphrase is over. His matches are good. He's everything a midcard AEW star should be. Someday, he will need to drop the title so that he can address the world title-sized elephant in the room, but until that day, there is no reason to go off-course with the National Champion. It will be a tremendous battle of two former WWE NXT Champions, but it feels like Andrade has been building to this fever pitch of popularity for some time. It is going to take more than Tommaso Ciampa to dethrone him, as almost all of the WINC staff believes. title: Royce Keys Welcomes Carmelo Hayes To 946
raw_title: WWE's Royce Keys Discusses Adding Carmelo Hayes To 946, Future Of Faction
summary_src: Royce Keys, the leader of 946 on "WWE Raw," spoke about the future of the faction, as well as adding Carmelo Hayes to the stable.
body: Keys, the leader of 946, sat down on " Busted Open Radio " to talk more about the dangerous faction and his friend, Hayes, getting involved. After months of not appearing on "WWE SmackDown," Hayes joined in the beatdown of the Usos and Solo Sikoa on Monday. "That my dog, you know, way, way before I even set foot in the door," Keys said of "'Melo." "He's a great addition. He's got a chip on his shoulder like we all do. There's more to come... More to come with the destruction and chaos. People are genuinely afraid of us, so we like that." Keys started his beatdown of the Bloodline alongside Sikoa, in addition to LA Knight, at SummerSlam, where the trio defeated Jacob Fatu and the Usos during night one. Keys was off WWE TV for a few weeks before returning to cause chaos alongside OTM as a surprise on the August 24 edition of "Raw." Launched in 2024, it’s the bridge for talent already active on the indie circuit who are interested in wrestling for WWE and vice versa. There are those who argue it’s also a means to control another wrestling market, homogenize training methods & wrestling style, and/or prevent or delay talent from signing with AEW. The persistence of those arguments is a big part of why so much attention’s been paid to a string of departures from the ID program over the past few weeks. We still don’t have anything but questions and arguments to go on about the program as a whole, and now we have this game of work or shoot to play with Sloane Jacobs and Beyond Wrestling. It’s something I happened to stumble across on social media. Tuesday (Oct. 13), WWE ID posted this on X/Twitter: WWE ID would like to apologize to @WrestlingOpenRI for Sloane Jacobs’ behavior last night. WWE ID values @WrestlingOpenRI and @WrestlingOpen as important places for independent wrestlers to grow and develop. Beyond has been a WWE ID partner from its inception. Jacobs’ ID contract is her second stint with WWE; she was signed to a developmental contract for several months in 2022, including a few televised matches on Level Up and NXT. She’s currently allied with Evolve Women’s champ Nikkita Lyons, but until this past was still wrestling on the indies as The Notorious Mimi — including for Beyond and its sister show Wrestling Open. That promotion accepted ID’s apology, ` reposting its message with `: “nothing but love for the program” but can’t even be bothered to call me the correct name righttttt Which Beyond replied to with a screenshot of her profile listing both Mimi and Jacobs, and writing: No disrespect intended. Hope you’re well and appreciate all you’ve done or did for Open. As you can see I’ve got plenty of messages to answer so I’m not going to continue to engage. Best of luck with everything. title: Medical Examiner Rules PAC Died of Bronchial Asthma
raw_title: Medical examiner determines Ben Satterley’s cause of death as bronchial asthma
summary_src: The cause of death of Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, has been determined as bronchial asthma.
body: The cause of death of Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, has been determined as bronchial asthma. Edward Lewis, senior sports reporter for the California Post, first reported the determination on Friday. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office ruled Satterley’s death as natural following its investigation. No additional medical details surrounding the determination have been made public. Satterley died on September 27, less than 24 hours after wrestling Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. As detailed in John Pollock’s obituary , Satterley was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois. Emergency services responded and he was pronounced dead at 4.08 pm local time. Authorities said shortly afterward that there were no indications of trauma or foul play and that his death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed, with the cause and manner of death remaining pending while additional testing was completed. Born in Newcastle upon Tyne, Satterley began wrestling in 2004 and became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships and established a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion. He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion. After returning to Dragon Gate and winning the Open the Dream Gate Championship, Satterley joined AEW in 2019. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and also held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was the September 26 loss to Andrade at All Out. Satterley also appeared later that night during the AEW World Championship main event between Will Ospreay and Jon Moxley.

llm_long: The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has ruled that Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, died of bronchial asthma. The determination classifies his death as natural. The senior sports reporter for the California Post first reported the ruling.
Satterley died on September 27 in Des Plaines, Illinois. He was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant. Emergency services responded and pronounced him dead at 4:08 pm local time.
Authorities stated there were no indications of trauma or foul play. His death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed and additional testing completed before the cause was finalized.

Satterley was born in Newcastle upon Tyne and began wrestling in 2004. He became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships including a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion.

He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments there included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns, and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion.

Satterley joined AEW in 2019 after returning to Dragon Gate. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was a loss to Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out on September 26.

When the deal was announced in early 2024, Bajaria was quoted , “(WWE) has been very under-distributed outside the US. Co-CEO Ted Sarandos acknowledged the disappointing performance in a recent chat, saying the service was “Not growing as fast as I want us to.” Former Fox and Disney executive Peter Rice will replace Bajaria.

title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s Crown Jewel plans put money and power ahead of safety
raw_title: WWE’s Crown Jewel plans put money and power ahead of safety | Opinion
summary_src: Saudi Arabia right now isn’t the safest place in the world. But that likely won’t stop WWE. The country has been rocked by several attacks over the last few weeks by Iranian-backed forces from Yemen.
body: Saudi Arabia right now isn’t the safest place in the world. But that likely won’t stop WWE. The country has been rocked by several attacks over the last few weeks by Iranian-backed forces from Yemen. Between October 7 and October 11, 17 people have died dead and 333 people injured in attacks that have taken place at Riyadh’s airport. In a fair world filled with common sense, WWE would naturally find an alternative for their event in Riyadh next month, prioritizing safety concerns over money. And recent reports do indicate there is a backup plan. Unfortunately, that is not exactly how the world operates currently. There is money to be made, after all, and relationships to keep. So as of right now, WWE will be sending their talent and production team to what will essentially be an active warzone. There was also an incident the following year that saw Vince McMahon reportedly clash with the Saudi Arabian government over the airing of one of their shows locally following a pay dispute. Coincidentally, the plane meant to take the talent home suddenly developed engine trouble, leaving a majority of the roster stranded in Saudi Arabia for an extra six hours. Now, the two incidents have never been fully linked to one another, and it’s never been fully established that the Saudi Arabian government deliberately held WWE talent hostage. But it is easy to see how some could see the two incidents being connected. This time around, the situation seems more unstable than controversial. The country is in the middle of a war with Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh has been attacked 20 times this month alone. The US State Department has issued a level 3 advisory urging Americans to reconsider travel to the country, and the Australian government is specifically advising citizens to not travel there. At this point, that makes sense and is a good call. There is no reason for anyone to travel to Saudi Arabia right now, let alone for a pro wrestling show that could be held anywhere else. While Canelo Alvarez still plans to head there for his next fight at the end of this month, other events are backing out . “Hard times reveal true friends,” Turki Alalshikh, the Chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority, wrote on social media after confirming Canelo would continue on. But there are two things that will make WWE go. One is relatively simple – there’s way too much money on the table. WWE staying away will not only prevent them from getting a big payday, it also poses many risks with their relationship with Saudi Arabia. And the second stretches beyond WWE. TKO’s Zuffa Boxing, which is heavily promoted across WWE television, is financially backed by the Saudi Arabian government. The last thing TKO would want to do is imperil that relationship by backing away from their contractual deals, even if they are risking lives by doing so. title: In Memoriam: PAC’s Cause of Death Revealed After Sudden Passing at 40
raw_title: PAC’s Cause of Death Revealed After Sudden Passing at 40
summary_src: PAC’s cause of death has finally been revealed weeks after the AEW star was found unresponsive inside a rental car near Chicago O’Hare International Airport.
body: The New York Post reported on October 16 that the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office determined Benjamin Satterley, better known to wrestling fans as PAC, died from bronchial asthma. His manner of death was officially ruled natural. A spokesperson for the medical examiner’s office confirmed the finding following the investigation into Satterley’s sudden September 27 death . The ruling brings an answer to a case that had remained open while officials waited on additional testing following the initial autopsy. Satterley was discovered unconscious inside a rental vehicle outside a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois, at around 4 p.m. on September 27. First responders rushed to the scene and attempted life-saving measures, but the 40-year-old wrestler was pronounced dead at approximately 4:08 p.m. The circumstances surrounding his death immediately raised questions because there were no obvious signs of trauma or foul play. Police noted that Satterley had saliva on the front of his shirt, while medication was also found inside the vehicle. The specific medication was redacted from the publicly released incident report. His phone provided another look at what he had been doing before his death. Google Maps was still open with directions to Chicago O’Hare International Airport, where Satterley was preparing to catch a flight back to the United Kingdom. A woman who spoke with police said Satterley had planned to stop at CAVA for lunch before heading to the airport after his flight had been delayed. The 911 call later revealed just how suddenly the situation unfolded. The woman who found Satterley said his vehicle was still running while he remained completely unresponsive inside. “We’ve been banging on the window for I want to say, like, five minutes now. His face is, like, straight down. Apparently their eyes are open, too. I don’t see his chest moving at all.” The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office performed an autopsy shortly after Satterley’s death but did not immediately announce a cause. Officials said additional testing was needed before a final determination could be made. That delay led to plenty of questions about what examiners were looking for, but the final ruling now makes clear that Satterley died from bronchial asthma and that his death was natural. Satterley had been in the Chicago area for AEW All Out and wrestled Andrade the night before his death. His sudden passing stunned the wrestling world, with AEW, WWE and numerous wrestlers paying tribute to him in the days that followed. PAC’s death remained one of wrestling’s biggest unanswered stories for nearly three weeks, but the medical examiner has now closed the biggest question surrounding what happened. The official ruling is bronchial asthma, with the manner of death listed as natural. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.

A spokesperson for the medical examiner’s office made official the finding after the investigation into Satterley’s sudden September 27 death .

summary_src: Samoa Joe doesn’t have a problem with wrestlers slapping their thighs to make strikes sound better, but he does have one pretty simple rule — don’t let everyone see you doing it. Once fans can spot the slap, Joe believes the whole trick has basically stopped working.
body: Speaking to SHAK Wrestling , Joe was asked about the long-running debate surrounding thigh slaps in wrestling. While some fans enjoy the extra pop they can give kicks and other strikes, Joe’s issue isn’t really with the technique itself. “I think if people are seeing it, you probably shouldn’t be doing it.” “Yeah, absolutely. Like, the fact that we’re having that conversation, you know, to me, it sucks.” “Yeah, it really does. It just sucks. It sucks that we’re having that conversation.” For Joe, the issue seems pretty straightforward: the technique itself isn’t the problem as long as nobody notices it. Once fans start watching the slap instead of buying into the strike, part of the illusion wrestling is trying to create is already gone. title: On the Record: Becky Lynch Says Triple H Offered to Keep Paying Her When She Needed Time Away From WWE
raw_title: Becky Lynch Says Triple H Offered to Keep Paying Her When She Needed Time Away From WWE
summary_src: Becky Lynch says Triple H went out of his way to make sure she could step away from WWE without immediately losing her paycheck when she hit a point of burnout. Lynch revealed that when she told Paul “Triple H” Levesque she needed time away, his response was to offer a way for her existing ...
body: Lynch opened up about the situation during the 2026 espnW: Women + Sports Summit while discussing how WWE has supported her as both a performer and a mother. The conversation started with Lynch recalling how supportive WWE had been when she first became pregnant while she was champion. Vince McMahon congratulated her immediately, and Lynch said the company placed no pressure on her to rush back after giving birth. She then revealed that WWE showed her the same kind of flexibility years later when she reached another difficult point in her career. Instead of trying to convince Lynch to stay on the road, Levesque offered to extend the arrangement she already had so she could continue getting paid while taking the time she needed. “And he was like, ‘Well, let’s just, whatever you’re on, let’s just prolong it so that at least you can get paid until you feel like you’re ready to come back.’” The larger issue, according to Lynch, is that professional wrestling can still be a brutal business to navigate as a parent. WWE operates year-round, and performers have historically spent several nights every week traveling from city to city. “But the thing about wrestling is that it’s 52 weeks a year. You’re in a different city, right? Sometimes four, five nights a week and you’re on the road.” “WWE has been very good at facilitating like, ‘Okay, you’re a mom. Okay, we’re not going to put you on live events. You’ll be at TV.’” “I’ll put her to bed on a Sunday night, get on a red eye, do Monday Night Raw, and then fly back as early as I can. So really, I only miss one sleep.” Derek Holloway Derek Holloway is a writer at Ringside News specializing in professional wrestling news, rumors, and results. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: On the Record: Becky Lynch Says Becoming a Mom at Height of WWE Run Was About Proving Women Don’t Have to Choose
raw_title: Becky Lynch Says Becoming a Mom at Height of WWE Run Was About Proving Women Don’t Have to Choose
summary_src: Becky Lynch was sitting on top of WWE when she decided to start a family, and she now says part of that decision was about proving women shouldn’t have to sacrifice one dream to have another.
body: Speaking during the 2026 espnW: Women + Sports Summit , Lynch revealed that the same event actually played a role in changing how she viewed motherhood years earlier. “I will say this panel has a lot to answer for because in 2019 I was sitting on this panel and I was with this sprinter Shelly-Ann Fraser, and she was talking about how she had a two-year-old and she came back, and I was like, ‘Oh, it can be done. You can do that. You can go have a kid and come back and be at the top of your game.’ Six months later…” That realization came while Lynch was experiencing the biggest run of her WWE career. She had already main-evented WrestleMania and was in the middle of a 399-day championship reign when she eventually stepped away from WWE after becoming pregnant. Lynch said she had always wanted a family and felt she had found the right person to build one with in Seth Rollins. What she didn’t accept was the idea that motherhood automatically meant surrendering everything she had worked for professionally. “Well, you know, for me, I always wanted to have a family. I met the perfect partner. And, you know, for me, it didn’t feel like I was giving up my top spot. It felt like I was doing something with my top spot because before it was, if you go off and you have a kid, well then that’s it. Goodbye.” Lynch’s goal was bigger than simply proving that she personally could make a comeback. She looked at the biggest male wrestlers and saw that they were never expected to choose between becoming fathers and remaining at the top of WWE. “I wanted to show that I could have everything, you know, like the top men, they don’t have to choose whether they have a family or they’re on top of the game. And I was like, ‘Huh, well, if they don’t have to choose, why would I have to choose?’ And it was the best decision I’ve ever made.” Years later, Lynch believes that mindset has become much more common inside WWE. She pointed to the growing number of mothers in the locker room and said women now understand that having children doesn’t automatically mean walking away from their careers. For Lynch, becoming a mother wasn’t the end of her run as one of WWE’s biggest stars. She came back, won more championships and helped prove the exact point she wanted to make when she first stepped away. title: John Bradshaw Layfield named new president of Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame
raw_title: Former WWE Champion named new president of the Tragos/Thesz Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) The following press release was issued on Friday to announce the new president of the George Tragos/Lous Thesz Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame. WATERLOO, Iowa – The National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum ‘s George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame announced Wednesday that Gerry Brisco is stepping down as president of its board of directors and moving into an advisory role. John Bradshaw Layfield will replace Brisco as president, effective immediately. “I’m happy to be leaving the board in the capable hands of JBL, and I am confident that he and his support team will ensure that the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame continues to grow and remain the best,” said Brisco, who won multiple championships in the NWA and WWE and is a member of multiple halls of fame, including the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame. “I’m honored that Mr. Brisco has chosen me to help continue the incredible success he has worked so hard to achieve,” said Layfield. “The team and I look forward to growing the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame and moving forward in building the Global Hall of Fame brand.” Global Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame, LLC, which will work closely with the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame, was created to expand opportunities to serve the Hall of Fame, the Dan Gable Museum, professional wrestlers and the sport of professional wrestling. “The GPW Hall of Fame will not affect fans or the enshrinement of members of the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame,” said Layfield, who serves as president of the organization. “We will announce more details in the future, but we view this as a win-win situation for both the GPW Hall of Fame and the Tragos/Thesz Hall of Fame.” Powell’s POV: Briscoe did a terrific job as president, and hopefully JBL will do the same. It’s been a few years since I last attended the annual Hall of Fame weekend in Waterloo, Iowa, but I had a great time and highly recommend it.
summary: Gerry Brisco has stepped down as president of the George Tragos/Lou Thesz Professional Wrestling Hall of Fame and transitioned to an advisory role. John Bradshaw Layfield immediately assumes the presidency and expressed his commitment to building on Brisco's success while expanding the Global Hall of Fame brand. The announcement was made by the National Wrestling Hall of Fame Dan Gable Museum.

title: Kaitlyn has no plans to wrestle again
raw_title: Kaitlyn on whether she wants to wrestle again, the best match of her career, winning the WWE Divas Championship
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Do you think this version of yourself would ever wrestle again? “I hope no one hates me for this, but I don’t really want to get back in the ring. I respect wrestling a lot, and I find it very entertaining. I love the artistry of it. I don’t think I could ever have the appreciation that I have now if I had never been a professional wrestler. Because there are so many aspects to the performance. There’s so many things to think about. The psychology of the match, connecting with people, telling a story with your face and your body, protecting your face and your body, protecting the person that you’re in the ring with, helping them perform to their best. Knowing where the cameras are, knowing how much time you have, being able to change it up if the people in the audience aren’t buying it, if they don’t care about it, so there’s so much to it. It’s such a beautiful art form, so I will always love it and deeply respect it. I don’t really watch it, but occasionally I will if there’s someone that I’m still friends with or that I love. Occasionally I’ll watch a match, but I don’t know. I don’t think I am gonna get back in the ring because I don’t have this burning desire to do that.” Not everybody gets to be the Divas Champion, and you were only there for four years, but you got to be the person there. You got to win the Divas Championship. So take me to that day when you found out that you’re going to win. “Just like everything in my wrestling career, it was so surreal. I didn’t really have time to process it, but I knew that Eve wanted to leave, and again, we had such a beautiful relationship; she elevated me so much, and she wanted to leave and start a family and do something different in her life. So I felt this enormous honor to be the person that received the title from her in her farewell match; it was so important because there were multiple things happening. Also yeah, wrestling is scripted and written, and when you’re the champ, they decide you’re going to be the champ. But I think that in a lot of ways is more powerful than you just randomly winning a match. This is just how I see it. I became a person who was worthy of holding the championship, and especially knowing the way that I started, that was so significant to me. I did it. I was scared and afraid that I wasn’t going to be able to live up to being the type of champion that Eve was. Then to be able to win the title in my hometown as a babyface was very cool in front of all my friends and family, and Houston wrestling fans are so supportive, and every once in a while people still recognize me around here. But it was just one of the coolest and most profound moments of my life.” “So we were getting some of that stuff. title: Former MITB Winner Says Edge’s Original Cash-In Changed WWE Forever
raw_title: Former MITB Winner Says Edge’s Original Cash-In Changed WWE Forever
body: Containing a contract that guarantees a championship match of choice at any time, any place (within a calendar year), the Money in the Bank briefcase is one of the most coveted possessions in pro wrestling. Few people admire its career-altering ability more than Nic Nemeth , known as Dolph Ziggler in WWE , who won the prized Money in the Bank briefcase in 2012. Ever the underdog, Ziggler used the briefcase to capture the World Heavyweight Championship and establish himself as a main event talent . In an exclusive interview shared with Heavy, Nemeth praised Edge for being the first Money in the Bank winner to showcase the briefcase’s game-changing power. Nemeth believes that Edge’s inaugural cash-in forever changed the WWE landscape, saying, “The first one, we didn’t know what it was. Edge comes out and he’s standing there with Vince, and he hands him the briefcase. I’m asking, is this how it works? Is this the thing? “What a great introduction and loophole for people like myself. Because that was the way some people could only ever kick in that door and make it to that real gold circle in Vince’s eyes ,” Nemeth told Casino.org . Play Nemeth also said he believes the Money in the Bank should be reserved for rising stars trying to claw their way to the top, not established megastars. “ When you’re already in the gold circle, get the hell out of here . You can show up on a Monday or Friday and go, I’m fighting for that title, and everyone goes, yay! Save that other stuff for us,” Nemeth told Casino.org . Money in the Bank has largely been a tool to fast-track midcard wrestlers into the WWE elite. Edge, CM Punk and Nemeth (formerly Dolph Ziggler) all experienced a meteoric rise after successfully cashing in the Money in the Bank briefcase. Penta, the winner of this year’s Men’s Money in the Bank Ladder match, is determined to experience a similar ascension. During the Oct. 12 episode of RAW , Penta sent a strong warning to reigning champions, and declared that he will cash in to become a World Champion . He added , “This briefcase means everything to me. Because now I have the power in my hands. So champs, watch your back. Because you don’t know when, you don’t know where, but when Penta decides to cash in, I will become a World Champion!” Penta didn’t just declare his championship goal; he did it in style. Over the years, WWE superstars have begun customizing the generic green-and-yellow MITB briefcase with designs that match their own flair and persona. Naomi had the warning tape briefcase. Edge flashed a Rated-R briefcase. Tiffany Stratton debuted a Barbie-themed briefcase. Perhaps no design is better than Penta’s “Dinero Del Banco” briefcase, which comes equipped with pyro(!). Like so many legends before him, Penta could use the tricked-out briefcase to capture his first World Championship . Jalyn Smoot Jalyn Smoot is a sports journalist covering the NBA for Heavy.com. body: Officials have determined what killed wrestling star Benjamin Satterley . A spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office told the California Post on Friday that following a probe into his sudden death , investigators concluded Satterley — who performed in AEW rings as “Pac” — passed away from bronchial asthma. The manner of his death was officially ruled natural, the rep added. Satterley was discovered unconscious in a rental car outside of a CAVA in Des Plaines, Ill. at around 4 p.m. on Sept. 27. A 911 caller stated she had found Satterley “passed out” in his ride, and authorities formally pronounced him deceased just minutes after getting to the scene. First responders wrote in an incident report that there were no injuries or “suspicious markings” on Satterley when they located his body. They did note, however, that he had saliva on the front of his shirt and medication in his vehicle. The incident report also stated that one officer on the scene was able to make contact with a woman who knew Satterley, and she told them that the wrestler had stopped for lunch before heading to the airport. Satterley’s phone had Google Maps open and a route to O’Hare Airport was on display, according to the report. Satterley had been in the area for his gig with AEW. On Sept. 26, he wrestled against Andrade at the NOW Arena in Chicago. He ended up losing in the All Out pay-per-view contest, but he later showed up in during the main event matchup between Jon Moxley and Will Ospreay.
summary: Officials ruled Benjamin Satterley, known in AEW as Pac, died of natural causes from bronchial asthma. The 37-year-old was found unconscious in a rental car outside a Des Plaines, Illinois restaurant on September 27 while heading to the airport after an AEW event. First responders noted medication in the vehicle, saliva on his shirt and no signs of injury or foul play.

body: AEW star Benjamin Satterley, known to fans as "Pac," died of bronchial asthma, the California Post reported, citing a spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner's Office. Benjamin Satterley was found unresponsive in a rental car parked outside a CAVA restaurant on Mannheim Road in Des Plaines , Illinois, at around 4 p.m. local time on September 27. He was pronounced dead at the scene. His death came less than a day after he competed at AEW All Out 2026 on September 26. He challenged Andrade El Ídolo for the AEW National Championship but lost, and later appeared in the main event. AEW announced his death and paid tribute to the wrestler, remembering his career and contributions to the sport. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans," AEW said. He soon earned nicknames such as “The Super Superman” and “The Man That Gravity Forgot” for his athleticism and high-flying style. He began wrestling internationally in 2007 and performed as Adrian Neville in WWE from 2012 to 2018. After joining AEW in 2019, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. News of Satterley’s death prompted tributes from wrestlers and wrestling executives. Fellow wrestler Will Ospreay remembered him as both an exceptional performer and a close friend. “The greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being,” Ospreay wrote on X. “Honored to have shared the ring with you so many times. You truly are such a hero to myself and many others.” AEW president Tony Khan also paid tribute to Satterley, writing, "Benjamin Satterley defined excellence, as a beloved husband & friend to his many loved ones, + in his wrestling knowledge, skill, unprecedented athleticism, professionalism, consistency + dedication to the sport that he loved & traveled the world to pursue. May Ben rest in peace." WWE chief content officer Triple H , who worked with Satterley during his time in WWE, also mourned his death.

summary_src: Less than one month ago, the professional wrestling world was rocked by the news that Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as Pac in AEW and Neville in WWE, died at the young age of 40-years-old.
body: Because of his age and the circumstances, it was certainly understandable that speculation ran rampant as fans tried to digest and process the loss of a beloved wrestler gone far too soon. It only took days for reports to get out offering some information on the circumstances surrounding his death. He was found in his car unresponsive but additional testing would be needed to determine an exact cause of death. The word on that was it would be a number of weeks before that would be the case but there was no reason to suspect foul play. The New York Post is now reporting a spokesperson for the Cook County Medical Examiner’s office revealed investigators have determined he died of natural causes, namely bronchial asthma. title: Cop claims WWE wrestler 'grinded' on him at ringside in 'sexualised lap dance'
raw_title: Cop claims WWE wrestler 'grinded' on him at ringside in 'sexualised lap dance'
body: An off-duty sheriff’s deputy has launched a lawsuit against WWE and one of its stars. This comes after he claimed he was subjected to a “sexualised lap dance” while working security at a televised event in Chicago, Illinois, USA. Noel Lucas, a Cook County Sheriff’s officer doing private in Illinois, off-duty security work, has filed a 14-count claim against World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), its subsidiary Event Services LLC, and wrestler Kenneth Crawford, known to fans as Montez Ford of tag team The Street Profits. The incident is alleged to have happened during Monday Night Raw at the Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois, on July 6, during a show broadcast live on Netflix . According to the lawsuit, obtained by the Daily Mail, Lucas was directed by a WWE employee to take up a position near ringside and was instructed to remain at his post. But as The Street Profits made their entrance, the filing claims Ford approached Lucas “without warning or consent” and performed an explicit routine over him. “Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff [Lucas], repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized [sic] ‘lap dance,’” the lawsuit reads. Lucas also reportedly alleges the wrestler moved increasingly closer during the routine, with physical contact escalating. He claims Crawford’s left inner thigh was “repeatedly” rubbing against his leg. The deputy says the moment exploded online after airing and being shared in a promotional clip. Consequently, the fallout has reportedly followed him back into daily life. When Lucas returned to his full-time job at a local courthouse the next day, he says members of the public recognised him from viral clips and mocked him. “Members of the public recognized [sic] him from the videos of the encounter that had circulated on social media and mocked him, thrusting their hips in his direction, imitating the sexual movements [allegedly performed during the broadcast],” the lawsuit states. Lucas claims the situation also hit his family. Moreover, he alleged his children were “mocked and ridiculed” at school because of the viral footage, while he has suffered “substantial humiliation, embarrassment, and emotional distress”. The suit reportedly includes claims of assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress, and alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. It also alleges a breach of the Illinois Right of Publicity Act, arguing WWE and Ford used Lucas’ clearly visible image for commercial promotion without authorisation. Lucas is seeking unspecified damages, punitive damages, legal fees, and a court order stopping WWE from continuing to use his identity. A case management hearing is set for December 10. summary_src: When WWE heads for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia early next month, assuming it still happens, of course, they’ll do so with a card that features two champion vs. champion matches for the Crown Jewel championship. body: Link WWE Geno Mrosko is a lifelong pro wrestling fan who has been covering it since becoming a Manager at Cageside Seats in 2011. When WWE heads for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia early next month, assuming it still happens , of course, they’ll do so with a card that features two champion vs. champion matches for the Crown Jewel championship. That means World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will be taking on WWE Champion Sami Zayn. Are they going to spend much time actually building to this match? Probably not. That was evidenced by this week’s episode of Friday Night SmackDown , where Zayn made mention of the matchup and pushed off actually doing anything to promote it until Monday Night Raw next week when they’ll be in the same building. Instead, we got United States Champion Trick Williams interrupting to say he wants to settle up on the disrespectful interaction the two had a couple weeks back. summary_src: Indian veteran pacer Bhuvneshwar Kumar could be set for a spectacular comeback to international cricket after being drafted into the T20I squad for the last T20I against the West Indies.
body: Bhuvneshwar Kumar's comeback was confirmed recently when the selectors included him in the squad for the upcoming five-match T20I series in New Zealand. However, recent circumstances mean that he has a chance of donning the international colors earlier than expected. If Bhuvneshwar Kumar does feature in the playing XI for the fifth T20I at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru, it will end a lengthy wait. His last appearance in international cricket came during the tour of New Zealand in late 2022. Bhuvneshwar Kumar played the third T20I of the series on November 22, 2022, at McLean Park in Napier. He ended with figures of 0-35 in four overs as New Zealand were bowled for 160 in the first innings. His fellow pace bowling partners, Arshdeep Singh and Mohammed Siraj, picked up four wickets each to bundle out New Zealand for 160 from 130-2. India scored 75-4 in nine overs, before rain had the final say. With the visitors managing to hit the DLS par score just in time before rain interrupted, the match was declared a tie. The veteran pacer's last international appearance on home soil was during the three-match T20I series against Australia during the build-up to the T20 World Cup 2022. On September 25, 2022, the pacer recorded figures of 1-39 in three overs in the high-scoring series finale in Hyderabad. Bhuvneshwar Kumar dismissed Cameron Green in the first innings, but was the most expensive bowler on show as Australia posted 186-7. India managed to chase down the score with a ball to spare and complete a turnaround in the series from a 0-1 deficit. 34 of Bhuvneshwar Kumar's 87 T20I appearances have come on home soil, which does not include his years of experience in the Indian Premier League (IPL). With the series on the line against West Indies, he comes across as a massive boost to the bowling unit that has largely struggled so far. The fifth T20I between India and West Indies is scheduled to be held on Saturday, October 17.

title: In Memoriam: All Elite Wrestling Star Pac’s Cause of Death Revealed After Investigation Into His Sudden Passing
raw_title: All Elite Wrestling Star Pac’s Cause of Death Revealed After Investigation Into His Sudden Passing
body: All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley ’s (a.k.a. Pac) cause of death has been revealed. A Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office spokesperson told the California Post on Friday, October 16 that after an investigation, it was determined that Benjamin died from bronchial asthma. Benjamin was pronounced dead on September 27 after his body was found behind the wheel of a rental car in a Des Plaines, Illinois, parking lot. He was 40. When authorities arrived on the scene of Benjamin’s death , they “did not find any injuries or suspicious markings on him besides what appeared to be saliva on the front of his shirt,” according to a report from the Des Plaines Police Department obtained by Us on October 5. Benjamin’s family broke their silence about his death with a statement read by AEW on-air personality Renee Paquette during an episode of Dynamite on September 30. The statement added, “Thank you to all of Ben’s fans for their support over the years. We send you our love and have been so moved to see so many people saying so many wonderful things about his impact on their lives, whether great or small. We will love you forever, Ben, and our lives will never be the same without you. Thank you, the Satterley family.” Benjamin’s widow, Natalie Satterley, later shared her devastation over the loss. “The cruelty of having all of our future hopes and dreams snatched away will never feel real,” Natalie wrote via Instagram on Monday, October 12. “You were so excited to get home to us, you were going to shoot hoops all week with your best mates, we were going to set up your new home gym and take [dog Wolfie] for some autumnal walks, have pizza at Rudy’s on your cheat day, go to the match, see [comedian] Sam Campbell live.” Continue with Google --> --> --> --> Continue with Facebook --> --> Continue with Amazon --> Continue with Apple We won't post to any of your accounts Continue with Google --> --> --> --> Continue with Facebook --> --> Continue with Amazon --> Continue with Apple We won't post to any of your accounts

title: Legal Watch: Montez Ford, WWE Sued Over Alleged Unwanted Contact
raw_title: Montez Ford, WWE Sued Over Alleged Unwanted Contact
body: Posted in: Sports , TV , WWE | Tagged: montez ford , wrestling , WWE Raw Report: A Cook County Sheriff's officer has filed a lawsuit against Montez Ford and the WWE over an alleged incident during WWE Raw. A Cook County Sheriff's officer has reportedly filed a civil lawsuit against World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), performer Montez Ford , and a company subsidiary. The suit stems from an interaction at the July 6, 2026 episode of Monday Night Raw at Allstate Arena in Rosemont, Illinois. The complaint was reportedly filed Wednesday, October 14, 2026, in the Circuit Court of Cook County, according to POST Wrestling's report on the complaint . The alleged incident took place during the entrance of The Street Profits at the live Netflix broadcast of Raw . The officer alleges that a WWE employee directed him to his ringside position, that he was never told he would be part of the performance, and that he did not consent to the contact he describes. "Defendant Crawford then began performing a sexually provocative dance immediately in front of and over Plaintiff, repeatedly thrusting and gyrating his hips and pelvis towards Plaintiff, performing a sexualized 'lap dance.'" POST Wrestling's account of the filing adds that Ford allegedly "moved his body increasingly closer to" and that his "left inner thigh repeatedly rubbed against Plaintiff's leg." These passages represent the plaintiff's version of events as presented in the court filing. Neither outlet reports a response from the defendants disputing or confirming the reports, and the incident no longer appears in the version of the show streaming on Netflix at this time, nor can it be found in the company's social media posts from the event. The complaint reportedly contains 14 counts. POST Wrestling lists assault, battery, and intentional infliction of emotional distress among them, along with claims under the Illinois Gender Violence Act and the Illinois Right of Publicity Act. The publicity claim relates to the footage itself. FOX 32 Chicago reports that the complaint alleges WWE shared video of the interaction on TikTok and Instagram, and that Ford also shared footage on his own social media. POST Wrestling reports that the officer alleges the clip's circulation led to public ridicule and emotional distress. As for remedies, POST Wrestling reports that the officer seeks unspecified monetary damages, punitive damages, and court costs. He also seeks an order barring further use of his identity. A case-management hearing is reportedly set for December 10, 2026. FOX 32 Chicago quotes Lucas's attorney, Whitney Barr , as saying, "[The Plaintiff] was there to do his job, not to be made a part of WWE's entertainment." Barr also stated, per the same outlet, that "Entertainment is not a defense to unwanted sexual contact." As the matter proceeds toward its scheduled December 10 case-management hearing, any formal answer from the defendants or any change to the docket would clarify the competing positions.

A Cook County Sheriff's officer has by most accounts filed a civil lawsuit against World Wrestling Entertainment, performer Montez Ford , and a company subsidiary.
