title: WWE strikes intriguing content partnership as pro wrestling's popularity continues to soar
raw_title: WWE strikes intriguing content partnership as pro wrestling's popularity continues to soar
body: WWE announced a strategic content partnership with Bleacher Report on Monday. Bleacher Report will have the global rights to highlights across WWE’s programming, including "Monday Night Raw," "Friday Night SmackDown," NXT and premium live events, the company said in a news release. Bleacher Report will also have a presence at certain WWE premium live events. "Bleacher Report has long been at the intersection of sports and culture," WWE executive vice president Alex Varga said in a statement. "Our partnership with B/R reinforces WWE’s commitment to bringing our content to a global audience." Bleacher Report general manager Bennett Spector added, "WWE fans don’t just watch. They are highly engaged, analyze every detail and debate the sport all week long. That’s exactly the kind of passionate fandom B/R and House of Highlights were built for. "This partnership gives us the opportunity to bring fans closer to the biggest moments happening today while also tapping into the incredible history and personalities that have made WWE part of sports culture for generations." On the surface, the partnership appeared to be just another way for WWE to further its global reach across social media. WWE boasts more than 102 million followers on Facebook, 40.1 million followers on TikTok, 35 million followers on Instagram and 13 million followers on X. But the deal comes days after Paramount reached a settlement with states that sued to block the Warner Bros. Discovery takeover. Warner Bros. Discovery announced in June 2025 it planned to keep TNT Sports and Bleacher Report under Global Networks, separating it form its TV and film endeavors. Sportico reported in December that was still the plan for the end of 2026. Bleacher Report previously hosted AEW pay-per-views on its streaming platform before discontinuing it in 2024. Khan has repeatedly welcomed the merger and reiterated his happiness after All Out over the weekend. "Now, we enter something that I consider more of a known quantity and I’m very excited about it. I think we’ve proven that AEW is a feather in the cap of a media company that we are a great partner, and for me, I’ll work to make sure that AEW fits in any corporate structure. I’ll work very hard, and I think I’ve proven time after time that I am the ultimate corporate soldier, and that is why AEW continues to grow and expand as the media landscape changes and I think that’s why Warner Bros., even as the company has evolved and changed, AEW has always been a very important part of the portfolio for years and years and I expect that’s gonna continue with AEW and Warner Bros. for many years to come."

title: In Memoriam: Cause of death revealed for All Elite Wrestling star Pac
raw_title: Cause of death revealed for All Elite Wrestling star Pac
body: 0 Benjamin Satterley, known as Pac, died of natural causes, the Cook County (Illinois) Medical Examiner’s Office ruled. A cause of death has been determined in the death of wrestler Benjamin Satterley , also known as Pac in All Elite Wrestling. Satterly died of bronchial asthma, according to the Cook County (Illinois) Medical Examiner’s Office. The death was ruled natural. The 40-year-old wrestler died on Sunday, Sept. 27 after he was found inside a vehicle at a Cava parking lot in the city of Des Plaines, Illinois, just outside of Chicago O’Hare International Airport. According to a police report , Pac was found "unconscious and unresponsive, slumped over, in a vehicle." Responding authorities attempted life saving measures, but hewas later pronounced dead at the scene. Officials noted they "did not find any injuries or suspicious markings on him besides what appeared to be saliva on the front of his shirt." An autopsy was perfomed the following day. Pac became a prominent wrestler after joining WWE in 2012 as Neville, becoming one of the best Cruiserweight stars with the company until he departed in 2017. He then joined upstart All Elite Wrestling in January 2019, where he worked for the remainder of his career. He held multiple AEW Championships while being part of major factions like the Death Triangle and Death Riders. AEW held a tribute show in honor of Pac on Wednesday, Sept. 30.

title: Austin Creed Hints at New UpUpDownDown Successor in AEW Era
raw_title: Austin Creed Hints at New UpUpDownDown Successor in AEW Era
body: Speaking with Phid McAwesome at PAX Australia , Creed discussed leaving the gaming channel behind and hinted at the possibility of working with his former Da Party teammates again. Creed spent years building UpUpDownDown into a popular channel for wrestling fans. It gave them a chance to see their favorite WWE superstars outside the ring. The channel featured wrestlers playing video games, taking part in challenges, and showing their personalities away from their regular TV appearances. However, Creed’s departure from WWE in May meant he had to leave the project behind. Despite losing access to the channel, the AEW star seems confident that he can create something new. When asked about how it felt leaving UpUpDownDown, Creed said, One big question is whether Creed could reunite with Da Party for another gaming project. The group includes Creed, Tyler Breeze, Adam Cole, and Claudio Castagnoli. All four share a love for video games, and their chemistry made their gaming sessions popular with wrestling fans. Cole, Castagnoli, and Creed are now signed to AEW, while Breeze is a free agent. Since none of the four are currently under WWE contract, working together on a new project may be easier than it was when they were part of WWE. Creed addressed the possibility but also admitted he wouldn’t confirm any plans. “None of the Da Party members are currently signed with WWE. And that would lead me to believe that there is at least the chance that something will happen. The chance of something to be created is available. I will not confirm or deny if anyone has been filming anything or if anyone has been creating assets for a new YouTube channel. I will not confirm or deny that,” Creed said. Creed then explained that his friendships with WWE Superstars helped make UpUpDownDown successful. He wants to build similar connections with the AEW locker room before starting a similar project. “I would hope that maybe there would be a chance to do something with video games, I don’t know. I cannot say. But that rapport with the locker room is first and foremost the most important thing,” Creed said. body: AEW All Out was live and loud from the sold-out NOW Arena in Chicago, Illinois, on HBO Max PPV for another historic night from a town and venue synonymous with All Elite Wrestling! With seven championships up for grabs over nine matches, only one title changed hands. The main event saw AEW World Champion Will Ospreay retain his title over AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley with appearances by the Death Riders, United Empire and AEW Women’s World Tag Team Champions The Brawling Birds. Until tonight, Ospreay had never beaten Moxley, and he needed everything he learned from Moxley and more to successfully defend his AEW World Championship. The AEW World Tag Team Titles belong to the Young Bucks for a record-setting fourth time after pulling them down to win the wild and chaotic ladder match over Cope and Cage and FTR. We were treated to yet another spectacular AEW World Trios Championship match with Swerve Strickland and The New Level outlasting former champions ”Hangman” Adam Page and Brodido in a match that saw a lot of personal feelings come back to the surface between Strickland and Page in the very building where they nearly ended each other’s careers two years ago. Thekla defeated Willow Nightingale to earn a shot at AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné next month at AEW WrestleDream, and Moné came out after the match to stare down her next challenger. The Brawling Birds retained the AEW Women’s World Tag Team Titles in a violent Chicago Street Fight with Divine Dominion. AEW National Champion Andrade El Ídolo turned away PAC in the opening contest to notch his fifth successful defense. “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada provided “Psycho Killer” Tommaso Ciampa with a match he’s wanted for a long time, but it was Okada who kept the AEW International Title. title: In Memoriam: Wrestler 'Pac' dies in Des Plaines, Illinois one day after AEW competition in nearby Hoffman Estates — Benjamin Satterley death
raw_title: Benjamin Satterley death: Wrestler 'Pac' dies in Des Plaines, Illinois one day after AEW competition in nearby Hoffman Estates
body: Benjamin Satterley, an English-born wrestler known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide, has died. He was 40. WLS CHICAGO (WLS) -- Benjamin Satterley, the professional wrestler known to fans as "Pac," died Sunday, less than 24 hours after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates, a northern suburb of Chicago, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner. Satterley, 40, wrestled Saturday night at NOW Arena before his death was reported Sunday in nearby Des Plaines. The medical examiner has not yet determined a cause of death and said it may be several weeks before autopsy results are available. The news shocked fans who watched the English-born wrestler perform the night before, including Jayson Weidman, who attended the event. Inside NOW Arena on Saturday, Satterley competed for All Elite Wrestling under the ring name Pac. The English wrestler, who previously performed in WWE as Adrian Neville, was known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. "There are wrestlers that can do incredible things, and then there's wrestlers who can do things that you question how it's even humanly possible that they can do what they're doing. Pac was one of those wrestlers," Weidman said. Satterley, who was from Newcastle upon Tyne, began his wrestling career in 2004 and signed in 2019 with All Elite Wrestling, where he held multiple championships. He competed and lost to Andrade El Ídolo on Saturday in Chicago in the AEW National Championship. Weidman said he purchased his seat specifically in hopes of being close to Pac and his group, the Death Riders. "It was such a special moment for me to be able to see him wrestle," Weidman said. SEE ALSO: Chris Spatola, ESPN analyst and son-in-law of Duke legend Coach K, dies suddenly at 47 He quickly rose to prominence, earning nicknames like "The Super Superman" and "The Man That Gravity Forgot." He began his international journey in 2007 and wrestled under the name of Adrian Neville from 2012 to 2018. After signing with AEW, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. According to Weidman, Pac wrestled in Saturday's opening match and later returned during the main event. "He looked healthy as can be, and it's unbelievable how less than 24 hours, he could possibly be gone," Weidman said. The Cook County Medical Examiner said Satterley died shortly after 4 p.m. Sunday at 2761 Mannheim Road in Des Plaines. A restaurant employee at that address said Satterley never entered the business. Outside the location, at least one fan left a vase on the sidewalk in tribute to the wrestler. All Elite Wrestling also paid tribute to Satterley on its Facebook page, writing: "The very best of us. Truly one of a kind. We love you and we miss you, Ben. We always will." As fans continue to mourn Satterley's death, Weidman said the wrestler's legacy extends beyond his accomplishments in the ring. title: In Memoriam: AEW star Pac's death leaves pro wrestling world in disbelief
raw_title: AEW star Pac's death leaves pro wrestling world in disbelief
body: The death of pro wrestling star Pac left the pro wrestling world in utter disbelief on Sunday night. All Elite Wrestling (AEW) announced Pac’s death just one day after he wrestled against Andrade El Idolo for the national championship at All Out in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. He was 40. Many pro wrestlers posted heartfelt tributes to Pac, whose real name is Benjamin Satterley, on social media with many in shock because most had just seen him wrestle on the pay-per-view. Pac was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. He was a member of The Death Riders faction who supported their leader, Jon Moxley. He also competed for WWE before joining AEW under the name Adrian Neville. He was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion. Pac got his start on the independent circuit in 2004 and quickly became a fixture at Pro Wrestling Guerrilla. He also performed at Dragon Gate USA, Wrestle Zone Wrestling, One Pro Wrestling, Frontier Wrestling Alliance and elsewhere. Pro Wrestling Illustrated named him the 11th best wrestler in the world in 2017.
summary: The death of pro wrestling star Pac left the pro wrestling world in utter disbelief on Sunday night. All Elite Wrestling revealed Pac’s death just one day after he wrestled against Andrade El Idolo for the national championship at All Out in Hoffman Estates, Illinois.

title: Benjamin Satterley, globetrotting wrestler known as Pac, dies at 40
raw_title: Benjamin Satterley, globetrotting wrestler known as Pac, dies at 40
body: Share Add NBC News to Google Sept. 27, 2026, 10:22 PM EDT / Updated Sept. 29, 2026, 8:31 PM EDT By Rudy Chinchilla Benjamin Satterley, the hard-hitting and high-flying professional wrestler known to fans worldwide simply as Pac, has died, All Elite Wrestling announced Sunday night. He was 40. News of his death came the day after he’d wrestled during AEW’s “All Out” pay-per-view Saturday night at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, outside Chicago. A cause of death was not immediately provided. In a statement Tuesday, the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said Satterley was found in Des Plaines, around 2 miles north of the Chicago O’Hare International Airport. An autopsy was performed Monday, it said, and a cause and manner of death will be determined after additional testing, which could take several weeks. Des Plaines police said in a statement Monday that there were no immediate indications of foul play and that the circumstances surrounding Satterley’s death were not considered suspicious. In announcing his death, AEW highlighted Satterley’s “incredible in-ring ability.” “A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” it said. Satterley first began training at 18 and made a name for himself on the British independent scene before embarking on a globetrotting career in which he performed in some of the biggest promotions on the planet, including AEW, World Wrestling Entertainment (where he went by Adrian Neville), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre. His high-flying offense, made all the more impressive by the brawny physique on his stocky frame, earned him the nickname “The Man That Gravity Forgot.” When he started training and had to choose a name, Satterley couldn’t think of anything else. “It was only meant to be kind of a temporary thing, but then it kind of — it’s one of those names that kind of, it just stuck,” he said. Satterley debuted on All Elite Wrestling in 2019, where he’d eventually earn the moniker “The Bastard.” In AEW, he won the All-Atlantic Championship in 2022 and became one of the company’s more prominent wrestlers as part of the Death Riders faction, with whom he’d earn the AEW World Trios Championship alongside fellow members Claudio Castagnoli and Wheeler Yuta in 2025. It followed another Trios title in 2022 alongside Penta El Zero Miedo and Rey Fénix as part of the “Death Triangle.” Between the ropes, few wrestlers could combine speed, agility, technique and raw power quite like Satterley. He could twist and wind his body off the top turnbuckle with his signature “Black Arrow,” or he could use his “Brutalizer” to tie up an opponent’s arms and neck on the canvas. On the microphone, his promos conveyed no-nonsense intensity that relayed an ultimately simple message to opponents: I’m here to hurt

body: TNA Wrestling Ryan Nemeth is the wrestling equivalent of: "You can go out but you have to take your brother with you." He's not the first terrible wrestling brother to ride the familial gravy train (Tonga Loa also springs to mind) but it is overly egregious how he is being booked as a singles talent. There was literally zero reason to care about the match, as Orso was not going to win, and even if he did, that's just the lesser of two evils. Because unfortunately, he's not very compelling either. And he's a heel. It was a heel vs heel match between two bad wrestlers. Nemeth won because of course he did, and now he goes on to a match that contains Fabian Aichner, KC Navarro, Cedric Alexander, and Rich Swann. He sticks out like a sore thumb from that crop because he simply doesn't belong. Without his surname he wouldn't even be in the sport let alone the company, and thus let alone the X-Division title picture. It's like a cruel catch to having someone as talented as Nic Nemeth. We just have to endure this constant over-pushing of someone who couldn't feasibly beat an egg. What does he bring to the table? What is he doing for the tag title? What is he doing for the show? It's all negative; he's a net negative. To be clear, Ryan as a lackey to his brother – fodder for a challenger or someone to play spoiler in interference — makes sense. As usual, it's TNA pushing the envelope too far and cutting its own nose off to spite its face, as well as its audience. I'd love to have been a fly on the wall when someone came up with this match and all of the subtext around it. But only because a fly has a maximum lifespan of 30 days, so I wouldn't have to worry about it much longer. When Marella and Hartwell eventually returned to TNA programming, so did Rae's spitefulness. In Hartwell's case, it led to her being purposely omitted from TNA Knockouts World Championship opportunities, with the most recent instance coming after she made Xia Brookside, the reigning champion, tap out. Instead of giving a title match to Hartwell afterward, Rae granted one to Gabby Forza, a TNA newcomer. Tonight, Hartwell avenged herself by coaxing Rae into slapping her in the face. Rae was shocked to learn that Marella had filmed the whole encounter, which he then intended to show the TNA board as reason to suspend her next. Rae was surely aware that she was being filmed by TNA's big cameras in the first place. So why would we, as viewers, have reason to believe she was genuinely shocked by Marella's secondary recording? title: Former WWE Tag Team Champions Sign With TNA
raw_title: Former WWE Tag Team Champions Sign With TNA
body: On April 24, WWE began conducting a long list of talent cuts. This included the entire Wyatt Sicks stable, which consisted of Dexter Lumis, Joe Gacy, Nikki Cross, Erick Rowan and Bo Dallas. Five months later, Lumis and Gacy have revealed their next chapter. Gacy and Lumis, now wrestling as Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw, respectively, made a surprise appearance during Thursday's episode of TNA Impact! in San Antonio, Texas. The duo attacked Matt and Jeff Hardy, revealing their identities afterward. Following the attack, TNA Wrestling announced on X (formerly Twitter) that Sawyer and Shaw have signed with the promotion. The pair have adopted the new tag team name, "Syx." This is Shaw's second tenure with TNA. He previously worked in the promotion from 2010 to 2015. Gacy and Lumis captured the WWE Tag Team Championship on one occasion, emerging victorious in a six-pack tag team match at SummerSlam 2025. They held the titles for 196 days , eventually losing them to Tama Tonga and Solo Sikoa on the Jan. 23 episode of SmackDown .

title: MLW Finally Gets Its Tubi Deal (Exclusive)
raw_title: MLW Finally Gets Its Tubi Deal (Exclusive)
body: At long last, MLW ( Major League Wrestling ) is headed to Tubi under a new deal. Starting tonight, Thursday, Sept. 17 at 8 p.m. ET, the pro-wrestling promotion’s flagship series MLW Fusion will stream (for free) live on the on-demand/FAST platform. News episodes will premiere each Thursday in the same time slot. This was actually the deal that was meant to happen five years ago. At the time, however, WWE allegedly pressured Tubi into canceling the deal, leveraging its relationship with Tubi-owner Fox — WWE’s SmackDown aired on the broadcast network back then. The done deal was undone the night before I was set to exclusively report it. WWE and MLW settled out of court, with the former paying the latter $20 million. Related Stories Movies R.L. Stine's 'The Babysitter' Adaptation Coming to Tubi in 2027 (Exclusive) TV Buffalo Bills' Long-Suffering Fans to Be Focus of Documentary 'Just One Before I Die' (Exclusive) MLW has undergone some significant changes since then. For starters, actor Paul Walter Hauser has joined Court Bauer and Bryan Walsh as executive producer; additionally, Major League Wrestling signed with Artists First for representation in March 2025. And in fall 2025, MLW partnered with Danny McBride’s Don Gato Tequila and moved its headquarters from New York to Charleston, South Carolina. MLW Fusion was relaunched in May 2026; the company’s pay-per-view events are now distributed by Live Nation’s Veeps. MLW Fusion episodes are also available on Veeps and NJPW World. “Wrestling should be easy to find and free to watch,” said Bauer, the founder and CEO of Major League Wrestling. “We built MLW around that, no paywalls, no subscription barriers, nothing standing between a fan and the show, and Tubi shares that same fan-first philosophy at scale. Starting Sept. 17, Tubi’s 110 million monthly active users have a front row seat on Thursday nights to the hardest hitting hour in pro wrestling, and it won’t cost a dime.” MLW Fusion “serves up a distinctive brand of pro wrestling, blending cutting-edge, new-era wrestling with the grit, colorful characters and throwback flavor of ’rasslin,” the company says. “Built around big fights, heated rivalries, championship stakes and an anything-can-happen attitude, Fusion brings a rowdy, hard-hitting edge to the modern wrestling landscape. MLW will also continue to produce live special events alongside the weekly series.”
summary: Per The Hollywood Reporter: MLW is headed to Tubi under a new deal. ET, the pro-wrestling promotion’s flagship series MLW Fusion will stream live on the on-demand/FAST platform.

The agreement revives a partnership originally planned five years earlier that was derailed after WWE allegedly influenced Tubi-owner Fox to pull out. Since then MLW has added Paul Walter Hauser as an executive producer alongside Court Bauer and Bryan Walsh, signed with Artists First for representation, partnered with Don Gato Tequila, and relocated its headquarters from New York to Charleston.

body: MLW announced on Wednesday that it will present MLW Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7, marking the promotion's first pay-per-view event in seven years. The show will stream live worldwide on Live Nation's VEEPS from Cicero Stadium in Chicago. The PPV return comes after MLW recently moved its flagship MLW Fusion series to Tubi. New episodes air Thursday nights. Saturday Night SuperFight will bring together the championship stories and rivalries that have been developing on the weekly program. "We're not coming back to pay-per-view to play it safe. November 7 is where championships will be decided, rivalries will come to a head. The best fighters in MLW will be expected to deliver on the biggest stage we've had in years. Chicago always brings an incredible atmosphere, and we're giving that crowd — and fans watching around the world — a night of super fights," Bauer said. [H/T Fightful ] MLW's current roster includes World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross, Matt Riddle, Místico, Austin Aries, The Good Brothers, CONTRA Unit and ZAMAYA. The promotion is expected to announce additional matches and championship bouts in the weeks leading up to the event. MLW will remain in the Chicago area the following night, as the promotion is scheduled to hold an MLW Fusion television taping at Cicero Stadium on November 8. body: Major League Wrestling (MLW) has been able to bring in some of the biggest and baddest competitors onto its roster with some making an immediate impact and having their eyes on gold. Savage insisted in an interview with OutKick Dropkick that Contra should still be on everyone’s radar. "Contra is a cast of misfit toys that nobody wants, nobody wants to be around because they're dangerous people, and that camaraderie that we all have together, each background that they are from, we're the dangerous people in the locker room that people usually avoid. So, you put those people in a group together and we work well together." Savage said everyone on the MLW roster is on notice, including MLW world heavyweight champion Killer Kross. Savage said he is seeking to bring gold back to Contra. "I'd list everybody on the roster – all of them. They're all on the list," he said. "The main guy at the top of my list is going to be the heavyweight champion, Killer Kross. There’s other guys along the way that I'm sure I'll get my hands on, but the main goal, the main prize is to carry the gold and the top honor at MLW, to take the heavyweight championship. Kross won the Battle Riot match at Battle Riot VIII during the start of the year. He has held the belt every day since then, putting away any opponent who has stepped up to him. Savage has been in pro wrestling for a while, making his name on the independent scene. But for those who are unfamiliar with his game, he said he wants fans to know just how dangerous he could be. "Basically, want them to know and feel how unhinged and how heinous I can be. I think the sense of danger has been lost in wrestling a lot. A lot of it's good in entertainment and stuff like that, but there hasn't been a big sense of fear and danger that feels absolutely real," he explained to OutKick Dropkick. "When I walk out the curtain, I want them to feel that oh s--- moment that this is about to get serious and ‘I need to be on my guard, my toes to pay attention about what's about to happen because who knows, I could be next.’ That's the feeling I want to introduce to people and what's coming up. For me, I feel that elevated danger is going to start to rise more and more." MLW announced earlier this month it would show its weekly series, "Fusion," on Tub i. "It’s incredible to be honest," Savage said. "Man, to already be part of the MLW roster and be part of Contra is already amazing, and then getting a Tubi deal to air free on Thursdays is absolutely insane. They're moving so fast at connecting all these pieces, it's actually incredible. "They're one of the fastest growing wrestling companies out there. So, it's an insane feeling to be a part of. So happy about that."

body: The Hollywood Reporter broke the news of the deal Thursday morning. The outlet reported that "Fusion" will air for free on the streaming service beginning tonight at 8 p.m. EST, and will continue to air in the same timeslot each week. The length of the deal was not revealed in the report. MLW just recently revived "Fusion," bringing the show back after a three-year hiatus in May 2026. Prior to the Tubi deal, the show had been airing for free on YouTube. As noted in the Hollywood Reporter report, MLW CEO Court Bauer is adamant that wrestling should be accessible to all. Tubi reportedly has around 110 million monthly users. "We built MLW around that, no paywalls, no subscription barriers, nothing standing between a fan and the show, and Tubi shares that same fan-first philosophy at scale," Bauer told THR. MLW filed its antitrust lawsuit against WWE in January 2022, alleging the bigger company pressured third parties, including Tubi, which is owned by Fox, to abandon contracts and relationships with MLW. The suit alleged Stephanie McMahon was the WWE official who convinced Tubi to end its deal with the promotion, as "WWE SmackDown" was airing on Fox at the time. The companies didn't reach a settlement in the suit until December 2023 . It was revealed the following February, in a TKO Group Holds earnings report, that the settlement cost WWE $20 million . MLW wasn't named, but the report cited the "antitrust lawsuit at WWE."

The pact arrives nearly five years after MLW's antitrust lawsuit against WWE, which claimed WWE influenced Tubi to drop its relationship with the promotion and was settled in December 2023. MLW revived its free weekly show Fusion on YouTube in May and will now expand its no-paywall approach on the Fox-owned streaming platform.

llm_long: MLW has reached a television streaming agreement with Tubi. The partnership includes a rights fee along with a revenue share tied to library content integration. The deal was finalized in August.

The agreement arrives nearly five years after MLW filed an antitrust lawsuit against WWE. The suit claimed WWE influenced Tubi to drop existing and potential deals with MLW. Tubi was owned by Fox, which broadcast WWE SmackDown during that period.
The lawsuit named Stephanie McMahon as the WWE executive who applied pressure on Tubi regarding MLW. A settlement between the parties was reached in December 2023.
MLW brought back its program Fusion in May following a three-year break. The show has been available at no cost on YouTube.

MLW owner Court Bauer stated that the promotion was built on a model with no paywalls or subscription barriers between fans and the content. He noted that Tubi follows a similar fan-first approach on a larger scale.

title: CMLL talents look to increase popularity among American pro wrestling fans with latest opportunity
raw_title: CMLL talents look to increase popularity among American pro wrestling fans with latest opportunity
body: Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL) is one of the most historic pro wrestling promotions on the planet. The company was founded in 1933 and continues to honor Lucha Libre style wrestling to this day. As pro wrestling’s popularity has increased dramatically over the years, CMLL has had the need to get more eyeballs on its product. Among the steps the company has taken, CMLL partnered with All Elite Wrestling (AEW) to feature its superstars on its programming. The partnership has allowed CMLL legends like Místico to appear at AEW and Ring of Honor shows while still being the generational figure that he is in Mexico. The same has held true for a lot of CMLL talent. The next step was to find a footing in the United States. With immense potential, CMLL held its first solo event in Las Vegas as part of Slam Fest during WrestleMania weekend . The action-packed event saw the likes of Blue Panther, Ultimo Guerrero, Persephone, Tessa Blanchard, Místico, Hechicero, Templario, Angel de Oro and others showcase their talent. Passionate pro wrestling fans could easily get hooked on the athleticism and storytelling that CMLL brings in the ring. But what about watching it at home? Where can the average pro wrestling fan watch incredible Lucha Libre? MyAEW was launched with that concept in mind – giving fans access to events they normally wouldn’t be able to find elsewhere. CMLL’s New Japan Pro-Wrestling Fantastica Mania Mexico 2026 was added to the event schedule. Several more shows were added to the docket after that, including the company’s anniversary event which was held back on Sept. 18. Castro said that while AEW has given CMLL as platform to showcase the best it has to offer, trying to carve out an audience and build a brand in the United States is a challenge in and of itself. "Mostly brand recognition," Castro told OutKick Dropkick when asked what were some of the obstacles in the way of growth in the U.S. "I believe that our talents’ work speaks for itself. Anyone that enjoys wrestling, even if you like it by 5% compared to a fan, you will enjoy a CMLL show. It's not all about the drama and the storytelling, and that, I think that's what has made such a good connection with AEW and with New Japan Pro-Wrestling, we're heavily focused on the sports. So, even if you've never seen wrestling and you go to a CMLL show, you will enjoy it. It's fun. It'll make you gasp, it will make you scream, you'll have fun, and then you're gonna want to know more." Ultimately, Castro said the biggest obstacle is doing something CMLL has never done before and if fans can get eyes on the product, they will return. But what would success look like to Castro come September 2027? Persephone celebrates with tag team partner Thunder Rosa during a show on May 28, 2025, at El Paso County Coliseum. body: A new name representing Vietnam will grace the NJPW ring soon. Ares, a three-time champion in Vietnam Pro Wrestling, is expected to appear as part of NJPW’s October 12 Road to King of Pro Wrestling card in Korakuen Hall. Teaming with IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji, Ares will face off against G1 winner Ryohei Oiwa and Zack Sabre Jr. in tag action. Tsuji made an appearance last month at a VPW event to personally recruit Ares to NJPW’s Noge Dojo. Cagematch.net records show that Ares has worked for VPW since 2022, carrying their openweight title for a total of 518 days. He dropped their top belt last month to Da Butcherman in the main event of their annual Rumble card. “Never before has a Vietnamese pro wrestler made it to a stage like this,” he wrote. “When Tsuji offered Ares a position in the Noge Dojo, everyone on their roster and on the staff were moved to tears.” NJPW will present two nights of Road To action from Korakuen Hall before heading to Ryogoku Sumo Hall for this year’s King of Pro Wrestling card. Both lineups for NJPW’s upcoming Korakuen Hall shows were confirmed on Monday. Here’s how they look: Tuesday, October 6 – NJPW Road to King of Pro Wrestling Night 1 Wednesday, October 7 / NJPW Road to King of Pro Wrestling Night 2

title: Franco Colombo Dead, Former CMLL Wrestler & Booker Dies At Age 73
raw_title: Franco Colombo Dead, Former CMLL Wrestler & Booker Dies At Age 73
body: Coronado's niece took to Facebook to break the news, writing: "Today, a legend passed away, my uncle Javier Esparza Coronado. I ask for your prayers for the whole family. My uncle was very loved by everyone. When we were little, we enjoyed taking walks together as a family. God has called him to his side; he is now with my father in heaven. We will always remember you, Uncle. Say hi to everyone who has gone before us." Coronado trained under Diablo Velasco and wrestled with CMLL whilst it was called EMLL beginning in the 1970s, working the majority of his career unmasked save for a stint as "La Silueta" and holding the Mexican Welterweight title for 92 days as 1980 became 1981. He departed the promotion in the late 1980s before returning in a backstage capacity, overhauling its developmental system and being credited for hiring much of CMLL's current trainers or having trained them as they were wrestlers. Coronado and CMLL parted ways for the final time in 2021. Per " LuchaBlog " the reasoning for his departure varied from him being asked to take a pandemic-related pay cut and choosing to leave, to being pushed off the programming committee by someone implied to be Julio Cesar Rivera. Despite spending decades with the company, CMLL has yet to address Coronado's passing at the time of writing.
summary: Coronado's niece took to Facebook to break the news, writing: Today, a legend passed away, my uncle Javier Esparza Coronado. I ask for your prayers for the whole family.

llm.headline: Franco Colombo Passes Away at 73
llm.summary: Former CMLL wrestler and booker Javier Esparza Coronado, known as Franco Colombo, has died at age 73. He began wrestling in the 1970s under trainer Diablo Velasco, captured the Mexican Welterweight Championship for 92 days in 1980-81, and later returned to overhaul the promotion's developmental system and train many current coaches before leaving the company for the last time in 2021. His niece announced the news on social media, while CMLL has not yet publicly commented on his death.

llm_long: Franco Colombo, whose real name was Javier Esparza Coronado, has passed away at the age of 73. His niece announced the news on social media, requesting prayers for the family and recalling how loved he was by everyone. She remembered family walks from childhood and noted that he is now in heaven with her father.

Coronado began his wrestling career in the 1970s after training under Diablo Velasco. He worked for CMLL when it was still known as EMLL, competing mostly unmasked except for a period as La Silueta. During that time he held the Mexican Welterweight Championship for 92 days spanning 1980 and 1981.

He left the promotion in the late 1980s but later returned in a backstage role. In that capacity he revamped the company's developmental system and played a key part in hiring or training many of CMLL's current trainers.
Coronado and CMLL separated for the last time in 2021. Reports indicated the split involved either a pandemic-related pay cut that led to his exit or him being removed from the programming committee.
As of the time of his passing, CMLL had not issued any statement regarding Coronado's death.

title: Match Made: Gabe Kidd vs. Shota Umino, United Empire vs. Knockout Brothers title matches added to NJPW King of Pro Wrestling

body: Two more title showdowns have been confirmed for NJPW’s next trip to Ryogoku Sumo Hall. NJPW announced two matchups on Monday, adding to the growing lineup for King of Pro Wrestling on October 12 in Tokyo. In singles action, IWGP Global Heavyweight Champion Gabe Kidd will defend his belt against Shota Umino as part of the show. Umino confronted Kidd at Sunday’s Destruction in Kobe show shortly after he defended against Drilla Moloney. While Kidd initially planned to not re-appear in NJPW until 2027, a call-out and subsequent brawl with Umino might’ve changed his mind. Umino will be looking to regain the title in his upcoming rematch against Kidd. He previously lost the belt in July, dropping it as part of a Road to the G1 Climax card in Korakuen Hall. It was also confirmed on Monday that the United Empire trio of Will Ospreay, Great-O-Khan and HENARE will defend their gold next month. Ospreay and Co. will put their belts on the line against OSKAR & Yuto-Ice of the Knockout Brothers, along with a yet-to-be-revealed third tag partner. Here’s an updated look at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling, which is headlined by a highly anticipated title clash between Yota Tsuji and G1 winner Ryohei Oiwa.
summary: NJPW revealed two matchups on Monday, adding to the growing lineup for King of Pro Wrestling on October 12 in Tokyo. IWGP Global Heavyweight Champion Gabe Kidd will defend his belt against Shota Umino as part of the show.

Separately, the United Empire trio of Will Ospreay, Great-O-Khan and HENARE will defend their trios titles against OSKAR, Yuto-Ice and a mystery partner from the Knockout Brothers.

llm_long: Gabe Kidd will defend the IWGP Global Heavyweight Championship against Shota Umino at NJPW King of Pro Wrestling on October 12 in Tokyo. The matchup was officially added to the card following Umino's confrontation with Kidd at the Destruction in Kobe event. Umino challenged Kidd right after the champion retained the title against Drilla Moloney.

Umino previously held the Global title before losing it to Kidd in July during a Road to the G1 Climax show at Korakuen Hall. He will now have the opportunity to regain the belt in this rematch. Kidd had originally indicated plans to step away from NJPW until 2027, but the direct challenge and ensuing brawl prompted his continued involvement.

In addition, the United Empire team of Will Ospreay, Great-O-Khan, and HENARE will defend their trios titles at the same event. They are set to face OSKAR and Yuto-Ice from the Knockout Brothers, who will be joined by an undisclosed third partner.

body: However, it seems that Tsuji's stance on AEW has softened in recent weeks and "Gene Blast" is willing to smooth things over. body: Yuya Uemura, Kosei Fujita and Yushin Hatazawa have been removed from Sunday’s NJPW Destruction in Kobe card. New Japan announced on Saturday that Uemura and Hatazawa are unable to compete because of illness, while Fujita has suffered an injury to his right knee. No further information was given on Fujita’s injury or how long he is expected to be sidelined. The changes affect two matches on the card at Kobe World Memorial Hall. Uemura and Fujita had been on opposite sides of a six-man tag, with Aaron Wolf, Taichi & Uemura scheduled to face TMDK’s Fujita, Ryohei Oiwa & Zack Sabre Jr. That has been reduced to a tag match, with Wolf & Taichi taking on Oiwa & Sabre. Hatazawa was due to team with Tatsuya Matsumoto against Masatora Yasuda & Taisei Nakahara in the kickoff match. NJPW has canceled that contest. Taichi missed action earlier in the Road to Destruction tour due to illness, but remains scheduled for Sunday. The show is headlined by Yota Tsuji defending the IWGP Heavyweight Championship against Hirooki Goto. title: NJPW's Jeff Cobb Explains Parts Of WWE That Were 'Shocking' To Him
raw_title: NJPW's Jeff Cobb Explains Parts Of WWE That Were 'Shocking' To Him
body: "The first time I went to Saudi Arabia was very interesting. being on a chartered jet to go from Miami direct to Riyadh in Saudi Arabia, 16, 17 hours on a chartered jet was crazy, the first time I'd been in one. But it was interesting to see how pro-wrestling across the world, and not just WWE, but pro-wrestling affects people all over the world. We did a meet and greet there and people came up to me and said 'Oh I loved your stuff in New Japan.' That was a shock, because not to downplay NJPW's popularity or influence, but to hear people in Saudi Arabia say that they watched me in New Japan Pro-Wrestling was very surreal." Despite only being in WWE for less than a year, there is so much that one can learn from being part of such a massive company. Jeff Cobb understood that even after being in the wrestling business for many years already, and when he was asked what did he learn in WWE, he revealed that the fans can sometimes be a bit too passionate at times. "Fan interaction, definitely," Cobb said. "It's definitely huge in Japan, and Japan has the most wonderful fans I've ever dealt with in my career. In WWE it's a little more strange, because fans will wait at airports. There are times, with an early morning flight or a late one, and I have no idea why the fans know when these flights come in, but fans will wait at baggage claim. Part of me can be annoyed by that, but another part of me makes me appreciate fans more, because they're so passionate that they want to come to the airport at 5 in the morning for a chance to interact with one of us." Cobb would round off by saying that he was actually expecting a much more muted response from the NJPW crowd when he returned to the company in August. However, he has been welcomed with overwhelmingly positive messages from people who are happy to see him back in NJPW, and his experiences with the fans in WWE have made him appreciate the Japanese fans more. Cobb will get the chance to get closure on his time with his former stable, the United Empire, when he goes one-on-one with current faction leader Callum Newman at NJPW Destruction in Kobe on September 27.
summary: But it was interesting to see how pro-wrestling across the world, and not just WWE, but pro-wrestling affects people all over the world. Jeff Cobb understood that even after being in the wrestling business for many years already.

After joining WWE, Cobb noted that being part of a large organization offered many learning opportunities even after years in the business. When asked what he had learned, he highlighted fan interactions as a key aspect, observing that WWE fans can be particularly passionate.

Cobb explained that while fan engagement is significant in Japan, where audiences are wonderful, WWE fans sometimes wait at airports for early morning or late flights. He mentioned fans appearing at baggage claim despite the inconvenient hours, creating a mix of annoyance and greater appreciation for their dedication.

title: On the Record: AEW's Kevin Knight Recalls 'Monotony' Of Katsuyori Shibata's Training At NJPW Dojo
raw_title: AEW's Kevin Knight Recalls 'Monotony' Of Katsuyori Shibata's Training At NJPW Dojo
body: "At the time, I feel like I hated the monotony, the monotony of it all," Knight said. "We did the same thing every single day, the same warm up, the same rolls, the same squats, the same drills. And there wasn't much detailed feedback, if I can say that correctly, because you know, Shibata's English isn't the best. "So we just had to go off of vibes, you know, straight vibes. We had to feel him out if he liked it or not. We had to, you know, really trust our instincts in there with Shibata-san, because he has a very unique way of training. And with that language being in front of his unique way of training, it was very hard to engage, you know, if we were doing it correctly, or what he was exactly looking for." In the end, Knight feels that Shibata's teachings helped make him a better overall performer, something that's hard to argue given Knight's success in AEW since joining the promotion in 2025. When asked what's the best bit of wisdom that Shibata imparted to him, Knight revealed it was getting him to change his mindset towards how quickly he did things, a sharp contrast from Knight's background as a football player. "I would say patience," Knight said. "He would always say 'Be patient,' whether that's in the ring or out of the ring. And I always think about that, because I came from a football world, where you've got to do everything fast, fast, fast, you know? So being able to be patient and slow everything down was so foreign to me. I always tell myself that, like, I don't have to move at a thousand miles per hour. I can slow myself down, whether I'm talking, wrestling, whatever it is. And yeah, just having that patience has gotten me to where I'm at, and it's paying dividends."
summary: I feel like I hated the monotony, the monotony of it all, Knight explained. And with that language being in front of his unique way of training, it was very hard to engage.

llm.headline: Kevin Knight Reflects on Shibata's NJPW Dojo Training
llm.summary: AEW wrestler Kevin Knight described the repetitive daily regimen under Katsuyori Shibata at the New Japan Pro-Wrestling dojo, noting the identical warm-ups, rolls, squats and drills with minimal verbal feedback due to the language barrier. Knight said the experience forced him to rely on instincts and vibes to gauge approval, calling the approach unique and challenging. He ultimately credits Shibata's emphasis on patience in and out of the ring with improving him as a performer, contrasting his prior football background.
llm.speaker: Kevin Knight
llm.quote: He would always say 'Be patient,' whether that's in the ring or out of the ring.

llm_long: Kevin Knight looked back on his time training at the New Japan Pro-Wrestling dojo under Shibata. He described the daily routine as highly repetitive, featuring the same warm-up, rolls, squats, and drills every session.

Knight noted the limited detailed feedback during training. Communication challenges arose because of the language barrier, leading the trainees to rely on instincts and overall vibes to gauge whether their performance met expectations.

He found Shibata's training approach unique and at times difficult to fully engage with due to the combination of the method and the language difference. Despite these obstacles, Knight ultimately credited the experience with improving him as a performer.

When reflecting on the most valuable lesson from Shibata, Knight highlighted the emphasis on patience both inside and outside the ring. This advice stood in contrast to his prior background in football, where speed was constantly required.

Knight explained that learning to slow down his movements and actions felt unfamiliar at first. He continues to apply this mindset across wrestling, speaking, and daily life, which he says has contributed to his success.

body: Another vignette has been posted by AEW with the tease of a debut at WrestleDream. The same style of vignette aired on this past week’s episode of Dynamite, heavily teasing the arrival of Ilja Dragunov. A second video was posted on Friday evening with the tag “AEW WrestleDream” in the post, indicating a debut on Saturday’s pay-per-view in Orlando. Dragunov left WWE after his contract expired, ending a seven-year relationship with the company. During his tenure at WWE, he became an NXT U.K. Champion and then came to the U.S. and won the NXT Championship in September 2023. Dragunov was moved to the Raw roster after WrestleMania 40 and moved to SmackDown after an injury took him out for a year. His lone title on the main roster was the U.S. Championship he won in October 2025 from Sami Zayn and lost to Carmelo Hayes in December. WrestleDream takes place at the Addition Financial Arena in Orlando on Saturday night.
summary: AEW released a new vignette on Friday that heavily hints at Ilja Dragunov making his debut during Saturday's WrestleDream pay-per-view in Orlando. The video follows a similar teaser that aired on Dynamite earlier in the week. Dragunov recently departed WWE after his contract expired, following a seven-year run where he captured the NXT UK Championship, NXT Championship, and United States Championship.

title: SmackDown Match Halted After R-Truth Injury
raw_title: Match stopped on WWE SmackDown following R-Truth injury
summary_src: A match on SmackDown was stopped after R-Truth appeared to suffer an injury. During his match against Damian Priest on Friday, Truth went for a missile dropkick off the turnbuckle. Upon impact, he remained on the ground but was conscious and moving.
body: A match on SmackDown was stopped after R-Truth appeared to suffer an injury. During his match against Damian Priest on Friday, Truth went for a missile dropkick off the turnbuckle. Upon impact, he remained on the ground but was conscious and moving. The match stopped as the referee checked on Truth, then threw the match out, holding up the X sign. Afterwards, Priest exited the ring immediately grabbed a steel chair. The referee stopped him as Fraxiom ran out to check on Truth. Priest then dropped the chair and made his exit as the segment ended. According to False Finish , the stoppage was legitimate. Fightful Select reported that Priest was set to win the match, with Fraxiom coming out after the match to make the save following a post-match beatdown. A similar situation happened to R-Truth back on the November 1, 2022 edition of NXT. A match between him and Grayson Waller was stopped after he tore his quad, requiring surgery that kept him out of action for over a year. The stoppage was confirmed to be legitimate.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

The incident spread across social media, with fans criticizing Moose’s execution while others debated what went wrong. Moreover, both wrestlers have since addressed the situation. This week’s TNA iMPACT celebrated 35 years of The Hardys, who took charge of booking the show. One of the night’s biggest matches was a five-way ladder match featuring Elijah, Jason Hotch, Ricky Sosa, Trey Miguel, and Moose. During the match, Moose tried to powerbomb Sosa from the ring toward a ladder setup on the outside. The move did not go as planned, and Sosa took an awkward fall on the floor. He was supposed to hit the ladder and possibly break it. But Sosa narrowly avoided hitting the ladder and hit the floor directly. Clips of the spot spread on X. Some fans criticized Moose’s execution, while others pointed out how Sosa landed badly on the floor. Fans of Moose also expressed frustration with what they saw as a recurring issue. title: On the Record: Tatum Paxley Defends WWE Recruiting Strategy and Opens Up On Influences
raw_title: Tatum Paxley Defends WWE Recruiting Strategy and Reveals Influences
body: In an interview with Complex Garps, Paxley argued that a genuine commitment to wrestling matters more than an individual's route into the industry. "Because, to me, you really only get far if you have a genuine love for the business," Paxley said. She also emphasized that performers should be satisfied with their professional choices rather than remain in an environment that does not make them happy. "And if you're not happy here, then, you know, you're welcome to go elsewhere," she added. Paxley's own journey provides context for her position. Before joining WWE, she competed in powerlifting, giving her direct experience with the transition from another athletic discipline into professional wrestling. Her wrestling influences also include Bliss, whom she has identified as her favorite wrestler. In an interview with Denise Salcedo, Paxley recalled sharing the ring with Bliss and Charlotte Flair while she was still friends with Izzi Dame, whose idol was Flair. "Her idol is Charlotte Flair. Mine's Alexa Bliss, and we got to have a match against the two of them," Paxley said. She described the experience as an opportunity to compete alongside a wrestler she had long admired, recalling her initial disbelief at standing in the ring with Bliss. "I'm like, 'Will I ever get the chance to stand in the ring with Alexa Bliss?' And then I was. I'm standing there staring at her like, 'Oh my gosh… how did this happen?'" Paxley said. Paxley later teamed up with Bliss and Flair on SmackDown. Her partnership with Bliss subsequently produced a major milestone when the pair defeated Fatal Influence, consisting of Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid, to capture the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship. Separately, Paxley explained that her finishing move, Cemetery Drive, draws inspiration from Suzu Suzuki, the reigning World of Stardom Champion at the time of the October 14 report by Fightful. "The finish, I had seen a wrestler — who goes by Suzu Suzuki — pull it out… When I had seen that move, I had not been so drawn to a move that heavy before. I had to take inspo from it, and I even tried different variations of my current finish. No matter what I do, I have to add this twist into it. It has to have this twist, and I just worked out on it for such a long time and then when I finally got to pull it out, I was like, ‘Yeah, this is perfect.’ It’s one of those things you look at and you’re like, huh!? That’s what I want people to think when they see me so my finish works really well with that," Paxley said. According to Fightful, Cemetery Drive has also played a role in Paxley's championship success in NXT, where she won both the NXT Women's North American Championship and the NXT Women's Championship. Her recent tag team title victory marked another achievement following her transition to WWE's main roster.
summary: Speaking with Complex Garps, Paxley argued that a genuine commitment to wrestling matters more than an individual's route into the industry. Because, to me, you really only get far if you have a genuine love for the business, Paxley explained.

raw_title: WWE star Penta subtly pays tribute to Pac after wrestler's shocking death at 40
body: Benjamin Satterley, the All Elite Wrestling star known as Pac and former WWE competitor known as Neville, was firmly on the mind of Penta during "Monday Night Raw." Penta subtly paid tribute to Satterley as he took part in a tag team match with Je’Von Evans against Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh. During the Luchador’s entrance, Penta was seen with the word "Pac" emblazoned on his left boot. Pac was on the minds of the pro wrestling world after AEW announced the wrestler’s death on Sunday night. He was 40. WWE broadcasted a tribute graphic to him to begin "Monday Night Raw." Penta and Pac competed against each other in AEW and at least once in Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre (CMLL). Satterley died Sunday hours after he competed against Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. "Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans." The Des Plaines Police Department told OutKick Dropkick there were no indications of foul play and the circumstances around Satterley’s death were not deemed to be suspicious. Police said the cause of death would be determined by the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office. Satterley was found "passed out" outside of a CAVA restaurant at around 4 p.m. local time, the California Post reported, citing 911 audio. An official who arrived on the scene reportedly said Satterley was dead on arrival. Satterley was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. Before wrestling in AEW, he was with WWE and known as Neville . Satterley was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion.

body: Part of Deion Sanders and his Colorado football program, WWE legend Goldberg's son, Gage Goldberg , has now opened up about his own pro-wrestling aspirations. Gage Goldberg is a Class of 2024 middle linebacker from Boerne Champion High School in Boerne, Texas. Recently appearing on the Colorado Football Coaches Show, the 20-year-old opened up about his interest in pursuing a pro-wrestling career . "Yes, sir, it's definitely there," he said. However, while Gage has always been interested in wrestling, his father was quite reluctant about it once. "Actually, when I was younger, he didn't want me to do it whatsoever," Gage said. "And then once he started to go back, once I started to get involved a little bit, then it started to change. "Once I started getting involved a little bit, then it started to change. It's up to me. So, I mean, I would love to do it. Honestly, I would love to have that opportunity to do it, and I feel like it would be a great thing to do after football," he said. In a 2024 interview, Gage disclosed that Triple H had discussed with him the possibility of pursuing a career in WWE. At one point, he was even offered a WWE NIL deal, which his father, Bill Goldberg , turned down on behalf of his son, feeling the financial terms were very low. Gage is currently a walk-on linebacker at the University of Colorado and is focused on his college football career. However, he is still open to pursuing a pro-wrestling career later in the future. Meanwhile, his father, Bill Goldberg wrestled his last match against Gunther last year in 2025.

body: “I secretly liked the WWE when I was younger. It was kind of a tell for knowing I was gonna be gay,” Harris said during an interview with Sam Roberts. While appearing as a guest on the Sam Roberts’ Show for SiriusXM on September 15, the How I Met Your Mother actor chatted with the host about all manner of topics including his upcoming film Sunny Dancer , but what piqued my gay interest most was when he reminisced about liking WWE as a child and what that implied about his sexuality growing up. In a clip of the interview shared to Sam Roberts’ X account on September 21, the star sits in a studio with Roberts as he asks Harris whether he’s always been into WWE, saying, “Who doesn’t love WWE?” Harris replied with, “I secretly liked the WWE when I was younger. It was kind of a tell for knowing I was gonna be gay.” Roberts then jokingly asked whether he should be doing some self exploration to which Harris said, “No,” but then started discussing WWE saying, “You know, like tight shorts; they’re oiled up…grappling…it’s like, ‘I’m not supposed to be liking this as much as I am.’” And he has a point. There is something incredibly homoerotic lying beneath the surface of the testosterone-fueled spectacle. It’s a tangle of limbs, overt exclamations of masculinity, brawls between rivals that get intimately close. You could cut the tension with a proverbial sword — All the while, being cheered on by the masses, with no one batting an eye. The actor also revealed that he had a love for He-Man and the Masters of the Universe , another action-packed series that began in the 1980s featuring a very buff, nearly naked hero with a sassy blunt-banged bob, wearing nothing but tiny brown underwear, boots, and a harness. He collected those action figures, too, by the way. In the interview Roberts confirms that Harris secretly liked WWE while he starred in Doogie Howser saying, “Oh, if I’d known that me and Doogie are into the same s**t, it would have been awesome.” To be honest, Harris was definitely onto something, especially given that in recent years, queer and trans folks have been making a splash in the WWE scene with wrestler Aaron Rourke aka “The Dime Piece” or “Evil Gay,” being the first out gay wrestler to win a WWE title in March of 2026 and trans wrestler Gabbi Tuft returning to the sport as her fully-realized self in 2024 after beginning her medical transition in 2021 following open heart surgery in 2019. title: WWE NXT champ reflects on tremendous accolades 4 years into pro wrestling career: 'Force to be reckoned with'
raw_title: WWE NXT champ reflects on tremendous accolades 4 years into pro wrestling career: 'Force to be reckoned with'
body: WWE NXT star Kelani Jordan added another line to her already impressive pro wrestling resume just four years after she initially signed with the company and reported to the Performance Center. She was the first NXT women’s North American champion, she won the Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) Knockouts Championship and, on Sunday at Heatwave, she defeated Kendal Grey to win the NXT Women’s Championship for the first time in her first opportunity. OutKick Dropkick asked Jordan in a recent interview what the accolades meant to her. "It feels great. Also, it's a good reminder to, like, whenever there's moments where I'm like maybe down or feel like, oh no, I'm like kind of like plateauing or shoot, like what's happening, I think it's a good reminder to like, hey, you were the first ever North American champion, you were a TNA Knockouts champion , now you're the NXT women's champion. "It just allows me to take a moment to reflect and be like, hey, like you're very talented and you're good. Like you don't have these titles for no reason or had those titles for no reason. So, I think it's a great reminder that Kelani Jordan is a force to be reckoned with." Over the course of the year, Jordan has demanded respect from fans and the rest of the women’s locker room. She said in May she was better than all the women that were called up to Raw and SmackDown after WrestleMania 42. "But definitely when you have the title, you automatically get a little bit more respect. You know what I'm saying? Just because I mean it's proven in your work. You're the champion. So you have something around your waist or over your shoulder to like speak for that." Jaida Parker was the first one to step up to Jordan on Tuesday night. Parker is coming off a big win in a submission match against Nattie, which also took place on Heatwave. She’s certainly proved to be a worthy contender. "Yeah, I'm not surprised that Jaida Parker came out. I had a feeling someone was going to come out, but I'm not surprised that it was her because we have a lot of history and like she said, she feels like she has a chip on her shoulder because we faced each other before. "But I know Jada is going to bring a lot of fight. I know she's great at talking, but I'm great not only at talking, but I walk the walk. So, I am ready for Jaida's games, her tactics. She can talk, but when she's in the ring with me is, you know, talking — is that going to work?" Jordan and Parker’s match for the NXT Women’s Championship is set for this coming Tuesday on the CW Network.

title: Top 50 good guys in wrestling history

body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Some folks might try to tell you it’s the villains that make sports-entertainment fun. And why not? It’s the baddies in the black hats who get to throw fireballs, electrocute millionaires and run people over with monster trucks. But it’s the good guys who give the fans something to believe in, a hero to look up to and a reminder that, more often than not, good does triumph over evil. Here, we present the 50 Superstars that wrestling fans grew up admiring — and still do today. ( PHOTOS ) Agree? Disagree? Let us hear about on the WWE Classics Facebook page . Diamond Dallas Page’s career in sports-entertainment is well-documented — from the moment he drove the Pink Cadillac carrying Rhythm & Blues to the ring at WrestleMania VI, to his legendary rivalry with “Macho Man” Randy Savage. Beloved by WCW fans and the WWE Universe, the New Jersey native represented a working class hero — a tireless competitor who earned every accolade. Following the formation of The New World Order, DDP was one of the first WCW competitors to stand up to the notorious faction, becoming an “everyman hero” as he outright refused to join their ranks. During his heated rivalry with “Macho Man,” Page defended both his honor and that of his wife, Kimberly, against Savage’s brutish, nWo-inspired tactics. No matter the odds, DDP never backed down from a fight, earning the moniker of “WCW’s People’s Champion.” ( WATCH ) Quick and agile despite being one of the most muscular grapplers of his era, Johnson’s smooth moves helped him become a popular attraction in areas of the country that were still struggling with segregation. The racial barriers Johnson broke are remembered today, but “Soul Man” wasn’t motivated by politics — he just wanted to entertain. “What set my dad apart from a lot of guys wasn’t the fact that he was this incredible black wrestler,” Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson once said of his WWE Hall of Fame father. “It was just that he was a great wrestler.” — RYAN MURPHY “My dad was a local hero,” The Road Dogg said of his legendary father, Bob Armstrong. A major star in Alabama and Georgia during the ’60s and ’70s, the WWE Hall of Famer’s “salt of the earth” appeal endeared him to Southern fans who favored substance over style. “He was one of them,” WWE official Scott Armstrong added. “He came from very humble beginnings and never hid that. He got up in the morning and had fried eggs and grits and gravy and did his thing.” A champion not only to folks in Dixie, but to his four sons — Brian, Brad, Scott, and Steve — the blue collar "Bullet” had his boys behind him when he took on rivals like Roddy Piper ( WATCH ) and Bobby Duncum, who he battled in a 1973 gorefest in The Omni Coliseum. “My father had a white singlet on and it was stained red,” Road Dogg vividly remembered. “He had to go the hospital and have a blood transfusion, but my father won and we won a 1974 Cadillac.” — R.M. body: WWE announced earlier in the week that Cody Rhodes will challenge Sami Zayn for the WWE Championship on the next "Raw." The timing is interesting at first glance, but with major regional tensions escalating in Riyadh, the currently scheduled Zayn vs. Roman Reigns match could change. Meanwhile, Rhodes is still in the middle of his heated rivalry with Randy Orton, which makes any potential pivot feel jarring. Rhodes and Orton are expected to meet face-to-face on tonight's show. After Money in the Bank 2026, Tiffany Stratton is once again the women's briefcase-holder. She's scheduled to make her first appearance post-win tonight. Also celebrating their latest big win are the new Women's Tag Team Champions, Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss. They dethroned Fatal Influence's Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid last Friday. In singles competition, R-Truth and Damian Priest will go head-to-head tonight after recently ending their tag-team, while Paige and Nikki Bella battle for a potential shot at the Women's Championship. Check out Friday night's full "WWE SmackDown" lineup below, which starts at 8 p.m. ET on USA Network: AAA Cruiserweight Championship: Rey Fenix (c.) def. Ricky Saints Corbin is suddenly just gone. Orton slams Cody into the ring post, then puts him in the ring to miss a punt. Orton takes a Cody Cutter, and Cody lines up a punt! And there's Corbin. That was hilarious. He rushes back in the ring out of nowhere to attack Rhodes and save Orton — because bad guys. Cody counters the End of Days and nails a super Cody Cutter. Orton shouts at him from the ramp that he "won't do it." Cody lines up a punt! He nails Corbin! Oh my God. Orton with the greatest reaction of all time. Incredible. He can't believe it. The crowd chants "one more time." SAVAGES. Cody nails the snap scoop slam and fires off jabs before the Bionic Elbow and Disaster Kick. Cody wants the Cross-Rhodes — then, ultra-predictably, Orton pulls him out of the ring for the DQ win to end the match and start a beatdown around the announce desk. Corbin knees Cody, then misses a running attack to taste the steel post. They each land Clotheslines to hit the mat. Corbin lands a huge Deep Six for a near-fall. He kicks at Cody and launches him into the corner with a hard Irish Whip. Cody throws the chair out of the ring and starts to go at it with Corbin, Clotheslining him out of the ring. Cody then demands a quick match, and it's on. OK. Things are happening. Corbin says he doesn't see what everyone else sees about Cody. A lot has changed since he was around, but Cody's whining hasn't, he says. Corbin then taunts Cody for not having a killer instinct, like Orton has been saying. Corbin says he doesn't need any friends and enjoys hurting people, unlike "good guy" Cody. How have they just ignored Cody's title match on Monday for the entire show? Cody grabs a chair and brings it to the center of the ring. He says he's going to sit there until Orton appears — and instead he gets Baron freaking Corbin.

title: Mike Bailey explains crisp in-ring style

body: AEW wrestler Mike Bailey, who is a high-flyer, has shown that they are capable of wrestling that style while also appearing to be in a real fight when they are in the ring. Not only is Bailey a capable high-flyer, but their offense and movement in the ring is crisp and tight. Everything they do appears to have momentum behind it whether they are whipping someone off the ropes or bouncing off of them. Bailey said the key to their wrestling looking so crisp and their matches looking like they are in a real fight is that they have cultivated a narrow set of moves they are comfortable with. “But I think that this is a general thing about professional wrestling, but also a good piece of advice for professional wrestlers,” said Bailey during an exclusive interview on Radican Worldwide available now for PWTorch VIP members ahead of AEW’s WrestleDream PPV on Oct. 17. “But nothing looks as good as what you’re comfortable doing, right? I’ve been doing pro wrestling for 20 years, and I have actively cultivated a very narrow skill set, right? I know that all the moves that I do are the things that I do best. “All the situations that I put myself in are situations that I know how to deal with better than anyone on earth. And I think, you know, I still train martial arts regularly. I still, I still train very hard to, you know, stay sharp within those situations.” Bailey said they have gotten to the point where they can do the moves they want to do in the ring without having to second-guess what they are doing, so that they can put the majority of their attention on the moves that need their attention. “But I think at this point, it doesn’t have to be a conscious effort, but I also think that that’s impossible,” said Bailey. “I think that if you are second-guessing every movement in the ring, you are doing things wrong. title: Match Made: What is India's record in home T20I series deciders before IND vs WI 2026?
raw_title: What is India's record in home T20I series deciders before IND vs WI 2026?
summary_src: India is set for a massive series decider in the upcoming fifth T20I against West Indies, with the score level at 2-2 after back-and-forth wins so far.
body: India, however, has a dominant record when it comes to series deciders at home in the shortest format. They are yet to suffer a defeat in a home T20I series decider, recording nine wins while two contests ended in a no result. Half of these contests have come since the start of the decade, including memorable wins over heavyweights like England, Australia, and New Zealand. The latter was India's last home series decider success as well. In the 2023 home series against the Blackcaps, the Men in Blue lost the opening match in Ranchi, before levelling the series in Lucknow. The series decider took place at the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, where Shubman Gill struck his maiden T20I hundred to help India post 234-4. In reply, New Zealand were bowled out for 66, falling short by 168 runs. It is still India's largest win in the format to date. The last home T20I series decider that ended in a no result was the fifth T20I against South Africa in 2022. The series was level 2-2 after India made a comeback after losing the first two matches. The fifth T20I in Bengaluru, however, was washed out due to rain after only 3.3 overs were bowled. The last time India lost a series decider was during the tour of West Indies in 2023. The hosts took a 2-0 lead, before the Men in Blue won the next two matches to push for a series decider. In the fifth T20I, West Indies chased down a 166-run target with two overs to spare to clinch the series 3-2. India went unbeaten in T20I series for three years after that series loss, with the streak coming to an end with an unprecedented 0-2 loss in Ireland a few months ago.
summary: The latest: the latest: India, that explained, has a dominant record when it comes to series deciders at home in the shortest format. They are yet to suffer a defeat in a home T20I series decider, recording nine wins while two contests ended in a no result.

title: In Memoriam: Former WWE star PAC’s cause of death revealed
raw_title: Former WWE star PAC’s cause of death revealed - REPORT
summary_src: PAC’s passing was announced by All Elite Wrestling (AEW) on September 27. This deeply shocked the pro wrestling community because the British star had competed just a day earlier at AEW All Out.
body: The former WWE star was reportedly found unresponsive inside a vehicle in the parking lot of a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois. He was preparing to travel back to the United Kingdom. Authorities subsequently responded to the scene and confirmed his death. According to earlier reports, police discovered saliva on Satterley’s shirt and medication inside the vehicle. However, the exact cause of death was undetermined. According to a recent report by the New York Post , the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office determined the cause of death of the 40-year-old wrestler. He died from bronchial asthma, with his death officially ruled as natural. After departing WWE in 2018, PAC joined AEW in 2019. He went on to become the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the AEW International Championship. He established himself as a formidable competitor in the promotion. Following news of his death, tributes poured in from across the wrestling industry. The veteran’s passing marked a heartbreaking loss for wrestling fans worldwide. Hence, bringing an end to the career of a performer admired for his remarkable in-ring ability and contributions to pro Wrestling. Following the news of PAC's passing, WWE Superstar Finn Balor took to his official X/Twitter handle and posted a clip of him remembering the British star. The former Judgment Day member thanked the wrestling veteran for being a great friend. He recalled how they first met as young wrestlers on mats in a church basement in Newcastle. Furthermore, Balor revealed that he cherished their memories in Japan, NXT, WWE, and visits to their families, noting that their similar upbringings and values strengthened their bond.
summary: The former WWE star was by most accounts found unresponsive inside a vehicle in the parking lot of a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois. Per a recent report by the New York Post , the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office determined the cause of death of the 40-year-old wrestler.

summary_src: A freak injury saw a WWE SmackDown match come to an immediate stop as a referee threw up the "X" sign, indicating that it was legitimate.
body: R-Truth was facing Damian Priest as part of their feud tonight on the show. However, the match had to be stopped thanks to an injury tonight. The doctor rushed into the ring to check as Damian Priest stood in the corner, still in character, but unable to hide the concern on his face as well. The referee then had a word with the doctor and threw up the "X" sign, which is the symbol used by the company to signal to people at the back that an injury was legitimate and not part of the storyline. Doctors rushed out and took Truth to the back, while Damian Priest had a kayfabe moment where he was pretending he was going to attack his former partner until Axiom and Nathan Frazer made their way out to stop any attack from happening. Further updates are awaited, but the injury is legitimate, as the original plans had Priest defeating Truth and ending the WWE match properly, after which Fraxiom were supposed to come out.
