llm.headline: Necro Butcher Signs WWE Legends Deal
llm.summary: Dylan Summers, known as The Necro Butcher, announced on his Facebook page that he has signed a basic legends deal with WWE. The offer arrived the day after he walked out of his regular job. Per the update from PWInsider, the pact opens the door for various projects already discussed while he continues to work his independent dates.

llm_long: Necro Butcher announced that he signed a basic legends deal with WWE. The agreement was confirmed as accurate by sources within the company. WWE President Nick Khan led the effort to secure the deal.

The signing stands out because Necro Butcher built his reputation almost entirely outside of wrestling's largest promotions. He became known for an exceptionally violent style that frequently featured weapons and the elements of deathmatch wrestling.

Necro Butcher's real name is Dylan Keith Summers. Born on July 13, 1973, in West Virginia, he made his professional wrestling debut in 1998. Over time he faced several prominent names from the 2000s independent scene, including Bryan Danielson, Kevin Steen, Eddie Kingston, Chris Hero, Claudio Castagnoli and Samoa Joe.

He also appeared in the 2008 film The Wrestler starring Mickey Rourke. A 2005 match against Samoa Joe at IWA Mid-South's Something to Prove event in Philadelphia gained a reputation for its brutality, highlighted by a moment in which Joe kicked him off arena bleachers onto the concrete floor.

More than two decades later the match received renewed attention when it became the focus of an episode in the seventh season of Dark Side of the Ring. The episode examined the bout along with Butcher's life and career. The full episode was later released on YouTube in July and has accumulated more than 700,000 views.

Butcher moved from being featured in the documentary to signing the WWE Legends deal months afterward. The contract typically permits the use of a wrestler's name and likeness for merchandise, video games and other projects while allowing for possible appearances.

summary_src: Thekla’s wild spider-themed entrance at AEW WrestleDream came with a little extra help from the indie wrestling scene. After the show, the identities of the two men who carried Thekla to the ring on her custom throne were finally revealed.
body: Thekla went all-out for her AEW Women’s World Championship match against Mercedes Moné, making her entrance on a custom-made throne designed around her Toxic Spider character. Two men carried the throne down the entranceway while Thekla sat on top, giving her one of the more elaborate entrances of the night. Those two men weren’t just random extras hired for the entrance either. They were independent wrestlers Dante Casanova and Daniel Lacey, both of whom have been putting in work outside AEW. Casanova confirmed their involvement after WrestleDream when he took to Instagram and uploaded a backstage photo alongside Lacey and Thekla. The picture showed all three together after helping bring the Toxic Spider’s special entrance to life. Lacey has competed for several independent promotions, including CCW, BRCW and FIP. Casanova has also built up experience across the indie scene with appearances for AWE, HAW and 1FW, and he’s even stepped inside the ring for ROH. Thekla may not have left WrestleDream with the championship, but she definitely made sure her arrival felt like a big deal. Now fans know that two working indie wrestlers, Dante Casanova and Daniel Lacey, were the men underneath that massive spider-themed throne helping her make the entrance happen. title: Massive Price Tag for WWE WrestleMania in Saudi Arabia Revealed
raw_title: Massive Price Tag for WWE WrestleMania in Saudi Arabia Revealed
summary_src: WWE is getting paid some serious money to bring WrestleMania to Saudi Arabia, and the price tag is absolutely insane. We’re not talking about a normal Saudi Arabia payday, either. According to Dave Meltzer, the company is set to collect a whopping $150 million for the event.
body: During the October 18 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer revealed the figure while discussing WWE’s upcoming business in Saudi Arabia. The conversation turned to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and whether major sporting events in the region would still take place. That’s when Meltzer dropped the financial details. He explained that sources in Saudi Arabia had previously told him WrestleMania would cost more than $100 million, but new financial information he saw that morning pointed to an even bigger number. “So I saw one of the stock things. Okay, so it looks like, you know, we didn’t know this. I actually just found this out, like this morning. It looks like the WrestleMania price is 150 million. I knew it was over 100 because people in Saudi Arabia told me it’s north of 100 million. You usually. They get 55 to go. It’s 150 million for WrestleMania.” “And that is, you know, you don’t want to put that in jeopardy.” “There’s a UFC show in Saudi Arabia November 28th or December 5th, which I would say that’s in jeopardy. There’s the Canelo fight, which has not been canceled yet, but there’s certainly lots of talk about it.” He also said organizers were already preparing backup plans in case things take a turn for the worse. Meltzer wasn’t exactly thrilled with the idea of companies continuing to run major events in the region under the current circumstances, either. “I mean, we’re in the middle of a war and it’s obviously they shouldn’t go.” Still, that’s one heck of a payday. WWE has been collecting huge checks from Saudi Arabia for years, but this WrestleMania deal is on another level. With $150 million potentially coming WWE’s way, it’s pretty clear why keeping this arrangement intact is such a big deal. title: Contract News: WWE Pulled Ilja Dragunov From Television After He Refused New Contract
raw_title: WWE Pulled Ilja Dragunov From Television After He Refused New Contract
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov didn’t just walk away from WWE when his contract expired. WWE apparently stopped putting him on television once it became clear he wasn’t sticking around, and now we know more about what went down behind the scenes.
body: “Ricochet and Ilya, they left on their own. You know, I mean, they wait for their contract to expire. They want, you know, they, you know, Ricochet, I can’t say he wanted out. He was debating it, but they kind of knew that, look, he wouldn’t sign a new deal.” Things got interesting when Meltzer explained what WWE did after Dragunov refused to sign. Instead of continuing to feature him on television until his deal expired, the company decided to keep him off TV altogether. “And Ely is the same way, Eli. They kept off TV because they wanted him to sign a new deal and he would not sign the new deal. And they figured did it like, look, look, he’s not signing the new deal. We’re not gonna put him on TV because it may mean that he can go if he won’t sign the new deal.” Meltzer also pointed out that Dragunov’s exit was different from some of the former WWE stars who ended up in AEW after being released. He claimed several of those wrestlers wanted to return to WWE once Triple H took over creative from Vince McMahon, but their AEW contracts prevented them from making an immediate move. “In the case of some of those guys, it was Vince McMahon’s decision. And then Vince is out and Levesque is in. And Levesque did want them back immediately, you know, Swerve included. And you know, Swerve said no and the rest of them said yes, but they couldn’t get out of their deals.” “They had the vignette ready and they knew it was going to be any day now, but they didn’t want to put it on if he wasn’t going to be at the pay per view. I mean, the plan and the hope absolutely was for him to be on the pay per view.” Dragunov eventually got his visa situation sorted out a nd made his AEW debut as planned. So WWE wanted Dragunov to stay, Dragunov wouldn’t sign, and WWE decided to stop using him on television. Now he’s working for the competition, and the same guy WWE kept off its shows is getting a fresh start in AEW. llm_long: Ring of Honor will hold its annual year-end event, Final Battle, in San Antonio, Texas this December. The show is set for the Boeing Center at Tech Port on Friday, December 4.
A promotional poster for the event features several wrestlers including ROH champion Bandido, Místico, Máscara Dorada, ROH women’s champion Athena, Lee Moriarty, and Deonna Purrazzo.
The Boeing Center at Tech Port previously hosted a pair of TNA Impact tapings in September.
This marks the fifth edition of Final Battle since Tony Khan took ownership of Ring of Honor.
Athena has closed the Final Battle event in each of the past three years with title defenses. She defeated Billie Starkz in both 2023 and 2024, and Persephone the year before that.
Athena originally won the ROH women’s title at Final Battle in 2022.

title: On the Record: AEW’s Television Future Still Not Guaranteed Despite Tony Khan’s Positive Discusses With David Ellison
raw_title: AEW’s Television Future Still Not Guaranteed Despite Tony Khan’s Positive Talks With David Ellison
summary_src: Tony Khan may be feeling pretty good about AEW’s future under Skydance, but that doesn’t mean the company is out of the woods just yet.
body: Following AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 , Khan confirmed that he’s had several conversations with David Ellison about AEW’s future. Khan made those discussions sound very encouraging, saying Ellison was excited about working with AEW and that the Warner Bros.-Paramount merger could open up new opportunities. However, during the October 18 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer wasn’t ready to celebrate just yet. He acknowledged that Khan has good relationships with important executives, including Ellison, but made it clear that friendly conversations don’t guarantee anything once the new company starts making business decisions. Meltzer wasn’t suggesting that AEW is about to lose its television home. In fact, he believes the company is safe for the immediate future and doesn’t expect its programming to suddenly disappear from TBS or TNT. The bigger question is what happens once Ellison and his team start deciding which programming deals they want to keep. “But he’s had the conversations and I have no doubt that the conversations have gone great because they’re still there. They’re still going to be there for, you know, a year and a couple of months at worst. I don’t see them cutting them, you know, or taking them off TBS and TNT.” The problem is that AEW isn’t the only property the new ownership has to consider. Meltzer pointed out that Skydance will eventually have to make difficult financial decisions, and AEW will be competing with major sports properties for a place in the company’s budget. “If the numbers keep going the way they are, it’s a best case scenario for them. It’s still not, nothing’s a guarantee because they’re gonna have to make some, you know, you know, Ellison and, and his crew are going to make some hard decisions to cut something.” “They’re not going to cut, you know, the NCAA basketball tournament. It’s, they’re not going to cut. I don’t think they’re going to be cutting the NHL.” Meltzer then warned against anyone claiming to know exactly how the situation will play out. He suggested that the next few months could provide a much clearer picture once executives begin making decisions about the company’s future. “Eventually someone’s going to make the hard decisions. I don’t know what they are. It’s, it’s up in the air and anything that you hear from anyone, probably for the next, I don’t know, short period of time, I think you should throw out the window in, in three, four months if you start hearing stuff from reliable people, you know, then, then you gotta listen. But right now I just say that anyone who says that they know they’re full of.” This isn’t the first time questions have been raised about AEW’s position under the new corporate structure. llm.headline: This Day In Wrestling History: October 18
llm.summary: On October 18, several notable events took place across wrestling history. In 1954, George Becker and Bobby Becker won the NWA Southern Tag Team titles in Charlotte. In 1963, Bruno Sammartino defended the WWWF World Championship against The Crusher in Pittsburgh. Additional events included a 1962 card in Greensboro and the 2005 TNA Bound for Glory main event featuring AJ Styles versus Sting.

llm_long: On October 18, 1954, a live wrestling event took place in Charlotte, North Carolina. Lou Plummer defeated Tiger Joe Marsh, and Tinker Todd defeated Al Cortez. George Becker and Bobby Becker defeated Mr. Moto and Kinji Shibuya to capture the NWA Southern Tag Team championships in the Mid-Atlantic version.

In 1962, Mid-Atlantic Wrestling held an event at the Greensboro Coliseum in North Carolina before 2,705 fans. Rip Hawk and Rock Hunter defeated George Becker and Billy Two Rivers in a best of three falls match. The Great Bolo defeated Johnny Weaver, while Ray Villmer and Reggie Parks beat John Smith and Ivan Kameroff in another best of three falls bout.

On October 18, 1963, WWWF World Champion Bruno Sammartino defeated The Crusher using a backbreaker in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Boxing legend Jersey Joe Walcott served as the special referee for the match.

A Mid-Atlantic Wrestling show occurred in Raleigh, North Carolina, in 1966. Boris Malenko and Missouri Mauler defeated Aldo Bogni and Bronco Lubich in a bout called the Battle of the Bullies. The Red Demons beat Abe Jacobs and Jesse James, and Paul DeMarco defeated Tinker Todd.

In 1968, Mid-Atlantic Wrestling presented an event at the State Fairgrounds in Richmond, Virginia. Paul Jones and Nelson Royal defeated Rip Hawk and Swede Hanson in a two out of three falls match. Aldo Bogni and Bronco Lubich beat Billy Hines and Jimmy Hines, while Tinker Todd defeated Bob Burns.

During a 1977 WWWF television taping in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, World Champion Superstar Billy Graham attacked High Chief Peter Miavia ahead of a scheduled match. Graham broke Miavia's ukulele and left him bloodied. In 1978, Abdullah The Butcher defeated Billy Robinson in Utsunomiya, Japan.

summary_src: AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026, is officially in the books, and the betting odds were almost dead-on. The oddsmakers correctly picked nearly every winner on the card, but one championship upset gave fans who backed the underdogs a chance to walk away with some serious cash.
body: Before the show, BetOnline.ag released betting odds for 10 matches. Will Ospreay, Jon Moxley, Mercedes Moné and The Young Bucks were all massive favorites, with some of those lines offering almost nothing in return for a $100 wager. Now that AEW WrestleDream is in the books , we can see just how much money someone could have made betting on the winners. And while the bookmakers got most of their predictions right, the biggest payday came from the one match they got wrong. Here’s a look at all 10 winners, their odds going into the show, and how much someone would have made by placing a $100 bet on each one. These payouts are based on the betting odds provided before WrestleDream. Profit represents money won beyond the original $100 wager, while total payout includes the original stake. The biggest winner for bettors wasn’t Ospreay, Moxley or any of the other huge favorites. It was Adam Page and Brodido. Swerve Strickland and The New Level entered their AEW World Trios Championship match as -400 favorites, while Page, Brody King and Bandido were sitting at +250. The underdogs ended up winning the titles, which means a $100 bet on Page and Brodido would have paid out $350, including $250 in pure profit. The Young Bucks were at the complete opposite end of the spectrum. Matt and Nick Jackson entered as massive -5000 favorites against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight, and they retained their AEW World Tag Team Championships. But anyone betting $100 on the Bucks would have made a whopping $2 in profit. That’s right, risk $100 to win two bucks. Jon Moxley wasn’t much better. His -3000 odds against Mark Davis meant a $100 winning bet would have earned just $3.33. Will Ospreay’s -2000 odds in the Clockwork Carnage match would have produced $5 in profit, while Mercedes Moné’s win over Thekla at -1500 would have made bettors $6.67. Those were winning bets, but nobody was getting rich off them. The oddsmakers had a pretty impressive night when it came to predicting the actual winners. Of the 10 matches with betting lines, nine had a clear favorite. Eight of those nine favorites won their matches. That gives the oddsmakers an 88.9% success rate in matches where one wrestler or team was favored to win. The only real upset came when Adam Page and Brodido defeated Swerve Strickland and The New Level to capture the AEW World Trios Championships. Even more interesting, every favorite listed at -500 or shorter won. The Young Bucks, Moxley, Ospreay, Mercedes Moné, Persephone and Divine Dominion all delivered. The bookmakers clearly knew which way most of this card was heading. Picking winners is one thing. Actually making money is another. title: Chad Gable Says Shoulder Injury Fueled His Drive
raw_title: WWE's Chad Gable Explains How Shoulder Injury Created 'Competitive Fire' Within Him
summary_src: WWE Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable explained how his shoulder injury created da "competitive fire" rather than jealousy within him.
body: Gable spoke more about the injury, which he suffered during his Worlds Collide 2025 match against El Hijo del Vikingo , on " Insight with Chris Van Vliet ." He said the way things worked out that led to the mask vs. mask match and everything that followed are "unfathomable to think about." "It's the kind of stuff you can't write even if you wanted to," Gable said. "It's just happenstance. To me, at the end of the day, it tells me, even more reason, I can stop believing in coincidence. Like, some things were just meant to be. Things were meant to play out a certain way, and that's out of our control. I'm no longer a believer in coincidence." He said that he was having what he would call the peak of his career right before he was injured. He was creatively fulfilled and doing a lot, but then, he said it all came crumbling down. "It was one of those stories you hear about, where it's like, right at the peak, the bottom just fell out," Gable explained. "It doesn't get much more tragic for a guy like me, who values progress and achievement at such a high level.... It just all came to a halt, and I didn't have a choice at that point. I was told, 'This needs to get fixed.'" "I never gave it a chance to really settle in, because it was like, 'We got stuff to do here, man,'" he said. "Then, there was some pretty gnarly bumps in the Money in the Bank match, as well, that took their toll... Woke up the next day and man, I don't think I've ever felt that level of fragility that I felt the next day. Almost like any little thing I did, I was just going to ruin myself." Gable said the time spent at home following the injury was anxiety-inducing, but he had faith in all the people he talked to about what was in store for him. He said that the FOMO was real, watching Kaiser take the character he created and transform it, transcending into a success no one expected. "What it did, fortunately for me, it didn't create any jealousy," he said. "It created just like, this competitive fire that I think, if you're coming up against me, it's one of my strongest assets, is my competitive fire. I'm not a hater. I don't look down on anyone else's success, but I will challenge you and I will try and be better than you."
summary: Chad Gable discussed his shoulder injury from the Worlds Collide 2025 match against El Hijo del Vikingo on Insight with Chris Van Vliet. He described being at the peak of his career creatively before the injury caused everything to collapse, calling the sequence of events leading to the mask vs. mask bout something that could not have been scripted. Gable stated the experience ended his belief in coincidence and instead reinforced that some things are simply meant to be.

title: Scotty 2 Hotty Shares Stone Cold Doctor Visit Story
raw_title: Scotty 2 Hotty Recalls Stone Cold Steve Austin Taking Him To Doctor's Appointment
summary_src: Former WWE star and AEW producer Scotty 2 Hotty recalls Stone Cold Steve Austin taking him to a doctor's appointment prior to having neck fusion surgery
body: "I had cervical fusion by Dr. Youngblood in San Antonio," Scotty said. "Stone Cold went first, and then everybody [went]. Edge went, Lita went, Bob Holly, Benoit went...I think that Angle may have ended up going, but I don't think so. But there were a bunch of us. Yeah, cervical fusion. 5, 6, 7." "Actually, Austin went to my first doctor's appointment with me, which is wild," Scotty said. "I remember him being in the room before the doctor came in and he takes the x-rays out of the envelope, he sits them on the table...turns on the light, and he starts looking at them and goes, what was the line, 'I'm not a doctor, but I did stay in a Holiday Inn Express last night.' But how cool is that that he went with me to that? So cool man."

title: AEW scrapped Dynamite seventh-anniversary plans after PAC death
raw_title: AEW scrapped Dynamite seventh-anniversary plans for PAC tribute show
summary_src: The September 30 episode of AEW Dynamite was originally planned as a seventh-anniversary show before the company changed course following PAC’s death.
body: The September 30 episode of AEW Dynamite was originally planned as a seventh-anniversary show before the company changed course following PAC’s death. Tony Khan revealed the original plans for the episode, which took place at the Petersen Events Center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, during the post-AEW WrestleDream media scrum on Saturday. “I didn’t talk about it at all for an important reason, because the show where we were going to talk about this, and it was going to be the seven-year anniversary show, it was far more important to celebrate the life of PAC. What would have been seven years of Wednesday Night Dynamite, where we would have marked this, it wasn’t the most important milestone. “And Ben’s in our hearts every night. As far as a one-night tribute show, that was the best we could do. It was perfect. And I think everybody who participated gave it their very best for him. And so that would have been where we would have talked a lot about the seven-year anniversary.” Dave Meltzer also addressed the original plans on Sunday’s Wrestling Observer Radio. “They were going to talk about the length that they’ve been on the air and the longest prime-time wrestling show in Turner history,” Meltzer said on the show. “And he said that once it became the PAC show, they were never going to mention that at all on the air, and that he made the call: no pushing the pay-per-view on that show. They really lost a lot of time that they could have done building it.” The first edition of AEW Dynamite aired on TNT on October 2, 2019. PAC wrestled on that show, defeating Hangman Page in the third match of the night. Meltzer awarded the match three and a half stars. Following PAC’s death on September 27, Khan announced that the September 30 episode would be dedicated to the late wrestler. The tribute show featured matches and tributes honoring PAC, and also Bryan Danielson’s return to the ring. Following PAC's death, Tony Khan shifted the focus to a tribute show instead. Khan discussed the change during the post-WrestleDream media scrum and noted that the anniversary was no longer the priority.

Following PAC's death, Tony Khan shifted the focus to a tribute show instead. Khan discussed the change during the post-WrestleDream media scrum and noted that the anniversary was no longer the priority.

llm_long: The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has ruled that Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, died of bronchial asthma. The determination classifies his death as natural. The senior sports reporter for the California Post first reported the ruling.
Satterley died on September 27 in Des Plaines, Illinois. He was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant. Emergency services responded and pronounced him dead at 4:08 pm local time.
Authorities stated there were no indications of trauma or foul play. His death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed and additional testing completed before the cause was finalized.

Satterley was born in Newcastle upon Tyne and began wrestling in 2004. He became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships including a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion.

He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments there included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns, and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion.

Satterley joined AEW in 2019 after returning to Dragon Gate. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was a loss to Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out on September 26.

title: Austin Creed Was Completely Burned Out Before Leaving WWE
raw_title: Austin Creed Was Completely Burned Out Before Leaving WWE
summary_src: Austin Creed may be enjoying his new life in AEW, but the former Xavier Woods has admitted that his final years in WWE came with some serious exhaustion.
body: During an interview with Fightful at PAX Australia , Creed opened up about the three-month break he took following his WWE departure. For the first time in his 23-year wrestling career, he was able to spend an entire summer at home with his children instead of constantly being on the road. “I’ve never been home for the summer. I’ve been wrestling 23 years. And I’ve been wrestling 23 summers.” Creed explained that finally having that time with his family made him realize just how much he had been missing. More importantly, it gave him a chance to establish a healthier balance between his career and personal life. “For me this was the first time that I got to be home for the summer with my kids so I got to actually, you know, be there and be dad, which was really cool and so it also helped me to figure out how to build a foundation to have a better work life balance than I had previously.” The former New Day member didn’t sugarcoat how exhausted he had become. Between wrestling, running his YouTube channel and making appearances, Creed admitted that his packed schedule had taken a toll. He also explained why he kept pushing himself despite feeling that way. “I was very burnt out. Yeah. Very burnt out. You know, wrestling constantly doing the YouTube channel constantly, doing appearances constantly everywhere, which is important to me because I want to be able to hustle.” Creed said his motivation was always to make the most of his career while his body could still handle the demands of professional wrestling. He knows that eventually there will come a point when he can’t perform at the same level, and he doesn’t want to be financially forced to continue. “I want to be able to build what I can while I can because once my body doesn’t want to do it anymore, I don’t want to have to feel like I have to keep doing it, you know? So, sure there’s sacrifice.” However, the time away from wrestling also helped Creed understand that he doesn’t need to accept every opportunity that comes his way. He said having an entire summer to himself allowed him to reconsider his priorities and become more selective about his commitments. “Being able to have that summer really allowed me to figure out what I want my life to look like and what I will say yes to, what I will say no to, what I’m comfortable doing, what I’m not comfortable doing, what I will get out of bed for and leave my house for, and what I will not.” Creed explained that establishing those boundaries has completely changed how he approaches his career and personal life. “And so having that mindset now has really, really given me a new center. And it feels really good to be able to have that balance.” Creed is now back inside the ring, but it sounds like he has no intention of returning to the exhausting routine that dominated his WWE career. title: AEW May Be Planting Seeds for Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight Split
raw_title: AEW May Be Planting Seeds for Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight Split
summary_src: Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight might be one of AEW’s most exciting tag teams right now, but it looks like the company could already be setting the stage for them to go their separate ways. Some interesting moments during AEW WrestleDream have Dave Meltzer convinced that a breakup could be coming.
body: Fletcher and Knight challenged The Young Bucks at AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 . The match was packed with crazy moves and near falls, but there were also a couple of moments that might end up meaning a whole lot more down the road. During the match, Knight accidentally connected with Fletcher while trying to break up a move. The Young Bucks eventually took advantage and picked up the victory after hitting Knight with the BTE Trigger. On the October 18 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer praised the match but also pointed out that AEW appeared to be deliberately teasing trouble between Fletcher and Knight. He said it wasn’t just something that happened at WrestleDream, either, because the company had already dropped hints during Dynamite. “There are two spots in there where teased the future split, which, you know, you can see it coming, and they teased it on Wednesday as well.” That doesn’t mean a breakup has been officially confirmed, but Meltzer clearly believes AEW is building toward something. Rather than having Fletcher and Knight suddenly turn on each other, the company appears to be using small mistakes and moments of miscommunication to create tension between them. What makes the situation more interesting is how strongly Meltzer praised both men. He believes they’re developing into major stars, especially after their performance against The Young Bucks. “Three years from now, man, you know, they’ll be two of the top guys in this business.” Meltzer also had enormous praise for the match itself, calling it one of the greatest tag team matches he’s ever seen. “That Young Bucks match was legit like one of the greatest tag team matches I’ve ever seen.” AEW hasn’t announced any plans to separate Fletcher and Knight, and neither wrestler has turned on the other. Still, between the accidental contact at WrestleDream and the earlier television hints, there may be more to their recent problems than a couple of mistakes. For now, Fletcher and Knight are still together, but AEW might already be laying the groundwork for a major split. If Meltzer is right, that spectacular match against The Young Bucks could eventually be remembered as one of the first signs that things were about to fall apart. body: “Yeah, we’ll see him Wednesday. And I know who he’ll be against. title: Cody Rhodes Calls Marvel Studios Visit Wonderful
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Says His Visit To Marvel Studios Was 'A Wonderful Meeting With Wonderful People'
summary_src: Cody Rhodes discusses his visit to Marvel Studios from back in August, noting it was 'a wonderful meeting with wonderful people.' Back in August, Cody would take to social media to share a photo of himself visiting Marvel studios, and has yet to confirm any tidbits from the…
body: Cody Rhodes discusses his visit to Marvel Studios from back in August, noting it was ‘a wonderful meeting with wonderful people.’ Back in August, Cody would take to social media to share a photo of himself visiting Marvel studios, and has yet to confirm any tidbits from the meeting about what potential role he could have in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. While speaking to Brandon Davis in a new interview , Cody Rhodes would be asked if he has been asked much about the meeting while doing media for Street Fighter. “You know, there’s one guy (Andrew Schulz) in particular who was sitting next to me on this couch pretty much all day who is teasing things that aren’t real, and if they were real, I wouldn’t say anything, and guessing characters that are great, great characters because I grew up I mean, I learned every Marvel character you could from the trading cards, and then, of course, I had the animated series, and we have it again now. It’s been heavily discussed, but I never discuss it. That’s the beauty. I’ve said nothing other than that was just a photo at a wonderful office after a wonderful meeting with wonderful people. (It’s a pretty cool office.) Yeah, it is, really, and also the whole history. If they had said to you, hey, this character, something like that, and you go in there, there’s a whole library. You could take 30 minutes and go, got it, know it, you know?” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Cody Rhodes described his August visit to Marvel Studios as a wonderful meeting with wonderful people. While promoting Street Fighter, he told Brandon Davis that the encounter has been heavily discussed in media but he has revealed no details about any potential role in the MCU. Rhodes noted that fellow guest Andrew Schulz teased fictional ideas during interviews, while he himself grew up collecting Marvel trading cards and watching the animated series.

title: Why Austin Creed Isn’t Recreating UpUpDownDown in AEW After WWE Exit
raw_title: Why Austin Creed Isn’t Recreating UpUpDownDown in AEW After WWE Exit
summary_src: Austin Creed may have left UpUpDownDown behind when he walked away from WWE, but the former Xavier Woods isn’t worried about starting over.
body: During an interview with Fightful at PAX Australia , Creed was asked about walking away from UpUpDownDown, the gaming platform he spent years building during his WWE career. Considering how closely the channel was associated with his personality and success outside the ring, the interviewer wanted to know how difficult it was to leave that part of his career behind. Creed’s answer was pretty straightforward. He isn’t worried about losing the platform because he believes he has the creativity to build something new whenever he wants. The conversation then turned toward the possibility of reuniting DaParty, the popular gaming group featuring Creed, Tyler Breeze, Adam Cole and Claudio Castagnoli. With none of the members currently signed to WWE, Creed acknowledged that the opportunity to create something together is now available. “I will say that you are correct none of the DaParty members are currently signed with WWE. And that would lead me to believe that there is at least the chance that something will happen, that the chance of something to be created is available.” Creed then offered an interesting tease when asked whether a new gaming project was already being developed. He wouldn’t confirm anything, but he also refused to rule out the possibility that filming or preparations for a new channel had already started. “I will not confirm or deny if anyone has been filming anything or if anyone has been creating assets for a new YouTube channel. I will not confirm or deny that.” However, when the conversation shifted toward creating an UpUpDownDown-style channel featuring AEW talent, Creed explained why he doesn’t want to rush into anything. He said developing real relationships with his new coworkers is much more important than immediately putting them in front of a camera. Creed explained that the chemistry behind UpUpDownDown wasn’t something that happened overnight. Many of the wrestlers who appeared on the channel had known each other for years, dating back to their time in WWE developmental or working together on the independent wrestling scene. title: On the Record: Austin Creed Admits He Wanted to Join AEW While Still Working for WWE
raw_title: Austin Creed Admits He Wanted to Join AEW While Still Working for WWE
summary_src: Austin Creed didn’t just start thinking about AEW after leaving WWE. The former Xavier Woods has confirmed that he was already interested in joining Tony Khan’s company while he was still working for WWE, and his reasoning had a lot to do with wanting to wrestle a different style.
body: During an interview with Fightful at PAX Australia , Creed was asked whether he had ever considered jumping to AEW while watching his friends and former colleagues compete there. He didn’t hesitate to confirm that the idea had crossed his mind. “Yeah, definitely. Just to experience another style. There’s definitely a very specific WWE style and very specific AEW style.” The interviewer pointed out that Creed and Kofi Kingston looked noticeably different during their first match on AEW Dynamite. The two former New Day members were moving at a much faster pace than fans had become accustomed to seeing during their WWE run. Creed agreed with that observation and explained that the faster style wasn’t something new to him. In fact, he reminded fans that he originally made a name for himself working in TNA’s X Division, where athleticism and high-speed wrestling were major parts of his presentation. “Just a different style and I think that for a long time being seen in that way people forget. So like if you’ve been watching wrestling a long time, you know, I came up in the X Division. So like this is what I was born to do.” He also pointed out that Kingston had a similar background. Long before The New Day became one of WWE’s most successful factions, Kingston was known for his high-flying offense and fast-paced matches. Creed said AEW has given both men the chance to revisit that side of their wrestling careers. “And Kofi was always that fast moving high flyer. And so it’s just refreshing to be able to have the chance to move around like that again.” Creed wasn’t interested in turning the conversation into an attack on WWE. Instead, he explained that having two major wrestling companies with different approaches is a good thing for both performers and fans. For him, the biggest benefit of joining AEW has been the opportunity to do something different after spending so many years working in WWE’s system. “I think it’s great that there’s two different styles. I think it’s great that people have options of what they want to watch and what they’re interested in. And for me as a performer, it’s nice to be able to do something different than what I’ve been doing for a while. It’s a different kind of fulfillment, you know what I mean?” Creed also explained that joining AEW has allowed him to face wrestlers he has never worked with before, including younger talent who actually grew up watching him and Kingston compete in WWE. “And so to be able to be at AEW and have these matches with people that yes, we have history with some people, some people we have no history with. We’re meeting them for the first time. And there are some people who watched us when they were growing up and wanting to be wrestlers.” That realization has also made Creed appreciate just how much his career has changed since his early days in the business. “That’s crazy to think like I was always the young guy in the locker room and now I’m definitely not. So it’s been a really cool shift

title: Shingo Takagi Angers Wife Natsupoi Over Favorite Wrestler
raw_title: Shingo Takagi Learns the Hard Way as He Angers Wife Natsupoi by Naming WWE’s Stephanie Vaquer as His Favorite Female Wrestler (Full Video with Subtitles)
body: Shingo Takagi Learns the Hard Way as He Angers Wife Natsupoi by Naming WWE’s Stephanie Vaquer as His Favorite Female Wrestler (Full Video with Subtitles) 29 seconds ago Photo courtesy of meraWRESTLING X account Photo courtesy of meraWRESTLING X account New Japan Pro-Wrestling superstar Shingo Takagi is learning the hard way what the trials and tribulations of marriage is all about. Takagi is married to STARDOM superstar Natsupoi and the two are set to team up on Oct. 29th for the first time to take on Hirooki Goto & Yuna Mizumori. Takagi & Natsupoi announced their marriage earlier this year and recently, Takagi made a crucial mistake that has apparently cost him dearly. Both Takagi & Natsupoi were talking to reporters after a practice session when Takagi was asked about Natsupoi’s ability as a wrestler. Takagi began to speak when Natsupoi asked him who his favourite women’s wrestler was and Takagi wisely motioned to Natsupoi. They continued the heated conversation about Vaquer and a novice Takagi asked if they were done with the topic. Natsupoi assured him that she wasn’t done in the least bit. Takagi, to his credit, tried to make amends by praising Natsupoi’s ability as a wrestler but the damage had already been done and he had reached a point of no return. An angry Natsupoi then began complaining about the practice session they just had by telling Takagi that they only practiced his signature moves and she was the only one getting thrown around. Hoping for a bit of help, Takagi reminded Natsupoi that they were in the middle of a interview and motioned to the interviewer. The interviewer didn’t get hint that Takagi was desperately sending and suggested that he talk it out with Natsupoi. The interviewer received a subtle death stare from Takagi but still seemed clueless by suggesting Takagi apologize to his wife. Eventually, Natsupoi got up and told Takagi she wasn’t going home that evening then proceeded to leave. Here is the full video with subtitles of the entire exchange between Shingo Takagi and Natsupoi. Entire video credit goes to meraWRESTLING :

Natsupoi eventually stood up, told Takagi she would not be returning home that night, and left the interview. The full exchange was captured on video by meraWRESTLING.

body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game BIRTHRIGHT HEADLINES IN 8 MAN TAG ACTION: 10/15 WWE NXT LIVE REPORT FROM KITCHENER, ONTARIO By Dan Orgill on 2026-10-16 08:10:00 I attended the NXT show at the Kitchener Memorial Auditorium in Kitchener, Ontario. The venue holds about 7000 people, but the arena was cut in half for the show. So with the stage setup, I’d estimate 2000-2500 fans. Looked to be about 85% full for what was available. My seat was $53 Cdn. So a pretty good deal these days. Lizzy Rain via pinfall despite attempted interference by Birthright. Arianna heeled the crowd on the mic prior to the match. 3. Saquon Shugars vs. Jackson Drake (North American Championship) Drake retained via pinfall after a distraction by members of Vanity Project Kendal Grey via pinfall. Perros took the mic after an early exchange and also heeled the crowd. The two Canadian girls made sure they’d get heat, and they did. Vanity Project retained after interference from the other members. Myka Lockwood chokeslammed Bravo ( Tyler Bate ) which led to him taking Vanity’s finisher and the pin. Match of the night, easily. Bate & Dunn are SO good. Lockwood’s outfit ( all black leather ) and her mannerisms are clearly modelled after Chyna. 7. Izzi Dame vs. Thea Hail vs. Zaria - Triple Threat (North American Championship) Zaria retained after pinning Hail. Hail is a little firecracker, but she looked so tiny next to the other women. Not a smooth match at certain points. Zaria looks like a star in her appearance and entrance, 100%. 8. Birthright vs. Shiloh Hill, Tavion Heights, Tony D'Angelo, Shawn Spears (8 man tag) Lexis King took the mic before Spears came out. He said he only saw 3 men on the other team, so he’d help us all learn to count. He counted off the members of birthright, the 3 babyfaces, the ring announcer, so he was at 9. Told the ref he made 9 1/2, cue Shawn Spears music….massive 10 chants from the crowd. Birthright did the honours after a spear & choke slam by D’Angelo. Spears thanked the crowd after, and indicated it could be his last time wrestling in Canada with WWE.

The injury occurred during a match against Je’Von Evans at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles. Rusev experienced complete numbness in his arms, requiring him to roll out of the ring.
Medical staff considered stopping the match as Rusev reported he could not feel his hands. After regaining sensation, he re-entered the ring and completed the bout despite significant pain.
Rusev's wife CJ Perry noted that he received medical clearance in September. She emphasized that he finished the July match to do what was right for business rather than having the bout stopped.
Perry addressed online rumors suggesting Rusev avoided putting others over. She clarified that he consistently works to create strong stories and support the business.

title: Will Ospreay Makes Another Joke About His Wife Alex Windsor After Controversial AEW Promo
raw_title: Will Ospreay Makes Another Joke About His Wife Alex Windsor After Controversial AEW Promo
summary_src: Will Ospreay just can’t resist making jokes about his wife, Alex Windsor, and his latest comment might sound familiar to anyone who remembers his controversial wedding night promo.
body: During a recent interview with WKMG News 6 , Ospreay was asked about the challenge of defending his AEW World Championship in the eight-man Clockwork Carnage Match. Since he would be entering the match first, Ospreay knew he’d need some serious stamina to survive. However, instead of giving a typical answer about his conditioning, Ospreay couldn’t help himself and slipped in a joke about his wife. “I mean, it is, but thankfully, I’m a cardio machine. I’m very good at that. Ask the wife.” “I got a good wife, man. So here’s what I did to treat her—I took her upstairs, I smashed the life out of her, bruv. I said, ‘Babe, clean yourself up, I gotta go to Houston.’” The remark drew criticism online, with some fans accusing Ospreay of being disrespectful toward his wife. He later defended the joke during an interview with 107.7 The Bone, claiming he was actually talking about beating Windsor at Mario Kart. Ospreay also made it clear that he wasn’t interested in apologizing to anyone who took offense, pointing out that his wife, his boss and AEW’s television partners had no problem with what he said. As for his latest cardio joke, Ospreay actually backed up his claims inside the ring at WrestleDream. He entered the Clockwork Carnage Match first and survived all seven challengers before securing the deciding fall with just two seconds remaining. Ospreay hit Adam Copeland with a Hidden Blade and pinned him to finish with three points, retaining the AEW World Championship. body: Will Ospreay discusses his adoration for the pro wrestling industry, noting how far he would go to remain a pro wrestler. Ospreay has always been someone who adores the world of professional wrestling, not being shy in speaking about his early days of wrestling being in his own back garden on a trampoline before continuing to develop his skills in other backyard wrestling promotions before beginning his formal training in the industry. While speaking to WKMG News 6 in a recent interview before AEW WrestleDream, Will Ospreay would speak about how blessed he is to be in the position he is in, while also noting the lengths he would go to remain a part of the industry, even if it were made illegal overnight. “I’m so blessed to be able to be in this position, to be able to just do something that… I love doing, like I’ve said it so many times, if wrestling became like illegal tomorrow, like I’d be in my garden wrestling. Like I’d happily, like I’d be like the criminal mastermind of like an underground, Mafia wrestling run promotion. Do you know what I mean? That’s just me.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Ilja Dragunov Set For AEW Dynamite Debut
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov speaks at WrestleDream presser, will make AEW in-ring debut on October 21 Dynamite
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut on the October 21 episode of Dynamite. Tony Khan made the announcement during the WrestleDream post-show press
body: Ilja Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut on the October 21 episode of Dynamite. Tony Khan made the announcement during the WrestleDream post-show press conference on after Dragunov was revealed as AEW’s latest signing earlier in the pay-per-view. Khan asked Dragunov whether he was ready to begin wrestling for the promotion on Wednesday. “How about this Wednesday night? Based on what we said backstage, I think you’ve said you’re ready to start fighting this Wednesday night on Dynamite.” Dragunov later made his enthusiasm for getting started clear. At the press conference, Dragunov described his arrival in AEW as “very, very overwhelming” and “a new breath of fresh air.” “The way I’ve got welcomed here, I know it feels just plainly right,” he said. Asked which members of the AEW roster he wanted to wrestle, Dragunov named Jon Moxley, Samoa Joe and Kyle Fletcher before suggesting that the list extended much further. A better question is who not. Like, for real, if I think about all the competitors here at AEW, it is hard to say who I do not want to wrestle. Dragunov also discussed his decision to sign with AEW after his WWE contract expired in August. He said that after almost 14 years in professional wrestling, he wanted an environment in which he could continue to bet on himself and satisfy his desire to compete. Asked for his early impressions of AEW, Dragunov cited “freedom” and “trust,” describing the promotion as “a landscape of limitless opportunities.” Khan also explained why AEW only began airing vignettes teasing Dragunov’s arrival in the days immediately before WrestleDream. According to Khan, Dragunov informed him during Wednesday’s Dynamite that he would be able to collect his visa the following day. AEW had prepared the vignette in case his arrival needed to be delayed by another week or two, but accelerated the plans once his availability for WrestleDream became certain. Khan said he had not wanted to promote Dragunov for the pay-per-view until the company knew he could attend.

The news came at the WrestleDream post-show press conference after Dragunov was revealed as the promotion's newest signing. Dragunov called the opportunity overwhelming and a fresh start while naming Jon Moxley, Samoa Joe and Kyle Fletcher among those he hopes to face.

title: Riyadh Airport Reopens With WWE Crown Jewel Still In Doubt
raw_title: Riyadh airport reopens amid uncertainty over WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reportedly reopened on Sunday as questions remain regarding WWE holding Crown Jewel in the city on November 7. The airport had been closed since last Saturday.
body: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reportedly reopened on Sunday as questions remain regarding WWE holding Crown Jewel in the city on November 7. The airport had been closed since last Saturday. Saudi coalition officials said Thursday that it had been targeted 20 times this month, leaving 17 people dead and 333 wounded. However, there are conflicting reports about the airport’s status, with some news outlets continuing to describe it as closed. FlightStats listed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, primarily domestic flights, while Flightera showed at least one international passenger flight as having landed. Many international airlines are still suspending flights to Riyadh. Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been canceled or postponed following increased attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament, part of Riyadh Season, was originally scheduled for October 21–24 but has been postponed until December 27–30. The UCI Urban Cycling World Championships, scheduled for November 3–7 in Riyadh, have been canceled. However, the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli boxing match scheduled for October 31 is still expected to proceed. “Sources within WWE concurred that tweet put even more pressure on TKO not to cancel its two planned shows. I can’t say everyone of course, but everyone that I have been in contact with after this past week would rather not go there right now. In the past, going to Saudi Arabia was “optional,” in a sense that one would not be punished financially for not going, but at times there have been people told if they voluntarily choose not to go, it’s fine, except they may have to drop championships or have pushes toned down.” As of this writing, WWE has not announced any plans to postpone, reschedule or relocate Crown Jewel. He joined the F4WOnline team in 2019 and was named Managing Editor in the summer of 2026. Born in Calgary, Alberta, Ian has covered professional wrestling for more than 15 years.

The Six Kings Slam tennis event was postponed to December while the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships set for early November were canceled.

title: Channing Lorenzo Injured At NXT Live Event
raw_title: Channing 'Stacks' Lorenzo Seemingly Injured At WWE NXT Live Event
summary_src: Channing "Stacks" Lorenzo seemingly suffered an injury during Friday's "WWE NXT" live event in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada.
body: According to a fan report on Reddit , paramedics rushed down to the ring and fit him in a neckbrace before stretching him out of the venue. Lorenzo had been teaming with his fellow BirthRight members Lexis King, Charlie Dempsey, and Uriah Connors to take on Tony D'Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill, and Shawn Spears in the show's main event. A fan in attendance noted that he may have sustained an injury while taking a back body drop from the ring to the floor. Another indicated that Lorenzo had either jumped or fell off the top turnbuckle and collided face-first with the ringside barricade; he was said to have then landed "hard" on the floor, appearing unresponsive. Spears, a native of Canada, addressed the crowd after the match , saying that "unfortunately, things happen in this ring." He went on to call WWE a family before thanking the crowd for coming out to the show. Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer reported that, as of Friday night, Lorenzo was still in the hospital. On Saturday afternoon, Connors provided a further update on Lorenzo's condition, writing on X: "My boys alive and well!! We can't be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his a**." My boys alive and well!! We can't be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his ass🫡 #BIRTHRIGHT Lorenzo is a regular fixture on "NXT," with his most recent in-ring outing resulting in and him and Connors losing to Mini Vikingo and Chazz "Starboy" Hall in the first round of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.
summary: Channing Lorenzo was removed from the ring on a stretcher wearing a neck brace after a main event tag match at a WWE NXT live event. He was teaming with Lexis King, Charlie Dempsey and Uriah Connors against Tony D'Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill and Shawn Spears when the incident occurred. Per the Wrestling Observer, Lorenzo remained hospitalized as of Friday night, with Uriah Connors issuing an update on his condition the following day.

llm_long: Rusev returned to the ring at the WWE live event in Hawaii on October 16. The appearance marked his first match since sustaining an injury on July 27.
The injury occurred during a match against Je’Von Evans at the Intuit Dome in Los Angeles. Rusev experienced complete numbness in his arms, requiring him to roll out of the ring.
Medical staff considered stopping the match as Rusev reported he could not feel his hands. After regaining sensation, he re-entered the ring and completed the bout despite significant pain.
Rusev's wife CJ Perry noted that he received medical clearance in September. She emphasized that he finished the July match to do what was right for business rather than having the bout stopped.
Perry addressed online rumors suggesting Rusev avoided putting others over. She clarified that he consistently works to create strong stories and support the business.

title: Riyadh Airport Reopens as WWE Crown Jewel’s Saudi Arabia Status Remains Uncertain
raw_title: Riyadh Airport Reopens as WWE Crown Jewel’s Saudi Arabia Status Remains Uncertain
summary_src: WWE may have just gotten some good news ahead of Crown Jewel, but the company isn’t out of the woods yet.
body: The airport had been closed since last Saturday following a series of attacks in the region. Saudi coalition officials said Thursday that the airport had been targeted 20 times this month, with 17 people killed and 333 wounded. That has raised serious questions about whether WWE can safely get its wrestlers, staff and production crew into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. Now there are signs that things may be improving. According to flight tracking information, FlightStats listed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, with most of those being domestic flights. Flightera also showed at least one international passenger flight had landed at the airport. However, there is a pretty big catch. Some news outlets are still describing the airport as closed, and several major international airlines continue to suspend flights to Riyadh. So while some planes appear to be getting in, that doesn’t mean WWE can start booking everyone on flights and call it a day. Canelo Alvarez’s October 31 fight against Christian Mbilli is still expected to go ahead in Riyadh. Saudi entertainment official Turki Alalshikh recently claimed that Canelo personally reached out to confirm he was still planning to fight. The airport situation is only part of the problem. Riyadh’s recent airport attacks have already raised security concerns about Crown Jewel , while Saudi Arabia has also been considering canceling additional Riyadh Season events . For now, WWE is still operating under the assumption that Crown Jewel will take place in Riyadh on November 7. No location change has been announced, and the company is continuing preparations for the show. WWE now has less than three weeks to figure out whether Riyadh is actually going to be ready for Crown Jewel. The airport may be showing signs of life again, but with other sporting events already getting canceled and international travel still disrupted, this is far from a done deal. title: Chad Gable Remembers WWE Match Against Kurt Angle
raw_title: Chad Gable Recalls WWE Match With Kurt Angle, Getting Pulled Over Afterwards
summary_src: WWE Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable recalls his lone singles match with Kurt Angle in 2019, revealing that he was pulled over for speeding after
body: Beyond the match being a dream come true for Gable, he revealed that he and Angle benefited from a rarity not often seen during the days of Vince McMahon running "Raw." That, coupled with the match being a dream come true and it taking place in the Midwest near Gable's home state of Minnesota, resulted in it being a wonderful night for Gable. Alas, there was one thing that occurred afterward that only slightly marred it. "The cool thing I do remember about that is, in a very rare occurrence on a 'Monday Night Raw' live, we actually ended up getting more time than we were supposed to, in the moment. So we just got to wrestle. And to be able to just go in there and just be wrestling on the fly, winging it with Kurt Angle of all people, it's like 'This is happening?' And this is in Chicago, which is great, the crowd is always great. It was a great night man, except I got a speeding ticket on the way home."
summary: Chad Gable described his match with Kurt Angle on Monday Night Raw as a dream come true. The bout took place in Chicago near his home state of Minnesota and the pair were given extra time in a rare occurrence under Vince McMahon's era allowing them to wrestle on the fly. Gable said it was a wonderful night except for receiving a speeding ticket on the drive home.

title: I Just Think AEW Has The Greatest Tag Team Division In The History Of Wrestling — Chris Sabin
raw_title: Chris Sabin: I Just Think AEW Has The Greatest Tag Team Division In The History Of Wrestling
summary_src: Chris Sabin thinks that AEW has the greatest tag team division in the history of pro wrestling and that you can't argue that. Earlier this year, the Motor City Machine Guns (Sabin and Alex Shelley) would sign with AEW after being released by WWE.
body: Chris Sabin thinks that AEW has the greatest tag team division in the history of pro wrestling and that you can’t argue that. Earlier this year, the Motor City Machine Guns (Sabin and Alex Shelley) would sign with AEW after being released by WWE. The pair would share the ring with several other top tag teams in the promotion at AEW All In, and are currently one match into a best of five series with FTR. While speaking to MuscleManMalcolm in a new interview, Chris Sabin would speak about the moment at All In, noting his belief that AEW has the greatest tag team division in wrestling history. “It was a pretty surreal moment, especially, like, being out there with, like, Adam Copeland and Christian Cage. Like, these are two guys that I watched growing up. So then we have them. We have the Young Bucks out there who was, like, if anyone knows the history of the Motor City Machine Guns, were tied with the Young Bucks. You know, we’ve wrestled them so many times. TNA, Independents, PWG, everywhere. You know, we’ve never wrestled FTR before. Never had a match. So that was a cool moment to be out there with them. Yeah, man, I don’t know. I just think AEW has the greatest tag team division in the history of wrestling. I think that you can’t argue that, and we’re just excited to get in the mix with everyone, you know?” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: CJ Perry Opens Up On Serious Mental Health Struggles After Leaving WWE

summary_src: CJ Perry is opening up about how difficult life became after stepping away from WWE, and it wasn’t simply a matter of missing the spotlight.
body: Speaking on Nick Club Wrestling Happy Hour , Perry was asked why she decided to write a fictional spy novel instead of following the traditional wrestler autobiography route. Her answer quickly turned into a much deeper discussion about how much her life has changed since leaving WWE. “I’m so lucky and so blessed and so, so grateful to have done so many things in my life, but I just, you know, within my personal life, I still wanted I wanted to grow more, you know? And I had I’ve resolved so many things with my husband over the last couple years, and I’ve grown so much from leaving WWE till now. Like, I’m a different person.” That’s when Perry admitted that her mental health had been particularly difficult to manage during certain periods of her life. “I’m really, really a different person. I’ve really focused on my mental health. I There were a couple years that I was very manic with my mental health, and I was really struggling.” Perry explained that one of the hardest things about leaving WWE was losing the feeling that came with performing live. She described the rush of appearing in front of enormous crowds as something that was almost impossible to recreate outside professional wrestling. “Uh I feel like as a performer, you know, there’s no greater high that you get, no greater adrenaline rush and dopamine hit that you get than when you’re performing live.” She went further, explaining that WWE provided an experience so intense that she still gets goosebumps just thinking about it. “And I To be able to do it at such a high level in WWE, there’s There’s really no higher level, you know? You’re performing in front of 100,000 people, and they’re either booing you or cheering you, and that’s like Just thinking about I get goosebumps. And it’s just an instant adrenaline rush that really no drug will ever satisfy.” However, Perry eventually realized that constantly chasing that feeling wasn’t necessarily healthy for her. She had to find a way to build a fulfilling life without depending on the excitement of performing inside a WWE ring. “And so, I really had to go on a journey to find happiness without it. title: Comeback Watch: CJ Perry Opens Up On What It Would Take for Her to Return to WWE

summary_src: CJ Perry isn’t done with WWE just yet, and the former Lana already knows exactly what she wants to do if the company brings her back. While her husband Rusev has returned to WWE, Perry remains absent from television, but she’s making it clear that she would love another opportunity.
body: Speaking on Nick Club Wrestling Happy Hour , Perry was asked whether she could see herself returning to WWE or getting involved in professional wrestling again. She didn’t hesitate to express interest, but explained that any comeback would need to make sense creatively. “I mean I would love to do something back in wrestling. I’d love to do something back in WWE if the story calls for it and it’s the right fit.” Perry believes WWE already has plenty of women competing for championships. Instead of joining that crowded field, she thinks her greatest value would come from working as a manager or an on-screen character who can help develop storylines and get other talent over. “I believe that my strong suit and where I can help move the needle in storytelling and and on the business side I think is definitely as a manager and as a character and you know, I don’t I don’t think they need any new women fighting for championships out there.” She continued by explaining that WWE’s women’s division already has considerable talent, but she still believes there’s a place for someone with her experience on the microphone and in character-driven storytelling. “I think they have a very very strong roster and a lot of options but I do believe I’m a very good storyteller. I believe I’m very strong on the mic, and I’m I I yeah, I and I would love to do something in the future.” “You know, Paul Heyman’s been around for a long time, so I like to hope and believe that age wouldn’t stop me.” “Uh but, it’s all about story. It’s all about We don’t see all the back ends in WWE. That’s the biggest thing I’ve learned over time is And when you guys asked earlier about stories, like if you pitch something or not, like we don’t know everything on the back end.” Perry finished by pointing out that rejected ideas can eventually become reality in WWE. She recalled how Rusev once pitched working with Kurt Angle before his return, only for the idea to be dismissed at the time. I’ll be ready if they call me. I mean, that’s why I’m in acting class.” For now, Perry remains outside WWE’s weekly television product, but she clearly isn’t ready to close that chapter. title: Legendary WWE Star Announces She's Finalized Divorce at 42

body: A longtime wrestling star has confirmed that she has officially finalized her divorce at the age of 42. Eva Marie, a former WWE star, has finalized her divorce from her longtime husband, Jonathan Coyle. The WWE alum actually “quietly” finalized her divorce last August, but it feels like it has been longer than that. “It feels like so much longer than a year,” she told Page Six. View this post on Instagram Marie is “thankful” that she and her husband, 44, did not share any children. Marie filed for divorce in December 2024 after 10 years of marriage. She told Page Six that “it was a combination of many things.” Marie said that she realized when she turned 40 that life is short and you shouldn’t put anything off – even divorce. “You only have one life, and you know, with my marriage, we were like business partners,” Marie shared. “I really felt like Jonathan and I were doing a disservice to one another because we just had a very transactional business relationship. We got along, we were totally best of buddies, but that’s not really what a marriage is, nor should it be, nor is that what I wanted it to be,” she added. title: Maria Kanellis Details 2017 WWE Return Path
raw_title: Maria Kanellis Recounts How Her WWE Return Came About After TNA Run
body: Maria Kanellis recently spoke about how her and Mike Bennett’s 2017 WWE signing came after their stint in TNA. The duo signed with WWE back in June of 2017, returning at Money in the Bank. It was of course a return for Kanellis, who had last been with the company in 2010. Maria spoke about her return on Insight With Chris Van Vliet , noting that the wedding angle for Laurel Van Ness (aka Chelsea Green) got them on WWE’s radar. You can check out the highlights below: “Okay, I’ll try and cut it short. So we’re in Ring of Honor. We’re doing all this new Japan stuff. It’s incredible, but we’ve kind of met our ceiling. So that would have been in 2015, end of 2015. I get a call from David Lagana, who is writing for TNA at the time, and he goes, ‘Hey, we would love for you to come over, work for TNA. We’ll put you guys in a main storyline. Think it’d be awesome.’ All this stuff. So I’m like, okay, cool. ‘Will I have control? Will I be able to still play a character that I want to play?’ He said, ‘Yeah, we’ll give you a lot of control.’ So I had a lot of control over what we were doing and the direction we were going. Then Mike became The Miracle. “We show up in TNA, and that year, everybody. Bobby Lashley is in, Drew McIntyre, The Hardys were there. There was just a killer roster. The Bullet Club was in and out at the time. So we were in everybody’s storylines at the time. A lot of times are the ones that are getting made a fool of, but you always need the fool in order to make a star. So we do this whole year. We build up this storyline into the wedding of Laurel Van Ness, who is Chelsea Green, The Hot Mess and Braxton. We do that wedding, and I kid you not, the crowd did not shut up once the whole time they are chanting, and everybody is playing their role, Mike is this drunk husband guy, and then we’ve got Allysin Kay, and we’ve got Laura. Even the pastor was incredible. Everybody is spot on. And then I leave the ring looking like Cruella De Vil. I’ve got this big boa on, and I’m screaming. And there’s this photo of me, and then Chelsea Green is in the ring, and she’s just makeup everywhere. Then we get the phone call from WWE, and we were convinced we were going to end up staying in TNA, and then we get the phone call.”
summary: Maria Kanellis explained on Insight With Chris Van Vliet how the Laurel Van Ness wedding storyline in TNA drew WWE's attention to her and Mike Bennett. The pair had been working in Ring of Honor and New Japan through late 2015 when a call from writer David Lagana brought them to TNA with promises of a main storyline and creative control. They signed with WWE in June 2017 and returned at that year's Money in the Bank event, marking Kanellis' first appearance with the company since 2010.

David Lagana, who was writing for TNA at the time, called Kanellis and invited the duo to join with the promise of a main storyline and significant creative control. Kanellis and Bennett accepted the offer and arrived in TNA during a stacked year that featured talents including Bobby Lashley, Drew McIntyre, The Hardys and Bullet Club.

The couple found themselves inserted into multiple storylines, often positioned as the fools to help elevate other stars. Their TNA run culminated in the wedding storyline for Laurel Van Ness, portrayed by Chelsea Green, alongside Braxton. During the wedding segment, the crowd remained loud throughout as Mike Bennett played a drunk husband, with strong performances from Allysin Kay, Laura and the pastor.

Kanellis left the ring dressed like Cruella De Vil wearing a big boa and screaming while Chelsea Green appeared with makeup running down her face. A photo from that moment contributed to WWE taking notice, leading to a phone call that brought them to the company.
Kanellis and Bennett signed with WWE in June 2017 and returned at the Money in the Bank event. The appearance marked a return for Kanellis, who had previously been with WWE until 2010.

title: Eric Bischoff Says Hulk Hogan Lived His Character
raw_title: Eric Bischoff Admits WWE HOFer Hulk Hogan 'Lost Sight Sometimes Of Who Terry [Bollea] Was'
summary_src: Eric Bischoff thinks fellow WWE HOFer Hulk Hogan got lost in the character.
body: Hulk Hogan was one of WWE's biggest stars for years, with a persona larger than most of the roster. However, according to Eric Bischoff, he often lost sight of who Terry Bollea was beneath the gimmick. "He was in character all the time," he said during an appearance on " Planet Tyrus ." Bischoff explained that Hogan would go out into public knowing he had to be 'The Hulkster,' and when he'd be approached, he was never Terry Bollea. "He lived it. And, over time, I think he lost sight sometimes of who Terry was and who Hulk was." Recalling the documentary made about Hogan after his passing , Bischoff stated that anyone watching will get glimpses of Terry Bollea, which he believes was important for fans to see. Tyrus then weighed in, recalling the many controversies that Hogan was involved in, while praising the late veteran for always owning the worst parts of himself. "He didn't blame every mistake [on someone else], he told it like it was. He wasn't perfect; he didn't always say the right thing," he said. "Who the f*** does?" Tyrus emphasized that, unlike the average person, Hogan constantly had to contend with the possibility of being recorded, despite being human like everyone else. "He could have made a lot of excuses. No one would've interrupted him if he blamed 'this one' and 'this one,'" Tyrus noted. Tyrus, a Black American wrestler himself, addressed the leaked recording and urged people to show empathy toward Hogan. Additionally, Tyrus emphasized that he doesn't want wrestlers to be measured by their race and instead by whether they're good or not, expressing that someone like Booker T should be considered a great wrestler and not a great Black wrestler.
summary: Eric Bischoff explained on Planet Tyrus that Hulk Hogan stayed in character as The Hulkster at all times in public and over the years sometimes lost sight of who Terry Bollea really was beneath the persona. Bischoff noted that the documentary made about Hogan after his death shows glimpses of the man behind the gimmick. Tyrus added that Hogan owned his mistakes without blaming others and was not perfect.

Bischoff noted that the documentary made about Hogan after his death shows glimpses of the man behind the gimmick. Tyrus added that Hogan owned his mistakes without blaming others and was not perfect.
llm.speaker: Eric Bischoff
llm.quote: He was in character all the time.

llm_long: Hulk Hogan became one of WWE's biggest stars with a larger-than-life persona. Eric Bischoff noted that Hogan remained in character constantly and often struggled to separate his real identity from the gimmick.
Bischoff explained that Hogan would appear in public fully as The Hulkster. He said Hogan was never seen as Terry Bollea when approached by fans and lived the character for years.

Bischoff recalled that over time Hogan sometimes lost sight of the distinction between Terry and Hulk. He pointed to a documentary released after Hogan's passing that offered glimpses of the man behind the character.
Tyrus discussed Hogan's many controversies and praised him for owning his mistakes without shifting blame. He observed that Hogan was not perfect and often said the wrong things, like anyone else.
Tyrus highlighted that Hogan faced constant scrutiny and the risk of being recorded at all times. He noted that Hogan could have made excuses for his errors but instead told the truth as he saw it.
As a Black American wrestler, Tyrus called for empathy regarding Hogan's leaked recording. He stressed that wrestlers should be judged on their ability rather than their race.

title: Success Or Failure? — AEW WrestleDream 2026
raw_title: AEW WrestleDream 2026: Success Or Failure?
body: Taking a look across the entirety of AEW WrestleDream 2026 , there are both positives and negatives to take away from the show, whether that be creative booking decisions, match quality, winners & losers, or something more. Ever since returning to AEW programming, Chris Jericho’s work has been some of the most unsung in the company, and he proved once again at WrestleDream how great he is for his age, putting in a strong performance against the rising Nick Wayne. It might not have all been perfect, with a kickout at one from Jericho feeling forced and a slightly awkward finish, but for the most part these two vastly exceeded expectations. This was a fun, hot match in which both showed good personality and talent, and it importantly finished with Nick Wayne going over and standing tall after beating the multi-time world champion. Given that they had only won the gold at All Out 2026, many fans had predicted a Young Bucks title retention far in advance for WrestleDream. However, the sheer quality of their show-stealer against Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight had the fans on the edge of their seats, going wild for the match they were seeing. The in-ring work was stunning, the pace of the contest was wild, the near-falls were electric, and all four men looked like a million bucks. This was among the best matches of the whole night and it elevated the entire PPV. Whether it be due to poor placement on the card or a lack of character development for names such as Dani Luna and Hyan, the fans simply didn’t care all too much for the fatal four way match for the TBS Championship at AEW WrestleDream 2026. There was some good in-ring work and a nice showcase for underdeveloped stars in the midcard division, but it was severely lacking a spark to take it to another level. Unfortunately, this ended up being one of the weaker bouts on the PPV. Andrade El Idolo has been impressive as AEW National Champion, but with him now on the periphery of the main event scene, it could be argued that he no longer needs this belt. At WrestleDream 2026, he successfully defended the gold against Tommaso Ciampa, who was in dire need of a big win. Over recent months, Ciampa lost to Darby Allin for the AEW World Title, came up short in his feud with Chris Jericho, and was defeated by International Champion Kazuchika Okada … all the while putting in some of the best work of his career. In another entertaining display, Ciampa lost once again, and it was a huge shame. Ciampa deserves to win a championship, and he should have beaten Andrade. At All Out 2026, Swerve Strickland & New Level vs. Adam Page & Brodido was a match of the year contender, leading to very high expectations for their 2-out-3-falls rematch at WrestleDream 2026. Unfortunately, the stipulation was pretty redundant and the match itself failed to generate the same levels of quality, excitement, structure and storytelling.
