title: William Regal Urges Wrestlers To Sell Pins And Kickouts Better
raw_title: WWE's William Regal: Wrestlers Should Pay More Attention To Pin Attempts & Kick-Outs
summary_src: 42-year industry veteran William Regal offers valuable advice about wrestling pin attempts and kick-outs.
body: Such was the case this weekend as the 42-year industry veteran offered valuable advice about match pin attempts and kick-outs. "We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts (even comedy bouts)," he wrote on X . "If you don't win you would make less money in the story we're telling. Every TV bout, if there's a pin, the cameras focus in. Please pin and kick out like your life and career depend on it. In story, it does." As an example of the kick-outs and pins he's looking for, Regal referenced a match between in-ring legends AJ Styles and Amazing Red from the early 2000s, in which both competitors aggressively applied every pin, with their opponent's shoulders both covered and stacked. Regal noted that every subsequent kickout was equally as forceful, almost as if "their life depended on it." 20 years later, he believes that art has since been lost. "Let's not insult the intelligence of our audience who are giving us their precious time," Regal continued. "In a fight scene in a movie (which is what wrestling is) we know the punches don't really hit but if we saw that we would eventually stop watching it. Your audience and fans deserve better. If you can't be uncomfortable for a few seconds being stacked up in a pin, maybe this isn't for you." I work for WWE but watch a lot of wrestling worldwide. This goes for all wrestlers in all companies. I have worked in Wrestling for 42 years. An observation. We are portraying trained pro fighters with instincts ( even comedy bouts). If you don't win you would make less money in... Regal himself spent multiple decades competing in the ring, with his official retirement match pitting him against Claudio Castagnoli (formerly WWE's Cesaro) in 2013. The former WWE Intercontinental Champion has remained involved in the business in a non-wrestling capacity since then.
summary: WWE veteran William Regal advised wrestlers to treat every pin attempt and kick-out with maximum intensity as if their career depended on it. He pointed to an early 2000s match between AJ Styles and Amazing Red as the ideal example where both men covered shoulders fully and exploded out with force. Regal stressed that this approach respects the audience's time and maintains the realism of the pro wrestling story.

llm_long: William Regal shared advice for wrestlers on how to better sell pin attempts and kickouts during matches. The longtime industry veteran emphasized that wrestlers are portraying trained professional fighters with instincts.

He stressed that in the story being told, failing to win would result in earning less money. Regal urged performers to treat every pin and kickout in television matches as if their life and career depended on it, especially since cameras focus closely on those moments.

As an example, Regal pointed to an early 2000s match between AJ Styles and Amazing Red. In that bout, both competitors applied pins aggressively by fully covering and stacking their opponent's shoulders.
Regal observed that each subsequent kickout in the match was delivered with equal force. He believes this approach to selling pins and kickouts has been lost over the past 20 years.

He encouraged wrestlers not to insult the intelligence of audiences who invest their time. Regal compared wrestling to fight scenes in movies, noting that visible lack of effort would cause viewers to stop watching.

Regal, who competed for multiple decades before retiring, made the comments after working in the business for 42 years. He has remained involved in wrestling in a non-wrestling role since his 2013 retirement match.

title: Bron Breakker Lands on His Neck During Scary Spot at WWE Live Event
raw_title: Bron Breakker Lands on His Neck During Scary Spot at WWE Live Event
summary_src: Bron Breakker had another really scary landing on his neck during a WWE live event, and the footage is tough to watch. Breakker somehow managed to finish the match afterwards, but right now there’s no word on whether he actually walked away without an injury.
body: The moment happened during WWE’s October 17 live event, where Breakker teamed with Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta. The babyface trio eventually won the match, but a clip involving Breakker and Knight has since started making the rounds online. Breakker was setting Knight up for his Frankensteiner from the top rope, something fans have seen him pull off plenty of times before. This time, however, Knight slipped out just as Breakker was jumping toward the turnbuckle, and everything went sideways from there. Breakker appeared to lose his footing on the turnbuckle and came crashing down in a really ugly way. He landed around his neck and upper-body area, and the referee immediately rushed over to check on him. Thankfully, Breakker was able to keep going and finish the match. That’s obviously a positive sign, but there’s currently no confirmation from WWE or Breakker about whether he was actually hurt during the spot. The footage is even harder to watch because this isn’t the first time Breakker has had a nasty landing on his neck. Back at Survivor Series: WarGames in November 2025, things went badly wrong during a Doomsday Device spot involving Cody Rhodes and CM Punk. Breakker didn’t get the full rotation and came down directly on his neck. Bryan Alvarez later described just how frightening it looked while discussing the match on Wrestling Observer Radio . Now Breakker has had another frightening close call less than a year later. The fact that he finished the October 17 match is encouraging, but until there’s an actual update on his condition, it’s probably too early to say he came out of this one completely fine. title: Roman Reigns Snubs Cody Rhodes While Picking Guests for His Head of the Table

summary_src: Roman Reigns just brought a little Tribal Chief energy into the Street Fighter universe, and Cody Rhodes definitely didn’t make the guest list. In a new video, Reigns was asked which characters he’d invite to sit at the Head of the Table, and he had an answer ready for just about everybody.
body: “Yeah, because she’d probably kick us in the mouth if we said no.” Ken also made the cut without much trouble. Reigns described him as exactly the kind of person you’d actually want hanging around the table. Ryu wasn’t so lucky. Reigns apparently thinks the guy would spend the entire dinner looking for somebody to fight, which immediately got him kicked off the invitation list. “Ryu? No, he’d just be fighting. He doesn’t stop. Bad guest.” Then came Guile, who is played by Cody Rhodes in the movie, and Reigns didn’t even need to explain himself. Considering the history between Reigns and Rhodes in WWE, his answer was about as predictable as it gets. Dhalsim, played by Vidyut Jammwal, had no such problem. Reigns immediately gave him a spot and showed some love to his Street Fighter co-star. M. Bison was another yes, with Reigns joking that keeping him close might be the smarter option considering what’s coming with the Dark Hado. “Bison? For sure. He’s gonna be mastering the Dark Hado pretty soon, so we gotta bring him close.” Of course, there was never going to be much debate when Akuma himself came up. Reigns made it clear that his own character isn’t simply getting invited to the table — he’s taking the best seat. The video comes as Reigns recently revealed that playing the character required extensive martial arts training, but this time he got to have a little more fun mixing his WWE persona with the movie — and sneaking in another shot at Cody along the way. Reigns may be stepping into Akuma’s world on the big screen, but he’s clearly not leaving the Tribal Chief completely behind. If there’s a Head of the Table anywhere, he apparently plans on claiming it. title: Jacy Jayne Cried During Priest's WrestleMania Cash-In
raw_title: Jacy Jayne Says She Cried Watching This WWE MITB Cash-In
body: "When Damian Priest cashed in at WrestleMania, I was in the audience," Jayne said. "Now, I know him and we're friends, and it's like really funny looking back on this. But, I actually cried. Just because I knew his story about being on the indies and how long it took him to get there. He was never like the 'first round draft pick,' so to say. So, for him to get the briefcase, A, was a big deal. And then B, to cash in at WrestleMania, like I could only imagine how he was feeling in that moment. When I heard the crowd erupt, it just made me emotional. There's something about genuine crowd reactions that makes me really, really emotional." While she didn't capture the briefcase in her first MITB attempt, Jayne had an impressive showing at the event in 2026. It would be Tiffany Stratton to ascend the ladder and grab the guaranteed title shot for the second time of her career.

llm.summary: Jacy Jayne was in the live audience when Damian Priest cashed in his Money in the Bank contract at WrestleMania. She became emotional watching the moment due to her knowledge of his long journey from the independents and the genuine crowd reaction. Jayne had an impressive showing in the 2026 women's ladder match though she did not win the briefcase, which was retrieved by Tiffany Stratton for the second time in her career.

llm_long: Jacy Jayne was in the audience when Damian Priest cashed in his Money in the Bank contract at WrestleMania. Jayne cried as she watched the moment unfold. She explained that she knew Priest's journey from the independent circuit and how long it had taken him to reach that level.

Priest was never considered a first round draft pick in the business. Jayne noted that securing the briefcase was already a major accomplishment for him. Cashing it in at WrestleMania made the achievement even bigger, and she tried to imagine his emotions at that time.

The crowd's eruption when Priest cashed in triggered her emotional response. Jayne stated that genuine crowd reactions always make her really emotional. She and Priest are now friends, and she finds it funny to look back on the moment. "When Damian Priest cashed in at WrestleMania, I was in the audience," Jayne said.
Jayne did not win the women's Money in the Bank briefcase in her first attempt at the event. She delivered an impressive performance in the ladder match.

title: On the Record: Paige Collett Says Medical Marijuana Saved Her Life as She Fires Back at Critics
raw_title: Paige Collett Says Medical Marijuana Saved Her Life as She Fires Back at Critics
summary_src: Paige Collett is fed up with people treating her like some kind of drug addict just because she smokes weed. The JCW wrestler says marijuana is the reason she’s still able to chase her wrestling dreams, and she’s got a message for anyone judging her without knowing what she’s been through.
body: Collett took to Twitter on October 18 and went off on people who see her smoking and immediately assume she’s some kind of party girl. She says the reality couldn’t be further from the truth. She’s battling a chronic illness, and medical marijuana has been a lifesaver. “People see me smoking and judge me & typecast me! I’m a strong advocate for medical marijuana. It has saved my life and it lets me continue to pursue my wrestling dream.” And she’s not stopping there. Collett says she’s made the decision to stay away from ketamine infusions and opioids, but people still lump her in with others who use recreational drugs simply because they’ve seen her smoking around them. And the pain doesn’t just show up when she’s wrestling. Collett has previously opened up about how her condition affects physical intimacy , saying even something most people wouldn’t think twice about can leave her recovering for days. So when strangers see Collett smoking marijuana and decide she’s just out partying, she’s not exactly going to sit there and take it. As far as she’s concerned, weed has helped keep her wrestling career alive while she’s dealing with a condition that once took away her ability to walk. title: Contract News: Carlos Silva Holds Backstage Meeting Over Expiring Talent’s TNA Contracts
raw_title: Carlos Silva Holds Backstage Meeting Over Expiring Talent’s TNA Contracts
summary_src: TNA Wrestling has some big decisions to make, and a whole bunch of wrestlers could soon be sitting down to discuss their futures with the company. With numerous contracts getting ready to expire, TNA management has already held a backstage meeting to address the situation.
body: There’s also a creative reason behind the push to get contracts sorted out. Silva wants TNA to be able to plan storylines further in advance, something that’s obviously difficult when the company doesn’t know which wrestlers will still be under contract a few months down the road. The timing is especially important because Fightful Select noted that a large number of TNA contracts are also coming up in December. That gives the company a relatively short window to figure out who will be staying and who could potentially be heading elsewhere. For now, there’s no indication that the meeting involved any specific departures or that certain wrestlers have decided against signing new deals. The discussion was intended to prepare talent for upcoming negotiations rather than announce any roster changes. Still, TNA has plenty of work ahead of it. With Bound For Glory approaching and December bringing another wave of expiring contracts, Silva is trying to get ahead of the situation before it becomes a bigger headache. Whether TNA manages to keep everyone it wants is another story. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. body: Penta’s Money in the Bank victory adds fresh momentum to an already active WWE card market, led by a new Topps NOW release and strong prior sales. Penta added one of WWE’s most important career-building achievements when he captured the Money in the Bank briefcase in New Orleans, and the win immediately created a new talking point for collectors. In WWE storylines, the briefcase holder earns a guaranteed future world title match, which means the hobby now has a clear catalyst tied to one of the company’s most popular stars. Topps quickly marked the occasion with a new Topps NOW card built around Penta’s post-match celebration. The image shows him perched on top of the ladder with the briefcase raised overhead, a visual that is easy for wrestling collectors to identify with the match-ending moment. For wrestling card collectors, that combination matters. A major televised victory is one thing, but a same-window card release with serial-numbered parallels and autographs gives the market an immediate focal point. That often helps define which card becomes the go-to commemorative piece from a wrestler’s latest milestone. Money in the Bank is more than a trophy moment. It signals that a wrestler is being positioned near the top of the card, and collectors often respond before the eventual championship match even happens. The briefcase itself has become one of WWE’s most recognizable story devices, and winning it can reshape how a performer is viewed by both fans and the market. His mask, presentation, and high-energy lucha libre offense help create memorable images, and memorable images tend to become collectible moments. In wrestling cards, visual identity is often a major factor in long-term interest, and Penta has one of the most distinct looks in the category. There is also the simple issue of momentum. Collectors tend to react when a wrestler moves from respected performer to realistic headline-level threat. A Money in the Bank win can be that bridge. summary_src: Gillberg thinks WWE left some pretty obvious money on the table when it came to his parody of Goldberg. Not only did he never get the Goldberg vs.
body: Speaking on Developmentally Speaking , Gillberg talked about Goldberg’s apparent dislike of the parody character and wondered why WWE never released a battle pack featuring the two of them. Considering the entire Gillberg gimmick was built around mocking Goldberg, he couldn’t understand why WWE never cashed in on the obvious pairing. “They — I don’t know how they didn’t make a battle pack of Goldberg-Gillberg.” According to Gillberg, WWE eventually produced merchandise based around the Festival of Friendship but somehow left him out. He even claimed that an image featuring those involved in the segment didn’t include him. “I don’t understand. I don’t understand. I was on the Festival of Friends. They did the entire Festival of Friends — everybody on it but me. Even the picture, you know what I mean? But not me.” Gillberg then dropped a much more interesting explanation for why that might have happened. He claimed he’d heard that Goldberg actually had language in his contracts preventing WWE from giving Gillberg certain merchandise opportunities. “Because I heard that Goldberg had in his contracts that Gillberg gets nothing — no action figures, no video games, no nothing.” That’s Gillberg’s claim, and he didn’t say that he’d personally seen Goldberg’s contract or confirmed the language himself. Still, if what he heard was accurate, it would certainly explain why a character so closely connected to Goldberg never received the kind of merchandise treatment Gillberg expected. It’s also why Gillberg still seems confused about WWE never putting the two together in something as simple as a battle pack. More than two decades after the parody became part of WWE history, he still believes Goldberg and Gillberg merchandise practically sold itself. body: At TNA Bound for Glory 2026, former AEW star Max Caster made his TNA Wrestling debut in a losing effort to Moose. Caster stated during his pre-match rap promo, “I drop bombs. You don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” The line was a reference to the recent Houthi missile/projectile attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. TNA apologized for what Caster said and noted that the company will no longer be working with him . After a match at the ACW event on Saturday, Caster stated the following about his future… “I don’t know if everybody here is aware of what happened with me this past week. If you don’t know, in the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. And I put out a statement. I addressed it. I apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get to apologize to was all the fans. So, guys, I really appreciate the support. Everybody who’s reached out after this happened, thank you. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time. A lot of people were excited to come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show. But you know what? Thank you, guys, here tonight at ACW, for welcoming me. And for that, I say I love you, and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time. Wow. So, I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring, it feels like I’m at home, just like you guys made me feel here tonight. So finally, for the last time in a long time, you are looking live at the best wrestler alive. title: Adriana Rizzo Breaks Silence on Wrestling Future Following WWE Release
raw_title: Adriana Rizzo Breaks Silence on Wrestling Future Following WWE Release
summary_src: Adriana Rizzo isn’t done with wrestling just because WWE decided to let her go. The former NXT star is already thinking about what’s next, but there’s one thing she needs to get through before she can really start shopping around.
body: Speaking with Pario Magazine , Rizzo was asked whether she still planned on pursuing wrestling following her WWE release . She revealed that she’s currently waiting out her 30-day period before she starts seriously looking at other opportunities. “I think, um, right now I’m still within my 30 days, so I haven’t — once I get past the 30 days, I’ll really kind of start looking into options and see what’s out there. So that’s — I’m just kind of waiting until those 30 days are up right now. Yeah.” So Rizzo isn’t announcing her retirement or walking away from wrestling. She’s basically waiting until she’s free to see who’s interested and what kind of opportunities are sitting out there for her. Her WWE exit came after a pretty unlucky run in NXT. Dave Meltzer previously reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that WWE saw something in Rizzo, but two straight knee injuries seriously hurt the momentum she had going . “And then she had two straight knee injuries, and that pretty much killed her.” The timing got even worse when Tony D’Angelo moved away from the gimmick Rizzo had been attached to. Once that happened, Meltzer said there wasn’t really an obvious spot left for her in the act. “And with that gimmick that. That left no room for her. And I guess they just made the decision that they didn’t think that she was going to make it.” Meltzer previously threw AEW and Ring of Honor out there as places that could potentially take a chance on Rizzo, but there’s been no indication that either promotion has actually made a move. Rizzo herself isn’t naming names yet either. For now, she’s simply counting down those 30 days before seeing who might want to talk. WWE may have pulled the plug on her NXT run, but Rizzo clearly isn’t ready to do the same with her wrestling career. title: On the Record: Austin Creed says he thought about joining AEW while still working for WWE
raw_title: Austin Creed says he thought about joining AEW while still working for WWE
body: While speaking with Phid McAwesome at PAX Australia, Austin Creed (formerly known as Xavier Woods) discussed whether he ever considered joining AEW while still working for WWE. Here is what Creed had to say… “Yeah, definitely. Just to experience another style. There’s definitely a very specific WWE style and a very specific AEW style. Just a different style, and I think that for a long time, being seen in that way, people forget. So, if you’ve been watching wrestling a long time, you know I came up in the X Division. So, this is what I was born to do, you know what I mean? It’s just refreshing to have the chance to move around like that again. And I think it’s great that there are two different styles. I think it’s great that people have options for what they want to watch and what they’re interested in. For me as a performer, it’s nice to be able to do something different from what I’ve been doing for a while. It’s a different kind of fulfillment, you know what I mean? And so, to be able to be at AEW and have these matches with people that, yes, we have history with some people, some history with others, or no history with others—we’re meeting them for the first time. And there are some people who watched us when they were growing up and wanted to be wrestlers. That’s great. You know, it’s crazy to think that I was always the young guy in the locker room, and now I’m definitely not. It’s been a really cool shift in just how how I’m able to look at wrestling now, and I’m really enjoying it.”
summary: The latest: while speaking with Phid McAwesome at PAX Australia, Austin Creed discussed whether he ever considered joining AEW while still working for WWE. There’s definitely a very specific WWE style and a very specific AEW style.

body: Many of my long-time readers have been asking “where have you been”, as my column volume has dropped off a bit. Well, for one, I write when I want… There’s no schedule for yours truly, as I just write when I’m feeling it… But, there’s some method to the madness as to why I took a few weeks off. No, it wasn’t for the 9/22/2026 column , as I’ve clearly followed that up with my 10/15/2026 column . I’ve been saying it for YEARS how dangerous putting on big events is within the Middle East. I’m not afraid of that topic. His death was officially ruled as bronchial asthma. If left undiagnosed or untreated, it is indeed lethal as asthma is inflammation of your airways. Now, here’s what I’m curious about… A Wellness Policy isn’t just about drug testing. In fact, it’s often a program offered by most corporation for insurance purposes as a means to help get costs down. WWE implemented one for drug testing specifically, following the death of Eddie Guerrero in late 2005 and then ramped up its seriousness during mid 2006 due to Chris Benoit’s downfall and then the online pharmacy stuff right afterward. To a normal company, it’s usually bloodwork and a physical examination. WWE’s Wellness Policy did both the examination and the drug testing, and in FACT, it saved MVP’s life when he was in the WWE and an examination found an unknown heart condition that he’s treated ever since. THIS is why ALL pro wrestlers in a corporate wrestling setting NEED TO BE INSURED and with that, required to have regular physical examinations. The physical activity of performing, along with maintaining your look, makes it essential to require your performers to be examined for any health reasons. Treat wrestlers like human beings and employees, not bulls going against a matador. They aren’t just “independent contractors”, and often times, you have to save people from themselves. There are MULTIPLE studies out there that show men, in particular, refuse to see a doctor. Just doing various Google searches of various studies shows that 50% of men refuse to do annual examinations, 65% of men will avoid going to the doctor unless they absolutely have to, and men are more unlikely to see a doctor versus women by a big margin of various polls (ranging from 33% to 50%, depending on the survey). I don’t know what happened to PAC. Was he diagnosed previously with asthma or not? Did he just forget to take his treatments? Did he forget his inhaler when an episode came up? I don’t know… BUT, if you have performers putting their bodies on the line, you should require regular examinations of the human beings you’re employing. We don’t have the full facts here, but I strongly implore both WWE and AEW to TAKE CARE OF YOUR WRESTLERS and PROTECT YOUR WRESTLERS FROM THEMSELVES. However, WWE implemented the serious Wellness Policy during 2006 and then later implemented a concussion protocol. That has SAVED LIVES. title: On the Record: Max Caster Announces Wrestling Hiatus After TNA Incident, Says He Plans To Seek Therapy
raw_title: Max Caster Announces Wrestling Hiatus After TNA Incident, Says He Plans To Seek Therapy
body: Max Caster announces he is stepping away from pro wrestling after TNA Bound For Glory incident Share on Twitter --> Max Caster has announced that he will be stepping away from professional wrestling for an extended period following his controversial departure from TNA Wrestling. Caster made his TNA debut at Slammiversary, answering an open challenge from Moose. However, his appearance drew controversy after he referenced the bombing in Riyadh during his pre-match rap. During a recent appearance at an ACW event, Caster addressed the situation, apologized to fans and reflected on his brief stint with the promotion. “In the span of one day, I started a contract and ended a contract with TNA Wrestling. I put out a statement , I addressed it and apologized to a lot of people, but the one group I didn’t get the apologize to is all the fans,” he said. “I really appreciate the support, everybody who has reached out after this happened. A lot of people were excited to watch TNA for the first time or come back to the product, and now a lot of people are disappointed that I’m not on the show.” Caster also thanked ACW for welcoming him before revealing that he intends to take an extended break from in-ring competition to focus on his personal well-being. “Thank you guys here at ACW for welcoming me,” he continued. “For that, I say, I love you and thank you. I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be, but I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time.” Caster concluded by revealing that he plans to seek therapy before eventually returning to wrestling. “I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home.” Caster did not provide a timetable for his return or indicate where he might wrestle next. Max Caster appeared at tonight’s ACW show and once again addressed what happened with him and TNA. llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Johnny Gargano's Inspiring WWE Journey
raw_title: Johnny Gargano
body: Johnny Gargano More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email superstar stats Superstar Stats Johnny Gargano NXT Champion; NXT North American Champion; NXT Tag Team Champion; WWE Tag Team Champion Johnny Gargano’s journey is proof that with heart and determination, anything is possible in WWE. Known as Johnny Wrestling, Gargano has faced countless setbacks and heard “no” more times than he can count. Labeled too small to succeed and even rejected after a 2015 WWE tryout, the self-described “chubby kid from Cleveland” refused to give up on his dreams. From play-wrestling on mattresses to aspiring to be the next Shawn Michaels, Gargano’s rise is a testament to grit and passion. He first made waves in NXT as one-half of the iconic tag team #DIY with Tommaso Ciampa. Together, they elevated NXT’s tag division, delivering unforgettable matches and capturing the NXT Tag Team Title. After parting ways with The Blackheart, Gargano formed The Way — a tight-knit group including his wife Candice LeRae, Austin Theory and Indi Hartwell — showcasing his loyalty and leadership. Despite heartache, personal struggles and setbacks, Gargano always bounces back stronger. He became the first-ever NXT Triple Crown Champion, competed in more TakeOvers than any other Superstar and delivered some of NXT’s greatest matches — all while staying true to his fans and his principles. Returning to WWE on August 22, 2022, Gargano wasted no time making an impact, superkicking Theory and reigniting his passion. Since his summer 2023 return from injury, he reunited with Ciampa, and #DIY’s triumphant victory over A-Town Down Under crowned them WWE Tag Team Champion once again. title: Rumor Claims TNA Wrestling Planning Wyatt Sicks Reunion Soon?
raw_title: Rumor Claims TNA Wrestling Planning Wyatt Sicks Reunion Soon?
body: All five were let go after WrestleMania 42 in April, part of a round of cuts in which WWE and TKO released or declined to renew more than two dozen names. Kofi Kingston and Austin Creed were among them, as were the Motor City Machine Guns. All four of those wrestlers have since signed with AEW. The Wyatt Sicks went a different way. Their 90-day non-compete periods expired over the summer, and most of the group went straight to the independents rather than to a promotion. Joseph Sawyer, known in WWE as Joe Gacy, is the reigning GCW World Champion and has kept tagging with Samuel Shaw, formerly Dexter Lumis. Sawyer also worked a six-man tag for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling on September 11 alongside Erick Redbeard, the former Erick Rowan, and AEW's Evil Uno. Sawyer and Shaw were WWE Tag Team Champions for nearly 200 days, taking the titles from Montez Ford and Angelo Dawkins in July 2025 and anchoring a SmackDown division that carried much of that summer. Their defenses included the Six Pack TLC match at SummerSlam 2025 at MetLife Stadium. Taylor Rotunda, who played Uncle Howdy, is the only member of the group who has not returned to the ring. Sawyer and Shaw alone would reshape the TNA tag division overnight. A team that held WWE's tag titles for two-thirds of a year and worked a SummerSlam stadium main card is a bigger signing than anything TNA has made in that division recently, and the two have stayed a team on the independents rather than drifting into singles work. They arrive ready to go. The name is the obstacle nobody can solve with money. WWE owns Wyatt Sicks, Uncle Howdy and everything attached to them, which is why all five are working under their own names or older ones. Whatever TNA builds cannot reference the character it is actually buying. title: Kevin Owens Explains NXT Gatineau Appearance

summary_src: Kevin Owens talks about his NXT live event return. On October 17, WWE held an NXT live event in Gatineau, Quebec, Canada.
body: This was Owens’ first match in an NXT ring since 2019. Following the match, Owens cut a promo for the fans explaining why he said yes to the show. The clip was posted online by a fan . With that said, another thing that really helped me say ‘yes’ when they asked me if I want to be a part of this show, was knowing that I get to share the ring with people that are shaping the future of what WWE will be. The four idiots we just beat – very talented idiots – but still, not the best attitude. These three, I just said the future; quite frankly, I think you’re really looking at the present. So for that, Tony, thank you. Kendall, thank you. Shiloh, thank you. It was an honor and a pleasure. Thank you guys so much.” Owens says it was Steve Carino who asked him to perform on the show, and he couldn’t say no to him. Steve, I can genuinely say, without a doubt, if you’re not familiar with his career, go back and watch. One of the greatest of all time. I met him in 2004. He took me under his wing, and without him, I am telling you, I would not be standing here right now. Tonight, or ever, I would have never had the career I had without him. So Steve, I’m not going to make you come out here, because I know you won’t want to, but you’re back there. I love you. Thank you. Anytime you need anything, I’m here. Anytime you guys need anything, I’m here. I’m at the Performance Center, you know it. Well, you guys can’t tell me, you don’t have my phone number… just know, if they ask me to be here for you guys, I’ll be here. Thank you.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Twitter: @1ReneeMichelle You could say that wrestling found Renee Michelle, thanks to a little help from former WWE Superstar Duane Gill. The onetime Gillberg approached Michelle at the first sports-entertainment event she attended and asked if she would consider giving the ring a try. Michelle agreed, and only four years later, she is one of America’s top prospects. She has held the MCW Women’s Title three times and the ECWA Women’s Title twice, and has built a reputation outside the east coast, traveling as far as Japan and India to compete. Michelle counts daredevils like Lita, Jeff Hardy and Jushin Liger among her inspirations, as well as Chigusa Nagayo, the iconic grappler who took Michelle under her wing while she trained in Japan. Able to adapt to her environment with chameleon-like deftness, Michelle will have to adjust to her biggest challenge yet when she takes part in the inaugural Mae Young Classic.

body: In a social media post, he thanked fans for their response to the match that headlined Saturday’s AEW pay-per-view, saying he was proud of himself for trying something new. “Thank you all for watching #AEWWrestleDream & being part of Clockwork Carnage,” he wrote. “The fact a company like @AEW & @TonyKhan put faith in trying something that’s not been done before. Grateful for all the reviews for it, proud of myself for daring to try something new. All love guys.” The first-ever Clockwork Carnage match took place Saturday in Orlando , with Ospreay defending the AEW World Championship against Samoa Joe, Speedball Mike Bailey, Konosuke Takeshita, Darby Allin, Adam Copeland, Ricochet, and Kazuchika Okada. Bailey and Takeshita were eliminated before all eight competitors made it to the ring, eliminating them from the match. Towards the end of the second phase, the remaining six wrestlers all had two points except for Copeland, who had zero. The final few moments suddenly saw Copeland earn two points. He was preparing to go for a third when Ospreay took him out with the hidden blade, pinning him with just seconds to go and earning three points for the win . llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Joe Hendry Names Favorite WWE Entrance Themes
raw_title: Joe Hendry Reveals Favorite WWE Entrances Themes From Past & Present
body: "Okay, so [my] favorite theme of all time is The Rock's Hollywood theme," Hendry said. "That just, like, as a fan, it gave me goosebumps watching that. I think some really iconic ones? Obviously, Steve Austin's glass smash, and 'The Game' by Motorhead is iconic as well." Hendry then segued into a discussion about current WWE themes, a polarizing subject within the WWE fanbase due to the overall negative reception to themes created by WWE's inhouse composer Def Rebel . Hendry was careful to avoid any criticism of modern WWE themes, insisting that there were plenty of strong ones. In terms of ones he thinks that work, Hendry believes they feature a certain quality, with Trick Williams' theme song having that in abundance. "On the current roster, there are some great songs," Hendry said. "I think ultimately songs that are about crowd interaction [work best], so I think they did a really great job with Trick's song. There's so many good ones."

title: On the Record: Nikki Bella Says She’s Single But “Not for Sale”
raw_title: Nikki Bella Says She’s Single But “Not for Sale”
summary_src: Nikki Bella may be single, but that doesn’t mean she’s looking for someone to start shopping around for her next boyfriend. The WWE Hall of Famer made that hilariously clear after Brie Bella announced her relationship status and immediately tried to play matchmaker.
body: Speaking on The Nikki & Brie Show , the sisters were talking with Gillie and Wallo about some of the predictable pickup lines they’ve heard because of their wrestling careers. When the conversation turned to whether either Bella had actually been interested in someone who tried the classic “Do you want to wrestle?” approach, Brie pointed out that Nikki still hasn’t met that person. That was all Brie needed before announcing that her sister was available and asking whether their guests knew anybody. Nikki immediately pumped the brakes on that idea. She might be single, but she definitely wasn’t asking Brie to start taking applications on her behalf. The timing made the exchange even funnier considering what had happened to the sisters the previous night. Nikki and Brie had already revealed that a man repeatedly approached them during dinner at their hotel, despite security stepping in several times. Brie joked that Nikki was the one who could give the guy a chance since she’s the single twin. “That’s why she was on the dumb shit last night. She was like, ‘Go ahead. You got a chance with her.’” Nikki wanted absolutely no part of that suggestion. Being single was one thing, but that particular guy definitely wasn’t making the cut. “Ew. Try — sick. Not that one. And that’s what bothered me about her — is she immediately saw who the single twin was.” Apparently, the man had chosen to sit next to Nikki during the encounter, which made her wonder how he’d figured out which sister was single: “So he sat next to me.” Nikki also admitted that she might initially entertain someone who approaches her, but that doesn’t mean they’re getting unlimited time to make an impression. Once somebody crosses a line, she’s perfectly comfortable shutting the whole thing down. “No, that’s crazy. That’s crazy. And I should’ve been like, ‘Yeah,’ but I’m also the first one to, like, tell someone, like, ‘Bye,’ or, like, be also, like, very confrontational too. Like, I don’t care. Like, I’ll entertain, and then I’ll be like, ‘Go now.’ You know what I mean? Which is so rude. I just wanna, like, just nip it from the beginning.” So yes, Nikki is single, but Brie probably shouldn’t start running a matchmaking service just yet. Nikki’s “not for sale” response made it pretty clear that being available doesn’t mean she’s looking for just anybody. title: Bayley Makes Surprise Appearance at Big Time Wrestling’s 30th Anniversary Show
raw_title: Bayley Makes Surprise Appearance at Big Time Wrestling’s 30th Anniversary Show
summary_src: Bayley went back to where her wrestling journey started, and the moment clearly hit her harder than she expected. The WWE star returned to Big Time Wrestling for its 30th anniversary show on October 18 and ended the night fighting back tears as the crowd welcomed her home.
body: Bayley wasn’t originally there to wrestle, but she still found her way into the action. She became the impromptu special guest referee for Aaron Solo’s match against Starboy Charlie and ended up playing a pretty important role in the finish. Things got messy when Solo tried to use his championship belt against Charlie. Bayley wasn’t having any of it and stopped Solo from using the title, giving Charlie the opening he needed to turn things around. Bayley grabbed the microphone as fans started chanting “Welcome back” at her. The reaction clearly got to her, and she admitted she was trying her best not to start crying in front of everybody. “I get too emotional — I don’t wanna cry in front of you guys. Thank all of you for coming out tonight. This is a very, very special show tonight.” There was a pretty good reason the night meant so much to Bayley. Long before WWE fans knew her by that name, Big Time Wrestling was one of the places where her career first started taking shape. Bayley’s first recorded wrestling appearance came for BTW on September 19, 2008, in Newark, California. Wrestling as Davina Rose, she teamed with Shane Ballard in a losing effort against Melissa Coates and Shannon Ballard. Nearly two decades later, Bayley got to walk back into the promotion as one of WWE’s biggest names and hear the same local crowd welcome her home. She didn’t need a match of her own to make the return special, as getting emotional in the ring showed just how much coming back to BTW still meant to her. title: Mysterious Toni Storm Tapes Surface at AEW WrestleDream With Clues About Her Disappearance
raw_title: Mysterious Toni Storm Tapes Surface at AEW WrestleDream With Clues About Her Disappearance
summary_src: Toni Storm has been missing from AEW television since March, but somebody just dropped a pretty bizarre clue about her whereabouts — and it came on a cassette tape handed to a fan at WrestleDream.
body: The mystery started at AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026 , when content creator Astrid Pizarro was handed a package by someone she didn’t identify. Inside was a cassette marked “Toni Storm Tapes,” wrapped in paper stamped “confidential” with instructions to “play me.” The really interesting part? It was labeled “one out of five.” Pizarro said she was the only person in her area who received one, and she has no clue where the other four ended up. “I was handed out the tape at WrestleDream by somebody. I opened it, it just said ‘play me.’ Thankfully my dad and my brother have a cassette player, so I was able to play it today. I was the only one in my area that got it, and it says one out of five. I don’t know who the other four people are.” Pizarro eventually uploaded the audio to YouTube, revealing that Renee Paquette narrates the recording. According to the storyline, nobody has seen or heard from Storm since March 18, 2026, but a mysterious package recently arrived at AEW headquarters in Jacksonville containing five cassette tapes with no return address. And apparently, Storm had been secretly recording just about everything. “It was long rumored that Toni had a recording device inside her purse capturing every conversation, every meeting, every moment. Well, now those rumors are true. These are the Toni Storm tapes.” The first cassette, titled “Mundanities,” gives fans a look at Storm’s daily routine, and it’s exactly the kind of insanity you’d expect from the Timeless One. One recording features her delivering a morning motivational speech that sounds more like she’s preparing to ruin somebody’s day. “I am capable, strong, and ready to make the day my mistress. Today, I choose misery, conflict, and hostility in all that I do. I exude fragility, pettiness, and an unfillable void to everyone I see.” “I face the day with resentment and scorn. My mind is a mess. My heart is in shambles. And my body is barely holding it together like an overstuffed garbage bag. But damn it, I am timeless.” Another recording features Storm talking to her 12-year-old cocker spaniel, Chanty. What begins with her calling him a good boy quickly turns into an absolutely unhinged lecture about who’s in charge. “Now, you listen to me. I own you. I created you, and I can end you. You are nothing without me. You worship the ground I walk on, or I will make your life a living hell.” There’s also a recording of Storm giving wrestling students career advice, which apparently includes one very important fashion requirement. “Lesson number four, if you want to make it in this business, you’ve got to get yourself a cool hat.” Another track, titled “Cinema,” features audio from the disastrous production of Storm’s unreleased movie, “Toni, Toni, Toni.” But one detail really sticks out. raw_title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Veronica West Explains Why She Dropped Fallyn Grey Ring Name
summary_src: Veronica West is clearing up why she ditched the Fallyn Grey name after leaving WWE, and it turns out she had no interest in going back to her old identity. The former WWE EVOLVE star says she’s tired of the comparisons, tired of people getting her name wrong, and ready to do things her own ...
body: West took to Twitter on October 19 after fans kept asking why she wasn’t using Fallyn Grey anymore. She explained that Fallyn was the character she created when she first broke into wrestling, and she spent years building that identity on the independent scene. But everything changed when she signed with WWE ID and became Veronica Haven. “Fallyn Grey was who I was when I first started prowrestling. She was the blueprint I crafted, and I spent years building that name on the independent scene. It was a character and an identity I poured so much of myself into. When I signed with WWE ID, I became Veronica Haven and had to conform to what was needed of me creatively. I wasn’t able to continue using that name after I was released.” “However, I didn’t want to go back to Fallyn Grey because of the constant mispronunciations and comparisons to other wrestlers. I needed a fresh start and a name that I could truly make my own.” West also pointed out that there’s something pretty fitting about all this. Her fallen angel character has always been about losing everything and fighting to rebuild, and that’s essentially what she’s doing after her WWE departure. “My character’s backstory has always been that of losing everything and starting from nothing. Loss, uncertainty, and persistence has always been the common theme. And thanks to Fallyn, I don’t have to completely start from nothing this time. 🫀” So that’s the end of Fallyn Grey and Veronica Haven, at least for now. West has already had to reinvent herself more than once, and this time she wants to be the one calling the shots. WWE may have been one chapter of her career, but she’s making it clear that the story isn’t over just because that door closed. title: U.S. State Department Issues New Middle East Travel Warning Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: U.S. State Department Issues New Middle East Travel Warning Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: WWE just got another reason to be nervous about Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. The U.S.
body: The warning comes as WWE continues preparing for Crown Jewel on November 7, despite serious concerns about travel into Saudi Arabia. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh showed signs of resuming operations on October 18 after being shut down for more than a week following deadly attacks . However, getting everyone into the country safely remains a major question. Now the State Department’s official TravelGov account has issued a warning urging Americans in the Middle East to stay on high alert, specifically pointing to attacks by Iranian-backed Houthi forces against Saudi Arabia. The warning goes on to address the attacks that have already caused major problems for Saudi Arabia’s airports and other infrastructure. “Americans currently in the Middle East should exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment. Be aware of potential flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions.” “Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.” That’s a pretty serious concern for WWE, considering the company needs to transport its wrestlers, production crew and equipment into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. Even if some commercial flights have resumed, that doesn’t mean international travel is anywhere close to normal. The State Department also urged Americans traveling to or from the Middle East to monitor airport operations and prepare backup plans. It warned that Iran and groups supporting the country could target additional American interests overseas, including U.S. businesses and institutions. And this isn’t just a general warning with no connection to Saudi Arabia. The State Department currently has the country under a Level 3 travel advisory , telling Americans to reconsider travel because of armed conflict, terrorism and the threat of drone and missile attacks. As Ringside News previously covered , the repeated attacks on Riyadh’s airport have raised serious concerns about whether WWE can safely run Crown Jewel as scheduled. Saudi Arabia has also considered canceling additional Riyadh Season events . There’s also a major financial issue hanging over the situation. It was recently indicated that WWE’s parent company, TKO, has faced additional pressure to keep its Saudi Arabia events on schedule following public assurances from Saudi entertainment official Turki Alalshikh about Canelo Alvarez’s upcoming fight in Riyadh. WWE also has a backup venue in the United States available if Crown Jewel cannot take place in Saudi Arabia. However, no relocation has been announced, and the company is still moving forward with preparations for November 7. Like, first story was, like, how much money he had and who he was and whatever — ‘I’m a hot shot.’ And then the second one, he’s like, ‘Hey, so, you know, I spoke — was it to a scientist or something?’ And he’s like, ‘You wanna know something crazy about identical twins?’” That’s when dinner took a seriously disgusting turn. The man claimed he had an identical twin brother who had died, then started bragging about the size of his penis compared to his late brother’s. “He knows we’re identical twins. But what he said about it was like, ‘Did you know that one has a big d ** and one has a micro penis?’ He said ‘c k,’ by the way. He told you that. He said, ‘Big ‘c k.’ He goes, ‘So I am the one with the big ‘c**k.’”* “So then he was like, ‘Who do you think has the micro c ** and the big c***?’ And I was like, ‘This is when he needs to go — kicked out.’”* Security escorted the man away, but he STILL wasn’t finished. He eventually returned with another story, this time claiming he was a cancer survivor and inviting the sisters to a cancer event. And when that failed to impress them, he apparently figured a stack of cash might do the trick. “And then he’s, ‘You guys wanna go to a cancer event with me?’ And we’re like — the security guy’s like, ‘Leave them alone, boy.’ And then he went like this — he’s sitting and he pulls out a bunch of cash and he’s got tons of hundreds, trying to show us, flash us. And I’m like… corny, corny, corny.” But the most disturbing part of the encounter didn’t come until later. According to the sisters, they found out the man had allegedly been trying to make his way upstairs to their hotel room. “He was nuts. The sisters were eating at the same hotel where they were staying, and once their guests realized that, one immediately warned them not to do it again because it was dangerous. Nikki also said the man’s behavior reminded her of American Psycho , comparing his unsettling demeanor to a serial killer. “You had to see how he did it too. summary_src: Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo suffered a nasty injury at a WWE NXT live event, but there’s finally some encouraging news after the wrestler was stretchered out of the arena and taken to the hospital.
body: The scary incident happened during the October 16 NXT house show in Sudbury, Ontario, where Stacks teamed with Charlie Dempsey, Lexis King and Uriah Connors against Tony D’Angelo, Tavion Heights, Shiloh Hill and Shawn Spears. Things went wrong when Stacks took a back body drop over the top rope and crashed onto the floor, forcing WWE to stop the match . Medical personnel rushed to check on Lorenzo before placing him on a stretcher and taking him out of the arena. Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer later confirmed that Stacks had been transported to a nearby hospital , while Dave Meltzer noted that there were concerns he may have suffered a concussion. “Thank you for coming out tonight. Unfortunately things happen in this ring that are unexpected. You’ve heard us say 1000 times we’re one big family in WWE. You all are included and are a part of our family. When something serious such as this takes place it’s not easy. I’m sorry we had to end the night like this. From the bottom of my heart, thank you all for coming out tonight.” “My boys alive and well!! We can’t be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his ass.” Stacks’ injury turned what was supposed to be another routine NXT live event into a frightening situation, but at least fans have gotten some encouraging news since he was taken to the hospital. Whether he needs additional recovery time remains to be seen, and WWE will have to wait until he’s medically cleared before bringing him back into action. title: Paige Collett Drops Steamy Photos to Celebrate 56 Days Without Sugar
raw_title: Paige Collett Drops Steamy Photos to Celebrate 56 Days Without Sugar
summary_src: Paige Collett is showing off a little skin for a cause, and the JCW wrestler has a pretty good reason to celebrate. She’s officially gone 56 days without sugar, and she’s using some revealing new photos to bring attention to her ongoing battle with chronic illness.
body: On October 19, Collett took to Twitter and shared two provocative photos of herself posing in black lace underwear, including one in black and white. But this wasn’t just about getting attention. She used the post to celebrate her progress with cutting sugar from her diet while spreading awareness about Complex Regional Pain Syndrome, or CRPS. The photos come just one day after Collett fired back at people judging her for smoking medical marijuana . She explained that cannabis has played a major role in helping her manage chronic pain and continue pursuing her wrestling career, despite strangers assuming she’s simply out partying. “People see me smoking and judge me & typecast me! I’m a strong advocate for medical marijuana. It has saved my life and it lets me continue to pursue my wrestling dream.” Collett’s health struggles have been anything but easy. As Ringside News previously covered , she says a wrestling bump during training under WWE Hall of Famer Rikishi triggered the condition, eventually leaving her dependent on a wheelchair. She spent years searching for answers before fighting her way back to walking and wrestling. She’s also opened up about how CRPS affects her personal life , explaining that even physical intimacy can leave her dealing with days of pain and recovery. Now Collett is trying another approach to managing her health, and she’s clearly proud of sticking with it for 56 days. Whether cutting sugar will continue helping her symptoms remains to be seen, but she’s using the milestone to get people talking about CRPS while giving her followers something else to look at. Collett has already spent years fighting to get her life and wrestling career back, so she’s not taking the small victories for granted. And if posting a few steamy photos gets more eyes on a condition she’s been battling for years, she apparently has no problem putting that attention to good use. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Admits Going Off Script on WWE TV Has Gotten Him in Trouble With Triple H
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Admits Going Off Script on WWE TV Has Gotten Him in Trouble With Triple H
summary_src: Drew McIntyre isn’t afraid to throw WWE’s creative plans out the window when he thinks something isn’t working — even if it means getting an earful from Triple H backstage.
body: McIntyre explained that WWE’s creative team works closely with talent to develop storylines, with Triple H overseeing the overall direction. However, he believes wrestlers who understand their characters should have a major say in how those stories are told. “These days, it’s very much a collaboration and has been for a few years now with myself personally anyway and generally across the board. If you know your character, you can work with the writers, etc., and get the character into the story. But it’s very important to me to make sure the creative matches what I’ve got going on in my head. Like the writers, the creative team, Triple H leading the creative team, they kind of set out, here’s the story, here’s what we’re thinking, here’s who we’re thinking you’re going to work with and this is where we’d like to get to.” Drew said that while WWE might have a destination in mind, the process of getting there is something he helps shape every week. He also made it clear that nobody needs to tell him what Drew McIntyre would say because, well, he’s Drew McIntyre. “Then it goes week to week. Like how we get there, that’s kind of a collaboration. Like when I go out there and I’ve got an interview in the microphone, I’m not getting handed a piece of paper that says here’s what you’re saying. Here’s all the words you’re saying because that’s what Drew McIntyre would say. Because my response, which I’ve said in real life, is no, you wouldn’t. What do you mean? I’m Drew McIntyre. I know what I would say.” McIntyre explained that he’ll go back and forth with WWE’s writers to make sure everything sounds believable. If he doesn’t believe what he’s saying, he doesn’t expect the audience to buy it either. “So, we have to go back and forth about what we want in the paper, where we’re going next, and make sure it’s in line with what’s in my head. Because if I don’t believe it, sure as hell, the fans are not going to believe it. They can see in your eyes, even if they don’t know or they can’t articulate it subconsciously, they’re like, you feel it. I don’t believe this and I have to believe it. So, they believe it. So, we very much work together every step of the way to create, you know, the storylines of where we’re going and make sure we’re getting the right emotional reaction.” But here’s where things get interesting. McIntyre admitted that even after WWE’s creative team agrees on a plan, he sometimes changes everything in front of the live audience. Depending on how Triple H feels about those decisions, Drew either gets congratulated backstage or finds himself in trouble. “Then on top of that, you’re in front of a live crowd. Sometimes they don’t react to the stuff on the paper and I’m very much the big ad-libber and sometimes it gets me a big slap on the wrist when I get to the back or a high five like good move out there.” And apparently, dealing with an angry Triple H isn’t exactly a pleasant experience. summary_src: Drew McIntyre has absolutely no problem running his mouth about CM Punk, but now he’s taking things a step further. The former WWE Champion says that if their issues ever turned into a real fight, Punk wouldn’t stand a chance — and he even used Punk’s UFC career to make his point.
body: McIntyre claimed he actively avoids Punk backstage and doesn’t particularly enjoy being around him. However, he acknowledged that both men understand how to put their personal feelings aside when it’s time to work together. That’s when he took a pretty wild shot at what would happen if they ever stopped being professional. “But also, we have to be professional and not pan each other’s heads. When I say we pan each other’s heads, I would murder him. You see him in UFC? Would look like that if it got real in there.” “Oh, for real life? I don’t care how many jiu-jitsu guys that tell me like, ‘Yeah, I’m MMA bros.’ Did you fight for the UFC? No, shut up. I said, ‘I will crush you. I’m giant and Scottish and many fights happen.'” McIntyre then joked about how people approach professional wrestlers and ask whether they would use wrestling moves in an actual fight. He made it clear that wouldn’t be his approach. “Guys are like, ‘Hey man, I’m going to — you’re going to chokeslam me? You got a tombstone?’ I was like, ‘No, I’m going to punch [you].’ I say the C word with a thick Scottish accent. Oh, Jesus. He’s a psycho. Yeah, I am. Don’t push me.” Of course, this isn’t the first time McIntyre has made his feelings about Punk known. As Ringside News previously covered, Drew admitted that his issues with Punk were personal , explaining that their genuine frustrations helped make their 2024 rivalry work so well. summary_src: Drew McIntyre may have been away from WWE television for months, but don’t expect him to come crawling back begging for another opportunity.

He’s gotten bigger, leaner and more flexible, and at 41 years old, he believes he’s moving better than he has in years. “But it’s been the opposite. I’ve gotten bigger. I’ve gotten leaner. I’ve gotten more flexible. And I feel in the best shape of my life, which is bizarre.” When asked how much longer he plans to wrestle, Drew said he doesn’t see himself slowing down anytime soon. He admitted there were periods when the wear and tear of his career started catching up with him, but those days appear to be behind him. “As long as I enjoy it, I guess. As long as the fans are enjoying what I do. I can’t imagine slowing down. Like I say, I’ve never felt as physically good. There’s times where I felt really beat up like a couple of years ago and I was like, ‘Wow, I’m feeling my age and feeling like how long I’ve been wrestling,’ and now I just feel unbelievable.” McIntyre also revealed that he’s been getting back inside the ring without an audience just to work on his speed and conditioning. He pointed to a recent social media video of himself running the ropes that generated more than 10 million views across his platforms. According to Drew, even his trainer was surprised by how much his movement had improved compared to his last stretch in WWE. “And my trainer was there and he’s been watching me and coming to shows the past year, year plus. And he’s like, ‘The way you’re moving in the ring.’ I was wrestling barefoot as well, rolling around all over the place. He was like, ‘You were not moving like this before. Like, I don’t know what you moved like when you were younger, but you were not moving like this when you were last wrestling.'” Naturally, all that preparation raises the question of when McIntyre will actually return to WWE. Unfortunately for fans looking for a specific date, Drew wasn’t interested in giving one away. Instead, he teased that his return could happen sooner or later, while making it clear that Hollywood remains his immediate focus. “So, I can’t wait till people can see, you know, how I am in the ring, how I’m moving now. And, you know, maybe I’ll be back soon. Maybe I’ll be back later, but for now, we’re focused on Hollywood Drew.” But Drew wasn’t finished. He immediately followed that up with a warning about what WWE fans can expect when he finally comes back. title: Drew McIntyre Mocks CM Punk’s Body Transformation With Brutal Physique Insult
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Mocks CM Punk’s Body Transformation With Brutal Physique Insult
summary_src: Drew McIntyre just can’t help himself when it comes to CM Punk. Even when the Scottish Warrior tries to give his longtime rival a compliment, he somehow finds a way to turn it into an insult — and this time, Punk’s physique was the target.
body: That’s when CM Punk’s name came up. McIntyre admitted he’s genuinely surprised Punk is still wrestling at 48 years old and even acknowledged that his rival has improved his physical condition. For a brief moment, it almost sounded like Drew was going to say something nice about Punk. That didn’t last long. “I’ve still got a few more years in the wrestling first and like you know I’m amazed Punk’s still going. There’s one thing I can compliment him on. He’s 48. He’s still going. And he got himself in better shape.” McIntyre immediately made sure nobody confused that compliment with actual praise. He clarified that Punk was only in better shape compared to how he looked previously, before delivering a pretty nasty assessment of his rival’s physique. “I mean, better shape for him. Let’s not go crazy now. He doesn’t look like me. He’s just better shape for him. So skinny, so fat at the same time. Before now, he just got in all right shape.” But Drew wasn’t finished. He then mocked fans who have praised Punk’s body transformation, suggesting people are getting carried away with how much his rival has improved. “Everyone’s like, ‘Have you seen the changes? He looks so good.’ I’m like, remember, we’re WWE. Like he’s not walking to Mr. Olympia. He’s like if he walks on to Mr. Bloody Chicago, the local area that he lives in stage, never mind Mr. Olympia.” “Yeah, I hear that a lot. It’s just not intentionally funny. I just tell the truth.” So while Punk has been getting attention for improving his physique, McIntyre apparently thinks the comparisons should stop right there. Drew might be willing to admit Punk looks better than he used to, but he clearly isn’t about to put his rival in the same category as himself. Their WWE rivalry may have ended inside Hell in a Cell, but McIntyre is still taking every opportunity to get one more shot in — even if it’s about Punk’s body. title: Andrade Recalls Origin Of His Pants-Off Routine In AEW
raw_title: Andrade El Idolo Didn't Realize Fans Were Chanting For Him To Take His Pants Off At First
summary_src: Andrade El Idolo has become one of the most popular stars in AEW, and it all started when he began to take his pants off. Andrade removing his bottoms has become commonplace in AEW, but even he was confused by the chant at first. Speaking to Renee Paquette on Close Up, Andrade gave the origin…
body: Andrade El Idolo has become one of the most popular stars in AEW, and it all started when he began to take his pants off. Andrade removing his bottoms has become commonplace in AEW, but even he was confused by the chant at first. Speaking to Renee Paquette on Close Up , Andrade gave the origin story of taking his pants off. “I love wrestling and I respect the ring. In the ring, I like to show who I am. I know I’m a good wrestler. One moment, I was beating some wrestler, and the people started saying something, but I didn’t understand it. I asked the ref, ‘What are the people saying?’ ‘The people are saying to take your pants off.’ ‘What?’ It was weird because it’s usually ‘Tables! This is awesome!’ But people saying ‘take your pants,’ I don’t understand. I’m in there, I’m beating him, I’m heel. ‘Maybe they want more punches,’ but they continued (to chant for me to take my pants off). I go over to ref Aubrey, ‘What did they finally say?’ ‘Take your pants off.’ ‘What? No.’ ‘Yeah, they want your pants off.’ Okay, you want the pants off. I take my belt off, my zipper down, and the people go crazy. Okay, I’ll take my pants off. I always have trunks to cover me because something can happen with the pants; they can rip. This is why I always wear trunks, not because I was prepared. One time I didn’t have trunks; I had boxers. People started that chant, so I took my pants off, and people [cheers]. ‘I am the heel.’ The people chant, ‘Take your pants off,’ So, I took my pants off,” he recalled. Andrade successfully defended the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream. He initially did not understand the crowd's reaction and had to ask the referee what they were saying. Once he realized the chant, Andrade obliged by taking off his belt and unzipping, which has since become a regular part of his act and helped boost his popularity in AEW.

During an interview, Andrade explained that he respects the wrestling ring and aims to show his true self inside it. While facing an opponent as a heel, he heard the audience chanting but could not make out the words.

He asked the referee what the crowd was saying and learned they were chanting for him to take his pants off. This confused him because he expected typical wrestling chants such as tables or this is awesome.
Andrade then approached referee Aubrey to confirm the chant. Once he understood the request, he removed his belt and unzipped his pants, which caused the audience to react strongly.
He always wears trunks underneath to avoid any wardrobe issues if the pants tear. On one occasion when he wore boxers instead, the crowd still chanted for him to remove his pants, and he complied.
Andrade successfully defended the AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream.

title: Results Recap: WWE SmackDown , grades (Sept. 4): CM Punk retains; is Johnny Gargano leaving WWE?
raw_title: WWE SmackDown results, grades (Sept. 4): CM Punk retains; is Johnny Gargano leaving WWE?
body: OK, some ranting needs to be done off the top here because WWE has created an insane mess in its world title scene, and the overbooking is atrocious. With Sami Zayn, Gunther, Kevin Owens and Finn Balor all emerging to play a part in the finish of tonight's match, that's how we got to Gargano taking the loss. On a positive note, I like what's being created here with Punk continuously defending his title with interference or shenanigans. That can lead to something good, whether for a heel turn or in his immediate future feuds. Will it? I don't have faith, but the potential is there. The absolute worst part of all this is that Zayn is getting a handout title shot next week despite ruining both the most recent title match and No. 1 contender match. You know, the exact same booking that led to his title win against Cody Rhodes and Gunther in June — the last time Zayn won a match . Booking doesn't get any lazier than this. How are we supposed to care? And why should we, when Zayn has immediate enemies in Gunther, Owens and Balor who will surely ruin his match? Or at least, they should . WWE has created a scenario where the Punk vs. Zayn rematch would be booked improperly if none of those three plays a role in the finish. That's where we're at. I like that all three went after Zayn to start the night, but that has to continue if there's even a shred of logic or continuity to be had anywhere here. The easy solution for WWE to make it clear before next week's match that suspensions or some kind of punishment would be dealt in the case of interference. That doesn't make Zayn's title shot any more excusable, but it's a fix for the rest of the issues around this. Anyway, as for the Gargano match itself, it was very good. What would you expect out of a pairing between him and Punk in Gargano's hometown of Cleveland? Johnny Wrestling's literal rise to his feet was overdue and arguably should've happened when Zayn briefly held gold. But this was a nice spot for it. In the end, we may have seen the last of the former NXT staple in WWE, as he addressed the crowd in what felt like a goodbye after the show went off the air. It's amazing what Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes can do without a completely random celebrity interjection, isn't it? (No. No, it's not at all. It's what we knew these two were capable of — and should have delivered — ahead of the biggest event of the year.) At least we're getting it at all, but this feud simply can't end on Sunday in Atlanta. It's too good. Running joke. What's going on with Blake Monroe has become a literal joke. Two weeks in a row, she and Giulia fight — while geared up this time — only not to wrestle. At least they're getting some airtime, I guess. But this is just silly now. Celebrity Night's Main Event. Lil Yachty made a music video for his Baron Corbin match this weekend. I would ask who this is for, but the answer is obviously the TKO overlords. Poor Trick Williams is being kept from audiences for this. (Please don't) fight

title: Cody Rhodes Picks Favorite Dusty Promo, Bans AI Voice
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Names His Favorite Dusty Rhodes Promo, Vows ‘No AI Dusty’ In WWE
body: Cody Rhodes recently named his favorite Dusty Rhodes promo and said that there will never be an AI Dusty Rhodes voice in WWE. Dusty Rhodes is one of the most influential promo guy in wrestling history and has a number of famous, top-tier promos. His most famous is the “Hard Times” promo, which has crossed into mainstream culture and was recently used in a Zach Bryan song. Rhodes spoke on Last Mean about his father’s promos and why “Hard Times” isn’t in fact his favorite. He also said that there is a rule in WWE: no Dusty Rhodes AI voice. You can see the highlights below: “Well, he loved Billy Graham. Not the wrestler Billy Graham. Pastor Billy Graham. He loved Martin Luther King Jr. He grew up in the Southern Baptist church. The church he went to majority was all Black. And Thunderbolt Patterson, a famous, famous wrestler who — later in life, I think they’ve seen how great he was and what a [trendsetter] — Dad stole a great deal from Thunderbolt, stole a great deal from Bob Dylan. Michael Hayes is very similar. They’d find these things that they liked and weave them into the promo.” “I can tell you that a lot of people always want to quote ‘Hard Times.’ And I just — ‘Hard Times’ to me was cool, but I’d actually seen it before. Because he cut a similar one on Oie Anderson in the Georgia Championship Wrestling situation pre — again, they were playing without cable at the time. And then when cable becomes a thing, and when these things start to last forever — like our Last Meal here, this lasts forever. This lasts forever. No pressure, right? They were doing stuff that didn’t last forever, so they could get away with rehashing, revisiting. “But my favorite promo he ever did was with my brother Dustin. ‘The view never changes,’ talking about neglecting Dustin and wanting to be his partner. And I like that because our family, for better or for worse, probably — who knows? Our family has lived out in front of them. As much as it’s a performance in WWE is however you want to look at it, the character Cody Rhodes is pretty real. You know, I think the main difference is Runnels and Rhodes, you know? Like there’s not [much difference]. And to be able to do that promo with my brother and share that moment was kind of the only way he could apologize and tell him he loved him. So, that one stands out to me a lot.” “So much of his promo work was really, really special. And I’m going to go ahead and get on a high horse here about the old man and his promos. This is going to get me in trouble, but let’s do it… If you’re going to teach people how to do an interview in modern wrestling, you have to have done one yourself. And I am so grateful that he was the promo coach there at NXT near the end, because his legacy goes on. “The last chapter continues, right? Like, so many wrestlers don’t get a good proper last chapter. I wish Hulk Hogan had more a proper last chapter. They don’t get that last chapter where they give back. And he had a great last chapter.
