body: October 19 2003 was the date of WWE No Mercy that year, and the main event was Brock Lesnar vs The Undertaker in a Biker Chain WWE Championship match. Our own Dave Meltzer would describe it as a match that “dragged,” with one of the bigger being that the chain gimmick didn’t even really come into play until nearer the end. Here is what Dave had to say about Brock Lesnar vs The Undertaker at WWE No Mercy 2003: “Lesnar power bombed his way out of a triangle. Lesnar hit an F-5, but Undertaker got his foot on the ropes. Lesnar went to the top, but Undertaker choke slammed him off the top. Undertaker finally went for the chain, but Nunzio climbed up to stop him. Nunzio managed to get the chain and take a bump to the floor. At this point, Chuck Palumbo and Johnny Stamboli hit the ring, but Undertaker laid them out and cleaned house on them fast. Undertaker gave Lesnar the last ride, and then did pretty spectacular running dive over the top onto Palumbo & Stamboli. Undertaker came into the ring and got the chain, but Vince came out and shoved Undertaker, who crotched himself on the ropes. title: Drew McIntyre Calls Out WWE Wrestlers Who Can’t Improvise During Matches
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Calls Out WWE Wrestlers Who Can’t Improvise During Matches
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has a problem with wrestlers who need every second of their matches planned out — and he’s not keeping quiet about it.
body: McIntyre believes experienced wrestlers should already know how to work a match without needing every move planned in advance. He explained that the live crowd should dictate how a match unfolds, not some predetermined sequence that might have worked in another city. “Unless it’s a stunt practice stunts, but when it comes to the matches like you should know what you’re doing. We could talk about it a bit. You got 10 minutes, you got 15 minutes, you got 20 minutes. Go out there and listen to the crowd wrestle. Like I can’t stand when people plan stuff from beginning to end because you don’t know how the crowd’s going to react.” Drew then explained why that approach drives him crazy. Just because something worked in one city doesn’t mean another audience will react the same way, and wrestlers who refuse to adjust are setting themselves up for a disaster. “If you plan out this choreographed match, you walk out there and the crowd are just sitting on their hands. They’re like, ‘Huh?’ But they liked it in Chicago last week. You’re not Chicago. Different crowds like different things.” Things got even more interesting when the host asked what happens when wrestlers don’t get the reaction they expected. According to McIntyre, that’s where some talent expose themselves because they haven’t learned how to improvise. Drew said he’s experienced situations where he tries to change direction in the middle of a match, only for the other wrestler to freeze because they weren’t prepared for anything outside the original plan. “Yeah. I mean, they’ve not learned how to improvise in the moment. And sometimes, like, a lot of people are good at listening, but some people panic and it’s not fun if you’re in live TV and somebody panics and you’re talking to them like, ‘Hey, this ain’t working. We’re going to go this direction now.’ And they kind of freeze up and that’s when things look choppy.” “Not choppy in the good way. I like if it looks kind of makes it look real. If it’s kind of choppy and you get really physical with each other, but if things start messing up in an obvious way, it is not good. If there’s a miscommunication or somebody trying to tell the other person, let’s go this direction and they’re not quite ready.” But Drew also pointed to a bigger issue within WWE. The company doesn’t run nearly as many non-televised live events as it used to, which means younger wrestlers have fewer opportunities to practice their craft in front of actual audiences. “And I mean, things are different now. We don’t have as many non-televised shows now as we used to where people kind of practice game. And there is more now. People are getting their reps in. Um, and the talent are finding their feet, especially the younger talent.” That issue is something WWE management has already been addressing. As Ringside News previously covered, Triple H and Nick Khan explained why WWE was bringing back more house shows , with younger wrestlers needing additional in-ring experience being
summary: McIntyre believes experienced wrestlers should already know how to work a match without needing every move planned in advance. Just because something worked in one city doesn’t mean another audience will react the same way.

title: Solo Sikoa parties with rival Carmelo Hayes at wedding
raw_title: WWE’s Solo Sikoa breaks character as life of party at Carmelo Hayes’ wedding
body: While they are on-screen rivals, WWE star Solo Sikoa was going hard at Carmelo Hayes and Kelani Jordan's wedding over the weekend. A video from the reception has gone viral from the reception. Hayes appears to have his arm around him as they're dancing in the middle of a circle. The Bloodline member appeared to be the life of the party. Of course, this is iconic, considering that Sikoa and Hayes' last interaction in WWE programming was violent. During the Oct. 12, 2026, edition of Monday Night RAW, Hayes joined Royce Keys' 946 faction, attacking Bloodline members Sikoa, Jey Uso, and Jimmy Uso. Hayes and Jordan tied the knot on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. They got engaged on Tuesday, July 1, 2025, before getting married the following October. They are both two of WWE's top rising stars. Hayes just joined 946, and he is a former United States Champion. During his time in NXT, he won the North American Championship and was the final Cruiserweight Champion. Additionally, he won the NXT Championship in April 2023 at Stand & Deliver, beating Bron Breakker to win the title. Hayes held the title for 182 days before losing it to Ilja Dragunov. His wife, meanwhile, joined WWE a year after him in 2022. She made her NXT debut in October 2022 before making her on-screen debut in June 2023 at Gold Rush. She became the inaugural Women's North American Champion in a six-woman ladder match at NXT Battleground in June 2024. She beat Kendal Grey at Heatwave on Aug. 30 to win the NXT Women's Championship for the first time. She has also worked in Total Nonstop Action (TNA), winning the Knockouts World Championship in September 2025, before losing it to Léi Yǐng Lee. While she hasn't made her main roster debut yet, Jordan competed in the 2026 Royal Rumble.

body: AEW WrestleDream took an unexpected turn as mysterious cassette tapes attributed to Toni Storm surfaced at the pay-per-view, offering a bizarre and unsettling glimpse into the former AEW Women’s World Champion’s world. Paquette proceeded to highlight each track with the next one being about Storm’s 12-year-old cocker spaniel, Chanty. “Oh, Chanty. That’s a good boy, Chanty. Who’s a good Chanty? Take a chance. Take a chance, Chanty. Oh, what a beautiful boy. Now, you listen to me. I own you. I created you, and I can end you. You are nothing without me. You worship the ground I walk on, or I will make your life a living hell. When company comes over, they’re here to see me, not you.It’s not a time for your little tricks or performances. It’s not amateur hour with Chantsy. It’s my time. You will greet them. You will wait till I make one witty remark, and then Luther will escort you down to the basement to eat your rubbish. Otherwise, you have one job and one job only. To f*ck. You are a hunting machine and I want you to scour this damn neighborhood making onto anything that moves because mama is in the mood to sell and I can make a pretty good penny off of whatever half freak hamster you manage to knock up. Call it something exotic like a ham dog. You hear me? You worthless wanted beast. Okay, Chanty, let’s go for a walk.” The tape features a couple more tracks titled ‘Seminar’, where Storm shares her wisdom with wrestling students. “Lesson number four, if you want to make it in this business, you’ve got to get yourself a cool hat.” Paquette introduced Track 4, titled “Cinema,” describing it as “chronicling the failed production of her self-funded, unreleased major motion picture.” The final track was labelled “Death,” with Paquette concluding the recording by stating, “These are the Toni Storm Tapes.” Storm’s last AEW appearance was on March 18 when she was found bloodied on the floor backstage . body: WWE has more than six months left to prepare storylines for its biggest event of 2027. Ripley has been posting updates on her recovery on social media. She has started weight training, but she hasn’t shared any in-ring activities. body: Kyle Fletcher shares that he tries to watch every single matches he participates in back to take feedback and apply it to himself. Fletcher has been one of the top rising talents in AEW over the past couple of years, and has developed into one of the top in ring competitors not only in AEW but in the world of pro wrestling. Now, he has shared a part of his development that helps him improve as a pro wrestler after every match. While speaking to Westwood One Sports Night in a new interview , Kyle Fletcher was asked if he watches his matches back, with the Australian wrestler noting that he does in order to take feedback and apply it to himself for the future. “Yeah. I try and watch every single match of mine back. I think it’s the- I think it’s a very important part of the feedback loop, being able to watch myself objectively removed from it and look at it as a finished product and be able to take that feedback and apply it to myself.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Kyle Fletcher revealed that he makes a point to review every one of his matches afterward. title: WWE Should Break Up Judgment Day Now
raw_title: Why Now is The Time For WWE to End The Judgment Day Faction Once and For All
body: A case can even be made that the mere existence of the faction is doing more to hinder than help everyone still in it. That's a strange statement to make when two of the members currently hold gold and the group gets more screen time than almost anyone on Raw most weeks, but that's exactly why it's time for WWE to call it quits with them. They're overexposed, uninteresting and stuck in the same stories. Liv Morgan and Stephanie Vaquer have been at odds over the Women's World Championship since February, Dominik Mysterio has been feuding with his father Rey Mysterio on and off for four years, and the rest of Judgment Day are treading water. Raw could use a significant shakeup in the worst way, and breaking up Judgment Day once and for all could be what benefits both the brand and everyone associated with the stable. The incarnation of the stable with Ripley, Damian Priest, Dominik Mysterio, Finn Bálor and JD McDonagh was peak Judgment Day, but it had also run its course. Ripley and Priest had already begun to embrace the audience as babyfaces, so removing them from their ranks gave the group a fresh coat of paint. It also put Morgan in a prominent position on Raw for the first time in her career, a spot she has shined in ever since. Her stock skyrocketed, and within a matter of months, she was one of the most popular performers—male or female—in the entire company. As such, it made sense for her to win the Women's World Championship at WrestleMania 42. Unfortunately, the fallout left a lot to be desired, and she went until SummerSlam four months later without defending her title. Stephanie Vaquer regaining the gold in her native Chile was a fun moment, but all it ended up being was just that: a moment. She won back the belt at Money in the Bank not long after, and currently, there aren't any obvious challengers waiting in the wings. She's stuck doing the same shtick and being bogged down by Judgment Day isn't doing her or the title any favors. That would have allowed Perez to subtly tease tension with Morgan and plant the seeds for an eventual (successful) cash-in on her. Perez and Morgan weren't exactly on the same page in the wake of WrestleMania 42, but their dissension was quickly forgotten about and never acknowledged again. Perez was the perfect addition to Judgment Day in 2025. She had just been called up to the main roster from NXT and the group served as a vehicle to introduce her to the audience in an organic way, not to mention she instantly had chemistry with everyone already in the faction. Morgan vs. Perez being the ultimate endgame is acceptable, but it shouldn't be taking this long to get there. The Bloodline have obviously been a focal point of the flagship show this year, along with The 946 as part of their ongoing rivalry with the Roman Reigns-led group. The Vision, for some reason, still have a presence on the program as well and remain relevant largely thanks to Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed. That has automatically made The J
summary: The long-running Judgment Day faction has become overexposed and repetitive on Raw. Members remain stuck in the same stale storylines, including Liv Morgan and Stephanie Vaquer's ongoing feud over the Women's World Championship and Dominik Mysterio's years-long issues with Rey Mysterio. Breaking up the group could provide a much-needed shakeup for the brand and fresh opportunities for everyone involved.

llm.headline: This Day in Wrestling History: October 19
llm.summary: On October 19, multiple title changes took place across several promotions including Fred Blassie winning the NWA Southern Heavyweight Title, Johnny Valentine capturing the NWF World Heavyweight Title, Bobby Shane taking the NWA Florida Television Title, Carlos Colon regaining the WWC Universal Heavyweight Title, and Hector Guerrero & Dr. D claiming the AWA World Tag Team Titles. The date also marks the passing of Mike Graham, the on-screen Vince McMahon versus Stephanie McMahon match, Kurt Angle's induction into the TNA Hall of Fame, and the debut of Celebrity Championship Wrestling. Keiji Mutoh & Masahiro Chono defeated Kensuke Sasaki & Kazuo Yamazaki to win the IWGP Tag Team Titles.

llm_long: On October 19 in wrestling history, several title changes took place across various promotions. Fred Blassie defeated Wild Bull Curry to capture the NWA Southern Heavyweight Title for the fourth time in 1956.

In 1972, Johnny Valentine beat Abdullah The Butcher to win the National Wrestling Federation World Heavyweight Title in Cleveland, Ohio. On the same date that year, Bobby Shane defeated Tim Woods in Tampa, Florida, to claim the NWA Florida Television Title for the second time.

Carlos Colon defeated Abdullah The Butcher in San Juan, Puerto Rico, in 1985 to win the WWC Universal Heavyweight Title for the fourth time after the belt had been held up from a prior match between them. In 1987, Hector Guerrero and Dr. D defeated Jerry Lawler and Bill Dundee to take the AWA World Tag Team Title in Memphis, Tennessee.

Keiji Mutoh and Masahiro Chono defeated Kensuke Sasaki and Kazuo Yamazaki to win the IWGP Tag Team Title in Kobe, Japan, in 1997. That same day, Atsushi Onita and Kintaro Kanemura beat Hisakatsu Oya and Mr. Gannosuke for the FMW World Brass Knuckles Tag Team Title in Sendai, Japan.

In 2001, Vader and 2 Cold Scorpio became the inaugural Pro Wrestling Noah Global Honored Crown Tag Team Champions by defeating Jun Akiyama and Akitoshi Saito in a tournament final in Yokohama, Japan. On the same card, Tatsuhito Takaiwa defeated Yoshinobu Kanemaru to win the Pro Wrestling Noah Global Honored Crown Junior Heavyweight Title.

Also in 2001, Road Dogg defeated Jeff Jarrett to become the first World Wrestling All-Stars World Heavyweight Champion in Perth, Australia. Black Warrior defeated Negro Casas to win CMLL's Legend Of The Silver Mask tournament that year as well.

title: Billy Gunn Calls Triple H's 2019 AEW Jab A Dick Move
raw_title: Billy Gunn Says Triple H's Shot At AEW At 2019 WWE Hall Of Fame Was 'A Dick Move' That Only Hurt Him
summary_src: D-Generation X was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2019, with Triple H, Road Dogg, Sean Waltman, Billy Gunn, Shawn Michaels, and Chyna all going into the Hall. Gunn was already working for AEW at the time of their induction, though AEW had yet to run a show when the ceremony took place.…
body: D-Generation X was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2019, with Triple H, Road Dogg, Sean Waltman, Billy Gunn, Shawn Michaels, and Chyna all going into the Hall. During the ceremony, fans chanted “AEW” while Gunn and DX were on stage. Triple H responded that Vince McMahon would buy that “pissant company” just to fire Gunn again. Speaking to Kenny McIntosh on Inside The Ropes , Gunn reflected on the incident, saying, “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool. I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go. The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. They like to stir up shit. When you have somebody in another company, which was me, they can’t believe it, and then you see me, they have to do it. It’s like an unwritten thing in a book. ‘If another guy is in another company, we have to say or do something.’ They started chanting it, and you get a response from the guy leading the company.” Vince McMahon has not purchased AEW and is no longer involved with WWE after a lawsuit was filed against him by former employee Janel Grant, who accused Vince of sexual assault and sex trafficking. Triple H responded to the chants by saying Vince McMahon would buy that company just to fire Gunn again. Billy Gunn later reflected on the moment in an interview. He stated that he expected some form of AEW reference because the company was popular at the time and he had joined it.

Gunn explained that Tony Khan allowed him to attend the Hall of Fame ceremony without issue. He noted that he anticipated a reaction from Triple H once the chants began. Gunn added that he prepared himself mentally for whatever comment might come.

body: Kyle Fletcher doesn’t think that his current character is too far off what he imagined it would be as a kid dreaming of being a wrestler. Fletcher is one of the top wrestlers under the age of 30 in the world of professional wrestling, and continues to grow as a performer in All Elite Wrestling. Now, he has spoken about his current character. While speaking to Westwood One Sports Night in a new interview, Kyle Fletcher was asked if his wrestling character is what he imagined it would be as a kid. “That’s actually a very interesting question. I don’t think it’s too far… off what I pictured when I was a kid, just because, I think the person that I am, and I think about this quite a lot, I think the person that I am today, not just in wrestling, but in general, is an accumulation of all the things that I loved as a kid growing up, an accumulation of- I looked at just people and wrestlers in whatever I loved, tattoos. I loved collecting Pokemon cards. I loved, music. I loved wrestling and I look at myself and I go, ‘oh, that’s pretty much everything that I am.’ I loved dressing nice. I loved pink, and it’s like, everything is, everything makes sense. You know, I’m just the same, the same person, just a larger version, I guess. So yeah, I can’t say it’s too far away from what I pictured because if you gave 10-year-old Kyle SmackDown vs. Raw 2009 or whatever, I’d probably create exactly what you see in front of me in Create-A-Wrestler.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

llm_long: Adriana Rizzo is currently waiting out the remainder of her 30-day non-compete period following her release from WWE before exploring future in-ring options. The former NXT talent stated that she has not yet begun looking into possibilities and will start considering what is available once the window closes. Rizzo added that she is simply waiting until those 30 days are up right now.

Rizzo signed with NXT in 2022. She made her television debut nearly a year later as part of the D’Angelo Family stable led by Tony D’Angelo. She was among the NXT roster members released by WWE in early September. During an interview with Pario Magazine, Rizzo explained her current stance on returning to wrestling. She noted she remains within the 30-day period so has not taken any steps yet. Rizzo said she will begin looking into options and see what is out there after the non-compete expires.
Rizzo last appeared for NXT at a live event on August 21 where she lost a singles match to PJ Vasa. Her release came as part of broader cuts to the developmental brand’s roster.

body: October 18, 2026 By Laurence Gibbons Raw , Pro Wrestling , WWE , WWE Universe WWE Raw streams live on Netflix globally from the Pechanga Arena in San Diego, CA. Enjoy our WWE Raw preview before the show at 8/7c. The Pechanga Arena was the setting for WWE Vengeance in 2001 , where the WWF and WCW World Championships were unified. Roman Reigns will return to WWE Raw following a week promoting the new Street Fighter movie. It seems a shame that Cody Rhodes isn’t WWE Champion, as he is also in the Street Fighter movie. A WWE Crown Jewel showdown between Reigns and Rhodes, whilst the two are seen on the big screen playing Akuma and Guile, seems a missed cross-promotional dream match. Reigns will instead face Sami Zayn at WWE Crown Jewel. The World Heavyweight Champion will surely turn his attention to Zayn on WWE Raw. But he may have something to say about the 946’s destruction of The Bloodline last week. The 946 grew in numbers again last week when Carmelo Hayes joined the faction . His crowbar strikes played the deciding factor in the mass brawl last week. It’s a great move for Hayes whose career seemed to have stalled on WWE SmackDown. We will get our first look at the bigger 946 this week. Only one match has been announced for WWE Raw. JD McDonagh faces Joe Hendry in a bid to stop the singing Scotsman from teasing him about the size of his head. IYO Sky seems set to battle Raquel Rodriguez for the WWE Women’s Intercontinental Championship. Whether this will happen this week or later on is yet to be determined. Rodriguez might expect Sky to prove her worth by facing Roxanne Perez first. Meanwhile, Perez thinks she should have another crack at Chelsea Green, whom she beat last week, but this time with the Women’s Championship on the line. Talking of titles, Ethan Page was sent running backstage by WWE Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable. Page had just launched an assault on Rey Fenix. Fenix and Gable share a mutual respect after their superb title match last week. Page vs. Fenix or Gable seems likely. body: Kyle Fletcher recalls a bump that made him feel like he was pissing blood and made his ‘insides fall out of his butthole.’ Fletcher has been a wrestler on the AEW roster who has never been afraid of taking bumps that cause the normal person to wince, including bumps from tops of cages and to the outside of the ring in ugly landings. Now, he has named one that rests at the top of the list. While speaking to Westwood One Sports Night in a recent interview, Kyle Fletcher was asked about the nastiest bump he has taken in pro wrestling, recalling a bump he took while facing Mark Briscoe. “The one that comes to mind when I’ve been asked this question before is I took a suplex… from the top of the guard rail to the floor from Mark Briscoe, and you can see, you can, people have like put up the clip and you can see in my face, it literally- I landed directly on my tailbone and it felt like my insides exploded. It felt like… I don’t know how graphic I want to get. It felt like I was pissing blood and my insides fell out my butthole at the same time it was it was the weirdest feeling ever, and I literally just had to go, give me a minute, and I had to make sure that I was okay. I lay there for probably like 30 seconds going, ‘can I keep wrestling?’ Then I went, yeah, I think I can keep wrestling, and then I got up and kept wrestling.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Match Made: What is the Crown Jewel Championship? How the champion-vs-champion match works and every past winner
raw_title: What is the Crown Jewel Championship? How the champion-vs-champion match works and every past winner
summary_src: The WWE men’s and women’s Crown Jewel Championships were introduced in 2024 and, at least in storyline, should be the most prestigious titles in the company. For anyone who skipped the last two Crown Jewel PLEs, the championships are only awarded once a year and are never defended.
body: The WWE men’s and women’s Crown Jewel Championships were introduced in 2024 and, at least in storyline, should be the most prestigious titles in the company. For anyone who skipped the last two Crown Jewel PLEs, the championships are only awarded once a year and are never defended. WWE’s men’s and women’s world champions from Raw and SmackDown face each other with neither of their regular titles on the line. Instead, the winner receives an enormous Crown Jewel Championship belt, carries it around for a few hours, and then it goes back on display at the WWE Experience in Riyadh. Many fans have not warmed to the idea of the Crown Jewel titles, but if professional wrestling were a real sport where winners and losers weren’t predetermined, these would arguably be the most important championships in the industry. In theory, the matches determine who the ultimate champion in WWE actually is. The Crown Jewel Championship at least kicks that concept up a notch. The first Crown Jewel champions were determined on November 2, 2024 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Cody Rhodes won the inaugural men’s Crown Jewel Championship by defeating World Heavyweight Champion Gunther. Liv Morgan became the inaugural women’s Crown Jewel Champion that same night, defeating WWE Women’s Champion Nia Jax. World Heavyweight Champion Seth Rollins won the men’s Crown Jewel Championship by defeating WWE Champion and 2024 Crown Jewel winner Rhodes. On the women’s side, Stephanie Vaquer defeated Tiffany Stratton to win the Crown Jewel Championship. The two Crown Jewel Championship matches are already set. Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan will face WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green, while World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will face WWE Champion Sami Zayn. Morgan has an opportunity to become the first wrestler to win the Crown Jewel Championship twice after capturing the inaugural women’s title in 2024. Neither Reigns nor Zayn has previously competed in a Crown Jewel Championship match. Zayn would also figure to have plenty of his ride-or-die fans in attendance should the event ultimately take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. There are still plenty of questions surrounding this year’s Crown Jewel event , including where exactly it will take place. One thing that does appear set to continue, however, is the tradition introduced in 2024: WWE’s top men’s and women’s champions facing each other to determine who leaves as that year’s Crown Jewel Champion. title: Bron Breakker falls awkwardly at Hawaii live event

body: During WWE’s tour in Honolulu, Hawaii, Breakker and The Vision teamed up against LA Knight, Penta and Oba Femi. Earlier this year, Breakker was sidelined for several weeks following a hernia injury in February that required surgery. He eventually returned to WWE at WrestleMania 42, attacking Seth Rollins and setting up their rivalry. Currently, Breakker is focused on cementing himself as one of WWE’s next top stars, a pursuit that resulted in a clash with Femi not too long ago on Raw. title: Injury Update: Jade Cargill Opens Up On Past Neck Injury Left Her Struggling to Lift Opponents
raw_title: Jade Cargill Reveals Past Neck Injury Left Her Struggling to Lift Opponents
summary_src: Jade Cargill has built her WWE career around her incredible strength, but there was a point when a neck injury made even lifting another wrestler a serious challenge.
body: Speaking in a workout video published on the Women’s Health YouTube channel , Cargill revealed that she dealt with a neck injury approximately two years ago. She explained that a pinched muscle affected her ability to hold people up, which was especially difficult considering how much her wrestling style depends on strength. “A move in the gym that I do that makes me feel strong is actually pull-ups. I had an injury about 2 years ago with my neck. I had a pinched muscle. I could barely hold people up. So, me being able to do that and continue at least to get to 10, to get to 20, it means the world to me these days.” For someone whose signature offense involves lifting opponents into the air, that kind of physical limitation is a big deal. Cargill didn’t specify exactly when the injury happened or how long it affected her, but she made it clear that being able to perform those exercises again is something she doesn’t take for granted. This also isn’t the first time Cargill has addressed problems with her neck. Back in April, Cargill shut down accusations that she used performance-enhancing drugs and mentioned that neck issues had affected her lifting. Cargill also explained that she’s become more careful with her body as she gets older. Between WWE’s demanding schedule and the physical punishment that comes with wrestling, she now places greater importance on stretching and recovery. “How I go about bulletproofing my body is stretching. It’s something that I really put an emphasis on and I really take my time in doing now as I’m getting older, especially in the sport that we do and we’re taking all these bumps.” The WWE Superstar also admitted that maintaining her physique is currently more important than constantly pushing for heavier weights. She knows there isn’t a traditional offseason in WWE, and she’s not interested in risking an injury just to prove how much she can lift. title: On the Record: Jade Cargill Opens Up On How WWE Legend Chyna Inspired Her Muscular Physique
raw_title: Jade Cargill Reveals How WWE Legend Chyna Inspired Her Muscular Physique
summary_src: Jade Cargill didn’t develop her muscular physique by accident, and it turns out a WWE legend played a major role in inspiring the look she’s known for today.
body: “All my life, I’ve been muscular, and it’s something that I just wanted to put the pedal to the metal. I looked up to the great China. I seen her. She was a woman that walked in, owned the room, and I wanted to do the exact same thing.” That inspiration eventually followed Cargill into college, where she began taking strength training more seriously. After discovering that her school had a strength and conditioning coach, she decided to pursue the powerful look she had admired for years. “So, I got in college, seen we had a strength and conditioning coach, and I just said, ‘That’s what I want to do, and I want to look strong as ever.'” Interestingly, Cargill’s connection to Chyna isn’t something that only she has noticed. Back in 2022, Tommy Dreamer compared Jade Cargill to Chyna while discussing her athletic ability and potential as a professional wrestler. At the time, Dreamer praised Cargill’s natural gifts and saw similarities between the two performers. Cargill went on to explain that while Chyna remains her biggest fitness inspiration, the women she currently shares the ring with in WWE also motivate her to keep improving. Seeing other female wrestlers in tremendous shape reminds her that she can’t afford to slack off. “My biggest gym motivation or inspiration, I would say, was China. Just seeing her embody and go out there and just shine so bright, I was like, that’s exactly what I want to do. but also all the women athletes that we have in our company really motivate me.” She admitted that being surrounded by other impressive athletes sometimes makes her feel like she needs to work even harder. “And when I feel like I’m slacking and I’m in the ring with these women and they look just as phenomenal, I’m like, ‘Okay, I got to get back in the gym and go a little harder.'” Chyna helped change how muscular women were presented in WWE, and Cargill is now carrying some of that same inspiration into her own career. For Cargill, the goal was never simply to have big muscles. She wanted the kind of presence that made people pay attention the moment she walked into a room, just like Chyna did. body: “I get my best ideas when I work out. I get really hyped when I work out. Working out is my therapy, but looking good when you’re naked is a bonus as well.” Cargill certainly puts in the work to maintain that physique. She explained that she trains her core five days a week and demonstrated several exercises, including Russian twists, bicycles, in-and-outs, and planks. According to Cargill, those exercises aren’t just about having visible abs, either. They’re also essential to performing her power moves inside the ring. “If you ever see me pick somebody up for a stalling suplex, just know it is all core.” “I actually did this for 3 minutes one time and I was very proud of myself at 34 years old that I could do a three-minute plank. She’s also been outspoken about her confidence outside the gym. Earlier this year, Cargill explained why she prefers playing a heel in WWE , acknowledging that feeling good about how she looks is part of her natural personality. At the end of the day, Cargill isn’t making any apologies for enjoying the results of her training. Her workouts help her perform in WWE, give her a mental escape, and keep her looking exactly how she wants. And as she pointed out herself, looking good naked doesn’t hurt, either. title: Debating Triple H's Focus on Survivor Series WarGames
raw_title: Debating Triple H's Obsession With WWE's Survivor Series WarGames Match
body: The two-ring, steel cage war of attrition has become a staple of the pro wrestling calendar, but should it be, or has its yearly usage at the big-four premium live event watered down its effectiveness? Let's debate each side of the argument, including Triple H's seeming obsession with keeping it on the schedule, and come to a conclusion. Yes, the creative team may introduce story threads that will ultimately culminate at WrestleMania, but there has always been a sense of the mundane and lackluster when it comes to the post-SummerSlam months in WWE. There was the Deadly Game tournament and brand warfare before Triple H introduced War Games as a main event marketing tool. Since then, the match has helped Survivor Series regain prestige as one of WWE's elite shows of the year, while also paying off long-running rivalries that have dominated airwaves for months. It worked well for The Bloodline story in 2022 and again a year later, when Cody Rhodes and Co. faced The Judgment Day. It has also emphasized the importance of factions in WWE, and if history teaches us anything, it is that factions, groups, trios, and the like allow for more creative opportunities and, as a result, better TV. Look no further than the aforementioned Bloodline and Judgment Day, both of whom, at their peaks, were central and driving forces on Raw and SmackDown. Every year, without fail, WWE would trot out the event, headlined by matches that lacked the hate or longevity around them to justify taking place in the namesake steel structure. The result was diminishing returns and the long-overdue elimination of the event from the WWE schedule in 2022. The show had so watered down the Hell in a Cell concept that it took a legitimate, long-running rivalry with legitimate dislike between the competitors to justify bringing it back, which Triple H and his creative team did in October of 2024 when CM Punk and Drew McIntyre delivered an instant classic at Bad Blood. While this year's event is an exception, thanks to the excellently crafted Bloodline vs. 946 feud, the War Games match risks the same overexposure. Just like it did in NXT, when its introduction meant the conclusion of a long-running or intensely personal, faction-based rivalry, it became a staple of the Survivor Series amid the height of the Bloodline story. It served a purpose involving The Judgment Day, too. Over the years, in both the developmental and main roster brands, the continued promotion of the War Games match has spoiled the creative direction of some of the top feuds in WWE. There is no question about where programs are heading, and as a result, the excitement that once existed is in danger of wearing off. The moment The Bloodline and 946 began feuding, it was abundantly clear that the creative team was booking toward Survivor Series. While it is absolutely a positive for the writers to have an endgame in mind and a direction to take stories, there is a certain level of predictability that can settle in. That p
summary: The two-ring steel cage match has turned into an annual Survivor Series highlight under Triple H, helping restore the event's status after the post-SummerSlam lull that once featured Deadly Games and brand warfare. It has successfully paid off extended storylines such as The Bloodline in 2022 and Cody Rhodes versus The Judgment Day in 2023 while stressing the role of factions in WWE programming. The discussion weighs whether yearly repetition at the premium live event has reduced the match's impact or remains a needed creative anchor.

body: In today's surveillance era, where smartphone cameras are ubiquitous, many fans took notice of Thekla's post-match actions, which drew a wide range of reactions on social media from amusement to some suggesting the Toxic Spider was being disrespectful. "LMAOOOO Thekla not selling the finish of the match. I love her. [sic]," read one post. "What happened here? Anyway, Thekla should have sold the damage from Mercedes Moné's finisher," said another Twitter account. Further fanning the flames of the Thekla vs. Mercedes feud, Mercedes Mone seemed to dismiss her otherwise strong match against Thekla during the WrestleDream 2026 media scrum. "Uh, I mean, it's not one of my favorite matches," said Mercedes before seeming to deliver an in-character response to her rival. "I told you guys that I'm not scared of a little spider. She's more like a chihuahua that doesn't stop talking and just (makes chihuahua noises.)" "She's not toxic ," Mercedes continued. "I'm sick of toxic people." "Mercedes Mone flat out buried Thekla. I'm crying son," read a tweet in response to Mercedes' apparent jab. Whether or not Mercedes Mone and Thekla have any real-life animosity remains to be seen, but it doesn't matter if that's how fans perceive it. One of the oldest phrases in professional wrestling is "personal issues draw money." Typically that quote speaks to the spirit of simulated drama, but if real-life issues can be safely incorporated into wrestling storylines, all the better. Charlotte Flair and Becky Lynch famously went off script during a belt exchange ceremony on SmackDown in 2021. In what was supposed to be an innocuous exchange of championship belts with both stars switching brands, tensions ensued when Charlotte Flair dropped the WWE Raw Women's Championship on the ring mat. While the moment soured their once-tight bond, it led to increased interest in their ensuing Survivor Series match. "We were supposed to exchange the titles. I grab it out of her hand unknowingly, I'm 'Becky Two Belts' for a second then I toss her the title, then she tells Sonya (Deville) to pick it up. Then she challenges me to a fight, and I back out of it and I go. So everybody was supposed to get their moment there," said Lynch of how the segment was supposed to go before it went left. "The title dropped," explained Charlotte. "I didn't drop it on purpose." "If anyone knows how important the [WWE Raw women's title] is to me—I would never be dismissive of the title in the way that it was presented that I did." AEW is no stranger to backstage drama. Punk's yearlong crashout on his ex-employer continues to be the subject of heated discussions within the wrestling community. Punk returned to WWE for an unlikely and successful run that continues to this day. llm_long: Will Ospreay defended the AEW World Heavyweight Championship in a Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream 2026. The unique format was designed by Pro Wrestling EVE, with whom Ospreay has collaborated. Ospreay entered the bout early in his title reign following an emotional win over Kenny Omega at AEW All In 2026.

In Clockwork Carnage, wrestlers enter every three minutes until all eight participants are in the match. Any wrestler pinned or submitted before the final entrant arrives is eliminated. Once the last wrestler enters, the remaining competitors begin a 15-minute scoring period where each pinfall or submission counts as one fall.

Ospreay and Konosuke Takeshita opened the match at a fast pace. Takeshita executed a gorilla press from the top rope followed by a flying clothesline on Ospreay. The action continued with Takeshita delivering a dive to the outside onto Ospreay.

Mike Bailey entered wearing United Empire colors, though commentary noted that alliances do not apply in Clockwork Carnage. Takeshita eliminated Bailey and focused his attack on Ospreay. Ospreay and Bailey later showed a moment of solidarity with a United Empire high-five before Takeshita interrupted it.

Ricochet attempted to form a temporary alliance with Takeshita against the United Empire members. The partnership broke down when Ricochet tried to roll up Takeshita. Ricochet then hit a dive onto Ospreay on the outside before Takeshita dropped him with a headbutt.

Ospreay and Bailey delivered a double superplex to Takeshita, but Ospreay's attempt to steal the pin failed. Darby Allin entered using a skateboard, performing an ollie on Ricochet's back and setting up a table outside the ring. Kazuchika Okada's music played as the match continued.

title: Crown Jewel status, Street Fighter, more — Psyko’s random thoughts on wrestling
raw_title: Psyko’s random thoughts on wrestling: Crown Jewel status, Street Fighter, more
body: Not a lot can be written about this situation that hasn’t already been covered, but while I do feel like WWE should seriously consider moving the show outside of Saudi Arabia, I don’t think it’s as simple as having every wrestler and employee boycott the show. We have to remember that we’re not in the Vince McMahon era of WWE anymore, where wrestlers could just skip the show if they wanted to. We’re in the TKO era, and from everything that’s been reported, the only people who can make the call are Ari Emanuel and his partners. Nick Khan and HHH have no power over this decision. In fact, from what’s been reported, they’re actually against going to Saudi Arabia for this show, just like many of the wrestlers and crew members, but it’s out of their hands at this point. The biggest roadblock right now isn’t the money because TKO isn’t going to lose any money if it moves the show elsewhere. The biggest problem is that TKO is scared of being on bad terms with the Saudi government if it doesn’t hold the show in a few weeks. Since the Saudi government already has money invested in TKO boxing and the next big event is still happening, it has put TKO in a very awkward position. The other thing to consider is this: Do you see wrestlers risking their jobs over this? While it’s great that wrestlers have options outside of WWE, nobody outside of WWE is going to pay them the amount of money they’re making in WWE, with the exception of AEW. However, AEW’s roster is already more than full, so for most wrestlers, the only option is to do their jobs, even if they really don’t want to. The only reason I could see TKO moving this show out of Saudi Arabia is if the Saudi government cancels the whole thing, which I doubt will happen. I get that modern wrestlers, especially those who come from the indie circuit, have the mindset that everybody knows wrestling is scripted and fake. However, that doesn’t mean you can’t make an effort to make it believable for those who buy tickets or watch on television. In any other combat sport, if a smaller guy fights a bigger guy, the smaller guy would have to fight from underneath for the entire match and would probably get killed before the end of it. So why, in wrestling, is that same smaller guy able to go move for move with a heavyweight? That makes no sense. The same goes for heavyweight wrestlers. I get that you’re able to do flips and dives, but that’s not why we buy a ticket to see you wrestle. We want to see you beat the living shit out of your opponent, not hit a 450 splash from the top rope and perform suicide dives. Wrestlers really need to learn how to work to their size because, if they don’t, they’re just hurting themselves and the matches they’re in. When you fail to make a match feel believable, all you’re doing is performing moves for the sake of doing moves, and that has become forgettable. title: On the Record: WWE's Joe Hendry Details His 'Unconventional' Amateur Wrestling Background

body: "I think the thing about my amateur wrestling days is — it's very me, it's very unconventional," Hendry said. "It all started because I'd just started professional wrestling ... and I found that people weren't taking me seriously." While he's perfectly okay with using comedy in his wrestling, Hendry also wanted to be respected as a threat in the ring as well. He already had some history with judo, but Hendry decided to train as a grappler, too. It was something he felt came naturally to him. "MMA has progressed massively, but back when this was happening — this was, like, 12 years ago, when MMA wasn't as big in the U.K., and I would just go to MMA gyms and roast everyone in grappling," Hendry continued. That only lasted for a short while, however, as he eventually progressed to training in a more serious gym in Scotland and found himself facing more talented competition. That included former UFC fighter Paul Craig. "I don't know if I ever took him down, to be honest," Hendry stated. After defeating a wrestler who was slated to participate in the Commonwealth Games, Hendry decided to take a chance on entering himself. He continued training and, before participating in the Commonwealth Games, he won the British Championship in freestyle wrestling for his weight class. "That was one of the greatest days of my life," he said. "To be able to call my dad on the phone and say, 'I'm British Champion.' ... It's not often that I get emotional. ... I'll never forget that phone call." In 2018, Hendry joined Team Scotland for the Commonwealth Games, which were taking place in Australia. He was initially set to face Australian UFC fighter Robert Whittaker. "I was like, 'I must be living in a simulation, because don't tell me that the pro wrestler is about to face the UFC Middleweight Champion at the Commonwealth Games," Hendry said. Hendry reached out to UFC veteran and noted pro wrestling fan Chael Sonnen ahead of the fight, looking for advice. According to Hendry, he knew that he was heavily outmatched, but Sonnen encouraged him to talk some trash regardless. Sonnen wrote a promo for Hendry to deliver, but the fight never took place, as Whittaker learned he would have to vacate his UFC title if he decided to participate in the Commonwealth Games.

The signing stands out because Necro Butcher built his reputation almost entirely outside of wrestling's largest promotions. He became known for an exceptionally violent style that frequently featured weapons and the elements of deathmatch wrestling.

Necro Butcher's real name is Dylan Keith Summers. Born on July 13, 1973, in West Virginia, he made his professional wrestling debut in 1998. Over time he faced several prominent names from the 2000s independent scene, including Bryan Danielson, Kevin Steen, Eddie Kingston, Chris Hero, Claudio Castagnoli and Samoa Joe.

He also appeared in the 2008 film The Wrestler starring Mickey Rourke. A 2005 match against Samoa Joe at IWA Mid-South's Something to Prove event in Philadelphia gained a reputation for its brutality, highlighted by a moment in which Joe kicked him off arena bleachers onto the concrete floor.

More than two decades later the match received renewed attention when it became the focus of an episode in the seventh season of Dark Side of the Ring. The episode examined the bout along with Butcher's life and career. The full episode was later released on YouTube in July and has accumulated more than 700,000 views.

Butcher moved from being featured in the documentary to signing the WWE Legends deal months afterward. The contract typically permits the use of a wrestler's name and likeness for merchandise, video games and other projects while allowing for possible appearances.

title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG
raw_title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG | Wrestling Timelines
body: The 2000s was a turbulent time for WWE . It started wonderfully, if you only watched the TV product. Stone Cold Steve Austin was written out of storylines in November 1999, but no matter; as early as January 2000, Triple H had evolved into a main event-level heel. The Rock replaced Austin as the top babyface, more than adequately, by setting a record of consecutive attendances in excess of 10,000 fans. Underneath, powered by Chris Kreski’s overlapping, brilliant creative direction, Kurt Angle, Edge and Cstohristian, the Hardy Boyz, and countless more acts connected with the people. 2000 was arguably the best year in WWE history; while it was not as fascinating nor as futuristic as 1997 , the top-to-bottom match quality had never been better. A greying cloud hovered overhead the entire time. In December 1999, the media went after the WWF. Wrestling was over, and outrage is timeless. Various hit-pieces were penned by various outlets, generating so much attention that Coca-Cola pulled its sponsorship. WWE’s TV carriers got spooked by the pressure applied by the Parents Television and Media Council; Vince McMahon, in turn, made halfhearted, on-off attempts to tone down the product. With the Rock and a returning Steve Austin drawing so much money, a lack of sponsors was not an issue. And then, in 2003, with the Attitude Era fad dead, the Rock and Austin left. Stars were made eventually, John Cena and Batista most notably, but business wasn’t great. In order to ensure maximum profits, WWE had to behave.

title: Billy Gunn Comments On Brawl Out Incident
raw_title: Billy Gunn Weighs In On Brawl Out, 'Certain Veterans Aren't Going To Put Up With That Shit'
summary_src: What started as one of the greatest returns in wrestling history ended in wrestling tragedy as the relationship between CM Punk and AEW flamed out in two years.
body: What started as one of the greatest returns in wrestling history ended in wrestling tragedy as the relationship between CM Punk and AEW flamed out in two years. Speaking to Kenny McIntosh on Inside The Ropes , Billy Gunn, who works as a coach in AEW, reflected on the incident. “I wasn’t around for that. I knew the incident that happened, and it was what it was. They just have to realize that sometimes, there are certain veterans that aren’t going to put up with that shit, no matter what. If you’re a young buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. I think that’s what happened. I don’t know the whole details; that’s between them,” he said. Gunn said he didn’t pay attention to the media stuff surrounding the incident. Asked about how things like that were handled during his time, Gunn replied, “Vince (McMahon) had things under control really good. I don’t have to like you to work with you. I just have to do business. 99.9% of the guys always do that. There will be a spat every now and then where you just pull them into a room, shut the door, and you don’t do it in public or in front of the boys. If you have a problem, we fix it now, so that when you walk out the door, we don’t have a problem anymore. That’s how grown-ass people deal with shit. Nowadays, we don’t, and that’s sad.” Punk was suspended by AEW for his role in the incident. He returned a year later, but was fired after another incident at AEW All In 2023. Gunn, who serves as a coach in AEW, stated that he was not present for the incident. He noted that some veterans will not tolerate certain behavior and suggested that attempting to challenge them can lead to consequences.

He indicated that he was not familiar with all the details of the situation and chose not to follow the related media coverage. Gunn emphasized that the specifics remain between those directly involved.

When asked about handling similar issues during his earlier career, Gunn pointed to the approach taken under Vince McMahon. He explained that wrestlers were expected to conduct business professionally regardless of personal feelings.

Gunn described a method of addressing conflicts privately by pulling individuals into a room to resolve problems immediately. He contrasted this with current practices, calling the shift away from such discretion unfortunate.
Following the incident, Punk received a suspension from AEW. He made a return one year later before being fired after a separate event at All In 2023.

summary_src: WWE star Roman Reigns has shared his pro wrestling Mount Rushmore, based entirely on one parameter: the money they brought in.
body: "Only one metric matters: the money," he proclaimed. "The first day I went around the ring, my dad told me: 'Don't ever be confused, this ring is only about money. It's a business. Don't treat it any other way.'" With that made clear, Reigns named Hulk Hogan, "Stone Cold" Steve Austin, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, and John Cena as his picks. "They were all critical. We wouldn't be here today without those four, for sure," he said. While each star on his list is a behemoth in his own right, Reigns was asked if any of them could be considered his G.O.A.T. "I think I'd go with Hulk. ... It's hard to not say Steve, but then Dwayne — I really respect how he did it, and I really respect — it was just lighting in the bottle, no one picked it up so quickly," he said.
summary: Roman Reigns declared that money is the only metric that matters in the wrestling business, recalling advice from his father on his first day in the ring. He listed Hulk Hogan, Steve Austin, The Rock and John Cena as his WWE Mount Rushmore, crediting all four as critical to the industry's current state. Reigns added that while it was difficult to choose, he considers Hulk Hogan his personal GOAT.

title: Mike Bailey Jokes That He Might've Disrespected Michael Oku By Putting French TV Host In A Half Crab
raw_title: Mike Bailey Jokes That He Might've Disrespected Michael Oku By Putting French TV Host In A Half Crab
summary_src: Mike Bailey had a great time in France. AEW visited the country for the Grand Slam France event on Tuesday, October 6. If you ask Mike Bailey, this was a huge step towards pushing wrestling into mainstream culture in France.
body: AEW visited the country for the Grand Slam France event on Tuesday, October 6. If you ask Mike Bailey, this was a huge step towards pushing wrestling into mainstream culture in France. “I think it’s very fascinating to see how pro wrestling is captured by the media lens all over the world, right? Pro wrestling is ingrained in American culture as it is for many, many other countries, but France is still a few years behind. Pro Wrestling is evolving, I think bringing AEW and Grand Slam to the Adidas Arena is a huge step in pushing pro wrestling to the mainstream in France, but sometimes they just feel like, ‘Our audience, if we just talk about it, they might not know what it is, so we kind of have to show them.'” Bailey told Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp in a new interview. Continuing on, B ailey talked about putting a submission hold on a television host during his media tour before the show. “I think just asking a pro wrestler to put the host in a hold might not be the best idea. But I have been doing this for 20 years. I have been put in similar situations many, many times and I think that the half crab— which might be disrespectful to Michael Oku because he is the master of the half crab and I was kind of relatively on his turf, right? He’s English but still, Europe. But I think it was a much smarter hold than a high elbow guillotine or an open hand slap to do to a news presenter. This is the thing, he’s not gonna fight his way out of it. Not only do I have a fantastic half crab, but I have an even better straight ankle lock. So once that locked in, I have full control of him. Also when I’m sitting on his lower back, he’s not going to be able to wriggle himself out. So I can sit there comfortably as long as I want which was a big part of my plan.”

title: Riyadh Airport Stays Closed After Houthi Strikes
raw_title: Report: Riyadh International Airport remains highly restricted following Houthi attacks
summary_src: Saudi Arabia, which is scheduled to host WWE next month, has reported 20 attacks on the country as of late.
body: King Khalid International Airport, the main travel hub in Saudi Arabia, remains incredibly restricted after suffering attacks earlier in the month. The airport has been closed since last week due to a deadly bombing by the Iran-backed Houthis earlier this month. Despite plans to reopen by Sunday, the airport was “still shut as of Monday,” per Bloomberg. The airport is currently operating under a Notice to Airmen Advisory (NOA), which says that departures and landings can only occur if they’ve been given prior permission. The airport is reportedly not available for emergency landings currently. Riyadh has been under attack as of late, just weeks before WWE and a high-profile boxing match remain scheduled to take place in the Saudi capital. WWE’s November 7 trip to Riyadh for Crown Jewel remains on despite Saudi Arabia reporting that it suffered 20 attacks from the Houthis so far this month. Just a week before then, Riyadh is expected to welcome high-profile boxer Canelo Alvarez for a match against Christian Mbilli. The U.S. Department of State Consular Affairs provided a security alert on Monday morning, warning Americans to “exercise heightened vigilance” while visiting the Middle East. The Canadian government, which is currently recommending a full avoidance of all non-essential travel to Saudi Arabia, is suggesting citizens who wish to leave the country by air “should consider using airports in neighbouring countries.” Instability in the region has caused many international sports, entertainment and business events in the area to be postponed. The annual Six Kings Slam, a tennis exhibition featuring a half-dozen of the top men’s players in the world, was moved from October to late December. The Saudi International golf tournament, typically a final event on the European and Asian tour, was postponed indefinitely. The Asian Football Confederation is reportedly considering delaying the 2027 Asian Cup, which is scheduled to begin in January, by a year. Yet to follow in the footsteps of these major events are combat sports or professional wrestling, with the Canelo fight and Crown Jewel still on the schedule. With less than a month to go until either event, a rescheduling or postponement, if it were to happen, would be a last-minute call.
summary: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remains shut down and highly restricted following deadly attacks by Iran-backed Houthis earlier this month. The facility is operating under a Notice to Airmen that requires prior permission for any departures or landings and is unavailable for emergency use. WWE's Crown Jewel event on November 7 and a Canelo Alvarez boxing match the week prior are both still scheduled to proceed in the Saudi capital despite the ongoing security issues.

title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG
raw_title: WWE Trades Ruthless Aggression For PG | Wrestling Timelines – Page 3
body: After failing to renew the deal on the cheap, the CW Network makes the decision to drop WWE SmackDown from its airwaves. This is embarrassing, and significantly affects WWE’s bottom line. While nowhere near close to fatal - SmackDown finds a new home on MyNetworkTV in October - it’s an echo of WCW’s demise. But really, it’s a tale as old as time. SmackDown is among the highest-viewed shows on the station. In June 2008 , it draws strongly with teenagers and young adult males - elusive demographics that every television executive dreams of capturing - and yet, it does not matter. This is something of an exaggeration, but to understand this disconnect, think of it like a maths question: what is 3 million multiplied by 0? It doesn't matter if SmackDown on the CW Network draws, say, 3 million viewers. Ad execs believe that wrestling fans have 0 money. Blue-chip companies hold the opinion that wrestling fans are uneducated - how dumb must they be, if they believe in this fake crap?! - and thus poor. They can’t afford fancy things, so why waste money targeting them? By June 2008, WWE earns a meagre $1,154,000 from TV rights fees - and this factors in Raw, SmackDown, and ECW . WWE makes more money doing house shows, which is why the calendar is so brutal. Vince knows that there is a safe containing a vast fortune that WWE is yet to crack, and sets about transforming his company in order to open it up.
summary: After failing to renew the deal on the cheap, the CW Network makes the decision to drop WWE SmackDown from its airwaves. This is embarrassing, and significantly affects WWE’s bottom line.

title: ICW: NHB Loses Default Judgment in Rachel Price Lawsuit
raw_title: Update On Lawsuit Against Independent Promotion Icw: Nhb
body: Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin DMFirst Veer Game UPDATE ON LAWSUIT AGAINST INDEPENDENT PROMOTION ICW: NHB By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 10:39:00 There was a "proof hearing to determine the amount and extent of damage" won by plaintfiff Rachel Price in her lawsuit against independent promotion ICW: No Holds Barred on 9/24 in Newark, New Jersey. Price was officially given a default judgment on 7/21. During the hearing. Price was ordered to submit "a supplemental certification with any additional medical bills and the amount of the outstanding lien" within 30 days, which should be sometime in the next week. After that, the court should issue a ruling about what would be owed to Price. As previously noted, the promotion stopped responding and appearing before the United States District Court of New Jersey after their initial attorney removed himself from the case. In her lawsuit, Price alleged she was working for the venue at a 6/25/22 ICW: NHB event when there was an announcement made that those with vehicles in a lot adjacent to the move their vehicles. Price claims she exited the venue via a side door to move her vehicle, but poor lighting, a lack of railing, no signage and a lack of employees stationed at the door caused her to fall from the landing to the floor below, at least three feet, where she was injured. Price has alleged she has permanent personal injuries and is suing for over $75,000. Court records indicate that the parent company of the Heart Ballroom never responded and a summary judgment was ruled against them. Whether Price recovered any damages from them is unknown. ICW: NHB did iitially respond to the lawsuit, basically stating that any issues that happened were the responsibility of the venue, not them, as they had merely rented the space for the evening. On 1/29, ICW: NHB's attorney withdrew from the case as he had relocated. Since then, the court has not heard from anyone new representing the promotion and have not heard from its owner Danny "Demanto" Purdue either. There had been a settlement conference set for 3/10 but no one representing ICW: NHB appeared to take part. The court advised on 4/30 that Price could request a summary judgment against ICW: NHB. Price did that and on 6/2, the Court informed Price she could file a motion of final judgment against ICW. She did just that on 7/2, while also alleging the promotion had shifted its assets under a new LLC, NHB Merch and is seeking to amend her lawsuit to include the new LLC as well as the company's owner Danny Purdue (aka Danny Demanto) in order to prevent them from being able to be held liable for anything she may be awared in the lawsuit she filed back in 2024. In that filing, Price claimed the promotion has shifted everything under the new LLC and is now running under the company name No Holds Barred - The Chains. As of this writing, the court has not ruled on that request. ICW: NHB owner Purdue previously made reference to the lawsuit on the mic at an ICW: NHB

summary_src: Eva Marie is opening up about what really went wrong in her marriage to Jonathan Coyle, and according to the former WWE Superstar, their relationship had reached a point where they were more like business partners than husband and wife.
body: The former Total Divas star filed for divorce in December 2024 after 10 years of marriage, bringing an end to a relationship that WWE fans watched unfold on reality television. As Ringside News previously covered , the couple had separated before the divorce filing, with irreconcilable differences cited in the paperwork. During a recent interview with Page Six , Eva explained that there wasn’t one explosive incident that destroyed the marriage. Instead, she began questioning her future after turning 40 and realizing that the relationship wasn’t giving either of them what they deserved. She recalled how spending more time in California while working on her treatment and recovery centers helped set things in motion. However, the real turning point came when she took a serious look at what her marriage had become. Eva then explained how turning 40 changed her perspective. She compared her own marriage to her parents’ relationship, which has lasted more than five decades, and admitted that what she had with Jonathan simply wasn’t the same. “But when I turned 40, I had like kind of this aha moment of you only have one life and you know, with my marriage, there is nothing like I we were like business partners. So like I look at my parents and my parents have been married for 53 years and to me it like they have true blue like ride or die love till death do you part type of a marriage and I really felt like Jonathan and I were doing a disservice to one another because we just had a very transactional business relationship.” “We got along, we were totally, you know, best of buddies, but that’s not really what a marriage is, nor should it be, nor is that what I wanted it to be. So I was like, you know what? I’m 40 years old like I always I want to live my life to the fullest and I want to be as honest and as happiest as I possibly can be and I want that for him as well.” The interviewer pointed out that leaving a relationship can be especially difficult when things aren’t necessarily terrible. Eva agreed, explaining that there wasn’t some dramatic moment where either person had done something that made the marriage impossible to continue. “For sure and I think that as individuals, you know, a lot of times because there wasn’t this like massive turning point of like you know, this turmoil of oh my goodness, either he should leave me or I should leave him type situation, which I thank God for cuz I’m sure that is like really traumatic all as well for individuals.” Eva went on to explain that staying in a familiar situation can sometimes prevent people from finding what actually makes them happy. “But I think a lot of us in our life, we stay in situations, whether it’s business or even you know, your personal relationships because it is comfortable, because it is easy. llm_long: Andrade El Idolo retained the AEW National Championship by defeating Tommaso Ciampa at WrestleDream. The match took place on Saturday at Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida. Andrade secured the pinfall using The DM.

The contest featured extended striking exchanges along with multiple near falls. Andrade executed the Three Amigos on the floor and followed with a split-legged moonsault inside the ring. Both wrestlers incorporated elements of Andrade's routine of removing his entrance pants during the bout.

Ciampa removed a layer of his gear to reveal trunks with the phrase "I Just Know," referencing Andrade's catchphrase "How you know?" After Andrade removed his pants, he delivered several running double knees and hit Dia de los Muertos for a near fall.

Ciampa answered with a running knee and sent Andrade into a camera operator at ringside before earning another two-count. Ciampa first attempted to bring the title belt into the ring but was stopped by referee Aubrey Edwards. He then introduced a chair, which drew the referee's attention away.

The sequence mirrored events from Wednesday's Dynamite, where Ciampa had used the National title behind the referee's back. This time Andrade reversed the attempt and drove Ciampa onto the championship belt with a DDT. Ciampa kicked out, but Andrade immediately followed with The DM to retain the title.

title: Timeless Toni Storm's AEW Return Build Begins

body: Link @astridpizzaro After WrestleDream this weekend, AEW head honcho Tony Khan promised that Timeless Toni Storm would be back in the company. Khan also made it clear that when his four-time Women’s World champion returned, she’d be looking for the person who took her out back in March of this year. What TK didn’t mention? The build for the Timeless One’s comeback seems to have started at WrestleDream . Small packages appear to have been strategically placed around Addition Financial Arena in Orlando, Florida on Saturday night. At least one was found by its intended target, an internet content creator named Astrid Pizarro. They did what the folks behind viral marketing campaigns hoped she would do… created content about it. Pizarro found something wrapped in brown paper with the word “Confidential” stamped on it, and and“Play Me” scribbled in marker. It’s also marked with a kiss in red lipstick. The cassette tape within is labeled “Mundanities”, and its narrated by Renee Paquette. The next track Paquette intros is about Toni’s 12-year-old cocker spaniel: “Oh, Chanty. That’s a good boy, Chanty. Who’s a good Chanty? Take a chance. Take a chance, Chanty. Oh, what a beautiful boy. Now, you listen to me. I own you. I created you, and I can end you. You are nothing without me. You worship the ground I walk on, or I will make your life a living hell. When company comes over, they’re here to see me, not you.It’s not a time for your little tricks or performances. It’s not amateur hour with Chantsy. It’s my time. You will greet them. You will wait till I make one witty remark, and then Luther will escort you down to the basement to eat your rubbish. Otherwise, you have one job and one job only. To f*ck. You are a hunting machine and I want you to scour this damn neighborhood making onto anything that moves because mama is in the mood to sell and I can make a pretty good penny off of whatever half freak hamster you manage to knock up. Call it something exotic like a ham dog. You hear me? You worthless wanted beast. Okay, Chanty, let’s go for a walk.” Over the rest of the tape, Storm gives wrestling advice to students like, “if you want to make it in this business, you’ve got to get yourself a cool hat.”* “Fantastical. Mysterious. Timeless. These are the Toni Storm Tapes.” Will these provide meaningful information about Toni’s absence, the kayfabe reason for it, and maybe even clues about what she’ll do when she returns? Does it further distract from the (generally believed to be happy) reason she’s been out? WWE used these sorts of marketing campaigns in the past for Wyatt-related acts, even incorporating augmented reality game elements in them. Those were interesting and really excited a portion of the audience, but ultimately didn’t lead to much. Are these just awareness raising tactics? Or will the return of Timeless Toni Storm be the next evolution of this kind of pro wrestling story? * A properly-sized one , as we all know that tiny hat was holding the

The signing comes after Shotzi returned to TNA earlier this month, wasting little time getting herself involved in the Knockouts Division. Her appearance immediately got fans talking about whether she was simply making a one-off appearance or had something more permanent lined up. Now we have our answer. Shotzi is no stranger to the wrestling business. The California native made her professional wrestling debut in 2014 before eventually making her way to WWE, where she became an NXT Women’s Tag Team Champion alongside Ember Moon. She also spent time on WWE’s main roster, becoming known for her distinctive personality, bright green hair, and willingness to take some pretty wild risks in the ring. Following her WWE departure, Shotzi continued wrestling outside the company, and her recent TNA appearances made it clear that she wasn’t planning to disappear from the spotlight anytime soon. TNA didn’t just announce her signing either. Apparently, she’s been riding motorcycles since she was 18, has traveled across America hunting ghosts for her YouTube series Chamber of Horrors , and even studied musical theatre at AMDA in Hollywood. She’s also a massive horror movie fan who dreams of directing her own horror film someday. And that’s just the beginning. TNA revealed that Shotzi is obsessed with Elvis Presley, owns her own chicken farm, and once managed to ride every attraction across all four Walt Disney World theme parks in one day. The company also noted that she was named PWI’s 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and appeared on the magazine’s cover. Shotzi also made a point of celebrating her heritage. Then there’s the detail about her wedding, which sounds like something straight out of a wrestling storyline. Shotzi revealed that she didn’t just get married and call it a day. She actually wrestled while still wearing her wedding dress. “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day.” As Ringside News previously covered, Shotzi’s future became a major topic of discussion following her departure from WWE and subsequent appearances outside the company. Her return to TNA gave fans another reason to wonder what she had planned next, but the company’s latest announcement makes it clear that she’s officially part of the roster. Now Shotzi has a fresh opportunity to establish herself in TNA’s Knockouts Division, and there are plenty of potential opponents waiting for her. She’s already proven that she isn’t afraid to take chances, and with a new contract in place, it looks like the next chapter

title: Comeback Watch: Eva Marie Confirms She’s Open to Another WWE Return
raw_title: Eva Marie Confirms She’s Open to Another WWE Return
summary_src: Eva Marie isn’t shutting the door on WWE just yet. The former Superstar has made it clear that she would absolutely consider stepping back into the ring, and she still has plenty of love for the company that helped launch her career.
body: Eva hasn’t wrestled for WWE since her second run with the company ended in 2021. That comeback saw her return to Monday Night RAW with the Eva-Lution character, eventually becoming involved in a storyline with Piper Niven, who was introduced on WWE television as Doudrop. During a recent interview with Page Six, Eva was directly asked whether she would ever return to the wrestling ring. She didn’t hesitate with her answer, making it clear that WWE remains an important part of her life. “Of course, yes and yes. So, WWE will always hold a special place in my heart because, like I said, they took a chance on a no-name kid who never wrestled a day in her life.” Eva then reflected on how different her background was before entering professional wrestling. While she grew up watching WWE during its WWF days thanks to her three older brothers, she wasn’t someone who had spent years training to become a wrestler. Instead, soccer was her sport before WWE came calling. “Soccer was my sport, so like when it came to the wrestling ring, and I was a fan, of course, of WWE back in the day when it was WWF because I have three older brothers.” Despite getting her start without wrestling experience, Eva eventually developed an appreciation for portraying a villain on television. She specifically pointed to her 2021 return as a time when she felt particularly comfortable embracing the character. “I think like I played a bad guy on So, I was a heel in WWE, and there’s nothing nothing better to play. Like when I went back in 2021, I had the best time ever because I really embraced that character.” As Ringside News previously covered , Eva later revealed that WWE originally had different plans for her final run, including a longer storyline involving her partnership with Piper Niven. She has also discussed the challenges of balancing WWE training with filming Total Divas , which played a role in her decision to seek additional development during her first stint with the company. While Eva clearly remains interested in wrestling again, she didn’t reveal any current discussions with WWE or suggest that a comeback is already being planned. For now, it’s simply an open invitation from someone who still has a soft spot for the business. Still, Eva Marie’s willingness to return is bound to get a reaction. She was never exactly the most universally loved performer during her WWE career, but that was also part of what made her heel character work. Whether WWE would ever bring back the Eva-Lution is another question entirely, but Eva herself is clearly game for another round.
