summary: The latest: eva hasn’t wrestled for WWE since her second run with the company ended in 2021. That comeback saw her return to Monday Night RAW with the Eva-Lution character, eventually becoming involved in a storyline with Piper Niven, who was introduced on WWE television as Doudrop.

title: Eva Marie Left Speechless When Asked About Current Relationship With Ex-Husband Jonathan Coyle
raw_title: Eva Marie Left Speechless When Asked About Current Relationship With Ex-Husband Jonathan Coyle
summary_src: Eva Marie had plenty to say about her divorce from Jonathan Coyle, but one question about where things stand between them today actually managed to leave the former WWE Superstar struggling for words.
body: Eva and Jonathan’s marriage ended after a decade together, with the former Total Divas star filing for divorce in December 2024. Their relationship had been featured extensively on WWE’s reality series, making the split particularly interesting for longtime fans who watched their romance play out on television. During a recent interview with Page Six , Eva discussed moving forward with her life following the divorce. However, things got a little awkward when the interviewer asked whether she and Jonathan were currently on good terms, bad terms, or somewhere in between. Eva admitted that she hadn’t really prepared herself for that question, especially since she hasn’t publicly discussed the divorce very much. “You know, that’s a Wow. Out of all the things that I would think like to prepare myself because, you know, I’m not really that public with and I nor have I been talking about my divorce.” After struggling to come up with an answer, Eva kept things pretty simple. The interviewer suggested that perhaps Eva simply wished him well from a distance, and the former WWE star agreed. She didn’t exactly sound interested in maintaining a close friendship with her ex-husband. “Yeah, I wish him well over there, and that’s about it, you know?” “Yeah. I don’t know. I’m stumped. I’m like, ‘Damn, girl, I am not lost for words.’ And you have just stumped me because that one is like you know now that I you have my wheels turning it’s it’s more so I’m trying to find the word where it’s like there’s no real bad blood in in me but I also have it’s not like we’re best friends or I’m calling them up you know.” That response says quite a bit about where things stand. Eva wasn’t accusing Jonathan of doing anything wrong, and she made it clear that she doesn’t harbor serious resentment toward him. At the same time, she wasn’t pretending they’re still close friends who regularly check in on each other. As Ringside News previously covered , Eva filed for divorce after 10 years of marriage. The couple originally met at a CrossFit gym and tied the knot in 2014, with their relationship becoming part of the storylines featured on Total Divas. Eva has also spoken about why she chose to keep the divorce private rather than turn the situation into a public spectacle. Now that the marriage is officially behind her, Eva seems perfectly comfortable wishing Jonathan the best without keeping him involved in her everyday life. She may not have found the perfect words immediately, but she eventually made her position pretty clear: there’s no major bad blood, but they’re not exactly buddies either. H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.
summary: Per Ringside News: eva and Jonathan’s marriage ended after a decade together, with the former Total Divas star filing for divorce in December 2024. That explained, things got a little awkward when the interviewer asked whether she and Jonathan were right now on good terms, bad terms, or somewhere in between.

title: Eva Marie Opens Up On She Gave Up More Than Fans Realize in Divorce Settlement

summary_src: Eva Marie’s divorce is behind her, but getting to that point apparently cost her more than most people realize. The former WWE star says she gave up quite a bit during the split, but there was one thing she absolutely refused to lose — her name.
body: Speaking to Page Six , Eva revealed that her divorce from Jonathan Coyle was legally finalized around August 22, 2025. Even then, she still had some loose ends to clean up before she could really feel like that chapter was closed. One of the biggest remaining pieces was the Texas home she previously shared with Jonathan. Once the house was sold and the remaining assets were sorted out, Eva said she finally had everything in place to move forward. “It was finalized August 22nd, but then I was able to sell the house in Texas and get all those assets kind of dialed in.” Apparently, keeping the name wasn’t completely uncontested either. When asked whether Jonathan pushed back on it during the divorce, Eva admitted there was at least some resistance. “Um, a little bit, you know, which I understand to a certain degree because Natalie Eva Marie is a brand, you know.” “God gave me the platform, gave me the opportunity with WWE, gave me the platform that I have today, which I’m so grateful for, that if God gave it to me, He’s the only one that can take it away, and nobody else can do that.” “I go by Natalie Eva Marie. That is, like, my legal name. I got rid of my married name.” Eva may have walked away from the marriage giving up more than she expected, but her name was apparently the one thing that wasn’t negotiable. Natalie Eva Marie is now legally hers, and she made sure the identity behind her WWE career stayed with her as she moved into the next chapter. body: SAN DIEGO -- As Money in the Bank came to an end on October 10th, Raquel Rodriguez's Saturday night was far from over. She still had to make the five-hour drive from New Orleans to Bossier City, Louisiana. The two jumped into a car, and what started as another trip between WWE events turned into something resembling a ride in a DeLorean, transporting Rodriguez back to her childhood. “It almost feels like you know those road trips that we have going from New Orleans to Bossier City are the same road trips that we had going from Harlingen, Texas, to Corpus Christi to watch my dad wrestle, and that's something so beautiful,” Rodriguez said. González competed on the South Texas wrestling circuit during the 1980s and 1990s under the names Ricky "Desperado" González and Speedy González. Sometimes, his wrestling schedule kept him away from home. Other times, he would load up the family and bring them along to watch him compete. “It’s an amazing connection that I have with my dad, and I'm so grateful that I get to experience that with him,” Rodriguez said. After Rodriguez graduated from college and her basketball career came to an end, González encouraged her to follow in his footsteps and step inside the wrestling ring. Before her WWE tryout, her father took her to Laredo, Texas, for a practice match to help prepare her for the next chapter of her life. A decade later, Rodriguez has established herself as one of WWE's top female wrestlers, with her father supporting her every step of the way. “That's another reason that I'm able to wake up grateful,” Rodriguez said. “Because I can take my dad slash my driver slash my security with me on a lot of trips.” Rodriguez has held the championship for 84 days after defeating Sol Ruca on Monday Night Raw on July 27. She was struck in the nose earlier in the match but continued competing despite blood dripping from her face, knowing that a little spilled blood was nothing compared to the opportunity to capture her first singles championship in WWE. She is grateful to be the first Mexican woman to hold the championship, to travel around the world and to be part of The Judgment Day, one of WWE's longest-running factions. The Judgment Day has undergone several transformations since its original lineup featured Edge, Damian Priest and Rhea Ripley. The faction now consists of Rodriguez, Dominik Mysterio, Liv Morgan, JD McDonagh and Roxanne Perez. The two later captured the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship for the first time and have since enjoyed four championship reigns together. llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

title: Billy Gunn calls Triple H's AEW joke a dick move

body: Link WWE.com In April of 2019, Billy Gunn was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame as a member of D-Generation X. Gunn had just taken a job with Tony Khan’s All Elite Wrestling, which launched as a WWE “challenger brand” a few months earlier. Billy was given permission to take part in the ceremony, during which D-X star and WWE executive Shawn Michaels made a joke about the ROH/independent show ALL IN that served as proof of concept for AEW, and fellow D-Generate and higher-ranking exec Paul “Triple H” Levesque called it a “pissant company” . Gunn looked back on that moment in an interview he did last month with Inside The Ropes : “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool. I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ “I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go. The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. “It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. They like to stir up shit. When you have somebody in another company, which was me, they can’t believe it, and then you see me, they have to do it. It’s like an unwritten thing in a book. ‘If another guy is in another company, we have to say or do something.’ They started chanting it [the crowd had done the Young Bucks ”too sweet, whoop, whoop” chant], and you get a response from the guy leading the company.” The chant could have been answered with something about The Bucks specifically, but I also don’t think anyone was too surprised that AEW took fire — probably not even Tony Khan. In the end, it actually served as good publicity for a while, until Punk’s run with TK’s fed ultimately made things very tribal in the pro wrestling world. Did it seem outrageous to you at the time? Shotzi actually wrestled a couple of matches for TNA back in 2018 and 2019, and even then, she was hoping it would eventually lead to her becoming part of the Knockouts Division. It didn’t happen at the time, but several years later, she finally got what she wanted. “Oh, it has been a long time coming! You know, I had like a couple of matches back in like 2018–19 with TNA, hoping I would become a Knockout then, and I’m finally here, and it feels good! It was the right time.” There’s another big reason TNA appealed to Shotzi, and it goes beyond simply having another place to wrestle. She wants actual stories to sink her teeth into, and that’s always been her favorite part of professional wrestling. Fans already got a taste of where things could be heading when Shotzi crossed paths with Rosemary and Allie. She’s not giving away exactly what’s coming, but she’s clearly excited about getting weird with those two on television. “Yes, that’s what really excites me because that’s my favorite part of pro wrestling — the storytelling and, you know, like how wild the stories get. So, I mean, if you saw the last episode of TNA, I have a little bond with Rosemary and Allie.” For Shotzi, that’s exactly the kind of stuff she wants to spend more time doing. She’s looking forward to having fun with her character rather than simply bouncing from match to match. “So yeah, I’m excited to see where that goes on TV, and I’m looking forward to having a lot of fun and focusing on a storyline.” Shotzi also isn’t shy about how highly she rates TNA’s women’s division. She believes the Knockouts have always had something a little different from every other women’s roster in wrestling, especially when it comes to embracing darker characters and letting things get wild. “I’ve always said the Knockouts division has that extra spice that no women’s division has ever been able to replicate. And, you know, they’ve got their darkness and girls doing wild stuff on TV every week.” That’s also where Shotzi believes she can bring something TNA doesn’t currently have. In her eyes, nobody in the division is quite doing what she does, and she plans on filling that hole herself. “But yeah, I feel like nobody like me is on there right now, and I want to bring that ballsiness to the Knockouts division.” TNA officially announced Shotzi’s signing on October 19, ending any speculation that her recent appearances were simply a short-term deal. She had already made her presence felt after returning to the company earlier this month, but now she’s sticking around for whatever comes next. summary_src: R-Truth is finally speaking out after his scary injury on WWE SmackDown, and while the veteran Superstar says he’s doing okay, he’s also sharing a hospital photo that has fans concerned about what happened during his match against Damian Priest.
body: On October 19, 2026, R-Truth took to Twitter to address his condition following the October 16 episode of SmackDown. Truth thanked fans for their support and shared a photo of himself wearing a hospital gown while sitting in front of an MRI machine, smiling and giving a thumbs-up. Truth started by reassuring everyone that he’s doing okay and appreciating the overwhelming support he’s received since the incident. “I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I’m grateful for you all.” Of course, Truth couldn’t resist throwing in a little humor at Damian Priest’s expense. He joked that his former tag team partner nearly killed him during their match before making it clear that he intends to return. “…On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn’t think he was ThAt serious… But ok, I’ll be back” The update comes after R-Truth was legitimately injured during his match against Damian Priest on October 16. Truth landed awkwardly after delivering a missile dropkick from the top rope, prompting the referee to check on him and stop the match before its planned conclusion. The injury came during an already heated rivalry between Truth and Priest, who had been feuding since their tag team partnership fell apart. What was supposed to be another chapter in their storyline ended with a legitimate medical concern instead. Now Truth is giving fans some much-needed reassurance while making it clear that he isn’t finished with WWE just yet. The hospital photo might look concerning, but his message was positive, and he’s already talking about getting back into the ring. There’s still no official timetable for his return, but at least Truth hasn’t lost his sense of humor. title: Billy Gunn calls Triple H's AEW joke a dick move
raw_title: Billy Gunn: Triple H’s AEW jab at D-X’s WWE HoF induction was a ‘d*ck move’
body: Link WWE.com In April of 2019, Billy Gunn was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame as a member of D-Generation X. Gunn had just taken a job with Tony Khan’s All Elite Wrestling, which launched as a WWE “challenger brand” a few months earlier. Billy was given permission to take part in the ceremony, during which D-X star and WWE executive Shawn Michaels made a joke about the ROH/independent show ALL IN that served as proof of concept for AEW, and fellow D-Generate and higher-ranking exec Paul “Triple H” Levesque called it a “pissant company” . Gunn looked back on that moment in an interview he did last month with Inside The Ropes : “I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time and I was there and they were all wondering how I got to go there, and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool. I went, asked, and he said ‘100%. Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ “I didn’t know what they were gonna do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that if they were, Hunter was going to have something to say. Once I set myself up for that, I just let it go. The only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of trying to save face, and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. “It’s the wrestling business. It’s what we do. They like to stir up shit. When you have somebody in another company, which was me, they can’t believe it, and then you see me, they have to do it. It’s like an unwritten thing in a book. ‘If another guy is in another company, we have to say or do something.’ They started chanting it [the crowd had done the Young Bucks ”too sweet, whoop, whoop” chant], and you get a response from the guy leading the company.” The chant could have been answered with something about The Bucks specifically, but I also don’t think anyone was too surprised that AEW took fire — probably not even Tony Khan. In the end, it actually served as good publicity for a while, until Punk’s run with TK’s fed ultimately made things very tribal in the pro wrestling world. Did it seem outrageous to you at the time? title: "Sensational" Sherri passes away
raw_title: "Sensational" Sherri passes away - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE is saddened to learn of the death of WWE Hall of Famer "Sensational" Sherri. She was 49. She passed away at her mother's home in Birmingham, Ala. Friday morning, according to her husband of 10 years, Robert Schrull. "It's a great loss to the wrestling world," he told WWE.com. The couple resided in St. Petersburg, Fla. In the early 1980s, Sherri began her career in the AWA. In 1985, she defeated Candi Devine to become the AWA Women's Champion. Their rivalry lasted more than a year, with the championship trading hands on several occasions. It was during this time that she began perfecting her skills as a manager, leading "Playboy" Buddy Rose and "Pretty Boy" Doug Somers to the AWA Tag Team Championship. On June 28, 1986, Martel would win the AWA Women's Championship for a third and final time from Candi Devine. On July 24, 1987, "Sensational" Sherri debuted in WWE, pinning her trainer and mentor the Fabulous Moolah to become Women's Champion. Sherri defended the gold against Debbie Combs, Velvet McIntyre, and Desiree Peterson. She quickly earned the reputation as someone who would do anything to win, even if it meant using unsavory tactics. Her rivalry with Moolah continued as they became the captains for the first-ever female Survivor Series teams in 1989. Sherri held the championship for 15 months before losing to Rockin' Robin. In the early ‘90s WWE phased out the Women's Division, leaving Sherri to focus on managing the male wrestlers. Her first client was "Macho Man" Randy Savage. It was during this time that she became "Sensation Queen." The couple had rivals with Miss Elizabeth, Hulk Hogan, Dusty Rhodes and Sapphire. In 1991, "The Million Dollar Man" Ted DiBiase enlisted her services. After that relationship dissolved, she took on the managerial duties of Shawn Michaels. In 1994, Sherri appeared in WCW as "Sensuous" Sherri managing Ric Flair during his rivalries with Sting and Hulk Hogan. After separating from Flair, she became "Sister" Sherri guiding Harlem Heat to seven WCW Tag Team Championships. Sherri was enshrined in the WWE Hall of Fame in 2006. "Million Dollar Man" Ted DiBiase was her presenter.

title: NJPW adds two title matches to King of Pro Wrestling 2026
raw_title: NJPW adds two title matches to King of Pro Wrestling 2026
body: With the Destruction tour now over, NJPW is gearing up for its biggest event of the fall . Two new title bouts have been confirmed for NJPW King of Pro Wrestling 2026, which takes place from Sumo Hall in Tokyo on October 12. The event will see Gabe Kidd defend his IWGP Global Heavyweight Championship against Shota Umino. Plus, the NEVER Openweight Six-Man Tag Team titles will be on the line with United Empire (Will Ospreay, HENARE & Great-O-Khan) defending against Unbound Company (Yuto-Ice, OSKAR, and a partner to be announced). Umino is finally getting his rematch against Kidd after Kidd won the Global title in controversial fashion this July . In that bout, there was a pre-match angle where Kidd bloodied Umino and disrespected NJPW. Umino still chose to go forward with the defense and ended up losing his title. We were originally supposed to get a Kidd vs. Umino matchup in the G1 this summer, but Umino suffered a concussion that led to him forfeiting all but of one his matches in the tournament. Ospreay is heading back to Japan for the first time since winning the NEVER titles with HENARE & O-Khan in May. As tension between Ospreay and United Empire leader Callum Newman persists, we’ll see how that impacts the road to Wrestle Kingdom. Before King of Pro Wrestling, HENARE & O-Khan will put their IWGP Tag Team titles on the line against Yuto-Ice & OSKAR on October 6. title: IYO SKY Tapped For Women's Intercontinental Title Run
raw_title: IYO SKY Needs a Change: Four New WWE Directions
body: This is the direction WWE has already started to set up. Raquel Rodriguez has held the Women's Intercontinental Championship since beating Sol Ruca on the July 27 episode of Raw, and SKY challenged her in four-way title matches on WWE's South America tour in September. Rodriguez came out on top in each of those matches. SKY has never held the Women's Intercontinental Championship. She has already won the NXT Women's Championship, the WWE Women's Championship, the Women's World Championship and the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship. Rodriguez is part of The Judgment Day, which has targeted SKY on Raw for months, so a program between the two would build on a story that is already in place. It would also give the title a challenger who is a former Women's World Champion. SKY and Rhea Ripley , who teamed as Rhiyo, won the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship from The Kabuki Warriors on the January 5 episode of Raw. They held the titles for 53 days before losing them to Nia Jax and Lash Legend on the February 27 episode of SmackDown. Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley won the titles by beating Fatal Influence on the October 9 episode of SmackDown. Ripley is recovering from surgery for a torn meniscus and does not have a return date, so a Rhiyo reunion would have to wait. SKY teamed with Sol Ruca to beat Rodriguez and Perez on the August 10 episode of Raw. A run with Ruca would give both women something to do while Ripley is out, and the tag titles can be defended on either brand. SKY spent close to two years as a heel in Damage CTRL after debuting on the main roster with Bayley and Dakota Kai at SummerSlam in 2022. That run included her Money in the Bank win in 2023 and her cash-in on Bianca Belair at SummerSlam later that year to become WWE Women's Champion. She turned face in July 2024. A heel turn would change how she is presented after a string of near misses since SummerSlam. Losing to Morgan and falling short in a Money in the Bank qualifier give her reasons to be frustrated, and her run as a heel included her biggest singles win in WWE. On the other hand, she has become one of the more popular women on the roster as a face, and a turn would mean dropping her story against The Judgment Day. A brand switch would give SKY a new set of opponents. Chelsea Green holds the WWE Women's Championship and is set to face Morgan for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship at Crown Jewel . SmackDown also has Jade Cargill and Charlotte Flair, who are in the middle of their own issues after Cargill attacked Flair before the October 9 tag title match. The Women's Intercontinental Championship is the best option. WWE has already put her in title matches with Rodriguez on the road and had her name herself as the next challenger on Raw. Winning a title she has never held in WWE would give her a clear accomplishment after losing at SummerSlam, and she would be a champion who can work with almost anyone on the Raw roster. summary: WWE has laid groundwork for IYO SKY to pursue the Women's Intercontinental Championship currently held by Raquel Rodriguez. SKY challenged Rodriguez unsuccessfully in four-way title matches during the September South America tour after Rodriguez defeated Sol Ruca to win the belt on the July 27 Raw. A singles program would build on months of targeting by The Judgment Day and position the former Women's World Champion as a credible challenger for the midcard title.

body: R-Truth is assuring fans that he’s all right following the injury he suffered on WWE SmackDown last week. On Monday, Truth shared a photo of himself from that evaluation and thanked fans for their support. Truth, while assuring everyone that he’ll be back, did further his storyline issues with Priest by claiming that Priest tried to kill him in their match. “I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I’m grateful for you all,” Truth wrote. “On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn’t think he was ThAt serious… But ok, l’ll be back” Truth & Priest are former tag team partners and even had one reign as WWE Tag Team Champions earlier this year. Their partnership ended with Priest turning heel in September. After Truth’s injury on Friday, Priest went and got a steel chair before Nathan Frazer & Axiom ran down to prevent the attack. llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

title: WWE Stars Make Surprise Appearance at NASCAR Phoenix Race
raw_title: WWE Stars Make Surprise Appearance at NASCAR Phoenix Race
body: The Miz, whose real name is Mike Mizanin, is a longtime WWE wrestler who signed with the company in 2004. The 46-year-old out of Cleveland, Ohio is a two-time WWE champion and a former headliner of WWE’s largest show of the year, WrestleMania, in 2011. Paul Heyman is a longtime wrestling manager. In WWE, the 61-year-old wrestling legend has worked alongside some of the company’s biggest stars in history, including Brock Lesnar, CM Punk, and Roman Reigns. The two WWE stars were seen at the driver’s meeting prior to the Freeway Insurance 500 at Phoenix. “WWE’s Paul Heyman and The Miz are here in Phoenix,” wrote motorsports insider Bryan Nolen via X. The Miz and Paul Heyman were also spotted on pit road talking it up with Jeff Dickerson, owner of Spire Motorsports. “Spire owner Jeff Dickerson talking (& recruiting?) WWE’s Paul Heyman and the Miz,” via Braking Bob on X . Standing atop the spotter’s stand high above the 1.0-mile track, The Miz posted a “Miz Method” video to his Instagram. Noting how loud it is at a NASCAR race, Mizanin added the caption, “Yelling a Miz Method lesson at the top of my lungs and NASCAR still has me on mute.” “Team work makes the dream work. Everybody sees the driver but watch what happens around him when everybody does their job perfectly. Surround yourself with people who make you a better version of yourself,” Miz said in the video . The Miz and Paul Heyman are not the first WWE stars to make appearances at NASCAR races in the past, let alone this season. Last year at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, WWE women’s star Chelsea Green served as the honorary pace car driver. Tyler Reddick captured his sixth win of the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season on Sunday at Phoenix. After overtaking Chase Briscoe following a late-race restart, the driver of the No. 45 drove to victory in the Freeway Insurance 500. Reddick, who has the most Cup wins of any driver this season, made up tremendous ground in the championship battle. While there are only three races left in the season, Reddick is 56 points behind points leader Kyle Larson in the seventh position. Larson finished a disappointing 34th after exiting the race early due to a right-front tire failure that sent him into the wall. Meanwhile, Christopher Bell went on to finish fourth and is now only five points behind Larson in the second position. Denny Hamlin wound up finishing 28th on Sunday after tire problems of his own. Despite the difficult finish, the driver of the No. 11 managed to gain points on Larson as he is now 31 points behind with three races left. John Breeden John Breeden is a NASCAR contributor at Heavy Sports. He has five years of sports journalism experience. He graduated from James Madison University in May of 2022 with a degree in media arts and design. John is also a sports reporter for the Daily News-Record in Harrisonburg, Virginia. Previously, John was a sports writer for JMU's The Breeze and a NASCAR content writer for Sportskeeda. More about John Breeden

body: "I was very adamant that this was the best path for AEW and the best path for the company. There's a number of reasons I felt that way, but he was the one with a vision for it. He believes in AEW. I think he's a great TV and film leader and I think he was the only buyer interested in and excited about and has kept TNT, TBS, and HBO MAX under the same roof. title: How AEW Can Improve This New Concept — Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: Clockwork Carnage: How AEW Can Improve This New Concept
body: By Andrew Kelly Published Oct 19, 2026, 1:00 PM EDT Andrew Kelly is a pro wrestling writer from The Wirral, England. With bylines on many pro wrestling websites, Andrew has proven himself to be very knowledgeable in the realms of WWE, AEW and more. Andrew is one of TheSportster's Match Reviewers and has covered the best matches of superstars like Cody Rhodes, MJF, Bianca Belair and more. He's also written hundreds of lists and features covering wrestling current events and history. He is also an MA Graduate from the University of Manchester, and a BA Graduate from Liverpool John Moores University, both in Creative Writing. Sign in to your TheSportster account AEW hosted its first ever Clockwork Carnage match at the WrestleDream 2026 PPV, which saw Will Ospreay defend the AEW World Championship against a sea of talented opponents in Samoa Joe, Kazuchika Okada, Konosuke Takeshita, Mike Bailey, Ricochet, Adam Copeland and Darby Allin. The match itself was pretty fun, with non-stop action, brilliant in-ring work, and interweaving storylines, but it wasn’t perfect in execution. The Clockwork Carnage matchup is one that can stay on AEW programming, but there are improvements that must be implemented to make it better the next time around, in terms of booking, match structure, and rules. One of the biggest issues of AEW’s first Clockwork Carnage match was the predictability of the outcome. Will Ospreay won the AEW World Title as recently at All In: London 2026 and was the brains behind the creation of the bout, so there is no way he was losing, especially when you consider the rest of the field wherein there was no obvious alternative for AEW to book. In the future, AEW shouldn’t book such an obvious outcome - for instance it would have been harder to call had Ospreay been in the ring with bigger names like MJF, Kenny Omega, Jon Moxley and others. AEW booking any other championship across any division would provide more unpredictability than AEW’s top prize, or else they could have number one contenders determined in Clockwork Carnage showdowns. After Konosuke Takeshita & Mike Bailey got eliminated from Clockwork Carnage, the remaining six wrestlers battled it out for 15 minutes to score as many points as possible. This led to 11 falls in 15 minutes, which felt like a little overkill. Sure, it made sense for wrestlers to not exert energy in kickouts or tap out quicker than usual to avoid passing out, but there were still definitely way too many. It soon became clear that any finisher was going to score a point, whereas if it were harder to get a point on the board, then the whole match would have felt more intense, hard-to-call, and dramatic. Next time around, AEW should consider perhaps half the number of pinfalls and submissions for a more effective production. title: R-Truth updates fans after SmackDown injury scare
raw_title: WWE’s R-Truth breaks silence after match was stopped after he ‘almost passed away’
body: During the Oct. 16, 2026, edition of Friday Night SmackDown, WWE Superstar R-Truth's match against his former tag team partner Damian Priest was abruptly stopped, causing concern that he suffered a legitimate injury. According to the former 24/7 Champion, he "almost passed away" on Friday night, blaming Priest. He took to X, formerly Twitter, to share an update from the hospital . He smiled and had his thumb up while sitting on a CT scan machine. "I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes," he wrote. "Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I'm grateful for you all. "…On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… [Damian] Priest tried to kill me,, I didn't think he was ThAt serious… But ok, l'll be back," R-Truth added. On Oct. 16, Truth and Priest faced in a singles match. Truth went for a top-rope dropkick, hitting the move but injuring himself in the process. The referee stopped the match, and WWE medical personnel came out to check on him. This didn't stop Priest from attacking him before Fraxiom (Axiom and Nathan Frazer) came out to stop him. It was later reported that Truth was "all right" and was going to be evaluated the following week. Luckily, it appears he is "OK," as he put it in his post. This is unlikely to be the final chapter in their feud. The tensions between Truth and Priest were boiling for months, and it came to a head in September 2026. Priest turned on Truth after they failed to win the AAA World Tag Team Championship from the War Raiders (Ivar and Erik). Truth and Priest have crossed paths several times over the last couple of years, dating back to the former trying to get into the Judgment Day stable in 2023. They later began teaming up and won the Tag Team Championship in March 2026, holding the titles for 147 days.
summary: During his October 16 match against Damian Priest on SmackDown, R-Truth injured himself on a top-rope dropkick, prompting the referee to halt the bout and bring out medical staff. Priest continued the attack until Fraxiom intervened. From the hospital, R-Truth posted a photo of himself on a CT scan machine giving a thumbs-up and stated he is okay while thanking fans for their support.

title: Ex-WWE Referee Shares Honest Take on WWE Championship Changing Hands So Quickly

body: Zayn is already in his second title reign in a matter of months. He first won the title at Night of Champions in June. That reign was short-lived, as CM Punk defeated him to become champion nine days later. Zayn’s second reign has lasted longer, approaching the 40-day mark. However, given that the WWE Championship has changed hands so quickly already, the title scene has become more unpredictable. “I don’t mind it under the right circumstances. When you have [superstars] like Sami Zayn, you’ve got [CM] Punk, you’ve got [Kevin Owens], you can even throw in Johnny Gargano, who’s finally got off the road cases. In the situation, if it’s presented correctly, I don’t mind it,” Korderas told The Game Plan . Despite the current circumstances on SmackDown, Korderas also believes that Roman Reigns’ lengthy reign makes sense on Raw. “On the other side, you look on the Raw side and Roman Reigns having basically a stranglehold on the championship over there, that works for that title in that situation. So again, it’s all situational.” Korderas explained why Roman Reigns ‘ World Championship reign makes sense as part of WWE’s long-term plans for Raw. The former WWE referee pointed to Reigns’ booking, as well as Oba Femi’s emergence, to explain why ‘The Tribal Chief’ should hold the title for longer. “Each story is different. Going back to Money in the Bank, when people talk about LA Knight, who had a great match against Roman Reigns. But if LA Knight wins the championship, if he beats Roman Reigns, then what? The long-term plan here is Oba Femi and Roman Reigns,” Korderas told The Game Plan . Korderas feels that once Oba Femi becomes champion, the moment will be more significant. “Let’s not get that confused. So people say, ‘Well, it’s okay if he loses it and then wins it back.’ No, it’s not okay. Because in that case, Oba Femi now has beaten someone who has already beaten Roman Reigns, as opposed to having two guys meet who look seemingly unbeatable.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. title: On the Record: Grayson Waller Calls Out WWE Stars Who “Complain and Moan” Online and to Dirt Sheets
raw_title: Grayson Waller Calls Out WWE Stars Who “Complain and Moan” Online and to Dirt Sheets
summary_src: Grayson Waller has a message for WWE stars who disappear from television and then start complaining about their booking online — do something about it. The current NXT Champion says he could have easily gone down that road himself, but instead, he went back to NXT and changed his own situation.
body: Speaking on NotSam Wrestling , Waller opened up about why returning to NXT became so important after things weren’t going the way he wanted on WWE’s main roster. For Waller, the first step was reminding himself just how good he could be when given the opportunity. That confidence certainly isn’t lacking anymore. Now that he’s sitting on top of NXT as champion, Waller believes RAW and SmackDown will eventually realize they dropped the ball with him. “Part of the reason that I wanted to go back to NXT was because I needed to remind myself first — that took the first few weeks. Now that I’m the NXT Champion, I know how good I am. Now my job is to remind the guys on RAW and SmackDown — hey, you fumbled the ball back, and you’re gonna regret it.” Waller then turned his attention toward wrestlers who handle their own frustrations very differently. He said some talent disappear from WWE television and immediately start complaining on social media or taking their grievances to wrestling dirt sheets. Waller made it clear that’s not how he wanted to handle his own situation. In his mind, wrestlers basically have two lanes when things aren’t working out, and he chose to actually make something happen rather than publicly complain about it. “You’ve got two lanes. Some wrestlers will disappear — they will go on Twitter and complain and moan and go to the dirt sheets and say certain things. But that’s not me.” Instead of waiting around for WWE to suddenly change its mind about him, Waller decided he needed to take control of what he could. Going back to NXT became his way of forcing the issue and rebuilding the momentum he felt he’d lost. “I sat there and went, ‘Things aren’t going the way I need them to go, so I’m gonna do something about it. I’m gonna make that happen for myself.’ And that’s exactly what I’ve done for myself.” Now Waller has the NXT Championship around his waist and a pretty big chip on his shoulder about proving WWE’s main roster wrong. If his plan was to make people pay attention again instead of complaining about being overlooked, he’s clearly convinced that returning to NXT did exactly that. title: Judge Upholds Maryland Child Victims Act in WWE Ring Boy Case
raw_title: Judge denies WWE and McMahons’ effort to throw out ring boy lawsuit on U.S. constitutional challenge to Maryland Child Victims Act
summary_src: A federal judge on Monday rejected an effort by WWE, its parent company TKO, Vince McMahon, and current U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon, to
body: U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar ruled that the law is constitutional as applied to the case. The lawsuit may now move forward toward the discovery phase, where depositions are conducted, and evidence is exchanged. A teleconference is set for November 17 to set future deadlines. The case would still be at least several months away from a potential trial. Monday’s ruling does not address whether the alleged abuse happened or whether the defendants are responsible for it. The ring boys also overcame an earlier motion to dismiss in May , which narrowed the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. Claims by two of the plaintiffs remain against Linda McMahon, while all seven proceed against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. In 2023, Maryland passed the Child Victims Act, which eliminated any time limits for filing civil lawsuits related to child sexual abuse. If not for the new law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs’ claims would have expired years ago. The former ring boys allege they were abused in a variety of states but, importantly, they all claim that some of the abuse they were subjected to happened in Maryland. Maryland’s state-level Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025, ruling that the law was valid under the state’s constitution, allowing this and other cases to move forward. But the defendants’ recent challenge was based on arguments related to the U.S. Constitution, which the Maryland Supreme Court decision couldn’t address, but which Monday’s ruling by Judge Bredar did. Bredar, however, is a federal judge at the district level. The defendants could eventually try to appeal his ruling to the higher appellate court, the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals. In this context, a right to due process refers to a guarantee that people have under the Fourteenth Amendment, to not have their rights violated by unfair or arbitrary laws. WWE and the McMahons argued that Maryland did that by taking away their protection from these lawsuits by removing the time limit for bringing such cases to court. In his ruling, Bredar said the U.S. Constitution gives states broad power over lawsuit deadlines. A deadline to sue is a rule set by lawmakers, in this instance, the Maryland state legislature. And lawmakers can change those deadlines, Bredar ruled, even for very old claims. A court can strike down a change like this only if the change serves no purpose. The defendants did not “show how their particular hardships make the [Maryland Child Victims Act] arbitrary or irrational,” Bredar wrote. Instead, the defendants were trying to “hold the [Maryland] legislature to a stricter standard than is required under the Due Process Clause” of the Fourteenth Amendment. title: Undefeated Farid Basharat Weighs In On UFC release: They don’t like the way I fight
raw_title: Undefeated Farid Basharat comments on UFC release: They don’t like the way I fight
summary_src: Farid Basharat believes his technical style isn't what UFC wants: "I think they're trying to go for brawlers."
body: 29-year-old Basharat confirmed his departure from the UFC roster recently, stating that the company “did not want to give me a new contract.” After a UFC campaign which saw him earn all but one of his wins via decision, Basharat believes his departure from the company comes due to his fighting style and what the UFC is hoping to receive from performers nowadays. “I don’t think I fit the direction they’re trying to move in,” Basharat said. “I think they’re trying to go for brawlers, spill your blood whether you win or lose type of stuff. Me, the way I fight, it’s just high IQ, intelligent, defeat the opponent where they’re weak and don’t fight them where they’re strong. And I just don’t think that’s where they’re going for.” Basharat later explained that he believes UFC is cultivating an audience which values finishes that end via finish, and doesn’t care as much about the actual level of skill being displayed. This goes against his fighting style, and he believes this type of company isn’t sustainable, he stated. “A lot of the fanbase are equating entertainment to finishes, and that’s just not the case … It’s sad that a lot of the fanbase is being brainwashed into believing that. I think the company, the UFC, is manufacturing a fanbase that doesn’t appreciate good quality fighting. They just appreciate these rock’em type fights where, even if it’s a mismatch, even if it’s a low-level fight, as long as there’s blood, as long as it’s a first-round finish, we’re happy. And in my opinion, you can’t build a sport off that. Because you might do well for a couple of years ratings-wise, but sooner or later it’s going to delegitimize the sport and the fans are going to be left wanting high-quality fights.” Basharat said he wasn’t sure where he would go next in his career, but assured fans he’s not done fighting. A potential avenue for him could be joining his brother, Javid, on the PFL/MVP MMA roster sometime down the line.

title: Legal Watch: Judge Rejects WWE and McMahons’ Attempt to Dismiss Ring Boy Lawsuit
raw_title: Judge Rejects WWE and McMahons’ Attempt to Dismiss Ring Boy Lawsuit
summary_src: WWE, TKO, Vince McMahon and Linda McMahon just took another loss in their attempt to shut down the “ring boy” lawsuit before it gets much further. A federal judge rejected their latest argument for dismissal, meaning the seven former ring boys can keep pushing their case toward discovery.
body: WWE and the McMahons argued that having to defend themselves after so much time has passed creates serious problems. Several people connected to the allegations are dead, including former WWF ring announcer Mel Phillips and former executives Pat Patterson and Terry Garvin, while other potential witnesses have also passed away. The judge found that states have broad authority when it comes to setting and changing deadlines for lawsuits. In his view, the defendants hadn’t shown that Maryland acted irrationally by reopening the door for childhood sexual abuse claims. “Defendants do not show how their particular hardships make the [Maryland Child Victims Act] arbitrary or irrational.” “Instead, Defendants attempt to hold the [Maryland] legislature to a stricter standard than is required under the Due Process Clause.” The judge didn’t completely brush aside the problems that come with litigating allegations from the 1980s and 1990s. He simply made it clear that his job at this stage wasn’t to decide whether those problems make the lawsuit harder to defend, but whether Maryland had the constitutional authority to change its law. In the end, Bredar found that Maryland lawmakers had a legitimate reason for removing the old time limit. “But the Court’s role here is to interpret the United States Constitution and to resolve disputes that arise under it. The Maryland General Assembly created its statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims and, in response to a legitimate and pressing issue, decided to alter it in a rational way.” This ruling absolutely does not mean the seven plaintiffs have proven their allegations. Bredar wasn’t deciding whether the alleged abuse happened or whether WWE, TKO or either McMahon was responsible, and the defendants have denied the central claims in the lawsuit. The seven men say they were minors when they were sexually abused while working around WWF events in the 1980s and 1990s . All seven accuse Phillips of abuse, while one also alleges abuse by Patterson and another alleges sexual harassment involving Garvin. Their lawsuit claims WWE and the McMahons were negligent in allowing the alleged conduct to happen. This also isn’t the first time the plaintiffs have survived an attempt to stop the case . An earlier ruling left seven plaintiffs moving forward, with all seven pursuing claims against Vince McMahon, WWE and TKO, while two still have claims against Linda McMahon. There’s also still a chance this latest ruling gets challenged. Bredar is a federal district judge, meaning the defendants could eventually try taking the issue to the Fourth Circuit Court of Appeals, but POST Wrestling reported that they hadn’t immediately responded when asked whether an appeal was coming. So this isn’t a verdict against WWE or the McMahons, but it is another attempt to stop the case that didn’t work. title: Judge Allows Ring Boy Lawsuit Against WWE To Proceed
raw_title: Judge Denies WWE and McMahons’ Effort To Throw Out Ring Boy Lawsuit
summary_src: TRIGGER WARNING – SEXUAL ABUSE On Monday, a federal judge rejected an effort by WWE, TKO, Vince McMahon, and Linda McMahon, to have the ring boy lawsuit dismissed because of the argument that a Maryland law the case was brought under violates the U.S. Constitution.
body: U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar ruled that the law is constitutional as applied to the case. The lawsuit may now move forward toward the discovery phase. The Maryland Child Victims Act of 2023 was upheld in a Maryland Supreme Court ruling earlier this year. The Act eliminates the statute of limitations in negligence claims in regard to lawsuits by child abuse victims. The defendants argued that the Act is illegal under the US Constitution and the Maryland Constitution. A teleconference is set for November 17 to set future deadlines. The lawsuit was originally filed in October 2024. You can read the full lawsuit here .
summary: A U.S. District Judge denied WWE and the McMahons' motion to dismiss the ring boy lawsuit. The ruling upholds the Maryland Child Victims Act of 2023, which removes the statute of limitations for child abuse victims' negligence claims, allowing the case to advance toward discovery. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish upcoming deadlines in the suit originally filed in October 2024.

llm_long: A U.S. District Judge ruled that Maryland's Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the lawsuit filed by former WWE ring boys. The decision allows the case to proceed to the discovery phase, where depositions will be conducted and evidence exchanged. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish future deadlines.

The ruling does not determine whether the alleged abuse occurred or if the defendants bear responsibility. The case remains several months away from any potential trial. The ring boys had previously overcome a motion to dismiss in May that reduced the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven.

Claims by two plaintiffs continue against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs proceed with claims against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. The former ring boys allege abuse in multiple states but claim some of the incidents took place in Maryland.

Maryland enacted the Child Victims Act in 2023, removing time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving child sexual abuse. Without the law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs' claims would have expired years earlier. Maryland's state Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025 under the state constitution.

The defendants challenged the law on U.S. Constitutional grounds, specifically arguing it violated due process rights under the Fourteenth Amendment by eliminating protections from old lawsuits. The federal judge determined that the U.S. Constitution grants states broad authority over lawsuit deadlines.

This week, I’m looking at the best ring technicians in WWE’s men’s divisionn and the performers whose in-ring limitations are becoming increasingly difficult to ignore. In his years in NXT, Carmelo Hayes rose to the top based on his ability to put on captivating matches. His remarkable athleticism, fluid transitions, creative offense, and convincing selling allowed him to deliver exciting, fast-paced matches with a variety of opponents. He shined as the NXT Champion and seemed destined for greatness on the main roster. As the newest member of the 946, Hayes finally finds himself as an important player in a top program. Positioned alongside WWE’s hottest new faction in its battle against the Bloodline, Hayes has the spotlight like never before. His affiliation with the group gives him an identity and a purpose beyond simply being a great wrestler, and allows him to share mic time in a way that can help mask any weaknesses in his promo game. One thing’s for sure: He will elevate the quality of any match he’s involved in. For the first time, Hayes has a legitimate shot at becoming a major player on Raw. Chad Gable’s face turn and subsequent Intercontinental Championship run have been a mixed bag. title: US Issues Security Alert Before WWE Crown Jewel

body: The situation in the Middle East remains volatile with WWE Crown Jewel 2026 now less than three weeks away. On October 18, the US State Department Bureau of Consular Affairs i ssued a new security alert advising that Americans in the region should “exercise heightened vigilance” due to the ongoing complex security environment. The alert urged Americans traveling to or from the Middle East to monitor information about airport and airline operations and to have a contingency plan in place if their original travel plans get disrupted. The alert applies to 12 countries, including Saudi Arabia. The State Department’s travel advisory for Saudi Arabia remains at a level three, which means Americans citizens are advised to reconsider traveling there amid the strikes that have been carried out by the Iranian-supported Houthis group. WWE Crown Jewel is still being promoted for Saturday, November 7 in Riyadh as part of the annual Riyadh Season festival. A backup location in the United States is on the table if WWE does end up needing to change its plans. A star-studded tennis tournament was supposed to be held in Riyadh this week but has been postponed to December . The Future Investment Initiative, a major investment conference nicknamed “Davos in the desert” has also been postponed . The conference was scheduled to begin next week but has been moved to 2027, with the new dates to be announced. Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn and Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green to determine the ceremonial Crown Jewel Champions for 2026 are official for the November 7 PLE. title: WWE Shut Down Grayson Waller’s Plan to Wear Stephanie Vaquer’s NSFW Championship Photo on NXT
raw_title: WWE Shut Down Grayson Waller’s Plan to Wear Stephanie Vaquer’s NSFW Championship Photo on NXT
summary_src: Grayson Waller tried to bring Stephanie Vaquer’s nearly naked championship photo to WWE television, but somebody backstage clearly wasn’t having it.
body: The WWE Superstar revealed that he had a T-shirt made featuring Vaquer’s viral Instagram photo, where she posed wearing nothing but the Women’s World Championship. His plan was to wear the shirt on NXT, but WWE put the brakes on that idea before it ever made it in front of the cameras. During an appearance on NotSam Wrestling , Waller was talking about his habit of wearing shirts designed to get under other wrestlers’ skin. He’s gotten away with plenty over the years, but apparently putting Vaquer’s barely covered body across his chest was a little too much for WWE. Waller explained that he had the shirt made after seeing the photo Vaquer posted to Instagram , which paid tribute to Shawn Michaels’ famous championship pose. The shirt was ready to go, but WWE never allowed him to wear it on NXT. “There’s some that haven’t ended up on TV. I don’t know if you remember that Stephanie Vaquer broke the internet recently. She did an Instagram story like Shawn Michaels — there was a T-shirt with that on it. That didn’t end up on TV.” “If anyone wants it, you can buy it. There’s some fan who will pay some crazy money for it.” Waller also admitted that even he has some boundaries when it comes to trolling other WWE stars. He loves stirring the pot, but he’d prefer to pick on somebody who can actually step into the ring with him afterward. That’s where the Vaquer shirt became a bit of a problem, since the two aren’t exactly going to settle their differences in a singles match. “I love to cause chaos, but I think if I can’t fight you, if we can’t fight after this, then that’s the line. Stephanie Vaquer doesn’t feel like we won’t have a match — that’s where my line is.” Vaquer originally shared the revealing photo after the October 5 episode of RAW, using the Women’s World Championship to cover herself in a pose that immediately drew comparisons to Shawn Michaels. The image took off online, and apparently Waller figured it would look even better on a shirt during NXT. Vaquer has since lost the Women’s World Championship to Liv Morgan at Money in the Bank , but her viral photo nearly got another moment on WWE television thanks to Waller’s latest attempt at stirring up trouble. Instead, WWE shut it down, and Waller is now sitting on a shirt he thinks some fan will pay ridiculous money to own. Considering his track record of trolling just about everybody, it’s probably only a matter of time before he finds another way to get himself in trouble. title: Ospreay Retains AEW World Title at WrestleDream
raw_title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller
body: DMFirst Veer Game Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-19 12:02:00 Ospreay Survives Eight-Man Gauntlet War to Keep AEW Gold at WrestleDream Will Ospreay walked out of WrestleDream on Sunday, October 18, 2026, still holding the AEW World Championship after beating seven opponents in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The stipulation forced Ospreay into a brutal two-stage format, starting as a gauntlet with staggered entrances before shifting into a 15-minute scored-fall period once eight men had entered. It was a chaotic, physically demanding structure that tested every competitor in the field. Ospreay drew the first entrance, meaning he would have to face all seven challengers to keep his title. Konosuke Takeshita came in second, followed by Ospreay's United Empire teammate 'Speedball' Mike Bailey as the third entrant. Bailey, a Canadian wrestler, was among the group chasing the title before Takeshita pinned him to eliminate him from advancing to the second stage. Ricochet entered fourth, and Darby Allin, the TNT Champion, came in fifth carrying a table that would factor into the match later. International Champion Kazuchika Okada arrived sixth, and Adam Copeland made his entrance as the seventh competitor shortly after Bailey's elimination. Joe pulled level with Allin and Ospreay by locking in the Coquina Clutch on Ospreay, then went for another Musclebuster before Copeland speared him out of it to claim his first fall of the match. Copeland then equalized again with a spear on Ricochet with just over a minute remaining, and a follow-up spear on Okada briefly put him in position to walk away as champion. With Copeland's retirement plans looming and Ospreay now having survived one of AEW's most grueling title defenses yet, the promotion heads into its next chapter with its World Championship picture wide open for fresh challengers.

The show will be available for purchase in the United States through PPV.com, HBO Max, Amazon, DAZN, Fubo, YouTube, and cable or satellite providers. International fans in the UK and other markets can access it via MyAEW.

Eight wrestlers will compete across two phases. The Entry Phase begins with two competitors and adds a new entrant every three minutes until all have entered, with any wrestler pinned or submitted during this phase being eliminated.

Surviving wrestlers advance to the 15-minute Scoring Phase, where the competitor with the most pins or submissions is declared the AEW world champion. llm_long: Billy Gunn commented on the incident involving CM Punk that led to his departure from AEW. The event occurred after what had been viewed as one of the biggest returns in wrestling history, ultimately resulting in the end of Punk's relationship with the promotion after two years.

Gunn, who serves as a coach in AEW, stated that he was not present for the incident. He noted that some veterans will not tolerate certain behavior and suggested that attempting to challenge them can lead to consequences.

He indicated that he was not familiar with all the details of the situation and chose not to follow the related media coverage. Gunn emphasized that the specifics remain between those directly involved.

When asked about handling similar issues during his earlier career, Gunn pointed to the approach taken under Vince McMahon. He explained that wrestlers were expected to conduct business professionally regardless of personal feelings.

Gunn described a method of addressing conflicts privately by pulling individuals into a room to resolve problems immediately. He contrasted this with current practices, calling the shift away from such discretion unfortunate.
Following the incident, Punk received a suspension from AEW. He made a return one year later before being fired after a separate event at All In 2023.

body: After competing on WWE’s house show tour in Hawaii, Bayley flew home to help Kirk Whit’s Big Time Wrestling celebrate its 30th anniversary. Bayley started attending Big Time Wrestling shows as a teenager and then began her career there at 18 years old. The indie promotion held its 30th anniversary show in San Jose, California on Sunday (October 18). The card included names like Rob Van Dam, Andrade El Idolo, Mustafa Ali, Bandido, Mike Bailey, and Zoey Serrano — and Bayley also stopped by to be part of the festivities. At the show, Bayley gave a speech in the ring thanking the fans. She then showed up as the impromptu special guest referee during a match between Aaron Solo (her ex-fiance) and Chazz “Starboy” Hall. Bayley went to stop Solo from using a title belt as a weapon, which led to her accidentally striking him in the face with the belt. She then counted the pin after Hall hit a reverse rana, a dive to the outside, and a Shooting Star Press. During the speech she gave, Bayley pointed out that her mother and some of her friends were in the crowd at the show. Bayley was in action at both of WWE’s house shows in Honolulu, Hawaii this weekend. Sol Ruca defeated IYO SKY, Bayley, and Lyra Valkyria in a four-way match on Friday night’s card . Ilja Dragunov explains his decision to leave WWE for AEW after his WrestleDream debut. Former WWE United States Champion Ilja Dragunov left the promotion in August 2026 after his contract expired. He chose not to renew, and reports noted that while company officials considered him a great talent, they didn’t believe he was a “numbers mover” for the money he was asking. After weeks of speculation and reports pointing towards it, Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at the WrestleDream pay-per-view this past Saturday. Appearing at the WrestleDream post-show press conference , Ilja Dragunov explained why he left WWE for AEW. He said he always has the urge to step up and fight. He explained that if an environment starts holding him back from competing at his best, he has to step away to find fresh air and new challenges. “Then, I feel like I’m getting stuck somewhere. Not because of external factors, just feeling stuck in general, because I have this urge to fight. I love to fight, and I want to compete, and I want to step up. If I feel that the air in a certain environment gets thinner for me, I need to breathe. That’s what I did today, here. If I need a place to breathe new, fresh air, see a new landscape, and see what the world can offer me to satisfy this hunger for competition — that’s the easiest answer I can give to that question,” Dragunov said. title: Jonathan Coachman Questions WWE’s Decision to Drag John Cena Into Nikki Bella-Paige Feud
raw_title: Jonathan Coachman Questions WWE’s Decision to Drag John Cena Into Nikki Bella-Paige Feud
summary_src: Jonathan Coachman isn’t a fan of WWE dragging John Cena into Nikki Bella’s current storyline with Paige. In fact, the former WWE commentator thinks the company is outright disrespecting Cena by repeatedly using his history with Nikki as part of the rivalry.
body: Speaking on The Coach & Bro Show , Coachman questioned why WWE is still leaning so heavily on a relationship that ended years ago. Nikki and Cena were together for several years and were engaged before splitting in 2018, but both have long since moved on with their lives. Coachman pointed out that Cena is now married, making WWE’s decision to keep bringing up his past relationship with Nikki even stranger to him. “How long ago did Nikki Bella date and do that reality show with John Cena? Probably more than five years ago. Cena is either married or in a long-term relationship with a beautiful young lady that resembles Nikki Bella.” Paige teased the Five Knuckle Shuffle before Nikki stopped her, while Nikki later put Paige in Cena’s STF. Paige then went even further by hitting Nikki with an Attitude Adjustment for a near fall. For Coachman, that wasn’t just a couple of harmless wrestling callbacks. He felt WWE was deliberately making Cena’s old relationship with Nikki part of the story and questioned why the company would want to do that to one of its biggest stars. “So you put Nikki and Paige in a rivalry, and in the match, they do the ‘AAA,’ and the announcers say, ‘Clearly, that’s disrespecting because she dated Cena.’ Then Nikki did an STFU because that’s one of Cena’s moves.” Coachman then directly questioned WWE’s creative thinking behind the whole thing. From his perspective, repeatedly connecting Nikki to Cena this many years later doesn’t do Cena any favors, especially when he’s moved on from that part of his life. “Vince, as a creative, if you’re doing that, why are we doing storylines that completely disrespect John Cena at this point?” Coachman also sees another problem with the angle: newer WWE fans might not even understand what they’re supposed to be watching. Nikki and Cena’s relationship was once a huge part of WWE’s reality television world, but that doesn’t necessarily mean every current viewer knows the history behind Paige using an Attitude Adjustment against her. “And the new people probably don’t even know what they’re watching.” Whether WWE keeps leaning into the Cena references remains to be seen, but Coachman has made his position pretty clear. He thinks the company is digging up old history at Cena’s expense when Nikki and Paige should be able to make their feud personal without him. title: O’Shea Jackson Jr. Revealed as Mystery Guest for Cody Rhodes and Charlotte Flair Interview
raw_title: O’Shea Jackson Jr. Revealed as Mystery Guest for Cody Rhodes and Charlotte Flair Interview
summary_src: Cody Rhodes and Charlotte Flair are getting some Hollywood company for their upcoming interview, and the mystery guest has finally been revealed. Ice Cube’s son, O’Shea Jackson Jr., is joining the two WWE stars for a special sit-down with Paul Heyman’s son, Jacob Heyman.
body: Jackson confirmed the news on Monday, October 19, revealing that he’ll be part of The Roundtable , which premieres Wednesday, October 21, on Heyman Hustle TV. The actor made the announcement in an Instagram post shared with the platform, joking that fans probably weren’t expecting him to be the surprise guest. And naturally, he couldn’t resist calling himself the heel of the group. “I know what you’re thinking. ‘There’s no way…’ That’s right folks Wednesday October 21st you will be able to catch the roundtable convo between @americannightmarecody @charlottewwe @jacob.heyman. And the heel that you love to hate. Me.” Jackson, who portrayed his father Ice Cube in the 2015 movie Straight Outta Compton , then dropped the jokes and explained how much the opportunity meant to him. He described the conversation as surprisingly personal and even therapeutic. “All fun aside, this was truly an honor to even be able to sit with Charlotte, Cody, and Jacob. An amazing conversation and look into things from their perspective. And honestly very therapeutic. I’m so grateful to everyone involved and my friends over at @heymanhustletv for even thinking of ya guy. You will not wanna miss this.” The announcement ends the mystery that started Friday when Charlotte Flair revealed that she and Cody Rhodes would be sitting down with Jacob Heyman alongside an unnamed special guest. Heyman Hustle TV had already started teasing the project on October 8, asking why The Roundtable would show a side of Cody Rhodes that fans had never seen before. The interview also comes as Cody has been opening up about his life outside the ring. He recently admitted that he’s become increasingly isolated from the WWE locker room , while Charlotte has continued carving out her own legacy beyond her father’s legendary wrestling career. Fans won’t have to wait much longer to see what these four discussed. Heyman Hustle TV is scheduled to release the official trailer on Monday, October 19, at 6:45 PM ET, with the complete episode premiering Wednesday, October 21. title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller
raw_title: Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-19 12:02:00 Ospreay Survives Eight-Man Gauntlet War to Keep AEW Gold at WrestleDream Will Ospreay walked out of WrestleDream on Sunday, October 18, 2026, still holding the AEW World Championship after beating seven opponents in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The stipulation forced Ospreay into a brutal two-stage format, starting as a gauntlet with staggered entrances before shifting into a 15-minute scored-fall period once eight men had entered. It was a chaotic, physically demanding structure that tested every competitor in the field. Ospreay drew the first entrance, meaning he would have to face all seven challengers to keep his title. Konosuke Takeshita came in second, followed by Ospreay's United Empire teammate 'Speedball' Mike Bailey as the third entrant. Bailey, a Canadian wrestler, was among the group chasing the title before Takeshita pinned him to eliminate him from advancing to the second stage. Ricochet entered fourth, and Darby Allin, the TNT Champion, came in fifth carrying a table that would factor into the match later. International Champion Kazuchika Okada arrived sixth, and Adam Copeland made his entrance as the seventh competitor shortly after Bailey's elimination. Joe pulled level with Allin and Ospreay by locking in the Coquina Clutch on Ospreay, then went for another Musclebuster before Copeland speared him out of it to claim his first fall of the match. Copeland then equalized again with a spear on Ricochet with just over a minute remaining, and a follow-up spear on Okada briefly put him in position to walk away as champion. With Copeland's retirement plans looming and Ospreay now having survived one of AEW's most grueling title defenses yet, the promotion heads into its next chapter with its World Championship picture wide open for fresh challengers.

llm_long: Chad Gable has explained the real purpose behind the creation of the El Grande Americano character. He stated that the character was developed solely to generate heat and was never intended to be presented as a comedic act.

Gable noted that while the character may have included ridiculous elements, its core aim was not to be 'ha-ha funny.' He emphasized that entertaining the audience was a secondary aspect but not the primary goal.
According to Gable, the character was designed in a mean-spirited way to take jabs at luchadores. This approach was meant to draw negative reactions from the crowd rather than laughs.

title: On the Record: Vince Russo Blasts WWE Agents Over Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing at Live Event
raw_title: Vince Russo Blasts WWE Agents Over Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing at Live Event
summary_src: Bron Breakker’s nasty neck landing at a recent WWE live event has Jonathan Coachman wondering why the spot was happening in the first place.
body: Speaking on The Coach & Bro Show , Coachman reacted to footage of Breakker crashing down around his neck and upper body during WWE’s October 17 live event. Breakker was attempting his top-rope Frankensteiner on Knight when things went wrong, leading to the frightening landing. Coachman admitted he couldn’t tell exactly what was supposed to happen. However, if Knight made the mistake that caused Breakker’s fall, he believes nearly injuring somebody WWE views as a major star is exactly the kind of thing that can create backstage heat. “Not quite sure if he was supposed to land there or whatever was supposed to happen. Someone’s getting heat for that, and I’m guessing it’s LA Knight. That’s the kind of stuff, if indeed it was his fault and you almost hurt one of the cash cows, that’s a way to get heat. I’m not saying he has it.” Coachman was careful not to claim Knight actually has backstage heat, since he doesn’t know who was responsible for the spot going wrong. His bigger problem was Breakker attempting the move at all during a live event. Breakker regularly uses the Frankensteiner, but Coachman already considers it dangerous. With Breakker working late on the card and the ring potentially getting slick as the show went on, he couldn’t understand why the risk was necessary at a non-televised event. “If you’re Breakker, and I know you do that move — that move, which I think is dangerous — and he’s doing it, he’s always on at the end of the show, and everything is slick, why are we doing that move in front of 6,000 people in Hawaii at a house show?” Vince Russo took the conversation in a different direction and put more of the responsibility on WWE’s producers and agents. Russo argued that the mentality backstage has changed from the days when protecting important talent was treated as protecting the company’s ability to make money. According to Russo, agents also don’t necessarily know everything wrestlers plan on doing during their matches anymore. Even when they do, he doesn’t believe most producers today approach risky spots with the same business-first mentality he remembers from previous generations. “Number one, this isn’t the way it used to be, where the talent was in on the entire match. So there’s a lot going on in the match that the agents don’t even know about. title: Federal Court Rejects WWE McMahons Constitutional Challenge
raw_title: Federal Court Rejects WWE, Mcmahons' Constiutional Challenge In Ring Boys Lawsuit
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS FEDERAL COURT REJECTS WWE, MCMAHONS' CONSTIUTIONAL CHALLENGE IN RING BOYS LAWSUIT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 15:22:00 The following press release was issued: Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case DiCello Levitt Represents Survivors as Federal Court Upholds Application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act, Allowing Claims Against WWE and the McMahons to Proceed In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023, which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler, a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. The WWE Ring Boys sexual abuse lawsuit alleges that WWE employees, including ringside announcer and ring crew chief Melvin Phillips Jr., recruited underage boys to assist with wrestling events and used their positions to groom, exploit, and sexually abuse them. The plaintiffs further allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The U.S. District Judge in Maryland issued a 26-page opinion upholding the state's Child Victims Act of 2023. The law removed time limits for civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse.
The ruling allows the survivors' claims against WWE and the McMahons to move forward. It follows an earlier court decision that largely denied the defendants' initial motions to dismiss.
The lawsuit alleges that WWE employees recruited underage boys to work at wrestling events. Those employees are accused of using their positions to groom and sexually abuse the minors.
The plaintiffs claim that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse. They further allege that no reasonable steps were taken to prevent it.

body: On Monday, TNA Wrestling officially announced the signing of Shotzi Blackheart. Asked if she’s looking forward to doing weekly TV in TNA, Shotzi replied, “That’s what really excites me because that’s my favorite part of pro wrestling, the storytelling and how wild the stories get. If you saw the last episode of TNA, I have a little bond with Rosemary and Allie. I’m excited to see where that goes on television. I’m looking forward to having a lot of fun and focusing on a storyline.” Fans can learn more about Shotzi’s signing by clicking here .
