title: End of an Era: Keith Lee’s AEW Status Gets Backstage Update Three Years After Last Match — Report
raw_title: Keith Lee’s AEW Status Gets Backstage Update Three Years After Last Match — Report
body: 0 A new backstage update has shed light on Keith Lee ‘s current status with All Elite Wrestling. In June 2026, reports emerged that AEW had discussed bringing Lee back to television several months earlier. However, those discussions did not lead to a return, and no timeline was provided for his comeback. A subsequent report in July suggested that people within the wrestling industry believed Lee might have retired. However, Lee has not publicly announced his retirement from professional wrestling. During the latest Fightful Select Q&A, via EWrestlingNews , Sean Ross Sapp stated that AEW has no current creative plans for Lee. The update comes as the former WWE star continues to remain away from in-ring competition. Lee last wrestled on the December 23, 2023, episode of AEW Collision: Holiday Bash, where he defeated Brian Cage. He was scheduled to face Swerve Strickland at AEW Worlds End later that month but was pulled from the card after failing to receive medical clearance. Dustin Rhodes replaced him in the match. In early 2024, Lee underwent two surgeries after dealing with health issues that had affected him for an extended period. He subsequently remained absent from AEW programming, leaving his wrestling future uncertain. In September, Lee made a rare social media appearance after nearly a year away from the platform. He shared a photograph alongside Darius J. Wright, a self-described consciousness explorer who promotes alternative spiritual beliefs. The post prompted discussion among fans about Lee’s apparent association with Wright. The post Keith Lee’s AEW Status Gets Backstage Update Three Years After Last Match — Report appeared first on Wrestlezone .

llm_long: A U.S. District Judge ruled that Maryland's Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the lawsuit filed by former WWE ring boys. The decision allows the case to proceed to the discovery phase, where depositions will be conducted and evidence exchanged. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish future deadlines.

The ruling does not determine whether the alleged abuse occurred or if the defendants bear responsibility. The case remains several months away from any potential trial. The ring boys had previously overcome a motion to dismiss in May that reduced the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven.

Claims by two plaintiffs continue against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs proceed with claims against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. The former ring boys allege abuse in multiple states but claim some of the incidents took place in Maryland.

Maryland enacted the Child Victims Act in 2023, removing time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving child sexual abuse. Without the law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs' claims would have expired years earlier. Maryland's state Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025 under the state constitution.

The defendants challenged the law on U.S. Constitutional grounds, specifically arguing it violated due process rights under the Fourteenth Amendment by eliminating protections from old lawsuits. The federal judge determined that the U.S. Constitution grants states broad authority over lawsuit deadlines.

The show kicked off with the Hardys, Matt & Jeff, who acted as guest general managers of the show, in honor of their 35th year in the pro wrestling business. The Hardys talked about their own legacy, but then put the shine on other newly crowned champions starting with new X-Division Champion Amazing Red, followed by new TNA World Champion Leon Slater. The Nemeths were backstage complaining about their match against each other, booked by the Hardys. Breakdown: With the episode of Impact being “booked” by the Hardys, I expected some wacky pairings and match concepts. In this short backstage segment, the Nemeth brothers came at odds when Nic Nemeth assumed his younger brother, Ryan, would take the fall in their match later in the evening. I’m not sure what they are expecting to achieve with this, but perhaps they are moving away from the Nemeths as a tag team. Santino Marella was backstage, enjoying his night off, when he was interrupted by The System. The System demanded a spot on the show, but Santino declared he was on vacation. Bear Bronson drew an issue with Eddie Edwards’ defense of Ricky Sosa. Breakdown: A split of the System may be coming soon and I can get behind that. The TNA Tag Team Champions, Nic & Ryan Nemeth, were booked by The Hardys to face off against each other on Impact this week with a stipulation that if they one intentionally took the fall, the Nemeths would be stripped of the tag titles. After avoiding contact with each other, The Hardys would appear on the entrance ramp to reiterate that the Nemeths would be stripped of the titles if they refused to fight each other. Nic Nemeth would score the victory over Ryan Nemeth shortly thereafter. Nic Nemeth complained that he was not included in the TNA World Title number one contenders ladder match. Expressions demanded The Hardys give AJ Francis a shot at the TNA World Championship. The Hardys countered by giving Francis & Expressions a match against the Hardys. Harley Hudson told The Righteous that she wanted to accompany them to the ring for the match against Syx, but they refused to allow her to join them. A match booked by the Hardys as a face-off of two of the Hardys’ recent rivals featured The Righteous and Syx in a table match. body: Almost a year ago, rumors emerged about AEW stars Mike Bailey and MVP feuding with each other; however, the rumors were later refuted. However, the Hurt Syndicate member refuted the claim and called Bailey one of the “nicest guys.” Now, recently, speaking to The Wrestling Classic , Bailey opened up and shared more about the origins of the feud rumors. “ It started with a story that we both saw online, and we’re both like, ‘What the f**k is this?’ “ It’s the most ridiculous premise on earth, right,” Bailey said. “These two pro wrestlers who are battling in the ring. Kevin Knight and I literally had a match with them at All In for the AEW World Tag Team Championships, and people are like, ‘Oh, I’m hearing rumors that these two don’t like each other.’ And it’s like, ‘What do you make of that?’ “ The story had just gotten a lot of traction because there are some circles online who revel in that kind of stuff. And we’re like, ‘Well, we should address it. We should do something about it.’ Ever since the humorous backstage video between Bailey and MVP came out and went viral, Bailey claimed that their greeting each other with a “f**k you” has become a running gag between them. summary_src: Ludwig Kaiser just took a loss in court. The WWE Superstar’s attempt to get his misdemeanor battery charge thrown out was denied on October 19, and newly updated court records reveal that Kaiser personally took the stand during the hearing.
body: According to court records obtained by Ringside News , the judge denied Kaiser’s motion to dismiss following Monday’s hearing in Orlando, Florida. The ruling means the battery case against Kaiser, whose real name is Marcel Barthel, will continue, with a pretrial conference now scheduled for December 17, 2026. And the hearing wasn’t just a quick appearance before the judge. The court docket confirms that Kaiser was sworn in and testified as a defense witness, while Richard Reap, the man accusing him of battery, also took the stand for the prosecution. The state also introduced evidence during the proceedings, including a CD admitted as State’s Exhibit 1 and four photographs entered as a composite exhibit marked State’s Exhibit 2. The docket doesn’t explain what the CD contains or what the photographs depict. The court also invoked the rule of sequestration, a procedure generally used to keep witnesses from hearing each other’s testimony before taking the stand. As Ringside News previously covered , Kaiser was arrested in May following an April 23 confrontation with Reap at an Orlando apartment complex. Reap accused Kaiser of punching and pushing him during an argument, while Kaiser’s legal team maintained that he was acting in self-defense. Kaiser’s attorneys had filed a motion seeking dismissal under Florida’s Stand Your Ground law , arguing that Reap was the aggressor and that Kaiser acted to protect himself and Bazarte. The defense also accused Reap of making threats involving Immigration and Customs Enforcement. For now, Kaiser is still facing the misdemeanor battery case, and his next scheduled court date is December 17. With both Kaiser and his accuser already having testified and the judge refusing to toss the charge, this legal battle is far from finished. title: Evolution of Triple Threat Matches in Pro Wrestling
raw_title: THEN, NOW, FOREVER – Triple Threat Matches: The Rock vs. Undertaker vs. Kurt Angle, Brock Lesnar vs. John Cena vs. Seth Rollins, more
body: Because of their frequency in contemporary pro wrestling, it’s hard to imagine that once upon a time, a triple threat match, triangle match, or three-way dance was a special attraction that happened very rarely. I remember when I started watching ECW in 1997. They talked about a mythical match dubbed The Night the Line Was Crossed. The match was special and talked about as something extraordinary, which intrigued me as a fan for several reasons. First, because of the three wrestlers involved: Sabu, Shane Douglas, and Terry Funk. Second, the match went to a 60-minute draw. Third, it was a three-way dance, something that was still very rare at the time. Over the last 20 years, the triple threat match has increased in frequency to the point that it is no longer a special attraction. It has become increasingly commonplace, frequently appearing on WWE television every week. Many fans complain that the triple threat match has become too common and is often used as a crutch to ensure a protected wrestler doesn’t have to take the fall. However, a well-designed and well-executed three-way match can still be a work of art. In fact, I would argue that some of the best matches in WWE history have been triple threat matches. What makes a triple threat different, and what makes one special? With three wrestlers involved, the pacing is often faster, and the action can remain nearly nonstop while still allowing sufficient time for selling. Adding another competitor also increases the chances of an upset or a surprise finish. Near falls can become more dramatic, further emphasizing the unpredictability of the contest. As with any match stipulation, there are good versions of triple threat matches that are booked for the right reasons and executed well, and there are bad versions that feel like little more than a watered-down singles match. Sometimes, a triple threat match diminishes a feud that would have been more important and substantial as a one-on-one contest. In other words, the whole can become less than the sum of its individual parts. In this week’s article, I’ll look at three triple threat matches that exemplify the stipulation done right. Chaos is the one word that could describe the WWF Championship picture during the first eight months of 2002. By the time Brock Lesnar won the championship at SummerSlam, he had become the sixth WWE Champion of the calendar year. Some chaos is good because it creates unpredictability and a sense that anything can happen. However, too much chaos can be detrimental. When the boat is constantly rocking, it’s hard to stay on your feet and pay attention. None of the competitors is able to maintain control for long, and the match never settles into a predictable rhythm. One of the things that made this match stand out at the time was the relatively rare sight of wrestlers stealing one another’s finishers. While that has become commonplace in contemporary wrestling, this was one of the earliest examples I can remember seeing
summary: Triple threat matches were once rare special attractions as seen in ECW's 1997 Night the Line Was Crossed bout featuring Sabu, Shane Douglas and Terry Funk that ended in a 60-minute draw. Over the past two decades the format has become commonplace on WWE television and is frequently criticized for being overused as a booking device to protect certain wrestlers from taking a loss. The piece examines multiple notable examples from wrestling history.

title: Judge Denies Ludwig Kaiser's Motion To Dismiss Battery Case
raw_title: Judge denies Ludwig Kaiser’s motion to dismiss battery case
summary_src: The battery case against WWE star Ludwig Kaiser is moving forward after a judge denied his motion to dismiss.
body: The battery case against WWE star Ludwig Kaiser is moving forward after a judge denied his motion to dismiss. A hearing regarding the motion was scheduled for today (October 19), and court records list the motion as being “denied.” A pre-trial conference is scheduled for December 17, 2026, where the two sides will attempt to figure out a resolution or decide if the case is going to trial. Kaiser’s defense was attempting to get the misdemeanor battery charge against him dismissed under Florida’s “Stand Your Ground” law. The argument was that Kaiser was justified in using the amount of force he used against the alleged victim (Richard Reap) because he reasonably believed it was necessary to protect himself and his girlfriend Andre Bazarte from “imminent use of unlawful force.” The case stems from an April incident between Kaiser and Reap at the Orlando, Florida apartment complex they lived at. Both sides agree that Kaiser and Bazarte were being affectionate toward each other in an elevator, but their stories differ from there. Reap claims he told the couple to “please have some manners,” which led to Kaiser attacking him. Kaiser says Reap swore at him and Bazarte, along with making a racist remark about calling ICE on Bazarte. Kaiser admits that he did push Reap during their confrontation but says he only did so after Reap aggressively came toward him. In Kaiser’s version of events, he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him. Kaiser says he left the area with Bazarte before things could escalate further than that. It’s listed that a CD and four photos were entered into evidence by the state, with those presumably being the elevator surveillance footage and photos of Reap. The original arrest report said police viewed surveillance video of the incident and saw Reap being punched and pushed, and they also observed a scratch on Reap’s head in person. Reap has obtained his own attorney who specializes in personal injury, which could indicate that he’s considering a civil suit against Kaiser. This legal situation has coincided with the most successful period of Kaiser’s WWE career so far, earning high praise for his work as El Grande Americano in Lucha Libre AAA. raw_title: WWE Not in Talks to Extend Saudi Arabia Deal Beyond WrestleMania 43
summary_src: WWE may be getting ready to hit the brakes on making any new long-term commitments to Saudi Arabia.
body: “#WWECrownJewel is happening because @TKOGrp and @WWE still have money to collect on prior site-fee commitments and need to secure the deposit tied to #WrestleMania43.” So Crown Jewel going ahead doesn’t necessarily mean WWE is already planning the next round of Saudi shows. In fact, Avignon claims the opposite is happening behind the scenes right now. “I’m told there haven’t been meaningful talks about renewing or extending the Riyadh Season relationship beyond the current commitments.” That’s where things get especially interesting considering everything happening in the region. Political and security tensions have been escalating, and Avignon believes TKO executives Ari Emanuel and Mark Shapiro are more interested in finishing the business they already have than signing WWE up for anything else right now. “With political tensions in the region escalating, it looks like Ari Emanuel and Mark Shapiro are trying to finish the existing business, collect what’s owed, and avoid locking WWE into anything new for now.” Basically, the claim is that WWE isn’t walking away from a pile of money that’s already on the table, but TKO also doesn’t appear eager to immediately put more WWE events on that table. Once WrestleMania 43 is finished, the company could have a much bigger decision to make. That doesn’t mean TKO itself is done doing business in Saudi Arabia. Avignon noted that Zuffa Boxing still has a relationship there, so this isn’t being framed as the company completely packing its bags and leaving the market. “Saudi Arabia still has the @Zuffa_Boxing relationship, so TKO isn’t exactly walking away from the market.” “This looks more like WWE finishing the chapter already on the books before deciding what comes next.” The timing certainly isn’t great for WWE’s Saudi relationship. Crown Jewel is scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, while recent attacks and travel disruptions have already created questions about how WWE will safely get its wrestlers, staff and production operation into and out of the country. The U.S. State Department has also warned Americans in the Middle East about potential flight cancellations , airspace closures and further travel disruptions. King Khalid International Airport has shown signs of returning to operation following a lengthy shutdown, but the situation remains anything but normal. None of this means WWE has decided to pull out of Saudi Arabia once WrestleMania 43 is over. The key part of Avignon’s report is simply that meaningful extension talks apparently aren’t happening right now, which is pretty notable considering how important Saudi events have become to WWE’s business over the years. For now, WWE appears to still have money to collect and shows to run before it can close the book on anything. Once those obligations are handled, however, what happens next between WWE and Riyadh Season suddenly looks a lot less certain.htt H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade
summary: The latest: #WWECrownJewel is happening because @TKOGrp and @WWE still have money to collect on prior site-fee commitments and need to secure the deposit tied to #WrestleMania43. So Crown Jewel going ahead. None of this means WWE has decided to pull out of Saudi Arabia once WrestleMania 43 is over.

title: Will Ospreay Calls Out Absent MJF Over Title Belt

summary_src: AEW Men's World Champion Will Ospreay addresses the absent MJF flaunting his own World Title belt, while calling himself the Real AEW World Champion
body: "What are you going to do to solve this problem?" Ospreay said to Khan. "There's a governing body that hands these out, there's a whole team around this thing, and he can just walk in with the belt?" "Where has he walked into?" Khan said. "He hasn't been here!" "Oh yeah, to be fair, he's been hiding away," Ospreay said. "Let him go there. If he ever wants to come out and find out who the real champion is, he knows where I am. B***h." MJF has been away from AEW since All In, where he came up short in winning a guaranteed World Title shot in the Casino Gauntlet match won by rival Andrade El Idolo. Instead, MJF has set his sights on New Japan Pro Wrestling, calling out G1 Climax winner Ryohei Oiwa for a match and promising to defend the "actual" AEW World Title. Despite that, many have expected that MJF will return to AEW by the end of the year and renew his feud with Ospreay, whom MJF defeated to win the AEW International Championship on 2024 episode of "Dynamite" before Ospreay regained the title at All In .

title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s Backstage Reaction to Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing
raw_title: WWE’s Backstage Reaction to Bron Breakker’s Scary Neck Landing
summary_src: Bron Breakker’s scary neck landing looked like the kind of thing that could get somebody in serious trouble backstage, but apparently WWE isn’t playing the blame game here. In fact, the word backstage is basically to no-sell the whole thing, hope Breakker is fine and move on.
body: During a recent Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC of WrestleVotes were asked what WWE’s reaction was after Breakker’s nasty fall at the October 17 live event. According to WrestleVotes, people backstage don’t seem interested in turning the accident into a bigger story than it already is. “People backstage are like, ‘Let’s no-sell this a little bit and hope he’s done.’” Breakker was teaming with Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta when everything went wrong. He tried going for his usual top-rope Frankensteiner on Knight, but Knight slipped out and Breakker came crashing down around his neck and upper body. It looked brutal, and the referee immediately went over to check on him. Breakker somehow kept going and finished the match, but there still hasn’t been an official announcement from WWE about whether he suffered an injury. WrestleVotes believes Breakker was almost certainly checked out after the match. At the same time, WWE apparently wants to get past the whole thing pretty quickly rather than keep drawing attention to it. “I’m sure there were medical personnel checking on him. But at the same time, they want to get over this quickly.” “It was a house show — it was probably a simple sort of mistake. There’s no heat on anybody.” For now, WWE apparently wants this to be nothing more than one very scary house show mistake. Nobody’s getting blamed, nobody’s catching heat, and if Breakker is okay, it sounds like the company would be more than happy to put the whole thing behind them. llm.headline: Ludwig Kaiser Motion To Dismiss Battery Case Denied

llm_long: A judge denied a motion to dismiss the battery case against WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser. The hearing on the motion took place on October 19 and court records show it was denied. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17 2026 to determine whether the case will proceed to trial or reach a resolution.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. According to Kaiser he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him and instead left the area with his girlfriend. Police reports indicate surveillance video showed Kaiser punching and pushing Reap and that Reap had a visible scratch on his head.

The state entered a CD and four photos into evidence believed to be elevator surveillance footage and images of Reap's injuries. Reap has retained a personal injury attorney which may signal plans for a civil suit against Kaiser.

title: Legal Watch: Reason Behind Montez Ford’s WWE Absence Amid Lawsuit
raw_title: Reason Behind Montez Ford’s WWE Absence Amid Lawsuit
summary_src: Montez Ford’s WWE absence suddenly looks a lot less mysterious. With Ford now facing a lawsuit over his viral RAW interaction with a security guard, some fans naturally wondered if that’s why he’s disappeared from television, but apparently the two have nothing to do with each other.
body: During a recent Q&A, WrestleVotes was asked straight up whether Ford’s time away was connected to the lawsuit. According to the backstage word they’ve received, Ford is actually off television because he and Bianca Belair recently welcomed a new addition to their family. “Montez Ford and Bianca Belair recently welcomed an addition to their family. So, according to people we speak to, that’s the reason he’s off TV.” WrestleVotes then addressed the lawsuit itself and noted that WWE managed to keep the situation pretty tightly under wraps before it eventually became public. “This lawsuit was kept as quiet as it could be before it broke.” The lawsuit was filed by Noel Lucas, an off-duty Cook County Sheriff’s officer who was working security during the July 6 episode of Monday Night RAW . Lucas is suing Ford, WWE and WWE subsidiary Event Services, LLC over Ford’s interaction with him during The Street Profits’ entrance. Lucas alleges Ford performed an unwanted sexualized “lap dance” directly in front of him. The lawsuit includes 14 counts, including assault, battery, intentional infliction of emotional distress and alleged violations of the Illinois Gender Violence Act. Things got even more attention after another camera angle of the incident surfaced . That footage puts Lucas’ reaction in clearer view, showing him sitting almost completely still during the interaction before giving a blank stare and shaking his head once Ford moved away. Apparently, that’s not the case. WrestleVotes’ backstage word is that Ford’s absence is about his family, while the lawsuit is an entirely separate situation that happened to become public while he was already away. title: On the Record: Billy Gunn says Triple H calling AEW a “pissant company” was a “dick move”
raw_title: Billy Gunn says Triple H calling AEW a “pissant company” was a “dick move”
body: WWE Hall of Famer Billy Gunn spoke with Kenny McIntosh in an interview published to the Inside The Ropes YouTube channel. Here is an excerpt… McIntosh: “In January 2019, you signed with AEW, the new company that was starting up. Then, that April, you went into the WWE Hall of Fame with D-Generation X. Of course, the crowd started chanting for AEW, and Hunter [Triple H] had to get on the microphone and say Vince [McMahon] would buy that ‘pissant company’ just to fire you again. I know you’ve said you’ve let it go, but in the moment, or when you went backstage afterward, was there a conversation about what that was all about, or did you just accept it for what it was?” Gunn: “No, because I knew it was coming. I kind of knew they were going to do something about AEW because it was hot at the time, and I was there. They were all wondering how I got to go there, and that was because Tony Khan was super cool. They were going to stick us in, so I went and asked him, and he said, ‘100%.’ He said, ‘Of course you can. I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were going to do, but I knew they were going to do something. I also knew that Hunter was going to have something to say about it. Once I prepared myself for that, I just let it go. The only one who got hurt out of that whole deal was him. I don’t want to say it, but it was a dick move. It was kind of an attempt to save face, and you didn’t need to because it was going to happen. That’s the wrestling business. That’s what we do, and that’s what they like to stir up. When you have somebody in another company, and I’m not trying to be egotistical, but I’m sure a lot of people didn’t think I was going to make it because I worked for another company. Then, when you see me, they have to do something. It’s like an unwritten rule in a book: if another guy is in another company, we have to say something and do something.”

title: Ring Boy Lawsuit Advances Against WWE
raw_title: Ring boy plaintiffs get ‘significant victory’ as lawsuit against WWE, McMahons moves forward
summary_src: The “ring boy” plaintiffs suing WWE, TKO, and Vince & Linda McMahon got a “significant victory” in court today as their lawsuit was allowed to continue. Post Wrestling reports that federal judge James K.
body: The “ring boy” plaintiffs suing WWE, TKO, and Vince & Linda McMahon got a “significant victory” in court today as their lawsuit was allowed to continue. Post Wrestling reports that federal judge James K. Bredar ruled on October 19 that the Maryland Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the case . The suit from the seven anonymous plaintiffs will now move into the discovery phase ahead of a potential trial, which Post Wrestling says would still be at least several months away. The lawsuit concerns WWE’s ring boy scandal of the 1980s and 1990s, where former ring announcer Mel Phillips is accused of having recruited teenagers to the ring crew for the purpose of sexually abusing them. All of the plaintiffs have alleged abuse by Phillips. One also alleges that he was abused by Pat Patterson, while another says they were sexually harassed by Terry Garvin. In 2023, the Maryland Child Victims Act was passed and allowed for victims of childhood sexual abuse to bring civil lawsuits no matter how long ago the alleged abuse happened. WWE, TKO, and the McMahons, in their attempt to get the lawsuit dismissed, argued that their constitutional rights relating to due process were being violated. With the alleged abuse having happened decades ago and with key figures like Phillips, Patterson, and Garvin being deceased, WWE, TKO, and the McMahons said it would be too difficult to litigate the case. Judge Bredar admitted that the timeframe could make it difficult to gather evidence but said the Maryland Child Victims Act was a rational way to address the statute of limitations concerning childhood sexual abuse claims. Greg Gutzler, the lead attorney for the plaintiffs, said after today’s ruling: Post Wrestling says WWE, TKO, and the McMahons did not immediately respond to a question from the outlet regarding whether they plan to appeal Bredar’s decision. The case, centered on alleged sexual abuse of teenagers working as ring crew in the 1980s and 1990s by Mel Phillips with additional claims against Pat Patterson and Terry Garvin, will now enter the discovery phase. Per the Wrestling Observer, the development represents a significant victory for the plaintiffs with a potential trial still months away.

llm_long: A U.S. District Judge ruled that Maryland's Child Victims Act is constitutional as applied to the lawsuit filed by former WWE ring boys. The decision allows the case to proceed to the discovery phase, where depositions will be conducted and evidence exchanged. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish future deadlines.

The ruling does not determine whether the alleged abuse occurred or if the defendants bear responsibility. The case remains several months away from any potential trial. The ring boys had previously overcome a motion to dismiss in May that reduced the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven.

Claims by two plaintiffs continue against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs proceed with claims against Vince McMahon, WWE, and TKO. The former ring boys allege abuse in multiple states but claim some of the incidents took place in Maryland.

Maryland enacted the Child Victims Act in 2023, removing time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving child sexual abuse. Without the law, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs' claims would have expired years earlier. Maryland's state Supreme Court upheld the Act in 2025 under the state constitution.

The defendants challenged the law on U.S. Constitutional grounds, specifically arguing it violated due process rights under the Fourteenth Amendment by eliminating protections from old lawsuits. The federal judge determined that the U.S. Constitution grants states broad authority over lawsuit deadlines.

title: Comeback Watch: Why Jordynne Grace Still Hasn’t Made Her WWE TV Return
raw_title: Why Jordynne Grace Still Hasn’t Made Her WWE TV Return
summary_src: Jordynne Grace has been missing from WWE television for months, but apparently fans shouldn’t read that as a sign she’s heading out the door. The latest backstage word is much simpler — WWE just doesn’t have a creative spot for her right now.
body: During a recent WrestleVotes Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC were asked what’s actually going on with Grace and when fans might see her again. Joey said the specific thing he’s heard recently is that Grace simply isn’t included in WWE’s current creative plans. “The thing that I’ve heard recently is she’s not in the creative plans. That doesn’t mean they don’t want plans for her.” Joey pointed to just how crowded the women’s side of SmackDown has become. WWE already has several ongoing stories eating up television time, and with the show back to two hours, somebody inevitably gets squeezed out. “But when you look at where she is on the women’s roster, they’ve got full-blown stories. They’ve got Fatal Influence, Charlotte’s group, Jade Cargill’s group — that’s one story. They’ve got Tiffany with the briefcase. They’ve got Nikki and Paige and Chelsea Green — that’s another story.” For Joey, Grace’s disappearance isn’t some huge mystery or indication that WWE has suddenly soured on her. He believes it’s basically a numbers problem when WWE only has so much television time to spread around. “Numbers thing. How many different female stars can you feature on a two-hour SmackDown? Someone can’t always be featured, and she unfortunately falls under that category.” TC then pushed back on any idea that Grace could be on her way out of WWE. Based on the people he’s spoken with, that’s not the impression he’s getting at all. “She isn’t on her way out — that’s not the sense based on the people I have spoken to.” Grace hasn’t exactly been sitting around waiting for the phone to ring, either. She recently spent several weeks secretly preparing for a bodybuilding competition , something TC believes WWE may simply be allowing her to finish before figuring out where she fits next. “It’s one of those things, like, when you’re done with the bodybuilding, we’ll see where we can plug you in where we might not need you.” TC also used Johnny Gargano as an example of how quickly things can change in WWE. Gargano went months without much happening before suddenly finding himself right back in the mix once WWE had something for him. “Look at Johnny Gargano — did nothing for months and then now finds himself in a number one contender’s match, Money in the Bank qualifying match. It happened at a moment’s notice.” That’s basically how TC sees Grace’s situation playing out as well. She might not have anything waiting for her this week, but that doesn’t mean WWE has given up on finding something. “I think they still really like her and don’t see her on her way out.” There had previously been talk about potentially pairing Grace with Ivy Nile , with vignettes filmed for the possible team and the “Iron Built” trademark connected to the idea. raw_title: C4 Wrestling Running Final Event At Preston Event Center On November 27
summary_src: C4 Wrestling is set to leave the Preston Event Center. On Monday, C4 announced that they will hold their final event at the Preston Event Center in Ottawa on November 27. The event will be their 19th anniversary show.
body: On Monday, C4 announced that they will hold their final event at the Preston Event Center in Ottawa on November 27. The event will be their 19th anniversary show. At the time, Ottawa wasn’t exactly known as a hotbed for independent professional wrestling. Over the years, the region has seen its share of promotions come and go. Some found success, but very few managed to sustain it. Many were one-off events, short-lived organizations, or groups that simply burned themselves out. When I launched C*4, my goal was simple: to bring Ottawa the best independent professional wrestling possible. It wasn’t about perceived star power. It wasn’t about superficial appearances, outdated beliefs, or an old boys club deciding what professional wrestling in this city should look like. It was about giving talented people opportunities. Allowing wrestlers to face opponents they might never otherwise have the chance to work with. Building relationships with the larger independent wrestling world. Giving local talent a platform where their work could be seen beyond Ottawa, rather than having their opportunities begin and end here. There were people who doubted us. There were people who wanted us to fail. But here we are. We made our own path. And if it all ended tomorrow, I think most would agree that C*4 has left a lasting mark, not just on professional wrestling in Ottawa, but on Canadian independent wrestling as a whole. Over the years, we’ve faced countless challenges. Some bigger than others. But we’ve always found a way forward. And now, as we prepare to enter our twentieth year, we’re facing another massive challenge. For a long time, we’ve been looking ahead to 2027 as a year of celebration. Twenty years of C*4 is something I never could have imagined when we started, and we ve been working toward making it something truly special. Unfortunately, a few months ago, we received news that completely changed those plans. Almost overnight, we went from planning how to celebrate our twentieth year to figuring out how to survive it. On November 27th, C*4 Wrestling will celebrate our 19th anniversary. It will also be our final event at the Preston Event Centre. After nine years, we will be saying goodbye to a building that has become synonymous with C*4 Wrestling. This wasn’t our decision. Due to circumstances beyond our control, continuing at Preston is simply no longer possible. That said, we understand the circumstances surrounding the situation, and we have nothing but appreciation for the years we’ve spent there. Some of the greatest nights in C*4 history happened inside those walls, and we’ll always look back on our time there fondly. Not an announcement we were looking forward to making, but here we are. You can find results from around the wrestling world at Fightful’s results section .
summary: C4 Wrestling will present its 19th anniversary event as the final show at the Preston Event Center in Ottawa on November 27. The promotion launched with the goal of delivering the best independent wrestling to the area by providing opportunities for talent, creating unique matchups and building connections with the wider independent scene. Over the years Ottawa has seen many short-lived promotions come and go while C4 sustained operations.

title: WWE’s Internal Reaction to Ilja Dragunov Joining AEW
raw_title: WWE’s Internal Reaction to Ilja Dragunov Joining AEW
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov’s jump to AEW apparently isn’t causing any hard feelings inside WWE. In fact, the latest backstage word is that people who worked with Dragunov are happy for him and WWE management isn’t holding his decision against him either.
body: During a recent WrestleVotes Q&A, JoeyVotes and TC were asked how WWE reacted to Dragunov showing up at WrestleDream and officially becoming All Elite . According to WrestleVotes, the people who know Dragunov personally were happy to see him land somewhere else. That attitude apparently goes beyond just Dragunov’s friends. WrestleVotes said there isn’t some automatic resentment backstage whenever somebody leaves WWE and decides they can make better money somewhere else. “There is no animosity when it comes to talent leaving and going to get their bag.” “We talked about how people in WWE were suggesting Sheamus go to AEW and not be disrespected by the offer he was getting from AEW. Go out there and get your money.” When it comes specifically to Dragunov, WrestleVotes said the feeling is basically the same from both sides of the curtain. His friends are happy for him, and even management apparently isn’t bitter about seeing him become part of AEW. “From that side of things, they wish him well. From the management side of things, they wish him well.” That makes Dragunov’s departure a little more interesting than simply WWE deciding it was finished with him. The latest report suggests the company would have preferred things to work out differently, but once Dragunov made his move, there wasn’t any backstage grudge over it. Dragunov officially debuted for AEW at WrestleDream after his WWE contract expired in August and visa issues delayed his arrival. Tony Khan quickly made things official afterwards, confirming that the former WWE star had signed with the company. Dragunov has since explained that he wanted a fresh environment where he could “breathe ,” find new competition and avoid feeling stuck. He didn’t specifically blame WWE for that feeling, instead framing AEW as the new landscape he needed at this stage of his career. So while Triple H apparently didn’t want to lose Dragunov, WWE isn’t treating his AEW move like some kind of betrayal. The backstage reaction sounds much more like wishing him well, letting him chase what he wants and moving on without any bad blood. title: Where Things Stand With WWE Running Another Evolution Event
raw_title: Where Things Stand With WWE Running Another Evolution Event
summary_src: WWE fans hoping Evolution would finally become an annual event probably shouldn’t get too excited. Despite the positive reaction to last year’s all-women’s PLE, the latest word is that another Evolution isn’t expected anytime soon.
body: “The only thing I can say about Evolution, going back to the first Evolution in 2018 — the running tale within WWE is the show drew lesser numbers on the WWE Network viewership, both live and replay, than most of the TakeOvers around that time, which they were not happy about.” “They seemed to get over that last year, but now it is nowhere to be found. I don’t think it’s coming soon.” TC doesn’t necessarily think that’s a bad thing either. Instead of WWE forcing Evolution onto the calendar every year, he believes spacing the shows out could actually help keep the concept feeling special. “It’s better off every couple of years, where you’re not shoehorning it, since it feels special when it pops up on the calendar. All-women’s wrestling is not everyone’s cup of tea.” Joey then got to what may be the biggest issue from WWE’s perspective — the numbers. According to him, an all-women’s event simply doesn’t attract the same level of audience as WWE’s regular major programming, making the company less interested in pouring the same resources into it. “It doesn’t draw as many eyeballs as a RAW or SmackDown or PLE does. WWE doesn’t want to put the resources in for something that isn’t going to return the same type of numbers that a standard PLE would.” That’s a pretty different picture from the optimism coming out of last year’s Evolution. Rhea Ripley openly pushed for the event to become annual , saying the women had proven what they could do and hoping fans would come away believing WWE needed to run the show every year. For now, that doesn’t appear to be happening. WWE hasn’t announced Evolution 3, and if the latest word is accurate, fans could be waiting a while before the all-women’s PLE makes another comeback. The door doesn’t sound permanently closed on Evolution, but yearly shows apparently aren’t part of the plan. WWE may instead treat the event as something that comes around every few years when the timing and business make sense. title: Ex-WWE Official Shares Honest Take on Behind-the-Scenes Content
raw_title: Ex-WWE Official Shares Honest Take on Behind-the-Scenes Content
body: The former WWE referee spent 22 years with the company and witnessed several changes. However, the company’s content, including Unreal on Netflix and LFG on A&E, has given fans a behind-the-scenes look. Fans now have a better idea of what goes into the creative aspects of WWE’s programming. Additionally, they can learn more about what the training is like for WWE superstars as they put matches together. WWE sharing behind-the-scenes content can be viewed as a sign that the company is adapting to the times. However, former referee Jimmy Korderas feels that some areas should still be protected. “I think putting it out there the way they do on shows like Unreal , it makes me question, too, because this industry is predicated on making your audience believe something that isn’t real. So is Unreal just that? It’s not real, but we’re going to make people believe it is? So maybe the greatest work of all, where they’re making people think, ‘See, I told you so,’ and ‘No, that wasn’t what it was,’ but they’re going to make you believe it.” “I’m not entirely convinced that all of what you see on that show is in fact legit, and nothing more than just another television show.” YouTube has been a platform for WWE to post vignettes and retrospectives of certain feuds. Superstars have also used X to generate additional interest. “It’s one of those things in today’s wrestling in 2026, now going into 2027, it’s completely different how you run angles. We’ve seen a lot of times on WWE where they’ll run angles on their social media, as opposed to running them on TV,” Korderas told The Game Plan . “And people would say, ‘Why wouldn’t you run it on TV? That’s where the biggest audience is.’ But now we’re finding out that some of the stuff that [WWE streams] online is getting more views than what people would have seen on television, on Netflix, or wherever.” “It makes you think, especially me, like the old head me going, ‘That should have been on TV.’ Yeah, but it’s on social media, and it got 12 million views. Maybe that was the right decision.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. He began writing for Heavy in 2025 after providing MMA coverage for Sportskeeda. title: El Grande Americano Motion To Dismiss Denied
raw_title: Latest On Criminal Case Against El Grande Americano, Wwe's Marcel Barthel
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 18:04:00 There was a hearing earlier today in Orlando, Florida related to the misdemeanor battery charge against WWE star Marcel Barthel aka Ludwig Kaiser aka El Grande Americano before the County Court of the Ninth Judicial Circuit, in and for Orange County, Florida. The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune from criminal prosecution under Florida law. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing. At the end of the hearing, Barthel's motion to dismiss was denied with a new pre-trial hearing set for 12/17. Barthel was arrested in May on charges of battery, pleading not guilty after learning of a warrant for his arrest on charges of battery and traveling from Mexico to Florida to turn himself in to authorities. A arrest affidavit stated that Orlando Police responded to an apartment complex (we are not publishing the address) at approximately 6:37 PM on 4/23 following reports of a physical altercation on the 12th floor of the building. The complainant, identified as Richard Reap, told officers that he entered an elevator around 6:30 PM and encountered Barthel alongside an unidentified woman. Reap alleged that the pair were acting in what he described as an “uncontrollably intimate” manner while inside the elevator. Reap stated that after exiting onto the 12th floor, he told the couple to “please have some manners.” According to the affidavit, Reap alleged that Barthel immediately responded by punching him multiple times, pushing him to the ground, and threatening additional violence. Barthel's attorney, in the motion to dismiss, argued that he used only non-deadly force, was lawfully present in the common area of his apartment complex, and reasonably believed his actions were necessary to protect both himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force. The motion emphasizes that Florida law does not require a person in those circumstances to retreat before defending themselves. The filing cites Florida's Stand Your Ground statutes, arguing that Barthel has established a "prima facie" claim of self-defense. Under the cited law, the defense contends the burden now shifts to the State to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Barthel was not entitled to statutory immunity. Since his arrest, Barthel's attorneys filed a motion to secure the video footage from the elevator, which one would think would prove what took place during the incident.

Barthel argued that his use of force was justified under Florida law and that he should be immune from prosecution, with both he and the accuser Richard Reap testifying. The judge denied the motion to dismiss per PWInsider, scheduling the next pre-trial hearing for December 17.

llm_long: A judge denied a motion to dismiss the battery case against WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser. The hearing on the motion took place on October 19 and court records show it was denied. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17 2026 to determine whether the case will proceed to trial or reach a resolution.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. body: Ludwig Kaiser’s attempt to get a misdemeanor battery charge dismissed was denied on Monday, per online court records. Kaiser, real name Marcel Barthel, remains in a legal battle in connection with an incident on April 23 in which he is alleged to have punched a man multiple times inside an elevator in Orlando, Florida. An affidavit says that Richard Reap, the man who they named as the one subject to the alleged assault, was attacked after telling a couple acting in an “uncontrollably intimate” way to “please have some manners.” Barthel also claimed that Reap had come toward him “aggressively raising his hands and getting very close to him.” Barthel said he pushed Reap away many times, noting that he was advancing towards him in a “threatening manner.” It was claimed that he used non-threatening force, thus defensible by law. Judge Andrew L. Cameron shot down this attempt to dismiss on Monday, records show. The Orange County Clerk of Courts database is now listing that a pre-trial conference will take place on December 17. Barthel is mainly a member of WWE’s AAA roster at the moment, portraying the masked persona El Grande Americano. He has remained on TV amid his ongoing battery case, currently holding AAA’s top title, the Mega Championship.

title: Billy Gunn on AEW’s “Brawl Out” incident: “If you’re a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit”

body: WWE Hall of Famer Billy Gunn spoke with Kenny McIntosh in an interview published to the Inside The Ropes YouTube channel. Here is an excerpt… McIntosh: “[CM] Punk debuted in 2021, and then there were these nights in wrestling that people talk about, like Montreal and All Out 2022, where Punk did the press conference and then there was an incident backstage. You were in AEW at that point. Were you seeing this stuff going on? Were you thinking, ‘What are we going to do?’ How were you looking at it as someone in AEW?” Gunn: “So, I wasn’t around for that, and I don’t watch any of that media stuff. It’s got nothing to do with me. It’s just whatever. It’s for them to talk or whatever. I knew about the incident that happened back then, which was what it was. They just have to realize that sometimes there are certain veterans who just aren’t going to put up with that sh*t, no matter what. If you’re a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. So, I think that’s what happened. I don’t know all the details. That’s between them. And, of course, the media stuff—I don’t watch that because it’s got nothing to do with me either.” McIntosh: “Back in the day, if something happened for real backstage, it would be like, ‘Let’s make an angle out of it.’ You’d work together and do something.” Gunn: “They do, but nothing like that. Vince [McMahon] had things under control really well. There’s this couple of things: I don’t have to like you to wrestle with you or work with you. I don’t have to like you. I don’t have to do anything. I just have to do business. There’d be that every speck now and then where you’d pull someone into a room. You pull them into a room, shut the door. You don’t do it out in public, and I don’t do it in front of the boys. If I have something bad to say about coaching and I’m about to lose my sh*t, I don’t do it in front of people. title: On the Record: Billy Gunn Discusses About Triple H’s AEW Comments at 2019 WWE Hall of Fame Ceremony
raw_title: Billy Gunn Talks About Triple H’s AEW Comments at 2019 WWE Hall of Fame Ceremony
body: Billy Gunn recently did an interview with Inside the Ropes where he discussed a number of topics pertaining to his involvement with WWE & AEW. As you may recall, Gunn was involved in the WWE Hall of Fame Induction ceremony in 2019 as part of De-Generation X. There was some intrigue around this due to Gunn having recently signed with AEW to be a coach. Triple H responded to some fans chanting “AEW” by saying that Vince McMahon would buy that “pissant company”, which generated some online hubbub at the time. People still do ask about it, and Gunn had the following to say: I knew it was coming. I kind of knew that they were going to do something AEW because it was hot at the time, and I was there, and they’re all wondering how I got to go there and that’s because Tony Khan was super cool, because they were going to stick us (DX) in and I went and asked and he said 100%. He said ‘Of course you can, I would never hold you back from that.’ I didn’t know what they were going to do, but I knew they were going to do something. And I also knew that if they were, that Hunter was going to have something to say about it. So once I set myself up to let all that, I just let it go, you know, and the only one that got hurt out of that whole deal was him (Triple H). Like, and I don’t want to say it, but it was just a dick move, right? It was it was kind of trying to save face and you didn’t need to because it’s going to happen. It’s the wrestling business. That’s what we do. That’s what they like to stir up. So they’re when you have somebody in another company…it’s one, they can’t believe it because I’m sure a lot of the people didn’t think I was going to make it because I did work for another company. And then when you see me and then they have to do it, it’s like an unwritten thing in a book. If another guy is in another company, we have to say something and do something. And they started chanting it (AEW) and they would…and then you get a response from the guy that’s leading the company.” If using any of the above quotes, please credit Inside the Ropes, with a h/t to 411mania.com for the transcription.

title: R-Truth Shares Positive Injury Update
raw_title: R-Truth Provides Injury Update After Concerning WWE SmackDown Scene
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » R-Truth Provides Injury Update After Concerning WWE SmackDown Scene R-Truth has shared an update on his condition following his injury on WWE SmackDown. R-Truth faced his former tag team partner Damian Priest in a singles match on last week’s WWE SmackDown. However, the bout was stopped early after he appeared to injure himself after delivering a top-rope dropkick to Priest. He stayed down on the mat after the impact, and the referee held up the X sign after checking on him. WWE star R-Truth, whose birth name is Ron Killings, took to social media to share an update on his health. He posted a photo of himself in a hospital and wrote, “I am OK. Thank you all for your support, concerns, and get well wishes. Wow, it truly feels amazing to feel and be loved. I’m grateful for you all.” The 52-year-old wrestler then seemingly joked, “On 10/16/2026, I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me; I didn’t think he was that serious… But ok, I’ll be back.” Last week’s SmackDown featured R-Truth’s first match. This was since Damian Priest turned on him on the September 11 episode in Mexico City. It was also the former 24/7 Champion’s first singles match since December 2025 . Truth and Damian Priest enjoyed a 147-day WWE Tag Team Championship run before dropping it to MFT’s Tama and Talla Tonga on the August 14, 2026, episode of SmackDown. Priest ended their partnership after failing to defeat the War Raiders for the AAA World Tag Team Championship on the September 11 episode of the blue brand. title: Lexis King Drops Brutal Zilla Fatu Diss Track Mocking His Dead Father and Prison Past
raw_title: Lexis King Drops Brutal Zilla Fatu Diss Track Mocking His Dead Father and Prison Past
summary_src: Lexis King just took his beef with Zilla Fatu to a whole new level, and apparently nothing is off-limits. The WWE NXT star dropped a diss track targeting Fatu on October 19, 2026, taking shots at everything from his tattoos and prison past to his late father, Umaga.
body: King released the music video for a track titled “Zilla Vanilla” on Twitter, complete with an ice cream truck and a catchy chorus mocking his NXT rival. But once you get past the jokes about vanilla ice cream, some of the lyrics get pretty nasty. “Zilla vanilla? You soft as a pillar. Your pops was a G, but my dad had the trigger?” King didn’t stop there. He also went after Fatu’s criminal history, making a particularly nasty joke about the six years Fatu spent behind bars. “But who were we kidding? This kid got him in prison? Six years in the pen and the soap kept on slipping?” “Your tattoos are tripping? You got no self respect? It looks like some children drew it on at your sketch?” King then followed that up with another jab about Fatu’s interactions with women. “You stay missing with women like you running in place. Last time you touched a girl, you got smacked by Grace.” The song also references Fatu’s injured hand, which ties directly into their ongoing WWE NXT storyline. King and the rest of BirthRight have been making Fatu’s life miserable ever since he refused to join their faction. “And I know why? Cause we busted your hand. And speaking of busting, that won’t be in your plans.” The music video itself takes a much lighter approach than some of the lyrics, with King performing in front of an ice cream truck while people dance around him. He even renamed his rival “Zilla Vanilla” and repeatedly mocked him for being soft. What’s pretty wild is how personal King decided to make this. Their feud started because Fatu wouldn’t join BirthRight, but now King is dragging dead relatives, prison time, and sexual jokes into a wrestling rivalry. He clearly isn’t interested in keeping things strictly about what happens inside the ring. For now, Fatu hasn’t responded to the track, but considering he already beat King once and got jumped by BirthRight afterward, he has plenty of reasons to want another shot at him. King might be having fun making music videos, but he’s also giving Fatu a whole lot more ammunition for their next confrontation. title: Ludwig Kaiser Motion To Dismiss Battery Case Denied
raw_title: WWE Star Ludwig Kaiser's Motion To Dismiss Battery Charge Denied, Per Court Records
summary_src: The motion to dismiss battery charges against WWE star Ludwig Kaiser/El Grande Americano were denied on Monday, according to court records.
body: According to Fightful , citing court records, Kaiser's motion to dismiss the case under Florida's "Stand Your Ground" law, which he filed back in July, was denied during a hearing on Monday. The outlet reported a pre-trial conference is set for December 17. With "Stand Your Ground," Florida law states that individuals can use force in self-defense, or in defense of another, if they reasonably believe it necessary to avoid the other person's "imminent use of unlawful force." In Kaiser's case, he was accompanied by girlfriend, fellow AAA star Andrea Bazarte. The alleged victim in the battery case, Richard Reap, reportedly told police that Kaiser and Bazarte were "aggressively kissing" in an elevator, and he asked them to "please have some manners." According to Kaiser, they were hugging when Reap began cursing at them and told them to have some respect "before he called ICE on that b****," referring to Bazarte. In both parties' account of the events, an altercation did take place. The incident took place in April, but Kaiser, the current AAA Mega Champion known as El Grande Americano, was not arrested until May, ahead of his mask-vs-mask match against the original El Grande Americano, Chad Gable. When Kaiser was made aware of the charges, he reportedly traveled from Mexico back to Florida to turn himself in.
summary: Per Fightful Select citing court records, a judge denied Ludwig Kaiser's July motion to dismiss his battery charge under Florida's Stand Your Ground law during a Monday hearing. A pre-trial conference is scheduled for December 17. The April incident involved Kaiser and his girlfriend AAA wrestler Andrea Bazarte in an elevator with the alleged victim Richard Reap, where both sides agree an altercation occurred after words were exchanged.

llm_long: A judge denied a motion to dismiss the battery case against WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser. The hearing on the motion took place on October 19 and court records show it was denied. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17 2026 to determine whether the case will proceed to trial or reach a resolution.

Kaiser's defense sought dismissal under Florida's Stand Your Ground law. The argument claimed he used necessary force to protect himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force by the alleged victim Richard Reap. The incident occurred in April at an Orlando apartment complex where both men lived.

Both parties agree that Kaiser and his girlfriend were being affectionate in an elevator. Their accounts diverge afterward with Reap stating he asked the couple to have manners before Kaiser attacked him. Kaiser claims Reap swore at them and made a racist remark about calling ICE on his girlfriend.

Kaiser acknowledges pushing Reap after Reap moved toward him aggressively. According to Kaiser he did not retaliate when Reap threw a soft drink bottle at him and instead left the area with his girlfriend. Police reports indicate surveillance video showed Kaiser punching and pushing Reap and that Reap had a visible scratch on his head.

The state entered a CD and four photos into evidence believed to be elevator surveillance footage and images of Reap's injuries. Reap has retained a personal injury attorney which may signal plans for a civil suit against Kaiser.

title: Judge lets WWE Ring Boys lawsuit proceed
raw_title: Federal judge allows the "Ring Boys" child sexual abuse case filed against Vince McMahon, Linda McMahon, WWE, and TKO to move forward
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) The DiCello Levitt law firm issued the following press release on Monday regarding a federal court allowing the “WWE Ring Boys” child sexual abuse litigation to move forward. In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023 , which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler , a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. The WWE Ring Boys sexual abuse lawsuit alleges that WWE employees, including ringside announcer and ring crew chief Melvin Phillips Jr., recruited underage boys to assist with wrestling events and used their positions to groom, exploit, and sexually abuse them. The plaintiffs further allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The litigation is led by DiCello Levitt’s Greg Gutzler and Adam Prom and includes Scott Gilmore , Mark A. DiCello , Bobby DiCello , and Emma Bruder , with local counsel Murphy, Falcon & Murphy. The case is John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. , Case No. 1:24-cv-03487, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland. DiCello Levitt LLP is one of the leading plaintiffs’ law firms in the United States. Nationally recognized for our work in high-stakes class actions, mass torts, and complex litigation, we have recovered more than $25 billion for clients, including individuals, businesses, and communities. We take on some of the world’s most powerful interests, pursuing justice that reshapes industries and improves lives. Built for trial, DiCello Levitt is among the few plaintiffs’ firms with a dedicated trial center, where our acclaimed trial lawyers bring both art and science to courtroom preparation and trial strategy. title: On the Record: TNA Officially Announces Signing Of Shotzi Blackheart
raw_title: TNA Officially Announces Signing Of Shotzi Blackheart
body: TNA Wrestling has officially confirmed the signing of former WWE Superstar Shotzi Blackheart, adding another established name to its women’s division. The company announced the news in a press release, noting that the signing was first reported by Busted Open on SiriusXM. Blackheart, a California native who began her professional wrestling career in 2014, previously competed in WWE, where she held the NXT Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Ember Moon. Her arrival follows appearances at TNA’s live events in Dothan, Alabama, in mid-October. In addition to confirming her signing, TNA shared 10 personal facts about Blackheart, offering fans a closer look at her interests and accomplishments outside the wrestling ring. Blackheart also studied musical theatre at the American Musical and Dramatic Academy (AMDA) in Hollywood. A passionate horror movie fan, she hopes to direct her own horror film someday. Among her wrestling accomplishments, TNA highlighted that Blackheart was named Pro Wrestling Illustrated’s 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and appeared on the magazine’s cover. The company also revealed several lesser-known details about her personal life, including her obsession with Elvis Presley and the fact that she owns a chicken farm. Another unusual accomplishment involved visiting Walt Disney World, where she managed to ride every attraction across all four theme parks in a single day. Blackheart also spoke about her heritage, stating, “I’m proudly Filipino.” One of the more memorable facts involved her wedding day, which featured both a marriage ceremony and a wrestling match. “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day,” Blackheart revealed. The announcement officially confirms Blackheart’s status with TNA following her recent appearances for the promotion. TNA has not yet disclosed additional details regarding the length or terms of her contract.
summary: The latest: the signing of former WWE Superstar Shotzi Blackheart, adding another established name to its women’s division, TNA Wrestling has officially made official. TNA shared 10 personal facts about Blackheart, offering the audience a closer look at her interests and accomplishments outside the wrestling ring.

title: On the Record: TNA Officially Confirms Shotzi Blackheart Signing
raw_title: TNA Officially Confirms Shotzi Blackheart Signing
body: Shotzi Blackheart has officially joined TNA Wrestling, adding another familiar name to the Knockouts division. TNA confirmed her signing on Monday after she appeared at last week’s television tapings in Dothan, Alabama. News of the deal was first reported by Busted Open on SiriusXM. Blackheart arrives with experience across several major promotions. She began wrestling in 2014 and held the NXT Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Ember Moon during her WWE career. She also became MLW Women’s Champion before her contract with that company expired earlier this month. MLW hopes to continue booking Blackheart for as long as her contractual arrangements allow. To introduce its newest signing, TNA shared 10 facts about Blackheart, offering fans a glimpse at her interests and achievements outside the ring: She investigates the paranormal and has travelled across America hunting ghosts for her YouTube series, CHAMBER OF HORRORS. PWI named her its 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and featured her on its cover. She rode every ride across all four Walt Disney World theme parks in a single day. Speaking about her heritage, she said: “I’m proudly Filipino.” Recalling her wedding day, she revealed: “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day.” Blackheart joins a division currently led by Knockouts World Champion Indi Hartwell. M By Elegance, also known as Maggie Lee, holds the Knockouts TV Championship, while Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler are the Knockouts Tag Team Champions. The signing comes during a difficult time for Blackheart, whose real name is Ashley Urbanski. Following the death of her brother Dean, she withdrew from CMLL’s Women’s International Grand Prix, which takes place this Friday. Marina Shafir has replaced her on Team International.
summary: Shotzi Blackheart has officially joined TNA Wrestling, adding another familiar name to the Knockouts division. Her signing on Monday after she appeared at last week’s television tapings in Dothan, Alabama, TNA made official.

body: While the world waits with bated breath to see if WWE relocates its upcoming show, it feels like an appropriate time to take the temperature of the American pro-wrestling landscape. This is the first AFP pound-for-pound power rankings of the best pro-wrestlers in AEW and WWE. While Darby Allin’s effort in Saturday’s inaugural “Clockwork Carnage” has surely affected his evaluation, there’s no shame in losing to the king. As TNT Champion, Allin has staged four successful title defenses since dethroning Kevin Knight at “All In,” scoring victories over the likes of Mark Davis, Kyle Fletcher, and the CMLL World Heavyweight Champion, Hechicero. Now, the only question is whether or not he opts to tread familiar water in Roman Reigns, or set his sights on WWE Undisputed Champion, Sami Zayn. Andrade El Idolo hasn’t lost in an All Elite Wrestling ring since April, quietly building one of the strongest bodies of work in 2026. Since dethroning Mark Davis for the AEW National Championship, Andrade has recorded six title defenses, punctuating his case on Saturday with a victory over Tommaso Ciampa . With the Casino Gauntlet contract in hand, and victories earlier in the year over the likes of Swerve Strickland and Kenny Omega, the world is Andrade’s oyster. If Jon Moxley was baptized by fire in last year’s Continental Classic, his reign as AEW Continental Champion has absolved him of all his previous sins. The WWE has a history of insisting upon itself. In the case of Oba Femi, its made the “Ruler” a walking contradiction. Right now, he’s treading water, biding his time until his long-awaited clash with Roman Reigns at next year’s “WrestleMania.” Still, it feels like he has more momentum than any wrestler in the world. The highlights of his 2026 campaign include winning the King of the Ring Tournament and retiring Brock Lesnar in Hell in a Cell. Persephone’s case is two-fold: (1) her impressive record and (2) her status as CMLL’s top women’s champion. As TBS Champion, she’s staged four successful title defenses, including last Saturday’s four-way dance with Dani Luna, Queen Aminata, and Hyan. A day later, she put her CMLL World Women’s Championship on the line, conquering AZM in Arena Mexico. Roman Reigns has only wrestled seven times in 2026. Still, it’s difficult to deny the “Tribal Chief’s” strength of schedule. With notable victories over CM Punk, Seth Rollins, and Penta; Reigns has cultivated an aura of inviolability. He is more than a man; more than an obstacle to overcome. He is a colossus. title: On the Record: Billy Gunn Recalls CM Punk & The Elite’s Backstage Clash at AEW All Out 2022
raw_title: Billy Gunn Recalls CM Punk & The Elite’s Backstage Clash at AEW All Out 2022
body: Billy Gunn, who has been with AEW since its early days, discussed the situation during an interview with Inside The Ropes . He explained that he wasn’t directly involved in the incident. Gunn said, “So I knew the incident that happened back in the thing, which was what it was, and they just have to realize that sometimes there’s certain veterans that just aren’t going to put up with that, no matter what. Right?” “And if you’re a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. So, I think that’s what happened. And I don’t know the whole details. That’s between them and then, you know, of course, the media thing that I don’t watch, ’cause it’s got nothing to do with me either.” Gunn was also asked whether real backstage disagreements could become wrestling storylines. He compared the situation to how conflicts were handled during WWE’s earlier years. Gunn explained, “They do, but nothing like that. Like, Vince had things under control really good. I don’t have to like you to wrestle with you or to work with you. Don’t have to like you. I don’t have to do anything. I just have to do business. And mostly 99.9% of the guys always did that. Right?” Gunn then described how disagreements should be resolved behind closed doors. He continued, “There’ll be that every speck now and then where you just pull them into a room, you know? You pull them into a room, you shut the door. So you don’t do it out in public, like, and I don’t do it in front of the boys. It’s just like, if I have something bad to say about coaching and I’m about to lose my I don’t do it in front of people. I take them somewhere where nobody else can hear it because it’s nobody else’s business.” He believes private conversations help prevent unnecessary tension. Gunn explained that people should resolve problems before returning to work. He added, “You pull them into a room, you shut the door, and you go, ‘All right, here we go. What are we doing?’ Like, if you got a problem, we need to fix it now. We’ll fix it now, so when we walk out the door, we don’t have a problem anymore. Right? And that’s how grown-ass people deal with sh*t. But nowadays, we don’t, and that’s sad. But there’s going to be people that are going to do that.” The post Billy Gunn Recalls CM Punk & The Elite’s Backstage Clash at AEW All Out 2022 appeared first on Wrestlezone .

body: For the first time since it was first run back in 2000, the Jersey J-Cup will take place at “The Mecca” in Ridgefield Park, New Jersey from February 20 and 21, 2027. The news was announced during JCW (Jersey Championship Wrestling) Nightmare in Bergen County event, also taking place at legendary north Jersey arena. This tournament has sported some incredible lineups. During the initial run with the original JCW, winners included Low Ki (2001), Reckless Youth (2002), Jay Lethal (2003) and Super Dragon (2004). During the NWS era, winners included Rhett Titus (2008) and R.J. Brewer (2010). After the tournament came back in 2014, notable northeast indie wrestler Chris Dickinson won the first tournament. And since its full time return in 2023, Jordan Oliver (2023), Masha Slamovich (2024 & 2025), and Charles Mason have etched their names into the winner’s ledger. As yet, the lineup for the 2027 tournament isn’t available, but that’s something to keep an eye on in the coming weeks and months. As always, we’ll aim to provide any further updates on the 2027 Jersey J-Cup as soon as we hear more.

Tony Khan and his creative team did not overthink the situation, book a shocking outcome for the sake of it, or worry too much about whether the audience would sniff out the finish. They produced the finish everyone inside Wembley Stadium wanted to see, with Ospreay capturing the title in his hometown, resulting in one of the most memorable and emotional moments in company history. Dating back to last summer, WWE has adopted a creative strategy to try and stay ahead of the audience. Most famously, it had Seth Rollins feign a knee injury to surprise fans with a Money in the Bank cash-in at the conclusion of the 2025 SummerSlam event. That works in the moment and creates buzz, but it is gimmicky and does not encourage long-term buy-in to the stories and rivalries that play out each week.
