title: Injury Update: WWE banned these 5 dangerous wrestling moves after seeing talent seriously injured
raw_title: WWE banned these 5 dangerous wrestling moves after seeing talent seriously injured
body: From the likes of Triple H tearing his quads, Mick Foley ticking off almost every injury possible, and retirement inducing neck injuries to the likes of Edge and Kurt Angle, it's safe to say things can and do go wrong in WWE. While we might see more high flyers in the modern era, there's also a limitation when it comes to certain moves that, frankly, have cost people their careers. Here, then, are FIVE dangerous wrestling moves WWE has banned over the years. Some will argue we might be set to see a return of this being used in the Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes feud but that is only because they are two of the very best around. The reason? Multiple concussions and head injuries suffered as a result of poor timing or the move simply not going as planned. One of the best things about growing up watching the Attitude Era was some of the brutal and downright dangerous steel chair shots we got to see. WWE moved to ban the head shot during the PG-era and it has remained largely the same since. Ultimately, head injuries and concussions are too costly and in the end, outside pressures have forced WWE's hand really. Anyone who saw Brock Lesnar try and fail this move against Kurt Angle at WrestleMania 20 will know exactly why this was banned. On another day, Lesnar would have broken his neck and in reality, could have died. While many of us are accustomed to seeing Triple H or Seth Rollins hit a pedigree, the early inception of the move was quite scary. Instead of the move involving falling to the mat with your chest and body breaking the fall, Triple H instead planned on lifting the arms up fully behind the back and simply planting his opponent on his head. Obviously, this move never made it to TV and WWE quickly adapted it for The Game to keep on using over his career. Another move that on rare occasions we do see. But in essence, the original piledriver has been banned ever since Stone Cold Steve Austin broke his neck and spinal cord against Owen Hart. Anyone who has watched WWE for a long time will have seen the footage and when you look back, it's amazing Stone Cold went on to wrestle again, never mind have the success he did. We still see the piledriver on the odd occasion but much like the punt, it seems reserved for only the highest level of performer. summary_src: It has been six months nearly to the day since Kairi Sane last wrestled on US soil. And it could be a while before she wrestles in America again. According to a report on Fightful Select, Sane needs to reach a deal with a US-based promotion before she can begin the process of applying for […]
body: It has been six months nearly to the day since Kairi Sane last wrestled on US soil. And it could be a while before she wrestles in America again. According to a report on Fightful Select , Sane needs to reach a deal with a US-based promotion before she can begin the process of applying for a work visa. “Kairi remains a free agent after her WWE deal expired when they released her earlier in the year,” the report reads. “Fightful Select has reported that ongoing conversations have ensued since free agency, and that she also has multiple standing offers in Japan.” “There were reports recently that the belief is that visa issues are holding up a deal, but it’s actually the opposite,” the Fightful report explains. “Kairi’s US visa has expired, and would need to either be sponsored by a wrestling company or agency for renewal. As she’s not signed by AEW yet, that hasn’t happened. Once she signs, an expedited visa can be approved in as little as 15 business days. But this isn’t a situation of waiting on the visa right now for her debut, she isn’t signed and no deal is finalized.” Sane does have one future appearance booked for American audiences. She will be taking part of Chris Jericho’s Rock N’ Wrestling Rager at Sea in November. Because the event takes place in international waters, Sane does not need a US visa to participate. Sane’s last match was a tag team match on the April 20 episode of Monday Night Raw. She teamed with Asuka in a losing effort to Iyo Sky & Rhea Ripley. Sane was signed with WWE from 2016 to 2021, and then again from 2023 until this year. She is otherwise best known for wrestling as KAIRI in Stardom.
summary: Per Fightful Select, Kairi Sane has been a free agent since her WWE release earlier this year. She requires a contract with a US-based promotion to sponsor and renew her expired work visa before she can wrestle in America again. The report notes she has multiple standing offers in Japan and that ongoing talks continue, but no deal with AEW or anyone else has been finalized.

Zayn briefly acknowledged Reigns and then started making his way to the ring. Reigns would then join Zayn for their in-ring segment. Reigns stated that it was good to see Zayn, and they hugged. The two champions started bonding because Zayn said he finally understood what Reigns was talking about when he was The Tribal Chief, specifically referring to the disrespect that champions receive and the burden that comes with being champion. Reigns went on to state that the most important title Zayn has ever held is the title of ‘Honorary Uce.’ He asked Zayn if he was there to talk about the 946 and to serve The Bloodline. Zayn responded by saying he appreciates his time in The Bloodline, but he’s the head of his own table now. Roman stated that Zayn’s belt is A title, but the belt he has is THE title. They got into a back-and-forth, and then Reigns said maybe the Undisputed WWE Title hasn’t meant anything since he lost it at WrestleMania 40. As Reigns was leaving, Mr. Money in the Bank Penta showed up and went face-to-face with Reigns. Penta then faced off with Zayn in the ring.

Zayn replied that he values his Bloodline history but now leads his own table, prompting Reigns to call his own World Heavyweight Championship THE title while labeling Zayn's Undisputed WWE Championship merely A title before their verbal exchange continued.

What did the Tribal Chief have to say about the latest in the Bloodline vs. 946 rivalry, including the latter's newest member, Carmelo Hayes? Find out the answer to that and more with this recap of the October 19 Netflix broadcast, including grades and analysis of each of the night's matches and biggest segments. WWE Champion Sami Zayn, ever desperate to be taken seriously in that role, kicked off Raw and asked the fans in San Diego who was there to "ride or die with the Last Real Good Guy." World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns, whom Zayn zipped past backstage on his way to the ring, interrupted and entered to a thunderous ovation. Chants of "OTC" greeted him as he entered the ring and came face-to-face with the former "Sami Uso." "I can't believe I'm saying this, and I might be the only one in here saying it, but it's good to see you," Reigns said. The former Bloodline teammates engaged in a mid-ring embrace before Zayn admitted to getting everything the Tribal Chief preached. The pleasantries came to an end when Reigns questioned Zayn's motivation for being there and a potential allegiance to 946. Then they verbally battled over which championship was more important. Then, the Last Real Good Guy took exception to the disrespect Reigns has shown him by not even sweating him. "Knowing your track record, you might not even have that championship come Crown Jewel," Reigns said to close out the segment. As he exited the arena, Penta arrived, a not-so-subtle reminder that the luchador has the Money in the Bank briefcase and, one day, will come for the world championship.

body: RAF13, under the Real American Freestyle banner, is Friday, Sept. 18 at the Watsco Center at the University of Miami in Coral Gables. The Bound for Glory PPV, under the TNA Wrestling banner, is Sunday, Oct. 11 at the Yuengling Center in Tampa. RAF, a new company, is the unscripted version of professional wrestling, featuring freestyle wrestling from some of the best wrestlers in the world. TNA Wrestling, in its 24th year, is one of the top scripted type pro wrestling companies in the world. Below are some video interviews I conducted to hype the companies, shows and talent. After a five-year hiatus, Kiera Hogan made her triumphant return to TNA Wrestling at TNA Lockdown in August in Chicago. Hogan was the mystery partner of Allie at TNA Lockdown in August in Chicago. She replaced an injured Rosemary to help Allie retain the TNA Wrestling Knockouts tag team titles in a steel cage by defeating The Elegance Brand (Heather by Elegance and M by Elegance) (with Mr. Elegance and The Personal Concierge). Hogan is now a 3-time TNA Wrestling Knockouts tag team champion. She also won gold twice with Tasha Steelz. As Fire, she teamed with her life partner Adrenaline (ROH's Diamante) to win the tag team titles in WOW - Women Of Wrestling, the women's pro wrestling group. TNA Wrestling is in San Antonio, Texas with back-to-back nights of action at the Boeing Center at Tech Port on Thursday and Friday, September 24-25. TNA Wrestling and Real American Freestyle interviewer and ring announcer McKenzie Mitchell is a WWE alum. Fashion meets wrestling in a first-of-its-kind book by Mitchell, which is titled "THREADS OF TRIUMPH: Professional Wrestling's Most Iconic Looks." "THREADS OF TRIUMPH" features wrestling's most intriguing costumes from the 1940s to today, including the looks of big names like "Macho Man" Randy Savage, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, The Undertaker, Shawn Michaels, Ric Flair, Rey Mysterio, Becky Lynch, Bianca Belair, and many more. A foreword by one of wrestling's best, Mercedes Moné, completes the all-star package. Mitchell, 32, is a glamorous third-generation jewelry entrepreneur from Dexter, Missouri. She marries the stunning imagery in her book with the wrestlers' thematic choices behind their outfits, including how they select every button, every swatch, to mold their persona and story. The dive into this artistry is something that hasn't been published before and will appeal to the most die-hard wrestling fans and the wrestling curious alike. Chris Jericho, a multi-time world champion in pro wrestling, dubs McKenzie's idea to write an entire book on pro wrestling fashion "a brilliant one, and this book shines brighter than the sequins on the boots I'm wearing right now!" iMPACT also airs on Sportsnet 360 in Canada and TNA+ worldwide.

title: Cody Rhodes Praises WWE's Top Pay Scale
raw_title: Cody Rhodes On WWE Pay Structure: 'That Next Level Pay Is Now Comparable With Sports'
body: During a recent interview with "Flagrant," Rhodes offered a glimpse into how WWE's pay structure has evolved by citing company President Nick Khan. "Nick Khan had a great quote about 'These guys are going to do well. These guys are going to do really well and then these couple guys, they're going to do next level.' And that next level pay is now comparable with sports," Rhodes said. "That's the part that I'm so proud of being a wrestler because when you'd hear baseball contracts and NBA contracts, and you know as a wrestler that you could go all over the world and be known and be seen, but you weren't on that level. You were on the level of penetration but not that level of income. Now, modern TKO and Nick have made it that you are." Rhodes described the money being made in the pro wrestling business as "very good," with amounts cited in WWE contracts now being guaranteed. "The American Nightmare" believes his late father, Dusty Rhodes, would have been particularly "shocked" by today's payouts. Upon returning to WWE in 2022, Rhodes propelled to the main event scene, where he went on to win the Undisputed WWE Championship on three separate occasions. He currently finds himself in a feud with Randy Orton, his former mentor in the stable known as Legacy and a 14-time world champion.

title: Drew McIntyre Maintains Ring Shape During WWE Hiatus
raw_title: Drew McIntyre details how he has stayed in ring shape during WWE absence
summary_src: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre has spent more time on the movie set than between the ropes this year, but that doesn’t mean he’s not staying in shape for his inevitable in-ring return. McIntyre talked about his busy filming schedule in an appearance on Busted Open Radio.
body: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre has spent more time on the movie set than between the ropes this year, but that doesn’t mean he’s not staying in shape for his inevitable in-ring return. McIntyre talked about his busy filming schedule in an appearance on Busted Open Radio . “I had an itch so bad that I’ve been getting back in the ring and just moving around,” McIntyre said. “Even when I was in Barcelona, I spent three months in Barcelona filming The Last Druid with Russell Crowe after I finished Highlander . I literally lived there for three months and I said, ‘I can’t do this. I gotta get in a ring.’” “One of the extras, one of the stuntmen was a local indie guy and he told me they have a ring there,” McIntyre said. “So I went down and I started just rolling around in the ring and beating up some of his guys just to get my fix.” “I feel bad for those guys,” he said. “The way I wrestle, I practice the way I play. I was beating the crap out of them with no cameras there.” McIntyre said he had also been training at Rusev’s wrestling school in Nashville. “I put a little video out hitting the ropes,” he said. “I think Bron Breakker is the only man that hits the ropes faster than me on planet Earth. And it got over eight million views on my own socials , so people are excited to see Drew come back. I miss the live fans. I miss the buzz, the adrenaline, but I am enjoying what I’m doing right now.” McIntyre won the Undisputed WWE Championship from Cody Rhodes in Germany in January of this year, but lost it back to Rhodes in March in Portland, Oregon. He then lost an unsanctioned match to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas in April and has not wrestled since.

McIntyre has also trained at Rusev's wrestling school in Nashville per the Wrestling Observer.

llm_long: Drew McIntyre has been focusing on film work this year but continues to maintain his in-ring conditioning during the hiatus. He described an intense desire to return to wrestling and began seeking opportunities to train in rings while on location.

While filming The Last Druid in Barcelona for three months following Highlander, McIntyre located a local wrestling ring through a stuntman who worked on the indie scene. He used the ring to roll around and spar with the stuntman's associates to satisfy his need for wrestling activity.

McIntyre admitted feeling remorse for the intensity of his sessions, noting that he trains as he competes and delivered heavy impacts even without cameras present. He has also been training at Rusev's wrestling school in Nashville.
A video McIntyre posted of himself hitting the ropes received over eight million views on his social media. He believes only Bron Breakker hits the ropes at a faster pace.

McIntyre expressed missing the energy from live audiences and the adrenaline of performing but stated he is currently enjoying his ongoing projects. His most recent matches were a title win over Cody Rhodes in Germany in January, a title loss to Rhodes in Portland in March, and an unsanctioned loss to Jacob Fatu at WrestleMania 42 in Las Vegas in April.

title: Legal Watch: Federal Court Rejects Wwe, Mcmahons' Constitutional Challenge In Ring Boys Lawsuit
raw_title: FEDERAL COURT REJECTS WWE, MCMAHONS' CONSTITUTIONAL CHALLENGE IN RING BOYS LAWSUIT - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS FEDERAL COURT REJECTS WWE, MCMAHONS' CONSTITUTIONAL CHALLENGE IN RING BOYS LAWSUIT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 15:22:00 The following press release was issued: DiCello Levitt Represents Survivors as Federal Court Upholds Application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act, Allowing Claims Against WWE and the McMahons to Proceed In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023, which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler, a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Anya Rune Announces Wrestling Hiatus
raw_title: Former WWE EVOLVE Star Anya Rune Announces Wrestling Hiatus
summary_src: Former WWE EVOLVE star Anya Rune is stepping away from professional wrestling, and she’s not even sure when she’ll be back.
body: Rune broke the news on social media Monday nigh t, October 19, admitting that she never imagined she’d be making an announcement like this. She also acknowledged that some fans would be disappointed, but made it clear that taking a break is something she needs to do. Rune then explained that she’s putting wrestling on hold indefinitely, hoping that spending time away might help her rediscover the passion she once had for it. “I need to take a step back from wrestling. Both for my physical and mental health. I don’t know how long this is going to last but I’m hoping to find a new love for it in the time I will be spending away. I will be keeping my social media somewhat active, it’ll just be less wrestling related content.” She didn’t sugarcoat how she’s feeling about wrestling either. While she still appreciates the opportunities and experiences the business has given her, the love she once had for it simply isn’t there right now. “I have unfortunately fallen out of love with wrestling but that doesn’t mean I don’t love everything its given me.” The announcement comes just weeks after Ringside News covered Rune’s WWE release on September 4 . She was among several talents let go from WWE’s developmental system after competing on WWE EVOLVE as part of the WWE ID program. Before signing with WWE, Rune wrestled on the independent scene under the Airica Demia name and earned a WWE ID contract in March 2026. She eventually adopted the Anya Rune character for EVOLVE, but her time with the company was cut short before she could move into a regular NXT role. Rune had also reacted to her WWE departure , thanking fans who continued to support her after she was let go. Now, barely six weeks later, she’s announcing a break from wrestling altogether. The timing is particularly unfortunate considering how recently she earned her WWE opportunity. Rune went from getting her foot in the door with the company to losing that opportunity and now stepping away from the ring in a matter of months. She hasn’t specified whether her WWE release contributed to her decision, and she hasn’t offered a timetable for returning. For now, Rune is putting herself ahead of wrestling, and she’s not making any promises about when she’ll be back. Whether this turns into a short break or something much longer remains to be seen, but she’s clearly reached a point where forcing herself to keep wrestling isn’t what she wants to do. body: Korderas admitted that he was surprised by the outcomes of both the men’s and women’s ladder matches. Tiffany Stratton and Penta won the briefcase in their respective ladder matches. As a result, they will have one year to cash in for a title match of their choosing. Stratton and Penta have both been booked strongly, particularly before the Money in the Bank PLE. However, Korderas explained why WWE may have more difficulty finding the right moment for Penta to cash in. Jimmy Korderas also explained what the coming months could look like for Tiffany Stratton and Penta. The former WWE referee believes that Stratton already has an ongoing story that could end similarly to her previous cash-in. “As for Penta, they have a year to cash in. But I wouldn’t want them carrying around the briefcase for an entire year. That’s the other thing too,” he said. “I think Penta is the one that’s going to be a challenge.” Korderas also reacted to the Money in the Bank ladder matches and felt that both matches delivered. The former WWE referee believed that Roxanne and Bron Breakker would emerge as the winners. Korderas also explained that the men’s match made it clear that WWE is very high on Penta. He noted that the company went against the norm, particularly with how it tends to book future cash-ins. “As for the men, I think a lot of people expected Bron Breakker. Cass absolutely demolished Lee with a chokeslam onto the ringside barricade before delivering a massive boot to Mysterio. Meanwhile, Page turned his attention to the Intercontinental Champion, planting Gable with a fisherman’s buster. Page wasn’t finished, either. He grabbed Gable’s Intercontinental Championship and held it up, making his intentions pretty clear. To drive the point home, Page delivered another fisherman’s buster to Gable, leaving the champion laid out after an already exhausting title defense. The attack was especially interesting considering Gable had just successfully defended his championship against two of WWE’s most accomplished high-flyers. Instead of getting a moment to enjoy his victory, he found himself on the receiving end of a beating, with Page standing tall and holding his title. Ethan Page certainly made a statement on RAW, and having Big Cass involved made the attack even more dangerous. Gable is still the Intercontinental Champion, but Page has now put himself directly in the championship picture without having to wrestle a match. title: Latest On Criminal Case Against El Grande Americano, Wwe's Marcel Barthel
raw_title: LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 18:04:00 There was a hearing earlier today in Orlando, Florida related to the misdemeanor battery charge against WWE star Marcel Barthel aka Ludwig Kaiser aka El Grande Americano before the County Court of the Ninth Judicial Circuit, in and for Orange County, Florida. The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune from criminal prosecution under Florida law. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing. At the end of the hearing, Barthel's motion to dismiss was denied with a new pre-trial hearing set for 12/17. Barthel was arrested in May on charges of battery, pleading not guilty after learning of a warrant for his arrest on charges of battery and traveling from Mexico to Florida to turn himself in to authorities. A arrest affidavit stated that Orlando Police responded to an apartment complex (we are not publishing the address) at approximately 6:37 PM on 4/23 following reports of a physical altercation on the 12th floor of the building. The complainant, identified as Richard Reap, told officers that he entered an elevator around 6:30 PM and encountered Barthel alongside an unidentified woman. Reap alleged that the pair were acting in what he described as an “uncontrollably intimate” manner while inside the elevator. Reap stated that after exiting onto the 12th floor, he told the couple to “please have some manners.” According to the affidavit, Reap alleged that Barthel immediately responded by punching him multiple times, pushing him to the ground, and threatening additional violence. Barthel's attorney, in the motion to dismiss, argued that he used only non-deadly force, was lawfully present in the common area of his apartment complex, and reasonably believed his actions were necessary to protect both himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force. The motion emphasizes that Florida law does not require a person in those circumstances to retreat before defending themselves. The filing cites Florida's Stand Your Ground statutes, arguing that Barthel has established a "prima facie" claim of self-defense. Under the cited law, the defense contends the burden now shifts to the State to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Barthel was not entitled to statutory immunity. Since his arrest, Barthel's attorneys filed a motion to secure the video footage from the elevator, which one would think would prove what took place during the incident.
summary: The latest: the hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing.

The Usos each hit suicide dives on opposite ends of the ring. Solo takes Keys into the ring to try to land the Samoan Spike, but Hayes hits him with a crowbar, just like last week. 846 begins to completely beat down the Bloodline, as Jaida shows off some handcuffs. Gable sneaks out underneath Rey, ripping his feet out from under Rey to ram him face-first into the top turnbuckle. Lee launches Gable off the apron with a Hurricanrana, and Rey hits him with a top-rope West Coast Pop. Gable starts to work over Lee's leg, cranking and twisting until he bounces off the ropes to take a German Suplex and super kick. Lee baseball slide kicks Rey into the announce desk. Uh-oh. He has the dive set up. He hits the ropes, and Gable enters for a big belly-to-belly Suplex for the near-fall.

body: WWE veteran Kevin Nash has a theory about why Roman Reigns defeated LA Knight. A few days ago at the WWE Money in the Bank PLE, Reigns defeated Knight to retain his World Heavyweight Championship. title: Ex-WWE Referee Raves About Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Potential
raw_title: Ex-WWE Referee Raves About Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling’s Potential
body: TSN is one of Canada’s biggest and most historic networks, giving the company a platform to succeed. MLP’s show Mayhem aired on TSN, and MyAEW, thanks to the company’s working relationship with Tony Khan’s AEW. Korderas praised MLP’s production value and in-ring talent. He feels that the company can establish itself as the premier destination for pro wrestling in Canada. Jimmy Korderas raved about MLP’s potential as a pro wrestling company. The roster consists of a mix of independent wrestlers, local Canadian talent, and AEW stars. At MLP Northern Rising earlier this month, AEW stars Adam Copeland and Andrade El Idolo were among the wrestlers featured. The event took place at Mattamy Athletic Centre, formerly known as Maple Leaf Gardens, an iconic venue. Mattamy Athletic Centre could become a regular venue for MLP’s biggest events, further helping to establish the company. While the partnership with AEW is positive, Korderas believes the best is still yet to come for MLP. “[MLP], who are a growing company, I think they have something there. They have a product that I think can grow into something much bigger, at least in Canada, if not further on, because they are on the MyAEW platform now too. So [fans] can see it everywhere. And it is a good product,” Korderas told The Game Plan . He added: “It is different. I think it’s a different presentation from what everybody else is doing because they have a nice mix of talent.” “They have a nice mix of how they present their wrestling on television. It’s not as produced as WWE, nobody is. I mean, they’re different from everybody else. AEW is more wrestling focused, like in-ring focused than anything else,” Korderas told The Game Plan . “That’s where MLP is different, where they do a little bit of everything. Because back when Vince McMahon used to say – and I know people hated this – was, ‘We’re a variety show. We have a little bit of everything for everyone'” “If you concentrate on one single niche audience, then you’re missing out on a whole bunch of people watching your product and enjoying it,” he said. “You can do comedy? There’s a place for comedy. There’s a place for hardcore, a place for straight up wrestling.” “I think that’s what MLP’s bread and butter is right now, is they’re a nice mix. And using social media and having a collaboration with AEW definitely helps.” Giancarlo Aulino Giancarlo Aulino is sports writer who covers UFC for Heavy.com. He began writing for Heavy in 2025 after providing MMA coverage for Sportskeeda. Giancarlo is an experienced journalist and interviewer, having covered soccer clubs Toronto FC and Inter Toronto FC as a full-season reporter, and also producing sports coverage for Toronto radio station VIBE 105.5FM. title: Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn build toward Crown Jewel
raw_title: Raw recap & reactions (Oct. 19, 2026): Roman Reigns’ very busy night
summary_src: Stranded on Death Row Roman Reigns was a busy man this week. That has nothing to do with the song reference above this sentence, but I’ll get to it I promise. Let’s talk about Roman and Sami Zayn first.
body: Let’s talk about Roman and Sami Zayn first. They started the build for their Crown Jewel match with some nice visual storytelling. Peep what happened when Raw started: Sami “big dogged” Roman, which set the stage for their verbal back and forth. Now, to his credit, Roman reached out to Sami for help in this 946 situation. He reminded the Undisputed Champion about his honorary Uce status after the two bonded on the burden that comes with holding a championship. The problem came when they argued over which one of those titles is the championship. This is a basic story that wouldn’t do much for me if not for the history between these two. Sami pointed out Roman’s arrogance since the Tribal Chief once called the Undisputed Championship the championship but now it’s secondary since it’s not on his shoulders. Roman said it’s not about arrogance; it’s about the man holding the title. The World Heavyweight Champion also told the world the Undisputed Championship hasn’t “meant shit” since WrestleMania XL . Reasonable people can disagree on that, but I mean, yeah. This isn’t just about which title is more important now; it’s a battle for supremacy between two guys who consider themselves family. Ish. And about Sami finally earning Roman’s respect. That is, of course, if Sami makes it to Crown Jewel as champion, a possibility Roman happily mentioned. That led to a brief showdown between Roman and Penta during the latter’s entrance for his match, and then a backstage interview that showed Roman on his way out of the arena. That’s how this usually works these days: Roman shows up early, talks his trash, then leaves to let his cousins handle the dirty work. For once, The Bloodline outsmarted 946. Jimmy & Jey Uso lured 946 to come out and play, Solo Sikoa surprised them, with Roman being the very big surprise. That led to a visual I’m sure WWE will put on a loop from now until Survivor Series . Now, back to the song. There’s a real Death Row Records vibe to 946 right now that I love. Royce Keys is Suge Knight. Carmelo Hayes is Tupac. OTM is Tha Dogg Pound, and Jaida Parker is Lady of Rage. They have a ‘90s Hip Hop aesthetic that speaks to my heart. That said, I still need a bit more from them on the verbal front. Like I said last week, an explanation or two would be cool. They don’t need to be very deep or long explanations either. I just don’t know how many times they can show up on grainy footage, look menacing, and tell us ain’t nobody safe. Even when they got to the ring, Royce picked up the mic to emphasize the few people safe from their wrath. If you’ve ever seen the Prince of Space episode of Mystery Science Theater 3000 , it’s a lot like the insane amount of times the titular hero reminds the bad guys how ineffective their weapons are against him. It’s a cool catchphrase I just want a bit more from Suge, Pac, and crew. All that aside, War Games can happen tomorrow and it would be extra hot. We’re already at the tipping point and we’re not even a month a

summary_src: On a night that saw Roman Reigns join the war against the 946, here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/19/26 episode of "WWE Raw!"
body: If you missed the show, as always, you can check out our "WWE Raw" 10/19/26 live blog to catch up on everything that went down Monday night. We keep things factual and objective over there, not to mention comprehensive, which is not something that happens in this space. Here, you get the WINC crew's subjective opinions, and only about the matches and segments that stood out to us the most. So please join us as we present three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/19/26 episode of "WWE Raw!" WWE Now that it's officially Crown Jewel season, it made sense for this edition of "Raw" to open up with a verbal confrontation between World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns and Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn ahead of their Men's Crown Jewel Championship match. With that said, I really struggled to understand the point of what they were saying to each other and the connection between things that they were bringing up. I had a hard time digesting why Reigns was bringing up The 946 to Zayn in the first place, and it wasn't made any easier by the fact it had no relevance to anything else going on in this segment, was incredibly unnecessary to throw into there in the first place, and had the video about Carmelo Hayes joining The 946 to kick off the show when it had nothing to do with this opener. It had no relation to Reigns and Zayn's subsequent debate about who the better champion was or their preceding conversation about Zayn now learning firsthand what Reigns tried teaching him in The Bloodline in terms of what being a champion entailed, making everything feel like it was kind of all over the place. I know that there will be those who did enjoy seeing this because it's Reigns and Zayn, but it just didn't click for me at all and was not my cup of tea. WWE After Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn went from talking about whether or not Zayn's title was important to talking about 946, Penta reminded them that he has El Dinero en el Banco briefcase. As Reigns was making his way up the ramp, Penta appeared. He did his Penta walk and then fist bumped some fans before standing directly in front of Reigns, forcing him to look him in the eye. Penta made his way to the ring and stared down Zayn. Without saying a word, Penta conveyed so much. He put both men on notice that he could come for them at any time and cash in his shot at one of their titles. Following the staredowns, he wrestled Bron Breakker. They were evenly matched until Breakker speared Penta. Penta was able to kick out, but Austin Theory attempted to interfere. Luckily for Penta, Je'Von Evans was there to hit Theory and Breakker with the briefcase. Penta landed the Destroyer to defeat Breakker relatively clean. That's a big deal for a match involving The Vision, let alone a match in WWE. Penta looked like a big deal from the moment his music and pyro hit to him standing tall in victory. title: Shotzi Blackheart plans to continue indie bookings after TNA signing
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart explains what her TNA signing means for future bookings
summary_src: Despite signing for TNA Wrestling, Shotzi Blackheart is still ready to perform in the indies. A few days ago, Blackheart appeared on a TNA taping and was later announced as TNA’s newest roster addition.
body: Despite signing for TNA Wrestling, Shotzi Blackheart is still ready to perform in the indies. A few days ago, Blackheart appeared on a TNA taping and was later announced as TNA’s newest roster addition. Recently, speaking on Busted Open , Blackheart opened up in detail about joining TNA and what the new signing means for her future indie bookings. “I’m still gonna be busting my butt on the indies, taking as many bookings as possible and just having a good time. But yeah, TNA is where I’m at, and I’m hoping to do some really fun things at TNA. I’m really excited to work with all the girls there ,” the former WWE Superstar said. She also shared the reason behind joining TNA. “ It has been a long time coming. I had a couple matches back in like 2019, maybe 2018, with TNA, hoping I would become a Knockout then. And I’m finally here, and it feels good.” “ I’ve definitely had my ups and downs. Definitely had my doubts. But I feel like consistency is key, and eventually you get your day if you just stay consistent. So that’s just what I kept telling myself, even when I felt like my career was going into the gutter. I just was like, if I just stick with it, I will get my moment ,” she added. A former WWE Superstar for several years, Shotzi has past experience wrestling for TNA, specifically for the Impact Wrestling banner. She wrestled a couple of matches in 2018 and 2019. A few days after the news of her TNA taping appearance came out, Blackheart also wrestled on ACW Mischief Night ​2 in a three-way Casket match for the ACW Women’s Title and won it. title: Sami Zayn Retains WWE Title vs Cody Rhodes on Raw

body: Monday's bout was significant in terms of the impact it could have had on what may be the main event of the Crown Jewel premium live event on Nov. 7. Grading WWE Raw 🔠 Bleacher Report 1h Live: Monday Night Raw 🔴 Bleacher Report 1h WWE Must End Judgment Day 🚫 Bleacher Report 7h WWE already announced that Zayn would face Roman Reigns in a champion vs. champion match at Crown Jewel, and the two faced off in a tense moment during Raw: Rhodes had a chance to throw a wrench into those plans, however. Adding even more intrigue to the match is the fact that there was plenty of history between Zayn and Rhodes going into it. When Zayn became WWE champion for the first time back in June at Night of Champions, he won it from Rhodes in a Triple Threat that also included Gunther. While Zayn and Rhodes were once friends, that changed in the weeks prior to that match, as Sami proved he was willing to do whatever it took in order to become a world champion. On the Sept. 11 episode of SmackDown in Mexico, Zayn won the WWE title back from Punk, and he subsequently retained it in a title defense against Kevin Owens one week later. After being robbed of his WWE Championship rematch about four months ago, Rhodes finally got it on Monday night against the man who beat him for the title in the first place.

WWE had already set a champion versus champion match between Zayn and Roman Reigns for Crown Jewel. Rhodes had an opportunity during the Raw contest to alter those plans.

Zayn and Rhodes entered the match with a notable history between them. Zayn first captured the WWE championship from Rhodes in a Triple Threat match at Night of Champions in June that also featured Gunther.

Their prior friendship had deteriorated in the lead-up to that June encounter, with Zayn demonstrating a willingness to take any measures necessary to win the world title. Zayn later regained the WWE title from CM Punk on the September 11 episode of SmackDown in Mexico.

Zayn followed that victory by successfully defending the championship against Kevin Owens the following week. Rhodes, who had been denied a WWE Championship rematch roughly four months earlier, received the opportunity on Monday night against the same opponent who had originally taken the title from him.

body: TNA Wrestling has confirmed the signing of Shotzi Blackheart. Fightful Select had initially reported last Wednesday that Blackheart had signed a deal after her appearance at the promotion’s IMPACT television tapings at the Dothan Civic Center in Dothan, Alabama. TNA Wrestling has signed Shotzi Blackheart, as first reported by Busted Open on SiriusXM. A California native, Blackheart made her pro wrestling debut in 2014 and formerly was the NXT Women’s Tag Team Champion (with Ember Moon). She appeared at the TNA live events in Dothan, Alabama, in mid-October. Here are 10 Fun Facts about Shotzi Blackheart: 1. Has been riding motorcycles since she was 18. 2. Is a paranormal investigator and has hunted ghosts all over America for her YouTube series, CHAMBER OF HORRORS. 3. Majored in musical theatre at AMDA in Hollywood. 4. Is a huge horror movie fan and one of her dreams is to direct her own horror film. 5. Was named PWI’s 2025 Independent Wrestler of the Year and appeared on the magazine’s cover. 6. Is obsessed with Elvis Presley. 7. Has her own chicken farm. 8. Rode every ride across all four Walt Disney World theme parks in one day. 9. “I’m proudly Filipino.” 10. “I got married and wrestled in my wedding dress all on the same day.”

title: Drew McIntyre Details Triple H's Hollywood Shift
raw_title: Drew McIntyre explains how Triple H changed WWE’s approach to Hollywood
summary_src: Comparing leadership between Vince McMahon and Triple H, Drew McIntyre recently shared how the latter changed the promotion’s approach to Hollywood.
body: Comparing leadership between Vince McMahon and Triple H, Drew McIntyre recently shared how the latter changed the promotion’s approach to Hollywood. After recently completing filming a few roles in some upcoming projects with top Hollywood names, McIntyre sat down with Busted Open , where he discussed Triple H’s role in changing WWE’s approach to the industry. “ These days, both the lads see it as, ‘Hey, if this is good for you and your brand, you want to do it, that’s awesome.’ And if it works for our brand, if it helps everybody, if it gets more eyes on the product, they’re all about it, ” McIntyre discussed. The former World Champion further opened up on Vince McMahon’s leadership and compared it with the current one. “Vince [McMahon] was very much like, ‘I need you here.’ McIntyre, being fair, added that with the live events schedule back in the day, McMahon needed his wrestlers. He claimed that his entire life consisted of wrestling every single week until the past few years. “ But as I say, Nick [Khan] and Paul [Levesque] are very much of the mindset, if it makes sense, if it helps everybody and helps your brand, which in turn helps our brand, because I’m not going anywhere anytime soon ,” he finished. McIntyre, 41, is set to be a part of The Last Druid with Russell Crowe and The Highlander with Henry Cavill, Crowe, and other big names. llm_long: Drew McIntyre compared the leadership styles of Vince McMahon and Triple H regarding WWE talent pursuing opportunities in Hollywood. McIntyre recently completed filming for multiple upcoming projects alongside major names in the industry.

During an interview, McIntyre explained that the current approach under Triple H and Nick Khan supports wrestlers taking on external projects. The mindset is that such opportunities benefit both the individual and the overall brand when they make sense.

McIntyre noted that Vince McMahon previously required wrestlers to remain available due to the demanding live event schedule. Under that leadership, McIntyre's career focused entirely on weekly wrestling commitments for years.
The former world champion stated that the shift allows for projects that help everyone involved. He emphasized his long-term commitment to WWE while pursuing these outside endeavors.
McIntyre, who is 41 years old, is involved in the films The Last Druid alongside Russell Crowe and The Highlander with Henry Cavill and Crowe.

title: No DQ Match Set For Next Week’s WWE Raw
raw_title: No DQ Match Set For Next Week’s WWE Raw
body: WWE has announced a No Disqualification match for next week’s episode of WWE Raw. It was announced on Monday night’s show that Bayley and Lyra Valkyria will do battle under no DQ rules, a match that was set up when Bayley came out to cost Valkyria her match against Lola Vice. Bayley and Valkyria brawled after the match, with Bayley coming out on top. Valkyria fled and Bayley got on the mic to lay out the challenge to her former friend-turned-rival. The two have been feuding for months, coming back into focus when Bayley returned last month for the first time since Valkyria had beaten her at Saturday Night’s Main Event in July. The match is the first announced for next week’s show, which will continue the build toward WWE Crown Jewel on November 7th. Next week’s WWE Raw takes place on Monday from the Save Mart Center in Fresno, California and airs live on Netflix.
summary: WWE has revealed a No Disqualification match for next week’s episode of WWE Raw. The match is the first revealed for next week’s show, which will continue the build toward WWE Crown Jewel on November 7th.

title: Kevin Nash hails Oba Femi as WWE's next major star
raw_title: Kevin Nash believes WWE has its next major star in Oba Femi
summary_src: Kevin Nash believes Oba Femi has a ‘rocket up his a**’ and is WWE’s next big star. Speaking on the latest edition of the Kliq This podcast, WWE veteran Kevin Nash heaped praise on Femi’s current run and how certain things have helped his character. “Am I the only one that realizes that the guy […]
body: Kevin Nash believes Oba Femi has a ‘rocket up his a**’ and is WWE’s next big star. “ Am I the only one that realizes that the guy with the rocket up his a** is Oba Femi? ” Nash said. “ When he came down, it was very exaggerated, kind of cartoony, Bushwhacker-y kind of a thing. Now he does that for maybe six to eight steps and then he just drops out of that and goes into kind of a cool jazz version of the original ,” Nash further addressed the presentation changes Femi underwent and how it helped him. Nash also believes Femi’s exchange with Paul Heyman a few weeks ago also potentially made Heyman join forces with Femi. “ When he was leaving the ring after he told Heyman to go [expletive] off because Heyman wanted to pull him in and be his next guy, he was basically dumping Bron Breakker and saying, ‘You’re my boy.’ And he said, ‘I’m not a Paul Heyman guy.'” “From just how well things are going, and he feels it, you could just see … he’s just a nice guy. You see it in his eyes. You can see it in his face, his smirk. He’s just going to get better and better and better and better ,” Nash said, before comparing Femi to Disney’s Lion King. “ It’s more like a Disney-type thing where he’s the Lion King. The Lion King’s not necessarily bad. He’s just … the hyenas aren’t going to [expletive] with him ,” he finished. Femi made his main roster jump earlier this year and faced off against Brock Lesnar in his main roster rookie year itself, before retiring him at WWE SummerSlam 2026. A former WWE NXT Champion, Femi is also the 2026 WWE Men’s King of the Ring winner. He is also expected to take on Roman Reigns next year at WWE WrestleMania 43. Nash explained that Femi now performs that entrance for only six to eight steps before transitioning into a cooler version of the original presentation. The former wrestler pointed out that Femi's recent interaction with Paul Heyman saw him tell Heyman to go fuck off after Heyman tried to recruit him as his next guy.

According to Nash, during that segment Femi was effectively rejecting the idea of being a Paul Heyman guy while addressing his relationship with Bron Breakker. Nash observed that Femi is a nice guy whose confidence is visible in his eyes, face and smirk, and that he is only going to get better and better.

He compared Femi's position to that of the Lion King in a Disney story, saying the hyenas are not going to mess with him. Femi made the jump to the main roster earlier this year. He faced Brock Lesnar during his rookie year on the main roster and retired him at WWE SummerSlam 2026.

title: Legal Watch: Former WWE Tag Team Star Chad 'dick' Wicks Arrested
raw_title: FORMER WWE TAG TEAM STAR CHAD 'DICK' WICKS ARRESTED
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS FORMER WWE TAG TEAM STAR CHAD 'DICK' WICKS ARRESTED By Mike Johnson on 2026-09-30 21:42:00 Former WWE star Chad Wicks, 48. was arrested in Mason City, Iowa on 9/29 at 6:19 PM local time and booked into Cerro Gordo County Jail on charges of Unsafe Turn or Failure to Give Signal, Improper Rear Lamps, Failure to Provide Proof of Financial Liability, and Driving While License Denied, Suspended, Cancelled or Revoked (DUS). He was listed as being booked into the jail for "detox." PWInsider.com can confirm Wicks bonded out at 12:22 local time today, paying a cash bond of $1,501.51. Wicks, who retired in 2007, would have been best known as one half of The Dicks tag team on Smackdown, performing for the company in 2005 and 2006 after a run in then-WWE developmental Ohio Valley Wrestling as Chad Toland.

body: TheSportster’s rating system will take a look across the entire episode of this week’s Monday Night RAW to determine the best match on the show, the weakest showcase on the card, and how everything else stacked up in between too. To learn more about how we rank wrestling matches on TheSportster, please check out our match ranking criteria guide here Joe Hendry has been a thorn in the side of The Judgment Day for several weeks, taking every opportunity to make fun of JD McDonagh’s head. In a rematch from early last month , these two competitors faced off once again on Monday Night RAW. A frustrated McDonagh attacked Hendry during his entrance, before taking aim at a guy in a Funko Pop mask at ringside. The match eventually began with Hendry taking it to his opponent, at one point selling how hard and big McDonagh’s head was after punching him. A Funko Pop figure was thrown into the ring to play some mind games, as the giant Funko Pop issued a headbut to Dominik Mysterio. McDonagh slowed things down and exerted some control over the contest before Hendry began fighting back, until more shenanigans ensued between those at ringside, with McDonagh hitting the giant Funko Pop guy with a guitar. One final piece of interference helped McDonagh to score the win with a running headbutt . The whole match was a complete misfire, with awful comedy, an overbooked presentation, and a lack of anything redeemable. Hendry & McDonagh did their best given the scenario, but it was still pretty terrible. Ahead of her match at Crown Jewel against Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan, WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green appeared on Monday Night RAW to team with Iyo Sky to take on the Judgment Day pairing of Roxanne Perez & Raquel Rodriguez. The match opened with some decent exchanges between Sky & Perez, with the babyfaces running wild for a few minutes, but it wasn’t long before the Judgment Day slowed the match down by slamming Sky into the barricade. raw_title: Will Ospreay on being asked about WWE: “I’d rather focus on AEW – I couldn’t really care less about any other promotion”
body: While speaking with Brandon Kravitz, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay was asked whether he gets tired of being questioned about WWE. Here is what Ospreay had to say… “I know it’s a part of the gig. People always ask, and I can only give my opinion. I don’t really care about it. I’d rather focus on AEW, and I’d rather focus on what we’re able to do here and what I believe AEW is doing to change the face of professional wrestling. I love what we present. I love what we do. I love our wrestling. I love everything that we’re all about. So, I couldn’t really care less about any other promotion.”

title: Lizard Music Starring The Rock Gets Release Date
raw_title: Lizard Music Starring The Rock Gets Release Date
body: The newest film from Benny Safdie featuring The Rock is Lizard Music , and it now has an official release date. Deadline reports that Amazon MGM Studios has set a December 25th, 2027 premiere date for the film, which Safdie is writing and directing. The film reunited Safdie with his Smashing Machine lead in Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson. Johnson was reported in October of last year to be starring in the film. Lizard Music follows a boy (Theo Clark Leber) left to his own devices who stumbles upon a secret late-night broadcast of lizards playing otherworldly music, and a hidden door to the extraordinary swings open. His search for answers leads him to an eccentric and whimsical old man nicknamed The Chicken Man (Dwayne Johnson) and his beloved companion, an 85-year-old chicken named Claudia – the boy and the old man become kindred spirits who find each other at just the right time. title: Tommaso Ciampa Open To NJPW Appearances And Shingo Takagi Match
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa Open To NJPW Appearances And Shingo Takagi Match
body: Tommaso Ciampa is open to stepping into a New Japan Pro Wrestling ring, with Shingo Takagi high on his list of dream opponents. Speaking to SB Nation’s James Dator ahead of AEW WrestleDream 2026, Ciampa discussed the possibility of making appearances for NJPW and named the wrestler he would love to face. “Shingo [Takagi] always jumps out at me as someone I’ve always wanted to share a ring with,” he said. While the prospect interests him, Ciampa explained that a lengthy tour or a place in the G1 Climax might be difficult to fit around his physical needs and personal life. A shorter run, however, is something he would welcome. “I don’t know that my body or personal life at this point bodes well for a full-on tour or G1 Tournament, but doing a show here or there, or three shows, I’d be 100% open to that.” Ciampa has wrestled in Japan just once, during his time with WWE. He also appeared on ROH and NJPW crossover events in North America in 2014, competing in Canada and the United States. For now, his attention turns to AEW WrestleDream 2026, where he is scheduled to challenge Andrade for the National Championship.

Fantasy Book Adam Copeland’s Opponent For NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 | Question Of The Day by Anthony Mango October 16, 2026 0 244 views ReddIt Facebook Twitter Email Copy URL TRENDING (*UPDATED*) – Late-Breaking WWE RAW **SPOILERS** (10/19/26) – Everything Going Down! 0 Keith Lee-AEW Update 0 Adam Copeland / New Japan Pro-Wrestling (Image credit: AEW, NJPW) Welcome to another eWrestlingNews Question of the Day ! My question for you today is “Who do you think would be the best opponent or your favored option to step in the ring with Adam Copeland at Wrestle Kingdom?” My immediate response for any situation like this regarding someone’s retirement is to say that it isn’t up to me or anyone else to make that decision for the person who is bowing out. Who should Copeland face? Ideally, whoever he wants to face, full-stop, end of the conversation. Naturally, he might not have a preference, or his choice could be already booked in some other angle or otherwise unavailable. For instance, I highly doubt the plan is for MJF to face Copeland considering the setup for MJF to face Ryohei Oiwa with the “Real AEW World Championship” on the line. In general, it would make more sense (in my mind, at least) for Copeland to face someone who is more of a New Japan guy than to just step in the ring with another person from AEW. Will Ospreay versus Callum Newman makes more sense than for Copeland to be inserted into that story, or for Copeland to face Kenny Omega, who I’d guess could be up against Yota Tsuji, and it would be very odd if Copeland was just up against Jon Moxley. If he’s going to face someone effectively at random, it should be someone from New Japan’s roster, instead of fighting Gabe Kidd for the global title. My eyes go straight to Zack Sabre Jr. as a potential option. I would think that might kill two birds with one stone, as I know if I were a wrestler, I’d want to step in the ring with Sabre just based on his wrestling skills. He’s a skill-based “let’s put on a great wrestling match” type of opponent in a general sense, and to do that in front of that crowd would be quite the achievement to check off. If Christian Cage is out for several months, we can also count out the idea of a tag team match, unfortunately. It just wouldn’t be the same if Cope is teaming with someone else against The Knock Out Brothers, would it? The one other person who would be my backup idea, if we rule out just having Copeland against someone like Kazuchika Okada or my Zack Sabre Jr. idea, would be Shota Umino, who could always appear on Dynamite and Collision and do something with The Death Riders to help set up something with Copeland so that they aren’t just fighting each other blindly. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Takes Shot at WWE Stars for Being ‘Catchphrase Merchants’
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Takes Shot at WWE Stars for Being ‘Catchphrase Merchants’
summary_src: Drew McIntyre doesn’t need a catchphrase to get a WWE crowd eating out of the palm of his hand, and he plans to prove it when he’s back.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , McIntyre explained how acting has changed the way he looks at delivering promos. One thing he’s still trying to master is dialing down his intensity, because once a live crowd gets going, his plan to stay calm usually goes straight out the window. “It’s hard for me to take it down because I get so excited. My adrenaline gets so high, and I love it so much when I’ve got that audience that, when I’m in a real serious, deep promo, I try so hard to keep myself at a two.” McIntyre admitted that “two” doesn’t usually last very long. Once the adrenaline hits, he can quickly find himself yelling and getting so fired up that even his Scottish accent becomes thicker. “I’m like, ‘I’m going to be at a two, I’m going to be at a two.’ Then I get out there and it’s clearly an eight or a nine, then I go to like a 12 and I start ranting and my Scottish accent gets so thick.” Roman Reigns is someone McIntyre believes has already mastered the opposite approach. Drew praised Reigns for being able to stay restrained and make the audience lean in to hear what he has to say. “Roman and a few of the guys are real good at living around two and just keeping things — you’re going to have to lean in, Jake-style, to listen. And I’m working on that, and maybe with the lessons I’ve learned, I’ll be able to apply that when I get back.” Still, Drew doesn’t want to get so focused on the camera that he forgets about the thousands of people sitting in the building. He wants the live audience involved because he knows they’re desperate to feel like they’re part of the show. “But at the same time, I think you’re doing the crowd a disservice — the live crowd — if you’re kind of doing your thing just for the camera when you’ve got 20,000 people around you. It’s fun to bring them in, make them part of the show, because they want to be part of the show desperately.” “I don’t mean I’m going to start doing catchphrases because everybody does catchphrases. Everyone and their mother does catchphrases. I just want them to pay attention to the material and feel involved.” When Van Vliet pointed out that Drew doesn’t really have a catchphrase of his own, McIntyre said that’s completely intentional. He believes he could create one and get the audience chanting along if he wanted to. “I don’t want a catchphrase. I know I could say something and get them to chant along.” Apparently, Drew is going to put that claim to the test whenever “Hollywood Drew” finally returns to WWE. summary_src: Roman Reigns and The Bloodline may have just found their next major fight, and it looks like things are headed straight for WarGames. body: Speaking on the October 19 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Meltzer addressed the closing segment from RAW, which saw Roman Reigns reunite with Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso and Solo Sikoa to fight 946. The segment ended with the family standing tall, but according to Meltzer, this isn’t where the feud ends. As Ringside News previously covered , things got ugly when The Usos came to the ring armed with weapons and called out 946. Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price and Carmelo Hayes answered the challenge, and it didn’t take long for the situation to turn into an all-out brawl. But the bigger news came when Alvarez started discussing the possibility of WWE building toward a WarGames match involving the two factions. He barely got the question out before Meltzer interrupted. “I mean, if this is. If this is, like, their War Games idea, I mean.” Alvarez went on to say that the match could do extremely well considering how strongly the crowd reacted to the confrontation. Meltzer then made it clear once again that WarGames is WWE’s planned direction for the feud, saying, “It is their WarGames. Yeah.” That would make plenty of sense considering WWE has been building this fight for weeks. The feud took another major turn on October 12 when Carmelo Hayes revealed himself as an ally of 946 and helped destroy The Usos and Solo Sikoa. Roman getting involved now gives the family some serious backup. The timing also lines up with Survivor Series: WarGames on November 28. WWE hasn’t officially announced the match, and there are still questions about how the teams will be put together. Roman, Jimmy, Jey and Solo are currently united against a group that includes Keys, Nima, Price, Hayes and Jaida Parker, but the final WarGames lineup remains to be seen. title: Match Made: Speculation on Will Ospreay vs. Adam Copeland World Title Match After WrestleDream
raw_title: Speculation on Will Ospreay vs. Adam Copeland World Title Match After WrestleDream
summary_src: Adam Copeland isn’t retiring without getting his hands on Will Ospreay first. AEW has already started teasing a match between the two, and the current belief is a World Championship showdown is coming. In fact, he thinks the company could pull the trigger as soon as Full Gear.
body: Speaking on the October 19, 2026 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer addressed what happened between Ospreay and Copeland at AEW WrestleDream and the backstage interaction that followed. According to Meltzer, AEW is making it pretty clear that these two are eventually going to fight over the company’s biggest championship. The situation started at AEW WrestleDream on October 17 , where Ospreay successfully defended the AEW World Championship in the eight-man Clockwork Carnage Match. Copeland came incredibly close to winning the title, but Ospreay pinned him in the closing seconds to retain. Copeland wasn’t happy afterward and shoved Ospreay, but things eventually cooled down and the two shook hands. Meltzer believes that moment was no accident. “Yeah. So, you know, at the end of the pay per view, they did the thing where Osprey and Copeland shook hands. It was pretty clear that they’re going to do that match.” “So it would not shock me if that was the full gear main event.” While he isn’t certain about the timing, Meltzer sounded convinced that AEW is building toward Ospreay defending his championship against the former WWE Champion. “Ospreay and Adam Copeland are going to be doing a championship match at some point.” “Will Ospreay is one of the best wrestlers in the world, if not the best. Adam Copeland is very smart. He works his ass off. He’s very good.” Meltzer also pointed to Copeland’s recent matches as proof that he can still deliver when it matters. He specifically praised Copeland’s ability to structure matches and said he has no concerns about the two working together. AEW hasn’t officially announced Ospreay vs. Copeland, and there’s no confirmation that it’ll happen at Full Gear. But between their confrontation at WrestleDream, the handshake afterward and the backstage tease, the company certainly isn’t hiding the possibility. Copeland has a limited amount of time left before retirement, and Ospreay is sitting at the top of AEW with the World Championship. If the company wants to give Copeland another major title match before he walks away, this looks like the fight they’re setting up. title: Match Made: Roman Reigns vs. Penta’s Huge WWE RAW Ratings May Have Changed Company’s Plans for Mexican Stars
raw_title: Roman Reigns vs. Penta’s Huge WWE RAW Ratings May Have Changed Company’s Plans for Mexican Stars
summary_src: WWE may have found a new formula for pulling in viewers, and Penta is a big reason why. His match against Roman Reigns in Mexico City delivered some of RAW’s biggest numbers of the year. Now the belief is that WWE has taken notice, and it could mean a lot more opportunities for Mexican wrestlers ...
body: “Penta showed. He drew, you know, him and Roman drew the second biggest rating of this entire year for, for Raw. And that’s a worldwide number, not a Mexico number, and that is big in the United States.” And WWE already knows how successful that match was. As Ringside News previously covered , the September 14 episode drew more than three million global Netflix views, with both WWE and Netflix extremely pleased with the numbers. Netflix was so impressed that it wanted WWE to start putting bigger names and matches on RAW more often. But Meltzer says there’s another part of the equation. With Nielsen placing greater emphasis on Hispanic households, having Mexican wrestlers in major television roles is becoming increasingly valuable for WWE. “So having Mexican stars in higher positions and more is more valuable right now to WWE than it was two months ago. And they know it. You know, this is their business.” He made it clear that the wrestlers need to be involved in meaningful programs, including championship matches, rather than simply filling spots on the card. “But having them in key spots as top guys as at the championship level, that’ll make a difference if, if they’re, you know, as long as they have some charisma to them.” There’s already evidence that Penta’s performance changed his own standing in WWE. Ringside News previously covered how Penta wasn’t originally supposed to win Money in the Bank , but his match against Reigns helped change those plans. He eventually walked away with the briefcase, putting him in position for another major championship opportunity. title: On the Record: Ric Flair Calls Out WWE’s Developmental System for Making Young Talent “Practice Wrestle” Each Other
raw_title: Ric Flair Calls Out WWE’s Developmental System for Making Young Talent “Practice Wrestle” Each Other
summary_src: Ric Flair doesn’t think WWE has an athleticism problem when it comes to developing its next generation of stars. His issue is that he believes too many young wrestlers are learning by “practice wrestling” each other instead of getting the kind of real-world experience he had coming up.
body: Flair doesn’t believe there’s some massive talent gap between the two companies either. In his eyes, the biggest difference is that WWE has decades of history behind it while AEW is still relatively young. “The only distance — the only thing in between, in my opinion, WWE and AEW is the length of all the time the business has been open. You’re talking about 50 or 70 years as opposed to five years.” When it comes to the wrestlers themselves, Flair believes both companies have plenty of athletic talent. He sees a bigger difference in how WWE and AEW allow those wrestlers to perform. “But there’s equal athleticism on both. Um, Tony’s a daredevil and he lets the guys go wide open. The WWE is like, you know, trying to stay in that G-rated for commercials.” That’s when Flair turned his attention to WWE’s developmental system, and he wasn’t exactly sold on how things are being done. Flair estimated WWE has close to 120 wrestlers in developmental at the moment. “The problem is the WWE is — their developmental program has got 120 people in it, close to that.” “And they’re trying to bring these kids up, and all they’ve done is practice wrestle each other with no real opportunity to go out and learn how to work, and they’re on TV one time and, man, you don’t — make it, impress somebody, you’re not there next week.” The host then asked how things worked when Flair was learning the business, and his answer was pretty simple. Instead of spending most of his time inside one developmental system, Flair was constantly traveling and wrestling wherever he could. “And there’s nobody I didn’t wrestle. I mean, I wrestled — I mean, from Bruiser Brody to Stan Hansen to Lou Thesz, Harley Race, Pat O’Connor. I mean, I wrestled all of them.” That’s really Flair’s problem with WWE’s system — not that today’s wrestlers aren’t talented, but that he believes talent can only learn so much by repeatedly working with the same developmental group. For someone who learned by traveling everywhere and wrestling just about everybody, Flair clearly thinks today’s prospects need more chances to learn the hard way before the television cameras start rolling. What do you think about Ric Flair’s criticism of WWE’s developmental system? Do younger wrestlers need more experience outside the Performance Center before being put on television? Let us know in the H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

title: IYO SKY Could Be Getting WWE Women’s Intercontinental Title Match Soon
raw_title: IYO SKY Could Be Getting WWE Women’s Intercontinental Title Match Soon
summary_src: IYO SKY might be next in line for a shot at the WWE Women’s Intercontinental Championship. She pinned Raquel Rodriguez on the October 19, 2026 episode of WWE RAW, and that victory may have earned her a much bigger opportunity.
body: Speaking on the October 19 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Meltzer discussed SKY teaming with Chelsea Green against Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez on RAW. The match ended with SKY catching Rodriguez in a cradle for the pinfall, giving her a victory over the reigning Women’s Intercontinental Champion. Meltzer believes WWE didn’t book that finish for no reason. He expects the result to lead directly into a championship match between SKY and Rodriguez. “Sets up intercontinental championship match relatively soon. Probably within the next few weeks.” That would be a pretty quick turnaround, but WWE has already been building tension between the two. As Ringside News covered during the October 12 episode of RAW , Rodriguez confronted SKY backstage while Roxanne Perez was arguing with Adam Pearce. Rodriguez accused WWE of forgetting about SKY, which led to an argument between the two women. Now SKY has pinned Rodriguez in the middle of the ring, giving WWE an obvious reason to put them together again with the championship on the line. Meltzer also had plenty of praise for SKY’s performance on RAW, particularly her exchanges with Perez. He felt the match was one of the stronger parts of the show and made it clear that SKY stood out. WWE hasn’t officially announced SKY as the next challenger, and there’s no date set for a title match. But Meltzer clearly believes that’s where things are going, especially after WWE had SKY pin the champion rather than Roxanne Perez. For now, Rodriguez still has the gold, but SKY has already beaten her. If WWE follows up on Monday’s finish, Rodriguez could find herself defending the Women’s Intercontinental Championship against someone who just proved she can put her shoulders on the mat. title: Ludwig Kaiser Stand Your Ground motion denied
raw_title: WWE star Ludwig Kaiser’s battery case dismissal motion denied
body: Earlier this year, WWE Superstar Ludwig Kaiser, aka Marcel Barthel, was arrested in Florida . Kaiser, currently performing as El Grande Americano in WWE's Mexican wrestling promotion AAA, was arrested on battery charges in Orange County, Florida. Kaiser's legal team aimed to have the misdemeanor battery charge dropped by invoking Florida's "Stand Your Ground" law. The claim was that Kaiser was justified in applying the level of force he did against the alleged victim because he reasonably believed it was needed to defend himself and his girlfriend, Andre Bazarte, from the "imminent use of unlawful force." A pre-trial conference is scheduled to take place on Dec. 17, 2026. Earlier this year, Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful and trusted media personality Raj Giri had opened up and shared details about Kaiser's arrest and charges. Previously, the charges were suspected to be domestic charges, but they were later dismissed by Sean Ross Sapp. "This is what I heard regarding the Ludwig Kaiser situation. He was in the apartment elevator with Andrea Bazarte and they were being affectionate, but nothing crazy or out of the ordinary. [Richard] Reap allegedly didn't say anything in the elevator but once he got out on the 12th floor, he allegedly said something to Kaiser to the effect of 'you need to show some f'n respect before I call ICE on that b**ch.' Kaiser got out of the elevator and they had a little scuffle, but no punches were apparently thrown," Giri wrote.
summary: WWE performer Ludwig Kaiser, also known as Marcel Barthel and currently wrestling as El Grande Americano in AAA, had his motion to dismiss a misdemeanor battery charge denied in Orange County, Florida. Kaiser's legal team argued he acted in self-defense under the state's Stand Your Ground law to protect himself and his girlfriend Andre Bazarte from imminent unlawful force. A pre-trial conference is set for December 17, 2026, per details first reported earlier this year by Fightful Select's Sean Ross Sapp and Raj Giri.

title: A&E and WWE to debut new in-ring competition series “WWE LFG” in early 2025
raw_title: A&E and WWE to debut new in-ring competition series “WWE LFG” in early 2025 - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email New York, NY – December 6, 2024 – A&E and WWE today announced an expansion of its programming partnership which will include the debut of “WWE LFG ( Legends & Future Greats ),” a new competition series that features in-ring matches along with a behind-the-scenes look at rising talent vying for a coveted WWE contract while being mentored by WWE Legends such as Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Undertaker, Shawn Michaels and Booker T. Additionally, WWE & A&E will launch “WWE’s Greatest Moments,” a series that will provide fans a front-row seat to relive the iconic events that have shaped WWE history. A new season of the hit-series “WWE Rivals” will also complement this winter’s WWE programming slate on A&E, which will add more than 180 hours of original content over the next three years. "Literally filled with blood, sweat, and tears, there's never been a series that combines in-ring action, behind-the-scenes reality, high-stakes drama, and some of WWE's greatest icons all in one package. From total unknowns to legends, ‘LFG’ will give viewers a raw, ground-up, 360-degree view of what it truly takes to make it in the WWE," said Rob Sharenow, President of Programming, A+E Networks. "Our collaboration with WWE has clearly struck a chord with audiences, and we’re excited to continue producing premium content that resonates with a diverse viewership." “A&E has proved to be an excellent home for WWE content, and we’re excited to partner with their fantastic team on these new show concepts and the latest season of WWE Rivals,” said WWE Chief Content Officer Paul “Triple H” Levesque. “WWE LFG” will offer viewers an inside look at the rigorous training process, featuring iconic WWE Legends such as Paul “Triple H” Levesque and Shawn Michaels and weekly regular coaches Undertaker, Booker T, Mickie James and Bubba Ray Dudley as they mentor a new generation in weekly matches on their quest to become the next WWE Superstars. Executive producers for WWE are Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Lee Fitting, Ben Houser, Shawn Michaels and Jeremy Borash. Elaine Frontain Bryant and Brad Abramson serve as Executive producers for A&E. "WWE’s Greatest Moments" will feature legendary play-by-play announcer Michael Cole hosting half-hour episodes with various WWE Superstars & Legends, including “Stone Cold” Steve Austin, Hulk Hogan, Kevin Owens and others, to share vivid recollections and perspectives on the most remarkable moments in wrestling history. “WWE Rivals” will return with an all-new season this winter celebrating some of the most iconic and beloved rivalries from the WWE including a never-before-seen look at Hulk Hogan vs. Ultimate Warrior and Roman Reigns vs. Seth Rollins . Executive Producers for WWE are Paul “Triple H” Levesque, Lee Fitting, Ben Houser and Marc Pomarico. llm_long: Chad Gable retained the Intercontinental Championship in a triple threat match on Raw against Bron Breakker and Dominik Mysterio.

The competitors traded holds early with Lee applying a side headlock to Mysterio before tossing Gable from the ring. Lee then exchanged strikes with Mysterio and delivered a dropkick to both opponents in the corners.
Gable responded by suplexing both men at the same time. After a commercial break, Gable landed multiple forearms on Lee as the action continued with frequent reversals.

Lee attempted a Styles Clash but was interrupted by Mysterio's crossbody. Gable applied the Ankle Lock on Lee, who escaped only to be caught in the hold again while Mysterio targeted Gable from the top.

The match featured several high-impact moves including a hurricanrana over the top rope, a West Coast Pop, a double stomp, and multiple suplexes. Mysterio hit a 619 on both opponents followed by a Frog Splash on Lee that was broken up by Gable.
Gable ultimately secured the victory by rolling up Mysterio. Following the match, Mysterio and Gable were attacked by Ethan Page while Lee was assaulted by Big Cass on the outside.

raw_title: Multiple-weight world champion granted release from ZUFFA Boxing without fighting once
summary_src: Shakur Stevenson has been granted his release from ZUFFA Boxing without ever stepping into the ring for the promotion. Stevenson confirmed on his YouTube channel that he was no longer with the Saudi Arabian-backed boxing promotion, which is of course headed by UFC and WWE owners TKO/Dana White.
body: Shakur Stevenson has been granted his release from ZUFFA Boxing without ever stepping into the ring for the promotion. Stevenson confirmed on his YouTube channel that he was no longer with the Saudi Arabian-backed boxing promotion, which is of course headed by UFC and WWE owners TKO/Dana White. “I requested to be released from Zuffa Boxing,” Stevenson revealed on his YouTube channel. “Now, over the weekend, my request has been granted. I’ve been in camp for like eight weeks, preparing for fights that I was told was going to happen and have not happened. It is what it is. This is the business of boxing. I’m not mad at anyone, I’m not pointing fingers. I am taking my career in my own hands and starting my own promotional company and I’m willing to work with other promoters and anybody else that’s willing to be as serious about my career as I am.” As of writing, ZUFFA Boxing has not responded publicly to the news. Stevenson was in talks to fight WBO welterweight champion Devin Haney, but those appeared to have stalled to a point that Stevenson wanted to get out of his contract with TKO Group. title: Penta Basks in MITB Glory on Raw
