body: Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn faced off for the first time since both captured world championships, and The OTC followed up by taking the fight to The 946 with The Usos and Solo Sikoa. Penta took down Bron Breakker with the help of Je'Von Evans. Chad Gable again defended his Intercontinental Championship successfully. Lola Vice defeated Lyra Valkyria thanks to a timely Bayley intervention. This was the foundation of an important show as WWE heads toward Crown Jewel on November 7. Check out all the fallout from Raw below. Penta is Mr. Money in the Bank, and he looks extremely confident carrying around the briefcase. In some ways, he is already carrying himself as a world champion, which makes the luchador a big deal every time he appears. With this in mind, WWE should not rush the cash-in. Penta could continue to taunt the world champions while he chooses the perfect time to strike. The luchador could wait until the next major WWE show in Mexico or at least call his shot at a major premium live event, whether it be the Royal Rumble or WrestleMania. A quick cash-in disrupts the stories of both world champions and would take longer-term story builds off the table. Especially if Penta is going to have a lengthy run as champion, WWE should establish a clear direction for his reign before giving him the title rather than hot-shotting the change for immediate buzz. While The Genius of the Sky would be a great titleholder, she does not need the belt right now, especially with multiple younger, less proven stars waiting for their shot. In particular, WWE has set up Lola Vice as an immediately credible threat coming off an NXT Women's Championship reign. She even holds her own pinfall over Rodriguez. While Rodriguez is a veteran who deserved a singles accolade, it is time to move on to a younger star such as the 28-year-old Vice. WWE needs to keep building fresh names, and Sky losing to Rodriguez only for Vice to pull off the win would solidify the former MMA fighter as a real threat on Raw. Is there a bigger story on Raw that WWE has fallen short on building than the rivalry between Lyra Valkyria and Bayley? Since Valkyria's initial heel turn, WWE has been noticeably inconsistent in its presentation of her. Despite Valkyria's two wins over Bayley, The Role Model still feels more important to the weekly product. The Valkyrie's frequent absences from television have not helped. Next week, the two will collide in a No Disqualification match that may end this story. The match needs more than strong action; it needs a memorable moment that gives this rivalry lasting significance. This could mean Bayley and Valkyria pulling off the best spot of the night in the ring or a brawl outside of the ring that leads to a memorable fall in the backstage area. The goal should be to convince fans that these two matter, and whatever comes of this rivalry, both should be moving into the title picture afterward. title: On the Record: Ric Flair Admits He Does Nothing for AEW Despite Still Working for Tony Khan
raw_title: Ric Flair Admits He Does Nothing for AEW Despite Still Working for Tony Khan
summary_src: Ric Flair has a pretty sweet deal with AEW, and he’s not even trying to hide it. The WWE Hall of Famer openly admitted that he still works for Tony Khan despite doing absolutely nothing for the company.
body: Speaking during an October 15, 2026 interview on NewsNation’s BIFF , Flair discussed his relationship with the AEW President and had nothing but good things to say about him. He praised Khan for his generosity and his ability to juggle multiple responsibilities, including running AEW and his involvement with the Jacksonville Jaguars. That’s when Flair casually admitted that his own arrangement with Khan doesn’t involve much work. “He’s got that Learjet. He’s got a beautiful girlfriend. He’s a nice guy. He’s generous. I work for him. I work for him and I don’t do anything.” “You know, I think he takes care of me out of respect for me, you know?” Flair made it clear that his relationship with Khan goes beyond business, once again pointing to the personal respect between them. “He He He grew up on me and um He’s it it’s just a wonderful guy.” As Ringside News previously covered , Flair signed a multi-year agreement with AEW in November 2023. The deal was announced shortly after he appeared on AEW Dynamite as Tony Khan’s special gift to Sting. It also included a promotional partnership involving Flair’s Wooooo! Energy drink. Flair played a role in Sting’s retirement storyline leading up to AEW Revolution 2024, but he hasn’t been a regular presence on AEW television since then. That apparently hasn’t changed his relationship with Khan. In fact, Flair shut down rumors about returning to WWE in September 2026, making it clear that he remains loyal to AEW because Khan allows him to pursue outside business opportunities. Flair also stressed that the two are personal friends. Flair didn’t reveal how much money he receives under his AEW arrangement or whether his current agreement still includes guaranteed payments. However, he certainly made it sound like Khan is happy to keep him connected to the company whether he’s appearing on television or not. title: On the Record: Ric Flair Says Tony Khan Could Be the Greatest Wrestling Promoter of All Time
raw_title: Ric Flair Says Tony Khan Could Be the Greatest Wrestling Promoter of All Time
summary_src: Ric Flair has a pretty massive opinion of Tony Khan, and he’s putting him in some serious company. The WWE Hall of Famer believes the AEW President could go down as the greatest promoter in professional wrestling history.
body: Speaking during an October 15, 2026 interview on NewsNation’s BIFF , Flair discussed how much backstage politics influence professional wrestling. He explained that creative decisions aren’t always made by one person and suggested both WWE and AEW have groups of people involved in determining what happens on television. That’s when he made a huge prediction about Khan’s place in wrestling history. “I mean with Tony Khan who runs runs AEW who is really one of the most wonderful people I’ve ever known. Uh Tony has a group of people which I’m sure they do at WWE that um he circles up with and Tony Tony does it right there. So Tony Khan may be the greatest promoter of all time.” Flair went on to praise Khan for handling AEW while also maintaining responsibilities with the Jacksonville Jaguars. He seemed particularly impressed by Khan’s schedule and his ability to keep multiple major operations running at the same time. This isn’t the first time Flair has suggested Khan could accomplish something huge in professional wrestling. As Ringside News previously covered , Flair claimed in April 2026 that he wouldn’t be surprised if Khan eventually purchased WWE. He pointed to the Khan family’s financial resources as one reason such a deal wouldn’t shock him. Flair also believes AEW deserves more credit when compared to WWE. During the same interview, he argued that the biggest difference between the companies comes down to how long each has been in business. He also insisted that the quality of the wrestlers isn’t what separates the two promotions. “The The only distance The only thing in between, in my opinion, and WWE and AEW is the length of all the time the business been open.” “But there’s equal athletic athleticism on both. Um Tony’s a daredevil and he lets the guys go wide open.” Flair’s praise shouldn’t come as a complete surprise considering his relationship with Khan. The Nature Boy has been connected to AEW since 2023 and reaffirmed his loyalty to the company in September 2026. He’s made it clear that he considers Khan a personal friend and appreciates the freedom he has while working with AEW. Still, calling Khan a potential greatest-of-all-time promoter is a different level of praise. Vince McMahon spent decades building WWE into a global powerhouse, while Khan launched AEW in 2019 and has spent the years since trying to establish a serious alternative. Flair clearly believes Khan has the ability to take things much further. Whether Khan ever reaches that level is another story. AEW has accomplished plenty in its relatively short existence, but Flair is already putting its president in a conversation normally reserved for the biggest names in wrestling history. That’s a major endorsement from someone who spent more than five decades working for some of those promoters. title: Grayson Waller Made Vaquer T-Shirt That Didn't Air
raw_title: Grayson Waller Had A T-Shirt With Stephanie Vaquer On It That He Couldn't Wear On TV
summary_src: Shortly after winning the WWE Women's World Championship, Stephanie Vaquer took a photo wearing nothing but the title. Grayson Waller was looking to use that photo as heat against Myles Bourne, Stephanie's boyfriend. The shirt exists, but it never made TV.
body: Shortly after winning the WWE Women’s World Championship, Stephanie Vaquer took a photo wearing nothing but the title. Grayson Waller was looking to use that photo as heat against Myles Bourne, Stephanie’s boyfriend. “There are some that haven’t ended up on TV,” Waller told Sam Roberts on Not Sam Wrestling when asked if a T-shirt he’s made couldn’t be worn on TV. “Stephanie Vaquer kind of broke the internet recently. She did an Instagram story posing like Shawn Michaels. There was a t-shirt with that on it. That didn’t end up on television. If anyone wants it, bribe me with some money. There is some fan who would pay some crazy money for it. I love to cause chaos, but if we can’t fight about this, there is the line. Stephanie Vaquer doesn’t feel like I should be doing that, are we going to have a match? That’s not going to happen. That’s where my line is.” Waller has worn T-shirts taking shots at Zilla Fatu, Cruz Montana, and others. He is set to defend the NXT Championship against Tony D’Angelo at NXT Halloween Havoc. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Grayson Waller created a T-shirt using Stephanie Vaquer's recent Instagram photo but it never made it to television. title: Ric Flair Claims WWE Doesn’t Want Him in the Building Because of His AEW Ties
raw_title: Ric Flair Claims WWE Doesn’t Want Him in the Building Because of His AEW Ties
summary_src: Ric Flair says WWE doesn’t want him in the building anymore, and he believes his relationship with AEW is the reason. The WWE Hall of Famer claims his connection to Tony Khan’s company has made it difficult for him to attend events where his own daughter, Charlotte Flair, is wrestling.
body: Speaking during an October 15, 2026 interview on NewsNation’s BIFF , Flair was asked about Charlotte’s wrestling career and whether he still follows her matches. He made it clear that he watches everything she does, but attending those matches in person has become another story. Flair then explained that his AEW relationship has created problems when it comes to being welcomed at WWE events. According to the Nature Boy, WWE isn’t exactly interested in having someone connected to its biggest competitor walking around backstage. “If I’m not If I’m not there Well, I can’t go to a lot of them now cuz I work with AEW and they and they They don’t They don’t like to bring me into the building.” Flair was quick to clarify that this isn’t about personal problems with WWE talent or management. He believes it’s simply a matter of the two companies being competitors. “Um not because I don’t get along with the guys. It’s just that, you know, the competition” This isn’t the first time Flair has pointed to AEW as the reason he can’t attend certain WWE events. As Ringside News previously covered , Flair made a similar claim ahead of WrestleMania 41, explaining that his relationship with Tony Khan was keeping him from attending the event. Flair also shut down WWE return rumors in September 2026 , making it clear that he remains loyal to Tony Khan. He explained that he and Triple H are still friends, but he has no intention of disrespecting Khan by creating the impression that he’s returning to WWE. Now Flair is once again saying his AEW connection is keeping him from being welcomed at WWE events. WWE hasn’t publicly confirmed that it doesn’t want Flair inside its buildings, so for now, that’s his side of the story. Jimmy and Jey Uso had called out the group looking for a fight, and Solo eventually joined them. Unfortunately for the family, 946 had the numbers advantage and started beating them down until Roman’s music hit. That’s a pretty interesting development considering Solo previously tried to take Roman’s place as the Tribal Chief. The two spent months fighting over control of the Bloodline, and their issues created a massive divide within the family. Now they’re hugging in the ring after fighting alongside each other, which is a pretty big change from where things stood before. Of course, one hug doesn’t mean all their problems have magically disappeared. WWE hasn’t made it clear whether Roman and Solo have officially settled their differences, but the footage certainly gives people something to talk about. With 946 now targeting the family, it looks like Roman and Solo might have a good reason to stop fighting each other for a while. title: Royce Keys Discusses Leading The 946 On Raw
raw_title: WWE Star Royce Keys Opens Up About Being The 'Face Of' The 946
summary_src: Royce Keys opens up about his position as the "face of" the 946, a group that's calling shots and wreaking havoc on the "WWE Raw" locker room.
body: During a recent interview with "Busted Open Radio," Keys opened up about his position as the "face of" 946, a group that's calling shots and wreaking havoc on the "WWE Raw" locker room. "I'm a natural born leader," Key said. "And so collectively, I wanted these four with me. You look at the great leaders of every faction in this business. The stuff you see with us, like arriving together, working out together, that's all us. We do that in every town. So it is my responsibility, the big brother role, to look after everybody, scold everybody, make sure we're all learning. They can teach me some things, and I'm going to teach them some things. So we're one unified unit." Last week, the 946 lineup was elevated to five members: Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, Jaida Parker, and Carmelo Hayes. The latter made his presence known in the "Raw" main event , which pitted 946 against The Bloodline's Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso, and Solo Sikoa. Hayes unmasked himself, then helped beatdown The Bloodline members with a crowbar. Jaida Parker marked her arrival by running over Jacob Fatu with a car and proclaiming "Ain't nobody safe." Nima and Price emerged alongside Keys in the stable's original reveal, which again targeted The Bloodline, in August. Parker, Nima, and Price's 946 onboarding coincided with their official call ups to WWE's main roster.

Some of the bigger title changes include Triple H winning the WWE Intercontinental Championship in 2002, AJ Styles winning the TNA World Heavyweight Title in 2013 and AJ Styles & Dragón Lee winning the WWE World Tag Team Titles in 2025. The earliest October 20th entries are from 1968, when Alberto Muñoz won the Mexican National Middleweight Title and the Mexican National Welterweight Title was vacated. Karloff Lagarde won the Mexican National Welterweight Title in 1972. Dusty Rhodes and Manny Fernández won the NWA World Tag Team Titles (Mid-Atlantic Version) in 1984. Masanobu Fuchi won the AJPW World Junior Heavyweight Title. Samson Fuyuki and Toshiaki Kawada won the All Asia Tag Team Titles. Gen’ichiro Tenryu and Stan Hansen won the AJPW World Tag Team Titles. The WWE Intercontinental Title was listed as defunct and then won by Triple H. Chris Benoit and Kurt Angle won the WWE Tag Team Titles. Buchanan and D’Lo Brown won the GHC Heavyweight Tag Team Titles in 2007. Four titles changed hands in 2013: AJ Styles won the TNA World Heavyweight Title, Chris Sabin won the TNA X-Division Title, Gail Kim won the TNA Knockouts Title, and Jesse and Robbie E won the TNA World Tag Team Titles. In 2019, Exterminador won the Occidente Heavyweight Title and Ace Austin won the IW X-Division Title. In 2025, the WWE World Heavyweight Title was vacated and AJ Styles and Dragón Lee won the WWE World Tag Team Titles. raw_title: WWE legend The Great Khali poses in pink onesie in Netflix photoshoot as fans left totally baffled - www.the-sun.com
body: The 7ft 1in giant, who once struck fear into his opponents inside the ring, showed off a completely different side in the hilarious pictures. Khali, 54, appeared in a pink and white polka-dot onesie complete with matching bows on his head. The former world heavyweight champion was pictured lounging on a pink bed inside a bedroom decorated with fairy lights, cuddly toys and posters. title: In Memoriam: PAC Had Blood Clot Issues and Lung Problems Before His Death at 40
raw_title: PAC Had Blood Clot Issues and Lung Problems Before His Death at 40
summary_src: PAC’s sudden death at 40 shocked the wrestling world, but it turns out he had been dealing with health problems years before his passing. The former AEW star experienced blood clot issues in 2023 and had a history of problems with his lungs.
body: Speaking on the October 19, 2026 episode of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer revealed that one of PAC’s friends had told him about the wrestler’s previous medical issues around the time of his death. Meltzer explained that while the full extent of those problems wasn’t widely known, PAC’s lung issues were something people close to him were aware of. “He did have lung issues. This is not something that came out of nowhere that nobody knew.” Meltzer then revealed that PAC had also dealt with blood clot issues back in 2023, something that adds another piece to his medical history before his death on September 27. “I don’t know how well that was known but one of his friends had told me like, you know, really like the week of his death, you know about the, he had the blood clot issues when in 2023. And he said that he had had some, some lung issues. And so this is. The lung issues are consistent with, with what happened.” Meltzer also shared information from Canadian physician Dr. Alex Patel, who explained how severe asthma attacks can become deadly when the airways become inflamed and restricted. While most cases can be managed with inhalers and medication, some attacks can get out of control very quickly. “Unfortunately you know, usually, you know, you would have the inhaler with you, and I don’t know, you know, you know, it may have happened so quick. There was stuff in his car, in the rental car, but he may not have been able to. It may have happened so quick. He wasn’t able to get it.” As Ringside News previously covered , PAC was discovered inside his running rental car outside a CAVA restaurant on September 27. The woman who called 911 said people had been trying to get his attention for several minutes without any response. Emergency crews arrived and attempted to save him, but he was pronounced dead at 4:08 p.m. The situation was especially shocking because PAC had wrestled Andrade at AEW All Out just one night earlier. By the following afternoon, he was dead at just 40 years old. Meltzer admitted that the more he learned about the situation, the harder it became to process. “And just a. It’s a horrible situation. The more you learn about it, it’s. It doesn’t get better. It gets. It gets worse.” For now, there’s no established connection between PAC’s blood clot problems in 2023 and the bronchial asthma that ultimately took his life. But learning that he had been dealing with previous lung issues makes his sudden passing even more heartbreaking, especially considering he was still competing inside the ring just hours before his death. title: 82-Year-Old Wrestling Legend Tiger Jeet Singh Sends Fan to Hospital With Sword, Then Blames Him for Getting Hit
raw_title: 82-Year-Old Wrestling Legend Tiger Jeet Singh Sends Fan to Hospital With Sword, Then Blames Him for Getting Hit
summary_src: Wrestling legend Tiger Jeet Singh returned to Japan after 14 years away, and things got completely out of hand when he struck a fan in the head with his sword. The 82-year-old wrestling veteran left the man bleeding and needing an ambulance during a live event in Tokyo.
body: The incident happened on October 17, 2026, during Megumi Kudo’s 40th anniversary wrestling show at Yoyogi National Stadium in Tokyo. Singh, who became one of Japan’s most notorious villains during his wrestling career, was serving as a special observer for a tag team match featuring Tatsumi Fujinami and Masakatsu Funaki against Mitsuya Nagai and Shiro Koshinaka. Singh made his entrance alongside his son, former WWE wrestler Tiger Ali Singh, and his grandson. Everything seemed to be going as planned until Singh charged toward the crowd with his trademark saber and started swinging it around. According to Sports Hochi , he struck a male spectator in the forehead, leaving him bleeding. The injured fan was taken backstage for emergency treatment before being transported to a nearby hospital by ambulance. Fortunately, the wound wasn’t deep, and the man suffered only minor injuries. He received treatment to prevent infection and was eventually able to return to the arena, pick up his car and drive himself home. But Singh wasn’t exactly losing sleep over what happened. Speaking to Tokyo Sports after the incident, the wrestling legend made it clear that he believed the fan was responsible for getting hit. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right? All he had to do was get out of my way.” His son, Tiger Ali Singh, didn’t exactly disagree. The former WWE star pointed out that announcements had been made warning spectators to be careful, arguing that the injured man should have moved when his father approached with the sword. “The announcer was saying, ‘Please be careful!’ They were warning him it was dangerous, but he didn’t move out of the way. I’m sure he won’t make the same mistake again. Just like my father said, this was an accident.” The show’s organizer, Megumi Kudo, took a different approach and apologized for the incident. The event was supposed to celebrate her 40 years in professional wrestling, but Singh’s entrance ended up becoming one of the biggest stories coming out of the show. Singh has a long history of terrorizing crowds in Japan, particularly during his famous rivalry with Antonio Inoki. Charging toward spectators with his saber was part of what made him one of the country’s most feared wrestling villains during the 1970s and 1980s. Apparently, turning 82 hasn’t changed his approach. The good news is that the fan escaped without serious injuries. The bad news is that Singh doesn’t seem particularly interested in taking responsibility for what happened. His first appearance in Japan in 14 years ended with someone being rushed to the hospital, and he’s still insisting the guy should have known better than to stand in his way. body: Doha, Qatar – TOD by beIN is expanding its world-class sports offering with the addition of All Elite Wrestling (AEW) , giving fans across the Middle East and North Africa access to one of the fastest-growing wrestling promotions in the world. Known for its high-octane action, compelling storytelling and globally recognised roster, AEW has rapidly built a passionate international fanbase since its launch in 2019 by AEW CEO, GM and Head of Creative Tony Khan. Featuring some of the sport's biggest names, including Will Ospreay, Kenny Omega, MJF, Chris Jericho, Jon Moxley, Adam Copeland, Christian, Mercedes Moné, Darby Allin, Kyle Fletcher, Thekla, Orange Cassidy, Willow Nightingale, Hikaru Shida, Kofi, Austin Creed and many more, AEW has become one of the world's premier wrestling organizations, attracting sold-out arenas, record-breaking pay-per-view events and millions of viewers each week. As wrestling continues to grow in popularity across MENA, TOD by beIN will bring fans weekly episodes of AEW Dynamite and AEW Collision , alongside major live premium events, allowing both long-time followers and newcomers to experience the excitement of the promotion. The upcoming calendar features blockbuster moments, including the highly anticipated AEW All Out event from Chicago on 26 September. For viewers discovering AEW for the first time, the promotion offers a unique blend of world-class athleticism, unforgettable rivalries and larger-than-life personalities, making it one of the most exciting entertainment experiences in global sport today. AEW programming will be available on TOD by beIN across MENA, with weekly episodes and major live events joining the platform's growing catalogue of premium sports and entertainment content.

title: Tyler Breeze Recalls Failed Tag Team Pitch With Xavier Woods

summary_src: Tyler Breeze was on the chopping block early in his NXT tenure when he had his evaluation with Bill DeMott, who was the head trainer at NXT at the time. Speaking to Certified Mark Show, Breeze recalled the evaluation and how it went so poorly that he definitely thought he was getting fired. "If I’m…
body: Tyler Breeze was on the chopping block early in his NXT tenure when he had his evaluation with Bill DeMott, who was the head trainer at NXT at the time. “If I’m going down, I’m going down swinging. He said, ‘You don’t make any pitches.’ That was where I went, ‘Actually, we did make a pitch. You never got back to me on it.’ He goes, ‘What pitch?’ I said, ‘Me and Woods as a tag team.’ He goes, ‘We got back to you guys.’ I said, ‘No, you didn’t. We pitched it. We showed you the gear. We showed you everything. Why did nothing come from it?’ He goes, ‘We told Woods about it.’ I said, ‘Is that right?’ ‘Yeah.’ It was a tiny room, I opened up the door, and I go, ‘Woods, did they ever tell you anything about our tag team?’ He goes, ‘No.’ ‘Okay.’ I look right back at Bill, and I go ‘oof.’ I see what’s happening here and it’s a bunch of bullshit. From there, I got fired up and I started going [pitching multiple things]. As I’m swinging, Canyon (Ceman) goes, ‘Lets end it here before it goes down this path.’ At the time, right before I went and did the evaluation, I had a staph infection that I saw the trainer for. ‘What does this mean?’ ‘You have to go get it drained. You’ll be out for probably two weeks.’ We had this thing; it went horribly. I said, ‘You know what, I have a staph infection; I’ll be back in two weeks.’ I walk out and Woods is like, ‘What is that?’ I said, ‘By far the worst evaluation that anyone could ever get I’m definitely fired. Good knowing you, I guess,'” he said. Woods and Breeze had a short-lived tag team called the Hollywood Express during their time in FCW. The two would reunite as partners on the gaming channel UpUpDownDown. Woods is currently signed to AEW, wrestling as Austin Creed. Breeze is a free agent. Even me and the Forgotten Sons, they would go, ‘Okay, well, what kind of music do you like for your theme song?’ Or, ‘What do you think about — what would you want to do in this match, in this circumstance?’” That was noticeably different from Ryker’s experience after reaching Raw and SmackDown . He said there were times on the main roster when matches were far more tightly controlled. “Instead of, you know, at times on the main roster, Raw and SmackDown, there was a lot of, like, man, micromanaging your matches. And, you know, not all the time, but there was a lot of micromanaging.” Triple H still had the final call in NXT, but Ryker didn’t have a problem with that. In fact, he admitted that when Triple H stepped in and suggested changing something, his idea was usually better anyway. “And it was, you know, Hunter still had the ultimate say-so. If he’d go, ‘Eh, maybe you should try this,’ and if he did that, dude, half of the time what he wanted you to do was going to be better.” For Ryker, the important part was that Triple H was willing to listen before making that call. title: End of an Era: Ex-WWE Star Jaxson Ryker Explains Why He Retired From Wrestling After 23 Years
raw_title: Ex-WWE Star Jaxson Ryker Explains Why He Retired From Wrestling After 23 Years
summary_src: Jaxson Ryker has been offered chances to wrestle again since calling it a career, but don’t expect another comeback match. The former WWE star says he’s perfectly happy staying retired, especially now that his body feels “100 times better” without wrestling.
body: Speaking on Developmentally Speaking , Ryker was asked whether he immediately planned to continue wrestling after WWE released him or if he was already thinking about doing something else. By that point, retirement had already started creeping into his mind because his neck and lower back were giving him serious problems. “No, I think I had in the back of my mind that it was time to start maybe pursuing other things. My body, when I got released from WWE, my body was hurting real bad. I’d had a neck injury and a lower-back injury that was causing some — causing some numbness in my arm and my hand. Just really, really excruciating pain for the most part.” “I always told myself years ago, if I got to where I didn’t enjoy it anymore or my body hurt really bad, I’d walk away on my own. I didn’t want to be 50 and crippled. And so when it happened, man, I was like, ‘Okay, well, what do we do?’” “So, I was like, ‘Let’s just do kind of an independent run. I could go all over these places. I’ve worked for NWA and just do an independent run.’ And that’s basically what I did for the — well, I took three, four months off after they released me because I had a 90-day no-compete clause.” That became what Ryker personally considered his retirement run beginning in 2022. He only worked a handful of matches before finally deciding his body had given him the answer he needed. “And then after that, I started — this was the beginning of 2022 — I started kind of what I called my retirement run. I had a series of six or eight matches and ended in August of 2023. That’s when I had my last match, man. So, I knew it was time to kind of walk away. My body was just not feeling good.” Ryker did get the traditional emotional goodbye when the time came. After his final match, he untied his boots and left them sitting in the ring before heading backstage and realizing that chapter of his life was really over. “No, man. I get asked that quite often. And, you know, of course, when I had that last match and I did the old untie my boots and put them in the ring, and I get to the back and I’m like, ‘This is it.’” That could have easily turned into one of those wrestling retirements that lasts until somebody calls with the right offer. Ryker says those calls have actually come, including from friends and promoters asking if he’d consider getting back in the ring one more time. “But I’ve gotten, even since then, three years ago, I’ve had people call me, buddies of mine, promoters, ‘Hey, man, would you consider one more match?’” So far, none of those offers have tempted him. Ryker says retirement has been good to him physically, and that’s a feeling he’s not interested in giving up just to squeeze another match out of his career. “And I am so content in my retirement life. ’Cause my body feels 100 times better, you know. body: "We're at least 24 hours in, and you know what the biggest thing that is disheartening to me as it stands today, and look, I don't know, Conrad, I am so far on the outside looking in, but obviously Max said it, and I saw the TNA statement. body: Drew McIntyre has never actually seen Elijah Holyfield wrestle, but he still believes the WWE NXT prospect has big things in his future. The son of boxing legend Evander Holyfield, Elijah signed with WWE in 2024 after playing college football at the University of Georgia and having a brief career in the NFL. McIntyre, Jacob Fatu, Royce Keys, Joe Hendry, Ethan Page, and Michael Hayes are among the WWE personalities in the cast. The scripted microdramas are produced like TikTok-style vertical videos. McIntyre described himself as the “right-hand man” of the James Bond-esque main character, who is played by actor Chase Mattson. “It’s fun, It’s a really fun watch,” McIntyre told Van Vliet. “Hopefully everyone goes into it with that idea. Like, I’m about to have a little fun watch. You might be surprised about the romantic elements, the comedic elements, and at the center there is heart. And it is a very fun watch.” McIntyre should be returning to WWE programming soon after taking several months away as his Hollywood profile continues to grow. title: Legal Watch: Keanu Carver’s Protection Order Extended as Court Pushes Arianna Grace Hearing Back
raw_title: Keanu Carver’s Protection Order Extended as Court Pushes Arianna Grace Hearing Back
summary_src: Keanu Carver’s legal problems aren’t going away anytime soon. The former WWE NXT star was supposed to be back in court on October 20 over the protection-order case involving Arianna Grace, but that hearing has now been pushed back another month.
body: According to court records obtained by Ringside News , new filings entered on October 19 show that Carver, whose real name is Kevin Robertson, will now have his next injunction review on November 17, 2026, at 9:00 AM before Judge Bryanna Bynum at the Criminal Justice Center in Sanford, Florida. The docket shows that Robertson’s attorney filed an unopposed motion to continue the hearing on October 19. A notice of appearance was also filed on behalf of Robertson that same day. The court subsequently issued an order continuing the temporary injunction and scheduling the November hearing. The October 19 order is listed in the court docket as follows: “ORDER CONTINUING TEMPORARY INJUNCTION SET FOR 11/17/2026 AT 9AM @ CJC CR-4A; JUDGE BYNUM” That means the existing temporary protection order remains in place while both sides wait for their next day in court. Under the previously issued injunction, Robertson is prohibited from contacting Grace, whose real name is Bianca Carelli, and must remain at least 500 feet away from her. As Ringside News previously covered , Carelli filed her petition on September 14, accusing Robertson of stalking, harassment and domestic violence. A judge granted a temporary injunction that same day before continuing it following a September 22 hearing. The October 20 date was supposed to be the next opportunity for the court to review the matter. The case has already produced some troubling allegations. Text messages previously covered by Ringside News showed Carelli repeatedly telling Robertson to stop contacting her, stay away from her home and respect her boundaries. The latest court documents confirm that the civil case remains open. The temporary injunction has not been dissolved, and the October 19 continuance does not amount to a final ruling on Carelli’s allegations. The records provided also do not establish that Robertson has been criminally charged. So while Carver’s WWE run appears to be over, the legal battle is far from finished. Another hearing has been pushed back, the temporary restrictions remain in place, and Robertson now has until November 17 before the case is scheduled to return to Judge Bynum’s courtroom. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Opens Up On Who Really Came Up With His Viral “I Prayed for This” CM Punk Line
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Reveals Who Really Came Up With His Viral “I Prayed for This” CM Punk Line
summary_src: Drew McIntyre’s “I prayed for this, and it happened” line about CM Punk is still all over the internet, but there’s a secret behind that infamous insult. It turns out Drew wasn’t even the one who came up with it.
body: “I mean, I knew talking to Triple H during the day that this is going to be so good. Like, I had an idea and it was too much. It would have offended a lot of people, which I’m very good at.” Drew explained that Triple H helped him pull back from his original idea before personally coming up with the line that would eventually become one of the most memorable insults of their entire feud. “He helped me reel it back, and then Hunter himself came out with the line which I ended up using, cuz I had such an extreme version and he dialed it back.” And Triple H wasn’t finished there. According to McIntyre, Hunter actually demonstrated how he should say it. Drew was so impressed that he decided to copy the delivery exactly. “I knew in that moment when Hunter delivered the line by toning me down a little bit, I went, ‘Wow, that is genius.’ Cuz I’m going to use that exact tone.” That’s where things got particularly nasty. Instead of coming out screaming about how much he hated Punk, McIntyre wanted to sound like he actually felt bad for him. He started the promo by talking about how devastating injuries can be, only to reveal that he was thrilled Punk had gotten hurt. The result was the infamous “I prayed for this, and it happened” moment. What started as a vicious shot at an injured CM Punk became an internet meme, with people using Drew’s face and those words for everything from sports victories to everyday situations. McIntyre admitted he knew the line would work when Triple H first suggested it, but he never imagined it would still be everywhere years later. “I didn’t think I’d be seeing it to this day for everything, no matter like what, if it’s sports or it’s well outside of wrestling, outside of wrestling. It’s constantly, it’s me pointing, ‘I prayed for this and it happened.’” Of course, the line was only one part of Drew’s bitter rivalry with Punk. The two spent months attacking each other on WWE television, social media and in interviews before settling things inside Hell in a Cell at WWE Bad Blood 2024. Even after their feud ended, McIntyre has continued taking personal shots at Punk . Drew also made it clear that the reason their rivalry worked so well was because neither man needed to pretend they liked the other. “There was a lot of, you know, programs, rivalries that were very big and spectacular and had their moments. Ours was just consistent. And to this day, it was consistent hatred. And people can feel that. You get two guys that are good at their job. They don’t have to like each other, but they understand when they’re in there, they’ll be professional.” So Triple H gave Drew McIntyre the line that turned into one of WWE’s biggest memes, and Drew made sure nobody would forget it. The crazy part is that McIntyre apparently had something even more offensive ready to go before Hunter talked him out of it. Now that might be the one promo idea Drew should explain next. title: Dave Scherer Discusses AAA's Success and Ladder Safety
raw_title: Is War Games Becoming A Trope, Moves That Shouldn’T Be Done From A Ladder, AAA Is Fun And More
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-10-20 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . Did the WWF ever give serious consideration to main eventing a PPV with a one-on-one match between Hulk Hogan and Ted DiBiase? Not that I am aware of. Hell, they never even put the Title on him so I doubt they were looking to do him vs. Hogan on PPV back then. AAA has great action and solid storytelling. Anyone looking to product a wrestling show could learn from that. It’s the backbone of what makes a company successful. If the wrestlers are going to do dives off the top of a ladder, wouldn't it be safer to have them stand with their feet perpendicular to the top step, rather than parallel? Ability level aside, the way Tiffany Stratton was balancing on the top of that ladder looked awkward and she didn't appear completely comfortable. They should do dives in a way where the ladder is as stable as possible. In Stratton’s case, it was not even close as the ladder was moving as she was launching. Also, rather that do any flip move that requires torque off of a ladder, splashes make much more sense to me. You leave the ladder and immediately go downward, rather than trying to get height off of it. Personally I agree with the reader that feels War Games has had its day. If it happens every year in November without fail then we know it's a crutch for the booking to go down the route of two groups feuding for months and needing War Games to settle it. The best Survivor Series event I ever saw was 2002 which also didn't have the traditional survivor matches. It had an amazing card and was capped off with the first elimination chamber. Would we not be better off with a less is more approach with all these matches? The fact that it’s done because it’s November is an issue when the creative leading up to it isn’t great, for sure. We don’t seem to notice that when the booking is strong and the fans want to see the talents in the cage. But I agree, right now it’s more of a trope and that should never be the case with a match like that. That’s all on creative. Sure, there are politics involved as well, but it comes down to whether Creative wants to pull the trigger or not. You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com .
summary: Per PWInsider, Dave Scherer praised AAA for delivering great action paired with solid storytelling that serves as the foundation for a successful wrestling company. He also questioned whether WarGames is turning into a trope and suggested safer positioning for wrestlers performing dives from the top of ladders after observing Tiffany Stratton's balance on the structure.

title: Comeback Watch: Drew McIntyre Teases New Moves and More Violence for His WWE Return
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Teases New Moves and More Violence for His WWE Return
summary_src: Drew McIntyre hasn’t wrestled in WWE since WrestleMania 42, but he’s already planning some surprises for when he gets back. The former WWE Champion has spent months working on his body, and he’s now moving better than he did in his 20s.
body: Speaking during an interview with Chris Van Vliet on INSIGHT , McIntyre explained that his time away from WWE has allowed him to completely change how he trains. Instead of simply focusing on getting bigger, he’s been putting serious work into his footwork, balance, flexibility and conditioning. “I’ve been working out a lot. Like I’ve been building my body from the ground up, like improving my, you know, foundation. I didn’t realize how important it was till the past year and I’ve got like a great base now.” McIntyre said he’s been training barefoot and working with his trainer to improve his stability. That’s made a huge difference in how he moves, especially considering he’s now heavier than he’s ever been. “I’ve been working real hard in a way that my cardio and agility is, I’d say my whole life, but really for sure the past 12 years, is right now the best I’ve been. Like I feel great agility-wise. Bigger than I’ve ever been. I’m moving better than I have.” And Drew isn’t kidding about getting bigger. He revealed that he now weighs 285 pounds after gaining another 10 pounds of muscle. Despite the added size, he believes he’s in better physical condition than he was before stepping away from WWE. The improvements have also given McIntyre some ideas about what he wants to do when he starts wrestling again. He explained that people have been sending him old clips of his matches, and some of the moves he used to perform actually surprised him. “I’ve got a feeling some of my offense is going to be unique. I saw some videos of myself people had sent me, were highlight videos, and I was like, I didn’t realize I did that. Guess I’m going to start stealing for myself.” That doesn’t mean Drew is simply going to repeat everything he used to do. He believes his improved conditioning will allow him to perform some of those moves even better than he did when he was younger. “Forgot I did half the moves, and I physically can do them easily now and probably better than I did them when I was in my 20s.” McIntyre has already given people a glimpse of his progress. As Ringside News previously covered , he shared footage of himself running the ropes in September, showing that he was back inside a wrestling ring despite his extended absence from television. That video picked up millions of views, and Drew said people have been asking when he’s coming back ever since. But while he’s clearly preparing for an eventual return, he isn’t letting anyone rush him. “I know the audience, our fans are wanting me back. I see the messages every day and I appreciate it. I appreciate it. Just give me a little second and I’ll be back. Just a little second. When I decide.” McIntyre has been keeping busy with acting projects during his WWE absence, and he made it clear that Hollywood Drew isn’t finished yet. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Opens Up On Insane Sword Attack He Pitched to Vince McMahon for WWE
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Reveals Insane Sword Attack He Pitched to Vince McMahon for WWE
summary_src: Drew McIntyre carried a massive sword to the ring for years in WWE, but he never got to do the one thing he really wanted with it. He actually pitched Vince McMahon an idea that involved chopping someone’s arm off on television.
body: Speaking during an interview with Chris Van Vliet on INSIGHT , McIntyre revealed that he wanted to pull off a brutal sword attack using the same kind of practical effects seen in Saving Private Ryan . The idea was to make it look like he had actually severed someone’s arm, and he took the pitch directly to McMahon. “I also pitched, you know, to the big man himself. I was like, hey, you know, in Saving Private Ryan, and he, Vince, had never seen Saving Private Ryan.” That made things a little awkward because Drew was counting on Vince understanding the reference. McIntyre explained that the movie used performers with amputations to create realistic-looking injuries, and he wanted WWE to try something similar. His plan was to have a fight break out, possibly at WrestleMania, before moving the action backstage. WWE would then switch to a pre-recorded segment where Drew would finally use his sword on another person. “I think Mania or something. We should have a fight sequence. We end up backstage. Then we hit the pretape where I swing the sword at somebody.” “And finally, all those years later, Agent of Shadows, Drew McIntyre is going to go shanking. I’m stabbing some people. Finally.” McIntyre also explained that working on Highlander made him realize he should have taken sword-fighting lessons back when he carried the weapon on WWE television. After learning from professional stunt teams, he was amazed at how much he could actually do with one. As for his WWE entrance, McIntyre hasn’t completely ruled out bringing the sword back . He still has a personal attachment to the weapon, which was named Angela after his late mother, but felt it no longer fit the darker direction his character had taken. So Vince McMahon never gave Drew McIntyre the green light to chop someone’s arm off on WWE television, but Drew eventually got to swing a sword at people in Hollywood instead. Considering how far he wanted to take the original angle, it’s probably one of the more outrageous pitches that never made it onto WWE television. STAMFORD, Conn. & INDIANAPOLIS, Ind., June 24, 2024 – WWE and Indiana Sports Corp today announced a first-of-its-kind partnership that will bring WWE’s three largest stadium events – WrestleMania , SummerSlam and Royal Rumble – to Indianapolis. Kicking off with Royal Rumble on February 1, 2025, Lucas Oil Stadium will host all three Premium Live Events including a two-night SummerSlam and two-night WrestleMania in future years. “Indianapolis is a fantastic city for major events and we’re excited to invite the WWE Universe to Lucas Oil Stadium for Royal Rumble in 2025, and a future SummerSlam and WrestleMania,” said Chris Legentil, WWE EVP, Talent Relations & Head of Communications at WWE. “Patrick and the team at Indiana Sports Corp have done a phenomenal job bolstering local economics and tourism, and we’re proud to partner with them to shine a light on the great state of Indiana.” WWE and Indiana Sports Corp will also work with community partners across the state to create a legacy program that will leave an impact well beyond the three Premium Live Events. More details will be announced at a later date. Since its inception in 1979, Indiana Sports Corp has hosted more than 500 national and international sporting events, including Super Bowl XLVI, the College Football Playoff National Championship, Men’s & Women’s NCAA Final Fours and 11 Big Ten Football Championship Games. In total, these events have led to more than $4 billion in direct spending in the community. Ahead of the general on-sale date for Royal Rumble 2025, which will be announced at a later date, fans can register now to receive an exclusive presale offer by visiting https://www.wwe.com/royalrumble-2025-presale .

title: Top 50 good guys in wrestling history
raw_title: Top 50 good guys in wrestling history - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Some folks might try to tell you it’s the villains that make sports-entertainment fun. And why not? It’s the baddies in the black hats who get to throw fireballs, electrocute millionaires and run people over with monster trucks. But it’s the good guys who give the fans something to believe in, a hero to look up to and a reminder that, more often than not, good does triumph over evil. Here, we present the 50 Superstars that wrestling fans grew up admiring — and still do today. ( PHOTOS ) Agree? Disagree? Let us hear about on the WWE Classics Facebook page . Diamond Dallas Page’s career in sports-entertainment is well-documented — from the moment he drove the Pink Cadillac carrying Rhythm & Blues to the ring at WrestleMania VI, to his legendary rivalry with “Macho Man” Randy Savage. Beloved by WCW fans and the WWE Universe, the New Jersey native represented a working class hero — a tireless competitor who earned every accolade. Following the formation of The New World Order, DDP was one of the first WCW competitors to stand up to the notorious faction, becoming an “everyman hero” as he outright refused to join their ranks. During his heated rivalry with “Macho Man,” Page defended both his honor and that of his wife, Kimberly, against Savage’s brutish, nWo-inspired tactics. No matter the odds, DDP never backed down from a fight, earning the moniker of “WCW’s People’s Champion.” ( WATCH ) Quick and agile despite being one of the most muscular grapplers of his era, Johnson’s smooth moves helped him become a popular attraction in areas of the country that were still struggling with segregation. The racial barriers Johnson broke are remembered today, but “Soul Man” wasn’t motivated by politics — he just wanted to entertain. “What set my dad apart from a lot of guys wasn’t the fact that he was this incredible black wrestler,” Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson once said of his WWE Hall of Fame father. “It was just that he was a great wrestler.” — RYAN MURPHY “My dad was a local hero,” The Road Dogg said of his legendary father, Bob Armstrong. A major star in Alabama and Georgia during the ’60s and ’70s, the WWE Hall of Famer’s “salt of the earth” appeal endeared him to Southern fans who favored substance over style. “He was one of them,” WWE official Scott Armstrong added. “He came from very humble beginnings and never hid that. He got up in the morning and had fried eggs and grits and gravy and did his thing.” A champion not only to folks in Dixie, but to his four sons — Brian, Brad, Scott, and Steve — the blue collar "Bullet” had his boys behind him when he took on rivals like Roddy Piper ( WATCH ) and Bobby Duncum, who he battled in a 1973 gorefest in The Omni Coliseum. “My father had a white singlet on and it was stained red,” Road Dogg vividly remembered. “He had to go the hospital and have a blood transfusion, but my father won and we won a 1974 Cadillac.” — R.M. title: Is War Games Becoming A Trope, Moves That Shouldn’t Be Done From A Ladder, Aaa Is Fun And More
raw_title: IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-10-20 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . Did the WWF ever give serious consideration to main eventing a PPV with a one-on-one match between Hulk Hogan and Ted DiBiase? Not that I am aware of. Hell, they never even put the Title on him so I doubt they were looking to do him vs. Hogan on PPV back then. AAA has great action and solid storytelling. Anyone looking to product a wrestling show could learn from that. It’s the backbone of what makes a company successful. If the wrestlers are going to do dives off the top of a ladder, wouldn't it be safer to have them stand with their feet perpendicular to the top step, rather than parallel? Ability level aside, the way Tiffany Stratton was balancing on the top of that ladder looked awkward and she didn't appear completely comfortable. They should do dives in a way where the ladder is as stable as possible. In Stratton’s case, it was not even close as the ladder was moving as she was launching. Also, rather that do any flip move that requires torque off of a ladder, splashes make much more sense to me. You leave the ladder and immediately go downward, rather than trying to get height off of it. Personally I agree with the reader that feels War Games has had its day. If it happens every year in November without fail then we know it's a crutch for the booking to go down the route of two groups feuding for months and needing War Games to settle it. The best Survivor Series event I ever saw was 2002 which also didn't have the traditional survivor matches. It had an amazing card and was capped off with the first elimination chamber. Would we not be better off with a less is more approach with all these matches? The fact that it’s done because it’s November is an issue when the creative leading up to it isn’t great, for sure. We don’t seem to notice that when the booking is strong and the fans want to see the talents in the cage. But I agree, right now it’s more of a trope and that should never be the case with a match like that. That’s all on creative. Sure, there are politics involved as well, but it comes down to whether Creative wants to pull the trigger or not. You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com .

title: In Memoriam: Famed wrestler ‘Pac’ died at 40 of an asthma attack in Des Plaines, officials say
raw_title: Famed wrestler ‘Pac’ died at 40 of an asthma attack in Des Plaines, officials say
body: A famed professional wrestler who died last month after a match in the Chicago suburbs suffered a fatal asthma attack, authorities confirmed Monday. Benjamin Satterley, 40, who performed under the name “Pac,” was found dead Sept. 27 in Des Plaines. An autopsy revealed the respiratory condition caused his death, the Cook County medical examiner’s office said. Satterley’s body was spotted in a rental car on the 2700 block of Mannheim Road, less than one mile from O’Hare International Airport. Satterley was alone and in the driver’s seat when he was found, authorities said, and there were no signs of foul play. A respiratory inhaler was found in a backpack in the car’s trunk, a Des Plaines police spokesperson said Monday. Satterley was part of Florida-based All Elite Wrestling. He was in the Chicago area that weekend for the company’s All Out promotion at the Now Arena in Hoffman Estates. Satterley previously had wrestled in other organizations, including in WWE under the ring names “Adrian Neville” and then “Neville.” Over 28 million people in the U.S. have asthma, according to the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America. It can be triggered by pollution, allergens, stress and other factors. On average, between 9 and 11 people in the U.S. die from asthma daily, the foundation reports. Avoiding triggers, taking medications to prevent symptoms and being prepared to treat asthma episodes if they occur are the best ways to manage asthma, the foundation said.
summary: Per Chicago Tribune: a famed professional wrestler who died last month after a match in the Chicago suburbs suffered a fatal asthma attack, authorities made official Monday. Benjamin Satterley, 40, who performed under the name Pac, was found dead Sept. 27 in Des Plaines.

title: Tiger Jeet Singh accidentally injures fan with sword

summary_src: Tiger Jeet Singh recently returned to Japan in what was said to be his first wrestling-related appearance in the country in 14 years. However, the moment will likely not be remembered by most in attendance as a triumphant return.
body: Link Image from the Tiger Jeet Singh Foundation’s Facebook page Tiger Jeet Singh recently returned to Japan in what was said to be his first wrestling-related appearance in the country in 14 years. However, the moment will likely not be remembered by most in attendance as a triumphant return. While seeing the 82-year-old icon was surely a highlight for fans, the October 17th appearance at the Yoyogi National Stadium Gymnasium No. 2 in Shibuya, Japan, was marred by Singh accidentally injuring a fan with his sword. Japanese media reported that as Singh made his way to the ring while wildly swinging his trademark saber, the blade made contact with a fan’s forehead, and medical personnel at the venue attended to the man before an ambulance was called. According to Sports Hochi , the man was treated at a nearby hospital, but fortunately his injury was said to be minor. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right?” Singh said to Tokyo Sports . “All he had to do was get out of my way.” The Indian star’s son, former WWE star Tiger Ali Singh , backed up his father. “The announcer was saying, ‘Please be careful!’ They were warning him it was dangerous, but he didn’t move out of the way,” Tiger said. “I’m sure he won’t make the same mistake again. Just like my father said, this was an accident.” “I believe there were shortcomings in our corner team setup,” the Japanese star said at a post-show press conference. “I deeply apologize for injuring the fans who came to enjoy the show. I’m truly sorry. I think you were able to see the Shin you all wanted to see. However, I’m truly sorry that he [the fan] got injured. title: On the Record: Drew McIntyre Opens Up On His Wife Keeps Adopting Cats While He’s Away Filming

summary_src: Drew McIntyre might be busy building a Hollywood career, but his wife has apparently been building something of her own back home — a small army of cats. The former WWE Champion revealed that his wife, Kaitlyn Galloway, has adopted two rescue cats while he’s been away working on movies.
body: “Big cat, fat, fat black cat, massive. And I was just like, how is this cat living on the street and so massive, but the whole neighborhood was feeding him. He was in the HOA page. His name was Stormy because he lived in the storm drain.” Kaitlyn had already been letting the cat into their garage and feeding him, but Drew didn’t realize she had bigger plans. While he was on a flight, he happened to notice a message on the neighborhood page announcing that Stormy was getting adopted. The name of the person taking him in looked awfully familiar. “Oh, cool. That’s weird. It’s the same name as my wife. I started communicating with her and she’s like, ‘Yeah, I’ve got some news.’ I said, ‘What news would that be?’ ‘Yeah, we’re taking him in and it’s happening, so deal with it.’” That idea didn’t survive negotiations with his wife. Drew also suggested Donatello and considered Boomer because the cat was so big and constantly made noise running around the house. They eventually settled on something much simpler. “But we somehow we landed on Jasper. So he’s Jasper now. And he’s so large, maybe even larger. Just eats everything in sight.” “Then I found out later, okay, we got some news. We got another cat. She was outside in the cold. What was I supposed to do? And I was like, okay, we find another home or something. No, no, she lives with us now. But you get to pick the name.” Drew wasn’t exactly buying that naming arrangement anymore, considering how things went with Jasper. This time, however, the couple agreed on Penny Lane. McIntyre admitted that the newest addition doesn’t always treat him as nicely as she treats his wife. “We collaborated and we came to Penny Lane. Like she’s kind of copper color and occasionally she’s nasty to me and loves her, so I call her Penny Dreadful. But yeah, we’re building an army of cats.” The new additions come after McIntyre suffered the loss of his beloved cat Chaz earlier this year . Drew explained that Chaz’s memory is still part of their home, and Jasper has already picked up some of his old habits, including hanging around the dinner table looking for food. McIntyre confirmed that the household now has three cats, but he’s not convinced the number will stay there. In fact, he joked that if Kaitlyn keeps this up, his retirement plans might have less to do with wrestling and more to do with running a cat sanctuary. “These cat cafes and we’re going to end up owning one 100% or cat farm. Come here. Be my friend.’ And Jasper has ended up being my buddy.” Of course, this isn’t the first time the McIntyre household has taken in a rescue cat . Recently, speaking to Sam Roberts on Not Sam Wrestling, WWE NXT Champion Grayson Waller opened up about how he had planned to use that photograph on his T-shirt to generate heat and mentally challenge Vaquer's boyfriend, Myles Borne. "There are some that haven't ended up on TV," Waller said when asked if a T-shirt he's made couldn't be worn on TV . "Stephanie Vaquer kind of broke the internet recently. She did an Instagram story posing like Shawn Michaels. "There was a t-shirt with that on it. That didn't end up on television. If anyone wants it, bribe me with some money. There is some fan who would pay some crazy money for it. I love to cause chaos, but if we can't fight about this, there is the line. Stephanie Vaquer doesn't feel like I should be doing that, are we going to have a match? That's not going to happen. That's where my line is," he finished. Wearing a Vaquer T-shirt would not have been new for Waller, who has in the past worn T-shirts referencing his opponents Zilla Fatu, Cruz Montana, and others. However, despite the perfect opportunity to amp up his level as a heel, WWE did not allow Waller to go ahead with the idea. Waller is now scheduled to defend his WWE NXT Championship against Tony D'Angelo at NXT Halloween Havoc.
summary: WWE NXT Champion Grayson Waller planned a T-shirt featuring Stephanie Vaquer's recent viral Instagram photo to create heat and target her boyfriend Myles Borne. The shirt was ultimately not allowed to appear on television. Waller discussed the decision during an interview with Sam Roberts on Not Sam Wrestling, noting there are limits to the chaos he aims to cause.

body: Speedball Mike Bailey says that there are absolutely no half measures when it comes to Will Ospreay, noting he does not hesitate. Ospreay is currently the AEW World Champion and the leader of the US branch of the United Empire faction, which Speedball is a part of alongside Andrade El Idolo, the Brawling Birds and Francisco Akira. While speaking to The Wrestling Classic in a new interview , Speedball Mike Bailey spoke about Will Ospreay, noting that the AEW World Champion does not hesitate in the ring. “There are absolutely no half measures with Will Ospreay. There is nothing that he does, not a single movement, not a decision that he hesitates on. Everything is 100%, and I mean, that gets him in trouble sometimes. You see him overcommit, make decisions a bit too fast, and that might be his one flaw. But I mean, watching him go is absolutely impressive. The commitment and force with which he moves forwards, and that’s something that the first time we wrestled, which was at PWG in 2015, I could feel about Will Ospreay, and it’s something that he has maintained to this day. That has taken him to where he is now, which is AEW World Champion, the best wrestler in the world.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: On the Record: Booker T Says WWE Wrestlers Were Afraid of Getting Backstage Heat for Taking Naps
raw_title: Booker T Says WWE Wrestlers Were Afraid of Getting Backstage Heat for Taking Naps
summary_src: Booker T was warned pretty early into his WWE run that taking a nap backstage could get him heat, but he wasn’t about to lose any sleep over it. Instead of following the unwritten rule, Booker deliberately tested it by telling Jim Ross exactly where he was going to sleep. Speaking on the Hall of ...
body: “I would just find a corner and go to sleep, you know. But I remember — I always think about the first time when I got to WWE, and I was in the locker room and I was nodding off, you know, and I was catching a nap.” “And this guy came in. He was so scared, and he goes, ‘Hey, Book, you know, hey man, I wouldn’t do that around here if I was you.’ And I go, ‘What?’ He goes, ‘Taking a nap. That’s not cool. You can get a lot of heat.’ And I go, ‘Taking a nap?’ He goes, ‘Yeah.’” Booker wasn’t exactly terrified by the warning. If anything, hearing how serious the other wrestler was about it made him want to find out whether this supposed rule was actually real. “Okay. And he was scared. He was really frightened, to the point where I go, ‘Let me test this theory, because I’m going to take a nap or they’re going to have to fire me.’ Right?” Booker didn’t quietly sneak away to see if anybody would notice either. Since Jim Ross was the person who signed his WWE contract, Booker decided to go straight to him and basically announce that he was about to break this supposed backstage rule. “So, the person that signed my contract was JR — Jim Ross. I remember walking after this guy told me that. I left, I was walking out, and I passed Jim Ross and I said, ‘Hey, Jim.’ He goes, ‘Yeah, Book.’ I said, ‘If anybody’s looking for me, I’ll be in my car taking a nap.’” Ross’ reaction wasn’t exactly the dressing-down Booker had been warned about. He simply acknowledged him and let Booker carry on. “He goes, ‘All right.’ I kept walking. And he didn’t say nothing.” That was pretty much all Booker needed to hear. As far as he was concerned, if one of the top people involved in bringing him to WWE didn’t care, he wasn’t going to worry about some mysterious backstage heat. “So, I said, ‘I’m going to go to the top guy and test this theory, because if I can’t take a nap, somebody’s going to come and tell me why I can’t take a nap.’” Booker also didn’t see sleeping as him being lazy backstage. He viewed it as part of getting himself physically ready to perform later that night. “Because me taking a nap is me preparing for tonight. I’m getting ready.” If WWE actually had a problem with that, Booker wanted somebody with authority to explain the logic to him. Apparently, that conversation never happened. “And when someone could, you know, tell me why I can’t prepare and get ready for tonight — because I don’t practice. I don’t do a lot of stuff like that like a lot of those guys did — somebody got to tell me. Somebody got to explain it.” In the end, Booker’s little experiment apparently settled the issue for good. He kept taking his naps, nobody came looking to punish him for it, and the supposed backstage rule never became a problem again. “And no one ever explained it to me. And no one ever said anything to me about taking naps, you know, my whole career.” Booker basically called WWE’s backstage bluff on day one and never heard another word about it. title: Injury Update: WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW
raw_title: WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW
body: 01:00 Featured Video Usos Call Out 946 📢 WWE Rumors on Scary Bron Breakker Fall, R-Truth's Injury vs. Damian Priest and Ilja Dragunov in AEW Mike Chiari Oct 20, 2026 Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe and All Elite Wrestling. R-Truth Speaks After Injury Bleacher Report 21h Breakker Should Be WWE's Monster Heel Bleacher Report 2d Full Grades from Latest Raw Bleacher Report 10m Bron Breakker avoided injury despite a scary fall from the top rope during a match at a WWE live event on Saturday night. Teaming with fellow Vision members Bronson Reed and Austin Theory against Oba Femi, LA Knight and Penta in the main event, Breakker lost his footing on the top rope during a spot with Knight and appeared to land awkwardly on his neck: Breakker was fortunately fine after the spot, as evidenced by the fact that he competed in a hard-hitting singles match against Penta on Monday night's episode of Raw. According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), there was "no heat" on anyone for the spot that went awry, as it was considered "a simple sort of mistake." WrestleVotes added that people backstage in WWE decided to "no-sell" the situation rather than making it a major talking point within the company. Given his high-impact style, Breakker does have a penchant for putting himself in harm's way at times during his matches. At the same time, his speed, explosiveness and athleticism are what set him apart from most other Superstars, so it makes sense for him to lean into it. Breakker was lucky to walk away from the fall with nothing significantly wrong with him, and the fact that he is already back in the ring and performing at a high level is a good sign that he should be OK moving forward. Damian Priest was reportedly the one who made the decision to end his match against R-Truth early on SmackDown last week. According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t WrestlePurists ), Priest "made the call" to quickly move to the finish once he realized that Truth had gotten injured. When Truth was unable to get up after executing a missile dropkick, Priest calmly spoke to the referee and went outside the ring to grab a steel chair. That allowed Fraxiom time to run down and protect Truth from Priest, prompting Priest to leave the ring without inflicting further damage. On Monday, Truth posted a photo of himself on X, seemingly preparing to undergo an MRI: Truth noted in the post that he is "OK," while joking that Priest "tried to kill" him. Priest and Truth held the WWE Tag Team Championships together from March until dropping them to The MFTs in August. Despite that run of success, Priest turned on Truth shortly after they lost the championships, noting within the storyline that he felt Truth was holding him back. A former world heavyweight champion, Priest is now able to portray a more serious character once again, and it could help him move back up the card in the singles ranks on SmackDown.

title: AJ Francis Claims AJ Styles Has Been Ducking Him for Years
raw_title: AJ Francis Claims AJ Styles Has Been Ducking Him for Years
summary_src: AJ Francis isn’t backing down from his claim that he’s the greatest AJ in TNA history, and now he’s calling out AJ Styles for supposedly avoiding him.
body: “I think AJ Styles agrees with me that I’m the greatest AJ that ever stepped in TNA because if he didn’t agree with me, he’d actually do something about it and he’s been ducking me for years. So I don’t think that he actually disagrees. I think he agrees I’m the greatest AJ to ever step foot in TNA. And you know, AJ Styles been ducking me for years.” “You know, Avery’s apparently ducking me because Frankie Kazarian’s telling him to. You know, maybe, just maybe, ducking is what runs in the Styles family. Maybe, you know, if it’s blood deep, blood in, blood out. Maybe they scared of AJ Francis on that family tree because they know I chopped that shit down.” The conversation then turned to Avery getting opportunities because of his famous father. Francis actually defended Avery’s position in TNA, explaining that he has no problem with second-generation wrestlers benefiting from their family connections. However, that doesn’t mean he’s planning to go easy on him if they ever meet inside the ring. When the interviewer pointed out that Francis still wanted to beat up Avery, he made his intentions clear. “Oh, I beat the shit out of Avery Styles for sure. I beat him. I give him the ass whooping his daddy fucking gave him a long time ago.” Francis was then told that facing Avery would be an opportunity to see whether the young wrestler could handle the pressure. He wasn’t interested in giving Avery much of a chance. “No, he gonna sink. He going to sink. Put belt to ass. I’m from the 90s. In the 90s, we used to beat children. You know what I’m saying? I was one of them children that used to get beat.” For now, these are Francis’ claims, and there’s nothing establishing that AJ Styles has actually been avoiding him. Still, Francis seems determined to get a confrontation with someone in the Styles family, whether that’s the father or the son. title: Keanu Carver Released By WWE
raw_title: KEANU CARVER RELEASED BY WWE
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS KEANU CARVER RELEASED BY WWE By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-05 11:34:00 WWE NXT star Keanu Carver was removed from WWE's internal roster and is gone from the company, PWInsider.com has learned. Carver (real name Kevin Robertson) was served with an order of protection preventing him from contacting a contracted WWE NXT talent (who PWInsider.com is not naming) after she filed for the order against him, alleging Carver, who she was formerly involved with, had stalked her and engaged in domestic violence. The talent filed for the order on 9/14 and it was ruled on 9/22 during a court hearing that the order would continue. PostWrestling.com was the first to report on the matter. Their report noted: "The petition alleges that the petitioner and Robertson dated and that the relationship recently ended. In the days that followed the breakup, Robertson allegedly made a series of unwanted visits to the petitioner’s home and made unwanted calls to the petitioner, as many as 44 times in one day. The 49-page filing includes many screenshots showing calls to the petitioner and stills from a security camera outside the petitioner’s home depicting Robertson’s alleged repeated unwelcome visits." The petition details multiple alleged incidents of unwanted visits and calls after their break-up. The petitioner says that Robertson came to the petitioner’s home on September 4 at 7 a.m., “intoxicated and under the influence of drugs and alcohol.” The petition does not specify what “drugs” Robertson was allegedly using. On September 8, the filing claims that Robertson again returned to the petitioner’s residence when the petitioner was not there. Robertson allegedly waited at the door. When he found the petitioner in their car, the petitioner tried to put the vehicle in reverse to drive away. He allegedly grabbed the vehicle, said he needed help, and “said he had drugs on him and he saw cops and his phone was 1% and he had no way to get home.” The petition claims Robertson returned to the petitioner’s home later in the night, knocked on the door, and circled the residence “all night long, finally leaving around 8 am or so.” The next day, on September 9, the petitioner claims Robertson called “a total of 25 times” and came to the petitioner’s residence when no one was home. Robertson allegedly returned again early the next morning at 2:01 a.m. The petition states Robertson proceeded to knock on the door “[a]ll night long” again, and “called my phone from a blocked number, called me on x (FKA twitter), made incoherent sounds, circled my apartment building.” Carver took to his Twitter account on 9/29, writing, "yall gone sound dumb ash in a month" and "Fake ass virtue signaling mfs everything done inna dark come to light" before later deleting the tweets and writing, "Keep god first" before deleting that and his Twitter account. There is a court hearing on 10/20 in regard to the issue in Seminole County, Florida.

title: Backstage Buzz: AJ Francis Claims He Got Backstage Heat in WWE Because a Celebrity Wanted to Meet Him Instead of Brock Lesnar
raw_title: AJ Francis Claims He Got Backstage Heat in WWE Because a Celebrity Wanted to Meet Him Instead of Brock Lesnar
summary_src: AJ Francis says he actually got himself into trouble backstage in WWE because someone wanted to meet him instead of Brock Lesnar or Randy Orton. That’s right, according to the former Top Dolla, simply having a celebrity guest request him was enough to upset people behind the scenes.
body: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis discussed why he’s much happier working for TNA than he was during his time in WWE. He explained that TNA recognizes his contributions and gives him opportunities to show what he can do. That wasn’t always his experience in WWE, where he believes his own popularity sometimes worked against him. “You know, when I was, you know, in WWE, sometimes you become a victim of your own success. Like, Expressions, who’s with me now in TNA. I remember one time I got a little bit of heat in WWE because when Expressions was backstage as like a celebrity fan before Money in the Bank in London, they asked him who did he want to see and he could have saw Brock Lesnar, he could have saw Randy Orton and he said Top Dolla and they’re like why do you want to see Top Dolla? Like what is, what is, what do you want to see him for?” Francis believes the entire situation showed how differently he was viewed in WWE compared to TNA. Instead of being pleased that a guest wanted to meet him, he claims people were questioning why anyone would make that choice. “So, it’s like I was a victim of success back then that I had fans. You know what I’m saying? And then now that narrative’s completely changed. Now, when I’m in TNA, I get an opportunity to show exactly how good I am. And now people are starting to realize how good I am.” The situation also marked the beginning of Francis’ friendship with Expressions. Francis explained that Expressions had already been following his career since Hit Row’s time in NXT, but their relationship became much closer after that initial meeting. “So he booked his own travel to Slammiversary. We teed it up and then he did my entrance at Slammiversary and that got like 5 million views across all social media. And you know, from that point on, the rest is history.” Francis now has Expressions working alongside him in TNA, and he believes the partnership has been a success. More importantly, he feels the company values the connections and creativity he brings instead of questioning why someone would want to work with him. Francis didn’t identify which WWE personnel allegedly gave him heat over the Money in the Bank incident, so his account remains his side of what happened. Either way, he’s making it clear that he hasn’t forgotten how he was treated during his WWE run, especially when he compares it to the opportunities he’s getting in TNA.
