title: Meltzer Shares Details On Pac's Lung Problems
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Details Past Health Issues Faced By Late AEW Star Pac
summary_src: Benjamin "PAC" Satterly died unexpectedly in September at age 40. Dave Meltzer provided more info on Satterly's past health issues.
body: During an episode of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer provided more information regarding Satterly's health. Meltzer stated that in the U.S., only about 3,000 to 4,000 deaths per year are due to bronchial asthma. He pointed out that most are over the age of 65. "We don't know if he had an inhaler in his car. He did have lung issues. This isn't something that came out of nowhere that nobody knew. I don't know how well it was known, but one of his friends had told me that really the week of his death — he had the blood clot issues in 2023 — and said that he had some lung issues. And so the lung issues are consistent with what happened unfortunately. Usually, you'd have the inhaler with you and I don't know, it may have happened so quick. There was stuff in his rental car, but it may have happened so quick that he wasn't able to get it. It's a horrible situation the more you learn about it. It doesn't get better, it gets worse," he said.
summary: Dave Meltzer discussed the health background of the late AEW wrestler Pac on Wrestling Observer Radio. He noted that Pac had known lung issues consistent with the reported cause of death and had also dealt with blood clot problems in 2023. Meltzer added that the situation becomes sadder with more information, as Pac may not have had time to use an inhaler that was possibly in his rental car.

title: Ludwig Kaiser battery case hits defense snag
raw_title: Ludwig Kaiser’s defense suffers a setback in Florida battery case
summary_src: Ludwig Kaiser’s defense team lost a key decision on Monday (Oct. 19) when a judge denied its motion to dismiss his ongoing battery case under Florida’s “Stand Your Ground” law. Kaiser (real name Marcel Barthel) was arrested on May 20, 2026, in Orange County, Florida, on a battery charge.
body: Kaiser (real name Marcel Barthel) was arrested on May 20, 2026, in Orange County, Florida, on a battery charge. The German wrestler was later released after making bail. TMZ reported it had obtained a police report on the incident, which occurred on April 23 in the building where Kaiser was living. According to TMZ , the report said Kaiser was in an elevator with a female companion (later revealed to be his girlfriend, AAA talent Andrea Bazarte), and the two started kissing and became “uncontrollably intimate.” After the elevator stopped at the 12th floor, a neighbor told the couple to “please have some manners,” which led to Kaiser allegedly punching the man repeatedly, pushing him to the ground, and threatening him. Kaiser flew back to Florida and turned himself in after learning about an arrest warrant while in Mexico on May 19. He was placed in custody and released on $1,000 bond. His attorney entered a “not guilty” plea on his behalf. Legal documents later filed by Kaiser’s defense team described a much different scene of what allegedly occurred during the April elevator ride. In Kaiser’s account, he pushed the neighbor in order to protect Bazarte, and the man threw a soft drink bottle at the wrestler. According to the defense, there were no physical blows during the incident. But on Monday, records show that Judge Andrew L. Cameron shot down the attempt by Kaiser’s legal team to dismiss under “Stand Your Ground”. The next step in the case will be a pre-trial conference scheduled for December 17, where the two sides can attempt to reach a resolution or decide if the case is going to trial. Meanwhile, Kaiser has been able to actively compete in AAA as Grande Americano after the court cleared him for international travel, even winning the promotion’s AAA Mega Championship from Dominik Mysterio last month at Triplemania 34 . title: Santino Marella Re-Signs With TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Santino Marella Re-Signs With TNA Wrestling
summary_src: Santino Marella isn’t going anywhere when his current TNA deal runs out. The Director of Authority has revealed that he’s officially re-signed with the company for another year, saying TNA’s current momentum made staying an easy decision.
body: Speaking on The Johnny I Pro Show , Marella addressed all the recent talk surrounding TNA contracts coming up at the end of the year. According to Santino, TNA President Carlos Silva got ahead of the situation and approached him about sticking around. “Okay, yeah, I mean, there’s a lot of talk about TNA contracts expiring at the end of the year. Carlos is very proactive, and he talked to me last week and said, ‘Of course, we’d love you back.’ So, I signed for another year with TNA.” Marella didn’t sound like he needed much convincing either. He pointed to where TNA is heading right now and the momentum surrounding the company since Impact moved to AMC as major reasons why another year felt right. “It feels like the right thing to do. It’s the right time — the direction we’re going, the momentum we have. Ever since we started with AMC, it’s been incredible. The locker room continues to shine.” Interestingly, Santino is even enjoying some of the negativity TNA has been getting online. He sees the increased criticism as a sign that more people are paying attention, especially after he felt the company proved doubters wrong heading into Bound for Glory. “I notice there’s more hate online this year, which is a good thing. They were doubting us going into Bound for Glory — we showed it to everyone, threw it in their faces.” Things got considerably more personal by the end of that year. After Santino teamed with Mike Santana, Steve Maclin and The Hardys against Team NXT in a Steel Cage match, Grace turned on her father and sided with Stacks, giving Santino a low blow after locking herself inside the cage with him. His authority role has continued to evolve in 2026 as well. TNA’s AMC debut introduced another wrinkle when Daria Rae arrived as Director of Operations, immediately clashing with Santino and claiming she could do his job better than him. That power struggle is something Marella expects to keep playing with now that he’s sticking around. He sees himself as someone making decisions with the audience in mind, while Daria approaches things from a much more business-focused perspective. “Being an authority figure, of course, we have an issue with Daria Rae, who’s imposing her authority. She’s business-oriented, but I think I come from the perspective of fans more, and we butt heads a little bit. It makes for entertaining TV.” H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

title: AJ Francis Claims He Helped TNA Land Its AMC Television Deal
raw_title: AJ Francis Claims He Helped TNA Land Its AMC Television Deal
summary_src: AJ Francis believes he deserves some serious credit for helping TNA land its television deal with AMC.
body: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis was asked why he decided to sign another deal with TNA instead of looking elsewhere. His answer was pretty simple. He believes TNA recognizes what he brings to the company, and he feels his work has helped the promotion grow. Francis specifically pointed to the company’s AMC television deal as an example. While he acknowledged that names like The Hardys, Nic Nemeth and Moose have all contributed to TNA’s success, he believes his role has been just as important. Francis then made an even bigger claim about what he’s accomplished during his time with the promotion. According to him, nobody in TNA has done a better job of helping babyface wrestlers become more popular. “But nobody did a better job of building babyfaces over the last two years than me. Um, you know Joe Hendry, Mike Santana, you know even KC Navarro and Rich Swann, now BDE, you know Elijah, you know I could go on forever.” Those names include several wrestlers Francis has worked with during his current TNA run. His rivalry with Joe Hendry helped establish their on-screen relationship, while his more recent program with Elijah allowed him to combine his music career with professional wrestling. Francis believes that ability to help opponents become bigger attractions is something TNA understands and appreciates. “You know, and so like I felt like I have a home in TNA because they recognize what I bring to the table.” He also explained that his time in TNA has allowed him to take on a bigger creative role. Francis previously compared his position in WWE to being an offensive lineman, while describing his position in TNA as being the quarterback. When asked whether that comparison still applies, he didn’t hesitate. “Absolutely. I’m calling the plays. You know what I’m saying? And they sending me out there first to set the tone. And I’m doing it, you know, I’m doing it every time. And I’m making the most out of my opportunities. Whether I get 40 seconds backstage or eight minutes in the ring, you know, it doesn’t matter. I’m going to make the most of my opportunities. I always have, always will.” Francis also pointed to his rivalry with Elijah as an example of what happens when he’s given creative freedom. He described the storyline involving music, identity rights, their matches and Expressions getting hit with a guitar as some of the best work of his career. “That was probably the most, I think if you start from the beginning of me and Elijah’s storyline to the end of it at Lockdown. I mean, that’s probably the best storyline in wrestling this year. It’s the best, it’s the best creative, most creative storyline in wrestling this year. And I stand on that.” Francis isn’t claiming he single-handedly secured TNA’s television deal, but he certainly believes he played an important role in helping the company reach that point. His argument is that building popular wrestlers and delivering memorable storylines contributed to the promotion’s growth. W

Despite this gap in her time competing in WWE, Morgan has remained a staple of WWE programming and is currently the WWE Women’s World Champion. It’s like all the same tools, but maybe just used differently, and so it was cool to use my WWE experience and see how that translated to film. I feel like I was actually more comfortable and more prepared because of prior experience, but filming is like a completely different beast than what WWE is. So I feel like I learned a lot as well. title: AJ Francis Calls Out TNA’s Old Management for Giving Titles to the Wrong People
raw_title: AJ Francis Calls Out TNA’s Old Management for Giving Titles to the Wrong People
summary_src: AJ Francis has some complaints about how TNA used to be run, and he’s not keeping them to himself. The former WWE Superstar believes the company’s previous leadership had an outdated way of deciding who deserved opportunities, especially when it came to championships.
body: Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Francis was asked how TNA has changed since he joined the company and how its move to AMC has affected the promotion. He immediately pointed to the difference in leadership, explaining that he prefers Silva’s approach over the way the company operated in the past. Francis believes the previous administration relied too heavily on traditional professional wrestling thinking. He praised Silva for bringing a different approach to managing the company and credited him with securing TNA’s television deal. “Uh, you know, I think just the leadership style has changed. I think the old leadership style was much more like oldtimey pro wrestling and I love how Carlos runs TNA.” Francis then defended Silva against people who have criticized his leadership, arguing that outsiders don’t understand everything he’s done for the promotion. Francis didn’t stop there. He explained that he’s able to communicate directly with Silva and appreciates the way he runs TNA. “Like that’s huge, right? And so like to have someone like that at the helm that I can, I mean I talked to him today, like he’s my favorite boss I ever worked for and I think that having him at the helm has been such a big help, such an improvement.” One of the biggest differences, according to Francis, is that Silva approaches wrestling more like a legitimate sports organization instead of relying on the same philosophy that’s been used in the business for decades. Francis believes that approach could finally benefit him, especially considering how long it’s been since he last held championship gold in TNA. “And his leadership style is more so of like real sports, right? Um, he doesn’t ignore what’s right in front of his face, right? Like it’s a damn shame that it’s been two years since I’ve been a champion in TNA. And Carlos recognizes that, right?” That’s when Francis took his biggest shot at the company’s previous approach to handing out championships. He suggested that wrestlers who had already put in the work were sometimes passed over in favor of newer talent who hadn’t accomplished nearly as much. “The old wrestling leadership style would be like, ‘Well, he’s still got a lot to prove, but let’s put a title on this guy who’s been here six months who nobody gives a shit about.’ Like that’s the, that’s the old wrestling style, right? And Carlos, Carlos recognizes what’s in front of his face.” “I do it because I’m trying to steal the show. I do it because I want to prove that I’m the best big man in the business and that I should be TNA World Heavyweight Champion. Um, I think that there’s only a matter of time before these things come to fruition because of the work that I’m putting in.” Francis clearly believes TNA is in better hands with Silva running the show, and he’s hoping that change eventually leads to a world championship run. He hasn’t accused any specific former executive of holding him back, but he certainly doesn’t miss the old way of making decisions

title: Legal Watch: Maryland Federal Judge Allows Child Sexual Abuse Lawsuit Against WWE and McMahons to Move Forward - The MoCo Show -
raw_title: Maryland Federal Judge Allows Child Sexual Abuse Lawsuit Against WWE and McMahons to Move Forward - The MoCo Show -
body: In a 26-page opinion issued Monday, October 19, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar upheld the application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023, which eliminated the statute of limitations for civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The defendants argued that applying the law to allegations dating back approximately 40 years violated their constitutional right to due process, particularly because several individuals connected to the allegations have since died. However, Bredar rejected that argument, finding that Maryland lawmakers had a legitimate reason to eliminate the filing deadlines for childhood sexual abuse claims. The lawsuit, known as the “Ring Boys” case, involves seven men who allege they were sexually abused as minors while helping set up wrestling rings and performing other duties for WWE, then known as the World Wrestling Federation (WWF), during the 1980s and 1990s. According to reporting by Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling , all seven plaintiffs allege abuse by former ring announcer and ring crew chief Mel Phillips Jr. One plaintiff also alleges abuse by former WWE executive Pat Patterson, while another alleges sexual harassment by former executive Terry Garvin. All three men died before the lawsuit was filed. The plaintiffs allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the alleged abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The defendants have denied the central allegations. Maryland’s Supreme Court upheld the Child Victims Act under the state constitution in 2025. The defendants subsequently challenged its application under the U.S. Constitution, arguing that allowing decades-old claims to proceed would make it difficult to mount an effective defense because witnesses have died, memories have faded and evidence may no longer be available. In Monday’s ruling, Bredar acknowledged those difficulties but determined that they did not make the law unconstitutional. “The Maryland General Assembly created its statute of limitations for child sexual abuse claims and, in response to a legitimate and pressing issue, decided to alter it in a rational way,” Bredar wrote. The decision follows a December 2025 ruling in which the court largely denied earlier motions to dismiss, reducing the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. According to Thurston, claims by two plaintiffs remain against Linda McMahon, while all seven plaintiffs’ cases continue against Vince McMahon, WWE and TKO. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler, a partner at DiCello Levitt, one of the law firms representing the plaintiffs. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality,” Gutzler added. As reported by Thurston, the case can now move toward discovery, during which evidence is exchanged and witnesses

body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) I feel like you’ve gotten bigger since the last time I saw you! “I have gotten bigger since the last time you saw me. title: Word On Visa Status Of Kairi Amid Free Agency

body: A new report has a bit of context on the visa status of Kairi as she remains a free agent. As noted , Kairi remains a free agent after her WWE deal expired following her release from the company. There were some reports recently suggesting that visa problems are preventing a deal from being done, but Fightful Select reports that it’s actually her free agency causing visa issues. Kairi’s US visa has expired and she needs to be sponsored by an employer or agency to get renewed. Kairi is not yet signed by AEW and thus her visa is not approved. Should she sign on with AEW or another promotion, an expedited visa is said to be able to be approved in as little as 15 business days.

llm_long: Chad Gable retained the Intercontinental Championship in a triple threat match on Raw against Bron Breakker and Dominik Mysterio.

The competitors traded holds early with Lee applying a side headlock to Mysterio before tossing Gable from the ring. Lee then exchanged strikes with Mysterio and delivered a dropkick to both opponents in the corners.
Gable responded by suplexing both men at the same time. After a commercial break, Gable landed multiple forearms on Lee as the action continued with frequent reversals.

Lee attempted a Styles Clash but was interrupted by Mysterio's crossbody. Gable applied the Ankle Lock on Lee, who escaped only to be caught in the hold again while Mysterio targeted Gable from the top.

The match featured several high-impact moves including a hurricanrana over the top rope, a West Coast Pop, a double stomp, and multiple suplexes. Mysterio hit a 619 on both opponents followed by a Frog Splash on Lee that was broken up by Gable.
Gable ultimately secured the victory by rolling up Mysterio. Following the match, Mysterio and Gable were attacked by Ethan Page while Lee was assaulted by Big Cass on the outside.

title: Will Ospreay Says Wrestling Has Evolved Past Full Kayfabe
raw_title: Will Ospreay Feels Wrestling As 'Evolved' Past Needing Full Kayfabe Protection
summary_src: Will Ospreay feels that wrestling has 'evolved' past needing to have full kayfabe protection on wrestling shows in 2026.
body: Will Ospreay feels that wrestling has ‘evolved’ past needing to have full kayfabe protection on wrestling shows in 2026. In 2026, kayfabe is not protected near as much as in decades past in professional wrestling, with programs such as WWE: Unreal and AEW: All Access delving into the backstage aspects of pro wrestling companies. While speaking to Real Radio Monsters in a recent interview, Will Ospreay spoke about kayfabe in modern pro wrestling, noting that while some things do need to be protected, wrestling has evolved past needing full kayfabe protection. “I mean it can still be done to this day and age for sure. It can be, but just like, I think, you don’t go into like a cinema. I like the Avengers and like Spider-Man and I love Batman. I don’t go into those things and instantly just go, well, ‘they’re not protecting the business.’ Do you know what I mean? I go into there knowing that I’m going to be sucked into a story and sucked into that universe. So like, it’s the same thing with wrestling. Whenever you walk into any arena that we do, we’re all characters and we’re all there to perform a show. Sometimes it gets dictated onto like social media where people act as their characters from there and they can cut promos there and it can promote over over to like different sources and different places but just like- I feel like wrestling has kind of evolved from that standpoint, like once upon a time it needed to be protected and I still feel like aspects of it do need to be protected, that’s why I’m not the biggest fan of the the backstage like stuff that’s being shown. I just think there are some things that fans need to see and some things that fans don’t need to see, and I don’t think fans need to know what time cues are. I don’t think they need to know when the commercial break’s coming up. I don’t think they need to be… Like, it just seems like one big ego fest. Look how amazing we are, the guys behind the camera. It’s like, shut up.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Will Ospreay believes professional wrestling in 2026 has moved beyond the need for complete kayfabe protection. He pointed to shows like WWE: Unreal and AEW: All Access that explore backstage elements while noting some aspects still require safeguarding. Ospreay compared the experience to watching superhero films where audiences accept the story without demanding protection of the business.

llm_long: Will Ospreay believes professional wrestling has evolved beyond the need for full kayfabe protection in 2026. He noted that while certain elements should still remain protected, the industry no longer requires the strict maintenance of character that was once standard.

Ospreay compared modern wrestling to films such as those featuring Avengers, Spider-Man, and Batman. He explained that audiences enter those stories knowing they are fictional yet allow themselves to become immersed without questioning the protection of the craft.

According to Ospreay, wrestlers perform as characters when entering an arena to present a show. Social media sometimes extends this performance, with wrestlers staying in character to cut promos and promote events across platforms.

He expressed reservations about programs that reveal backstage aspects of wrestling companies. Ospreay stated that some information, including time cues and commercial break details, should not be shared with fans as it detracts from the experience.
Ospreay described excessive backstage exposure as resembling an ego-driven display focused on those working behind the camera rather than enhancing the product for viewers.

raw_title: Tiger Jeet Singh Comments On Cutting A Fan With His Sword, Blames The Fan
summary_src: Tiger Jeet Singh made a rare appearance in Japan on October 17 at Yoyogi National Stadium Gymnasium No. 2 in Shibuya, Japan. During his entrance, he swung his trademark saber and ended up cutting a fan on the forehand.
body: Tiger Jeet Singh made a rare appearance in Japan on October 17 at Yoyogi National Stadium Gymnasium No. 2 in Shibuya, Japan. During his entrance, he swung his trademark saber and ended up cutting a fan on the forehand. According to Sports Hochi , medical personnel at the venue attended to the man before an ambulance was called. He was treated at a nearby hospital, but this injury was said to be minor. Speaking to Tokyo Sports , Singh said, “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right? All he had to do was get out of my way.” Tiger Ali Singh, Jeet’s son, said, “The announcer was saying, ‘Please be careful!’ They were warning him it was dangerous, but he didn’t move out of the way. I’m sure he won’t make the same mistake again. Just like my father said, this was an accident.” Megumi Kudo, who was celebrating her 40th Anniversary, apologizing for the fan being injured.
summary: Tiger Jeet Singh appeared at a show in Tokyo on October 17 and accidentally cut a fan on the forehead with his saber during his entrance. The spectator received treatment at a hospital for a minor injury after being attended by medical staff. Singh told Tokyo Sports the fan should have moved out of his way and that it was the fan's fault, while his son Tiger Ali Singh noted warnings were given beforehand. Megumi Kudo, who was celebrating her 40th anniversary, apologized for the incident.

raw_title: KAIRI Clarifies Wrestling Status for Chris Jericho Cruise Amid AEW Rumors
summary_src: KAIRI is heading out to sea with Chris Jericho, but anyone expecting her to lace up the boots on the cruise is going to be disappointed. The former WWE star has now made it clear that she won’t be wrestling at all during the trip, even as questions continue to swirl about her AEW future. ...
body: Speaking with Weekly Pro Wrestling magazine , KAIRI revealed that she’s already getting herself ready for an eventual return to the ring. She’s been training, working on her conditioning and even has some fresh gear almost ready to go. “I’m continuing to train and work on my physical conditioning in preparation for my return. I’ve also started working on a new costume, and it’s almost finished.” Then Chris Jericho’s Rock ‘N’ Wrestling Rager at Sea came calling . For someone who spent years sailing into WWE as the “Pirate Princess,” KAIRI couldn’t resist the chance to take that character onto an actual ship. KAIRI also wanted whatever she did first after WWE to actually mean something to her. The cruise checked that box immediately. “After leaving WWE, I wanted my first wrestling-related activity to be something I genuinely wanted to do, and this was it.” Here’s where things get interesting, especially with all the AEW talk surrounding her. KAIRI isn’t getting into the ring on the cruise, period. “I won’t be wrestling in matches this time. We’re planning merchandise sales, autograph sessions, and things like that.” So instead of throwing elbows and dropping Insane Elbows, KAIRI will be spending her time meeting fans. That’s actually a big part of why she wanted to do the cruise in the first place. “More than anything, I want to cherish the opportunity to meet the overseas fans in person — the people who have continued supporting me since my WWE days. Being able to meet them directly is very important to me.” There has also been plenty of talk about KAIRI eventually landing in AEW, but nothing has been signed publicly. Sean Ross Sapp recently made that part clear when discussing where things stood. The more interesting tease might actually be that new costume sitting somewhere almost finished. KAIRI is clearly preparing to wrestle again, but she’s keeping everyone waiting when it comes to where — and when — the Pirate Princess will actually make that return. title: Natalya Praises Rhea Ripley's Generosity
raw_title: Nattie: Rhea Ripley Is So Giving And Very Unselfish
summary_src: Nattie has high praise for Rhea Ripley. Counting only televised matches, Ripley and Nattie have shared the ring almost 20 times since 2019. This includes their extended feud throughout the back half of 2021.
body: Speaking with The West Sport for a new interview , Nattie said that Rhea Ripley will be in the best shape of her life when she comes back. “I feel like when Rhea comes back, she’s going to show everybody that she’s not only physically in the best shape of her life but she’s also mentally feeling rested, rejuvenated.” As it turns out, ‘The Eradicator’ might be turning Nattie into a dog person. “I went to her house and her dogs — I said to Rhea, ‘I’m a big cat person’ but then after seeing her dogs, all of the sudden I was just like a dog person. Her dogs are like her babies with her husband. They love their dogs but their dogs, you could tell they were so loved. These dogs were the sweetest animals and I was like, that’s because they have parents that love them. You know when you meet good kids, you know that they have good parents. Rhea is turning me into a dog person and I told her when I was at her birthday.” Nattie took her praise a step farther, saying that Ripley is giving and very unselfish. “She’s really one of my favorite people to wrestle because she’s so giving. People don’t realize that about her. When you’re in the ring with her, she’s very very very unselfish. We just had this really magical chemistry, I think she’s one of my top three in the world that I’ve ever wrestled. I just love locking up with her. I’d love a big juicy feud with her when she’s back.” Ripley has out of action since June. While her in-ring return date is currently unknown, she was recently announced for the Wrestlepalooza Perth Pre-Show event. Learn more here . title: Netflix Reports Q3 Earnings Amid Layoffs
raw_title: Netflix faces plenty of questions and unrest going into Q3 earnings
summary_src: WWE’s largest broadcast partner, Netflix, heads into its third-quarter earnings release amid significant changes.
body: WWE’s largest broadcast partner, Netflix, heads into its third-quarter earnings release amid significant changes. Tonight, the world’s largest streamer will report its Q3 results and take questions, less than a week after purging about 1,000 staff members , representing six percent of its workforce. The cuts included chief content officer Bela Bajaria and head of film David Lin. It was a major statement from the company that analysts viewed as a response to a 40% drop in its stock over the past year and engagement (read: viewership) failing to increase at the level of expectations and in comparison to YouTube. Her replacement is Peter Rice, a former executive at Disney and Fox, with a history of dealing with WWE. In 2018, Rice was serving as chairman and CEO of Fox Networks Group and was among the people in the room negotiating for WWE’s rights to SmackDown. The Hollywood Reporter detailed the closure of the deal , which was the most important in WWE’s history up to that point. Sports have become the thing that keeps people from churning their streaming subs…My bet is that (Netflix) is going to have to think about this as a calendar year. This is one of the reasons why, by the way, Netflix really likes the WWE. It’s a full year-round of events. Netflix has an overarching issue of scale, and it explains why they were so aggressive in the bid for WBD and its endless IP it could integrate (a subject Nick Khan has noted several times regarding WWE’s IP and further monetizing). However, Wall Street was not as keen during its attempted bidding war with Paramount Skydance and saw the stock plummet and has yet to recover. title: Drew McIntyre says Triple H shaped his famous promo line
raw_title: Drew McIntyre credits Triple H for memorable WWE promo line
summary_src: Without Paul “Triple H” Levesque’s input, Drew McIntyre’s “I prayed for this and it happened” promo line never would have happened. McIntyre uttered the remark during a January 2024 promo directed at CM Punk, mocking him for his triceps injury.
body: Without Paul “Triple H” Levesque’s input, Drew McIntyre’s “I prayed for this and it happened” promo line never would have happened. McIntyre uttered the remark during a January 2024 promo directed at CM Punk, mocking him for his triceps injury. It’s proven to have staying power, with McIntyre telling Insight with Chris Van Vliet that he still sees himself pop up in memes more than two years later. He discussed the process of creating the promo and said his original intention was to say something more extreme. Paul “Triple H” Levesque helped McIntyre come up with a toned down version and the right cadence to deliver the line. “I mean, I knew talking to Triple H during the day that this is going to be so good. I had an idea, and it was too much. It would have offended a lot of people, which I’m very good at,” McIntyre said. “He helped me reel it back, and then Hunter himself came out with the line, which I ended up using because I had such an extreme version. And he dialed it back in the way he said it and the cadence of how it’s to be said, he said it like that. And I just went — I got so excited. McIntyre and Punk had a heated feud that included Punk defeating McIntyre in a Hell in a Cell match in October 2024. They still keep up kayfabe to this day, insisting that the hate they have for each other is legitimate. “I’ve been very, very fortunate how things have kind of organically fell in my lap. And WWE has been amazing the whole time, allowing me to do these things,” McIntyre said. “Historically, we weren’t allowed to do outside projects. It was very much, ‘You wrestle for WWE, that’s it.’ “But Nick Khan, Triple H, and the whole team have been very open to, ‘Hey, if it makes sense for the company, if it makes sense for your brand, which in turn makes sense for our brand. We’re going to protect you from things we don’t think are worth it.’ But ‘The Killer’s Game,’ the ‘Highlander’ which led to ‘Last Druid’ and now ‘Agent of Shadows,’ they have all just kind of organically came my way. And I feel very fortunate, and it’s been fun to see how I fare in that world.” Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

McIntyre originally planned a more extreme version that would have offended many people but Triple H helped tone it down and suggested the exact wording and delivery cadence. The Scot told Insight with Chris Van Vliet that the line still generates memes over two years later.

title: Where Things Stand With Dralistico and RUSH in AEW After Cryptic Tweets
raw_title: Where Things Stand With Dralistico and RUSH in AEW After Cryptic Tweets
summary_src: Dralistico’s cryptic “Maybe not for long?” post suddenly makes a lot more sense, and RUSH’s own mysterious message apparently has nothing to do with leaving AEW.
body: Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer addressed both posts after they sparked plenty of questions about the future of La Facción Ingobernable. When it comes to Dralistico, Alvarez believes the message behind that handcuffed photo was pretty easy to read. “Regarding the Dralistico and RUSH tweets we talked about last night: Dralistico’s AEW deal expires in December, and based on that tweet one would presume he wants out.” That’s a much more specific timeline than what had previously been reported. Alvarez had earlier said Dralistico’s contract was expiring “fairly soon,” but now December appears to be the month to watch. Dralistico certainly hasn’t been subtle with the imagery either. He recently posted a photo of himself behind bars with his hands cuffed and added one very short message. Dralistico hasn’t wrestled for AEW since the June 6 Collision taping, where he teamed with RUSH and Sammy Guevara in an unsuccessful challenge for the AEW World Trios Championship. Between that lengthy absence, his December contract expiration and the handcuffed photo, Alvarez believes it’s reasonable to read the post as Dralistico wanting out. The situation with RUSH is apparently completely different. He got fans talking on the same day when he tweeted another cryptic message: “See you 2027.” That immediately raised questions about whether RUSH might also be disappearing from AEW, but Alvarez says there’s a much simpler explanation. According to him, RUSH’s visa has expired, and he isn’t expected to have the situation resolved until the new year. More importantly, Alvarez says there isn’t any indication that RUSH is unhappy with AEW or looking for an exit. His absence is reportedly a legal work issue rather than anything involving his relationship with the company. “From all accounts it appears RUSH is happy in AEW, he just can’t legally work right now.” That clears up what initially looked like two LFI members possibly sending exit teases at almost exactly the same time. Instead, Dralistico is the one with a contract reportedly running out in December and a post that Alvarez believes could signal he wants out, while RUSH apparently just has to wait for his visa situation to get sorted. Dralistico still hasn’t outright announced that he’s leaving AEW, so his December expiration doesn’t guarantee an exit. However, with only a couple of months left on his deal and that “Maybe not for long?” message hanging out there, his future suddenly looks a lot more interesting than RUSH’s. WWE has fallen into the same traps with Corbin, his gimmick is lacking in depth, and his presence on TV remains a harsh reminder of some of WWE’s darkest days. Outside of the “Broke” Corbin gimmick, he has forever been amongst WWE’s least interesting acts. Ever since returning to WWE in 2026, it is hard to pin down what his personality is exactly supposed to be outside of “generic heel”. He comes to the ring with a drawling voice, acts unlikable, and cheats his way to victories, and while it can sometimes be an effective way of drawing heat, fans are starting to get bored. There have been glimpses over the years of Corbin’s quality at portraying an effective character, most notably during his brief run as “Broke” Corbin and during a babyface spell in NXT that invigorated his entire career (until a second main roster call-up where he was completely wasted and misused), but time and time again he has been left with dead-end booking. His return in 2026 provided Triple H with the chance to repackage Corbin and try something new… only for him to return as the same old Corbin. title: AEW's Pac Dies at 40 in Illinois Parking Lot
raw_title: Exclusive | Heartbreaking call AEW star Pac received as paramedics worked to save his life
body: The wife of AEW star Benjamin Satterley, known as Pac, called his cellphone as police investigated the wrestler’s death after finding him slumped over in his vehicle, a newly released report revealed. Natalie Taylor, Satterley’s spouse, called her husband’s phone on Sept. 27 as law enforcement was on scene after his passing in the parking lot of a CAVA restaurant in Des Plaines, Ill , according to a Cook County Medical Examiner report released to the California Post Monday. When police answered her call, she “reported that she last spoke with Satterley” less than three hours before he was pronounced dead at just 40 years old . “Satterley told his wife that he was stopping at the restaurant CAVA before heading to O’Hare Airport,” officials wrote in the report. They added that Taylor informed them that Satterley had been diagnosed with a redacted medical condition and he had been prescribed medication. They also noted she told them he had “no history of illicit drug or alcohol abuse.” Satterley was discovered passed out in his car just before 4 p.m. by a 911 caller who stated she could not see any signs of life from the wrestler as he was slumped over in the driver’s seat of his rental car. “I don’t see his chest moving at all,” she told police dispatch during the call. After toxicology reports found nothing extraordinary, officials determined Satterley died of bronchial asthma and deemed his passing natural, the medical examiner report stated. Satterley had been in the area for his role with AEW, as he wrestled against Andrade at the NOW Arena in Chicago on Sept. 26. Taylor wrote in an emotional Instagram post on Oct. 12 that she and Sattereley had been looking forward to his return home from Illinois. “You were so excited to get home to us,” Taylor said, “you were going to shoot hoops all week with your best mates, we were going to set up your new home gym and take Wilfie for some autumnal walks, have pizza at Rudy’s on your cheat day, go to the match, see Sam Campbell live.

He was pronounced dead at age 40. His wife Natalie Taylor called his phone while authorities were on scene and told them she had spoken to him less than three hours earlier as he planned to stop at the CAVA eatery before heading to O'Hare Airport.

title: In Memoriam: Cause Of Death Released For Wrestler PAC, Found In Des Plaines
raw_title: Cause Of Death Released For Wrestler PAC, Found In Des Plaines
body: DES PLAINES, IL — Professional wrestler Benjamin "PAC" Satterley died of bronchial asthma, according to Cook County Medical Examiner's Office records, which classified his death as natural. Satterley, 40, was found unresponsive inside a vehicle outside a Des Plaines restaurant Sept. 27, a day after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates. The medical examiner’s record lists his death at 2761 Mannheim Road. No secondary cause of death was listed. As Patch previously reported , a passerby alerted police after noticing an unresponsive man in a vehicle around 4 p.m. Satterley was alone in the rental vehicle, and authorities reported no signs of trauma or foul play. His cause and manner of death were initially pending. Satterley had been in the Chicago area for AEW's All Out event at NOW Arena, where he competed against Andrade El Ídolo the previous evening. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began wrestling in 2004 and became known internationally for his high-flying style. He joined AEW in 2019 and held multiple championships with the organization. AEW announced his death the evening of Sept. 27, recognizing his contributions and memorable matches.

llm_long: The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office has ruled that Benjamin Satterley, known professionally as PAC, died of bronchial asthma. The determination classifies his death as natural. The senior sports reporter for the California Post first reported the ruling.
Satterley died on September 27 in Des Plaines, Illinois. He was found unresponsive in a vehicle outside a restaurant. Emergency services responded and pronounced him dead at 4:08 pm local time.
Authorities stated there were no indications of trauma or foul play. His death did not appear suspicious. An autopsy was performed and additional testing completed before the cause was finalized.

Satterley was born in Newcastle upon Tyne and began wrestling in 2004. He became closely associated with Dragon Gate, where he held multiple championships including a record 447-day reign as Open the Brave Gate Champion.

He signed with WWE in 2012 and performed as Adrian Neville and later Neville. His accomplishments there included the NXT Championship, two NXT Tag Team Championship reigns, and two runs as WWE Cruiserweight Champion.

Satterley joined AEW in 2019 after returning to Dragon Gate. He became the inaugural AEW All-Atlantic Champion, later renamed the International Championship, and held the AEW World Trios Championship as part of Death Triangle. His final match was a loss to Andrade El Idolo for the AEW National Championship at All Out on September 26.

body: Tiger Jeet Singh has defended his actions at Megumi Kudo’s anniversary card over the weekend, where a fan was injured during his entrance. Singh, 82, was accompanied to the ring at Yoyogi National Gymnasium on Saturday, with son Tiger Jeet Singh Jr. (Tiger Ali Singh in WWF) and his grandson, Sarjen, for the Zero1 card. Singh was a special guest before a tag match involving Masakatsu Funaki & Tatsumi Fujinami against Shiro Koshinaka & Mitsuya Nagai. He came out to his popular song, “Saber Tiger”, brandishing his sword and directing the weapon at fans. One fan ended up being cut by the sword, requiring medical attention and treated for what were described as minor injuries by Tokyo Sports . Kudo apologized at the post-match press conference, and while Singh Jr. stated his father struck him by accident, the elder Singh did not apologize when speaking with reporters. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. He’s at fault. You know that, he just had to run away from me”. It was Singh’s first trip to Japan since 2012, and he is a legendary figure in Japanese wrestling history. Singh had a major feud with Antonio Inoki, which featured a famous scene where Singh attacked Inoki at a shopping center in 1972.

body: Sami Zayn and Roman Reigns opened the Oct. 19 episode of WWE Monday Night Raw in San Diego with a face-to-face segment. Zayn holds the Undisputed WWE Championship, while Reigns carries the World Heavyweight title. The pair collide at Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Nov. seventh. Zayn set up the confrontation in the opening promo of the Oct. 16 episode of SmackDown. In that promo, the Undisputed WWE Champion told Penta, the reigning Mr. Money in the Bank, to target Reigns. Zayn also promised to deliver a message to the Tribal Chief in person on Raw. Zayn won the Undisputed WWE Championship for the first time at Night of Champions on June 27, beating Cody Rhodes and Gunther in a triple-threat match. CM Punk took the title nine days later in Zayn’s first defense on the July sixth episode of Raw. Zayn regained the championship on the Sept. 11 episode of SmackDown. Reigns won the World Heavyweight Championship from Punk at WrestleMania 42 Night Two on April 19 in Las Vegas. The Tribal Chief hit two Spears to close the 33-minute main event. Reigns retained against L.A. Knight at Money in the Bank on Oct. tenth. Zayn came out first and asked the crowd who would “ride or die” with the champion. Reigns followed to a loud ovation and opened with “It’s good to see you.” The two champions hugged in the middle of the ring, and WWE posted the moment on X . Zayn told Reigns the burden of holding the top title, something the Tribal Chief described during the pair’s Bloodline days, finally makes sense. The Undisputed WWE Champion pointed to the constant disrespect that follows a world titleholder. Reigns agreed the title brings that burden. Reigns shifted the conversation, saying the most important title Zayn ever held was “Honorary Uce.” The nickname dates to the Bloodline storyline that ran from 2022 into early 2023. The World Heavyweight Champion asked whether Zayn came to Raw to talk about titles or to serve The Bloodline in its feud with The 946. The 946, a faction led by Royce Keys, has feuded with The Bloodline since the Aug. 24 episode of Raw. Zayn showed appreciation for the Bloodline years, then claimed the head of a separate table. The argument turned to which championship carries more prestige. Zayn backed the Undisputed WWE Championship, while Reigns called the World Heavyweight belt “the” title and Zayn’s only “a” title. Reigns went further, arguing the champion matters more than the belt. The Tribal Chief suggested the undisputed belt “hasn’t meant —- since WrestleMania 40.” Rhodes beat Reigns for the undisputed title at that event in April 2024. Zayn fired back that the Tribal Chief should not dismiss the Undisputed WWE Champion as a threat. Reigns closed the exchange with a warning about Crown Jewel. Citing Zayn’s track record, the World Heavyweight Champion said the undisputed title might change hands before the two meet in Riyadh. body: KAIRI says that ‘various things are already in motion’ regarding where she may wrestle next once she returns to the ring. Back in April of this year, KAIRI was released from her WWE contract, and despite being able to show up somewhere else in July, she has yet to show up anywhere as of this writing. That being said, there has been attention thrown her way from the likes of Tony Khan and AEW, as well as an announcement about her appearing as part of the upcoming Chris Jericho Rock N Wrestling Rager At Sea. While speaking to Weekly Pro Wrestling in a recent interview, KAIRI was asked about where she will wrestle next, noting that while she can’t give specific details, there are already various things in motion. “I can’t give you any specific details just yet, but various things are already in motion. I’d be happy if everyone could wait just a little longer. Every day, I’m enjoying the experience of challenging myself with new things. Once I return to wrestling, I might be more excited than ever before.”

title: 7 Greatest Champions of the WWE Renaissance Era
raw_title: 7 Greatest Champions of the WWE Renaissance Era
body: WWE’s push into the mainstream has been successful, but it wouldn’t have happened without the incredible work of the men and women who have held championship gold. These champions are stars from previous eras and ones who have recently made names for themselves. They have been the highlights of WWE’s Renaissance Era and will be listed below. The Tribal Chief stood atop WWE for most of the Renaissance Era. As the era began, Reigns was two years into his record-breaking four-year world-champion reign. He carried the Universal Championship on his waist, but after a winner-take-all match at WrestleMania 38, he became the Undisputed World Heavyweight Champion. He held the championship for two more years before losing it at WrestleMania 40. It was an iconic reign that included multiple high-profile defenses, where he always came out the victor. Roman Reigns took time off from WWE after his defeat, but the championship gold wouldn’t stay hidden for long. At WrestleMania 42, Reigns toppled CM Punk to become the World Heavyweight Champion once again. A championship that he still holds today, competing in high-profile matches at every event. Reigns was a star before this era, but during this time, he became a god in WWE. Cody Rhodes returning to WWE at WrestleMania 38 was a watershed moment for the American Nightmare. He finally returned to the company where he got his start, and it started his path to becoming the biggest babyface champion of the Renaissance Era. The fans rallied behind Cody Rhodes as he tried to finish his story and win the one championship that had eluded him. After a few heartbreaking defeats, Rhodes finally captured the WWE Championship in an emotional WrestleMania 40 finish. Rhodes became a fantastic babyface champion, taking on all comers and becoming the face of World Wrestling Entertainment. His reign lasted an impressive 378 days and included amazing title defenses against the best competitors WWE had to offer. Cody Rhodes added 2 more WWE Championship victories to his resume during this time, becoming the man everyone chased. title: The Strange WWE Program Between Gunther and Danhausen, Analyzed
raw_title: The Strange WWE Program Between Gunther and Danhausen, Analyzed
body: October 20, 2026 By Josh Prost WWE , Pro Wrestling , SmackDown , WWE Universe Gunther started 2026 on an extremely high note. He ended 2025 by defeating John Cena in his final match. Then he defeated AJ Styles to end his career at the Royal Rumble. He followed that up by beating Seth Rollins on night one of WrestleMania: Vegas. But since then, things haven’t been going well for him. He had repeated opportunities to capture the Undisputed WWE Championship, but for one reason or another, couldn’t capture it. That has made him extremely mad, demanding answers over the past few months. But instead of answers, he’s gotten Danhausen. WWE’s breakout hit of this year has repeatedly bothered him, causing him to get angry and yell. That’s why he’s been yelling at Danhausen and trying to beat him up. Any other wrestler would’ve just ignored him and gone back to their business. But Gunther wants to take him out once and for all. Instead of getting back in the Undisputed WWE Championship picture, he’s forced himself to feud with someone many wrestlers don’t take seriously. That seems like a waste of time, as Danhausen probably knows he’ll get beat up. Gunther is taking the bait from a comedy wrestler instead of focusing on title pursuits. I t’s clear that mention wasn’t random. At some point, this feud has to be over between them. Halloween Havoc is the perfect time to do that. Danhausen is the host of the PLE, and a Gunther return to NXT would make the fans very happy. It doesn’t have to be an actual match. Gunther could just beat him up like he did last Friday to stop the constant interruptions he’s been having to deal with. Doing that could definitely end their feud enjoyably. But Gunther takes wrestling seriously, which is why he’s taken so much offense at Danhausen. He’s taking his eyes off the Undisputed WWE Championship picture, which is a huge mistake. Gunther started off the year extremely happy, but over the course of the past few months has gotten very angry. Some of the blame has been directed towards SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis and his decisions on the Undisputed WWE Championship title matches, but most of it has been directed towards Danhausen. He’s clearly not walking away from feuding with him, forcing him to step away from title ambitions due to his serious view of wrestling. That has caused many fans to be mad about his direction. However, it seems he is determined to beat up Danhausen, which could prove to be advantageous if it motivates him to get back to winning championships. title: Legal Watch: Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case
raw_title: Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case
body: Back Federal Court Rejects Defendants’ Constitutional Challenge in WWE ‘Ring Boys’ Sexual Abuse Case Oct 19, 2026 DiCello Levitt Represents Survivors as Federal Court Upholds Application of Maryland’s Child Victims Act, Allowing Claims Against WWE and the McMahons to Proceed In a 26-page opinion issued today, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar of the District of Maryland rejected the defendants’ latest attempt to dismiss the survivors’ claims. At issue was the constitutionality of Maryland’s Child Victims Act of 2023 , which eliminated time limits for filing civil lawsuits involving childhood sexual abuse. The law recognizes that survivors often delay disclosing abuse due to the lasting effects of trauma, giving them an opportunity to pursue justice when they are ready to come forward. DiCello Levitt, together with Murphy, Falcon & Murphy, represents the survivors in John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. “This ruling is a significant victory for our clients and for other survivors of childhood sexual abuse who have waited years for the opportunity to seek justice,” said Greg Gutzler , a partner at DiCello Levitt who leads the litigation. “Trauma does not follow a legal deadline, and Maryland’s Child Victims Act recognizes that reality. Our clients have waited years to hold those responsible accountable. We will not stop fighting until their voices are heard and they have their day in court.” The ruling follows the court’s December 2025 decision largely denying the defendants’ earlier motions to dismiss. The WWE Ring Boys sexual abuse lawsuit alleges that WWE employees, including ringside announcer and ring crew chief Melvin Phillips Jr., recruited underage boys to assist with wrestling events and used their positions to groom, exploit, and sexually abuse them. The plaintiffs further allege that WWE leadership, including Vince and Linda McMahon, knew or should have known about the abuse but failed to take reasonable steps to prevent it. The litigation is led by DiCello Levitt’s Greg Gutzler and Adam Prom and includes Scott Gilmore , Mark A. DiCello , Bobby DiCello , and Emma Bruder , with local counsel Murphy, Falcon & Murphy. The case is John Doe 1 et al. v. World Wrestling Entertainment, LLC et al. , Case No. 1:24-cv-03487, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland. The WWE ventured to Santiago, Chile, for an untelevised live event last month, featuring a stacked card, including Liv Morgan vs Vaquer, with Becky Lynch serving as the special guest referee for the match. Given it was non-televised, no one expected Morgan to lose her WWE Women's World Championship, but the wrestling promotion had other ideas. body: Former WWE ID Talent Anya Rune, known on the independent wrestling scene as Airica Demia, has announced that she is stepping away from wrestling for the time being. Demia made the announcement via her social media on Monday night, saying that she needs to take a step back from wrestling, for both her physical and mental health. She added that she doesn’t know how long her time away will last, but she hopes to find a new love for wrestling while gone as she has currently fallen out of love with it. I need to take a step back from wrestling. Both for my physical and mental health. I don’t know how long this is going to last but I’m hoping to find a new love for it in the time I will be spending away. I will be keeping my social media somewhat active, it’ll just be less wrestling related content. I have unfortunately fallen out of love with wrestling but that doesn’t mean I don’t love everything its given me. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin Ospreay Retains AEW Title in Clockwork Carnage Thriller By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-19 12:02:00 Ospreay Survives Eight-Man Gauntlet War to Keep AEW Gold at WrestleDream Will Ospreay walked out of WrestleDream on Sunday, October 18, 2026, still holding the AEW World Championship after beating seven opponents in the promotion's first-ever Clockwork Carnage match. The stipulation forced Ospreay into a brutal two-stage format, starting as a gauntlet with staggered entrances before shifting into a 15-minute scored-fall period once eight men had entered. It was a chaotic, physically demanding structure that tested every competitor in the field. Ospreay drew the first entrance, meaning he would have to face all seven challengers to keep his title. Konosuke Takeshita came in second, followed by Ospreay's United Empire teammate 'Speedball' Mike Bailey as the third entrant. Bailey, a Canadian wrestler, was among the group chasing the title before Takeshita pinned him to eliminate him from advancing to the second stage. Ricochet entered fourth, and Darby Allin, the TNT Champion, came in fifth carrying a table that would factor into the match later. International Champion Kazuchika Okada arrived sixth, and Adam Copeland made his entrance as the seventh competitor shortly after Bailey's elimination. Joe pulled level with Allin and Ospreay by locking in the Coquina Clutch on Ospreay, then went for another Musclebuster before Copeland speared him out of it to claim his first fall of the match. Copeland then equalized again with a spear on Ricochet with just over a minute remaining, and a follow-up spear on Okada briefly put him in position to walk away as champion. With Copeland's retirement plans looming and Ospreay now having survived one of AEW's most grueling title defenses yet, the promotion heads into its next chapter with its World Championship picture wide open for fresh challengers.

The show will be available for purchase in the United States through PPV.com, HBO Max, Amazon, DAZN, Fubo, YouTube, and cable or satellite providers. International fans in the UK and other markets can access it via MyAEW.

Surviving wrestlers advance to the 15-minute Scoring Phase, where the competitor with the most pins or submissions is declared the AEW world champion. title: Edge
raw_title: Edge
body: Edge More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email superstar stats Superstar Stats Edge Buy the Song Career Highlights WWE Champion; World Heavyweight Champion; World Tag Team Champion; WWE Tag Team Champion; Intercontinental Champion; WCW U.S. Champion; 2001 King of the Ring; Money in the Bank Ladder Match winner; Royal Rumble Match winner (2010, 2021); 2012 WWE Hall of Fame Inductee In another life, Edge could have been a rock star. From his voluminous hair to his long leather jackets and double-horns signature pose, every detail of his WWE image screamed it. As the pyro blasted into the air behind him on the entranceway before he stepped into the ring, he injected arenas with the energy of a packed concert – without the dangers of crowd-surfing and mosh pits. There was even a legion of groupies – Edgeheads – who tracked his every move. It's no surprise, then, that Edge is a guitar collector and grew up listening to KISS, a band famous for their flamboyant outfits and outrageous stage antics. What is a surprise is how a shy high schooler from the little town of Orangeville, Ontario, evolved into The Rated-R Superstar. Edge had some fine company as he worked his way up the independent scene in the '90s: his childhood friend and partner for countless five-second poses, Christian. When Edge was signed to a WWE contract in 1997, it was only a matter of time before Christian would also climb the ladder, following his best bud into uncharted territory. "E&C" made sweet music as a tag team, using a lot more than just Con-Chair-Tos to claim seven championships together. A Triple Threat Ladder Match victory at WrestleMania 2000 over The Hardy Boyz and The Dudley Boyz laid the foundation for a series of landmark Tables, Ladders & Chairs (TLC) contests, and some of the greatest tag team action of all time. Of course, tag teaming wasn't Edge's only specialty, as he masterfully crafted a singles career and captured a whopping 31 total titles – many of them the WWE Universe didn't even see coming. Beyond his ability to capitalize on opportunities, Edge became known as The Master Manipulator because he wasn't afraid to cross the line in order to rattle the competition. After he made history in 2006 as the first man to ever cash in the Money in the Bank contract, he rubbed his WWE Championship triumph in the face of all challengers with an R-rated celebration on Raw; more explicitly, a frolicking good time with Lita on a bed placed right in the middle of the squared circle. Mind games were taken to a whole new level by the self-proclaimed "most-watched champion." A debilitating injury forced Edge to retire in 2011 but, in the 2020 Royal Rumble Match, The Ultimate Opportunist made an incredible return to the squared circle and immediately set out to add numerous epic matches to hs already storied career. 24:16 Karl Anderson More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Faction reveals that shook WWE: WWE

title: Roman Reigns Treated Street Fighter Role Like WWE Main Event
raw_title: Roman Reigns Says He Viewed Street Fighter Role Like Main Event In WWE
summary_src: For his performance as Akuma in "Street Fighter," Roman Reigns was able to draw from his WWE experience, specifically as a main eventer.
body: During an interview with Sam Robert's " Notsam " radio show, Reigns explained that his character only makes an impact during the third act of the film, and as such, he treated it like competing in the main event of a WWE show. "I just try to keep that type of weight on it, you know what I mean? ... The stakes are as high as can be, so you need to be able to come in and match what everybody's done," the Tribal Chief explained. While he found his feet on set, Reigns is still well aware that he's not a full-time professional actor, and admitted that it wasn't exactly easy for him to step into Akuma's shoes. "It really helped me to be able to see what [my castmates] had done and the way they had led the film, and it kind of set the tone for what needed to be matched," he admitted. "It wasn't easy, but there were a bunch of things that I was able to rely on from wrestling to kind of help me to take this on." Reigns also explained that working in front of an audience was definitely something that helped him portray Akuma. Still, while there might be similarities between his "Street Fighter" character and the Tribal Chief, he considers character work as "a dial" which he can tune, allowing him to adjust the amount of influence he draws from his WWE persona.
summary: Roman Reigns told Sam Roberts on the NotSam Wrestling podcast that he approached his Street Fighter movie part as the third-act climax, comparing it to performing in a WWE main event. He said he studied his co-stars' work to match the established tone and relied on skills from wrestling to help portray Akuma. Reigns noted that performing in front of an audience also aided his transition into the role.

summary_src: Ilja Dragunov’s AEW debut wasn’t just a stressful waiting game for Tony Khan — Dragunov was losing patience with the visa process himself.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov explained that applying for a U.S. visa wasn’t exactly new territory for him. The frustrating part was simply waiting when all he wanted to do was get back to wrestling. “I mean, it’s not the first time that I needed to apply for a visa in the US, so that was familiar. But of course, since everything I wanna do is work and fight and perform, I just couldn’t wait for things to happen quicker.” “And from the company’s side, they were helping me in that process in every way possible, so it was smooth. It took around, I guess, around a month, which was still too long for me. But putting it into perspective, it was very fast, and after the appointment, everything was so quick.” Then came the middle-of-the-night email that changed everything. Dragunov was awake around 2 AM in Germany because his girlfriend was touring Japan with Sendai Girls, and he decided to check his inbox. “So, on that day when I realized I could travel back to the States, it was 2 AM in the morning. I was awake anyway around that time since my girlfriend is touring with Sendai Girls in Japan.” That’s when Dragunov realized his passport was ready to be picked up. Instead of waiting around another day, his mind immediately went to whether he could grab it and get on a plane that same day. Dragunov immediately contacted AEW, and that’s when everything went into overdrive. Flights were arranged almost immediately, and only seven hours later he was on a plane heading back to the United States. “So I reached out to AEW — to the company — and everything went extremely quickly. Everything got booked, and I was, in seven hours, on my flight back to the States. I didn’t want to wait another single second anymore.” That frantic timeline lines up with what Tony Khan revealed following WrestleDream. Khan said AEW was still uncertain about Dragunov’s availability while Dynamite and Collision were airing live, with confirmation finally arriving that Dragunov would be able to pick up his visa the following day. “Some people asked about the timing of the vignettes that suggested your arrival at WrestleDream on Wednesday and then having a second vignette on Friday. Well, there’s a lot of uncertainty in wrestling. On Wednesday night, in the middle of the show, at 2 AM your time, we got the message that Ilja was able to pick up the visa the next day, and we found that out during the live broadcast.” Everything ultimately fell into place just in time. Dragunov made his official AEW debut at WrestleDream on October 17, bringing an end to the uncertainty that had followed him since his WWE contract expired in August. What looked like a carefully planned surprise on television was much more chaotic behind the scenes. Dragunov went from checking an email at 2 AM in Germany to sitting on a flight back to the United States just hours later, and he clearly wasn’t interested in wasting another second once that passport was ready. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up On WWE Tried to Keep Him Before AEW Move
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals WWE Tried to Keep Him Before AEW Move
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says leaving WWE wasn’t something he had already decided months before his contract expired. In fact, when he wrestled his final WWE match in April, Dragunov says he had absolutely no idea that it would end up being the last time fans saw him compete for the company.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked whether he already knew his WWE run was coming to an end when he competed in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal ahead of WrestleMania 42. According to Dragunov, that wasn’t the case at all. “No, absolutely not. Everything that I can talk about — that is not exciting. I didn’t know at the time that I was leaving. I was just waiting.” Dragunov wasn’t sitting at home with one foot already out the door either. He still wanted to wrestle and compete, but things simply reached a point where his WWE career wasn’t moving forward. “Again, I love what I do. I wanna compete and work and do this and that, and it just got a little stuck. But it’s nothing new to anybody. It was obvious. Time just passed by, and then I reached the expiration of my contract.” By the time his contract expired in August, however, Dragunov’s feelings had changed. As the months passed and he looked at where his career was heading, he began realizing that a change might be exactly what he needed. “And like I already said after the show at the press conference at WrestleDream, I felt over time that, with how things are working out and how I’m feeling — because I make a lot of things depending on how I feel about it, always have the courage to do — I felt it was time to breathe some new, fresh air.” Helwani then asked the obvious question: did WWE actually try to keep him? Dragunov confirmed that the company had no intention of simply letting him walk away. “Did they try to re-sign me? I mean, a lot of things were written over the internet. Yeah, there was no intention of the company to let me go.” That makes his departure a little more interesting than simply reaching the end of a contract and being allowed to leave. Dragunov said there were several things he had to weigh, including the offers on the table and what he wanted creatively. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things. It was an accumulation of the offers, because we know it’s a business, but it was also based on my feeling — how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Where can I see myself staying forever?” Dragunov also had to consider just how much of his adult life he’d already spent under the WWE umbrella. After joining WWE in his 20s and remaining there for years, he started wondering whether staying in the same place was really what he wanted for the next stage of his career. “Because you gotta consider a lot of factors. I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a long time.” That’s where AEW and the opportunity to experience something completely different entered the picture. Dragunov didn’t frame his WWE departure as some ugly breakup, but rather as a chance to find out whether another environment might fit him better. “The beautiful thing is we have a lot of opportunities, and for me personally, after being so long with another company, to not seek out new opportunities — maybe even a place where I see myself more fitting — who wouldn’t

title: Rush's AEW Return Delayed Until 2027 By Visa Issues
raw_title: Latest Backstage Update On AEW Contract Situations Of Rush And Dralistico
summary_src: A backstage update on the AEW contract situations of Rush and Dralistico reveals two different stories regarding this pair of lucha libre brothers
body: When it comes to Rush, however, the situation appears to be a bit different. Despite the appearance of Rush's previous tweets, Alvarez says they are entirely visa related, as Rush's visa has expired some time in the recent past. Furthermore, Rush's new visa isn't expected to come in until the start of 2027, all but confirming that the new year would be the soonest that AEW fans would see Rush again. It was further noted that, despite the speculation, Rush "is happy in AEW" by all familiar with the situation. If that is the case, it would be yet another occurrence of visa issues affecting AEW plans, as Alvarez' "Wrestling Observer Radio" co-host Dave Meltzer had previously reported that Ilja Dragunov's arrival in the promotion had been delayed due to him waiting for a new visa. Rush himself has dealt with this problem in the past, revealing in early 2024 that his absence from TV during the first part of the year had been due to a combination of recovering from an injury and visa issues . AEW/Lee South Having watched and followed the careers of Rush and Dralistico dating back to when I started following CMLL in 2015, I find this whole situation annoying, exhausting, and probably just the first part of a situation that's going to get even more annoying. But assuming there are no twists and turns coming, it does appear that Dralistico is going to be departing AEW sooner rather than later, while Rush will be sticking around. If that is the case then all I can do is sit here and say praise be! Dralistico leaving AEW is not only the best move for him, but it's the best move for AEW and it's quite frankly the best move for his older brother if he has any hope of becoming a more consistent presence on AEW TV. Now to be clear; I am not a big fan of Dralistico, and haven't been going back to his days where he was the replacement Mistico in CMLL. There's some talent there, but he's always been wildly inconsistent, even at his best, he's doing stuff at a level that other luchadors do far better, and I think he's been an anchor of sorts to Rush, because Dralistico without being paired with Rush doesn't work. So him leaving doesn't hurt AEW, and Dralistico going to AAA or the Mexican indies could be what breathes him new life. It also frees Rush to go off and be Rush, which, when motivated, is one of the most dynamic and exciting luchadors in the world. Of course, there's no guarantee Rush doesn't combust anyway (he's volatile in his own right), nor no guarantee that he gets the sustained AEW push he's looking for. But ultimately, if the idea is Dralistico leaves and Rush stays, it strikes me as a positive for both, and for AEW, who now no longer has to worry about keeping Rush paired with a guy they've seemingly never had much interest in.
summary: Dave Meltzer reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that Rush's absence from AEW stems from an expired visa with his new one not expected until the start of 2027. Sources close to the situation indicated that Rush remains happy in AEW despite the setback. This marks another instance of visa problems impacting AEW talent plans following a similar delay for Ilja Dragunov.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Explains Why His WWE Contract Negotiations Went Nowhere
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Explains Why His WWE Contract Negotiations Went Nowhere
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has finally explained why he completely disappeared from WWE television during the final four months of his contract.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was specifically asked why fans didn’t see him on WWE television between his final match in April and his contract expiring in August . Dragunov admitted the real explanation probably isn’t nearly as exciting as some of the theories that popped up while he was gone. “Again, everything I can say is not as exciting as people made it. Of course, at some point in time, you don’t have creative — you’re just waiting for the next opportunities to come.” Dragunov believes part of the problem was simply how crowded WWE had become. New wrestlers were coming into the picture, existing storylines were already packed, and there was only so much television time available to go around. “Because a lot of new people came up, a lot of stories were full. We all know there is only a certain amount of time for certain people.” So Dragunov waited. There wasn’t some dramatic backstage incident that he pointed to or a secret plan to leave WWE months ahead of time — another creative opportunity just never materialized before his deal reached the finish line. “Everything I know is that the expiration of my contract came and that the negotiations did not lead anywhere.” Helwani then asked Dragunov directly about one of the bigger questions surrounding those negotiations: did WWE ask him to take a pay cut? That’s where Dragunov decided there were some details he wasn’t willing to make public. “Did they offer me a pay cut? To be honest, I am too much of a discreet businessman to talk about these kinds of things.” “Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, ‘Okay, I MUST stick with here.’” That adds another piece to Dragunov’s explanation of how his WWE exit actually happened. He previously revealed that he had no idea his appearance in the Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April would become his final WWE match, because he hadn’t decided at that point that he was leaving. Dragunov also confirmed that WWE didn’t simply want to get rid of him. He said there was “no intention of the company to let me go,” but as his contract ran down, the two sides ultimately couldn’t reach terms that made staying feel like the right choice for him. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things. It was an accumulation of the offers, because we know it’s a business, but it was also based on my feeling — how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Where can I see myself staying forever?” Dragunov still isn’t revealing the private details of those WWE negotiations, especially when it comes to money. What he is making clear is that months without creative followed by an offer he didn’t find satisfying ultimately made the decision to find that “fresh air” somewhere else a whole lot easier. title: Why WWE’s Cody Rhodes is ‘excited’ about Street Fighter featuring 3 wrestlers

body: Among the stars of the new Street Fighter movie are former WWE rivals Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns, but another professional wrestler, Hirooki Goto, is also in it. This makes the "American Nightmare" happy. He is "proud" of having three wrestling stars represent their industry in the blockbuster movie, as he told Denise Salcedo. "So the fact that you have Roman [Reigns], you have [Hirooki] Goto, and me all in this, and everyone's vastly different. I'm excited for wrestling," he continued. Rhodes and Reigns play Guile and Akuma, respectively, in the new Street Fighter movie. Goto played E. Honda in the movie as well. This is one of Rhodes' first major acting roles. While he previously had a small role in the Stephen Amell-led Arrow series, he had his first major acting role in The Naked Gun last year. He played a bartender and shared the screen with Liam Neeson. Reigns has had roles in other blockbusters in the past. He starred in Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw, playing Mateo Hobbs. He also voiced one of the Zebros in Zootopia 2. Another one of his former foes, CM Punk, voiced the other Zebro. Street Fighter has made over $50 million to date at the box office. It led the domestic box office in its opening weekend, grossing over $30.7 million.
