title: Results Recap: How to Assess Digital PR Campaign for Wrestling Brands
raw_title: How to Assess Digital PR Campaign Results for Wrestling Brands - PWInsider
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin How to Assess Digital PR Campaign Results for Wrestling Brands By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-20 10:39:00 For a wrestling promotion, a busy news cycle can make a campaign look successful before anyone checks what it achieved. A press release may be picked up, a new show may trend locally, or a talent announcement may circulate across social media. Those signals matter, but how to assess digital PR campaign results depends on connecting attention to a goal: selling tickets, growing an audience, strengthening a brand, or making a new venture credible. Before a campaign begins, decide what it is meant to change. Promoting a live event calls for different measures than announcing a streaming partnership or introducing a new wrestling brand. If the objective is ticket sales, track visits to the event page, ticket referrals and purchases during the campaign period. If the aim is awareness, look at relevant audience reach, branded searches and meaningful coverage in outlets that wrestling fans actually read. Set a baseline as well. Compare results with a similar period, a previous event or the normal level of traffic and engagement. Without that context, a rise in mentions may simply reflect a major show, a viral moment or a news story unrelated to the PR work. Where possible, use tagged campaign links and dedicated landing pages so that referral activity can be distinguished from general traffic. Coverage volume is easy to report, but it is not the same as influence. A list of placements can include duplicate syndication, brief mentions and stories that reach audiences with little interest in the promotion. Review the quality of coverage: Was the key announcement accurately described? Did the story include the information fans need? Was the outlet relevant to the intended audience? Did coverage lead readers to take a next step? A useful report combines a few types of evidence instead of treating one metric as proof of success: Reach: relevant outlets, estimated audience, social sharing and search visibility. Action: ticket purchases, registrations, merchandise activity or inquiries, when these can be attributed responsibly. Reputation: accuracy of coverage, message inclusion, sentiment and the quality of conversations around the announcement. Keep the measurement proportional. A smaller independent promotion may not have access to sophisticated attribution tools, and that does not make its results unmeasurable. A consistent spreadsheet of placements, links, dates and outcomes can reveal useful patterns. Avoid claiming that PR caused every sale or follower increase; other marketing, talent activity and the event itself may also contribute. Digital PR can include press release writing and distribution, pitching journalists, securing editorial coverage, online publishing and reporting. title: Why Ilja Dragunov Only Negotiated With AEW After His WWE Exit
raw_title: Why Ilja Dragunov Only Negotiated With AEW After His WWE Exit
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov apparently didn’t spend his free agency shopping himself around the wrestling world before landing in AEW. The former WWE star says AEW was the only promotion he spoke to, and everything came together pretty quickly once he was ready to figure out his next move.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked whether he had conversations with any other wrestling companies after his WWE contract expired in August. According to Dragunov, there really wasn’t some huge bidding process happening behind the scenes. “If I gotta be honest, everything went down so fast. Everything I did was just giving myself a rest — that’s pretty much what I did for the most part.” After spending years under the WWE umbrella, Dragunov’s first priority wasn’t immediately finding another contract. He took some time for himself, but once things started moving with AEW, they moved very quickly. “When things clicked, they clicked very fast. Yes, I only spoke to AEW.” That also clears up any questions about whether Dragunov entertained offers from several promotions before ultimately choosing Tony Khan’s company. At least according to Dragunov, AEW was the only conversation he had. Helwani then asked when Dragunov actually signed his AEW contract. Dragunov didn’t give an exact date, but indicated it happened fairly soon after his WWE deal reached its expiration. “I think it was possibly just a minor time after my contract expired. It was a very easygoing expiration.” That’s particularly interesting considering Dragunov previously revealed WWE had no intention of simply letting him go. He said there were negotiations before his contract expired, but ultimately nothing about the situation gave him the feeling that he absolutely needed to remain with the company. “Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, ‘Okay, I MUST stick with here.’” Dragunov had also spent the final months of his WWE contract without a television storyline. His last match came during WrestleMania 42 weekend in April, and he previously explained that he spent the months afterwards waiting for another creative opportunity while WWE’s television time and existing storylines remained crowded. Once his contract expired in August, Dragunov eventually found the change he was looking for in AEW. He previously described wanting “new, fresh air” and a different landscape where he could satisfy his hunger for competition. There was still one thing holding up his actual arrival — his visa. Dragunov revealed that after finally learning his passport was ready , he contacted AEW and was on a flight back to the United States just seven hours later, allowing everything to come together for his WrestleDream debut. So despite all the speculation that surrounded Dragunov’s future after WWE, his version of events is actually pretty straightforward. He took some time to rest, only talked to AEW, and once the two sides clicked, it apparently didn’t take long to make him All Elite. title: Dralistico Reportedly Closing in on AEW Exit: Where Could the Mexican Star End Up?
raw_title: Dralistico Reportedly Closing in on AEW Exit: Where Could the Mexican Star End Up?
body: Bryan Alvarez of F4WOnline addressed Dralistico’s status after the La Faccion Ingobernable member and his brother Rush drew attention with a pair of social media posts. On October 19, Dralistico shared an edited photo of himself in handcuffs and behind bars in a post on X , with the caption “Maybe not for long?” Fans took the post as a sign that he wants to leave AEW. “Regarding the Dralistico and Rush tweets we talked about last night: Dralistico’s AEW deal expires in December, and based on that tweet one would presume he wants out,” Alvarez wrote. Dralistico, whose real name is Carlos Munoz Gonzalez, is the son of La Bestia del Ring and the brother of Rush and WWE’s Dragon Lee. He began his career in CMLL in 2010 under the name Dragon Lee before becoming the second Mistico in 2012. During his time in CMLL, he won the CMLL World Tag Team Championship, the CMLL World Trios Championship and the CMLL World Welterweight Championship. He left the promotion in 2021 and joined his father and brother Rush in La Faccion Ingobernable, also known as LFI. He has worked on AEW and ROH programming for several years. His notable matches include an AEW International Championship challenge against Orange Cassidy in 2023 and an ROH World Championship match against Bandido in 2025. He missed time late in 2025 with an ear injury that required surgery and returned on the March 7 episode of Collision. Dralistico leaving would not be a surprise. He has barely been used since his return from surgery, and a wrestler who is healthy and not on television is usually a wrestler who is looking at his options. The post on X was about as clear a message as he could send without saying it directly, and Alvarez’s read on it matches what most fans took away from it. For AEW, losing Dralistico would be a small loss on paper, but it would further thin out La Faccion Ingobernable at a time when Rush cannot work. The group has not been a priority for months, and with one brother likely leaving and the other unavailable until 2027, AEW has little reason to keep it going in its current form.

body: Lasting from March until August, the feud saw Francis and Elijah face off in a number of matches on both pay-per-view and television. Speaking with The Wrestling Classic for a new interview , AJ Francis reflected on the feud, saying that it’s probably the best storyline in wrestling this year. “Just look at the feud I had with Elijah. From the stuff we did in the studio where he’s like haunting my mind to me stealing his name, image, and likeness, to us having the match and me hitting Expressions in the head with a guitar and me getting the Expressions medical fund. Just the opportunity to be creative and do different things. That was probably the most — if you start from the beginning of me and Elijah’s storyline to the end of it at Lockdown, I mean that’s probably the best storyline in wrestling this year. It’s the best, most creative storyline in wrestling this year. I stand on that. Not only that, but we had banger fucking matched at Slammiversary and at Lockdown. title: Tommaso Ciampa Eyes Match With Shingo Takagi In NJPW

body: It's not all fun and games. Ciampa has aspirations of wrestling in NJPW and has his sights set on one man. In an interview with SBNation , Ciampa said he wants to wrestle former IWGP Heavyweight Champion, Shingo Takagi. "Shingo [Takagi] always jumps out at me as someone I've always wanted to share a ring with. I don't know that my body or personal life at this point bodes well for a full-on tour or G1 Tournament, but doing a show here or there, or three shows, I'd be 100% open to that," he said. Takagi has had his share of matches with AEW talent as of late. Over the summer, he wrestled the late PAC and Claudio Castagnoli in a tag match and blamed them for his poor showing in the G1. After calling out Castagnoli, he defeated him at Destruction last month . He is scheduled to face a returning Jon Moxley at Power Struggle on November 3 .

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Speaks On Brock Lesnar No-Selling His Offense at WWE Royal Rumble
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Addresses Brock Lesnar No-Selling His Offense at WWE Royal Rumble
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov isn’t exactly haunted by the way Brock Lesnar steamrolled him at the Royal Rumble. Months after that quick elimination left fans frustrated and even got some eye-rolls backstage, Dragunov says he barely gave the whole thing another thought.
body: Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked about his brief showdown with Lesnar at the 2026 Men’s Royal Rumble. For Dragunov, getting in the face of someone like Lesnar was exactly what his character was supposed to do. “I said it before, honestly, if you really understand the persona that I have been in the ring for the most part of the time, I’ve been facing monsters. And at the end of the day, you can’t change certain things.” The moment itself was pretty brutal. Dragunov stepped up to Lesnar and started throwing his trademark chops, only for Brock to basically brush them off, scream in his face and dump him over the top rope. Dragunov knows most people probably wouldn’t be lining up to pick a fight with Lesnar. That’s also exactly why he believes backing down would’ve made no sense for him. “I can’t change anything about it, but my best career moments were made by my vulnerability. I wasn’t becoming a name by being the person who dominates at all times.” That’s really the whole Dragunov formula. He gets absolutely destroyed, somehow keeps coming and makes people care about whether he can fight his way back. Dragunov also isn’t mad that people were upset for him. He admitted the whole thing possibly could’ve been handled differently, but he’s definitely not sitting around replaying that Lesnar elimination in his head. So while plenty of people saw the Royal Rumble spot as Dragunov getting completely brushed aside, he clearly doesn’t look at it that way. If anything, fans getting angry on his behalf fits perfectly with a career that’s largely been built around watching Dragunov take a beating and desperately wanting to see him fight back. title: Top Takeaways from Lucha Underground Binge
raw_title: TOP FIVE LIST: Takeaways from binging four season of Lucha Underground including Penta, Rey Fenix, Ricochet, Inter-gender wrestling
body: Working in my own store that carries a lot of pro wrestling merchandise, I spend all day on Mondays with wrestling on the TV in-store. I will watch something until the start of Raw, then pick it back up the next week. In doing so, I was finally able to complete the entire series, and what a wild series it was. On the first episode, you saw Pentagon Jr. and Rey Fénix. They were never announced as brothers on this show, but there was a unique focus on these two characters. They were both incredible in the ring. The first time I watched years ago, I felt a little bit like I did when first watch Rey Mysterio Jr. arrive in WCW. The way Fénix worked the ropes was so unique. Pentagon had this unique charisma that you could not ignore. They were set up to be key characters, and the people running this show, including Konnan’s eye for talent, knew they had something special in these two. Mil Muertes was a reskinned Judas Masias, who came in as a possessed killer, paired with Catrina who controlled him to do her will. Santos Escobar was under a mask as King Cuerno. A hunter who came in to stalk his prey. I could not believe how mishandled this talent was in WWE after watching him perform in “The Temple.” Ricochet, again under a mask, was Puma, Konnan’s new protege, who was trying his talent against top tier opponents for the first time. My favorite character was Sexy Star. It was very unfortunate that she made the decisions she made to blackball her from a career she was very good at. A woman in an abusive relationship finally decided to stand up for herself, and become a fighter. She was able to fight off her abuser, and in doing so, realized she had everything it took to defeat men in a competitive fight. She even worked her way to being the promotion’s champion for a brief moment. Well-defined background, very good in the ring, and beautiful to attract viewers and look great on posters. Perhaps one of wrestling’s biggest losses, but that was a decision of the performer to deserve her fate of no longer being accepted. I was hesitant to accept this when I first viewed Lucha Underground, but came to not only accept it, but enjoy it. I have previously stated my appreciation for the character of Sexy Star, but I also liked seeing competent women mix it up with men, who were confident in selling offense and even taking clean losses to the women on the roster. In a world where we go to theaters and accept Wonder Woman, Harley Quinn, or Atomic Blonde as viable cinema, why can’t this extend to wrestling? I have often said that Asuka would make me more nervous to fight than many of the men on the roster. That said, I completely understand that corporate WWE will not be entertaining this again any time soon. We had Chyna as the Intercontinental Champion, but that was the exception that won’t be happening again any time soon. title: Contract News: 'A Lot of TNA Wrestling Contracts Coming Up' Soon: 6 Stars We Want to See Jump to WWE, Including Matt & Jeff Hardy
raw_title: 'A Lot of TNA Wrestling Contracts Coming Up' Soon: 6 Stars We Want to See Jump to WWE, Including Matt & Jeff Hardy
body: According to FightFul, “ a lot of contracts are coming up in December ” for some on the TNA roster. It means that quite a few talented wrestlers could be on the free agent market to begin 2027. With that in mind, we take a look at six TNA stars we would love to see make the jump to WWE early next year. Reports in the summer claimed that WWE is trying to make an effort to improve their tag division. However, they decided to do so after cutting The New Day and The Motor City Machine Guns. They could certainly use some veteran teams with charisma, and TNA has a few that might be available in a couple of months. One that WWE should check in on if they hit the open market is The Righteous. The duo of Dutch and Vincent are a well-traveled team that has also competed in AEW. They have a very unique gimmick and presentation that could appeal to the WWE audience. Moose has done everything possible in TNA, so it just seems like a matter of time before he eventually takes his talents elsewhere. He has been open about his desire to one day compete in WWE. If the multi-time world champion is open to first working in NXT, he would be a great veteran for the black and gold brand before he makes the jump to the main roster. Moose could also be a potential candidate to be a member of 946 in the future. The Hardys are not just one of the greatest tag teams in WWE and TNA history. title: Judge denies WWE dismissal in ring boy lawsuit
raw_title: Judge rejects WWE and McMahons’ motion to have ‘ring boy’ lawsuit dismissed
summary_src: A federal judge on Monday (October 19) rejected a motion to dismiss the “ring boy” lawsuit against WWE/TKO, Vince McMahon, and U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon.
body: Link Photo by Jim Spellman/WireImage A federal judge on Monday (October 19) rejected a motion to dismiss the “ring boy” lawsuit against WWE/TKO, Vince McMahon, and U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon. In 2024, a lawsuit was filed against former WWE boss Vince, his wife Linda, and WWE/TKO on behalf of five survivors of what’s dubbed the “Ring Boy Scandal.” The seven plaintiffs who filed the suit claim they were sexually abused when they were minors in the 1980s and 1990s and setting up rings and running errands for WWE. All of the seven men allege abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips, while one alleges sexual abuse by former WWE executive Pat Patterson, and one alleges sexual harassment against former WWE Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. Phillips, Patterson, and Garvin have all passed away. However, the suit claims negligence by the McMahons and WWE/TKO for allegedly allowing the abuse to take place and continue. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling on Monday reported U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar rejected an effort by WWE/TKO and the McMahons to have the lawsuit dismissed on grounds that the Maryland Child Victims Act, which the plaintiffs used to file the case, violates the U.S. Constitution. In their motion for dismissal, WWE/TKO and the McMahons cited difficulties in litigating a case based on alleged abuse from decades ago where the accused abusers are no longer living. The defendants contended the 14th Amendment of the Constitution protects people’s rights against unfair or arbitrary laws, which they argued that using the Child Victims Act would do. (The Maryland law eliminates time limits for filing lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.) According to Thurston, Bredar wrote in his ruling that the defendants did not “show how their particular hardships make the [Maryland Child Victims Act] arbitrary or irrational.” Since Bredar ruled the law is constitutional for use in the case, the lawsuit will now go to discovery phase, and a teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to set additional deadlines. The plaintiffs claim abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips. One plaintiff also alleges sexual abuse by former executive Pat Patterson, and another alleges sexual harassment by former Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. All three accused individuals have since passed away.

The suit accuses the McMahons and WWE of negligence for allegedly allowing the abuse to occur and continue. The case was filed under the Maryland Child Victims Act, which removes time limits for lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.

WWE, TKO, and the McMahons argued that the Maryland law violates the 14th Amendment by being unfair or arbitrary, especially given the decades-old allegations and the deaths of the accused. The judge ruled that the defendants failed to demonstrate how the law is arbitrary or irrational in this case.
With the motion to dismiss denied, the lawsuit will proceed to the discovery phase. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish additional deadlines.

title: What worked and didn’t work with Roman and Sami, Funko Pop hijinks, The 946-Bloodline build to WarGames, more — WWE RAW HITS & MISSES (10/19)
raw_title: WWE RAW HITS & MISSES (10/19): What worked and didn’t work with Roman and Sami, Funko Pop hijinks, The 946-Bloodline build to WarGames, more
body: Roman – Sami – HIT: This was a fun moment to start the show with a reunion between Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn. There was a lot to like about it. Their interplay was strong, as were their performances. I’m okay with Reigns trying to recruit Zayn to help The Bloodline against The 946, as well as Zayn refusing to help. My problem with the segment was when they were arguing over which of their titles is the more important. That stuff is stupid and unproductive. I already don’t care about the Crown Jewel concept (beyond the Saudi Arabia of it all), and this doesn’t do anything to make me care more about their match. So while I liked parts of this opening segment, it is a marginal Hit because it didn’t end as strong as it started. Sky & Green vs. Judgment Day – HIT: This was a good tag team match to continue the build between Chelsea Green and Liv Morgan for their meaningless Crown Jewel match, as well as setting up Iyo Sky as the next challenger for Raquel Rodriguez’s Intercontinental Title. I was glad that Green didn’t take another loss. Sky getting the pin for their team gets her into that IC Title picture while getting Green some needed momentum after her loss to Roxanne Perez last week. Funko Pop – MISS: Making fun of JD McDonagh for having a big head is okay in general, but the Funko Pop figure bit has been lame. Overall, I like Joe Tessitore, but he was way too much like Michale Cole in his over-the-top geeky responses to all of these jokes. The match quality between McDonagh and Joe Hendry was fine, but the backdrop was far too silly. Maybe the destruction of Hendry’s guitar over the head of the mascot will be the end of the silliness. That’s probably too much to hope for. Valkyria vs. Vice – HIT: Lyra Valkyria’s obsession with Bayley is costing her. Not only did it set up this match against Lola Vice, which she didn’t want, but it also helped lead to her losing it. The match itself was good. WWE is doing a nice job of establishing Vice, particularly her spinning backfist finisher, which looked very strong here. The no-disqualification match next week between Valkyria and Bayley should be very good and blow off their feud. Gable vs. Mysterio vs. Lee – HIT: This was a great IC Title match with a predictable finish. I know some people were buying into Rey Mysterio possibly wining to become the new WWE Champion, but there was no way that Chad Gable was going to lose the title before defending it against Ethan Page. But Gable, Mysterio and Dragon Lee put on such a great match that the predicability of it didn’t take away from my enjoyment of it. It made sense to have this match given the storyline between Gable and the luchadores. The attack from Ethan afterwards should finally get him his IC Title match. Big Cass also being involved attacking Mysterio and Lee was interesting. He didn’t seem to be working with Ethan, but with Rusev healthy again after his recent injury, a budding faction is a possibility.

title: Ilja Dragunov Explains WWE Exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up About Decision To Leave WWE, 'Nothing Felt Satisfying'
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at AEW WrestleDream, where he was announced as the company's newest signing. Dragunov departed WWE in August after not wrestling since April. His contract expired, and he made the decision not to renew.
body: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at AEW WrestleDream, where he was announced as the company’s newest signing. Dragunov departed WWE in August after not wrestling since April. His contract expired, and he made the decision not to renew. Speaking to Ariel Helwani on the Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov detailed his decision to leave WWE. Asked if he knew his last match would be in April, Dragunov replied, “No, absolutely not. Every tale I have to tell about that is not very exciting. I didn’t know I was leaving at the time. I was just waiting. I love what I do. I want to compete and work. It’s nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. Time just passed by, and I reached the expiration of my contract. I felt that, over time, with how things were working out and how I’m feeling, it was time to breathe new and fresh air.” “Yeah, there was no intention of the company to let me go,” he said. Asked if he was unhappy with the offer, he replied, “It was an accumulation of a lot of things. The offer, as we all know, is a business, but it’s also based on my feelings. How do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? You have to consider all the factors. I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a very long time. The landscape changed. Now, we have other opportunities. After such a long time being in the company, not seeking out new opportunities at a place where I see myself more fitting- who wouldn’t do that?” Asked if he was asked to take a pay cut or was given a raise, he said, “I’m too discreet and too much of a businessman and a gentleman to talk about these kinds of things. Everything I can say is that there was nothing that I felt satisfied with and nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘I must stick with this.'” Dragunov was still under contract until August, but kept off TV from April until his deal expired. Asked if they knew he wouldn’t be coming back, he replied, “Anything I can say is not as exciting as people made it. At some point in time, you don’t have creativity, and you’re waiting for the next opportunity to come. A lot of new people came up. A lot of stories were full. There is only a certain amount of time for certain people. I’m not going to go too deep into that. Everything I knew was that the expiration of my contract came, and negotiations didn’t lead anywhere.” Dragunov is set to make his in-ring debut in AEW on Wednesday’s Dynamite. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show, Dragunov said he did not know his last match would be in April, that nothing felt satisfying as time passed, and it was an accumulation of factors including how things were working out and his desire for fresh air.

title: Rush Confirms AEW Happiness Amid Expired Visa
raw_title: Rush Confirms His Visa Has Expired, Addresses Whether He's Happy In AEW
summary_src: AEW star Rush took to social media on Tuesday to confirm his visa has expired, and he addressed whether or not he's happy in the company.
body: Rush shared a photo of himself in a pool, looking out toward the ocean. He started the post by saying, "Everyone loves gossip!" "But they actually got two things right," Rush continued. "I'm happy at my home, #AEW, and my visa has expired." Earlier on Tuesday, it was reported by F4WOnline's Bryan Alvarez that Rush's visa has been expired for some time. According to Alvarez, the star's new visa isn't expected to come in until the start of next year. Rush has previously posted, in regards to his AEW absence, that fans would see him "maybe next year," leading many to believe he was unhappy with his status in the company. I'm happy at my home, #AEW , and my visa has expired. pic.twitter.com/dMc8Pwz8nw Dave Meltzer said on " Wrestling Observer Radio " that he's not sure when Rush's contract is up. In addition to Rush's own words in his most recent post, it was noted in previous reports that he is happy in AEW, despite the visa issues that have been plaguing him and other stars, including the recently-debuted Ilja Dragunov . Rush is reportedly healthy while waiting out his visa issues. His last match took place on the July 1 edition of "AEW Collision," where he defeated Jordan Cruz. Rush also notably faced off against then-AEW World Champion MJF in a no count out match at the beginning of June on an episode of "AEW Dynamite." Alvarez confirmed that Rush's brother, Dralistico's contract is soon coming to an end. After his post on Monday, it appears likely Dralistico will not remain with AEW.
summary: Rush addressed online speculation by confirming he remains happy with AEW while revealing his visa has expired. title: Ilja Dragunov details reasons for WWE exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov explains WWE departure: ‘The landscape in this beautiful business changed’
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov had a gut feeling that leaving WWE would work out for him. During a Tuesday appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show, Dragunov described leaving WWE as a decision he made to bet om himself.
body: Ilja Dragunov had a gut feeling that leaving WWE would work out for him. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things,” Dragunov said. “An accumulation of, of course, the offering, because we all know, at the end of the day, it’s the business. But it’s also definitely based on my feeling of, like, how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Is the scenery change something where I can see myself staying forever? Because you’ve got to consider a lot of factors. Like, I spent the most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a very, very long time. And the landscape in this beautiful business changed. So the beautiful thing is nowadays we have other opportunities. And for me personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe a place where I see myself more fitting — who wouldn’t do that?” When asked if WWE’s offer included a raise or pay cut, Dragunov didn’t want to go into detail about what was being offered. “To be honest, I’m too much discreet and too much of a businessman and a gentleman myself to talk about these kinds of things,” he said. “Everything I can say is that it was nothing that I felt satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘Okay, I must stick with what I hear.’” Dragunov said he did not know the 2026 Andre the Giant Memorial Battle Royal in April would end up being his last match for the company. The first time he started to feel like WWE maybe wasn’t the right place for him was around March-April 2026. After dropping the United States Championship at the end of 2025, Dragunov thinks there could have been more time to go into a story that was “outside of just holding a championship.” Returning from ACL surgery and winning the US title in October 2025 was an amazing moment for Dragunov, and he’s grateful for all of the beautiful people he got to spend time with in WWE. He has no regrets about his tenure there. Dragunov described his AEW WrestleDream arrival as a “fairytale.” He appreciates the warm welcome the fans gave him and all the work AEW put into making his debut special. Everything has been collaborative so far between Dragunov and AEW. Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut on Dynamite this Wednesday night. He told Helwani that he does not know the identity of his opponent yet. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: Ilja Dragunov said his decision to leave WWE came from multiple factors including the financial offer, his desire for a creative change of scenery after spending most of his 20s with the company, and the evolving opportunities in the wrestling business. He expressed that after such a long tenure it made sense to explore places where he might fit better long term. Dragunov declined to discuss specifics of WWE's contract offer, citing his discretion as a businessman.

title: Roman Reigns Explains His Part-Time WWE Schedule
raw_title: Roman Reigns On His WWE Schedule: 'Quality Over Quantity'
summary_src: Commenting on his part-time WWE schedule, Roman Reigns emphasized that the quality of his in-ring performances is more important than their frequency.
body: "Quality over quantity, every single day of the week," Reigns stated during an interview with Sam Roberts on his " notsam " radio show. "I don't like to fall down at all, and I — for some reason — chose to do that for a living, but that's a part of the deal. But yeah, it's got to be on a Saturday or a very important Sunday. It's got to check off one of my dates, you know what I mean?" Reigns' response was partially in jest, but in the past, he gave a more serious answer about his part-time schedule. Assessing the business side of pro wrestling, Reigns said he doesn't believe he should be doing live events based on his value as a main eventer. title: Tatum Paxley reflects on path to WWE Women's Tag Team title
raw_title: 'I was so lost': How Tatum Paxley went from college dropout to WWE champion
body: Not long ago, the new WWE Women's Tag Team Champion had no idea what her future held. But fast forward to today, and just over two months have passed since Paxley's main-roster debut on "WWE SmackDown" in August . "Oh man, I don't know if I've had a better week in my life," Paxley told Uncrowned. "It's one of those moments that is very 'pinch me, I'm dreaming.' I can remember it so well, standing in the ring, holding my title up, hearing the pyro. I just remember slowly looking over, and there's Alexa Bliss. "It's just so unbelievable. It's truly a dream come true for me, because she was such an inspiration for me getting here, and to be able to do this with her, and then to have Charlotte [Flair] in the back supporting us — it's just a dream come true." That shiny gold title hasn't left Paxley's side since she and Bliss beat the former champions, Fatal Influence — Fallon Henley and Lainey Reid. For Paxley, it's her third title under the WWE umbrella overall — she also won the top Women's Championship and North American Championship of the promotion's developmental brand, NXT. The drive to adapt came fast for Paxley, and she quickly learned that the performative nature of an endeavor like wrestling was perfect for her personality and athleticism. Normally, the jump from NXT to a WWE main-roster show like "SmackDown" can be jarring, but the change has fit Paxley like a glove, and she knew it was inevitable. "It has been super seamless for me. Personally, the transition from NXT to 'SmackDown' has been super calm," Paxley said. "I feel like it's just because I knew how ready I was. That's not to say that I was rushing by any means, but I just knew for a long time, when I get that call, I know who I am, I know how to connect with the audience, I know how to go in the ring. Like, I'm going to be ready. Then I get the call, I have like some of the best people that have taken me under their wing [with] Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss. It has just been super seamless. It just feels right. Paxley likes not having a plan; she's built her career with blinders on, to an extent. That may almost seem counterproductive in a business as calculated as professional wrestling, but Paxley took it so far as even insisting on staying in the dark ahead of her WWE debut in August. She recalled thinking that producer Michael Hayes was ribbing her when told she'd premiere in the long-awaited Charlotte Flair vs. Jade Cargill match. "I'm someone who doesn't really like to know the plan. I don't like to know the direction. I like to really live in the moment," Paxley said. "I have the quality to really overthink something. So I find the less I know, the better. "So when I originally got word that main roster was looking at me, I was like, 'Cool. Don't tell me nothing,' and just kind of just went about my life. People would slowly start kind of telling me what they knew and who I would be [working] with, so I had a little bit of an idea of what was happening. But I tried not to

The company had since shifted focus to its EA Sports UFC titles after acquiring the UFC license. The announcement follows a teaser photo and comes as EA is reportedly set to be sold to Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, which has ties to boxing promotions.

llm_long: A teaser photo was posted on Tuesday hinting at the return of the EA Fight Night boxing video game series. No additional details were provided at the time of the announcement.

The most recent entry in the series was Fight Night Champion, which was released in 2011. Following that release, EA shifted its focus to the UFC after acquiring the license for the mixed martial arts organization.
EA went on to release five EA Sports UFC titles between 2014 and 2026. Several boxers have appeared in the EA UFC games, including Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua.

Fury and Joshua are scheduled to face each other in December in one of the most anticipated heavyweight boxing matches in decades. EA is in the process of being sold to Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, which has been heavily involved in Zuffa Boxing.

body: Ilja Dragunov says he has no regrets about his encounter with Brock Lesnar at the 2026 WWE Royal Rumble, despite some fans feeling Lesnar’s response to his chops was disrespectful. During the match in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on January 31, Dragunov chopped Lesnar several times in the corner. Lesnar no-sold the chops, screamed at Dragunov, and then eliminated him from the Rumble. The new AEW signing addressed his interaction with Lesnar in the Rumble during Tuesday’s edition of The Ariel Helwani Show , with Helwani asking how he felt about fans who believed Lesnar had disrespected him. “First of all, that’s a shout-out to all the fans that are feeling with me and are passionate with me and get angry for me in that sense. I love all of you guys, and you’ve been sticking around with me forever. So I appreciate your concern. “But I said it before, honestly, if you really understand the persona that I have been in the ring for the most part of the time, I’ve been facing monsters. And at the end of the day, you can’t change certain things. You have a person like Brock Lesnar standing in front of you. Most people would run away as soon as that happens. That’s simply what would happen. Dragunov made his AEW debut on Saturday at WrestleDream 2026 in Orlando, Florida. body: Four weeks after All Out and we have our second AEW PPV, WrestleDream, in a row that felt inconsequential. Predictable match after predictable match. Right up to, and including, that main event match. This was not a good showing for AEW. Before you get too mad, of course the in ring work was great. It always is, but like I said on the Dynamite Post Show with Wade Keller, 7 years in I want more than just good matches. I get that this PPV build was weird due to the untimely death of Pac but, for me, that’s all the more reason to do something that might stand out on this PPV. I don’t want a hot shot angle or anything but just something to give AEW back that spark they had just a few months ago. We need to relish every Bucks PPV match we get going forward because I don’t know how many more we are going to get. Then when they are against two wrestlers the caliber of Knight and Fletcher, come on. Going forward, I thing we all know where the Bucks are headed, especially since it looked like Swerve and The New Level are going their separate ways. We are FINALLY going to get to see The Young Bucks vs. The New Level, something I have been wanting to see for ten years or more. I cannot wait. For Fletcher, I laid this out last week: It’s time for him to move up the card. If that means the Continental Title, so be it, but I want him to eventually dethrone Ospreay. For Knight, this one is a little harder to see where he is going. He could very easily slide right back into the TNT Title picture and it would work for him. While Fletcher is turn-key ready for the main event, Knight is about where Fletcher was two years ago and just needs to keep getting better. Erik Krol and Todd Martin are the first two members of the AEW’s “No Fun Club” (reference to the latest PWTorch VIP Post-PPV Roundtable ) and I have put in my application to be the third. What are we watching with Andrade? This guy has the look, can go in the ring, and has the ability to come across well on the mic. Sadly, what we get is a guy who is enamored with a catch phrase, taking selfies during matches, and wrestled a triple threat each match because he has to fight his pants! If you have read my column before, then you know what this means, Andrade is on Kazuchika Okada level for me. A bust. Okada lost me months ago, so even when he tried to turn it on, like the France match with Will Ospreay, it’s too late. I have lost faith in both. Going forward, Andrade needs a curator to help him with certain things. Wade Keller and I laid out tiny tweaks to the selfie spot and his overused catchphrase in our Wade Keller Post-show after Dynamite last week. First, make the way he gets to the catchphrase seem more organic. Not what they did on Dynamite. Second, put the selfie spot during his entrance. Make it something everyone is looking forward to. title: Bully Ray Questions WWE Enzo Amore Reunion With Big Cass
raw_title: Bully Ray Has Concerns About WWE Bringing Back Enzo Amore To Pair With Big Cass
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray outlined his concerns with WWE bringing back Enzo Amore to team with former tag partner Big Cass.
body: Fans have since been wondering when, or if, Amore will make his return, as Cass has been seemingly directionless on "WWE Raw." On " Busted Open Radio ," Bully Ray and Dave LaGreca pondered what's next for Cass, and if that involves his former tag team partner. "The first thing that comes to mind if you bring Enzo in now is Big Cass is a failed experiment," Bully Ray said. "If they were to bring in Enzo now, it would be like, 'We need to salvage this guy, and the only way we can salvage him is putting him back with this other guy,'" he said. "When Enzo and Cass first hit the scene, to me, they were equals. Enzo, the guy that can talk. Cass, the guy that can kick your a**. I wouldn't see them as equals again." The hosts agreed that it may not be possible to capture the "lightning in a bottle" that the team once had. LaGreca said it's a different audience now, and some fans will remember the team, but as Bully Ray said, the rest of the WWE universe "would need a reprogramming."

body: “The fact that this guy is already considering declaring an emergency when there obviously isn’t one – and that a lot of people in this country are OK with it – is a sad statement on where we are as a country.” Trump has since continued to leave the door open to some form of emergency declaration ahead of the midterms. In an October interview with Time , he again declined to rule out declaring a state of emergency before voters head to the polls. There are major limits to what such a declaration could actually accomplish when it comes to elections. States and local governments handle much of the administration of elections, while federal authority is constrained by the Constitution and federal election laws; Trump’s August exchange did not itself create any new presidential authority over state election administration. Now he’s doing exactly that again, with the midterms just weeks away. Foley clearly isn’t backing away from political posts when he believes something coming out of the Trump administration deserves a response. title: Ilja Dragunov Isn’t Worried About Getting Lost on AEW’s Stacked Roster
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Isn’t Worried About Getting Lost on AEW’s Stacked Roster
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov isn’t worried about becoming just another name on AEW’s ridiculously stacked roster. The former WWE star says getting lost in the shuffle isn’t a fear he has at all, because he’s spent his entire career betting on himself.
body: Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring , Dragunov was asked whether AEW’s loaded roster made him think about how he would stand out from everyone else. For Dragunov, that’s apparently not something he spent much time worrying about. “I mean, we basically talked about this right now. I didn’t consider how stacked the roster is because, like, that’s a fear I don’t have.” That confidence also played a pretty big role in Dragunov walking away from WWE. He believes in trusting his instincts, and leaving the company was another example of him being willing to take that gamble on himself. “I was always betting on myself. I bet on myself when I left WWE. I’m betting on myself still, and I’m betting on what my gut is telling me.” Dragunov also thinks AEW has already shown that it sees something different in him. He pointed directly to the way the company presented his arrival at WrestleDream, where his debut was treated like a major deal before Tony Khan officially confirmed that he was All Elite. “And the way the people — the company — introduced me, I think it speaks for itself that I stick out from all the rest in that roster.” For Dragunov, standing out isn’t about trying to manufacture something just because the roster is crowded. He believes wrestlers who are genuinely different naturally pull people’s attention toward them. “And, you know, people who stick out and are not like anybody else, you kind of, like, put the objective on them.” That’s also where Dragunov slipped in an interesting observation about wrestling today. He suggested that too many wrestlers are trying to look or act like everyone else, and that’s when getting overlooked becomes a real problem. “And only if you are like everybody else or try to be like everybody else — which is also, like, an unfortunate thing happening nowadays, unfortunately — then you get overlooked.” Dragunov doesn’t believe he falls into that category, and he’s got 14 years of experience to back up that confidence. As far as he’s concerned, standing out has never been the problem. “But I haven’t been overlooked once in my 14 years of career.” AEW certainly isn’t short on talent, so Dragunov will have plenty of competition for television time as his run gets going. He just doesn’t sound interested in worrying about any of that, especially when being different has worked out pretty well for him for the last 14 years. title: Ilja Dragunov details WWE exit and AEW arrival
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov on his AEW fairy tale, WWE regrets, Lesnar’s no-selling, and Gunther’s booking
summary_src: Fresh off a Saturday night debut at AEW’s WrestleDream PPV, and with his first AEW match tomorrow night on Dynamite to promote, Ilja Dragunov stopped by The Ariel Helwani Show this afternoon (Oct. 20).
body: Link Ricky Havlik for All Elite Wrestling Fresh off a Saturday night debut at AEW’s WrestleDream PPV, and with his first AEW match tomorrow night on Dynamite to promote, Ilja Dragunov stopped by The Ariel Helwani Show this afternoon (Oct. 20). Dragunov left WWE when his last contract expired, and spoke a little bit about that decision and the one to join AEW at the post-PPV media scrum, but he went a little more in depth with Helwani. The lack of creative for his character after dropping the United States title last December was a red flag for the Mad Dragon: ”After I dropped the belt, things kind of went in directions where I felt like, ok, it could have been better. There could have been more time to go into a story, into something that is outside of just holding a championship, captivating for the people… It never changed anything about my work mentality, because I love what I do, and I make every minute count for myself. But we all have feelings, and… especially if we’re in a business like this, we want to devote ourselves to this…” “There was no intention of the company to let me go… It was an accumulation of a lot of things. Of course, the offering, because we all know at the end of the day, it’s a business. But also, it’s definitely based on my feeling of how I want to work creatively. I spent most of my twenties in WWE. That’s a very, very long time, and the landscape in this beautiful business changed… the expiration of my contract came and the negotiations didn’t lead anywhere. There was nothing that I felt satisfying. Nothing that gave me the perspective of, ‘Oo, I must stick with what I have here.’ I had a gut feeling. I think things will work out for me, that I can bet on myself… Change always requires guts. It requires courage. It requires dealing with the possibility that things could not work out your way. It all came down to betting on myself and believing it’s going to be all right.” That also sets up a great line from Ilja about the polarizing reaction he gets from wrestling fandom: “I don’t see it as a defeat. I’m glad that people are upset for me, and maybe it could have worked out a different way… “I have two categories of people watching my work. Either people who are extremely behind me, really get me, really get emotionally invested in me, or it’s the polar opposite, the people who think I’m the cringiest person in the world. But I love it that way because people care.” This clip also includes Helwani asked if Dragunov leaves with any regrets, which he dismisses with, “No, why should I?” before talking about what he got out of his seven years there, and expressing gratitude for the opportunities he got during that time. Asking about his old friend and epic rival Gunther’s booking this year got Dragunov to be slightly critical of his old company: “I guess my feelings the same feeling as a lot of other people share — if you are the person to retire John Cena, it’s kind of like a standard that you should keep a certain level

He cited a lack of creative direction after losing the United States title last December as a key factor in his decision to leave when his contract expired. Dragunov also touched on his excitement for his new chapter in AEW, where he is set to wrestle on Dynamite.

title: WWE Covered Hip Surgery For Psicosis
raw_title: WWE Reportedly Covered Hip Surgery Costs For Former AAA Star Psicosis
summary_src: WWE has reportedly covered the hip replacement surgery costs for AAA Hall of Famer Psicosis, at the request of Psicosis' long-time rival Rey Mysterio
body: The decision to pay for the surgery, which is believed to have cost $44K, came from WWE President Nick Khan, and helped by Psicosis being under a WWE Legend's Contract. However, Meltzer describes the operation as being "spearheaded" by WWE luchador Rey Mysterio. Along with Juventud Guerrera, Psicosis is considered to be a key rival for Mysterio during the early portion of his career. Their rivalry spanned promotions such as AAA, the Japanese promotion WAR, ECW, and WCW, where the two notably competed in the acclaimed opening match at Bash at the Beach 1996, the site of the formation of the nWo. Even separate from his matches with Mysterio, Psicosis has had a memorable career, winning the WCW World Cruiserweight Championship twice, the AAA World Tag Team Championships with Joe Lider, and the Mexican National Welterweight Championship twice. He would briefly compete for WWE from 2005 to 2006 as part of the controversial Mexicools stable alongside Guerrera and Super Crazy. He had continued to compete in Mexico up until two years ago, when he was forced to have emergency surgery on his hip following an injury . He was inducted into the AAA Hall of Fame later that year.
summary: WWE paid for former AAA and WCW star Psicosis's hip surgery that reportedly cost $44,000. The decision came from President Nick Khan with the help of Psicosis being under a WWE Legends Contract. Per Dave Meltzer, Rey Mysterio spearheaded the effort due to their longstanding rivalry that began in AAA and continued through WAR, ECW and WCW.

title: MJF Replaces Billy Gunn At Create-A-Pro Event
raw_title: Billy Gunn off indie show due to ‘contractual obligations,’ top AEW name added
summary_src: Billy Gunn won’t be making his scheduled appearance for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend, but the Long Island fans are getting a significant makegood.
body: Billy Gunn won’t be making his scheduled appearance for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend, but the Long Island fans are getting a significant makegood. Create-A-Pro announced today that, due to contractual obligations, Gunn will not be at their Base Brawl event in North Merrick, New York this Saturday (October 24). However, former AEW World Champion MJF and AEW broadcaster Alicia Atout will now be doing meet and greets at the event. Those who purchased meet and greet packages for Gunn will have their money refunded, as will anyone who purchased a New Age Outlaws meet and greet. Road Dogg will still be at the show. which is a fundraiser for Merrick Bellmore Little League. MJF, who got his start in wrestling by training at Create-A-Pro, responded to the announcement of him replacing Gunn: “Perfect replacement. I [too] am an ass man.” Create-A-Pro is owned by Brian Myers and Pat Buck. MJF remains close with the school/promotion and returned this May for a victory over Max Caster. Originally, it was supposed to be MJF vs. Nic Nemeth at that event before TNA Wrestling changed its policy to not allow its wrestlers to face AEW names on the indies. On the same night as Saturday’s Create-A-Pro show, AEW will be in Winston-Salem, North Carolina for Collision. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

title: Ilja Dragunov explains decision to leave WWE for AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov reveals why he rejected WWE's offer to stay, frustrations that led to AEW move
body: Speaking Tuesday on "The Ariel Helwani Show" , Dragunov said he didn't know he was leaving the company when he competed in his final WWE match in April. "I didn't know at the time I was leaving. I was just waiting," Dragunov told Uncrowned. "I'm a person who loves what they do. I want to compete, I want to work, I want to do this and that. I just got a little stuck. But it's nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. "So, the time just passed by and then I reached the expiration of my contract, and I felt, over time, that OK, how everything is working out, and how I'm feeling — because I do a lot of things depending on how I feel about it. I've always had the courage to do so. I felt it was time to breathe some new fresh air." WWE letting Dragunov go was somewhat of a stunning decision to hear. After recovering from an ACL tear, Dragunov returned last year and made his "SmackDown" debut, winning the aforementioned U.S. title in his first appearance on the program. That alone showed the faith the company appeared to have in someone with his in-ring talent. "It was an accumulation of a lot of things," Dragunov said. "The [deal WWE was] offering — as we all know, at the end of the day, it's a business. But also, it's definitely based off my feeling of, do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Is the scenery change something where I can see myself stay forever? "You have to consider a lot of factors. I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That's a very, very long time, and the landscape in this beautiful business changed. The beautiful thing is, nowadays we have a lot of other opportunities, and for me personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe at a place where I see myself more fitting, who wouldn't do that?" "There was nothing that I felt [was] satisfying," Dragunov added of WWE's offer, "and nothing that gave me the perspective of like, 'OK, I must stick with what [I have] here.'" The U.S. title run was refreshing and well-deserved for Dragunov, whose initial main-roster run was cut extremely short on "Raw" by a knee injury. Dragunov, 33, still looks back very fondly at his final year in WWE and how it started. But once the title left his possession, he admits his mind started to wander. "After I tore my ACL, I had been fortunate to win a championship straight on my comeback, which was an amazing moment for me that I still cherish," Dragunov said. "I think that after I dropped the belt, things kind of went two directions where I feel like, 'OK, it could have been better. It could have been more time to go into a story, something that is outside of just holding a championship, captivating for the people.' So, around April, maybe even a month before that, I was just thinking about it. "It never changed anything about my work mentality, because I love what I do and I make every minute count for myself, but we all have feelings, and we all want to — especially in a business like this.
summary: Ilja Dragunov appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show and said he did not know he would be departing WWE during his final match in April. He explained that he grew frustrated feeling stuck in the company despite his desire to compete regularly and decided to let his contract expire before seeking a new environment. After recovering from an ACL tear, he had returned and captured the United States Championship on his SmackDown debut last year.

body: Ilja Dragunov says he “needs to wrestle in Japan,” believing his in-ring style would connect with the people. During an interview with TMZ on Tuesday, the new AEW signing was asked who he would still like to work with in his career. Dragunov instead said it wasn’t a matter of who he wanted to work with, but rather where. “I wouldn’t say it’s necessarily who I want to work with, but where I want to work. “Back in the day when I started with wXw, they had a working relationship with Big Japan Pro Wrestling. And when I joined wXw, it’s kind of like this time was passed. “And the one thing that I didn’t do in my career so far, multiple things that I didn’t do in my career so far, but specifically something that I need to do is to wrestle in Japan. I need to wrestle in Japan. Because that’s the place where I think my style belongs, and I think I would connect with the people, with this culture for professional wrestling in a whole different way.” Dragunov wrestled on three wXw shows co-promoted with Combat Zone Wrestling and Big Japan Pro Wrestling in 2013. However, all three events took place in Germany. During his time with wXw, Dragunov became a one-time wXw Unified World Wrestling Champion, a three-time wXw World Tag Team Champion and a two-time wXw Shotgun Champion. Dragunov made his AEW debut at WrestleDream 2026 in Orlando on Saturday, where Renee Paquette introduced him as the company’s newest signing. body: "They just have to realize that sometimes there's certain veterans that just aren't going to put up with that s*** no matter what," Gunn said. "If you're a young little buckaroo and you want to poke the bear, get ready to get bit. So, I think that's what happened. I don't know the whole details, that's between them." Gunn said that during his time in WWE, things like that usually didn't happen. He said then-chairman Vince McMahon had things under control backstage, and most guys knew they didn't have to like one another in order to do business together. He said there'd be a confrontation every now and then, but wrestlers worked it out all behind-the-scenes. "That's how grown a** people deal with s***," he said. "Nowadays, we don't, and that's sad, but there's going to be people that are going to do that."

Gunn, who serves as a coach in AEW, stated that he was not present for the incident. He noted that some veterans will not tolerate certain behavior and suggested that attempting to challenge them can lead to consequences.

He indicated that he was not familiar with all the details of the situation and chose not to follow the related media coverage. Gunn emphasized that the specifics remain between those directly involved.

When asked about handling similar issues during his earlier career, Gunn pointed to the approach taken under Vince McMahon. He explained that wrestlers were expected to conduct business professionally regardless of personal feelings.

Gunn described a method of addressing conflicts privately by pulling individuals into a room to resolve problems immediately. He contrasted this with current practices, calling the shift away from such discretion unfortunate.

body: According to Fightful Select , House personally confirmed that he was released from the WWE ID program. His departure comes only about seven months after WWE handed him an ID contract in March 2026. House had already gotten some exposure within WWE’s system under a different name. He competed as CJ Valor on WWE EVOLVE, giving fans a chance to see him work beyond his appearances on the independent scene. His road into WWE ID started even earlier this year. House participated in WWE’s tryouts in Orlando in January before eventually receiving his contract two months later, making his run with the program a pretty short one. Marcus Mathers and Laynie Luck have also moved on, while Veronica Haven departed earlier in the year. That means several names associated with WWE ID have now left while the company continues bringing new wrestlers into the developmental pipeline. House’s situation stands out a little differently because he wasn’t part of WWE ID for very long. He went from taking part in the Orlando tryout in January to signing in March, appearing on WWE EVOLVE as CJ Valor and now being released just months later. WWE ID’s roster continues to change pretty quickly, and House is now the latest name to find himself on the outside. At this point, his next move remains to be seen following the end of his brief run in the program. title: Ilja Dragunov explains exit from WWE for AEW
raw_title: New AEW signee Ilja Dragunov explains why he left WWE
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) New AEW signee Ilja Dragunov has addressed his decision to leave WWE. “It was an accumulation of a lot of things,” Dragunov said on The Ariel Helwani Show. “An accumulation of, of course, the offering, because we all know, at the end of the day, it’s the business. But it’s also definitely based on my feeling of, like, how do I want to work creatively? Do I need a scenery change? Is the scenery change something where I can see myself staying forever? Because you’ve got to consider a lot of factors. “Like, I spent most of my 20s in WWE. That’s a very, very long time. And the landscape in this beautiful business changed. So the beautiful thing is, nowadays we have other opportunities. And for me personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe a place where I see myself more fitting. Who wouldn’t do that?” Check out the show below or via YouTube.com Powell’s POV: It felt like Dragunov went as far as WWE was going to push him. His in-ring style makes him a really good fit in AEW. Dragunov made his AEW debut in a non-wrestling appearance at Saturday’s AEW WrestleDream. His first AEW match is scheduled for Wednesday’s AEW Dynamite. [H/T to F4Wonline.com transcribing the quotes]
summary: New AEW signee Ilja Dragunov cited an accumulation of factors for leaving WWE after spending most of his 20s there. He pointed to the business offering, the desire for a creative scenery change, and the current opportunities available in the industry as reasons to seek a place where he feels he fits better. The landscape of the business has changed since he first joined WWE.

title: Santino Marella Officially Re-Signs With TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Santino Marella Officially Re-Signs With TNA Wrestling
body: Santino Marella is staying in TNA Wrestling. As initially reported by The Johnny I Pro Show , TNA announced today that Santino Marella re-signed with the promotion to stay on board as the Director of Authority. Marella is also a former WWE Superstar, debuting on the roster in April 2007. He remained with the promotion until May 2016, when he was released. During his WWE run, he became a two-time Intercontinental Champion, a United States Champion, and a WWE Tag Team Champion with Vladimir Kozlov. In 2009, he also won the Miss WrestleMania Battle Royal at WrestleMania 25, posing as “Santina Marella.”

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Responds to MJF Trashing His AEW Debut at WrestleDream 2026
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Responds to MJF Trashing His AEW Debut at WrestleDream 2026
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has heard MJF’s shot at his AEW debut, and he’s not exactly rushing to fire back. After MJF mocked his elaborate WrestleDream entrance and called him a “Russian/German loser,” Dragunov made it pretty clear he doesn’t consider MJF’s words important enough to worry about.
body: The interviewer tried to get a little more out of him, but Dragunov wasn’t interested in turning it into some big war of words. As far as he’s concerned, there are more important problems to worry about. “Come on. Like, please. I’m Russian-German. We handle problems of relevance.” MJF started the whole thing after WrestleDream, when he posted his not-so-glowing review of AEW’s latest pay-per-view. Along with ripping AEW World Champion Will Ospreay, MJF took aim at Dragunov’s orchestra-themed presentation. “Russian/german loser debuts by pretending he’s a ‘composer’…cool.” “No — chops and elbows and boots and throws and… come on. Like, I handle problems of relevance.” “And especially in Russian culture, we talk about things with depth, but we do not get hurt by words. If I got hurt more by words, I wouldn’t be sitting here nowadays. So, please, come on.” MJF may have been looking for a reaction when he mocked Dragunov’s WrestleDream debut, but he definitely didn’t get much of one here. Dragunov seems far more interested in throwing chops, elbows, boots and bodies than getting dragged into a social media argument. title: Key Moments Building Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn Story
raw_title: Five Moments That Shaped Roman Reigns And Sami Zayn Before Their Crown Jewel Showdown
body: Zayn aligned with Reigns and The Usos, Jey Uso and Jimmy Uso, in spring 2022. For months, Zayn trailed the faction and took attacks meant for Reigns and The Usos. Solo Sikoa joined The Bloodline at Clash at the Castle in September 2022. On the Sept. 23, 2022, episode of SmackDown, Reigns ordered Zayn to remove a Bloodline shirt. Jey tore the shirt off, and Reigns presented Zayn with a new one reading "Honorary Uce." Zayn put it on, acknowledged Reigns as the Tribal Chief, and the two embraced in the ring. Jey did not look happy with the decision. The Bloodline headlined Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 26, 2022, at TD Garden in Boston. Reigns, Jey, Jimmy, Sikoa, and Zayn faced Kevin Owens, Drew McIntyre, Sheamus, Ridge Holland, and Butch. Jey entered the event suspicious, having overheard Owens urge Zayn to turn on the group. Late in the match , Owens hit Reigns with a Stunner, and Zayn grabbed the referee's arm to stop the count. Zayn followed with a low blow and a Helluva Kick to Owens, a longtime friend. Jey hit a splash and pinned Owens for the win. After the bell, Jey accepted Zayn as a member of The Bloodline. Reigns retained the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship against Owens at the Royal Rumble on Jan. 28, 2023, at the Alamodome in San Antonio. Jimmy, Jey, and Sikoa attacked Owens after the match . Reigns handed a steel chair to Zayn and demanded a shot on Owens. A moment of hesitation drew several slaps. Zayn swung the chair into Reigns instead. Jimmy, Sikoa, and Reigns beat Zayn down. Jey did not take part, left the ring, and walked up the ramp. Zayn's time in The Bloodline was over. Zayn attacked Reigns from behind on the following SmackDown and demanded a title match. Reigns accepted and promised to hurt Zayn in front of family and a home crowd. The bout went to Elimination Chamber on Feb. 18, 2023, at the Bell Centre in Montreal. Jimmy interfered during the match and attacked Zayn. Paul Heyman later produced a steel chair for Reigns, and Jey came to the ring but did not strike Zayn. Zayn charged for a Spear, Reigns moved, and Jey took the hit instead. Reigns struck Zayn with the chair and scored the pin after a Spear to retain. Reigns and The Usos lost a six-man tag team match to Sikoa, Jacob Fatu, and Tama Tonga at Crown Jewel on Nov. 2, 2024, in Riyadh. Zayn ran in during the post-match attack and helped fight off Sikoa's group. Reigns went for a Superman Punch on Sikoa, as Zayn threw a Helluva Kick. Sikoa moved, and the kick hit Reigns. On the Nov. 8 SmackDown, Zayn told Reigns the kick was an accident. Later that night, Sikoa attacked Reigns and waved Zayn into the ring, only to take a kick to the face. Reigns, Zayn, Jey, and Jimmy stood together to close the show. The reunited group added Punk as the fifth member for Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 30, 2024, at Rogers Arena in Vancouver. The team beat Sikoa, Fatu, Tama Tonga, Tonga Loa, and Bronson Reed. Reigns pinned Sikoa after a double superkick from The Usos, a Helluv
summary: Sami Zayn joined The Bloodline alongside Roman Reigns and The Usos in spring 2022, often absorbing punishment for the group. Solo Sikoa arrived in September 2022 at Clash at the Castle, and later that month on SmackDown Reigns had Zayn discard his prior shirt before presenting him with an Honorary Uce one, leading to an embrace while Jey Uso appeared displeased. The faction then competed at Survivor Series WarGames that November in Boston against Kevin Owens, Drew McIntyre, Sheamus, Ridge Holland and Butch, where Zayn prevented a pin on Reigns and attacked Owens before Jey secured the victory and began to accept Zayn.

title: Andrade explains leaving AEW for WWE
raw_title: Andrade opens up about his decision to leave AEW for WWE
summary_src: A few years ago, Andrade El Idolo parted ways with AEW and joined WWE; He has now opened up about that decision. After spending a couple of years in AEW from 2021 to 2023, Andrade parted ways with the promotion and joined WWE.
body: A few years ago, Andrade El Idolo parted ways with AEW and joined WWE; He has now opened up about that decision. After spending a couple of years in AEW from 2021 to 2023, Andrade parted ways with the promotion and joined WWE. The current AEW National Champion recently sat down for an interview with Renee Paquette on AEW’s Close Up , where he explained the decision. The 36-year-old explained that while personally the decision felt good, professionally he was a little sad. “Personally was good, but professionally is a little sad because my contract was expired in this moment. So I need to pick a decision, like I need to go for my personal life because I was married in this moment, or my professional life ,” he shared. “ So I pick my personal life and need to make a decision. But I went with Tony [Khan] and say thank you for the opportunity, the contract expire, and I hope see you in the future. And I need to move for my personal life, or for myself, for a better relation ,” he added. Andrade further claimed that he always had a good relationship with AEW, and after he was done with WWE in 2025, Tony Khan gave him this opportunity. Hoping to pay back Khan with his in-ring work, El Idolo wants to help the promotion. “ I am here to help the company. They want the best for this company. They want the best for me. I want to represent this company very well. This is how I need to pay Tony for this second chance or second opportunity ,” he finished. After returning to AEW in Oct. 2025, El Idolo was soon removed from television after WWE had sent a cease-and-desist letter to AEW, claiming Andrade had violated terms of his contract. Following a lengthy legal battle , the Mexican wrestler officially came back in Jan. 2026. He has been a regular part of the promotion since. title: Drew McIntyre Shares 2006 Talk With PAC
raw_title: Drew McIntyre recalls early-career conversation with PAC
summary_src: Long before PAC and Drew McIntyre became two of the top names in the modern wrestling industry, they had their humble beginnings in the UK’s indie circuit. On Sept. 27, 2026, PAC passed away after he was found dead in his car after AEW All Out 2026.
body: Long before PAC and Drew McIntyre became two of the top names in the modern wrestling industry, they had their humble beginnings in the UK’s indie circuit. On Sept. 27, 2026, PAC passed away after he was found dead in his car after AEW All Out 2026. Recently, speaking on What’s Your Story? With Steph McMahon , McIntyre opened up about an early-career conversation he had with PAC. Reflecting on a conversation he had with the late AEW star in 2006, McIntyre recalled, “ I remember, we mentioned Ben [Benjamin Satterley] PAC. I remember in 2006, 2007 we were doing shows in London, and he was just incredible. Most insane high flyer I’d ever seen, the precision. “ And I’d tell him, ‘You’re going to be the one that makes it big from the UK.’ And he said, ‘No, you’re going to do it.’ And then to watch his journey and how far he came and how much he achieved, it was awesome ,” McIntyre added. The former WWE Champion also opened up about how proud he is of the representation of the British and Scottish people in WWE and the wrestling world. “ And he was complimentary to myself and it was so cool that so many people now from the UK have done so much for the world. Generally it was Americans and Canadians with a couple of Brits sprinkled in maybe here and there, but to see just the worldwide representation of WWE, specifically from the UK and even Scotland, there’s only five million people in Scotland ,” McIntyre added. “ And we’ve had more people than I can count, about eight or nine different superstars, and most of them were girls. Which really, really blew my mind. “ Two decades ago, in 2006, the two faced off against each other at RQW Not Just For Christmas 2006 in London, where PAC defeated Drew McIntyre, aka Drew Galloway, via count-out. title: Ilja Dragunov Explains WWE Exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Talks WWE Departure, Says Their Offer To Retain Him Wasn't 'Satisfying'
summary_src: AEW's newest signee Ilja Dragunov spoke about his WWE departure back in August and said the company's offer to retain him wasn't "satisfying."
body: Ahead of stepping back in the ring on TV for the first time since April, Dragunov appeared on " The Ariel Helwani Show " to discuss his WWE departure. It was revealed that Dragunov's contract expired in August , and the star told Helwani that the story of his departure isn't very exciting. "I love what I do. I want to compete. I want to work," Dragunov said. "It just got a little stuck. But, it's nothing new to anybody. It was pretty obvious. So, the time just passed by and then I reached the expiration of my contract... I felt over time that, 'Okay, with how everything is working out and how I'm feeling, because I make a lot of [decisions] depending on how I feel about it, I've always had the courage to do so, I feel it is time to breathe some new, fresh air.'" The star said that despite things written online at the time, WWE had no intention of letting him go. He said his departure was the accumulation of many things, including what he wanted creatively. Dragunov said he pondered the scenery change, and if it was somewhere if he could see himself staying "forever." "I spent most of my 20s in WWE," he explained. "That's a very, very long time. The landscape in this beautiful business changed... For me, personally, after such a long time being with a company, to not seek out new opportunities, maybe another place more fitting, who wouldn't do that?" AEW/Ricky Havlik Dragunov reiterated that his departure story isn't as exciting as it was made out to be. He said at some points in WWE, you just don't have creative and are waiting for the opportunities to come. He explained that a lot of new people came up toward the end of his time in WWE, and there is only so much time for so many people. When Helwani inquired as to whether or not Dragunov was asked to take a pay cut, like New Level's Kofi and Austin Creed , AEW's newest star stayed mum on the topic. "To be honest, I'm much too discrete and too much of a businessman and a gentleman myself to talk about these kind of things," Dragunov said. "Everything I can say, is there was nothing I felt satisfying, and nothing that gave me the perspective of, 'Okay, I must stick with it [here.]'" "The Mad Dragon" said he's always had faith in himself and he's never been one to question his beliefs. He explained he always follows his gut feelings in life, and it's always worked out for him. The star said that many people want to change, but that change requires courage. "It also requires [dealing] with the possibility that things could not work out your way. I was aware of all these things," he said. "April was the last point in time I was in the ring. The feeling that maybe, 'I'm not right where I am.' I already had it before... It all came down to bet on myself and believe it's going to be alright. That's what I did my entire 14-year-long professional wrestling career."
summary: Ilja Dragunov's WWE contract expired in August. He appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show ahead of his first TV match since April and said the promotion made an offer to keep him that was not satisfying. Dragunov cited creative desires and a need for fresh air after feeling things had gotten stuck.
