body: -Hype for tonight’s show centered around the Montana-Lennox match that’s been promoted quite a bit better than anything that’s going to run at Halloween Havoc. -It’s not often that NXT opens with a talk segment, but Tony D’Angelo showed up first as the show has a lot of work to do to make Halloween Havoc seem like a big deal. He immediately called out Grayson Waller, who obliged by heading to the ring with his own mic. Waller said that back in their beginnings, he knew they’d meet at some point. He said they were signed at about the same time and even teamed together at WarGames. They talked about not liking – and even resenting – each other. Waller said that D’Angelo was chosen and he didn’t even know what any of this was. He said he had to take Tony upstairs and show him what a WarGames match is because he didn’t know. D’Angelo countered by saying Waller was more about viral moments than championships. Waller again took down D’Angelo verbally in response. Waller stayed in a heel context but just ate D’Angelo alive on the mic. Waller said the title means more than when Bron had it (low bar; Breakker had a terrible title run), more than when Trick had it (I wish I could say Trick had a great run, but all his best presentation was when he was chasing and not the champ) and it would be more than anything D ever did. D’Angelo interrupted and yelled out some final threats. This wasn’t a bad segment or anything, but I came away wanting to see Waller destroy D’Angelo for being an interloper in wrestling, which certainly wasn’t the intent. -Earlier today, Layla Diggs was talking to some people in the locker room when Izzi Dame showed up and stirred it up, leading to a match later tonight. -In the parking lot for some reason, Birthright talked big ahead of their next Dusty Cup match. After they headed inside, we could see a truck approaching from a distance. Announcers didn’t mention it, but it seemed like something with implications. But maybe it was just a truck. [c] -Chantel Monroe got a brief pre-taped hype segment. I saw a ton of her on Evolve and the biggest work she had to do was on the mic, which she’s really starting to get down. body: Here's everything we hated and everything we loved from the October 20 edition of "WWE NXT." The problem with the booking here for me doesn't necessarily come in Zilla Fatu being the man to cost BirthRight or El Hijo de. Dr Wagner Jr. and Galeno advanced to the semifinals in the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic. It more so comes from the fact that "NXT" has been positioning BirthRight as a dominant faction on the brand others should be on the lookout for. BirthRight has been talking a big game about wanting to be noticed, only to then immediately lose an important match and be left laid out by Zilla. Not only does it make BirthRight look bad as a stable, but it also makes it really hard to take them as a serious threat both by other wrestlers and as a viewer without giving them credible wins that will help to achieve that means to an end. If "NXT" really wanted to have Zilla cost BirthRight to really get under their skin, then I can't see a reason not to at least have him wait until the semifinals or even the finals to do so and put BirthRight and El Hijo de. Dr Wagner Jr. and Galeno against different opponents in the quarterfinals. At least doing it that way would give BirthRight a little more credibility by getting them further in the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic and gives them that much more fuel in order to advance the ongoing storyline between BirthRight and Zilla by increasing the stakes. WWE "NXT" fans got a taste of Chantel Monroe two weeks ago when she and 19 others competed in a battle royal to determine the number one contender for the NXT Women's Championship. Tonight, we got a second look, courtesy of a 30-second vignette. After watching this vignette, we've now got a good idea of Chantel's character. She's confident (maybe even a little vain), glamorous, and diva-like. As a former Auburn gymnast, we know she's athletic, too. "Open your ears, look at me, and pay attention because the reflection of perfection, Chantel Monroe, is gracing your screen," Chantel said while holding up a handheld mirror. "Can you tell I'm pure entertainment and love attention? So yeah, the NXT women's locker room better watch out, because when the show-stopping diva steps in the ring, it's not just a match, it's an experience." A prop, in her case a mirror, will instantly allow fans to link something tangible to her. In her short introductory video, we also saw that she's wrestled main roster talent Maxxine Dupri on "WWE Main Event," which means she already has decent in-ring experience under her belt. Chantel physically appeared on "NXT" as well, specifically in a backstage segment with Kendal Grey and Wren Sinclair. title: Natalya thanks Nick Khan for outside WWE bookings
raw_title: Natalya credits Nick Khan for giving her opportunities outside WWE
summary_src: A WWE veteran, Natalya recently found herself wrestling for other indie promotions while still being part of the WWE roster. Recently, speaking on The West Sport, Natalya opened up and credited WWE President Nick Khan for allowing her opportunities outside of the promotion.
body: A WWE veteran, Natalya recently found herself wrestling for other indie promotions while still being part of the WWE roster. Recently, speaking on The West Sport , Natalya opened up and credited WWE President Nick Khan for allowing her opportunities outside of the promotion. “ It takes an extraordinary amount of courage to be able to go, I know I’m performing and firing on all cylinders, but I have to leave because I don’t want to be the last girl at the party. “ Natalya claimed for nearly two decades she wrestled in WWE and never got to do anything outside the promotion. However, when her friend, Josh Barnett, wanted her to Bloodsport, she was allowed to do so. “ For me, I’m not going to be around forever. But I’m in the best shape of my life. And I feel like in the last year, especially stepping outside of WWE, Nick Khan has allowed me to work outside of the company in places that really fulfill my soul ,” she said. Natalya claimed that Khan allowed her to do Bloodsport, NWA, Reality of Wrestling, GCW, AAA, and other stuff. “ It just lit my soul. It just set me free. And so I feel like I’m doing amazing work. But I also admire AJ [Styles] and [John] Cena in the way that they beat the house. So you never know. I’m not going to be here forever ,” she finished. Natalya, 44, last wrestled at AAA Triplemania 34 in the AAA Reina de Reinas championship number one Contendership Fatal Four Way bout. title: MLW star Lady Frost Responds To Tessa Blanchard signing: 'It's good for business'
raw_title: MLW star Lady Frost reacts to Tessa Blanchard signing: 'It's good for business' | OutKick
body: Pro wrestling star Tessa Blanchard signed with Major League Wrestling (MLW) earlier this week, bolstering an already stacked women’s division. Lady Frost, who joined MLW earlier this year, reacted to Blanchard’s arrival in an interview with OutKick Dropkick. Lady Frost signed with Major League Wrestling in April 2026. (MLW) "First of all, it’s an incredible signing," she said. "We understand the pedigree that comes with Tessa Blanchard and you’ve heard high tides raise all ships. And I think everyone is just going to want to up their game even more. "I’ve been in the ring with Tessa. I’ve done tours in Mexico and it’s good for business." MLW said Blanchard will make her debut appearance at Fightland on Sept. 12 in Charleston, South Carolina. Tessa Blanchard, who currently competes in CMLL, has signed with MLW. (CMLL) "Heavy is the crown, but legacy isn't handed to you... it’s forged under pressure," she said in a news release. "I’ve earned my place as one of the best in the world at what I do, but I’m not coming to MLW to rest on the Blanchard name. "MLW is bringing some of the purest, hardest-hitting action in the sport today, and the ‘Undeniable Diamond’ belongs right at the top of it." Frost told OutKick Dropkick she wouldn’t rank the MLW women’s division among the rest of the pro wrestling world but agreed the roster is "stacked." "It is stacked. I don't do rankings. That's not my department. I do the fighting," she said. "I get in there and I do my job and it's for the fans to decide. We make it very easy for them. Too easy. "It's $15 to show up to a live event and it's free on YouTube. So, they can make that decision themselves. I know fans have a lot to say about rankings and wrestling and they really have no idea, but you can go ahead and chime in." Lady Frost is set for a matchup against Corinne Joy on Saturday as MLW holds its Kings of Colosseum event. The matches can be seen on YouTube, beIN Sports and Veeps.
summary: Pro wrestling star Tessa Blanchard inked a deal with Major League Wrestling earlier this week, bolstering an already stacked women’s division. Lady Frost, who joined MLW earlier this year, reacted to Blanchard’s arrival in an interview with OutKick Dropkick.

body: Which Superstars with shared finishing maneuvers did it better? And what exactly do we mean by coolest? If you were cool you wouldn’t be asking that question. Pure intensity, pure mayhem, pure Warrior. Whenever Ultimate Warrior’s music hit, all hell would inevitably break loose. But nothing demonstrated the sheer electricity and powerful essence of such a wild Superstar like his Gorilla Press Slam. Putting her own spin on the Gory Neckbreaker — a move innovated by Mexican ring legend Gory Guerrero — Victoria felled many a female in WWE with the chiropractic nightmare she called the Widow’s Peak. In executing the maneuver, the raven-haired aggressor would hoist her opponents back-to-back over her shoulder then drop them savagely to the canvas, twisting their necks backward in a sickening show of force. Incapacitating such iconic Divas as Torrie Wilson, Stacy Keibler and WWE Hall of Famer Trish Stratus, the Widow’s Peak earned Victoria her second Women’s Championship in a Fatal 4-Way Match on the Feb. 23, 2004, edition of Raw, when she used the dreaded maneuver to take out Lita. — JAMES WORTMAN Some wrestling moves are precision holds, designed to stretch opponents’ limbs past their breaking points. Others are about hitting a dude so hard his head might pop off. JBL’s Clothesline from Hell clearly falls into the latter category. The big Texan took a cue from fellow Lone Star State native Stan Hansen, as both men enjoyed recklessly throwing their beefy arms at foes like big league sluggers swinging for the fences. JBL almost always connected, knocking the poor sap across the ring from him into next week. Hell probably sounded like a vacation after getting clobbered by The Wrestling God’s signature clothesline. — BOBBY MELOK If finding a four leaf clover is considered good luck, then finding yourself in Dean Malenko’s Texas Cloverleaf must be just the opposite. Watch Malenko execute the Texas Cloverleaf in an underrated classic It’s a hold that looks awesome as it inflicts pain and certainly spells bad luck for anyone finding themselves locked in it. — TOM LIODICE A close-fisted punch in a WWE match usually garners an admonishment — almost always unheeded — from the referee. However the rule book goes out the window when Roman Reigns lands his breathtaking Superman Punch. A jumping, cross-body right hand delivered with phenomenal impact, the blow is made all the more devastating by the incredible torque generated by The Shield member’s 250-pound frame. title: Was Tito Santana Considered As a Possible Face of WWE? — Ask 411 Wrestling
raw_title: Ask 411 Wrestling: Was Tito Santana Considered As a Possible Face of WWE?
body: I am your party host, Ryan Byers, and I am here to answer some of your burning inquiries about professional wrestling. If you have one of those queries searing a hole in your brain, feel free to send it along to me at [email protected] . Don’t be shy about shooting those over – the more, the merrier. Did the Ultimate Warrior or Randy Savage say anything negative in shoot interviews towards the other? Not that I’m aware of. With Randy Savage passing away in 2011, shoot interviews were definitely “a thing,” but we hadn’t yet made it into the era where wrestlers were dropping new interviews every couple of weeks and we now know what Maven had for breakfast the morning after he eliminated the Undertaker from the Royal Rumble. We have more shoot interviews out there from the Warrior, but none of them that I was able to track down were particularly negative on Savage. In fact, he spoke about the two of them working well together and having a collegial relationship. I’ve heard before that when the WWF decided to give main-event pushes to smaller guys who weren’t obviously on steroids in the early 1990s, Tito Santana was one of the talents they considered as the face of the company, a position that ultimately went to Bret Hart and later Shawn Michaels. You want to know who doesn’t seem to believe that Tito Santana was “in the mix” to become the WWF Champion? In 2022, the man from Mission, Texas sat down with WSI – Wrestling Shoot Interviews and was asked about the longstanding rumors that he was on a shortlist of four names to take the belt off of Ric Flair. Tito denied that he had ever heard about such a list at the time that these events were going down. He went on to say that, after Bret Hart won the championship, he was approached by Pat Patterson backstage with Patterson telling him that the decision for a new champ had come down to him and the Hitman. However, Santana went on to say that, just a couple of hours later, Ted DiBiase came up to him, and DiBiase reported that Pat Patterson had also told him that he was the last guy under consideration before the call was made to go with Hart. In other words, Tito felt like Pat Patterson had been blowing smoke up his ass. I don’t totally deny the notion that Tito Santana’s name may have been mentioned as a potential WWF Champion at one point in time, but given the longstanding history of wrestlers trying to overstate their importance in the pecking order as opposed to understate it, if Santana himself doubts he was ever a serious contender, then he was probably never a serious contender. Given his still-protected status and fans’ memory of him as a popular ethnic babyface during the height of Hulkamania and a former Intercontinental Champion, I don’t think that he would have had a credibility issue at all as WWF Champion in 1992, particularly if they tuned down the new cornball gimmick just a bit. Andrade El Idolo hasn’t lost in an All Elite Wrestling ring since April, quietly building one of the strongest bodies of work in 2026. Since dethroning Mark Davis for the AEW National Championship, Andrade has recorded six title defenses, punctuating his case on Saturday with a victory over Tommaso Ciampa . With the Casino Gauntlet contract in hand, and victories earlier in the year over the likes of Swerve Strickland and Kenny Omega, the world is Andrade’s oyster. Right now, he’s treading water, biding his time until his long-awaited clash with Roman Reigns at next year’s “WrestleMania.” Still, it feels like he has more momentum than any wrestler in the world. The highlights of his 2026 campaign include winning the King of the Ring Tournament and retiring Brock Lesnar in Hell in a Cell. Persephone’s case is two-fold: (1) her impressive record and (2) her status as CMLL’s top women’s champion. As TBS Champion, she’s staged four successful title defenses, including last Saturday’s four-way dance with Dani Luna, Queen Aminata, and Hyan. A day later, she put her CMLL World Women’s Championship on the line, conquering AZM in Arena Mexico. Roman Reigns has only wrestled seven times in 2026. Still, it’s difficult to deny the “Tribal Chief’s” strength of schedule. With notable victories over CM Punk, Seth Rollins, and Penta; Reigns has cultivated an aura of inviolability. title: RVD Speaks On Possibility of Another AEW Run
raw_title: RVD Addresses Possibility of Another AEW Run
summary_src: RVD still thinks he has another wrestling run left in him, and AEW sounds like a pretty good place to make it happen. The WWE Hall of Famer believes he could have a “really good run” there and already has a few familiar names he’d be interested in getting back in the ring with. Speaking ...
body: “Yeah. They’ve definitely proven themselves. You know, like, it was so easy when they first came out to be like, ‘Yeah, well, let’s see how long they stick around.’ And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with any of us that felt that way because promotions over the years come up all the time.” RVD said AEW has clearly managed to fill a void in wrestling and believes the company will continue growing. He also noted that plenty of fans he speaks with aren’t necessarily picking one company over another and instead watch both AEW and WWE. “‘Oh, they got Major League Baseball money. This shit’s for real,’ and they got this and that, and it never lasts. And those guys, you know, really fill the void, and so it’s cool. Congrats to AEW, and they’re just going to keep growing. You know, I always check with the fans and ask what they watch, and a lot of people are watching both products. I don’t know how much international distribution they have, but obviously they must be on in the places that they’re going to, at least.” There’s also something about AEW’s environment that stands out to RVD. From his perspective, the company feels more wrestler-driven and gives talent more room to express themselves than what he remembers from his time in WWE. “But yeah, pretty cool. And it still — and I think always will — be coming across as, and I think for valid reasons, the boys being the ones that are kind of running the show more.” RVD contrasted that with his WWE experience, where he felt some wrestlers were worried about their jobs and hesitant to push back. AEW, in his eyes, comes across as a place where wrestlers have more freedom to do things their own way. “You know, whereas WWE was like a lot of people afraid for their job and doing whatever they’re told, and sometimes afraid to go against it or say the wrong thing or whatever. And this seems more like guys that want to be out there expressing themselves with their talent and doing it their way.” That’s when RVD started thinking about what another AEW run could actually look like. Rather than immediately naming some of the company’s younger stars, he pointed toward several veterans with whom he already shares plenty of history. RVD then threw one more name into the conversation — Jeff Hardy. The two have plenty of history together, and Van Dam wouldn’t mind getting one more match with his former rival. “And I also think I wouldn’t mind having one more match with Jeff Hardy, you know?” None of this means RVD is actively pushing Tony Khan to book those matches. He made it clear that Jericho, Christian Cage, Adam Copeland and Hardy are simply ideas he likes rather than matches he’s desperate to make happen. “But these aren’t things that I, you know, dream about and, ‘Oh, I gotta make it happen.’ It just sounds like good ideas, you know?” H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

title: Dragon Lee Re-Signs With WWE
raw_title: Dragon Lee Re-Signs With WWE
summary_src: Dragon Lee isn’t going anywhere after all. After weeks of questions about his expiring WWE contract, the luchador has reportedly worked things out with the company — and he could be sticking around for another five years. According to PWInsider, WWE and Lee have come to terms on a new contract.
body: There had been some reason for fans to wonder what Lee might do next. His brother Dralistico is also nearing the end of his AEW deal, and the two recently filed a trademark for “Hermanos Lee,” which naturally got people wondering whether something involving the brothers could be coming. That wasn’t just a guess either. The indication he received was that people inside WWE weren’t expecting Lee to start looking around once his deal was up. “I was given the indication that, like, people don’t anticipate Dragon Lee looking to leave WWE.” Now it looks like they had good reason to feel that way. Lee originally signed with WWE in December 2022 on a three-year deal before getting a one-year extension in 2023 after making his way onto the main roster. He’s also spent a good chunk of 2026 chasing the Intercontinental Championship. Lee has challenged for the title four times this year, including another unsuccessful shot on the October 19 episode of Monday Night RAW. So after all the questions about whether Dragon Lee might hit free agency, WWE appears to have taken that possibility right off the table. If the reported five-year term checks out, Lee won’t just be staying — WWE has apparently locked him down for the long haul. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up On Why He Was Able to Keep His Name After WWE Exit
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals Why He Was Able to Keep His Name After WWE Exit
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov didn’t have to leave his identity behind when he walked out of WWE. Unlike plenty of wrestlers who have been forced to rebrand after leaving the company, Dragunov was able to take his name straight to AEW with him.
body: Dragunov explained that he’d already spent his entire independent career wrestling under that name. When WWE signed him, the company didn’t ask him to change it or come up with a new identity. “They never asked me to change it. I had this name before. I had this name for my entire independent career. I came to WWE with this name, and I left WWE with this name.” That also meant Dragunov didn’t suddenly find himself searching for a new name once his WWE run was over. He confirmed that he kept the rights to Ilja Dragunov, something he’s especially happy about considering how closely the name is tied to everything he’s accomplished in wrestling. “So, there was never a point where they asked me to change the name or anything like that. So, I kept the rights for this name, and I’m very happy about that because, I mean, this name is connected to my entire career.” For Dragunov, there really wasn’t an alternative identity sitting around anyway. From the independents to NXT UK, NXT, WWE’s main roster and now AEW, he’s always been Ilja Dragunov. That made at least one part of Dragunov’s jump from WWE to AEW incredibly simple. He may be starting a completely new chapter of his career, but fans won’t have to get used to calling him anything different. title: WWE Writers Were Allegedly Expected to Take the Blame for Vince McMahon’s Decisions
raw_title: WWE Writers Were Allegedly Expected to Take the Blame for Vince McMahon’s Decisions
summary_src: Jimmy Jacobs says wrestling fans have spent years blaming WWE’s creative writers for decisions they were never actually in charge of. According to the former WWE writer, when Vince McMahon didn’t want someone on television, the creative team often ended up taking the heat for it anyway.
body: Speaking to Till Five Wrestling , Jacobs explained that there’s a major difference between being a writer and actually being the person running creative. He described WWE’s writers as advisers who could bring ideas to the table but couldn’t force the person at the top to use them. “There is such a misconception about what the job of creative is. Writers aren’t the head of creative. That’s one thing, but the writers are a different thing. The writers aren’t shot-callers. They’re advisers to the king. That’s what they are.” Jacobs said that distinction wasn’t just lost on fans either. In his experience, plenty of wrestlers and veteran personalities also talked about WWE creative without really understanding what happened behind the scenes. “And for some reason, nobody — none of the fans — understands this. A bunch of the wrestlers don’t understand this. A bunch of the old marks. Like, who’s that guy with the plug up his butt? Rip Rogers. Is that his name? Rip Rogers.” Jacobs specifically remembered seeing Rip Rogers pitch an idea involving Brock Lesnar on social media while he was working on WWE’s creative team. Whatever Rogers suggested immediately told Jacobs that he didn’t understand how WWE’s creative system actually operated. “I remember being on the creative team and him tweeting something about Brock Lesnar should do something, something, something that let me know, ‘Oh, this old guy has no idea how this works. He has no idea how this works.’” That frustration extended to fans who listened to former wrestlers discuss the business and then assumed they understood WWE’s internal creative process. Jacobs argued that unless someone had actually worked on that side of the company, they couldn’t really know how those decisions were being made. You want to know what the creative process is? If you’re on the side of the creative process, you know what the creative process is. If you’ve never been on that side, you don’t know what it is.” What really surprised Jacobs was discovering that even some WWE talent didn’t completely understand the system. After spending a few months inside the company, he realized wrestlers themselves sometimes didn’t know exactly where their creative decisions were coming from. “I was shocked. I was actually shocked going into WWE. Once I got there for a few months, I was like, ‘Oh, the wrestlers don’t know what the creative process is. They don’t know what it is.’” “Like when these people, man, some of these people that talk about this stuff, it’s like, ‘Oh, you know, creative has nothing for him. Well, then creative should be fired if they have nothing for him.’” Jacobs then spelled out what he says was actually happening whenever wrestlers heard that line. With McMahon holding final creative authority, Jacobs said it ultimately meant the boss simply didn’t want that wrestler on his show. “It’s like, yo, let me smarten you up. title: On the Record: Details begin to emerge in death of All Elite Wrestling star Pac
raw_title: Details begin to emerge in death of All Elite Wrestling star Pac
body: Benjamin Satterley, the pro wrestling star known as Pac, was found dead in Illinois on Sunday hours after he had wrestled for the All Elite Wrestling (AEW) National Championship at All Out. The Des Plaines Police Department told OutKick Dropkick there were no indications of foul play and the circumstances around Satterley’s death were not deemed to be suspicious. Police said the cause of death would be determined by the Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office. AEW announced Satterley’s death late Sunday, sending shock and disbelief across the pro wrestling world. "All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac," the company said. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. "Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley’s family, friends and fans." AEW owner Tony Khan also paid tribute to Satterley in a separate post. "Benjamin Satterley defined excellence, as a beloved husband & friend to his many loved ones, + in his wrestling knowledge, skill, unprecedented athleticism, professionalism, consistency + dedication to the sport that he loved & traveled the world to pursue," he wrote on X. "May Ben rest in peace." Satterley was found "passed out" outside of a CAVA restaurant at around 4 p.m. local time, the California Post reported, citing 911 audio. An official who arrived on the scene reportedly said Satterley was dead on arrival. Satterley, 40, was one of the first wrestlers to sign with All Elite Wrestling in 2019. He was a two-time trios champion and the inaugural all-Atlantic champion. Before wrestling in AEW , he was with WWE and known as Adrian Neville. Satterley was a two-time cruiserweight champion, an NXT champion and two-time NXT tag team champion. WWE Chief Content Officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque added to the chorus of tributes.

title: Ilja Dragunov reflects on Lesnar Rumble moment
raw_title: Ex-WWE star Ilja Dragunov has no regrets about infamous Brock Lesnar moment
body: Almost everyone remembers Brock Lesnar no-selling Ilja Dragunov at the 2026 WWE Royal Rumble , and the released Superstar has talked about it extensively. "My best career moments were made by my vulnerability. I wasn't becoming a name by being the person who dominates at all times. I became a name on moments where I got beaten down badly," he continued. At one point in the Royal Rumble , Lesnar was backed into a corner by Dragunov. The former United States Champion delivered several chops to the "Beast Incarnate's" chest. However, he was not fazed whatsoever. Lesnar screamed in Dragunov's face before tossing him over the top rope, eliminating him with ease. This ended Dragunov's 11-minute run in the battle royal. The "Beast Incarnate" would be eliminated a few moments later by Cody Rhodes and LA Knight.
summary: Former WWE star Ilja Dragunov discussed the memorable 2026 Royal Rumble segment where Brock Lesnar no-sold his chops and quickly eliminated him. Dragunov said his best career moments came from showing vulnerability rather than constant dominance. Lesnar tossed him out after an 11-minute stay while the Beast Incarnate was later eliminated by Cody Rhodes and LA Knight.

summary_src: AEW performer Jeff Jarrett recently discussed the comedy spot from the Tommaso Ciampa vs Andrade match at WrestleDream this past weekend. body: “I mean, funny, don’t draw money is such a situational [concept]. I just don’t think you can paint it as…look, creative is subjective. Did you hear the reaction? They [the crowd] loved it. title: Zaria Offers NXT Title Match, Izzi Dame Turns It Down
raw_title: WWE Star Rejects Championship Opportunity at NXT Halloween Havoc
body: The confrontation took place during the October 20 episode of WWE NXT . Zaria confronted Dame after her victory over Layla Diggs. After weeks of mind games and attempts to expose the champion's past, Dame finally got the reaction she wanted. However, Zaria offered her a championship match, which Dame surprisingly turned down. After Dame defeated Layla Diggs, Zaria came to the ring to confront her. The champion questioned what Dame was trying to prove and stated that she was tired of the mind games. Zaria also pointed out that Izzi Dame could have earned a shot at the NXT Women's North American Championship in other ways. However, she decided to end their back-and-forth by offering Dame a title match at Halloween Havoc on Saturday, October 31. Dame gave Zaria a thumbs-up before taking the microphone and accepting the match. However, she then surprised the champion by turning down the title opportunity. "Don't worry about putting that little title on the line. See you at Halloween Havoc, Princess," Dame told Zaria before leaving the ring. Calling Zaria "princess" was her one final taunt before they face off at the upcoming event. For Zaria, the upcoming match is a chance to silence Dame and put an end to the mind games without worrying about defending her championship. The post WWE Star Rejects Championship Opportunity at NXT Halloween Havoc appeared first on Wrestlezone .

After weeks of mind games from Dame, Zaria offered her a shot at the NXT Women's North American Championship for Halloween Havoc. Dame initially appeared to accept before rejecting the title opportunity and promising to see Zaria on October 31.

title: AJ Francis Praises Carlos Silva's TNA Leadership
raw_title: Former WWE star says Carlos Silva recognizes his value amid two-year TNA championship absence
summary_src: AJ Francis praised Carlos Silva’s leadership capabilities in TNA while expressing he knows his value and contributions to the promotion. Speaking with Justin Dhillon of The Wrestling Classic, Francis discussed the change in TNA’s leadership style with Silva at the helm.
body: AJ Francis praised Carlos Silva’s leadership capabilities in TNA while expressing he knows his value and contributions to the promotion. Speaking with Justin Dhillon of The Wrestling Classic, Francis discussed the change in TNA’s leadership style with Silva at the helm. He also touched on not being a champion in the promotion for nearly two years, noting Silva has recognized the situation unlike others in leadership positions. “His leadership style is more so of real sports. He doesn’t ignore what’s right in front of his face. It’s a damn shame that it’s been two years since I’ve been a champion in TNA. And Carlos recognizes that. The old wrestling leadership style would be like, ‘Well, he’s still got a lot to prove, but let’s put a title on this guy who’s been here six months who nobody gives a sh*t about.’ Like that’s the old wrestling style. And Carlos recognizes what’s in front of his face.” Francis explained the difference between the former TNA management’s approach and current leadership under Silva. He praised the TNA President’s modern outlook on wrestling and credited him for securing the promotion’s TV deal with AMC . “That’s huge, right? And so to have someone like that at the helm that I can, I mean I talked to him today, he’s my favorite boss I ever worked for and I think that having him at the helm has been such a big help, such an improvement.” Francis debuted on TNA Wrestling in 2024 and shortly after won the Digital Media Championship. He has expressed interest in pursuing the TNA World Championship. Rosanne previously contributed to Sportskeeda as an Assistant Content Manager. When not consumed by wrestling, Rosanne is a musician and an aspiring artist.

Francis noted it has been nearly two years since he last held a championship in the promotion and said Silva recognizes that fact unlike previous regimes. He contrasted Silva's approach with the old wrestling style of ignoring established performers in favor of pushing newer ones.

body: According to California Post's Edward Lewis, Satterley was found "passed out" in a vehicle in a CAVA restaurant parking lot at 4 p.m. on Sunday before being pronounced dead in Des Plaines, IL. When a medical dispatch team arrived at the Mediterranean-themed restaurant, they couldn't confirm if he was breathing, the report added. "This is going to be a slumper," authorities said in the audio. "We can't confirm breathing at this time." "This is going to be a slumper in a car. We cannot confirm breathing yet. At this point, we're still on the phone getting further," added the authorities. Witnesses at CAVA called 911 when they noticed PAC unconscious, even searching for medical equipment to help the wrestler until medics arrived. "There was an ambulance, police and a fire truck, all outside," a witness told The Post. A spokesperson for the Des Plaines Police Department ruled out foul play in the veteran wrestler's death, telling The Post that there were "no indications of foul play and the circumstances surrounding the death are not considered suspicious." A cause of death is pending "additional testing" following an initial autopsy, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner's office. Notably, the CAVA restaurant is located near Chicago O'Hare International Airport, suggesting PAC was preparing for a flight later in the evening. He and his fellow wrestlers had competed the previous night at AEW's All Out pay-per-view at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. AEW Stars Pay Tribute to PAC as Fans Speculate on Cause of Death AEW will honor the life and legacy of PAC during Wednesday's "AEW Dynamite," the company's CEO Tony Khan announced on Monday. "I've never met a person who was more beloved by his peers and his friends," Khan said during an ROH taping after a 10-bell salute was held in honor of PAC. "And it was such a pleasure to spend time with Ben outside of wrestling as well, whether it was just having dinner or watching the football match or traveling. "Ben is a very first-class person, and he left behind a lovely wife and a lot of great friends and a legacy that will last forever," added Khan, via F4WOnline. Khan highlighted that the tribute show will be held at the Petersen Events Center in Pittsburgh, the same venue where PAC wrestled in the main event of the fourth-ever episode of "Dynamite" in 2019 against Jon Moxley. "He's somebody I knew would be a big part of the company and somebody that outside of wrestling also became a big part of my life, just like for the wrestlers in the back and so many people around wrestling — Ben has been a huge part of their lives," Khan said. PAC was a part of the original AEW roster in 2019 after spending seven years in WWE. Wrestlers from both promotions have poured in their tributes since his tragic passing. The post PAC Cause of Death: New Details Emerge About Ex-WWE, AEW Star appeared first on HEAVY .
summary: A spokesperson for the Des Plaines Police Department ruled out foul play in the veteran wrestler's death. PAC was a part of the original AEW roster in 2019 after spending seven years in WWE.

title: Christopher Daniels Saw Greatness In AJ Styles From First Match
raw_title: Christopher Daniels Says That He Could Tell The Day That He First Wrestled AJ Styles That He Was Going To Be Special
summary_src: Christopher Daniels discusses the early days of his rivalry with AJ Styles, noting that he knew he was going to be special then. Daniels' and Styles' careers have been linked throughout their time as in ring competitors, with both men now being retired from full time in ring competition.
body: Christopher Daniels discusses the early days of his rivalry with AJ Styles, noting that he knew he was going to be special then. While speaking to Going Ringside in a new interview , Christopher Daniels was asked for good AJ Styles stories. “All good AJ Styles stories, man. Every time I got to wrestle him was a pleasure. I wrestled him all around the world. I tagged with him all around the world.” Daniels continued, noting that he saw greatness in AJ early on in his career. “I saw greatness in him early on. Before TNA was a thing, I got to wrestle him at the NWA tournament, 53rd anniversary show. That was the first time I ever wrestled him. You could tell that day that he was going to be something special. Once TNA started, he was there from the very beginning, and he became world champion almost within the first year, and I feel like that was the beginning of a career that’s Hall of Fame worthy.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Christopher Daniels told Going Ringside that the first time he faced AJ Styles was at the NWA 53rd anniversary tournament before TNA existed. Daniels said he could tell that day Styles was going to be something special. Once TNA launched, Styles was there from the start, won the world title within his first year, and went on to a career Daniels considers Hall of Fame worthy.

title: WWE couple become parents; announce the birth of their child
raw_title: WWE couple become parents; announce the birth of their child
body: A popular WWE couple has now become parents again. Former WWE Superstar Sarah Logan, aka Valhalla , is now the mother of another child. Married to WWE Superstar and former AAA Tag Team Champion Erik, the two parents recently welcomed their new child to the world. The War Raiders member recently shared the happy news and the family member addition on social media, marking another special milestone for the couple outside the wrestling ring and career. Erik, also known as Raymond Rowe, announced the birth of their third child on Instagram on Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026. They also shared an update on how the mother and newborn are doing following the birth. "Dena Elizabeth Rowe. Born at 2:13 PM on 10/20/26. 9lbs and 21in long. Both mama and baby are healthy and safe. God's gifts are truly endless," Erik wrote on Instagram, while also sharing a close-up, heartwarming picture of their family. Apart from their time together outside of WWE , Erik and Sarah also maintained a close bond during their time together within the promotion. While Erik teamed up with Ivar as part of The War Raiders, Logan performed as their support, Valhalla.
summary: A popular WWE couple has now become parents again. Married to WWE Superstar and former AAA Tag Team Champion Erik, the two parents recently welcomed their new child to the world.

In 2023, Ace Austin and Chris Bey won the IW World Tag Team Titles and Maya Yukihi, Mayumi Ozaki, and Suwama won the AJPW Television 6-Man Tag Team Titles. title: The Bloodline Will Destroy 946 at Survivor Series
raw_title: Don't Be Fooled, The Bloodline Will Destroy 946 at WWE Survivor Series
body: NXT Results & Grades 🔠 Bleacher Report 10h Breakker, Dragunov, More Rumors 👂 Bleacher Report 20h Full Grades from Latest Raw Bleacher Report 21h Keys and Co. have been spectacular. They have grabbed the ball and run with it, oftentimes resulting in the best segment of any WWE Raw episode. They have been menacing, physical, and violent when necessary, and have presented a front against The Bloodline that fans can buy into as being legitimate. Keys looks the part of a dominant big man who can stand across the ring from Roman Reigns and throw fists. Nima and Prince may be inexperienced, but they have held up their end of the bargain. Hayes is almost too good to be involved as just another face in a faction, but it has helped lift him out of the creative abyss he found himself in and relocated him to the main event. Then there is Parker, whose on-screen aura is that of a star. She may be the biggest name of the bunch when all is said and done. No, the 946 will be destroyed at Survivor Series because that is the nature of things in WWE. The group has been heated up and introduced to the masses with the sole purpose of ultimately putting the Bloodline over in a high-profile match. No match is more significant to feuding factions than War Games. As if there were not already a perceived hierarchy difference between the two groups, the Bloodline is led by the biggest star in the company, Reigns. The same Reigns who has dominated WWE as the Tribal Chief for the last five years. He rarely loses big matches and is in the midst of his greatest run to date, one that has seen him deliver consistent Match of the Year candidates in his World Heavyweight Championship defenses. With him on what appears to be a collision course with Oba Femi for WrestleMania 43, upper management in the company is going to look to keep Reigns as strong as possible, and that is unlikely to include a War Games loss to a 946 faction that does not currently have clear direction even beyond its feud with Reigns and Co. Add to that a storyline that sets up for at least one big return in the form of former Women's World Champion Naomi, who can confront and take out Parker, and you have a scenario that sets up for the Bloodline to stand tall. The only saving grace for the 946 could be the role of Jacob Fatu. The Samoan Werewolf was run over by Parker in her main roster debut and while that would seemingly lead to him returning and siding with his cousins, there is history with Keys that could lead him to side with the heels. Especially considering his role in the Bloodline was against his will and the result of a loss to Reigns. Barring some major storyline swerve or the decision to add LA Knight to the 946 team at Survivor Series and get his win back from Money in the Bank, Reigns, The Usos, and Solo Sikoa will pick up the win at Survivor Series. summary: Keys and Company have impressed on Raw with menacing and physical performances that fans can believe as a legitimate threat to The Bloodline. Nima, Prince, Hayes and Parker have all elevated their roles in the faction, with Parker especially standing out as a potential future star. The group will be destroyed by The Bloodline at Survivor Series as is typical for such storylines in WWE.

summary_src: Karl Anderson says Seth Rollins once got a planned WWE loss changed after taking the issue directly to Vince McMahon. The Good Brothers were apparently supposed to pin Rollins while he was World Heavyweight Champion, but by the time Rollins returned from speaking with Vince, that finish was gone.
body: Speaking on the latest episode of Talk’n Shop , Anderson and Luke Gallows were discussing one of the biggest differences they noticed between working in WWE and promotions such as NJPW. Anderson said that in Japan, the booker’s decision was generally the decision, since everyone understood they were performing a show with predetermined winners and losers. “And also, you know, in Japan, at least with New Japan Pro Wrestling, and we’ve seen it with Pro Wrestling NOAH again, why it shocked me so much when we went to WWE — the direction from the booker, because this is all a work, right? And who writes the f****** show tells you who’s going to win. It shouldn’t be a f******— it wasn’t like the time when we were supposed to pin Seth Rollins.” Gallows jumped in with a comparison to an actor objecting to something written into a movie. That opened the door for Anderson to explain exactly what he remembered happening with Rollins. “It’s like if Tom Cruise doesn’t want to get hurt in the movie.” Before getting into the story, Anderson made sure there was no confusion about his relationship with Rollins. Both he and Gallows stressed that they’re friends with the former World Heavyweight Champion and weren’t trying to bury him. According to Anderson, WWE’s original direction was pretty straightforward: The Good Brothers were supposed to pin Rollins despite him being World Heavyweight Champion at the time. Even Anderson and Gallows were somewhat surprised by the call, but they were prepared to go along with it. “The direction was Good Brothers pin Rollins. He was the World Heavyweight Champion. Even we were like, ‘All right, whatever.’ And Rollins goes, ‘Really?’ And then he talked to the guy a little bit. He goes, ‘I don’t know. Let me just go talk to Vince. Maybe they’ll figure it out.’” That’s apparently when everything changed. Anderson claimed Rollins went to speak with Vince McMahon and returned with a different finish, one that instead had Rollins pinning Anderson before The Good Brothers attacked him afterwards. “He comes back, and it changed where Rollins rolled me up, and then we beat him down after.” Anderson isn’t pretending that one finish would have completely changed The Good Brothers’ WWE careers. Still, he admitted that pinning the reigning World Heavyweight Champion certainly could have helped them at the time. “It doesn’t matter. It does. And again, in the grand scheme of things, no one even remembers what I’m even talking about now. If we would’ve pinned the World Heavyweight Champion, maybe that would’ve helped us. I don’t know, you know?” “But again, this is where it takes me to the WWE thing that threw me off. How did the whole — this is where the writers confuse me. title: Latest On Criminal Case Against El Grande Americano, Wwe's Marcel Barthel
raw_title: LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin LATEST ON CRIMINAL CASE AGAINST EL GRANDE AMERICANO, WWE'S MARCEL BARTHEL By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-19 18:04:00 There was a hearing earlier today in Orlando, Florida related to the misdemeanor battery charge against WWE star Marcel Barthel aka Ludwig Kaiser aka El Grande Americano before the County Court of the Ninth Judicial Circuit, in and for Orange County, Florida. The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune from criminal prosecution under Florida law. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing. At the end of the hearing, Barthel's motion to dismiss was denied with a new pre-trial hearing set for 12/17. Barthel was arrested in May on charges of battery, pleading not guilty after learning of a warrant for his arrest on charges of battery and traveling from Mexico to Florida to turn himself in to authorities. A arrest affidavit stated that Orlando Police responded to an apartment complex (we are not publishing the address) at approximately 6:37 PM on 4/23 following reports of a physical altercation on the 12th floor of the building. The complainant, identified as Richard Reap, told officers that he entered an elevator around 6:30 PM and encountered Barthel alongside an unidentified woman. Reap alleged that the pair were acting in what he described as an “uncontrollably intimate” manner while inside the elevator. Reap stated that after exiting onto the 12th floor, he told the couple to “please have some manners.” According to the affidavit, Reap alleged that Barthel immediately responded by punching him multiple times, pushing him to the ground, and threatening additional violence. Barthel's attorney, in the motion to dismiss, argued that he used only non-deadly force, was lawfully present in the common area of his apartment complex, and reasonably believed his actions were necessary to protect both himself and his girlfriend from imminent unlawful force. The motion emphasizes that Florida law does not require a person in those circumstances to retreat before defending themselves. The filing cites Florida's Stand Your Ground statutes, arguing that Barthel has established a "prima facie" claim of self-defense. Under the cited law, the defense contends the burden now shifts to the State to prove by clear and convincing evidence that Barthel was not entitled to statutory immunity. Since his arrest, Barthel's attorneys filed a motion to secure the video footage from the elevator, which one would think would prove what took place during the incident.
summary: The hearing was regarding Barthel's motion to dismiss, where Barthel argued for a dismissal on the grounds that Barthel's use of force was legally justified and that he was immune. Both Barthel and Richard Reap, who filed the charges against him testified at the hearing.

title: Christopher Daniels Urges Fans to Support All Wrestling
raw_title: Christopher Daniels On Tribalism In Wrestling: If You're A Professional Wrestling Fan, I Think You Should Support All Pro Wrestling
summary_src: Christopher Daniels discusses tribalism in professional wrestling, noting that he thinks fans should support all pro wrestling.
body: Christopher Daniels discusses tribalism in professional wrestling, noting that he thinks fans should support all pro wrestling. Tribalism in professional wrestling has grown over the last few years, as many fans have taken sides of the ‘AEW vs WWE war’, with heavy criticism being levied by both sides at the other company. While speaking to Going Ringside in a new interview , Christopher Daniels was asked about tribalism, noting his belief that professional wrestling fans should support all pro wrestling. “If you’re a professional wrestler, professional wrestling fan, I think you should support all professional wrestling, and, WWE is, they’re the the oldest game in the in the game, they’re the oldest group in the game. But AEW is coming along strong. AEW is great, and hopefully if you like professional wrestling, AEW presents tremendous professional wrestling week in and week out. So if you’re against that, I don’t know what to tell you. Go watch something else. That’s fine. But we’ve got plenty of fans, and we’re making more fans along the way. And I look forward to showing them professional wrestling each and every week.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Christopher Daniels shared his thoughts on wrestling tribalism during an interview with Going Ringside. The AEW performer said that if you're a professional wrestling fan you should support all pro wrestling, praising both AEW and WWE for what they bring to the industry. Daniels added that AEW delivers strong weekly shows, is gaining more fans, and those who dislike it can simply watch something else.

Tribalism has increased in recent years with many fans dividing themselves along the lines of an AEW versus WWE rivalry. This has led to significant criticism directed at each company from supporters of the other.

In a recent interview, Daniels expressed that anyone who is a professional wrestler or a fan of professional wrestling ought to back the entire industry. He highlighted WWE as the longest established promotion in the business.

According to Daniels, AEW has a substantial fan base and continues to attract new supporters. He looks forward to presenting professional wrestling to them each week.

title: The Dogs Opens Up On NSFW Name They Originally Wanted to Use in AEW
raw_title: The Dogs Reveal NSFW Name They Originally Wanted to Use in AEW
summary_src: David Finlay and Clark Connors almost had a very different name when they arrived in AEW. Before settling on simply “The Dogs,” the former War Dogs members wanted to call themselves the “Raw Dogs” — but WWE’s Monday Night Raw apparently made that a little difficult.
body: “Yeah. Too many. Too many. I was the, like, the fifth leader, which is like four too many. So, you know, but the merch was good. So, we were like, ‘Yeah, let’s run with it.’” Finlay described what they eventually did as something of a hostile takeover. They got what they could out of the Bullet Club name before eventually moving on. Things changed once Finlay and Connors made their way to AEW. That’s when they revealed that “The Dogs” actually wasn’t their first choice for a team name. “Well, when we came over here, we just became The Dogs, but we really wanted to pitch the name Raw Dogs. But I think there’s an issue with that whole Monday Night thing.” The obvious reference was WWE’s Monday Night Raw , and Finlay and Connors didn’t suggest they were particularly heartbroken about having to find another option. Still, they definitely liked the way “Raw Dogs” sounded. “But it sounds cool because we’re raw f****** dogs, you know?” That’s how they ultimately landed on the much simpler “The Dogs.” They also like the fact that, despite how obvious the name might sound, it hasn’t really been associated with another major wrestling team before them. “But The Dogs also is a sick name. It’s just no one’s ever done it before. No one’s been The Dogs.” Schiavone agreed that the name could work, especially once AEW keeps using it and viewers become accustomed to hearing Finlay and Connors referred to that way. For him, it’s the kind of name that should become more natural over time. “Yeah. You know, I mean, the more you say it, the more you use it, the more everybody gets used to it, and the more it becomes part of the vernacular of AEW.” Connors couldn’t really argue with that logic. Now that “The Dogs” is what they’re going with, he agreed that repetition should help make the name stick. So “The Dogs” may not have been Finlay and Connors’ original plan, but it looks like it’s here to stay. “Raw Dogs” apparently ran into a pretty obvious wrestling problem before it ever had the chance to make it onto AEW television. TNA Wrestling announced a very special night at the Dothan Civic Center on Tuesday, October 13, to mark the start of the 35 th year of Jeff and Matt Hardy as professional wrestlers. The wrestling legends, aka, The GOATs, have been given full creative control of that night’s show, which will air October 15, as Thursday Night iMPACT! on AMC, per TNA Director of Authority Santino Marella. Every element of the October 13 th show in Dothan will be orchestrated from the minds of Jeff & Matt. They are the matchmakers, will set the surprises and match stipulations, and of course play a huge role themselves in-ring during the evening. The October 13 th TNA show in Dothan will air Thursday, October 15 on AMC. To celebrate this special anniversary night, every fan in attendance is encouraged to dress like Jeff or Matt from any era of their historic careers. The two best-dressed fans – one as Matt, one as Jeff – will be crowned the winners and be the first in line for the post-show meet and greet with the real Hardys. A special commemorative photo – of The Hardys and The Hardy Look-Alikes – will be taken and featured on TNA’s social media outlets and the TNA website. Special Hardy merchandise will be available exclusively at the Dothan shows to honor the Hardys’ 35 th year. The Hardys have held countless championships during their illustrious careers, which began on October 15, 1992, in North Carolina. They are recognised by fans, peers and media as the greatest tag team in professional wrestling history and are the only duo to have held the WWE/World, WCW, TNA, ROH, Raw and SmackDown Tag Team Championships. title: Comeback Watch: Taylor Wilde Was Supposed To Win Knockouts World Title During TNA/IMPACT Comeback Run
raw_title: Taylor Wilde Was Supposed To Win Knockouts World Title During TNA/IMPACT Comeback Run
body: It was in 2021 that former TNA Knockouts Champion Taylor Wilde returned to then-IMPACT Wrestling. She had been away from wrestling since 2011. Purrazzo shared that without Scott D’Amore being aware, Lucha Libre AAA threw her into a title-versus-title bout that she would be winning and went on to become Reina de Reinas Champion. Purrazzo said the match against Wilde was supposed to happen at Slammiversary that year. At the 2021 Slammiversary, Purrazzo had a mystery opponent, and it was revealed to be Thunder Rosa. Wilde had no clue about any of these plans. Purrazzo: “I remember — I don’t even know if we’ve talked about this beforehand. You were coming back and you were challenging me and I was also going to Mexico for AAA, and Mexico had sprung on me that it was gonna be the Reina de Reinas Title versus the Knockouts Championship and winner-take-all, and Scott (D’Amore) didn’t know that. So we’re working towards a program, me and you at Slammiversary, where you are going to become the Knockouts Champion and now AAA has put this stipulation on a match that no one agreed to, and I remember being like — to the writers — ‘Hey, I’m so happy to go to AAA and do this match but if you want Shantelle to win, by all means. She can go to Mexico and have that match.’ I don’t want to say I have to be the champion for this, because it threw a wrench in everyone’s plans and so, not to say that about myself as like, I’m such a good person but I think it was a really great example of the time and the space that the locker room had and the respect we had for each other, and respect for you coming in as a veteran in our locker room.” Wilde has not wrestled since 2023. During her last run, she captured the Knockouts World Tag Team Titles with KiLynn King.

Deonna Purrazzo revealed that Lucha Libre AAA had scheduled a title-versus-title match for her without the knowledge of TNA's Scott D'Amore. The plan called for Purrazzo to win the bout and become the Reina de Reinas Champion.
The scheduled match between Purrazzo and Wilde was planned for Slammiversary in 2021. Instead, Purrazzo faced a mystery opponent at the event, who turned out to be Thunder Rosa.

Wilde was unaware of the AAA stipulation that had been added to the planned program. Purrazzo expressed willingness to let Wilde win the match and travel to Mexico for the Reina de Reinas Championship bout if that was preferred.
The situation highlighted the respect within the locker room at the time. Purrazzo noted it showed consideration for Wilde as a veteran returning to the promotion.
Wilde has not wrestled since 2023. In her final run with the company, she held the Knockouts World Tag Team Titles alongside KiLynn King.

body: Upon Ilja Dragunov’s in-ring debut for All Elite Wrestling, he spoke to TMZ’s Inside The Ring podcas t. During the chat, he stated that he thinks he sticks out on the AEW roster and that he’s always betting on himself. “I didn’t consider how stacked the roster is because it’s a fear I don’t have. I was always betting on myself. I bet on myself when I left WWE. I’m betting on myself still, and I’m betting on what my gut is telling me and the way the people, the company introduced me, I think it speaks for itself that I stick out from all the rest on that roster. People who stick out and are not like anybody else, you kind of put the objective on them and only if you are like everybody else or try to be like everybody else — which is also like an unfortunate thing happening nowadays, unfortunately — then you get overlooked. But, I haven’t been overlooked once in my 14 years of career.” Dragunov’s first match will be against ‘Speedball’ Mike Bailey on the 10/21 Dynamite.

title: Fans Urged to Support Ilja Dragunov

Every time Ilja Dragonuv wasn't utilized by World Wrestling Entertainment, the online discourse was the same - where is he? Why isn't he being utilized? Why isn't be on TV? Why isn't he getting pushed? The Russian-born German star has been beloved for his unhinged intensity, stiff striking, and emotionally charged physical storytelling. The "Unbesiegbar" (Unbeatable) Mad Dragon, Dragunov gained international acclaim before signing with WWE, where captured the WWE NXT UK Championship by ending GUNTHER's insane 870-day reign with an instant classic. He moved to the United States, where he held the WWE NXT title and eventually, the main roster, where he won the WWE United States Championship. Recognized for his intense in-ring style, marked by his signature Torpedo Moskva flying headbutt and H-Bomb forearm strike, Dragonuv excels at believable, hard-hitting encounters and dramatic, resilient selling that position him as one of the most physical performers in modern professional wrestling. He was the exact style of performer that Paul Levesque's NXT popularized themselves utilizing, so it was was unthinkable that under Levesque's creative direction that Dragonuv wouldn't be a massive part of WWE, yet it didn't truly happen. An ACL tear hobbed his momentum for sure, but his return was well received, as was his U.S. title run. However, once 2026 began, other than being unceremoniously tossed from The Royal Rumble by Brock Lesnar, there was nothing truly memorable for Ilja creatively and then, he chose to exit the company. The outpouring of shock and anger over the exit was palapable, to the point I even received emailed accusing me of lying when PWInsider.com broke the news of his exit. No matter how you feel about Dragonuv's run in WWE, the one constant was that die-hard wrestling fans loved his work and loudly complained online when he wasn't utilized in a stronger manner. If they truly believe WWE whiffed the ball on Dragnonuv, those same fans will get the chance to see him step up to bat tonight for All Elite Wrestling on Dynamite. As famously stated in Field of Dreams, "If you build it, they will come." AEW Dynamite airs tonight (Oct. 21) with a live show emanating from Watsco Center in Coral Gables, Florida. This is the first episode of Dynamite during the four week build to Full Gear, which takes place on November 14. One of the big stories at WrestleDream was the reveal that former WWE star Ilja Dragunov is officially All Elite. title: Jaxson Ryker details severe injuries after WWE exit

summary_src: Former WWE star Jaxson Ryker opened up about his decision to step away from wrestling, revealing the persistent injuries and body aches that contributed to it. Ryker emphasized the toll of wrestling on his body following his WWE release in 2021.
body: Former WWE star Jaxson Ryker opened up about his decision to step away from wrestling, revealing the persistent injuries and body aches that contributed to it. Ryker emphasized the toll of wrestling on his body following his WWE release in 2021. In his interview with Developmentally Speaking, the former WWE star revisited his decision to retire in 2023, reflecting on his brief return to the independent wrestling scene before ultimately calling it quits for good. “No, I think I had in the back of my mind that it was time to start maybe pursuing other things. My body, when I got released from WWE, my body was hurting real bad. I’d had a neck injury and a lower-back injury that was causing some numbness in my arm and my hand,” said Ryker. “Just really, really excruciating pain for the most part. I always told myself years ago if I got to where I didn’t enjoy it anymore or my body hurt really bad, I would walk away on my own. I didn’t want to be 50 and crippled. And so when that happened I was like, ‘Okay, well, let’s just do an independent run. I could go all over these places. I’ve worked for NWA and that’s basically what I did for the, I took three, four months off after they released me.” He expressed no interest in stepping foot in the ring again despite being approached to do so. “I’ve had people call me, buddies of mine, promoters, ‘Hey, man, would you consider one more match?’” And I am so content in my retirement life. ’Cause my body feels 100 times better, you know. I don’t ache and moan and groan anymore as much as I used to. The wrestling business changed for me. And I think my views in life changed. What was important to me changed. And so it was, no. I sat back and I was like, ‘Dude, I’ve given 23 years of my life to pro wrestling. I’ve escaped with, I mean, I’ve had broken fingers and nose and stuff, but never broken a neck or anything crazy.’ And I was like, ‘I’ve had a blessed career, and I’ve got to do a lot, a lot of stuff that a lot of guys never get to or never will get to do.’” Ryker signed with WWE in 2021 and made his main roster debut in 2020 as part of The Forgotten Sons. After the stable disbanded, Ryker was briefly paired with Elias until their alliance imploded and ultimately led to a singles rivalry before his WWE release. body: Billy Gunn was one of the first signings in AEW, originally signed to work as a coach and producer, but he did end up in the ring. Speaking to Kenny McIntosh of Inside The Ropes , Gunn revealed his original AEW talent contract. “My contract, I had 12 dates a year. I really wasn’t going to wrestle, but I told Tony, ‘If you need me to, I’ll do it here and there.’ I still had a talent contract and employee contract. I was mostly producing and coaching. The talent one was little because (I wasn’t sure) if I would even fill those dates. Lo and behold. They cracked me out and I’m working both shows and working all the time, about to fall apart,” he said. Gunn had 23 matches for AEW in 2020 and 34 matches in 2021. He has not wrestled for AEW since January 2026. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

llm_long: Billy Gunn has been part of All Elite Wrestling since 2020. He insisted that his sons Austin and Colten complete their college education before pursuing careers in the promotion.
Gunn stated that he refused to help get his sons hired by AEW until they graduated. He emphasized that his own success in wrestling did not guarantee they would succeed in the same field.

On the day Austin Gunn graduated, he handed his diploma to his father and immediately asked when they could start in wrestling. Gunn had required college graduation as the first condition before any discussion of entering the business.
Colten Gunn also decided to pursue wrestling after having a different career path mapped out until age 60. The choice surprised both Gunn and his wife, given the demanding nature of the profession.

Gunn explained that his frequent absences from home, including 300 days on the road each year early in his career, made him hesitant for his sons to follow the same path. He wanted them to have more stable family lives than he experienced.
Although Gunn trained his sons to a certain point, he required them to seek and complete AEW tryouts on their own. He did not ask for them to be hired simply because they were his children.

We spend a lot of time on the German indies because in times where he wasn’t in the tag team as the Aussie Open. They spent some time in Germany. I spent my time there with wXw as well. We were touring together. It was like years ago, and then when our way split it up and I signed, he signed, he did his thing. title: Ilja Dragunov Calls Emotional Expression Wrestling's Toughest Element
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Says That The Expressive Part Of Wrestling Is 'The Real Exhausting Part'
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says that the expressive part of wrestling is 'the real exhausting part' of the industry noting that it is harder than moves.
body: Ilja Dragunov says that the expressive part of wrestling is ‘the real exhausting part’ of the industry noting that it is harder than moves. Dragunov is a performer who has never shied away from being expressive in his pro wrestling career, and it is a part of his all round package that fans commonly point to when discussing his abilities in the wrestling industry. “It is definitely the part of expressing yourself. It is the vocality. It is the expressions. This part of portraying what you’re doing is at times much harder than any move that you can do. Like this pressure that your body handles. You’re screaming out when you punch, when you get hit. You constantly focus to include the audience, to have this roundabout vision at all times, it is extremely exhausting, and also, it’s not just comes down to what’s the next cool looking thing that I can do. It’s like, how do I handle what happened right now to me? How does it change me as a person during this beautiful fight that I’m expressing, during this play with my opponent? That’s the real exhausting part, and it’s physically exhausting.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Ilja Dragunov explained that the most draining aspect of pro wrestling is the expressive side, including vocality, facial expressions and audience engagement. He noted this is often harder than performing physical moves, as it requires constant focus on reacting authentically to the action and involving the crowd throughout a match. The comments come from a recent interview reported by Fightful Select.

Dragunov highlighted vocality and facial expressions as key components that require significant effort. He noted that portraying reactions during matches creates substantial pressure on the body.

The performer emphasized the need to scream during strikes or when receiving them. He described maintaining constant awareness of the audience while focusing on the in-ring action as extremely tiring.

According to Dragunov, wrestling involves more than performing impressive maneuvers. It centers on reacting authentically to events in the match and showing personal change throughout the performance.
He characterized this emotional and physical exhaustion as the true demanding part of the industry. Dragunov has consistently incorporated strong expressiveness throughout his career.

body: Ric Flair appreciates the generosity Tony Khan has shown him during their friendship. Since 2023, Flair has been under contract with AEW despite only making very rare appearances for the company. He originally debuted as part of Sting’s retirement tour and with a sponsorship deal for his “Wooooo! Energy” drink. That sponsorship is no longer in place, but Flair remains with AEW. He praised Khan in an interview with Biff Poggi of NewsNation, saying he believes Khan still takes care of him out of respect. “He’s a nice guy, he’s generous. I work for him, and I don’t do anything,” Flair said about Khan. “I think he takes care of me out of respect for me. He grew up on me. He’s just a wonderful guy. It’s not that the guys at the WWE — I just think they’re all kind of hanging onto their job, because you never know. [WWE has] fired so many people that were an intricate part of my career when I was there. I don’t understand the rhyme or reason for it. Some of the people — the guys that did my documentary on Peacock, two of the guys that did it have been fired.” “I think Nick Khan is pretty much the boss over there, but at the same time, I don’t know how much power Nick Khan has. He used to be the man,” Flair said. “But, you know, Hunter is the booker now, or the head of creative they call it.” Flair, 77, believes the only thing separating WWE and AEW at this point is the fact that WWE has existed for so much longer. He is impressed by Khan’s ability as a promoter and thinks Khan could be the greatest promoter of all time. “It’s internal. I don’t know who makes the final decision,” Flair responded when asked generally about who makes the political decisions in wrestling. “With Tony Khan, who runs AEW, who is really one of the most wonderful people I’ve ever known, Tony has a group of people, which I’m sure they do at WWE, that he circles up with. And Tony does it right there. Tony Khan may be the greatest promoter of all time.” Poggi asked if Flair meant Khan could be the greatest wrestling promoter or the greatest promoter in any industry. title: RVD Claims WWE Wrestlers Feared for Their Jobs Unlike in AEW
raw_title: RVD Claims WWE Wrestlers Feared for Their Jobs Unlike in AEW
summary_src: RVD believes AEW gives its wrestlers something he didn’t always see during his years in WWE — the freedom to speak up and express themselves.
body: “Yeah. They’ve definitely proven themselves. You know, like, it was so easy when they first came out to be like, ‘Yeah, well, let’s see how long they stick around.’ And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with any of us that felt that way because promotions over the years come up all the time.” RVD admitted he’d seen plenty of companies arrive with serious financial backing and promises of becoming the next big thing, only for them to eventually disappear. AEW has managed to get past that stage, and he believes the company has established itself as a legitimate alternative. “‘Oh, they got Major League Baseball money. This shit’s for real,’ and they got this and that, and it never lasts. And those guys, you know, really fill the void, and so it’s cool. Congrats to AEW, and they’re just going to keep growing.” Van Dam also pays attention to what wrestling fans tell him they’re actually watching. From those conversations, he’s noticed plenty of people aren’t exclusively choosing WWE or AEW and instead follow both companies. “You know, I always check with the fans and ask what they watch, and a lot of people are watching both products. I don’t know how much international distribution they have, but obviously they must be on in the places that they’re going to, at least.” That’s when RVD got into what he believes separates the two promotions. To him, AEW still comes across as a company where the wrestlers themselves have a bigger hand in what they’re doing. “But yeah, pretty cool. And it still — and I think always will — be coming across as, and I think for valid reasons, the boys being the ones that are kind of running the show more.” His description of WWE was much different. RVD claimed there were wrestlers who feared losing their jobs, which could make them reluctant to question directions or push back against something they were being told to do. “You know, whereas WWE was like a lot of people afraid for their job and doing whatever they’re told, and sometimes afraid to go against it or say the wrong thing or whatever.” By comparison, RVD believes AEW gives its wrestlers more room to show what they can do on their own terms. That’s a big part of why the promotion feels more wrestler-driven to him. “And this seems more like guys that want to be out there expressing themselves with their talent and doing it their way.” RVD isn’t claiming every wrestler’s experience in either company is the same, but his own impression of the two environments is pretty clear. After watching AEW survive the early skepticism, he sees its wrestler-driven approach as one of the things that continues to separate it from the WWE environment he remembers. title: Dominik Mysterio Discusses WWE 2K26 Street Fighter DLC
raw_title: Dominik Mysterio Talks WWE 2K26 Street Fighter DLC, Rey Mysterio, AAA, Judgment Day in B/R Interview
body: Mysterio is one of five WWE Superstars who will be included in the WWE 2K26 x Street Fighter Elite DLC Pack, which features wrestlers playing the roles of Street Fighter characters. Dom is cast as Ken, and he's joined by Rey Mysterio as Ryu, Bianca Belair as Cammy, The Rock as M. Bison and Ultimate Warrior as Blanka. Full Grades from Latest Raw Bleacher Report 23h Why It's Time to End Judgement Day Bleacher Report 23h NXT Results & Grades 🔠 Bleacher Report 12h The characters in the game are modeled specifically after WWE Mattel action figures depicting Superstars as Street Fighter characters, which makes it extra special from Dominik's perspective. "I've been in a couple of 2K games with WWE the past couple years now, but this is special," Mysterio said. "It's Street Fighter, it's not only a DLC pack that you have to pre-order and get separately, but also they made it an action figure. I have a couple at the house, and it's in, like, an old arcade-style box, and they're super cool. I have a couple in my game room, and it's just cool to be a part of the whole Street Fighter franchise." Dirty Dom revealed that he wasn't told about the Ken action figure ahead of time and didn't know about it until he saw photos. At that point, he instantly wanted to get one in his possession. "I didn't know until I started getting tagged in the pictures of me as Ken, and I was like, 'What is going on? Did someone make this custom, or like, what is it,'" Mysterio said. "And then the company ended up telling me, like, 'Oh no, you're part of this DLC pack in 2K26.' And I was like, 'What? This is so sick.' I found out kind of like the old-fashioned way where I just kept getting tagged. And then as soon as I saw it, I was like, 'How do I get my hands on this action figure?'" Ken has long been among the most popular characters in the Street Fighter video game franchise, which first launched in 1987 and truly rose to prominence with the release of Street Fighter II in 1991. Dominik feels he and Ken have some similarities, noting that Ken's bio describes him as a fighter who comes to the United States to "get humbled because he's too cocky." Dom also acknowledged that both he and Ken have luscious heads of hair, quipping that he may have to "golden up the tips of the good old mullet" at some point in order to match Ken. Fittingly, Mysterio likes to play the Street Fighter video game series with some of his fellow WWE Superstars, and Ken is his character of choice when his back is against the wall in a "glass break in case of emergency" situation since he knows how to do all of his combos. "Of course, I would do it in the game and real life," Dom said of beating up his dad. "Even if I gotta get a red gi and show up at his house and, you know, hit him with a good, old-fashioned swift kick. But yeah, I would definitely do some damage because he doesn't play video games.
