Bailey is coming off Clockwork Carnage, which saw him eliminated by Konosuke Takeshita in Phase 1, so he’ll be itching to get back in the win column. Does Bailey make a statement against the newest member of All Elite Wrestling, or does Dragunov prove why he’s All Elite with a victorious debut? After TBS & CMLL World Women's Champion Persephone retained her TBS Championship in a hard-hitting 4-Way Match at WrestleDream over Hyan, Dani Luna and Queen Aminata, she’ll find out her next challenger tonight! Aminata will fight former champion Maya World, and the winner becomes the #1 contender for the TBS Championship! World, who announced she was cleared to wrestle on the WrestleDream Buy-In, was the TBS Champion until Persephone took the title from her at All In: London with the help of Dr. Britt Baker, D.M.D. World’s partner, Hyan, carried the torch in her absence, and now World gets her own chance to get back in the TBS Title picture. Aminata has been so close to her first gold in AEW after taking AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné to the limit in Paris and nearly winning the TBS Championship at WrestleDream. Aminata owns the lone victory between the two from an ROH encounter with World in December 2023. Does World earn the chance to take back the TBS Championship, or will Aminata’s relentless nature be too much for World to overcome in her first match since early September? The Don Callis Family gets another crack at the Young Bucks! After Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight fell short against Matt and Nick Jackson in a classic WrestleDream match, a pair of Callis’ heavy hitters step up as Mark Davis and Jake Doyle fight Matt and Nick Jackson in an AEW World Tag Team Championship Eliminator. Davis and Doyle, who beat AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley and Gabe Kidd in Paris two weeks ago, are two of the Don Callis Family's biggest weapons. Davis gave Moxley all he could handle at WrestleDream and left him a bloody mess. Do the Bucks hold off another wave from the Don Callis Family, or do Davis and Doyle earn a shot at the AEW World Tag Team Championship with a win tonight in Florida?

McIntyre explained that he had carried the sword for years without using it to stab or chop anyone despite fans wondering when he would. He stuck the sword in the ring and in Adam Pearce's table before making his pitch to McMahon.

McIntyre referenced the film Saving Private Ryan in his pitch and described using amputee actors to realistically lop off limbs in a fight sequence. The proposed sequence would end backstage before transitioning to a pre-tape where McIntyre swings the sword and severs an arm.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Says He Needs To Wrestle In Japan: 'That’s The Place Where I Think My Style Belongs'
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Says He Needs To Wrestle In Japan: 'That’s The Place Where I Think My Style Belongs'
body: There’s a slight chance that we’ll see Ilja Dragunov wrestle in Japan in the future. At AEW WrestleDream, Ilja Dragunov made his highly anticipated debut in All Elite Wrestling. Dragunov previously worked for WWE, where he had many incredible matches. Despite being popular with fans, WWE didn’t seem to have much planned for him on television. In the end, Dragunov declined WWE’s offer for a new contract and became a free agent. He later signed with AEW and is currently scheduled to make his in-ring debut for the company on the October 21 edition of AEW Dynamite. TMZ’s Inside the Ring recently spoke with Dragunov, where the wrestler was asked about wrestlers he’d like to work with outside AEW. Dragunov didn’t have an answer for that, but he did mention one of the places he’d like to have a match: Japan. Dragunov believes his style of wrestling belongs there. “I wouldn’t say it’s necessarily who I want to work with, but where I want to work. Back in the day when I started with wXw, they had a working relationship with Big Japan Pro Wrestling. And when I joined wXw, it’s kind of like this time was passed. And the one thing that I didn’t do in my career so far, multiple things that I didn’t do in my career so far, but specifically something that I need to do is to wrestle in Japan. I need to wrestle in Japan. Because that’s the place where I think my style belongs, and I think I would connect with the people, with this culture for professional wrestling in a whole different way.” Dragunov has never worked for a Japanese promotion before, but with AEW’s partnership with New Japan Pro Wrestling, this could change in the future. AEW wrestlers frequently work New Japan’s shows, and seeing Dragunov wrestle someone like Zack Sabre Jr. or compete in the G1 Climax would be an incredible experience for the fans. title: On the Record: WWE Accused of “Dropping the Ball” on Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
raw_title: WWE Accused of “Dropping the Ball” on Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has barely gotten started in AEW, and Jonathan Coachman is already wondering how WWE let this one get away. After watching Dragunov’s WrestleDream debut, Coachman and JD both came away believing WWE could have done a whole lot more with him.
body: Speaking on 2 Count Tuesday , JD said Dragunov’s AEW presentation was even better than he expected. Everything from the music to his look screamed top star to him, and he thinks Dragunov could eventually follow the same path Swerve Strickland did. “If they take Dragunov, I look at it more like a Swerve Strickland. When Swerve came in, it took him a little bit of time to find his footing, and he eventually became a world champion.” JD doesn’t just see Dragunov as someone who could have a nice run in AEW either. He thinks there’s legitimate World Champion potential there, and possibly even someone who could eventually become one of the faces of the company. “I think if they let Dragunov be Dragunov, I think he could be a world champion just like Swerve was, and he can be an ace for that company. That’s how high I think of Dragunov.” “I don’t know why WWE would let him go. I don’t know why WWE dropped the ball on him. I don’t know why they didn’t give him the resources to be a top guy. He’s got top-guy potential, and he’s top-guy shit.” Coachman jumped right on that point, and he put a lot of the responsibility on WWE creative. He wants to know what was actually being written for someone like Dragunov before his run with the company came to an end. “Yeah, it’s that last question — you’ve got to give creative. And this is why I’ve been calling for creative to be called on the carpet, is walk in and show me what you have written. Show me what you have done, because a guy like that, you’ve got to give him creative.” “I’m so tired of hearing people — whether it’s Tony… Oh, they got to — well, Tony doesn’t say it, but Triple H does — ‘He’s got to get himself over. He’s got to get herself over.’” For Coachman, WrestleDream was a pretty good example of what he’s talking about. Dragunov already looks and sounds like a star, so he doesn’t think AEW needs to make every appearance another 15- or 20-minute match just to prove how good he is. “And last night, you talked about the presentation — or at WrestleDream — when you look like a star, sound like a star, and then you go out there and have not 15- or 20-minute matches every time. Make it — change it up just a little bit.” Instead, Coachman wants AEW to keep finding different ways to showcase him. That’s where he believes creative needs to earn its money instead of expecting Dragunov to figure everything out by himself. “Present him differently all the way. But this is where creative’s got to step up, and they’ve got to step up for him.” It’s way too early to know whether Dragunov actually becomes the kind of AEW star JD thinks he can be. But after one presentation, they’re already asking the question WWE probably doesn’t want to hear — did the company let a future top guy walk right out the door? title: Double Champ Bandido Headlines AEW Dynamite At Coral Gables' Watsco Center
raw_title: Double Champ Bandido Headlines AEW Dynamite At Coral Gables' Watsco Center
body: Source: Photos N Effect / Wikimedia Commons A masked luchador carrying two championships into the building will headline AEW Dynamite live from the Watsco Center at the University of Miami on Wednesday, with the show airing on TBS and streaming on HBO Max. Bandido, the current Ring of Honor World Champion, arrives in Coral Gables as one of the promotion's most decorated active stars, known for blending high-flying lucha libre with hard-hitting power moves. According to the Miami Herald , Bandido also recently teamed with Brody King and Adam “Hangman” Page to capture the AEW Trios Titles, defeating Swerve Strickland and New Level, Austin Creed and Kofi, in a best-two-of-three-falls match. That victory makes him a double champion heading into Wednesday's taping, pairing his individual Ring of Honor reign with group gold won alongside two of AEW's biggest names. Bandido's path back to the top of Ring of Honor has been anything but simple. He first won the ROH World Championship on July 11, 2021, defeating Rush at Best in the World, only to vacate the title five months later in December 2021 after testing positive for COVID-19, according to Fightful . He recaptured the title in April 2025 by defeating veteran Chris Jericho in a Title vs. Mask match at AEW Dynasty, a notable reversal since Jericho had beaten Bandido during the luchador's AEW debut back in September 2022. That current reign has now stretched more than 560 days, the second longest in the title's history, and the Herald notes that Bandido has held the ROH World Championship across his two reigns for more combined days than anyone else. Outside of Ring of Honor and AEW, Bandido has also wrestled for CMLL and New Japan Pro Wrestling, and he has been recognized by ESPN as one of the 30 best pro wrestlers under 30 and ranked No. 11 among the top 500 wrestlers in the world by Pro Wrestling Illustrated. In accordance with Mexican lucha libre tradition, Bandido's real identity has never been revealed; he is a fourth-generation luchador whose younger brother competes professionally under the ring name Gravity, according to Wikipedia . Bandido's run with Brody King didn't start with trios. The pair formed the tag team Brodido in the summer of 2025 and won the AEW World Tag Team Championship before losing the titles that November. The trio expanded over the summer of 2026, when Bandido, King and Page won the AEW World Trios Championship at Arena Mexico in Mexico City, only to drop the titles to Swerve Strickland and the New Level at AEW All In: London, held at Wembley Stadium. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Explains Why He Doesn’t Get Defensive When Wrestling Is Called “Fake”
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Explains Why He Doesn’t Get Defensive When Wrestling Is Called “Fake”
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has seen plenty of wrestlers get fired up when someone calls professional wrestling “fake,” but that’s not a fight he’s interested in having.
body: The topic came up as Cody was explaining kayfabe to Andrew Schulz and how difficult it can sometimes be for people outside the wrestling world to understand where the performance ends and reality begins. He’s seen interviews take a turn pretty quickly once someone drops what he jokingly called the “F-word.” “I’ve seen several times when you can tell a wrestler instantly — especially when it’s a split-screen interview — when somebody drops the F-word in there, and then a wrestler will be like, ‘Well, I broke my neck.’” Cody understands why wrestlers react that way, especially considering the very real physical toll that comes with the job. It’s just not the approach he personally likes to take when someone questions wrestling’s legitimacy. Instead, Cody takes what he described as a softer approach. He doesn’t need to argue about whether the match itself is “real” when the emotions fans experience watching it absolutely are. “I typically take a softer approach to the feeling you have when you come to an event is a real feeling. It’s a real feeling, man. And that’s usually why I don’t ever use the F-word in that regard.” There’s another reason Cody doesn’t like getting defensive about it. Once a wrestler gets hung up on proving wrestling isn’t fake, he thinks the actual interview can quickly grind to a halt. “But also, that’s where wrestling interviews sometimes can go to die.” When the host suggested that wrestlers sometimes just need to let the subject go, Cody agreed. Getting dragged into an argument isn’t going to accomplish much if it kills the rest of the conversation: “You got to let it go.” “Yeah. Like, you remember when Tyson got interviewed and all of a sudden called that guy a rat? Do you remember that?” After watching the Tyson clip, Cody came back to his own philosophy. He’d rather keep his cool and, if the opportunity presents itself, drop a good wrestling sound bite without letting the entire interview turn into an argument. “Yeah. But it did — that’s again where a lot of wrestling interviews can go to die. I always just, you know, try and keep the composure. If there’s an opening to put my little sound bite in there, great.” Cody isn’t trying to convince every skeptic that wrestling is something it isn’t. For him, the better argument is what fans actually feel when they’re watching it, and he’d rather let that speak for itself than turn an interview into a debate over the word “fake.” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

title: Cody Rhodes Claims 99.9% of Wrestlers Don’t Want to Give Up Their Spot
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Claims 99.9% of Wrestlers Don’t Want to Give Up Their Spot
summary_src: Cody Rhodes believes John Cena’s final WWE run could end up being remembered for something much bigger than wins, losses or championships. In Cody’s eyes, Cena spent an entire year doing everything he could to elevate other wrestlers instead of choosing just one person to pass the torch to.
body: Speaking to Andrew Schulz , Cody discussed the difference between simply losing to another wrestler and truly putting that person over. Cody described it as the difference between “doing the job” and “doing the honors,” with the latter involving an established star doing everything possible to make the moment belong to the wrestler they’re elevating. “I think John probably will go down because he spent an entire year doing the honors. He didn’t just pick one.” Schulz pointed out that Cena essentially took a bet on several different wrestlers during that run. Cody agreed, stressing that Cena did much more than simply agree to take a loss and move on. “Yeah, he took a bet on a few, you know. He definitely did more than just doing the favor.” For Cody, that’s the big difference between simply “doing the job” and actually giving someone the full spotlight. He believes Cena understood exactly how to make those moments matter for the wrestlers he was working with. “It was — he did the honors, and that’s the way you want to do it.” Cena wasn’t the only veteran Cody gave credit to. When Schulz asked for other examples of wrestlers who knew how to give back, Cody quickly pointed toward Triple H and The Undertaker. “Oh man, I mean, you mentioned Triple H. Triple H is a great example. Gosh, all — probably all your faves. The Undertaker.” Cody also admitted there’s naturally some selfishness involved when it comes to eventually giving up a spot. Wrestlers can spend years fighting to reach a certain level, so he understands why they might not exactly be eager to let it go. “Yeah. Great. You know, like, you know, and sometimes there’s a selfishness to it as well because you go so long until it’s time.” “I’d say 99.9% of wrestlers perhaps don’t want to let go. And it’s when you have—” “I am not going to get into Wrestling with Shadows with you, but you know what?” Cody’s larger point was that truly putting someone over involves a lot more than simply losing a match. That’s why Cena stands out so much to him — Cody believes his final run was an extended effort to give several wrestlers something meaningful rather than making his farewell all about himself. title: WWE's Worst Storyline Has Ruined The Judgment Day
raw_title: WWE's Worst Storyline Has Ruined The Judgment Day
body: The size of JD McDonagh’s head has been a minor joke in WWE for many years, being used as an easy jibe here and there. In 2026, it was made the subject of an entire storyline. Babyfaces such as Joe Hendry and JD McDonagh have taken aim at both McDonagh and Dominik Mysterio of The Judgment Day, resulting in a truly awful attempt at a “comedic” storyline from WWE. For several weeks, babyfaces have been bringing out people dressed as giant Funko Pops, with it being asserted that McDonagh is the offspring of one of these figures. WWE’s handling of The Judgment Day in 2026 has killed the group forever, especially for those in the men’s division. Dominik Mysterio began the year as both Intercontinental & AAA Mega Champion, but has since lost both championships, come up short in his feud with Finn Balor, feuded with Danhausen for six months in a feud that ended in a remarkably bad “Human Monies On A Pole” match at SummerSlam , and then began teaming with McDonagh in their various battles against Funko Pop-obsessed babyfaces. It hasn’t just been a poor year for Mysterio & McDonagh. Liv Morgan might’ve spent much of 2026 as Women’s World Champion , but her reign with the belt was one of the worst in recent memory. She has hardly any defenses, served mostly as a manager and cheerleader for her stablemates, and had no memorable feuds to shout about. Additionally, Judgment Day’s bad luck continued as Money In The Bank favorite, Roxanne Perez, had plans for her to win changed ahead of the show , leading to a frustrating defeat. Triple H has done far too much damage to this once great group. Fans have been begging for some time for members of The Judgment Day to go their separate ways, especially with how badly 2026 has gone. Triple H needs to end the faction in order to save the individual careers of everyone involved. Mysterio & Morgan no longer generate the same level of heat they once did, the slow-burn breakup of the women’s division members of the group has gone beyond the point of fans caring about it, and overall there is a lack of interest in anything the faction does. The Judgment Day has been on the ropes for a while, but this recent Funko Pop travesty is the ultimate nail in the coffin.

body: Link Image from Syko Stu’s Instagram Last year, independent wrester Syko Stu was involved in a high-profile incident with MMA fighter Raja Jackson at a KnokX Pro event in Sun Valley, California in August of last year. The incident led to reactions from pro wrestlers, as well as from Raja’s father . The 26-year-old Jackson was arrested and charged, saying he was not guilty . He eventually made a deal with L.A. prosecutors in which he pleaded no contest to one felony count of battery with serious bodily injury, and guilty to another felony count personal infliction of great bodily injury and engaging in violent conduct in exchange for a 90-day jail sentence, two years of probation, and $81,703.38 in restitution to Smith. Jackson was released late last month after serving his sentence. Stu continued: “I was out on the slam… I don’t remember anything until, I believe it was Tuesday. I woke up in the hospital…I was going in and out of consciousness the whole time. I do remember waking up on Tuesday and saw some of the wrestlers. [KnokX Pro owner] Rikishi was there, and we were talking.” Regarding the difficult recovery he endured, Stu said: “I really had to relearn how to walk. I couldn’t walk after that for a while. I did have a severe traumatic brain injury. I lost two teeth. I shattered my maxilla. I know there’s more stuff, but I can’t remember off the top of my head. When asked about previously saying the had forgiven Jackson for the incident, Stu said that statement taken “a little bit of context.” “What I actually said was, ‘I’m not holding a grudge.’ I never said anything about forgiveness. Everybody can learn something from this. I just didn’t want to hold a grudge because that brings the negative energy into it.” he said. “When you have to let something go, it kind of helps you heal from it. As far as forgiveness, when we’re in the courtroom and I was reading that statement, I don’t think the LA Times heard the same statement that I read.” Stu also indicated that while he was hospitalized, Rampage had called and wanted him to call back. body: Why It's Time to End Judgement Day Bleacher Report 1d Penta Takes Control, More Raw Fallout 💪 Bleacher Report 23h Debating Triple H's Obsession With WarGames Match 👨‍⚖️ Bleacher Report 2d That is not an indictment of the newly formed group, either. Keys and Co. have been spectacular. They have grabbed the ball and run with it, oftentimes resulting in the best segment of any Raw episode. They have been menacing, physical, and violent when necessary, and have presented a credible threat to The Bloodline. Then there is Parker, whose on-screen aura is that of a star. She may be the biggest name of the bunch when all is said and done. No, The 946 will be destroyed at Survivor Series because that is the nature of things in WWE. The group appears to have been built up to put The Bloodline over in a high-profile match. No contest is more significant to feuding factions than WarGames. As if there were not already a perceived gap in status between the two groups, The Bloodline is led by the biggest star in the company: Reigns. The same Reigns who has been a dominant force in WWE since becoming The Tribal Chief in 2020. He rarely loses big matches and is in the midst of his greatest run to date, delivering consistent Match of the Year candidates in his World Heavyweight Championship defenses. Add to that a storyline that sets up at least one big return in the form of former women's world champion Naomi, who can confront and take out Parker, and you have a scenario in which The Bloodline could stand tall. The only saving grace for The 946 could be the role of Jacob Fatu. Parker ran over The Samoan Werewolf in her main roster debut, and while that would seemingly lead to him siding with his cousins, there is history with Keys that could lead him to align with the heels, especially considering his role in The Bloodline was against his will and the result of a loss to Reigns. body: As we’ve been following closely , former WWE Tag Team Champion Dragon Lee’s WWE contract is set to expire soon. WWE’s use of Dragon Lee since his 2022 debut has drawn heavy scrutiny. The Chief Content Officer explained that he wanted the luchador to be around for years to come. Now, The Game is trying to make good on his word. With Dragon Lee’s ongoing WWE negotiations and the Hermanos Lee trademark, many AEW loyalists questioned if RUSH was WWE-bound. While some say Dragon Lee burned a bridge with AEW, some are still pushing Tony Khan to make a Hail Mary offer. title: Legal Watch: WWE, Vince and Linda McMahon Lose Bid To Dismiss Sexual Abuse Lawsuit
raw_title: WWE, Vince and Linda McMahon Lose Bid To Dismiss Sexual Abuse Lawsuit
body: 0 A federal judge on Monday rejected WWE, TKO, Vince , and Linda McMahon’s effort to have the ring boy sexual assault lawsuit dismissed. Eight anonymous plaintiffs filed the lawsuit in 2024. They claim they were sexually abused in the 1980s and 1990s. This was when they were setting up rings or running other errands in WWE (then known as WWF). They alleged abuse by former ring announcer Mel Phillips. One also accused inaugural Intercontinental Champion Pat Patterson, and another named former executive Terry Garvin. Phillips, Patterson, and Garvin passed away years before the lawsuit was filed. The plaintiffs claim former WWE owners Vince and Linda McMahon were negligent in allowing the abuse to happen. The former ring boys overcame an earlier motion to dismiss in December 2025, which narrowed the number of plaintiffs from eight to seven. All plaintiffs remain anonymous under “John Doe” aliases. The defendants have denied the primary allegations. However, U.S. District Judge James K. Bredar ruled that the Maryland law is constitutional as applied to the case. The case will now proceed to discovery, during which both sides will gather evidence and take sworn depositions. A teleconference to schedule future deadlines will take place on November 17. However, any potential trial remains at least several months off. Maryland passed the Child Victims Act in 2023, which eliminated any time limit for filing civil lawsuits related to child sexual abuse. Had the new law not come into effect, the statute of limitations on the plaintiffs’ claims would have lapsed years ago. The plaintiffs claim the named WWE executives assaulted them in different states, but, importantly, said some of them happened in Maryland. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Speaks On Whether He Blames WWE for His Departure
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Addresses Whether He Blames WWE for His Departure
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov says he could feel something changing in WWE well before his contract actually expired.
body: Speaking to The TakeDown on SI , Dragunov looked back at what he described as a “very complicated” period of his career. A huge part of that was recovering from the ACL tear that kept him out of action and putting everything he had into getting himself back into the ring. All that work initially seemed to pay off in a huge way. Dragunov said he essentially won the United States Championship as soon as he returned, and he still looks back on that moment as something special. “I came back, and I won the United States Championship basically on my return, which was an awesome, memorable moment.” Things didn’t stay that way forever. Once Dragunov dropped the championship and moved into whatever came next, he started getting a feeling that his situation inside WWE had changed. Dragunov isn’t pointing fingers at WWE or blaming any particular person for that feeling. In fact, he went out of his way to stress how much respect he still has for the company after spending seven years there and giving WWE most of his twenties. “And I don’t blame anybody. I’m a gentleman and I have way too much respect for the last seven years that I — the most of my 20s — that I spent with the company.” “But I felt like it is fine for me and reasonable to ask myself, ‘Is there more? Is there a new air I can breathe?’” “Again, everything I can say is not as exciting as people made it. Of course, at some point in time, you don’t have creative — you’re just waiting for the next opportunities to come.” Dragunov said WWE’s crowded roster and already-full storylines were part of the situation. Eventually his contract expired in August, and negotiations between the two sides didn’t produce anything that convinced him he absolutely needed to stay. “Everything I can say is there was nothing I felt was satisfying and nothing that gave me the perspective of, like, ‘Okay, I MUST stick with here.’” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

body: In a latest tweet posted via his X account , Big Daddy Cool revealed that he had been travelling a lot lately. However, until two years ago, that was not possible for him due to major injuries. He said that he had herniated discs in his back and problems in his left quad, with the muscle atrophying at an alarming rate. The WWE legend underwent stem cell procedures for his issues and was able to regain the quality of life while not undergoing surgery. You can read Nash’s tweet below: “I sent my MRI’s to the specialist @BioXcelleratorand they felt the stem cell treatment could prevent a surgical procedure. I don’t thank the medical advances that saved my quality of life and allowed me to return 100% surgery free. If you are in a position that mimics mine please consider @BioXcellerator . I don’t know anyone that has just one back surgery.” Kevin Nash made his professional wrestling debut in 1990 and got signed by the global juggernaut, WWE, in 1993. He debuted under the name Diesel as Shawn Michaels’ bodyguard and then went on to become a top singles star, winning multiple titles including the WWE Championship. He and Scott Hall left WWE to join rival promotion, WCW, in 1996, where they formed the infamous faction, nWo, alongside Hulk Hogan.

title: Amazing Red Signs With TNA After X-Division Title Win
raw_title: Amazing Red Signs With TNA After X-Division Title Win
summary_src: Amazing Red’s wild TNA comeback isn’t stopping with the X-Division Championship. Just 10 days after walking into Bound For Glory as a Hall of Famer and walking out with the title, Red has reportedly signed with the company for another run.
body: According to PWInsider , Amazing Red has officially signed with TNA Wrestling and committed to the promotion. TNA hasn’t announced the deal publicly yet, but the report states that everything is done. “TNA Hall of Famer The Amazing Red, who won the X-Division Championship at Bound for Glory earlier this month, has officially signed with the promotion, PWInsiderElite.com can confirm. The promotion has yet to officially announce the deal, but we can confirm it is done and Red has committed to the promotion.” That’s a pretty big development considering Red’s Bound For Glory appearance initially looked like it could be a special one-night deal. He was there to be inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame, but during his speech, Red suddenly announced that he was entering the vacant X-Division Championship match later that night. Red didn’t just show up for the nostalgia pop either. He hit KC Navarro with the Code Red, got the three-count and became X-Division Champion for the fourth time in his career . The belt had been left vacant after Leon Slater exercised Option C to challenge Nic Nemeth for the TNA World Championship. Red’s surprise entry turned the originally planned six-man match into a seven-man scramble, and he ended up leaving with the championship. The whole thing was already a crazy full-circle moment for Red. Before Bound For Glory, he hadn’t held the X-Division Championship since September 25, 2010, putting more than 16 years between his previous reign and his latest one. Red has remained busy outside TNA as well, running House of Glory Wrestling in New York City alongside Brian XL. The 44-year-old has been part of the wrestling scene since the independent boom of the early 2000s, including the early days of Ring of Honor, while his TNA history also includes an NWA Tag Team Championship run with Jerry Lynn. So much for Bound For Glory being a nostalgia appearance. Amazing Red went from Hall of Fame inductee to champion in a matter of hours, and now he’s reportedly sticking around to see where this comeback goes next. body: Bandido reflects on his final conversation that he had with PAC and the fact they exchanged their respective football clubs shirts. It has been almost a month since the tragic passing of PAC, who was a staple of the AEW roster in recent years, as well as an important member of the Death Riders faction. PAC’s passing would come less than 24 hours after he would compete at AEW All Out and for one AEW roster member, he is hoping to keep PAC with him for as long as he can. While speaking to Jimmy V3 in a new interview , Bandido would be asked about PAC, recalling their final conversation and how they exchanged shirts of their football clubs. “Yeah, you know, PAC, he always was a very good person with me. I met him in Japan. We spent time together in Dragongate and he was a good person with me. The day before he passed away, we spent time (together). He gave me a Newcastle shirt. I gave him my home team shirt, which is Santos Laguna’s shirt, and he said, ‘thank you.’ The last thing that I can remember from him is, ‘I love you, brother,’ and I will have that words in my heart forever, forever. So I want to have him with me for as much time as is possible, you know?” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Bandido recalled his last conversation with PAC the day before the AEW star's passing. The two exchanged shirts from their favorite football clubs, Newcastle for PAC and Santos Laguna for Bandido. Bandido told Jimmy V3 that PAC's final words to him were "I love you, brother," which he will carry in his heart forever.

title: Gurv Sihra Updates Collapsed Lung Recovery

body: It sounds like Gurv Sihra should be back in the ring soon after suffering a scary injury last month. Formerly known as Sunil Singh in WWE, Sihra suffered a collapsed lung while competing at an indie show in Canada on September 19. It was a frightening experience that left Sihra feeling lucky to be alive. He did not immediately grasp the severity of the situation and finished the tag match he and his brother Harv were competing in. But when they got backstage, Gurv couldn’t get to his feet and was still struggling to breathe. He was taken to the hospital and treated for a collapsed lung. Gurv posted a new update last night saying his lungs are now back to normal. He still isn’t able to fly but expects to be cleared soon. “The road to recovery continues,” Gurv wrote. “X-Rays show my lungs are back to normal & there is very little air bubbles left in my chest-cavity from the collapsed lung. I still can’t fly at the moment, however, I should be cleared soon. Thank you all for your continued love & support.” Gurv and his brother Harv team together as The Bollywood Boyz on the indies and are best known for the time they spent in WWE as allies of Jinder Mahal. They debuted for WWE in the Cruiserweight Classic in 2016 and appeared on NXT, 205 Live, and the main roster before being released in 2021. The match where Gurv suffered this collapsed lung took place for Pure Power Wrestling in Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada. The Bollywood Boyz defeated Shaun Martens & Sydney Steele to win Pure Power’s Tag Team titles. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

title: In Memoriam: AEW wrestler Pac’s death exposes pro wrestling’s labor problem
raw_title: AEW wrestler Pac’s death exposes pro wrestling’s labor problem
body: Save Few things are more difficult to get down in immutable ink than the history of professional wrestling . Born on the carnival circuit, the pseudo-sport maintained a here today-gone tomorrow feeling until relatively recently. Promoters scraped out regional fiefdoms where transient performers would fight for a spell before jumping ship in search of better deals. Sometimes they took their name with them; other times they molded themselves to whatever gimmick their new promoter needed on the roster. It makes a mess of any timeline, and that’s before you get to the kayfabe — the illusion — of it all, the fact that all these real men and women are deadly serious about keeping up their fake characters. Gorgeous George, one of the most famous faces of wrestling’s Golden Age, didn’t make it to his 50th birthday. “Macho Man” Randy Savage and his ex-wife/manager Miss Elizabeth both died before reaching Social Security eligibility. High-flying technical wrestler Eddie Guerrero died at 38. Windham Rotunda, who freaked out the WWE for years as a swamp-dwelling cultist named Bray Wyatt, passed away at the age of 36. And earlier this week, All Elite Wrestling star Pac died in the parking lot of an Illinois chain restaurant, just a day after his most recent match. HIs cause of death is still unknown. Born Benjamin Satterley in a blue-collar community in Newcastle upon Tyne, England, he first came to national attention stateside in the WWE, where he wrestled under the decidedly English name Neville. He took the cruiserweight title twice before jumping for AEW in 2018. His star rose exponentially as a regular heel for the young promotion. At the time of his passing, he was only 40 years old. Playing a fake brute who’s willing to take a folding chair to the face to settle a disagreement is hell on a body. Learning how to fall and pretending you have superpowers can’t cancel out physics. If a 240-pound man turns you upside down and drives your head into a padded floor, you’re going to feel it the next day (and probably several days after). The wear and tear is cumulative, adding up over time like it does for all contact sports. Just take a boxer’s blown-out ears and a running back’s trick knee and expand it to account for the fact that, in wrestling, shots to the back of the skull are frequently necessary to move the story along. Recruiting almost exclusively among the huge and jacked — it’s easier to appear larger-than-life on camera if you’re real-world large — makes the list of heart conditions start to pile up. It’s all a recipe for a brief career, and a correspondingly short life. The average star of WWE or AEW signs on as an independent contractor, meaning they are responsible for their own health insurance and are subject to being fired for nearly any cause. The situation is exacerbated by wrestling’s employer-employee relationship. Staying true to its seasonal carny roots, almost all professional wrestlers are gig workers. title: Syko Stu Details Year-Long Recovery From Raja Jackson Assault
raw_title: Syko Stu opens up on recovery after Raja Jackson attack: ‘I was off work for an entire year’
summary_src: Syko Stu opened up on his recovery process after suffering an attack from Raja Jackson at a 2025 independent show.
body: Many in the wrestling world and beyond watched with disgust in 2025 after footage surfaced of streamer Raja Jackson, son of ex-UFC star Rampage Jackson, brutally attacking independent professional wrestler Syko Stu. The attack, live-streamed on Kick from a KnokX Pro event in California last year, landed Jackson a 90-day prison sentence over a felony battery charge. The 26-year-old, who paid $81,000 in restitution to Stu and is serving a two-year probationary period, finished his prison sentence over the summer. A year removed from the disturbing incident, Stu continues to battle with the effects of the attack. Among the injuries due to the flurry of punches he took were a shattered maxilla, numerous broken teeth and a severe traumatic brain injury. Stu believes his short-term memory has been significantly affected by the head injury: “My wife, she’ll tell me something, then five minutes later I’ll forget it,” he said. After the incident, Stu recalled being in the hospital for five days. He was only released once he was able to pass a series of tests, including showing that he could walk. Stu hasn’t wrestled since suffering his injuries in 2025. He said that one of his bigger concerns with performing again is less about his physical state, and more about whether his changed mental state could make it harder to put together matches. “It’s all psychology,” Stu said about wrestling. “You’re telling the story, but you’re telling it with your body. You still need the same psychology to put it together to make the match make sense.” When asked if he plans to wrestle again, Stu seemed inclined to eventually return. “My doctors tell me I shouldn’t,” he said. “But, you know, it’s one of those things. You have a love for something so much you really want to find any way that you can make it happen. Whether it’s gonna happen or not still remains to be seen.”

Jackson received a 90-day prison sentence for felony battery, paid $81,000 in restitution and is on two-year probation. Stu was hospitalized for five days, has seen his short-term memory impacted and was off work for a full year as he continues to deal with the aftermath.

llm_long: At a KnokX Pro event on August 23 2025, Raja Jackson knocked independent wrestler Syko Stu unconscious during a planned spot that escalated beyond the script.
Raja slammed Stu and then delivered more than 20 unanswered legitimate strikes to his head until independent wrestler Doug Malo intervened and pulled him away.
Syko Stu has limited memory of the incident itself. He recalled Raja filming backstage, which is unusual, and remembered calling a finish that involved one wrestling punch after a beer can spot.

Stu stated he was unconscious from the initial slam and has no recollection of the following events. He woke up in the hospital on Tuesday after being admitted on Saturday and remained in and out of consciousness until then.
During his hospital stay, medical staff would not show him video of the incident or discuss it. Wrestler Rikishi visited him there as he began to recover.

Stu was discharged from the hospital on Thursday. He now participates in word exercises during rehabilitation but continues to experience short-term memory issues such as forgetting things within minutes, repeating actions, and failing to recall names and faces.

title: Dave Meltzer: WWE Gets $150M For Riyadh WrestleMania
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Reveals Compensation WWE Will Receive For Holding WrestleMania In Riyadh
summary_src: Dave Meltzer has learned the amount WWE is set to be paid by the Saudi Arabian government for holding WrestleMania 43 in Riyadh next year.
body: "It looks like the WrestleMania price is $150 million," he said. "I knew it was over $100 [million] because people in Saudi Arabia told me it's north of $100 million. Usually, they get $55 [million] to go. ... [They] don't want to put that in jeopardy." Meltzer reaffirmed his understanding that there are "contingency plans" in place, just in case WWE is not able to make the date in Riyadh. Currently, the United States government has issued a Level 3 travel advisory, encouraging U.S. citizens against traveling to the country. If the government were to raise that advisory to Level 4, it would prevent WWE from holding Crown Jewel in Riyadh. Meltzer believes that would act as a "bail-out" for the company, as the decision would be out of WWE's hands and there'd be no risk of insulting Turki Al-Sheikh, the chairman of the country's General Entertainment Authority. In recent weeks, Al-Sheikh made a post on X regarding the upcoming Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli boxing match, stating that the fight was still on and the current situation in Saudi Arabia would reveal the country's "true friends." Meltzer interpreted the post as a message to WWE along with other companies, with the subtext being that they would not respond kindly to any organization canceling planned events in Saudi Arabia.

He noted the promotion normally receives $55 million for Saudi Arabia events and does not want to risk that relationship. Meltzer added that contingency plans exist if WWE cannot make the date, with a potential U.S. government Level 4 travel advisory serving as a way out that would not offend Turki Al-Sheikh.

body: Ilja Dragunov makes his AEW debut against “Speedball” Mike Bailey. You can catch AEW Dynamite LIVE at 8pm ET/5pm PT on TSN2, TSN.ca and the TSN App. “The Mad Dragon” has arrived in All Elite Wrestling. Ilja Dragunov was the man behind the metronome vignettes and made his first appearance in the company this past Saturday night’s WrestleDream pay-per-view. On Wednesday night, the Moscow native makes his in-ring debut against a man he’s met once before in the United Empire’s “Speedball” Mike Bailey. For the uninitiated, Dragunov is one of the most intense competitors currently in the industry. Born in Russia and raised in Germany, Dragunov first made his name in one of Europe’s top promotions, Westside Xtreme Wrestling (wXw). Among those he did battle with were WALTER (now WWE’s Gunther), the late John “Bad Bones” Klinger and Tommy End (former AEW performer Malakai Black). He became the company’s first Triple Crown champion, winning wXW’s Unified World Wrestling Championship, Shotgun Championship and World Tag Team Championships. Dragunov left Germany for England and WWE NXT UK where he restarted his rivalry with WALTER, who he defeated for the NXT UK Championship, and took on the likes of Chris Hero and Pete Dunne. Relocating to the United States, Dragunov took NXT by storm, facing off with Donovan Dijak and Trick Williams before defeating Carmelo Hayes for the NXT Championship. Moving to the WWE main roster, Dragunov made an early splash with wins over former IWGP World Champion Shinsuke Nakamura and Ricochet before defeating current WWE Champion Sami Zayn for the United States Championship last October. He kept the title for two months, defending it against Johnny Gargano and Tommaso Ciampa among others, before dropping it to old rival Hayes. Choosing to depart WWE at the expiration of his contract, Dragunov immediately jumped into the deep end in AEW with a debut match against Bailey. It will be the first time the two have met in a decade. Much has changed since then. One of wXw’s calling cards is its annual 16 Carat Gold Tournament, a single-elimination tournament normally held over three days in the spring. A yearly tradition since 2006, the tournament counts Shingo Takagi, Zack Sabre Jr., Zayn (as El Generico) and Dragunov himself in 2017 among its winners. Some of the biggest stars in the industry have participated in the event, including the late PAC and current and former world champions Will Ospreay, Seth Rollins (as Tyler Black), Eddie Kingston, Adam Cole, Drew McIntyre (as Drew Galloway) and Cody Rhodes. The 2016 edition was won by ZSJ, but it’s the first round of that tournament that is of particular interest. On March 11 in Oberhausen, Dragunov went one-on-one with Bailey. title: Comeback Watch: Drew McIntyre Busts Out New Move While Training for WWE Return
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Busts Out New Move While Training for WWE Return
summary_src: Drew McIntyre wasn’t kidding when he said his WWE return would come with some new moves. The former WWE Champion just climbed to the top rope during training and busted out a flying arm drag while continuing to prepare for his eventual in-ring comeback.
body: McIntyre showed off the unexpected move in an Instagram post on October 21 . The 285-pounder went up top before launching himself into the flying arm drag, then popped back up and yelled “Olé!” to celebrate pulling it off. Drew clearly enjoyed proving he still has a few tricks hiding in his moveset. He joked about suddenly going full lucha while tagging Chivas in the post. The timing makes the clip even more interesting because McIntyre recently teased that his moveset could look noticeably different whenever he finally wrestles again. During an interview with Chris Van Vliet on INSIGHT , Drew revealed that his time away from WWE has allowed him to rebuild his body and work heavily on his balance, agility and conditioning . “I’ve been working real hard in a way that my cardio and agility is, I’d say my whole life, but really for sure the past 12 years, is right now the best I’ve been. Like I feel great agility-wise. Bigger than I’ve ever been. I’m moving better than I have.” McIntyre currently weighs around 285 pounds, but the extra size apparently hasn’t slowed him down. He previously said old highlight videos had reminded him of moves he’d completely forgotten he used to perform, and that got him thinking about bringing some of them back. “I’ve got a feeling some of my offense is going to be unique. I saw some videos of myself people had sent me, were highlight videos, and I was like, I didn’t realize I did that. Guess I’m going to start stealing for myself.” Drew went even further by claiming he can now perform some of those old moves more easily than he could during his 20s. Considering what he just pulled off from the top rope, he appears pretty serious about testing that theory. “Forgot I did half the moves, and I physically can do them easily now and probably better than I did them when I was in my 20s.” Of course, nobody should expect McIntyre to suddenly turn into a full-time high-flyer. When Van Vliet previously asked whether fans should expect some new additions to his offense, Drew gave a pretty simple description of what he has planned. McIntyre hasn’t wrestled for WWE since WrestleMania 42, and he’s been taking his time before getting back into the ring. He previously told fans asking about his return to give him “a little second,” making it clear that he’ll come back when he decides the time is right. The latest training footage doesn’t give fans a return date, but it does show exactly what McIntyre has been talking about. If a 285-pound Drew is now climbing to the top rope and throwing flying arm drags while promising new offense, his eventual WWE comeback could look a little different from the version fans last saw. title: Results Recap: WWE enters the online casino market but has no intention of becoming an operatorWWE, the world's largest wrestling promotion, continues to convert its intellectual property into revenue streams beyond the ring. Online casino games have emerged as a new avenue, one the company is pursuing exclusively through brand and content licensing to third-party developers. WWE itself takes on no gambling operator functions, keeping its focus on what it does best: creating characters, storylines, and spectacular shows. The strategy revolves around the promotion's most recognizable assets. WWE Superstars, marquee events, and weekly programs serve as the raw material that partners transform into gaming products for the US market. WWE, in turn, collects licensing fees without investing in technology development or taking on the regulatory risks of the gambling business. Who WWE is launching gaming projects with and on what terms The timeline of partnerships shows that WWE is building an entire network of licensing agreements covering different segments of the gaming market. In July 2025, the company signed an exclusive multi-year agreement with Fanatics Betting and Gaming. Under the terms of the deal, Fanatics takes full responsibility for the production and distribution of WWE-themed online casino games in the United States. In January 2026, VGW joined the list of partners, receiving rights to use the brand across its portfolio of online social games. The agreement with VGW includes access to WWE Superstars' likenesses, the promotion's digital channels, and its flagship programs, including SmackDown, WrestleMania, and SummerSlam. In parallel, the WWE and Fanatics partnership has expanded well beyond the casino segment. As early as 2025, the companies extended their collaboration to merchandising, digital content, and fan engagement activities. A telling example was the inclusion of Logan Paul's IMPAULSIVE in a joint digital content network. In essence, WWE is building an ecosystem in which the brand meets audiences at a wide variety of touchpoints — from podcasts and merchandise to slots. From a logo on a slot to full-scale storytelling within the game The first set of products released under the Fanatics deal already included several titles with distinctive names: WWE Blackjack Raw Multiplier Melee SmackDown Big Money Entrance other branded games from the launch portfolio The most ambitious release, however, was the slot WrestleMania: Road to Gold, launched in March 2026 through Fanatics Casino in partnership with White Hat Studios. The game features 20 WWE Superstars, and the promotion's key events are embedded directly into the mechanics and progression structure: SummerSlam Survivor Series Royal Rumble Elimination Chamber Money in the Bank This is the key distinction between basic branding and what WWE brings to the table. In a typical licensed slot, the brand serves as a visual wrapper: a familiar logo, thematic colors, a couple of recognizable symbols on the reels. In WrestleMania: Road to Gold, the promotion's narrative logic is transplanted into the game itself. Major events define the stages of progression, and WWE Superstars function not as decoration but as the substantive core of the gameplay experience. This approach gives partners significantly more material to work with and turns each product into something greater than just another licensed slot. Why WWE does not need its own casino or sportsbook The logic of the business model is entirely transparent. For WWE, the primary value lies in monetizing intellectual property and expanding its digital ecosystem, not in managing gambling infrastructure. Both sides benefit: WWE maintains its focus on characters, storylines, and audience engagement while generating additional licensing revenue with no operational costs related to development or distribution Partners gain a recognizable brand backed by decades of accumulated loyalty — a critical advantage for standing out in the crowded online casino market The promotion's rights and recognizable properties remain the central asset in this arrangement. WWE Superstars such as Cody Rhodes and Rhea Ripley already possess well-established identities in the eyes of audiences. WrestleMania and SummerSlam have long since become globally recognized entertainment brands. And the weekly shows provide a continuous stream of new stories, rivalries, and characters that shows no sign of running dry year after year. WWE's deals fit into a broader trend. Online casino operators are looking for ways to reach audiences that previously had no interest in gambling. The standard toolkit is well known: welcome deposit bonuses, free spins, cashback, loyalty programs, and no deposit bonuses at online casinos, which allow players to try games without risking their own money. These mechanics still reliably attract new players, but competing on them alone is becoming increasingly difficult, as nearly every platform offers similar promotions. As a result, operators are increasingly betting on emotional brand connections, and a partnership with a wrestling promotion delivers exactly that kind of tool. A WWE fan comes not for the bonus, but for the beloved characters and storylines that have long been part of their leisure time. The bottom line comes down to three elements. WWE monetizes its intellectual property through licensing. Development, the technology platform, and distribution are handled entirely by partners. And the gaming products use the promotion's characters and events not as a visual layer, but as the substantive foundation on which the entire user experience is built.

The similarities become less obvious once the action begins. WWE performers train for physically demanding, choreographed contests, while boxers must respond to opponents genuinely trying to defeat them. Strength, timing, and confidence can help in both disciplines, but success in one doesn't guarantee success in the other. Their heavily publicized encounter ended in the sixth round when Danis was disqualified following illegal grappling attempts. Paul had controlled much of the contest with his jab, but the chaotic ending overshadowed his performance. title: Nile Remains Active on WWE Roster
raw_title: Another Star May Have Re-Signed With WWE
body: According to Fightful Select , Nile's contract was due to expire at the beginning of October. However, she is still listed as an active talent on WWE's roster page, and she appeared on the October 6 episode of NXT in a battle royal to determine the number one contender for the NXT Women's Championship. That match was won by Wren Sinclair, who was impersonating Lady Shani. Her NXT appearance came after a long stretch away from WWE's main shows. Nile has been off Raw since March, and she has wrestled only two matches on the show this year. Most of her work in 2026 has come on WWE Main Event, where she has wrestled 12 times, including matches against NXT talent such as Thea Hail, Wendy Choo and Lizzy Rain. Fightful Select reported in early September that Nile's contract was set to expire soon and that it had not heard whether she had negotiated a new deal. The same report said WWE had plans for her and that creative had a "big change" in store. Fightful Select later reported that the change was a tag team with Jordynne Grace. According to Fightful, vignettes pairing the two were filmed over the summer, with the hope that they would air in September, and its sources linked the team to the WWE trademark "Iron Built." The vignettes never aired. In May 2025, she won the tournament to become number one contender for the WWE Women's Speed Championship but lost to Sol Ruca in the title match. Grace has also been off television, and a WrestleVotes report said WWE does not have her in its creative plans at the moment, while adding that she is not on her way out. Nile still being on the roster is a good sign that the company sees value in her, even after a year in which she was barely used on Raw. Her name staying on the roster page and her appearance on NXT television right after her contract was due to expire both point to her still being under contract, and they suggest the company wants her visible again. The Grace team is still the best path for her. Both women have strength-based styles and are competing in bodybuilding, the vignettes are already filmed, and the women's tag team division needs new challengers. Tatum Paxley holding the tag titles with Alexa Bliss also gives Nile a built-in story against her former partner. The concern is that WWE has had this plan ready since the summer and still has not pulled the trigger. If Nile did sign a new deal, the company should use it as a reason to finally air those vignettes and give both women something to do on television. body: NJPW Tanahashi Jam 2 to Feature Stars from NOAH, DDT and More 4 hours ago Image Credit: New Japan Pro Wrestling Image Credit: New Japan Pro Wrestling NJPW have announced the first matches for the upcoming Tanahashi Jam 2. They will face the trio of Hartley Jackson, Ryohei Oiwa and Pro Wrestling NOAH’s Kaito Kiyomiya. On the opposite side, . Oiwa and Kiyomiya have a strong connection, with Kiyomiya having a strong influence on Oiwa’s time in NOAH. title: Chad Gable Builds Strong Intercontinental Title Run
raw_title: Chad Gable Is Quietly Having a Huge Title Run
body: Gable won the title from Penta on night two of SummerSlam on August 2 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Wrestling in front of his home state crowd, Gable reversed a second Mexican Destroyer attempt into the Ankle Lock and made Penta tap out. It was the first Intercontinental Championship win of his career. He earned that title shot the hard way. On the July 13 episode of Raw in Dallas, Gable won a number one contender's gauntlet match that lasted more than 38 minutes, getting past Dominik Mysterio, Dragon Lee, Ethan Page, Je'Von Evans, Joe Hendry and Rusev. Since winning the title, Gable has defended it four times on Raw, which works out to a televised title match every 20 days. He beat Rey Mysterio on the August 17 episode in Buffalo, Dragon Lee on the September 14 episode in Mexico City and Rey Fenix on the October 12 episode in Bossier City, Louisiana. Most recently, he retained in a triple threat against Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio on the October 19 episode in San Diego. Those were not short matches either. According to Cagematch , the Fenix match ran 18 minutes and 35 seconds, the first Dragon Lee match went 15 minutes and 39 seconds, and the triple threat lasted 15 minutes and 35 seconds. The Mysterio match on August 17 went just over 13 minutes. The televised defenses are only part of the picture. Cagematch lists 13 more successful defenses at live events since SummerSlam, bringing his total to 17 without a loss. He defended against Ethan Page several times on WWE's summer tour, beat Dominik Mysterio in both a singles match and a triple threat in Canada, and won four straight fatal four-way matches against Dragon Lee, Ethan Page and Penta on the South America tour in September. He also defended the title at two NXT live events in the Carolinas against Saquon Shugars and Uriah Connors, and won a three-way against Ethan Page and Je'Von Evans in Honolulu on October 16. The run is also the payoff to a long chase. Gable came up short against Sami Zayn in multiple Intercontinental Championship matches in 2024, including a match at Clash at the Castle in June that year that lasted more than 22 minutes. Two years later, he finally got the title in his home state. Gable's reign is a throwback to the way a midcard title is supposed to be booked. He is defending the championship on television on a regular basis, he is doing it against a mix of veterans and younger stars, and the matches are getting real time on Raw. Four televised defenses in 80 days is a steady pace for a secondary title, and the live event defenses show he is putting the belt on the line nearly every time he works. It also matters who he is beating. Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee and Rey Fenix are some of the best workers on Raw, and Gable's style matches up well with each of them. Those matches have made the Intercontinental Championship feel like one of the more important parts of the show, which is what a strong champion should do. Gable has since defended the title four times on Raw, including victories over Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee, Rey Fenix and a triple threat retention against Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio.

title: On the Record: Swerve Strickland Explains Why WWE and AEW Will Never Hold a Crossover Event
raw_title: Swerve Strickland Explains Why WWE and AEW Will Never Hold a Crossover Event
summary_src: Swerve Strickland doesn’t see WWE and AEW ever putting their differences aside for a massive crossover show. In fact, he doesn’t believe it’ll happen in his lifetime because there are simply too many top stars both companies would want to protect.
body: Speaking to Billboard , Swerve was directly asked whether he could ever see WWE and AEW working together for a cross-promotional event. He didn’t dance around the question and immediately shut down the idea. For Swerve Strickland, the biggest obstacle isn’t whether the wrestlers would want to do it. He believes it all comes down to control, marketing and WWE protecting the stars it has spent years building. “It’s control. It’s all about marketing. It’s like the NFL, WWE has to protect their shield. There’s no way they’d allow any of our wrestlers to look better and be better [than them].” Swerve pointed to Oba Femi as a perfect example. WWE has positioned him as a dominant force, so Swerve doesn’t believe the company would suddenly put him into a crossover situation where that presentation could be compromised. “Obi Femi is a world beater. You gotta protect that and make sure he keeps looking good. Gunther, have to protect that. Roman [Reigns], have to protect that. Cody [Rhodes], have to protect, even more so because of AEW. There’s a lot of that happening.” Cody’s situation would obviously bring another wrinkle considering his history with AEW before returning to WWE. Swerve believes those kinds of factors would make figuring out winners and losers a political headache before the wrestlers even got into the ring. “You wanna see Seth [Rollins] and Ospreay. That’s the generational thing, but who do you protect? Who has the leverage?” The funny part is that Swerve says the wrestlers themselves aren’t nearly as concerned about any of that. He revealed that he’s good friends with Carmelo Hayes, Je’Von Evans and Oba Femi and would happily work with them without caring who actually got their hand raised. “Us in the locker room, we just wanna have these matches. I’m good friends with Carmelo [Hayes], Jevon [Evans] and Oba. Those are my boys. I love those guys. I don’t care who wins. Double DQs. I don’t care.” So while the locker rooms might be willing to make something happen, Swerve believes the business side makes a WWE-AEW supershow nearly impossible. There are plenty of dream matches waiting on paper, but getting two competing promotions to agree on who gets protected could be a much bigger fight than anything happening inside the ring. title: By the Numbers: Swerve Strickland Questions the Credibility of Five-Star Wrestling Match Ratings
raw_title: Swerve Strickland Questions the Credibility of Five-Star Wrestling Match Ratings
summary_src: Swerve Strickland isn’t losing any sleep over those Wrestling Observer five-star ratings. In fact, the AEW star thinks some of those supposed five-star classics might be closer to four stars once you step outside the Observer bubble.
body: Speaking to Billboard , Swerve was talking about balancing wrestling with his career in hip-hop when he got an interesting question. What’s harder — putting on a five-star wrestling match or creating a five-mic album? Swerve didn’t even hesitate. He knows both ratings are completely subjective. What sounds like a perfect album to one person might only be a four or four-and-a-half to somebody else, and Swerve thinks wrestling ratings work exactly the same way. “Both parts are subjective, ’cause five mics for one person might be four-and-a-half or four to other people.” Then came the Wrestling Observer shot. Swerve casually joked that some of those five-star matches might lose a star once you ask somebody outside the publication. “Five-star match to Wrestling Observer were more like four [star] to anybody else.” Swerve wasn’t just trying to get a cheap shot in either. His bigger point was that creating an album capable of winning over hardcore fans, casual listeners, critics and people who weren’t already interested in you is incredibly difficult. That’s also why Swerve puts so much weight behind the five-mic label. For him, a real classic can’t just be hot when it drops — people still need to be talking about it years later. “To me, a five-mic album stands the test of time. There’s all-time great lyricists that haven’t been able to pull that off and I’m not even at that level as a pure lyricist.” Swerve knows that puts the bar ridiculously high, and he’s not pretending he’s already reached it himself. He believes genuine classics are rare for a reason. So Swerve isn’t exactly buying the idea that every five-star wrestling match should automatically be treated like an untouchable classic. Ratings are subjective, but when it comes to creating something that can survive years of changing tastes, he’s putting a five-mic album above anything the Wrestling Observer can hand out. Red was inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame during the Bound for Glory 2026 pre-show and then entered the Ultimate X match for the vacant title later that night. Leon Slater, who is now the TNA World Champion, chose to give up the X-Division title as he exercised “Option C” for a shot at the World Championship. This run is Red’s first time back in TNA since 2011. He is a founder of indie promotion House of Glory, where he competes in the ring and operates the HOG training school. Earlier this week, TNA confirmed the signing of Shotzi Blackheart and re-signing of Director of Authority Santino Marella . There is expected to be more contract news coming over the next several weeks as TNA addresses its wrestlers who have deals coming up before the end of the year. title: Ex-UFC fighter Michael ‘Venom’ Page says MMA fighters need to form union: ‘We have to move as one’
raw_title: Ex-UFC fighter Michael ‘Venom’ Page says MMA fighters need to form union: ‘We have to move as one’
summary_src: Former UFC fighter Michael "Venom" Page believes fighters should form a union to help get better treatment.
body: Michael “Venom” Page believes a fighters’ union might be needed to help improve treatment for competitors in MMA. MVP signed to the UFC roster in 2024, joining after a lengthy Bellator run which saw him put together an impressive compilation of knockout wins. Now out of the UFC, Page told BBC Sport he wants to encourage fighters to form an alliance in MMA for better benefits. “It’s less about speaking out now, it’s more about forming a union and coming together,” he told BBC. “We have to move as one … If all fighters said ‘we’re not gonna do it’, then UFC doesn’t exist. That’s the important thing for fighters to remember. It’s not just the machine of UFC, you guys are the nuts and bolts that help the machine move.” Page said that frustration around fighter pay is an issue you often don’t hear from the competitors themselves, as they fear backlash from promoters. UFC, which is currently in the first year of a seven-year, $7.7 billion deal to stream on Paramount+ in America, has long been accused of underpaying athletes. The company agreed to a settlement worth $375 million in 2024 for a class action lawsuit alleging that the company had engaged in antitrust behavior to keep the pay of its fighters low. Former UFC Middleweight Champion Sean Strickland recently expressed frustration over the company’s pay structure, teasing that he might even want to leave the brand soon. “[Conor] McGregor makes 30 million to fight for 30 second and they don’t want to pay us a fraction of it,” he wrote on X. “Contemplating just going to 205 [pounds] knocking out my contract then scrapping with Jake Paul. That sounds fun.” UFC CEO Dana White downplayed Strickland’s complaints, denying the claims that Strickland had made about pay. “When isn’t Sean upset about something?” he said at a press conference.

B finished second with 36 percent of the vote. -28 percent of our voters gave the best match of the show honors to “The Young Bucks” Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight for the AEW Tag Team Titles. Will Ospreay vs. Samoa Joe vs. Mike Bailey vs. Adam Copeland vs. Konosuke Takeshita vs. Kazuchika Okada vs. Ricochet vs. Darby Allin in a Clockwork Carnage match for the AEW World Championship finished a close second with 24 percent of the vote. Powell’s POV: Jake Barnett gave the show a B grade, and I gave it a B during our same-night audio review. Our readers also voted an AEW Tag Team Title match (Brody King and Bandido vs. Kazuchika Okada and Konosuke Takeshita) as the best match of the 2025 WrestleDream event. Last year’s WrestleDream received a B grade from 29 percent of our voters. The 2024 WrestleDream finished with an A from 35 percent of the vote. The 2023 received an A grade from 61 percent of the voters. Thanks to everyone who took the time to vote in the polls.
summary: 42 percent of voters awarded an A grade to the 2025 AEW WrestleDream pay-per-view while 36 percent gave it a B. The Young Bucks versus Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight received 28 percent of the vote for best match with the eight-man Clockwork Carnage bout for the AEW World Championship finishing second at 24 percent. Editor Jason Powell and Jake Barnett both scored the event a B in their review.

title: WWE Faces Pressure Over Saudi Crown Jewel Amid Attacks
raw_title: As missiles rain down on Riyadh, WWE's Crown Jewel dilemma is becoming unavoidable
body: That the Saudi security situation has deteriorated in the weeks after this year's Crown Jewel was first announced on Sept. 1 is an understatement. Since then, we've seen the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen launch a barrage of missile attacks on Riyadh airport , claiming the lives of at least 20 people and injuring at least 370 in what is already the deadliest attack on Saudi soil in more than a decade. Right now, WWE is insisting that the show will go ahead — a decision that flies in the face of what other businesses and sports events are doing. Just this week, we've seen a bunch of major events in Riyadh postponed, including Saudi Arabia's annual Davos in the Desert, as well as the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and Saudi International golf tournament. Why is WWE plowing ahead with Crown Jewel when others are playing it safe? As ever, money talks. Anyone who has spent five minutes following TKO's financials knows how important the Saudis are for WWE — in recent years, they've contributed around one quarter of the company's live-event revenues. The average Saudi show brings in more money than this year's WrestleMania. All of which brings us to Turki Alashikh, the man who controls the Saudi purse strings. Perhaps the most intriguing twist in this whole Crown Jewel saga is the reports that WWE insiders are worried that Alashikh's glazing of Saul "Canelo" Alvarez — who is set to fight in Riyadh on Oct. 31 – on social media is a preemptive dig at those in TKO towers. Would the country really pull the plug on SaudiMania if WWE canceled Crown Jewel? All common sense would suggest not. But that's the problem with relying on one source for such a hefty chunk of your revenue — you can't really afford to call their bluff. On the other hand, it's not like the other course of action is safe either, with the risk of missiles raining down on Riyadh airport. So what's a TKO executive to do? If it's so dangerous, you might ask, why is "Canelo" fighting there on Halloween? Well, you'd probably have to ask him. Which is sort of the point: "Canelo" is one man who can make his own decision whether to go to Riyadh to collect his purse or not. (He's also a man who gets punched for a living, so he probably has a different outlook on risk than your typical Wall Street suit.) More seriously, "Canelo" isn't a corporate entity like TKO. He doesn't have to take a whole production crew, or send dozens of supporting talent on commercial jets into Riyadh airport. He doesn't have to justify the fallout to shareholders should the proverbial mess really hit the fan. He's never going to be dragged in front of Congress like the bosses of Enron and Facebook when they faced scandals. In that situation, I don't doubt they could weather the storm in the long run. But the more pertinent question would be, why they didn't see the dark clouds on the horizon beforehand? If you're going to jump into bed with an absolute monarchy in one of the world's most unstable regions, can you real
summary: Missile strikes by Houthi rebels on Riyadh have killed at least 20 people and injured over 370 since WWE announced this year's Crown Jewel event. Multiple major business and sports gatherings in the city have been postponed for safety reasons while WWE maintains the show will proceed. The promotion's decision is driven by the significant financial contribution from Saudi events which account for roughly one quarter of its live event revenue per TKO financials.

title: Ilja Dragunov On Whether He Reached Out to Other Promotions Apart from AEW Following WWE Exit, When He Signed With AEW & More
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov On Whether He Reached Out to Other Promotions Apart from AEW Following WWE Exit, When He Signed With AEW & More
body: As noted , Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at WrestleDream this past Saturday. Dragunov appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show on Tuesday to discuss his WWE departure, his decision to join All Elite Wrestling, and more. During the conversation, Helwani asked Ilja whether he reached out to other promotions apart from AEW following his WWE exit. Dragunov also revealed exactly when he signed with the Tony Khan-led company, reasons behind his delayed arrival, and more. On whether he reached out to other promotions apart from AEW? “If I got to be honest, like, everything went down so fast. Everything I did was just giving myself a rest. That’s pretty much what I did for the most part. But then when things click, they click very fast.” “I think it possibly has been just like a minor time after my contract expired. It was an easygoing expiration.” “Because of exactly that [visa issues], because I’m a German citizen and I need to have a visa to work in the states.” “Oh, for sure! Everybody who knows me—my best friends, my family, and the love of my life, they all know that the only thing I’m absolutely terrible at is sitting here right now; it drives me crazy because I want to move and do things, and yeah, I literally couldn’t wait, and when this beautiful day on Saturday approached, it was an absolute relief for me to let it all out. And yeah, upcoming, like, tomorrow, on Wednesday, on Dynamite, it’s going to be the next relief when I’m going to finally debut and can finally have the option to fight again and express my art.” Dragunov will make his AEW in-ring debut against “Speedball” Mike Bailey on tonight’s Dynamite .

McMahon was driving at approximately 115 mph when he attempted to overtake another vehicle. He crashed into the back of that vehicle and then hit a median with his Bentley.

Every time Ilja Dragonuv wasn't utilized by World Wrestling Entertainment, the online discourse was the same - where is he? Why isn't he being utilized? Why isn't be on TV? Why isn't he getting pushed? The Russian-born German star, 33, has been beloved for his unhinged intensity, stiff striking, and emotionally charged physical storytelling for as long as he's been performing. The "Unbesiegbar" (Unbeatable) Mad Dragon, Dragunov gained international acclaim before signing with WWE, where captured the WWE NXT UK Championship by ending GUNTHER's insane 870-day reign with an instant classic. He moved to the United States, where he held the WWE NXT title and eventually, the main roster, where he won the WWE United States Championship. Recognized for his intense in-ring style, marked by his signature Torpedo Moskva flying headbutt and H-Bomb forearm strike, Dragonuv excels at believable, hard-hitting encounters and dramatic, resilient selling that position him as one of the most physical performers in modern professional wrestling. He was the exact style of performer that Paul Levesque's NXT popularized themselves utilizing, so it was was unthinkable that under Levesque's creative direction that Dragonuv wouldn't be a massive part of WWE, yet it didn't truly happen. An ACL tear hobbed his momentum for sure, but his return was well received, as was his U.S. title run. However, once 2026 began, other than being unceremoniously tossed from The Royal Rumble by Brock Lesnar, there was nothing truly memorable for Ilja creatively and then, he chose to exit the company. The outpouring of shock and anger over the exit was palpable, to the point I even received emailed accusing me of lying when PWInsider.com broke the news of his exit. No matter how you feel about Dragonuv's run in WWE, the one constant was that die-hard wrestling fans loved his work and loudly complained online when he wasn't utilized in a stronger manner. If they truly believe WWE whiffed the ball on Dragonuv, those same fans will get the chance to see him step up to bat tonight for All Elite Wrestling on Dynamite.
