title: Vince Russo Goes Nuclear on Fans for Bastardizing the Term “Pop” in Wrestling
raw_title: Vince Russo Goes Nuclear on Fans for Bastardizing the Term “Pop” in Wrestling
summary_src: Vince Russo has had enough of wrestling fans calling every loud crowd reaction a “pop.” The former WWE writer went off on fans for what he believes is the completely wrong use of the term, and he gave a pretty wild explanation for where “pop” supposedly came from in the first place.
body: “Me talking about the damn use of the word ‘pop’ by the marks. So let me educate you guys to make you understand what a pop is. Because when Roman Reigns comes out, bro, that’s not a pop — it’s a reaction.” Russo said the way wrestlers traditionally used the term was completely different. In his telling, the entire idea was about deliberately building a match or storyline toward one huge reaction. “The origin of ‘pop’ and how that word was used within the boys — because the boys would say, ‘We build to the pop.’” That’s where Russo’s explanation took a very NSFW turn. He claimed the wrestling term came from the phrase “pop a nut,” comparing the structure of building toward a major wrestling reaction to building toward a sexual climax. “Okay, here’s where that came from. There’s a term that we use as men called ‘pop a nut.’ And ladies and gentlemen, what ‘pop a nut’ means is when you are having sex with a woman, okay? And you are saying, ‘I’m coming, I’m coming,’ and then you pop the nut — then you come.” Russo wasn’t finished with the comparison either. He argued that the key part is the buildup, because that’s what separates what he considers a real wrestling pop from an instantaneous crowd reaction. “So you’re building and building towards that moment of ejaculation, and then you pop the nut. That’s where the term ‘pop’ came from. You build towards the pop.” To give a wrestling example, Russo pointed toward the classic hot-tag formula. The babyface gets beaten down, repeatedly comes close to reaching their partner and finally makes the tag after several failed attempts, giving the crowd the payoff it has been waiting for. “You build — think about a hot tag. Think about back in the day, the babyface is in trouble, he’s getting his ass kicked, he goes to the corner, they pull him back. Finally, after three attempts — the hot tag, the house pops!” That’s Russo’s problem with fans using the same word for somebody simply receiving a huge entrance reaction. He insists a traditional “pop” needs to have something building toward it rather than happening the second someone’s music hits. “That is where it comes from, guys. That’s where the pop in wrestling comes from. You build towards the pop.” Russo then directly called out fans for what he sees as the term being thrown around incorrectly. As far as he’s concerned, entrances can get enormous reactions, but that still doesn’t make them pops under his definition. “What you guys are talking about are instantaneous reactions. That is not the definition of a pop in wrestling. An entrance is not a pop! That is a reaction.” He wrapped things up by asking fans to stop “bastardizing” the word. Russo also admitted he doesn’t know exactly when wrestling fans started using “pop” to describe entrance reactions in the first place. “A pop, like a climax, is built to — for the pop. So can we stop bastardizing that word and using a word that we have no freaking idea what the hell that word means? I don’t know when ‘pop
summary: Because when Roman Reigns comes out, bro, that’s not a pop — it’s a reaction. Russo explained the way wrestlers traditionally used the term was completely different. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin From WWE to Boxing: 4 Wrestlers Who Stepped Into the Ring By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-21 10:20:00 Professional wrestling and boxing share the same basic setting: two competitors, a ring, and an audience expecting a fight. The similarities become less obvious once the action begins. WWE performers train for physically demanding, choreographed contests, while boxers must respond to opponents genuinely trying to defeat them. Strength, timing, and confidence can help in both disciplines, but success in one doesn't guarantee success in the other. Several familiar WWE personalities have tested themselves in boxing or related combat sports. Their experiences range from impressive victories to painful reminders that fighting experience matters more than reputation. John Morrison built his wrestling reputation around remarkable athleticism. His acrobatic moves, agility, and impressive physical conditioning helped distinguish him during several WWE runs. His debut demonstrated that athleticism can transfer successfully when accompanied by appropriate preparation. One victory, however, doesn't establish how someone would perform against an experienced professional boxer. Logan Paul's relationship with boxing began before his WWE career. His fights against fellow internet personality KSI introduced him to competitive combat sports, while a 2021 exhibition against Floyd Mayweather attracted considerable attention. Paul subsequently became a recognizable WWE performer, combining his athletic ability with a talent for attracting audiences. In October 2023, he returned to boxing against mixed martial artist Dillon Danis in Manchester, England. Their heavily publicized encounter ended in the sixth round when Danis was disqualified following illegal grappling attempts. Paul had controlled much of the contest with his jab, but the chaotic ending overshadowed his performance. Security personnel entered the ring as tensions escalated between the fighters and their teams. Paul's unusual career reflects the growing overlap between sports entertainment and combat sports. His previous boxing experience also makes his transition different from that of wrestlers encountering competitive striking for the first time. Bart Gunn's boxing story began with WWE's controversial Brawl for All tournament in 1998. Unlike traditional wrestling matches, the competition involved genuine fighting under rules combining boxing and wrestling elements. title: Cody Rhodes Recalls Dusty Rhodes' Flying Colonel Status
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Recounts Learning That His Dad Dusty Rhodes Was A 'Flying Colonel'
summary_src: There are Cody lies and Dusty legends. Cody Rhodes recounted a Dusty Rhodes legend. Speaking to Jacob Heyman on The Roundtable, Cody explained how he found out that his father, Dusty, was a Flying Colonel.
body: There are Cody lies and Dusty legends. Cody Rhodes recounted a Dusty Rhodes legend. Speaking to Jacob Heyman on The Roundtable , Cody explained how he found out that his father, Dusty, was a Flying Colonel. “WWE, I used to be so mad at this, would fly my dad coach. Don’t ever put me in charge of WWE because of these legends; that ain’t happening. They used to fly my dad coach, and I wasn’t going to let that happen because I needed him to go to Sacramento to help me in angle with Rey Mysterio. A few weeks before that flight, we’re all sitting there, and my financial manager is talking to me, and my dad walked by. We’re talking airline status. [My financial manager] is telling me, ‘You’re at diamond again. Just keep spending on that Amex. My dad walked by, and my manager said, ‘Dusty, you have to have so many air miles. What is your status?’ He said, ‘Colonel. Flying Colonel.’ The Flying Colonel program was Delta Air Lines’ very first customer loyalty and recognition program, created originally in 1940. title: Results Recap: WWE’s Matt Cardona gives totally ‘biased’ review of Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes in Street Fighter
raw_title: WWE’s Matt Cardona gives totally ‘biased’ review of Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes in Street Fighter
body: Naturally, as a professional wrestler, WWE Superstar Matt Cardona loved seeing Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes in Street Fighter. He wrote a review of the video game movie on X, formerly Twitter. Cardona gave it glowing praise, but he knows that he is "biased." Rhodes and Reigns are part of the Street Fighter ensemble, which is led by Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji. The "American Nightmare" plays Guile, while the "Tribal Chief" plays Akuma. Street Fighter finished atop the domestic box office during its opening weekend, grossing $30.8 million domestically. It has made over $50 million worldwide to date. This is one of Rhodes' biggest movie roles. He previously appeared as a bartender in the Liam Neeson-led Naked Gun reboot in 2025. Earlier in his career, he had a recurring role in the Stephen Amell Arrow series for The CW. Reigns has had roles in blockbusters, such as Fast & Furious Presents: Hobbs & Shaw. However, Street Fighter is his biggest role to date. He did voice one of the Zebros in Zootopia 2 last year. The other Zebro was voiced by his former rival, CM Punk. While they are riding the high of Street Fighter's success, Reigns and Rhodes are back in WWE. The "Tribal Chief" appears bound for a WarGames match next month. He will likely lead the Bloodline into battle against Royce Keys' 946. Meanwhile, Rhodes is on Friday Night SmackDown and always in the Undisputed WWE Championship scene. He has also had an on-and-off feud with Randy Orton.
summary: Cardona gave it glowing praise, but he knows that he is biased. Rhodes and Reigns are part of the Street Fighter ensemble. While they are riding the high of Street Fighter's success, Reigns and Rhodes are back in WWE.

raw_title: Adam Copeland recalls teenage Christian Cage jumping into Demolition’s car
summary_src: According to Adam Copeland, a 16-year-old Christian Cage climbed uninvited into Demolition’s car 36 years ago today.
body: According to Adam Copeland, a 16-year-old Christian Cage climbed uninvited into Demolition’s car 36 years ago today. Copeland said he and Cage would sometimes “stage ambushes” of wrestlers in the parking lot. On this occasion, Cage jumped into the car of Crush (Brian Adams). “This street and this entrance is where Jay and I used to come and annoy and accost all of the wrestlers coming in. We found out that they would park back here and come into the building. So we would always just kind of stage ambushes. “And I’ll never forget the one in particular, and I think it was the last show I came to here. It was Demolition versus Legion of Doom and the Ultimate Warrior. “Jay and I were both big Demolition guys, so we came running out here and Demolition was packing their car and Brian Adams, Crush, was in the front seat. And Jay hopped in the front seat with Brian Adams and just started telling him all of his career highlights and everything like that. “And I was back at the trunk with Ax and Smash annoying them. Years later, Jay’s on a flight. Who sits down beside him? Brian Adams, Crush. And Jay told him the story and he actually still remembered it. And that all happened right here. Copeland defeated Steve Maclin in the main event of MLP Northern Rising at the former Maple Leaf Gardens, now known as the Mattamy Athletic Centre. After the show, Copeland said during the post-event press conference that he believes wrestling at Maple Leaf Gardens is likely a “white whale” for Christian as well. Copeland also revealed on the October 14 episode of AEW Dynamite that Cage suffered three broken ribs and a collapsed lung during the ladder match at AEW All Out. Up next for Copeland, he is scheduled to team with Will Ospreay in a match against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight on tonight’s episode of AEW Dynamite. title: Ric Flair Praises Tony Khan's Generosity
raw_title: Ric Flair Speaks About Tony Khan: "He’s A Nice Guy... I Work For Him & I Don’t Do Anything"
summary_src: Ric Flair heaps praise onto Tony Khan. Biff Poggi of NewsNation conducted an interview with two-time WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair. As the conversation moved along, Flair opened up about his relationship with AEW President Tony Khan.
body: Biff Poggi of NewsNation conducted an interview with two-time WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair. As the conversation moved along, Flair opened up about his relationship with AEW President Tony Khan. “He’s a nice guy; he’s generous. I work for him and I don’t do anything. I think he takes care of me out of respect for me. He grew up on me. He’s just a wonderful guy. It’s not that the guys at the WWE — I just think they’re all kind of hanging onto their job because you never know. They’ve fired so many people that were an intricate part of my career when I was there. I don’t understand the rhyme or reason for it. The guys that did my documentary on Peacock, two of the guys that did it have been fired.” Flair went on to state that Tony Khan may be the greatest wrestling promoter of all time. In early 2026, Fightful Select reported that it was believed that Flair was still under contract to AEW.
summary: In an interview with NewsNation, Ric Flair described AEW President Tony Khan as a nice, generous and wonderful person who pays him out of respect despite Flair not having set duties. Flair contrasted the situation with WWE, noting that the company has fired people who played key roles in his career including two involved in his Peacock documentary. Per Fightful Select, Flair remains under contract with AEW into early 2026.

llm_long: Ric Flair has spoken about the generosity shown to him by Tony Khan. Flair has remained under contract with AEW since 2023 while making only rare appearances for the promotion.
Flair first joined AEW as part of Sting’s retirement tour and with a sponsorship for his “Wooooo! Energy” drink. Although that sponsorship deal has ended, he continues to be part of the company.
In an interview, Flair described Khan as a nice and generous person who continues to take care of him out of respect. He noted that Khan grew up watching him and called Khan a wonderful guy.
Flair contrasted his experience with AEW to the situation at WWE. He observed that many longtime WWE employees have been let go and expressed uncertainty about the decision-making process there.

At 77 years old, Flair stated that the main difference between WWE and AEW is WWE’s much longer history. He praised Khan’s skills as a promoter and suggested that Khan could be the greatest promoter of all time.
When asked about decision-making in wrestling, Flair said he believes Khan consults with a group of people before making choices, similar to practices at other companies.

body: Link @AEWonTV Ilja Dragunov’s AEW debut remains the biggest story to come out of the promotion’s WrestleDream PPV this past Sunday. But I bet the second most talked about thing that happened in Orlando, Florida’s Addition Financial Arena on Oct. 18… Tommaso Ciampa “wrestling” Andrade El Ídolo pants, and the pants kicking out . Denise Salcedo’s reaction to the spot pretty much mirrors my own. It was an amusing moment, made more so by the crowd’s enthusiastic buy in (no pun intended). Too much of the match focused on pants-related gags for my liking, but I acknowledge that Ciampa mocking and/or being frustrated with Andrade’s current Latin Lover schtick has been a part of their feud over the International title. And “psycho” is right there in Tommaso’s nickname, which makes snapping like this seem in character. “I felt like it was a little bit of him trying to have fun and play mind games like Orange Cassidy might do. In this case, we see Andrade play mind games with his opponent a lot and he’s always having fun, taking selfies during the match. I felt like Tommaso was trying to reverse the mind games on him. In this case, it’s not a legal fall, but I think he’s having fun. It’s fun within the context of the sport, but on the other hand, it’s important to remember that it is a spot and they’re both great wrestlers and I’m glad they got back to the wrestling after that… At least that’s how it seems, even after you account for the percentage of noise coming from those who just stoke tribalism around anything from either AEW or WWE that sparks debate among the wider community. The chatter’s continued since Sunday, and Jeff Jarrett’s sort-of defense of Ciampa vs. Pantalones has been generating another round of discussion. “I mean, ‘funny don’t draw money’ is such a situational [concept]. I just don’t think you can paint it as… look, creative is subjective. Did you hear the reaction? They loved it. So I just think — and I get it, to each his own. It’s [that sort of spot] not for everybody.” Double-J is on Tony Khan’s payroll, but he makes a good point about the crowd reaction. title: Identity of Person Who Told Paul Heyman to Cut His Ponytail
raw_title: Identity of Person Who Told Paul Heyman to Cut His Ponytail
summary_src: Paul Heyman’s son Jacob Heyman just took credit for one of the biggest changes to his father’s iconic look. According to Jacob, he’s the reason Paul finally said goodbye to the signature ponytail that wrestling fans had associated with him for years.
body: Speaking during HeymanHustleTV Presents: The Roundtable , Jacob was sitting alongside Cody Rhodes, Charlotte Flair and O’Shea Jackson Jr. as the group swapped stories about growing up with famous fathers. When the conversation turned to things about their parents that fans might not know, Jacob decided to drop some “breaking news.” “This is breaking news. I’ve never revealed this to the world, but, uh — I told him to cut the ponytail. That was my idea.” Jacob wasn’t backing away from the claim either. He doubled down and made it clear that getting rid of the ponytail was his suggestion. That prompted another surprised reaction from the table: “You’re the one.” Cody Rhodes then decided to have a little fun at Paul’s expense, joking that Jacob might actually deserve some gratitude for making it happen. “My dad’s played a heel on TV for — what was it? — 40 years. And he’s the biggest babyface of my life. He’s my hero. He’s my best friend. And I couldn’t ask for a better dad.” Paul may have originally imagined CM Punk taking the ponytail as a wrestling trophy, but Jacob is now taking some of the credit for its eventual disappearance. More than a decade later, fans finally have another piece of the story behind one of Heyman’s biggest changes in appearance. Sign in to your TheSportster account Jordynne Grace earned herself the reputation for being one of the best women’s wrestlers on the planet during her time outside of WWE , so there was a lot of anticipation for her arrival in the company back in 2025. Since then, she’s had a less than impressive NXT run and a main roster call-up that has led to pretty much nothing - she’s had just six matches on Friday Night SmackDown and hasn’t been seen in any capacity for four months. With reports emerging of WWE’s lack of creative plans for Grace, it spells potential disaster for her future in the promotion, and it may very well spell the end of time in WWE; and it is all down to Triple H 's creative. One thing is for sure - wasting the talents of Jordynne Grace is a major creative blunder from Triple H . Unfortunately for Grace, it appears plans may have changed and are no longer happening, as a new report from WrestleVotes via Fightful Select has revealed that the latest coming out of WWE is that she is not currently involved in creative plans. For someone as talented as Grace to not be involved in WWE’s creative plans for over six months, it is a very real problem. When it comes to creative plans in WWE, blame must fall on Triple H. Jordynne Grace is among the most talented and impressive in-ring workers in the company, and while she hasn’t quite yet shown serious qualities as a character, much of this comes from the fact that WWE didn’t give her much to go on when she arrived on SmackDown. She has still displayed a lot of potential since coming to WWE, having standout showdowns with the likes of Stephanie Vaquer & Giulia in NXT, impressing in her appearance at the 2025 Evolution PLE, and having highly regarded feuds against names in Roxanne Perez & Blake Monroe. title: Injury Update: Damian Priest Responds to R-Truth Blaming Him for Scary WWE SmackDown Injury
raw_title: Damian Priest Responds to R-Truth Blaming Him for Scary WWE SmackDown Injury
summary_src: Damian Priest has officially responded to R-Truth blaming him for the scary injury that stopped their WWE SmackDown match early. Priest isn’t accepting any responsibility either, joking that Truth nearly ended his own life just because he was so desperate to beat him.
body: Speaking on Off the Ropes , Priest was asked about Truth’s recent update following their October 16 match. Truth had shared a photo from a medical facility and joked that Priest “tried to kill” him, and apparently that accusation made its way back to Priest. “You know that guy tried to blame me? I’ve been told he posted some stupid thing that he’s good, but I tried to, like, end his life.” Damian Priest immediately turned the accusation back around on Truth. As far as he’s concerned, Truth was the one who took the risk that led to the match being stopped, all because he wanted the victory. “He tried to end his own just to win a match against me. And guys, it explains who he is.” The exchange comes after Truth was legitimately hurt during their October 16 SmackDown match. Truth landed awkwardly after delivering a missile dropkick from the top rope, leading the referee to check on him before stopping the match ahead of its planned finish. Truth finally addressed the situation on October 19 and thankfully had some reassuring news. He shared a photo of himself in a hospital gown in front of an MRI machine while thanking fans for all the messages he’d received . “I AM OK, Thank you ALL for your support, concerns and get well wishes , Wow, It truly feels amazing to feel and be loved I’m grateful for you all.” Naturally, Truth couldn’t give everyone a completely serious injury update. He decided to keep his storyline with Priest going by accusing his former tag team partner of nearly killing him before promising that he’ll eventually be back. “…On 10/16/2026 I almost passed away… Damien Priest tried to kill me,, I didn’t think he was ThAt serious… But ok, I’ll be back” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

title: New Data Shows Chad Gable is WWE’s Iron Man Champion
raw_title: New Data Shows Chad Gable is WWE’s Iron Man Champion
body: Gable won the title from Penta on night two of SummerSlam on August 2 at U.S. Bank Stadium in Minneapolis. Wrestling in front of his home state crowd, Gable reversed a second Mexican Destroyer attempt into the Ankle Lock and made Penta tap out. It was the first Intercontinental Championship win of his career. He earned that title shot the hard way. On the July 13 episode of Raw in Dallas, Gable won a number one contender’s gauntlet match that lasted more than 38 minutes, getting past Dominik Mysterio, Dragon Lee, Ethan Page, Je’Von Evans, Joe Hendry and Rusev. Since winning the title, Gable has defended it four times on Raw, which works out to a televised title match every 20 days. He beat Rey Mysterio on the August 17 episode in Buffalo, Dragon Lee on the September 14 episode in Mexico City, and Rey Fenix on the October 12 episode in Bossier City, Louisiana. Most recently, he retained in a triple threat against Dragon Lee and Rey Mysterio on the October 19 episode in San Diego. Those were not short matches either. According to Cagematch , the Fenix match ran 18 minutes and 35 seconds, the first Dragon Lee match went 15 minutes and 39 seconds, and the triple threat lasted 15 minutes and 35 seconds. The Mysterio match on August 17 went just over 13 minutes. The televised defenses are only part of the picture. Cagematch lists 13 more successful defenses at live events since SummerSlam, bringing his total to 17 without a loss. He defended against Ethan Page several times on WWE’s summer tour, beat Dominik Mysterio in both a singles match and a triple threat in Canada, and won four straight fatal four-way matches against Dragon Lee, Ethan Page and Penta on the South America tour in September. He also defended the title at two NXT live events in the Carolinas against Saquon Shugars and Uriah Connors, and won a three-way against Ethan Page and Je’Von Evans in Honolulu on October 16. The run is also the payoff to a long chase. Gable came up short against Sami Zayn in multiple Intercontinental Championship matches in 2024, including a match at Clash at the Castle in June that year that lasted more than 22 minutes. Two years later, he finally got the title in his home state. Gable’s reign is a throwback to the way a midcard title is supposed to be booked. He is defending the championship on television on a regular basis, he is doing it against a mix of veterans and younger stars, and the matches are getting real time on Raw. Four televised defenses in 80 days is a steady pace for a secondary title, and the live event defenses show he is putting the belt on the line nearly every time he works. It also matters who he is beating. Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee and Rey Fenix are some of the best workers on Raw, and Gable’s style matches up well with each of them. Those matches have made the Intercontinental Championship feel like one of the more important parts of the show, which is what a strong champion should do.
summary: Gable won the title from Penta on night two of SummerSlam on August 2 at U.S. Wrestling in front of his home state crowd, Gable reversed a second Mexican Destroyer attempt into the Ankle Lock and made Penta tap out.

title: Is War Games Becoming A Trope, Moves That Shouldn’t Be Done From A Ladder, Aaa Is Fun And More
raw_title: IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin IS WAR GAMES BECOMING A TROPE, MOVES THAT SHOULDN’T BE DONE FROM A LADDER, AAA IS FUN AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-10-20 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . Did the WWF ever give serious consideration to main eventing a PPV with a one-on-one match between Hulk Hogan and Ted DiBiase? Not that I am aware of. Hell, they never even put the Title on him so I doubt they were looking to do him vs. Hogan on PPV back then. AAA has great action and solid storytelling. Anyone looking to product a wrestling show could learn from that. It’s the backbone of what makes a company successful. If the wrestlers are going to do dives off the top of a ladder, wouldn't it be safer to have them stand with their feet perpendicular to the top step, rather than parallel? Ability level aside, the way Tiffany Stratton was balancing on the top of that ladder looked awkward and she didn't appear completely comfortable. They should do dives in a way where the ladder is as stable as possible. In Stratton’s case, it was not even close as the ladder was moving as she was launching. Also, rather that do any flip move that requires torque off of a ladder, splashes make much more sense to me. You leave the ladder and immediately go downward, rather than trying to get height off of it. Personally I agree with the reader that feels War Games has had its day. If it happens every year in November without fail then we know it's a crutch for the booking to go down the route of two groups feuding for months and needing War Games to settle it. The best Survivor Series event I ever saw was 2002 which also didn't have the traditional survivor matches. It had an amazing card and was capped off with the first elimination chamber. Would we not be better off with a less is more approach with all these matches? The fact that it’s done because it’s November is an issue when the creative leading up to it isn’t great, for sure. We don’t seem to notice that when the booking is strong and the fans want to see the talents in the cage. But I agree, right now it’s more of a trope and that should never be the case with a match like that. That’s all on creative. Sure, there are politics involved as well, but it comes down to whether Creative wants to pull the trigger or not. You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com .

title: Clark Connors Shares Original Name Idea for The Dogs

summary_src: Clark Connors says The Dogs originally had a different name in mind when the former Bullet Club War Dogs arrived in AEW. Connors, David Finlay, and Gabe Kidd are known simply as The Dogs in AEW.
body: Clark Connors says The Dogs originally had a different name in mind when the former Bullet Club War Dogs arrived in AEW. “When we came over here, we just became The Dogs, but we really wanted to pitch the name Raw Dogs, but I think there’s an issue with that whole Monday Night thing, but it sounds cool because we’re raw f—ing dogs, you know?” “But The Dogs also is a sick name. It’s just no one’s ever done it before. No one’s been The Dogs.” Connors, Finlay, and Kidd teamed with Death Riders Claudio Castagnoli, Daniel Garcia, and Wheeler Yuta in a win over the Bang Bang Gang and the Conglomeration in a 12-man tag team match at Saturday’s Tailgate Brawl ahead of AEW WrestleDream in Orlando, Florida. Prior to that, Connors and Finlay lost an AEW World Tag Team Championship match to Matt and Nick Jackson, the Young Bucks, at AEW Collision Grand Slam France on October 6. title: Injury Update: Damian Priest Underwent Medical Procedures After Dealing With Multiple Injuries
raw_title: Damian Priest Underwent Medical Procedures After Dealing With Multiple Injuries
summary_src: Damian Priest has been wrestling with a beat-up body for a long time, but things are finally starting to turn around. The WWE star says he’s feeling “a lot better” after quietly undergoing procedures to ease his pain — and he somehow never took a day off while doing it.
body: Speaking on Off the Ropes , Priest was asked how his body is holding up these days. His immediate answer was basically what you’d expect from someone who has spent years getting slammed into a wrestling ring for a living. “Well, we’re never okay — that’s what we do. No bitching and moaning. I don’t like talking about how my body is. I’m not the only one banged up — my opponent is banged up too.” “But I’m feeling a lot better. I got some procedures done and never took a day off. I got some stuff done to ease the pain, and I feel a lot better.” Priest didn’t get into exactly what those procedures were, so he’s keeping those details to himself for now. What he did say is that fans should already be able to notice a difference in how he’s looking and moving. “I think people can see it visually, and I’m training daily and getting back to the shape I used to be in.” It’s not just his body that’s feeling different either. Priest admitted he’s in a much better headspace now and actually had to check himself after realizing he wasn’t approaching his career with the same positive mentality he normally prides himself on. “I’m training better and in a better headspace too. For someone who thinks positively about my career, I did the opposite and had to check myself a bit.” That’s a pretty big turnaround from what Priest revealed back in December 2025. At the time, he admitted his body was taking a beating, with multiple shoulder tears along with problems involving his knees and back . Priest was so determined to keep going that WWE actually had to make him slow things down. Even then, he made it clear that surgery would always be his last resort because he’d rather rehab, get treatment and stay in the game. “If I don’t need surgery, I won’t do it. I’ll figure it out — rehab, treatment, whatever it takes — just keep me in the game.” Almost a year later, that approach seems to have Priest feeling much closer to himself again. He’s still not pretending his body is magically 100%, but after procedures, daily training and a mental reset, things sound a whole lot better than they did last December. title: MJF Serves as Special Guest Referee for Create-A-Pro

summary_src: AEW star MJF will be donning a referee shirt when he appears for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend. The indie promotion has announced that MJF will serve as the special guest referee for a 10-man tag match at its Saturday, October 24 show in Long Island, New York.
body: AEW star MJF will be donning a referee shirt when he appears for Create-A-Pro Wrestling this weekend. The indie promotion has announced that MJF will serve as the special guest referee for a 10-man tag match at its Saturday, October 24 show in Long Island, New York. It will pit teams managed by Road Dogg and (indie manager) Sidney Bakabella against each other. Team Road Dogg has Create-A-Pro co-owner Brian Myers on the team, along with Anthony Greene, Aaron Rourke, Bobby Orlando & Nick Robles. Bakabella’s team has Leo Sparrow, Dante Drago, Bryce Donovan, Vinny Scalice & TJ Crawford. Create-A-Pro is MJF’s original home promotion and where he trained to become a wrestler. He was added to this event as a make-good after Billy Gunn had to cancel his bookings due to “contractual obligations.” Along with refereeing, MJF will be available for a meet and greet. “Unfortunately due to contractual obligations, Billy Gunn will no longer be appearing at #CAPBaseBrawl this Saturday in North Merrick, NY,” Create-A-Pro announced on Tuesday . “Road Dogg will still be in attendance. Any pre purchased Meet & Greet package for Billy Gunn or the New Age Outlaws will be refunded “As a replacement we will present a special Meet & Greet with the real AEW World Champion @The_MJF! We will also be adding a Meet & Greet with AEW announcer Alicia Atout! A show ticket must be purchased to attend all Meet & Greets.” Brookside Educational Center is hosting the show, which is a fundraiser for Merrick Bellmore Little League. title: Carlie Bravo Claims ROH Has More Hungry Talent Than AEW

summary_src: Carlie Bravo sticks up for Ring Of Honor. Competing alongside Shane Taylor Promotions, Carlie Bravo has been a essential part of the promotion since 2023. Pushing back against the online criticism, Bravo recently spoke with Wrestling Republic and said that ROH has more killers than AEW does.
body: Competing alongside Shane Taylor Promotions, Carlie Bravo has been a essential part of the promotion since 2023. Pushing back against the online criticism, Bravo recently spoke with Wrestling Republic and said that ROH has more killers than AEW does. “I love Ring Of Honor. I love Ring Of Honor. We all see the bullshit sometimes, the negative bullshit that gets spoken about it. But, I think Ring Of Honor got more killers than AEW does and in a sense of hungry. People are hungry. You can’t tell me Red Velvet not hungry, you know what I’m saying? You can’t tell me Dalton Castle & The Outrunners not fucking hungry. Swirl, Infantry, STP, we got people on there that are freaking monsters that are waiting at the gym to go freaking crazy. Adam Priest, you got people that are just waiting to get a moment to go. I think that hunger pushes a lot. We take a lot of pride in Ring Of Honor, you know what I’m saying? We went from one Death Before Dishonor, we had the titles the whole time, then we the lost the belts at the next one. I love that, you know what I’m saying? I love that we can give back to that company like that and make it not just what it was but what it could possibly be.” Bravo continued by putting over more names on the ROH roster. “At the last ROH taping, it was AR Fox versus Bandido. Like, what are we talking about? That’s a main event anywhere. I saw Hechicero and Bandido and it blew my freaking mind. Konosuke Takeshita and Bandido blew my mind. We had the last couple television champions, Nick Wayne, Lio Rush, Action Andretti, we got killers. I mentioned the tag team belts, we got Mistico and Mascara Dorada as the tag champs. Before that, me, Cap, and Shane was the Trios Champions. Then, Dalton and The Outrunners was doing it. Now, Lethal and Swirl got it. Deonna Purrazzo, women’s pure champion. Longest reigning men’s pure wrestling champion of all time, Lee Moriarty talking that wave. Who is fucking with that roster?” ROH Final Battle was recently announced for December. title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out People Who Credit Dusty Rhodes for His Work Ethic
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out People Who Credit Dusty Rhodes for His Work Ethic
summary_src: Cody Rhodes is tired of people assuming his work ethic comes from being Dusty Rhodes’ son. The WWE star says he’s spent years hearing about the massive shadow his father left behind, but the person who actually deserves credit for teaching him to work hard is his mother.
body: Speaking during HeymanHustleTV Presents: The Roundtable , Cody discussed growing up as the child of a wrestling legend alongside Charlotte Flair, Jacob Heyman and O’Shea Jackson Jr. That’s when he pushed back on the idea that he’s constantly working because he feels some responsibility to live up to Dusty’s legacy. “I’m not working hard because Dusty Rhodes told me to work hard. And I’m not even working hard — it’s unrelated to him now. It’s put out there as like, ‘Oh, you got that big, you know, you got the boots to fill, the shadow,’ like all that.” “It’s like, ‘Oh, you know, you’re Dusty’s kid. You know, you’re Cube’s kid. You know, you’re Ric’s kid. You got — you know, you’re Paul’s kid. You got to do more than everybody else.’ Fuck, I was already going to do more than everybody else.” “My work ethic doesn’t come from my father. It comes from my mom. She don’t get no credit.” Cody also made it clear that Dusty himself wasn’t the person putting all that pressure on him. According to Cody, his father never sat him down and demanded that he surpass what he had accomplished in wrestling. “My dad never told me that. People on the outside told me that, you know. I was never told to like, ‘All right, you got to, you know, top me,’ or like, ‘You got to be better than this.’” Cody isn’t distancing himself from Dusty’s legacy, but he clearly wants people to separate that legacy from his own drive to succeed. For him, constantly turning everything he accomplishes into another comparison with his father can eventually make an incredible family connection feel more like a burden. body: 0 WWE ‘s Drew McIntyre details how Triple H helped him with the “I prayed for this, and it happened” promo. The things sometimes he comes up with, I went, ‘How do you think of that, Triple H?’ That is genius. That is going to be so good. And I know as a fan I would lose my mind. Didn’t think I’d be seeing it to this day for everything, no matter if it’s sports or outside of wrestling. It’s constantly me pointing, ‘I prayed for this, and it happened,'” McIntyre continued. body: On " Busted Open Radio ," Bully Ray said he believes Naomi's return is imminent. Despite the star being on the run of her career before announcing her pregnancy last summer , the Hall of Famer doesn't believe she should jump right back into the women's division, not while 946 is terrorizing the Bloodline. "To me, that's very flat. You can always go back to that one day," Bully Ray said. "We know that Naomi and Jimmy are married. This entire Bloodline thing is about family. She is a part of the family. I want her involved, but when is the right day to bring her back?" Bully Ray and co-host Dave LaGreca pondered that question, with LaGreca wondering if she makes her big return at WarGames itself. Bully Ray said he thinks it needs to be before the event, and it needs to be a dramatic moment. "I want to see a moment in time where Jaida Parker is going to do something really bad to one of the Bloodline members," he said. "Technically, it should be Jimmy. The whole blowtorch idea, I know it's preposterous and they'll never do it, but can you imagine if the 946 is holding down Jimmy. He's on his knees. They got his arms. He can't move, and here comes Jaida Parker with a blowtorch or whatever [and out comes Naomi.]"

summary_src: WWE’s Crown Jewel situation in Saudi Arabia just got a whole lot more uncomfortable. With the company supposed to bring its roster to Riyadh on November 7, the U.S.
body: The move came on October 21, and the timing couldn’t be much worse for WWE. Reuters reported that the State Department ordered the departures because of increased security threats connected to the Iran-aligned Houthis in Yemen. There were initially even more alarming reports about how far the order went. AFP cited a diplomatic source claiming all American embassy staff and their families had been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia, while families of embassy personnel were also being ordered out of several other Gulf countries. “All American staff and their families have been ordered to depart from the US embassy in Saudi Arabia.” Reuters described the confirmed U.S. action more narrowly, reporting an ordered departure involving non-emergency personnel and family members in Saudi Arabia. Either way, the U.S. government is now actively moving people out of the country while WWE is preparing to move an entire wrestling production into it. None of this means WWE has canceled Crown Jewel. The November 7 show remains on the schedule, and there hasn’t been an announcement from WWE saying the event is being relocated or called off. Still, the clock is ticking pretty fast now. WWE has a little over two weeks before Crown Jewel, and with the U.S. pulling diplomatic personnel and families out while attacks continue, the question of whether WWE can safely get everyone into Riyadh and back home is only getting bigger. llm_long: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reopened on Sunday after being closed since the previous Saturday. Questions continue about whether WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel scheduled for November 7 in the city.

Saudi coalition officials reported the airport had been targeted 20 times during the month, resulting in 17 deaths and 333 injuries. Conflicting reports persist, with some outlets still listing the airport as closed.
Flight data showed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, mostly domestic, and at least one international passenger flight landed. Many international airlines continue to suspend service to Riyadh.

Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been canceled or postponed amid increased attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament was delayed from October to December, and the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships set for November were canceled.
The Canelo Alvarez versus Christian Mbilli boxing match planned for October 31 is still expected to take place. WWE has not announced any changes to Crown Jewel as of the latest reports.

body: With WWE Crown Jewel scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7, the U.S. State Department has ordered nonessential diplomatic personnel and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia The news comes amid escalating attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group in the region. Multiple upcoming events in Riyadh have been canceled or postponed. The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh also issued a new security alert Wednesday warning of further attacks. The alert also states that King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remains suspended. Security Alert: U.S. Mission Saudi Arabia (October 21, 2026) Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area. U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport. Reuters reported on Wednesday that the US State Department was preparing to issue an order to nonessential diplomatic personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott later clarified the news on X writing that the order applied for non-essential employees and their families in Saudi Arabia only. “The U.S. Department of State issued an ordered departure for non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members in Saudi Arabia only. Iranian-supported Houthis have increasingly engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The safety and security of Department personnel and their families remain our highest priority, and we will continue to take all necessary steps to protect and support them.” As of this writing, WWE has not announced any plans to postpone, reschedule or relocate Crown Jewel. Flight data showed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, mostly domestic, and at least one international passenger flight landed. Many international airlines continue to suspend service to Riyadh.

Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been canceled or postponed amid increased attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament was delayed from October to December, and the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships set for November were canceled.
The Canelo Alvarez versus Christian Mbilli boxing match planned for October 31 is still expected to take place. WWE has not announced any changes to Crown Jewel as of the latest reports.

llm_long: A match on SmackDown between R-Truth and Damian Priest was halted after Truth appeared to suffer an injury. Truth attempted a missile dropkick from the turnbuckle and stayed on the mat afterward while remaining conscious and moving.

The referee checked on Truth and then stopped the match, signaling the X sign to indicate a legitimate injury. Priest left the ring and retrieved a steel chair, but the referee intervened to prevent further action.
Fraxiom came to the ring to check on Truth as Priest dropped the chair and exited the area. Reports confirmed that the match stoppage was legitimate.

The original plan for the match had Priest winning followed by a post-match attack that Fraxiom would interrupt to make the save. Truth previously suffered a torn quad during an NXT match in November 2022 that required surgery and kept him sidelined for more than a year.

title: Wren Sinclair Was Told She Was “Too Old” for WWE Before Signing
raw_title: Wren Sinclair Was Told She Was “Too Old” for WWE Before Signing
summary_src: Wren Sinclair made it to WWE, but apparently there was a point when she was being told that ship had already sailed. The NXT star revealed that before finally getting signed in 2023, she actually heard that she was “too old for WWE” and should start looking somewhere else.
body: Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring , Wren was asked whether she thinks she’d still be wrestling today if WWE hadn’t eventually come calling. She initially wanted absolutely nothing to do with imagining that alternate timeline. “Um, let’s just not say I didn’t get signed. Um, no, I’m kidding.” Once the question got a little more serious, so did Wren. She admitted there were definitely moments before WWE when injuries had her wondering whether continuing to chase wrestling was even worth it. “Yeah. Um, so I think wrestling holds a really special place in my heart, and I definitely think there were times, um, injuries, where you question whether or not it’s worth it.” Then came the part that makes her eventual WWE signing even more interesting. Wren revealed that she was actually told at one point that she was too old for WWE and should turn her attention somewhere else. “Um, there were times in the process where I actually heard, like, uh, that I’m too old for WWE, um, and to, like, look elsewhere and whatnot.” “And I think at the end of the day, um, I’m not sure because I think I love this so much that it hurts sometimes when it doesn’t love you back.” “Um, and I’m a big proponent of mental health. So, depending on the journey that happened after, uh, said not being signed, um, I’m not sure.” Thankfully for Wren, she never had to find out how that version of the story ended. WWE ultimately signed her in 2023, and after everything it took to get there, she’s joking that the company is going to have a pretty difficult time getting rid of her now. “But I’m glad that I’m here, and I’m going to hold on to this, and I’m just never going to let them fire me.” Being told she was “too old” could have easily been the moment Wren decided to walk away, especially with injuries already making her question her future. Instead, she eventually got the WWE opportunity she was chasing, and now she’s holding onto it as tightly as she can. title: Swerve Strickland doubts AEW-WWE crossover event
raw_title: Swerve Strickland doubts WWE x AEW show will ever happen: ‘Not in my lifetime at least’
summary_src: Swerve Strickland doubts that we’ll ever see AEW and WWE come together for a cross-promotional event. Though Tony Khan has sounded open to collaboration if the logistics were to make sense, a full-on AEW & WWE event would seem to be a near-impossibility given the current landscape of competition.
body: Swerve Strickland doubts that we’ll ever see AEW and WWE come together for a cross-promotional event. “No,” Strickland responded when asked about the possibility. “Not in my lifetime at least.” One of the obvious barriers is that, when co-promoting a show, AEW & WWE would want to protect their talent and have them win. As a performer, Strickland isn’t concerned with that and would be fine with every match ending in a double DQ if he got to face opponents like Oba Femi, Je’Von Evans, and Carmelo Hayes. “It’s control. It’s all about marketing. It’s like the NFL, WWE has to protect their shield. There’s no way they’d allow any of our wrestlers to look better and be better [than them],” Strickland said. “Oba Femi is a world beater. You gotta protect that and make sure he keeps looking good. Gunther, have to protect that. Roman [Reigns], have to protect that. Cody [Rhodes], have to protect, even more so because of AEW. There’s a lot of that happening. The Billboard article was largely centered around Strickland’s pursuits in hip-hop. It would be a dream come true for Strickland to reach heights like winning a Grammy Award, but wrestling is his first love. His AEW World Championship reign from 2024 means more than a Grammy would. “Wrestling has always been my true love,” he said. “A Grammy is more like, ‘Oh my God. How is this even possible?’ That’s another dream, but that’s what this World title was for me. I’m the only person to come from 205 Live and be a World Champion. I’m the only one. If you were ever to ask anyone from the 2017, 2018, 2019 class, and it would have been me out of all those guys? No way. Even me, no way. We don’t see it. A lot of people at that time didn’t see it. Same way in music. ‘Him? Who just did On the Radar ? He got some clicks and stuff, but no way.'” Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

Swerve Strickland expressed doubt that cross-promotional events between the two companies will occur during his lifetime. He cited control and marketing as the primary reasons preventing such collaborations.

According to Strickland, WWE prioritizes protecting its image and ensuring its top stars maintain an advantage. He noted that talents like Obi Femi, Gunther, Roman Reigns, and Cody Rhodes are shielded to preserve their standings.
Strickland indicated he no longer seeks out specific opponents for fantasy matches. He now aims to position himself as the desired fantasy match for others.

title: What Worked and Didn't in AEW's Clockwork Carnage
raw_title: Big Vinny V: What did and didn’t work in AEW’s Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream
summary_src: All Elite Wrestling tried something new at WrestleDream, and innovation is always a good thing. Now that Clockwork Carnage has happened, was it a success? What worked in the match, what didn’t, and what should AEW change if they try it again?
body: All Elite Wrestling tried something new at WrestleDream, and innovation is always a good thing. Now that Clockwork Carnage has happened, was it a success? What worked in the match, what didn’t, and what should AEW change if they try it again? If you’re reading this, you’re probably familiar with the rules of Clockwork Carnage, but here’s a brief summary: Eight men compete in a match with two phases. The first is similar to a Royal Rumble, with pinfalls and submissions resulting in eliminations from the match. Once the eighth man enters, the second phase begins, and all surviving wrestlers compete in a 15-minute Iron Man match. AEW World Champion Will Ospreay invented the match, which became part of the story. He entered the match first, survived the first phase, and went on to win the scoring portion, pinning Adam Copeland with seconds to spare to pull out of a tie with Copeland, Samoa Joe, and Darby Allin. Most of the best parts of the match were Rumble-adjacent. Wrestling crowds love their countdowns and surprises, always rising to their feet to see who’s coming out next, even when they know who that person is. And with a new entrant every few minutes, there was always something exciting going on during the first phase. With so many participants in the match, it also delivers dream matchups, even if just for a few minutes. Clockwork Carnage was the first time Adam Copeland ever wrestled Ospreay, Okada, Konosuke Takeshita or Speedball Bailey. And if you don’t count Royal Rumbles, it was the first time he competed against Samoa Joe or Ricochet as well. There was a lot going on in the second phase of the match, a lot more than typically happens in AEW. Between the first eight matches of the main show and the first phase of Clockwork Carnage, there were 12 finishes (pins or submissions) in about three hours of ringtime, or one finish every 15 minutes. The 15 minutes of phase two then produced eleven finishes in 15 minutes. That’s a blistering pace in any promotion, but especially in AEW, where some of the biggest spots in each match are built around false finishes and nearfalls. After four hours of seeing people kick out of finishers, often at a count of one, it was bizarre to see so many wrestlers go down after just one shot. A side effect of that flurry of action is that some of the biggest results were lost in the shuffle. Did you even remember that Allin pinned Ospreay? A victory over the reigning world champion should have been a gigantic moment, but it was nearly forgotten because barely a minute went by before Allin also pinned Copeland, then was pinned himself by Ospreay. This all means that wrestlers who are normally protected are suddenly doing jobs left and right. Going into Clockwork Carnage, Copeland had only been pinned twice all year, first by Dax Harwood when FTR defeated Cage and Cope at Dynasty in April, and then by Jon Moxley in an eight-man tag team match at Grand Slam Mexico in August. He was then pinned three times in 15 minut
summary: All Elite Wrestling introduced the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream featuring eight competitors in two phases. The first phase functioned like a Royal Rumble with pinfalls and submissions causing eliminations while the second phase shifted to a 15-minute Iron Man match once the final man entered. Will Ospreay who created the concept entered first survived the opening phase and secured the victory by pinning Adam Copeland in the closing seconds to break a tie with Copeland Samoa Joe and Darby Allin per the Wrestling Observer.

title: WWE announces "WWE Campus Rush" recruitment tour
raw_title: WWE announces "WWE Campus Rush" recruitment tour - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email STAMFORD, Conn., October 11, 2022 – WWE today announced “WWE Campus Rush,” a multi-campus college athlete recruitment tour which will visit top NCAA Division I universities in search of the next generation of WWE Superstars. WWE Superstars such as Big E, Bianca Belair, Omos, Madcap Moss and Raquel Rodriguez, all of whom have transitioned from college athletics to a career in WWE, will address student athletes at each tour stop and educate them about the global leader in sports entertainment. In conjunction with each university, student athletes will learn about WWE’s “Next In Line” (NIL) program and the resources that they can utilize including brand building, social media, fan engagement, media training and more. Each stop of the tour will include a lively competition that features student athletes facing off on the microphone to cut the best WWE-style promo. “WWE Campus Rush” will begin tomorrow, October 12 at the University of Mississippi and will visit a total of eight universities from five conferences during the fall semester, including: Looking ahead to 2023, ‘WWE Campus Rush” will visit the University of Florida, University of Michigan, Michigan State University, University of North Carolina, Texas A&M University, University of Oklahoma, Auburn University, University of Illinois, and Northwestern University. “WWE Campus Rush will serve as a core pillar in our commitment to finding the next generation of WWE Superstars among today’s elite college athletes,” said James Kimball, WWE’s Head of Talent Operations and Strategy. “The talent pipeline from college sports to WWE has proven to be effective, as evidenced by current champions Roman Reigns and Bianca Belair, and we are looking forward to visiting major college campuses around the country to introduce ourselves in a new way.” WWE launched its “Next In Line” program in December 2021 and currently has 25 active athletes with NIL partnerships. Three athletes from the inaugural class have joined the company following their graduation from school and have started training full-time at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Fla. Additionally, WWE has exclusively hosted more than 100 college athletes from more than a dozen different sports at multi-day talent tryouts in 2022. WWE signed nearly 50 athletes from those events in a growing effort to find the most talented athletes in the world.

title: Damian Priest Details Split From R-Truth
raw_title: Damian Priest Explains Why He Turned On R-Truth, 'This Is An Individual Business'
summary_src: Damian Priest explains why he turned on R-Truth. Since ending his partnership with Truth in September, Damian Priest has shown fans an entirety different side of his character. Speaking in a new interview with WWE Radio's Off The Ropes, Priest took a moment to explain his current mindset.
body: Since ending his partnership with Truth in September, Damian Priest has shown fans an entirety different side of his character. Speaking in a new interview with WWE Radio’s Off The Ropes , Priest took a moment to explain his current mindset. “It’s one of those things that I’m just looking around, looking and reading the room and I seeing everybody or a lot of others achieve things that I want and progressing. What are they doing? What am I not doing? Everybody’s just doing what they gotta do and I’m over here playing with my friends. That’s the difference. Am I doing a job or am I pretending to do a job? I was pretending, I was playing. I was trying to appease other people instead of, you know, worrying about myself. You might be in a tag team for a minute, but at the end of the day, this is an individual business. This is not a team sport. You gotta start thinking about yourself, because when I sign a contract, I’m not signing a contract with the Judgment Day. I’m not signing a contract with R-Truth. I’m signing a contract for Damian Priest. So, Damian Priest needs to be the priority. Once I put that into focus and kind of started — I had to go back home and remember how I started this journey and what got me here. Once I started doing that and then focusing on, on me, I already feel — I haven’t even done what I’m setting out to do yet, but I already feel good about it. It’s just a whole different vibe, a whole different feel. I’m in a really good place now.” Check out the current lineup for the October 23 episode of SmackDown by clicking here. title: TNA Legend Sends Message to Fans Divided Over WWE and AEW
raw_title: TNA Legend Sends Message to Fans Divided Over WWE and AEW
body: 0 Former TNA star Christopher Daniels believes professional wrestling fans should support the entire industry rather than focus on rivalries between promotions. WWE remains one of the industry’s longest-established promotions, while AEW has built its own audience since launching in 2019. The company continues to present weekly programming featuring established names and emerging talent. Daniels also encouraged fans who enjoy professional wrestling to give AEW a chance, noting that the promotion continues to attract new viewers. “Listen, if you’re a professional wrestling fan, I think you should support all professional wrestling. And, you know, WWE is the oldest game in the game. They’re the oldest group in the game, but AEW is coming along strong. AEW is great, and hopefully, if you like professional wrestling, AEW presents tremendous professional wrestling week in and week out. “So, if you’re against that, I don’t know what to tell you. Go watch something else. That’s fine. But we’ve got plenty of fans, and we’re bringing more fans along the way, and I look forward to showing them professional wrestling each and every week,” Daniels said. Daniels began his professional wrestling career in 1993 and went on to compete for several major promotions, including WWE, WCW, and ECW. He made televised appearances for WWE as an enhancement talent but never signed a full-time contract. Daniels later established himself as a prominent figure in TNA Wrestling, where he became a three-time X Division Champion and earned recognition for his work in the company’s X Division. After leaving TNA in 2014, Daniels joined Ring of Honor, where he continued wrestling and eventually captured the ROH World Championship. In 2019, he signed with AEW alongside Frankie Kazarian and Scorpio Sky as part of SoCal Uncensored. Daniels also served as AEW’s head of talent relations, contributing to the promotion’s development behind the scenes. The 32-year veteran officially retired from in-ring competition on January 18, 2025, following a Texas Death Match against “Hangman” Adam Page on AEW Collision. Someone like Bron Breakker knows exactly how that feels in 2026 . Thankfully, the Raw talent has started to see a positive change in his booking. The same can't be said on SmackDown for a former world champion. Gunther was once a man retiring legends left and right, but now he shows up on Friday nights with next to nothing to do. How can something once so right go so wrong? Gunther is one of the best technical wrestlers in the world. Of that there is no doubt. Whether it be under his slimmed down current name or as Walter, Gunther is an old-school master technician who can sell a story like few others. He's the perfect heel, a man who can get booed with ease every time he picks up the mic. Gunther came to the WWE main roster already with a legacy intact. Triple H, newly in charge of creative, saw how great the Ring General was and turned him into the greatest Intercontinental Champion of all-time. After that came a King of the Ring crown and two runs with the World Heavyweight Championship. Then he found the ultimate way to keep going when out of the title scene. Gunther became a career killer, retiring a trifecta of legends in Goldberg, John Cena, and AJ Styles. No matter what happens for the rest of his time in the ring, such a stunning accomplishment can't be taken away from him. After such a powerful 2025 and a dominant start to 2026, Gunther's run in WWE has turned cold since beating Styles at Royal Rumble. Going into WrestleMania season, reports were that he would face Rey Mysterio at the biggest show of the year in another retirement angle. At the last moment, Gunther was given a WrestleMania saving match with Seth Rollins, which he won. This should have been what turned his fortunes around. It looked possible when Gunther got away from Raw and jumped ship to SmackDown, where he immediately challenged WWE Champion Cody Rhodes. The feud didn't work. title: TNA Signs Hall of Famer to New Deal After Bound For Glory Title Win — Report
raw_title: TNA Signs Hall of Famer to New Deal After Bound For Glory Title Win — Report
body: 0 Amazing Red has reportedly signed a new contract with TNA following his return at Bound For Glory 2026. Red’s return to TNA initially appeared to centre on his Hall of Fame induction at the October 11 event. However, he surprised fans by announcing during his induction speech that he would compete for the vacant X-Division Championship later that night. The veteran wrestler bested BDE, Rich Swann, KC Navarro, Fabian Aichner, Cedric Alexander, and Ryan Nemeth in a seven-man scramble to capture the title. He secured the victory by hitting KC Navarro with the Code Red, earning his fourth reign with the championship. “TNA Hall of Famer The Amazing Red, who won the X-Division Championship at Bound for Glory earlier this month, has officially signed with the promotion, PWInsiderElite.com can confirm. The promotion has yet to officially announce the deal, but we can confirm it is done and Red has committed to the promotion,” the report stated. Red previously held the X-Division Championship in 2010. His latest victory ended a gap of more than 16 years between reigns and added another milestone to his TNA career. The 44-year-old is also the founder of House of Glory Wrestling, an independent promotion based in New York. Red helped establish himself as one of the X-Division’s influential performers during his earlier TNA runs between 2002 and 2004 and 2009 and 2011. The title had become vacant after Leon Slater exercised Option C to challenge for the TNA World Championship. Slater subsequently won the world title , defeating Nic Nemeth in the Bound For Glory main event. Fans can revisit WrestleZone’s full coverage of the event here . title: U.S. Embassy Orders Staff Exit From Saudi Arabia
raw_title: Report: U.S. Embassy orders ‘non-emergency’ staff to leave Saudi Arabia
summary_src: "Non-essential" U.S. Embassy staffers in Saudi Arabia, which is scheduled to host Crown Jewel next month, have been ordered to leave.
body: U.S. Embassy staffers are being pulled out of Saudi Arabia, per a new report. “Non-essential” U.S. Embassy staff and their families were ordered to leave the country on Wednesday, per a report from AFP. Reuters was told that others in the Gulf region could be ordered to leave soon as well. The order highlights ongoing caution in the country following numerous attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis. The group most notably struck Riyadh International Airport earlier this month, an attack which left 13 dead and over 300 injured. The airport remained highly restricted as of early this week, Bloomberg reported. Many commercial airlines have temporarily suspended their service to Riyadh International, the largest travel hub in the country. An upcoming boxing match between Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli remains scheduled to take place in Riyadh 10 days from now. On November 7, just a week later, WWE is expected to visit the city for Crown Jewel. Business conferences, a major annual tennis tournament, and an international golf stop set to take place in Riyadh have all been postponed due to the attacks.
summary: Non-essential U.S. Embassy personnel and their families were directed to depart Saudi Arabia on Wednesday amid security concerns following Houthi attacks, including a recent strike on Riyadh International Airport that killed 13 and injured over 300. Several commercial flights to the airport have been suspended and multiple sporting and business events in Riyadh postponed. WWE's Crown Jewel event remains scheduled for November 7 in the city.

title: Match Made: Roman Reigns vs Sami Zayn- 5 Things WWE Fans Need to Know Before Crown Jewel

body: Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn are headed for a collision in Riyadh, and this time both men are holding championship. At WWE Crown Jewel 2026, World Heavyweight Champion Reigns will face Undisputed WWE Champion Zayn in a Champion vs Champion match for the Men’s Crown Jewel Championship. Fans have wanted this rematch for years, and it comes with plenty of history attached. Here is what you need to know about Roman Reigns vs Sami Zayn before the bell rings. This is a clash of the two brands. Reigns represents Raw as World Heavyweight Champion, while Zayn arrives as the Undisputed WWE Champion from SmackDown. The winner takes home the Crown Jewel Championship, a special title WWE has attached to the Saudi Arabia event in recent years. Seth Rollins won the men’s version last year in Perth, so the bar for a memorable main event is already set. Longtime fans know this story. Zayn became the Honorary Uce of The Bloodline, earning his place beside The Tribal Chief before turning on Reigns at Royal Rumble 2023. This led to their Elimination Chamber 2023 showdown in Montreal, where Roman Reigns retained the WWE Universal Championship in front of a suprised crowd. It remains one of the most emotional WWE storylines of the last decade, and this match is a long-awaited sequel. The Head of the Table is back on top. He beat CM Punk at WrestleMania to win the World Heavyweight Championship, then retained against LA Knight at Money in the Bank with a Spear. That marked his fifth successful title defense. WWE has also leaned into a new Reigns, who is fighting his battles without his family interfering at ringside. That makes him look more dangerous and more self-reliant than ever. Zayn’s rise to WWE Champion came as a surprise when he beat Punk. According to many experts, WWE made the title change with a Crown Jewel main event in mind. Whether thatreport is fully accurate or not, the timing certainly fits. Zayn is the ultimate fan favorite, and a Riyadh crowd should give him a warm welcome. He has also won multiple world titles since he last stood across from Reigns, which gives him a different kind of confidence this time. The question everyone is asking is who wins. Many analysts expect Reigns to come out on top and move on to the men’s WarGames match, but WWE loves a curveball. If Zayn pulls off the upset, it would instantly become one of the biggest WWE title moments of the year. Keep an eye on possible Bloodline callbacks and interference too, because Crown Jewel is rarely predictable. Roman Reigns vs Sami Zayn works because it has everything a premium live event needs: two world champions, a personal backstory, and a stadium crowd ready to explode. It’s a rare case where the story and the stakes both feel earned. Whether you’re a fan of The Original Tribal Chief or a believer in Zayn finally getting his redemption, this is the match to watch at WWE Crown Jewel 2026. title: Ilja Dragunov Details AEW Visa Approval Process

body: "I mean, it's not the first time I've had to apply for a visa in the United States," Dragunov said. "That part was already quite familiar to me. But of course, since...everything I want to do is work and fight and perform, I just couldn't wait for things to happen quicker. But from the company side, they were helping me in that process in every way possible. So it was absolutely smooth. It took around, I guess, around a month, which was still too long for me, but...if put in perspective, very fast." title: On the Record: Tama Tonga Speaks On Controversy Over Ilja Dragunov Post After His AEW Debut
raw_title: Tama Tonga Addresses Controversy Over Ilja Dragunov Post After His AEW Debut
summary_src: Tama Tonga has officially responded after Dave Meltzer questioned the timing of his recent Ilja Dragunov post. The WWE star says there wasn’t some old-school wrestling playbook behind it — he simply thought it was a good clip to post.
body: The whole thing started when Tonga recently uploaded footage from Dragunov’s WWE run showing him no-selling Dragunov’s chops on SmackDown. The timing immediately got people talking because the post came only days after Dragunov made his AEW debut. “He did a post of Ilja, and he showed Jey chopping him and basically no-selling him. I don’t know if he was trying to get brownie points or someone told him to do it — I couldn’t tell you.” Meltzer found the whole thing interesting because it reminded him of an old-school promotional tactic. He compared it to something promoters such as Bill Watts and Ole Anderson would do when wrestlers left their territories for WWE. “But I saw that post and was like, ‘That’s an interesting shot.’ It’s like I haven’t seen that one used — that’s like out of the Bill Watts, Ole Anderson playbook of the ’80s.” According to Meltzer, those promoters would sometimes dig up footage of departing wrestlers getting beaten up and put it back in front of fans. He saw at least some similarity between that tactic and Tonga suddenly posting the Dragunov clip. “They would take stars of WWE who used to work in their territory and show clips of them getting beaten up.” “Hey, I seen Dave Meltzer talk about my post yesterday. I put out a post on Dragunov. Boy, it started stirring some s***.” Tonga then questioned why everyone was reading so much into the clip in the first place. As far as he’s concerned, it was simply a good post. Then came Tonga’s response to Meltzer comparing the move to an old wrestling playbook. He jokingly dubbed Meltzer “Great Uncle Dave” before making it clear he wasn’t following anybody’s blueprint. “Great Uncle Dave over here said I took it from a playbook. I don’t even read a playbook, bruh.” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

Takechi previously competed against the House of Torture at last year's Purge Night of Torture event and teamed with Uemura earlier this year at Wrestle Kingdom.

title: Swerve Strickland Says WWE-AEW Co-Promotion Will Never Happen
raw_title: Swerve Strickland Explains Why Cross-Promotional Event Between WWE & AEW Won't Happen
summary_src: Swerve Strickland explained why he doesn't believe a WWE and AEW co-promoted event will ever happen in his lifetime.
body: While stars have jumped between the companies since AEW's inception in 2019, there have never been any co-promoted events between them. According to former AEW World Champion Swerve Strickland, who recently spoke with Billboard , that's never going to happen, at least not in his lifetime. Strickland said it's all about control and marketing. "It's like the NFL, WWE has to protect their shield," Strickland told the outlet. "There's no way they'd allow any of our wrestlers to look better and be better [than them]. Obi Femi is a world beater. You gotta protect that and make sure he keeps looking good. Gunther, have to protect that. Roman [Reigns], have to protect that. Cody [Rhodes], have to protect, even more so because of AEW." Strickland said it's even more difficult when it comes to WWE's women, like Rhea Ripley, being protected. Many fans want to see Seth Rollins and AEW World Champion Will Ospreay wrestle a match , in part, thanks to previous heat between them on social media , but Strickland questioned once again who would be protected. "Us in the locker room, we just wanna have these matches," he said. "I'm good friends with Carmelo [Hayes], Jevon [Evans] and Oba. Those are my boys. I love those guys. I don't care who wins. Double DQs. I don't care." Like AEW and NJPW, WWE currently has a partnership with TNA Wrestling , established at the beginning of 2025. Ahead of WrestleMania 41, the company announced it had acquired AAA .

He explained to Billboard that WWE prioritizes protecting its top stars and image above all else. Strickland cited examples including Gunther, Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes, Rhea Ripley and noted the difficulty in determining protection for a potential Seth Rollins versus Will Ospreay match.
