title: Contract News: Amazing Red Reportedly Signs TNA Contract Following Title Victory
raw_title: Amazing Red Reportedly Signs TNA Contract Following Title Victory
body: TNA Wrestling Hall of Famer Amazing Red has reportedly signed a contract with the promotion following his successful return at Bound For Glory 2026. According to PWInsider, the veteran high-flyer has finalized a deal to remain with TNA after capturing the X-Division Championship and receiving his Hall of Fame induction at the company’s recent pay-per-view. The championship had previously been relinquished by Leon Slater, who exercised TNA’s “Option C” provision to exchange the X-Division Title for an opportunity at the TNA World Championship. Slater subsequently won the TNA World Championship, leaving the X-Division Title available for a new champion. For Amazing Red, the victory marked his fourth reign as X-Division Champion and his first since 2010. Red was one of the defining performers of TNA’s original X-Division, helping establish the fast-paced, high-flying wrestling style that became a signature part of the promotion’s identity. His latest run also marks his first stint with TNA since 2011, bringing him back to the company where he achieved some of his greatest success. The reported signing comes as TNA continues making moves to secure talent for its roster. Earlier this week, the promotion officially confirmed the signing of Shotzi Blackheart, while Director of Authority Santino Marella also agreed to a new contract. Additional contract developments are expected in the coming weeks, with several TNA talents reportedly approaching the expiration of their current agreements before the end of 2026. While fans await official confirmation of Red’s new deal, the reported agreement suggests that his Bound For Glory appearance was more than a one-night return. With the X-Division Championship back around his waist, Amazing Red appears set to begin another chapter with the promotion he helped establish more than two decades ago.

title: Drew McIntyre Details Six-Month WWE Hiatus for Acting
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Discusses Taking Time Away From WWE To Pursue Acting Work, Putting on More Muscle
body: During a recent interview with Insight with Chris Van Vliet , former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre spoke about his career, taking over six months off from WWE to pursue acting work, and whether he’s put on muscle to prep for his WWE return. Below are some highlights from Insight: “Ever, by far since I started wrestling at 15 years old. I have not had six months off. I started doing shows and wrestling basically every weekend or every second weekend when I was 16. My summer job was wrestling at the Butlins holiday camp since I was about 17, and when I tore my bicep, I was out for three months in NXT. I was going stir crazy, so I’d drive down to the PC just to work with Shawn and watch tapes and stuff because you’ve got Shawn Michaels; use him if you’re at the PC. I’ve heard somebody literally say, ‘Who’s the Rockers?’ One time while Shawn was standing there, learn your history for the love of God. When I broke my neck, I was out for eight weeks physicality-wise, but I was doing promos in the second or third week for Evolve and a few other independent companies locally, where I’d take off the brace, cut the promo, head to the back. So this is by far the most amount of time I’ve ever had off.” “Yeah, very, very busy. It has not felt like time off until the past couple of weeks, few weeks, where I’ve actually been at the house with the missus and the cats. It’s been nice, but I’ve been working a lot. It’s been very different. I’ve spent my whole life on the road from town to town, from country to country, 52 weeks a year, no reruns, no offseason in WWE, or the time I was away from WWE, I was even busier than the WWE schedule. So to spend time in the same place was very bizarre. To live in a different country, to live in Spain, was insane. I can tell you now, I’ve learned exactly no extra Spanish words that I knew when I got there.” “No, I just like to look good. Obviously, I’m in the best shape of my life. I feel physically great. I’m sure you saw the clip that was out there when I was running the ropes. I was just rolling around the ring at Miro’s school, Rusev; you’re very welcome. It’s here in Nashville, and my buddy was like, I’ve never seen anybody hit the ropes so fast because he’s not seen Bron Breaker, the only other man that’s faster than me. He got a little clip, a 15-second clip, and it blew up online. I think over 8 million views, so people seem to be excited about the idea that I’m coming back to wrestling, but I’m just seeing what happens right now. I’m enjoying myself. Hollywood Drew is jumping from project to project, and when the time is right, WWE is home.” Drew McIntyre recently said he’s still been training in the ring despite focusing on his acting work this year. He also appears in Agent of Shadows , which debuts on ReelShort on October 23.
summary: Drew McIntyre told Insight with Chris Van Vliet that his current time away from WWE is the longest break he has taken since beginning his wrestling career at age 15. The former champion used the more than six months off to focus on acting projects while also adding muscle in preparation for his return. llm_long: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre revealed he took more than six months away from the company to focus on acting opportunities. McIntyre told Insight with Chris Van Vliet that this break marks the longest time off he has had since beginning his wrestling career at age 15.

He explained that by 16 he was already performing shows nearly every weekend and at 17 his summer job involved wrestling at the Butlins holiday camp. Previous injuries had sidelined him for shorter periods, including three months for a torn bicep in NXT and eight weeks of physical limitation after breaking his neck.

During the neck injury recovery he still cut promos for Evolve and other local independent companies within the first few weeks. McIntyre described the past six months as very busy rather than a true break until only the most recent couple of weeks when he stayed home with his wife and cats.

He noted the unusual experience of remaining in one location after a lifetime spent traveling town to town and country to country for 52 weeks a year with no offseasons. McIntyre spent part of the hiatus living in Spain but admitted he learned no additional Spanish words during that time.

The Scottish wrestler said he has maintained top physical condition simply because he enjoys looking good and feels better than ever. A 15-second clip of him running the ropes at Miro's school in Nashville recently surfaced online and surpassed 8 million views.

summary_src: The best and the worst of the October 21 edition of AEW Dynamite.
body: Here's the very good and the very bad from this week's "AEW Dynamite." AEW/Speedy Ruiz Nick Wayne has beaten Chris Jericho twice. Why is this feud still going? I'm sure they're building to some kind of point about maturity, and Jericho seeing himself in Wayne, but it's all moving too slowly. This week was a lot of yelling and a lot of stalling. I'm terrified the next step could be a Jericho win, or worse, a Jericho tag team. I feel like, by beating him twice, Wayne has sucked all the juice he can out of this rivalry, and should be moving on to bigger, better things, and yet here he is, stuck in the Jericho vortex, likely being taken out to sea on a cruise. It just feels like this feud either needs to end or escalate, and since it was neither, this segment was a little underwhelming, even if I do like where Wayne's character seems to be going. AEW/Speedy Ruiz Normally, it wouldn't be a great thing for AEW to have their AEW World Tag Team Champions The Young Bucks be beaten in such a dominant and quick manner by another team because you want to keep your champions looking strong. In the case of Mark Davis and Jake Doyle dominating Matt Jackson and Nick Jackson in what was essentially a squash Eliminator Match, I actually think it was the perfect call. The Don Callis Family has been positioned as major players on the AEW roster, but their overall win-loss record as a stable doesn't always reflect that and can be inconsistent depending on what the situation of specific storylines they're involved in calls for. For that reason, I think it was genius for The Young Bucks to get in, no offense of any kind against Davis and Doyle, because it instantly makes them feel like a serious threat to the AEW World Tag Team Championship and is an effective way to establish them as a dominant tag team without having to do too much work to position them as such. Something about it just worked really well, and it was a shocking and great way to kick off this "Dynamite" in a manner that was attention-grabbing and engaging. AEW/Speedy Ruiz Last year was the first women's Blood & Guts match, and it was absolutely fantastic, so I guess I just assumed we'd be getting another one this year, to go alongside the men's bout set for two weeks in Jacksonville. If there's going to be a women's version of the hardcore bout, however, it wasn't officially or clearly set up tonight. It kind of sucks either way, because if the women are getting a match, they'll barely have any build. Last year's match was six-on-six, and right now, the heels only have five women, with the babyfaces clocking in at just four. Next week's episode would be making the teams official, and then boom, Blood & Guts the next week. Which, I suppose I shouldn't complain about, because getting a thrown-together women's Blood & Guts match is better than none at all. title: AEW Sets Blood & Guts Match For November 4
raw_title: AEW Dynamite recap, reactions (Oct. 21, 2026): Blood, guts, & heel turns
summary_src: When I thought AEW was going to zig for AEW Dynamite (Oct. 21, 2026), they zagged in a major way. I assumed the biggest story would be the in-ring debut for Ilja Dragunov in the main event.
body: AEW built teams for Blood & Guts with an unexpected crew of babyfaces, a heel turn from Jay White unfolded on the Death Riders, and several more directions were established for upcoming TV specials and the Full Gear PPV. All that and more on the WrestleDream fallout episode came from Watsco Center in Miami, Florida. After Okada cheated with his title belt to help Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight defeat Will Ospreay & Adam Copeland in tag team action (match details further down below), the Callis Family goons went to work pounding their foes. Darby Allin ushered in the surprise return of Steven Borden from injury, and the Young Bucks also joined the fracas. The Callis Family’s mission is to beat down the champions and take their gold soon after. AEW made Blood & Guts official for November 4. It will be Ospreay, Copeland, the Bucks, Allin, & Borden against Fletcher, Okada, Knight, Wardlow, Davis, & Doyle. The story came together quickly in a manner that feels natural. That is an appealing list of all-stars for Ospreay’s team. This matchup feels fresh with a lot of first-timers for Blood & Guts. As for a potential women’s Blood & Guts, there was a backstage scene with Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness beating up the Brawling Birds and Wrathlander backstage. It seems the unifying goal would be to beat up the tag champs and challengers so bad that both heel teams would step into their spots at Full Gear. Add in Willow Nightingale opposite rival Thekla, and we have five versus five. Sounds good to me. On the surface, Divine Dominion with the Sisters of Sin doesn’t make sense, so I like the idea of a common goal to buy into them as a team for Blood & Guts. After Jon Moxley defeated Roderick Strong in an eliminator match (more detail down below), the Continental champion exited the ring. The Dogs duo of David Finlay and Clark Connors swooped in like vultures to pick the bones of Strong. Once Mox noticed, he put a stop to that beatdown. Boom! The Dogs attacked Moxley. Gabe Kidd ran in to corral his pals, boom again. Connors speared Kidd. The Bang Bang Gang are instantly relevant again. I enjoyed their babyface schtick, but they were going upward. Every single member knows how to be heel, so there is no learning curve there. The Bang Bang Gang came run wild with guns blazing. The addition of the Dogs makes sense as former Bullet Club members, and their tension with Moxley has been brewing for weeks. Kidd with the Death Riders is an interesting development. Most of what I’ve seen from Kidd is from AEW, so I’m curious how he does in a babyface role. With the death of PAC, fans wanted the Death Riders to be fan favorites. This does the trick to give them a feud against fresh heels. Also, Claudio Castagnoli was awesome in that scene as a one-man army. AEW made the in-ring debut for Ilja Dragunov feel like a big deal. Could it live up to the hype? I have a mixed reaction about his victory over Mike Bailey. On the positive, the two wrestlers put on a show

The teams formed after Okada used his title belt to assist Fletcher and Knight in defeating Ospreay and Copeland in a tag bout, leading to a post-match beatdown that brought out the babyface side including a returning Steven Borden from injury. After Okada cheated with his title belt to help Kyle Fletcher & Kevin Knight defeat Will Ospreay & Adam Copeland in tag team action (match details further down below), the Callis Family goons went to work pounding their foes. Darby Allin ushered in the surprise return of Steven Borden from injury, and the Young Bucks also joined the fracas. The Callis Family’s mission is to beat down the champions and take their gold soon after. AEW made Blood & Guts official for November 4. It will be Ospreay, Copeland, the Bucks, Allin, & Borden against Fletcher, Okada, Knight, Wardlow, Davis, & Doyle. The story came together quickly in a manner that feels natural. That is an appealing list of all-stars for Ospreay’s team. This matchup feels fresh with a lot of first-timers for Blood & Guts. As for a potential women’s Blood & Guts, there was a backstage scene with Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness beating up the Brawling Birds and Wrathlander backstage. It seems the unifying goal would be to beat up the tag champs and challengers so bad that both heel teams would step into their spots at Full Gear. Add in Willow Nightingale opposite rival Thekla, and we have five versus five. Sounds good to me. On the surface, Divine Dominion with the Sisters of Sin doesn’t make sense, so I like the idea of a common goal to buy into them as a team for Blood & Guts. After Jon Moxley defeated Roderick Strong in an eliminator match (more detail down below), the Continental champion exited the ring. The Dogs duo of David Finlay and Clark Connors swooped in like vultures to pick the bones of Strong. Once Mox noticed, he put a stop to that beatdown. Boom! The Dogs attacked Moxley. Gabe Kidd ran in to corral his pals, boom again. Connors speared Kidd. The Bang Bang Gang are instantly relevant again. I enjoyed their babyface schtick, but they were going upward. Every single member knows how to be heel, so there is no learning curve there. The Bang Bang Gang came run wild with guns blazing. The addition of the Dogs makes sense as former Bullet Club members, and their tension with Moxley has been brewing for weeks. Kidd with the Death Riders is an interesting development. Most of what I’ve seen from Kidd is from AEW, so I’m curious how he does in a babyface role. With the death of PAC, fans wanted the Death Riders to be fan favorites. This does the trick to give them a feud against fresh heels. Also, Claudio Castagnoli was awesome in that scene as a one-man army. AEW made the in-ring debut for Ilja Dragunov feel like a big deal. Could it live up to the hype? I have a mixed reaction about his victory over Mike Bailey. On the positive, the two wrestlers put on a show
summary: Following the WrestleDream fallout on Dynamite from Miami, AEW established teams for the November 4 Blood & Guts event. Will Ospreay, Adam Copeland, The Young Bucks, Darby Allin and Steven Borden will face Kyle Fletcher, Kazuchika Okada, Kevin Knight, Wardlow, Brody King, and Claudio Castagnoli in the match. title: On the Record: Eric Bischoff Weighs In On Pac Tribute Show, Says Recent AEW Deaths Are 'Concerning'
raw_title: Eric Bischoff Comments On Pac Tribute Show, Says Recent AEW Deaths Are 'Concerning'
body: "You still feel the emotion everybody else is feeling," Bischoff said. "To have to go out and perform as a character and focus on what you're doing in the ring for your own safety as well as the person you're in there with, has got to be challenging." Co-host Conrad Thompson said that while he wasn't saying there was any foul play, sometimes "life just throws you a curveball," and said the recent passings reminded him of an era in the 1990s and early 2000s where it felt as if a lot of guys in their early 40s were dying. Bischoff wasn't as convinced. "Every once in a while, someone will get struck by lightning, but you've got two guys at 40 years old — something's going on," he said. "It is not natural. It's not something that you can just go, 'Sometimes, something happens.' It's concerning and hopefully we're not seeing a pattern like we experienced back in the '90s when it was common, I guess. Relatively speaking. It happened too often, let's put it that way. Let's hope we're not revisiting that. But, you know, somebody might want to take a look at that." Causes of death for Williams and Satterley have yet to be released by officials. Initial reports indicated Satterley's death did not appear suspicious .

body: Danielson announced Wednesday that he'll return to wrestling at AEW's tribute to Pac, and he'll team up with the Death Riders to honor Benjamin Satterley. Grading AEW Dynamite 🔠 Bleacher Report 7h New AEW Rumors👂 Bleacher Report 2d Luka, Rookie Exchange Words 🍿 Bleacher Report 2h Satterley, known in AEW as Pac, died at the age of 40 on Sunday, a day after competing against AEW National Champion Andrade El Ídolo in the opening match of Saturday's All Out pay-per-view. Satterley also competed in WWE as Neville, winning multiple championships across both companies. Danielson, who competed in WWE for years before joining AEW in 2021, was a founding member of Blackpool Combat Club alongside Pac and Jon Moxley. The BCC eventually turned on Danielson and formed the Death Riders. Danielson and Pac met in the ring in July 2024, when Danielson beat him in a singles match in the Owen Hart Foundation tournament semifinals. Danielson came into the ring emotional on Wednesday, and Moxley seemingly wasn't happy to see him at first, but the two eventually made amends and hugged it out. Whether Danielson plans to make any other appearances remains to be seen, but it wouldn't be surprising if he made a one-match return to honor the late Satterly. Either way, it was a touching tribute to a wrestling icon.

title: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley, known as 'Pac', dies aged 40
raw_title: Wrestler Benjamin Satterley, known as 'Pac', dies aged 40
body: All Elite Wrestling (AEW) said it was "saddened to announce the passing" of Satterley, 40, who they said had signed with them in 2019. The wrestler's death was confirmed just a day after he participated in AEW's "All Out" event at an arena in Chicago on Saturday evening. "A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability," AEW said in a statement. Satterley held multiple AEW Championships, and the organisation said he had competed in "some of the most memorable matches in AEW history". Prior to his partnership with AEW, he also performed in World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE), New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Consejo Mundial de Lucha Libre in Mexico. He had a number of different personas during his career including Pac, Adrian Neville and "The Man that Gravity Forgot". The latter was in reference to a signature finishing move which saw him spin 360 degrees from the top rope of the wrestling ring and land on his opponent. Many of the tributes paid to Satterley have expressed shock at his death. WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman described it as a "truly terrible loss" and said he was a "tremendous talent and even finer human being". AEW President Tony Khan said he "defined excellence" as a husband, friend and in his wrestling knowledge, skill and "unprecedented athleticism". "The greatest export from our country. Also the greatest human being," fellow British wrestler Will Ospreay wrote on X, sharing a photo of the pair in the ring together. "I am in shock. This is heartbreaking," AEW wrestler Evil Uno said. "We have lost another great person, a great soul, a true professional." "To be able to work with him and watch how incredible he is was something else. "He was a Geordie lad that took on the entire wrestling world and has left a mark that will not be forgotten, and will not be taken away very soon," he told BBC Radio Newcastle.
summary: The latest: the latest: All Elite Wrestling explained it was saddened to announce the passing of Satterley, 40, who they said had inked a deal with them in 2019. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world.

That’s a time period where you don’t have your own brand guidelines. You don’t even know the things you like. So it’s just, hey, this will work. You have to do an appearance. So if I was to do that appearance today with the undashing mask, I would have just done full gear. Yeah, it feels more comfortable if you do full gear while you’re being performative and also meeting fans. You’re in the line of the question that you’ve asked many times, but you’re in the line of are you in character or are you out of character? I think if you’re undashing Cody Rhodes on TV and you’re at Axxess, you’re technically supposed to be in character, so I’d say full gear.” “You know, now I say it, and it’s not so much haunting. I should frame it differently. You asked me the question on one of our talks, and I think I should frame it more as, what’s a good way? The question’s a good question, and the question’s an important question, and I kind of give it a dramatic answer. That’s something you should ask yourself, like me, before I do anything. Because there are probably times, the best prime example is Undashing Cody Rhodes to be in some sort of character, and then there’s times when that’s not a good call at all, also not to waste anyone’s time, right? Not to waste your time, not to waste someone else’s time, or you don’t want to look back at these interviews and think, man, I was just completely full of it, or I was trying to sell a ticket versus actually having a conversation.” “So here’s what I wanted to tell them, and I don’t know them, and I almost contacted you and said, Oh, I want them to know this. They’re telling this funny story about Dusty promoing Ric off the line, and Ric kind of going back and forth. I can’t tell you that that is actually true, but I can tell you it was rooted in these things like that did actually happen, where a simple conversation about something then needed to heat up to where the vocals changed, and the next thing you know they were going back and forth. Because remember there’s no texting, email was not a thing. I mean, it was literally the landline at your house. So, as funny and as outlandish as it was, it felt a little bit like that could have been a thing that actually happened. title: TNA wrestling star Mila Moore has one wrestling dream – involving Taylor Swift
raw_title: TNA wrestling star Mila Moore has one wrestling dream – involving Taylor Swift
body: When asked about leaning into her unapologetic heel persona - including a viral moment where she refused to count a pinfall as a special guest referee because she was checking her nails - Moore admitted she is having the time of her life. "I've never heard a crowd. When I didn't count, I remember genuinely in that moment being like, oh my gosh," Moore said. "It was that was the most fun I've ever had in a match being out there. They hated me. But it was a lot of fun that match was. It was a lot of pressure too because I didn't realize how much the refs, I don't think people realize how much the refs do." She added: "That was great. I think it's helped me come out of my shell completely also. Even backstage too, it just I feel so much more comfortable and like I'm able to have fun which is the goal I feel like at the end of the day there." Moore’s rise has been heavily tied to her alliance with the faction Order Four, taking on the intentionally convoluted title of Secretary of Strategic Affairs. She credited wrestling veteran Ali for masterminding the group's success. "Honestly, I feel like this whole thing was Ali's idea. He is just a genius in every aspect of wrestling," she revealed. "And he came up to me with the idea, I think somebody in creative came up with the title, Secretary of Strategic Affairs, which no one can say or remember or it's like the worst title. It's just the longest title ever. "And even the first time he introduced me before he was like, I hope I say it right... But yeah, this whole thing was Ali's idea. He's such a creative genius really when it comes to wrestling." Before causing chaos at the recent Bound for Glory pay-per-view, Moore made her UK debut performing for Pro-Wrestling: EVE, an experience she won't soon forget. "I actually, so, Eve, I did Eve, that was my first show in the UK ever. So that was amazing," she recalled. "But my sister lives in London, so I was able to visit her, visit my nephews, and wrestle. And she came to watch. It was awesome. It was honestly one of the best shows I've ever been at." Looking ahead to TNA's upcoming Destination X pay-per-view on November 15 in Canada, Moore already has her sights set on championship gold. Asked who she would like to step into the ring with next, the star didn't hesitate to target the top of the women's division. "Oh, that's a good one. For a future match, oh, maybe I would say Masha Slamovich right now because she has the TV title," Moore stated. "Maybe Indi Hartwell. Actually I've trained with Indi a few times. She's our our new knockouts champ, so maybe I mean that would be the first to go after, right?" TNA Wrestling is heading toward Destination X which is on Sunday, November 15, in Edmonton, Alberta. Tickets for TNA Destination X and all TNA live events can be found at www.tnawrestling.com/events . Fans in the USA can watch Thursday Night iMPACT! in its home of AMC and AMC+. iMPACT also airs on Sportsnet 360 in Canada and TNA+ worldwide.

raw_title: WWE’s Tama Tonga Responds To Claims He Took a Shot at Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut
body: 0 Tama Tonga has responded after his social media post featuring Ilja Dragunov sparked speculation about a possible dig at the former WWE star following his AEW debut. The WWE wrestler has now addressed the conversation. He made it clear that his intentions may have been far less calculated than some observers suggested. The controversy began […] The post WWE’s Tama Tonga Responds To Claims He Took a Shot at Ilja Dragunov After AEW Debut appeared first on Wrestlezone . Tama Tonga has responded after his social media post featuring Ilja Dragunov sparked speculation about a possible dig at the former WWE star following his AEW debut. The WWE wrestler has now addressed the conversation. He made it clear that his intentions may have been far less calculated than some observers suggested. The controversy began when Tonga shared footage from SmackDown showing him absorbing Dragunov’s chops without selling their impact. The timing attracted attention because Dragunov had recently appeared in AEW. On Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer discussed Tonga’s post and questioned whether it was intended as a message to Dragunov. However, Meltzer acknowledged he did not know the reasoning behind the upload. “I don’t know if he was trying to get brownie points or someone told him to do it — I couldn’t tell you,” Meltzer said. He also compared the move to promotional tactics used by Bill Watts and Ole Anderson during the 1980s, when footage of wrestlers being beaten were used to promote competing promotions. “It’s like out of the Bill Watts, Ole Anderson playbook of the ’80s,” Meltzer explained. Tonga subsequently addressed the discussion on social media. He suggested that people were reading too much into a clip he simply considered worth sharing. He then rejected the suggestion that he had borrowed an old promotional strategy. “Great Uncle Dave over here said I took it from a playbook. I don’t even read a playbook, bruh,” Tonga said. "I put a post out about Dragunov and it started some sh*t" – Tama Tonga On Twitter by u/PrinceJohn_ in SquaredCircle Tonga also pushed back against wrestling reporters who contacted him seeking confirmation about the post, telling them to “get the f*ck outta here.” He accused Meltzer of making things up, while insisting nobody inside WWE instructed him to publish the footage. Neither the timing of the post nor Meltzer’s comparison establishes that Tonga intended to take a shot at Dragunov. For now, Tonga has dismissed the theory, leaving the online speculation without confirmation. body: October 22 2000 was the date of the WWF No Mercy PPV that year, which included the bizarre match between Rikishi and Steve Austin. It had been revealed that Rikishi “did it for The Rock” and ran over Stone Cold at Survivor Series back in 1999, and this was meant to be Austin’s revenge. Here is some of what Dave had to say about Rikishi vs Steve Austin from WWF No Mercy 2000: “But the biggest story as far as selling PPV buys was the return of Austin, and the competition of the first ever New York Mets vs. New York Yankees world series. Austin’s match left more questions than answers about his physical condition. He went out fast, and did a total gimmick oriented performance with Rikishi that had some brawling, no wrestling and only one or two bumps, and ended without any kind of a finish, even a stunner, leading one to believe they’re actually trying for long-term business. It seemed one more suited for a Raw episode or a bad movie than a PPV main event, but that’s probably why it was put early on the show, and they ended the show with long matches that on paper, and for that matter in the ring, figured to be excellent wrestling matches. “After bloodying Rikishi up, he put him in the bed of his truck, drove him outside the arena, deposited him on the ground, and went to run him over. A police car made the save, but in the process, Austin, who was drinking while driving, perhaps as another way to subtly get him over for an eventual heel turn, crashed into the police car twice, with the idea he had seriously injured an innocent officer, and was swarmed by officers, arrested and taken out. While most seem to think his close television alliance with Jim Ross is being pushed as a way for him to eventually turn on Ross to go heel, it is going to be interesting to watch the crowd manipulation involved in this one, being that Austin’s face turn was precipitated by the hoards of fans who cheered him while he was portrayed as such a strong heel.” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. title: AEW Group Changed Name Due To WWE RAW Concerns
raw_title: AEW Faction Dropped Original Name Over Potential WWE Conflict
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » AEW Faction Dropped Original Name Over Potential WWE Conflict David Finlay and Clark Connors had a different name in mind for their AEW faction before settling on The Dogs. However, a potential conflict with WWE reportedly got in the way. The duo originally wanted to call themselves the Raw Dogs, but the name was difficult to use because of its connection to RAW. Finlay and Connors currently compete in AEW alongside Gabe Kidd as The Dogs. The trio previously established themselves as members of the War Dogs faction in NJPW. During a recent appearance on What Happened When with Tony Schiavone , the wrestlers discussed how they came up with their current name. Connors revealed that The Dogs wasn’t their first choice when they arrived in AEW. The duo had another name in mind, but it came with a potential problem. “Well, when we came over here, we just became The Dogs, but we really wanted to pitch the name Raw Dogs. But I think there’s an issue with that whole Monday Night thing,” Connors said. “But it sounds cool because we’re raw f*cking dogs, you know?” he said. Despite having to go with another name, the duo seems happy with the result. Connors explained that The Dogs also has a strong identity and pointed out that no other major wrestling team had used the name the same way. “But The Dogs also is a sick name. It’s just no one’s ever done it before. No one’s been The Dogs,” Connors stated. Schiavone agreed that the name could become more recognizable as AEW continues featuring the faction on TV. He suggested that fans would get used to hearing it as the group appeared more often. Connors agreed. title: Results Recap: A Tribute to PAC Review: Wrestling at Its Finest — AEW Dynamite
raw_title: AEW Dynamite: A Tribute to PAC Review: Wrestling at Its Finest
body: Posted in: AEW , Sports , TV | Tagged: AEW Dynamite , pac , recaps , wrestling El Presidente reviews AEW Dynamite's emotional tribute to PAC, comrades, featuring Jon Moxley, Bryan Danielson's return, and wrestling at its finest. The show opened in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, with Excalibur and Tony Schiavone addressing the tragic loss of Benjamin Satterley , the man the world knew as PAC , "The Bastard." Excalibur spoke about Benjamin as a person, while Schiavone delivered remarks from the ring on behalf of All Elite Wrestling. Comrades, even my pet capybara Esteban, who typically only cries when his truffle supply runs low, shed a tear during this opening tribute. The broadcast then shifted to PAC's final on-camera appearance following All Out , where Jon Moxley addressed the Death Riders after his loss to AEW World Champion Will Ospreay . In that moment, Moxley spoke about getting back up after defeat—a lesson I myself learned after the CIA sabotaged my attempt to corner the international market on commemorative wrestling action figures. PAC was shown as the last member of the Death Riders to leave the frame, a haunting final image that will stay with me longer than the time I got stuck in an elevator with Steven Seagal for six hours. The AEW roster gathered on stage for a solemn 10-bell salute. The Death Riders' music played as a spotlight illuminated PAC's empty chair, draped with his towel—a simple but powerful symbol. Moxley received final words from his stablemates and walked past that chair on his way to the opening contest, carrying the weight of loss into battle like a true warrior. This reminded me of the time Kim Jong-un and I had to eulogize our favorite sushi chef—we honored him by eating seventeen courses in his memory. Moxley defended his AEW Continental Championship against Orange Cassidy , and in a moment that will live forever in wrestling history, Moxley applied PAC's signature Brutalizer submission hold during the closing stretch before finishing Cassidy with the Death Rider for the pinfall victory. But the true shock came in the aftermath, comrades, when Bryan Danielson made a surprise appearance. The two former rivals stood face to face, then embraced—a powerful moment of unity in grief that even moved the hardened capitalist pig executives at Warner Brothers Discovery. Page then teamed with Kenny Omega and the AEW World Tag Team Champions The Young Bucks in an 8-man tag match against the Don Callis Family 's Kevin Knight , Kyle Fletcher , and RPG Vice . The Elite secured victory when Page hit a Buckshot Lariat on Trent Beretta , Omega delivered a V-Trigger, the Bucks followed with a BTE Trigger, and Omega pinned Beretta after a One-Winged Angel. The four men embraced emotionally in the ring afterward, reminding us all that even in the cutthroat world of professional wrestling, solidarity among workers—I mean, wrestlers—is paramount. Cash Wheeler and Jay White shared their own tribute messages, followed by a deeply moving mom

At the style they worked, I’ve never seen one as good. If this show had streamed live, people, well other than the 400 fans at the American Legion Hall in Reseda, the entire hardcore wrestling world would be talking about it as match of the year and North American tag team match of the decade.

title: Cody Rhodes Expects Six or Seven More Years in WWE
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Thinks He'll Wrestle Six Or Seven More Years, Doesn't Want To Wrestle Until He's 50
summary_src: Cody Rhodes gives the latest update on his wrestling future. Cody recently revealed that he signed a new contract with WWE, which he says will be his last, though he didn't give a contract length. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight, Cody gave further color on his future wrestling plans.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Cody gave further color on his future wrestling plans. “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract, but that’s going to go for a while, and if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I’d love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go. I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years. Six, seven? I didn’t mean it like that, but yeah, you know that’s a kids’ thing, right? Had to have Carmelo Hayes explain to me what that was, and I still didn’t get it. Yeah, six, seven years. I’d say so. Yeah, and I don’t want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome,” he said. Asked if he plans on wrestling until he’s 50, he replied, “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s. I don’t want to overstay my welcome in a sense of this, right? So, I have been given so much from wrestling, and you have to think about my career in its totality. The things that we don’t talk about, the things that I don’t get asked about anymore. You have to think about all that. I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point, and I think that’s in that time frame, a point where you just have to stop taking. It’s giving me everything. I am talking to you today, the first time I talked to you, I was a mid-card talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the mid-card. Mid-card’s beautiful. I heard Triple H explain mid-card in a way that changed my perception of it forever. But I was a mid-card talent with a ceiling that was right above my head, and I’m talking to you today as someone who got to play Guile from Street Fighter, created by Capcom, a game that I played growing up as a little kid. Again, be careful what you wish for, but also I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get hopefully more, hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far and so blessed so far that I think wrestling. I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in.”
summary: Cody Rhodes told Chris Van Vliet that he recently signed what he considers his final WWE contract. He estimates he has around six or seven years left before he would like to step away from full-time wrestling to avoid overstaying his welcome. Rhodes added that he has no desire to wrestle into his 50s.

title: Cody Rhodes Recalls Early Hollywood Acting Pursuit
raw_title: Cody Rhodes looks back on moving to Hollywood at 19 to study acting
summary_src: While Cody Rhodes has Street Fighter on his résumé this year, his 19-year-old self once moved to Hollywood to pursue an acting career. Rhodes told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that he did not audition or book any roles then.
body: While Cody Rhodes has Street Fighter on his résumé this year, his 19-year-old self once moved to Hollywood to pursue an acting career. “I didn’t book any roles. I didn’t go on an audition. I got my Challenge for the Actor by Uta Hagen book, and I attended Comprehensive Technique with Howard Fine, and then instead of moving on to scene study, I became a stage manager at the Howard Fine Studio just to do Comprehensive Technique again, because I needed the kindergarten level, the first grade level,” said Rhodes. “I needed to completely build up, which was something I was saying on the carpet the other day for the premiere. I hope there’s so many more things for me to do in this world because I need to flex the muscle. “Wrestling can do so much for you as a storyteller, but the transition is different. You’ve seen it with John, you’ve seen it with Dwayne, you’ve seen it with Batista. My gosh, and some of the material he’s taking on. This isn’t a walk in the park. This is challenging. I was very challenged by Street Fighter, and you need those reps, and you need that time.” Despite moving to Hollywood at a young age, Rhodes maintains that wrestling has always been his first choice and top priority. Following in his late father Dusty Rhodes’ footsteps, Cody began his wrestling career in 2006 before making his WWE Raw debut a year later against Randy Orton. “I’m usually really quick to say no, because I grew up loving wrestling so much, and that was all I ever wanted to do. The story about seeing the picture at eight years old and wanting to win the WWE title, it’s a real story. But there’s a couple quotes from a 19-year-old where I might have said acting was the first dream, and even my brother has gone on to you know, Dustin’s good for a hot moment on social media, as you know. I think he’s gone on to say, oh, he always wanted to be an actor. I always wanted to be in entertainment, and the first love I had in the whole world, other than my mom, my sister, and my dad, was wrestling. So I think wrestling was always the thing.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. From a kindergarten teacher to PR Associate to turning her lifelong passion for the industry into a career, Rosanne is currently writing for F4W Online where she focuses on wrestling news, analysis, and storytelling. Rosanne previously contributed to Sportskeeda as an Assistant Content Manager. When not consumed by wrestling, Rosanne is a musician and an aspiring artist.

Instead of advancing to scene study, he took a position as stage manager at the Howard Fine Studio to repeat the foundational course.
Rhodes explained that he required basic level training to build his skills from the beginning. He expressed a desire to continue exploring new opportunities in order to develop his abilities further.

He noted that wrestling provides strong storytelling experience, yet the shift to acting presents distinct challenges. Rhodes cited the transitions made by other wrestlers into film roles as examples of the difficulties involved. He found his work in Street Fighter particularly demanding and emphasized the need for repeated practice.

Despite his early attempt at acting, Rhodes has maintained that wrestling remained his primary interest and top priority. He followed his father Dusty Rhodes into the profession, starting his wrestling career in 2006 and debuting on WWE Raw the following year against Randy Orton.

Rhodes stated that he typically declines other opportunities because of his lifelong passion for wrestling. He recalled a childhood desire to win the WWE title. While some past comments from age 19 suggested acting as an initial dream, he affirmed that wrestling was always his first love in entertainment.

body: The Rock returned to the ring for the first time in a serious manner in over a decade when he teamed with Roman Reigns against Cody Rhodes & Seth Rollins at night one of WrestleMania 40. On Insight with Chris Van Vliet , Cody was asked if he was ever supposed to have a one-on-one match with The Rock. “Oof. It’s not that I’m evading that answer. It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40 and another guy who he’s given all, continues to give all as part of the board. He could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring. That’ll be up to him. That’ll certainly be up to him if there’s more and what those matches might be. I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that,” he said. Rock has not appeared on television since WWE Elimination Chamber 2024 when Cody turned down Rock’s demand for his soul, and was immediately attacked by John Cena.

With WrestleMania 43 on the horizon, Triple H and WWE Creative have a chance to make the event feel special with a few key storytelling and character-development changes. From elevating new stars to making every championship match count, here are changes that could help make next year's WrestleMania an event fans won't want to miss. Why The Bloodline Will Destroy 946 💀 Bleacher Report 18h Dragon Lee, Jordynne Grace, More 🤫 Bleacher Report 18h Breakker, Dragunov, More Rumors 👂 Bleacher Report 1d Create New WrestleMania Main Eventers WrestleMania needs fresh faces in its biggest matches, and Triple H should use the months leading up to the event to establish new main-event contenders. WrestleMania 43 should feature stars who are ready to take the next step, giving audiences a reason to be excited about the company's future as well as its present. Let Established Stars Put Over the Next Generation Creating new main-eventers means very little if WWE refuses to let them win the matches that matter most. Triple H needs to be willing to book rising stars to defeat established names cleanly on the WrestleMania stage, giving them a career-defining moment that can change their standing overnight. Established Superstars can still play important roles without winning every major match, and passing the torch can benefit everyone involved. A young wrestler defeating a respected veteran at WrestleMania gives fans a memorable moment while creating new possibilities for the months ahead. WWE should use WrestleMania 43 to establish who belongs at the top of the card, rather than simply reinforcing the existing pecking order. Stop Overloading WrestleMania WrestleMania has grown into a massive two-night spectacle, but adding more matches does not automatically make the event better. Both nights should have a distinct identity, with a carefully paced lineup that builds toward the biggest matches and strongest moments. title: Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods sign 5-year AEW deals
raw_title: Former WWE stars sign new 5-year AEW deal
body: Earlier this year at AEW All In 2026, former WWE Superstars Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods made their All Elite Wrestling debut . Going with Kofi and Austin Creed, the duo made their debut in the Trios title match. Paired with Swerve Strickland, the three of them won the AEW Trios Championship before losing it to Adam Page, Bandido, and Brody King at AEW WrestleDream 2026. Now, Fightful Select has reported a major update on New Level's [Kofi & Austin Creed] AEW contract. "New Level signed five-year AEW contracts," Fightful Select said. According to the report, Kofi and Creed were pitched to join AEW and work with Strickland. It was also added that Strickland played a major role in bridging the relationship between the duo and AEW, as Tony Khan was hesitant to speak with them before their WWE contract was over. Just days after making their AEW debut, Kofi and Creed of The New Level appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show, where they opened up in detail about their alleged WWE pay cut. "Compensation was definitely a big part, but more so, we wanted to work. We wanted to go out there and showcase our skills and showcase our talents. We wanted to do what we love. We love going out there and messing with fans, threatening to ground kids, and really garner reactions to people, and send them home with incredible memories they'll never forget. I don't know exactly what's out there. I will say, it was more than 50 percent, which a lot of people don't know," Kofi said.

They teamed with Swerve Strickland to capture the Trios Championship in their first match before dropping the titles to Adam Page, Bandido and Brody King at WrestleDream 2026. Per Fightful Select, the pair has now signed five-year contracts with AEW after Strickland helped facilitate talks with Tony Khan.

body: We’ve been following the sluggish ticket sales of Bound for Glory. Just a week ago, the flagship TNA event had distributed just over 700 tickets, leaving the Tampa Yuengling Center over 70% empty. This past week, WWE and TNA’s partnership came under question. WWE has a history of comping tickets to make an event look full and add to the gate in terms of merchandise. title: El Desperado Pulled From NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 & CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom Due To Spinal Stenosis And Hernia
raw_title: El Desperado Pulled From NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 & CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom Due To Spinal Stenosis And Hernia
body: You are using an outdated, unsupported browser. Please upgrade your browser to experience this site properly. New Japan Pro Wrestling announced that they have pulled El Desperado from their upcoming Super Junior Tag League 2026 tournament due to spinal stenosis and a hernia in his leg. It was also announced that Masatora Yasuda will be replacing El Desperado as Mistico’s tag team partner for the tournament. It was also announced that El Desperado has also been pulled from their upcoming co-promoted CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom event on November 15 at the Arena Mexico in Mexico City, Mexico as well. We apologise to fans who were looking forward to seeing Desperado compete, and appreciate your understanding. In a video released on YouTube, Desperado stated: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms, but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that, and asked to continue wrestling, while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don’t worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he’ll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that’s it. I’m off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) ‘Gaspe’ Invitational. I can’t move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we’ll be going ahead as planned. Show up.” New Japan Pro-Wrestling joins fans in wishing Desperado a speedy, full recovery.
summary: New Japan Pro Wrestling revealed that they have pulled El Desperado from their forthcoming Super Junior Tag League 2026 tournament due to spinal stenosis and a hernia in his leg. It was additionally revealed that El Desperado has also been pulled from their forthcoming co-promoted CMLL x NJPW Lucha Kingdom event on November 15 at the Arena Mexico in Mexico City.

title: Cody Rhodes Discusses Potential Match With The Rock
raw_title: Cody Rhodes comments on possible match against The Rock in WWE
summary_src: Cody Rhodes addressed possibly wanting a singles match against The Rock given their storied WWE history. When Chris Van Vliet asked Rhodes about a potential match against The Rock on the Insight Podcast, Rhodes said the decision ultimately rests with him.
body: Cody Rhodes addressed possibly wanting a singles match against The Rock given their storied WWE history. “It’s not that I’m evading that answer. It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40 and another guy who he’s given all, continues to give all as part of the Board. He could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring. That’ll be up to him,” stated Rhodes. “That’ll certainly be up to him if there’s more and what those matches might be. I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that.” Following WrestleMania 40, it seemed the chapter had closed on Rhodes’ rivalry with The Rock. However, last year, The Rock confronted the then Undisputed WWE Champion with a pitch to join forces. Rhodes’ refusal led to John Cena’s heel turn at Elimination Chamber. Since then, The Rock has remained absent from WWE television and with his Hollywood commitments keeping him busy, the possibility of an in-ring return remains uncertain. title: Contract News: Kofi and Austin Creed’s AEW Contract Lengths Revealed
raw_title: Kofi and Austin Creed’s AEW Contract Lengths Revealed
summary_src: Kofi and Austin Creed aren’t just sticking around AEW for a short run. The New Level have reportedly signed five-year contracts with the company, and Swerve Strickland apparently played a major role in helping bring the two longtime WWE stars through the door.
body: According to Fightful Select on October 22, both Kofi and Creed agreed to five-year AEW deals. That gives AEW a pretty serious long-term commitment from the duo after their arrival at All In. There’s also an interesting story behind how the relationship came together. Fightful reported that The New Level were pitched for AEW with the idea of working with Swerve Strickland, who ended up becoming an important link between the two sides. Strickland played a big part in bridging that relationship while Kofi and Creed were still unavailable for direct negotiations. Tony Khan wouldn’t speak with them until they were contractually free, meaning Swerve was apparently helping lay the groundwork before AEW could actually get involved. That makes the timing of their eventual contracts even more interesting. Kofi previously revealed that he and Creed weren’t officially signed to AEW until less than 24 hours before All In , so things apparently moved pretty quickly once they were legally free to negotiate. Since arriving, Kofi and Creed have also made it clear that AEW offered them more than another place to wrestle. Speaking on Inside the Ring , Creed said the freedom to continue building his presence in gaming was a major benefit of the move . “The ability to do stuff in that space in the way that I want to do it, knowing that I will be the one reaping the fruits of my labor as that tree grows, and possibly being able to bring other people in the locker room into that to bear that fruit as well.” Kofi revealed that those outside opportunities were actually discussed while their contracts were being negotiated. He described their AEW deals as particularly wrestler-friendly when it comes to pursuing projects away from the ring. “There’s a lot of things in there that are very, I guess, player-friendly, right? Like wrestler-friendly, you know, in terms of being able to go out and do what it is that you want to do.” The New Level may have gotten their AEW contracts done at the last possible minute before All In, but these clearly aren’t short-term deals thrown together for one big appearance. With five-year contracts in place and Swerve helping open the door in the first place, AEW appears to have had much bigger plans for Kofi and Creed from the start. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Admits “Cody Fatigue” Has Already Set In Among WWE Fans

summary_src: Cody Rhodes knows his wrestling career isn’t going to last forever, and he’s already thinking about when it’ll be time to walk away.
body: Cody jokingly admitted that his old retirement promise didn’t exactly hold up. With his 40th birthday already behind him, he called it another one of his old “Cody lies.” “I just think the — I just signed my last contract. I say last contract — that’s gonna go for a while. And if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies.” “With all that said, my time with WWE could go — I mean, just to give you a real answer here and not politic around you — probably, probably seven. Seven years.” “Six, seven. Yeah. I didn’t mean it like that, but yeah. You know, that’s the kids’ thing, right? To have Carmelo Hayes explain to me what that was and I still didn’t get it. Yeah, six, seven years, I’d say.” The bigger issue for Cody isn’t hitting one specific age. He simply doesn’t want to reach a point where fans are ready for him to leave and he’s still hanging around. “And I don’t want to say that in a final, like a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” One thing Cody does seem pretty certain about is wrestling into his 50s. While he made it clear there’s nothing wrong with other wrestlers doing it, that’s not how he sees his own career playing out. “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s.” “I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point.” Cody believes that moment probably falls somewhere inside the six-to-seven-year window he’s imagining now. He’s not ready to leave yet, but he already understands that he doesn’t want to keep taking opportunities forever. “And I think that’s in that timeframe — a point where you just have to stop taking.” It’s especially striking for Cody when he looks at how dramatically his career has changed. He remembered his first conversation with Van Vliet coming at a time when he was still a WWE midcard wrestler who felt like there was a very obvious ceiling above him. “It’s given me everything. I am talking to you today — the first time I talked to you, I was a midcard talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the midcard. Midcard’s beautiful.” Now Cody’s career has taken him far beyond anything he could have imagined back then. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Speaks On Whether WWE Planned a Singles Match With The Rock
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Addresses Whether WWE Planned a Singles Match With The Rock
summary_src: Cody Rhodes still isn’t saying whether WWE ever actually planned to put him in the ring with The Rock. What he will say is that he personally believes The Rock might still have a couple of matches left in him — and Cody isn’t ruling out being involved in one of them. Speaking to Chris ...
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Cody was taken back to Elimination Chamber in Perth, where he publicly called out The Rock for a one-on-one match. Van Vliet wanted to know whether that challenge was actually supposed to lead somewhere. “Oof. It’s not that I’m evading that answer. It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think, personally, he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally.” Cody never confirmed that WWE had a match between them booked or even formally planned. Instead, he explained that he can also see a scenario where The Rock decides his WrestleMania 40 appearance was the perfect way to finish his in-ring career. “But I also know, looking at WrestleMania 40 — and another guy who has given all, continues to give all as part of the board — he could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring.” Ultimately, Cody Rhodes believes that decision belongs entirely to The Rock. If he wants to wrestle again, Cody thinks there are still matches on the table, but nobody else can make that call for him. “That’ll be up to him. That’ll certainly be up to him, if there’s more and what those matches might be.” As for whether Cody himself would want one of those matches, there wasn’t much mystery there. He made it clear that practically any wrestler would jump at the opportunity to share the ring with The Rock. “I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that.” Cody also believes WWE is currently in such an unpredictable period that it’s difficult to completely dismiss almost any major match. He pointed to the company’s continued momentum and argued that wrestling fans are watching an era where unexpected things can still happen. “This isn’t me trying to justify anything, but, yeah, no, you are part of an era that’s the most unpredictable time in wrestling, really. It’s unpredictable.” That’s where Cody finally left the door open for the match everyone has been wondering about. He still wouldn’t say that Cody Rhodes vs. The Rock was ever officially the plan, but he isn’t ready to say it’ll never happen either. title: Vince McMahon Accused of Being a “Psychopath” and “Abuser”
raw_title: Vince McMahon Accused of Being a “Psychopath” and “Abuser”
summary_src: Jimmy Jacobs isn’t holding back when it comes to what it was like working for Vince McMahon in WWE. The former WWE writer called McMahon a “psychopath,” a “bully” and an “abuser” while explaining why he found working under him so difficult.
body: “There is no pleasing the mad king. I had a challenging time working for Vince. Yeah.” When the interviewer suggested that people who genuinely loved wrestling sometimes had a particularly difficult time working with McMahon, Jacobs took things much further. He said he viewed McMahon as a “crazy person” before repeatedly describing him as a psychopath. “Vince is a—he was a crazy person. Vince McMahon was like a psychopath. Like a psychopath. Vince McMahon was a psychopath.” Jacobs made it clear he wasn’t simply throwing the word around for dramatic effect. In his personal assessment of McMahon, he believed that was genuinely the type of personality he was dealing with. “That’s the sort of personality type he is, right? He’s like an overt malignant narcissist. Not to use catchphrase words, because I’m not using that hyperbolically. I’m using that like that’s his personality type.” “I was around Vince McMahon not very long before I saw, ‘Oh, I wouldn’t trade places with this guy for one second.’ Not for one second.” Jacobs then offered an even harsher assessment of McMahon’s character. These were Jacobs’ personal claims and descriptions of his former boss, but he didn’t leave much room for interpretation about how he felt. “Because for everything he has, he has nothing because he’s a psychopath. And when you’re a psychopath, you’re incapable of love. And so Vince McMahon’s a bully. He’s a maniac. He’s an abuser.” Jacobs also addressed the negative stories that have emerged about McMahon over the years. From his own experience around him, Jacobs claimed those stories fit with the person he knew. “He’s all of the things that, you know, ‘Oh, this has come out. Is this like Vince?’ Every story you’ve heard about him, it’s something like true. Like, that’s who he is.” “So yeah, it’s hard. It’s hard to work for bullies and psychopaths. That’s challenging, and I had a challenging time with that, and other people did too.” Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out Wrestling Social Media for Creating Fake Controversies
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out Wrestling Social Media for Creating Fake Controversies
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has a problem with the way wrestling controversies are being created on social media these days.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Cody admitted wrestling media is much harder to navigate now than it used to be. He joked that he was about to get on his “boomer high horse” before explaining exactly what bothers him. “Dude, media is hard these days. I bet you just did your Mount Rushmore. They’re already coming for you. They’re already — it’s hard. Like, it’s not what it used to be. And this is specific to the wrestling media.” Cody believes there are certain wrestling conversations that can appear much bigger online than they actually are. From his perspective, something being discussed heavily on social media doesn’t automatically mean it was already a genuine issue elsewhere. “I’m gonna get on my little boomer high horse here, right? I’m not a boomer, but I want to be. Okay, so there are conversations that take place online in the wrestling community. Here’s what I just wish that people would know: they only take place online.” He then gave an example of how quickly that can snowball. Somebody might claim a wrestler is getting heat over something, and suddenly dozens of people are responding to a controversy that Cody says wasn’t actually happening in the first place. “And I’ll give you a prime example — and this is gonna sound… I feel so bad that I’ve now gone into this rant. Somebody will say something like, ‘I can’t believe she’s getting so much heat for this.’ And then 50 people will reply.” That’s where Cody thinks social media can actually create the very controversy people believe they’re simply discussing. Once the wrestler involved responds or signal-boosts it, the online chatter becomes something much more real. When Van Vliet asked what he meant, Cody immediately became reluctant to even repeat the subject because that would risk starting the conversation all over again. Once Chris mentioned the “best friends” topic, Cody made it clear he’d rather leave it alone. Van Vliet then asked the bigger question: with so much noise surrounding Cody at this stage of his career, how does he decide which opinions actually deserve his attention? Cody admitted his earlier claim that these conversations “only” happen online was too absolute. “I think probably the most important thing is don’t be absolute. So I just gave you an absolute. I said those conversations are only taking place there. That’s not true. That conversation might be happening, right? But then there might be a conversation over here that’s important, and a mentor or a voice.” For Cody, the voices that ultimately need to carry the most weight are the fans actually showing up to WWE events. Those are the people giving their time and energy to the product, and he believes their reactions have to be prioritized over all the other noise surrounding him. “And then there’s, of course, the most important voices — the ones in the arena with us. The ones who are there giving their time and their energy to you to be entertained and to take an escape. I think it’s prioritizing that. That’s wh
summary: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Cody admitted wrestling media is much harder to navigate now than it used to be. And this is specific to the wrestling media. Cody believes there are certain wrestling conversations that can appear much bigger online than they actually are.

title: Reason Behind Dralistico’s Cryptic Jail Tweet Amid AEW Exit Speculation
raw_title: Reason Behind Dralistico’s Cryptic Jail Tweet Amid AEW Exit Speculation
summary_src: Dralistico’s AEW future might not be heading toward an exit after all. Despite his contract reportedly running out in December and that bizarre “behind bars” post getting everyone talking, AEW apparently wants to keep him around.
body: Dave Meltzer revealed on Wrestling Observer Radio that AEW plans to make Dralistico a new contract offer. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll accept it, but the company apparently isn’t planning to just let his deal expire without trying to keep him. “From the AEW standpoint, they are going to make him an offer.” That’s a pretty big change from how things looked just a few days ago. Dralistico recently posted an AI-generated image of himself behind bars with his hands cuffed and wrote, “Maybe not for long?” “I was told from people close to him that the thing with the bars and everything, that’s because of the visa issue.” Meltzer also specifically pushed back on the idea that Dralistico is counting down the days until he can leave. He compared the situation to Rey Fenix and said this apparently isn’t another case of a luchador desperately wanting out of AEW. “It’s not because he can’t wait to leave like Fenix. His contract is up soon.” The visa explanation also makes Dralistico’s lengthy absence a little more interesting. He hasn’t wrestled for AEW since the June 6 episode of Collision , when he teamed with RUSH and Sammy Guevara in a losing effort against The Conglomeration for the AEW World Trios Championship. Dralistico originally debuted for AEW in December 2022 before officially signing in October 2023. He’s only wrestled 51 matches across AEW and Ring of Honor since arriving, so his run hasn’t exactly been packed with television time. Of course, AEW wanting Dralistico back doesn’t mean he’s staying. His current contract is still expiring in December, and there’s no indication yet that he’s agreed to whatever the company plans to put in front of him. raw_title: Cody Rhodes says he still feels the effects of Randy Orton’s punt kick from WWE WrestleMania
summary_src: Cody Rhodes claims he still feels the effects of Randy Orton’s punt kick to the face at WWE WrestleMania. Rhodes believes the orbital fracture significantly slowed him down and affected his work. He disclosed his peripheral vision being impacted on the Insight Podcast.
body: Cody Rhodes claims he still feels the effects of Randy Orton’s punt kick to the face at WWE WrestleMania. “I think we skated by with a little bit of an orbital fracture, and that’s not on anyone’s fault but my own…It was bad….I think we skated by a little bit of an orbital fracture, and I think I am mad at myself for doing so because it’s affected my work since, super slowed down.” Rhodes briefly recalled his pectoral muscle injury in 2022 , and cited his passion for wrestling preventing him from staying away from the ring. “I’m letting you know that’s not good. If you’re a young wrestler, don’t do it. Don’t! Live to fight another day. Something about me can’t not want to go. I don’t know what it is. I love it too much. Maybe it’s ego. I don’t know, but I just can’t not. Yeah, that was a nasty one.” After his WrestleMania appearance, Orton returned at SummerSlam to cost Rhodes the Undisputed WWE Title in his bout against CM Punk. The two have since continued their rivalry on SmackDown. title: Cody Rhodes Stays Quiet On Marvel Studios Meeting
raw_title: WWE's Cody Rhodes Remains Tight-Lipped About Marvel Studios Meeting Over The Summer
summary_src: Though he remains discreet on if there are plans in motion for him to star in any upcoming films or shows, Cody Rhodes describes his summer visit to Marvel Studios.
body: "There's one guy [Andrew Schulz] in particular, who was sitting next to me on this couch pretty much all day, who is teasing things that aren't real, and if they were real, I wouldn't say anything, and guessing characters that are great, great characters, because I grew up... I learned every Marvel character you could from the trading cards, and then, of course, I had the animated series, and we have it again now. It's been heavily discussed, but I never discuss it," the former three-time Undisputed Champion said. "That's the beauty. I've said nothing other than that was just a photo at a wonderful office after a wonderful meeting with wonderful people." Coming off the highly charged role as Guile in Kitao Sakurai's "Street Fighter," Rhodes is flying back in the ring with a lot of rage and disdain after his recent loss to his former friend turned nemesis, Randy Orton, at Sunday Night's Main Event back in September. Last week on "WWE SmackDown," Rhodes got his hands on "The Viper" by hitting him with a Cody Cutter before Baron Corbin interrupted their impromptu fight.

title: Injury Update: Cody Rhodes’s WrestleMania 42 Injury Was Worse Than Initially Believed
raw_title: Cody Rhodes’s WrestleMania 42 Injury Was Worse Than Initially Believed
summary_src: Cody Rhodes came back from his nasty WrestleMania 42 eye injury almost immediately, but apparently he was dealing with more than everyone realized. Cody now says he suffered a minor orbital fracture that affected his peripheral vision and “super slowed down” his work after WrestleMania.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on October 22, Cody looked back at the injury he suffered during his match against Randy Orton. While he managed to avoid a more serious fracture, he admitted there was still some orbital damage. “I think we skated by with a little bit of an orbital fracture, and that’s not on anyone’s fault but my own… It was bad.” “I think we skated by a little bit of an orbital fracture, and I think I am mad at myself for doing so because it’s affected my work since, super slowed down.” The injury didn’t just leave Cody with a nasty-looking swollen eye either. When Van Vliet asked whether his peripheral vision had been affected, Cody confirmed that it had been impacted to some degree. “Yeah, just to a degree, to a little bit, and I feel like that’s—you can’t go out there QB1 and saying you’re in your prime, and you’re the best you’ve ever been if you’re dealing with something that’s a bit of a hindrance like that.” The good news is Cody says he’s finally past it. Whatever issues he was dealing with following WrestleMania aren’t something he considers an ongoing problem anymore. “I showed up the next night. I am toxic as can be when it comes to physical stuff. Toxic as can be. I can go. Tape it up. I can go.” It’s hardly the first time Cody has done that. His torn pectoral muscle in 2022 became one of the most memorable examples when he still wrestled Seth Rollins inside Hell in a Cell despite the gruesome injury. Cody knows that kind of mentality isn’t something younger wrestlers should be copying. In fact, he went out of his way to warn them against following his example when they’re legitimately hurt. “I’m letting you know that’s not good. If you’re a young wrestler, don’t do it. Don’t! Live to fight another day.” The problem is Cody doesn’t seem entirely sure how to follow his own advice. Whether it’s his love of wrestling or simply his ego, he admitted there’s something inside him that makes sitting on the sidelines incredibly difficult. “Something about me can’t not want to go. I don’t know what it is. I love it too much. Maybe it’s ego. I don’t know, but I just can’t not. Yeah, that was a nasty one.” Cody previously explained that returning so quickly after WrestleMania was about consistency and proving he could continue being WWE’s “QB1 .” Now he’s admitting that decision came with a price, as the injury continued affecting his work and vision even after he was back on television. Paige got the better of her former tag team partner, Nikki Bella, while Rey Fenix retained his AAA Cruiserweight Championship against Ricky Saints. "SmackDown" ended with a match between Cody Rhodes and Baron Corbin, during which Rhodes finally delivered the punt after Randy Orton appeared near the ring. However, the punt was aimed at Corbin, leaving Orton watching in shock from the ramp. The show also had an unfortunate moment when veteran star R-Truth suffered an injury during his match against his former tag team partner, Damian Priest, which ended in a no contest.

title: AEW Star Will Ospreay Dealt With Body Dysmorphia During NJPW Run
raw_title: AEW Star Will Ospreay Dealt With Body Dysmorphia During NJPW Run
body: During a recent interview with "Muscle & Fitness," Ospreay opened up about his battle with body dysmorphia when he was competing for New Japan Pro Wrestling at the age of 24, explaining that he faced many insecurities in the gym along with online criticism about his in-ring shape. "I first discovered my body dysmorphia, and I won the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Championship, in October of 2017," Ospreay revealed. "And I remember one tweet was saying 'he is in the worst shape,' and they were right ... I didn't understand working out, why you do sets, and why you focus on one body part, and macro counting. I would go to the gym, but I really didn't know what I was doing, I'll be honest, and I was so embarrassed to ask the boys, they're all jacked, I felt like such an idiot, to try and (ask) 'could I workout with you?' so I never went to the gym." During his struggles with body dysmorphia, Ospreay would discover MusclePharm's weekly workouts while he was wrestling in New Zealand and partnered with a personal trainer in order to achieve the physical appearance he was looking for in a healthy way. "I just said, alright, I'm gonna do these for the next six weeks," he said. "Within four weeks, I packed on so much muscle mass, and I started to understand how it worked. And then I invested in a personal trainer, his name is Iestyn Ress, and he really broke down macro counting, and how to count my calories, and why I do a push day and a pull day. It was so simple, but I just never had the courage to ask for help. And I always tell people now, the people in the gym, they're fighting the same demons that you're probably fighting." Nearly a decade later, Ospreay is arguably in the best shape of his entire career and is now the face of the men's division in AEW after defeating Kenny Omega at All In: London last weekend to become world champion. In addition to Ospreay's win, six other title changes occurred at All In, including Mercedes Mone becoming the AEW Women's World Champion, and Darby Allin defeating Kevin Knight for the TNT Title with the help with his former tag team partner, Sting.
summary: Ospreay opened up about his battle with body dysmorphia when he was competing for New Japan Pro Wrestling at the age of 24. I first discovered my body dysmorphia, and I won the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Championship, in October of 2017, Ospreay disclosed.

title: Cody Rhodes plans WWE run of six to seven years
