summary_src: Cody Rhodes discussed his current WWE contract and addressed previous statements on plans to wrestle until the age of 40. The WWE star told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that he estimates his current contract to run for another six or seven years.
body: Cody Rhodes discussed his current WWE contract and addressed previous statements on plans to wrestle until the age of 40. “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract, but that’s going to go for a while, and if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I’d love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go,” said Rhodes. “I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years……Yeah, six, seven years. I’d say so. Yeah, and I don’t want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” In the same interview, Vliet referenced AJ Styles’ statement of not wanting to wrestle into his 50s, and questioned whether Rhodes felt the same sentiments. “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s. I don’t want to overstay my welcome in a sense of this, right? So, I have been given so much from wrestling, and you have to think about my career in its totality. The things that we don’t talk about, the things that I don’t get asked about anymore. You have to think about all that. I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point, and I think that’s in that time frame, a point where you just have to stop taking. It’s giving me everything.” “I am talking to you today, the first time I talked to you, I was a mid-card talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the mid-card. Mid-card’s beautiful. I heard Triple H explain mid-card in a way that changed my perception of it forever. But I was a mid-card talent with a ceiling that was right above my head, and I’m talking to you today as someone who got to play Guile from Street Fighter, created by Capcom, a game that I played growing up as a little kid. Again, be careful what you wish for, but also I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get hopefully more, hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far and so blessed so far that I think wrestling. I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. title: On the Record: RevPro’s Andy Quildan on pulling Leon Slater match from MyAEW feed: ‘Maybe we did the wrong thing’
raw_title: RevPro’s Andy Quildan on pulling Leon Slater match from MyAEW feed: ‘Maybe we did the wrong thing’
body: Among the numerous headlines from RevPro’s massive 14th anniversary show last month, one was, unfortunately, tied to industry drama. Those who watched the prominent BritWres brand’s London event via MyAEW PPV noticed that one match didn’t air on the feed: TNA Wrestling’s Leon Slater facing fellow UK star Liam Slater. Initially, many wondered whether the match not airing on MyAEW was a decision made by TNA, who has pulled their talent from matchups involving AEW wrestlers in the past. But, in the days that followed, it came out that RevPro owner Andy Quildan was actually the one who made the move not to put the match on the service. Quildan initially explained to F4WOnline’s Dave Meltzer that he wanted to avoid any issues that could come from putting a TNA talent on an AEW service. He also stressed that the decision came without any influence from either company. In a recent interview with POST Wrestling, RevPro’s Quildan was asked if he will continue to black out appearances from TNA stars when they present shows on MyAEW going forward. Still reflecting on the decision, Quildan was undecided. “I’m not sure, to be honest,” he said. “I was trying to make everyone’s life as easy as possible. My role, as an independent wrestling promoter, has always been to get the match in the ring to try and have foresight. You try to envision every single problem that could occur before it becomes a problem. And the last thing we want is for anything to become an issue on the day, or post-show, or anything like that. And it’s crazy; with the benefit of hindsight, maybe we did the wrong thing, because that almost created more attention on the situation. I think, as we do with everything, we have to learn, we have to evolve, we have to adapt and move forward.” “I don’t want to be involved in any wrestling politics. I always say, we are open to do good business with anyone. I know in business it’s almost impossible, especially when there’s so much tribalism that goes around, but I want to be on the good side of everyone. And I want everyone to know that when they do business with us, we will do good business and we will try and do best by the company, and I don’t want anything to be received as, we’re trying to sneak people into places.” As a way to make up for the blackout, RevPro has uploaded Slater’s match onto Youtube for free. In regard to RevPro’s future on MyAEW, Quildan noted that he plans to be selective about which shows could be sold as PPVs on the service. He explained that some of the venues they run don’t have a reliable internet connection, and that he wouldn’t want to sell PPVs for shows where a feed might struggle to stay on air. title: WWE NXT Expected to Go Head-to-Head With AEW Blood & Guts on November 4
raw_title: WWE NXT Expected to Go Head-to-Head With AEW Blood & Guts on November 4
summary_src: WWE NXT is about to find itself in a pretty unusual Wednesday night fight. The November 4 episode is expected to move away from its normal Tuesday slot, putting NXT directly against AEW’s annual Blood & Guts edition of Dynamite.
body: Upcoming listings for NXT, including Netflix and Futon Critic , currently have the show airing Wednesday, November 4. The move comes because The CW will have coverage tied to the U.S. midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3. “I don’t know this 100%. I was told by people who know that CW wants to move NXT to that Wednesday. It probably will be moved because if it’s on Tuesday, it’ll be preempted on far too many stations.” The problem for WWE is that Wednesday isn’t exactly an empty night. AEW already has Blood & Guts lined up for November 4, with two Blood & Guts matches set for what is traditionally one of Dynamite’s biggest special episodes of the year. “That’s the night of Blood and Guts. AEW has the two Blood and Guts matches they set up tonight that are going to be pretty wild.” Things get even stranger because NXT wouldn’t be WWE’s only programming running that night. WWE EVOLVE airs Wednesdays at 8 PM ET on Tubi, while Main Event recently moved to the same time slot on Rumble. That means WWE could have three different shows airing against AEW Dynamite at the same time. As Meltzer pointed out, WWE wouldn’t just be competing with Blood & Guts — its own shows would also be competing with each other for wrestling fans. “WWE will actually have three shows going against Blood and Guts. They’re going to have NXT, which isn’t 100% but is probable, the Evolve show, and the Main Event show, all at the same time.” For AEW, the timing means Blood & Guts suddenly has a lot more wrestling competition than expected. Meltzer described the situation as WWE going up against one of AEW’s signature shows while simultaneously splitting its own Wednesday night audience across three programs. “They’re competing with themselves on three levels, and they’re competing with one of AEW’s signature shows of the year on their own night.” This doesn’t appear to be WWE deliberately moving NXT to Wednesday just to counter AEW, since the midterm election coverage is driving the expected schedule change. Still, the end result is another NXT versus Dynamite showdown, only this time WWE could have three different shows fighting for viewers on the exact same night. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Speaks On Wrestling Tribalism After Joining AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Addresses Wrestling Tribalism After Joining AEW
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov isn’t interested in picking sides when it comes to the tribalism between wrestling fans.
body: Speaking to Jon Alba of The TakeDown on SI , Dragunov was asked about the divided wrestling fanbase and all the different styles currently being shown on national television. For Dragunov, the tribalism ultimately comes from the same place that makes wrestling work in the first place — emotion. “I mean, this is a good question. I mean, there are multiple questions layered into this about tribalism. I believe this is an emotionally driven business because, at the end of the day, wherever you watch professional wrestling, people go there to feel something.” Dragunov didn’t criticize fans for preferring one promotion over another either. As far as he’s concerned, people finding that emotional connection with wrestling is what actually matters. “You know, this is what they want to do. If they do it on one side, that’s okay. If they do it on the other side, that’s okay.” That attitude also ties into how Dragunov approaches his own matches. While wrestling can come in plenty of different forms, he has always viewed what he does as a combination of legitimate-looking combat and art. Dragunov then pointed to some of the wrestlers who helped shape that philosophy. His list stretched across different eras and styles, but they all shared the ability to make what happened inside the ring feel like something more than just a collection of moves. “That’s what all my role models did, like Kobashi, Terry Funk, Roddy Piper, William Regal, Meiko Satomura.” That’s also a big part of why Dragunov believes AEW is the right place for him now. He feels the company is looking for exactly the kind of dramatic, fight-heavy wrestling he’s spent his career trying to create. “And I feel like these values and what I’m standing for, to really be, in my mind, about the most dramatic and beautiful fight, is what AEW is looking for.” Dragunov isn’t trying to turn his arrival in AEW into another WWE-versus-AEW argument. For him, the bigger opportunity is getting to bring his own idea of what wrestling should feel like to a company he believes is actively looking for it. body: El Desperado has been ruled out of the NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 due to injury. New Japan Pro-Wrestling announced on Thursday, October 22, that one-half of the current IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions, El Desperado, has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. El Desperado and Mistico were originally drawn in Block A. However, with the former having been ruled out, Mistico will now team with NJPW Young Lion Masatora Yasuda. Desperado said his body has reached its limit and apologized to fans. No timeline is currently set for his return. Here’s what he said: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles, I’m currently unable to stand, walk, or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that and asked to continue wrestling while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. “For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW.” -> Mistico & Masatora Yasuda -> Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X -> Yoshinobu Kanemaru & DOUKI -> Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi -> Master Wato & KUUKAI -> KUSHIDA & Nick Wayne -> Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita -> YOH & Hyo -> Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young -> Titan & Daiki Nagai -> SHO & Dick Togo -> Blake Christian & Lee Johnson The tournament will get underway in Saitama, Japan, on October 24. title: Ilja Dragunov Feels Creative Freedom In AEW
raw_title: Former WWE Star Ilja Dragunov On His Experience Since Joining AEW: 'I Feel Freedom'
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has praised his AEW experience so far, explaining how joining the promotion has given him a sense of freedom.
body: Dragunov, who was let go by WWE earlier this year, debuted in Tony Khan's promotion at the WrestleDream pay-per-view . Following his AEW debut, the former WWE United States Champion spoke to " The Takedown on SI ," saying that his initial impressions of the company are great and that he felt a great sense of freedom there. "It lets my heart beat faster, and I feel like I re-fell in love with professional wrestling in some kind of way. The experience that I've had so far is having people around me that really want to portray everything that is going on in my mind, that really understand what I'm doing," said Dragunov. "They want to enhance what I'm doing and they want to put it into the right light, what I'm doing. And I feel if you can describe it with some word, I feel freedom." He has spoken positively about his AEW stint so far, describing it as a collaborative effort in which he and the AEW creative team have agreed on many creative decisions. Dragunov's debut had a major hurdle as he had to renew his visa , which all came together at the last minute. His decision to leave WWE was down to the TKO-owned promotion failing to offer him a satisfactory contract , prompting him to explore new opportunities. Dragunov has started his AEW career on a positive note, defeating Mike Bailey in the main event of the October 21 episode of " AEW Dynamite ."

title: Shayna Baszler Signs With TNA Wrestling

summary_src: Shayna Baszler isn’t just passing through TNA after winning championship gold at Bound For Glory.
body: Speaking to Denise Salcedo on October 22 , Baszler was asked whether she planned on staying with TNA following her championship victory alongside Zoey Serrano. Baszler confirmed the signing and made it clear she expects to be around for a while. “I mean, yeah, that’s what being a champion means, right? And the funny part about it is, we were so confident of the win that, yeah, I signed with TNA knowing we were going to win those titles and that I’d have to be around to put those on the line and beat up anyone that tries to come near them.” Shayna Baszler and Zoey Serrano aren’t planning on playing it safe with the titles either. She wants to defend them against basically anyone willing to step up, whether that’s inside TNA or somewhere else. “So, for the time being, that’s what’s going to happen. You should be seeing lots of broken limbs. We want to defend against everyone all over the place. So, we will carry these into wherever and invite anyone that wants to come in as well.” Baszler also explained why she decided to sign with TNA at this point in her career. She had been spending time coaching and producing at WWE NXT and EVOLVE, and she admitted that helping younger wrestlers develop had become something she genuinely loved. “But, you know, number one, if a friend calls you to help beat someone up, you help them beat someone up and then ask them why after that. That’s a Ronda Rousey thing. So when Zoey calls me, like, okay, yeah, I’ll beat someone up if you need me to help you beat someone up.” The bigger turning point came from Baszler’s Bloodsport match against Natalya. Afterwards, Nattie reminded her that they could still perform at a high level, and Baszler said that made something click for her about how much she still has left. “But I think, honestly, that match I had with Nattie at Bloodsport, she grabbed me afterwards and was like, ‘This is what I want people to know. We can still go.’ And it’s like, yeah, wait a second. Yeah, I can still go. And there’s still no one that can do the things I do the way that I do it.” Baszler isn’t ready to move completely into the coaching side of wrestling just yet. She still feels she has something unique to offer inside the ring, and until she’s satisfied someone else can carry that style forward, the itch to compete isn’t going away. “And I think until I’m satisfied that that banner can be carried, I think I’ll always have this itch to spread the gospel of legitimacy. So I think TNA is the perfect place for me right now.” Baszler and Serrano defeated Allie and Kiera Hogan for the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships at Bound For Glory on October 11. Baszler ultimately choked Allie out to secure the titles, but until now, it wasn’t clear exactly what her long-term status with the company looked like. title: Penta Recalls Stress Before Roman Reigns Bout
raw_title: Penta Recalls Stressful Day Leading Up To Roman Reigns Match
summary_src: Penta was quite stressed out before his match with Roman Reigns. The bout between Penta and Reigns took place on the September 14 edition of WWE Raw. Despite his loss, fans argue that Penta emerged from the match as a new main event player for WWE.
body: Penta was quite stressed out before his match with Roman Reigns. The bout between Penta and Reigns took place on the September 14 edition of WWE Raw. Despite his loss, fans argue that Penta emerged from the match as a new main event player for WWE. In a new interview with Busted Open Radio, Penta recalled the hours leading up to the championship bout. “Now I’m relaxed, I can tell you what happened all day but that day, it was too much stress for me because I have a lot of things in my brain. The first thing is against Roman Reigns, first time ever. Mexico City. My family is there. Hours before that, you saw my arrival shot in the arena with the horse. Two hours before my match, maybe three, problems with the horse. Maybe it’s not here, maybe it’s delayed, maybe something. You need makeup, I need to go the ring, I practice this. Oh, you have an interview. Oh, you have a meet and greet. To be honest, two days later than my match, I started sitting in my garden like, ‘Wow.’ I promise you, two days later because in that moment, everything is on my brain. Hey Penta, you need interview. Oh, Roman is here. Oh, the horse will come. I become crazy in that moment. When I opened my eyes, they were like, ‘You are next.’ Oh shit. Everything was too fast, but in the same moment, I try to enjoy every moment and every interview. The name is Mexico here is a penacho, I use it for my presentation. The guys, ‘Hey, I’m gonna be late.’ Come on. Everything was rushed but at the end of the day, it was perfect.” Continuing on, Penta admitted that he learned a lot from Reigns. “I learned a lot facing Roman Reigns. To be honest, I know now why he is one of the best wrestlers or the best wrestler in the universe. The character, the Shakespeare, every move you can breathe, you can enjoy every move. Bro, it’s different. But I like it, I like that style, I like feeling this moment in the ring when it’s the big dog basically. He looks at me, I look at him, the whole crowd is with me, thank god. Everything was so special and magic.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Penta felt overwhelmed in the hours leading up to his match against Roman Reigns on the September 14 episode of WWE Raw in Mexico City. The luchador dealt with family being present, a complicated horse entrance that faced last-minute issues, makeup, an interview, a meet and greet, and the pressure of facing Reigns for the first time. In an interview with Busted Open Radio, Penta said he only began to process the experience two days afterward while sitting in his garden.

She said there were plenty of things Rousey did behind the scenes that fans — and sometimes even the women in WWE’s locker room — never knew about. “I’ve heard people be like, ‘Ronda didn’t really care about wrestling.’ Like, Ronda, she might hate me telling this story, but there was a time where Ronda had a pay-per-view match and got six minutes cut off of her match because a match before had gone over their time.” Baszler stressed that losing six minutes wasn’t some minor inconvenience. With wrestlers trying to tell an entire story within a limited window, she said even having a single minute taken away can make a huge difference. “And it’s like, to take six minutes from a match is huge. To take one minute from a match, in order to build a story and get emotion involved, it takes time.” According to Baszler, Rousey made it clear during that meeting that money and fame weren’t keeping her in WWE. She wanted to help push women’s wrestling forward, and she was apparently willing to walk away if WWE told her that wasn’t going to happen. “I don’t need to be here to make money. I don’t need to be here to get famous. I’m here to help advance this. And if you’re telling me right now that’s never going to happen, then I’m done. I only want to improve this.” What stood out to Baszler was that Rousey never tried to make the incident public or use it to make herself look good. In fact, she doesn’t even believe most of the women sharing the locker room with Rousey knew what she had done. “And she, you know, no one will ever—she’s not going to tell you that story. She’s not going to tweet about it. She’s not going to go on a thing and talk about it. And nobody’s going to know about the stuff she did like that behind the scenes on her own dime just to argue for the women’s locker room.” “I don’t even think girls in the locker room even knew she did that, you know what I mean? So, just the stuff she would do like that. And then on top of, yeah, like you said, bringing her name and bringing new eyes. There’s many MMA fans that would never have watched professional wrestling because it’s that scary F-word, right? It’s not real. And I think they tuned in just because, ‘Let’s see what happens here.’ And then, much like Ronda, becoming a fan, got sucked into the story.” Whether Rousey ever gets credit for everything she did is another question. Baszler thinks that recognition could come eventually, but she also suggested Rousey was never particularly interested in getting praised for those things in the moment. “So, you know, will she ever get the credit? Maybe years down the road. But I think that’s something Ronda, for her own sanity, I’m glad she doesn’t care to receive the credit in the moment because she did a lot. But I could tell you a hundred more stories like that, you know what I mean?” Salcedo then pointed out that Rousey’s status

title: Blake Monroe Responds To NXT Star Stealing Name and Gimmick - TWNP-Wrestling News

body: It hasn’t even been a full year since Blake Monroe left NXT. Yet, this past Tuesday’s NXT on CW aired a video of an Evolve talent set to make her debut. The name of this talent really raised eyebrows, as Chantel Monroe is coming to NXT. Not only does Chantel have the same last name as the SmackDown Superstar, but the WWE Next-In-Line (NIL) star also has a similar gimmick. Now, Blake Monroe reacts to the controversial teaser for Chantel Monroe’s NXT debut. There has been a quicker churn rate for the NXT-WWE pipeline as of late. For instance, Mariah May debuted in NXT as Blake Monroe, and within a year got promoted to SmackDown. These faster-paced call-ups have raised concerns that talents are joining the Main Roster before they are ready. Case in point, Blake Monroe made her SmackDown debut in London back in June. However, she didn’t make her in-ring debut until October. Even then, Blake Monroe’s first WWE match was delayed with many false starts against Giulia. All of that said, WWE still needs to fill the hole growing in the developmental system as NXT stars transition to the Main Roster. One of the lucky names to help fill that gap is Chantel Monroe. The NIL Superstar is expected to make her NXT debut soon, and it’s drawn a lot of criticism from the Internet Wrestling Community. While Blake Monroe has had a turbulent transition from AEW to WWE , she’s starting to settle into a regular role on SmackDown. That said, many things about Blake Monroe’s NXT presentation were stripped away for her WWE run. Fans of Mariah May noted that her mirror entrance was noticeably lacking compared to her NXT days. Perhaps that’s because WWE was saving it for another Monroe? Chantel Monroe’s NXT teaser featured the 26-year-old star looking into a mirror and telling people to pay attention to her. The teaser focused on a lot of close-up shots of Chantel Monroe’s face and makeup. Much of the content was very reminiscent of how Blake Monroe was introduced to the WWE Universe. Understandably, WWE fans took to social media to call out the name and character resemblance. While Chantel Monroe might have had a Next in Line WWE contract, many think she’s next in line to be Blake Monroe. The All-American gymnast signed with WWE in 2022 and started training after her graduation from Auburn in 2023. By 2024, Derrian Gobourne had her first matches at NXT House Shows under her real name. Even with Mariah May under the WWE banner, Derrian Gobourne’s name was changed to Chantel Monroe in 2025. Now, it appears that she will keep the name after her spotlight aired on NXT. With all the chatter surrounding the Chantel Monroe vignette, the Evolve star is taking the drama in stride: While fans came at the new NXT star, she didn’t deny Blake Monroe was an inspiration. title: Penta Feels Power From Money In The Bank Victory
raw_title: Penta Feels Like He Has 'The Fucking Power In His Hands' After Money In The Bank Win
summary_src: Penta is on top of the world. After failing to capture the World Heavyweight Championship from Roman Reigns, Penta was widely expected to return to the midcard scene. Instead, he changed the trajectory of his career by winning the Money In The Bank briefcase just a few weeks later.
body: After failing to capture the World Heavyweight Championship from Roman Reigns, Penta was widely expected to return to the midcard scene. Instead, he changed the trajectory of his career by winning the Money In The Bank briefcase just a few weeks later. Speaking with Busted Open Radio for a new interview , Penta said that he sometimes can’t believe what is happening with his career right now. “Actually, I want to be honest with you. Sometimes, I can’t believe it, what is happening right now. But at the same time, I feel know what is my responsibility now in this business. Every time more [children] come to me, every child uses my t-shirt, my mask, cero miedo, he can say it in Spanish but he tried. When I saw that, it’s like okay, I know now my responsibility with the crowd. I feel great because now my brother started growing up in different kinds of stuff, he is in SmackDown now and I am Raw. But, the time when my brother came to Raw, amazing too.” Continuing on, Penta said that he has the “fucking power in his hands” with the briefcase. “But, as for a briefcase, I actually feel like that. I have the fucking power in my hands basically because at one time, I don’t know where, I don’t know when, but when I feel it in my soul that it is the perfect time for a cash-in, I will. Now, I started thinking something, Roman, you know Sami. I don’t know because it’s my first time but at the same time, I want to do the best, forget the world champions, you know? But for now, I enjoy every presentation with my briefcase, with fire, everything involving about it. I enjoy it.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: On the Record: Joe Hendry Speaks On Possibility of Turning Heel in WWE
raw_title: Joe Hendry Addresses Possibility of Turning Heel in WWE
summary_src: Joe Hendry might be one of WWE’s biggest fan-favorites right now, but that’s definitely not how this character was supposed to work. Hendry says he originally created his current persona with the expectation that wrestling fans would absolutely hate him.
body: Speaking with TV Insider , Hendry was asked whether he could eventually show a darker side instead of sticking with the upbeat character that fans have embraced. His answer revealed that the audience already changed his plans once before. “When I was putting together who Joe Hendry is, and I made the music video and all that, it was with the intention that he would be universally hated.” Obviously, things didn’t exactly go according to plan. Instead of rejecting the character, fans latched onto Hendry, his music and everything else surrounding the gimmick: “The opposite happened.” Rather than fighting against that reaction, Hendry allowed the character to go wherever the fans wanted to take it. That’s also why he isn’t locking himself into staying a babyface or eventually turning darker. “So, you know, the audience dictated what happened there, and I think they will continue to dictate that.” That approach has worked out pretty well for Hendry so far, with the character becoming far more popular than he originally intended. The funny part is that one of wrestling’s most naturally likable acts was apparently designed to get exactly the opposite reaction. As for whether fans eventually get a darker Joe Hendry, he’s leaving that decision open rather than forcing a change. If his character takes another unexpected turn, Hendry seems perfectly happy letting the audience decide where things go next. title: Damian Priest Feels Better After 2025 Reduced Schedule
raw_title: Damian Priest Reflects On Reduced Schedule In 2025, ‘I Had To Check Myself A Little Bit’
body: During the back half of 2025, Priest worked a reduced in-ring schedule to help out with some of his nagging injuries. Now, just a year later, he is in a good place both physically and mentally. “Well, we’re never okay. It is what we do, you know. No bitching and moaning, I don’t like overly talking about how my body is because I’m still showing up to do the job. It’s not an excuse. I’m not the only one banged up. So if my opponent’s banged up too, we’re on an even playing field. So I don’t like to rely on that. But, I’m feeling a lot better. I got some procedures done while I never took a day off, you know what I mean? So, I got some stuff done to ease pain and I feel a lot better. I think people can see it visually. I’m training differently, I’m getting back into the shape that I used to be in and it’s all because I feel better. I’m in a better head place too, you know — I got myself down and for somebody who likes to think positively of myself and my career, I started doing the opposite and I had to check myself a little bit. So that came with my health, physically and mentally. I’m in a good place now, man. It is what it is.” Damian Priest told WWE Radio’s Off The Ropes in a new interview . title: Possible Reason Behind Daria Rae’s TNA Television Absence
raw_title: Possible Reason Behind Daria Rae’s TNA Television Absence
summary_src: Daria Rae has been missing from TNA television for more than a month, but that absence is finally about to end. The former Sonya Deville is set to return on the October 22 episode of TNA iMPACT!, and it sounds like she may have been keeping pretty busy while her character was suspended. During a ...
body: During a PWInsider Q&A , Mike Johnson was asked where Rae had disappeared to after TNA wrote her off television. Johnson pointed out that the company already gave fans the storyline explanation, but confirmed she’s now ready to pop back up. “The storyline was she was suspended, but she is slated to return on tonight’s episode, which was pre-taped.” Rae was suspended from her Director of Operations role back in September after things got physical with Indi Hartwell. The two had been butting heads for weeks, with Rae repeatedly blocking Hartwell from getting a shot at the TNA Knockouts World Championship before eventually slapping her. That gave TNA an easy reason to get Rae off television, but apparently she had plenty going on away from wrestling too. Johnson said he knows Rae had several acting commitments and believes that’s what she was working on during her absence. “I know she had a lot of acting commitments, so my belief is she was working on those.” That doesn’t necessarily mean TNA suspended Rae specifically because of those acting commitments, since Johnson made it clear that part is his belief. Either way, the timing worked out pretty nicely, allowing Rae to handle outside projects while her character served the storyline suspension. Things also didn’t exactly stop moving while she was gone. Santino Marella stepped in and gave Hartwell the Knockouts World Championship opportunity Rae had spent so much time trying to keep away from her. Now Rae is walking back into a TNA that kept moving without her, which could make things pretty interesting for the Director of Operations. After more than a month away, fans won’t have to wait much longer to find out what she has to say about everything that happened behind her back. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin TNA HYPES CALGARY DEBUT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-22 11:07:00 TNA issued the following: TNA Wrestling Brings Its First-Ever Live Events To Calgary, Alberta: Back-to-Back Nights Of Action-Packed Pro Wrestling on November 18-19 TNA Producer and Wrestling Legend Lance Storm Is In Calgary November 5-6 To Preview The TNA Live Events In Calgary TNA Wrestling is coming to Calgary, Alberta, for the first-time with two nights of action-packed pro wrestling at the WinSport Event Centre. The TNA live events in Calgary are Wednesday & Thursday, November 18–19 and will be filmed to be broadcast as episodes of Thursday Night iMPACT on AMC and AMC+ in the U.S., Sportsnet 360 in Canada and TNA+ worldwide. It marks TNA’s first ever shows in Calgary and the debut at the WinSport Event Centre, one of the city’s premier live entertainment destinations. Fans can purchase tickets at Ticketmaster: Wednesday, November 18: https://www.ticketmaster.ca/tna-impact-on-amc-calgary-alberta-11-18-2026/event/11006528B56273B5 Thursday, November 19: https://www.ticketmaster.ca/tna-impact-on-amc-calgary-alberta-11-19-2026/event/11006528B56473BD Both nights will include a post-show Meet & Greet, giving fans direct access to their favorite TNA stars for autographs, photos and one-on-one moments. Stars on the shows will include wrestling legend Matt Hardy, current TNA World Champion Leon Slater, TNA Knockouts World Champion Indi Hartwell, TNA World Tag Team Champions Nic Nemeth and Ryan Nemeth, plus Moose, Trey Miguel, Xia Brookside, Mustafa Ali, Elayna Black, Cedric Alexander, Brian Myers, Eddie Edwards, KC Navarro, Joe Alonzo, Fabian Aichner, Avery Styles, Ricky Sosa, Elijah, Frankie Kazarian, Mila Moore, Harley Hudson and many others. LANCE STORM MEDIA TOUR TNA producer and wrestling legend Lance Storm will be in his hometown – Calgary, Alberta – on Thursday and Friday, November 5-6, for a two-day media tour to preview the TNA live events in Calgary. Residing in Calgary, Storm is one of Canada’s most accomplished professional wrestlers, having competed in ECW, WCW and WWE. His championship accolades include the WWE Intercontinental Championship, WCW United States Championship, WCW Cruiserweight Championship and multiple tag team titles in WWE and ECW. After retiring from full-time competition in 2004, Storm has continued to contribute to professional wrestling as a trainer and producer. CALGARY: A WONDERFUL WRESTLING CITY

title: TNA Signs Newly Crowned Knockouts Tag Champion Shayna Baszler
raw_title: TNA Wrestling announces signing of newly crowned champion
summary_src: Shayna Baszler is officially under contract with TNA Wrestling after debuting for the company at Bound for Glory. The October 11 pay-per-view saw former WWE wrestlers Baszler & Zoey Serrano (Zoey Stark) defeat Allie & Kiera Hogan to become the new Knockouts Tag Team Champions.
body: Shayna Baszler is officially under contract with TNA Wrestling after debuting for the company at Bound for Glory. The October 11 pay-per-view saw former WWE wrestlers Baszler & Zoey Serrano (Zoey Stark) defeat Allie & Kiera Hogan to become the new Knockouts Tag Team Champions. TNA then sent out an announcement today confirming that the promotion has signed Baszler to a contract: Before joining TNA, Baszler, Serrano, and TNA on-screen authority figure Daria Rae (Sonya Deville) were already allies from their time in WWE. Baszler & Serrano’s tag team has been given the name “Apex” in TNA. Baszler told Denise Salcedo that, while she doesn’t feel like her career is anywhere close to the end, she has been thinking about her legacy more often lately. With a background in MMA before bringing that style into her pro wrestling career, Baszler wants her legitimacy to be what people remember. Baszler was released by WWE in May 2025 but has maintained a good relationship with the company, including spending some time helping out backstage in NXT . In addition to signing Baszler, TNA has also added Shotzi Blackheart and Amazing Red to its roster, along with re-signing Director of Authority Santino Marella . Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: TNA Wrestling has signed Shayna Baszler to a contract after she and Zoey Serrano defeated Allie and Kiera Hogan at Bound for Glory on October 11 to win the Knockouts Tag Team titles. The team is now known as Apex in TNA. Baszler, who was released by WWE in May 2025, said she has been considering her legacy more while stressing that her career is far from over.

At the October 11 pay-per-view event, Baszler teamed with Zoey Serrano to defeat Allie and Kiera Hogan, winning the Knockouts Tag Team Championship.
TNA issued an announcement confirming the signing of Baszler to a contract with the company.
Baszler, Serrano, and on-screen authority figure Daria Rae had previously been allies during their time in WWE.
The tag team of Baszler and Serrano is now known as Apex in TNA.
TNA has also added Shotzi Blackheart and Amazing Red to its roster while re-signing Director of Authority Santino Marella.

title: Match Made: Jason Hotch Vs. Mustafa Ali 2 Out Of 3 Falls Headlines TNA IMPACT In Dothan
raw_title: Jason Hotch Vs. Mustafa Ali 2 Out Of 3 Falls Headlines TNA IMPACT In Dothan
body: Jason Hotch defends the TNA International Championship against Mustafa Ali in a 2 Out of 3 Falls Match on TNA iMPACT tonight at 9 p.m. ET on AMC from Dothan, Alabama. Hotch won the title from Ali in a four-way with John Skyler and Special Agent 0 at Bound for Glory on October 11 . The match was billed as the end of Order 4, with all four former stablemates fighting for Ali’s title. Hotch countered Ali’s pin attempt into a roll-up to win. TNA calls Ali his “former leader.” Rich Swann, KC Navarro, Cedric Alexander and Fabian Aichner meet in a four-way to become No. 1 contender to the TNA X Division Championship. All four were in the seven-way scramble at Bound for Glory that Amazing Red won for the vacant title. Avery Styles wrestles his first singles match against Joe Alonzo, with Frankie Kazarian at ringside. Kazarian won the Call Your Shot Gauntlet at Bound for Glory and said he will use the title shot on the TNA World Tag Team Championship with Styles as his partner. Director of Operations Daria Rae returns from suspension to open the show. TNA says “unfinished business with Indi Hartwell looms” over her return. Hartwell won the TNA Knockouts World Championship from Xia Brookside at Bound for Glory. Allie and Kiera Hogan will also address the Knockouts division. They lost the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championship to Shayna Baszler and Zoey Serrano at Bound for Glory, in Baszler’s TNA debut. TNA Thursday Night iMPACT! airs Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET on AMC and streams on TNA+.

It is the first Destination X since August 2017. Leon Slater defends the TNA World Championship against Trey Miguel in the main event. Miguel earned the title shot by winning a ladder match against Moose, Elijah, Ricky Sosa and Jason Hotch on the October 15 episode of iMPACT . Slater won the title from Nic Nemeth at Bound for Glory . Honma, who is 49 years old, posted a message the morning after the operation. He expressed eagerness to recover and return to activity.
The wrestler is scheduled to retire from in-ring competition in 2027. He made the announcement earlier this year at an event in his hometown of Yamagata.
Honma decided to retire after medical examinations revealed issues with his neck. He is focusing on improving his physical condition to allow for one final match in Yamagata in 2027.

summary_src: One week after debuting on Rumble, WWE Main Event returned to the airwaves this week for another episode. Four matches were advertised for the show, including the WWE Women’s Champion and WWE Tag Team Champions in action.
body: Main Event kicked off with one-third of Fatal Influence and former WWE Women’s Tag Team Champion Lainey Reid taking on reigning WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green. Lainey was notably flying solo, with Fallon Henley and Jacy Jayne nowhere to be found. The less experienced Reid controlled much of the early match until Chelsea turned things around with a flurry of offense. Lainey weathered the storm and got multiple near falls, but Chelsea was too elusive when Reid went for a running knee to put the finishing touches on an upset. Lainey slid out of Chelsea’s first Un-Pretty-Her attempt but couldn’t avoid the second, and the WWE Women’s Champion went on to win. Reaction: Interesting call to have the WWE Women’s Champion opening Main Event. The pessimist in me says it’s because they still don’t necessarily see Chelsea as more than a short-term, transitional champ. On the optimistic side, for their second week on a new platform, featuring someone who is currently over with the audience is a smart move, with the hope of getting more viewers. Chelsea expectedly got a warm reaction from the live crowd in this one and will continue to deal with Judgment Day as Crown Jewel lingers. As for Lainey, this was just her third singles match since being promoted to the main roster, after splitting two contests with Brie Bella over the summer. This match was obviously meant to showcase Green, but Reid asserted herself well and showed she can hack it on her own. Just seconds after the bell, Ruca rolled Candice up and picked up one of the quickest pinfall victories ever! Candice immediately stormed out of the ring, grabbed a mic, and demanded the match be restarted. Sol didn’t require much convincing and quickly agreed. Candice grabbed control right from the jump, nailing Sol with the microphone as the ref went to call for the bell to restart the match. Sol used some of her standard gymnastic offense to get the upper hand. It was at this point that we were sent to a picture-in-picture commercial break. Yes, even on Rumble, they do picture-in-picture commercials. The match seemed up for grabs, with both ladies down after Sol slid out of a Candice submission and turned it into an electric-chair drop. Candice pulled Sol into the corner for a tornado DDT, but Sol pulled off a crazy reversal, which sent Candice into the splash zone. Ruca ran to the corner and dropped LeRae with a Sol Snatcher to pick up her second win of the night! title: Cody Rhodes Again Dangles Idea of Future Match With The Rock
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Again Dangles Idea of Future Match With The Rock
body: “It’s not that I’m evading that answer,” Rhodes said. “I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do.” Rhodes pointed to WrestleMania 40 as a fitting final performance if The Rock decided to leave it there, but he made it clear the decision is not his to make. “That’ll be up to him. That’ll certainly be up to him, if there’s more and what those matches might be,” Rhodes said. He also said he would not turn down the opportunity. “I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that,” Rhodes said. “So maybe a match like that does happen. Maybe.” The two have only faced each other in one match. On night one of WrestleMania 40 in April 2024, The Rock teamed with Roman Reigns to beat Rhodes and Seth Rollins. The next night, Rhodes beat Reigns in a Bloodline Rules match to win the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship, in a match that also saw The Rock interfere. The night one tag match remains The Rock’s most recent WWE match. The story began when The Rock slapped Rhodes at the WrestleMania 40 kickoff event in February 2024 and aligned himself with Reigns and The Bloodline. The Rock returned in 2025 and set up the Elimination Chamber angle in which Rhodes turned down his offer, and John Cena turned heel and attacked Rhodes. Rhodes also discussed The Rock during an appearance on Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. “That’s the most complicated male relationship I have in my life,” Rhodes said. He noted that the history between the two goes beyond what fans see on television. “Our families have been linked for longer than people see,” Rhodes said, describing it as a “territorial tie” between the families. He then reflected on the WrestleMania 40 storyline. “There’s just a huge amount of reality with what happened at WrestleMania 40,” he said, describing it as The Rock “coming in, him taking my thing away, and me taking it back.” Rhodes also praised The Rock’s Final Boss persona as “one of the best characters” in wrestling. A Cody Rhodes vs. The Rock singles match is the one piece of the WrestleMania 40 story that never got its ending. The Rock was the heel who took the spotlight, and Rhodes overcame him and The Bloodline to finish his story. Fans never got the moment where Rhodes beat The Rock himself, and that is the match that would close the loop. The Rock’s schedule is the biggest obstacle. His film career and business commitments limit how often he can wrestle, and Rhodes is right that it is ultimately his call. But The Rock has not ruled out a return, and Rhodes’ new contract means he will be around for years. That gives both sides plenty of time to find the right WrestleMania for it.

title: El Desperado Withdraws From Super Jr Tag League
raw_title: El Desperado Announces Injury, Will Miss NJPW Super Jr Tag League
body: NJPW have announced that El Desperado will miss the upcoming Super Jr. Tag League due to injury. The IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champion has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. El Desperado posted a video on his YouTube channel addressing the injury, describing his symptoms, and his stepping away from the tournament. In it, he announced that Masatora Yasuda would be filling in for him, teaming with Mistico. The transcription of the video from the NJPW website is as follows: My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms, but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that, and asked to continue wrestling, while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don’t worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he’ll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that’s it. I’m off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) ‘Gaspe’ Invitational. I can’t move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we’ll be going ahead as planned. Show up. El Desperado is also scheduled for a big singles match against his partner Mistico at the upcoming CMLL x NJPW event Lucha Kingdom on November 16th, but not statement has been made on whether he will be able to compete in Mexico City. Everyone here at Monthly Puroresu wishes El Desperado a speedy recovery.
summary: NJPW announced that El Desperado will miss the upcoming Super Jr Tag League after being diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. The IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champion described losing strength in his left leg along with pain, pins and needles that prevent him from standing, walking or sitting for extended periods. Masatora Yasuda will replace him and team with Mistico.

title: Bayley Drops Bikini Video During WWE Hawaii Tour
raw_title: Bayley Drops Bikini Video During WWE Hawaii Tour
summary_src: Bayley is making the most of WWE’s recent trip to Hawaii, and apparently that includes throwing herself off a boat.
body: Bayley posted the clip to Instagram alongside several other photos from her time in Hawaii. She kept the caption pretty simple, using a collection of emojis to sum up everything she got up to during the trip. The video showed Bayley enjoying some downtime on a boat before doing a somersault straight into the water. title: Dispensa Lawsuit Against AEW and Moxley Stays in Michigan
raw_title: Dispensa lawsuit against AEW and Jon Moxley will stay in Michigan where incident occurred
summary_src: Injury case brought by production worker shoved at 2023 AEW Dynamite in Detroit will not be moved to Florida
body: Christopher Dispensa, who worked on AEW’s production team, sued AEW and Moxley (whose legal name is Jonathan Good) in May 2025. He alleges that during a match, Moxley deviated from the plan and shoved him to the floor at the May 10, 2023 show at Little Caesars Arena, allegedly leaving him with injuries that required cervical spine and shoulder surgery. The defendants asked the court to dismiss or put the case on hold so it could be refiled in Florida, where Dispensa lives, where most of his doctors are located, and where AEW is headquartered. Judge Catherine Heise rejected the defendants’ arguments in an order filed on October 5, which followed a hearing on September 17. She wrote that the incident, the likely fact witnesses, and the arena are all in Detroit, and in fact, the courthouse is “within healthy walking distance” of the arena. Medical witnesses who are in Florida can testify remotely, the judge wrote, and moving the case to a Florida court would present the problem of having an out-of-state court apply Michigan law to an injury that happened in Michigan. The judge also found that the defendants waited too long to make the request to move the case. They filed their motion to move the case to Florida on July 7, nearly ten months after AEW answered the complaint in September 2025. The defendants said they would not raise a three-year time-limit statute of limitations defense if the case was allowed to be litigated in Florida. But the judge expressed concern that in that scenario the case might get thrown out regardless. Heise wrote that she “is not confident that a Florida court would honor such an agreement or even an order so stating from a Michigan court.” The order does not rule on the merits of Dispensa’s injury claims, only that the case will continue to be litigated in a Michigan court before Heise. Dispensa’s claims include counts of assault and battery against Moxley, negligence and gross negligence against both Moxley and AEW, and negligent hiring, training, supervision, and retention against AEW. Dispensa has demanded a jury trial. A settlement conference with the court is scheduled for December 22, 2026. The docket shows the parties met for an earlier settlement conference on July 29, 2026, which resulted in those discussions being “held for further settlement.”
summary: A judge ruled that Christopher Dispensa's lawsuit against AEW and Jon Moxley will remain in Michigan. Dispensa claims Moxley went off-script during a 2023 match at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit and shoved him, causing injuries that led to cervical spine and shoulder surgery. The court determined that the incident location, witnesses and arena in Detroit made Michigan the proper venue, noting remote testimony options for Florida-based medical witnesses and that Michigan law would apply to the in-state injury.

title: Meltzer Details WWE's Financial Stakes For Crown Jewel

summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, despite the U.S. government advising Americans not to travel to the country.
body: On Wrestling Observer Radio , Bryan Alvarez stated he thinks WWE won't go to Saudi Arabia. He believes the fact that WWE is even considering going is a bad thing. Dave Meltzer agrees that going to Saudi Arabia right now is a terrible idea, but points to why WWE will most likely still go. "There's three shows upcoming, which would be two UFCs and the WWE, their (TKO) profit margin for the quarter would be down between $70 and $90 million which is about a quarter of their profit for the quarter," Meltzer explained. If they don't go, they would also be risking WrestleMania. Meltzer believes those factors are why WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. A recent tweet from Saudi's General Entertainment Authority director Turki Al-Sheikh seemed directed at WWE and TKO .
summary: Dave Meltzer acknowledged that holding the Crown Jewel event in Saudi Arabia at this time would be a poor decision. He noted that skipping the show along with two upcoming UFC events would reduce TKO's quarterly profit margin by $70 to $90 million, representing roughly one-quarter of their expected profit. Meltzer added that failing to proceed could also jeopardize WrestleMania, making it likely WWE will still go forward with the Saudi Arabia show.

body: "I can confirm it is [for] five years," Meltzer said. "I've seen people speculate it and everything, but I in fact did get it confirmed. It is a five year deal. So yeah, he's signed with WWE." The topic then turned to Lee's brother, AEW's Dralistico, who caused a stir earlier this week when he posted an AI photo of himself in prison, leading many to believe he was looking to leave AEW and possibly join Lee in WWE. Meltzer confirmed earlier reporting by co-host Bryan Alvarez that Dralistico's deal was up in December and that there was some belief in the industry that Dralistico wanted to leave. At the same time, however, Meltzer noted he had received info that suggested that Dralistico's picture had a different intent than the one many interpreted it to have. "I know, from an AEW standpoint, that they [believe that] they [WWE] are going to make him an offer," Meltzer said. "[But] I was told, from people close to him, that the thing with the bars and everything, that's because of the visa issue. It's not because he can't wait to leave, like Fenix."
summary: Dave Meltzer confirmed Dragon Lee signed a five-year contract with WWE. He also addressed Dralistico's situation, noting the AEW star's contract expires in December with belief he wants to leave, though the recent AI prison photo was related to visa issues rather than a desire to depart like his brother Fenix. Meltzer added that AEW expects WWE to make Dralistico an offer.

body: The video showed Tonga no-selling chops from Dragunov before laying out the Russian-born star. title: Top NXT Star Was Told She Was Too Old Before WWE Signing
raw_title: Top NXT Star Was Told She Was Too Old Before WWE Signing
body: 0 WWE NXT star Wren Sinclair has opened up about her professional wrestling journey. She revealed being told she was too old for WWE. Before signing, she was even advised to look elsewhere. Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring , Wren Sinclair was asked whether she would still wrestle today. The question focused on what might have happened without WWE. Sinclair initially joked about imagining that alternate timeline. She then opened up about her love for wrestling. She said, “Let’s just not say I didn’t get signed. No, I’m kidding. Yeah. So I think wrestling holds a really special place in my heart, and I definitely think there were times, injuries, where you question whether or not it’s worth it. there were times in the process where I actually heard, like that I’m too old for WWE, and to, like, look elsewhere and whatnot.” Sinclair explained that wrestling sometimes made her question everything. Despite those difficult moments, her passion never completely disappeared. “And I think at the end of the day, I’m not sure because I think I love this so much that it hurts sometimes when it doesn’t love you back. I’m a big proponent of mental health.” “So, depending on the journey that happened after said not being signed, I’m not sure. But I’m glad that I’m here, and I’m going to hold on to this, and I’m just never going to let them fire me.” WWE eventually signed Sinclair in 2023, giving her another opportunity. Now, she is preparing for the biggest match of her career. Sinclair will challenge Kelani Jordan for the NXT Women’s Championship scheduled for NXT Halloween Havoc. summary_src: The Hurt Syndicate’s strange AEW booking has led to plenty of questions, and now there’s another interesting wrinkle to the story. Sean Ross Sapp says there have been situations where members of the group didn’t want to put other wrestlers over.
body: Speaking on The Hump , Sapp was asked what’s actually going on with The Hurt Syndicate and why Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP haven’t been featured consistently lately. He admitted he doesn’t know the exact reason behind their current booking. However, Sapp then addressed something that’s apparently been talked about regarding the group behind the scenes. While he didn’t say they’ve refused every creative idea thrown their way, he confirmed there have been occasions where they didn’t want to lose to certain opponents. “Listen, I know there’s been a lot of talk about them like not wanting to put people over. There’s definitely been some situations where they haven’t wanted to. That has been a thing.” Sapp didn’t identify which members of The Hurt Syndicate were involved in those situations, who AEW wanted them to put over or whether those disagreements directly caused their recent lack of television time. So there’s still plenty about the situation that isn’t known. The update comes after The Hurt Syndicate’s AEW presence has noticeably cooled off in recent months. Despite Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP competing at All In in August, the faction hasn’t been anywhere near as consistently featured on Dynamite and Collision since then. Another recent report from Self Made Pro suggested fans shouldn’t expect that to change anytime soon. He claimed the group would appear intermittently on Collision for “random things” rather than returning as a serious weekly act. “They’re gonna show up intermittently on Collision to do random things.” He went even further by arguing that The Hurt Syndicate’s run as a major AEW act has essentially already ended, even if the faction itself hasn’t officially broken up. “I talk about how a lot of people’s runs end way before they actually end, and the Hurt Syndicate’s AEW run has already ended in real terms. So there you go, as in terms of a serious, consistent act.” For a group loaded with veterans like Lashley, Benjamin and MVP, protecting their credibility clearly matters. The bigger question is how AEW finds meaningful opponents and storylines for The Hurt Syndicate if there are certain finishes the group isn’t willing to do. title: TNA Impact Recaps Bound For Glory Title Changes
raw_title: TNA IMPACT FEUD TRACKER: Clarke’s assessment of latest developments including Nemeths-Hardys, Allie in a paranormal realm, Leon Slater’s contenders
body: TNA Impact opened its broadcast this week recapping the highlights from their biggest show of the year, Bound For Glory including a number of title changes leading into a new season of storylines going into the fall. The show kicked off with the Hardys, Matt & Jeff, who acted as guest general managers of the show, in honor of their 35th year in the pro wrestling business. The Hardys talked about their own legacy, but then put the shine on other newly crowned champions starting with new X-Division Champion Amazing Redd, followed by new TNA World Champion Leon Slater. The Nemeths were backstage complaining about their match against each other, booked by the Hardys. Breakdown:With the episode of Impact being “booked” by the Hardys, I expected some wacky pairings and match concepts. In this short backstage segment, the Nemeth brothers came at odds when Nic Nemeth assumed his younger brother, Ryan, would take the fall in their match later in the evening. I’m not sure what they are expecting to achieve with this, but perhaps they are moving away from the Nemeths as a tag team. Santino Marella was backstage, enjoying his night off, when he was interrupted by The System. The System demanded a spot on the show, but Santino declared he was on vacation. Bear Bronson drew an issue with Eddie Edwards’ defense of Ricky Sosa. Breakdown: A split of the System may be coming soon and I can get behind that. The TNA Tag Team Champions, Nic & Ryan Nemeth, were booked by The Hardys to face off against each other on Impact this week with a stipulation that if they one intentionally took the fall, the Nemeths would be stripped of the tag titles. After avoiding contact with each other, The Hardys would appear on the entrance ramp to reiterate that the Nemeths would be stripped of the titles if they refused to fight each other. Nic Nemeth would score the victory over Ryan Nemeth shortly thereafter. Nic Nemeth complained that he was not included in the TNA World Title number one contenders ladder match. Breakdown: It was a bit jarring to hear Tom Hannifan talking more glowingly of Nic Nemeth while Matt Rehwoldt put over Ryan Nemeth strongly. The segment was basically for comedy. Expressions demanded the Hardys give AJ Francis a shot at the TNA World Championship. The Hardys countered by giving Francis & Expressions a match against the Hardys. Breakdown: Another segment that was meant for comedy, it did not do much for me. I continue to want more for Francis, but TNA clearly sees him as a comedy figure. Harley Hudson told The Righteous that she wanted to accompany them to the ring for the match against Syx, but they refused to allow her to join them. A match booked by the Hardys as a face-off of two of the Hardys’ recent rivals featured The Righteous and Syx in a table match. Breakdown: The match was not very long but it was decent action while it lasted. The TNA tag team division does seem to be heading in the right direction with the addition of Syx. The Nemeths argued backstage with Nic expecting Ryan to take the fall, possibly signaling a shift away from them as a tag team.

title: NJPW Star Forced Out Of Super Jr. Tag League
raw_title: NJPW Star Forced Out Of Super Jr. Tag League
body: In a YouTube post, Desperado addressed the issue and what happened: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms, but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that, and asked to continue wrestling, while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don’t worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he’ll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that’s it. I’m off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) ‘Gaspe’ Invitational. I can’t move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we’ll be going ahead as planned. Show up.” In NJPW, El Desperado has held the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Championships five times and is the current title holder with Místico. title: End of an Era: WWE Discussing Plans for Rey Mysterio’s Retirement in 2027
raw_title: WWE Discussing Plans for Rey Mysterio’s Retirement in 2027
summary_src: Rey Mysterio has spent months saying he’s not ready to put a date on retirement, but WWE might already be thinking about his final run. There’s been growing backstage talk that 2027 could finally be the year the legendary luchador calls it a career inside the ring.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , there have been recent “rumblings” within WWE about a major retirement coming next year. The name at the center of those conversations is Mysterio. “According to those that WrestleVotes spoke to, there have been rumblings of a legendary retirement within WWE in 2027, with that talk centering around Rey Mysterio.” Before anyone starts circling a WrestleMania date, nothing is officially locked in yet. The source didn’t know exactly when or where Rey would wrestle his final match, but said the chatter at WWE television lately has pointed toward 2027 being the end of the road. “A source confirmed that they didn’t have any direct knowledge of when or where an official retirement would take place — instead indicating that recent chatter at TV has pointed towards next year marking the end of the road for Rey Mysterio as an active wrestler.” WWE has apparently gone beyond simply wondering when Rey might be finished. The company has reportedly kicked around ideas for how to handle his farewell if he does decide that next year is the right time. “According to the same source, WWE has discussed ideas on how to present his farewell.” Retirement wouldn’t necessarily mean Rey is packing up and disappearing from WWE either. There’s reportedly a feeling that he could stick around and help the next generation once he’s done taking bumps himself. “Much like his counterpart AJ Styles, there’s a feeling among many within WWE that Rey will remain involved once his in-ring days are behind him, as he’ll continue to play a vital role in the development of next-generation talent in WWE and AAA.” “I think I’m just going to wing it and see where this road takes me, you know, because I’m really enjoying the moments right now that I’m living inside the ring, whether as a wrestler or as a GM.” Rey also said he was feeling “really, really good” physically and enjoying a schedule that doesn’t beat him up four or five nights every week anymore. Between wrestling, his GM duties and his involvement with AAA, he sounded pretty happy with where things stood. So this isn’t Rey Mysterio announcing his retirement, and there isn’t a confirmed farewell match sitting on WWE’s calendar. For now, it’s backstage chatter — but WWE apparently thinking about how to send him off makes 2027 a whole lot more interesting. If Rey does decide next year is it, WWE will have plenty of time to make the goodbye count instead of having his career quietly wind down. After everything he’s meant to the company and lucha libre as a whole, there’s no shortage of directions WWE could go if it really is preparing for one last ride. title: Legal Watch: Judge Denies AEW and Jon Moxley’s Request to Move Assault and Battery Lawsuit to Florida
raw_title: Judge Denies AEW and Jon Moxley’s Request to Move Assault and Battery Lawsuit to Florida
summary_src: AEW and Jon Moxley tried to get a former production worker’s lawsuit moved from Michigan to Florida, but the judge wasn’t having it. The case is staying in Detroit, and one of the reasons is pretty simple — that’s where the whole thing allegedly happened.
body: According to POST Wrestling , Wayne County Judge Catherine Heise denied AEW and Moxley’s request in an October 5 order. The ruling came after a September 17 hearing over where Christopher Dispensa’s lawsuit should actually play out. AEW and Moxley had plenty of reasons for wanting Florida. Dispensa lives there, most of the doctors who treated him are there and AEW is headquartered there, so they argued it would make more sense to handle the case in a Florida court. The judge saw things differently. The alleged incident happened during the May 10, 2023 episode of AEW Dynamite at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, and several potential witnesses are also in the area. Heise even pointed out just how close everything is. The courthouse handling the lawsuit is “within healthy walking distance” of Little Caesars Arena, while any doctors sitting down in Florida can simply testify remotely. Then there’s the timing. AEW and Moxley didn’t file their motion asking to move the case until July 7, nearly 10 months after AEW answered Dispensa’s complaint in September 2025. The defendants tried to deal with another potential headache by saying they wouldn’t use Florida’s three-year statute of limitations as a defense if the case was moved. Heise wasn’t willing to gamble on whether a Florida court would actually go along with that arrangement. She “is not confident that a Florida court would honor such an agreement or even an order so stating from a Michigan court.” Dispensa originally sued AEW and Moxley in May 2025 over an incident that allegedly happened during Moxley’s match against Kenny Omega on Dynamite. Dispensa, who worked on AEW’s production crew, claims Moxley went away from what had been planned and shoved him to the floor. He alleges that the shove left him with serious neck and shoulder injuries that eventually required cervical spine and shoulder surgery. His lawsuit includes assault and battery claims against Moxley, negligence and gross negligence claims against Moxley and AEW, along with negligent hiring, training, supervision and retention claims against the company. This ruling doesn’t mean Dispensa has won any of those claims, and it doesn’t decide whether Moxley or AEW actually did anything wrong. It just means AEW and Moxley didn’t get the change of scenery they wanted, so the legal fight stays in Michigan. There could still be a way for everyone to avoid taking this thing all the way to a jury. Another settlement conference is scheduled for December 22 after the two sides previously met on July 29 and left those discussions “held for further settlement.” For now, AEW and Moxley are stuck fighting this one in Detroit, but the actual allegations at the center of the lawsuit still have to be sorted out. With another settlement meeting coming in December, this case could either find its way toward a deal or move one step closer to a jury hearing the whole story. title: On the Record: Rob Van Dam Says WWE Stars Were Afraid To Speak up Backstage
raw_title: Rob Van Dam Says WWE Stars Were Afraid To Speak up Backstage
body: 0 WWE Hall of Famer Rob Van Dam has discussed backstage culture. He explained why some WWE stars were afraid to speak up. RVD also compared WWE’s environment with AEW’s approach to wrestling. Speaking on his 1 of a Kind with RVD show , Van Dam was asked about potentially appearing in AEW again. The discussion also touched on AEW’s recent growth and roster. Van Dam praised the promotion for establishing itself over time. He said, “They’ve definitely proven themselves, you know. Like, it was so easy when they first came out to be like, “Yeah, well, let’s see how long they stick around.” And I don’t think there’s anything wrong with any of us, you know, that felt that way, because promotions over the years come up all the time. Oh, they got Major League Baseball money. This shit’s for real, and they got this and this, and it never lasts.” He then congratulated AEW and discussed its continued growth. “And those guys, you know, really fill the void, so it’s cool. Congrats to AEW, and they’re just going to keep growing, you know. I always check with the fans and ask what they watch, you know, and a lot of people are watching both products, you know, and I don’t know how much international distribution they have, but obviously they must be on in the places that they’re going to, at least, you know.” Van Dam then explained what he sees as a major difference between WWE and AEW. He suggested AEW gives wrestlers more freedom to express themselves. “So, but yeah, pretty cool. And it still, and I think always will, be coming across as, and I think for valid reasons, the boys being the ones that are kind of running the show more, you know, whereas WWE, you know, was like a lot of people afraid for their job and doing whatever they’re told and sometimes afraid to go against it or say the wrong thing or whatever.” He added that AEW feels different for its performers. “And this seems more like guys that want to be out there expressing themselves with their talent and doing it their way.” RVD previously appeared in AEW, sharing the ring with stars like Swerve Strickland, Jack Perry, the Dark Order, and others. Piper, for the second year running, was handed a lame duck at 'Mania. He was expected to make the best of a bad situation, but even industry titans like Roddy could never be considered miracle workers .

body: PWInsider , as well as Fightful , which cited Netflix listings, confirmed the news. "NXT" will air on Wednesday, November 4, the same day as "AEW Dynamite: Blood & Guts." Fightful noted that it will be the first time the shows will go head-to-head on a Wednesday night since 2021. "Dynamite" is usually shifted to Tuesdays, when necessary, during the MLB playoffs every year. The episode of "NXT" will feature the fallout of Halloween Havoc, set for Saturday, October 31, live from the WWE Performance Center. NXT Women's Champion Kelani Jordan is set to defend her title against Wren Sinclair , and NXT Champion Grayson Waller will face Tony D'Angelo . Shiloh Hill and Naraku are set to go one-on-one in a battle of the poison mist, and a "Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal" match between Charlie Dempsey and Zilla Fatu has also been booked. AEW revealed its lineup for the men's Blood & Guts match on the most recent edition of "Dynamite." Steven Borden returned from injury, to challenge the heel team , on behalf of himself, Darby Allin, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay, Adam Copeland, and the Young Bucks. The team will take on the Don Callis Family's Kyle Fletcher, AEW International Champion Kazuchika Okada, Kevin Knight, Mark Davis, Jake Doyle, and Wardlow.

title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Breaks Down WWE Future, Addresses Whether Fatigue Has Set In Among Fans
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Discusses WWE Future, Addresses Whether Fatigue Has Set In Among Fans
body: Cody Rhodes opened up about his wrestling future during a recent appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet . As noted , The American Nightmare recently signed a new deal with WWE. It’s reportedly a five-year contract. Rhodes had previously said that he’d retire at 40. Now that he’s 41 and just signed a new contract, Chris Van Vliet asked Cody how long he plans to wrestle. He also touched upon the fatigue setting in among fans and explained why he doesn’t want to stick around for too long. Here’s what he said : “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract, but that’s going to go for a while, and if I’m able to do what I’ve been able to do, because I would love this year not to be just one movie, but perhaps two movies, and I’d love to kind of be able to share that at some point, get that going, and be in that. With all that said, my time with WWE could go. I mean, just to give you a real answer here, and not politic around you, probably seven years. Six, seven? I didn’t mean it like that, but yeah, you know that’s a kids’ thing, right? Had to have Carmelo Hayes explain to me what that was, and I still didn’t get it. Yeah, six, seven years. I’d say so. Yeah, and I don’t want to say that in a final sense. I just know that I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” On why he doesn’t want to wrestle after turning 50; touches upon ‘Cody fatigue’ “Well, I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my 50s. No shame to anyone who wrestles in their 50s. I don’t want to overstay my welcome in a sense of this, right? So, I have been given so much from wrestling, and you have to think about my career in its totality. The things that we don’t talk about, the things that I don’t get asked about anymore. You have to think about all that. I have shed so much of my skin for the industry, but I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point, and I think that’s in that time frame, a point where you just have to stop taking. It’s giving me everything. “I am talking to you today. The first time I talked to you, I was a mid-card talent at WWE, and no shame to anything in the mid-card. Mid-card’s beautiful. I heard Triple H explain the mid-card in a way that changed my perception of it forever. But I was a mid-card talent with a ceiling that was right above my head, and I’m talking to you today as someone who got to play Guile from Street Fighter, created by Capcom, a game that I played growing up as a little kid. Again, be careful what you wish for, but also I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get hopefully more, hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far and so blessed so far that I think wrestling, I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in.” On whether he genuinely believes that ‘Cody fatigue’ has set in “Well, no, maybe. But I think you can only go so far, and you’re only supposed to go so far.”
