title: 5 Iconic WWE October PLE’s — Fall Classics
raw_title: Fall Classics: 5 Iconic WWE October PLE’s
body: October 22, 2026 By Daniel Sinasac WWE , History , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe October is another month that hasn’t gotten the full love that it deserves. Months that have housed shows like the Royal Rumble, WrestleMania, SummerSlam, and Survivor Series are ones that are marked on any wrestling fan’s calendar. Those shows have a strong foothold in certain months, hyping excitement as they approach. However, that leaves other months to fly under the radar when it comes to epic shows. As the leaves change, WWE fans wait for November to bring Survivor Series, but the previous month is no slouch in the PLE department. October has been home to many iconic shows that don’t get the credit they deserve. As fans look to bigger shows, they sometimes miss the amazing PLEs October has offered. No Mercy 1999 was filled with solid matches, highlighted by a match of the year. Chyna and Jeff Jarrett’s IC Championship match was more fun than it should have been. The Good Housekeeping stipulation hid the obvious deficiencies, and Chyna’s win was an historic moment. The Rock and British Bulldog, and Steve Austin battling Triple H were solid contests. They weren’t tearing the house down, but were engaging matches that kept the fans happy. The solid matches were the appetizer for the main course that was the ladder match between Edge & Christian and The Hardy Boys . It was the first time a tag team ladder match had taken place, and the originality with which it was presented set the tone for everything that came after. It foreshadowed the classic TLC matches that followed. Related Articles Hank and Tank or the Wagner Brothers – Which Team NEEDS a Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic Finals Berth? title: Cody Rhodes Believes The Rock Still Has a Couple of WWE Matches Left
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Believes The Rock Still Has a Couple of WWE Matches Left
body: By Jitu Jangir | October 22, 2026 at 7:22 PM IST 3 min read Cody Rhodes believes The Rock still has a few matches left in his wrestling career. During his latest interview with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes discussed the possibility of facing The Final Boss in a singles match and explained why WrestleMania 40 could also have been a fitting conclusion to The Rock's in-ring career. During his latest appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes was asked about the possibility of finally facing The Rock in a singles match. The conversation turned to WWE Elimination Chamber 2024 in Perth, Australia, where Rhodes publicly challenged The Rock to a one-on-one match during an appearance on The Grayson Waller Effect. Despite the challenge and their subsequent rivalry, the two have never faced each other in a singles match. When Van Vliet asked whether WWE had ever planned for that match to happen, Rhodes admitted that he wasn't sure how to answer the question. However, he did share his personal belief that The Rock could still compete in a few more matches before officially ending his wrestling career. “It's not that I'm evading that answer. It's that I don't really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40, and another guy who he's given all, continues to give all as part of the board, he could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring.” “That'll be up to him. That'll certainly be up to him if there's more and what those matches might be. I don't think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn't want a match like that.” The Rock made his in-ring return at WrestleMania 40 in April 2024, teaming with Roman Reigns against Rhodes and Seth Rollins in the main event of Night One. The Rock and Reigns won that match before Rhodes defeated Reigns the following night to capture the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. Their rivalry continued in 2025 when The Rock returned to WWE television and told Rhodes that he wanted his soul. Rhodes eventually rejected his offer at Elimination Chamber, leading to John Cena's shocking heel turn against The American Nightmare. Despite those developments, Rhodes and The Rock have yet to settle their differences inside the ring. For now, WWE has not announced another match involving The Rock, and Rhodes did not confirm that a singles encounter between them is being planned. Still, Rhodes believes another in-ring appearance is possible, leaving the door open for one of WWE's biggest unresolved rivalries to eventually reach its conclusion. Quotes transcribed by Sacnilk. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Says The Undertaker Belongs Among Wrestling's All-Time Greatest Stars
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Says The Undertaker Belongs Among Wrestling's All-Time Greatest Stars
body: During his latest appearance on INSIGHT with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes turned the tables on the interviewer and asked him to name his personal Mount Rushmore of professional wrestling. Van Vliet selected Stone Cold Steve Austin, The Rock, Hulk Hogan and The Undertaker. Rhodes agreed with The Undertaker's inclusion and explained why he considers The Deadman such an important figure in wrestling history. According to Rhodes, The Undertaker remained a respected and dependable presence during periods when wrestling was extremely popular and when it wasn't receiving the same mainstream attention. “I think Undertaker's a great choice, and I would have put him on my list before. I think he's a great choice because you need a guy like The Undertaker always and forever.” “And when I say that, what I mean is there are times when wrestling is cool as cool gets. We're living in one, right? Then there's times when wrestling is, you just tell that one guy to the side about it, you know, like, ‘Hey, I watch wrestling.’ Right now we're in this wonderful period.” The Undertaker made his WWE debut at Survivor Series in 1990 and went on to become one of the company's most recognizable Superstars. His career stretched across several major periods in WWE history, including the New Generation Era, the Attitude Era, the Ruthless Aggression Era and the modern era. During that time, he became a multiple-time World Champion, built his legendary WrestleMania undefeated streak and developed a reputation as one of WWE's most respected locker room leaders. Rhodes specifically pointed to The Undertaker's ability to carry himself as a leader while continuing to evolve his character and remain interesting to fans. “Undertaker, he floated in all periods, and you need the guy to hang in and lead the room and lead the talk and keep doing things to remain interesting. And again, the way everyone looks at Taker as the sheriff and the guy, right, who was standing there to pass that on to you, and for good reason. That's a great list.” The Undertaker's influence also extended beyond his matches. He became known as a veteran who helped maintain standards backstage, earning the nickname of WWE's locker room sheriff because of the respect he commanded among fellow wrestlers. He also explained that wrestling's biggest names helped build upon the work of previous generations, making it difficult to separate their individual contributions. Rhodes discussed the influence of Hulk Hogan and his own father, Dusty Rhodes, noting how their work helped professional wrestling grow during the 1980s. He also praised the lasting impact Dusty had on younger wrestlers during the final chapter of his career. While Rhodes did not reveal a definitive Mount Rushmore of his own during the conversation, he made it clear that The Undertaker would be a deserving choice. Quotes transcribed by Sacnilk. Per the agreement, Bleacher Report will hold global highlight rights across WWE’s programming slate, including Monday Night Raw , Friday Night SmackDown , NXT and WWE Premium Live Events such as WrestleMania ® , with content distributed across Bleacher Report, House of Highlights, B/R Wrestling — Bleacher Report’s dedicated wrestling brand — and their associated social and digital platforms. Adding WWE to its portfolio reflects B/R’s broader strategy to serve fans across the full spectrum of sports and sports culture, particularly around properties that inspire passionate, year-round conversation. Beyond highlights, Bleacher Report will have a ringside presence at select WWE PLEs, with B/R and House of Highlights content teams capturing original storytelling, talent-driven content and behind-the-scenes moments. “WWE fans don’t just watch. They are highly engaged, analyze every detail and debate the sport all week long. That’s exactly the kind of passionate fandom B/R and House of Highlights were built for,” said Bennett Spector, General Manager, Bleacher Report. “This partnership gives us the opportunity to bring fans closer to the biggest moments happening today while also tapping into the incredible history and personalities that have made WWE part of sports culture for generations.” "Bleacher Report has long been at the intersection of sports and culture,” said Alex Varga, EVP, WWE. "Our partnership with B/R reinforces WWE’s commitment to bringing our content to a global audience." WWE coverage will begin rolling out across Bleacher Report and House of Highlights platforms leading into WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday, October 10.

title: WWE’s Potential Dates for John Cena Classic Revealed
raw_title: WWE’s Potential Dates for John Cena Classic Revealed
summary_src: WWE still hasn’t locked down a date for the John Cena Classic, but the calendar is starting to get pretty crowded. Two dates are apparently still in play for December, while another option has now basically been crossed off the list.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , WWE still hasn’t decided whether the John Cena Classic will happen on December 12 or December 19. Cena has already confirmed the event is coming in December, but exactly where it lands remains up in the air. “As for the rumored John Cena Classic — which Cena himself has said will take place in December — a source couldn’t confirm whether the event is more likely to follow WrestlePalooza on December 12 with a stateside event that evening or take place the following weekend on December 19 — which would put it up against AEW Worlds End, as well as AAA Guerra De Titanes later that same evening.” December 12 would make for one seriously loaded day. WWE could hold WrestlePalooza overseas earlier in the day before following it up with the John Cena Classic back in the United States that evening. December 19 would be a very different story. That date would put Cena’s event directly against AEW Worlds End, while AAA Guerra De Titanes is also scheduled for later that night. There is at least one December date that WWE apparently isn’t too interested in. December 5 isn’t considered a likely option because the company doesn’t want to load up its schedule with major events on three straight weekends. “One source from WWE noted that Saturday, December 5 is not likely an option, as the company doesn’t want to present major events on three consecutive weekends. Meanwhile, December 26 is already on the calendar for WWE, as they’re set to host their annual holiday show at Madison Square Garden.” That also leaves December 26 effectively occupied by WWE’s annual holiday show at Madison Square Garden. For now, December 12 and December 19 remain the two dates worth watching. There’s also another interesting piece of the puzzle that has nothing to do with the calendar. Cena apparently still wants fans to have some kind of say in what happens at the event. “Additionally, a source noted that the voting aspect of the event is still something that John Cena would like to see happen. We’re told that several ideas have been floated internally to make that a possibility.” That voting element hasn’t been finalized either, but WWE is kicking around multiple ideas to make Cena’s vision work. Exactly what fans would be voting on wasn’t specified in the latest report. WWE clearly has some decisions to make before the John Cena Classic is ready for primetime. Between potentially creating a massive doubleheader on December 12, jumping into an already packed December 19 and figuring out Cena’s fan-voting idea, there’s still quite a bit left to settle before the event becomes official. title: The REAL Reason WWE Won't Cancel Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
raw_title: The REAL Reason WWE Won't Cancel Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
body: Over the last several weeks, advice from the likes of the US Embassy and State Department have been increasing in severity over their recommendations against travel to the Riyadh region of Saudi Arabia in the face of regular attacks and bombings in the area, including at the airport where many of those attending Crown Jewel 2026 may be arriving in just over two weeks time. According to WRKD Wrestling , several talents were reportedly opposed to traveling for Crown Jewel, which has prompted some dissatisfaction by WWE. Per Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer Radio , WWE is reportedly unhappy with employees voicing concerns, which doesn’t bode well for WWE’s intentions ahead of the show. Fans and critics alike have been asking why WWE hasn’t halted plans and changed venues given the dangers and risks posed, but there are some unsatisfactory answers which may explain the hesitation to move the show, much like how WWE didn’t change plans for Night Of Champions 2026 in the country earlier this year. WWE’s multi-year relationship with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has featured a whole host of controversies over the years, prompting a lot of negativity surrounding the fact that WrestleMania 43 will be held in the country, just a year after an awful Royal Rumble PLE that was hampered by the location. Just this week, it emerged via a new Morgan Stanley research summary that WWE would be earning at least $150 million in site fees for taking the major spectacle to Saudi Arabia. “Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens. He fears nothing. My country is home to the two Holy Mosques, land of peace, safety, rich civilization, deep history, and kind-hearted people. Thank you to everyone who checked in and showed support. Hard times reveal true friends.”

summary_src: WWE’s WarGames plans are starting to come into focus, and The Bloodline vs. 946 apparently won’t be stopping at the four-on-four fight fans saw on RAW. The company is planning to go five-on-five this year, which leaves one open spot on each side and two potentially huge reveals still to come.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , the plan as of Monday was to use five-person teams for this year’s WarGames match. That means Roman Reigns, The Usos and Solo Sikoa aren’t quite a complete team just yet. “Amid the rumors following Monday Night Raw and the four-on-four showdown between The Bloodline and 946, a source indicated that as of Monday, the plan is for this year’s WarGames match is to feature teams of five.” WWE has switched between four-on-four and five-on-five versions of WarGames over the years, so there was still some question about which direction the company would take this time. According to the latest update, WWE is sticking with the five-person format it has recently used on the main roster. “Since bringing back the match concept, WWE has utilized different formats, with teams ranging from four to five members on each side. However, it appears that this year’s installment will follow the recent trend on the main roster and feature the traditional five-on-five setup, pitting The Bloodline against The 946.” That suddenly makes the biggest question surrounding this feud pretty obvious — who gets those final two spots? Roman, Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso and Solo already have four places covered for The Bloodline, while Royce Keys, Carmelo Hayes, Bronco Nima and Lucien Price make up the four-man group they’ve been fighting. Jaida Parker has also been heavily involved with 946, including during Monday’s wild closing segment, but the report doesn’t say who WWE has in mind as the fifth competitor for either team. For now, those spots remain wide open. The latest update also adds another piece to what Dave Meltzer reported following RAW. While discussing whether Monday’s huge Bloodline and 946 brawl was setting up WarGames, Meltzer made it clear that was WWE’s direction : “Well, it is.” That’s when Roman’s music hit and San Diego came unglued. Reigns stormed the ring, reunited with his family and helped send 946 packing after dropping Keys with a Superman Punch and Nima with a Spear. Roman standing alongside Solo and The Usos already gave WWE its core WarGames team, but apparently the family still needs one more person before they can walk into the cage. With 946 also needing another competitor, WWE now has two mystery spots it can play with on the road to Survivor Series. Those fifth-member reveals could end up being just as important as the match itself. WWE already has the two sides ready for war, and now it has a couple of open spots that could add another wrinkle to the rivalry before November 28. title: WWE Planning Loaded NXT Show Against AEW Blood & Guts
raw_title: WWE Planning Loaded NXT Show Against AEW Blood & Guts
summary_src: NXT vs. AEW Dynamite is officially back for one night, and WWE apparently isn’t planning to show up quietly. The November 4 episode of NXT is now confirmed to be going head-to-head with AEW Blood & Guts, and WWE has been told to load up the show.
body: Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer confirmed the Wednesday night showdown after there had previously been some uncertainty about whether NXT would actually make the move. He added that NXT was told to load up the show. “Confirmed that November 4th NXT and AEW are going head-to-head. That’s the Blood and Guts show and NXT was told to load it up.” That last part makes things especially interesting. There’s no word yet on exactly what WWE plans to add to NXT, but being told to “load it up” certainly suggests the company isn’t treating this like an ordinary episode. “I don’t know this 100%. I was told by people who know that CW wants to move NXT to that Wednesday. It probably will be moved because if it’s on Tuesday, it’ll be preempted on far too many stations.” Now that move is confirmed, and WWE couldn’t have landed on a much bigger night for AEW. November 4 is the annual Blood & Guts edition of Dynamite, with AEW already planning two Blood & Guts matches for the show. Meltzer had previously suggested that NXT might need to come out of Halloween Havoc with a major angle to give viewers a reason to tune in that Wednesday. With Alvarez now reporting that NXT has actually been told to load up the episode, it looks like WWE is preparing for a fight once the two shows go head-to-head. There will be even more WWE programming fighting for attention that night too. EVOLVE airs Wednesdays at 8 PM ET on Tubi, while Main Event also occupies the same time slot on Rumble, meaning WWE could have three shows running while Blood & Guts is happening. The schedule change may have started because of election coverage, but November 4 is no longer looking like a simple one-week move for NXT. With WWE reportedly loading up the show and AEW already bringing out Blood & Guts, wrestling fans are getting another full-blown Wednesday night showdown. title: New Rumor Opens Up On WWE is Plotting a Major Send-Off for Another Legend in 2027
raw_title: New Rumor Reveals WWE is Plotting a Major Send-Off for Another Legend in 2027
body: According to people WrestleVotes spoke with , there have been rumblings of a legendary retirement within WWE in 2027, and that talk has centered on Mysterio. A source said they did not have direct knowledge of when or where an official retirement would take place. Instead, the source indicated that recent chatter at TV has pointed toward next year being the end of the road for Mysterio as an active wrestler. The same source said WWE has discussed ideas for how to present his farewell. There is also a feeling among many within the company that Mysterio will stay involved after his in-ring career ends, much like AJ Styles , and that he would continue playing a key role in developing the next generation of talent in WWE and AAA. Styles wrestled his final match at the Royal Rumble in January and has since moved into a role helping younger wrestlers. Mysterio has addressed the idea of retirement himself. In an August interview on WWE’s Raw Recap, he said he had been asking himself whether it was getting close to his time to retire. “I certainly don’t feel like I am,” he said, while adding that he always listens to his body and that the moment “can just pop up one day out of nowhere.” In the same interview, he spoke about his role as AAA’s general manager. “I am enjoying the position of being AAA’s GM and seeing the young rising stars come up in the game,” Mysterio said. The 51-year-old has stayed active on Raw. He beat Big Cass on the October 12 episode and challenged Chad Gable for the Intercontinental Championship twice since August, losing a singles match on the August 17 episode and a triple threat with Dragon Lee on the October 19 episode. He has also worked on AAA programming, teaming with El Grande Americano on the October 3 episode of AAA on FOX. If 2027 is the year, WWE has time to do it right. Mysterio is one of the most important wrestlers of his generation, and his career has connected fans across the United States and Mexico for more than three decades. A farewell run that includes WWE and AAA would reflect that, and it would give fans in both countries a chance to see him one last time. The more important part of this report may be what comes after. Mysterio has already shown how much he cares about the people around him, from helping get Psicosis his surgery to the time he has spent working with younger talent. A role developing wrestlers in WWE and AAA would put that experience to good use, especially with AAA now part of the WWE family. WWE should take the AJ Styles approach and give Mysterio a clear final stretch with a defined ending. He has earned a send-off that matches his place in wrestling history, and announcing it ahead of time would let fans enjoy the final run instead of wondering when it will end.
summary: Per people WrestleVotes spoke with , there have been rumblings of a legendary retirement within WWE in 2027, and that talk has centered on Mysterio. If 2027 is the year, WWE has time to do it right.

title: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton: A Rivalry Spanning Over a Decade

body: One of the current main-event storylines on WWE programming is “The American Nightmare” Cody Rhodes versus “The Viper” Randy Orton. Whether you consider this a continuation of their WrestleMania headlining feud – or perhaps a make-good for the shortcomings and unnecessary detours that derailed that program – Cody and Randy are once again standing face-to-face, man-to-man, on WWE SmackDown. Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes have a relationship that stretches back well over a decade. Cody’s first match on WWE main roster programming was against Orton, and he later became one of Randy’s henchmen alongside Ted DiBiase in the heel group Legacy. After Legacy broke apart, Cody and Randy had a brief feud that is often forgotten. Even before Cody’s departure from WWE, the two found themselves on opposite sides of another storyline, with Orton representing The Authority and Cody standing alongside his brother Goldust and their father, “The American Dream” Dusty Rhodes. That program also marked Dusty’s final major character appearance on professional wrestling television. Since Cody’s return to WWE, he and Randy had largely been portrayed as friends. That friendship came to a dramatic end when Randy viciously attacked Cody, transforming their WrestleMania main-event title match into a personal grudge match. Unfortunately, in the weeks that followed, the feud seemed to lose its way. Or, perhaps more accurately, a hot feud became a dumpster fire. The introduction of Pat McAfee into the program, along with an abundance of meta nonsense, left many wrestling fans frustrated. A lackluster match at WrestleMania did little to remove the sour taste the program had left behind. Now, four months later and following a 100-day absence, Randy has returned to attack Cody, and in many ways, we are right back where we started in January. Hopefully, this time WWE keeps the destination in mind and takes a more straightforward route to get there. Cody and Randy have too much significant history—or should I say Legacy—for this story not to receive a climactic conclusion worthy of their long relationship. In this week’s column, we will explore three matches from the lengthy and interconnected history between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton. The breakup of Legacy in 2010 and the subsequent feud between its members and Randy Orton ultimately did little for Cody Rhodes – and, frankly, I’m not sure it was supposed to. It’s easy to forget now, but after Legacy broke apart, many fans, and probably WWE Creative, believed Ted DiBiase Jr. was more poised and ready to be elevated up the card than Cody Rhodes. Cody was the tagalong. In the end, however, the feud did little for Cody and even less for DiBiase, as neither man was established as a truly believable threat to Randy Orton. Cody’s first real momentum as a singles star came the following year in his feud with Rey Mysterio. That program involved Mysterio damaging Cody’s face and Cody subsequently wearing a mask. On paper, it sounds bizarre. I
summary: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton are currently feuding once again on WWE SmackDown in what some view as an extension of their WrestleMania main event program. Their history dates back more than ten years, beginning with Rhodes' first main roster match against Orton, followed by Rhodes joining him in the Legacy faction alongside Ted DiBiase. After Legacy disbanded the pair had a short feud, and later opposed each other in a program featuring The Authority against Rhodes, his brother Goldust and their father Dusty Rhodes, which served as Dusty's last significant on-screen role.

title: WWE Considering Bringing Back Sin Cara Character
raw_title: WWE Considering Bringing Back Sin Cara Character
summary_src: WWE could be getting ready to bring Sin Cara back, but not necessarily the man who previously wore the mask. The company has reportedly started kicking around ideas for resurrecting the character with an entirely new wrestler taking over the role.
body: According to PWInsider , there have been early pitches within WWE centered around bringing the Sin Cara character back. Nothing has been finalized yet, but the concept is officially being discussed. The biggest twist is that WWE apparently isn’t looking at this as a comeback for the previous Sin Cara. If the company actually moves forward with the idea, the current pitch would put somebody new underneath the mask. There’s no word yet on who WWE might have in mind for the role, and the report doesn’t indicate how far along those conversations have gotten. For now, these are simply early pitches, so there’s no guarantee Sin Cara will actually return to television. The timing is pretty interesting considering the previous Sin Cara was just talking about wanting another shot at the character last month. Speaking to TMZ’s Inside the Ring in September, he admitted he would happily return to WWE and put the mask back on if the company ever approached him. “For me, I wouldn’t mind coming back. If they would ask me or we would talk, ‘Hey, you want to portray Sin Cara again?’ I would love to do that definitely again and give it another shot.” He also explained that he’s matured considerably since his original WWE run and believes he would approach things differently today. His first stint ended after he publicly requested his release in November 2019, with WWE eventually granting it the following month. “It’s something that I really think about sometimes in my head. Like, what if this and what if that happen? And in wrestling, anything is possible. You understand that?” Apparently, something involving Sin Cara really could happen again — just potentially without him. WWE owns the character, and if these early pitches eventually turn into actual plans, fans could end up seeing a completely new wrestler trying to make the mask their own. That creates an interesting wrinkle after the former Sin Cara openly talked about wanting another chance just weeks ago. WWE hasn’t committed to bringing the character back yet, but if it does, the bigger story may quickly become who the company trusts to inherit the mask. title: Powell Reviews AEW Dynamite With Dragunov Debut Win
raw_title: Powell's AEW Dynamite Hit List: Thoughts on the Mark Davis and Jake Doyle squashing the Young Bucks, Ilja Dragunov's debut match, the build to Blood & Guts
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Ilja Dragunov vs. Mike Bailey: A good win for Dragunov in a competitive match with Bailey. I probably would have avoided putting this match in the main event spot to avoid making it seem like a former secondary champion in WWE is a bigger deal than everyone else on the show, but saving this for last was probably more about television ratings than anything. Bailey was a good first opponent because he is over with the fans and was a lock to have a good match with Dragunov. Furthermore, the company didn’t have to give away a main event player facing Dragunov on night one. I wouldn’t ask Dragunov to bury his former employer, but AEW should drive home the message that he chose to leave WWE when his contract expired rather than this being a case of AEW picking up a WWE cut casualty. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight vs. AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland: What is up with Ospreay teaming with babyfaces who are going to challenge him for the AEW World Championship? He’s teamed with Andrade El Idolo a few times since Andrade won the contract that gives him a title shot with seven days’ notice. Ospreay and Copeland were not in the same orbit until Ospreay pinned Copeland to win the Clockwork Carnage match, which Copeland followed by telling Ospreay that he’s coming for his title. Anyway, the match was entertaining and seemed to move Ospreay and Copeland away from one another and into matches with Fletcher and the interfering Kazuchika Okada, respectively. The post-match angle felt contrived, as it conveniently set up the Blood & Guts match, but that’s become the norm for most WarGames-style matches since they became calendar events. As much as I loved the Davis and Doyle squash win over the Bucks, I really could have done without the Bucks coming out to help run off the Callis Family heels just one match later. Nick Wayne and Chris Jericho: A soft Hit for a decent segment. Wayne is in a better place than he was when his feud with Jericho started, and it was good to hear Jericho put him over verbally without calling for a rematch. The follow-up program is crucial for Wayne. It should be all about adding to the momentum he gained from beating Jericho (insert pyro here) in two of their three matches. Orange Cassidy and Jay White vs. Wheeler Yuta and Daniel Garcia: A minor Miss for a match that seemed to happen so they could establish a quick relationship between Cassidy and White before White turned on Cassidy later in the show. By the way, if the Death Riders are so committed to greatness, shouldn’t Jon Moxley put more pressure on Yuta and Garcia to win some meaningful matches?
summary: Ilja Dragunov defeated Mike Bailey in a competitive main event match on AEW Dynamite. The placement was viewed as a ratings decision rather than elevating the newcomer above the rest of the roster. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight faced AEW World Champion Will Ospreay and Adam Copeland in tag team action while the show built toward the upcoming Blood & Guts event.

TNA stars are entering an NXT Women’s Battle Royal to determine the #1 contender to Kelani Jordan’s NXT Championship at Halloween Havoc. After many attempts at capturing the NXT Women’s Championship, Kelani Jordan finally made it to the top. Now, she has to contend with 20 other hungry Superstars. That’s because Robert Stone has booked a women’s battle royal to determine Kelani Jordan’s next challenger. Kelani Jordan made it clear on NXT that her reign wouldn’t feature “open challenges.” She noted Wren Sinclair’s suspension and Kendal Grey’s absence essentially left her without any contenders. This assertion drew the ire of NXT General Manager, Robert Stone. The former Robbie E stated that Kelani Jordan won’t decide the next challenger because a 20-Woman Battle Royal will. Since Kelani Jordan won’t give out open challenges, Robert Stone opened the door for other companies. The NXT GM announced that five brands will be involved in the Women’s Battle Royal. The most shocking of these companies is TNA. As a former TNA star himself, Robert Stone was the perfect person to announce the company’s return to WWE TV. Now, we have word on who some of these talents will be. Halloween Havoc takes place on Halloween night. As this holiday event approaches, WWE is trying to lock down the card. To draw some excitement, NXT is hosting a multi-company Women’s Battle Royal. Here are the competitors who will vie for a chance to challenge Kelani Jordan at Halloween Havoc: This match features many Champions., including the TNA Knockouts and TNA Knockouts Television Champions. So, it seems like WWE is trying to shine a light on the Division, as TNA is struggling to fill the venue for Bound for Glory. Hopefully, this extra attention on CW will help TNA sell more tickets in Tampa. Many believe that while WWE is featuring TNA talent on NXT next week, not much in their deal is changing. WWE is aware they received some bad press last week. They’re also trying to drum up some interest in the Women’s Battle Royal by adding other companies. Creative team members felt adding The Elegance Brand, Indi Hartwell, and Xia Brookeside would increase the buzz in light of the trending news surrounding WWE and TNA’s partnership going south. Interestingly, the last time TNA talent appeared on NXT was during last November’s Gold Rush. At the time, Kelani Jordan was the TNA Knockouts Champion. She defended the Title in a Triple Threat Match against Jordynne Grace and Léi Yǐng Lee. Léi Yǐng Lee defeated Kelani Jordan to become the new TNA Knockouts Champion.
summary: It’s been almost three months since an NXT talent appeared on iMPACT Wrestling television, and almost a year since someone from TNA appeared on NXT on CW. Less than a week later, WWE claps back by booking TNA talent on next week’s NXT.

title: Judge Keeps AEW Moxley Lawsuit In Michigan

summary_src: A judge has denied AEW and Jon Moxley's request to move a civil lawsuit to a Florida court. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling first reported the news on Thursday, referencing the lawsuit that former production worker Christopher Dispensa filed back in May 2025.
body: A judge has denied AEW and Jon Moxley’s request to move a civil lawsuit to a Florida court. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling first reported the news on Thursday, referencing the lawsuit that former production worker Christopher Dispensa filed back in May 2025. As some fans may remember, Dispensa filed the suit alleging negligence, civil assault, and battery over an incident where he was pushed to the floor by Moxley. Thurston’s new report notes that the judge chose to keep the case in Michigan, where the incident occurred in May 2023. Back in July, AEW asked to move the case to Florida because that’s where Dispensa and most of his doctors live. Furthermore, a second settlement conference with the court is set to take place on December 22, 2026. The first conference was held in July of this year. Fightful will update fans when a new update surfaces on the Chris Dispensa’s lawsuit. In the meantime, check out the current lineup for Saturday’s episode of AEW Collision by clicking here.
summary: A judge denied AEW and Jon Moxley's request to transfer former production worker Christopher Dispensa's civil lawsuit from Michigan to Florida. Dispensa filed the suit in May 2025 alleging negligence, civil assault and battery after being pushed to the floor by Moxley during an incident in Michigan in May 2023. A second settlement conference is scheduled for December 22 2026 after the first one took place in July.

llm_long: A judge denied a request from AEW and Jon Moxley to transfer a civil lawsuit filed by former production worker Christopher Dispensa to a Florida court. Brandon Thurston of POST Wrestling reported the development on Thursday. The lawsuit, which Dispensa filed in May 2025, remains in Michigan where the alleged incident took place in May 2023.

Dispensa's suit accuses Moxley of negligence along with civil assault and battery after an incident in which Moxley pushed him to the floor. AEW had sought to move the case to Florida in July because Dispensa and most of his doctors reside there. The judge ruled against the transfer and kept the matter in Michigan.
A second settlement conference between the parties is scheduled for December 22, 2026. The initial settlement conference occurred in July of this year.

title: Injury Update: Injury Rules El Desperado Out of NJPW Super Jr. Tag League 2026, Replacement Set
raw_title: Injury Rules El Desperado Out of NJPW Super Jr. Tag League 2026, Replacement Announced
body: El Desperado has been ruled out of the NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 due to injury. New Japan Pro-Wrestling announced on Thursday, October 22, that one-half of the current IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions, El Desperado, has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. El Desperado and Mistico were originally drawn in Block A. However, with the former having been ruled out, Mistico will now team with NJPW Young Lion Masatora Yasuda. Desperado said his body has reached its limit and apologized to fans. No timeline is currently set for his return. Here’s what he said: “My sincerest apologies, but I will not be appearing at Super Jr. Tag League. I’m currently dealing with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles, I’m currently unable to stand, walk, or even sit upright for long periods of time. From the start of this year I’d noticed some strange sensations in my left glute, and there was some tingling in my legs from around March. At that point I expressed to the company that I was having some symptoms but that I had no issues with strength or anything like that and asked to continue wrestling while staying in contact with the medical and training staff. “For this Super Jr. Tag League, Mistico was scheduled to wrestle with me, and we can’t just send him back with nothing to say for it, so I have chosen (Masatora) Yasuda to replace me. Some of you might think ‘with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,’ but I’d like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW.” -> Mistico & Masatora Yasuda -> Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X -> Yoshinobu Kanemaru & DOUKI -> Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi -> Master Wato & KUUKAI -> KUSHIDA & Nick Wayne -> Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita -> YOH & Hyo -> Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young -> Titan & Daiki Nagai -> SHO & Dick Togo -> Blake Christian & Lee Johnson The tournament will get underway in Saitama, Japan, on October 24. The top scorers from each Block will battle in the final at NJPW Power Struggle on November 3. El Desperado , NJPW , NJPW Super Junior Tag League , Yash Mittal

body: On Friday, October 23, CMLL will present their Grand Prix de Amazonas main event this year. The 11-on-11 matchup will feature talent from all over the world, including those from the AEW roster. Considering the partnership between the two promotions, it should not be shocking to see All Elite Wrestling having a heavy presence on this major bout coming up in Arena Mexico. Here are six AEW stars to compete in the CMLL Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026. It should be no surprise that Persephone will compete for Team CMLL for the Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 match. While she has signed a dual contract with both CMLL and AEW, Perse is still the CMLL World Women’s Champion and is the face of the company’s Amazonas division. Holding gold in both promotions as the TBS Champion as well, all eyes should be on Persephone in this match on the October 23 show. On Team World, there will be several stars from the AEW roster competing. Queen Aminata is someone who has been a featured star on AEW TV as of late. After coming up short against Persephone in a TBS Championship four-way at AEW WrestleDream 2026, Aminata might be looking to score a pinfall over Persephone to get another opportunity. Another AEW star who will be part of Team World in the Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 is Harley Cameron . The former AEW Women’s World Tag Team Champion will look to make her presence felt in this bout. Making her CMLL debut, Cameron can make her mark in this Cibernetico bout on October 23. Someone who has been a force wherever she goes in AEW or elsewhere is Megan Bayne . One half of Divine Dominion will be part of the Team World in the CMLL Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 match. With her mixture of size, power and agility, Bayne should hold her own and could make it to the very end of this 11-on-11 main event showdown. In 2026, Thunder Rosa became the latest star to sign a dual contract with AEW and CMLL. The former AEW Women’s World Champion will be part of Team CMLL in the Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026 bout. While she is the current Mexican National Women’s Champion, Rosa should have some interesting interactions with both Team CMLL as well as Team World during this contest. Shotzi was scheduled to take part of the CMLL Grand Prix de Amazonas 2026, but she had to be pulled after a passing in her family. In her place, AEW’s Marina Shafir will take her place and look to continue The Death Riders’ presence in CMLL. Wanting a standout performance, Shafir will come in with a chip on her shoulder after not being originally announced for this match and should come in with a fire that no other competitor might have in this match from Arena Mexico. title: Rey Mysterio Rumored To Retire In 2027
raw_title: Backstage News On Potential Upcoming Retirement Of WWE Hall Of Famer Rey Mysterio
summary_src: A new report revealed there is backstage chatter regarding the potential in-ring retirement of WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , there are internal rumblings of Rey Mysterio retiring in 2027. A source told the outlet there is chatter backstage that the legendary luchador could be wrapping up as an active wrestler next year. That source did, however, tell WrestleVotes they had no direct knowledge of when or where Mysterio's potential retirement match could happen. It was not noted if there were plans for him to a have a retirement tour run, like Cena. The source said that WWE creative minds have discussed ideas on how to present Mysterio's farewell to fans, however. The current on-screen AAA general manager is expected to remain a part of the company behind-the-scenes, helping younger talent in both WWE and AAA. The Hall of Famer began his career on the independent scene in 1989. He signed with WCW in 1996 and helped popularize lucha libre in the states, and was pivotal in establishing a cruiserweight division in the promotion. Mysterio joined WWE in 2002, with a hiatus from 2015 to 2018, where he worked elsewhere, including NJPW and Lucha Underground.
summary: Per Fightful Select, internal WWE chatter suggests Rey Mysterio may retire from in-ring competition next year. A source indicated creative has brainstormed ways to present his farewell to fans though no specifics on timing, location or a potential retirement tour are known. The WWE Hall of Famer, currently serving as on-screen AAA general manager, is expected to stay with both companies in a backstage role mentoring young talent.

title: Syko Stu Reflects On Raja Jackson Altercation
raw_title: Syko Stu Looks Back On Infamous Raja Jackson Incident
summary_src: In August 2025, Syko Stu (Stuart Smith) was brutally attacked by Raja Jackson at an independent show. Smith has opened up about the incident for the first time
body: They had shaken hands prior to the in-ring incident and he didn't expect things to escalate the way that they did. After the beer can spot, they decided to make it an angle.
summary: Syko Stu has looked back on the well-known in-ring incident with Raja Jackson. The pair had shaken hands before the situation unfolded and he did not anticipate it escalating. Following a beer can spot the decision was made to turn the moment into an angle.

llm.headline: Syko Stu Reflects On Raja Jackson Altercation
llm.summary: Syko Stu has looked back on the well-known in-ring incident with Raja Jackson. The pair had shaken hands before the situation unfolded and he did not anticipate it escalating. Following a beer can spot the decision was made to turn the moment into an angle.

llm_long: At a KnokX Pro event on August 23 2025, Raja Jackson knocked independent wrestler Syko Stu unconscious during a planned spot that escalated beyond the script.
Raja slammed Stu and then delivered more than 20 unanswered legitimate strikes to his head until independent wrestler Doug Malo intervened and pulled him away.
Syko Stu has limited memory of the incident itself. He recalled Raja filming backstage, which is unusual, and remembered calling a finish that involved one wrestling punch after a beer can spot.

Stu stated he was unconscious from the initial slam and has no recollection of the following events. He woke up in the hospital on Tuesday after being admitted on Saturday and remained in and out of consciousness until then.
During his hospital stay, medical staff would not show him video of the incident or discuss it. Wrestler Rikishi visited him there as he began to recover.

Stu was discharged from the hospital on Thursday. He now participates in word exercises during rehabilitation but continues to experience short-term memory issues such as forgetting things within minutes, repeating actions, and failing to recall names and faces.

title: US Embassy In Riyadh Issues Advisory As WWE Crown Jewel Draws Closer

body: A security alert has been issued by the US Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for US citizens. In the statement, issued on Thursday, October 22, the Riyadh-based Embassy has advised US citizens to take “extreme caution” when using airports in Saudi Arabia. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended, while airports in Dammam and Jeddah are operational with “some delays and cancellations.” “Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area. U.S. citizens are reminded to follow the guidance of national alerts released by Saudi Arabia’s Civil Defense via cellular broadcast. “U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom. Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations. “U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. We recommend checking your flight departure status directly with the airline and with the airport.” Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. title: Cody Rhodes Keeping a List of Wrestlers Who Didn’t Support His Street Fighter Movie
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Keeping a List of Wrestlers Who Didn’t Support His Street Fighter Movie
summary_src: Cody Rhodes is apparently keeping receipts when it comes to which wrestlers supported his new Street Fighter movie. The WWE star admitted he’s been paying close attention to who showed up, who promoted the film and, more importantly, who didn’t.
body: That led Cody into a much broader point about wrestlers supporting each other’s success outside the ring. While wrestlers might say they want to see their peers succeed, Cody believes the real test comes when it’s actually time to show that support. “You could be, but also, Seth—wrestlers always tell each other how much they want each other to do great, but then in those moments, they don’t necessarily support. Seth showed up at the Street Fighter premiere. He’s a real one. He’s a real one. And trust me, I kept track of who showed up, who didn’t, who posted, you know, who didn’t show up.” When asked whether he really had a list of people who didn’t post about Street Fighter, Cody confirmed it without hesitation. He also admitted there was more than a little pettiness involved: “Oh, yeah.” Cody then explained why the lack of support bothered him so much. With three wrestlers involved in Street Fighter, he sees the movie’s success as something that could help move the entire wrestling industry forward rather than simply benefiting him. “Oh, deep pettiness. Deep. Because, I mean, there’s three wrestlers in this movie, and you can’t throw up a, ‘Hey, go see this thing, guys’? What are we doing? We’re trying to move the ball forward.” Cody made it clear that he views the opportunity as something that can benefit everybody in wrestling. At the same time, he jokingly acknowledged that he’s obviously getting a little extra out of the movie doing well. “It’s for everybody. And yeah, is it a little better for me? Sure.” Cody didn’t name any of the wrestlers who landed on the wrong side of his list, so he’s keeping that part to himself for now. Rollins, however, clearly isn’t one of them after making the effort to attend the premiere despite the complicated history between the two WWE stars. title: Parks Highlights Dragunov's Top AEW Matchup Possibilities
raw_title: PARKS’S TAKE: Looking at Ilja Dragunov’s list of standout potential opponents on AEW roster
body: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW last night on Dynamite, defeating “Speedball” Mike Bailey in the show’s main event. The positioning of Dragunov in the last match immediately put him on the map as someone who should be taken seriously by the fans and a threat to the major titles in the company. Even when he was in WWE, Dragunov always seemed like a better fit for AEW. His hard-hitting, aggressive intensity is much closer stylistically to what AEW offers. In that way, Dragunov was a unicorn in WWE, which actually helped make his matches stand out even more. However, it was clear he was unlikely to get above a certain level on Raw or Smackdown. With Dragunov now in AEW, there are a ton of enticing matchups for him. Here are a few that are high on my anticipation list: -Jon Moxley: AEW’s resident hard hitter could meet his match with Dragunov. In fact, Dragunov would even fit in with the motif of the Death Riders should they look to add a new member. -Claudio Castagnoli: These two could just end up trading chops and uppercuts for 15 minutes. I’d be fine with that. -Konosuke Takeshita: Dragunov’s European offense melds well with the Japanese strong style, as does his selling. Takeshita would be able to give as well as he takes. -Nick Wayne: Wayne has recently found his stride as an overconfident, cocky heel who fans will want to see his comeuppance. They’ll also want to see him get bashed around and bruised by the violent Dragunov. -Kyle O’Reilly: This would give Dragunov a little bit of a different work in an opponent who prefers to work holds. Dragunov’s facial reactions have been a strength and he could satisfactorily convey the pain that O’Reilly’s holds bring.
summary: Ilja Dragunov opened his AEW run by beating Mike Bailey in the main event of Dynamite, instantly positioning him as a serious contender for major titles. His intense, hard-hitting style that stood out as unique in WWE now aligns closely with AEW's product. Among the most anticipated future opponents are Jon Moxley, who could even recruit him into the Death Riders, Claudio Castagnoli for a stiff chops-and-uppercuts battle, and Konosuke Takeshita.

title: WWE Live Event Sees Styles Challenge Ambrose for Title
raw_title: 10 YEARS AGO – WWE LIVE EVENT REPORT: AJ Styles vs. Dean Ambrose for WWE Title, plus Ziggler, Kane, Bray Wyatt, Naomi, Alexa Bliss, Usos, Corbin
body: The following is a report originally published here 10 years ago this week… (1) Dolph Ziggler defeated Tyler Breeze to retain the Intercontinental Championship. Dolph scored the pinfall after hitting a Super Kick. Great opening contest with fast-paced action. (2) SmackDown Tag Champion Heath Slater & The Hype Bros (w/Mascot Cowboy Joe) defeated Viktor & The Vaudevillains. Slater pinned Simon Gotch after the “Smash Hit” DDT. This was a entertaining six man tag match. Cowboy Joe is the mascot for the Wyoming Cowboys basketball and football teams. (3) Apollo Crews defeated Curt Hawkins. Crews won with a spin out powerbomb. Solid match up, but afterward Curt Hawkins tells us all we need to face the facts, challenges anyone to come out and face the facts, then “The Demon” Kane’s music hit and he came out to answer the challenge. (4) Kane defeated Curt Hawkins. Kane won via chokeslam in less than 10 seconds. Bray Wyatt cut a promo on the video screen about Randy Orton. (5) Baron Corbin defeated Jack Swagger. Corbin wins via roll up. (6) Randy Orton defeated Bray Wyatt. Orton attempted an RKO, but Wyatt reversed it into a “Sister Abigail.” Then Orton countered into a roll up and Wyatt kicked out, Finally the Viper hit the RKO out of nowhere for the win. Another great match with Orton being really over with the crowd and doing what he does best. Mostly all the fans had their phones lit up as “fire flies” during Wyatts’s entrance. Afterward, Orton circled around, took pictures, and signed autographs for the fans. Styles cut a promo on the video screen about his match with Ambrose later in the night and said he is “the face that runs the place.” (7) Naomi & Natalya defeated Alexa Bliss & Carmella. Naomi pinned Alexa for the win. Towards the end of the match Naomi tried to tag in Natalya, but since Natty is still playing her heel role, she stepped off the apron and walked to the back. Afterwards Naomi danced. (8) American Alpha defeated The Usos. Alpha gets the win with a Grand Amplitude on Jimmy. Solid tag team match. (9) A.J. Styles defeated Dean Ambrose to retain the WWE World Championship. Ambrose almost had the match won, but A.J. hit him with a low blow and Styles Clash for the finish. Great performances by both men as always. The match went about 20 minutes with plenty of action and near falls. Afterwards Styles grabbed the mic and said, “I’m the face that runs the place, the champ that runs the camp, and still the WWE World Champion!” Ambrose then delivered a Dirty Deeds on A.J. to send the crowd home happy. BIGGEST POPS: Orton Ambrose Styles (mixed reaction) Kane Ziggler Wyatt (ring entrance) Hype Bros and Slater Naomi Crews MOST HEEL HEAT: Hawkins Breeze Wyatt (as he taunted the crowd) Usos Styles (mixed reaction) Corbin Vaudevillains and Viktor Natty (when she walked out on Naomi) We still invite live event reports in 2026 to be published here at PWTorch! title: Cody Rhodes Plans Retirement in Six to Seven Years
raw_title: WWE’s Cody Rhodes gives fresh timeline on retirement after signing ‘last contract’
body: In the next decade, Cody Rhodes will retire from professional wrestling after signing his latest contract with WWE , which will be his "last" one. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet, the "American Nightmare" gave an update on the timeline for his retirement. He previously told Van Vliet that he was going to retire at 40. Rhodes, who is now 41, reinforced that the latest contract he signed will be his "last." However, it will "go for a while." If all goes well, he plans to retire within the next six or seven years. "With all that said, my time with WWE could go probably seven years, six [or] seven [years]," he said, before saying he didn't mean to make a "6-7" joke. He definitely doesn't want to wrestle into his 50s, like legends such as Rey Mysterio are currently doing. Rhodes has been given so much from the industry, but he also knows it's almost his time to "stop taking" from it. It sounds like Rhodes will retire from WWE within the next decade, so fans should buckle up. He is still at the top of the company, but he seems to understand that Father Time is undefeated. Some of his decision to hang it up might depend on his success in Hollywood. After having a small role in the Liam Neeson-led Naked Gun reboot, he starred in the Street Fighter movie alongside his former WWE rival, Roman Reigns. The movie has been a hit so far, grossing over $50 million to date. It topped the domestic box office with its $31.1 million haul during its opening weekend.
summary: Cody Rhodes confirmed to Chris Van Vliet that the new contract he signed with WWE will be his final one. Now 41, he expects to step away from the ring in six or seven years and does not want to wrestle into his 50s. Rhodes acknowledged that the industry has given him much and feels it is nearly time to stop taking from it.

title: Jim Ross returns home after hospital stay
raw_title: Jim Ross back home and “on the mend” after recent hopsital visit
summary_src: Conrad Thompson provided an encouraging update on Jim Ross, who had to be in the hospital "due to low oxygen."
body: Jim Ross is back home after a recent hospital visit earlier this month. The 74-year-old posted on social media on Oct. 12 that he had to be back in the hospital “due to low oxygen.” The event came after his second brain procedure, and he added in his post that he weighed 198 pounds. On the latest episode of “Grilling JR,” co-host Conrad Thompson offered encouraging news about Ross. I finally got an update on the Voice of Wrestling, Mr. Jim Ross. As you all know, J.R. had to do a little outpatient visit recently, and it turns out he got a little bit of a chest cold. He’s got some sort of infection in his chest. They said his oxygen was low, so he spent the night in the hospital, but I’m happy to report that he is home and on the mend. They still haven’t gotten his shunt hooked back up yet, so we’re hoping for that sooner rather than later. Thompson added that Ross was still “under the weather.” He also called back to a quote from Ross, “Hey, man, if it wasn’t for bad luck, I’d have no luck at all,” as a way to show their support for his recovery. Ross has undergone a pair of operations on his brain over the past two months. In August, he had a shunt inserted to address problems he was experiencing regarding his memory and balance. This month, he had a second procedure, which he stated was to address an issue with the shunt. Ross last appeared on an AEW broadcast at Double or Nothing this past May.
summary: Jim Ross was hospitalized earlier this month due to low oxygen levels following his second brain procedure. The 74-year-old spent one night in the hospital after developing a chest infection and cold. Per the latest Grilling JR podcast, Ross is now home and recovering though still under the weather with his shunt yet to be reconnected.

summary_src: WWE has added another young athlete to its developmental system, and this one has already been through the company’s tryout process twice. Former Michigan State track and field athlete Elly Finch has officially signed with WWE and is headed to the NXT Performance Center.
body: According to a report by PWInsider , WWE has signed the 23-year-old Finch to a developmental contract. She participated in WWE tryouts in both January and August 2026 before ultimately landing a deal. “WWE has signed Elly Finch, 23, who took part in January and August 2026 tryouts to a WWE developmental deal, PWInsider.com has confirmed.” Finch will now be part of the incoming class at the WWE Performance Center, where she’ll begin the next stage of her transition into professional wrestling. She comes in with an athletic background that goes well beyond her time competing in track and field. Before getting WWE’s attention, Finch competed as a shot put thrower for Michigan State’s track and field team. title: WWE Pitches Revival Of Sin Cara Character
raw_title: Backstage News On Internal WWE Pitch To Revive Defunct Luchador Character
summary_src: Two different backstage reports reveal there has been an internal pitch within WWE creative to revive the defunct luchador character Sin Cara
body: Many will recall that the Sin Cara character was created in 2011 after WWE signed the luchador Mistico. The gimmick would ultimately be portrayed by both Mistico and the luchador Hunico, who took over the gimmick after Mistico was out with injury in mid-2011; upon his return, the two would feud, culminating in a mask vs. mask match where Mistico defeated Hunico. The latter would later don the character again following Mistico's departure in 2014, and continued to portray Sin Cara until he requested and received his release in 2019 . While the character was seen as a strong merchandise mover, the Sin Cara character was largely perceived as a flop , particularly the Mistico incarnation, as the character never moved past the midcard and became well known for botches. For years, Mistico's time as Sin Cara was seen as significantly hindered his career; he has since seen a career resurgence back in CMLL as the promotion's top star, being credited for the promotion's boom period over the last few years. PW Insider is reporting that there have been early pitches based around the idea of resurrecting the Sin Cara character in WWE. False Finish has learned that Myzteziz Jr. was under consideration to resurrect the Sin Cara character pic.twitter.com/IEZiJ4zdKd Now yes, the argument from people in favor of this will be that it was only a favor because Mistico was a bust under the gimmick. He was, but I would argue that was WWE's fault, a result of WWE trying to turn Mistico into something he wasn't instead of playing to his strengths, something that's led to him succeeding in every other company he's worked for. Furthermore, if Sin Cara failing was just a Mistico problem, why did Hunico never get the gimmick over after? Either way it doesn't matter; the character failed, and bringing it back a decade later isn't going to suddenly revitalize it anymore than WWE bringing back the LWO revitalized that concept. I should also point out that it's comical WWE is attempting this when they already have a Mistico knockoff gimmick in house in Myzteziz Jr., and may be pursuing Dralistico, himself a Mistico knockoff! I've already spent too much time on this, so I will again reiterate; this is a silly, stupid, bad idea on WWE's part. And if they knew better, they'd kill this in the crib right now before it goes beyond the pitch stage.
summary: WWE officials have received internal pitches about bringing back the Sin Cara luchador gimmick that was active from 2011 through 2019. The character was originally created for Mistico, then portrayed by Hunico after an injury and later full-time following Mistico's 2014 exit from the company. Hunico continued as Sin Cara until requesting and receiving his release in 2019, with the persona viewed as a merchandise success but an overall in-ring disappointment that never rose above the midcard.

title: Swerve Strickland Claims Highest In-Ring Level For Black Wrestler
raw_title: AEW's Swerve Strickland: I Perform At 'Highest Level' For A Black Wrestler In History
summary_src: AEW's Swerve Strickland told Billboard that he feels that he performs at the "highest level" you could see in pro wrestling history for a Black star.
body: In a recent interview with Billboard , Strickland spoke about his career as both a professional wrestler, as well as a rapper and hip-hop artist, both professions where he continues to grow and find new successes. He told the outlet that when future generations look back on his path in wrestling, they'll see his in-ring ability took him the farthest out of anything. "Not me being a caricature of hip-hop, and not me being a caricature of a Black wrestler," Strickland said. "I'm being me. My success in pro-wrestling is genuinely because of my ability in the ring. It's not because they're trying to push an agenda, it's because I perform at a really, really high level — probably the highest level you could see of a Black wrestler in the history of the game." Strickland said there were a lot of Black talents who became "household names" in wrestling back in the day, such as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and Booker T, but you could rarely say they were the best wrestlers on their respective shows. He said that's due to who they had to compete with, like the Shawn Michaels and the Eddie Guerreros of the wrestling world. He, however, feels like he competes at the highest level with anyone in AEW. "Me and Okada. Me and Kenny [Omega]. Me and [Will] Ospreay. Me and Hangman [Adam Page]," he said. "I have to be pure and genuinely me as possible and get there because of actual ability rather than just co-signs."

He stated that future generations will recognize him for performing at the highest level of any Black wrestler in history. title: On the Record: Thekla Responds to Criticism Over Her Behavior Around Young Wrestling Fans
raw_title: Thekla Responds to Criticism Over Her Behavior Around Young Wrestling Fans
summary_src: Thekla knows her behavior around some of AEW’s youngest fans probably isn’t going to win her any role model awards, but she doesn’t seem too worried about it.
body: “I did one of my famous dumb bitch quotes. There’s this clip of me saying it on the stage, and there’s like two small children standing right next to me as I’m calling this girl a dumb bitch, and everybody cheering, and those kids just look at me.” The moment quickly took on a life of its own online, especially because of the kids’ reactions. Thekla said people kept pointing out just how funny and inappropriate the whole situation looked, which eventually led Renee Paquette to ask whether Thekla was really “for the children.” “For a long time, people pointed out how hilarious and wrong the whole situation is, and Renee [Paquette] asked me in an interview, I think, you know, jokingly, ‘Is Thekla for the children?’ And I said, ‘Hell yeah, Thekla is for the children. You know, shout out to my toxic toddlers.’ Now it’s becoming a bit.” Apparently, those two kids weren’t exactly traumatized by their encounter with Thekla either. Their father eventually reached out and revealed that both children were actually big fans of hers. That left their dad with one pretty uncomfortable vocabulary lesson to handle. Thekla joked that somebody was eventually going to teach them what the word meant anyway, so it might as well have been “Auntie Thekla.” “We have got to figure out how we explain that to the young ones. I’m sure somebody will, you know, teach them the hard way, anyway, at some point. Let it be Auntie Thekla.” What started as an unintentionally hilarious moment with two young fans has now basically become part of Thekla’s act. Instead of running away from the criticism, she’s leaned straight into it, and her “Toxic Toddlers” now have their own origin story. Some of you might think 'with your connections you can come up with a bigger name than a Young Lion,' but I'd like for you to think of this as a key step to the future of NJPW. And don't worry about Mistico. Even with his partner like this, he'll show up for the fans like Mistico always does. I have complete trust in him. So that's it. I'm off Super Jr. Tag League, and Yasuda is in. Ah, and as for (November 9 Shin Kiba 1st Ring produce event) 'Gaspe' Invitational. I can't move, but my desire to see something truly horrific trumps all that, so we'll be going ahead as planned. Show up." New Japan Pro-Wrestling joins fans in wishing Desperado a speedy, full recovery.

title: Drew McIntyre Volunteers to Become New Sin Cara After WWE Revival Report
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Volunteers to Become New Sin Cara After WWE Revival Report
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has apparently found the perfect role for his WWE comeback — Sin Cara. After reports surfaced that WWE has discussed bringing the masked character back with a new wrestler, McIntyre wasted absolutely no time throwing his 285-pound hat into the ring.
body: McIntyre reacted to the Sin Cara report on Twitter by reposting the recent video of himself pulling off a flying arm drag during training. His message was short and pretty hard to misunderstand. The joke couldn’t have been timed much better. Just one day earlier, McIntyre had surprised fans by climbing to the top rope and busting out the high-flying move while continuing to prepare for his eventual WWE return. After landing the flying arm drag, Drew jumped back to his feet and yelled “Olé!” He then joked on Instagram about suddenly adding some lucha libre to his arsenal. Now he’s putting that newfound lucha experience to good use by jokingly volunteering for WWE’s latest idea. According to PWInsider, there have been early pitches within the company to resurrect the Sin Cara character with somebody new underneath the mask. Nothing has been finalized, and there’s currently no word on who WWE might actually have in mind. The report only noted that the idea has been pitched, so McIntyre’s post appears to be him having some fun with the timing rather than any indication he’s seriously being considered for the role. “For me, I wouldn’t mind coming back. If they would ask me or we would talk, ‘Hey, you want to portray Sin Cara again?’ I would love to do that definitely again and give it another shot.” For now, WWE hasn’t even committed to bringing Sin Cara back, let alone revealed who could end up underneath the mask. McIntyre, however, has already made his pitch — and apparently one flying arm drag was all the qualification he needed. McIntyre’s response probably isn’t going to end with him showing up under the Sin Cara mask, but it does make his sudden lucha experiment a whole lot funnier. If nothing else, Drew clearly knows how to have some fun with WWE rumors while he’s preparing to get back in the ring. title: AAA Builds Weakly To Heroes Inmortales PPV
raw_title: Big Vinny V: A Viewer’s Guide to AAA Heroes Inmortales
summary_src: Nearly six weeks have passed since TripleMania 34, but it has been an uneventful six weeks in the world of AAA. They have devoted precious little time to building to Heroes Inmortales, a three-week event that begins this Saturday.
body: Nearly six weeks have passed since TripleMania 34, but it has been an uneventful six weeks in the world of AAA. They have devoted precious little time to building to Heroes Inmortales, a three-week event that begins this Saturday. We don’t even have a full card yet, but here’s a look at what we do know, and which matches are worth your time. Imagine, if you will, that after Roman Reigns defeated CM Punk at WrestleMania this year, both Reigns and Punk decided to take the next month off … which, come to think of it, is more or less what actually happened. But what if, after five weeks of mutual absence, they announced on SmackDown that Reigns and Punk would be doing a rematch a week later. Wouldn’t that be weird? Well, that’s basically what AAA is doing with El Grande Americano and Dominik Mysterio. After they met in the main event of what was theoretically AAA’s biggest show of the year, neither has appeared much on AAA television. Their only appearance: a tag team match on October 3, when Dominik Mysterio & Omos defeated Americano & Rey Mysterio. (They also competed against each other in a trios match on the WWE/AAA Worlds Collide show.) Then last week, out of nowhere, the elder Mysterio announced that his son would be getting his championship rematch this weekend, on seven days’ notice. No, this does not feel like a rematch of the biggest match of the year. In fact, it’s not even the most intriguing match of the night. That honor would go to La Catalina, who will be defending her Reina de Reinas championship on a AAA show for the first time. Her opponents will be former champion Lady Flammer and La Hiedra, who is one-half of the AAA Mixed Tag Team Champions and also Flammer’s stablemate in Las Toxicas. Hiedra spent a lot of time in Flammer’s shadow during the latter’s 1,000-plus-day championship reign. The time seems right for an outright split. Also on Saturday night, Los Perros Del Mal will defend the AAA Trios Championships against Mister Iguana & La Parka & Nino Hamburguesa. It will be a fun match with a lot of action and Los Perros will retain. BANGER ALERT! BANGER ALERT! Rey Fenix’s one-on-one defense of the AAA Cruiserweight Championship against Mini Vikingo should be stellar. The two have met twice before this year, with Fenix successfully defending his championship both times. The first was a singles match that aired in August on AAA TV; the second was a four-way (also including Jack Cartwheel and Nathan Frazer) on the second night of TripleMania in Mexico City. Our own Dave Meltzer gave the first match **** and the second *****1/4. We’re practically guaranteed to see the best match of any given week whenever these two meet. WWE is clearly high on Mini Vikingo, featuring him at Worlds Collide and on NXT, and a title change seems likely. Only one match has been announced for this evening: El Fiscal vs. Abismo Negro Jr. The build for this has been quite odd. Fiscal lost to Taurus on AAA TV last week after Negro interfered. title: On the Record: Sol Ruca Explains Why a Heel Turn Might Never Happen in WWE
raw_title: Sol Ruca Explains Why a Heel Turn Might Never Happen in WWE
summary_src: Sol Ruca has spent her WWE career showing fans her fun-loving side, but she’s definitely curious about what would happen if she went in the complete opposite direction. The NXT star admitted she’d love to experiment with being a heel, even though she’s previously been told it might never happen.
body: Speaking on The Finish , Ruca was asked whether she could eventually turn heel and evolve her character beyond the bubbly babyface fans have gotten to know. Ruca said it’s something she’d absolutely be interested in trying. “I have no idea. I think I would love to be able to try that.” The problem is that apparently some people have a hard time imagining her as the bad guy. Ruca revealed she’s previously been told she probably won’t ever turn heel because her natural personality makes it difficult to picture. “I have been told in the past that I most likely will not be heel ever because of just how I am naturally. I am quite a bubbly and, like, [likable] person.” That doesn’t mean Ruca has completely given up on showing fans a darker side. She believes it might simply take the right person or storyline to finally bring it out of her. “So, I don’t know. I feel like it’s going to take a very special person to really get that side out of me, but I guess we’re just going to have to wait and see.” Ruca didn’t hint that a heel turn is actually being planned, so fans probably shouldn’t expect her personality to suddenly change overnight. Still, she’s clearly open to getting outside her comfort zone if WWE ever gives her the chance. For someone whose personality has apparently been the biggest reason people can’t picture her as a villain, that could actually make the turn even more interesting if WWE eventually pulls the trigger. Ruca just needs to find that “special person” capable of bringing out a side fans haven’t seen before. body: TNA Wrestling has made a unique announcement for its October 13 television taping in Dothan, Alabama. In celebration of Matt & Jeff Hardy entering their 35th year in pro wrestling, TNA is hyping that the duo will have “complete control” of the Impact episode that’s being taped on October 13. The show is set to air on October 15, with The Hardys serving as on-screen matchmakers for the entire broadcast: Matt Hardy responded to the announcement by joking that he’s aiming to win Booker of the Year. This show is happening in the immediate aftermath of Bound for Glory, where Matt & Jeff are set to take on the former Joe Gacy & Dexter Lumis in a falls count anywhere match. The pay-per-view is being held in Tampa, Florida on October 11. Dothan Civic Center is hosting Impact tapings on both October 13-14. For the first night, TNA is encouraging fans to dress up like Matt or Jeff Hardy from any era of their career. There will also be special merchandise on sale to celebrate their 35th year in wrestling. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
