body: September 22, 2026 By Steph Franchomme TNA Wrestling , IMPACT , North America , Pro Wrestling AJ Francis revealed in our interview that being a heel is easier for him, mostly because he’s bigger than most of the TNA roster, and it makes him look more credible when he faces a smaller wrestler. AJ Francis is a wrestler we love to hate. At TNA Lockdown , he defeated Elijah, thanks to EXPRESSIONS. Francis would do anything to win, even if it means lying, cheating, or stealing. Since “The Phenomenal Son” Avery Styles arrived in the iMPACT Zone , he has been on Francis’ radar. He wants to be his first opponent in his first match on TNA Wrestling. Then, Moose and Frankie Kazarian are not exactly okay with that. Could the match happen live this week on TNA iMPACT or live on October 11 at TNA Bound for Glory ? In an interview with Last Word on Sports Pro Wrestling and WorldWide Wrestling , AJ Francis discussed various subjects. This includes his TNA Lockdown match against Elijah, Avery Styles, his Championship goals, his football past, his passion for music, and more. “It was awesome. It felt like history in the moment too. Once the bell rang, one, two, three, I knew that we had put on a masterpiece. Matt Rehwoldt said on commentary, when Elijah was getting in the cage, “This match is going to be a litmus test for the guys in the back for what to expect for the rest of the night.” That’s exactly what it was. It set a standard of what to be expected for the rest of the night. “I love those opportunities to go out there and perform. I say it all the time, putting me on first is dangerous. You might want to save me for later in the show because if you put me on first, it’s going to be a hell of a match to follow. When we’re on top of the cage fighting it out, it’s just one of those crazy moments. You dream of moments like that. I’ve been in cage matches on the indies plenty of times, but I’ve never been in a cage that was structurally strong enough to hold my body weight while I sit on it. “So to be able to have a moment like that from all the cage matches that I loved as a kid, it really was an awesome moment. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin From WWE to Boxing: 4 Wrestlers Who Stepped Into the Ring By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-21 10:20:00 Professional wrestling and boxing share the same basic setting: two competitors, a ring, and an audience expecting a fight. The similarities become less obvious once the action begins. WWE performers train for physically demanding, choreographed contests, while boxers must respond to opponents genuinely trying to defeat them. Strength, timing, and confidence can help in both disciplines, but success in one doesn't guarantee success in the other. Several familiar WWE personalities have tested themselves in boxing or related combat sports. Their experiences range from impressive victories to painful reminders that fighting experience matters more than reputation. John Morrison built his wrestling reputation around remarkable athleticism. His acrobatic moves, agility, and impressive physical conditioning helped distinguish him during several WWE runs. In April 2023, Morrison entered a different kind of contest when he faced Harley Morenstein at Creator Clash 2 in Tampa, Florida. The event brought together internet personalities and entertainers for competitive boxing matches. Morrison approached the fight with considerable aggression. He knocked Morenstein through the ropes during the opening round before securing a third-round technical knockout with a powerful right hand. His preparation involved more than relying on wrestling fitness. Morrison later discussed training with experienced fighters, including former UFC heavyweight Josh Barnett, and learning through demanding sparring sessions. The victory brought immediate attention. Morrison even challenged influencer boxer KSI afterward, suggesting an interest in further crossover opportunities. His debut demonstrated that athleticism can transfer successfully when accompanied by appropriate preparation. One victory, however, doesn't establish how someone would perform against an experienced professional boxer. Logan Paul's relationship with boxing began before his WWE career. His fights against fellow internet personality KSI introduced him to competitive combat sports, while a 2021 exhibition against Floyd Mayweather attracted considerable attention. Paul subsequently became a recognizable WWE performer, combining his athletic ability with a talent for attracting audiences. In October 2023, he returned to boxing against mixed martial artist Dillon Danis in Manchester, England. Their heavily publicized encounter ended in the sixth round when Danis was disqualified following illegal grappling attempts. Paul had controlled much of the contest with his jab, but the chaotic ending overshadowed his performance. Security personnel entered the ring as tensions escalated between the fighters and their teams. title: Sin Cara Revival Reportedly Being Pitched in WWE
raw_title: Sin Cara Revival Reportedly Being Pitched in WWE
body: A familiar face, or rather a masked one, might soon be making a comeback in WWE. PWInsider (via Fightful ) reports that early pitches are being made in WWE about potentially reviving Sin Cara. Additionally, PWInsider notes that if WWE moves forward with the idea, a new wrestler will take up the mantle of Sin Cara. Two different wrestlers previously competed under the moniker of Sin Cara in WWE. Luis Ignacio Urive Alvirde, aka Místico, portrayed the role of Sin Cara from 2011 to October 2013. Later, Cinta de Oro, who also wrestled in WWE as Hunico, became the second Sin Cara in WWE. He initially appeared as an impostor version of Sin Cara, Sin Cara Negro, back in 2011. However, Cinta de Oro later became the official version of Sin Cara starting in 2013. He portrayed the character until December 2019, when he was released from the promotion. The wrestler voluntarily requested to be released at the time. WWE has not yet announced a return for the wrestler. However, with WWE’s recent acquisition of Lucha Libre AAA and the surge in popularity of Mexican and luchador stars in WWE, it makes sense that the creative team would contemplate a return of the popular gimmick.

title: Eric Bischoff Makes Surprising Admission About the Real Hulk Hogan
raw_title: Eric Bischoff Makes Surprising Admission About the Real Hulk Hogan
body: During an appearance on the Planet Tyrus podcast , Bischoff discussed how the late WWE legend struggled to separate his wrestling persona from Terry Bollea, the man behind the red-and-yellow gear. For Hogan, being the Hulkster wasn't something he could simply switch off when the cameras stopped rolling. "He was in character all the time," Bischoff said, explaining that Hogan understood what fans expected whenever he stepped outside his home. Whether he was working or running errands, people wanted to meet Hulk Hogan, not Terry Bollea. "He lived it," Bischoff continued. "And, over time, I think he lost sight sometimes of who Terry was and who Hulk was." Bischoff had a front-row seat to Hogan's career, including his blockbuster WCW run and transformation into Hollywood Hogan as the leader of the New World Order. The two remained closely associated long after WCW's collapse, making Bischoff one of the people most familiar with the demands of maintaining wrestling's biggest celebrity persona. But the conversation also turned to the controversies that followed Hogan outside the ring, particularly the leaked recording in which he repeatedly used racial slurs while discussing his daughter Brooke Hogan's relationship with a Black man. The recording became public in 2015, prompting WWE to terminate its relationship with Hogan and remove references to him from its website. WWE reinstated him to the Hall of Fame in 2018. Tyrus, who is Black, defended Hogan's handling of the scandal, arguing that the wrestler eventually accepted responsibility instead of blaming others. "The difference is: he owned it," Tyrus said. "He sincerely apologized, and he owned it. And that to me was the greatest strength of any man!" Tyrus also acknowledged that Hogan had made serious mistakes, but questioned whether anyone could withstand the scrutiny that came with his level of fame. "He wasn't perfect; he didn't always say the right thing," Tyrus said. "Who the f*ck does?" Those comments come as Hogan's personal life continues to receive scrutiny more than a year after his July 2025 death at age 71. His daughter Brooke has been especially outspoken about the difference between the wrestling icon audiences admired and the father she knew. She recently revealed that their relationship fundamentally changed after Hogan had an affair with her friend Christiane Plante, saying she forgave him but never felt he treated her the same way afterward. Brooke also criticized Netflix's four-part documentary Hulk Hogan: Real American , calling it "missing 98 percent of real life" and arguing that it failed to address the family's more difficult history. Bischoff, meanwhile, believes the documentary offered audiences something they rarely got during Hogan's career: glimpses of Terry Bollea without the wrestling character. title: Contract News: 5 Things Cody Rhodes Must Do Before He Finishes His Final WWE Contract
raw_title: 5 Things Cody Rhodes Must Do Before He Finishes His Final WWE Contract
body: Rhodes has already accomplished more than most wrestlers ever do. He won the Royal Rumble in 2023 and 2024, beat Roman Reigns at WrestleMania 40 to win the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship, and has held the WWE Championship multiple times since. He is currently on SmackDown in a feud with Randy Orton, who cost him the WWE Championship match against CM Punk at SummerSlam in August. Even with all of that on his resume, there are still a few things left for him to check off before he calls it a career in WWE. Rhodes and The Rock have only wrestled against each other once, when The Rock teamed with Roman Reigns to beat Rhodes and Seth Rollins on night one of WrestleMania 40. The Rock was also involved in the Bloodline Rules match the next night, and John Cena’s heel turn in February 2025. But Rhodes has never faced him in a singles match. That is something that needs to happen in the next couple of years. Rhodes has held the WWE Championship more than once, but he has never held the World Heavyweight Championship that WWE introduced in 2023. That title is held by Roman Reigns , who is set to face Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn in a champion vs. champion match at Crown Jewel . Winning both of WWE’s top men’s titles would round out his resume, and a world title match against Reigns would bring back one of the biggest rivalries of his career. Rhodes competed in Money in the Bank ladder matches in 2010, 2011, 2012, and 2013 during his first run with WWE but never won the briefcase. Since returning to the company in 2022, he has been in the main event picture and has not needed it. A Money in the Bank win late in his career would be a different look for him. It would give him a reason to chase the title again after losing it, and the cash-in would give WWE a moment that fans would remember. Rhodes has been one of WWE’s top babyfaces since his return at WrestleMania 38 in 2022. He turned down a chance to go to the dark side at Elimination Chamber in 2025, when he refused The Rock’s offer, which led to John Cena turning heel instead. That is exactly why a heel turn would work. Rhodes has spent four years as the hero, and turning on the fans would be the biggest shock WWE could deliver with him. His heel work in Ring of Honor, in NJPW, and during his first WWE run shows he can play the role, and he showed a darker edge on the October 16 episode of SmackDown when he hit Baron Corbin with a punt kick during his feud with Randy Orton. If Rhodes does turn, he should not do it alone. Rhodes led The Nightmare Family in AEW, so he already has experience at the head of a group. Leading his own faction in WWE would give a heel run more weight and would give younger wrestlers a chance to be featured alongside one of the company’s biggest stars. A Rhodes-led group would also give him something different from the one-on-one feuds that have defined his WWE return, and it would set up battles with the established factions on both brands.

title: Fan Hospitalized After Tiger Jeet Singh Attack Says He Wishes the Cut Was Deeper
raw_title: Fan Hospitalized After Tiger Jeet Singh Attack Says He Wishes the Cut Was Deeper
summary_src: The wrestling fan who got cracked in the head by Tiger Jeet Singh’s saber apparently isn’t angry about it at all.
body: Speaking to Tokyo Sports after attending the October 21 Strong Style Pro Wrestling event at Korakuen Hall, the fan opened up about the bizarre incident for the first time. He revealed that when he saw Singh charging toward him at the October 17 show, his first reaction wasn’t exactly fear. The longtime wrestling fan admitted he doesn’t even remember the saber actually making contact with his forehead. All he remembers is suddenly feeling the impact and realizing that Tiger Jeet Singh had just nailed him. “I don’t remember being stabbed. Suddenly there was a ‘bang,’ and I thought, ‘I’ve been hit, this is awesome.’” The man, a 38-year-old office worker from Yokohama, has been watching professional wrestling since elementary school. He grew up seeing Singh and Abdullah the Butcher on television and always wanted the chance to experience them in person. “I used to watch Singh and Abdullah the Butcher on TV. I wanted to see them in person, but I never thought I’d actually be attacked.” The attack definitely looked scary in the moment. Singh was making his entrance at Megumi Kudo’s 40th anniversary show when he started swinging his trademark saber through the crowd and caught the fan directly in the forehead. The man was left bleeding and eventually taken to the hospital by ambulance. Thankfully, the injury wasn’t serious, and doctors were able to close the wound with medical staples. Apparently, that’s where the disappointment comes in. Instead of being upset about getting his head busted open, the fan wishes Singh had done enough damage to leave him with a permanent souvenir. “I wish they had cut a little deeper… I’m actually a little shocked.” He isn’t holding a grudge against Singh either. Asked about potentially seeing the wrestling legend again if Singh makes another trip to Japan, the fan made it clear he’d happily be there. That reaction is pretty wild considering what Singh himself said after the incident. Rather than apologizing, the legendary heel blamed the fan for standing in his path when he came charging through the crowd. “It was a mistake for him to be in front of me. It’s his fault. You know that, right? All he had to do was get out of my way.” Tiger Ali Singh backed up his father and pointed out that fans had been warned to be careful during the entrance. The show’s organizer, Megumi Kudo, took a different approach and apologized over what happened. The fan did get another pretty nice surprise out of the ordeal. He’s a huge supporter of Sareee, and after hearing what happened, she sent him a ticket to her December 28 show along with an autographed photo as a get-well gift. “I’m actually kind of happy about it. As long as I’m able to move, I’ll continue to support Sareee.” What initially looked like a nightmare situation apparently turned into one of this fan’s favorite wrestling memories. Dragunov did not compete at WrestleDream. He is scheduled to have his first match in the promotion on the upcoming episode of Dynamite.

title: New U.S. Embassy Security Alert Warns of Airport Threats Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
raw_title: New U.S. Embassy Security Alert Warns of Airport Threats Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
body: 0 The U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia has issued another security warning amid regional tensions and threats against airports, raising further questions about travel arrangements ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026 in Riyadh. The warning comes as WWE prepares for its annual premium live event in Saudi Arabia on November 7. The show is scheduled to take place at Riyadh Season Stadium in the King Abdullah Financial District, with WWE continuing to promote the event despite growing security concerns. The latest advisory follows reports of attacks targeting Saudi airports and warnings about possible flight cancellations, airspace closures, and travel disruptions. The situation has also prompted questions about whether WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel as planned. The October 21 advisory warned that Iran-backed Houthi forces had attacked civilian airports and other critical infrastructure, resulting in casualties and significant travel disruption. It also noted that the conflict could escalate beyond the immediate region. The alert specifically noted that operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remained suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam were operating, although delays and cancellations were reported. U.S. citizens were advised to exercise extreme caution when using airports in Saudi Arabia and check directly with airlines and airport authorities for updates. Despite the security concerns, WWE has not announced a change to Crown Jewel’s scheduled date or location. The event remains advertised for November 7 in Riyadh, with the promotion continuing its build toward the annual champion-versus-champion matches . According to PWInsider , WWE still plans to proceed with the event and has contingency plans in place, including working with a security firm experienced in the Middle East and North Africa region. llm_long: A federal judge rejected a motion to dismiss a lawsuit against WWE and TKO, Vince McMahon, and Linda McMahon. The case involves seven plaintiffs who allege they were sexually abused as minors in the 1980s and 1990s while working as ring boys for WWE.

The plaintiffs claim abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips. One plaintiff also alleges sexual abuse by former executive Pat Patterson, and another alleges sexual harassment by former Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. All three accused individuals have since passed away.

The suit accuses the McMahons and WWE of negligence for allegedly allowing the abuse to occur and continue. The case was filed under the Maryland Child Victims Act, which removes time limits for lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.

WWE, TKO, and the McMahons argued that the Maryland law violates the 14th Amendment by being unfair or arbitrary, especially given the decades-old allegations and the deaths of the accused. The judge ruled that the defendants failed to demonstrate how the law is arbitrary or irrational in this case.
With the motion to dismiss denied, the lawsuit will proceed to the discovery phase. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish additional deadlines.

title: Joe Hendry Believes He Can Become Top WWE Draw

summary_src: Joe Hendry believes he can move the needle for WWE. Hendry became a top star in TNA Wrestling in 2024-25, which led to him signing with WWE and winning the NXT Championship. He has had a consistent presence on WWE TV since joining Raw at the beginning of the year.
body: Hendry became a top star in TNA Wrestling in 2024-25, which led to him signing with WWE and winning the NXT Championship. He has had a consistent presence on WWE TV since joining Raw at the beginning of the year. Speaking to Scott Fishman of TV Insider , Hendry was asked about his hopes for his career. “I’m just always looking to get better at what I do. I know in my heart that I can be a top draw for WWE. I know people have things to say about that, but the truth is I know that I can be a top guy, I know that I can be an asset to the professional wrestling business because I have the metrics to prove it. And those are facts, you know? I had the most viewed clip in all of wrestling in 2024. I wrestled Randy Orton at WrestleMania, which did insane numbers on social media. My WrestleMania shirt was a bestseller. I won the NXT Championship. I have the metrics to prove that I can draw in the professional wrestling business, and my goal is to be somebody who can deliver for the company. I saw in an interview that [WWE President] Nick Khan was asked what WWE is looking for from talent. It is someone that can move the needle for the company immediately or in the near future. I believe that I’m somebody who can do that. I’ve had metrics in the past to prove that I think I can be a top guy for WWE. So I’m looking to acquire the skills to do that as quickly as I can,” he said. Hendry has been making fun of JD McDonagh by using a Funko Pop on recent episodes of Raw. He stars in the company’s first-ever microdrama Agent of Shadows , which premieres on October 23.

body: The report did not say when Mysterio plans to retire , but backstage chatter indicates that the former WWE Champion will be calling it an in-ring career next year. Mysterio, the current AAA general manager, is expected to remain with the company in an executive position, while also developing the next generation of WWE stars. While Rey Mysterio is contemplating retirement, his lineage is at the genesis of their budding careers . Mysterios’ son, Dominik, is a former Intercontinental Champion and AAA Mega Champion. His daughter Aalyah has also reported to the WWE Performance Center for training. Dominik Mysterio isn’t satisfied with just being a second-generation star, however, and previously stated that he wants to retire his legendary father. During an appearance on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dirty Dom called it his “birthright” to retire his father, Rey Mysterio. “I’ve been talking about it. I’ve been wanting him to retire. I want him out of here, you know?” he began. “ There’s only room for so many Mysterios in WWE . “There’s one pushing 60, and I think it’s time for him to kick rocks; that’s just how I see it.” “It’s my birthright. I would lose my absolute s**t if it’s not me,” Dominik said of his father’s last match. “I’ve got to take his mask, and I’ve got to take his name.” WWE has not confirmed which city will host Rey Mysterio’s last match, but Dominik Mysterio has the perfect venue in mind. “Auditorio Fausto Gutierrez Moreno, super historical arena down in Tijuana, Mexico,” Dominik said. “I believe my dad has wrestled there, debuted there. My great-uncle and most of my godfathers wrestled there [too].” Regardless of when Rey Mysterio retires, his imprint on pro wrestling will never be forgotten. Mysterio began his career in 1989, beginning on the independent scene. He signed with WCW in 1996, becoming a heralded cruiserweight star and helping popularize lucha libre in America. Mysterio joined WWE in 2002 and boasts one of the most impressive resumes in the promotion’s history. Mysterio, 51, is a former Royal Rumble winner and one of the most revered high-flyers. During his storied career, Mysterio captured the WWE Championship, World Heavyweight Championship, Tag Team Championships and the Cruiserweight Championship. title: Nic Nemeth Wants Final Run Like Peers
raw_title: TNA's Nic Nemeth Ponders Final Run For Him And Other Wrestlers Of His Generation
summary_src: TNA star Nic Nemeth ponders what the road to retirement might look like for himself and other wrestlers of his generation.
body: Last year, John Cena officially retired from in-ring competition. Next year, Adam "Edge" Copeland will do the same. Their former colleague Nic Nemeth, meanwhile, is showing no signs of slowing down. That hasn't stopped him from pondering what his own future road to retirement might look like, though. "I would like to do a cool thing," Nemeth said on "Busted Open Radio." "I would like to do my last show in LA, my last show in Cleveland, my last time fighting for a title, all these different things and go, 'This is my last one.' We'd all like to have a last year run. I don't know how that works. I know it can work out for some people, and a lot of people in our business don't get to call those shots. But when you do and you mean something, hopefully we see more and more of those, because I know we like it." Nemeth, a former collegiate wrestler, kicked off his professional wrestling career under the WWE banner in 2004. At the time, Cena and Copeland were steadily building themselves as major singles stars on WWE's main roster. Other names such as The Miz, Mickie James, and Nemeth himself were working their way up WWE's developmental system. Eventually, Nemeth hopes that all the in-ring performers of his generation, now veterans to the business, receive a moment of recognition before making their own farewells. In his case, "The Showoff" appears to be further away from his. "I love when someone who's done so much, or someone that I've been in the ring with, to get everybody giving them their moment, and enjoy what they did and the sacrifices they made," Nemeth said. "I love that stuff." Nemeth is currently signed to TNA, where he reigns as one-half of the TNA World Tag Team Champions. He lost the TNA World Championship to Leon Slater at Bound For Glory on October 11.

title: Allie & Kiera Hogan Retain Knockouts Tag Title In TNA Impact Open Challenge
raw_title: Allie & Kiera Hogan Retain Knockouts Tag Title In TNA Impact Open Challenge
body: On Thursday's episode of "TNA Impact" in Brampton , Allie and Hogan laid out an open challenge for their titles. Indie standouts Shazza McKenzie and Vipress answered the call and put up a decent fight. McKenzie and Allie kicked off the action with a lock-up, which the former used as leverage to corner the latter against the ropes. When McKenzie sought to follow-up with a chop, Allie dodged it and fired off right hands instead. The Canada native followed with a Thesz Press before whipping her tag team partner into McKenzie in the opposite corner. Hogan continued the attack with a sliding kick and a hip attack. McKenzie found a brief moment of reprieve when Vipress tagged in and nailed Hogan with a back elbow and dropkick. McKenzie herself then fired off stomps on Hogan in the corner. Hogan escaped the headlock that followed and rocked McKenzie with a thrust kick. Allie and Vipress returned as the legal competitions shortly after, with the former delivering a drive-by knee. Hogan tossed McKenzie out of the ring, leaving Vipress alone in the ring to eat Allie's codebreaker and Hogan's Face The Music. Allie then pinned Vipress for the win. Allie originally captured the KO Tag Team Titles alongside Rosemary at Slammiversary. A recent injury, however, has kept Rosemary sidelined and unable to defend the titles, hence Allie's new alliance with Hogan. Hogan, an already two-time Knockouts Tag Team Champion in her own right, returned to help Allie at TNA Lockdown , with the two going on to best The Elegance Brand's Heather and M by Elegance in a steel cage to retain the titles. The exact timetable for Rosemary's own return is unknown, though she is reportedly set to miss a "significant amount of time" due to her injury.
summary: Allie and Hogan laid out an open challenge for their titles. Hogan, an already two-time Knockouts Tag Team Champion in her own right, made a comeback to help Allie at TNA Lockdown .

title: On the Record: Nic Nemeth Responds to Dave Meltzer's 'Gossipy' Take on WWE Relationship Hurting TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Nic Nemeth Responds to Dave Meltzer's 'Gossipy' Take on WWE Relationship Hurting TNA Wrestling
body: While Vince McMahon was the greatest promoter in wrestling history, there were many things about his business practices that frustrated fans. One of the most prominent was his unwillingness to work with other promotions for much of his nearly 40 years in the business. However, with him out of the picture, the current regime led by Nick Khan and Triple H is open to doing business with competitors. The most notable example of this change in strategy is their ongoing working relationship with TNA, which became official early last year. At first, it seemed like a very good thing for TNA. Via a talent exchange, TNA was able to get its wrestlers on WWE’s highly viewed shows, and WWE stars (mostly from NXT) appeared on episodes of Impact. Several NXT stars even won TNA championships, including Trick Williams , who had a lengthy reign with the brand’s top title. However, some viewers of the sport feel there has been an imbalance that benefits WWE. “ It’s a bad situation ,” Wrestling Observer’s Dave Meltzer claimed this month. “This always happens when you work with WWE historically. The fanbase sees the WWE guys as superior because they are booked as superior, and then when it ends, you have to draw with your inferior guys. TNA’s ticket sales are way down now. It looks like most saw this going in. “That WWE worked with TNA as a way to hurt AEW, the key being to send talent so TNA has better leverage for a TV deal. In that sense, the deal did short-term work out great for TNA, but now they have to struggle with the post-deal period.” In an exclusive conversation with Casino.org , current TNA Champion Nic Nemeth was asked whether he agrees with Meltzer’s take on the WWE-TNA relationship issues. Well, the multi-time WWE titleist doesn’t buy the reporter’s “gossipy” views on the situation. “Meltzer’s kind of story that he’s concocted about this, I don’t really want to get into that, but I think it’s been fruitful for both of us,” the man once known as Dolph Ziggler in WWE said. “It’s really helped us long-term, especially having that name with us. I think physically, I think we lost the battle more than we won the battle when it came to wins and losses with NXT and TNA guys and girls coming back and forth. “It really helped us get that AMC deal and get on a great channel. And they’ve been such incredible partners. I get fired up. I’m watching like Caddyshack or Christmas Vacation with my parents on AMC, and there’s a commercial every time I’m watching; it’s the Hardys, it’s me, it’s TNA. And I’m like, ‘This is incredible!'” he added. “What a great partner that we have. So I can’t really speak for a guy who’s using gossipy kind of algorithms to put something together.” “As someone who’s been behind the scenes for both places. I think it has really, really worked out for us,” Nemeth said.

title: AEW wrestler 'PAC,' Benjamin Satterley, dead at 40
raw_title: AEW wrestler 'PAC,' Benjamin Satterley, dead at 40
body: The death is sudden, as he wrestled at AEW's All Out pay-per-view on Saturday night in the greater Chicago area. Satterley challenged Andrade for the AEW National Championship in the evening's opening pay-per-view match, losing the title tilt before later reappearing during the show's main event between Will Ospreay and Jon Moxley. All Elite Wrestling is saddened to announce the passing of Benjamin Satterley, aka Pac. A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability. Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. Our condolences go out to Satterley's family, friends and fans. Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp reported Monday that Satterley was found dead in a rental car at approximately 4 p.m. ET Sunday afternoon, and that Illinois' Cook County medical examiner's office has ruled out any indications of foul play or trauma. Debuting as a professional wrestler in his native England in 2004, Satterley quickly established himself as one of the most acclaimed high-flying workers of his generation. He competed extensively on the British independent scene before wrestling around the world for promotions including Pro Wrestling Guerrilla, Ring of Honor, New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Dragongate. Satterley's breakout into the sport's mainstream began when he signed with WWE in 2012, performing under the ring name "Neville." Nicknamed "The Man That Gravity Forgot" because of his spectacular aerial offense, Satterley became one of the standout performers of WWE's developmental brand, NXT, before moving to the company's main roster in 2015. During his six years with WWE, Satterley became a two-time WWE Cruiserweight Champion, one-time NXT Champion and two-time NXT Tag Team Champion. After parting ways with the WWE in 2018, Satterley returned to the independent scene and captured another title with Japan's Dragongate before becoming one of AEW's earliest major signings in 2019, performing under the ring name "PAC." Satterley remained with AEW for the next seven years, competing both as a singles wrestler and, more often, as part of several prominent factions. He formed the Death Triangle in 2020 alongside Penta and Rey Fenix before joining Jon Moxley's Death Riders in 2024. During his time in AEW, Satterley became the promotion's inaugural All-Atlantic Champion in 2022 and twice captured its World Trios Championship. His first trios title reign also made him the first wrestler in AEW history to hold two championships simultaneously. Satterley remained an active member of AEW's roster through the final days of his life. In the week before All Out, he defeated Adam Priest and Ace Austin in televised AEW matches. body: TNA Wrestling has officially announced the signing of former WWE Superstar Shayna Baszler, confirming that the accomplished professional wrestler and mixed martial artist has joined the company’s roster. The signing was first reported by Denise Salcedo of Instinct Culture before TNA confirmed the news in an official press release. Baszler has already made an immediate impact in the promotion, capturing championship gold during her TNA debut at Bound For Glory on October 11, 2026. Teaming with Zoey Serrano under the name The Apex, Baszler defeated the competition to become one-half of the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions. The championship victory marked a successful beginning to Baszler’s TNA career, with the former WWE star securing a title in her first appearance for the promotion. Baszler brings extensive experience to TNA, having established herself as a multi-time champion in both singles and tag team competition throughout her professional wrestling career. Before becoming a prominent figure in professional wrestling, Baszler also enjoyed a lengthy career in mixed martial arts. Her MMA record includes 15 victories, with 13 of those wins coming by submission, highlighting the grappling background that has become a defining element of her in-ring style. Baszler made her professional wrestling debut in 2015 before going on to establish herself as one of the industry’s most recognizable submission specialists. With her TNA contract now officially confirmed, Baszler enters the promotion as an active champion alongside Serrano, positioning The Apex as an established force in the Knockouts tag team division. TNA has not disclosed the length or financial terms of Baszler’s contract. BREAKING: TNA Wrestling has signed @QoSBaszler, as first reported by Instinct Culture’s @_denisesalcedo.

title: Indi Hartwell Retains Knockouts Title On TNA Impact
raw_title: Indi Hartwell Retains KO Title Against Former Champ Xia Brookside On TNA Impact
summary_src: Indi Hartwell retained the Knockouts World Championship in a rematch against Xia Brookside during "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Indi Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside in an impromptu match for her Knockouts World Championship during "TNA Impact." Hartwell defeated Brookside for the title at Bound For Glory earlier this month. She came out during Thursday's show to interrupt Daria Rae in her return and subsequent promo, prompting Rae to book the rematch immediately despite Hartwell not being in ring gear. Brookside then made her entrance to get the match underway, taking advantage relatively quickly by attacking the left arm on the outside of the ring. She brought the action back inside the ring, further targeting the arm on the mat but unable to put the match away. Hartwell fought her way back into the bout and sought for a Full Nelson slam, but due to the damage done to her arm she couldn't complete it. That allowed Brookside to take advantage and go right back to the arm. Brookside looked for the Darkside DDT but Hartwell slipped out from her grasp, connecting with a big boot and the slam for the winning pinfall. After the match, Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler entered the ring to ambush Hartwell. Baszler choked the Knockouts World Champion out before posing with her belt, as Rae watched on from the entrance ramp with amusement on her face.
summary: Indi Hartwell defended her TNA Knockouts World Championship against Xia Brookside in an impromptu match on Thursday's episode of TNA Impact. Brookside targeted Hartwell's left arm throughout the bout after interrupting Daria Rae's return promo, which led to the immediate title match. Hartwell overcame the damage to hit a big boot and Full Nelson slam for the pinfall victory.

Brookside entered and quickly targeted Hartwell's left arm on the outside of the ring. She continued working over the arm inside the ring but could not secure a pinfall.
Hartwell mounted a comeback and attempted a Full Nelson slam. The damage to her arm prevented her from executing the move, allowing Brookside to resume attacking the injured limb.

Brookside went for her Darkside DDT, but Hartwell escaped and hit a big boot followed by a slam to score the winning pinfall. After the match, Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler ambushed Hartwell in the ring.
Baszler choked out the champion and posed with the Knockouts World Championship belt. Rae observed the scene from the entrance ramp with visible amusement.

body: Ospreay enters AEW All Out for his first world title defense after completing his decade-long chase with a scintillating win over Kenny Omega at All In London last month . Ospreay defeated Omega at Wembley Stadium to capture the AEW World Championship, then personally sought out Moxley as the first challenger of his reign. Moxley, a four-time AEW World Champion and the current AEW Continental Champion, is the last wrestler to pin Ospreay and he featured heavily in Ospreay's run to the belt. Notably, Saturday pits AEW and WWE head-to-head on the same night in the Chicago market , as WWE and AAA hold Worlds Collide at Allstate Arena in nearby Rosemont. Uncrowned will carry live coverage of both events. AEW All Out takes place this Saturday, Sept. 26, at NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois, in the Chicago metropolitan area. The inaugural AEW All Out event took place at the same venue — then known as the Sears Centre Arena — in 2019, and this year's show marks the fifth time in eight years that All Out takes over the building. Saturday's pay-per-view card begins at 8 p.m. ET, while the pre-show begins at 7 p.m. ET. AEW All Out 2026 is available to watch live on pay-per-view in the United States through HBO Max, YouTube, Amazon Prime, PPV.com and Sling. It can be seen internationally through Amazon Prime, PPV.com and MyAEW. With AEW Women's World Champion Mercedes Moné still healing from the broken nose she suffered during her title-winning match at All In, former champions Willow Nightingale and Thekla are instead slated to meet in a high-stakes title eliminator to determine who challenges Moné at AEW WrestleDream on Oct. 17. All Out also features an almost-assuredly bonkers three-way ladder match for the AEW World Tag Team Championship, as Christian Cage and Adam Copeland defend against FTR and The Young Bucks. Five additional title matches are set for the card as well. llm_long: A federal judge rejected a motion to dismiss a lawsuit against WWE and TKO, Vince McMahon, and Linda McMahon. The case involves seven plaintiffs who allege they were sexually abused as minors in the 1980s and 1990s while working as ring boys for WWE.

The plaintiffs claim abuse by former WWE ring announcer Mel Phillips. One plaintiff also alleges sexual abuse by former executive Pat Patterson, and another alleges sexual harassment by former Vice President of Operations Terry Garvin. All three accused individuals have since passed away.

The suit accuses the McMahons and WWE of negligence for allegedly allowing the abuse to occur and continue. The case was filed under the Maryland Child Victims Act, which removes time limits for lawsuits related to child sexual abuse.

WWE, TKO, and the McMahons argued that the Maryland law violates the 14th Amendment by being unfair or arbitrary, especially given the decades-old allegations and the deaths of the accused. The judge ruled that the defendants failed to demonstrate how the law is arbitrary or irrational in this case.
With the motion to dismiss denied, the lawsuit will proceed to the discovery phase. A teleconference is scheduled for November 17 to establish additional deadlines.

body: El Desperado is out of NJPW's Super Jr. Tag League after a diagnosis of spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda replaces him as Mistico's partner. Copy link Get more Wrestling News in Google Choose us as a and our stories show up more in your Google results. El Desperado is out of NJPW’s Super Jr. Tag League, which begins Saturday, October 24, in Kumagaya, Saitama. NJPW announced that he has been diagnosed with spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda will replace him as Mistico’s partner, a choice Desperado made himself. In a video released on YouTube, Desperado said: “My left leg has no strength, and with the pain and pins and needles I’m currently unable to stand, walk or even sit upright for long periods of time.” He said he first noticed symptoms at the start of the year and that the pain began around June. He kept wrestling on painkillers. “I said I could still wrestle, but I was taking the issue far too lightly. My body had reached its limits,” he said. On choosing Yasuda, Desperado said: “I want to give Yasuda this opportunity to team alongside a global megastar like Mistico, and to see what he can make of this spot.” Desperado and Mistico had entered the A Block as a debut team. The A Block also includes Unbound Co. (Taiji Ishimori and Robbie X), HOUSE OF TORTURE (DOUKI and Yoshinobu Kanemaru), Ryusuke Taguchi and Kazuma Sumi, and Master Wato and KUUKAI. The A and B Block winners meet in the final at Power Struggle on November 3 at Hiroshima Sun Plaza Hall . body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. In a new interview with Chris Van Vliet , WWE star Cody Rhodes was asked again about his timeline and plan for retiring from WWE. First, here is what the 41-year-old Rhodes said after being reminded that he once said he would retire at 40 years old. “Yeah I did [say that], didn’t I? Told you an old Cody lie, huh?” The American Nightmare talked about the final WWE contract that he recently signed, and guessed that he has six or seven years left in the ring. He certainly won’t be falling on the ground for a living by the time he reaches 50 years old. “I just signed my last contract. I say last contract - that’s gonna go for a while…my time with WWE could go, just to give you a real answer here and not politic around you, probably seven? Seven years? Six, seven? …I definitely don’t want to wrestle into my fifties. No shame to anyone who wrestles into their fifties. I don’t want to overstay my welcome.” Rhodes is grateful that he was able to play Guile in the Street Fighter movie, which is a video game series that he loved to play growing up. Cody talked about how you have to “stop taking” at some point, but it doesn’t like he plans to do that anytime soon. “I have shed so much of my skin for the industry. But I have also been given so, so, so much. I think there’s a point where you have to stop taking. I’m not there, but there’s a point. And I think that’s in that time frame. A point where you just have to stop taking. …I don’t know how many moments like this I can take, and I can get. Hopefully more. Hopefully a lot more. But I’ve been so lucky so far, and so blessed so far.” Rhodes briefly admitted that ‘Cody fatigue’ is a real thing in WWE, before quickly backtracking, and then landing somewhere in the middle. “I mean, Cody fatigue is already pretty set in…Well, no. title: Chris Jericho Set to Play Real-Life Pro Wrestling Legend in Prime Video Series
raw_title: Chris Jericho Set to Play Real-Life Pro Wrestling Legend in Prime Video Series
body: By Jeremy Dick Published Oct 22, 2026, 9:58 PM EDT Jeremy has been a freelance writer and editor since 2014, having contributed to a variety of entertainment websites. He is a self-professed expert on all things pop culture and Bob Saget's biggest fan. Dislikes include onions, heights, and talking about himself in the third person. Sign in to your CBR account New casting information has been revealed for The Greatest , the upcoming miniseries coming to Prime Video in November. It primarily focuses on the rise of boxing legend Muhammad Ali, but it will also feature an appearance from legendary pro wrestling pioneer Gorgeous George. Deadline reports that Chris Jericho plays Gorgeous George in The Greatest . He will first appear in the fourth episode of the eight-episode series, which is set to premiere on Nov. 4 . The real-life Gorgeous George is known for revolutionizing pro wrestling, much in the way Ali did for boxing. He became famous in the 1940s and 1950s, standing out with his flamboyant appearance and arrogant persona. The wrestler, whose real name was George Raymond Wagner, played himself in the 1949 film Alias the Champ . More recently, Adam Demos played Gorgeous George in the 2025 drama Queen of the Ring . In the world of pro wrestling, he inspired countless legends to follow in the decades after his run. That includes names like Ric Flair, Hulk Hogan, and "Superstar" Billy Graham. title: Cedric Alexander Wins X-Division Number One Contender Match
raw_title: Cedric Alexander Becomes Number-One Contender For X-Division Title On TNA Impact
summary_src: After winning Thursday's four-way number one contenders match, Cedric Alexander will face Amazing Red for the X-Division Championship next week on "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Cedric Alexander is one step closer towards reclaiming his lost X-Division Championship after winning a four-way number one contender's match on Thursday's episode of "TNA Impact." He will have the opportunity to face TNA Hall of Famer Amazing Red for his title on next week's show. As most X-Division style matches tend to be, the beginning of it started off lightning fast, as Alexander rocked KC Navarro, Rich Swann, and Fabian Aichner before the commercial break. Coming back from the break, Alexander and Swann joined a temporary alliance with a Doomsday Device on Navarro. Aichner stormed in with a neat moonsault. On the ring apron, Alexander connected an STO on Swann. In a sequence, Navarro, then Aichner (crossbody), flew off the ropes and onto Swann and Alexander on the outside. However, The System's Brian Myers and Bear Bronson came in with a Roster Cut and Side Walk Slam on Aichner, respectively, opening the opportunity for Alexander to connect a moonsault on Aichner for the pinfall victory. Alexander first won the X-Division Championship against the former two-time champion, Leon Slater, in a two-out-of-three falls match on the May 14 edition of "Impact." He'd go on to carry the title for 101 days, dropping it back to Slater at Lockdown this past August. After getting inducted into this year's Hall of Fame at Bound for Glory, Red would go on to secure the title for the fourth time in his career later on in the show in a seven-way scramble match. Next Thursday will mark his first title defense.
summary: Cedric Alexander defeated KC Navarro, Rich Swann and Fabian Aichner in a four-way match on TNA Impact to become the number one contender for the X-Division Championship. He will challenge Amazing Red for the title on next week's episode. The fast-paced bout featured several high-flying spots before Alexander secured the pinfall on Aichner following interference from Brian Myers and Bear Bronson.

Fabian Aichner landed a moonsault during the bout. Alexander delivered an STO to Swann on the ring apron while Navarro and Aichner executed dives from the ropes onto Swann and Alexander on the floor.
Brian Myers and Bear Bronson interfered by hitting a Roster Cut and Sidewalk Slam on Aichner. This allowed Alexander to connect with a moonsault on Aichner to secure the pinfall victory.

title: Shotzi Blackheart Officially Joins TNA Knockouts
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart Officially Debuts On TNA Impact
summary_src: On Thursday night's episode of "TNA Impact," Shotzi Blackheart made her first appearance as an official Knockout.
body: Earlier this week, TNA confirmed Shotzi Blackheart , a former WWE NXT Women's Tag Team Champion, as the newest member of its Knockouts division. Tonight on "TNA Impact," she then made her official first moves. Coming off their loss at Bound For Glory, the now-former Knockouts Tag Team Champions Allie and Kiera Hogan headed to the ring to address their futures in the company. Allie voiced her wish for a title rematch against Apex. Hogan, however, had no interest in doing so, declaring Allie as the "weakest link" of their team. Cue the arrival of Tasha Steelz, who charged down to attack Allie with Hogan's help. The pair laid in a series of stomps, a leg drop, and a splash, leaving Allie on the receiving end of a two-on-one Fire N' Flava reunion. That changed when Blackheart ran down herself to even the odds. Hogan and Steelz eventually retreated as Allie celebrated her newfound ally. "The Ballsy Badass" has previous experience in TNA, having wrestled for the promotion in 2018 and 2019. Thursday night's appearance marks her first as an official roster member, though. Interestingly, Blackheart's first two in-ring outings in TNA both involved Allie. The first pitted her and Tessa Blanchard against Allie and Hogan. The second saw Blackheart and Allie collide in singles competition. Blackheart departed from WWE in mid-2025 and subsequently signed with MLW, where she went on to the capture the company's women's division title. Due to taping delays, she still reigns as the MLW Women's Featherweight Champion on MLW programming.

title: Shayna Baszler Recalls Ronda Rousey Fighting For WWE Women's Time
raw_title: Shayna Baszler reveals how Ronda Rousey fought for WWE women’s division backstage
summary_src: Shayna Baszler recently dismissed the rumors that Ronda Rousey did not care about wrestling and instead revealed how she fought for the women’s division in WWE.
body: Shayna Baszler recently dismissed the rumors that Ronda Rousey did not care about wrestling and instead revealed how she fought for the women’s division in WWE. In a recent interview with Denice Salcedo, Baszler opened up about how Rousey helped the women’s division flourish in WWE and fought for it. “I’ve heard people be like, ‘Ronda didn’t really care about wrestling.’ She might hate me for telling this story, but there was a time where Ronda had a pay-per-view match and got six minutes cut off of her match because a match before had gone over their time. “And to take six minutes from a match is huge. To take one minute from a match, in order to build a story and get emotion involved, it takes time. “ When that happened, she bought her own ticket and flew herself to headquarters to have a meeting with creative at that time to be like, ‘Guys, this keeps happening. The women keep losing time. I need to know right now, is this going to change? Because if it’s not, I don’t need to be here. I don’t need to be here to make money. I don’t need to be here to get famous ,” Baszler recalled. “ I’m here to help advance this. And if you’re telling me right now that’s never going to happen, then I’m done. I only want to improve this.’ “ She’s not going to tell you that story. She’s not going to tweet about it. She’s not going to go on a thing and talk about it. Nobody’s going to know about the stuff she did like that behind the scenes on her own dime just to argue for the women’s locker room. I don’t even think girls in the locker room knew she did that.” She further revealed how she had a conversation with Rousey about this, and how Rousey had found a hack about making sure their meeting doesn’t get canceled. “I remember her telling me that and I’m like, ‘Why did you buy your own ticket? They would have flown you there to have a meeting.’ “And she’s like, ‘No, because if I buy my own ticket, they can’t cancel the meeting on me because I bought my ticket. So I’m going to make sure.’ It was just the little stuff like that that she thought about. You knew she was serious.” While Shayna Baszler is now a part of TNA Wrestling , Rousey last appeared in AEW before fighting her career’s retirement MMA match against Gina Carano. title: Chris Jericho Cast as Gorgeous George in Muhammad Ali Series
raw_title: Chris Jericho to play Gorgeous George in upcoming Muhammad Ali series
summary_src: Current AEW star Chris Jericho will be appearing on the small screen in an acting role once again, playing a role he is familiar with and of someone many wrestling fans are familiar with as well.
body: Current AEW star Chris Jericho will be appearing on the small screen in an acting role once again, playing a role he is familiar with and of someone many wrestling fans are familiar with as well. Announced by Deadline on Thursday , Jericho will play the legendary Gorgeous George in the upcoming Prime Video series chronicling the life of boxer and mainstream icon Muhammad Ali. The full eight episode series comes out on Wednesday, November 4 with Jericho’s appearance coming in episode four. The two men met in 1961 with Ali taking inspiration from the wrestling star on how to rile up crowds and a style of reciting poems and phrases that caught on in pop culture. “The Greatest features defining moments in Ali’s life and career, both in and out of the ring, that have been well documented, and moments that took place outside the spotlight. The world remembers an icon, but The Greatest is about a man, a husband, a father, a brother and a son.” Jericho has made several appearances on TV outside the wrestling ring this year as he appeared in CBS’ Tracker and Apple TV’s Margo’s Got Money Troubles. title: Jason Hotch Retains TNA International Title
raw_title: Jason Hotch Earns Decisive Win Over Mustafa Ali On TNA Impact
summary_src: Jason Hotch beat Mustafa Ali to retain the International Championship in the main event of "TNA Impact."
body: TNA Jason Hotch defeated Mustafa Ali in a Two Out of Three Falls match to retain the International Championship in the main event of "TNA Impact." Ali went on to score the first fall with a roll-up. He sought to press that advantage but Hotch came back at him to send him to the outside once more, following up with a tope. He brought Ali back into the ring and went to the top rope for a double stomp, but Ali rolled out of the ring again. Hotch gave chase and delivered a moonsault to take him out on the floor, smashing his face against the apron repeatedly. Ali crawled toward the International title belt, followed again by Hotch to prompt the challenger to turn around and strike him with the belt. That caused a disqualification to provide Hotch the equalizing fall. Ali brought Hotch back into the ring and went for the cover for the win, but Hotch kicked out. Ali tried twice more to no avail and began to argue the count with the referee. Hotch ran back at Ali but got sent into the referee instead, allowing Ali to deliver a low-blow before ripping off Hotch's belt and beating him with it. Hotch still managed to fight back into the contest, beating Ali back with the belt before returning to the ring and eventually hitting a GTH for the winning pinfall. Hotch emerged victorious in the Order Four four-way for the title at Bound For Glory, pinning Ali to begin his second reign as International Champion. He had previously held the title after dethroning Ali in June, only to lose it back to him at Lockdown in August. They held two wins apiece in singles action between TNA and Warrior Wrestling prior to Thursday's Two Out of Three Falls match.
summary: Jason Hotch defeated Mustafa Ali in a two-out-of-three-falls match on TNA Impact to keep the International Championship. Ali scored the first fall by roll-up before Hotch evened it via disqualification after Ali used the title belt as a weapon. The bout ended in chaos with Ali delivering a low blow and striking Hotch with his own belt.

title: WWE NXT Ratings Drop Against NBA Opener

body: The return of the NBA made WWE NXT take a ratings hit this week. This past Tuesday’s show averaged 655,000 viewers on The CW, down 10.5% from the previous week’s 732,000 and their third-lowest audience since August 25. The episode also averaged a 0.10 rating in the 18-49 demo, down 28.6% from last week. The show went head-to-head with the opening night of the NBA regular season as well as NHL games on various cable networks and streaming services. Featured matches included Cruz Montana vs. Dion Lennox, Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic matches, and a show-opening confrontation between Tony D’Angelo and NXT Champion Grayson Waller. As compared to the same week in 2025, overall viewership was up 24.8% with similar competition while the 18-49 rating was up 42.9%. It’s the second straight week the show has been up year-over-year in both categories. Listed below are the last 11 weeks of overall viewership and 18-49 demo ratings for WWE NXT on The CW as well as the 10-week average in both categories. This week’s show was down 1.3% in overall viewers and 16.7% in 18-49 as compared to recent averages. title: Earlier Start Time Set For Final WWE Raw Before Crown Jewel
raw_title: Earlier Start Time Set For Final WWE Raw Before Crown Jewel
body: The first WWE Raw episode of November will take place a little earlier than usual as the company makes plans for Crown Jewel. WrestleVotes Radio On Fightful Select reports that the November 2nd episode of WWE Raw is currently set to air live starting at 6 PM ET/3 PM PT instead of the usual 8 PM ET/5 PM PT. According to the report, the plan is to air Raw live at the earlier time from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn so that they can tape WWE Smackdown on the same night. The episodes will be the final shows before Crown Jewel, and the company is filming the shows on the adjusted schedule to accomodate travel to Saudi Arabia for WWE Crown Jewel. As noted , that week’s WWE TV schedule also has another change in place as WWE NXT will take place on Wednesday, November 4th instead of Tuesday, November 3rd so that it doesn’t go up against election night coverage. That means that NXT will be going head-to-head against the Blood & Guts episode of AEW Dynamite. WWE Crown Jewel is set to take place on November 7th and, as has been noted, is still scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia despite the US State Department currently at a level three warning about travel to the region.

body: TNA Wrestling Tonight's "TNA Impact" brought us a surprise title rematch, an expected title rematch, and Avery Styles' first one-on-one match. Was the show a success? That depends on who you ask, but as always, you can count on Wrestling Inc. to deliver your weekly dose of the good and the bad. If I were Cedric Alexander, I would have invoked my contractual rematch for the TNA X-Division Championship tonight, or even next week. Instead, the ex-titleholder jumped through two matches in which the numbers put him at a great disadvantage. Alexander received his contractual rematch at Bound For Glory, where he and six others competed in a chaotic scramble for the X-Division Title. Unlike Scott Steiner, I know that meant Alexander's odds of winning back the championship were one in seven, or 14%. Had he waited until after BFG (in storyline), however, he could have elevated that number to 50% through a one-on-one against Amazing Red. Alas, that didn't happen, as the seven-way scramble ultimately panned out in Red's favor, making him the new X-Division Champion. On this week's "Impact," Alexander sought to secure another rematch by wrestling in a four-way number one contender's match, which meant his odds increased to 25%. Still not great, though, and like BFG, he didn't have to be pinned or submitted to lose. The System member won in this case to earn himself a one-on-one title shot against Red next week. It should be a solid in-ring performance, too. I can't say that Alexander, a heel, took the most practical or realistic approach to get there, though. TNA Wrestling Shayna Baszler has been a longtime favorite wrestler of mine, and I would be lying if I said I hadn't gotten used to seeing her not being utilized in WWE during her time in the company. With that in mind, it's a really nice change of pace to see TNA using her to her fullest potential by sending her right to the top of the Knockouts Division. I know that Hartwell has just begun her reign as Knockouts World Champion, but she's already had enough singles and tag team matches with Brookside and her feud with Daria Rae is already growing old for me. The Knockouts World Championship picture has largely also been featuring the same players week after week, so it's a nice change of pace to have some fresh blood be infused into it to bring it back to life a little bit. If anyone in the Knockouts Division were to be a double champion (whether it actually comes to fruition or is just an idea to plant into minds of the TNA fans), Baszler would be the perfect pick. Her style makes her feel like a threat to anyone on the TNA roster. Whenever TNA decides to hold the match, Baszler and Hartwell should put on a banger of a match with one another and it will be something that I'm looking forward to seeing. TNA Wrestling It might be unfair to judge Avery Styles with less than 20 matches on his resume, especially against his father AJ Styles, legitimately one of the best wrestlers of all time. It would be fair

summary_src: Several new matches were announced for next month’s TNA Destination X including a pair of Ultimate X bouts. Announced by Santino Marella on Thursday’s Impact, there will be a pair of Ultimate X matches involving both the women and the men.
body: Several new matches were announced for next month’s TNA Destination X including a pair of Ultimate X bouts. Announced by Santino Marella on Thursday’s Impact , there will be a pair of Ultimate X matches involving both the women and the men. On the women’s side, the winner will earn a future shot at the Knockouts title while on the men’s side, the winner earns an X-Division title match. Participants were not announced for either bout. The streaming special will also feature the return of the World X Cup for the first time since 2008. The Cup features a mini-tournament of sorts with two four-way matches featuring international wrestlers where the respective winners advance to match to determine the World X Champion. No participants were announced. The new additions join the previously announced TNA World title match between Leon Slater and Trey Miguel. llm_long: TNA Wrestling will hold its 2026 Destination X event on November 15 at the Edmonton EXPO Centre in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada.
During the October 22 episode of Thursday Night iMPACT, the promotion announced that two Ultimate X matches will take place at the show.

One Ultimate X match will be for men and the other for women. The men's winner will earn a future shot at the X Division Championship, while the women's winner will receive a future shot at the Knockouts World Championship.
The World X-Cup tournament is also returning for Destination X and will include wrestlers from around the globe.
The tournament format consists of two Fatal 4-Way matches, with the winners of those bouts advancing to meet in the World X-Cup final later that night.

title: Two Title Matches Added To AEW WrestleDream 2026
raw_title: Two Title Matches Added To AEW WrestleDream 2026
body: AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo made another successful defense of his crown against UK standout Michael Oku, and issued a challenge to anyone in the locker room to step up to the "Real Latino Man." That challenge was answered by none other than Tommaso Ciampa, who set the match in stone with a knee to the champion after Andrade beat Ciampa to the punch by kissing him on the cheek. Fans will get a preview of this match this week on "AEW Dynamite" when Andrade teams up with Will Ospreay to take on Ciampa and Samoa Joe. Immediately after, The Brawling Birds sat at ringside to see who would be their next challengers to the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships. The team of Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron, now known as Wrathlander, faced off with the Sisters of Sin and Divine Dominion in a three-way tag team match to determine the number one contenders. Wrathlander picked up the surprise victory and sealed their spot on the WrestleDream card as Statlander continues her quest to become the second-ever AEW Women's Triple Crown Champion, while Cameron hopes to become the first-ever two-time holder of the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships. At the time of writing, a total of seven matches are confirmed for WrestleDream, with all of the bouts having championships on the line. The only titles currently not on the line at the time of writing are Persephone's AEW TBS Championship, Darby Allin's AEW TBT Championship, and Kazuchika Okada's AEW International Championship. However, Darby and Okada have a chance to qualify for the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match via two title matches this Wednesday.

body: Wren Sinclair recently opened up about her difficult introduction to WWE NXT. On the No Contest Wrestling Podcast , Sinclair reflected on joining WWE NXT for the first time, her introduction to the brand, and her debut match. “There was no preparation really because I literally just got there maybe like a week or so ago, and immediately they were like, thrown in. “ I was like, ‘Oh, this is terrifying. I’m going to be in a ring with all of these women that I do not know. I can’t create any alliances. We met like a couple days ago ,'” she added. Sinclair also added that there was no preparation. However, things have completely changed now, but Sinclair noted that it was terrifying then to get thrown in a ring with people she did not know. “ It’s not like, oh, a singles match. It’s like, oh, all of them.” Sinclair’s first WWE NXT match was a multi-woman NXT Women’s Title number 1 Contendership match in 2024. Sinclair recalled feeling terrified ahead of the bout. She noted that she had just met the other competitors a couple of days earlier and had no opportunity to build alliances with them in the ring.
The match format added to the pressure. Instead of a singles contest, Sinclair found herself in a multi-woman match for the NXT Women's Title number one contendership.
She emphasized that there was no real preparation involved. Sinclair pointed out that the experience felt overwhelming at the time because she was suddenly competing against unfamiliar opponents.
Sinclair observed that circumstances have since improved for her in NXT. Her initial debut, however, remained a daunting introduction to the brand's environment.

body: LOUISVILLE, Ky. (WDRB+WAVE) — A former WWE star is coming to Louisville for a Halloween-themed wrestling event next weekend. Tyler Breeze will take part in Powerbomb Pro Wrestling’s “A Really Bad Dream on Logan Street” Saturday, Oct. 24, at Logan Street Market. body: Link TNA Manolo Has Pizzazz learned all of life’s lessons from decades of professional wrestling. Manolo has been covering the sport for over ten years on Cageside Seats. TNA is stacking the Destination X PPV by bringing back a variety of specialty gimmick matches. Santino Marella broke the news. Destination X is about taking risks. Ultimate X is one of the riskiest matches in TNA, and there will be two of them on PPV. The women will compete to determine the #1 contender for the Knockouts Championship, and the men will compete to determine the #1 contender for the X-Division Championship. In addition, the World X-Cup returns. There will be two four-way matches with wrestlers from around the world. The winners advance to the final on that same night. title: Sol Ruca Learned to Stand Up For Herself From Becky Lynch

summary_src: Sol Ruca recently claimed that WWE veteran Becky Lynch taught her to stand up for herself. During a recent interview with KRON 4, Sol Ruca opened up about what she learned from working with Becky Lynch during their WWE Women’s Intercontinental title feud.
body: Sol Ruca recently claimed that WWE veteran Becky Lynch taught her to stand up for herself. During a recent interview with KRON 4 , Sol Ruca opened up about what she learned from working with Becky Lynch during their WWE Women’s Intercontinental title feud. “ She is one of the greatest of all time for a reason. She is so, so good at what she does. She’s so good at the character work ,” Sol Ruca shared. “ I think I’ve learned a lot from her, especially in the character aspect of it. Seeing how her brain works, seeing how she’s able to take these promos and these segments and really make it her own and really know what people are going to bite on, know what the fans are going to enjoy, and being able to turn nothing into something.” The former WWE Women’s IC Champion also shared that Lynch is really good at questioning WWE’s creative and has taught her to take a stand for herself. “I think she’s really, really good at that. I think she’s really good at questioning creative and really just trying to make everything the best that it can be. “ So I definitely learned to be able to stick up for myself a little bit when I disagree with certain things. I think she’s really good at doing that in a respectful way and being able to perform at the best of her ability and just giving the fans what they wan t,” she finished. Lynch was recently involved in the Women’s World title match at WWE Money in the Bank 2026, while Ruca performed in the Women’s Money in the Bank ladder match in the same PLE. Shotzi Blackheart pulled a ‘Rick Rude’ to appear in two televised wrestling promotions on the same night (Oct. 22, 2026). Shotzi is beefing with a Stardom invasion in MLW, and she made a surprise appearance in TNA during a heel turn reunion. The ‘Rick Rude’ is a reference to the man himself appearing on WWE Raw and WCW Nitro on the same night back on November 17, 1997. That was a historic moment in wrestling history. Several wrestlers have gone on to do the same to varying degrees of importance over the years. Shotzi can add her name to the list. Shotzi had her eye on a dream match against Saya Kamitani. When Rina and Lady Frost crowded the MLW women’s champion, Scarlett Bordeaux had Shotzi’s back. They were still outnumbered, then Zamaya ran in as a surprise ally for Shotzi and Scarlett. Over on TNA Impact starting at 9 pm ET on AMC, Shotzi arrived as a surprise. Kiera Hogan turned heel by dumping Allie as her tag team partner and reuniting with Tasha Steelz as Fire ‘n Flava. While they pounded Allie, Shotzi ran in for the rescue. Both MLW Fusion and TNA Impact were taped episodes. In the TV timeline for MLW, Shotzi is women’s champion, so that means she’ll be present for a while longer on Fusion. title: Billy Gunn Reveals Reason AEW Paired Him With Acclaimed
raw_title: Billy Gunn explains why AEW paired him with The Acclaimed
summary_src: Despite having his sons in AEW, Billy Gunn was paired with The Acclaimed in the promotion. Speaking with Inside The Ropes during his latest UK tour, Gunn was asked about his partnership with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens of The Acclaimed.
body: Despite having his sons in AEW , Billy Gunn was paired with The Acclaimed in the promotion. Speaking with Inside The Ropes during his latest UK tour, Gunn was asked about his partnership with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens of The Acclaimed. Talking about their pairing despite having his own two sons in the promotion, Gunn said, “ They wanted me to kind of just go with The Acclaimed because they were getting [there]. They just needed, like, I still have equity in this business. “ So with me with them, it kind of makes people take notice a little bit. When you put me with them, you have a tendency to watch now instead of just going, ‘Hey, these are just two more wrestlers ,'” Gunn added. He claimed that his presence with them made people look out for The Acclaimed and realize that they were good. Gunn finished by claiming that Acclaimed was not just him, but it was the three of them. “ Because The Acclaimed wasn’t just me. It was all three of us. Everything just kind of fell into place to where we had Max doing the rap and then Anthony would do the hometown, and then he would do the ‘Scissor Me Daddy Ass’ and the place would go nuts.” While Gunn and Bowens are still with AEW, Caster recently parted ways with Khan’s promotion and joined TNA Wrestling. However, things soon took a different turn following his Saudi Arabia rap verses at his TNA Bound for Glory debut. llm_long: Billy Gunn has been part of All Elite Wrestling since 2020. He insisted that his sons Austin and Colten complete their college education before pursuing careers in the promotion.
Gunn stated that he refused to help get his sons hired by AEW until they graduated. He emphasized that his own success in wrestling did not guarantee they would succeed in the same field.

On the day Austin Gunn graduated, he handed his diploma to his father and immediately asked when they could start in wrestling. Gunn had required college graduation as the first condition before any discussion of entering the business.
Colten Gunn also decided to pursue wrestling after having a different career path mapped out until age 60. The choice surprised both Gunn and his wife, given the demanding nature of the profession.

Gunn explained that his frequent absences from home, including 300 days on the road each year early in his career, made him hesitant for his sons to follow the same path. He wanted them to have more stable family lives than he experienced.
Although Gunn trained his sons to a certain point, he required them to seek and complete AEW tryouts on their own. He did not ask for them to be hired simply because they were his children.

title: Shayna Baszler Discusses WWE Coaching After TNA Move
raw_title: Shayna Baszler addresses WWE coaching future following TNA signing
summary_src: A wrestling and MMA veteran, Shayna Baszler recently joined forces with Zoey Serrano in TNA Wrestling. After parting with WWE in 2025, she became more involved with the promotion in a non-wrestling role and was more focused on coaching the young talent.
body: A wrestling and MMA veteran, Shayna Baszler recently joined forces with Zoey Serrano in TNA Wrestling. After parting with WWE in 2025, she became more involved with the promotion in a non-wrestling role and was more focused on coaching the young talent. Recently, speaking with Denice Salcedo , Baszler opened up about her WWE coaching career following her recent TNA signing. “ There’s been some thought because word got out somehow. I’ve been coaching, producing part-time at NXT and Evolve and all that. “That is something that I found that I have fallen in love with, watching these young athletes grow and learn to love pro wrestling ,” she added. Baszler further added that TNA’s her favorite place right now and she still has the liberty to go coach in WWE. “ TNA is the perfect place for me right now. Thankfully, there’s a good relationship so I can still coach when I’m available. I’m obviously not as available as I was, but that door I guess is still there. “ I can coach when I need a cane and have to sit in a chair. Beating people up right now is what I’m able to do right now, and let’s just ride it till the wheels fall off, ” she said. “ Nobody’s told me no ,” Baszler answered when asked if she could coach if she had the time. “To be fair, I did ask people that mattered, ‘Hey, I’m thinking about helping Zoey out. Are there any issues with that? Nobody told me not to do it and that I wouldn’t be welcomed back ,” she added. “ Now again, there’s maybe some discussion to be had about my availability and all that, and we might have to revisit some of that at some point. I’m not someone that’s going to burn bridges either. I’m very thankful to WWE and everything they did for me and the platform they gave me ,” Baszler finished.
