title: Results Recap: Hall’s WWE Raw Review 7.14.97
raw_title: Hall’s WWE Raw Review 7.14.97
body: Monday Night Raw Date: July 14, 1997 Location: Freeman Coliseum, San Antonio, Texas Attendance: 7,731 Commentators: Vince McMahon, Jim Ross It’s title time as we need some new Tag Team Champions. Steve Austin and Shawn Michaels had held the titles but Michaels was suspended for a backstage fight with Bret Hart. While you get your head around Michaels and Hart not getting along, consider that Austin has to team with someone he picks to face Owen Hart/British Bulldog, who won a tournament. We’re also on the road to Summerslam and Hart is going to need something to do. Let’s get to it. We open with a recap of Canadian Stampede and Bret Hart being a national hero in Canada, but we’re not in Canada tonight are we? Here is the Hart Foundation to get things going. Bret Hart immediately blasts San Antonio (I’m surprised it took that long) and gets to the point: he has a contract that says he gets a WWF Title shot at Summerslam but if he loses, he can never wrestle on American soil again. Bret promises to kill the Undertaker like a dead star and win the title for the fifth time. Owen Hart isn’t worried about facing Steve Austin at Summerslam because Austin is already losing the Tag Team Titles tonight. Then at Summerslam, Austin will have to give Owen a kiss on his…uh, certain area. British Bulldog is ready to beat Ken Shamrock at Summerslam and if he doesn’t, he’ll eat dog food (along with losing the European Title). That leaves us with Brian Pillman, who loves all of the abuse that Dusty Rhodes has given Dustin over the years. At Summerslam, he’ll finish Dustin’s heart for good and if he loses, he’ll wear a dress on Raw. Oh and Jim Neidhart, who doesn’t have a match at Summerslam, will shave his goatee if any of the team loses at Summerslam. If Jim Cornette didn’t come up with most of those ideas, I’ll eat my hat. Do I have a hat? Anyway, this brings out Steve Austin, who is joined by Shamrock, the Patriot, Sid and Shawn Michaels, with the question being which one Austin will pick as his partner tonight. This was basically “here’s most of the Summerslam card” in one segment. The Headbangers are on a golf course, which is some clue for a contest. This is fallout from Lawler attacking Scott a few weeks back and Papa Paduzki wanting revenge. Before the match, Ivan sings as the fans probably have absolutely no idea who he is. Lawler and Christopher jump them to start and send the good guys out to the floor. This lets commentary wonder if Lawler and Christopher are related as Scott is back with a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker to Christopher. Lawler dropkicks Christopher by mistake but Scott gets taken into the wrong corner again. That means a jumping right hand and northern lights suplex have Scott in more trouble. Lawler seems to have Scott done but Christopher asks to finish instead. The Tennessee Jam misses though and Christopher superkicks Lawler by mistake. Ivan comes back in for his wild flailing and the Polish Hammer (ax handle to the chest) finishes Lawle

title: End of an Era: ‘It’s my birthright’- Dominik Mysterio Opens Up On who he wants to retire Rey Mysterio
raw_title: ‘It’s my birthright’- Dominik Mysterio reveals who he wants to retire Rey Mysterio
body: The former Intercontinental Champion also has a specific venue in mind for the potential retirement match, hoping to bring the family rivalry to a historic arena in Mexico. His comments come amid reports that Rey could retire from in-ring competition in 2027, although WWE has not confirmed his plans. Speaking on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dominik explained that he has long wanted his father to step away from wrestling and believes he should be the one to make it happen. He said: “I’ve been talking about it. I’ve been wanting him to retire. I want him out of here, you know? There’s only room for so many Mysterios in WWE. There’s one pushing 60, and I think it’s time for him to kick rocks; that’s just how I see it.” Dominik was even more direct when discussing the prospect of being involved in Rey’s final match. “It’s my birthright. I would lose my absolute s*** if it’s not me,” he said. “I’ve got to take his mask, and I’ve got to take his name.” The 28-year-old also revealed where he would like the match to take place, pointing towards the Auditorio Fausto Gutierrez Moreno in Tijuana, Mexico. “I believe my dad has wrestled there, debuted there. My great-uncle and most of my godfathers wrestled there [too],” Dominik explained. The venue would carry personal significance for the Mysterio family, making it a fitting choice for a potential final chapter in their long-running rivalry. Rey, who began his wrestling career in 1989, remains one of the most respected figures in the sport. He helped popularise lucha libre in the United States during his time in WCW before joining WWE in 2002. The former WWE Champion was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2023 and was named general manager of AAA in May. Reports have suggested that Rey could retire from active competition in 2027, with the expectation that he would continue working in an executive capacity and help develop younger talent. However, no official retirement date or venue has been announced, leaving Dominik’s dream match dependent on what Rey decides to do next. × Sign in to TalkingPoints Comment, react and follow the stories you care about. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin 10/22 TNA THURSDAY NIGHT IMPACT ON AMC REPORT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-22 23:04:00 Welcome to this week's TNA Thursday Night Impact on AMC report! Tom Hannifan and Matthew Rehwoldt are on the call from Dothan, Alabama! Daria Rae came out to cut a promo, blaming Santino Marella and Indi Hartwell for hatching a scheme to ruin her career. Daria has taken TNA to new heights and won't stop. Indi would never had won the Knockouts title if Daria had been there, because she doesn't deserve it. Indi Hartwell came out on stage. She mockingly welcomed Daria back but said it appears her time away did nothing to help her, as Daria is still the same bitter and selfish person. She can blame anyone she wants but while she was at home, Indi became the Knockouts Champion. Daria said it won't last long. Indi asked if she was going to slap her and get suspended again. Daria said she doesn't have to, as Xia Brookside has a rematch clause and will take on Indi right here, right now, so good luck. Hartwell is still in street clothes as she had no time to prepare. Xia worked over Indi early but the champ caught her with a clothesline. She booted Xia to the apron, then nailed a big boot that sent her to the floor. Xia grabbed the Knockouts title belt but Indi drtilled her with a big boot on the floor. The crowd chanted for Indi. Xia cut her off and sent her into the apron, then the ring steps. Xia stomped on Indi's elbow, which was draped across the ring steps. Xia controlled the flow of the action, focusing her assault on the arm and elbow. Indi made a comeback with a spinebuster. She went for the Hurt Donuts but Xia snatched her and went for an armbreaker. Brookside followed up with a Codebreaker for a two count. Hartwell made a comeback and scored the pin. Daria Rae came out on stage as Zoey Serrano and Shayna Baszler attacked Hartwell. Baszler choked Indi out. TNA Champion Leon Slater cut a promo backstage. He said he feels good and is the youngest TNA Champion of all time. He's going to walk into his first-ever title defense against Trey Miguel and he knows Trey is ready to risk it all to capture the belt and Leon is counting on it. He warned Trey that f he doesn't come in with the fire, he's going to get beat. Trey walked in and they faced off, then embraced each other. He said Leon made history and he's ready to make more history at the PPV. Miguel said he's only had one title shot in the past and he doesn't know if or when he gets another, so he's telling Slater that he's willing to do whatever it takes to walk out with the belt. body: Chelsea Green already has Liv Morgan waiting for her at Crown Jewel. First, she has to make sure she actually gets there as champion. That victory was enough to put Perez in position for the championship match she felt she deserved. Now the stakes are much bigger. Green is supposed to face Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan in the Champion vs. Champion match at Crown Jewel. If Perez takes the WWE Women’s Championship tonight, that entire situation changes just two weeks before the show. The Judgment Day could become important too. Perez won’t necessarily be walking into this alone, and Green has a lot more than one challenger to worry about. A normal match clearly wasn’t enough for Giulia and Blake Monroe. Now there are no normal match rules keeping them under control. Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley haven’t had much time to enjoy becoming champions. The new WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions make their first defense tonight against Michin and B-Fab. Bliss and Paxley are still a relatively new team, so holding the championships is one thing. Figuring out how to keep them when other teams start coming after them is another. title: On the Record: Nikki Bella Opens Up On Where She Stands on Getting Married Again
raw_title: Nikki Bella Reveals Where She Stands on Getting Married Again
summary_src: Nikki Bella may be single, but getting married apparently isn’t anywhere near the top of her current wish list. The WWE Hall of Famer revealed that finding a husband isn’t even on her vision board right now, although she’s definitely not opposed to having a man — and some good sex — in her life. ...
body: During the October 23 episode of The Nikki & Brie Show , Nikki and Brie Bella spoke with Amanda Hirsch about manifestation and the vision boards they create to represent their goals. The sisters explained that they enjoy getting together with wine, buying magazines and cutting out pictures of things they want to accomplish. When Hirsch asked about the size of their boards, Brie joked that Nikki’s was massive. Nikki explained that she simply has a lot of dreams before pointing out that marriage isn’t currently one of the things she’s trying to manifest. “I got a lot of dreams. She has, I think, yeah, more. Maybe it’s because she has, as far as, like, husband and life. But even though that’s not on my vision board right now…” That doesn’t mean Nikki has completely crossed romance off the board. Later in the conversation, she reconsidered whether there might be room for at least one particular addition. Brie didn’t need much convincing and immediately told her sister exactly what she thought was missing: “Girl, you need a man.” Brie immediately agreed and had a few more suggestions for what her sister should add. “Girl, you need a man. And, like, good sex, and have, like, a good-looking guy and, like, half-naked.” The comments come shortly after Nikki made it clear that being single doesn’t mean she’s desperate to find somebody. During another recent episode of The Nikki & Brie Show, Brie announced that her sister was single and asked their guests whether they had any available friends. Nikki immediately pumped the brakes on Brie trying to shop around for her next boyfriend : “Okay, I’m not, like, for sale.” So while Nikki might be willing to add a good-looking man to that vision board, a wedding apparently isn’t part of the picture right now. She’s got plenty of dreams she’s looking to manifest, and finding another husband isn’t currently one of them. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: Ari Emanuel Speaks On Possibility of Relocating WWE Crown Jewel Amid Security Concerns
raw_title: Ari Emanuel Addresses Possibility of Relocating WWE Crown Jewel Amid Security Concerns
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is still on for Saudi Arabia, at least for now. TKO executive chair and CEO Ari Emanuel says the November 7 show remains set for Riyadh, but the company is monitoring the situation every day and is already looking at where the event could be moved if things get worse. During an ...
body: During an appearance on Fox News , Bret Baier asked Emanuel directly whether Crown Jewel would still happen amid the escalating security situation in Saudi Arabia. Emanuel said nothing has been canceled at this point. “Right now, everything’s still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far, so good. Nothing’s been canceled.” That doesn’t mean TKO is simply crossing its fingers and hoping everything works out. When Baier asked whether Emanuel was receiving government briefings and if there was a point where TKO could pull the show, Emanuel revealed that the company has an entire team working on the situation. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” That last part is especially interesting because it’s the first clear indication that TKO is looking at backup options for Crown Jewel. Emanuel didn’t reveal any potential alternate locations, and he didn’t say that WWE has decided to move the event, only that the company is considering where it could go if Riyadh becomes unworkable. The update comes as travel into Saudi Arabia has become a much bigger concern. The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh issued a security alert on October 22 warning Americans to use “extreme caution” at Saudi airports amid attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh also remains shut down, according to the latest Embassy alert. Airports in Jeddah and Dammam are still operating, although both have been dealing with delays and cancellations. “Operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remain suspended. King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam are operational with some delays and cancellations.” The Embassy has also warned about the possibility of additional attacks on airports, airspace closures and sudden flight cancellations. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia currently need special authorization to use any airport in the country. Despite all of that, WWE hasn’t pulled the plug on Crown Jewel. Emanuel’s comments make it clear that Riyadh remains Plan A for November 7, but TKO isn’t going into the next two weeks without a Plan B either. For now, Crown Jewel is staying exactly where WWE planned it, but that could change quickly depending on what happens in Saudi Arabia. With TKO checking the situation daily and already looking at possible alternatives, the company appears to be preparing for the possibility that a last-minute move could become necessary. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Bret Baier asked Emanuel directly whether Crown Jewel would still happen amid the escalating security situation in Saudi Arabia. Nothing has been canceled at this point. Right now, everything’s still set, Emanuel explained.

title: On the Record: Leon Slater Discusses winning the TNA World Championship, roots in Yorkshire and his thoughts on Destination X
raw_title: Leon Slater talks winning the TNA World Championship, roots in Yorkshire and his thoughts on Destination X
body: Home » Leon Slater talks winning the TNA World Championship, roots in Yorkshire and his thoughts on Destination X The newly crowned TNA World Champion is ready to show a different side of himself in the ring. But as Leon Slater sees it, carrying the title also means carrying the hopes of the people and places that helped him get here. For Leon Slater, the moment the referee’s hand hit the mat for three (against the legendary Nic Nemeth) was almost too big to take in. “I remember hitting the Swanton 450, hearing 1, 2, 3, and just sitting back, like kneeling and just going, ‘Oh my God! Like I can’t believe like what’s just happened,’” he recalled in conversation with Soundsphere’s Dom Smith. “It was relief, it was joy, it was euphoria, it was all of these feelings you could possibly imagine wrapped into one.” At 22, Slater had become TNA’s youngest World Champion. The achievement still feels unreal. He hasn’t even watched the match back: he wants to hold on to the memory as it felt in the moment, rather than let the footage become the version he remembers. “When you watch the footage back, the memory almost becomes like a third-person memory,” he explained. “So, I want to keep this as a first-person memory for as long as possible.” That instinct says something about Slater’s approach. He knows the importance of the milestone, but he doesn’t want the story of winning the title to replace the feeling of having lived it. The win is a new chapter, not a finish line, and the person who once had to believe in his own potential now has to defend his place at the top. Slater has never been short on belief. But for him, confidence has to be earned again and again in the ring. “The last thing that I want to become is someone that is just talk and is no action,” he said. He knows his self-assurance can invite questions: is he confident, or is he cocky? His answer is simple: the work has to back up the words. “I think it’s impossible to call it arrogance when I’m backing it up in the ring on the mic, and as I’ve got this on my shoulder.” There is another kind of pressure attached to the championship. Slater has been supported by family, mentors, peers and fans, and he remembers the people in the business who publicly backed him before he had the world title, and is glad to prove them right. He specifically points to Matt and Jeff Hardy as people who “stuck their neck out” for him. “I can’t let those sacrifices go to waste,” he said. “I don’t want to make those people that have believed in me look stupid.” Rather than shrink from the weight of that responsibility, Slater welcomes it. “Pressure is an absolute privilege,” he said. “I’m glad to be in this position. I welcome the pressure.” That attitude is already shaping how he thinks about his future in TNA. title: Wren Sinclair Praises Total Divas Impact
raw_title: Wren Sinclair explains why WWE Total Divas was important for women’s wrestling
summary_src: Emerged as a revolutionary step in women’s wrestling sports entertainment, WWE’s Wren Sinclair feels that the show was empowering. Speaking on No-Contest Wrestling, Sinclair shared her thoughts on WWE Total Divas and why the show was important for women’s wrestling. “I love Total Divas.
body: Emerged as a revolutionary step in women’s wrestling sports entertainment, WWE’s Wren Sinclair feels that the show was empowering. Speaking on No-Contest Wrestling , Sinclair shared her thoughts on WWE Total Divas and why the show was important for women’s wrestling. “ I love Total Divas. I loved reality TV growing up. I don’t know why. Maybe that’s why I’m kind of confrontational nowadays. I used to watch Total Divas, obviously Keeping Up with the Kardashians, The Bad Girls Club. Avid watcher of that, ” Sinclair said. When further asked what the show meant to her, Sinclair added that it helped highlight the women wrestlers when the television shows did not. “ I feel like it highlighted the women sometimes when the television didn’t. It allowed you to get a grasp of what they actually go through. I know a lot of times in the show, their segments got cut, their promos got cut, etc. So you never really got to learn who they were ,” she said. “ And I feel like that show, it felt like I was in Natty’s house sometimes playing with her cats. It felt like you got to know them. I feel like I know some of them and I haven’t even met them. “ But I feel like it really showed people that they’re people and they’re legitimate professional wrestlers. They’re in this too, even though they don’t have the ball all the time. So I feel like it was empowering.” The first season of WWE Total Divas aired in 2013, and the show ran till 2019. The series gave viewers an insider look into the professional and personal lives of the women WWE wrestlers, including some behind-the-scenes footage. title: Backstage Buzz: Triple H’s Plans for Bobby Roode’s WWE Backstage Future Revealed
raw_title: Triple H’s Plans for Bobby Roode’s WWE Backstage Future Revealed
summary_src: Bobby Roode hasn’t wrestled in years, but WWE apparently has some pretty big plans for him behind the scenes.
body: Speaking with Stephanie McMahon on the October 22 episode of What’s Your Story? , Hayes discussed how his own role in WWE has evolved over the years. That’s when he recalled Triple H approaching him with a pretty blunt reminder about the future. “But yeah, I just made up my mind that this is your new path, and go for it. And I’ll tell you, Trips came up to me one day and he goes, ‘So Michael, you know you’re not gonna be around forever.’” Hayes couldn’t resist having some fun with Triple H’s choice of words: “What does that mean, life or work?” Triple H then explained exactly what he meant. Hayes said Triple H compared his current position to the role the legendary Pat Patterson once held and made it clear that he wanted Roode prepared to eventually follow in Hayes’ footsteps. “You’re our Pat Patterson. I need you to make Bobby Roode Michael.” That apparently got Hayes thinking about the reality that somebody will eventually have to take over responsibilities he’s handled behind the scenes. Judging by his assessment, Roode has already made some serious progress. “And I said, ‘Okay, that’s a really good point, because I’m not gonna be here forever.’ And boy, has he come along.” Stephanie agreed that Roode has a bright future in the role, and Hayes went even further with his praise. He believes Roode can become great at the job, although there’s still one part of working behind the scenes that he wants him to master. “No, I see great things for him. He’s just gotta get out of the stuff where—I don’t know how to really categorize it. This stuff happens in this industry that’s just out of your control, and it’s just gonna happen. And you just gotta kind of let it go and say, ‘Okay.’” Stephanie understood exactly what Hayes meant. She explained that there’s no point burning energy complaining about something that’s going to happen anyway when that energy could be spent figuring out how to make it work. “Yeah, so much energy about bitching about doing it, because you’re going to do it. It’s happening anyways. So save the energy to do it and find a way to do it.” That brought Hayes back to a lesson Vince McMahon once gave him. Instead of explaining why an idea wouldn’t work, Hayes learned that his job was to figure out how to make it work. “I still have problems sometimes. You actually told that story too. You said, ‘Find a way to make it work. Don’t tell me how it doesn’t work.’ That’s what Vince—‘Tell me how you can make it work.’ He said, ‘Michael, I have many people out on the street telling me why it don’t work. I need somebody to tell me how it will work.’” The comments give a lot more context to where Roode stands in WWE these days. His profile was quietly moved into the alumni section of WWE.com in September, but there was never any indication that he’d actually left the company , as he’s continued working as a producer after stepping away from the ring. title: Michael Hayes Confronted Chelsea Green Over Her WWE Character
raw_title: Michael Hayes Confronted Chelsea Green Over Her WWE Character
summary_src: Michael Hayes has found himself in plenty of Chelsea Green drama lately, but apparently he’s also responsible for giving her some pretty important advice. The WWE Hall of Famer revealed that he once pulled Green up over something that was missing from one of her matches — Chelsea Green herself.
body: Speaking with Stephanie McMahon on What’s Your Story? , Hayes explained that one thing he constantly pushes with younger wrestlers is making sure their personalities don’t disappear once the bell rings. Putting together a technically good match is fine, but Hayes wants to actually see the character too. “But, you know, I think pretty much they just told you who went over and, you know, not the details. Right? And are you bringing your character into a match? You know, that’s a theme I go with a lot with kids today. Like, I’ll hear how they’ll run the match. That’s a good match. Where’s your character?” That’s when Hayes brought up Green, and even he seemed to realize that mentioning her name might be dangerous territory these days. “You know, like I did that with Chelsea one time. I always get in trouble when I talk about—” Stephanie immediately knew where this was going. Considering everything that’s happened between Hayes and Green lately, she couldn’t believe he was willingly stepping back into it. Hayes wasn’t about to bury Green this time. Stephanie pointed out that Chelsea is great with her character, and Hayes completely agreed before revealing what he’d actually told her. “She’s fantastic. Yes. But I told her, I said, ‘Chelsea, where was your character?’ I said, ‘I’m not telling you, you can’t wrestle and do good moves.’ Everybody can’t be Chelsea.” Apparently, Chelsea didn’t argue or need the point explained five different ways. Hayes said she immediately understood what he was getting at and gave her plenty of credit for picking it up so quickly. “And she got it right away. She’s very smart. She’s very smart.” Of course, Hayes talking about Chelsea Green is always going to get a little more attention after their WWE Unreal drama. Green wasn’t happy when she first saw footage of Hayes questioning her potential , although she eventually changed her tune and credited his criticism with pushing her to another level. Chelsea may have gotten over it, but her mother definitely had something to say. At SummerSlam, Green’s mom walked right up to Hayes, introduced herself and hit him with a simple “F*** you” over what she’d seen on Unreal , leaving Hayes with a story he immediately went backstage and told everyone. This time, though, Hayes had nothing but praise for Green. His problem wasn’t that she couldn’t wrestle — he just wanted more Chelsea Green in a Chelsea Green match, and apparently she understood exactly what he meant. title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Details His Wrestling Influences, Being In AEW With Samoa Joe & More
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Details His Wrestling Influences, Being In AEW With Samoa Joe & More
body: Ilja Dragunov recently weighed in on his influences as a wrestler and what it’s like to be in AEW with the likes of Samoa Joe. Dragunov debuted on AEW WrestleDream and then won his in-ring debut on Dynamite against Mike Bailey. Dragunov spoke about who influenced him getting into wrestling during his interview with TMZ Inside the Ring. You can see highlights below: “So when I started to do to pursue professional wrestling, I had different influences that made me start. And it wasn’t necessarily the American wrestling-ish style or however you would call it. Like, my role models are [the] Kabashis, Mako Satamuras. Terry Funks, Roddy Pipers. William Regals. And coming from continental Europe, we have our own legends like Axe Dieter, Klaus Karlhoff, René Lazartes. “These are — where I come from, and what people inspired me, professional wrestlers are fighters. And that’s how we entertain. We don’t entertain first and then we are fighters or portraying fighters; we are fighters in the first place.” “Coming over to the States is definitely of course, like a different direction. But this is the beautiful thing about AEW being a place for people who are really expressing this craft. Like, people being there like a Samoa Joe, who was highly influential on me when I didn’t even know how to put on a wristlock. To know that this person is there for instance, just as an example — yeah, it clicks with me and resonates with me. And I feel like, ‘Okay, okay, that feels good.”

title: WWE Crown Jewel Stadium Construction Underway in Saudi Arabia Amid Security Concerns
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel Stadium Construction Underway in Saudi Arabia Amid Security Concerns
summary_src: WWE may be keeping backup plans in its pocket for Crown Jewel, but Saudi Arabia is clearly still moving forward like the show is happening in Riyadh. New footage making the rounds online shows construction already underway on the massive Riyadh Season Stadium ahead of the November 7 event.
body: The stadium is obviously still in the early stages of being put together, but the scale of the project is already pretty clear. Crews can be seen working across the huge site as preparations continue with just over two weeks remaining before Crown Jewel. There’s still plenty of work to be done before WWE can actually move in and start setting up its own production. However, the construction activity makes it clear that preparations on the Saudi side haven’t stopped despite the growing security concerns surrounding the event. That’s particularly interesting after TKO executive chair and CEO Ari Emanuel revealed that Crown Jewel remains scheduled for Riyadh while the company monitors the situation daily. Speaking on Fox News, Emanuel said everything remains set for the time being. “Right now, everything’s still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far, so good. Nothing’s been canceled.” TKO isn’t operating without a backup plan, though. Emanuel also revealed that a team is monitoring developments and looking at where Crown Jewel could potentially be moved if holding the event in Riyadh becomes impossible. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” Those precautions come amid serious travel concerns in Saudi Arabia. The U.S. Embassy issued a security alert on October 22 warning Americans to use “extreme caution” at Saudi airports following attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis . King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh also remains suspended according to that alert, while airports in Jeddah and Dammam are operating with delays and cancellations. U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia currently require special authorization to use airports in the country. title: WWE Employees Hated Vince McMahon’s Company-Wide Social Media Mandate
raw_title: WWE Employees Hated Vince McMahon’s Company-Wide Social Media Mandate
summary_src: Vince McMahon apparently didn’t just want WWE employees using social media — he wanted everybody in the company thinking about it.
body: Speaking with Michael Hayes on What’s Your Story? , Stephanie explained that Vince never wanted WWE getting so far ahead of a new trend that audiences couldn’t keep up. His goal was to stay just slightly ahead of everybody else, and Stephanie believes he recognized the importance of social media very early. “He didn’t—he never wanted to be ahead of the curve. He always wanted to be slightly ahead of the curve, but he didn’t wanna be so far ahead that people didn’t understand what was going on. But he just needed to be slightly ahead of the curve. Social media, yeah. I mean, that was—he saw that before anybody else.” At the time, Stephanie was overseeing WWE’s digital and social media operations. After attending a conference, she returned with an idea she’d heard about making social media a small responsibility spread across the entire company. “And I remember, because I was in charge of digital and social at the time, and I had been at a conference and come back and I said, ‘Oh, they said it was really interesting that it wasn’t, you know, a hundred percent of one person’s job. It was one percent of a hundred percent of the people’s jobs.’” Vince apparently heard “one percent” and decided that wasn’t nearly enough. His response was to make social media everybody’s problem in a much bigger way. “And he said, ‘No, it’s a hundred percent of a hundred percent.’” According to Stephanie, things quickly reached the point where every WWE department was expected to explain exactly what it was doing on social media. That mandate didn’t exactly go over well with employees who couldn’t figure out why posting online suddenly had anything to do with their actual jobs. “And it was like everything became about social media, and then all the department heads had to report back what their departments were doing in social media. And people hated it because they had no idea. They were like, ‘Why? What does my job have to do with social media?’” Hayes remembered that period as well and specifically recalled Vince putting Michael Cole in charge of WWE’s social media efforts. “I remember when he put Michael Cole in charge of social media.” Vince’s mandate may have driven people inside WWE crazy at the time, but Stephanie’s story shows just how aggressively he wanted the company to jump onto something once he believed it mattered. What started as her sharing one idea from a conference suddenly turned into every department having to explain its social media strategy. summary: Per Ringside News: speaking with Michael Hayes on What’s Your Story? , Stephanie explained that Vince never wanted WWE getting so far ahead of a new trend that audiences couldn’t keep up. That mandate didn’t exactly go over well with employees who couldn’t figure out why posting online suddenly had anything to do with their actual jobs. And it was like everything became about social media.

title: On the Record: Ilja Dragunov Opens Up On the Legends Who Inspired His Hard-Hitting Style
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals the Legends Who Inspired His Hard-Hitting Style
body: 0 AEW star Ilja Dragunov has revealed his wrestling inspirations. The former WWE star is known for his hard-hitting style and his matches often feel like real fights inside the ring. Speaking in an interview with TMZ Sports , Dragunov recently discussed his influences and explained how several legends shaped his approach. His inspirations include wrestlers from different wrestling backgrounds. He said, “So when I started to do to pursue professional wrestling, I had different influences that made me start. And it wasn’t necessarily the American wrestling-ish style or however you would call it. Like, my role models are [the] Kabashis, Mako Satamuras. Terry Funks, Roddy Pipers. William Regals. And coming from continental Europe, we have our own legends like Axe Dieter, Klaus Karlhoff, René Lazartes.” He believes wrestling should feel physical and authentic. “These are — where I come from, and what people inspired me, professional wrestlers are fighters. And that’s how we entertain. We don’t entertain first and then we are fighters or portraying fighters; we are fighters in the first place.” He discussed joining AEW and believes AEW allows wrestlers to express their craft. “Coming over to the States is definitely of course, like a different direction. But this is the beautiful thing about AEW being a place for people who are really expressing this craft. Like, people being there like a Samoa Joe, who was highly influential on me when I didn’t even know how to put on a wristlock. To know that this person is there for instance, just as an example — yeah, it clicks with me and resonates with me. And I feel like, ‘Okay, okay, that feels good.'” [H/T: 411mania ] The post Ilja Dragunov Reveals the Legends Who Inspired His Hard-Hitting Style appeared first on Wrestlezone .

However, appearances by legends such as The Rock and "Stone Cold" Steve Austin have not been confirmed. WWE has more than enough star power on its active roster to fill out the two-night weekend and still have a handful of notable names left over. Of course, anything can change creatively between now and then, and there's no telling who could be sidelined with an injury. These are the way-too-early match card predictions for WrestleMania 43. From the moment Oba Femi decisively defeated Brock Lesnar at WrestleMania 42, it was clear he was destined to win a world title sooner rather than later. Realistically, he should have already challenged for and won the World Heavyweight Championship by now (specifically at SummerSlam following his King of the Ring victory that earned him a title shot), but all signs point to WWE holding off on him having his crowning moment at WrestleMania 43. That would explain why Reigns has had a stranglehold on the prestigious prize since 'Mania back in April and will likely continue to reign as champ through the spring spectacle. Femi has repeatedly called out Reigns on post-show panels but has yet to cross paths with him on WWE TV. When they do finally go face-to-face, it will be a massive deal. WWE is attempting to keep Femi busy with random obstacles such as Lesnar and The Vision in the meantime. Expect Femi to win the men's Royal Rumble (the exact match where he made his main roster debut earlier this year) and set his sights on The Tribal Chief from there. That leaves him without an obvious opponent at the event, and the same can be said for all of The Vision. They've been at odds with Oba Femi as of late but are virtually guaranteed to come out on the losing end of that feud. Ideally, Bron Breakker would be in a marquee match at 'Mania next April, especially after missing this past year's installment due to injury (that was where he returned but didn't wrestle), but similar to Keys, there isn't one match that's a "must" for him to have unless he jumps ship to SmackDown or leaves The Vision. WWE has previously used multi-person tag team matches at WrestleMania to get wrestlers without clear storylines onto the card. That could be the case for The Vision and The 946. If built up properly, this could be a fun brawl and a solid showcase for everyone involved. A Street Fight stipulation would make for the most exciting scenario and allow them to go all out. Morgan recently regained the gold at Money in the Bank but has no challengers waiting in the wings. Her rivalries with Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch have been done to deat
summary: Per Bleacher Report: there has been speculation about the top matches at WrestleMania 43 and whether WWE will bring back familiar faces for the event. These are the way-too-early match card predictions for WrestleMania 43.

title: Ari Emanuel Monitors WWE Crown Jewel Amid Saudi Tensions
raw_title: Ari Emanuel addresses WWE Crown Jewel status amid Saudi Arabia security concerns
summary_src: Ari Emanuel, executive chairman and CEO of TKO Holdings, has addressed the status of WWE Crown Jewel amid growing security concerns in the Middle East. During an interview with Fox News, Emanuel addressed concerns surrounding TKO’s upcoming events including WWE’s Crown Jewel in Riyadh.
body: Ari Emanuel, executive chairman and CEO of TKO Holdings, has addressed the status of WWE Crown Jewel amid growing security concerns in the Middle East. During an interview with Fox News , Emanuel addressed concerns surrounding TKO’s upcoming events including WWE’s Crown Jewel in Riyadh. He indicated that, as of the interview, no events had been cancelled and that the company was closely monitoring developments while considering alternative arrangements if necessary. “Right now, everything is still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far so good. Nothing’s been cancelled.” “We have a whole team kind of working on this, and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” The uncertainty comes amid heightened regional tensions and security warnings issued by the U.S. State Department for nonessential diplomatic personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia. The developments follow reports that King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh had been attacked 20 times during the month, raising further concerns about security and travel disruptions. WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is currently scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7. However, a potential backup location in the United States has reportedly been discussed should the security situation force a change of plans. Americans in the region are advised to exercise heightened vigilance due to the complex security environment.

title: Drew McIntyre Teases WWE Return as Sin Cara
raw_title: Drew McIntyre hilariously teases WWE return as popular masked wrestler
body: Currently wrestling as Mistico in AEW and CMLL, the luchador was once known as Sin Cara in WWE. However, throughout Sin Cara's existence in WWE, the masked wrestler gimmick was portrayed by several performers. Recently, PWInsider reported that early pitches had been made to revive the Sin Cara character, although this time with a different wrestler taking on the role. Now absent from in-ring action for several months , former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre reacted to the news on social media and teased his comeback . McIntyre posted a video as a response to the post, where he was seen pulling off some high-flying action, with a caption saying, "I'm ready." The gimmick was originally portrayed by Místico, but was later taken over by Hunico after Místico was suspended for 30 days in 2011. Following Místico's return, it eventually led to a Sin Cara Negro vs. Sin Cara Azul feud that culminated in a Mask vs. Mask match at the Oct. 16, 2011 WWE SmackDown taping in Mexico City. Following Mistico's release in 2014, Hunico became the new Sin Cara, and the character remained a part of WWE until 2019. While McIntyre teased returning as the new masked Sin Cara, it should also be noted that McIntyre is not a stranger to the high-flying Lucha Libre style. "The Scottish Warrior" wrestled a couple of matches in AAA over a decade ago, in 2014 and 2015. McIntyre is currently away from wrestling, busy filming a few big Hollywood projects as well as a microdrama produced by WWE called Agent of Shadows. As of now, there are no confirmed updates on McIntyre's return.
summary: Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre reacted to PWInsider reports of early pitches to revive the Sin Cara character with a new wrestler. The Scottish star posted a social media video showing himself performing high-flying moves with the caption "I'm ready." The masked luchador gimmick was originally played by Mistico in WWE before being portrayed by multiple performers including Hunico.

title: 51-year-old WWE legend may follow in John Cena, AJ Styles’ footsteps by retiring soon
raw_title: 51-year-old WWE legend may follow in John Cena, AJ Styles’ footsteps by retiring soon
body: Over the last year alone, fans lost Goldberg , AJ Styles , and John Cena to retirement , and now, 51-year-old WWE legend Rey Mysterio may be joining them in 2027. WrestleVotes on Fightful Select reports that there's been "chatter backstage" at WWE about Mysterio possibly retiring in 2027. In turn, the promotion has started laying out plans for his farewell. While he is still a top in-ring performer, it's not surprising that the 51-year-old Mysterio is planning on hanging up the boots and mask soon. He has been wrestling for decades, and he has accomplished everything he can in WWE. WWE is likely planning the perfect final opponent for Mysterio. Gunther would be a great option, considering he was on a tear of retiring legends over the last couple of years. Retiring Mysterio could get him back on track after a year full of feuding with the likes of Danhausen. However, the best option is his son, Dominik Mysterio. Like Gunther, Mysterio has been on a skid over the last year. Retiring his father would give him much-needed legitimacy. The father-son duo has squared off several times previously. Their most notable encounter was at WrestleMania 39, which the elder Mysterio won. They would not have another televised singles match until the July 1, 2024, edition of Monday Night RAW, which Rey Mysterio also won. They have not had another singles match since. The last time that they shared the ring was the Oct. 5, 2026, edition of RAW. Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh defeated the LWO's Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee. In addition to his work in WWE, Mysterio is the general manager of Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide. He introduced the idea of the AAA tournament to determine Roman Reigns' challenger for the Mexico City episode of RAW in September 2026.
summary: Over the last year alone, the audience lost Goldberg , AJ Styles , and John Cena to retirement . WrestleVotes on Fightful Select reports that there's been chatter backstage at WWE about Mysterio possibly retiring in 2027.

llm.headline: Rey Mysterio eyed for 2027 retirement
llm.summary: Per Fightful Select, there has been backstage chatter at WWE about 51-year-old Rey Mysterio possibly retiring in 2027, prompting the company to begin planning his farewell. Mysterio has been a top in-ring performer for decades and has accomplished everything possible in WWE. Potential final opponents being discussed include Gunther and his son Dominik Mysterio.

title: Saturday Night SuperFight on VEEPS Nov 7 — MLW is coming to PPV
raw_title: MLW is coming to PPV: Saturday Night SuperFight on VEEPS Nov 7
body: Major League Wrestling (MLW) today announced that MLW Saturday Night SuperFight will stream live worldwide on Live Nation’s VEEPS on Saturday, November 7, at 8 p.m. ET from Cicero Stadium in Chicago. Saturday Night SuperFight marks MLW’s return to pay-per-view for the first time in seven years and represents the biggest premium live event on the league’s 2026 calendar. The event arrives amid significant momentum for MLW, following the launch of its flagship weekly series, MLW Fusion , Thursday nights at 8 p.m. ET on Tubi. Saturday Night SuperFight will serve as the culmination of the championship quests, epic rivalries, and escalating conflicts unfolding each week on Fusion , with MLW raising the stakes for a loaded night of must-see title fights and marquee matchups. “MLW is on a roll, and now it’s time to go bigger,” said MLW Founder and CEO Court Bauer. “We’re not coming back to pay-per-view to play it safe. November 7 is where championships will be decided, rivalries will come to a head, and the best fighters in MLW will be expected to deliver on the biggest stage we’ve had in years. Chicago always brings an incredible atmosphere, and we’re giving that crowd — and fans watching around the world — a night of super fights.” “MLW has built a highly engaged global audience, and Saturday Night SuperFight is the kind of must-see moment fans want to experience as it happens,” said Kyle Heller, Co-Founder and Chief Content Officer of VEEPS. “We’re excited to bring MLW’s return to pay-per-view to fans around the world and give them the opportunity to watch the biggest matches, rivalries, and championship moments unfold live.” MLW’s roster features some of the most recognizable and compelling athletes in professional wrestling, including MLW World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross, Matt Riddle, Místico, Austin Aries, The Good Brothers, CONTRA Unit, and emerging powerhouse ZAMAYA. Matches and championship bouts for Saturday Night SuperFight will be announced in the weeks ahead. MLW and Live Nation’s VEEPS will also collaborate on a collection of limited-edition Saturday Night SuperFight merchandise created exclusively for the event. Additional details about the collection and its availability will be announced soon. MLW Saturday Night SuperFight is executive produced by Court Bauer, Paul Walter Hauser, and Bryan Walsh. Chicago has become one of MLW’s strongest markets, with consecutive sellouts and a passionate fan base that has helped define the league’s success in the city. MLW returns to Cicero Stadium the following night, Sunday, November 8, for an MLW Fusion television taping. Tickets start at $10 and are available at MLWLucha.com.

title: Joe Hendry Comments on Street Fighter Fan Ideas
raw_title: WWE star Joe Hendry reacts to fan social media posts suggesting his inclusion in Street Fighter
summary_src: Joe Hendry addressed the social media posts teasing him portraying Joe in Street Fighter given the same first name and his popularity among wrestling fans.
body: Joe Hendry addressed the social media posts teasing him portraying Joe in Street Fighter given the same first name and his popularity among wrestling fans. In an exclusive interview with TV Insider , Hendry acknowledged seeing fans suggest the idea on social media but explained that he is still developing his skills outside professional wrestling. Hendry also praised Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns for successfully expanding their careers beyond the wrestling ring. “I did see some tweets like that, but the thing is Cody and Roman as two examples who have conquered the world of professional wrestling. They’re so skilled at all things professional wrestling that they are now able to explore these avenues. I’m still building those skills. So I’m very excited to be part of this micro-drama, and that is allowing me to kind of build those skills. But yeah, those guys are on another level, and never say never, but like who knows.” Hendry discussed his role in WWE’s collaborated microdrama with ReelShorts titled Agent of Shadows, and WWE’s latest venture into short-form storytelling. “I had never heard of microdramas before, but I think that the concept is smart. Throughout the history of media, the way people consume content has always depended on storytelling. I think that WWE has often been at the forefront of how that’s done. If you look at the first WrestleMania, for example, the distribution for that, and then the emergence of the WWE Network. WWE has made some real innovations in media. And so to see them cross over into micro-dramas and this format early to me is exciting. It makes a lot of sense to me. When I arrive at an airport, and I see everyone scrolling on their phones, this looks like a useful way for people to consume our storytelling in a way that is convenient and is digestible for them, and keeps them engaged.” The microdrama also features WWE stars Drew McIntyre, Nikkita Lyons, Ethan Page and Jacob Fatu. This is not Hendry’s first venture as he released an exclusive WWE album ‘ Beyond Belief ’ which released on October 10. Hendry discussed his involvement in WWE’s microdrama with ReelShorts called Agent of Shadows. He noted that he had never heard of microdramas before but believes the concept is smart because media consumption has always depended on storytelling. Hendry said WWE has often been at the forefront of innovations in media, citing the first WrestleMania distribution and the emergence of the WWE Network.

He expressed excitement about WWE crossing over into microdramas early, as it allows convenient and digestible storytelling for fans scrolling on their phones at places like airports. This is not Hendry’s first venture outside wrestling, as he released his exclusive WWE album Beyond Belief on October 10.

title: Sol Ruca Sparks Dating Speculation With NXT Star Ricky Smokes
raw_title: Sol Ruca Sparks Dating Speculation With NXT Star Ricky Smokes
summary_src: Sol Ruca and Tyler Bate have been one of WWE’s most well-known couples for years, but something definitely looks different now.
body: Ruca and Bate started dating in September 2023 after meeting through WWE’s NXT division. They weren’t exactly shy about their relationship either, with fans getting plenty of glimpses of the couple together over the years. Fast-forward to October 23, and Ruca’s social media looks very different. She uploaded photos featuring Smokes as the two hung out together, while the photos she previously had with Bate appear to be gone. Bate’s account seems to tell a similar story, with photos of Ruca no longer appearing there either. Neither of them has announced a breakup, but when a longtime wrestling couple suddenly scrubs each other from social media, people are obviously going to notice. Then there’s Smokes. On one of Ruca’s recent posts from Hawaii , he dropped a comment that wasn’t exactly subtle: “Mahalo baby.” Ruca’s response didn’t do much to cool down the speculation, as she said, “;) hi bb” Calling someone “baby” and getting a flirty “hi bb” back is going to get people talking. Throw in Ruca posting Smokes while her photos with Bate have disappeared, and it’s pretty easy to see why fans might wonder whether something has changed in her personal life. That said, nobody involved has actually confirmed anything yet. Ruca and Bate haven’t publicly announced that they’ve broken up, and Ruca hasn’t said she’s dating Smokes, so it would be jumping the gun to officially declare either one. Still, there’s clearly enough happening on social media to raise some eyebrows. After nearly three years of Ruca and Bate being together, the disappearing photos and her cozy exchange with Smokes certainly make this one worth keeping an eye on. title: Match Made: Ranking WWE and AEW's Hottest Storylines From Roman Reigns vs. 946, Sami Zayn to New Level's Rise
raw_title: Ranking WWE and AEW's Hottest Storylines From Roman Reigns vs. 946, Sami Zayn to New Level's Rise
body: Let's face it. Many of us watch a lot of wrestling, and we can't wait to tell anyone who will listen how much we know about our favorite pastime. Some of the best characters know how to break the fourth wall and appeal to savvy fans for the maximum reaction. That's what makes someone like Kevin Owens so relatable or adds background to a rivalry years in the making. It makes us want to discover more about our favorite wrestlers and be a part of the communal experience. With that in mind, these are the hottest storylines in WWE and All Elite Wrestling right now. Jay White's shocking heel turn was the reset that AEW Dynamite needed following WrestleDream. The Bang Bang Gang has been wildly popular since the New Zealand wrestler returned at Forbidden Door. However, the stable has lacked a clear direction for months, and White has struggled to regain momentum as a singles competitor. Conversely, The Death Riders have become fan favorites after Pac's tragic passing and Jon Moxley's touching performance at his tribute show. The group needed a foil, and the newest iteration of The Bang Bang Gang makes perfect sense. This also gives David Finlay and Clark Connors something interesting to do and makes Gabe Kidd an exclusive member of The Death Riders. The three were floundering as a trio, and Kidd fits much better with Mox and his pupils. There's so much potential here. Finlay has a long history with White dating back to their time with New Japan Pro Wrestling, and their Bullet Club lore could eventually lead to a conflict with The Elite. The company capitalized on Owens' long-awaited return at SummerSlam and pivoted to the matchup fans have clamored for since 2023. 20 years of pent-up animosity between the two has set the stage for memorable segments that masterfully blurred the lines between fiction and reality. This entry would rank higher, but the rivalry has admittedly cooled off a little since their Undisputed Championship match and the build to Money in the Bank. Nevertheless, it's still an integral part of SmackDown's world title scene that will likely culminate in a triple threat match with Sami Zayn. Most weeks, their interactions are the best thing on the blue brand. There's still plenty of interest in another one-on-one match or a long-overdue Owens' world title run. "The Honorary Uce" has been linked to The Tribal Chief and The Bloodline since 2022. As such, many fans were disappointed when they never crossed paths after Zayn's first WWE title win at Night of Champions. Fortunately, their upcoming match at Crown Jewel offers a rewarding new chapter to their turbulent friendship. This time, the dynamic has flipped because the Canadian star has carved his own lane as a heel champion, and Reigns refuses to acknowledge his accomplishments. Zayn has been on fire on the microphone since he regained the title, and he held his own in their first war of words. Still, the OTC got the last word in a segment that perfectly encapsulated their history toget

title: On the Record: Sol Ruca Says She’d Love To Turn Heel In WWE Despite Being Told It May Never Happen
raw_title: Sol Ruca Says She’d Love To Turn Heel In WWE Despite Being Told It May Never Happen
body: After WrestleMania 42, Sol Ruca was announced as the newest member of the WWE Raw roster. She wrestled her first match on Raw on the April 20 edition of the show, defeating Liv Morgan. Since then, Ruca has become one of the most popular names on the roster. She’s also had a Women’s Intercontinental Championship reign that lasted 57 days. Ruca made her wrestling debut in 2022 and has worked as a babyface since then. She recently talked about a potential heel turn in the future. During an interview with KRON 4 , Sol Ruca was asked about the possibility of turning heel in the future. Ruca said that she would love to play the role of a heel, but was previously told that she may never get to do so. “I have no idea. I think I would love to be able to try that. I have been told in the past that I most likely will not be heel ever because of just how I am naturally. I am quite a bubbly and liked person.” Ruca says that it would take a “very special person” to bring this side out of her. “So I don’t know. I feel like it’s gonna take a very special person to really get that side out of me, but I guess we’re just gonna have to wait and see.” There have been numerous wrestlers in the past who never turned heel because they were just too over with the fans. But there’s always a chance that WWE could choose to switch things up and eventually introduce a new version of Ruca on television. body: Joe Hendry expanded on his future WWE plans and his focus on cementing himself as the next needle mover in the company. The Raw star told TV Insider that he is always looking to better himself in the ring, and has a firm belief that he can be the next top guy in WWE. Hendry reflected on the numbers and data since his NXT debut, WrestleMania match against Randy Orton and contributions with his WWE album. “I’m just always looking to get better at what I do. I know in my heart that I can be a top draw for WWE. I know people have things to say about that, but the truth is I know that I can be a top guy, I know that I can be an asset to the professional wrestling business because I have the metrics to prove it. And those are facts, you know? I had the most viewed clip in all of wrestling in 2024. I wrestled Randy Orton at WrestleMania, which did insane numbers on social media. My WrestleMania shirt was a bestseller. I won the NXT Championship. I have the metrics to prove that I can draw in the professional wrestling business, and my goal is to be somebody who can deliver for the company.” Hendry also discussed WWE’s expectations for its talent, recalling an interview in which Nick Khan outlined the qualities the company looks for in its performers. The WWE star expressed confidence in his ability to make an immediate or near-future impact, pointing to past metrics as evidence of his potential to become a top star. “I saw in an interview that Nick Khan was asked what WWE is looking for from talent. It is someone that can move the needle for the company immediately or in the near future. I believe that I’m somebody who can do that. I’ve had metrics in the past to prove that I think I can be a top guy for WWE. So I’m looking to acquire the skills to do that as quickly as I can.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. title: Killer Kross Recalls WWE Merger Promise For Acting Opportunities
raw_title: Former WWE Star Killer Kross Recalls Failed Entertainment Industry Promise From TKO
summary_src: Former WWE star Killer Kross (previously known as Karrion Kross) had inquired about getting more involved in Hollywood after a company-wide meeting.
body: Killer Kross' love for film has been something fans have been exposed to through his promos and social media posts, as well as his short film. However, while he's since become an independent filmmaker and actor, Kross claims there was an opportunity to open this door from within WWE. "A couple of years ago, we had this in-house meeting at WWE where, you know, the bosses were there and they were talking about how the merger with TKO was going to provide some sort of transitionary connective tissue into getting into different types of lanes of entertainment," he claimed during an interview on " The Wrestling Classic ." Kross further detailed the meeting, recalling that it was akin to a university lecture, and suggesting that WWE took the topic seriously. He then said that he followed up with WWE after the meeting, making it clear that he didn't want to leave wrestling, but he was interested in branching out into acting. "I have a background in theater and such, and I went into all that and I just said, 'What's the right way to go about doing this?'" Kross stated. Essentially, he wanted to take WWE up on the offer and become an ambassador for the promotion in film, much like Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns have been doing lately. "I was told to follow up in October, and I'd be flown into Los Angeles and they'd introduce me to all these people, ... and I followed up and none of that ever happened," Kross claimed. After following up a second time, he became frustrated with WWE, and went out on his own, producing his own short film in the process and has since continued to expand in film, teasing unreleased projects, as well as another film, "Godshot" that's slated for release soon.
summary: Killer Kross recalled a meeting held inside WWE a couple of years ago where executives discussed how the upcoming merger with TKO would create pathways into other areas of the entertainment industry. He described the session as similar to a university lecture and said the company appeared to take the subject seriously. Kross later followed up with WWE about his theater background and interest in acting while making it clear he did not want to stop wrestling.

raw_title: WWE SmackDown preview (Oct. 23, 2026): Women’s wrestling is taking over WWE SmackDown
summary_src: SmackDown airs tonight (Oct. 23) with a live show emanating from Toyota Arena in Ontario, California. This is the second episode of SmackDown during the four week build to Crown Jewel, which takes place on November 7 and is somehow still scheduled for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. SmackDown airs tonight (Oct. 23) with a live show emanating from Toyota Arena in Ontario, California. This is the second episode of SmackDown during the four week build to Crown Jewel, which takes place on November 7 and is somehow still scheduled for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. I guess that’s because TKO/WWE prioritizes profits and stock price over wrestler safety. WWE typically isn’t afraid to book more than one women’s match on a two hour wrestling television show. In fact, three bouts in the women’s division are currently scheduled for tonight’s episode of SmackDown. First up is Raw star Roxanne Perez challenging WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green for the gold. Roxanne recently beat Chelsea in a non-title match thanks to a minor assist from Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan. Will Liv and the rest of the Judgment Day show up tonight to ensure Roxanne wins the title, thus changing the Crown Jewel women’s match to Morgan vs. Perez? Does Money in the Bank contract holder Tiffany Stratton plan to be at ringside to neutralize any of that interference and/or cash in so she can take Chelsea’s title herself? The next women’s title match on tonight’s card features WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions Alexa Bliss & Tatum Paxley making their first title defense against Michin and B-Fab. It will be a pretty big surprise if Jade Cargill’s Baddies bring home the gold, especially if Charlotte Flair is around to beat the shit out of them and/or Jade for attacking her a couple of weeks ago. Will former tag champs Fatal Influence make a statement to the new champs after the match is over? Last but not least is Giulia vs. Blake Monroe in a Street Fight. This is only The Glamour’s second televised match since she joined the main roster back in April. Will Giulia get her win back from their first bout earlier this month, or can Monroe find the right weapons under the ring to finish off The Beautiful Madness and end their feud? If women’s wrestling is your thing, then it looks like WWE has you covered on tonight’s SmackDown. Bakusai vs. WWE Tag Team Champions MFT is scheduled for tonight in a non-title match. Shinsuke Nakamura and Kyoki pretty much have to win this one if they want to remain viable contenders for the gold. Then again, there aren’t really any other babyface teams on the blue brand, so maybe it doesn’t even matter if they lose. - It isn’t fair to Charlotte Flair that she doesn’t have a championship around her waist. Does The Queen plan to do something about that by challenging Women’s United States Champion Jacy Jayne? - Finn Balor wasn’t around last week, so we got more hi-jinks between Danhausen and Gooner. Will Balor return tonight to smash that shit-eating grin off the Ring General’s face? - GM Nick Aldis says there will definitely be a rematch between CM Punk and Kevin Owens

title: WWE Proceeds With Saudi Arabia Crown Jewel Plans
raw_title: Backstage Update On WWE Taping And Travel Plans Ahead Of Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
summary_src: WWE is going ahead with its plan to host Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia on November 7, but one show ahead of the PLE will likely be taped in advance.
body: WWE WWE is going ahead with its decision to travel to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel, and a report has revealed its plans ahead of the show. Although Saudi Arabia is currently in conflict with the Houthis, with several infrastructure sites, including the airport, reportedly being bombed, WWE remains intent on hosting Crown Jewel in the country on November 7. " PWInsider " has confirmed that the plan is to hold the show in the Middle Eastern country despite the US government issuing a Level 3 travel advisory. The report also noted that a Level 4 advisory would prohibit Americans from traveling to the country. Recently, the US State Department had ordered its diplomats and their family members to leave the country due to the conflict. " Fightful Select " also has an update on Crown Jewel, with its report revealing that WWE plans to tape the "WWE SmackDown" before Crown Jewel on the same day as "WWE Raw" airs from the Barclays Center in New York. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin How to Assess Digital PR Campaign Results for Wrestling Brands By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-20 10:39:00 For a wrestling promotion, a busy news cycle can make a campaign look successful before anyone checks what it achieved. A press release may be picked up, a new show may trend locally, or a talent announcement may circulate across social media. Those signals matter, but how to assess digital PR campaign results depends on connecting attention to a goal: selling tickets, growing an audience, strengthening a brand, or making a new venture credible. Before a campaign begins, decide what it is meant to change. Promoting a live event calls for different measures than announcing a streaming partnership or introducing a new wrestling brand. If the objective is ticket sales, track visits to the event page, ticket referrals and purchases during the campaign period. If the aim is awareness, look at relevant audience reach, branded searches and meaningful coverage in outlets that wrestling fans actually read. Set a baseline as well. Compare results with a similar period, a previous event or the normal level of traffic and engagement. Without that context, a rise in mentions may simply reflect a major show, a viral moment or a news story unrelated to the PR work. Where possible, use tagged campaign links and dedicated landing pages so that referral activity can be distinguished from general traffic. Coverage volume is easy to report, but it is not the same as influence. A list of placements can include duplicate syndication, brief mentions and stories that reach audiences with little interest in the promotion. Review the quality of coverage: Was the key announcement accurately described? Did the story include the information fans need? Was the outlet relevant to the intended audience? Did coverage lead readers to take a next step? For wrestling, context matters. A profile of a rising performer, an interview about a promotion’s community work and a calendar listing for an upcoming event serve different purposes. They should not all be judged by the same standard. A calendar listing might help with local discovery; a thoughtful profile may build a talent’s reputation over time. Record both the placement and its likely role in the broader campaign. A useful report combines a few types of evidence instead of treating one metric as proof of success: Reach: relevant outlets, estimated audience, social sharing and search visibility. Action: ticket purchases, registrations, merchandise activity or inquiries, when these can be attributed responsibly. Reputation: accuracy of coverage, message inclusion, sentiment and the quality of conversations around the announcement. Keep the measurement proportional. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin WWE'S FIRST-EVER MICRODRAMA 'AGENT OF SHADOWS' IS NOW STREAMING, FULL DETAILS ON STORY AND FORMAT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-23 09:19:00 WWE's first-ever Microdrama Agent of Shadows is now streaming on Reelshort. For the uninitiated, a microdrama is a short-form scripted drama designed to tell a story in very small chunks, usually through bite-sized episodes that last anywhere from 1 to 3 minutes. The idea is basically to appeal to the younger Tik Tok/social media type audience. The format has gained a lot of steam internationally in recent years, particularly in China. For Agent of Shadows , there are 72 episodes. The plot - "The world's greatest secret agent must protect and care for his six-year-old daughter while posing as her nanny. Now, without revealing his true identity, he must win his daughter's (and her mother's) trust, while secretly thwarting corrupt suitors, mafioso strongmen, and even a megalomaniacal billionaire who's using his family to get to him." Michael Hayes, Drew McIntyre, Jacob Fatu, Nikkita Lyons, Joe Hendry, Ethan Page and Booker T are among those appearing over the course of the story. We are told that those on both the Reelshort and WWE sides worked hard to slip easter eggs in for the WWE audience, including Booker T's crown from his King Booker run and Drew using one of his actual swords from his ring entrance. body: Michael Hayes recalled a conversation with Triple H where he was informed to mentor Bobby Roode to take over his spot. Hayes told Stephanie McMahon on What’s Your Story? Podcast about his stance to be positioned as the heel in WWE. And how Triple H approached him to train Roode as the next ‘Michael Hayes’. “But yeah, I just made up my mind that this is your new path, and go for it. And I’ll tell you, Trips came up to me one day and he goes, ‘So Michael, you know you’re not gonna be around forever.’ You’re our Pat Patterson. I need you to make Bobby Roode ‘Michael.’” “And I said, ‘Okay, that’s a really good point, because I’m not gonna be here forever.’ And boy, has he come along. No, I see great things for him. He’s just gotta get out of the stuff where, I don’t know how to really categorize it. This stuff happens in this industry that’s just out of your control, and it’s just gonna happen. And you just gotta kind of let it go and say, ‘Okay.’” Roode currently works as a backstage producer for WWE, having transitioned into the role after a neck injury in 2022 forced him to step away from in-ring competition. title: Ilja Dragunov Credits Kofi and Austin Creed for AEW Move
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Says AEW Success Of Ex-WWE Stars The New Level Caught His Attention
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov has discussed the role The New Level, the duo of Kofi and Austin Creed, played in convincing him to join AEW after leaving WWE.
body: AEW Ilja Dragunov is a man with a new sense of freedom after joining AEW, and he has some old friends in WWE, Kofi and Austin Creed, to thank for his decision to switch promotions. Dragunov is the latest star to leave WWE for AEW, debuting in the promotion at WrestleDream , just two months after his WWE exit. The former NXT Champion stated that the success Creed and Kofi, who also debuted in AEW a few months ago, enjoyed immediately after joining the promotion convinced him that signing with Tony Khan's company would be the right move for his career. "I mean, it would be a lie if it wouldn't, right? [That the New Level's success attracted him to AEW] You see people perform in a way that they didn't perform in a while anymore. I can tell, hopefully, or just feel, or can try to imagine a certain happiness if I watch them, what they're doing, and just reconnecting with these people that you shared some time with. You can just tell that it's definitely a new place and something they appreciate [being] a part of," explained Dragunov in his interview with " The Takedown on SI ." The New Level's AEW debut got off to a strong start, as they teamed up with Swerve Strickland to win the Trios Championship on their first night at All In, before losing the titles at WrestleDream. Dragunov's AEW run has had a similar start. Although he didn't win a title, he main-evented " AEW Dynamite " in his in-ring debut, defeating "Speedball" Mike Bailey on the October 21 episode. Dragunov and The New Level were rumored to have left WWE due to contract issues, with The New Level reportedly being asked to take a pay cut of more than 50%.
summary: Ilja Dragunov joined AEW two months after leaving WWE and debuted at WrestleDream. He told The Takedown on SI that the immediate success and renewed performances of his former WWE colleagues Kofi and Austin Creed, known as The New Level, convinced him that AEW was the right destination for his career. Dragunov described feeling their happiness and reconnection in the new environment.

title: Backstage Buzz: TNA Changed Original Creative Plans for October 15 Impact Show
raw_title: TNA Changed Original Creative Plans for October 15 Impact Show
summary_src: Matt Hardy and Jeff Hardy were given some real creative control over the October 15 episode of TNA Impact, but they didn’t get everything exactly the way Matt wanted it.
body: Speaking on The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy , Matt explained that he specifically wanted a tables match as part of the Hardys’ 35th anniversary celebration. Considering how closely he and Jeff have been associated with tables throughout their careers, it felt like an obvious addition. “But in my mind, too, I also wanted to see a tables match. I feel like a tables match is something that, you know, the Hardys are very famous for in this day and age. Obviously, tables, ladders, and chairs — we’re very closely associated with all that.” Once Matt started thinking about who should actually be in the match, he landed on two teams that had caused plenty of problems for the Hardys. His thinking was pretty simple — let their enemies beat the hell out of each other. “And I was like, ‘Huh, who would we put? Who would I put if I was legitimately booking the show?’ I feel like I’d probably book two of our most hated rivals, you know, The Righteous and The Sicks, and maybe they can destroy one another. They’ll do us a favor by just sticking them together in a match.” That’s how The Righteous and The Sicks ended up in the tables match, but Matt’s original vision didn’t stop with simply picking the participants. “And we put those guys in a tables match. And in reality, if I would have formatted the show, I would have put that match before the Ryan and Nic segment, I think, because I really like, if you have an opening segment, have a hot match that people are invested in after that. And I would have probably done The Sicks.” Matt confirmed that was how he’d hoped the episode would actually play out. Instead, Nic Nemeth vs. Ryan Nemeth came immediately after the opening segment, while the tables match happened later in the show. “That’s what I was, yeah. Whenever I was thinking about it, that is kind of how I was hoping to roll it out.” Matt didn’t seem upset that TNA changed things around, though. He figured there may have simply been a production reason for the switch, especially since the tables match needed more time than the Nemeth segment. “But, you know, I don’t know if there was even a difference in the format where they needed a little more time, and the reason it might have been a shorter segment is why they did it.” Matt Hardy also acknowledged that putting the tables match later may have actually given everyone more room to work with. “Because the Ryan and Nic segment wasn’t that long, and we needed more time for that tables match, and they may have had more time if they did it following that.” The Hardys clearly had legitimate input when it came to putting together their anniversary episode, but that didn’t mean they were handed complete control over every minute of Impact. Matt had his preferred running order, while TNA ultimately made some adjustments when it came time to put the final show together.
