title: Comeback Watch: WWE Rumor Claims Sin Cara Character Could Return: 8 Current Stars Who Could Don the Mask, Including Axiom
raw_title: WWE Rumor Claims Sin Cara Character Could Return: 8 Current Stars Who Could Don the Mask, Including Axiom
body: Now, according to PW Insider, there has been a recent push backstage to bring back the character Sin Cara . Mexican star Mistico was under the mask when the character debuted in 2011. Then, when he had creative differences with management, he was replaced by Hunico. The character never really took off with fans, but it is still owned by WWE and can be used by any performer. If WWE does decide to bring the character back, we take a look at seven stars who could be the next Sin Cara. As a tag team, Cruz Del Toro and Joaquin Wilde have showcased some impressive athleticism and skill. However, during stints in Legado del Fantasma and the LWO, they never built a fanbase. Both are still under contract with the company because WWE clearly sees value in them and has used their talents in AAA. If Sin Cars returns, it would not be a surprise if either man were under the mask. NXT star Romeo Moreno is an exciting young talent with potential. The company could continue his development on the black and gold brand over the next couple of years. However, on a pure athleticism level, he would be a good fit to be the new Sin Cara. And because he is only 24, he could work under the mask for the next two decades. A case can be made that Fraxiom is the best tag team on any brand in WWE. However, promoting their tag division continues to be a weakness for the company. So it means that both Axiom and Nathan Frazer will always be in danger of being in the next round of roster cuts unless the company gives them a serious long-term creative push. If that push doesn’t come — and it really should — either man would make a ton of sense as the new Sin Cara. While the assumption would be that that character would be a native of Mexico, the Spanish and English stars’ skill sets are a great fit for the character. Development talent Kale Dixon has been off NXT TV for months due to a rumored injury and after his tag team with Uriah Connors was dissolved. While he is bigger than the two men who previously donned the mantle, he has a ton of athletic talent, is young, and is in creative limbo. Returning to the ring as a very different version of the character makes some sense. French independent star Elio LeFleur saw his debut run in the company curtailed due to a shoulder injury earlier this year. It would make sense to bring him back as the character fans previously saw to give French wrestling fans a favorite star. However, if WWE coaches feel his character was not connecting with the audience, he certainly has the athleticism and wrestling style to be a fun option as the next Sin Cara. One last option to be the new Sin Cara could be Noam Dar. The long-time NXT talent has stuck with the company because he is a reliable veteran talent and teacher. However, he has never gotten an extended opportunity on the main roster. Donning the mask might be his best route, as he would offer the company a performer they can trust to take over the character.
summary: Per PW Insider, now there has been a recent push backstage to bring back the character Sin Cara . If WWE does decide to bring the character back, we take a look at seven stars who could be the next Sin Cara.

title: On the Record: Shayna Baszler Says WWE Door Remains Open Despite Her TNA Wrestling Run
raw_title: Shayna Baszler Says WWE Door Remains Open Despite Her TNA Wrestling Run
summary_src: Shayna Baszler may be collecting championship gold in TNA Wrestling, but that doesn’t mean she’s completely done with WWE.
body: Baszler addressed the situation during a recent interview with Denice Salcedo , where she opened up about her coaching work with WWE following her departure in 2025. While her in-ring career has taken her to TNA, she admitted that helping younger wrestlers develop has become something she genuinely loves. “There’s been some thought because word got out somehow. I’ve been coaching, producing part-time at NXT and Evolve and all that. That is something that I found that I have fallen in love with, watching these young athletes grow and learn to love pro wrestling.” Baszler isn’t looking to give up wrestling just yet, though. She recently joined forces with Zoey Serrano in TNA, making her debut at Bound For Glory earlier this month. The move has given her another opportunity to compete, but she doesn’t believe it necessarily closes the door on her coaching responsibilities in WWE. “TNA is the perfect place for me right now. Thankfully, there’s a good relationship so I can still coach when I’m available. I’m obviously not as available as I was, but that door I guess is still there.” And when it comes to choosing between coaching and getting physical inside the ring, Baszler made it pretty clear where her priorities are right now. She figures she’ll have plenty of time to help younger talent when her wrestling days are behind her. “I can coach when I need a cane and have to sit in a chair. Beating people up right now is what I’m able to do right now, and let’s just ride it till the wheels fall off.” Things got even more interesting when Salcedo asked Baszler directly whether WWE would still allow her to coach if her TNA schedule permitted it. Rather than claiming she had some special arrangement worked out, Baszler gave a simple answer, saying, “Nobody’s told me no.” Baszler also revealed that she didn’t just show up in TNA without considering how WWE might react. Before agreeing to work alongside Serrano, she actually reached out to people whose opinions mattered to her and made sure the move wouldn’t create problems. “To be fair, I did ask people that mattered, ‘Hey, I’m thinking about helping Zoey out. Are there any issues with that?’ Nobody told me not to do it and that I wouldn’t be welcomed back.” That doesn’t mean everything has been officially settled. Baszler acknowledged that her increased responsibilities in TNA could eventually force both sides to revisit how much time she can dedicate to WWE. However, she made it clear that maintaining a positive relationship with the company is important to her. “Now again, there’s maybe some discussion to be had about my availability and all that, and we might have to revisit some of that at some point. I’m not someone that’s going to burn bridges either. I’m very thankful to WWE and everything they did for me and the platform they gave me.” Baszler and Serrano captured the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships at Bound For Glory, giving Baszler a fresh start in the ring. title: Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi eyed for WrestleMania 43
raw_title: Exclusive update on WWE WrestleMania 43 plans
summary_src: In the new issue of the Wrestling Observer Newsletter, Dave Meltzer provided an update on where the WWE WrestleMania 43 plans stand six months out. There is still plenty of time for things to change between now and April 2027, but Roman Reigns vs.
body: There is still plenty of time for things to change between now and April 2027, but Roman Reigns vs. Oba Femi has pretty consistently looked like the direction for one of the WrestleMania 43 main events. Meltzer confirmed that is the case. However, while Cody Rhodes vs. CM Punk would make sense for the other headliner of the two-night event, Meltzer says that is not the current plan. The report does not state which match is currently penciled in as the other main event opposite Reigns vs. Femi. Reigns is currently the World Heavyweight Champion on Raw, while Sami Zayn is the Undisputed WWE Champion on SmackDown. The respective Women’s Champions are Liv Morgan and Chelsea Green (with Green serving as interim champion while Rhea Ripley is out of action). Plans for WrestleMania 42 in 2026 went through a number of changes in the months preceding the event, with injuries playing a particularly big factor. The two main events were Rhodes vs. Randy Orton and Punk vs. Reigns. WrestleMania 43 is taking place from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with April 10-11, 2027 the expected dates . title: On the Record: Joe Hendry Discusses First WWE Microdrama ‘Agent of Shadows’ & Top Guy Aspirations
raw_title: Joe Hendry Talks First WWE Microdrama ‘Agent of Shadows’ & Top Guy Aspirations
body: Say his name, and he appears. Joe Hendry not only can be found Mondays on WWE Raw via Netflix , but in the company’s first ever microdrama Agent of Shadows . The short-form vertical series premieres October 23 under the ReelShort platform. At the center of the story is secret agent Adam Hawke, portrayed by microdrama regular Chase Mattson. Adam goes undercover as a nanny to protect his estranged daughter from a criminal syndicate. Former WWE Champion Drew McIntyre plays Roscoe, his right-hand man and tech expert. Hendry is among the cavalcade of pro wrestling superstars and legends featured including Jacob Fatu, Nikkita Lyons, Michael Hayes, and Booker T . For Hendry, this is another opportunity that has come within a whirlwind year. The viral performer caught fire in TNA Wrestling before securing an official WWE contract. He quickly ascended up the ranks from NXT , looking to reach new heights. We caught up with the Scottish entertainer to talk about what he has been up to and where the entertainer sees himself going. Micro-dramas have really exploded in popularity. What were your first thoughts about WWE collaborating with ReelShort for Agent of Shadows ? Joe Hendry: I had never heard of microdramas before, but I think that the concept is smart. Throughout the history of media, the way people consume content has always depended on storytelling. I think that WWE has often been at the forefront of how that’s done. If you look at the firs t WrestleMania , for example, the distribution for that, and then the emergence of the WWE Network. WWE has made some real innovations in media. And so to see them cross over into micro-dramas and this format early to me is exciting. It makes a lot of sense to me. When I arrive at an airport, and I see everyone scrolling on their phones, this looks like a useful way for people to consume our storytelling in a way that is convenient and is digestible for them, and keeps them engaged. Well, I have the best character. I had to really challenge myself to embrace this role. I, Joe Hendry, play Joe Hendry, the greatest character in all of media. So, yeah, I had fun with it. It looks like a crazy time on set with such a hodgepodge of WWE superstars and legends involved. Take me through what that was like. I’m excited to see Michael Hayes in it because he is a super charismatic person, so it’s cool to see him there. He’s so involved in our shows, it’s cool to see him on this side of the camera again. So I’m excited. That’s the role I’m probably most excited to see as a viewer. But, it was cool to be on set with Drew. title: Bully Ray Picks LA Knight For 946
raw_title: Bully Ray Says One WWE Name Works Best As Next Member Of 946, Dismisses Drew McIntyre
summary_src: 946 need one more member to compete in a WarGames match against The Bloodline at WWE Survivor Series, but Bully Ray argues that it shouldn't be Drew McIntyre.
body: WWE WWE legend Bully Ray has named the wrestler who would be a perfect fit in the 946 faction. It seems that 946 and The Bloodline are on a collision course for a Survivor Series match next month , with the former still needing one more member. Fans have discussed several potential candidates, including Drew McIntyre, whom Ray dismissed as a suitable option. Instead, the Hall of Famer suggested LA Knight as the right pick. "Drew McIntyre is a complete disconnect for 946," Ray began on " Busted Open ." "The real answer is because that's logical, and sometimes people just want to come up with these ideas, like suggesting Drew McIntyre so they can say, 'I suggested Drew McIntyre' if it was ever Drew McIntyre. That feels very, very forced, just as if people say, 'Oh, well, Roman Reigns is going to be with 946.' There's one name that works best — LA Knight. Why? Because it makes sense in the story. And what was the last thing we heard in this story?" The Hall of Famer explained how Knight had stuck with Solo Sikoa on the belief that the latter wouldn't go back to The Bloodline. With Sikoa now once again pledging allegiance to his family , Knight would be aggrieved, which would make sense for him to join 946. "Solo after guaranteeing to LA Knight that he was not going to go back to the Bloodline, said, 'Are we cool?' LA Knight said, 'Yeah,' and then Solo last night went back to the Bloodline, which leads me to believe that LA Knight is not going to be cool, and now LA Knight is going to have to do something about it," he said. Ray proposed a storyline in which Knight would likely have to turn heel if he joined 946, but argued that it wouldn't have to be a definitive heel turn like John Cena's betrayal of Cody Rhodes. He suggested that Knight could argue that Sikoa had forced him to join 946.

Ray instead named LA Knight as the best choice because it aligns with the ongoing story. title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s WrestleMania 43 Main Event Plans Revealed
raw_title: WWE’s WrestleMania 43 Main Event Plans Revealed
summary_src: WWE already has a major WrestleMania 43 match in mind, but fans expecting Cody Rhodes vs. CM Punk might be disappointed. While Roman Reigns vs.
body: “There has been a lot of talk this week that the two main events for WrestleMania in 2027 would be Rhodes vs. Punk on night one and Reigns vs. Femi on night two. From what we were told, the latter is accurate but the former is not the current plan.” Meltzer explained that Rhodes vs. Punk would make sense considering both stars are on SmackDown and WWE has largely kept them apart since their August 1 SummerSlam championship match. That still doesn’t mean the company is planning to pull the trigger. “Rhodes vs. Punk would make sense and I could see the argument for it as they are the two top stars on the Smackdown brand and have been kept apart aside from their 8/1 SummerSlam title match. But right now that is not the plan.” Of course, WWE still has six months before WrestleMania 43, and Meltzer made it clear that nothing is set in stone. Plans have changed plenty of times before, and there’s no guarantee the current direction will stick. “We’re only in October and historically these plans will change multiple times anyway, whether due to injuries or other situations.” Reigns is currently holding the World Heavyweight Championship on RAW, while Sami Zayn is the Undisputed WWE Champion on SmackDown. That leaves plenty of possibilities for how WWE could get to Reigns vs. Femi, especially if the company wants to put a championship on the line. There’s also still no word on what WWE has planned for the other main event. Meltzer didn’t name a replacement for Rhodes vs. Punk, so that part of the WrestleMania card remains a mystery. WrestleMania 43 is expected to take place April 10 and 11, 2027, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. WWE is also scheduled to return to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel on November 7, although ongoing tensions in the Middle East could complicate those plans. WWE and TKO officials have maintained that the event is still moving forward. For now, Reigns vs. Femi appears to be the match WWE wants, while Rhodes vs. Punk is off the table under the current plans. With six months left before WrestleMania, there’s still plenty of time for WWE to change its mind. He said doctors have restricted him to trips lasting no longer than three to four hours, putting Seattle out of reach for the time being. “I Want To Sincerely Apologize To My Agent, Steve Solomon, Washington State Horror Con @wahorrorcon, @bigeventny, And Especially All My Fans In Seattle For Having To Cancel My Scheduled Appearance. “Unfortunately, I Am Dealing With A Blood Clot In My Leg, And My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First.” Flair isn’t downplaying the situation either. The Nature Boy acknowledged that blood clots can become life-threatening and made it clear he’s taking his doctors’ advice seriously. “Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening. We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice.” The good news is that Flair already has a treatment plan in place. He revealed that he’s scheduled for a procedure on the affected vein, which his doctors believe could eventually allow him to travel more freely again. “I’m Scheduled To Have A Procedure To Strip The Affected Vein, Which My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward.” Flair finished by apologizing again to the fans who were expecting to see him in Seattle. Despite his disappointment over having to cancel, he’s putting his recovery ahead of his appearance schedule. “Please Know This Decision Was Not Made Lightly. I Am Truly Sorry For The Inconvenience And Disappointment, And I Am Incredibly Grateful For Your Patience, Understanding, And Continued Support. “I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support. Much Love, Ric Flair” This isn’t Flair’s first serious health concern in recent years. In 2025, he revealed that he was battling melanoma and later dealt with a torn rotator cuff that forced him to leave an AEW Dynamite taping before appearing on the broadcast . For now, Flair’s focus is once again on his health rather than keeping every appearance on his schedule. He’s already got a procedure lined up, and he’s hoping that taking care of the blood clot will eventually get him cleared to hit the road again. title: Who Made the Call to Load Up WWE NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
raw_title: Who Made the Call to Load Up WWE NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
summary_src: WWE is apparently making sure NXT doesn’t walk into its November 4 fight with AEW empty-handed. The show has already been told to load up for its head-to-head battle with Blood & Guts, and now it’s been revealed who allegedly made that call.
body: “NXT would have to load up given they are on an unfamiliar night. Nick Khan allegedly already made that call.” Still, once WWE knew where NXT was landing, apparently nobody wanted to just throw a normal episode out there. Meltzer expects a major angle at Halloween Havoc to help set up the Wednesday show, while AEW already has plenty planned with two Blood & Guts matches. “Besides going head-to-head with AEW, it would also go head-to-head with Main Event and with Evolve. I’d expect a major angle at Halloween Havoc to build to that show, and also expect AEW to load up its show, although it’s already one of AEW’s biggest TV shows of the year with the two Blood & Guts matches.” NXT could still have a tough night in the ratings regardless of what WWE throws at the show. Moving to an unfamiliar night is already a challenge, and going directly against Blood & Guts certainly isn’t going to make things easier. “One would expect NXT to be hurt significantly from the unfamiliar night and competition, but it’s better than being pre-empted in many markets. AEW will be hurt by the competition.” That adds some extra context to Bryan Alvarez’s earlier report that WWE had been told to make the November 4 episode something special. At the time, Alvarez confirmed the head-to-head battle and said NXT had been instructed to bring plenty to the table . “Confirmed that November 4th NXT and AEW are going head-to-head. That’s the Blood and Guts show and NXT was told to load it up.” WWE will actually have three shows running that night, with NXT, EVOLVE and Main Event all overlapping with AEW. That’s a lot of wrestling fighting for attention, but the real battle is obviously going to be NXT walking onto Wednesday night against Blood & Guts. The move may have happened because of election coverage, but WWE clearly isn’t treating November 4 like some throwaway schedule change. Now the big question is just how far the company is willing to go when it comes time to actually load up NXT. title: Austin Creed and Kofi Ink Five-Year AEW Deals
raw_title: Deeper Look At Austin Creed & Kofi's AEW Deals
summary_src: Austin Creed and Kofi, who debuted in AEW at All In, look set to remain with the promotion for a long time, as details of their contract lengths emerge.
body: AEW Austin Creed and Kofi seem to be planning to stay in AEW for the long run as new details emerge about the length of their contracts. Creed and Kofi debuted in AEW at All In and got off to a strong start, winning the Trios Championship alongside Swerve Strickland. A few weeks into their AEW run, " Fightful Select " reported that the duo had signed five-year deals with Tony Khan's promotion. Strickland reportedly played a significant role in bringing them to AEW, with Khan initially reluctant to approach the celebrated tag team duo while they were still under contract with WWE. Teaming with Strickland was also one of the first ideas that they were pitched before their AEW debut. The trio, who lost the Trios Championship to "Hangman" Adam Page and Brodido at the recent WrestleDream pay-per-view, weren't scheduled to hold the titles for long, as per the same report. It's well known that Khan doesn't skimp on purchasing music rights for his wrestlers' entrances, despite the high costs . He did the same for The New Level, who used A$AP Ferg's "New Level" as their entrance theme, with the aforementioned report stating that the song was approved on the day of All In. The report claimed that the delay was due to waiting for approval from Sony, which owns RCA Records, the label that released the song. Creed had revealed in an interview that they had less than a week to secure the rights to use the song, and had to speak to someone who knew A$AP Ferg's manager to get the deal over the line.
summary: Per Fightful Select, Austin Creed and Kofi signed five-year contracts with AEW. Swerve Strickland played a key role in recruiting the duo from WWE, and teaming with him was one of the first concepts presented to them. The group won the Trios Championship at All In but lost the titles to Hangman Adam Page and the Briscoes at WrestleDream, as they were not planned to hold the belts long-term.

body: On Wrestlers Being Afraid Of Getting Heat: “It was like that around there. It really does, because I guess I’ve been willing to get fired a lot of times as far as the business goes. “The only thing I always said is, ‘The only thing you can do is fire me.’ And when I hear guys talk like that, man, it really hurts me. ‘I couldn’t stand up because that guy had more stroke than I did, and I could get fired.’ You end up getting fired anyway. So why not tell somebody to go take a hike or go jump in the lake? When I really want to get my point across, I say go jump in a lake.”

title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Still Set for Riyadh
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Is Confirmed For Riyadh (For Now)
body: WWE now finds itself between a rock and a hard place with tensions increasing in the middle east less than a month before the promotion is set to travel to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel. There was no mention of the PLE during WWE Money in the Bank earlier this month, but recent updates suggest WWE will still make the trip. "Right now, everything is still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far so good. Nothing's been cancelled," said TKO CEO Ari Emanuel during a Fox News appearance (h/t Cagesideseats.com. ) "We have a whole team kind of working on this, and if that doesn't happen, where we can move it. It's a daily monitoring." Turki Alalshikh, chairman of Saudi's General Entertainment Authority and co-founder of Zuffa Boxing with WWE parent company TKO, recently tweeted "Hard times reveal true friends," seemingly putting the pressure on promotions like WWE to move forward with current plans to travel to Riyadh. On the morning of October 13, 2026, WWE Chief Content Officer Paul Levesque took to X to post a Crown Jewel poster, confirming the event was to commence live from Riyadh on November 7, 2026. This week, the United States ordered diplomats to leave Saudi Arabia amid fears of escalating attacks. Where to Watch/Stream: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is available on ESPN Unlimited in the United States. Crown Jewel can be viewed internationally through Netflix. Though WWE is still planning its trip to Saudi Arabia, backup plans have reportedly made as was confirmed by Emanuel. As of this writing, the backup city is undisclosed. "They're going to cancel when they feel there's no hope," said Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio. (h/t Yahoo! ) "Nobody wants to go, I mean let's be serious, nobody wants to go right now. Everyone knows the situation, it's high alert for people, no one is advised to go there right now. Most likely, the show will be moved but they're not going to say anything until there's no hope and whatever, and that may be this week. I mean they may look at that and go 'There's no hope.' But they'll fight it until whenever they make the decision, but I mean yeah, it ain't looking good, it ain't looking good at all but they're not going to say anything. They're not going to say anything until the day they say it isn't happening. Could be any day now, they may hold out later." WWE's partnership with Saudi Arabia, while never short of controversy and strife , is one of its most lucrative partnerships with the industry leading promotion getting an estimated $50 million from Saudi Arabia per show as part of a 10-year agreement signed in 2018. WWE Royal Rumble 2026 was held in Saudi earlier this year at a staggering price of $100 million , while WrestleMania 43 is currently planned for 2027 as part of an reported $250 million deal. WWE has not yet announced a date for WrestleMania 43, which is rare given the promotion typically announces its WrestleMania date a y
summary: WWE remains scheduled to hold Crown Jewel in Riyadh amid rising Middle East tensions. TKO CEO Ari Emanuel confirmed that the November event is currently proceeding as planned while a team monitors the situation daily. Saudi General Entertainment Authority chairman Turki Alalshikh posted a message seemingly urging partners including WWE to follow through with commitments.

title: World X Cup and Dual Ultimate X Bouts Set for TNA Destination X
raw_title: World X Cup and Ultimate X matches added to TNA Destination X
summary_src: A World X-Cup Tournament and two Ultimate X matches are among the additions to TNA’s Destination X event next month.
body: A World X-Cup Tournament and two Ultimate X matches are among the additions to TNA’s Destination X event next month. On Thursday’s edition of Impact, TNA revealed that the World X-Cup would take place at the November 15 event and feature eight wrestlers from various countries. The eight will be divided into pairs for fatal four-way matches, with the two winners meeting later in the night. The X Cup concept has appeared in various forms since 2003, when it debuted as the Super X Cup and was won by Chris Sabin. The inaugural World X Cup was held the following year with a Team U.S. vs. Team Canada theme, with follow-ups in 2006 and 2008. Two Ultimate X matches will take place at Destination X. The men’s match will determine the next contender for the X Division championship held by Amazing Red. The Knockouts’ version will determine the next contender for the Knockouts Championship belonging to Indi Hartwell.
summary: TNA announced on Impact that its November 15 Destination X event will include a World X-Cup Tournament featuring eight international wrestlers split into fatal four-way matches with the victors clashing in the final. Two Ultimate X matches were also added, with the men's bout crowning the next X Division title challenger to Amazing Red and the Knockouts version determining the next challenger to Indi Hartwell's Knockouts Championship. The X Cup format dates back to 2003 and has been held in various iterations since.

Santino Marella revealed that the card will include two Ultimate X matches, one for the men and one for the women.

The winner of the men's Ultimate X will earn a future shot at the X Division Championship currently held by Amazing Red. The women's Ultimate X winner will receive a title opportunity against Knockouts Champion Indi Hartwell. The World X-Cup tournament is also returning to Destination X and will feature eight international wrestlers divided into two fatal four-way matches.

The winners of those fatal four-way matches will then compete in a final later that same night to crown the World X Champion. The World X-Cup concept first appeared in 2003 as the Super X Cup, which was won by Chris Sabin, with the inaugural World X Cup taking place the following year.
The most recent World X-Cup prior to this return was held in 2021, with past tournament winners including Samoa Joe, Dezmond Xavier and Ace Austin.

title: WWE Survivor Series WarGames To Feature 5v5 Teams
raw_title: Backstage News On Number Of Participants For WWE Survivor Series Men's WarGames Match
summary_src: The WWE WarGames match will once again feature five wrestlers per team at Survivor Series, with a report revealing the potential lineups.
body: WWE This year's Survivor Series will feature a WarGames match, with five wrestlers from each team set to compete against each other. With the 2026 Survivor Series fast approaching, speculation is mounting about the WarGames match and who could be involved. " Fightful Select " reports that this year's WarGames match will feature five wrestlers on each team, with The Bloodline likely to face off against the 946 faction, led by Royce Keys. So far, only four wrestlers from each group have been involved in the storyline between the two factions. The Keys-led faction consists of Keys himself, OTM, and Carmelo Hayes. Meanwhile, The Bloodline comprises Roman Reigns, the group's de facto leader, The Usos, and Solo Sikoa, who recently reunited with his family. Jacob Fatu could likely join the four stars, while Sami Zayn — who recently featured alongside Reigns — could be another option. There is no indication yet as to who will be the fifth member of 946. Since being introduced to the main roster in 2022, The Bloodline have featured prominently in the WarGames match, competing at Survivor Series 2022 and Survivor Series 2024, emerging victorious on both occasions. Last year's men's WarGames match saw The Vision get the better of a team that included The Usos and Reigns, as well as Cody Rhodes and CM Punk. Survivor Series 2026 will take place in Houston, Texas, on November 28, and no matches have been announced for the show yet.
summary: This year's WWE Survivor Series will include a men's WarGames match with five wrestlers on each side. Per Fightful Select, The Bloodline is expected to battle a faction led by Royce Keys known as 946. So far only four members from each group have been active in the storyline, with Jacob Fatu and Sami Zayn among the possible additions for The Bloodline while the fifth man for 946 remains unclear.

title: Ari Emanuel Weighs In On the Status of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
raw_title: Ari Emanuel Comments on the Status of WWE Crown Jewel 2026
body: TKO Executive Chairman Ari Emanuel recently commented on the status of WWE Crown Jewel. There has been a lot of speculation around the status of WWE Crown Jewel due to heightened tensions in the Middle East. Earlier this week, the US State Department cautioned Americans in the Middle East to “exercise heightened vigilance.” On Thursday, another security alert was issued, this time by the US Embassy in Riyadh, urging Americans to take extreme caution when using airports in Saudi Arabia. TKO boss Ari Emanuel was asked about the status of WWE Crown Jewel during his recent appearance on Fox News . Emanuel said nothing’s canceled as of now. “Right now, everything is still set. This weekend, coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have, in the middle of November, a Freeze Art Show. So far, it’s good. Nothing has been canceled.” When asked if TKO and WWE were getting briefed by the US government and whether the show would be canceled in any circumstance, Emanuel said: “Yeah, we have a whole team working on this, and kind of when, if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” As things stand, Crown Jewel is scheduled to take place on November 7. 411Mania will provide the latest updates on its status when they are available.
summary: There has been a lot of speculation around the status of WWE Crown Jewel due to heightened tensions in the Middle East. TKO boss Ari Emanuel was asked about the status of WWE Crown Jewel during his recent appearance on Fox News .

title: Conrad Thompson Targets Podcasts With Heyman and Hayes
raw_title: Conrad Thompson Wants To Do Podcasts With Paul Heyman And Michael Hayes
body: Conrad Thompson wants to reshape the way people think about Michael Hayes. Thompson’s podcast network is already loaded with huge names like Jeff Jarrett, Tony Schiavone, Eric Bischoff, Jim Ross, and JBL. As it turns out, there are two white whales that Thompson is still chasing. “ Obviously Paul Heyman would be a big white whale for me, as would Michael Hayes.” Conrad Thompson told Fightful in a new interview. “Michael Hayes would not only give you the territory stuff, but he could give you the WCW stuff, look at this really long uninterrupted run behind the scenes in WWE. He’s not very online and, obviously, that’s by design. So if you could actually hear him in his natural state, just talking wrestling, there’s a reason he’s been so successful and been with WWE for so long. I think that the narrative out there maybe doesn’t give him full credit for that. So I would love to reshape the way people think about Michael Hayes one day.” Continuing his praise of Hayes, Thompson highlighted his involvement in some of the most pivotal moments in wrestling history. “That’s unprecedented and the idea that he was behind the scenes in a major way, in on a lot of really critical moments in history, he’s in the room where it’s being discussed for the first time. I think he could be tremendous and clearly he’s a natural entertainer. He knows how to spice it up. So I think the genre will welcome him whenever he’s ready.” Also, head over to our YouTube channel to check out more of our recent interviews.
summary: Conrad Thompson told Fightful he is still pursuing two major podcast guests: Paul Heyman and Michael Hayes. Thompson, whose network already features Jeff Jarrett, Tony Schiavone, Eric Bischoff, Jim Ross and JBL, believes a conversation with Hayes would highlight his long behind-the-scenes contributions in WCW and WWE while reshaping public perception of him. He noted Hayes is rarely online by design and praised the executive's unprecedented involvement in key wrestling history.

title: Results Recap: STARDOM To The World 2026 : Suzu Suzuki retains in No DQ war, Triangle of Madness defend trios titles
raw_title: STARDOM To The World 2026 Results: Suzu Suzuki retains in No DQ war, Triangle of Madness defend trios titles
body: Suzu Suzuki walked through a bloody, weapon-heavy path to retain her World of STARDOM Championship on Saturday night. Going 23 minutes against HATE faction leader Natsuko Tora, Suzuki was able to retain her world title in the main event of STARDOM To The World 2026, which took place at the Yokohama Budokan. Suzuki, known for her background in deathmatch wrestling, was able to fight within her own wheelhouse this weekend, facing Tora in a no disqualification matchup. However, it didn’t feel like a one-on-one bout at times, as Tora was able to lean on run-in attacks and assistance from HATE teammates to help her regain control of the bout. The lengthy main event included tons of plunder. Both women were cut open around the forehead early on following the use of a barbed wire baseball bat. Suzuki and Tora took turns using a staple gun on each other at one point, and Suzuki had to battle through a blinding blue mist to the eyes. Chairs, tables and ladders were all utilized as well. Tora looked as though she was closing in on a huge win late, connecting with a huge Death Valley Driver then wrapping chain around her hand for a lariat. But Suzuki countered the move, connected with her Tequila Shot, then a pair of Bridging German Suplexes. The champ arranged a pile of chairs in the ring and landed a third Bridging German Suplex, finally earning her the pinfall victory. Tora, who had a brief 34-day run with the title in 2024, was looking to join a short list of wrestlers to have carried the STARDOM world title twice. Tam Nakano, Mayu Iwatani, and Io Shirai remain the only names who have achieved such an accomplishment. Saturday was Suzuki’s first time defending the title since STARDOM wrapped up its 5Star Grand Prix tour this summer. Between her showing this week, plus outings against Sayaka Kurara and Utami Hayashishita in June, Suzuki has delivered big performances as champ. The champ took quite the beating early on from Sohrei, who had a hot start to the fight. Hanan would often find an opening and connect with a big move, only to have that momentum thwarted by Sohrei moments later. The match became much closer in the second half and, by the end, went the way of the champ. After kicking out at one from a powerbomb, Hanan went on a huge run of moves to retain: A bridging fallaway slam, busaiku knee, then a trio of bridging backdrop suplexes for the pinfall victory. Saturday’s co-main event felt like the best championship showing from Hanan since she captured the belt in April by beating Konami. Previous title matchups included wins over Saya Iida and Bea Priestley. After the match, Hanan was challenged by HATE’s Ruaka. title: Conrad Thompson Denies AEW Ties or Clickbait in Roman Reigns Critique
raw_title: Conrad Thompson denies his Roman Reigns criticism driven by AEW or clicks
summary_src: Conrad Thompson appeared on the Fightful Wrestling podcast this week, and the conversation inevitably turned to his ongoing beef with Roman Reigns.
body: The mortgage broker and podcaster was asked by Fightful ’s Sean Ross Sapp about Reigns saying during a recent appearance on the Club Shay Shay podcast that Thompson was using his name to get views for his shows. The WWE World Heavyweight Champion also insinuated Conrad was attacking him because of ties he may have to AEW. According to Thompson, he wasn’t looking to increase his ratings nor does he have any allegiance to AEW. As he pointed out, he’s friends with multiple people employed by WWE, including his sister-in-law, Charlotte Flair. Thompson’s critiques of Reigns caused a stir among wrestling fans in early August when he called the champ “the most overrated main eventer in WWE history” during an episode of 83 Weeks , the podcast he co-hosts with Eric Bischoff. He continued defending his position on his various podcasts, including on the September 25th episode of Something to Wrestle , which he hosts with John Bradshaw Layfield. During that show, he once again called Reigns overrated, before stating: “It’s also true that never have I ever seen a Roman Reigns T-shirt out in the wild. Not once.” Thompson later appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show and broke down why he feels Reigns is an “ industry plant .” “They [WWE] forced him to be on top and to always win over and over and over,” Thompson said to Helwani. “I give you the longest entrance. I let you go on last. You’re always the main event, and you always win. Well, I think that formula would work for pretty much anybody.” Conrad also said on Helwani’s show: “AEW is making wrestling for fans, and I think WWE is making wrestling for investors.” During the October 14 episode of Club Shay Shay , host Shannon Sharpe asked Reigns if he was bothered by Thompson’s attacks. “No, because the truth is, are there a lot of people watching that guy’s show? So, you’re gonna say stuff,” Reigns replied. “You already know I’m a metric mover. They know I give views and all that stuff. So, it’s fine. It is what it is.” The OTC then seemingly insinuated Thompson’s motivation was related to connections he has elsewhere. “If you look at the guy’s background, you already know where his support system — You know what I mean? All you got to do is scroll a little bit, and you see who he’s a fan of and stuff like that, and who he’s connected to,” Reigns said. “But no, if they want to use my name to get views, that’s the industry right now.” Though Reigns didn’t outright say it, Thompson has been linked to AEW in the past. His Starrcast fan conventions have been aligned with AEW events, and he co-hosts podcasts with AEW personalities Jim Ross and Tony Schiavone. However, Conrad has previously denied having any official deal with Tony Khan’s promotion. Thompson told Sapp that he’s been surprised by all the attention he’s received for his comments. “I shared my opinion about Roman — that I was ready for something new. And then everyone else started talking about it. And that’s what I kind of found so silly is if my opinio
summary: Conrad Thompson told Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp that his criticism of Roman Reigns was not motivated by a desire for more views or any connection to AEW. title: WrestleMania 43 Main Event Plans in Doubt
raw_title: Expected WWE WrestleMania 43 Main Event May Not Happen After All
body: Though WWE is roughly half a year from WrestleMania 43, there have been strong indications across Raw and SmackDown that Oba Femi will challenge Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship while Punk would battle Rhodes, presumably for SmackDown's WWE Championship. Cody Rhodes Admits WWE Fans Have 'Cody Fatigue'—Here's Why He Should Turn Heel After Reigns recently defeated both LA Knight and Penta in separate marquee world title defenses, Reigns vs. Femi, barring an injury, appears to be a virtual lock for WrestleMania 43 next April in Saudi Arabia. There are, however, plenty of indications that Punk vs. Rhodes isn't a lock at all. Despite multiple recent teases of Rhodes vs. Punk II on both Raw and SmackDown, the WWE Championship scene on the blue brand is much more complicated than what's going on with Reigns. Namely, current WWE Champion Sami Zayn seems to have a smorgasbord of challengers lined up, all of which could drastically alter the WWE title picture. Among the key ones? His longtime nemesis Kevin Owens, Randy Orton, Gunther and Penta, the current holder of the Money in the Bank briefcase. Penta is the real wild card here. The former AEW star has taken WWE by storm in recent months after a stellar world title match against Reigns in Mexico City. That bout propelled Penta to winning the coveted MITB match, which he was not originally slated to win. Even more, Penta's virtual overnight success has WWE rethinking its plans for some of its Mexican-born stars and even considering bringing back the old Sin Cara character to capitalize on Penta's recent success. There is certainly a world in which Penta cashes in prior to WrestleMania 43, defeats Zayn, wins the WWE title and then defends it in the Mania event. There is also the potential for Penta to "call his shot" and challenge for the title at WrestleMania itself, where he could potentially win it in the show's headliner. While virtually no match will be bigger than Reigns vs. Femi on the SmackDown side, there are so many moving pieces in the blue brand's world title picture that Punk vs. Rhodes is far from a certainty, as should be the case. Perhaps Zayn holds onto the title and battles his friend-turned-foe Owens one more time in the WrestleMania Saturday main event. Maybe the Royal Rumble winner chooses to face SmackDown's WWE Champion and ends up main-eventing Night One of WrestleMania. Maybe a wild card like Orton becomes WWE Champion prior to WrestleMania. Although Femi vs. Reigns is the best and most obvious direction on Raw, there's no need to rush into Punk vs. Rhodes, which just happened at SummerSlam anyway, if there's not an intriguing story to tell. And if WWE refuses to turn Rhodes heel, then there's no reason to run back Punk vs. Rhodes, no matter how big it sounds on paper.
summary: WWE appears set for Roman Reigns to defend the World Heavyweight Championship against Oba Femi at WrestleMania 43. However the expected Cody Rhodes versus CM Punk match for the WWE Championship is far from certain with Sami Zayn facing a crowded field of potential challengers including Kevin Owens, Randy Orton, Gunther and Penta.

title: Ari Emanuel Confirms WWE Crown Jewel Still On In Saudi Arabia
raw_title: TKO's Ari Emanuel Comments On Status Of WWE Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on November 7. TKO's Ari Emmanuel appeared on FOX News to discuss the situation.
body: WWE is moving ahead with holding Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia despite the enormous risks it's taking in doing so. The show is scheduled for November 7 and will take place amidst an ongoing conflict with the Houthis that has recently targeted several airports in Saudi Arabia, resulting in multiple deaths and injuries. The U.S. government recently ordered its diplomats and their families to leave the country as it also advises Americans not to travel to Saudi Arabia. TKO's Ari Emmanuel appeared on Fox News on Thursday to confirm that "everything's all set" with holding the show in Saudi Arabia. UFC has an upcoming show in Abu Dhabi that's still scheduled to take place. "Nothing's been canceled. (...) We have a whole team kind of working on this and if that doesn't happen, where we can move it. It's a daily monitoring," Emmanuel stated. WWE will be taping the "SmackDown" before Crown Jewel on November 2 , following the episode of "Raw" that will air at 6 PM ET. That show will take place at the Barclays Center in New York. On November 9, "Raw" will emanate from Columbia, South Carolina. Two matches have already been announced for Crown Jewel . Dave Meltzer explained that TKO has a financial incentive to hold the show as scheduled in Riyadh. He also said they risk losing WrestleMania 43 in Riyadh if they move Crown Jewel.
summary: TKO's Ari Emanuel stated that everything is set for WWE Crown Jewel on November 7 in Riyadh despite the ongoing regional conflict with the Houthis and recent U.S. government travel warnings. He noted a team is monitoring the situation daily and that nothing has been canceled, with UFC's Abu Dhabi event also proceeding as planned. WWE will tape SmackDown on November 2 at Barclays Center in New York following that night's Raw before heading to Columbia, South Carolina for the November 9 Raw.

title: Comeback Watch: Road Dogg Makes In-Ring Return After 11 Years
raw_title: Road Dogg Makes In-Ring Return After 11 Years
summary_src: Road Dogg actually did it. After more than 11 years without an official match, the WWE Hall of Famer stepped back into the ring at Jeff Jarrett’s All-Star Super Slam on October 22 and officially ended his decade-plus wrestling drought.
body: My World with Jeff Jarrett took to Twitter and confirmed Road Dogg competed at the Hendersonville Pig Fest event while celebrating the show on Twitter the following day. Road Dogg teamed with Jarrett and Jay Lethal for the special anniversary match. “Last night @RealJeffJarrett’s All-Star Super Slam was a SMASH HIT! 💥 Huge thanks to everyone who was part of such a special night at the Hendersonville Pig Fest!” The match saw Road Dogg, Jarrett and Lethal take on QT Marshall, Elijah Drago and Brady Booker. It was part of a show celebrating Jarrett’s 40 years in professional wrestling, but Road Dogg’s return ended up giving fans another pretty big milestone to celebrate. That’s because Road Dogg hadn’t officially wrestled since January 25, 2015. His previous match came at WWE Royal Rumble, where he teamed with Billy Gunn as the New Age Outlaws in a loss to The Ascension. The comeback is even more surprising considering what Billy Gunn said about his longtime tag team partner earlier this year. While discussing the possibility of another New Age Outlaws reunion, Gunn made it sound like Road Dogg’s physical condition meant another match simply wasn’t happening . The event itself featured plenty of other madness, including a Concession Stand Brawl, a Micro Madness Match, a Lucha Libre Showcase and the appropriately named Pigfest 10-Man Gauntlet Battle Boar-Yal. Still, Road Dogg wrestling again after more than a decade away was always going to be one of the night’s biggest surprises. What started as an unexpected comeback announcement is now officially in the books. After 11 years spent working around the wrestling business without competing, Road Dogg finally reset the clock and proved he could still get back inside the ring one more time. summary_src: Penta is amazed by the WWE Money in the Bank briefcase win and has explained his plans for his cash-in.
body: WWE WWE's Penta is still in disbelief over winning the men's Money in the Bank match and has explained his plans for the cash-in. The Mexican star has been on a roll in WWE over the last few months, starting with his impressive performance in a match against Roman Reigns before winning the Money in the Bank briefcase . In an interview with " Busted Open ," Penta said he understands the responsibility that comes with holding the briefcase, particularly when it comes to being a role model for young fans. "Sometimes I can't believe what happened. At the same time, I know what is my responsibility now in this business, you know? Because every time more children go to me, every child uses my t-shirt, my mask, say Cero Miedo , can't say in Spanish, but he tries. When I saw that, it's like, 'Okay, I know now my responsibility with the crowd,'" he said. "As for the briefcase, I actually feel like I have the fu**ing power in my hands, basically, because at one time, I don't know where, I don't know when, but when I feel in my soul it's the perfect time for cash in, I will, you know?" The Money in the Bank holder admitted that he hasn't yet decided on whom he would cash in his briefcase, the WWE World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns, or the WWE Champion Sami Zayn. He stated that he wants to enjoy his time with the briefcase and the extravagant presentation that comes with it. "So now I start thinking sometimes Roman [Reigns], you know, Sami [Zayn], I don't know. Because it's my first time, but at the same time, I wanna do the best to get the World Championship, you know? But for now, I enjoy every presentation with my briefcase, with fire [pyro], you know, everything involved about it," he added. Penta recently came face-to-face with both champions, Reigns and Zayn, on "Raw" before facing Bron Breakker, whom he defeated to maintain his momentum following his Money in the Bank win.

title: On the Record: Ray Petree
raw_title: Ray Petree | Revisiting the Toni Storm vs. Mariah May ‘Hollywood Ending’
body: In the years since the global COVID-19 pandemic , the word “cinematic” has infiltrated professional wrestling nomenclature. The sentiment, shared by the likes of Roman Reigns and Paul Heyman, implies that professional wrestling can ascend to a higher plane of existence. Professional wrestling isn’t prestige television, nor is it the Marvel Cinematic Universe. It’s an art form unto itself that tells its tales through the catharsis of combat. In their self-styled “Hollywood Ending,” Toni Storm and Mariah May tackled that sentiment. This match was recommended to me by KELSON , from AEW Fan Hub. If you’d like to recommend me a match to me, please email me at [email protected] This match works on two levels: as a standalone match and within its greater context. The context being that this is the end of a trilogy of wars waged over the women’s world championship, cleverly weaving in elements from their 14-month-long saga. It’s also the sixth match in a pay-per-view rife with grudge matches, many of which suffer from the aforementioned imperfect storm: the bloat of “lore” and an inability to exercise brevity. “Hangman” Page could have settled his score with MJF using Christopher Daniels’ Angel’s Wing , but he opted to punctuate the affair with a Buckshot Lariat . Swerve Strickland could have put Ricochet away with a Vertebreaker through the table and the subsequent House Call , but chose to enter a second finishing stretch instead. Kyle Fletcher couldn’t meet his comeuppance with a Spanish Fly from the top of the cage, followed by the Hidden Blade , because Will Ospreay wanted to kill him with the Tiger Driver ‘91 . It’s a classic example of Chekhov’s Gun misfiring. All too often, AEW’s pay-per-view spectacles fail to eliminate what’s inessential. Narrative elements are either totally absent or blatantly overused, bereft of any subtlety. Of all the matches on this show, it’s this no-holds-barred, falls-count anywhere match that improbably finds the common sense that exists somewhere in the middle. May famously betrayed Storm at the top of the entryway, shortly after she won the Owen Hart Foundation Tournament. That’s precisely where this match begins and, ultimately, where it ends. Everything in between carries with it that same keen attention to detail. Storm using the “shoe,” May’s champagne celebration, Storm whipping May with the championship belt… It all feels pertinent. Even when Storm and May steal each other’s finishing maneuvers, it doesn’t feel self-indulgent, because they’ve both quite literally portrayed the other. What they managed to accomplish in fewer than 13 minutes is astonishing, drawing from 14 months’ worth of television in a way that feels organic and purposeful. The only thing this match could be accused of exercising an excess of is blood, which Storm spills profusely. title: Big E Marries Kristen Yim With Stars From Multiple Promotions Attending
raw_title: WWE's Big E Gets Married, With Wrestlers In Attendance
body: Congratulations are in order for WWE's Ettore "Big E" Ewen and Kristen Yim as the happy couple officially married on Wednesday. According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer, wrestlers from WWE, AEW, and TNA were in attendance for the pair's wedding, including Mia Yim, Seth Rollins, Becky Lynch, Kofi, and Austin Creed (formerly Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods). As seen on his Instagram stories , WWE broadcaster Peter Rosenberg also attended, with the dance floor becoming a hot spot for him and his peers. Big E and Kristen, the sister of WWE star Mia Yim, went on their first date at the premiere of Montez Ford and Bianca Belair's Hulu show "Love & WWE" in early 2024. In the "The Player's Tribune," Big E revealed that he and his now-wife had been communicating via direct message before arranging to hang out at the premiere. It was there that Big E then became truly enamored. "I just felt an energy with Kristen I'd never felt before," Big E wrote. "We were at this premiere with all these beautiful people, all these famous actors and entertainers, and none of them even registered. For me, there was only one other person in the room that night. And what's crazy is, I knew I wanted to see her more after that." After more than a year of dating, Big E and Kristen got engaged in May 2025 , with the former proudly touting that he "couldn't wait" to be the latter's husband. Since sustaining a neck injury in 2022, Big E has taken a giant step back from in-ring competition. He remains signed to WWE as an on-screen host and talent scout, however.

Swerve Strickland appeared without Kingston and Creed during a backstage segment with the new AEW World Trios Champions, “Hangman” Adam Page and Brodido. Strickland demanded a rematch after his team lost the titles, and Page agreed that they deserved another opportunity. Swerve then called for the match to happen at Full Gear before trying to turn things considerably more personal. Strickland brought up his violent history with Page and demanded that the Trios Championship rematch be held under Texas Death rules. Page immediately rejected that stipulation because he knew Swerve’s request wasn’t really about the championships. The wrestling story will still be waiting for The New Level when they return, but Big E’s wedding was obviously a night Kingston and Creed weren’t going to miss. After everything the three experienced together during their WWE run, their friendship clearly extends well beyond whichever company logo happens to be on their paycheck. title: Another Major Event in Saudi Arabia Postponed as New Missile Attack Raises WWE Crown Jewel Concerns
raw_title: Another Major Event in Saudi Arabia Postponed as New Missile Attack Raises WWE Crown Jewel Concerns
summary_src: WWE’s Crown Jewel plans in Saudi Arabia are facing even more questions after another major international event in Riyadh was postponed and a ballistic missile targeting the city was intercepted Friday morning.
body: On October 23, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Statistics announced that the United Nations World Data Forum and Second Saudi Statistical Forum, scheduled for November 9 through November 12 in Riyadh, have been pushed back to 2027. That’s just two days after WWE is supposed to hold Crown Jewel at Riyadh Season Stadium on November 7. According to Reuters , Saudi officials said the decision was made to ensure international participation and deliver a successful event. They did not specifically blame security concerns for the postponement. This is now the second major international event in Riyadh to get pushed back. Saudi Arabia’s Future Investment Initiative conference, originally scheduled for October 26 through October 29, was also postponed until 2027. And the security situation isn’t getting any better. Early Friday morning, Saudi air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile heading toward Riyadh shortly after 4 a.m. local time. Officials also confirmed another missile was intercepted near Khamis Mushait, along with two drones targeting southern Saudi Arabia. No casualties or damage were reported from the latest interceptions. The developments come just one day after the U.S. Embassy warned Americans to use extreme caution at Saudi airports . The October 22 alert stated that operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh remained suspended following attacks on airports and other infrastructure. That creates another problem for WWE, which still has to get its wrestlers, production crew and equipment into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. TKO executive Ari Emanuel addressed the situation during an interview with Fox News earlier this week. Despite the security concerns, he maintained that the company’s upcoming events were still moving forward. “Right now, everything’s still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far, so good. Nothing’s been canceled.” Emanuel also confirmed that TKO has people evaluating the situation and looking at possible alternatives in case events can’t take place as scheduled. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” That’s especially important now that two major events in Riyadh have already been postponed. WWE hasn’t announced any changes to Crown Jewel, but TKO is clearly preparing for the possibility that plans may need to change. For now, Crown Jewel remains scheduled for November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium. WWE hasn’t announced a postponement or relocation, and there’s no confirmation that the company has decided to move the show. title: Austin Creed Confident In Adapting To AEW Style
raw_title: Austin Creed On Adapting To AEW's Style: 'Kofi And I Are Very Much Chameleons'
summary_src: Austin Creed is confident that he and Kofi can adapt to their new surroundings in AEW, explaining how he did the same during his time in TNA Wrestling.
body: AEW Austin Creed is confident that he and his tag team partner, Kofi, can adjust to their new surroundings in AEW. After spending 16 years in WWE, Creed left the promotion and is now finding his footing in his new home, AEW. Creed and Kofi recently spoke to " Yahoo Sports ," where Creed discussed his past experience adjusting to a new wrestling promotion, citing his stint in TNA Wrestling to make his case. "From my point of view, your boy was born in the [TNA] X-Division. So, I mean, this ain't no thing. We can switch it up as much as we want to," said Creed. "I feel like Kofi and I are very much chameleons in that aspect. As soon as you drop us in an environment, we see what needs to be done and we are able to adapt fairly quickly." Creed had a three-year spell in TNA before joining WWE in 2010, competing several times for the X-Division Championship, which he never won. Later in the interview, Kofi also spoke confidently about how he and his New Level partner can adjust to and fulfill any role they're given in AEW. "We are jacks of all trades, you know, Swiss Army knives. We can do it all and we do it all very, very well," added Kofi. The former WWE Champion spoke glowingly about their time in AEW, saying that their energy has blended well with the promotion's atmosphere. Creed and Kofi have revealed, following their move to AEW, that they had many opportunities away from the wrestling ring too. The two have discussed how their AEW deals provide them with opportunities beyond wrestling, which they are excited about. In the ring, the duo got their AEW careers off to a strong start by winning the Trios Championship, which they unfortunately lost at the WrestleDream pay-per-view.

Creed cited his three years in TNA's X-Division as evidence of his ability to switch styles, describing himself and Kofi as chameleons who adapt to any environment. Kofi echoed the sentiment, calling the pair jacks of all trades and Swiss Army knives who can fulfill any role in their new promotion.

title: Vince McMahon battled WCW's lingering shadow in 2001
raw_title: The Summer of 2001: Vince McMahon’s fight with the ghost of WCW
summary_src: After Rewind-A-Wai covered WWF SummerSlam 2001, John Pollock reflects on the decline of WWF's business and mishandling of the invasion.
body: The summer of 2001 was a confusing time for the World Wrestling Federation, operating off the fumes of its Attitude Era boom with a decline in momentum, while handling the most coveted storyline with its real-life competitor. Ask a fan of this era about the “Invasion storyline,” and you’re likely to be met with a groan, scream, or laundry list of alternative ideas that would have given some resuscitation in its dying days. If there is an underlying theme from the Monday Night War, it was the real-life vitriol possessed by the warring companies, WWF and WCW, making Monday night a firing zone with attacks lobbed back-and-forth, talent being scooped, shoot interviews, and conveying to fans that in a world of make-believe this feud among companies was real. Every fan had their “dream card”, fantasy booking their favorites with the opposition and asking “what if?” It was Marvel fighting DC, Jason vs. Freddy, and Jay-Z vs. Nas. It sounded really simple on paper. The problem was one company buying out the other, and over time, it was so transparent the scars that Vince McMahon wore from that head-to-head era. The man who frequently stated that he loved competition has acted in the opposite way throughout his career, circumventing anything non-WWE in the market space. This is the man who signed Curt Hennig to thwart the XWF, put himself on ECW programming to counter Wrestling Society X, made up with Jim Ross when he was linked to the World of Sport reboot, and used his son-in-law’s sub-brand as the counterattack to shut down AEW in its tracks on Wednesday nights. Taking us back to 2001, Vince McMahon has acquired WCW for a bargain. McMahon had kicked the tires months earlier in hopes of securing WCW as a distressed asset of the Turner empire. Its brand-new relationship with TNN provided the network with exclusive cable rights to WWF and wasn’t going to bend and allow WWF to run a competitor on another broadcaster without a significant fee. It quelled McMahon’s desire to acquire his competitor, but months later, it was a fire sale, and McMahon bought the assets of WCW, including its undervalued tape library, and committed to several years of advertising dollars toward Turner. WCW was a perfect bridge from the Attitude Era to another golden road paved with pay-per-view revenue off the fantasy match-ups and stories they could tell. Yes, many of the major stars had guaranteed deals and had no incentive to break those contracts to go on the road, nor was WWF interested in upsetting its salary structure for those big names. Hulk Hogan, Sting, Bill Goldberg, Kevin Nash, Scott Hall, and even Eric Bischoff would not be around to launch the invasion. The audience didn’t care because the idea of WCW was strong enough that even a diminished army of WCW names was enough to propel its July pay-per-view into the stratosphere and produce one of the largest non-WrestleMania numbers in the company’s history. summary: During the summer of 2001 the WWF was losing steam from its Attitude Era peak while attempting to capitalize on its real-life purchase of rival WCW through the Invasion storyline. Fans often recall the angle with disappointment and point to missed opportunities that could have revived interest. The Monday Night War had featured genuine animosity between the promotions with on-air shots talent raids and shoot promos that made the rivalry feel authentic.

title: End of an Era: Ex-WWE & AEW Star Retires From Wrestling After 24 Years in the Business
raw_title: Ex-WWE & AEW Star Retires From Wrestling After 24 Years in the Business
body: In his retirement message, Gowen revealed the best moment of his career came when he wrestled in front of his family during his AEW appearance. He also opened up about his struggle with drug addiction. Moreover, he explained how he got the chance to rebuild his life and find his love for wrestling again. Gowen shared the news on Facebook on Wednesday. He posted his first-ever promotional picture along with a more recent photo to reminisce on his wrestling journey. The former WWE and AEW star also thanked the promoters who gave him opportunities. He also thanked the fans who supported him throughout his career. "My in-ring career has come to an end. Thank you to every promoter who gave me an opportunity to wrestle. I've had the privilege of performing for every major company over the past 24 years. Special thank you to the fans for not rejecting me. Pro wrestling provided a direction and outlet for a very lost kid. All I ever wanted to be was a professional wrestler and I accomplished that solely because you accepted me not as a sideshow act but as a legitimate pro wrestler. I'm deeply grateful," Gowen wrote. Gowen had several opportunities across different promotions. However, his favorite wrestling memory came during his appearance for AEW in May 2025. He faced Ricochet on the May 14 episode of AEW Dynamite: Beach Break at the NOW Arena in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. Although Gowen lost, the experience meant a lot to him because his wife, children, and parents were there to watch him wrestle. Looking back, Gowen wrote, "The best moment of my career was wrestling for AEW in front of my wife, kids, and parents." Gowen also revealed that he had struggled with drug addiction in the past. It almost destroyed his career. However, he eventually got a chance to turn his life around. "That was the cherry on top after burning my career to the ground as a result of my crippling drug addiction then having the opportunity to not only rebuild my life but my passion then sharing that with the world while enjoying every second of it," he added. Gowen ended his message by thanking God and the people who believed in him. He described himself as "the luckiest guy in the world." Zach Gowen's biggest run in mainstream wrestling came in 2003 and 2004, when he competed for WWE. He became part of a storyline involving Hulk Hogan's Mr. America character, WWE Hall of Famer Roddy Piper, and Sean O'Haire. Gowen also worked behind the scenes more recently. He took on a production role for Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling at its Northern Rising PPV on October 3 in Toronto. He had also wrestled for the promotion in August, defeating Michael Allen Richard Clark. body: TNA One of TNA's recent signees Ricky Sosa will be sitting out of in-ring action for the time being after it was revealed on this week's episode of "TNA Impact" that he's suffered a "severe back injury." As part of its weekly show, "Impact" provides an "injury report" segment that details the rosters' current injuries (both storyline and real) and the expected timeframes of how long they'll be out of action. In last night's segment, TNA announced that the European star obtained his back injury during the number one contenders ladder match for the TNA World Championship on the October 15 edition of "Impact." During the match, Moose powerbombed Sosa out of the ring. Moose attempted to send Sosa crashing through a propped-up ladder, but Sosa's back grazed the ladder before landing on the floor. As of this report, TNA said that Sosa is unable to compete, but did not provide a timeframe of how long he'll be out of in-ring competition. Sosa officially signed with the promotion at Sacrifice this past March. His first big feud under contract was against former talent Eric Young. Sosa scored a major victory over the veteran on the "Countdown to Slammiversary" in June. After he turned his attention towards The System. That rivalry officially ended at Bound for Glory earlier this month with a win over the System's leader, Eddie Edwards.

The injury occurred during the number one contenders ladder match for the TNA World Championship on the October 15 edition of Impact when Moose powerbombed him out of the ring and his back grazed a propped-up ladder. Sosa, who signed with TNA at Sacrifice this past March and feuded with Eric Young, is currently unable to compete.

The injury occurred during the number one contenders ladder match for the TNA World Championship on the October 15 edition of Impact when Moose powerbombed him out of the ring and his back grazed a propped-up ladder. Sosa, who signed with TNA at Sacrifice this past March and feuded with Eric Young, is currently unable to compete.

llm_long: Ricky Sosa has been sidelined with a severe back injury. The announcement came during the October 22 episode of TNA Wrestling's Thursday Night iMPACT on AMC.
Sosa competed in a ladder match on the October 15 episode of Thursday Night iMPACT. The bout was a main event that offered a future shot at the TNA World Championship.
During the match, Moose executed a powerbomb on Sosa and sent him out of the ring. Sosa's back grazed a propped-up ladder before he landed directly on the floor.
The injury update was part of the TNA Injury Report, which also included notes on Trey Miguel and Jason Hotch. Further details on Sosa's status will be provided when available.

title: WWE to Tape SmackDown Go-Home with Raw in Brooklyn
raw_title: WWE reportedly has a plan for SmackDown the night before Crown Jewel
summary_src: All the attention is on Sat., Nov. 7’s Crown Jewel premium live event, currently scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
body: Unlike a couple of their recent go homes for PLEs in the Kingdom (2025’s Night of Champions and this past February’s Royal Rumble ), Crown Jewel 2026’s wasn’t announced for Saudi in advance. Or anywhere else for that matter. Whether that was an intentional move to give WWE some flexibility given the Iran War’s destabilizing impact on the Middle East/North Africa (MENA) region, or it just worked out that way? We don’t know. We are however hearing (from Fightful Select ) that WWE’s set with a plan. That plan is to tape the Crown Jewel go home editions of Raw and SmackDown together at Brooklyn’s Barclays Center on Mon., Nov. 2. That means a pre-taped final push for the event from the blue brand, and an earlier start time for the red one. To not keep the New York crowd there too late for SmackDown ’s taping, Raw will start at 6 p.m. ET. Netflix streams Raw live on Mondays whenever it happens, so the stream will begin two hours early on Nov. 2. Then wherever Crown Jewel ends up happening, the fallout edition of Raw will be at the Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, South Carolina, streaming live at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix. Got it? title: Major WrestleMania 43 Main Event Rumor Killer Emerges
raw_title: Major WrestleMania 43 Main Event Rumor Killer Emerges
body: "There has been a lot of talk this week that the two main events for WrestleMania in 2027 would be Rhodes vs. Punk on night one and Reigns vs. Femi on night two," Meltzer wrote. "From what we were told, the latter is accurate, but the former is not the current plan." Fightful Select previously said WWE had set Reigns vs. Femi aside for WrestleMania , and some people it spoke with think the bout could close the show. That report also had Rhodes and Punk in prominent spots, and one source floated a second match between them after SummerSlam. WWE has been building toward Reigns vs. Femi since at least June, when it was reported as the fallback if The Rock does not wrestle at WrestleMania 43. Femi called out Reigns on the WrestleMania 42 post-show in April, and he did it again after beating Bronson Reed at Money in the Bank in October. Femi has had a big 2026. He beat Brock Lesnar in the opening match of night two at WrestleMania 42, won the King of the Ring tournament by beating Jey Uso at Night of Champions in June, and beat Lesnar again in a Hell in a Cell match at SummerSlam, though Lesnar beat him at Clash in Italy in May. Reigns won the World Heavyweight Championship from Punk at WrestleMania 42 and is set to face Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn in a champion vs. champion match at Crown Jewel . Rhodes and Punk last met at SummerSlam in August, when Punk kept the Undisputed WWE Championship after a returning Randy Orton interfered. Orton hit Rhodes with an RKO, and Punk followed with the GTS for the win. Punk has since lost the title to Zayn, while Rhodes is now in a feud with Orton on SmackDown. Of the two updates, Reigns vs. Femi carries more weight. WWE has protected the match for most of the year, and it is not hard to see why. Femi has beaten Lesnar twice and won King of the Ring, and a win over Reigns at WrestleMania would go a long way toward making him a top star. Holding the match until next April gives WWE time to build it the right way instead of rushing it onto a smaller show. Rhodes vs. Punk not being the current plan for the night one main event does not rule it out. Meltzer's wording leaves room for things to change, and WrestleMania plans often shift between October and April. But with Rhodes tied up with Orton and Punk no longer champion, a rematch of their SummerSlam match is not the obvious direction it might have seemed a few months ago. That leaves an open question for night one. If The Rock does compete, his match could change the entire card. If not, WWE will need a main event that can stand next to Reigns vs. Femi, and the Rhodes and Orton feud could be one option to watch as the road to Riyadh takes shape. title: In Memoriam: Cause of death revealed for wrestler 'Pac,' who died after AEW competition in Chicago area
raw_title: Cause of death revealed for wrestler 'Pac,' who died after AEW competition in Chicago area
body: A cause of death has been revealed for wrestler Benjamin Satterley, known as "Pac," who dies in Des Plaines after a Hoffman Estates AEW competition. CHICAGO (WLS) -- A cause of death has been revealed for Benjamin Satterley, an English-born wrestler known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. He died last month after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates, a northern suburb of Chicago, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner. The medical examiner says 40-year-old Satterley died from bronchial asthma. He wrestled Sept. 26 at NOW Arena before his death was reported the next day in nearby Des Plaines. The news shocked fans who watched the English-born wrestler perform the night before, including Jayson Weidman, who attended the event. Inside NOW Arena on Saturday, Satterley competed for All Elite Wrestling under the ring name Pac. The English wrestler, who previously performed in WWE as Adrian Neville, was known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. "There are wrestlers that can do incredible things, and then there's wrestlers who can do things that you question how it's even humanly possible that they can do what they're doing. Pac was one of those wrestlers," Weidman said. Satterley, who was from Newcastle upon Tyne, began his wrestling career in 2004 and signed in 2019 with All Elite Wrestling, where he held multiple championships. He competed and lost to Andrade El Ídolo on Saturday in Chicago in the AEW National Championship. Weidman said he purchased his seat specifically in hopes of being close to Pac and his group, the Death Riders. "It was such a special moment for me to be able to see him wrestle," Weidman said. He quickly rose to prominence, earning nicknames like "The Super Superman" and "The Man That Gravity Forgot." He began his international journey in 2007 and wrestled under the name of Adrian Neville from 2012 to 2018. After signing with AEW, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. According to Weidman, Pac wrestled in Saturday's opening match and later returned during the main event. "He looked healthy as can be, and it's unbelievable how less than 24 hours, he could possibly be gone," Weidman said. The Cook County Medical Examiner said Satterley died shortly after 4 p.m. Sunday at 2761 Mannheim Road in Des Plaines. A restaurant employee at that address said Satterley never entered the business. Outside the location, at least one fan left a vase on the sidewalk in tribute to the wrestler. All Elite Wrestling also paid tribute to Satterley on its Facebook page, writing: "The very best of us.
