body: MLW comes to you from a sold-out Chattanooga, Tennessee , with a loaded card headlined by a violent No Holds Barred MLW World Heavyweight Championship fight . Killer Kross puts the richest prize in MLW on the line against Josh Bishop , the new force inside The Skyscrapers. Templario begins his reign as MLW World Middleweight Champion. Lady Frost battles Corinne Joy . Big Damo marches into action with Josef Samael . The 2026 Opera Cup brackets are revealed. And MLW Nation will learn the main event for MLW FIGHTLAND in Charleston. Killer Kross defends the MLW World Heavyweight Championship against Josh Bishop in a No Holds Barred main event from sold-out Chattanooga. Bishop has become a dangerous new piece in The Skyscrapers’ war machine, and the group has made no secret of its championship ambitions. The Skyscrapers have already loomed over the tag team division, but now Bishop gets a direct shot at the biggest belt in Major League Wrestling. For Kross, this is not just a title defense. It is a test of how far The Skyscrapers are willing to go to claim more gold… and how much punishment the champion is willing to absorb to keep his throne. No holds barred means no excuses. No clean lanes. No easy escape. Just the Blood King, a Skyscraper, and the MLW World Heavyweight Championship hanging in the balance. A new reign begins as Templario defends the MLW World Middleweight Championship against rising middleweight player Diego Hill . Fresh off defeating KUSHIDA in Mexico to capture the title, Templario kicks off his reign against one of the most exciting young athletes in MLW. He brings power, precision, and the pride of CMLL into his first defense. But Diego Hill is not entering empty-handed. As the protégé of the legendary Blue Panther , Hill has learned the value of technique, timing, and lucha tradition from one of the sport’s great maestros. Templario wants to establish dominance immediately. Hill wants to turn a major opportunity into a career-changing upset. The middleweight division gets a championship fight with international stakes. Lady Frost takes on Corinne Joy in a women’s division clash loaded with new energy. Frost has already made her arrival felt in MLW, bringing athleticism, confidence, and a cold-blooded edge to every fight. Corinne Joy steps deeper into the spotlight with a massive following behind her and the ambition to turn online buzz into in-ring momentum. Corinne and Jazzy Yang have made it clear they are looking to influence the women’s title picture sooner rather than later. But Lady Frost is not here to be anyone’s stepping stone. This is a chance for one woman to make a statement while the division keeps heating up. Big Damo steps into action with Josef Samael in his corner as he battles Andrew Everett . Damo brings size, power, and blunt-force violence. Josef Samael brings prophecy, manipulation, and the violent doctrine of CONTRA Unit. summary_src: Michael Hayes agrees with the praise of Bobby Roode. Guest appearing on Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast was WWE producer Michael Hayes. Hayes shared that Chief Content Officer Paul 'Triple H' Levesque has identified who could replace Hayes in that lead producer role.

Hayes shared that Chief Content Officer Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque has identified who could replace Hayes in that lead producer role. “But yeah, I just made up my mind that this is your new path and go for it, and I’ll tell you, Trips came up to me one day and he goes, ‘So Michael, you know you’re not gonna be around forever.’ You’re our Pat Patterson. I need you to make Bobby Roode ‘Michael.’” There have been several occasions when those within WWE have praised Roode for his producer work.

title: Tiffany Stratton Injury Update After Money In The Bank Fall
raw_title: Backstage Update On Tiffany Stratton After Rough Landing At WWE Money In The Bank
summary_src: New updates have been released on Tiffany Stratton following her high-risk ladder fall at Money in the Bank earlier this month.
body: WWE Though she's now a two-time WWE Women's Money in the Bank recipient, the high reward came with a very high risk. And now, it remains to be seen what Tiffany Stratton's injury status is after her ladder fall on October 10. In New Orleans, Stratton climbed to the top of a high ladder to execute a high-risk Senton Bomb. However, the ladder jerked violently, causing Stratton to crash short of Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend, and Lola Vice. Instead, she landed on her head and neck when she came down. As of this report, no confirmation was made on if she'll appear at tonight's show at the Toyota Arena in Ontario, California.
summary: Tiffany Stratton executed a high-risk Senton Bomb off a tall ladder during the Women's Money In The Bank match on October 10 but the ladder shifted and she landed awkwardly on her head and neck. The two-time contract winner crashed short of her intended targets Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend and Lola Vice. No word has been given on whether Stratton will appear at tonight's WWE event in Ontario, California.

llm_long: Tiffany Stratton became a two-time WWE Women's Money in the Bank winner. During the match on October 10 in New Orleans she attempted a high-risk Senton Bomb from the top of a tall ladder.
The ladder shifted suddenly as Stratton launched herself. She fell short of her intended targets and landed on her head and neck.
The incident occurred while Charlotte Flair, Lash Legend, and Lola Vice were in the ring area. Stratton has not received medical clearance as of the latest available information.

title: Comeback Watch: MLW returning to PPV with Saturday Night SuperFight

body: MLW is returning to pay-per-view with Saturday Night SuperFight 2026 taking place this November. It was announced today that MLW is partnering with VEEPS (a Live Nation-owned streaming platform) for the PPV, which is set to be held at Cicero Stadium in Cicero, Illinois on November 7. Streaming live on VEEPS, the show has an early-bird pre-order price of $9.99 for the next 48 hours. That rises to $19.99 after the early-bird special, and then $24.99 if you wait to order until the day of the show. MLW and VEEPS first entered into their partnership this May with episodes of MLW Fusion being hosted on the platform. It was noted in the initial announcement that “quarterly premium live PPV supercards” would be coming soon. Fusion now premieres weekly on Tubi every Thursday as part of a recently announced deal , though the show is still available on other platforms like VEEPS and YouTube starting on Saturdays after the initial Thursday airing. “MLW is on a roll, and now it’s time to go bigger,” Bauer said in a statement to The Takedown on SI . “We’re not coming back to pay-per-view to play it safe. November 7 is where championships will be decided, rivalries will come to a head, and the best fighters in MLW will be expected to deliver on the biggest stage we’ve had in years. Chicago always brings an incredible atmosphere, and we’re giving that crowd — and fans watching around the world — a night of super fights.” Bauer, actor/wrestler Paul Walter Hauser, and Bryan Walsh are listed as executive producers of the Saturday Night SuperFight PPV. No matches have been announced yet. The card will include wrestlers from MLW and talent from CMLL. World Heavyweight Champion Killer Kross and new signing Masha Slamovich are among the top names in MLW. It’s noted that Austin Aries, The Good Brothers, Matt Riddle, Mistico, Contra Unit, and Zamaya are also expected to compete at Saturday Night SuperFight. title: Ric Flair Hospitalized Hours After Announcing Blood Clot Diagnosis
raw_title: Ric Flair Hospitalized Hours After Announcing Blood Clot Diagnosis
body: TMZ Sports reported that the WWE icon lost his balance after leaving Wagamama in Tampa and injured his face. The outlet reported that he cut his head and eye open, and was bleeding extensively from his eye. Flair’s bloody fall in Tampa occurred hours after he announced his blood clot diagnosis on social media. Flair canceled a scheduled fan appearance in the Seattle area, saying that doctors advised him to limit travel after discovering a blood clot in his leg. The WWE Hall of Famer shared the news in a post on X , where he apologized to his agent, Steve Solomon, the Washington State Horror Con, Big Event NY, and his fans in Seattle. “Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first,” Flair wrote. Flair referred to Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts as a reason he is approaching the issue with caution. Hurts, 28, will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season due to blood clots. “Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts . The complications involving blood clots in his lungs. It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly. I must follow medical advice,” he wrote. “I’m scheduled to have a procedure to strip the affected vein, which my doctors expect will allow me to be cleared for more travel afterward,” he wrote. “Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment. I’m incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support,” Flair added. “I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road.” It is unclear how his fall will impact the timeline of that procedure. This is not the first event Flair has missed due to a blood clot. The Nature Boy missed the Cauliflower Alley Club’s 60th reunion in Las Vegas, where he was honored with the Iron Mike Mazurki Award. Jerry Lawler and Jimmy Hart accepted the award on his behalf. Flair explained his absence via video. “I have a blood clot in my leg. So, I can’t travel the five or six-hour trips that it takes to get there,” he said. Days later, he flew to Philadelphia for a signing. In a social media post, the WWE alum wrote “a little blood clot is not going to keep me from coming to Philly!” Hopefully, the WWE icon makes a speedy recovery from his fall in Florida. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Opens Up On Roman Reigns Had Heavy Stunt Involvement in Street Fighter Movie
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Reveals Roman Reigns Had Heavy Stunt Involvement in Street Fighter Movie
summary_src: Roman Reigns wasn’t just showing up to look intimidating in Street Fighter. The WWE Superstar had plenty of stunt work to deal with while playing Akuma, and Cody Rhodes says the movie’s production team made sure neither of them got special treatment just because they’re professional wrestlers.
body: Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes opened up about filming Street Fighter and how different the movie’s fight choreography was from what he’s used to doing in WWE. Rhodes, who plays Guile in the film, explained that stunt coordinator John Valera didn’t assume he already knew everything simply because of his wrestling background. “I’m so glad he didn’t look at me and go, ‘Oh, he’s a wrestler. He’s got it.’ I’m glad he looked at me and said, ‘Oh, he’s a wrestler. Maybe he knows a different way,’ because of how we did this combat.” Rhodes admitted that he needed plenty of help learning how to fight for the camera. While WWE involves physical contact and carefully planned movements, movie fights require a different approach to make everything look convincing on screen. “I needed all the help I could. I’m used to punching a guy on the forehead, getting a little bit of contact, maybe not too much. In this world, a lot of across the frame, a lot of whimsy.” That’s when Rhodes brought up Roman Reigns, revealing that his fellow WWE Superstar had a significant amount of stunt work while portraying Akuma. According to Rhodes, the production didn’t assume Reigns knew everything about movie fighting either. “And Roman Reigns, who’s also in the movie, he was heavily stunt involved in terms of his role as Akuma.” Rhodes explained that the stunt team understood professional wrestling experience didn’t automatically translate into Hollywood fight choreography. Both men had to approach the process differently, and Rhodes said he trained every day to get comfortable with what was required. “They knew to not make the mistake of thinking the wrestlers know what they’re doing. So every day I trained.” Reigns taking on a stunt-heavy role is another example of WWE stars expanding into Hollywood while continuing their wrestling careers. With Rhodes playing Guile and Reigns portraying Akuma, Street Fighter gave both men an opportunity to show what they could do outside the ring. Rhodes made it clear that being a WWE Superstar didn’t mean he could walk onto the set and immediately handle everything. The same production that worked extensively with him also had Reigns involved in demanding stunt sequences for Akuma. Now that the movie has been released, audiences can see the results of that work for themselves. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.
summary: Speaking on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes opened up about filming Street Fighter and how different the movie’s fight choreography was from what he’s used to doing in WWE. Per Rhodes, the production didn’t assume Reigns knew everything about movie fighting either. And Roman Reigns.

title: Backstage Buzz: Real Reason WWE Plans to Load Up NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
raw_title: Real Reason WWE Plans to Load Up NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
summary_src: WWE apparently got a serious confidence boost the last time NXT went head-to-head with AEW, and now the company wants to turn things up a notch. After beating Dynamite in the ratings, WWE isn’t interested in playing it safe when NXT goes against Blood & Guts on November 4.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez revealed that WWE actually wasn’t very confident going into its previous head-to-head battle with AEW Grand Slam France. That’s why fans got what was basically a normal NXT instead of WWE stacking the show with everything it had. “Normal show, like they don’t even care. So then they announced that this will be head-to-head, and I was told they have been told to load it up.” Apparently, WWE wasn’t convinced NXT was going to win that night. Rather than load up the card and potentially still lose, the company decided to just put on its usual show and see where the numbers landed. “Then I was told they gained a lot of confidence from the last time they went head-to-head. So what happened is the reason they didn’t load up NXT — they thought maybe they might not win on Tuesday head-to-head, so they thought, ‘Well, we’ll just do a show.’” AEW wasn’t taking that same approach. Dynamite had a much more loaded lineup, including an Ospreay title match, but WWE still ended up coming out ahead in the ratings. “Dynamite had a loaded-up show, you know, the Ospreay title match. They didn’t have confidence. They thought they were going to lose. Most of us figured NXT was gonna win, but you have to remember, when NXT and AEW went head-to-head and they were both on normal nights for years, Dynamite almost always won.” That win apparently changed the mood in a big way. Alvarez said WWE went from not being sure it could beat AEW to basically having a “we’re gonna crush them” attitude going into the next showdown. “So they didn’t have confidence, and now that they won, it was sort of like, ‘We’re gonna crush them.’ So they will load up against Blood and Guts. They don’t wanna lose again Tuesday night after winning last time.” That certainly makes November 4 a lot more interesting. Dave Meltzer previously reported that Nick Khan allegedly made the call to load up NXT , and now Alvarez is saying WWE’s newfound confidence after the last ratings win is a major reason they’re going harder this time. The funny part is that this whole fight wasn’t even supposed to happen because WWE wanted another Wednesday night war. The CW moved NXT because election coverage on November 3 would have resulted in the show being preempted in too many markets, dropping WWE directly onto AEW’s night in the process. AEW already has two Blood & Guts matches planned, so Dynamite wasn’t exactly going to be a quiet night anyway. Now WWE wants to bring some extra firepower of its own, and after winning the last round, it sounds like the company really doesn’t want to hand AEW the bragging rights back. Roman Reigns also worked on the Street Fighter movie alongside Rhodes, and he’s the current World Heavyweight Champion. It’s one of those things where if I don’t flex that muscle, if I don’t get reps at it, I’m not going to get any good at this whole thing. Action, that’s a ton of fun, and comedy, that’s an easy place for me to plug into. But because of Dave Bautista, John Cena, of course, and The Rock, they’ve made it so that we can walk into a lot of these rooms and they know we have something to offer. So I’d like to keep doing that. It’s definitely going to work in a sense of with wrestling. It’s not like it used to be where you can only pick one or the other.” Elsewhere in the interview, Rhodes explained how Nick Khan and Triple H made it “very easy” for him to shoot Street Fighter. title: WWE Still Discussing Rock's Praise For Tony Khan
raw_title: Update On Internal WWE Reaction To Rock Praising Tony Khan In PAC Tribute
body: The Rock had kind words for Tony Khan in his PAC tribute video, something that is reportedly still being discussed in WWE. As noted at the start of the month, the WWE star and TKO board member posted a video where he spoke about PAC following the latter’s passing. In the video, he referred to Tony Khan as his friend and said AEW “is growing into this phenomenal wrestling company.” It had been noted that people in WWE weren’t upset about the video, though they were “surprised” by Rock’s comments about Khan and AEW. Meltzer noted that people “have their theories” on the matter, but that it seems likely it’s simply a matter of Rock having love for the industry and wanting to send condolences to the people in AEW, where PAC worked, instead of saying nothing because of the perceived “wrestling war” he isn’t part of. Rock commented on the matter in early October, commenting on an Instagram post about the matter: “you’re right brother, and humanity matters to me. I was born into this business and I’ve seen it all, but when one of our own passes away, I don’t care nor do I see “our competition”, I care about the wrestlers and how it affects them. I’ve been there. To me, humanity matters most.”” In other Rock news, it was noted that while Rock was originally advertised to appear at the WWE tryouts in Hawaii, he did not appear. title: Ric Flair Hospitalized After Tampa Fall

summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair was reportedly taken to a Tampa hospital following a fall Friday morning.
body: Ric Flair was reportedly rushed to a Tampa hospital after a fall on Friday, just hours after he posted to social media that he was unable to fly to an appearance due to a blood clot in his leg. TMZ reported the WWE Hall of Famer fell outside of a restaurant in the Florida city Friday morning. According to the outlet, Flair was hanging out at the bar and left his drink and phone behind as he left the restaurant and walked across the street. Sources told TMZ Flair suddenly fell and suffered injuries to his face, including a cut to his head. The "Nature Boy" was taken to a local hospital by ambulance. There was no word on why Flair abruptly left the location. Just before 10 a.m., Flair took to X (formerly Twitter) and posted a statement that he was unable to attend Washington State Horror Con in Seattle, due to being unable to travel the distance because of a blood clot. Flair said as disappointed as he was, he had to put "his health and recovery first." He thanked fans for their patience, understanding, and continued support. Flair noted in the post that he is scheduled to have a procedure done on the impacted vein, but did not say when. He told fans that his doctors expected he will be cleared for more travel following the procedure, but it's unclear what impact his recent fall may have on his health. title: WWE Execs Still Upset Over Rock's AEW Praise
raw_title: Report: Some Within WWE Feeling 'Sting' Over The Rock's Comments On Tony Khan
summary_src: According to a new report, there are some within WWE still feeling the "sting" over Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson's comments about AEW and its president, Tony Khan.
body: Following the death of AEW star Pac , real name Benjamin Satterley, WWE star, and member of the TKO board of directors, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson took to social media to pay tribute to WWE's former Neville . In his Instagram video , Johnson not only expressed condolences for Satterley's family and friends, but also praised AEW and its president Tony Khan, calling the promotion a "phenomenal wrestling company." Meltzer said that while no one is questioning the tribute to Satterley, to some within the company, the "sting still hasn't gone away" regarding The Rock's comments on Khan and AEW. Meltzer also noted that while The Rock was initially briefly advertised for the latest slate of WWE tryouts in Hawaii, a location special to the star after he spent time there growing up, he didn't end up appearing. The Rock hadn't been featured on ads for the tryouts for a while leading up to the event. The veteran wrestling journalist said that he doesn't believe Johnson meant anything other than sending condolences to the AEW locker room and Khan, due to the wrestling industry being a big part of his life. Johnson hasn't addressed the situation further, and AEW did not bring it up his comments during their tribute episode to the late Satterley, " AEW Dynamite: A Tribute to Pac ."
summary: Following the death of AEW wrestler Pac, real name Benjamin Satterley, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson posted an Instagram tribute that praised AEW and its president Tony Khan as running a phenomenal wrestling company. Per Dave Meltzer, some within WWE remain bothered by those comments despite the sincere condolences for Satterley, who had previously performed in WWE as Neville. The Rock was initially advertised for recent WWE tryouts in Hawaii but ultimately did not appear at the event.

title: Injury Update: AEW Tacked on Injury Time to Dralistico’s Contract Amid Exit Speculation
raw_title: AEW Tacked on Injury Time to Dralistico’s Contract Amid Exit Speculation
summary_src: Dralistico might already be gone from AEW if it wasn’t for one thing — injury time. His contract should have expired by now, but AEW tacked on extra months that will keep him around until December, and WWE could be waiting on the other side.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez revealed that Dralistico’s original deal has essentially run its course. The only reason he’s still under contract is because AEW added time for the period he missed due to injury. “I do know that Dralistico’s contract would already have expired, but they tacked on injury time, which takes his contract through December.” That makes his recent “Maybe not for long?” post look even more interesting . Dralistico shared a photo of himself behind bars and handcuffed earlier this month, immediately setting off speculation that he was counting down the days until his AEW deal was finished. AEW hasn’t completely given up on keeping him either. Alvarez said there were talks about a new deal when the injury time was added, but right now there’s a chance that Dralistico could end up heading elsewhere. “Apparently, when they tacked on the injury time, there were discussions of re-signing. So we’ll wait and see, but Dralistico will either go to WWE and team up with his brother or end up under the mask as Sin Cara.” The brother Alvarez is talking about is Dragon Lee, which would obviously give Dralistico a pretty easy connection if WWE comes calling. There’s also been recent talk about WWE possibly dusting off the Sin Cara character with somebody new under the mask , and Alvarez threw that out as another possibility. More importantly, Alvarez doesn’t think WWE is some long-shot option here. He actually put the chances of Dralistico attempting to make the jump at better than 50 percent, although a big offer from AEW could obviously change things pretty quickly. “I would say it’s a better than 50% chance he attempts to go to WWE, but they might throw a million dollars at him, and he might stay. Either way, he’s getting paid.” Dralistico hasn’t wrestled for AEW since the June 6 Collision taping, where he teamed with RUSH and Sammy Guevara in a failed bid for the AEW World Trios Championship. That long absence already had people wondering what was going on before his handcuffed photo added even more fuel to the fire. For now, Dralistico is still an AEW wrestler and there’s no deal with WWE on the table that we know of. But with injury time being the only thing keeping his current contract alive until December, the next couple of months could get very interesting. title: Ex-WWE Writer Calls Vince McMahon a Psychopath
raw_title: Former WWE writer unleashes on ‘psychopath’ Vince McMahon: ‘He was a crazy person’
summary_src: Jimmy Jacobs, who has drawn praise for his tenure as a writer on WWE’s creative team from 2015 to 2017, recently opened up about his time in the company, as well as what it was like working with then-WWE boss Vince McMahon.
body: According to Jacobs, McMahon came off as a “psychopath” who routinely bullied his employees. Jacobs, who later enjoyed stints on the creative teams at TNA and AEW after his time at WWE, is also an active professional wrestler , perhaps best known for his time in Ring of Honor. Currently, he’s doing work with Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling in Canada and coaches at the House of Truth wrestling school in the Detroit area of Michigan. One of his more entertaining contributions while working for WWE’s creative was pitching “ The List of Jericho ,” which helped rejuvenate the run Chris Jericho was on at the time. However, while speaking on the After the Bell podcast, Jacobs indicated that his time at WWE had its share of difficulties, and it started at the top. “He was a crazy person. Vince McMahon was a psychopath,” Jacobs said. “That’s the sort of personality type he is, right? He’s like an overt malignant narcissist — not to use catchphrase words, because I’m not using that hyperbolically. That’s his personality type. “I was around Vince McMahon not very long before I saw, ‘Oh, I wouldn’t trade places with this guy for one second.’ Not for one second. Because for everything he has, he has nothing, because he’s a psychopath. And when you’re a psychopath, you’re incapable of love.” His stinging characterization of his former employer continued with Jacobs saying, “Vince McMahon’s a bully. He’s a maniac. He’s an abuser. All the things that have come out, every story you’ve heard about him, it’s something like true. That’s who he is.” According to Jacobs, McMahon was hard on most people, but he did treat his favorites differently. “The people that I saw Vince treat well: Roman Reigns, Brock Lesnar, The Undertaker, and Blackjack Lanza…But other than the names I listed, at different points, he would bury, be down on, [saying] ‘This guy doesn’t know what he’s doing,’ everybody else.” He concluded his thoughts on McMahon by reiterating that he thinks the former wrestling promoter/executive is legitimately a psychopath. “It’s what it is. There’s a lot of other psychopaths out in the world, but Vince McMahon’s one of them. Because he has that sort of personality type, he’ll take risks. He’ll step on people,” Jacobs said. “He’ll do what it takes to get what he wants, and that’s really what a psychopath ends up being: Somebody that will take anything in reality and use it to get what they want…So you don’t love people, you use people.” What do you think, Cagesiders? title: Tony Khan Reacts To Adam Copeland's 2027 Retirement Plan
raw_title: AEW's Tony Khan Talks Adam Copeland Retirement Announcement, Christian Cage's Injury
summary_src: AEW CEO Tony Khan addresses Adam Copeland's retirement announcement and the recent injuries sustained by his tag team partner, Christian Cage.
body: October 14 turned out to be an emotional day for many wrestling fans as they learned of Adam "Edge" Copeland's plan to officially retire from in-ring competition in 2027. No definitive time or place has been attached to Copeland's sendoff yet, but according to AEW CEO Tony Khan, the time leading up to it will surely be memorable. "Abosolutely I knew Adam was going to say that 2027 is his last year," Khan said on the AEW WrestleDream media call, referencing Copeland's announcement made on "AEW Dynamite." "I'm very close with Adam. I speak to Adam very regularly, and of course, as the producer of the show, I'm going to talk to him about what he wants to say on the microphone." "... I think he'll have a great run here throughout the next year," Khan continued. "Into 2027, I don't know how much longer exactly Adam will want to go, but I would say this is what he talked to me about, that 2027 was going to be the last year he would want to wrestle. I've accepted that. I think that Adam is somebody that has accomplished so much in wrestling." Copeland, a former world champion in WWE, initially retired from wrestling in 2011 due to spinal stenosis . Nine years later, he made a miraculous return to action as a surprise entrant in the 2020 Men's Royal Rumble, with his neck back to great strength. He went to wrestle for WWE for an additional three years before jumping over to AEW in the fall of 2023. In 2026, "The Rated R Superstar" reunited with his long-time friend Christian Cage, and even enjoyed a reign as AEW Tag Team Champions. title: Jimmy Jacobs calls Vince McMahon a psychopath
raw_title: Jimmy Jacobs unleashes on ‘psychopath’ Vince McMahon: ‘He was a crazy person’
body: According to Jacobs, McMahon came off as a “psychopath” who routinely bullied his employees. Jacobs, who later enjoyed stints on the creative teams at TNA and AEW after his time at WWE, is also an active professional wrestler , perhaps best known for his time in Ring of Honor. Currently, he’s doing work with Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling in Canada and coaches at the House of Truth wrestling school in the Detroit area of Michigan. One of his more entertaining contributions while working for WWE’s creative was pitching “ The List of Jericho ,” which helped rejuvenate the run Chris Jericho was on at the time. However, while speaking on the After the Bell podcast, Jacobs indicated that his time at WWE had its share of difficulties, and it started at the top. “He was a crazy person. Vince McMahon was a psychopath,” Jacobs said. “That’s the sort of personality type he is, right? He’s like an overt malignant narcissist — not to use catchphrase words, because I’m not using that hyperbolically. That’s his personality type. “I was around Vince McMahon not very long before I saw, ‘Oh, I wouldn’t trade places with this guy for one second.’ Not for one second. Because for everything he has, he has nothing, because he’s a psychopath. And when you’re a psychopath, you’re incapable of love.” His stinging characterization of his former employer continued with Jacobs saying, “Vince McMahon’s a bully. He’s a maniac. He’s an abuser. All the things that have come out, every story you’ve heard about him, it’s something like true. That’s who he is.” According to Jacobs, McMahon was hard on most people, but he did treat his favorites differently. “The people that I saw Vince treat well: Roman Reigns, Brock Lesnar, The Undertaker, and Blackjack Lanza…But other than the names I listed, at different points, he would bury, be down on, [saying] ‘This guy doesn’t know what he’s doing,’ everybody else.” He concluded his thoughts on McMahon by reiterating that he thinks the former wrestling promoter/executive is legitimately a psychopath. “It’s what it is. There’s a lot of other psychopaths out in the world, but Vince McMahon’s one of them. Because he has that sort of personality type, he’ll take risks. He’ll step on people,” Jacobs said. “He’ll do what it takes to get what he wants, and that’s really what a psychopath ends up being: Somebody that will take anything in reality and use it to get what they want…So you don’t love people, you use people.” What do you think, Cagesiders? summary_src: Sean Legacy credits CM Punk. Taking to Instagram, WWE NXT talent Sean Legacy shared the story of how a conversation with CM Punk led to him improving his physique. Legacy wrote: "A few months ago, I had a conversation with @cmpunk at a live event about his diet and workouts.
body: Taking to Instagram, WWE NXT talent Sean Legacy shared the story of how a conversation with CM Punk led to him improving his physique. “A few months ago, I had a conversation with @cmpunk at a live event about his diet and workouts. I’ve looked up to him for years, but that conversation hit at a time when I really needed it. It made me want to demand more of myself and follow through. Since then, I’ve been eating cleaner, pushing myself in the gym, doing cardio five/six days a week, and putting in the ring work and conditioning. You can see the difference in these pictures. What you can’t see is how much better I feel mentally. I feel more focused, more confident, and better than I ever felt. I’m sharing this because maybe somebody else needs that same push. I didn’t realize how much of what I was looking for would come from taking better care of myself. Eating better. Moving more. Showing up consistently. Sometimes the things you keep putting off are the things that could change how you feel every day.
summary: WWE NXT wrestler Sean Legacy shared on Instagram how a conversation with CM Punk at a live event motivated him to overhaul his diet and training regimen. He began eating cleaner, hitting the gym harder, doing cardio five or six days a week, and improving his ring conditioning, resulting in visible physical changes and major mental benefits including greater focus and confidence. Legacy said the discussion came at the right time and he hopes sharing his experience might motivate others.

Their discussion focused on Punk's approach to diet and training. Legacy began eating cleaner, intensifying his workouts, and increasing his time training in the ring as a result.
Legacy has since reduced his weight from 217 pounds to 199 pounds. He shared before and after photos that highlight the visible change in his physique.
WWE released a behind-the-scenes vlog from the NXT house show. The video includes footage of Legacy approaching Punk backstage to compliment him on maintaining his body.
Legacy officially joined the NXT roster near the beginning of 2026. He had previously impressed officials through the WWE ID program and appearances on WWE Evolve.

Punk decided to enhance his own conditioning in the weeks leading up to WrestleMania 42. He has followed a strict meal plan and gym routine while working with trainer Jay Ferruggia, who also works with other WWE performers including Chad Gable.

title: WWE Signs Several Female Athletes to Join Performance Center
raw_title: WWE Signs Several Female Athletes to Join Performance Center
summary_src: WWE has added four new female recruits to its roster, and they’re already making moves in Orlando. The company has signed Gabriela Martinez Asensi, Silvia Likki, Elly Finch, and Tayleigh Robertson, bringing in athletes from several different sports as they begin their professional wrestling careers.
body: According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer, all four women signed with WWE and relocated to Orlando, Florida, within the past week. Each participated in WWE tryouts before earning a contract and joining the company’s Performance Center. Gabriela Martinez Asensi comes from Spain and has a background in collegiate tennis. She previously played for the University of Missouri and is fluent in Spanish, English, and German. She also works as a fitness coach and has built a substantial social media following through her Instagram account . Silvia Likki is another recruit with an established social media presence. The Italian CrossFit athlete has more than 200,000 Instagram followers and brings a background in strength and conditioning to WWE. She has shared her fitness journey through her Instagram page . Elly Finch is also joining the company after competing in track and field at Michigan State University. PWInsider was the first to break the news of her signing earlier this week, before Alvarez confirmed the additional recruits. Finch can be found on Instagram . Rounding out the group is Tayleigh Robertson, who has experience in amateur wrestling and bodybuilding. She attended Snow College and Utah Tech, giving her a competitive sports background before making the jump to WWE. Her Instagram account offers a look at her athletic background. The four signings show WWE continuing to recruit athletes from outside professional wrestling. With backgrounds ranging from tennis and track and field to CrossFit and amateur wrestling, all four will now have the opportunity to develop their skills at the Performance Center. There is no word yet on when any of these recruits will make their WWE television debuts, but they’ve already taken the first major step by signing contracts and moving to Orlando. Now they’ll have to prove they can turn their athletic experience into success inside a wrestling ring. title: El Desperado Withdraws From Super Junior Tag League
raw_title: NJPW Star El Desperado Injured, Withdraws From Super Junior Tag League
summary_src: NJPW announced that El Desperado is injured and out of the Super Junior Tag League, but revealed his replacement to team alongside Mistico.
body: One-half of the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions is not cleared to compete, and has been pulled from New Japan Pro-Wrestling's Super Junior Tag League. NJPW announced on its website on Thursday that El Desperado is injured, and a new competitor will team alongside Mistico as a substitute in his place during the tournament. According to NJPW's statement, El Desperado is suffering from spinal canal stenosis, as well as a hernia, and will be unable to compete in the tournament that kicks off on Saturday. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda will now team with Mistico. El Desperado revealed in his own statement that he is currently able to walk, stand, or even sit upright for long periods of time due to the injury, which is bothering his left leg. The star said he's been having issues with tingling and other odd sensations since March, but the pain began in June and worsened in the last few months. He wanted to continue to wrestle throughout the rest of the year, but his "body has reached its limits," and he apologized to fans. The champion said that NJPW fans should consider the Young Lion's inclusion in the tournament as a "key step to the future of NJPW." Desperado said he wanted to give Yasuda the opportunity to team alongside Mistico, who he called a "global megastar," to see what he can do. He said he has trust in Mistico to pull through and show up for the fans like he always does.
summary: NJPW announced that El Desperado has been forced out of the Super Junior Tag League due to spinal canal stenosis and a hernia. Young Lion Masatora Yasuda will replace him and team with Mistico in the tournament that begins Saturday. El Desperado remains one-half of the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions.

body: Willow Nightingale is still working her way back to 100 percent after the hand injury she suffered this summer. On the road to AEW All In 2026, Nightingale’s status for the pay-per-view was complicated by a hand injury . She worked the PPV despite being hurt and has remained in action. However, she’s done so at less than 100 percent. Nightingale did a Q&A on Instagram today and said she is still using a bone stimulator to help speed up the natural healing process. “It’s better, but not 100% healed,” she responded. “Still using that bone stimulator everyday, even if I have to fit it in while stuck in traffic.” Nightingale had a month-long reign as AEW Women’s World Champion before dropping the title to Mercedes Mone at All In this August. The most recent match that Nightingale took part in was an eight-person tag bout on the Grand Slam France edition this month where The Conglomeration lost to The Death Riders. This week marked the four-year anniversary of Nightingale’s AEW signing being officially announced. She’s become one of the most popular babyfaces in the company and was the first women’s triple crown champion in AEW history, holding the Women’s World Championship, TBS Championship, and Women’s Tag Team titles at different points. summary_src: A new report revealed more on the free agency status of former WWE ring announcer Samantha Irvin following her lengthy non-compete clause.
body: Former WWE ring announcer Samantha Irvin, now going by her real name, Samantha Johnson, will soon hit free agency, though she may not be immediately headed to AEW alongside her husband, Ricochet, like many fans may think. Irvin left WWE in October 2024 , but with her departure came a lengthy non-compete clause . According to a new report from Fightful Select , Irvin is a free agent this month. The outlet reported that after leaving WWE, she had an official non-compete clause, compared to the 90-day "termination period" that many stars have after being released from the company, which is not a true non-compete. It was previously reported that her contract allowed her to quit at any time, but if she didn't see out her three-year deal, a two-year non-compete would be imposed. Stars released, or those who do not have their deals renewed, are often paid for their 30-day or 90-day "termination periods," but Irvin was not. Fightful Select confirmed Irvin joining AEW has been discussed, but she won't be jumping on board immediately. After her departure from WWE, Irvin was open about not liking her position as a ring announcer , and said she wanted to be a manager or other on-screen character instead. Irvin has focused mainly on her music career , releasing multiple singles, including the song "Make Me." Plans for a potential AEW career for her, possibly as a manager for Ricochet and The Demand, were not noted in the latest report. The stable are former AEW World Trios Champions, and Ricochet recently competed in the Clockwork Carnage match at AEW WrestleDream, challenging for Will Ospreay's AEW World Championship.

title: Alice Crowley Reflects On Early Start In Wrestling
raw_title: Alice Crowley Reflects On Her Career, Speaks About Future Goals
summary_src: Alice Crowley speaks about her career and future goals. Ahead of the start of the CMLL Women's Grand Prix, Fightful's Luis Pulido spoke to participant Alice Crowley.
body: Ahead of the start of the CMLL Women’s Grand Prix, Fightful’s Luis Pulido spoke to participant Alice Crowley. She opened up about her career thus far in wrestling and said the following: “I would say, honestly, I should have probably started a little bit later than what I did because I started at 14, but I, I think it helped me be able to get to, you know, obviously be here and like at 23, not a lot of women can say that you know they’ve done these things at this point in their career. I would say it’s definitely because of the time that I took when I was younger training instead of waiting till I turned 18 or whatever. Most places require you to be, but the place I trained at only required a parent, guardian, or somebody to be present, which I appreciated because my parents would always go with me. I think if I didn’t start that young, I wouldn’t be where I am right now, for sure. It’s genuinely just because of the fact that I have been able to get all of my reps in earlier, way early on, so now that I’m even when I was 20 going on 21 going on into 22 and now 23, I was still, you know, being able to figure that part out.” Adding on to that, Crowley was asked about her future goals in wrestling. “I would say that this is probably one of my goals, I mean, I feel that I can still consider it as one of my goals as it hasn’t happened yet, we still got a few days, but wrestling in Arena México was definitely, of for sure one of my goals, and to be able to say that I’m I’m doing it at 23 is just mind-blowing, it’s still mind-blowing, it’s like still even right now, and wrestling for CMLL just one of the longest running companies in existence, you know, if not the longest running company in existence, you know, it’s just… I’m so grateful, so thankful.”

Crowley said she was happy to be placed in that position on such a platform even though she did not win the title.

title: WWE Airport Test: Oba Femi Passes While Others Fail
raw_title: WWE RISING STARS & FADING STARS –The Airport Test: Who’s Got The Look? Oba Femi is among those who do, but several simply don’t
body: They say, “looks aren’t everything,” but physical appearance counts for a lot. Looks play a major role in determining and reinforcing social status. We unconsciously believe attractive individuals to be more intelligent, persuasive, trustworthy, and skilled, even when lacking any objective evidence. In the image-is-reality world of professional wrestling, looks are even more important. The Airport Test is a concept attributed to former WWE head Vince McMahon, though it has long been used by promoters, talent scouts, and wrestling veterans. It is a traditional evaluation of whether a wrestler possesses a larger-than-life presence that naturally turns heads. It poses a simple hypothetical question: If this wrestler walks through a crowded airport in plain civilian clothes, do regular people turn their heads, stop and stare, or ask, “Who is that?” The Airport Test is one way of gauging whether a wrestler possesses “The It Factor”: a combination of physical presence, size, and marketability. Archetypal tough guys like Goldberg, massive behemoths like Andre the Giant and The Undertaker, and hyper-muscular freaks of nature like Brock Lesnar and Batista are classic examples of wrestlers who pass this standard with flying colors. Standing nearly six feet tall with the physical conditioning of a bodybuilder, iconic platinum-blonde hair, natural beauty, and commanding confidence, Cargill is the epitome of a striking look. The fact that she uses a wig takes nothing away from her undeniable star presence. She looks like a Greek goddess and undoubtedly turns heads instantly in public. Onlookers may not know who she is, but they instantly recognize that she is someone important. Cargill may not be a top ring performer, but she certainly looks great on a promotional poster. Oba’s remarkable appearance is the trait that most sets him apart from his peers. One of the most physically imposing stars ever to emerge from NXT onto the main roster, Oba Femi stands roughly 6-4 and is blessed with a massively muscular frame without appearing muscle-bound or slow—reminiscent of Brock Lesnar or Bobby Lashley rather than Hulk Hogan. Oba has a broad, strong jawline and a prominent forehead, giving his face a solid, sculpted look that complements his mighty frame. “The Ruler” maintains an intense, unblinking focus, which projects unshakable confidence. He looks every bit the warrior-king character he portrays, making him the quintessential embodiment of a wrestling champion. Standing 6-3 with superhero proportions, long dark hair, movie-star good looks, and a commanding presence, Reigns naturally draws eyes wherever he goes. It was Reigns’s remarkable look that caused Vince McMahon to push him as WWE’s lead babyface in 2015 despite early fan rejection. body: My final ballot for this year’s Wrestling Observer Hall of Fame is complete. Looking at my final list, what fascinates me the most is that I have overlooked a lot of people over the years who I think are no-brainers now. I’ll get to those I missed, but sorting out all of these names does make me realize that Hall of Fame ballot choices can be quite fluid – some people make it some years, others get left out upon further reflection. Opinions evolve, especially when judging wrestlers who are still on weekly television and are still at their peak. There’s also so much chatter about the Hall of Fame each year, there is always the matter of persuasion. Well, after weeks of analyzing and thinking it over, I’ve come down to my final choices for this year’s ballot. I made the case for these four here . JYD was a big draw in Mid-South and the same for the Von Erichs in Texas, enough to where I think they all deserve in. Pro wrestling history would feel incredibly different without them. And JYD was really close last year! He should get in. I still feel strongly about The Briscoes’ influence on tag team wrestling in the 2010s, and Becky Lynch’s importance in regards to the rise of women’s wrestling in this country can’t be overstated. Jon Moxley has been such an integral part of AEW, he has to be in too. I originally had The Hardy Boyz on my ballot in previous years. I still think they should still be in, as their style and look paved the way for many similar teams in the early-to-mid 2000s like The Young Bucks. The problem here isn’t their eligibility, but the fact that I can only pick six people, and I had to make a tough choice. But there will be future ballots! I am voting for Jeff Jarrett for one reason: TNA. Without a viable second promotion in the wake of WCW’s demise, we wouldn’t have seen the likes of AJ Styles, Samoa Joe, Christopher Daniels, Frankie Kazarian, the Motor City Machine Guns, Amazing Red, Low Ki, and so many others wrestle on a national platform. Granted, many of them were found through ROH first, but TNA was the promotion that brought them to weekly television. There are some caveats that make me think he will struggle. He never became a main event star in WWE, he was WCW Champion at a time when that promotion was in a freefall, and TNA’s story has always been more about survival than success. But he was the one most successful in running a secondary promotion in the mid-2000s that brought attention to the next generation of big stars, and that counts for something. As I mentioned earlier, I have made some big omissions in past ballots, and I am stunned I never thought much about Samoa Joe until now. Upon further reflection, I think he’s a no-brainer, as he has built an incredible legacy for himself. After all, a lot of the early Ring of Honor buzz was because of him and his run as ROH World Champion. body: On the October 22 edition of TNA Thursday Night IMPACT, Shotzi Blackheart made her official return as the newest signing to the company. Now that the former WWE star has arrived, it should be interesting what she has in store for the fans. From championship gold to unfinished business, there is a ton of potential for Blackheart in TNA Wrestling moving forward. Here are some potential Shotzi Blackheart TNA Wrestling plans after her return. Making her official return to TNA Wrestling on the October 22 IMPACT, Shotzi Blackheart came out to make the save for Allie against Kiera Hogan and Tasha Steelz. Hogan and Allie had been a pairing since Kiera’s return to the company at TNA Lockdown 2026. Winning the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships, it seemed like Kiera was a good friend and partner for Allie until she turned her back on her to reunite Fire N’ Flava with Tasha Steelz. Now that the battle lines are drawn, Shotzi teaming with Allie against Fire N’ Flava feels like the first order of business for “The Ballsy Badass.” Before being betrayed by Kiera Hogan, Allie proclaimed that she wanted the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships back. At TNA Bound For Glory 2026, Shayna Baszler made her debut with the company to team Zoey Serrano to defeat Allie and Kiera Hogan to win the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships. Now known as Apex, Baszler and Serrano are looking to exert their dominance on the Knockouts tag team division. While they will undoubtedly be a tough challenge, Allie and Shotzi Blackheart could make for a unique duo that might have what it takes to dethrone Apex down the line. Shotzi Blackheart is no stranger whatsoever when it comes to tag team action throughout her career. During her time in WWE NXT, Shotzi formed a group with both Gigi Dolin and Tatum Paxley called Chemical X. Since her WWE release, Blackheart has been in the ring as a partner and opponent to Dolin, now known as Priscilla Kelly, on multiple occasions. With Shotzi signing with TNA Wrestling, she may now open the door for PK to join her in the company sooner rather than later. At TNA Bound For Glory 2026, Indi Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside to win the TNA Knockouts World Championship. Then, Hartwell was forced to give Brookside her rematch and defeated her once again on the October 22 TNA Thursday Night IMPACT. With Brookside taken out twice, Indi might have to face new challenges from the Knockouts division. Considering her success since leaving WWE, Shotzi Blackheart feels like someone who could be a more than formidable challenger for the new TNA Knockouts World Champion. title: Sheamus Posts Intense Gym Workout
raw_title: Sheamus Shares New Gym Photos, Former WWE Coworkers Respond
summary_src: Former WWE star Sheamus shared new gym photos on Instagram, and many of his former coworkers jumped in his comments to respond.
body: WWE Former WWE star Sheamus, now going by S. Farrelly, may not be immediately jumping back between the ropes following his WWE departure , but he's not skipping any time in the gym. The star took to Instagram on Friday to share some snapshots while training , and a number of his former co-workers took to his comments. Sheamus shared two photos and a video of himself hitting seated shoulder shrugs with 120 pound weights, alongside the caption, "shrug it out." Finn Balor was the first star in his comments, leaving a toilet emoji, seemingly in reference to Sheamus' face while lifting the impressive weight. "Settle down fella," CM Punk commented, alongside a fire emoji. Grayson Waller called the star a "machine," while Bayley left a comment about missing him. Plenty of fans left comments as well, with many saying they hope he ends up in AEW. As of a Fightful Select report on October 1, there had been no discussions between Sheamus and AEW as of that time . The outlet reported that some performers within the company's locker room would like to see Sheamus become "All Elite." The star also recently booked a convention appearance on the same day as AEW Full Gear , but reportedly asked to be able to leave the event early, as he indicated he had a wedding to attend, making wrestling fans suspicious. Sheamus' most recent match came last November. He teamed alongside John Cena and Rey Mysterio to defeat Dominik Mysterio, JD McDonagh, and Balor. body: The MLW World Tag Team Championships will be defended in a Chicago Street fight at MLW Saturday Night SuperFight. MLW announced on Friday that the Good Brothers will defend their championships against Glasgow Boys On Top at the November 7th PPV. The match comes after GBOT attacked CJ Gallows an d then mocked the situation on this week’s show. Gallows, the son of Doc Gallows, was said on the show to be on the hospital with a concussion, fractured jaw, damaged teeth and a bruised lung. “Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson cut short an overseas trip to be at CJ’s side. From the hospital, the World Tag Team Champions delivered their answer: Glasgow Boys On Top will get the championship fight they have been demanding — and everything that comes with a Chicago Street Fight. For Gallows, this is a father’s reckoning. For Anderson, it is about standing beside his brother and making GBOT answer for what they did to his family. The champions are putting their titles on the line to get their hands on the men responsible, with no disqualifications to save them when the fight turns ugly. GBOT wanted a title shot badly enough to send a message through the champion’s son. Now, the ruthless Scots have forced open a door that could lead straight to the World Tag Team Championship — if they can survive the fury waiting on the other side. MLW has already levied fines against Glasgow Boys On Top, with contract termination still a possibility. But no fine can settle this score, and no championship victory can erase the image of CJ lying in a hospital bed. In Chicago, the Good Brothers intend to make GBOT feel every bit of it.”

title: Willow Nightingale Gives Hand Injury Update
raw_title: AEW Star Willow Nightingale Provides Update On Hand Injury
summary_src: Former AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale took to her Instagram stories to provide an update on her hand injury.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Former AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale has been battling a hand injury since the end of August , days before she defended, and lost, her championship to Mercedes Mone at AEW All In London 2026 . The star took to her Instagram stories on Friday to address how she's healing, as she hasn't wrestled in a little over two weeks. Replying to a fan question during a Q&A session on her stories, Nightingale revealed her hand is "better," but still not 100 percent healed. She posted the update alongside an image of herself driving using a machine on her left hand. "Still using that bone stimulator every day, even if I have to fit it in while stuck in traffic," Nightingale said. After losing her championship in London, Nightingale battled Thekla at AEW All Out on September 26 in an effort to earn a shot at Mone and the gold at AEW WrestleDream. Thekla defeated Nightingale at the Chicago-area pay-per-view, then went on to lose her title opportunity against "The CEO." The broken hand is the second injury for Nightingale in 2026. In May, she had to forfeit her spot in the 2026 women's Owen Hart Foundation tournament , as well as vacate her TBS Championship, due to a shoulder injury. Nightingale's most recent match, a mixed eight-person tornado tag, took place on October 6, but didn't air until " AEW Collision: Grand Slam Paris " on October 10. She teamed alongside her Conglomeration stablemates Kyle O'Reilly, Orange Cassidy, and Roderick Strong in a loss to the Death Riders' Marina Shafir, Claudio Castagnoli, Daniel Garcia, and Wheeler Yuta.
summary: AEW star Willow Nightingale has been sidelined with a hand injury since late August. In an Instagram Q&A, she revealed her hand is improving but not fully healed and that she continues daily use of a bone stimulator. The injury is her second of 2026 after an earlier issue forced her to forfeit a scheduled appearance in May.

title: Ric Flair Hospitalized After Fall With Head Injuries
raw_title: Legendary wrestler Ric Flair, 77, hospitalized with head injuries hours after revealing blood clot
body: Per the TMZ report, which included photos and video of the 77-year-old wrestler down on the sidewalk being attended to paramedics, Flair suffered a "nasty" fall while walking across the street after leaving Tampa's Wagamama bar and restaurant. TMZ reported that Flair sustained cuts on his head and around his eye, that his eye was "bleeding extensively," and that it is also believed he may have sustained a concussion. The incident occurred just hours after Flair canceled an appearance at a fan convention in Seattle due to a blood clot in his leg. In a social media post Friday, Flair referenced the ongoing situation with Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, whose season recently ended due to the discovery of blood clots in his lungs , and said he is scheduled to have a procedure to address the issue soon. Unfortunately, I Am Dealing With A Blood Clot In My Leg, And My Doctors Have Limited My Travel To 3–4 Hours. Seattle Falls Outside That Range, And As Disappointed As I Am, I Have To Put My Health And Recovery First. Blood Clots Are Extremely Serious And Can Be Life-Threatening. We Have Seen This Recently With Jalen Hurts And The Complications Involving Blood Clots In His Lungs. It Is A Reminder That This Is Not Something To Take Lightly, And I Must Follow Medical Advice. I'm Scheduled To Have A Procedure To Strip The Affected Vein, Which My Doctors Expect Will Allow Me To Be Cleared For More Travel Afterward. Please Know This Decision Was Not Made Lightly. I Am Truly Sorry For The Inconvenience And Disappointment, And I Am Incredibly Grateful For Your Patience, Understanding, And Continued Support. I Look Forward To Getting Healthy And Seeing You All Down The Road. Thank You For The Love And Support. Flair is a two-time WWE Hall of Famer and widely considered to be one of the greatest talents in pro-wrestling history. Flair's status following his hospitalization Friday is currently uncertain. Uncrowned will continue to update this story as it develops.
summary: Ric Flair, 77, fell while crossing a street in Tampa after leaving a restaurant, suffering cuts to his head and eye along with heavy bleeding and a suspected concussion. The incident happened hours after he canceled a Seattle fan convention appearance due to a blood clot in his leg that limits his travel. Flair had posted on social media about the clot and his upcoming medical procedure, referencing the seriousness of the condition.

title: TKO’s Ari Emanuel Speaks On Possible WWE Crown Jewel Relocation Amid Saudi Arabia Attacks
raw_title: TKO’s Ari Emanuel Addresses Possible WWE Crown Jewel Relocation Amid Saudi Arabia Attacks
body: 0 TKO CEO Ari Emanuel comments on the status of WWE Crown Jewel. The eighth annual WWE Crown Jewel Premium Live Event is scheduled to take place at Riyadh Season Stadium in KAFD, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, November 7, 2026. However, the recent attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group on King Khalid International Airport have cast uncertainty over the safety of talent, staff, and fans traveling into the region ahead of the show. The U.S. State Department recently issued a security warning for Americans traveling to or from the Middle East, including Saudi Arabia, to exercise “heightened vigilance.” The U.S. Embassy in Riyadh also instructed American citizens to exercise extreme caution when using airports in Saudi Arabia and check directly with airlines and airport authorities for updates. PWInsider recently reported that WWE still plans to host Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia and has contingency plans in place, including hiring a security firm experienced in the Middle East and North Africa region. In a recent interview with Fox News to promote his memoir, TKO CEO Ari Emanuel addressed WWE Crown Jewel’s status. He said the event is still set to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as planned. “Right now, everything is still set. This weekend, coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have, in the middle of November, a Frieze Art show. So far, so good. Nothing has been canceled.” Emanuel was then asked if they were being briefed by the government and what they’d do in a scenario where they have to cancel the show. He said, “We have a whole team working on this. And if that doesn’t happen, we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan vs. WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green – Women’s Crown Jewel Championship World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns vs. Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn – Men’s Crown Jewel Championship. She is originally from Spain and is fluent in Spanish, English, and German. Meanwhile, Likki is a CrossFit athlete from Italy with over 200,000 followers on Instagram. And Robertson is an an amateur wrestler and bodybuilder who went to Snow College and Utah Tech. All forr underwent tryouts for WWE recently. Zayn described himself as the smartest competitor who finds ways to survive, positioning himself as the current WWE Champion. He noted that with eight billion people in the world, only one man holds the title and becomes the target for others.

Rey Mysterio then confronted Zayn, expressing uncertainty about his brother Penta's intentions regarding a potential cash-in. Mysterio emphasized his longstanding friendship with Zayn but warned that disrespect toward his family would create issues, while also mentioning his own problems with Ricky Saints.
Zayn responded by urging calm and stating there were no problems between them. He advised focusing on Roman Reigns and reiterated that his issues were only with those showing disrespect.

Trick Williams interrupted the segment and made his way to the ring. Williams addressed Zayn directly, rejecting the idea that he lacks the ability to survive and highlighting his own growth over ten months in the company.

title: WWE Remembers "Exotic" Adrian Street
raw_title: WWE Remembers "Exotic" Adrian Street - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE is saddened to learn that Adrian Street has passed away. Born the son of a coal miner in Wales, Street enjoyed a nearly 60-year career that spanned the globe, as his flamboyant style entertained audiences and reimagined what was possible in sports-entertainment. After competing as Kid Tarzan, “Exotic” Adrian Street was introduced to the world in bold fashion, as Street would make his way to the ring adorned in pastels and glitter with his glam-rock entrance music providing the perfect soundtrack. Accompanied by his long-time manager and future wife, Miss Linda, Street worked throughout the UK, Germany, Mexico and Canada before finally settling in the Continental Championship Wrestling promotion in Birmingham, Alabama. Street estimated that he competed in somewhere between 12,000 and 15,000 matches, but his influence stretched well-beyond in-ring competition. Street is credited with designing the gear worn by Mick Foley’s “Dude Love” during his rivalry with “Stone Cold” Steve Austin. Street also starred alongside Ron Perlman in the 1981 film “Quest for Fire” and performed in the band “The Pile Drivers.” WWE extends its condolences to Street’s family, friends, and fans.

title: Comeback Watch: WWE Hall of Famer Makes In-Ring Return After Nearly 12 Years
raw_title: WWE Hall of Famer Makes In-Ring Return After Nearly 12 Years
body: 0 WWE Hall of Famer Road Dogg recently returned to the ring for his first official match in more than 11 years. The former WWE Tag Team Champion competed at Jeff Jarrett’s All-Star Super Slam event in Hendersonville, Tennessee, on October 22. His return was confirmed by the My World with Jeff Jarrett podcast. They shared a post celebrating the success of Jarrett’s event the following day. Road Dogg has remained involved in the wrestling business during his lengthy absence from in-ring competition. He previously worked as a WWE producer and held creative responsibilities. He mainly filled in for a role as co-lead writer for SmackDown, before departing his creative position earlier in 2026. Road Dogg’s participation had been announced ahead of the show. His return to competition ended a break that lasted more than a decade. Road Dogg teamed with Jarrett and Jay Lethal in a six-man tag team match against QT Marshall, Elijah Drago, and Brady Booker. The match took place during an event celebrating Jarrett’s 40 years in professional wrestling as part of Hendersonville Pig Fest. The appearance marked a notable milestone for Road Dogg. He had not wrestled in an official match since January 25, 2015. His last match before Thursday’s return took place at WWE Royal Rumble 2015, where he teamed with Billy Gunn as the New Age Outlaws against The Ascension. Road Dogg was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2019 as a member of D-Generation X. Beyond his accomplishments as a performer, he spent years contributing to WWE’s production and creative operations. title: Tiffany Stratton Attempts Money in the Bank Cash-In During October 23 WWE SmackDown
raw_title: Tiffany Stratton Attempts Money in the Bank Cash-In During October 23 WWE SmackDown
summary_src: Tiffany Stratton nearly cashed in her Money in the Bank contract on WWE SmackDown, and Liv Morgan was seconds away from being forced to defend her championship. Stratton showed up after Chelsea Green’s title defense against Roxanne Perez and cleared the ring before making her move.
body: The chaos went down on the October 23, 2026 episode of WWE SmackDown , where Chelsea Green defended her WWE Women’s Championship against Roxanne Perez. Green had her hands full throughout the match, especially with Raquel Rodriguez getting involved behind the referee’s back. Raquel pushed Green off the turnbuckles while the referee was checking on Perez, allowing Perez to hit a Shining Wizard for a near fall. IYO SKY eventually came out to confront Raquel, leading to another confrontation at ringside. Despite the interference, Green managed to counter Perez’s Pop Rox and hit UnprettiHER to retain her championship. The trouble wasn’t over for Green. Liv Morgan attacked her immediately after the match, with Raquel joining in. IYO tried to fight them off, but Perez helped turn the numbers back in their favor as the group continued beating down Green and SKY. That’s when Tiffany Stratton’s music hit. Stratton rushed to the ring carrying her Money in the Bank briefcase and went after Perez, Morgan, and Rodriguez. IYO also got involved, hitting Raquel with a missile dropkick as the two women fought back against the attack. Things got even more interesting when Morgan tried using the briefcase against Stratton. IYO stopped her with a strike, allowing Stratton to land a kick of her own. Stratton then handed her briefcase to the referee, appearing ready to officially cash in her Money in the Bank contract. However, she decided to hit Morgan with the briefcase first before going through with the cash-in. That decision cost her the opportunity. While Stratton was discussing the cash-in with the referee, Perez and Rodriguez managed to drag Morgan out of the ring and get her to safety. The match never officially started, meaning Stratton still has her Money in the Bank contract. Stratton made it clear that she’s looking for an opportunity to take Morgan’s Women’s World Championship, but The Judgment Day managed to protect their champion this time. With Morgan also scheduled to face Green at Crown Jewel, Stratton’s involvement could create another problem for both champions. Do you think Tiffany Stratton should have cashed in immediately instead of attacking Liv Morgan with the briefcase first? Let us know what you think in the comments. body: 0 Samantha Irvin could be getting closer to a possible AEW career. According to a new update, the former WWE ring announcer, who now goes by her real name, Samantha Johnson, is set to become a free agent in October 2026 after a non-compete period following her WWE exit. Johnson left WWE in October 2024. However, her departure came with an unusual contract arrangement that set her apart from most WWE stars who leave the company. According to Fightful Select , AEW has discussed bringing Johnson into the company for an on-screen role several times. However, an immediate debut is reportedly not in the plans, and she may not appear on AEW TV anytime soon. Fightful Select reported that Johnson had a non-compete clause in her contract. This was different from the 30-day or 90-day periods often described as non-competes when WWE releases talent or allows their contracts to expire. Those periods usually involve talent receiving pay while their agreements wind down. Johnson’s reported contract allowed her to leave WWE at any time. However, if she quit before completing her three-year deal, she would face a two-year non-compete restriction. Unlike released WWE stars who are typically paid during their termination periods, Johnson reportedly received no payment during this time. With the restriction ending in October 2026, Johnson will soon have more freedom to explore opportunities in pro wrestling again. AEW could be a potential destination for Johnson as her husband, Ricochet, has emerged as a key part of the AEW roster for a few years now. Moreover, she has been backstage at several AEW events earlier. According to Fightful Select, AEW has discussed bringing Johnson into an on-screen role on multiple occasions. However, the latest report did not confirm that she had signed a deal or reveal when she might debut. title: Charlotte Flair Provides Latest On Ric Flair’s Condition After Hospitalization
raw_title: Charlotte Flair Provides Update on Ric Flair’s Condition After Hospitalization
summary_src: Ric Flair’s scary trip to the hospital finally has a positive update, and it came straight from his daughter, Charlotte Flair. After the WWE Hall of Famer was rushed to a Florida hospital following a nasty fall on Friday, October 23, Charlotte confirmed that her father is going to be okay.
body: Later Friday evening, Charlotte addressed her father’s condition on social media after news broke that Flair had been hospitalized in Tampa. Rather than simply telling everyone he was recovering, she shared a funny moment involving her father and a reference to one of wrestling’s most famous rivalries. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok)” Charlotte was referring to The Ultimate Warrior, giving everyone a glimpse of Flair’s sense of humor despite the frightening situation. More importantly, her message offered some much-needed reassurance about his condition. Flair was taken to the hospital Friday morning after falling while walking across the street near Wagamama in Tampa. The 77-year-old suffered cuts to his head and eye, with significant bleeding around his face. Emergency responders treated him at the scene before transporting him to a nearby hospital. The incident came just hours after Flair revealed that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg . Doctors had already restricted his travel to three or four hours, forcing him to cancel an appearance at Washington State Horror Con in Seattle. He also disclosed plans to undergo a procedure to address the affected vein. There has been no confirmation that the blood clot played any role in Friday’s fall, and Charlotte didn’t provide specific details about his injuries or whether doctors had cleared him to leave the hospital. Still, after everything that happened Friday, Charlotte’s update is the news everyone was hoping to hear. Flair went from announcing a serious medical problem to being taken away in an ambulance on the same day. At least now his daughter says he’s going to be okay, and judging by the story she shared, the Nature Boy hasn’t lost his sense of humor. body: WWE Chelsea Green retained the WWE's Women's Championship against Roxanne Perez on "SmackDown" , despite Judgment Day getting involved. Green backed Perez in the corner and she used the turnbuckle to take her down. Perez worked her arm and rolled her up. Green put her in a body scissors and then took her down again for a pin attempt. Perez sent her to the outside, but Green got in the ring and landed a dropkick and a crossbody. Perez rolled out of the ring and caught a baseball slide attempt. Back in the ring, Perez sent her into the ringpost and stomped on her arm over the rope. After the break, Perez superplexed Green. Green connected with a clothesline, enzuiguri and meteora. Perez blocked the Unprettier and pinned her. Green got pushed off the turnbuckle by Raquel Rodriguez. Perez landed a Shining Wizard. IYO SKY attacked Rodriguez and landed a headscissors. Perez landed a crossbody on SKY. Green reversed Pop Rox into Unprettier for the win. Morgan attacked her after the match. She & Rodriguez double teamed Green. SKY suplexed Morgan. Perez pummeled SKY. Tiffany Stratton returned and cleaned house. SKY landed a dropkick on Rodriguez. Morgan swung Stratton's briefcase, but missed. Stratton considered cashing in, but swung at Morgan with the briefcase instead. Rodriguez & Perez pulled Morgan from the ring before she could finish cashing in.

Despite interference from multiple wrestlers including Raquel Rodriguez, IYO SKY, Liv Morgan and Tiffany Stratton's return, Green reversed Perez's Pop Rox into the Unprettier to score the pinfall victory. Randy Orton got involved, but it was Rhodes who delivered the final blow. Cody nailed Corbin with a punt kick to the head, and that’s how the show went off the air. Now Corbin is paying the price, and there’s another problem WWE has to deal with. Corbin is still the United States Champion, which means WWE currently has a titleholder who can’t compete. title: Liv Morgan Recalls Early WWE Training Advice
raw_title: Liv Morgan On Early Days Of Her WWE Training: 'Shut Up & Keep Your Eyes Open'
summary_src: Liv Morgan learned one important lesson she's kept with her since starting her WWE training.
body: WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan continues to be at the forefront of the women's division in WWE, recently defeating Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch in a Triple Threat at Money in the Bank 2026. Although it's her fourth world title reign, Morgan's climb to the top wasn't easy, and while appearing on First We Feast's "Hot Ones," she recalled the key advice that's kept her going since. "Day one, starting [out], it was a lot of, ... 'Shut up and keep your eyes open,' you know?" Morgan recalled about her early days in the WWE system. "We're not even allowed in the ring for 30 days, back in my day when I started. Like, you were not allowed to even set foot in the WWE ring. You had to sit and watch from the sidelines. So I just remember learning to shut the f*** up!" In the past, Morgan reflected on her three-day WWE tryout , admitting how intimidating the physical demands of a wrestler were to her at the time, especially because she lacked an athletic background beyond competitive cheerleading. Despite originally seeing her signing as an achievement on its own, she later learned that she had a long way to go to achieve her dreams, which she eventually did. Now that she's carrying gold again, Morgan will have the eyes of the locker room set on her again, especially WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green, who she's set to face for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship at the upcoming Night of Champions. At the same time, the current Ms. Money in the Bank, Tiffany Stratton, could potentially cash-in on either of them at any time, making it a hostile environment for any champion right now.
