title: Indi Hartwell Finds Closure in WWE NXT Return
raw_title: Indi Hartwell Discusses Her Recent Return To WWE NXT, Sharing The Ring With Zaria
summary_src: Indi Hartwell has discussed her recent return to WWE NXT and getting the opportunity to share the ring with Zaria on the show.
body: Indi Hartwell has discussed her recent return to WWE NXT and getting the opportunity to share the ring with Zaria on the show. On the October 6th edition of WWE NXT, several TNA names would feature as part of a number one contenders battle royal for the NXT Women’s Championship, including Indi, with Wren Sinclair eventually winning the match. While speaking to Joey Karni in a new interview , Indi Hartwell spoke about her brief return to WWE NXT, noting that it brought her closure while also nothing what it meant to share the ring with Zaria. “I think I was so happy and smiley because I was kind of worried that the, the audience wouldn’t remember me or not that they wouldn’t remember me, but that they wouldn’t care anymore because the business moves fast and a lot has happened in NXT since the I was there. So that’s why I was so happy, and yeah, I guess it did give me a sense of closure. I was able to talk with old coaches and producers and people that I worked with there because when you get released, you don’t get to say bye to some people. So yeah, I feel like it was a bit of also a lot of momentum going into Bound for Glory. I got to have a moment with Zaria in the ring, which was cool. Her and I have never ever crossed paths before. So yeah, two Aussies facing off in NXT ring on TV, I think is pretty special.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Royce Keys Blames Jacob Fatu For Creating 946
raw_title: WWE's Royce Keys Explains How Jacob Fatu Is Responsible For The Formation Of 946
summary_src: WWE star Royce Keys says it wasn't his doing to establish 946, but Jacob Fatu's.
body: WWE In Royce Keys' eyes, the blood is all on Jacob Fatu's hands. With the establishment of 946 (Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, Jaida Parker, and the newly recruited Carmelo Hayes ) that forced Fatu to get hit by a car and to be out indefinitely (storyline wise), it appears Keys sees this all as Fatu's doing and not his. On "Notsam Wrestling," the leader of 946 explains their deeply tied background, and how Fatu drove this madness to a head. "I went back to what I used to be. You know, that's all before the positive things. Like, I left Oakland, East Palo Alto. I left all that behind. And you know, there's something that triggered where I had to bring it back...It might have been when Jacob turned his back on me," Keys said. "That might have [been] that instance that made me realize I need to be who I used to be in order to be successful." After the heinous suffering he felt at the hands of Fatu in their street fight match on the August 3 edition of "WWE Raw," Keys said that seeing and tasting his own blood triggered something in him. And now, with feral tendencies on his mind, Keys wants to act on those unconscious impulses once Fatu returns to the ring. "The history's there. People know that I've known Jacob 14, 15 years, right? And when we go at it, there's only one thing that has to be done. Somebody can't get up. 'Cause if you get up, then you know, I didn't do my job...I believe when you're going at it with somebody, you got to put them down...And, you're going to get put down," he concluded.

He added that tasting his own blood after their street fight on the August 3 edition of WWE Raw triggered his current feral mindset.

Keys stated that the group's actions, which resulted in Fatu being hit by a car and written off television indefinitely in storyline, stemmed directly from Fatu's own choices.

"I went back to what I used to be. You know, that's all before the positive things. Like, I left Oakland, East Palo Alto. I left all that behind. Keys said.

Keys revealed that the street fight on the August 3 edition of WWE Raw, where he suffered heavily at Fatu's hands, caused him to see and taste his own blood, awakening feral tendencies within him. He expressed that their 14 or 15 years of knowing each other means their next confrontation can only end with one man unable to get up.
"The history's there. Somebody can't get up," Keys said. Keys concluded that in such a fight both men must aim to put the other down permanently or risk failing to finish the job.

body: Indi Hartwell is open to reuniting InDex now that she and Shaw share a roster once again in TNA. While Indi Hartwell and Samuel Shaw (then working under the Dexter Lumis ring name) shared a roster in WWE NXT, they would be paired up as part of ‘The Way,’ with the two being married on an episode of WWE NXT. Now, the pair are both on the TNA roster, sparking fan intrigue about a potential future reunion. While speaking to Joey Karni in a new interview, Indi Hartwell spoke about potentially reuniting with Shaw in TNA. “I honestly, I think it’s something that a lot of people want to see with like, anytime I’m at a signing or a convention or a show, someone will bring up how they loved index. It’s even years later, it’s something that is always brought up and like, honestly, for me, it’s probably the most fun I’ve had in my career, and I’m so proud of that storyline. We’re both open to doing something again because I feel like we never really got closure on it. It’s still open. So yeah, I’m interested in doing more with that.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: AEW Talent Accused of Ignoring Referee Instructions During Matches
raw_title: AEW Talent Accused of Ignoring Referee Instructions During Matches
summary_src: AEW referees have plenty to worry about during live television, but apparently getting wrestlers to actually listen to them can sometimes be part of the problem.
body: Speaking on The Certified Mark Show , Remsburg explained that referees are constantly receiving instructions through their earpieces during AEW television. Tony Khan is one of several people who can speak directly to him while he’s working a match. “Sure. So I have—there are, I believe, four people that can talk to me. Tony Khan, boss, booker. He’s timing the show. He’s head of creative. Everything he sees and wants is on him.” The show’s director is also feeding Remsburg information about commercial breaks, replays and other production cues. Meanwhile, the match producer and ringside medical staff have their own lines of communication with the referee. “I have the director of the show basically telling us when we’re going to commercial break, telling us when we’re coming out of commercial break, tells me when to hold a belt up to the camera, tells me when I can take the belt down from the camera, tells me when we’re going into replay, all that good stuff.” “I have the coach of the match, which is the producer, coach, whatever you want to call it. They kind of are the conduit between the wrestlers and the television product. They’re telling you what to look out for. They can talk to the camera guys, and then I can talk to the doctor or medical professional that’s at ringside.” Most of what Remsburg then passes along to the wrestlers involves timing, but that’s not all. Referees can also tell talent to adjust their positioning or appearance so everything comes across properly on television. “Most are time-related. But sometimes it’s, you know, ‘Hey, we can’t see your face. Your hair is in your face. Your tag is out on your tights.’ If they’re turned sideways, tell them to turn so hard cam can see that because ultimately what we’re doing is a television product.” Remsburg explained that keeping everything on track is especially important because one match running long can screw with the rest of the show. If the opening match goes several minutes over, everyone scheduled afterwards could end up paying for it. “If the first match goes four or five minutes over time, that’s an egregious sin. You’ve now taken time away from the rest of the show, and that’s not—you know, the wrestlers don’t want to be responsible for that, and the referee doesn’t want to be responsible for the one that’s giving poor messaging. So we’re all just doing our best to keep the ship on track.” That’s where things can occasionally get tricky. Remsburg said Tony Khan and AEW’s coaches understand that referees are doing their best to relay those instructions, but that doesn’t necessarily mean every wrestler is going to listen. “I think that the coach and Tony look out for the referees, definitely. He sees us hustling. He sees what we’re trying to do. The coach understands that, you know, while we are sometimes doing our best to relay messages and make people go on time, some matches are going to go over time. Some wrestlers are going to do their best to listen to the referee. Som

title: Ric Flair Hospitalized After Fall in Tampa
raw_title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Hospitalized After Falling Outside Restaurant, While ‘Dealing’ with Blood Clot in His Leg
body: His daughter Charlotte Flair said in a social media post that the WWE legend is "going to be ok" Flair, 77, had canceled a Seattle appearance hours before the fall as doctors limited his travel due to a blood clot in his leg Ric Flair is recovering in the hospital after a fall outside a restaurant in Florida. The retired WWE legend, 77, was injured in a fall outside Wagamama in Tampa on Friday, Oct. 23, TMZ reported. The incident occurred hours after Flair revealed on Instagram that an upcoming appearance was being canceled due to a blood clot in his leg. In photos obtained by TMZ, Flair is seen lying on his back while surrounded by medical staff. He is also pictured being transported into an ambulance. Flair left his phone and drink behind as he walked across the street after visiting the restaurant that morning, per the outlet. He reportedly cut his head in the fall and his eye was "bleeding extensively." Flair's daughter, WWE wrestler Charlotte Flair , shared an update on his condition in a post on X on Saturday, Oct. 24. "Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head … (ps: he's going to be ok)," she wrote. The wrestling legend had shared a lengthy post about his health, hours before he fell. "I want to sincerely apologize to my agent, Steve Solomon … and especially all my fans in Seattle for having to cancel my scheduled appearance," said Flair. "Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first." "Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs," he continued. "It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice." Flair said that he is scheduled to undergo a procedure "to strip the affected vein," which will hopefully allow him to travel more and continue with his work commitments. "Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment, and I am incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support," he concluded. In June 2025, the former wrestling star revealed to PEOPLE he had skin cancer for "the second time in three years." Flair announced in an Instagram post a month later that he was "cancer-free." PEOPLE has reached out to Flair's representative for comment.
summary: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair, 77, fell outside a restaurant in Tampa, Florida on October 23, cutting his head and injuring his eye. The incident came hours after he canceled a Seattle appearance because doctors restricted his travel due to a blood clot in his leg. His daughter Charlotte Flair stated on social media that he is going to be okay.

title: Matt Hardy Says Jeff May Take Time Off For Neck Injury
raw_title: Matt Hardy says Jeff Hardy may take time off due to neck injury
summary_src: Jeff Hardy may be taking some time off from TNA Wrestling to address a nagging neck injury, according to his brother Matt Hardy.
body: Jeff Hardy may be taking some time off from TNA Wrestling to address a nagging neck injury, according to his brother Matt Hardy. In January, Jeff revealed that he had been working with two bulging discs in his neck following The Hardys NXT Tag Team Championship match against DarkState at NXT Halloween Havoc 2025. During a recent episode of The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy, Matt was asked about potentially developing his “Booker Matt” character and responded: “It’s going to be interesting to see what my next character is, especially if Jeff takes a little time off to try and work on his neck a little bit. That may be happening, I guess we’ll see.” “He’s had this bulging disc that’s been bugging him for a year now. I think he’s done everything he can do in his power. I think he’s maybe going to take some time off and see what he can do to get it fixed up and correct it as much as possible.” The last time Jeff wrestled was at TNA’s TV tapings in Dothan, Alabama, on October 13, where he and Matt defeated AJ Francis and Expressions. The Hardys are also coming off a loss to Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw in a Falls Count Anywhere match at TNA Bound for Glory 2026 at the Yuengling Center in Tampa, Florida. title: Three Reasons Bloodline vs The 946 Fits WarGames
raw_title: WWE Survivor Series WarGames 2026: Three Reasons The Bloodline Vs. The 946 Belongs Inside
body: Royce Keys' war with the family dates back to July. At SummerSlam on Aug. 1, LA Knight, Solo Sikoa, and Keys beat Jimmy Uso, Jey Uso, and Jacob Fatu. Fatu won a Street Fight against Keys on the Aug. 3 Raw and kept the Tongan Death Grip locked on after the bell with Reigns' approval. Keys returned on Aug. 24 with Bronco Nima and Lucien Price, the former NXT tag team OTM, and attacked The Usos, Sikoa, and Knight. Keys revealed the trio's name, The 946, in a vignette posted on Sept. 4. Jaida Parker, who aligned with OTM in NXT in January 2024, made a Raw debut on Sept. 28 by running down Fatu with a car in a parking lot. WWE later posted video of the Bloodline member being loaded into an ambulance. Carmelo Hayes joined the group on Oct. 12. The faction has four men, with Parker in its corner. The Bloodline has matched that count. Reigns picked Sikoa to team with The Usos in the Oct. 12 six-man tag team match. On Oct. 19, all four stood together in the ring. WWE has booked five-man teams for each men's WarGames match since 2022, so each side is one man short. A healthy Fatu would give the family a fifth member. The 946 has done most of its damage away from the ring. Keys, Nima, and Price set The Usos' car on fire on the Sept. 7 Raw , then abducted Sikoa on Sept. 21 before a Money in the Bank qualifying match. Neither attack happened inside a ring. Scheduled fights have not contained the feud either. After Reigns retained the World Heavyweight Championship against Knight at Money in the Bank on Oct. 10, The 946 appeared in the crowd. The Usos and Sikoa ambushed the group, and the brawl spilled into the parking lot. Parker drove off with the rest of The 946 in a truck. The Oct. 12 six-man tag match ended in a no contest after Hayes struck Sikoa with a crowbar, with the referee already pulled from the ring by Parker. On the Oct. 19 Raw , The 946 retreated through the crowd after Reigns speared Nima. WarGames takes that option away. The roofless steel cage surrounds two rings, and members enter at timed intervals until both full teams are inside. WWE's version of the match is decided by pinfall or submission. The Bloodline won the first men's WarGames match at Survivor Series on Nov. 26, 2022, in Boston. Reigns, The Usos, Sikoa, and Sami Zayn beat The Brawling Brutes, Drew McIntyre, and Kevin Owens. Jey pinned Owens after a low blow and a Helluva Kick from Zayn. The family split into two sides for the 2024 match in Vancouver. Reigns, The Usos, Zayn, and CM Punk beat a team featuring Sikoa and Fatu. A spear ended the match, with Sikoa taking the pin. Two years later, both former opponents are aligned with Reigns. Reigns and The Usos returned to the cage at Petco Park in San Diego on Nov. 29, 2025. Punk and Cody Rhodes completed the team, which lost to Bron Breakker, Bronson Reed, Logan Paul, McIntyre, and Brock Lesnar. Jey has been in every men's WarGames match at Survivor Series, including a 2023 win alongside Rhodes. What's your take? Post it in our fre
summary: The Bloodline and The 946 have been feuding since July. The rivalry escalated with a SummerSlam six-man tag match, a post-match attack by Jacob Fatu on Royce Keys, and Keys returning with former NXT tag team OTM to form The 946. body: October 23, 2026 By Michael Joseph Sugue, Manager SmackDown , News , Pro Wrestling , WWE , WWE Universe , WWE Women This week’s October 23, 2026 WWE SmackDown saw B-FAB and Michin challenge for the WWE Women’s Tag Team Championship, held by Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley. It was only two weeks ago that Tater and Lexy won the titles off of Fatal Influence. However, B-FAB and Michin, with Jade Cargill would bring on the pain , and a their tactics, to shock Alexa and Tatum in Ontario, California . The WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley looked liked a force when they won the titles off of Lainey Reid and Fallon Henley of Fatal Influence. And that’s why we thought they’d be ready and able to defend their titles for the first time after a stunning showing. Well, this week, they did work like a well-oiled machine, taking control for most of the match. However, the number’s game would soon catch up. One slip from Tatum Paxley and it was game over, as Jade Cargill and her crew had a plan in place all along. Paxley would try to go for the Cemetery Drive, only for Michin to sidestep her at the last moment. With Paxley lying on the second rope, Cargill would blast her. A groggy Paxley would stand before a waiting Michin, as she set her up for the Styles Clash, resulting in B-FAB and Michin becoming #AndNEW WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions. Was it clean? Absolutely not. But all’s fair in love and war . Congratulations to our new WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions, B-FAB and Michin. Puzzling. The word is puzzling. It was a great move for Paxley and Bliss to breathe new life into the division, and now, they’re not champions anymore. It’s not to say B-FAB and Michin are terrible performers, but this was such a random title change that it could definitely hurt their reign as a whole. We don’t know what direction WWE is taking, but this is not a great move with no plans in place. Nevertheless, we are happy B-FAB and Michin are going to make a run; it’s just unfortunate it’s at the expense of Tatum Paxley and Alexa Bliss. Charlotte Flair has taken to social media to issue an update on her father, Ric Flair , after the WWE legend was hospitalised after collapsing on Friday. Ric Flair, 77, whose real name is Richard Morgan Fliehr, was rushed to hospital after cutting his head and eye open during a fall after he left a restaurant in Florida on Friday afternoon. Ric is one of the most iconic figures in professional wrestling , having been involved in the sport for over 50 years. Currently, he is signed to All Elite Wrestling (AEW) in an ambassador role, in which he makes special appearances. Following his recent trip to the hospital, Ric’s daughter, Charlotte, who is also a WWE star, delivered an update on social media . Charlotte, 40, has revealed that her father was joking with the doctor following his fall while assuring fans that her father will be fine. She wrote: “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of [the Ultimate] Warrior dropping him on his head …(Ps: he’s going to be ok).” Flair's joke referred to a 1993 incident in which the late Superstar injured him during a match. A suplex from Warrior caused Flair to land on his head, dislodging an inner-ear chip that severely affected Ric's balance and equilibrium for months. Prior to his fall, Ric himself recently took to social media and issued an apology for having to cancel a scheduled appearance at the Washington State Horror Con. Flair revealed that he was unable to attend as he is currently dealing with a blood clot in his leg. It is unknown if the blood clot issue was related to his fall.

title: Drew McIntyre Shares Awkward Robert Downey Jr. Encounter
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Recalls Meeting Robert Downey Jr. And Sam Jones
summary_src: Drew McIntyre recalls meeting Robert Downey Jr as well as Sam Jones in two separate stories of meeting the popular actors. In recent years, McIntyre has become one of several WWE superstars to begin to find his footing in the acting world, working with names such as Russell Crowe and more.
body: Drew McIntyre recalls meeting Robert Downey Jr as well as Sam Jones in two separate stories of meeting the popular actors. In recent years, McIntyre has become one of several WWE superstars to begin to find his footing in the acting world, working with names such as Russell Crowe and more. While speaking to Sidewalks Entertainment in a new interview, Drew McIntyre was asked about meeting big name actors, with McIntyre recalling meeting Robery Downey Jr and Sam Jones in two separate instances. “Yeah, I don’t really get that excited about that. I’m excited to talk and learn from a lot of people. Like, I remember one time I got an L.A. restaurant. I turned around, get in my car, and Robert Downey Jr. was there, and I was, ‘oh, hey, man, I’m a fan of your work,’ and I started turning away because I know what it’s like when people are kind of up on your business. I realized as I turned away, he wanted to keep talking, but I committed to turning, so I kept turning. I was like, ‘ah, damn it, he wanted to keep talking,’ and now I’ve turned, and we’re both awkwardly waiting for our cars. So I kind of wish I continued that conversation, because I am a fan, but I also know what it’s like when people are up on you and asking too many questions, and somebody really that was exciting to me is usually cult figures. I did a signing once in Knoxville, Tennessee, and Flash Gordon was there, the actor that played him. I can’t remember the name, Sam (Jones), off the top of my head. But I was leaving, and I was like, oh, my brother loves him, and I’m a big fan of Flash Gordon as well, my is brother obsessed. Then I heard my name getting shouty, just “DREW!” a big booming voice and I knew he was right there, and as I turned, it was like a scene from the movie Ted, I just heard the Flash Gordon theme. He was motioning me over and I went over and I did exactly say the Ted line with the teddy bear movie where he says, ‘thanks for saving every one of us,’ he was lovely, signed a picture for my brother, which my brother proudly has on his wall, but I’ve met so many Hollywood actors.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

The WWE star had just finished eating at a Los Angeles restaurant and was getting into his car when he spotted the actor. McIntyre told Downey Jr. that he was a fan of his work before turning away because he did not want to impose on him.

As McIntyre turned, he realized Robert Downey Jr. actually wanted to continue the conversation. Having already committed to leaving, McIntyre kept turning and both men ended up waiting awkwardly for their cars. McIntyre later said he wished he had kept talking since he is a genuine fan of the actor's work.

McIntyre explained that he understands what it feels like when people crowd celebrities and ask too many questions. He noted that he gets more excited about meeting cult figures than mainstream stars. The wrestler added that he is excited to talk with and learn from many different people.

In a separate story, McIntyre described meeting Sam Jones, the actor who played Flash Gordon, at a signing event in Knoxville, Tennessee. As McIntyre was leaving, he heard Jones shout his name in a booming voice. When he turned around, it felt like a scene from the movie Ted as he heard the Flash Gordon theme playing.

McIntyre quoted the line from Ted, saying 'thanks for saving every one of us' to Jones. The actor was friendly, signed a picture for McIntyre's brother, and the signed photo now hangs proudly on his brother's wall. McIntyre's brother is a big fan of Flash Gordon, as is McIntyre himself.

title: Conrad Thompson Shares Cryptic Update After Ric Flair’s Hospitalization
raw_title: Conrad Thompson Shares Cryptic Update After Ric Flair’s Hospitalization
summary_src: Ric Flair’s health scare has everyone waiting for answers, and now his son-in-law Conrad Thompson has shared a message that could be good news for the WWE Hall of Famer.
body: On October 24, Thompson took to social media with a simple message that appeared to suggest someone close to him had returned home. However, he didn’t specifically identify who he was talking about. The timing is interesting considering Flair was hospitalized Friday morning after falling outside a restaurant in Tampa . The 77-year-old suffered cuts to his head and eye, leaving him bleeding before emergency responders arrived and transported him to the hospital. Later that evening, Flair’s daughter Charlotte gave everyone some reassurance when she revealed that her father was going to be okay. She even shared a joke he made to his doctor about The Ultimate Warrior. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok)” Thompson’s latest post could be another positive development, especially since he’s married to Flair’s daughter Megan. However, there’s one important detail that makes the message difficult to confirm as an update on Flair. Thompson also hosts the Grilling JR podcast with Jim Ross, who recently dealt with his own hospitalization. The 74-year-old WWE Hall of Famer was hospitalized earlier this month after experiencing low oxygen levels. Thompson had already confirmed on the October 22 edition of the podcast that Ross was back home and recovering. That means Thompson’s Saturday message doesn’t definitively establish that Flair has been discharged. Neither Flair nor his family has provided additional details confirming his release from the hospital. Flair’s hospitalization also came just hours after he revealed that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg . Doctors had restricted his travel and scheduled a procedure to address the issue, although there’s no indication that the blood clot caused his fall. For now, Charlotte’s confirmation that her father is going to be okay remains the clearest update on Flair’s condition. Thompson’s message certainly sounds encouraging, but until someone confirms exactly who he was referring to, it’s too early to say the Nature Boy has officially returned home. After everything that happened Friday, that confirmation would be welcome news. title: The Miz Feared WWE Firing After Talking Smack Clash With Daniel Bryan
raw_title: WWE's The Miz Thought He'd Be Fired After Intense Talking Smack Promo
summary_src: WWE star The Miz explained why he thought he'd be fired after his intense "Talking Smack" promo involving Daniel Bryan back in 2016.
body: WWE's "Talking Smack" ran as a weekly series on the WWE Network for just under a year, and its most famous moment came shortly after the show got underway. In August 2016, then-Intercontinental Champion The Miz went face-to-face with "Talking Smack" co-host Daniel Bryan , in a fiery segment where the then-retired Bryan told Miz he was a coward and didn't like the way he wrestled. Miz perceived it as Bryan thinking less of him for not being an independent scene darling, like Bryan, and went off. During the promo, Miz said that while Bryan called him a coward, Bryan was "the one that doesn't get in the WWE ring again." The shocking line caused Bryan to walk off the set, though Miz thought he was going to get punched, and it also led the "A-Lister" to believe he was going to be in a lot of trouble, something he explained in a video of his greatest moments posted to WWE Vault . "In my head, I'm going, 'What did I just say? What did I just say? Did I just get myself fired?'" Miz explained. "I remember getting a text from Kevin Dunn and Vince and they were like, 'We are popping off of this. This is awesome.' And I'm like, 'Wow. I did it.' The next week, I got to be the start of the show. From then on, that title was made to look like a main event title." Miz explained that he already had a bad night before the heated segment, as he had just been drafted to "WWE SmackDown." When he arrived at the show that night, he found out that he'd just be in a dark match, which he wasn't happy about.
summary: During an August 2016 episode of WWE's Talking Smack, Intercontinental Champion The Miz had an intense exchange with co-host Daniel Bryan. Bryan called Miz a coward for his in-ring style, prompting Miz to fire back that Bryan was the one unwilling to return to a WWE ring. Miz later revealed he immediately worried the heated promo had gotten him fired, though he received positive texts from Kevin Dunn and Vince McMahon.

Miz responded by pointing out that Bryan was the one who would not return to the WWE ring. The exchange escalated to the point where Bryan walked off the set, leaving Miz concerned that he might be fired for his comments.
After the segment, Miz worried that he had crossed a line and would face serious consequences. He recalled thinking he might have just gotten himself fired from WWE.

Miz received positive feedback from Kevin Dunn and Vince McMahon, who were excited about the segment. This led to Miz opening the following week's show and helped elevate the perception of the Intercontinental Championship as a main event title.
Prior to the Talking Smack appearance, Miz had been drafted to SmackDown. He was disappointed upon learning he was only scheduled for a dark match that night.

title: On the Record: Indi Hartwell Weighs In On TNA Knockouts World Title Victory At Bound For Glory 2026
raw_title: Indi Hartwell Comments On TNA Knockouts World Title Victory At Bound For Glory 2026
body: Hartwell defeated Xia Brookside to win her first title in TNA Wrestling , a year after missing out on the opportunity at last year's Bound for Glory. In an emotional message following her win, the Aussie star spoke about how glad she was to have won the title after embarrassing herself last year. "First of all, it's crazy what can change in a year. Last year at Bound For Glory, I was going for the title, trying to bring it home, NXT had it. I didn't get the job done, in fact, I feel like I completely humiliated myself, embarrassed myself. My family was right there in the front row. And yeah, I didn't bring it home, but this year finally turned the toy belt into the real thing," she said. The match was refereed by TNA Hall of Famer Mickie James, whom Hartwell idolized, and said that James' presence meant a lot to her. She also spoke about the trials and tribulations she had to go through to reach her goal, making the achievement even more worthwhile. "And the crazy part is that Mickie James was special guest ref, and before the match, I was kind of just going over my own thoughts and understanding how big and how special this is," she said. "To have Mickie there, someone who I used to watch on TNA TV, I used to watch her have crazy matches, and now she's out there refing me. She was there for me to win my first title here in TNA, so, yeah, I'm so grateful. I'm grateful for all the hiccups, all the roller coasters, like all the times I failed, 'cause, I mean, it all led to this, and if I had to do it all over again, I would. I'd go through all the hard sh*t because it's always worth it in the end." Hartwell's win comes three years after her NXT Women's title win, which was cut short after she was called up to the main roster.

summary_src: Kevin Nash and Kane may be on completely different sides politically, but Nash isn’t letting that get in the way of their friendship.
body: Kevin Nash addressed the situation on Twitter after his recent political exchanges attracted attention. He pointed out that he and Glenn Jacobs are still friends despite having very different political views. “The amazing piece of information is that @GlennJacobsTN and myself are friends. His political views are his as mine are mine.” Their disagreement over politics apparently hasn’t changed anything between them personally. Nash instead went after the hostility he sees on social media and argued that political differences don’t need to completely divide people. “The hatred on this app is so sad. United we stand divided we fall. Everyone gets one vote. Make it count.” Nash’s comments come after he once again went after Donald Trump on Kliq This, this time while discussing claims he’d seen surrounding Trump’s cryptocurrency venture. Nash made it clear he was repeating someone else’s argument before laying out allegations about who supposedly lost and made money from the cryptocurrency. With the U.S. midterm elections approaching, Nash also encouraged people to use their own vote rather than turning political disagreements into personal hatred. Whatever he and Kane might say about each other’s politics publicly, Nash clearly doesn’t believe it has to become personal. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.

title: Drew McIntyre Calls CM Punk A Piece Of Crap
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Talks WWE 'Beef' With CM Punk: 'He's A Genuine Piece Of Crap'
summary_src: Drew McIntyre says he's had to fake none of his animosity towards 'piece of crap' CM Punk.
body: WWE Ever since the 2024 Men's Royal Rumble when Drew McIntyre injured CM Punk, their onscreen rivalry has just become more and more personal. The hate between McIntyre and Punk led to heated exchanges in a Strap Match and a bloody Hell in a Cell match. According to McIntyre during an interview on Bradley Martin's " RAWTALK PODCAST ," the heat between them is very real. "He's a piece of crap," McIntyre stated plainly. I avoid him whenever I can avoid him." He then emphasized that Punk has had several altercations with fans over the years, using that to prove his rival genuinely isn't a good person. "He tries to play – now he's different, he's better at hiding it now than he used to be, like back in the day everybody couldn't stand him; he was so full of himself," McIntyre recalled, harkening back to Punk's WWE exit and how he believes it was a disrespectful move toward WWE after years of elevating him. Despite his feelings, McIntyre claims he doesn't allow that to get in the way of putting on a good show for fans. "I can be professional. I'm very good at my job. You put us together, you don't have to find the real in it – like, he doesn't like me, I can't stand him, you put us together, it's magic for the audience." WWE Drew McIntyre further claims he could beat CM Punk in a legitimate fight, laughing off 'The Second City Saint's' infamous attempt to establish himself as an MMA fighter post-WWE . "I will crush you! I'm giant and Scottish, do you know how many fights I've been in?" he laughingly asked. "I can't stand him. He's a genuine piece of crap, good at hiding it these days." McIntyre opined that Punk has burned bridges everywhere else and WWE is his last chance to continue wrestling, which is why he plays along with the corporate side of the promotion and is good-natured. "Behind those eyes he's crying, because he wants to be a d**k non-stop; very Charles Manson-like," McIntyre said. "Just talks to the audience, convinces them he's such a good guy, they buy into his BS." All the love Punk continues to get from the audience rubs McIntyre the wrong way, but still admitted that his rival has a legitimate love for pro wrestling unlike some of the other wrestlers who come into the industry today after first establishing prior careers or wanting to use WWE to jump into Hollywood.
summary: Drew McIntyre told Bradley Martin's RAWTALK PODCAST that his dislike for CM Punk is genuine and that he avoids the fellow WWE star whenever possible. McIntyre cited Punk's past fan altercations and what he saw as a disrespectful exit from WWE years ago after the company had elevated him, adding that Punk used to be so full of himself that everybody couldn't stand him. He noted that while the heat is real he remains professional and focuses on delivering good matches for the audience.

body: At FLEX Wrestling in New York on Friday, October 24, Angel Medina, best known as Angel from the tag team Da Baldies in ECW, officially retired. He lost to HC Loc in a bout refereed by Tony DeVito, Angel’s partner as Da Baldies. Angel and Loc have been feuding throughout the year in FLEX. Angel competed regularly until 2019, when he went on a hiatus before returning to the ring in 2024 for a handful of matches. He made his in-ring debut in 1996 and started wrestling for ECW in 1998, wrestling as Spanish Angel. He is a former six-time IWA Puerto Rico Hardcore Champion.

title: Three More Athletes Added to WWE — Report
raw_title: Three More Athletes Added to WWE — Report
body: 0 WWE has expanded its developmental talent pool with three more female athletes reportedly signing contracts and relocating to Orlando, Florida, to begin training at the Performance Center. The latest additions bring experience from different sporting backgrounds, with the company continuing to look beyond established wrestling talent for its next generation of performers. According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer , Gabriela Martinez Asensi, Silvia Likki, and Tayleigh Robertson have all joined WWE after participating in tryouts. Elly Finch was also among the recruits, though PWInsider had already reported on her signing earlier this week. Martinez Asensi arrives from Spain with a background in collegiate tennis, having played for the University of Missouri. She is also a fitness coach with a significant social media following and speaks Spanish, English, and German. Her athletic experience and ability to communicate across three languages give her a varied background as she begins learning professional wrestling. Likki, meanwhile, brings experience from the CrossFit world. The Italian athlete has built an Instagram audience of more than 200,000 followers, and her strength and conditioning background could provide a foundation as she develops her in-ring skills at the Performance Center. Robertson ( Instagram ) offers a different kind of wrestling experience. She has competed in amateur wrestling and bodybuilding and attended Snow College and Utah Tech before making the move into WWE’s developmental system. All three athletes completed WWE tryouts before receiving their contracts. Their backgrounds reflect the variety of sporting experience the company continues to draw upon when recruiting talent for its future roster. Finch, whose signing was previously reported, also joins the group after competing in track and field at Michigan State University. Her addition was confirmed alongside the other recruits in Alvarez’s report. There has been no announcement regarding when any of the new signings might appear on WWE television. Their immediate focus will be training at the Performance Center, where they will work to turn their athletic backgrounds into wrestling skills. For now, the three recruits have taken their first steps toward a WWE career. Their next test will be between the ropes, where athletic credentials must translate into success in the ring. PAC wrestled his final ever match at AEW All Out this past Saturday September 26 when he unsuccessfully challenged Andrade El Idolo for the National Championship, and those across the professional wrestling industry have already begun to pay tribute to him across social media including WWE COO Triple H, PAC's stablemate Marina Shafir, members of the AEW roster, and AEW President Tony Khan. AEW World Champion Will Ospreay will be in action as he goes head-to-head with Ricochet in a non-title match. Ospreay successfully defended the AEW World Championship against Death Riders leader Jon Moxley in the main event of All Out, with the closing moments of the match featuring Ospreay delivering a Storm Breaker and a Hidden Blade to Moxley amidst interference from the rest of The Death Riders, United Empire, and The Brawling Birds. Baker ensured that Persephone would dethrone Hyan's tag team partner Maya World as TBS Champion at the AEW All In Buy In show on August 30 when she became involved in the match, with Baker, Persephone, and Hikaru Shida later scoring a win against Hyan, Rosa, and World in a trios match at the "Dynamite" Rebel Heart special on September 9. We are live. Excalibur says Benjamin Satterly (known as PAC in AEW) was only a b*****d in name. He says Benjamin was humble and warm, and while he appeared quiet at first, he would light up when talking about his passions including the animals in his garden. He says there will never be another man like Benjamin and says he loves and misses him. Tony Schiavone is standing in the ring, and says AEW is a family. He says everyone in AEW was grief stricken upon finding out the news of Benjamin's death, then says Benjamin taught everyone a lot about being a b*****d in the ring and a great human being behind the curtain. He says Benjamin taught him to be kind, and says he will be honored tonight with this episode of "Dynamite" before throwing it to a video of Jon Moxley speaking after All Out and says it was the last time Benjamin was caught on camera. In the video, Moxley says Will Ospreay was better than him in their AEW World Championship match. He says he gave everything he had, but loss happens in wrestling, life, opportunities, people, and not always getting what one deserves. He says every day is a gift and says walking out in front of a sold out crowd surrounded by teammates, then says Ospreay was the better man and congratulates him. He says all Ospreay has earned is more hard work and says he knows which eulogy he wants to have. He says every day is a gift to do something

Owned by wrestling historian and podcaster Conrad Thompson, this dual-plated Reggie Parks masterpiece is now featured as a premier lot in Heritage’s Fall Sports Catalog Auction, and bidding has already exceeded $100,000.00. Spanning the absolute peak of WWE’s 1980s National expansion, this legendary title belt is distinguished by its unprecedented lineage. Unlike most championship belts that were quickly retired or cycled out of rotation, this exact physical artifact was carried through sold-out arenas by four separate WWE Hall of Famers: Tito Santana, Randy "Macho Man" Savage, Ricky "The Dragon" Steamboat, and The Honky Tonk Man. Most notably, the belt serves as the central centerpiece of WrestleMania III on March 29, 1987. title: Michael Hayes Heartbroken After Split From Hardys
raw_title: Michael Hayes States That He Was Heartbroken When He Was Split From The Hardys In WWE
summary_src: Michael Hayes was invested in the duo. In the year 1999, current WWE producer Michael P.S.
body: In the year 1999, current WWE producer Michael P.S. Hayes served as the manager for The Hardys (Matt Hardy & Jeff Hardy). He cornered them as they won their first WWF Tag Team Championship. Hayes was kicked out of the group in August 1999. While speaking to Stephanie McMahon on the What’s Your Story? podcast , Hayes expressed that his heart was broken when he was split from Matt and Jeff. “Then The Hardys thing didn’t pan out,” Hayes said. “It was funny. Once they dropped the titles, I was specifically told and produced to tell them they’re going back to the starting box and going back to foundation and you’re beginning at the beginning and you would start over and earn it and be a real tyrant, and then Vince (McMahon) goes, ‘God! He can’t be like that to those kids. They should beat him up. Why is he being so mean? Nobody would listen to that. No, get him away from them,’ and then when he told me that, it broke my heart. I was invested and I did what you told me to do…” Matt and Jeff have publicly expressed their appreciation for Hayes. Matt wrote on social media that they will always be grateful to Hayes.
summary: In 1999 Michael P.S. Hayes managed The Hardys and was in their corner when they won their first WWF Tag Team Championship. He was removed from the group in August 1999 after Vince McMahon decided Hayes was too harsh on Matt and Jeff following their title loss. While speaking to Stephanie McMahon on the What’s Your Story? podcast, Hayes said the decision broke his heart because he had become invested in the role.

llm_long: In 1999, Michael P.S. Hayes managed The Hardys, consisting of Matt Hardy and Jeff Hardy. He was in their corner when they captured their first WWF Tag Team Championship.
Hayes was removed from the group in August 1999. During an appearance on the What’s Your Story? podcast with Stephanie McMahon, he described feeling heartbroken by the split.

Hayes explained that after The Hardys lost the titles, he was instructed to act as a strict authority figure. He was directed to tell them they needed to return to basics, start from the beginning, and earn their way back.

The approach changed when Vince McMahon decided the harsh treatment was unsuitable for the team. McMahon ordered Hayes to be taken away from The Hardys, stating that no one would accept such behavior toward them.
Hayes noted that he had become invested in the role and had followed the original directions given to him. Both Matt Hardy and Jeff Hardy have since voiced their gratitude toward Hayes.

raw_title: Scotty 2 Hotty Details Origins Of Too Cool Tag Team In WWE
summary_src: Scott Garland (AKA Scotty 2 Hotty) recently detailed the origins of Too Cool, including how Rikishi was integrated into the group.
body: WWE Scott "Scotty 2 Hotty" Garland and Brian "Grand Master Sexay" Christopher were a popular mid-card tag team during the Attitude Era, originally debuting as heels before getting over with fans. The two had plenty of memorable moments together, most often with their dance routines alongside other talent. Looking back at his time with the team in an interview on "Insight with Chris Van Vliet," Garland recalled how their pairing came together. "Right before WrestleMania of '98 in Boston, I was sitting home," he said. "I had been home for weeks or months, and they had done nothing with me up to this point. So I'm ready to get released." The veteran was then randomly paired with Christopher to take part in the tag team battle royal that opened up WWE WrestleMania 14. "He was a heel, I was a babyface up to that point; we had wrestled each other a bunch of times, and also we were just thrown into this match as a tag team. It made no sense whatsoever!" he proclaimed. At first, the two didn't have a tag team name, nor were their gimmicks harmonized. Garland bumped into Vince McMahon in catering, and told him about their individual past gimmicks. "I said, 'I don't know if you know this or not,' and I know he didn't know it, 'But a few years ago, on the independents, I wrestled as Scott 'Too Hot' Taylor ... and Brian was 'Too Sexay' Brian Christopher.'" McMahon took the information in, and the following week on television, they became Scott "Too Hot" Taylor and "Too Sexay" Brian Christopher, with their tag team referred to as "Too Much." WWE Garland recalled that they went by "Too Much" for about a year before being rebranded as "Too Cool" by Vince Russo. The choice was made right before Christopher suffered an injury, and upon his return, WWE wanted them to do something similar to The Hardy Boyz, wearing street clothes instead of normal wrestling gear. "'We want you to dress like the kids are dressing in the malls.' That was the only direction we got," he recalled. "They got these baggy jeans in the hip-hop shops. We could wear those in the ring and get knee pads and knee braces and all those good stuff underneath and still be able to wrestle in them." While the two worked well as a tag team, the inclusion of Rikishi led to many memorable moments, such as the three men danced together in the 2000 Royal Rumble before Rikishi eliminated both men. "Rikishi Too Cool didn't start until December [1999]. That iconic moment at the Royal Rumble where the three of us dance together? That was four weeks later," he added. Rikishi's pairing with Too Cool was less than a year according to Garland, but having the legendary Samoan with them was a highlight of his career. As iconic as it would become, Garland didn't originally see the pairing working with Rikishi. "I'm like, 'This doesn't make any sense. He doesn't fit with what Brian and I are doing.' I go, 'I don't see this working,'" he recalled. "But that first night, there was just something — it's one of those thin

title: MVP Diagnosed With a Heart Condition
raw_title: MVP Diagnosed With a Heart Condition
summary_src: MVP just revealed something about his health that fans didn’t know — he has a heart condition. The AEW star opened up about being diagnosed with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome, a condition that affects the heart’s electrical system.
body: Speaking on Marking Out with MVP and Dwayne Swayze , MVP discussed the recent death of PAC , along with The Butcher and longtime wrestling fan Sign Guy. The conversation turned to heart problems after MVP brought up losing several friends in the business over the years. That’s when he explained why he’d decided to get his own heart checked. MVP then revealed that he has Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. He learned more about his heart health after undergoing a scan and speaking with his cardiologist, who told him that his results looked good despite the condition. “I got one, and I’m good to go. As a matter of fact, my cardiologist told me, you know, I got the Wolff-Parkinson-White thing, you know, but that’s not fatal. But he said, ‘I don’t know about the rest of you. I don’t know what else you got going on.’” The doctor even managed to get a laugh out of the situation. According to MVP, his cardiologist was confident about his heart but made it clear that anything else going wrong with his body would be somebody else’s problem. “He said, you know, ‘But as far as the heart goes, you’re good. You’re not going to die of a heart attack. You might, you know, whatever else you got going on is a different doctor you got to talk to, but my heart’s good.’” MVP wasn’t sharing his diagnosis just to talk about himself. He had a warning for wrestlers approaching middle age, especially those who spent years drinking, smoking, partying or using performance-enhancing drugs. He urged them to stop assuming they’re healthy simply because they feel fine. “So, I said all that to say this. Man, if you’re—and women pay attention too, but this is primarily for men. If you’re a man and you’re in your 40s, especially if you’ve lived a wrestler’s lifestyle, a bodybuilder’s lifestyle, eating lots of red meat, you know, if you’ve been on the gas and were eating lots of red meat, hard drinking, smoking, partying, go get a CT scan.” He also encouraged people to book an appointment rather than making excuses about the cost. “Book an appointment. It doesn’t cost a lot. It’s really inexpensive. It’s like, I think, less than 100 bucks.” MVP ended his warning by bringing up the people who could be left behind if someone ignores a serious health problem. He said having children and loved ones depending on you should be reason enough to take the issue seriously. “But do yourself a favor, man, for your loved ones, well, for yourself, for your kids, go get a CT scan. Get your heart checked. Make sure that you’re in good shape, because heart disease is a silent killer. You think you’re okay until you’re not.” For MVP, the good news is that his cardiologist has reassured him about his heart health. His newly disclosed condition doesn’t appear to be stopping him from continuing his wrestling career, but he’s not interested in seeing anyone else take unnecessary chances. After losing people he knew in the business, he wants others to get checked while they still have the opportunity. Steve

body: Sam Holloway is the latest name to part ways with WWE’s ID program. Holloway, who was recruited to WWE’s program a little under two years ago, confirmed the news via social media on Monday. title: Michael Hayes Recalls Hiding From André The Giant
raw_title: Michael Hayes Recounts André The Giant Agenting Matches
summary_src: Michael Hayes discusses André. The latest episode of Stephanie McMahon's What's Your Story? podcast featured an extensive chat with WWE producer Michael Hayes. As they were going over Hayes' life and pro wrestling career, Hayes brought up that André the Giant agented matches.
body: As they were going over Hayes’ life and pro wrestling career, Hayes brought up that André the Giant agented matches. André held a show in Ohio that The Freebirds (Michael Hayes, Terry Gordy & Buddy Roberts) were scheduled for. Hayes forgot they were booked, so the night before, he drank and took valium. Gordy and Roberts had to carry him into the venue. “We were in Pittsburgh and there was no hotel rooms so Terry (Gordy) slept on the grass by the pool at the Howard Johnson. We got up the next morning and there was a flight to New Haven or something and there was a flight to Atlanta, and it didn’t take long and all of a sudden, we’re changing our flights and here comes André (the Giant), and we hid, all three of us are hiding behind this pillar, like, ‘I hope he don’t see us. Please don’t see us,’” Hayes said about himself, Terry Gordy, and Buddy Roberts. “‘God, I hope he don’t see us.’” Hayes was asked why they were afraid, and he said, “Well, because I’d already got in trouble for showing up when his first time he was an agent.” Hayes was then asked to clarify if he meant to say André the Giant was a match agent, and he replied, “He was an agent. He was running a show in Youngstown, Ohio, and we were staying in Columbus and I thought we were off. So I drank about, I don’t know, 10 or 12 beers, and had taken some valium.” He continued, “We pull up to the school, and I go, ‘What are we doing here?’ Terry goes, ‘We’re going to work.’ ‘Work!?’ I walked in and literally like the cartoon you see, they’re both holding me up and André’s there playing Cribbage or whatever and drinking his wine. ‘He drunk!’ They go, ‘No, he’s not,’ and they let me go. Wham! Faceplant. Really bad.” Hayes added the following about André, “He was very instrumental in talking us up. Him and I were close when he would come to Georgia. I would take him around and stuff, and I blew that.” Hayes has reached 31 consecutive years with WWE. He shared that Chief Content Officer Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque talked to him about his future, and that can be read about here .

After Hayes partied heavily the night before and needed to be carried into the building, the group later tried to avoid André at an airport by hiding behind a pillar. Hayes explained they were afraid because he had already been in trouble for showing up unprepared the first time André served as agent.

raw_title: Latest Update On Current Plans For WWE WrestleMania 43 Main Events
summary_src: The main events of WWE WrestleMania 43 have recently been discussed, but one of them looks more concrete than the other.
body: According to Meltzer, the idea of having Roman Reigns defend the WWE World Heavyweight Championship against Oba Femi on night two of the event is still very much the plan, which was part of the original report from Fightful Select. However, the part that isn't the plan at the moment is to have Cody Rhodes take on CM Punk in the main event of night one, which Fightful didn't outright report as it was only mentioned that Rhodes and Punk would just have major roles to play. Meltzer noted that the bout is not the current direction, though he did say that it would make sense since the two men are the biggest stars on "WWE SmackDown" right now, and have been purposely kept apart since their initial interaction after WWE SummerSlam 2026. Meltzer rounded off by saying that since the show is still just under six months away, these plans are naturally subject to change due to various circumstances like injuries. One thing that is still subject to change is the date of the event itself as nothing has been officially announced by WWE. The weekend of April 10 and 11 has supposedly been penciled in, though WWE is keeping the date under wraps for now , not just because the logistics of the even taking place in Saudi Arabia being more difficult than if it took place in North America, but because it also prevents companies like AEW running a show directly opposite WrestleMania 43.

title: Eric Bischoff Credits DDP's Authenticity For Getting Over In WCW
raw_title: WWE HOFer Eric Bischoff Disagrees With How Diamond Dallas Page Got Over In WCW
summary_src: According to Eric Bischoff, it was a simplification of Dallas Page's onscreen persona that won him over with fans, rather than his finishing move.
body: Iconic finishers can be an important part of what makes a pro wrestler memorable, and sometimes it's the defining element that gets the wrester over with an audience. As the man who popularized the move that would eventually be synonymous with Randy Orton as the RKO , Diamond Dallas Page's Diamond Cutter was set apart on the roster, and to many fans, a huge contributor to his popularity in WCW. However, as stated on "83 Weeks," Eric Bischoff shared his belief that it was something else. "I know, for Page, that finish, in his mind, is what made him; I disagree," Bischoff said. He went on to praise the finisher, stating that there was plenty of spectacle behind it. "It's not what got him over. What got him over was when he became Page Falkinburg; when he allowed himself to go out and be authentic." Bischoff argued that Page was at his best when he started moving away from his larger-than-life gimmick, noting that at the height of his popularity, he was simply being himself and nothing more while his prior gimmicks were not memorable. "Once he started losing all that, then he started getting over, and I think because he was getting over, the Diamond Cutter became more effective as a finish," he further explained. "So it probably feels like the Diamond Cutter was responsible; it was really Page shifting out of the 'I want to be someone else's gimmick' phase, and finally allowing himself to become authentic, because that's what the audience connected with." Before Page, John Laurinaitis used the move in his career, and Orton has stated that it was from Laurinaitis that he borrowed the move and made it his own.
summary: On his "83 Weeks" podcast, WWE Hall of Famer Eric Bischoff disagreed with Diamond Dallas Page's belief that the Diamond Cutter finisher is what made him popular in WCW. Bischoff praised the move but said Page truly connected with fans when he dropped the larger-than-life character and became authentic as Page Falkinburg. Bischoff noted that Page's earlier gimmicks were forgettable and that being himself propelled him to the height of his popularity.

title: On the Record: Conrad Thompson Responds To Roman Reigns Controversy, 'I Just Shared My Personal Wrestling Opinion'
raw_title: Conrad Thompson Responds To Roman Reigns Controversy, 'I Just Shared My Personal Wrestling Opinion'
summary_src: Conrad Thompson just has an opinion. In recent weeks, Thompson has remained in the headlines, with many criticizing him for his opinions about Roman Reigns and his workload. Speaking with Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Conrad explained himself.
body: In recent weeks, Thompson has remained in the headlines, with many criticizing him for his opinions about Roman Reigns and his workload. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Conrad explained himself. Then, he responded to the claim that he talks about Reigns for clicks. “Listen, I slipped it in, my casual opinion—which I’ll admit I do very rarely. I’m normally trying to put myself in the John Stockton position and trying to get the ball to the Karl Malone’s of the world, which would be the Jeff Jarrett’s or the Eric Bischoff’s or whomever. So people listen for their opinions, but Eric and I happened to be doing a SummerSlam review and I said that Seth and Roman had the match of the night, the match of the weekend, but I was ready for something new, and I shared my opinion about Roman that I was ready for something new. Then everyone else started talking about it. That’s what I found so silly is that my opinion is so ridiculous and I’m so irrelevant. Then why the hell is everybody still talking about it? Like even today, my phone was blowing up. People were talking about it on WWE radio. It’s like, that was forever ago. Then when Roman is saying that, he’s doing it for clicks — on Ariel Helwani’s show? On Busted Open? My point was all of my podcasts for the last two months would have had Roman in the thumbnails and we would have been talking about that, but that wasn’t my intent.” Continuing on, Thompson admits that he finds the entire situation amusing. “I never want my opinion to be what everyone’s talking about, but in this particular case, it was my opinion. So when people are telling me I’m wrong, I’m like, ‘I don’t think you can be wrong in your opinion.’ You like some things more than you like other things. That’s where I was with it. But yeah, the bias thing I thought was weird. Like, yes, I’m friendly with Cody, but I’m friendly with a lot of people in the locker room, including my sister-in-law who works there; one of my best friends, who helps run creative. It’s like Eric Bischoff gets talent from TKO every single weekend for Real American Freestyle. I’m Switzerland. I just shared my personal wrestling opinion and people got bent out of shape about it. I found it amusing.” Elsewhere in the interview, Conrad Thompson said that he wants to do podcasts with Paul Heyman and Michael Hayes. Check out his full comments by clicking here .
summary: Thompson has remained in the headlines, with many criticizing him for his opinions about Roman Reigns and his workload. Then, he responded to the claim that he talks about Reigns for clicks. Listen, I slipped it in, my casual opinion—which I’ll admit I do very rarely.

(Daiki Nagai & Titan) in the third tournament match on the show after Eagles pinned Nagai after hitting him with Hyperion. Unbound Co.’s Taiji Ishimori and Robbie X defeated Ryusuke Taguchi and Kazuma Sumi in the next match. Robbie X hit X Xpress on Sumi to pick up the win The Swirl (Blake Christian & Lee Johnson) defeated YOH and Hyo in the fifth tournament match. Christian pinned Hyo after Christian and Johnson hit him with Brainrot. Master Wato and KUUKAI defeated Mistico and Masatora Yasuda in the main event. Yasuda is replacing the injured El Desperado in the tournament. Wato pinned Yasuda following an assisted Tsutenkaku German suplex. After the main event, Mistico raised the arm of his partner Yasuda, who had to be helped to the back. title: Independent Promotions Gain Traction in Wrestling
raw_title: The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-24 08:43:00 Professional wrestling has undergone significant changes as independent promotions attract growing attention from fans, performers, and industry professionals. While major organizations continue to dominate mainstream wrestling, smaller companies are creating opportunities for alternative storytelling, distinctive wrestling styles, and closer connections between performers and audiences. Independent wrestling has existed for decades, but digital platforms and changing viewing habits have made it easier for regional promotions to reach supporters beyond their local communities. Fans can now discover emerging talent, follow independent events, and purchase merchandise directly from organizations that previously depended almost entirely on live attendance. This development has created an increasingly diverse wrestling environment where creativity and entrepreneurial thinking are essential. Running a successful independent promotion requires more than organizing entertaining matches. Financial management, venue coordination, marketing, and audience engagement all contribute to building a sustainable business. Understanding these responsibilities reveals why independent wrestling has become an important part of modern sports entertainment. Behind the excitement of live wrestling is a demanding business operation. Independent promoters must coordinate venues, negotiate performer agreements, arrange insurance, manage ticket sales, and organize promotional campaigns. Unlike major wrestling companies with extensive administrative departments, smaller promotions often rely on limited teams handling several responsibilities simultaneously. Managing equipment and office resources is another part of operating efficiently. Promotions regularly produce contracts, event schedules, merchandise labels, promotional materials, and documentation for performers and venues. As organizations expand or replace their office equipment, they may accumulate unused supplies that still have commercial value. A promotion retiring an older office printer, for example, could recover money from unopened replacement cartridges through www.selltoner.com . Redirecting funds from surplus office inventory toward event production is one practical example of how smaller entertainment businesses can make better use of their existing resources. These operational decisions rarely attract attention from wrestling audiences, but they contribute to financial stability. Promotions that manage their expenses carefully have greater flexibility to invest in production quality, talent development, and memorable live experiences. summary: Smaller wrestling companies are drawing increased interest from audiences, wrestlers and insiders by offering unique match styles, fresh narratives and stronger performer-fan bonds. While the biggest promotions still lead the industry, digital tools and evolving consumption patterns now allow regional groups to connect with viewers far outside their home markets and generate revenue beyond ticket sales.

title: Drew McIntyre Compares WWE Leadership Styles
raw_title: WWE's Drew McIntyre Details Change In Leadership From Vince McMahon To Triple H
summary_src: Drew McIntyre believes Triple H has a more realistic take on WWE's creative direction compared to Vince McMahon.
body: Drew McIntyre was one of the first modern examples of a wrestler reinventing themselves after coming up short in WWE. Following his release in 2014, McIntyre returned to the independent scene before making his way back to WWE three years later, where he'd go on to have a dominant run on "NXT" before reaching the top of the main roster. This journey allowed McIntyre to work under both Vince McMahon and Triple H. "[McMahon] saw things a little different, very much the kind of black and white [mentality] — good guy, bad guy, keep things a little simpler," he recalled during an interview on Bradley Martin's "Raw Talk." "You know, [Triple H] is bit more, kind of [seeing] in shades of gray — which, that's the real world." McIntyre then recalled seeing The Bloodline story play out, expressing that it made him excited to tell stories in a similar vein. "In 2022, we really started going from Drew the Big Hero of Covid, the Scottish Warrior, to going down the path of becoming a bad guy," he said. McIntyre then clarified that his character was not a heel in a black-or-white sense, as there's an aspect of his character that's just reacting to fans' opinions of him. "It's been this very fun character arc we've been on for the past four years, because Triple H is very open to making it like real life, and just living in shades of gray," McIntyre explained. He then circled back to McMahon again, explaining what the former WWE Chairman emphasized. "He had a very specific way of how he saw things. Like, keep it like — 'Don't talk about things that happened a month ago, two months ago, certainly not years ago; let's live in the now!'"
summary: Drew McIntyre discussed working under both Vince McMahon and Triple H in WWE. He described McMahon as viewing things in black and white with simpler good guy versus bad guy dynamics while seeing Triple H as operating in shades of gray more reflective of the real world. McIntyre cited the Bloodline storyline as inspiration for his own character shift in 2022 from heroic Scottish Warrior to a more nuanced antagonist.

body: When one pay per view ends, the build for the next begins. And so, with the dust still settling after Clockwork Carnage and WrestleDream, the focus in AEW now turns to Full Gear next month. Here’s a look at what the card for Full Gear might look like, starting with what we already know, moving on to what sure seems likely, and finishing with some speculation about what the rest of the show might look like. It was announced on Dynamite that both of AEW’s tag team championships would be on the line at Full Gear. Davis & Doyle earned their shot by defeating the champions in dominant fashion in an eliminator match on Dynamite. The team known as Wrathlander got here by defeating the Sisters of Sin and Divine Dominion in a three-way for a title shot at Grand Slam France: Collision. Fletcher pinned Copeland to win a tag team match on Dynamite, then laid out Ospreay with the AEW World Championship belt after the match. Challengers earning title shots by pinning the champion’s partner has become something of a trope in AEW lately, and this seems like another example. In that same segment, Okada distracted Copeland and interfered in the match, leading to Copeland’s defeat at Fletcher’s hands. He also wiped Copeland out after the match. Okada also pinned Copeland during the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream, and Copeland never got his win back—just when he had Okada beat at the end, he was attacked from behind and pinned by Ospreay instead. The Mone-Shafir matchup is easy to explain: Mone was celebrating her win over Thekla on Dynamite and asked who was next, and Shafir came out to confront her. So there you go. Aminata defeated Maya World on Dynamite to win a TBS title shot. The only question is when that match will take place. To be honest, it will probably happen before Full Gear—AEW has a lot of TV time to fill between now and then—but with no other obvious challenger on the horizon, we’ll list this match here for now. As for the trios titles, Strickland challenged Page to a rematch on Dynamite, and Page accepted, but then balked at the idea of a Texas Death match. The stip is the only reason the match has not been rubber stamped yet, and that figures to be sorted out sooner or later. AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley: With the Bang Bang Gang turning heel on Dynamite and joining the Dogs in a brawl with the Death Riders and Conglomeration, Jay White makes an obvious choice to be Moxley’s next challenger. (Well, his next challenger on PPV—Moxley is sure to defend his title several times on TV between now and then.) AEW National Champion Andrade El Ídolo: Andrade was not on Dynamite, so nothing was done to set up a new challenger. One quick option: Kevin Knight, who suddenly finds himself without a tag team partner, assuming Fletcher does go on to challenge Ospreay. title: New U.S. Intelligence Warning Raises More Concerns Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia
raw_title: New U.S. Intelligence Warning Raises More Concerns Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia
summary_src: WWE’s Crown Jewel situation in Saudi Arabia just got another serious development. U.S.
body: According to CBS News , Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton issued the warning in an October 23 memo sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The document, first reported by Axios, warned that Iran has increased its efforts to target American personnel in the Middle East and other countries. Clayton didn’t hold back when describing what U.S. intelligence officials have uncovered. “The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries.” That’s a serious warning with Crown Jewel now just two weeks away. The memo doesn’t identify specific targets, reveal which countries are involved beyond the Middle East, or say whether an attack is imminent. There’s also no indication that WWE, its wrestlers or Crown Jewel are being specifically targeted. Still, the warning comes as the U.S. government is already taking precautions across the region. The State Department ordered non-essential embassy personnel and their families to leave Saudi Arabia earlier this week, while several other diplomatic facilities have reduced staffing. U.S. military officials have also been quietly scaling back their presence at certain locations because of ongoing threats. A U.S. official explained to CBS News that the threats from Iran and the Iranian-backed Houthi movement in Yemen are directly influencing those decisions. “The threat of Houthi attacks and of Iranian terror plots targeting U.S. officials are informing our decisions on staffing adjustments for embassies on RO [Restricted Operations] Status in the region.” That puts another layer of concern on WWE’s upcoming trip. As Ringside News previously covered , the U.S. government had already ordered diplomatic personnel out of Saudi Arabia ahead of Crown Jewel. The situation in Riyadh has also been getting worse. Saudi air defenses intercepted a ballistic missile targeting the capital early Friday morning, while additional missiles and drones were intercepted elsewhere in the country. The U.S. Embassy also warned Americans to use extreme caution at Saudi airports , with operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh suspended following attacks on airport infrastructure. WWE isn’t the only organization facing questions about holding a major event in Riyadh. Saudi Arabia has already postponed two international gatherings until 2027, including the United Nations World Data Forum, which had been scheduled for November 9 through November 12. The Future Investment Initiative conference, originally set for October 26 through October 29, was also postponed. Those developments are particularly concerning because Crown Jewel is scheduled for November 7, right between the dates of those two postponed events. body: Charlotte Flair has provided a positive update on her father after Ric Flair was taken to hospital following a fall in Tampa, Florida. On Friday night, Charlotte posted on X that the 77-year-old was expected to be OK, while also sharing a joke her father apparently made to his doctor. Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head… The comment referred to The Ultimate Warrior, whom Flair wrestled during the early 1990s. A further potentially positive update came on Saturday from Conrad Thompson. Thompson did not identify the person he was referring to, although the timing of the post points to Flair. He is Ric Flair’s son-in-law, having married Flair’s daughter Megan Fliehr in 2018. TMZ reported on Friday that Flair fell after leaving a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa and suffered cuts to his head and eye. He was attended to by medical personnel before being transported to hospital by ambulance. Earlier that day, Flair had announced that he was dealing with a blood clot in his leg and would be unable to attend the Washington State Horror Con in Seattle. He said doctors had restricted his travel and that he was scheduled to undergo a procedure on the affected vein.
