title: Injury Update: Ric Flair Shows Off Injured Eye After Hospitalization and Calls Out Reckless Facebook Posts
raw_title: Ric Flair Shows Off Injured Eye After Hospitalization and Calls Out Reckless Facebook Posts
summary_src: Ric Flair is battered, bruised and apparently dealing with some Facebook drama on top of everything else. The WWE Hall of Famer finally broke his silence after a nasty fall sent him to a Florida hospital, sharing a photo of his injured face and promising he’ll be okay. But he also had a bone to ...
body: Flair was rushed to the hospital on October 23 after taking a nasty spill outside a restaurant in Tampa. The 77-year-old suffered cuts around his head and eye, leaving him bleeding before paramedics arrived. Now, a day later, the Nature Boy is letting everyone see the damage for themselves. On October 24, Flair posted an update on Twitter alongside a photo showing him smiling with a bandage covering his right eye. He thanked the doctors at Tampa General Hospital for taking care of him until 4:30 in the morning and made it clear that he’s focused on recovering. “Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger. Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay!” That’s the good news. The strange part came immediately afterward, when Flair suddenly turned his attention to his Facebook account. Apparently, some things were posted while he was in the hospital, and Flair wants absolutely nothing to do with them. He revealed that he doesn’t even own his Facebook page anymore and apologized for what he called reckless posting behavior. “And Just So You Know For Those Who Were Asking And Wondering, I Don’t Own My Own Facebook Page Anymore. I Apologize For The Reckless Posting Behavior On My Facebook When I Was In The Hospital. It Was Completely Inappropriate!” Flair didn’t explain what was posted, who controls the page or why the content upset him. But he clearly wasn’t happy about it, especially considering he was dealing with a medical emergency at the time. The whole situation comes at a rough time for Flair. Hours before his fall, he revealed that he had a blood clot in his leg and needed a medical procedure. Doctors had already restricted his travel, forcing him to cancel an upcoming appearance in Seattle. His daughter Charlotte Flair offered some reassurance Friday night, telling everyone her father was going to be okay. She also revealed that he was already joking with his doctor about The Ultimate Warrior dropping him on his head. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok)” Now Flair is speaking for himself, and despite the nasty-looking injury, he seems determined to put the whole ordeal behind him. He’s not giving a timeline for when he’ll be fully recovered, but he’s made two things very clear: he’s going to be okay, and whatever happened on his Facebook page while he was hospitalized didn’t sit well with him. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Flair was rushed to the hospital on October 23 after taking a nasty spill outside a restaurant in Tampa. The 77-year-old suffered cuts around his head and eye, leaving him bleeding before paramedics arrived.

title: Master Wato and KUUKAI win NJPW Super Junior Tag League opener
raw_title: Master Wato & KUUKAI win main event as NJPW Super Junior Tag League opens
summary_src: Master Wato & KUUKAI topped the opening night of NJPW’s Super Junior Tag League with a victory over Místico & Masatora Yasuda.
body: Master Wato & KUUKAI topped the opening night of NJPW’s Super Junior Tag League with a victory over Místico & Masatora Yasuda. The 2026 tournament began Saturday at Kumagaya Civic Gymnasium in Saitama, drawing an announced crowd of 1,112. All 12 teams were in action across the two blocks. Yasuda was a late addition to the field after El Desperado withdrew from the tournament because of spinal canal stenosis and a lumbar disc herniation. Desperado personally recommended the Young Lion as his replacement alongside Místico. Yasuda received a main-event opportunity immediately and came close to an upset with a Boston Crab on Wato. However, KUUKAI assisted his partner in setting up a super Tsutenkaku German suplex, with Wato pinning Yasuda after 13:32. AEW’s Blake Christian & Lee Johnson also made a winning start. Competing as The Swirl, they defeated IWGP Junior Heavyweight Champion YOH & Dragongate’s Hyo when Christian pinned Hyo following Brainrot. Nick Wayne had less success in his tournament debut alongside KUSHIDA. House of Torture’s Yoshinobu Kanemaru sprayed Wayne with whisky as KUSHIDA was preparing to attack DOUKI, allowing DOUKI to catch KUSHIDA with a victory roll for the three-count. United Empire’s Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young defeated SHO & Dick Togo, although the finish created tension between the partners. Young made a blind tag before covering Togo immediately after Akira had hit the Fireball, with NJPW noting that Akira was unhappy with his partner afterward. Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita, Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X and DOUKI & Kanemaru were the other tournament winners, leaving three teams in each block tied on two points. The tournament, whose 12 original teams were announced earlier this month, continues on Sunday at Korakuen Hall. The second night is headlined by the two B Block winners Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita and The Swirl. KUSHIDA & Wayne will attempt to get their first points against Místico & Yasuda, while Ishimori & Robbie X meet DOUKI & Kanemaru in another match between opening-night winners. The block winners will advance to the tournament final at Power Struggle in Hiroshima on November 3.
summary: Master Wato and KUUKAI defeated Místico and Masatora Yasuda in the main event to kick off the 2026 NJPW Super Junior Tag League at Kumagaya Civic Gymnasium in Saitama in front of 1,112 fans. All 12 teams competed across two blocks on the opening night. Yasuda stepped in after El Desperado withdrew due to spinal canal stenosis and a lumbar disc herniation, with Desperado recommending the Young Lion as his replacement; AEW's Blake Christian and Lee Johnson also won their first match as The Swirl.

title: Kevin Nash Recalls Shawn Michaels Hospital Angle
raw_title: Kevin Nash Remembers WWE's Shawn Michaels Checking Into Hospital To Sell A Storyline
summary_src: Hall of Famer Kevin Nash recalls how well Shawn Michaels did on selling a hospital visit for a WWE storyline.
body: WWE In his prime, Shawn Michaels was never short of being a "Showstopper." Wrestling during some of the most highly watched eras in WWE history, his believability captured fans. WWE Hall of Famer and good friend to Michaels in real life, Kevin Nash, recalls one scenario in which fans actually believed Michaels was hospitalized after his match. Frantic by what they saw, it appears many within the WWE Universe called the hospital where Michaels was staying (storyline wise), seeking information on HBK. "I remember when we did the Shawn Michaels thing, when he took the blow and he went down, and I remember when I pitched it, I said, 'We can't have the commentators talk...We have to have the locker rooms come out, heels and babyfaces, kind of standing to make sure that he's f***ed, and then take him out...' I'm pretty sure we checked him into a Springfield hospital. So, people called. Shawn was in the hospital. So...you can make s*** real. But you can't make s*** half real," Nash said on his "Kliq This" podcast. The quote above comes from a conversation Nash and his co-host Sean Oliver had over the debate of believability in today's wrestling, and how everyone plays a role on how it sells, from the in-ring stars down to the commentators at ringside.
summary: Kevin Nash pitched a detailed angle where Shawn Michaels sold a serious injury after taking a blow in a match. The plan involved both heels and babyfaces coming from the locker room to stand around Michaels before he was taken out on a stretcher. Nash said they checked Michaels into a Springfield hospital as part of the storyline, leading fans to call the facility seeking updates on his condition.

llm_long: Kevin Nash recalled an angle involving Shawn Michaels that convinced fans the wrestler had been hospitalized following a match. Nash pitched the idea for the segment where Michaels took a blow and went down during a show. The plan included having both heels and babyfaces from the locker room come out to stand around Michaels to emphasize the severity of the situation.

Commentators were instructed not to talk during the scene to heighten the realism. Michaels was then taken out of the arena as part of the storyline. The promotion checked Michaels into a Springfield hospital for the angle. Fans called the hospital seeking information on HBK after believing he was truly injured.

Nash shared the memory on his "Kliq This" podcast while discussing believability in wrestling with co-host Sean Oliver. He stated that everyone from the in-ring performers to the ringside commentators plays a role in selling the action. Nash added, "you can make s*** real. But you can't make s*** half real."
The former WWE Hall of Famer described Michaels as a Showstopper whose work during highly watched eras captured fans with its believability.

raw_title: Hulk Hogan’s Beachfront Mansion Sells for Nearly $5 Million Below Asking Price
summary_src: Hulk Hogan’s beachfront Florida mansion has officially been sold more than a year after his death. The late WWE legend’s Clearwater property went for $5.9 million, a massive drop from the nearly $11 million asking price it hit the market with earlier this year.
body: According to TMZ , Hogan’s estate has now offloaded the 5,400-square-foot mansion. The property was originally listed for $10.989 million in January, meaning the final sale came in roughly $5 million below that initial asking price. The mansion was more than just another piece of Hogan’s real estate portfolio. He bought the Clearwater Beach property for $3.3 million back in 2012 and spent his final years there before his death on July 24, 2025. The beachfront home features five bedrooms and five-and-a-half bathrooms, along with a massive 1,000-square-foot primary suite. That suite includes a sitting area, Gulf-facing terrace, morning bar, spa-style bathroom and huge walk-in closet. Hogan’s estate also managed to sell another property right next door. His 2,062-square-foot guest cottage, which has three bedrooms and two-and-a-half bathrooms, reportedly went for another $2.8 million. It’s unclear whether the same buyer picked up both properties. If they did, the combined purchases would come to $8.7 million for Hogan’s mansion and neighboring cottage. The mansion first went on the market about six months after Hogan’s death with an asking price just shy of $11 million . His longtime friend Martha Thorn of the Thorn Collection and Coldwell Banker Realty handled the listing. The sale also comes while Hogan’s estate has been dealing with other matters following his death. Celebrity branding firm Carma HoldCo Inc. filed a lawsuit seeking at least $10 million in damages over allegations involving Hogan’s Real American Beer venture, claims that Hogan’s side has disputed. Whatever happens with those separate legal issues, one major piece of Hogan’s estate has now changed hands. The Clearwater mansion where the wrestling icon spent his final years is officially under new ownership, along with his neighboring guest cottage. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: The property was originally listed for $10.989 million in January, meaning the final sale came in roughly $5 million below that initial asking price. The mansion first went on the market about six months after Hogan’s death with an asking price just shy of $11 million .

title: Match Made: Undertaker vs Kane – WWE Bragging Rights 2010
raw_title: Undertaker vs Kane – WWE Bragging Rights 2010 | WON Flashback
summary_src: October 24 2010 was the date of WWE Bragging Rights that year, and probably the worst match on that card was The Undertaker vs Kane in a Buried Alive match. The match got a 1* in that week’s Wrestling Observer Newsletter, and our own Dave Meltzer was certainly not a fan of the Nexus run […]
body: “Kane beat Undertaker in 16:53 in the Buried Alive match to keep the World title. The match opened with a “We Want Blood” chant which must have thrilled the company on a live show. Fortunately that ended quickly. Mostly brawling in the stands. Crowd was dead in this match as well. Undertaker started throwing chairs in the ring and also threw in the top of the announcers table, which accidentally hit Kane. When Undertaker got in the ring, Kane grabbed a chair and nailed Undertaker in the gut and hit Undertaker with three chair shots to the back. “The one thing I’ve noticed about chair shots to the back is because wrestling has had so many years of chairs to the head, people don’t react to chairs to the back because they expect them to the head. I’m wondering if you just need to put a moratorium on chairs for a little while, so people will react just seeing the chair used as opposed to now where they expect a hard shot to the head and don’t react unless they get it. “More chair shots by Kane and two choke slams. Since there were no pins, Kane had to carry Undertaker to near the entrance area where they had a tombstone and an open grave for someone to be put in. Kane tried to put him in the grave, but Undertaker caught Kane in the gogoplata. Kane started tapping, but no submissions here. Kane then passed out. Undertaker threw him in the grave. He was about to start burying him, but he spotted Paul Bearer. He threw Bearer’s face in the dirt. He was about to choke slam Bearer into the grave when Nexus all attacked him. They all first bumped for Undertaker, until the numbers game became too much. They were beating him down, and Kane emerged from the grave. As they held Undertaker, Kane nailed him with the urn. The Nexus guys started shoveling dirt on him when Kane told them to leave. Kane then did his magic stuff which caused a tractor positioned near the site to drop tons of dirt on Undertaker, and leave him buried alive once again. *’” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. He has more than ten years of experience covering mixed martial arts, pro wrestling, football and gaming across a number of publications, starting at SEScoops in 2012. He previously also worked for PROGRESS Wrestling as Head of Media as well as working on the social channels of the company.
summary: Kane got past Undertaker in 16:53 in the Buried Alive match to keep the World title. Undertaker kicked off throwing chairs in the ring and additionally threw in the top of the announcers table, which accidentally hit Kane.

title: Backstage Buzz: Sheamus's AEW Future Still Unclear Despite Backstage Advocates
raw_title: Sheamus's AEW Future Still Unclear Despite Backstage Advocates
body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 24, 2026, 1:04 PM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. His favorite wrestlers are The Rock and CM Punk, despite the latter doing his level best to make us all dislike him. Sign in to your TheSportster account Sheamus left WWE earlier this year after almost 20 years with the company. The Celtic Warrior is now a free agent, and as is often the case when big stars leave WWE, the wrestling world is expecting him to show up in AEW any day now. The thing is, despite Sheamus's star power, that still seems unlikely to happen. Fightful shared an update on Sheamus's post-WWE status during a Q&A. Apparently, unlike some other departing WWE talent, there is no urgency from AEW to bring the Irishman in. In fact, Sheamus is believed to have had talks with other promotions regarding where he might wrestle next, but it's unclear if one of those promotions is AEW. That doesn't mean Sheamus doesn't have people advocating for him in AEW. The same report notes that Adam Copeland (Edge) and Claudio Castagnoli (Cesaro) have both been lobbying to make Sheamus All Elite. That's to be expected, though, since Castagnoli worked extensively with Sheamus in WWE as The Bar, and Copeland is good friends with Sheamus outside of wrestling. A lack of urgency to make Sheamus a part of the AEW roster now that he's a free agent continues the narrative that there are some in the company who have suggested signing him might not be a good idea . It doesn't sound like anyone has a problem with Sheamus specifically, but some are concerned that the trend of picking up anyone WWE lets go has led to the AEW roster becoming too bloated. There are already a lot of wrestlers in AEW. So many that, despite two shows a week and more PPVs than ever before, there are still a lot of talented competitors who are struggling to get screen time. If Sheamus were to become All Elite, his notoriety would mean he immediately debuts on a big show, gets a spot high on the card, and competes against top wrestlers who can match the star power he brings. That all makes sense. However, it's not like AEW has held off from signing other former WWE Superstars lately. Kofi and Austin Creed were brought in almost as soon as their non-compete clauses expired. Even more recently, Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut. A combination of AEW's growing roster and Sheamus's age might be what prevents AEW from bringing him in, but even then he's 48, that's only three years older than the recently signed Kofi.
summary: Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. The thing is, despite Sheamus's star power, that still seems unlikely to happen.

title: Ric Flair out of hospital, provides update after fall

summary_src: Ric Flair is assuring fans that he’s going to be okay after taking a scary fall in Tampa, Florida on Friday. The 77-year-old wrestling icon is now out of the hospital and home recovering after being treated for an injury to his eye.
body: Ric Flair is assuring fans that he’s going to be okay after taking a scary fall in Tampa, Florida on Friday. The 77-year-old wrestling icon is now out of the hospital and home recovering after being treated for an injury to his eye. He s ent out a tweet this afternoon thanking everyone for their messages and prayers, along with thanking the medical staff at Tampa General Hospital for the care they gave him. Flair was in the hospital until the early morning after suffering a fall outside of Wagamama restaurant and bar on Friday. In his tweet, Flair apologized for the fact that his Facebook account continued to post as normal during his hospitalization. Flair does not currently have access to that account amid a legal dispute with a digital talent agency that he says has fraudulently taken control of it. TMZ first reported the news of Flair’s hospitalization on Friday, writing that he “suddenly fell and injured his face” after getting up from the Wagamama bar and crossing the street. Flair was “bleeding extensively” from his eye after the fall and was taken to the hospital by ambulance. Flair suffered this fall just hours after announcing that he wouldn’t be able to make a scheduled convention appearance this weekend due to another medical issue. Originally, Flair was supposed to be across the country for Washington State Horror Con, but he is unable to travel long distances at the moment due to a blood clot in his leg. The blood clot has been an ongoing issue for months, and Flair is scheduled to undergo a procedure soon to strip the affected vein. title: Ric Flair Updates Fans on Recovery After Hospital Stay
raw_title: Ric Flair posts from home, says he is focused on recovery after hospitalization
summary_src: Ric Flair has posted an update from home after being hospitalized following a fall in Tampa, Florida.
body: Ric Flair has posted an update from home after being hospitalized following a fall in Tampa, Florida. The 77-year-old shared a photograph on Saturday showing him covered up to his neck by a blanket and wearing a medical dressing over his right eye. In the post on X , Flair thanked those who had sent messages and prayers and expressed his appreciation to the staff and doctors at Tampa General Hospital, saying they had cared for him until 4:30 a.m. Flair said he would respond to people individually as he regained his strength. I am focused on my healing and recovery right now. I will be okay! Flair also addressed activity on his Facebook account while he was hospitalized. He said he no longer owns his own Facebook page and apologized for what he described as “reckless posting behavior” on the account during his hospital stay, calling it “completely inappropriate.” Flair was taken to hospital on Friday after sustaining a fall in Tampa. Earlier the same day, he had announced that a blood clot in his leg had forced him to cancel an appearance in Seattle and that he was due to undergo a procedure on the affected vein.
summary: Ric Flair posted a photo from home on Saturday after being hospitalized in Tampa following a fall. The 77-year-old thanked well-wishers, the staff and doctors at Tampa General Hospital who treated him until 4:30 a.m., and stated he is focused on healing while regaining strength. He also clarified that he does not own his Facebook page and apologized for reckless and inappropriate posts made on the account during his time in the hospital.

llm_long: Ric Flair was hospitalized in Tampa after suffering a fall on Friday morning. The incident occurred outside a restaurant where he had been at the bar. He left his drink and phone behind before walking across the street and falling suddenly.
The fall caused injuries to his face, including a cut to his head. Flair was transported to a local hospital by ambulance. The reason for his abrupt departure from the restaurant remains unknown.
Hours earlier, Flair had posted on social media explaining that he could not fly to an appearance in Seattle. He cited a blood clot in his leg as the reason he was unable to travel the distance.

In the statement, Flair expressed disappointment over canceling his scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con. He emphasized that he needed to prioritize his health and recovery. Flair mentioned that a procedure is scheduled for the affected vein, after which doctors expect him to be cleared for more travel.

Flair has a history of significant health problems. In 2017, he underwent surgery for a severe intestinal blockage that resulted in a month-long hospital stay. He attributed those issues to heavy drinking and was given only a 20 percent chance of survival at the time.

title: Comeback Watch: Drew McIntyre’s WWE Return Status Takes New Turn After Latest Announcement
raw_title: Drew McIntyre’s WWE Return Status Takes New Turn After Latest Announcement
summary_src: Drew McIntyre’s WWE comeback might have to wait a little longer. The Scottish Warrior has been missing from WWE television for six months, and November 7 was looking like a possible date for his return.
body: On October 24, WWE’s official UK account confirmed that McIntyre will appear at Zuffa Boxing 12 on November 7 at the Copper Box Arena in London. He’ll be joined by fellow WWE Superstar Bayley, with VIP meet-and-greet tickets now available for the event. The announcement puts a serious dent in speculation that McIntyre could make his return at Crown Jewel, which is scheduled for the same date at Riyadh Season Stadium. While WWE hasn’t officially ruled him out of the Premium Live Event, having him advertised for an appearance in another country makes a surprise return considerably less likely. McIntyre hasn’t appeared on WWE programming since WrestleMania 42 Night One, where he lost to Jacob Fatu in an Unsanctioned Match. Since then, he’s been busy working on Hollywood projects, including Highlander and The Last Druid . With those filming commitments now wrapped up, questions about his WWE return have only grown. McIntyre also added to the speculation by sharing footage of himself training inside a wrestling ring , but he never provided an official comeback date. McIntyre recently addressed the subject while speaking to Collider about Agent of Shadows . When the conversation turned toward potentially bringing Chase DeMoor into WWE, McIntyre made it clear that he wasn’t ready to discuss his own return. “The wheels are turning. The wheels are turning. Like leave that with me. I mean right now we’re talking today about Hollywood Drew. We’re not worrying about my comeback right now, but the wheels are turning.” Now WWE’s latest announcement gives a better idea of where McIntyre will be on November 7, and it apparently won’t be inside a wrestling ring in Saudi Arabia. Instead, he’ll be meeting fans alongside Bayley at a boxing event in London. Of course, WWE could always change its plans, but McIntyre’s advertised appearance makes Crown Jewel an unlikely destination for his comeback. After six months away, fans are still waiting to see when the Scottish Warrior will finally return to television. At least one thing is clear — WWE has plans for him on November 7, even if those plans don’t involve wrestling. title: Bryce Remsburg Names Lincoln Financial Field as Potential All In Venue
raw_title: Bryce Remsburg: If AEW Was Looking For A Domestic Stadium To Host All In, I Do Think Lincoln Financial Field Would Be In The Conversation
summary_src: Lincoln Financial Field hosting the event is a possibility. In September 2026, Fightful Select reported that the general feeling from those connected to AEW is that the 2027 installment of All In will take place in North America in some form.
body: In September 2026, Fightful Select reported that the general feeling from those connected to AEW is that the 2027 installment of All In will take place in North America in some form. All Elite Wrestling referee Bryce Remsburg guest appeared on The Certified Mark Show and was asked about the chances of AEW running a show at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. He stated that if AEW were looking for a domestic venue to host All In, Lincoln Financial would be in the conversation. He doesn’t think it’ll happen in 2027, but does believe it’s a possibility in the future. “I will say, the fact they’ve hosted wrestling before, which is WrestleMania, is a positive. That means they know what they’re doing, they know what to do, and I will say Philadelphia has been one of the best (places for) AEW since it started so, if we were looking for a domestic stadium to host All In at, I do think The Linc would be in the conversation. I don’t think it’s gonna happen next year… I’m not sure we have demand for a Linc show… But never, ever, ever say never. I’ll say that.” He continued, “There’s no way I could say, ‘No way it’s never happening. Definitely not…’ I’m saying this with actual insider knowledge. It is possible. It’s definitely possible.” The 2026 All In event took place at Wembley Stadium in London, England. The show was headlined by Will Ospreay defeating Kenny Omega to become AEW World Champion.
summary: AEW referee Bryce Remsburg appeared on The Certified Mark Show and discussed the possibility of All In being held at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia. Per Fightful Select, he noted the venue has previously hosted WrestleMania and that Philadelphia has been one of AEW's strongest markets since the promotion launched. Remsburg believes the stadium would be in the conversation for a domestic All In but does not expect it to happen in 2027.

title: WWE HOFer JBL Dismisses Long-Standing Rumor Of HBK/Vader Beef
raw_title: WWE HOFer JBL Dismisses Long-Standing Rumor Of HBK/Vader Beef
summary_src: JBL says stories about Shawn Michaels and Vader's bad blood in WWE are overblown.
body: WWE At SummerSlam 1996, Shawn Michaels defended the WWE Championship against Vader, in the main event. The match is often recalled for Michaels breaking character mid-match after Vader wasn't positioned correctly for a spot , and claims that the 'Heartbreak Kid' further complained about Vader backstage to the point where the returning veteran was taken off screen. Despite the online consensus, John 'Bradshaw' Layfield claims that the accusations levied against Michaels for all these years have largely been incorrect. "The part about Shawn not liking to work with Vader because he was stiff? That's a hundred percent not true," he claimed during an episode of " Something To Wrestle ." JBL admitted that Michaels was a bit of a perfectionist about in-ring work at this time, but asserts that HBK actually didn't care about how Vader worked, because he was a tough guy. "Shawn didn't mind contact, so that wasn't an issue," he said. What JBL does think affected Vader's run in WWE was the timing of him coming into the promotion, because by 1996, Vader's body had largely begun to fail him and he had begun to lose confidence in his own ability . "[Vader] gets down there [WWE], and has to be off the gas [steroids], and when that comes, you know he's not as big, he's not as strong, he's not the physically imposing guy, and physically he can't quite do what he did." The veteran further emphasized that the Vader fans saw in WWE wasn't the one fans got used to who competed in Japan or WCW, and Michaels was actually upset because he expected that Vader. "Shawn had all the pressure in the world," JBL added, pointing out that the New Generation Era brought added pressure to big stars. "There was so much pressure on him, on Bret [Hart], and the champions of those days."
summary: The match is often recalled for Michaels breaking character mid-match after Vader wasn't positioned correctly for a spot . That's a hundred percent not true, he claimed during an episode of  Something To Wrestle . JBL admitted that Michaels was a bit of a perfectionist about in-ring work for now.

body: UFC Featherweight contender Kevin Vallejos has staked his claim at a fight against Alexander Volkanovski for the 145lb title, should Volk survive against Movsar Evloev at UFC 333. Speaking to MMA Fighting , Vallejos has claimed that he wants the current champ (who recently appeared in the Street Fighter movie alongside Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns) to retain the belt so he can get the big title fight at some point next year. Vallejos is set to face Aljamain Sterling in November, and if he beats the former champ in Doha, he will very likely be given a chance at the 145lb gold. “I would like Volkanovski (to win at UFC 333),” Vallejos claimed. “I would like that because if I knock Sterling out, I would like to fight Volkanovski. I would like to take the title away from Volkanovski. “Evloev also has everything he needs to win,” Vallejos continued. “He (Evloev) is 20-0, he has a very good record. But beating a guy who dominated the entire division for a long time — I think (beating Volkanovski holds) more weight when it comes to winning the title.” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals When He Considered Leaving WWE
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Shares When He Thought About Leaving WWE
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov officially departed WWE in August when his contract expired, and he decided not to renew his deal. Dragunov had been off WWE TV since April when he competed in the Andre The Giant Memorial Battle Royal. He joined AEW after his deal expired, making his debut at AEW WrestleDream.
body: Ilja Dragunov officially departed WWE in August when his contract expired, and he decided not to renew his deal. Dragunov had been off WWE TV since April when he competed in the Andre The Giant Memorial Battle Royal. He joined AEW after his deal expired, making his debut at AEW WrestleDream. Speaking to Ariel Helwani on The Ariel Helwani Show , Dragunov was asked when he thought of leaving WWE. “After I tore my ACL, I was fortunate to win a championship straight back on my comeback, which was an amazing moment for me that I still cherish. After I dropped the belt, things went into directions where I feel like it could’ve been better and more time to go into a story or something outside of holding a championship. Around April, maybe even a month before that, I was already just thinking about it. It never changed anything about my work because I love what I do and I make every minute count, but we all have feelings and we all want to devote ourselves to this, but I know it’s part of the business. I wouldn’t change that,” he said. Elsewhere during the interview, Dragunov gave more insight into his decision to leave WWE. You can find his full comments here . Dragunov made his AEW in-ring debut on Wednesday’s Dynamite, defeating “Speedball” Mike Bailey. title: Ric Flair’s Facebook Posts Raise Questions After He Claims He No Longer Owns His Page
raw_title: Ric Flair’s Facebook Posts Raise Questions After He Claims He No Longer Owns His Page
summary_src: Ric Flair says he doesn’t own his Facebook page anymore, but something about that explanation isn’t adding up. The WWE Hall of Famer blasted the people behind his account for posting content while he was hospitalized, calling their behavior reckless and inappropriate.
body: On October 24, Flair broke his silence after being hospitalized following a nasty fall in Tampa . He shared a photo of himself with a bandage over his injured right eye and thanked the doctors at Tampa General Hospital for treating him. But his message took an unexpected turn when he started talking about Facebook. “And Just So You Know For Those Who Were Asking And Wondering, I Don’t Own My Own Facebook Page Anymore. I Apologize For The Reckless Posting Behavior On My Facebook When I Was In The Hospital. It Was Completely Inappropriate!” Flair didn’t explain exactly which posts upset him, but a look at his verified Facebook page gives a better idea of what was happening while he was dealing with his medical emergency. The account continued sharing wrestling clips, throwback photos and promotional content throughout the time Flair was hospitalized. One post featured an old clip of Flair with the caption, “Only true champions can carry the gold! WOOOOOO!” Another featured wrestling footage with the caption, “Teamwork Makes The Dream Work! WOOOOOO!” Other posts included a throwback photo of Flair in a pink robe with the caption, “I May Wear Pink, But Stealing Hearts Is My True Signature Move!” Another showed an old photograph of Flair alongside the message, “I’m Just A Humble Nature Boy… With A Little Extra Charm!” There’s nothing particularly unusual about those posts on their own. They’re the kind of nostalgic wrestling content that regularly appears on Flair’s social media accounts. The issue is that they continued going out while Flair was in the hospital with injuries to his face. It’s entirely possible those posts were scheduled in advance and simply continued publishing without anyone stopping them. There’s no confirmation of who actually uploaded the content or whether the person managing the account knew what was happening with Flair at the time. The account also appears to have been professionally managed, with AP Brand Group a possible connection. However, there’s no confirmation that the company was responsible for these particular posts or currently controls Flair’s Facebook presence. But here’s where things get even more confusing. Despite Flair saying he no longer owns his Facebook page, the account also shared the same health update that appeared on his official X and Instagram accounts. That raises an obvious question about how his personal statement ended up on a page he claims is no longer his. Of course, owning a Facebook page and having access to publish content are two different things. Flair could still have some involvement with the account, or whoever manages it could simply be sharing his statements across multiple platforms. The matching post doesn’t prove Flair personally has access, but it does suggest that someone handling the Facebook page is still distributing his official updates. title: Backstage Buzz: Word On Elayna Black Potentially Joining AEW

body: Before signing with WWE, Elayna Black wrestled multiple matches on AEW Dark in 2020. Elayna Black is currently signed to the TNA Wrestling roster and competes in the Knockouts division. However, in the latest Fightful Select Answers Q&A , Sean Ross Sapp was asked if it was possible for Black to make a return to AEW. Sapp referenced how Black spoke about being open to joining AEW last year before she ultimately signed with TNA. Despite her comments on The Ariel Helwani Show , Sapp says that he never heard of any overtures between her and AEW in the time between her WWE release and TNA signing. Although there were some claims that she skipped extra work in AEW for a WWE tryout, Sapp says that a source in AEW said there was no issue stemming from that. title: Leon Slater Calls TNA World Title Reign Surreal
raw_title: Leon Slater Says TNA World Championship Is 'Finally Beginning To Feel Mine'
summary_src: Leon Slater comments on his TNA World Championship reign. At TNA Bound for Glory, Leon Slater defeated Nic Nemeth and became the youngest TNA World Champion in the company’s history. He accomplished his goal five years earlier than he predicted.
body: At TNA Bound for Glory, Leon Slater defeated Nic Nemeth and became the youngest TNA World Champion in the company’s history. He accomplished his goal five years earlier than he predicted. Speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast , Slater commented on his title reign. “It feels very surreal, man. It took a while for it to settle in because I kind of felt like I was carrying Nic Nemeth’s belt around for a while just because I’ve so used to seeing him with it,” Slater said. “Obviously, I still live at home, which is a great balance to have between my professional life and my personal life. So as any other 22-year-old does after he wins a world title, I hopped on GTA with my friends the other day. I was playing my PlayStation, and I had the TNA Championship set up on my TV table, and I was on the party with my friends. I go, ‘You know what I’m looking at right now?’ They go, ‘Oh yeah, we’re driving through Los Santos, whatever.” I go, “No, no, bro. I’m looking at the TNA World Championship.” Like, it’s in my room as I’m playing, and it was just so difficult for me to compute. This is the same room I’ve sat in for the past, you know 10-15 years. It’s the same game I’ve been playing for the past 13 years, and the only difference is I’ve got the actual TNA World Championship on my TV table. So, it’s finally beginning to feel mine. I’m excited for it to take me in a new direction. I’m excited to take it in a new direction as well and make some magic as TNA World Champion.” Slater is currently scheduled to defeat the title against Trey Miguel at TNA Destination X. title: Leon Slater Says Option C Promo Made Him TNA's Top Guy
raw_title: Leon Slater Feels Like His Option C Promo At TNA Lockdown Was The Moment He Became 'The Guy' In TNA
summary_src: Leon Slater comments on his Option C promo at TNA Lockdown. On the show, Leon Slater competed in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match for the TNA X Division Title. He defeated Cedric Alexander to become the new champion.
body: On the show, Leon Slater competed in a Last Man Standing Steel Cage match for the TNA X Division Title. He defeated Cedric Alexander to become the new champion. Later that night, Slater announced that he’s exercising Option C to go after Nic Nemeth’s TNA World Title. Speaking on the I Love Wrestling Podcast , Slater was asked if the night he enacted Option C was the moment he stamped his spot as a future main eventer in TNA. “Yeah, absolutely. I think it’s rare that we get these pinpoint moments in wrestling. I’m not comparing here but just to use an analogy, the Austin 3:16 promo for example. You can point to that moment and you go, ‘Yeah, that’s when he became who he is.’ I feel like, for me, in my TNA run, the moment of me cashing in Option C was like, ‘Leon’s not the kid anymore. He is the guy now.’ Obviously being able to follow through on that at Bound for Glory just solidified that even further. I think people are going to look back on that Option C promo and that cash in in Chicago and use that as a moment to where I entered the next chapter of my career, which is where I am now.” Later, Slater says that as soon as Carlos Silva handed him the title at Lockdown, he knew that he wanted to go for the TNA World Championship. “I knew, as soon as he [Carlos Silva] handed it to me, I’m not going to lie. It’s not even a thing of like me thinking the X Division is below me now because I don’t think the X Division will ever be below anyone. It is one of the most legendary divisions in all of professional wrestling and it influenced and changed the game more than I can even put into words. But over the course of me having that initial reign, I feel like I did things that I could never even imagine. Whether it was having the title every week for three or four months on NXT television and having it on that platform or having it on SmackDown against Carmelo Hayes or having it walking into John Cena’s final match. You know all of these moments and all of these matches that I’ve managed to have. This is even excluding all the stuff I did in TNA with the championship, my matches with Je’Von [Evans] and Myron [Reed] and Cedric [Alexander] and Rich Swann. I felt like I had such a beautiful run as X Division champion that I just couldn’t see a world where me being as close to–I feel like I’m a very similar person now to when I was holding the X Division. So I think it’d be difficult for me to take that to new heights or different heights as this version of myself. So I feel like it was time to move on from that and move up to the World Heavyweight Title division and see if I could hang there and see if what I thought in my head was true. It turns out it is.” Elsewhere in the interview, Slater commented on his TNA World Title win. Fans can read his full comments here . body: U.S. intelligence officials have warned Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Iranian plans to attack Americans have reached “advanced stages,” according to The New York Times. In a headline report , the Times said Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sent Rubio a memo warning of a significant increase in Iranian efforts to target U.S. personnel. The memo stated that intelligence agencies had received information indicating that Iran had “substantially increased efforts to target U.S. personnel.” The lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries. U.S. officials told the Times that agencies now assess the threat against Americans in the Middle East and elsewhere to be at its highest level since the war with Iran began in February. The intelligence reportedly includes potential targets outside the Middle East, including in Europe. One official added that Iran’s ambitions to carry out attacks exceeded its ability to do so. The warning adds to security concerns surrounding Saudi Arabia, where WWE is scheduled to stage Crown Jewel in Riyadh on November 7. As reported on Wednesday , nonessential U.S. Embassy personnel and their families have been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia. The Times now reports that the drawdown was directly connected to recent intelligence concerning Iranian attack plans. Despite the security situation, TKO executive chair Ari Emanuel said on Friday that Crown Jewel remained scheduled to proceed. Emanuel said TKO has a team monitoring developments daily and that the company could move an event if circumstances required it. Friday’s edition of WWE SmackDown included multiple promotional spots for Crown Jewel.

title: Injury Update: MVP Shuts Down Rumors The Hurt Syndicate Refused to Put Wrestlers Over in AEW
raw_title: MVP Shuts Down Rumors The Hurt Syndicate Refused to Put Wrestlers Over in AEW
summary_src: MVP is done hearing that The Hurt Syndicate doesn’t want to put people over in AEW. After weeks of chatter about Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP supposedly pushing back on creative, MVP jumped on Twitter and basically called the entire story BS.
body: MVP responded on Twitter after an account brought up several rumors surrounding the faction. Those included claims that The Hurt Syndicate had refused to put certain wrestlers over, that MVP was influencing Lashley and Benjamin to say no to ideas, and that he had backstage heat with important members of AEW creative. MVP didn’t dance around any of it. He flat-out denied the claims and even hinted that he may now have an idea where some of the rumors are coming from. “Rumor? Nah man. You are absolutely Wrong!!!! None of this is true. But now I know where this whisper campaign is coming from! 😉” Apparently that wasn’t enough, because MVP then opened Twitter and saw even more talk about The Hurt Syndicate. That’s when he really went off, calling the stories “blatant lies” and demanding to know who was feeding them to people. “So I open up Twitter to see lies being reported about The Hurt Syndicate. BLATANT LIES!!! Who is the source of these lies?” MVP also went directly after the idea that The Hurt Syndicate didn’t want to put other wrestlers over. According to him, they actually wanted to work with younger talent and were even willing to drop the AEW World Tag Team Championships back to Private Party. “To the contrary, we wanted to work with younger talent! We wanted to drop the tag titles BACK to Private Party!!! STOP BELIEVING THE BS!” That Private Party comment certainly gets right to the heart of the controversy. Lashley and Benjamin previously took the AEW World Tag Team Titles from Private Party, and MVP is now saying The Hurt Syndicate wanted to eventually return the favor. All of this comes after Sean Ross Sapp recently addressed the group’s situation on The Hump. While Sapp said he didn’t know why The Hurt Syndicate hasn’t been featured as consistently lately, he claimed there had been situations where members of the group didn’t want to put other wrestlers over . “Listen, I know there’s been a lot of talk about them like not wanting to put people over. There’s definitely been some situations where they haven’t wanted to. That has been a thing.” Sapp didn’t say which members allegedly pushed back, who they supposedly didn’t want to lose to or whether any of it had anything to do with their reduced television presence. Now MVP is pushing back hard against the narrative that The Hurt Syndicate has been difficult when it comes to putting other talent over. Whatever is actually happening with The Hurt Syndicate’s AEW booking, MVP clearly isn’t staying quiet while these stories make the rounds. He’s denying the rumors, saying the group wanted to help younger talent and even claiming they were ready to put the titles back on Private Party. title: Ilja Dragunov Explains Exit From WWE For AEW
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Reflects On Final Stretch Of WWE Run, Decision To Join AEW
summary_src: Now that he is "All Elite," Ilja Dragunov has reflected on his final year on the WWE roster.
body: AEW/Speedy Ruiz After weeks of rumors and reports, Ilja Dragunov is officially "All Elite." The former WWE Superstar made his AEW debut at the WrestleDream pay-per-view on October 17 , and has already had a successful in-ring debut against "Speedball" Mike Bailey on "AEW Dynamite." His move to AEW comes after a seven year run with WWE that did see the "Mad Dragon" see success, but according to the man himself, could have ended a lot better. Dragunov recently spoke to The Takedown on Sports Illustrated, and admitted that he needed to breathe new air after his return from injury in October of last year. "It has been a very complicated time for me because, you see, I came back from an ACL tear that happened in the most unexciting way possible. I worked myself through rehab and was training very hard, and was very dedicated. I came back, and I won the United States Championship basically on my return, which was an awesome, memorable moment. But then certain times, like after I dropped the belt and I was going through my next performances, I felt like I felt in my gut things are different. And I don't blame anybody. I'm a gentleman and I have way too much respect for the last seven years that I the most of my 20s that I spent with the company. But I felt like it is fine for me and reasonable to ask myself, 'Is there more? Is there a new air I can breathe?'" Dragunov has been open about his departure from WWE since his arrival in AEW, stating that he didn't feel that WWE's renewed contract offer was enough for him to commit his future there, and decided to take his talents elsewhere. It's not yet known the length of his AEW contract, though AEW fans will be hoping he sticks around for many years to come.
summary: Ilja Dragunov made his AEW debut at WrestleDream on October 17 and picked up a win over Mike Bailey on Dynamite. The former WWE star recently told The Takedown on Sports Illustrated that his seven-year run ended on a sour note after he returned from an ACL tear, captured the United States Championship on his first night back, then sensed a shift following the title loss. Dragunov said he needed fresh air and a new environment.

Nothing’s been cancelled,” he said. “We have a whole team kind of working on this, and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin The Rise of Independent Wrestling Promotions in Modern Sports Entertainment By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-24 08:43:00 Professional wrestling has undergone significant changes as independent promotions attract growing attention from fans, performers, and industry professionals. While major organizations continue to dominate mainstream wrestling, smaller companies are creating opportunities for alternative storytelling, distinctive wrestling styles, and closer connections between performers and audiences. Independent wrestling has existed for decades, but digital platforms and changing viewing habits have made it easier for regional promotions to reach supporters beyond their local communities. Fans can now discover emerging talent, follow independent events, and purchase merchandise directly from organizations that previously depended almost entirely on live attendance. This development has created an increasingly diverse wrestling environment where creativity and entrepreneurial thinking are essential. Running a successful independent promotion requires more than organizing entertaining matches. Financial management, venue coordination, marketing, and audience engagement all contribute to building a sustainable business. Understanding these responsibilities reveals why independent wrestling has become an important part of modern sports entertainment. Behind the excitement of live wrestling is a demanding business operation. Independent promoters must coordinate venues, negotiate performer agreements, arrange insurance, manage ticket sales, and organize promotional campaigns. Unlike major wrestling companies with extensive administrative departments, smaller promotions often rely on limited teams handling several responsibilities simultaneously. Managing equipment and office resources is another part of operating efficiently. Promotions regularly produce contracts, event schedules, merchandise labels, promotional materials, and documentation for performers and venues. As organizations expand or replace their office equipment, they may accumulate unused supplies that still have commercial value. A promotion retiring an older office printer, for example, could recover money from unopened replacement cartridges through www.selltoner.com . Redirecting funds from surplus office inventory toward event production is one practical example of how smaller entertainment businesses can make better use of their existing resources. These operational decisions rarely attract attention from wrestling audiences, but they contribute to financial stability. Promotions that manage their expenses carefully have greater flexibility to invest in production quality, talent development, and memorable live experiences. title: Charlotte Flair Says Vulnerability Boosts Her Strength
raw_title: WWE's Charlotte Flair: 'Being Vulnerable Makes You Powerful'
summary_src: WWE star Charlotte Flair opened up on how embracing vulnerability allowed her to connect with fans better.
body: WWE's Charlotte Flair reflected on how her latest run has allowed her to embrace her vulnerability for a greater connection with fans. Flair spoke to Russell Wilson and Kyle Long for " Set, Hut! " about the pressure that came with being Ric Flair's daughter, her prevalence in the main event picture and the disconnect with fans that came as a result. "Being Ric's kid came with a lot of hate. I have been a bad guy for the last 10 years. I love it. But I tore my knee two years ago. I came back and I had kind of a disconnect with the fans," she explained, going on to say that, as the Charlotte character grew, so did the "armor due to the fans' criticism." "But then I learned while I was gone, being vulnerable is what makes you powerful and resilient and strong," she continued. Flair said that was the goal of her Player's Tribune article , opening up to the audience and separating the "Bada**" that was Charlotte and the real-life Ashley Fliehr behind that character. She said that allowed her to connect with the audience on a different level. "Being able to share that side of me with the audience, from being on top for 10 years. I have won 14 titles, I am synonymous with gold. But I haven't had a title match since in the last year since I lost at WrestleMania. It's like, how is this my best year? Which is crazy to think, but really it's the bond with the fans." She added that when she does turn heel, she's aware that it's going to mean more because she has had the opportunity to share who she really was. But she has learned that it's not her "The Queen" character that made her who she was, rather everything she has gone through in her personal life to get to this point.

title: Zack Sabre Jr. Recalls Shibata's 2021 NJPW Return Reaction

summary_src: Zack Sabre Jr. looks back on the exhibition. On day 19 of the 2021 New Japan Pro-Wrestling G1 Climax tournament, an exhibition match took place, and one of the participants was Zack Sabre Jr.
body: On day 19 of the 2021 New Japan Pro-Wrestling G1 Climax tournament, an exhibition match took place, and one of the participants was Zack Sabre Jr. His opponent was not known and coming out to face Sabre Jr. was Katsuyori Shibata, who had not wrestled in NJPW since 2017 up until that point. While guest appearing on CMLL’s Esto es Lucha Podcast , Sabre Jr. said he’s never experienced anything like when the audience gasped at hearing Shibata’s music that night. “It was an exhibition, but, his return… it was obviously during the COVID restrictions where the Japanese fans were restricted from being able to vocally cheer or make any noise and I’ve never experienced anything like the silent gasp of when the first bars of his theme music played where it was like, I felt in sync with the audience. That epitomized the power of pro wrestling.” Shibata is currently signed to AEW/ROH. He is a member of The Opps with Samoa Joe, HOOK, and ROH World Television Champion Action Andretti.

title: Fans Clown AEW Over Kamille’s Birthday Post Amid Her Continued TV Absence
raw_title: Fans Clown AEW Over Kamille’s Birthday Post Amid Her Continued TV Absence
summary_src: AEW tried to wish Kamille a happy birthday, but the post ended up reminding fans of a completely different question — where the hell has she been? The former NWA Women’s Champion has barely been seen on AEW television this year, and fans wasted no time calling the company out over it.
body: AEW posted a birthday message for Kamille on Twitter on October 24 . Instead of simply joining in with birthday wishes, plenty of fans immediately turned the replies into a discussion about her lengthy absence from television. One fan couldn’t understand how Kamille managed to disappear from AEW programming all over again after finally returning earlier this year: “I don’t understand how she disappeared again.” Another fan went directly after Tony Khan and demanded an answer about Kamille’s whereabouts. Some fans were apparently surprised to even be reminded that Kamille remains part of AEW. One questioned whether she was actually still on the company’s roster. Another fan took things a little further and openly mocked the fact that Kamille is still employed by AEW despite barely appearing: “She still works there? LOLOLOLOLOL.” One reply even turned AEW’s birthday message into a joke about how much time Kamille has spent away from television. “Happy birthday. I’m glad you got two years off for your birthday present from AEW. 🤷‍♂️” The reaction comes after Sean Ross Sapp recently confirmed during a Fightful Q&A that Kamille is still under contract with AEW. He also said there hasn’t been a long-term creative plan for her since she was originally removed from television during her storyline with Mercedes Moné. Kamille briefly returned at Dynasty on April 12 , attacking Willow Nightingale backstage before defeating Big Anne on the Zero Hour pre-show. Three days later, she lost to Nightingale in a TBS Championship match on Dynamite and disappeared from AEW television again. According to Sean Ross Sapp, that short comeback was essentially what AEW had planned for her at the time . Kamille was brought back to pick up a quick victory before putting over Nightingale, rather than to begin another extended run. “There was never a long term plan for her after she was taken off TV for the Mercedes angle ever. They brought her back to get a quick win and put over Willow in her challenge. That’s it. There’s never been a long term plan.” Kamille has remained busy with projects outside AEW, but her wrestling appearances have been extremely limited. Her only match since losing to Nightingale came for Diamond Championship Wrestling, with the bout airing in August. AEW’s birthday post certainly got people talking about Kamille again, just probably not in the way the company expected. With her still under contract but nowhere to be found on television, fans clearly haven’t forgotten about her absence. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.
summary: The latest: AEW posted a birthday message for Kamille on Twitter on October 24 . Instead of simply joining in with birthday wishes, plenty of the audience immediately turned the replies into a discussion about her lengthy absence from television.

title: Billy Gunn Explains Joining The Acclaimed In AEW
raw_title: Billy Gunn Details Thought Process Behind Joining The Acclaimed In AEW
summary_src: Billy Gunn recently shared his thoughts on the reasoning behind his pairing with Anthony Bowens and Max Caster in AEW, explaining what he brought to the group.
body: AEW Billy Gunn's pairing with Max Caster and Anthony Bowens as The Acclaimed might not have made sense on paper , but after the angle started rolling, Gunn leaned heavily into his Attitude Era character and became "Daddy A**" while their stable exploded in popularity amongst AEW fans. Speaking on "Inside the Ropes," Gunn explained the genesis of the group. "I still have equity in this business, so [putting] me with them, it kind of makes people take notice a little bit," Gunn said. The veteran joked that he might come off as arrogant, but he genuinely believes his inclusion legitimized Caster and Bowens. "The Acclaimed wasn't just me — it was all three of us. It was just — everything just kind of fell into place." Gunn fondly recalled their shared entrance, which saw Caster rapping, Bowens calling out the hometown, and him joining them all to "scissor" taunt at the end. Gunn acknowledged that fans were originally confused by the taunt, but the people eventually got it. "I am a parent's worse nightmare. Like, the first half of my career I'm pointing at my crotch, and the second half I'm 'scissoring' people — like a lesbian!" he exclaimed. In recent years, Gunn seems to have heavily drawn back on his in-ring appearances, competing on occasion outside of AEW. His last match for his former promotion took place on "AEW Collision" back in January. Both Caster and Bowens have since parted ways with AEW , with Caster specifically being at the center of controversy after debuting in TNA and being cut loose due to the content of his pre-match rap. Caster then announced his hiatus from wrestling shortly after.
summary: Billy Gunn joined Max Caster and Anthony Bowens to form The Acclaimed in AEW. On Inside the Ropes, Gunn said his presence drew attention due to his equity in the business and helped legitimize the duo as the trio's chemistry developed naturally. He recalled their popular entrance with Caster's rap, Bowens naming the hometown and the group ending with the scissor taunt that fans eventually embraced.

llm_long: Billy Gunn has been part of All Elite Wrestling since 2020. He insisted that his sons Austin and Colten complete their college education before pursuing careers in the promotion.
Gunn stated that he refused to help get his sons hired by AEW until they graduated. He emphasized that his own success in wrestling did not guarantee they would succeed in the same field.

On the day Austin Gunn graduated, he handed his diploma to his father and immediately asked when they could start in wrestling. Gunn had required college graduation as the first condition before any discussion of entering the business.
Colten Gunn also decided to pursue wrestling after having a different career path mapped out until age 60. The choice surprised both Gunn and his wife, given the demanding nature of the profession.

Gunn explained that his frequent absences from home, including 300 days on the road each year early in his career, made him hesitant for his sons to follow the same path. He wanted them to have more stable family lives than he experienced.
Although Gunn trained his sons to a certain point, he required them to seek and complete AEW tryouts on their own. He did not ask for them to be hired simply because they were his children.

title: Zack Sabre Jr. Refuses To Claim TMDK Leadership
raw_title: Zack Sabre Jr. Would Never Claim To Be Leader Of TMDK, Says It Belongs To Australian Wrestling
summary_src: It is more fulfilling for Zack Sabre Jr. to see people within the group thriving as opposed to being the leader. The T.M.D.K.
body: It is more fulfilling for Zack Sabre Jr. to see people within the group thriving as opposed to being the leader. The T.M.D.K. (The Mighty Don’t Kneel) faction has different branches within the pro wrestling space. It originates in Australia. It started with Shane Haste and Mikey Nicholls, who are scheduled to reunite in Pro Wrestling NOAH on 10/25. The New Japan Pro-Wrestling branch consists of Zack Sabre Jr., Robbie Eagles, Kosei Fujita, Ryohei Oiwa, Bad Dude Tito, and Hartley Jackson. Sabre Jr. was interviewed for CMLL’s Esto es Lucha Podcast and stated that he would never claim to be the leader of the group. “Shane Haste very smartly came up with ‘The Frontman’ because there is no leader. Mikey Nicholls and Shane Haste started T.M.D.K. in 2006, 2007, when the Australian independent wrestling scene was really sort of still trying to create something. I would never claim to be the leader of T.M.D.K., because it would never be mine. T.M.D.K. belongs to Australian wrestling, and as much now, I think with (Ryohei) Oiwa and (Kosei) Fujita, I think something that two Australian wrestlers, Mike and Shane, two people that I spent a lot of time with in the NOAH Dojo and really worked their asses off to make something from nothing in Australia to get to where they got to and now, when I see Fujita and Oiwa with the T.M.D.K. colors and T.M.D.K. flags, winning the biggest tournaments in Japan, that’s much more fulfilling for me rather than claiming to be a leader.”
summary: Zack Sabre Jr. says it is more fulfilling to watch members of TMDK thrive rather than position himself as the group's leader. He credits Shane Haste and Mikey Nicholls with founding TMDK in Australia in 2006 or 2007 and insists the faction belongs to Australian wrestling. The New Japan Pro-Wrestling branch features Sabre Jr., Robbie Eagles, Kosei Fujita, Ryohei Oiwa, Bad Dude Tito and Hartley Jackson, while Haste and Nicholls are set to reunite in Pro Wrestling NOAH on October 25.

title: Ric Flair Hospitalized After Fall in Tampa
raw_title: WWE Legend Ric Flair, 77, Hospitalized After Falling Outside Restaurant While ‘Dealing’ with Blood Clot in His Leg
body: His daughter Charlotte Flair said in a social media post that the WWE legend is "going to be ok" Ric, 77, had canceled a Seattle appearance hours before the fall as doctors limited his travel due to a blood clot in his leg Ric Flair is recovering in the hospital after a fall outside a restaurant in Florida. The retired WWE legend, 77, was injured in a fall outside Wagamama in Tampa on Friday, Oct. 23, TMZ reported. The incident occurred hours after Ric revealed on Instagram that an upcoming appearance was being canceled due to a blood clot in his leg. In photos obtained by TMZ, Ric is seen lying on his back while surrounded by medical staff. He is also pictured being transported into an ambulance. Ric left his phone and drink behind as he walked across the street after visiting the restaurant that morning, per the outlet. He reportedly cut his head in the fall and his eye was "bleeding extensively." Ric's daughter, WWE wrestler Charlotte Flair , shared an update on his condition in a post on X on Saturday, Oct. 24. "Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head … (ps: he's going to be ok)," she wrote. Also on Oct. 24, Ric shared a photo of himself sitting in a chair with a bandage over his eye. "Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger," he wrote in the caption of his Instagram post . "Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay," added Ric. The wrestling legend previously shared a lengthy post about his health, hours before he fell. "I want to sincerely apologize to my agent, Steve Solomon … and especially all my fans in Seattle for having to cancel my scheduled appearance," said Ric. "Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first." "Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs," he continued. "It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice." Ric said that he is scheduled to undergo a procedure "to strip the affected vein," which will hopefully allow him to travel more and continue with his work commitments. "Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment, and I am incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding, and continued support," he concluded. In June 2025, the former wrestling star revealed to PEOPLE he had skin cancer for "the second time in three years." Ric announced in an Instagram post a month later that he was "cancer-free."
summary: The 77-year-old retired WWE star fell outside a Florida restaurant on October 23, cutting his head and causing extensive bleeding around his eye. He had canceled a scheduled appearance in Seattle that same day after doctors restricted his travel due to a blood clot in his leg. His daughter Charlotte Flair later posted on social media that her father is going to be okay.

body: According to Sean Ross Sapp of Fightful Select , Francis’ current TNA deal is set to expire toward the end of the year. During his time with the promotion, Francis captured the TNA Digital Media Championship and brought back the Canadian International Heavyweight Championship. He’s also been involved in several major storylines, working with names like Joe Hendry, Mike Santana and Elijah. Francis recently made it clear that he’s happy with how things are going in TNA. During an interview with The Wrestling Classic , he explained why he feels more appreciated by the company than he did during his WWE days. “I felt like I have a home in TNA because they recognize what I bring to the table.” Francis also praised the creative freedom he’s been given, explaining that he’s able to play a bigger role in putting together his storylines. “I’m calling the plays. You know what I’m saying? And they sending me out there first to set the tone.” Before finding success in TNA, Francis competed in WWE as Top Dolla and also made appearances for NWA and MLW. However, his latest run has given him a chance to establish himself as a regular part of TNA programming. For now, there’s no indication that Francis is looking to jump to another promotion. Both sides want to work out a new deal, so unless something changes during negotiations, it looks like he’ll be sticking around. raw_title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Gets Promising Health Update After Being Hospitalized
body: ‘The Nature Boy’s fall came hours after he had shared a health update on social media. Flair, 77, broke his silence and shared a promising health update after being hospitalized yesterday. The WWE Hall of Famer issued a statement on his X account, saying that he will be okay after the fall. Flair posted a photo alongside the statement, which showed his right eye bandaged. He expressed his gratitude to the hospital staff and doctors for taking care of him well into the early morning hours. “Thank you all for the messages and prayers! I will get back to you each individually as I get stronger. Thank you to all the Tampa General Hospital staff and doctors that put up with me until 4:30 a.m. I appreciate you all and thank you for everything you did for me. I am focused on my healing and recovery right now,” Flair wrote on X . “I will be okay! And just so you know, for those who were asking and wondering, I don’t own my own Facebook page anymore. I apologize for the reckless posting behavior on my Facebook when I was in the hospital. It was completely inappropriate!” Flair wrote. Although Flair’s fall was a scary situation, particularly because of his age, it is nice to see that he received a promising health update. Ric Flair was forced to cancel an appearance in Seattle, Washington, because of a blood clot in his leg. The WWE Hall of Famer was told that he had to limit his travel, so he regrettably canceled his appearance. Flair revealed that he will be undergoing a procedure soon to address the issue. He then apologized to fans for the inconvenience, but said that he will be prioritizing his health. “I am truly sorry of the inconvenience and disappointment. I’m incredibly grateful for you patience, understanding, and continued support. I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road,” Flair wrote on X . Flair’s hospitalization led to fans extending their best wishes to the pro wrestling legend on social media. His daughter, WWE superstar Charlotte Flair took to social media to update fans on her father’s health. While Flair did sustain some injuries from the fall, most noticeably on his eye, Charlotte reassured fans that he will be okay. Charlotte even shared that her father did not lost his sense of humor, saying that late WWE legend Ultimate Warrior was to blame. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell because of Warrior dropping him on his head. title: The Miz Recalls Early Locker Room Backlash After First WWE Tag Title Victory
raw_title: The Miz Recalls Upsetting WWE Locker Room On The Day Of First Tag Title Win
summary_src: Among the many issues between The Miz and the WWE locker room early in his career, the wrestler recalled "ruffling feathers" on the night he won the tag title.
body: The Miz dealt with numerous problems during his early years in the WWE locker, including the infamous stories of him enduring extreme hazing from the veterans at the time , who didn't consider his entry point into the business through "Tough Enough" as legit. Unfortunately, that wasn't the only time he'd worked the locker room up, as he recounted on WWE Vault how the night he first won tag team gold with John Morrison ended with backstage heat. "We used to shoot 'ECW' before 'SmackDown,' and so me and John Morrison went on ECW — I think it was a CM Punk match — and we went on commentary and we just ripped it apart, and people were upset about that," he recalled. "Then we go out on this match, and we end up winning the tag titles, and we upset even more people because we were celebrating while the story was supposed to be with the other tag team." The Miz claimed that he and Morrison were told to celebrate like they "had just won the Superbowl," and considering it was the first time he won gold in WWE, it wasn't hard for him to act excited. However, the locker room took issue with both wrongs taking place on the same night. Despite that, The Miz recalled the tag team being asked to appear on commentary again the next week, meaning the higher-ups were happy with them. "We were ruffling feathers, a lot of feathers," he recalled. "We started a show called 'The Dirt Sheet' that really, really ruffled feathers. ... 'Going into business for yourself' is what I believe the comment was." "The Dirt Sheet" ended up being one of WWE's earliest forays into a web show , becoming so popular that WWE brought it into live television.
summary: The Miz explained on WWE Vault that he and John Morrison drew heat from the locker room on the night they captured their first WWE tag team championships. After cutting loose on commentary during an ECW taping that preceded SmackDown, the duo was instructed to celebrate wildly upon winning the titles, which clashed with the planned focus on the opposing team. This excitement, especially as it marked Miz's initial WWE gold, further upset veterans who already viewed his Tough Enough background skeptically.

title: UFC 336 to feature two championship fights in Toronto, interim welterweight title added
raw_title: UFC 336 to feature two championship fights in Toronto, interim welterweight title added
summary_src: On Saturday’s broadcast from Abu Dhabi, it was confirmed that two title fights will occur on January 30, when UFC 336 takes place in Toronto.
body: Two championship fights are coming to Toronto, with the UFC releasing a pair of announcements for its first major card of 2027. On Saturday’s broadcast from Abu Dhabi, it was confirmed that two title fights will occur on January 30, when UFC 336 takes place in Toronto. The major note is that the latest interim title is being added to the mix, allowing Carlos Prates and Michael Morales to compete for a belt. An interim welterweight title is being introduced due to champion Islam Makhachev being unable to fight in January. A fight between Makhachev and Prates was being targeted for the January 30 event. Announcer Jon Anik told fellow broadcaster Daniel Cormier that he was informed of the news two days ago. Prates (24-7) is 7-1 in the UFC and on a three-fight winning streak with recent stoppages of former champions Jack Della Maddalena and Leon Edwards in his last two fights. He also has the distinction of being awarded a performance of the night bonus for all seven of his wins inside the promotion. Morales (19-0) has an unblemished record with seven wins in the UFC but has not competed since last November when he stopped Sean Brady. In addition, UFC flyweight champion Joshua Van (18-2) will make the third defense of his title when he meets Manel Kape at UFC 336. Van won the title last December when Alexandre Pantoja sustained an arm injury right away in the first round, and Van was declared the winner by TKO. Pantoja received a rematch in September, with Van winning by unanimous decision, and will be a heavy favorite to be named ‘Fighter of the Year’. Kape (23-7) has been victorious in his last four fights, including Brandon Royval and Kyoji Horiguchi by stoppage. The championship fights are the first announcements for UFC 336 as the UFC returns to Toronto for the first time since January 2024. The card in Canada coincides with its pay-per-views moving to a subscription model on Paramount+ in the country, while its preliminary fights will continue to air on Rogers Sportsnet and Fight Pass.
summary: Two championship fights are coming to Toronto, with the UFC releasing a pair of announcements for its first major card of 2027. Officially, two title fights will occur on January 30, when UFC 336 takes place in Toronto.

The duo later joined forces with Billy Gunn to win the AEW World Trios Championships. Although his latest social media post has fueled discussion about a possible NJPW appearance, a visit to the LA Dojo does not necessarily indicate that a deal is being negotiated.
