title: AEW Sets Women's Blood & Guts Teams on Collision
raw_title: Women’s Blood & Guts teams set, Jay White unveils The Last Outfit on AEW Collision
summary_src: AEW finalized the teams for its women’s Blood & Guts match on Saturday’s Collision, while Jay White named his new faction and Josh Alexander earned a TNT Championship opportunity.
body: AEW finalized the teams for its women’s Blood & Guts match on Saturday’s Collision, while Jay White named his new faction and Josh Alexander earned a TNT Championship opportunity. Collision aired live from the LJVM Coliseum in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, with the women’s Blood & Guts match confirmed for November 4 in Jacksonville, Florida. The setup followed a match between Wrathlander (Kris Statlander & Harley Cameron) and Divine Dominion’s Megan Bayne & Lena Kross. The match ended by disqualification when Thekla, Julia Hart & Skye Blue of the Triangle of Madness became involved. Willow Nightingale came out carrying a chain and initially helped Statlander & Cameron clear the ring before the numbers turned against them. Backstage later in the show, Nightingale said she had spoken with AEW Women’s World Tag Team Champions Jamie Hayter & Alex Windsor, collectively known as the Brawling Birds. That set the women’s Blood & Guts lineup as Nightingale, Statlander, Cameron, Hayter & Windsor against Thekla, Hart, Blue, Bayne & Kross . Statlander & Cameron are also due to challenge Hayter & Windsor for the Women’s World Tag Team Championship at Full Gear. The women’s match joins the previously announced men’s Blood & Guts contest between Team Ospreay and the Don Callis Family. Josh Alexander quickly defeated Blade Brown before declaring that it was time for him to bring championship gold to the Don Callis Family. Alexander challenged TNT Champion Darby Allin to a match on Wednesday’s Fright Night Dynamite in St. Louis, with AEW subsequently making the title defense official. He then turned his attention to Adam Copeland, noting that Copeland had been attacked by the Callis Family on Dynamite and was not expected to be in Winston-Salem. Copeland nevertheless appeared and hit Trent Beretta and Rocky Romero with spears. Mark Davis & Jake Doyle then attacked him from behind, with Alexander joining the beatdown. The TNT Championship match joins Persephone’s defense against Queen Aminata and the third FTR-Motor City Machine Guns match on the October 28 Dynamite lineup. Jay White opened Collision alongside the Bang Bang Gang and The Dogs following their alliance on Wednesday’s Dynamite. White briefly teased reviving the Bullet Club name before rejecting the idea. body: Mini Vikingo has said he needs surgery on an elbow injury, ruling out his planned AAA World Cruiserweight Championship match against Rey Fenix. I injured my elbow at NXT and the doctors say I need surgery, but I don’t want to lose this match. Fenix told Vikingo that he had earned his opportunity and promised to try to remain champion until his return. Fenix then said the Cruiserweight Championship would instead be defended in an open challenge next week during the second night of Héroes Inmortales and wondered aloud who the challenger would be. Vikingo had earned the match against Fenix by defeating Jack Cartwheel, Joaquin Wilde and Nobu San in a four-way contender’s match earlier this month. The injury had already prevented Vikingo from wrestling on Tuesday’s edition of NXT. General Manager Robert Stone announced during the October 20 broadcast that he had not been medically cleared for a scheduled six-man tag. Big Mami also made her return to AAA television following the World Trios Championship match. Los Perros del Mal (Daga, Angel & Berto) retained against La Parka, Mr. Iguana & Niño Hamburguesa after interference from Karmen Petrovic. Daga delivered a low blow to La Parka while the referee was distracted, allowing Angel to roll him up for the pin. The champions continued their attack afterward, with Petrovic targeting Niño Hamburguesa at ringside. Big Mami then came out to make the save, throwing Petrovic into the ring and attacking her. She prepared to deliver a hip attack before Daga pulled Petrovic to safety. Big Mami last wrestled for the promotion in 2025. She and Niño Hamburguesa have a lengthy history together, including a 775-day reign as AAA World Mixed Tag Team Champions from 2017 until 2019. El Grande Americano retained the AAA Mega Championship against Dominik Mysterio in the main event despite repeated involvement from Dorian Roldán and Omos. Omos eventually pulled the referee from the ring during a pin attempt. AAA General Manager Rey Mysterio then arrived and attacked Omos with a chair before also striking Dominik. Americano followed with a headbutt and pinned Dominik once the referee recovered. The match followed Dominik earning another opportunity at the championship earlier this month. La Catalina also retained the AAA Reina de Reinas Championship against Flammer and La Hiedra. Although the Las Tóxicas members initially worked together against the champion, tensions again emerged between them. Catalina ultimately capitalized, hitting Flammer with a running knee for the victory.

title: Matt Hardy Recalls Watching First Hell In A Cell Match
raw_title: Matt Hardy Says He'll Never Forget Seeing Classic WWE Match Up Close
summary_src: During the early days of his WWE tenure, Matt Hardy and his brother Jeff were able to watch one of the company's most iconic matches and debuts.
body: AEW In 1997, WWE's Badd Blood: In Your House became an iconic event for the company, despite a mostly forgettable undercard. However, the main event saw The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels in a heated clash, competing in the first-ever Hell in a Cell match, leading to Kane making his monstrous debut. At the time, Matt Hardy was only 23 and his WWE career hadn't taken off just yet, but he vividly recalled watching the show's main event. "It was impressive, yeah," Hardy said about seeing the cell lowered down before the match during an episode of his " The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy " podcast. "I'll never forget sitting back and watching that match, and that was the first time I was like, 'Whoa,'" Hardy continued. "Shawn Michaels is like — we knew he was great, but he was on another level in that match. Such a stand-out. It was so incredible to watch." Hardy also expressed that The Undertaker was great to watch as well, because the "Deadman" didn't just steamroll Michaels like he did many of his other opponents at the time. Hardy also commented on seeing Kane backstage without the mask before the match, detailing the history that he and Jeff had with Glenn Jacobs prior to WWE. "We worked with him in Smokey Mountain when he was Unabomber," Hardy recalled. "It was so weird, because we're like, 'This is crazy, this guy's getting this amazing character, he's Undertaker's brother. We were around him when he was Isaac Yankem.'"
summary: In 1997, a 23-year-old Matt Hardy attended WWE's Badd Blood: In Your House and watched the first-ever Hell in a Cell match between The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels from a unique vantage point. On his "The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy" podcast, Hardy said he was impressed as Michaels performed on another level while The Undertaker avoided simply dominating his opponent as he often did. Hardy added that seeing Kane make his monstrous debut during the bout left a lasting impression.

summary_src: Earlier this year, reports said Eric Young was no longer with TNA and had joined WWE. Now, more updates have emerged. In an online Q&A, PWInsider’s Mike Johnson shared that former TNA World Champion Eric Young is now working for WWE NXT as a producer for the brand.
body: Earlier this year, reports said Eric Young was no longer with TNA and had joined WWE. Now, more updates have emerged. In an online Q&A, PWInsider’s Mike Johnson shared that former TNA World Champion Eric Young is now working for WWE NXT as a producer for the brand. Johnson added that Young has been with the promotion since July 2026. However, Johnson was not sure about Young’s in-ring future. Earlier this year, TNA shared a press release announcing Young and the company parting ways. Later, Fightful Select reported Young was potentially returning to WWE, having maintained a positive relationship with Triple H. Our Bryan Alvarez had also reported that Young was “expected to be a ‘player/coach’ in NXT.” Young made his debut for TNA as a member of Team Canada in 2004. He remained with the promotion before signing with WWE in 2016. He was later part of WWE’s roster cuts announced on April 15, 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic. He later re-signed with the promotion in 2022 but did not appear on TV. Soon after, he returned to TNA (then known as Impact Wrestling) at Slammiversary 2023. title: Mini Vikingo Injured, Fenix Issues Cruiserweight Open Challenge
raw_title: Mini Vikingo injured, open challenge for Cruiserweight title set for AAA Heroes Inmortales week two
summary_src: With Mini Vikingo ruled out, an open challenge has been issued for the AAA Cruiserweight championship. Recently on AAA Heroes Inmortales Week 1, a backstage segment aired where Mini Vikingo was shown in the trainer’s room when Rey Fenix showed up.
body: With Mini Vikingo ruled out, an open challenge has been issued for the AAA Cruiserweight championship. Recently on AAA Heroes Inmortales Week 1, a backstage segment aired where Mini Vikingo was shown in the trainer’s room when Rey Fenix showed up. Vikingo claimed that while he wanted to fight Fenix for the title, he had suffered an elbow injury while wrestling in WWE NXT. Vikingo revealed that the doctors had advised him to undergo surgery. With Vikingo now unable to compete, their scheduled Cruiserweight championship match at AAA Heroes Inmortales was called off. Fenix further shared that instead he’ll be defending the belt in an open challenge next week during Heroes Inmortales Week 2 on Oct. 31, 2026. As of now, Fenix’s opponent has not been announced. Vikingo was scheduled to compete on the Oct. 20, 2026 episode of NXT, but it was later announced that he was not cleared to compete. Vikingo last wrestled on the Oct. 13 episode of NXT on The CW, where he and Chazz ‘Starboy’ Hall lost to Vanity Project (Brad Baylor & Ricky Smokes) in the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic tournament. During a backstage segment on Week 1, Vikingo informed Fenix he could not compete, leading Fenix to announce an open challenge for the championship on Heroes Inmortales Week 2 airing October 31, 2026. Vikingo's most recent match was a loss with Chazz Hall to Vanity Project on the October 13 episode of NXT, and he was subsequently pulled from the October 20 card as he was not medically cleared.

title: Indie Wrestler Amber Nova Arrested For DUI
raw_title: Updated: Independent Star Amber Nova Arrested For Dui, Tmz Incorrectly Cites Her As AEW & NXT Wrestler
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin UPDATED: INDEPENDENT STAR AMBER NOVA ARRESTED FOR DUI, TMZ INCORRECTLY CITES HER AS AEW & NXT WRESTLER By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-24 19:04:00 Amber Judith Flora, 34, who wrestles under the ring name Amber Nova, primarily on the Florida independent scene was arrested for DUI on Friday 10/23 by The Orlando Police Department . Nova was charged with DUI and refusal to take a breathalyzer. She was arrested at 5:40 AM and released after posting bond that same morning. She is slated for a 11/2 court hearing. TMZ, which picked up the story referred to Nova as both an AEW and NXT "wrestler." Nova worked several AEW TV matches in 2022 and twice for WWE NXT as an enhancement talent in 2018 and 2019. Nova was never, ever under contract to either promotion, so referring to her as related to either company is quite a stretch. 10/25 12:32 AM Update: TMZ has removed the AEW mention in the headline and story of their article, but still refers to Nova as a "former" NXT wrestler. summary: Amber Judith Flora, who performs as Amber Nova on the Florida independent circuit, was arrested by Orlando police on October 23 for DUI and refusing a breathalyzer test. The 34-year-old was taken into custody at 5:40 a.m., posted bond and was released the same morning with a court date set for November 2. TMZ initially described her as an AEW and NXT wrestler, though she only appeared in enhancement matches for those promotions years ago and was never under contract with either.

body: A brand new update has emerged on AJ Francis’ current TNA contract status and future with the promotion. Currently a regular on TNA programming, Fightful Select recently reported that Francis’ current contract with TNA Wrestling is set to expire at the end of this year. However, the report also noted that Francis is interested in remaining with the promotion, and TNA is also hoping to retain him. It was further reported that a deal about Francis’ new contract with TNA is expected to get done. Since joining TNA in 2024, Francis won and held the TNA Digital Media and Canadian International Heavyweight Championships for very short reigns. Both titles are now defunct. Before joining TNA, Francis was a part of the WWE roster for a few years and even wrestled in the indies. A former football player, Francis believes football was harder on his body, while his wrestling career is now peaking. A few months ago, Francis also referred to himself as the LeBron James of wrestling. llm_long: The Intercontinental Championship belt from WrestleMania III is heading to auction at Heritage Auctions. The belt played a central role at the event on March 29, 1987, when it changed hands in a highly regarded match.

The title was won during the bout between Ricky Steamboat and Randy Savage. That match is recognized by historians, wrestlers, and fans as one of the greatest and most influential contests in wrestling history.

Between 1985 and 1989 the Intercontinental Championship was held by several defining figures from WWE's golden era. The Savage versus Steamboat match at WrestleMania III is frequently cited as one of the best WrestleMania matches even as the event approaches its 40th anniversary.

The auction takes place during a period of strong growth in the high-end wrestling memorabilia market. Heritage Auctions previously sold Hulk Hogan's photo-matched WrestleMania I boots for over one million dollars and his WrestleMania II world heavyweight championship belt for more than four hundred thousand dollars.
The multi-champion Intercontinental title is viewed as a museum-grade artifact and is anticipated to attract significant bidding interest.

body: Link WWE & AAA Manolo Has Pizzazz learned all of life’s lessons from decades of professional wrestling. Manolo has been covering the sport for over ten years on Cageside Seats. Rey Mysterio is a thorn in the side of Dominik Mysterio. Once again, Rey influenced the finish for Dominik versus El Grande Americano for the AAA Mega Championship. Dom was on the losing end both times. I’ll let you be the judge if that sounds fishy from father to son. The first instance was Rey running in as backup referee to count the pin that crowned Grande over Dominik at Triplemania 34. The second occasion happened at Heroes Inmortales on Saturday night (Oct. 24, 2026). Grande versus Dominik was a wild affair in the main event. It started with shenanigans when Dorian Roldan hot Grande with a chair during introductions. Dominik took advantage for the 619, but that wasn’t enough to keep Grande down for a quick pin. The middle of the match also had shenanigans when Omos arrived to cause trouble. As Grande ran the ropes to deliver a headbutt, Omos tripped the Mexican hero. Pimpinela Escarlata took umbrage, so Omos goozled the exotico. Grande saved his friend by colliding into Omos on a suicide dive. The champion popped a headbutt to Roldan, then he blasted Dom with a headbutt. Victory was in Grande’s hand. That was until Omos pulled the referee out of the ring on the three-count. If you guessed that the finish had more shenanigans, then you are correct. This is where Rey came in. He swung around the ring post for a 619 to Omos. Rey grabbed a chair to tenderize the giant. When Dom tried to snatch the weapon from his father, Rey socked his son with the chair too. Grande sealed the deal with a headbutt for victory. Some will say that Rey did the right thing to even the playing field for Grande. Others will argue that Rey overstepped his bounds as AAA general manager. And there is a contingent of Dirty Dom loyalists who will claim this is jealousy from a deadbeat dad. One thing is certain. body: Just fresh off his role in Street Fighter, WWE’s Cody Rhodes has opened up about his plans for more Hollywood roles. During his recent appearance on The Rich Eisen Show , Rhodes opened up in detail and revealed his plans for more Hollywood roles while remaining in WWE. “ Do I have the bug? Hard have the bug. But also, I think it’s probably important to say wrestling is my whole life. You said day job. It is the day job. I don’t think it would ever not be ,” Rhodes answered when asked if he had caught the acting bug. “It’s definitely my plan. Hopefully it goes according to plan. It’s one of those things where if I don’t flex that muscle, if I don’t get reps at it, I’m not going to get any good at this whole thing. “ Action, that’s a ton of fun, and comedy, that’s an easy place for me to plug into. But because of Dave Batista, John Cena, of course, and The Rock, they’ve made it so that we can walk into a lot of these rooms and they know we have something to offer ,” Rhodes added. He further claimed that he would like to keep doing that while working with wrestling. Rhodes believes that it’s not like what it used to be in the past, where one had to choose between either of them. “New York Times just did this great article on Roman [Reigns] and I about, well, will this produce more wrestling in the TV-film space? And I think they’re right to say it will. I hope ,” he finished. Last year, Rhodes did a small role in The Naked Gun and followed it up with The Street Fighter. Similar to Rhodes, Roman Reigns. CM Punk, Drew McIntyre, and Chelsea Green are all experiencing a career in Hollywood. Rhodes estimated that his time with the company could last around six or seven more years. He expressed a desire not to overstay his welcome in the industry.
When asked about wrestling into his 50s, Rhodes said he does not want to continue that long. He emphasized his gratitude for what wrestling has provided him throughout his career.

body: At TNA Bound For Glory 2026, Amazing Red defeated KC Navarro, Fabian Aichner, Rich Swann, BDE, Cedric Alexander and Ryan Nemeth to win the TNA X-Division Championship. On the same night as his Hall of Fame induction, Red made history with starting his fourth reign with the X-Division gold. Now that he has the title, Red could drop it to any number of talented members of the TNA Wrestling roster in the coming weeks and months. Here are five potential options to become the nextTNA X-Division Champion after Amazing Red. In 2026, Cedric Alexander finally completed his journey to become TNA X-Division Champion. Ending the historic reign of Leon Slater, Alexander showcased what has made him one of the most underrated in-ring competitors for years. On the October 22 episode of TNA Thursday Night IMPACT, Alexander beat Fabian Aichner, Rich Swann and KC Navarro to become the number one contender for the X-Division Title. Now that he has his opportunity, The System member could start a second run with the X-Division Championship by taking out Amazing Red. Since arriving in TNA Wrestling, Fabian Aichner has been on the hunt for the TNA X-Division Championship. After getting his opportunities, Aichner has to be frustrated that he hasn’t gotten that all-important victory. The former Giovanni Vinci has everything it takes to be a champion and may just be one more shot away from the gold. With his combination of size, strength and athleticism, Aichner would make for an ideal TNA X-Division Champion if he can dethrone Amazing Red. After signing with TNA Wrestling in 2026, many fans now believe the sky is the limit for Ricky Sosa . At just 21 years old, Sosa is one of the youngest members of the TNA roster right now. Considering his rapid rise in wrestling, Sosa could join his friend Leon Slater by winning gold in his early years in the business. Clashing with a legend like Amazing Red, Sosa might just have the speed, youth and size on his side that will make him the next TNA X-Division Champion somewhere down the line. KC Navarro is a protégé of Amazing Red, having gotten his start in pro wrestling thanks to the current TNA X-Division Champion. Over the past year, Navarro has emerged as a rising star who feels on the cusp of championship gold. After coming up short against Nic Nemeth for the TNA World Title and in the seven-way X-Division Title match at Bound For Glory 2026, Navarro might just need a singles bout against Amazing Red for a championship he has helped put on the map. Navarro being the one to dethrone Red for the TNA X-Division Championship would be fitting and a true passing of the torch moment. Since signing with TNA Wrestling, Avery Styles has truly felt like a star on the rise in a major way. At just 19 years, Styles is the youngest star in TNA today and has the lineage that he has to live up to. body: The GHC National Championship was up for grabs at Pro Wrestling NOAH’s Wrestle Odyssey II event on October 25th at Ryōgoku Sumo Hall in Tokyo, Japan. Naomichi Marufuji made his fifth defense of the belt since winning it in May 2026. He put the title on the line against Luis Mante. Mante arrived on the scene as the M.P.I. (Mysterious Phantom Invader) character and then eventually revealed his identity. Mante has been with Dragongate since 2019. He defeated Marufuji with a pop-up powerbomb and is now the new GHC National Champion. Mante is the 18th holder of the belt.
summary: Luis Mante defeated Naomichi Marufuji at Pro Wrestling NOAH's Wrestle Odyssey II on October 25 at Ryogoku Sumo Hall in Tokyo to win the GHC National Championship. Marufuji was making his fifth defense of the title he won in May 2026. Mante, who first appeared in NOAH as the Mysterious Phantom Invader before unmasking and has been part of Dragongate since 2019, finished the match with a pop-up powerbomb to become the 18th champion.

His challenger was Luis Mante, who originally debuted in the promotion under the Mysterious Phantom Invader persona before revealing his true identity.
Mante has been a member of Dragongate since 2019.
He defeated Marufuji by delivering a pop-up powerbomb to capture the championship.
Mante became the 18th wrestler to hold the GHC National Title.

Daga finished off Parka with a roll-up pin, stealing the victory for Los Perros. After the match, Los Perros continued their attack on their opponents. Flammer pulled her out of the ring, and once again, tensions flared between her and La Hiedra. title: Randy Savage’s WrestleMania III Intercontinental Title Belt Sells for Insane Price at Auction
raw_title: Randy Savage’s WrestleMania III Intercontinental Title Belt Sells for Insane Price at Auction
summary_src: One of the most famous championship belts in WWE history just sold for an absolutely massive price. The Intercontinental Championship used during Randy Savage and Ricky Steamboat’s legendary WrestleMania III match has officially been auctioned off for $716,750.
body: On October 25, 2026, the auction closed through Heritage Auctions with a final bid of $587,500. Once the buyer’s premium was added, the final price climbed all the way to $716,750. This isn’t just a belt connected to one famous match either. The championship was used from 1985 through 1988 and was held by Tito Santana, Randy “Macho Man” Savage, Ricky “The Dragon” Steamboat and The Honky Tonk Man during one of WWE’s biggest eras. Its biggest piece of history came at WrestleMania III on March 29, 1987. Savage walked into the Pontiac Silverdome as Intercontinental Champion before Steamboat defeated him in a match that remains one of the most celebrated bouts in WrestleMania history. Steamboat’s victory ended Savage’s championship reign and put this exact belt right in the middle of one of wrestling’s most famous matches. While Hulk Hogan vs. Andre the Giant headlined WrestleMania III, Savage and Steamboat’s match became a classic in its own right. The belt itself certainly shows its age after years on the road. Heritage Auctions noted that it measures 48.5 inches from end to end and has visible wear from being carried around during its years as WWE’s active Intercontinental Championship, including a piece of black tape on the reverse. The massive sale also continues a pretty wild year for vintage WWE memorabilia at Heritage Auctions. Hulk Hogan’s photo-matched WrestleMania I boots sold for $1.037 million in February, while his WrestleMania II photo-matched championship belt fetched $414,800 in August. Getting a championship belt connected to one WWE Hall of Famer would already make for a serious collectible, but this one passed through the hands of four of them during WWE’s 1980s boom. Someone was clearly willing to pay a huge premium to own a physical piece of that history. H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.
summary: Savage walked into the Pontiac Silverdome as Intercontinental Champion before Steamboat got the win over him in a match that remains one of the most celebrated bouts in WrestleMania history. Andre the Giant headlined WrestleMania III, Savage and Steamboat’s match became a classic in its own right.

summary_src: Andrade El Idolo just can’t stay away from the fans at ringside, but this time his usual selfie routine ended with him getting jumped. During the October 24 episode of AEW Collision, Andrade found another woman in the crowd and stopped for a photo before Tommaso Ciampa came crashing into the moment.
body: The woman was clearly excited when Andrade approached her at ringside. She pulled out her phone and the two started taking a selfie together, continuing the little routine Andrade has been doing at AEW shows lately. This one didn’t get the usual happy ending, though. Ciampa interrupted the selfie by attacking Andrade, immediately turning the ringside interaction back into business between the two wrestlers. After Collision, the identity of Andrade’s latest selfie partner was revealed. Independent wrestler Leah Night took to her Instagram Story and confirmed that she was the woman sitting at ringside during the segment. Night isn’t simply a random fan who happened to score a selfie on television either. She has competed across the independent wrestling scene for promotions including Marvelous, SSPW, ASE, TBD and WE Adrenaline, among others. Andrade has now made these ringside interactions a pretty regular part of his AEW appearances. At WrestleDream, he stopped for a selfie with another woman in the crowd and even kissed her on the cheek before continuing with the show. That woman was later revealed to be independent wrestler Madisyn Maxxwell , who has worked for promotions including LPW, WOW, CCW and UFW. Just days before that, Andrade pulled a similar move on Dynamite with independent wrestler Kelly Madan . The routine goes back even further to AEW Grand Slam France, where Andrade approached another woman in the crowd, took a selfie and received a kiss on the cheek. She was later identified as Instagram personality bad.oce, who is known around the French wrestling scene. Andrade’s ringside selfie streak is clearly becoming a recurring part of his AEW act, but Ciampa finally found a way to ruin the fun this time around. With Leah Night now revealed as the latest woman involved, Andrade has added yet another indie wrestling name to his growing list of ringside encounters. title: Backstage Buzz: Eddie Guerrero’s Daughter Sherilyn Guerrero Set to Make Wrestling Debut After Heated Confrontation
raw_title: Eddie Guerrero’s Daughter Sherilyn Guerrero Set to Make Wrestling Debut After Heated Confrontation
summary_src: Eddie Guerrero’s daughter is following in her father’s footsteps, and she’s already got her first opponent lined up. Sherilyn Guerrero is officially making her professional wrestling debut on November 14, and things are already getting personal before she’s even had her first match.
body: The announcement came during Reality of Wrestling’s Sherri Martel Classic event, where Sherilyn got into a confrontation with Mystii Marks. Marks blamed Guerrero for losing her match and decided to take things a step further by hitting her. Sherilyn wasn’t having it. She got back up, grabbed a microphone and challenged Marks to face her on November 14. Just like that, Eddie Guerrero’s daughter had her first wrestling match booked. Sherilyn has already been putting in work to prepare for her wrestling career. She attended Bayley’s 2026 Lodestone camp and also visited WWE’s Performance Center in Orlando, Florida, where she shared a photo of herself outside the building. Of course, Sherilyn has some pretty big shoes to fill. Her father, Eddie Guerrero, was one of WWE’s most popular stars before his death in 2005. Now his daughter is getting her own opportunity to step inside the ring and see what she can do. Sherilyn’s first match is still a few weeks away, but she’s already got some unfinished business with Mystii Marks. Now we’ll find out whether Eddie Guerrero’s daughter can make a name for herself in the wrestling business. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. title: Comeback Watch: Former TNA World Champion Quietly Returns to WWE in Backstage Role
raw_title: Former TNA World Champion Quietly Returns to WWE in Backstage Role
summary_src: Eric Young quietly made his way back to WWE after leaving TNA earlier this year. The two-time TNA World Champion has apparently been working behind the scenes in NXT for months, although that doesn’t necessarily mean fans should expect to see him back in the ring.
body: Mike Johnson of PWInsider revealed the news during a recent Q&A after being asked about Young’s whereabouts. According to Johnson, speculation that Young could return to WWE after requesting his TNA release turned out to be right. “That was the assumption for a lot of people when Young asked for and received his TNA release and it was correct.” Johnson revealed that Young actually started working for WWE shortly after his TNA departure. Rather than returning as an active wrestler, he has been working behind the scenes as a producer for NXT since July. As for whether Young could eventually step back into the ring, that part remains up in the air. Johnson didn’t rule it out, but he also hasn’t heard anything indicating that a wrestling return is part of the plan. The update fills in a pretty big blank surrounding Young since his TNA exit. TNA announced on July 1 that the longtime company veteran had been released, but Johnson now says Young actually asked for his release before moving into his new WWE role. At the time, TNA publicly acknowledged Young’s long history with the promotion while confirming that his departure was effective immediately. The company wished the former two-time World Champion well without revealing what he planned to do next. “TNA Wrestling has come to the terms on the release of Eric Young effective immediately. EY has had a legendary TNA career, including twice as TNA World Champion. We wish him the best in his future endeavors.” Young’s departure came during a larger period of changes within TNA that also saw several other names leave the company. His exit stood out considering just how closely connected he has been to TNA throughout different eras of his career. This also isn’t Young’s first time under the WWE umbrella, but his latest stint is taking a very different form behind the scenes. Whether that producer role eventually leads to another appearance in front of the cameras remains the big unknown. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: AEW Changes Jay White’s Faction Name Following Fan Backlash
raw_title: AEW Changes Jay White’s Faction Name Following Fan Backlash
summary_src: AEW apparently heard the reaction to its newest faction name loud and clear, because “The Last Outfit” didn’t even make it through the night. After Jay White introduced the name on Collision, the group quickly got a rebrand following a wave of backlash from fans.
body: White had announced during the October 24 episode of AEW Collision that his new alliance with the Bang Bang Gang and The Dogs would be known as The Last Outfit . The name immediately caught heat online, with plenty of fans making it clear they weren’t exactly sold on it. Things changed pretty quickly after the show. AEW uploaded a new video of White cutting a promo on Twitter , and this time he introduced the faction under a completely different name — The Cut. White worked the new name into a promo that also took aim at Jon Moxley and the Death Riders. He described his crew as the group capable of finally cutting the Death Riders out of AEW. “We are top-shelf high rollers, the golden gun slingers, some dirty dogs, your Collision cowboys. We are the last outfit capable of slicing out the cancer that is Jon Moxley & the Death Riders from the heart of AEW!” White then dropped the group’s new name at the end of the promo. After introducing The Last Outfit only hours earlier, the faction was now being presented as The Cut. The sudden switch comes after The Last Outfit name received a ton of negative reaction from fans following Collision. With AEW releasing the new promo after the show, the faction’s original name appears to have been dropped almost immediately in favor of The Cut. The group itself hasn’t changed, as White remains aligned with Juice Robinson, Ace Austin, Austin Gunn, Colten Gunn, David Finlay and Clark Connors. Finlay and Connors joined forces with White and the Bang Bang Gang on Dynamite after the group went after the Death Riders. White had even teased bringing back the Bullet Club name before originally settling on The Last Outfit. That carried some extra weight considering both White and Finlay previously led versions of Bullet Club during their time in New Japan Pro Wrestling. Now the group has already gone through two names before its run has really gotten started. Whatever AEW ultimately has planned for White’s new crew, The Last Outfit appears to have had one of the shortest runs of any faction name in recent memory. AEW uploaded a new video of White cutting a promo on Twitter , and this time he introduced the faction under a completely different name — The Cut.

title: Contract News: Samantha Irvin Turned Down WWE Record Deal Before Her Departure
raw_title: Samantha Irvin Turned Down WWE Record Deal Before Her Departure
summary_src: Samantha Irvin is clearing up one of the biggest stories surrounding her WWE exit, and according to her, people have had it wrong for the last two years. Irvin says she didn’t leave WWE to chase a music career — and she actually turned down a record deal from the company because she wanted to ...
body: Irvin jumped on Twitter and directly addressed the idea that music was behind her WWE departure. She revealed that WWE was willing to help her go down that road, but she had zero interest in making it her next career move. “WWE offered me a record deal, to which I politely declined because I have no interest in the music business! My interest was in managing wrestlers. And that’s all I’ve ever expressed.” Irvin did release some music after leaving WWE, but she says people read way too much into it. According to her, she was simply having fun with some of her former Cirque du Soleil colleagues and making something for fans who already knew her as a singer. “I made some songs last year for fun & videos with my colleagues from Cirque du Soleil and released independently for my singing fans from before wrestling but other than that, I made no proclamations about or efforts towards a ‘music’ career 🙏🏽” It’s also not like Irvin still had something to prove as a singer. She pointed out that she already had a pretty successful run in that world long before WWE came calling. “Singing career wise, I’ve had a fantastic one, though!!! Saw the world multiple times over ❤️” One fan wasn’t buying it and told Irvin that wasn’t what people were hearing when she originally left WWE. Irvin fired back with a very simple response about what she says she actually wanted all along. That’s where things get interesting, because a very different story came out after Irvin left WWE in October 2024. Bryan Alvarez reported at the time that she had outside projects she wanted to pursue but couldn’t figure out how to make them work alongside her WWE schedule. “She’s got some outside projects she wants to do, couldn’t come to terms with how it worked with WWE and off she goes.” Dave Meltzer also reported that Irvin had been thinking about leaving for nearly a year because she wanted to focus more on music. Two years later, Irvin is now flat-out saying that wasn’t what she was trying to do. “She’s actually been thinking about it for a year. She’s a singer, she also plays the flute, but she wants to get more involved in her music. It was just something that she’d been talking about for a long, long time, and finally pulled the trigger on it. And that’s about it, really.” The timing couldn’t be much better for Irvin to clear all of this up. Fightful Select recently reported that her two-year WWE non-compete is coming to an end this month, while AEW has already discussed the possibility of using her in an on-screen role at some point down the road . After two years of people talking about Irvin supposedly leaving wrestling behind for music, she’s now telling fans that was never the plan in the first place. With her non-compete finally wrapping up, the bigger question now is whether she’ll finally get the chance to become the wrestling manager she’s been talking about. title: Toni Storm AEW Return Pushed to 2027
raw_title: BS Meter on WWE WrestleMania 43 and Survivor Series Plans, Massive AEW Stars Return Date, More
body: That's an exclamation point of a discussion point, considering WWE's fast approaching a possible event in Saudi Arabia and AEW has a big show of its own on the way. Naturally, the rumor mill loops in conversations about counterprogramming between the two companies, plus a major retirement and quite a few other things of note. To help fans keep pace with the latest buzz on the rumor mill, let's put the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss. It feels like Toni Storm is on the way back to AEW soon. But according to Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), Storm won't actually be back competing in a ring until "2027 at the earliest." A huge Storm marketing campaign fired up at WrestleDream in mid-October, but it didn't feel like the little hints that created viral moments were a sign of an immediate return. Fans haven't seen her in the ring since early in the year, so little hints by the month could build some serious hype, though. We'd probably hear even more buzz if an in-ring return was about to happen. AEW seems content to dripfeed this one for the next several months, which is great: There's a lot of storyline and character stuff they could do to explain away the absence in kayfabe before a big return next year. Let the counterprogramming talk begin in earnest. According to Wrestling Observer Live's Bryan Alvarez (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), NXT's strong showing against an episode of AEW Dynamite has given them a green light to load up big time against the upcoming Blood & Guts. WWE hasn't had any problems counterprogramming AEW with pretty much anything in the past. But the fact a normal NXT show is sparring well in the ratings with AEW's big weekly hitters is a pretty big deal right now. Fair enough. WWE would counterprogram Blood & Guts anyway. But feeling good about recent head-to-heads enough to take the risk makes sense. And if WWE can somehow win or come close, it's going to cause a ruckus online. Here comes the obvious faction stuff. According to Wrestling Observer Radio's Dave Meltzer (h/t Mrosko ), WWE is indeed positioning The Bloodline to go against 946 at Survivor Series. Cliche or not, the writing has been on the wall for a while. WWE kept Roman Reigns out of it for as long as it could, but it was stretching believability that he wouldn't take issue with, you know, his family members getting hit by cars and stuff. Now, 946 has Carmelo Hayes in the fray as another member, too, setting up the big event. Trust that there have been much, much worse builds to a Survivor Series event. This is great. It's a great use of Hayes, and there's room for Jacob Fatu to come back for this too. Fun wrinkle: One could see Fatu actually aligning with either faction, so that's a wild card. And if he does, that probably means even more people will get involved, making the next few weeks really interesting. A legend could be on his way out next year.

title: Oba Femi Emerges as WWE's Future Star in 2026
raw_title: New Truths About WWE and AEW Revealed in 2026
body: From the rise of Oba Femi to the return of Roman Reigns to the top of the business, WWE offered a fresh yet also familiar look at its current direction. While Kenny Omega and The Young Bucks seemed to begin the final chapters of their careers and Will Ospreay finally became the top guy, AEW seemed to prepare for a new Elite-less future. This and more established new truths about the state of the two biggest wrestling companies in the world. It did not take long for Oba Femi to make an impression in WWE, but it was 2026 that clearly showcased that he is the man WWE can build the brand around. It has become so clear that even AEW wrestlers like Swerve Strickland are taking time out of their day to put him over. WWE has bet everything on The Ruler, and it is already paying off. The 28-year-old star won King of the Ring despite WWE not wanting him to be world champion yet, and fans did not bat an eye. While Gunther retired three men in one year, Oba ending the career of Brock Lesnar made The Ruler look like the true Career Killer, defeating The Beast Incarnate at both WrestleMania and SummerSlam. While WWE repeatedly plays it slow with young stars, Oba is the exception, and fans have welcomed that change with open arms. No one is hotter in all of WWE, and the only disappointment is that WWE keeps delaying The Ruler's true ascension, dethroning Roman Reigns. After letting go of both New Day and Motor City Machine Guns, WWE made a firm statement on its commitment to tag team wrestling. The men's tag team division has been in shambles for a while as The Vision barely seem to notice their gold and The MFTs are feuding with the lowest standing stars on SmackDown. The women's tag team division was a big part of WWE at the end of 2025 with the feud of Asuka and Kairi Sane vs. Rhea Ripley and Iyo Sky. However, WWE released Sane while Asuka went on hiatus followed by breaking up Ripley and Sky between brands. Since that time, it has been a hot potato that has gotten no one over. Meanwhile, AEW picked up the teams WWE let go and delivered one of its best years for tag team wrestling, led by The Young Bucks. As FTR and MCMG continued a Best of 5 Series and the newly named New Level have delivered one of the best feuds in the history of the World Trios Championship with Hangman Adam Page and Brodido, AEW is doubling down. The women's tag team division is still developing, but Divine Dominion raised the bar with their title reign and finished their run with the gold in two brutal, memorable battles with The Brawling Birds. It is clear WWE has decided tag team wrestling has no value to the current product, and AEW is the only company that will deliver consistently great tag team action for years to come. Despite repeated lip service from WWE about the importance of women's wrestling, no matches have been reportedly cut for time more often including the infamous six-minute Liv Morgan vs. Stephanie Vaquer at WrestleMania 42. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Opens Up On How Much New WWE Wrestlers Make: 'You'd Be Shocked'
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Reveals How Much New WWE Wrestlers Make: 'You'd Be Shocked'
body: During a new appearance on " Flagrant ," with his Street Fighter co-star Andrew Schulz, Rhodes was asked about WWE's pay structure and explained just how different the wrestling business is financially from the one his father, Dusty Rhodes, experienced. "The wrestling economy is different now because there's other places you can go wrestle," Rhodes said. "The money in wrestling and sports entertainment is very good." Rhodes said wrestlers from his father's generation would be surprised by today's salaries, adding that even his mother initially struggled to understand the numbers involved. "If you were my dad or [wrestlers from his generation], you'd be shocked," Rhodes said. "My mom didn't get it." According to Rhodes, even wrestlers entering WWE's developmental system are now receiving guaranteed six-figure deals. "The contracts are guaranteed now," Rhodes said. "That's a huge responsibility." He added that "everything is six figures for new developmental wrestlers." Rhodes also shared a saying from WWE President Nick Khan about the earning potential within the company. Some wrestlers are going to "do well," others will do "really well," and then a select few will "do next level." That highest tier, according to Rhodes, has reached a level comparable to other major professional sports. "That next-level pay is now comparable with sports," Rhodes said, pointing to the type of contracts seen in Major League Baseball and the NBA. For Rhodes, that is something to celebrate beyond his own paycheck. He credited WWE's current TKO era and Khan with helping bring wrestler compensation to that level and said it is something he is proud of as a wrestler. The conversation comes shortly after Rhodes confirmed that he has signed a new contract with WWE. Rhodes did not disclose his salary during the "Flagrant" interview, and his comments about WWE's "next-level" earners weren't a direct statement about the value of his own deal. As one of the company's biggest stars, however, his new contract comes at a time when he says WWE's highest-paid performers can earn money comparable to athletes in traditional professional sports. The deal also comes with an interesting reality: Rhodes has increasingly discussed how much longer he actually wants to wrestle. Rhodes reiterated on "Flagrant" something he has discussed elsewhere recently: he does not envision wrestling indefinitely. His reasoning has less to do with injuries or his position in WWE than his daughter. Rhodes recalled that Dusty was around much more during his childhood once Cody was about eight years old. He remembers having his father at games and other important moments, and he wants to provide that same presence for his daughter as she grows up. That has given Rhodes a rough timeline for when he wants to step away from full-time wrestling. It also adds context to his new WWE contract. summary_src: Tony Khan has been making moves behind closed doors with Paramount Skydance, and his latest trip to Los Angeles is raising questions about what AEW could have in the works.
body: The AEW President already confirmed he’s been speaking with David Ellison about the company’s future, but those conversations have now moved into another round of business meetings. Whatever happened in those meetings hasn’t been disclosed, but Khan’s reaction afterward has caught Dave Meltzer’s attention. During the October 25, 2026 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer revealed that Khan flew from Florida to Los Angeles on Friday, October 23, for meetings with Skydance. The AEW boss then headed to North Carolina for Collision, making the Los Angeles stop part of an already packed schedule. “Tony Khan had meetings with Skydance yesterday, Friday. He went from Wednesday, which was — oh God, where were they? They were in Orlando, Miami or Gables. Actually, technically they were Coral Gables, Florida. Flew to LA for meetings and then, you know, flew to, I think it’s Winston-Salem tonight for Collision.” Meltzer didn’t reveal who attended the meetings or what was discussed, but he did share what he learned about Khan’s reaction. According to Meltzer, Khan left the discussions in an unusually positive mood, even compared to his previous conversations about the relationship. “And what I could say is, I don’t know any of the details yet, but I do know that he came out of the meetings extremely happy, much happier than he has been about this. He’s always been happy about this relationship. He’s always been beaming about it from day one. But he definitely came out of these meetings the happiest he’s been.” The timing is worth paying attention to. Khan already confirmed during the October 17 AEW WrestleDream post-show press conference that he’d spoken with David Ellison multiple times about the company’s future. title: Silvia Likki Has Not Signed With WWE Despite Previous Reports
raw_title: Silvia Likki Has Not Signed With WWE Despite Previous Reports
summary_src: Silvia Likki isn’t WWE-bound after all. Despite being named as one of four new female recruits heading to the WWE Performance Center, Ringside News has learned that the Italian CrossFit athlete has not signed with the company.
body: The confusion started after Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer reported that Likki had signed with WWE alongside Gabriela Martinez Asensi, Elly Finch and Tayleigh Robertson. All four women were said to have relocated to Orlando, Florida, within the past week after participating in WWE tryouts. However, Ringside News has since learned that Likki has not signed a WWE contract, contradicting the original report. While she was among the names linked to WWE’s recruiting efforts, she should not be considered an official addition to the company’s roster. Likki is a CrossFit athlete from Italy who has built a sizable following on social media, including more than 200,000 followers on Instagram . Her athletic background made her an interesting prospect for WWE, which regularly recruits talent from outside professional wrestling. The original report also identified Martinez Asensi, a former University of Missouri tennis player from Spain, along with Finch, who competed in track and field at Michigan State University, and Robertson, who has experience in amateur wrestling and bodybuilding. Those three names remain part of the previously reported recruiting class, but the new information changes the situation surrounding Likki. title: Comeback Watch: Ric Flair Returned to Same Bar the Night After Bloody Fall That Sent Him to Hospital

summary_src: Ric Flair suffered a nasty fall, busted up his face, and spent the night in the hospital — but that apparently wasn’t enough to keep him away from his regular bar. The WWE Hall of Famer returned to the same establishment the following night, on the very day he was released from the hospital.

According to Meltzer, the establishment is one Flair visits regularly, and it’s close enough to his home that he doesn’t even need to drive there. “Ric Flair, he was drinking. So he was supposed to be in Seattle for, you know, an autograph thing. And I guess he’s had problems with blood clots, so he was not allowed to fly.” Flair had already canceled his scheduled autograph appearance in Seattle because of a blood clot in his leg . Doctors had restricted his travel, and Flair announced the cancellation that Friday morning. Meltzer explained that the Nature Boy then visited his usual drinking spot, which has apparently become part of his daily routine. “So he said the bar he was at is the bar he is always at. That is his place. It’s right by his house. He doesn’t have to drive there, could walk there. And he goes there early in the morning, and that’s his day.” Things took a bad turn when Flair stepped outside. Meltzer said Flair left his phone behind at the establishment before attempting to cross the street, where he suffered the fall that left him with a bloody head injury and significant damage around his eye. “And he went there, and I’m not sure exactly what happened. Like, he’d left his phone, so he wasn’t leaving, but he went to go across the street and fell down and hit his head, messed up his eye really bad.” Flair was taken to Tampa General Hospital following the fall , where he remained overnight before being released on October 24. Flair had just spent the night receiving medical treatment for injuries to his head and eye, yet he returned to the very establishment he’d visited before the accident. Meltzer didn’t specify exactly when Flair was discharged or how much time passed before he returned, only that he was back there the following night. title: Marc Summers Says WWE Tried To Hire Him As Announcer
raw_title: Legendary TV Host Marc Summers Recalls WWE Trying To Hire Him Away From Nickelodeon
summary_src: Legendary TV host Marc Summers recalled the then-WWF attempting to hire him away from Nickelodeon during his "Double Dare" days.
body: Legendary TV host Marc Summers, who many fans of a certain age remember fondly for his work on "Double Dare," which aired on Nickelodeon, originally from 1986 to 1993, could have ended up working for the then-WWF, according to the star himself. During the show's initial run, it featured two "Super-Slop-a-Mania" episodes with stars from the then-WWF. Summers is hosting a 40-year "Double Dare" reunion, which will be streamed on his website , and in a teaser for the special, posted by @MrTonyMaurizio on X (formerly Twitter), he said that the first edition of "Super-Slop-a-Mania" was his favorite episode of "Double Dare." "Gorilla Monsoon against Bobby 'The Brain' Heenan, okay? Wrestling could not have been bigger," Summers said. "In fact, WWE back in the day wanted to hire me away from Nickelodeon and put me on as an announcer on that show, but they offered me zero money, so I wasn't going to do it." He said that he knew Heenan from his days working at just 16-years-old at a place called Starlight Musicals in Indianapolis. Summers said he and Heenan sold refreshments and would guide people to their seats. He called him the "nicest guy in the world." "Heenan was great," Summers said. "Gorilla had like two degrees from insane colleges and they were both brilliant and fun and funny and that was my favorite episode of all time." Instead of working for the soon-to-be WWE, Summers would go on to host a show on the Food Network, as well as return to Nickelodeon to host the "Double Dare" revival in 2018. His life was even the subject of an off-Broadway musical, titled "The Life and Slimes of Marc Summers."

Summers said his favorite was the one featuring Gorilla Monsoon against Bobby Heenan and that WWE wanted to hire him away from Nickelodeon to work as an announcer. He turned down the offer because it paid zero money; Summers already knew Heenan from his teenage days selling refreshments together at Starlight Musicals in Indianapolis.

title: Myles Borne Calls Out Fans for Using “What?” Chants Against Him on WWE NXT
raw_title: Myles Borne Calls Out Fans for Using “What?” Chants Against Him on WWE NXT
summary_src: Myles Borne had NXT fans hitting him with the infamous “What?” chants recently, but there was one pretty big problem with their plan — he couldn’t even hear them. In fact, Borne didn’t realize fans were chanting at him until he went back and watched the segment with closed captions.
body: During an appearance on The Finish with Corey Smith and Tor Smith , Borne was asked whether the chants bothered him considering his hearing impairment. Instead of being annoyed by the situation, Borne found the whole thing pretty hilarious. Borne revealed that the closed captions were actually what tipped him off to what the crowd had been doing. As far as he was concerned, fans were wasting a whole lot of energy trying to get a reaction he couldn’t give them. “I mean, the only reason I even knew there was a ‘What?’ chant is because when I watched it back, there was closed captioning, so I was able to pick up on it. But, I mean, to me, that just shows me, you’re really doing ‘What?’ chants to a guy that can’t even hear? Like, you know, you’re wasting your energy. You’re going to have to be a lot louder than that if you want to try to get my attention.” Borne wasn’t offended once he realized what had happened either. If anything, knowing that fans were repeatedly shouting at someone who couldn’t hear them only made the situation funnier to him. “I think it’s funny. They know the situation, and yet they’re sitting there yelling and just keep saying it. I love it.” Borne eventually saw exactly what the fans had been chanting when he watched everything back. His response wasn’t anger — he jokingly thanked them for the effort. “So, you know, once I saw that, once I watched it back and saw what they were saying, great. Thank you. I appreciate it.” The “What?” chant has been used by wrestling crowds for decades to interrupt promos and get reactions from wrestlers, but Borne’s situation gave it a pretty unusual twist. Fans were trying to get under his skin in real time while he was completely unaware of what they were doing. Borne clearly isn’t losing any sleep over the chants, and his reaction might actually make things tougher for fans trying to mess with him going forward. After all, it’s pretty difficult to derail someone’s promo when they don’t even realize you’re trying. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: Borne was asked whether the chants bothered him considering his hearing impairment. The closed captions were actually what tipped him off to what the crowd had been doing, Borne disclosed.

title: Meet Bradford wrestler who has become the youngest world champion in history
raw_title: Meet Bradford wrestler who has become the youngest world champion in history
body: Growing up in Bradford, Leon Slater was a huge fan of professional wrestling, playing with action figures of his favourite superstars like two-time WWE champion Dolph Ziggler. Now, at 22, Slater is a world champion himself – the youngest in any of the big federations to hold a top prize. And, in a full circle moment, it was Nick Nemeth – the former Dolph Ziggler – that he defeated to claim the TNA (Total Nonstop Action) World Heavyweight title and fulfil his childhood dream. Slater, who was brought up and still lives in Bradford, joined US based wresting company TNA in 2023. Leon Slater after his title win at TNA Bound For Glory earlier this month (Image: TNA Wrestling) Before this summer he had already held the X Division title, the company’s secondary belt. He agreed to “cash in” that title in exchange for a world heavyweight title opportunity, which was scheduled for Bound For Glory in October, one of TNA’s biggest annual events. In the show stopping main event, Slater pinned Nemeth after a Swanton 450 to claim the title. Leon Slater faces Nick Nemeth at TNA Bound for Glory (Image: TNA Wrestling) This week, the TNA champion spoke to the T&A (Telegraph & Argus) about growing up in Bradford and breaking the record for being the youngest person to claim a world title. He said: “I believe I’m the youngest world champion in professional wrestling history, out of any company in the past 100 years. It’s super, super cool.” Asked about his Bradford roots, he said: “I’m born, bred and still live in Bradford. "I was born in the BRI, I live in Wilsden right now, and lived in Frizinghall for a bit, so Bradford will always be my home. "To get to represent the city on this type of platform is unbelievable. Leon Slater faces Nick Nemeth at TNA Bound for Glory (Image: TNA Wrestling) “We had Zayn Malik, we had Dynamo, and for a while that was it. It is great that I’ve joined that list. “It is crazy, but I was super lucky to be raised in a family environment that pushed a supreme self belief in me. "I always envisaged this is what my life would be, I’ve always manifested that this is the position I’d be in. “It is difficult being from Bradford some times because people give us a bad name, but those people don’t know what they are talking about. They say: ‘Bradford is Bradford,’ but I say ‘Bradford is BRADFORD!’ “We have a lot of hard workers, a lot of grafters and I feel like that’s been instilled in me since day one. I wouldn’t be here today if it wasn’t for that.” Asked how he got into the business, he said: “I’ve always been a fan, even before I can remember. “When I turned nine and figured out how to use Google I looked for West Yorkshire wrestling schools. "I found a school in Wakefield called UK Wrestling and started when I was nine years old. "They moved to Batley and I followed them round while I tried to learn my craft as much as I could.” Covid disrupted his career slightly, but when restrictions were lifted he worked with Sheffield based Pursuit Pro

body: AEW has officially announced an Artist of Stardom Championship match for the Halloween Fright Night edition of Collision on Saturday, October 31. The Triangle of Madness (Thekla, Julia Hart, and Skye Blue) will defend the titles against Hazuki, Koguma, and Fuwa-chan on the show. title: Stephanie Vaquer and Myles Borne’s Relationship Status Cleared Up After Breakup Rumors
raw_title: Stephanie Vaquer and Myles Borne’s Relationship Status Cleared Up After Breakup Rumors
summary_src: Stephanie Vaquer and Myles Borne aren’t done with each other after all. The two WWE stars had fans convinced their relationship was over after they unfollowed each other on Instagram and removed photos together.
body: The breakup speculation started back on September 2, 2026, when fans noticed that Vaquer and Borne were no longer following each other on Instagram. Photos of the couple had also disappeared from their accounts, along with comments they previously left on each other’s posts. At the time, neither wrestler addressed the situation, leaving fans wondering whether they had quietly gone their separate ways. However, things have changed considerably since those initial rumors started circulating. Vaquer and Borne have since shared new photos together on social media, including pictures of themselves working out at the gym. Their recent activity makes it clear that the two are still spending time together, despite the earlier social media changes that had everyone questioning their relationship. That’s a pretty big difference from what fans were seeing in September. Back then, the missing photos and mutual unfollows made it look like something had gone wrong. Now they’re appearing together again, and there’s little reason to keep treating the original breakup speculation as fact. Borne had previously opened up about how their relationship started during an interview with Denise Salcedo. He admitted that both were interested in each other early on, but he was so nervous around Vaquer that he would actually avoid running into her backstage. Vaquer eventually took matters into her own hands and invited him to dinner. Their relationship became public knowledge after that, which is why the sudden disappearance of their social media interactions caught so much attention in the first place. Neither Vaquer nor Borne has publicly explained why they unfollowed each other or removed their earlier photos. It’s also unclear whether they went through a brief rough patch or simply decided to make some changes to their social media accounts. title: Is Carmelo Hayes Following Dragunov To AEW?
raw_title: Is Carmelo Hayes Following Dragunov To AEW?
body: Hayes has not wrestled since August 14, when he lost to Baron Corbin in a United States Championship match on SmackDown in Boston, his hometown. WWE has not explained his absence from television since then. Over the weekend, Hayes blacked out his profile picture on X . That kind of change is often read as a sign of tension between a wrestler and the company they work for. His handle still reads @Carmelo_WWE. AEW star MJF added to the speculation by posting an old photo on his Instagram Story of himself wrestling Christian Casanova, the name Hayes used on the independent scene before he signed with WWE. Hayes and Dragunov have a long history together. Hayes won the NXT Championship from Bron Breakker at NXT Stand & Deliver in April 2023 and held it for 182 days before losing it to Dragunov at NXT No Mercy that September. That match was named NXT's Match of the Year for 2023. The two picked up their rivalry on the main roster. Hayes beat Dragunov for the United States Championship in an open challenge in December 2025 and held the title for about three months before losing it to Sami Zayn on SmackDown in March. Hayes also has a personal tie to WWE that could factor into any decision. His partner, Kelani Jordan, is the reigning NXT Women's Champion. If Hayes is unhappy, it is easy to see why. He was a top star in NXT, a former NXT Champion and a top pick in the 2024 WWE Draft who went on to hold the United States Championship. Since losing that title, he has gone from a featured midcard act to a wrestler who has not been on television in two months. That is a tough spot for someone with his track record. Losing Hayes would hurt WWE. He is still young, he can work with anyone on the roster, and he has already shown he can carry a title. AEW would have plenty of ready-made stories for him, starting with a reunion with Dragunov and a history with MJF from their independent days. Fans should not read too much into a blacked-out profile picture on its own. Hayes has not said anything publicly, and there is no report on his contract status. Still, the long absence and the timing of these signs make it worth watching what he does next. title: The Miz Has Mixed Feelings About WrestleMania 27 Main Event
raw_title: The Miz Has Mixed Feelings On WWE WrestleMania 27 Main Event Victory
summary_src: Looking back on his first WWE WrestleMania main event, The Miz referred to it as his favorite match while also explaining his mixed feelings on it.
body: WWE WWE WrestleMania XXVII marked the first time The Miz ever wrestled in the show's main event, which saw the then-WWE Champion put his title on the line against John Cena. Luckily for Miz, he got help from Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, which set up the WrestleMania XXVIII "Once In A Lifetime" match for the following year. Despite the match being a milestone for his career and setting up one of the biggest WrestleMania main events of recent history, Miz has mixed feelings on the match today. "Main event, sold out! Georgia Dome, 65,000 people! And, they told me: 'Mike, you're gonna have pyro.' I was like: 'What? I never get pyro; I never get anything!'" he recalled during an appearance on WWE Vault . Miz noted that he had low expectations for his WWE presentation at the time, as it even took a while to land on music he approved of. "But now I'm getting pyro?" Ultimately, Miz's pyro wasn't what he expected, but this was nowhere near what actually made the night uncomfortable to look back on for him. After taking a spear onto concrete, Miz's head was accidentally slammed into the ground, resulting in a concussion. "I wanted to be tackled into an audience, I've never seen that happen! And you know I was like, 'Do we have any extras? Can we just put seats there?' And they were like, 'Well, we can't do that.' I was like, 'You know, just spear me onto the thing!' That was a dumb move, because I got knocked out, do not remember any of this!" After hitting his head, Miz still finished the match, largely due to the help of Cena, The Rock, and referee Mike Chioda. "I don't like watching that match, even though, people always ask, 'What's your favorite match?' It's like, that one [WM XVII], and they're like 'Why?' Because it's the main event of WrestleMania and not everyone gets to main event WrestleMania," he stated.
summary: The Miz achieved a career milestone by wrestling in the main event of WrestleMania 27 as WWE Champion against John Cena. He received unexpected pyro for his entrance in front of 65,000 fans at the Georgia Dome but had low expectations for his presentation at the time. The match left him with mixed feelings today after he took a spear onto concrete and accidentally had his head slammed into the ground.

title: On the Record: Myles Borne Speaks On Grayson Waller Wearing Stephanie Vaquer Shirt on WWE NXT
raw_title: Myles Borne Addresses Grayson Waller Wearing Stephanie Vaquer Shirt on WWE NXT
summary_src: Myles Borne isn’t exactly losing sleep over Grayson Waller wearing a Stephanie Vaquer shirt on NXT. In fact, Borne thinks Waller’s attempt to troll him completely backfired because all he really did was spend his own money supporting Vaquer.
body: During an appearance on The Finish with Corey Smith and Tor Smith , Borne was asked about Waller recently showing up on NXT wearing Vaquer’s merchandise. Borne had already reacted to the stunt on social media, but he made it pretty clear that Waller wasn’t getting under his skin. As Borne sees it, Waller literally paid money for Vaquer’s shirt just to try and mess with him. That’s not much of an insult when the money is ultimately helping the person you’re supposedly trying to use as bait. “Yeah, I mean, he literally went out and spent his own hard-earned money on her T-shirt. I mean, all you did was put money on our table. You put food on our table that night. Thank you. I appreciate it. So, if you thought you got me, that’s not getting me. You’re contributing. You’re a fan at that point.” Borne wasn’t finished there either. He thinks Vaquer’s shirt actually stole the entire segment because people were paying more attention to what Waller was wearing than anything coming out of his mouth. “And I hate to say it, but everyone took away the T-shirt. You wore a T-shirt, and no one cared about what you were saying. They cared about the T-shirt because, at the end of the day, she, like it or not, she’s the biggest star.” So if Waller wants to keep rocking Vaquer merch, Borne isn’t going to stop him. As far as he’s concerned, Waller can keep opening his wallet because he’s not getting the reaction he’s looking for. “So, I mean, wear the T-shirt if you want to. I really don’t care. You just put food on our table. So, if you thought you got me, you didn’t get me.” Waller wore the shirt during the October 14 episode of NXT when he pulled up to the parking lot and cut a promo about Borne facing Tony D’Angelo for a shot at his NXT Championship. However, this wasn’t the Stephanie Vaquer shirt Waller previously revealed WWE refused to let him wear on television. That other shirt featured Vaquer’s viral Instagram photo where she recreated Shawn Michaels’ famous championship pose while wearing nothing but the Women’s World Championship. Waller had the image turned into a shirt and wanted to wear it on NXT , but WWE shut that idea down before it ever reached television. “There’s some that haven’t ended up on TV. I don’t know if you remember that Stephanie Vaquer broke the internet recently. She did an Instagram story like Shawn Michaels — there was a T-shirt with that on it. That didn’t end up on TV.” Instead, Waller showed up in regular Vaquer merch, and that apparently didn’t have the effect he was hoping for either. Borne has basically flipped the troll attempt around on him, and now Waller has the distinction of publicly buying merchandise for the woman he was trying to use to mess with his challenger. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: WWF Red Letter IC Belt Sells For Record $716,750
raw_title: WWF Red Letter Intercontinental Championship Belt Becomes Most Valuable Wrestling Title Ever Sold At $716,750
summary_src: A WWF Red Letter Intercontinental Championship title belt has become the most valuable wrestling title ever sold at $716,750.
body: A WWF Red Letter Intercontinental Championship title belt has become the most valuable wrestling title ever sold at $716,750. Across wrestling history, many pieces of memorabilia and historic items in the industry have sold for high prices to fans and collectors alike, with Hulk Hogan’s 1986 WWF World Championship previously holding the record for $414,800. However, that record has now been broken with a new sale earlier this weekend. On October 25th, Conrad Thompson would take to social media, revealing that a red letter WWF Intercontinental Championship belt had broken the previous record, selling for $716,750 on October 24th on Heritage Auctions. You can check out the description of the belt on the auction site below. Between 1985 and 1988, the Intercontinental Championship belonged to some of the most memorable personalities of WWE’s boom years. Tito Santana wore it with pride and athleticism. Randy “Macho Man” Savage made it feel as important as any prize in wrestling. Ricky “The Dragon” Steamboat brought grace and precision, while The Honky Tonk Man held on through swagger, shortcuts, and sheer nerve. Together, they helped give the belt its lasting reputation as the working man’s championship, awarded to the wrestler counted on to perform every night. No match captures that reputation better than Savage and Steamboat at WrestleMania III. On March 29, 1987, the two delivered a fast, beautifully timed contest that ended with Steamboat winning the title. Though Hulk Hogan and Andre the Giant headlined the show, Savage and Steamboat produced the match that many fans and wrestlers still remember as the evening’s masterpiece. It remains widely regarded as one of the finest bouts ever staged. For fans who grew up during wrestling’s 1980s explosion, this belt is instantly recognizable. It recalls packed arenas, larger-than-life characters, and champions who could truly work. More than gold and leather, it represents an era and a standard that still resonate generations later. Heritage Auctions created waves in the wrestling world by realizing $1,037,000 for Hogan’s photo-matched WrestleMania I boots in February of 2026. The iconic boots were worn when Hogan teamed with Mr. T in the main event of Vince McMahon’s creation which helped take wrestling into the mainstream. Heritage Auctions further established itself as the leading auction house for high-quality wrestling material by selling Hogan’s WrestleMania II photo-matched belt for a staggering $414,800 in August 23, 2026. We are including an online dissertation which gives the wrestling world a complete history of the offered belt through the eyes of historian Conrad Thompson. Thompson is widely regarded as the belt expert. His analysis delves into how the belt reached its current state and the relevance of the men who held the prize during wrestling’s renaissance of the 1980’s. The Intercontinental Championship was held between 1985 and 1988 by several prominent figures during WWE’s expansion period. Holders included Tito Santana, Randy Savage, Ricky Steamboat, and The Honky Tonk Man.

A notable match involving the title took place at WrestleMania III on March 29, 1987, when Randy Savage faced Ricky Steamboat. Steamboat won the championship in a bout widely regarded as one of the event’s standout performances.

title: Dominik Mysterio Details AAA's Biggest Gain From WWE

summary_src: Dominik Mysterio has explained the biggest way AAA has benefited from WWE's involvement through main roster names appearing.
body: Dominik Mysterio has explained the biggest way AAA has benefited from WWE’s involvement through main roster names appearing. Since WWE acquired AAA, several of their main roster and NXT stars have made their way onto AAA programming, including the likes of Dominik Mysterio who has captured the Mega Championship in the promotion. While speaking to Ring Rust Radio, Dominik Mysterio was asked about what the biggest way AAA has benefited from WWE’s involvement, pointing to the main roster stars that have appeared in the promotion. “I mean, just, you know, if you look at all the names that have been able to go down there and work with AAA, that’s main roster talent. You know, you have guys like Chad (Gable), (El) Grande, myself, Roxanne going down there, Damien Priest, you know, I believe Young OG’s gone down there, Je’Von, he’s gone down there for a couple of AAA shows, so it’s like, just the amount of talent that circulates through all of AAA, not only that, but also, like, just the mega powerhouse that WWE is, and the exposure that they give them, you know, it’s absolutely second to none. So it definitely benefited Triple A in a massive way to partner up with them.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Cody Rhodes Recalls Pac Tribute Organized By Kevin Owens
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Remembers Pac, Says Kevin Owens Set Up Camera For WWE Stars To Pay Tribute
summary_src: Cody Rhodes remembered late AEW star Pac, and said that Kevin Owens set up a camera for other WWE stars to pay tribute to the former Neville.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik The entire professional wrestling world was rocked by the passing of AEW star Pac , real name Benjamin Satterley, just after AEW All Out 2026, an event where the star wrestled for the AEW National Championship . In the days that followed, many wrestlers he worked with, including in WWE, shared their memories of him . WWE released a YouTube video of various talents pouring their hearts out and sharing more. Cody Rhodes, who worked with Satterley in both companies, told WrestleTalk during an interview that it was one of Satterley's close friends, Kevin Owens, who set up the camera at a TV taping for the stars to share their grief . "He had a camera set up for all of us to go speak to, if we wanted to speak about Ben," Rhodes said. "I thought long and hard about, 'What's my relationship there?' Because we weren't, you know, incredibly great friends, but if you look at your career and you look over across the ring at these milestones, SummerSlam at Barclays Center, and to have the 'Arrow' crossover match, and there he is. There's Ben. Then you look at my time away and being one of the OGs when AEW started and there's Ben. I'm looking through our texts and you start to think, 'Wow, we were married to each other at one point during live events when it was Stardust vs. Neville.'" Rhodes said that he never met another wrestler who knew himself more than Satterley, which he called "intimidating" as he tried to figure out who he was as both a person and an on-screen character. Rhodes said that he is a better human, a wrestler, and storyteller for having known and learned from him.
