In the period following his passing, numerous wrestlers who had shared rings with him in both AEW and WWE offered tributes and personal recollections.
WWE produced a YouTube video featuring several performers expressing their thoughts and emotions about Satterley.

Cody Rhodes, who had faced Satterley across multiple promotions, revealed during a WrestleTalk interview that Kevin Owens arranged a camera setup at a television taping so colleagues could record messages if they chose.
"He had a camera set up for all of us to go speak to, if we wanted to speak about Ben," Rhodes said.

Rhodes explained that he reflected deeply on their connection, noting they were not extremely close yet appeared together at significant career points including a SummerSlam match at Barclays Center and an "Arrow" crossover bout.

He recalled Satterley's presence during his own hiatus from WWE and as an original figure when AEW launched, while reviewing old text messages that highlighted their shared history such as working live events as Stardust versus Neville.

Rhodes observed that he had never encountered another wrestler who possessed such a complete understanding of his own identity, describing the quality as intimidating while he navigated his personal and character development.
He concluded that knowing Satterley and absorbing lessons from him had improved him as a person, wrestler, and storyteller.

title: Liv Morgan Feared WWE Would Stop Her From Auditioning for Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo
raw_title: Liv Morgan Feared WWE Would Stop Her From Auditioning for Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo
summary_src: Liv Morgan thought her latest movie opportunity might get shut down before she even had the chance to audition.
body: During an interview with Japanese outlet Real Sound to promote the movie, Morgan opened up about how she landed her first major feature film role. Since WWE operates with PG programming, she wasn’t sure the company would be comfortable with her appearing in a movie that definitely doesn’t fall into that same category. Morgan was prepared for WWE to reject the idea altogether. Instead, she discovered that Takashi Miike apparently has some pretty big fans inside WWE’s executive ranks. “It was an audition. My initial concern was that the script wasn’t rated PG (suitable for all ages). Since the WWE shows I belong to are rated PG, I was prepared for the company to tell me, ‘Absolutely not.’” Things went in a completely different direction once WWE learned who was directing the movie. According to Morgan, several executives were fans of Miike and gave her the green light to go after the role. “But there are many big fans of director Takashi Miike among the WWE executives, and they kindly gave me permission, saying, ‘If it’s a movie by Director Miike, it’s OK, go ahead and audition.’” Morgan ultimately landed the role and spent time in Japan filming Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo in May 2025. The movie also stars Shun Oguri, Lily James and Shotaro Mamiya, with Morgan appearing as Megan, a mysterious woman who comes to Japan to train as a sushi chef. Fans finally got their first look at Morgan in the movie when NEON released its first trailer in August 2026 . Her appearance in the footage confirmed that this wasn’t simply a small credit with her name attached, as she was shown alongside members of the film’s main cast. Morgan’s concern about getting WWE’s approval turned out to be unnecessary, but the reason she got the green light is probably the more surprising part of the story. Had Miike not already had fans in high places inside WWE, Morgan’s first major movie opportunity might have played out very differently. title: Marina Shafir Sends Message to Mercedes Moné
raw_title: Marina Shafir cuts promo on Mercedes Moné following AEW Collision
summary_src: Marina Shafir cut a promo directed at AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné following AEW Collision.
body: Marina Shafir cut a promo directed at AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné following AEW Collision . On Saturday’s show in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, Shafir made Trish Adora tap out to PAC’s Brutalizer submission hold to pick up the win for the Death Riders over Shane Taylor Promotions in an eight-person mixed tag match. Shafir also later participated in the show-closing brawl involving the Death Riders, the Conglomeration, and Jay White’s new faction, The Cut, which was briefly known as The Last Outfit. AEW then posted a backstage promo from Shafir, where she had the following to say to Moné: “Mercedes, we all know you’re not a p—sy. I just needed to get your full attention. I actually have a lot of respect for you. You are in a league of your own. And as much as it might pain you to think or to even say, you know that I am too. That’s where the difference lies between you and me. You need to swing your dominance in between your legs. And I don’t. I can’t even compliment myself. I don’t need bells and whistles. I don’t need affirmations. I don’t need a dance. I don’t need production. I just need the opportunity to work. All of the work that I have been doing these last three years has gotten me here. But there’s something else that I need. I need to stand across the ring from you. And I want to show everyone exactly who I am, but most importantly, I need to show you.” Shafir also confronted Moné at AEW Dynamite on Wednesday as Moné was celebrating her AEW Women’s World Championship title defense against Thekla at AEW WrestleDream. Shafir came out and confronted Moné, who backed off and left the ring area. Ian Carey Ian Carey is the Managing Editor at F4WOnline and is based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. title: On the Record: Liv Morgan Explains How She Landed Role in Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo
raw_title: Liv Morgan Explains How She Landed Role in Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo
summary_src: Liv Morgan didn’t get handed her Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo role because she was a WWE Superstar either. She actually had to audition for the part, and apparently it didn’t take long for the people behind the movie to realize they had found their Megan.
body: During her interview with Japanese outlet Real Sound , Morgan explained exactly how she landed her first major feature film role. She recorded herself performing two scenes, sent the audition tape to the production team and waited to see what happened. The response ended up being about as good as an actor could hope for. After watching Morgan’s audition, the production team apparently decided right away that she was the person they wanted for Megan. “I filmed myself performing the two designated scenes and sent the tape (video) to the production team. After watching the footage, the production team said, ‘She’s Megan!’ and chose me.” Morgan was already looking to branch out into more movies and television at the time, which made the opportunity even bigger for her. Once she saw the names attached to the project, she knew this wasn’t something she wanted to pass up. “It was a time when I really wanted to try more movies and dramas, and with Shun Oguri and Lily James in the lead roles, Takashi Miike directing, and NEON involved, I felt incredibly fortunate to have seized such a valuable opportunity.” Morgan spent time away from WWE television in May 2025 while filming the movie in Japan. She stars as Megan, a mysterious woman who comes to Japan to train as a sushi chef, alongside Shun Oguri, Lily James and Shotaro Mamiya. Fans eventually got their first look at Morgan in the movie when NEON released the trailer in August 2026 . Now it’s clear that her WWE fame may have opened plenty of doors throughout her career, but when it came to Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo, she still had to send in the tape and win the role herself. summary_src: Charlotte Flair provides a positive update on her father, WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair, after he suffered a fall on Friday.
body: WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair suffered a scary fall on Friday morning . According to his daughter Charlotte Flair, though, it seems that he emerged from it okay, both physically and mentally. Following the news of Ric's fall, Charlotte took to X to provide an update on his condition, noting that her father had jokingly blamed the situation on his late WWE colleague The Ultimate Warrior. "Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head," Charlotte wrote . "... (ps: he's going to be ok)." Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head... Ric, 77, had reportedly exited a Tampa bar, leaving his phone and drink behind, when he suddenly fell as he walked across the street. The collapse resulted in multiple injuries, including cuts to Ric's head and eye, the latter of which was said to be bleeding extensively afterward. An ambulance then escorted "The Nature Boy" to a local hospital, where he recovered for several hours. "Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers!" Ric himself wrote after the incident. "I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger. Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay!" Just hours before his fall, Ric revealed that he was unable to make a public appearance due to a blood clot in his leg preventing him from traveling certain distances. It is unknown if that clot factored into his collapse and subsequent trip to the hospital.
summary: Ric Flair suffered a fall outside a Tampa bar on Friday morning that caused cuts to his head and eye. Charlotte Flair shared that her father is going to be okay and joked about the incident with doctors. Ric, 77, spent several hours in a local hospital and later thanked fans for their messages and prayers.

title: Is WWE's Cody Rhodes heel turn finally happening?
raw_title: Is WWE's Cody Rhodes heel turn finally happening?
body: It was last week that we saw Rhodes, now well into his fourth year as WWE's golden boy, finally deliver the punt kick he first teased at SummerSlam . There was just one catch: It wasn't Randy Orton on the receiving end of Rhodes' size 10 boot, but Baron Corbin. (Who knows, maybe Corbin had been teasing Rhodes backstage about his Guile hairdo.) On Friday's "SmackDown," Rhodes had calmed down slightly, as he squared off against Randy Orton, the man who has been on his tail for months now. Though just in case we'd forgotten about Cody's new ruthless streak, he made sure to request the most violent stipulation possible (at least in modern WWE) for their upcoming match at Crown Jewel : Last man standing. With scenes like that, it's only natural to ask the obvious question: Are we finally on the verge of witnessing that Cody heel turn — the long-mooted narrative H-bomb the WWE creatives have been keeping tucked up their sleeves for much of the past few years? Not so fast, you might think. After all, we've been here before — quite literally in this case. Last August, when Rhodes beat the paste out of John Cena on "SmackDown" in order to force him to sign the contract for their upcoming SummerSlam match, I suggested we might just be about to see the arrival of "Dark Cody." And what happened? Within 48 hours, both men were hugging it out in a tearful embrace. So why might this time be different when it comes to Heel Cody? First off, there's that aforementioned Randy Orton feud. After years of scrambling around trying to find an opponent that feels like a genuine menace to "The American Nightmare," WWE has finally done it. Orton hasn't just beaten Rhodes, he's also gotten into his head, leaving Rhodes more concerned about revenge than winning back his old world title. Indeed, you need only to look at the numbers. As of this weekend, Rhodes has now been without the WWE Championship for 119 days. That's 14 days longer than the gap between Cody dropping the belt to Cena and then winning it back last year. That means it's the longest we've seen Rhodes go without gold since he finished his story at WrestleMania XL in 2024. And that's all down to Randy Orton. Given that, is it any wonder that Rhodes has been losing his cool in (kayfabe) interviews with Michael Cole, dropping F-bombs like it's the Attitude Era all over again? title: Jeff Jarrett Wishes For Shawn Michaels Rematch
raw_title: AEW's Jeff Jarrett Wishes He'd Have Gotten Rematch With This WWE Hall Of Famer
summary_src: AEW star Jeff Jarrett revealed on "My World" that he wishes he could have gotten a rematch with one fellow WWE Hall of Famer.
body: AEW Jeff Jarrett has accomplished so much within the professional wrestling industry over the years, from working in both WCW and the then-WWF during the "Monday Night Wars," as well as creating a promotion of his own with TNA. There are many things the current AEW star hasn't done, however, and on an episode of "My World," he revealed one thing he wishes he got to do back in his heyday. "I think the thing that jumps off the page, would be I never really got a 'rematch' with Shawn Michaels off of 'In Your House,'" Jarrett said. "That always comes to my mind is having a rematch with Shawn." The two WWE Hall of Famers faced off at WWF In Your House 2: The Lumberjacks in Jarrett's hometown of Nashville in July 1995. He and Michaels fought for the Intercontinental Championship, which Michaels won to begin his third reign with the title. The only other time the pair were in the ring together was during a 10-man tag team match in November 1994. They were on the same side and teamed with Diesel, Jim Neidhart, and Owen Hart. Co-host Conrad Thompson joked that it would be hard to book a rematch after one of the competitors quit and walked out. Jarrett infamously walked out of WWF , for the first time, following the "In Your House" match due to creative tension with Vince McMahon. "I didn't get to do it! I killed it!" Jarrett admitted, with a laugh.

body: Pro-wrestler Amber “Nova” Flora was arrested in Florida over the weekend for a DUI and refusing to submit to a DUI test, according to police. Flora, 34, who goes by Amber Nova in the ring, was taken into custody in Orlando on Friday at 5:40 a.m., according to the Orlando Police Department. She was released less than five hours later after posting $2,000 in bail. Flora attended a mandatory court appearance on Saturday, with the wrestler set to return for a follow-up hearing next Monday, TMZ reported . Flora, who was born in New Jersey, made a name for herself in the SHINE Wrestling circuit, where she claimed the Nova Championship in 2023. Prior to SHINE, Flora had a brief stint in losing matches at WWE’s NXT wrestling program and at All Elite Wrestling. Prior to her wrestling career. Flora worked as an emergency medical technician and studied at the Technical College of the Lowcountry, in South Carolina.

title: Independent Wrestler Jadis Quinn Claims They Were Jumped By Group After Homophobic Confrontation
raw_title: Independent Wrestler Jadis Quinn Claims They Were Jumped By Group After Homophobic Confrontation
summary_src: Independent wrestler Jadis Quinn says they were jumped by four people at a bar in Hagerstown after being hit with homophobic slurs.
body: Quinn took to Facebook to describe the incident, claiming three men and a woman confronted them before things turned physical. The wrestler says they were outnumbered and targeted simply for being themselves. “It finally happened. Called multiple slurs then outnumbered by 3 grown men and a woman.” But Quinn says the attack wasn’t the end of it. According to the wrestler, security guards at the bar were friends with the alleged attackers and actually threw Quinn to the ground when they tried to defend themselves. “Gay bashing still happens, and even defending yourself gets you thrown to the ground by security guards who were also friends with my attackers.” Quinn insists they weren’t bothering anyone before the confrontation started. They say they were simply minding their own business when the group allegedly decided to attack them. “All I did tonight, was be my true authentic self .. and for some reason, that got me physically attacked.” The wrestler was furious over what happened and questioned how someone could end up getting attacked just for being themselves. Quinn also called out the people they say jumped them and the security guards who allegedly helped protect those responsible. “Genuinely I ask, what the f ** has happened to society? Minding my business, being myself, and not bothering anyone.. and I get attacked .. honestly, why? For what?”* “To the people who attacked me tonight, and the guards who protected them.., are yall ok with yourselves? Cause genuinely, I’m concerned for you own mentality” Quinn, known in the independent wrestling scene as “The Twink Temptress,” has competed for several regional promotions. They also made history at the 2025 Shane Shamrock Memorial Cup when they faced Aaron Rourke in the tournament’s first match between two openly LGBTQ wrestlers. It’s unclear whether Quinn suffered any injuries or filed a police report. The allegations have not been independently verified, and neither the bar nor the people accused of attacking Quinn have publicly responded in the information available. For now, Quinn is putting the alleged attackers on blast after what they describe as a homophobic confrontation that turned violent. What was supposed to be a night out following a wrestling show ended with Quinn claiming they were jumped by four people and then thrown to the ground by security. They’re making sure everyone knows exactly what they say happened. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.

title: Samoa Joe Picks Brock Lesnar As Hardest-Hitting Opponent

summary_src: Former AEW World Champion Samoa Joe named the opponent who hit him hardest in the ring.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Throughout his lengthy career spanning many promotions, from Ring of Honor, to TNA, to WWE, and now, AEW, Samoa Joe has faced off against many hard-hitting opponents. The star, recently returned to AEW with his sights set on Will Ospreay's AEW World Championship , sat down with "SHAK Wrestling" and played a game to determine just who hit him hardest in the ring. He was given two names to start with, and the winner stayed on. Joe was first tasked with choosing between Brock Lesnar and Kurt Angle. "Kurt, I think it's the battle of technique vs. raw, unbridled power," Joe said. "I think they both, they have great technique. They both have their own kind of reserved power, but I think when you talk about the balance, I think Brock hits a little bit harder. Kurt, maybe a little bit more technical prowess." Lesnar beat out Shinsuke Nakamura, Bryan Danielson, and Claudio Castagnoli for Joe, though he had to think a bit when comparing Lesnar to Castagnoli. He said "The Beast Incarnate" also hit harder than Nigel McGuiness and Necro Butcher, though Butcher was another name Joe to think about for a moment. Minoru Suzuki was also beaten out by Lesnar, as well as Low Ki, with some further contemplation that Joe called "the choice of a generation." "We're going to go destructive potential, but extreme enthusiasm, and effort and a very, very close call, but we're going to stick with Brock," Joe said. Finally, when Lesnar was compared to Kenta Kobashi, Joe once again choose Lesnar. He said he faced off against an older Kobashi, who was a touch less explosive, and named "The Beast" his hardest-hitting opponent.

title: Rey Pegasus Details His Unique High-Flying Approach

body: Rey Pegasus first made a name for himself in the promotion by winning the 2026 Torneo de Escuelas. He teamed up with Tornado in the tournament, and ultimately defeated Estudiante Jr. & Feroz and Pantera Jr. & Psycotic to win it. Speaking with Fightful’s Luis Pulido , Pegasus was asked about his high-flying style of wrestling. “That’s exactly what has made the difference. I was well aware that the World Wrestling Council has magnificent aerial wrestlers; that’s why, during my training at the schools, I focused specifically on coming up with moves that were very different from anything the company had seen before: very different aerial moves because, obviously, the audience likes to see something different. I believe my training has always been about making a difference and not being like everyone else, and that’s what has helped us. It’s helped us with Tornado as well. All the new moves I’ve introduced & that we’ve incorporated into our matches have really helped me a lot. People say that wrestling has already been invented, but we’re always looking for that extra something—that element that makes everything look different to please the audience, to please the media, and to please everyone who comes to watch us make that difference. That was precisely the idea—to get people to turn their attention to us, not to set that standard and say, ‘Okay, look, he does very different things’—and to this day, that’s what’s helping us.” Elsewhere in the interview, Pegasus talked about meeting fellow wrestlers in Torneo de Escuelas. raw_title: Natural Talent: WWE megastar Seth Rollins entertains as an engaging NFL analyst
body: ⚽️ Check out the Premier League Sponsors Directory for 2026-27 Asked for an example of her husband’s passion for the NFL, Rebecca Quin immediately turns to the soda bread story. Shortly before Thanksgiving last year, Richy Quin, a sculptor and chef who lives and works in Ireland, visited his younger sister and her husband at their home in Los Angeles. Richy had not spent a lot of time with Rebecca’s husband, Colby Lopez, and wasn’t very familiar with the NFL, given the suburbs of Dublin were not exactly an American football hotbed when he and Rebecca were growing up. But Richy was game to spend some time with his brother-in-law, an obsessed fan of the Chicago Bears, and sat down in the family’s living room to see what this NFL thing was about. “When you’re around Colby and you don’t know him that well — and my brother wouldn’t have spent much time with him in person — he’s quite quiet,” Rebecca says. “He’s reserved and thoughtful, and you can have very normal conversations with him. But when he watches the Bears, he turns into an animal. An animal! I find it hilarious and entertaining. “So my brother is with us and he’s telling me, ‘Yeah, I’ll watch some American football with Colby, this will be great.’ Three plays in, and I mean literally three plays in, my brother says, ‘Uh, I think I’m going to go make some soda bread.’ He was like, ‘This is too much for me!’” Rebecca reports the soda bread was delicious, so the afternoon was not a total loss for Richy. If the names above are not familiar, we understand. You are probably more familiar with the couple’s professional names. Rebecca Quin is better known as Becky Lynch, one of the all-time greats in pro wrestling who is currently signed with WWE. Colby Lopez, her husband, is of course Seth Rollins, a fellow WWE megastar and the obsessed Bears fan who scares family members into cooking soda bread. Plenty of WWE performers are fans of traditional sports, but Rollins is sui generis in that he has translated his passion for the NFL into legitimate sports broadcasting assignments. Since 2022, he has appeared on the NFL Network’s flagship morning show, “Good Morning Football,” and last year joined the show as an official guest host. He was a studio analyst for Netflix’s 2025 NFL Christmas Day broadcast between the Detroit Lions and Minnesota Vikings, and earlier this year worked as a commentator on Netflix’s presentation of “Skyscraper Live,” which featured American free climber Alex Honnold scaling the 1,667-foot Taipei 101 building. Rollins has also added guest-hosting “The Rich Eisen Show” to his growing sports broadcasting résumé, and he has made appearances on Radio Row at the Super Bowl since 2022. “If we went back to 1989, ‘The NFL Today’ and CBS are not going to have The Ultimate Warrior on,” said Kyle Brandt, the long-running host of “Good Morning Football.” “This is perfect timing for Seth. Sports shows today will take someone who’s interesting, has something to say and has a perspective. Set

raw_title: Roxanne Perez Tells Nikki Bella Old Age Is Making Her Forget Who Beat Her Twice
summary_src: Nikki Bella might want to check her memory because Roxanne Perez says old age is catching up with her. The Judgment Day star just fired back at the WWE Hall of Famer for calling her irrelevant, reminding Nikki that she’s already beaten her twice.
body: On October 25, Perez went after Nikki on Twitter after seeing her comments from SmackDown. Nikki had questioned why Roxanne was getting a shot at Chelsea Green’s WWE Women’s Championship before her, calling Perez the least relevant member of The Judgment Day. Roxanne clearly wasn’t impressed. She brought up her previous wins over Nikki, questioned whether Bella’s age was affecting her memory and then offered to beat her again. “Just saw that the least relevant member of the Bella twins mentioned me! I beat Chelsea one on one silly! Old age must be making you forget I’m the only member of the judgement day to beat you 2x. ☆ That’s one way to remind someone about their losing record. Nikki wanted to know why Roxanne was getting a championship opportunity, and Perez pointed out that she’d already beaten Chelsea Green in a singles match to earn it. The argument started during the October 16 episode of WWE SmackDown, when Nikki complained about Perez getting a title match ahead of her. Nikki didn’t think Roxanne deserved to be in that position, but Perez clearly thinks the Hall of Famer needs a reminder of what’s happened inside the ring. And Roxanne didn’t just bring up Nikki’s age. She also took Nikki’s famous Bella Twins catchphrase and turned it against her, telling her she can look but can’t win. body: There’s a story in The Sentinel-Record about the Arkansas Walk of Fame. One of the inductees for 2026 is Sid Eudy, a.k.a. Sycho Sid. The induction happened on October 24th. Eudy passed away in August 2024. In April 2026, WWE posthumously inducted him into the Hall of Fame via the Legacy Wing. He is a two-time WWF Champion. The son of Eudy publicly shared his thoughts about WWE’s honoring of his father and noted that it was disappointing and disrespectful. In late August, there was a Sycho Sid Memorial Benefit Show in Memphis, Tennessee. One of the participants was WWE talent Jordynne Grace.

title: WWE Signs Former Michigan State Athlete Elly Finch
raw_title: WWE Reportedly Signs Former Michigan State Track & Field Athlete To Developmental Deal
summary_src: A former shot put thrower for Michigan State's Track and Field team has reportedly inked a developmental deal with WWE.
body: According to PWInsider , 23-year-old Elly Finch has inked a developmental deal with WWE after impressing at her latest company tryout, held during the 2026 SummerSlam weekend in Minnesota. Finch, a former shot put thrower for Michigan State's Track and Field team, initially participated in a WWE tryout hosted at the WWE Performance Center this past January. A bump to the head kept her sidelined for a portion of it. Still, she managed to show enough potential that WWE officials invited her back for another one, this time centered around "The Biggest Party of the Summer." "The second or third day, I hit my head and they said I had a concussion, so I had to sit out a couple days. But it's fine," Finch said in a January 2026 Instagram video . "I did my promos and everything, so I still had a blast. Anyway, my WWE recruiter called me the other day, and she said that, unfortunately, I didn't get signed, but they want to invite me back for an extended tryout, which they often do if they like someone, but they kind of want to see a little more from them. So I was invited to the SummerSlam tryout they're hosting in like six-ish months." Following her official signing, Finch is expected to be part of the incoming WWE NXT Performance Center class. The latest group, announced last month , included former WWE ID prospect Zoe Sager, Aussie indie standouts Scott Green and The Tuckman, and WWE Hall of Famer Rey Mysterio's daughter Aalyah Gutierrez. WWE has held two additional tryout experiences since SummerSlam. The first took the company to Colombia ; the second emanated from the state of Hawaii last weekend.
summary: Per PWInsider, 23-year-old Elly Finch signed a developmental contract with WWE after a successful extended tryout held during SummerSlam weekend in Minnesota. The former Michigan State shot put thrower first attended a Performance Center tryout in January 2026 where a concussion sidelined her for part of the event but still completed her promos. WWE officials invited her back for further evaluation after expressing interest in her potential.

title: Samoa Joe Prioritizes Fun Matches Over Retirement Plans
raw_title: AEW's Samoa Joe Shares Thoughts On In-Ring Retirement
summary_src: Former AEW World Champion Samoa Joe discusses his priorities.
body: AEW The biggest stars of the previous pro wrestling generation are all seemingly hanging their boots one after the other, with John Cena, AJ Styles, and Adam 'Edge' Copeland who recently announced that 2027 will be his final year of active in-ring competition . Samoa Joe made a name for himself in TNA, where he often had intense rivalries with Styles , has since become a major player in AEW. But, in light of all the retirements, Joe was asked about his thoughts surrounding retirement and his approach to his career at this stage, during a recent interview with " SHAK Wrestling ." "Really just, putting on fun matches for the fans [is my priority], you know?" he said. "Listen, what my time frame is? Kind of still... Not quite nailed down, but I will say this: I want to leave as many good memories I can while I [still] have the opportunity [to]." Outside of pro wrestling, the acting bug has also bitten Joe, mainly with his role as the physical actor of "Sweet Tooth" in the "Twisted Metal" television series, and several video game roles like 2025's "Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii" and the upcoming "Deadlock." But, even with these doors now open to him, he still plans to keep giving back to the wrestling industry. "It sounds super noble and all this stuff, but you know in reality I've had this amazing journey that – is really not fraught with a lot of heartache and despair," he explained, also proclaiming how much he's loved travelling all his career. "There's a lot of places that have a lot of love for you, as long as you have the best intentions and yeah, I'd like to sprinkle a little bit back before I'm done, and hopefully leave the pro wrestling industry a much better place than I found it."
summary: AEW star Samoa Joe, who rose to prominence in TNA through his rivalries with AJ Styles, discussed his mindset amid recent retirement announcements from wrestlers like John Cena, AJ Styles, and Adam Copeland. In an interview with SHAK Wrestling, Joe said his focus is on delivering enjoyable bouts for fans while creating lasting memories, noting that his own timeline remains undecided. He has also taken on acting work outside wrestling, including as the physical performer for Sweet Tooth in the Twisted Metal series and voice roles in upcoming video games.

Samoa Joe built his reputation in TNA through notable rivalries, including those with AJ Styles. He has since established himself as a key figure in AEW.

When asked about his own retirement plans during an interview, Samoa Joe emphasized his focus on delivering enjoyable matches for audiences. He added that his exact timeline remains undecided but that he aims to create positive memories while he continues to perform.

Despite these acting pursuits, Samoa Joe intends to continue contributing to professional wrestling. He described his career as largely positive, highlighted his enjoyment of traveling, and expressed a desire to give back to the industry and improve it before he departs.

title: In Memoriam: Kalisto Nearly Died From COVID and Was Ready to Quit Wrestling
raw_title: Kalisto Nearly Died From COVID and Was Ready to Quit Wrestling
summary_src: Kalisto came dangerously close to walking away from professional wrestling for good. The former WWE United States Champion revealed that he nearly died from COVID after his WWE release, spending roughly two and a half months in the hospital before seriously considering retirement.
body: During an interview with David Otunga, Kalisto opened up about two terrifying experiences that nearly cost him his life. The first happened years earlier when he landed on his head during a wrestling match in Mexico. The second came after his departure from WWE when he suffered a severe case of COVID. Kalisto explained that he had kept much of his medical situation private, but the experience was serious enough to leave him hospitalized for an extended period. “I had two near-death experiences. That one uh where I landed on my head and the co—” “Yeah, I was uh in the ER for like two and a half months. I didn’t I didn’t tell anybody, you know. I I don’t like, you know, spreading my medical history out there, you know. I’m a private person.” The former WWE star admitted that being hospitalized during the pandemic was an incredibly difficult experience, especially because he was dealing with everything alone. The illness came just months after he was released from WWE in April 2021. “And um but yeah, it was it it was hard, man. I mean, I was alone and I mean, obviously, there was a time of COVID and it was right after I got released actually after um a couple months later. Then I was there in the hospital a couple months later and and uh it was it was hard. It was hard.” Things got so bad that Kalisto began questioning whether continuing his wrestling career was worth it. He had already survived one near-fatal accident earlier in his career, and now another major health scare had pushed him toward retirement. “I I was about to retire um after what I was talking to you. I’m going back to the story where I had COVID that I almost died. I wanted to retire again. Everything comes back in full circle.” However, everything changed when Mojo Rawley invited him to participate in a private charity wrestling event for children with autism and their families. Kalisto was booked in the main event alongside a young fan named Little Joey, who wanted to become his tag team partner. Kalisto explained that he even purchased a matching outfit so they could make their entrance together. Drawing on his previous experience as a special education teacher, he also prepared the children for the loud noises that would happen throughout the match. “So, I went to um Party City and I ended up getting the same outfit like, ‘Hey man, I want to be part of your so we could look like a tag team.’ So I ended up dressing like him and we were the greatest showmen, but the greatest showman and we did like a little entrance and I did the match.” Little Joey ultimately scored the winning pinfall, and the reaction from the children and their families completely changed Kalisto’s outlook on his future. He admitted that he arrived at the event already convinced that his wrestling career was finished. However, seeing the happiness he brought to the children made him realize he wasn’t ready to walk away. “I had my mindset already set that I was gonna retire I’m done I had co I nearly died um

title: Backstage Buzz: AAA Had Plans to Unmask Penta and Abandon His Character
raw_title: AAA Had Plans to Unmask Penta and Abandon His Character
summary_src: Penta could have lost a whole lot more than a match if one major AAA storyline had actually gone ahead. According to Kalisto, there were plans for him to unmask Penta and basically kill off the character before his own move to WWE changed everything.
body: Speaking with David Otunga , Kalisto, now known as Samuray del Sol, opened up about his history with Penta in Mexico. The former United States Champion said he wasn’t surprised at all to see Penta eventually make it to WWE and find success. “No, I knew. I knew the minute he went to WWE, I knew he was going to go above and beyond, and he still is. I’m very happy for him and for Rey Fénix, too, because they worked really hard.” Then Kalisto dropped the much bigger revelation. Before leaving Mexico for WWE, he says the plan was for him to unmask Penta, with the loss apparently ending the Penta character completely. “Not a lot of people know this, that before I left for WWE, I was supposed to demask him, and no more Penta. It was going to be gone. It was no longer going to exist. He was going to go back to Dark Dragon.” Obviously, that never happened. Kalisto left for WWE, Penta kept the character and turned it into something much bigger than anyone involved in those original plans could have known at the time. “But when I left, he kept the character. He made it work. And look at him now.” Kalisto has no hard feelings about how things played out either. Both men went their separate ways and built their own identities, with Kalisto pointing out how “Cero Miedo” and “Lucha, Lucha” became major parts of their respective careers. “He went on his own path. I went on my own path. You know, his scream ‘Cero Miedo,’ my scream ‘Lucha, Lucha.’ So we both have some good, good strong screams, you know, and great connections.” The two eventually got another chance to wrestle years later in Guadalajara, shortly before Penta signed with WWE. Kalisto revealed that he won the match, although both men were being especially careful because neither wanted anything happening to Penta right before such a huge career move. “We had this cool match that nobody knows about. We had it in Guadalajara, and he was already getting close to going to WWE. I think this was a couple years back, right before he got signed. So, yeah, I did a match with him, and I won. We were both careful because, I mean, of course, I don’t want him to be hurt or anything, you know, right before going over there.” Now Kalisto is watching his old rival enjoy another huge run, including Penta’s Money in the Bank victory. He isn’t ruling out the possibility of them ending up across the ring from each other again someday either. “I’m just really happy when I saw him win the briefcase, man. He’s going to go further. And I just—hey, man, who knows? Maybe we could meet one day, or never say never, right? So, hey, he’s doing great.” Had Kalisto stayed and AAA followed through with the original plan, one of wrestling’s most recognizable masked identities might have disappeared years ago. Instead, Penta kept the mask, kept the character and eventually carried it all the way to WWE. title: On the Record: Joe Hendry Opens Up On What Went Wrong With His WWE Plans for Logan Paul
raw_title: Joe Hendry Reveals What Went Wrong With His WWE Plans for Logan Paul
summary_src: Joe Hendry isn’t done with Logan Paul just yet — but things didn’t exactly go according to plan. Hendry has now opened up about what happened with their WWE feud, and it turns out there was a reason things never went any further.
body: During a new interview about his WWE career , Hendry was asked about his future on Monday Night RAW and which stars he’d like to face next. That’s when he brought up Logan Paul and admitted their rivalry hit a roadblock after Paul suffered an injury. “Well, I mean, you know, I’m in a tough spot right now. Um, so I was in a feud with with Logan Paul. He he he got um injured so I couldn’t uh we we you know I couldn’t take that where he needed to go and maybe do some more songs about Logan. Who knows? Then I had problems with uh with the the vision and the judgment day. I got problems with everybody.” Hendry had already been taking shots at Paul through his music, including his song “Fire Logan Paul.” But it sounds like he wanted to do a lot more with the feud before the injury got in the way. He didn’t say exactly what else was planned, but he clearly wasn’t ready to move on. And Logan Paul isn’t the only WWE star Hendry has problems with. He’s also been dealing with The Vision and Judgment Day, leaving him with plenty of enemies and no clear direction. But there’s one thing he knows he wants — championship gold. “So I’m I’m in a I’m in a tough spot here. I got problems with everyone. But I mean for me my goal is to be um is to be a champion in WWE. I, you know, when I got to NXT and I became NXT champion, so I I mean, I know I can do it. I know that I can that that I can be a top star in the WWE. I have the tools to do it. So, that’s what I’m trying to do.” Hendry isn’t just looking for another feud to keep himself busy. He wants to become one of WWE’s top stars, and he’s already looking at one title in particular. “I’m trying to um become one of the top guys over a long period of time. That’s that’s my long-term goal. Um, and yeah, I think now I need to think about how can I get myself into the title picture. So, you know, I’m looking at the Intercontinental title picture is looking pretty cool right now.” So Hendry has a decision to make. He can try to finish what he started with Logan Paul, or he can go after the Intercontinental Championship and take his WWE career in a different direction. Either way, he’s making it clear that he’s aiming for something bigger. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. title: On the Record: Joe Hendry Speaks On Idea of Possible WWE Heel Turn
raw_title: Joe Hendry Addresses Idea of Possible WWE Heel Turn
summary_src: Joe Hendry has WWE fans singing his name every week, but what if he decided to give them a reason to boo instead? Hendry was just asked about turning heel, and his answer came with a pretty surprising confession about his character.
body: During a new interview discussing his WWE career , Hendry was asked whether he’d ever consider ditching his fan-favorite act and becoming a bad guy. He didn’t rule anything out. “Interesting question. Yes. I I mean never say never. You just never know. Anything can happen in the WWE.” But here’s where things get interesting. Hendry revealed that the character fans love today wasn’t even supposed to be popular. He actually created the whole thing with the intention of making people dislike him. “It’s funny. I originally my this is the character that I’ve designed and the the person that I like that I’m portraying was was designed to be hated and people just happen to like it, you know.” That’s right. The entrance music, the confidence, and the whole Joe Hendry act were originally meant to get under people’s skin. Instead, fans started cheering, singing along, and turning him into one of wrestling’s most recognizable personalities. Hendry admitted that the reaction wasn’t what he originally had in mind. “I guess that that’s always intriguing. Yeah. I mean like it’s it was absolutely designed to be hated by everyone and people just liked it.” And according to Hendry, that’s just how wrestling works sometimes. You can create a character with one reaction in mind, but the fans ultimately decide whether they’re going to cheer or boo. “You can’t you can’t force it. Like the the audience are going to like you say they’re a huge part in dictating our paths.” Hendry also made it clear that he knows exactly how important those fans have been to his career. He even credited their support for getting him opportunities at WrestleMania and the Royal Rumble. “Well, they’re they’re a huge part of the show. They’re as big a part of the show as as the performers. So, you know, to have the fan support, you know, I wouldn’t be here without the fan support. I got the Wrestlemania opportunity. I got the Royal Rumble opportunity because of the fan support. So, ultimately, I’m always grateful to the fans because it’s them that are putting me in these positions.” For now, Hendry isn’t saying a heel turn is coming, and WWE hasn’t announced anything suggesting a character change. But considering he originally built the character to be hated, it wouldn’t exactly be unfamiliar territory for him. The funny part is that Hendry spent years trying to get fans to hate his character, only for them to turn him into a star. Now the question is whether WWE will ever give him the chance to play the bad guy he originally wanted to be. title: Joe Hendry Says Job Is To Give Absolute Best With Creative

body: Joe Hendry speaks on creative that he doesn’t necessarily agree with and how it shapes how he performs for fans in segments or matches. Being a professional wrestler can be frustrating at times for talent that has their actions and on screen personality shaped by the creative team of their respective promotions, particularly when it draws backlash from fans for one reason or another. While speaking to the Michael Fairman Channel in a new interview, Joe Hendry was asked about segments or moments where he hasn’t agreed with the ideas WWE creative presents him with. “I think in professional wrestling, your job is to give it your absolute best with the collaboration that you have, and that’s what I always try to do. I always try to give the best I can with the tools that I have available, and that’s what pro wrestling really is because it’s a collaboration. You’ve got these, you know, you are your own brand, but ultimately you’re working together to try and entertain the audience, and that’s, you know, it’s a group of people working together to try and do that. So my goal is to try and execute for the company as best I can.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: WWE Stock Report: Punk-Owens Feud Loses Steam

body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Some places do power rankings. Here at Cageside, we do a stock report. In this weekly series, we identify three Superstars (or groups of Superstars) who are on their way up, and three that are moving in the opposite direction. After a busy week that included WWE booking a Last Man Standing match in Saudi Arabia, Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable having the best match on Raw again, and Tiffany Stratton almost cashing in the Money in the Bank contract on Liv Morgan, a lot of fortunes were changed. With that in mind, let’s see whose stock decreased the most this week: Kevin and CM are two of my favorite wrestlers in WWE, yet I find it difficult to care about their upcoming rematch in Brooklyn. A lot of that comes from each star’s apathy towards fighting each other again. KO said he was ready to move on from Punk after making sure he didn’t win the Money in the Bank contract on Oct. 10. Nothing has happened since then to change his mindset, as they’ve only been involved in talking segments backstage. Naturally, Owens said he doesn’t even know why Aldis booked this rematch. Punk doesn’t give a shit either, as he called the entire thing a “monumental waste” of his time. If the two wrestlers in the feud don’t care about fighting each other, then why should the fans? Speaking of not caring, there are even fewer reasons to be invested in the feud between MFT and Bakusai. WWE’s booking of the main roster tag titles usually leaves a lot to be desired, and that was once again the case this week when the scheduled match between these two teams was called off due to pre-match tomfoolery where Kyoki stole Haku’s stick. I guess it’s better than being relegated to digital exclusives again, but not by much. The “big head” feud between Hendry and JD McDonagh seems like the kind of really dumb storyline that’s right out of Vince McMahon’s playbook. It’s usually an anchor weighing a wrestler down to be part of this kind of angle, especially for a babyface on the losing end of it. Hendry was that guy on this week’s Raw when he lost to a flying headbutt from JD, after McDonagh blasted a giant Funko Pop with a guitar. I don’t know if Hendry is at rock bottom, but he’s pretty close to that point. WWE played hot potato with the women’s tag team titles when Cargill helped her Baddies win the gold on SmackDown to abruptly end Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley’s reign at 14 days. Even if their reign doesn’t last long either, Michin and B-Fab desperately needed a win like this to give them credibility for being more than just low card henchwomen. body: Jay White’s newly formed AEW faction has apparently undergone a name change just hours after being introduced as The Last Outfit. However, AEW subsequently released a digital exclusive in which White referred to the group by a different name. We are the last outfit capable of slicing out the cancer that is Jon Moxley and the Death Riders from the heart of AEW. We are The Cut. The Cut consists of White, Juice Robinson, Austin Gunn, Colten Gunn, Ace Austin, David Finlay and Clark Connors. At the end of the night, Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X, Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young, and Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita are the teams remaining with perfect 2-0 records. Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi defeated Master Wato & KUUKAI in the opening tournament match when Taguchi made KUUKAI tap to an ankle lock. Both teams now sit at 2 points with 1-1 records. United Empire (Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young) defeated Unbound Co. (Titan & Daiki Nagai) in the second tournament match. A story is building between Akira and Young and the tensions in the United Empire. On yesterday’s show , Young blind tagged himself in and stole a pin and today Akira accidentally hit Young with a boot to the face. They still picked up the win after Akira hit Fireball on Nagai and got the pin to improve to 2-0. Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X improved to 2-0 after defeating DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru, dropping the HOT team to 1-1. It was Ishimori, rather than the HOT team, that would take advantage of the referee being out of position, hitting Kanemaru with a low blow before cradling him for a three count. YOH & Hyo are now 1-1 after defeating SHO & Dick Togo, who drop to 0-2. After the match, Sho gave YOH and Hyo a low blow and appeared to produce a document stating that the two stuffed cats now belong to House of Torture. Time Splitters V.2 (KUSHIDA & Nick Wayne) defeated Mistico & Masatora Yasuda in the semi-main event to get their first win of the tournament. KUSHIDA got the pin on Yasuda after a moonsault, dropping Yasuda and Mistico to 0-2 to start the tournament. Ichiban Sweet Boys (Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita) defeated The Swirl (Blake Christian & Lee Johnson) in the main event, pinning Johnson after the Interceptor. The two teams had a brief stare down after. After the main event, Eagles cut a promo in English, noting that the screen in Korakuen Hall now has translations available. That was also mentioned by Chris Charlton earlier. Eagles promised they aren’t going to lose a single match in the tournament. Fujita said he’d like to have another match against The Swirl, then said something Charlton said he could get fined for before throwing down the microphone. Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi submitted Master Wato & KUUKAI to reach 1-1 while United Empire defeated Unbound Co. amid growing internal tensions and Ishimori & Robbie X beat DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru.

title: Injury Update: Former WWE Star Kaylia Capri Injured in Car Accident
raw_title: Former WWE Star Kaylia Capri Injured in Car Accident
summary_src: Kaylia Capri was supposed to be in the ring Saturday night, but a car accident ruined those plans. The former WWE star revealed she was injured in the crash and had no choice but to miss her scheduled wrestling appearance.
body: Capri, who went by Alexis Gray during her WWE run, was booked for Reality of Wrestling’s Sherri Martel Classic in Texas City, Texas, on October 24. Instead of competing, she ended up dealing with injuries from a car accident that happened the same day. On October 25, Capri took to Twitter to explain what happened and apologize to fans who were expecting to see her. She confirmed that her injuries were minor, but admitted she was heartbroken over missing the show. “To all my fans who came out to support me @TheOfficialROW irl & via YT Yesterday I literally am so sorry. I got into a car accident yesterday. I’m suffering minor injuries but I won’t sit and act like I’m not heart broken.” Capri didn’t explain what caused the crash or how serious the damage was. She also didn’t say whether she needed hospital treatment or how long she might be out of the ring. The former WWE talent has been working the independent wrestling scene since her September 2023 WWE release , and she’s been building her career outside the company . Saturday’s Sherri Martel Classic was another opportunity for her to get in front of fans, but the accident put a stop to that. For now, Capri hasn’t announced when she’ll wrestle again. She’s dealing with minor injuries and a missed booking, but at least she was able to walk away from the accident and let everyone know what happened. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Instead of competing, she ended up dealing with injuries from a car accident that happened the same day. Capri took to Twitter to explain what happened and apologize to the audience who were expecting to see her.

title: Tyrese Haliburton Shares Injury Comeback Video With WWE Stars
raw_title: NBA Star Tyrese Haliburton Posts Comeback Video Featuring Numerous WWE Talent
summary_src: NBA Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton is on his way towards his court comeback, and the WWE helped him make that announcement.
body: Don't just call it a comeback, but a relentless drive to win. NBA Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton is making his return to the court this Wednesday, and he had a little help from some WWE friends to make the announcement. On X [formerly known as Twitter] and across Haliburton's social media pages, the basketball star posted a video of his comeback journey after tearing his right Achilles tendon in Game 7 of the NBA Finals. Along with his journey, clips of WWE stars were shown, including Charlotte Flair, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, and Seth Rollins, who have all faced career-derailing injuries in their time, and their path towards redemption to get back into the ring. At the end of the video, you can hear Hall of Famer and WWE's Chief Content Officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque drop his famous three words, "Are you ready?" The road to return is paved by a relentless pursuit of winning. @WWE #ZeroDoubt pic.twitter.com/GBz1pNZM85 A big fan of wrestling, Haliburton has appeared on WWE programming several times over the years, including his most recent appearance at Saturday Night's Main Event on July 18, where he helped Rollins even the odds with his attack on Roman Reigns and the 2026 Finals Champion and New York Knicks member Jalen Brunson. Haliburton and the Pacers will face the New Orleans Pelicans at the Smoothie King Center this Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET.

The clip features footage of WWE performers Charlotte Flair, Cody Rhodes, CM Punk and Seth Rollins who have overcome their own serious injuries to return to competition. It concludes with WWE Chief Content Officer Paul "Triple H" Levesque saying his signature line "Are you ready?"

title: Anthony Bowens Recalls Signing With AEW
raw_title: Anthony Bowens Looks Back On Signing With AEW, Forming The Acclaimed
summary_src: Anthony Bowens looks back on his big break of signing with All Elite Wrestling and forming The Acclaimed in 2020.
body: Anthony Bowens spent his early pro wrestling days like many talents do, grinding on the independent circuit. In 2020, though, he received a big break that landed him on global television. During a recent interview with the " Michael Fairman Channel ," Bowens looked back on that big break, which centered on him inking a contract with All Elite Wrestling . "I think once AEW opened up, I was like this is the place I probably should be," Bowens said. "They were putting the focus on the younger guys. It was a different type of style than WWE. It was an alternative and wrestlers were like more free to perfect their craft and I thought that seems like the place I should go. Then. fortunately, I got a tryout with them in September of 2020, I want to say. One thing led to another and ended up signing in October of 2020, and then had a crazy journey ever since." Bowens made his AEW debut on the October 6, 2020 edition of "AEW Dark" (taped September 25). Weeks later, he and Max Caster officially joined forces to form The Acclaimed, earning their first team victory over Aaron Solow and Angel Fashion on the same brand. The 35-year-old initially agreed to sign with WWE shortly before . After flying down to Florida and meeting with AEW CEO Tony Khan to discuss his potential plans for The Acclaimed, however, he ultimately chose to come aboard AEW instead. Together, Bowens and Caster became a successful and popular act in AEW, with reigns as World Tag Team and Trios Champions to their names. Surprisingly, they weren't too familiar with one another beforehand, however. "I trained in Create A Pro in New Jersey. Caster trained in Create A Pro Long Island. I knew him from training. I would go out there and I would train a little bit in Long Island, so I knew him from there. I think we wrestled each other once in a multi-man match, but I didn't really know much about him," Bowens said. "Then I found out we were going to be paired together, I was like, 'Okay, well, we need to figure this out and quick,' because if the owner has an idea for us and a team name for us, we got to be able to deliver. Also, be cordial to each other and learn about each other because this guy is going to be tethered to me for a long time. So we got to become friends real quick." Tony Khan initially saw the Create A Pro graduates compete separately on "AEW Dark." In his case, Bowens teamed with Lee Johnson; Caster had singles and trios performances under his belt. Upon feeling pressure from WWE, Khan then made an enticing offer for them to join forces and be regularly featured on AEW programming. Six years later, Bowens and Caster are now both free agents once again. The former's post-AEW moves remain unknown. Caster, meanwhile, has taken a step back from in-ring competition in order to undergo therapy.
summary: Anthony Bowens discussed his early independent wrestling days before receiving a tryout with All Elite Wrestling in September 2020. He signed with AEW the following month after feeling the promotion offered a better fit for younger talent seeking creative freedom compared to WWE. Weeks after his debut on AEW Dark, Bowens teamed with Max Caster to create The Acclaimed.

title: Ex-WWE Star Makes Surprise TNA Debut, Costs the Hardys Match at Bound For Glory
raw_title: Ex-WWE Star Makes Surprise TNA Debut, Costs the Hardys Match at Bound For Glory
body: After their WWE release as part of the post-WrestleMania 42 talent cuts, former Wyatt Sicks members Joseph Sawyer (Joe Gacy) and Samuel Shaw (Dexter Lumis) showed up in TNA in September. Under the new team name syX, they revealed themselves as the mystery attackers who took out multiple wrestlers backstage for several months. Matt Hardy challenged them to a falls-count-anywhere match at TNA Bound for Glory. The former Wyatt Sicks members took on the Hardys in a chaotic falls-count-anywhere match that lasted nearly 13 minutes at TNA Bound for Glory. The wrestlers fought all over the Yuengling Center, and Jeff Hardy even performed a Swanton Bomb off the balcony onto Samel Show through a table. However, Joseph Sawyer broke up the pin by booting the referee in the face. The action spilled to the entrance ramp, where the Hardys set up tables and a ladder. They set Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw onto the tables. However, their old Wyatt Sicks partner Eric Redbeard made a surprise appearance and put Matt and Jeff Hardy through the tables. It was legal since there were no disqualifications. sYX then dragged the Hardys to the ring, where Erick Redbeard made Matt Hardy watch as the other two slammed him inside the ring. They then gave Jeff Hardy a suplex-powerbomb combo and stacked them on top of each other. Sawyer powerbombed Shaw on top of them both for the pinfall and walked out of TNA Bound for Glory with the victory. title: Cody Rhodes Thinks The Rock Has Matches Left
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Believes The Rock Will Wrestle In WWE Again
summary_src: While some believe that Dwyane "The Rock" Johnson's in-ring career has unofficially finished, Cody Rhodes thinks he still has some gas left in the tank.
body: The in-ring future of Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson has been a recurring topic of conversation in recent years, with matches against Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes both on the table at one point. As of 2026, though, neither singles match has yet to materialize. According to Rhodes, hope for his dream clash might not be lost as he believes there is still some gas left in the WWE legend's tank. "It's not that I'm evading that answer. It's that I don't really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do," Rhodes told "Insight With Chris Van Vliet" when asked about a potential singles bout against The Rock. "I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40, and another guy who he's given all, continues to give all as part of the board, he could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring. That'll be up to him. That'll certainly be up to him if there's more and what those matches might be. I don't think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn't want a match like that." The Rock, now 54, last competed on night one of WrestleMania 40, where a tag match pitted him and Reigns against Rhodes and Seth Rollins. " The Final Boss" pinned Rhodes to secure victory for his team and the added stipulation of Bloodline Rules for the following night's Undisputed WWE Championship main event. At the time, The Rock suggested that more in-ring outings might be in store for him . Two-and-a-half years later, none have occurred; he has, however, appeared in additional storylines involving The Bloodline and Rhodes, the latter of which resulted in John Cena's famous heel turn at Elimination Chamber 2025.
summary: Cody Rhodes told Chris Van Vliet that he personally believes Dwayne Johnson has a couple of matches remaining in his WWE career. Rhodes noted that The Rock could also view his WrestleMania 40 segment as a fitting end to his in-ring performing days since he serves on the board. He added that no wrestler would turn down the chance to face The Rock.

Rhodes noted that he does not know exactly how to answer questions about facing The Rock. He added that the decision on any future matches would be entirely up to The Rock himself. The Rock, aged 54, last wrestled on night one of WrestleMania 40. In that tag team match, he teamed with Roman Reigns to defeat Cody Rhodes and Seth Rollins under Bloodline Rules. The Rock pinned Rhodes during the WrestleMania 40 tag match. That result added the Bloodline Rules stipulation to the Undisputed WWE Championship main event on night two.

At the time of WrestleMania 40, The Rock indicated that additional in-ring appearances could happen. No further matches have taken place in the two-and-a-half years since. The Rock has continued to appear in storylines involving The Bloodline. Those segments included one with Rhodes that led to John Cena's heel turn at Elimination Chamber 2025.

title: Nick Wayne & KUSHIDA Score First Super Junior Tag League Win
raw_title: Nick Wayne & KUSHIDA earn first win in NJPW Super Junior Tag League
summary_src: Nick Wayne & KUSHIDA picked up their first victory of the 2026 NJPW Super Junior Tag League on Sunday at Korakuen Hall.
body: Nick Wayne & KUSHIDA picked up their first victory of the 2026 NJPW Super Junior Tag League on Sunday at Korakuen Hall. The pair defeated Místico & Masatora Yasuda in A Block action after losing their opening match to DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru on Saturday. Wayne began the match against Místico, with the two exchanging signs of respect before reaching a stalemate. KUSHIDA and Wayne later focused their offense on Yasuda, who is replacing the injured El Desperado in the tournament. Místico helped turn the match back in his team’s favor, while Yasuda continued to withstand sustained offense from the Timesplitters V.2 pairing. KUSHIDA eventually isolated Yasuda after Místico was taken out of the equation and scored the pin following a moonsault. The result moves Wayne & KUSHIDA to two points after the first two rounds. They next face Master Wato & KUUKAI on Monday at Korakuen Hall. The match gives Wayne another opportunity against Wato, who defeated him during this year’s Best of the Super Juniors tournament. NJPW’s Japanese preview highlighted that previous result heading into Monday’s meeting. AEW’s other representatives, Blake Christian & Lee Johnson, were unable to maintain their unbeaten start. The Swirl lost Sunday’s B Block main event to 2025 tournament winners Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita. Christian & Johnson controlled a significant portion of the match before Eagles & Fujita rallied, with the Ichiban Sweet Boys ultimately securing the victory with the Interceptor. Eagles & Fujita therefore moved to four points and share the B Block lead with United Empire’s Francesco Akira & Jakob Austin Young. Akira & Young defeated Titán & Daiki Nagai earlier on the card, with Akira pinning Nagai following the Fireball. Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X are the only unbeaten team remaining in the A Block after defeating DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru. Ishimori used House of Torture’s tactics against them, delivering a low blow to Kanemaru while the referee was distracted before using a Gedo Clutch for the pin. Elsewhere, Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi upset opening-night winners Master Wato & KUUKAI, while YOH & Hyo earned their first victory by defeating SHO & Dick Togo. The tournament continues on Monday with a second consecutive night at Korakuen Hall.
summary: Nick Wayne and KUSHIDA defeated Místico and Masatora Yasuda in A Block action at NJPW Super Junior Tag League on Sunday at Korakuen Hall. The victory came after the pair lost their opening match to DOUKI and Yoshinobu Kanemaru the previous day. KUSHIDA pinned Yasuda with a moonsault to give the team two points, with their next bout set against Master Wato and KUUKAI on Monday.

title: Match Made: Sean Grande weighs in — WWE walkout vs. the NBA's lockout
raw_title: WWE walkout vs. the NBA's lockout: Sean Grande weighs in - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email Since last Monday’s unprecedented walkout on Raw SuperShow, WWE and NBA fans have been all over Twitter and Facebook comparing WWE’s walkout to the NBA’s lockout. Being an office comprised of WWE and NBA fans ourselves, the WWE.com staff had been having the same discussions all week. So, to bridge the gap between our two worlds, we “tagged-in” Boston Celtics play-by-play announcer and lifelong WWE fan, Sean Grande (@ SeanGrandePBP ) to get his insight into the similarities between the two situations. We felt Sean was the perfect person to interview because like Jerry “The King” Lawler, Sean has had an unpleasant experience with physicality at his announce table. WWE.com: What similarities at all does WWE's current situation have to the NBA's lockout? SEAN GRANDE: On the surface, none. The NBA lockout is about the revenue generated by the league, and how the team owners and players should divide it. WWE's walkout seems to be more about work environment, but on closer inspection, the common theme is the very striking image of potential high-stakes combatants standing together. Whether that's Kevin Garnett standing with Dwyane Wade, or Mark Henry standing with Wade Barrett. The biggest similarity of all is that grievances which should be settled behind closed doors are interfering with the fans' enjoyment of the product they love. WWE.com: A full-scale WWE walkout will not only affect WWE talent and management, but also WWE office employees, arena employees, local businesses near arenas and TV networks. Will the NBA lockout have similar affects? GRANDE: It already has. When there's an NBA game or a WWE event at your local arena, there are hundreds of people involved in creating that spectacle, most of whom you never see. When the arena goes dark because of a labor stoppage, all those jobs disappear. Restaurants, local businesses ... they all suffer. In the NBA, we've already lost the pre-season, which for some individuals and businesses, represents 5-10% of their annual income. If [WWE Chief Operating Officer] Triple H has learned anything from his legendary predecessor ... it's that the show must go on, for everyone's sake. WWE.com: After watching Jerry Lawler put through a table at ringside and seeing Mark Henry only get fined instead of fired, would you have walked off Raw like "The King," Michael Cole, Booker T and Justin Roberts did last Monday? GRANDE: I'll only say this: Three years ago, [forward] James Posey went after a ball out-of-bounds, and he put both Cedric Maxwell and me over the courtside table and through two chairs. We both dusted ourselves off, and finished the game. I think that is what Triple H was talking about Monday night. Fans are paying to see Kobe Bryant and Paul Pierce, John Cena and CM Punk, settle their disputes in the ring and on the floor, with tables if need be, not at a table. Fans pay us to perform, not whine.

title: AJ Francis Recalls Backstage Heat Over Celebrity Fan Choice
raw_title: AJ Francis says he got backstage heat in WWE after celebrity fan chose him over Brock Lesnar
summary_src: AJ Francis says he received backstage heat during his WWE run after a celebrity guest wanted to meet him instead of Brock Lesnar or Randy Orton.
body: AJ Francis says he received backstage heat during his WWE run after a celebrity guest wanted to meet him instead of Brock Lesnar or Randy Orton. Speaking to The Wrestling Classic , Francis recalled how Expressions, now his partner in TNA, requested to meet him backstage before WWE Money in the Bank 2023 in London. Francis, then known as Top Dolla, said people questioned why Expressions wanted to meet him rather than one of WWE’s bigger stars. “When I was in WWE, sometimes you become a victim of your own success. Expressions, who’s with me now in TNA, I remember one time I got a little bit of heat in WWE because when Expressions was backstage as a celebrity fan before Money in the Bank in London, they asked him who did he want to see,” Francis said. “He could have saw Brock Lesnar, he could have saw Randy Orton, and he said Top Dolla. And they’re like, ‘Why do you want to see Top Dolla? What do you want to see him for?'” Francis contrasted the experience with his current position in TNA, where he believes he has more opportunities to demonstrate his abilities. “So it’s like I was a victim of success back then that I had fans. And then now that narrative’s completely changed. Now, when I’m in TNA, I get an opportunity to show exactly how good I am. And now people are starting to realize how good I am,” he finished. Francis and Expressions recently teamed against The Hardys at the October 13 TNA Impact tapings. Francis previously said he believes his wrestling career is peaking. body: After making his official in-ring debut in the indies in June, Avery Styles signed with TNA Wrestling in August. Though he hasn't had his first match in the promotion yet, the 19-year-old is being mentored by his father's long-time friend and rival, Frankie Kazarian. Kazarian is guiding Avery Styles through the early stages of his career and recently got him a major opportunity for his in-ring debut. On this week's episode of TNA iMPACT, Kazarian informed Styles that he'd join him in the Call Your Shot Gauntlet match at Bound For Glory. The pay-per-view will take place at the Yuengling Center in Tampa, Florida, on Sunday, October 11. The winner of the Call Your Shot Gauntlet match receives a trophy and the right to challenge for any championship of their choice at a time of their choosing. In addition to AJ Styles' son and Frankie Kazarian, Bear Bronson of The System has been confirmed for the contest. title: Eric Bischoff Calls For Soap Opera Style In Wrestling
raw_title: WWE HOFer Eric Bischoff Explains Necessity Of 'Episodic' Storytelling In Wrestling
summary_src: According to Eric Bischoff, the key to successful pro wrestling storytelling is to draw from soap operas.
body: WWE Eric Bischoff has consistently criticized the storytelling in modern pro wrestling, previously warning AEW to not allow storytelling to become secondary to wrestling , while on the other hand praising Triple H and Bruce Prichard for winning back WWE fans after Vince McMahon lost the audience with his storytelling. However, Bischoff believes wrestling needs to go further, becoming more akin to a soap opera. "It is a male, testosterone — and sometimes female — testosterone-driven, action-driven, combat — it's fake combat, but perceived combat — but I think it has to have that soap opera feel in order to be episodic," he opined during an episode of his " 83 Weeks " podcast. "If it's going to be successful, it should be episodic," he added. "We should create the same need, desire, whatever you want to call it, for the audience. When that show's over? They should already be looking forward to next week to find out what happened or where a story goes." Bischoff further opines that this is what's missing in pro wrestling more often than not, as wrestling can't just be a fight without an angle behind it. He also proclaimed that episodic storytelling is what made WCW thrive under his regime. "It was very unique at the time." Bischoff acknowledged that some fans do enjoy matches without much story, but he believes this is the minority of the audience.
summary: WWE Hall of Famer Eric Bischoff argued that pro wrestling must embrace a soap opera feel to succeed as episodic television. He said stories need to create anticipation so fans are eager for the next episode to see what happens next. Bischoff previously praised Triple H and Bruce Prichard for regaining WWE audience interest after Vince McMahon lost them with his approach to storytelling.

llm_long: Eric Bischoff has long been critical of storytelling in modern professional wrestling and previously cautioned AEW against letting narratives take a backseat to in-ring action.
He has praised Triple H and Bruce Prichard for regaining WWE fans after Vince McMahon lost much of the audience through his approach to storytelling.
Bischoff now argues that wrestling must evolve further to resemble a soap opera in order to succeed as episodic entertainment.

"It is a male, testosterone — and sometimes female — testosterone-driven, action-driven, combat — it's fake combat, but perceived combat — but I think it has to have that soap opera feel in order to be episodic," he said on his "83 Weeks" podcast.

Bischoff added that if wrestling is going to thrive it should create a strong desire in viewers so that when an episode ends audiences are already eager to tune in the following week to learn what happens next in the stories.
He stated that the absence of such elements is what is missing most often in pro wrestling because matches cannot simply be fights without underlying angles.
Bischoff pointed to the episodic storytelling during his time in charge of WCW as the factor that helped the promotion stand out and succeed at the time.
While acknowledging that a portion of fans prefer matches with minimal story, Bischoff maintained this group represents only a minority of the overall audience.

title: Former WWF Wrestler “Wildman” Jack Armstrong Passes Away at 79
raw_title: Former WWF Wrestler “Wildman” Jack Armstrong Passes Away at 79
summary_src: “Wildman” Jack Armstrong has passed away at the age of 79. The longtime professional wrestler’s death was announced by his close friend Laura Creavalle, who had recently traveled to Los Angeles to be by his side as his health declined.
body: Creavalle shared the sad news on Facebook , calling Armstrong her best friend and remembering how much he helped her when she was a struggling bodybuilder. She revealed that Armstrong even bought her first posing suit and gave her a place to live when she was broke and homeless. “As to my post a few days ago. I m sorry to announce that I loosed my best friend Wild Man Jack Armstrong today. He was a great wrestler and and even better friend the stories are 2 many to share but he bought my first posing suit in LA and I lived with him for many years when I was a beginner struggling bodybuilder. Broke and homeless.” Just days before announcing his death, Creavalle revealed that she had returned to Los Angeles for the first time in 19 years specifically to spend time with Armstrong. She said his health was failing and that she wanted to be there to help him. Creavalle also revealed that Armstrong had undergone the amputation of one of his legs and was on dialysis. Despite everything he was dealing with, she said he hadn’t lost his sense of humor and that she was hoping he would make it to his 80th birthday. “I m in LA after 19 yrs to b with my best friend Jack Armstrong , used to b a professional wrestle, his best friend was Rocky , the Rock ‘s father , they used to share rooms together when they were on the road. He has known the Rock since he was a baby. His health is failing so I have decide to come out hear to help . They had to remove one of his legs n he is on dialysis, but his sense of humour still stays. He is 79. I m hoping he makes it to 80. I m glad just to be here by his side” Armstrong had a wrestling career that stretched more than three decades, beginning in 1963. He worked under several different names over the years, including Lenny Solomon, Super Scorpion, Ali Ben Khan, Black Jack, Red Rhodes and Sailor Jack. He also spent time with the WWWF and later returned during the WWF era, stepping into the ring with names including Ricky Steamboat, Bret Hart, Jesse Ventura, Mil Máscaras and Tony Atlas. Armstrong also worked extensively throughout the territories and made appearances in Japan. Later in his career, Armstrong became part of Herb Abrams’ Universal Wrestling Federation. He even teamed with Cactus Jack, better known today as Mick Foley, to defeat David Sammartino and Jay Strongbow Jr. during a UWF television taping in 1990. Armstrong’s final documented match came at UWF Blackjack Brawl in September 1994, where he defeated Mando Guerrero to become the inaugural UWF Junior Heavyweight Champion. The promotion never held another event, leaving Armstrong as the only wrestler to ever hold the championship. Creavalle’s final memories also showed that Armstrong’s wrestling connections went well beyond the matches on his record. According to her, he was close friends and road roommates with Rocky Johnson and had known The Rock since he was a baby, leaving behind ties to several generations of the wrestling business.
