Although audiences primarily see dramatic matches, impressive athletic movements, and carefully developed storylines, the work behind these performances requires considerable physical preparation. Wrestlers frequently manage demanding travel schedules, regular training sessions, and repeated physical impacts while maintaining the conditioning needed to perform consistently. In previous decades, wrestling culture often emphasized toughness and the ability to continue performing despite discomfort. Today, greater attention is being given to recovery, injury prevention, and long-term physical well-being. Modern performers increasingly recognize that maintaining a successful career involves understanding when to train, when to rest, and how to manage the demands of professional competition. From improved training facilities to more individualized recovery programs, the industry is adopting practices commonly associated with other professional sports. These changes are helping wrestlers approach physical preparation more systematically while highlighting the importance of protecting their bodies throughout demanding careers. Recovery facilities have become an increasingly important consideration for professional athletes, including wrestlers who regularly experience demanding physical workloads. Training centers and private fitness facilities may incorporate relaxation areas, massage services, hydrotherapy equipment, and other amenities intended to support structured recovery routines. Saunas have also become a familiar feature in many wellness environments. Their popularity reflects an interest in combining physical relaxation with dedicated time away from strenuous activity. For wrestlers who spend considerable time traveling between events, access to a comfortable wellness facility can provide a welcome opportunity to unwind. When evaluating sauna installations, understanding the difference between a full spectrum sauna or far infrared sauna can help facility owners and individual users explore different infrared heating technologies. Comparing these approaches provides useful information when selecting equipment for a dedicated relaxation space. The overall design of a recovery area also matters. title: Kalisto Refused WWE’s Offer to Buy His Wrestling Character Before Vince McMahon Changed His Mask
raw_title: Kalisto Refused WWE’s Offer to Buy His Wrestling Character Before Vince McMahon Changed His Mask
summary_src: Kalisto wasn’t about to hand over everything he built just to get into WWE. The former United States Champion revealed that WWE wanted to buy his Samuray Del Sol name and mask design when he first joined the company, but he turned them down.
body: During an interview with David Otunga, Kalisto opened up about the importance of owning his wrestling identity. The discussion started when Otunga brought up Sin Cara and how WWE owned the rights to his original mask design, forcing him to create a different version after leaving the company. Kalisto explained that he was determined to avoid the same situation. Even though WWE was interested in purchasing his character, he wasn’t willing to give up something he had spent years creating. “When I first came in, they wanted to buy the Samurai soul name and design. I said no. I mean, I was flattered. I’m like, man, that’s pretty cool, but uh God forbid if anything, I want to go back to the same, you know, I want to still use this all this stuff.” His decision meant he could continue using his original wrestling identity outside WWE. However, that didn’t mean the company was leaving his appearance completely alone. Kalisto revealed that Vince McMahon specifically wanted fans to see his eyes and mouth, which was a major departure from the fully covered masks he had worn throughout his career. “So, uh I said no. And you know, I just took the eyes and the mouth out because uh besides that, Vince wanted to see my eyes and my mouth. And I’ve always wrestled everything covered.” Kalisto admitted that he eventually became so comfortable with the WWE-style version of his mask that going back to his original design became difficult. He explained that he now struggles to breathe while wrestling with his entire face covered. “And this is this actually now I’m used to it but now I can’t wrestle because I can’t like this I’ll start breathing I won’t be able to breathe you know I have to use this mask now.” The former WWE star also explained that his mask represents far more than his appearance. He incorporated different designs representing his wrestling background, his time as the original Octagon Jr., and his journey toward becoming one-half of the Lucha Dragons. “I mean, it’s it’s something that I’ve worked my whole life with and I guess it’s just progressed and progressed and I I made everything into a meaning. The type of highf flyier that I am my wings the three styles the first octagon junior too but also the journey that led me to be a lucha dragon. uh my mask representing hope and it’s just everything started being a meaning because I lived through it.” Kalisto made it clear that protecting his character was one decision he wasn’t willing to compromise on. WWE may have gotten him to change his mask, but the company never got ownership of the original identity he created before signing his contract. H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.
summary: The latest: kalisto opened up about the importance of owning his wrestling identity. The discussion kicked off when Otunga brought up Sin Cara and how WWE owned the rights to his original mask design.

title: Jerry Lynn Reveals Cornette Wanted Him For The Brood
raw_title: Jerry Lynn Says Jim Cornette Pitched Him On Leading WWE Attitude Era Faction
summary_src: According to Jerry Lynn, Jim Cornette once tried to bring him into WWE to lead a faction that featured some very prominent wrestlers.
body: After becoming one of the standouts of ECW in the 1990s, Jerry Lynn had a brief stint in WWE in 2001, wrestling a few dozen matches for the company before returning to the independent scene. Prior to that run, however, Lynn was nearly recruited to WWE by Jim Cornette during his time there, with Lynn revealing on "What Happened When" that he was almost the leader of a memorable stable. "Jim was trying to bring me in — it's funny — he was trying to bring me into WWF to be in The Brood before they brought in Gangrel, but I was too small," Lynn said. "Which I understand. It was still a majority big man's business, you know?" Beyond that interaction, Lynn said that his history with Cornette was limited, though he did learn a lot from the former manager and booker. "What a mind for the business," Lynn stated of Cornette. As indicated by Lynn, it was Gangrel who wound up leading The Brood alongside Edge and Christian, with the group forming in late 1998 before joining the Ministry of Darkness in early 1999 and breaking up later that year. Briefly, a version of the faction referred to as The New Brood featured Gangrel and the Hardy Boyz, though that iteration had an even shorter lifespan. Meanwhile, Lynn went on to wrestle in the early years on TNA (while it was still under the NWA banner) as well as appearing in Ring of Honor and many other independent promotions, until his in-ring retirement in 2013. These days, Lynn works in AEW as a coach and producer.
summary: Jerry Lynn disclosed that Jim Cornette tried to recruit him to WWF in the late 1990s to lead the stable that became The Brood. Cornette ultimately passed on Lynn because of his size in an era dominated by bigger wrestlers. Gangrel ended up filling the role alongside Edge and Christian, with the group forming in late 1998.

title: On the Record: AJ Francis reflects on being a "victim of success" in WWE
raw_title: AJ Francis reflects on being a "victim of success" in WWE
body: AJ Francis says he received backstage heat during his WWE run after a celebrity guest wanted to meet him instead of Brock Lesnar or Randy Orton. Speaking to The Wrestling Classic , Francis recalled how Expressions, now his partner in TNA, requested to meet him backstage before WWE Money in the Bank 2023 in London. Francis, then known as Top Dolla, said people questioned why Expressions wanted to meet him rather than one of WWE’s bigger stars. “When I was in WWE, sometimes you become a victim of your own success. Expressions, who’s with me now in TNA, I remember one time I got a little bit of heat in WWE because when Expressions was backstage as a celebrity fan before Money in the Bank in London, they asked him who did he want to see,” Francis said. “He could have saw Brock Lesnar, he could have saw Randy Orton, and he said Top Dolla. And they’re like, ‘Why do you want to see Top Dolla? What do you want to see him for?'” Francis contrasted the experience with his current position in TNA, where he believes he has more opportunities to demonstrate his abilities. “So it’s like I was a victim of success back then that I had fans. And then now that narrative’s completely changed. Now, when I’m in TNA, I get an opportunity to show exactly how good I am. And now people are starting to realize how good I am,” he finished. Francis and Expressions recently teamed against The Hardys at the October 13 TNA Impact tapings. Francis previously said he believes his wrestling career is peaking. For the uninitiated, a microdrama is a short-form scripted drama designed to tell a story in very small chunks, usually through bite-sized episodes that last anywhere from 1 to 3 minutes. The idea is basically to appeal to the younger Tik Tok/social media type audience. The format has gained a lot of steam internationally in recent years, particularly in China. For Agent of Shadows , there are 72 episodes. The plot - "The world's greatest secret agent must protect and care for his six-year-old daughter while posing as her nanny. Now, without revealing his true identity, he must win his daughter's (and her mother's) trust, while secretly thwarting corrupt suitors, mafioso strongmen, and even a megalomaniacal billionaire who's using his family to get to him." Michael Hayes, Drew McIntyre, Jacob Fatu, Nikkita Lyons, Joe Hendry, Ethan Page and Booker T are among those appearing over the course of the story. We are told that those on both the Reelshort and WWE sides worked hard to slip easter eggs in for the WWE audience, including Booker T's crown from his King Booker run and Drew using one of his actual swords from his ring entrance. title: Booker T Defied WWE Locker Room Nap Warning
raw_title: Booker T explains why he refused to stop napping backstage in WWE
summary_src: Booker T says he was warned that taking naps backstage in WWE could get him heat with other wrestlers, but he refused to change his routine. Speaking on his Hall of Fame podcast, Booker recalled how another wrestler warned him against sleeping in the locker room.
body: Booker T says he was warned that taking naps backstage in WWE could get him heat with other wrestlers, but he refused to change his routine. Speaking on his Hall of Fame podcast , Booker recalled how another wrestler warned him against sleeping in the locker room. Rather than follow the unwritten rule, Booker decided to test it by telling Jim Ross, who had signed his WWE contract, that he was going to take a nap in his car. “ I remember the first time when I got to WWE, and I was in the locker room, and I was catching a nap. This guy came in, and he was so scared. He goes, ‘Hey, Book, I wouldn’t do that around here if I was you.’ I go, ‘What?’ He goes, ‘Taking a nap. That’s not cool. You can get a lot of heat ,'” he shared. However, Booker T shared that no one ever told him why he couldn’t nap before his matches, and he decided not to follow that rule. “ I go, ‘Taking a nap?’ He was really frightened, to the point where I go, ‘Let me test this theory, because I’m going to take a nap or they’re going to have to fire me.’ The person that signed my contract was JR, Jim Ross. I remember walking out, and I passed Jim Ross. I said, ‘Hey, Jim, if anybody’s looking for me, I’ll be in my car taking a nap.’ He goes, ‘All right.’ “ Me taking a nap is me preparing for tonight. I’m getting ready. Somebody’s got to tell me why I can’t prepare and get ready for tonight… No one ever explained it to me, and no one ever said anything to me about taking naps my whole career ,” he stated. Booker also discussed WWE’s backstage culture at the time, saying some wrestlers were afraid to stand up for themselves because they feared losing their jobs. “ A lot of the guys, it’s like anything. A bully keeps messing with you if you don’t fight back. That’s why when I hear a lot of these stories from these guys that worked in the business, and they talk about what happened back then, and they weren’t willing to say anything because they didn’t want to get fired, that hurts me. It really hurts me. “ I guess I’ve been willing to get fired a lot of times as far as the business goes. The only thing I always said was, ‘The only thing you could do is fire me ,'” he concluded. title: WrestleMania III Intercontinental Belt Sells for Record $716,750
raw_title: WWE WrestleMania III Intercontinental title belt sells for record amount
summary_src: The WWE Intercontinental Championship belt Ricky Steamboat won from Randy Savage in their legendary match at WrestleMania III has sold for a record amount. The belt, owned by Conrad Thompson, sold for $716,750 at a recent auction.
body: The WWE Intercontinental Championship belt Ricky Steamboat won from Randy Savage in their legendary match at WrestleMania III has sold for a record amount. The belt, owned by Conrad Thompson, sold for $716,750 at a recent auction. The sale took place at Heritage Auctions’ Fall Sports Catalog Auction on Saturday, October 24. The price includes Heritage’s 22% buyer’s premium on top of the final bid of $587,500. In addition to Savage vs. Steamboat at WrestleMania III, the belt was also used from 1985 to 1988 in matches involving champions Tito Santana and The Honky Tonk Man. It is reportedly the highest price for a championship belt sold at auction, surpassing Hulk Hogan’s WrestleMania II WWE Championship belt, which sold for $414,800 this summer. The highest price paid for any wrestling memorabilia on record is for the boots used by Hulk Hogan at the first WrestleMania, which sold for $1,037,000 in February. Thompson acquired the belt from WWE in 2020, trading the original Intercontinental Championship belt worn by Pat Patterson. Owned by Conrad Thompson, who obtained it from WWE in 2020 in exchange for the Pat Patterson-worn original title, the belt was used from 1985 through 1988 featuring champions such as Tito Santana and The Honky Tonk Man. Per the Wrestling Observer, the price tops Hulk Hogan’s WrestleMania II WWE Championship belt that fetched $414,800 earlier this year.

STEAMBOAT By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-22 00:30:00 The auction for the WWF Wrestlemania III Intercontinental Championship belt fought over by Randy Savage and Ricky Steamboat - and held as well as Tito Santana and The Honky Tonk Man is heading towards completion with 48 hours left. The bidding as of this writing is $125,000. For more, visit www.WrestlemaniaBelt.com . The following press release was previously issued about the auction: LEGENDARY WRESTLEMANIA III INTERCONTINENTAL CHAMPIONSHIP BELT HEADS TO HERITAGE AUCTIONS As the high-end wrestling memorabilia market shatters records, a premier multi-champion artifact from the Golden Era hits the auction block Between 1985 and 1989, the Intercontinental Championship belonged to the definitive personalities of WWE's golden era.”— Conrad ThompsonNEW YORK, NY, UNITED STATES, October 9, 2026 /EINPresswire.com/ -- Heritage Auctions has officially opened the auction for one of the most historically significant physical artifacts in professional wrestling history: the definitive 1985–1989 WWF Intercontinental Championship belt. Owned by wrestling historian and podcaster Conrad Thompson, this dual-plated Reggie Parks masterpiece is now featured as a premier lot in Heritage’s Fall Sports Catalog Auction, and bidding has already exceeded $100,000.00. Spanning the absolute peak of WWE’s 1980s National expansion, this legendary title belt is distinguished by its unprecedented lineage. Unlike most championship belts that were quickly retired or cycled out of rotation, this exact physical artifact was carried through sold-out arenas by four separate WWE Hall of Famers: Tito Santana, Randy "Macho Man" Savage, Ricky "The Dragon" Steamboat, and The Honky Tonk Man. Most notably, the belt serves as the central centerpiece of WrestleMania III on March 29, 1987. It was captured by Ricky Steamboat during his legendary, show-stealing masterpiece against "Macho Man" Randy Savage—a bout widely celebrated by historians, peers, and fans as one of the greatest and most influential matches of all time. "Between 1985 and 1989, the Intercontinental Championship belonged to the definitive personalities of WWE's golden era," said Thompson. "No match captures that reputation better than Savage and Steamboat at WrestleMania III. We are approaching the 40th anniversary of that match, and still, to this day, it is referenced by wrestlers and fans alike as one of the best WrestleMania matches of all time.” This marquee offering arrives amidst a historic explosion in the high-end wrestling memorabilia market. Heritage Auctions previously revolutionized the hobby by realizing $1,037,000 for Hulk Hogan’s photo-matched WrestleMania I boots, followed by the $414,800 sale of Hogan’s WrestleMania II WWF World Heavyweight Championship belt. So I’m sorry to all the male artists, but you’re out for this. I’m on a bit of a K-pop binge at the moment. I really am. I’m really enjoying it. title: Tommaso Ciampa Vows To Take AEW National Title From Andrade
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa cuts promo on Andrade El Idolo following AEW Collision
summary_src: Tommaso Ciampa cut a promo directed at AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo following AEW Collision. Andrade retained the title against Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream, picking up the win after delivering a Willow’s Bell DDT onto the championship belt, followed by The DM.
body: Tommaso Ciampa cut a promo directed at AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo following AEW Collision. Andrade retained the title against Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream , picking up the win after delivering a Willow’s Bell DDT onto the championship belt, followed by The DM. On Saturday’s AEW Collision , Ciampa attacked Andrade following a tag team win by Andrade and Mike Bailey. After the show, AEW posted a backstage video of Ciampa where he said: “I’ll be the first to admit, I made a mistake. WrestleDream, it’s on me. I made a mistake. I took him too lightly. I thought this is a two-trick pony. I thought he’s a selfie in a pair of pants. I took him too lightly. I took him as a joke. That’s on me. It won’t happen again. Andrade, listen to me. It will not happen again. Now, next time we see each other, next time you put that national title on the line, I’m coming for blood. I’m coming for it all. I’m taking the national title. And I don’t need to make any promises. The entire world, watch.” Andrade first won the title at AEW Redemption in Montreal, Quebec, Canada on July 26, defeating Mark Davis of the Don Callis Family for it. His first title defense was against Jack Perry and Nick Wayne in a three-way on Dynamite three days later. Since then, he’s had successful title defenses against Gabe Kidd, The Beast Mortos, and Daniel Garcia. He also defended the title against PAC at AEW All Out 2026 in what would be PAC’s final wrestling match before passing away the next day. Andrade also defended the title against Michael Oku at Grand Slam France and against QT Marshall at a Big Time Wrestling show in San Jose on October 18. In a backstage promo posted by AEW, Ciampa admitted he underestimated Andrade at WrestleDream where Andrade retained the AEW National Championship against him with a Willow’s Bell DDT onto the belt followed by The DM. Ciampa promised that the next time Andrade defends the national title he will come for blood and take the championship.

llm_long: Tommaso Ciampa issued a challenge to AEW National Champion Andrade El Idolo in a backstage promo after AEW Collision. Ciampa admitted he underestimated Andrade during their previous encounter and vowed the mistake would not be repeated.

Andrade retained the AEW National Championship against Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream. He secured the victory by driving Ciampa's head into the title belt with a Willow’s Bell DDT before finishing with The DM.

Following a tag team victory for Andrade and Mike Bailey on Saturday’s AEW Collision, Ciampa launched an attack on Andrade. The incident led to the backstage video where Ciampa declared his intent to take the title.

In the promo, Ciampa stated he would come for blood in their next meeting when the national title is on the line. He emphasized that the entire world should watch as he aims to capture the championship.

Andrade first captured the AEW National Championship by defeating Mark Davis at AEW Redemption in Montreal on July 26. He has since defended the title successfully against multiple opponents including Jack Perry, Nick Wayne, Gabe Kidd, The Beast Mortos, and Daniel Garcia.
Additional defenses came against PAC at AEW All Out 2026, Michael Oku at Grand Slam France, and QT Marshall at a Big Time Wrestling event in San Jose on October 18.

title: Drew McIntyre Eyes Russell Crowe As On-Screen Ally
raw_title: WWE's Drew McIntyre Teases On-Screen Partnership With Academy Award Winning Actor
summary_src: Former World Heavyweight and Undisputed Champion Drew McIntyre says this renowned actor wants to join forces with him in the WWE.
body: WWE Once he comes back, WWE Superstar Drew McIntyre is gunning to reposition himself as the next world champion. And he won't stop at nothing to get there, even if he has to bring one of his co-stars from the film to the ring. On the "Joe Vulpis Podcast," the former one-time World Heavyweight Champion said that Academy Award winning actor and co-star in "The Last Druid" and "Highlander," Russell Crowe, has his sights set on following McIntyre to the ring. Though, it's a conversation "The Scottish Warrior" will have to have with WWE management first. "Russell was legitimately talking about...he wanted to do something a couple of times," McIntyre said. "Oh, he got all excited about us doing something together in the same team, and talked about WrestleMania, or whatever. He talked about us having a manager, like an assistant, kind of like you. It was more of a heel thing he was coming up with. He had some great ideas. He's willing to do it." It's been nearly 200 days since WWE fans last saw McIntyre compete in the ring. His last match, featured at WrestleMania 42, was a loss to Jacob Fatu, in an Unsanctioned Match. Their rivalry came to a head after Fatu cost McIntyre his third reign with the Undisputed Championship, allowing Cody Rhodes to claim his third reign with the title on the March 6 edition of "WWE SmackDown." Since that unfortunate defeat, McIntyre has transitioned his time by accepting several different movie roles not only for the two films mentioned above, but also for "Hexed" and WWE and ReelShort's recently released micro-drama, "The Agent of Shadows," as its main character, Roscoe.
summary: Drew McIntyre revealed that his "The Last Druid" and "Highlander" co-star Russell Crowe has expressed interest in appearing alongside him in WWE as a manager or assistant in a heel role. McIntyre said Crowe got excited about the idea multiple times, including potential involvement at WrestleMania, and came up with several concepts. The Scottish Warrior noted he will need to discuss the possibility with WWE management upon his return, which has been nearly 200 days since his last match at WrestleMania 42.

llm_long: Drew McIntyre plans to return to WWE competition with the goal of becoming the next world champion. The former World Heavyweight Champion indicated he is open to enlisting an unlikely on-screen ally from his film work to help achieve that aim.

McIntyre revealed on the Joe Vulpis Podcast that his co-star Russell Crowe from the upcoming movies The Last Druid and Highlander has expressed interest in appearing alongside him in WWE. Crowe specifically talked about teaming up and even suggested a heel-style manager or assistant role for himself.

"Russell was legitimately talking about...he wanted to do something a couple of times," McIntyre said. He added that Crowe got excited about working together at WrestleMania or similar events and came up with several strong ideas for the partnership.

The Scottish Warrior noted that any involvement from Crowe would first require discussions with WWE management before moving forward. Crowe has shown clear willingness to participate in such a storyline.
McIntyre has been absent from WWE programming for nearly 200 days.

That defeat followed Fatu's interference that prevented McIntyre from securing a third reign as Undisputed Champion. Cody Rhodes subsequently captured his third title reign on the March 6 episode of WWE SmackDown.

In the time away from the ring, McIntyre has focused on acting projects. These include roles in The Last Druid, Highlander, Hexed, and the lead part of Roscoe in the WWE and ReelShort micro-drama The Agent of Shadows.

title: JBL Praises WWE's AAA Integration
raw_title: JBL Believes AAA Is WWE's First Successful 'Integration' Of Another Promotion
summary_src: According to JBL, WWE's acquisition of AAA has been the first time the larger promotion has successfully brought another wrestling company into the fold.
body: Ever since WWE first took on the territories with Vince McMahon and Hulk Hogan to create a global wrestling promotion, WWE has been at the top of the industry. In the years that followed, WWE went on to acquire competitors WCW and ECW, though many fans would argue that any integration into WWE was less than successful. Last year, WWE announced the acquisition of Mexican-based Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide , and fans expected much of the same, but commentator John "Bradshaw" Layfield believes the promotion still retains it's core identity while simultaneously overlapping with WWE programming on occasion. "WWE never did an integration very well," Layfield said on an episode of " Something To Wrestle ." "The first integration that they have done well, by the way, is AAA." JBL further argued that WWE's previous attempts at bringing in other promotions failed because of the mindset McMahon developed when he took on the territories, as he never forgot how territories wanted to end WWE before it took off. Because of that, he made a vow to always keep WWE at the forefront. El Hijo Del Vikingo, former two time AAA Mega Championship, shares JBL's enthusiasm for the AAA/WWE relationship, describing it as a "win-win for everyone." In an interview earlier this year, Vikingo shared how he believes that WWE fans and AAA fans are getting exposed to both promotions' wrestlers, while the performers get to experience new audiences and have matches they wouldn't have had otherwise.
summary: John "Bradshaw" Layfield stated on "Something To Wrestle" that WWE's acquisition of Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide represents the company's first successful integration of another promotion. JBL noted that AAA has kept its core identity while occasionally overlapping with WWE programming. He explained that past efforts with WCW and ECW struggled because of Vince McMahon's mindset from competing against the territories.

llm_long: WWE has long been the leading promotion in the wrestling industry after expanding from its territorial roots under Vince McMahon and Hulk Hogan. The company later acquired WCW and ECW, though many observers viewed those integrations as unsuccessful.
WWE acquired Mexican promotion Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide last year. Commentator John Bradshaw Layfield stated that this integration has succeeded where previous ones did not.
Layfield noted on a podcast that WWE has handled the AAA partnership effectively. He explained that the promotion has kept its core identity while appearing alongside WWE programming at times.

According to Layfield, past integration efforts struggled due to the approach developed when McMahon first expanded against the territories. McMahon maintained a focus on keeping WWE dominant following early resistance from those territories.

Former two-time AAA Mega Champion El Hijo Del Vikingo also expressed support for the relationship between the promotions. He described the arrangement as beneficial for fans of both WWE and AAA as well as for the wrestlers involved.
Vikingo indicated that the partnership allows fans to see performers from each promotion while giving wrestlers opportunities to reach new audiences and participate in different matches.

body: Speaking on the Battleground Podcast , Wilson elaborated on this pitch. “I hate to say it, but it probably involves me trimming some of this hair. title: Women's Blood & Guts Match Set For AEW Dynamite
raw_title: Women's Blood & Guts Match Set For AEW Special
summary_src: For only the second time in history, the AEW women's division will step inside Blood and Guts on November 4.
body: AEW/Lee South All Elite Wrestling will present its annual Blood and Guts edition of "AEW Dynamite" on November 4, and after the men's match was made official this past week, the women's match was also made official following the events of the October 24 episode of "AEW Collision." During "Collision," Divine Dominion's match with Wrathlander ended in a disqualification when The Sisters of Sin interfered on behalf of Megan Bayne and Lena Kross. As Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron were being beaten down, Thekla ran down to join in on the action before Willow Nightingale made the save for her two former tag team partners with a steel chain. Backstage, Nightingale stated that Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness may have escaped the taste of her steel chain for now, but she wants to give them a taste of some real steel on November 4 by issuing the challenge for Blood and Guts. REVENGE IS ON THEIR MINDS! Divine Dominion and the Sisters of Sin have pushed @willowwrestles and Wrathlander too far, and now they're calling for BLOOD & GUTS! Watch #AEWCollision LIVE on TNT & HBO Max! pic.twitter.com/fRZkXcvIEb Nightingale explained that she had gotten off the phone with The Brawling Birds, two women who also hate Divine Dominion and the Triangle of Madness, and agreed to join forces with Statlander, Cameron, and Nightingale for Blood and Guts. Wrathlander weren't too impressed with the idea considering they are challenging both Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor for the AEW Women's World Tag Team Championships at AEW Full Gear 2026, but they will have no choice but to coexist as the match was made official shortly after "Collision" went off the air. #AEWDynamite #BloodandGuts Wednesday 11/4 at 8/7c on TBS & HBO Max! 1-Cage /2-Rings /3-Words BLOOD and GUTS! Alex Windsor/Harley Cameron/ @jmehytr / @willowwrestles / @callmekrisstat vs @toxic_thekla / @TheJuliaHart / @Skyebyee / @meganbayne / @Lena_Kross WEDNESDAY, 11/4 Jacksonville pic.twitter.com/ZETvVmxCBL November 4 will mark only the second time in AEW history that the women's division will compete in a Blood and Guts match, with the first bout taking place last year in Greensboro, North Carolina . Megan Bayne and the Triangle of Madness also teamed up in that bout, as did Nightingale, Statlander, Cameron, and Hayter, who will all enter the double-cage structure for the second time, while Lena Kross and Alex Windsor will enter for the first time.
summary: AEW has officially booked a women's Blood and Guts match for the November 4 edition of Dynamite. The challenge was issued by Willow Nightingale after she, Kris Statlander and Harley Cameron were attacked by Megan Bayne, Lena Kross, Thekla and the rest of Divine Dominion and the Sisters of Sin on the October 24 episode of Collision. Nightingale, Statlander and Cameron will look to settle the score inside the steel cage with their rivals.

raw_title: Triple H Fires Up Metallica Crowd at Las Vegas Sphere Concert
summary_src: Triple H wasn’t running a WWE show this weekend, but that didn’t stop him from getting a crowd fired up. The WWE Chief Content Officer was caught on camera rallying fans before Metallica took the stage at the Sphere in Las Vegas.
body: Triple H attended Metallica’s “Life Burns Faster” residency alongside his wife, Stephanie McMahon, and he clearly wasn’t interested in just sitting back and watching. Footage shared on Facebook showed The Game getting the crowd going before the concert started, looking right at home playing to thousands of fans. The longtime Metallica fan also took to Twitter on October 23 to share his reaction to the show, and he didn’t need many words to explain how he felt. Triple H later shared footage of himself getting the crowd ready, with Stephanie behind the camera. He even gave his wife credit for filming the moment. “Getting the crowd ready for METALLICA at @SphereVegas!!! Camerawork by: @StephMcMahon” Stephanie also had a great time, thanking Metallica for the experience while giving her husband an anniversary shoutout. Metallica’s “Life Burns Faster” residency features 24 shows at the Sphere, with performances scheduled through March 13, 2027. Triple H spends most of his time making sure WWE crowds have something to cheer about, but this time he was just another Metallica fan having a good time. Of course, when you’ve spent decades getting wrestling audiences on their feet, it’s probably hard to turn that off. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: Triple H attended Metallica’s Life Burns Faster residency alongside his wife, Stephanie McMahon, and he clearly wasn’t interested in just sitting back and watching. Footage shared on Facebook showed The Game getting the crowd going before the concert kicked off, looking right at home playing to thousands of the audience.

title: U.S. Orders Non-Emergency Staff and Families Out of Saudi Arabia Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: U.S. Orders Non-Emergency Staff and Families Out of Saudi Arabia Ahead of WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: WWE’s upcoming trip to Saudi Arabia just got hit with another major security concern. The U.S.
body: The U.S. Mission Saudi Arabia announced the order on October 25 , although it officially went into effect on October 23. The embassy pointed directly to attacks by Iranian-backed Houthis and warned that the situation could escalate quickly. “Effective October 23, 2026, the Department of State ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and U.S. government employee family members to leave Saudi Arabia due to safety risks.” The embassy said Houthi attacks have already targeted civilian airports and other critical infrastructure in Saudi Arabia. Those attacks have caused casualties and major travel problems, with officials warning that things could get worse with little notice. “Iranian-supported Houthis have engaged in hostilities against Saudi Arabia, including attacks on civilian airports and other critical infrastructure resulting in civilian casualties and severe travel disruptions. The hostilities have the potential to escalate rapidly beyond that immediate area.” The restrictions on U.S. government personnel are pretty serious too. Employees still working in Saudi Arabia now need special authorization just to use an airport in the country following recent missile and drone attacks. “U.S. government employees working in Saudi Arabia require special authorization from Chief of Mission to use any airport in Saudi Arabia following recent missile and UAV attacks on airports in the Kingdom.” That obviously matters with WWE currently scheduled to bring a large group of American wrestlers, employees and production staff into Riyadh for Crown Jewel on November 7. There is no indication WWE or Crown Jewel itself has been targeted, but getting everyone into and out of the country could become its own problem if the airport situation continues. King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh partially reopened on October 25 for domestic flights and some international flights operated by national carriers. Some flights normally based there have been moved to Prince Naif bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Qassim, while airports in Jeddah and Dammam are operating with delays and cancellations. The embassy isn’t telling all American citizens to leave Saudi Arabia, but it is warning them about possible attacks, airspace closures and major travel disruptions . Anyone who does use an airport in the country is being urged to exercise “extreme caution.” “U.S. citizens should be aware of potential attacks on airports, airspace closures, flight cancellations, and travel disruptions. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia.” All of this comes while WWE’s Crown Jewel plans remain unchanged publicly. TKO executive Ari Emanuel recently acknowledged that the company has a team monitoring the situation every day and looking at where the event could potentially be moved if necessary. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” Crown J
summary: Per Ringside News: there is no indication WWE or Crown Jewel itself has been targeted, but getting everyone into and out of the country could become its own problem if the airport situation. Please take extreme caution if you choose to use airports in Saudi Arabia. All of this comes while WWE’s Crown Jewel the plan remain unchanged publicly.
llm_long: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh reopened on Sunday after being closed since the previous Saturday. Questions continue about whether WWE will proceed with Crown Jewel scheduled for November 7 in the city.

Saudi coalition officials reported the airport had been targeted 20 times during the month, resulting in 17 deaths and 333 injuries. Conflicting reports persist, with some outlets still listing the airport as closed.
Flight data showed 113 arrivals scheduled for Sunday, mostly domestic, and at least one international passenger flight landed. Many international airlines continue to suspend service to Riyadh.

Several major sporting events in Saudi Arabia have been canceled or postponed amid increased attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament was delayed from October to December, and the UCI Urban Cycling World Championships set for November were canceled.
The Canelo Alvarez versus Christian Mbilli boxing match planned for October 31 is still expected to take place. WWE has not announced any changes to Crown Jewel as of the latest reports.

body: According to Fightful Select , AJ Francis’ contract with TNA Wrestling is set to expire toward the end of this year. The report also stated that Francis intends to remain with the company and that TNA Wrestling is interested in retaining him, with a new deal expected to be finalized soon. Francis made his debut in TNA Wrestling at Hard To Kill in January 2024. Later that year, he won his first title in the company, the TNA Digital Media Championship. In June 2024, he revived the long-retired Canadian International Heavyweight Championship. He re-signed with the promotion earlier this year. Most recently, Francis teamed up with Expressions to face The Hardys, but they were unable to secure a victory.

They took you inside the wrestling world, from the champions and challengers to the rivalries, personalities, controversies, and occasional foolishness that made professional wrestling such wonderful entertainment. Every Sunday, we’ll travel around the wrestling world, revisiting the week’s biggest matches, championship developments, memorable moments, and questionable decisions. title: Jeff Jarrett Defends CMLL Aniversario Appearance
raw_title: AEW's Jeff Jarrett Defends CMLL Appearance
body: For the first time in legendary career, Jeff Jarrett stepped inside a CMLL ring as he took on Blue Panther at the promotion's 93rd Aniversario event on September 18, with the live Arena Mexico audience lighting up for his appearance. Many fans online, however, didn't feel the same. On a recent episode of the "My World" podcast , Jarrett addressed this mixed reaction as part of a larger discussion about his current place in the wrestling business. "I pick my spots here and there," the WWE Hall of Famer said. "I don't just say pickfest, but the CMLL show, there was a lot of hate online. Well, same thing that they didn't like Tommaso dropping the elbow [on Andrade's pants at AEW WrestleDream ]. It's not for everybody, but if you were in the arena at the CMLL anniversary show this year, me against Blue Panther. Some people, there's nothing I could ever do for them to say, 'Oh, you should never wrestle again or you should never be on a show like that again.' Well, I listen and the crowd liked that. Let's agree to disagree. I guess what I'm saying is I pick my spots." At CMLL 93 Aniversario, Blue Panther, a former CMLL World Middleweight Champion, defeated Jarrett in less than nine minutes. Elsewhere, CMLL World Heavyweight Champion Hechicero successfully defended his title against AEW's Claudio Castagnolo and NJPW's Zack Sabre Jr. For Jarrett, the event simultaneously marked his first televised match inside Arena Mexico, making him one of a select few who've performed in Arena Mexico, Madison Square Garden, Wembley Stadium, and the Tokyo Dome. It also served as the stage for one of his few in-ring outings in 2026, something he indicated as intentional. "I'm not a every week Dynamite, Collision guy or whatever, but in different spots here and there, I know without beyond a shadow of a doubt I can contribute and I can do a right short term storyline to help elevate a guy if that's what is called to," Jarrett said. "I can do certain things, whether I'm in a promo against someone or a line with someone. With my verbal skills and kind of wisdom and my connection with the audience, I can help contribute to a storyline. So you got to pick your spots. But as far as contributing to the overall growth of a product, I absolutely think that I know my role ... I'm not some main event guy that needs to be going every week at 59 years of age." Since joining AEW in 2022, Jarrett has balanced two different on-screen roles: in-ring talent and broadcaster. The latter role typically calls for him to co-host AEW pay-per-view pre-shows, such as the WrestleDream Buy In , alongside RJ City and Renee Paquette. The former has resulted in the 40-year veteran wrestling nearly four dozen matches under the AEW banner so far. His latest AEW in-ring appearance took place at the Grand Slam Mexico event on August 5, where he, Brillante Jr., Mascara Dorada, Orange Cassidy and Roderick Strong picked up a victory over Nick Wayne, The Dogs (Clark Connors and David Finlay) and The Swirl (B

title: Marina Shafir Calls Out Mercedes Mone In AEW Digital Exclusive

body: Marina Shafir had a pointed message for Mercedes Mone in a video posted following this weekend’s episode of AEW Collision. As noted , Shafir stepped up to Mone on Wednesday night’s episode of AEW Dynamite, issuing a challenge for the AEW Women’s World Championship and telling Mone to “not be a pussy.” Shafir spoke in a digital exclusive after Collision. She noted that she was trying to get Mone’s attenion and respected her, but that Mone needs to make shows of dominance while she doesn’t. “Mercedes, we all know you’re not a pussy. I just needed to get your full attention. I actually have a lot of respect for you. You are in a league of your own, and as much as it might pain you to think or to even say, you know that I am too. But that’s where the difference lies between you and me. I know. You need to swing your dominance in between your legs, and I don’t. I can’t even compliment myself. I don’t need bells and whistles. I don’t need affirmations. I don’t need a dance. I don’t need production. I just need the opportunity to work. All of the work that I have been doing these last three years has gotten me here. Here. But there’s something else that I need. I need to stand across the ring from you and I want to show everyone exactly who I am. But most importantly, I need to show you.” The match between Mercedes Mone and Marina Shafir has not yet been made official. summary_src: WWE star Penta raves about his opportunity to challenge Roman Reigns for the company's World Heavyweight Championship.
body: Penta may have lost to Roman Reigns on "WWE Raw" last month , but he still walked away feeling like a winner. During an interview with "Busted Open Radio," the high-flying luchador raved about his time sharing a ring with "The Tribal Chief" in his hometown of Mexico City. "I learned a lot facing Roman Reigns because, to be honest, I know now why he is one of the best wrestlers, or the best wrestler in the universe. The character, the Shakespeare, every move, you can breathe, you can enjoy every move," Penta said. "It's a different chip, but I like it, that chip. I like that style. I like this moment in the ring when it's the big bog, basically. He looks at me. I look at him. The whole crowd is with me, thank God. Everything was so special and magic, brother, because I can't imagine one moment like that in Mexico. When? How? Bro, but now I feel, and I am thankful with WWE, with life, with God, with all my fans, with all the people who believe in me." The match between Penta and Reigns took place in the main event of "Raw" in Mexico City on September 14, with the latter's WWE World Heavyweight Championship on the line. At one point, Penta seemed on the verge of victory when he delivered a devastating springboard Mexican Destroyer on the defending champion. Reigns kicked out, however, and eventually picked up the win for himself with a spear. This bout marked the first one-on-one faceoff between Reigns and Penta. For Penta, it also marked the first televised world title opportunity of his WWE career. As the 2026 Money in the Bank winner , he now has the option of making a rematch at any time and location of his choosing.

title: 12 Bad Wrestling Stories That Wasted Great SWERVE Ideas
raw_title: 12 Bad Wrestling Stories That Wasted Great SWERVE Ideas
body: Have you ever considered where the term "angle" actually comes from? Consider it at its most literal and the simplicity reveals itself. A character is walking down a straight path, or a storyline is progressing in the expected fashion, before an angle - a twist, a turn, a development in the route ahead - occurs that changes the trajectory. A promo exchange isn't an angle unless a development happens within it that drives change. A post-match beatdown isn't an angle unless the actions have consequences that transform the future. An entire feud isn't an angle, but should be furnished with angles in order to keep itself interesting. The swerve takes the angle and diverts it yet again, creating a whiplash effect so shocking that it feels as much like a distraction from something gone wrong as a dramatic storyline gone right. Vince Russo loved them because confounding expectations was his bread and butter even when adopting the mindset proved bad for business. He helped craft a couple of incredible ones before it all went wrong, but more often than not... In the summer of 1998, The Undertaker rather gradually (well, gradually for the lightning quick times) turned heel over the summer, first (worked) shooting on how he'd been overlooked for opportunities to justify linking up with his estranged brother Kane before offering their services to Vince McMahon to take down WWE Champion Stone Cold Steve Austin . For 'The Deadman', it was "just business" until that didn't work, and he made it personal. When Plan A (simply beating Austin fair and square) failed, and Plan B stuttered (the deadly duo won a Triple Threat, but McMahon himself held on to the belt), Plan C brought about an unlikely reunion between The Undertaker and Paul Bearer that existed to get the gold and remove Kane from the picture too. It almost worked, but when the belt remained out of his reach, 'Taker went off the reservation with a power-mad turn as the leader of the Ministry Of Darkness and decided to go for the whole organisation rather than the title itself. He spoke of a higher/greater power acting as his guiding force in all of this, and that becomes important later. In the meant though, he targeted McMahon's family, stealing Stephanie McMahon's childhood teddy bear and setting it on fire to illustrate that he was prepared to colour outside the lines to get what he wanted. The bizarre side effect of this was a face turn for Vince, who looked sympathetic trying to protect his daughter over worrying about whatever hell-raising Stone Cold Steve Austin was up to. After months of Undertaker's cryptic comments, the overlord figure driving his plan for domination over McMahon was...Vince McMahon, who wanted to keep screwing with Stone Cold Steve Austin because he'd won the World Title back at WrestleMania XV . The swerve resulted not just in half the characters' last three months not making any sense, but also in a genuine lack of faith in the future of the McMahon/Austin programme. McMahon

title: Paige Stranded in Scotland After Chaotic Flight and Train Nightmare
raw_title: Paige Stranded in Scotland After Chaotic Flight and Train Nightmare
summary_src: Paige is having an absolute nightmare trying to get out of Scotland. Between losing her seat, having her flight canceled and then finding out the trains weren’t running either, the WWE Superstar basically ran out of ways to leave the country.
body: Paige took to Twitter to share the whole travel disaster, joking that Scotland apparently doesn’t want to let her go. She said she got up early and made it to the airport, only to discover that her ticket had somehow been given away. “Scotland I love you but why won’t you let me leave??? 😂 got up early to catch my flight, got there, they GAVE MY TICKET AWAY. They said they had to accommodate passengers on a previously delayed flight???? Never heard of that before. So I had zero seat.” As frustrating as that already sounds, losing the seat ultimately didn’t matter because the flight wasn’t going anywhere anyway. Paige said a storm hitting Scotland led to most flights being canceled. “Then the flight ultimately doesn’t leave. Scottish storm is going tf off. So most flights were cancelled.” Paige wasn’t ready to give up and tried coming up with another way home. Her backup plan was to take a seven-hour train to London and catch a flight from there, but that plan died pretty quickly too. “Tried to go get a 7 hour train to London to try and catch a flight from there. Trains are cancelled..” At that point, Paige was pretty much stuck. She’s now hoping to finally make her escape tomorrow and promised fans an update on whether attempt number two goes any better. “so now I gotta try and leave tomorrow.. I’ll let ya know how it goes 🥹😂😅” The travel headache comes shortly after Paige’s last WWE match on the October 16 episode of SmackDown, where she defeated Nikki Bella. Now her opponent isn’t another wrestler — it’s apparently the entire Scottish transportation system. Hopefully Paige’s next attempt goes a whole lot smoother and she can finally get out of Scotland without another flight or train throwing a wrench into things. After the day she’s had, simply getting a seat and actually leaving might feel like a win. title: On the Record: Mick Foley Opens Up On Why His WWE Segments With The Rock Were Never Rehearsed
raw_title: Mick Foley Reveals Why His WWE Segments With The Rock Were Never Rehearsed
summary_src: Mick Foley and The Rock gave WWE fans some of the funniest moments of the Attitude Era, but it turns out the two weren’t sitting backstage rehearsing their lines. Foley says their chemistry worked because neither man knew exactly what the other was going to say.
body: During a recent fan Q&A in Germany , Foley was asked about his time working with Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson and how the two managed to make their segments feel so spontaneous. The interviewer specifically brought up their comedic timing and how Foley knew when to interrupt The Rock or let him continue talking. Foley explained that the answer was pretty simple. They didn’t rehearse anything, and they certainly weren’t following a script. “The key is that we never rehearsed anything. And we never had anything written down. Because I think if I had Dwayne, ‘Hey, I’m going to interrupt you and say your catchphrases,’ he would have said, ‘Nein, nein. Du kannst nicht meine catchphrases haben.'” Foley was joking that The Rock probably wouldn’t have agreed to let him steal his famous catchphrases if they’d discussed everything ahead of time. Instead, they just went out there and played off each other. He explained that being able to react naturally was much more important than memorizing what somebody else wanted them to say. “So, we were acting and reacting instead of trying to remember. And I think that’s really important. They’re trying to remember instead of speaking from the heart. And I would much rather have someone make many mistakes and speak from the heart than to get everything perfect that someone else has told them to say.” That approach helped make The Rock and Mankind one of WWE’s most memorable pairings. Their Rock ‘n’ Sock Connection became a huge part of the Attitude Era, with their backstage comedy and unexpected partnership giving fans something different from the usual championship rivalries. Foley’s comments also show just how much freedom he and The Rock had when they were working together. Instead of worrying about getting every line right, they trusted each other enough to make things up as they went along. More than two decades later, those moments are still remembered by WWE fans, and Foley clearly believes the lack of rehearsal was a big reason they worked. Sometimes the best wrestling television happens when two performers are allowed to be themselves instead of following a script. title: Kofi Reflects On KofiMania As Childhood Dream
raw_title: AEW Star Kofi Looks Back On Kofi-Mania In WWE: 'Childhood Dream Come True'
summary_src: AEW's Kofi recently reflected on historic KofiMana run that led to him becoming WWE Champion at WrestleMania 35 and what it meant to him.
body: WWE In 2019, Kofi defeated Bryan Danielson at WrestleMania 35 to become WWE Champion, the crowning moment of the fan-driven "KofiMania". The brief time in WWE's history is one its most important, especially in the last decade. The fans' organic support forced WWE to pay attention and propelled him to becoming the champion that WWE never planned for. Although his title reign came crashing down in seconds , "KofiMania" is still talked about with awe and respect. On The Mick and Kenny Show , Kofi reflected on "KofiMania" and how when he went to work every week, it was perfect, but it did come at the cost of Mustafa Ali. Kofi doesn't know what would've happened if Ali had stayed healthy and if it would've been MustafaMania instead. "It felt great because winning the WWE Championship was a childhood dream come true. When I was a little kid, that's all I ever used to dream about was being a WWE Superstar. We would have Royal Rumbles with all the kids in my neighborhood, in my yard. And whoever won we'd picture ourselves being at WrestleMania. For me it was a dream come true and I'm very fortunate for that moment. It's never lost on me, there were so many people that were affected positively. The first African-born champion in the history of the business is a big deal."
summary: In 2019, Kofi won the WWE Championship by defeating Bryan Danielson at WrestleMania 35, marking the peak of the fan-supported KofiMania movement that pushed WWE to create a title run they had not originally planned. The period remains one of the most memorable in recent WWE history despite the reign ending quickly. Speaking on The Mick and Kenny Show, Kofi recalled how the experience felt perfect each week at work while noting it came at the expense of Mustafa Ali's injury, wondering if it might have led to MustafaMania instead.

body: Former ECW boss Paul Heyman was sweating profusely by the time reached the climax of the exhilarating promo he cut on Vince McMahon on the Survivor Series 2001 go-home SmackDown. That pay-per-view was the end of the Invasion as we all knew it, and what a shame nobody got to know the one Heyman laid out in a scathing diatribe. He ripped into McMahon for his cold and ruthless attitude to the wrestling business and in doing so took a freezing cold storyline and almost heated it all the way back up. WWE and The Alliance weren't at war , and nobody felt it, but McMahon had been at war with the industry for years and for a split second, that felt as though it lay at the heart of the saga. Heyman was only too happy to make it personal when given the chance to get in the Chairman's face one last time too. Laying out a fairly truthful version of how McMahon's world domination tour took hold in the mid-80s, he said; " Your father went around the country and shook the hand of every promoter in this country and swore to them he'd never compete against them... and when your father DIED you competed. With your ruthless, merciless take-no-prisoners attitude you ran them all out of business didn't you Vince?! " The future "advocate" was unbelievably adept as a television talker before he permanently entered his hack years in the 2010s, and with his potted history of McMahon's autocratic journey to the top of the industry he made complete sense of a storyline that had otherwise been business-killing slop. Nobody expected this. Within a week of it airing, nobody needed to remember it. The swerve in the road was anything but too little, but it was too late. WWE won, WWE had already won , and the wrestlers still clinging on to their "WCW" t-shirts wore different ones for their Sunday Night Heat jobs instead. title: On the Record: Mick Foley Opens Up On His Biggest Regret About Working With Shawn Michaels in WWE
raw_title: Mick Foley Reveals His Biggest Regret About Working With Shawn Michaels in WWE
summary_src: Mick Foley had one of the most memorable matches of his WWE career against Shawn Michaels, but there’s one thing about their time together that still bothers him. Foley wishes they had gotten a bigger storyline, and he believes it could have led to a WrestleMania match.
body: During a recent fan Q&A in Germany , Foley was asked about his match against Michaels at WWE In Your House: Mind Games in 1996. The interviewer praised the match and wanted to know whether Foley realized they were doing something special while it was happening. Foley immediately praised Michaels and explained that their match remains one of his personal favorites, sitting just behind his 2004 encounter with Randy Orton. “This is my Lieblingsmatch, das ist mit Randy Orton. 2004. Aber es ist Nummer zwei. Nummer zwei, Shawn was so great.” Foley then explained that being WWE Champion during that period came with an enormous amount of pressure. Michaels was expected to carry the company, handle media appearances, headline shows, and consistently deliver great matches. According to Foley, the workload was taking its toll on Michaels by the time they worked together. “But back when Shawn was a champion and Bret Hart before him, Hulk Hogan, you know, was a champion for a long time. Um, there was a lot of pressure on the champion. Like the company revolved around the champion. And they had to do a lot of media. They had to be in the main event. They had to be a lot of great matches every night. And Shawn was worn out.” Foley recalled approaching Michaels with some ideas for their match. Michaels was receptive, and the two went on to deliver a performance that fans still talk about today. “And so I said, ‘Hey, I have some ideas.’ He said, ‘Good.’ I laid out some ideas for him. And he liked them.” Despite how well they worked together, Foley admitted that he still wishes WWE had given them a longer rivalry. In particular, he would have loved the opportunity to face Michaels on the biggest stage of them all. “So my one regret is that we did not have a bigger program, like a bigger storyline that could have ended up like I would have loved to have wrestled Shawn at WrestleMania. Like I just I wish we could have had more time together in the ring and uh in the storyline.” Foley and Michaels never got that WrestleMania match, despite proving how well they could work together at Mind Games. Their 1996 encounter remains one of the most celebrated matches of Foley’s WWE career. It’s a missed opportunity that clearly hasn’t left Foley’s mind. Both men went on to have legendary careers, but a bigger rivalry between them could have given WWE fans another classic, especially if it had ended at WrestleMania. title: 15 Secret WWE Pasts Of Top AEW Stars
raw_title: 15 Secret WWE Pasts Of Top AEW Stars
body: One of the blessings of having AEW as part of the wrestling landscape is having something that differs from the juggernaut WWE . All Elite Wrestling has managed to carve out a space for itself by doing something different from the glossy, big-budget approach to the squared circle. It's been great for fans, and it's given talented wrestlers who might not be a good fit for WWE's distinct in-house style somewhere to thrill us all. That being said, many of the performers on Tony Khan's roster have had dalliances with WWE . No matter how small the role has been, some of the biggest and most surprising names in AEW have played a part in WWE. Buried beneath the ether, we have scoured the history books to find some of these shocking appearances and put them into one handy list for you to check out. From shock offers to refereeing, to one of the world's greatest wrestlers nearly being given the name 'Cheesy' and beyond, these are the secret WWE appearances that some of All Elite Wrestling's most significant performers don't want you to see. As well as being known as The Cleaner, The Best Bout Machine, The God of Professional Wrestling, and all manner of other cool-sounding nicknames, Kenny Omega is justifiably and widely considered the best wrestler to have never set foot inside a WWE ring. It's no secret that WWE made plenty of advances to sign the elite Canadian over the years, but Kenny remains WWE's great white whale. While Omega has never wrestled for WWE , he did appear very briefly on the dearly departed WWE Network. Clocking in at less than a minute, Kenny cut a short promo on Cru Jones while the pair were in the Deep South Wrestling developmental territory, and this short and sweet tirade about rainbows and leprechauns aired on WWE's in-house channel and on their YouTube a week after the first All In. Coincidence, eh? It might be a slight reach to include this as part of Omega's career in any way , but whatever way you slice it, you can find footage of Kenny Omega on WWE's programming. It's not quite a WrestleMania performance, but it's on record nevertheless. Terry Bezer hasn't written a bio just yet, but if they had... it would appear here.

title: Amber Nova Arrested on DUI Charges
raw_title: Former WWE NXT and AEW Wrestler Amber Nova Arrested for DUI—Police Say Four Breath-Test Attempts Produced No Sample
body: The 34-year-old performer, whose real name is Amber Flora, has competed on the independent circuit and made appearances on national wrestling television. TMZ reported the arrest the following day, citing jail records and court docket information. The reports reviewed through October 25 did not identify a plea or resolution of the charges. The encounter occurred near South Orange Blossom Trail and McLeod Road in Orlando. Ringside News reported that documents identified Orlando Police Department Officer Alvin Silverio as the arresting officer and indicated that no collision was involved. Flora was released at 10:07 a.m. after posting $1,000 bail on each charge, for a total of $2,000. She attended a mandatory court appearance on October 24. The reported docket information lists November 2 as a compliance date. Ringside News said it obtained nine pages of law enforcement documents filed in Orange County. Its account of that paperwork describes what officers reported observing after Flora was taken to the Orange County Sheriff's Office DUI Testing Center. Officers noted bloodshot, glassy eyes, a flushed face and an odor of alcohol on her breath. They described her speech as slow and slurred, while also recording that she was cooperative during the initial observation period. When she was escorted to the testing room, officers reported that she walked slowly and swayed from side to side. According to the outlet's account of the testing records , Flora initially declined to provide a breath sample. Officers explained the consequences of refusing and started the testing equipment to give her an opportunity to proceed. The first testing sequence ran from 3:06 a.m. to 3:17 a.m. Two attempts were marked "NSP," which the report identified as meaning no sample provided. Flora asked to speak with an attorney during the process, according to the officer's account. Before the refusal was finalized, she requested another opportunity to take the test. Officers restarted the equipment. Two more attempts, between 3:19 a.m. and 3:31 a.m., also failed to produce valid samples. Police alleged that Flora continued talking during the periods when she was supposed to provide a sample. The officer recorded a refusal at the end of that second sequence. The described paperwork contains no measured blood alcohol concentration. Nova faced Nikki Cross on the August 8, 2018 episode of NXT, with Cross winning the match, according to WWE . She returned for the January 23, 2019 episode, teaming with Tanea Brooks in a loss to Kairi Sane and Io Shirai. She also worked for Impact Wrestling. In an October 2020 interview with Fightful , Nova discussed seeking a larger opportunity after those appearances. She said she remained interested in tryouts with major promotions and continued training while the pandemic limited openings. Her AEW appearances included an April 14, 2021 match against Kris Statlander on Dynamite. Statlander won in her return to competition, as documented in the promo

No crash occurred and she was released after posting $2,000 bail following a court appearance on October 24 with a compliance date of November 2. Four breath-test attempts at the Orange County Sheriff's Office DUI Testing Center produced no sample according to law enforcement documents obtained by Ringside News.

body: Having departed WWE two years ago, Samantha Irvin is about to become a free agent. Via Fightful Select , the real-life Samantha Johnson's two-year non-compete is set to expire later this month. Samantha requested her WWE exit in October 2024 , having spent several years as the company's go-to ring announcer for so many major matches and moments, most memorably her emotional announcement of Cody Rhodes' WWE Championship win at WrestleMania 40. As part of being granted her release, Samantha was unable to appear for any other wrestling promotions for two years . And as for the reason for wanting out of WWE, she wanted to be utilised as more than just a ring announcer, whereas WWE seemingly didn't have any real interest in letting her expand beyond that ring announcing gig. Of course, there has long been speculation that Samantha Johnson would join AEW in an on-screen capacity once those two years were up. Fightful notes this is something that's been discussed in AEW "a number of times", though she isn't expected to immediately join Tony Khan's outfit as soon as she hits free agency. Given that Samantha is married to AEW star Ricochet, Fightful adds that she's been backstage at "dozens" of AEW shows and has a "great" relationship with the promotion. So, the story here is that Samantha Johnson will soon become a free agent, there have been internal AEW talks of bringing her in, she's been at various AEW events, has a great relationship with AEW... but she's not expected to land in the company just yet. 5 Ups & 4 Downs From WWE SmackDown (23 Oct - Results & Review) Once described as the Swiss Army Knife of WhatCulture, Andrew can usually be found writing, editing, or presenting on a wide range of topics. As a lifelong wrestling fan, horror obsessive, and comic book nerd, he's been covering those topics professionally as far back as 2010. In addition to his current WhatCulture role of Senior Content Producer and Presenter, Andrew previously spent nearly a decade as Online Editor and Lead Writer for the world's longest-running genre publication, Starburst Magazine, and his work has also been featured on BBC, TechRadar, Tom's Guide, WhatToWatch, Sportkskeeda, and various other outlets, in addition to being a Rotten Tomatoes-approved film critic. Between his main day job, his role as lead panel host of Wales Comic Con, and his gig as a pre-match host for Wrexham AFC games, Andrew has also carried out a hugely varied amount of interviews, from the likes of Robert Englund and Eli Roth to Kevin Smith and the Russo Brothers, to Kevin Conroy and Frank Miller, to Bret Hart and Sting, to Mickey Thomas, Joey Jones, Phil Parkinson, and Brian Flynn, to many, many more. Where his beloved Wrexham AFC is concerned, Andrew is a long-standing season ticket holder and an FSA Award-winner for his time co-hosting the Fearless in Devotion podcast.

Manders announced on social media that he split his head open in the Boston match and was physically unable to compete the following day.

He expressed that he was incredibly gutted to miss the October 25 RevPro show and issued huge apologies to Shire, the people in the match, the RevPro team and all the fans. Manders described it as an unfortunate birthday week involving travel but noted that is how it goes sometimes.

In a follow-up announcement he confirmed he would no longer make his scheduled RevPro appearances in England because of the injury sustained the previous night. He stated he was gutted, disappointed and upset as he had been looking forward to getting back there, seeing everyone and doing what he loves.

Manders added that wrestling is everything to him and pulling out of the dates is not something he takes lightly. He said he needs to focus on getting healthy and doing what he can to get back in the ring while also getting off social media for a while.
Manders apologized to everyone who supported him, reached out or was looking forward to seeing him and said he needs some time to himself to deal with everything and get his head right.

title: Drew McIntyre Ranks His HIAC With CM Punk Among WWE's Best
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Believes WWE's Best Hell In A Cell Match Comes Down To His & One Other
summary_src: According to Drew McIntyre, there is only one other Hell in a Cell match that might surpass he and CM Punk at WWE Bad Blood 2024.
body: WWE At WWE Bad Blood in 2024, Drew McIntyre and CM Punk had a heated Hell in a Cell match, where both men made extensive use of various weapons, resulting in plenty of blood. Leading up to the match, the rivalry became increasingly personal, making the stakes feel genuine. So much so that McIntyre boldly believes his Hell in a Cell match rivals the first-ever iteration of the match between The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels at WWE Badd Blood 1997. "From a story perspective, from a match perspective, I'll argue all day: it's one and two between us and 'Taker and Shawn, the first ever Hell in a Cell," he proclaimed during an appearance on " The Hall of Fame " podcast. McIntyre argued that his clash with Punk deserves such high praise because of the nature of their relationship, asserting yet again that he genuinely hates "The Second City Saint." McIntyre argued that, in the end, rather than Punk defeating him fair and square, it was something else that did him in. "I lose to blood loss, not CM Punk, 'cause he can't beat me on his best day," he said. "17 staples in my head!" It wasn't only McIntyre who has praised by the showing, as the bloody match also impressed many others, like Eric Bischoff . During an episode of his podcast, he praised McIntyre's performance in the match, specifically how he conveyed emotion. Bischoff also highlighted the story and the emotion surrounding it, while also praising the match production and blood utilization throughout.
summary: Drew McIntyre stated that from a story and match standpoint his 2024 Hell in a Cell bout against CM Punk at Bad Blood ranks as one or two alongside the inaugural 1997 Hell in a Cell between The Undertaker and Shawn Michaels. McIntyre emphasized the personal hatred between himself and Punk that elevated the contest and claimed he ultimately lost due to blood loss rather than being beaten by Punk. He noted receiving 17 staples in his head following the match.

He claimed that he lost due to blood loss rather than being defeated by Punk, stating on the podcast, "I lose to blood loss, not CM Punk, 'cause he can't beat me on his best day."
McIntyre added that he received 17 staples in his head following the match.
Eric Bischoff praised McIntyre's performance on his own podcast, noting how the wrestler conveyed emotion throughout the contest.

body: Anthony Bowens has fueled internet speculation about a potential move to New Japan Pro-Wrestling. The former AEW World Tag Team Champion posted a photo of himself standing outside the NJPW LA Dojo on Friday, leaving fans wondering about his next career destination. The timing of the social media post aligns with a scheduled event at the facility. AEW star Kevin Knight was locked in to conduct training seminars at the venue on that exact same day. While the photo has generated significant buzz across the wrestling community, there is currently no official confirmation that Bowens is in active contract talks with New Japan management. Questions about his future have intensified due to his current contract situation. Bowens’ deal with Tony Khan’s promotion is believed to have expired on October 1. His last televised match for the company took place on the AEW All In London Buy-In pre-show, where his team, The Opps, lost an eight-man tag team encounter against Lio Rush and The Rascalz. During an October 12 media interview, the tag team specialist dropped a hint regarding his upcoming career decisions. Bowens acknowledged that while the wrestling landscape is unpredictable, he already has a specific path in mind. “I know deep down what I want to do and we’ll see if it works out,” Bowens stated on 10/12. The veteran performer achieved major success throughout his multi-year run on national television. title: Jonathan Gresham Open To ROH Return Under Tony Khan
raw_title: Jonathan Gresham Comments On Chances Of Returning Work For ROH Under AEW's Tony Khan
summary_src: Jonathan Gresham comments on if he would ever like to return to ROH, should the opportunity present itself.
body: TNA Back in the July 2022, a heated argument ensued between AEW President Tony Khan and former ROH talent Jonathan Gresham. Gresham, the then ROH World Champion, was upset that he was instructed to drop his championship to Claudio Castagnoli just minutes before stepping through the curtain at Death Before Dishonor, among other things. After doing what he was asked, Gresham asked for his release from ROH, which Khan granted. However, the two have not spoken to one another since, despite multiple attempts from Gresham. Even though things look grim at the moment, the former champion hopes that one day he and Khan can settle things, and that he can return to his old stomping grounds in ROH. "I'm never going to say never, but I've reached out several times to apologize in person when they've come here to Atlanta...I'm just going to say 'no' was the answer that I got. And that's fair," the former ROH Pure and World Champion said on "Grapsody Podcast." "The way that I went off, I probably wouldn't want to talk to me either. But again, I think we should also look at why did he go off? I just didn't arrive at the show and go, 'You know what, motherf***er?' That's not what happened. There was a reason why, a buildup, frustration. And to be honest, to this day, I, again, I do not agree with how I went about it, but I think that I had good reason to be upset." Coming back from two serious strokes, "The Octopus" is not only back in the ring fighting, but he is also coaching and scouting the next new recruits through PRODUCE Wrestling. Earlier this month, he was made the chairman of the talent advisory council for the promotion. Furthering his mark in the industry, he is also launching his own promotion, M.A.G. (Modern Age Grappling), which will premiere on January 9, 2027.
