summary_src: Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo just gave fans the update they’ve been waiting for after his scary injury at an NXT live event, and he certainly looks to be in much better spirits.
body: Stacks took to his Instagram Story with a photo from the hospital, where he could be seen wearing a neck brace while flipping off the doctor. Even after everything that happened, his sense of humor clearly wasn’t going anywhere. “Doc was concerned about my ‘attitude’.. Told ’em it’s a preexisting condition. The show goes on.” Stacks followed that up with an even more encouraging photo. The next slide showed him back in the gym, suggesting he’s already feeling well enough to get back to training after the frightening incident. That’s a pretty welcome sight considering how bad things looked just over a week ago. Stacks was injured during the October 16 NXT live event in Sudbury, Ontario, after taking a back body drop over the top rope and crashing onto the floor during an eight-man tag team match. The situation was serious enough that WWE stopped the match while medical personnel checked on him. Stacks was eventually placed on a stretcher and taken out of the arena before being transported to a nearby hospital. There were concerns afterwards that Stacks may have suffered a concussion, although WWE never publicly confirmed the exact nature of his injury. Uriah Connors offered the first encouraging update the following day , telling fans that his BirthRight teammate was doing okay. “My boys alive and well!! We can’t be stopped, last of a dying breed! Thanks for checkin on em, I got his ass.” Now fans have finally heard directly from Stacks himself, and seeing him already back in the gym is certainly a much better image than the stretcher scene from Sudbury. He still hasn’t revealed exactly what he injured or when he’ll be cleared to wrestle again, so his in-ring return remains up in the air for now. And it doesn’t matter.” For Brie, money doesn’t cancel out whatever somebody might be dealing with personally. She said people can still have their own problems regardless of how successful their life might look from the outside. The conversation then shifted into something a little darker. Brie recalled a discussion she and Nikki had with someone just the day before about how reaching a certain level of success can completely change the way other people treat you. “It’s so true. I’m so happy you put that in your book. I am too. Because that’s very true. We were just talking to someone about that yesterday, about that, like, where people, you get to a certain level of success, and they don’t—they feel like they could throw negativity at you. They feel like they can turn their back on you.” Brie said that conversation also included a warning about the people who stay close to you. According to her, they were told things can become particularly scary when someone around you doesn’t simply admire what you’ve accomplished but actually wants the life you have. “And he had said, like, one of the scariest things are when you have people that are around you that want to be you or your life. He goes, ‘And that’s when it gets really scary.’ Then you just really realize how alone you are. That’s so true.” Brie’s comments show that her experience with success hasn’t just been about dealing with random criticism online. She’s also become more aware of how money and recognition can change relationships, especially when jealousy starts creeping into the picture. title: Steve Austin’s Match-Worn Knee Brace From 1999 Sells for Big Money at Auction
raw_title: Steve Austin’s Match-Worn Knee Brace From 1999 Sells for Big Money at Auction
summary_src: One of “Stone Cold” Steve Austin’s old knee braces just found a new home, and this wasn’t some replica somebody picked up at a merch stand.
body: The brace was sold through Heritage Auctions and is believed to date from around 1999. Austin signed the top in gold paint pen and wrote “5-8-99” next to it, with an old WWF authentication sticker sitting nearby. This thing definitely doesn’t look like it spent the last 27 years sitting untouched in a display case either. There are scratches and paint loss across the brace, while only three of the four Velcro fasteners still work. The fourth one might actually explain why Austin stopped using it. The top button is broken off, and Heritage noted that the damage may have been what finally ended the brace’s run inside the ring. There’s also quite a paper trail backing the piece up. Along with the WWE letter signed by Linda McMahon, the brace came with authentication from Heritage Auctions, PSA/DNA and Beckett Authentication Services. Getting your hands on something Austin actually wore isn’t exactly easy either. Heritage noted that very few of his match-worn items have made it onto the open market, with his famous wrestling vests apparently remaining especially difficult for collectors to find. His knee braces have already proven they can bring in some crazy money. The brace Austin wore for his WrestleMania 38 comeback sold for $58,045, while Heritage sold another one for a whopping $115,900 in May 2026. That’s what makes these braces more than just another piece of signed Stone Cold memorabilia. They’re beat-up pieces of gear that actually went through Austin’s matches with him, and collectors clearly aren’t having much trouble opening their wallets whenever one finally hits the market. title: Glam WWE wrestler, 34, 'smelled strongly' during early morning drink driving stop
raw_title: Glam WWE wrestler, 34, 'smelled strongly' during early morning drink driving stop
body: Ex-WWE wrestler Amber “Nova” Flora has been busted for an early-morning DUI (Driving Under the Influence) arrest in her Florida hometown. Cops claimed the 34-year-old looked dazed and smelled strongly of alcohol during a roadside stop. Flora, who performs in the ring as Amber Nova and has appeared for WWE NXT, AEW and Impact Wrestling, was taken into custody in Orlando on Friday (October 23) and booked at 5.40am local time, according to the Orlando Police Department. Newly released police documents lay out what officers say happened in the hours before her arrest. An Orlando officer, Alvin Silverio, pulled Flora over at around 1.48am near South Orange Blossom Trail and McLeod Road, with no crash reported. She has been busted for an early-morning DUI (Driving Under the Influence) arrest (Image: ambernova73/Instagram) In his account, the officer said Flora had bloodshot, glassy eyes, a bloated face and a strong odour of alcohol on her breath. Her speech was described as slow and thick-tongued, and she appeared confused, though she was initially cooperative. Flora was then taken to the Orange County Sheriff’s Office DUI Testing Center, where officers said she swayed from side to side as she was escorted inside, the New York Post reported. Police reports state she first declined a breath test, but agreed to try after being warned about the legal consequences. Cops claimed the 34-year-old looked dazed (Image: ambernova73/Instagram) However, officers reportedly say the breath test never produced a valid result. Between 3.06am and 3.31am, police recorded four attempts across two machine cycles - but claim Flora continued talking during the testing windows, meaning the machine couldn’t get a proper reading. She also asked to speak to her attorney during the process. The test was officially logged as a refusal at 3.31am, and she was arrested on suspicion of DUI and refusing to submit to a DUI test, eWrestlingNews reported. Flora was reportedly released less than five hours after being booked, at 10.07am, after posting bond. The bond total was listed as 2,000 (1,000 for each count), with bail also reported as £1,500. She attended a mandatory court hearing on Saturday, 24 October. Her next compliance deadline is scheduled for 2 November 2026, with the case still ongoing. Flora is a 34-year-old American independent wrestler best known for her “American Muscle Mechanic” gimmick and appearances across big-name promotions including WWE NXT, AEW and Impact Wrestling. Born on November 2, 1991, she was born in Hackettstown, New Jersey, and grew up largely in Hilton Head Island, South Carolina, before later relocating to Orlando, Florida. Before stepping into the ring, Flora studied at the Technical College of the Lowcountry and worked as a certified Emergency Medical Technician (EMT). title: Crown Jewel Still Going Ahead As Planned Despite Heightened Risk In Saudi Arabia
raw_title: Crown Jewel Still Going Ahead As Planned Despite Heightened Risk In Saudi Arabia
body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 26, 2026, 6:56 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. His favorite wrestlers are The Rock and CM Punk, despite the latter doing his level best to make us all dislike him. Sign in to your TheSportster account You would think that with the ongoing attacks on Saudi Arabia, there would be no way Crown Jewel will go ahead as planned in Riyadh on November 7, 2026. However, with less than two weeks to go, the latest on the situation claims that, despite internal pressure, WWE is pushing ahead with plans to stage a major PLE in a country where civilian-targeted attacks are ongoing. The latest news on what exactly WWE plans to do surrounding Crown Jewel comes courtesy of Fightful . The site claims that, according to sources within WWE, there are currently no plans to either cancel Crown Jewel or move the show to a venue outside of Saudi Arabia. That's despite growing internal pressure from staff and Superstars who, understandably, aren't comfortable with traveling to the Middle East given the current climate. The update on plans for Crown Jewel comes after the US government ordered diplomats to be flown out of the region late last week, as reported by Reuters . Government officials and their families deployed in Saudi Arabia have all been ordered to return, with a follow-up mandate expected in the coming days that will see diplomats in surrounding countries also removed from their posts. The unrest in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East comes amid ongoing attacks by the group Houthis. Houthis has now claimed responsibility for recent attacks on a Saudi oil pipeline and, more worryingly for those in WWE, Riyadh airport. The airport in which those working Crown Jewel will presumably fly to and depart from should Crown Jewel be allowed to go ahead on November 7. I say allowed, as we are fast approaching a point where it feels like the decision to hold this show needs to be taken out of WWE's, or perhaps more specifically TKO's, hands. It seems almost unfathomable that, as the US government removes its employees from a country where foreign nationals are being targeted, WWE remains insistent that it will send its wrestlers and employees in and potentially risk their lives. I'm unsure if the government can step in and prevent anyone from the US from traveling to a country should the circumstances dictate it. It's starting to feel more and more likely that's what it's going to take to get Crown Jewel moved. Either that or those who will be ordered to fly to Saudi Arabia in less than two weeks take a united stand. If everyone in the company refuses to travel, then there's not much TKO can do about it.

title: Eric Bauza, Voice Actor Behind WWE Animated Movies and Bugs Bunny, Dead at 46
raw_title: Eric Bauza, Voice Actor Behind WWE Animated Movies and Bugs Bunny, Dead at 46
summary_src: The entertainment world has lost another familiar voice. Eric Bauza, the Emmy Award-winning actor best known for voicing Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, has died at the age of 46.
body: Bauza’s family confirmed his passing in a statement shared on his official Instagram account on October 25, 2026. The family described his death as sudden and said more information would be released. “Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly. More details to come.” The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner has since listed hypertensive cardiovascular disease as his cause of death. Bauza died on October 25 at his residence. Bauza had several connections to WWE throughout his career. He voiced Dino and Bam Bam in The Flintstones & WWE: Stone Age SmackDown! , Rolf Rodriquez in The Jetsons & WWE: Robo-WrestleMania! , and Big Earl in Scooby-Doo! and WWE: Curse of the Speed Demon . He also recently worked on Coyote vs. Acme , which featured John Cena in a live-action role. Bauza provided the voices of several Looney Tunes characters in the movie, including Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck. Outside WWE, Bauza built an impressive career that included work on SpongeBob SquarePants , Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles , Rick and Morty , The Fairly OddParents , and X-Men ’97 . He became one of the most recognizable voices in modern animation, taking on characters that generations of fans grew up watching. His work earned him three Children’s and Family Emmy Awards, including recognition for his performances in Looney Tunes Cartoons , Bugs Bunny Builders , and Teen Titans Go! Bauza’s death comes as a shock to the animation industry and fans who followed his work for decades. His connection to WWE’s animated movies also means wrestling fans have heard his work in several projects that brought their favorite Superstars into the cartoon world. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: Myles Borne Calls 'What?' Chants a Waste of Energy
raw_title: Myles Borne Tells Fans They Are 'Wasting Their Engery' By Chanting 'What?' At Him
summary_src: Since turning on Tavion Heights and showing a new side of himself, fans have booed Myles Borne when he's set foot in the WWE Performance Center. During a recent promo, he received "What?" chants from the NXT Universe despite the fact that he's deaf and can't hear the chants.
body: Since turning on Tavion Heights and showing a new side of himself, fans have booed Myles Borne when he’s set foot in the WWE Performance Center. During a recent promo, he received “What?” chants from the NXT Universe despite the fact that he’s deaf and can’t hear the chants. Speaking to Korey Smith and Tor Smith on KRON4 , Borne was asked how he felt about the “What?” chants. “The only reason I knew there was a ‘What?’ chant is that when I watched it back, there was closed caption, so I was able to pick up on it. To me, it just shows me…you’re really doing ‘What?’ chants to a guy that can’t hear? You’re wasting your energy. You have to be a lot louder than that if you want to try and get my attention. I think it’s funny. They know the situation, and yet they are sitting there yelling. Keep saying, ‘What?’ I love it. Once I watched it back and saw what they are saying, great, I appreciate it,” he said. title: In Memoriam: Brooke Hogan Calls Out WWE Stars for Honoring Hulk Hogan After His Death But Barely Visiting Him in Hospital
raw_title: Brooke Hogan Calls Out WWE Stars for Honoring Hulk Hogan After His Death But Barely Visiting Him in Hospital
summary_src: Brooke Hogan is tearing into the people who showed up on WWE television to honor her father after his death, accusing them of barely giving him the time of day when he was still alive.
body: Hulk Hogan’s daughter shared a photo of WWE’s tribute to her father and made a brutal accusation about the stars and legends standing on that stage. According to Brooke, not a single person pictured spent more than an hour visiting him in the hospital, and some didn’t bother showing up at all. The picture showed dozens of WWE Superstars, legends, and company officials standing together with their heads lowered as the company paid tribute to Hogan following his death the previous day. Brooke wasn’t impressed by the public display of respect. She put one message across the photo, taking aim at everyone standing on that stage. “Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed.” That’s a serious accusation against the people WWE gathered to honor one of the biggest names in wrestling history. Brooke is claiming that the same people who stood together for a televised tribute couldn’t make time for her father when he was still alive and dealing with his health problems. The tribute featured Triple H alongside WWE Superstars and wrestling legends as the company held a ten-bell salute for Hogan. WWE also aired a video looking back at his career, celebrating his accomplishments and the role he played in turning professional wrestling into a global business. But Brooke clearly has a different perspective on how some of those people treated her father behind the scenes. Instead of naming one or two individuals, she posted the entire group photo and made her accusation against everyone pictured. Her latest post comes after she spent the previous day expressing her anger over the sale of Hulk Hogan’s Clearwater Beach mansion . Brooke explained how much the home meant to her, recalling time spent with her father in the garage, watching television together, listening to music, and being there during his recovery from multiple surgeries. She also accused unnamed people of using her father for financial gain and selling the property for profit. The mansion sold for $5.9 million after originally being listed for $10.989 million, leaving Brooke furious that a home filled with family memories was gone. Now her frustration has shifted to the wrestling business itself. Brooke appears to have little patience for the people who participated in WWE’s tribute when she believes they failed to show up for her father during his hospital stays. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: Hulk Hogan’s daughter shared a photo of WWE’s tribute to her father and made a brutal accusation about the stars and legends standing on that stage. Per Brooke, not a single person pictured spent more than an hour visiting him in the hospital, and some didn’t bother showing up at all.

body: October 26 has been a very busy day for pro wrestling title changes over the years. According to wrestlingdata.com , there have been around 318 major/notable title changes on this date historically. Some of the bigger title changes include Harley Race winning the AJPW/PWF Heavyweight Title in 1982, Rey Mysterio Jr. winning the WCW Cruiserweight Title in 1997 and Batista winning the WWE World Heavyweight Title in 2008. The earliest October 26th entry is from 1973, when Enrique Vera won the Mexican National Heavyweight Title. In 1982, Chief Jay Strongbow and Jules Strongbow won the WWF World Tag Team Titles and Harley Race won the AJPW/PWF Heavyweight Title. Rey Mysterio Jr. won the WCW Cruiserweight Title in 1997. Diamond Dallas Page won the WCW United States Heavyweight Title in 1998. The British Bulldog won the WWF European Title in 1999. Batista won the WWE World Heavyweight Title in 2008. In 2011, Gail Kim and Madison Rayne won the TNA Knockouts Tag Team Titles and Bobby Roode won the TNA World Heavyweight Title. Akitoshi Saito and Go Shiozaki won the GHC Heavyweight Tag Team Titles in 2012. Four titles changed hands on October 26th, 2021. Fabian Aichner and Marcel Barthel won the NXT Tag Team Titles. Gigi Dolin and Jacy Jayne won the NXT Women’s Tag Team Titles. Mandy Rose won the NXT Women’s Title. Robbie Eagles and Tiger Mask #4 won the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Titles. Jeff Hardy and Matt Hardy won the TNA World Tag Team Titles, and Masha Slamovich won the TNA Knockouts World Title. At the end of the day, like it or not, she’s a bigger star. Wear the T-shirt if you want to; I really don’t care. You can put food on our table. title: Match Made: Eddie Guerrero vs Rey Misterio Jr – WCW Halloween Havoc 1997
raw_title: Eddie Guerrero vs Rey Misterio Jr – WCW Halloween Havoc 1997 | WON Flashback
summary_src: October 26 1997 was the date of WCW Halloween Havoc that year, and the best match on the card by far was Eddie Guerrero vs Rey Misterio Jr. The match got ****3/4 in that week’s Wrestling Observer Newsletter, and our own Dave Meltzer was a huge fan, writing at the time that it was “arguably […]
body: “The Rey Misterio Jr. vs. Eddie Guerrero mask vs. cruiserweight title, won by Misterio Jr., in a finish apparently not finalized until just minutes before the show started, was arguably the single best match on a WCW PPV show dating back more than six years to the prime of Ric Flair and the February 24, 1991 War Games match from Phoenix. Because of sentimental and memorable reasons, some may compare it with the Jushin Liger vs. Brian Pillman match in 1992, but this match was clearly due to the sport advancing over five years, of a higher quality if both were judged by the same standards. “Rey Misterio Jr. (Oscar Gutierrez) pinned Eddie Guerrero in 13:51 to retain his mask and win the WCW cruiserweight title. Not sure exactly what went down in the closing minutes to get the finish changed. Misterio Jr. was adamant and vocal about not losing his mask for the very reasons that were brought up in the video piece that was actually put together with the express idea of building up to his losing his mask. At one point a few days before the match, Eric Bischoff personally called Misterio Jr. up and told him that if he didn’t lose the match that it would considered a contract breach and he’d be both fired and even threatened him with a lawsuit, and you can imagine considering how popular Misterio Jr. is with nearly everyone in the company, how that went over. No doubt both sides agreed to a compromise at the end. Based on sketchy details from a variety of sources, Guerrero was still going over one hour before the show went on the air, but over the next half hour to 45 minutes, Misterio Jr. and Bischoff met, probably with Misterio Jr.’s agent Michael Scott as well, and they apparently came up with a face saving compromise. Apparently Misterio Jr. agreed to lose the match but at that point Bischoff agreed to change the finish. In the days preceding the event, there was a lot of speculation that Bischoff would change the finish provided Misterio Jr. agree to lose the mask at some point in the near future, but I’m not sure if that’s what ended up being agreed to in the meeting. “This was as good as modern pro wrestling can get with innovative moves, flawless execution and incredible psychology, drama and very good announcing all wrapped up into one package. The only thing that would keep me from listing this as the match of the year is that it wasn’t long enough to be ranked ahead of some of the best 20+ minute matches. Guerrero rammed Misterio Jr.’s head into the steps. Misterio Jr. tried a handspring into his rana into a huracanrana stop, but Guerrero reversed the spot in the middle into a back suplex. Guerrero used a great spinning backbreaker (quebradora in Lucha terms) and followed with the old 70s Billy Robinson style backbreaker. In one for the all-time highlight reel, Misterio Jr. was balancing on the top rope and turned the move into a twisting DDT. title: Pro wrestling legend Ric Flair recovering after falling outside Tampa restaurant
raw_title: Pro wrestling legend Ric Flair recovering after falling outside Tampa restaurant
body: By Bob D'Angelo, Cox Media Group National Content Desk October 26, 2026 at 4:50 am PDT By Bob D'Angelo, Cox Media Group National Content Desk October 26, 2026 at 4:50 am PDT TAMPA, Fla. — Professional wrestling legend Ric Flair is recovering after falling outside of a west-central Florida restaurant on Friday. Flair, 77, a WWE Hall of Famer known as “The Nature Boy,” allegedly fell while leaving Wagamama , an Asian fusion restaurant in downtown Tampa, TMZ reported. He was taken by ambulance to an area hospital after suffering injuries to his eye and face, according to the celebrity gossip outlet. Flair, a 16-time world heavyweight wrestling champion – who touted himself as a “stylin’, profilin’, limousine riding, jet flying, kiss-stealing, wheelin’ n’ dealin’ son of a gun” during his heyday in the ring, posted an update on his social media accounts . Flair published a photograph of himself wearing an eyepatch, adding that he “will be okay.” “Thank you all for the messages and prayers! I will get back to you each individually as I get stronger,” Flair wrote . Thank you to all the Tampa General Hospital Staff and doctors that put up with me until 4:30 a.m. I appreciate you all and thank you for everything you did for me! I am focused on my healing and recovery right now.” Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger. Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay! And Just So You Know For Those Who Were Asking And Wondering, I Don’t Own My Own Facebook Page Anymore. I Apologize For The Reckless Posting Behavior On My Facebook When I Was In The Hospital. It Was Completely Inappropriate! Flair, whose legal name is Richard Morgan Fliehr, fell hours after he announced that he had to cancel a scheduled appearance in Seattle because of a blood clot in his leg, WTVT reported. Flair apologized on social media , adding that his doctors had limited his traveling time to three to four hours. title: Bollywood Boyz Set For PWR Debut In India
raw_title: Former WWE tag team The Bollywood Boyz comment on PWR debut confirmed for 2027
summary_src: The Bollywood Boyz (Gurv and Harv Sihra) are set to make their Pro Wrestling Rebellion (PWR) debut in 2027. The brothers, who previously competed in WWE as The Singh Brothers, were announced for PWR’s upcoming event in New Delhi, India, via the promotion’s official X account.
body: The Bollywood Boyz (Gurv and Harv Sihra) are set to make their Pro Wrestling Rebellion (PWR) debut in 2027. The brothers, who previously competed in WWE as The Singh Brothers, were announced for PWR’s upcoming event in New Delhi, India, via the promotion’s official X account. They reacted with a post on X reflecting on how their wrestling journey began in the country through Ring Ka King 15 years ago. They described the upcoming appearance as their biggest show in five years. “Our biggest break in wrestling came through India, with Ring Ka King 15 years ago. This will be our biggest show in 5 years in New Delhi, India Everything we’ve worked for, post WWE, comes down to this. Going back to our parents’ home country. Where they immigrated from,” posted The Bollywood Boyz. Last month, Gurv Sihra suffered a collapsed lung during a tag team title match at a Pure Power Wrestling event in Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada. In a recent update shared, he revealed that X-rays showed his lungs had returned to normal, with very little air remaining in his chest cavity. However, he remains unable to fly and is awaiting medical clearance, though he expects to be cleared soon. Following their WWE departure in 2021, the brothers went on to compete for several promotions, including DEFY Wrestling, GCW and AEW. title: Contract News: New TNA signings to be Set soon: Which free agents could sign with the company?
raw_title: New TNA signings to be announced soon: Which free agents could sign with the company?
body: In recent weeks, a number of new faces have joined the TNA Wrestling roster coming out of this year’s Bound for Glory event. Just in the past week, TNA has announced the signings of both Shotzi Blackheart and Shayna Baszler, and per Fightful Select, there are reportedly more set to be announced in the coming weeks. Here are more new signings we could see be announced by TNA soon. Erick Rowan’s second spell in WWE lasted just under two years After their WWE release back in April, Wyatt Sicks members Dexter Lumis and Joe Gacy, now known as Samuel Shaw and Joseph Sawyer, debuted in TNA under the name Syx. The pair were in action against the Hardys at Bound For Glory, with them picking up the win thanks to an appearance from Erick Redbeard (Rowan), who was also sporting Syx merchandise. Following his appearance at Bound For Glory, Redbeard could reunite with his former stablemates in TNA. Sheamus leaves WWE having never captured the Intercontinental Championship after years of chasing After leaving WWE and officially becoming a free agent on October 1, there has been a lot of speculation about where Sheamus may end up next. Ahead of TNA Bound For Glory, Sheamus was reportedly considered for the spot that ultimately went to Max Caster against Moose. With TNA having interest in Sheamus, he would make for a statement signing for the company. While his former Acclaimed teammate Max Caster has already finished up with TNA after debuting at Bound For Glory, Anthony Bowens is also now a free agent following the expiration of his AEW contract. Bowens signing for TNA would be a good move for both parties, as it would allow Bowens to shine as a singles star similar to how Mike Santana did. Among the most shocking releases from WWE back in April were Aleister Black and Zelina Vega, who had just weeks prior been reportedly set for a major role at WrestleMania. Black and Zelina have since made their return to the indies as Tommy End and Xelina, where they will hopefully show their worth to fans around the world. A move to TNA would allow the pair to finally thrive at the top of the card.

title: Comeback Watch: Leon Slater Hopes Six-Sided Ring Returns At TNA Destination X
raw_title: Leon Slater Hopes Six-Sided Ring Returns At TNA Destination X
body: Leon Slater is set to defend the TNA World Title at Destination X, and he hopes the six-sided ring returns for the show. Slater will defend his World Championship against Trey Miguel at the November 15th PPV, which will make the event’s return for the first time since 2017. Slater said during his appearance on I Love Wrestling that Miguel is the “perfect” first challenger for him because of their past battles in the promotion. He also spoke about his excitement for the PPV itself. You can see the highlights below: “I think Trey is a perfect first challenger for me. I’ve said this before and I’ll say it again: Trey has been a sort of measuring stick for me during my time here at TNA. Before I was the X-Division champion, I would always be pitted up against him and the rest of the Rascalz gang. And I would always fail, you know what I mean? I would never win. I would always feel like they were leagues and leagues above me in terms of skill. And again, it was a great learning experience, but I felt like I was never quite at his level. “And as time’s gone on and we’ve run into each other more and more, every time we stepped in the ring I feel myself getting closer and closer and closer. And it may be arrogant and cocky of me to say, but I feel like I’ve surpassed him now. Trey Miguel is an all-time TNA great, especially in the X-Division. But there’s one thing he’s never done, and that is hold the TNA World Title, which I hang around my shoulder right now. So not only am I walking in with a title on my shoulder, I’m also walking in with a little extra chip on my shoulder being that Trey Miguel has been someone I’ve loved to test myself from in the past. And I think he is, like I said, the perfect first person for me to test my World Championship skills against at Destination X.” “I was just praying that the six-sided ring would come back, to be real. And I don’t know if it is, I don’t know if it isn’t. But man, I hope it does because I’m sure like you, growing up a TNA fan, that’s what we loved, right? So to get the chance to compete in a six-sided ring — as much as people said it sucked back in the day, and it’s way harder and it hurts way more than a four-sided ring — and that hurts enough, trust me. I would love the chance to be TNA World Champion and wrestle in a TNA six-sided ring. “So man, I’m super excited for Destination X. I’m super excited to head back to Edmonton, it’s always a super hot crowd there. And you know, the days following in Calgary, I believe, on the 18th and 19th of November. It’s a super exciting time to be a TNA World Champion and it’s a super exciting time to be a TNA wrestling fan.” Leon Slater , TNA Destination X , Trey Miguel , Jeremy Thomas

title: On the Record: Leon Slater Doesn’t Take Representing TNA Lightly, Recalls Reaction To World Title Win
raw_title: Leon Slater Doesn’t Take Representing TNA Lightly, Recalls Reaction To World Title Win
body: Leon Slater recently recalled his immediate reaction to winning the TNA World Championship at TNA Bound For Glory and what holding the title means to him. Slater defeated Nic Nemeth at the PPV earlier this month to become the youngest TNA World Champion of all time. Slater spoke during his interview with I Love Wrestling about what it felt like to win the title and what it means to him to represent the company. You can see the highlights below: “It’s a great feeling, man, it really is. And it’s very difficult to put into words, because it’s something that I had pictured since I was a kid, you know what I mean? Even as a wrestling fan before I had got into wrestling, everybody pictures what it’d be like to win the world title. So when that feeling finally hits, it’s a difficult one to manage. “But the fact that I am the TNA World Champion now means a lot more than just being able to carry this beautiful belt around with me in interviews, and to the ring and stuff like that. It means that I have the trust of management. It means I have the trust of my peers in the locker room. And kind of most importantly it means I have the trust of the audience, that I am the guy that can represent TNA. That when as a TNA fan, if you go like, ‘I watch TNA’ and someone goes, ‘Oh what’s on that show?’ You go, ‘Leon Slater’s on that show.’ “And I’m proud to be that person that represents TNA in 2026. So it’s a great feeling and it’s a feeling that I am very, very proud of. And it’s a feeling that I hold very close to my heart and I don’t take lightly, that’s for sure.”
summary: Leon Slater recently recalled his immediate reaction to winning the TNA World Championship at TNA Bound For Glory and what holding the title means to him. Slater got the win over Nic Nemeth at the PPV earlier this month to become the youngest TNA World Champion of all time.

title: The Dogs Look Back On Chain Match With Bang Bang Gang
raw_title: The Dogs Reflect On Chain Match Against Bang Bang Gang, Didn't Have A Long Time To Work On It
summary_src: At AEW Redemption, the Dogs (David Finlay & Clark Connors) took on the Bang Bang Gang (Jay White & Juice Robinson) in a double chain match. The Dogs won, but the match was not well-received by fans.
body: At AEW Redemption, the Dogs (David Finlay & Clark Connors) took on the Bang Bang Gang (Jay White & Juice Robinson) in a double chain match. Appearing on What Happened When with Tony Schiavone and Conrad Thompson , the duo looked back on the match. Thompson kicked off the conversation by saying it was “brutal” when describing the physicality of the match. Schiavone: “You had a long time to work on it, too, I understand.” Schiavone: “I thought it was a good match. You’re probably thinking, ‘We should’ve done this. We should’ve done that. Maybe we should’ve done something else.'” Finlay: “If you want violence, we’re your guys. We’re good at violence.” Connors: “It’s one of those things where a match like that, sometimes you want to do it differently. You look where you are on the card, you see what else is on the show. We’re old school like that. We don’t want to take away from a deathmatch later on in the show. We wanted to do it our way. We were happy with what we did with it. I took the best bump anyone has ever seen, but no one fucking saw it because they missed the camera cut.” Connors: “I fell off the top rope onto the steel steps. It made Darby look like some jabroni. Beautiful bump.” Schiavone: “That is old school, not wanting to take away from another match on the card.” Finlay: “We kind of approached it with, ‘Let’s use the tools we’ve been given and stick within those parameters. Sometimes that works out, sometimes it makes it a little more difficult or doesn’t feel as rewarding after. ‘Ah, we should’ve been selfish.'” Connors: “It’s also about setting expectations. It’s a double chain match. It’s a blood feud. People come in and they are expecting something. I still feel happy with the product we put out there, but you also think back on stuff, ‘That could’ve been better.’ It’s a learning experience. All fun. Getting hit with a chain is not fun. It sucks, actually. It’s miserable.” The Dogs and Bang Bang Gang are now aligned and using the name The Cut. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: David Finlay and Clark Connors appeared on What Happened When with Tony Schiavone and Conrad Thompson to discuss their double chain match against Jay White and Juice Robinson at AEW Revolution. The duo reflected on the physicality of the bout, their desire not to overshadow a later deathmatch on the card, and Connors noted taking what he felt was an impressive bump that was missed due to a camera cut. They expressed overall satisfaction with how the match turned out.

body: A few days ago, WWE legend Ric Flair suffered a terrifying fall in Tampa, Florida, and was sent to a hospital . TMZ reported that Flair injured his face outside a Wagamama after spending time at the restaurant's bar. According to sources close to TMZ, Flair left his drink and phone behind, crossed the street, and fell. A few hours later, Flair shared a health update on social media, where he talked about his injury and revealed his eye patch as a result of the fall. "Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! Moments after Flair shared his latest health update, the post was filled with well-wishes from Snoop Dogg, his daughter Charlotte Flair, Nikki Bella, and many other celebrities. Later, Flair's daughter and WWE Superstar Charlotte Flair also talked about her father's health. "Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he's going to be ok)," she wrote. Ric Flair, 77, is now out of any immediate danger and is back online on social media.

raw_title: David Finlay Looks Back On NJPW Exit & Choosing AEW Over WWE NXT

body: After spending the majority of his adult life in New Japan Pro Wrestling, David Finlay decided to take his talents west and signed with AEW in March 2026 . The move came after weeks of speculation that he would be heading to WWE, particularly "WWE NXT . However, he would choose to reunite with his old Bullet Club War Dogs, Gabe Kidd and Clark Connors, in All Elite Wrestling. This meant that he would have felt comfortable with either option, but wasn't until his representation presented him with the overall packages that Finlay knew he'd have more freedom in AEW. "Just the overall package of like, obviously pay and schedule, but just like alright, all my friends are in AEW. Then like my brother and dad are in NXT, cool. But yeah, it didn't have any bearing on it, like it would have been cool, but it's like no, I want to go keep doing what I'm doing, have the freedom to do what I want to do and if I can be with my friends, that's a great bonus." There was one other reason he chose AEW over WWE, that being that as a former two-time IWGP Global Heavyweight Champion and someone who has wrestled at the Tokyo Dome eight times, he didn't exactly want to go ack to square one. "I think I would have struggled re-humbling myself to the level that they would have wanted me to humble myself to. It's like I've already been here and I've already proven myself." There was a point in time where David Finlay looked to be the next top foreign heel in NJPW, but after 11 years working his way through New Japan's system, he decided to move back to the United States permanently. The main reason for this was simple, his own family who he feels like is owed some quality time with him after all the years he's been in Japan. "I had a kid," Finlay said. "It sucked, like my wife has been in the picture the entire time I've been in Japan so like we're used to that, no problem. But when like I leave for a G1, come back, and my kid's got 20 new tricks, I'm like 'I've missed so much,' which comes with wrestling...I grew up with my dad being on the road five days a week. I don't feel like I missed out, cool, it would have been great to have him home more, but I don't feel like I missed out. But also if there's an opportunity to be home more, I feel like I owe that to my family." As for as when he knew he wanted to leave NJPW, that revelation came to him almost a year before he actually left. With that said, he also felt like he owed it to his mentor Gedo to give everything he could in his last year with the company. title: NOAH Launches Neo Green Boys Recruitment Tournament
raw_title: Pro Wrestling NOAH Announces Neo Green Boys Recruitment Program & Tournament
summary_src: The Neo Green Boys. Pro Wrestling NOAH announced the Neo Green Boys recruitment program and league. The recruitment program is to bring in aspiring wrestlers, and it will be streamed on NOAH's YouTube channel and other platforms.
body: Pro Wrestling NOAH announced the Neo Green Boys recruitment program and league. The recruitment program is to bring in aspiring wrestlers, and it will be streamed on NOAH’s YouTube channel and other platforms. Below is a quote from Akihiro Takeda, who is the Director of NOAH’s parent company, CyberFight: “Through this audition program, I hope to encourage a wider range of people with diverse personalities to aspire to become professional wrestlers for various reasons. We want to create a situation where wrestlers are already well-known through this program by the time of their debut match. Starting with this event, we would like to create a new recruitment method, separate from general applications and scouted applicants, where they can proceed to an entrance test after going through this audition.” The judges for the program will be Keiji Muto (Great Muta), Naomichi Marufuji, and Kenoh (tentative judge). The final judging will take place in March 2027. Those who make it past the final selection stage will train at the NOAH Dojo. NOAH noted that this does not guarantee their pro in-ring debut. With that, there is the Neo Green Boys League competition for current NOAH rookie wrestlers . The final match is scheduled for NOAH The New Year 2027 on January 1st at Korakuen Hall. The winner will head overseas. The tourney starts on December 5th. The final will consist of the two wrestlers who have the best records in the tournament. Below are the dates and matches:

Akihiro Takeda, director of NOAH's parent company CyberFight, stated that the audition is intended to encourage a wider range of people with diverse personalities to pursue professional wrestling for various reasons. The goal is for participants to become well-known through the program by the time of any potential debut match.

The initiative seeks to establish a new recruitment approach separate from standard applications or scouting, allowing candidates to advance to an entrance test after completing the audition process. Judges for the program include Keiji Muto, Naomichi Marufuji, and Kenoh as a tentative judge.

Final judging for the recruitment program is set for March 2027. Successful candidates who pass the final selection will train at the NOAH Dojo, though this does not ensure a professional in-ring debut.

In conjunction with the recruitment effort, NOAH is holding the Neo Green Boys League for current rookie wrestlers. The tournament begins on December 5th and concludes with a final match on January 1st at Korakuen Hall during NOAH The New Year 2027.
The league final will feature the two wrestlers with the best records from the tournament. The winner is scheduled to head overseas.

body: Larger-than-life stars such as Hulk Hogan, Ric Flair, Bruno Sammartino, The Undertaker, Bret Hart, Shawn Michaels, The Rock, and "Stone Cold" Steve Austin are popular answers, and rightfully so. They are, after all, some of the most important contributors to the industry's long and illustrious history. Who are the Superstars deserving of a spot on the modern era of WWE and AEW's Mount Rushmore? Let's take a look, with each star determined based on their historical significance and the quality of their work. AEW has only been in existence since 2019, making it far easier to compile a foursome of the most important and deserving stars in company history. Omega was one of the faces of pro wrestling globally at the start of AEW and a guy without whom it would have been far more difficult to get the project off the ground. He had credibility amongst fans, regardless of where their allegiances lay, and he was arguably the best wrestler in the world at the start of his run there. That he became a creative centerpiece, won two world titles, battled a serious health issue to come back, and still delivered an instant classic against Will Ospreay at All In 2026 certainly does not hurt his case for inclusion. Debuting on night one at AEW Double or Nothing in Las Vegas, Moxley wasted little time becoming the heart and soul of the company. One of the most decorated and respected stars on the roster, Moxley has become the "ace" of AEW, the promotion's standard-bearer and tone-setter. Like him and his style of wrestling or not, no one can downplay his importance to the company and his success since emerging from the stands in the MGM Grand Garden Arena seven years ago. From the moment he first set foot in an AEW ring, it was clear that MJF was going to be the company's first homegrown star to capture a world title. His work belonged in the 1980s NWA; his promo skills would have been right at home in the Attitude Era, and his willingness to get heat at any cost reminded some of the territory days. The total package: he was a breakout star from day one, and he was positioned as such, working with Cody Rhodes, Chris Jericho, Hangman Page, and Jon Moxley in relatively short order. Throw in one of the best rivalries in company history with CM Punk, and one of the biggest business-driving programs with Adam Cole, and you have someone synonymous with the company and its growth and evolution. He moves to the beat of a drummer that may not be on planet Earth, shows no fear in any aspect of his game, and has won nearly every championship that he can in AEW. title: Stu Grayson Discusses Explosive Canadian Style With Josh Alexander
raw_title: Stu Grayson Reflects On Recent MLP Matchup With Josh Alexander, Wrestling An Explosive 'Canadian Wrestling' Style Match
summary_src: Stu Grayson reflects on his recent Maple Leaf Pro match with Josh Alexander and how they wrestled an explosive Canadian style.
body: Stu Grayson reflects on his recent Maple Leaf Pro match with Josh Alexander and how they wrestled an explosive Canadian style. At Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling Northern Rising on October 3rd, Grayson and Alexander would face off in a Canadian Championship unification match, with Alexander walking away with the victory. While speaking to Fightful Overbooked’s In The Weeds in a new interview , Stu Grasyon reflected on the match with Alexander. “Listen, Josh and I, the last time we wrestled each other, I think it was 2018 in Montreal, and, we had a really, really good time. We always matched up really well. We are both huge- I don’t know how to say that we we’re both classic Canadian pro wrestlers. So what we like to do is what I now call the new style of Canadian pro wrestling, the explosive Canadian technical style, which is yes. We wrestle the way of the new age of pro wrestling, more innovative and so on. But Canadian pro wrestling has always been about being technically sound, but we are more explosive more than ever. So if you look at guys like myself with all the power moves that I do, the high flying, Josh Alexander with the striking, the technical, guys like Speedball and Kenny, whether it’s the high flying, the striking, we’re very, very explosive. So our styles works really well, because we kind of do the same thing, but the foundation is the same. But then we both went on to do our own things in a different way. So our style has always worked really well against each other. So wrestling Josh Alexander is always so much fun. The match itself was extremely physical, and we told each other, we are going out there and fucking brace yourself. You know, I’m coming in, know you’re doing the same thing. We’re gonna push and see how far we can get this, and, uh, it was almost- let’s test each other and let’s see which one of us can actually keep on going, and, uh, that’s what we did. That’s how I like to wrestle, and I know that Josh needed to show that he could do it because he just came back from a knee injury, and he didn’t get as much in the ring time as he would have wanted because he’s like me. We want to be in the ring almost every day. You know what I mean? When you don’t get to do that and you have something huge coming up, you feel like, oh, I have something to prove, and it’s not even to anyone. It’s to yourself. I am just as good as I was before the injury or whatever break I needed to take, and I was the perfect guy for him to test himself against. So we had a blast. Once it was all said and done, honestly, I drove home, Toronto, to Ottawa. It was about a five-hour drive. Listening to music, had a good time, went to bed, slept really well. I woke up in the morning. My pillow was covered with blood because of the screwdriver. I had three big-ass holes in my head. But otherwise, it was good.”

title: Stephanie Vaquer Calls Out Fans Expecting Free Personalized Videos
raw_title: Stephanie Vaquer Calls Out Fans Expecting Free Personalized Videos
summary_src: Stephanie Vaquer is calling attention to something that apparently happens more often than people realize — people getting access to private phone numbers and then expecting personalized videos for free.
body: The fan admitted they didn’t know each other and claimed that a producer had passed along the contact information. “No, buddy, I’m a fan of yours. A producer from here gave me your contact information. Can you help me out with the shoutout?” The person eventually agreed to help, but the screenshot included another message showing just how awkward the request was. “I don’t know whether to tell him to f*** off or laugh… I’d rather just laugh…” Vaquer used that exchange to make a bigger point about personalized videos. She explained that people often assume recording one quick message costs nothing, without realizing how much time performers can actually spend making them. “It’s funny, but people don’t realize that sometimes we spend six or seven hours recording videos. That’s basically an entire day every week, and everyone thinks, ‘Making one video doesn’t cost you anything.’” For Vaquer, this isn’t simply about whether she feels like doing someone a favor. She explained that these videos are part of her job and are paid, regulated work. “Guys, this is part of my job. I’m not trying to be rude, but some people need to understand that, in my case, this is paid work and it’s regulated.” Vaquer also can’t necessarily record whatever someone asks for whenever she wants. She said using her image requires permission, making these seemingly simple requests more complicated than fans might realize. “To make a video, I have to use my image, and for that, I need to ask for permission, which isn’t easy. That’s it.” Vaquer’s point was ultimately bigger than the example she shared. Personalized videos can represent hours of actual work, and she’s making it clear that people shouldn’t expect performers to hand that work out for free simply because they’ve managed to get someone’s contact information. title: Contract News: Major Latest On Max Caster After TNA Departure
raw_title: Major Update on Max Caster After TNA Departure
body: 0 Max Caster’s TNA Wrestling departure has led to new backstage details. The former AEW star was released after Bound For Glory. Now, a report has revealed more about his original plans. Caster made his TNA debut at Bound For Glory. He faced Moose in an open-challenge match but lost. His appearance ultimately became a one-time outing with the company. Caster delivered a freestyle rap during his entrance. One line referenced the recent attack in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The reference sparked controversy because of the timing. TNA subsequently cut ties with Caster following the incident. Reports had suggested he would appear at additional tapings. TNA President Carlos Silva personally made the decision to fire Caster. He reportedly worked on a per-appearance deal rather than a long-term contract. TNA also reportedly did not know what he planned to say in his freestyle before the show. According to Fightful Select , Caster was initially booked for Bound For Glory only. However, the company later added him to its Dothan, Alabama tapings. “Max Caster was originally only set to work TNA Bound for Glory, but was then added to the Dothan, Alabama tapings. The shows had to be rewritten after he was taken off those shows.” The report confirms that Caster had been scheduled for more appearances. His removal forced TNA to make changes to its taping plans. Following the controversy, Caster announced an extended break from wrestling. His future plans remain unclear at this time. The post Major Update on Max Caster After TNA Departure appeared first on Wrestlezone .

body: Night three of NJPW Super Junior Tag League 2026 saw Mistico & Masatora Yasuda pick up their first victory of the tournament. Mistico & Desperado — the current IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Champions — were expected to be one of the top duos in the tournament. Instead, Mistico has been paired with a Young Lion and suffered defeats in their first two matches. Their luck changed on Monday with Mistico & Yasuda defeating Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X on night three. A Block now has three teams with 2-1 records and three at 1-2. Things are similarly close in B Block, though Titan & Daiki Nagai are now the only winless team in the tournament. Next up is an event in Ibaraki on Tuesday (October 27) with three A Block matches. It’s a fast-moving tournament with only four shows remaining before the finals are held at Power Struggle on November 3. The winning team should be in line for an IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team title shot, but we’ll have to see how the situation with the belts plays out with Desperado injured. title: TNA Impact Viewership Jumps To Two-Month High
raw_title: TNA Impact Viewership & Ratings Report: 10/15/2026
summary_src: The post-Bound for Glory episode of TNA Impact saw a significant increase in viewership, reaching a two-month high, while ratings also improved.
body: TNA Wrestling The post-Bound for Glory episode of " TNA Impact " saw a significant increase in viewership and ratings, with viewership reaching a two-month high. The October 15 episode of "Impact," which took place in Dothan, Alabama, saw a huge jump in average viewership, rising from 214,000 the previous week to 252,000, as per " Wrestlenomics ." The episode drew its highest viewership in nearly three months, with the previous high recorded on the July 23 episode, which averaged 307,000 viewers. The episode's viewership was also 24% higher than the four-week average. It was good news for TNA even in the 18-49 key demographic ratings, as it rose from 0.03 for the Bound for Glory go-home show of " Impact " to 0.05. That rating matches the highest "Impact" has recorded since the aforementioned July 23 episode, which also drew a 0.05 rating. The October 15 episode's rating was also 0.02 points higher than the four-week average. The October 15 episode of "Impact" saw the Hardys serve as the show's storyline bookers, with the duo interacting with new X-Division Champion Amazing Red and new TNA World Champion Leon Slater, who learned the identity of his next opponent during the show. That turned out to be Trey Miguel, who won a five-way #1 Contenders Ladder match. The episode also saw the Hardys defeat AJ Francis and Expressions in a tag team match, while former world champion Nic Nemeth picked up a win over his brother, Ryan Nemeth.

The show, which took place in Dothan, Alabama, also improved in the key 18-49 demographic, rising from a 0.03 to a 0.05 rating that ties its best mark since July 23. The episode featured The Hardys acting as storyline bookers and interacting with new X-Division Champion Amazing Red.

body: 0 Former TNA World Champion Eric Young has reportedly returned to WWE. However, he is currently working behind the scenes. A new report has revealed his role with NXT. According to PWInsider’s Mike Johnson , Eric Young is working as an NXT producer. He reportedly began working with the company in July 2026. Johnson shared the update during an online Q&A session. He was asked about the former TNA World Heavyweight Champion’s whereabouts. He wrote, “That was the assumption for a lot of people when Young asked for and received his TNA release, and it was correct. He started working for WWE as a Producer for NXT in July. I don’t know if he will wrestle.” The report confirms Young’s backstage role with NXT. However, his future as an in-ring performer remains uncertain. Young first joined TNA in 2004 after spending years with the company before joining WWE in 2016. WWE released Young during its roster cuts in April 2020. The cuts happened during the COVID-19 pandemic. He later re-signed with WWE in 2022 but didn’t appear on television. Young eventually returned to TNA and continued wrestling there. A few months ago, he requested his release from the promotion. His departure sparked speculation about another WWE return. WWE has also made no official announcement about his in-ring future. For now, Young appears to be helping NXT backstage. Fans will have to wait for further updates about his future. body: Sol Ruca is one of the newer talents on the main roster, and hasn’t been in the wrestling business long as she got started at the Performance Center in NXT in 2022. Though she might not have as much experience as others, she’s already won championships and competed on high-level PLEs. Her first title on the main roster was the WWE Intercontinental Championship, which she captured by defeating Becky Lynch, regarded as one of the greatest female wrestlers in WWE history. Speaking to Korey Smith & Tor Smith on KRON4 , Sol was asked what she learned from working with Becky. “She is one of the greatest of all time for a reason. She is so good at what she does and the character work. I’ve learned a lot from her, especially in the character aspect of it. Seeing how her brain works, seeing how she’s able to take these promos and segments and make it her own and know what the fans are going to bite on and enjoy. Being able to turn nothing into something. She’s really good at that. She’s really good at questioning creative and trying to make everything the best that it can be. I definitely learned to be able to stick up for myself a little bit when I disagree with certain things. She’s really good at doing that in a respectful way and being able to perform at the best of her ability and giving the fans what they want,” she said. Solva has yet to compete on TV since WWE Money in the Bank when she was part of the women’s Money in the Bank ladder match. Lynch will take on Stephanie Vaquer on Monday’s WWE Raw. title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Shares Health Update After Nasty Fall & Blood Clot Diagnosis
raw_title: WWE Legend Ric Flair Shares Health Update After Nasty Fall & Blood Clot Diagnosis
body: WWE legend Ric Flair has given fans a health update after being diagnosed with a blood clot and taking a nasty fall outside a restaurant in Florida. The 77-year-old ex-wrestler, who used to go by the nickname Nature Boy, shared an update on Instagram from his hospital bed, posting a photo of himself wrapped in a blanket with an eye patch taped over his right eye. According to TMZ , Flair had been at a restaurant in Tampa on October 23 before walking outside and taking a sudden, hard fall in the street. He sustained deep cuts to his head and eye, prompting medics to rush him in an ambulance to Tampa General Hospital, where he was treated until the early morning hours for potential concussion concerns. Despite the ordeal, Flair seemed in good spirits on his update, publicly thanking the hospital staff and promising to personally reply to fans’ well-wishes as he regains his strength. According to reports , the former wrestler wasn’t about to let a trip to the ER slow him down as patrons spotted Flair back at his usual neighborhood bar the very same evening he was released. The visit came just hours after Flair was forced to pull out of a scheduled convention appearance in Seattle. At the time, the 16-time world champion revealed he was dealing with a dangerous blood clot in his leg, which doctors warned made long distance flying impossible. Amid the initial wave of worry, supporters received welcome reassurance from Flair’s daughter, WWE superstar Charlotte Flair , who shared an update on her own X account to let followers know about her father’s health. “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…,” she wrote in the caption. “(ps: he’s going to be ok.)” Across both posts, fans, celebrities, and those in the wrestling community expressed their support for Nature Boy. Snoop Dogg commented, “Love u Rick,” while Killer Mike of Run the Jewels wrote: “Heal Up, Champ! Woooooooo.” WWE referee Charles Robinson wrote: “Get well Champ. Love you.” Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head… Flair also used his social media statement to address and apologize for “reckless posting behavior” on his official Facebook page while he was hospitalized. Clarifying that he no longer owns the account, he slammed the unauthorized video posts uploaded during his medical emergency as “completely inappropriate.” The confusion stems from an ongoing legal dispute in which Flair previously filed a $10 million lawsuit against a digital talent agency , which he accuses of seizing control of his official social assets and monetizing his legacy without consent. As Flair focuses on his recovery, the wrestling community continues to rally behind one of the most decorated champions in history.
summary: WWE legend Ric Flair has given the audience a health update after being diagnosed with a blood clot and taking a nasty fall outside a restaurant in Florida. Per TMZ , Flair had been at a restaurant in Tampa on October 23 before walking outside and taking a sudden, hard fall in the street.

title: Kevin Nash Praises Roman Reigns vs LA Knight At MITB
raw_title: WWE HOFer Kevin Nash Thinks MITB Title Match Made A Statement
summary_src: WWE legend Kevin Nash has praised the clash between LA Knight and Roman Reigns at Money in the Bank and explained why Reigns retained the title.
body: WWE Roman Reigns retained the WWE World Heavyweight title against LA Knight at Money in the Bank , a match Kevin Nash believes set a standard for the night. The match opened the show at the PLE , where the duo put on a showing that took fans through a series of emotions. Nash said on " Kliq This " that he enjoyed it despite being convinced beforehand that Reigns wouldn't lose. "I knew he wasn't going to lose," began Nash. "It was the opening match. It was kind of a 'follow that' motherf***ers match. You know, they had a great match. I thought LA Knight was great. I thought Roman was great. I thought there was some great false finishes." Nash pointed out one factor outside the pro wrestling ring that could have convinced WWE's creative team to keep the title on Roman Reigns: the "Street Fighter" movie. The WWE Hall of Famer argued that the creative team would have wanted Reigns, who played Akuma in the movie, to appear on the red carpet still holding the world championship. "So, it's like, do you put this movie out, which they're hoping does huge, huge numbers; it's Street Fighter, you've got Roman as one of the featured guys. And do you want the water cooler jargon to be, 'Hey, that guy is so-and-so in the movie. You know, he used to be the WWE champion up until Saturday when he got beat.' Or do you just say, 'Hey, man, that's the WWE champion.' Like, this is one of those moments in life where we don't get these moments as pro wrestlers very often — to be on a red carpet and to be a star and to be our champion," wondered Nash. Reigns seems to have moved on from Knight, with him and the rest of the Bloodline feuding with 946 as the two groups seem to be set to battle it out at Survivor Series.
summary: WWE Hall of Famer Kevin Nash called Roman Reigns' successful defense of the World Heavyweight Championship against LA Knight the opening match of Money in the Bank. Nash said on his "Kliq This" podcast that the bout featured strong performances from both men along with multiple false finishes and set a high bar for the rest of the premium live event. He added that the upcoming "Street Fighter" movie, in which Reigns appears as Akuma, likely influenced the decision to keep the title on Reigns for the red carpet appearances.

title: Cody Rhodes Calls WrestleMania 40 Night Two Peak Art
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Weighs In On Singles Match With The Rock, WrestleMania 40 As ‘Peak Wrestling’
body: Cody Rhodes has spoken about whether he will ever go one-on-one with The Rock following their WrestleMania 40 feud. Rhodes and the Final Boss feuded in the leadup to WrestleMania 40 and battled in a tag team match on night one before Rhodes ultimately won the title from Roman Reigns on night two. They also had a semi-feud in the leadup to WrestleMania 41 when Rock famously asked for Rhodes’ “soul,” which facilitated John Cena’s heel turn. The WWE star was asked on Insight With Chris Van Vliet , if there he was ever going to have a singles match with The Rock, and spoke about whether it will ever happen. He also reflected on whether night two of WrestleMania 40 was “peak wrestling,” as Van Vliet put it. You can see the highlights below: “To me, wrestling is never a dirty word for me, right? But I’d actually say it’s peak art, and I tell people all the time who misunderstand wrestling and think, oh, there’s goofiness to what we do. There’s a lot of goofiness to what we do. There is, and some nights it’s what you think. Then other nights, it’s better than any other story you might have ever seen, and I’m not saying that was, but I know when you’re in one of those moments, and there have been so many significant moments throughout history, and they’re not always loaded with drama. Just think about Steve spraying the beer. Think about Hogan slamming Andre, like that. Those moments, they rise to the highest points of- I’m using the word I never thought I’d use, art. It’s one of the reasons all the great wrestlers that I grew up loving were big-time film buffs. This is their way of telling stories, and this is their canvas-the squared circle, the ring. But you name it. Somebody who is a big film buff or a huge music fan, and not that everyone isn’t, but even on a deeper connective level, how do I put this together? How do I entertain?” “Oof. It’s not that I’m evading that answer. It’s that I don’t really know how to answer because I think personally he has a couple of matches probably left to do. I think that personally, but I also know looking at WrestleMania 40 and another guy who he’s given all, continues to give all as part of the board. He could easily say that was a great final piece as a performer in a wrestling ring. That’ll be up to him. That’ll certainly be up to him if there’s more and what those matches might be. I don’t think any wrestler would ever look you in the eye and tell you they wouldn’t want a match like that.” Cody Rhodes , The Rock (Dwayne Johnson) , Wrestlemania 40 , Jeremy Thomas

title: Former WCW and WWF Wrestler Jumbo Baretta Passes Away at 59
raw_title: Former WCW and WWF Wrestler Jumbo Baretta Passes Away at 59
summary_src: The wrestling world has lost another veteran, as Julio Barrera, better known to fans as Jumbo Baretta, has passed away at the age of 59. Baretta spent nearly three decades in professional wrestling, competing for WCW, WWF, and several NWA territories while also making a name for himself in Japan.
body: Baretta spent nearly three decades in professional wrestling, competing for WCW, WWF, and several NWA territories while also making a name for himself in Japan. His career took him into the ring with some of wrestling’s biggest names, including Sting, The Road Warriors, and several Japanese legends. The Cauliflower Alley Club announced Baretta’s passing , sharing a personal tribute from someone who had known the former wrestler for nearly 40 years. This one truly hurts. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Jumbo, a good friend whom I was honored and privileged to know for nearly 40 years. I send my sincerest condolences to his family and friends. Rest in peace old friend.” Born in Tampa, Florida, in 1967, Baretta began his professional wrestling career in 1986 after training under Boris Malenko, the father of wrestling veterans Dean and Joe Malenko. Standing 6-foot-5 and weighing more than 300 pounds, Baretta had the size to stand out in an era filled with larger-than-life wrestlers. Baretta got his start in the Florida wrestling scene, working for Championship Wrestling from Florida and other regional promotions. One of his biggest accomplishments came on October 17, 1989, when he teamed with Dennis Knight to defeat The Nasty Boys, Brian Knobbs and Jerry Sags, for the Florida Tag Team Championship. The pair held the titles until November 12, 1989, when they lost to Mark Starr and Lou Perez. His career also included appearances for Jim Crockett Promotions and WCW between 1989 and 1990. During that period, Baretta shared the ring with Sting, Tommy Rich, The Rock ‘n’ Roll Express, and The Road Warriors. Although he never became a major television star, he worked against several of the biggest names in the business during that era. Baretta also took his career overseas, where he competed under the name Johnny Barrett. Beginning in 1989, he worked for Japan’s Universal Wrestling Federation, a promotion known for its realistic, submission-heavy wrestling style. His opponents included Nobuhiko Takada, Akira Maeda, and Minoru Suzuki. After the Japanese UWF closed, Baretta continued competing overseas. In 1991, he joined Pro Wrestling Fujiwara Gumi, where he faced Yoshiaki Fujiwara and Masakatsu Funaki. His Japanese appearances continued into 1992, giving him experience in a wrestling environment very different from the American territorial system. Baretta eventually returned to the United States, making several WWF appearances in 1995. He also remained active on the Florida independent circuit, wrestling for promotions including the Professional Wrestling Federation, Global Wrestling Alliance, Suncoast Pro Wrestling, and International Championship Wrestling Alliance. His connection to the Malenko family remained an important part of his career. In addition to training under Boris Malenko, Baretta worked as an assistant trainer at Malenko’s wrestling school. In June 2010, he won the inaugural Malenko Cup Battle Royal in Riverview, Florida. Baretta cont

title: WWE’s Growing Presence in India Comes as Country Cracks Down on Online Gambling
raw_title: WWE’s Growing Presence in India Comes as Country Cracks Down on Online Gambling
summary_src: WWE is expanding its presence in India through Netflix, but another part of the country’s digital entertainment industry is facing a major crackdown.
body: WWE’s push into the Indian market took a major step forward when Ringside News reported in December 2024 that the company would move its programming from Sony Pictures Networks India to Netflix. That transition officially took place on April 1, 2025, ending a broadcasting relationship that had lasted more than two decades. In March 2025, WWE President Nick Khan confirmed that the company was considering bringing a major Premium Live Event to India . Speaking about the company’s discussions with Netflix, Khan revealed that India was one of the first markets identified as a priority. Khan also explained how closely WWE’s international plans were connected to Netflix’s priorities. “At the top of that list was India. If it’s important to Netflix, assume it’s important to us.” WWE continued promoting its presence in the country when Liv Morgan and Dominik Mysterio traveled to Mumbai in April 2025. As Ringside News previously covered , the two Superstars took part in a Bollywood-inspired promotional photoshoot to celebrate WWE’s arrival on Netflix India. However, while WWE was expanding its streaming business, the Indian government was preparing significant restrictions on another form of online entertainment. India enacted the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act in August 2025. The legislation, which took effect alongside implementing rules on May 1, 2026, established nationwide restrictions on online money gaming, including games involving financial stakes and the expectation of monetary winnings. The law covers games based on skill, chance, or a combination of both. It also prohibits advertising and promoting prohibited online money games, while restricting financial transactions connected to those services. The crackdown has particular significance for the online gambling industry, including websites and operators associated with crypto casinos in India . Cryptocurrency-based gambling does not automatically fall outside the restrictions simply because digital assets are used instead of traditional currency. According to the Indian government’s explanation of the regulations , the restrictions are designed to address financial harm and other risks associated with online money gaming while supporting permitted social games and esports. That creates a significant difference between WWE’s streaming expansion and the challenges facing real-money gaming businesses. Netflix operates as a subscription entertainment service, providing access to WWE programming alongside movies, television series, and other content. Online casino operators, however, face restrictions when their services involve users staking money or money-equivalent assets in the expectation of financial returns. The distinction is especially important as India’s government has also targeted the advertising and promotion of prohibited online money games. title: Cody Rhodes Says Jason Momoa Has Tools To Be WWE Star
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Thinks 'Aquaman' Star Would Make Good WWE Superstar
summary_src: Former WWE Champion Cody Rhodes has named a fellow member of the Street Fighter cast whom he feels would be a good fit for WWE.
body: Cody Rhodes believes that actor and fellow Street Fighter star Jason Momoa could one day be a part of WWE. Momoa, who is an acclaimed actor, has drawn some comparisons with Roman Reigns, Rhodes' former rival, something that Reigns acknowledged too . Rhodes, in an appearance on ESPN's " The Rich Eisen Show ," confidently said Momoa has the "tools" to be a WWE Superstar while also detailing his strategy for bringing in actors when he's on set. "It would be amazing [if Momoa joined WWE], and he's got all the tools for it already," Rhodes began. "I think I try to slowly, with everybody in the production [of Street Fighter], explain how we're very open [to collaborating in WWE]. We love to have guests. We love to try a celebrity moment. We love to promote the things that our boys and girls are in. So throughout the course of the deal, it was fun to explain to a whole different bubble, I'm in the wrestling bubble, what I do. That's an open invite." Rhodes went on to say some stars in the Street Fighter movie would be a great fit for WWE, including bodybuilder and actor Olivier Richters, who played Zangief. Rhodes noted that the 7'2" actor would easily fit into WWE and joked that he would be willing to slam him, a la Hulk Hogan slamming Andre the Giant. "There's some wrestlers in the cast. They may not know they're wrestlers, you know, like Olivier, the Dutch giant who plays Zangief, is seven foot. Who knows? I think he's the biggest actor. That's a no-brainer. Get him out," said the former world champion. "You don't have to do anything. People run into you. Maybe one guy slams you, maybe it's me, right?" He hopes many actors, including those he worked with on the film, will switch to WWE sometime in the future.
summary: Cody Rhodes told ESPN's The Rich Eisen Show that Jason Momoa possesses all the tools needed to succeed as a WWE Superstar. Rhodes explained his approach of gradually introducing the WWE world to actors on the Street Fighter set and extending an open invitation for collaborations, celebrity appearances and cross-promotion. He added that several other stars from the film, including Olivier Richters, would also be great fits for WWE.
