title: WWE Extra Never Invited Back After Trying to Get Photo With The Undertaker
raw_title: WWE Extra Never Invited Back After Trying to Get Photo With The Undertaker
summary_src: One WWE extra apparently ruined their chances of getting another opportunity with the company, all because they wanted a picture with The Undertaker. What seemed like an innocent attempt to meet a wrestling legend turned into a costly mistake, as the person was never invited back to work for WWE.
body: Former WWE Superstar James Ellsworth revealed the story during a recent interview Developmentally Speaking , where he discussed his early days working as an extra before landing a full-time WWE contract in 2016. Ellsworth explained that being backstage for the first time could be overwhelming, especially when names like Vince McMahon, Triple H, Stephanie McMahon, and The Undertaker were walking around like it was just another day at the office. Ellsworth said he was lucky to have spent years wrestling on the independent scene before getting backstage at WWE. That experience helped him keep his cool around major stars, something he believes younger wrestlers might struggle with. He then brought up someone who apparently couldn’t resist trying to get a picture with The Undertaker. “The first time I went up there I took it all in. I was like, this is cool, but after that again I was, you know, mentally prepared for it. Thank God I didn’t go when I was younger cuz I knew how to keep my cool and not, you know, like, ‘Oh my God, it’s The Undertaker. I need to get a picture,’ or anything stupid like that, which it’s funny somebody did that. That’s why I say it.” That person apparently never got another shot at working backstage for WWE. Ellsworth made it clear that extras weren’t supposed to treat the workplace like a meet-and-greet, and asking major stars for pictures could have consequences. “You know, they were never invited. They were never invited back again. And, you know, those things like you don’t want to go there and be like, ‘Wow, it’s The Rock. I got to get a picture.’ Or you’re just an extra. They’re going to, you know, tell you here’s the door.” Ellsworth didn’t name the person involved or reveal when the incident took place. He also didn’t say whether The Undertaker had any issue with the photo request or who decided not to bring the extra back. The only detail he provided was that someone tried to get a picture and never received another invitation. It’s a tough way to lose an opportunity, especially considering how many independent wrestlers hope that one WWE appearance might lead to something bigger. Extras are often brought in to play security guards, stand in the background, or take a beating in a quick television match. But those appearances can also be a wrestler’s first chance to make an impression on WWE officials. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.

He additionally didn’t say whether The Undertaker had any issue with the photo request or who decided not to bring the extra back.

title: Comeback Watch: Former WWE Star Open to Returning After Eight Years Away
raw_title: Former WWE Star Open to Returning After Eight Years Away
summary_src: James Ellsworth believes his WWE story might not be completely over, even though it’s been years since he was a regular part of the company.
body: Speaking with Developmentally Speaking , Ellsworth was asked whether he knew his WWE contract was coming to an end and if there had been any discussions about keeping him around. He explained that his departure was actually a little strange because WWE first released him in November 2017 before bringing him back several months later in 2018. “Well, it was weird how it happened. Like, in November 2017, they let me go, but then they brought me back a couple of months later. So they never stopped paying me. I was getting paid that whole time. So when the contract was actually up, it was right around when they had Paige fire me, and I was like, ‘Oh, I guess that’s it.’” Ellsworth has his own theory about why WWE never kept him around permanently. Unlike wrestlers coming through NXT, WWE hadn’t spent years developing him before suddenly putting him on the main roster. “But again, it goes back to they have time and money invested in people from NXT. It’s a system. They have to keep bringing people up. So when they bring people up, it’s television. You only have so much time. People have to go. There’s people that have to go.” That’s why Ellsworth believes WWE probably never looked at him as somebody who absolutely needed to remain on television every week. Instead, he thinks the company sees him as a recognizable character who can disappear for years and still get a reaction whenever he randomly shows up again. “So I’m a guy like, ‘This ain’t really our guy. This is a character we could bring back every five or ten years, and people will remember it.’ You know, I’m like The Boogeyman or something. They could bring it back whenever, and people react to it. So I feel like that’s how they look at me, you know, and probably always have.” That doesn’t mean Ellsworth thinks his only option is showing up for the occasional nostalgia appearance. He still believes there was a role WWE could have kept him in permanently, especially after his run alongside Carmella showed what he could do without needing to be the wrestler everyone was supposed to take seriously. “Do I think I could have stayed on there and been like a manager like I was with Carmella? They call it a heater in the business, and done that forever? Yes.” Ellsworth believes that role could still work today. He’s confident he could return as somebody’s manager, handle the talking and help get another wrestler over without needing the spotlight himself. “I think I could still go there and do that and be somebody’s manager or a heater, whatever they want to call it, talk for somebody and put them over. I think I could do that for the rest of my life. But it’s not up to me. It’s up to them.” Whether WWE ever actually makes that call remains to be seen, but Ellsworth certainly isn’t closing the door himself. title: Jeff Cobb Found WWE Face Paint More Annoying Than Lucha Mask
raw_title: Jeff Cobb Says He Was Told 'He Was Going To Wear Paint Like You Did In Japan' In WWE
summary_src: Jeff Cobb discusses the differences between wearing paint in WWE as JC Mateo and wearing a mask in Lucha Underground. During Cobb's time in WWE, he would feature as part of the MFT faction alongside the likes of Tama Tonga, Talla Tonga and more.
body: Jeff Cobb discusses the differences between wearing paint in WWE as JC Mateo and wearing a mask in Lucha Underground. During Cobb’s time in WWE, he would feature as part of the MFT faction alongside the likes of Tama Tonga, Talla Tonga and more. During his time in the faction, he, along with his fellow faction mates, would wrestle under face paint. While speaking to SOTO619 in a new interview , Jeff Cobb was asked about which was more annoying to wrestle under, face paint or a mask. Cobb would note the paint was more annoying, also noting that he was told ‘he was going to wear paint like you did in Japan.’ “Paint. Because I’ve never done that before. Although, to be fair, I’ve never done the mask thing before. But the paint was truly different. Because I was told, you’re going to wear the paint like you did in Japan, and I never wore paint in Japan. I think they got me confused with somebody else. But yeah, paint was hard because I had to find paint. But, yeah, the paint was definitely the hardest just for the fact that, like, with the mask, I could put it on. I couldn’t breathe, but I could put it on, and then when I’m done, I could take it off. But the paint took forever to get off. I had to use the wipes. Then I found out the wipes that I used got recalled.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Jeff Cobb revealed that wearing face paint as part of the MFT faction in WWE was more difficult than wrestling in a mask during his Lucha Underground run. He explained that he had never worn paint before and was told he would wear it like he did in Japan, though he never did so there and believes the company confused him with another wrestler. Cobb noted the paint required extra effort to obtain and apply compared to simply putting on a mask.

llm_long: Jeff Cobb said that wearing face paint during his WWE stint was more annoying than wrestling in a mask for Lucha Underground. Cobb was part of the MFT faction in WWE alongside Tama Tonga and Talla Tonga, where the group competed while wearing face paint.

In a new interview with SOTO619, Cobb was asked to compare the two experiences and stated that the paint proved more difficult. He explained that he had never worn paint before, although he had also never worn a mask prior to Lucha Underground.

Cobb revealed that WWE officials instructed him to wear the paint like he had in Japan, but noted they had confused him with another wrestler since he never wore paint there. The paint required him to locate the right product and took a long time to remove using wipes, which he later discovered had been recalled.
In contrast, Cobb said the mask could simply be put on and taken off after the match, even though breathing was difficult while wearing it.

title: Buddy Matthews Pulls Out of WSW MegaMania Tour
raw_title: AEW’s Buddy Matthews off indie tour due to ‘scheduling conflicts’
summary_src: Buddy Matthews’ return to the ring won’t be happening on World Series Wrestling’s MegaMania tour.
body: Buddy Matthews’ return to the ring won’t be happening on World Series Wrestling’s MegaMania tour. It was first announced in May that Matthews would be returning home to Australia for the October-November indie tour, but World Series Wrestling has revealed that he is no longer able to make it due to “scheduling conflicts.” Though disappointed that Matthews won’t be on the shows, WSW said they completely understand that schedules can change. They hope to have Matthews on another tour in the future. The announcement didn’t state if the scheduling conflict is personal or professional in nature. Matthews is signed to AEW but has not wrestled since February 2025 due to an ankle injury that ultimately required surgery. In July of this year, Matthews started to hint that he was cleared to return to the ring. The MegaMania tour begins on October 29 and runs through November 2. Matthews made a surprise appearance for WSW in May to set up his now-canceled appearance on the events. AEW is in St. Louis, Missouri this Wednesday (October 28) for its Halloween-themed Fright Night Dynamite episode. This Saturday’s Collision episode is also being taped that night. Emanuel appeared on Fox News on October 22 and was asked about TKO’s various events scheduled for in the Gulf States. “Right now, everything is still set. This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have in the middle of November a Frieze art show. So far so good. Nothing’s been cancelled,” he replied. “We have a whole team kind of working on this, and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” The United States Department of State has previously issued multiple alerts for Americans in the region, including a recent message that warned of potential attacks on airports following attacks on airspaces by Iran-supported Houthis. The U.S. government also recently ordered a partial evacuation of the embassy in Saudi Arabia of for non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members. Cauliflower Alley Club confirmed the news of his passing in a social media post. “Rest in Peace, My Friend Jumbo Beretta. This one truly hurts. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Jumbo, a good friend whom I was honored and privileged to know for nearly 40 years. I send my sincerest condolences to his family and friends. Rest in peace old friend,” Cauliflower Alley Club posted. Beretta’s wrestling career kicked off in 1986 where he was mentored by Boris Malenko. He competed in Championship Wrestling, World Wrestling Council and NWA among other promotions. Around 1989, he competed in WCW where he faced the likes of Sting, The Rock ‘n’ Roll Express and The Road Warriors. By 1995, Beretta had also competed in a handful of matches for WWE. title: On the Record: James Ellsworth Opens Up On WWE Had No Creative Plans for Him After Vince McMahon Hired Him
raw_title: James Ellsworth Reveals WWE Had No Creative Plans for Him After Vince McMahon Hired Him
summary_src: James Ellsworth went from getting destroyed by Braun Strowman to becoming a regular on WWE SmackDown, but there’s something fans didn’t know about his sudden rise. WWE apparently had absolutely no idea what to do with him after Vince McMahon decided to hire him.
body: While speaking on Developmentally Speaking , Ellsworth explained that his WWE career started in an unusual way. After impressing McMahon during his 2016 match against Braun Strowman, he was offered a contract and immediately brought to SmackDown without going through NXT. Ellsworth admitted that he initially assumed he would be heading to WWE’s developmental system, but McMahon had other ideas. “When they call and they’re like, ‘Hey, you’re coming to SmackDown.’ I’m like, ‘All right, well, am I going to NXT?’ Because that, you know, that’s what everybody does. They’re like, ‘No, man. Vince wants you. Vince wants you on SmackDown.’ They’re like, ‘We don’t know what the future holds.'” The problem was that WWE already had months of television planned before McMahon suddenly decided Ellsworth needed to be part of the show. According to Ellsworth, that meant the writers had to make room for someone who wasn’t originally supposed to be there. “So they have all this television written for months and months and months. They have ideas for months. Now Vince is going into this writer room and going, ‘Hey, you got to write stuff for this guy,’ which means, you know, and you live and you learn, which means now they got to take somebody off the show to give me their time, and now they got to rewrite all this stuff just to put me on.” Ellsworth even suspected that his arrival may have annoyed some people behind the scenes because WWE had already invested time and money into wrestlers coming through NXT. Meanwhile, he was getting television time simply because McMahon personally wanted him there. “It probably got on their nerves at first, like, ‘Why is Vince, what’s okay?’ You know, because again they have time and money invested in the people they bring through NXT, and I get that. I understand it.” Things didn’t get any less confusing once Ellsworth actually started appearing on SmackDown. He recalled being told he would work with The Miz, only for that plan to change to AJ Styles. Ellsworth admitted that facing Styles was intimidating because of how talented he was in the ring. “Soon as I got there they’re like, ‘Oh, you’re going to be working with The Miz.’ Then The Miz switched to, ‘No, no, you’re gonna work with AJ Styles.’ And I’m, you know, so every week I’m like, ‘What’s going on? I’m wrestling The Miz? Oh, that’s easy. Oh, I’m wrestling AJ? I’m scared to death because he’s so awesome I don’t know what to do.'” Ellsworth said WWE continued figuring things out as his character developed, with no real plan beyond whatever the company wanted to do that particular week. “They were winging me the whole time because they had nothing planned for me at all ever. They just had to plan week to week with me and get to know me and see what I could really do on the microphone and everything.” Despite the lack of direction, Ellsworth became a regular part of SmackDown, worked with AJ Styles, and eventually joined Carmella as her on-screen ally. title: Tony Khan Explains Hurt Syndicate's Sporadic AEW Appearances

summary_src: Tony Khan has explained why The Hurt Syndicate have appeared sporadically on AEW television, with their last appearance coming at All In.
body: AEW AEW's Tony Khan has explained The Hurt Syndicate's absence from the promotion. The Hurt Syndicate have made sporadic appearances in AEW lately, with their last match coming at All In , when they teamed up with Big Boom AJ and QT Marshall to defeat Shane Taylor Promotions . Khan spoke about the Hurt Syndicate during the WrestleDream media call, explaining how the group are hired guns in AEW, and that they could appear anytime. "The Hurt Syndicate and Mick Foley both involved in Double or Nothing, which I thought was one of the best shows of the year, and AEW All In London, one of the best shows of the year," Khan said. "In the ring, The Hurt Syndicate have said they are for hire, so we could see them any place, any time, I think, for the right amount of money. And certainly, one thing they did not want to do was beat up Big Justice and The Rizzler. They were happy to work with Big Boom A.J., Big Justice and The Rizzler, and turned things around." Khan stated that the group would work under the right conditions, which is why they collaborated with Big Justice and The Rizzler. The AEW CEO said that he gets along well with all members of the group and the trio has his respect. "The Hurt Syndicate, they won't work with just anybody, but they are for hire under the right circumstances, kind of like The A-Team. And I think it'll be interesting to see as they get involved. I have a lot of respect for Bobby and Shelton and MVP, and they could come in as hired guns for potentially anybody here," he added. The group will likely be a part of AEW for the foreseeable future, as MVP revealed earlier in the year that he and Shelton Benjamin had recently signed contract extensions, while also praising Tony Khan and the way he has treated them in the promotion.

Khan added that the group specifically chose to work with Big Justice and The Rizzler rather than oppose them.

title: James Ellsworth Opens Up On How WWE Continued Paying Him After His 2017 Release
raw_title: James Ellsworth Reveals How WWE Continued Paying Him After His 2017 Release
summary_src: Getting released from WWE usually means a wrestler’s time with the company is coming to an end, but James Ellsworth says his situation was a little different.
body: While speaking on Developmentally Speaking , Ellsworth opened up about how his WWE departure actually played out. After becoming a regular on SmackDown and working alongside Carmella, he was released in November 2017. However, according to Ellsworth, his payments never stopped, even while he was away from WWE television. “Well, it was weird how it happened. Like in November 2017, they like let me go, but then they brought me back a couple of months later. So they never like, they never stopped paying me. I was getting paid that whole time.” Ellsworth didn’t explain why WWE continued paying him or provide details about how his contract was structured during that period. What he did make clear was that the money kept coming even after he was initially let go. He eventually returned to WWE television in 2018, once again becoming involved in Carmella’s storylines. But when his contract finally reached its end, Ellsworth said he started getting the message that his time with the company was finished. That realization came around the time Paige, who was serving as SmackDown General Manager, fired him as part of an on-screen storyline. “So when the contract was actually up was right around when they had Paige fire me and I was like, ‘Oh, I guess I’m, that’s it.'” Ellsworth said he understood why WWE eventually moved on from him. Unlike wrestlers who spent years training in NXT, he had been brought directly to the main roster after Vince McMahon personally offered him a job. Ellsworth believed that made it easier for WWE to move on from his character when the company needed television time for new talent. “They have time and money invested in people from NXT. They have to, it’s a system. They have to keep bringing people up. So when they bring people up, it’s television. You only have so much time. People have to go. There’s people that have to go.” He also believes WWE views him as the type of character who can disappear for years and still get a reaction whenever the company decides to bring him back. “I’m a guy like, this ain’t really our guy. This is a character we could bring back every five or 10 years and people will remember it. You know, I’m like the Boogeyman or something. They could bring it back whenever and people react to it. So I feel like that’s how they look at me, and probably always have.” Ellsworth hasn’t given up on the idea of working for WWE again. He believes he could still contribute as a manager, similar to the role he played alongside Carmella, although he knows that decision isn’t his to make. “Do I think I could have stayed on there and been like a manager like I was with Carmella, they call it a heater in the business, and done that forever? title: WWE NXT Viewership Drops To 655,000

summary_src: WWE NXT's average viewership and key demographic ratings fell following a huge rise in both metrics the previous week.
body: WWE " WWE NXT " viewership and ratings dropped after reaching their highest levels in six weeks the previous week. The developmental brand's viewership fell from the previous week's 732,000 to 655,000 for the October 20 show, an 11% drop, according to " Wrestlenomics ." While the fall is significant, the show's viewership is still higher than the month-long average of 641,000. The 18-49 key demographic rating, meanwhile, witnessed an even greater percentage-wise drop, falling from 0.14 to 0.10. What could be even more disappointing for WWE is that the rating is also lower than the four-week average of 0.11. Viewership and ratings for October, though, are higher than they were during the same period last year, with the former up by 8% and the latter by 10%, respectively. Last week's show featured the final two quarterfinal matches of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic, with the teams of Hank and Tank and The Wagner Brothers advancing to the final four. The show also featured a segment involving NXT Champion Grayson Waller and former champion and No. 1 contender Tony D'Angelo ahead of their clash at Halloween Havoc. The show ended with a clash between Cruz Montana and Dion Lennox, which ended in a no contest after Montana was arrested as all hell broke loose during the match.

title: On the Record: Alexa Bliss Opens Up On WWE Planned to Reunite Her With Bray Wyatt Before His Death
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Reveals WWE Planned to Reunite Her With Bray Wyatt Before His Death
summary_src: Alexa Bliss and Bray Wyatt never got the reunion they were supposed to have in WWE, and now Bliss is revealing what was planned before everything fell apart.
body: While speaking with Brandi Rhodes on Shot of Brandi , Bliss opened up about her relationship with Wyatt while discussing her favorite Halloween costumes. She picked her dark Alice in Wonderland outfit because she wore it during their Firefly Fun House storyline, which brought back memories of their time together. Bliss explained that the last time she worked with Wyatt was at WrestleMania, when she turned against him during his match with Randy Orton. That wasn’t supposed to be the end of their story, either. According to Bliss, WWE had plans to bring them back together, but things took a very different turn. “I never got to have that closure with Bray because the last time I was with him it was WrestleMania and I turned on him against Randy, and then we were supposed to join back together after this one WrestleMania, and then I found out I was pregnant.” Bliss said Wyatt then became ill, leaving their planned reunion unfinished. With both of them dealing with major changes in their lives, they never found the opportunity to reconnect on WWE television. “And then he had gotten sick and so he was out for a while, and so it just never, it was like ships in the night, right?” Even though their WWE storyline never got its intended ending, Bliss said something Wyatt mentioned during an interview stayed with her. He had spoken about their characters always sharing a connection, and those words meant a lot to her after his passing. “And he did that interview where he was like, ‘Well, Alexa and I will always be connected in some way.’ And I just felt like a sense of comfort.” Bliss eventually got an opportunity to revisit their work when Universal Orlando created a Bray Wyatt-inspired attraction for Halloween Horror Nights. She was allowed to participate as a scare actor, including spending time in a Firefly Fun House setting where footage of Wyatt played on a television. That experience brought back some painful memories, but Bliss said it also helped her finally say goodbye. “I felt like, I finally was able to close that chapter. Right, like it’s over. It’s over. It’s over. It’s done.” She admitted that being inside the attraction was one of the first times Wyatt’s death truly hit her. Having the chance to return to something they created together gave her a moment she never got in WWE. “Yeah, and I think that was one of the first times that it actually hit me that he was actually gone and so it was so cool to be able to do that, that Universal let me do that because I was like, I feel like this is me saying goodbye.” For Bliss, the reunion with Wyatt that was supposed to happen in WWE will always be one of those unfinished stories. While fans never got to see their characters come back together, she was eventually able to find some peace by revisiting the world they helped create. The champions Thekla, Julia Hart, and Skye Blue will face the team of Hazuki, Koguma, and Fuwa-chan. The match will be taped on Wednesday, October 28 at the Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis, Missouri.

The title match was arranged after the Triangle of Madness made their first successful defense of the Artist of Stardom Championship last month at Stardom to the World in Yokohama. They defeated the team of Natsupoi, Aya Sakura, and Yuna Mizumori. Hazuki, Koguma, and Fuwa-chan then confronted the champions and demanded the belts.

Fuwa-chan later defeated Julia Hart in a singles match at Stardom's September 29 event at Korakuen Hall in Tokyo. The Triangle of Madness are also set to compete at AEW Blood & Guts on Wednesday, November 4 in Jacksonville, where they will team with Divine Dominion against Kris Statlander, Harley Cameron, Willow Nightingale, and the Brawling Birds.

Thekla, Skye Blue, and Julia Hart captured the Artist of Stardom titles on July 18 during the first night of the 5 Star Grand Prix in Tokyo. They defeated the team of Ami Sohrei, Hina, and Lady C to become the 37th champions.

title: On the Record: Alexa Bliss Opens Up On Ryan Cabrera Had No Idea Who She Was Before They Started Dating
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Reveals Ryan Cabrera Had No Idea Who She Was Before They Started Dating
summary_src: Alexa Bliss and Ryan Cabrera have been married for years, but their relationship got off to a pretty hilarious start. As it turns out, Cabrera didn’t even know who the WWE Superstar was when people started linking them together.
body: During her appearance on Shot of Brandi with Brandi Rhodes , Bliss explained how she and Cabrera first connected. The conversation started when Rhodes mentioned that she assumed The Miz had introduced them, which led Bliss to explain that Miz loves taking credit for their relationship. According to Bliss, the entire situation started because whoever was managing Cabrera’s social media accounts kept interacting with her posts. That caused people to assume the two were already dating, even though they hadn’t met. “So there was a rumor that Ryan and I were dating because whoever was running his socials at the time was liking and replying to literally every one of my tweets. It was aggressive.” Those rumors eventually made their way to The Miz, who knew Cabrera and decided to ask him about the supposed relationship. That’s when Cabrera gave an answer Bliss still finds hilarious. “And Mike reached out to him and going, ‘Hey, I heard you’re dating Alexa Bliss.’ And Ryan goes, ‘Is that a clothing brand?’ Or, ‘I’ve heard you’re tied to Alexa Bliss.’ He goes, ‘Is that a clothing brand?'” Bliss explained that Miz had to tell Cabrera she was actually a professional wrestler. Miz then offered to introduce them the next time she was in town, although that wasn’t exactly how their relationship started. Instead, Bliss and Cabrera began talking because the rumors about them wouldn’t go away. “And then Ryan and I ended up messaging because the rumor just kept going.” Things started moving when Cabrera mentioned that he was traveling to Orlando for a performance. Bliss happened to live there, which gave them an opportunity to meet. “And he was like, ‘Well, it was nice chatting with you. I’m on my way to Orlando.’ And I was like, ‘Oh my God, I live in Orlando.’ And he had a show there and he was like, ‘You wanna come to my show?'” Bliss confirmed that the show was at Disney, making the beginning of their relationship even more fitting considering their shared love for the parks. She also made it clear that The Miz still tries to take full credit for bringing them together. The funny part is that Cabrera went from having no idea who Alexa Bliss was to eventually marrying her. And while Miz helped get the conversation started, Bliss made it clear that their actual connection happened after they began messaging each other. body: AEW Last week on "AEW Dynamite" , the Bang Bang Gang aligned with The Dogs after attacking the Death Riders and kicking Gabe Kidd out of the latter faction. On "Collision" , AEW's newest faction revealed they were The Last Outfit. The name caused a lot of confusion on social media, especially those who didn't realize that outfit has multiple meanings such as in the military and the mob (Al Capone's mob was called The Outfit). White said there's a new sheriff in town and they're coming for the Death Riders. "You are blessed with the privilege of witnessing the sickest, the slickest, the quickest draws in the West. Top shelf high rollers, golden gun slingers, some dirty dogs, your Collision cowboys. We are the last outfit capable of slicing out the cancer that is Jon Moxley and the Death Riders from the heart of AEW. We are...The Cut," White explained. title: Pat Tanaka Dropped By Management Over Missed Bookings
raw_title: Former WWE & AWA wrestler dropped by management company over missed events
summary_src: Pat Tanaka, best known for his work in the AWA and WWF in the late 1980s and early 1990s, is being dropped by his management company over reliability concerns. KWK Brand Talent Management announced over the weekend that it will no longer represent Tanaka for bookings or appearances.
body: Pat Tanaka, best known for his work in the AWA and WWF in the late 1980s and early 1990s, is being dropped by his management company over reliability concerns. KWK Brand Talent Management announced over the weekend that it will no longer represent Tanaka for bookings or appearances. The decision comes after multiple missed bookings, including an event for Cleveland-based Absolute Intense Wrestling last month. Tanaka missed a seminar and a show for AIW, giving them a convoluted story that included a supposed car wreck and a newly booked flight that Tanaka said would both take off and land at 7 p.m. Tanaka ultimately ghosted AIW and did not appear for his bookings. “We love to gamble on these wild card old timers so I’m sure we will be in this situation again with one of these guys down the road,” AIW wrote . “As for Pat’s flight and when it is landing that is to be continued but he’s allegedly been up in the air for quite some time at this point……….he is a very nice guy on the telephone though when he does answer and we wish him the best.” Tanaka also missed a show for World Classic Professional Big Time Wrestling on Ohio this past weekend, which led to KWK Brand cutting ties with him (outside of an existing commitment for action figures). With partner Paul Diamond/Kato, Tanaka was one-half of The Orient Express in WWF and one-half of Badd Company in the AWA. His career included time spent in the CWA, ECW, and WCW as well. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

The decision follows Tanaka failing to show for a seminar and match with Absolute Intense Wrestling last month, where he provided an implausible excuse involving a car wreck and a flight scheduled to depart and arrive at the same time before ghosting the promotion. AIW publicly commented on the situation while wishing Tanaka well.

The decision was made after Tanaka failed to appear for a seminar and a show with Absolute Intense Wrestling last month. He provided an unclear explanation involving a car wreck and a flight that was said to take off and land at the same time before ultimately not showing up.

Tanaka also missed an event for World Classic Professional Big Time Wrestling in Ohio over the weekend. This latest absence prompted KWK Brand to end its representation of him, aside from an existing commitment related to action figures.

His career also included appearances in the CWA, ECW, and WCW.

title: On the Record: Alexa Bliss Opens Up On She Had a Non-Negotiable Demand Before Returning to WWE
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Reveals She Had a Non-Negotiable Demand Before Returning to WWE
summary_src: Alexa Bliss made one thing very clear before returning to WWE in 2025 — her daughter was coming with her. The former Women’s Champion revealed that she actually worked it into her contract so she could bring Hendrix on the road, calling it a “non-negotiable” part of coming back.
body: Speaking with Brandi Rhodes on Shot of Brandi , Bliss opened up about trying to balance WWE’s travel schedule with being a mom. She said Hendrix was barely a year old when she was working everything out, and disappearing for several days every week simply wasn’t something she was willing to do. “It’s definitely really hard, but I am in so much of the phase of I don’t wanna miss anything she does. So that was one of the biggest things of coming back. I worked it into my contract that she travels with me. I was like, ‘I need to be able to bring my daughter along. That’s non-negotiable,’ because she, at the time, was only barely a year, and I was like, ‘I’m not leaving her on the road multiple days a week.’” There’s another wrinkle too because Bliss isn’t the only parent constantly traveling for work. Her husband, Ryan Cabrera, has spent years touring as a musician, so somebody needed to have Hendrix with them. “And she has two touring parents because Ryan tours every weekend. He has for the past 10 years. He’s still on a tour every weekend. And so I said, ‘She needs to go with one of us and it’s gonna be me.’” Of course, bringing a toddler on the road means Bliss isn’t exactly traveling light anymore. She joked that the days of showing up with two little bags disappeared once she started bringing everything Hendrix needed. “That was just something that it’s a lot of growing pains because now instead of traveling with two cute little bags, you’re traveling with 10 because you have, at first it was a Pack ‘n Play, a travel Pack ‘n Play and a stroller and a car seat. Now I’m very grateful for the opportunity to bring her on the road because I get to be there for everything, right?” Bliss learned just how important that arrangement was when she went on one WWE UK tour without Hendrix. She said flights were around $30,000, so her daughter stayed home that time. “And selfishly, I did feel bad when I went on the UK tour without her because flights were like $30,000.” While Bliss was away, Cabrera sent her a video of Hendrix discovering the moon for the first time. It was an adorable moment, but watching it happen through a phone screen hit Bliss pretty hard. “Well, luckily she adjusts really well. She’s been on two UK tours and she adjusted after the second day. I went on the tour and Ryan sends me a picture, or a video, of her discovering the moon for the first time, and she was so excited. She was like, ‘Moon, moon.’ She was jumping up and down, pointing at the moon, and I was so sad that I had to live that moment through a screen because I was like, ‘Oh, I should have been there for that or she should have—’” Brandi called that feeling “mom guilt,” and Bliss knew exactly what she meant. That’s also why her solution these days is pretty simple. “Yeah, the mom guilt. It’s crazy. I don’t ever wanna feel mom guilt, so I just bring her with me.” Hendrix has apparently gotten pretty comfortable with WWE life too. Bliss said her daughter can nap backstage eve

title: On the Record: Alexa Bliss Opens Up On Why Ryan Cabrera Told Her Never to Cook Again
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Reveals Why Ryan Cabrera Told Her Never to Cook Again
summary_src: Alexa Bliss tried to impress Ryan Cabrera with a homemade breakfast when they first started dating, but things went so badly that he told her never to cook again. The WWE Superstar thought she was doing something sweet for her future husband before he headed out for an early round of golf.
body: While appearing on Shot of Brandi with Brandi Rhodes , Bliss admitted that cooking isn’t exactly one of her strongest skills. The subject came up while the two were preparing cheddar cheese soup, with Bliss explaining why Cabrera had previously told her to stay away from the kitchen. Bliss said the incident happened early in their relationship. She wanted to surprise Cabrera with breakfast before he left to play golf, hoping to make a good impression as his new girlfriend. “So this is when Ryan and I were first dating and he had to get up early for golf, and I was like, ‘Okay, I’m gonna be the super awesome girlfriend and I’m gonna have breakfast ready for him.'” She decided to make scrambled eggs and a bagel, but the eggs didn’t come out the way she expected. In fact, Bliss knew something was wrong before Cabrera even took a bite. “And so I made him eggs and I knew they didn’t quite look right.” Bliss described the eggs as looking more like little burnt pellets. Despite that, Cabrera ate everything she prepared without making a single complaint. She assumed the breakfast had gone over well, but she found out the truth later that day. The couple attended a game night at a friend’s house, where someone asked everyone to reveal a lie they had told their significant other. Cabrera wasted absolutely no time exposing Bliss’ terrible cooking. “And Ryan proudly and loudly says, ‘I told her this morning that her eggs are great and they were terrible.'” Bliss was stunned because Cabrera had eaten the entire breakfast and acted like nothing was wrong. But he wasn’t finished explaining how he felt about her cooking. “I love you. I appreciate the sentiment. You are never cooking again.” Rather than getting upset, Bliss admitted that she was actually relieved. She already knew the eggs were terrible and wasn’t exactly looking forward to making another breakfast. “I was more relieved because I was like, I knew they were bad.” Bliss explained that she used to cook regularly during her bodybuilding days, when she had to prepare her own meals. However, life on the road with WWE eventually changed that. Constant travel and limited time at home made it difficult to keep up with cooking, and she gradually lost the habit. There was at least some redemption during her appearance with Brandi Rhodes. Bliss was put in charge of cooking the bacon for their soup, and she managed to get through the job without burning it. Rhodes even joked that she would tell Cabrera to give Bliss another chance in the kitchen. It sounds like Cabrera’s cooking ban has worked out pretty well for Bliss, especially since she wasn’t too upset about giving up breakfast duty in the first place. And after successfully handling the bacon, she might finally have a reason to challenge that old rule. What do you think about Ryan Cabrera telling Alexa Bliss never to cook again after her breakfast disaster? Have you ever had a cooking attempt go this badly? Share your stories in the comments. H Jenkins

title: Brooke Hogan Criticizes WWE Over Father's Hospital Visit
raw_title: Hulk Hogan’s daughter Brooke slams WWE for not visiting her father in the hospital before tragic death
body: Last year, in Jul. 2025, WWE legend Hulk Hogan passed away due to an acute myocardial infarction , aka a heart attack. Despite all of Hogan's controversies, the late wrestler was one of the most popular names in the entertainment industry. He is also often regarded as one of the key figures in turning pro-wrestling into a household name. Shortly after Hogan's death, TMZ and Netflix released a documentary about Hogan's passing and career, and many people spoke in it. However, since Hogan passed away, his daughter Brooke Hogan has been extremely open about her father's death . She often brought up his wife, Sky's role in it, the police investigation behind it , the hospital's role, and much more. Recently, sharing a few stories on her Instagram, Brooke Hogan began reflecting on her memories with her father. However, as she progressed through the stories, things started becoming dark. Toward the end of her Instagram stories, Hogan took a shot at the people who were with her father before his tragic death. "Not one of those people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital…if they even showed," wrote Brooke Hogan while showing a picture of WWE's Hulk Hogan tribute on RAW. She also continued her attack on a few more unnamed people while also celebrating her relationship with Hogan's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel, as well as McDaniel's relationship with Hogan before their divorce in 2021. Hogan was then married to Sky Daily from 2023 to 2025, until his death. Despite Brooke's comments on Sky regarding her father's death, nothing concrete has been proven.
summary: Hulk Hogan died last July from a heart attack. His daughter Brooke has been vocal about events surrounding his passing and recently shared Instagram stories reflecting on memories with her father. In the posts she claimed none of those present with him remained at the hospital longer than an hour if they visited at all.

title: US Intelligence Memo Raises Saudi Arabia Security Concerns For WWE Crown Jewel
raw_title: Intelligence Memo Indicates Increased Danger As WWE Plans Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
summary_src: A United States intelligence memo indicates an increase in danger in Saudi Arabia as WWE continues with its plans to hold Crown Jewel in Riyadh
body: As the date for WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia gets closer and closer, the more questions are raised about whether the show should go on , as attacks on Saudi Arabia continue. And now with less than a week till Crown Jewel, even more cause for concern has emerged. The New York Times reports that a recent US intelligence memo sent by Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned of dangers facing State Department employees in "the Middle East and other regions," with Iran said to be in "advanced stages" of planning attacks against Americans in the area. While there is no mention of WWE, or any other entertainment acts, in the report or the memo, many believe it's another indicator that WWE should postpone, or move, Crown Jewel to another location outside of Saudi Arabia. The event will not only be put together largely by American personnel, but will take place in the Riyadh Season Stadium, which is expected to seat a sizable crowd. Construction of the temporary stadium was supposedly underway as of late last week, around the same time Clayton's memo became known. Despite the memo, all indications, including the construction of the stadium, continue to suggest that WWE will throw caution to the wind and head to Saudi Arabia. When asked about the ongoing conflict last week, TKO CEO Ari Emanuel stated that while TKO and WWE were monitoring the situation daily in the event that Crown Jewel would need to be moved, all signs pointed towards the PLE, and other TKO events in the Middle East, proceeding as planned. WWE continued to advertise Crown Jewel as taking place in Riyadh later that night on "SmackDown," when they announced Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match would take place on the show .
summary: A recent US intelligence memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton warned of Iran being in advanced stages of planning attacks against Americans in the Middle East. The warning comes less than a week before WWE Crown Jewel is scheduled to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia at the temporary Riyadh Season Stadium. Many are now questioning whether the show should proceed as planned given the increased danger to American personnel involved.

Rhodes proposed the stipulation during a confrontation on SmackDown. Orton responded by cautioning Rhodes to be careful what he wished for.
The two wrestlers have a long history that dates back to Rhodes' first stint in WWE. They have been feuding for much of 2026.

title: Matt Jackson Explains Repeated Young Bucks Promo Photos
raw_title: Matt Jackson Jokes About Why The Young Bucks Use The Same Promo Pictures For Graphics For Long Periods Of Time
body: Matt Jackson explains to fans why The Young Bucks use the same promo pictures for graphics for long periods of time. For The Young Bucks, their match graphics are usually ones that feature renders of the tag team for several pay-per-views in a row, with fresh promo pictures being rare for the brothers. Now, Matt Jackson has explained why this happens from time to time. “He hates the direction. He used to hate school picture day, yearbook day, and all that stuff. He’s always complaining to my mom, like, ‘God, I got to do these freaking photos, Mom? Yeah, you have to. Everyone has to, Nick. You go to the school? Yeah, you got to take a picture.’ Look at the point. Look at his face.” Matt continued, joking that this is the reason the pair have several pay-per-views in a row of the same promo pictures without updates. “This will be the only time you see us do this in 2026. When you’re complaining and you’re like, God, these photos have been used for 20 of the matches. You know what everyone goes, ‘all the Young Bucks matches that I love this year, it’s like the same freaking graphic,’ because he doesn’t want to do photos.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Matt Jackson revealed that his brother Nick dislikes taking new promotional pictures, comparing it to his childhood aversion to school picture day and yearbook photos. This reluctance leads to The Young Bucks frequently using the same renders for multiple AEW pay-per-view graphics in a row. Jackson joked that the repeated images will only appear this way through 2026.

kind.quote: He hates the direction. He used to hate school picture day, yearbook day, and all that stuff.

Jackson revealed that his brother Nick dislikes taking photos and often complains about the process. He compared Nick's attitude to how he used to hate school picture day and yearbook day when they were younger. "He hates the direction. Jackson said. He added that Nick would complain to their mom about having to take the photos.

Jackson noted that this reluctance is the reason the same images appear for extended periods. He joked that fans notice when the same graphic is used for many of their matches throughout the year. "This will be the only time you see us do this in 2026," Jackson continued. He pointed out that the repeated graphics stem directly from Nick not wanting to do new photos.

title: Sol Ruca Overcomes Imposter Syndrome On WWE Main Roster
raw_title: Sol Ruca: Especially As An Athlete, I Feel Like A Lot Of Us Have A Bit Of Imposter Syndrome
summary_src: Sol Ruca speaks about her arrival on the WWE main roster and how she has managed to shake 'a bit of imposter syndrome.' In April of 2026, the former NXT Women's North American Champion would arrive on the WWE main roster and soon after would capture the women's Intercontinental…
body: Sol Ruca speaks about her arrival on the WWE main roster and how she has managed to shake ‘a bit of imposter syndrome.’ In April of 2026, the former NXT Women’s North American Champion would arrive on the WWE main roster and soon after would capture the women’s Intercontinental Champion, remaining staple of the WWE Monday Night RAW women’s division since then. While speaking to the Fresno Bee in a new interview, Sol Ruca would briefly speak about dealing with imposter syndrome as an athlete. “It was kind of like, ‘Wow, I do know what I’m doing. This is where I should be. Especially as an athlete, I feel like a lot of us have a bit of imposter syndrome, thinking, ‘I don’t know if this is right for me. This isn’t something I was passionate about when I was a little kid.’ But now I’m passionate about it, and that was definitely a bit of reassurance that this is where I’m supposed to be, I’m in the right place, and this is something I want to continue doing.”
summary: Sol Ruca arrived on the WWE main roster in April 2026 after her time as NXT Women’s North American Champion. She soon captured the women’s Intercontinental Championship and has been a regular in the Monday Night RAW women’s division. In an interview with the Fresno Bee, she discussed feeling imposter syndrome as an athlete before realizing she belongs and is passionate about her current path.

The former NXT Women’s North American Champion arrived on the main roster in April 2026. She soon captured the women’s Intercontinental Championship after her arrival.

Ruca has remained a regular presence in the WWE Monday Night RAW women’s division since winning the title. While speaking to the Fresno Bee, she addressed how she managed to shake off a bit of imposter syndrome as an athlete.

Ruca explained that she reached a point of realization where she affirmed her place in the company. She noted that many athletes experience imposter syndrome and question if their path is correct, especially if it was not a childhood passion.
Ruca stated that she has since become passionate about her role and received reassurance that she belongs in WWE and wants to keep performing there.

title: Jeff Jarrett Praises AEW's Clockwork Carnage Match
raw_title: Jeff Jarrett Loved Seeing AEW Try 'New Things' At WrestleDream
summary_src: Jeff Jarrett has spoken highly of the AEW WrestleDream main event, which featured the Clockwork Carnage match won by Will Ospreay.
body: AEW AEW's Jeff Jarrett was pleased to see the promotion experiment with new ideas at the WrestleDream pay-per-view. WrestleDream's main event saw the debut of the Clockwork Carnage match, in which Will Ospreay retained his AEW World Championship . Jarrett was full of praise for the show as a whole but was particularly impressed with the new match, which he was convinced would be a success. "I just sat there and looked at the players in the Clockwork Carnage, and I said, I think there's probably people that are not really sure because you've never seen it how it's going to play out. But when I kind of walked through it and thought it through, I'm like, this is going to steal the show," he said. "I thought that was fantastic." Jarrett, a fan of new, innovative ideas in pro wrestling, likened the Clockwork Carnage match to one that he had a role in creating, the King of the Mountain match, which was a staple in TNA Wrestling. "I love innovative. I love trying new things. I love having the audience get engaged at a different level," added Jarrett. "When you see that you can be eliminated and how it's drawn out, I just thought Clockwork Carnage exceeded everybody's expectations. I was really high on it going in. I think it can become a staple in so many ways. I just think the progression, I loved it. I can't help but say that when I think of a match with two stages, King of the Mountain [comes to mind]. [You have] Got to qualify and then you got to climb. And there was, you know, a lot of, uh, haters on that for years and years and years." He reiterated his love for the new match type in AEW, although host Conrad Thompson had a differing opinion, stating that he wasn't a fan of the match and arguing that it shouldn't have main-evented a pay-per-view and should have been reserved for a TV special.
summary: Jeff Jarrett enjoyed AEW's WrestleDream pay-per-view and was especially impressed by the new Clockwork Carnage match that headlined the show. Will Ospreay retained his AEW World Championship in the innovative bout. Jarrett compared it to the King of the Mountain match he helped create for TNA, saying he loves when promotions try new things to engage audiences at a different level.

llm_long: Jeff Jarrett expressed his approval for All Elite Wrestling's willingness to try fresh concepts during the WrestleDream pay-per-view event. The main event at WrestleDream featured the first-ever Clockwork Carnage match where Will Ospreay successfully defended his AEW World Championship. Jarrett offered strong praise for the overall show but highlighted the innovative match as especially impressive and one he believed would succeed.

He recalled analyzing the participants in the Clockwork Carnage bout and concluding that despite initial uncertainty from some viewers it would ultimately steal the show. Jarrett described the match as fantastic and noted that it surpassed all expectations with its elimination format and progression.

A longtime advocate for creative approaches in professional wrestling Jarrett compared the Clockwork Carnage to the King of the Mountain match he helped develop for TNA Wrestling which required qualification before climbing. He emphasized his enthusiasm for matches that engage audiences on new levels and stated he was very positive about the Clockwork Carnage beforehand believing it could grow into a regular feature for the promotion.

title: Buddy Matthews pulled from WSW return
raw_title: ‘Scheduling conflicts’ pull AEW’s Buddy Matthews from indie comeback
body: Link AEW Aussie Buddy Matthews injured his ankle at AEW Grand Slam Australia in February of 2025, and hasn’t wrestled since. He did make a surprise appearance in his home country this May at an independent show, which set up his planned October return to that promotion (World Series Wrestling or WSW). In July, Matthews seemed to indicate he’d finally been cleared by doctors . But the 38-year-old from Melbourne hasn’t wrestled — and now that planned October return to WSW is off. It posted the following on Instagram yesterday (Oct. 25): We have just learnt, that due to scheduling conflicts, Buddy Matthews will no longer be appearing on the WSW MEGAMANIA Tour. We’re really disappointed that Buddy won’t be joining us this time around, but we completely understand that schedules can change. We hope to welcome Buddy Matthews back to World Series Wrestling on a future tour! 🇦🇺🔥 It’s not clear what the conflict is. WSW’s MegaMania tour begins this Thursday (Oct. 29) and runs through Monday, Nov. 2. AEW’s is in St. Louis, Missouri for a live Dynamite on Wednesday; it will tape next Saturday’s Collision afterwards. Matthews’ wife, WWE’s Rhea Ripley, is also currently sidelined with an injury. We’ll likely learn eventually if there’s anything deeper going on here. In the meantime, we’ll just hope this announcement doesn’t mean Matthews or anyone close to him are facing new challenges. title: Titan and Nagai first team eliminated from NJPW Super Jr. Tag League
raw_title: First elimination emerges in 2026 NJPW Super Jr. Tag League
summary_src: A team was officially eliminated from the NJPW Super Jr. Tag League at Monday night's Korakuen Hall card.
body: One team has been mathematically eliminated from this year’s NJPW Super Jr. Tag League following night 3 from Korakuen Hall in Tokyo, Japan on Monday evening. The tournament’s first elimination emerged in the opening block match of the night, where AEW’s The Swirl took down Daiki Nagai and Titan. In a match that saw Nagai get split open in the closing minutes, Blake Christian and Lee Johnson took out CMLL luchador Titan at ringside before giving Nagai their Brainrot double-team finisher for the pinfall. Despite getting close to victory many times, Titan and Nagai have gone winless through three matches. With just two more matches remaining in their Round Robin run in the tournament, there’s no way they can qualify for the tour’s grand finals. The main event of the night saw Mistico and Young Lion Masatora Yasuda stay alive in their Jr. Tag League tournament bid, taking down Robbie X & Taiji Ishimori. After nearly getting put away by Robbie X, Mistico was able to lock in his La Mistica submission for the sudden tap-out. The duo of Mistico and Yasuda, which was made on short notice following El Desperado’s departure from the tournament due to injury, had been winless up until today. KUSHIDA and Nick Wayne picked up their second victory of the tournament on Monday, scoring a competitive win over Kuukai and Master Wato. The closing sequence of the match saw veteran KUSHIDA score his Back to the Future suplex on Kuukai for the three-count. With just one win to their name, Kuukai and Wato are on the bubble for potential elimination by tomorrow’s show. An undefeated record fell early on Monday night, as the duo of Hyo and YOH took down Francesco Akira and Jakob Austin Young. After inadvertently wiping out Akira with a strike (making it two matches in a row where the embattled United Empire teammates have accidentally come to blows), Austin was rolled up for the pinfall result. Another flawless record was brought to an end when SHO and Dick Togo took down Kosei Fujita and Robbie Eagles on Monday night. Utilizing a stuffed animal they stole from Hyo in an earlier match on the tour, the House of Torture team loaded up the plushie and struck Eagles in the head with it for a shady pinfall win. The result spared Togo and SHO from elimination, as they had entered Monday winless. 23-year-old Kazuma Sumi was close to scoring a big win on Monday alongside tag partner Ryusuke Taguchi, facing House of Torture’s DOUKI and Yoshinobu Kanemaru. But his momentum was stopped by a whiskey mist to the face from Kanemaru, allowing DOUKI to score a bridged German Suplex for the pinfall win. Here’s a look at the updated blocks for the junior tag league. Tomorrow’s show will focus on A Block action from Ibaraki.
summary: Titan and Daiki Nagai became the first team mathematically eliminated from the 2026 NJPW Super Jr. Tag League after losing their third straight match on night three at Korakuen Hall. AEW's Blake Christian and Lee Johnson, billed as The Swirl, defeated them when they hit their Brainrot finisher on Nagai for the pin following a ringside attack on Titan. In the main event, Mistico forced Robbie X to submit with La Mistica, keeping Mistico and Masatora Yasuda alive in the tournament.

raw_title: Former WWE wrestler passes away
body: In the wrestling industry for over 40 years, veteran Jumbo Baretta is no more. Recently, the Cauliflower Alley Club shared the news that former wrestler Julio Barrera, a.k.a. Jumbo Baretta , has passed away. "Rest in Peace, My Friend Jumbo Beretta. This one truly hurts. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Jumbo, a good friend whom I was honored and privileged to know for nearly 40 years. I send my sincerest condolences to his family and friends. Rest in peace old friend," Cauliflower Alley Club wrote on social media. Baretta's wrestling career began in 1986. He started his career by training under Boris Malenko, the father of Joe and Dean Malenko. Early in his career, he would work for various Florida promotions, including Championship Wrestling from Florida and the World Wrestling Council in Puerto Rico. He also won the NWA Florida Tag Team Championship with Dennis Knight in 1989. The duo dropped the titles to Lou Perez and Mark Starr a month later. Later on, from 1989 to 1990, Baretta worked for World Championship Wrestling [WCW], where he had matches against Sting, Tommy Rich, the Rock 'n' Roll Express, and the Road Warriors. In 1989, he also wrestled for the Japanese promotion, Universal Wrestling Federation. Having worked a few matches for WCW, Baretta also wrestled a couple of matches in WWE (then known as WWF) in 1995, where he lost against Kama and The Blu Twins (Eli Blu & Jacob Blu). Later, in his career, he worked for various promotions and wrestled his last match in 2013. The unfortunate news comes just days after the passing of AEW's PAC and another f ormer AEW wrestler, "The Butcher" Andy Williams. As of now, the cause of Baretta's death is not known.
summary: The Cauliflower Alley Club announced that longtime wrestler Julio Barrera, known as Jumbo Baretta, has died. Baretta spent more than 40 years in the industry after beginning his career in 1986 under trainer Boris Malenko. He competed in Championship Wrestling from Florida, World Wrestling Council in Puerto Rico, and WCW from 1989 to 1990, capturing the NWA Florida Tag Team Championship with Dennis Knight in 1989.

body: We are weeks into the Skydance merger and still wondering how that will affect AEW. He pointed to Ellison being a supporter of AEW and believes the company will be stronger with the merger . Much happier than he's been about this relationship — he's always been happy about this relationship, he's always been beaming about it since Day One — but he definitely came out of these meetings the happiest he's been. And obviously there were moves made already, there's two wrestling moves that Skydance already made and neither of them were positive." Meltzer said that Women of Wrestling will get another season, but it won't be syndicated. He also said that a channel on Roku that aired Women of Wrestling and NWA 24/7 has been canceled. Meltzer said it doesn't sound like anything was cut back for AEW after Khan's meetings.

The exchange comes just one day after Irvin tried to clear up the story surrounding her October 2024 WWE departure. title: Ilja Dragunov Explains Facing Brock Lesnar at Royal Rumble
raw_title: AEW's Ilja Dragunov Addresses Brock Lesnar No-Selling His Offense At WWE Royal Rumble
summary_src: An interaction between Ilja Dragunov and Brock Lesnar at this year's WWE Royal Rumble caught the attention of fans, and Dragunov has commented on the exchange.
body: WWE As "The Beast Incarnate," Brock Lesnar was presented as the most dominant athlete on the WWE roster for years, bulldozing his way through most of the competition. At the men's Royal Rumble match earlier this year, Lesnar had a brief spot with AEW's latest acquisition, Ilja Dragunov , where he "no-sold" Dragunov's offense before eliminating him from the match moments later. Looking back at the interaction during an interview on "The Ariel Helwani Show," Dragunov offered his take. "If you really understand the persona that I have been in the ring most of the time, like, I've been facing monsters," he argued. "At the end of the day, you can't change certain things. You have a person like Brock Lesnar standing in front [of you]; most people would run away as soon as that happens, you know?" The wrestler maintained that he did the best he could to stay in character and continue portraying himself as mentally and physically tough, without being able to control Lesnar's reaction. Fortunately for him, Dragunov feels that his character has always been more based around vulnerability rather than domination. "It's always the way how I fought back and how I recovered after those moments, because these moments make great stories," he explained. "So I don't see it as a defeat." Dragunov acknowledged his fans that were mad about the spot, but expressed that it wasn't something he lingered on. When it comes to his career in WWE, Dragunov claimed he has no regrets. He also acknowledged that his character can be polarizing to fans, but he believes that's a positive thing in the wrestling industry.
summary: During an interview on The Ariel Helwani Show, AEW's Ilja Dragunov reflected on his brief 2024 Royal Rumble encounter with Brock Lesnar. Dragunov noted that his established persona involves battling monsters and that most people would flee from someone like Lesnar. He explained that he stayed true to his mentally and physically tough character despite Lesnar no-selling his offense before eliminating him, adding that his character has always centered on vulnerability.

title: Buddy Matthews Pulled From WSW Australia Tour

summary_src: AEW's Buddy Matthews has been pulled from an upcoming tour, World Series of Wrestling announced on Monday.
body: Buddy Matthews won’t be making his return as part of this week’s World Series of Wrestling tour. Back in May, Matthews was announced for a series of dates with Australia’s World Series of Wrestling promotion. As part of the tour, Matthews would do a show in New Zealand as well as four nights in Australia. It would be his first time working shows since early 2025, when the AEW star suffered an ankle injury. However, just days before the tour was scheduled to kick off, Matthews has been scrapped from the lineup. “We have just learnt, that due to scheduling conflicts, Buddy Matthews will no longer be appearing on the WSW MEGAMANIA Tour. We’re really disappointed that Buddy won’t be joining us this time around, but we completely understand that schedules can change. We hope to have Buddy Matthews back to World Series Wrestling on a future tour! Thank you for understanding and continued support.” While we haven’t seen Matthews in ages, the AEW talent announced two months ago that he’s officially cleared to compete once again.
summary: Buddy Matthews has been removed from the World Series of Wrestling MEGAMANIA Tour in Australia and New Zealand due to scheduling conflicts. The dates would have marked his first appearances since suffering an ankle injury in early 2025 while with AEW. WSW expressed disappointment but hopes to book Matthews for a future tour.

The promotion announced on Sunday via Instagram that the AEW star will no longer appear on the events. World Series Wrestling expressed disappointment over Matthews' absence but stated they understand that schedules can change and hope to welcome him back on a future tour.

Matthews had been announced for the tour back in May, which was set to include a show in New Zealand and four nights in Australia. It would have marked his first wrestling matches since suffering an ankle injury in February 2025 at AEW Grand Slam Australia.

The injury occurred during his entrance for a match against Kazuchika Okada and required surgery. Matthews made a surprise appearance for World Series Wrestling in May to set up the now-canceled appearances. The MegaMania tour is scheduled to begin on October 29 and run through November 2.

Flora appeared for a mandatory court date Saturday, Oct. 24, and a compliance date was set for Nov. 2, according to TMZ’s account of court docket records. According to Ringside News’ account of the documents , officers at the DUI testing center described Flora’s eyes as bloodshot and glassy, her speech as slow and her walking as unsteady. The report also said officers noted an odor of alcohol and described her as appearing dazed and confused. These were officers’ reported observations, not a determination of guilt. Ringside News reported that Flora initially refused a breath test, then was given another opportunity to take one. Officers reportedly made four attempts across two testing sequences, but none produced a valid sample. The outlet said the paperwork classified the situation as a refusal at 3:31 a.m. and did not include a breath-alcohol reading. The 34-year-old wrestler has appeared for WWE’s NXT and Impact Wrestling and won the SHINE Nova Championship in 2023, TMZ reported. According to her X profile , Flora is a muscle car mechanic, former EMT and a radio host on Orlando's Real Radio 104.1.

body: Link WWE via X/Twitter Samatha Irvin (real name Samantha Johnson-Mann) is believed to be a free agent after her two-year WWE non-compete clause is believed to have recently expired . She walked away from her role in WWE as a ring announcer on October 21, 2024, and since that time she has independently released several songs. But Irvin’s two passions could have once intertwined, as she revealed over the weekend that WWE once wanted to become involved in launching a music career for her. “WWE offered me a record deal, to which I politely declined because I have no interest in the music business!” Samantha posted Saturday (Oct. 24) on X (Twitter). “My interest was in managing wrestlers. And that’s all I’ve ever expressed.” She continued: “I made some songs last year for fun & videos with my colleagues from Cirque du Soleil and released independently for my singing fans from before wrestling but other than that, I made no proclamations about or efforts towards a ‘music’ career 🙏🏽 Singing career wise, I’ve had a fantastic one, though!!! Saw the world multiple times over.” Though she seems intent on not dedicating her full attention to music, Irvin could soon be entertaining wrestling fans again soon. On Friday, Fightful Select reported that AEW, where her husband Ricochet works, has “has internally discussed bringing her in a number of times, but it was made clear that it isn’t going to happen immediately upon her free agency.” Irving offered a humorous reply on X to the report about being “internally discussed,” though she didn’t actually reveal anything with her message. title: Brooke Hogan Shares Heartfelt Reaction To Hulk Hogan Estate Sale
raw_title: Brooke Hogan Reacts To Sale Of Hulk Hogan's Florida Mansion: "The Sick Feeling Is Indescribable"
summary_src: Brooke Hogan's post about the news. Terry Bollea, a.k.a.
body: Terry Bollea, a.k.a. Hulk Hogan’s estate, sold the late wrestler’s Florida mansion for $5.9 million. Bollea’s daughter, Brooke Hogan, took to her Instagram Story and wrote a lengthy post about the news. “The sick feeling is indescribable. This house was where dad and Jen envisioned growing old together. Where we brought him back to…surgery after surgery. Pool days. The smell of gasoline in his garage. His workouts downstairs. We cooked, we watched Jerry springer, we played music, we cried. I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he’d open the garage door. I’d sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in. His whole environment, his energy, his work, his relationships: First Jen-who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone…the truth teller… I’m sure to everyone’s delight. And now it’s all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him…used for **cking everyone else’s gain. Saddest ending I’ve ever seen. You know who TF you are.” In a series of posts following that, Brooke continued writing about her father. She shared a photo of WWE doing a 10-bell salute for Bollea and noted that not one of the people on stage stayed longer than an hour at the hospital with him. “Let’s not forget who was there for the 15 years before the vultures swooped in conveniently. Took this photo thinking “this is what I want to remember about my dad. How silly with his little guard dog, Duke… Took pictures when no one was looking I thought were priceless. Celebrating his Gawker win, forgetting I was the subject of the sex tape. Steve and I weren’t assholes. We supported his relationships and what came with them. Jen and I were the nurse crew. Notebooks, records, prescription pickups, overnights, switching shifts. This woman spent more time in the trenches thar ANY of us did. He LOVED her dearly. And she loved him. She wanted to be there till his last breath despite the trauma she endured that I witnessed.. She asked for nothing. She could have fought for money. She left with a tiny fraction, a Tahoe, and a 3 bedroom house. And vanished. No smear campaign. Just grace. She was pure love and grace. Their breakup was devastating for me. I loved her, but I knew my dad was in the best care with her too. This is Jen with my dad’s blood on her shirt, missing fingernails.. Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed. [Photo of WWE stars giving Hogan a ten bell salute.] And I’ve had to hear everyone say I’m the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior and brainwashing, fake, greedy people… “I should have been there.” “Everyone else” was there till the end. NO. They were there AT the end. To collect.

Brooke Hogan posted on Instagram Story about the sale, describing the indescribable sick feeling and recalling family memories in the home including surgeries, pool days, workouts, cooking, watching Jerry Springer, playing music and crying. She expressed sadness over the property being sold for profit after what she described as her father being used for others' gain throughout his life.

title: Comeback Watch: Buddy Matthews Pulled From Wrestling Return Just Days Before Scheduled Tour
raw_title: Buddy Matthews Pulled From Wrestling Return Just Days Before Scheduled Tour
summary_src: Buddy Matthews’ return to the wrestling ring has hit another setback, even though he’s already been cleared to compete.
body: World Series Wrestling announced that Matthews will no longer appear on its MEGAMANIA tour due to scheduling conflicts. The tour was supposed to include one show in New Zealand and four nights in Australia, giving Matthews his first matches since suffering an ankle injury. The promotion confirmed the change in a statement and made it clear that it hopes to bring Matthews back for another tour. “We have just learnt, that due to scheduling conflicts, Buddy Matthews will no longer be appearing on the WSW MEGAMANIA Tour. We’re really disappointed that Buddy won’t be joining us this time around, but we completely understand that schedules can change. We hope to have Buddy Matthews back to World Series Wrestling on a future tour! Thank you for understanding and continued support.” Matthews has been out of action since early 2025 after suffering an ankle injury. However, he announced two months ago that he had officially been medically cleared to return to the ring. That makes his sudden removal from the tour even more frustrating for fans who have been waiting to see him wrestle again. World Series Wrestling hasn’t provided any additional details about the scheduling conflict, and there’s no word on when Matthews will actually return to action. For now, Matthews remains cleared to wrestle, but his first match back will have to wait. With his planned appearances in Australia and New Zealand now off the table, it’s unclear whether his next match will happen in AEW or somewhere else. title: Buddy Matthews Pulled From WSW Australian Tour

summary_src: Buddy Matthews hasn't appeared in AEW since February 2025 after injuring his ankle during his entrance. He was cleared to wrestle last August.
body: AEW Buddy Matthews was scheduled to compete for World Series Wrestling's (WSW) MEGAMANIA tour that will hit five cities across two countries, Australia and New Zealand between October 29 and November 2. However, Matthews been pulled just days before the tour was scheduled to start. WSW posted on Instagram that Matthews would no longer be appearing. They wrote the following message to fans: "We have just learnt, that due to scheduling conflicts, Buddy Matthews will no longer be appearing on the WSW MEGAMANIA Tour. We're really disappointed that Buddy won't be joining us this time around, but we completely understand that schedules can change. We hope to welcome Buddy Matthews back to World Series Wrestling on a future tour. Thank you for your understanding and continued support." Several AEW stars are scheduled to appear on the tour including National Champion Andrade El Idolo, Sammy Guevara, Brian Cage, and Cassie Lee. AEW has several big shows lined up with Fright Night Dynamite and Collision, Blood and Guts, and Full Gear. They will debut in Monterrey, Mexico in December for Winter Is Coming and will close out the year with Worlds End. The annual C2 tournament is scheduled to begin on November 18 and culminate at Worlds End. In August, Matthews was cleared to return to wrestling following an injury at Grand Slam Australia in February 2025. He injured his ankle during his entrance , but finished his match against Kazuchika Okada. In a video, he shared that he had to relearn to walk after his surgery. A few months prior to being cleared, Matthews appeared in WSW to attack Donovan Dijak .

The promotion announced on Sunday via Instagram that the AEW star will no longer appear on the events. Matthews had been announced for the tour back in May, which was set to include a show in New Zealand and four nights in Australia. It would have marked his first wrestling matches since suffering an ankle injury in February 2025 at AEW Grand Slam Australia.
