title: Meltzer Criticizes WWE For Proceeding With Crown Jewel
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Believes WWE Crown Jewel Will Move Forward As Planned
summary_src: Dave Meltzer now believes that WWE Crown Jewel will move forward as planned, despite Meltzer's opinion that doing the show will be a terrible look for WWE
body: Neflix Despite ongoing attacks from Iran and Houthi forces from Yemen , and memos from the US State Department suggesting that Americans could be targeted in the weeks to come, WWE appears to be full speed ahead when it comes to holding WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on November 7. And it's becoming apparent to those like Dave Meltzer that there will be no change to where the show takes place. On Sunday morning's "Wrestling Observer Radio," Meltzer didn't hold back while discussing Crown Jewel with co-hosts Garrett Gonzalez and Paul Fontaine. "It's a terrible look...for WWE to go to Saudi Arabia right now," Meltzer said. "It's basically...it's like, we know what they are. We know they are. But it's like, not everyone knows what they are, and now it's harder to deny, you know what I mean? You can't deny it." Perhaps the only thing Meltzer was willing to give WWE/TKO higher ups was the idea that former WWE Chairman Vince McMahon would've refused to go to Saudi Arabia in this situation, emphatically saying McMahon would've done the same. More importantly, for perhaps the first time, Meltzer seemed to resign himself to Crown Jewel taking place in Riyadh, and that the show wouldn't be moved elsewhere, as Meltzer previously suggested/hoped would be the case . "The people who run the company, the way they're wired, they always want to make money," Meltzer said. "Money is in front of everything, okay, so they're going to make that decision. I mean, they could bomb the airport the day before, they're still going to go. That's just how it is." This is one where I think even the most ardent Dave Meltzer hater would say he's right on the money; WWE Crown Jewel is going to take place in Riyadh and there's no one, no fan nor media member, who can do anything to stop it. Well, almost no one. The truth is there is one group of individuals who could possibly put a halt to this insane idea of holding Crown Jewel in a warzone, and that's the WWE roster. It wouldn't be without risk; we've all seen how petty WWE can be towards its talents that don't do what they want. But in a world where there's now another major wrestling promotion out there that can offer work, and where two of the top stars booked for Crown Jewel (Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns) are getting acting roles in Hollywood films (albeit ones facing steep declines at the box office), I dare say the talent has options if they want to put their foot down and go 'Hey, our lives aren't worth the money this show will generate, money that won't go to most of us anyway." Sadly, this isn't going to happen; the only thing that would be more surprising than the WWE roster taking a stand or some wrestlers even walking out would be if WWE reversed course and postponed/moved Crown Jewel. We know this because this isn't the first time talent has been put in a position to take a stand and didn't do so. Perhaps the most notable one was the 2019 fiasco where over 200 WWE talents and crew members were left behind i

Meltzer noted WWE knows the situation but that it is now harder to deny. He added that Vince McMahon would have made the same decision to proceed.

title: On the Record: John Cena Explains Why He Was Determined to Make His WWE Rap Career Legitimate
raw_title: John Cena Explains Why He Was Determined to Make His WWE Rap Career Legitimate
summary_src: John Cena wasn’t about to become another wrestler who dropped a rap album just to cash in on his popularity. The WWE legend actually wanted respect from the hip-hop community, and he knew putting his name on a record wasn’t going to be enough.
body: While appearing on The Romesh Ranganathan Show alongside Jessica Biel to promote Matchbox: The Movie , Cena opened up about his music career and why earning credibility in hip-hop mattered so much to him. The conversation started when Romesh Ranganathan praised Cena’s song with Bumpy Knuckles, admitting he initially had doubts about a wrestler trying to become a rapper. However, hearing Cena work with established hip-hop talent completely changed his opinion. Cena explained that getting legitimate artists involved was exactly what he wanted from the beginning. He wasn’t looking for an easy celebrity music project. He wanted people who actually lived and breathed hip-hop to recognize that he was serious about the genre. “That was really the the roots of like how can I get the hip-hop community like the rap community to understand that I’m I’m trying to be authentic. I’m doing my best.” Rather than simply relying on his WWE fame, Cena brought in artists from the New England hip-hop scene and worked closely with Bumpy Knuckles, also known as Freddy Foxxx, to help guide the album. “And uh we got local artists from the New England scene and we kind of had Freddy Fox Bumpy Knuckles oversee the whole thing. And that you know with with enough resource you can make anything happen.” Cena’s debut studio album, You Can’t See Me , was released in 2005 and featured his cousin Tha Trademarc. The album also gave WWE fans his entrance theme, “The Time Is Now,” which became one of the most recognizable songs in wrestling. But Cena made it clear that he wanted something more than wrestling fans buying the album because they recognized his name. He wanted experienced rappers and dedicated hip-hop listeners to hear the finished product and come away impressed. “The throughline and the ethos of it was to just make an album hopefully that hip hop heads and rappers would be like all right I didn’t see that one coming.” Ranganathan told Cena that his approach had worked, explaining that the collaboration with Bumpy Knuckles convinced him Cena wasn’t simply pretending to be a rapper. For Cena, the entire experience was also about pursuing something he genuinely loved. He described the album as a passion project and looked back on making it as something he was grateful to experience. “And of course do it to scratch an itch and it’s a passion project and that’s uh gosh what a fun experience to have gone through.” Cena eventually became one of WWE’s biggest stars and built a successful Hollywood career, but his early rap work remains a major part of his wrestling identity. His music wasn’t just another piece of WWE merchandise to him. He wanted to prove he belonged in hip-hop, and he went out of his way to earn that respect. H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.

title: Eddie Guerrero's Daughter Sherilyn Set For In-Ring Debut
raw_title: WWE legend Eddie Guerrero’s daughter set to make pro-wrestling debut
body: WWE legend Eddie Guerrero's daughter, Sherilyn Guerrero, is set to make her pro-wrestling debut . She is scheduled to make her in-ring debut for Booker T's Reality of Wrestling promotion on Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026. Guerrero was recently hosting ROW's Sherri Martel Classic when she was confronted by Mystii Marks. However, before Guerrero left the ringside area, she was slapped and attacked by Marks. Guerrero followed it up by delivering a promo and issuing a challenge to Marks for a match at the Reality of Wrestling show on Nov. 14, 2026. Guerrero began training with Booker T's Reality of Wrestling training school last year in Texas in Oct. 2025. She is currently signed to WWE in a developmental deal. She also shared a photo of herself outside of the WWE Performance Center in Orlando earlier this month. Earlier this year, in Mar. 2026, Guerrero had opened up about training with Booker T during an appearance on The Magic of Wrestling. "I started training in around October, actually, and it was really cool. I got an ankle sprain in December, so I had to sit out for a bit and then just start it back," she said. "Something about recovery helps you kind of recalibrate your intention and things with this. And oh man, training is just different now. Coming back into it and the coaches I have, they're so great in the ring and out the ring. She was hopeful about having her debut match before the end of 2026 and it now is very close to getting fulfilled. Within a year of beginning her wrestling training, Guerrero will be having her first in-ring match against Mystii Marks.
summary: Sherilyn Guerrero will make her pro wrestling debut against Mystii Marks for Booker T's Reality of Wrestling promotion on November 14, 2026. She began training at Booker T's Reality of Wrestling school in October 2025 and is currently signed to a WWE developmental deal. The matchup was set after Marks slapped and attacked Guerrero during the recent Sherri Martel Classic event, prompting a promo and challenge from Guerrero.

title: On the Record: John Cena Explains How He Responds When People Tell Him Wrestling Is Fake
raw_title: John Cena Explains How He Responds When People Tell Him Wrestling Is Fake
summary_src: John Cena has heard the “wrestling is fake” line more times than he can count, but it apparently doesn’t bother him at all. Instead of getting annoyed, Cena says he immediately realizes the person probably has no idea what professional wrestling actually involves.
body: During an appearance on The Romesh Ranganathan Show alongside Jessica Biel, Cena got onto the subject while discussing another stereotype — that London has bad food. Cena called that idea a sign of ignorance and quickly realized it reminded him of something wrestling fans have probably heard plenty of times. “So, to me, that is a sign of ignorance. Like someone has not been to London in a long time. People come up to me all the time like, ‘You know wrestling’s fake, right?’ To me, I don’t get mad at that, right? That is an indication of they have no idea what I do. Like, ‘Oh, I gotta start you from square one.’ Okay.” Cena didn’t leave the comparison there either. He explained that London has become one of his favorite cities partly because of its coffee culture, international restaurants and the sheer number of different cuisines available. “The reason I love London, maybe yours is similar, is because it’s such a food city. I love cafes and great coffee, and Londoners take that seriously. There’s like books this thick of greatest coffee places in London that come out every year, and places fight to be in that book.” As far as Cena is concerned, anybody still claiming London doesn’t have good food probably hasn’t spent enough time actually exploring what’s available. He believes the reputation might have made more sense decades ago, but doesn’t think it reflects the city today. “And it is such a city for great chefs and great restaurants of international appeal. Any, the best of any cuisine you want, you can find it here. People who say that there’s no good food in London, it is just, they have no clue. They’ve either never been or they’ve never looked hard enough or they don’t know what’s going on. Maybe 35, 40 years ago you could say that with some tact. Not now. That does not apply. You’re clearly going to the wrong places, and you just haven’t done your homework.” That’s when Cena brought things right back to wrestling. For him, hearing somebody casually dismiss professional wrestling as “fake” tells him they’re looking at the business through an outdated or surface-level understanding of what wrestlers actually do. “It is literally like, ‘So, you know wrestling’s fake, right?’ Or like, ‘Is wrestling fake?’ Like, ‘Oh, okay. Sit down. It’s been a while. It’s been a while. It’s not the ’70s anymore. Come on, let’s talk.’ You know, I feel bad for the person who says that. I hope you don’t shoulder any burden because that’s not the truth. But man, London is such a great food city.” After spending decades inside the ring, Cena clearly isn’t interested in getting defensive every time somebody throws the “fake” label at wrestling. His reaction is basically the opposite — he sees it as a sign that there’s a much bigger conversation to be had about what professional wrestling actually is. body: 0 Former WWE Superstar Kairi (Kairi Sane) is reportedly still negotiating with AEW amid offers from Japanese promotions. title: Stacks Updates Fans After NXT Live Event Injury
raw_title: Stacks provides update following injury at NXT live event: ‘The show goes on’
summary_src: Channing "Stacks" Lorenzo broke silence on his recent injury on Sunday night, telling fans that "The show goes on."
body: NXT’s Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo is being a cool customer about his recent setback. News broke just over a week ago that Stacks suffered a serious injury at NXT’s live event in Sudbury, Ontario, Canada. Local attendees saw Stacks take a hard fall to the floor during a tag match, an injury which required him to be stretchered out of the venue. After being off TV for last week’s episode of NXT TV, Stacks broke his silence in a new Instagram Story update. Posting a photo of him in the hospital, seemingly from the night he was injured, he wrote: “Doc was worried about my ‘attitude’ … Told ’em it’s a preexisting condition. The show goes on.” A second image showed Stacks on his feet and back to working out: “Right back to the grind,” the caption reads. While it remains unclear how long Stacks could be out of the ring for, the recent updates show the former Heritage Cup Champion is in good spirits as he continues to recover.
summary: Channing “Stacks” Lorenzo was stretchered out of an NXT live event in Sudbury, Ontario after taking a hard fall during a tag team match. The former Heritage Cup Champion missed last week’s episode of NXT TV and shared hospital photos on Instagram along with the message that the doctor was worried about his attitude, which he called a preexisting condition. In a follow-up post, Stacks showed himself back on his feet and working out while stating he is right back to the grind.

title: 5 Superstars Who Could Shake Up WWE Survivor Series: WarGames In Houston
raw_title: 5 Superstars Who Could Shake Up WWE Survivor Series: WarGames In Houston
body: Punk held the Undisputed WWE Championship from the July 6 Raw until Sept. 11, when Sami Zayn took it in Mexico City. Kevin Owens returned from neck fusion surgery on Night Two of SummerSlam on Aug. 2 and won a four-way match for a title shot. Punk retained against Owens on the Aug. 21 SmackDown in Toronto. During the Sept. 11 title change, Owens accidentally struck Punk with the belt. Owens went after Punk throughout the men's Money in the Bank ladder match on Oct. 10 in New Orleans, using a steel ladder, low blows, and a Pop-Up Spinebuster. Neither man won the briefcase. Survivor Series is familiar ground for Punk, who returned to WWE at the 2023 edition and has worked both men's WarGames matches after that. On the Oct. 16 SmackDown, general manager Nick Aldis checked on Owens in the medical office before Punk walked in and demanded a match. Aldis said both men needed to be at 100 percent and made clear the fight should happen in an official setting. The general manager also ordered the two to stay apart. Cody Rhodes retained the Undisputed WWE Championship against Randy Orton in the WrestleMania 42 main event on April 18 in Las Vegas, then took a punt after the bell. Rhodes lost the title at Night of Champions on June 27. Orton returned on Night One of SummerSlam on Aug. 1 and hit Rhodes with an RKO during a title match against Punk. At Sunday Night's Main Event on Sept. sixth in Atlanta, Orton hit Rhodes and a referee with low blows before scoring the pin. On the Oct. 2 SmackDown, Orton pulled the referee out to stop a Rhodes pin in a Money in the Bank qualifier that Owens won. Rhodes waited in the ring for a promised face-to-face with Orton on Oct. 16, and Baron Corbin answered instead. During the Corbin match, Orton yanked Rhodes to the floor and drove the former champion into the steel steps. Rhodes won by disqualification, punted Corbin, and stared down Orton to close the show. At Survivor Series 2024 in Vancouver, Gunther retained the World Heavyweight Championship by choking out Damian Priest with a sleeper. Aldis cost Gunther a tag match at Saturday Night's Main Event, then lost by submission to the Austrian on Night One of SummerSlam. Gunther also lost a triple threat at Night of Champions and the SummerSlam four-way won by Owens. On the Sept. 25 SmackDown, Finn Balor hit Gunther with a Coup de Grace, and Punk scored the pin to take a Money in the Bank spot. Gunther attacked Danhausen before the bell on the Oct. 9 SmackDown, and Balor made the save. Gunther returned moments later and laid out Balor. Gunther vented at a chair on Oct. 16, expecting to find Aldis sitting in it. Danhausen turned around instead, wearing an arm cast and a neck brace. Gunther promised more damage. Bron Breakker pinned Punk with a Spear to win the men's WarGames match at Survivor Series 2025 in San Diego. A masked attacker, later revealed as Austin Theory, hit Punk with a superkick and a Curb Stomp right before the finish. Rhodes was also on the losing team. T

body: By Shawn Van Horn Published Oct 26, 2026, 1:00 PM EDT Shawn Van Horn is a Features Writer & Editor for The Sportster. He is also a Senior Author for Collider. Shawn has followed pro wrestling for most of his life is well-versed in current events of WWE and AEW. He lives in small town Ohio, where he likes to watch rasslin' and movies. Sign in to your TheSportster account AEW 's MJF is not only a phenomenal wrestler, but he's arguably the greatest character in the sport as a heel who rarely breaks kayfabe. At the age of 30, he's already wrestled nearly every big name AEW has to offer. Many fans once hoped to see MJF sign with WWE , where his gimmick is perfectly suited for the company's sports entertainment focus. With MJF choosing to re-sign with AEW a few years ago, it seems more likely that he'll never work with Triple H and TKO. This means fans will never get to see MJF's pick for his number one dream match. MJF has faced them all in AEW, including a few names no longer with the company, like Cody Rhodes and CM Punk . With Rhodes and Punk back in WWE, MJF will never wrestle them again unless he were to sign with WWE. Because the forbidden door will remain forever closed between AEW and WWE, fans will never get to see so many dream matches. As fun as it would be to see, MJF won't go toe-to-toe with Roman Reigns, Randy Orton, Sami Zayn, and so many others. And he'll never have an in-ring battle with the dream match he wants the most. This year, during an interview with Chris Van Vliet , MJF told the host who his ultimate dream match was. “I think this answer is going to shock people, because also, I will say I can’t pick people that are retired. John (Cena) would have been my answer, but he’s retired, so I’m gonna say Kevin Steen... "No, I want Kevin Steen, the one that I watched in Ring of Honor. Not saying Kevin Owens isn’t spectacular. Kevin Owens is one of the best wrestlers in the world, and it sucks that he’s hurt right now. It kills me. But Kevin Owens can’t exactly say some of the things that Kevin Steen was able to say back in the day. So I want Kevin Steen. That’s a dream match for me. I think that would probably go down as one of the greatest matches of all time and one of the greatest promos of all time." (h/t Fightful ) Kevin Owens is one of the best and most well known wrestlers on the planet. Since 2014, he has been signed with WWE, where he has won an NXT Championship and a Universal Title, along with several midcard belts . With how talented he is, Owens should have had several more world title runs by now, but that hasn't hurt his legacy. From his battles with Sami Zayn, to his run as an evil heel and a hilarious babyface, Owens can do it all. But before he was KO, he went by his real name of Kevin Steen in Ring of Honor. Kevin Steen was in Ring of Honor from 2007 through 2014 . There, in a company that didn't cater to families and kids, Steen could have more of a raw edge. The rumors were reported as fact elsewhere and then walked back. All along, those close to the promotion have denied that any cancellation had happened. Variety reported that WOW - Women of Wrestling , which previously aired as a syndicated weekly series distributed by Paramount, would begin to air weekly live episodes from Los Angeles' L.A Live with WOW owner Jeannie Buss having an camera appearances as part of the new season when it premieres. The belief is that the series would end as a syndicated series and instead air from one broadcast home live. There had been whispers a few years ago that if the series made it to season five, it would air live on CBS, but whether that turns out to be the case obviously remains to be seen. WOW Champion Santana Garrett was doing promotion about the fifth season as recently as last month, including an interview here on PWInsider.com. The promotion continues to release content on their YouTube channel as well as their weekly podcast, but their website has removed all references to their syndicated television series, but no events for LA Live have been officially announced. title: Sol Ruca Told She'll Likely Never Turn Heel
raw_title: Sol Ruca’s been told she’ll probably never turn heel
summary_src: If you were watching her last big NXT feud earlier this year, you might be under the impression that Sol Ruca’s already been a pro wrestling villain.
body: Even as she was being jeered on The CW though, the powers-that-be at WWE never wavered in their belief that the good vibes California girl character was the hero of that story. Ruca’s remained the babyface she’s been ever since debuting for the company four years ago, and sounds like she’s been told she’ll be playing to the crowd and popping them with Sol Snatchers for her entire career. Appearing on The Finish , the 27-year-old was asked if there’s “a world where Sol turns heel and evolves her character in that way: “I have no idea — I think I would love to be able to try that. I have been told in the past that I most likely will not be heel ever, because of just how I am naturally. I am quite a bubbly and like, light person, so I don’t know. “I feel like it’s gonna take a very special person to really get that side out of me, but I guess we’re just gonna have to wait and see.” It is a never say never business, and even John Cena turned eventually. I actually don’t think we’ll have to wait too long to officially see Ruca break bad. Creative has to have been intrigued by the reaction she was getting at the PC, and I’m sure she could lean into that and turn up the “haughty b**ch” elements of her performance. summary_src: The latest addition to the AEW calendar is a Dynamite/Collision episode from Oklahoma City this December. It was announced today that AEW’s go-home show for Worlds End 2026 will take place at OG&E Coliseum in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma on Wednesday, December 16.
body: The latest addition to the AEW calendar is a Dynamite/Collision episode from Oklahoma City this December. It was announced today that AEW’s go-home show for Worlds End 2026 will take place at OG&E Coliseum in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma on Wednesday, December 16. It will be a live Dynamite/Collision episode leading into that Saturday’s pay-per-view. Tickets are going on sale to the general public this Friday (October 30). “Oklahoma City! AEW is returning this December with #AEWDynamite & #AEWCollision LIVE at the OG&E Coliseum on Wednesday, December 16,” AEW wrote. :Witness the final moments before #AEWWorldsEnd!” Thekla, Skye Blue, The New Level (Kofi & Austin Creed), and Will Ospreay are the five wrestlers included on AEW’s advertising graphic for the show. This is AEW’s first trip to the state of Oklahoma since a January 2026 Dynamite from Tulsa. As for Oklahoma City, it’s AEW’s first time back since making its Oklahoma City debut with the 2023 edition of Holiday Bash three years ago. The Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota is hosting Worlds End 2026 on December 19. At least most of the card should be finalized after this go-home episode of Dynamite/Collision, including the Continental Classic finals being set. Worlds End is AEW’s last pay-per-view of 2026. It follows November’s Full Gear PPV, which is being held in Phoenix, Arizona on November 14. title: Legal Watch: Amber Nova, former NXT, AEW pro wrestler, arrested in Florida on DUI charge
raw_title: Amber Nova, former NXT, AEW pro wrestler, arrested in Florida on DUI charge
body: By Bob D'Angelo, Cox Media Group National Content Desk October 26, 2026 at 10:17 am PDT By Bob D'Angelo, Cox Media Group National Content Desk October 26, 2026 at 10:17 am PDT ORLANDO, Fla. — Amber Nova, who wrestled professionally for the NXT and AEW promotions, is facing DUI charges after she was arrested in Central Florida early Friday, online records state. Nova, whose legal name is Amber Judith Flora, was arrested in Orlando, according to Orange County online court records. She was accused of driving under the influence and was arrested after refusing to undergo DUI testing. Flora, 34, was released later Friday after posting $2,000 bond, court records show. Documents filed Saturday in Orange County court records indicate that the Orlando Police Department stopped Flora at around 12:38 a.m. ET on Oct. 23. Flora was arrested after refusing to take an alcohol breath test at 1:48 a.m. ET, according to an affidavit. At the Orange County Sheriff’s Office DUI testing facility, she was asked twice to provide a valid sample between 3:06 a.m. and 3:17 a.m.; however, she refused to provide a sample, the document stated. The affidavit also noted that Flora asked to speak with her attorney. According to Yahoo Sports , Flora has wrestled in several promotions, including TNA Wrestling, All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and NXT, which has its headquarters in the Orlando area. The New Jersey native worked as an emergency medical technician before she began competing in the squared circle in 2016. Yahoo Sports reported that Flora’s wrestling character is based on her father’s job as a mechanic and the 1973 Chevrolet Nova car she owns. She was driving the Nova at the time of her arrest, an arrest citation notes. Flora won the Shine Nova Championship in 2023 by defeating Ivelisse. Her most recent match occurred on Sept. 19, when she lost to Nat Castle in a match for the IWF championship in Brockport, New York, Yahoo Sports reported.

title: 10 Banned Segments WWE Had To Censor
raw_title: 10 Banned Segments WWE Had To Censor
body: Thankfully, the streaming behemoth can't get involved to limit what you read about here. They're far too busy poring over WWE content and trimming off the bits they deem offensive, insensitive and/or too violent. Sometimes, such heavy-handed PR handling is understandable, but it can get a little too much. Countless segments or moments have been censored, edited out or full on banned generally over the years. Common sense dictates that retrospectively regrettable racist skits or anything that might get the company in legal hot water should hit the bricks, but there's a mix of 'yeah, fair enough' and 'they deleted that?!' here. Top stars are included too. Brock Lesnar found himself in trouble with Netflix, so did Seth Rollins, Bron Breakker, Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan. Then, there's Vince McMahon and some of his frankly unnecessary work from a pay-per-view 20+ years ago. John Cena has been brought into the chat on SmackDown , Ric Flair planted one on a member of the women's division, Lita 'slipped out' during a raunchy, controversial in-ring moment, and Roddy Piper surely wanted to have another think about his antics at WrestleMania VI. Oh yes, it's all been kicking off on WWE's watch for a long time now. The outfit is no stranger to controversy . Whilst they'd argue against a few instances of censorship, management at TKO likely wish they could blast select entries from the mass consciousness and wash their hands of them. Did some/all of these moments deserve to get banned? You decide. The main crux of Paige's feud with Nikki Bella has been the pair's respective sexual pasts. That's it in a nutshell, and it feels like a proper throwback to the Diva days when WWE's women focused more on sexuality than pure wrestling skills. It didn't take long for things to get fraught either; Nikki has mentioned her counterpart's old sex tape more than once during promos. Paige decided to fire back in a big way on the 4 September 2026 SmackDown . There, as both traded lines about their respective pasts, the Brit unleashed a tide by saying she’d built her career “on hustle, loyalty and respect”. Meanwhile, Bella “just slept with it”. That was a clear nod towards Nikki's prior relationship with John Cena. The then-couple got engaged inside the ring at WrestleMania 33, but they'd never tie the knot before splitting. Clearly, this was something these women agreed on before the cameras started rolling, but lines like that will always grab attention. Their confrontation aired on USA Network, but Netflix cut it out of on demand replays for SmackDown. Some fans on social media have chimed in to say they don't like that approach, because wrestling is scripted entertainment and Nikki was obviously fine with what was said. Netflix didn't care. They'd made their minds up, and thus wiped the line from existence. Interestingly, WWE themselves kept the promo intact on their own YouTube and official website recaps of the show. title: Alexa Bliss Includes Daughter Travel In WWE Contract
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Says Traveling With Her Daughter Was Worked Into WWE Contract: "'That’s A Non-Negotiable'"
summary_src: Alexa Bliss speaks about being on the road with her kid. Brandi Rhodes rolled out a new episode of A Shot of Brandi, and guest appearing on the show was Alexa Bliss. Bliss dove into traveling with her daughter on the road and shared that it was included in her current WWE contract.
body: Bliss dove into traveling with her daughter on the road and shared that it was included in her current WWE contract. She added that it was a non-negotiable. “Road life’s a little different. I have my daughter with me now on the road every week.” She continued, “It’s definitely really hard, but I am in so much of the phase of I don’t want to miss anything she does. That was one of the biggest things of coming back. I worked it into my contract that she travels with me. I was like, ‘I need to be able to bring my daughter along. That’s a non-negotiable.’ She, at the time, was only barely a year, and I was like, ‘I’m not leaving her on the road multiple days a week.’ She has two touring parents because Ryan (Cabrera) tours every weekend. He has for the past 10 years. He’s still on a tour every weekend and so I said, ‘She needs to go with one of us and it’s gonna be me.’ That was just something that it’s a lot of growing pains because now instead of traveling with two cute little bags, you’re traveling with 10 because at first, it was a Pack ‘n Play, a travel Pack ‘n Play, a stroller and a car seat. Now I’m very grateful for the opportunity to bring her on the road because I get to be there for everything…” Bliss and Tatum Paxley are coming off a short reign as WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions. They held the belts for 14 days before dropping them to Michin and B-Fab.

The mother of one explained the challenges of adjusting to life on the road with a child, noting that her husband Ryan Cabrera also tours every weekend. She emphasized not wanting to miss any milestones in her daughter's life at that stage.

llm_long: Alexa Bliss revealed that traveling with her daughter is part of her current WWE contract and described it as a non-negotiable condition for her return. She explained that road life has changed since she now brings her daughter along every week.

Bliss noted that it is really hard but she does not want to miss any of her daughter's milestones, which became one of the biggest factors in deciding to come back. At the time of her return her daughter was barely a year old, so she insisted on not leaving her behind for multiple days a week.

Bliss stated that her husband Ryan Cabrera tours every weekend and has done so for the past 10 years, leading her to decide that their daughter should travel with one of them and that it would be her. She described the experience as involving a lot of growing pains, shifting from traveling with two small bags to managing 10 items including a Pack ‘n Play, travel Pack ‘n Play, stroller and car seat.

Bliss expressed gratitude for the opportunity to bring her daughter on the road so she can be present for everything. Bliss and Tatum Paxley recently ended a 14-day reign as WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions after losing the titles to Michin and B-Fab.

We’re also checking out standout action from Combat Zone Wrestling, Beyond Wrestling, Greektown, and TWE. Whether you missed these shows or are looking for your next great match, here are my picks from October 23–25! 5. body: Nearly Average Wrestling announced NAW MERCY, a new wresting video game that draws inspiration from classic arcade games like Mortal Kombat. Nearly Average Wrestling Announces Arcade-Style Fighting Game: “NAW MERCY” LOS ANGELES, CA – The Comedy Wrestling Universe of Nearly Average Wrestling (NAW), created by actor and comedian Shane Hartline (The Pitt, Station 19, Obi-Wan), is expanding with a brand new video game, NAW MERCY. The game is being developed in partnership with Leroy Patterson of TACKBOARD GAMES. Gameplay will feel similar to a traditional arcade fighting game format and will feature an original soundtrack with music from The Jim Johnstons, Kyle Helf, and more! Inspired by classics like Mortal Kombat and WrestleMania: The Arcade Game, NAW MERCY will bring the bizarre world of NAW’s live shows and Twitch streams to life through over-the-top combat, outrageous characters, and the absurd humor synonymous with NAW. Players familiar with the NAW universe will recognize characters from NAW’s live events and weekly Twitch broadcasts, alongside recognizable faces from the wrestling world at large, including independent superstars such as EFFY, Shane Haste, and more. NAW MERCY is designed to grow, with new characters and special appearances to be added over time. Players can expect up to 4-on-4 gameplay, a story mode, unique special moves, destructible environments, and plenty of surprises inspired by the ever-expanding NAW universe. The official teaser trailer for NAW MERCY is available on NAW’s Instagram page, @nearlywrestling , and on Shane Hartline’s YouTube channel . About NAW or NEVER Created by Shane Hartline, NAW or NEVER is a wrestling comedy experience combining professional wrestling, live comedy, and audience participation. The show features aspiring performers and established personalities competing to impress celebrity guest judges through 60-second wrestling promos. NAW broadcasts live every Monday at 11 PM ET / 8 PM PT on Twitch and hosts live events. Fans can check out Fightful’s interview with Shane Hartline by clicking here .

title: Alexa Bliss Recalls Planned Reunion With Bray Wyatt

body: Alexa Bliss further reflects on her memories with Bray Wyatt. As of this writing, it has been three years since the passing of Windham Rotunda, a.k.a. Bray Wyatt. Towards the later stages of Rotunda’s first run in WWE, he was featured alongside and connected to Alexa Bliss. Bliss spoke further about Rotunda while she was on Brandi Rhodes’ ‘A Shot of Brandi’ show . Bliss had the opportunity to be a scare actor for the Wyatt Sicks’ haunted house at Halloween Horror Nights. She said that helped her say goodbye to Rotunda. Bliss also shared that they were supposed to reunite on WWE programming. “I was in it,” Bliss said about the Wyatt Sicks’ haunted house at Halloween Horror Nights. “I got to actually be a scare actor for a few hours. So I walked through it the first time… It’s super heavy because it’s all of Windham’s ideas, and that’s one thing he always said: He always wanted a house at Halloween Horror Nights and to see it happen was so cool but it was so bittersweet knowing that he would never see it. The first time I walked through… it feels like someone hit you in the gut. You’re just like, ‘Oh my God.’ But I really wanted to be in the house. I never got to have that closure with Bray because the last time I was with him, it was WrestleMania and I turned on him against Randy (Orton), and then we were supposed to join back together after this one WrestleMania and then I found out I was pregnant, and then he had gotten sick, and so he was out for a while… It was like ships in the night, and he did that interview where he was like, ‘Well, Alexa and I will always be connected in some way,’ and I just felt a sense of comfort, because I got to do the Firefly Funhouse scene, where I was next to the TV that was just playing Windham over and over and over and over and it was so cool to be a part of that again but also so heartbreaking after I did it. I felt like I finally was able to close that chapter. It’s over, and I think that was one of the first times that it actually hit me that he was actually gone, and so it was so cool to be able to do that, that Universal let me do that because I was like, I feel like this is me saying goodbye. This is me going back to where it started and this is me saying goodbye and they let me have that moment.” The entire Wyatt Sicks faction (Bo Dallas/Uncle Howdy, Nikki Cross, Joe Gacy, Dexter Lumis & Erick Rowan) was released from WWE in April 2026.

title: Jumbo Baretta Passes Away at 58 or 59
raw_title: WWF, WCW alum Jumbo Baretta passes away
summary_src: Jumbo Baretta, a Florida-based wrestler who appeared for WWF and WCW, has reportedly passed away.
body: Jumbo Baretta, a powerhouse who appeared in WCW and WWF between the 80s and 90s, has passed away. While an exact birth date isn’t known, records show that he was 58 or 59 years old. Baretta, real name Julio Barrera, had his passing announced by the Cauliflower Alley Club on Sunday afternoon. This one truly hurts. I am deeply saddened by the passing of Jumbo, a good friend whom I was honored and privileged to know for nearly 40 years. I send my sincerest condolences to his family and friends. Rest in peace old friend. pic.twitter.com/3gJyxfZnyN “I am deeply saddened by the passing of Jumbo, a good friend whom, I was honored and privileged of knowing for nearly 40 years. I send my sincerest condolences to his family and friends. Rest in peace old friend.” Born in Tampa, Florida, Baretta got his start in the mid-80s, getting trained by Boris Malenko. He pursued a career in professional wrestling shortly after becoming an accomplished amateur wrestler, winning back-to-back state titles for Hillsborough High School. Training under the watch of Malenko, Baretta latched onto wrestling quickly. “I was only supposed to come in twice a week,” he told the Tampa Bay Times in 1993. “But I came in all the time.” Early years in his career saw him work spots in Florida and Puerto Rico. By 1989, Baretta started appearing on WCW programming, standing across from talents like Sting, The Road Warriors, and The Midnight Express. He also put together numerous tours in Japan during this time period. Baretta would have a short WWF stint in 1995, appearing once on Monday Night Raw and also on the Wrestling Challenge. He would make sporadic in-ring appearances through the 2000s and early 2010s. After a career in wrestling, Baretta spent over three decades working for the city of Tampa’s Parks and Recreation.

title: By the Numbers: Saudi Arabia’s GEA Chairman Pushes WWE Crown Jewel Ticket Sales Despite Security Concerns
raw_title: Saudi Arabia’s GEA Chairman Pushes WWE Crown Jewel Ticket Sales Despite Security Concerns
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is still on for Saudi Arabia, and one of the country’s biggest entertainment officials is now actively pushing ticket sales for the show.
body: On October 26, Alalshikh took to Twitter and promoted Crown Jewel and specifically pushed the Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn match for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship. More importantly, he included a direct call for fans to buy tickets, marking the first time he’s actively promoted ticket sales for this year’s event. “Roman Reigns takes on Sami Zayn for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship at RiyadhSeason 🔥🏆 November 7 🗓️ Riyadh Season Stadium – KAFD 📍 Book your ticket now 🎟️” The timing definitely stands out because questions about Crown Jewel haven’t exactly gone away over the last few days. The show remains scheduled for November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium, but the security situation in Saudi Arabia has become a much bigger part of the conversation. Just one day earlier, the U.S. Mission Saudi Arabia announced that the State Department had ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members to leave the country. The order actually went into effect on October 23 and cited safety risks connected to attacks by Iranian-backed Houthis. “Effective October 23, 2026, the Department of State ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and U.S. government employee family members to leave Saudi Arabia due to safety risks.” The embassy also pointed to attacks on civilian airports and other infrastructure, warning that the situation could escalate quickly. U.S. government employees who remain in Saudi Arabia currently require special authorization to use airports following recent missile and drone attacks . Those travel concerns could become especially important for WWE considering how many wrestlers, employees and production staff would need to get into Riyadh for Crown Jewel. There has still been no indication that WWE or Crown Jewel itself is being targeted, and the latest promotion from Alalshikh makes it clear that Saudi officials are continuing to move forward with the event. WWE’s side has been keeping a close eye on things too. TKO executive Ari Emanuel recently confirmed that a team has been monitoring the situation daily and considering where Crown Jewel could potentially be moved if holding the event in Saudi Arabia becomes an issue. “Yeah, we have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when—and if that doesn’t happen, where we can move it. It’s a daily monitoring.” For now, though, there has been no change to the November 7 plan, and Alalshikh’s latest promotion is another strong public signal that preparations are continuing. With tickets now being actively pushed while the security situation remains fluid, the next several days could tell a lot about whether WWE’s plans stay exactly where they are. summary_src: Cody Rhodes reveals that the injury he suffered at the hands of rival Randy Orton at WWE WrestleMania 42 are still affecting him months later
body: If not for the negative reaction surrounding Pat McAfee's involvement , the talk of Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton's WrestleMania 42 match may have been the punt kick Orton delivered to Rhodes that may have legitimately connected with Rhodes' face. Months later, the wounds from that moment haven't entirely healed. Discussing the punt on "Insight with Chris Van Vliet," Rhodes admitted that he was still experiencing effects from the broken orbital bone he suffered from the match, whether it occurred via Orton's punt kick or an earlier punch . "I think we skated by with a little bit of an orbital fracture, and I think I'm mad at myself for doing so, because it's affected my work since," Rhodes said. "[It] super slowed down...you know what I mean, [my peripheral vision]. Yeah, to a degree, to a little bit. And I feel like that's...you can't go out there, QB1, and say you're in your prime and you're the best you've ever been, if you're dealing with something that's a bit of a hindrance like that. But at this point, we're out of the woods. I got through it, I showed up the next night." Rhodes may be upset with himself over working through these negative effects, but it hasn't stopped him from continuing on, including facing Orton in a Last Man Standing match at WWE Crown Jewel next month . Rhodes conceded that he was "toxic" when it came to dealing with serious injuries, but admitted he wasn't going to stray from his mindset, even as he implored others to not use him as an example. "I'm letting you know, that's not good," Rhodes said. "If you're a young wrestler, don't do it. Don't. Live to fight another day. I just, I can't. Something about me can't not want to go. I don't know what it is. I love it too much. Maybe it's ego, I don't know. But I just can't not. So yeah, that was a nasty one."

On Insight with Chris Van Vliet, Rhodes revealed the injury has slowed his peripheral vision and impacted his in-ring work since the event. He noted that he has moved past the worst of it after appearing the following night.

title: Jeff Cobb Recalls WWE Mix-Up Over Face Paint
raw_title: Jeff Cobb Says He Thinks WWE “Got Me Confused With Somebody Else” After They Told Him “To Wear The Paint Like You Did In Japan”
body: Jeff Cobb, who wrestled as JC Mateo, was released from WWE back on May 2nd, 2026 about one year into his three year deal with the company. Cobb recently spoke to SOTO619 after his match with Lio Rush at PRODUCE Wrestling, and was asked which was more annoying, to wrestle in face paint or in a mask. Cobb wore a mask during his time with Lucha Underground, when he wrestled as Matanza, and wore face paint in WWE as JC Mateo while with the MFT’s. He answered that paint was more annoying because he had never done that previously, before revealing that WWE told him, “ you’re going to wear the paint like you did in Japan .” However, he never wore paint in Japan. Adding, “ I think they got me confused with somebody else. “ “Paint. Because I’ve never done that before. Although, to be fair, I’ve never done the mask thing before. But the paint was truly different. Because I was told, you’re going to wear the paint like you did in Japan, and I never wore paint in Japan. I think they got me confused with somebody else. But yeah, paint was hard because I had to find paint. But, yeah, the paint was definitely the hardest just for the fact that, like, with the mask, I could put it on. I couldn’t breathe, but I could put it on, and then when I’m done, I could take it off. But the paint took forever to get off. I had to use the wipes. Then I found out the wipes that I used got recalled.” Jeff Cobb made wrestled his first post WWE match for PRODUCE Wrestling against Lio Rush back in August after his 90 day non-compete clause had expired. Cobb then made a surprise return to New Japan Pro Wrestling during the G1 Climax 36 finals on August 16, 2026 , turning on Callum Newman and joining Unbound Co. title: Alexa Bliss Recalls Planned Reunion With Bray Wyatt
raw_title: Alexa Bliss & Bray Wyatt Were Supposed To Reunite On WWE TV
body: Alexa Bliss further reflects on her memories with Bray Wyatt. As of this writing, it has been three years since the passing of Windham Rotunda, a.k.a. Bray Wyatt. Towards the later stages of Rotunda’s first run in WWE, he was featured alongside and connected to Alexa Bliss. Bliss spoke further about Rotunda while she was on Brandi Rhodes’ ‘A Shot of Brandi’ show . Bliss had the opportunity to be a scare actor for the Wyatt Sicks’ haunted house at Halloween Horror Nights. She said that helped her say goodbye to Rotunda. Bliss also shared that they were supposed to reunite on WWE programming. “I was in it,” Bliss said about the Wyatt Sicks’ haunted house at Halloween Horror Nights. “I got to actually be a scare actor for a few hours. So I walked through it the first time… It’s super heavy because it’s all of Windham’s ideas, and that’s one thing he always said: He always wanted a house at Halloween Horror Nights and to see it happen was so cool but it was so bittersweet knowing that he would never see it. The first time I walked through… it feels like someone hit you in the gut. You’re just like, ‘Oh my God.’ But I really wanted to be in the house. I never got to have that closure with Bray because the last time I was with him, it was WrestleMania and I turned on him against Randy (Orton), and then we were supposed to join back together after this one WrestleMania and then I found out I was pregnant, and then he had gotten sick, and so he was out for a while… It was like ships in the night, and he did that interview where he was like, ‘Well, Alexa and I will always be connected in some way,’ and I just felt a sense of comfort, because I got to do the Firefly Funhouse scene, where I was next to the TV that was just playing Windham over and over and over and over and it was so cool to be a part of that again but also so heartbreaking after I did it. I felt like I finally was able to close that chapter. It’s over, and I think that was one of the first times that it actually hit me that he was actually gone, and so it was so cool to be able to do that, that Universal let me do that because I was like, I feel like this is me saying goodbye. This is me going back to where it started and this is me saying goodbye and they let me have that moment.” The entire Wyatt Sicks faction (Bo Dallas/Uncle Howdy, Nikki Cross, Joe Gacy, Dexter Lumis & Erick Rowan) was released from WWE in April 2026.

Bliss revealed that she and Wyatt were originally supposed to reunite on WWE television.

title: Alexa Bliss Includes Daughter Travel In WWE Contract
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Says Traveling With Kid Was Put In WWE Contract
body: Bliss dove into traveling with her daughter on the road and shared that it was included in her current WWE contract. She added that it was a non-negotiable. “Road life’s a little different. I have my daughter with me now on the road every week.” She continued, “It’s definitely really hard, but I am in so much of the phase of I don’t want to miss anything she does. That was one of the biggest things of coming back. I worked it into my contract that she travels with me. I was like, ‘I need to be able to bring my daughter along. That’s a non-negotiable.’ She, at the time, was only barely a year, and I was like, ‘I’m not leaving her on the road multiple days a week.’ She has two touring parents because Ryan (Cabrera) tours every weekend. He has for the past 10 years. He’s still on a tour every weekend and so I said, ‘She needs to go with one of us and it’s gonna be me.’ That was just something that it’s a lot of growing pains because now instead of traveling with two cute little bags, you’re traveling with 10 because at first, it was a Pack ‘n Play, a travel Pack ‘n Play, a stroller and a car seat. Now I’m very grateful for the opportunity to bring her on the road because I get to be there for everything…” Bliss and Tatum Paxley are coming off a short reign as WWE Women’s Tag Team Champions. They held the belts for 14 days before dropping them to Michin and B-Fab.

title: Ilja Dragunov Shares Thoughts On GUNTHER's Recent WWE Booking
raw_title: AEW's Ilja Dragunov Comments On How WWE Has Used GUNTHER Since He Retired John Cena
summary_src: Ex-WWE star Ilja Dragunov reflects on GUNTHER's rise and if his run still remains as relevant as it did before.
body: WWE One of the most acclaimed rivalries to have ever come out of the now defunct "WWE NXT UK" was between former WWE star Ilja Dragunov and the former NXT United Kingdom Champion GUNTHER (WALTER). Refusing to give up, despite having it all stacked against him, Dragunov was the only man to topple GUNTHER of his historic 870-day reign to become the new champion at "WWE NXT" TakeOver 36. Since their brutal rivalry, GUNTHER went on to retire the likes of Hall of Famers Goldberg, AJ Styles, and the former "Never Seen 17" World Champion, John Cena. But now, it seems GUNTHER's push has plateaued, which fans, along with Dragunov, have seen as of late. "I guess my feelings are the same feelings as a lot of other people share. If you are the person to retire John Cena, it's kind of like a standard that you should keep a certain level of that, in my opinion," GUNTHER's former on-screen adversary told Ariel Helwani. "For me, he is one of the best. He will be one of the best of all time. He's a dear friend of mine for, I don't know, maybe since 2014, '15...We are dear friends to each other... I know he's good. I know he will always do good and whatever he does, it's going to be awesome. But I can, of course, imagine that after the standard that he set and the standard of how he got betrayed, that this is not necessarily the level that we're working at right now." Not able to reach a contractual agreement, Dragunov left the WWE after seven years this past August to join AEW, where he made his first appearance for the promotion at WrestleDream. As for GUNTHER, he is still waiting in the wings for another shot at the Undisputed Championship. In the meantime, he's feuding with Finn Balor.
summary: Former NXT UK rival Ilja Dragunov discussed GUNTHER's current WWE trajectory after the Austrian star retired John Cena. Dragunov noted that beating Cena should maintain a high standard of booking and expressed that many fans feel the same way. He described GUNTHER as one of the best performers of all time and a close friend since around 2014 or 2015.

body: Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will settle their feud in a Last Man Standing match at WWE Crown Jewel on Nov. 7. The show takes place at Riyadh Season Stadium in Saudi Arabia. General Manager Nick Aldis made the match on the Oct. 23 SmackDown. The two men share 18 years of history and seven months of hostility. In 2008, Orton formed The Legacy, a faction built around Rhodes and Ted DiBiase Jr. The group backed Orton through three WWE Championship reigns in 2009. The Legacy members met in a triple threat match at WrestleMania XXVI on March 28, 2010. Orton won that bout by pinning DiBiase after an RKO. The former stablemates landed on the same side years later. Orton returned from an 18-month absence at Survivor Series: WarGames on Nov. 25, 2023, as the fifth member of Rhodes’ team. On the Oct. 3, 2025, SmackDown, the pair lost a tag team match to Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed of The Vision. Reed scored the pin on Orton. Orton won the men’s Elimination Chamber match on Feb. 28 to earn a title shot at WrestleMania 42. Rhodes took the Undisputed WWE Championship from Drew McIntyre on the March 6 SmackDown. Orton attacked Rhodes on SmackDown one week later. Rhodes retained against Orton on Night One of WrestleMania 42 on April 18 with a Cross Rhodes. Orton attacked after the bell and closed the show standing over Rhodes with the title belt in hand. WWE television did not see Orton again until SummerSlam on Aug. 1. By then, the championship belonged to CM Punk. Sami Zayn won it at Night of Champions on June 27 by rolling up Rhodes in a triple threat with Gunther, and Punk beat Zayn on the July 6 Raw. At SummerSlam, Orton came through the crowd during Rhodes’ title match against Punk and hit an RKO. Punk won with a GTS. The punt has hit Rhodes at two WrestleManias. Orton used it during the WrestleMania XXVI triple threat and again after the bell at WrestleMania 42. Rhodes lined up the same kick late in the Sept. 6 headliner of Sunday Night’s Main Event at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. Orton raised both hands, Rhodes paused, and referee Eddie Arango stepped between the two. Orton landed low blows on Arango and Rhodes, then won with an RKO, as referee Charles Robinson crawled back in to count. Baron Corbin interrupted a Rhodes promo on the Oct. 16 SmackDown, and the two had an impromptu match that ended in a disqualification when Orton interfered. Orton missed a punt at Rhodes on the outside, and Corbin blocked a Rhodes attempt on Orton. The show ended with a super Cody Cutter and a punt from Rhodes to Corbin, as Orton watched. Orton has 14 world titles to his name. One of those reigns began with a Last Man Standing win over Triple H at No Mercy in 2007. Triple H beat Orton under the same rules at One Night Stand on June 1, 2008, and Orton broke his collarbone in the loss. title: Legal Watch: Amber Nova, former NXT, AEW pro wrestler, arrested in Florida on DUI charge - WSB-TV
raw_title: Amber Nova, former NXT, AEW pro wrestler, arrested in Florida on DUI charge - WSB-TV
body: By Bob D'Angelo, Cox Media Group National Content Desk October 26, 2026 at 1:17 pm EDT By Bob D'Angelo, Cox Media Group National Content Desk October 26, 2026 at 1:17 pm EDT ORLANDO, Fla. — Amber Nova, who wrestled professionally for the NXT and AEW promotions, is facing DUI charges after she was arrested in Central Florida early Friday, online records state. Nova, whose legal name is Amber Judith Flora, was arrested in Orlando, according to Orange County online court records. She was accused of driving under the influence and was arrested after refusing to undergo DUI testing. Flora, 34, was released later Friday after posting $2,000 bond, court records show. Documents filed Saturday in Orange County court records indicate that the Orlando Police Department stopped Flora at around 12:38 a.m. ET on Oct. 23. Flora was arrested after refusing to take an alcohol breath test at 1:48 a.m. ET, according to an affidavit. At the Orange County Sheriff’s Office DUI testing facility, she was asked twice to provide a valid sample between 3:06 a.m. and 3:17 a.m.; however, she refused to provide a sample, the document stated. The affidavit also noted that Flora asked to speak with her attorney. According to Yahoo Sports , Flora has wrestled in several promotions, including TNA Wrestling, All Elite Wrestling (AEW) and NXT, which has its headquarters in the Orlando area. The New Jersey native worked as an emergency medical technician before she began competing in the squared circle in 2016. Yahoo Sports reported that Flora’s wrestling character is based on her father’s job as a mechanic and the 1973 Chevrolet Nova car she owns. She was driving the Nova at the time of her arrest, an arrest citation notes. Flora won the Shine Nova Championship in 2023 by defeating Ivelisse. Her most recent match occurred on Sept. 19, when she lost to Nat Castle in a match for the IWF championship in Brockport, New York, Yahoo Sports reported.
summary: Per WSB-TV: nova, whose legal name is Amber Judith Flora, was arrested in Orlando, per Orange County online court records. She was accused of driving under the influence and was arrested after refusing to undergo DUI testing.

title: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved — TNA Impact 9/10/2026
raw_title: TNA Impact 9/10/2026: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
body: TNA Wrestling Two of TNA's top titles were put on the line during tonight's "Impact," while the company also continued building various storylines on the road to Bound For Glory 2026. With such a busy show, our crew had no problem finding things to love and to hate. Former World Champion Moose is willing to put his entire TNA Wrestling career on the line, for a simple rematch against Frankie Kazarian? I can understand Moose wanting a rematch against the self-proclaimed "King of TNA," especially after he inadvertently allowed Kazarian to win their Escape The Cage match at Lockdown. Is it really worth putting his job (in storyline) at risk, though? To me, the terms of this upcoming match seem pretty extreme and imbalanced. As far as we know right now, no additional stipulations — such as a steel cage, no disqualification, or even Kazarian's newly-minuted crown — have been added to it, which means the stakes are high for just one person, and that's Moose. If Kazarian wins, he'll get bragging rights as being the one to send Moose, a 10-year company veteran, out of TNA. If he loses, he doesn't actually lose anything; at worst, the score for their recent feud would be even and likely lead to a rubber match. Even more puzzling is the fact that these career-implications came out of nowhere. We know that Moose signed a five-year contract in 2023 , which means he should have at least two years left there. The timing just doesn't line up. I'm all for weaponizing one's career as a match stipulation when it fits the story surrounding it. This Kazarian-Moose narrative as is just doesn't seem juicy enough to warrant it yet, though. TNA Wrestling A few weeks ago after Lockdown aired, I wrote a love piece on Elayna Black's performance in her Knockouts World Title challenge against Xia Brookside. And this week, I'm giving her another love. Well, not just to her, but her match with Heather by Elegance tonight. Black and Heather put on a barnburner of a fight. I like that there was no B.S.; it was a straight-to-the point wrestling match. Both women looked fantastic with their calls and responses. There weren't many shenanigans tonight by the Elegance Brand, which was a breath of fresh air for a change. Black's gut wrench suplex was crisp. I'm glad she came out the victor in this contest. I felt tonight's opening contest brought me back to a time when the Beautiful People roamed the Impact Zone, and I couldn't help but to smile a bit. As we know, TNA has changed its formula on how it handles its promotion now. A lot has been stripped down. However, its stripes haven't changed with how dominant the Knockouts Division truly is. title: Jesse Ventura Criticizes Trump on Livestream
raw_title: Jesse Ventura unloads on Donald Trump, pushes conspiracy theories amid WWE absence
summary_src: Jesse Ventura returned to the WWE fold in 2024, and was part of the relaunch of a franchise he was once synonymous with, Saturday Night’s Main Event.
body: When Saturday Night’s Main Event returned with much fanfare in 2024, so did Ventura . However, The Body reportedly upset some of the powers-that-be at WWE when he vocally criticized a steel cage match between Damien Priest and Drew McIntyre, and his appearances at the event were subsequently more limited. Veteran wrestling journalist Dave Meltzer reported at the time Ventura only had a one-year deal with WWE, and that it had expired. Nevertheless, Jesse did make a special appearance during the pre-show program of Saturday Night’s Main Event on the night of John Cena’s final match in December 2025. Further appearances seem unlikely based on Ventura’s recent Twitch livestream with controversial left-wing voice Hasan Piker. The 75-year-old hasn’t changed his opinion on President Trump, calling the Republican a “coward” and a “bully.” The always-outspoken former Minnesota governor also dove into other controversial waters by repeating unfounded conspiracy theories related to the 9/11 attacks on New York City and the assassination of John F. Kennedy. A portion of his talk with Piker did focus on wrestling, notably when he discussed trying to start a union in the then-WWF in the 1980’s. As he’s previously said in the past , he claimed the effort was torpedoed when Hulk Hogan told Vince McMahon of the plan. “Hulk Hogan’s an office stooge. Now, let me explain: In the earlier years of territory wrestling, the worst thing you could be is an office stooge,” Ventura said. “They’re the most unliked people in the business.” But his most seething comments came at the expense of the current commander-in-chief. “If Donald Trump would’ve gone in the military, he would’ve been the guy that wet his bed, cried for his mom, went hysterical, and would be carted out in the middle of the night. The man’s a coward,” Ventura said to Piker, adding, “He’s a bully. All bullies are cowards. That’s why they’re bullies.” As a veteran of the Vietnam War, Ventura has frequently contrasted himself with Trump, who received five deferments from military draft during the conflict. “My whole family has fought at war for this country — my entire immediate family. Here’s the part that pisses me off, Hasan: I did two tours, 17 months, so did my brother. Southeast Asia, right? That was at the same time Donald Trump was running and hiding like the coward he is. Why didn’t he join us in the Vietnam War? I’ve heard him talk. He’s said he should be a general.” Piker injected by saying Trump “had bone spurs,” which was a reason Trump cited for a medical exemption. “Well, fine and dandy, never stopped him from golf, did it? I’ve never heard him cancel a golf date,” Ventura said. The former Navy Seal also attacked the Republicans as a whole, calling them “fascist and anti-Constitution.” “I support the Constitution. If you want to change, then change the Constitution. If you want to change things, do it the way it’s supposed to be done,” he said. “Now, you don’t just go to war unconstitutionally.
summary: Jesse Ventura appeared on a Twitch livestream with Hasan Piker where he called President Trump a coward and a bully. The 75-year-old former governor also repeated conspiracy theories about the 9/11 attacks and the JFK assassination. Ventura's recent WWE involvement included a limited role at Saturday Night’s Main Event in 2024 and a pre-show appearance in December 2025, but further appearances now seem unlikely.

title: On the Record: Brooke Hogan Makes It Clear She Has No Beef With WWE Stars After Hulk Hogan Tribute Comments
raw_title: Brooke Hogan Makes It Clear She Has No Beef With WWE Stars After Hulk Hogan Tribute Comments
summary_src: Brooke Hogan wants everyone to know she has no problem with WWE Superstars. After her comments about the company’s tribute to Hulk Hogan were taken as a shot at the roster, Brooke is clearing things up. She says she never accused WWE stars of being the problem.
body: On October 26, 2026, Brooke addressed the situation on Instagram Stories, specifically responding to reporters who suggested she had an issue with WWE talent. She made it clear that wasn’t what she said. “Hey reporters: I don’t have beef with the stars of WWE. Nor did I say that. Do your job right or don’t do it at all.” Brooke went on to explain that she’s talking about people who attended public tributes for her father despite, in her view, doing very little for him when he was alive. She believes some were more interested in being seen on camera than actually supporting him during his health problems. “I’m saying I watched people show up to public tributes… that didn’t give a shit when I was in the trenches with him. But they’ll show up to get their face on camera…” And Brooke made sure to point out that some of the people she’s talking about weren’t just connected to wrestling. She included people who were supposed to be close to her father. The clarification comes after Brooke shared a photo from WWE’s tribute to Hulk Hogan , which showed Triple H, WWE Superstars, legends, and officials standing together to honor the late WWE Hall of Famer. Brooke questioned how much time the people pictured had actually spent visiting her father in the hospital. “Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed.” Her original post put the people in that photo under scrutiny, but Brooke’s latest statement makes clear she doesn’t have a personal issue with WWE stars. This also comes after Brooke expressed her frustration over the sale of Hulk Hogan’s Clearwater Beach mansion and accused unnamed individuals of profiting from the property . Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.

title: Backstage Buzz: WWE Signs Former AAA Talent for Backstage Role
raw_title: WWE Signs Former AAA Talent for Backstage Role
summary_src: WWE is bringing another veteran into the mix at AAA, and this time it’s someone who already knows the company pretty well. Ricky Marvin has signed a new deal to return to AAA as a trainer and occasional producer, putting his decades of wrestling experience to work behind the scenes.
body: According to False Finish , Marvin has agreed to return to the WWE-owned promotion, where he’ll help train talent and occasionally produce matches. The move brings him back to a company where he previously held championship gold, although his responsibilities will be much different this time around. False Finish shared the following update on his signing: “Sources tell False Finish that Ricky Marvin has signed with Lucha Libre AAA as a trainer and occasional producer.” Marvin has plenty of history with AAA. He previously competed under the Bengala character before returning to his Ricky Marvin name. He later became part of Los OGTs alongside Averno and Chessman, with the group winning the AAA World Trios Championship. The Mexican wrestling veteran has been around since 1995, making his professional debut when he was just 15 years old. He went on to build a career that took him across Mexico, Japan, and the United States, earning a reputation for his fast-paced wrestling style. Some of Marvin’s biggest accomplishments came during his lengthy run with Pro Wrestling NOAH in Japan. He captured the GHC Junior Heavyweight Championship and won the GHC Junior Heavyweight Tag Team Championship three times, working alongside names such as Kotaro Suzuki, Taiji Ishimori, and Super Crazy. He also spent time in CMLL, where he held the Mexican National Lightweight Championship and CMLL Japan Super Lightweight Championship. His career included appearances in Lucha Underground, giving him experience working in several different wrestling environments. Now Marvin is returning to AAA at a time when the promotion is operating under WWE’s ownership. WWE announced its acquisition of AAA alongside Fillip in April 2025, bringing the Mexican promotion into its growing wrestling operation. For Marvin, the new position means he’ll be helping the next generation rather than focusing entirely on his own matches. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll also wrestle for AAA, but his new responsibilities will put him in a position to work directly with the company’s talent. WWE continues making changes behind the scenes at AAA, and bringing back someone with Marvin’s experience gives the promotion another veteran who knows the Mexican wrestling business inside and out. Now the question is how much influence he’ll have on the talent and matches fans see going forward. What do you think about WWE bringing Ricky Marvin back to AAA as a trainer and producer? Let us know your thoughts in the comments. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.
summary: Per False Finish , Marvin has agreed to return to the WWE-owned promotion, where he’ll help train talent and occasionally produce matches. False Finish shared the after update on his signing: Sources tell False Finish that Ricky Marvin has inked a deal with Lucha Libre AAA as a trainer and occasional producer.

title: Alexa Bliss Requires Daughter Travel in WWE Deal
raw_title: Alexa Bliss Had a Non-Negotiable WWE Demand in Current Contract
body: During an appearance on A Shot of Brandi with host Brandi Rhodes, Bliss discussed life on the road after giving birth to her daughter and explained a condition she built into her WWE contract. "It's definitely really hard, but I'm in so much of the phase of, 'I don't want to miss anything she does,'" Bliss said. "So that was one of the biggest things about coming back. I worked it into my contract that she travels with me. I was like, 'I need to be able to bring my daughter along. That's non-negotiable,' because at the time, she was barely a year old, and I was like, 'I'm not leaving her on the road multiple days a week.'" Bliss explained that her schedule was not the only one the family had to plan around. Her husband, musician Ryan Cabrera, also spends much of his time touring. "She has two touring parents because Ryan tours every weekend. He has for the past 10 years. He's still on tour every weekend," Bliss said. "And so I said, 'She needs to go with one of us, and it's going to be me.'" She admitted that bringing a young child on the road came with an adjustment period. "That was just something that involved a lot of growing pains because now, instead of traveling with two cute little bags, you're traveling with 10 because you have, at first, a Pack 'n Play, a travel Pack 'n Play, a stroller, and a car seat," she said. "Now I'm very grateful for the opportunity to bring her on the road because I get to be there for everything." Bliss also opened up about Bray Wyatt during the same conversation, saying the two were set to reunite on television before her pregnancy and Wyatt's illness got in the way. "I never got to have that closure with Bray because the last time I was with him it was WrestleMania," she said, adding that they "were supposed to join back together after this one WrestleMania, and then I found out I was pregnant." The WrestleMania she referenced was WrestleMania 37 in April 2021, where Bliss turned on Wyatt during his match with Randy Orton. Wyatt died in August 2023. Bliss stepped away from WWE after challenging Bianca Belair for the Raw Women's Championship at the Royal Rumble in January 2023, and she announced her pregnancy later that year. She returned to the company as a surprise entrant in the women's Royal Rumble match in February 2025. Since her return, Bliss has worked her way back into the title picture. She and Tatum Paxley won the WWE Women's Tag Team Championship from Fatal Influence on the October 9 episode of SmackDown, with Bliss stepping in after Charlotte Flair was attacked backstage by Jade Cargill, Michin and B-Fab before the match. Bliss' comments show how much the travel schedule can shape a wrestler's decision to come back. WWE's calendar keeps talent on the road for several days a week, and for a parent with a young child, that can be the deciding factor. llm_long: Jumbo Baretta, whose real name was Julio Barrera, has passed away at the age of 59. The Cauliflower Alley Club confirmed the news of his death in a social media post on Sunday afternoon. Born in Tampa, Florida, Baretta was an accomplished amateur wrestler who won back-to-back state titles for Hillsborough High School before turning pro.

He began his professional wrestling career in 1986 after being trained by Boris Malenko. Baretta competed in Championship Wrestling from Florida, the World Wrestling Council in Puerto Rico, and various NWA territories in his early years. In 1989 he won the NWA Florida Tag Team Championship alongside Dennis Knight before losing the titles to Lou Perez and Mark Starr one month later.

That same year he started appearing in WCW where he faced opponents including Sting, Tommy Rich, the Rock 'n' Roll Express, the Road Warriors, and the Midnight Express. He also participated in tours for Japan's Universal Wrestling Federation during that period.
By 1995 Baretta had wrestled a handful of matches in WWE, losing to Kama as well as to Eli Blu and Jacob Blu.

title: Jeff Jarrett Defends Comedy In Wrestling
raw_title: WWE HOFer Jeff Jarrett Pushes Back On 'Funny Don't Draw Money'
body: Andrade El Idolo may have successfully defended his AEW National Championship against Tommaso Ciampa at AEW WrestleDream , but the talk of their match was less about the result and more regarding pants. Not only did the match feature Andrade taking off his ring pants, as has become a staple of his act, but Ciampa countered him by taking of his own wrestling trunks to reveal another pair, followed by him attacking, and even attempting a pinfall, on Andrade's pants. The comedic spot drew a mixed reaction from many watching at home, but that's not what matters most to Jeff Jarrett. Analyzing the spot on "My World," Jarrett talked up the positive crowd reception the spot got, and pushed back against the idea that comedy wrestling doesn't draw money. "'Funny don't draw money' is such a situational...I just don't think you can paint...creative is subjective," Jarrett said. "Period, just period. But here's the thing...look I've had a long career, so I have been a part of Saturday Morning Memphis TV, I've been apart of 'Superstars' and 'Challenge' and 'Raw' and 'Nitro' and 'Thunder' and 'Worldwide' and 'Impact,' we can go on and on and on. "And when you have a live, quote unquote, focus group, for the most part they're going to tell you 'Did that work or not?' Conrad, you had a live studio audience watching, but we also had, I don't know, what was it, 7 or 8K at the financial arena? Did you hear the reaction? So I just think, and I get it, to each his own. It's not for everybody." Despite the controversy, Andrade and Ciampa's issues don't appear to be over, as Ciampa attacked Andrade this past Saturday on "Collision" before being stopped by Andrade's stablemate "Speedball" Mike Bailey. As such, it appears the two have another match on the horizon, as well as another chance to use Andrade's pants to comedic effect.
summary: During an AEW WrestleDream title match, Andrade El Idolo removed his ring pants and Tommaso Ciampa responded by stripping his trunks to reveal another pair underneath before attacking and attempting to pin the pants. Jeff Jarrett analyzed the comedic spot on his "My World" podcast and highlighted the strong positive reaction it received from the live crowd. The WWE Hall of Famer pushed back against the notion that "funny don't draw money," stressing that creative is subjective based on his extensive experience across multiple promotions.

The wrestling world is still reeling from the untimely deaths of The Butcher and PAC last month. At Progress Chapter 199, where he battled Luke Jacobs, Eddie Kingston revealed that he didn’t leave his house for five days after the deaths of Williams and PAC and seriously considered leaving the business. I don’t know why you guys like me; I really don’t, but I thank you guys so much. Every fan who hit me up to tell me your story about mental health and your f**ked-up life, and you tell me I helped you, bullsh*t, you helped me,” Eddie Kingston said.
