title: Sami Zayn echoes Bret Hart's 1997 attitude shift
raw_title: Raw recap & reactions (Oct. 26, 2026): How Sami Zayn echoes Bret Hart’s 1997
summary_src: Bad to Be Good I don’t feel old but today is the day where I officially sound old. The 1996 Survivor Series turns 30 in a few weeks. That night in Madison Square Garden welcomed Bret Hart back to the game for his first match since WrestleMania XII.
body: Link WWE Marcus Benjamin has loved wrestling since his early days on the planet. He once Superkicked a tooth out of a friend’s mouth. Sweet Chin Music indeed. He’s analyzed and covered wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2021. Bad to Be Good I don’t feel old but today is the day where I officially sound old. The 1996 Survivor Series turns 30 in a few weeks. That night in Madison Square Garden welcomed Bret Hart back to the game for his first match since WrestleMania XII . Bret found himself in a very different WWF than the one he left that fateful night in Anaheim. He wrestled the man who became the catalyst for a new attitude in the territory, and witnessed a different dynamic. Fans cheered Steve Austin but gave the traditional babyfaces tepid responses. That shift inspired a heel turn several months later and gave us Bret at his peak. Seriously, the man was on fire in ‘97. He was pissed at the audience for not responding to him how they used to. He hated that someone like Stone Cold got the props and respect usually saved for clean-cut cats like Bret. The Hitman saw himself as not just a good guy but the good guy. He didn’t change; American values changed. Sami Zayn sounds a lot like that right now with his Last Real Good Guy gimmick and I love it. After promptly scooting Adam Pearce out of the ring, Sami let loose. He scolded the crowd for cheering people like Roman Reigns, Trick Williams, and CM Punk instead of him. As Sami put it, that’s his fault; he gave the crowd much more credit than they deserve. He thought they were smart enough to see greatness but they only cheer for people who constantly remind them of their greatness. The audience loves people who talk a good game rather than those who let their actions do the talking. The rebel in me loves that he essentially called the audience sheep. I’m the guy who wishes Nirvana went with Kurt Cobain’s first title for Nevermind . Sami channeled a lot of that energy. Much like Bret in the late ‘90s, Sami’s words rang true. American pop culture did change as we headed to the year 2000. Antiheroes, vigilantes, and rebels were en vogue. Fast forward to 2026 where pop culture is more homogenized and the edict is “follow the leader” rather than do what you like. Of course, Sami is a jerk while being right, which doesn’t help his case. I loved him saying the only people worthy of being mentioned in the same breath as him are named Shawn, Eddie, or Kurt, plus he took credit for The Bloodline’s success. That nicely tied the whole thing back to Roman. The Undisputed Champ mentioned Je’Von Evans in his promo, which promoted an appearance from the Young OG. Shocking no one since this is a wrestling show, that led to a title match between the two. This was Je’Von’s first big title shot since coming to Raw . It was just a taste as he and Sami whetted my appetite for more. Sami backed up everything he said in that promo while Je’Von showed why the territory is high on him. summary_src: WWE NXT’s Myles Borne has addressed the bullying and criticism from wrestling fans. During a recent interview with KRON 4, Borne was asked about his heel turn and his different side, where he is not afraid to make enemies.
body: WWE NXT’s Myles Borne has addressed the bullying and criticism from wrestling fans. During a recent interview with KRON 4 , Borne was asked about his heel turn and his different side, where he is not afraid to make enemies. “ My whole life I’ve dealt with bullies and people who just always wanted to look at the fact that I had hearing aids and I had a speech impediment ,” Borne said. He added that for years he had to be the bigger person and treat people the way he wanted to be treated, but not everyone reciprocated that. “I remember there were so many times, these intrusive thoughts of wanting to do something to this bully or to this person, and I couldn’t because I was always taught you only defend yourself when someone puts their hands on you. You never start something, but you finish it ,” he said. Borne further added that some of his fans only liked him because “ ‘Oh, he’s the deaf guy .'” However, the former champion added that the same fans would later go to social media and talk about his speech or criticize it. Later, in the interview, Borne further opens up about how other people with disabilities also feel the same way. He added that the one thing they hate more than anything is people feeling sorry for them. “ There are so many people who have other disabilities, hearing impairment, whatever disability you want to call it, who feel the same way. The one thing we hate more than anything is people who pander to us and feel sorry for us. That’s not what you do. Don’t feel sorry. Why do you feel sorry for me? Because you think I can’t do what you do? Well, guess what? I’m the one in the ring, and everyone else that felt sorry for me is watching me on TV from home ,” he said. Recently turned heel, Borne is a former WWE NXT North American and Tag Team Champion. llm_long: WWE NXT wrestler Myles Borne opened up about facing lifelong bullying during a recent interview with KRON 4. Borne discussed his recent heel turn and how he is no longer afraid to create enemies with others. He revealed that throughout his life he has dealt with bullies who focused on his hearing aids and speech impediment.

Borne explained that for years he chose to be the bigger person by treating others the way he wanted to be treated though not everyone responded in kind. He recalled having intrusive thoughts about confronting his bullies but refrained because he was taught to only defend himself if someone put their hands on him and never to start a fight but always to finish one.

The former champion noted that some fans initially supported him only because he was known as the deaf guy. Borne said those same supporters would then criticize his speech on social media. He added that many people with disabilities including hearing impairments share his feelings and particularly dislike when others pity or pander to them.

Borne stated that he does not want sympathy because others assume he cannot do what they can and pointed out that he is the one performing in the ring while they watch him on television from home. Borne is a former WWE NXT North American Champion and Tag Team Champion who recently turned heel.

title: Results Recap: WWE Raw , grades (Oct. 26): Liv Morgan survives Becky Lynch; Sami Zayn retains again

body: We've reached the point where it's genuinely baffling how many times WWE can rinse and repeat the same thing it's been doing week after week for years now with The Judgment Day stable. Baffling and unbearably annoying, which is probably the point. But eventually things reach a place where all of this has the opposite of its intended effect. We thought the big Judgment Day breaking point would come when Finn Balor separated from the group, but nope. Here we still are six months later. A Women's World Championship No. 1 contender match between the former titleholder Stephanie Vaquer and Becky Lynch was expected to be the big spotlighted match of tonight's "Raw." It was advertised and everything. To start the show, "Raw" GM Adam Pearce announced that wouldn't be the case though, as Vaquer isn't medically cleared to compete. Whether that's kayfabe or legit is unknown, but hopefully it's kayfabe, because another injury to Vaquer would be a bummer. We wish her the best regardless. That meant Lynch was simply getting a title shot without needing a win. That is its own issue, but whatever. Lynch vs. Liv Morgan for the gold. Let's go. The pair put on a phenomenal main-event match, as one would expect. But as I alluded to off the top, it was ruined by Judgment Day shenanigans, just like countless matches of the past have been throughout this stable's run. An absolutely deflating ending. There's no shock or surprise with any of this anymore. The real surprise is why Judgment Day doesn't immediately attack Morgan's opponents to end her matches in DQs. Logically, there's no reason to waste our time with such a good match only to make it mean literally nothing. The ending severely docked the score of a good showing for each. It didn't end there, though. WWE again teased a Tiffany Stratton cash-in. But it was the exact same thing they did on Friday . Days ago! Dominick Mysterio pulled Morgan out of the ring when Stratton had Morgan dead to rights. Re-read what I said earlier. This is all exhausting and unexciting. Surely Stratton will cash in on Chelsea Green after the Crown Jewel champ vs. champ match because Morgan keeps escaping. I should probably just ask ChatGPT, since that's what WWE does, after all. OK, I have to finally admit it. Sami Zayn is operating on another level as champion, because his promo was one of the best of the year. WWE gave him time, and he maximized it with passion, dropping multiple truth bombs. Better yet, the guy also wrestles weekly and on multiple shows. Zayn is arguably the best thing going in WWE right now, and it might not be particularly close. Surprisingly, Zayn's promo prompted a Je'Von Evans appearance and match — for the world title. Now, Evans was never going to win the match, but WWE has done such a tremendous job with Zayn's character that there were actually some shreds of doubt tonight. Rhodes proposed the stipulation during a confrontation on SmackDown. Orton responded by cautioning Rhodes to be careful what he wished for.

On SmackDown, Rhodes wanted to fight Orton immediately, but Orton declined. SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis then booked their Last Man Standing match for Crown Jewel.

title: TNA Wrestling stars to re-sign with the company: Three more names that could agree new deals
raw_title: TNA Wrestling stars to re-sign with the company: Three more names that could agree new deals
body: It has been a busy few weeks for new TNA signings and contract renewals, with the promotion announcing that Shayna Baszler and Shotzi Blackheart have joined the roster and both Santino Marella and Daria Rae have agreed new deals. This time of year is typically a busy one for TNA when it comes to talent re-signings, and according to Fightful Select , more new contract announcements will be on the way “in the coming weeks.” Here are three more names that could potentially be in line for new deals in the near future: 2026 has been a breakout year for England’s own Xia Brookside, with the second-generation star climbing to the very top of the promotion by becoming TNA Knockouts World Champion. While that reign came to an end at this month’s Bound for Glory pay-per-view – where she lost to Indi Hartwell – Brookside is someone who TNA will likely be eager to keep given her success this year. According to Fightful , Brookside’s current deal will run through 2026. There’s yet to be any word regarding interest from other promotions, but TNA shouldn’t wait any longer in tying down the 28-year-old. It has almost been a year since Elayna Black signed with TNA Wrestling, with the former WWE NXT star being unveiled as a member of the company’s roster during its premiere episode on AMC back on January 15. Black has consistently been featured on TV throughout the year, and has been in championship contention on several occasions; including challenging for Xia Brookside’s TNA Knockouts World Title at LockDown 2026 and, most recently attempting to dethrone M By Elegance for the Knockouts Television Title on the October 8 Impact. With her deal also reportedly running through 2026, Black could build upon her success this year by capturing her first singles title in pro wrestling in 2027. The re-signing of Leon Slater must have already either happened or be in the works as “The Youngest in Charge” is now THE guy in TNA Wrestling. Slater became the youngest TNA World Champion ever at Bound for Glory by defeating Nic Nemeth, and he now looks set to carry the flag for the promotion heading into 2027. In order to do that however, he will need to be re-signed to a new deal, given that his existing contract is due to expire in the fall of this year. Again, it’s hard to imagine TNA putting the title on him if he was set to depart the company, so this one is certainly the likeliest announcement we should be hearing in the coming weeks.

body: TNA Wrestling could have more contract news to share following its latest round of signings. According to Fightful Select , the promotion is expected to announce several additional deals through media outlets in the coming weeks. AJ Francis could be among those announcements, with the star reportedly keen to remain in TNA when his current contract expires later this year. TNA recently confirmed the arrivals of Shotzi Blackheart and Shayna Baszler, along with new deals for Santino Marella and Daria Rae. Blackheart debuted during the company’s recent television tapings in Dothan, Alabama. Baszler made her debut at Bound for Glory, where she captured the Knockouts World Tag Team Championship alongside Zoey Serrano. The latest report follows word that TNA president Carlos Silva spoke with roster members at recent tapings about upcoming contract discussions. Several deals are reportedly due to expire in December, making the coming weeks an important period for the company. TNA is said to want agreements secured early so its creative team can plan ahead. Beyond Francis, the report did not identify which other wrestlers have contracts approaching their end. Who would you most like to see TNA sign or keep on its roster? Share your thoughts in the comments.

summary_src: HAYATA suffered a torn ACL. It was at Pro Wrestling NOAH's Wrestle Odyssey II event that HAYATA defended the GHC200 Championship against Shuji Kondo. As the bout was ongoing, Kondo knocked HAYATA off the ring apron, and he went back-first into the guardrail.
body: It was at Pro Wrestling NOAH’s Wrestle Odyssey II event that HAYATA defended the GHC200 Championship against Shuji Kondo. As the bout was ongoing, Kondo knocked HAYATA off the ring apron, and he went back-first into the guardrail. HAYATA immediately grabbed at his left knee and could not make it back into the ring for the referee’s count. NOAH provided an update and shared that HAYATA suffered a torn ACL in his left knee. As a result, he will no longer be competing in the 2026 NOAH Jr. Grand Prix tournament. HAYATA is the first-ever GHC200 Champion. He has been with NOAH since 2016. Owned by wrestling historian and podcaster Conrad Thompson, this dual-plated Reggie Parks masterpiece is now featured as a premier lot in Heritage’s Fall Sports Catalog Auction, and bidding has already exceeded $100,000.00. Spanning the absolute peak of WWE’s 1980s National expansion, this legendary title belt is distinguished by its unprecedented lineage. Recently, speaking on A Shot of Brandi, Wyatt’s former on-screen partner, Alexa Bliss , opened up about bidding goodbye to him and never getting that closure with him. “ He did that interview where he was like, ‘Well, Alexa and I will always be connected in some way.’ And I just felt like a sense of comfort because I got to do the Firefly Fun House scene where I was next to the TV that was just playing Windham over and over and over. And it was so cool to be a part of that again, but also so heartbreaking after I did it. I felt like I finally was able to close that chapter ,” she said. “ I think that was one of the first times that it actually hit me that he was actually gone. And so it was so cool to be able to do that, that Universal let me do that because I was like, I feel like this is me saying goodbye ,” Bliss said. “ This is me going back to where it started and this is me saying goodbye, and they let me have that moment.” Addressing the closure she never got with him, Bliss shared, “ I never got to have that closure with Bray because the last time I was with him it was WrestleMania and I turned on him against Randy [Orton]. And then we were supposed to join back together after this one WrestleMania, and then I found out I was pregnant. And then he had gotten sick, and so he was out for a while, and so it just never, it was like ships in the night, right?” Bliss formed a partnership with Bray Wyatt in 2020 and remained with him till 2021, before breaking up. However, following Wyatt’s return in 2022, Bliss would again start having brief backstage moments teasing her alliance with him. Unfortunately, WWE never followed up on those as Wyatt went on a hiatus after Royal Rumble 2023, before passing away later that year. title: Tony Khan Extremely Happy After Skydance Meeting
raw_title: Tony Khan Reportedly ‘Extremely Happy’ After His Meeting With Skydance Executives
body: AEW President and CEO Tony Khan reportedly met with Skydance executives in Los Angeles, California, recently. Paramount Skydance completed its merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) earlier this month. The combined company has been named Skydance, with David Ellison serving as its chairman and CEO. Khan has previously spoken about his conversations with Ellison, claiming that the latter is a supporter of AEW and the company will be better off post-merger. On the latest edition of Wrestling Observer Radio (WOR) [via Wrestling Inc. ], Dave Meltzer reported that Tony Khan came out of the meetings with Skydance executives “extremely happy.” Meltzer stated: “I don’t know any of the details yet, but I do know that [Khan] came out of the meetings extremely happy. Much happier than he’s been. … He’s always been happy about this relationship; he’s always been beaming about it since day one, but he definitely came out of these meetings the happiest he’s been. And obviously there were moves made already. … There’s two wrestling moves that Skydance already made, and neither of them would look positive.” Meltzer also provided a clarification on his recent report regarding Women of Wrestling. After initially reporting that Skydance has canceled Women of Wrestling, he clarified that it will get another season, though it won’t be syndicated. Meltzer added that a channel on Roku that used to air WOW and NWA 24/7 has been canceled. Khan previously shared his excitement for the merger. You can check his comments HERE .
summary: AEW President Tony Khan recently met with executives from Skydance in Los Angeles following the company's merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Per Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio, Khan emerged from the discussions extremely happy, even more positive than in prior conversations about the partnership. Skydance has already taken two wrestling-related actions since the merger.

body: Share Follow ABC7 on Google CHICAGO (WLS) -- Benjamin Satterley, the professional wrestler known to fans as "Pac," died Sunday, less than 24 hours after competing at an All Elite Wrestling event in Hoffman Estates, a northern suburb of Chicago, according to the Cook County Medical Examiner. Satterley, 40, wrestled Saturday night at NOW Arena before his death was reported Sunday in nearby Des Plaines. The medical examiner has not yet determined a cause of death and said it may be several weeks before autopsy results are available. The news shocked fans who watched the English-born wrestler perform the night before, including Jayson Weidman, who attended the event. Inside NOW Arena on Saturday, Satterley competed for All Elite Wrestling under the ring name Pac. The English wrestler, who previously performed in WWE as Adrian Neville, was known for high-flying moves that delighted fans worldwide. "There are wrestlers that can do incredible things, and then there's wrestlers who can do things that you question how it's even humanly possible that they can do what they're doing. Pac was one of those wrestlers," Weidman said. Satterley, who was from Newcastle upon Tyne, began his wrestling career in 2004 and signed in 2019 with All Elite Wrestling, where he held multiple championships. He competed and lost to Andrade El Ídolo on Saturday in Chicago in the AEW National Championship. Weidman said he purchased his seat specifically in hopes of being close to Pac and his group, the Death Riders. "It was such a special moment for me to be able to see him wrestle," Weidman said. He quickly rose to prominence, earning nicknames like "The Super Superman" and "The Man That Gravity Forgot." He began his international journey in 2007 and wrestled under the name of Adrian Neville from 2012 to 2018. After signing with AEW, he became the inaugural AEW International Champion and a two-time AEW World Trios Champion. According to Weidman, Pac wrestled in Saturday's opening match and later returned during the main event. "He looked healthy as can be, and it's unbelievable how less than 24 hours, he could possibly be gone," Weidman said. The Cook County Medical Examiner said Satterley died shortly after 4 p.m. Sunday at 2761 Mannheim Road in Des Plaines. A restaurant employee at that address said Satterley never entered the business. As if the excitement wasn’t high enough, we’re just 11 days from AEW WrestleDream in Orlando! In the main event, AEW World Champion Will Ospreay defeated AEW International Champion “The Rainmaker” Kazuchika Okada to retain his title in an unbelievable match, which marked the first time Ospreay beat Okada in a championship bout. As Ospreay celebrated in the ring with “Speedball” Mike Bailey, Samoa Joe appeared on the ramp to end the night, sending a message that he’s ready for Clockwork Carnage after qualifying by beating “Jungle” Jack Perry earlier in the night. AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Moné got everything she could handle from Queen Aminata in front of a Parisian crowd that was fully behind Aminata’s quest to win her first AEW gold. Moné overcame Aminata in the end to get the win, but she could not celebrate for long because her WrestleDream opponent, Thekla, hit the ring to cut Moné in half with a spear! The night began with ROH World Champion Bandido turning away AEW World Trios Champion Kofi while both men’s trios partners made their presence felt, specifically Swerve Strickland and “Hangman” Adam Page. Later, Swerve and The New Level challenged Page, Bandido and Brody King to face them in a 2-out-of-3 falls match for the AEW World Trios Championship at WrestleDream! TNT Champion Darby Allin was left a bloody mess in his defense against former champion “The Protostar” Kyle Fletcher, but somehow Allin was able to leave Paris with a successful defense in a brutally violent encounter. Plus, Mark Davis and Jake Doyle earned a huge win for the Don Callis Family in tag team action over Gabe Kidd and AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley! The night began with the ROH World Championship on the line! Kofi, one third of the AEW World Trios Champions, made his way to the ring to a raucous ovation inside the Adidas Arena, accompanied by another third of the champions, Austin Creed. The champion came out next, and he wasn't alone either — Bandido was flanked by Brody King for this championship tilt. title: Brian Solomon on WWE Magazine, John Cena, and Starting Over
raw_title: Brian Solomon on WWE Magazine, John Cena, and Starting Over
body: Brian Solomon answered a newspaper ad for a WWF copy editor in 1999, hoping for a job close to the wrestling he loved. Seven years inside the company’s magazines brought assignments with Vince McMahon, Pat Patterson, and an emerging John Cena. But when those seven years came to an end, Solomon faced a difficult question: what comes after WWE? Brian Solomon grew up in the Brooklyn neighborhoods of Dyker Heights and Bensonhurst during the 1970s and 1980s. Family trips into Manhattan brought graffiti-covered subway cars and glimpses of the old Times Square. Speaking with Pro Wrestling Stories on September 17, 2026, he contrasted those childhood scenes with the city’s later transformation. "Either we took the subway, which was a nightmare, because in those days, every inch of everything was covered with graffiti. Every square inch. And the odds of being a victim of a crime were no joke. There was a very serious chance that you were going to be mugged or held up or something." Driving into Manhattan brought its own education, and this was the part of Brian’s account that stuck with me most. His childhood memories included adult theaters, street crime, and people openly using substances around Times Square and 42nd Street. He was a child trying to make sense of what he saw. "When we’d drive into the city, you would get to around that kind of Times Square, 42nd Street area, and everything was there. My dad’s trying to drive by as fast as possible, and I’m trying to read the titles of the movies on the marquee! But that’s how bad it was." The transformation of Times Square in the 1990s stood out in his memory. Wrestling was already part of that New York childhood. The World Wrestling Federation even brought shows to his elementary school gym. Watching WrestleMania III in 1987 turned that familiarity into a regular interest. “I became a wrestling fan when I was 12 years old: WrestleMania III.” Brian’s grandfather took him to his first live show that July, at Madison Square Garden . The card included Ricky Steamboat pursuing The Honky Tonk Man ’s Intercontinental Championship , The British Bulldogs against The Hart Foundation , and Rick Rude ’s Garden debut. “So that was it. You get spoiled. My grandfather took me, and it was July 1987.” His interest faded briefly in high school, then returned around 1991, just as the business was entering a less successful period. “But then all of a sudden, right about ’91 or so, I got into it bigger than ever. The whole business was declining at that point, but my interest wasn’t; it was actually growing. And really, since that moment, I’ve just been a die-hard wrestling fan.” No ads. No interruptions. title: By the Numbers: WWE Crown Jewel 'still set' to go ahead in Riyadh: Start time, matches, tickets and how to watch in the UAE
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel 'still set' to go ahead in Riyadh: Start time, matches, tickets and how to watch in the UAE
body: Add on Google WWE is returning to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel, with the annual wrestling event scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7. The show will feature some of WWE's biggest stars, including Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn , Liv Morgan and Chelsea Green , with two championship matches confirmed during Monday Night Raw on October 12. The event is still scheduled to take place in Riyadh despite recent missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. Speaking to Fox News on October 23, TKO Group Holdings chief executive Ari Emanuel confirmed the plans were unchanged, saying: "Right now, everything is still set." However, he said the company was monitoring the situation daily and considering alternative locations should the event need to be moved. Crown Jewel is part of Riyadh Season and continues WWE's partnership with Saudi Arabia, a partnership that began in 2018. The kingdom is also preparing to host WrestleMania 43 in 2027, which will be the first time WWE's flagship event has taken place outside North America. Crown Jewel will take place on November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium in the King Abdullah Financial District. The main show is scheduled to begin at 10pm Saudi Arabia time, which is 11pm in the UAE. Tickets went on sale on October 2 through Webook. Prices range from 80 Saudi riyals to 600 Saudi riyals ($21 to $160), depending on seating category. Availability and prices may change closer to the event. Crown Jewel will stream live on Netflix in the UAE and other international markets covered by WWE's streaming agreement. In the US, the event will be available through the ESPN app with an ESPN Unlimited subscription. Four matches have been confirmed for Crown Jewel, including two champion-versus-champion contests, a Last Man Standing match and a tag team title bout. World heavyweight champion Roman Reigns is scheduled to face WWE champion Sami Zayn for the men's Crown Jewel Championship. Zayn won his first WWE championship at Night of Champions in Riyadh in June, before losing it nine days later. He recaptured the title on September 11. The two have a long history together, having previously been allies in The Bloodline before their relationship broke down. Women's world champion Liv Morgan is set to take on WWE women's champion Chelsea Green for the women's Crown Jewel Championship. Their rivalry developed on Raw, when Morgan dismissed Green's championship reign before Green lost a non-title match against Roxanne Perez. Both contests follow Crown Jewel's champion-versus-champion format, with separate titles awarded to the winners rather than either wrestler's existing championship being defended. Seth Rollins and Stephanie Vaquer won the respective men's and women's Crown Jewel titles at last year's event in Perth, Australia. Cody Rhodes will face his former mentor Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match, following an announcement on SmackDown on October 23. The rivalry intensified after Orton attacked Rhodes following their WrestleMania 4

He sits down with Chris Van Vliet in Orlando, FL to discuss winning the WWE Championship twice after more than a decade in the company, being part of The Bloodline and becoming an Honorary Uce, the huge reaction to hitting Roman Reigns with a chair, the story behind the “not feeling very Ucey” line with Jey Uso, his WrestleMania 38 match against Johnny Knoxville, El Generico, the decades of history with Kevin Owens, and more! “It’s cool. Yeah, here’s the thing that’s funny about it because even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew, and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, you know what, maybe the ship sailed. I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that. Then I was close, but if I lost after losing that match, I was like, well, you can’t tell this story again. Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, underdog who finally wins the big one- we burnt that card; that card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen. I’ve said this before in other interviews, or to friends, or my wife, or whatever. I’ve had a tremendous career, and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never [got it]. You know what I mean? You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture.” “I don’t think anything changed, and that’s actually the point. It’s that I kept doing what I do, which is making sure that everything I’m involved in is as good as it could possibly be. Eventually, a lot has to happen, even when you’re doing good work and you’re great and all this stuff to win the WWE Championship. It is like there is no such thing as a fluke win. I know when I won it the first time and it was nine days, in character you could say I was a fluke. There’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. To even be in the periphery of it is insane. To even be in the mix, to even be in the discussion, to even have title matches, even if you’re losing them, is extremely one in a billion already to be put in that position. So to win it, there’s an immeasurable number of variables that are required to be in that position. So there’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. title: On the Record: Brooke Hogan Clarifies Comments About WWE Stars After Hulk Hogan Tribute
raw_title: Brooke Hogan Clarifies Comments About WWE Stars After Hulk Hogan Tribute
body: 0 Brooke Hogan has clarified her recent comments about WWE Superstars following criticism of the company’s tribute to her late father, Hulk Hogan . Brooke’s earlier comments drew attention after she shared a photograph of WWE’s tribute to Hulk Hogan on her Instagram Stories and claimed that those pictured had spent little time with him in the hospital. “Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed,” she wrote in the original post. The comments followed Brooke’s reaction to the sale of her father’s Clearwater, Florida, mansion for $5.9 million. She described the property as a place filled with family memories and accused unnamed individuals of benefiting from her father’s death. Hulk Hogan died on July 24, 2025, at the age of 71. WWE honored the wrestling legend following his death with a tribute celebrating his career and impact on the industry. Brooke addressed the controversy through her Instagram Stories . She denied having a personal issue with WWE talent and explained that her frustration was directed at people she believes failed to support her father while he was alive. “Hey reporters: I don’t have beef with the stars of WWE. Nor did I say that. Do your job right or don’t do it at all,” Brooke wrote. Brooke explained that her criticism focused on people who attended public tributes. These were for her father despite allegedly failing to support him during his health struggles. She also extended her comments beyond the wrestling industry, referencing people she considered friends and family. “I’m saying I watched people show up to public tributes… that didn’t give a shit when I was in the trenches with him. But they’ll show up to get their face on camera…” Brooke added. She maintained that her frustration was not directed at WWE Superstars as a group. Instead, she questioned the sincerity of people who publicly honored her father. But in her view, were absent when he needed support. The post Brooke Hogan Clarifies Comments About WWE Stars After Hulk Hogan Tribute appeared first on Wrestlezone .

title: Results Recap: How Sami Zayn echoes Bret Hart’s 1997 — Raw & reactions
raw_title: Raw recap & reactions: How Sami Zayn echoes Bret Hart’s 1997
body: Link WWE Marcus Benjamin has loved wrestling since his early days on the planet. He once Superkicked a tooth out of a friend’s mouth. Sweet Chin Music indeed. He’s analyzed and covered wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2021. Bad to Be Good I don’t feel old but today is the day where I officially sound old. The 1996 Survivor Series turns 30 in a few weeks. That night in Madison Square Garden welcomed Bret Hart back to the game for his first match since WrestleMania XII . Bret found himself in a very different WWF than the one he left that fateful night in Anaheim. He wrestled the man who became the catalyst for a new attitude in the territory, and witnessed a different dynamic. Fans cheered Steve Austin but gave the traditional babyfaces tepid responses. That shift inspired a heel turn several months later and gave us Bret at his peak. Seriously, the man was on fire in ‘97. He was pissed at the audience for not responding to him how they used to. He hated that someone like Stone Cold got the props and respect usually saved for clean-cut cats like Bret. The Hitman saw himself as not just a good guy but the good guy. He didn’t change; American values changed. Sami Zayn sounds a lot like that right now with his Last Real Good Guy gimmick and I love it. After promptly scooting Adam Pearce out of the ring, Sami let loose. He scolded the crowd for cheering people like Roman Reigns, Trick Williams, and CM Punk instead of him. As Sami put it, that’s his fault; he gave the crowd much more credit than they deserve. He thought they were smart enough to see greatness but they only cheer for people who constantly remind them of their greatness. The audience loves people who talk a good game rather than those who let their actions do the talking. The rebel in me loves that he essentially called the audience sheep. I’m the guy who wishes Nirvana went with Kurt Cobain’s first title for Nevermind . Sami channeled a lot of that energy. Much like Bret in the late ‘90s, Sami’s words rang true. American pop culture did change as we headed to the year 2000. Antiheroes, vigilantes, and rebels were en vogue. Fast forward to 2026 where pop culture is more homogenized and the edict is “follow the leader” rather than do what you like. Of course, Sami is a jerk while being right, which doesn’t help his case. I loved him saying the only people worthy of being mentioned in the same breath as him are named Shawn, Eddie, or Kurt, plus he took credit for The Bloodline’s success. That nicely tied the whole thing back to Roman. The Undisputed Champ mentioned Je’Von Evans in his promo, which promoted an appearance from the Young OG. Shocking no one since this is a wrestling show, that led to a title match between the two. This was Je’Von’s first big title shot since coming to Raw . It was just a taste as he and Sami whetted my appetite for more. Sami backed up everything he said in that promo while Je’Von showed why the territory is high on him. title: Sami Zayn Details Name Ideas Presented In NXT
raw_title: Sami Zayn Explains How He Ended Up As 'Sami Zayn' In NXT, Presented Different Categories Of Names
summary_src: Before he was Sami Zayn in WWE NXT, Sami was El Generico on the independent scene. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight, Sami was asked if there was any talk of him wearing…
body: Before he was Sami Zayn in WWE NXT, Sami was El Generico on the independent scene. In WWE, he shed the mask and took on a different name and persona, which isn’t uncommon when joining the promotion. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Sami was asked if there was any talk of him wearing a mask in NXT. “I didn’t know when they signed me because I also knew, you know, well, you signed me for what you saw. So I’m assuming you liked what you saw, I don’t know what they wanted out of me. So there’s a lot to me, and there’s a lot of avenues you could take. So one was this masked type character. So I’ll clarify. Let me elaborate. But when they’re asking you to come up with names or whatever. I didn’t know what they wanted out of me, so I sort of had these categories, because again, I just didn’t know what they wanted out of me. I know I look like a redhead; I could look Irish or Sheamus’s cousin on TV if you wanted me to be Sheamus’s little cousin, I could be that. Maybe they want me for that. I’m also French Canadian. I’m also Arab, and there’s the Mexican stuff or the masked stuff. So I was presenting all these different categories of names, not just broad names,” he said. Asked how he ended up with the name “Sami Zayn,” he replied, “So I think what I did see as a huge opportunity is to kind of be myself. A huge part of that is obviously my ethnicity and my religion, I guess, to an extent. Just like it’s a big part of who I am. Not that it’s a day-to-day thing, but it’s a big part of the concoction that has made me who I am. To be able to represent that in a way that has never really been represented was very attractive to me. Because as an Arab, you have heightened awareness of it. Growing up in the 80s, 90s, and especially in a post 9/11 world where the stereotypes and the racism and all that stuff is just crazy, and it’s normalized and it’s accepted, and it was sort of like the only way you saw your people represented in Western culture. I was a child of the West. My household was Arab and Muslim, but for all intents and purposes, I look like just some white kid. So, the idea of kind of smashing that boundary a little bit of being an Arab and not playing the caricature, especially the heel caricature of an Arab.” The comparison of Muhammed Hassan was brought up, as he ended up being a heel caricature of an Arab. Sami said, “Yeah, who wasn’t actually Arab himself, ironically. But just not playing into those stereotypes, not even reintroducing, but introducing a concept of like, hey, Arabs are just normal people. What is this groundbreaking idea!? My mom almost named me that, she didn’t, and Zayn is an Arab name, but both of them are extremely Western-passing. People could pronounce them. Doesn’t trip people up. llm_long: Sami Zayn explained that before joining WWE NXT he had been performing as El Generico on the independent circuit and was unsure what character the promotion wanted from him upon signing. During a conversation with Chris Van Vliet on the Insight podcast Zayn revealed there was initial discussion about a masked character for him in NXT.

Zayn said he prepared multiple categories of name ideas because he did not know what direction NXT officials envisioned for him after seeing his independent work. He noted that his red hair could support an Irish persona such as being presented as Sheamus's cousin while his French Canadian Arab and Mexican wrestling background offered other avenues including masked options.

Zayn described viewing his ethnicity and religion as central to his identity and saw a major opportunity to portray an Arab character in a way that had not been done before in WWE. He recounted growing up in the West with an Arab Muslim household yet appearing as a white kid and wanting to break stereotypes that were especially prevalent in the post 9/11 era where Arab portrayals were often normalized as negative caricatures.
When the topic of Muhammad Hassan was raised as an example of a previous Arab heel caricature Zayn agreed noting that Hassan was not actually Arab.

title: Why Rumors Of WWE Moving WrestleMania 43 To The Sphere Are Untrue
raw_title: Why Rumors Of WWE Moving WrestleMania 43 To The Sphere Are Untrue
body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 27, 2026, 6:39 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Josh is a writer at TheSportster and a lifelong wrestling fan who has been doing news coverage of WWE and AEW for many years. Pro wrestling got its hooks in him at the age of ten and he's been watching ever since. His favorite wrestlers are The Rock and CM Punk, despite the latter doing his level best to make us all dislike him. Sign in to your TheSportster account Despite growing pressure to move or even outright cancel Crown Jewel amid escalating conflict in the Middle East, WWE remains adamant that the show will go ahead in Saudi Arabia as planned. There are even already doubts being cast over WrestleMania 43 too, which is also set to emanate from Saudi, although early rumors of a venue change are seemingly unfounded. The latest on where WrestleMania might take place should Saudi Arabia no longer be a viable option is that WWE has considered holding its biggest show of 2027 in The Sphere instead. The Las Vegas venue is one of the most famous in the world, offering a truly unique experience due to both the walls on the inside and the outside effectively being giant screens. Triple H and Stephanie McMahon were at The Sphere last week for a Metallica concert, which might be what spurred rumors of WrestleMania being moved there. According to Fightful , there is no evidence to suggest The Sphere is even being considered for a replacement WrestleMania 43 location, and even if it were, the venue likely wouldn't be available when WWE needs it. WrestleMania 43 weekend is currently locked in for April 10 and 11, 2027. John Mayer is performing at The Sphere across both of those nights. There's no room to bring the event forward a week, as Oprah Winfrey has the venue booked on April 3 and 4, and Mayer has The Sphere all to himself, and his fans, the weekend after on April 17 and 18, too. If WWE really does want to move WrestleMania 43 from Riyadh to The Sphere, then it will have to shift its calendar by a full two weeks. The venue is currently free two weeks before WrestleMania is slated to take place, across the weekend of March 27 and 28, or two weeks later, near the end of the month, on April 24 and 25. The idea that WrestleMania might need to be moved isn't the pressing issue right now. That's a problem for a later date, as right now WWE needs to figure out what's going on with Crown Jewel. Every time the situation in Saudi Arabia becomes more severe, fans wait for an announcement that the show is being moved or canceled. However, even after the US government ordered diplomats and their families in Saudi Arabia to return home, there has still been no indication from WWE that Crown Jewel plans are being changed , and the show is now less than two weeks away.

title: John Cena Returning to RAW on November 2
raw_title: WWE legend John Cena to make RAW return really soon
body: It has almost been a year since John Cena 's last appearance on Monday Night RAW, but the retired WWE legend will be returning soon. WWE announced that Cena would be coming back for the Nov. 2, 2026, edition of RAW , which will emanate from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. It's unknown in what capacity he will return, whether he will be an emcee or appear in a backstage segment. He won't, however, likely take any bumps , as he has ruled them out since hanging up the jean shorts. The reason for Cena's return to RAW is unknown. Maybe WWE is trying to spice up the final episode of the show before Crown Jewel on Saturday, Nov. 7. He also hosted WrestleMania 42 earlier in the year. Perhaps he'll take on a similar role on RAW next week. Either way, fans only have to wait six days to find out. Cena recently retired from in-ring competition in December 2025. He concluded his year-long retirement tour with a match against Gunther at Saturday Night's Main Event on Dec. 13. He tapped out, losing his final match. Gunther has since retired AJ Styles and is currently feuding with Danhausen on Friday Night SmackDown. The retirement tour gave Cena's fans around the world a chance to see him before he hung it up. During the run, he won a record-setting 17th world championship and turned heel for the first time in years. He also got to run it back with past foes like CM Punk, Randy Orton, and Styles. Now, he is fully retired from being a WWE Superstar. While he has made a handful of appearances since, he will never wrestle again. He is still an actor, with his last project, Matchbox: The Movie, coming out earlier in the month on Apple TV.
summary: WWE has confirmed that retired star John Cena will appear on the November 2, 2026 episode of RAW from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn. It remains unclear what role he will play, though he is not expected to take any in-ring bumps following his retirement. Cena last appeared on RAW nearly a year ago and wrapped up his in-ring career with a loss to Gunther in December 2025.

title: Sami Zayn Explains His Slow Heel Turn Process
raw_title: Sami Zayn Details His Gradual Heel Turn, Gives The Cheer-Boo Ratio He's Trying To Reach
summary_src: Sami Zayn started the year as the babyface underdog, just fighting to win his first WWE Championship.
body: Sami Zayn started the year as the babyface underdog, just fighting to win his first WWE Championship. He failed at WWE Royal Rumble, losing to Drew McIntyre, and the slow descent into becoming a heel started then as he defeated Carmelo Hayes to win the WWE United States Title and feuded with Trick Williams, who was quickly gaining in popularity despite being a heel. “There’s a lot of evolution that’s happened, and part of what I’ve liked about this sort of turn is that it wasn’t done as a conventional turn. It wasn’t done, good guy, good guy, good guy. Now I’m bad. You know what I mean? It was just like a very gradual process. It all started when I lost to Drew at the Royal Rumble. I realized, well, as I said earlier, we’ve played this card, can’t play it again, so something needs to change now. I’d like it to be gradual, and I’d like it to just feel the audience, and I’d like to obviously nudge the audience in a certain direction, but I want to do it in this sort of delicate way, right? There were things that, again, unexpected gifts that fall from the sky, or just hands that you’re dealt that you don’t know are going to be dealt, that sometimes put us on a fast track one way, or took us in a different direction another way. So, for example, when I beat Carmelo Hayes for the title, it went from like 80-20 cheers, it went from like 90-10. I had 10 to work with in the beginning, and I’d like to get that number to like 70-30. Maybe 60-40,” Zayn explained about his heel turn process while speaking with Chris Van Vliet on Insight . He continued, “Yeah in January or whatever, just enough to hear one or two guys going boo! I’m like, okay, I can work with that, and I’ll just gently tip those scales. There was this fine balancing point that I wanted to get to, and I couldn’t get to it when I wanted to get to it because that’s just weekly television, and that’s the hand you’re dealt sometimes. A lot of it is just as I said, rolling with the punches, being in the pocket, being present, and dealing with it, and all that kind of stuff. But then when I beat Carmelo Hayes overnight, I was at like 70-30 at that point, and then it just went like 90-10 in the other way as soon as I beat him, and the stuff with Trick was all contributing to it at that time as well. But then when I beat Carmelo, it was like a light switch. So okay, that’s gonna accelerate the process a little bit. I didn’t want to take this character and go well, now I’m a bad guy, crumple it up and do something else. I really like evolving into things. If you look at the trajectory of the character, if you go back starting in 2019 maybe, each little chapter has kind of seamlessly bled into the next thing.” Zayn is now the reigning Undisputed WWE Champion who fights for his ride or dies. Elsewhere in the interview, Sami explained how he ended up with the name “Sami Zayn” in WWE. You can find his full comments here .

Zayn described the approach as a delicate evolution where he reads and nudges the crowd reaction over time.

title: Sami Zayn Recalls Bulletproof Confidence Before Knoxville Match
raw_title: Sami Zayn: Johnny Knoxville Is Just Perfect. I Hate Him
summary_src: At WrestleMania 38, Sami Zayn and Johnny Knoxville battled in one of the most memorable WrestleMania matches of all-time as the two engaged in a Jackass-filled wrestling match.
body: At WrestleMania 38, Sami Zayn and Johnny Knoxville battled in one of the most memorable WrestleMania matches of all-time as the two engaged in a Jackass-filled wrestling match. The build up to the match featured a number of stunts and social media gags, including Knoxville giving out Zayn’s phone number. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Zayn was asked when he knew the match could be something special. “Well, I kind of knew. So I’ll have these, this is gonna sound cocky for sure, but I’ll have these moments. Let’s say I’ve put something together and I’ve thought of it and I’ve reviewed it a bunch of times in my head, where I’m just like, oh my God, these people have no idea what’s about to hit them. Okay, I’m exaggerating. What I’m trying to say is, I’ll go, this is bulletproof, there’s no way this is not going to get them. But then there is self-doubt. So right up until the curtain, I would fluctuate between oh my god, even if you hate me, even if you hate wrestling, and you somehow got dragged to this show, this will get you. There’s no way around it,” he said. Asked if Knoxville had any wrestling experience, Zayn replied, “No. [He’s done stunts] Yeah, he’s not a wrestler. He’s not an athlete. But he’s a great man. He was perfect. I think he was just perfect. I mean, I hate him. It’s this gnawing thing that just doesn’t really go away. I don’t want to get into all that now, but he’s relentless. He really is. What I mean by he’s perfect is you can’t really replicate that match with [anyone else]. At that time, that match could only be Sami Zayn versus Johnny Knoxville. You couldn’t put two other people in there and have the same match. That’s kind of what I liked about it. Is like all the things that happened. It’s easy to watch it and reduce it to just oh there was a bunch of weapons and stuff, but in fact it was just a wrestling match, and those gadgets, that’s his signature offense, because his signature offense is from the Jackass world. He doesn’t have wrestling moves. He has Jackass stunts. So the moves were replaced by the Jackass stunts, but they still serve the same function.” The bout featured a bowling ball to the nuts, a mousetrap table, a giant hand slapping Sami, Wee Man hitting a bodyslam, and much more. Asked if any particular spot hurt more than another, Zayn said, “The table was crazy. That mousetrap table, that was a big one that really hurt. But that’s the one kind of sore spot because it almost gets reduced to a comedy match. Part of what I love about it is it had a little bit of everything. There are comedic elements, but there’s also some actual violence and some pretty serious bumps.” Knoxville was victorious in the match, and the feud continues to this day. Elsewhere during the interview, Zayn discussed the evolution of his heel turn in 2026. You can find his full comments here .

He described fluctuating between total confidence that the Jackass-inspired match and its accompanying stunts would be undeniable even to non-fans and moments of self-doubt right up until they went through the curtain. body: Former AEW World Tag Team and World Trios Champion Max Caster stated that he’ll be stepping away from pro wrestling following his situation at TNA Wrestling’s 2026 Bound For Glory pay-per-view. Caster had spent the last five years of his career with All Elite Wrestling. While doing a virtual signing for K & S WrestleFest , Caster was asked about the possibility of him returning to AEW, and he said, ‘Never say never,’ but for right now, he’s saying no to wrestling bookings. “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never. However, I am saying no to wrestling bookings right now, and that would be a wrestling booking so, I don’t know.” Following up on that, Caster said he agreed to do the signing before the Bound For Glory situation. He said it will be his last wrestling-related appearance for an undefined amount of time. “I agreed to do the virtual signing a couple months ago, I think. I’m honoring this… especially because we know Brian (Myers). I gotta respect Brian too so, this is my last wrestling thing for a while, so whoever’s here, I’m sure somebody is clipping this, waiting for me to say something crazy. I’m gonna try not to today. But, this will be the last time you guys see me for an undefined amount of time.”

body: With her two-year WWE non-compete clause expected to expire this month, Samantha has now opened up about being offered a record deal by WWE before her exit. Recently sharing a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), Samantha revealed how the promotion had offered her a record deal, which she politely declined because she always wanted to manage wrestlers. “ WWE offered me a record deal, to which I politely declined because I have no interest in the music business! My interest was in managing wrestlers. And that’s all I’ve ever expressed. “ I made some songs last year for fun & videos with my colleagues from Cirque du Soleil and released independently for my singing fans from before wrestling, but other than that, I made no proclamations about or efforts towards a “music” career 🙏🏽 Singing career wise, I’ve had a fantastic one, though!!! Saw the world multiple times over, ” she wrote. Samantha Irvin joined WWE in 2021 and remained a part of the promotion till 2024. Despite her short time at the promotion, she developed herself as one of the most popular ring announcers in the company. However, since her departure from WWE, Samantha has stayed away from pro-wrestling due to her contract, which is rumored to end this month. However, despite that, she is not reportedly expected to join AEW immediately . title: Brooke Hogan Criticizes WWE Stars For Hulk Hogan Tribute
raw_title: Brooke Hogan Blasts WWE Stars Over Hulk Hogan Tribute and Hospital Visits
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » Brooke Hogan Blasts WWE Stars Over Hulk Hogan Tribute and Hospital Visits Brooke Hogan has criticized members of the WWE roster who paid tribute to her late father, Hulk Hogan , questioning their support for the wrestling legend during his final days. She shared her comments on Instagram Stories following reports that her father’s beachfront mansion in Clearwater, Florida, had sold for $5.9 million. Brooke expressed sadness over the sale, recalling the memories she shared with her father at the property. Brooke described the home as a place filled with family memories, including time spent together after her father’s surgeries, watching television, listening to music and sharing meals. She also criticised unnamed individuals whom she accused of benefiting from her father’s death. Her comments then turned towards the wrestling personalities who appeared in WWE’s televised tribute to Hulk Hogan following his death in July 2025. Brooke shared a photograph of WWE personalities paying tribute to her father and questioned whether those pictured had genuinely supported him while he was receiving medical care. “Not ONE of these people stayed longer than an hour in the hospital… if they even showed,” Brooke wrote. She also pushed back against criticism over her decision to distance herself from people she described as toxic, fake and greedy. Brooke disputed claims that others had remained by her father’s side until the end, alleging that some had only appeared when his death was imminent. Brooke also paid tribute to her father on July 24, 2026, marking the first anniversary of Hulk Hogan’s death. She shared several photos of them together on Instagram alongside an emotional message about missing him and hoping they would reunite in another lifetime. “Though the rest of my life will feel like I have to live so long without you, hopefully it’s only seconds on your end till we’re together again. I’m right behind you, daddy,” Brooke wrote in her tribute. Hulk Hogan, whose real name was Terry Bollea, died from an acute myocardial infarction, commonly known as a heart attack. His medical records also noted a history of atrial fibrillation and chronic lymphocytic leukemia. title: Danhausen Is Taking Over WWE’s 2026 Halloween Week, and It Makes Perfect Sense

He’s also hosting the October 30 SmackDown, which will also be filled with his many antics. That means that he’s hosting three Halloween specials in five days. Fans may think this is a Danhausen overload, but this is perfect in terms of his character and the celebration of Halloween itself. He’s not too funny, but he’s not too serious either. Hosting many specials throughout the week will be a great way for more fans to know what he’s all about. Having WWE use him for Halloween-related promotions is a great idea for many reasons. That’s actually not a bad thing, as he, as a Halloween costume, is pretty easy to make. But like the Snickers commercial , it won’t be forced, as the spooky guy is who his character is. Having him do all the Halloween-related festivities isn’t a departure from his usual antics in any way, which makes everything easy. When watching the specials this week, fans will definitely be expecting many wacky things. His debut at the Elimination Chamber in February had him come out of a coffin inside a box, and he walked out with many dancers wearing his face paint surrounding him. He’s had Minihausen’s all throughout his tenure, starring alongside him at WrestleMania: Vegas and at SummerSlam, while tagging with him in a win at Backlash over Kit Wilson and The Miz. Expecting something normal this week is completely out of the question. Maybe he’ll be in charge of decorating the ring and the barricade surrounding it this week. title: Sami Zayn Recalls Bloodline Story Evolution
raw_title: Sami Zayn discusses evolution of The Bloodline alliance and turnaround from initial WWE plans
summary_src: Sami Zayn reflects on his time with The Bloodline in 2022 and how their alliance evolved over time. The Undisputed WWE Champion explained how his involvement with Roman Reigns’ faction was filled with the absurdity and ability to adapt creatively as the storyline unfolded.
body: Sami Zayn reflects on his time with The Bloodline in 2022 and how their alliance evolved over time. The Undisputed WWE Champion explained how his involvement with Roman Reigns’ faction was filled with the absurdity and ability to adapt creatively as the storyline unfolded. He told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that the overall blueprint was narrated towards a title match, the unexpected developments with The Usos, particularly Jey, expanded the story. “Well, that’s kind of what makes it work from the jump. That was in the conception of the idea; it’s so ridiculous, that’s part of the appeal of it. My intent in the beginning was more to be kind of like on the periphery, it evolved, and that’s part of the beauty of it. When I say part of the skill set, part of why I loved it so much is the week-to-week adaptation,” said Zayn. “I had some ideas and I had an overarching blueprint, which more or less kind of came to fruition, which starts here and ends in a championship match eventually down the road with Roman. That’s kind of the blueprint in your head, but some of the week-to-week stuff that you don’t account for, those are just gifts that fall into your lap, and then it’s playing with those gifts, and that’s that adaptability and the improvisational skills and the storytelling skills that I think are really what we do, or a crucial part of what we do, or a crucial part of being really good at what we do, is adapting to those things when they come to you, whether it’s in a match or whether it’s in a storyline. I know this was the plan, but hang on just a sec. Now we’ve got this thing with Jey, and you got to run with it because it’s interesting, and you hadn’t accounted for it ahead of time.” “But now you’ve got this gift that fell from the heavens, and running with it. Sometimes that happens in matches, and sometimes it happens in promos, or a lot of times, what’s happened to me, especially most recently with this WWE title thing, is it’s happened in kind of overarching storytelling, where yeah, I know this wasn’t where we were going, but hang on a sec. This is really interesting, and we should probably elaborate on this.” Zayn’s friendship with The Bloodline concluded at Royal Rumble 2023 when Reigns urged him to attack his friend, Kevin Owens after his title match. A month later at Elimination Chamber, Zayn challenged Reigns for the Universal Championship. Three years later, at WWE Crown Jewel on November 7, Reigns and Zayn will face each other in a champion vs. champion match. title: Rey Mysterio's Wife Appears to Confirm 2027 Retirement
raw_title: WWE legend Rey Mysterio’s wife seemingly confirms retirement news with subtle IG move
body: After reports surfaced that suggested WWE's Rey Mysterio was going to retire in 2027, his wife, Angie Gutierrez, seemed to confirm the news. She reposted a video on Instagram where a wrestling content creator celebrated the Hall of Famer's career after the news surfaced. The video's thumbnail read, "Rey Mysterio is retiring 2027." The Mysterios got married on May 15, 1996. They dated for six years before tying the knot. They have two kids together, both of whom are in WWE. Dominik Mysterio is a two-time former Intercontinental Champion and a former AAA Mega Champion. His sister, Aalyah, recently started training at the Performance Center . The exact date of Mysterio's retirement is unknown. Reports stated that there has been "chatter backstage" about his impending retirement in 2027, and WWE is starting to lay out plans for it. He is 51 (and will turn 52 on Dec. 11), and Father Time is undefeated. While Mysterio is still performing at a high level, it makes sense that he wants to start winding down his career. Plus, he has accomplished almost everything imaginable in WWE. He has won world championships, midcard championships, a Royal Rumble, and is a Hall of Fame inductee. He and his son also became the first father-son duo to win tag team gold in 2021. Who retires him is the question on everyone's mind. The "Career Killer" Gunther—who has retired John Cena, Goldberg, and AJ Styles—is an option, though he has had limited interactions with Mysterio. They had one televised match during the Oct. 28, 2022, edition of Friday Night SmackDown. The "Ring General" retained the Intercontinental Championship during his 666-day reign. A more likely option is his son, Dominik Mysterio. They previously fought at WrestleMania 39, with the elder Mysterio winning. They faced off again during the July 1, 2024, edition of Monday Night RAW, which Rey Mysterio also won. The last time they shared the ring was during the Oct. 5, 2026, edition of RAW. Rey Mysterio and Dragon Lee lost to Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh.

title: WWE Seemingly Didn't Even Scout Jeff 'JC Mateo' Cobb Before Signing Him (WWE News)
raw_title: WWE Seemingly Didn't Even Scout Jeff 'JC Mateo' Cobb Before Signing Him (WWE News)
body: Jeff Cobb has recalled a rather embarrassing moment behind the scenes in WWE that pretty much exposed just how little company top brass knew about him before he signed on the dotted line. During a chat with SOTO619wrestling , Cobb (who worked in WWE as JC Mateo between 2025-2026) revealed how he found out about the MFTs painted face gimmick. When producers told him about it, they added: "You’re gonna wear the paint like you did in Japan". There was just one problem with that: Cobb hadn't actually wrestled wearing face paints. Ever. Not even once. WWE had mixed him up with another worker, which leads Jeff to assume that they didn't even properly scout him before he joined the promotion . "I think they got me confused with somebody else", he said. It wasn't exactly a great sign that he was going to be used well. As Mateo, Jeff did form a solid tag-team with Tama Tonga, but it was never one that Triple H put his full creative might behind. MFTs was a vehicle to get Solo Sikoa over and that was it. Other members such as JC, Tama, Tonga Loa and newcomer Talla Tonga acted as heavies/muscle for Solo during his various feuds. Then, without much warning, Cobb was released on 2 May 2026 and that was very much that . According to Jeff, wrestling with the paint was "more annoying" than wearing a mask. He wasn't a fan of it at all. WWE thought he'd be fine, because he'd done it before. body: At WWE Elimination Chamber 2023 in Montreal, Sami Zayn challenged Roman Reigns for the WWE Championship. The bout was the culmination of Zayn joining the Bloodline and then stabbing Roman in the back with a chair at the Royal Rumble. The crowd support for Zayn had never been higher, but Reigns walked out of Montreal with another successful title defense under his belt on his road to being champion for 1316 days. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Zayn was asked if he felt he should’ve won in Montreal. “At the time, I thought there was a case to be made for it, but going back to the domino effect thing, I don’t know. I really don’t know. I don’t think it’s ludicrous to say I should have. If you were watching at that time, I think anybody could have made that argument. But it was just again timing, and Cody was also red hot at that time, and they were building to something. Then it leads to Cody the next year, and then it’s more gratifying. Whatever it is, just yeah, I don’t know. Could, should, would- would it have worked? I think so. But who’s to say?” he replied. Zayn would go on to headline night one of WrestleMania 39, teaming with Kevin Owens to defeat The Usos (Jimmy Uso & Jey Uso) to win the WWE Tag Team Championships. Elsewhere during the interview, Sami reflected on his feud with Johnny Knoxville. You can find his full comments here .
summary: Sami Zayn reflected on his WWE Championship match against Roman Reigns at Elimination Chamber 2023 in Montreal. In an interview with Chris Van Vliet, Zayn stated that while timing and plans for Cody Rhodes factored into the decision, he does not think it is ludicrous to argue he should have won the bout. Zayn added that he believed it could have worked but noted the eventual path led to a more gratifying payoff for Rhodes the following year.

kind.quote: I don’t think it’s ludicrous to say I should have.

llm_long: Sami Zayn challenged Roman Reigns for the WWE Championship at Elimination Chamber 2023 in Montreal. The match followed Zayn's time in the Bloodline and his chair attack on Reigns at the Royal Rumble. Reigns retained the title that night on his path toward a 1,316-day championship reign.

Zayn discussed the bout during an interview with Chris Van Vliet on Insight. When asked if he believed he should have won in Montreal, Zayn replied "At the time, I thought there was a case to be made for it, but going back to the domino effect thing, I don’t know." He added that it was not ludicrous to argue he should have won and that anyone watching at the time could have made that case.

Zayn pointed to timing as a key factor in the decision. He noted that Cody was also extremely popular then and that officials were building toward a larger story. This sequence eventually led to Cody's payoff the following year, which Zayn described as more gratifying.

Zayn expressed uncertainty about the potential outcome. He stated "Could, should, would- would it have worked? I think so. But who’s to say?" The crowd support for him in Montreal had reached its peak during that period. Following the Elimination Chamber event, Zayn headlined night one of WrestleMania 39. He teamed with Kevin Owens to defeat The Usos, consisting of Jimmy Uso and Jey Uso, to capture the WWE Tag Team Championships.

title: An EXCELLENT Sign For AEW's Next TV Deal (AEW News)
raw_title: An EXCELLENT Sign For AEW's Next TV Deal (AEW News)
body: Tony Khan is "extremely happy" after meeting with Skydance on Friday in Los Angeles, according to Wrestling Observer head Dave Meltzer . The Observer chief reported that Khan was "the happiest he's been" after crunch talks with combined Warner Bros Discovery and Paramount figureheads. WBD and Paramount had previously merged to formed Skydance, which triggered reports concerned about AEW 's television future. Would there even be a place for products like Dynamite and Collision post-merger? It appears that everything is heading in a positive direction on that front. Khan is chuffed, but Meltzer was keen to point out that Tony has "always been happy about this relationship" and has been "beaming about it since day one". At least publicly, the All Elite head honcho hasn't been worried about what'll happen to his core TV shows . Before The Observer shared this report, Khan had already gone on record to praise Skydance CEO David Ellison - he started the company in 2006, merged with Paramount in 2026, then eventually merged with Warner Bros Discovery this year. Tony believes that Ellison is a strong supporter of pro wrestling, so he's thrilled to be working under his banner. AEW recently promoted the WrestleDream pay-per-view on 17 October , and it's full steam ahead on television ahead of 14 November's Full Gear. Khan will have some major plans in mind when hyping that PPV on Dynamite and Collision, so the last thing he needed was to come out of talks with Skydance fretting. title: Morgan Retains WWE Women's Title vs Lynch

body: Vaquer's injury led general manager Adam Pearce to name Morgan vs. Lynch as the main event for the WWE Women's World Championship . Sami Zayn defeated "The Young OG" Je'Von Evans to retain the Undisputed WWE Championship. IYO SKY defeated WWE Women's Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez in a non-title match. Morgan retained her championship against Lynch in a no-contest. Pearce opened Raw in the ring to announce that Vaquer couldn't make the advertised number-one contender match due to injury. Pearce also said that Morgan and Lynch would battle for the title later in the show. Zayn then entered the ring to complain about Reigns and his lack of television time. The Undisputed WWE Champion demanded television time. Zayn criticized Trick Williams and CM Punk for constantly promoting themselves, arguing that he remains the most underrated talent. The champ took it further, claiming he was responsible for The Bloodline's popularity at its peak and for Raw's success on Netflix. Evans interrupted after hearing his name and entered the ring, demanding that Sami say whatever he wanted to his face. Zayn explained that he owed the young challenger no respect before leaving the ring. Pearce intercepted the champ on the entrance ramp and announced an immediate title match against Evans. Sami spent much of the match selling Evans' high-impact offense, although the contest lacked intensity. Mr. Money in the Bank Penta intercepted Zayn on the entrance ramp as the champion tried to escape during the match. The threat of a cash-in sent the champ back into the ring, setting up a spectacular false finish. Evans hit an OG Cutter, but the count was just shy of three. A later Helluva Kick resulted in a three-count against the challenger. WWE World Tag Team Champions The Vision (Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed) stormed the ring after the match. Breakker and Reed hit multiple spears and Tsunamis to end the segment. Penta and Evans were later announced as the challengers for the WWE World Tag Team Championship at Crown Jewel. The match often looked rehearsed, with obvious communication and verbal cues. That said, there were several hard bumps. Garbage cans, tables, chairs, and everything in sight became a weapon. The hard-hitting spots compensated for the match's uneven flow. Bayley secured the victory after delivering an elbow through a table and applying a submission hold with a kendo stick positioned across Valkyria's face. WWE has transformed the physical and dangerous SKY into a happy-go-lucky babyface for the children. The match featured some athletic spots but leaned heavily into sports entertainment. It was odd to have Rodriguez lose cleanly in non-title action. Roxanne Perez, visibly angry, attacked the victor after the match alongside the WWE Women's Intercontinental Champion. title: Max Caster Says Anthony Bowens Still Works For AEW
raw_title: Max Caster Comments On Anthony Bowens' AEW Status: "He Still Works There"
summary_src: Max Caster comments on his former tag partner's status. In early October, Fightful Select reported that former AEW World Tag Team Champions Anthony Bowens and Max Caster were free agents, as they were no longer with All Elite Wrestling.
body: In early October, Fightful Select reported that former AEW World Tag Team Champions Anthony Bowens and Max Caster were free agents, as they were no longer with All Elite Wrestling. Bowens did a media appearance and addressed his future , but did not clarify whether he was still officially with AEW. During Caster’s virtual signing with K & S WrestleFest , he stated that Bowens is still with AEW. “He’s wrestling.” It was brought up that Anthony Bowens left AEW around the same time as Caster, and Caster replied, “He’s still there. I don’t wanna speak for him too much but he still works there.” On Bowens’ social media, he posted a photo of himself training at the NJPW Dojo.
summary: Per Fightful Select, Max Caster and Anthony Bowens became free agents in early October after leaving AEW. During a virtual signing, Caster confirmed that Bowens remains with the company and is actively wrestling. Bowens recently shared a photo of himself training at the NJPW Dojo on social media.

llm_long: Max Caster told fans during a virtual signing for K & S WrestleFest that Anthony Bowens remains with All Elite Wrestling. Caster made the comment after it was noted that Bowens had left AEW around the same time as him in early October.

He responded that Bowens is still there and added he did not want to speak for him too much but confirmed Bowens still works for the promotion. Caster also stated simply that Bowens is wrestling. Bowens had appeared on media without clarifying his official status with AEW after Fightful Select reported both men were free agents.

On his social media Bowens shared a photo of himself training at the NJPW Dojo. The former AEW World Tag Team and World Trios Champion said he is saying no to wrestling bookings for now. When asked about possibly returning to AEW he replied with the phrase “Never say never.”
Caster explained he agreed to the signing a couple months earlier before the Bound For Glory situation and is honoring the commitment because he respects Brian Myers.
