title: Sami Zayn Criticizes Wrestling Fans for Acting Like They Know Everything
raw_title: Sami Zayn Criticizes Wrestling Fans for Acting Like They Know Everything
summary_src: Sami Zayn doesn’t have a problem with wrestling fans criticizing what they see on television. What gets him is when people talk like they completely understand what’s happening inside the ring when, according to Zayn, there’s a whole other side of wrestling that viewers simply can’t see.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Zayn got onto the subject while praising Kevin Owens and explaining why he believes Owens doesn’t always get enough credit for certain parts of his work. In particular, Zayn praised Owens’ ability to stay present, read what the audience is feeling and adjust what he’s doing instead of simply going through a predetermined series of moments. The problem is that those decisions aren’t always obvious to somebody watching from home. When Van Vliet pointed out that most wrestling fans have never experienced what it’s actually like to perform inside a ring, Zayn agreed and said people sometimes speak with a level of certainty that their experience doesn’t really support. “Dude, let me tell you something. And I don’t want to sound like I’m trashing fans. I am a fan, but I notice I do this in other facets of my life. But when I tell you, people have no clue what they’re talking about — but that’s fine. There’s no way you can know what you’re talking about. So you’re making your comments uninformed, which is totally fine, but maybe just don’t have that same level of conviction. You know what I mean? People speak with such conviction when they don’t know what the hell they’re talking about. And I’m not saying they do it and I don’t. We do it in other things. I do it with sports or movies or whatever. Like, ‘Why would they do that?’ Well, dude, you don’t even know what the hell you’re talking about.” Zayn wasn’t saying fans need to become wrestlers before they’re allowed to criticize wrestling. In fact, he made the opposite point — audiences absolutely have the right to judge entertainment without knowing how it was made. He compared it to watching hockey. Zayn admitted he’ll sometimes watch a player make a mistake and immediately wonder how they could possibly screw something up, despite never having played hockey at that level himself. “Right. But it’s not my job to be on a movie set to be able to appreciate movies, right? So the same way our fans don’t need to know this level of wrestling to be able to comment on it. It’s their right. But I guess what I’m getting at is, you know, I watch hockey. I’m a hockey guy, right? And sometimes I’m blown away. I never played hockey — I mean, I played hockey, but I never played in a league or whatever. So when there’s blunders, I’ll be like, ‘Oh, how does he give up the puck? Who makes that pass?’ Because I’m a fan, right? But there are times when I take inventory of what they’re doing, and I’m like, ‘Oh my God, these are the most skilled human beings on the planet. How are they doing this?’” Van Vliet pointed out that somebody watching hockey on television gets a completely different view from the player actually standing on the ice. Zayn said wrestling works the same way. A wrestler sees and processes things that someone watching from the outside doesn’t. title: Fans Accuse WWE of Using Green Screen for Solo Sikoa’s Promo on October 26 RAW
raw_title: Fans Accuse WWE of Using Green Screen for Solo Sikoa’s Promo on October 26 RAW
summary_src: Solo Sikoa was supposed to be sending a warning on RAW, but fans ended up paying way more attention to what was happening behind him. Apparently, something about the whole segment just looked a little too fake for people to ignore.
body: During the October 26 episode of RAW , Sikoa cut a parking lot promo with The Bloodline standing behind him. He accepted Royce Keys’ challenge before warning him that he wasn’t safe and saying he would soon find out that The Bloodline runs the place. Pretty straightforward Bloodline stuff. Then fans started looking at Roman Reigns and The Usos in the background. Almost immediately, people on Twitter started wondering whether Roman and The Usos were actually there when Sikoa filmed the promo. The way everyone looked in the shot had some viewers convinced WWE had dropped Sikoa in front of a green screen, while others wondered if AI or some other production trick was involved. One fan took to Twitter and made it clear he wasn’t buying the scene at all. “Yo, no bull****, but Roman and The Usos are not actually there, are they???? This gotta be AI or a green screen Solo is talking in front of. 😭” Another fan couldn’t quite explain what was wrong with it — they just knew something felt off and wondered if he was actually cutting a promo in front of a green screen. “Brother, is Solo cutting this promo in front of a green screen or something? Because why does this segment feel so off lmao.” Someone else thought the whole thing looked more like a commercial than a backstage WWE segment and once again believed Sikoa was in front of a green screen. “Idk what it is about this video, but it looks so fake lmao. Did they green screen Solo?? 😭😭 S*** looks like a commercial.” Another fan didn’t even bother asking the question, saying, “This promo being cut on a green screen is frying me.” Then there was one fan who came up with their own theory about how this whole thing might have happened, and naturally Roman Reigns was at the center of it. “I need to know how many takes it took before Roman got bored and said, ‘How can we do this so I can get out of here?’ And then I need to know how long Solo was in front of the green screen LMFAO.” To be clear, there’s no confirmation WWE actually used a green screen, AI or anything else to put the segment together. Fans are basically working off what they saw on television, and sometimes weird lighting, camera settings and post-production can make a perfectly normal shot look strange. Still, once people noticed it, they couldn’t unsee it. Sikoa was standing there trying to tell Royce Keys that he wasn’t safe, while a chunk of the audience was busy trying to figure out whether Roman Reigns and The Usos were even in the same parking lot. Do you think WWE actually used a green screen for Solo Sikoa’s RAW promo, or was there something else making the whole segment look so strange? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Backstage Buzz: CM Punk Threatened Wrestlers During WWE Backstage Meeting Over Thefts
raw_title: CM Punk Threatened Wrestlers During WWE Backstage Meeting Over Thefts
summary_src: Booker T has seen plenty of weird stuff happen inside WWE locker rooms, but apparently there was a point where wrestlers had a much bigger problem than backstage drama. People’s stuff kept disappearing, and eventually the veterans decided they needed to have a little chat with everyone.
body: During an episode of the Hall of Fame podcast , Booker was asked whether he considered himself a locker-room leader during his WWE run, especially while working on SmackDown alongside The Undertaker. Booker said he was definitely one of the guys willing to speak up when something wasn’t right, even if he wasn’t interested in bossing everybody around. That brought back one particular memory. Booker said WWE went through a stretch where belongings were disappearing from the locker room, including things like wallets and iPads. Eventually, the wrestlers held a meeting to deal with it themselves. “I was kind of a locker-room leader, but I didn’t try to boss nobody around or anything like that. But I would definitely say something if something was out of line. I was one of the guys who was going to speak up about the burglaries. Guys were stealing stuff in the locker room. Like, if you leave your iPad or your wallet, it was just like a string of thefts, burglaries, whatever the word is. And we had a meeting about it. I remember having that meeting, and it was just the boys. They appointed me. ‘Book, you going to say something?’ All right, all right, I’ll go say something.” Booker wasn’t the only veteran who addressed the room. Big Show stepped up too, and his message was pretty straightforward — they were supposed to be a family, and stealing from each other wasn’t something they did. “Big Show had said something as well, and the third person was CM Punk. He said something. Big Show goes, ‘Look, guys, we’re family. We don’t do that. That’s not what we do.’” Booker T followed with basically the same approach, trying to get the message across without turning the whole thing into a confrontation. “And then I went and did my part. I said, ‘Hey, guys, look here. We’re family, all right? That’s just the way we do stuff here. We don’t do that.’” Then CM Punk got his turn — and diplomacy apparently wasn’t really on the agenda: “And then CM Punk: ‘If I catch you, you’re in trouble.’” Booker laughed while remembering how quickly Punk changed the tone of the meeting. While he and Big Show were trying to appeal to whoever was stealing the stuff, Punk basically went straight to letting the culprit know what would happen if he caught them. Booker explained that he preferred handling things a little differently. The goal wasn’t just to scare whoever was responsible into stopping — he wanted to actually figure out who was doing it. “Because we were the locker-room leaders. Like I said, I thought it was a diplomatic approach. You want to go from a diplomatic approach, and you want to try to find out who the culprit is. You want it to stop, but more importantly, you want to find out who it is. You don’t want to intimidate him. Exactly. You calm down a little bit. It was one of those types of situations.” Booker never revealed whether they actually caught the person responsible, but the story definitely shows three very different approaches to being a locker-room leader
summary: Per Ringside News: booker was asked whether he considered himself a locker-room leader during his WWE run, especially while working on SmackDown alongside The Undertaker. WWE went through a stretch where belongings were disappearing from the locker room, including things like wallets and iPads, Booker explained.

body: With the tournament already approaching its final stretch, NJPW was in Ibaraki on Tuesday with three Super Junior Tag League matches. Mistico & Masatora Yasuda notched their first victory of the tournament earlier this week but were not able to keep up that momentum here, losing to DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru. There were also wins for Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi and Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X. A Block now has Ishimori & Robbie X and DOUKI & Kanemaru tied for the lead with six points. Because Ishimori & Robbie X have already defeated DOUKI & Kanemaru in the tournament, they own the tiebreaker and are in possession of the A Block lead at the moment. The tournament resumes this Friday (October 30) with B Block matches. After that, there are shows on Saturday (October 31) and Sunday (November 1) before the finals are held at Power Struggle on November 3. The winning team will likely earn a shot at the IWGP Junior Heavyweight Tag Team titles, depending on how the injury situation with El Desperado shakes out. title: Sami Zayn Thought WWE Title Hopes Were Over After McIntyre Loss
raw_title: Sami Zayn believed the ship had sailed on WWE Championship hopes after loss to Drew McIntyre
summary_src: Sami Zayn kicked off the year by challenging Drew McIntyre for the Undisputed WWE Championship at Royal Rumble. Zayn felt the loss had ended his pursuit for the title. Zayn explained on the Insight Podcast that he began to accept the possibility of becoming a World Champion had passed.
body: Sami Zayn kicked off the year by challenging Drew McIntyre for the Undisputed WWE Championship at Royal Rumble. Zayn felt the loss had ended his pursuit for the title. Zayn explained on the Insight Podcast that he began to accept the possibility of becoming a World Champion had passed. Despite coming close during his time in The Bloodline, Zayn felt the underdog narrative had become redundant for him, and the momentum was beginning to fade. “Here’s the thing that’s funny about it because even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew, and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, you know what, maybe the ship sailed. I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that. Then I was close, but if I lost after losing that match, I was like, well, you can’t tell this story again.” “Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, underdog who finally wins the big one- we burnt that card; that card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen.” “I’ve had a tremendous career, and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never [got it]. You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture.” Zayn won the Undisputed WWE Championship at Night of Champions, but his reign was cut short after just nine days when CM Punk returned to SmackDown and defeated him for the title. He eventually got his revenge on Punk in September and reclaimed the title. llm_long: Sami Zayn began the year by facing Drew McIntyre for the Undisputed WWE Championship at the Royal Rumble. Following the defeat, Zayn believed his opportunity to become world champion had ended.

Zayn stated on a podcast that he started to accept the possibility of winning the title had passed him by. He noted that despite coming close during his involvement with The Bloodline, the underdog story felt worn out and his momentum had decreased.

Zayn explained that after the loss to McIntyre he concluded the Cinderella narrative of the persistent underdog finally winning the big one could not be repeated. He felt fans could only be drawn into that story a limited number of times and that the timing was no longer right.

Zayn reflected that he had already enjoyed a strong career and viewed a world title as an optional addition rather than an essential part of his legacy. He emphasized the need to consider the larger perspective beyond any single accomplishment.
Zayn later captured the Undisputed WWE Championship at Night of Champions. His first reign lasted nine days before CM Punk defeated him on SmackDown.
Zayn regained the title in September after securing revenge against Punk.

body: Grey took to Instagram and uploaded a photo dump covering her weekend, including some moments from the recent NXT live event. But the wrestling photos weren’t the only ones getting attention. In a couple of the shots, Grey posed by the pool in a black bikini top while still rocking a pair of jeans, shades and a chain around her waist. She also showed off her abs for good measure while enjoying some downtime. Another photo had a completely different vibe. Grey was at the beach wearing a pink string bikini while holding a tiny teacup pig, which probably wasn’t the combination anyone expected to see when scrolling through an NXT wrestler’s weekend photos. The post comes at a pretty good time for Grey considering she’s finally back doing what she does best. She returned to the ring at WWE’s October 15 live event in Kitchener and defeated Karmen Petrovic in her first match since August 30. For the moment, though, Grey seems to be enjoying being back on the road and having a little fun in between shows. Between wrestling again, hanging out by the pool and somehow finding a teacup pig at the beach, she definitely packed plenty into one weekend. title: WrestleMania 43 Sphere Speculation Gets a Reality Check — Report
raw_title: WrestleMania 43 Sphere Speculation Gets a Reality Check — Report
body: 0 WWE WrestleMania 43 is still scheduled for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in April 2027. However, ongoing tensions in the Middle East have raised questions. Fans have also wondered whether Las Vegas could host the event again. The speculation grew after Eric Bischoff discussed a possible backup plan. He said he would be surprised if The Sphere wasn’t considered. However, a new report has offered a reality check. According to Fightful Select , WWE currently has no plans to use The Sphere in Las Vegas as a backup venue. The report also highlighted scheduling conflicts at the popular venue. The report stated, “There is no indication that WWE is planning to use The Sphere in Las Vegas as a backup WrestleMania venue, despite recent speculation, @FightfulSelect has learned. The venue has John Mayer performances scheduled during the internally targeted April 10–11 dates, as well as at the end of the month. Oprah Winfrey is also there April 2-4.” These existing bookings make The Sphere a difficult option. The report doesn’t completely rule out future changes. However, there is currently no indication of WWE planning this move. WWE WrestleMania 43 remains scheduled for Riyadh in April 2027. WWE has not announced any venue change so far. The ongoing regional tensions have fueled speculation about alternative locations. WWE previously moved WrestleMania 42 to Las Vegas. The event was originally planned for New Orleans. It was later scheduled for April 18 and 19. This decision brought WrestleMania to Las Vegas for two consecutive years. The Sphere was suggested as a possible alternative venue. However, the latest report doesn’t support that speculation. As of now, WrestleMania 43 is still expected in Saudi Arabia. title: Rome Red Cats Welcome Qt Marshall And Tripp Bennett To Ownership Group
raw_title: ROME RED CATS WELCOME QT MARSHALL AND TRIPP BENNETT TO OWNERSHIP GROUP
body: Posted by Staff Reports | Oct 27, 2026 | Top Local Sports | 0 | AEW Executive and Professional Wrestler QT Marshall Joins Accomplished Businessman and Entrepreneur Tripp Bennett as New Partial Owners of the Rome Red Cats ROME, GA — October 26, 2026 — The Rome Red Cats are proud to announce the addition of QT Marshall and Tripp Bennett to the organization’s ownership group. The two accomplished businessmen and sports entertainment entrepreneurs join as partial owners, bringing extensive experience in professional athletics, business development, live entertainment, and community engagement. Already successful business partners through One Fall Wrestling (1FW), Marshall and Bennett share a passion for sports, entertainment, and creating experiences that bring communities together. Their investment in the Rome Red Cats represents an exciting opportunity to contribute to the organization’s continued growth while helping strengthen its connection to fans, local businesses, and the greater Rome community. QT Marshall: Bringing International Sports Entertainment Experience to Rome QT Marshall, whose real name is Michael Cuellari, is an internationally recognized professional wrestler, television personality, producer, and executive with more than two decades of experience in professional wrestling. Currently serving as Senior Vice President of Creative Coordination for All Elite Wrestling (AEW), Marshall plays a significant role behind the scenes of one of the world’s leading professional wrestling organizations. His career has taken him around the globe, providing extensive experience in talent development, television production, live event operations, marketing, and sports entertainment. In addition to his executive role with AEW, Marshall is a partner in One Fall Wrestling (1FW), a rapidly growing professional wrestling promotion based in Georgia that produces more than 100 live events annually. Through 1FW, Marshall has helped bring professional wrestling, nationally recognized athletes, and celebrities to communities throughout the Southeast, emphasizing affordable, family-friendly entertainment. Marshall has already established a strong connection with the Rome community. Earlier this year, 1FW made its debut in Rome with Rumble in Rome, attracting more than 1,300 enthusiastic fans to the Forum River Center. The overwhelmingly positive response led to the promotion’s upcoming return on November 20 for Rome Rampage, another major live wrestling event. “Rome is a community that takes tremendous pride in its sports and entertainment,” said Marshall. “When we brought 1FW here earlier this year, the response was incredible. It showed me how passionate the people of Rome are about supporting something they believe in. When the opportunity came along to become part of the Rome Red Cats, it was something I wanted to be involved with. Tripp and I have built a successful partnership through professional wrestling, and we’re excited to bring our experience,

title: AJ Francis Expected To Re-Sign With TNA
raw_title: WWE Hit Row Alum Gets Major Contract Update — Report
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » WWE Hit Row Alum Gets Major Contract Update — Report Former WWE star AJ Francis could be staying with TNA Wrestling beyond 2026, with a new report revealing the status of his current contract. The former Hit Row member has established himself in TNA since arriving in 2024, and his next move may already be taking shape. According to Fightful Select , Francis’ existing agreement is approaching its expiration date. However, that doesn’t necessarily mean the former Top Dolla is preparing to pack his bags for another promotion. Fightful Select confirmed that Francis’ TNA deal is scheduled to expire toward the end of 2026. The report also indicates he wants to remain with the promotion and that a new agreement between the two sides is expected to be reached. Francis has spent the past two years building his position in TNA after previously wrestling for WWE. During his time with the promotion, he captured the TNA Digital Media Championship and the Canadian International Heavyweight Championship. Both titles have since been discontinued. The 36-year-old originally signed with WWE in January 2020 after spending five years playing defensive line in the NFL. His football career included stints with the Miami Dolphins, Seattle Seahawks, and Washington, along with time on the rosters of the New England Patriots, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and New York Giants. Francis eventually transitioned into professional wrestling, becoming part of Hit Row under the name Top Dolla. Although the group’s WWE run was relatively brief, he has continued his wrestling career since leaving the company. For now, a WWE return or a Hit Row reunion remains unconfirmed. The latest report instead points toward Francis continuing with TNA, provided both sides complete a new deal. The news also arrives amid reports that TNA is preparing to announce more contract agreements in the coming weeks. With several deals reportedly approaching expiration, securing Francis could help the promotion maintain continuity as it plans its future roster. Francis’ contract situation is not yet officially resolved, but indications are positive for TNA. Rather than entering free agency, the former NFL player may be ready to stay in the game with the promotion where he has spent the past two years. title: Bronson Reed Explains 50-Pound Weight Loss
raw_title: Bronson Reed Comments On Physical Transformation, Wanted To Stand Out Upon WWE Return
summary_src: WWE star "Big" Bronson Reeds describes what inspired him to transform his body and how much weight he's lost in the course of it.
body: WWE "Big" Bronson Reed studied the art of perfecting his body while recovering from his torn bicep injury that occurred this past February. Before his comeback at WWE's first-ever Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6, Reed posted a picture online, displaying a more shredded version of himself. Feeling good and ready to pick up where he last left off, the king of Tsunamis explained what propelled him to create this new image of himself, as well as how much weight he's lost so far. "The way I did it is, I really just locked in," Reed began in his interview on "Cheap Heat." "You know, I've had serious injuries before, but this was a serious one with my bicep. I was like, what can I do to sort of stand out when I return? Last time I got injured, I joined The Vision...I thought, you know what, I'm just going to get into great shape. I have a coach in Australia that helps me. He helped me with my nutrition and my strength and conditioning. I was able to drop 50 pounds in those six months when I was injured." Though he couldn't capture a singles win over Oba Femi at Money in the Bank earlier this month, needless to say, that loss has only fueled his fire to stand out in another way among his Vision cohorts. At this time, the Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory are carrying the World Tag Team Championships.
summary: Bronson Reed focused on nutrition and conditioning with an Australian coach while recovering from a torn bicep suffered in February. The WWE star dropped 50 pounds during his six-month absence and returned at Sunday Night's Main Event on September 6 with a noticeably more shredded physique. Reed said he wanted to stand out upon his comeback after previously joining The Vision during an earlier injury recovery.

He explained that he locked in on his goals after reflecting on past injuries and deciding he needed to stand out upon his comeback. Reed said that when he was previously injured he had joined The Vision, but this time he chose to get into great shape with help from a coach in Australia.

The coach assisted Reed with both nutrition and strength and conditioning throughout the recovery period. Currently Bron Breakker and Austin Theory of The Vision hold the World Tag Team Championships.

title: On the Record: Sami Zayn Calls Out The Undertaker’s “Never Be Satisfied” Mentality
raw_title: Sami Zayn Calls Out The Undertaker’s “Never Be Satisfied” Mentality
summary_src: Sami Zayn remembers WWE having a pretty intense mentality when he first arrived in NXT. The message was basically that everyone needed to be chasing the very top, but Zayn thinks taking that mindset too literally can leave a locker room full of miserable people.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Zayn was originally asked whether becoming WWE Champion was something he dreamed about as a kid. That eventually turned into a much bigger conversation about constantly chasing accomplishments and never allowing yourself to enjoy what you’ve already done. Zayn brought up The Undertaker’s WWE Hall of Fame speech as an example. He made it clear he has enormous respect for Undertaker, but one part about never being satisfied stuck with him because his own outlook is a little different. “And that’s a slippery slope. Sure. Okay, I don’t want to get myself in trouble. I remember distinctly — let me preface this by saying I have all the respect in the world for The Undertaker, okay? But I remember him saying distinctly in his WrestleMania Hall of Fame speech, he was almost like a TED Talk, right? He kind of gave his thing of, like, here were my three rules during my career, whatever. And he said something along the lines of, like, ‘Never be content,’ or ‘Never be satisfied.’ And I remember thinking, wow, that is such a different mentality from what I have. On some level, I completely agree, and I actually embody that as well.” Zayn understood the point was really about staying hungry, but he thinks there’s a big difference between wanting more and convincing yourself that whatever you’ve already accomplished isn’t good enough. That mentality was something he heard plenty of during his early WWE days. Zayn recalled NXT having a particularly aggressive way of getting that message across, including telling wrestlers that if they didn’t want to become the next John Cena, they didn’t belong there. “And I think that’s it. But the term, I guess the exact phrasing of not being satisfied — I’m saying the difference between being aspirational and not being satisfied. I know that sounds like a small difference, but it could be a chasm. There could be a world of difference there. Because if you’re not satisfied, then you’re just not appreciating what you’re doing while you’re doing it. You know what I’m saying? This isn’t enough, and this isn’t enough. And there’s a dangerous line where you just become — I don’t want to say, what’s the word I’m looking for here? You just want to appreciate what you’re doing. You want to be satisfied. I think you should be satisfied if you’re doing good work and you’re proud of it. But take inventory of it and go like, I’m getting to do this incredible thing. Is there more I’d like to achieve? Absolutely. And you can be aspirational. And obviously, I am aspirational, or I wouldn’t be sitting in this chair right now talking to you. I wouldn’t have ended up here. But I just think it’s such a slippery slope. We do talk about that. I’ve heard that, and Undertaker’s Hall of Fame speech was not the only time I’ve heard that since I got to this company. When I first got to NXT, there was a lot of that. I know the messaging is correct in what they’re saying, of like, have that hunger, strive for more. But the w

title: Backstage Buzz: Original Plans for Sami Zayn’s WWE Heel Turn Revealed
raw_title: Original Plans for Sami Zayn’s WWE Heel Turn Revealed
summary_src: Sami Zayn’s recent change in attitude wasn’t something WWE just decided to flip on overnight. He’d actually been working toward it for months, and one major loss convinced him that the version of Sami everyone knew had pretty much run its course.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Zayn was asked about the strange spot his character has been in lately. He’s clearly been acting more like a heel, but crowds haven’t always treated him like one, with cheers and boos following him depending on the night. That was actually part of the plan. Zayn said he never wanted the usual wrestling heel turn where somebody suddenly decides they’re a bad guy. He wanted fans to slowly start changing how they felt about him. It all really started after Zayn lost to Drew McIntyre at the Royal Rumble. At that point, he felt like WWE couldn’t keep going back to the same story of Sami Zayn being the lovable underdog desperately chasing his first world championship. “Yeah, I think it’s kind of — I don’t know when this is going to air, but today’s date is what? October 6th? Seventh? Yeah, October 7th. Okay, so it’ll probably air within two weeks. I’m only saying that because it really sometimes does evolve week to week. There’s a lot of evolution that’s happened, and part of what I’ve liked about this sort of turn is that it wasn’t done as a conventional turn. It wasn’t done, ‘Good guy, good guy, good guy, now I’m bad.’ You know what I mean? It was just a very gradual process, and it all started when I lost to Drew at the Royal Rumble. I realized, well, we’ve played this card. Can’t play it again. So something needs to change now.” Sami Zayn wanted to take his time with it. Instead of forcing the crowd to hate him, he planned on gently pushing them in that direction and seeing how they reacted along the way. “And I’d like it to be gradual, and I’d like to just feel the audience. I’d like to obviously nudge the audience in a certain direction, but I want to do it in this sort of delicate way. And there were things that, again, unexpected gifts that fall from the sky, or just hands that you’re dealt that you don’t know are going to be dealt, that sometimes put us on a fast track one way or took us in a different direction another way.” Zayn even had a rough idea of where he wanted the crowd split to be. At the beginning, he estimated around 90 percent of the audience was still cheering him, and he wanted to slowly chip away at that instead of immediately turning everyone against him. “So, for example, when I beat Carmelo Hayes for the title, it went from like 80-20 cheers. It went from like 90-10. I had 10 to work with in the beginning, and I’d like to get that number to like 70-30, maybe 60-40. So 90% cheers in January or whatever. Just enough to hear one or two guys going, ‘Boo.’ Like, okay, perfect. I can work with that, and I’ll just gently tip those scales.” Weekly television had other ideas, though. Zayn said there were points where he couldn’t get the exact crowd reaction he wanted, so he basically had to roll with whatever came his way. “There was this fine balancing point that I wanted to get to, and I couldn’t get to it when I wanted to get to it because that’s just weekly television, and that’s the hand you’re de

title: Drew McIntyre Explains WWE's Openness To Outside Projects
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Teases WWE Return, Explains Ability To Do So Many Outside Projects
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has discussed why he believes WWE is more open to its wrestlers appearing in movies than it was during the Vince McMahon era.
body: WWE Drew McIntyre has discussed why WWE is now more open to allowing its wrestlers to feature in movies and talked about his return to the ring. McIntyre is currently off WWE television as he is busy in Hollywood, filming movies like " The Last Druid " and "Highlander." He's not the only WWE wrestler acting in movies, as the likes of Roman Reigns, Becky Lynch , and Cody Rhodes have also taken on acting roles recently. McIntyre attributes this to the new management being more open to wrestlers taking on projects outside WWE. "I think a lot of people have talked about it, like Vince was very much like, I need you here. And to be fair, we had so many live events back in the day. My entire life up until the past few years was wrestling every single week, 52 weeks a year, three times a week, minimum," said McIntyre. "But you know, as I said, Nick [Khan] and Paul [Levesque] are very much of the mindset, like if it makes sense, if it helps everybody and helps your brand, which in turn helps our brand [it's good], because I'm not going anywhere anytime soon." McIntyre recalled his early years in WWE, when he shared the ring not only with the likes of Triple H and Shawn Michaels, who were a generation ahead of him, but also with legends like Ric Flair. He reminded fans — and his peers — that he is just 41 years old and that they will be seeing more of him soon. "I remind everyone my age all the time. I just turned 41 the other week. I'm 285 pounds. I'm the biggest I've ever been. You see the way I'll be hitting ropes, I'm the fastest I've ever been. My body feels fantastic. My mind's right. My body's right. It's just whenever I decide to bring Hollywood Drew back to WWE, it's going to get rolling," warned McIntyre. McIntyre is currently focused on his Hollywood career but has also been hitting the ring ropes, where he showed off his impressive physique in what could be an ominous sign for his peers in WWE.
summary: Drew McIntyre is currently away from WWE television while filming movies including The Last Druid and Highlander. He credited new leadership under Nick Khan and Paul Levesque for being open to wrestlers taking on outside projects if they benefit all parties and the brand. McIntyre noted that previous management required near-constant wrestling appearances year-round unlike the current approach.

title: Cody Rhodes Reveals Kevin Owens Set Up Tribute Camera For PAC
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Shares That Kevin Owens Set Up Camera At WWE Event So People Could Speak About Benjamin Satterley (PAC)
summary_src: Cody Rhodes speaks further about Benjamin Satterley. As of this writing, it has been almost a full month since the passing of Benjamin Satterley, a.k.a.
body: As of this writing, it has been almost a full month since the passing of Benjamin Satterley, a.k.a. PAC. There have been tributes from wrestlers, personalities, companies, and promotions across the wrestling world. While doing his media run to promote the Street Fighter movie, Cody Rhodes was interviewed by WrestleTalk , and he was asked to share words about Satterley. He mentioned that Kevin Owens set up a camera at a WWE event so people could speak about Satterley. “I wanna share something that was really nice, and I hope he doesn’t mind me sharing but Kevin Owens, at the most recent TV, decided that — and I hope you get to see these. Maybe they’ll just be for the family — but he had a camera set up for all of us to go speak to, if we wanted to speak about Ben, and I thought long and hard about what’s my relationship there because we weren’t incredibly great friends but, if you look at your career and you look over across the ring at these milestones: SummerSlam in Barclays Center. To have the Arrow crossover match, and there he is, there’s Ben, and then you look at my time away and being one of the OGs when AEW started and there’s Ben, and I’m looking through our texts and you start to think, wow, we were married to each other at one point through live events when it was Stardust versus Neville. I was riding with Brodie (Lee) and you, and they were going over what has better exports: Newcastle or Rochester, New York, and both of them to not be here anymore… What I’ll say about Ben is never did I meet a wrestler of my generation or even younger, whatever it be, that knew himself more, that knew who he was more, and when you’re like me, you’re someone who’s trying to find out who I am. Who I am on screen, who I am behind the scenes, how do I look, how do I talk. That’s almost intimidating, and I’m better off as a human, as a wrestler, as a storyteller for having met him to learn that lesson. I mean, a better way to put it is the ultimate bullsh*t meter. The ultimate person to know what’s performative, what’s not, and when you could go at the level he went in the ring, you have that right and that ability and he will be beyond missed. It will echo and it will echo throughout wrestling schools all across the country, who wanna emulate the style that he had, and I would say to those who are doing that, nobody looked like they were taking more risks but was more sufficient, efficient, and safe. A pro’s pro, a man’s man, an incredible human being.” All Elite Wrestling honored Satterley’s life and career with a tribute show . WWE put out a video tribute on YouTube that featured wrestlers, including Kevin Owens, speaking about the multi-time champion.
summary: Nearly a month after Benjamin Satterley's passing, Cody Rhodes shared during a WrestleTalk interview promoting the Street Fighter movie that Kevin Owens arranged a camera at the most recent WWE TV taping. The setup allowed wrestlers to record personal messages about Satterley, which may be kept for the family. Rhodes reflected on his own career intersections with Satterley, including their SummerSlam match in Barclays Center.

Rhodes explained that he reflected deeply on their connection, noting they were not extremely close yet appeared together at significant career points including a SummerSlam match at Barclays Center and an "Arrow" crossover bout.

He recalled Satterley's presence during his own hiatus from WWE and as an original figure when AEW launched, while reviewing old text messages that highlighted their shared history such as working live events as Stardust versus Neville.

Rhodes observed that he had never encountered another wrestler who possessed such a complete understanding of his own identity, describing the quality as intimidating while he navigated his personal and character development.
He concluded that knowing Satterley and absorbing lessons from him had improved him as a person, wrestler, and storyteller.

title: WWE Launches ID Independent Development Program
raw_title: WWE launches new indie wrestling development program
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email October 29, 2024 – WWE today announced the launch of a first-of-its-kind developmental program designed to provide up-and-coming independent wrestlers a pathway to a potential career in WWE. The program will be called WWE ID , short for WWE Independent Development™. “WWE ID is the latest in our efforts to identify and support the journey of up-and-coming wrestlers, in turn raising the profile of and strengthening the independent wrestling ecosystem,” said WWE Chief Content Officer Paul “Triple H” Levesque. Following the 2021 launch of WWE’s NIL program, WWE ID has been constructed to support independent wrestling prospects and wrestling schools with world-class training, development and mentorship. Under the program, WWE will provide prominent independent wrestling schools with the WWE ID official designation, with the goal of providing new trainees and existing talent at these select institutions with enhanced developmental opportunities. Booker T’s Reality of Wrestling (Houston), Cody Rhodes’ Nightmare Factory (Atlanta), Seth Rollins’ Black and Brave Academy (Davenport, Iowa), Elite Pro Wrestling Training Center (Concord, N.H.) and KnokX Pro Academy (Los Angeles) are the first WWE ID independent wrestling schools to earn the official designation. Additionally, WWE ID will identify top independent wrestling prospects with an official WWE ID “prospect” designation and support their developmental journey by providing financial opportunity and assisting with training, mentorship and development, including access to world-class facilities, best-in-class ring training, athletic trainers and more. WWE ID will give fans the opportunity to follow the paths of these standout prospects on the independent wrestling scene through curated, behind-the-scenes content, as well as highlights and matches showcased across WWE’s social platforms. To learn more about WWE ID and WWE’s recruiting process, please visit recruit.wwe.com .

The program offers world-class training, development and mentorship following the 2021 NIL launch, with participating schools receiving an official WWE ID designation. WWE Chief Content Officer Paul Levesque described it as an effort to strengthen the independent wrestling ecosystem.

title: Bobby Lashley Flexes His New Tesla Cybertruck Purchase
raw_title: Bobby Lashley Flexes His New Tesla Cybertruck Purchase
summary_src: Bobby Lashley has a new ride, and apparently he had one very specific reason for buying it. The AEW star has joined the growing list of wrestling names with a Tesla Cybertruck, but he seems more interested in what the truck can do than simply showing it off.
body: Lashley took to Instagram and uploaded a video revealing his recent Cybertruck purchase. The clip started by asking a pretty simple question: “Why would you even get a Tesla?” Lashley’s answer didn’t require much explaining. The video showed Lashley sitting casually behind the wheel while the Cybertruck appeared to drive itself, with dramatic orchestra music playing in the background. Lashley was basically just chilling in the driver’s seat and letting the vehicle do the work. He also had some fun comparing himself to the famously bulky-looking truck in the caption. He’s certainly not the first wrestling name to get his hands on a Cybertruck either. Jade Cargill , Liv Morgan and Booker T have all previously revealed their own purchases. Kane joined that list earlier this year and took things a little further by customizing his Cybertruck with orange decals and “Big Orange Machine” branding as a nod to his famous WWE nickname. He proudly declared, “I love my Cybertruck!” while showing it off in March. Now Lashley has joined the Cybertruck club as well. His truck might not have the “Big Orange Machine” treatment, but considering Lashley’s caption about the two having the same build, he’s already found his own way to make the purchase fit his personality. Would you trust a Cybertruck to handle the driving while you sit back like Bobby Lashley, or would you rather keep your hands on the wheel? Let us know what you think in the comments. He underwent emergency surgery for his injury and was sent to a specialist. Hager’s fiance Patricia Blackburn told Slap News that Hager had a detached retina and had to undergo additional surgery to rettach it. It was discovered this week that Jake had a detached retina, he underwent surgery to reattach, which doctors have said went better than expected. Send your love and prayers to Jake and Patricia as they navigate a very sensitive and unpredictable recovery Jake Hager is 1-2 in his Power Slap career. llm_long: Jake Hager suffered a brutal injury during his Power Slap 23 bout against Johnny Magna. The match took place on September 17 and ended in a TKO loss for Hager after he began bleeding from the eye following repeated slaps.

The fight was stopped immediately and Hager was sent for emergency surgery after sustaining a globe fracture. Power Slap co-owner Dana White described the injury as the worst seen in the UFC, Power Slap or any related promotion and refused to air replays of the blow.

Hager’s fiancée Patricia Blackburn revealed this week that doctors discovered he had a detached retina requiring additional surgery to reattach it. Blackburn stated that the procedure went better than expected and asked fans to send love and prayers to the couple during what she called a sensitive and unpredictable recovery.

Hager stands at 1-2 in Power Slap after winning his April debut by third-round knockout against Devon Jenkins and signing a six-fight contract with the promotion. It remains unclear whether he will be able to fulfill the remaining dates on that deal following the severity of the eye injury.

title: Sami Zayn Dislocated Shoulder Twice vs. John Cena
raw_title: WWE star dislocated shoulder twice during John Cena match
summary_src: Sami Zayn reflected on responding to John Cena’s open challenge for the United States Championship on the May 4, 2015 edition of WWE Raw in Canada. Zayn suffered a dislocated shoulder in the bout and revealed on the Insight Podcast that it happened twice.
body: Sami Zayn reflected on responding to John Cena’s open challenge for the United States Championship on the May 4, 2015 edition of WWE Raw in Canada. Zayn suffered a dislocated shoulder in the bout and revealed on the Insight Podcast that it happened twice. However, h was so focused on the match that Zayn did not fully process the pain he was experiencing. “I don’t know (the amount of pain), nominal, because I kind of couldn’t focus on it. I had other things to do. I had a different task at hand. Your body has this amazing ability to kind of compartmentalize things. It kind of hit more after the fact. The adrenaline was running high. It actually dislocated twice. The first time it subluxed, which is popping out and popping back in, happened so fast that I almost wasn’t sure it happened.” He added feeling slightly disoriented in the match but it did not detour him from the ultimate goal of wanting to defeat Cena. “Yeah, that’s the one that happens on the stairs, out and in so fast that I was actually confused, ‘Did I imagine that? Am I okay? What just happened? What was that pop?’ But it was moving and it was fine. I just didn’t know what happened. But then maybe two, three minutes into the match, he gives me a back suplex, and then it goes out and it doesn’t really come back in. I remember the doctor going like, ‘You good? What do you want to do?’ I’m like, ‘Well yeah, just stick around, stand by, because I don’t know what’ll happen, but I got a job to do.’ So I couldn’t really focus on it. But that was a really special night too.” Cena retained the US title in the bout despite Zayn being a favored pick by the audience in his home country. Zayn has often expressed how Cena has been supportive of his WWE Title pursuit and career. Following his first Undisputed WWE Championship win, Zayn recalled an emotional text from Cena, who told him he had done it his way. title: Injury Update: Jake Hager Undergoes Surgery to Repair Detached Retina After Power Slap Injury
raw_title: Jake Hager Undergoes Surgery to Repair Detached Retina After Power Slap Injury
summary_src: Jake Hager’s recovery from his horrific Power Slap eye injury has hit another serious hurdle. The former WWE star needed another surgery after doctors discovered a detached retina, though there is at least some encouraging news coming out of the procedure.
body: Slap News took to Instagram and shared the latest update provided by Hager’s fiancée, Patricia Blackburn. According to the post, doctors discovered sometime this week that Hager had suffered a detached retina in his injured eye. That meant another trip into surgery, this time to reattach the retina. Thankfully, doctors apparently felt the procedure went even better than they expected. “It was discovered this week that Jake had a detached retina. He underwent surgery to reattach, which doctors have said went better than expected. Send your love and prayers to Jake and Patricia as they navigate a very sensitive and unpredictable recovery. The former WWE and AEW star suffered the original injury at Power Slap 23 in Lubbock, Texas, back in September. Hager took a brutal strike from Johnny Magna that left him bleeding from his left eye and ear, and the fight was immediately stopped. Hager later underwent emergency eye surgery after suffering a globe rupture . For a while, there wasn’t much information about exactly how much damage had been done or what his chances were of regaining his vision. There was finally some encouraging news on October 8 when Slap News reported that Sinn Bodhi had revealed Hager could see out of his injured left eye. However, it was still unclear how much of his vision would ultimately return, and the possibility of additional surgeries was already on the table. Unfortunately, that possibility has now become reality with doctors discovering the detached retina. The good news is that the latest surgery apparently went better than expected. Still, Blackburn’s update makes it clear that Hager isn’t out of the woods yet, describing his recovery as both “sensitive and unpredictable.” For now, there’s no clear timetable for Hager’s recovery or any indication of how much vision he’ll ultimately regain. After multiple surgeries following such a serious eye injury, the focus remains on how his eye responds to treatment from here. title: Samoa Joe Predicts New Level Will Shine In AEW
raw_title: Samoa Joe Says New Level Was 'Restrained' In WWE, Will Reach Full Potential In AEW
summary_src: Samoa Joe, who traded WWE for AEW, believes The New Level, Kofi and Austin Creed, will take their wrestling to another level in Tony Khan's promotion.
body: AEW Austin Creed and Kofi have enjoyed a new lease of life in AEW after years in WWE, with Samoa Joe believing the move will allow them to showcase their full repertoire. Joe knows a thing or two about trading WWE for AEW, with the veteran star finding considerable success in Tony Khan's promotion, including two reigns as world champion . He recently spoke to " The Takedown on SI ," where he asserted that AEW fans would have a chance to see The New Level take their wrestling to another level and showcase things they have never seen from Creed and Kofi. "I think if anything, you're going to start seeing the kind of the range and the variety and the actual flexibility they have stylistically," said Joe. "You know, I think for a lot of years, you might have seen a more restrained version of what they were in the past [in WWE], and I think now you're going to kind of see them to their full potential." The New Level aren't worried about adapting to their new surroundings in AEW , insisting they can thrive in any environment. They explained that their new tag team name reflects their desire to take themselves to a new level while bringing a higher level of competition to AEW . Creed and Kofi were part of a team that helped revive tag team wrestling in WWE for years, alongside the likes of The Usos. The duo could look to recreate that success in AEW, where they would face teams like FTR, Cage and Cope, the Motor City Machine Guns, and potentially The Young Bucks, who could be their biggest rivals in AEW. Kofi has admitted that a rivalry with Kenny Omega and The Young Bucks was one of the main reasons that he and Creed joined AEW.

title: NXT Halloween Havoc Go-Home Preview

summary_src: NXT presents the Halloween Havoc go-home show from the Performance Center in Orlando tonight, with their fall PLE on tap this Saturday night. The field in the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic will be whittled down to two, with the semifinals scheduled to go down tonight.
body: The top two matches on the Halloween Havoc card are locked in, with Grayson Waller and Kelani Jordan scheduled to defend NXT’s top two prizes this Saturday, and both stories are intriguing in their own ways. For Grayson Waller and Tony D’Angelo, they gave us a history lesson on last week’s show, talking about their beginnings in the paint splotch NXT 2.0 days. Tony D asserted himself early in that promo battle last Tuesday, but looked a little foolish when Grayson went meta and pointed out that D’Angelo hasn’t had the same edge since he dropped his mafia boss gimmick. In this writer’s opinion, they may have waited a little too long to remind us all of the personal history between these two to make the title match at Havoc feel important. Instead of nullifying the win and needing to completely redo his #1 contender’s match, GM Robert Stone made Sinclair’s title match with Kelani Jordan official for Halloween Havoc. Adding another layer of suspense was the return of former NXT Women’s Champion Kendal Grey, who is finally medically cleared after dealing with vestibular issues late this summer. While many in the NXT audience dread the possibility of this match leading to tension in the WrenQCC, will The Standout continue her championship reign and do what she can to drive a wedge between Wren and Kendal? Elsewhere on the Havoc Card, Izzi Dame takes on Zaria, inexplicably without the Women’s North American Championship on the line. Plus, Naraku takes on Shiloh Hill, and Zilla Fatu goes head-to-head with Charlie Dempsey, with the latter featuring the return of NXT’s ‘Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal’ stipulation. How will the participants in those three singles grudge matches look to get the upper hand on their opponents on the last show before the PLE? The return of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic has delivered high-octane tag team action in recent weeks, narrowing the field to four. The tournament semifinals go down on tonight’s show, with the two winning teams presumably moving on to Halloween Havoc in the Dusty Cup Finals. One semifinal match features the NXT Tag Team Champions, the Vanity Project, taking on Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno. Smokes and Baylor of the Vanity Project will compete in just their second tournament match after earning a first-round bye and defeating Mini Vikingo and Chazz “Starboy” Hall in the quarterfinals. Across the ring will be the team that has arguably been the most impressive in the tournament so far. Dar and Moreno knocked off Los Americanos in the first round, then upset one of the best NXT tag teams of this decade, Fraxiom, in the quarterfinals. title: John Cena to Reveal Details on Raw for His New Classic
raw_title: John Cena hypes WWE Raw appearance: ‘The wait is over, the speculation ends’
summary_src: We should find out some of the details for WWE’s first-ever John Cena Classic when Cena appears on Raw next week. Last night, it was announced that Cena would be appearing on the November 2 episode of Raw from Brooklyn, New York.
body: We should find out some of the details for WWE’s first-ever John Cena Classic when Cena appears on Raw next week. Last night, it was announced that Cena would be appearing on the November 2 episode of Raw from Brooklyn, New York. It’s his first time back on the show since retiring from in-ring competition. Cena sent out a tweet this morning hyping up the appearance and confirming that he’ll be starting the build to the John Cena Classic. “Make sure not to miss #WWERaw next week. SPECIAL START TIME OF 6PM EST! The wait is over, the speculation ends 11/2,” he wrote. “Let’s build this ‘Never Seen’ CLASSIC! OUR time is NOW!” Cena is now an ambassador for WWE after retiring from the ring in December 2025. The John Cena Classic was his idea and is intended to be WWE’s version of an All-Star Game, spotlighting talent from both the main roster and NXT. A fan vote will be held to determine the John Cena Classic Champion, with wrestlers eligible to win even if they lose their matches. It’s likely going to be a ceremonial championship that is not defended. The John Cena Classic, which will be taking place this December , has been in the works for some time. Cena first announced the show during his appearance at WWE Backlash this May. He and WWE did not have the entire idea worked out then. And while the details have since been figured out internally, WWE has still yet to officially announce the date and location for the event or reveal where it will be airing. That could come during Cena’s Raw appearance. Along with Raw happening live from Brooklyn next Monday, WWE will pre-tape the November 6 episode of SmackDown that night. The company is still scheduled to be in Saudi Arabia for Night of Champions 2026 on November 7. title: On the Record: John Cena Set to Opens Up On Details About John Cena Classic on November 2 WWE RAW

summary_src: John Cena is coming back to RAW next week, and apparently he’s finally ready to explain what the hell the John Cena Classic actually is. After letting fans speculate about the tournament, Cena says the waiting game ends in Brooklyn.
body: Cena took to Twitter ahead of the November 2 episode of RAW and teased a pretty big night. Not only will he be back on WWE television, but he confirmed that he’s finally going to reveal details about the John Cena Classic. Cena didn’t reveal anything early either. Instead, he told fans they’ll have to tune in if they want answers. “Make sure not to miss #WWERaw next week. SPECIAL START TIME OF 6PM EST! The wait is over, the speculation ends 11/2. Let’s build this ‘Never Seen’ CLASSIC! OUR time is NOW!” So yeah, Cena is clearly having some fun with this. The “Never Seen” line is an obvious play on “You Can’t See Me,” while “OUR time is NOW” gives his entrance theme another little shoutout. Beyond that, though, Cena is keeping his mouth shut about what the tournament actually involves. WWE previously announced that Cena will appear on the November 2 edition of RAW at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn. It’ll be his first appearance on Monday Night RAW in nearly a year, so his return was already going to be a big deal even before he started teasing a tournament reveal. Cena may be retired from the ring, but he clearly isn’t completely disappearing from WWE. He’s been pretty open about missing the company since calling it a career, and now he’s coming back with something that already has fans guessing about what he’s cooked up. For now, Cena wants everyone to keep guessing for a few more days. Come November 2, though, he says the speculation is officially over. title: On the Record: Sami Zayn Weighs In On winning the WWE Title after years of being an underdog character
raw_title: Sami Zayn comments on winning the WWE Title after years of being an underdog character
body: During an interview with Chris Van Vliet, Sami Zayn commented on winning the WWE Title after years of being an underdog character. Here is what Zayn had to say… “Here’s the thing that’s funny about it: even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew [McIntyre], and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, ‘You know what? Maybe the ship sailed.’ I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that, I was close. But if I lost after losing that match, I was like, ‘Well, you can’t tell this story again.’ Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, the underdog who finally wins the big one—we burned that card. That card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen. I’ve said this before in other interviews, or to friends, or my wife, or whatever. I’ve had a tremendous career, and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never got it. You know what I mean? You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture. I don’t think anything changed, and that’s actually the point. It’s that I kept doing what I do, which is making sure that everything I’m involved in is as good as it could possibly be. Eventually, a lot has to happen, even when you’re doing good work and you’re great and all this stuff, to win the WWE Championship. It is like there is no such thing as a fluke win. I know when I won it the first time and it was nine days, in character, you could say I was a fluke. There’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. To even be in the periphery of it is insane. To even be in the mix, to even be in the discussion, to even have title matches, even if you’re losing them, is extremely one in a billion already, to be put in that position. So to win it, there’s an immeasurable number of variables that are required to be in that position. So there’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. So I just think kind of slow and steady wins the race. You keep doing good work, and then it’s timing, and that’s the thing that a lot of people don’t account for. There are so many variables that are out of your control. Of course, you control what you can control, but there are so many variables that are just not yours to play with. title: On the Record: Sami Zayn Explains Why His First WWE Championship Win Was More Special Than His Second Reign
raw_title: Sami Zayn Explains Why His First WWE Championship Win Was More Special Than His Second Reign
body: Sami Zayn answers which WWE Championship reigns mean more to him. Earlier in June, Sami Zayn became the WWE Champion for the first time in his career. He defeated Cody Rhodes and Gunther in a triple-threat situation at the Night of Champions premium live event. His first WWE Title victory took him over 13 years, but he lost the belt only 9 days later. There weren’t a lot of fans who thought Zayn would win the WWE Title in the first place, let alone regain the belt from CM Punk. Zayn recently sat down for an interview with Chris Van Vliet on Insight , where he was asked which of his two WWE Title reigns meant more to him. The WWE Champion said that while his second title reign has been “really rewarding,” it was his first time winning the belt that meant more to him. “Well, I’d say the first win. That’s more special because the first is the first, right? But I’m really enjoying what I’m doing right now, and I know it’s only been maybe a month or I don’t even know how long it’s been, but I like this trajectory I’m on currently, and having some fun to tell some stories and have these challengers all waiting in the wings and get to do this like kind of character work. That’s been really rewarding. That’s really fun.” His second title reign has been much better than his first one as well. Zayn has defended the title numerous times against other stars, with his last match taking place against Je’Von Evans on the October 26 edition of Monday Night Raw.
summary: Sami Zayn answers which WWE Championship reigns mean more to him. Earlier in June, Sami Zayn became the WWE Champion for the first time in his career.

title: Bully Ray Says Some Promotions Fail To Maximize Talent
raw_title: Bully Ray On Royce Keys: 'Some Places' Don't Know How To Use Talent To Max Potential
summary_src: Bully Ray isn't surprised by Royce Keys' strong booking in WWE, taking a veiled dig at other promotions for failing to get the best out of their wrestlers.
body: WWE Bully Ray has seemingly taken a veiled dig at AEW over how it handled Royce Keys, formerly known as Powerhouse Hobbs, compared to WWE. Keys, who debuted in WWE at the start of the year after six years in AEW, has been featured in a prominent storyline on WWE television, leading the 946 against The Bloodline. Ray said on " Busted Open " that he isn't shocked by how effective Keys has been in WWE, criticizing other promotions for not knowing how to get the best out of their wrestlers. "I'm not nearly as shocked [as to how Keys has been used in WWE]," said Ray. "Some places just don't know how to utilize talent to their maximum potential." Ray believes that Keys' screen time and the way she has been utilized on WWE television, which he hinted wasn't the case in AEW, come down to timing. He considers timing an important factor in any wrestler's success in pro wrestling. "A term that you hear over and over and over again in the world of professional sports entertainment — timing is everything," Ray added. "Now, that goes for real life, but my god, timing is everything truly when it comes into play in our world. It really does. Timing was right for Royce Keys." WWE has pushed several former AEW stars, including Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, and Penta, and Keys — the leader of 946 — could be next in line. Keys is aiming high in WWE, outlining his goal of winning a championship by the end of the year . However, WWE appears to have even bigger plans for him, with reports indicating that the TKO-owned promotion sees him as a potential future world champion . For now, Keys and his 946 group are set to battle it out with The Bloodline, with the match likely set to take place at Survivor Series at the end of November.

body: UFC fighter Khamzat Chimaev recently discussed his rivalry with Sean Strickland, saying that he will ‘chase’ him across weight classes if he has to, just to get to fight him in the octagon. Speaking to Red Corner MMA , Chimaev said that he believes will happen, even if he has to move up to Light Heavyweight or Heavyweight: “We will make this matchup, bro, don’t worry, if I’ve got to light heavyweight, heavyweight, wherever he goes I will go after him. “Yeah, I’m the hunter and he’s (Strickland) a chicken running away” the Middleweight fighter added. “If he goes (to heavyweight) I will go up. Who cares, I don’t care, bro, so for the pay I’m here.” It is not confirmed if the UFC are planning to put Chimaev and Strickland in the octagon together anytime soon, but when it does (likely) happen, it could end up being the main event of a numbered PPV-level card on Paramount+. title: On the Record: Max Caster Praises Tony Khan for Financially Supporting Wrestlers, Breaks Down Possibly Returning to AEW
raw_title: Max Caster Praises Tony Khan for Financially Supporting Wrestlers, Discusses Possibly Returning to AEW
body: During a recent interview with K&S WrestleFest , former AEW star Max Caster praised his former AEW boss Tony Khan for financially supporting wrestlers and the wrestling business. He also spoke about possibly returning to AEW at some point, saying, “never say never.” Caster recently exited AEW. He wrestled one match for TNA Wrestling at Bound for Glory. Below are some highlights (via Fightful ): “I always gotta shout out Tony Khan, because he’s supporting a lot of wrestlers living right now… including me. I’m still living off AEW money… That’s a guy who, for whatever reason in his heart, is supporting wrestling and supporting wrestlers.” “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never. However, I am saying no to wrestling bookings right now, and that would be a wrestling booking, so, I don’t know.” “I agreed to do the virtual signing a couple months ago, I think. I’m honoring this… especially because we know Brian (Myers). I gotta respect Brian too, so this is my last wrestling thing for a while, so whoever’s here, I’m sure somebody is clipping this, waiting for me to say something crazy. I’m gonna try not to today. But this will be the last time you guys see me for an undefined amount of time.” As previously noted , Max Caster recently stated that he’s taking a hiatus from the ring and undergoing therapy.
summary: Former AEW star Max Caster praised his former AEW boss Tony Khan for financially supporting wrestlers and the wrestling business. He additionally spoke about possibly returning to AEW at some point, saying, never say never. Caster recently exited AEW.

llm_long: WWE announced that John Cena will return to Monday Night RAW on November 2, 2026. The episode will take place at the Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. This marks his first live RAW appearance since retiring from in-ring competition.

Cena last appeared on RAW almost a year ago. WWE has not revealed his role for the show, which could include serving as an emcee or appearing in a backstage segment. He will not take any bumps, having ruled them out after retirement.

The reason for his return is unknown but comes ahead of Crown Jewel on November 7, 2026 in Saudi Arabia. Cena hosted WrestleMania 42 earlier this year and announced the inaugural John Cena Classic tournament at WWE Backlash in May 2026.

He retired from in-ring action in December 2025 after a year-long retirement tour that included 18 matches. His final match was a loss by tapout to Gunther at Saturday Night's Main Event on December 13, 2025. Cena has signed a five-year WWE ambassador agreement and remains involved with the company through special appearances and non-wrestling roles.

title: Perry Saturn Recovers After Third COVID-19 Bout
raw_title: WWE legend contracts COVID-19; shares post-hospitalization update
body: Recently, after a series of health mishaps in the wrestling world , fans were again concerned when the news of legend Perry Saturn's hospitalization became public. Former WWE wrestler and YouTuber Maven recently revealed that Saturn had been in and out of the hospital and unreachable for several days. Saturn has now explained what happened. Speaking on his YouTube channel, Saturn revealed that he contracted COVID-19 for the third time despite being vaccinated. Saturn further shared that when his breathing worsened, he lost his voice and had trouble talking; he returned to the emergency room, where doctors also diagnosed an upper respiratory infection. Saturn stayed in the ER for about 48 hours, coughing up thick mucus and finding it hard to get relief. He stated that a doctor acknowledged uncertainty about the issue, and after limited help for his cough, he brought along his own over-the-counter medicine. Once treatment began, his condition improved, and two days later, he was back up. The WWE legend is currently recovering but still requires his cough medicine. Saturn also hilariously compared his illness with the feeling of having Yokozuna sitting on his chest with Rikishi on his lap. Saturn, 60, is a former ECW, WWE, and WCW star, where he spent the most successful years of his career. While he also actively wrestled in the indies, fans became aware of him through his work in the above-mentioned three promotions. He also successfully managed to win several tag-team and singles titles across all of these promotions. Now retired from in-ring action, his last match dates back to 2013.
summary: Former WWE star Perry Saturn was hospitalized after contracting COVID-19 for the third time despite being vaccinated. He also suffered an upper respiratory infection that caused him to lose his voice, cough up thick mucus and struggle to breathe, leading to a 48-hour stay in the emergency room. Saturn has since improved with treatment and is now recovering at home while still using cough medicine.

body: Sami Zayn considers his association with The Bloodline in WWE will be remembered as a key highlight in his career. On the Insight Podcast , Zayn named his time in The Bloodline and run as Honorary Uce as the part of his career he believes he will be best remembered for. “Probably Bloodline stuff. I think that’s probably what I’d be best remembered for if my career ended before I won the world title or whatever; it might still be what I’m most remembered for 20 years from now if people remember anything about me 20 years from now. But I was also just very proud of it. But I’ve had so many things throughout my career. I’m just giving you the answer of what I think would be best remembered, but also simultaneously something I’m extremely proud of, but there’s a ton of stuff in my career I’m extremely proud of.” He also discussed the trajectory from his feud with Johnny Knoxville and their WrestleMania match to working with Roman Reigns and The Usos . He admitted it was impossible to know how things might have unfolded differently, noting that his career had been shaped by a series of unpredictable events and circumstances beyond his control. “No idea. I can’t even fathom it. I don’t know, because it just is. So I can’t play what-ifs or hypotheticals. I don’t even know how to answer that because everything is such a domino effect in this company and in life, but in this company, it’s almost impossible to say what would have happened if X or if Y, these variables.” “The biggest break I ever had in my career, minus Bloodline and WWE stuff, what got me booked in the United States to begin with had nothing to do with me. It was because another wrestler from Canada called Sexy Eddie went to the States, and I won’t get into the gory details here, but there are gory details because he got cut open and there was a bunch of blood and he was just an insane showman and he captured people’s imaginations in this one night where all of a sudden these people were like who are these Canadian guys? Because of that I got booked. So the biggest break in my career had nothing to do with me. It was because Sexy Eddie got cut open and had blood spewing out of his arm but still decided to put on a show. If he doesn’t put on that show, I don’t know how my career would have gone. Maybe I’d still be here. Maybe I’d still be in this chair. Maybe I’d be WWE Champion. Maybe I wouldn’t. I have no idea. title: Max Caster Leaves Door Open for AEW Return
raw_title: Max Caster on possible AEW return after TNA firing: ‘Never say never’
body: Link AEW Max Caster has made it clear that he’s not currently accepting any new wrestling bookings following his highly-publicized exit from TNA, but he recently did not rule out returning to AEW. Earlier this month, Caster made his TNA debut for the promotion’s Bound for Glory PPV (Oct. 11). As he walked to the ring, Caster performed one of his trademark freestyle raps and immediately ignited controversy. The former AEW tag champ referenced recent attacks on Saudi Arabia in one of his bars. He rapped : “This the firing squad, I drop bombs, you don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” By the end of the following day, TNA announced it was parting ways with Caster. He soon issued a public apology and then made a surprised appearance at Awesome Championship Wrestling’s Mischief Night II in Poughkeepsie, New York, on October 17. Caster also got on the mic and told the fans in attendance that night that he was taking a prolonged break from wrestling . “I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be. But I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time,” he said. “So I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right, so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home just like you guys made me feel here tonight. So finally, for the last time in a long time, you are looking at the best pro wrestler alive.” While a return to TNA seems unlikely at the moment, Caster indicated during a virtual signing with K&S WrestleFest on Monday (Oct. 26) that he would be open to another run in AEW. “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never,” Caster replied. “However, I am saying no to wrestling bookings right now, and that would be a wrestling booking so, I don’t know.” Regarding his appearance for K&S WrestleFest , he said: “I agreed to do the virtual signing a couple months ago, I think. I’m honoring this…This is my last wrestling thing for a while, so whoever’s here, I’m sure somebody is clipping this, waiting for me to say something crazy. I’m going to try not to today. But, this will be the last time you guys see me for an undefined amount of time.” The former AEW star, who held both World Tag Team Championship and World Trios Championship for the promotion, also put over his former employer. “I always got to shout out Tony Khan, because he’s supporting a lot of wrestlers living right now, including me. He soon issued a public apology and then made a surprised appearance at Awesome Championship Wrestling’s Mischief Night II in Poughkeepsie, New York, on October 17. Caster also got on the mic and told the fans in attendance that night that he was taking a prolonged break from wrestling . “I don’t know what my next move is. I don’t know where I’ll be. But I will be stepping away from the ring for an extended period of time,” he said. “So I’m gonna go home, I’m gonna go to therapy, I’m gonna get it right, so that the next time I’m in the ring it feels like I’m at home just like you guys made me feel here tonight.
