title: Susan St. James Dies at 80
raw_title: Susan St. James, wife of Dick Ebersol, passes away at 80
summary_src: Actress Susan St. James, who appeared as a guest at the second WrestleMania, died on Monday at the age of eighty.
body: Actress Susan St. James, who appeared as a guest at the second WrestleMania, died on Monday at the age of eighty. St. James, who was the wife of Dick Ebersol, had been battling pancreatic cancer, with a rep for St. James confirming her passing to PEOPLE . She was born Susan Jane Miller but changed her name when pursuing a career in Hollywood. She has many film and television credits on her resume, including her role as Sally McMillan in ‘McMillan & Wife,’ where she received a pair of Emmy nominations. In 1984, she took on the role of Kate McArdle and co-starred with Jane Curtin in ‘Kate & Allie, ’ which aired on CBS for six seasons. In October 1981, she hosted an edition of Saturday Night Live with The Kinks as the musical guest. It was a noteworthy episode because it featured Eddie Murphy’s first sketch as Buckwheat. It was from this episode that she met producer Dick Ebersol, and the pair were married six weeks later. Ebersol and Vince McMahon became business partners in 1985 off the success of WrestleMania and the WWF’s ventures on MTV. The pair produced the first episode of Saturday Night’s Main Event in May that year, which led to a six-year run on NBC before moving to Fox. It returned to NBC in 2006 and is now in its latest incarnation as a Peacock exclusive. The relationship opened the door for St. James to be among the long list of celebrities involved with WrestleMania 2 in April 1986. St. James was utilized as a broadcaster alongside Vince McMahon for the New York portion of the event. McMahon and Ebersol’s working relationship rekindled in 2000 when the XFL was launched, and NBC was seeking an alternative after losing the NFL. NBC became a partner in the league, which famously launched to a gigantic first weekend of viewership but plummeted in the ensuing weeks. The league was dissolved after one season with heavy losses for both sides. Ebersol and St. James suffered the ultimate tragedy in 2004 with the death of their 14-year-old son, Teddy. Ebersol was on a charter jet with his sons, Teddy and Charlie, which crashed in Colorado. Dick and Charlie survived, but the pilot and Teddy did not. Ebersol, 57, had been in Los Angeles over the Thanksgiving weekend and attended the USC-Notre Dame football game Saturday. Charles is a senior at the University of Notre Dame; a third Ebersol son, 18-year-old Willie, is a USC freshman. Ebersol’s wife, actress Susan Saint James, flew with the family to Colorado on Sunday; they own a home in Telluride, about 40 miles south of the Montrose airport. After dropping her off, Ebersol and their two sons boarded a jet for South Bend, Ind., to return Charles to Notre Dame before heading home to Litchfield, Conn. Since the accident, Ebersol’s wife has been staying at St. Mary’s Hospital and has requested privacy for her family. St. James is survived by Ebersol, four children, and seven grandchildren.
summary: Actress Susan St. James, wife of Dick Ebersol, passed away on Monday at age 80 after battling pancreatic cancer. St. James appeared as a guest at the second WrestleMania and had a long career in television with starring roles in McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie. She met Ebersol after hosting a 1981 episode of Saturday Night Live, and the couple later connected with Vince McMahon to produce the first WrestleMania.

While the Hardy's would later become one of the most iconic tag teams in pro wrestling history, during the majority of the 90s the pair would be largely used as…
body: Matt Hardy recalls how he used to sew he and Jeff Hardy’s ring gear during their time with WWE in the 90s as enhancement talent. While the Hardy’s would later become one of the most iconic tag teams in pro wrestling history, during the majority of the 90s the pair would be largely used as enhancement talent in the company to build up other teams in the ring. Despite their status within the company however, the pair would still need gear, and this is where Matt would step in. While speaking to The Stunner in a new interview, going through Matt Hardy’s Wikipedia page, the elder Hardy brother would share how he sewed the tights that the pair would wear during the 90s on WWE TV. “I did. Yes. I sewed all of the tights we wore. All of the tights that you saw us wear on WWE TV in the 90s, I sewed all of those as well. So we didn’t have a ton of money, and tights were so expensive back then. So our mom had dad when we were younger. I dusted off our old sewing machine and taught myself how to sew, and then I started making our tights.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Matt Hardy taught himself to sew and created all the tights he and Jeff Hardy wore on WWE television throughout the 1990s while working as enhancement talent. The elder Hardy brother explained that the family lacked funds for expensive professional gear, so he revived an old sewing machine from their mother to make the outfits. He shared the details in a new interview while reviewing his Wikipedia page.

title: Raw Fallout Features Stratton Cash-In Tease and Zayn Retention
raw_title: A Tiffany Stratton Swerve Loading, Champion Sami Zayn is Thriving, More WWE Raw Fallout
body: Liv Morgan learned she would defend the Women's World Championship against Becky Lynch and needed The Judgment Day to save her from The Man and a Tiffany Stratton cash-in attempt. Sami Zayn made a surprise appearance and retained the Undisputed WWE Championship against Je'Von Evans thanks to Bron Breakker, with Penta looming as a potential cash-in threat. These events and more highlighted a show with major fallout on the road to Crown Jewel. Since winning the Money in the Bank briefcases, both Penta and Tiffany Stratton have teased cash-ins multiple times. Raw was especially egregious with both looking ready to cash in on the same night. These failed fake-outs do nothing but make the Money in the Bank holders look bad. This has been especially true for Stratton. On SmackDown and Raw, WWE contrived situations where Liv Morgan only remained champion because Tiffy forgot what she was doing until The Judgment Day pulled the champion to safety. Fake-outs like this hurt Austin Theory's credibility after his MITB win in 2022, and his eventual failed cash-in only compounded the problem. Penta should not be cashing in any time soon, so fake-outs only make it look like he is failing in his plans repeatedly. At least Stratton does look like she will be successfully cashing in soon, but WWE needs to write situations that are better timed to make everyone look competent. The most forgettable outcome would be for Tiffy to finally catch Liv and walk away with the gold, but that is not the most likely scenario. Instead, the teases have set the stage for a swerve: Stratton cashing in on Chelsea Green. It would be especially heartbreaking if Green managed to beat Morgan for the Women's Crown Jewel Championship, only to immediately lose her world title. This makes more sense for everyone involved and lets Tiffy lean into a more natural heel role by turning on her own friend. His opening promo and match against Je'Von Evans delivered, adding necessary weight to a show that was otherwise understaffed. As a test of how far Zayn can go, this segment was a rousing success that made clear the fresh heel can carry the gold for a while. The best outcome would be for The Last Real Good Guy's antics to keep him strong until WrestleMania 43 where someone can step up to finally humble him. In the meantime, there is no reason to hot-shot the title anymore. Cody Rhodes and CM Punk have had their time at the top, and there is plenty of time to sell Kevin Owens chasing Zayn before he wins big. summary_src: WWE NXT Women's Champion Kelani Jordan has discussed what she found easy and one aspect of pro wrestling she initially struggled with.
body: WWE WWE NXT Women's Champion Kelani Jordan has detailed what she found tough to get to grips with in her early years in WWE. Jordan, like many on the "WWE NXT" roster, transitioned from another sport to pro wrestling, having previously been a gymnast . She transferred many of her gymnastics skills to pro wrestling and found high-flying moves easy to perform, but struggled to make her wrestling look realistic as gymnastics had taught her to be perfect. "So some things were a struggle, like some things were easy, as in a sense of, like, body control, air awareness, like those things. High-flying came very natural, and I wasn't really, like, afraid of anything. But the struggle was, like you said, not being perfect, 'cause like gymnastics, you're judged on a scale of perfection. So if something was rough around the edges, for me that was way more difficult," she explained on " Wrastlin' with E & Matt ." Jordan also highlighted other differences between wrestling and gymnastics, pointing out how wrestling requires you to work with another person. She also noted that wrestlers must react to their surroundings, unlike in gymnastics, where she was taught to block out external distractions. "But also, gymnastics isn't a contact sport. I don't have to depend on anyone else. I don't have to touch anyone else, so that was a big difference. But also, even when it comes to, like, speaking in promos, in gymnastics you're taught to tune everyone out, whereas in wrestling, you have to listen to the fans and just, like — you're still in the moment, but it's like you have to be aware of what's being said." Jordan's transition from gymnastics to pro wrestling has paid off, as she captured the NXT Women's Championship just three years into her wrestling career. She has also held the NXT Women's North American Championship and the TNA Knockouts Championship, making her one of the rising stars in WWE.

She said high-flying moves came naturally due to her body control and air awareness but struggled with making wrestling look realistic because gymnastics emphasized perfection. Jordan also noted that wrestling requires working with a partner and reacting in the moment unlike her previous sport.

title: Comeback Watch: John Cena Returning To WWE Raw Next Week—What Will He Announce?
raw_title: John Cena Returning To WWE Raw Next Week—What Will He Announce?
body: The company revealed on this week's episode of Monday Night Raw that the 17-time world champion will appear on next week's episode of Raw on Netflix, which is the "go-home" show to the Crown Jewel PLE. Following the announcement of Cena's return, the legendary star took to X, formerly Twitter, to tease that he would be making yet another blockbuster announcement on Raw from the Barclays Center in Brooklyn: After retiring in December 2025, Cena last appeared on WWE programming at Backlash in May, where he made a surprise appearance to announce the creation of "The John Cena Classic." At the time, Cena revealed a few details regarding plans for the event, including: A format pitting rising NXT stars against established main roster performers Fan voting to determine the champion, so that, in a unique twist, a WWE superstar could lose his or her match and still win the John Cena Classic Cena himself has repeatedly admitted that he isn't sure how the John Cena Classic will work or if it will work at all. Back in September, he told WrestleRant (h/t Ringside News ), "Even with the John Cena Classic, I'm still swinging big. Like, I'm in the clubhouse, dude. I'm retired. I made it. But I want to put my name on an event that hopefully is a way to to bring people together and and I'm really excited about it and it also might fail." Although WWE has revealed remarkably few details about the event, a brainchild of Cena himself, there has long been speculation that it will function somewhat similarly to Cena's retirement show. Last December on Saturday Night's Main Event , Cena lost to Gunther in his final match and also used that stage to highlight young up-and-coming talents, including Je'Von Evans, TNA's Leon Slater, Oba Femi and Sol Ruca. Those stars all benefitted from their presence on that show. Slater is now TNA's World Champion while Evans just challenged for the WWE Championship on this week's Raw. Meanwhile, Ruca would go on to win the Women's Intercontinental Championship, and Femi is already one of the top stars in WWE, with an expected WrestleMania 43 main event possibly on the horizon. The John Cena Classic had previously been confirmed to take place at some point in December. At one point, WWE was targeting Dec. 12 for the event, but WrestlePalooza will take place on that day instead. The likeliest date for the JCC remains Dec. 19, even though that would put it head-to-head with both AAA and AEW's Worlds End pay-per-view. With the announcement of Cena's return on next week's Raw, which will be a double taping alongside SmackDown, the expectation is that Cena will reveal the official date and venue for the John Cena Classic as well as perhaps some of the scheduled performers and matches. That taping also featuring CM Punk vs. Kevin Owens, so WWE is clearly hoping that the addition of Cena's major announcement will result in more buzz and excitement and strong viewership for Raw on Netflix.
summary: On this week's episode of Monday Night Raw that the 17-time world champion will appear on next week's episode of Raw on Netflix. With the announcement of Cena's return on next week's Raw, which will be a double taping alongside SmackDown.

title: 12 Cursed Comparisons That DOOMED Promising Wrestlers
raw_title: 12 Cursed Comparisons That DOOMED Promising Wrestlers
body: At first, comparing one wrestler to another who earned fanfare from audiences years before isn't the worst thing. In fact, it can be rather complimentary and often a sure sign that people (including those backstage making key decisions for massive companies like WWE ) see a bright future for someone. All too often, there's a bitter dose of realism lurking just beneath such observations though; and it's waiting like Edge/Adam Copeland in the corner to deliver a spear . In reality, referring to a promising wrestler as 'the next coming of...' can actually prove to be a creative noose that stifles their development rather than aiding it. Can those afflicted with this curse come out on the other end with a smile? Of course they can, but not without spreading their wings and seeking ways to break free from pesky comparisons following them around like an unwanted shadow. Rather ironically, it's them who need to get out of someone else's shadow! Various hopefuls on this list have been likened to heroes of yesteryear like The Undertaker, Goldberg, John Cena, Brock Lesnar, Eddie Guerrero and even The Ultimate Warrior . Unfortunately, despite the best of intentions from those gushing with praise, that didn't do the stars-to-be any long term favours. Suddenly, and without warning, those they reminded fans/critics/management of became a cruel measuring stick nobody involved even asked for. 'Aw, it turns out they're not as good as this iconic wrestler I decided they're like after all'. Linda Miles was co-winner of the second Tough Enough season alongside Jackie Gayda. Looking back, neither woman was really ready for top tier WWE TV, but things were doubly unfair on Linda because she was immediately compared to Chyna because of her super strong physique. Company announcers even mentioned that on-air from time to time. Linda's ascent and reimagining as dominatrix Shaniqua also fell just a few short years after Joanie Laurer left WWE, so management wanted to position her as an improvement. She wasn't just 'the next Chyna', Shaniqua was better than. Except she wasn't - it wasn't even close. Nobody's gonna claim that Chyna was Chad Gable between the ropes, but she had more to offer than WWE fancied pretending she did in 2003-2004. Being brutally honest, the pressure of living up to her body proved to be too much for Miles. The 'too much, too soon' bug walloped Linda as well. Reportedly, her ego got far too big and rubbed a few folks the wrong way backstage. Those in charge had quickly created a monster by acting like this genuine rookie was better than an iconic 'Attitude Era' favourite . Shaniqua wasn't long for the biz. She wrestled her last match on the independent scene after leaving WWE behind in '04, then went on to give wrestling the middle finger. Looking back, higher-ups definitely got ahead of themselves by claiming she was Chyna 2.0. Lifelong wrestling, video game, music and sports obsessive who has been writing about his passions since childhood. Jamie
summary: Per WhatCulture.com: comparing one wrestler to another who earned fanfare from audiences years before isn't the worst thing. It can be rather complimentary and often a sure sign that people see a bright future for someone.

body: News WWE AEW ROH NJPW INDIE Editorial Results Events Profiles News AEW Max Caster Says 'Never Say Never' To AEW Return After TNA Firing AEW Max Caster Says ‘Never Say Never’ To AEW Return After TNA Firing by Thomas Lowson October 27, 2026 0 0 views ReddIt Facebook Twitter Email Copy URL TRENDING (*UPDATED*) Late-Breaking WWE RAW **SPOILERS** (10/26/26) – Everything Going Down! 0 Max Caster in AEW. (Image credit: AEW) Could Max Caster return to All Elite Wrestling, despite leaving the promotion earlier this year? Fans shouldn’t count the idea out just yet. Appearing at a virtual signing with K&S WrestleFest on Monday, October 26, Caster was asked about a second run with AEW. He said, “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never. However, I am saying no to wrestling bookings right now, and that would be a wrestling booking so, I don’t know.” Explaining his appearance for the virtual signing, Caster said it was booked months earlier, and despite his current stance on bookings, he wished to honor it. Later in the signing, Caster discussed his time with AEW and shared his appreciation for AEW President Tony Khan for helping him and others. He said, “I always got to shout out Tony Khan, because he’s supporting a lot of wrestlers living right now, including me. I’m still living off AEW money. That’s a guy who, for whatever reason in his heart, is supporting wrestling and supporting wrestlers.” Caster’s exit from AEW was confirmed in October 2026 and he swiftly debuted for TNA Wrestling, appearing at their Bound for Glory event. During the show, Caster made a remark during one of his raps that would result in him being fired from the promotion shortly after. He said, “This the firing squad, I drop bombs, you don’t even have to fly to Riyadh.” eWrestlingNews was founded in 1999 and has been covering wrestling news 24/7 ever since. With a strong team of writers, editorialists, and social managers, we strive to provide to you the most up-to-date wrestling news and information around the web.

title: WWE Proceeds With Crown Jewel In Saudi Arabia
raw_title: Latest Backstage News On WWE Traveling To Saudi Arabia For Crown Jewel & WrestleMania
summary_src: WWE is still planning to hold Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia, with a report shedding light on the situation on the ground in the country.
body: WWE A new update has provided details on the status of Crown Jewel and whether WWE will hold the event in Saudi Arabia. It seems there has been no change to WWE's plans to hold the upcoming Crown Jewel in the Middle Eastern country, with the set continuing to be built for the show on November 7. " Fightful Select " has reported that its sources have confirmed work is continuing at the Crown Jewel venue. According to these sources, the situation on the ground in Saudi Arabia is not as severe as media reports suggest. The outlet also cited a report by journalist Ariel Helwani, who claimed that a Power Slap show, which is to be held a day before Crown Jewel, will also go ahead. The crew for the event will reportedly fly into Bahrain and take a five-hour bus drive over the border to Saudi Arabia. "Fightul" also provided an update on WrestleMania 43, which will be held in Saudi Arabia in April 2027, although the exact date has yet to be finalized. The report revealed that the date was originally set to be announced during the week of Crown Jewel, though it remains unclear whether WWE will proceed with that plan. WWE is going ahead with the show in Saudi Arabia despite recent reports highlighting the alarming situation in the region, including a government report warning that Iran is planning to target Americans in the region. TKO is standing firm on its decision to have WWE host Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia, as well as a UFC event later in December. The promotion has confirmed several matches for the November 7 show, including champion-versus-champion bouts between Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn, and Liv Morgan and Chelsea Green. The heated rivalry between Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes will also continue at the show, while The Vision will defend the World Tag Team Championship against Je'Von Evans and Penta in a tag team match confirmed this week on "WWE Raw."
summary: Per Fightful Select, construction continues at the Crown Jewel venue in Saudi Arabia for the November 7 event with no change to plans. Sources indicate the situation on the ground is not as bad as media reports have suggested, and the Power Slap show scheduled the day before will also proceed with crew flying into Bahrain before a five-hour bus trip over the border. Fightful Select added that WrestleMania 43 is still set for Saudi Arabia in April 2027 though the exact date has not been finalized and was originally slated to be revealed during Crown Jewel week.

title: Matt Hardy Recalls WWE Removing Hardys From TV
raw_title: Matt Hardy Recalls The Hardys Being Taken Off WWE Television Due To Jeff Rejecting Pitches Due To 'Being Uncomfortable'
summary_src: Matt Hardy reflects on the first time WWE would attempt to split he and Jeff Hardy up as a tag team, noting Jeff being uncomfortable. Over the years, the Hardy brothers have squared off on a number of occasions and feuded, and always have found their way back to each other as a tag team…
body: Matt Hardy reflects on the first time WWE would attempt to split he and Jeff Hardy up as a tag team, noting Jeff being uncomfortable. Over the years, the Hardy brothers have squared off on a number of occasions and feuded, and always have found their way back to each other as a tag team in pro wrestling. In a new interview with The Stunner where he would fact check his Wikipedia page, Matt Hardy spoke about the first attempt WWE made to split up the brotherly tag team, noting that Jeff was uncomfortable with some pitches, leading to both brothers being taken of WWE TV. “There was a storyline for our characters and they wanted us to split up and there was a couple things that we were asked to do and Jeff was uncomfortable and didn’t want to do it so we were off TV for a while as a punishment, I guess. But we still did live events, and then they put us back together because we knew we weren’t ready to separate and split up as a team yet.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Matt Hardy discussed the first time WWE tried to break up The Hardy Boyz tag team. He explained that Jeff Hardy felt uncomfortable with some proposed storyline elements, which led to both brothers being removed from television for a period. They continued working live events before WWE reunited them on TV since the team was not ready to split.

llm_long: In 1997, WWE presented Badd Blood: In Your House, which featured a mostly forgettable undercard but became iconic due to its main event. Kane made his monstrous debut by interfering during the bout.

Matt Hardy was 23 years old at the time and had not yet established his WWE career. He watched the event and recalled the moment the cell was lowered before the match. Hardy described the experience as impressive on his "The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy" podcast.

"I'll never forget sitting back and watching that match, and that was the first time I was like, 'Whoa,'" Hardy said. He noted that Shawn Michaels performed on another level in the match despite already being known as great. Hardy called Michaels' performance a standout that was incredible to watch.

Hardy also praised The Undertaker's work in the match. He observed that the Deadman did not simply overpower Michaels as he had done with many previous opponents. The bout stood out to Hardy for this balanced approach.

Before the match, Hardy saw Kane backstage without his mask. He and his brother Jeff had prior history with Glenn Jacobs from working together in Smoky Mountain Wrestling. Hardy remembered Jacobs performing as Unabomber during that time.

Hardy found it strange to witness Jacobs receiving the new character as The Undertaker's brother. He recalled being around Jacobs earlier when he portrayed Isaac Yankem. This backstage glimpse added to the memorable night for Hardy.

title: Jake Hager's Family Gives Health Update After Eye Injury
raw_title: Ex-WWE Star Jake Hager’s Family Shares Health Update After Gruesome Eye Injury
body: For those unfamiliar, Power Slap is UFC CEO's Dana White 's slap-fighting league where competitors take turns hitting each other with full-force, open-handed slaps to the face while the defender stands completely still with their hands behind their back. While he underwent emergency surgery after the event—where a brutal strike from opponent Johnny Magna caused his eye to bleed and led to a controversial referee stoppage—it was reported that the former world champion may require extra surgeries in the future. The incident occurred during the second round of his match when Magna landed a devastating blow to Hager's left eye. Despite protests from Hager's corner claiming a foul, officials awarded Magna the victory via TKO, prompting shocked reactions from fans and executives alike, with White calling it one of the worst injuries he had ever seen in combat sports. After the event, official updates on Hager's condition have been shared primarily through family statements rather than his personal social media accounts, which have remained quiet as he recovers out of the spotlight. His partner, Patricia Blackburn, previously confirmed that he underwent initial emergency procedures. "Jake is currently recovering from an emergency eye surgery," Blackburn shared in a statement to Slap News and on her official Instagram account. "We're taking things one day at a time and keeping the details private, but your kindness, support, and genuine concern have meant more than you know." Other reports revealed that as the blood cleared during subsequent check-ups, doctors discovered a detached retina, which required an urgent secondary surgery that went better than expected. Across social media, fans and those in the wrestling community have expressed their support for Hager. Power Slap competitor Jonathan Correa wrote underneath Blackburn's statement, "Watching it took off my hat and I took a knee for a prayer on my living room." Retired UFC fighter Alan Jouban wrote: "Hope all the best." One user wrote, "This is the part of the sport we never want to have happen, hope you heal up quickly brother," while another commented, "Prayers to my power slap parents." Hager, who performed as Jack Swagger during his WWE tenure and later competed in AEW, retired from traditional pro wrestling in 2025 to operate a Florida-based trucking company, before making brief independent appearances earlier this year.
summary: Former WWE performer Jake Hager suffered a severe eye injury during a Power Slap event when opponent Johnny Magna landed a hard slap in the second round. Hager required emergency surgery after the controversial TKO stoppage, with Dana White describing it as one of the worst combat sports injuries he has seen. His family has provided the public updates on his condition while he recovers away from social media.

title: Injury Update: Denim Obsession, McRib Disasters & Wrestling’s Wildest Injuries — AEW’s Orange Cassidy
raw_title: AEW’s Orange Cassidy: Denim Obsession, McRib Disasters & Wrestling’s Wildest Injuries
body: What happens when the most laid-back wrestler in AEW meets a radio show full of grown men who believe jeans are survival equipment? Apparently, a beautiful friendship is born. And somebody might be getting a custom denim duster. AEW superstar Orange Cassidy joins Rizz, Moon Valjean, Lern, and Rafe Williams in the studio for another funny podcast packed with professional wrestling stories, questionable fashion advice, fast-food disasters, and injuries that will make you appreciate your boring office job. First up, the crew tackles one of the most controversial returns in fast-food history: the McRib is back! Orange Cassidy admits there’s something strangely exciting about a sandwich that disappears and reappears whenever McDonald’s feels like messing with everybody. Rizz thinks it’s gross, Rafe loves it, and Lern introduces everyone to the horrifying sight of an unsauced McRib. Apparently, barbecue sauce isn’t just a condiment. It’s a disguise. Orange takes one look at the gray, suspiciously rib-shaped creation and immediately questions whether he wants it anywhere near his body. A perfectly reasonable response from a man who regularly gets thrown around a wrestling ring. Then the conversation turns to Orange Cassidy’s true passion: denim. Jeans in the wrestling ring? Absolutely. Jeans on airplanes? Obviously. Jeans for practically every occasion? Why would anyone wear anything else? Orange explains why he prefers wrestling in denim, how modern stretchy jeans have changed the game, and why he considers the fabric a protective layer between himself and the rest of humanity. That’s when Rafe Williams reveals his theory about airplane survival : if a plane crashes and the survivors need to elect a leader, nobody’s choosing the guy wearing sweatpants and Crocs. They’re choosing the man in jeans and work boots. Orange Cassidy agrees so enthusiastically that Rafe may have finally found his soulmate. Rafe tells the tragic story of his teenage attempt to reinvent himself with a full-length, acid-wash denim duster. What was supposed to be a legendary fashion statement became a school-day disaster when an upperclassman tore the coat apart almost immediately. Orange is genuinely impressed. The two start discussing matching denim dusters, water skiing in jeans, and the possibility of Lern’s mom making custom outfits. Somewhere, Levi’s marketing department is wondering why nobody invited them. The crew also gets into Orange Cassidy’s famously relaxed wrestling persona . While other wrestlers scream, flex, and cover themselves in body oil, Orange prefers to keep things simple, move at his own pace, and occasionally wrestle with his hands in his pockets. He even reveals a backstage wrestling secret: some performers use conditioner to keep their hair looking wet during matches. body: AEW star Speedball Mike Bailey released a new vlog this week , addressing where they were when Will Ospreay got surrounded and attacked by The Don Callis Family last week on AEW Dynamite. Speedball explained that they were busy getting ready for their match against the debuting Ilja Dragunov. Below are some highlights: “Did workout number one this morning after this coffee is going to be workout number two. And uh I have been thinking a lot about Wednesday. Good match, you know, good times. I got exactly what I wanted, which is yet another one of the world’s best wrestlers. Finally, where the best wrestle. Shout out to Ilia. He ****ing brought it. He’s going to do amazing, and I’m very excited to see where this goes in the next couple months, and as for myself, I am where I usually am. You know, I feel like great performances aren’t lost on the AEW audience. summary_src: On his podcast, TNA's Matt Hardy revealed that his brother, Jeff may be taking some time off in the near future to deal with an ongoing health issue.
body: TNA As TNA prepares to go on their annual Canadian tour in November, Jeff Hardy is preparing to take time off. It's customary for Hardy to be written out whenever TNA travels internationally due to his past legal issues. However, he is also dealing with legitimate health issues. On an episode of The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy , Matt detailed some health issues his brother is dealing with. He was joking about what his next character would be if Jeff took a little time off. The Hardys booked the October 15 episode of iMPACT to celebrate 35 years in the professional wrestling business. He joked that Booker Matt could be his next character. "Its going to be interesting to see what my next character is going to be, especially if Jeff takes a little time off to try and work on his neck a little bit. That may be happening, I guess we'll see." Matt continued, "That nagging, it's been a year now since he's had this bulging disc. It's been bugging him and he's going to, you know I think he's done everything he can in his power and he's going to take some time off and see what he can do to get it fixed up and correct it as much as possible." Prior to TNA heading north, The Hardys will take part in the Chris Jericho Rock 'N' Rager at Sea November 7-11. For the first time ever, "AEW Collision" will be live from the Jericho Cruise . TNA Destination X is scheduled for November 15 in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada.

body: Matt Hardy recalls the degree of which he would have had creative control over the ‘Broken’ character if he had stayed with TNA. In May of 2016, Matt would debut the ‘Broken’ Matt Hardy character, which was born out of a career resurgence for the largely tag team wrestler. The character would flourish, with Hardy bringing the character with him to both WWE and AEW in the future. While speaking to The Stunner in an interview where he would fact check his Wikipedia page, Matt Hardy spoke about the level of creative control he had over the ‘Broken’ Matt Hardy character in TNA. “That’s not fully correct. I did. I worked with Jeremy Borash, who was like our guy. And while I was at home, I definitely had very much input. But, you know, they would say, like, we’re hoping to go in this direction, and if we would have stayed in TNA instead of returning to WWE, and that’s just because Jeff Jarrett, he came in, and he was kind of going through a darker point in his life, and we had a little bit of a falling out, and they were talking about changing the money that we’d already agreed to. We went back there. If I would have stayed, though, I would have probably had almost complete creative control. I’d been very close to it.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

Hardy cited a falling out with Jeff Jarrett over a proposed change to their previously agreed compensation as the reason they ultimately left.

raw_title: Max Caster On A Possible AEW Return After TNA Exit: ‘You Never Say Never’
body: Max Caster says "you never say never" about returning to AEW, but that he is turning down wrestling bookings for now. He also thanked Tony Khan: "I'm still living off AEW money." Copy link Get more Wrestling News in Google Choose us as a and our stories show up more in your Google results. Max Caster says he won’t rule out a return to AEW, but that he is not taking any wrestling bookings right now. Caster was asked about going back to AEW during a virtual signing with K&S WrestleFest on Monday. “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never,” Caster said. “However, I am saying no to wrestling bookings right now, and that would be a wrestling booking so, I don’t know.” Caster said the signing would be his last wrestling appearance for a while. “I agreed to do the virtual signing a couple months ago, I think. I’m honoring this… This is my last wrestling thing for a while, so whoever’s here, I’m sure somebody is clipping this, waiting for me to say something crazy. I’m going to try not to today,” he said. “But, this will be the last time you guys see me for an undefined amount of time.” “I always got to shout out Tony Khan, because he’s supporting a lot of wrestlers living right now, including me. I’m still living off AEW money,” Caster said. “That’s a guy who, for whatever reason in his heart, is supporting wrestling and supporting wrestlers.” Caster’s AEW contract expired on October 1 , and he made his TNA debut against Moose at Bound for Glory on October 11 in Tampa. During his entrance, he rapped, “I drop bombs. You don’t even have to fly to Riyadh,” a day after a deadly missile attack on the city’s main airport. TNA said the next day that “making light of violent attacks is wrong” and that Caster “will no longer be wrestling for TNA.” Caster later apologized to TNA president Carlos Silva and the company’s office, saying he “went too far.” On October 17, Caster told the crowd at Awesome Championship Wrestling’s Mischief Night II in Poughkeepsie, New York, that he was stepping away from the ring for an extended period and going to therapy. Caster is a two-time AEW World Tag Team Champion with Anthony Bowens as The Acclaimed, and a former AEW World Trios Champion. title: Chris Sabin Targets AEW Tag Titles With MCMG
raw_title: Chris Sabin Discusses His Goals Following AEW Signing
summary_src: Motor City Machine Guns' Chris Sabin has outlined what he and Alex Shelley want to achieve in AEW and revealed the one team he wants to wrestle the most.
body: AEW Motor City Machine Guns' Chris Sabin has outlined the team's primary goal in AEW. Sabin and Alex Shelley returned to AEW in July 2026 , four years after their last appearance in the promotion. Sabin recently spoke to " MuscleManMalcolm " and revealed that their goal is to win the tag team titles, which would make them the first team to capture tag team gold in four major promotions — WWE, AEW, TNA, and NJPW. "For sure, absolutely. That's 100% the goal [winning the tag team titles in AEW]. And you know, if we do win that championship, we'll be the first team to win titles in AEW, New Japan Pro Wrestling, TNA, and WWE. That's a pretty cool accomplishment," he said. Sabin spoke about the moment in All In, where the best of the best tag teams in AEW came face-to-face, which included them, The Young Bucks, FTR, and Christian Cage and Adam Copeland. He pointed out Motor City Machine Guns' history with The Young Bucks, having wrestled them in many promotions over the years, stating that they are the foremost on the list of teams he wants to wrestle. "If anyone knows the history of the Motor City Machine Guns, we're tied with the Young Bucks. We've wrestled them so many times [in] TNA, independent, PWG, everywhere," he added. "We [MCMG and Young Bucks] just had the best chemistry, and we just want to reignite that feud again. We want to make sure we still have that chemistry. We think we will and you know we that that's who we want to wrestle the most in AEW is the Young Bucks." One of the teams Sabin said he would like to face, FTR, are currently competing against the Motor City Machine Guns in a best-of-five series, which is tied at 1-1 . Perhaps a win in this series could lead them to challenge The Young Bucks for the AEW World Tag Team Championship, bringing their journey and rivalry with the duo full circle.

title: Kelani Jordan Calls Raw Debut An Awesome Experience
raw_title: Kelani Jordan Says It Was An 'Awesome Experience' To Make WWE Raw In-Ring Debut
summary_src: It was a highlight moment for Kelani. Coming up on October 31st is the 2026 NXT Halloween Havoc Premium Live Event. On the marquee for the show is Kelani Jordan defending the NXT Women's Championship against Wren Sinclair.
body: Coming up on October 31st is the 2026 NXT Halloween Havoc Premium Live Event. On the marquee for the show is Kelani Jordan defending the NXT Women’s Championship against Wren Sinclair. Going into the match, Jordan chatted with Justin Dhillon of The Wrestling Classic , and she was asked about making her Monday Night Raw in-ring debut in September. Jordan was in a Money in the Bank qualifier with Raquel Rodriguez and Lola Vice. “It was so cool. It’s just crazy to see the difference. One, you’re performing in front of however many — I don’t even know the number there. So, I mean, we did have a Stand & Deliver with that many people there, but it’s just so cool to be in the ring with Raquel (Rodriguez) too, who I never really got to work a one-on-one or even in a multi-person match and then to be there for Lola’s debut because we have a lot of history, a lot of story. So, I don’t know,” Jordan smiled. “It was just an awesome experience to be able to be on a big stage, something that you worked for your whole career so being on Raw and being on Netflix, it was a super big turning point in my career, and I think also, it just allowed people to get more eyes on me. I didn’t give ‘em too much of Kelani Jordan but I gave them just enough to hopefully that they kept wanting to see what more I could do.” Several days after Jordan’s debut, Fightful Select reported that she is planned for a main roster run after she finishes up as NXT Women’s Champion. Jordan stated that when the time is right, she’d love to show what she can do regularly on one of the main roster brands. “Of course when the time is right, be able to get on the big show, whether it’s Raw or SmackDown, whatever it is. I wanna be able to show what I can do on a different brand. But right now, my focus is just to have an iconic NXT Women’s Championship reign and a legacy here in NXT.” The Halloween Havoc go-home episode of NXT is airing on 10/27. title: Gargano Links Son's Reactions to His SmackDown Planking Story
raw_title: Johnny Gargano explains why he spent months planking on WWE SmackDown
summary_src: Johnny Gargano has explained how his son’s reaction to seeing him lose in WWE may have impacted his character’s decision to spend months planking backstage. Gargano was seen simply lying down backstage on WWE programming for much of 2026.
body: Johnny Gargano has explained how his son’s reaction to seeing him lose in WWE may have impacted his character’s decision to spend months planking backstage. Gargano was seen simply lying down backstage on WWE programming for much of 2026. He wouldn’t stop until CM Punk offered him a WWE Championship match on the September 4 SmackDown in his hometown of Cleveland. During a recent episode of his vlog , Gargano explained how his son Quill impacted his character’s story: “Quill watches the show. He watches SmackDown, and he loves video games. And in his head, when you win or you get a championship like those (motioning to belts displayed on his wall), you get the treasure. It’s a treasure to him. “ And I don’t know how many times over the past year, we would fly out on Thursday, and before I would leave, Quill would ask me, like, ‘Dad, are you gonna win? You gonna get the treasure?’ And I would tell him, ‘I try, man. I’m really, really going to try.’ “And then I would have a match on SmackDown, and I’d lose, and I’d come back through the curtain, and Candice would have the phone in her hand. She’d be on FaceTime, and she’d show me Quill just crying, bawling his eyes out, saying, ‘Daddy lost. Daddy’s not going to get the treasure. There’s no treasure.’ “And, like, that broke me. So in my head, it was easier to just not try than to get up and fail and let people down. And I’m not saying that’s right. I’m not saying that’s the way to go about things, but that’s what I did. “ Gargano said the match against Punk for the WWE title in Cleveland “changed everything.” “I got a chance at the WWE Championship, a title I have dreamed my whole life of. And I took a leap of faith, and I stood up. And that reaction to me changed everything because it showed me that it didn’t matter. It showed me that people still believed in me.” Gargano also explained why his character is loyal to Sami Zayn. “I am loyal to the people that are loyal to me. And Sami Zayn was loyal to me, and I ride or die for the people that are loyal to me.” He concluded his vlog by saying it was time that he bring home some “treasure.” Gargano teamed with Zayn and later Ricky Saints in the main event of WWE SmackDown on Friday against Rey Fenix and Trick Williams, who would later be joined by Penta after the match was made a six-man tag. Prior to that, Gargano dropped a singles match to Trick Williams on the October 16 SmackDown. He also competed in a Money in the Bank qualifying triple threat match won by Kevin Owens, also involving Cody Rhodes, in the main event of the October 2 SmackDown. The match was rated four and a half stars by Dave Meltzer. Gargano’s full vlog is available below. The video is queued to his comments about his son’s reaction to his WWE losses. title: WWE Adds Last-Minute Match to October 27 NXT

summary_src: WWE has added another match to tonight’s NXT, and this one came together because Saquon Shugars and Sean Legacy apparently couldn’t keep things calm backstage. After getting into it in the locker room last week, they’ll now get the chance to settle things in the ring.
body: NXT General Manager Robert Stone took to Twitter and sent out the updated card for the October 27 episode and confirmed that Shugars vs. Legacy has officially been added to the show. The match comes after the two had a confrontation during the October 20 episode of NXT. Things apparently got heated enough in the locker room that WWE decided there was really only one way to deal with it — put them in a match. Now Shugars and Legacy will meet one-on-one as part of tonight’s Halloween Havoc go-home episode. It’s another addition to what was already a pretty packed NXT card. Jackson Drake will defend the NXT North American Championship against E.K. Prosper, who is getting another shot at gold after recently challenging Grayson Waller for the NXT Championship. Both Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic semifinals are happening tonight as well. NXT Tag Team Champions Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes of Vanity Project will face Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno, while Hank Walker and Tank Ledger take on Galeno and El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. Chantel Monroe will also make her official NXT singles debut against Lizzy Rain. Monroe has already competed on Evolve and LFG and appeared in NXT’s 20-woman No. 1 Contender’s Battle Royal, but tonight will be her first proper one-on-one match on NXT television. With Shugars vs. Legacy now added, WWE has five matches lined up for the October 27 show as NXT gets through its final episode before Halloween Havoc on October 31. WWE NXT airs live from the WWE Performance Center in Orlando at 8 PM ET on The CW, with international viewers able to watch through Netflix. Ringside News will have live coverage. title: Dustin Rhodes Writing Second Biography
raw_title: Dustin Rhodes working on a second book, “My hands were tied with the other company”
summary_src: Rhodes' career goes back to 1988 and has worked for every North American company, including many stints with WWF since 1990.
body: Dustin Rhodes is penning a second biography, citing restrictions in his last offering. When asked on X about the idea of writing a book, the AEW performer responded, “I am in the middle of writing my second book. This one will be way more in depth over my whole career, ups and down. Back to glory and doing it my way. My hands were tied with the other company.” In 2010, Rhodes and co-author Mark Vancil released Cross Rhodes: Goldust, Out of Darkness through Gallery Books. Rhodes’ career goes back to 1988 and has worked for every North American company, including many stints with WWF since 1990. After his firing by WCW in 1995, he was hired by the WWF and became Goldust, the character he’s been most closely connected to throughout his career. As the character, he worked with the WWE across multiple stints until 2019, when his contract expired, and he signed with AEW, where he continues to wrestle and work as a producer. Rhodes has been inactive since July 2025, when he dropped the TNT title to Kyle Fletcher and attacked after the match to send him away for double knee surgery.

Rhodes responded to a fan on X on Friday by confirming the existence of the new project, stating it will cover his whole career in much greater detail.

He described the upcoming book as addressing the ups and downs, a return to glory, and doing things his own way. Rhodes added that his hands were tied with the other company during the writing of his first book. His initial autobiography titled "Cross Rhodes: Goldust, Out of the Darkness" was released in 2010 while he was under contract with WWE, which co-published the memoir.

Rhodes joined AEW in the promotion's first year of 2019 and has remained there under a long-term contract. He won the AEW TNT Championship in his home state of Texas at All In 2025 before losing the title to Kyle Fletcher in a Chicago Street Fight last summer.

title: Backstage Buzz: Kevin Owens Allegedly Furious Backstage Over WWE Crown Jewel Saudi Arabia Situation
raw_title: Kevin Owens Allegedly Furious Backstage Over WWE Crown Jewel Saudi Arabia Situation
summary_src: Kevin Owens apparently isn’t too thrilled about WWE’s upcoming trip to Saudi Arabia. There’s been plenty of talk about people backstage being pissed over the Crown Jewel situation, and now Jonathan Coachman has actually put a name to some of that frustration.
body: Speaking on Two Count Tuesday , Coachman said he heard from one of his connections about what’s going on behind the scenes. He admitted he normally doesn’t give wrestling dirt sheets much credit, but this time he says they’ve got it right. According to Coach, he’s been given names of WWE talent who are furious backstage. The interesting part is that none of them have said anything publicly yet. “I got one of my connections yesterday, and I rarely put over the dirt sheets, but they’re correct. Because the names that have been given to me that are backstage furious over this — but we haven’t seen one talent, not one, talk about this or address this.” That’s when Kevin Owens entered the conversation. JD pointed out that WWE has booked Owens vs. CM Punk as a taped match for the Barclays Center next week. He wondered whether that match was originally supposed to happen at Crown Jewel before plans changed because Owens didn’t want to go to Saudi Arabia. “They booked Kevin Owens vs. CM Punk in a taped match for the Barclays Center next week. So I think that was gonna happen at Crown Jewel, but it’s not happening because they don’t wanna go to Saudi.” Jonathan Coachman didn’t dance around it. He said Kevin Owens was specifically one of the names he had been given, and he respects Owens for saying something backstage. “Correct. Kevin Owens was one of the names that was told to me yesterday. So I respect that he’s saying something backstage.” That gets even more interesting considering what WrestleVotes recently said about talent refusing the trip. According to that report, WWE stars can technically say they’re staying home, but they wouldn’t get paid for the show and there could potentially be some awkward consequences waiting for them afterwards. “They could say they’re not going, and they won’t get paid, and the rest of their career will be reflective of that. Not the pay, but the stigma — the position that they might find themselves no longer in. They can say, ‘I’m staying home. I’m watching it on my couch. You can figure it out,’ but things may be different when they go back to work.” And apparently this isn’t just one or two people quietly complaining. WrestleVotes previously said a longtime WWE source described the situation backstage as “absolute disarray,” with people still unsure exactly what’s going to happen with the November 7 show. Meanwhile, WWE is carrying on like everything is normal. Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority chairman Turki Alalshikh was promoting Crown Jewel tickets on October 26 and pushing Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship. Ari Emanuel has also said there’s a team watching the situation every day and looking at alternatives in case WWE eventually has to take Crown Jewel somewhere else. For now, the show is still scheduled for November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium. title: WWE Announces Shows Across Australia and New Zealand This Year
raw_title: WWE Announces Shows Across Australia and New Zealand This Year
body: WWE has announced a string of live shows across Australia and New Zealand when the professional wrestling company heads our way this December. With Perth’s RAC Arena already set to host SmackDown on Friday, December 11th, followed by Wrestlepalooza: Perth and Raw on Monday, December 14th, the WWE has today announced new dates in Melbourne, Brisbane and Auckland. The shows will mark the WWE’s first in Brisbane in seven years and the first New Zealand visit in 10 years. body: New Japan’s Super Junior Tag League featured three matches in the A Block on Tuesday as the round-robin portion nears its conclusion. The teams of DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru and Robbie X & Taiji Ishimori came out of Tuesday’s show in Ibaraki with six points each, each having one more round-robin match before next week’s final. DOUKI & Kanemaru defeated Místico & Masatora Yasuda (a late substitution for the injured El Desperado) in the main event. Robbie & Ishimori improved to 3-1 in the A Block, beating Master Wato & KUUKAI after X used the X Xpress to pin KUUKAI. Elsewhere, Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi beat KUSHIDA & Nick Wayne in a seventeen-minute match, ending with Taguchi rolling up KUSHIDA for the cover and increasing their point total to four. The final A Block matches are Saturday in Kyoto with Robbie X & Taiji Ishimori vs. Nick Wayne & KUSHIDA, DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru vs. Master Wato & KUUKAI, and Místico & Masatora Yasuda vs. Ryusuke Taguchi & Kazuma Sumi. The winning teams from A and B Blocks will meet in the final at Power Struggle next Tuesday in Hiroshima. Here’s a look at the updated blocks for the junior tag league. title: Max Caster Confirms Anthony Bowens Still With AEW
raw_title: Max Caster gives update on Anthony Bowens’ AEW status
summary_src: Max Caster has departed AEW, but it seems like his former Acclaimed partner Anthony Bowens is still with the promotion. It was reported that both Bowens and Caster had their AEW contracts set to expire at the start of October 2026.
body: Max Caster has departed AEW, but it seems like his former Acclaimed partner Anthony Bowens is still with the promotion. It was reported that both Bowens and Caster had their AEW contracts set to expire at the start of October 2026. Caster departed the company and is no longer included on the AEW website roster page . Bowens is still listed, though, and Caster told K&S WrestleFest that Bowens still works for AEW. Caster, who did not want to speak for Bowens too much, did not say whether Bowens has re-signed with AEW or what the resolution of Bowens’ contract situation was. “He’s still there,” Caster said during a virtual signing. “Yeah, I don’t want to speak for him too much, but he still works there.” As The Acclaimed, Caster & Bowens were one-time Tag Team Champions for AEW but no longer team together. Caster has decided to step away from wrestling for the moment following a controversial appearance at TNA Bound for Glory 2026. Bowens posted a photo of himself at the NJPW Dojo in California last Friday. Caster said this K&S WrestleFest virtual signing was agreed to a couple of months ago, and he wanted to fulfill the appearance despite taking a break from wrestling. He said he’ll be away for an “undefined amount of time.” When asked if he could return to AEW in the future, Caster did not fully close the door on the possibility. He spoke highly of AEW boss Tony Khan for how Khan takes care of wrestlers. “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never,” Caster told K&S WrestleFest. “However, I am saying ‘no’ to wrestling bookings right now. And that would be a wrestling booking, so I don’t know.” Caster, in his first move post-AEW, debuted for TNA in a loss to Moose at Bound for Glory on October 11. A line in his entrance rap about the ongoing violence in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia led to TNA severing ties with Caster shortly after the pay-per-view. title: Backstage Buzz: Possible Plans for WWE Crown Jewel if Saudi Arabia Event Gets Canceled
raw_title: Possible Plans for WWE Crown Jewel if Saudi Arabia Event Gets Canceled
summary_src: WWE apparently doesn’t have a backup city waiting around for Crown Jewel if the company pulls the plug on Saudi Arabia. According to Jonathan Coachman, if the November 7 show gets canceled, fans shouldn’t expect WWE to simply pack everything up and run the event somewhere else next weekend.
body: Speaking on Two Count Tuesday , Coachman said he received word about what WWE would reportedly do if Crown Jewel can’t happen in Saudi Arabia. Instead of relocating the show on short notice, he claims the entire event would be postponed until a much later date. “By the way, I also got word — if they’re canceling it, they won’t do the show. It’s canceled and postponed to a much, much later date. It will not happen next weekend anywhere else. That’s what I was told yesterday.” Ari Emanuel previously confirmed that there’s a team monitoring the situation every day and looking at potential alternatives . That naturally opened the door to speculation that WWE could simply move Crown Jewel to another location and still hold the show on November 7. According to Coachman, that apparently isn’t the plan. If his information is accurate, WWE would instead scrap the November 7 event entirely and bring Crown Jewel back at some point down the road. Coachman didn’t say how far into the future the show could be pushed or what would happen to the matches already announced. All of this comes while things are pretty messy behind the scenes. WrestleVotes previously said a longtime WWE source described the situation as “absolute disarray ,” with talent and staff unsure exactly what’s going to happen as the show gets closer. There’s also been talk about talent potentially refusing to make the trip. WrestleVotes said WWE stars can technically stay home, but they wouldn’t get paid for the show and could potentially return to work with a different standing in the company. Publicly, though, Crown Jewel is still moving forward. Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority chairman Turki Alalshikh was promoting tickets on October 26, and Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn for the WWE Crown Jewel Championship is still being advertised. As of now, WWE hasn’t canceled, postponed or relocated Crown Jewel, so the November 7 show remains on the schedule at Riyadh Season Stadium. But if things do change, Coachman claims WWE’s backup plan isn’t another city next weekend — it’s no Crown Jewel at all until a much later date. Do you think postponing Crown Jewel would be the right move if WWE decides it can’t hold the show in Saudi Arabia, or should the company try to find another location? title: John Cena Plugs WWE Raw Appearance Next Week: 'The Wait Is Over, The Speculation Ends'
raw_title: John Cena Plugs WWE Raw Appearance Next Week: 'The Wait Is Over, The Speculation Ends'
summary_src: John Cena plugs his WWE Raw appearance next week by saying "the wait is over, the speculation ends," hinting he'll reveal details about the John Cena Classic
body: After several months away, John Cena is set to be back on "WWE Raw" next week, as announced by the promotion during last night's "Raw." And just in case there was any doubt over what Cena would be doing on the show, the 17 time World Champion has removed all forms of suspense. Taking to X on Tuesday morning , Cena plugged his upcoming appearance and made one notable reference to his upcoming John Cena Classic competition, all but confirming that's what his appearance would relate to. "Make sure not to miss WWE Raw next week," Cena tweeted. "SPECIAL START TIME OF 6PM EST! The wait is over, the speculation ends 11/2. Let's build this 'Never Seen' CLASSIC! OUR time is NOW!" It was back in May that Cena first announced the John Cena Classic during an appearance at WWE Backlash . At the time, the announcement received a polarizing response, largely because Cena revealed almost no details about the competition, beyond that it would feature present and future stars and would feature a fan voting element that would allow wrestlers who competed in the competition to move on, even if they lost matches. Cena has since suggested all the key details are figured out , and even admitted that the Classic could be considered "non-canon" to WWE storylines . Given the lack of detail surrounding the competition, Cena's tease would seem to suggest that all the information regarding it will be revealed next Monday during his appearance. That would likely include the date for the Classic, which previous reports had suggested could happen on December 12 . Some recent speculation has suggested the Classic could be timed to take place on December 19, which would put it against AEW Worlds End and the finals of AEW's Continental Classic tournament.
summary: After a number of months away, John Cena is slated to be back on WWE Raw next week, as revealed by the promotion during last night's Raw. And just in case there was any doubt over what Cena would be doing on the show. Make sure not to miss WWE Raw next week, Cena tweeted.

title: Injury Update: Jonathan Coachman Calls Out Tony Khan for Not Booking Hurt Syndicate Despite Paying Them
raw_title: Jonathan Coachman Calls Out Tony Khan for Not Booking Hurt Syndicate Despite Paying Them
summary_src: Jonathan Coachman isn’t buying Tony Khan’s explanation for why the Hurt Syndicate have barely been around AEW lately. In fact, he thinks Khan talking about the group like they can randomly show up whenever they want is pretty ridiculous when he’s the guy booking the show.
body: Speaking on Two Count Tuesday , Coachman went after Khan over his recent comments about Bobby Lashley, MVP and Shelton Benjamin’s absence from AEW television. Khan previously described the Hurt Syndicate as “hired guns” who are available for the right price and could show up “any place, any time.” That explanation didn’t sit well with Coachman at all. Coachman said if Tony Khan’s name wasn’t attached to the comments, he would have assumed they came from a teenager talking about wrestling like everything happening on television was real. “If you read that statement from Tony Khan and it wasn’t a name attached to it, you would swear it was either a 16-year-old or a young Tony Khan, which is what he is, talking about a show as if it’s real life.” Coachman’s bigger issue is pretty simple — Khan runs AEW. He books the wrestlers, pays them and ultimately decides whether or not they appear on television, so Coachman doesn’t understand why Khan is acting like the Hurt Syndicate’s appearances are somehow out of his hands. “Tony, this is a show you put together. These are guys you pay. This is one of the most dynamic threesomes in wrestling, and it’s because of you they’re going through this. It’s because of you they aren’t on the show. So to say you never know when they are gonna show up is ridiculous, because you control where they show up — you’re paying them.” The Hurt Syndicate haven’t exactly been all over AEW television recently. Their last match came at All In, where they teamed with Big Boom AJ and QT Marshall to defeat Shane Taylor Promotions. Khan addressed their absence during the WrestleDream media call, pointing to the group’s previous involvement at Double or Nothing and All In before leaning into their “for hire” gimmick. “The Hurt Syndicate and Mick Foley both involved in Double or Nothing, which I thought was one of the best shows of the year, and AEW All In London, one of the best shows of the year. In the ring, the Hurt Syndicate have said they are for hire, so we could see them any place, any time, I think, for the right amount of money.” Coachman clearly isn’t interested in the storyline explanation. From his perspective, the Hurt Syndicate is one of the strongest acts AEW has, and if Lashley, MVP and Benjamin aren’t being used, the responsibility falls directly on the person running the company. Do you agree with Jonathan Coachman that Tony Khan should be doing more with the Hurt Syndicate, or do you think keeping them off television for a while could make their return feel bigger? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Susan Saint James Passes Away at 80
raw_title: Susan Saint James, WrestleMania 2 celebrity guest, dead at age 80
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Actress Susan Saint James died on Monday at age 80 following a bout with pancreatic cancer. Saint James appeared as a guest commentator at WrestleMania 2 for the New York portion of the three-city show. A rep for Saint James confirmed her death to People.com . Powell’s POV: Saint James was married to former NBC executive Dick Ebersol for 45 years. Ebersol was the producer of the WWF Saturday Night’s Main Event series and helped launch the show on NBC. I remember my mom being a fan of the Kate & Allie sitcom that ran on CBS and featured Saint James and Jane Curtin. The show ran for six seasons from 1984-1989. Saint James previously starred with Rock Hudson in the McMillan & Wife crime series. My condolences to her family and friends.
summary: Actress Susan Saint James died Monday at age 80 after battling pancreatic cancer. She served as a guest commentator for the New York segment of WrestleMania 2. She was married for 45 years to former NBC executive Dick Ebersol, who produced the WWF Saturday Night’s Main Event series.

Since then, he has continued to feud with United Empire. Upon his return, Cobb addressed his time in WWE by saying he never left, but was on hiatus. Cobb was with WWE for less than a year when he was released in April as part of the post-WrestleMania 42 cuts. While with the MFTs, they began wearing face paint as G.o.D. (Tama and Tanga Loa) did at times during their run in NJPW. During an appearance on SOTO619 , Cobb weighed in on having to wear face paint. During his time in Lucha Underground, he wrestled under a mask and was asked which one was harder. "Paint. Paint because I had never done that before. Although to be fair, I didn't, I'd never done the mask thing before. But the paint was truly different because I was told, 'you're going to wear the paint like you did in Japan'. And I never wore paint in Japan. I think they got me confused with somebody else. But, yeah paint was hard because I had to find paint. The paint was the hardest just for the fact that like with the mask, I could I put it on – I couldn't breathe – but I could put it on and then when I'm done, I could take it off. But the paint took forever to get off and I had to use the wipes. But then I found out the wipes that I used got recalled. But then for some reason, the makeup lady still used them."
summary: Jeff Cobb explained that WWE officials mistakenly thought he had worn face paint during his previous NJPW run, which led to him being required to wear it while aligned with Solo Sikoa and the MFTs. Cobb, who had actually never used face paint before, found the experience more difficult than wearing a mask in Lucha Underground. He returned to NJPW in August at the G1 Climax finale, turning on Callum Newman and United Empire to join Unbound Co., and has since continued feuding with United Empire.

The October 26, 2026 episode at the Save Mart Center gave us a last-minute main-event change, a disqualification finish, and a second Money in the Bank cash-in tease for Tiffany Stratton that left the people wanting more. The CIA would have called it a "controlled operation." I call it a bourgeois tease. Comrades, any revolution begins with a sudden change of plans, and Adam Pearce opened Raw with one. Stephanie Vaquer was not medically cleared, so the advertised No. 1 contender's match against Becky Lynch was scrapped. In its place, Pearce made Liv Morgan vs. Lynch for the Women's World Championship. Then Sami Zayn interrupted, because nothing happens in this business without a champion demanding to be acknowledged. Zayn complained about a lack of respect and said Roman Reigns was making a mistake by focusing on The 946 instead of him. I once heard a similar complaint from a general in my cabinet who felt underappreciated after I gave his palace to a llama. The plot thickened when Je'Von Evans walked out and challenged Zayn's standing as champion. Pearce, a man who rules his locker room like a regional governor with a clipboard, ordered Zayn to defend the Undisputed WWE Championship against Evans immediately. That is how the show got both of its title-match announcements in a single opening segment. Efficient, comrades. Even I would approve it without a firing squad. Zayn vs. Evans was an impromptu title match, and it nearly turned into a coup. Penta arrived with his Money in the Bank contract and a referee, apparently intending to cash in. Bron Breakker attacked Penta at ringside, and Evans took out Breakker. When Evans returned to the ring, he missed a springboard attempt. Breakker and Bronson Reed attacked Evans and Penta while Logan Paul watched like a landlord inspecting a property. Breakker speared both men, and Reed hit Tsunami splashes. Later, Breakker, Reed, and Paul gave brief comments about the attack, and WWE reiterated that Penta and Evans will challenge for the tag titles. body: Tony D’Angelo talks about his character shift and The Family’s breakup, noting that ‘a lot of behind the scenes stuff’ caused it. In July of last year, The Family would break up in WWE NXT, sending it’s members in different directions and leading to Tony D’Angelo taking an extended absence from NXT programming before returning in February of this year with a new look, character and speech pattern. While speaking to Denise Salcedo in a new interview, Tony D’Angelo spoke of his character shift in NXT. “It’s been fun. You know, I enjoy it because, I’ve said this before, but you know, the Don character, so to speak is just one part of who I am and who I was. Now we got this Tony D’Angelo, who’s a badass bruiser. Who’s just, it’s just another part of who I am. So I’ve had fun with both and I just, I’m thankful that the fans have, stuck with me, because sometimes transitions can be a little weird, with wrestlers. But it’s been, I can’t say, you know, it hasn’t been fun. It’s sometimes it is stressful for sure. It was a little difficult, but I don’t have to stay clean shaven anymore. I got this beard now, so it’s kind of cool.” Tony also shared that there were ‘a lot of behind the scenes stuff’ that caused the change in his character and the breakup of The Family. “Well, there were, I’ll say this, there were a lot of behind the scenes stuff that caused the change and the breakup and all this other stuff, you know, nothing bad, but just, you know, backstage things happen. So now we we pivoted, I went on that little hiatus and now I am this version of Tony D and it’s still fun. You know, I’m still an ass kicker. I just- I had to go to speech therapy. You know, I used to have an accent, but now, you know, some people had a hard time understanding what I was saying. So I had to- the WWE, thank you. They paid for it, and now I can speak like a normal human, apparently.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

llm_long: Tony D'Angelo revealed that backstage developments played a major role in both the dissolution of The Family and the evolution of his on-screen persona in WWE NXT. The group split in July of last year, which sent its members in separate directions and prompted D'Angelo to step away from NXT television for an extended period.

He returned to programming in February of this year sporting a fresh appearance, altered mannerisms, and a modified way of speaking. D'Angelo told Denise Salcedo that portraying the new version of his character has been enjoyable because it represents another facet of his personality.

He explained that the original Don character was only one side of who he is while the current Tony D'Angelo is a badass bruiser that also comes naturally to him. D'Angelo expressed gratitude that fans have supported him through the transition, acknowledging that such changes can sometimes feel strange for wrestlers and that the process involved stress and difficulty.

He noted that one practical benefit of the shift is no longer needing to remain clean-shaven, allowing him to grow a beard. The wrestler confirmed there was considerable behind-the-scenes activity that directly led to the breakup and the character adjustment, describing it as routine backstage occurrences rather than anything negative.

Following the hiatus, D'Angelo said the creative team pivoted and he returned as this updated version of himself, still functioning as an ass kicker. He disclosed that he underwent speech therapy because some viewers had trouble understanding his previous accent, with WWE covering the cost so he could now speak more clearly.

title: Jimmy House Discusses WWE ID Exit and Evolve Plans
raw_title: Jimmy House Talks WWE ID Departure, Details His EVOLVE Future
summary_src: Jimmy House discusses his departure from WWE ID. In a new interview with Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp, House confirmed that he was released from the program a few weeks ago. Since then, he's been trying to build up some momentum to carry forward.
body: In a new interview with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp, House confirmed that he was released from the program a few weeks ago. Since then, he’s been trying to build up some momentum to carry forward. “So I think there are some assumptions around because I went back to Jimmy House here on the indies and whatnot. So there’s been assumptions and I see things online where people are assuming that I’m not with the program anymore and all that is true. I was released a little over a month ago now. Since then it’s just kind of been trying to pick up where I left off as Jimmy House and take all the lessons I learned through the WWE ID program and tried to build as much momentum as I can and carry it forward and see what’s next for me, really.” Continuing on, Jimmy House revealed that he has segments/matches that will likely air on future episodes of WWE Evolve. House also noted that Evolve was his first experience with TV wrestling. “I have a couple more things on Evolve myself, so I’m not sure exactly when they’re all scheduled to be released and whatnot, but I’m still on there for the next few months at least. It was my first true TV experience. Reality of Wrestling does record TV style. So does Dustin’s and so does Phoenix Championship Wrestling in Arizona. But I definitely think that when you’re at Evolve, you learn their flavor of it and you start to learn exactly what all you need to smarten people up about in regards to particular spots that need to be filmed a particular way or when it comes to break spots and whatnot. So definitely things that you wouldn’t normally experience on the indies that you would learn on something like an Evolve. That’s why, again, I’m just so grateful for the experience because had I not spent the six months there coming out of it, I don’t think I would be as confident as I am to parlay those skills into whatever’s next for me.” Also, head over to Fightful’s YouTube channel to check out more of our recent interviews.

Sign in to your TheSportster account Ever since 2018, WWE has been heading to Saudi Arabia ( and Australia for one year ) for the Crown Jewel PLE, which has become a consistent part of the WWE calendar. Crown Jewel has featured an array of celebrity attraction showdowns, bizarre moments, tournaments, and more, though there have only ever been a handful of title changes. Whether it be major world championships changing hands, tag team titles being won, or midcard belts up for grabs, some of these title changes have been far better than others. These will be assessed by booking quality, the quality of match that the title changed hands in, the crowd reaction and moments, and a sprinkle of hindsight to see how successful the title change ultimately ended up being. In 2024, WWE created the Crown Jewel Championship. WWE’s two men’s and women’s world champions would battle it out to win a brand new belt and receive a Super Bowl-esque ring, though the concept has proven to be completely pointless. The accomplishment means nothing, the wrestlers don’t carry the prize with them, and it only serves to weaken two of the four world champions. Therefore, the title wins of Cody Rhodes, Liv Morgan, Stephanie Vaquer, and Seth Rollins must be lumped into together as being the worst world title wins in the history of the Crown Jewel PLE . Technically these aren’t title “changes”, but they are worth a mention given that they are the new focus of this show. Before Roman Reigns’ title win in the summer of 2018, Brock Lesnar had been a part-time Universal Champion for a long, plodding, and frustrating 504 days. When Reigns was forced into vacating the title and a match was set between Braun Strowman and Lesnar, fans were unanimous in wanting a new champion. However, Baron Corbin arrived before the bell to attack Strowman, leaving him weakened to be dismantled by Lesnar within a little over three minutes. In an awful booking choice that led to another 156 days of a Lesnar title reign, Strowman lost the match with Lesnar crowned once again. The whole thing was a booking disaster, a poor match, lazy booking, and something which the audience were very unhappy with.
