title: Ex-WWE Exec Says 2019 Saudi Plane Delay Was Exaggerated
raw_title: Former WWE executive thinks 2019 Crown Jewel plane incident was ‘exaggerated to some degree’
summary_src: As WWE prepares for another controversial visit to Saudi Arabia, former company executive George Barrios reflected on an incident that happened during his time with the promotion. Barrios was co-president of WWE when the roster was delayed in Saudi Arabia after Crown Jewel 2019.
body: As WWE prepares for another controversial visit to Saudi Arabia, former company executive George Barrios reflected on an incident that happened during his time with the promotion. Barrios was co-president of WWE when the roster was delayed in Saudi Arabia after Crown Jewel 2019. The incident (where some questioned whether they were being held hostage ) played a part in a shareholder lawsuit that WWE settled for $39 million in 2020. Appearing on My World with Jeff Jarrett & Conrad Thompson, Barrios said he believes the incident has been “exaggerated to some degree.” He said issues like this aren’t actually as uncommon as fans would think, recalling the time a different country other than Saudi Arabia instituted an airport fee and forced WWE to pay it if they wanted to leave. “I don’t know what the right phrase — I think it was exaggerated to some degree,” Barrios said about the 2019 situation. “And again, look, back to doing business in other countries, there were other runways around the world where our plane was delayed. I remember somebody calling like, ‘Hey, to get [out], there’s a new fee.’ It was not in Riyadh, it was in a different country, I won’t name it. But we’re getting called, our plane had been delayed and somehow it had gotten serious enough that it reached my desk. Usually this stuff is just getting handled, but it reached my desk because a new fee had been instituted in this country — airport fee — that was a lot of money to get out. And somebody said, someone could look at this and say, ‘You’re being extorted to be let out of the country.’ I guess it depends on how you want to look at it. “But in that moment, there was a fee. And so what did I say? I said, ‘Pay the f***ing fee. We’re coming home, right? So I don’t even know why you’re calling me. Yes, it’s a lot of money. But yeah, we’re paying the airport fee.’ If anybody’s listening and is going to charge me with a violation of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, I say bullsh*t, it was then law in that country and we obeyed it.” Barrios then clarified that he wasn’t trying to say the 2019 Saudi incident was the exact same thing as what went on with this other undisclosed country. “So when you ask about what happened in Saudi Arabia, I think for the most part, I don’t know exactly, and I’m not trying to say there was an analog there — I’m just saying there was a delay and then we got out, and I’ll leave it at that,” he said. The 2019 Crown Jewel event was held on a Thursday. Because of the plane incident, talent missed that Friday’s SmackDown episode before making it home by Saturday. Barrios departed WWE in early 2020 and recently released a book about his time with the company. WWE announced an “expanded” partnership with the Saudi government days after Crown Jewel 2019 and has maintained a close relationship with the country since. title: Contract News: Samantha Irvin Denies Breaching WWE Contract and Trashing Company After Exit
raw_title: Samantha Irvin Denies Breaching WWE Contract and Trashing Company After Exit
summary_src: Samantha Irvin is still dealing with fans coming after her over the way she left WWE, and this time she shut down a couple of accusations in one sentence. After a fan claimed she breached her contract and trashed WWE, Irvin made it clear she says neither of those things happened.
body: The latest exchange started after a video showed Alexa Bliss singing during a TMZ tour. One fan tagged Irvin and suggested that could have been her if she hadn’t supposedly burned bridges with WWE. “Could’ve been you if you didn’t breach contract and trash talk WWE.” Irvin didn’t exactly write an essay defending herself. Instead, she fired back with a pretty simple response, making it clear she never breached her contract, didn’t talk trash about WWE and never had any interest in doing music tours. “Didn’t breach, didn’t talk trash, didn’t want to do the above 🙏🏽” It’s another round of Irvin trying to clear up what she says are misconceptions surrounding her October 2024 WWE departure . Just days earlier, Irvin found herself arguing with another fan after insisting that she didn’t leave WWE to pursue a career in the music business. That fan pointed out that Irvin released music after leaving the company and accused her of lying about her intentions. Irvin pushed back by explaining that she had independently released songs since 2013 and that making music didn’t automatically mean she wanted to enter the music industry. “The chick who has independently released songs since 2013 and had a 2 year non compete made art. Just cause your nana knitted you a sweater doesn’t mean she’s started a clothing line, bruh.” She also recently revealed that WWE actually offered her a record deal before her departure and claimed she turned it down because music wasn’t what she wanted from the company. According to Irvin, what she really wanted was an opportunity to manage wrestlers. “WWE offered me a record deal, to which I politely declined because I have no interest in the music business! My interest was in managing wrestlers. And that’s all I’ve ever expressed.” That goes against the narrative that followed Irvin after she left WWE, when reports suggested outside projects and music played a role in her decision. Irvin has spent the last few days making it pretty obvious that she doesn’t agree with that version of events. Irvin clearly isn’t interested in letting fans write the story of her WWE departure for her. Two years later, she’s still willing to jump into the replies herself whenever she feels like someone has the wrong idea about how things actually went down. Do you think Samantha Irvin has done enough to clear up the misconceptions surrounding her WWE departure, or do you think fans will keep questioning her side of the story? Let us know what you think in the comments. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years, delivering trusted news and backstage updates to fans around the world.
summary: One fan tagged Irvin and suggested that could have been her if she hadn’t supposedly burned bridges with WWE. Could’ve been you if you didn’t breach contract and trash talk. Instead, she fired back with a pretty simple response, making it clear she never breached her contract.

title: 4 Reasons Why John Cena Is Heading Back To WWE Raw
raw_title: 4 Reasons Why John Cena Is Heading Back To WWE Raw
body: John Cena returns to WWE Monday Night Raw on Nov. 2 at Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York. The company announced the appearance on Oct. 26, and a WWE post on X opened with “CENA IS BACK.” The show starts at 6 p.m. ET on Netflix and is the final Raw before Crown Jewel on Nov. 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Backlash on May 9 was Cena’s last WWE television appearance, and the company has not said what the plan is for Brooklyn. Cena announced the John Cena Classic at Backlash in Tampa, Florida. The one-night event will feature talent from the main roster and NXT. Cena confirmed the tournament was still on track at Fan Expo Canada in Toronto in August, then said on NBC’s “Today” show that it will take place in December. WWE has not announced a date or a city for the show. WrestleVotes Radio reported on Fightful Select on Oct. 22 that WWE is considering Dec. 12 and Dec. 19. Dec. 12 is the date of Wrestlepalooza in Perth, Australia, and Dec. 19 is the night of AEW Worlds End. Cena revealed at Backlash that the event will crown the first holder of a brand-new WWE championship. Fans will vote for the winner, and every participant is eligible, so a wrestler can lose a match and still win the title. WWE has not shown the belt, and no image of the design has been released. Currier reported that the title will likely be ceremonial rather than a championship that gets defended. Cena introduced the spinner belt on SmackDown in 2005, shortly after beating John Bradshaw Layfield for the WWE Championship at WrestleMania 21. WWE has not said whether the new belt will be unveiled on Raw in Brooklyn or at the event itself. Cena retired from in-ring competition on Dec. 13, 2025, losing to Gunther at Saturday Night’s Main Event XLII. Days before that match, the retiring star revealed a new five-year deal to stay with WWE as an ambassador. The farewell run included a record 17th world championship, won at WrestleMania 41 in April 2025. Cena did not work the first Crown Jewel in 2018, but lost to Solo Sikoa at Crown Jewel 2023 in Riyadh. At Night of Champions in Riyadh on June 28, 2025, Cena beat CM Punk. Crown Jewel 2025 took place in Perth, Australia, where Cena defeated AJ Styles. The 2026 show remains scheduled for Riyadh Season Stadium despite recent U.S. security alerts for Saudi Arabia, and WWE has not announced any role for Cena. WrestleMania 43 is set for Riyadh in April 2027, and it will be the first edition of the event held outside North America. The exact date has not been made public. WWE has booked NXT Stand & Deliver and an official WrestleMania 43 watch party at Madison Square Garden’s Infosys Theater for that weekend. WrestleVotes Radio reported on Fightful Select that WWE had no plans to reveal the date in October. A separate Fightful Select report said Saudi sources viewed Crown Jewel as a possible spot for the announcement. title: Former AEW wrestler, 48, collapses in ring, dies
raw_title: Former AEW wrestler, 48, collapses in ring, dies
body: Williams was born Dec. 12, 1977, in Buffalo, New York. His path to professional wrestling began later than most performers. He initially suffered a serious knee injury during training, and during his recovery he learned to play guitar. In 1998 , he helped form Every Time I Die, becoming the band's rhythm guitarist and remaining with the group for more than two decades. MORE: Wife of 'Coach', longtime Hollywood actress and singer, dies at 82 Williams began training seriously for wrestling in the mid-2010s, working with Josh Barnett and making his professional debut in 2016 . He became known on the independent circuit as part of The Butcher and The Blade, initially teaming with Braxton Sutter, who later wrestled as The Blade. The partnership became a fixture of independent wrestling before moving to a larger stage. In late 2019, Williams and Sutter joined All Elite Wrestling . The Butcher and The Blade made their surprise AEW debut by attacking Cody Rhodes and soon became regulars in the promotion's tag-team division. They later faced teams including the Young Bucks, FTR, the Lucha Brothers and Jurassic Express, and challenged for the AEW World Tag Team Championship in 2021. MORE: Former Broncos, Giants wide receiver dies at 57 after cancer battle Williams and The Blade remained with AEW for several years, later appearing in Ring of Honor . Their AEW contracts expired in June 2026. Williams also continued performing independently after the group's 2022 breakup, returning to wrestling while maintaining his connection to the music community. On Saturday, Sept. 5, Williams was wrestling at an Enjoy Wrestling event at Mr. Smalls Theatre in Millvale, near Pittsburgh. He collapsed near the end of a tag-team match with The Blade. Medical personnel administered CPR before an ambulance took him to a hospital, and the event was canceled. The Allegheny County Medical Examiner's Office later confirmed that Williams died that night .
summary: His path to professional wrestling began later than most performers. MORE: Former Broncos, Giants wide receiver dies at 57 after cancer battle Williams and The Blade remained with AEW for a number of years.

title: AEW’s emotional tribute to Pac showcased pro wrestling at its very best
raw_title: AEW’s emotional tribute to Pac showcased pro wrestling at its very best
body: Link Jarrett Bailey has been covering the NFL at SB Nation since 2023. PITTSBURGH — Emotion. That’s a word you’ll read a lot in this piece because there was an immeasurable amount of it inside the Petersen Events Center for a very somber episode of AEW Dynamite . What was expected to be AEW’s first show following an incredible All Out Pay-Per-View ended up being an event of mourning, grief, and celebrating the life of Benjamin Satterly, aka “The Bastard” Pac. Satterly passed away Sunday at age 40, less than 24 hours after performing at All Out in Chicago in a tremendous one-on-one contest with Andrade el Idolo for the National Championship. So in Pittsburgh, where he wrestled his first Dynamite main event, the promotion honored their fallen friend — something they’ve had to do far too often. Since its inception in 2019, AEW has seen four of its wrestlers lose their lives. In December 2020, Jon Huber, known to AEW fans as Mr. Brodie Lee, passed away after a battle with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. The Brodie Lee Celebration of Life episode of Dynamite is still one of the best shows AEW has ever done, as it featured Huber’s son, Brodie, getting involved in a six-man tag-team match to help John Silver, Hangman Page, and Alex Reynolds defeat MJF and The Inner Circle. The end of the show featured AEW chairman Tony Khan officially retiring the red strap design of the TNT Championship, the design of the title Huber made famous in the company. Huber’s widow, Amanda, and Brodie then placed his boots in the center of the ring as Cody Rhodes, Preston Vance, and Khan consoled them. In January 2023, Jay Briscoe (real name Jamin Pugh) lost his life in a car accident. The January 25, 2023 episode of Dynamite featured Jay’s brother, Mark, in the main event against their longtime friend and rival, Jay Lethal. Mark Briscoe won the match with the Jay Driller as the locker room poured out to meet Mark on the entrance ramp and celebrate the win, as well as the life of his brother. And just two weeks ago, Andy Williams, aka The Butcher, passed away following an independent show. Williams had been a fixture of AEW’s tag team division as one half of The Butcher and the Blade. His death occurred in the same week in which AEW was set to have a special episode of Dynamite to honor Rebel, an AEW star who is battling ALS. That Saturday on Collision , AEW paid tribute to Williams. And then came Wednesday. The entire locker room, once again, poured onto the entrance stage, bowed their heads, and paid respects to Satterly with a 10-bell salute. And as they raised their heads, one thing was heartbreakingly clear: This locker room isn’t just sad; it’s tired. Tired of mourning. Tired of 10-bell salutes. Tired of the sobs you only cry from losing someone close to you. Tired of making tribute posts on social media talking about how much they’ll miss their now-deceased friends. Through all the grief, though, came (and this is absolutely not hyperbole) the greatest episode of wrestl

title: On the Record: Scott D’Amore Opens Up On Why AEW’s Adam Copeland is Wrestling at MLP Northern Rising
raw_title: Scott D’Amore Reveals Why AEW’s Adam Copeland is Wrestling at MLP Northern Rising
body: D'Amore explained that Copeland has always had an appreciation for one of Canada's most historic venues. Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling, MLP, will celebrate a milestone event with Northern Rising this Saturday. The event takes place at Mattamy Athletic Centre, formerly known as Maple Leaf Gardens. It is a historic venue, as it served as the home of the Toronto Maple Leafs until 1999. The venue also has a rich pro wrestling history. It frequently hosted WWE events, particularly during the company's boom period when it became part of mainstream culture. Copeland has been open about his dream to wrestle at the former Maple Leaf Gardens and will finally get his wish. He headlines the event against former TNA star Steve Maclin . MLP founder Scott D'Amore revealed that there was a lengthy process before securing Adam Copeland for Northern Rising. Copeland, who has been a lifelong pro wrestling fan, used to attend events at Maple Leaf Gardens. But he never had the opportunity to wrestle there. "Somebody shared an interview with me from one Adam [Copeland] had done a couple of years ago, where he talked about how his white whale was he's always dreamed of wrestling at Maple Leaf Gardens, and he never got the opportunity. He started with [ WWE ] months after they stopped running Maple Leaf Gardens, so he just missed it by a matter of months," D'Amore told The Game Plan . After learning of Copeland's dream to wrestle at the venue, D'Amore reached out and sent a feeler out. Copeland is a legendary Canadian pro wrestler, so having him not only appear but also wrestle at Northern Rising is significant. "I texted him and I said, 'Hey, a certain pudgy old roommate of yours might be able to make this happen.' And he was like, 'Keep me posted. Seriously.' So we kept in touch. We had talked about it briefly last year. It didn't work out for last year." D'Amore revealed that Copeland agreed to wrestle for MLP at this year's Northern Rising and was ecstatic about it. However, approval from AEW was obviously still required. D'Amore expressed gratitude towards AEW founder Tony Khan for being gracious and allowing Copeland to perform at the historic venue. "[Copeland] gets paid very well and treated very well by AEW to be a wrestler there. Adam clearly has more of his career in the rearview mirror than he does in the windshield ahead. So, it would be fair for a company like AEW to say no and protect him, and be extra cautious," D'Amore told The Game Plan . "Instead, the response from Tony Khan was, 'That's pretty cool, him wrestling there,' and he gave the green light. So with that, we were off to the races." summary_src: Tony D'Angelo speaks on having to adjust to an ever changing roster in WWE NXT and adapting to the other roster members around him. Tony has been in NXT for several years now, and has seen many wrestlers come and go to the WWE main roster. As of late, more names such as Cruz Montana…
body: Tony D’Angelo speaks on having to adjust to an ever changing roster in WWE NXT and adapting to the other roster members around him. Tony has been in NXT for several years now, and has seen many wrestlers come and go to the WWE main roster. As of late, more names such as Cruz Montana and Grayson Waller have joined the young talent being signed to the companies developmental brand. While speaking to Denise Salcedo in a new interview, Tony D’Angelo spoke about the ever changing roster in WWE NXT, noting that you have to be versatile while dealing with the shifting faces around you. “Yeah. I think you have to be versatile and you have to be able to adjust, especially if you want to be in this job for a long time, you know, and I have seen a lot of people come and go and some people come in and they’re here for two seconds and then they get flung up to the main roster and then they got, you know, they were called up too early. They didn’t have enough experience and then people go, ‘ah, what the heck?’ Then they’re gone. Or, you know, they sit for too long and they don’t change their stuff up and then they eventually get passed on too. So like, yeah, you have to be versatile and be able to adapt for this job. I think that’s super important. But you also have to be coachable, and, you know, some people are stubborn, which I understand I can be stubborn at times as well. But, yeah, I think I’m very good at adapting to my situation, whatever I’m in.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Tony D'Angelo discussed the importance of adapting to WWE NXT's constantly shifting roster during an interview with Denise Salcedo. The veteran NXT performer noted that wrestlers must remain versatile to have long careers, citing examples of talents who were called up too soon without enough experience or who stagnated by not evolving their characters. He has witnessed numerous wrestlers come and go to the main roster over his years in the developmental brand.

title: WWE Announces Major Title Match at Crown Jewel
raw_title: WWE Announces Major Title Match at Crown Jewel
body: Bron Breakker and Austin Theory will defend the WWE World Tag Team Championships against the high-flying duo Je’Von Evans and Penta . The championship bout was announced Monday on RAW, with Paul “Triple H” Leveque later confirming it via social media. “Strength in (even) numbers,” Leveque wrote on Instagram. “Bron Breakker and Austin Theory will defend the WWE World Tag Team titles against Mr. MITB Penta and Je’Von Evans at WWE Crown Jewel.” Tensions have been brewing between Bron Breakker and the top-rope specialists since Money in the Bank in New Orleans. Breakker has been on a warpath since losing the Men’s Money in the Bank Ladder match to Penta, squandering his golden opportunity for a potential World Championship reign. Since MITB, Breakker has twice ambushed Penta and ominously warned the skilled luchador, “Good luck cashing in” on the Oct. 12 episode of RAW . Breakker attacked Penta once more on Monday night, thwarting his cash-in attempt during the WWE Championship match between Sami Zayn and Je’Von Evans. Play Now, Penta could be in line for two championship wins in the next year, as he looks to snatch the Tag Team titles from The Vision. For Je’Von Evans , the Crown Jewel match is all about payback. Not only did Breakker ruin his chances of becoming WWE Champion on Monday, but Breakker nearly ended his career at Money in the Bank. As you may recall, Breakker tipped over a ladder while Evans was at the summit, sending the Young OG plummeting 20 feet out of the ring and through the roof of an ambulance. Earlier in the same match, Breakker severely damaged Evans’ ribs with a devastating Spear. Evans was sidelined from in-ring competition for several weeks following the MITB. His WWE Championship against Sami Zayn marked his first match since Oct. 10. Now, after Breakker cost him two shots at a World Championship, Evans is seeking revenge at Crown Jewel. “They wanna come after me… Bron, The Vision, the whole squad wants to come after us,” Evans said to Adam Pearce backstage following The Vision’s ambush. “I’m not going for that. It’s not finished. I’m not going for that, bro.” Penta added, “We want Bron Breakker and Austin Theory. Because we want the Tag Team titles,” prompting Adam Pearce to make the match official. WWE Crown Jewel will be held on Saturday, Nov. 7, in Riyadh, the capital city of Saudi Arabia. The show will air on ESPN Unlimited in the US and Netflix internationally. In addition to the newly added WWE World Tag Team Championship match, Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will compete in a Last Man Standing match at Crown Jewel. Plus, WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn will take on World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns in the Men’s Crown Jewel Championship match. title: Stu Grayson Recalls Stabbing Hand During Ring Setup
raw_title: Stu Grayson Recalls Stabbing His Hand While Setting Up A Ring, Using Crazy Glue And Duct Tape To Patch It Up Before Wrestling
summary_src: Stu Grayson recalls an instance where he stabbed himself in his own hand while setting up a ring and how he patched himself up after. Injuries in professional wrestling are going to happen, as people throwing themselves down for a living is not exactly the number one industry for worker safety.
body: Stu Grayson recalls an instance where he stabbed himself in his own hand while setting up a ring and how he patched himself up after. Injuries in professional wrestling are going to happen, as people throwing themselves down for a living is not exactly the number one industry for worker safety. However, some injuries come from freak incidents, including during things as ‘boring’ as ring setup. While speaking to Fightful Overbooked’s In The Weeds in a recent interview , Stu Grayson spoke about using duct tape instead of stiches for injuries. “The amount of time I should have gone stitches and I just used duct tape. It’s fucking crazy. I used to travel with duct tape and a little bit of crazy glue and I would just continuously just crazy glue duct tape my skin. Move on to the next match.” Stu also went on to share an instance where he stabbed himself in the hand while trying to set up a ring. “The craziest place not as in it’s crazy as in it’s really, really a huge problem. It was my hand. I was fixing a ring, and while I’m going to try to make it so you can see it, but I was cutting. So I always fix rings when I’m on shows because I’m the guy who gets things done with his hands. So I’m fixing a turnbuckle and I have a long knife, and as I’m trying to cut the rope, I stab my hand. So the knife came in here and came out here. So it was all the way in my hand. So I had to pull it out. Then I said, can you go get my crazy glue?’ I used the crazy glue, then I duct taped my hand, and then I went on to wrestle. That’s just how it is.”

He used Crazy Glue and duct tape to close the wound and continued wrestling in subsequent matches. Grayson made the comments during a recent interview on Fightful Overbooked's In The Weeds podcast.

body: Link Rusev and Lana’s Instagram We don’t know whether or not it has anything to do with why Rusev hasn’t appeared on WWE television since July (he has worked some house shows, as he did on the Oct. 16-17 Hawaiian swing), but who cares! CJ “Lana” Perry and her husband are having a baby! The couple shared the news with People today (Oct. 27). They’ve been doing in vitro fertilization (IVF) since last year, and had their embryo transfered on Aug. 10 of this year. Two positive pregnancy tests confirmed the transfer was successful, and now the couple are ready to tell the world. She described their experience with IVF as an “emotional experience” they’re happy to be on the other side of: “You start with so much hope. As you wait to see how many embryos continue developing through day three and then day five, the numbers can get smaller. Then comes the wait for the genetic testing results. Every stage feels like another hurdle. “Our first embryo to come back with normal genetic testing results was a boy, and he was the one we transferred. When they gave me the option to find out the sex, I wanted to know immediately! There’s so much uncertainty during IVF that I wanted as much information as possible.” The couple will be having a son, and the proud papa’s already got a name picked out. Miro Barnyashev (Rusev’s real name) has been waiting a long time for this moment: “Ten years ago, I had a vision of naming our son Bear, and we chose his middle name to honor my father. Bear will be his first grandson.” No jokes about El Hijo del Rusev facing off against Maxel Hardy, though. Rusev knows his son’s future already: “I’m excited for his future at Real Madrid! We have plans to move to Spain to enroll him in the Real Madrid Football Academy!” Whatever the future holds for Bear, congrats to his mother and dad! Sami Zayn is currently in his second run as WWE Undisputed Champion. He won the title from CM Punk on SmackDown last month. Below are some highlights: “It’s cool. Yeah, here’s the thing that’s funny about it because even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew, and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, you know what, maybe the ship sailed. I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that. Then I was close, but after losing that match, I was like, well, you can’t tell this story again. Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, underdog who finally wins the big one- we burnt that card; that card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. “You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen. I’ve said this before in other interviews, or to friends, or my wife, or whatever. I’ve had a tremendous career, and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never [got it]. You know what I mean? You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture.” “I don’t think anything changed, and that’s actually the point. It’s that I kept doing what I do, which is making sure that everything I’m involved in is as good as it could possibly be. Eventually, a lot has to happen, even when you’re doing good work, and you’re great and all this stuff, to win the WWE Championship. It is like there is no such thing as a fluke win. I know when I won it the first time, and it was nine days, in character you could say I was a fluke. There’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. To even be in the periphery of it is insane. To even be in the mix, to even be in the discussion, to even have title matches, even if you’re losing them, is extremely one in a billion already to be put in that position. title: On the Record: Max Caster Praises Tony Khan, Opens Up On He’s Still Living off AEW Money After Departure
raw_title: Max Caster Praises Tony Khan, Reveals He’s Still Living off AEW Money After Departure
body: 0 Former AEW star Max Caster praises Tony Khan for financially supporting wrestlers. Max Caster was with All Elite Wrestling from November 2020 to October 2026. During his time with the promotion, he won the AEW World Tag Team Championship with his “The Acclaimed” partner Anthony Bowens. He also captured the World Trios Title with Bowens and Billy Gunn. During a virtual signing for K & S WrestleFest , Max Caster praised All Elite Wrestling President Tony Khan for financially supporting many pro wrestlers. He also said he’s still living off AEW money even after departing the promotion. “Here’s one for the dirt sheets. I always gotta shout out Tony Khan because he’s supporting a lot of wrestlers living right now, including me. I’m still living off AEW money. So that’s a guy who, for whatever reason in his heart, is supporting wrestling and supporting wrestlers,” Max Caster said. After leaving AEW, Max Caster debuted for TNA Wrestling at the Bound for Glory pay-per-view earlier this month and competed against Moose. However, as he was making his signature rap entrance, he delivered an unapproved line referencing the recent attacks in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The promotion had to issue a public apology and sever ties with Caster after the public outrage over the segment. After his TNA run ended after just one night, Max Caster apologized for his actions, but clarified he didn’t intend to offend anyone with the rap. He later announced that he’s stepping away from pro-wrestling “for a long time.” He said he’d undergo therapy and get things right the next time he returns to the ring. summary_src: FTR have had plenty of chances to leave AEW and potentially make their way back to WWE, but Cash Wheeler says there’s a pretty simple reason they’ve never pulled the trigger. For him, AEW still gives FTR things they wouldn’t necessarily get anywhere else.
body: Speaking on Going Ringside , Wheeler was asked why he and Dax Harwood have kept AEW as their home base since arriving in 2020 instead of bouncing between major promotions. Wheeler started with the obvious answer for a guy who has spent most of his career in a tag team — he believes AEW has the best tag team division in wrestling. But there’s also something about being part of a company that’s still figuring out how big it can become that appeals to him. “Just because it’s the home of the best tag team division in the world, and it is a place where, as you said before, it’s still so young and growing. It’s exciting to be part of that as opposed to being part of something that’s already a known entity, that’s established, that’s always going to be there no matter what, just because it’s been part of pop culture now for 60-plus years.” Wheeler never mentioned WWE by name there, but the comparison was pretty obvious. Instead of returning to a company that has been established for decades, he likes the idea of helping build something that’s still relatively new. “Whereas AEW, it’s seven years old. It’s in second or third grade, technically. It’s brand new, and it’s exciting to be part of that, to be building that up, and to see the growth the company has had since we debuted there in 2020 to now in 2026. Just to see how the TV show has grown, to see how the attendance has grown, to see how the fan base has grown, and to see new people discovering it.” There’s another part of AEW’s existence Wheeler clearly values too. Having another major wrestling company around means more jobs and, perhaps even more importantly for wrestlers, another place they can negotiate with. “And just knowing that it gives so many other people in our industry — not just the wrestlers, but people backstage — so many job opportunities now. And it helps give wrestlers leverage, honestly, which is not something we’ve had much of for the past 20-plus years that I’ve been in it.” Then there’s the actual wrestling. Wheeler pointed to the number of tag teams FTR have been able to work with during their AEW run, while also noting that being with the company hasn’t stopped them from wrestling elsewhere. FTR have been able to head to places like New Japan Pro-Wrestling and Mexico while still calling AEW home. “There are tag teams across the board that you can’t find anywhere else. And then you get a chance, like we’ve done with our AEW tenure, to go wrestle in New Japan Pro-Wrestling and work those tag teams, or go to Mexico and wrestle some of the luchadors down there.” For Wheeler, that combination pretty much kills any reason to start looking elsewhere. title: Comeback Watch: Vince Russo held Discusses with WWE this summer about shocking return to creative after 27 years
raw_title: Vince Russo held talks with WWE this summer about shocking return to creative after 27 years
body: Hey, hey, it's Conrad Thompson — and the rumor and innuendo that shocked me the most this past summer was that the highly controversial Vince Russo was in talks to make a shocking return to WWE creative. One of the most important — and notorious — figures in modern pro-wrestling history, Russo was a key player during American wrestling's hottest-ever period in the late '90s to early 2000s. As WWE head writer from 1997 onwards, Russo's edgy storylines, emphasis on shock value and crash TV tactics helped WWE turn the tide in the Monday Night Wars vs. WCW. In late 1999, he made a sensational — but ultimately ill-fated — move to quit WWE on short notice to become head writer and executive producer of WCW. A return to WWE all these years later would again send shockwaves around the industry — and that is what was under discussion. I heard that Russo, now 65, had a series of conversations with WWE President Nick Khan about a possible return to WWE this past summer. Russo has remained involved in wrestling for much of the past quarter-century. He had several stints — again, I have to reach for the word "controversial" here — with TNA, he's podcasted and contributed to many documentaries and, most recently, he served as the lead creative for Juggalo Championship Wrestling (JCW). But no one would have predicted that WWE would be interested in returning Russo to the creative team after 27 years. The New Yorker's place in wrestling history has been a hot topic ever since his time in WCW didn't work out. Russo's WCW was marred by some of the most controversial booking decisions in wrestling history, including the decision to put the WCW World Championship — the belt that Ric Flair, Booker T, Hulk Hogan and Goldberg lent so much credibility to — on actor David Arquette. Now, it's a fact that Russo helped pull WWE out of its very average "New Generation" era, which was filled with horrible gimmicks like Duke the Dumpster and Sparky Plugg, into the "Attitude Era," where "Raw" was reaching 10 million viewers in the U.S. alone. It's also a fact that Russo's WCW run was horrible and led many in wrestling to exclaim, "See? Without Vince McMahon reining him in, Russo sucks!" But, all that said, I think JCW fans would argue that Russo could add value to WWE. I am not saying that a consensus would believe he is the secret sauce to reinvigorate WWE, but I do believe a segment of the fanbase would believe Russo could contribute. Only, I don't think he'll get the chance. Not because he's not talented, but because he is Vince Russo. There are two generations of wrestlers and WWE personnel who have strong, negative opinions of him — some of whom may have never even met him. His reputation precedes him, to say the least. Vince Russo in the WWE creative room today? Won't work. Any idea from his mouth will be met with more pushback and less of an open mind than if the identical idea came from someone sitting right next to him. We saw on "WWE Unreal" when Road Dogg was correct

summary_src: Months in the making, the “Undeniable Diamond” arrives November 7 in Chicago.
body: Months in the making, the “Undeniable Diamond” arrives November 7 in Chicago. CHICAGO, IL — Major League Wrestling today announced that Tessa Blanchard will make her highly anticipated MLW debut against Keyra at Saturday Night SuperFight on Saturday, November 7, live from a sold-out Cicero Stadium at 8 p.m. ET. Months of anticipation have led to this moment. The “Undeniable Diamond” is finally stepping into an MLW ring, and she intends to make an entrance the entire sport will be talking about. With the wrestling world watching MLW’s biggest event of the year, Blanchard has the stage to turn a long-awaited debut into an emphatic statement. Blanchard brings an international pedigree forged against world class competition. In CMLL, she captured the World Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Lluvia and won the Women’s International Grand Prix, establishing herself as a force in the sport’s most storied arenas. Those accomplishments fuel the confidence of a competitor who expects to command the spotlight every time she steps through the ropes. At Saturday Night SuperFight, reputation meets expectation. After months of waiting, Blanchard will finally have the opportunity to show MLW Nation exactly why she calls herself the “Undeniable Diamond.” A victory in Chicago would make an immediate splash… and put the entire women’s division on notice. Keyra has every intention of ruining that moment. Making her own MLW debut, the hard-hitting luchadora brings fierce strikes, explosive offense and the confidence to meet Blanchard head-on. While the anticipation surrounds Tessa’s arrival, Keyra sees an opportunity to seize the headlines for herself. Spoiling one of MLW’s most anticipated debuts would ensure nobody forgets hers. Two debuts. One winner. Will the “Undeniable Diamond” shine under the SuperFight spotlight, or will Keyra turn Tessa’s big night into her own breakthrough? SUPER GRUDGES. SUPER RIVALS. SUPER DEBUTS. SUPER TITLE FIGHTS. Saturday Night SuperFight Saturday, November 7 | 8 p.m. ET Cicero Stadium | Chicago, IL SOLD OUT | Watch exclusively on VEEPS

title: Ilja Dragunov Reveals Why He Let WWE Contract Expire
raw_title: AEW's Ilja Dragunov Explains Decision To Let WWE Contract Expire
summary_src: AEW's Ilja Dragunov gives a more detailed explanation regarding his decision to leave WWE for AEW when his contract expired earlier this year
body: AEW/Faecbook AEW's Ilja Dragunov has started off with a bang in his new promotion, debuting thunderously at AEW WrestleDream and then defeating "Speedball" Mike Bailey in his first match a few days later on "AEW Dynamite." At the same time, his media appearances have seen him relive his time in WWE, particularly the reason he decided to let his WWE contract expire and head to AEW. In an interview with Jon Alba of "The Takedown on SI," Dragunov admitted he had been thinking about a career change for some time before his contract came due. "It's been a very complicated time for me," Dragunov said. "But you see, I came back from my ACL tear...[which] that happened in the most unexciting way possible. I worked my way through three rehabs, and was training very hard and was very dedicated. I came back, and I won the United States Championship, basically on my return, which was an awesome, memorable moment. "But then, at certain times after I dropped the belt and I was going through my next performances, I felt...just like, in my gut, things are different. And I don't blame anybody. I'm a gentleman, and I've way too much respect for the last seven years, the most of my 20s, that I spent with the company. But I felt like it is fine for me, and reasonable to ask myself 'Is there more? Is there a new era I can breathe?'" While it's still too early to tell where Dragunov will find himself in the overall standing of the AEW roster, he's so far very happy with how his debut has gone, having described himself as feeling "freedom" ever since he walked through the curtain at WrestleDream.

title: Meltzer: WWE Crown Jewel Still Set For Riyadh
raw_title: Dave Meltzer: WWE Crown Jewel Is Going Forward In Riyadh Unless Something Big Happens
summary_src: WWE is still planning to hold Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. A fourth match was added to the card during Monday's episode of "Raw".
body: WWE As we get closer to November 7 and more travel warnings come from the U.S. government , wrestling fans wonder if WWE will actually go through with holding their Crown Jewel PLE in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. TKO's Ari Emmanuel recently said they are monitoring the situation daily, but "nothing has been canceled" . Keeping the show in Riyadh provides a large financial incentive for TKO along with making sure they keep WrestleMania 43 in the city, according to Dave Meltzer. On Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer said there was a boxing event last weekend where the boxers flew into Bahrain before driving five hours to Riyadh. They say everything is fine and security has been great. There is another show this weekend. "Unless something catastrophic happens between now and next Tuesday, they're going," he explained. Meltzer believes that it's possible Nick Khan could make the trip over to Riyadh with WWE. "I don't think Ari is going. The Board of Directors aren't going. But it's not the Board of Directors choice and it's not Nick's choice." Ari is the one making the choice and he's probably too busy to go, unless he's got some meetings there. I doubt he would go. I don't know if Nick would go or not and it's immaterial, it's not his choice. Vince wasn't on the plane either when they were held hostage. He got out of town on his own plane." Meltzer had previously pointed out some of WWE's talent was held hostage and they returned to Saudi Arabia a few months later. WWE also went into war zones for "Tribute to the Troops" shows.
summary: Dave Meltzer reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that WWE's Crown Jewel event remains scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. He noted the large financial incentive for TKO and the importance of keeping WrestleMania 43 in the city. Meltzer added that unless something catastrophic occurs in the coming days, the show is going forward, with Ari Emmanuel making the final decision.

summary_src: TNA Wrestling is coming to Sport1 in Germany on November 3. From Sport1: TNA Wrestling is coming to SPORT1: Starting Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the network will air the wrestling shows weekly at 10:15 p.m.
body: TNA Wrestling is coming to SPORT1: Starting Tuesday, November 3, 2026, the network will air the wrestling shows weekly at 10:15 p.m. on free-to-air TV. A German commentary duo—Denis Pötzsch and Walandi Tsanti—will host the broadcasts. With TNA, SPORT1 is adding an internationally established wrestling brand to its lineup, appealing to long-time fans as well as viewers who are just discovering the sport. Over 20 Years of History, a Modern Product TNA stands for “Total Nonstop Action” and combines over 20 years of history with a modern, dynamic wrestling product. On SPORT1, the shows will feature German commentary and be available to everyone for free. Pötzsch and Tsanti at the Microphone For the German commentary, SPORT1 is relying on Denis Pötzsch and Walandi Tsanti. Both are familiar with the business from various sports and entertainment backgrounds. For Denis Pötzsch, the launch brings things full circle: he previously provided commentary for the shows back in the Impact era. Walandi Tsanti is also no stranger to wrestling fans: he provided commentary for WWE SmackDown for ten years. Andreas Gerhardt, Chief Content & Distribution Officer: “We’re expanding our sports lineup step by step, and TNA Wrestling fits perfectly into this strategy. The brand has a long tradition and is, at the same time, a modern, fast-paced product. This allows us to reach die-hard wrestling fans as well as people who are watching the sport on our channel for the first time. Starting in November, TNA will be on free-to-air TV on SPORT1.” Denis Pötzsch, commentator: “Walandi and I are really looking forward to bringing TNA Wrestling to fans on SPORT1 as commentators. TNA is a fascinating wrestling brand with over 20 years of history, and at the same time, it’s an extremely modern, dynamic product. For me personally, it’s also a very special homecoming, since I had the opportunity to provide commentary for the shows back in the Impact days. What can viewers expect on SPORT1? In three words: ‘Total Nonstop Action.’” Fightful has coverage of TNA iMPACT! every Thursday beginning at 9 PM ET.

title: On the Record: Vince McMahon Feared WWE Was “Risking the Company” With Saudi Arabia Deal
raw_title: Vince McMahon Feared WWE Was “Risking the Company” With Saudi Arabia Deal
summary_src: Vince McMahon apparently had some serious doubts about WWE’s Saudi Arabia deal before the company ultimately decided to move forward.
body: Speaking on My World with Jeff Jarrett , Barrios looked back at how WWE’s relationship with Saudi Arabia developed in 2017 and 2018. At first, he said the country was treated like any other international market WWE was considering for major events. That started changing as discussions continued. What began as a fairly straightforward event deal grew into a much bigger strategic relationship covering the Middle East. “I would say Saudi Arabia was no different in that we were having them, other than, as we are continuing to have them, the idea of what the deal could be keeps getting bigger. It’s morphing from a country — what I’d call a transactional relationship — to a broader strategic relationship for the entire region in the Middle East.” Barrios said WWE was also looking at Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 initiative and the possibility of being part of the country’s efforts to open itself up. Internally, he said the deal was complicated, but there wasn’t much debate about whether WWE should actually be doing business there. Then Jamal Khashoggi disappeared. Barrios said WWE was only weeks away from signing an agreement when that happened, and suddenly companies considering doing business in Saudi Arabia began pulling back. WWE had to seriously reconsider what it was about to do as well. That led to several private meetings between Barrios, Michelle Wilson and McMahon. According to Barrios, those conversations brought out a much more vulnerable side of McMahon than most people normally got to see. “I still remember him saying at one point — and I hadn’t internalized this the way he had — he actually said, ‘I feel like we’re risking the company.’ You know, he very seriously goes, ‘I feel like this is risking the company.’” That comment apparently changed the way Barrios looked at the situation too. McMahon wasn’t simply worried about whether the Saudi deal itself would work. His concern was that WWE could damage everything it had built elsewhere by going through with it. “And his fear was, I remember him saying, ‘There’s a chance that you unwind all the good you’ve done,’ right? Because at this point, we’re now riding high. We are now rock stars.” The timing made that concern even bigger. body: Major League Wrestling announced that Tessa will face Keyra at MLW Saturday Night SuperFight on November 7. Tessa Blanchard’s Highly Anticipated MLW Debut Set for Saturday Night SuperFight Against Keyra Months in the making, the “Undeniable Diamond” arrives November 7 in Chicago CHICAGO, IL — Major League Wrestling today announced that Tessa Blanchard will make her highly anticipated MLW debut against Keyra at Saturday Night SuperFight on Saturday, November 7, live from a sold-out Cicero Stadium at 8 p.m. ET. Months of anticipation have led to this moment. The “Undeniable Diamond” is finally stepping into an MLW ring, and she intends to make an entrance the entire sport will be talking about. Blanchard brings an international pedigree forged against world class competition. In CMLL, she captured the World Women’s Tag Team Championship alongside Lluvia and won the Women’s International Grand Prix, establishing herself as a force in the sport’s most storied arenas. Those accomplishments fuel the confidence of a competitor who expects to command the spotlight every time she steps through the ropes. At Saturday Night SuperFight, reputation meets expectation. After months of waiting, Blanchard will finally have the opportunity to show MLW Nation exactly why she calls herself the “Undeniable Diamond.” A victory in Chicago would make an immediate splash… and put the entire women’s division on notice. Keyra has every intention of ruining that moment. Making her own MLW debut, the hard-hitting luchadora brings fierce strikes, explosive offense and the confidence to meet Blanchard head-on. While the anticipation surrounds Tessa’s arrival, Keyra sees an opportunity to seize the headlines for herself. Spoiling one of MLW’s most anticipated debuts would ensure nobody forgets hers. Two debuts. One winner. Will the “Undeniable Diamond” shine under the SuperFight spotlight, or will Keyra turn Tessa’s big night into her own breakthrough? body: Orange Cassidy speaks on his theme song situation, noting that he has two very expensive them songs that he enjoys equally. Cassidy is a pro wrestler, who like some iconic names, has more than one theme song that he uses depending on the situation he’s in having used both Jefferson Starship’s ‘Jane’, as well as The Pixies’ ‘Where Is My Mind.’ While speaking to STL Sports Central in a new interview, Orange Cassidy discussed his theme song situation, noting that he has ‘two very expensive theme songs’ that he likes equally. “So, I’m lucky because I have two songs that I alternate between, and the first one that I always have used before AEW and I’ve used now is Jefferson Starship’s ‘Jane.’ We couldn’t get the rights to that for AEW and Tony Khan was like, oh, well, what about the Pixies’ ‘Where Is my mind?’ He got that. So then when I started using the Pixies, Jefferson Starship was like, yeah, you can use this too now. So, I have two very expensive songs that I can use that, I mean, they’re both equally, I like them both. They do the right thing for me in that moment.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Preston Vance Reveals Brodie Lee Jr. Suggested Mask Throw
raw_title: Preston Vance Looks Back On Heel Turn, Says It Was Brodie Lee Jr's Idea To Throw Mask At His Feet
summary_src: Brodie Lee Jr.'s involvement in Preston Vance's heel turn. It was on a November 2022 episode of AEW Rampage that Preston Vance left the Dark Order to join La Facción Ingobernable.
body: It was on a November 2022 episode of AEW Rampage that Preston Vance left the Dark Order to join La Facción Ingobernable. As Vance was walking up the entrance ramp, he crossed paths with Brodie Lee Jr. Vance took his ’10’ Dark Order mask and threw it at the feet of Brodie. Vance looked back on that during his appearance on The Certified Mark Show and shared that the run-in with Brodie was Brodie’s idea. “‘What’s the best way to do this?’ You have to involve Little Brodie and he wanted to be involved, and the whole thing of me taking the mask and throwing it at his feet was his idea. Little Brodie’s idea, and I’m like, ‘Are you sure?’ He’s like, ‘Yeah,’ and I’m like, ‘Alright.’ It was kind of like a coming out moment for me in wrestling. It felt like a big deal, and then Twitter really blew up on it… The whole throwing the mask at the feet was Little Brodie’s idea so I always think — because I get asked that all the time. ‘I can’t believe you would do that,’ and I’m like, ‘No, it was literally his idea.’” Present day, Vance is currently engaged in a storyline in ROH where he is trying to get back into the Dark Order, but John Silver will not approve.
summary: Preston Vance discussed his 2022 heel turn on AEW Rampage where he left the Dark Order to join La Facción Ingobernable. He explained that crossing paths with Brodie Lee Jr. and throwing his '10' mask at the child's feet was entirely Brodie Lee Jr.'s own idea, which Vance initially questioned before agreeing to it. The moment became a significant point in Vance's career that generated major social media reaction, and he now competes in an ongoing ROH storyline.

And Miro's apparently already planning the kid's athletic career ... joking he wants to move the family to Spain so Bear can attend Real Madrid's football academy. The baby news marks another big chapter for the couple, who tied the knot in 2016, separated in 2023, and eventually found their way back to each other. Perry says they've both dreamed of becoming parents for years ... and after everything they've been through, they can't wait to meet their son.

body: WWE star Rusev (Miroslav Barnyashev) and his wife CJ Perry are expecting their first child. After sharing last year that they were utilizing IVF (in vitro fertilization) in the hopes of having a baby, the couple announced via People today that Perry is pregnant. Miro and I have both always wanted to be parents, so being given this blessing fills our hearts with so much gratitude,” Perry told People. “After everything it took to get here, we can’t wait to meet our little boy.” Rusev and Perry have been married since 2016, but there was a period where they separated before reconciling and getting back together. They broke up in winter 2023 but announced in March 2025 that their relationship was back on. On-screen, Rusev and Perry have worked together in both WWE and AEW. Rusev returned to WWE in 2025, and Perry (formerly known as Lana) also signed a WWE Legends contract at the time. She would love to appear on WWE television again if the timing and story are right. Rusev has been away from WWE programming since July, when he suffered an injury during a match against Je’Von Evans. He’s since been medically cleared to return and has worked a couple of WWE house show dates. Internal discussion regarding plans for Rusev’s return to TV has been going on since September . title: Bishop Kaun Explains Forming The Demand With Ricochet
raw_title: Bishop Kaun Details How The Demand Got Started, Thinks Two Other Wrestlers Were Supposed To Be With Ricochet
summary_src: Bishop Kaun discusses The Demand. The Demand in All Elite Wrestling consists of Ricochet, Bishop Kaun, and Toa Liona. They are former AEW World Trios Champions.
body: The Demand in All Elite Wrestling consists of Ricochet, Bishop Kaun, and Toa Liona. They are former AEW World Trios Champions. Kaun detailed how the group started, as he was appearing on The Certified Mark Show . He thinks there were supposed to be two other people paired with Ricochet, but said those people are currently with The Demand. “Honestly, we forced his hand,” Kaun responded when asked how he and Toa Liona were paired with Ricochet. “We saw him cutting this promo. It was like, hey, he’s looking for people. He wants to start this group, he needs a faction, and Toa and I were just looking at the landscape. We were like, ‘Okay, here’s possible people that could be in this group with him.’ Nah, that’s ours for the taking. Fortunately, we’re having tag matches at that time. Every time Toa and I wrestle, our backs are against the wall. We can’t mess up. We have to show out every single time. We feel like we are still not respected after being here for how many years. So we had a match; Ricochet was on commentary. ‘Hey, we gotta show out for this guy. We need to show him and we’re gonna take this opportunity, and no, we’re in this group with him.’ So, literally, we had our match; we get to the back. A producer pulls us aside. He’s like, ‘Yeah, it’s y’all three. He wants you. You impressed him,’ so, yeah, I know we impressed him. We were beating ass out here so, we truly forced his hand. I think it was supposed to be two other guys — nah — we stepped over them, got our spot.” Kaun was asked if he knew who those two talents were supposed to be and said, “I mean, I think they’re in our group right now actually…” In regard to who those two other individuals could be, The Demand has an on-screen alliance with ROH World Six-Man Tag Team Champions Lethal Twist (Jay Lethal, Blake Christian & Lee Johnson).

title: Former WWE Executive Claims 2019 Saudi Arabia Plane Incident Was Exaggerated
raw_title: Former WWE Executive Claims 2019 Saudi Arabia Plane Incident Was Exaggerated
summary_src: The infamous WWE Crown Jewel 2019 plane situation has been surrounded by rumors for years, and George Barrios just gave his side of what happened. The former WWE co-president doesn’t claim to know every little detail, but he thinks the whole thing got blown way out of proportion.
body: Speaking on My World with Jeff Jarrett , Barrios was asked about the flight delay that left a bunch of WWE talent stuck in Saudi Arabia after Crown Jewel 2019. Conrad Thompson brought up all the rumors that followed, including speculation that WWE talent had somehow been prevented from leaving the country, and asked Barrios what he understood actually happened. Barrios didn’t exactly give the conspiracy theories much oxygen. “Yeah, I think it was kind of — I don’t know what the right phrase is — I think it was exaggerated to some degree.” He then brought up another travel nightmare WWE dealt with in a completely different country. Barrios wouldn’t say where it happened, but WWE apparently had a plane sitting around because a new airport fee suddenly needed to be paid before they could leave. And apparently, this wasn’t some tiny fee either. “It was not in Riyadh. It was in a different country. I won’t name it, but we’re getting called. Our plane had been delayed, and somehow it had gotten serious enough that it reached my desk, right? Usually, this stuff is just getting handled, but it reached my desk because a new fee had been instituted in this country — an airport fee that was a lot of money to get out.” Someone even pointed out that the whole thing could look a lot like WWE was being shaken down just to leave the country. “And somebody said you could — someone could look at this and say, ‘You’re being extorted to be let out of the country.’ I guess it depends how you want to look at it.” Barrios apparently wasn’t interested in sitting around debating it. He just wanted everyone on the plane and headed home. “But in that moment, there was a fee. And so, what did I say? I said, ‘Pay the f***ing fee. We’re coming home,’ right? So I don’t even know why you’re calling me. Yes, it’s a lot of money, but yeah, we’re paying the airport fee.” He even threw in a joke about the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act while insisting WWE was simply paying a legal airport fee. “But if anybody’s listening and is going to charge me with a violation of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, I say, ‘F*** it.’ That was the law in that country at the time, and we obeyed it.” That story wasn’t Barrios saying the exact same thing happened in Saudi Arabia. In fact, he went out of his way to make sure nobody walked away thinking that was his point. When it came to Crown Jewel 2019 specifically, Barrios admitted he doesn’t know exactly what caused the delay. His basic takeaway was much less dramatic than some of the stories that have followed the incident for years. “So when you ask, Conrad, about what happened in Saudi Arabia, I think for the most part, I don’t know exactly, and I’m not trying to say there was an analog there. I’m just saying there was a delay, and then we got out, and I’ll leave it at that.” Of course, plenty of people weren’t willing to leave it at that back in 2019. The incident kicked off years of speculation about what was really happening behind the scenes,

Munich, Germany (October 27, 2026) – Anthem Sports & Entertainment, Inc. announced today a new broadcast partnership between TNA Wrestling and SPORT1 , bringing the promotion’s weekly flagship series Thursday Night iMPACT! to viewers throughout Germany. The partnership marks an important return for TNA, which has a long and rich history in the country. Starting November 3, SPORT1 will feature German-language broadcasts of the Thursday Night iMPACT! series, with exclusive commentary and localization, while showcasing TNA’s legendary roster of pro wrestling legends alongside exciting, emerging stars. This move is a further continuation of the platform’s global expansion initiative, focused on increasing TNA’s television presence across Europe and around the world. Through SPORT1, German wrestling fans will now have regular access to acclaimed TNA programming, ensuring they will be able to enjoy the promotion’s signature brand of hard-hitting action, blockbuster stories, and larger-than-life personas—conveniently located on one of the country’s top sports media. Andreas Gerhardt, Chief Content & Distribution Officer of SPORT1, said: “Professional wrestling has a passionate and established fanbase in Germany, and we are pleased to welcome TNA Wrestling to SPORT1. TNA combines compelling personalities, athletic competition and entertaining storytelling, and we look forward to introducing its weekly programming to our audience.” Carlos Silva, President, TNA Wrestling and Anthem Sports Group, said: “Germany has always been an important market—both for professional wrestling and TNA, in particular. title: Vince McMahon Initially Doubted How Much Wrestling Fans Would Watch on WWE Network
raw_title: Vince McMahon Initially Doubted How Much Wrestling Fans Would Watch on WWE Network
summary_src: Vince McMahon apparently had one pretty basic question before WWE launched the Network — how much wrestling could people possibly want to watch? George Barrios says WWE eventually got the answer, and he made sure Vince didn’t forget that he had questioned the idea in the first place.
body: Speaking on My World with Jeff Jarrett , the former WWE co-president looked back at the creation of the WWE Network and how the company went from selling expensive individual pay-per-views to offering them as part of a much cheaper monthly streaming subscription. “We’re going to pivot the pay-per-view from a high-priced model — 50 bucks a month, where we have to split it with the cable companies — to where we can now go direct, and we’re going to lower the price to $10, right? That becomes the essence of the WWE Network.” There was just one problem. Vince wasn’t completely convinced people wanted that much wrestling. Barrios remembered McMahon calmly asking him a pretty hilarious question while they were preparing everything for launch. “And I remember Vince, at one point before the launch, going, ‘George’ — probably one of the few times he used the F-word, but very calmly — ‘How much f***ing wrestling do you think people can watch?’” “And the amount of consumption of the Network content that wasn’t the pay-per-views was staggering, right? It was hundreds of hours of people spending time.” Once Barrios had the numbers, he couldn’t resist having a little fun with his boss. During a meeting, Barrios pulled up WWE’s fancy new viewing charts and reminded Vince of that question he had asked before the Network launched. “So I remember, you know, and I’m a wiseass, we have now all these fancy charts, and we’re in a meeting. There’s a few of us, and I go to Vince, kind of like to needle him, I go, ‘Hey, Vince, remember when you asked me how much wrestling people could watch?’ I put it in front of him, and it turns out quite a f***ing bit.” Vince apparently took being proven wrong pretty well. Barrios said McMahon could laugh at himself in situations like that, despite his reputation and the amount of success he’d already had in wrestling. Instead of getting pissed about Barrios rubbing the numbers in his face, Vince apparently just chuckled and accepted that his guy had been right. “And so he just did that little chuckle. That was the real Vince, you know, that third Vince shows up where he’s like, ‘Yeah, you got me. I’m the king. I’m Vince. I’m the king of wrestling, and this f***ing guy just showed up and was right. People really want this stuff.’” For Barrios, the moment was bigger than simply winning an argument with Vince. The WWE Network became one of the projects he remains proudest of from his time with the company, and those early viewing numbers gave WWE something it had never really had before — a direct look at just how much wrestling its hardcore audience was willing to consume. What do you make of Vince McMahon initially questioning whether fans would actually watch enough wrestling to make WWE Network work? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Rusev and CJ Perry Expecting First Child
raw_title: WWE's Rusev And CJ Perry Announce They're Expecting Their First Child
summary_src: WWE's Rusev and former WWE star CJ Perry announce that they are expecting their first child in early 2027, after a "wild and emotional journey"
body: For more than a decade , WWE's Rusev and former WWE star CJ Perry have been among wrestling's most notable power couples, even withstanding a separation in late 2023 . And now the couple are ready to embrace a more worthwhile challenge; parenthood. People Magazine reports that Perry and Rusev are expecting their first child, due on April 28 2027. The great news comes after what they called a "wild and emotional" journey. "We started IVF in 2025, and on August 10, 2026, we had our embryo transfer," Perry said. "We were so nervous. We had to wait nine days for our first pregnancy test on August 19, followed by another on August 21 to confirm the pregnancy. Those days felt like the longest of our lives! There was a lot of surrendering, letting go and trusting God through the uncertainty." Rusev joked that the couple were planning on moving to Spain, with the idea of enrolling their son into the youth academy of La Liga football powerhouse Real Madrid. He also revealed that the couple was planning to name their son Bear Petrov Barnyashev, a tribute to Rusev's father. "Ten years ago, I had a vision of naming our son Bear, and we chose his middle name to honor my father," Rusev said. "Bear will be his first grandson." The news comes as Rusev has been off WWE since July, when he lost a singles match to Je'Von Evans. It has since been confirmed that the former AEW TNT Champion was suffering from a neck injury that caused his hands to go numb in the match. Upon recovering, Rusev was then beset with illness; he had been hoping to be cleared before the end of September, though that did not materialize.

The couple began the IVF process in 2025 and had their embryo transfer on August 10, 2026, enduring a nervous wait for positive pregnancy tests. Rusev plans to name the boy Bear Petrov Barnyashev after his father and joked about moving to Spain so the child could join Real Madrid's youth academy.

title: Sami Zayn Discusses Origin of His WWE Ring Name
raw_title: Sami Zayn Reveals the Origin of His Ring Name & WWE Character, on Wanting To Break Boundaries
body: During a recent interview with Insight with Chris Van Vliet , WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn spoke about the birth of Sami Zayn in NXT and wanting to show himself when he joined WWE. Zayn, real name Rami Sebei, said he wanted to break boundaries with his character and did not want to portray the heel caricature of an Arab. Below are some highlights: “I’ve heard it. I’ve heard many comparisons with the ring work and the career parallels and all that stuff; there’s some overlap.” “That was interesting. Yeah, that was very interesting. It was an interesting experience because I’d stayed hidden for so long, successfully, which in today’s world seems incomprehensible. This was during the internet, but still not to the level that it’s at today, obviously.” “I didn’t know when they signed me because I also knew, you know, well, you signed me for what you saw. So I’m assuming you liked what you saw, I don’t know what they wanted out of me. So there’s a lot to me, and there’s a lot of avenues you could take. So one was this masked type character. So I’ll clarify. Let me elaborate. But when they’re asking you to come up with names or whatever. I didn’t know what they wanted out of me, so I sort of had these categories, because again, I just didn’t know what they wanted out of me. I know I look like a redhead; I could look Irish or Sheamus’ cousin on TV. If you wanted me to be Sheamus’ little cousin, I could be that. Maybe they want me for that. I’m also French Canadian. I’m also Arab, and there’s the Mexican stuff or the masked stuff. So I was presenting all these different categories of names, not just broad names.” “So I think what I did see as a huge opportunity is to kind of be myself. A huge part of that is obviously my ethnicity and my religion, I guess, to an extent. Just like it’s a big part of who I am. Not that it’s a day-to-day thing, but it’s a big part of the concoction that has made me who I am. To be able to represent that in a way that has never really been represented was very attractive to me. Because as an Arab, you have heightened awareness of it. Growing up in the 80s, 90s, and especially in a post 9/11 world where the stereotypes and the racism and all that stuff is just crazy, and it’s normalized, and it’s accepted, and it was sort of like the only way you saw your people represented in Western culture. I was a child of the West. My household was Arab and Muslim, but for all intents and purposes, I look like just some white kid. So, the idea of kind of smashing that boundary a little bit of being an Arab and not playing the caricature, especially the heel caricature of an Arab.” “Yeah, who wasn’t actually Arab himself, ironically. But just not playing into those stereotypes, not even reintroducing, but introducing a concept of like, hey, Arabs are just normal people. What is this groundbreaking idea!? That was very attractive to me. So I was putting out names that were like Sami Zayn. Sami’s an Arab name. I was almost named Sami.
summary: WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn spoke in a recent interview with Chris Van Vliet about creating his ring name and character in NXT. Real name Rami Sebei, he explained wanting to break boundaries and avoid playing a heel Arab caricature. Zayn also addressed comparisons to another wrestler and staying hidden from the internet before signing with WWE.

title: Preston Vance Says Brodie Lee Jr. Pitched Mask Throw
raw_title: Preston Vance Recalls Brodie Lee Jr.'s Involvement In Heel Turn
body: It was on a November 2022 episode of AEW Rampage that Preston Vance left the Dark Order to join La Facción Ingobernable. As Vance was walking up the entrance ramp, he crossed paths with Brodie Lee Jr. Vance took his ’10’ Dark Order mask and threw it at the feet of Brodie. Vance looked back on that during his appearance on The Certified Mark Show and shared that the run-in with Brodie was Brodie’s idea. “‘What’s the best way to do this?’ You have to involve Little Brodie and he wanted to be involved, and the whole thing of me taking the mask and throwing it at his feet was his idea. Little Brodie’s idea, and I’m like, ‘Are you sure?’ He’s like, ‘Yeah,’ and I’m like, ‘Alright.’ It was kind of like a coming out moment for me in wrestling. It felt like a big deal, and then Twitter really blew up on it… The whole throwing the mask at the feet was Little Brodie’s idea so I always think — because I get asked that all the time. ‘I can’t believe you would do that,’ and I’m like, ‘No, it was literally his idea.’” Present day, Vance is currently engaged in a storyline in ROH where he is trying to get back into the Dark Order, but John Silver will not approve.

title: Sami Zayn Felt Title Window May Have Closed Before Winning
raw_title: Sami Zayn Thought The Ship May Have Sailed On Being WWE Champion After Royal Rumble 2026
summary_src: Sami Zayn has had multiple shots at the WWE Championship over the years, and it looked like his time may have come at WWE Royal Rumble 2026 when he faced Drew McIntyre for the title. The story was that Sami had never beaten Drew, so it would make sense for Sami to beat Drew. He…
body: Sami Zayn has had multiple shots at the WWE Championship over the years, and it looked like his time may have come at WWE Royal Rumble 2026 when he faced Drew McIntyre for the title. The story was that Sami had never beaten Drew, so it would make sense for Sami to beat Drew. Sami eventually got his moment at WWE Night of Champions, winning the Undisputed WWE Title in a triple threat match against Gunther and Cody Rhodes. Now, Sami is a two-time champion. Asked how it makes him feel to be a champion by Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Sami said, “It’s cool. Yeah, here’s the thing that’s funny about it because even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew, and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, you know what, maybe the ship sailed. I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that. Then I was close, but after losing that match, I was like, well, you can’t tell this story again. Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, underdog who finally wins the big one- we burnt that card; that card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen. I’ve said this before in other interviews, or to friends, or my wife, or whatever. I’ve had a tremendous career, and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never [got it]. You know what I mean? You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture.” Sami is set to face Roman Reigns for the Crown Jewel Championship at WWE Crown Jewel. Elsewhere during the interview, Sami looked back on his match against Johnny Knoxville at WrestleMania 38. You can find his full comments here .

title: Johnny Gargano explains son's influence on his WWE return
raw_title: Johnny Gargano planked for six months to avoid disappointing his son further
summary_src: Whether you thought they were a smart way to remain on-screen when creative had nothing for him, or tedious, unnecessary “comedy”, Johnny Gargano’s months of catatonia are over. On SmackDown, that’s meant a WWE title shot against CM Punk and a role by current WWE champ Sami Zayn’s side.
body: Link Johnny Gargano with his son Quill, from Candice LeRae’s Instagram Whether you thought they were a smart way to remain on-screen when creative had nothing for him, or tedious, unnecessary “comedy”, Johnny Gargano’s months of catatonia are over. On SmackDown , that’s meant a WWE title shot against CM Punk and a role by current WWE champ Sami Zayn’s side. It also means Gargano is no longer planking while mute, and can explain why he was in his previous kayface state. Which Johnny did on the latest edition of his vlog with a story about his & Candice LeRae’s son, Quill: “Quill watches the show. He watches SmackDown, and he loves video games. And in his head, when you win or you get a championship like those [motions to title belts displayed on the wall], you get the treasure. It’s a treasure to him. “And I don’t know how many times over the past year, we would fly out on Thursday, and before I would leave, Quill would ask me, like, ‘Dad, are you gonna win? You gonna get the treasure?’ And I would tell him, ‘I try, man. I’m really, really going to try.’ “And then I would have a match on SmackDown, and I’d lose, and I’d come back through the curtain, and Candice would have the phone in her hand. She’d be on FaceTime, and she’d show me Quill just crying, bawling his eyes out, saying, ‘Daddy lost. Daddy’s not going to get the treasure. There’s no treasure.’ “And, like, that broke me. So in my head, it was easier to just not try than to get up and fail and let people down. And I’m not saying that’s right. I’m not saying that’s the way to go about things, but that’s what I did.“ From there, he talked about how that match against Punk ultimately made the difference: “I got a chance at the WWE Championship, a title I have dreamed my whole life of. And I took a leap of faith, and I stood up. And that reaction to me changed everything because it showed me that it didn’t matter. It showed me that people still believed in me.” Which all sounds very much like babyface Johnny Wrestling, but he’s still pledging allegiance to Zayn: “I am loyal to the people that are loyal to me. And Sami Zayn was loyal to me, and I ride or die for the people that are loyal to me.” But he also closed things out by saying he needs to collect some “treasure” to bring home to Quill.
