Michin approached Jade Cargill backstage on that show while holding a kendo stick and accused the reigning WWE Women's Champion of causing her an injury. Prior to the March 20 SmackDown, B-Fab and Michin's most recent televised matches had been defeats against Cargill.

The dynamic changed during the March 20 SmackDown when Cargill declined to face Rhea Ripley, who had won the Women's Elimination Chamber match, and attempted to exit the ring. B-Fab and Michin prevented her departure, initially suggesting a confrontation before aligning with Cargill.

The three then assaulted Ripley, finishing the attack with Cargill's Jaded maneuver. In a subsequent post on X, Cargill referred to B-Fab and Michin as friends due to their common adversary in Ripley. The group remained united even after Ripley captured the WWE Women's Championship at WrestleMania 42.

On May 23 at Saturday Night's Main Event in Fort Wayne, Indiana, Cargill, B-Fab and Michin defeated Ripley, Charlotte Flair and Alexa Bliss in a match that lasted 16:45. Cargill secured the victory by pinning Ripley with Jaded following a pump kick from one of her partners.

B-Fab and Michin competed against Flair and Bliss in a tag team match on the May 15 SmackDown. After Bliss executed Sister Abigail on B-Fab and covered for the pin, Cargill dragged Bliss from the ring, resulting in a disqualification that spared B-Fab from being pinned.
The trio continued their assault on Flair and Bliss following the bell. Bliss shared images of her bruised elbow on X the following day.

title: What Really Happened With Solo Sikoa’s Strange-Looking Promo on October 26 WWE RAW
raw_title: What Really Happened With Solo Sikoa’s Strange-Looking Promo on October 26 WWE RAW
summary_src: Turns out WWE didn’t use AI or a green screen for that weird-looking Solo Sikoa promo on RAW. The whole thing looked strange enough to get fans questioning whether Roman Reigns and The Usos were even really there, but the actual explanation is much simpler.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez explained what WWE actually did with the segment and why it ended up looking so different from the company’s usual backstage promos. For starters, the promo wasn’t filmed live during the October 26 episode . Alvarez said WWE actually taped it the previous week, even though the company never mentioned that on television. “In Solo’s promo, there’s Roman Reigns and The Usos. If you haven’t figured it out already, even though they didn’t announce it, it was filmed last week at last week’s show.” That explains when WWE got everyone together, but it doesn’t explain why the whole thing looked so damn weird. According to Alvarez, WWE decided to experiment with the way the promo was filmed. Sikoa was positioned clearly in the foreground while Roman and The Usos were deliberately blurred in the background, with the camera able to shift the focus between them. “The other thing that confused people is that Solo’s promo was filmed in a unique way. What they were basically doing — I realize I’m a movie star, but I don’t know what the terms are — they were doing the focus, pull focus or whatever.” Basically, WWE was playing around with depth of field and shifting the focus depending on who they wanted viewers looking at. That isn’t exactly some groundbreaking Hollywood trick, but it’s not something fans normally see during WWE promos either. “It’s — you got one in the foreground, and the people in the background are blurry, and you can pull focus on the other people, and the person in the front gets blurry. The point is, they don’t ever film like that, and for some reason, they filmed this one like that.” That unusual look is what sent fans down the rabbit hole in the first place. During the October 26 episode of RAW, Sikoa cut a parking lot promo with Reigns and The Usos behind him while accepting Royce Keys’ challenge. Instead of paying attention to Sikoa’s warning, plenty of viewers immediately started trying to figure out what was going on with the people standing behind him . Some thought Sikoa had been filmed in front of a green screen. Others wondered whether WWE had somehow used AI to create the background. One fan even joked that Roman probably got bored during filming and WWE found a way to let him leave early. Alvarez says none of that happened. “And so, like, everyone thought, ‘Is that AI? Or is Solo on a green screen, and they put Roman Reigns and The Usos?’ No, they just decided to try something different, and it was weird-looking.” So there wasn’t some elaborate production trick separating Sikoa from the rest of The Bloodline. WWE simply tried shooting the promo differently, and the result looked unusual enough that fans thought they were watching a green screen. The funny part is that WWE’s little camera experiment ended up becoming a much bigger talking point than whatever Sikoa was actually trying to say. title: Matt Hardy Says Jeff Refused Storylines Leading to 2001-02 WWE Absence
raw_title: Matt Hardy says WWE punished The Hardys after Jeff refused storyline ideas
summary_src: Matt Hardy says The Hardys were taken off WWE programming in late 2001 and early 2002 because his brother Jeff Hardy refused to take part in storylines pitched to the brothers. In December 2001, Matt, Jeff, and Lita were written off WWF television following attacks by The Undertaker.
body: Matt Hardy says The Hardys were taken off WWE programming in late 2001 and early 2002 because his brother Jeff Hardy refused to take part in storylines pitched to the brothers. In December 2001, Matt, Jeff, and Lita were written off WWF television following attacks by The Undertaker. The brothers were absent from television until the Royal Rumble on January 20, 2002, although they continued working non-televised live events during that period. During a recent interview with The Stunner , Matt spoke about what led to the brothers being off WWE TV. Matt didn’t reveal exactly what the rejected storylines involved, saying only that Jeff was uncomfortable with what was asked. “There was a storyline for our characters, and they wanted us to split up. And there was a couple things that we were asked to do, and Jeff was uncomfortable and didn’t want to do it. “So we were off TV for a while, as a punishment, I guess. But we still did live events, and then they put us back together because we knew we weren’t ready to separate and split up as a team yet.” Asked if he could reveal anything specific that Jeff had refused to do, Matt responded: “Yes, but nothing I can say on here because I would like to stay married.” WWE ultimately split up The Hardys in 2002, with Jeff working a singles storyline with The Undertaker that summer. Matt would begin his Matt Hardy Version 1 character and win the promotion’s Cruiserweight Championship in February 2003. Jeff Hardy was released from WWE in April 2003 and later joined TNA. Matt was released in April 2005, though he would be rehired a few months later. Jeff returned to WWE in August 2006, and The Hardys reunited on WWE programming that November. body: Monroe’s career changed in a big way at the beginning of October, as s he was able to defeat Laynie Luck to win the WWE ID Women’s Championship . As a result of the title win, she also received a WWE ID contract. Months before winning the belt, Monica Monroe attended a WWE tryout during SummerSlam weekend in Minnesota. As it turns out, she was invited to the tryout by AJ Styles. “It wasn’t just a typical, you know, the WWE Recruit page reached out to me. It was actually AJ Styles that reached out to me. It was a combination of those two who got me in. I think, of course, five years of hard work was really what got me in, being at Reality Of Wrestling. But, it was finally like acknowledged and seen. title: Jake Hager Undergoes Second Eye Surgery
raw_title: Former WWE & AEW Star Jake Hager Reportedly Undergoes Second Eye Surgery
summary_src: Former WWE and AEW star Jake Hager reportedly underwent a second eye surgery following a brutal injury during a Power Slap event in September.
body: AEW Following a gruesome injury suffered during a Power Slap event at the end of September, former WWE and AEW star Jake Hager, once known as Jack Swagger, has reportedly undergone a second eye surgery. The athlete took a brutal slap during the second round of his match-up against Johnny Magna that left him bleeding from his left eye. According to Slap News on Instagram , citing Hager's fiancé, Patricia Blackburn, Hager underwent the second surgery to repair a detached retina that was discovered during follow-up appointments after his first emergency surgery . "He underwent urgent surgery to reattach it, which doctors said went better than expected," the Slap News post read. The star went down with injury at Power Slap 23 in Lubbock, Texas. Hager's team tried to have Magna's hit ruled a foul, as the slap neared his eye, but Hager's opponent was awarded the victory due to referee stoppage. Hager revealed he was retired from professional wrestling , following his run in AEW that ended in 2024, in August 2025. He has wrestled two matches since the announcement, the most recent being a June loss to Alberto El Patron at a World Wrestling Council event. At the time of his retirement announcement, he revealed he was running his own trucking company around Florida. The former Bellator fighter joined Dana White's Power Slap promotion in March . He made his debut at Power Slap 19 in April 2026. He knocked out Devin Jenkins in the third round. Since his signing, Hager is 1-2, including the second-round loss to Magna.

The injury, which caused bleeding from his left eye, led to an initial emergency surgery followed by a second procedure after a detached retina was discovered in follow-up exams. Hager's team argued the slap should have been ruled a foul but the referee stopped the bout and awarded the win to Magna.

llm_long: Jake Hager suffered a brutal injury during his Power Slap 23 bout against Johnny Magna. The match took place on September 17 and ended in a TKO loss for Hager after he began bleeding from the eye following repeated slaps.

The fight was stopped immediately and Hager was sent for emergency surgery after sustaining a globe fracture. Power Slap co-owner Dana White described the injury as the worst seen in the UFC, Power Slap or any related promotion and refused to air replays of the blow.

Hager’s fiancée Patricia Blackburn revealed this week that doctors discovered he had a detached retina requiring additional surgery to reattach it. Blackburn stated that the procedure went better than expected and asked fans to send love and prayers to the couple during what she called a sensitive and unpredictable recovery.

Hager stands at 1-2 in Power Slap after winning his April debut by third-round knockout against Devon Jenkins and signing a six-fight contract with the promotion. It remains unclear whether he will be able to fulfill the remaining dates on that deal following the severity of the eye injury.

title: TNA Wrestling Announces New TV Deal With SPORT1
raw_title: TNA Wrestling Announces New TV Deal With SPORT1
body: TNA Wrestling is expanding its international television presence through a new broadcasting agreement with SPORT1, bringing the promotion’s weekly programming to free-to-air television in Germany beginning Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Under the agreement, TNA programming will air every Tuesday at 10:15 p.m. local time, featuring German-language commentary from Denis Pötzsch and Walandi Tsanti. The partnership will make TNA’s weekly shows available to viewers without a paid television subscription. SPORT1 confirmed the arrangement in an official announcement, highlighting TNA’s more than 20-year history and its position as an established international wrestling promotion. The network described the addition as part of its strategy to expand its sports and entertainment programming while attracting both longtime wrestling fans and new viewers. Andreas Gerhardt, SPORT1’s Chief Content & Distribution Officer, commented on the agreement and explained why the promotion was a natural addition to the network’s lineup. “We’re expanding our sports lineup step by step, and TNA Wrestling fits perfectly into this strategy. The brand has a long tradition and is, at the same time, a modern, fast-paced product. This allows us to reach die-hard wrestling fans as well as people who are watching the sport on our channel for the first time. Starting in November, TNA will be on free-to-air TV on SPORT1.” The broadcasts will feature an experienced German commentary team. Pötzsch previously worked on TNA programming during the promotion’s Impact era, while Tsanti brings extensive wrestling broadcasting experience, having provided German commentary for WWE SmackDown for ten years. For Pötzsch, the new agreement represents a return to a promotion he has covered previously. He expressed enthusiasm about reuniting with TNA programming and working alongside Tsanti to introduce the product to SPORT1 viewers. “Walandi and I are really looking forward to bringing TNA Wrestling to fans on SPORT1 as commentators. TNA is a fascinating wrestling brand with over 20 years of history, and at the same time, it’s an extremely modern, dynamic product. For me personally, it’s also a very special homecoming, since I had the opportunity to provide commentary for the shows back in the Impact days.” Pötzsch concluded by teasing what viewers can expect from the broadcasts, adding, “What can viewers expect on SPORT1? In three words: ‘Total Nonstop Action.’” The agreement provides TNA with another television outlet in an important European wrestling market, while giving German fans access to the promotion’s programming with familiar commentary voices.

The arrangement in an official announcement, highlighting TNA’s more than 20-year history and its position as an established international wrestling promotion, SPORT1 made official.

title: Comeback Watch: Max Caster Leaves Door Open To AEW Return After TNA Exit
raw_title: Max Caster Leaves Door Open To AEW Return After TNA Exit
body: Max Caster is leaving the door open to an AEW return, but wrestling is on hold for now. Speaking during Monday’s K&S WrestleFest virtual signing , Caster addressed whether he could return to AEW following his brief stint in TNA. “It’s wrestling, right? You never say never,” Caster said. “However, I am saying no to wrestling bookings right now, and that would be a wrestling booking so, I don’t know.” Caster explained that he was honouring an earlier commitment by attending the signing. Beyond that, he has no timetable for another wrestling appearance. “I agreed to do the virtual signing a couple months ago, I think. I’m honoring this… This is my last wrestling thing for a while, so whoever’s here, I’m sure somebody is clipping this, waiting for me to say something crazy. I’m going to try not to today,” he said. “But, this will be the last time you guys see me for an undefined amount of time.” He also expressed gratitude to Tony Khan, saying his AEW earnings are still supporting him. “I always got to shout out Tony Khan, because he’s supporting a lot of wrestlers living right now, including me. I’m still living off AEW money,” Caster said. “That’s a guy who, for whatever reason in his heart, is supporting wrestling and supporting wrestlers.” Caster’s AEW contract expired on October 1. He made his TNA debut against Moose at Bound for Glory on October 11, but his arrival quickly sparked controversy. During his entrance, Caster rapped, “I drop bombs. You don’t even have to fly to Riyadh,” a day after a deadly missile attack on the city’s main airport. TNA responded the following day, stating that “making light of violent attacks is wrong” and confirming Caster “will no longer be wrestling for TNA.” He later apologised to TNA president Carlos Silva and the company’s office, admitting he “went too far.” On October 17, Caster told fans at Awesome Championship Wrestling’s Mischief Night II in Poughkeepsie, New York, that he was taking an extended break from the ring and going to therapy. The former Acclaimed star leaves his next chapter open after winning two AEW World Tag Team Championships with Anthony Bowens and holding the AEW World Trios Championship.

title: End of an Era: Amazing Red Believes He Could Convince AJ Styles to Come Out of Retirement
raw_title: Amazing Red Believes He Could Convince AJ Styles to Come Out of Retirement
summary_src: Amazing Red has AJ Styles on his mind for one more match, and he thinks there might actually be a way to pull it off. With Styles now retired, Red has noticed something about his old rival that makes him wonder if wrestling could eventually drag him back into the ring. During an interview with ...
body: During an interview with Sports Matters TV in association with Wrestle Slam , Red was asked about potential dream matches following his TNA Hall of Fame induction and X-Division Championship victory. The interviewer specifically floated the idea of Red convincing Styles to come out of retirement for one more match in TNA. Turns out Red has already been thinking about it. He compared the situation to his own experience with Will Ospreay, who kept pushing Red to wrestle again after he had stepped away. Eventually, it worked. “I totally agree with you. I feel like, just because I’ve been thinking that also. And the way Will Ospreay took me out of retirement and just kept pushing me, pushing me, and then I kind of came back.” That experience apparently has Red wondering whether the same thing could happen with Styles. Red said he’s noticed Styles continuing to train and spending time at the dojo while helping his son. From Red’s perspective, those are signs that Styles hasn’t completely left wrestling behind just because his in-ring career is over. “I see what you see, where I see AJ training. I see AJ going to the dojo. I see him following his son and making sure he’s doing here and there. And you can tell, you can tell. I don’t think you can leave wrestling.” Red knows firsthand how difficult it can be to completely walk away. He compared wrestling to an ex-girlfriend who keeps finding her way back into your life, even when you need some time apart. “I think there are moments where we have to step away, for sure, if it’s a mental break, physical break, but wrestling is such a hard thing to leave. It’s just one of those ex-girlfriends that just doesn’t leave you alone.” As for actually getting Styles back in the ring, Red jokingly suggested he might have to take a slightly different route and go through Styles’ son first. “And I feel like if the timing is right for him, maybe I have to go through his son to get to him, you know? Who knows?” That got Red thinking about another pretty wild possibility. Even if he never gets another match with Styles himself, he could potentially end up facing the next generation of the family with the X-Division Championship involved. “But even thinking that that’s kind of a possibility, isn’t that crazy? I could probably wrestle AJ Styles’ son at some point for the X-Division title. It’s just so crazy. So crazy.” Red and Styles were both huge parts of the X-Division’s early identity, so the idea of them sharing a TNA ring again naturally carries some history with it. Red isn’t saying Styles is coming back, but he clearly hasn’t ruled out trying to tempt his old rival into putting the boots on one more time if the timing ever feels right. Would you want to see Amazing Red and AJ Styles share the ring one more time, or is there another opponent you’d rather see Red face during his current run? Let us know what you think in the comments. Subhojeet Mukherjee Subhojeet Mukherjee has covered pro wrestling for over 20 years

And the way Will Ospreay took me out of retirement and just kept pushing me, pushing me, and then I kind of came back. That experience apparently has Red wondering.

title: Chris Bey Marks Two-Year Anniversary Of Neck Injury
raw_title: TNA's Chris Bey Reflects On Two-Year Anniversary Of Catastrophic Neck Injury
summary_src: TNA star Chris Bey reflected on the two-year anniversary of his life-altering neck injury and shared a video of his recovery.
body: It's been two years since a life-altering injury changed the course of TNA star Chris Bey's life , and he's looking back on his recovery journey to mark the occasion. Bey suffered an accident during a match on an October 2024 "TNA iMPACT" taping that left him temporarily paralyzed, with a broken neck that required surgery. Bey took to X (formerly Twitter) on Tuesday to share a post about his journey. He shared a video, complete with photos and videos of himself first in the hospital, accompanied by gym photos and videos from more recent times. One clip shows Bey using a walker to get around, followed by another of him hitting a squat jump. Other clips show Bey using a leg press machine and completing box jumps. The final part of the video shows an emotional Bey from his first time walking to the ring during a TNA event . "2 years ago my life changed forever with a tragic injury," Bey wrote. "Truth is, my story began that day. My new story. The Greatest Story Ever Told. I'm forever grateful for the love every single one of you has given me." 2 years ago my life changed forever with a tragic injury. Truth is, my story began that day. My new story. The Greatest Story Ever Told. I'm forever grateful for the love every single one of you has given me. None of this is possible without God, without... pic.twitter.com/rWx1gWOxLv Bey said that year one was all about him learning to walk again and defying the odds. His last year was about challenging himself in the gym, and he questioned what was ahead for the next year. "Stick with me on this never ending journey, I'll be sure to keep motivating you, and even more certain I'll keep surprising you," Bey concluded. "Thank you. I love you. #GSET" Bey has made appearances with TNA since the injury. He helped announce the signing of Ricky Sosa during TNA Sacrifice back in March.

He expressed gratitude for the support from fans, saying he is forever grateful for the love every single one of them has given him. Bey credited God, his doctors, physical therapists, occupational therapists, and his partner BB for making his progress possible.

During the first year after the injury, Bey focused on learning to walk again while defying the odds and regaining the ability to function. In the second year, he challenged himself in the gym as part of his ongoing recovery.

Bey noted that only God knows what year three will bring and invited people to follow him on his never-ending journey where he plans to keep motivating and surprising others. Since the injury, Bey has made several on-screen appearances for TNA, including at the 2025 Bound For Glory pay-per-view where he helped introduce Ricky Sosa as the promotion's newest signee.

title: Several AEW Wrestlers Pushing Back Against Taking Losses on TV
raw_title: Several AEW Wrestlers Pushing Back Against Taking Losses on TV
summary_src: There are apparently some wrestlers in AEW who really don’t want to stare at the lights on television. A new backstage report claims certain talent have actually pushed back on taking pins, with some wrestlers apparently happier getting pushed in ROH than showing up on Dynamite just to lose.
body: Speaking during a Self Made Session , Self Made Pro claimed this isn’t just a case of one or two wrestlers being difficult about doing jobs. According to the report, there are plenty of people hanging around AEW’s midcard who aren’t exactly excited about losing on television every week. “They’re not the only people that don’t love to job. There are plenty of people in AEW populating your favorite midcard that don’t like losing on TV every week.” Things apparently get even more interesting inside the Don Callis Family. Self Made Pro claimed there are members of the group who haven’t won a single match this year but have still turned down taking pins on television. “There are people in the Don Callis Family who have won zero matches this year that have also turned down jobbing and eating pins on TV.” Nobody was named, so there’s no point playing detective with the Don Callis Family roster. But the report claims this attitude has also helped keep certain wrestlers over in Ring of Honor. Apparently, some would rather actually get pushed there than pop up on Dynamite just to put somebody else over. “There are guys in Ring of Honor mainly because they’d rather be on Ring of Honor pushed than jobbing on Dynamite.” Self Made Pro also argued that it’s pretty easy for established main eventers like Will Ospreay and Hangman Page to be team players. Those guys already know one loss isn’t going to suddenly knock them down the card. “There’s no issues when it comes to being team players when you’re Will Ospreay or Hangman Page, because they’re main eventers. They’re gonna be okay. The no-job people in AEW, or who pout about jobbing — it’s easier to be all about the team when your spot is solidified.” For somebody fighting just to keep their spot, though, taking another loss can apparently feel a whole lot different. Self Made Pro said some wrestlers are naturally thinking about their own future before worrying about whether losing makes for a great angle. “But when you’re worried about your own stock in AEW, it becomes, ‘What happens to me?’ rather than, like, ‘Oh, this is a great angle,’ because the priority is yourself, because you don’t know what’s gonna happen to yourself, and there are plenty of people like that.” That concern makes a little more sense with another recent Self Made Pro report claiming some lower-card AEW contracts could simply be allowed to expire rather than being renewed. If wrestlers already aren’t sure where they stand, apparently some of them aren’t too interested in making that situation worse by becoming the person everybody beats on TV. What do you make of the reported situation with some AEW talent behind the scenes, and how much control should wrestlers have over their own booking? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: What Happened to AAA After TripleMania
raw_title: How did AAA get so stale, so fast? | Big Vinny V
summary_src: Earlier this year, AAA was on fire. However, after putting on one of the year’s best matches in May and following it with their biggest show of the year in September, it feels like all their momentum is gone.
body: Let’s start at the beginning. The mask match at Noche de Los Grandes between El Grande Americano and Original Grande Americano was one of the year’s best, and the hottest AAA has been in years. The victory propelled El Grande Americano to TripleMania 34, where he would face Dominik Mysterio for the AAA Mega Championship in what was on paper the biggest match the promotion had to offer. Since then, however, AAA has mostly been putting out shows with pretaped matches and segments, devoid of any feeling of urgency or newsworthiness. Let’s look at what AAA has put on TV since TripleMania, one episode at a time: AAA Lucha Libre 34: The only matches on this episode were dark matches taped before TripleMania, with El Fiscal defeating Dinamico and La Hiedra beating Faby Apache. The two matches, combined, went less than nine minutes. AAA Lucha Libre 35: These matches were also taped before TripleMania— weeks before, in the middle of August. Mister Iguana beat Taurus, Texano Jr. beat Dinamico, and La Hiedra won a three-way over Adelicious and Lady Shani. About 20 minutes of old matches with no title changes, no upsets, nothing to get excited about. AAA Lucha Libre 36: This was the October 3 episode, the only live episode between TripleMania and Heroes Inmortales, and it still felt like a rerun. La Parka defended the AAA Latin American Championship against Mister Iguana in a match we have already seen before, this time with no winner. And Omos & Dominik Mysterio defeated El Grande Americano & Rey Mysterio in a mashup of the two main events at TripleMania, which we had already seen and setting up the younger Mysterio to face Americano yet again at Heroes Inmortales. AAA Lucha Libre 37: The matches on this show and the next were taped at the October 3 event. Los Americanos (Rayo & Bravo) beat the Tokyo Bad Boys, and Mini Vikingo won a four-way (over Jack Cartwheel, Joaquin Wilde, and Nobu San) to win a AAA Cruiserweight Championship match against Rey Fenix at Heroes Inmortales. Put a pin in that for now. AAA Lucha Libre 38: Two more matches: Taurus defeated El Fiscal, and Los Wagner Brothers defended the AAA Tag Team Championships against El Mesías & Mecha Wolf. The former led to Fiscal challenging Abismo Negro Jr. to a match at Heroes Inmortales; the latter led to nothing. This brings us to Night One of Heroes Inmortales, which aired this past Saturday. And what did we get on that show? Los Perros Del Mal defended the AAA Trios Championships against La Parka & Mister Iguana & Nino Hamburguesa, a match in which the tecnicos never had a prayer and were booed throughout. Catalina defended her AAA Reina de Reinas Championship in a three-way against Lady Flammer and La Hiedra, but that felt more like the start of the split in Las Tóxicas, not the payoff to a month-long build. Then came the main event, where Americano defeated Dominik Mysterio after interference from Rey Mysterio, Omos, and Dorian Roldan. We have been watching these same five men do the same thing
summary: AAA followed its strong Noche de Los Grandes mask match and TripleMania 34 title bout between El Grande Americano and Dominik Mysterio with a string of low-energy television episodes. The post-TripleMania shows have featured only pretaped dark matches from weeks earlier, including short bouts such as El Fiscal over Dinamico, La Hiedra over Faby Apache, Mister Iguana over Taurus, Texano Jr. over Dinamico, and La Hiedra in a three-way win. The programming has lacked any sense of urgency or new developments according to the Wrestling Observer.

title: Sami Zayn Doesn't Think It's 'Ludicrous' To Say He Should Have Beaten Roman Reigns At WWE Elimination Chamber 2023
raw_title: Sami Zayn Doesn't Think It's 'Ludicrous' To Say He Should Have Beaten Roman Reigns At WWE Elimination Chamber 2023
body: Sami Zayn won the WWE Championship two times this year. Both of these victories were somewhat unexpected for fans. But there was another time when Zayn could’ve won the WWE Title, and a lot of fans were rooting for him as well. That was during the Elimination Chamber premium live event in 2023, when Zayn challenged Roman Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. There were several moments in this match when fans, even if for a second, thought that Zayn could realistically take the title belt off Reigns. But at the end of their 30+ minute match, Reigns walked out victorious. The match took place in Montreal, so Zayn had support from a hometown crowd. He recently sat down for an interview with Chris Van Vliet on Insight , where he was asked if he should’ve won the title that night. Zayn starts by saying that there was a case to be made for his victory in Montreal, and he doesn’t think it’s ludicrous to say the same. “At the time, I thought there was a case to be made for it, but going back to the domino effect thing, I don’t know. I really don’t know. I don’t think it’s ludicrous to say I should have. If you were watching at that time, I think anybody could have made that argument.” He implied timing to be one of the reasons why he didn’t win against Reigns. “But it was just again timing, and Cody was also red hot at that time, and they were building to something. Then it leads to Cody the next year, and then it’s more gratifying. Whatever it is, just yeah, I don’t know. Could, should, would- would it have worked? I think so. But who’s to say?” Following Elimination Chamber, Reigns defended his title against Cody Rhodes at WrestleMania. When Zayn lost, many fans thought it was because WWE was saving this moment for Rhodes. But at WrestleMania, Reigns ended up beating him as well. Things eventually worked out for them. Rhodes finished his story a year later at WrestleMania and ended Reigns’ title reign. Zayn, on the other hand, had to wait three more years before he could finally win his first WWE Championship. It wouldn’t be wrong to say that the WWE Title picture on SmackDown is way more interesting than the World Heavyweight Championship scene over on Raw, and Zayn is one of the biggest reasons for this. summary_src: Amazing Red wants to bring AJ Styles out of retirement. Styles finished up his in-ring career earlier this year, losing to Gunther at the Royal Rumble event in January. Since then, plenty of fans and wrestlers have asked 'The Phenomenal One' to get back in the ring.
body: Styles finished up his in-ring career earlier this year, losing to Gunther at the Royal Rumble event in January. Since then, plenty of fans and wrestlers have asked ‘The Phenomenal One’ to get back in the ring. In a new interview, SportsMattersTV’s Jerry Coughlan went on a spiel about how Amazing Red could be the one to bring AJ out of retirement. Red agreed with this take, comparing wrestling to an ex-girlfriend that won’t leave you alone. “I totally agree with you. I feel like just cause I’ve been thinking that also and the way Will Ospreay took me out of retirement and just kept pushing me and then I kind of came back. I see what you see where I see AJ training, I see AJ going dojo to dojo. I see him following his son and making sure he’s staying here and there. You can tell — It’s just, I don’t think you can leave wrestling. I think there’s moments where we have to step away for sure, if it’s a mental break or a physical break, but wrestling is such a hard thing to leave. It’s just one of those ex-girlfriends that just don’t leave you alone. I feel like if the timing is right for him and maybe I have to go through his son to get to him, who knows? But even though thinking that’s kind of a possibility, isn’t that crazy? I could probably AJ Styles’ son at some point for the X-Division title. It’s just so crazy.” Check out the current lineup for the October 29 episode of TNA iMPACT by clicking here. Fightful will have full coverage of the show as it airs. title: JBL Explains Why John Cena Never Turned Heel
raw_title: JBL Says John Cena Had the Hardest Job of Any Champion in Wrestling History
body: “I don’t think there was a right time, and I think one of the reasons was because we tried that with Steve. We tried that with Stone Cold and he was so freaking popular, and he was selling all the merch. When do you turn a hot babyface heel? When they’re the hottest. It just didn’t work with Steve, and I think Vince took that and thought, ‘I’m not going to make the same mistake with John.’ And so he never did. I was in a ton of meetings where people were pitching, ‘Oh, can we turn him heel? Can we turn him?’ Vince said, ‘No.’ The numbers were like 50 or 60% of the merch was his. He was making a fortune for the company selling all of his stuff, and there was all kinds of pressure to turn him heel his entire career. And Vince just wouldn’t do it. I think he wouldn’t do it because he tried it with Steve, and Steve was so popular, and it just didn’t work. People wanted Steve; Steve was already a heel. What are you going to do? Make Steve flip off more people, drink more beer, cuss more people out? Steve already did that. So I think that was the reason that Cena never turned heel. “And then they tried it, and I just don’t think people wanted it. You’re going to have some dips**t on the internet say, ‘Oh, JBL is talking about how Cena turning heel didn’t work’ and put some little clip on there, and make it sound like I’m bashing him. I’m not. Cena was so freaking popular, just like Stone Cold, that people didn’t want to see him turn heel. Plus he had been there for so long. It didn’t work, and I think it didn’t work because of who John is. He was ‘Hustle, Loyalty, Respect,’ and all of a sudden now he’s not. I get that it’s a work; you turn a babyface heel when they’re the hottest. But with certain guys, I just don’t think you can do it.” “I thought the idea was fantastic. And Cena, I remember when he came in, he was a heel at the very beginning. He was a great heel. He was really freaking good. It’s just that all of a sudden he caught lightning in a bottle. I’ve always thought Cena had the hardest time out of any champion in the history of wrestling, literally in history. He went from the Attitude Era, where you could flip off the boss and use any type of language you wanted, to a G-rated era, and he still had to fill arenas, and he did it. I think that’s the hardest role anybody’s ever had, and Cena was able to do it.”

He noted that Austin was already a heel character who flipped off people, drank beer, and cussed, leaving no effective way to amplify that persona after the turn. JBL added that when they eventually tried turning Cena heel, fans simply did not want it because Cena had been a babyface for so long.

He pointed out that Cena's 'Hustle, Loyalty, Respect' slogan made the shift feel inconsistent, even though it is a work. JBL recalled that Cena started as a great heel when he first came in but caught lightning in a bottle as a face.
He stated that Cena had the hardest championship role in wrestling history, transitioning from the Attitude Era's freedom to a G-rated era while still filling arenas.

body: Welsh hopeful Mason Ryan was drawing double takes from people long before he inked a WWE developmental deal in 2009. He resembled Batista during his formative years as a wrestler on the UK independent circuit. Sadly, Ryan would never quite reach the heady heights of 'The Animal' when he signed on with the big time. A stint in FCW proved fruitful, at least. There, Mason won the development league's top belt and seemed primed for bigger things to come on Raw or SmackDown. By late-2010, he was working SmackDown house show loops in Europe and was surely raring go to on mainline television. Ryan joined CM Punk's new Nexus incarnation in early-2011 , and that appeared to be the best possible spot for someone who had bodyguard vibes but still needed experience. Working with guys like Punk and John Cena regularly would only help him improve, wouldn't it? Injuries and a start/stop booking style for the Nexus generally scuffed his promise, and people just couldn't shake the 'he looks like Batista on a WWE tribute show' vibes. It turns out that physically resembling a dreamscape mirror image of someone in the main event mix doesn't always do one any favours. Watch this space if anyone who looks like Roman Reigns shows up in years to come. Physically blessed? Sure, but emerging from the shadow of obvious comparison can prove to be too difficult for some. Big Mason was put back to developmental in 2012 then released in 2014 without really achieving much at a tippy top level. title: TNA Wrestling Lands New TV Deal in Germany, Premiere Date Locked In
raw_title: TNA Wrestling Lands New TV Deal in Germany, Premiere Date Confirmed
body: 0 TNA Wrestling is expanding its international television reach, with the promotion set to debut on SPORT1 in Germany. The agreement marks another step in TNA’s efforts to expand its audience beyond the United States. The promotion has continued to build its television presence following its move to AMC earlier this year. The German television deal arrives during a significant period for TNA’s domestic television presence. The promotion launched Thursday Night iMPACT! on AMC on January 15, 2026, following a multiyear media rights agreement announced in December 2025. Under the agreement, AMC airs TNA’s flagship weekly show every Thursday from 9 p.m. to 11 p.m. ET. Episodes are also available through AMC+, extending the show’s reach beyond traditional television. SPORT1 announced that TNA Wrestling will premiere on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 10:15 p.m. local time. The weekly broadcasts will feature German commentary from Denis Pötzsch and Walandi Tsanti. SPORT1 will broadcast TNA Wrestling every Tuesday, with Pötzsch and Tsanti providing German commentary. Both commentators bring experience in wrestling coverage, with Pötzsch previously calling TNA programming during the Impact era and Tsanti having spent a decade providing commentary for WWE SmackDown. Andreas Gerhardt, SPORT1’s Chief Content and Distribution Officer, welcomed TNA’s addition to the channel’s programming lineup. “We are expanding our sports programming step by step, and TNA Wrestling fits perfectly into this strategy,” Gerhardt said, according to SPORT1’s announcement. He added that the promotion combines a long history with a modern wrestling product, allowing the channel to reach established fans and viewers discovering TNA for the first time. summary_src: George Iceman might have some decisions to make pretty soon. The Personal Concierge’s TNA deal is coming up, and apparently TNA isn’t the only place interested in having him around.
body: According to False Finish, a source with knowledge of the situation indicated that Iceman’s contract with TNA is coming up soon and there’s interest in him outside the company. The report didn’t name any specific promotions, so there’s no word yet on who might be looking at him or whether Iceman is actually considering leaving. The timing definitely makes things interesting. TNA has a bunch of contracts coming up over the next couple of months, with President Carlos Silva recently holding a talent meeting and telling the roster the company plans to work on getting new deals done. A lot of contracts are coming up in December. Iceman has been around TNA for a while, but becoming Ash By Elegance’s Personal Concierge is what really gave him his spot on television. He eventually became the mouthpiece for the entire Elegance Brand as the group grew to include Heather By Elegance, M By Elegance and Mr. Elegance. He’s mostly there to talk trash, cause problems and make the Elegance Brand even more obnoxious, but TNA has actually gotten him into the ring too. Iceman made his TNA in-ring debut at Sacrifice 2025, teaming with Ash and Heather By Elegance. Funny enough, this isn’t the first time his contract has become a topic. Back in June, there was already a report that his deal was coming up. Iceman didn’t exactly clear things up afterwards, instead posting that no matter what people heard or what happened, “the show must go on.” Now we’re several months down the road and his contract situation is back in the conversation, except this time there’s reportedly outside interest attached to it. Nothing says Iceman is definitely leaving TNA, but he could have a few options on the table when it’s time to figure out what’s next. Where would you like to see the TNA star end up if he does decide to make a move? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Drew McIntyre Calls Roman Reigns His Kryptonite
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Refers To WWE Rival As His Kryptonite: 'I'm Gonna Get Him'
summary_src: WWE star Drew McIntyre referred to one WWE rival as his "kryptonite" and vowed he was going to "get him" before it's all said and done.
body: WWE Former Undisputed WWE Champion Drew McIntyre has had plenty of excellent feuds throughout his career, most recently, against Cody Rhodes, then Jacob Fatu, before his hiatus from the company due to Hollywood obligations . On a recent episode of " Insight with Chris Van Vliet ," "The Scottish Psychopath" was asked about his greatest rivalries, outside of the one seemingly rooted in real life, against CM Punk . McIntyre named former WWE star Sheamus, now going by S. Farrelly, who he's known for over 20 years and fought against across the globe, as well as Seth Rollins. There's one man, who stands out among everyone to McIntyre, however. "Roman [Reigns], my kryptonite," McIntyre said. "Still haven't defeated [him] to this day. Need to get him before it's all said and done. Him and his stupid family." McIntyre and Reigns have faced off one-on-one five times throughout their careers, with their most recent bout taking place for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship at Clash at the Castle 2022 in Wales . McIntyre has often blamed Reigns and the rest of the Bloodline for costing him opportunities. In 2025, the men were on opposing WarGames teams, with McIntyre's heel team getting the win over Reigns, the Usos, Rhodes, and Punk. Reigns is headed into this year's WarGames match as World Heavyweight Champion, seemingly set to team with the Bloodline against the 946 rather than defend his title on the show. McIntyre has been teasing his WWE return in various interviews, after last being seen at WrestleMania 42 in April.

On the Insight with Chris Van Vliet podcast, McIntyre said he must defeat Reigns and his family before his career ends. The pair last met at Clash at the Castle 2022 for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship.

summary_src: Paul Heyman apparently had his fingerprints all over the opening of this week’s RAW. A new backstage report claims the entire Sami Zayn and Je’Von Evans situation, along with Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed getting involved afterwards, came from ideas Heyman personally pushed for.
body: Speaking during a Self Made Session , Self Made Pro reported that Heyman was the one who pitched bringing those specific names together for the opening portion of RAW. That doesn’t mean Heyman sat down and wrote Sami Zayn’s promo or personally produced everything fans saw on television. Instead, the claim is that the basic idea of putting Zayn, Evans, Breakker and Reed together came from Heyman. “I was directly told that the opening of RAW — specifically Sami Zayn’s promo, Je’Von Evans coming out, having a match with Sami, and the post-match involving Bron Breakker and Bronson Reed — was told this was the brainwork of Paul Heyman in terms of pitching things for these to happen.” The report specifically made that distinction clear. Heyman’s involvement was apparently more about putting the pieces together and pitching which wrestlers should interact rather than handling the actual writing or production. “Not in terms of producing the segments or writing, but in terms of making the pitch for these people to be involved with each other. That was a Paul Heyman thing, and he had a lot of influence on the show overall.” That pitch ended up taking up a pretty big chunk of the October 26 RAW . Zayn opened things by going off on Adam Pearce before declaring himself the most underrated wrestler in the world. He took shots at Roman Reigns’ schedule, brought up CM Punk, Trick Williams and several other WWE stars, and eventually demanded that everyone start acknowledging him. That brought out Evans, who wasn’t interested in listening to Zayn complain. After the two went back and forth, Pearce made an Undisputed WWE Championship match between them on the spot. Zayn retained after hitting Evans with the Helluva Kick, but things didn’t end there. Breakker attacked Evans afterwards, Penta tried to intervene, and Reed joined the mess before Breakker and Reed left Evans and Penta laid out. So while Heyman apparently wasn’t sitting backstage writing every line of Zayn’s promo, the bigger picture of what fans saw was his idea. And if the report about his influence over the rest of RAW is any indication, this wasn’t the only part of the show where Heyman had some input. What did you make of the way RAW opened this week and the wrestlers WWE brought together during the segment? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Bully Ray Praises WWE's Use of Royce Keys
raw_title: Bully Ray Explains How the ‘Timing Was Right’ for Royce Keys in WWE
body: During a recent edition of Busted Open Radio , WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray praised WWE for the creative handling of Royce Keys since joining WWE and becoming the leader of The 946 . He noted that “some places” don’t understand how to maximize their talent, hinting at Keys’ past stint in AEW. Speaking on Royce Keys, Bully said he isn’t shocked about how the wrestler is being utilized in WWE. He stated (via WrestlingInc.com ), “I’m not nearly as shocked [as to how Keys has been used in WWE]. Some places just don’t know how to utilize talent to their maximum potential.” Bully Ray continued that the timing was perfect for Keys in WWE, explaining, “A term that you hear over and over and over again in the world of professional sports entertainment — timing is everything. Now, that goes for real life, but my god, timing is everything truly when it comes into play in our world. It really does. Timing was right for Royce Keys.” Keys and The 946 are currently embroiled in a heated feud with The Bloodline in WWE.

title: Backstage Buzz: Kevin Owens, Sami Zayn Rumored To Be Unhappy With WWE Crown Jewel Plans
raw_title: Kevin Owens, Sami Zayn Rumored To Be Unhappy With WWE Crown Jewel Plans
body: 0 WWE Crown Jewel is facing growing uncertainty amid security concerns surrounding Saudi Arabia. Reports suggest that several people within the company are unhappy about the planned trip to Riyadh. The Premium Live Event is scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. However, security concerns in the region have reportedly raised questions among WWE talent and staff about proceeding with the show as planned. Former WWE personality Jonathan Coachman has addressed the situation, claiming that several WWE stars are unhappy about the company’s Crown Jewel plans. Speaking on The 2 Count , Coachman said he had received information about talent who were reportedly furious about the situation. “The names that I got given to me, that are backstage furious about this, but we have not seen one talent, not one has talked about this, has addressed this.” Coachman specifically named Kevin Owens, Danhausen and Sami Zayn as stars who reportedly do not want to travel to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel. “Some of the names I got that do not want to go – Kevin Owens, Danhausen, Sami Zayn.” Coachman also questioned the apparent lack of public comments from WWE talent about the situation, suggesting that the company and its parent organization, TKO, may have instructed performers not to discuss the matter publicly. “So to me it is glaring that WWE and TKO have told their talent clearly ‘You do not comment on this.’” Reports from Fightful Select have indicated that several staff members and talent are unhappy about traveling to Saudi Arabia under the current circumstances. Dave Meltzer also reported on Wrestling Observer Radio that WWE was unhappy after some non-wrestling employees expressed concerns about making the trip. Despite the reported concerns, WWE and its partners in Saudi Arabia continue to promote Crown Jewel and its advertised matches. Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority (GEA) Chairman Turki Alalshikh recently highlighted the men’s Crown Jewel Championship match between Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn. title: Sami Zayn reflects on not winning WWE title in Montreal
raw_title: Sami Zayn on whether he should have beaten Roman Reigns to win the WWE Championship in Montreal, looks back on working with Johnny Knoxville
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Insight With Chris Van Vliet with guest Sami Zayn Host: Chris Van Vliet Podcast available via Podcasts.Apple.com When you hear that you’re a two-time WWE champion, how does that make you feel? “It’s cool. Yeah, here’s the thing that’s funny about it because even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew [McIntyre], and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, you know what, maybe the ship sailed. I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that. Then I was close, but after losing that match, I was like, well, you can’t tell this story again. Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, underdog who finally wins the big one- we burnt that card; that card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. “You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen. I’ve said this before in other interviews, or to friends, or my wife, or whatever. I’ve had a tremendous career, and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never [got it]. You know what I mean? You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture.” You become the champion for the first time in June; if you thought that window had closed, what changed? “I don’t think anything changed, and that’s actually the point. It’s that I kept doing what I do, which is making sure that everything I’m involved in is as good as it could possibly be. Eventually, a lot has to happen, even when you’re doing good work, and you’re great and all this stuff, to win the WWE Championship. It is like there is no such thing as a fluke win. I know when I won it the first time, and it was nine days, in-character, you could say I was a fluke. There’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. To even be in the periphery of it is insane. To even be in the mix, to even be in the discussion, to even have title matches, even if you’re losing them, is extremely one in a billion already to be put in that position. So to win it, there’s an immeasurable number of variables that are required to be in that position. So there’s no such thing as a fluke WWE title win. “So I just think kind of slow and steady wins the race. title: End of an Era: Hall Of Fame Legend Believes He Can Lure AJ Styles Out Of Retirement
raw_title: Hall Of Fame Legend Believes He Can Lure AJ Styles Out Of Retirement
body: No Result View All Result HOME Headlines About Contact Privacy Policy WWE WWE News, WWE Rumors and Spoilers WWE Raw Results WWE NXT Results WWE Smackdown Results WWE EVOLVE WWE PPV Results Saturday Night’s Main Event Results WWE House Show Results AEW AEW News and Rumors AEW Dynamite Results AEW Collision Results AEW PPV Results AEW Results Ring of Honor Results TNA TNA Wrestling News and Rumors TNA IMPACT Results TNA PPV Results COLUMNS Hustle In Laiman’s Terms Between The Flips and Fists Tim Rose Jr. Powerrr Play! Cohen’s Commentary El Gringo Loco Cool Points LOP Hall Of Fame No Result View All Result --> Home » News » TNA Wrestling News and Rumors » Hall Of Fame Legend Believes He Can Lure AJ Styles Out Of Retirement Share on Twitter --> Could AJ Styles eventually be convinced to come out of retirement? One TNA Wrestling Hall of Famer believes he might be able to make it happen. During a recent interview with SportsMattersTV, reigning TNA X-Division Champion Amazing Red discussed the possibility of convincing “The Phenomenal One” to return to the ring following his retirement earlier this year. Styles officially ended his in-ring career after losing to GUNTHER at the WWE Royal Rumble in January. Despite stepping away from competition, the former WWE Champion has remained involved in wrestling, something Red believes could eventually lead to another match. Red pointed to his own experience with Will Ospreay, who helped convince him to return to wrestling after previously retiring. “I totally agree with you. I feel like just cause I’ve been thinking that also and the way Will Ospreay took me out of retirement and just kept pushing me and then I kind of came back,” Red said. “I see what you see where I see AJ training, I see AJ going dojo to dojo. I see him following his son and making sure he’s staying here and there.” According to Red, walking away from professional wrestling permanently is much easier said than done. “You can tell — It’s just, I don’t think you can leave wrestling. I think there’s moments where we have to step away for sure, if it’s a mental break or a physical break, but wrestling is such a hard thing to leave. It’s just one of those ex-girlfriends that just don’t leave you alone.” Red also floated the possibility of getting to Styles through his son, who has been pursuing his own wrestling career. “I feel like if the timing is right for him and maybe I have to go through his son to get to him, who knows? But even though thinking that’s kind of a possibility, isn’t that crazy? I could probably [wrestle] AJ Styles’ son at some point for the X-Division title. It’s just so crazy.” Red was inducted into the TNA Hall of Fame earlier this month during Bound For Glory weekend, where he also captured the vacant X-Division Championship. Styles, meanwhile, has given no indication that he intends to reverse his retirement decision. title: Chris Bey Marks Two Years Since Neck Injury
raw_title: Chris Bey reflects on two-year anniversary of broken neck
summary_src: Today marks two years since the last time Chris Bey competed in a professional wrestling ring. On October 27, 2024, Bey — one of the top young names in TNA Wrestling at the time — suffered a broken neck while he and his tag team partner Ace Austin were facing The Hardys at a television […]
body: Today marks two years since the last time Chris Bey competed in a professional wrestling ring. On October 27, 2024, Bey — one of the top young names in TNA Wrestling at the time — suffered a broken neck while he and his tag team partner Ace Austin were facing The Hardys at a television taping. It was originally unknown if Bey would ever be able to walk again, but he spent the first year of his recovery getting back on his feet and being able to live an independent life . Year two was about rebuilding himself in the gym. As he enters year three, Bey isn’t sure what’s next. He’s excited to keep surprising people as he continues what he calls the “Greatest Story Ever Told.” Bey has bonded with WWE star CM Punk over their shared love of the gym and trying to get in the best shape possible. Whether Bey’s own in-ring career will ever resume is still an open question. Bey told The Sportster this summer that he’s focused on making music, along with finding ways to still contribute to wrestling by helping younger talent. He is keeping the mindset of “never say never” when it comes to possibly wrestling again at some point. llm_long: Today marks two years since Chris Bey last competed in a wrestling ring. On October 27 2024 Bey suffered a broken neck during a TNA iMPACT television taping where he and tag team partner Ace Austin faced The Hardys in a match that took place after the Bound For Glory event.

The injury left him temporarily paralyzed and required surgery with doctors initially uncertain if he would ever walk again. Bey posted on X sharing a video that included hospital photos from right after the injury images of him using a walker early in recovery and recent clips of him performing squat jumps leg presses and box jumps in the gym.

In the post Bey wrote "2 years ago my life changed forever with a tragic injury" and added that the truth is his story began that day as his new story which he calls the Greatest Story Ever Told. He expressed gratitude for the support from fans and credited God the doctors physical therapists occupational therapists and the love of his life BB for making his progress possible.

Bey described year one of recovery as learning to walk again defying the odds and regaining the ability to function independently while year two focused on challenging himself in the gym. As he begins year three Bey stated that only God knows what comes next but he plans to keep motivating others surprising people and continuing the journey with the mindset of never say never regarding a possible return to wrestling.
Bey has focused on making music and helping younger talent while maintaining his bond with WWE star CM Punk over their shared commitment to gym training and peak physical condition.

title: Comeback Watch: WWE’s Current Plans for Rusev’s Return Revealed
raw_title: WWE’s Current Plans for Rusev’s Return Revealed
summary_src: Rusev’s WWE comeback might look a little different than fans were expecting. After an injury messed with the company’s original plans for him, WWE apparently has a new direction ready to go — and it ties directly into something that just happened on RAW.
body: While speaking during a Self Made Session , Self Made Pro revealed that Rusev is expected to join Ethan Page and Big Cass, with WWE planning to make the three an official stable right away. “I can also tell you that expect Rusev, Ethan Page, and Big Cass to be a formal stable immediately.” That’s a pretty big development considering Rusev was originally supposed to be involved with Page before his injury got in the way. WrestleVotes previously reported that WWE had been looking for someone to pair with Page , and Rusev was initially the guy they had in mind. With Rusev still working his way back, WWE went in another direction and put Cass alongside Page instead. “It was supposed to be Rusev. Rusev’s dealing with a little injury. He’s on his way back.” At the time, it looked like Rusev had simply lost his spot in the whole thing. Turns out WWE may have just decided to make the idea bigger. Page and Cass officially got things rolling on the October 26 edition of RAW when they teamed against Intercontinental Champion Chad Gable and Dragon Lee. They didn’t waste much time proving the pairing was serious either, as Page caught Lee with an Ego Plex to pick up the win for his team. Now Rusev is apparently about to enter the picture and turn the duo into a full three-man stable. That would also give Rusev an immediate direction after spending months away from WWE television. His absence started after the July 27 episode of RAW, when he landed awkwardly on his neck during a match against Je’Von Evans and experienced numbness in his hands. Rusev still finished the match before quickly heading backstage, which initially led to some speculation that he was pissed about losing. CJ Perry later cleared that up, explaining that Rusev was actually in considerable pain and wanted WWE’s medical team to check him out. Things finally started moving in the right direction in September when Perry revealed that Rusev had been medically cleared. He returned to the ring at WWE’s October 16 live event in Honolulu , wrestling Joe Hendry in his first match in nearly three months. Rusev’s injury may have forced WWE to change the original plan, but it clearly didn’t kill the idea of putting him alongside Page. Instead, his time away may have accidentally helped turn a two-man pairing into an entirely new faction. What kind of impact do you think Rusev could make once he gets back on WWE television, and how would you book his first night back? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Contract News: Samantha Irvin Responds to Allegations of Breaching WWE Contract After Exit
raw_title: Samantha Irvin Responds to Allegations of Breaching WWE Contract After Exit
body: 0 Samantha Irvin has pushed back against allegations that she breached her contract and spoke negatively about WWE following her departure from the company. Irvin announced her departure from WWE on October 21, 2024, after more than three years with the company. She began as a ring announcer in WWE’s developmental system before moving to SmackDown and eventually Monday Night RAW. Her distinctive announcing style and memorable introductions helped establish her as one of WWE’s most recognizable ring announcers. She also introduced matches during both nights of WrestleMania 40 in April 2024. Following her exit, Irvin explained that she wanted to explore opportunities beyond ring announcing, particularly the possibility of managing wrestlers. She also addressed speculation about music, noting that WWE had offered her a record deal that she declined. Irvin addressed the claims on X after a fan tagged her while commenting on a clip of Alexa Bliss performing her song “I’M JUST DRUNK” during the TMZ tour. The fan suggested Irvin could have been in Bliss’ position had she not allegedly breached her contract and criticized WWE. “could’ve been you if you didn’t breach contract and trash talk wwe,” the fan wrote. Irvin directly rejected both allegations, clarifying that neither was the reason behind her WWE exit. “Didn’t breach, didn’t talk trash, didn’t want to do the above ??,” Irvin responded. Irvin’s departure also came with a reported two-year non-compete clause that limited her ability to pursue opportunities with other wrestling promotions. Reports in October 2024 indicated that the restriction would run for 24 months. Irvin later confirmed in October 2025 that she had one year remaining on the clause. The restriction has fueled speculation about her potential return to professional wrestling, with reports suggesting AEW has discussed bringing her into the company as her non-compete clause nears its end . title: Johnny Gargano Reveals Reason For Months Of Planking On SmackDown
raw_title: Johnny Gargano Explains Months Spent Planking On WWE SmackDown, Why He Got Back Up
summary_src: Johnny Gargano explains why he spent months planking backstage on WWE SmackDown, and what were the moments that helped him snap out of his funk
body: After years of "NXT" glory , final beats , and the occasional tag title reign with now AEW star Tommaso Ciampa , Johnny Gargano entered a new stage of his career this past summer; the planking stage. Gargano spent most of this year sitting on a table, practically comatose, in a character development that left many fans confused. Now, on his latest YouTube vlog , Gargano is attempting to clear up just why he spent so much time planking. "Everyone's wondering why," Gargano said. "'Why were you laying around, feeling sorry for yourself for six months Johnny? What was going on?' Well, it's complicated, but the easy answer is right there [points to photo of himself holding titles]. I feel like everyone expected me to be that guy. And I tried to be that guy, and I couldn't. And I felt like I was letting a lot of people down. And I hated that." Gargano explained that, as he was struggling, his son Quill would be asking him when he was going to "get the treasure," or win a championship. After yet another defeat on "SmackDown," Gargano came to back to see his wife, Candice LeRae, facetiming Quill. "She'd show me Quill just crying, balling his eyes out, saying 'Daddy lost, and he's not going to get the treasure. There's no treasure,'" Garagano said. "That broke me. So in my head, it was easier to just not try then to get up and fail and let people down. And I'm not saying that's right, I'm not saying that's the way to go about things, but that's what I did." Gargano snapped out of it when CM Punk challenged him to a Undisputed WWE Championship match in September, in Gargano's hometown of Cleveland . Gargano credits the fan reaction for ultimately keeping him out of his stupor, even after he lost to Punk. "Even when I gave them no reason to, they still believed in me," Gargano said. "And that just showed me...I don't know. If I try, if I really, really try, I think I can make anything happen."
summary: After enjoying success in NXT including multiple title reigns with Tommaso Ciampa, Johnny Gargano entered a new phase this past summer where he spent months sitting motionless on a table on SmackDown. In his latest YouTube vlog, Gargano explained that the pressure of living up to expectations as a top star left him feeling like he was letting everyone down, including himself. He also shared how his young son Quill kept asking when he would win a championship, adding to the emotional weight after losses.

llm_long: Johnny Gargano has explained the reasons behind his six-month hiatus from wrestling earlier this year. Gargano was seen planking backstage instead of competing in matches since the beginning of the year. He returned to the ring in August when he faced CM Punk in Cleveland.

During a vlog, Gargano addressed why he had been inactive for half a year. He stated that everyone expected him to be a certain guy and that he tried to live up to that but felt he was letting a lot of people down.

After losses on SmackDown, Gargano would see videos of Quill crying because his daddy was not getting the treasure. This affected Gargano deeply and led him to decide it was easier not to try than to fail repeatedly and let people down. He also thanked the fans for their continued support and Sami Zayn for showing him the way.

title: Comedian Roasts Shawn Michaels, Vince McMahon and Goldberg in Bret Hart Halloween Candy Parody
raw_title: Comedian Roasts Shawn Michaels, Vince McMahon and Goldberg in Bret Hart Halloween Candy Parody
summary_src: Kyle Fields has found another excuse to bring fake Bret Hart back, and Halloween gave him plenty to work with. This time, a bag of candy was all it took for “The Hitman” to start unloading on some very familiar names from wrestling history.
body: Fields took to Instagram with his latest parody, titled “Bret Hart Reviews Halloween Candy.” Instead of simply deciding which candy belongs in the trick-or-treat bag, fake Bret somehow turned almost every piece into another story about Shawn Michaels, Vince McMahon, Goldberg or somebody else he apparently still has a problem with. Things started harmlessly enough with Reese’s Peanut Butter Cups. M&M’s were where things immediately went off the rails. Fake Bret had some thoughts about the red and yellow ones before casually claiming he had history with the green one. “You know, the red one and the yellow one are gay. I hooked up with the green one in Germany.” Then came Sugar Daddy, and naturally Fields found a way to drag Shawn Michaels into it: “Shawn used to have a sugar daddy in Portland.” Snickers somehow became another Shawn and Vince joke, with fake Bret remembering people supposedly laughing whenever the two returned from getting food together. “You know, there were a lot of snickers when Shawn and Vince would come back from the hot dog stand sharing a footlong.” There was absolutely no chance Fields was getting through a Bret Hart parody without mentioning Goldberg, and Hershey’s Krackel gave him the perfect setup. “You know, I can hear my neck crackle when I was kicked by Bill Goldberg.” Airheads went to Eric Bischoff, and fake Bret Hart wasn’t exactly handing out compliments as he called him the “dumbest, stupidest person.” “I’ll tell you who was an airhead — Eric Bischoff. He’s gotta be the dumbest, stupidest person. You know, he legally can’t make toast.” Then it was right back to Shawn and Vince once Dots came out, saying, “You know, it didn’t take the boys long to connect the dots with Shawn and Vince.” Fields finished things off with Starburst, which somehow became a joke about Bret getting busted open during his wrestling career. “You know, I got juiced so many times for Vince over the years, it didn’t even matter.” This comes just over a month after Fields imagined Bret recording Cameo videos, where Goldberg, Shawn, Vince, Cody Rhodes and Dean Malenko all ended up catching strays. Before that, he even sent his fake version of “The Hitman” to Calgary Traffic School. At this point, Fields barely needs a setup for these things. Give fake Bret a handful of Halloween candy and somehow Goldberg is kicking him in the head again while Shawn and Vince are sharing a footlong. Which Halloween candy joke from Kyle Fields’ latest fake Bret Hart parody got the biggest laugh out of you? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Rusev And CJ Perry Announce They’re Expecting Their First Child, A Baby Boy
raw_title: Rusev And CJ Perry Announce They’re Expecting Their First Child, A Baby Boy
body: Rusev and CJ Perry (whom a lot of fans may remember as Lana) recently announced that they’re expecting their first child. The couple first started dating each other in 2013, after working together on WWE television. Three years later, they tied the knot with each other. In 2023, the couple separated from each other. But just a few months later ( according to TMZ ), they started talking to each other again and eventually rekindled their relationship. They renewed their wedding vows in early 2025. Rusev and Perry recently announced via PEOPLE that they are expecting their first child through in vitro fertilization (IVF). The couple said that they’re expecting a baby boy and are planning to name him Bear Petrov Barnyashev. “We’re so excited and incredibly thankful. Miro and I have both always wanted to be parents, so being given this blessing fills our hearts with so much gratitude,” said Perry. “After everything it took to get here, we can’t wait to meet our little boy.” Rusev recently made his return to WWE during a house show in Hawaii on October 16. He had been on the sidelines due to an unknown injury, which he suffered while wrestling Je’Von Evans back in July. title: Contract News: WWE Signs Former Sumo Wrestler and College Football Player to NXT Contract
raw_title: WWE Signs Former Sumo Wrestler and College Football Player to NXT Contract
summary_src: WWE has been keeping an eye on Hidetora Hanada for a while, and now things have apparently gotten a lot more serious. More than a year after he first got involved with the company, the 24-year-old Japanese athlete is taking the next step toward becoming an actual WWE Superstar.
body: According to PWInsider , WWE has signed Hanada to an NXT contract. The 6-foot-1, 280-pound prospect brings a pretty unusual résumé with him, having already competed in both sumo wrestling and American football before making the move into WWE. This is a big step up from where things stood back in February 2025. At the time, Hanada announced that he had received an offer through WWE’s NIL program while playing defensive line for Colorado State. He was also set to intern with WWE as part of his school curriculum, giving him a chance to see how the company operated behind the scenes. Hanada even got invited to the Royal Rumble in Indianapolis, and the experience clearly got his attention. He talked about being blown away by the atmosphere and how different WWE felt compared to football and sumo. “The crowd erupted with deafening cheers every time a star wrestler appeared. The sheer intensity and excitement of WWE were unlike anything I had ever experienced, completely different from football or sumo wrestling.” He was also fascinated by everything WWE handled behind the scenes, from cameras and sound to stage production and set design. “Experiencing this entirely new world firsthand, I am incredibly grateful to be involved with WWE, one of the highest levels of entertainment. I hope to learn a lot from this invaluable experience and apply it to my future endeavors!” Apparently that experience didn’t end with an internship. Hanada has a legit combat sports background from before his football days. He competed in sumo internationally in Japan in 2018 and Taiwan in 2019 before appearing at the 2022 World Games in Alabama. He transitioned into American football in 2022 and eventually played for Colorado State. Hanada also tried to take things further by pursuing an NFL opportunity, but he wasn’t selected following the tryout process. Now his next shot is coming inside WWE. Going from sumo to college football to WWE is already a pretty wild career path, and Hanada’s move from an NIL deal to an actual NXT contract shows the company saw enough during that process to keep him around. There’s no word yet on when he’ll make his NXT debut, so the next thing to watch is how quickly WWE can turn all that athletic experience into something that works inside a wrestling ring. What do you want to see from this talent once he eventually makes his way onto NXT television? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Bully Ray Praises WWE Raw Women's Division

summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray has great praise for the "Raw" women's division this week, especially Becky Lynch and Liv Morgan.
body: It's no secret that the "WWE NXT" women's division has long impressed WWE Hall of Famer Bully Ray. Coming out of this week's episode of "WWE Raw," though, the rising stars might now have some unexpected competition for his attention. On "Busted Open Radio," Ray heaped praise for the women wrestling on WWE's red brand, particularly the six given the spotlight during the October 26 broadcast. "For as long as I can remember now, I've been coming on this show and putting over the NXT women's division," Ray said. "Putting them over to the point where I've said that they are the best women's division in the WWE. I believe that they are the best women's division in all of wrestling. Those NXT women bust their a**, they perform. NXT does a great job of constantly turning over new quality female talent. But I'll be damned if the women on Monday Night Raw last night did not give those NXT women a run for their money and put on an amazing job last night." Monday night's episode of "Raw" took WWE to Fresno, California, where six women competed across three contests. The first pitted Lyra Valkyria against her former tag team partner Bayley in a No Disqualification Match, with "The Role Model" emerging victorious after making Valkyria tap out to a kendo stick-assisted crossface. The second saw WWE Women's Intercontinental Champion Raquel Rodriguez battle IYO SKY in a non-title bout. SKY picked up the win after reversing a Tejana Bomb into a roll-up. Slotted in the "Raw" main event was a title match between WWE Women's World Champion Liv Morgan and her challenger, Becky Lynch. This bout particularly amazed Ray as it pitted one of WWE's arguable all-time greats against a fast-improving champion. "I believe that since the Busted Open after Raw in Philadelphia, where Liv Morgan sat and said, 'Start watching as of tonight, because tonight everything changes for Liv Morgan.' We kind of had heard that song and dance before from Liv. Start, stop, start, stop, gas, breaks. But I'll be damned if from that day she has not stepped up her game every time she goes out there," Ray said. "And when Liv is in the ring with women who are technically better wrestlers than her, perception wise better wrestlers than her, she steps up to the plate and she delivers. There are some that consider Becky Lynch to be the best women's wrestler in the WWE. It's a discussion, but there's some who believe that. Well, Liv Morgan stood toe-to-toe and went blow-for-blow with Becky Lynch last night." Initially, plans called for Lynch to collide with Stephanie Vaquer in a number one contender's match. When "Raw" General Manager Adam Pearce later revealed that Vaquer was not medically cleared to compete , they pivoted to Morgan vs. Lynch for the championship in the show's main event. According to Ray, the chemistry between Morgan and Lynch was evident last night, and potentially better than what fans would have seen in the ring from Lynch and Vaquer.
