body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email 02:00 A look back at the legendary career of WWE Hall of Famer “Bullet” Bob Armstrong. Catch WWE action on WWE Network, FOX, USA Network, Sony India and more. WWE is saddened to learn that “Bullet” Bob Armstrong , a WWE Hall of Famer and patriarch of the legendary Armstrong wrestling family, has passed away at age 80. Equal parts strongman and showman, Armstrong, who was born Joseph James in Marietta, Ga., on Oct. 3, 1939, proved himself as one of the most tenacious grapplers on the planet during the territorial days of sports-entertainment. He secured his toughman reputation long before he ever set foot in the ring, thanks to his tour of duty in the U.S. Marine Corps and his seven-year tenure as a member of the Fair Oaks (later Cobb County) Fire Department. Armstrong, however, didn’t rest on his laurels when he was between the ropes. He handled himself well in the rough-and-tumble southeastern territories by employing an assortment of holds and moves, including his feared sleeper and Georgia Jawbreaker. He also possessed the gift of grappling gab, giving him the uncanny ability to wear down a rival with his words as well as with his strength. His chosen trade later became a family business, as Armstrong’s four sons — Joseph, aka Scott Armstrong, Brad, Steve and Brian, aka WWE Hall of Famer “Road Dogg” Jesse James — followed in their father’s footsteps. The Armstrong boys often found themselves in their dad’s corner, as “Bullet” Bob partnered with each of his sons at various points in a competitive career which spanned over six decades. For his part, Armstrong often credited his beloved wife, Gail, as the secret to his success. Upon being inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2011 , the self-proclaimed “ol’ war horse” also made the case that his many triumphs likely benefited from divine intervention, too. “I think somebody up there likes me,” Armstrong said during his 2011 WWE Hall of Fame induction speech. “I got to live my dream.” WWE extends its condolences to Armstrong’s family, friends and fans. title: Contract News: Who will take over from Bruce Prichard after WrestleMania 43? — Major WWE departure expected soon
raw_title: Major WWE departure expected soon: Who will take over from Bruce Prichard after WrestleMania 43?
body: A major WWE departure is reportedly expected to take place soon with the exit of company executive Bruce Prichard. Bruce Prichard currently serves as WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent – he is essentially the second man in creative behind Triple H . For example, when HHH is absent from a live show for whatever reason, Prichard is usually the man running it in his place. According to PWInsider , the expectation is that Prichard will retire from his role after WrestleMania 43 season next April, but will remain connected to WWE “on a consulting basis.” Despite that arrangement, he wouldn’t retain his current duties and he wouldn’t even live in Stamford near the company headquarters. One source said his time with WWE would end with WrestleMania itself, but another noted that the timeline could end up changing due to the nature of the wrestling business. Prichard was notably one of Vince McMahon’s top right hand men in a couple of separate stints with WWE, this one beginning in 2019 after a previous departure in 2008. Since Triple H took over leading creative from McMahon, Prichard has remained in his role but has long been described as one of the final remnants of the McMahon era . According to PWInsider, there’s no word yet on who will take over from Prichard when he leaves his current role. With the exit of Bruce Prichard, a spot will open up as Triple H’s new second in WWE creative, and there isn’t really an obvious replacement. The lead candidate would probably be Ed Koskey, who is currently WWE’s Senior Vice President of Creative, who works directly with Prichard. Koskey has been featured heavily on WWE Unreal as one of the faces of the creative team, and he essentially oversees the creative of both Raw and SmackDown. He has been with WWE since 2001, so as far as tenure and seniority in the current setup, it would seem like he’d be the most likely replacement as things stand right now. Other candidates include Raw lead writers Alexandra Williams and Jonathan Baeckstrom, and SmackDown lead writers John Swikata and Ryan Ward. There’s also a case to be made for current NXT head of creative Shawn Michaels , who has of course been so closely connected to Triple H throughout their careers, or perhaps Jeremy Borash, who has been running AAA creative alongside The Undertaker for the past year.
summary: The latest: a major WWE departure is by most accounts likely to take place soon with the exit of company executive Bruce Prichard. Bruce Prichard right now serves as WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent – he is essentially the second man in creative behind Triple H .

title: WWE Signs Athlete With Sumo and Football Background
raw_title: WWE’s New Signing Has a Background Few Wrestlers Can Match — Report
body: Skip to content Wrestling News Home » WWE’s New Signing Has a Background Few Wrestlers Can Match — Report WWE has reportedly signed another athlete with an unusual sporting background. Hidetora Hanada has taken the next step in his athletic career after competing in two very different sports. Hanada has taken an unusual path to WWE. His athletic career includes international sumo competitions, American college football, and an attempt to make it to the NFL. According to PWInsider , WWE has signed Hanada, who played college football for Colorado State University while continuing to compete in sumo wrestling. His signing comes into effect after he spent time building a relationship with WWE through its Name, Image, and Next in Line (NIL) program. Hanada first connected with WWE in 2025. He signed an NIL deal with the company in February that year. That gave him a chance to explore pro wrestling while completing his college sports commitments. In May 2025, Hanada visited WWE Headquarters in Stamford, Connecticut. He even shared the visit on social media after previously taking part in a WWE tryout. His college career ended in December 2025 when he graduated from Colorado State University. With his football commitments behind him, Hanada has now reportedly signed with WWE and is ready to begin a new chapter in sports entertainment. WWE has increasingly recruited athletes from outside pro wrestling lately. Hanada’s experience in both sumo wrestling and American football makes him an interesting addition. He has also competed internationally. Born in Japan, Hanada started competing in sumo during high school. He won gold medals at the Junior World Sumo Championships in both 2018 and 2019. He also won the All-Japan Championship during his freshman year at university. Hidetora Hanada went on to represent Japan at the 2018 World Championships in his home country and the 2019 competition in Taiwan. He later competed at the 2022 World Games in Alabama, where he won gold in the heavyweight division. Hanada left Japan to pursue American football in the United States. He joined Colorado State University and played defensive line for the Rams. He also tried to reach the NFL through the International Player Pathway program but did not secure a spot with a team. title: Five names who will make their first appearance in Japan — AEW stars to debut in NJPW
raw_title: AEW stars to debut in NJPW: Five names who will make their first appearance in Japan
body: Over the past few months, there has been several AEW stars who have been making their presence felt in New Japan Pro Wrestling. From Will Ospreay to Kenny Omega, these names have helped to put a significant spotlight on what’s going on in NJPW. As 2026 is winding down, there seems to be an increase in the number of AEW names making their way over to Japan to appear in the top promotion in the country. On the Road to King of Pro Wrestling, MJF shocked the world by sending a video message to Ryohei Oiwa. Challenging the G1 Climax 36 winner, Maxwell Jacob Friedman wants a battle of the headlocks against the TMDK member. While he was focused on his IWGP Heavyweight Title bout against Yota Tsuji at King of Pro Wrestling 2026, Oiwa has stated that he wants to shut MJF up. This should lead to MJF finally making his long awaited first appearance in Japan to square off with Oiwa sooner rather than later. In January 2026, Tommaso Ciampa signed with All Elite Wrestling and has become one of the most prominent stars on the roster. The former TNT Champion has gone on record several times to say that he would love to appear in NJPW. Ciampa is the kind of performer who should right at home in New Japan Pro Wrestling based on his style. “The Psycho Killer” arriving in NJPW would lead to some exciting matchups with the likes of Zack Sabre Jr., Hirooki Goto or Shota Umino. Another pair of new AEW stars who might make their first appearance in New Japan is The New Level . Debuting in AEW at All In London 2026, Kofi and Austin Creed have felt like a breath of fresh air to the roster. The New Level have brought their infectious energy to the AEW trios scene, but they could do the same in NJPW. Looking at the New Japan tag team picture, a duo like The Knockout Brothers or United Empire could make for ideal opponents for The New Level if they make the trip over to Japan to appear in NJPW. At AEW WrestleDream 2026, Ilja Dragunov made his official debut to the company as the newest signeee. “The Mad Dragon” has felt like one of the best free agent signings who has a tremendous upside in the promotion. During the WrestleDream post-show media scrum, Dragunov stated that he would love to make the trip to Japan and wrestle in the country. From Shingo Takagi to Boltin Oleg, there are some tantalizing matchups in store for Ilja Dragunov in New Japan Pro Wrestling. Another AEW star who has made it clear that he is keen to appear in NJPW is Adam Copeland . On the October 14 edition of AEW Dynamite and Collision, Copeland announced that 2027 will be his final year in pro wrestling. “The Rated R Superstar” recently revealed his desire to wrestle in one of the most famous buildings in the business, the Tokyo Dome. With NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 in the Dome this upcoming January, it would make sense if Cope was part of the card to check this legendary arena off his list before he officially retires. title: Injury Update: WWE Star Returns To Wrestling Seven Months After Shoulder Injury
raw_title: WWE Star Returns To Wrestling Seven Months After Shoulder Injury
body: 0 Elio LeFleur has finally returned to the ring after spending seven months out with a serious shoulder injury. The former WWE Men’s Speed Champion made his comeback before the October 27 episode of NXT aired. The injury came just when LeFleur was picking up the pace. This year, in February, he won the Men’s Speed Championship in a triple threat match against Jasper Troy and Eli Knight. The match lasted less than 90 seconds, with LeFleur picking up the win to claim his first WWE championship. However, his reign lasted only 34 days before the shoulder injury forced him to relinquish the title. On the March 31 episode of NXT, LeFleur appeared with his arm in a sling and announced he was vacating the championship. The injury also forced him to pull out of a tag team contender’s tournament alongside Eli Knight. According to False Finish , LeFleur wrestled in a dark match before the show went live. This was an important moment for the French luchador, who had been out of action since injuring his shoulder at an NXT live event in March 2026. LeFleur suffered the injury on March 20 during an NXT live event in Lakeland, Florida. He was competing in an eight-man tag team match when the injury happened. Doctors later diagnosed him with a torn labrum and damage to the ligaments in his shoulder. The injury required surgery, which he successfully underwent in early April. His recovery was expected to take around six months. However, LeFleur spent seven months away from the ring before returning on October 27. Although the match did not air on NXT, his return was an encouraging sign after such a long absence. It is yet to be seen when LeFleur will return to TV and resume regular competition on NXT. body: Link Marcus Benjamin has loved wrestling since his early days on the planet. He once Superkicked a tooth out of a friend’s mouth. Sweet Chin Music indeed. He’s analyzed and covered wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2021. All Good? I’m somewhat at a loss for words when it comes to this feud between Grayson Waller and Tony D’Angelo. Maybe after typing a few words, I’ll find my way to some semblance of a point. Then again, the story itself mirrors my current aimlessness. Geno called this creatively bankrupt and I agree. It started with Grayson visiting Tony’s home…and doing nothing. Just to play mind games. Tony showed up late, then the action moved to the Don’s old hangout: the restaurant. While I liked seeing the old place, it ended with the champ leaving a “note” for his challenger. That note, which he apparently wrote on parchment, instructed Tony to meet him where it all started. That meant the Performance Center where they treated us to a nice pull a part brawl but nothing else. Grayson is an agitator so I’m not surprised at him trying to get under Tony’s skin. This just seemed to piss him off more though, which is the opposite of what I assume he wants. There’s just nothing interesting here. I don’t know if it’s the talent, the story, or an unfortunate combination of both that’s falling flat. Tony and Grayson can mix it up in the ring but they both have a ceiling. And that ceiling doesn’t elevate them beyond mid-card guys. Tony’s Don persona had more personality. Grayon’s schtick hasn’t changed since he first left NXT. Both need revitalization but this story is doing them no favors. I can’t remember being less interested in a Men’s NXT Championship match. Meh. NXT is a very middle-of-the-road wrestling program. title: Sami Zayn Felt His WWE Title Window Had Closed
raw_title: Sami Zayn believed the time had passed for him to become WWE Champion
body: WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn previously believed that his opportunity to win a WWE Championship had passed him by when he didn’t beat Drew McIntyre for the title at the Royal Rumble PLE in January, but he did eventually capture his first WWE Championship at the Night of Champions in June. Zayn is now currently in the midst of his second reign with the WWE Undisputed Championship. “It’s cool,” said Zayne in response to a question from Chris Van Vliet on Insight about how it feels to be a champion in WWE. “Yeah, here’s the thing that’s funny about it because even at the start of this year, which was nine months ago, ten months ago now, whatever, I was wrestling Drew and I didn’t win. I had kind of just battled with it and went, you know what, maybe the ship sailed. I was real close a couple of years ago with all the Bloodline stuff and all that, and even in the fallout of that. Then I was close, but after losing that match, I was like, well, you can’t tell this story again. “Maybe it’ll happen in some different way, and it did happen in a bit of a different way. But the Cinderella story, underdog who finally wins the big one, we burnt that card. That card was done after losing to Drew because you can only tell that story so many times. You can get them on board once, twice, three times, and it wasn’t the right time. It wasn’t. I didn’t have the momentum that I had a year or two prior to that. But I had to kind of struggle to accept that maybe I just missed the window, slipped through the cracks, and it just won’t happen.” Zayn said he didn’t believe he had to win a WWE Championship to validate his career. “I’ve said this before in other interviews, or to friends, or my wife, or whatever,” said Zayn. “I’ve had a tremendous career and winning the world title at that point is just the cherry on top. It would be nice to have, but it’s not like if I never win it, it’s like I never got it. You know what I mean? You don’t live and die by these things. You kind of just got to look at the big picture.”
summary: Sami Zayn thought his chance to win the WWE Championship was gone after failing to defeat Drew McIntyre at the Royal Rumble in January. He went on to capture his first WWE Championship at Night of Champions in June and is now in his second reign as Undisputed Champion. Zayn shared these reflections in an interview with Chris Van Vliet.

title: Kelani Jordan Defends Controversial NXT Promo
raw_title: Kelani Jordan stands by controversial WWE NXT ‘fat a**es and catchphrases’ promo
summary_src: WWE NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan still stands by one of her controversial promos.
body: WWE NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan still stands by one of her controversial promos. Last year after winning her TNA Knockouts Championship, Jordan appeared on a live episode of NXT and delivered a controversial promo, where she addressed fans caring about women with “fat a**es and catchphrases” rather than their in-ring skills. Recently, speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Jordan was asked if she stands by those quotes, and without any hesitation, Jordan responded in the affirmative. “ Yes, that was one of the biggest turning points in my career and also the evolution of Kelani Jordan. So yes, I still stand by that because I think people sometimes forget about the talent that’s in the ring. “ They’re so drawn to other things, and I’m like, ‘Hello, the most elite athlete is literally standing right in front of you ,'” she said. “ And I think they forget. History maker, North American champion, TNA, now NXT Women’s Champion. I feel like sometimes they just tend to forget until I’m back in the ring again. “ I feel like a lot of times, when you’re all like rainbows and butterflies, people are like, ‘She’s so cute,’ but they don’t always take you seriously. I’m tired of being an underdog. I know what I bring to the table. I just think I needed to change something, and that’s when I changed. No more happy-go-lucky ,” Jordan finished. Jordan is currently scheduled to face Wren Sinclair at NXT Halloween Havoc 2026 for the women’s championship. title: John Cena Returns to WWE Raw Next Week
raw_title: John Cena Classic: Details Revealed for Upcoming Tournament as John Cena Returns to WWE Raw for 1st Time Since Retirement
body: Announced on Monday and further hyped up by the man himself, John Cena will be making his return to WWE Raw for the first time since his retirement this past December . Cena, who was also announced for next Wednesday's NXT (a show that just so happens to be going up against AEW due to WWE moving NXT off of Election Night on Tuesday), tweeted about his upcoming appearance , saying, "Make sure not to miss WWE Raw next week. SPECIAL START TIME OF 6 PM EST! The wait is over; the speculation ends 11/2. Let's build this 'Never Seen' CLASSIC. OUR time is NOW!" First announced in May at WWE Backlash, the John Cena Classic news caught people off guard and came with a mixed response , fitting given the reactions Cena garnered throughout his WWE career. Cena described the tournament without much detail, simply saying it would take place in December, feature present and future stars, and include a voting element. That seemed to be the part that confused a lot of people, as the voting would allow fans to choose a 'winner' of a match even if they didn't win. Essentially, making the tournament feel like a fan vote. Cena has offered some additional details over the last few months when pressed, including that his tournament would be largely non-canonical to existing WWE storylines. His most recent tweet with the language "the speculation ends" seems to suggest that Cena and WWE have figured out the specifics of this tournament and that they are ready to reveal those details to the fanbase. It seems that information such as the tournament's timeline, possible wrestlers taking part, and most importantly, the rules and specifics on how the voting will work (anybody else feel like this will be a Club WWE exclusive?) will be unveiled on Monday. Cena is set for a busy week as, in addition to his appearance on Raw on Monday, he'll be live for NXT on Wednesday. It seems like Cena's presence there will be to either introduce the NXT competitors in this tournament or set up a tournament to qualify for the John Cena Classic. It should also give some wrestlers a chance to bump shoulders with the 17-time champion and perhaps cause a little chaos in the process. Wednesday's NXT is a big one as it will also feature the finals of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic , where Cody Rhodes will present the winners with the trophy bearing his father's name. Up until this point, the John Cena Classic has felt hypothetical, as in, WWE could change their minds at any point, pull the tournament, and hope fans wouldn't even remember it existed in the first place. Well, come Monday, that hypothetical tournament becomes very real. The John Cena Classic will certainly be interesting if nothing else. WWE has utilized voting elements before, but that was for match types at events such as Taboo Tuesday. They've never forayed into voting on match outcomes and who advances from a match, hence why Cena is calling this a never-before-seen tournament. The voting is going to be both the most exciting a

title: Teams, Stakes & Matchup — Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic Final
raw_title: Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic Final: Teams, Stakes & Matchup
body: 0 The finalists for the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic have been confirmed after two semi-final matches on the October 27 episode of WWE NXT . The winners will receive the tournament trophy from Cody Rhodes . The final will take place on Wednesday, November 4, instead of the usual Tuesday night slot, due to election coverage. Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno will face Hank Walker and Tank Ledger in the finals of Dusty Rhodes Classic. In the semifinals, Dar and Moreno beat NXT Tag Team Champions Vanity Project. Meanwhile, Walker and Ledger defeated AAA World Tag Team Champions El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno. This week’s NXT episode opened with Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno taking on Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes of Vanity Project. Dar competed despite suffering a head injury during an untelevised NXT live event a few days earlier. Vanity Project looked to take advantage of Dar’s condition by keeping him away from Moreno. The champions also attacked Dar outside the ring. However, he managed to get back into the match and fired up after tagging in. He tried to catch Smokes off guard with a quick roll-up, but Baylor countered by dropping him neck-first across his knee. Despite the punishment, Dar kept fighting. The match then got chaotic as both teams accidentally took their own partners out of the action. Vanity Project eventually hit their signature Hit It and Quit It, but Moreno broke up the pin attempt before the match could end. Moreno and Dar then hit Smokes with a pair of spinning backfists. Dar followed up with the pinfall to eliminate the champions from the tournament. The second semi-final saw Hank & Tank face El Hijo de Dr. Wagner Jr. and Galeno for the other spot in the final. The AAA champions started strong. At one point, Galeno helped Wagner Jr. launch himself over the top rope to take out Walker and Ledger at ringside. Galeno continued to dominate with standing splashes on both members of the opposing team. However, Walker and Ledger eventually found an opening and hit a double-team move on Wagner Jr. Galeno had to break up the pin attempt to keep his team in the match. The AAA champions fought back with a moonsault from Wagner Jr., followed by a frog splash from Galeno. Ledger stopped the referee from counting to three, keeping his team’s hopes alive. Walker and Ledger then took control again. They hit Galeno with shoulder tackles before climbing to the top rope. Both men connected with simultaneous splashes on the AAA champion, allowing Ledger to score the winning pinfall. The final of Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic will see Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno take on Hank Walker and Tank Ledger. The winners will earn a future opportunity to challenge the NXT Tag Team Champions. title: Next TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions after Apex: Who could dethrone Shayna Baszler & Zoey Serrano?
raw_title: Next TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions after Apex: Who could dethrone Shayna Baszler & Zoey Serrano?
body: At TNA Bound For Glory 2026, Shayna Baszler made her debut to team with Zoey Serrano to defeat Allie and Kiera Hogan to win the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships. Baszler and Serrano have now since become the duo known as Apex in TNA Wrestling, While this reign should go on for some time, it is interesting to look at who might be able to dethrone Apex for the titles down the line. Here are three potential options to become the next TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions after Apex. The Elegance Brand have been one of the mainstays in the TNA Knockouts tag team division over the past two years. Heather and M By Elegance are former TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions and have remained a consistent fixture in the title scene. While there has been some tension as of late, winning back the gold might be the best way to rectify that. M By Elegance trying to become a double champion as the TNA Knockouts World TV Champion would be an intriguing direction to take The Elegance Brand. On the October 22 episode of TNA Thursday Night IMPACT, Kiera Hogan turned heel on Allie and reunited with Tasha Steelz in a beatdown. Hogan and Steelz, better known as Fire N’ Flava, were the first TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions when the titles were brought back in 2021. Now that they are back together, Tasha and Kiera should find themselves with an opportunity at regaining those titles. Fire N’ Flava have the experience and aggression to be placed in a position to become two-time TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Champions before long. While Allie was turned on by Kiera Hogan and attacked by Tasha Steelz on the October 22 TNA IMPACT, she did have some backup of her own. Shotzi Blackheart made her re-debut in TNA Wrestling by helping Allie from this attack from Fire N’ Flava. Since being released from WWE in 2025, Shotzi has been one of the busiest pro wrestlers in the business, appearing for various independent promotions all over the world. Shotzi and Allie could make for a formidable pairing and could find themselves in line for a shot at the TNA Knockouts World Tag Team Championships sometime soon. body: Read Time: 7 Minute, 31 Second World Wrestling Entertainment continues making headlines as major storylines develop across Raw, SmackDown, and upcoming premium live events. However, WWE faces questions beyond the wrestling ring as Crown Jewel approaches. Meanwhile, Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn, Cody Rhodes, and Randy Orton remain central figures in several important storylines. The women’s division also continues generating excitement, especially following Monday night’s dramatic episode of Raw. Additionally, backstage rumors suggest WWE has significant plans for Survivor Series: Wargames and several emerging superstars. Here is the latest WWE news, confirmed developments, and reported rumors heading into November. WWE’s upcoming Crown Jewel event has become one of the biggest stories surrounding the company. The premium live event has plans to take place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. However, recent reports have raised questions about security concerns and potential disruptions. According to PWInsider, preparations for Crown Jewel have begun despite concerns surrounding regional security. Furthermore, WrestleVotes reportedly described considerable uncertainty within WWE regarding the event’s future. Reports have mentioned potential airport threats and airspace restrictions that could complicate travel arrangements. Nevertheless, WWE has not confirmed a cancellation or relocation. title: NXT Delivers Mixed Bag Before Halloween Havoc
raw_title: WWE NXT - 10/27/2026: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
summary_src: Everything we loved, and everything we very much didn't, from this week's edition of "WWE NXT."
body: WWE The "WWE NXT" ship sailed on. Halloween Havoc is just on the horizon, and beyond the horizon, Wednesday's Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic Finals. Before all that though, there was the pressing matter of Jackson Drake defending the North American Title against EK Prosper. You can read all about it over on the WWE NXT 10/27/2026 Live Blog. But enough bloviating, let's get to the best and the worst of the pre-Halloween Havoc edition of "WWE NXT." WWE As a child of the Attitude Era, I have an affinity for wild brawls in pre-recorded segments in areas outside of areas, where the babyface and heel face off and it feels ever-so-slightly ridiculous. I thought that may have been the case here tonight, but instead, NXT Champion Grayson Waller sent his Halloween Havoc challenger, Tony D'Angelo, off on a wild goose chase. A wild goose chase that ultimately ended right back at the WWE Performance Center with just two minutes to spare in the show. I thought we were off to a good start when Waller posted a video that played on the broadcast in the corner during the middle of a match, giving this a major sense of urgency that he was headed to D'Angelo's home. I didn't expect any craziness at the level of, say, AEW's Swerve Strickland and "Hangman" Adam Page, but I at least thought it would be interesting. Seeing the video sent D'Angelo into a rage, and he left the PC to seemingly go defend his family against Waller, but when he showed up, the champion wasn't even there, and it didn't appear like he ever went inside. The story then took us to what I believe was the same restaurant "NXT" filmed the D'Angelo Family segments in, which was a nice touch. That's absolutely where a ridiculous, glass-smashing, pasta-throwing brawl could have taken place that would have been much more interesting. But, no, Waller just left him a paper telling him to "meet where it all began." Even Booker T commented that Waller was just sending D'Angelo on a scavenger hunt at that point. "Where it all began" meant the Performance Center, which I thought was pretty lame. Waller cut a promo on D'Angelo in the ring, and the challenger rolled up in his truck, and Waller stormed out to the parking lot for a brawl, with just a minute or two left in the show. It was all very much same old, same old, with security trying to separate them. Not a single meatball or wine glass to be thrown, a complete missed opportunity. It feels like WWE just refuses to go the extra mile anymore, and "NXT" is usually the show that gets to do that. This seemed very half-thought-out, and I hated it because there was an opportunity to make this feel a little more fun and unique, and borderline ridiculous would have been just fine before Halloween Havoc. Shiloh Hill/X Shiloh Hill is a deeply weird individual. I almost wonder if he is simply too different for this antiseptic era of wrestling. Too weird to live, too rare to die, and definitely too creative to be stuck in "WWE NXT." As long as he's stuck here, though, I

title: Tony D'Angelo Says NXT Roster Inexperience Hurt His Title Run
raw_title: Tony D’Angelo says inexperienced NXT roster affected his championship reign
summary_src: Tony D’Angelo has opened up about his WWE NXT Championship reign. Recently, speaking to Denise Salcedo, former champion D’Angelo opened up about his NXT title reign, where he claimed that the roster’s inexperience affected his run, since he did not have a lot of people to work with.
body: Tony D’Angelo has opened up about his WWE NXT Championship reign. Recently, speaking to Denise Salcedo , former champion D’Angelo opened up about his NXT title reign , where he claimed that the roster’s inexperience affected his run, since he did not have a lot of people to work with. “ I didn’t have a whole lot to work with, so to speak. A lot of people with inexperience, which is not their fault. They, as in the main roster, took a bunch of people, and those were all the people that had experience and had been in main events and long matches and knew how, you know, their promos were tip-top ,” Angelo said. D’Angelo believes that had he been the champion in a different era, people would have talked differently about his run. “ I think had I been champion in a different era, I think people would talk differently about it for sure, but I’m not offended. It is what it is. “ I think I still showed that I can be champion and carry a brand, and it was a difficult time because, like Shawn [Michaels] said, everybody left. So I held it together when we were in this little transition period. And I’m okay with that. I really am ,” he finished. D’Angelo is now scheduled to face Grayson Waller at Halloween Havoc 2026 for the WWE NXT Championship. title: WWE Plans Live Events in Maine Before Crown Jewel
raw_title: Note On WWE Live Event Plans Ahead of Crown Jewel
body: WWE has a few live events scheduled for next week after leaving for Crown Jewel, and a new report has a bit of detail on the plans for them. As noted , the company is taping both Raw and Smackdown next Monday so they can leave for Crown Jewel after. However, they also have live events scheduled for Portland, Maine on September 5th and Bangor, Maine on September 6th. Fightful Select reports that while (obviously) Crown Jewel has priority, the plan as of now is to still have a decent roster of talent for the live events. There are a number of major stars not scheduled for Crown Jewel as of now, which currently has four matches announced in Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn, Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green, Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton, and The Vision vs. Penta and Je’Von Evans. The report also notes that in addition to the live events, main roster talkent are likely to make “cameos” on upcoming NXT live events. Details on which talent and which shows were not specified. WWE Crown Jewel takes place on November 7th in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia from Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD. It will air live on ESPN Unlimited in the US and on Netflix internationally.

body: (1) ROMEO MORENO & NOAM DAR vs. THE VANITY PROJECT (Brad Baylor & Ricky Smokes) – Dusty Classic semifinal match Moreno got bumped to the floor immediately. Dar had his head taped up from an injury suffered at the hands of VP during a live event this weekend, so the baked-in story was that the Vanity Project would be focused on it. Dar took a few bumps but was able to make the tag, and Moreno took over on offense. Breaking news: apparently, next week’s show is on Wednesday (which likely means a non-live post-show for us since our host doesn’t work properly when two shows are attempted at once). The finals will be on that show, so my month-long assumption that the finals would be wrestled on Halloween Havoc because of the perfect timing is out the window. Dar sold on the outside as Moreno checked on him as the match went to split-screen. [c] Baylor had Moreno downed. In an inset promo, Grayson Waller was filming a selfie video outside of Tony D’Angelo’s house. He said he was going to see if anyone was home. Messing with family is the new NXT way, it would seem. Dar made the hot tag and got a rollup on Smokes for two. He threw kicks at Smokes, and when he covered up, he went with a European uppercut. Dar covered again for two. Moreno tagged in for a double suplex and a cover for two. Moreno set up Smokes on the babyface corner and tagged Dar, but Smokes raked the now-exposed injured forehead and ran for the tag. Baylor ran himself right into an armbar for two. Somewhere I missed some blood, because the ref had his gloves on. VP slowed it down and double-teamed but Moreno neutralized the illegal man, allowing Dar to catch Baylor in an ankle-lock. Everyone got involved for a mess of activity for about thirty seconds, ending in a jawbreaker by Baylor on Dar. VP set up an assisted spike piledriver for a long two, broken up by Moreno. All four ended up in the ring again, but Moreno and Baylor bumped to the floor, where Moreno hit a suplex on the mat outside. Dar caught Smokes in a leg submission and they rolled outside. Myka Lockwood tried to get involved but couldn’t convert. Both men tagged. Moreno hit a missile dropkick, then took Baylor up in a corner. He hit a cutter from above as Dar hit one on Smokes inside the ring also. VP double-teamed on offense but Moreno countered and Smokes ended up hitting Baylor from above. Dar tagged in and he and Moreno hit high-low to beat the champions and move on to the finals. I know that’s the NXT way, but it doesn’t have to be. title: AEW Rising and Fading Stars: Nick Wayne, Blood & Guts, Davis & Doyle
raw_title: AEW RISING AND FADING STARS: Kline’s slotting of what’s going on with Nick Wayne, Women’s Blood & Guts, Davis & Doyle, Marina Shafir
body: Another week of AEW television is in the books. We had the debut of Ilija Dragunov with vignettes hyping his match debut. Honestly, it felt like they put more into his match debut than a lot of other Dynamite main events. I’m pretty sure there have been title matches in the main event slot that got less build throughout Dynamite. For me, his debut was fine. It should have been at the top of the second hour but it was fine. Let me rant for a second. I don’t get why the Will Ospreay tag match was not in the main event? Then you end it the same way with Steve Borden throwing out the Blood and Guts challenge to end the show. Let’s look back at who I felt shined and who did not as much. Well, that was a fun way to set up the next AEW World Tag Title opponents for the (not so) Young Bucks. Having watched wrestling for a long, long, time this also made me like the Bucks even more. In the ’90s trying to get a main event caliber team to do what the Bucks did would have been difficult. With Davis & Doyle, they are different from almost every other featured tag team. They are big and bad men who can dominate and make it look real. Doyle especially looks like a guy you could have swapped with a Hercules Hernandez and Doyle becomes the Power part of Power & Glory. Both showed up in AEW with very little fanfare but have proven why they are a good signing. Injuries aside, both have done well for themselves, especially Davis. I am excited to see if they pull the trigger on a Davis & Doyle title win. With the story they are telling about the broken down Bucks, it works. If Davis & Doyle win, the first team I would have them beat is the other two big guy team, The Hurt Syndicate. Wow, was I amused by Wayne last week. The smugness, the T-shirt, the pyro, I loved it all! To me this is the foundation, finally, being poured on a future main event guy. Wayne has some over-emoting issues while on promos, almost like he was in theatre where you are taught to emote to the person in the last row. I think works for him while he is wrestling, but it’s a bit much on promos. I think it can and will be fixed with time. Other than a Je’Von Evans and Leon Slater, who is a more impressive early-20s wrestler on a national wrestling show? The three of them are the potential future. Marina has quietly become a well-protected female star in AEW. She doesn’t wrestle that much, but when she does there seems to always be a story around it. Marina isn’t in random matches on Dynamite (hint hint, Will Ospreay), so her coming out to challenge Mercedes didn’t feel above Marina at all and it could have. Mercedes Mone should also be included in this because of how she acted during their interaction. When the Death Riders music hit, I loved how the camera stayed on her and you could read her lips when she dropped the f-bomb. She was not happy at all and it was great. This won’t be a Match of the Year type of match, but I think it will be different from a typical Mercedes match. Well, other than

title: Myles Borne vs Tavion Heights Set for Weapons Wild at NXT Halloween Havoc
raw_title: Myles Borne vs. Tavion Heights Set for Weapons Wild Match at NXT Halloween Havoc
body: Their rivalry took another turn on the October 27 episode of NXT , when a heated confrontation left the final stipulation in the hands of a spinning wheel. The former tag team partners exchanged accusations inside the ring, with security stepping in before their verbal battle turned into a fight. However, the intervention only delayed the inevitable as the animosity between them continued to grow. Borne accused Heights of holding him back, claiming that his former partner had leached onto him before he lost everything in 2026. Heights fired back by suggesting Borne had lost sight of who he really was and was now trying to shift the blame. The former Olympian also made it clear that Borne's betrayal at NXT Heatwave had changed his outlook. Heights described himself as a "weapon in human form" and the "God of suplexes," promising to thrive when the pressure is highest. As security struggled to keep the rivals apart, Danhausen's laugh echoed through the WWE Performance Center. The Halloween Havoc host then had his druids spin the "Spin the Wheel, Make a Deal" wheel to determine the match stipulation. The wheel landed on Weapons Wild, confirming that Borne and Heights will face off in a hardcore-style contest featuring weapons around the ring. Although the match has no disqualifications, competitors can win only through pinfall or submission inside the ring. The stipulation adds another layer to a feud rooted in betrayal and broken trust. With both men eager to prove their point, the rivalry is set to move beyond words — and there will be plenty of hardware around to make their argument. NXT Halloween Havoc takes place on October 31 at the WWE Performance Center. Borne and Heights will join a card that also features Kelani Jordan defending the NXT Women's Championship against Wren Sinclair, Grayson Waller facing Tony D'Angelo, Zaria taking on Izzi Dame, and Shiloh Hill battling Naraku. The post Myles Borne vs. Tavion Heights Set for Weapons Wild Match at NXT Halloween Havoc appeared first on Wrestlezone .

body: WWE Hall of Famer Booker T recently recalled threatening to fight Fit Finlay over a stiff kick. Booker T recalled that during his time, Finlay was a stiff worker, which he didn’t mind. However, once Finlay had kicked him painfully near the kidneys, following which he had confronted the Irish wrestler. The former World Champion says he warned Finlay that if he ever happened again, it would lead to fight. And it never happened again. “ I didn’t mind stiff, but I needed safe at the same time. And I remember working a match with Fit Finlay, and he snapped me and kicked me in the back, but he caught me in the kidney area. Man, it really hurt, man. It really, really hurt ,” he said. Booker T emphasized while he accepted stiff wrestling, he wanted it to be safe. “ I remember telling him when he came back through the curtain, I said, ‘Bro, kick me like that again, we’re going to be fighting next time when you come back through the curtain.’ But that never happened. Never happened again. But, you know, I get it. I get it. I stiffed a lot of guys ,” he finished. Fit Finlay and Booker T have faced each other multiple times both in singles and multi man matches, both across WWE and WCW. title: Bruce Prichard Needs Serious Surgery, To Work From Home
raw_title: More On Bruce Prichard Reportedly Stepping Back From WWE Role Next Year
body: A new report has some additional context on the report Bruce Prichard is stepping away from his role in WWE next year. As noted , PWInsider reported on Tuesday evening that Prichard is expected to retire from his role as Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent, likely after WrestleMania 43. The report noted that Prichard would remain part of WWE in a consulting basis, but would no longer live in Stamford. Fightful Select has some additional context from the matter. The outlet reports that according to sources familiar with the matter, Prichard would still be part of WWE (as PWInsider noted) but would be working from home much more. The report goes on to say that the WWE executive needs a “very serious” surgery done that would result in his coming off the road and working from home. It was also noted that Prichard has already been not feeling well physically but has remained on the road, including filling in for Triple H in terms of running shows the last couple of weeks while the WWE CCO was on vacation. An internal memo said to have been sent earlier this year within WWE about Prichard’s status, but there’s no word on the details of the memo. The report also points out that Prichard working from home could lead to a return on Something to Wrestle, which he hosted with Conrad Thompson, but that those conversations have not happened as of now. Thompson spoke with Fightful last week and was asked about the potential of Prichard to return to the podcast, which is now hosted by Thompson and JBL. Thompson had noted that “I’m sure if and when the time is right and he is no longer living in Stamford, then then we’ll be able to figure something out. But I think that’s going to be the foreseeable future for a little while.”
summary: Per Fightful Select, Bruce Prichard is expected to step back from his full-time WWE Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent duties next year after WrestleMania 43 due to needing a very serious surgery. The report states he will remain with the company on a consulting basis while working from home more often and no longer living in Stamford. Prichard has continued working on the road despite not feeling well physically, recently filling in for Triple H to run shows.

title: Match Made: Some questions about Pearce’s decision to make Sami defend his tilte, Sami vs. Evans, Bayley vs. Valkyria, Bloodline-946 follow-up — WWE RAW HITS & MISSES (10/26)
raw_title: WWE RAW HITS & MISSES (10/26): Some questions about Pearce’s decision to make Sami defend his tilte, Sami vs. Evans, Bayley vs. Valkyria, Bloodline-946 follow-up
body: Opening Segment – HIT: Raw got off to a good start with Sami Zayn interrupting GM Adam Pearce to get some stuff off his chest. Zayn was good in his unhinged rant, but it did go on a little too long. Je’von Evans was also good in his interruption. This set up Pearce making an impromptu WWE Title match which was nice for the fans, but doesn’t make much sense. Why does Zayn have to defend his title multiple times a week, but Roman Reigns only defends his every few months? Earlier this year, why didn’t Pearce make Liv Morgan defend her World Title for months? How does he have the authority to make a WWE Title match on Raw when that title “belongs” to Smackdown? You don’t want a heel to have actual things to complain about that make sense, like having to defend a title multiple times in a week. So, I’ll call this a minor Hit. Zayn vs. Evans – HIT: I won’t complain too much about this match being made in an illogical way, because it was a good match. I suspect that it will end up better than Zayn’s defense against Trick Williams will be on Smackdown, but time will tell. WWE isn’t going to take the title off of Zayn before Crown Jewel, so the outcome was never in doubt, but they still had a good match with some fairly believable near falls. The bit of a distraction with Penta and Bron Breakker at ringside worked well enough to help Zayn get the win. The post-match beating with The Vision destroying both Penta and Evans worked very well to set up the WWE Tag Team Championship match at the PLE. The Vision comes across as so much more intimidating and strong as a faction when Austin Theory and Maxxine Dupri aren’t there. Bayley vs. Valkyria – HIT: This was the best match of the night. It was a fitting end (presumably) to the long feud between Bayley and Lyra Valkyria. These two beat the crap out of each other. There were several multiple memorable spots, the most memorable of which was when Bayley leaped through the ropes, crashing into Valkyria through the table. They seemed to find a way to use just about every weapon that ever gets used in a WWE no disqualification match. It was physical, intense, and fun to watch from start to finish. Bayley got the win, which will push Valkyria further into the abyss. I’m curious to see what they have planned for both of them going forward. Sky vs. Rodriguez – HIT: Iyo Sky continues to be the best babyface in WWE. She is a great performer in and out of the ring. The fans are consistently behind her. She was able to overcome Raquel Rodriguez’s huge size advantage to get the win in the end. This should set up Sky for a future Intercontinental Championship match. Follow up on 946-Bloodline – MISS: Last week’s show ended with a huge angle with The Bloodline coming together with Roman Reigns leading them to finally get the better of The 946. summary_src: Uncertainty continues to surround next weekend’s WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh amid ongoing security concerns.
body: Uncertainty continues to surround next weekend’s WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh amid ongoing security concerns. So far, four matches have been confirmed for the PLE: Roman Reigns takes on Sami Zayn and Chelsea Green collides with Liv Morgan in separate Crown Jewel title match plus Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton look to settle their score in a Last Man Standing match while the WWE World Tag Team titles will also be defended following The Vision’s explosive interaction with Je’Von Evans and Penta on Monday’s Raw. With just over a week remaining before Crown Jewel, WWE could still have a few surprises in store. From potential title changes to major returns and rivalries reaching a boiling point, here are some matches and events that could take place at the PLE. Following last week’s events on Raw involving The Bloodline and 946, Sikoa reunited with The Bloodline. Additionally, he cut a promo with The Bloodline by his side on Monday’s Raw, accepting Royce Keys’ challenge for a singles match next week. Leading up to Money in the Bank, Knight acknowledged Sikoa’s efforts in standing up to Reigns and The Usos. The two already have a shared history given their rivalry which was briefly sidelined with a common disdain for The Bloodline. Their past conflicts provide WWE with a natural storyline to revisit, especially if Knight views Sikoa’s reunion as another betrayal that cannot go unanswered. Knight’s popularity among the fans, on display going into his recent Money in the Bank World Title match against Reigns, could see him being added to Crown Jewel. This time he confronts Sikoa for going back on his intentions, setting up a singles match between the two. Rollins’ absence since SummerSlam has left a significant gap with fans waiting to see when the former World Heavyweight Champion will make his return. However, Rollins has continued to compete at WWE live events, teaming up with LA Knight and Solo Sikoa against 946, leaving the door open for his comeback to play a major role in the ongoing storylines. His potential comeback at Crown Jewel could have major implications on two feuds: the ongoing tension with The Vision or joining 946 in their vendetta against The Bloodline (more on that below). The most compelling option would be for Rollins to return by targeting The Vision, especially given the unfinished business between he and Breakker. Such an angle would give his comeback immediate direction while laying the groundwork for a major feud in the weeks ahead. Regardless of which direction WWE chooses, Crown Jewel offers a high-profile opportunity to bring Rollins back into the spotlight. His eventual return to television is long overdue, with reports suggesting WWE is waiting for the right time to bring him back. title: John Cena Is Coming to WWE NXT & Fans Won’t Want To Miss It
raw_title: John Cena Is Coming to WWE NXT & Fans Won’t Want To Miss It
body: 0 John Cena is adding another stop to his WWE schedule. The former Undisputed WWE Champion is set to appear on an upcoming episode of NXT. The announcement comes as his long-awaited plans for a special tournament begin to take shape, leaving fans with more than one reason to tune in. During the October 27 episode of WWE NXT on The CW, commentary confirmed that Cena would appear live at the WWE Performance Center on Wednesday, November 4. The appearance comes just two days after his scheduled return to RAW on November 2. Cena has been teasing details about the John Cena Classic, a tournament he first announced at WWE Backlash in May. The concept will bring together talent from NXT and WWE’s main roster. Interestingly, fans play a major role in deciding who earns the distinction of becoming the tournament’s standout competitor. Cena fuelled the tease on X , writing, “The wait is over, the speculation ends 11/2. Let’s build this ‘Never Seen’ CLASSIC! OUR time is NOW!” He has promised to provide answers during his upcoming RAW appearance. His subsequent NXT appearance could offer another opportunity to explain how the tournament will work. Nevertheless, WWE has not confirmed what he will announce on either show. The John Cena Classic is currently targeted for December. However, WWE has yet to reveal its official date, location, or broadcast platform. The proposed championship format will also allow fan voting to influence the outcome, potentially giving participants a chance to earn the title without winning their individual matches. Cena won’t be the only attraction on the November 4 NXT broadcast. The show will feature the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic finals, with Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno facing Hank Walker and Tank Ledger. Cody Rhodes is scheduled to present the trophy to the winners, while Cruz Montana and Dion Lennox will compete in an unsanctioned match. With Cena’s return and major tournament business on the agenda, NXT looks set for a busy night — and fans may finally get a clearer picture of the Classic. Netflix revealed its weekly top 10 on Tuesday for the week ending October 25th, and the October 19th episode of Raw ranked at #9 with 2.5 million views based on 4.3 million hours viewed. This week’s show was steady with the October 12th episode’s 2.5 million views. body: Oh, to have WrestleMania 34's mixed tag-team match back again . That captured lightning in a bottle. Ex-UFC mauler Ronda Rousey looked like the second coming of Kurt Angle when she teamed with the Olympian vs. Triple H and Stephanie McMahon whilst making this pro wrestling malarkey look like a breeze. People got proper excited about Ronda's potential after that, and a singles run followed. Throughout it all, Rousey wore a kilt in honour of Roddy Piper, and even assumed his 'Rowdy' nickname. On comms, announcers told how Piper had passed his gimmick down to the MMA star. So much for that once the honeymoon period of Rousey in WWE wore off. WWE's audience never got in step with the idea that Ronda was Piper's echo in the company. After all, they weren't really anything alike; Roddy had been a silver-tongued devil on the microphone, and he was pure chaos inside the ring. Conversely, Rousey was nervy, stumbled over her words and was controlled during matches. Ultimately, Ronda never had the right attitude for wrestling. She didn't appreciate it when fans booed her (another point at odds with the Piper comparison when he'd embraced any reaction and ran with it), and that caused major rifts. Nothing about Rousey's presentation screamed Roddy either. It never did even when she was wearing the kilt, 'Rowdy' t-shirt and leather jacket. This was somebody who needed no-frills presentation cosplaying as a great for cheap brownie points. It was so see through whether they were actually good friends before the legend's passing or not. body: Some additional details have been reported on the rumor that Vince Russo had some talks about a possible WWE return earlier this year. Conrad Thompson reported on Tuesday that he had “heard” that Russo had discussions with WWE President Nick Khan during the summer about a possible return to the company. However, he said when he followed up a couple of weeks ago, he was told that the possibility of a Russo return “died on the vine.” Fightful Select has reported that sources at WWE Headquarters did say to them that Russo had conversations with Nick Khan, and that Russo was either at WWE HQ at some point or considered to visit there. However, there’s no word on how serious the conversations between Khan and Russo were. The report also notes that word of Russo and Khan talking did not make it much further and that none of the agents, producers, writers, or staff who are on the road had heard about it. Fightful notes some “influential names” laughed the idea off and that some people who work closely with Khan said it was never brought up to them. Russo himself has not yet commented on the matter — but don’t worry, he probably will soon enough.
summary: Conrad Thompson reported hearing that Vince Russo had discussions with WWE President Nick Khan during the summer regarding a possible return. Per Fightful Select, sources confirmed the conversations took place and Russo was either at WWE Headquarters or considered visiting. The possibility ultimately went nowhere, with the news not reaching most WWE staff, agents, producers or writers, and some influential figures dismissed the idea.

title: End of an Era: Huge Creative Changes Coming To WWE As Top Executive Set To RETIRE! (WWE News)
raw_title: Huge Creative Changes Coming To WWE As Top Executive Set To RETIRE! (WWE News)
body: Long-time WWE man Bruce Prichard is reportedly getting set to step away from the company. First reported by Mike Johnson over at PWInsider , Prichard is expected to retire from his position as Executive Director - Creative Writing & Talent (CWT) once WrestleMania 43 is done. Johnson notes that Bruce will remain "connected" to the company on a consultancy basis, but he would no longer retain his current duties and would no longer be based in Stamford, Connecticut. On this topic, Fightful Select adds that Bruce Prichard needs a "very serious" surgery, and that, post-WrestleMania 43, he'll still be doing work for WWE, but will be working from home. Fightful also points out that Prichard filled in for Triple H in running shows during the past few weeks while the Game was on vacation, and that an internal memo about Bruce's status was sent out earlier this year, though the details of that memo were not made public. Additionally, False Finish believes that situations such as the retirement of Bruce Prichard in a full-time role are something that will be happening "quite a bit" in the coming years, with WWE heading in a new direction and "currently contracted talent" expected to transition over to roles behind the scenes and in the office. The 63-year-old Prichard has been in the wrestling business dating all the way back to 1973, when he started selling posters for Paul Boesch's Houston Wrestling at just 10 years of age. The young Bruce would eventually start ring announcing and helping out with TV production for Boesch, and would also work for Bill Watts' UWF before landing in the then-WWF in 1987. By the summer of 1988, Prichard debuted his Brother Love character and The Brother Love Show, and would even be the Undertaker's first manager when the Phenom arrived at the 1990 Survivor Series. Bruce has had several spells with WWE over the decades, initially leaving shortly after that '91 Survivor Series, returning the following year and staying with the promotion until 2008, and then later returning in 2018 for the run he's currently on. In addition to working in various backstage roles for WWE, Prichard has also worked for the likes of TNA and MLW, and, of course, launched his hugely successful Something to Wrestle With podcast with Conrad Thompson - though commitments have meant that JBL has filled in alongside Conrad in recent times. body: While his Something to Wrestle With co-founder Bruce Prichard is reportedly getting ready to wind down his full-time days with WWE , Conrad Thompson has made quite the bold claim about one of the most opinion-splitting names in pro wrestling history. Writing in his new Conrad's Corner column over at Yahoo! Sports , Thompson says that Vince Russo held talks over a sensational WWE return this summer, and that Vinny Ru had a "series of conversations" with WWE President Nick Khan. However, when Conrad followed up on this topic several weeks ago, he was told that a potential Russo return had "died on the vine". Additionally, Fightful Select notes that, per a source familiar with this situation, Vince Russo either visited WWE HQ at one point, or he was at least "under consideration" for a visit there. This report notes that any Russo news did not make it to the wider WWE staff, and that no agents, producers, or writers on the road had heard about it, though some "influential names" laughed off the idea of a return for the former WCW World Heavyweight Champion. Vince Russo first joined the then-WWF back in 1992, initially serving as a freelance writer for WWF Magazine and becoming the editor of said mag two years later using the Vic Venom pseudonym. Once 1996 rolled around, and with the company in dire need of a creative refresh, Russo was brought onto the creative team. Pulling plenty from the Jerry Springer-style car-crash TV of the time, Russo - who'd become head writer in 1997 - played a major part in making the WWF product edgier, delivering more controversial segments and storylines, amping up the violence, profanity, sexual tone, and speed-running through character turns and swerves. October 1999 would see Vince Russo make the big jump to WCW after Ted Turner's promotion looked to turn the tide of the Monday Night Wars, though Russo would leave WCW as soon as January 2000, only to then return in March of that year. Now an on-screen character, skip ahead to July 2000 and we got the infamous Bash at the Beach PPV , where an awkward worked-shoot situation between Russo and Hulk Hogan led to a lawsuit and to Hogan never again stepping foot in a WCW ring. And by September 2000, Russo had become the WCW World Heavyweight Champion, winning that belt in a steel cage match against Booker T. Remaining with WCW until it was purchased by Vince McMahon in 2001, Vince Russo would have an uber-brief WWE return in 2002, where he was to serve as a consultant, before the New Yorker opted to take a gig with TNA instead. Russo would work for TNA on and off until 2014, and he most recently served as a writer, investor, and on-screen character for Juggalo Championship Wrestling, though his JCW exit was confirmed last month. title: TNA Wrestling on Sport1 — Germany
raw_title: Germany: TNA Wrestling on Sport1
body: Anthem Sports & Entertainment has announced a new broadcast partnership between TNA Wrestling and Sport1, bringing the promotion’s weekly flagship series Thursday Night iMPACT! to viewers throughout Germany. Starting on November 3rd, Sport1 will feature German-language broadcasts of the Thursday Night iMPACT! , with commentary and localisation, while showcasing TNA’s roster of pro wrestling stars. This move is a further continuation of the platform’s global expansion initiative, focused on increasing TNA’s television presence across Europe and around the world. Andreas Gerhardt, Chief Content & Distribution Officer of Sport1, commented: “Professional wrestling has a passionate and established fanbase in Germany, and we are pleased to welcome TNA Wrestling to Spoer1. TNA combines compelling personalities, athletic competition and entertaining storytelling, and we look forward to introducing its weekly programming to our audience.” Carlos Silva, President, TNA Wrestling and Anthem Sports Group, added: “Germany has always been an important market—both for professional wrestling and TNA, in particular. We are excited to join forces with Sport1 to bring TNA content back to fans across the country. Sport1 has firmly established itself as a major platform in sports and sports entertainment, making them an ideal partner as we continue expanding TNA’s international presence. We look forward to giving German fans a consistent destination to experience TNA every week.” The SPORT1 partnership comes on the heels of significant growth and momentum for TNA Wrestling. Since launching its US TV partnership with AMC Global Media, Thursday Night iMPACT! has delivered multiple ratings increases, while TNA’s collaboration with WWE continues to bring talent from both companies together across their respective programmes. TNA has also expanded its global distribution and direct-to-consumer offerings, reaching fans in 200 countries and engaging more than 26 million social media followers. TNA’s current roster includes World Champion Leon Slater and World Tag Team champions Nic Nemeth & Ryan Nemeth, along with names such as Jeff Hardy, Indi Hartwell, Moose, Mustafa Ali, Matt Hardy, Cedric Alexander, Santino Marella, Erick Redbeard, Kiera Hogan and many more.
summary: Anthem Sports & Entertainment has revealed a new broadcast partnership between TNA Wrestling and Sport1, bringing the promotion’s weekly flagship series Thursday Night iMPACT! to viewers throughout Germany. Starting on November 3rd, Sport1 will feature German-language broadcasts of the Thursday Night iMPACT! , with commentary and localisation, while showcasing TNA’s roster of pro wrestling stars.

title: Callum Newman Reveals Shoulder Pop During G1 Match With Aaron Wolf
raw_title: Callum Newman Says His Shoulder 'Popped' In G1 Bout Against Aaron Wolf
summary_src: Callum Newman suffered a shoulder injury at NJPW Dominion, going into the annual G1 Climax tournament with what he said was a dislocated shoulder. Newman still competed in every match of the tournament, making it to the semifinals before losing to Ryohei Oiwa.
body: Callum Newman suffered a shoulder injury at NJPW Dominion, going into the annual G1 Climax tournament with what he said was a dislocated shoulder. Newman still competed in every match of the tournament, making it to the semifinals before losing to Ryohei Oiwa. In his seventh match of the tournament, he faced Aaron Wolf, and says his shoulder popped. “The match before (the semifinal against Oiwa) I got put through a table, and before that, with Aaron Wolf, my shoulder went again,” he said while speaking to NJPW . He continued, “He gave me one of those judo throws and it popped- not popped out but I felt it move and then I felt this bolt of electricity down my arm. So that was concerning, and then sure enough, Oiwa is one of the best at throwing armdrags and using arm holds. I’d have much rather somebody who wrestles like I do, someone that runs and throws a lot of kicks. Smart, I guess.” Wolf was victorious in the match, but Callum Newman bounced back to defeat HENARE on the final night of block action to make the semifinal.
summary: Callum Newman entered the G1 Climax tournament with a dislocated shoulder sustained at NJPW Dominion. During his bout against Aaron Wolf, he felt his shoulder pop and move after a judo throw, sending an electric sensation down his arm, before going on to reach the semifinals. He lost to Ryohei Oiwa in the semifinals after also being put through a table in a prior match.

title: George Barrios Details Meeting To Finalize WWE/Saudi Arabia Deal; Says There Were Armed Guards, A Prince Was In His Boxer Shorts & Had Hookah

summary_src: In-depth information from George Barrios. Jeff Jarrett and Conrad Thompson rolled out a new episode of Jarrett's My World podcast featuring former WWE Co-President and Board member George Barrios.
body: They did a deep dive into WWE’s relationship with Saudi Arabia and further elaborated on what Barrios discussed in his book. Barrios detailed how the deal was finalized. He remembers people not being eager to fly to Riyadh to represent WWE. He said fellow former Co-President Michelle Wilson wasn’t going because she’s a woman, and that would have been a complex situation to handle. Barrios added that he thinks Vince McMahon did not want to go, so he was the next person up. Barrios’ wife was not a fan of him traveling to Saudi. He dove into the details of arriving at the meeting. He said there were guards armed with machine guns. Barrios remembers one of the Princes being in his boxer shorts and having a hookah setup. Barrios said the Prince was shouting at him because he felt WWE was being greedy with their terms of the deal. “I remember Michelle’s not going because she’s a woman and that adds a level of complexity at that point in time, less so, but then, it was an issue. Vince (McMahon), I don’t think wanted to go honestly and so I’m like, ‘F*ck it. It’s me,’” Barrios smiled. “I’m up… I like to consider myself this tough street kid. I’ve been in a million fights; I’m not scared of anybody. Blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, but I was like, I was a little worried, and I remember Carol, my wife, was a little worried… We had made the decision: I’m going. We’re going. We’re gonna get this deal done. It’s the night before the earnings call. So usually, I’m home late anyway, because we were prepping… At this point, we hadn’t even been prepping. We were working on this. But I come home, it’s like 1 o’clock in the morning… gotta turn on the lights and I gotta pack and she’s like, ‘Pack? Where are you going?’ I go, ‘After the earnings call, I’m flying to Riyadh,’ and she’s like, ‘What!?’ My own personal things, explaining that, she was worried about it. But I get out and I will tell you… I have negotiated deals in every part of the world. I am very comfortable in every part of the world, even when the customs are very different… Broken bread in China, Thailand, India, everywhere, you know? There’s always been someone that’s the guy. That guy was Will, and when Will left, TJP stepped up, and when TJ left, nobody wanted to step up. It was just an open space, and then HENARE got hurt, Akira got hurt, and I was the hardest worker. “I said to them, to their faces, somebody has to do something or this group is going to go downhill. And they didn’t want to. So I was like f*** it, it’s got to be me. And I sacrificed a lot, threw all I had into this, every match I had was flying the flag for UE. “Then the boys came back from injury, I brought in Jake Lee, who’s a phenomenal wrestler, Andrade El Idolo, one of the best wrestlers in the world. So then Will wants to come back when the group is peaking. He said he’d do things my way but he didn’t. And then he made his own group in America without telling us.” Newman continued, confirming that he wasn’t given a heads up on Ospreay’s decision to start a US version of the group. “Nobody did. I got a message from one of the other boys saying ‘you know Mike Bailey’s in the group?’ and I’m like, ‘no, I didn’t’. They go ‘do you know Alex Windsor’s in, Jamie Hayter’s in?’ I didn’t know, no. The only way I would find out is looking on f***ing Twitter. So thanks, I guess. All the hard work, all the sacrifice means f*** all,” he stated. Ospreay and Newman will team at NJPW Power Struggle to challenge for the IWGP Tag Team Championships.

title: Callum Newman Criticizes AEW Stars' NJPW Approach
raw_title: Callum Newman: AEW Wrestlers Feel NJPW Is Easy, It's Not Easy
summary_src: AEW seems set to have a big presence at NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 with Kenny Omega, Jon Moxley, MJF, and Will Ospreay all appearing on recent NJPW shows to set up future NJPW matches. This doesn't sit well with former IWGP Heavyweight Champion Callum Newman.
body: AEW seems set to have a big presence at NJPW Wrestle Kingdom 21 with Kenny Omega, Jon Moxley, MJF, and Will Ospreay all appearing on recent NJPW shows to set up future NJPW matches. This doesn’t sit well with former IWGP Heavyweight Champion Callum Newman. “I’m not salty about them, I just feel angry because when their wrestlers want to make a name for themselves in Japan, they feel NJPW is an easy in for them just because they have AEW on their resume. New Japan is not that easy. For all the people who do all the squats in that Dojo every day to get here, an AEW wrestler who can hop, skip and jump their way into a main event rubs me the wrong way. “Because most of those guys as well, they only come in to do one show. They never do a full tour, never know how hard touring actually is. They fly in day before, do a match and fly back home. That’s it. I don’t think they get the schedule,” Newman said while speaking to NJPW . Moxley, Omega, and Ospreay are all former IWGP Heavyweight Champions and have done G1 Climax tournaments. Omega and Ospreay were the top gaijins in NJPW before moving to AEW. Fans can find more comments from Newman about Ospreay by clicking here .
summary: Former IWGP Heavyweight Champion Callum Newman expressed frustration with AEW wrestlers who view NJPW as an easy opportunity to make a name for themselves simply because of their AEW background. He noted that many only appear for single shows without experiencing full tours or the demanding daily dojo training and travel schedule required in New Japan. Newman made the comments in an interview with NJPW, as Kenny Omega, Jon Moxley, MJF and Will Ospreay have been building toward matches at Wrestle Kingdom 21.

body: By Josh Coulson Published Oct 28, 2026, 7:12 AM EDT Josh studied Journalism and Media and Cultural Studies at the University of the West of England, graduating in the summer of 2014.. Sign in to your TheSportster account Stephanie Vaquer was supposed to return to the ring on Monday after working through an ankle injury. Her return match against Becky Lynch was changed at the last minute, and now the latest on the former World Champion suggests we might not see her back in the ring for a very long time. Vaquer announced that she was ready to make her return, confirming that she had recovered from the injury that briefly kept her sidelined. That's why fans were puzzled when Liv Morgan replaced her on Raw. No official confirmation on what exactly is going on with Vaquer has been shared by WWE, but reports suggest an illness prevented her from competing on Monday. It won't just be Monday either. The latest from PWInsider claims Vaquer is considered to be out of action indefinitely, with no known date for when fans can expect to see her again, or even a vague window. The details of the supposed illness haven't been shared, but, oddly, it would be something that dictates Vaquer to be AWOL for the foreseeable future. Vaquer was reportedly not even in attendance on Raw this week, which would make sense if she's suffering from an illness. The indefinite label given to her absence could mean anything at this stage. It might mean she is suffering from something that will prevent her from wrestling for months, or it might simply be something that can't be quantified via a timeframe. It could even be a case of the sources reporting on the situation not knowing specific details. It's been a rough month or so for Vaquer between injuries and dropping the World Title back to Liv Morgan after only four weeks with the championship. There was speculation among fans that the reason Vaquer lost the title was because of an injury. Whether that's true or not, the aftermath of that title loss has been plagued with problems, and now, with her three-way rivalry against Morgan and Lynch ongoing, we might not see Vaquer again for a long time. Vaquer's WWE career is still young, yet she ascended to the top of the card the moment she arrived. Even though it feels like she has been a WWE Superstar for years, Vaquer didn't sign with the promotion until 2024 and made her main roster debut a little over a year ago. She still has a lot more to give whenever she's cleared to return.

title: Ex-WWE Co-President Downplays 2019 Crown Jewel Plane Delay
raw_title: Former WWE Co-President Speaks About 2019 Crown Jewel Plane Incident: “I Think It Was Exaggerated To Some Degree"
summary_src: The former WWE Co-President spoke about the situation. WWE's relationship with Saudi Arabia was a focus point during former WWE Co-President and Board member George Barrios' appearance on My World With Jeff Jarrett.
body: WWE’s relationship with Saudi Arabia was a focus point during former WWE Co-President and Board member George Barrios’ appearance on My World With Jeff Jarrett . Barrios spoke about the 2019 Crown Jewel plane incident, where some felt WWE talents were being held hostage. Barrios said that situation has been slightly exaggerated. He stated that there was a new airport fee that had been instituted. “I think it was exaggerated to some degree, and again, look, back to doing business in other countries, there were other runways around the world where our plane was delayed. I remember somebody calling us like, ‘Hey, there’s a new fee –’ it was not in Riyadh. It was in a different country; I won’t name it. But we’re getting called. Our plane had been delayed… It had gotten serious enough; it had reached my desk. Usually this stuff is just getting handled. But it reached my desk because a new fee had been instituted in this country — airport fee — that was a lot of money… to get out… Someone could look at this and say you’re being extorted to being left out of the country. I guess it depends how you wanna look at it. But in that moment, there was a fee… What did I say? I said, ‘Pay the f*cking fee. We’re coming home, right? So I don’t even know why you’re calling me. Yes, it’s a lot of money but yeah, we’re paying the airport fee.’ If anybody’s listening and is gonna charge me with a violation of the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, I say bullsh*t. That was the then law in that country and we obeyed it. So when you ask about what happened in Saudi Arabia, I think for the most part — I don’t know exactly and I’m not trying to say there was an analog there. I’m just saying there was a delay and then we got out… I’ll leave it at that.” Elsewhere in the chat, Barrios did a deep dive about the meeting to close the WWE/Saudi deal. That can be read here .
summary: Former WWE Co-President and Board member George Barrios appeared on My World With Jeff Jarrett and discussed the 2019 Crown Jewel plane incident in Saudi Arabia. Barrios said the situation where some felt WWE talents were being held hostage was exaggerated to some degree. He explained it involved a new and substantial airport fee instituted in another country that delayed the plane until resolved.
