title: End of an Era: Bruce Prichard Set to Retire From Full-Time WWE Role After WrestleMania 43
raw_title: Bruce Prichard Set to Retire From Full-Time WWE Role After WrestleMania 43
summary_src: Bruce Prichard’s days working full-time behind the scenes in WWE are repocoming to an end. He isn’t expected to completely disappear from the company, but a major change is apparently coming after WrestleMania 43.
body: According to PWInsider , Bruce Prichard is expected to retire from his position as WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent following WrestleMania season next year. The 63-year-old is still expected to remain connected to WWE as a consultant, but he would no longer keep his current responsibilities or live in Stamford. One source specifically pointed to WrestleMania as the end of Prichard’s full-time run, although another cautioned that the timeline could always move around a little. Fightful Select has since provided more details on what’s behind the change, and Prichard’s health appears to be a major factor. According to sources familiar with the situation, Prichard is expected to remain with WWE after stepping down from his current position, but he’ll be working from home much more frequently. Prichard needs a very serious surgery that is expected to take him off the road . Fightful added that he is already feeling rough physically, making the move away from WWE’s regular travel schedule even more understandable. That lines up with the recent revelation that Prichard is preparing to undergo neck surgery. Conrad Thompson previously revealed that Prichard only recently learned how badly his neck had been damaged from an angle all the way back in 1991. That was when The Ultimate Warrior attacked Prichard’s Brother Love character to write him off WWF television. More than three decades later, the damage from that angle is apparently still causing problems serious enough to require surgery. Prichard stepping away from his full-time position would also be a pretty significant backstage change for WWE. He returned to the company full-time in 2019 and eventually became one of the most influential people in the creative structure, first working closely with Vince McMahon and later with Paul “Triple H” Levesque. Prichard has also been trusted to run television tapings whenever Levesque isn’t there. PWInsider reports that WWE’s RAW, SmackDown and NXT writing teams currently fall underneath Prichard in the company hierarchy. There’s no word yet on who WWE might put in his position once he steps away, and with WrestleMania still months away, the company has plenty of time to figure that out. For Prichard, though, this doesn’t sound like a complete goodbye to WWE. Instead, it looks like his role is being reshaped around a much lighter workload as he deals with a serious physical issue and prepares to leave the road after years of being one of WWE’s most important behind-the-scenes figures. Who do you think WWE should turn to once Bruce Prichard steps away from his full-time creative position after WrestleMania 43? Let us know what you think in the comments. summary: Per PWInsider , Bruce Prichard is likely to retire from his position as WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent after WrestleMania season next year. One source specifically pointed to WrestleMania as the end of Prichard’s full-time run, although another cautioned that the timeline could always move around a little.

summary_src: Tony D’Angelo isn’t making excuses for his WWE NXT Championship reign, but he believes things would have played out much differently if he had more experienced talent to work with.
body: During a recent interview with Denise Salcedo , D’Angelo reflected on his time as NXT Champion and explained why he believes his title reign hasn’t received the recognition it deserves. According to D’Angelo, WWE had moved several established NXT stars to the main roster, leaving him without many experienced opponents who knew how to handle lengthy main event matches and major storylines. “I didn’t have a whole lot to work with, so to speak. A lot of people with inexperience, which is not their fault. They, as in the main roster, took a bunch of people, and those were all the people that had experience and had been in main events and long matches and knew how, you know, their promos were tip-top.” D’Angelo made it clear that he wasn’t blaming the younger wrestlers for their lack of experience. Instead, he believes the timing of his championship run put him in a difficult situation that other NXT Champions didn’t necessarily have to deal with. He also suggested that fans might remember his reign differently if it had taken place during another period in NXT’s history. “I think had I been champion in a different era, I think people would talk differently about it for sure, but I’m not offended. It is what it is.” Despite those challenges, D’Angelo believes he proved something important during his time at the top of the brand. He pointed to a conversation with Shawn Michaels, who acknowledged that NXT had lost much of its established talent during that period. “I think I still showed that I can be champion and carry a brand, and it was a difficult time because, like Shawn [Michaels] said, everybody left. So I held it together when we were in this little transition period. And I’m okay with that. I really am.” D’Angelo isn’t looking to rewrite history, but he clearly believes his championship run deserves more credit considering the circumstances. While other champions had established stars to help build their reigns, D’Angelo feels he was tasked with keeping NXT together during a major roster transition. His comments also offer a look at the challenges NXT faces whenever WWE calls up its most experienced performers. D’Angelo believes he did his job when the brand needed someone to lead the way, even if his championship reign didn’t receive the same attention as others. Per D’Angelo, WWE had moved a number of established NXT stars to the main roster, leaving him without many experienced opponents who knew how to handle lengthy main event matches.

title: Former WWE Executive George Barrios Opens Up On Saudi Prince Confronted Him in Underwear During Tense Deal Negotiations
raw_title: Former WWE Executive George Barrios Reveals Saudi Prince Confronted Him in Underwear During Tense Deal Negotiations
summary_src: WWE’s massive Saudi Arabia deal came together during one of the strangest business meetings former company executive George Barrios ever experienced.
body: Barrios said fellow WWE Co-President Michelle Wilson wasn’t going because of the complications surrounding women traveling to Saudi Arabia at the time. He also believed Vince McMahon had no interest in making the trip, leaving Barrios to handle the negotiations himself. “I remember Michelle’s not going because she’s a woman and that adds a level of complexity at that point in time, less so, but then, it was an issue. Vince, I don’t think wanted to go honestly and so I’m like, ‘F ck it. It’s me.'”* Even Barrios, who had negotiated major business deals around the world, admitted he was nervous. His wife wasn’t thrilled when he informed her at approximately 1 AM that he would be flying to Riyadh immediately after WWE’s earnings call. Things only got more uncomfortable once he arrived. Barrios recalled driving into a dark compound surrounded by armed guards. His meeting, originally scheduled for 7 PM, didn’t begin until approximately 11 PM. Inside, he found something he never expected from a high-level international business negotiation. “Go into this meeting, it’s almost like a man cave. It’s dark. It’s — I don’t know — five, six, probably six… two rows of three of these giant TVs, all with YouTube with all different things on them. It’s like this giant man cave with one of the most senior Princes in the Kingdom, who’s in his boxer shorts with a hookah and the meeting starts with him f cking yelling at me because he thinks we’re being a little greedy on the terms of the deal.”* Barrios then went into another room with the prince’s second-in-command to work through the financial terms. However, the armed security and guards carrying boxes in and out of the room had him imagining the worst. “These guards are walking in and out with little boxes and I’m like, God man, I’m going out in one of those boxes. I bet it’s at the end of this thing.” While Barrios laughed about the experience during the podcast, he admitted the situation genuinely made him uncomfortable. “So, like I said, I like to pretend I’m not afraid of anything. I was a little uncomfortable. It was the most unique kind of business dealing I’d ever had.” Despite the bizarre circumstances surrounding the negotiations, Barrios made it clear that his experiences working with Saudi Arabia were largely positive once the partnership got underway. He acknowledged that WWE faced significant logistical challenges because Saudi Arabia had limited experience hosting productions of that size. Even something as basic as distributing tickets became a major obstacle because the country’s ticketing infrastructure was practically nonexistent at the time. “They can be a little slow sometimes, and as they were getting their sea legs on putting together these large-scale events… A lot of our team — there were a lot of late nights — kind of working through all the logistics of it because you guys know how hard it is to put on major events and now you’re doing it in a country that’d never done it before.” Barrio

title: Stephanie Vaquer Out Indefinitely With New Ailment
raw_title: WWE star Stephanie Vaquer ‘out indefinitely’ with another ailment
body: It has been a year full of injuries for Stephanie Vaquer , and the former WWE Women's World Champion is on the shelf "indefinitely." New reports (via Fightful) have surfaced about her absence . Initially, PWInsider's Mike Johnson speculated that her hiatus was due to an illness. False Finish's Cory Hays later added that she would be "out indefinitely." This is not great news for Vaquer, as she is in the middle of a feud with Becky Lynch. They were supposed to square off during the Oct. 26 edition of Monday Night RAW. However, while "La Primera" said she was cleared from a kayfabe ankle injury, general manager Adam Pearce opened the show by saying she was not good to go. Vaquer recently returned from a three-month hiatus during the Aug. 3 edition of RAW. She had been absent from WWE after her WrestleMania 42 match against Liv Morgan. Vaquer lost the Women's World Championship after 210 days to the 2026 Royal Rumble winner at the Showcase of the Immortals and took a well-deserved break after. She attacked Morgan, who was holding the title, during the Aug. 3 episode of RAW. Vaquer unsuccessfully challenged Morgan for the title a month later during the Sep. 7 episode of RAW. A few days later, WWE shocked the world and had Vaquer win the title back during an untelevised house show in Santiago, Chile. Lynch was the special guest referee of the match. Sadly, her second reign did not last very long. She lost the title back to Morgan nearly a month later at Money in the Bank on Oct. 10. "La Primera" joined the main roster during the RAW after WrestleMania 41 in April 2025. She immediately made a splash, winning the battle royal at Evolution a couple of months later to earn a Women's World Championship match. She then beat Iyo Sky at Wrestlepalooza to win the vacant title and held it for 210 days.
summary: Stephanie Vaquer is sidelined indefinitely according to reports from Fightful and PWInsider. The former WWE Women's World Champion had just returned from a three-month absence on the August 3 episode of RAW where she attacked Liv Morgan. Her current storyline feud with Becky Lynch has been impacted as she was pulled from their scheduled match on the October 26 edition of RAW.

summary_src: Kelani Jordan isn’t taking back her controversial comments about women getting attention in WWE for their bodies and catchphrases instead of their wrestling abilities.
body: During an October 28, 2026 interview with The Wrestling Classic , Jordan was asked about a previous NXT promo where she took aim at the way certain women receive attention. title: WWE Struggles With Cody Rhodes Booking
raw_title: WWE's Growing Cody Rhodes Problem
body: Yet, as 2026 comes to a close, WWE finds itself facing a growing problem surrounding the American Nightmare, through little fault of the future Hall of Famer's own. He was a made man, the face of both pro wrestling's No. 1 company and its new era. Well, when one reaches such heights and then spends two years in and around the WWE title picture, a certain perception sets in. Rhodes is a champion, has been a champion, and anything he does outside the realm of the championship feels like a step down. Even if it is a feud with a fellow future Hall of Famer and the man who was instrumental in Rhodes' early development as an on-screen presence and in-ring worker, Randy Orton. Rhodes had become so synonymous with the gold that involving him in a storyline that does not involve it, or at least feature it in the periphery, feels less than for a star of that magnitude. At the same time, fans had begun to express their displeasure with the second-generation star's constant presence in the title picture, so it was clear WWE Creative had to do something to right the ship rather than allowing Rhodes to face the backlash of an audience who wanted something different. Perhaps devising a way to keep him in the title picture without holding the gold, all while combating the great threat of Orton, would have been a better way to have one's cake and eat it, too. Regardless, Rhodes has reached such heights within WWE that, like Attitude Era "Stone Cold" Steve Austin and The Rock, when he is not battling for the top prize in the company, it feels like a step down for the performer, not to mention an empty feud, devoid of stakes. That is where Rhodes finds himself, and no forcing a different story is going to convince the audience otherwise. Except if the company's own history has dictated anything, it is that the edginess fans demand out of their top stars cannot be manufactured in a scripted storyline. In 2014, the creative team produced a feud in which Bray Wyatt actively attempted to drag the top babyface to new depths, to unleash a side of himself that fans had never seen before, all so he could prove to the world that everyone had a dark side. Cena resisted, and the feud never quite hit like fans had hoped for, even if it did provide a cool visual or moment a few times. In fact, the times Cena showed the greatest edge to his character came nearly a decade earlier, when he fought through pain, suffering, and blood to defeat JBL and Umaga in grueling I Quit and Last Man Standing matches, respectively. They appreciated his toughness and willingness to fight fire with fire, without the creative team hammering home that he needed to do so to be accepted by the audience or to retain his WWE title. Fast forward, and we have a similar scenario, where Rhodes finds himself on the receiving end of Orton's schemes, all so the company can manufacture some edge for its biggest babyface. body: Amazing Red discussed the possibility of bringing AJ Styles out of retirement for a match, as well as the unlikely prospect of a future feud with Styles’ son, Avery. In his interview with SportsMattersTV, Red was asked about the possibility of facing Styles for a match post retirement. While acknowledging that a wrestler’s passion for the business never truly fades, Red described the possibility of facing Avery for the X Division Championship someday. “I totally agree with you. I feel like, just cause I’ve been thinking that also, and the way Will Ospreay took me out of retirement and just kept pushing me, and then I kind of came back. I see what you see, where I see AJ training, I see AJ going dojo to dojo. I see him following his son and making sure he’s going and staying here and there. And you could tell it’s just I don’t think you can leave wrestling,” said Red. “I think there’s moments where we have to step away for sure if it’s a mental break, physical break, but wrestling is such a hard thing to leave. It’s just one of those ex-girlfriends that just doesn’t leave you alone. I feel like if the timing is right for him and maybe I have to go through his son to get to him who knows? But even thinking that that’s kind of a possibility, isn’t that crazy? I could probably wrestle AJ Styles’ son at some point for the X Division Title. So crazy” Red and Styles feuded heavily in the early 2000s when they were emerging as standout performers in the X Division. While Styles retired from wrestling this year, he has attended a few indie events to cheer for his son who made his in-ring debut in June. At Bound for Glory, he competed in his first official TNA bout in the Call Your Shot Gauntlet match. title: On the Record: Kelani Jordan Says WWE NXT Wrestlers Tried Kicking Her Out of Locker Room After TNA Title Win

summary_src: Kelani Jordan thought bringing the TNA Knockouts Championship to WWE NXT would be something worth celebrating, but she claims the reaction backstage was anything but welcoming.
body: During an October 28, 2026 interview with The Wrestling Classic , Jordan opened up about her experience winning the TNA Knockouts Championship and returning to NXT with the title. The interviewer asked whether that experience helped her realize how difficult things could get in the locker room, especially when she wasn’t receiving the respect she believed she deserved. Jordan explained that she expected other wrestlers to come after her championship. What she didn’t expect was the reaction she received after bringing the title back to WWE. “Yes, because so I went into hostile territory, brought the title back to, you know, home turf and people turned on me. Not only the girls in the locker room, which is, you know, to be expected whenever you’re holding a title. Whenever you’re holding a title, there’s a target on your back, no matter what title it is.” The situation wasn’t limited to the locker room, either. Jordan said fans also turned against her, which left her confused because she believed other wrestlers had been praised for similar accomplishments. She pointed to another wrestler winning a championship outside WWE and receiving a much more positive response. “But the fans also turned on me. I’m like, ‘Hold on. Trish went and got the title and you guys were like, Yeah! I went and you guys called me a traitor.’ I’m like, ‘Wow.’ So, that was a big like turning point. But like I said, with the girls in the locker room, of course they’re going to want what I have.” Jordan acknowledged that championship success naturally creates jealousy and competition. She figured other women would approach NXT management looking for opportunities to challenge her, which she considered a normal part of being champion. “So, they’re probably like, ‘All right, let me go to Mr. Stone or if it was Ava at the time to get a match against Kelani.'” However, things apparently went beyond wrestlers simply wanting a shot at her title. When the interviewer brought up how some women seemed to resent her success, Jordan claimed that certain members of the locker room were actually trying to remove her from it. “People were kicking me out the locker room that hadn’t even done anything yet. I’m like, ‘Oh, hell no.'” Jordan didn’t identify which wrestlers she was referring to, but she made it clear that she wasn’t happy about being treated that way after everything she had accomplished. The experience also helps explain why Jordan has moved away from her previous cheerful personality in NXT. Between winning championships, dealing with backlash from fans, and feeling disrespected by fellow wrestlers, she’s reached a point where being nice isn’t her priority anymore. Jordan went to TNA, won its Knockouts Championship, and returned to WWE expecting her accomplishments to speak for themselves. body: Former WWE writer Jimmy Jacobs has shared his experiences working under Vince McMahon, describing a workplace culture marked by fear, unpredictable criticism, and the constant pursuit of approval. Jimmy Jacobs characterized Vince McMahon as a “bully,” “maniac,” and “psychopath” during an appearance on the After the Bell podcast During his time in WWE’s creative department, Jacobs worked directly within the system responsible for developing the company’s television storylines. His recollections offer a former employee’s perspective on McMahon’s management style and how it allegedly affected writers and performers behind the scenes. Jacobs’ comments focus on the pressure employees faced, the close scrutiny of creative decisions, and the difficulty of knowing how McMahon would react to their work. Jacobs joined WWE’s creative team in 2015 after establishing himself as a professional wrestler on the independent circuit. He remained with the company until 2017, gaining firsthand experience of its creative process under McMahon’s leadership. According to Jacobs, McMahon maintained close control over WWE’s television content, from major storyline decisions to individual words in scripts. That level of oversight could leave employees anxious about how their work would be received. Jacobs recalled a culture in which people increasingly focused on avoiding negative reactions rather than simply producing their best work. In his account, the possibility of criticism or losing a job influenced how employees approached their responsibilities. His description highlights the challenges of working within a highly centralized creative structure, where approval from one senior executive could have a substantial effect on an employee’s professional experience. One of Jacobs’ strongest criticisms concerned the effect McMahon’s reactions allegedly had on those working around him. Jacobs described situations in which wrestlers could deliver performances they considered successful but subsequently receive harsh criticism. Experiences like these, he suggested, could leave performers questioning their judgment and wondering where they stood. He also portrayed approval as difficult to predict. Employees might receive positive feedback at one point and face criticism later, creating uncertainty about what McMahon expected. Jacobs characterized the culture as one in which people spent considerable energy trying to avoid McMahon’s anger while continuing to seek his approval. That is the context behind his description of McMahon as a “bully, maniac, and psychopath” These comments reflect Jacobs’ personal recollections, not an independently established assessment of McMahon’s personality or the experiences of every WWE employee. title: George Barrios Recalls Closing WWE Saudi Deal

Vince (McMahon), I don’t think wanted to go honestly and so I’m like, ‘F*ck it. It’s me,’” Barrios smiled. “I’m up… I like to consider myself this tough street kid. I’ve been in a million fights; I’m not scared of anybody. Blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, but I was like, I was a little worried, and I remember Carol, my wife, was a little worried… We had made the decision: I’m going. We’re going. We’re gonna get this deal done. It’s the night before the earnings call. So usually, I’m home late anyway, because we were prepping… At this point, we hadn’t even been prepping. We were working on this. But I come home, it’s like 1 o’clock in the morning… gotta turn on the lights and I gotta pack and she’s like, ‘Pack? But I get out and I will tell you… I have negotiated deals in every part of the world. By that point, Jordan had already become the inaugural NXT Women’s North American Champion and captured the TNA Knockouts Championship. Despite those accomplishments, she felt people still weren’t taking her seriously as someone who belonged at the top of the division. Jordan explained that her original happy-go-lucky personality may have contributed to the problem because people saw her as a likable underdog rather than a legitimate championship threat. “Yeah, I think people I feel like a lot of times like when you’re all like rainbows and butterflies, people are like, ‘Aw, she’s so cute.’ But they don’t always take you seriously. They may love you in the beginning, but when it’s time to truly get after truly chase like a champion or someone with more equity and more experience, you want to make sure like they’re you’re believable.” Jordan said she was tired of entering matches as the person nobody expected to win. She believed her accomplishments should have already established her credibility, but she kept finding herself in the same position. “Like you are actually maybe the underdog, but you on a right day you could win and I think that was kind of I always was like the black What’s it called? The black horse black dark horse in the match and the dark horse and I was like, ‘I’m tired of being the underdog. Like I know what I bring to the table. I just think people I need to change something.’ And that’s when I changed like, you know, no more happy-go-lucky.” The interviewer then asked Jordan how frustrating it was to accomplish so much without receiving the NXT Women’s Championship match she wanted. Jordan explained that she had been patiently waiting for her turn, only to realize that approach was allowing other people to move ahead of her. “Yes. It was super frustrating and I’m like, ‘I’ve literally have done all of this and it’s almost like I was patiently waiting my turn.’ And that’s when I realized, ‘Okay, there’s no more being nice and waiting in line because that’s how you get passed by.'” What frustrated Jordan even more was being placed in situations where she had to compete just to earn another opportunity. She believed her track record should have been enough to justify receiving a direct championship match. “So, it was very annoying and very frustrating when I never got a chance for the Knockouts Championship. And I know people like to say, ‘Oh, well, you got a chance for a chance.’ I’m like, ‘No, but all I need is the big one. I don’t need a chance for a chance. I just need the chance and I’ll get it done.'” The interviewer pointed out that Jordan had a history of making the most of her championship opportunities, suggesting that she usually needed only one or two attempts to win a title. body: Orange Cassidy offers up advice to this year’s competitors in the AEW Blood And Guts match set for next week’s AEW Dynamite. Last year, Cassidy would compete in his first ever AEW Blood And Guts match as he would feature as part of Darby Allin’s team that would face off with The Death Riders inside the double steel cage structure. While speaking to STL Sports Central in a new interview, Orange Cassidy was asked what piece of advice he would give the other participants in the bout. “You better hope that the people… that are in there with you on your team, you can trust them and they’re good because you rely heavily, heavily, heavily on your team. So you better have good teammates.” Cassidy continued, reflecting on not wanting to declare for the match last year. “Nope. Never did. I, you know, I had to- Mark Briscoe had me declare (for) the Blood and Guts last year. I did not want to do that, and you can hear it in my voice when I say, because I’d rather not be involved in it. But when you’re friends and the people you’re standing next to shoulder to shoulder with want you to fight, you fight.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Orange Cassidy advised this year's AEW Blood & Guts participants to ensure they have trustworthy and skilled teammates since the match relies heavily on teamwork. He reflected on competing in the 2024 edition as part of Darby Allin's team against The Death Riders, noting he initially did not want to participate. Cassidy said Mark Briscoe convinced him to declare for the match last year and that he would rather avoid it but joined because his friends wanted him to fight alongside them.

title: WWE Blocked Shotzi Blackheart From Working With TNA Despite Partnership
raw_title: WWE Blocked Shotzi Blackheart From Working With TNA Despite Partnership
summary_src: Shotzi Blackheart’s move to TNA might look like something that came together after her WWE exit, but apparently she was trying to get there way before that. In fact, she was asking WWE to let her work TNA dates while she was still under contract.
body: During an interview on The G , Shotzi explained that the idea started after she returned from ACL surgery. She had spent a long time away from the ring and was basically desperate to start wrestling again, so she saw WWE’s working relationship with TNA as an opportunity. “Yeah, you know, I was kind of talking to TNA when I was still signed with WWE. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was just really hungry to get in the ring, and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA.” Shotzi didn’t just throw the idea out there either. She actually started talking with Tommy Dreamer about making something happen, and according to her, Dreamer was completely down for it. WWE apparently wasn’t. “I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit, and he was totally down, but for some reason, I wasn’t allowed to.” So that was pretty much the end of Shotzi’s TNA idea while she was still with WWE. Things obviously changed once her WWE run ended, but Shotzi didn’t immediately run over to TNA and sign another contract. After dealing with the ACL injury and everything surrounding the end of her WWE run, she wanted some time to just wrestle on the independents and get comfortable being herself again. “But, you know, when I got released, I needed a second to just be on the indies and do me before signing another big contract.” That ended up lasting around a year and a half, and Shotzi says that period helped her rebuild something she badly needed — confidence. Once she finally felt like herself again, that’s when TNA started making sense. “And, you know, after a year and a half of just doing me and gaining my confidence back, I felt like, okay, this is the time for me to get back on TV, for me to come to TNA on absolute fire with the most confidence and the biggest balls I have ever had in my career. So, I’m really coming to TNA fired up.” It’s pretty wild that Shotzi eventually landed exactly where she had been trying to go while still with WWE. The difference is that she’s arriving on her own terms this time, after spending more than a year rebuilding herself instead of simply jumping straight from one company to another. Do you think more WWE talent should be allowed to take advantage of the company’s working relationship with TNA when they’re looking for additional ring time? summary_src: Stephanie Vaquer missed this week's WWE Raw after being ruled medically unfit to compete, with a report revealing the reason behind her absence.
body: WWE Stephanie Vaquer's absence from WWE television and this week's episode of " WWE Raw " was reportedly due to an illness. Vaquer was scheduled to face Becky Lynch, with the winner earning a shot at Liv Morgan's Women's World Championship. "Raw" General Manager Adam Pearce announced at the start of the show that Vaquer was absent and had not been medically cleared to compete. " PWInsider Elite " has reported that her absence from the Red brand this week was due to an illness rather than an injury. The outlet said that there's no news on how long she would be out. Vaquer hasn't wrestled on WWE television since Money in the Bank, where she competed in a triple threat match against Lynch and Morgan, with the latter winning to regain the title. Reports had suggested that Vaquer suffered an ankle injury during the match, although she competed at two WWE live events just a few days later. The originally scheduled clash between Vaquer and Lynch was changed to a match between Lynch and Morgan for the WWE Women's World Championship. The match, which main-evented "Raw," ended in a disqualification after Judgment Day members Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez interfered, helping Morgan retain her title. With Vaquer still in the picture, the rivalry between the three women appears far from over.
summary: Stephanie Vaquer was pulled from her scheduled match against Becky Lynch on this week's WWE Raw after not being medically cleared. Per PWInsider Elite, the reason for her absence was an illness rather than any injury. Vaquer last appeared on television in the triple threat match at Money in the Bank and there is currently no word on how long she will be sidelined.

title: Sami Zayn Credits Sexxxy Eddy For Career Breakthrough
raw_title: Sami Zayn Credits Sexxxy Eddy For The Biggest Break In His Career
summary_src: In 2026, Sami Zayn has become a household name in the world of wrestling, but his grind started in Canada in 2002. Over two decades later, Zayn ascended up the WWE ladder when he was linked to Roman Reigns and the Bloodline in the midst of Roman's historical run as WWE Champion. But it was…
body: In 2026, Sami Zayn has become a household name in the world of wrestling, but his grind started in Canada in 2002. Over two decades later, Zayn ascended up the WWE ladder when he was linked to Roman Reigns and the Bloodline in the midst of Roman’s historical run as WWE Champion. But it was the early years that created the biggest break for Sami. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Sami was asked whathis career looks like without the Bloodline. “No idea. I can’t even fathom it. I don’t know, because it just is. So I can’t play what-ifs or hypotheticals. I don’t even know how to answer that because everything is such a domino effect in this company and in life, but in this company, it’s almost impossible to say what would have happened if X or if Y, these variables. I’m not the only one with these stories, but tons of people will tell you if this one thing hadn’t happened, my entire career, my entire life would be different, and sometimes it’s super small things. Sometimes it’s things that have nothing to do with you. “I’ve told this story before, but the biggest break I ever had in my career, minus Bloodline and WWE stuff, what got me booked in the United States to begin with had nothing to do with me. It was because another wrestler from Canada called Sexxxy Eddy went to the States. I won’t get into the gory details here, but there are gory details because he got cut open and there was a bunch of blood, and he was just an insane showman, and he captured people’s imaginations in this one night where all of a sudden these people were like who are these Canadian guys? Because of that I got booked. So the biggest break in my career had nothing to do with me. It was because Sexxxy Eddy got cut open and had blood spewing out of his arm, but still decided to put on a show. If he doesn’t put on that show, I don’t know how my career would have gone. Maybe I’d still be here. Maybe I’d still be in this chair. Maybe I’d be WWE Champion. Maybe I wouldn’t. I have no idea. But there’s such a crazy domino effect that takes place that you can’t even begin to get your head around.” Zayn is referring to his match against eXceSs 69, Eddy, and Kevin Steen (Kevin Owens) at CZW High Stakes II: Night Sho​w in 2004. The bout was booked after Eddy sliced an artery against The Arsenal at CZW Tournament of Death 3. Elsewhere during the interview, Zayn commented on winning the WWE Championship. You can find his full comments here .
summary: Sami Zayn discussed his early days starting in Canadian wrestling in 2002 during an appearance on Chris Van Vliet's Insight podcast. He explained that one small event from those years became the biggest break of his career and credited Sexxxy Eddy with providing that opportunity. Zayn said he cannot imagine his path without the Bloodline storyline that elevated him alongside Roman Reigns.

llm_long: Sami Zayn revealed that the biggest break in his wrestling career before joining WWE and linking up with Roman Reigns and the Bloodline came from an incident involving fellow Canadian wrestler Sexxxy Eddy. Zayn explained that Eddy traveled to the United States and performed in a match at CZW Tournament of Death 3 where he sliced an artery against The Arsenal, resulting in significant blood loss.

Despite the injury, Eddy continued as an insane showman and captured the audience's imagination that night, prompting promoters to ask who these Canadian guys were. That led directly to Zayn getting booked in the United States for the first time, along with Kevin Steen who later became known as Kevin Owens.

The specific follow-up match occurred at CZW High Stakes II: Night Show in 2004 when Zayn faced eXceSs 69, Eddy, and Steen. Speaking on Chris Van Vliet's Insight podcast, Zayn said he has told this story before and that the breakthrough had nothing to do with him personally.

"It was because Sexxxy Eddy got cut open and had blood spewing out of his arm, but still decided to put on a show." Zayn added that if Eddy had not put on that show, he does not know how his career would have gone and noted the crazy domino effect that takes place.

He stated he cannot even fathom what his career would look like without the Bloodline storyline during Roman's historical run as WWE Champion because everything is such a domino effect. Zayn emphasized that he is not the only one with these stories and that sometimes it is super small things or events that have nothing to do with you that change an entire career and life.

title: 4 Potential Foes for Rey Mysterio Retirement Tour

Next was the conclusion of John Cena's illustrious career on December 12, 2025, who, fittingly, also lost to Gunther at Saturday Night's Main Event . To kick off this year, "The Phenomenal" AJ Styles brought his career to a close. He wrapped up his decorated decade with the company at the Royal Rumble in February, losing to none other than Gunther in a retirement stipulation match . Most recently, we witnessed the end of Brock Lesnar's career following his defeat to Oba Femi in the Night 1 main event of SummerSlam . Despite the loss, he shared a memorable passing-of-the-torch moment with Femi after the match. Fast-forwarding to today, rumors are circulating that Rey Mysterio could be the next star to hang up his boots. According to a number of sources, a retirement tour next year is "quite possible." Despite the chatter, WWE has yet to confirm any plans, and Mysterio has made no official retirement announcement. Much like Cena, Mysterio has previously stated that he wants to announce his final match well in advance so fans can see him compete one last time. Now, the question many fans may be asking is: why would 2027 be the right time for "The Ultimate Underdog" to call it a career? While a few factors come into play, the most obvious one is his age. Mysterio is set to turn 52 in December. While he has certainly looked incredible throughout his second WWE run – most recently in last week's Intercontinental Championship Triple Threat match on Raw against Chad Gable and Dragon Lee – he has been relying on stem cell treatments to keep competing. After wrestling for over 30 years, what better time to call it quits than while still being able to perform at a high level? If 2027 does end up being the final time we see Mysterio in the ring, it is essential that WWE give him the proper farewell tour he rightfully deserves. With that in mind, here are four dream opponents he needs to face before calling it a career. Kicking off the list is a very familiar rival in CM Punk. Their legendary feud began in late 2009 before peaking in 2010, and while Punk's character is vastly different today, revisiting this matchup would serve as a great callback to one of Mysterio's most memorable rivalries. title: WWE’s Netflix Deal Has an Unexpected UFC Twist
raw_title: WWE’s Netflix Deal Has an Unexpected UFC Twist
body: 0 WWE’s Netflix deal has revealed an unexpected connection to UFC. The two companies operate under the same corporate parent, TKO Group Holdings. Now, a legal document has revealed an interesting detail about their media rights negotiations. WWE signed a major deal with Netflix in January 2024. The agreement was reportedly worth $5 billion over ten years. It brought WWE RAW to the streaming platform in January 2025. The move ended Raw’s decades run on television. However, the agreement also included a surprising UFC connection. A unredacted portion of a legal document revealed the detail. According to Wrestlenomics’ Brandon Thurston, WWE’s Netflix agreement included a special provision. The deal gave Netflix “a right of first negotiation” for UFC’s domestic media rights. Thurston reported the development on X, formerly known as Twitter the following a ruling. The ruling came from Delaware’s Court of Chancery last week. The provision reportedly offered Netflix an opportunity to negotiate first. However, Netflix ultimately passed on the UFC media rights deal. Reports suggested the streaming giant preferred major marquee events. It reportedly wasn’t interested in acquiring UFC’s entire event schedule. Paramount Skydance eventually secured the UFC’s domestic media rights. The seven-year agreement is reportedly worth $7.7 billion. The deal began in January 2026. Thurston pursued the removal of redactions from the legal document. His reporting was connected to a WWE shareholders’ lawsuit. WWE’s general counsel had reportedly sought to keep the information hidden. Thurston shared another detail about the court’s decision. He wrote, “Despite affidavit from WWE GC, claims of harm were deemed too general and “[i]t does not matter that the case settled and preempted the court’s need to rely on the information.” He added, “WWE’s attorneys raised this in the merger lawsuit as part of litigation about whether post-merger media rights evidence should be included at (the ultimately cancelled) trial. WWE argued merging with UFC benefited media rights deals, contrary to plaintiffs’ expert’s assertion.” The document has now revealed more about WWE’s negotiations. It also shows Netflix had an opportunity to pursue UFC rights. However, the company ultimately chose not to move forward. title: Netflix reportedly had first-negotiation rights for UFC as part of WWE deal
raw_title: Netflix reportedly had first-negotiation rights for UFC as part of WWE deal
body: The reasoning was sound. Netflix already had a deal with UFC's parent company, TKO, which saw the streamer air WWE Raw every Monday night. UFC seemed like a natural fit, especially as its numbered fight cards closely mirrored Netflix's event-based strategy for live sports. As it turns out, Netflix not only had genuine interest in a UFC deal, but it also had the right to negotiate with TKO before any other company as part of its WWE contract, according to recently unredacted court filings published by wrestling reporter Brandon Thurston. The filings state that Netflix's media rights deal with WWE "includes a right of first negotiation for UFC domestic rights." Those rights ultimately landed at Paramount, but Netflix's ambitions to land the UFC appear to have been serious. Shortly after UFC and Paramount announced their pact, TKO president Mark Shapiro revealed that the promotion had gotten "pretty close with Netflix" but the streamer "didn't want to have the volume" of UFC content that Paramount ultimately licensed. Shapiro suggested Netflix wanted only the numbered UFC cards that include the organization's best fights, leaving lesser inventory like Fight Night and Dana White's Contender Series to be sold elsewhere. TKO, of course, preferred the deal that created a one-stop-shop for all UFC content. Netflix's first-negotiation clause being revealed now is a bit ironic, given that many analysts suggest the streamer needs to lean into regularly scheduled live sports rather than one-off events to combat slipping engagement metrics. Netflix recently fired Bela Bajaria , the streamer's content chief and one of the architects of the event-based sports strategy. The streamer is reportedly considering a partnership with Fox One that would bring Fox's live sports and news content into the Netflix platform. Additionally, one prominent analyst suggests Netflix look to buy NBCUniversal once it completes its spinoff from Comcast to secure its own live sports portfolio. No one knows how much a UFC deal would've helped Netflix's engagement woes, but the timing of this news is even more interesting, as many expect Netflix to change course on live sports. The post Netflix reportedly had first-negotiation rights for UFC as part of WWE deal appeared first on Awful Announcing .

title: David Otunga Analyzes Montez Ford Lawsuit Footage
raw_title: Attorney & Former WWE Star David Otunga Comments On Montez Ford Lawsuit
summary_src: David Otunga has analyzed footage of the incident involving WWE star Montez Ford that led to a lawsuit, arguing that the plaintiff has a case.
body: Former WWE star and attorney David Otunga has analyzed new footage of Montez Ford "sexually provocative dance" against a security guard on "WWE Raw." Ford is being sued by Noel Lucas , a security guard who alleged that he was given an "unwanted lap dance" during the July 6 episode of " Raw ." After watching footage of Ford's alleged assault and battery from another angle, Otunga conceded that Lucas has a case. "These are civil claims, so we're talking about liability and damages. They're not criminal. Now, I still think Montez was entertaining the crowd and trying to get Lucas to break that serious expression and trying to get him to laugh. But you can be trying to make somebody laugh and still cross a legal line," he said on his YouTube channel . "This new footage appears to show repeated contact. Lucas says he didn't consent, and a jury could reasonably find unwanted rubbing during a sexualized dance offensive. Now, you don't need a bruise or a broken bone for battery." Otunga presented arguments for both sides, noting that Lucas could claim Ford rubbed against him without permission, while the WWE star could argue that the "contact was incidental to the dance." However, the former WWE wrestler pointed out that the repeated contact was significant and that the rules surrounding battery apply equally to men and women. "A man shouldn't have to accept contact we'd immediately question if it happened to a woman. The basic battery rule is the same. Being male, being a security guard, or being physically capable doesn't mean that you have to laugh it off and just accept it," he said. Otunga concluded by suggesting that WWE could settle the case, noting that a settlement doesn't necessarily mean the accused has admitted guilt. This isn't the first time a wrestler has faced a lawsuit, as AEW's Jon Moxley was also recently sued by a production crew member who alleged that Moxley shoved him and caused injury.
summary: Former WWE performer and attorney David Otunga reviewed additional footage of Montez Ford performing a sexually provocative dance on a security guard during the July 6 episode of Raw. Otunga stated that Noel Lucas, who is suing Ford for an unwanted lap dance, has a viable civil case involving liability and damages for alleged assault and battery. He noted that even if Ford was attempting to entertain the crowd and make Lucas laugh, repeated contact without consent could cross a legal line and a jury might find the sexualized dance offensive.

title: Netflix Censors Liv Morgan During October 26 WWE RAW Replay
raw_title: Netflix Censors Liv Morgan During October 26 WWE RAW Replay
summary_src: Netflix has been pretty busy cleaning up WWE replays lately, and Liv Morgan just became the latest person to get the edit treatment. This time, though, it wasn’t because of blood, swearing or someone throwing up a middle finger.
body: During the October 26 episode of RAW , Dominik Mysterio carried Liv away on his shoulders following her match against Becky Lynch. The live broadcast showed the whole thing, including a few shots from behind as Dominik walked off with her. Apparently, Netflix took another look at those shots afterwards and decided some of them weren’t staying. On the replay, portions showing Liv’s backside were censored. One of the final shots also appeared to potentially show a little more of her nether region than intended, which would pretty much explain why Netflix decided to cover things up. Basically, if you watched Monday Night RAW live, you got one version. If you went back and watched it on Netflix, you got the cleaned-up version. And Netflix has been doing this quite a bit with WWE lately. LA Knight flipping off Roman Reigns during their World Heavyweight Championship match at Money in the Bank aired without an issue live . When the replay went up, Netflix conveniently switched to another camera angle right before Knight gave Reigns the finger. The September 28 RAW replay got similar treatment after Jacob Fatu was hit by a car. Netflix briefly cut the screen to black before the impact and even muted the sound of Royce Keys slamming an SUV door. There have also been instances of blood getting blurred, profanity being censored and other questionable shots disappearing once WWE shows hit replay. Liv’s situation is obviously a little different since Netflix may have simply been trying to avoid leaving an accidental wardrobe malfunction sitting there on demand. Either way, Netflix apparently saw enough in the footage to decide replay viewers didn’t need to see everything that made it onto the live broadcast. What do you think about Netflix continuing to clean up moments from WWE shows once they hit replay? Let us know what you think in the comments. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

There are even those who would prefer to work exclusively on Ring Of Honor programming so they don't need to stare at the lights on Dynamite or Collision. This could, if it's allowed to go unchecked long term, be something to fret about for Khan . AEW was once renowned as a harmonious, largely politics free space, but... wrestling is wrestling . title: On the Record: AEW Head Tony Khan "Had a Great Visit" Recently with Skydance Team
raw_title: AEW Head Tony Khan "Had a Great Visit" Recently with Skydance Team
body: Posted in: AEW , HBO , Max , Paramount+ , Sports , TV | Tagged: aew , Skydance While it remains to be seen how it will play out, AEW head Tony Khan revealed he just returned from "a great visit" with the Skydance team. After beating back the WWE's bestest buddy, Netflix, and getting the merger between Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery across the finish line, Skydance co-CEO David Ellison has gotten what he wished for – and now, the really hard part begins. With an estimated $80 billion dollars in debt on the books when the deal was signed, Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz are on a mission to find an estimated $6 billion in cost savings over the next three years. This week, the multimedia company announced it would return to a mandatory in-office, five-day workweek and that some employees would be offered a voluntary buyout if they were looking to leave. But to reach the cost-cutting targets set, the company will have to lean hard into layoffs, downsizing, and tech streamlining. Meanwhile, Ellison has a whole lot of promises to keep regarding streaming, linear networks, and theatrical distribution. How does AEW fit into all of this? With Paramount having a deal with TKO (the owner of the WWE) in place for UFC, and AEW head Tony Khan having a deal in place over at Warner Bros. Discovery for wrestling programming, there's been a whole lot of speculating as to who Skydance might end up backing when the dust settles. In a video update on Tuesday night to promote Wednesday night's AEW "Fright Night" Dynamite , Khan noted that he was "very thrilled" to be a part of the newly formed Skydance. "I've just been back from Los Angeles; I had a great visit out there with the Skydance team. And I'm so excited about the future of AEW in the years to come. It's great to be able to bring wrestling to all of you on TBS every week on Dynamite; TNT every week, on Collision. And, of course, all these shows on HBO Max: the TV, the pay-per-views… this is just an awesome time for AEW," Khan shared, adding that they will be joined by the Warner Bros. executives putting on AEW Advance (the live digital preshow). title: Results Recap: Live Report and Review of GCW Presents Shotzi Blackheart’s Drive-In From Hell
raw_title: Live Report and Review of GCW Presents Shotzi Blackheart’s Drive-In From Hell
body: I drive up on the drive-in movie theater in Brownsville, PA. This was the closest that GCW has ever been to my home and it was a very special event as it was “Shotzi Blackheart’s Drive-In From Hell”. We would have a spooky or otherwise Halloween coded event at a real drive-in. They had the old school concession stand, where I got a slushie in a Hocus Pocus cauldron. There were VIP seats and bring your own seats general admission, which was where I was, and you could see perfectly. We had a spooky shed set up in front of the ring and the entrants to the opening scramble made their way to the ring and as the event went on air everyone was introduced. The loudest reactions were for Felix Koz, Blizzy Blake and Zach Thomas.nThis crowd seemed to be more of a local indie wrestling crowd than a GCW crowd. Some of the people that got the best reactions were Gory, Facade, Dani Mo and Juni Underwood, who are from Pittsburgh or have wrestled extensively in the Pittsburgh area, in Juni’s case. The other people who got big reactions throughout the night were people that had been or currently are on national TV, like The Blackhearts (Lio Rush and Shotzi Blackheart), Megan Bayne, and Priscilla Kelly. Felix got the crowd into the event with his polka dancing and Blizzy left them in awe with his high flying maneuvers. However, in the end it was Kavron Kanyon that got the win. In what was the best traditional match of the day, Juni Underwood faced off against Leon King. I have been a big fan of King since the first time I saw him wrestle and this was a good match to show off his skills. This was my friend’s first time seeing Leon King wrestle and she said that she loved everything about him. Leon is flashy and arrogant, but also very athletic. This was a fantastic back and forth match, with Juni having fun with the crowd and King playing the role of the egotistical arrogant foe. In the end, Juni got the win with a very impressive Flamingo Driver. Make sure to keep watching both of these wrestlers as their stocks continue to rise. The former GCW tag team champions, Busta and the Brain, Jordan Oliver and Alec Price, defeat the former Chikara wrestlers Legion of Rot, Hallowicked and Frightmare, with UltraMantis Black in their corner. The Busta and the Brain were just too quick and too young for the spooky veterans to keep up with. In what would be the first hardcore match of the night, Vipress defends her GCW Ultraviolent Championship against Dani Mo. The Ultraviolent Championship is usually held in Deathmatches, but Pennsylvania has silly rules, so we get a really good hardcore match. This is the most fun that I have had watching a Vipress match in a really long time. Dani appears to have improved their hardcore skills with being at JCW and really seemed to be enjoying the match. This is a fast paced match, that incorporates both wrestlers’ athletic ability, along with the weapons. Vipress gets the win, much to the crowds dismay, after throwing powder in Dani’s eyes

body: 0 WWE NXT star Tony D’Angelo has opened up about his championship reign. The former champion believes the roster’s inexperience affected his run. D’Angelo won the NXT Championship at WWE Stand & Deliver. He defeated Joe Hendry, Ethan Page, and Ricky Saints in a fatal four-way match. However, his reign ended after 147 days at NXT Heatwave. Now, D’Angelo has explained why his first title run was difficult. He believes the changing NXT roster played a major role. They, as in the main roster, took a bunch of people, and those were all the people that had experience and had been in main events and long matches and knew how, you know, their promos were tip-top.” The former champion believes NXT lost several experienced performers. “I think had I been champion in a different era, I think people would talk differently about it for sure, but I’m not offended. It is what it is. I think I still showed that I can be champion and carry a brand, and it was a difficult time because, like Shawn [Michaels] said, everybody left. So I held it together when we were in this little transition period. And I’m okay with that. I really am.” [H/T: f4wonline ] D’Angelo’s reign included successful title defenses against Naraku. He defeated him at The Great American Bash and again in a Street Fight. However, Grayson Waller eventually dethroned him at NXT Heatwave in a fatal four way match. title: Matt Hardy Recalls Booking TNA Impact Episode
raw_title: Matt Hardy Details Experience Booking An Episode Of TNA Impact
summary_src: Matt and Jeff Hardy booked the October 15 edition of TNA Impact, a role Matt enjoyed and is eager to take on again in the future.
body: TNA Wrestling Matt Hardy has discussed his experience of booking " TNA Impact " and whether that's a role he wants in the future. The Hardys took charge of booking for the post-Bound for Glory edition of "Impact," which aired on October 15. Hardy spoke about booking the show on " The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy ," revealing that it was an idea set forth by TNA booker Delirious , who wanted them to take charge to celebrate their 35th anniversary in wrestling. "It was extremely interesting. So, it had been out that October 15th was like our wrestling anniversary," he began. "I said, 'Well, first and foremost, if we were booking the show, I mean, the first thing, you know, when people think about the Hardy Boys, they think about ladders, ladder matches.' I said, 'We got to have a ladder match on it.' And then just depending on whatever the finish was of Bound for Glory, whether Nic [Nemeth] won and retained or whether Leon [Slater] became the champion, Leon was going to be in that first segment with us." The duo also had ideas for the Nemeths, who faced each other in a singles match that night, with Jeff suggesting a bra and panties match. Hardy said the show they helped book was well received and also saw an increase in ratings . Hardy, who has previously discussed taking on a backstage role after retiring, spoke about the possibility of becoming a booker in the future. "It was fun. I enjoyed it," he said. "Just figuring it all out was real interesting to us, especially when we went there and we were talking about the show and, like, laying it out and blocking everything out and how we're going to do the segments and, you know, what pretapes are going to be, who we got to represent, how can we do it, and everything else. And I'm sure eventually I'm going to be doing that as well somewhere, wherever it may be." He said he would be keen to take on the role of lead booker if the opportunity arises.

Hardy explained on his podcast The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy that the first priority for the episode was including a ladder match because fans associate the Hardy Boyz with ladders and ladder matches. He noted that Leon Slater was scheduled to appear in the opening segment with them regardless of whether Nic Nemeth retained the title or Leon Slater became champion at Bound for Glory.

The Hardys also developed plans for a singles match between the Nemeths that evening, with Jeff Hardy proposing a bra and panties match for it. Hardy reported that the episode they booked received positive feedback and achieved higher ratings. He described the process of laying out the show, blocking segments, determining pretapes, selecting representatives and structuring everything as both interesting and enjoyable.
Hardy stated he is sure he will eventually take on a booking role somewhere and would be keen to serve as lead booker if the opportunity arises.

title: Shotzi Blackheart Reveals WWE Blocked TNA Run
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart says WWE denied her request to wrestle in TNA
summary_src: Shotzi Blackheart disclosed that she asked WWE for permission to compete in TNA during her tenure with the company, but her request was denied.
body: Shotzi Blackheart disclosed that she asked WWE for permission to compete in TNA during her tenure with the company, but her request was denied. In an interview with Generation Of Wrestling Podcast, Blackheart revealed that she spoke with Tommy Dreamer about the possibility of competing in TNA after returning from an ACL injury in 2024. While Dreamer appeared receptive to the idea, other WWE executives ultimately denied her request. “I was trying, I was kind of talking to TNA when I was still signed with WWE. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was really hungry to get in the ring and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA. I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit and he was totally down, but for some reason I wasn’t allowed to,” said Blackheart. “And then when I got released, I needed a second to be on the indies and do me before signing another big contract.” “After a year and a half of just doing me and gaining my confidence back, I felt like, ‘Okay, this is time for me to get back on TV, come to TNA on absolute fire with the most confidence and the biggest balls I have ever had in my career.’ So, I’m really coming to TNA fired up.” Blackheart addressed the importance of authenticity in the ring as a wrestler, citing she is focused on winning TNA gold. She additionally highlighted the mental toll from recovering to concerns about her return to the ring was more difficult than the physical rehabilitation. She credited spending time with friends, leaning on her support system, enjoying nature, and writing with helping her navigate the recovery process. “Yeah, it’s almost more grueling mentally than physically, showing up to PT and doing the workouts that you’re told to do is the easy part, right? But the mental part of the pain and the struggle to walk and the struggle of knowing whether or not you’re going to be able to come back to doing the thing that you love is so so hard. Getting past that mental point is so difficult. But I just tried to stay focused on the physical and hang out with friends as much as possible, finding my support system and seeking out nature and writing a ton. I did a lot of writing while I was recovering from my ACL surgery and just reconnecting with all the things that you love.” Blackheart suffered the torn ACL at an NXT taping in a match against Lyra Valkyria. In May 2025 she parted ways with WWE and competed across GCW, MLW, MLP before signing with TNA Wrestling this month. title: Grayson Waller Calls Out NXT Talent for Acting Like Fans Around John Cena
raw_title: Grayson Waller Calls Out NXT Talent for Acting Like Fans Around John Cena
summary_src: Grayson Waller already has a problem with the way the NXT locker room is reacting to John Cena’s upcoming appearance. Cena hasn’t even shown up yet, and Waller says some of the younger talent are already acting more like fans than WWE wrestlers.
body: During an appearance on Busted Open After Dark , Waller revealed he was backstage at NXT when the graphic announcing Cena for the November 3 episode appeared. According to Waller, the reaction from the locker room immediately caught his attention. “So, I was backstage tonight when the graphic came up. You should have heard the kids. ‘Oh, John!’ It was tough. I felt like I was at a fan meet-and-greet or something. They were all excited, and it put a smile on my face, too. “I’m the only one here who’s been in the ring with John Cena twice. I’ve been on the mic against John Cena, and I survived. And not everyone does. “But all I hope for John next Wednesday is that he wipes his feet, knocks on the door, and asks me permission to come into my house. And if he wants to get in my ring, he needs to ask permission, too. “And I’m sure maybe he’s talking about this John Cena Classic, giving some NXT superstars an opportunity. Well, those opportunities I’ve taken. So maybe he needs to come and sit down under my learning tree, and I can tell him how things run in NXT now.” Bully Ray then asked Waller if he was basically saying most of the locker room was marking out over Cena while he was looking at the appearance as an opportunity. Waller joked that around five percent of the roster didn’t even know who Cena was before admitting he was just messing around. His bigger point, however, was completely serious. “I’m messing with you. I wish I was just messing with you. I’m just making fun of the kids. “But they were very excited, and I understand because they’ve never seen John Cena in person. What a cool opportunity to come down to NXT. I’ve stood across from John Cena. I’m not the same as them. “I handed in my mark card the day I started at NXT, and for these kids, they need to do the same. They need to carry themselves as equals. We are all on this one WWE brand now. We represent WWE, and it’s cool to show respect to the legends and understand and learn from them and all that. But don’t be a fan. “If any of them are going up and asking for photos or wearing his merch next week, I’m going to go and talk to them directly. You need to — if you want to be this, if you want to be a champion, if you want to main-event WrestleMania, when you get here, you have to treat these people as equals because that’s who they are. “You are on their level, and I don’t think a lot of the kids look at it that way.” Waller’s argument is pretty simple: respect Cena and learn whatever you can from him, but don’t suddenly turn into a fan when he walks through the door. As far as Waller is concerned, anyone who wants to eventually occupy Cena’s spot needs to start carrying themselves like they belong alongside him rather than lining up for a picture. The 17-time World Champion is scheduled to appear on the November 3 edition of NXT, and Grayson Waller certainly sounds ready to keep an eye on how everyone behaves once he actually gets there. title: Orange Cassidy Explains Preference For Wrestling In Denim
raw_title: Orange Cassidy On Wrestling In Denim: I Don't Know Why Anybody Would Want To Wrestle In Anything Else
summary_src: Orange Cassidy explains his reasoning for wearing denim jeans while wrestling, not knowing why other talent don't wrestle in denim too. One of Cassidy's trademarks is the fact that he wrestles in denim jeans, and comes to the ring in a denim jacket.
body: Orange Cassidy explains his reasoning for wearing denim jeans while wrestling, not knowing why other talent don’t wrestle in denim too. One of Cassidy’s trademarks is the fact that he wrestles in denim jeans, and comes to the ring in a denim jacket. This is a part of his character that sets him apart from many wrestlers, as he foregoes the use of tights or trunks in lieu of being lazy. While speaking to The Rizzuto Show in a new interview , Orange Cassidy talked about wrestling in denim, noting he doesn’t know why other wrestlers don’t. “Yeah, it’s like… I don’t know why anybody would want to wrestle in anything else. It’s the most comfortable, durable fabric.” Orange also explained why he uses a drawstring instead of a belt when wearing jeans. “Yeah. The future is now with denim. So if you really want it, like, and then when I wrestle in denim, I have like a drawstring instead of a- because you can’t wear a belt. People that wear belts when they wrestle, it’s crazy to me. you want the belt rubbing up against your uh your stomach” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Orange Cassidy discussed his choice to wrestle in denim jeans during an interview with The Rizzuto Show. He called denim the most comfortable and durable fabric available and questioned why other wrestlers would choose anything else. Cassidy also noted that he uses a drawstring in his jeans instead of a belt because a belt would rub against the stomach during matches.

title: WWE 2K26’s final Ringside Pass launches today, adding four more wrestlers including Earthquake and Typhoon
raw_title: WWE 2K26’s final Ringside Pass launches today, adding four more wrestlers including Earthquake and Typhoon
body: The sixth and final Ringside Pass for WWE 2K26 launches today, bringing an end to the game’s previously announced content roadmap. Ringside Pass Season 6 adds four more playable superstars – Raw member and The 946 leader Royce Keys, Mexican AAA luchador Octagón Jr, and the classic tag team The Natural Disasters, consisting of Typhoon and the late Earthquake. All four wrestlers are claimed immediately through Tier 1 of the Premium Track of Season 6, giving players instant access to them. Also available as part of the Premium Track are new persona outfits for existing superstars, including AJ Styles Masked and Bray Wyatt ’23. The Free Track, meanwhile, includes persona outfits of its own including AJ Styles Retro, Rhea Ripley ’20 and Eddie Guerrero ’05. Ringside Pass Season 6 is the final confirmed paid DLC for the game, and is included for owners of the Monday Night War edition of the game (or can be bought separately). The first Ringside Pass season for WWE 2K26 added AAA wrestlers Mr Iguana, Psycho Clown, El Hijo Del Vikingo and Flammer to the game’s roster. This was followed by Season 2 which added Demolition (Ax, Crush and Smash) and Kelly Kelly. Season 3 then added Matt Cardona, Brian Pillman, La Parka and Torrie Wilson, as well as NBA star Tyrese Haliburton in the free tier. Then Season 4 added Matt Hardy, Jeff Hardy, musician Jelly Roll and AAA wrestler Lady Shani. Finally, Season 5 added Danhausen, Bam Bam Bigelow, Brie Bella and Pagano. Also available today as a separate purchase is the previously announced WWE 2K26 X Street Fighter Elite Pack , which includes playable versions of action figures depicting WWE superstars as Street Fighter characters. The pack features The Rock ‘Final Boss’ as M. Bison, Rey Mysterio as Ryu, Bianca Belair as Cammy, Ultimate Warrior as Blanka and Dominik Mysterio as Ken.
summary: Per Video Games Chronicle: the sixth and final Ringside Pass for WWE 2K26 launches today, bringing an end to the game’s previously revealed content roadmap. Ringside Pass Season 6 adds four more playable superstars – Raw member and The 946 leader Royce Keys.

title: Queen Aminata Praises Mercedes Mone After Title Match
raw_title: Queen Aminata: I Don't Think People Give Mercedes Mone Enough Credit. She's Amazing
summary_src: At AEW Grand Slam France, Queen Aminata challenged Mercedes Mone for the AEW Women's Championship. Though Aminata came up short in her efforts to win her first title in AEW, she learned a lot from the match.
body: At AEW Grand Slam France, Queen Aminata challenged Mercedes Mone for the AEW Women’s Championship. Though Aminata came up short in her efforts to win her first title in AEW, she learned a lot from the match. Speaking on CMLL Informa , Aminata was asked about having a role model in wrestling, and she noted her match against Mercedes. “Growing up watching wrestling, I didn’t really have a role model, so I just wanted to make myself my own role model. Now that I’ve faced her in Paris, after that match, something stuck in my head. I want to be as good as this woman is. She is amazing. I don’t think people give her enough credit. I feel like I’m a different wrestler because of that match. It was in France, and I grew up in France. Of course, it’s the one and only Mercedes Mone. I want to do it again. I really want to wrestle her again. She’s amazing,” she said. Aminata is set to challenge Persephone for the AEW TBS Championship on Wednesday’s AEW Dynamite. Another hungry challenger is also looking for her first AEW gold when Queen Aminata challenges for the TBS Title against TBS & CMLL World Women's Champion Persephone! Plus, the Best-of-5 Series between FTR and the Motor City Machine Guns is tied 1-1 after FTR stole one on Collision, but the two sides will meet in Match #3 tonight in St. Louis! Get ready for a night of frightful delight in the form of the best professional wrestling in the world! Check out everything you need to know for Fright Night Dynamite! Alexander would go on to taunt Adam Copeland, who showed up to confront Alexander, only to be jumped by Mark Davis and Jake Doyle. title: Orange Cassidy Names Broken Orbital Bone as Worst Injury
raw_title: Orange Cassidy Recalls Breaking Orbital Bone As His Worst Injury, Vomiting Blood As A Result
summary_src: Orange Cassidy discusses the worst injury he has suffered in the world of professional wrestling, pointing to breaking his orbital bone.
body: Orange Cassidy discusses the worst injury he has suffered in the world of professional wrestling, pointing to breaking his orbital bone. Cassidy is a workhorse in the industry of pro wrestling and rarely takes time off unless he has suffered an injury, missing time due to dislocating his shoulder and tearing a pec in the past. While speaking to The Rizzuto Show in a new interview, Orange Cassidy was asked about what the worst injury he’s suffered in wrestling has been, pointing to breaking his orbital. “I broke my… orbital bone in my sinus on my face. I mean, I don’t want to get too… It happened, and I broke my face, and when you rupture the sinus, the blood goes down your throat and into your stomach. I didn’t know this. I was very nauseous, and I went out back at the small little building we were wrestling at, and I leaned over and my friend took a video of it and it looked like- funny enough around October, The Exorcist, the blood was shooting (out). It was just straight blood because all of it was just going down into my stomach and it came back up. I got knee’d in the face.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Orange Cassidy told The Rizzuto Show that breaking his orbital bone and rupturing his sinus was the worst injury of his pro wrestling career. He understands that real change starts at the local level and with people who are engaged in their communities. I’m honored to join the Advisory Council and look forward to working with AFP to help more Americans make their voices heard.” Jacobs was elected mayor of Knox County in 2018 and won a second term through September 1, 2026. As mayor, he has focused on fiscal responsibility, limited government, workforce development, and economic growth, with Knox County adding more than 2,500 jobs and $217 million in capital investment under his leadership. He is the author of Mayor Kane . He and his wife of more than 30 years, Crystal, live in Knox County with their family. body: AEW AEW's newest signee, Ilja Dragunov, has opened up about his reaction to his debut at WrestleDream . Dragunov received a great ovation when he came out at WrestleDream , months after leaving WWE. The former WWE United States Champion recently spoke to " Battleground Podcast " about the moment, explaining why it felt like a fairytale moment for him. "What is definitely going through my mind is just rethinking about the beautiful moments to come out to my entrance at WrestleDream on the pay-per-view on Saturday, which was absolutely incredible, the welcoming of the crowds on my side, the music I was craving to hear again for such a long time because it carried me through my whole beginnings of my career. And have this perfect presentation of just to transfer through my entrance what I'm all about. That was a fairytale," he said. Dragunov admitted to feeling nostalgic and immensely excited before heading to the ring, explaining how he wanted to perform with all his heart. "Nostalgia to a certain extent because I don't remember what I felt the last time, like something is actually in the version that I am today, taking me back to the days that wrestling was just a passion only and not like what I do majorly with my life. But also freedom, trust, excitement, you know, because even if it's an entrance, a 30-minute match, whatever it is that I need to do, I will get it done with all the devotion and all the heart that I have, which is also like one of the major characteristics that make me stick out," added the former WWE star. He expressed happiness with how dedicated AEW is to presenting his character, noting the thought and effort that went into his debut entrance. Dragunov revealed that he spoke to Tony Khan immediately after his debut, and the AEW CEO had only good things to say about his first appearance on AEW television, explaining that the moment felt right.

title: Injury Update: Billy Corgan Says His Wife's Youth Was an 'Advantage' Because Women His Age Were 'Broken'
raw_title: Billy Corgan Says His Wife's Youth Was an 'Advantage' Because Women His Age Were 'Broken'
body: Mendel was 19, and Corgan was 44, when they began dating in 2012. The 59-year-old rocker unpacked that theory during an Oct. 22 appearance on The New York Times' Popcast . When hosts Jon Caramanica and Joe Coscarelli asked whether the couple's generational divide helped their relationship, Corgan seemed to know he was approaching dangerous territory. "I don't wanna make all the feminists mad," he said. Then he went there anyway. Corgan explained that he had "met a lot of broken women" before Mendel, particularly women from his own generation who had experienced abuse and other hardships. He stressed that he wasn't blaming them for what happened to them, saying there was "nothing wrong with them." Instead, Corgan argued that building a relationship became harder "if you're broken and they're broken." Mendel, he said, came from a younger generation with "a different sense of self-confidence." Then came the line that made the age gap considerably harder to ignore. "Her youth was an advantage because she hadn't been wounded like so many people are," Corgan said. He added that Mendel was "really open to love and the possibility" and "just decided not to judge me for who I was." The couple eventually became engaged in 2022, married in 2023, and now share three children. Perhaps unsurprisingly, Corgan has previously encountered at least one famously outspoken older woman who decided she wasn't interested in tolerating him professionally. Sharon Osbourne briefly managed the Smashing Pumpkins before quitting spectacularly in 2000. Her official explanation was unforgettable: "I quit for medical reasons. Billy Corgan was making me sick!!!" Osbourne later described disagreements with Corgan and complained about his behavior when they didn’t see eye to eye. "I don't need stupid little boys making faces at me," she said. And Corgan hasn't limited his career to alternative rock. He jumped into professional wrestling in 2015 as TNA's Senior Producer of Creative and Talent Development, eventually becoming company president in August 2016 while financially investing in the promotion. That relationship also ended dramatically. After a dispute over TNA's finances and a failed legal attempt to gain control of the company, Corgan departed later that year. He wasn't finished with wrestling, however, purchasing the National Wrestling Alliance in 2017.
