title: Ex-WWE Exec Recalls Tense Saudi Deal Trip
raw_title: Ex-WWE exec’s story has it all: A Saudi prince in his underwear, a hookah and armed guards
summary_src: Former WWE Co-President George Barrios recently appeared on Jeff Jarrett’s My World podcast to promote his new memoir, and he shared some interesting tales about his time in the company.
body: Perhaps the wildest story he told related to when he was sent to Riyadh to finalize the deal between WWE and Saudi Arabia . Barrios said he believes the reason he was sent to Saudi Arabia for the negotiations was because then-WWE boss Vince McMahon didn’t want to make the trip. He also noted that WWE’s other co-president at the time, Michelle Wilson, stayed behind “because she’s a woman, and that adds a level of complexity at that point in time.” He told Jarrett and co-host Conrad Thompson: “I like to consider myself this tough street kid. I’ve been in a million fights. I’m not scared of anybody. Blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, but I was like, I was a little worried, and I remember Carol, my wife, was a little worried.” Barrios said he made the flight right after an earnings call, and he noted the meeting took place weeks after the highly-publicized death of journalist Jamal Khashoggi. (The CIA later stated Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman had ordered Khashoggi’s assassination, though the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia has denied any role in his death.) Soon enough, Barrios found himself in “the most unique kind of business meeting I’ve ever been in. First thing is we’re scheduled to start at 7 PM. We don’t start till like 11 PM.” “We drive into this compound. It’s pitch black. Get out, there’s guards everywhere strapped with machine guns. Go into this meeting — it’s almost like a man cave,” he said. “Two rows of three of these giant TVs, all with YouTube with all different things on them. It’s like this giant man cave with one of the most senior Princes in the Kingdom, who’s in his boxer shorts with a hookah, and the meeting starts with him f**king yelling at me because he thinks we’re being a little greedy on the terms of the deal, and me going into this side room with his number two guy to hammer out the deal. “And it’s me and a couple of my guys, junior guys, and them, and it’s this small room with these overstuffed couches, very nice, and these guards are walking in and out with little boxes, and I’m like, ‘God man, I’m going out in one of those boxes. I bet it’s at the end of this thing,’” Barrios joked. llm_long: A former WWE executive described a tense trip to Riyadh to finalize the business agreement between WWE and Saudi Arabia. He explained that Vince McMahon did not want to make the journey himself. The executive also noted that the company's other co-president at the time, a woman, remained behind due to the added complexity that would have created.

The executive admitted feeling some worry ahead of the travel, despite considering himself a tough individual who had been in many fights. His wife expressed concern as well. The flight followed an earnings call, and the meetings occurred weeks after the widely reported death of journalist Jamal Khashoggi.

Upon arrival, the group entered a compound that was pitch black with armed guards present everywhere. The meeting, which was scheduled for 7 PM, did not begin until around 11 PM. It took place in a large room resembling a man cave, featuring multiple large TVs playing YouTube content.

The senior prince involved in the discussions was dressed in boxer shorts and using a hookah. The session opened with the prince yelling at the executive over perceived greediness in the deal terms. The executive then moved to a side room with the prince's top aide to negotiate the specifics of the agreement.

The smaller negotiation room contained overstuffed couches, and guards repeatedly entered and exited carrying small boxes. The executive recalled feeling uncomfortable and joked internally that he might leave in one of those boxes.

summary_src: October 28 2018 was the date of the first WWE Evolution PPV event. body: October 28 2018 was the date of the first WWE Evolution PPV event. It was a major success, with our own Dave Meltzer saying that it “could not have gone better.” It was overshadowed, however, by the fact that it was taking place around the time of the company’s Crown Jewel event in Saudi Arabia, a show that originally did not have women on the card. Here is some of what Dave had to say about WWE Evolution in 2018: “The Evolution PPV, clearly designed as a way to avoid the controversy they got on the first trip to Saudi Arabia because they had no women on the show, could not have gone better. The atmosphere was off the charts, and it felt far more like an NXT show with WWE production and star power. There were a lot of shows with better wrestling, but this was a case where planning and practicing everything out worked out for the best. You could make a strong case for this being the best main roster PPV show of the year, and it absolutely was if judged by fan reaction. The last woman standing match where Becky Lynch retained the Smackdown title over Charlotte Flair was given nearly a half hour, and by the end, reached a level of intensity that few matches reach and in that regard, was the best main roster match this year, men or women, and easily one of the three best women’s matches in company history, and easily the best-ever on the main roster. “But three days earlier, WWE announced that it was, in fact, going to Saudi Arabia for the 11/2 Crown Jewel show, despite mounting criticism. WWE was never going to cancel the show on its own. The decision came down to would they be told by people in the government that they couldn’t go, or shouldn’t go. And that was a strong concern. Last week, top company officials were told that it was less than 50 percent that the show would take place in Saudi Arabia, and that Vince McMahon was expected to be outright told he shouldn’t, or even couldn’t go. “As noted last week, McMahon put money before everything, which is often considered good for the head of a major company, but in this case, it was may have been shortsighted. Business leaders of far bigger and more important companies were pulling out of Saudi Arabia at the same time. After years of trying to change the perception of wrestling companies as bottom of the barrel entertainment, McMahon assured that WWE would be seen as even worse than that to many people for going on with the show. But from his standpoint, there were nine more years of the deal in place, worth $400 million, that he would be risking if he didn’t go.” Jake Jeremy Jake Jeremy is the Head of Audience Development at F4WOnline, having previously worked as a Combat Sports, Gaming and Pro Wrestling writer, successful Editor in Chief and Sports Coordinator. title: On the Record: Booker T Announces Josiah Jean Has Signed WWE ID Contract
raw_title: Booker T Announces Josiah Jean Has Signed WWE ID Contract
summary_src: Josiah Jean just took a pretty big step toward WWE, and Booker T personally showed up to deliver the news. What started as Jean talking about his problems with AJ Francis ended with him getting one of the biggest announcements of his career.
body: “I see so much of myself in this young man right here. So much. Hardworking. I mean, since day one here at Reality of Wrestling, it’s always been about putting the work in, trying to get to that next level, trying to do exactly what it takes to stay on track. That’s what it’s about here at Reality of Wrestling. “And me personally, I want to say I’m proud of you, all right? You’ve done a hell of a job, especially over this last year, especially over these last few months.” Booker then revealed that Jean had already gotten an opportunity to impress WWE behind the scenes. According to him, Jean attended a WWE tryout in Orlando a couple of months ago and represented Reality of Wrestling during the process. That apparently went pretty damn well. “Josiah got a tryout with WWE a couple of months ago, and then he went out there to Orlando, Florida, and he represented Reality of Wrestling. “The work that this young man, Josiah ‘The Rocket,’ has put in, WWE has honored you with a WWE ID contract. “So, I just want to say congratulations to The Rocket, Josiah Jean. This is the beginning of the journey. Now, can you dig it, sucka?” The announcement came right after Jean addressed his falling-out with AJ Francis and House Money. Jean said he originally aligned himself with Francis because he was looking for an experienced wrestler who could help guide him, but he eventually felt like the relationship became completely one-sided. “Since day one, I’ve tried to go out and earn it. But, you know, my best, it wasn’t enough. At the right time, I was looking for an OG. I was looking for somebody that was going to put me on the right path. “But I found AJ Francis. Yeah, I found House Money. But all that turned into was me saving AJ Francis’ ass time after time again. All that turned into was Josiah Williams getting an opportunity and somehow AJ Francis taking it away.” Jean then made it clear that he was done following somebody else and planned on walking his own path. Booker had a little advice for him on that front too, warning Jean that wrestling can be a pretty ruthless business. “In this business, sometimes you’ve got to learn the hard way, all right? Learn the hard way. Smiling in your face and stabbing you in your back in this business. How many times have you heard me say it? DTA. DTA. Don’t trust nobody.” Jean may be going his own way in Reality of Wrestling, but he now has something much bigger waiting in front of him. A WWE ID contract doesn’t guarantee where his career goes from here, but Booker made one thing pretty clear when he handed him the news — this is only the beginning of the journey. What do you think about WWE continuing to bring promising independent wrestlers into its ID program? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Cody Rhodes Says Wrestling In Strong Cultural Spot
raw_title: WWE's Cody Rhodes Assesses Wrestling's Place In Culture
summary_src: WWE star Cody Rhodes believes that pro wrestling is in a great place right now, highlighting how firmly it has established itself in the mainstream.
body: Cody Rhodes has assured pro wrestling fans that wrestling is currently in a great place, not just due to what's happening within the ring but outside of it. Rhodes, who featured in the "Street Fighter" movie alongside fellow wrestlers Roman Reigns and Hirooki Goto, said that having three wrestlers in one movie is a great moment for the wrestling community as a whole. He believes it shows how far wrestling has come and how firmly it has established itself in the mainstream. "I really think it's a moment for all of wrestling to be proud. It's kind of our moment. I'm so lucky that I got offered this role , and you work your whole life and you want these things," he began in his conversation with Denise Salcedo . "You get three wrestlers in a movie. I remember going to see Guardians and people being curious how Dave Batista would be, and then the first big laugh was a Drax moment, was a Batista moment. I felt like, yeah, that's the wrestler. So, the fact that you have Roman , you have Goto, and me, and everyone's vastly different. I'm excited for wrestling." "The American Nightmare" pointed out how business is booming in pro wrestling, and that it's no longer a struggle to be clubbed with mainstream entertainment anymore. "We are in the best place the business has ever been," added Rhodes. "If you are a wrestling fan, a wrestler, someone who was casually in, or as hardcore as you and I, you'll remember the days when it wasn't a thing that we could all share. And it wasn't a thing that, you know, the great word 'mainstream.' Mainstream wrestling doesn't have to fight for mainstream anymore. Nick Khan as president and Triple H as an executive and a creative leader, we've put ourselves in the right place. I don't think we're in the rooms anymore where we feel like we shouldn't be." Rhodes predicts that wrestlers will get more opportunities in other projects in the future if they do good work, something his friend John Cena has always said.
summary: Cody Rhodes believes pro wrestling sits in an excellent position both inside and outside the ring. The WWE star highlighted his upcoming role in the Street Fighter movie alongside Roman Reigns and Hirooki Goto as proof of wrestling's mainstream acceptance. Rhodes shared his excitement during an interview with Denise Salcedo, noting how far the industry has advanced.

title: Jimmy House Learned Heel Work In WWE EVOLVE
raw_title: Jimmy House Says He Learned How To Work Heel In WWE EVOLVE
summary_src: Jimmy House learned how to work heel in WWE EVOLVE. During his time in the WWE ID program, House competed on EVOLVE as a member of The Mog Squad faction. As it turns out, this was his first time working as a heel.
body: During his time in the WWE ID program, House competed on EVOLVE as a member of The Mog Squad faction. As it turns out, this was his first time working as a heel. “Personally for myself, the straightforward answer is I learned at least the bare bones of how to work heel or what I should be looking for to work heel because, I said this on an interview the other day, but up until that point, I had never worked heel on the indies.” Jimmy House told Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp in a new interview. “Second to that, I had maybe done heel in practice, like maybe three times or something like that. It’s a guilty thing that I didn’t go out of my way to work on. So all my babyface reps on the indies were of that last year and when we went to Evolve and we learned about the Mog Squad stuff.” House continued on by joking about how he was the “unc” of The Mog Squad. “It’s hard to put that over as a babyface faction at least off rip, right? So I started to try to find out who I am as a heel, but then who I am as a heel with this mogging twist to it, which, you you try to learn how to be a heel and then you learn what mogging is and then all these subcategories of mogging. Me being the 30 year old of the group, being the oldest by about five to seven years, I was very much the unc of the group. Actually I think one regret that I have of Evolve is we never got to the point to where I could dive into the unc side. ‘Cause I had some ideas in regards to different promos we could have done to lean into the unc side and not knowing different things that they’re talking about. But anyways that was a big transition, understanding what I need to be doing as a heel and then how to mog on top of it. So it was a different challenge.” Elsewhere in the interview, Jimmy House talked about his WWE ID departure. Check out his full comments by clicking here.
summary: Jimmy House revealed that his time in the WWE ID program competing on EVOLVE as part of The Mog Squad marked his first experience working as a heel. He told Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp that prior to that he had never worked heel on the independents and had only done it a handful of times in practice. House joked that he served as the "unc" of The Mog Squad while beginning to develop his heel persona with a mogging twist.

summary_src: The UFC has confirmed the main event for the upcoming UFC Sydney Fight Night, which will be taking place on February 6, 2027 from the Afterpay Arena in Sydney, Australia.
body: The UFC has confirmed the main event for the upcoming UFC Sydney Fight Night, which will be taking place on February 6, 2027 from the Afterpay Arena in Sydney, Australia. Quillan Salkilld will be headlining for the first time on a UFC card, and he’ll be doing it in his home country against fellow top-10-ranked Lightweight fighter Benoit Saint Denis. No other bouts have been announced for the event thus far. Salkilld (13-1) is the current #7 ranked fighter in the Lightweight division, and he is undefeated in six UFC bouts (including five stoppage wins and five Performance of the Night bonuses). Salkilld’s last win came at UFC Vegas 120 back in August, when he submitted Mateusz Gamrot. Saint Denis (17-4, 1 NC) will be coming into the fight trying to be get back to winning ways, having most recently lost to Paddy Pimblett via submission at UFC 329 back in July. The commentators pointed out that was the first pin attempt of the match. Gonzalez hit a spinebuster onto the garbage can for a nearfall at 7:00. He punched a thin wooden board over Bobby’s face and gave him a papercut between his fingers, earning a “You sick f—!” chant. Bobby splashed onto chairs over Gonzalez and got a nearfall at 9:30. Alfonso hit a big boot onto a chair in Bobby’s hands and got a nearfall at 11:00, and we got a “this is awesome!” chant. Alfonso created a door bridge in the ring, but Bobby hit a low blow uppercut. Gonzalez hit a second-rope uranage through the door bridge. He tied Orlando in a Sharpshooter and was using the kendo stick in Bobby’s legs too! Orlando tapped out. That was fun. Alfonso Gonzalez defeated Bobby Orlando in a Chicago street fight at 13:45. 2. Laynie Luck vs. Aleah James vs. Jazzy Yang in a three-way. The commentators said this was the Bloodstone debut for both Aleah and Jazzy. It’s apparently Aleah’s birthday! Jazzy hit a hard knee lift to Aleah’s ribs at 3:00, and she jawed at the crowd. Jazzy hit a Russian Leg Sweep for a nearfall. The crowd chanted, “F— Ohio!” at Yang. summary_src: TNA Wrestling is getting a new television home in Germany, and fans won’t need a subscription to watch it. Starting next week, the company is officially heading back to German free-to-air television. SPORT1 announced that it will begin airing TNA Wrestling every Tuesday starting November 3, 2026.
body: SPORT1 announced that it will begin airing TNA Wrestling every Tuesday starting November 3, 2026. The weekly broadcasts will air at 10:15 PM with German commentary. The network is bringing in Denis Pötzsch and Walandi Tsanti to handle commentary, and both guys already have plenty of wrestling experience. Pötzsch previously called TNA programming during the company’s Impact era, so this is basically a homecoming for him. Tsanti should also be pretty familiar to German wrestling fans after spending ten years calling WWE SmackDown. SPORT1 Chief Content & Distribution Officer Andreas Gerhardt explained that bringing TNA aboard fits directly into the network’s plans to expand its sports programming. “We are expanding our sports programming step by step, and TNA Wrestling fits perfectly into this strategy. The brand has a long tradition while also being a modern, fast-paced product. This allows us to reach both die-hard wrestling fans and people who are experiencing the sport for the first time with us. Starting in November, TNA will be broadcast on free-to-air television on SPORT1.” Pötzsch is also pretty excited about getting behind the microphone for TNA again after previously working with the company years ago. “Walandi and I are really looking forward to presenting TNA Wrestling to fans on SPORT1 as commentators. TNA is a fascinating wrestling brand with over 20 years of history and at the same time an extremely modern, dynamic product. For me personally, it’s also a very special homecoming, as I was already on the microphone for the shows back in the Impact days. What can viewers expect on SPORT1? In three words: ‘Total Nonstop Action.’” Getting weekly free-to-air television is another nice distribution win for TNA, especially with SPORT1 specifically looking to introduce the product to people who may not already be wrestling fans. German viewers will get their first taste of the new arrangement on November 3. Do you think getting more weekly free-to-air television deals can help TNA expand its audience internationally? Let us know what you think in the comments. H Jenkins H Jenkins has been breaking pro wrestling news on Ringside News for nearly a decade, with his reports featured by TMZ, Forbes, The Sun, and more.
summary: The latest: SPORT1 revealed that it will begin airing TNA Wrestling every Tuesday starting November 3, 2026. In three words: ‘Total Nonstop Action.’ Getting weekly free-to-air television is another nice distribution win for TNA.

title: Comeback Watch: WWE Officials Laughed Off Vince Russo’s Potential Return — Report
raw_title: WWE Officials Laughed Off Vince Russo’s Potential Return — Report
body: 0 WWE officials reportedly laughed it off when asked about Vince Russo’s potential return. In the latest edition of his weekly column for Yahoo Sports’ Uncrowned , Conrad Thompson noted that Vince Russo was in talks with WWE President Nick Khan over the summer about returning to the company’s creative team. However, the talks didn’t materialize, as Thompson mentioned the proposal had “ died on the vine .” Vince Russo worked as WWE’s Head Writer from 1997 to 1999. His writing played a major role in Monday Night RAW overcoming WCW Nitro in the Monday Night Wars. He later left for WCW, but a series of controversial decisions, including putting the World Championship on David Arquette, damaged his reputation. He most recently announced his departure from Juggalo Championship Wrestling. According to Fightful Select , sources at WWE headquarters told them they knew Nick Khan had conversations with Vince Russo. However, they didn’t know how serious they were. Sources familiar with the situation noted Vince Russo was either at WWE HQ at one point or was considered for a visit. However, the rest of the company staff, including the agents, producers, writers, and other road crew, were unaware of the development. The report also mentioned that some influential people within the company laughed it off when asked about the Vince Russo situation. Even people who work closely with Nick Khan had no idea that the conversations took place. Several of them reportedly learned of it only after Conrad Thompson’s article came out. Neither Russo nor any WWE representative has publicly commented on the situation so far. The post WWE Officials Laughed Off Vince Russo’s Potential Return — Report appeared first on Wrestlezone .

During an appearance on CMLL Informa, Aminata discussed the impact of the championship match. She explained that growing up she did not have a role model in wrestling and instead made herself her own role model.

Aminata stated that after competing against Mone in Paris something stuck with her. She declared that she wants to be as good as Mone, describing her as amazing and noting that people do not give her enough credit. Aminata referred to her opponent as the one and only Mercedes Mone. She expressed a strong desire to wrestle Mone again, calling her amazing. Aminata is scheduled to challenge Persephone for the AEW TBS Championship on the upcoming edition of AEW Dynamite on Wednesday.

title: Robert Stone Recalls Balancing Teaching and TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Robert Stone Recalls Juggling Wrestling And Teaching During His TNA Run
summary_src: Robert Stone recalls how he would juggle wrestling and teaching during his TNA run, with his school encouraging him to stick with wrestling.
body: Robert Stone recalls how he would juggle wrestling and teaching during his TNA run, with his school encouraging him to stick with wrestling. During Stone’s in ring career, a large part of that would be with TNA wrestling, where he would wrestle under the ring name ‘Robbie E’ and would include several title wins, including an X-Division Championship victory. While speaking to Pro Wrestling Illustrated in a recent interview , Robert Stone spoke about juggling wrestling and his teaching job, revealing how his school encouraged him to continue wrestling when he attempted to resign after signing with TNA. “I finished school. I independent wrestled all throughout college. I got my degree. I got hired as a school teacher in a town over from where I grew up, high school phys ed and health, and then going into my second year of teaching, I had a tryout with TNA Wrestling and I got offered a contract. So, needless to say, at the time, the money was way less than what I was making teaching. But, you know, I had worked almost 10 years at this point in wrestling. I wasn’t going to give up the opportunity. I attempted to resign from school teaching that second year. But they encouraged me to stay, and they said, ‘whenever you can’t be here because of wrestling, that’s okay.’ I was like, ‘you’re sure? Like, we have live TV every week. I’m going to miss a lot of days.’ They encouraged me to stay, which was great because I was getting a teacher’s salary at the same time as getting money for my first wrestling contract. So it was a great way to start being a full-time wrestler. But I would be on live TV on a Thursday night on TNA, fly home Friday morning, get someone to cover my first period and come into school the next day still with hair gel in my hair. I brought, I won the X Division championship and I brought it in. Like all the students would watch me on Thursday night and then see me in school on Friday. They were fist pumping in the hallways. It was a wild time because you know, I’m on Spike TV, live TV every Thursday, and then I’m in school during the week. It was like, so for them, it was cool. Like, think about it, your teacher, like we’re watching them on TV every Thursday night. So it was very cool. But now, years later, yeah, once in a while, I have on Instagram or X, someone reaches out.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

body: Link Facebook Last week, a Cagesider who goes by the name Rivdee kicked off what they admitted was an “ambitious” project they came up with while throwing back some Steveweisers with a fellow rasslin fan: a daily Feed post where the community can discuss if a name from pro wrestling’s past was overrated, or underrated. We then looked up a few lists of who people had ranked as the greatest 50/100/500/eleventy billion wrestlers of all time and had some fun with that as well. I have 40-50 people that I'd love to get other opinions on if they are underrated/overrated/properly rated, if there's interest in this I'll make this a daily thing and happily do it. Nothing to do with politics/personal life behind the scenes, its about their wrestling careers and thats it Ill list 5 pros and cons for each guy being over or underrated My criteria will be based on money drawn, versatility, actual wrestling skill, heat, ability to reinvent themselves and others that fit I'm not putting John Cena/Rock/Austin types in here, but I am putting in some major names over the years and guys who were at least big deals regionally (like Eddie Gilbert who will be on this sooner than later) If you guys want I have a whole list ready to go, think it might a fun thing. title: On the Record: TNA’s Nic Nemeth Gets Candid About Personal Sacrifices & ‘Bound For Glory’ Challenge
raw_title: TNA’s Nic Nemeth Gets Candid About Personal Sacrifices & ‘Bound For Glory’ Challenge
body: Nic Nemeth has made a career out of stealing the show. The TNA Wrestling World Champion looks to do it once again on the company’s biggest stage at Bound For Glory . The veteran performer, previously known as WWE’s Dolph Ziggler, defends against emerging star Leon Slater in the main event of the October 11 pay-per-view. This collision has been building during Thursday Night iMPACT! each week on AMC . For “The Wanted Man,” it’s not only a chance to elevate his 22-year-old challenger. The match provides another opportunity to further cement his legacy and ability to deliver now more than two decades in the game. Here Nemeth opens up about his run and what it means to lead at the top. How do you compare being a TNA World Champion to other times you held a world championship? What’s the feeling you have right now? Nic Nemeth: It’s pretty damn cool. Anytime you’re any kind of champion or representative or even ambassador to the company, it’s being able to talk to different media outlets and do PR work. So that’s fantastic. Comparing it to other companies, f you want to compare world championships in TNA to those in WWE, that’s easy. I became champion by cashing in a contract on a very injured man who still almost beat me. Then when I came to the back I told Vince [McMahon] that I looked forward to being his champion. He said, “Yeah you’re just holding the title for a few weeks so I can get [Alberto] Del Rio heated up again.” And I went, “Okay, I guess I have a few weeks to try and change your mind.” He went, “Yeah okay,” and shrugged. That meant that there’s absolutely no one behind me, and there’s no long-term story. That’s fine. That’s life. That’s pro wrestling. That’s Hollywood. In TNA, they say, “We love your work. We love the way you talk. We love the media that you do. We love the reputation that you have to steal the show in every single main event of every pay-per-view that we have, so we are behind you. We want you to be the best here, and we feel that you’re the best representative to be world champion. And I went, “Yeah, that makes sense.” You’ve really stepped in this leadership role as the TNA World Champion as well. Even when there was some confusion regarding when a match with you and Jeff Hardy would air, you took responsibility for that. I felt like it made sense to me because I feel like I’m the main representative for TNA at this point on a regular basis, and I really appreciate that. But if I was in WWE, I would have done the same thing. Once you get to a point where you’re actually taking responsibility for things inside the ring and out, I feel like I’m a good ambassador for that. I was like, “Hey, man, I’m the world champ right now, and I got to tell you, it was a little confusing if we were going live tonight or not, to me included.” I said, “Listen. It happens. It’s on me. I should have been even clearer when I was promoting it. And you know what? We’ll fix it.” I think it also comes down to believing in the potential of TNA.
summary: Nic Nemeth has made a career out of stealing the show. The TNA Wrestling World Champion looks to do it once again on the company’s biggest stage at Bound For Glory .

body: The three have already been working together. Big Cass returned to WWE on the August 3 episode of Raw, when he attacked Je’Von Evans, and Page joined the Raw roster after WrestleMania 42. Page and Rusev have teamed on Raw since May, and Page and Big Cass faced Chad Gable and Dragon Lee in a tag team match on Monday’s episode of Raw. A trio of big, aggressive heels gives WWE a new group to put against the Raw roster’s babyfaces. Factions often work best with a fourth piece, though, whether it is a leader to do the talking or another wrestler to round out the group. Here are four options. Ludwig Kaiser has spent most of the past year as El Grande Americano, a role he took over in June 2025. He won the character outright by beating Chad Gable in a mask vs. mask match at AAA’s Noche de Los Grandes on May 30, and he has been working regularly for AAA since, where he holds the AAA Mega Championship. Kaiser has experience in a stable from his years in Imperium with Gunther, and he works the same arrogant, physical style as the rest of this group. Gable, the Intercontinental Champion, has also been battling Page for months and faced Page and Big Cass in a tag match on the October 26 Raw, which gives Kaiser a natural reason to get involved. Kaiser is also facing a misdemeanor battery charge in Orange County, Florida, stemming from an April incident. He has contested the charge, seeking dismissal under Florida’s Stand Your Ground law, but a judge denied that motion on October 19. A pretrial conference is set for December 17. Rollins has led a faction before, and his last group ended badly when Bron Breakker, Bronson Reed and Paul Heyman turned on him and took over The Vision in October 2025. Breakker later cost him his match against Gunther at WrestleMania 42. Returning with a new group of heavyweights behind him would give Rollins a direction and give the stable a leader who can carry the promos and main event matches. It would also set up a natural program with Breakker down the line. Pete Dunne has spent the past year as Rayo Americano alongside Tyler Bate’s Bravo Americano. Dunne has also made it clear he wants more. After returning to the independents with WWE’s permission for an ATTACK! Pro Wrestling show in 2026, he said he plans to prove he is “still one of the best wrestlers in the whole world.” Dunne would be the most technical wrestler in the group and would give the stable someone who can wrestle a different style than its three bigger members. He has not found a clear direction on the main roster since then. Adding Saints would require a move to Raw, but it would give the group its strongest talker after Rollins. title: Bruce Prichard Expected to Retire After WrestleMania 43
raw_title: Update on WWE veteran’s retirement plans
body: In the last year, several iconic WWE personalities have called it over. Last year, in Mid 2025, Goldberg retired from pro-wrestling after losing to Gunther. It was then followed by John Cena in Dec. 2025 and AJ Styles in Jan. 2026. Earlier this year, Brock Lesnar also retired from WWE , while Rey Mysterio has seemingly teased retiring soon . With retirements in question, AEW's Adam Copeland has also opened up about retiring from in-ring action next year in 2027. Recently, amongst all of these, Mike Johnson at PWInsider reported that long-term WWE veteran Bruce Prichard is also expected to retire from his position as Executive Director – Creative Writing & Talent (CWT) once WrestleMania 43 is done. It was further noted that, despite his retirement, Prichard will remain connected to the promotion on a consultancy basis. However, he would no longer retain his current duties nor would he be based in Stamford, CT. However, Fightful Select later added to this report and claimed that Prichard's retirement from a full-time role is something that will happen in the coming years. Fightful Select reported that with the promotion heading in a new direction, "currently contracted talent" is expected to transition over to roles behind the scenes. Fightful Select also added that Prichard plans to work from home after undergoing an upcoming neck surgery. "Bruce Prichard's plan is to work from home following a very serious surgery that he needs," Fightful Select wrote. It further added that despite PWInsider's report on him retiring, things currently suggest him remaining with the company and working in a remote position. It was noted that Prichard was the one running the last few shows, when Triple H was on vacation.
summary: Per PWInsider's Mike Johnson, longtime WWE veteran Bruce Prichard is expected to retire from his role as Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent once WrestleMania 43 concludes. He will stay with the company in a consultancy capacity but will no longer hold his current duties or be based in Stamford. Fightful Select later reported that Prichard's exit from a full-time position is planned for the coming years.

body: Robert Stone speaks on his time as the WWE NXT general manager, noting it has been the most rewarding of his career so far. Stone has been the NXT general manager for the past nine months, and has been involved in some of the brands top storylines as a result, as well as having fun relationships with the talent that work on the roster. While speaking to Pro Wrestling Illustrated in a recent interview, Robert Stone discussed his time as WWE NXT general manager so far, noting that it has been the most rewarding time of his career so far. “I mean, it’s a dream job. It really is. It’s a dream come true. You know, I worked as a- I’ve been in the industry for 26 years, did independent wrestling for almost 10 years, TNA for almost eight years, and then now with WWE for over seven years. When I look at all of that, everything in my career, I could honestly say the past seven months, well, nine months for two months, I was interim GM the past nine months of being in this role and, have been the most rewarding, the most fun. I’ve gotten to be in backstage skits with my boss, Shawn Michaels, who I idolized growing up. I got the rub and endorsement from William Regal to take over this role as the NXT general manager, who he was a past general manager, and you just look at all the GMs of the past through all the years of Raw and SmackDown, and they all are a part of history. You don’t forget someone that’s a general manager. You know, so I’m hoping that I’m going to ride this till the wheels fall off. I’m hoping this is a long lasting position that I’m in, and I hope in years and years to come, you’ll always remember that Robert Stone was the general manager of NXT and did a great job. Like, I feel like, you know, we’re just getting started.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: On the Record: Ric Flair Opens Up On He Needs Another Surgery and Possible Skin Graft After Bloody Fall
raw_title: Ric Flair Reveals He Needs Another Surgery and Possible Skin Graft After Bloody Fall
summary_src: Ric Flair isn’t finished dealing with the injuries from his nasty fall in Florida. The WWE Hall of Famer has now revealed that he needs another surgery and might even require a skin graft before he can put the whole situation behind him.
body: On October 28, 2026 , Flair took to Twitter and shared a photo of himself surrounded by medical staff at the USF Health Eye Institute. The 77-year-old appeared to be in good spirits, but his update made it clear that his recovery isn’t over just yet. “One More Surgery And One More Possible Skin Graft, And Then I Will Be Good To Go! Thank You @USFHealth Eye Institute! 🙏🏻” The update comes just five days after Flair suffered a bloody fall outside a Florida establishment on October 23 . He was taken to Tampa General Hospital with injuries to his face and eye, spending the night receiving treatment before being released the following day. Flair had already been dealing with a serious blood clot in his leg , which forced him to cancel a scheduled autograph appearance in Seattle because doctors wouldn’t allow him to fly. Things got even more concerning after his fall. During the October 25 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer claimed Flair had been drinking at a bar near his home before the accident. He also said Flair returned to that same establishment on October 24, the night after his hospitalization. Flair previously shared a photo of his injured eye and thanked the doctors who treated him. At the time, he assured fans that he was focused on getting better. “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery Right Now. I Will Be Okay!” Now, Flair’s latest update confirms that additional medical treatment is still ahead of him. While he didn’t provide a date for the next surgery or explain exactly why a skin graft might be necessary, he sounded confident about his recovery. The Nature Boy has had a rough stretch between his blood clot, hospitalization, and facial injuries. His latest photo shows him smiling alongside his medical team, but another surgery and the possibility of a skin graft mean he’s still got some healing to do. title: Steve Maclin Details Planning Street Fight With Adam Copeland
raw_title: Steve Maclin Talks About Planning The Match Against Adam Copeland At MLP Northern Rising
body: Steve Maclin talks about planning his match against Adam Copeland. Adam Copeland faced Steve Maclin at the MLP Northern Rising event. This was a Street Fight and also a first-time matchup between the two. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp, Maclin discussed planning this match. “Obviously in my head, too, and I explained it in the documentary. I’m going to probably say that a lot too. I explained it in the two part series on our YouTube page for Boots to Boots. But no, it’s like, ‘Alright, I have this idea. How do we want to do this match?’ I wasn’t sure where we were on the card yet and I had an idea that we might be main event, because why wouldn’t Adam Copeland be main eventing in the Maple Leaf Gardens in his dream match that he’s always wanted? I knew that we would be following matches like Stu Grayson and Josh Alexander, who tore the house down. So it’s like, ‘Alright, now creatively, what do we do that’s different from every other match?’ Like, how do we get to this moment and make the most of this? I think Adam and I, for the day, we put a love letter to our childhoods, of his childhood dream of wrestling there, but then also my childhood dream and everybody else’s childhood dream to pro wrestling where we’re doing all of the opponents that he’s ever faced or teamed with signature moves. It was just beautiful. I’ve never felt more comfort in a wrestling ring and more calmness than I did that night. Again, it’s something I’m going to be chasing for a long time where my ears were open to the people, but every bit of me was in the moment.” “When you have over 3,000 people there in that place, it’s electric energy all night. Canadian wrestling fans are a different breed than American wrestling fans, and the same with the UK. Everybody has their own niche of how they act and their energy. It’s fun to see and it’s always funny that I dreamed of wrestling in Canada, and then I was in WWE for so long, never even stepped foot in Canada except for one of the Takeovers in Toronto that we had early on. I was on the pre-show on that one, but before that I was never really in Canada and I’d been married to Canada pretty much since my time leaving WWE and TNA and then now just in the free agency.” Elsewhere in the interview, Maclin talked about being told about this match. title: Shotzi Blackheart Recalls Asking WWE For TNA Run
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart Says She Asked To Wrestle In TNA During WWE Run
body: Shotzi Blackheart wanted to have a run in TNA toward the end of her WWE run, but says her request was shot down. Blackheart is now part of the TNA roster, somewhere she has always had interest in. She recalled in a recent appearance on Generation of Wrestling how she asked to have a little run in TNA after she returned from her ACL injury in 2024. Blackheart noted that the idea was shot down by WWE, and also spoke about the difficulty of coming back from that injury. You can see the highlights below ( per F4W Online ): “I was trying, I was kind of talking to TNA when I was still signed with WWE. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was really hungry to get in the ring and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA. I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit and he was totally down, but for some reason I wasn’t allowed to. And then when I got released, I needed a second to be on the indies and do me before signing another big contract.” “After a year and a half of just doing me and gaining my confidence back, I felt like, ‘Okay, this is time for me to get back on TV, come to TNA on absolute fire with the most confidence and the biggest balls I have ever had in my career.’ So, I’m really coming to TNA fired up.” “Yeah, it’s almost more grueling mentally than physically, showing up to PT and doing the workouts that you’re told to do is the easy part, right? But the mental part of the pain and the struggle to walk and the struggle of knowing whether or not you’re going to be able to come back to doing the thing that you love is so so hard. Getting past that mental point is so difficult. But I just tried to stay focused on the physical and hang out with friends as much as possible, finding my support system and seeking out nature and writing a ton. I did a lot of writing while I was recovering from my ACL surgery and just reconnecting with all the things that you love.”

Her pitch, which included talks with Tommy Dreamer, was denied by the company. She later took time on the independents to rebuild her confidence before signing with TNA.

A second kick to Priest moments later gave Zayn the pin and a title match against Drew McIntyre at the Royal Rumble. Zayn attacked Yachty earlier in the bout, and the rapper later climbed onto the apron and got involved. Down the stretch, Zayn charged for the kick, but Williams struck first and scored the pin for the title. The match was the WrestleMania debut for Williams, and the win delivered a first main-roster championship. Five days later, Zayn crashed the SmackDown title celebration in the Gingerbread Man costume and attacked Williams and Yachty with a candy cane. title: Real Reason Behind Blake Monroe’s Delayed WWE SmackDown In-Ring Debut
raw_title: Real Reason Behind Blake Monroe’s Delayed WWE SmackDown In-Ring Debut
summary_src: Blake Monroe spent months telling everyone to be patient about her SmackDown in-ring debut, but behind the scenes, she wasn’t nearly as relaxed about the situation as she made it sound. After five months of waiting, Monroe admits she started wondering why the hell WWE wasn’t using her.
body: Speaking on Busted Open Radio , Monroe opened up about the long delay between arriving on SmackDown and finally wrestling her first official match as a member of the roster. Monroe said she was desperate to get in front of the crowd and initially trusted that WWE was simply waiting for the right time. After several months, though, that confidence started getting tested. “Definitely was. I love to work and be out in front of the crowd, but I can’t do that if I’m not out there. So I was chomping at the bit for five months, dying to get out there. I know better than anyone else — timing is everything. I knew in my heart, but it does get to a point months in where you’re thinking, ‘Alright, I train, go to the gym, dress like a million bucks, have my character and ideas, and wanna be out there.’” It wasn’t just frustration either. Monroe admitted she started looking around at other women getting opportunities and thinking about what she could have done if WWE gave those same chances to her. Eventually, that turned into some genuine self-doubt. “I see other girls — I can be better than them. I think if I had shots they had, I would have done more with it. And there is that natural hunger and desire. It can get to a point where you’re questioning yourself and, ‘Why is it not happening for me?’ Ultimately, it’s such a huge machine and so many moving parts and many unpredictable factors, like injuries and other things shifting around.” That also gives a little more explanation for why Monroe’s debut took so damn long. According to her, injuries and other pieces of WWE’s creative plans shifting around contributed to the delay rather than there being one specific issue keeping her off television. Monroe’s response was basically to keep showing up every week with ideas until WWE finally said yes to something. “And for me, it was just every single week turning up and saying, ‘I’m ready for this. Here’s 10 different things I wanna do on the show,’ until one of them sticks, and it did. And you cannot keep me in the back for another week. I did have moments where I questioned myself.” That persistence eventually paid off. After weeks of issues with Giulia, Monroe finally wrestled what WWE billed as her SmackDown in-ring debut on October 2 and walked away with the victory . What makes Monroe’s latest comments interesting is how different things actually felt behind the scenes compared to what she was telling fans at the time. She publicly preached patience and insisted timing was everything, but she was still human enough to wonder whether that opportunity was ever actually going to come. Do you think WWE waited too long to finally give Blake Monroe her chance on SmackDown, or did the delay ultimately work in her favor? Let us know what you think in the comments. It turns out that Keys has been playing wrestling video games for much of his life, which makes being part of WWE 2K26 hit even closer to home for him. "I got kids, so I play all the current stuff," Keys said. "In the past, I think one of my favorite ones that I was obsessed with as a kid was the Royal Rumble for Super Nintendo. And then another one was No Mercy. Then I got into the SmackDown vs. Raw games and the 2K. I even got some emulated games, the old WrestleFest game. I love them all." WWE fans are undoubtedly itching for the chance to play as Keys in WWE 2K26 given how significant a part of WWE programming he has been in recent weeks and months. On the Aug. 24 episode of Raw, Keys debuted the 946 stable with Bronco Nima and Lucien Price helping him attack The Usos, Solo Sikoa and LA Knight. In the following weeks, Keys added Jaida Parker and Carmelo Hayes to the group, making them an even bigger threat to The Bloodline in the process. Keys divulged that he was familiar with every member of 946 before bringing them into the stable, saying, "I knew everybody before we actually all got together. So, 946 is us. We've taken parts of how we grew up and where we're from and put them together, so it's something that's authentic and real." He also stressed the importance of every member playing their part and contributing something unique, which is why Hayes and Parker were fitting choices to align with 946. "We each bring something different," Keys said. "Melo's a little pit bull. When I take that leash off him, it's dangerous. And Jaida, she hits harder than some of the dudes. I always say it's like a pot of gumbo. You've got all these different flavors and mixtures in it, so it's gonna be hard for our opponents to adapt to it." Hayes surprised the WWE Universe during the Oct. 12 edition of Raw when he joined 946 by attacking The Bloodline with a crowbar. title: Netflix Edits Liv Morgan RAW Ending
raw_title: Netflix reportedly censors WWE star Liv Morgan’s near-wardrobe malfunction on RAW
body: The episode concluded with Dominik Mysterio, Morgan's on-screen love interest, carrying her out of the arena, saving her from being cashed in on by Money in the Bank winner Tiffany Stratton. According to Ringside News, if you watch the episode on Netflix now, the final shots, which showed her backside, have been edited . It makes sense, as the streaming service wanted to avoid a wardrobe malfunction being visible on the replay. Morgan retained the Women's World Championship despite losing to Becky Lynch during the Oct. 26 edition of RAW. It was a back-and-forth affair, but it ended in a disqualification after Roxanne Perez and Raquel Rodriguez interfered. They broke up a pinfall attempt from Lynch that might've won the match. Things broke down from there, as the Judgment Day attacked Lynch. Chelsea Green—who will face Morgan at Crown Jewel—came out to save her before Iyo Sky came out as well. Green then hit her finishing move on Morgan, prompting Stratton to come out. She tried to cash in her Money in the Bank contract but hesitated. The hesitation cost her a chance to become a two-time world champion. Mysterio pulled his kayfabe girlfriend out of the ring. The Judgment Day then retreated to close out the show.
summary: The Oct. 26 episode of WWE RAW ended with Dominik Mysterio carrying Women's World Champion Liv Morgan from the arena after Tiffany Stratton hesitated on a Money in the Bank cash-in attempt. According to Ringside News, Netflix has since edited the final shots that showed Morgan's backside to prevent any wardrobe malfunction from being visible on replay. Morgan had retained her title earlier in a disqualification loss to Becky Lynch following interference from Roxanne Perez, Raquel Rodriguez, Chelsea Green and Iyo Sky.

title: Backstage Buzz: Steve Austin’s Plans for 2027 After Wrapping Up First Off-Road Racing Season
raw_title: Steve Austin’s Plans for 2027 After Wrapping Up First Off-Road Racing Season
summary_src: “Stone Cold” Steve Austin isn’t slowing down anytime soon. The WWE Hall of Famer has officially wrapped up his first season of off-road racing, and he’s already making plans to get back behind the wheel in 2027.
body: Austin has spent much of 2026 competing with the Valley Off-Road Racing Association (VORRA) in Nevada under his Broken Skull Racing team. His final race of the season took place on October 24 at Monster Dash 2026, where he qualified well and got off to a strong start before failing to finish the second moto. On October 28, 2026, A ustin took to social media to reflect on his first year of racing and confirm that he’s returning for another season. “The 2026 Broken Skull Racing season is over. We compete in Stock Mod division, and will stay there again for 2027 season. Thanks to @valleyoffroadracingassociation for the great races this year. We will run the VORRA schedule next year and will also hit KOH, Mint, V2R. Thanks to our sponsors for all the help.” Austin drives a Kawasaki race car carrying the number 316, a reference to his famous Austin 3:16 catchphrase from his WWE career. His first season actually got off to a strong start. Austin won the Stock Mod category in his first two races, but things became more difficult as the year continued. During August’s Stomping Grounds 300, Austin made a mistake that knocked him out of the race and left his vehicle with what he described as “pretty good damage.” His final race in October also ended early, but that hasn’t changed his plans. Austin has made it clear that off-road racing is more than just something he does in his spare time. He’s put serious effort into building Broken Skull Racing and plans to expand his schedule next year with additional events beyond VORRA. While wrestling fans last saw Austin make an appearance at WrestleMania 41 in Las Vegas, where he announced the second night’s attendance, much of his attention these days has been on racing in Nevada. Austin might be retired from wrestling, but he’s found another way to compete. With two early wins under his belt and a full racing schedule planned for 2027, the Texas Rattlesnake isn’t finished chasing victories. What do you think about Steve Austin getting into off-road racing, and would you like to see WWE feature his racing career in a future documentary? Let us know in the comments. title: Comeback Watch: Where Things Stand With Vince Russo’s Potential WWE Return Following Discusses
raw_title: Where Things Stand With Vince Russo’s Potential WWE Return Following Talks
summary_src: Vince Russo’s name suddenly getting thrown around with WWE again made it sound like one of the wildest creative comebacks imaginable was somehow on the table. Turns out, things apparently weren’t nearly that serious.
body: According to PWInsider , Russo was actually the one who reached out to WWE President Nick Khan over the summer looking for a potential role with the company. And that was pretty much as far as it got. WWE sources said there was never any real movement toward hiring Russo at any point in 2026. Russo also hasn’t publicly addressed whatever conversations he had with Khan. That clears up a lot after Conrad Thompson dropped the claim that Vince Russo had been in talks about potentially returning to WWE creative. “Hey, hey, it’s Conrad Thompson — and the whispers that shocked me the most this past summer was that the highly controversial Vince Russo was in talks to make a shocking return to WWE creative.” Fightful Select later reported that people at WWE headquarters had heard about conversations between Russo and Khan , although nobody seemed to know exactly how serious they were. There was even talk that Russo either visited WWE HQ or was being considered for a visit. Almost nobody actually working on WWE’s creative product seemed to know a damn thing about it. Agents, producers, writers and other staff hadn’t heard anything about Russo potentially coming back. Some influential people inside WWE apparently even laughed when they were asked about it and now we know why. This also isn’t Russo’s first attempt at getting back into WWE. Vince McMahon briefly brought him back in 2002 with plans for him to run creative, only for that idea to fall apart almost immediately. Russo was offered a consultant role instead, turned it down and eventually went to TNA. Russo also admitted years later that he emailed McMahon offering to help WWE creative before McMahon’s exit from the company, but that went nowhere too. So, there were apparently conversations between Russo and Khan. But Russo wasn’t secretly sitting around waiting for WWE to hand him the creative book. He reached out looking for a job, WWE never moved toward hiring him, and the whole thing died right there. Would you have wanted to see what Vince Russo could do in WWE’s current creative system? Let us know what you think in the comments. Felix Upton Felix Upton has over 15 years of experience in media and wrestling journalism. His work at Ringside News blends speed, accuracy, and industry insight.

title: Ric Flair Needs One More Eye Surgery
raw_title: Ric Flair provides medical update on injured eye
summary_src: Ric Flair will be undergoing some more treatment after injuring his eye in a fall last week. The 77-year-old wrestling icon provided a medical update on social media today, sharing a photo with the team at the USF (University of South Florida) Eye Institute.
body: Ric Flair will be undergoing some more treatment after injuring his eye in a fall last week. The 77-year-old wrestling icon provided a medical update on social media today, sharing a photo with the team at the USF (University of South Florida) Eye Institute. Flair said he’ll need “one more surgery and one more possible skin graft” but is looking forward to getting his eye healed up. “One More Surgery And One More Possible Skin Graft, And Then I Will Be Good To Go!” Flair wrote. “Thank You @USFHealth Eye Institute!” This fall happened outside of Wagamama restaurant and bar in Flair’s current hometown of Tampa, Florida on October 23. He was left “bleeding extensively” from the eye and taken to the hospital by ambulance . After spending the night in the hospital, Flair was back home by Saturday . Flair hasn’t slowed down in the days since getting out of the hospital. On Monday, he posted a picture of himself (with his eye still covered and bandaged up) with his friend and former wrestler Joe Gomez in the area of Tropicana Field where the Tampa Bay Rays are playing in the World Series. A separate medical issue has limited Flair’s travel in recent weeks and months, with him currently unable to travel more than 3-4 hours at a time due to a blood clot in his leg. On the weekend this fall happened, Flair was originally supposed to be in Washington state for a convention before having to withdraw due to his travel limitations . He is scheduled for a procedure to strip the affected vein. Flair was scheduled to be a guest at the annual WrestleCade convention in Winston-Salem, North Carolina next month (November 27-29), but WrestleCade announced today that Flair’s management has informed them he will not be able to appear : Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: Ric Flair, 77, injured his eye in a fall outside a Tampa restaurant on October 23 and was hospitalized overnight. He shared an update from the USF Eye Institute, stating he requires one additional surgery and a possible skin graft before his eye fully heals. In the days following his release, Flair has continued his normal activities, including attending a World Series game at Tropicana Field.

llm_long: Ric Flair was hospitalized in Tampa after suffering a fall on Friday morning. The incident occurred outside a restaurant where he had been at the bar. He left his drink and phone behind before walking across the street and falling suddenly.
The fall caused injuries to his face, including a cut to his head. Flair was transported to a local hospital by ambulance. The reason for his abrupt departure from the restaurant remains unknown.
Hours earlier, Flair had posted on social media explaining that he could not fly to an appearance in Seattle. He cited a blood clot in his leg as the reason he was unable to travel the distance.

In the statement, Flair expressed disappointment over canceling his scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con. He emphasized that he needed to prioritize his health and recovery. Flair mentioned that a procedure is scheduled for the affected vein, after which doctors expect him to be cleared for more travel.

Flair has a history of significant health problems. In 2017, he underwent surgery for a severe intestinal blockage that resulted in a month-long hospital stay. He attributed those issues to heavy drinking and was given only a 20 percent chance of survival at the time.

title: WWE Executive Discussed Vince Russo Return
raw_title: WWE Exec Reportedly Spoke To Vince Russo About Returning
summary_src: Two different reports suggest that WWE executive Nick Khan spoke to former head writer Vince Russo about returning to WWE earlier this summer
body: Vince Russo/YouTube The most popular phrase in pro wrestling is "never say never," particularly when it comes to former WWE stars returning after less than amicable exits. But most would agree that statement didn't apply to Vince Russo, the former WWE head writer turned WCW/TNA booker with a reputation so polarizing that it seemed unlikely he'd ever get a job in a mainstream promotion again. But according to Conrad Thompson, it almost happened. Writing for Uncrowned , Thompson reported that Russo and WWE had talks about him returning over the summer. According to Thompson, the talks between WWE and Russo occurred just before Russo stepped down from his position as booker of indie promotion Juggalo Championship Wrestling in September, leading Thompson to conclude he and WWE had agreed to terms. However, Thompson clarified that not only were the two events unrelated, but that a WWE return was currently off the table for Russo, with Thompson's sources telling him weeks ago that talks "died on the vine." Fightful Select would later follow Thompson's report with one of their own on the subject, one that suggests there was some smoke to the fire. Those connected to WWE headquarters in Stamford, Connecticut did hear that Russo had conversations with WWE President Nick Khan. How serious the talks were, or what they entailed, remain unclear, but they appear to have progressed enough that Russo either visited WWE HQ, or was "under consideration" to do so. These talks, if they did occur, appear to have been kept close to Khan's vest, as much of the WWE's in-house staff had not only never heard of this, but were described as "laughing it off" when asked. Those who work closely with Khan also said they were unaware that he had been talking to Russo, only learning of the discussions when Thompson's story broke.
summary: Conrad Thompson reported that a WWE executive held talks with Vince Russo about a potential return over the summer. The discussions took place shortly before Russo left his booking role with Juggalo Championship Wrestling in September. Per Thompson and a subsequent Fightful Select report, the conversations ended without a deal and a WWE return is currently off the table.

PWInsider.com has confirmed with multiple sources that Bruce Prichard is expected to retire from his position as Executive Director - Creative Writing & Talent (CWT) after Wrestlemania season. We are told Prichard, 63, would remain connected to the company on a consulting basis but would no longer live in Stamford or retain his current duties. One source pegged Wrestlemania as the end of the run, but another cautioned that with pro wrestling being the way it is, there could always be a little leeway on the timeline. In the 1990s, Prichard was best known to fans on camera as Brother Love but primarily worked behind the scenes directly with Vince McMahon as one of his top lieutenants and producers. Prichard left WWE in 2008 and went on to become the host of one of the most popular pro wrestling podcasts Something to Wrestle With , where Prichard and co-host Conrad Thompson did deep dives into events and personalities from WWE’s history. The podcast became so popular that a version of it was brought to the WWE Network for a series of episodes. JBL often co-hosts the show with Thompson currently, but Prichard does still make appearances. As PWInsider.com broke at the time, Prichard was brought back to World Wrestling Entertainment full-time in 2019 to work in a top creative position on the creative team, working directly with Vince McMahon and later, Paul Levesque on creative, including running TV tapings when Levesque was not present. The belief is currently that all three writing teams for Raw, Smackdown and NXT fall under Prichards in the hierarchy of WWE. There is no word yet who might succeed Prichard in his current role, but the company has a lot of time to get there before Wrestlemania this Spring. Prichard originally broke into the business under the legendary Paul Boesch and worked for Impact Wrestling and MLW after exiting WWE in 2008. llm_long: Ric Flair was hospitalized in Tampa after suffering a fall on Friday morning. The incident occurred outside a restaurant where he had been at the bar. He left his drink and phone behind before walking across the street and falling suddenly.
The fall caused injuries to his face, including a cut to his head. Flair was transported to a local hospital by ambulance. The reason for his abrupt departure from the restaurant remains unknown.
Hours earlier, Flair had posted on social media explaining that he could not fly to an appearance in Seattle. He cited a blood clot in his leg as the reason he was unable to travel the distance.

In the statement, Flair expressed disappointment over canceling his scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con. He emphasized that he needed to prioritize his health and recovery. Flair mentioned that a procedure is scheduled for the affected vein, after which doctors expect him to be cleared for more travel.

Flair has a history of significant health problems. In 2017, he underwent surgery for a severe intestinal blockage that resulted in a month-long hospital stay. He attributed those issues to heavy drinking and was given only a 20 percent chance of survival at the time.

I think I can do that. Built a ring in my backyard, and now I’m still doing it. All this time, so. Yeah, it was one of those things. I went to a show in person, and after that, I was hooked. title: Contract News: TNA Talent Expected to Leave Company as Contract Nears Expiration
raw_title: TNA Talent Expected to Leave Company as Contract Nears Expiration
summary_src: George Iceman’s time in TNA appears to be just about over. Unless something changes at the last minute, The Elegance Brand is about to lose its Personal Concierge. According to PWInsider, Iceman’s current TNA contract expires early next month, and the two sides have not agreed to a new deal.
body: According to PWInsider , Iceman’s current TNA contract expires early next month, and the two sides have not agreed to a new deal. TNA is reportedly already preparing to move forward without him. And there may have been a pretty obvious clue on TV. The Elegance Brand appeared in a backstage promo on last week’s Impact on AMC without Iceman. That’s definitely unusual considering how closely he’s been attached to the group and how much of its talking he normally does. Iceman has been around TNA for a while. He originally appeared as a backstage insider dropping news and information before getting a much bigger role in 2024 as Ash By Elegance’s Personal Concierge. That eventually turned into The Elegance Brand, with Heather By Elegance, M By Elegance and Mr. Elegance joining the party. Iceman became one of the most recognizable parts of the whole act, usually serving as its mouthpiece. TNA even let him get physical every once in a while. Iceman made his in-ring debut at Sacrifice 2025 alongside Ash and Heather, although his main role remained outside the ring. Now it looks like the show might actually be going on without him. PWInsider also reports that Iceman has received interest from elsewhere, so he might not be sitting around for very long once his TNA deal officially expires. There’s no word yet on who has been sniffing around. His expected departure would also come during a pretty busy stretch for TNA’s roster. Steve Maclin, Tessa Blanchard , Eric Young , Dani Luna and Myla Grace have already moved on this year, while several more contracts are reportedly coming up over the next eight or nine weeks. TNA President Carlos Silva recently told talent that the company plans to work on getting new deals done, but clearly that doesn’t mean everybody is sticking around. For Iceman, the writing appears to be on the wall. His contract is almost finished, TNA has already started featuring The Elegance Brand without him, and there’s apparently outside interest waiting once he becomes available. What do you think about another potential departure as TNA continues making changes to its roster? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: George Barrios Recalls Finalizing WWE Saudi Deal

body: Former WWE Co-President and Board Member George Barrios recently detailed how the WWE-Saudi Arabia deal was finalized. Barrios recently appeared on Jeff Jarrett’s My World podcast , where he elaborated on how the deal came together. Barrios revealed that since Vince McMahon didn’t want to fly to Riyadh and former WWE Co-President Michelle Wilson wasn’t going because she’s a woman, he had no choice but to head to Saudi Arabia to finalize the deal. The former executive revealed that his wife wasn’t a fan of him traveling to Riyadh. Barrios further revealed that there were guards armed with machine guns, and one of the Princes was in his boxer shorts with a hookah setup beside him. George added that the Prince yelled at him because he felt that WWE was getting too greedy. He described the difficulties in dealing with logistics, as the country had a non-existent ticketing system. However, Barrios added that, for the most part, the Saudis were “really good partners.” Here’s what he said [quotes via Fightful ]: “I was a little worried”- George Barrios about traveling to Saudi Arabia “I remember Michelle’s not going because she’s a woman, and that adds a level of complexity at that point in time, less so, but then it was an issue. Vince (McMahon), I don’t think I wanted to go, honestly, and so I’m like, ‘F*ck it. It’s me!’ I’m up… I like to consider myself this tough street kid. I’ve been in a million fights; I’m not scared of anybody. Blah, blah, blah, blah, blah, but I was like, I was a little worried, and I remember Carol, my wife, was a little worried… We had made the decision: I’m going. We’re going. We’re gonna get this deal done. It’s the night before the earnings call. So usually, I’m home late anyway, because we were prepping… At this point, we hadn’t even been prepping. We were working on this. But I come home, it’s like 1 o’clock in the morning… I gotta turn on the lights, and I gotta pack and she’s like, ‘Pack? Where are you going?’ I go, ‘After the earnings call, I’m flying to Riyadh,’ and she’s like, ‘What!?’ My own personal things, explaining that she was worried about it. George Barrios describes the scene at the meeting; says the Saudi Prince yelled at him “But I get out and I will tell you… I have negotiated deals in every part of the world. I am very comfortable in every part of the world, even when the customs are very different… Broken bread in China, Thailand, India, everywhere, you know? title: Ric Flair Needs One More Surgery After Fall
raw_title: Ric Flair provides update, says he will be ‘good to go’ after one more surgery
summary_src: Ric Flair provides a positive update after suffering a fall last weekend in Tampa, Florida.
body: Recovering after suffering a nasty fall last week, Ric Flair is in good spirits. 77-year-old Flair was hospitalized last Friday after a fall outside a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa, Florida. The incident caused damage to Flair’s left eye, which was seen bandaged heavily afterward. While Flair was released from the hospital over the weekend, he continues to undergo procedures to help him recover from the recent incident. Flair noted in a new social media post that he will be “good to go” after another surgery and possibly a skin graft as well. Thanking the University of South Florida Eye Institute, here’s what Flair said: One More Surgery And One More Possible Skin Graft, And Then I Will Be Good To Go! Thank You @USFHealth Eye Institute! 🙏🏻 pic.twitter.com/NVANvRhloV “ One More Surgery And One More Possible Skin Graft, And Then I Will Be Good To Go! Thank You @USFHealth Eye Institute!” Flair is also currently dealing with a blood clot in his leg, which caused him to cancel an upcoming appearance in Seattle.
summary: Ric Flair, 77, was hospitalized last Friday after falling outside a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa, Florida, resulting in significant damage to his left eye. He has since been released but requires one additional surgery and a possible skin graft before being fully recovered. Flair is also managing a blood clot in his leg that led to the cancellation of a scheduled appearance in Seattle.

llm.headline: Ric Flair Needs One More Surgery After Fall
llm.summary: Ric Flair, 77, was hospitalized last Friday after falling outside a Wagamama restaurant in Tampa, Florida, resulting in significant damage to his left eye. He has since been released but requires one additional surgery and a possible skin graft before being fully recovered. llm_long: Ric Flair was hospitalized in Tampa after suffering a fall on Friday morning. The incident occurred outside a restaurant where he had been at the bar. He left his drink and phone behind before walking across the street and falling suddenly.
The fall caused injuries to his face, including a cut to his head. Flair was transported to a local hospital by ambulance. The reason for his abrupt departure from the restaurant remains unknown.
Hours earlier, Flair had posted on social media explaining that he could not fly to an appearance in Seattle. He cited a blood clot in his leg as the reason he was unable to travel the distance.

In the statement, Flair expressed disappointment over canceling his scheduled appearance at Washington State Horror Con. He emphasized that he needed to prioritize his health and recovery. Flair mentioned that a procedure is scheduled for the affected vein, after which doctors expect him to be cleared for more travel.

Flair has a history of significant health problems. In 2017, he underwent surgery for a severe intestinal blockage that resulted in a month-long hospital stay. He attributed those issues to heavy drinking and was given only a 20 percent chance of survival at the time.

title: By the Numbers: WWE Crown Jewel Moved to New Venue in Saudi Arabia as All Tickets Get Refunded
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel Moved to New Venue in Saudi Arabia as All Tickets Get Refunded
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel is getting a new venue just days before the November 7, 2026 event. After weeks of questions surrounding the show’s status in Saudi Arabia, Riyadh Season has confirmed that the event is being moved, and everyone who already purchased tickets will receive a full refund.
body: On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, the official Riyadh Season Twitter account announced the change, confirming that Crown Jewel will remain on the schedule but take place at a different venue. Fans who already purchased tickets will need to buy them again once the new ticket sale begins. “We would like to inform you that ‘WWE Crown Jewel’ has been moved to a new venue. All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours.” The announcement didn’t identify the new venue or explain why the change was made. However, the promotional image still lists Riyadh as the host city, with Crown Jewel scheduled for Saturday, November 7, at 12 PM ET. The announcement comes after weeks of uncertainty about WWE holding Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia due to ongoing security concerns in the region. TKO CEO Ari Emanuel previously confirmed that the company was monitoring the situation daily and considering alternatives if necessary. Jonathan Coachman also recently claimed WWE would postpone Crown Jewel rather than move it to another city if the Saudi Arabia event couldn’t go ahead. However, the latest announcement is about a venue change within Riyadh, not moving the show out of the country. The timing is also important for fans who already made plans to attend. Everyone with tickets will receive a refund, but they’ll have to purchase new ones when sales reopen within 48 hours of the announcement. Riyadh Season hasn’t explained whether previous ticket holders will receive any priority when purchasing seats. For now, Crown Jewel is still happening on November 7, with Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn among the advertised matches. WWE’s Saudi Arabia plans have already faced plenty of questions, and now fans are waiting to find out exactly where the show will take place. What do you think about WWE Crown Jewel changing venues this close to the event? Do you believe the show should still take place in Saudi Arabia? Let us know in the comments. body: In a post on X, Flair shared a photo of himself posing with multiple doctors and noted that he will be "good to go" after "one more surgery and one more possible skin graft." WWE's Growing Cody Rhodes Problem 🤨 Bleacher Report 34m Grading WWE NXT 🔠 Bleacher Report 15h Backstage Wrestling Rumors 🤫 Bleacher Report 22h TMZ Sports reported that Flair fell outside a Florida restaurant last Friday, causing him to suffer eye and facial injuries. Included in the post was a photo of Flair with a patch over one of his eyes. The 77-year-old Flair is widely regarded as one of the greatest professional wrestlers of all time, having been a major world champion on 16 different occasions. Flair has dealt with numerous health issues over the past several years, including undergoing emergency surgery to remove part of his bowel in 2017. He recovered to the point that he was able to wrestle the final match of his illustrious career in 2022, teaming with Andrade El Idolo to beat Jeff Jarrett and Jay Lethal. Most recently, Flair has worked with AEW, making periodic appearances for the company since 2023.
