title: Five Non-Obvious Will Ospreay Opponents
raw_title: Top Five Less-Than-Obvious Opponents for Will Ospreay to showcase a variety of match styles
body: Modern professional wrestling does a good job with the title chase and creating moments from them. Will Ospreay winning at Wembley Stadium, Stephanie Vaquer winning in Chile, and Cody Rhodes finishing his father’s story are all excellent examples of pro wrestling done well. The problem comes in when it’s time for the champion to have a series of credible challengers. The story doesn’t end when a champion achieves their highest goal; instead, it’s then time to create a legacy with that title run. I saw that as the issue with “Hangman” Adam Page’s run, and am seeing it in WWE with only having two credible contenders for Liv Morgan’s Women’s World Championship. With Will Ospreay, the company has a chance with a special performer to establish the company with real competition and a champion who is able to overcome each challenger for a long run. I want to see Osprey in matches with opponents who are different than what he usually faces. Too many of his opponents will be similar in having matches that are based in workrate. I love a five-star match, but the company has to be more. As I think about the roster and what potential awaits AEW, if it’s the direction Tony Kahn and crew want to see. This would require a split from The Death Riders. Claudio Castagnoli is a main event talent who has been a gatekeeper and tag performer for too long. The man is smart, strong, well-spoken, and knows how to build drama as a heel. If I ever decide to write my top five favorite matches, Sami Zayn vs. Cesaro in NXT will definitely be on the list. A strong beatdown after a full break from his faction and a heel turn, followed up with strong promos saying he’s seen the best and been in the ring with them. Tear Ospreay down as a “high-spot” player, then eventually make match stipulations that blows off the feud in a submission match, filling out some ground game for the champion. Another guy with main event potential, and not as damaged as who is truly like to see. I’d love to see his stablemate Lance Archer have a top program. After watching through Lucha Underground recently, I was reminded of his potential as a powerhouse who works very well with a high-flying opponent. His look and his ring work will make him easy to see as a legitimate threat. To achieve that look, he was recently very open about his use of steroids to enhance his physique. I actually agree with his take, but it’s still controversial to talk about. I hope that openness doesn’t keep fans from seeing the best that the “Half-Man, Half-Machine” can bring to the company. Here is a performer who has shown top level performance in trios, tag, and in singles; a veteran who has worked every style of wrestler who has been at a top level in WWE for multiple decades. Kofi is still in tremendous shape and still pulls off amazing maneuvers. The knowledge that Kofi could impart to Will during a face-face feud could really help Ospreay’s psychology in future matches and give Kofi one more run at the top of the card

After World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns suggested that Zayn might not make it to WWE Crown Jewel as Undisputed WWE Champion, Zayn has been doing everything in his power to prove The OTC wrong. llm_long: Trick Williams made his main roster debut on the January 2 episode of SmackDown by interrupting Sami Zayn during a promo about pursuing the WWE Championship. Williams announced his move to the brand and staked his own claim to the title. Zayn acknowledged the newcomer but cautioned that Williams still required humbling.

Both competitors appeared in a Fatal 4-Way match at Saturday Night's Main Event on January 24 in Montreal. The bout also featured Randy Orton and Damian Priest to determine the number one contender for the undisputed championship. Zayn secured the victory by pinning Priest after a Helluva Kick, despite Williams pulling the referee from the ring to break an earlier count.

Two days before WrestleMania 42, Williams and rapper Lil Yachty appeared on SmackDown with a performer dressed as the Gingerbread Man to mock Zayn. The performer received a Helluva Kick from Zayn in response. Williams then challenged Zayn for the United States Championship on night two of WrestleMania 42.

During the April 19 title match at Allegiant Stadium, Zayn attacked Yachty early, and the rapper later interfered from the apron. Williams countered a late charge from Zayn and scored the pinfall to win the United States Championship. The victory marked Williams' WrestleMania debut and his first main roster title.

Five days after the loss, Zayn returned to SmackDown in the Gingerbread Man costume, disrupting Williams' celebration and attacking both Williams and Yachty with a candy cane. The two met again at Backlash on May 9 in Tampa. Zayn faked an injury, delivered a Helluva Kick to Yachty, and ultimately pinned Williams after a missed kick allowed the Trick Shot to end the match.

Zayn captured the undisputed WWE Championship on June 27 at Night of Champions by rolling up Cody Rhodes in a Triple Threat match that also included Gunther. Johnny Gargano and Ricky Saints aligned with Zayn on SmackDown following the win. Williams interrupted Zayn's address to Gargano on the October 16 episode of SmackDown.

raw_title: WWE RUNNING NORTH AMERICA, CASHING IN THE BRIEFCASE, OF COURSE SAUDI ARABIA AND MORE - PWInsider.com
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin WWE RUNNING NORTH AMERICA, CASHING IN THE BRIEFCASE, OF COURSE SAUDI ARABIA AND MORE By Dave Scherer on 2026-10-28 10:00:00 You can send us questions for the PWInsider.com Q and A at pwinsider@gmail.com . After repeatedly saying that he was not coming back to The Bloodline, Solo Sikoa did a promo on Raw implying that he is back in The Bloodline. Make it make sense! I wish I could, I really do. Obviously he is needed for War Games but it should be as “the enemy of my enemy is my friend” not talking like the group is back together. My guess is that him saying that will be the impetus for LA Knight to join 946, at least for the War Games match. Solo has promised Knight he would not go back to the family and now he has. Plus, Royce Keys went after Solo but never Knight, so it would make sense for Knight to join Keys logically. Does it make sense creatively, given how over Knight is a face? That’s another question altogether. I’m very curious on the difference between WWE running the Saudi Arabia shows especially now where there’s some conflict and something could happen at the show, versus when they used to do the Tribute to the Troop shows in active military war zones where something could have happened at those shows as well. They are very different. WWE flew secretly to bases where they performed for the soldiers at the camp. Their location and itinerary were not common knowledge. In this case, the world knows where they are going. They know where they are flying into. And most importantly, they know the exact place and time where the WWE talent will be. This is a VERY different scenario. I know you hate the briefcase. Monday’s Raw was the perfect illustration why. Tiffany Stratton ran out with the briefcase and ref. She hit a moonsault. Then, she stands there forever wondering if she should cash in. It was ridiculously stupid. What say you? I see you’re ridiculously stupid and I raise you one. title: Stu Grayson Recalls Severing Nerve In Finger With Barbed Wire
raw_title: Stu Grayson Recalls Severing A Nerve In His Finger With Barbed Wire During Ring Of Honor Bout
summary_src: Stu Grayson recalls severing a nerve in his finger with barbed wire during a Ring Of Honor match with John Silver.
body: Stu Grayson recalls severing a nerve in his finger with barbed wire during a Ring Of Honor match with John Silver. Injuries in wrestling are a common danger for the performers in the ring, but sometimes, injuries can happen that fans can be unaware of in the moment, with wrestlers revealing them at a later date. While speaking to Fightful Overbooked’s In The Weeds , Stu Grayson spoke about a moment where he severed a nerve in his finger with barbed wire. “The only time I’ve ever cut my hand really well was actually in Ring of Honor, when we did myself and the Righteous versus Dark Order, at some point in the match, I am wrapping my knee with barbed wire. So then I’m going to knee strike John Silver in the face, and as I’m wrapping my leg, I’m stepping on the barbed wire. So as I pull, the barbed wire went inside my finger so far that it actually cut the nerve. So I lost the use of my finger for like a month. But the doctors told me, don’t worry, that’s going to get back to normal. You didn’t sever the nerve completely. So just wait a bit, and it’s going to come back, and about a month or two later, I had feelings in my fingers again. But that’s like a thing. It’s like one of the worst injuries I’ve had, and it’s nothing, really. It’s me. But it’s the kind of thing that no one in the ring even knew about. So the fans can’t even say, ‘oh, my God, he almost cut off his finger.’ Like, you don’t even see it. But it was so painful. But you can’t even brag about it because it’s just dumb.”
summary: Stu Grayson discussed an incident from a Ring of Honor match against John Silver where he wrapped his knee with barbed wire and accidentally pulled it into his finger, severing a nerve. He lost use of the finger for about a month but was told by doctors that the nerve was not completely severed and would recover with time. Grayson shared the story while speaking to Fightful Overbooked’s In The Weeds podcast.

title: Latest On Vince Russo-WWE rumors
raw_title: Update on Vince Russo-WWE rumors
summary_src: It doesn’t sound like there was ever really much of a chance of Vince Russo returning to WWE in 2026.
body: It doesn’t sound like there was ever really much of a chance of Vince Russo returning to WWE in 2026. A column Conrad Thompson published for Uncrowned this week broke the news that Russo “had a series of conversations with WWE President Nick Khan about a possible return to WWE this past summer.” However, Thompson noted that the idea “died on the vine” and did not lead to Russo being brought back to the company. Fightful backed up Thompson’s report but said it was unclear how serious the conversations between Russo and WWE were. PWInsider adds that it was Russo who initiated contact with Khan, and there was no movement toward officially hiring Russo at any point this year. Russo was part of WWE creative during the Attitude Era and went on to work for WCW, TNA Wrestling, and Juggalo Championship Wrestling. In 2021, when Vince McMahon was still in charge of WWE, Russo reached out to him about a potential consultant role. McMahon offered to have Russo watch WWE programming for a couple of weeks and send in his suggestions. Working for free wasn’t something Russo was willing to do, and McMahon then retracted the offer. Though a controversial figure in pro wrestling, Russo and Violent J of Insane Clown Posse both spoke highly of each other during Russo’s time with Juggalo Championship Wrestling. It was announced last month that Russo and JCW had parted ways under amicable terms . summary_src: Jay White apparently came pretty damn close to joining the Death Riders last year, and AEW reportedly had a huge angle planned to make it happen. The only reason fans never saw it was because White got hurt before AEW could pull the trigger.
body: Speaking during a Self Made Session , Self Made Pro discussed Jon Moxley’s victory over Swerve Strickland at AEW Dynasty 2025 and claimed the original finish was supposed to look completely different. title: Macho Man Randy Savage drops Flying Elbow on hobby with record sale of WWE championship belt
raw_title: Macho Man Randy Savage drops Flying Elbow on hobby with record sale of WWE championship belt
body: The holy grail of baseball cards just set another record at Heritage Auctions, but it was an historic, non-traditional sports relic that stole headlines in the Fall Sports Catalog Auction . The auction, which generated $25.6 million in sales, was topped by a restored example of the iconic 1909-11 T206 White Border Honus Wagner card, which sold for $1.98 million, a record for a restored Wagner. But the main event of the auction was a professional wrestling belt worn by such WWE legends as Randy Macho Man Savage, Tito Santana, Ricky Steamboat and The Honky Tonk Man. The 1985-88 WWE Intercontinental Championship belt worn by Tito Santana, Randy Savage, Ricky Steamboat and The Honky Tonk Man sold for $716,750, demonstrating the demand for historically significant professional wrestling memorabilia. It was a record for a championship wrestling belt, shattering the previous record set by Hulk Hogan’s WrestleMania II belt from earlier this year. The “Red Letter’ belt was purchased by wrestling memorabilia collector and noted wrestling podcaster Conrad Thompson. The championship belt was at stake in one of wrestling’s most famous matches, the March 29, 1987 bout between Macho Man Savage and Steamboat at WrestleMania III. Though the event was headlined by the main event between Hulk Hogan and Andre the Giant, the Savage-Steamboat match is widely regarded as one of the greatest matches in professional wrestling history, with Steamboat defeating Savage to capture the Intercontinental Championship. According to Heritage, the Reggie Parks-inspired belt was used from 1985-88 and won by four WWE Hall of Famers during professional wrestling’s golden era. It was not the only wrestling relic to attract big dollars in the auction as a Circa 1999 Stone Cold Steve Austin Match-Worn & Signed Knee Brace with WWE Letter Signed by Linda McMahon drew 39 bids and sold for $225,700. The sales follow two other record wrestling sales by Heritage this year. In February, it sold Hulk Hogan’s photo-matched WrestleMania I boots for $1,037,000 , followed in August by the $414,800 sale of his WrestleMania II championship belt .
summary: It was a record for a championship wrestling belt, shattering the previous record set by Hulk Hogan’s WrestleMania II belt from earlier this year. The championship belt was at stake in one of wrestling’s most famous matches, the March 29, 1987 bout between Macho Man Savage and Steamboat at WrestleMania III.

title: On the Record: Shotzi Blackheart Says WWE Wouldn’t Let Her Wrestle In TNA
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart Says WWE Wouldn’t Let Her Wrestle In TNA
body: Shotzi Blackheart says she begged WWE to let her have a run in TNA after returning from ACL surgery, and that Tommy Dreamer "was totally down, but for some reason I wasn't allowed to." Copy link Get more Wrestling News in Google Choose us as a and our stories show up more in your Google results. Shotzi Blackheart says she asked WWE to let her wrestle in TNA while she was still under contract, but was not allowed to. Blackheart told the Generation Of Wrestling Podcast that she made the request after returning from ACL surgery. “I was trying, I was kind of talking to TNA when I was still signed with WWE. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was really hungry to get in the ring and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA,” Blackheart said. “I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit and he was totally down, but for some reason I wasn’t allowed to.” “And then when I got released, I needed a second to be on the indies and do me before signing another big contract,” she continued. Blackheart signed with TNA this month and said she is arriving with more confidence than ever. “After a year and a half of just doing me and gaining my confidence back, I felt like, ‘Okay, this is time for me to get back on TV, come to TNA on absolute fire,'” she said. “So, I’m really coming to TNA fired up.” Blackheart tore her ACL in a match against Lyra Valkyria at an NXT taping. She said the mental side of the recovery was harder than the physical side. “It’s almost more grueling mentally than physically, showing up to PT and doing the workouts that you’re told to do is the easy part, right? But the mental part of the pain and the struggle to walk and the struggle of knowing whether or not you’re going to be able to come back to doing the thing that you love is so so hard,” Blackheart said. She said spending time with friends, finding her support system, getting out in nature and writing helped her through it. “I did a lot of writing while I was recovering from my ACL surgery and just reconnecting with all the things that you love,” she said. Blackheart has made a full recovery and has been wrestling since her return in 2024. She left WWE in May 2025 when her contract expired, and has since worked for GCW, MLW and other independent promotions. She held the MLW Women’s World Featherweight Championship for more than 200 days. TNA announced her signing on October 19. She previously wrestled for the company in 2018 and 2019, when it was known as IMPACT Wrestling. title: WWE Legend The Rock Unrecognizable After Stunning Transformation for New Role
raw_title: WWE Legend The Rock Unrecognizable After Stunning Transformation for New Role
body: The Rock, whose real name is Dwayne Johnson , is preparing to tackle another dramatic role and is fully immersing himself in character. Last year, the WWE legend earned critical acclaim for his portrayal of MMA pioneer Mark Kerr in The Smashing Machine . That film was directed by Benny Safdie, with whom ‘The Final Boss’ is reuniting for his latest film. Safdie and The Rock posted photos from the set of Lizard Music , which is being filmed in Brooklyn, New York. WWE legend The Rock underwent a full transformation for his new role in Lizard Music. The Rock plays Chicken Man, a 70-year-old man. The role requires a significant commitment from the WWE legend, as he needed make a physical transformation. The Rock notably packed on more muscle mass and had a hulking figure in The Smashing Machine . However, in Lizard Music , he is a lot leaner because he is playing an elderly man. In the first set photos that emerged, the WWE legend is sporting a wig, hat, and earrings on both his ears. Additionally, The Rock reportedly underwent five hours of makeup and prosthetic work each day. It will be interesting to see how The Rock’s performance is received by critics and audiences. He earned a Golden Globe nomination for The Smashing Machine . This proved that he is capable of taking on more dramatic roles that are less action-oriented than those in the Fast & Furious franchise. The Rock shared details about his role as Chicken Man in Lizard Music . He spoke highly of his cast and crew, particularly Safdie, who is directing the film. “I’m with Benny Safdie again. That’s my guy,” The Rock told Deadline . “I play a septuagenarian man. Now, I didn’t know what the hell that meant. So, I had to Google it. It means you’re in your 70s.” The WWE legend also explained his reasoning for ultimately agreeing to the play the role of an elderly man. At this stage of his career, The Rock noted that the role was another challenge, which he embraced. “We’re in our second week, and it has already been an unbelievable experience. It’s that thing I was telling the kids, ‘Run towards that thing.’ This is that thing that I ran towards and chased the challenge, and this was a challenge for me. I love Benny, he’s one of my best friends and embraced collaborators, so I can’t wait for you to see it,” The Rock said. The news was announced on the Riyadh Season Twitter/X page : “We would like to inform you that ‘WWE Crown Jewel’ has been moved to a new venue. All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours.” Powell’s POV: The Saturday, November 7 event was scheduled to be held at Riyadh Season Stadium. Based on the wording of the tweet, it looks like the show will be moved to a different location in Saudi Arabia. It’s unclear why the show was moved. WWE has yet to publicly address the change as of this update. نود التنويه أنه تقرر نقل عرض “WWE كراون جول” إلى موقع جديد، وسيتم استرداد كامل قيمة التذاكر لجميع المشترين، على أن يُعاد طرح التذاكر للجميع خلال الـ48 ساعة المقبلة. summary: WWE Crown Jewel scheduled for Saturday, November 7 has been relocated to a different venue in Saudi Arabia. The Riyadh Season Twitter account announced that all current ticket holders will be given a full refund while new tickets will go on sale to the public within the next 48 hours. WWE has not yet commented publicly on the reason for the venue change or the new location.

title: Royce Keys Calls WWE 2K26 Roster Spot a Great Accomplishment
raw_title: Royce Keys Says Being Added To WWE 2k26 Is 'A Great Accomplishment', Celebrates Not Having To Create Himself Anymore
summary_src: Royce Keys speaks about being added to WWE 2k26's roster, noting that it is a 'great accomplishment' and celebrates not needing to create himself. As part of the Season 6 Ringside Pass in WWE 2K26, fans will be able to add Royce Keys to their in game roster.
body: Royce Keys speaks about being added to WWE 2k26’s roster, noting that it is a ‘great accomplishment’ and celebrates not needing to create himself. As part of the Season 6 Ringside Pass in WWE 2K26, fans will be able to add Royce Keys to their in game roster. Additionally, Earthquake, Typhoon and Octagon Jr. will also be made playable with this season. While speaking to Bleacher Report in a new interview, Royce Keys spoke about his addition to the game. “It’s a great accomplishment because I think I’ve played almost every WWE video game, and I’ve always created myself,” Keys said. “And now I don’t have to do all the hard work of finding all the right moves, but it’s definitely a very high accomplishment for me.” Keys continued, noting his affection for the WWE games series. “I got kids, so I play all the current stuff,” Keys said. “In the past, I think one of my favorite ones that I was obsessed with as a kid was the Royal Rumble for Super Nintendo. And then another one was No Mercy. Then I got into the SmackDown vs. Raw games and the 2K. I even got some emulated games, the old WrestleFest game. I love them all.”
summary: Royce Keys will be added to the playable roster in WWE 2K26 as part of the Season 6 Ringside Pass alongside Earthquake, Typhoon and Octagon Jr. In an interview with Bleacher Report, Keys described the inclusion as a major personal milestone since he has created himself in nearly every prior WWE game and will no longer need to manually select his moveset. He also recalled growing up playing Royal Rumble on Super Nintendo, No Mercy, SmackDown vs. Raw titles and the 2K series while noting he now plays current games with his children.

title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 shifts to new Riyadh venue
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 moving to new venue, still expected for Saudi Arabia
summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is moving venues, but it appears the event will still be held in Saudi Arabia. The Riyadh Season social media accounts sent out a notice today saying that the November 7 PLE has been moved to a new venue.
body: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is moving venues, but it appears the event will still be held in Saudi Arabia. The Riyadh Season social media accounts sent out a notice today saying that the November 7 PLE has been moved to a new venue. Those who purchased tickets will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released within the next couple of days, seemingly indicating that Saudi fans will still have a chance to purchase them. Further details, including what the new venue is, were not announced. But the graphic still advertises the show for Riyadh and lists the same 12 p.m. Eastern/9 a.m. Pacific start time that was planned. PWInsider and Fightful have both reported that the PLE is still expected to be held in Riyadh. Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD (King Abdullah Financial District) was originally set to host the show. Other options in the area include “The Venue,” (anb Arena) which is where a Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli boxing match will take place this Saturday. The Six Kings Slam tennis tournament is also set to be held there this December (after being postponed from its original October dates). WWE has been monitoring the situation amid weeks of violence in Saudi Arabia that’s included the Iran-backed Houthi rebels targeting the main airport in Riyadh. TKO executive Ari Emanuel said last week that everything was still set for Crown Jewel to take place from Saudi Arabia. Setup for the event began in recent days . title: Royce Keys Eyes Bloodline WarGames Clash
raw_title: Royce Keys On The 946 Potentially Facing The Bloodline Inside WarGames: Just Take What We've Done Now And Multiply It By A Hundred
summary_src: Royce Keys discusses the possibility of The 946 battling The Bloodline inside WarGames, and what it would mean if they were to do so. Since forming on the WWE main roster, The 946 have had one specific target: The Bloodline.
body: Royce Keys discusses the possibility of The 946 battling The Bloodline inside WarGames, and what it would mean if they were to do so. Since forming on the WWE main roster, The 946 have had one specific target: The Bloodline. The two factions have gone to war, with Roman Reigns entering the fray on last week’s WWE Monday Night RAW, leading fans to expect the two factions to meet inside the WarGames double cage structure at Survivor Series. While speaking to Bleacher Report in a new interview, Royce Keys spoke about being aware of all 946 members before the faction began. “I knew everybody before we actually all got together. So, 946 is us. We’ve taken parts of how we grew up and where we’re from and put them together, so it’s something that’s authentic and real.” Keys also spoke about the strengths that each member brings to the faction. “We each bring something different,” Keys said. “Melo’s a little pit bull. When I take that leash off him, it’s dangerous. And Jaida, she hits harder than some of the dudes. I always say it’s like a pot of gumbo. You’ve got all these different flavors and mixtures in it, so it’s gonna be hard for our opponents to adapt to it.” Finally, Royce spoke about the possibility of The 946 facing off with The Bloodline inside WarGames. “It’s something we would love to be a part of,” Keys said. “If we are in it, just expect the unexpected, and just take what we’ve done now and multiply it by a hundred.”

The two factions have been feuding on WWE programming since The 946 formed on the main roster, with Roman Reigns getting involved on last week's Monday Night RAW. body: After spending the majority of his career in a tag team/faction, Bishop Kaun is currently on the hunt for Bandido and his ROH World Championship. Speaking with The Sportster for a new interview , Kaun explained why he’s finally going after a singles titles in ROH. “I think it’s just time. My legacy in Ring Of Honor has always been the greatest six man champion of all time. It’s awesome to be a tag champion, a trios champion, but I think it’s time to define my own legacy and why not take Bandido’s championship? He’s trying to be one of the greatest ROH world champions of all time? No, no, no, no. Not on my watch.” After touching on his history with Bandido, Bishop Kaun reassured fans of The Demand. “Again, I just think it’s my time to step out and showcase who I am as Bishop Kaun. All you ever see is me in STP, The Embassy, The Demand. I do love The Demand, I’m still a member of The Demand, but I think it’s time I create my own lineage and create my own dynasty here at Ring Of Honor.” Check out the current lineup for AEW Fright Night Dynamite by clicking here . title: Matt Hardy Questions AEW Fans' Reception Of Adam Copeland As Champion
raw_title: Matt Hardy Doesn't Think AEW Fans Would Accept Adam Copeland As World Champion
summary_src: If Adam Copeland were to win the AEW World Championship, Matt Hardy believes some of the company's fans would criticize the decision.
body: AEW/Speedy Ruiz Adam Copeland recently announced that he plan to retire by the end of next year , but before that, he's got his eyes set on the AEW World Championship. Copeland's former WWE rival Matt Hardy doesn't think all AEW fans will be happy if Copeland realizes his dream, which he explained during his " The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy " podcast. "It would be a great way to send him out," Hardy said. "It's just sometimes I get so concerned, because even the AEW fans — somebody like Adam, who's still an amazing performer at his age, and he can still go and have good matches — a lot of times they go, 'Well, he's just an older guy,' or, 'He's a WWE guy.' ... I feel like they would be a little critical of him as champion." As for his own feelings on the matter, Hardy said he'd be happy to see Copeland win the company's top title. Hardy doesn't see Copeland as someone who would politick his way into winning the belt, and that even as the AEW World Champion, he'd continue helping the younger talent in the locker room. So far, Copeland has had one shot at the title since his announcement, failing to capture the belt after being an entrant in the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream . Despite this, Hardy is still hopeful that Copeland will end up successful. "I wouldn't rule it out," he stated, while agreeing with his co-host Jon Alba that beating Will Ospreay for the belt would likely not be the best route.
summary: Matt Hardy believes some AEW fans might criticize Adam Copeland as world champion due to his age and past with WWE. Hardy discussed this on his podcast while noting Copeland remains an excellent in-ring performer. Hardy added he would personally support Copeland winning the title and praised his character for continuing to develop younger wrestlers.

title: Backstage Buzz: WWE Hall of Famer Booker T Threatened To Fight Fellow Wrestling Legend Backstage
raw_title: WWE Hall of Famer Booker T Threatened To Fight Fellow Wrestling Legend Backstage
body: 0 WWE legend Booker T has recalled threatening to fight fellow wrestling legend, Fit Finlay, backstage over stiff kicks during their match in WCW. The duo faced off in multiple matches between 1998 and 1999. However, one particular match with Finlay left Booker T in pain, prompting a reaction backstage. Speaking on his Hall of Fame podcast, Booker discussed the challenges of wrestling with stars known for their stiff and physical styles. Although Booker T had no problem with taking hard strikes, he thinks the safety and well-being of wrestlers is important. According to Booker, Finlay caught him near the kidney with a hard kick. He stated, “I didn’t mind stiff, but I needed safe at the same time. And I remember working a match with Fit Finlay, and he snapped me and kicked me in the back, but he caught me, like, in the kidney area. Man, it really hurt, man. It really, really hurt.” After the match, Booker T made his feelings clear to Finaly backstage. Booker recalled warning Finaly, “I remember telling him when he came back through the curtain, I said, ‘Bro, kick me like that again, you know, we’re going to be fighting, you know, next time when you come back through the curtain.'” That warning was enough to ensure the situation never happened again. Booker T also confirmed that it never happened again after that incident. Fit Finlay is famous for being a hybrid of a tough European technician and a hard-hitting brawler. And given his stiff style, absorbing hard strikes in matches was almost an occupational hazard for his opponents. Currently, Finlay works as a producer and coach for WWE, while Booker T is one of the voices of NXT broadcast. Booker T recently revealed that he thought he was going to lose his spot after making an on-air commentary mistake. Nonetheless, later in the interview, Booker T also acknowledged that he also delivered some stiff strikes to his opponents. One of the recipients of his strikes was Paul London. However, Booker maintained that the injury was accidental and a result of a collision at an unfortunate moment. title: Sami Zayn Details Real Emotions in WWE Title Loss to CM Punk
raw_title: Sami Zayn explains emotional reaction to WWE title loss to CM Punk
summary_src: Sami Zayn says there were genuine emotions behind his reaction to losing the WWE Championship to CM Punk. Zayn lost the title on the July 6, 2026 edition of WWE Raw from Chicago, just nine days after winning it at Night of Champions.
body: Sami Zayn says there were genuine emotions behind his reaction to losing the WWE Championship to CM Punk. Zayn lost the title on the July 6, 2026 edition of WWE Raw from Chicago, just nine days after winning it at Night of Champions. Speaking with Chris Van Vliet recently on Insight , Zayn explained that while he’s always in character on screen, some of his character’s emotions came from genuine feelings he has carried for years. Zayn was asked about his character’s “emotional” last few months and the emotions he showed following his title loss to Punk. “It’s in character, obviously. I’m not shooting. I am a professional, believe it or not, and I am in character when I’m doing these things. “ However, when Van Vliet mentioned that some of the tears Sami shed following the title loss “may have been real,” Sami responded: “ Because you’re accessing something real. And here’s the thing, everything I’m saying on TV, up to and including last week, where I’m talking about how I’m disrespected and I’m not viewed in the same kind of way that other champions are respected, it’s all coming from a real place. It’s all coming from insecurities I’ve had for a very long time.” “It’s coming from a real place. So, that’s why, when people are like, ‘Oh man, this character stuff, it feels real.’ Well, it’s 100% real. It did take me 20 years to win the title and I did lose it in nine days. That’s the character story. It’s also the real story.” “I have all these legitimate gripes as a character, but they all follow the real-life trajectory, not only of the character, but of the real person.” “My stuff has been so public and the character has so much of me and my real story in it that it’s so easy to blur that line, because, yeah, the character worked 20 years to get here and lose it in nine days, but so did the person. So people can buy it and I can buy it when it’s time to emote.” A little over two months after Zayn dropped the title to Punk, he won it back from Punk on the September 11 edition of Friday Night SmackDown in Mexico City, Mexico. Since regaining the title, Zayn has had successful title defenses against Kevin Owens on the September 18 SmackDown and against Je’Von Evans on the October 26 episode of Raw. Zayn is scheduled to face World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns in a champion-versus-champion match at WWE Crown Jewel on November 7. Zayn’s full appearance on Insight with Chris Van Vliet is available below. The video is queued to his comments referenced above. He joined the F4WOnline team in 2019 and was named Managing Editor in the summer of 2026. Born in Calgary, Alberta, Ian has covered professional wrestling for more than 15 years.

He noted that his promos about being disrespected and not viewed like other champions stem from real experiences.

llm_long: Sami Zayn began the year by facing Drew McIntyre for the Undisputed WWE Championship at the Royal Rumble. Following the defeat, Zayn believed his opportunity to become world champion had ended.

Zayn stated on a podcast that he started to accept the possibility of winning the title had passed him by. He noted that despite coming close during his involvement with The Bloodline, the underdog story felt worn out and his momentum had decreased.

Zayn explained that after the loss to McIntyre he concluded the Cinderella narrative of the persistent underdog finally winning the big one could not be repeated. He felt fans could only be drawn into that story a limited number of times and that the timing was no longer right.

Zayn reflected that he had already enjoyed a strong career and viewed a world title as an optional addition rather than an essential part of his legacy. He emphasized the need to consider the larger perspective beyond any single accomplishment.
Zayn later captured the Undisputed WWE Championship at Night of Champions. His first reign lasted nine days before CM Punk defeated him on SmackDown.
Zayn regained the title in September after securing revenge against Punk.

title: WWE Crown Jewel shifts venues within Riyadh
raw_title: WWE is moving Crown Jewel, but currently just to another venue in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
body: On Wednesday, WWE announced it would move Crown Jewel, but only to another location in Riyadh. Originally scheduled for Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD, the venue and WWE said Crown Jewel would be moved due to security concerns in the region. "We would like to inform you that "WWE Crown Jewel" has been moved to a new venue. All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours." News in the area reports that there have been explosions heard in Riyadh, as Saudi military forces intercepted ballistic missiles. These attacks over the last few weeks prompted the U.S. State Department to order nonessential employees to leave Saudi Arabia. Despite this, the WWE held firm that the event in Riyadh would still take place as scheduled. Wednesday's announcement initially made it sound like the company would move the event to a new country, but for now, staff members and wrestlers are still scheduled to go to Riyadh, just to an unnamed rescheduled location. The Crown Jewel PLE event began in 2018 and has been held every year other than 2020. Six of the seven iterations have been held in Riyadh, while last year's show was held in Perth, Australia. This is a unique event because in 2024 it was established that the PLE itself would have its own championship. It isn't contested on week-to-week television, but each year the top men's and top women's champions from Raw and SmackDown will meet in a match. The winner of those two matches will earn the men's or women's Crown Jewel Championship. There is still time to set another match. Every past Crown Jewel event has had at least five matches. Last year's in Australia had eight, while the most recent in Riyadh had seven.
summary: WWE announced it is relocating Crown Jewel to a different venue in Riyadh due to regional security concerns. The original site was Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD, with all existing ticket holders receiving refunds and new tickets going on sale within 48 hours. The event, which began in 2018 and has taken place annually except for two years, will still occur in the Saudi capital as staff and wrestlers remain scheduled to travel there.

summary_src: A new report reveals the contract of Elegance Brand's Personal Concierge, aka George Iceman, is set to expire soon, with him drawing interest from outside TNA
body: TNA/George Iceman/X Though TNA has recently been in talent acquisition mode, bringing in names such as Shotzi Blackheart and Shayna Baszler , there continues to be talk of the promotion losing more names as several contracts come due later this year . And one name to keep an eye on is a talent best known for what he does outside of the ring as opposed to inside it. False Finish reports that George Iceman, better known as the Elegance Brand's Personal Concierge, will see his contract expire soon, and that promotions outside of TNA are believed to be interested, though no promotions were named. A source with knowledge of the situation indicates to False Finish that George Iceman's contract with TNA is coming up soon and there's some interest outside of TNA pic.twitter.com/vMawf3wx2d Not to be mistaken for NBA legend George "Iceman" Gervin, George Iceman was a relatively unknown figure in wrestling before he debuted in TNA in early 2024 as the "Personal Concierge" for Ash By Elegance, fka WWE star Dana Brooke. Iceman has continued to serve as Ash's manager since, and has become an integral part of the Elegance Brand stable alongside Heather By Elegance, M By Elegance and Mr. Elegance. Primarily serving as the group's manager and mouthpiece, Iceman has competed in one match, teaming alongside alongside Ash and Heather at TNA Sacrifice 2025. It was a successful evening for Iceman, Ash, and Heather, as he helped the duo defeat Jody Threat and now AEW star Dani Luna in a 3 on 2 handicap match to win the Knockouts Tag Team Championships. Though best known for his TNA stint, Iceman has worked outside of the promotion, including Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling , where he managed Gisele Shaw when she defeated Kylie Rae to win the Maple Leaf Pro Wrestling Women's Canadian Championship at Northern Rising in May 2025. Iceman's MLP biography also reveals that he has experience promoting wrestling, having worked with the Canadian independent promotion Destiny Wrestling.
summary: Per False Finish, George Iceman, known as the Elegance Brand's Personal Concierge and manager for Ash By Elegance, will see his TNA contract expire soon. Multiple promotions outside of TNA have shown interest in the performer who joined the company in early 2024. This development comes amid broader discussions about several other TNA contracts set to expire later this year.

title: Bruce Prichard Needs Serious Surgery
raw_title: Additional Details On Reports Of Bruce Prichard's WWE Retirement
summary_src: Additional details regarding the reported retirement of WWE backstage official Bruce Prichard were revealed.
body: WWE After it was first reported by PWInsider on Tuesday that WWE backstage executive Bruce Prichard is set to retire following WWE WrestleMania 43 , new details surrounding his impending departure have been revealed. Prichard is currently the executive director of creative writing and talent, a position he's held in the company since June 2020. According to Fightful Select , Prichard is in need of "very serious surgery," and sources claimed that he would remain with WWE, but would be working more from home. An internal memo about the former Brother Love went out within the company earlier this year, regarding his status, but details weren't available. The outlet also reported Prichard has been filling in for Paul "Triple H" Levesque, running shows in recent weeks while Levesque has been out for vacation. Fightful also noted that when asked about the return of Prichard to the "Something to Wrestle" podcast, his co-host, Conrad Thompson, said that they may be able to "figure something out" when Prichard is no longer living in Stamford, Connecticut, the home of WWE headquarters. Thompson said that he believes that's going to be his former co-host's "foreseeable future," however. PWI reported that Prichard's reported new consulting role following his retirement would allow him to no longer live in Stamford. Fightful also noted that they heard Prichard's situation would likely allow him to move from the area, but conversations about him returning to the podcast haven't taken place. "Something to Wrestle" has continued with WWE Hall of Famer John Bradshaw Layfield behind the microphone with Thompson. A source noted to PWI that while Prichard's reported retirement, or role change, is rumored to happen post-WrestleMania next year, as with anything in professional wrestling, the timing is subject to change. No reports have indicated a potential replacement for him.
summary: Per Fightful Select, WWE executive Bruce Prichard requires very serious surgery and will continue working with the company from home after an internal memo was sent earlier this year about his status. Prichard, who has served as executive director of creative writing and talent since June 2020, has been filling in for Paul Levesque while he is on vacation. His co-host on the Something to Wrestle podcast, Conrad Thompson, indicated they may resume episodes once Prichard no longer lives in Stamford, Connecticut.

title: Myles Borne Finds WWE NXT 'What?' Chants Funny

summary_src: Myles Borne says he found it funny when fans at the WWE Performance Center chanted “What?” during one of his promos. Borne, who is partially deaf, cut a promo on the September 29 edition of NXT explaining his recent attacks on Tavion Heights.
body: Myles Borne says he found it funny when fans at the WWE Performance Center chanted “What?” during one of his promos. Borne, who is partially deaf, cut a promo on the September 29 edition of NXT explaining his recent attacks on Tavion Heights. During the promo, fans started giving him the “What?” treatment. Speaking with KRON4’s The Finish with Kor & Tor , Borne said he didn’t even realize there was a “What?” chant going on until he watched the segment back with closed captioning. “The only reason I even knew there was a ‘What?’ chant is because when I watched it back, there was closed captioning, so I was able to pick up on it. To me, that just shows me, you’re really doing ‘What?’ chants to a guy that can’t even hear? You’re wasting your energy. You’re going to have to be a lot louder than that if you want to try to get my attention.” “I think it’s funny. They know the situation, and yet they’re sitting there yelling and just keep saying the Whats. I love it.” “Once I watched it back and saw what they were saying, great, thank you. I appreciate it.” Borne is scheduled to face Heights in a Weapons Wild match this Saturday, October 31, at NXT Halloween Havoc. Borne is on a bit of a losing streak in NXT at the moment. Along with Heights, he dropped the NXT Tag Team Championships to the Vanity Project at NXT Heatwave on August 30. That same night, he dropped the NXT North American Championship to Jackson Drake. He’s since wrestled Heights three times at NXT non-televised live events, going to a double countout each time. His last match on record was a loss to Tony D’Angelo in an NXT Championship No. 1 contender’s match on the October 13 NXT show. Borne’s full interview with KRON4 is available below. llm_long: WWE NXT wrestler Myles Borne opened up about facing lifelong bullying during a recent interview with KRON 4. Borne discussed his recent heel turn and how he is no longer afraid to create enemies with others. He revealed that throughout his life he has dealt with bullies who focused on his hearing aids and speech impediment.

Borne explained that for years he chose to be the bigger person by treating others the way he wanted to be treated though not everyone responded in kind. He recalled having intrusive thoughts about confronting his bullies but refrained because he was taught to only defend himself if someone put their hands on him and never to start a fight but always to finish one.

The former champion noted that some fans initially supported him only because he was known as the deaf guy. Borne said those same supporters would then criticize his speech on social media. He added that many people with disabilities including hearing impairments share his feelings and particularly dislike when others pity or pander to them.

Borne stated that he does not want sympathy because others assume he cannot do what they can and pointed out that he is the one performing in the ring while they watch him on television from home. Borne is a former WWE NXT North American Champion and Tag Team Champion who recently turned heel.

title: Comeback Watch: Vince Russo Responds to Rumors of Potential WWE Return
raw_title: Vince Russo Responds to Rumors of Potential WWE Return
summary_src: Vince Russo has finally addressed all the talk about him potentially returning to WWE, but anyone hoping for a straight yes-or-no answer isn’t getting one. Russo says he has “nothing to talk about” right now — and he’s also pretty pissed at the people reporting the story.
body: Speaking on The Coach & Bro Show , Russo addressed the rumors after reports connected him to conversations with WWE President Nick Khan over the summer. Russo started by pointing out that he’s been reading stories about himself everywhere, but claims none of the people reporting on the situation actually bothered to contact him. “So I have made a reputation of not lying and telling the truth. Since 8 o’clock last night, I am reading all kinds of rumors about me from everybody — starting with Conrad Thompson, James Romero, Sean Sapp, a million different comments and stories. Let me be clear — none of those people contacted me or tried to contact me. And all of those people have my number. Let me tell you, don’t try to contact me now because I stated it already, and now it’s too late.” Russo then compared the situation to the recent speculation surrounding his run with JCW. His point was basically that if there’s something he wants people to know, he’ll eventually tell them himself. “I wanna make it clear to the audience listening to me — I do not lie. With everything you’re reading, just like the stuff you were reading about JCW, guys, when I have something to say, I will say it! If there is nothing to say, I’m not gonna say anything. Everyone went on about JCW, then I said, ‘Guys, I wasn’t ready to say anything and talk about it,’ and now I am, and I did, and made everything clear.” As for the WWE story specifically, Vince Russo didn’t confirm or deny that he reached out to Khan. Instead, he repeatedly said there’s simply nothing he’s willing to discuss right now. “So what I’m saying is, right now, there is nothing for me to talk about. I have nothing to talk about right now. If that changes and there is something I need to talk about, this audience will be the first to know. It’s that simple, and I wanted to make this clear.” Russo wasn’t finished either. He then took aim at the reporters covering the story, calling anyone who runs with something about him without contacting him first a “hack.” “A guy that does have a degree in journalism and worked for TV stations, and a guy that wrote three books — when you’re running with stories and you don’t contact the subject of those stories, bro, I’m sorry, you’re a hack, and you’re not properly doing your job.” Russo’s comments come after PWInsider reported that he was actually the one who reached out to Khan over the summer looking for a potential WWE role . WWE sources said nothing ever progressed toward officially hiring Russo at any point in 2026. Conrad Thompson originally kicked everything off by claiming Russo had been in talks about a shocking return to WWE creative. Fightful Select later reported that people at WWE headquarters had heard about conversations between Russo and Khan , although the seriousness of those talks was unclear. Holidays, weddings, funerals, and family events were all things he was willing to sacrifice, and the people working alongside him were expected to demonstrate that same level of commitment. “24/7/365, he didn’t take holidays. He He did what everybody in this business will talk about. He missed weddings, he missed funerals, he missed ball games. Is he He missed a lot. He sacrificed. And his work ethic is unparalleled. I’ve never been any Never have I met anyone that works as hard as Vince McMahon and it’s in It is both inspiring and and and and it is paralyzing because it will trying to keep up with him is absolutely impossible.” That wasn’t even the most concerning part of Heyman’s explanation. He said McMahon had a habit of pushing employees harder whenever they demonstrated additional talent or ability. Instead of rewarding someone for meeting expectations, McMahon would raise those expectations even further. Heyman described it as a situation where employees were pouring everything they had into a company that ultimately benefited McMahon more than anyone else. “It It is being a slave to the cause uh to which he benefits more than anyone. And and you just sit there and say, ‘How can I keep up with these expectations?’ Because his expectations change the the further you grow and the more ability you show, the more then he’s Oh, I can get more out of this person. He compared employees to vehicles that McMahon would continue driving until they could no longer function. “And it’s at the same time it’s it’s He’s riding He’s riding that He’s riding that vehicle until the wheels fall off. title: John Cena Drank for 10 Straight Days Before Iconic Shawn Michaels Match
raw_title: John Cena Drank for 10 Straight Days Before Iconic Shawn Michaels Match
summary_src: John Cena and Shawn Michaels’ famous hour-long RAW match has become one of the most remembered matches from Cena’s run on top, but apparently he didn’t exactly get much time to prepare for it. In fact, Cena was reportedly enjoying a beer when he found out what WWE had waiting for him the next night.
body: Speaking on The Coach & Bro Show , Jonathan Coachman recalled being in the UK when WWE decided Cena and Michaels would wrestle for around 60 minutes on RAW. According to Coachman, neither man had been given much advance notice about the plan. Coachman happened to be drinking with Cena when Dean Malenko walked over with the news. “I’ll never forget, we were in the UK, and Cena and Shawn Michaels did a 60-minute match. They weren’t told about it until the night before. I was standing there having a beer with John Cena — we were drinking together for 10 straight days. Then Dean Malenko walks up to Cena and whispers in Cena’s ear. John takes his beer, puts it on the counter, walks to the elevator, and he was gone.” Coachman had no idea what Malenko had just told Cena, so naturally, he asked. That was apparently all Cena needed to hear. He immediately put his beer down and disappeared, knowing he suddenly had one hell of a night ahead of him. “I was like, ‘Dean, what did you say to Cena?’ He goes, ‘Oh, I just got a call from the office, and he’s gotta go 60 minutes with Shawn Michaels tomorrow on RAW.’” Coachman said he later waited at Gorilla Position after the match because he wanted to show Cena some respect. He had traveled with Cena and understood the pressure that came with being the guy WWE was building its shows around. “And I waited at Gorilla. This is what the old-school mentality is. I used to ride with John. I wanted to respect him and the fact that he was responsible for the house. I stood there at Gorilla for him to walk back. He does his waddle and butt sticking out. You could smell the alcohol coming out of his pores because he was drinking for 10 straight days — and had a banger.” The match went down on the April 23, 2007 episode of RAW in London, with Michaels eventually defeating Cena after nearly an hour. Coachman’s story paints a pretty wild picture of how things worked back then — Cena went from drinking with the crew to suddenly being told he had to wrestle Shawn Michaels for an hour, and still went out there and delivered. What do you make of John Cena getting such little notice before being asked to wrestle Shawn Michaels for nearly an hour? Let us know what you think in the comments. Derek Holloway Derek Holloway is a writer at Ringside News specializing in professional wrestling news, rumors, and results. He focuses on delivering reliable coverage across WWE, AEW, and major wrestling promotions.

title: On the Record: Shotzi Blackheart Opens Up On WWE Rejected Her Request To Work With TNA Wrestling
raw_title: Shotzi Blackheart Reveals WWE Rejected Her Request To Work With TNA Wrestling
body: Shotzi Blackheart has revealed that she attempted to secure a run with TNA Wrestling while still under contract with WWE, but the company ultimately refused to grant her permission. During a recent appearance on the Generation of Wrestling podcast, Blackheart discussed her desire to return to the ring following her recovery from a torn ACL in 2024. The former WWE Superstar explained that she had been in contact with TNA’s Tommy Dreamer about potentially working for the promotion, with Dreamer reportedly interested in making the arrangement happen. “I was trying, I was kind of talking to TNA when I was still signed with WWE. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was really hungry to get in the ring and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA. I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit and he was totally down, but for some reason I wasn’t allowed to,” Blackheart said. Although the proposed arrangement never materialized, Blackheart eventually found herself with an opportunity to explore other promotions following her WWE departure in May 2025. Rather than immediately committing to another major wrestling company, she decided to spend time on the independent circuit and rebuild her confidence. “And then when I got released, I needed a second to be on the indies and do me before signing another big contract,” she explained. Blackheart said that the time away from a major television promotion allowed her to rediscover her confidence and prepare for the next chapter of her career. After officially joining TNA earlier this month, she believes she is returning to the spotlight with a renewed sense of determination. “After a year and a half of just doing me and gaining my confidence back, I felt like, ‘Okay, this is time for me to get back on TV, come to TNA on absolute fire with the most confidence and the biggest balls I have ever had in my career.’ So, I’m really coming to TNA fired up.” The former WWE star also opened up about the difficulties she experienced while recovering from her ACL injury, which occurred during an NXT match against Lyra Valkyria. While the physical rehabilitation was demanding, Blackheart admitted that the emotional and psychological challenges were often even more difficult. “Yeah, it’s almost more grueling mentally than physically, showing up to PT and doing the workouts that you’re told to do is the easy part, right? But the mental part of the pain and the struggle to walk and the struggle of knowing whether or not you’re going to be able to come back to doing the thing that you love is so so hard.” Blackheart credited her support system, friendships and personal interests with helping her navigate the recovery process. She explained that spending time outdoors, writing and reconnecting with activities outside wrestling played an important role in maintaining her mental well-being. “Getting past that mental point is so difficult. But I just tried to stay focused on the physical and hang out with fri

title: Paul Heyman Claims Vince McMahon Took Pleasure in Ruining His ECW Revival
raw_title: Paul Heyman Claims Vince McMahon Took Pleasure in Ruining His ECW Revival
summary_src: Paul Heyman still hasn’t forgotten what happened when WWE brought ECW back in 2006, and he’s making it clear that Vince McMahon was a huge part of the problem. According to Heyman, McMahon didn’t just take away his creative control.
body: During an interview with Graham Bensinger , Heyman was asked about the worst argument he ever had with McMahon. He immediately pointed to WWE’s decision to resurrect ECW in 2006, which was supposed to put Heyman back in charge of the promotion he helped make famous. However, Heyman claims that promise didn’t last long. He said McMahon began stripping away his authority almost immediately after telling him he would be running the brand. “2006 when he when he relaunched ECW, told me he was putting me in charge of it, and 30 seconds later started stripping me of any authority that I had in controlling or contouring or tailoring or or creating the product.” Heyman then explained why he believes McMahon approached the ECW revival the way he did. At that point, WWE had already established itself as the dominant wrestling promotion, and McMahon no longer had a major competitor capable of challenging him. According to Heyman, that created an opportunity for McMahon to bring back ECW, put its original creative mastermind in charge, and then demonstrate that he could control the product however he wanted. “And again, if you dumb it down to try to explain it to somebody that doesn’t understand, it goes like this. Vince had no one left to compete with. He was the only game in town. Any other game was a minor league. Wasn’t even a B team. It wasn’t even a C team. It It was Pee Wee League compared to WWE. So, he resurrects ECW. Which was going down in history and still goes down in history today as Paul Heyman’s vision. He puts Paul Heyman in charge. Paul Heyman is now representing ECW and Vince McMahon can change the ECW creative and the ECW product on Paul Heyman.” Heyman characterized the situation as Machiavellian, suggesting the creative disagreements went far beyond two people having different ideas about how a wrestling television show should operate. Bensinger then pushed back and asked whether Heyman genuinely believed that was McMahon’s motivation. Rather than backing away from the accusation, Heyman insisted that even after all these years, he still sees the situation the same way. “I can look at it in the most objective way today and I can tell you in my heart of hearts or in a cold-blooded business assessment, no matter what perspective I take in looking at it, it’s exactly what happened.” Heyman went even further, directly accusing McMahon of taking satisfaction in changing ECW against his wishes. He believes their personal power struggle damaged the brand, hurt WWE, and ultimately left the fans with an inferior product. “He got off changing ECW on me. And it became just such a personal battle that was one terrible for the product, terrible for the company, even worse for the audience.” Looking back on that period, Heyman didn’t attempt to soften how miserable the experience had become. WWE’s version of ECW was a major departure from the original promotion’s identity, and Heyman’s comments offer his explanation for why things went so badly behind
summary: Heyman was asked about the worst argument he ever had with McMahon. Paul Heyman is now representing ECW and Vince McMahon can change the ECW creative and the ECW product on Paul Heyman. Heyman characterized the situation as Machiavellian.

title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Moves to New Riyadh Venue
raw_title: WWE is finally moving Crown Jewel, but just to another venue in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia
body: "We would like to inform you that "WWE Crown Jewel" has been moved to a new venue. All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours." WWE's Crown Jewel 2026 Premium Live Event (PLE) is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 7. The annual event has been held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for six of its seven occurrences. News in the area reports that there were explosions heard Wednesday in Riyadh, as Saudi military forces intercepted ballistic missiles. Continued attacks over the past few weeks prompted the U.S. State Department to order nonessential employees to leave Saudi Arabia. Despite this, the WWE has held firm that the event in Riyadh would still take place as scheduled . Wednesday's announcement initially made it sound like the company would move the event to a new country, but for now, staff members and wrestlers are still scheduled to go to Riyadh, just to an unnamed rescheduled location. The Crown Jewel PLE event began in 2018 and has been held every year other than 2020. Six of the seven iterations have been held in Riyadh, while last year's show was held in Perth, Australia. This is a unique event because in 2024 it was established that the PLE itself would have its own championship. It isn't contested on week-to-week television, but each year the top men's and top women's champions from "Raw" and "SmackDown" will meet in a match. The winner of those two matches will earn the men's or women's Crown Jewel Championship. Women's Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green World Tag Team Championships: The Vision (champions) vs. Penta & Je'Von Evans There is still time to set another match. Every past Crown Jewel event has had at least five matches. Last year's in Australia had eight, while the most recent in Riyadh had seven.
summary: WWE announced that its Crown Jewel 2026 Premium Live Event, set for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has been relocated to a different venue within the same city. Ticket holders will receive full refunds, with tickets going back on sale within 48 hours. The move follows recent regional tensions including reported explosions and missile interceptions, though WWE has maintained the event will proceed in Riyadh as originally planned.

title: Ex-WWE EVOLVE Star Veronica West Recreates Another Iconic American Psycho Scene
raw_title: Ex-WWE EVOLVE Star Veronica West Recreates Another Iconic American Psycho Scene
summary_src: Veronica West apparently wasn’t finished with American Psycho after grabbing an axe and recreating one of the movie’s most infamous scenes earlier this month.
body: West uploaded another American Psycho video on Twitter , recreating the famous scene where Christian Bale’s Patrick Bateman walks viewers through his obsessive routine. The video starts with West in the bathroom noticing a camera and mouthing, “What the f***?” before heading into the kitchen and beginning her day. She then starts narrating her life in the same cold, overly serious style Bateman uses in the movie. Of course, West’s version is considerably more ridiculous, with references to bothering her parents, killing a bug and stealing her sister’s pudding cups. “I’m currently staying in Tucson, Arizona, in the Marina District, bothering my parents. My name is Veronica West, 22 years old. There is a bug on my mirror. I squash it, and it leaves a mark. I believe in taking care of myself with a balanced diet and rigorous exercise. I stole my sister’s pudding cups — dumb b****.” From there, West moves into the exercise and skincare portion of the routine, doing some stretching and jumping jacks before applying different products to her face. She keeps the dead-serious Bateman delivery going while throwing in some pretty wild descriptions of what she’s using. “After my IBS settles, I stretch. I make sure my muscles are intact. I will not look like a fool. I apply a banana bubble mask and let it soak into my skin. In order to keep myself young, I apply some anti-aging serum — it looks like semen. I shake up this hydrating spray and spray it on my face.” West saves one of the biggest American Psycho references for the end of the video. She puts her own spin on Bateman’s famous monologue about there being an “idea” of Patrick Bateman rather than a real person underneath everything, while flashing some very Bateman-esque smiles at the camera. “There is an idea of a Veronica West, some sort of abstraction, but there is no real me — just an entity and borderline personality disorder and IBS.” This isn’t West’s first time going full Patrick Bateman either. On October 19, she dressed up in his signature clear raincoat , grabbed an axe and recreated the infamous Paul Allen scene, even referencing Bateman’s Huey Lewis and the News speech with the caption, “One of their undisputed masterpieces☝️.” Apparently one American Psycho recreation just wasn’t enough. West has now gone from axe-wielding Patrick Bateman to skincare-routine Patrick Bateman in the space of nine days, so she seems pretty committed to keeping the bit going. Which American Psycho scene should Veronica West recreate next if she keeps this series going? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Michin and B-Fab Win First WWE Tag Titles
raw_title: Michin And B-Fab Discuss Winning Their First Championships In WWE
summary_src: Michin and B-Fab have finally secured gold in WWE. In line with their recent winning streak, the duo of Michin and B-Fab were able to defeat Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley for the Women's Tag Team Championships on the October 23 episode of WWE SmackDown.
body: In line with their recent winning streak, the duo of Michin and B-Fab were able to defeat Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley for the Women’s Tag Team Championships on the October 23 episode of WWE SmackDown. In a new interview with Complex Graps , Michin talked about winning her first title in the company. “It’s still surreal for me because I’ve been in WWE for almost a decade, but I’ve been wrestling for almost two decades now. I think growing up — being in WWE has always been my dream and of course when you hear somebody say, ‘Oh, I want to be in the NFL’ or ‘I want to be a movie star’, it’s like, okay, sure. Family and friends supported me, but it’s like, it’s good to have dreams but let’s be real. So, finally getting signed to WWE, that was the ceiling for me. There’s nothing else I could do. But then, I like to challenge myself and the next challenge was getting gold in WWE and because it took so long — understanding that one, being a babyface and doing things by the book and trying to be friends with everybody, it was difficult. No matter how hard I worked, I could split my face in the middle of the ring and I got [claps], then it was forgotten the next week. It was a dream to get gold in WWE, but as time went on I kinda accepted that maybe it wasn’t in the cards for me. But hey, I’m living my dream so I’m just going to be happy with that. Once again, aligning with B and Jade, it’s like, we actually may have a chance here. Now that we got Jade on our side, we really have a chance. It kind of reignited the fire of the new goal, of getting gold but also getting gold with B in this group. It’s surreal, man. We won it in my hometown, so I had family. My old next door neighbor was in the crowd. It was cool to like see my childhood out there, getting calls from my dad and my sister. It’s still surreal to this day.” B-Fab followed that up with a similar message, detailing that her slow but “crazy” evolution in WWE. “It’s definitely surreal, it hasn’t sunk in fully. I have those moments where I get emotional and it sinks in, but then I’m still kind of like, ‘Oh my gosh, this is crazy.’ For me, coming from managing, I was with Hit Row first and I was like managing them. Then went in to be with the Profits, doing some managing there. I finally was able to break off and wrestle on my own. I was like super happy to be able to do that and just happy about the growth. When I got put with Mia, I was like, okay cool. We have an actual tag team here, we can do more. All the evolution of everything was just really cool. Getting to transition from that spot of being in the manager position to being able to wrestle in the ring, it’s just crazy to see how everything has really just kept elevating from that spot.“ Check out the current lineup for the October 30 episode of SmackDown by clicking here . llm_long: B-Fab parted ways with The Street Profits in February 2025 and formed a tag team with Michin. Both wrestlers were absent from television programming at the beginning of 2026. They made their return on the February 20 episode of SmackDown.

Michin approached Jade Cargill backstage on that show while holding a kendo stick and accused the reigning WWE Women's Champion of causing her an injury. Prior to the March 20 SmackDown, B-Fab and Michin's most recent televised matches had been defeats against Cargill.

The dynamic changed during the March 20 SmackDown when Cargill declined to face Rhea Ripley, who had won the Women's Elimination Chamber match, and attempted to exit the ring. B-Fab and Michin prevented her departure, initially suggesting a confrontation before aligning with Cargill.

The three then assaulted Ripley, finishing the attack with Cargill's Jaded maneuver. In a subsequent post on X, Cargill referred to B-Fab and Michin as friends due to their common adversary in Ripley. The group remained united even after Ripley captured the WWE Women's Championship at WrestleMania 42.

On May 23 at Saturday Night's Main Event in Fort Wayne, Indiana, Cargill, B-Fab and Michin defeated Ripley, Charlotte Flair and Alexa Bliss in a match that lasted 16:45. Cargill secured the victory by pinning Ripley with Jaded following a pump kick from one of her partners.

B-Fab and Michin competed against Flair and Bliss in a tag team match on the May 15 SmackDown. After Bliss executed Sister Abigail on B-Fab and covered for the pin, Cargill dragged Bliss from the ring, resulting in a disqualification that spared B-Fab from being pinned.
The trio continued their assault on Flair and Bliss following the bell. Bliss shared images of her bruised elbow on X the following day.

body: Link @njpw1972 As we know thanks to the one and only Mr. Ares , New Japan Pro-Wrestling put on a big show today (Oct. 12) in Tokyo’s legendary Ryōgoku Kokugikan. The 2026 King of Pro Wrestling event didn’t disappoint, and included a lot of interaction with New Japan’s partner promotion in the United States, AEW. We knew that AEW World champion Will Ospreay would be on hand, as he was booked to defend the NEVER Openweight Six-Man belts with his “O.G.” United Empire mates HENARE and Great-O-Khan. They were unsuccessful, dropping the titles to the popular Knockout Bros tag team of Yuto-Ice and OSKAR who teamed with their new Unbound Co. brother Jeff Cobb. The finish saw HENARE to the Bros KOB finisher after accidentally headbutting O-Khan, and Ospreay was held back from breaking up the pin. Issues between Ospreay and United Empire’s leader in New Japan, Callum Newman, were also a factor in the match. After a ref bump, Newman showed up to slide his team a steel chair. Bruv didn’t use it, which led to a heated exchange between the two Englishmen. Will said post-match that he wants to challenge for the Knockout Bros for the IWGP Tag titles at next month’s big Power Struggle show, and Yuto-Ice agreed provided Ospreay’s partner is Newman… Seems like a big match between Newman and Ospreay should be coming our way soon, and with the Tokyo Dome less than three months away… We also appear to be on the verge of a Jon Moxley/Shingo Takagi clash. Takagi recently defeated Claudio Castagnoli, and has been lobbying for a match against his fellow former IWGP World champ. He used Moxley’s finisher while picking up another win for Unbound Co. besides teammate Daiki Nagai in King of Pro Wrestling’s opener, and then received this message via the big screen at Sumo Hall. “The Death Riders ride East; Jon Moxley returns to New Japan Pro Wrestling.“ Takagi responded by insisting he be Mox’s opponent. If that match happens in an NJPW ring, as we assume it would, it will be the first time Moxley’s wrestled there in more than two years. title: Meltzer Predicts WWE John Cena Classic on AEW PPV Date
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Thinks WWE Will Announce John Cena Classic For Same Day As AEW PPV
summary_src: Dave Meltzer says he would be on WWE announcing the John Cena Classic for the same day as the AEW PPV Worlds End, which will feature the finals of the C2
body: The first week of November is a big week if one is a fan of John Cena appearing on WWE TV, as the "Matchbox" star is set to be on both "WWE Raw" and "NXT," with Cena teasing that his "Raw" appearance will feature full details regarding his John Cena Classic competition scheduled for December. Most believe these details will include when, and where, the Classic will take place, though Dave Meltzer thinks he's already got it figured out. Discussing Cena's upcoming appearance on Tuesday's "Wrestling Observer Radio," Meltzer suggested WWE will be looking for a certain December date in order to combat a big AEW show. "It's going to be very interesting," Meltzer said. "We'll see if it's December the 19th. I'm kind of betting December 19, because that's the day of the AEW PPV." AEW is scheduled to run their end of the year PPV, Worlds End, on December 19 out of the Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota . If WWE decides to run the John Cena Classic against Worlds End, it would more than likely mean it would be competing directly against the finals of AEW's Continental Classic tournament, which has taken place at Worlds End ever since the first edition of the tournament three years ago. Counterprogramming AEW events has become almost as common as WrestleMania for WWE over the last few years, with the promotion using "NXT" and AAA to go head to head with AEW shows such as All In. Most recently, WWE ran a Worlds Collide taping in Chicago the same day AEW ran All Out in September, though WWE ultimately declined to air the show against the PPV, instead posting it on YouTube to go against AEW's tribute to PAC on "AEW Dynamite." The two sides will next go head to head next week, as "NXT" is moved to Wednesday to avoid mid-term election coverage on Tuesday night. Prior to the announcement of Cena's appearance, reports had indicated that "NXT" was looking to "load up the show" against "Dynamite," which will feature two Blood & Guts matches.
summary: Dave Meltzer believes WWE will schedule the John Cena Classic for December 19 to directly oppose AEW's Worlds End pay-per-view. Cena is set to appear on both WWE Raw and NXT in early November, where he is expected to provide full details about the December tournament. Worlds End is scheduled for that date at the Target Center in Minneapolis, with its finals likely clashing against the Cena Classic if WWE follows through.

title: WWE Crown Jewel Moves to New Saudi Venue
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel PLE moving to new venue, event expected to remain in Saudi Arabia
body: The WWE Crown Jewel PLE is moving to a new venue, but it is expected that the show will still be held in Saudi Arabia. The Riyadh Season Instagram account released the following statement : “We would like to advise that it has been decided to move the WWE Crown Goal show to a new location, and all buyers will be refunded in full, so that tickets will be re-released to all within the next 48 hours.” There were no other details released including where the show will be held, but the graphic accompanying the post on IG did list the same Nov. 7 date for the event and start time of 12 p.m. ET. The announcement comes a week after The U.S. State Department ordered nonessential diplomatic personnel and their family members to leave Saudi Arabia after a string of escalating attacks by the Iran-backed Houthi rebel group. Several scheduled events in Riyadh have already either been canceled or postponed to date.
summary: WWE's Crown Jewel premium live event is shifting to a different location in Saudi Arabia while keeping its scheduled November 7 date and 12 p.m. ET start time. The Riyadh Season Instagram account announced the change, stating that all ticket buyers will receive full refunds and new tickets will be available within 48 hours. The move follows the U.S. State Department's order for nonessential diplomatic staff to depart Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels, which has already led to other events in Riyadh being canceled or postponed.
