title: 911 Audio Indicates AEW Star Pac’s Eyes Were Open When His Body Was Discovered Inside a Rental Car
raw_title: 911 Audio Indicates AEW Star Pac’s Eyes Were Open When His Body Was Discovered Inside a Rental Car
body: 911 audio has revealed new details from the scene where the body of All Elite Wrestling star Benjamin Satterley (a.k.a. Pac) was found last month. “I was getting in my car and the person next to me is passed out in their car. She doesn’t look too well and the car’s running,” a caller told a Cooks County Sheriff’s Office dispatcher in audio obtained by TMZ on Wednesday, October 7, mistaking Satterley for a woman. The caller added, “I tried knocking on her window to see if she’s OK and she’s not responsive at all.” Satterley was found dead behind the wheel of an Enterprise rental car in the parking lot of a Cava restaurant in Des Plaines, Illinois, on September 27. He was 40. The individual who called police indicated they had tried banging on Satterley’s window for five minutes, but he was unresponsive. When asked approximately how old Satterley was, the caller said, “I can’t even tell, her face is straight down” adding, “Their eyes are open, too.” The caller confirmed Satterley was “definitely not” breathing. When authorities arrived at the Cava parking lot, Satterley was pronounced dead at the scene, according to a report from the Des Plaines Police Department obtained by Us on Monday, October 5. Once police searched Satterley’s vehicle, they found a wallet and phone in the center console. The wallet was used to confirm the late wrestler’s identity. Authorities “did not find any injuries or suspicious markings on him besides what appeared to be saliva on the front of his shirt.” Two suitcases and a backpack were found in the trunk of the car, with the backpack containing some medication. When Satterley’s phone was observed, Google Maps was open with O’Hare Airport in nearby Chicago listed as the intended destination. Less than 24 hours before his body was found, Satterley competed at the AEW All Out pay-per-view event in Hoffman Estates, Illinois. Satterley’s cause and manner of death are still pending, the Cook County Medical Examiner’s office told Us on September 28. An autopsy was performed on the same day his body was discovered, with results taking up to “several weeks.” The late wrestler’s body was announced by All Elite Wrestling on September 27. “A native of Newcastle upon Tyne, England, Satterley began his wrestling career in 2004 and went on to perform for wrestling organizations all over the world, captivating fans with innovative high-flying moves and incredible in-ring ability,” the company’s statement read. “Pac signed with All Elite Wrestling in 2019 and held multiple AEW Championships and competed in some of the most memorable matches in AEW history. body: Sol Ruca says she’s been told she will likely never turn heel in WWE because of her naturally bubbly personality. During a recent interview with KRON4’s The Finish with Kor & Tor, Ruca was asked whether she could turn heel in the future. “I have no idea. I think I would love to be able to try that.” “I have been told in the past that I most likely will not be heel ever because of just how I am naturally. I am quite a bubbly person.” “So I don’t know. I feel like it’s going to take a very special person to really get that side out of me, but I guess we’re just going to have to wait and see.” Sol Ruca recently got to wrestle in Hawaii, where she previously lived, when WWE presented two live events at the Neal S. Blaisdell Arena in Honolulu on October 16 and October 17. Ruca won a four-way match against Bayley, IYO SKY, and Lyra Valkyria on the first night and competed in a four-way Women’s World Championship match won by Liv Morgan , also involving SKY and Stephanie Vaquer, on the second night. Ruca was in the Women’s Money in the Bank ladder match won by Tiffany Stratton on October 10 PLE in New Orleans. She has since defeated Lyra Valkyria on the October 14 episode of WWE Main Event and Candice LeRae on the October 21 episode. Ruca’s full interview with KRON4 is available below. body: Speaking to First Coast News while promoting Blood and Guts on November 4 at VyStar Veterans Memorial Arena in Jacksonville, Khan was asked what fans should expect from the show. He started by breaking down the two-ring steel cage concept before calling Blood and Guts AEW’s biggest episode of Dynamite of the year. Khan then turned his attention to the price of actually getting into the building. He claimed AEW currently offers the most affordable tickets in televised professional wrestling and promised fans that the Jacksonville show would be worth what they spend. “Blood and Guts is a two-ring, double steel cage match with some of the greatest wrestlers in the world fighting it out, and the only way to win the match is to make your opponent submit or surrender. And it is just absolutely as advertised. You’re going to see some blood, and you’re going to see great wrestlers, great wrestling, and it’s going to be hard-hitting. It’s going to be exciting. “Wednesday Night Dynamite has become one of the top shows on cable, and this is our biggest episode of the year. So it’s very fitting for our debut at VyStar that we’re bringing this episode on Wednesday, November 4. “You can get your tickets now at AEWTIX.com. That’s AEWTIX.com, and I guarantee it’s going to be worth the value. AEW also has the most affordable tickets in TV wrestling. I guarantee you we’re not going to take an arm and a leg for this. This is going to be a good night at the wrestling matches, and I am very proud of what we’ve been able to do here. “It was being associated with the Jaguars, being associated with the city of Jacksonville, that made it possible to launch AEW. It was right out here in January of 2019 that we told the world we’re launching a new wrestling promotion. We said it 600 feet from where you and I are standing right now, and it’s coming here to VyStar. “You’ve got to be there for Blood and Guts, Wednesday, November 4. It’s going to be one of the greatest wrestling events ever in Jacksonville, I promise you.” Jacksonville obviously means a lot to Khan and AEW considering the company’s history with the city, so he isn’t treating this like just another Dynamite. Between calling it AEW’s biggest Dynamite of the year and promising fans won’t have to pay “an arm and a leg” to attend, Khan clearly wants a packed house when Blood and Guts comes to VyStar. title: Royal Rumble Wins by Entry Number
raw_title: Is No. 30 Really the Luckiest Spot? Royal Rumble Wins by Entry Number
body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin Is No. 30 Really the Luckiest Spot? Royal Rumble Wins by Entry Number By Kendall Jenkins on 2026-10-28 13:45:00 Every January the same question comes up in every group chat: which number do you want? Conventional wisdom says late is better. Come in at No. 30, skip the first hour of punishment and walk into a ring full of tired bodies. Draw No. 1 and you might as well start planning your elimination. The record book tells a more interesting story, and it says a lot about the difference between luck and booking. On paper, the Rumble is a numbers game. Thirty men enter at regular intervals, and the man at No. 1 has to survive the whole match while the man at No. 30 only has to survive the end of it. If the winner were selected at random, every number would have an equal 1-in-30 chance. With nearly 40 men's Rumbles in the books, that would mean each slot producing a winner once or maybe twice. Instead, a handful of numbers have stacked up several wins each, while plenty have never produced a winner at all. That pattern alone tells you the results are anything but random. No. 27 and No. 30 are the slots most often cited as the luckiest in Rumble history, with more winners than any others. It isn't hard to see why. A late entrant arrives fresh, gets a big crowd reaction, and can be booked as the final threat without anyone needing to explain how he survived an hour. Cody Rhodes is the textbook modern example. He came in at No. 30 in 2023 and went on to win, a booking that made sense both for the story and for the crowd that wanted him to finish it. At the other end of the draw, three men have won from the No. 1 spot: Shawn Michaels in 1995, Chris Benoit in 2004 and Edge in 2021. Those wins are memorable precisely because they go against the logic of the match. Lasting the full distance is a story in itself, the underdog who outlasts everyone, and it's one WWE only tells when it has the right performer to sell it. Not every winner comes from the extremes. Jey Uso won from No. 20 in 2025, a reminder that a mid-card entry can work just as well when the story points that way. A middle number lets the winner have a long enough run to build momentum without the near-impossible endurance angle of No. 1. Here's the catch. On television, entry numbers are drawn, but in reality they are decided by the creative team.. Every "lucky" number in the record book is a booking decision: who needs to look strong, who needs a long run, who needs a big pop late in the match. The No. 30 slot isn't lucky because of the number. It's lucky because it's where WWE puts the guy it wants to win. That's what makes Rumble number debates so much fun. You're not really asking about the odds. You're trying to read the minds of the people writing the show. Compare that with a game where the numbers genuinely are generated randomly. summary: Conventional wisdom holds that entering at number 30 in the Royal Rumble is advantageous because it means avoiding most of the match and facing a fatigued field. However, historical results show a more nuanced picture where certain entry positions have produced multiple winners over nearly 40 men's Royal Rumbles while others have zero. The data illustrates how booking decisions influence outcomes more than pure statistical probability.

Following her recovery from ACL surgery in 2024, Blackheart pitched the idea of appearing for TNA to WWE officials. The request was turned down even though NXT and TNA have an active partnership. At the time Blackheart was active on the NXT roster and also being considered for a potential storyline on SmackDown.

She explained that WWE believed adding TNA to her schedule would have been too much to manage alongside those commitments. Blackheart took to social media to follow up on the interview, stating there was no negativity behind her comments. In indirect remarks she noted that her intention was simply to express her longstanding desire to work with TNA and her enthusiasm for making it fit with an already full schedule.

Blackheart's WWE contract was not renewed in 2025, after which she spent time in MLW and on the independent scene. She is now signed to TNA Wrestling and made her debut for the promotion at a television taping in Dothan, Alabama this month.

body: According to Alfred Konuwa of Forbes , Crown Jewel will now take place at Kingdom Arena in Riyadh on November 7. The move comes after Riyadh Season suddenly announced on October 28 that Crown Jewel was changing venues. While the announcement confirmed the show was still happening in Riyadh, it initially stopped short of naming the replacement location. Riyadh Season also confirmed that anyone who purchased tickets for the original venue would be getting their money back. Fans will then have to purchase new tickets once they are released for the new location. “We would like to inform you that ‘WWE Crown Jewel’ has been moved to a new venue. All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours.” There’s still no official explanation for why WWE Crown Jewel was moved from Riyadh Season Stadium to Kingdom Arena so close to the event. The change comes after weeks of questions surrounding WWE and TKO’s plans in Saudi Arabia due to security concerns in the region. TKO CEO Ari Emanuel previously said the company was monitoring the situation daily and considering alternatives if necessary. Jonathan Coachman also claimed WWE would postpone Crown Jewel rather than move it to another city if the Saudi Arabia show couldn’t go forward as planned. That obviously isn’t what’s happening here. WWE and TKO are still moving forward with Crown Jewel in Riyadh, but fans who planned on attending will now be heading to Kingdom Arena instead. With the new venue apparently locked in, WWE can finally move past at least one of the biggest questions hanging over Crown Jewel. title: WWE Shifts Crown Jewel 2026 Venue Within Riyadh

body: "We would like to inform you that "WWE Crown Jewel" has been moved to a new venue. All ticket holders will receive a full refund, and tickets will be re-released to everyone within the next 48 hours." WWE's Crown Jewel 2026 Premium Live Event (PLE) is scheduled for Saturday, Nov. 7. The annual event has been held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, for six of its seven occurrences. News in the area reports that there were explosions heard Wednesday in Riyadh, as Saudi military forces intercepted ballistic missiles. Continued attacks over the past few weeks prompted the U.S. State Department to order nonessential employees to leave Saudi Arabia. Despite this, the WWE has held firm that the event in Riyadh would still take place as scheduled . Wednesday's announcement initially made it sound like the company would move the event to a new country, but for now, staff members and wrestlers are still scheduled to go to Riyadh, just to an unnamed rescheduled location. Veteran journalist Dave Meltzer reported Wednesday that the show is currently being moved to the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh , the same venue as this Saturday's controversial Saul "Canelo" Alvarez fight , though Meltzer added the situation remains fluid and could change again. The Crown Jewel PLE event began in 2018 and has been held every year other than 2020. Six of the seven iterations have been held in Riyadh, while last year's show was held in Perth, Australia. This is a unique event because in 2024 it was established that the PLE itself would have its own championship. It isn't contested on week-to-week television, but each year the top men's and top women's champions from "Raw" and "SmackDown" will meet in a match. The winner of those two matches will earn the men's or women's Crown Jewel Championship. Women's Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green World Tag Team Championships: The Vision (champions) vs. Penta & Je'Von Evans There is still time to set another match. Every past Crown Jewel event has had at least five matches. Last year's in Australia had eight, while the most recent in Riyadh had seven.

Last week, the U.S. State Department issued a Level 3 travel advisory for Saudi Arabia, urging Americans to reconsider travel to the country amid security concerns. The advisory cited the risk of drone and missile attacks, armed conflict, terrorism, and travel disruptions linked to hostilities involving Iran and Iran-backed Houthi forces. The department also ordered non-emergency U.S. government employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia because of safety risks. TKO CEO Ari Emanuel previously said the company was monitoring the situation daily and had contingency plans if circumstances required a change. Riyadh Season shared the update on its official X account, informing fans that the event would no longer take place at its originally announced location. According to the announcement, all ticket holders will receive a full refund. The organizers also confirmed that tickets will be available again within the next 48 hours, although details about the new venue and the ticketing process remain unclear. NoDQ reported that The Venue, also known as ANB Arena, is one potential replacement for WWE Crown Jewel 2026. The arena is scheduled to host the boxing event headlined by Canelo Alvarez and Christian Mbilli on Saturday, October 31. The fight could also play a role in WWE’s plans for Crown Jewel. Speaking on Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer said WWE’s decision to proceed with its November 7 event could depend on how the boxing event unfolds . He added that the show could help WWE and TKO assess security and travel conditions in Riyadh amid regional concerns. title: WWE Should End Breakker & Theory's Inactive Tag Title Reign
raw_title: Please, WWE, put this Vision title reign out of our misery | Big Vinny V
summary_src: Bron Breakker & Austin Theory won the WWE World Tag Team Championships from the Street Profits in June. They have not defended the titles on Raw since. If they’re never going to defend these belts, the WWE may as well put them on Je’Von Evans & Penta, or anybody else who will.
body: Bron Breakker & Austin Theory won the WWE World Tag Team Championships from the Street Profits in June. They have not defended the titles on Raw since. If they’re never going to defend these belts, the WWE may as well put them on Je’Von Evans & Penta, or anybody else who will. We could end the article right here and our case would be made, but let’s flesh this out a little. Those WWE World Tag Team Championships have not been defended on pay-per-view, either. They were defended one time on SmackDown, in August, when Cody Rhodes & Oba Femi beat the champs by disqualification. They have also been defended a dozen or so times at house shows, and those have usually been disqualifications as well. In short: nobody watching on television has actually seen Breakker & Theory win a match as a team since they won the belts, and not many at house shows have seen them win anything either. This on a show where whole storylines are woven around a champion who never shows up to work, but compared to the Vision, Roman Reigns may as well be Darby Allin. Since Breakker & Theory won their titles, Reigns has defended the WWE World Heavyweight Championship in three televised matches: against Seth Rollins at SummerSlam, against Penta in Mexico City, and against LA Knight at Money in the Bank. Literally anyone would be an upgrade at this point, but as it turns out, Raw ended with some excellent challengers named. At Crown Jewel, whenever and wherever that show takes place, the Vision will be defending those WWE World Tag Team Championships against Penta & Je’Von Evans. Penta currently holds the Money in the Bank briefcase, but he may not cash it in anytime soon. One could argue he should not do so until after WrestleMania . A tag team championship reign would, for lack of a better term, give him something to do between now and then. As for Evans, he’s the most gifted young performer to hit WWE since perhaps Randy Orton. It’s beyond time he won a championship belt, and these titles would be a great start.
summary: Bron Breakker and Austin Theory captured the WWE World Tag Team Championships from The Street Profits in June but have not defended them on Raw since. The titles received one pay-per-view defense that ended in disqualification on SmackDown in August along with several house show matches that mostly finished the same way. Per the Wrestling Observer, the duo has not been seen winning a televised match as champions and the writer argues the belts should be moved to Je’Von Evans and Penta or any active team that will actually defend them.

title: On the Record: Becky Lynch Opens Up On How She and Seth Rollins Handle Arguments at Home
raw_title: Becky Lynch Reveals How She and Seth Rollins Handle Arguments at Home
summary_src: Becky Lynch and Seth Rollins might spend their careers beating people up for a living, but apparently none of that follows them home. When things get heated between the WWE power couple, Becky says their solution is a lot less dramatic than you might expect.
body: During her appearance on So You Think You Can Sports with Elliott Glazer , Lynch was asked about Rollins and how the two originally met through wrestling. Becky kept things pretty simple when describing her husband. When Glazer asked what Rollins actually does, Becky had no problem putting him over, saying, “He’s a wrestler. He’s amazing. He’s incredible. He’s so good.” Things got a little more interesting when Glazer wondered how two professional wrestlers settle arguments at home. Specifically, he wanted to know whether things ever get physical. Becky immediately shut that idea down: “No, never.” Glazer kept the joke going, but Lynch made it clear that there are no wrestling moves getting busted out when they disagree. They handle things the boring old-fashioned way — by actually talking. Of course, that still left the question of who actually starts the arguments. When Glazer suggested Becky might be the one picking the fights, she didn’t exactly fight the accusation. So while Becky and Seth have both spent years fighting inside WWE rings, their arguments at home apparently end with a conversation instead of a Manhandle Slam or a Stomp. Becky might even be willing to take a little more responsibility for starting them, although she still couldn’t resist putting over her husband one more time. Who do you think would be harder to argue with in a wrestling household? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Stephanie Vaquer Out Indefinitely
raw_title: Former WWE Women’s Champion Stephanie Vaquer Out of Action 'Indefinitely’
body: At WWE Money in the Bank on Oct. 10, "La Primera" sustained an ankle injury that led to her hobbling around on crutches during the fallout episode of WWE Raw two days later. By the next weekend, however, Vaquer was seemingly okay to compete once more as she wrestled at a pair of WWE live events in Hawaii. On October 24, Vaquer dramatically threw her crutches to the floor in a social media video clip , declaring that she was medically cleared to compete in a televised match against Becky Lynch on Raw . The winner of that bout would have gone on to challenge Liv Morgan for the WWE Women's World Championship. Unfortunately for Vaquer, she never got that opportunity as doctors abruptly withdrew their medical clearance, with Raw General Manager Adam Pearce revealing the news at the top of the Oct. 26 broadcast. Since then, fan speculation has pointed to injury as the potential reason for Vaquer's absence. According to PWI Elite , however, the issue is actually believed to be illness-related. False Finish corroborated this report, adding that the two-time Women's World Champion will be out of action "indefinitely." Vaquer, a native of Chile, signed with WWE in July 2024 and immediately marked her debut at a live event in Mexico. Three months later, she officially came aboard the WWE NXT brand, where she went on to hold the NXT Women's North American and NXT Women's Titles. Vaquer has remained a fan favorite through both her NXT and WWE main roster runs. In Vaquer's absence on this week's Raw , Lynch directly vied for the WWE Women's World Championship in the main event. Morgan ultimately retained the title after her Judgment Day cohorts, Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez, caused a disqualification. She appeared to recover in time to wrestle at live events in Hawaii and was medically cleared for a televised match against Becky Lynch on October 26 that would have led to a title shot against Liv Morgan. However, doctors withdrew the clearance before the bout, and per PWI Elite and False Finish the two-time Women's World Champion is now sidelined indefinitely due to illness.

title: Michael Hayes Training Bobby Roode As His WWE Successor
raw_title: Michael PS Hayes Says He's Training Former WWE NXT Champ To Be His Replacement
body: WWE Professional wrestling is an ever-changing business, but when it comes to WWE, some of the most long-term, tenured people in the company are the producers and writers. One of those people is Michael PS Hayes, who first took on a backstage role in 1999. Hayes has remained in the position ever since, something he talked about on an episode of " What's Your Story? " He joked that young WWE producers these days are "very, very good" compared to the older generation, but joked they're not as good as him. Hayes said that Paul "Triple H" Levesque did, however, remind him that he wasn't "going to be around forever," and went as far as to name Hayes' replacement. "What does that mean? Life or work?" Hayes laughed. "He said, 'You're our Pat Patterson, I need you to make Bobby Roode [our] Michael.' I said, 'Okay. That's a really good point, because I'm not going to be here forever.' Boy, has [Roode] come along. Bobby's really, really good. He's going to be great... I see great things for him." Roode made a name for himself in TNA beginning in 2004, and hung up his wrestling boots following neck fusion surgery in September 2022 , after just six years wrestling in a WWE ring. He made the transition from in-ring competitor to match producer in August 2023. Hayes said that Roode just needs to realize that things happen in the industry that are out of one's control, and you just need to let things go. He said he personally also still has problems doing so sometimes, but said you can't "waste so much energy b*******," because "you're going to have to do things anyway."
summary: Michael Hayes revealed that Triple H told him he needs to train Bobby Roode to eventually take over his longtime producer role in WWE. Hayes, who began his backstage position in 1999, joked about the younger producers while acknowledging he will not be around forever. He praised Roode's progress in the role after the former TNA and NXT star hung up his wrestling boots.

body: After joining the brand in April, Monroe finally made her in-ring debut for SmackDown on October 2. She defeated Guilia in that bout. A few weeks later, Monroe took down Guilia again, this time in a highly acclaimed Street Fight. Speaking with Busted Open Radio , Monroe was asked about winning the audience over with her bouts against Guilia. “Yeah, I did. I feel like there’s nothing better as a performer than winning people over. It’s kind of nice to go in and you don’t already have that level of — I’m really new to SmackDown. That’s my second match, so people might not know me or they might, as I said, just think, ‘Oh, she’s a pretty face’ or ‘She’s funny in the backstages’. There’s no better feeling than proving people wrong and winning people over. I love to entertain, I love to make people feel something and hopefully throughout that match, people got that feeling.” Monroe went on to single out Nick Aldis, criticizing him for his fantasy booking. “The person I’m trying to win over is Nick Aldis because I have been on SmackDown for five months. I think I’m world championship material. I think I deserve a match with Chelsea Green and he did everything but book me in that match. He booked himself in a match at SummerSlam. He came out to Oasis. He fantasy booked himself. Well, fantasy book me because I’m the biggest star on the show and I deserve to be world champion. summary_src: TKO knows there are plenty of questions about heading to the Middle East right now, and the company finally addressed the situation with its own employees. With WWE Crown Jewel coming up fast, the message from the top was pretty simple — safety comes first.
body: According to PWInsider , TKO held a company-wide town hall over Zoom on October 28. The meeting included WWE, UFC, Zuffa Boxing and On Location, with each department basically giving everyone a quick rundown of what they have coming up. Most of the meeting was described as your typical “rah-rah” corporate stuff, but things got a little more serious when TKO President and COO Mark Shapiro brought up the company’s upcoming events in the Middle East. Shapiro made it very clear that everyone’s safety was “paramount.” That’s obviously going to get some attention considering everything happening around WWE’s upcoming Crown Jewel trip. The timing of the meeting is interesting too. It happened before news broke that Crown Jewel would be moving to a different venue in Riyadh , so that particular change wasn’t brought up during the call. All of this comes while the security situation in Saudi Arabia continues to raise some pretty serious questions. The U.S. State Department recently ordered non-emergency government employees and their families to leave the country because of safety risks tied to attacks by Iranian-backed Houthis. There have also been warnings about attacks on airports, possible airspace closures, canceled flights and travel disruptions. U.S. government employees still working in Saudi Arabia even need special authorization to use airports following recent missile and drone attacks. TKO hasn’t exactly been ignoring any of this. Ari Emanuel previously said the company has a team keeping tabs on the situation every day while WWE continues getting ready for Crown Jewel . There was some actual wrestling talk during the town hall as well. WWE President Nick Khan spoke about the company’s next crop of stars and specifically brought up Bron Breakker, Je’Von Evans, Sol Ruca and Oba Femi. So TKO isn’t hitting the panic button, but it clearly knows people inside the company are paying attention to what’s happening. Crown Jewel is still moving forward, and Shapiro apparently wanted employees to know that getting everyone through these upcoming Middle East events safely is at the top of the list. Do you think TKO’s message will ease concerns backstage ahead of WWE’s upcoming trip to the Middle East? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Details Why Vince McMahon’s Work Ethic Was ‘Impossible’ To Keep up With
raw_title: Paul Heyman Details Why Vince McMahon’s Work Ethic Was ‘Impossible’ To Keep up With
body: Paul Heyman and Vince McMahon are two individuals who have crossed paths many times throughout their careers. They had a working relationship when Heyman was running Extreme Championship Wrestling (ECW) and Vince McMahon held the reins of World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE). In 2001, ECW collapsed due to its financial struggles, and the promotion was purchased by McMahon. Heyman got a job in WWE as well, and he worked with McMahon’s company on and off over the next two decades. Heyman still works for WWE today, while McMahon is no longer part of the promotion. Paul Heyman recently appeared on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , where he talked about the best and worst parts of working with McMahon. He says McMahon’s expectations that everyone keep up with his work ethic was the worst part about working with him. “Well, the worst part is just he expects you to keep up with his work ethic and that’s impossible. 24/7/365. He didn’t take holidays. He did what everybody in this business will talk about. He missed weddings, he missed funerals, he missed ball games. He missed a lot. He sacrificed.” This isn’t a surprising statement, considering many other wrestling figures have said similar things about McMahon. The former WWE CEO worked harder than anybody in the company and expected other people to do the same. At times, this caused friction with other key figures in the company. Heyman continued, “And his work ethic is unparalleled. Never have I met anyone that works as hard as Vince McMahon, and it’s both inspiring and it is paralyzing because trying to keep up with him is absolutely impossible. It is being a slave to the cause to which he benefits more than anyone.” McMahon’s expectations of people kept changing the more they tried to keep up with it. “And you just sit there and say, ‘How can I keep up with these expectations?’ Because his expectations change the further you grow and the more ability you show. He’s [like] ‘Oh, I can get more out of this person.’ And it’s the exploitation of your gifts and your knowledge and your ability and your talent that drives him and makes him as successful as he had become. It’s at the same time, he’s riding that vehicle until the wheels fall off. You’re the vehicle and it’s your wheels that are falling off.” If this was the worst part about working with McMahon, what was the “best” part? In Heyman’s words, “Everything I just said.” In 2019, Paul Heyman was promoted to Raw’s Executive Director. He was working directly with McMahon until Bruce Prichard replaced him. McMahon left WWE in 2024 after resigning as TKO Executive Chairman and from the TKO Board of Directors. Also read: Riyadh Season Confirms WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Venue Change

title: Hidetora Hanada Signs WWE NXT Developmental Deal
raw_title: Former Sumo & Football Athlete Reportedly Signs WWE NXT Contract
summary_src: WWE has reportedly signed Hidetora Hanada, a former sumo wrestling star and collegiate football athlete and member of the WWE NIL program, to an NXT contract
body: WWE has never been shy about their interest in converting collegiate, or even pro, football players into pro wrestlers, including the likes of future WWE Hall of Famer The Rock and current WWE stars like Trick Williams and Roman Reigns . But never has the WWE had an athlete that was both a football player or a sumo wrestler. That has now changed, as PWInsider Elite reports that the promotion has signed 24 year old Hidetora Hanada to a developmental contract. Born in Wakayama, Japan, Hanada became interested in sumo wrestling through his father, an amateur sumo wrestler in his youth, and began competing in high school. He would go on to have a successful career, winning Gold in heavyweight at the 2018 and 2019 Junior World Sumo Championships, held in Osaka, Japan and Taoyuan, Taiwan respectively, before winning Gold in heavyweight at the 2022 World Games in Birmingham, Alabama. Despite the success, Hanada decided to pursue a career in American football, having been a fan of it from a young age. After participating in a Canadian Football tryout in 2023, he would enroll at Colorado State University as a defensive linemen; he would play in only two games for the school before suffering an injury in 2024, never playing again. Hanada would graduate from Colorado State in December 2025, and despite attempting alternate routes towards getting to the NFL, he was ultimately unsuccessful. Hanada transferring to professional wrestling isn't a complete surprise, however, as WWE has previously signed him to an NIL deal while he was at Colorado State. Earlier this year, Hanada stated that he would pursue a wrestling career with WWE if a final attempt to make the NFL didn't work out. It's unclear when Hanada will make his debut for WWE, or if he will formally be announced alongside another new Performance Center class, as is usually routine.

The Japanese athlete previously won multiple gold medals in heavyweight sumo competitions, including at the 2018 and 2019 Junior World Sumo Championships plus the 2022 World Games, before transitioning to pursue American football after a 2023 Canadian Football League tryout and enrolling at Colorado State.

He played football as a defensive lineman for Colorado State University, becoming the only Japanese player on the Rams roster. His sumo background traces back to his high school years in Japan. Hanada had previously tried out for the NFL without being selected and tried his hand at various sports in Japan before transferring from NSSU to Colorado State.

He joined WWE’s NIL program in February 2025 after expressing interest in professional wrestling last year. Hanada graduated from Colorado State in December 2025 with a bachelor’s degree in interdisciplinary liberal arts.

body: While next weekend’s WWE Crown Jewel will remain in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, it will have a new venue and one that is reportedly finalized. After news of the move came earlier in the day, a new report out by Forbes on Wednesday has the Saturday, November 7 premium live event’s new location as the Kingdom Arena — a 30,000-seat indoor venue that has hosted WWE events in the past including this past June’s Night of Champions. The show was originally set for Riyadh Season Stadium. It’s unknown what led to the move. TKO’s insistence on running upcoming events in Saudi Arabia despite t ravel alerts for U.S. citizens due to ongoing tensions and attacks on major airports by Houthi rebels has been a hot topic the past few weeks. Company leaders like TKO’s Ari Emanuel and UFC’s Dana White have continued to insist publicly they are going to meet their commitments to the country and Turki Al-Sheikh. WWE and Saudi Arabia have a multi-year partnership which accounts for a reported $50 million per show in revenue to WWE. The relationship is so strong that WWE will bring WrestleMania to the country this April for the first time ever. body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. TNA star Shotzi Blackheart made a lot of headlines today with the following remarks on the Generation Of Wrestling podcast about WWE not allowing her to work with TNA when she returned from a torn ACL circa late 2024. “I was kind of talking to TNA when I was still signed with WWE. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was just really hungry to get in the ring, and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA. I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit, and he was totally down, but for some reason I wasn’t allowed to. And then when I got released, I needed a second to just be on the indies, and do me before signing another big contract.” Shotzi didn’t like the “fake ass headlines” that she saw in pro wrestling media about her comment, so she later clarified on social media that she wasn’t dumping on WWE. She also provided an extra detail on what she meant by “for some reason I wasn’t allowed.” “There was no negativity behind my comment. At the time TNA was utilizing NXT talent. I was working in NXT, but I was also being pitched to start a potential SmackDown storyline, so my understanding was that adding a third storyline would have been a lot to juggle. The intention of my comment was simply to express how much I’ve always wanted to work with TNA and my enthusiasm for making it work alongside an already full schedule. title: Reason Behind TNA Star’s Extended Television Absence
raw_title: Reason Behind TNA Star’s Extended Television Absence
summary_src: Léi Yǐng Lee has been missing from TNA television for months, and now there’s finally an explanation for where she’s been. Despite the lengthy absence, fans apparently don’t need to start wondering whether she quietly left the company.
body: According to PWInside , Lee has been away from TNA because she took an extended trip back to China to visit her family. She reportedly hadn’t been back home in many years, so she was given an extended period away. More importantly, Lee is still under contract with TNA as of this writing. So her disappearance from Impact isn’t being treated as another departure during a year that has already seen quite a few roster changes. Lee hasn’t appeared on TNA television since her Knockouts World Championship program with Xia Brookside over the summer. The two had been feuding heading into Slammiversary, with their rivalry getting physical on Impact before their title match. Brookside defeated Lee at Slammiversary on June 28 to capture the Knockouts World Championship. Lee then got her rematch on the July 1 Impact taping in Albany, where Brookside retained the title in a No Disqualification match, which ended up being Lee’s last TNA appearance before her extended absence. It had already been a pretty eventful 2026 for Lee before she disappeared from TV. She entered the year as Knockouts World Champion and successfully defended the title against NXT’s Zaria at Genesis before eventually losing the championship during the spring. Lee didn’t stay away from the belt for long either. She defeated Arianna Grace on the May 7 episode of Impact to regain the Knockouts World Championship, kicking off another run that eventually led into her feud with Brookside. That makes her sudden disappearance after the Brookside program a lot easier to understand now. Lee wasn’t being quietly phased out of TNA — she simply headed home to spend some long-overdue time with her family, and she remains part of the roster. When do you think TNA should bring her back to television, and what kind of storyline should she return with? Let us know what you think in the comments. The October 23 edition of the blue brand saw new Women's Tag Team Champions, as well as a surprise six-man main event, but viewership was still down compared to the previous week. The show earned a 0.24 in the ever-important ages 18-49 demographic, down 25 percent from the October 16 episode's rating of 0.32. Viewership was down compared to the trailing four weeks average of 1,298,000 viewers by 17 percent. Compared to this time last year, however, viewership is up 18 percent, with 1,257,000 average viewers for October 2026, compared to October 2025's 1,063,000. The main event of the show was set during the night, and was originally meant to be Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn and Johnny Gargano taking on United States Champion Trick Williams and Rey Fenix. Ricky Saints and Penta got involved, however, and the Money in the Bank briefcase holder demanded a six-man tag. Penta, Fenix, and Williams scored the victory. Elsewhere on the show, the team of Michin and B-Fab won the Women's Tag Team Championships from Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley, thanks to some help from Jade Cargill on the outside. It was also revealed that Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will take their feud to Crown Jewel , currently still set for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where they'll face off in a Last Man Standing match.

It scored a 0.24 rating in the 18-49 demographic, a 25 percent decline from the prior week. Despite the drop amid college football season, viewership remains 18 percent higher than the same period last year.

TKO held a zoom meeting with staff today communicating the importance of safety surrounding the Saudi Arabia events that the company is holding, with Mark Shapiro speaking Mike Johnson of PWInsider described the meeting as “mostly a rah-rah meeting with each department.” Johnson also wrote that Shapiro stressed that the safety of everyone was “paramount.” The meeting was reportedly held before news that Crown Jewel was changing venues was announced. WWE Crown Jewel was originally scheduled for November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. However, Riyadh Season announced Wednesday that the event is moving to a different venue, with recent reports suggesting The Kingdom Arena , which hosted WWE Night of Champions in 2025 and 2026, will be where the event is now held. title: Paul Heyman Calls Vince McMahon Supremely Complicated
raw_title: Paul Heyman comments on whether Vince McMahon is ‘a good man’
summary_src: Paul Heyman gave an in-depth answer when asked whether Vince McMahon is a good man during a recent interview.
body: Paul Heyman gave an in-depth answer when asked whether Vince McMahon is a good man during a recent interview. During an appearance on In Depth with Graham Bensinger, Heyman referred to the former WWE chairman as a “supremely complicated human being of great accomplishment.” When Bensinger followed that up by asking if Vince McMahon is a good man, Heyman responded that he doesn’t believe McMahon would ever consider himself that. “No, I don’t think Vince ever considered himself a good man. I don’t think he cared about it. I don’t think that was part of his self-judgment. I don’t think he felt he was placed on this planet to be a good man. “Do I think he’s a man of great accomplishment? Yes. Do I regret the battles? And I had some battles with Vince.” Heyman continued to say that Vince enjoyed confrontation and “childish battles.” When asked for an example, Heyman answered the relaunch of ECW. “2006, when he relaunched ECW, he told me he was putting me in charge of it and 30 seconds later started stripping me of any authority that I had in controlling or contouring or tailoring or creating the product.” “He got off changing ECW on me. And it became just such a person battle that was terrible for the product, terrible for the company, even worse for the audience. That was the most miserable six months.” Heyman is not particularly active in WWE storylines currently. He no longer regularly accompanies The Vision for their matches. He was shown backstage taking a phone call from an unidentified person during September’s WWE Sunday Night’s Main Event, as The Vision celebrated Bronson Reed’s return . The identity of the caller has not been revealed. Heyman’s interview on In Depth with Graham Bensinger is available below. title: TKO Holds Town Hall, Stresses Safety For Middle East Events
raw_title: TKO Holds Town Hall Meeting, Mark Shapiro Emphasizes Safety In The Middle East
summary_src: TKO held a virtual town hall meeting on Wednesday, where President Marc Shapiro emphasized safety in the Middle East ahead of WWE Crown Jewel.
body: After it was announced via the Riyadh Season X (formerly Twitter) account on Wednesday that WWE Crown Jewel would be moving to a different venue in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, a new report revealed that TKO held a town hall meeting for all employees as questions remain about safety surrounding the premium live event in the Middle East. According to PWInsider , the meeting was held for all employees via Zoom, and the outlet's Mike Johnson called it "mostly a rah rah meeting." The town hall wasn't held specifically to address concerns surrounding Crown Jewel, as according to the report, each entity within TKO, including UFC and Zuffa Boxing, in addition to WWE, gave recaps on what's going on in their part of the company. Marc Shapiro, TKO President and COO, did comment on the upcoming events the company is holding in the Middle East, however, amid ongoing tensions and missile strikes. PWI was told that Shapiro said that the safety of everyone involved in these events is "paramount." The meeting, however, was held before Riyadh Season announced on social media that Crown Jewel would be moving, yet staying within the city, so the change in location of the event was not addressed in the town hall. It was reported on Monday by the New York Times that a recent United States intelligence memo warned of planned attacks against State Department employees and other Americans in "the Middle East and other regions" by Iran. Saudi Arabia remains at a level three "reconsider travel" advisory on the US Department of State website , with areas like the Yemen border at a level four "do not travel" advisory due to terrorism.

TKO President and COO Marc Shapiro addressed upcoming events in the Middle East amid regional tensions, stating that the safety of everyone involved is paramount. The meeting occurred before the announcement that WWE Crown Jewel would change venues in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

title: WWE Crown Jewel Moves to Kingdom Arena
raw_title: New location finalized for WWE Crown Jewel
summary_src: While next weekend’s WWE Crown Jewel will remain in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, it will be held at new venue in the same city.
body: While next weekend’s WWE Crown Jewel will remain in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, it will be held at new venue in the same city. After news of the move came earlier in the day, our Dave Meltzer reported that the Saturday, November 7 premium live event’s new location as the Kingdom Arena — a 30,000-seat indoor venue that has hosted WWE events in the past including this past June’s Night of Champions. (Meltzer said it was the same venue as this weekend’s Canelo Alvarez boxing event but that is being held at ANB Arena/The Venue.) The show was originally set for Riyadh Season Stadium. It’s unknown what led to the move. TKO’s insistence on running upcoming events in Saudi Arabia despite travel alerts for U.S. citizens due to ongoing tensions and attacks on major airports by Iran-backed Houthi rebels has been a hot topic the past few weeks. Company leaders like TKO’s Ari Emanuel and UFC’s Dana White have continued to insist publicly they are going to meet their commitments to the country and Turki Al-Sheikh. WWE and Saudi Arabia have a multi-year partnership which accounts for a reported $50 million per show in revenue to WWE. The relationship is so strong that WWE will bring WrestleMania to the country this April for the first time ever. Josh Nason Since 2011, Josh has been a contributing editor to Wrestling Observer/F4WOnline.com in addition to hosting the Sunday edition of Wrestling Observer Live, available on our site, Spotify and Apple Podcasts. He hosted the now-retired Punch-Out for 11 years. Bylines include Fight Magazine, Bloody Elbow, Bleacher Report, and other websites & magazines. He's a 2000 graduate of the University of Maine with a journalism degree, worked in pro sports for nearly a decade, and once was an indie ring announcer for Maine's EWA in 2000-01.
summary: WWE's Crown Jewel premium live event on November 7 will take place at the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia instead of the originally planned Riyadh Season Stadium. The 30,000-seat indoor venue previously hosted this year's Night of Champions in June. The reason for the venue change remains unknown while the company's ongoing Saudi partnership continues amid recent travel concerns.

title: Bryce Remsburg Says AEW Is Discussing WrestleMania Weekend Plans
raw_title: Bryce Remsburg Comments On AEW Potentially Holding Event Against WWE WrestleMania
summary_src: AEW referee Bryce Remsburg commented on the possibility of the company holding an event in the US to go up against WWE WrestleMania 43 next year.
body: AEW There's a big opportunity open for All Elite Wrestling, and many other small independent promotions in the United States, when WWE WrestleMania 43 takes place in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia next year. AEW could present a big show in the US that weekend, and while AEW President Tony Khan has yet to confirm anything, he has said it's "something to consider." In the latest update surrounding what could be in the cards in April 2027, AEW referee Bryce Remsburg commented on " The Certified Mark Show ," but kept things vague. "I think I can say that conversations are being had around what we might do that weekend, how about that?" Remsburg said. "There are some factors out of our control that would contribute to our decisions, so we'll kind of see what happens." It was reported back in July that WWE already expected a "significant presence" by AEW in the states when WrestleMania takes to Riyadh. WWE has already announced weekend events in New York City surrounding the "Showcase of the Immortals." A WrestleMania watch party is set for the city, along with AAA Eternal Glory and "WWE NXT" Stand & Deliver. According to the announcement, more fan experiences are set to be announced. As of this writing, the dates for WrestleMania 43 have yet to be announced, though the weekend of April 10 and 11 is reportedly being targeted . AEW has already announced a few events for 2027, including "AEW Dynamite: New Year's Smash" in Atlanta. AEW Dynasty is set for the M&S Bank arena in Liverpool on February 7.
summary: With WWE WrestleMania 43 scheduled for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in 2027, AEW has an opening to run a major domestic show that weekend. AEW President Tony Khan previously called it something to consider. Referee Bryce Remsburg told The Certified Mark Show that conversations are taking place about potential plans, though some factors remain out of the company's control.

title: Grayson Waller mocks NXT stars for marking out over John Cena
raw_title: Grayson Waller rips NXT marks, says John Cena better ask his permission to be there
summary_src: Due to election coverage next Tuesday night, NXT is moving to Wednesday (Nov. 4) and airing head-to-head against AEW’s Blood & Guts episode of Dynamite. WWE is whipping out the big guns for the battle with AEW, and that includes a rare NXT appearance for John Cena.
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Due to election coverage next Tuesday night, NXT is moving to Wednesday (Nov. 4) and airing head-to-head against AEW’s Blood & Guts episode of Dynamite. WWE is whipping out the big guns for the battle with AEW, and that includes a rare NXT appearance for John Cena. Speaking on Busted Open After Dark , NXT Champion Grayson Waller said it was pathetic how many NXT wrestlers were marking out for Cena backstage when the announcement was made. In contrast, Waller sees himself as John’s equal, and says Cena better ask for permission to enter his house. “I was [backstage] when the graphic came up. You should have heard the kids. ‘John Cena’s coming!‘ It was so sad. It was tough. I felt like I was at a fan meet-and-greet or something. They were all excited. It put a smile on my face too. I’m the only one here who’s been in the ring with John Cena. Twice. I’ve been on the mic against John Cena, and I survived. And not everyone does. But all I hope for John next Wednesday is that he wipes his feet, and he knocks on the door, and he asks me permission to come in my house. And if he wants to get in my ring, he needs to ask permission too. And I’m sure maybe he’s talking about this John Cena Classic, giving some NXT superstars an opportunity. Well, those opportunities I’ve taken. So maybe he needs to come and sit down under my learning tree, and I can tell him how things run in NXT now.” Waller reiterated that everyone on the NXT roster needs to stop being such marks for legends of the industry. “I handed in my mark card the day I started at NXT, and for these kids, they need to do the same. I think they need to carry themselves as equals. We’re all on this one WWE brand now. We represent WWE. And it’s cool to show respect to the legends, and understand and learn from them, and all that. But don’t be a fan. Like, if any of them are going up and asking for photos, or wearing his merch next week, I’m gonna go and talk to them directly. If you want to be this, if you want to be a champion, if you want to main event WrestleMania, when you get here, you have to treat these people as equals, because that’s who they are. You are on their level, and I don’t think a lot of the kids look at it that way.” When asked if he might get physical with John, Waller said he does owe Cena a receipt, but ultimately has nothing to gain from attacking a non-wrestler. “I don’t need the John Cena rub, you need the Grayson Waller rub. That’s why you’re coming to my show. I’m helping you, John. I’m being a kind person and helping you out, getting your face back out there.” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. body: 0 WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is set to take place at a new venue in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, following a last-minute change announced just days before the event. Riyadh Season earlier confirmed the move but did not reveal the new location. Now, a new report has revealed where the PLE will be held. On October 28, Riyadh Season announced that Crown Jewel would no longer take place at its originally planned venue. Organizers confirmed that the show would remain in Riyadh and that everyone who had already purchased tickets would receive a full refund. The timing of the decision raised more questions about WWE’s plans, especially given the security concerns in the region. body: The challenge came after The Death Riders’ Jon Moxley and Daniel Garcia lost to Jay White and David Finlay of The Cut in the opening match of Fright Night Dynamite. The match featured interference from both factions, with Ace Austin running through the crowd to distract the referee. Wheeler Yuta tried to stop him with a Busaiku Knee, but the distraction allowed Clark Connors to spear Garcia. White followed up with the Blade Runner to secure the victory for his team. Things didn’t end there. Members of The Death Riders and The Cut rushed to the ring after the match, leading to a brawl between the two factions. Claudio Castagnoli managed to get his hands on Connors and delivered a Giant Swing before The Cut retreated from the ring. That’s when Moxley took things a step further. Rather than simply demanding another tag team match, the AEW Continental Champion challenged The Cut to face The Death Riders in Anarchy in the Arena at Full Gear. The challenge sets up a potential major showdown between the factions, although AEW has yet to confirm the match or announce its participants. AEW Full Gear takes place on Saturday, November 14, 2026, at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona. The pay-per-view already has three championship matches confirmed, with several other rivalries continuing to develop. The three title matches have already been announced for the November 14 event. Moxley’s Anarchy in the Arena challenge could add another major match to the lineup if The Cut accepts and AEW makes it official. With The Death Riders and The Cut already attacking each other on Dynamite, an Anarchy in the Arena Match would give both factions the opportunity to settle their differences without the restrictions of a traditional tag team match. title: Comeback Watch: Toni Storm’s AEW Return Not Happening Anytime Soon Despite Mysterious WrestleDream Teases

summary_src: Toni Storm’s mysterious cassette tapes have fans wondering if she’s about to return to AEW, but it looks like they’re going to have to wait a little longer.
body: According to Fightful Select , AEW has begun setting the stage for Storm’s eventual comeback, but sources within the company say her in-ring return is not imminent. That doesn’t mean fans won’t see more of her storyline in the meantime, as other elements involving Storm could be introduced before she’s ready to wrestle again. It was also revealed that AEW originally had major plans for Storm throughout 2026. However, following her match against Marina Shafir at AEW Revolution in March, the company learned she would be unavailable until the end of the year at the earliest. She was subsequently removed from television, leaving fans with the mystery surrounding her backstage attack. There was apparently a much bigger plan behind that attack as well. AEW intended to plant several clues pointing toward different potential suspects responsible for taking Storm out. Fightful was told that the company had a particular person in mind to eventually reveal as the attacker, although the identity was deliberately left open in case creative plans needed to change. That brings everything back to the mysterious cassette tapes that surfaced at AEW WrestleDream on October 17, 2026. It wasl confirmed that the tapes were intentionally planted for select media members attending the event as part of the effort to tease Storm’s eventual return. Content creator Astrid Pizarro was among those who received a package containing a cassette labeled “Toni Storm Tapes.” The recording was marked as the first of five, leaving four additional tapes unaccounted for. “I was handed out the tape at WrestleDream by somebody. I opened it, it just said ‘play me.’ Thankfully my dad and my brother have a cassette player, so I was able to play it today. I was the only one in my area that got it, and it says one out of five. I don’t know who the other four people are.” The first tape, titled “Mundanities,” featured Renee Paquette narrating recordings supposedly taken from a device Storm secretly carried in her purse. The recordings offered an unusual look at Storm’s daily life, while the overall mystery connected back to her unexplained disappearance from AEW television. One particularly interesting detail was that the fifth and final cassette was labeled “Death.” With AEW already planning to drop clues about multiple potential suspects, that title could become an important part of the storyline as more recordings surface. Despite the renewed attention surrounding Storm, sources indicated that she hasn’t been spotted at many AEW events, if any, during her absence. That makes the recent developments particularly interesting, since AEW appears to be moving forward with the mystery without necessarily having Storm physically present at its shows. Tony Khan also addressed her status during the WrestleDream media scrum, confirming that Storm would eventually return to AEW without offering a specific date. “I can’t say when or where but I know ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm will be back in AEW.” For now,

title: John Cena Recalls Randy Orton Boot Prank Before Kurt Angle Match

body: John Cena made his WWE debut on the June 27, 2002 episode of WWE SmackDown, taking on Kurt Angle. The match was the beginning of one of the greatest WWE careers of all time, but it wasn’t without a little backstage ribbing. “In 2002, I went to Chicago as an extra talent–someone not to be used,” Cena said at a New York Q&A (via Undisputed ). “I was then told I was going to have a match against an Olympic gold medalist. Randy Orton tied my boots together in a locker where I couldn’t even reach them, so I had to cut the laces and wrestle with half of my laces. I had to go off campus to get one of the worst haircuts that people watching on television had ever seen.” He continued, “That was my welcome to the WWE, and it was better than I ever could have imagined. A moment that was supposed to be celebratory was also humbling. It was filled with tough love that belongs to our fraternity, and I was grateful to go through that.” Orton would become one of Cena’s greatest rivals during his WWE career, which ended in December.

Cena described the ribbing as tough love that marked his welcome to WWE.

title: On the Record: WWE's Charlotte Flair Opens Up On Advice That's Helped Her Accept Her Dad's Social Media
raw_title: WWE's Charlotte Flair Reveals Advice That's Helped Her Accept Her Dad's Social Media
summary_src: A conversation with a fellow WWE star helped Charlotte Flair change her perspective on her father's social media presence.
body: WWE WWE Hall of Famer Ric Flair has always been his daughter Charlotte Flair's biggest supporter, often times taking to social media or podcasts to criticize any storytelling that doesn't elevate her to the level he thinks she should be on. Outside of this, Flair also goes on social media tirades on occasion, causing controversy even at 77. Charlotte has admitted to feeling embarrassed over her father's posts in the past, but she now claims she has made peace with it all, with some help. "There's no one more proud. Like, he is my guy! Because, like, I was talking to Nattie the other day, and I was like, 'If he just takes to Twitter one more time.' ... But then Nattie was like, 'Dude, don't you think your dad's earned the right to?' And I had a different perspective," Charlotte recalled during an appearance on HeymanHustleTV's "The Roundtable." Since that conversation with Natalya, Charlotte has "eased up" on her reactions to her father's social media presence. Though she's always known it, she's more aware than ever that Ric wants the best for her, and his posts are his way of showing that. "He really just wants better for me 'cause he knows how good I am, and not 'cause I'm his kid," she continued. This past weekend, Flair was rushed to the hospital after a fall. However, "The Nature Boy" has since been released, and provided a more in-depth health update while also pointing out that the posts on his Facebook account are not being made by him, due to losing his account to a digital talent agency.

title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Explains Why Vince McMahon Doesn’t Think He’s a ‘Good Man’
raw_title: Paul Heyman Explains Why Vince McMahon Doesn’t Think He’s a ‘Good Man’
body: 0 Paul Heyman has shared his thoughts on his complicated relationship with Vince McMahon and explained why he believes the former WWE Chairman never saw himself as a good man. Speaking on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Heyman discussed both the good and bad sides of working with McMahon. While he praised McMahon’s achievements in wrestling, he also spoke about the challenges of working with someone whose ambition often came at a cost. During the interview, when Paul Heyman was asked about the best and worst parts of working with McMahon, he suggested that both came from his incredible work ethic. “The worst part is just he expects you to keep up with his work ethic and that’s impossible. 24/7, 365. He didn’t take holidays. He did what everybody in his business will talk about. He missed weddings. He missed funerals. He missed ball games. He missed a lot. He sacrificed. His work ethic is unparalleled. I’ve never met anyone that works as hard as Vince McMahon. And it is both inspiring and it is paralyzing because trying to keep up with him is absolutely impossible,” Heyman explained. Heyman also explained that McMahon pushed people harder when he saw their potential. “It’s the exploitation of your gifts and your knowledge and your ability and your talent that drives him and makes him as successful as he had become. And it’s at the same time it’s it’s he’s riding he’s riding that he’s riding that vehicle until the wheels fall off. You’re the vehicle and it’s your wheels that are falling off. What’s the best part about it? Everything I just said,” Heyman said. Heyman also spoke about McMahon’s childhood and how those experiences may have shaped his behavior. He said that McMahon wanted to create an environment where he could protect himself from being hurt. “It’s a fascinating study. It’s overcompensatory behavior. He didn’t like the universe that he was in. So he created his own universe in which no one could ever hurt him,” Heyman said. When Bensinger asked Heyman if he thought McMahon was a good man, he described the former WWE Chairman as a complicated person who had different priorities. “No, I don’t think Vince ever considered himself a good man. I don’t think he cared about it. I don’t think that was part of his self-judgment. I don’t think he felt he was placed on this planet to be a good man,” Heyman said. However, Heyman made it clear that he viewed McMahon’s character and achievements as two separate things. Despite their disagreements over the years, he still recognized what McMahon had accomplished in the wrestling business. “Do I think he’s a man of great accomplishment? Yes. Do I regret the battles? And I had some battles with Vince,” he added. The conversation then turned to Heyman’s professional disagreements with McMahon, especially their problems during WWE’s ECW relaunch in 2006. body: For the first time in the history of the company, an Anarchy in the Arena match will take place at AEW Full Gear. In a challenge made during Wednesday’s Dynamite after the opening bout, The Death Riders will take on The Cut in the anything goes match that spills all over the arena. As of this writing, the teams have not been announced but the Death Riders’ side appears to be Jon Moxley, Claudio Castagnoli, Gabe Kidd, Wheeler Yuta and Daniel Garcia while Jay White and David Finlay will represent The Cut with three other members. Moxley and Garcia fell to White and Finlay in the show opener after interference from Ace Austin and Clark Connors led to White hitting the Blade Runner on Garcia for the win. A brawl between both teams followed which was then followed by Moxley issuing the challenge. The formation of the new White and Finlay-led group last Wednesday came at the Death Riders’ expense. It will be the fifth-ever Anarchy match with the previous four taking place at Double or Nothing. Coincidentally, the last one took place in Glendale, Arizona, last year while this year’s show takes place in Phoenix. title: Will Ospreay AEW World Title Defense Locked In for Full Gear 2026
raw_title: Will Ospreay AEW World Title Defense Confirmed for Full Gear 2026
summary_src: Kyle Fletcher is getting another shot at Will Ospreay, and this time the AEW World Championship will be on the line. During the AEW Dynamite episode for October 28 2026, AEW officially confirmed that Fletcher will challenge Ospreay for the AEW World Championship at Full Gear on November 14.
body: The announcement came shortly after Fletcher defeated Jack Perry in a competitive singles match on Fright Night Dynamite. Fletcher had Don Callis in his corner as he battled Perry, with both men getting plenty of offense throughout the match. Perry nearly pulled off the victory after locking in the Snare Trap, but Fletcher managed to reach the ropes before eventually putting Perry away with a Brainbuster from the top rope. Fletcher wasn’t finished after picking up the win. With Mark Davis and Jake Doyle celebrating alongside him, Fletcher grabbed the microphone and reminded everyone that he had just beaten someone considered one of AEW’s original pillars. He also brought up his previous Full Gear victories over Adam Copeland and Will Ospreay, making it clear that he wanted to add another major win to his record. That’s when Fletcher turned his attention directly to Ospreay. He challenged the AEW World Champion to put his title on the line at Full Gear, promising to prove that he’s the best when the two meet again. AEW didn’t take long to make it official. Following a commercial break, the company confirmed that Will Ospreay will defend the AEW World Championship against Kyle Fletcher at Full Gear on November 14. AEW Full Gear takes place on Saturday, November 14, 2026. Fletcher now has an opportunity to defeat Ospreay on pay-per-view once again, but this time he’ll be walking into the match with the AEW World Championship up for grabs. After making his intentions clear on Dynamite, Fletcher has gotten exactly what he wanted. body: AEW/Speedy Ruiz Kyle Fletcher has already proven he can get the better of Will Ospreay in the past, which is why on the Fright Night edition of "AEW Dynamite," he threw out the challenge for an AEW World Championship match at AEW Full Gear 2026. Fletcher stated that he wants Full Gear to be a perfect night for The Don Callis Family, before reminding everyone that he has not only beaten the current AEW World Champion before, but he actually beat Ospreay at the Full Gear pay-per-view two years ago. Looking for lightning to strike twice, Fletcher dared Ospreay to put the title on the line at this year's event, and promised that if they come face-to-face again, it will end up just how their match in 2024 did, with Fletcher having his hand raised. The match was made official shortly after, marking the first time since AEW Revolution 2025 that Ospreay and Fletcher wrestling each other one-on-one. That bout took place in a Steel Cage and Ospreay emerged victorious, though a lot has changed since that night in Los Angeles. The two men will actually be locked in a cage before Full Gear as they will both compete in the men's Blood and Guts match on the November 4 episode of "AEW Dynamite." Fletcher will team up with the rest of his Don Callis Family members, while Ospreay will team up with The Young Bucks, Adam Copeland, Darby Allin, and the recently returned Steven Borden, which could play a major role in the Full Gear title match as neither Ospreay or Fletcher will be 100% heading into their title bout.

title: WWE Offered To Delay SmackDown For WNBA Finals
raw_title: WWE Was Willing To Move SmackDown To 9 PM ET On Friday To Help WNBA Finals Game 6
summary_src: Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will take place at 12:30 PM ET at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta, GA on Thursday. The game was without a venue and time in the days leading up to it as the Atlanta Hawks play on Thursday at 8…
body: Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will take place at 12:30 PM ET at the State Farm Arena in Atlanta, GA on Thursday. The game was without a venue and time in the days leading up to it as the Atlanta Hawks play on Thursday at 8 PM ET. According to ESPN, WWE was willing to help out the WNBA by pushing SmackDown back to a 9 PM ET start time if it meant Game 6 would begin at 7 PM ET on Friday and be held at State Farm Arena. The game is set to air on USA Network, the home of SmackDown. During the frantic negotiations over the weekend, an unlikely ally emerged — the WWE. At one point, sources told ESPN that Steve Koonin, the Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO, reached out to WWE president Nick Khan and asked if he’d be willing to move the telecast of this week’s Smackdown to accommodate Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Friday night. Smackdown usually airs at 8 p.m. ET on Friday nights on USA Network, which is the broadcast network for this game. If Game 6 were to be played from 7-9 p.m. at State Farm Arena, the WWE would have to move an hour later. Khan told him they’d be fine with the later broadcast window if it was needed to help the WNBA Finals play in a more appropriate arena. The plan fell through as the league didn’t want a potential Game 7 to be held on Tuesday against Election Night coverage.

WWE offered to assist the WNBA by shifting its SmackDown broadcast to a 9 PM ET start time. This adjustment would have allowed Game 6 to take place at 7 PM ET on Friday at State Farm Arena.

llm_long: WWE nearly stepped in to resolve a scheduling conflict involving game six of the WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries. The game had become a national story as the NBA, WNBA, multiple arenas and other parties worked to place it in prime time at State Farm Arena.

Instead the contest was set for Thursday at 12:30 pm Eastern. According to ESPN reporter Ramona Shelburne, Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO Steve Koonin, a former WWE board member, reached out to WWE president Nick Khan. Koonin asked if WWE would shift this Friday’s SmackDown to a 9 pm Eastern start so the WNBA game could air on USA from 7-9 pm Eastern at the preferred venue.

Khan, who has known Koonin for decades, responded that WWE would be fine with the later broadcast window if it helped the WNBA Finals secure a more appropriate arena. The proposed solution was ultimately dropped because it would have placed a potential game seven on Tuesday opposite Election Night coverage.

title: WWE Was Willing to Move SmackDown Start Time to Help WNBA Finals
raw_title: WWE Was Willing to Move SmackDown Start Time to Help WNBA Finals
summary_src: WWE was willing to change its Friday Night SmackDown schedule to help the WNBA solve a major problem with its Finals, and Nick Khan had no issue making the adjustment if it meant getting the game into a bigger arena.
body: According to ESPN , WWE was approached about moving SmackDown from its usual 8 PM ET start time to 9 PM ET on Friday, October 30, 2026. The proposed change would have allowed Game 6 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream to air on USA Network from 7 PM to 9 PM ET that night. The situation started because the WNBA was scrambling to find a suitable time for Game 6 at State Farm Arena in Atlanta. The Atlanta Hawks were already scheduled to play the Cleveland Cavaliers at the venue on Thursday, October 29, creating a scheduling conflict for the Dream. During negotiations over the weekend, State Farm Arena and Atlanta Hawks CEO Steve Koonin reached out to WWE President Nick Khan to see whether the company would be willing to accommodate the WNBA. ESPN explained how WWE became involved in the discussions. “During the frantic negotiations over the weekend, an unlikely ally emerged — the WWE. At one point, sources told ESPN that Steve Koonin, the Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO, reached out to WWE president Nick Khan and asked if he’d be willing to move the telecast of this week’s Smackdown to accommodate Game 6 of the WNBA Finals on Friday night.” The request would have required WWE to give up its normal 8 PM ET television start time, but Khan was willing to make it happen. Since both SmackDown and the WNBA Finals air on USA Network, moving WWE’s broadcast back an hour would have created enough room for the basketball game. ESPN provided more details about Khan’s response. “Smackdown usually airs at 8 p.m. ET on Friday nights on USA Network, which is the broadcast network for this game. If Game 6 were to be played from 7-9 p.m. at State Farm Arena, the WWE would have to move an hour later. Khan told him they’d be fine with the later broadcast window if it was needed to help the WNBA Finals play in a more appropriate arena.” Despite WWE’s willingness to cooperate, the proposed arrangement never happened. Moving Game 6 to Friday would have also pushed a potential Game 7 to Tuesday, November 3, which would have meant competing with Election Night coverage. The WNBA ultimately decided against that option and found another way to keep Game 6 at State Farm Arena without disrupting WWE’s television schedule. Instead, the WNBA announced that Game 6 would take place Thursday, October 29, at 12:30 PM ET. The Hawks also agreed to move their game against Cleveland to 8 PM ET that evening, allowing both games to take place at the same venue. As a result, WWE SmackDown will air at its regular 8 PM ET start time on Friday, October 30, with no changes necessary. While the scheduling adjustment ultimately wasn’t needed, the situation showed that WWE was prepared to make a significant television change to accommodate another major sporting event. Khan gave the green light to the proposal, but the WNBA ended up choosing a different solution. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling
summary: Per ESPN , WWE was approached about moving SmackDown from its usual 8 PM ET start time to 9 PM ET on Friday, October 30, 2026. Sources told ESPN that Steve Koonin, the Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO, reached out to WWE president Nick Khan and asked if he’d be willing to move the telecast.

The two share an extensive history when Fletcher and Mark Davis were Aussie Open and part of Ospreay’s United Empire before Fletcher (and later Davis) turned on the former friend. They have squared off four times in AEW dating back to March 2024. Ospreay is 3-1 with their last bout taking place at March 2025’s Revolution in a steel cage match. Ospreay is looking for his fourth successful title defense while this is Fletcher’s second shot at the top prize, falling in defeat to then-champion Hangman Page at September 2025’s All Out. Fletcher was joined in the ring by Mark Davis and Jake Doyle. Both men will challenge The Young Bucks for the AEW World Tag Team Championships at the same event.
Fletcher stated that he wants Full Gear to be a perfect night for The Don Callis Family. He reminded everyone that he previously defeated Ospreay at the Full Gear pay-per-view two years earlier.
Fletcher promised that if the two meet again it will end with his hand raised. The match was made official shortly after the challenge.
This will mark the first singles match between Ospreay and Fletcher since AEW Revolution 2025. Ospreay won that previous encounter inside a Steel Cage.

Both wrestlers will compete in the men's Blood and Guts match on the November 4 episode of AEW Dynamite. Fletcher will team with The Don Callis Family while Ospreay teams with The Young Bucks, Adam Copeland, Darby Allin, and Steven Borden.
