summary_src: Claudio Castagnoli was stretchered out following a brutal attack by The Cut during the AEW Dynamite episode for October 28 2026, raising questions about his immediate future on AEW television.
body: The incident happened during Fright Night Dynamite after tensions between The Death Riders and The Cut erupted into another brawl. Earlier in the show, Jon Moxley and Daniel Garcia lost to Jay White and David Finlay following interference from Clark Connors. Moxley later challenged The Cut to an Anarchy in the Arena Match at Full Gear on November 14. Things got much worse later in the night. Following Marina Shafir’s victory over Rachel Armstrong and her confrontation with Mercedes Moné, Connors attacked Moxley at the commentary desk. Several members of both factions quickly became involved, with The Cut eventually getting the upper hand. Castagnoli then rushed out and attempted to even the odds, using a garbage can to attack members of The Cut. However, the numbers eventually caught up with him. Finlay struck Castagnoli with his shillelagh, including a shot to the head, before White delivered a Blade Runner onto the exposed concrete outside the ring. When Dynamite returned from a commercial break, AEW aired a replay of the attack and showed Castagnoli being loaded onto a stretcher and taken away as medical personnel attended to him. The scene immediately raised questions about Castagnoli’s status, especially with The Death Riders involved in a major storyline heading into Full Gear. However, there has been no confirmation that Castagnoli suffered a legitimate injury or that AEW intends to write him off television. The stretcher angle could simply be part of the ongoing rivalry between the two factions. With Moxley already challenging The Cut to Anarchy in the Arena at Full Gear, Castagnoli’s condition could become another important part of the storyline. For now, it remains unclear whether he will miss television time or return to seek revenge. title: Comeback Watch: Vince Russo Finally Speaks On WWE Return Rumors With a Cryptic Response
raw_title: Vince Russo Finally Addresses WWE Return Rumors With a Cryptic Response
body: 0 Vince Russo has finally spoken about reports linking him to a potential WWE creative comeback, but the former head writer hasn’t provided the clarity many wrestling fans were waiting for. Instead, Russo addressed the speculation on The Coach & Bro Show while directing his frustration toward the journalists covering the story. The discussion follows reports that Russo had conversations with WWE President Nick Khan over the summer about a possible return to the company. However, Vince Russo stopped short of confirming or denying whether those discussions took place. Russo claimed that several people reporting on the story had failed to contact him before publishing their accounts. He specifically mentioned Conrad Thompson, James Romero, and Sean Sapp while insisting that he would share news directly when he was ready. “None of those people contacted me or tried to contact me,” Russo said, adding that they all had his number. He also warned them against approaching him for a comment after the reports had already circulated. The former WWE writer compared the situation to speculation surrounding his departure from Juggalo Championship Wrestling (JCW), explaining that he eventually addressed that situation when he felt ready. “When I have something to say, I will say it! If there is nothing to say, I’m not gonna say anything,” he stated. On the WWE speculation specifically, Russo remained firm that he had nothing to discuss at present. He added that his audience would be the first to hear from him if the situation changed. Vince Russo also questioned the reporting process, drawing on his own background in journalism and television. “When you’re running with stories and you don’t contact the subject of those stories, bro, I’m sorry, you’re a hack,” he said. Conrad Thompson had previously reported that Russo discussed a potential creative return with Khan , while PWInsider reported that the idea never progressed toward an official hire. Russo’s latest comments neither confirm those accounts nor rule out that conversations occurred. Russo previously served as WWE’s head writer from 1997 to 1999, helping shape the Attitude Era before leaving for WCW. For now, his WWE future remains uncertain — and the ball is firmly in his court to provide any further answers. title: Paul Heyman Calls Vince McMahon a ‘Dictator’ in Triple H Comparison
raw_title: Paul Heyman Calls Vince McMahon a ‘Dictator’ in Triple H Comparison
body: 0 Paul Heyman has offered a candid look at the contrasting leadership styles of Vince McMahon and Paul “Triple H” Levesque, drawing a sharp distinction between the former WWE chairman and the company’s current creative chief. In an interview with Graham Bensinger , Heyman also reflected on the personal and professional difficulties that shaped his relationship with McMahon. Asked about McMahon’s character, Heyman acknowledged his achievements but questioned whether being a good person was ever a priority for his former boss. “No, I don’t think Vince ever considered himself a good man. I don’t think he cared about it,” Heyman said. He described McMahon as “a supremely complicated human being of great accomplishment.” Paul Heyman identified McMahon’s extraordinary work ethic as both his greatest strength and one of the hardest parts of working for him. “24/7, 365. He didn’t take holidays,” Heyman explained, adding that matching McMahon’s dedication was “absolutely impossible.” He also recalled their most difficult professional conflict, which came during WWE’s 2006 revival of ECW. Heyman said the former WWE Chairman initially promised him control before quickly taking away his creative authority. “He got off changing ECW on me, and it became just such a personal battle that was, one, terrible for the product, terrible for the company, even worse for the audience,” Heyman said. “That was the most miserable six months.” The conversation then turned to how WWE creative operates under Levesque compared with McMahon’s leadership. Heyman described the former chairman’s approach bluntly: “Vince was a dictator. It was his money and therefore it’s his show.” Levesque, however, received a very different assessment from Heyman, who praised his willingness to consider ideas from others rather than insist on controlling every decision. “Paul Levesque is not a dictator. He’s a collaborator,” Heyman said. “He’s the best editor I’ve ever worked with in my entire life. Ever.” Heyman added that Levesque listens to people with different perspectives, making the current creative environment “a completely different experience.” Although Heyman left WWE in December 2006 following the ECW disagreements and returned in 2012, he remains an exceptional authority in comparing both leadership styles firsthand. His comments underline how differently two influential figures have approached shaping WWE television. When I had just gotten back from my ACL surgery, I was really hungry to get in the ring and I was begging WWE to let me have a run with TNA,” Blackheart said. “I was talking to Tommy Dreamer for a little bit and he was totally down, but for some reason I wasn’t allowed to.” “And then when I got released, I needed a second to be on the indies and do me before signing another big contract,” she continued. title: 8 Times Real-World CHAOS Derailed WWE – Page 3
raw_title: 8 Times Real-World CHAOS Derailed WWE – Page 3
body: The terrorist attacks against the United States on September 11, 2001, shut down much of life in the country as Americans reeled from the uncertainty of what was happening. Flights were grounded. Schools and offices closed. Public gatherings were suspended. For the WWF, superstars were in Houston preparing for a SmackDown taping later that Tuesday evening when news of the attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon circulated. The taping – like every other sporting event and concert – was cancelled. Two days later – on the night that it normally would air – SmackDown became the first public gathering of its size to take place in the wake of 9/11, broadcasting live. Rather than continuing the InVasion angle that saw the Alliance (former WCW and ECW wrestlers) trying to usurp control of the WWF, the storyline was put aside for the night. Vince McMahon rallied the troops as the company draped itself in the American flag and preached patriotism and unity in what was a seriously scary and uncertain time. The episode included sit-down “confessionals” from superstars as they shared their thoughts on the attacks. This gave us the infamous moment of Stephanie McMahon comparing terrorists hijacking planes and killing 3,000 people to her father’s steroid trial seven years earlier. Yep. Steph’s abhorrent comments aside, the show was exactly what it needed to be: a calm in a chaotic storm, a piece of normalcy at a time when nothing felt normal. People were still reeling and grieving, but for a couple of hours, SmackDown served as a distraction for them. Scott is a former journalist and longtime wrestling fan who was smart enough to abandon WCW during the Monday Night Wars the same time as the Radicalz. He fondly remembers watching WrestleMania III, IV, V and VI and Saturday Night's Main Event, came back to wrestling during the Attitude Era, and has been a consumer of sports entertainment since then. He's written for WhatCulture since 2014, establishing the Ups and Downs articles for WWE Raw and WWE PPVs/PLEs and composing pieces on a variety of topics.

title: Darby Allin Retains TNT Title Against Josh Alexander
raw_title: Darby Allin Defeats Josh Alexander, Escapes AEW Fright Night Dynamite With TNT Title
summary_src: Darby Allin is still TNT Champion after a victory over Josh Alexander in a brutal bout on "AEW Fright Night Dynamite."
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Josh Alexander tried his hardest to take out Darby Allin, but Allin is still TNT Champion after a brutal battle on " AEW Fright Night Dynamite ." The Don Callis Family member wasted no time taking it to the champion to start off the match, hitting two dragon screws to send him crashing into the ring barricade and the ring steps. Allin was briefly able to rally back in the ring, but Alexander hit him with a suplex on the apron. Allin countered by pushing Alexander off the top rope, sending him spine-first into the edge of the apron, giving himself time to recover. The champion looked for a coffin drop from the top rope to the floor, but Alexander caught him for a release German suplex. Back in the ring, Allin tried to choke Alexander with his own head gear and got him into the Scorpion Deathlock. Alexander got to the ropes, and Allin jumped to the top for a coffin drop, but Alexander got out of the way. Allin hit a dragon screw of his own to Alexander on the ropes, and finally connected with the coffin drop while Alexander was still laying on the middle rope. Both men spilled to the outside, where Alexander set up two chairs and hit a leaping tombstone piledriver to send Allin through them. When Allin was still able to kick out back in the ring, Trent Beretta and Rocky Romero ran out to aid Alexander. Steven Borden popped out of the crowd, wearing a clown mask, to take them out. Alexander got Allin in a hold in the middle of the ring off the distraction, but Allin was able to reverse it for the win.
summary: Darby Allin retained the AEW TNT Championship against Josh Alexander in a hard-hitting match on Fright Night Dynamite. Alexander attacked early with dragon screws and a suplex on the apron, but Allin fought back with a top-rope push that sent Alexander spine-first into the apron edge. Allin ultimately hit a Coffin Drop on a prone Alexander draped across the middle rope to escape with the title.

body: NXT Date: October 27, 2026 Location: Capitol Wrestling Center, Orlando, Florida Commentators: Vic Joseph, Booker T. It’s the last show before Halloween Havoc and that means it’s time to finalize the card. We probably already know most of the card but there is still a big wheel that needs to be spun to determine some details. Throw in the Dusty Classic needing some finalists and we should be in for a big night. Let’s get to it. Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic Semifinals: Romeo Moreno/Noam Dar vs. Vanity Project Non-title. Moreno gets jumped to start fast and Dar (banged up after a weekend match with the Project) gets caught in the wrong corner. Dar loses his bandages but gets sent into the corner for the tag off to Moreno. The Project sends Dar into the steps, leaving Moreno to make the save with a dive. We take a break and come back with Moreno fighting out of a chinlock as we get an insert video of Grayson Waller going to Tony D’Angelo’s house. Dar dives over for the tag back to Moreno and house is quickly cleaned. A suplex/slam combination gets two on Smokes so he rips at the cut on Dar’s forehead. Baylor escapes a cross armbreaker and gets two off a neckbreaker. Hit It And Quit It connects, with Moreno making the save. Dar’s ankle lock sends Smokes out to the floor, followed by a collision to send them into different corners. Moreno is in for a super TKO to Baylor (that looked great) for two and Hit It And Quit It backfires. A high/low finishes Smokes to send Dar and Moreno to the finals at 14:12. Rating : B. Well there’s your title match if Dar and Moreno win the thing, which is probably the big idea. I’m not wild on having the champions lose, but at least it should have a reason for the whole thing. Dar and Moreno are feeling like a good team and that’s something NXT has needing for a long time. Tony D’Angelo rants to Robert Stone that Grayson Waller better not have hurt his family. Then he leaves to go after Waller, making me wonder why he was yelling at Stone in the first place when he has some important things to worry about. Cruz Montana says the worst part about last week was the phone call that he had to make. For a split second, he was a different Montana and the version that he spent years trying to stop being. Now though his past comes with a future. They lock up to start and Monroe snapmares her down and resorts to mockery. Rain gets in a headlock takeover but is knocked into the corner just as fast as we take a break. We come back with Monroe grabbing a swinging neckbreaker for two. Rain is sent into the corner but wins a fight on the apron to take over. A pumphandle suplex lets Rain chop away in the corner, followed by a spinebuster. Rain tries a fireman’s carry but some shots to the neck put her down, allowing Monroe to grab a rollup, with the rope, for the pin at 8:29. Rating : C. Monroe never impressed me on Evolve and this wasn’t exactly a start that is making me change my mind. She’s completely fine but not exactly memorable,

body: Queen Aminata’s first-ever AEW title reign has finally arrived. Aminata defeated Persephone in the main event of this week’s AEW Dynamite, live from the Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis, Missouri. After surviving a belt shot to the head at ringside from Britt Baker, Aminata was able to rally back into the main event and score the Off With Her Head kick finisher for the pinfall victory. Various members of the AEW roster ran down to the ring and celebrated with Aminata shortly after the match wrapped up. A championship reign was a long time coming for Aminata. The Guinea-born talent was making her sixth challenge for the TBS title since 2024, having come up short in past title showdowns. The result puts an end to Persephone’s run as champ after 60 days. Her title reign kicked off as part of this year’s All In pay-per-view from Wembley Stadium, beating Maya World at the event’s pre-show. The co-main event on Wednesday night saw Darby Allin retain the TNT Championship, defeating Josh Alexander of the Don Callis Family in a physical matchup. After a match full of thudding bumps and a Callis Family vs. Steven Borden brawl at ringside, Allin caught Alexander with a roll-up for the sudden pinfall win. Wednesday’s win kicked off what is a busy week for Allin, who is scheduled to head over to Mexico City this Friday for a CMLL matchup against Hechicero.

title: Queen Aminata Wins TBS Championship During October 28 AEW Dynamite
raw_title: Queen Aminata Wins TBS Championship During October 28 AEW Dynamite
summary_src: Queen Aminata is the new AEW TBS Champion, and not even Britt Baker could stop her from taking the title. During the AEW Dynamite episode for October 28 2026, Aminata defeated Persephone to capture the championship despite Baker repeatedly interfering in the match.
body: The title match took place during AEW’s Fright Night Dynamite in St. Louis, Missouri, with Persephone putting her TBS Championship on the line against Aminata. The two women exchanged strikes early in the match before Aminata took control with her signature chocolate kisses and a running boot. Baker quickly became a problem for Aminata. She distracted the challenger long enough for Persephone to regain control, allowing the champion to target Aminata’s neck. Persephone continued working over the injured area and even ripped the kinesiology tape off the back of Aminata’s neck during the match. Aminata refused to stay down. She fought back with several clotheslines, a double stomp and a meteora that sent Persephone crashing over a chair at ringside. However, Baker wasn’t finished interfering. After already breaking up one of Aminata’s pin attempts without the referee noticing, Baker struck Aminata with the TBS Championship belt while the official was checking on Persephone. Persephone took advantage and delivered a moonsault from the top rope, but Aminata somehow kicked out. Baker was visibly frustrated at ringside as the champion failed to put her challenger away. That turned out to be Persephone’s last major opportunity. Aminata recovered and connected with a headbutt before delivering a running knee strike to secure the three-count and win the AEW TBS Championship. The victory gives Aminata a major championship moment on Dynamite, especially considering the lengths Baker went to in an attempt to help Persephone retain. Despite the distractions, the belt shot and Persephone’s offense, Aminata managed to walk away with the title. The result also raises questions about Baker’s involvement in the TBS Championship picture. Her repeated attempts to interfere weren’t enough to prevent the title change, and it remains to be seen whether she’ll continue targeting Aminata now that there’s a new champion. summary_src: Queen Aminata defeated Persephone to become TBS Champion in the main event of "AEW Dynamite: Fright Night."
body: AEW Queen Aminata defeated Persephone to claim the TBS Championship in the main event of "AEW Dynamite: Fright Night." Persephone was making the fifth defense of her title since winning it from Maya World at All In in August, having seen off Aminata in a four-way also involving Hyan and Dani Luna at WrestleDream . She started the match with all the confidence of a defending champion, looking to keep her challenger grounded and grinding her down in the middle of the ring on the mat. Aminata tried to fight back in instances but Persephone continued to be the more spiteful, taking her into the corner and biting at her head. She then knocked her out of the ring with a dropkick, calling for Britt Baker at ringside to grab a chair. Persephone sat Aminata on the chair and looked for a dropkick onto them, but Aminata escaped her and the action returned to the ring. Albeit with Persephone still at the advantage. Aminata managed to find some breathing space with a headbutt followed by a series of lariats, rolling Persephone up for two and then planting her with a neckbreaker. Persephone wiped her out with a spear to end the rally, continuing to target the neck of her challenger. Aminata managed to get Persephone seated on the chair from earlier, delivering a dropkick from the apron to send her crashing off of it. But then Baker struck Aminata with the TBS title belt as the referee checked on Persephone, throwing her into the ring to surely be finished off. However, Aminata kicked out at two, rocking Persephone with a headbutt and delivering Off With Her Head for the winning pinfall to claim the TBS Championship for herself.

Persephone was making her fifth defense since beating Maya World for the title at All In in August and had previously beaten Aminata in a four-way match at WrestleDream. The champion controlled much of the bout with mat work, biting and a dropkick but Aminata rallied with a headbutt, lariats, a nearfall and a neckbreaker before securing the victory.

body: For the first time in her career, Queen Aminata can call herself an AEW champion. Aminata defeated Persephone in the main event of Wednesday’s Fright Night Dynamite to win the TBS title, her first major singles title of any kind. She picked up the win despite Britt Baker’s interference. Baker hit Aminata with the title belt on the outside of the ring, but the challenger still kicked out of a moonsault afterward. Aminata hit a headbutt and the running Off With Her Head kick to pick up the pin and win, getting emotional afterward. Aminata was joined by several women from the locker room in the ring followed by confetti to close the show. It was her fifth crack at the title dating back nearly two years. She was also previously unsuccessful at dethroning ROH Women’s World Champion Athena (2024’s Death Before Dishonor) and AEW Women’s World Champion Mercedes Mone at this month’s Grand Slam Paris. She becomes the tenth TBS Champion in AEW history and ends the 60-day reign of Persephone which saw four successful title defenses. title: Toni Storm Return Not Imminent In AEW

body: Toni Storm is being teased for a possible return to AEW TV, but it reportedly won’t be happening right away. As noted , content creator Astrid Pizarro received a set of “Toni Storm tapes” at AEW WrestleDream that seemed to indicate Storm could be coming back into AEW storylines soon. The former Women’s World Champion has been off TV since she was written out via an mysterious attack on the episode of AEW Dynamite following AEW Revolution in March. Fightful Select cites sources as saying that Storm is not scheduled to return imminently, but that there could be “other elements involving her” that get woven into AEW TV. There has been no word of Storm being around at many, if any, AEW shows. It was reported back in March that Storm was not expected to available to return until the end of the year at the earliest, but most likely at some point in 2027. The absence is not said to be related to an injury, though any details beyond that have been kept quiet and something Tony Khan has refused to discuss.
summary: Toni Storm has been absent from AEW television since a mysterious attack on Dynamite after Revolution in March. Per Fightful Select, while teases involving her have appeared on recent shows, she is not scheduled to return anytime soon and other elements tied to her could be incorporated into storylines instead. She has not been present at most AEW events and was previously reported as unavailable until late 2026 or 2027 at the earliest, with Tony Khan declining to comment on the situation.

raw_title: Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher set for AEW Full Gear 2026
summary_src: Kyle Fletcher will look to take down AEW World Champion Will Ospreay in the main event of Full Gear on November 14.
body: Will Ospreay’s next assignment as AEW World Champion has been set. Ospreay will look to take down former TNT Champion Kyle Fletcher at Full Gear on November 14. The match will go down as part of a pay-per-view event from the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix, Arizona. Fletcher called for a title match against Ospreay on Wednesday night’s episode of Dynamite, making his case as the uncrowned world champion in AEW. His argument was persuasive to those behind the scenes, as just moments later it was confirmed that he will face Ospreay at the next PPV. The new matchup will be Fletcher’s second-ever attempt to become AEW World Champion. He previously tried to take the belt at last year’s All Out card, falling to Hangman Adam Page in a 38-minute bout. Ospreay will be looking to defend his world title for the fourth time. He has beaten Kazuchika Okada, Jon Moxley, and most recently prevailed in the company’s first-ever Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. While not made official yet, Jon Moxley of the Death Riders challenged Jay White’s The Cut faction to an Anarchy in the Arena match for this year’s Full Gear card. The special AEW match, which we only see once or twice a year, was thrown out after a huge brawl between the groups erupted on Wednesday night. We also saw another tease on Wednesday regarding an upcoming AEW World Trios Championships match, which will see Brodido and Hangman Adam Page face the New Level and Swerve Strickland. While the New Level as well as Page insist that the upcoming title showdown won’t be under Texas Death Match rules, Strickland once again expressed his enthusiasm for giving the match such a harsh ruleset. To prove his point, Strickland kidnapped Bandido on Wednesday, attacked and unmasked the luchador, then left him in a pool of his own blood.

body: 0 TNA Wrestling star Lei Ying Lee has been missing from television for nearly three months, leaving questions about her status with the promotion. A new report has now shed light on her absence, providing an important update on her future with the company. According to PWInsider , Lee remains under contract with TNA despite her extended time away from the ring. Her absence reportedly stems from a personal trip that has kept her away from regular programming since July. The report states that Lee travelled to China to spend time with her family after going many years without returning home. TNA officials reportedly gave her additional time away to make the trip, suggesting her absence isn’t related to a departure from the promotion. Lee’s last TNA appearance came during her Knockouts World Championship rivalry with Xia Brookside. Brookside defeated her to capture the title at Slammiversary on June 28, 2026, ending Lee’s championship run. Lee subsequently received another opportunity to reclaim the gold during the July 1 iMPACT! television tapings in Albany, New York. The two competed in a No Disqualification match, but Brookside retained the championship, with that contest marking Lee’s most recent appearance for TNA. The absence followed an eventful year for Lee. She had regained the Knockouts World Championship by defeating Arianna Grace on the May 7 episode of iMPACT! Her subsequent rivalry with Brookside brought another title change into the picture, before the champion successfully defended her gold in their rematch. Despite Lee’s prolonged absence, the latest report indicates she remains part of TNA’s roster. No confirmed timeline for her return to television has come to light. For now, Lee’s time away appears to be about family rather than unfinished business with TNA. While the Knockouts division continues without her on-screen presence, fans will have to wait for an official update before knowing when she could step back into the ring and resume her pursuit of championship gold. title: Toni Storm AEW Return Not Imminent

summary_src: AEW has plans going on regarding Toni Storm’s return. Recently at AEW WrestleDream, several mysterious tapes related to Storm surfaced at the PPV, which teased the return of “Timeless” Toni Storm. Now weeks later, Fightful Select shared a report regarding Storm’s return.
body: Recently at AEW WrestleDream, several mysterious tapes related to Storm surfaced at the PPV, which teased the return of “Timeless” Toni Storm. Now weeks later, Fightful Select shared a report regarding Storm’s return. As per Fightful Select’s report, their team spoke to AEW following the tapes teasing her return at WrestleDream. The report claims that as they spoke to people in AEW, it was communicated that “Storm’s in-ring isn’t imminent, but there could be other elements involving her that get worked in.” Storm’s last AEW appearance was on March 18, 2026, when she was found bloodied on the floor backstage. Her latest match dates back to her AEW Revolution 2026 win over Marina Shafir. At the AEW WrestleDream media scrum, Tony Khan shared an update regarding Storm’s absence . “I know we’ve been missing Timeless Toni Storm, but everybody’s just been doing absolutely fantastic. The women’s wrestling in AEW has seen the locker room absolutely step up in the absence of the former world champion. “We have a great world champion now in Mercedes Moné, who’s had her first successful defense of the world championship tonight. The former world champion, Timeless Toni Storm, is certainly on a lot of our minds, and I can’t say when or where, but I know Timeless Toni Storm will be back in AEW and looking to get payback for whoever it was that took her out.” Shounak Chakrabarti Shounak Chakrabarti is an experienced sports journalist with a lifelong passion for athletics and storytelling. title: Shawn Michaels Leads NXT’s Nostalgic 2012 WWE Ad Remake
raw_title: Shawn Michaels Leads NXT’s Nostalgic 2012 WWE Ad Remake
body: 0 WWE NXT is bringing back a memorable piece of wrestling history to promote its upcoming schedule change. Shawn Michaels and many other NXT stars have created a popular WWE ad remake, adding some humor while reminding fans about next week’s special episode. Michaels, who serves as WWE NXT’s Head of Creative, shared the video on social media. The clip is a remake of the commercial WWE released to promote the 1,000th episode of RAW. The original became a fan favorite thanks to its comedy and appearances from several WWE Superstars. In the remake, Michaels replaces Vince McMahon. He asks Zilla Fatu to spread the word about NXT temporarily moving to Wednesday night. Fatu then passes the message along incorrectly, with Wren Sinclair, Hank & Tank, Shiloh Hill, Kendall Grey, Grayson Waller, Kelani Jordan, and other NXT stars joining in as the announcement becomes increasingly confusing. At the end of the video, NXT GM Robert Stone comes with the actual announcement about the schedule change. Michaels shared the video on X and joked that he gave Fatu “ONE job… make sure everybody knows when #WWENXT is on next week.” The video also serves a practical purpose, as NXT will move from its usual Tuesday night slot to Wednesday for the week. The special episode airs Wednesday, November 4, at 8 p.m. ET/7 p.m. CT on The CW. The show will also feature appearances from two of WWE’s biggest names. John Cena will make a special appearance, and Cody Rhodes will be presenting the trophy to the winner of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic final, giving fans more reasons to tune in to the special broadcast. The schedule change will also put NXT directly against AEW Dynamite’s special Blood & Guts edition. The post Shawn Michaels Leads NXT’s Nostalgic 2012 WWE Ad Remake appeared first on Wrestlezone .

body: 0 AEW has reignited the mystery surrounding ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm with a series of unusual clues, but fans waiting for the former Women’s World Champion to return to the ring may need to exercise some patience. A new backstage report has provided an update on the plans behind her disappearance and what could come next. Toni Storm has been absent from AEW television since defeating Marina Shafir at Revolution in March 2026. She was subsequently written out of the storylines following a mysterious backstage attack, leaving her status and the identity of her attacker unresolved. According to Fightful Select , AEW sources have indicated that Storm’s in-ring comeback isn’t imminent, although the company could introduce more storyline elements involving her before she is ready to compete again. The latest clues emerged at WrestleDream on October 17 , when select media members and content creators received cassette tapes linked to Storm. The recordings were presented as part of an ongoing mystery, with five tapes reportedly distributed to different recipients. Astrid Pizarro was among those who shared details of the tapes online. The first recording, titled “Mundanities,” featured Renee Paquette narrating audio supposedly recorded by Storm. The fifth cassette reportedly carries the title “Death,” leaving more questions for AEW to answer as the mystery develops. Fightful Select also reported that AEW had planned to introduce clues pointing toward multiple possible suspects in the attack. Creative reportedly had a particular person in mind for the eventual reveal, but left room to change that decision if necessary. AEW President Tony Khan previously addressed Storm’s future during the WrestleDream media scrum, assuring fans that she would return without offering a timeframe. “I can’t say when or where but I know ‘Timeless’ Toni Storm will be back in AEW,” Khan said. Storm has also reportedly remained largely absent from AEW events during her time away. While the cassette campaign has pressed play on her storyline again, it doesn’t confirm an imminent return to the ring. For now, AEW appears ready to keep the mystery alive while Storm’s wrestling comeback remains uncertain. The next tape may provide another clue, but the full story is still unwinding. body: Asuka is set to join the police force in Osaka, Japan, for one day amid her ongoing WWE absence. Last seen losing to IYO Sky at WWE Backlash 2026 in May 2026, Asuka has been off WWE TV since then. Recently on social media , the former Women’s Champion announced her new upcoming role as a Police Chief in her hometown of Osaka, Japan. Asuka will now serve as the one-day police chief for the Oyodo Police Station on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. The police station in question is located in Kita Ward in Osaka City, which happens to be her hometown. Her new role as a one-day police chief is basically an attraction, where she will be giving away signed police merchandise and items to fans. TNT Champion Darby Allin prepared to defend his championship against Josh Alexander, as the Don Callis Family aimed to tighten its grip on AEW before Blood and Guts. Queen Aminata stood one victory from a career-defining moment, challenging Persephone for the TBS Championship, while FTR and the Motor City Machine Guns continued their best-of-five series. With “Blood and Guts” approaching and “Full Gear” on the horizon, the atmosphere was tense. title: Contract News: Three stars with expiring contracts that could cross the line — AEW stars to join TNA Wrestling
raw_title: AEW stars to join TNA Wrestling: Three stars with expiring contracts that could cross the line
body: TNA Wrestling has had a busy few weeks when it comes to acquisitions, with the likes of Shayna Baszler and Shotzi Blackheart signing with the promotion and both Daria Rae and Santino Marella signing new deals. According to a recent report from Fightful Select, more announcements could be on the way and speculation as already begun regarding what other new signings could arrive and what existing TNA stars could extend their stays. With some interesting AEW talent potentially departing Tony Khan’s company soon, we could see TNA bolster their roster with some recognisable names. Here are three AEW stars with expiring contracts that could cross the line to TNA Wrestling: According to reports from Fightful Select, Anthony Bowens should already be a free agent, with his AEW contract expiring on October 1 along with his former tag team partner Max Caster. However, there is a little bit of doubt about Bowens’ status now following comments from Caster during a recent K&S WrestleFest signing , where he said that Bowens was still with AEW. For what it’s worth Bowens is still listed as a member of the AEW roster page , unlike Caster who, of course had a controversial one-off appearance in TNA at Bound for Glory after exiting AEW. If Bowens is actually a free agent after all then TNA should definitely consider picking him up. Whether it be in the X-Division or potentially even the main event, Bowens still has a lot of untapped potential. Before arriving in AEW for its launch in 2019, Ortiz and his former tag team partner Mike Santana ( now Cruz Montana in WWE ) were fixtures of TNA between 2017 and 2019. Making up two members of the reformed Latin American Xchange faction, the pair won four TNA World Tag Team Championships together and revitalised the group along with Diamante and original members Homicide and Konnan. After Ortiz and Santana went their separate ways in AEW in 2023, the latter returned to TNA as a singles star whilst Ortiz remained where he was. It’s safe to say Santana’s bold career choice paid off, as he became TNA World Champion in 2025 and signed with WWE this past summer. While Ortiz and Santana famously are not all that friendly with each other anymore, there could perhaps be a chance for Ortiz to at least try to rebuild his own career in TNA in a similar way to his former tag partner, should he depart AEW when his contract is reportedly up this fall. Scorpio Sky is another notable AEW original who could be set to depart the company imminently, as it has been reported that his contract is due to expire in October. In AEW’s first three years of existence, Sky was among the strongest booked stars outside of the main event scene; becoming one half of the inaugural AEW World Tag Team Champions alongside Frankie Kazarian and a two-time TNT Champion in 2022. After several long-term absences however, Sky fell from grace entirely and only found a bit of consistency over the past year or so when he formed SkyFlight alongside Dante & Darius Martin

title: AEW Fright Night Dynamite Delivers Mixed Reactions
raw_title: AEW Dynamite 10/28/2026: 3 Things We Hated & 3 Things We Loved
summary_src: On a special Fright Night episode for Halloween, here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/28/26 episode of "AEW ﻿Dynamite!"
body: AEW/Speedy Welcome to Wrestling Inc.'s weekly review of "AEW Dynamite," the show that once again graced us with a Halloween-themed episode dubbed Fright Night! Of course, there wasn't much actual Halloween content on the show, and the WINC staff has some thoughts about that. We also have thoughts on Queen Aminata winning the TBS Championship , Darby Allin retaining the TNT Championship , and more! If you missed the show, please feel free to catch up by checking out our "AEW Dynamite" 10/28/26 live blog , which contains nothing but objective information on everything that went down Wednesday night. If you're more interested in the subjective opinions of the WINC crew, centered around the matches and segments we found most worthy of comment, you're in the right place. Here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/28/26 episode of "AEW Dynamite!" AEW/Speedy I feel like AEW had been on a hot stretch of themed episodes for awhile in 2026, but sadly, it ended with "Fright Night Dynamite," which was really disappointing when it came to being the company's Halloween episode. There were zero spooky-themed stipulation matches on the show tonight, though that's likely because of Blood & Guts next week, as well as the strict "no blood" rule enforced by the Missouri Athletic Commission. Outside of a few stars wearing costumes and some nice graphics, there was nothing that screamed "Halloween" to me at all. Though it is AEW, blood doesn't have to be necessarily used in a stipulation match, like a "Nightmare on Elm Street Fight" or whatever. Maybe that's more of a WWE-like gimmick, but I expected something a little more from an episode with "Fright Night" in the name. I think AEW has a bit of a problem right now, though it's obviously something that will right itself here soon, especially as we get to the end of the year, and it's not exactly something that anyone could have prepared for after a string of benefit and tribute shows. That problem is there are too many events trying to do too much in a short period of time. The build to WrestleDream was rushed, at no fault of anyone in AEW's, and it still feels like things are a bit chaotic and moving too quickly. Maybe Tony Khan and those booking tonight's show didn't want anything too over-the-top with Blood & Guts next week. We did get, however, another big announcement, that Anarchy in the Arena will take place at AEW Full Gear , only adding to the packed slate of things AEW has going on right now. I wasn't asking for much tonight — maybe a single stipulation match with something a little spooky and goofy. We did get a lot of good in-ring (nothing new for AEW), a fantastic title change in the main event, and some more setup for a few Full Gear matches, but I just wanted to feel more in the Halloween spirit. AEW/Speedy I will admit right off the top here that I've done a full 180 on Swerve Strickland demanding a Texas Death rematch for the AEW World Trios Championships, held by his arch
summary: Wrestling Inc. staff reviewed the October 28, 2026 episode of AEW Dynamite, noting a lack of Halloween elements despite its Fright Night theme. They praised Queen Aminata capturing the TBS Championship and Darby Allin keeping the TNT Championship while expressing disappointment over the overall themed presentation ending a strong run of special episodes.

body: Just months after his WWE debut, Royce Keys is already a WWE 2K26 playable character. Recently, speaking to Mike Chiari of Bleacher Report , Keys opened up about his new addition to the list of WWE 2K26’s playable characters. Keys was added to WWE 2K26 as part of Ringside Pass Season 6 on Oct. 28, 2026. “ It’s a great accomplishment because I think I’ve played almost every WWE video game, and I’ve always created myself,” Keys said. “And now I don’t have to do all the hard work of finding all the right moves, but it’s definitely a very high accomplishment for me ,” he said. “ I got kids, so I play all the current stuff,” Keys said. “In the past, I think one of my favorite ones that I was obsessed with as a kid was the Royal Rumble for Super Nintendo. And then another one was No Mercy. Then I got into the SmackDown vs. Raw games and the 2K. I even got some emulated games, the old WrestleFest game. I love them all ,” Keys added. Keys was added to the game as part of the Ringside Pass Season 6, where Earthquake and Typhoon of the Natural Disasters, and AAA’s Octagón Jr. were also a part of it. The Ringside Pass Season 6 introduces all of the above-named wrestlers. All four wrestlers also bring a total of 43 new moves and taunts with them. New personas, including AJ Styles Masked and Bray Wyatt ’23, new creation parts and moves for character customization, RXP boosts, Island VC, MyFACTION tokens, and more are also part of the Ringside Pass Season 6. The free tier has retro looks for AJ Styles, Rhea Ripley ’20, and Eddie Guerrero ’05. title: Rumor Roundup: Vince Russo WWE Discusses, new Crown Jewel match, WNBA Finals chaos, more!
raw_title: Rumor Roundup: Vince Russo WWE talks, new Crown Jewel match, WNBA Finals chaos, more!
body: Link WWE Part Of Rumor Roundup: Hottest WWE rumors, AEW rumors, and more! see all updates Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Is there really a chance that WWE might resort to bringing back Vince Russo to its creative team? Let’s see what today’s rumors have to say about it! Following up on Conrad Thompson’s claim that Vince Russo was in talks to return to WWE, Fightful The Hump’s Sean Ross Sapp says numerous WWE writers, producers, and agents hadn’t heard about that and “ completely laughed it off .” However, someone at WWE headquarters said Russo was indeed in the building and the conversation did happen. Even so, Sapp was outright told “ he is not coming in ,” and people outside of WWE headquarters were never told about it. title: Becky Lynch Details Real Animosity in WWE Storylines
raw_title: Becky Lynch explains how real-life animosity influences WWE storylines
summary_src: Becky Lynch has explained how WWE sometimes uses real-life animosities to influence the TV storylines. Recently, speaking on So U Think U Can Sports?
body: Becky Lynch has explained how WWE sometimes uses real-life animosities to influence the TV storylines. Recently, speaking on So U Think U Can Sports? with Eliot Glazer , Lynch addressed the scripted aspect of WWE and how the promotion interweaves reality, making it hard to identify what’s real and what’s not. “ Because it is, ” Lynch responded to being asked if WWE was scripted. “ Because there’s stories, there’s storylines that go behind it. But the beautiful part about wrestling is we interweave reality and scripted to the point where you kind of don’t know what’s real and what’s scripted.” “ There’s competition. There’s genuine competition. So there’s real animosity, and then there’s, you know, when you’re in a high-level atmosphere like that, you’re going to get two people that maybe don’t like each other ,” she said. “ And so some of that’s going to weave in. And that kind of is when it’s the most interesting. You want to see conflict. You want to see conflict. Conflict. You want to see fighting, ” Lynch added. Over the years, WWE has used real animosities several times in their storylines, namely, the Edge vs. Matt Hardy feud, Brett Hart against Shawn Michaels/Vince McMahon, Matt Riddle-Seth Rollins, and many more. title: Contract News: Anthony Bowens gave wrestling its unforgettable ‘He’s gay’ moment. Now his AEW contract is up.
raw_title: Anthony Bowens gave wrestling its unforgettable ‘He’s gay’ moment. Now his AEW contract is up.
body: The historic title wins, advocacy and magical 'He's gay' chant anchor Anthony Bowens' AEW legacy and career in pro wrestling. The bravado and joy he shows in the batter’s box exude a charisma equal to his love of the sport he first loved. His consistent callouts of homophobia on social media create rallying points pushing back on hate with defiance needed in our current time. The humor displayed in several viral skits with his partner genuinely speaks to an intersection of queer and pop culture with disarming charm. Gay pro wrestler reprises photo of him kissing boyfriend in front of anti-gay protesters Star pro wrestler Anthony Bowens clapped back with the perfect response to haters. And his role on the All Elite Wrestling roster over the last six years blended all of those things to deliver him historic firsts, stardom and an influence that put the marked shift of general pro wrestling audiences toward queer acceptance and celebration in the spotlight. Bowens’ contract with AEW expired on Friday, along with that of his The Acclaimed partner Max Caster, at least temporarily ending his tenure with the promotion. According to Fightful, there is still a chance that both could be re-signed as contract negotiations between the two parties were impacted by the untimely deaths of beloved AEW stars Andy “The Butcher” Williams and Pac in recent weeks. The hope is that Bowens remains with the company. Unlike Caster, who hasn’t appeared on AEW programming this year, Bowens was still involved on screen as a member of The Opps, though in a much diminished role compared to his heights with The Acclaimed. That presence does bode better odds of Bowens staying with the company, but there is a chance it could be the end of a groundbreaking run for Bowens. Bowens lays claim to being the first out gay male champion in AEW history , the first out gay AEW World Tag Team and Trios champion and one of the most public LGBTQ advocates pro wrestling has ever seen. If this is the end of this era of Bowens’ career, it is one that had a supreme impact on the state of mainstream pro wrestling. The title wins will remain in the record books, how he uses his voice won’t dissipate and his pro wrestling career isn’t going to end with an exit from AEW, but the mark he left on the company speaks to an influence speaks to more than those accomplishments. The obvious reflection point is June 23, 2003, the night that Bowens humorously declared he was gay on AEW programming after AEW wrestler Harley Cameron flirted with him. The moment sparked the Chicago crowd into a joyous chant of “He’s gay” celebrating Bowens. Sunday, fans and wrestlers around the world were shocked and saddened when the news of Pac's death broke. Fans and wrestlers alike have shared tributes, and Wednesday's episode of Dynamite was dedicated to his memory. Tony Khan also booked a special match between Will Ospreay and Ricochet, two of Pac's most talented rivals. It's been a sad few weeks in the wrestling world with the passing of Andy "The Butcher" Williams and now Benjamin "Pac" Satterley, but their legacies will live on forever. The show opened with Excalibur giving a speech about Pac from the announce table as the crowd chanted Pac's name. We then went to Tony Schiavone in the ring with a framed picture of Pac next to a huge memorial bouquet. Schiavone talked about the example Pac set for the locker room and the impression he left on everyone at AEW. He said this week's episode is for him. He then threw to a moment from All Out with Jon Moxley that ended up being the final thing Pac filmed for the company. It was a promo from Mox focused on Will Ospreay, but the words were strangely relevant. Pac was the last of the group to walk off screen. Schiavone asked for silence during a 10-bell salute. The entire roster stood on the stage wearing Pac shirts. Many of them were crying or close to it. Moxley then made his way to the ring for the first match. The opening contest saw Moxley put his Continental Championship on the line against Orange Cassidy. OC had a very memorable match against Pac some time ago at Revolution 2020, and Mox's ties to Pac are obvious. As Mox and OC started to feel each other out with some lockups, the announcers talked about the mood backstage throughout the day and how everyone is trying to live up to Pac's work ethic. Despite Moxley's clear size and power advantage, they worked it like a competitive match with a lot of technical wrestling. We all know how good Mox is, and we all know how good OC is, too. They might have very different styles, but both are pros who can adapt, so a good match is hardly surprising. At a time when everyone is sad, Moxley and Cassidy managed to inject some humor into the match and get the crowd in the right mindset. They knew the assignment and delivered in every way. summary_src: AEW’s Fright Night special ended with a bang when Queen Aminata upset Persephone to win the TBS Championship. Dynamite (Oct.
body: Link AEW Manolo Has Pizzazz learned all of life’s lessons from decades of professional wrestling. Manolo has been covering the sport for over ten years on Cageside Seats. AEW’s Fright Night special ended with a bang when Queen Aminata upset Persephone to win the TBS Championship. Dynamite (Oct. 28, 2026) also featured Jon Moxley issuing a challenge for Anarchy in the Arena, Darby Allin surviving a TNT title defense, Ilja Dragunov’s next target, and more from Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis, Missouri. Queen Aminata sent fright shivering down Persephone’s spine by winning the TBS Championship in an upset. Perse entered with cocky confidence alongside Britt Baker dressed as Miss Trunchbull. This was a tepid build coming into the match. However, AEW gave it the main event slot to close the show. Given that this episode had another unannounced extra long overrun, AEW ran a video package of big moments in St. Louis. Surely that was foreshadowing for fans to stick around to see another big moment on this night. That’s exactly what happened. Baker created distractions to help Persephone gain control. Aminata turned the tide with her running kick, but the impact knocked Perse out of the ring away from a pin. Aminata followed for a brutal jumping stomp off the apron to Perse seated on a steel chair. That tide didn’t last long. Baker crept up with the title belt to blast Aminata. Persephone taunted the crowd and landed a moonsault. Aminata snapped the crowd back in with a kick out. Loud support came from the crowd chanting Aminata’s name. The challenger escaped the champion’s crucifix lift to bop a headbutt. Aminata’s chance was there for a running kick clean on the money. 1, 2, 3, new champion. That was a feel-good title change. I’m sad that Persephone’s run is over, because it didn’t feel like it reached her full potential. On a personal level, it is nice to see Aminata’s hard work pay off in success. I think that’s the reason the crowd was behind her more than the storyline. The story of her rise was mediocre. Perhaps it was the lack of passionate promos on screen during the course of this arc. As it stands, the moment still hit big with the fans. And it gives Dynamite zest for the unexpected to happen from time to time. Catch up on the excellent play-by-play details from Claire Elizabeth. Let’s break the rest of the show. Jay White & David Finlay defeated Jon Moxley & Daniel Garcia. The finish came down to interference from The Cut. In the calamity, Clark Connors speared Garcia, and White closed with the Blade Runner to win. A melee erupted between The Cut and the Death Riders, and Moxley challenged thosee rapscallions to Anarchy in the Arena at Full Gear. The Death Riders made this a fun match for the start of this feud. Moxley countered the Blade Runner into a Paradigm Shift to get bragging rights on Switchblade. The corner train is a cool spot when it turns into a marathon. The cheap finish is understandable as typical heel faction fodder. Commentary bro

The episode also saw Jon Moxley issue a challenge for Anarchy in the Arena, Darby Allin retain his TNT title, and Ilja Dragunov name his next target. The Fright Night special featured an unannounced overrun and ran long with a video package highlighting moments in the city.

body: Jay White’s new AEW stable needed two names to survive one weekend. White christened the group The Last Outfit on the Oct. 24, 2026 episode of AEW Collision , per WhatCulture and F4W. The show aired on TNT and HBO Max from Winston-Salem, North Carolina. Hours later, an AEW backstage digital exclusive had White calling them The Cut, WrestleTalk and SEScoops reported. This is a storyline (kayfabe) development. As of Oct. 26, Wrestling Noticias reports the real reason for the name change has not been made public. The setup came three nights earlier. On the Oct. 21 AEW Dynamite , Jon Moxley beat Roderick Strong. Wrestleview and Sportskeeda reported that the Bang Bang Gang and The Dogs then jumped the Death Riders and The Conglomeration. Both outlets noted the group turned on Gabe Kidd as well. That alliance carries history. White, Juice Robinson, David Finlay and Clark Connors all share Bullet Club roots from their New Japan days. So when White opened Saturday’s Collision in the ring, the old name felt inevitable. He teased it, per WhatCulture and NoDQ’s coverage of the Oct. 24 show. Then he said his crew was more than a “club” and announced The Last Outfit. Fans did not buy it. WrestleTalk described reaction on YouTube and social media as largely negative. NoDQ quoted one fan calling it the “WORST name ive ever heard since Viking Experience.” I laughed, and then I conceded the point. By Oct. 26, AEW’s official roster page listed the group as The Cut, as reported by F4W . WhatCulture, citing POST Wrestling, said the Collision results page changed too. WrestleTalk noted the YouTube video title had not caught up when it published. Some coverage ties the change to fan feedback. Treat that as speculation, because no outlet has confirmed it. Here is why I think The Cut is the better name. The promo explains it for you. In AEW’s Oct. 25 backstage video, quoted by WrestleTalk and Wrestling Headlines, White aims straight at Moxley. He calls his crew the last outfit “capable of slicing out the cancer” of the Death Riders. Then he lands it: “We are The Cut.” Look at what happened to the rejected name. “The last outfit” survives as a lowercase phrase, demoted from brand to description. The surgical metaphor then becomes the title. The name now doubles as the mission, and that is tidy character writing. It also suits the man at the center. White already wrestles as the Switchblade, so a blade-themed faction fits him. In its coverage of the Oct. 25 video, SEScoops pointed out that White never addresses the switch. Inside the story, The Cut was simply always the plan. I respect a retcon that refuses to blink. The promo also leans hard into western imagery. In the Oct. 25 video, White calls his crew “top shelf high rollers, the golden gun slingers, some dirty dogs, your Collision cowboys.” SEScoops notes that “dirty dogs” nods to The Dogs. “Collision cowboys” is the Bang Bang Gang’s nickname on the show. As I read it, that roll call is a mission statement in costum
summary: The latest: the latest: Jay White’s new AEW stable needed two names to survive one weekend. Hours later, an AEW backstage digital exclusive had White calling them The Cut, WrestleTalk and SEScoops reported.

Without much effort, Cena said his failsafe costume is his entire WWE attire. “Yes. So the trope, the easy one, is the John Cena costume. title: End of an Era: TNA Hall of Famer Wants To Bring AJ Styles Out of Retirement for Another Match
raw_title: TNA Hall of Famer Wants To Bring AJ Styles Out of Retirement for Another Match
body: 0 Amazing Red has his sights set on a potential dream match with AJ Styles , suggesting the WWE Hall of Famer could eventually return to the ring if the timing is right. Styles officially retired from in-ring wrestling after losing to Gunther at the 2026 WWE Royal Rumble. However, he has not completely ruled out wrestling again. This is, particularly if he gets the opportunity to share the ring with his son, Avery Styles. Avery has already begun pursuing professional wrestling. He made his independent wrestling debut in June 2026 before joining TNA and making his in-ring debut in a multi-person outing at Bound For Glory on October 11. Amazing Red discussed the possibility during an interview with Sports Matters TV . The TNA Hall of Famer suggested that Styles’ continued involvement in his son Avery’s wrestling journey could provide a path toward getting the former WWE Champion back into competition. Red believes there could be a way to make another match with Styles happen, even if it means going through the next generation to get there. During the interview, Red explained that he has noticed Styles remaining involved in his son’s development, including accompanying him to training and the wrestling dojo. The TNA veteran believes those connections could eventually draw Styles back into the ring. “I see what you see, where I see AJ training. See AJ going to the dojo. I see him following his son and making sure he’s doing here and there. And you can tell, you can tell. I don’t think you can leave wrestling,” Red said. Red acknowledged that wrestlers sometimes need to step away from the business for mental or physical reasons. However, he believes the pull of professional wrestling makes retirement difficult to maintain permanently. “I think there are moments where we have to step away, for sure, if it’s a mental break, physical break, but wrestling is such a hard thing to leave. It’s just one of those ex-girlfriends that just doesn’t leave you alone,” he added. Red also suggested that Styles’ son could become a link between the two veterans, potentially creating an opportunity for another match. “And I feel like if the timing is right for him, maybe I have to go through his son to get to him, you know? Who knows?” Red said. The possibility has clearly crossed Red’s mind, and he admitted that the idea of facing Avery Styles for a championship could eventually lead to an unexpected encounter with the Phenomenal One. “I could probably wrestle AJ Styles’ son at some point for the X-Division title. It’s just so crazy. So crazy,” Red said. Red and Styles have a history dating back to their time in TNA, where both contributed to the promotion’s X-Division scene. Red recently returned to the TNA at Bound For Glory 2026, where he won the X-Division Championship after being inducted into the company’s Hall of Fame. title: Contract News: Austin Creed and Kofi Kingston Signed a 5 Year AEW Contract
raw_title: Austin Creed and Kofi Kingston Signed a 5 Year AEW Contract
body: Austin Creed and Kofi Kingston, the former WWE stars now performing together as The New Level, have reportedly signed five-year contracts with All Elite Wrestling (AEW). The reported agreements signal a long-term commitment between the two veteran performers and the promotion following their high-profile arrival at AEW All In: London 2026. Both wrestlers have agreed to five-year deals. The news offers a clearer picture of AEW’s plans for the duo, who left WWE earlier this year after spending years establishing themselves as members of The New Day. Although the pair’s AEW arrival was widely anticipated, the reported contract length suggests their new chapter is intended to extend well beyond their initial appearance. The reported five-year agreements are a significant development for The New Level. Under their former WWE identities, Xavier Woods and Kofi Kingston built a reputation as one of the company’s most successful and recognizable tag teams. Their move to AEW gives them an opportunity to continue competing together while introducing themselves to a different audience under a new team name. The reported contract length also provides a clearer indication of how long the promotion could have the pair available for its future programming. However, the full financial terms and other contractual details have not been publicly disclosed in the available report. The five-year duration is the central detail confirmed by recent reports, and further specifics should not be assumed without additional information. Before joining AEW, Creed and Kingston were two-thirds of The New Day alongside Big E . The group became one of WWE’s defining factions of the modern era, combining comedy, audience connection and championship success. Kingston also enjoyed a major singles achievement when he won the WWE Championship in 2019. Woods, meanwhile, captured the King of the Ring tournament in 2021, adding an individual accolade to his accomplishments as a tag-team wrestler. Their WWE chapter ended in 2026 following reported discussions about restructuring their contracts. Rather than continue under revised terms, the pair ultimately departed the company and explored a new opportunity. Their decision attracted considerable attention because of their long association with WWE and the popularity they had built as The New Day. Their AEW signing now gives them a fresh platform to pursue further success as a team. The duo made their AEW debut at All In: London on August 30, 2026, appearing as The New Level alongside Swerve Strickland. Their first outing produced an immediate championship moment. The trio won the Trios Championship Roulette Royale to capture the AEW World Trios Championship on their debut night. The victory gave Creed and Kingston an emphatic introduction to AEW and established their alliance with Strickland as an important part of their initial presentation. The result also demonstrated that AEW was prepared to place the newcomers in a prominent position

title: Comeback Watch: Absent AEW star to be repackaged upon return: Three names that could be rebranded before the end of the year
raw_title: Absent AEW star to be repackaged upon return: Three names that could be rebranded before the end of the year
body: While this year has given us the return of previously absent stars such as Britt Baker and Private Party, there are still a number of names on the roster who have been AWOL from AEW programming for some time. Whether they’ve been gone due to injury or creative reasons, we could soon be seeing some of these stars return, and when they do come back we could be seeing them with an all new character. Here are three AEW stars that could be repackaged upon their return: Buddy Matthews has been in the news this week after he was pulled from Australian promotion World Series Wrestling’s MegaMania Tour between October 29 – November 2. The reason given was “scheduling conflicts” which of course has led to speculation that he could be nearing a return to AEW very soon. AEW will be hosting Dynamite & Collision: Fright Night on October 28 in St. Louis, so we may very well see Matthews make his first appearance since suffering a serious ankle injury back in March 2025. With Matthews’ former stablemates Brody King and Julia Hart forming new alliances in Matthews’ absence, we could see AEW give Matthews an entirely fresh start, complete with a different presentation. As mentioned in the intro, Private Party did make a rather unexpected return to AEW TV after over a year away back in February. Sadly however, Isiah Kassidy and Marq Quen’s return was short-lived, as injuries took them both out just one month later. We haven’t seen or really heard much from Zay and Quen since, so it’s hard to predict when they could re-emerge on AEW programming. AEW Dynamite: Fright Night does have some significance to the pair however, with that same event being when they finally captured the AEW World Tag Team Titles back in February 2024. While it may not come during tonight’s Dynamite, Private Party returning with a new edge – perhaps as a part of a returning Hurt Syndicate – would be a great way for AEW to re-introduce them. Like Private Party, Kamille is another AEW star that had a blink and you’ll miss it return to the company in 2026. “The Brickhouse” returned back in April to target the then AEW TBS Champion Willow Nightingale, but vanished again as soon as she lost her title opportunity. Kamille’s entire AEW run has been a head-scratcher, with the former NWA World Women’s Champion being absent for far longer than she’s been on TV since becoming All Elite back in 2024. While AEW now has several physically imposing female stars, such as Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, Kamille could still carve out a spot for herself in the company if she was to return. Rather than playing the same role however, AEW could retool her character to separate her from the aforementioned Divine Dominion.

title: WWE's Top 5 Spookiest Superstars
raw_title: Wrestling with Halloween: WWE’s spookiest superstars
body: This Halloween season, check out the top five spookiest superstars to ever set foot in a WWE ring. Among WWE's roster of bionic rednecks and tribal chiefs lies The Boogeyman: a worm-eating demon who terrorized SmackDown from 2005 to 2007. Perhaps the most frightening-looking wrestler on this list, The Boogeyman grossed out audiences by devouring fistfuls of worms . Sometimes even his opponent would be forced to eat the worms after being defeated by the red-faced Boogeyman. His signature entrance featured The Boogeyman breaking a clock over his head as fog fills the arena. While not WWE's most technically gifted wrestler, The Boogeyman was a character firmly rooted in horror and horror comedy. The Boogeyman is simply absurd, but in a genuine way that only wrestling audiences could understand and love. The Boogeyman has made sporadic appearances in WWE for years, proving just how memorable and effective his horror imagery was. Fun fact: The Boogeyman is one of actor Timothée Chalamet's favorite wrestlers. Gangrel and his associates Edge and Christian - known collectively as The Brood - were WWE's resident vampires during the company's vaulted Attitude Era of the late 1990s. The Brood looked like they stepped out of the nightclub in Blade and walked to the ring in what many consider to be one of the greatest theme songs of the era. The song, titled after their name, would work great in any haunted house. Gangrel, with his vampire teeth, would drink blood from a goblet before and after matches. Were the members of The Brood really vampires? Only time will tell; Edge and Christian, who went on to have hall of fame careers, still look pretty good for their age. The masked, secret brother of The Undertaker made a frightening entrance when he confronted The Deadman at Badd Blood: In Your House in 1997. Kane's famous first appearance featured The Big Red Machine ripping open the door to the Hell in a Cell cage in order to attack The Undertaker. Kane cost his brother the WWE Championship in a match against Shawn Michaels that was all but over. Kane's freaky red appearance, coupled with his tragic backstory of having survived a house fire that permanently damaged his face made him one of WWE's most recognizable faces of horror. What really made Kane scary, however, was how he was able to match The Undertaker in power and size. Suddenly The Undertaker didn't seem as powerful. Kane enjoyed a long and storied career in WWE that included everything from him removing his mask to becoming a corporate, suit-wearing stooge, but it was during his time in the 90's with the red and black mask that Kane was truly terrifying. One of the most interesting and lore-rich characters WWE has ever presented, The Fiend Bray Wyatt broke wrestling conventions by not shying away from its horror influences and by not being afraid to get weird. summary: The Boogeyman, a worm-eating red-faced demon, terrorized SmackDown from 2005 to 2007 by forcing opponents to eat worms after matches and breaking a clock over his head during his fog-filled entrances. title: AEW Crowns New TBS Champion on Dynamite
raw_title: AEW Crowns New TBS Champion on Dynamite
body: 0 AEW has crowned a new TBS champion after a tough match on the October 28 episode of Dynamite . Queen Aminata earned the title after defeating Persephone for the first time in her career. Aminata earned her title shot on last week’s Dynamite when she defeated the returning Maya World in a number one contender’s match. Persephone defended her title with help from Britt Baker, who repeatedly tried to interfere. However, Aminata fought through the interference and picked up the biggest win of her AEW career. Aminata wasted no time once the match began. She rolled up Persephone after the opening lock-up, but Persephone managed to kick out. After that, Persephone trapped Aminata in a submission hold. However, she reached the bottom rope to break free and fought back with two clotheslines. Aminata kept the pressure on by slamming Persephone into the mat and hitting a double stomp off the ropes. However, when she went for the pin, Baker stepped in from the outside and broke up the count. Britt Baker’s interference continued to cause problems for Aminata. Persephone then ripped off the kinesiology tape on the back of her opponent’s neck and went for a springboard moonsault. However, Aminata countered the move by raising her knees. Persephone then tried to escape by rolling under the bottom rope. But Aminata wasn’t going to let her get away. She sat the champion on a chair and hit a meteora. With the referee checking on Persephone, Baker took advantage of the situation. She hit Aminata with the TBS Championship belt before throwing her back into the ring. Persephone quickly climbed to the top rope and landed a moonsault on Aminata. She went for the pin, looking close to retaining her title, but Aminata kicked out. The failed pin left Baker frustrated at ringside. Aminata eventually found the opening she needed. She hit a headbutt followed by a running knee strike that left Persephone unable to recover. Aminata then covered the champion and secured the three-count. After the match, Willow Nightingale, Thunder Rosa, Hyan, Maya World, Mina Shirakawa, Harley Cameron, and Kris Statlander came out to congratulate Aminata on her victory. title: Comeback Watch: Absent AEW Stars Return During Collision Taping in St. Louis — Spoiler
raw_title: Spoiler: Absent AEW Stars Return During Collision Taping in St. Louis
summary_src: The Hurt Syndicate is finally back after disappearing from AEW television for two months. And after all the rumors surrounding the group’s absence, Bobby Lashley, Shelton Benjamin and MVP didn’t exactly return quietly.
body: During AEW’s October 28 tapings for the October 31 Fright Night Collision, held in St. Louis, The Hurt Syndicate made their return to action. Lashley and Benjamin competed in a 2-on-3 handicap match against Griff Garrison and Soloroto, marking the faction’s first appearance since AEW All In on August 30. That’s a pretty notable return considering how much talk there’s been about the group lately. The Hurt Syndicate had been completely absent from AEW programming for roughly two months, which naturally led to questions about what the hell was going on. Things got even messier when reports started making the rounds claiming members of the group had pushed back against putting certain wrestlers over. Sean Ross Sapp recently claimed there had been situations where members of The Hurt Syndicate didn’t want to lose , although he didn’t identify who allegedly pushed back or which opponents were involved. MVP absolutely wasn’t having that version of events. He jumped on Twitter and called the claims about The Hurt Syndicate “blatant lies,” while also suggesting he might know where the rumors were coming from. “So I open up Twitter to see lies being reported about The Hurt Syndicate. BLATANT LIES!!! Who is the source of these lies?” MVP then went even further by directly addressing the idea that the group didn’t want to put other wrestlers over. He claimed the exact opposite was true, saying The Hurt Syndicate specifically wanted to work with younger talent and even wanted to drop the AEW World Tag Team Championships back to Private Party. “To the contrary, we wanted to work with younger talent! We wanted to drop the tag titles BACK to Private Party!!! STOP BELIEVING THE BS!” He also responded to another account that brought up several rumors surrounding the faction, including claims that MVP was influencing Lashley and Benjamin to reject creative ideas and that he had heat with important people behind the scenes. Once again, MVP completely denied it. “Rumor? Nah man. You are absolutely Wrong!!!! None of this is true. But now I know where this whisper campaign is coming from! 😉” Whatever was happening behind the scenes, AEW has now put The Hurt Syndicate back in front of the crowd. After two months away and plenty of chatter about their future, Lashley, Benjamin and MVP are officially back in the mix. What do you want to see AEW do with The Hurt Syndicate now that the group is finally back on television? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Grayson Waller Explains Switch to Wrestling Tights
raw_title: Grayson Waller: Roman Reigns Told Me Wearing Tights Made Me Look Like A Champion
summary_src: When Grayson Waller returned to NXT earlier this year, he ditched the boxing shorts for more traditional wrestling tights. The change coincided with a more serious approach to his character, and it led to his first NXT Title victory.
body: When Grayson Waller returned to NXT earlier this year, he ditched the boxing shorts for more traditional wrestling tights. The change coincided with a more serious approach to his character, and it led to his first NXT Title victory. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Waller explained why he underwent the change. “I look back and I kind of understand why people would have perceived me as a joke. For me, the boxing shorts were always I was a huge boxing fan. A lot of people think it was basketball shorts, but I thought it was a different look. It made me look unique, but I think it also didn’t make me look like a serious contender for the championship. So that was something where I was like, I need to change things up. I can’t just keep giving them the same thing. So first thing was I put the tights on, and actually the Rumble was the first time I kind of wore them in a match, and Roman came up and pulled me aside and said, ‘Hey, that’s the look. You look like a champion now.’ Hey, if Roman says that, all right, lad, whatever you need, I’m gonna keep the pants. But even coming back to NXT, I was like, I can’t walk out with the leopard shirts and all that. That vibe didn’t work. That’s an old me. So now, I am more serious. This is me. I feel comfortable now.
