title: On the Record: Grayson Waller Says He Hates WWE NXT Fans and Calls Them a Bunch of Fat Flops
raw_title: Grayson Waller Says He Hates WWE NXT Fans and Calls Them a Bunch of Fat Flops
summary_src: Grayson Waller has never exactly tried to make friends with wrestling fans, but the NXT crowd apparently holds a special place in his heart — for all the wrong reasons. In fact, Waller says insulting those fans is one of his favorite parts of showing up every week.
body: Speaking to Chris Van Vliet , Waller was asked about how much fun he seems to have whenever he gets into it with people in the crowd. Waller immediately singled out NXT fans, calling them “fat flops” before remembering one particular fan who gave him the perfect setup for an insult. “Especially the — I hate the NXT audience. I love interacting with them. A bunch of fat flops. You can smell them. Like, it’s heavy. “There was that one brother, one of my favorite lines, where I said, ‘You look like you can get Chick-fil-A on a Sunday.’ And he could. He could. He might. “But the problem is he might just get it Saturday and leave it out. Like, he wouldn’t refrigerate it. He’d just have it sitting there.” That wasn’t even Waller’s favorite time he ruined somebody’s night. He recalled doing commentary with Austin Theory when a kid sitting behind them wouldn’t stop yelling, so Waller decided to hit him with something personal during the commercial break. “That was a pretty good one. The one where the kid was the most upset was me and Theory did commentary one night, and there was a kid behind us yelling. “And when we were on break, I turned around and I said, ‘You’ve got the same haircut as your mom.’ And he did. It was like a little bob, and the realization on his face that it was right — like, I’ve never seen anything like it. He just sat down, and he was so upset. “And that made me really happy. Like, don’t — if you yell at me, I can yell back. That’s part of what this wrestling is like on the NXT shows. When there’s no cameras around, I can tell you exactly what you look like. And that’s a beautiful thing.” Van Vliet then brought up another viral Waller moment involving a young girl sitting ringside. Waller offered to let her touch the NXT Championship before yanking it away, but he somehow remembers the whole thing as a pretty “wholesome interaction.” Waller explained that he actually enjoys giving fans those kinds of memories because it’s his version of the experience a babyface might provide by taking pictures or giving hugs. He just prefers making kids believe ridiculous stories and then being a complete jerk to them. “I thought that was quite a wholesome interaction. You know, she was asking why I was there, which was confusing. Maybe her mom isn’t smart, didn’t teach her, like, ‘Hey, we’re at wrestling to watch wrestlers.’ “But I love that video, and I’m so glad someone got it because in the moment it was so fun telling her that Mason Rook ate my dad, and her genuinely going, ‘Really?’ Like, it was so much fun. “Sometimes those interactions we have with fans — because, you know, as a good guy, what do you do? You go hug them, you take a photo, you do the Cody Rhodes, everyone in the arena gets a photo. That’s great. “But for guys like me who don’t like the fans, I think we can still give them an experience that they can go home and think about, or something they can go home and, like, in ten years go, ‘I remember when this wrestler said this to

body: October 29, 2026 By Mark Justice WWE , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe , WWE Women WWE Royal Rumble 2027 Predictions are here for Saturday, February 6, 2027, at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona. We know it’s early, but hey, a little foresight could be fun. Roman Reigns and Liv Morgan won the Rumble matches last year, so the question on everyone’s mind as WWE approaches Mania season is: Who will win the prestigious Royal Rumble this year? The Royal Rumble Matches will determine who will main event WrestleMania against the world champions. With that being said, it is now time for the highly anticipated WWE Royal Rumble 2027 Predictions. Naomi is the odds-on favorite to win the Royal Rumble, as she will be on a journey to win back the title she never lost after relinquishing it due to maternity leave. Liv Morgan currently holds the title Naomi relinquished, so it would make sense for Naomi to return as a massive babyface, be a breath of fresh air on Raw, and take down Morgan’s reign of terror with Judgment Day for good. Rhea Ripley is another top option to win the Royal Rumble , as she will also be fighting her way back to regaining the title she never lost after relinquishing it due to injury. Chelsea Green currently holds the title Ripley relinquished. Once Stratton turns heel and cashes in on Green to betray their friendship, it would make sense for Ripley to return as a massive babyface to take down Stratton at Mania. However, Ripley already won the Royal Rumble in 2024, so it would be more fruitful for Naomi to win her first Rumble this year, solidifying her return to the company. Her impressive heel run before her departure left a lot on the table for fans to anticipate. Naomi’s new gimmick is desperately needed in the main event scene on Raw that has suffered and been plagued with mediocre title reigns. Oba Femi is the current betting favorite to win the Rumble, as Oba Femi is heavily rumored to battle Roman Reigns for the World Title in the main event of WrestleMania. Granted, Femi already won the King of the Ring Tournament, so it would feel redundant for him to win the Rumble to get a world title shot that he is already owed. However, it seems his title shot expired at SummerSlam. CM Punk, on the other hand, is another top option to win the Rumble , as he is also heavily rumored to battle Cody Rhodes for the WWE Title in the main event of WrestleMania. As an established name, it’s baffling that someone of his caliber has not added a Rumble win to his resume. Rumble 2014 was when he left WWE, and it would be poetic for him to win the Rumble in return. Femi has a long career ahead of him to win a Rumble. Giving him too much too soon could be detrimental to his babyface appeal. It would be wiser for Femi to dominate the Chamber to earn his title shot against Reigns, while Punk wins the Rumble to have one last hurrah before his career ends in the next five years. If Punk is not in the conversation to win the Rumble yet, it should start now

title: WWE Crown Jewel is Moving...to Another Location in Saudi Arabia
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel is Moving...to Another Location in Saudi Arabia
body: October 28, 2026 By Marilee Gallagher, Manager News , Pro Wrestling , Raw , SmackDown , WWE , WWE Universe , WWE Women After significant concerns from employees and fans as a result of the unrest and hostilities in the Middle East, WWE and Riyadh officially announced on Wednesday that WWE Crown Jewel was being relocated…to a new venue still very much in Saudi Arabia. In an Instagram post from Riyadh Season , it was announced that WWE Crown Jewel had been relocated from the custom-built and outdoor Riyadh Season Stadium to a to-be-announced venue. It was noted that all ticket holders would receive a full refund, with new tickets expected to go on sale within 48 hours. There is so much to unpack here. Riyadh’s page did not reveal the reason for the relocation, and WWE has yet to put out its own statement about it. One could speculate the venue change could be related to the recent airport closure brought about by the Houthi attacks earlier this month. It was reported a few days ago that flights in and out of King Khalid International Airport were being limited as the country worked to get the airport back to full operations. However, this wasn’t scheduled to happen until after Crown Jewel, impacting anyone trying to travel in and out of Riyadh for the PLE. The fact that the new venue has not been announced is also prompting concerns of safety. On Riyadh Season’s post, a user commented asking if there was any danger in telling people where the new venue would be. It seems like the location will be revealed or at least leaked when tickets go on sale, but that comment certainly encapsulates a real feeling of fear and uncertainty people have had about this event still being scheduled. Now, it is also possible, as one commenter noted, that the venue is being upgraded to a larger one. Plausible perhaps. Though it might appear like an odd choice to relocate the event given preparation and set building has already been underway . While not confirmed by WWE or Riyadh, according to Dave Meltzer , the new venue is the Kingdom Arena in Riyadh, which can hold approximately 30,000 people. Unlike the Riyadh Season Stadium, it is a permanent structure, one that could likely provide additional layers of safety should they be needed. It feels like news drops by the day as it relates to WWE Crown Jewel, be that from WWE itself or outside organizations. The company is said to be listening to guidance from the U.S. State Department on how to proceed, while it’s also been acknowledged the large sum of money and relationship currency TKO stands to lose should they cancel Crown Jewel or move it out of Saudi Arabia. The fact that Crown Jewel is moving to an undisclosed venue isn’t helping WWE’s case either, as most fans were hoping for a move out of the country or, at the very least, a reschedule to another date. Though the reality is, the hostilities in the Middle East sadly show no signs of letting up anytime soon. So as of now, WWE Crown Jewel is still being advertised
summary: Per Last Word On Sports: october 28, 2026 By Marilee Gallagher, Manager News , Pro Wrestling , Raw , SmackDown , WWE . Officially, WWE Crown Jewel had been relocated from the custom-built and outdoor Riyadh Season Stadium to a to-be-revealed venue.

body: October 28, 2026 By Nicholas Paul WWE , Featured , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe As we inch closer to the end of 2026 with a new year on the horizon, many fans are already speculating about which wrestler might be next to call it a career. One such legend might be closer to the end, as we know: the masked legend, Rey Mysterio. Over the last two years alone, four wrestlers have exited WWE, starting on July 12, 2025, when Goldberg lost to Gunther in his final match at Saturday Night’s Main Event . Next was the conclusion of John Cena’s illustrious career on December 12, 2025, who, fittingly, also lost to Gunther at Saturday Night’s Main Event . To kick off this year, “The Phenomenal” AJ Styles brought his career to a close. He wrapped up his decorated decade with the company at the Royal Rumble in February, losing to none other than Gunther in a retirement stipulation match . Most recently, we witnessed the end of Brock Lesnar’s career following his defeat to Oba Femi in the Night 1 main event of SummerSlam . Despite the loss, he shared a memorable passing-of-the-torch moment with Femi after the match. Fast-forwarding to today, rumors are circulating that Rey Mysterio could be the next star to hang up his boots. According to a number of sources, a retirement tour next year is “quite possible.” Despite the chatter, WWE has yet to confirm any plans, and Mysterio has made no official retirement announcement. Much like Cena, Mysterio has previously stated that he wants to announce his final match well in advance so fans can see him compete one last time. Now, the question many fans may be asking is: why would 2027 be the right time for “The Ultimate Underdog” to call it a career? While a few factors come into play, the most obvious one is his age. Mysterio is set to turn 52 in December. While he has certainly looked incredible throughout his second WWE run – most recently in last week’s Intercontinental Championship Triple Threat match on Raw against Chad Gable and Dragon Lee – he has been relying on stem cell treatments to keep competing. After wrestling for over 30 years, what better time to call it quits than while still being able to perform at a high level? If 2027 does end up being the final time we see Mysterio in the ring, it is essential that WWE give him the proper farewell tour he rightfully deserves. With that in mind, here are four dream opponents he needs to face before calling it a career. Kicking off the list is a very familiar rival in CM Punk. Their legendary feud began in late 2009 before peaking in 2010, and while Punk’s character is vastly different today, revisiting this matchup would serve as a great callback to one of Mysterio’s most memorable rivalries. Although Mysterio is currently on Raw and Punk is on SmackDown , there’s no reason why either man wouldn’t cross brand lines for a match. title: 5 Big Times Wrestling and Pop Culture Came Together — Beyond the Gear
raw_title: Beyond the Gear: 5 Big Times Wrestling and Pop Culture Came Together
body: October 28, 2026 By Daniel Sinasac WWE , Featured , History , Pro Wrestling , WWE Universe Wrestling and pop culture have always had this magnetic connection, and that will pay off soon because in a few short days, children from around the world will fill the streets, going from house to house, filling up their bags with as much candy as possible. Halloween is that magical time of year when anyone can be anything. Adults and children alike let their minds run wild as they prepare costumes for parties or cruising the streets. The sky is the limit for what costumes can be created, and it’s always a joy to see what each person has designed. In the world of WWE, the concept of dressing up as another entity is commonplace , considering wrestling and pop culture have been closely linked for decades. Many wrestlers have taken cosplaying to a whole new level, showing off various wardrobes as they head to the ring. The fans have grown fond of these talents and their ability to morph their ring gear to mirror other wrestlers or pop culture icons. As Halloween approaches, it seems appropriate to show these talents some love for their creativity. Rey Mysterio’s Luchador background has been an inspiration for his ring gear since he debuted in WWE. The master of the 619 has worn colourful attire his whole career, and it’s a big reason his connection with the audience has remained strong. Wres tling is an appearance-based industry, and no man’s look is more impressive than Rey Mysterio’s. When shows like WrestleMania and SummerSlam have taken place, Rey Mysterio has been adept at changing his ring attire to reflect pop culture icons. The wrestling world has seen Mysterio dress as the Joker (WrestleMania 25) , Daredevil (WrestleMania 19), the Flash (WrestleMania 20), and the Silver Surfer (SummerSlam 2007). These appearances have been iconic, showing a talent for dressing up as other figures from mainstream media. The hype for Rey Mysterio’s appearances at WWE’s biggest shows is warranted given his history. Dan has been a fan of wrestling since his grandmother sat him down to watch JYD and Sgt. Slaughter go to battle. That began a decades-long obsession with professional wrestling. An obsession that has developed into a love/hate relationship with the greatest entertainment medium in the world. title: Grayson Waller Explains Switch To Wrestling Tights
raw_title: Grayson Waller Talks Switching To Tights - Fightful | WWE News, AEW News, Pro Wrestling Backstage News
body: When Grayson Waller returned to NXT earlier this year, he ditched the boxing shorts for more traditional wrestling tights. The change coincided with a more serious approach to his character, and it led to his first NXT Title victory. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Waller explained why he underwent the change. “I look back and I kind of understand why people would have perceived me as a joke. For me, the boxing shorts were always I was a huge boxing fan. A lot of people think it was basketball shorts, but I thought it was a different look. It made me look unique, but I think it also didn’t make me look like a serious contender for the championship. So that was something where I was like, I need to change things up. I can’t just keep giving them the same thing. So first thing was I put the tights on, and actually the Rumble was the first time I kind of wore them in a match, and Roman came up and pulled me aside and said, ‘Hey, that’s the look. You look like a champion now.’ Hey, if Roman says that, all right, lad, whatever you need, I’m gonna keep the pants. But even coming back to NXT, I was like, I can’t walk out with the leopard shirts and all that. That vibe didn’t work. That’s an old me. So now, I am more serious. This is me. I feel comfortable now. So I think I had to change things because if you keep throwing the same thing at the wall and it’s not working, then what are you doing?” Waller is set to defend the NXT Title against Tony D’Angelo at NXT Halloween Havoc on Saturday. Fans can check out the lineup for the show by clicking here .

title: Grayson Waller Explains Risky NXT Return
raw_title: Grayson Waller says NXT move was risky but he has a lot to prove to WWE officials
summary_src: Grayson Waller does not perceive his transition from the WWE main roster to NXT as a demotion. He explained his thought process when Shawn Michaels approached him to return to NXT. On the Insight Podcast, Waller recalled Michaels requesting to meet with him and pitched his NXT comeback.
body: Grayson Waller does not perceive his transition from the WWE main roster to NXT as a demotion. He explained his thought process when Shawn Michaels approached him to return to NXT. On the Insight Podcast , Waller recalled Michaels requesting to meet with him and pitched his NXT comeback. Waller emphasized that his presence on TV almost every week makes a difference in impacting his WWE career, giving him regular opportunities to showcase his abilities against some of the brand’s top talent. “I don’t see it as that because I wasn’t told to do anything. I was asked. I was given an option by Shawn, and I chose to go and do that. So I didn’t look at it as a demotion because I’m on TV every week. I’m competing every week against some of the best kids in the world right now.” Waller also addressed how his WWE career might have unfolded had he not taken the opportunity to return to NXT. He described the move as risky but believed he needed a platform to showcase his abilities and remind WWE officials what he was capable of. “The one thing I’ll say, and I mean it. I’m always upfront and honest about situations. I could see the writing on the wall. They’re bringing up these kids from NXT who are super talented, and they’re giving them all the chances. I’m in the background, and it’s disappearing. You go lower and lower. You get more forgotten about. I was gone for sure. So when I say I took a risk to go to NXT, it’s a risk because you never know if it’s going to work out. But I trust in my ability, and I just needed a platform.” “So I think it was something that I needed to do because I need to show them who I am; I need to show them I love this. I’m so good. You are the guys who haven’t seen it. It’s not me; you’re fumbling the ball. I have everything ready to go, but you just don’t know. So I took it upon myself to kind of force it on them. I’m like, ‘Hey, you want to know what I can do? I’m going to show you.’” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. summary_src: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is still happening in Saudi Arabia, but the last-minute venue change has raised plenty of questions. Now, new details are coming out about who made the call to move the show and why WWE is heading indoors just days before the November 7 event.
body: After Riyadh Season announced that Crown Jewel was moving venues , Forbes revealed that Kingdom Arena in Riyadh would be the new location . The show was originally scheduled for the outdoor Riyadh Season Stadium inside the King Abdullah Financial District, but security concerns in the region appear to have played a role in the change. During the October 29 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer explained that the move was being presented as a safety decision, with Saudi organizers choosing to bring the event indoors rather than use the outdoor stadium. “The people at Riyadh posted that they were moving the show. They were building a stadium. They were. What’s. What’s they calling Riyadh Season Stadium. And it was outdoors and the WWE show was going to be there and they announced a move and that they announced that it was moving to. They laid. I don’t even know if it’s been officially announced, but they’re moving to Kingdom arena, which is the same building that the Canelo Alvarez fight on Saturday is going to be held. So some, you know, some people were like when it was first announced, thought like something big was up. But essentially the claim is, is that it is safer to run the show indoors than outdoors. Which makes sense. All the sense in the world. And so they’re going to move the show indoors.” Bryan Alvarez wasn’t completely sold on that explanation. He questioned how moving inside would eliminate the potential dangers surrounding the event. Meltzer responded that controlling access to an indoor arena could make security easier to manage, but he also raised another possible explanation involving ticket sales. “Yeah. Hey, look, maybe it’s just they didn’t sell enough tickets and they’re moving indoors like that WrestleMania.” Alvarez agreed that ticket sales could be a more likely explanation, although neither provided evidence that poor sales were responsible for the move. Whatever the actual reason, WWE has been addressing security concerns internally. Meltzer revealed that the company held a conference call with employees on October 28, where safety was presented as a top priority. “Yeah. But they had a conference call today, you know, with WWE employees to say that, like, security is their utmost concern for. Which it should be.” Meltzer also explained that the upcoming Canelo Alvarez boxing event in Saudi Arabia could serve as an important test ahead of Crown Jewel. He believes Saudi officials will point to that event as proof that major international shows can still take place safely in the region. “Yeah, well, like I said, they’re going. Unless something terrible happens in the Canelo fight on Saturday, because Saudi is going to use that and go like, look, no problems. And so far, you know, there’s been no problems. title: Why is WWE Wasting Gunther After Retiring John Cena and AJ Styles?
raw_title: Why is WWE Wasting Gunther After Retiring John Cena and AJ Styles?
body: To start the year, The Ring General taunted until AJ Styles stepped up and put his career on the line at Royal Rumble 2026, allowing Gunther to retire another legend. That same night, Gunther was also the runner-up in the men's Rumble match, solidifying his direction toward top gold once again in the new year. It is now October, and The Career Killer is the least relevant he has been in his main-roster run, feuding with Finn Bálor and Danhausen on SmackDown. What happened to Gunther? After Royal Rumble, Gunther ran into an angry Dragon Lee, looking to avenge his retired friend AJ Styles. This feud had some heat, but WWE never planned for Dragon to look like a serious threat to The Career Killer. Gunther would defeat and unmask Dragon, who would simply accept that loss. This left Gunther without any direction into WrestleMania 42 until he abruptly revealed he was helping Paul Heyman to fight Seth Rollins. Gunther did defeat Rollins at 'Mania, but the match was focused more on the return of Bron Breakker, transitioning The Visionary to another feud. The Career Killer was already so lost that WWE decided to move him to SmackDown for a fresh start. The Career Killer lost to The American Nightmare but with controversy since Gunther's leg was under the bottom rope. Less than three weeks later on SmackDown, the two fought again, but special guest referee Sami Zayn cost Gunther the match then caused a disqualification in the restarted contest. At Night of Champions, Zayn pinned Rhodes to take the WWE Championship, going on to lose the title to CM Punk eight days later on Raw. Time and again, The Career Killer lost without gaining any heat. His wins over John Cena and AJ Styles felt like a distant memory. Twice after Royal Rumble, WWE teased the possibility of Gunther retiring someone else. During his brief alliance with Paul Heyman, all signs pointed to Gunther eventually challenging Brock Lesnar. Instead, The Beast Incarnate chose Oba Femi as his final opponent. Instead into SummerSlam, WWE set up Gunther vs. Nick Aldis. The general manager stepped out of his authority role to fight in a WWE ring for the first time. All signs pointed to Gunther retiring Aldis after his first WWE match. Instead, despite The Career Killer winning, the talking point of the night was that Aldis looked good enough to wrestle multiple times in the future. As a consolation, Aldis threw Gunther in a No. 1 contender match on Night 2 of SummerSlam. Kevin Owens would go on to win that contest and leave The Career Killer with no real direction since. title: Grayson Waller Expected WWE Release After New Day Exit
raw_title: Grayson Waller Felt He Was Going To Be Released After New Day Left WWE
summary_src: At the beginning of May, New Day (Kofi Kingston & Xavier Woods) announced that they would be departing WWE. The duo had been aligned with Grayson Waller on television, but weren't prominently featured on a week-to-week basis.
body: At the beginning of May, New Day (Kofi Kingston & Xavier Woods) announced that they would be departing WWE. The duo had been aligned with Grayson Waller on television, but weren’t prominently featured on a week-to-week basis. Waller lost to Oba Femi on the April 21 episode of WWE Raw, and disappeared from TV until showing up at NXT at the end of July. Waller called out the NXT roster and aired his grievances, leading to his current run as NXT Champion. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight, Waller was asked if he felt he was close to being released by WWE prior to his NXT return. “100%. I could feel it, especially when the New Day left. I could feel it because when the New Day left, Oba destroyed me. He’s a very big man, very strong, and just beaten Lesnar. So I think he was very confident going into that match. Maybe I wasn’t prepared enough for Oba Femi, but then when I didn’t do anything for like another month, was not a great position to be in. I’m smart enough to know; I’m not going to pretend. I’m real enough to know. I know I have a lot of value to the company, but in that position, there’s other people who could also add that value. So I had to do something because I’m not going to sit back and let my dream disappear. If I didn’t do something about it, that would upset me if I didn’t do something,” he said. He is set to defend the title at NXT Halloween Havoc against Tony D’Angelo.
summary: Grayson Waller told Chris Van Vliet on Insight that he felt he was 100% close to being released from WWE once New Day left the company. The stablemates had been aligned on TV but were not featured prominently week to week. Waller was defeated by Oba Femi on the April 21 episode of Raw, remained off television for months, and then returned to NXT at the end of July where he called out the roster and began his current reign as NXT Champion.

llm_long: Grayson Waller has revealed he felt he was on the verge of being released by WWE after New Day's departure from the company. New Day, consisting of Kofi Kingston and Xavier Woods, announced their exit at the beginning of May.

The duo had been aligned with Waller on television although they were not featured prominently on a weekly basis. He then disappeared from television until appearing on NXT at the end of July. During that appearance Waller called out the NXT roster and expressed his grievances.

That moment launched his current run as NXT Champion. In an interview with Chris Van Vliet on Insight, Waller confirmed he believed he was close to being released prior to his NXT return. Waller noted that Oba Femi had just beaten Brock Lesnar and entered their match with confidence.

Waller admitted he may not have been prepared enough for the bout against the much larger opponent. Following the defeat he remained off television for about a month, a situation he recognized as precarious.

title: Real Reason for Stephanie Vaquer’s WWE RAW Absence Revealed
raw_title: Real Reason for Stephanie Vaquer’s WWE RAW Absence Revealed
summary_src: Stephanie Vaquer’s sudden absence from WWE RAW left fans wondering what was going on, especially after WWE pulled her from a major match against Becky Lynch. Now, Dave Meltzer has provided more details about why Vaquer missed the show and how her illness forced WWE to change its plans.
body: As previously noted, it was confirmed that Vaquer was not backstage for WWE RAW on October 26, 2026 and had not been medically cleared to compete. False Finish later indicated that Vaquer’s absence was illness-related and that she would be sidelined indefinitely, with no timetable established for her return. During the October 29 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio, Meltzer confirmed that Vaquer is dealing with an illness rather than an injury. He also said he had been told that her condition wasn’t considered terribly serious. “She’s ill. You know, it’s not anything. I was told nothing terribly serious or anything, but. But she’s, she’s ill and she’s out.” Bryan Alvarez then brought up the fact that Vaquer had been listed as out indefinitely. Meltzer explained that the wording didn’t necessarily mean she was dealing with a serious medical problem. Instead, WWE simply doesn’t know exactly when she’ll be ready to return. “Yeah, I mean, it’s indefinitely in the sense that, you know, it’s not like it’s a week. You know, it’s not. It’s. It’s something more serious, so. Or, no, I shouldn’t even say that. It’s something that’s indeterminate yet as far as when she’ll be back.” Meltzer also cleared up any speculation that Vaquer’s absence was part of a storyline. WWE originally intended to move forward with her match against Becky Lynch on RAW, but Vaquer became sick and couldn’t make the show. That forced the company to come up with a replacement match involving Lynch and WWE Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan. “But that’s why they didn’t do that match. She. It wasn’t about an injury and it wasn’t a worked storyline. They were going to do the match On Monday night and she got sick and could not, could not come.” The last-minute change also explains why Lynch’s championship match against Morgan ended in a disqualification. According to Meltzer, WWE didn’t want Lynch taking a loss in a match that wasn’t originally supposed to happen, so the disqualification allowed the company to avoid that outcome. “And, and that’s why they did the Becky lynch live, Morgan. And that’s why they did the dq, because they didn’t want to be Becky lynch, but it wasn’t a match that they had planned. And so the DQ that way, you know, to get out of it, essentially.” For now, Vaquer remains out of action with no confirmed return date, but Meltzer’s update makes it clear that WWE wasn’t planning some surprise storyline with her absence. The company had to change its plans because she was genuinely sick, and there’s still no indication of when she’ll be medically cleared. That also leaves her position in the Women’s World Championship picture up in the air. Steve Carrier Steve Carrier is the founder of Ringside News and has been reporting on pro wrestling since 1997. His stories have been featured on TMZ, Forbes, Bleacher Report, and more.
summary: The latest: as previously pointed out, Officially, Vaquer was not backstage for WWE RAW on October 26, 2026 and had not been medically cleared to compete. False Finish later indicated that Vaquer’s absence was illness-related and that she would be sidelined indefinitely, with no timetable established for her return.

Imagine how cool Penta would look with the WWE or World Heavyweight Championship around his waist. As proof of how far Penta had risen, he was even booked to win. Then an unfortunate event led to the masked wrestler doing so much more in TNA. At that year's TNA Redemption pay-per-view, Penta was supposed to face his brother in singles action, while the main event would see Aries putting his title on the line against Albero El Patron ( better known as Alberto Del Rio in WWE ). title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Moves to Kingdom Arena in Riyadh
raw_title: WWE Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia gets new location, but there’s a massive twist
body: Whether or not WWE would move Crown Jewel 2026, which is set to be held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has been a hot topic given tensions with Iran, and the location has been moved. However, it is not in the way some would expect. The show is still slated to be held in Riyadh but at Kingdom Arena instead of Riyadh Season Stadium, according to the Wrestling Observer's Dave Meltzer. Despite warnings and travel alerts from the U.S. government, WWE appears set to hold Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia. The PLE will take place on Saturday, Nov. 7. Crown Jewel will be held on Nov. 7. For those on the East Coast, the PLE will begin at 12 pm EST. It will air on ESPN's streaming service in the United States and Netflix elsewhere. It's not overly surprising that Crown Jewel is being held in Saudi Arabia. Traditionally, the PLE has been held there with the exception of last year's event, which was held in Perth, Australia. WWE has a multi-year partnership with Saudi Arabia. The company usually holds two PLEs in Saudi Arabia every year. In 2027, WrestleMania will be held in Riyadh. Four matches have been announced for the event. WWE will hold its annual champion vs. champion matches between Monday Night RAW and Friday Night SmackDown's world champions. That means that World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns will face either Sami Zayn or Trick Williams. Zayn and Williams will face for the Undisputed WWE Championship on the Oct. 30 edition of SmackDown. Women's World Champion Liv is also slated to face Chelsea Green or Nikki Bella. Green will defend the title against Bella during the Oct. 30 episode of SmackDown. Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will continue their feud with a "Last Man Standing" match. Lastly, The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory will defend the World Tag Team Championship against Penta and Je'Von Evans.
summary: WWE has shifted Crown Jewel 2026 from Riyadh Season Stadium to Kingdom Arena while keeping the event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on Saturday, November 7. The show begins at 12 pm EST and will stream on ESPN+ in the United States and Netflix internationally. This aligns with WWE's multi-year partnership that typically features two premium live events per year in Saudi Arabia, including WrestleMania in Riyadh in 2027.

title: Paul Heyman compares working for Triple H and Vince McMahon
raw_title: WWE veteran Paul Heyman breaks down working under Triple H and Vince McMahon
body: A wrestling veteran and WWE Hall of Famer, Paul Heyman has been a part of WWE for a few decades now. Regarded as one of the best creative minds in the wrestling industry, Heyman recently opened up about his experience working under both Triple H and Vince McMahon. Currently employed under Triple H's leadership , Heyman has also been a part of WWE long enough to work under McMahon for several years. Speaking to Graham Bensinger, Heyman compared working under Vince McMahon and Triple H. The Hall of Famer reflected on the differences between their creative visions. "Paul Levesque is not a dictator; he's a collaborator. See, Vince [McMahon] loves a blank piece of paper. Paul Levesque doesn't like the blank piece of paper; he accepts the fact that the paper has writing on it already. "He's the best editor I've ever worked with in my entire life, ever, because he's an open collaborator who walks in the room with no expectations of his own vision. His vision is to listen to very smart people that have different ideas than he does. So, he's a collaborator the likes of which I've never had the pleasure of working with," Heyman said. While not active much now on WWE TV, Heyman was recently in a partnership with Brock Lesnar before his retirement at WWE SummerSlam . He was also seen appearing on WWE TV for a few weeks during Bron Breakker's rivalry with Oba Femi. Before all of these, Heyman was the manager of Seth Rollins' Vision.
summary: WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman discussed his experiences working under both Vince McMahon and Triple H. Heyman described Triple H as a collaborator who listens to different ideas rather than starting from a blank page like McMahon. He called Triple H the best editor he has ever worked with because of his open approach with no personal expectations.

title: Tommaso Ciampa Recalls AEW Match With Chris Jericho
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa Discusses Personal Impact Of Wrestling Chris Jericho In AEW
summary_src: AEW's Tommaso Ciampa grew up as a fan of Chris Jericho's before eventually facing off against the veteran wrestler.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik At AEW Redemption 2026, Tommaso Ciampa faced "The Painmaker" Chris Jericho in a No Holds Barred match after getting a win up on Jericho during "AEW Dynamite's" Beach Break special. Speaking to The Sportster, Ciampa shared his excitement at getting to go up against another side of a man he has long looked up to. "When the Painmaker thing came up, that just felt like such a lay-up," he recalled. "I've been a Jericho fan since my childhood, and the only thing that we didn't get out of that feud was the Lionheart somewhere. Then I would have got every iteration [of Jericho]." Ciampa fondly recalled how they put the story together, expressing that he and Jericho seemed to have a lot of in-ring chemistry based off of their match at Beach Break. He also stated that the two of them grew to trust each other after their limited time in the ring together. "So when the ideas started flowing for Montreal, before we even got into the building on that one, I had already, in my head, gone: 'Nah, this is gonna be like really, really good,'" he added. Because of the stipulation, their match featured plenty of brutality, like Ciampa being driven through a barbed wire table, the use of hockey pucks with thumbtacks glued to them, and the moment that saw Jericho dropped through a glass mirror and table. Considering that Jericho is 55, Ciampa claims he was shocked to see his opponent keep up, and stated that he doesn't see himself doing anything similar when he hits that age. "He's inhuman! Like, I don't know how this guy does what he does," he said. "This takes a toll on me, and I'm 41, so I just can't fathom when you're in your 50s, how do you recover?"
summary: At AEW Revolution 2026, Tommaso Ciampa wrestled Chris Jericho in a No Holds Barred match after defeating him on the Beach Break episode of Dynamite. Ciampa explained that he and Jericho built strong in-ring chemistry and trust quickly, leading him to feel confident their Montreal bout would be very successful.

title: Heyman Details McMahon Dictator Style vs Triple H Collaboration
raw_title: Paul Heyman contrasts Vince McMahon’s ‘dictator’ style with Triple H’s collaborative approach to WWE creative
summary_src: Paul Heyman offered insight into the contrasting leadership styles of Vince McMahon and Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque in WWE.
body: Paul Heyman offered insight into the contrasting leadership styles of Vince McMahon and Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque in WWE. During his interview on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Heyman described McMahon as a ‘dictator’ who expected things to be done his way, emphasizing that ‘it was his money, and therefore it’s his show.’ He also recalled McMahon’s approach to creative discussions, and the convincing it took to embrace a pitch. “Well, Paul runs the creative. And it’s a much different environment with Paul running the creative than Vince, because they are distinctly different personalities. Vince was a dictator. It was his money, and therefore it’s his show. And you’re going to be the executive director, or you’re going to be the lead writer, or you’re going to be my top idea man.” “‘Graham, I see this is not half empty (as he imitates McMahon) it’s not half full. That is a percentage which I have in my mind, and you can’t talk me out of it.’ ‘Well, Vince, what’s in your mind?’ ‘I don’t know. Why don’t you tell me what’s in your mind, and talk me out of what’s in mine?’” “So, you better be good at pitching. And it’s the constant chase for Vince to buy into your ideas over his own. That’s the dynamic of pitching Vince McMahon. He’s right, he has the right to be wrong. It’s his show, give me your best shot. Because if you can sell Vince, you can sell the talent, you can sell the lieutenants, and you can sell the audience. So if you’re that good of a salesman, he’s going to buy it. And then it’s his idea because he gets the credit, because he’s the owner.” Paul Heyman discusses Triple H’s ‘collaborative’ style of creative decisions- In the same interview, Heyman praised Triple H’s approach to WWE creative. He cited him as a collaborative leader who values input from others rather than imposing his own vision. “That’s not the way it works today. Paul Levesque is not a dictator; he’s a collaborator. See, Vince loves a blank piece of paper. Paul Levesque doesn’t like the blank piece of paper. He accepts the fact that the paper has writing on it already. He’s the best editor I’ve ever worked with in my entire life, ever. Because he’s an open collaborator that walks in the room with no expectations of his own vision. His vision is to listen to very smart people that have different ideas than he does. So, he’s a collaborator the likes of which I’ve never had the pleasure of working with. It’s just a completely different experience.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. From a kindergarten teacher to PR Associate to turning her lifelong passion for the industry into a career, Rosanne is currently writing for F4W Online where she focuses on wrestling news, analysis, and storytelling. Rosanne previously contributed to Sportskeeda as an Assistant Content Manager. When not consumed by wrestling, Rosanne is a musician and an aspiring artist.

Heyman said McMahon would present an idea as a fixed percentage in his mind and require others to talk him out of it. llm_long: Paul Heyman described Vince McMahon as a supremely complicated human being of great accomplishment during a recent interview.

When asked if McMahon is a good man, Heyman said he does not believe McMahon would ever consider himself that. Heyman added that McMahon did not care about being viewed as a good man and did not feel he was placed on the planet for that purpose.
Heyman stated that McMahon is a man of great accomplishment. He expressed regret over past battles with McMahon, noting that McMahon enjoyed confrontation and childish battles.

As an example, Heyman pointed to the 2006 relaunch of ECW. McMahon told Heyman he was putting him in charge but then immediately began stripping him of any authority over controlling, contouring, tailoring or creating the product.

Heyman said McMahon got off on changing ECW and turning it into a personal battle that was terrible for the product, the company and even worse for the audience. He called it the most miserable six months.
Heyman is not particularly active in WWE storylines at present and no longer regularly accompanies The Vision for their matches.

title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Admits He’s Had Multiple Long-Term Relationships at the Same Time
raw_title: Paul Heyman Admits He’s Had Multiple Long-Term Relationships at the Same Time
summary_src: Paul Heyman has made it clear that marriage isn’t for him, but that doesn’t mean he’s stayed away from serious relationships. In fact, the WWE personality admitted he’s had plenty of long-term relationships over the years — and some of them were happening at the same time.
body: During an inteview with Graham Bensinger, Heyman opened up about his personal life and why he has no interest in getting married. He explained that he doesn’t like the idea of being legally obligated to stay with someone, arguing that relationships should be based on two people choosing to remain together. “Because at some point in it, your decision to stay is obligatory because of a piece of paper. If I wake up next to somebody, I want to know that they’re there because they chose to be there because they have the absolute freedom to walk out the door and they chose not to.” The conversation then turned to whether Heyman could see himself settling down in a long-term relationship without getting married. That’s when he admitted he’s already had several, including some that overlapped. “I have had many long-term relationships. Some of them at the same time.” The interviewer laughed at Heyman’s admission before asking a more specific question about whether he could see himself in a long-term monogamous relationship. Heyman didn’t rule it out, but he made it clear that he still wants the freedom to walk away. Heyman then explained that there’s one thing every meaningful relationship in his life has had in common. Whether it’s romantic or otherwise, he believes friendship is what holds everything together. “And some of those long-term monogous relationships, not not some of them, all of them are based on the one common thread of any relationship I’ve ever had in my life. Friendship.” Heyman also admitted that he wouldn’t want to date someone like himself. He explained that his children will always come first, followed by his dedication to pursuing his professional goals, leaving very little room for a romantic partner. “I would never date me. Why not? Oh, because number one, my children come first. That’s number one. We have to accept that premise. My children come first. Secondly, in many ways, my self-committed slavery to the cause of pursuing dreams is going to come second.” For Heyman, marriage isn’t necessary to maintain a serious relationship, and he’s not interested in changing his priorities to make one work. He’s had long-term relationships, he’s open to monogamy, and he believes friendship matters more than a marriage certificate. But his admission that some of those relationships happened at the same time certainly adds another side to his personal life that fans don’t usually hear about. title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Calls Marriage a “Trap” and Explains Why He Wants No Part of It
raw_title: Paul Heyman Calls Marriage a “Trap” and Explains Why He Wants No Part of It
summary_src: Paul Heyman has spent his career committing himself completely to professional wrestling, but don’t expect him to make that same kind of commitment through marriage. As far as Heyman is concerned, getting married is basically walking straight into a trap.
body: Speaking to Graham Bensinger , Heyman was asked whether he could ever see himself getting married. The answer was an immediate “no,” and when Bensinger pushed him on why, Heyman explained that he doesn’t like the idea of a piece of paper becoming part of the reason two people stay together. “Because it’s a trap. No, really. Because at some point in it, your decision to stay is obligatory because of a piece of paper. If I wake up next to somebody, I want to know that they’re there because they chose to be there, because they have the absolute freedom to walk out the door and they chose not to.” Bensinger brought up the obvious counterargument — a prenuptial agreement. That didn’t change Heyman’s mind either, because he believes a prenup just turns the whole thing into a financial arrangement with terms attached to how long the relationship lasts. “But a prenup is — so then you’re in an arrangement. A prenup says, ‘All right, if you’re here for five years, you get this much percentage of the money. You get this car, and you get this condo, and custody of the dog.’ A prenup makes it a financial arrangement.” Marriage isn’t the only place where Heyman’s priorities are pretty clear. He admitted that romantic relationships simply aren’t near the top of his list, with his children coming before everything and his professional pursuits also taking priority over his personal needs. Heyman knows that doesn’t leave much room for a partner, but he isn’t pretending otherwise. In his mind, spending time with someone already means giving them the limited personal time he could have spent on himself, and that’s a sacrifice he’s willing to accept. “When it comes to being in a relationship, I don’t care because I don’t put myself first or second. I put myself either third or fourth. I’ll put somebody ahead of me, but I’m always going to put the pursuits ahead of them, and I’m going to put my children ahead of everything else. “So it’s like someone will say, ‘Well, you don’t have time for us.’ I don’t have time for me. Us time is me time. I give you my me time, and I don’t have any me time. So I don’t have time for us because I don’t have time for me. And I don’t mind that. That’s the sacrifice that I’m willing to make.” And Heyman doesn’t sound particularly interested in slowing down so he can make more room for a relationship either. When Bensinger suggested he could work less and enjoy the fruits of everything he’s accomplished, Heyman gave a pretty wild explanation for why that idea doesn’t appeal to him. For Heyman, the work itself is what gives him the rush he’s chasing. body: It is a story four years in the making, originating in 2022, seemingly culminating a year later, and revisited here as both men stand atop their respective brands as the top dogs of Raw and SmackDown, respectively. He joined up with The Bloodline as an unofficial member of the faction, interfered in nearly all of their matches, and proved his loyalty over time. Along the way, Zayn was so entertaining and lovable that fans bonded with him. There was genuine emotion as they followed his story, from an independent conspiracy theorist to "Sami Uso," finally accepted by the group he had tagged along with for months. At the 2023 Royal Rumble, Zayn had grown tired of being treated like dirt by Reigns, berated and verbally assaulted. Faced with blasting his friend, Kevin Owens, with a steel chair, Zayn answered one last belittlement with a chair across the back of the Tribal Chief in one of the truly great moments in modern WWE history. The crowd erupted for Zayn that night, and a few weeks later in Montreal, they were rabidly behind him as he battled Reigns for the Undisputed WWE Universal Championship. He fell short of capturing the title then, thanks to interference from the Usos. Still, he would avenge the entire Bloodline experience at WrestleMania 39 when he teamed with Owens to defeat The Usos in the main event of Saturday's broadcast. Zayn would agree to set aside their past issues and join forces with The Bloodline and CM Punk for the main event of the 2024 Survivor Series: War Games. He has been so entertaining in the role that he is now a two-time WWE champion and the centerpiece of the SmackDown brand, a well-deserved spot for a guy who has consistently proven capable of getting (and staying) over. When he squares off with Reigns in Riyadh at Crown Jewel, he will do so not as The OTC's lackey, looking to upset him for the championship, but as a cunning and fully realized WWE main eventer with the very real possibility of defeating the face of the company in a high-profile champion vs. champion match, a fitting conclusion to their epic story. title: Heyman: Vikings Hid Lesnar's Elite Combine Numbers
raw_title: “Reluctant to Release”: Brock Lesnar’s Ex-Manager Reveals Vikings’ Attempt to Hide WWE Star’s Combine Results From Media
body: "He went out for the Minnesota Vikings training camp," Paul Heyman told Graham Bensinger . "They were reluctant to release to the media his combine numbers because he came out of WWE, and the Minnesota Vikings were concerned that the media would think this is a WWE stunt with these numbers because whether it was the 40-yard dash or the 100-yard dash or the quarter mile or with the standing jump or whatever it was, his combine numbers were of Olympic qualifying time." Brock Lesnar hadn't played organized football since his senior year of high school in 1995. Even so, in 2004 he walked away from a multimillion-dollar WWE contract to chase a roster spot with the Vikings. "Brock Lesnar has made a personal decision to put his WWE career on hold to prepare to try out for the National Football League this season. Brock has wrestled his entire professional career in the WWE, and we are proud of his accomplishments and wish him the best in his new endeavor." The numbers explain the interest. At 6'2″ and 285 pounds, he reportedly ran a 4.7-second 40-yard dash, jumped 35 inches, and did 30 reps on the 225-pound bench press, according to Pro Football Rumors . The idea started that spring, when his agent began calling teams about a tryout. Lesnar later told a Minnesota radio show he had "three wonderful years" in WWE, and regarding the NFL, he was blunt. "This is no load of bull; it's no WWE stunt. I am dead serious about this. I ain't afraid of anything and I ain't afraid of anybody. I've been an underdog in athletics since I was five. I got zero college offers for wrestling. Now people say I can't play football, that it's a joke. I say I can. "I'm as good an athlete as a lot of guys in the NFL, if not better. I've always had to fight for everything. I wasn't the best technician in amateur wrestling, but I was strong, had great conditioning, and a hard head. Nobody could break me. As long as I have that, I don't give a damn what anybody else thinks." At least six teams were interested, Minnesota included, but then he crashed his motorcycle in April and injured his groin. Nobody knew if football was still possible. Two months later he was healthy again and went back to the Vikings. He asked for another chance, and it paid off. They invited him to camp as a defensive lineman. "I'm a fortunate person to even get this opportunity," Lesnar said in a phone interview between practices with the Vikings. "I've worked hard, and whatever happens, happens. I hope I don't hear my name called. More than likely, it will." Lesnar's NFL attempt ended on August 30, when the Vikings let him go after he'd signed and played a few preseason games. After the release, the Vikings offered him a spot with NFL Europa as their representative. He said no because he wanted to stay in the States with his family. So football ended up being a side trip. title: WWE’s Potential SmackDown Move Ran Into Another Scheduling Problem — Report
raw_title: WWE’s Potential SmackDown Move Ran Into Another Scheduling Problem — Report
body: 0 WWE SmackDown reportedly considered a schedule change to help ESPN and the WNBA Finals. However, the proposed plan ultimately didn’t happen. The situation involved several parties trying to resolve a complicated scheduling issue. Game six between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries became a major scheduling story. Organizers wanted the game played in prime time at Atlanta’s State Farm Arena. However, the contest was ultimately scheduled for Thursday at 12:30 PM Eastern. New reporting has revealed WWE nearly became part of the solution. The company reportedly showed flexibility before the plan was abandoned. ESPN reporter Ramona Shelburne reported on X, formerly known as Twitter, Steve Koonin approached WWE president Nick Khan. Koonin, a former WWE Board member, currently leads the Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena. He reportedly asked Khan about moving Friday’s SmackDown to 9 PM Eastern. The proposed change would have allowed the WNBA game to air on USA Network. WWE SmackDown would then follow the basketball broadcast. The report didn’t clarify how WWE would have handled the change. The company could have started the live broadcast later. Another possibility was recording the show earlier for a delayed broadcast. However, WWE’s reported willingness, the plan eventually fell apart. The main concern involved the possibility of a game seven. Organizers didn’t want that deciding game competing with Election Night coverage. A potential game seven would have taken place on Tuesday. That would have created a scheduling conflict with U.S. midterm election coverage. As a result, the proposed arrangement was abandoned. Instead, game six was scheduled for Thursday at 12:30 PM Eastern and WWE SmackDown would remain in its regular time slot. title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Opens Up On Studio 54 Offered to Pay Him in Cocaine When He Was Just 19
raw_title: Paul Heyman Reveals Studio 54 Offered to Pay Him in Cocaine When He Was Just 19
summary_src: Paul Heyman has seen plenty of wild things throughout his career, but apparently nothing compares to what went down during his days at Studio 54.
body: While speaking with Graham Bensinger , Heyman looked back on his early career and explained how he went from being a teenage photographer to producing and promoting events at one of the most famous clubs in the world. He also revealed just how normal drug use was behind the scenes, claiming that cocaine was even offered as a form of payment. Heyman explained that when he first joined the staff as a house photographer, he was given three different options for how he wanted to get paid. Two involved money, while the third was something completely different. “My secret in Studio 54 was that I didn’t drink. I didn’t do drugs. Everybody was doing cocaine. There were people that were being paid in co- When I first started on staff as the house photographer, I was told by the person running Studio 54, ‘We can pay you three ways. We can pay you on the books, in which you’re going to pay taxes. We can pay you a little less in cash and do it do the what you want. Or we give you this much in cocaine and you do with it what you want.'” Heyman wasn’t interested in taking the cocaine. At just 19 years old, he decided it was smarter to get paid the normal way rather than risk getting himself into trouble. “And I just said, ‘Oh, just put me on books. I don’t need this trouble at 19 years old.'” That decision ended up working out pretty well for Heyman. While he claims everyone around him was either drinking or getting high, he was focused on getting work done and moving up the ladder. According to Heyman, being one of the few sober people in the building gave him a serious advantage. “Everybody else was either drunk or high, and I wasn’t. So, I had the run of the joint because I was the only one that was thinking straight. So, my ambitions could play out in the things that I wanted to accomplish here because everyone else was high.” Heyman went on to explain that his priorities were completely different from those of the people around him. While others were chasing their next high, he was chasing opportunities that could help build his career. “So, they’re skewed in that perspective, and I’m just trying to get the job done and move up the ladder, which was pretty easy because their pursuits including the chase of the high. And mine didn’t. Mine was the chase of the actual chase of accomplishment.” His approach paid off quickly. Heyman became Studio 54’s head photographer at 19 and was already producing and promoting Friday night events before turning 20. That experience eventually led to him organizing his first professional wrestling event at the nightclub, where he brought in names like Ric Flair, Dusty Rhodes, Magnum T.A., and Bam Bam Bigelow. Looking back, Heyman clearly believes staying away from drugs was one of the biggest reasons he was able to accomplish so much at such a young age. title: Grayson Waller Vows to Make WWE Regret Main Roster Booking
raw_title: Grayson Waller determined to prove himself on NXT after poor WWE main roster booking: ‘I’m going to make them regret it’
summary_src: Grayson Waller reflected on the differences between his initial run in NXT and his current stint with the brand. Waller told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that his perspective has changed from learning the ropes to becoming a veteran presence in the locker room.
body: Grayson Waller reflected on the differences between his initial run in NXT and his current stint with the brand. Waller told Chris Van Vliet on the Insight Podcast that his perspective has changed from learning the ropes to becoming a veteran presence in the locker room. He also discussed his desire to set an example for younger talent and prove to WWE’s main roster that they missed an opportunity by not making better use of him. “Well, the first time you get to NXT, you’re learning. So when I was there, there’s guys like Ciampa and Gargano and Pete Dunne, and I’m learning under them, working out what this is, working out who I am as a character, learning. People talk about the WWE style, but all those types of things. Now, I run this; I am NXT. These kids are here to learn from me. I don’t really want to help them. I’m not here to give them advice and things like that. I’m here to show them what a real WWE Superstar is like. I’m here to show them the work ethic you need to have. I’m going to show them the talent you need to have to have that championship and represent it. Because I think for a while a lot of those lads didn’t have someone to look up to.” “They didn’t have a Gargano or a Ciampa in the locker room to teach them how to do this. You’ve got a kid, a shot putter from six months ago, who’s the leader of the locker room. That’s not a great dynamic. So, I feel me going back there is now I’m fully me. I know who I am, and I’m just going to show the world. Part of it is I want to show the main roster, like Raw and SmackDown you had this. You had this in your hands, and you did nothing with it. So I’m going to make them regret it.” The NXT Champion recalled his conversation with Shawn Michaels about returning to NXT, explaining that it was a request rather than an order. He also highlighted the opportunity to compete regularly on television against talented performers. title: AEW Not Planning Immediate In-Ring Return For Toni Storm
raw_title: Backstage Update On Teased AEW Return Of Former Women's Champion Toni Storm
summary_src: A new report has revealed Toni Storm's status after recent hints suggested that the former AEW Women's World Champion would be returning soon.
body: AEW It looks like former AEW Women's World Champion Toni Storm could return to the promotion soon, with a new report providing additional details. Storm, who has been out of action since March, was rumored to be returning at the recent WrestleDream pay-per-view after some people noticed cassette tapes placed on their seats . However, that did not happen. " Fightful Select " is now reporting that AEW sources have indicated that her in-ring return isn't imminent, though the promotion could involve her in other ways. The report also highlighted that the former WWE star hasn't appeared on any recent AEW shows. The outlet revealed that AEW originally had plans for Storm for the rest of 2026 before she was written off television following an attack by a mystery attacker. AEW sources reportedly said that the promotion had settled on a name to be revealed as the attacker, with the storyline set to point the finger at several potential suspects. Reports from earlier in the year had stated that her absence was not down to injury . Many, including AEW's Tony Schiavone and Storm's personal butler, Luther , have speculated about who the mystery attacker could be. Schiavone suggested that Mercedes Mone or Thekla could be responsible, while Luther said it could be anyone jealous of Storm's success.
summary: Per Fightful Select, AEW sources say Toni Storm's in-ring return is not imminent although the promotion could still use her in other capacities. The former Women's World Champion has been absent from AEW television since March after being attacked by a mystery assailant. AEW had already mapped out creative plans for Storm through the rest of 2026 before she was written off the show, and the company had chosen a specific person to portray the attacker while building suspicion toward multiple suspects.

title: Stephanie Vaquer sidelined by illness from WWE Raw
raw_title: Update on Stephanie Vaquer after WWE Raw absence
summary_src: An illness forced Stephanie Vaquer to miss WWE Raw this week, but it doesn’t sound like the issue is anything too serious. The October 26 episode of Raw was set to be headlined by Vaquer vs. Becky Lynch in a number one contender’s match.
body: An illness forced Stephanie Vaquer to miss WWE Raw this week, but it doesn’t sound like the issue is anything too serious. The October 26 episode of Raw was set to be headlined by Vaquer vs. Becky Lynch in a number one contender’s match. With Vaquer unable to be at the show due to an illness , WWE instead had Lynch challenge Liv Morgan for the Women’s World Championship that night. It ended in a disqualification with Morgan’s Judgment Day stablemates Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez interfering just as Lynch was about to get the win. Our Dave Meltzer gave an update on the situation on Wrestling Observer Radio , noting that Vaquer’s illness is “nothing terribly serious.” There is no exact timeline for when she’s expected back yet. “She’s ill. It’s not anything — I was told it’s nothing terribly serious or anything,” Meltzer said. “But she’s ill and she’s out. Indefinitely in the sense that it’s not like it’s a week. It’s something that’s indeterminate yet as far as when she’ll be back. “But that’s why they didn’t do that match. It wasn’t about an injury, and it wasn’t a worked storyline. They were going to do the match on Monday night and she got sick and could not come. And that’s why they did the Becky Lynch-Liv Morgan. And that’s why they did the DQ, because they didn’t want to beat Becky Lynch. But it wasn’t a match that they had planned, so they did the DQ that way — to get out of it essentially.” Separate from this illness, Vaquer has dealt with ankle and shoulder injuries in 2026. She had a minor ankle injury following this month’s Money in the Bank PLE but was medically cleared for Monday’s Raw before the illness sidelined her again. Money in the Bank took place on October 10 and saw Morgan win the Women’s World Championship from Vaquer in a triple threat match that also included Lynch. Per Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio, the illness is nothing terribly serious but her return timeline remains undetermined.

summary_src: Shotzi Blackheart has a pretty simple request for wrestling fans planning to meet her — take a shower and put on some damn deodorant. Otherwise, don’t expect to be getting a hug.
body: Speaking on Knockouts and 3 Counts , Shotzi was asked about wrestling locker-room etiquette and whether she had any pet peeves or advice for younger wrestlers coming into the business. The host threw out several answers he’d previously received, including bringing your own wrist tape, keeping your gear bag nearby, respecting locker-room seating and, most importantly for Shotzi, “wash your balls.” That last one immediately got Shotzi’s attention, but her problem wasn’t really with people inside the locker room. Instead, she turned the advice toward some of the fans showing up at wrestling meet-and-greets. “Man, I really like the ‘wash your balls’ one, because, man, there’s, like, a lot of stinky people. I mean, this is more so for the fans and not, like, the locker room. Like, you know, if you’re coming to—” The host jumped in and noted that hygiene complaints involving fans had definitely come up before. Shotzi then made her rules for getting close to her at a meet-and-greet very clear — clean yourself up and wear deodorant. “Yeah, yeah. If you’re coming to a meet-and-greet, wash your balls and wear deodorant. That’s super important. And then if you do that, you might get a nice hug from me. But if you’re stanky and you didn’t wash your balls, I’m not going to hug you. I’m not.” So there you have it. Shotzi Blackheart isn’t asking fans to follow some complicated meet-and-greet rulebook — just handle the basics before showing up, especially if you’re hoping to walk away with a hug. What do you make of Shotzi Blackheart’s brutally simple advice for wrestling fans attending meet-and-greets? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Leon Slater Vows To Take TNA World Title In New Direction
raw_title: Leon Slater On Winning TNA World Title: 'I'm Excited To Take It In A New Direction'
summary_src: Leon Slater has opened up about becoming TNA World Champion and how he is still processing the achievement, while vowing to put his own stamp on the title.
body: TNA/YouTube New TNA World Champion Leon Slater has spoken in amazement about winning the title and vowed to put his own stamp on the championship. Slater became the youngest TNA World Champion at Bound for Glory after defeating Nic Nemeth, putting himself on the path to greater things. He recently spoke on the " I Love Wrestling Podcast ," where he admitted that he was still coming to terms with his achievement. "It feels very, very surreal, man. And, you know, it took a while for it to settle in because I kind of felt like I was carrying Nic Nemeth's belt around for a while just 'cause I was used to seeing him with it, you know?" he said. Slater explained that it was still hard for him to process being champion as he tried to maintain his normal routine of hanging out with friends and playing video games. He said he recently realized he was the TNA World Champion while playing a video game, noting that everything in his life — his house, friends, and hobbies — had remained the same, with the only major change being the world title beside him. The English star promised to take the title in a different direction and make it truly special. "It's the same game I've been playing for the past 13 years, and the only difference is I've got the actual TNA World Championship on my TV table, you know what I mean? So, it's finally beginning to feel mine. And I'm excited for it to take me in a new direction. And I'm excited to take it in a new direction, as well, and make some magic as TNA World Champion," added Slater. Since winning the world title, Slater has set his eyes on a few who could be challenging for his championship, with the first being Trey Miguel, who became the No. 1 contender for the world title after winning a ladder match on the " Impact " after Bound for Glory.

title: Grayson Waller Calls Home Invasion Mind Games
raw_title: Grayson Waller On Invading Tony D'Angelo's Home: This Is All Mind Games
summary_src: Grayson Waller is shrugging off his recent actions. The feud between Tony D'Angelo and Grayson Waller took a big leap on the October 27 episode of NXT, with Waller choosing to show up to D'Angelo's home.
body: The feud between Tony D’Angelo and Grayson Waller took a big leap on the October 27 episode of NXT, with Waller choosing to show up to D’Angelo’s home. Speaking with Busted Open After Dark , Grayson Waller implied that his actions were a direct result of Tony D’Angelo claiming that he can’t get into his head. “Yeah dude, it’s fun. If Tony knew anything about me, he knew I would be willing to do that. Remember last week when Tony said, ‘Oh, you can’t get in my head.’ Nah lad, I’m different. I got in his head tonight. I did exactly what I knew I could do. This is a great thing because I said tonight, I look back on my past and I miss that old Grayson. Remember when I went to Johnny Gargano’s house and beat him up in front of his wife and kid? Man, that was a Grayson who wanted it. You know what? This Grayson wants it too and I’m glad I found him.” Waller continued on and said that he’s playing a game that very few people are willing to play. “What did I do? I went to his house. Did I do anything? See, this is all mind games. I was offended last week when Tony said that I couldn’t get in his head. I went bet, watch what happens. Last week, I sent him on a wild goose chase. You know what Tony should be worrying about? He should be worrying about Halloween Havoc, he’s wrestling for the NXT title. But he’s not. He’s worried about his kid, he’s worried about his wife, he’s worried about his restaurant. You know what I’m worried about? Winning. That’s a game very few people are willing to play, but I’m willing to play. No wonder Myles Borne isn’t wrestling for this championship on Saturday, he doesn’t have it in him obviously if he thinks I went too far. This is what we do. There’s levels and I’m willing to go anywhere.” Grayson Waller will defend his NXT Championship against Tony D’Angelo at NXT Halloween Havoc. title: Roman Reigns Praise Prompted Grayson Waller Image Overhaul
raw_title: Roman Reigns’ stamp of approval inspired NXT star to make career-altering change
summary_src: Ever since his NXT return in July, Grayson Waller has been extensively revamping his persona and appearance. Waller acknowledged being mocked and ‘perceived as a joke’ due to the way he dressed with boxing shorts which people mistook for basketball shorts.
body: Ever since his NXT return in July, Grayson Waller has been extensively revamping his persona and appearance. Waller acknowledged being mocked and ‘perceived as a joke’ due to the way he dressed with boxing shorts which people mistook for basketball shorts. On the Insight Podcast , the NXT Champion reflected on his decision to alter his look, switching to tights for a six-man tag team match at Royal Rumble where he teamed with New Day against Motor City Machine Guns and Shinsuke Nakamura. Roman Reigns complimented him stating it made him look like a champion, and it was a statement Waller held in high regard. “I look back and I kind of understand why people would have perceived me as a joke. For me, the boxing shorts were always I was a huge boxing fan. A lot of people think it was basketball shorts, but I thought it was a different look. It made me look unique, but I think it also didn’t make me look like a serious contender for the championship. So that was something where I was like, I need to change things up. I can’t just keep giving them the same thing. So first thing was I put the tights on, and actually the Rumble was the first time I kind of wore them in a match, and Roman came up and pulled me aside and said, ‘Hey, that’s the look. You look like a champion now.’” “Hey, if Roman says that, all right, lad, whatever you need, I’m gonna keep the pants. But even coming back to NXT, I was like, I can’t walk out with the leopard shirts and all that. That vibe didn’t work. That’s an old me. So now, I am more serious. This is me. I feel comfortable now. So I think I had to change things because if you keep throwing the same thing at the wall and it’s not working, then what are you doing?” Waller was initially moved to the main roster in 2023 where he made an impression with The Grayson Waller Effect. After being drafted to Raw in 2025, Waller continued to feature in tag team storylines, first with Theory and later alongside The New Day. However, he later expressed frustration with the inconsistent creative direction , explaining that WWE wanted him to be more serious while placing him in comedic situations . His first main roster run ultimately left him feeling that he had not been given the opportunity to demonstrate his full potential. title: Liv Morgan’s NSFW RAW Moment Was Reportedly Censored on Netflix
raw_title: Liv Morgan’s NSFW RAW Moment Was Reportedly Censored on Netflix
body: 0 WWE Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan’s latest RAW appearance has sparked discussion. Reports claim Netflix censored part of her closing segment. The changes reportedly appeared when the episode became available for replay. Morgan defended her Women’s World Championship against Becky Lynch on WWE RAW. Lynch nearly secured victory after hitting the Manhandle Slam. However, Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez interfered in the match. The contest ended in disqualification, allowing Morgan to retain her title. Following the match, The Judgment Day attacked Becky Lynch. WWE Women’s Champion Chelsea Green then came out to help her. Iyo SKy also joined the fight and took down Morgan and Rodriguez. Tiffany Stratton also join in the chaos who followed up by hitting Morgan with an Unprettier. However, Dominik Mysterio soon intervened and carried Morgan away on his shoulders. His actions prevented Stratton from cashing in her Money in the Bank contract. The original live broadcast showed Mysterio carrying Morgan away. The camera angles also showed the moment from behind. However, reports claim Netflix edited portions of the footage for replay. The changes reportedly covered parts of Morgan’s backside in certain shots. One of the final angles may have captured more than intended. This isn’t the first time Netflix has reportedly modified WWE footage. The streaming giant has made changes to some content after live broadcasts in the past as well. The post Liv Morgan’s NSFW RAW Moment Was Reportedly Censored on Netflix appeared first on Wrestlezone .
summary: Reports claim Netflix censored part of her closing segment. The changes by most accounts appeared when the episode became available for replay.
