title: Ilja Dragunov Calls Gunther A Future GOAT
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Thinks Former WWE Rival Will Be 'A GOAT'
summary_src: AEW star Ilja Dragunov has named a former WWE rival who played a big part in his career, stating that he considers him one of the greats of the business.
body: AEW/YouTube Ilja Dragunov has enjoyed a great rise in pro wrestling, which he credits in part to his peers, including WWE's GUNTHER, whom he considers one of the greats of all time. Dragunov and GUNTHER rose up the ranks in Germany , having wrestled often in the German promotion wXw, before bringing their rivalry all the way to "NXT UK." The new AEW star has credited GUNTHER for his growth and believes that he will go down in history as a great wrestler. "Gunther [is] a dear friend of mine since, I don't know, [since] 2015. Like, so for such a long time, no other person in professional wrestling forged me more than he. [He's] A mastermind. He is one of the greatest, and he will be one of the greatest of all time when he decides to leave the boots in the ring," he said on the " Battleground Podcast ." Dragunov acknowledged the impact GUNTHER had on him as a wrestler, stating that the big growth in his pro wrestling career came after he faced the WWE star. "I mean, like, all the biggest peaks of progression I always had when I faced him. It's just as simple as that. What I could take [from GUNTHER] is, like, directness always gives you the best enhancement of your talents and strengths. So, he was always very straightforward with me, no sugarcoating," added Dragunov. GUNTHER predicted back in 2024 that Dragunov could be the next big thing on the main roster , with many expecting Dragunov to follow in GUNTHER's footsteps and become a more prominent figure on the WWE main roster. However, that ultimately didn't happen, as Dragunov's main roster run lasted just two years. GUNTHER, meanwhile, has gone on to become WWE World Heavyweight Champion, retire legends like John Cena and AJ Styles, and pave the way for a bright future in WWE.
summary: New AEW talent Ilja Dragunov discussed his long friendship and rivalry with WWE's Gunther that began in 2015 in the German promotion wXw and continued in NXT UK. Dragunov credited Gunther with forging him more than anyone else in wrestling and stated that his biggest career growth came from facing him. He added that Gunther is a mastermind who will be regarded as one of the greatest of all time upon retirement.

title: Grayson Waller Mocks NXT Stars' Excitement For John Cena
raw_title: Grayson Waller: Maybe John Cena Needs To Come Sit Under My Learning Tree, I Can Tell Him How Things Run In NXT Now
summary_src: John Cena is set to appear on the October 4 episode of WWE NXT. Grayson Waller isn't impressed. In a new interview with Busted Open After Dark, Waller criticized NXT wrestlers for marking out about the Cena announcement.
body: John Cena is set to appear on the October 4 episode of WWE NXT. Grayson Waller isn’t impressed. In a new interview with Busted Open After Dark, Waller criticized NXT wrestlers for marking out about the Cena announcement. “I was backstage tonight when the graphic came out, you should’ve heard the kids, ‘John Cena is coming!’ It was so sad, it was tough. I felt like I was at a fan meet and greet or something, they’re all excited. It put a smile on my face too. I’m the only one here who’s been in the ring with John Cena twice. I’ve been on the mic against John Cena and I survived, not everyone does. All I hope for John is that next Wednesday, he wipes his feet and he knocks on the door and he asks me permission to come into my house. If he wants to get in my ring, he needs to ask permission too. I’m sure he’s maybe talking about this John Cena Classic, giving some NXT superstars an opportunity. Those opportunities, I’ve taken. Maybe he needs to come sit down under my learning tree and I can tell him how things run in NXT now.” Continuing on, Waller joked that Cena wasn’t coming around to NXT when Tony D’Angelo was champion. “It’s true, he’s coming down here because of what I’m doing. Was John Cena coming around the last year or so when Tony was champion? No, but he wants to come down here now. I guess it’s like, maybe it’s a championship celebration. Maybe he’s going to do a rap song for me or something, celebrate the fact that I run NXT now.” Elsewhere in the interview, Waller explained why he broke into D’Angelo’s home. llm_long: NXT Champion Grayson Waller criticized his fellow NXT wrestlers for their excited reactions backstage when it was announced that John Cena would make a rare appearance on the show. Waller was speaking on Busted Open After Dark about the upcoming episode, which is moving to Wednesday, November 4, due to election coverage and will air against AEW's Blood & Guts.

He described the moment the graphic appeared as pathetic, saying the other wrestlers acted like kids at a fan meet-and-greet shouting about Cena's arrival. Waller contrasted their behavior by noting he is the only one on the roster who has faced Cena in the ring twice and gone against him on the microphone, surviving the experience.

He stated that Cena should wipe his feet, knock on the door, and ask permission before entering his house or his ring on the show. He explained that they are all on one WWE brand now and must carry themselves as equals while still showing respect and learning from the legends without acting like fans.

Waller warned that if any wrestlers ask for photos or wear Cena's merch next week, he will talk to them directly, emphasizing that to become champion or main event WrestleMania, they must treat these people as equals.

summary_src: Elayna Black is opening up about the treatment she received during her WWE career — and one particular comment about her appearance apparently stuck with her long after she left the company.
body: In a documentary published on TNA Wrestling’s YouTube channel , Black reflected on her time in WWE NXT and the frustrations she experienced while trying to establish herself. She explained that despite putting in the work, listening to coaches, and improving her performances, she continued watching other wrestlers receive opportunities that weren’t coming her way. Black said she couldn’t understand why her hard work wasn’t translating into more opportunities, especially when she believed she was doing everything WWE had asked of her. “I felt like I was doing everything right. I felt like I was taking all the advice. I felt like I was improving in every aspect that any coach was telling me to. I felt like I was doing it, but I wasn’t getting the opportunities that other people were getting, and I kind of was watching myself being passed over, and I didn’t understand why.” “I was told that I was not and would not be champion in that company because I looked like I couldn’t even crack an egg.” Black didn’t identify who made the comment, but she made it clear that the criticism she received about her appearance had a serious impact on her confidence. She explained that she entered WWE without having major insecurities about her body. That changed once she found herself under constant scrutiny, with people judging how she looked and whether she fit their expectations of a professional wrestler. “Very quickly, I started to become very, very insecure about my body. Yeah, that was definitely the first time that I was like, I never thought anything was wrong with my body, and then I get put into this position, and all these eyes in this different, you know, spotlight, and it’s a mind f** to be honest.”* Those struggles were made even more difficult by the fact that Black joined WWE at just 19 years old. She admitted that she spent much of her early career worrying about how others perceived her and whether she was doing or saying the wrong things. “I got signed when I was 19. So, I think for a while, honestly, like my first few years there, I was very worried about being perceived a certain way or like how people were going to view me or doing something the wrong way or saying something the wrong way and kind of like walking on eggshells because I wasn’t fully confident in myself and my work.” Black has since returned to TNA Wrestling, where she says she’s finally beginning to feel comfortable with herself again. After years of struggling with outside expectations, she believes she’s reached a point where she understands who she is both personally and professionally. “For the first time in a very long time, I feel confident in who I am as a person and as a character. title: On the Record: Chris Jericho Opens Up On TV Series About His Early Wrestling Career Is Close to Filming Pilot
raw_title: Chris Jericho Reveals TV Series About His Early Wrestling Career Is Close to Filming Pilot
summary_src: Chris Jericho’s life in professional wrestling could be headed to television — and this isn’t just some idea he’s throwing around.
body: During a recent interview with Skratch N’ Sniff , Jericho was asked whether his autobiography could ever receive the Hollywood treatment, especially following wrestling films like The Iron Claw and Queen of the Ring . That’s when Jericho revealed that plans are already underway to turn his first book, A Lion’s Tale , into a television series rather than a standalone movie. “Yeah, I don’t know, man. You know, it’s one of those things where whoever would play me, um we probably don’t even know. Like, you can’t say Brad Pitt because Brad Pitt’s older than me. But we are actually working on on something based on my first book, A Lion’s Tale, that we’ve been working on for a while, uh, of doing a a TV series based on that.” Jericho didn’t stop there. He explained that the project has already made significant progress behind the scenes and is approaching the pilot stage. He also revealed that the production has an actor in mind who bears a strong resemblance to him during his younger years. “Um, and so, so we’ve kind of moved it up the food chain and, and it’s getting pretty close to filming a pilot, and we do have an actor that, that is very similar to me when he was first starting out that was from the Letter Kenny series, if you ever watch that show.” While Jericho wouldn’t reveal exactly which Letterkenny actor is being considered, he made it clear that the physical resemblance is hard to ignore. When the interviewer praised the Canadian comedy series, Jericho offered another detail while keeping the actor’s identity under wraps. “Yeah. Yeah. I won’t say who it is in Letter Kenny, but there is a real facial uh uh similarity.” The potential series would focus on the early years of Jericho’s wrestling career, drawing from A Lion’s Tale , which documents his journey through the wrestling business before becoming an established international star. Rather than trying to squeeze that story into a two-hour movie, Jericho believes there’s enough material to build an entire television series. “Um, so yeah, I mean there might be something very very soon of not just an autobiography because that’s not enough because I’m, you know, Chris Jericho, right? I always have to push the the envelope that we might have a whole actual TV series about kind of the early years of my career which would be a lot of fun. So that’s something we’re working on and we’re getting, you know, we’re we’re moving to the pilot stage fairly fairly soon.” Jericho also confirmed that he isn’t simply lending his name to the project and leaving the creative decisions to somebody else. When asked how much involvement he’s had in bringing his story to television, he explained that he’s been part of the development process from the very beginning. “Since day one? Yeah, since day one. Like I said, you don’t just go, ‘Hey, let’s do a TV series.’ You know, hey, let’s make a record. Hey, let’s get a record deal. Like, you got to put a lot of time into it to to get it through all the different goal

llm_long: Beyond Wrestling issued a statement on Monday detailing the uncertain future of its weekly Wrestling Open Rhode Island events at Rhodes On The Pawtuxet in Cranston. The promotion's contract with the venue runs through the end of 2026. Unless there is a strong increase in Monday night attendance or sponsor revenue, the final weekly event will take place on December 28, 2026.

The month of November will serve as an evaluation period for the series that launched in March 2025. Drew Cordeiro urged fans who enjoy the shows to tell others, bring friends, and share the promotion's social media posts promoting the events.

Those interested in sponsoring the series can email beyondwrestling@gmail.com for detailed information. Cordeiro noted there remains a possibility of negotiating a new rental agreement for 2027 even without improved attendance. The statement thanked supporters of independent wrestling and specifically the Rhode Island events.

Monday's show marked episode 73 of Wrestling Open RI. Cordeiro described Rhodes On The Pawtuxet in Cranston as the nicest venue Beyond Wrestling has ever run and one with the most fan amenities encountered.

body: DMFirst Veer Game odds uden om ROFUS Jalwa Game Goa Game Raja Game MaanWin TNA'S BLESSING AND CURSE, BOWENS-AEW, WHY WWE CAN'T JUST CANCEL CROWN JEWEL AND LET INSURANCE COVER AND MORE By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-29 10:00:00 Any update on Anthony Bowens? His profile is still on the AEW roster page so is it possible he's resigned? We never reported he was gone from the company. To the best of my knowledge, he's still there. All of this talk of moving Crown Jewel got me thinking. Obviously, it's monstrously stupid to keep going ahead with the show in Saudi, but clearly the reason is financial. On that note, however, shouldn't a business like WWE have suitable insurance in place for situations like this, where outside circumstances force them to cancel a lucrative show? body: Throughout her time in WWE, Becker had a bit of an on screen rivalry with Paul Heyman. Most of their bickering came to fruition through the Talking Smack show, which returned in August 2020. At the same time, Heyman was just beginning his partnership with Roman Reigns. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, Becker said that Heyman paved the way for everybody in wrestling with a microphone. “It was great. Listen, we all know Paul paved the way for all of us microphone holders. It was really cool to get to spend that much like close time with him over the years. He taught me a lot. Did he get on my nerves all the freaking time? But hey, I love that man, thankful for him all the time.” Later on in the interview, Becker was asked to name people in WWE that made her laugh. Of course, Heyman’s name came up again. “Obviously Paul. Bayley was very hard. Zelina Vega / Thea. Sami Zayn or Kevin Owens, easily. I think one of my last interviews with Kevin Owens, we were in Paris before a pay-per-view. We got to walk around. It was literally trying to keep a kid with me. Like, ‘Stay focused here,’ he was like chasing down baguettes and ducks the entire time. One thing they teach you at NXT is you have to breathe through those moments because it is so hard not to laugh. Because these guys and girls are hilarious. They’re hilarious.” Elsewhere in the interview, Becker spoke about people from WWE still reaching out to her. Check out her full comments by clicking here.

title: Elayna Black Recalls Boyfriend Leaving Her, Dog Dying and WWE Firing Her as Life Fell Apart
raw_title: Elayna Black Recalls Boyfriend Leaving Her, Dog Dying and WWE Firing Her as Life Fell Apart
summary_src: Elayna Black says she reached a point where she was afraid to care about anything because everything she loved kept disappearing. Her boyfriend left her, her dog died, and then WWE fired her. By the time that phone call came, the former Cora Jade says she felt like she had absolutely nothing left.
body: In a documentary published on TNA Wrestling’s YouTube channel , Black revisited the string of personal losses that surrounded the end of her WWE career. While she’d previously discussed her serious health problems and the fallout from her release, this time she connected everything that had happened and explained just how badly it affected her. As Ringside News previously covered in June 2025 , Black suffered an ectopic pregnancy in January 2023 that caused internal bleeding and required emergency surgery. She later struggled with severe depression, and her mother had to help care for her during that period. Black also suffered a devastating knee injury in January 2024, tearing her ACL, MCL, and both meniscuses during a WWE live event against Lyra Valkyria. But those weren’t the only problems she was dealing with. Black revealed that her relationship also ended and her dog died, leaving her with one personal loss after another before WWE ultimately released her in May 2025. She summed up that entire stretch of her life without holding anything back. “Ectopic pregnancy, boyfriend leaves me, lose my knee, dog dies. And then, I got fired a few months later.” Black admitted that she eventually became so terrified of losing anything else that she started pretending nothing mattered to her. It was easier to convince herself she didn’t care than to risk having another important part of her life taken away. That changed when WWE fired her. Wrestling had been her entire identity since childhood, and even after everything else she’d lost, she wasn’t prepared for what losing her job would do to her. “I didn’t I was so scared of losing anything else that mattered to me that I didn’t want to pretend like anything mattered to me. So, when I got fired, inside I was like, ‘Oh, holy s ** I just I’ve lost the literal last thing. Like, I have lost everything. This was the very last thing and now I’ve lost this. I literally have nothing.'”* The release itself wasn’t completely unexpected. Black previously admitted she had a feeling WWE was going to let her go , even though she’d been featured prominently on NXT television. What made it worse was that wrestling was the one thing she’d spent her entire life working toward, and now that was gone too. Black eventually stepped away from professional wrestling in July 2025 , admitting at the time that the business was no longer good for her mental health. She didn’t know whether she’d ever get back the love she once had for wrestling, and continuing to force herself into the ring wasn’t helping. In the documentary, Black explained that she had reached a point where she was questioning why she was still wrestling at all. She was having anxiety attacks before matches and beating herself up over her performances afterward. “For a while I asked myself, I’m like, why am I doing this? Because I’m having anxiety attacks before I go out. I usually hate my matches and then afterwards I feel like s ** because I hated my match. Duri

She was still trying to figure out who she was, how to carry herself around the company, and whether people were judging her every move. Throw a public relationship into that situation, and things got even more uncomfortable. Black admitted she wasn’t nearly as confident as people might have assumed from watching her on NXT. Behind the character, she was constantly worried about saying the wrong thing, doing something that might upset somebody, or being perceived negatively. “I got signed when I was 19. So, I think for a while, honestly, like my first few years there, I was very worried about being perceived a certain way or like how people were going to view me or doing something the wrong way or saying something the wrong way and kind of like walking on eggshells because I wasn’t fully confident in myself and my work.” Then came her first public relationship during her WWE career, and that’s when Black says she finally understood just how little privacy came with being a recognizable wrestler. She wasn’t doing anything particularly unusual. She was dating, having fun, and sharing parts of her life on social media like plenty of other people her age. The difference was that everything she posted suddenly became something wrestling fans and news websites wanted to dissect. “I feel like the first time I kind of realized that all eyes were on me at all times was when I was kind of in my first public relationship when I first got into WWE.” “I was just living my life, having fun, you know, showing my life, and then, you know, slowly you start to realize, oh s ** like everyone’s eyes are on you, everyone has an opinion, everyone wants to say something, every everything you post is a dirt sheet, like that first year in WWE was the kind of the first time I realized like damn, people have people have a lot to say like about everything.”* Black knows exactly what that kind of attention looks like. title: Grayson Waller Eyes WWE Title After Near-Release Scare
raw_title: Grayson Waller feared release after New Day’s exit, now focused on WWE Championship ambitions
summary_src: Grayson Waller’s outlook on long-term ambitions has changed with his determination to prove his worth and becoming a potential WWE Champion someday. On the Insight Podcast, Waller affirmed he is ready now more than ever to pursue the WWE Championship.
body: Grayson Waller’s outlook on long-term ambitions has changed with his determination to prove his worth and becoming a potential WWE Champion someday. On the Insight Podcast , Waller affirmed he is ready now more than ever to pursue the WWE Championship. He credits revamping his persona and being perceived as a serious competitor a major attribution to the goal. “100% (aspire to be WWE Champion now). I think now I’ve established myself as a different person. Now I’m taking things seriously. I’m ticking a lot of the boxes that weren’t ticked for a long time. So when I do come back to the main roster, I hope they’re ready for what I’m bringing, because I see a gap. I see a gap in the market for a guy like Grayson Waller.” Waller was convinced WWE would release him after the New Day and squash match against Oba Femi on an edition of Raw earlier this year. The situation became concerning when he did not have a meaningful presence on WWE TV. “100% (thought would be released). I could feel it, especially when the New Day left. I could feel it because when the New Day left, Oba destroyed me. He’s a very big man, very strong, and just beaten Lesnar. So I think he was very confident going into that match. Maybe I wasn’t prepared enough for Oba Femi, but then when I didn’t do anything for like another month, was not a great position to be in. I’m smart enough to know; I’m not going to pretend. I’m real enough to know.” “I know I have a lot of value to the company, but in that position, there’s other people who could also add that value. So I had to do something because I’m not going to sit back and let my dream disappear. If I didn’t do something about it, that would upset me if I didn’t do something.” Following New Day’s WWE exit in May, Waller made his NXT comeback in July with a heated promo calling out the roster and management. At Heatwave, Waller defeated Tony D’Angelo, Cruz Montana, and Zilla Fatu for the NXT Championship. The duo had been aligned with Waller on television although they were not featured prominently on a weekly basis. He then disappeared from television until appearing on NXT at the end of July. During that appearance Waller called out the NXT roster and expressed his grievances.

That moment launched his current run as NXT Champion. In an interview with Chris Van Vliet on Insight, Waller confirmed he believed he was close to being released prior to his NXT return. Waller noted that Oba Femi had just beaten Brock Lesnar and entered their match with confidence.

Waller admitted he may not have been prepared enough for the bout against the much larger opponent. Following the defeat he remained off television for about a month, a situation he recognized as precarious.

title: On the Record: Chris Jericho Opens Up On He Personally Approves Every Wrestler Booked for His Cruise
raw_title: Chris Jericho Reveals He Personally Approves Every Wrestler Booked for His Cruise
summary_src: Chris Jericho isn’t letting just anybody step aboard his wrestling cruise.
body: During a recent interview with Skratch N’ Sniff , Jericho opened up about the work that goes into organizing his annual wrestling cruise. With the seventh edition approaching, he explained that the event is much more than a wrestling show on a boat. It’s an entire entertainment experience featuring live wrestling, rock bands, comedians, magicians, and even paranormal attractions. Jericho made it clear that the biggest factor in deciding who gets booked isn’t necessarily how popular someone is. Instead, he wants entertainers who can contribute to the nonstop party atmosphere he’s built around the event. “Well, when we came up with the idea for the Rock and Wrestling Rager, I mean, it’s wrestling combined with music combined with comedy, there’s paranormal elements to it, there’s magicians, there’s traveling minstrels.” The AEW star explained that he even turns down certain types of music despite being a fan of them himself. According to Jericho, the entire event needs to have a particular energy, and he isn’t interested in booking acts that could disrupt that atmosphere. “And the the biggest thing for me is I just want a party. I want party music that people can dance to and have fun to. You know, I love thrash metal, but I’ll I’ll probably never put a thrash metal band on the cruise because it just doesn’t fit the vibe of what we want.” That’s when Jericho revealed just how much control he maintains over the cruise’s entertainment lineup. Rather than leaving those decisions entirely to promoters or booking agents, he personally screens everyone involved, including the professional wrestlers. “So every, you know, and I book everybody, like everybody that’s on the cruise, every band, every wrestler, every comedian, I vetted and know kind of what their vibe is.” Jericho explained that his goal is to make sure guests are constantly surrounded by entertainment, regardless of where they are on the ship. That approach has helped the Rock ‘N’ Wrestling Rager reach its seventh edition, and he revealed that plans for an eighth cruise are already being discussed. “I just want everywhere that people go, their senses are being bombarded by a party vibe. And that’s why we’ve been able to do seven of them with an eighth one, you know, kind of in the works already.” The cruise’s entertainment lineup reflects that philosophy, with Fozzy headlining alongside acts such as Guardians of the Jukebox, The Iron Maidens, The Killer Dwarfs, and Downstait. Jericho explained that he deliberately mixes different styles of music to keep the experience entertaining for everyone attending. For Jericho, the Rock ‘N’ Wrestling Rager isn’t simply another opportunity to put on wrestling matches or perform with Fozzy. He’s treating the entire cruise as his own production, right down to deciding which wrestlers and entertainers belong on the ship. With a potential eighth edition already being considered, it doesn’t sound like Jericho plans to hand over those responsibilities anytime

title: Will Ospreay Explains Bringing Back Black Arrow After Pac's Death
raw_title: AEW World Champion Will Ospreay Looks Back On Performing Black Arrow For PAC
summary_src: Will Ospreay has explained his decision to perform the Black Arrow following Pac's death and revealed that he was scared to perform the move on AEW Dynamite.
body: AEW Will Ospreay has discussed his decision to perform the Black Arrow following the passing of fellow AEW star Pac . The passing of Pac left the pro wrestling community in shock, none more so than those who shared the ring with him often in AEW. Ospreay wanted to pay tribute in his own way by performing the Black Arrow, which was a signature move of Pac's, in his match with Ricochet on "AEW Dynamite." The English star revealed in a recent interview with Brandon Kravitz how he had to relearn the move, which he had put away years ago due to how dangerous it was. "After we lost him, we had the tribute match with myself and Ricochet. The amount of people that are hoping that one of us could pull off the Black Arrow, and I used to do it like years and years ago, but I haven't done it for years because it was just — I nearly didn't make the move, it had spooked me, and I never wanted to go near it again," he explained. The AEW World Champion said that performing the move would give him, his peers, and fans an "emotional release" as they processed the news of Pac's death. Ospreay added that he hadn't performed the move in its entirety until his match against Ricochet. "I couldn't get it off the top rope [when practising]. I was too scared. So, when I did it [in the match], that was the first time I had ever done it for, like, eight years. So, it was for me to be able to give not only the wrestlers backstage a little bit of a release, but fans a release. And I think that was something that made me so proud to be champion and so proud to be part of the roster," added Ospreay. He revealed that he was on his way to attend a Michael Jackson show in Vegas but changed his mind after learning of Pac's death, returning to his room to mourn the loss of his friend and cry.
summary: AEW World Champion Will Ospreay discussed paying tribute to Pac by performing his signature Black Arrow during the match against Ricochet on AEW Dynamite. Ospreay revealed in an interview that he had stopped using the move years earlier because of its danger but felt it was necessary to relearn it for the tribute bout. He described the moment as providing an emotional release for himself, fellow wrestlers, and fans following the loss of Pac.

title: Paul Heyman Claims Diverticulitis Prevented Lesnar's UFC Undefeated Run
raw_title: Paul Heyman: If It Wasn't For Diverticulitis, Brock Lesnar Would Still Be Undefeated In The UFC
summary_src: Paul Heyman has a strong take about Brock Lesnar. After his first run with WWE, 'The Beast' decided to turn his attention to the UFC. He quickly found success, winning the UFC Heavyweight Championship in just his fourth fight.
body: After his first run with WWE, ‘The Beast’ decided to turn his attention to the UFC. He quickly found success, winning the UFC Heavyweight Championship in just his fourth fight. He would hold the title for nearly two years before losing it to Cain Velasquez in October 2010. During his time with the promotion, Brock Lesnar battled a severe case of diverticulitis. In a recent interview with Graham Bensinger, Paul Heyman claimed that Lesnar would have remained an undefeated UFC champion had it not been for his health issues. “It’s one of those things, it’s just magic. It’s lightning in a bottle. He was my Aryan and I was his Jew. His name was perfect, what a name. Brock Lesnar, you don’t have to make up a name. He is the greatest athlete on the face of the planet and the only reason why he doesn’t get the credit he deserves is number one, there is a preconceived notion of what a professional wrestler is. Number two, because diverticulitis robbed him of so much more great athletic accomplishment. If he didn’t have diverticulitis, he would’ve never been defeated in UFC. Never. He’d still be champion today at 49. There’s nobody on this planet that could hang with him, no one. No one would get out of the first round with him, there’s no way.” Speaking about a separate part of Lesnar’s athletic career, Heyman explained why the Minnesota Vikings were hesitant to release his combine numbers. “He went out for the Minnesota Vikings training camp, they were reluctant to release to the media his combine numbers because he came out of WWE. The Minnesota Vikings were concerned that the media would think this is a WWE stunt with these numbers, because whether it was the 40 yard dash or the 100 yard dash or the quarter mile or the standing jump or whatever it was, his combine numbers were of Olympic qualifying time. At 6″3, 285 pounds and six weeks before training camp, right after leaving WWE, he flipped his motorcycle at like 90 or 100 miles an hour in Minnesota. He tore his groin and he fractured his pelvis and he tore everything all the way down to his knees and he broke his jaw. They had to wire his jaw shut. So, he cut the wires off of his jaw so he could eat and maintain body weight. He showed up at training camp recovering from a fractured pelvis, a torn groin, and everything else. He was beyond black and purple from the stomach down to the knees.” Brock Lesnar retired from in-ring competition at WWE SummerSlam in August. He lost to Oba Femi in his final bout. Speaking with Fightful, Conrad Thompson noted that he wants to do a podcast with Paul Heyman. Check out his full comments by clicking here. title: Vince Russo Comments On Reported WWE Talks
raw_title: Vince Russo gives sharp response to reports of WWE talks
summary_src: Vince Russo addressed the reports that he was recently in talks about returning to WWE’s creative team, but he didn’t give wrestling fans much insight.
body: Link Vince Russo’s Instagram Vince Russo addressed the reports that he was recently in talks about returning to WWE’s creative team, but he didn’t give wrestling fans much insight. Podcaster/mortgage broker Conrad Thompson was the first to claim Russo had met with WWE this past summer about possibly coming back to WWE after 27 years away from the company. Russo was with WWE when it hit a popular stride in the late 1990s, and he frequently gives himself a lot of credit for the Attitude Era. In 1999, he jumped ship to WCW, but his stint in that promotion ended in ugly fashion. Since that time, Russo has worked with TNA and Juggalo Championship Wrestling (JCW), as well as hosted podcasts. However, according to Conrad in a column for Uncrowned at Yahoo Sports , WWE President Nick Khan at least entertained the idea of a Russo return to WWE during a “series of conversations” the two men had. Thompson added that nothing came of the talks, and that when followed up with his sources on the topic “a few weeks ago, I was told it ‘died on the vine.’” Rumors later said numerous WWE employees hadn’t heard about meetings between Khan and Russo, adding these sources “completely laughed it off”, but that others “heard Nick Khan had conversations with Vince Russo, but aren’t sure how serious they were”. Another outlet reported it was Russo who initially contacted Khan — and not the other way around — and that there was never any serious progression. On Russo’s newest podcast, The Coach & Bro Show with Jonathan Coachman, the controversial New York native broke his silence about the reports. “I am reading all kinds of rumors about me from everybody,” Russo said before naming some of the sources of those rumors, like Thompson and Sapp. He continued: “First of all, let me be perfectly clear: None of those people contacted me. None of those people tried to contact me, and all of those people have my number. All of those people. And guys, let me tell you right now, don’t try to contact me now because I’ve stated this already, and now it’s too late. “I want to make it clear to the audience listening to this show, because this is all I care about. I do not lie. I am transparent. You know everything there is to know about me.” Though Russo did not confirm nor deny the reports, he did say: “What I’m saying is right now there is nothing for me to talk about. I have nothing to talk about right now. If that changes, Coach, and there is something I need to talk about, this audience is going to be the first one to know. It’s that simple, and I just want to make that perfectly clear.” Before he wrapped up his comments on the subject, though, Russo did throw some shots on the people who made the reports about him allegedly speaking with WWE. “When you’re running with stories and you don’t contact the subject of those stories, Bro, I’m sorry, you’re a hack,” he said. “I don’t know how else to put it. You’re a hack, and you’re not properly doing your job. Plain and simple.” What do

title: D-Von Dudley Defends Max Caster After TNA Release
raw_title: WWE HOFer D-Von Dudley Comments On TNA Firing Max Caster After Controversial Debut
summary_src: WWE legend D-Von Dudley is hopeful that Max Caster can turn his career around and has assessed the controversial promo that got him fired from TNA.
body: AEW/YouTube D-Von Dudley has backed Max Caster, following his dismissal from TNA Wrestling after a controversial rap. Caster was let go on the night of his TNA debut after delivering a rap that ridiculed the bombings in Saudi Arabia. On his podcast , D-Von Dudley said that pro wrestling promos are different today than they were in the past, arguing that society has become soft and will silence anyone who says anything mildly controversial. "You go back to the Attitude Era, you go back to the Hogan and Andre Era, even the Bruno Sammartino Era. Things that were said in the promos, nowadays [it] would get you kicked off the air, would get you silenced, would get you excommunicated from everything. And it seems to me that society has gotten soft," he said. "Now, they hit home. You know, they'll talk about your wife, your kids, your dog, you know, hell, even you dying, them pi**ing on your grave." The Hall of Famer said that social media amplifies every little thing and that, in his opinion, the incident was insignificant. He expressed sympathy for Caster and hopes the former AEW star can return to pro wrestling. "So, when I heard about it, I looked at the video and saw it, and I'll be honest with you, I really wouldn't have paid it any mind if the subtitles weren't down below saying what he said," he added. "It's sad. Max, my heart really goes out to you and your family because you truly did your best. You knocked it out of the park. You did great. And I hope and pray that we see you back at 100%. And if you are going for therapy or what have you, that's fine. Get yourself right." He reassured Caster that the pro wrestling community is backing him, and he thanked him for everything he has done for the pro wrestling business.
summary: WWE Hall of Famer D-Von Dudley voiced support for Max Caster after TNA fired him on the night of his debut for a rap that mocked the Saudi Arabia bombings. On his podcast, Dudley argued that modern society has grown overly sensitive and that promos from the Attitude Era, Hogan and Andre era, or Bruno Sammartino era would now result in immediate cancellation. He added that social media magnifies minor issues and expressed sympathy for Caster, viewing the controversy as insignificant.

kind.quote: It seems to me that society has gotten soft.

llm_long: D-Von Dudley has come to the defense of Max Caster following Caster's release from TNA Wrestling. Caster was dismissed from the promotion on the same night as his TNA debut after performing a controversial rap that mocked the bombings in Saudi Arabia.

On his podcast, D-Von Dudley explained that professional wrestling promos have changed significantly from previous eras and argued that society has become soft, leading to the silencing of anyone who says anything mildly controversial. Dudley pointed out that content from the Attitude Era, the Hogan and Andre Era, and even the Bruno Sammartino Era would now result in being kicked off the air, silenced, or excommunicated from everything.

The WWE Hall of Famer noted that modern promos hit home by discussing personal topics including someone's wife, kids, dog, or even death and desecration of a grave. Dudley stated that social media amplifies every minor incident and described the entire matter involving Caster as insignificant.

He expressed sympathy for Caster, saying his heart goes out to him and his family because Caster did his best, knocked it out of the park, and performed greatly. Dudley added that he hopes and prays to see Caster back at 100 percent and reassured him that the pro wrestling community is supporting him while thanking him for his contributions to the business.

title: Steve Maclin Praises Working With Rhino

summary_src: Steve Maclin comments on Rhino. One of the wrestlers Steve Maclin has shared the ring with multiple times is Rhino. They had a series of matches against each other in TNA Wrestling back in 2022.
body: One of the wrestlers Steve Maclin has shared the ring with multiple times is Rhino. They had a series of matches against each other in TNA Wrestling back in 2022. They also worked together in MLP recently. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp, Maclin shared the following about Rhino. “I love working with Rhino, just because it’s ECW, it’s WWE, that nostalgia feeling for me of guys that I’ve watched and here I am throwing ideas at them and like, ‘Oh, yeah, I like that.’ Dude, it’s still surreal to be able to do that. Because normally the old ways is you just sit there and you shut your mouth and you listen to what the veteran wants to do and you do what they [say]. But here I am with two guys that are willing to do anything and have the faith in me and the trust in me too. It just speaks volumes and I can’t thank them enough for the opportunity.” Elsewhere in the interview, he talked about planning his match against Adam Copeland at MLP Northern Rising. Fans can read his full comments by clicking here . Fans can also check out the two-part documentary highlighting Maclin’s journey to MLP’s Northern Rising on the Boots To Boots YouTube channel .

body: During what’s been a busy contract season for TNA Wrestling, an on-screen character reportedly could be departing the promotion. PWInsider reported this week that George Iceman, who has been the “Personal Concierge” for the Elegance Brand, is likely to exit TNA with his contract expiring in early November. False Finish noted that there’s been some interest in Iceman from outside of TNA, though that report did not name which promotion (or promotions) is interested. The Elegance Brand consist of Ash By Elegance (former WWE wrestler Dana Brooke), M By Elegance (Maggie Lee), Heather By Elegance (Heather Reckless), Mr. Elegance (Andreas John Ziegler), and The Personal Concierge (Iceman). The faction has achieved championship success during their run, including M By Elegance currently holding the Knockouts TV title as the inaugural champion. Iceman did not appear in a backstage segment with M By Elegance, Heather By Elegance, and Mr. Elegance on Impact last week. Before taking on this role, Iceman hosted a segment on TNA’s Before the Impact pre-show. He is from Canada and has promoted indie wrestling in the country The end of the year is when TNA has a lot of contracts coming due. The promotion has signed Shotzi Blackheart , Amazing Red , and Shayna Baszler in recent weeks, along with re-signing Director of Authority Santino Marella . Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

title: SmackDown Nearly Shifted For WNBA Finals
raw_title: WWE SmackDown Broadcast Was Reportedly Almost Moved To Accommodate WNBA Finals
summary_src: The WNBA Finals has sold out Game 6 and the WNBA was trying to find a time to schedule the game. WWE SmackDown was nearly moved to help out.
body: WWE has had a working relationship with the NBA with various basketball players appearing on WWE programming over the years. This year, Danhausen uncursed the New York Knicks before they went on a historic run to win the NBA Championship and Karl- Anthony Towns helped Danhausen at Saturday Night's Main Event . It seems that relationship extends to the WNBA. ESPN's Ramona Shelburne reported that "SmackDown" nearly moved this week's show to accommodate Game 6 of WNBA Finals. Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO Steve Koonin reached out to Nick Khan to ask if he'd consider moving "SmackDown" one hour later. Shelburne wrote on X (formerly Twitter): "Koonin, the former President of TBS, had known Khan for decades. Khan told him they'd be fine with the later broadcast window if that's what was needed to help the WNBA Finals play in a more appropriate arena. After that sign off however, new concerns were raised by WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert about playing a potential Game 7 on Tuesday, Nov. 3, Election Night. So that plan fell apart and the league moved back on to the idea of playing at 12:30 pm on Thursday." Smackdown will remain at its regularly scheduled time. The Dream announced earlier Wednesday that Thursday's Game 6 is sold out." Fun little aside: During the frantic negotiations over the weekend, an unlikely ally emerged– the @WWE . At one point, sources told ESPN that Steve Koonin Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO reached out to WWE President Nick Khan and asked if he'd be willing to move the... Friday's show will be hosted by Danhausen and called the "Very Nice, Very Evil SmackDown". Women's Champion Chelsea Green will defend her title against Nikki Bella. Men's U.S. Champion Trick Williams will challenge Sami Zayn for his Undisputed WWE Championship. On Saturday, Danhausen will host "NXT" Halloween Havoc.
summary: Per ESPN's Ramona Shelburne, Atlanta Hawks CEO Steve Koonin contacted WWE President Nick Khan about potentially moving this week's SmackDown one hour later to allow Game 6 of the WNBA Finals to take place at State Farm Arena. Khan agreed to the later broadcast window if it would help the league. The plan was ultimately scrapped after WNBA Commissioner Cathy Engelbert raised concerns about a possible Game 7 falling on Election Night, leading the league to abandon the arena change.

llm_long: WWE nearly stepped in to resolve a scheduling conflict involving game six of the WNBA Finals between the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries. The game had become a national story as the NBA, WNBA, multiple arenas and other parties worked to place it in prime time at State Farm Arena.

Instead the contest was set for Thursday at 12:30 pm Eastern. According to ESPN reporter Ramona Shelburne, Atlanta Hawks and State Farm Arena CEO Steve Koonin, a former WWE board member, reached out to WWE president Nick Khan. Koonin asked if WWE would shift this Friday’s SmackDown to a 9 pm Eastern start so the WNBA game could air on USA from 7-9 pm Eastern at the preferred venue.

Khan, who has known Koonin for decades, responded that WWE would be fine with the later broadcast window if it helped the WNBA Finals secure a more appropriate arena. The proposed solution was ultimately dropped because it would have placed a potential game seven on Tuesday opposite Election Night coverage.

body: TEAM TENSHIN, the organization that supports former MMA fighter, kickboxer, and current boxer Tenshin Nasukawa, is holding a festival on October 31st at Matsudo Central Park in Chiba, Japan. A collaboration with DDT Pro-Wrestling was advertised, and it would feature Nasukawa competing in ‘street pro wrestling.’ He was set to team with three-time KO-D Openweight Champion Yuki Ueno and Shinya Aoki in a six-man tag team match. As the news began to spread, the Japan Boxing Commission issued a statement, and it was announced that Nasukawa would no longer be competing on the show. Their regulations prevent pro boxers from participating in other combat sports, matches, or events. Nasukawa has an 8-2 record in boxing. He retired from kickboxing in 2022 with a 42-0 record.

The Japan Boxing Commission stepped in and canceled his participation, citing regulations that bar pro boxers from competing in other combat sports or events. title: By the Numbers: Tony D’Angelo Claims WWE Blames NXT Champion When TV Ratings Are Low
raw_title: Tony D’Angelo Claims WWE Blames NXT Champion When TV Ratings Are Low
summary_src: Tony D’Angelo just revealed that being WWE NXT Champion comes with a pretty uncomfortable responsibility — when the show’s television ratings aren’t doing well, he’s the first person WWE looks at.
body: During an appearance on the Battleground Podcast, D’Angelo was asked what he learned about being NXT Champion after winning the title at Stand & Deliver. That’s when he explained that the job involves a lot more than defending the championship. The person holding the title is expected to carry the brand, and that apparently includes answering for the show’s television numbers. D’Angelo admitted that being champion was far more stressful than he expected because everything eventually comes back to the person at the top. “Uh, you know, well a lot comes with it. Um you’re you’re the guy you know what I mean? The brand is on your shoulders. You know you’re the at the forefront of everything at commercials, media, uh you know all this stuff. And it it’s a lot more stressful because, you know, I’m trying to be PC here, but um crap rolls downhill.” He then got straight to the issue of television ratings, explaining that when NXT isn’t delivering the numbers WWE wants, he’s the person who gets looked at first. “So, uh you know, if the show’s not, you know, doing numbers or whatever, who’s the first person they look at? It’s me.” That’s a pretty revealing admission from someone who actually held the championship. D’Angelo didn’t say WWE executives directly blamed him for every disappointing rating, but he certainly made it clear that the responsibility landed on his shoulders whenever the show’s numbers weren’t where they needed to be. Despite that pressure, D’Angelo said he understood why WWE expected so much from him. He specifically mentioned Shawn Michaels and the confidence NXT management had in his ability to handle the position. “So, which is fine, you know, and I appreciate Sean and everybody, you know, telling me that, you know, my shoulders are strong enough to to carry it and that’s why they did that and that’s why I won. So, I’m okay with that. But, for sure, there’s a lot that goes on uh that you don’t really know until you’re champion.” The revelation raises an interesting question about how much responsibility WWE puts on the wrestlers at the top of NXT. Television ratings are influenced by everything from creative decisions and storylines to the overall presentation of the show, yet D’Angelo says the champion is the first person under scrutiny when those numbers aren’t performing. D’Angelo might have accepted that responsibility, but his comments make it clear that carrying the NXT Championship isn’t just about being the top wrestler on Tuesday nights. When WWE’s television numbers aren’t meeting expectations, the person wearing the title can find themselves answering for a problem that’s much bigger than any single wrestler. title: Elayna Black Says She Didn’t Care Who Paid the Most After WWE Fired Her

summary_src: Elayna Black wasn’t interested in starting a bidding war after WWE fired her.
body: In a documentary published on TNA Wrestling’s YouTube channel , Black explained that her decision to return to wrestling came with one major condition. Wherever she ended up, she needed to be somewhere that wasn’t going to make her mental health worse. Another big contract wasn’t worth putting herself through the same misery again. “Being in the mental state that I was in and kind of just realizing everything I had been through for the last 2 years, I knew that I wanted to end up somewhere that wasn’t going to make my mental health any worse.” And when it came to money, Black wasn’t remotely subtle. She made it clear that financial offers weren’t going to dictate her next move, even after losing the WWE job she’d spent her childhood dreaming about. “I didn’t care about the money. I didn’t care about who was going to pay me the most. I did not care about any of that. I just wanted to love wrestling again.” This wasn’t the first time Black addressed her decision to join TNA. As Ringside News previously covered in March 2026 , she explained that TNA’s creative freedom, backstage environment, and willingness to listen to her ideas helped seal the deal. She also admitted that immediately after WWE released her, she wasn’t even interested in signing somewhere else. But her latest comments make the stakes of that decision much clearer. Black wasn’t simply looking for more creative control or better opportunities on television. She was trying to avoid putting herself back into an environment that could wreck her emotionally. Black had already stepped away from professional wrestling in July 2025 , after reaching a point where the business wasn’t making her happy anymore. She later returned on TNA’s January 15, 2026, AMC debut, before officially announcing her signing on January 28 . The former WWE star explained that landing in TNA finally gave her a feeling she hadn’t experienced in a long time. Instead of questioning whether she belonged in wrestling anymore, she felt like she’d found the right place to start over. “For the first time in a long time, I felt like this is where I’m supposed to be, which took a long f ** time to get here, but here we are.”* Black’s comments also put a different spin on the usual conversation about wrestlers jumping companies for better contracts. She had already lived out her dream of making it to WWE, only to reach a point where she was questioning whether she wanted to wrestle at all. Whatever another promotion might have been willing to pay, she wasn’t interested in sacrificing her mental health to find out. Black now has a spot in TNA’s Knockouts division and another opportunity to build the wrestling career she once feared she’d lost. title: Tony D’Angelo Underwent Speech Therapy After Changing His WWE Character
raw_title: Tony D’Angelo Underwent Speech Therapy After Changing His WWE Character
summary_src: Tony D’Angelo didn’t just ditch the suits when he moved on from The Don. He actually had to go to speech therapy because his old WWE character had become so ingrained that even the way he talked needed some work.
body: Speaking on the Battleground Podcast , D’Angelo was asked what habit from his old mob-boss character was the hardest to leave behind. As it turns out, it was the accent he had spent years using as part of the gimmick. “Well, you know, I had to go to speech therapy because I had a little bit of an accent.” Once WWE started moving D’Angelo into the next evolution of his character, he had to consciously remind himself not to slip back into that familiar way of speaking. After playing The Don for so long, simply changing his voice wasn’t something he could immediately switch off. “So when I started the new evolution of Tony, I had to keep reminding myself and hold my tongue. That was the biggest thing, for sure.” The changes went beyond how D’Angelo sounded. He also stopped wearing suits because he wanted a clear separation between the new version of himself and the mob-boss character fans had gotten used to seeing. “But I stopped wearing suits. I wanted to separate myself from that other guy. And I was just telling Mark Henry that I also wanted to show versatility.” For D’Angelo, the whole change was also about proving he wasn’t stuck playing one type of character. He already showed WWE he could handle the more character-heavy material, but he also wanted people backstage to know he could work as a straight-up badass if that’s what they needed. “I can do the character stuff. I can go that route if you need me to, but I can also be a badass and fit into that role.” Ultimately, D’Angelo wants WWE’s decision-makers to know they have options with him. Whether they want another heavily defined character or something completely different, he feels this evolution has allowed him to show a lot more of what he can actually do. “So it’s just showing everybody what I’m capable of, and then the powers that be, whatever they want to do with me, they know what I’m capable of.” Going to speech therapy just to leave an old wrestling character behind shows how seriously D’Angelo took the change. The Don wasn’t simply a suit he could take off, and he clearly wanted the next version of Tony D’Angelo to feel different instead of looking like the same guy with a slightly updated presentation. title: On the Record: Orange Cassidy Opens Up On the Real Reason He Wrestles With His Hands in His Pockets
raw_title: Orange Cassidy Reveals the Real Reason He Wrestles With His Hands in His Pockets
summary_src: Orange Cassidy has made a career out of doing things in the wrestling ring that most people wouldn’t even attempt — including fighting opponents with his hands stuffed inside his pockets.
body: During a recent interview on Going Ringside , Cassidy was asked about his unusual wrestling style and how he manages to keep his balance while performing moves without using his hands. Host Scott Johnson wanted to know whether keeping his hands in his pockets creates legitimate difficulties during matches. Cassidy admitted that it’s nowhere near as easy as he makes it look. In fact, he challenged people to try doing everyday activities with their hands stuck in their pockets to understand how difficult it can be. “Oh, yeah, for sure. I mean, think about like try doing stuff with your hands in your pockets. It’s not, it’s not easy.” But Cassidy wasn’t finished explaining himself. He revealed that the whole thing is actually part of his strategy inside the ring. By keeping his hands in his pockets, he wants opponents to believe they’ve got an easy opportunity to take advantage of him. That’s when he catches them off guard. “Uh, that’s why I don’t keep them in the entire time. I just do, I just, I just use the, I put my hands in my pockets to kind of disarm the person I’m fighting so that they think they can get the advantage of me. But then, uh, it’s when I take them out of my pockets and I punch them in the face.” So there you have it. What looks like Cassidy being too lazy to fight is actually his way of getting opponents to lower their guard before he starts throwing punches. It’s a signature part of Cassidy’s character that has followed him throughout his AEW career. Whether he’s standing across from someone twice his size or going toe-to-toe with another top star, the hands-in-pockets routine has become one of the things that separates him from everyone else on the roster. And while plenty of wrestlers have questioned his unusual approach over the years, Cassidy clearly sees it as more than just a comedy routine. In his mind, there’s a tactical advantage to making someone think he isn’t taking the fight seriously. title: Stardom Continues Weekday Big Event Tests
raw_title: Stardom president to continue testing new event strategy
summary_src: Stardom President Taro Okada is planning to continue testing out his strategy of holding some of the company’s big events on weekdays rather than weekends.
body: Stardom President Taro Okada is planning to continue testing out his strategy of holding some of the company’s big events on weekdays rather than weekends. On Thursday (October 29), the women’s promotion held a show at Ota City General Gymnasium in Tokyo headlined by Suzu Suzuki retaining the World of Stardom Championship over Starlight Kid. An attendance of 1,994 was announced, with Tokyo Sports noting that this was just shy of the target (2,000) that was set. Okada said there are fans who can’t attend weekend shows, and those people have thanked him for giving them the chance to come to big matches on weekdays. He believes appealing to both weekend and weekday audiences will help Stardom reach more fans — and the only way to test that theory is to keep offering customers options. “In order for us to move to the next stage, we need to fill weekday events as well,” Okada said. “And we need to be able to meet the needs of all kinds of customers as much as possible so that people will choose Stardom. I think it won’t become established unless we persevere. We want to continue looking for opportunities to do so.” Stardom has five major weekday events on its October-November calendar, with this October 29 show having been a pay-per-view. The card also included Natsupoi, who is retiring from the ring soon , teaming with her husband Shingo Takagi to defeat Yuna Mizumori & Hirooki Goto. As president, one of Okada’s biggest goals for Stardom is to hold a show at the Tokyo Dome one day. He’s focused his international expansion strategy on partnering with other promotions rather than Stardom holding its own shows in international markets. Stardom has also looked to expand its reach by offering English commentary for select events and establishing a global YouTube channel . Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.

The October 29 event at Ota City General Gymnasium in Tokyo drew an announced attendance of 1,994, headlined by Suzu Suzuki retaining the World of Stardom Championship against Starlight Kid, narrowly missing the 2,000-fan target. Okada noted positive feedback from weekday attendees and stressed that filling those shows is necessary to grow the promotion and meet varied customer needs.

title: Jimmy House Thanks Gabe Sapolsky For WWE Opportunity
raw_title: Jimmy House Credits Gabe Sapolsky For Opening The Door To WWE For Him
summary_src: Jimmy House discusses his journey to WWE ID. Before joining the program in March, House participated in tryout for WWE in January. Before that, he had been in contact with the company for years.
body: Before joining the program in March, House participated in tryout for WWE in January. Before that, he had been in contact with the company for years. “So my personal story with my tryout actually starts about four years prior to that where I got my black belt in jiu-itsu and that was, in a way, a chapter closed for me because I wanted to use that success on top of some of the other things I had accomplished athletically at the time to parlay into something like maybe a professional wrestling or acting to see what my true potential in life is, to see how many people I can have an impact on. So I was very blessed because shortly after I got my black belt, I actually had a couple people at the time refer me to the recruitment department at WWE, which was entirely different than it is now. But within about a week and a half time frame, I had got a call from the recruitment department in Stanford, Connecticut, saying that they had been referred to me by a couple of different people and they would like me to put in a resume. At that time I thought that there was a likelihood that I could get a tryout. So I started learning bumps and rolls at Phoenix Championship Wrestling in Arizona under coach Dom Vitalli, but I never got the call back.” Jimmy House told Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp in a new interview. After talking with people from WWE, House decided to start at the very bottom of the wrestling industry. This would ultimately lead to the previously mentioned tryout, where he was a self proclaimed standout. “Then at that point, just how I am, once I put my name out as something, regardless of if it’s the short way or the long way, I have to continue to pursue that. It’d be just, if anything, for my ego and pride alone. But that being said, it forced me to move from Arizona to Austin, Texas, to try to put myself at the bottom of the barrel, to start on the indies, to start from the very bottom of professional wrestling—not in a negative way, but like at the bottom where everybody else starts. I’m really glad that that was a story for me. So then after a year on the indies is getting the call in November that I had eight weeks to prepare for that tryout. It was very full circle for me because I had that short term gratification taken away to some degree when I thought I was gonna get a tryout and then the call never came back. Then I forced myself to move and made all these different sacrifices so on and so forth and did the indies. Then I finally got that call back that essentially motivated me to even learn how to bump, to learn how to roll. So it was a huge accomplishment for me internally given the story that I just said. After that, I took it like, ‘Okay, I know how to do a bodybuilding prep. I’ve done that a couple of times. So I’m going to bodybuilding prep myself from a physique standpoint.’ I know how to train myself on an athletic basis. I have people that I can reach out to that that can help me prepare athletically for this and then in the ring

House credited Gabe Sapolsky with helping open that door for him before he officially joined the program in March.

An opponent has not been confirmed, nor has a streamer. Erich Richter of the New York Post reported that the Christmas Eve fight won’t be on Netflix due to changes in the company. There is some legitimate speculation that Netflix could be exiting or reducing its live sporting event reach, as the streaming giant fired Bela Bajaria as the Chief Content Officer earlier this month, perhaps signaling a change in strategy. Two of Paul’s last three fights were on Netflix, including the Mike Tyson bout and his last fight when he faced off against Anthony Joshua, who broke his jaw. Richter speculated that Paul’s Dec. 24 bout could be on DAZN PPV, as his last three fights before his Netflix bouts were. The New York Post also noted that there is speculation that former UFC fighter Darren Till could face Paul, and they reported that MVP have been in contact with Chris Eubank, Edgar Berlanga and YouTuber KSI.

body: Stardom held its Crimson Nightmare pay-per-view at Tokyo EBARE WAVE Arena Ota, featuring Suzu Suzuki defending the World of Stardom Championship against Starlight Kid and Natsupoi and Shingo Takagi teaming up against Yuna Mizumori and Hirooki Goto. Suzuki successfully defended the Red Belt in the main event, and after the match, she called out Maika to be her next challenger. This is expected to be her next title defense before facing off against 5Star Grand Prix winner Rina at Ryogou on Dec. 29. Natsupoi continued her retirement run with a win with her husband, Takagi, against Mizumori and Goto. On Shingo’s YouTube channel, the couple teased another tag match at Bound for Unbound in Korakuen Hall on Nov. 20. Their opponent was left as a mystery. Crimson Nightmare also featured Stars emerging victorious over H.A.T.E. in an elimination tag match. There was an announcement for the 2027 Cinderella Tournament , which will begin on March 16 and conclude on March 22, and there was an announcement for Stardom’s early 2027 shows in Osaka and Hiroshima.

title: Mark Cuban Recalls Taking Sheamus Table Bump
raw_title: Mark Cuban Says He Was Sore For Two Weeks After Sheamus Table Bump On WWE Raw
summary_src: Mark Cuban had a blast in WWE. Cuban first appeared for the company at Survivor Series in November 2003. He ended up taking an RKO from Randy Orton.
body: Cuban first appeared for the company at Survivor Series in November 2003. He ended up taking an RKO from Randy Orton. In a new interview with Build Or Break , Cuban spoke about the appearance and revealed his two rules. “Oh, I did it twice, I loved it. They reached out to me in 2003 after I just bought the Mavs. They said, ‘We have WWE coming to Dallas, would you like to participate because we’ll get celebrities come in to do cameos.’ ‘I’m happy to do it, but I have two rules. One, I get hit. Two, I get to hit somebody.’ So, I got RKO’ed by Randy Orton. We had to practice it and do this stuff, it was still hard. It still hurt.” After speaking about his 2009 appearance, Mark Cuban said that wrestlers deserve so much respect. “Then, I did it again in 2009. I did this whole thing with John Cena. There’s this guy, a wrestler named Sheamus. They were like, ‘Okay, Sheamus has never hit the canvas. We know your rules. You get to put him down so he hits the camera. But, on the flip side, he’s going to put you through a table. It was a real table. They told me, ‘He’s gonna put you right in the center of the table, it’ll just crack in half. Keep your head down because if your head is up when you hit, you’ll break your neck.’ I’m like, ‘My head will be down.’ He puts me through and we broke the table. I did my whole pretend I’m dead thing and I was sore for two weeks. My back hurt so bad. Those guys deserve so much respect. It may be orchestrated, but it’s still athletic and it’s still painful.” Back in 2025, Sheamus said that he didn’t know who Mark Cuban was before his Raw segment in 2009. Check out his full comments by clicking here. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Mark Cuban first appeared for WWE at Survivor Series in November 2003 after purchasing the Mavericks and took an RKO from Randy Orton. He returned in 2009 for a segment with John Cena that ended with Sheamus putting him through a real table. Cuban said he was sore for two weeks afterward and expressed respect for what wrestlers endure.

title: Match Made: Riddle vs. Kwon — MLW Fusion Preview (10/29/26)
raw_title: MLW Fusion Preview (10/29/26): Riddle vs. Kwon
body: Ladies and gentlemen, we are expanding our horizons! Tonight, we’re turning our attention to Major League Wrestling , where MLW Fusion brings tournament action, championship rivalries, and a collection of wrestlers who appear perfectly willing to beat the living hell out of one another. That’s right, folks. Tubi , the same streaming service where Thalia spends an alarming amount of time watching horror movies featuring questionable acting, questionable special effects, and women who apparently have difficulty keeping their clothes on, is also home to professional wrestling. Naturally, she’s already informed me that this makes MLW part of her department. I’ve informed her that she’s welcome to watch, but the wrestling coverage belongs to the scorpion. Tonight’s episode comes from Philadelphia’s legendary 2300 Arena, with two Opera Cup quarterfinal matches, a heavyweight collision, and several major developments ahead of MLW Saturday Night SuperFight. Our main event features Matt Riddle taking on CONTRA Unit’s Ikuro Kwon in an Opera Cup quarterfinal, with a place in the semifinals hanging in the balance. Riddle is one of those wrestlers whose relaxed personality can sometimes make you forget just how dangerous he is once the bell rings. His combination of striking, submissions, and explosive offense makes him a legitimate threat against practically anybody, and a tournament like the Opera Cup provides an excellent opportunity to demonstrate those abilities. Known as the Concrete Dragon, Kwon brings the ruthless mentality of CONTRA Unit into a tournament that the faction has already threatened to corrupt. Josef Samael has made no secret of his contempt for the Opera Cup’s traditions, and a Kwon victory would bring CONTRA another step closer to getting its hands on the prestigious trophy. Now, I appreciate a good villain as much as anybody, but threatening to destroy a historic wrestling trophy because you don’t like what it represents? That’s the kind of behavior that makes me wish somebody would bring back the old-fashioned wrestling commissioner who could suspend people for being complete jackasses. Adding another complication is MLW National Openweight Champion Austin Aries, who is expected to be in attendance scouting the competition. Aries has his own ambitions involving the Opera Cup, and I wouldn’t be surprised if he makes his presence felt before the evening is over. Stinger’s Pick: Matt Riddle. Kwon is dangerous, and CONTRA Unit’s involvement always raises the possibility of outside interference, but I’m going with Riddle to overcome the odds and advance to the semifinals. Whether he’ll be allowed to do it without somebody sticking their nose into the match is another question entirely. The evening’s other Opera Cup quarterfinal brings us a matchup with a little history behind it, as Diego Hill faces LaBron Kozone. title: What happened on the plane after WWE Crown Jewel 2019?
raw_title: What happened on the plane after WWE Crown Jewel 2019?
summary_src: The Crown Jewel 2019 plane incident resurfaced this week, and John Pollock looks back at the details that have emerged since.
body: Light being shed on years-long controversies usually requires a combination of time, a prominent executive’s exit from a company, and the magic wand of a book deal and ensuing PR tour. For WWE audiences, this effect now pertains to the story of a plane delay in Saudi Arabia seven years ago, ex-co-president George Barrios, and his comments on the My World podcast with Conrad Thompson and Jeff Jarrett . Headlines from the interview read that the situation of talent being stuck in the country after the Crown Jewel event was “exaggerated to some degree”, but the language used by Barrios doesn’t dismiss the theories regarding the talent and production team’s hold-up being more than “mechanical” in nature, as was originally stated. Crown Jewel was staged in Riyadh in October 2019 and was the fourth show of the WWE’s ten-year agreement with the General Entertainment Authority. WWE already endured plenty of backlash from the inaugural event in 2018, featuring an angle pitting the heel Daivari brothers as representatives of Iran confronting Saudi Arabia’s Mansoor and other prospects from the country. It leaned on real and deep-seated tension between the countries on a show mixed with propaganda messaging throughout the broadcast. That was mild compared to the November 2018 show, where WWE opted to stay the course and head to the country one month to the day after journalist Jamal Khashoggi was murdered at a Saudi Arabian consulate in Turkey. The Crown Jewel show of 2019 was arguably the most star-studded to date, with Tyson Fury and Cain Velasquez joining a giant-sized event consisting of nine matches and nearly sixty performers booked. It included a 10-man tag with team captains, Hulk Hogan and Ric Flair; an eight-team Tag Team Turmoil match, and a 20-man battle royal. Hours after the show, word started to trickle out that the WWE’s chartered flight was not leaving the country, with those on board left with questions as minutes turned to hours, and concerns turned to fear. A chartered WWE passenger flight operated by Atlas Air is currently delayed in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia due to a mechanical issue. The flight was scheduled to depart at 0300 local time on November 1. Our top priority is always to ensure our passengers arrive safely and on time at their destination. The aircraft is being repaired and will be inspected and certified before returning to service to transport our passengers to their final destination. We regret that operational disruptions delayed the flight and apologize to our passengers who were inconvenienced. The statement issued by WWE on behalf of the charter company was designed to quell concerns back home. Skepticism arose from talents who were not informed of any issues during the flight; if the answer was simply mechanical, why wasn’t that conveyed to those affected? The company added, “More than 175 Superstars, production crew and employees boarded a 747 charter flight back to the United States on Thursday. After the door closed, du

Fletcher, who is often compared to Orton and has a clean-shaven look with heavy ink, was left wondering what was happening after the incident. title: SiriusXM CEO touts WWE Radio audience growth
raw_title: SiriusXM CEO touts WWE Radio audience growth
summary_src: At least in the early going, rebranding its pro wrestling channel to “WWE Radio” has led to audience growth for SiriusXM.
body: At least in the early going, rebranding its pro wrestling channel to “WWE Radio” has led to audience growth for SiriusXM. The broadcasting company held its third quarter earnings call on Thursday, and SiriusXM CEO Jennifer Witz touted that the wrestling channel has grown its listenership by nearly 20 percent since switching over from Pro Wrestling Nation 24/7 to WWE Radio. The station is still anchored by Busted Open Radio as its main program. In addition to Busted Open and the rest of the talk show lineup, the channel now carries WWE’s podcasts, audio simulcasts of Raw, SmackDown & NXT, and its own commentary for PLEs. Partnering with WWE brought some criticism from fans, especially toward the hosts of Busted Open. The show no longer covers WWE’s biggest competitor in AEW, and AEW wrestler Thunder Rosa is gone from the Busted Open co-host lineup . There are still some interviews and segments on WWE Radio with wrestlers from the indies and TNA. Dave LaGreca, the main host of Busted Open, has insisted that his tone and coverage of WWE will not change despite the partnership. He said WWE President Nick Khan told him directly that WWE wants him to continue being himself and doesn’t want Busted Open to become “shill radio.” Sam Roberts and Peter Rosenberg are among the other hosts featured on WWE Radio. The commentary for PLEs is done by Vic Joseph & Booker T. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
