The broadcasting company held its third quarter earnings call on Thursday, and SiriusXM CEO Jennifer Witz touted that the wrestling channel has grown its listenership by nearly 20 percent since.

title: On the Record: Orange Cassidy Admits Years of Brutal AEW Matches Have Taken a Toll on His Body
raw_title: Orange Cassidy Admits Years of Brutal AEW Matches Have Taken a Toll on His Body
summary_src: Orange Cassidy has spent years getting thrown around, beaten down, and putting his body through some seriously brutal matches in AEW. And while he might look like he doesn’t have a care in the world, the punishment is apparently catching up with him.
body: During a recent appearance on Going Ringside , Cassidy was asked about the physical toll of competing in AEW since 2019. Host Scott Johnson pointed out how violent and physically demanding some of the company’s matches have become before asking whether all those years of punishment have finally started taking their toll. Cassidy didn’t try to pretend his body was feeling great. Instead, he admitted the wear and tear is real, but he’s found a pretty unusual way of dealing with it — simply refusing to think about how much he hurts. “Yeah, sure. But, uh, you know, you kind of block out that from your brain and, uh, try not to think about it because if I think about it then things start to hurt but if I don’t think about it then things don’t hurt.” That’s certainly one way to deal with years of getting slammed into the mat. Cassidy didn’t mention any specific injuries or suggest he was dealing with something that could keep him out of action, but he made it clear that his body hasn’t escaped the punishment. Cassidy has been part of AEW since its early days, competing in everything from championship matches to some of the company’s most physically demanding rivalries. His laid-back personality might make it seem like nothing bothers him, but there’s still a human being taking those bumps every time he steps between the ropes. And with Cassidy continuing to find himself caught up in physical confrontations involving the Death Riders, there doesn’t appear to be much opportunity for him to avoid taking more punishment. body: 0 Shotzi Blackheart clarifies her previous comments about WWE blocking her from working with TNA despite their working relationship. New TNA star Shotzi Blackheart recently revealed in an interview that she was in talks with the company while she was still signed to WWE. She said that after returning from injury, she wanted to utilize the working relationship between the two promotions for a potential crossover. Blackheart said she “begged” WWE to allow her to work with TNA Wrestling. However, she said she wasn’t allowed to do that for some reason. After multiple outlets covered her comments, Shotzi Blackheart took to X/Twitter to clarify. She said that while she was working in NXT, WWE also pitched a storyline on SmackDown. Blackheart noted that adding a third angle on TNA Wrestling would’ve been a lot to juggle. She clarified that her intention with the comments was only to express the enthusiasm she had for working with TNA at the time. “There was no negativity behind my comment. At the time TNA was utilizing NXT talent. I was working in NXT, but I was also being pitched to start a potential SmackDown storyline. So my understanding was that adding a third storyline would have been a lot to juggle. The intention of my comment was simply to express how much I’ve always wanted to work with TNA and my enthusiasm for making it work alongside an already full schedule,” Shotzi Blackheart said. title: In Memoriam: TNA Star Endured Life-Threatening Pregnancy, Breakup & Pet’s Death Before WWE Release
raw_title: TNA Star Endured Life-Threatening Pregnancy, Breakup & Pet’s Death Before WWE Release
body: 0 TNA Wrestling’s Elayna Black (Cora Jade) says she thought she lost everything after she faced multiple setbacks in life, including an ectopic pregnancy and a WWE release. The latest edition of the Immersed documentary, co-produced by TNA and Fight Network, detailed Elayna Black’s journey from rock bottom to finding success again in pro wrestling. Black’s mom and fellow TNA star Mustafa Ali also appeared in the episode to offer personal and professional perspectives on her journey. Elayna Black recounted the personal struggles she faced back in 2023 and 2024, including undergoing emergency surgery for an ectopic pregnancy. She said the condition was life-threatening and credited support from her family and friends for keeping her strong. The TNA star also looked back on undergoing surgery for a torn ACL she suffered during a match against Lyra Valkyria in January 2024. “I feel like I got hit back-to-back-to-back. I had an ectopic pregnancy. It’s not a viable pregnancy, and it’s very life-threatening. I was internally bleeding, like very bad. So, they had to rush me into emergency surgery right then and there. Those few months following that, I was the most depressed I’ve ever been in my life. I guess I didn’t realize, you know, postpartum depression is a very serious thing. You don’t even realize that it’ll happen to you, and it will, and it’s very scary, and it takes a lot of support and just strength to get through, and thankfully I did,” the TNA star began. “My mom was having to live with me because I was so depressed that I wasn’t eating. It was bad. On January 12th, I do a live event. I’m wrestling Lyra. Tear my ACL. Not only my ACL, my ACL, MCL, and both meniscuses.” Speaking further, Elayna Black revealed that apart from the ectopic pregnancy and ACL injury, she also had to deal with a breakup and the death of her pet dog before WWE released her in May 2025. “So, yeah. Ectopic pregnancy, boyfriend leaves me, lose my knee, dog dies. And then, I got fired a few months later…. I was so scared of losing anything else that mattered to me that I didn’t want to pretend anything mattered. So, when I got fired, inside I was like, “Oh, holy sh*t, I’ve lost the literal last thing. Like, I have lost everything. This was the very last thing, and now I’ve lost this. I literally have nothing,” the TNA star said. summary_src: WWE apparently isn’t putting all its eggs in the Saudi Arabia basket when it comes to WrestleMania 43.
body: According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select , sources have confirmed that The Sphere is not being considered as a backup location for WrestleMania 43 if WWE is forced to move the event out of Saudi Arabia. Despite WWE having internal interest in using the venue, the two sides haven’t gotten anywhere close to putting a deal together. The update also revealed that WWE’s interest in The Sphere hasn’t translated into serious discussions with the venue. “WrestleVotes on Fightful Select was told, as of this writing, that The Sphere in Las Vegas is not a backup plan for WWE in case they move WrestleMania 43 away from Saudi Arabia.” “While WWE has expressed interest internally in utilizing The Sphere, meaningful negotiations between the two sides have not transpired to our knowledge.” This isn’t the first time WWE and The Sphere have had trouble getting on the same page. Fightful Select previously revealed in March that the two sides couldn’t reach an agreement during WrestleMania 42 season over displaying Danhausen promotional material on the outside of the venue. But the biggest development from this latest update is that WWE apparently already has another option lined up if Saudi Arabia becomes too dangerous or difficult to host WrestleMania 43. The company just isn’t telling anyone what that plan involves. “We’re told WWE does have a backup blueprint for hosting WrestleMania domestically, should world events require a change of plans. However, those details are being kept secret.” “Regarding rumors of Las Vegas as a back-up plan, sources in Las Vegas who have basically tipped us off on all the Mania decisions as well as issues with the dates that had to be taken care of the past two years well ahead of time, said that the city does not have the dates available in April and is not able to spend the kind of money they have in the past to bring the event in.” WrestleMania 43 is officially scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia , although WWE has yet to announce the exact dates for the April 2027 event. For now, the company intends to move forward with those plans despite ongoing travel concerns. There’s also an enormous amount of money involved. It was previously stated that WWE’s November 7 event in Saudi Arabia is worth approximately $60 million, while WrestleMania 43 is worth well over $100 million . That gives WWE plenty of financial incentive to keep its Saudi Arabia plans intact unless circumstances make that impossible. The fact that WWE already has a domestic backup blueprint is a major development, especially with so much uncertainty surrounding the situation. The Sphere isn’t part of it, Las Vegas has its own obstacles, and WWE is keeping the actual details under wraps. For now, Saudi Arabia remains the destination, but WWE clearly has another option in mind if things go sideways. summary: Per WrestleVotes on Fightful Select , sources have made official that The Sphere is not being considered as a backup location for WrestleMania 43 if WWE is forced to move. But the biggest development from this latest update is that WWE apparently already has another option lined up if Saudi Arabia becomes too dangerous or difficult to host WrestleMania 43.

title: 3 Ways Liv Morgan's Attack On Chelsea Green Raises The Stakes For Crown Jewel

body: The Judgment Day interfered in the title bout before the attack began. Raquel Rodriguez shoved Green off the top rope while the referee was distracted. IYO SKY ran to ringside and brawled with Rodriguez. Perez took SKY out with a dive, but Green dodged Pop Rox and hit the Un-Pretty-Her for the pin. Morgan struck once the final bell rang and hit Green with ground-and-pound. Perez and Rodriguez joined in, and the trio beat down both Green and SKY. SKY tried to fight back, but the three-on-two numbers kept The Judgment Day in control. The Judgment Day also targeted Green on the Oct. 12 episode of Raw. After a face-to-face with Morgan about Crown Jewel, Green wrestled Perez in a non-title bout. Morgan and Rodriguez provided a distraction, and Perez won with Pop Rox. Morgan beat Nia Jax on Nov. 2, 2024, to become the first Women's Crown Jewel Champion. Dominik Mysterio and Rodriguez distracted Jax and the referee to set up the Oblivion finish. Tiffany Stratton tried to cash in during that bout, and Rodriguez stopped the attempt. Green did not finish the night alone. Stratton, the 2026 Miss Money in the Bank, ran in for the save, tossing Perez over the top rope and dropping Morgan with a knee lift. SKY and Stratton cleared the ring with a hurricanrana and a missile dropkick. Morgan grabbed the Money in the Bank briefcase and went after Stratton, but SKY countered, and Green answered with a superkick. Stratton nearly cashed in before Perez and Rodriguez pulled Morgan out of the ring. In a parking lot segment after the brawl, SKY promised to always have Green's back. Stratton joined the pair and talked about wanting to see Morgan's face after a cash-in. Green admitted the Stratton arrival came as a surprise, then suggested the trio go celebrate. Green does not get a clean week to recover. Nikki Bella challenges Green for the WWE Women's Championship on the Oct. 30 SmackDown in Charleston, W.Va. Crown Jewel follows eight days later on Nov. 7. Green wrestled a full title defense on Oct. 23 before the Judgment Day attack. Perez controlled the match through a commercial break after driving Green's shoulder into the ring post. A pair of diving clotheslines started Green's comeback before the finish. Morgan heads to Riyadh in a fourth Women's World Championship reign. At Money in the Bank on Oct. 10, Morgan pinned Stephanie Vaquer in a triple threat with Becky Lynch. Vaquer won the Women's Crown Jewel Championship in Perth, Australia, in 2025 by beating Stratton. A victory over Green on Nov. 7 would make Morgan the first woman to capture the Crown Jewel title twice. Morgan did not wait for Riyadh to start the fight. A blindside attack, two friends, and a beatdown turned Green's successful title defense into a mess. Crown Jewel is personal now. Morgan wants Green worn down long before the opening bell on Nov. 7. The problem for Morgan is simple. SKY now stands with Green, and Stratton has a briefcase aimed squarely at Morgan's title. The Judgment Day bailed out

title: Young Bucks Praise Tony Khan's Leadership
raw_title: AEW World Tag Team Champions: Tony Khan 'Doesn't Get Enough Praise'
summary_src: AEW World Tag Team Champions The Young Bucks have nothing but nice things to say about Tony Khan, saying Khan "doesn't get enough praise" from them
body: Now once again AEW World Tag Team Champions , the Young Bucks appear to be having the time of their AEW careers, prompting them to pay homage to their boss, Tony Khan. On the post-WrestleDream episode of "Being the Elite," Matt and Nick Jackson were discussing how proud they were of their WrestleDream match against Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight when Nick began talking about a brief moment where he looked in the camera and told Khan he wasn't sure how much longer he could perform at this level. He admitted he had no idea why he said it, but used that as a segue for both him and Matt to praise Khan as a boss and as a person. "I would do anything for Tony at this point," Nick said. "I love that man. We've given our entire careers to him, and he's given us so much. I don't think he gets enough praise and credit from us." "I texted him on his birthday about that," Matt said. "I said 'You changed my life dude. I'll never forget you.'" Alongside Kenny Omega, Cody Rhodes, and Brandi Rhodes, the Bucks and Khan were the key figures in launching AEW in 2019, with the Bucks noting in their autobiography that Khan had approached them about the idea for AEW the previous summer. Despite some bumps in the road, most notably the animosity between the Bucks and former AEW star CM Punk back in 2022 and 2023 , the Bucks have remained one of the top acts of AEW since its launch, with their recent tag title victory at All Out setting the record for most AEW World Tag Team Championship reigns in company history.

title: WWE’s Current Stance on AEW Dynamite New Year’s Smash Going Head-to-Head With SmackDown
raw_title: WWE’s Current Stance on AEW Dynamite New Year’s Smash Going Head-to-Head With SmackDown
summary_src: WWE apparently isn’t changing a damn thing just because AEW decided to run Dynamite on New Year’s Day. Even with AEW New Year’s Smash airing on Friday, January 1, 2027, WWE plans to stick with its original SmackDown taping schedule.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , a WWE source indicated that the company has no plans to reshape its schedule so SmackDown can go live head-to-head with AEW. Instead, the January 1 episode will still be taped several days in advance. WWE is planning a double taping on Monday, December 28 in Tampa, Florida. The decision was made so talent wouldn’t have to work on New Year’s Day, and WWE apparently isn’t interested in changing that plan regardless of AEW scheduling a live Dynamite opposite SmackDown. “With the announcement that AEW is going to air Dynamite: New Year’s Smash on Friday, January 1st, 2027, a WWE source indicated to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select that the company has no plans to reshape its taping schedule to go head-to-head live with the competition. “The 1/1/27 SmackDown will be taped in advance, and there will be a double taping scheduled for Monday, December 28th in Tampa, Florida. We’re told the decision to tape both shows that night was made to allow talent to avoid working New Year’s Day, and per a source, WWE intends to stick with that plan, regardless of what AEW has scheduled.” WWE also apparently isn’t expecting huge numbers from the holiday episode in the first place. There’s an internal expectation that the taped New Year’s Day SmackDown could draw a lower rating than a normal live episode, whether AEW is running against it or not. “There is an expectation internally that the ratings for the holiday edition of SmackDown could draw a lower number than the usual live broadcast, regardless of AEW airing a live episode against it.” The situation came together after AEW announced that New Year’s Smash will return with two nights of wrestling in Atlanta. Dynamite New Year’s Smash is scheduled for Friday, January 1 at Gateway Arena, followed by Collision New Year’s Smash at the same venue on Saturday, January 2. That Friday date puts Dynamite directly opposite SmackDown, creating a rare head-to-head night between the two companies. However, WWE isn’t treating it as enough of a reason to make talent work the holiday or rearrange a taping schedule that was already locked in. So while viewers will get AEW Dynamite and WWE SmackDown going against each other on New Year’s Day, only one side is currently expected to be live. WWE seems perfectly comfortable sticking with its taped show and letting the numbers fall where they may. Which show do you think will benefit more from the unusual New Year’s Day head-to-head between WWE and AEW? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Why WWE’s Gambling Connections Face Different Rules in Canada
raw_title: Why WWE’s Gambling Connections Face Different Rules in Canada
summary_src: WWE has no problem making money through sponsorship deals, and gambling companies have been part of that business for years. But things get a little more complicated when Canadian fans get involved.
body: WWE got into the gaming business with DraftKings back in March 2021, announcing a partnership that brought free-to-play prediction contests to major events like WrestleMania 37. The deal also gave DraftKings branding opportunities during WWE premium live events. Fans could make predictions about what might happen during the shows without putting actual money on the outcomes. It was a way for WWE to get involved with a gambling company without opening the door to traditional betting on scripted matches. There’s just one catch. DraftKings says its free-to-play pools aren’t available in Ontario, even though they’re offered in other parts of Canada. So a WWE fan watching in Toronto could find themselves unable to participate in something that a fan in another Canadian province can access. And that’s only part of the issue. Ontario opened its regulated online gambling market in April 2022, allowing private companies to offer sports betting and online casino games as long as they meet provincial requirements. The market operates under the oversight of the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario, with iGaming Ontario working directly with approved operators. Things got even tighter in February 2024 when Ontario introduced new restrictions on gambling advertisements. The province banned the use of active and retired athletes in online gambling marketing, except when they’re promoting responsible gambling. It also cracked down on the use of celebrities, entertainers, and social media personalities who are likely to appeal to minors. That’s where WWE becomes an interesting part of the conversation. Its biggest stars aren’t just wrestlers anymore. They’re television personalities, movie stars, influencers, and recognizable faces with millions of followers. John Cena and The Rock are two obvious examples of WWE names who built careers far beyond wrestling. And with WWE regularly looking for new sponsorship opportunities, those restrictions could become a factor whenever a company wants to advertise to Canadian wrestling fans. Toronto isn’t some random stop on the wrestling calendar. WWE has been running major events there for decades, including WrestleMania VI in 1990, WrestleMania X8 in 2002, and SummerSlam in 2019. AEW got in on the action too, bringing Forbidden Door to Scotiabank Arena in 2023. Both companies know there’s money to be made in the Canadian market, and sponsors know it as well. But gambling companies can’t necessarily run the same advertising campaigns everywhere WWE or AEW has an audience. The restrictions also affect which websites Canadian fans can legally use. Just because a gambling company operates in another province doesn’t mean it’s authorized to serve customers in Ontario. For fans trying to sort through the available options, some Canadian gambling comparison websites track operators serving the province, including the Ontario shortlist they maintain . Anyone looking for the official rules can also check the iGaming Ontario site
summary: WWE got into the gaming business with DraftKings back in March 2021, announcing a partnership that brought free-to-play prediction contests to major events like WrestleMania 37. The deal additionally gave DraftKings branding opportunities during WWE premium live events.

title: Sami Zayn Explains Avoiding Social Media Tribute To PAC
raw_title: WWE's Sami Zayn Explains Why He Didn't Post Anything About The Death Of AEW Star Pac
summary_src: The wrestling world was rocked by the death of Benjamin "PAC" Satterly last month. His good friend, WWE's Sami Zayn explains why he didn't post to social media.
body: WWE Last month the wrestling world was shocked by the untimely death of Benjamin "PAC" Satterly due to bronchial asthma . Fans and people within the industry took to social media to collectively share in their grief . AEW held a tribute show in his memory and other promotions acknowledged Satterly's death. A video was put together by his good friend, Kevin Owens featuring WWE talent . During an interview on Insight with Chris Van Vliet , WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn explained why he opted not to post anything on social media. He was worried Van Vliet was going to ask about Satterly and said he didn't know what to say. "I wasn't able to post anything, I haven't posted anything (pauses) because what do you even say in a tweet, you know what I mean? 'Hey, here's this guy that was like a brother to me, that I traveled the world with, that I grew up with'. Like this bond, it's hard to articulate what these bonds mean. And then I'm supposed to do it in a tweet or like an Instagram post with 10 pictures out of the hundreds of thou – you know what I mean? None of it will do it justice." He also said he's a bit of a perfectionist and Satterly was the same way. He feels it's impossible to give their friendship the tribute it deserves. He also feels guilty for not posting anything. "I start going down this path of 'who the f*** is this even for?' Who needs to know? I know and the people that matter know, you know what I mean? The people in our circle, his wife, his mom, me, my wife – my wife was extremely close too, she's profoundly affected by it. All of our close friends, all the guys we came up with, he meant something different to everybody. So you're allowed to just have that."
summary: WWE Undisputed Champion Sami Zayn told Chris Van Vliet he could not bring himself to post about the death of Benjamin "PAC" Satterly last month. Zayn described PAC as a brother he traveled the world and grew up with in the business, saying the depth of their bond could not be properly expressed in a tweet or Instagram post. A video tribute featuring WWE talent was assembled by Kevin Owens while AEW and other promotions paid their respects.

title: Comeback Watch: WWE Working on New Direction for Paul Heyman’s TV Return

summary_src: Paul Heyman has been missing from WWE television for a few weeks, and naturally, that’s raised questions about what the hell is going on with The Oracle. Now there’s finally some word on what WWE could have cooking for him behind the scenes.
body: According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , there is currently a working creative idea that could see Heyman return to WWE television relatively soon. The interesting part is that WWE may be looking to expand what he’s doing instead of simply throwing him right back into the exact same spot. The idea involves Heyman branching out into another program outside of The Vision. That doesn’t mean he’s completely ditching the group, though, because WWE still apparently wants him connected to the storyline. “According to those with knowledge of the situation, there is a working creative idea that would see Paul Heyman return to television relatively soon. The potential idea would involve Heyman in something outside of The Vision, although not completely dissociating from that storyline.” More specifically, Bron Breakker is expected to remain Heyman’s main connection to The Vision. That tracks with previous reporting that WWE sees Heyman as an important part of Breakker’s presentation regardless of what ultimately happens with the faction. “As it stands, the creative direction would allow Heyman to branch out into another program while still maintaining some connection to The Vision, specifically Bron Breakker.” Heyman was still involved with The Vision earlier this month, including the October 5 episode of RAW, where he pushed Bronson Reed to take care of Oba Femi. His most recent WWE television appearance came on October 12, and he hasn’t been seen on programming since. There’s no word yet on what this other program could actually be or who Heyman would be working with. For now, WWE apparently has an idea on the table to bring him back soon without completely pulling him away from Breakker and everything going on with The Vision. So Heyman’s absence doesn’t necessarily mean WWE has run out of things for him to do. title: Inside the 2005 Meeting — Brock Lesnar and Vince McMahon
raw_title: Brock Lesnar and Vince McMahon: Inside the 2005 Meeting
body: Brock Lesnar came to WWE chairman Vince McMahon in July 2005 to discuss money and time off. Before either subject came up, he was asked to take his shirt off. He left the meeting believing a comeback was close, but the contract that followed gave him a reason to walk away all over again. Brock Lesnar was relieved when he decided to leave WWE. The hectic, demanding schedule that came with the stardom of a WWE main-eventer had worn him down. He was also frustrated with his position on the card and his future earnings. Lesnar made it clear to McMahon that he wanted out, then agreed to stay through WrestleMania. His match against Goldberg at WrestleMania XX on March 14, 2004, became the end of that first WWE run. He wanted a different life and a chance to pursue professional football. Having grown up on a farm in South Dakota, Lesnar valued the privacy that wrestling stardom made difficult to protect. In his 2011 memoir, Death Clutch: My Story of Determination, Domination, and Survival , Lesnar used Kane (Glenn Jacobs) as an example. "He had the greatest gig ever, because he was a big star who wore a mask on TV." Lesnar enjoyed performing and entertaining the fans, but he also wanted to be present for his family. "Life on the road is just not for me. It’s not the life I choose to live." Even buying a private plane had failed to make the travel manageable. Leaving WWE did not give Lesnar unrestricted freedom to wrestle or fight elsewhere. As part of his release, he signed a non-compete agreement that became the central obstacle when his football attempt did not produce a place on an NFL roster. In April 2004, Brock Lesnar was involved in a motorcycle accident in Minneapolis. His later account listed a broken jaw, eight broken bones in his left hand, a bruised pelvis, and a serious groin injury. It also put his speed at 45 mph in a 25 mph zone before the collision. The accident disrupted Lesnar’s preparation for the NFL. Despite postponed workouts, he remained determined to make it onto a team. He returned to Phoenix for rehabilitation. He later singled out the groin injury as especially difficult to overcome. In late July 2004, he signed a one-year contract with the Minnesota Vikings after a second workout for the team. He attended training camp and participated in preseason games as a defensive lineman. On August 14, Lesnar made his preseason debut against the Arizona Cardinals, appearing on the kickoff team and during the closing minutes of Minnesota’s win. The Vikings released him on August 30. His work ethic and progress had impressed the team, but his limited football experience, minimal playing time, and lingering groin injury were obstacles he had not overcome. Coach Mike Tice’s assessment of the departure appeared in Associated Press coverage published the following day. "He gave me a hug," Tice recalled. "He was very happy for the chance." By Mike Johnson on 2026-10-29 13:29:00 As PWInsider.com exclusively broke this past Monday, WWE’s Executive Director - Creative Writing & Talent (CWT) Bruce Prichard is expected to retire from that position at Wrestlemania 43 and depart his full-time position for the company. As we noted, the expectation is that Prichard will remain connected to the company as a consultant, working from his home in Texas. The natural question that has been asked is who would be tapped to replace Prichard in his position. PWInsider.com can exclusively confirm that WWE is planning to promote from within and according to multiple sources, the plan is for the current head of WWE NXT and Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative, WWE Hall of Famer Shawn Michaels to essentially step into Prichard’s current role. Michaels, 61, is a former WWE Champion and considered one of the company’s greatest in-ring performers ever with a number of classic Wrestlemania performances under his belt. He officially retired from the ring in 2010, returning only for one bout at a WWE PPV in Saudi Arabia in 2018. Michaels, who is extremely close with WWE CCO Paul Levesque, stepped into his WWE NXT duties in September 2021. We are told that this succession plan has been in place for some time and that Michaels will start to prepare for the Prichard role in the months ahead. title: Bruce Prichard’s WWE Replacement After WrestleMania 43 Revealed

summary_src: Bruce Prichard is getting ready to step away from his full-time WWE role after WrestleMania 43, and the company apparently isn’t wasting any time figuring out who will replace him. In fact, WWE already has someone picked out, and it’s a name fans know very well.
body: According to PWInsider, WWE is planning to have Shawn Michaels take over Prichard’s position as Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent once Prichard steps down following WrestleMania 43 in April 2027. Rather than bring in someone from outside the company, WWE is looking to promote from within, with Michaels expected to move into one of the biggest creative positions behind the scenes. “The natural question that has been asked is who would be tapped to replace Prichard in his position. PWInsider.com can exclusively confirm that WWE is planning to promote from within and according to multiple sources, the plan is for the current head of WWE NXT and Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative, WWE Hall of Famer Shawn Michaels to essentially step into Prichard’s current role.” And this isn’t something WWE just came up with after word got out about Prichard leaving his position. The company has apparently been working on this transition for a while, giving Michaels plenty of time to prepare for the new responsibilities. “We are told that this succession plan has been in place for some time and that Michaels will start to prepare for the Prichard role in the months ahead.” It’s a pretty big move for Michaels, who has been running WWE NXT since September 2021. He’s also extremely close with WWE Chief Content Officer Paul “Triple H” Levesque, so the two working together in an even bigger capacity makes plenty of sense. But taking over Prichard’s job is a different situation from running NXT. Prichard currently sits above the writing teams for RAW, SmackDown, and NXT in WWE’s creative structure. He’s also been the person trusted to handle television tapings whenever Triple H isn’t available. If Michaels takes over those responsibilities, he’ll have a much bigger role in what fans see across WWE programming every week. The update comes after it was first revealed that Prichard is expected to leave his full-time position following WrestleMania 43. The 63-year-old isn’t expected to leave WWE completely, though. The current plan is for him to continue working as a consultant from his home in Texas rather than maintain his regular schedule with the company. Prichard’s health is also a major part of the situation. We previously revealed that he’s been dealing with serious physical problems and is preparing for surgery that will take him off the road. As previously noted , Prichard is facing neck surgery connected to an injury dating back to a 1991 WWF angle involving The Ultimate Warrior and his Brother Love character. More than three decades later, that damage is still causing problems. Prichard returned to WWE full-time in 2019 and became one of the most influential people behind the scenes, working under Vince McMahon before continuing in a major creative role under Triple H. It looked like Page was initially successful in that he was able to talk King down, but Swerve forced the issue with a video of him with a bloody, maskless Bandido. I thought there was more to come when Page and King set off to search for Swerve and Bandido, but we’ll have to wait for Collision or next week’s Dynamite to get the payoff. title: Shawn Michaels to Replace Bruce Prichard on WWE Creative

summary_src: Paul “Triple H” Levesque and Shawn Michaels could soon be working closely together on WWE main roster creative. Following the news that Bruce Prichard will be scaling down his WWE duties, PWInsider reported today that WWE’s succession plan is for Michaels to essentially replace Prichard.
body: Paul “Triple H” Levesque and Shawn Michaels could soon be working closely together on WWE main roster creative. Following the news that Bruce Prichard will be scaling down his WWE duties , PWInsider reported today that WWE’s succession plan is for Michaels to essentially replace Prichard . Prichard has been one of the key people in WWE creative as Executive Director but is stepping away from that role in 2027. The expectation is that Prichard will depart his position following WrestleMania 43 and become a consultant working from home. Michaels currently is in charge of NXT as Senior Vice President of Talent Development & Creative. The PWInsider report didn’t state if WWE already has someone in mind to take over Michaels’ NXT role. “PWInsider.com can exclusively confirm that WWE is planning to promote from within and according to multiple sources, the plan is for the current head of WWE NXT and Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative, WWE Hall of Famer Shawn Michaels to essentially step into Prichard’s current role,” the report said. Michaels and Levesque have been great friends for decades and are WWE Hall of Famers individually and as part of D-Generation X. When Levesque had heart issues in 2021, Michaels replaced him in NXT and has been running the brand since. Levesque now leads creative on the main roster. Prichard’s decision to step back comes after he’s experienced some health issues in recent years, including undergoing triceps and shoulder surgeries. He was away from WWE due to back issues for a period this year, and his friend Conrad Thompson shared earlier this month that Prichard is set to undergo neck surgery. The injury stems from a 1990s angle where Prichard, as his Brother Love character, was attacked by The Ultimate Warrior. Following retirement, Prichard will continue his connection with WWE in a consulting role. He will no longer perform his current duties or reside in Stamford. Plans for the exact timing remain subject to possible change.
Multiple wrestling journalists have confirmed the report about his upcoming retirement. Prichard first joined WWE in 1987 as an announcer. He later portrayed the on-screen character Brother Love.

title: Paul Heyman Sums up Vince McMahon in One Word, And It’s Perfect
raw_title: Paul Heyman Sums up Vince McMahon in One Word, And It’s Perfect
body: During an interview on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Heyman described Vince McMahon as a “dictator” who saw WWE as his show and contrasted him with Triple H , whose real name is Paul Levesque. “Well, Paul runs the creative. And it’s a much different environment with Paul running the creative than Vince, because they are distinctly different personalities. Vince was a dictator. It was his money, and therefore it’s his show. And you’re going to be the executive director, or you’re going to be the lead writer, or you’re going to be my top idea man,” Heyman said. Heyman explained that pitching an idea to McMahon meant trying to talk him out of a vision he already had in his head. He did an impression of McMahon to describe how those conversations went. “‘Graham, I see this is not half empty, it’s not half full. That is a percentage which I have in my mind, and you can’t talk me out of it.’ ‘Well, Vince, what’s in your mind?’ ‘I don’t know. Why don’t you tell me what’s in your mind, and talk me out of what’s in mine?” Heyman said. “So, you better be good at pitching. And it’s the constant chase for Vince to buy into your ideas over his own. That’s the dynamic of pitching Vince McMahon. He’s right, he has the right to be wrong. It’s his show; give me your best shot. “Because if you can sell Vince, you can sell the talent, you can sell the lieutenants, and you can sell the audience. So if you’re that good of a salesman, he’s going to buy it. And then it’s his idea because he gets the credit, because he’s the owner.” Heyman said the process works very differently under Triple H. “That’s not the way it works today. Paul Levesque is not a dictator; he’s a collaborator. See, Vince loves a blank piece of paper. Paul Levesque doesn’t like the blank piece of paper. He accepts the fact that the paper has writing on it already. He’s the best editor I’ve ever worked with in my entire life, ever,” Heyman said. “Because he’s an open collaborator that walks in the room with no expectations of his own vision. His vision is to listen to very smart people that have different ideas than he does. So, he’s a collaborator the likes of which I’ve never had the pleasure of working with. It’s just a completely different experience.” Triple H took over WWE creative in July 2022 after McMahon retired. McMahon later resigned from TKO, WWE’s parent company, in January 2024.

And his ruthless pursuit of success was at the very same time very psychological and overcompensatory behavior from being a child. And that it was a ruthless pursuit of becoming teflon, of becoming invincible and invulnerable and in a situation where no one could ever hurt him again.” Asked if McMahon considering himself “good”, Heyman rejected the premise of the question: “No, I don’t think Vince would consider — I don’t think Vince ever considered himself a good man. I don’t think he cared about it. I don’t think that was part of his self- judgment. I don’t think he felt he was placed on this planet to be a good man. “Do I think he’s a man of great accomplishment? Yes. Do I regret the battles? And I had some battles with Vince.” The follow-up to that was about those Heyman/McMahon battles, which Paul said involved a lot of back-and-forth “f**k you”s, because McMahon “liked confrontation”. title: Mark Shapiro says in TKO town hall that staff’s safety in Middle East is “paramount”
raw_title: Report: Mark Shapiro says in TKO town hall that staff’s safety in Middle East is “paramount”
summary_src: Mark Shapiro reportedly said in a recent TKO town hall that the staff's safety in the Middle East is "paramount" to the company.
body: A TKO town hall was held Wednesday via Zoom, according to PWInsider . Each department, including WWE, UFC, Zuffa Boxing, and On Location, gave a quick recap of what was going on. TKO President and Chief Operating Officer Mark Shapiro noted the company’s upcoming events in the Middle East. According to PWInsider, Shapiro “emphatically stated” that everyone’s safety was “paramount.” The meeting was held before it was announced that Crown Jewel would not be held at Riyadh Season Stadium. The Nov. 7 event reportedly will still be held in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. WWE President Nick Khan also spoke, talking about WWE’s upcoming stars. In an April TKO town hall before Night of Champions, which was also in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, Khan said that they would be “only going if it’s safe or if we’re allowed there.” He had also noted that he and Paul Levesque would attend. It is not clear if they would again make the trip for Crown Jewel. The Iran-backed Houthis have attacked civilian spaces over the past month, including King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. The U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia issued a security advisory on Oct. 25, warning Americans to exercise “extreme caution” when using any airports in the country. The Canelo Alvarez vs. Mbilli card is still expected to take place in Saudi Arabia on Oct. 31, a week before Crown Jewel. title: PWInsider: WWE Never Pursued Vince Russo Return
raw_title: Backstage Details On Recent Report That WWE Was In Talks To Re-Hire Vince Russo
summary_src: New details have emerged surrounding the recent report that WWE was in talks to re-hire Vince Russo.
body: The Hannibal TV/YouTube It was reported on Wednesday that WWE President Nick Khan reportedly had a meeting with former WWE Attitude Era head writer, turned WCW booker, and most recently, JCW creative mind, Vince Russo. According to Conrad Thompson, writing for Uncrowned , the polarizing figure had talks with WWE about a possible return to the company over the summer . According to new details in a report from PWInsider Elite , the story now making its rounds within the company is that it was Russo to reach out to Khan seeking a potential role in the company. WWE sources confirmed to PWIE that there was no movement to hire Russo at any point this year. Dave Meltzer also commented on Thompson's report on the latest edition of " Wrestling Observer Radio " when discussing Bruce Prichard reportedly stepping off the road into a consulting role with WWE following WrestleMania 43. Meltzer said that Russo isn't taking over for Prichard, and the entire story regarding a possible WWE return for Russo is basically "nothing." "Nick Khan calls, I don't want to say everyone, but you would be stunned, maybe not stunned, but you'd be surprised at some of the people Nick Khan has called and talked about for work," he said. "It would be names that would blow your mind, actually. I wasn't the slightest bit surprised that the discussion was there. It went nowhere. But, it couldn't work. Not in this day and age." Meltzer said he's not sure who called who, but by all accounts, nothing is happening on the Russo front. He also said he doesn't know who will replace Prichard. Russo has yet to comment on the recent reports.
summary: Per PWInsider Elite, it was Vince Russo who contacted WWE President Nick Khan about a potential role this past summer. Multiple WWE sources confirmed to the outlet that the company never had any intention or movement toward hiring him at any point in 2024. Dave Meltzer addressed the report on Wrestling Observer Radio, stating that the story is essentially nothing and Russo is not stepping into any position vacated by Bruce Prichard.

title: Queen Aminata Reacts To AEW TBS Title Victory
raw_title: Queen Aminata Makes First Comment On AEW TBS Title Win On Fright Night Dynamite
summary_src: Queen Aminata makes her first comments following an emotional AEW TBS Championship victory, her first title win in AEW, on Fright Night Dynamite
body: It was a night to remember for Queen Aminata at "AEW Fright Night Dynamite" on Wednesday, as she bested Persephone in the main event to capture the AEW TBS Championship . And even hours after the win, Aminata was still taking it all in on X with several posts. The first tweet saw Aminata pay homage to her late father, who passed away in late 2023 while she was recovering from injury. In a previous interview with Renee Paquette , Aminata admitted she almost quit wrestling after her father's death, but was inspired to keep going after finding photos of her wrestling in Japan on her father's phone. "Dad...I did it," Aminata tweeted. "I love you and I miss you so much." A few hours later, Aminata was back with a post featuring a photo of her smiling in her hotel room, with the TBS Championship over her right shoulder. "I still can't believe this, but I am your NEW TBS CHAMPION," Aminata tweeted. "The one and only is your brand new TBS Champion...omg!" I still can't believe this but I am your NEW TBS CHAMPION......The one and only is your brand new TBS champion..... omg 😱😱😱😱😱 pic.twitter.com/Y6UXMBfedu Aminata decided to save her third tweet on the matter till this morning, where she retweeted a post that showed the AEW women's locker room coming out to celebrate her victory. "Women empowerment," Aminata tweeted. "I love all my AEW women." Though Aminata had previously held championships on the independent circuit, including the Deadlock Pro Wrestling Women's World Championship late last year, her TBS Championship win marks the first time she has held a title in AEW. Like former TBS and AEW Women's World Champion Willow Nightingale, Aminata first gained notoriety in AEW by competing on its shoulder programs, "AEW Dark" and "AEW Dark: Elevation" during the COVID-19 pandemic. She would officially sign with AEW upon returning from injury around late 2023/early 2024 .

body: The spot saw Bron Breakker push Evans from the top of a ladder through the roof of an ambulance. Somehow, the ‘Young OG’ pushed through his injuries and appeared on the following episode of Raw. Speaking with Busted Open Radio , Evans broke his silence on the spot. “Like you said, it’s going to be remembered for decades. I’m grateful that I can be part of such a soon to be iconic moment. Who can say they’ve been part of a Money In The Bank ladder spot, which is insane, at 22. Not a lot of people can say that.” Je’Von was also asked to describe what he was feeling during that moment. “I don’t know. I feel going into the game, I already knew what it was, you feel me? I feel like I already knew what to expect, so I walked into the match open-minded for real. It was my first Money In The Bank match, number one I was just excited to be there. Number two, I was excited to be in the match. Number three, I was just nervous as hell.” Penta and Je’Von Evans are set to challenge for gold at WWE Crown Jewel. title: SiriusXM WWE Radio Listenership Up 20% From Launch Of Re-Branded Pro Wrestling Nation 24/7
raw_title: SiriusXM WWE Radio Listenership Up 20% From Launch Of Re-Branded Pro Wrestling Nation 24/7
body: WWE Radio is gaining ground on SiriusXM. Listening has climbed nearly 20% since the channel’s July launch and rebrand, according to CEO Jennifer Witz on today’s company earnings call. What We Know : SiriusXM shared the figure Thursday during its third quarter earnings call. WWE Radio took over channel 156 on July 27, replacing Pro Wrestling Nation 24/7. Busted Open Radio still anchors the daily lineup. Additionally, the channel now carries WWE podcasts, weekly show simulcasts and live event calls. WWE Radio recently moved up to Channel 93, placing it alongside other major sports programming including new local sports radio properties via Audacy. What Remains Unclear : SiriusXM did not disclose a raw audience number for WWE Radio compared to Pro Wrestling Nation 24/7. Likewise, it did not say how much growth came from SummerSlam , the channel’s first live event broadcast. Financial terms of the WWE partnership also remain private. What It Means : For SiriusXM, the numbers support its bet on fan-driven sports content. With heavy promotion from the WWE, it should come as no surprise to see increased usage and listening to the channel. The channel is marketed in all WWE programming and social media, plus includes high profile personalities from the company. As a result, WWE Radio could become a template for future brand-backed channels.

title: Shawn Michaels to replace Bruce Prichard in WWE creative
raw_title: Shawn Michaels reportedly expected to step into Bruce Prichard’s role
summary_src: Shawn Michaels reportedly will move from his WWE NXT role and take over Bruce Prichard's position after he steps down at WrestleMania 43.
body: There reportedly will be a shake-up to WWE’s creative and writing leadership following WrestleMania 43. Mike Johnson of PWInsider reported on Monday that WWE’s Executive Director – Creative Writing & Talent, Bruce Prichard, is expected to retire from his position at WrestleMania 43 next year. While he is departing from his full-time position at the company, the expectation is that he will remain connected with WWE as a consultant and work from home in Texas. On Thursday, PWInsider, citing multiple sources, reported that current head of NXT and Senior Vice President of Talent Development, Shawn Michaels, will step into Prichard’s role. Michaels, 61, is a close friend of WWE Chief Content Officer Paul Levesque and has been in his NXT role since September 2021. PWInsider added that this succession plan had been in place for some time and that Michaels will start to prepare for his new role months in advance.
summary: Bruce Prichard is expected to retire from his full-time role as WWE's Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent at WrestleMania 43 next year but will stay on as a consultant working from home in Texas. Shawn Michaels, who has led NXT since September 2021, will step into Prichard's position per PWInsider. The succession plan has been in place for some time and Michaels will begin preparing for the new duties months ahead of the transition.

summary_src: Grayson Waller has become the top star in NXT since returning to the brand in July, winning the NXT Championship and calling out anyone he feels isn't pulling their weight.
body: Grayson Waller has become the top star in NXT since returning to the brand in July, winning the NXT Championship and calling out anyone he feels isn’t pulling their weight. NXT has changed over the years with Shawn Michaels leading creative, AJ Styles taking on a bigger role as a coach and producer, and CM Punk making frequent visits to check in. Speaking to Chris Van Vliet on Insight , Waller commented on the influence of all three men. “AJ is a big one, especially since he’s been coming down to NXT recently and producing and working in the ring with guys, and he’s really, really fun to work with because I’m an AJ Styles fan. But he lets you go and lets you do you, and just makes everything better. He doesn’t force you to do things. ‘Hey, you need to do this.’ He’s just like, ‘What do you want to do?’ All right, ‘What if we do that?’ You’re like, oh, that’s the best idea. This is a young kid who just in 24 hours’ notice got put in the biggest match of his life, and he got beat. But seeing the look on their face when he came back through tells me everything I need to know about the future of the industry because those three guys are shaping it,” he said. title: WWE Not Considering Sphere As WrestleMania 43 Backup
raw_title: Backstage News On Possible Backup Venue For WWE WrestleMania 43
summary_src: WWE WrestleMania 43 is scheduled to take place some time next year in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Due to ongoing conflict, a backup venue has been rumored.
body: WWE Crown Jewel is scheduled to be live from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia on November 7 amidst increased danger as the conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis intensifies . The U.S. government has warned Americans against traveling to the country as it pulled out U.S. ambassadors and their families . On Wednesday, it was announced that Crown Jewel is being moved to a new venue , albeit still in Riyadh. One of the reasons that TKO is intent on keeping Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia is because it is the scheduled location for WrestleMania 43. As rumors have swirled about a potential backup venue in the U.S., a location in Las Vegas was suggested since WWE has held the last two WrestleManias in the city. One of the suggested venues was The Sphere. WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select has said that at this time, The Sphere is not being considered as a backup plan. WWE has had internal interest in having a show at the venue, but "no meaningful negotiations between the two sides have not transpired to our knowledge." They also report that WWE does have a "backup blueprint" should they need to move "The Show of Shows" back to North America and those plans are being kept secret. Fightful previously reported that WWE couldn't come to an agreement with The Sphere to display promotional material of Danhausen at the venue for WrestleMania 42. While a date for WrestleMania 43 hasn't been announced, there were two dates that WWE was considering last April ; the weekends of March 27 and April 10. "The Wizard of Oz Experience" is ongoing at The Sphere, including the weekend of March 27. John Mayer recently announced a residency at the venue beginning on April 8.
summary: WWE is keeping its upcoming Crown Jewel event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia despite the U.S. government travel warning and ongoing regional conflict. Per Fightful Select, The Sphere in Las Vegas is not currently viewed as a backup option for WrestleMania 43 even though the company has shown internal interest in the venue. No meaningful negotiations have taken place between WWE and The Sphere according to the report which notes the promotion does maintain a backup blueprint if needed.

title: Where Things Stand With TNA and OVW’s Working Relationship
raw_title: Where Things Stand With TNA and OVW’s Working Relationship
summary_src: TNA’s relationship with Ohio Valley Wrestling could be getting a lot more important in 2027. After months of talk about the two promotions working together, there’s now a new plan on the table that could change where TNA produces some of its weekly content.
body: According to PWInsider , TNA is planning to begin taping Xplosion from OVW’s Davis Arena in Louisville, Kentucky early next year. That would be a big significant change from the current setup, where Xplosion matches are taped alongside TNA Impact events. The reason apparently comes down to money. By producing Xplosion from Davis Arena instead of taking those matches on the road with Impact, TNA believes it can cut down on touring costs. The plan comes as TNA and OVW continue working toward a broader working relationship. We previously reported in June that the two sides were discussing an arrangement that could essentially see OVW serve as a developmental system for TNA , and the companies share some financial backers. TNA President Carlos Silva had also been spotted at several OVW events earlier this year while those discussions were taking place. However, PWInsider noted in its latest update that Silva hasn’t been seen at OVW events recently. There are still some pieces that apparently haven’t been communicated to the roster. TNA talent haven’t been given their 2027 calendars yet, so there could still be plenty more information coming about exactly how the company plans to structure its schedule next year. Either way, moving Xplosion to Davis Arena would give the developing TNA-OVW relationship something much more tangible. What started as talk about a possible developmental partnership could now result in TNA regularly producing one of its own shows out of OVW’s home building. Do you think taping Xplosion from OVW’s Davis Arena would be a good move for TNA as it heads into 2027? Let us know what you think in the comments. body: WWE has reportedly consulted Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles regarding the John Cena Classic. The report notes that Michaels and Styles were among several people consulted who do not typically have input on projects like this. The report also states that while the event was originally pitched as a “showcase and a milestone program for Club WWE,” a source indicated that it will likely stream elsewhere as well. Both Styles and Michaels were also the subject of reports on Thursday regarding Bruce Prichard’s role in WWE creative, with PWInsider reporting Michaels is expected to assume Prichard’s role and False Finish reporting that people within the Performance Center expect Styles to become more hands-on with NXT. The John Cena Classic is believed to be taking place in December, although WWE has not officially announced a date or location. Cena is scheduled to appear on Monday’s Raw from Brooklyn, where he has teased revealing more details about the event. Cena is also scheduled for the November 4 edition of NXT, which is set to go head-to-head with AEW Blood & Guts. title: Possible Shawn Michaels Replacement in WWE NXT Revealed
raw_title: Possible Shawn Michaels Replacement in WWE NXT Revealed
summary_src: Shawn Michaels is expected to move into a much bigger role in WWE after WrestleMania 43, but that leaves one pretty important question — who’s going to handle NXT once he’s gone? Well, a new update has pointed to a familiar name who could be getting a lot more involved with the brand.
body: According to False Finish, sources within WWE’s Performance Center expect AJ Styles to become more hands-on with NXT once Michaels moves into his new position. That doesn’t mean Styles has been officially chosen to replace Michaels, but there is apparently an expectation within the Performance Center that he’ll be taking on more responsibility. “Sources indicate to False Finish that those within the Performance Center expect AJ Styles to be more hands on within NXT as a result of Shawn Michaels promotion.” That’s an interesting name to have in the conversation. Styles has spent decades working around the world, including major runs in TNA, NJPW, and WWE. With that kind of experience, he certainly has plenty to offer younger talent trying to make it to the main roster. This comes after it was revealed that WWE is planning to promote Michaels into Bruce Prichard’s position as Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent following WrestleMania 43 in April 2027. Prichard is expected to step away from his full-time duties while remaining with the company as a consultant. According to PWInsider, WWE has already been preparing for Michaels to take over Prichard’s responsibilities, and this isn’t something that was just decided recently. “We are told that this succession plan has been in place for some time and that Michaels will start to prepare for the Prichard role in the months ahead.” Michaels has been running NXT since September 2021, so his expected promotion would leave WWE with another important position to figure out. He’s been responsible for the brand’s creative direction while also helping develop talent at the Performance Center, making his eventual departure from that role a pretty big deal. That’s where Styles could come in. While there’s no indication that WWE has offered him Michaels’ exact position, the expectation that he’ll become more involved with NXT raises questions about what the company might have planned for him. Whether that means working directly with talent, helping with creative, or taking on some other responsibilities remains to be seen. And there’s still plenty of time for things to change. Michaels isn’t expected to move into Prichard’s position until after WrestleMania 43, and WWE hasn’t announced any official plans for who will handle NXT once that happens. For now, Styles is a name worth keeping an eye on. Nobody has confirmed that he’ll be the next person running NXT, but people within the Performance Center are apparently expecting him to have a bigger presence once Michaels moves up. With months still to go before the transition, WWE has time to figure out exactly what that means. title: Orange Cassidy Names PAC His Greatest AEW Rival

summary_src: Orange Cassidy says PAC will always be his greatest rival. Speaking to Going Ringside in an interview published on Thursday, Orange Cassidy said that every time he got in the ring with PAC, it was special.
body: Speaking to Going Ringside in an interview published on Thursday, Orange Cassidy said that every time he got in the ring with PAC, it was special. Cassidy was asked about any rivalries he’s had in AEW that stick out in his mind, and answered: “There are multiple. Like obviously the stuff with the Death Riders and Moxley and Yuta. Chris Jericho is a very, very important one to me. But recently, I was reminded of the rivalry I had with PAC, and it’ll be one that I don’t think anybody will ever top. He and I, when we got in the ring together, it was special, and, I feel like he’ll be my greatest rival.” Cassidy also spoke about it having been a difficult period in the AEW locker room due to the recent deaths of PAC and Andy Williams . Cassidy said that being around the AEW locker room helps “take away some of the pain.” “I think being around everybody does help because we can support each other and be reminded of all the good things that those people have done for us. “And I think being with other people helps take away some of the pain that could be caused by it. But, I’m just lucky we got a great group of people all around us.” PAC and Orange Cassidy have had five different singles matches on AEW programming, the first at AEW Revolution 2020, which saw PAC defeat Cassidy in a match Dave Meltzer rated three and three-quarter stars. Cassidy defeated PAC for what was then known as the AEW All-Atlantic Championship on the October 12, 2022 Dynamite in Toronto in a match that Meltzer rated four and one-quarter stars. Their last singles match happened on the October 7, 2025 Title Tuesday edition of Dynamite, with Cassidy defeating PAC in a match Meltzer rated four stars. title: WWE Has Saved The Career Of This Failing Luchador
raw_title: WWE Has Saved The Career Of This Failing Luchador
body: By Andrew Kelly Published Oct 29, 2026, 3:00 PM EDT Andrew Kelly is a pro wrestling writer from The Wirral, England. With bylines on many pro wrestling websites, Andrew has proven himself to be very knowledgeable in the realms of WWE, AEW and more. Andrew is one of TheSportster's Match Reviewers and has covered the best matches of superstars like Cody Rhodes, MJF, Bianca Belair and more. He's also written hundreds of lists and features covering wrestling current events and history. He is also an MA Graduate from the University of Manchester, and a BA Graduate from Liverpool John Moores University, both in Creative Writing. Sign in to your TheSportster account With the success of Penta’s WWE arrival, the rise of AAA, and more focus being shared across lucha libre talent , fans had high hopes for the debut of former AEW star Rey Fenix , who was often considered to be one of the best in-ring workers on the planet. However, things were going terribly for a long time with WWE’s booking of Fenix, leaving him as one of the most misused wrestlers on the whole roster. It looked as though his WWE career was done and dusted before it had a chance to begin… however things have taken a positive turn. Fenix’s WWE career is in the process of being saved, and all it took was one small, simple piece of booking. Rey Fenix debuted in WWE on the Road To WrestleMania 41, instantly finding himself lost in the mix during a very busy period. Thanks to an injury to Rey Mysterio, Fenix was afforded an early opportunity to have a match at WrestleMania , taking on El Grande Americano. However, Fenix lost the match and quickly got lost in the shuffle. He wasn’t involved in any storylines for the next few months before entering a thrown-together tag team with Andrade - though this ended quickly after Andrade left the promotion. The luchador was left without any sort of direction for nearly a year, being used here and there in United States Championship open challenges to put others over, and being thrown around as fodder to elevate The MFTs . Fans were not reacting to Fenix because they’d been given zero reason to care about him, and this was all the fault of Triple H’s booking. It was slowly being considered by those aware of Fenix’s talents that his move over to WWE was a big mistake, especially since he was not being pushed at a time when the likes of Penta, Dragon Lee, Rey Mysterio and more luchadors were getting exposure. At AAA Noche De Los Grandes , Rey Fenix won the AAA Cruiserweight Championship in a victory that would prompt a change in his fortunes. For whatever reason, Triple H decided it was time to let Fenix do what he does best; wrestle in fast-paced, entertaining matches on television. All it took for Fenix to conjure up some love and support from fans was allowing him the freedom to showcase his style and do his talking between the ropes. title: WWE Sticking With Taped SmackDown Against AEW Dynamite on New Year's Day
raw_title: Backstage News On WWE SmackDown & AEW Dynamite Running Head-To-Head On New Year's Day
summary_src: "WWE SmackDown" and "AEW Dynamite" will go head-to-head on New Year's Day, but WWE isn't going to make special changes to its show.
body: New Year's Day 2027 will be a historic day in the world of professional wrestling as for the first-time ever, "WWE SmackDown" and "AEW Dynamite" will go head-to-head. It was recently announced that All Elite Wrestling will be running its annual New Year's Smash edition of "Dynamite" on Friday, January 1, meaning that AEW's flagship show will go up against a taped episode of "SmackDown" that will air on the same night. Despite WWE's efforts to counterprogram AEW and go out of its way to load up shows that go against AEW shows, it seems that the company isn't going to make any special arrangements for New Year's Day. According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , WWE has no plans on reshaping its taping schedule for the end of 2026, and has no intentions of airing a live "SmackDown" against "Dynamite," and will instead stick with the taped episode that will be filmed on December 28 at the Benchmark International Arena in Tampa, Florida, immediately after the final episode of "WWE Raw" for 2026. The main reason for this according to WWE sources is that it allows the talent to have New Year's Day off to enjoy celebrations with friends and family, and regardless of what AEW might have planned to kick off the new year, WWE isn't going to change its schedule just to try and beat "Dynamite" in the ratings. The ratings for that New Year's Day episode of "SmackDown" have been discussed internally, and some in WWE believe it will actually draw lower ratings than usual, even without the AEW competition, primarily due to it still airing in and around the holiday season. However, the fact that WWE isn't going to change its schedule is a sign of confidence that the show will outdraw "Dynamite" in the ratings, even with lower viewership than usual.
summary: WWE SmackDown and AEW Dynamite will air against each other for the first time on Friday, January 1, 2027, when AEW presents its annual New Year's Smash episode. Per Fightful Select, WWE has no plans to alter its taping schedule and will air a pre-taped SmackDown episode filmed on December 28, 2026, at the Benchmark International Arena in Tampa, Florida, right after the final Raw of the year instead of making it a live show. The decision allows talent time off around the holidays.

title: Major Latest On Stephanie Vaquer’s WWE Raw Absence Emerges: How Long Will She Be Away?
raw_title: Major Update on Stephanie Vaquer’s WWE Raw Absence Emerges: How Long Will She Be Away?
body: Vaquer was set to face Becky Lynch in the main event in a match to determine the No. 1 contender for the Women's World Championship. When Vaquer could not make it to the show, WWE changed the main event to Lynch challenging Liv Morgan for the title. The match ended in a disqualification when Morgan's Judgment Day stablemates Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez interfered just as Lynch was about to win. Dave Meltzer gave an update on Vaquer's status on Wrestling Observer Radio , saying the illness is not serious but that there is no set timeline for her return. "She's ill. It's not anything. I was told it's nothing terribly serious or anything," Meltzer said. "But she's ill, and she's out. Indefinitely in the sense that it's not like it's a week. It's something that's indeterminate as far as when she'll be back." Meltzer also explained how the absence changed the plans for Raw. "But that's why they didn't do that match. It wasn't about an injury, and it wasn't a worked storyline. They were going to do the match on Monday night and she got sick and could not come. And that's why they did the Becky Lynch-Liv Morgan. And that's why they did the DQ, because they didn't want to beat Becky Lynch. But it wasn't a match that they had planned, so they did the DQ that way, to get out of it essentially." The illness is separate from the injuries Vaquer has dealt with this year. She has been slowed by ankle and shoulder injuries in 2026, including a minor ankle injury suffered at Money in the Bank on October 10. She was medically cleared to compete on the October 26 episode of Raw before the illness kept her out. The good news is that Vaquer's issue is not expected to be serious. After dealing with ankle and shoulder injuries this year, she had been cleared to return to the ring, so an illness that is not considered serious is better news than another injury. The concern is that there is no clear timeline, which makes it harder for WWE to plan around her. Meltzer's explanation also clears up the confusing finish on Raw. The disqualification looked like a way to protect Lynch, and Meltzer said that was the reason for it. WWE did not want Lynch to lose a title match that was put together on short notice, and the DQ gave the company a way out without hurting her. title: 7 Wrestling Grudges That NEVER Really Ended
raw_title: 7 Wrestling Grudges That NEVER Really Ended
body: Wrestling is founded on confrontation. By its very nature, a great feud is built upon the believability that two (or more) people hate each other's guts and cannot stand the sight of one another, then taking that heat and turning it into hard-hitting, microphone-wielding beef for our entertainment. So it was in the beginning, so it will be forevermore . In some of the most beloved grudges of all time, this natural dislike for one another will spill into the real world. Be it from the dirt sheets or it just being so apparent that it's impossible to ignore, two performers can dislike one another so much that their issues with one another don't end when the camera stops rolling or they come back through the curtain. That brings us to today's list, and grudges that refuse to fully disappear. Sure, there might be moments of repair and short periods of peace between the two combatants , but underneath these minor moments of peace lies a raging war set to go on forever. Try as they may to let bygones be bygones, these are seven feuds that will never truly be over. It has warmed the soul to see Bret Hart get his flowers from all corners of wrestling's kingdom in recent years. Fans have a newfound appreciation of his peerless in-ring work and the engaging feuds he was part of, and wrestlers will regularly wax lyrical about why The Excellence of Execution is the perfect nickname for one of the best to ever engage in their craft. This has been compounded by WWE increasing their love for the Hitman. His match with Steve Austin at WrestleMania 13 was the first to be inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame, but there was a telling moment during that ceremony that suggests that Bret's feelings for WWE head honcho Paul Levesque aren't quite over. Bret was caught on camera rolling his eyes at Triple H after The Game shook his hand on stage at WrestleMania 41 . Bret's honesty is one of wrestling's greatest gifts, and the saying "a picture is worth a thousand words" is perfect for this moment. Bret never misses a chance to suggest that Levesque doesn't really have his respect as a wrestler or as a booker, and this was yet another golden example of this well-known theory. Terry Bezer hasn't written a bio just yet, but if they had... it would appear here.
summary: By its very nature, a great feud is built upon the believability that two people hate each other's guts and cannot stand the sight of one another. This natural dislike for one another will spill into the real world.

title: Pruett’s Pause: 10 Thoughts on AEW Dynamite
raw_title: Pruett’s Pause: 10 Thoughts on AEW Dynamite: Queen Aminata’s crowning moment, Darby Allin vs. Josh Alexander, Full Gear gets a main event and Anarchy in the Arena
body: By Will Pruett , ProWrestling.net Co-Senior Staffer ( @itswilltime ) – AEW likes to have their named shows (Fright Night, Beach Break) end with big babyface moments. This show was no exception, with Queen Aminata toppling Persephone (and Britt Baker) to win the TBVS Championship. This was a great moment for Aminata, who has battled back from injuries. I do wish we knew who Aminata was just a little bit more. A sit-down interview with Renee Young would have done her a lot of good in the last two weeks. AEW could have told a better story going into this match, knowing the moment was coming. – The Last Outfit is now The Cut, and I cannot say Jay White’s combination of two failed factions is off to an amazing start. While we did need a big heel force to stand up to The Death Riders, combining two factions people were not connecting to and turning them – then changing the name multiple times – is not the way to create that heel force. Jay White is a faction leader I enjoy, but the rest of this team seems completely interchangeable. The Cut does not feel special and does not seem like the vehicle that will make Jay White a main event star. – The Cut vs. The Death Riders in Anarchy in the Arena will create complete and total chaos in Phoenix, and it disrupts AEW’s calendar nicely. Jon Moxley is amazing in matches like this, and it should be a great time in a hardcore party match for folks who were there live. This keeps AEW from having to roll out another Moxley vs. Jay White singles match so soon after their last one. It also may make White’s journey to the Continental Championship have to run through the Continental Classic, which does start soon. – Kyle Fletcher had a fun match with Jack Perry (who thought he could do a Muscle Buster for some reason??!?) and followed it up with a challenge for Will Ospreay’s AEW World Championship. I like this match much more than I liked the Clockwork Carnage match at WrestleDream. There are actual stakes to a one-on-one title match that do not exist in an eight-man situation. Fletcher has a solid claim against Ospreay, and they are really great opponents for each other. I hope Ospreay manages to produce some memorable segments and promos in this journey. – Swerve Strickland as the only man in this six-man match who wants to go down the path of Texas Death is a nice storytelling device. It’s true to who Kofi and Austin Creed are. It has been true to who Hangman Page tries to be as well. Brody King being willing to do anything to find and help Bandido is also true. This story has more depth than most trios stories in AEW history, particularly because of the Swerve and Hangman history. When we finally see these men in Texas Death, it will be interesting and violent and exciting. Full Gear is going to be a wild show with this and Anarchy in the Arena. – The Motor City Machine Guns vs. FTR part three was alright, but this best-of-five series does feel like we are rushing through it. title: Lil Yachty Details Scary Vision Loss Scare
raw_title: Lil Yachty Opens Up About Temporarily Losing Vision In Left Eye: "I Literally Thought I Was Gonna Be Blind Forever"
summary_src: Lil Yachty opens up about his health scare. Songwriter, rapper, producer, and current WWE talent Lil Yachty sat down with Complex for an interview before his concert performance. Yachty revealed that he had a health scare and lost 80 percent of the vision in his left eye.
body: Songwriter, rapper, producer, and current WWE talent Lil Yachty sat down with Complex for an interview before his concert performance. Yachty revealed that he had a health scare and lost 80 percent of the vision in his left eye. He stated that he’s fine now. “I was sick for the last two weeks to be honest. I hadn’t did sh*t. I was in lockdown. I just got back right.” Yachty was asked to follow up on that, and he said, “Yeah, but not like coughing sick. I had a whole other sickness that I don’t even wanna talk about. I was down bad. I actually thought I was gonna die. But I almost did. I went blind in my left eye. Yeah, 80 percent. It was bad. I could not see at all.” He continued, “Scared the sh*t out of me. I literally thought I was gonna be blind forever. That type of sh*t… make you so grateful. All the sh*t we take for granted, like our eyesight, and you be like, ‘Oh my God bruh, I never knew.’ We get older in life and things become so minuscule to us… Majority of us have been blessed to have it our entire lives, and then it just becomes so minuscule. It is something to have your eyesight.” Yachty added, “I’m fine.” He continued, “I couldn’t see anyone. I was in a lockdown. I was just in a dark room alone.” Yachty was last on WWE TV on the 9/11 Friday Night SmackDown, where he was attacked by Baron Corbin, who was feuding with Yachty and Trick Williams at the time.
summary: Lil Yachty revealed in a Complex interview that he recently suffered a serious health issue that caused him to lose 80 percent of his vision in his left eye.
