title: Lil Yachty Eyes Full-Time WWE Role
raw_title: Lil Yachty Wants To Be Full-Time With WWE: “If I Climb The Ranks In WWE & Get The Checks That I Want, This Music Sh*t Can Kiss Me Goodbye"
summary_src: Lil Yachty states that he's stepping away from music if things line up correctly with WWE. Two-time Grammy-nominated music artist and producer Lil Yachty sat down with Complex for a chat.
body: Lil Yachty states that he’s stepping away from music if things line up correctly with WWE. Two-time Grammy-nominated music artist and producer Lil Yachty sat down with Complex for a chat. As the conversation moved along, Yachty spoke about his venture into WWE, where he is the manager/ally to United States Champion Trick Williams. He was asked what he has learned from WWE that he can take into his music performances. He said there’s no correlation because WWE is more militant. He stated that he loves it and is trying to be full-time with the company. Yachty added that if the pieces come together with WWE, he’ll never release another album and music can kiss him goodbye. “Nah, no correlation. It’s so much different; it’s so much more militant you gotta be in WWE. This is my show. I call the shots, I make the rules, I do what I want. WWE, it’s time, it’s cameras… producers. It’s so different. It’s like militant, and you gotta be on your sh*t… I always talk to wrestlers about this: You just don’t have the leeway you have. I can go up there, talk sh*t, f*ck up. You got X amount of time and you gotta make everything count and you gotta captivate that audience. You don’t see them again till next Friday, and you got a real small time in your segment to get your point across, your message across and be remembered for six more days until next Friday, and hope that you captivated so good that Friday, that, in them six days, you back on TV again. If you f*ck up or you do some bullsh*t, you might not be on TV that next week. It’s a lot more militant and disciplined, and I love it, man. I’d like to go full-time; I’m trying to go full-time. I won’t ever put an album out ever again.” He continued, “If I climb the ranks in WWE and get the checks that I want, this music sh*t can kiss me goodbye. I swear to God. I will be back flipping, getting thrown through tables and whatever else until my body give out on me.” Yachty has not been on WWE TV since he was attacked by Baron Corbin on the 9/11 Friday Night SmackDown. Yachty made his in-ring debut against Corbin at Sunday Night’s Main Event.
summary: Lil Yachty told Complex he is open to leaving music entirely if his WWE opportunity with United States Champion Trick Williams develops into a full-time position with the pay he desires. The two-time Grammy-nominated artist described WWE as far more structured and militant than his music career, noting the strict timing, cameras and producers involved. He expressed his love for the environment and said he is actively trying to make the transition permanent.

title: On the Record: Nia Jax Explains Why She Still Hasn’t Joined The Bloodline on WWE TV
raw_title: Nia Jax Explains Why She Still Hasn’t Joined The Bloodline on WWE TV
summary_src: Nia Jax might have the family connection to The Bloodline, but WWE still hasn’t pulled the trigger on actually putting her with the group on television. As it turns out, Jax is perfectly fine with that and has a pretty simple reason why.
body: During her appearance on the Keep It Aloha podcast , Jax was asked by a fan why she hasn’t joined The Bloodline on WWE television despite being part of the legendary Samoan wrestling dynasty. Jax pointed out that, technically, she already considers herself part of The Bloodline because of her family connection, even if that hasn’t translated into an on-screen role. She also brought up the family tree that Dwayne “The Rock” Johnson previously shared. But instead of automatically being thrown into the group because of who she’s related to, Jax said she actually appreciates getting the chance to establish herself on her own. “Well, technically, I am in The Bloodline. I don’t know if you saw the chart that Dwayne put up. I’m up there. But, you know, it all just depends on storyline for wrestling, right? Everybody wants, like, ‘Oh, why isn’t it just automatic being there?’ But I actually really appreciate the fact that I can carve out my own name by myself.” That doesn’t mean Jax is completely against getting involved if WWE ever decides the story calls for it. She made it clear that if the guys ever need some backup, there are several women in the family who could get that call. Jax specifically mentioned herself, Naomi and Tamina as options if the situation ever comes up. For now, though, she’s happy being part of the family without needing The Bloodline association on television. “But if the boys ever needed me, you know, they’ve got Naomi, they’ve got me, they’ve got Tamina. They can always call us whenever is needed. But technically, I am in The Bloodline, just not on TV.” So Jax isn’t sitting around wondering why WWE hasn’t put her in The Bloodline. She likes having her own identity, and whether that family connection ever becomes part of her television character will ultimately come down to whether WWE finds the right storyline for it. title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Admits He Needs Therapy But Says His Personal Issues Made Him Successful
raw_title: Paul Heyman Admits He Needs Therapy But Says His Personal Issues Made Him Successful
summary_src: Paul Heyman knows he needs therapy, but don’t expect him to rush into a therapist’s office anytime soon. The WWE veteran says his personal issues are a big reason he’s successful, and he has absolutely no interest in changing the things that made him who he is.
body: While speaking with Graham Bensinger , Heyman was asked whether he’d ever dealt with his personal issues in therapy. His answer was no, and he immediately questioned why he’d even bother when those same issues have helped him build his career. “Being as f*cked up as I am has made me who I am. It’s made me successful. I embrace my flaws.” Heyman then admitted that he probably has childhood trauma and could benefit from therapy. But he wasn’t treating any of that like some major revelation. He rattled off his personal issues like he was reading a grocery list. “Do I need therapy? Sure I do. Do I have childhood trauma? I’m sure I do.” And that was just the beginning. Heyman went on to describe himself as having ADHD, being addicted to the dopamine effect, and displaying overcompensatory behavior. He made those claims about himself without hesitation. “Do I exhibit every single symptom of overcompensatory behavior? Sure I do. Am I ADHD? Of course I am. Am I addicted to the dopamine effect? Of course I am.” “And you want to know what? I’m fine with it cuz it makes me me.” Heyman also pointed to his upbringing, explaining that he was raised around people whose lives had been affected by the Holocaust and the Great Depression. He believes those experiences played a role in shaping his family and his own personality. The bottom line is that Heyman isn’t denying he’s got problems. He’s admitting they exist and arguing that they’ve helped him get where he is today. After decades of success in professional wrestling, he doesn’t see much reason to start changing now. Heyman might believe therapy could help him, but he’s not exactly desperate to become a different person. As far as he’s concerned, the Wise Man wouldn’t be the Wise Man without all those flaws that came with him. title: On the Record: Paul Heyman Explains Why He Doesn’t Want WWE Fans Knowing the Real Him

summary_src: Paul Heyman has no problem playing one of WWE’s most confident personalities, but he doesn’t want fans getting too familiar with the real person behind the character. In fact, Heyman admits he’s uncomfortable being himself in public because it means letting people see his flaws.
body: While speaking with Graham Bensinger , Heyman was asked about his reluctance to show his true personality outside WWE. He didn’t try to deny it. Instead, he explained that being himself means exposing parts of his life he’d rather keep private. “It’s vulnerable. It’s flaws and all. It’s just me and I’m very private.” Bensinger then wanted to know what exactly Heyman was worried people might discover. But according to Heyman, there isn’t some huge secret he’s desperately trying to hide. He just knows he’s got personal issues like everybody else. “It’s not a concern. I’m just a terribly fu*ked up person like everybody else. I just embrace my f*cked-up-ed-ness.” Heyman then made it clear he isn’t interested in pretending he’s perfect just because he’s a major WWE personality. He believes everybody has their own problems, and he’s perfectly comfortable acknowledging his. “I’m special. I’m different. I’m f*cked up. You’re f*cked up in your way. He’s f*cked up in his way. She’s f*cked up in her way. All respect to everybody in the room. And I embrace it.” That’s a pretty different attitude from what fans usually see on WWE television. Heyman can stand in front of thousands of people and deliver a promo without blinking, but apparently, letting those same people see who he really is makes him uncomfortable. And he doesn’t seem interested in changing that arrangement. He can be the Wise Man when the cameras are rolling and keep the rest of his life to himself. For Heyman, there’s a clear difference between entertaining WWE fans and inviting them into his private world. He’s happy to give them the character they’ve followed for decades, but the real Paul Heyman isn’t necessarily part of the deal. title: On the Record: Paul Heyman on Why He Hates When Fans Catch Him Wearing Shorts and Flip-Flops in Public
raw_title: Paul Heyman on Why He Hates When Fans Catch Him Wearing Shorts and Flip-Flops in Public
summary_src: Paul Heyman doesn’t want WWE fans seeing him dressed like a regular guy, and he’s not joking about it. The Wise Man says it genuinely bothers him when people catch him wearing shorts and flip-flops because it ruins the image he’s spent years building.
body: While speaking with Graham Bensinger , Heyman was asked why he wears a suit and tie practically everywhere, even when he’s going out late at night. His explanation was simple — that’s what people expect from Paul Heyman. But unfortunately for him, there have been times when he’s been caught looking nothing like his WWE character. “Yeah, it’s what people expect of me. I’ve also been photographed like this in flip-flops and shorts, running down to the local convenience store.” Heyman explained that he’ll occasionally head to a convenience store wearing an old T-shirt and shorts, only for somebody to recognize him and ask for a selfie. And while he’d rather not be photographed looking like that, he’s not going to blow off a fan. “Some truck will go by and the guy will stop and go, ‘Hey, Paul Heyman, how you doing? Hey, can we take a selfie?’ And I’m not going to say no. I’m not going to be rude.” The problem is that those pictures end up online, leaving Heyman looking a whole lot different from the guy fans see every week on WWE television. He even joked about one of the more embarrassing possibilities. “So, I end up with a selfie and it ends up on the internet and there I am, you know, with a pair of shorts with one testicle hanging out and flip-flops.” When Bensinger asked whether that actually bothered him, Heyman said yes. And his reason had nothing to do with being embarrassed about his appearance. He simply doesn’t want fans seeing him out of character. “Because I’m out of character. That’s who they pay to see. If you ask a fan of Paul Heyman, their image of me is I swim in this.” Heyman even suggested that some fans believe he wears his suit around the clock, and he’d rather let them keep believing it. “People think I shower in this. And I’m not going to deprive them of that image because this is what they come to expect of the Wise Man.” So apparently, getting caught in flip-flops is a bigger deal to Heyman than most people would imagine. He’s spent decades selling the Paul Heyman character, and he’s not interested in ruining that image just because he needed something from the convenience store. Heyman may not actually sleep in a suit, but he certainly wants fans to think he does. And if maintaining that illusion means dressing like he’s headed to WWE television every time he leaves the house, so be it. title: Tommaso Ciampa Misses RKO On Kyle Fletcher In St. Louis
raw_title: Tommaso Ciampa Attempts RKO On Fellow AEW Star After Mistaking Him For Randy Orton
summary_src: Tommaso Ciampa attempts, and fails, to hit an RKO on a fellow AEW star after mistaking the individual for WWE star Randy Orton while in St. Louis
body: AEW/Facebook AEW's Tommaso Ciampa may be a psycho killer, but he's also a guy who likes to have fun, as evident by his "Glorious Bombing" with Johnny Gargano over the years, or his assault on Andrade El Idolo's pants at AEW WrestleDream . But his latest attempt at having a good time may have come back to haunt him. Taking to Instagram , Ciampa posted a video from St. Louis, Missouri, where "Fright Night Dynamite" and "Collision" were held this week. Remembering that St. Louis was the hometown of his former co-worker, Randy Orton, Ciampa declared that he was finally go to hit Orton with his own move, the RKO, out of nowhere, the return of a bit Ciampa did while in WWE. The video would then cut to hours later, where Ciampa appeared to have found Orton and was preparing to deliver an RKO. He would miss the move, however, and land back first on a trainer's table, quickly realizing that it was not Orton he nearly RKO'd, but the man who beat him for the AEW TNT Championship earlier this year, Kyle Fletcher . A befuddled Fletcher questioned what Ciampa was doing before the "Psycho Killer" admitted he thought Fletcher was "someone else." Still confused, Fletcher let the whole thing going, leaving Ciampa to groan in pain on the trainer's table. As eventful as Ciampa's adventures were prior to "Dynamite," he had just as much going on when the TBS/HBO Max cameras started rolling. Despite losing to Andrade at WrestleDream, Ciampa called out the luchador for a rematch, while also declaring that he was the best signing in AEW history. This prompted recent AEW signee and former Ciampa opponent Ilja Dragunov to come down to the ring and challenge Ciampa to a fight. Ciampa refused in order to focus on his "Collision" match with Matt Sydal, though its expected he and Dragunov will face off again sooner than later.

title: Tony Khan Praises AEW Ticket Affordability
raw_title: Tony Khan Says AEW Has ‘The Most Affordable Tickets in TV Wrestling’
body: AEW President Tony Khan spoke to First Coast News this week to promote AEW Dynamite: Blood & Guts, which is set for next week in Jacksonville, Florida. During the chat, Khan discussed the value and affordability of AEW’s ticket prices. Ticket prices have been a hotly debated topic in the wrestling community as of late, as WWE has been criticized for the rising price of its ticket sales. Below are some highlights of Khan’s comments: “Well, AEW is where the best wrestle. We have the best wrestlers, and I think we have the best fans. We built a huge following. AEW is now on in over 150 countries all over the world. We’ve just, in recent weeks, done incredible shows in Paris, in London, and Jacksonville is where we started, and the place where we’ve run the most shows of any city is in Jacksonville, but it’s always been in Daily’s place. We’ve never been to VyStar [Veterans Memorial Arena], and after all these years, I wanted to bring AEW’s biggest AEW Dynamite of the year, Blood and Guts, which, you know, I know we’re gonna talk a lot about what Blood and Guts is, but it is an incredible night of wrestling. It’s gonna be one of the most watched episodes on TV, and you’re gonna wanna be there in person to see this because it is so exciting, and you’ll see it in AEW.” “Blood and Guts is a two-ring double steel cage match with some of the greatest wrestlers in the world fighting it out, and the only way to win the match is to make your opponent submit or surrender, and it is just absolutely as advertised. You’re gonna see some blood, and you’re gonna see great wrestlers, great wrestling, and it’s gonna be hard-hitting. It’s gonna be exciting. Wednesday Night Dynamite has become one of the top shows on cable, and this is our biggest episode of the year. So it’s very fitting for our debut at VyStar that we’re bringing this episode on Wednesday, November 4th.” “I guarantee it’s gonna be worth the value, and AEW also has the most affordable tickets in TV wrestling. I guarantee you we’re not gonna take an arm and a leg for this. This is gonna be a good night at the wrestling matches, and you know, I am very proud of what we’ve been able to do here. It was being associated with the Jaguars, being associated with the city of Jacksonville, that made it possible to launch AEW. It was right out here in January of 2019 that we told the. We’re launching a new wrestling promotion. We set it 600 ft from where you and I are standing right now, and it’s coming here to VyStar. You gotta be there for Blood and Guts, Wednesday, November 4th. It’s gonna be one of the greatest wrestling events ever in Jacksonville, I promise you.” As previously reported , the latest update for Blood & Guts had it at about 3,068, with about 1,156 seats remaining. Tony Khan presents AEW Dynamite: Blood and Guts on Wednesday, November at the VyStar Veterans Memorial Arena in Jacksonville, Florida. The show will be broadcast live on TBS starting at 8:00 pm ET. It will also be simulcast on HBO

title: What AEW’s Future Really Looks Like — Tony Khan on Skydance
raw_title: Tony Khan on Skydance: What AEW’s Future Really Looks Like
body: Tony Khan reportedly flew to Los Angeles on Friday, October 23, to meet with Skydance, AEW’s new TV owner. Dave Meltzer shared the report on the October 25 Wrestling Observer Radio, as relayed by Ringside News. Neither AEW nor Skydance has confirmed the meetings. Meltzer said Khan then headed to Winston-Salem for Collision. He admits he doesn’t know the details. He did say Khan came out “extremely happy, much happier than he has been about this.” For kayfabe purists, everything here is real-world business news. Khan has stayed on message for weeks. Before the September 23 Dynamite, he said the merger “will make AEW stronger,” Wrestling Inc. reported. He also praised David Ellison as someone who “loves professional wrestling.” On October 6, the day the deal closed, Khan spoke on a Grand Slam Paris stream on X before Dynamite. “My first day working for Skydance… we’re going to have a great future here,” he said. On the WrestleDream media call around October 15, Slam Wrestling reported, Khan said he was excited Channing Dungey is returning. He also praised JB Perrette. After WrestleDream, Khan went further, according to POST Wrestling on October 18. “I’ve had a few great conversations with David Ellison about AEW,” he said. He called Ellison “a wrestling fan” his own age. He said the combination brings “more exciting opportunities” and “more resources.” Notice the pattern. Every quote is about mood and relationships. None of them mentions dollars or dates. That is normal for a promoter in public. It also means the quotes tell us how Khan feels, and little about what Skydance plans. So what is actually on paper? Cultaholic reported around October 11 that the Paramount Skydance deal was valued at $110 billion. AEW stays on TBS, TNT and HBO Max in the US until at least the end of 2027, per Cultaholic. That runs under a $555 million TV deal that began in early 2025. The history matters too. AEW has aired on WBD networks since 2019, when Dynamite debuted on TNT . Paramount Skydance announced plans to acquire WBD in February 2026, Cultaholic reported. The deal closed October 6, per POST Wrestling (October 18). It combined TBS, TNT, HBO Max, Paramount+, CBS and the Warner Bros. and Paramount studios. Wrestling Inc. reported around October 7 that the combined company is simply called Skydance. The sleeper detail is ownership. Skydance took over WBD’s minority stake in AEW, according to Cultaholic. My read: a partner with equity has a reason to want AEW to grow. Still, any honest look at AEW’s business model starts with that 2027 date. Khan’s comfort is contractual for now. The renewal is the real story. Then there is the awkward part. Sports Illustrated reported around October 16 that Paramount+ has a major distribution partnership with TKO Group. TKO owns WWE and UFC, and all UFC events stream on Paramount+, per SI. TKO is a direct AEW competitor. That means Skydance now does business with both sides of the wrestling war. Khan’s public answer is to court E

The rapper who has been aligned with Trick Williams on WWE programming recently spoke to Complex about his work in WWE. He described WWE as more “militant” than his music career, but also said he’s “trying to go full-time.” “You got a real small time in your segment to get your point across, your message across and be remembered for six more days until next Friday, you know, and hope that you captivated so good that Friday that in six days you’re back on TV again. So, it’s a lot more militant and disciplining. I love it, man.” “If I go full time, I’m trying to go full time, I won’t ever put an album out ever again.” “If I climb the ranks in WWE and get the checks that I want, this music s–t can kiss me goodbye. I swear to God, I will be back flipping, getting thrown through tables, and whatever else until my body give out on me.” Yachty first appeared on SmackDown on April 3 alongside Williams, who was preparing to challenge Sami Zayn for the United States Championship at WrestleMania 42. title: On the Record: Matt Hardy Explains Why TNA Is A 'Better Fit' Than AEW For He And Jeff Hardy
raw_title: Matt Hardy Explains Why TNA Is A 'Better Fit' Than AEW For He And Jeff Hardy
body: In an episode of his " The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy " podcast, Matt looked back at their time in AEW and expressed why he thinks TNA was a better decision for them . "Jeff and I had some frustrations while in AEW, you know, it's just – right now TNA is a much better fit for us," he admitted. Matt added that TNA has rejuvenated their love for wrestling again. At the same time, Matt noted that Jeff's issues in AEW were bad, and even he doesn't think they ever rebounded from the lost momentum. Interestingly, Matt still recited the wrestling adage of "never say never," suggesting they aren't closed off to an AEW return. "That's one thing I have truly learned in pro wrestling," he continued. "You never know where you're gonna end up. Don't ever say 'I'm never going to do this because,' because you'll end up being a hypocrite." While The Hardys are enjoying their run in TNA, Matt Hardy has been taking the prospect of retirement more seriously, it still isn't immediate to him but he also suggested what he and Jeff Hardy might do to keep themselves busy once they step away. "You never know where the twists and turns of life is going to take you, but yes I do feel like I'm not putting any kind of bookend on my wrestling career now, I'm not putting [it] on any timetable, I'm just going by how I feel," he explained. "I almost feel Jeff is all into music now, and he had a really successful outing at that Louder Than Life festival that he did and he loved it so much." Matt noted that Jeff has actually been slowing down on in-ring competition to do more music and is actively working at that transition. "I think me, on the other hand, I think I will transition to being a backstage role," he added, expressing that he's a lifer when it comes to pro wrestling, and wants to be active in ring for as long as he can and then later step out to help others and give back to the industry . "As of right now? I feel really good, I'll just keep doing what I love, man; I'd be silly not to!"

title: TNA inducts ODB, Konnan & Amazing Red into Hall of Fame
raw_title: TNA inducts ODB, Konnan & Amazing Red into Hall of Fame
body: Three names joined TNA Wrestling’s Hall of Fame on Sunday night. LAX member Konnan, Knockout wrestler ODB and X-Division stand-out Amazing Red were inducted at the Yeungling Center in Tampa Bay, Florida on Sunday night, just before this year’s Bound for Glory event took place. Tennessee’s ODB, a mainstay in the Knockout division through the mid-2000s to early 2010s, reflected on the “dirt roads, shady motels, truck stops, sleeping on air matresses, cheap-ass promoters and long car rides filled with some of the greatest conversations and memories of my life.” “And, somehow, those dirt roads led me right here, tonight, standing in front of you as a TNA Hall of Famer,” she said. She gave credit to her mother, the “original ODB,” who was in attendance: “I know it wasn’t easy watching your little girl chase her dream, but you never tried to change me. You loved me through every crazy chapter of my life, and a lot of who I am comes from you.” ODB ended her speech with advice: “Treat people with respect, look people in the eye. You’re no better than anyone else. Your titles, your matches, your gimmicks don’t mean s*** if you’re an asshole. Shake hands, stay humble, work hard. Love y’all.” “She slapped her ass, took a swig of her flask and said ‘Bitch, I’m doing things my way,'” Traci Brooks, who introduced ODB alongside Al Snow, said about her. “She proved to little girls everywhere, you don’t have to change who you are to fit in. Sometimes you have to let people be exactly who they are.” Konnan, who led the Latin American Xchange faction in TNA, was not present at the event but was inducted by NXT’s Cruz Montana (formerly Mike Santana). “This man showed us all what it meant to be a loud and proud Latino in this game,” Montana said. “The few years that I got to spend sitting under his learning tree was probably the greatest blessing I’ve ever been given in this business and in my life.” Amazing Red, a high-flying cruiserweight who went on three separate reigns with the X-Division title from 2003 to 2010, was visibly emotional while reflecting on his Hall of Fame status. “I was just a small Spanish kid from Brooklyn just chasing the dream, trying to make this a reality,” Red said, before taking a step back to fight tears. In a surprising twist, Amazing Red announced mid-speech that he’ll be part of tonight’s X-Division title showdown. “You really cannot watch pro wrestling in the year 2026 and not see someone or something that drew inspiration from the amazing trail that Red blazed,” Frankie Kazarian, who inducted Red, said. “His fingerprints are all over the industry.”
summary: The latest: LAX member Konnan, Knockout wrestler ODB and X-Division stand-out Amazing Red were inducted at the Yeungling Center in Tampa Bay. She gave credit to her mother, the original ODB, who was in attendance: I know it wasn’t easy watching your little girl chase her dream.

title: NXT Halloween Havoc Watchability Grades Revealed
raw_title: Your NXT Halloween Havoc watchability index | Big Vinny V
summary_src: If you’ve ever listened to the Bryan & Vinny Show, you’re probably aware that I am not the biggest NXT fan in the world. But I try to be a fair man. And NXT has a premium live event this weekend: Halloween Havoc airs this Saturday, on (appropriately) Halloween.
body: If you’ve ever listened to the Bryan & Vinny Show, you’re probably aware that I am not the biggest NXT fan in the world. But I try to be a fair man. And NXT has a premium live event this weekend: Halloween Havoc airs this Saturday, on (appropriately) Halloween. It should be a better show than NXT’s weekly product. But is it worth your time? Let’s preview the card one match at a time, giving each one a watchability grade of Must-See, Watch If You Have Time, or Skip It. This is a singles match for Jordan’s NXT Women’s Championship. The build for this is illogical to a mind-flaying degree. Sinclair had been suspended for attacking a referee, but stole Lady Shani’s mask to enter and win a battle royal for the Halloween Havoc title shot. The next week, NXT general manager Robert Stone plainly said that Sinclair should not have been allowed in the battle royal … then came out later to lift her suspension and make the Havoc match official. Whatever. Now we’re here, and the match should overdeliver compared to its nonsensical build. Jordan is perhaps the best athlete in NXT, with a track record of strong big-match performance. She has four singles matches this year that were rated **** or higher by our own Dave Meltzer. Sinclair’s resume isn’t nearly so strong, but she’s hugely popular with the NXT fans, and will be motivated to shine in what will be, by far, the highest-profile match of her career. Another singles match with gold on the line—in this case, Waller’s NXT Championship. Waller won that belt from D’Angelo at Heatwave in August, in a match that also included Cruz Montana and Zilla Fatu. D’Angelo had to fight his way back to a title shot, finally beating Myles Borne on the October 13 episode of NXT to win a shot here. What’s interesting here is that a title win would probably be bad news for D’Angelo. This month marks his five-year anniversary in NXT. He and Waller have called each other “cornerstones” of NXT in the build to this match, which is a nice way of saying “career minor-leaguer.” Waller had his time in the main roster. He has won championships at WrestleMania. Even if his career since then has not been as successful as anyone hoped, he has still walked a path that D’Angelo hasn’t. If D’Angelo wins here, it would show a lack of faith in him to ever take steps down that road. If he loses, it would likely mean he’s finally getting a shot at the big time. Watchability grade: Must-See, just to check D’Angelo’s status in the company Zaria is the NXT Women’s North American Champion, but her title is not on the line. That’s because Dame specifically said she did not want the title on the line here, because she wants to prove Zaria’s gimmick is fake and that she’s still the same nerd who was in band and drama classes in high school. It’s a god-awful storyline told in a series of wretched promos and I would not waste one second of my life watching the payoff if this were not my job. This will be a Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal match. The wheel

title: Sirius XM sees big audience growth for WWE Radio
raw_title: Partnering with WWE pays off for Sirius XM
body: That was part of what Sirius XM was banking on when they turned their dedicated pro wrestling channel into “WWE Radio” a few months ago. The satellite radio company’s CEO Jennifer Witz touted the growth of the channel since July, which still features Busted Open Radio as its flagship (albeit with less talk of non-WWE or WWE partner promotions). That show is now joined by WWE-produced podcasts and even audio simulcasts of streaming and televised show. On a stockholder call today (Oct. 29) to discuss Sirius’ latest earnings report, Witz says WWE Radio has already significantly increased the channel’s audience: “Sports is another powerful driver of fandom, uniting passionate communities around live programming and hometown teams. Listening to WWE Radio has grown nearly 20 percent since its July launch and rebrand, while monthly active sports listeners increased four percent year-over-year across our connected car and streaming platforms.” Personally, I remain convinced that monopolization and homogenization of pro wrestling is bad. It’s almost always bad for any product or market. Based on how it went in wrestling while WWE was the only major game in town for most of the 21st century, in wrestling it can create a sanitized, stagnant product that gradually loses fans. We’re not to the point yet where WWE is actually the only game in town. But most of their strategic moves of late — such as the co-opting of what was a relatively unbiased media outlet like Sirius’s pro wrestling channel — indicate they’d like to be. And even if Sirius loves that now, there’s a chance it could bite them later if people choose to stop following wrestling all together rather than seek out alternatives to WWE. * Psychologist and commentator Alex Williams’ 2002 national Google survey on the subject has come on Wrestling Twitter lately, so we’ll use that to back up this claim. Williams asked people to name a pro wrestler. Roman Reigns tied for the most commonly named active talent, which meant that 4 out of 503 respondents named him. But we can give Reigns the win, because the other person with 4 votes isn’t a wrestler. He has worked a program or two though… it was Mike Tyson. title: Dave Meltzer Explains WWE Crown Jewel Venue Switch
raw_title: Dave Meltzer Reveals Reason Behind WWE Crown Jewel Venue Change In Riyadh
summary_src: Journalist Dave Meltzer provides further reason as to why the 2026 WWE Crown Jewel premium live event changed venues.
body: Earlier this week, Riyadh Season revealed that the 2026 WWE Crown Jewel event would relocate to a new venue , with ticket holders receiving a full refund. Journalist Dave Meltzer has since reported that the November 7 premium live event will remain in the city of Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, just moving to the nearby Kingdom Arena. On "Wrestling Observer Radio," Meltzer provided further reason as to why. "They were building a stadium, Riyadh Season Stadium. It was outdoors and the WWE show was going to be there. They announced a move. I don't even know if it's been officially announced, but they're moving to Kingdom Arena, which is the same building that the Canelo Alvarez fight on Saturday is going to be held. Some people, when it was first announced, thought something big was up, but essentially, the claim is that it is safer to run the show indoors than outdoors, which makes all the sense in the world," Meltzer said. "So they're going to move the show indoors." The location of Crown Jewel has come into great question in recent months due to the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East. Originally, the PLE was set to take place inside the Riyadh Season Stadium, a temporary outdoor venue. Kingdom Arena, meanwhile, is an indoor venue with a 30,000 seat capacity. WWE has hosted multiple shows from the Kingdom Arena in the past, including the 2025 and 2026 Night of Champions PLEs. The upcoming Crown Jewel show has four matches confirmed so far, three of which revolve around championships.
summary: Riyadh Season announced that the 2026 WWE Crown Jewel premium live event will move to a different venue in the same city, with full refunds issued to ticket holders. Per Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio, the show is shifting from the planned outdoor Riyadh Season Stadium to the indoor Kingdom Arena for safety reasons. The November 7 event was originally set for the outdoor stadium but will now take place in the same building hosting the Canelo Alvarez fight.

summary_src: The Syx have been running through TNA’s tag team division lately, but Samuel Shaw, Joseph Sawyer and Erick Redbeard apparently aren’t above stopping everything to do something completely ridiculous.
body: During the show, all three members of The Syx ended up doing the viral “Tip Toeing In My Jordans” dance while the RiFF RAFF song played. Shaw got things started, breaking into the exaggerated tiptoe dance as the fans in attendance immediately lost their minds. Sawyer wasn’t going to let Shaw have all the fun. He followed him up with his own version of the dance before dropping down and doing what looked like a mini Spinaroonie on his knee, getting another big reaction from the crowd. Then it was Redbeard’s turn. The big man joined in with a dance of his own while fans cheered him on, meaning all three members of The Syx had officially gotten involved by the time the music stopped. The whole thing was a recreation of the “Tip Toeing In My Jordans” meme that has been all over social media. The trend features a creepy Rumpelstiltskin-like character doing an exaggerated tiptoe dance to RIFF RAFF’s 2014 track “Tip Toe Wing In My Jawwdinz,” with countless people and even sports teams recreating the dance since it went viral. It was definitely a different side of The Syx compared to what TNA fans have been seeing from them lately. Shaw, Sawyer and Redbeard have quickly made their presence felt in TNA’s tag team division, but their ACW appearance showed they can drop the serious act and have some fun when the opportunity comes along. Who do you think pulled off the “Tip Toeing In My Jordans” dance the best out of Samuel Shaw, Joseph Sawyer and Erick Redbeard? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Backstage Buzz: More WWE NXT Backstage Changes Expected in 2027 With Bayley and CM Punk Potentially Involved

summary_src: WWE apparently has more than just Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles to figure out when it comes to NXT in 2027. A new update suggests the company is planning additional changes behind the scenes, and Bayley and CM Punk could both end up playing bigger roles.
body: According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer, WWE is expected to make more changes to NXT’s office structure next year. Bayley is one name who could become involved depending on what she wants to do with her career, while Punk could also get more input into what happens with the developmental brand. And that’s not all. WWE’s ID program is apparently in line for some changes of its own in early 2027. “As of right now, it looks like Shawn Michaels replacing Bruce Prichard and AJ Styles getting his NXT role is the most likely scenario. It is believed there will be other NXT office changes in 2027 as well. Depending on what she wants to do with her career, Bayley could very well end up involved. Punk may also have more input. It is also believed the ID program will get ‘a fresh coat of paint’ in early 2027 as well.” The Bayley part is particularly interesting because Alvarez made it clear that her potential involvement depends on what she wants to do next. There’s no indication that she’s been offered a specific backstage job, but her name is apparently being discussed as part of NXT’s future. Punk’s situation is a little different. Rather than taking over a particular position, the expectation is that he could simply have more influence over the brand. Exactly what that would involve hasn’t been established. Meanwhile, the mention of WWE’s ID program getting a fresh coat of paint suggests changes could also be coming to how the company works with independent wrestling talent. Alvarez didn’t specify what those adjustments would look like. The latest information comes as WWE prepares for another major transition. Shawn Michaels is expected to replace Bruce Prichard as Executive Director of Creative Writing & Talent following WrestleMania 43 in April 2027, while AJ Styles is emerging as the likely person to assume Michaels’ NXT responsibilities. An earlier update indicated that people within WWE’s Performance Center were already expecting Styles to become more involved with NXT once Michaels moves into his new position. But Alvarez’s latest comments make it clear that WWE’s plans may go well beyond those two positions. Between possible new responsibilities for Bayley and Punk, additional office changes, and adjustments to the ID program, the company could be making several changes to its developmental operation next year. Nothing involving Bayley or Punk has been officially confirmed, and their potential responsibilities remain unclear. Still, it appears WWE has more changes in mind for NXT than simply replacing Michaels, with 2027 shaping up to be an important year for the brand. title: WWE’s Real Goal Behind Constantly Counterprogramming AEW
raw_title: WWE’s Real Goal Behind Constantly Counterprogramming AEW
summary_src: WWE clearly isn’t done going after AEW whenever the opportunity comes up, and the company’s constant counterprogramming apparently has a much bigger goal behind it. This isn’t just about beating AEW for one night and walking away with bragging rights.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez explained that WWE is trying to weaken AEW ahead of the company’s next television negotiations. AEW will eventually be heading into another contract year, and the changing media landscape means those negotiations could become incredibly important. Alvarez noted that there has already been a major sale in the media business, which creates even more uncertainty about what things will look like by the time AEW needs another television deal. “AEW is soon to be into a contract year, and there has just been a sale. And so, fact of the matter is, no matter what anybody says, nobody knows the future.” That’s why WWE is expected to keep counterprogramming AEW whenever it gets the chance. WWE doesn’t necessarily need to completely crush AEW’s audience either, because even taking away 5% or 10% of its viewers would still accomplish part of what the company is trying to do. “As long as there is that chance, WWE is going to want to make that happen. And so they are going to counterprogram all these events. And if they can even take away 5% of viewership, 10% of viewership, they want to chip away as much as they can because that’s just what they do.” Basically, WWE wants to keep chipping away at AEW’s numbers before the company eventually heads back to the negotiating table. If putting NXT or another WWE show against AEW can pull even a small percentage of viewers away, WWE is apparently willing to keep doing it. That doesn’t necessarily mean AEW is in danger of suddenly losing its television deal. Alvarez expects the company will probably end up with something similar to its current arrangement and remain on TBS and TNT, but WWE isn’t going to make that process any easier. “I would guess that they’re likely going to get a similar deal to what they’re getting right now, and it will be remaining on TBS and TNT, but WWE is going to do everything they can to try to prevent that from happening.” This all comes right before another WWE vs. AEW fight. NXT will go head-to-head with Blood & Guts on November 4, and WWE is already planning to load up its show after getting a big confidence boost from beating AEW the last time around. WWE wasn’t nearly as confident heading into that previous head-to-head battle, which is why NXT largely ran a normal show instead of loading up the card. After NXT still managed to come out ahead, that attitude changed , and WWE is now ready to come back much harder against Blood & Guts. So the November 4 battle and even beyond that are about more than simply which show gets the better number that night. WWE is looking to keep taking bites out of AEW’s audience wherever possible, with AEW’s eventual television negotiations looming in the background. body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. One thing that stood out to me over the last couple episodes of WWE Raw is there doesn’t seem to be a short-term creative direction for Oba Femi. He defeated Bronson Reed at Money in the Bank on Oct. 10, rejected Paul Heyman’s advances on the fallout episode of Raw, and now we’re waiting to see what’s next. It’s just two episodes of doing nothing, but I figured WWE would want Femi to be part of the upcoming Crown Jewel PLE in Riyadh, considering rumors that he will be in the main event there against Roman Reigns when WWE is back in Saudi Arabia next year for WrestleMania 43. This got me looking at Oba’s match listings on CageMatch , and I noticed that WWE already seems to be booking The Ruler like a special attraction who rarely ever wrestles on weekly shows like Raw (or SmackDown). Oba’s last Raw match on Netflix took place over three months ago (July 20) when he squashed JD McDonagh’s giant head in less than one minute. This was Oba’s only non-dark match of July. Femi’s only non-dark match in August was his Hell in a Cell victory over Brock Lesnar at the SummerSlam PLE. His only non-dark match in September was a disqualification win over Bron Breakker at Sunday Night’s Main Event. October is wrapping up in a couple days, and Femi’s only non-dark match of the month is his Money in the Bank PLE win over Reed. Oba has wrestled plenty of dark matches in between, but WWE fans who are paying for Netflix, Peacock, and ESPN Unlimited have only seen him fight four times over the last four months. That might not seem too out of place if we’re talking about a longtime top star like Roman Reigns, Brock Lesnar, Cody Rhodes, Randy Orton, or CM Punk, but the 28-year-old Femi is still in his rookie year on the main roster. Earlier this year, WWE tried to do a weekly open challenge with Femi that died out real quick, probably because it’s difficult to book the guy to steamroll everyone like Superman without burying most of the roster. Now we are on the opposite side of the coin where Oba is a special attraction who is apparently too good to wrestle on Raw on Netflix. title: Shawn Michaels to replace Bruce Prichard at WWE
raw_title: WWE Hall of Famer will reportedly fill Bruce Prichard’s position
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) WWE has a plan for when Executive Director – Creative Writing & Talent Bruce Prichard transitions into a consulting role next year. Mike Johnson of PWInsider.com reports that Shawn Michaels is expected to step into Prichard’s role. Johnson adds that the succession plan has been in place for some time. Powell’s POV: Once Michaels takes on the new role, his current position of Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative will open. There are reports that AJ Styles will take on a bigger role in NXT, which is logical, but I’m not sure if he’s interested in working on the creative side or whether he’d be good in that role. Either way, I view the NXT shakeup as a positive. While Michaels did good work over the years, it feels like the time has come for a change in NXT’s creative direction.
summary: WWE has a long-standing succession plan in place for when Bruce Prichard moves into a consulting role next year. Per PWInsider, Shawn Michaels is expected to step into Prichard's position as Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent. Michaels' current role as Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative will then become available, with reports that AJ Styles could assume a larger presence in NXT.

body: According to WrestleVotes Radio , The Sphere in Las Vegas is not a backup plan for WWE if WrestleMania 43 is moved from Saudi Arabia. While WWE has expressed internal interest in using The Sphere, meaningful negotiations between the two sides have reportedly not taken place. Fightful.com previously reported that the two sides were unable to reach an agreement during WrestleMania 42 season over displaying promotional material for Danhausen on the exterior of the venue. It’s believed that WWE has a backup plan to host WrestleMania domestically if world events force a change in plans, but the details are being kept confidential. Earlier this month, Dave Meltzer of F4WOnline.com was told by sources in the city that the necessary April dates are unavailable for WrestleMania . Those sources also reportedly said Las Vegas is unable to offer the level of financial incentives it has provided for previous events. summary_src: From Grayson Waller vs. Tony D'Angelo to Kelani Jordan vs. Wren Sinclair, here are Wrestling Inc.'s biggest draws and duds for "WWE NXT" Halloween Havoc 2026!
body: WWE This Saturday is Halloween, and "WWE NXT" is prepared to celebrate in style, with the 2026 edition of Halloween Havoc! The latest PLE from the developmental brand features six matches, two of which will be contested for a title, and will be hosted by none other than WWE's resident curse gremlin, Danhausen. But which of the matches announced for Halloween Havoc has the Wrestling Inc. staff in the spooky season spirit, and which are leaving us ready for November to start? That's what we're here today to find out. Here are our biggest draws and biggest duds for "WWE NXT" Halloween Havoc 2026! WWE "NXT" does a pretty good job of integrating its talents' antics on social media into the broadcast, when relevant to a storyline, and we've seen that in the feud pitting Shiloh Hill against Naraku. Hill has taken to TikTok and Instagram to share his journey exploring the science behind the ancient mist, and it's all so very "NXT"-coded — meaning silly to the point that it would never happen on the main roster — that it's charming. Hill himself is a charming, goofy babyface character, and the whole story works so well for him. If anyone was going to educate the masses on poison mist, it should be this guy. A match that may very well culminate in the use of black mist, which in WWE lore is blinding (as seen in Nidia in Jamie Noble's feud against Tajiri in 2003) should absolutely take place at Halloween Havoc. This feud started all the way back on the August 18 edition of "NXT," when Naraku, fresh out of the NXT Championship picture, cost Hill a shot at becoming number one contender for the North American Championship by spraying him in the face with mist. The pair went on to have their first match on September 1, which Naraku won by spraying mist into his hands , then raking Hill in the eyes. Hill started to research the effects of various colors of the mist ever since, through their second match, where Naraku accidentally hit the referee with blue mist . Naraku has warned Hill that he could bring any color of mist into their match at Halloween Havoc, including the dreaded black mist. Hill has been researching every color, even testing mists on himself and sharing them to social media, to ridiculous effects, like AI raccoons following him around. Hill could very well come prepared with a mist concoction of his own, or even an antidote. This match may not necessarily be an in-ring banger like fans can expect from NXT Women's Champion Kelani Jordan and Wren Sinclair, but on a low-stakes premium live event where only two titles are on the line, it's a fun bout with a great story behind it. The gimmick surrounding the mist fits the theme of Halloween Havoc perfectly and should be plenty of fun thanks to the unpredictability of Hill. WWE Halloween Havoc is one of the lowest-stakes "NXT" premium live events in recent memory, and there's perhaps no better example of that than the singles bout pitting Women's North American Champion Zaria against Izzi Dame. title: Jack Perry’s Condition After Scary Bumps on October 28 AEW Dynamite
raw_title: Jack Perry’s Condition After Scary Bumps on October 28 AEW Dynamite
summary_src: Jack Perry took some absolutely nasty bumps during this week’s AEW Dynamite, and there’s now an update on how he’s feeling after getting through the match. Considering how ugly a couple of those landings looked, there was plenty of reason for concern once the show was over.
body: Speaking on Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez revealed that Perry has been telling people he’s sore following his October 28 match against Kyle Fletcher. There was no indication of a more serious injury in the update, with soreness being the word coming from Perry after the match. “Hey, you want a scoop? I did hear that Jack Perry was telling people that he was sore.” That probably won’t come as much of a surprise to anyone who watched the match. Perry and Fletcher went pretty damn hard, with Perry taking several rough-looking bumps involving his neck and back during the bout. The one that really stood out came when Fletcher powerbombed Perry onto the edge of the ring. Perry came down awkwardly against the ring frame in a spot that looked brutal in real time, and Alvarez admitted he was shocked Perry apparently escaped with just soreness. “If you watch that match, he’s lucky he’s only sore. I thought he was going to get legitimately decapitated when he took that powerbomb into the ring frame. Absolutely brutal.” Perry still managed to finish the match despite everything he took. Fletcher eventually dragged him to the top rope and hit a Brainbuster to pick up the win, ending a match that featured several dangerous-looking landings along the way. For now, the good news is that the only word coming out of the match is that Perry has been telling people he’s sore. There’s been no indication from this update that he suffered a more serious injury, which is pretty remarkable considering just how nasty that powerbomb and some of the other bumps looked. What did you make of some of the dangerous-looking spots Jack Perry took during his match with Kyle Fletcher on Dynamite? Let us know what you think in the comments. The great state of Alabama is hosting the action, and I certainly hope the fine people of Dothan gave these wrestlers a proper Southern welcome. And if you’re looking for two wrestlers capable of putting on an excellent contest without needing fifteen people standing around ringside, you’ve come to the right place. Amazing Red’s combination of speed, creativity, and high-flying offense made him one of the most exciting performers of his generation, and the fact that he’s still competing at this level is a testament to his ability and dedication. Cedric Alexander, meanwhile, brings tremendous athleticism, technical skill, and enough experience to understand that defeating a champion requires more than simply hitting a few spectacular moves. The interesting thing about this matchup is that neither man needs to abandon his natural wrestling style to make the contest compelling. Both can move, both can strike, and both are capable of countering an opponent’s offense in ways that make even a relatively straightforward exchange entertaining. TNA built much of its early reputation on wrestlers who could deliver something different from the traditional heavyweight formula. Tubi , the same streaming service where Thalia spends an alarming amount of time watching horror movies featuring questionable acting, questionable special effects, and women who apparently have difficulty keeping their clothes on, is also home to professional wrestling. Now, I appreciate a good villain as much as anybody, but threatening to destroy a historic wrestling trophy because you don’t like what it represents? That’s the kind of behavior that makes me wish somebody would bring back the old-fashioned wrestling commissioner who could suspend people for being complete jackasses. Adding another complication is MLW National Openweight Champion Austin Aries, who is expected to be in attendance scouting the competition. title: WWE Expected To Pursue AEW's Dralistico
raw_title: Backstage Update On Potential WWE Interest In AEW Star Dralistico
summary_src: Dralistico's AEW future is up in the air, and if he becomes a free agent in the near future, there could be some interest from WWE.
body: AEW AEW and Ring of Honor star Dralistico has been in the news as of late as his future seems to be up in the air. The luchador posted an AI-generated image of himself sitting in a jail cell earlier this month, complete with the caption "Maybe not for long?" which implied that he could be on his way out of AEW/ROH when his contracts expires, and it seems that WWE could be interested in bringing him in. According to WrestleVotes Radio on Fightful Select , WWE is expected to show some interest in Dralistico when he becomes a free agent, with his contract reportedly set to expire this December. A source from within WWE has claimed that there is locker room support regarding the company signing the luchador, though that should come as no surprise according to WrestleVotes given that his real-life brother Dragon Lee already works for the company. There is a belief from the internal source that Dralistico could become a major signing for both WWE and AAA if he does sign either before the end of the year or the beginning of next year. Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer recently reported that AAA in particular would be the most ideal landing place for Dralistico as he wouldn't be welcomed back in CMLL due to his other brother, Rush, leaving the company in 2019 in controversial fashion. Dralistico hasn't wrestled in AEW since the June 6 episode of "AEW Collision," where he, Sammy Guevara, and Rush failed to capture the AEW World Trios Championships from The Conglomeration. His last appearance in Ring of Honor came just a few days later on the ROH YouTube special that aired on June 9, where teamed up with The Lethal Twist in a losing effort against Dalton Castle, The Outrunners, and Adam Priest.
summary: Per Fightful Select, WWE is anticipated to show interest in signing Dralistico when his AEW and ROH contract expires in December. A WWE source indicated locker room support for bringing in the luchador, partly due to his brother Dragon Lee already being with the company. There is an internal belief that he could become a significant acquisition for WWE and AAA around the end of this year or start of next.

title: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Venue Change Due to Security Issues
raw_title: Backstage Note on Why WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Is Moving Venues
body: As previously reported , Riyadh Season announced yesterday that WWE Crown Jewel 2026 was moving venues and ticket holders were being refunded. The announcement came after construction had already begun on a temporary outdoor stadium for the event. During today’s Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer elaborated further on the change, which occurs amid a myriad of security concerns surrounding the event. As noted, the U.S. State Department issued a Level 3 advisory, warning U.S. citizens not to travel to Saudi Arabia. Also, the U.S. Embassy in the country has issued multiple security alerts regarding travel in the region. Additionally, non-emergency government employees and their families were ordered by the Embassy to leave the region. This is due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the Iran War, with the Iranian-supported Houthi forces targeting airports and U.S. government officials in the region. Speaking on the situation, Meltzer stated, “They were building a stadium, Riyadh Season Stadium. It was outdoors, and the WWE show was going to be there. They announced a move. I don’t even know if it’s been officially announced, but they’re moving to Kingdom Arena, which is the same building that the Canelo Alvarez fight on Saturday is going to be held. So, some people were like — when it was first announced, thought like something big was up.” According to Meltzer, the venue is changing due to the belief that an indoor venue is safer than an outdoor one. He continued, “Essentially, the claim is that it is safer to run the show indoors than outdoors, which makes all the sense in the world. So they’re going to move the show indoors.” When Meltzer’s co-host Bryan Alvarez questioned why an indoor venue is safer, when an indoor venue could just as well be attacked like an outdoor one, Meltzer responded, “They think it’s safer because it’s easier to keep people out if it’s indoors. Instead of people sneaking in as easier –” Alvarez then jokingly questioned, “Instead of them climbing the giant walls of the stadium, they have to go through the doors to get in?” Meltzer then replied that rather than a safety issue, it could really be a matter of low ticket sales. “Hey, maybe it’s just that they didn’t sell enough tickets and it’s moving indoors like that WrestleMania.” Of course, Meltzer is referring to WrestleMania VII in 1991. The event was originally scheduled for the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, which would’ve held a huge capacity crowd. However, WWE (then WWF) later moved the event due to reported security concerns around the Gulf War and the charged angle with former WWE Champion Sgt. Slaughter portraying a pro-Saddam Hussein Iraqi sympathizer on TV. However, it’s stated the real reason the event moved to the Los Angeles Memorial Sports Arena nearby was due to low ticket sales. WrestleMania VII did go off as planned, but in a much smaller venue. Meltzer also reported that the venue change was a decision made by Saudi Arabia’s General Ente
summary: Riyadh Season announced that WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is moving venues with ticket holders being refunded after construction had started on a temporary outdoor stadium. The shift comes amid multiple security concerns including a U.S. State Department Level 3 travel advisory for Saudi Arabia, U.S. Embassy alerts, and orders for non-emergency government employees and families to leave the region. Dave Meltzer discussed the change on Wrestling Observer Radio, noting the outdoor Riyadh Season Stadium that was under construction for the show.

title: WWE Aims to Sever Skydance's AEW Ties
raw_title: WWE is going to do ‘everything they can’ to make sure Skydance cuts ties with AEW
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. Even though it’s been clear for a long time that WWE has a strategy for counterprogamming AEW, I still see plenty of wrestling fans in denial about what is staring them right in the face. Some of the skeptics roll their eyes at the notion that WWE is trying to significantly hurt AEW’s business, in part because WWE makes so much money that they can’t possibly see AEW as legit competition. Even if that were true, I think TKO / WWE’s risky refusal to pull its upcoming Crown Jewel event out of a war zone in Saudi Arabia shows that the almighty dollar rules all. With that extreme corporate greed in mind, one of the most obvious ways WWE can financially control the wrestling industry even more is to take measures that hurt AEW. That’s a primary motivation for all the counterprogramming we’ve seen. On today’s Wrestling Observer Live , Bryan Alvarez explained that even though a lot of WWE’s recent attempts to counterprogram AEW haven’t worked very well, WWE is going to keep doing it because AEW’s future potentially hangs in the balance next year as everyone waits to see if Skydance will renew their lucrative TV deal or drop them. “AEW is soon to be into a contract year. There has just been a sale. [The] fact of the matter is, no matter what anybody says, nobody knows the future…Whenever you have a merger like we’ve seen with Skydance / Paramount etc., and we’ve already seen this on the sports side of WBD, cuts are coming. Is there a chance that they will not pick up AEW? Yeah, of course. Of course there is. And as long as there is that chance, WWE is gonna want to make that happen. And so they are going to counterprogram all these events. And if they can even take away 5% of viewership, 10% of viewership, they want to chip away as much as they can because that’s just what they do. So far it has been immensely ineffective, but they don’t give up. …I would guess [AEW is] likely going to get a similar deal to what they’re getting right now, and it will be remaining on TBS and TNT. But WWE is gonna do everything they can to try to prevent that from happening.” What do you think about WWE’s business strategy to chip away at AEW’s numbers via counterprogramming? Will WWE be more successful at this goal over the next year while there is so much uncertainty about AEW’s future with Skydance? Let me know in the comments, Cagesiders. The TNA Knockouts TV Championship will also be defended tonight as M by Elegance of The Elegance Brand puts her title on the line against Jada Stone. Elijah will go up against Ryan Nemeth in singles action. John Skyler and AJ Francis will also collide in a singles match. Plus, The Hardys and syX will meet in a Slaughterhouse syX match. M caught Stone off a springboard and dumped her to the outside. M dragged her back into the ring for a cover, but Stone kicked out at two. M hit her with a suplex, but again a kickout. M got Stone on her shoulders, but Stone got out of it with a chinbreaker. M gave her a big boot and then went for a moonsault, but no one was home. Stone took advantage with a series of uppercuts and laid out M on the ropes for a successful Totally-Not-A-619. We also have some title shots with the TBS and TNT Titles on the line. That’s all in addition to the build towards Full Gear and Blood & Guts, which should make for a rather full show. That’s fine with Moxley, who chops away in the corner before it’s off to Garcia. The Cut stomps him down in the corner, which doesn’t last long either, as it’s back to Moxley. That means White bails out to the floor and Finlay takes over on Moxley’s leg. Now White is willing to come in and crank on said leg, followed by a chinlock. Garcia gets in a running clothesline and hammers away on both villains in the corner at the same time. The Dragontamer goes on and is broken up just as fast, with the brawl heading outside as we take a break. We come back with Garcia neckbreakering his way out of trouble and bringing Moxley back in. A bunch of rights and lefts in the corner have White rocked, and Moxley sends him outside for a whip into the steps. Back in, the Paradigm Shift connects, setting up the running corner clotheslines. There’s the cutter to White and a dive to Finlay, with Garcia getting two on White. Cue Ace Austin so Wheeler Yuta cuts him off, allowing Clark Connors to spear Garcia. The Blade Runner gives White the pin at 14:06. Rating : B-. This is what it should have been, with White looking to be on the way towards a big Continental Title match with Moxley. Have him win some matches against Moxley and company to set that up, and everything should go well. The Cut (thank goodness for that name change) is already feeling like a threat, and that’s nice to see. Post-match, the beatdown continues with Gabe Kidd’s save not working. Claudio Castagnoli comes in for the real save, though, and the Death Riders grab chairs to clean house. Moxley issues the challenge for Anarchy In The Arena at Full Gear. We look back at the challenge being thrown out for the women’s Blood & Guts on Collision. Fletcher bails outside for an early hug from Don Callis, so Perry goes outside for one from Taz. Another running dropkick knocks Fletcher off the barricade, but Fletcher gets in a leg lariat. We take a break and come back with Perry still in trouble off a slam. Another slam wakes Perry up a bit, and he gets in a hard clothesline. Fletcher is sent outside for some dives but catches the third into an apron bomb. Perry is fine enough to snap off a hurricanrana to the floor, but Fletcher snaps off a dragon suple

body: This week, it was reported that Shawn Michaels is expected to take over Bruce Prichard’s Executive Director role in WWE. In an update on the story, Bryan Alvarez of F4WOnline.co noted the following… “As of right now, it looks like Shawn Michaels replacing Bruce Prichard and AJ Styles getting his NXT role is the most likely scenario. It is believed there will be other NXT office changes in 2027 as well. Depending on what she wants to do with her career, Bayley could very well end up involved. Punk may also have more input. It is also believed the ID program will get “a fresh coat of paint” in early 2027 as well.” Punk has previously expressed interest in helping develop younger talent. During an April appearance on the All the Smoke podcast, Punk said he believes he can contribute to the wrestling business both as an active performer and behind the scenes. Bayley has also worked to develop younger talent through her Lodestone women’s wrestling camps. She held the first camp in Orlando in December of CM P2025, followed by a second in Las Vegas in April. A third camp took place in Texas last month.
summary: The latest: this week, it was reported that Shawn Michaels is likely to take over Bruce Prichard’s Executive Director role in WWE. It is believed there will be other NXT office changes in 2027 as well.

title: M By Elegance Retains TNA KO TV Title With Time Limit Draw Against Elayna Black
raw_title: M By Elegance Retains TNA KO TV Title With Time Limit Draw Against Elayna Black
body: At M's request, the entire Elegance Brand, excluding herself, was banned from ringside for this KO TV Title match. That didn't stop M from resorting to questionable tactics, however. At one point, the defending champion dragged Black to the outside with the intention of stomping on her hand while it sat atop the steel steps. Black managed to move out the way and stomp on her hand instead. The challenger then dropped M with a suplex onto the floor. When the action returned to the ring, M fired off kicks in the corner and bridged into a Northern Lights Suplex for a near fall. The Elegance Brand member continued her momentum by cinching in an arm bar while simultaneously wrenching back Black's fingers. A knee to Black's ribs followed, as did a drive-by single-leg dropkick along the apron. In the match's final moments, M went up top, looking to deliver a moonsault on her way down. Instead, she met the mat and a knee to the face. After taking a suplex next, M rolled outside the ring, asking how much time was left on the clock. When she reentered, she and Black traded roll-ups, the latter of which was followed by a Black Out from the challenger. Unfortunately for Black, this move ultimately proved pointless as the bell rang before the referee could count three on her subsequent cover. M captured the title by defeating Jada Stone in the finals of a competitive tournament on August 27. Black originally took on former "NXT" star Wendy Choo in the tourney. Due to the strict 10-minute time limit attached to the championship, however, both were disqualified when the clock ran out in their opening round bout. Black later earned a second chance to pursue it by winning a recent fatal-four-way match.
summary: The latest: the entire Elegance Brand, excluding herself, was banned from ringside for this KO TV Title match. The defending champion dragged Black to the outside with the intention of stomping on her hand while it sat atop the steel steps.

title: Booker T Says He Avoided WWE Locker Room Heat
raw_title: Booker T Explains Why He Never Got 'Heat' With The WWE Locker Room
summary_src: Booker T discusses his ability to evade heat in the WWE locker room.
body: WWE Coming to WWE after a successful run in WCW, after the promotion closed, often meant a wrestler would get buried or humiliated . But in the rare cases of Rey Mysterio, Goldberg, and Booker T, their careers prospered when they stepped into WWE. However, stepping into an established locker room after being a part of the WCW roster for years could've led to heat, but Booker claims he never ran into this whilst with WWE. "Nah, I never got heat. I always understood, you know, the locker room etiquette and stuff like that," he claimed during an episode of his " The Hall of Fame " podcast. "I was always, you know, one of the guys you know, I always thought the guys could turn to as far as that goes." Booker also asserted that he was outspoken, adding that backstage heat didn't matter to him, because the locker room weren't the ones cutting his cheque anyways. "I always thought if I didn't got heat with the boss, I was okay, and I don't remember ever getting heat with the boss," he explained. "A bully would keep messing with you if you don't fight back," Booker added, noting that backstage heat is only a debated topic because many guys were too afraid to call it out back in the day, because they were scared they'd get fired. "That irks me, man, it really irks me. Why not, you know, tell somebody to, you know, take a hike? Go jump in a lake?" Booker also criticized the wrestlers who kept locker room hazing because of heat a secret, pointing out that even though they were worried about getting fired, they usually got fired because of other circumstances anyway.
summary: Booker T joined WWE after WCW closed and saw his career thrive like fellow WCW stars Rey Mysterio and Goldberg. On his Hall of Fame podcast he explained that he never received backstage heat because he understood locker room etiquette, remained one of the guys, and focused on not upsetting the boss who signed his checks.

Booker T stated that despite the potential for locker room heat from being part of the WCW roster for years, he never encountered any such issues in WWE. During an episode of his "The Hall of Fame" podcast, Booker T said, "Nah, I never got heat."

He explained that he always understood locker room etiquette and positioned himself as one of the guys that others could turn to. Booker T added that he was outspoken and that backstage heat did not concern him since the locker room was not responsible for paying him.

He noted, "I always thought if I didn't got heat with the boss, I was okay, and I don't remember ever getting heat with the boss." Booker T described how a bully would continue messing with someone only if they did not fight back, and he criticized the idea that backstage heat was debated because many wrestlers feared calling it out due to worries about being fired.
He expressed frustration at wrestlers who kept locker room hazing secret out of fear of termination, pointing out that they typically ended up getting fired for unrelated reasons anyway.

body: Posted in: AEW , Sports , TV | Tagged: AEW Dynamite , recaps , wrestling Comrades, my AEW Fright Night Dynamite review: Queen Aminata seizes the TBS Title, The Cut wreck the Death Riders, and Esteban approves. Viva the queen! Greetings, comrades! It is I, your El Presidente, reporting to you live from the sulfurous depths of my volcano lair, where Esteban the capybara is lounging in a bubble bath of imported champagne and refusing to acknowledge the existence of Monday. I have just finished watching AEW Fright Night Dynamite from Chaifetz Arena in St. Louis, Missouri, and I have never been more proud of a working-class hero. Queen Aminata closed the show as the new TBS Champion, and the people's revolution has a new queen! Now, grab your finest cigar and an uncomfortable amount of rum, comrades, because we have a lot of ground to cover. Next week's Blood and Guts is in Jacksonville, Full Gear is on the horizon, and the CIA has been unusually quiet, which I assume means they are all watching wrestling too. The show opened with a tag team match as Jay White and David Finlay of The Cut took on AEW Continental Champion Jon Moxley and Daniel Garcia of the Death Riders. With Clark Connors , Ace Austin , Wheeler Yuta , and Claudio Castagnoli all lurking around ringside, I knew this was going to be less a wrestling match and more a diplomatic incident. The finish was pure backroom politics, comrades. With the referee distracted, Connors speared Garcia, and White picked up the pin after a Blade Runner. It was the kind of dirty business that reminds me of the time I shared a hot tub with dictator Fidel Castro and actor Gary Busey , and nobody could remember who stole the cigars, but everyone agreed the referee should have been looking elsewhere. Both groups and their allies then brawled, with Castagnoli swinging Connors while the Death Riders held the ring. Moxley closed the segment by challenging The Cut to Anarchy in the Arena at Full Gear . A match with no rules and no oversight? That is just my Tuesday cabinet meeting. A video package set up next week's women's Blood and Guts match, and the sides are drawn. Triangle of Madness and Divine Dominion will face The Brawling Birds, Wrathlander , and Willow Nightingale . The Brawling Birds, you will recall, are the AEW Women's World Tag Team Champions, so they are bringing gold and a grudge into a cage with two rings. I am already drafting a strongly worded telegram to the capitalists who did not give me a ticket to Jacksonville. A second package promoted both the men's and women's Blood and Guts matches, narrated and featuring Dean Malenko . Comrades, when a preview makes me want to storm a cage in my dress uniform, you know the production team did its job. title: Backstage Buzz: John Cena Classic Update, Backstage Roles, The Rock & More — WWE Rumors
raw_title: WWE Rumors: John Cena Classic Update, Backstage Roles, The Rock & More
body: The latest WWE rumors feature an update on the tournament, as well as new backstage roles after WrestleMania 43, The Rock and more. As previously reported, the John Cena Classic is expected to take place in December. The exact date is still unclear, but WWE is already preparing for the tournament in a big way. According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select , WWE wants to produce the best product possible for the John Cena Classic. The company reportedly brought in AJ Styles and Shawn Michaels as consultants to make the tournament “look and feel fresh.” The expectation is that Cena will give an update on the tournament during his appearance on the November 2 episode of WWE Raw in Brooklyn, New York. Play A source told WrestleVotes that the John Cena Classic was initially planned for Club WWE, but it would be streamed somewhere else. There would be a major shakeup backstage in WWE after next year’s WrestleMania 43. According to PW Insider , Bruce Prichard is set to retire from his role as executive director of creative writing and talent. He will remain as a consultant for the company. PW Insider later added that Shawn Michaels is expected to take over Prichard’s role after WrestleMania 43. Michaels will be working alongside his best friend, Triple H , in shaping the next generation of WWE programming. Play Michaels is currently serving as the senior vice president of talent development and creative and is in charge of NXT. But who replaces Michaels in NXT? False Finish reported that AJ Styles will likely step into the role, especially with the way he has been more involved in NXT and developmental since his retirement. When former WWE star Adrian Neville, more famously known as PAC, passed away, The Rock shared an emotional tribute on social media. It was reported by multiple outlets that WWE was surprised that The Rock mentioned Tony Khan and AEW , especially given his role as a TKO board member. According to The Wrestling Observer , The Rock praising Khan remains a talking point backstage in WWE. The Hollywood star has been absent from WWE programming since Elimination Chamber: Toronto last year.
