title: Comeback Watch: Wrestling legends loved Christian Watson’s WWE-style return to Packers-Panthers
raw_title: Wrestling legends loved Christian Watson’s WWE-style return to Packers-Panthers
body: What Christian Watson pulled off in the Week 8 game between the Green Bay Packers and Carolina Panthers was nothing short of a WWE -like storyline. Watson exited the contest in the second quarter with a chest injury and was even forced to make a trip to the hospital for further testing on his injury. At that point, we thought Watson’s night was over because who could possibly expect the Packers wideout to return to a game after all of that. However, we were dead wrong, as Watson came back to the stadium one quarter later, and not only did he return to the contest, he received a target immediately. MORE: NFL trade deadline tracker – Grades for every deal, list of available players If you’ve watched professional wrestling over the years, you’ve seen plenty of ambulance entrances and exits, so Watson’s return had a very WWE-style feel to it. WWE legend and Hall of Famer Triple H shared his reaction to Watson emerging from the ambulance to return to the game. The only thing missing, Triple H said, was entrance music. “This isn’t a video game… you did that!!! Next time we’ll work on getting you some entrance music,” Triple H said when getting wind of Watson’s postgame comments about his return. Fellow WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman revealed that the origin of the ambulance entrance was in 1991 in WCW, when the now-defunct company did something similar with Sting. MORE: Josh Jacobs assigns blame for ‘handcuff’ TD celebration And, we’re not clear if he’s joking, but Heyman said football is “pre-determined.” “We did this with (Sting) in 1991 in WCW (vs Ravishing Rick Rude), and the industry has repeated it with great success in numerous circumstances,” Heyman said. “My most sincere compliments to the (NFL) creative team. Nicely Done… I love football. Even though it’s pre-determined,” Heyman added. After the game, even Watson admitted he felt like he was in a scene from a WWE show. “I used to watch WWE as a kid,” Watson said. I felt like I was watching WWE Smackdown vs. Raw or something, seeing the cameras on me when I was coming out of the ambulance.” Watson went on to note that the trip to the hospital was spurred on by the fact that he was spitting out blood after his injury . However, everything checked out, which allowed him to make his epic return to the field. Watson finished the game with eight receptions for 113 yards, with two of those catches and 13 of those yards coming after his return. The Packers went on to win the game, 27-19, and improved to 5-3 on the season. title: Grayson Waller Credits Shawn Michaels For WWE Career
raw_title: NXT star says Shawn Michaels changed his life and WWE career: ‘Whatever he needs, I’m like a soldier now’
summary_src: Grayson Waller credited Shawn Michaels for playing a pivotal role in his WWE career. He discussed the extent of their professional relationship leading in him assisting backstage for varied NXT duties. Waller told Stephanie McMahon on What’s Your Story?
body: Grayson Waller credited Shawn Michaels for playing a pivotal role in his WWE career. He discussed the extent of their professional relationship leading in him assisting backstage for varied NXT duties. Waller told Stephanie McMahon on What’s Your Story? Podcast that he owes his wrestling career to Michaels. He clarified that his return to NXT was not a sudden development, revealing that he had remained involved behind the scenes by assisting with tryouts, supporting younger talent , and finding other ways to help Michaels and the brand. “Everything in my life is because of Shawn Michaels. I don’t mind saying that. He gave me opportunities before I deserved them or before I was ready. But it was because he believed in me, and even now he gave me my second chance to come back and do something, and I’ve learned all,” said Waller. “Everything I’m doing is because of what he’s taught me. And I always told him when I originally got drafted, I said, ‘Anything you ever need, tell me. I’m like a soldier.’ So I’ve been going back to NXT for three years. Whenever they needed me, even if it was just like a live event loop.” “I’ll go back and do that. I want to be around. I want to help. I want to do the tryouts. It’s not like I’m just randomly back in NXT out of nowhere. I’ve been in that system. I’ve been around. I know what Sean wants. I know what they got to do.” “Sometimes it’s hard when you’re in an office position to talk to the kids like you need to, because you have to be respectful and you have to be professional. I don’t need to be that. I can kind of tell you in my way, as a colleague and like them know, hey, this is what we’re doing. So I think a lot of it I owe to Sean because he’s given me a lot of opportunities to be in that position.” “But also I’ve put myself there by telling him, like, ‘Hey, this random loop, I’ll go do it. I’ll wrestle whoever. Who’s the guy? This is the guy. Do you think he’s good? Yeah, we’re not sure. I’ll wrestle him, and then I’ll let him know. This guy’s really good’. And I tell him the truth. So we’ve developed that relationship where he trusts me, and I trust him fully.” “I’m more respectful of him as a person than I am as him as a wrestler, which is crazy because he’s the greatest wrestler of all time. But all the things I’ve learned from him, I got a house now. I got all these things. That’s because of him taking a chance on me. So, whatever he needs, like I’m a soldier now.” Rosanne Raphael Rosanne Raphael is a wrestling writer with over three and a half years of experience covering all things related to the industry. From a kindergarten teacher to PR Associate to turning her lifelong passion for the industry into a career, Rosanne is currently writing for F4W Online where she focuses on wrestling news, analysis, and storytelling. Rosanne previously contributed to Sportskeeda as an Assistant Content Manager. When not consumed by wrestling, Rosanne is a musician and an aspiring artist.

title: Jimmy House Shares Dustin Rhodes' Early Career Advice
raw_title: Jimmy House Reveals Advice Dustin Rhodes Shared With Him Early In His Career
summary_src: Jimmy House knows that you have to pull off anything to be successful in wrestling. House has enjoyed much of his wrestling success as a member of The Mog Squad faction. Outside of WWE EVOLVE, the group has appeared for promotions like Reality Of Wrestling and Coastal Championship Wrestling.
body: Jimmy House knows that you have to pull off anything to be successful in wrestling. House has enjoyed much of his wrestling success as a member of The Mog Squad faction. Outside of WWE EVOLVE, the group has appeared for promotions like Reality Of Wrestling and Coastal Championship Wrestling. Speaking with Fightful’s Sean Ross Sapp for a new interview, House talked about working with the group and how he was ready for that chapter of his journey. “On the indies, like at ROW, it started to really get over. By the time I was coming out, there’s so many people doing the Mog Squad sign and stuff like that. People were starting to get drawn to it. We’re building some momentum. But at first, again, with the goal that I talked about, wanting to be a hero for kids, there’s an initial flinch there, just as a heel in general, right? But I understand how professional wrestling is, and a lot of times you need to know how to do both. Then second to that, there’s countless examples where somebody excels as a heel and it allows them to evolve into an even better babyface. So I was fully aware and ready for that particular chapter of the journey. But then when you specify it to the Mog stuff, it’s like this is our first time talking and, not to downgrade the Mog community, but it’s not necessarily a community that I mesh in, at least not naturally. So I can honestly say I gave my best go at it for sure. There’s probably many critiques that the age group of 20 to 25 could probably give me if they saw my work.” Jimmy House also shared some valuable advice he received from Dustin Rhodes early in his wrestling career. “But that said, I try to have as much fun with it as I could because I know it’s one of those things where, again, I think of Dustin, for example, and his story with Goldust where he’s presented this idea and he has to look up what the term androgynous means and he’s like, ‘Whoa, okay.’ But then he becomes one of the biggest legends of all time because he made this out of the blue character something that was iconic. So I was nowhere near the Goldust level, both from a skill and also the stuff that Dustin did standpoint. But I saw it as an opportunity to do the same thing where this is the exact opposite of me truly. But again, I think becoming a good professional wrestler is being. a good worker or a great worker and the term worker has so many different definitions. One of the definitions I learned early on from Dustin is being a great worker is your ability to pull off really anything that you’re asked of, to make it real and make it look great. So that was my first opportunity to do something like that in my wrestling career, because I’m really just myself on the indies and whatnot.” Elsewhere in the interview, House credited Gabe Sapolsky for opening his door to WWE. llm_long: Jimmy House believes that succeeding in wrestling requires the ability to perform any role presented. He has achieved considerable success as part of The Mog Squad faction. The group has competed outside of WWE EVOLVE for promotions including Reality Of Wrestling and Coastal Championship Wrestling.

In a recent interview with Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp, House discussed his experiences working with the group and expressed that he was prepared for that phase of his career. He noted that the Mog Squad act began gaining traction on the independents like at ROW, where crowds started performing the group's sign and showing interest as he made his entrance. House acknowledged building momentum with the faction.

House admitted an initial hesitation about the heel role due to his goal of being a hero for kids. He explained that professional wrestling often demands versatility in performing as both heel and babyface. House added that many wrestlers have thrived as heels before transitioning into stronger babyface characters.

Specifically regarding the Mog Squad, House said it was the first time he had worked in that style and that the associated community was not one he naturally connected with. He stated that he gave his best effort despite this.

House also recounted advice from early in his career involving Dustin Rhodes. He recalled Rhodes being given the Goldust concept, needing to research the term androgynous, and ultimately transforming it into an iconic character that made him a legend. House viewed the Mog Squad opportunity similarly as something opposite to his natural style.

House said he aimed to enjoy the experience as much as possible. He observed that becoming a good professional wrestler involves being a strong worker, noting that the term worker carries multiple definitions.

summary_src: The new venue for WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is now officially official. After tickets were refunded earlier this week and sales were paused, tickets are once again available for the November 7 PLE in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
body: The new venue for WWE Crown Jewel 2026 is now officially official. After tickets were refunded earlier this week and sales were paused, tickets are once again available for the November 7 PLE in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The show has been moved indoors to “The Venue” (ANB Arena), which is close to the outdoor stadium Crown Jewel was originally scheduled for. Whether Crown Jewel would be moved has been a huge question in recent weeks amid a period of turmoil and violence with the Iran-backed Houthi rebels attacking infrastructure targets like airports in Saudi Arabia. It was announced earlier this week that the venue for the show was in fact changing , but it’s staying in Saudi Arabia rather than being moved to the United States. It’s believed that one of the reasons for the switch from Riyadh Season Stadium at KAFD (King Abdullah Financial District) to “The Venue” is that being indoors is an added security benefit. Crown Jewel will stream live on the ESPN Unlimited app in the United States and on Netflix internationally starting at 12 p.m. Eastern time/9 a.m. Pacific on Saturday, November 7. title: On the Record: Shawn Michaels Admits WWE Main Roster Call-Ups Leave NXT Creative ‘Scrambling’
raw_title: Shawn Michaels Admits WWE Main Roster Call-Ups Leave NXT Creative ‘Scrambling’
summary_src: Shawn Michaels knows that building long-term stories in NXT comes with one pretty annoying problem — WWE can take one of his stars whenever it wants. And sometimes, he doesn’t even get the chance to properly finish whatever he was doing with them.
body: Speaking on Busted Open Radio , Michaels opened up about what happens behind the scenes when WWE suddenly decides it needs somebody from NXT on the main roster. He admitted that unexpected call-ups can throw NXT creative into a loop, but at this point, it’s simply something everyone working on the brand has learned to expect. “It might sound like a cop-out answer, but it really isn’t. There are certain things in the business that the real world throws us in a loop, but you learn not to sell too much. You gotta understand those things are gonna happen. If you are gonna be here in NXT, you just kinda get used to that possibility happening.” Michaels said experience has helped him get a better feel for when somebody might be moving up, and getting information ahead of time obviously makes things easier. The bigger problem comes when something unexpected happens on RAW or SmackDown and WWE suddenly needs an NXT wrestler immediately. He used a main roster injury as an example. If somebody important goes down in the middle of a storyline, WWE may decide an NXT talent is the best replacement rather than plugging in somebody who wouldn’t feel important enough for the spot. “There is a part of you, I will say, after you continue doing it for a while, you will do your best to have a feeling. Anytime you can reach out and get info, that’s helpful. But to your point, when it comes to something like an injury happening on the main roster, and they were going towards a certain storyline, and a major person went out, and they need a person in there, and they don’t wanna make it another person on the roster that doesn’t feel important — yeah, they can pull out another person, and boom, they’re there, and you’re done. And you don’t get an opportunity to finish up a storyline or something of that nature.” That means Michaels and the NXT creative team have to be ready for a wrestler to disappear from their plans without getting the traditional goodbye match or storyline conclusion. Rather than pretending those call-ups didn’t happen, Michaels said NXT can at least acknowledge them on television and explain why somebody is suddenly gone. The other part is having something ready in case it happens. Michaels admitted that NXT ends up scrambling quite a bit when plans suddenly change, so backup ideas have become a necessary part of running the show. “So those are always real possibilities. You have to do your best to just put those to the side. I will say that one thing that helps — again, things like this, everyone kinda understands what NXT is now, and so we are at least allowed to be able to go out there and say, from a TV standpoint, ‘This happened, so-and-so is called up, and there we have it.’ But then we also have to have a backup plan when it does happen.” For Michaels, though, that chaos isn’t entirely a bad thing. title: Rusev Details Post-Injury Illness and Recovery Timeline
raw_title: Rusev Says He Got Sick After Suffering Injury On WWE Raw, Doesn't Think The Two Incidents Were Related
summary_src: Rusev is waiting for his return. Back on the July 27 episode of WWE Raw, Rusev took on Je'Von Evans in a singles contest. After losing to Evans, Rusev quickly left the ring, leading to fan concern.
body: Back on the July 27 episode of WWE Raw, Rusev took on Je’Von Evans in a singles contest. After losing to Evans, Rusev quickly left the ring, leading to fan concern. After disappearing from television, Fightful Select reported that Rusev’s absence was related to injury. Then, in early September, CJ Perry confirmed the report. She also revealed that Rusev has been cleared for a return to the ring. In a new interview with TMZ Inside The Ring, Rusev said that he got sick after the injury. “Good. I’ve been out for what, two or three months or whatnot. Yes, I did get kicked in the head, my hands went numb. Felt better, finished the match. Then, I got a little sick after that. I don’t believe it was related, so I was out for that. But then, I’ve been ready. I’ve been good for about two months, I’m just waiting to go back to TV.” Rusev also spoke about resuming training and his return to the ring at WWE’s live events in Hawaii. “Yeah, I went to NXT. I went to Kech Academy, which is my school in Nashville, I’ve been trying to get ready. Then, they called me out of nowhere just to go to Hawaii for a couple of live events, of course I will. Spent three days in the beach, two great live events, sold out. It was just tremendous. Got to beat Joe Hendry’s ass. He thinks he’s some kind of a musician or something. He used to be my lawyer back ten years ago. So yeah, I had to beat his ass in Hawaii. But then the second night, me and Page head to team against Chad Gable and Rey Mysterio. Working these guys, it’s always a blast.” Fightful will update fans when more is known about Rusev’s return to WWE TV. In the meantime, check out the current lineup for the November 2 episode of Raw by clicking here. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Rusev suffered a kick to the head during his July 27 loss to Je’Von Evans on WWE Raw, causing his hands to go numb, but he finished the match. He later got sick, which he does not believe was connected to the injury, and was sidelined for two to three months before being cleared. Per his interview, Rusev has been training at his Nashville school and NXT, and recently returned to action at WWE live events in Hawaii.

title: Paul Heyman Compares NFL Star's Return To Classic WCW Sting Angle
raw_title: WWE's Paul Heyman Likens NFL Recovery To Classic WCW Sting Moment: 'Nicely Done'
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman agrees with the masses in the NFL that Thursday's game had some pro wrestling elements in it.
body: WWE Was it similar to a pro wrestling angle or not? That's the question that was on NFL viewers' minds both at home and live at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin, on Thursday, after Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson injured his ribs ahead of their victorious 27-19 point game to the Carolina Panthers. During one of their plays, Watson injured his ribs while landing a catch. He was coughing up blood, and was taken to a local hospital by ambulance. Based on the CT scans, Watson did not suffer any internal bleeding, and was cleared to return to the field later that evening. His return saw him exit through the side door of the ambulance, which immediately drew comparisons to an angle in the now defunct promotion, WCW, between "The Icon" Sting and The Dangerous Alliance. Back in 1991, Sting, who was the WCW United States Champion at the time, was facing a moral dilemma of whether his body was at 100 percent to put the title on the line against Rick Rude. If not, he had to forfeit the title. Though he wasn't fully recovered, Sting charged out of an ambulance truck at Clash of Champions 17 to defend his title. Unfortunately, that defense came at a loss, and Rude became champion. There at that match, Rude's former manager and WWE Hall of Famer Paul Heyman agreed with many on last night's comparisons of Watson to Sting saying on X [formerly known as Twitter], "We did this with @Sting in 1991 in WCW (vs 'Ravishing' Rick Rude), and the industry has repeated it with great success in numerous circumstances. My most sincere compliments to the @NFL's creative team. Nicely done!" He went on to plug his son's talk show, "The Roundtable," which premiered last Wednesday. We did this with @Sting in 1991 in WCW (vs Ravishing Rick Rude), and the industry has repeated it with great success in numerous circumstances. PS – Have you checked out The Roundtable? Over 1,000,000... https://t.co/btwVtRkNDF

After CT scans showed no internal bleeding, Watson was cleared and returned to the field that same evening by exiting through the side door of the ambulance. WWE's Paul Heyman likened the moment to a 1991 WCW angle where Sting, then the United States Champion, emerged from an ambulance truck while not fully recovered ahead of his title defense against Rick Rude.

llm_long: During Thursday night's NFL matchup between the Green Bay Packers and the Carolina Panthers, wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a rib injury after landing from a catch and required ambulance transport to a hospital. Watson was observed coughing up blood yet a CT scan revealed no internal bleeding, and despite a confirmed broken rib he received clearance to return after extra padding was applied to the injured area.

He made his reentry to the stadium via ambulance through a side door before rejoining the game, prompting immediate comparisons to pro wrestling angles from observers. Paul Heyman drew a parallel to a 1991 WCW angle at Clash of the Champions 17 involving Sting and The Dangerous Alliance, where Sting arrived by ambulance to avoid forfeiting the United States title and faced Rick Rude.

In that bout Sting competed while portrayed as far from 100 percent and ultimately lost the championship to Rude. Heyman shared the comparison on Twitter while promoting a roundtable discussion featuring his son Jacob alongside Cody Rhodes, Charlotte Flair and O'Shea Jackson Jr.

The Packers went on to defeat the Panthers 27-19, with Watson recording eight receptions for 113 yards in the contest. He added that seeing cameras focused on him emerging from the ambulance felt surreal yet exciting, especially with the crowd cheering his return.

title: Judge Rejects Tammy Sytch Bid to Review 17-Year Sentence
raw_title: Judge dismisses motion by Tammy Sytch to revisit her 17-year prison sentence
summary_src: Tammy Sytch filed a motion seeking a review of her sentence, related to the death of Julian Lasseter in 2022, which she is currently serving.
body: Tammy Sytch recently filed a motion seeking a review of her sentence, related to the death of Julian Lasseter in 2022, which she is currently serving. PWinsider.com first reported that Sytch filed a motion in Volusia County seeking a review of her conviction in November 2023, when she was sentenced to over seventeen years in prison for the death of Lasseter. Sytch pleaded no contest to multiple charges, including driving with a suspended license, driving under the influence, DUI with damage to a person, and DUI with property damage. In March 2022, Sytch struck Lasseter with her vehicle, and Lasseter died shortly afterward at the age of 75. It was revealed that Sytch’s blood-alcohol level was more than three times the legal limit, with a bottle of vodka found in her vehicle. Sytch’s motion is asking the court to revisit the sentence based on “failure to investigate causation”, “failure to investigate conflict”, as well as “omitted” and “new” evidence. Her arguments include her previous defense team not properly investigating Lasseter’s pre-existing medical conditions and whether other factors contributed to his death. She claims it was a “low-speed collision” and that Lasseter had a history of coronary disease, stenosis, and other cardiovascular and internal medical conditions. The argument added that toxicology reports showed Cialis and Adderall in his system and that he had broken his ribs after CPR was administered. The argument over conflict is that Assistant State Attorney Ashley Terwilliger of the prosecution failed to disclose she was married to physician Zachary Terwilliger, who declared the death of the victim. There was no evidence put forth of a conflict, but Sytch believes it should have been disclosed and investigated. The motion was addressed by Circuit Judge Christian Miller, who filed an interim order and dismissed the motion for failing to include the necessary facts or claims to move forward. The motion must be under oath stating that the defendant has read the motion or that it has been read to him or her, that the defendant understands its content, and that all of the facts stated therein are true and correct. The defendant shall either certify that the defendant can understand English or, if the defendant cannot understand English, that the defendant has had the motion translated completely into a language that the defendant understands. The judge added that if Sytch appealed and was successful, her entire case and full list of charges could be revisited at trial and she could end up with a harsher sentence than the one currently being served. Prosecutors were seeking a twenty-six-year sentence for Sytch, and she received a lighter sentence. Sytch is serving her seventeen-year sentence at the Lowell Correctional Institute in Ocala, Florida, and is scheduled to be released in December 2038, although she could reduce her time through various programs in the facility.
summary: Tammy Sytch filed a motion in Volusia County seeking review of her conviction and 17-year prison sentence for the 2022 death of Julian Lasseter. She pleaded no contest to charges including DUI manslaughter, driving with a suspended license, and property damage after striking the 75-year-old with her vehicle while having a blood-alcohol level more than three times the legal limit. The judge has dismissed the motion, which cited failure to investigate causation and conflict along with omitted and new evidence regarding Lasseter's pre-existing medical conditions.

title: On the Record: AJ Styles Has Been Quietly ‘Running Things’ at WWE Performance Center for Months
raw_title: AJ Styles Has Been Quietly ‘Running Things’ at WWE Performance Center for Months
summary_src: AJ Styles might already be doing a whole lot more behind the scenes in NXT than people realize. With all the talk about him potentially taking over once Shawn Michaels moves up, a new update makes it sound like AJ has basically been getting a head start for months.
body: According to Andrew Baydala , Styles has quietly been “running things” at the WWE Performance Center for months. That comes right as rumors continue to heat up about Styles potentially taking on a much bigger NXT role after WrestleMania 43. “Regarding the news/rumor that AJ Styles will take over for HBK in #WWENXT after #WrestleMania 43. Styles has been quietly running things in the WWE PC for months.” That doesn’t mean WWE has officially handed Styles the keys to NXT or named him Shawn Michaels’ replacement. But AJ being heavily involved at the Performance Center isn’t coming completely out of nowhere either. Styles previously revealed that he had been filling in for a coach while also producing matches and working directly with younger talent. That also makes Matt Hardy’s recent comments a little more interesting. Hardy believes Styles’ years grinding through the independent scene could influence the kind of talent he gives opportunities to if his power within NXT grows . “I think he’s definitely much more on the pulse of indie workers, and he would be much more willing to give someone a chance than someone like Shawn Michaels would be because I don’t think Shawn is quite on that same pulse.” Styles hasn’t officially been announced as the next guy running NXT, and the original report only said people within the Performance Center expect him to become more hands-on once Michaels moves up. But if AJ really has already been quietly taking on that kind of responsibility for months, WWE may not have to look very far whenever it’s time for somebody else to take a bigger seat at the table. Do you think AJ Styles is the right person to take on a bigger role in NXT once Shawn Michaels moves up? Let us know what you think in the comments. Done with his in-ring duties , Styles now works as a producer for several WWE NXT matches as well as a scout for talent. With Bruce Prichard reportedly looking to work remotely or retiring from the WWE main roster, NXT's Shawn Michaels is a heavy favorite to take over that role. With still time left for WWE WrestleMania 43, there are currently no confirmations about AJ Styles or Shawn Michaels' new role. title: The Introduction She Never Forgot — Molly Holly
raw_title: Molly Holly: The Introduction She Never Forgot
body: Molly Holly once wrestled in front of just six people in Florida, happy to earn a little extra money on weekends. The future two-time WWE Women’s Champion entered wrestling out of curiosity after her Subway manager invited her, never imagining how far it could take her. Her breakthrough came through an unexpected assignment, meant to prepare someone else for the spotlight. Nora Greenwald grew up in Forest Lake, Minnesota, in a family comfortable around weights and exercise. Her parents owned a gym, and she followed her father into powerlifting. By 14, she was bench-pressing 100 pounds, according to her 2006 interview with Jimmy Van. Gymnastics, which she began as a small child, helped her understand where her body was as she moved through the air. After moving to Florida, she worked at Subway. Her manager there, Tim Mahoney, was also a professional wrestler and invited her to give it a try. Nora remembered wrestling from childhood, but she had not followed it for years and did not realize women could wrestle the way the men she had watched did. As Nora put it in her 2006 interview with Jimmy Van : "I went just out of curiosity." That curiosity took her to a backyard training camp. Her gymnastics helped her learn the movements, and she began wrestling in 1997, working small independent shows as Starla Saxton. She kept a day job as a telemarketer while wrestling on weekends, initially enjoying the matches without expecting them to become a career. "I never dreamed I would actually make it to the big leagues," she reflected in her 2010 interview with WWE’s Ryan Murphy . Starla Saxton was a character she had chosen herself: an All-American Girl who scattered star-shaped confetti for the children in those small crowds. It gave her a chance to try out a personality as well as wrestling moves, even with only a few children in the audience. More experienced wrestlers helped her along. Jeff Bradley worked with her in the ring and offered advice, although she clarified to Van that she had not generally identified him as her trainer. Malia Hosaka became an opponent and traveling companion. In Jim McLennan’s March 2006 interview, Nora credited Hosaka with encouraging her to pursue WCW work and consider wrestling as a livelihood. She was still learning when WCW gave her tryout matches. Dean Malenko had initially declined to accept her at his school, but watching her wrestle Hosaka changed his mind. The invitation came after those early matches, giving her a chance to improve skills she had already begun using in front of audiences. "There was so much I didn’t know," Nora acknowledged on an October 2016 episode of X-Pac 1,2,360 featuring her and Shawn Daivari. Eddie Guerrero also stopped by Malenko’s school. Nora discussed those visits with Lanny Poffo in an interview recorded for Pro Wrestling Stories’ podcast, The Genius Cast , on January 15, 2019. body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) The Thursday, October 22, TNA Thursday Night Impact averaged 233,000 viewers for AMC, according to Brandon Thurston of Wrestlenomics.com . Thursday’s viewership count was down compared to the prior week’s 252,000 average. Impact finished with a 0.03 rating in the 18-49 demographic, down from the previous show’s 0.05 rating. Powell’s POV: The AMC+ and TNA+ streaming numbers are not included in the rating or viewership count for TNA Impact. TNA avoided the World Series last week. The Thursday Night Football game between the Chicago Bears and New England Patriots averaged 19.86 million viewers for Amazon Prime and local over-the-air simulcasts.

title: Ilja Dragunov Eyes AEW Continental Classic
raw_title: Ilja Dragunov Comments On Entering AEW's Continental Classic Tournament
summary_src: Ilja Dragunov addresses the possibility of him entering the 2026 AEW Continental Classic, which is slated to kick off next month.
body: Ilja Dragunov came into All Elite Wrestling "starving" for competition. Fortunately for him, there's a round-robin tournament that could potentially satisfy that appetite. On this week's edition of "AEW Advance," Dragunov addressed the possibility of him entering the 2026 Continental Classic, which is slated to kick off on the November 18 episode of "AEW Dynamite" in Denver, Colorado. "There's a lot of thought that I have on the Continental Classic," Dragunov said, "because looking back in 2023, Eddie Kingston, 2024, [Kazuchika] Okada, '25, [Jon] Moxley. This tournament represents mental toughness, because as far as I remember, all these people went through injuries, through setbacks, through really memorable moments, especially with Eddie, like a big emotional moment ... This tournament is representing strength, resilience, and I feel like the landscape of AEW is about to change. Why? Because I am here." According to Dragunov, it would be embarrassing, both for AEW and fans, if he were not cast in the 2026 Continental Classic, especially given that he embodies all of the attributes associated with it. Ultimately, he knows that the final decision rests in the hands of AEW officials, however. Jon Moxley, the reigning AEW Continental Champion , won last year's iteration by defeating Kazuchika Okada in the finals. Okada conquered the 2024 tournament with a finals victory over Will Ospreay. The Continental Classic typically stretches several weeks, with AEW Worlds End serving as the stage for its final faceoffs. This year's Worlds End event will take AEW to the Target Center in Minneapolis, Minnesota on December 19.
summary: Ilja Dragunov told AEW Advance that he is starving for competition and has been considering the 2026 Continental Classic tournament. He highlighted past winners Eddie Kingston in 2023, Kazuchika Okada in 2024 and Jon Moxley in 2025 while noting the event tests mental toughness through injuries and setbacks. Dragunov declared that the AEW landscape is about to change because of his presence and that excluding him would be embarrassing for the company and its fans.

The company's newest signee Ilja Dragunov appeared on the social media show AEW Advance where he was asked about possibly entering the event. Dragunov referenced his past with the winner of the first Continental Classic, Eddie Kingston.

He described the tournament as representing mental toughness, noting that all winners had gone through injuries, setbacks, and memorable moments. Dragunov highlighted the emotional aspect of the event, particularly with Eddie Kingston. He expressed admiration for Kingston's work while noting their unresolved issues from the past.

He characterized the Continental Classic as embodying strength, resilience, and intensity. Dragunov declared that the landscape of AEW is about to change because he is now part of the company. He emphasized that he is not the person who makes the decision about his involvement.

raw_title: Tatum Paxley set for WWE NXT Halloween Havoc role
summary_src: Tatum Paxley is returning to WWE NXT to be part of the Halloween Havoc 2026 festivities. Though she’s now on SmackDown, Paxley posted a tweet today revealing that she’ll be a panelist for Saturday’s PLE. The pre-show streams live at 6 p.m.
body: Tatum Paxley is returning to WWE NXT to be part of the Halloween Havoc 2026 festivities. Though she’s now on SmackDown, Paxley posted a tweet today revealing that she’ll be a panelist for Saturday’s PLE. The pre-show streams live at 6 p.m. Eastern time before the main card begins at 7 p.m. Eastern. “Yup yup yup it sure doesn’t seem right to have Tater Paxley NOT be at #halloweenhavoc,” she wrote. “SOOOO this year I’m coming to be one of the panelist cause i REFUSE to miss out on the show that gave me one of my best moments of my career! See you Saturday @WWENXT” Halloween Havoc 2025 is where Paxley dethroned Jacy Jayne for the NXT Women’s Championship last year. While on the brand, Paxley held the NXT Women’s Championship and Women’s North American Championship one time each. Paxley has aligned with Alexa Bliss and Charlotte Flair on the main roster. Bliss was one of her biggest wrestling inspirations when she was younger, and the two briefly held the WWE Women’s Tag Team titles together before dropping them to Michin & B-Fab last week. At Thursday night’s WWE house show in Youngstown, Ohio, Paxley & Bliss dressed up as characters from the movie “Dodgeball” for their loss to Michin & B-Fab, who were dressed as Chucky dolls . The WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida is hosting Halloween Havoc 2026 on Halloween night. Danhausen will be the host of the show, which airs live on The CW (and the ESPN Unlimited app) in the United States and on Netflix elsewhere. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: Tatum Paxley, now on SmackDown, will serve as a panelist for the Halloween Havoc 2025 pre-show. She made the announcement on social media, citing her memorable title win at last year's event where she defeated Jacy Jayne for the NXT Women's Championship. Paxley previously held both the NXT Women's Championship and the Women's North American Championship during her time on the brand.

title: Komander Sidelined With Injury

body: According to Dave Meltzer, Komander is currently sidelined with an injury. There is hope that he will return soon, although AEW has not provided a recovery timeline or a possible comeback date, nor has it disclosed the nature of the injury. This is not the first time the star has missed AEW-related events this year. He previously dealt with visa issues that kept him and The Beast Mortos away from ROH Supercard of Honor in May. Komander is known for his high-flying style and aerial offense, and he has competed regularly in AEW, its sister company ROH, and CMLL. McKenzie Mitchell was the ring announcer… 1. M by Elegance (w/Heather by Elegance, Mr. Elegance) vs. Jada Stone for the TNA Knockouts Television Championship. Jada dominated early with running strikes and a Slingshot Huracanrana. Stone got a two count after a standing Moonsault. Mr. Elegance went for a distraction but Jada sidestepped M to send her foot into Elegance and knock him off the apron. Jada dropkicked M to ringside and followed up with a Suicide Dive. Jada did a backflip that M reversed into a backdrop to dump Jada to ringside. M worked on Jada with methodical offense. Jada avoided M’s moonsault and gave her running strikes. Jada set up M with a huracanrana and hit M with a Tiger Feint Kick. Both women traded counters. M gave Jada a Superkick. Jada gave M a backflip into a Stunner. M went for a time out with the Elegance Brand. M and Heather sidestepped, which led to Jada giving Mr. Elegance a Moonsault. M by Elegance defeated Jada Stone via pinfall in 6:41 to retain the TNA Knockouts TV Championship. Hannifan wondered if Mr. Elegance has left the brand for good?… John’s Thoughts: I wasn’t the biggest fan of the visual pinfall that was broken up by Heather “arguing” with the referee (Makes the referee look like a dope for not focusing on her count and instead deciding to do something else). Thankfully they fixed that a bit by putting M on the handicap side with Mr. Elegance ending up as a distraction to her, only for M to overcome the handicap. Mr. Elegance being “done” makes for an interesting hook. Personally, I wouldn’t dissolve the brand so quick as to try to farm a story out of it. There was no explanation as to where The Concierge and Ash went aside from a vague throwaway sentence last week (they didn’t even say anything about The Concierge). It would be fun if they can drag out Heather’s pseudo-indentured servitude to M for a bit. Backstage, Alisha asked the camera “do you want to know something?” which means a System promo was starting. Bear assumed that meant Eddie was implying that The System shouldn’t support Cedric in his title match. Brian Myers played peacekeeper and said that it’s ultimately Cedric’s decision as to weather he needs help or not. Cedric said he’s the best X Division Wrestler in the world and will bring the title back to The System. Eddie assumed that meant Cedric was going to handle things on his own. summary_src: Last week, we got excited about a loaded card WWE was bringing to Youngstown, Ohio for a non-televised live event (aka a house show). That show was last night (Oct. 29), and based on what’s been shared from it on social media, it didn’t disappoint.
body: Link @VaquerBnks Last week, we got excited about a loaded card WWE was bringing to Youngstown, Ohio for a non-televised live event (aka a house show). We haven't really done the whole "brand warfare" thing in a while, but it is Survivor Series SZN. And it looks like WWE is bringing Men's Intercontinental champ Chad Gable to a SmackDown live event for a "Special Attraction" match. He'll face a member of the blue brand he's never gone one-on-one with before... CM Punk. In addition that, the rest of the line up for next Thursday's house show in Youngstown, Ohio (shout out to my rust belt peoples, who are getting their first visit from WWE since 2023 at Covelli Centre on Oct. 29) looks like something one of us might book. The poster is dope, too. We already told you about Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley’s Dodgeball costumes , but we didn’t tell you Women’s Tag champs B-Fab and Michin, along with Jade Cargill, wore Child’s Play-inspired gear. We also didn’t tell you that the Average Joes took Patches’ coaching into the ring with them against Fab… … that amazing sequence didn’t get them the win however, because when Bliss went to put B away with a Sister Abigail, Cargill showed up to kick Lexi in the face and ensure her Baddies remained belted. It wasn’t the only Spooky SZN shenanigans on the night. Zayn would eventually retain by pinning Kevin Owens after Rhodes had hit his finisher on KO several times, and after Sami closking Cody with the belt right before the ref recovered. title: Every WWE NXT Halloween Havoc, Ranked By Quality
raw_title: Every WWE NXT Halloween Havoc, Ranked By Quality
body: By Andrew Kelly Published Oct 30, 2026, 1:01 PM EDT Andrew Kelly is a pro wrestling writer from The Wirral, England. With bylines on many pro wrestling websites, Andrew has proven himself to be very knowledgeable in the realms of WWE, AEW and more. Andrew is one of TheSportster's Match Reviewers and has covered the best matches of superstars like Cody Rhodes, MJF, Bianca Belair and more. He's also written hundreds of lists and features covering wrestling current events and history. He is also an MA Graduate from the University of Manchester, and a BA Graduate from Liverpool John Moores University, both in Creative Writing. Sign in to your TheSportster account WWE’s developmental brand NXT has often been used to reimagine and bring back older wrestling concepts - both from the extensive histories of WWE and WCW. Halloween Havoc is one of the several old WCW PPVs that has been brought back, being used as both an NXT television special and more recently as a PLE. NXT Halloween Havoc has been hosted annually since 2020, offering a differing range of quality when it comes to match cards. Some have been fantastic and very enjoyable and some have fallen short of expectations, but which modern day iteration of Halloween Havoc is the greatest to date? The decision was made to make Halloween Havoc a PLE in 2024, but it resulted in the weakest iteration of the NXT event to date. The show peaked in the opening two matches with a fun TLC match between Tony D’Angelo and Oba Femi, plus a tag team match in which new marquee signings Giulia and Stephanie Vaquer teamed up to take on Roxanne Perez and Cora Jade. Things went downhill from there. title: Sunny Sytch Seeks to Vacate DUI Manslaughter Conviction
raw_title: WWE Hall of Famer Tammy ‘Sunny’ Sytch attempting to have conviction thrown out
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer Tammy “Sunny” Sytch, currently serving a prison sentence set to last until December 2038, is attempting to have her conviction thrown out.
body: WWE Hall of Famer Tammy “Sunny” Sytch, currently serving a prison sentence set to last until December 2038, is attempting to have her conviction thrown out. Sytch was convicted in 2023 on charges related to the death of Julian LaFrancis Lasseter, a 75-year-old man who was killed in a traffic accident involving Sytch that took place in Florida in March 2022. After pleading no contest, Sytch — who already had a history of DUI offenses — was sentenced to more than 17 years in prison for DUI manslaughter and driving without a license and causing injury/death. PWInsider reports that Sytch filed a motion earlier this month in an effort to have her conviction vacated. In the motion, Sytch alleges that she received ineffective counsel from her defense, claiming that the defense did not properly investigate other factors that led to Lasseter’s death, including Lasseter’s medical history that the motion says includes coronary artery disease, stenosis, and other serious cardiovascular and medical conditions. The motion also says toxicology results indicate Lasseter had Adderall and Cialis in his system. Along with this, Sytch says her counsel was ineffective because they did not investigate a conflict of interest where an assistant state attorney who helped prosecute the case was married to the physician who declared Lasseter’s death. Ineffective counsel claims are generally considered hard to prove, with the defendant having to show that their counsel was incompetent or made a serious mistake that affected the outcome of the case, rather than just making decisions that did not work out. The motion asked that Sytch be granted a new trial or other post-conviction relief. In response to this motion, the judge automatically denied it because it did not meet the correct parameters to be considered. Sytch can now either file a motion to appeal that decision or drop her attempt to have the conviction vacated. The judge warned that, if Sytch were successful in her attempt to get the conviction re-examined, her original plea would no longer apply and she could end up serving a longer sentence than the original 17 years. llm_long: Tammy Sytch, known as Sunny in WWE, is seeking to have her conviction overturned. She is currently serving a prison sentence in Florida following her 2023 conviction related to a March 2022 traffic incident in Ormond Beach that resulted in the death of 75-year-old Julian Lasseter.

The conviction included charges of DUI causing death, causing death while operating a vehicle with a suspended or revoked driver’s license, four counts of DUI causing injury, and three counts of DUI causing damage to property.

Sytch claims her defense counsel provided ineffective assistance by failing to investigate and present evidence about Lasseter’s pre-existing medical conditions, toxicology results, and possible alternative causes of death.

According to the motion, the incident involved a low-speed collision in which Sytch had slowed her vehicle and was moving toward a turnaround lane. The filing states that Lasseter had no significant physical injuries clearly explaining death from the impact itself.

Civil discovery revealed Lasseter had a substantial and long-standing medical history that included coronary artery disease, stenosis, and other serious cardiovascular and internal medical conditions. Toxicology records showed Adderall and Cialis in his system, and he suffered fractured ribs consistent with CPR administered at the scene.

The motion argues these records raise questions about whether emergency life-saving measures, pre-existing vascular disease, toxicology findings, a spontaneous medical event, or another medical circumstance contributed to or caused the aortic injury, hemorrhage, and death.

body: Rusev is all healed up and just awaiting his return to WWE programming. Aside from working a couple of WWE house show dates in Hawaii this month, we haven’t seen Rusev compete since July. He confirmed to TMZ’s Inside the Ring that his hands went numb during a match against Je’Von Evans on the July 27 episode of Raw. Rusev then got sick for a little bit after that, but he does not believe the issues are related. He’s now recovered from both and is ready to compete. “Good, good,” Rusev responded when asked how he’s feeling. “I’ve been out for what — two, three months or whatnot. But yes, I did get kicked in the head, my hands went numb, felt better, finished the match. Then, I got a little sick after that. Not related, I don’t believe it was related. So I was out for that. But then, I’ve been ready. I’ve been good for about two months. I’m just waiting to go back to TV.” Rusev said he’s been training at his school in Nashville and has visited the WWE Performance Center. In response to rumors that WWE could be planning for him to be part of a faction with Ethan Page and Big Cass upon his return to Raw, Rusev claimed that he has not heard that and said it sounds like “internet booking” with three bag guys being put together. Rusev played up that he might not want to be associated with Page anymore given that Page has replaced him with Cass. Earlier this week, Rusev and his wife CJ Perry (formerly known as Lana in WWE) revealed that they are expecting their first child . The baby, a boy, will be named Bear Petrov Barnyashev. Perry is under a Legends contract with WWE and has said she’d love to appear on television again in the future if the timing and storyline are right. title: Real Reason Jeff Hardy Was Written Off TNA Television
raw_title: Real Reason Jeff Hardy Was Written Off TNA Television
summary_src: Jeff Hardy is disappearing from TNA television again, but this isn’t some sudden creative decision after that brutal Slaughterhouse Syx Match. His absence was already coming, and the timing apparently worked out about as perfectly as TNA could have hoped.
body: According to Fightful Select , Hardy has been written off television following the October 29 episode of Impact, where Joseph Sawyer and Samuel Shaw absolutely wrecked him. But the angle was planned with TNA already knowing Hardy would need to miss the company’s upcoming shows in Canada. The bigger concern coming into all of this was Hardy’s neck. Matt Hardy recently revealed on The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy that Jeff has been dealing with bulging discs and would need some time away from the ring. Fightful reports that surgery doesn’t appear to be necessary right now, although the neck issues did contribute to the decision to give him some time off. That’s not actually the main reason Jeff will be missing the next stretch of TNA shows, though. TNA is heading to Canada, and Hardy’s previous legal issues prevent him from making the trip. Because of that, TNA has regularly had to find ways to remove him from television whenever the company heads north of the border. One TNA source described the situation as a “perfect storm.” Hardy couldn’t work the Canadian dates anyway, so having Syx take him out gives TNA a storyline explanation for his disappearance while also giving him a chance to rest his neck over the next couple of months. There could still be some Hardy material on television during that stretch. TNA can potentially film segments with him ahead of time and air them during the Canada shows, but he won’t physically be at those events. More importantly, this isn’t expected to be some lengthy disappearance. Those Fightful spoke with believe Hardy should be back for TNA’s December television tapings in Texas. He’s also still scheduled for some major appearances outside that Canadian loop, including the Jericho Cruise and WrestleCade. That makes the insane ending to the Slaughterhouse Syx Match make a whole lot more sense. Sawyer and Shaw trapped Jeff underneath a trash can before swinging fireman’s axes into it, leaving him completely motionless and giving TNA a pretty horrifying excuse to get him off television. So Syx may get to spend the next several weeks acting like they finally accomplished their mission, but TNA apparently already has an idea of when their victim will come crawling back. If everything goes according to plan, December could give Jeff the chance to pick up exactly where that axe-swinging nightmare left off. What do you want to see Jeff Hardy do when he returns to TNA after getting some time to heal his neck? Let us know what you think in the comments. body: Bull Nakano’s autobiography is set to be released on January 8, 2027. On social media , WWE Hall of Famer Bull Nakano shared with fans that her autobiography will be released next January by Wani Books. It’ll cover behind-the-scenes stories from her career, as well as her matches against Aja Kong, her time in the Gokumon-to faction, and more. My autobiography, “Bull Nakano: Monster,” will be released on January 8, 2027, by Wani Books! Thirty years after my retirement, I will reveal the secrets behind the scenes of my time in the ring, including my battles with the “Bad Ass” Aja Kong, the “Gokumon-to” faction, and the “Golden Cage” death match. I will also share my thoughts and struggles during that time. I have written about the good times and the hard times, as well as things I can only talk about now. I have also opened up about my life after retirement. This book is a compilation of my life, which I dedicated to professional wrestling. I hope fans who enjoyed my career and those who support the current generation of female wrestlers will enjoy it. Nakano wrestled for over 30 years before retiring from the business in November 2017. She was inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame in 2024.

summary_src: Mick Foley isn’t just taking shots at Donald Trump on social media anymore. This time, the WWE Hall of Famer went all-in with a direct message to Americans ahead of the midterms — and he’s straight-up asking people to vote Democrat, even if they normally wouldn’t.
body: Speaking on his YouTube channel on October 30 , Foley started by making one thing clear: he considers himself an independent voter. But he believes things have gotten serious enough that people should temporarily put their normal party preferences aside because, in his view, Congress hasn’t done its job when it comes to keeping Trump in check. “Hello everybody. My name is Mick Foley. I’m probably best known as a three-time WWE Champion, but I’m also a registered independent voter. That’s why I’m asking you to consider voting in a way you otherwise might not to stop the corruption. See, because this man, Donald Trump, seems to think he can do whatever he does without the oversight of Congress.” And Foley was just getting started. He absolutely unloaded on members of Congress for what he sees as their refusal to stand up to Trump, saying they simply haven’t had the guts to do it. He then dropped one of his strongest lines of the entire video by calling Trump the most corrupt president in American history. “And up until now, he’s been largely correct because these men and these women lack the fortitude, the courage, the backbone, and let’s call it what it is. They lack the balls to stand up to the most corrupt president in the history of the United States.” Foley then went after Elon Musk while talking about USAID. He argued that the agency was effectively dismantled after being branded fraudulent without that claim going through the proper legal process, and he blamed the changes for an enormous human toll. “Now, technically, they didn’t close it. They let the State Department take it over and effectively dissolved it, meaning there is no more USAID. And here’s the thing: it was the most effective aid organization in the history of the world. And it has been estimated that because of its closure, 600,000 human beings have died who otherwise would still be alive, the vast majority of them children.” Foley clearly wasn’t interested in letting Musk off easy either. He brought up Musk’s wealth and argued that somebody with those kinds of resources should be thinking about fighting extreme poverty instead. Once again, Foley’s bigger issue came back to Congress and what he believes was its failure to step in. “Because the richest man in the world didn’t think that their lives mattered. Here’s a man worth a trillion dollars, closing in on a trillion dollars. Keep in mind, I want you to know that in a book in 2005, the 2005 book by Dr. Jeffrey Sachs, The End of Poverty, it was estimated it would take $175 billion to put an end to extreme poverty. “And instead of us concentrating on doing something like that with a fraction of the money that this man’s worth, he sees fit to end the lives of 600,000 human beings. Breakker and Reed attacked Evans and Penta after Evans’ WWE Championship match against Sami Zayn. Penta then asked Adam Pearce for a tag title shot, and Pearce booked the match for Crown Jewel. The Observer also reported that the original Crown Jewel lineup included Gunther vs. Finn Balor . If that match is not happening, it was changed, and the workers setting up Riyadh Season Stadium saw posters from the old lineup. Promotional material featuring Gunther and Balor was spotted at one of the gates at Riyadh Season Stadium in KAFD. WWE has not announced the match, but the two have been tied together on SmackDown, with Balor saving Danhausen from a Gunther attack on the October 9 episode. The tag title match is the right call. Evans and Penta have been building toward a shot at The Vision, and a six-man match without a title on the line would have skipped a step. Doing the tag title match first gives WWE a clear story, and the six-man tag with Femi could still happen later. The bigger question is Gunther. The Observer’s report leaves the match’s status open. If Gunther vs. Balor is not happening, the posters at the stadium came from an older version of the card, and that would be a missed opportunity for Gunther, who has had a frustrating 2026 and has spent recent weeks in comedic segments with Danhausen. If WWE does not use Gunther vs. Balor at Crown Jewel, it should still find a big stage for it soon. Gunther has said he wants a proper program with Balor, and the match would give him the kind of spotlight he has been missing for most of the year. llm_long: During Thursday night's NFL matchup between the Green Bay Packers and the Carolina Panthers, wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a rib injury after landing from a catch and required ambulance transport to a hospital. Watson was observed coughing up blood yet a CT scan revealed no internal bleeding, and despite a confirmed broken rib he received clearance to return after extra padding was applied to the injured area.

He made his reentry to the stadium via ambulance through a side door before rejoining the game, prompting immediate comparisons to pro wrestling angles from observers. Paul Heyman drew a parallel to a 1991 WCW angle at Clash of the Champions 17 involving Sting and The Dangerous Alliance, where Sting arrived by ambulance to avoid forfeiting the United States title and faced Rick Rude.

In that bout Sting competed while portrayed as far from 100 percent and ultimately lost the championship to Rude. Heyman shared the comparison on Twitter while promoting a roundtable discussion featuring his son Jacob alongside Cody Rhodes, Charlotte Flair and O'Shea Jackson Jr.

The Packers went on to defeat the Panthers 27-19, with Watson recording eight receptions for 113 yards in the contest. He added that seeing cameras focused on him emerging from the ambulance felt surreal yet exciting, especially with the crowd cheering his return.

title: Blake Monroe says injuries delayed her SmackDown debut
raw_title: WWE SmackDown debut delay shook Blake Monroe’s confidence
summary_src: There’s been a lot of attention paid to Blake Monroe’s WWE career.
body: Debate about the former Mariah May continued throughout her NXT run, and some were ready to declare Monroe wrong for betting on herself when her didn’t have a match on SmackDown for five months after being called up earlier this year. Monroe told WWE Radio’s Busted Open today (Oct. 30) that injuries were a factor in the delay. She didn’t specify who or what was hurt, but it doesn’t sound like she was banged up. From there Blake gave an (at least partially in-character) answer about the importance of properly introducing a star of her magnitude: “SmackDown wanted me and they made a play for me, and I do think injuries changed a lot of things. And it’s just finding the right moment to debut someone like Blake Monroe. I’m not somebody that you just throw out there. I’m not somebody that will ever get lost in the shuffle. I’m not just the next girl. I’m ‘the girl,’ and I think it was all about waiting for the right time, the right story, the right opponent to show that I’m not just a pretty face and a big character, I can actually go in the ring.” The wait brought self-doubt, but the 28-year-old from England pushed through it: “I love to work. I love to be out in front of the crowd. I love to win people over, and I can’t do that if I’m not out there. So I was chomping at the bit for five months dying to get out there, and I know better than anyone else that timing is everything. I’ve achieved things in my career that would not have happened if I didn’t fail 10 times before and that’s so many different things, big and small. “So I knew in my heart, timing is everything, but it does get to a point months in where you’re thinking, ‘Alright, I train, I go to the gym every day, I dress like a million bucks, I have my character, I have ideas. I want to be out there. I see other girls I think I could be better than them. I think if I had the shots they had and the opportunities they had, I would have done more with it.’ “There is that natural hunger and desire, and it can get to a point where you question yourself and think, ‘Why is this not happening for me?’ But ultimately, it’s such a huge machine, there’s so many moving parts. There’s unpredictable factors like injuries and other things that shift around. For me, it was just every single week turning up and saying, ‘I’m ready for this. Here’s 20 different things I want to do on the show until one of them sticks,’ and it did. Now I feel like I’m on the show and you can’t ignore me. You cannot keep me in the back for another week. You cannot look at me and my peers and not use me now. “I did have moments where I questioned myself, so let that be a lesson to everyone out there. Even The Glamour questions herself, but I remembered who I am, what I did to get here, and I just kept working harder.” Hard work finally got The Glamour in the ring this month, and she picked up back-to-back wins over former Women’s United States champion Giulia. title: Best Royal Rumbles Ever, Ranked by How They Tell a Story
raw_title: Best Royal Rumbles Ever, Ranked by How They Tell a Story
body: Every Rumble season, a fresh batch of lists ranks the best Royal Rumbles, and I read them all. Wrestling Inc, TheSportster, FanSided and GiveMeSport each have a version. Most of them sort the matches by who showed up or how many stars a critic handed out. That approach misses what makes the Rumble special. The match is a format before it is a fight. It has a clock, entry numbers, a final four and a long chain of eliminations. Here is my rule for this list: a great Rumble uses its own structure as narrative. Entry numbers carry meaning, and the clock builds pressure. Eliminations land like plot beats, and the final four plays like a third act. I’ve spent a long stretch with these matches in our ongoing Ranking the Rumbles retrospective here at 25YL. This countdown boils that work down to six picks. Some of them will look familiar from other lists. The order, and the reasons behind it, should not. One note before we start. The storylines are scripted, including who enters where and who wins. I’ll flag the one spot where real life crashed into the fiction. FanSided’s power rankings named the 2001 men’s Rumble the greatest of all time. I understand the pick. Stone Cold Steve Austin won, and that win set up Austin vs. The Rock at WrestleMania 17. That handoff is also my problem with it. The 2001 Rumble matters most for what it launched. Its value sits in the next show on the calendar. Under my rule, that costs it. Austin’s victory reads as the opening scene of a WrestleMania story. The Rumble format works as a delivery system here, and the ending lands about where you’d expect. It still makes the list because the delivery works. A Rumble that hands off to an all-time main event is doing its job. It just does a different job than the five matches above it. The 2008 Rumble took place at Madison Square Garden. John Cena entered at No. 30 as a surprise return from injury, then won the whole thing. Our piece on Cena’s Garden return covers the night in full. This is the purest case of an entry number doing story work. The No. 30 slot carries built-in suspense because it is the last unknown. The 2008 match spent that suspense on the biggest possible reveal. The countdown before that final entrant becomes a drumroll. Everyone watching knows one name remains. The format asks the question, and Cena’s music answers it. Once Cena wins, the match has landed one great reveal and little else. The four entries above it build their stories across the whole running time. Batista entered at No. 28 and won the 2005 Rumble. The ending is why people still talk about it. Batista and John Cena went over the top rope together, leaving no clear winner. Then Vince McMahon came down to sort it out. He slid into the ring and tore both quadriceps. That injury was real, even though the storyline around it was scripted. I rank 2005 here because the format created its own crisis. The over-the-top rule demands one survivor. When two men hit the floor at once, the rule itself became th
summary: Every Rumble season, a fresh batch of lists ranks the best Royal Rumbles, and I read them all. Most of them sort the matches by who showed up or how many stars a critic handed out.

title: Halloween Havoc 1997 remembered for Mysterio-Guerrero classic
raw_title: Revisiting Halloween Havoc 1997: A wild event with an all-time classic match
body: Link Screenshot WCW’s YouTube channel WCW’s Halloween Havoc 1997 was a historic event for a number of reasons, including the main event between Hulk Hogan and Rowdy Roddy Piper in a steel cage. Miraculously, Vince McMahon never booked a Hogan vs. Piper singles match on a major pay per view during the WWF’s heyday in the 1980s. (I’m not counting the mostly forgotten The Wrestling Classic PPV from 1985, which the Hulkster won via DQ.) However, as great as the cage match sounds on paper, it wasn’t even the highlight of the night at Halloween Havoc . While the card was full of future Hall of Famers who would continue showing up on our TV screens for years, the event is now mainly remembered from two of WCW’s smallest stars, Rey Mysterio and Eddie Guerrero , who not only stole the show, but gave viewers a glimpse of wrestling’s future. Much more on Rey and Eddie later, but a little background first. Last week, I put up a poll for Cageside Seats readers to choose a Halloween Havoc for me to do a deep dive on, and 1997’s event edged out the 1993 Havoc . I do encourage anyone who’s a fan of that era of wrestling to give 1993’s a watch. The main event saw Cactus Jack take on Big Van Vader in a Texas Death Match, and the card features solid wrestling from legends like Ric Flair, Rick Rude, Steve Austin, Sting, Ricky Steamboat, Paul Orndorff, and many more. As for the poll winner: The 1997 event — the ninth Havoc overall — took place October 27 in the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Paradise, Nevada, and 12,457 very enthusiastic fans packed the venue. An important fact to keep in mind is that this Halloween Havoc occurred during WCW’s hottest streak, when the company had done the seemingly impossible feat of beating the then-WWF in ratings. In fact, the event was held during the still-legendary streak of the 83 consecutive weeks of WCW Monday Night Nitro beating Monday Night Raw in television ratings. The ultimate winner of the Monday Night War, WWE, has fortunately uploaded Halloween Havoc 1997 in its entirety on the company’s WCW YouTube page. The festivities started with some talk from the commentary team, and boy, what a team. WCW mainstay (and current AEW employee) Tony Schiavone was joined by the incomparable Bobby Heenan and Dusty Rhodes, who thankfully can’t hide his charisma behind an uncharacteristically clean-cut look. Mike Tenay joined the table for the first match between Yuji Nagata (with Sonny Onoo in his corner) against Último Dragón. What followed was an exciting match between two Japanese stars looking to impress the American crowd. Whereas Dragón used a more high-flying repertoire, Nagata employed something akin to Strong Style, and overall the match proved a strong way to kick off the night. Honestly, if you’re going do a re-watch of the show, don’t skip this one. This unannounced match between two stars who had competed in Japan’s Super J-Cup tournament a couple of years earlier is certainly worth attention for the simple fact of seeing a you
summary: WCW Halloween Havoc 1997 featured a steel cage main event between Hulk Hogan and Roddy Piper. The show is best remembered for Rey Mysterio versus Eddie Guerrero, which stole the card and previewed the future style of wrestling. A reader poll on Cageside Seats selected the 1997 event over the 1993 edition for a detailed retrospective.

title: End of an Era: Word On WWE Replacing Bruce Prichard After Retirement Following WrestleMania 43, Shawn Michaels & More In Discussion
raw_title: Backstage Note on WWE Replacing Bruce Prichard After Retirement Following WrestleMania 43, Shawn Michaels & More In Discussion
body: WWE is reportedly preparing to redistribute responsibilities after Bruce Prichard retires following WrestleMania 43 . Ed Koskey and Robert Roode have reportedly emerged as potential successors to the veteran executive. Dave Meltzer noted that Bruce Prichard recently learned about a neck injury dating back to 1991 that has worsened. He is expected to undergo surgery, although some sources within WWE have described the procedure as back surgery. The report stated his travels with WWE while his body is “beat up at his age, probably isn’t the best thing for him.” Meltzer also reports that Shawn Michaels could be a candidate , but taking on Prichard’s role would require him to travel to WWE television twice weekly. That would make it “very difficult to keep his position in NXT,” where he remains “very valuable for a number of reasons.” As Senior Vice President of Talent Development, Creative, and overseer of the creative aspects of NXT, Michaels is reportedly “up for doing more,” but Prichard’s administrative work differs from his current position. Koskey, in comparison, has extensive experience handling those responsibilities. Within NXT, Matt Bloom has always handled that aspect of the operation. The decision is likely to change multiple times as WrestleMania 43 approaches in April. Meltzer noted that NXT personnel haven’t been informed of any changes, though they might not receive that information until closer to the event. However, reports that Michaels could leave NXT to take on Prichard’s position may prompt those discussions “much sooner.” Meltzer noted that the reports may be “overblown at this point,” but their circulation could prompt WWE to address the situation sooner than originally expected. The plan is for the split of Bruce Prichard’s responsibilities to go between Ed Koskey and Bobby Roode. title: Mick Foley Fears Dementia Could Eventually Claim His Life After Years of Head Trauma
raw_title: Mick Foley Fears Dementia Could Eventually Claim His Life After Years of Head Trauma
summary_src: Mick Foley was in the middle of going after Donald Trump over money when he suddenly made a pretty unsettling admission about his own future. The WWE Hall of Famer says decades of head trauma have left him fearing dementia could eventually play a role in how his life ends.
body: Foley made the comment during an October 30 video on his YouTube channel , where he criticized Trump and claimed the president had enriched himself by $2.2 billion since returning to office. Foley used that figure to set up a comparison with what it took him 42 years of beating up his body in professional wrestling to earn. “So, I’m asking all of you who are reasonable. I’m talking to people who care about human lives, who care more about the well-being of survivors than they do about a man who has enriched himself to the tune of $2.2 billion since becoming president of the United States.” From there, Foley made things personal. He talked about spending decades wrestling through pain and pointed out that even now, years after his full-time career ended, he’s still dealing with damage from some of his most infamous matches. “If that’s not enough, if you’re okay with that guy making in three days what it took me 42 years of sacrifice, of suffering, of walking around in excruciating pain. If that’s not enough, let me put it to you this way. I lost five or six teeth along the way. Two more have to be pulled.” Those two teeth apparently go all the way back to one of the most famous matches of Foley’s career. He specifically blamed the damage on his June 28, 1998 Hell in a Cell match against The Undertaker before running through just how much punishment his body has absorbed over the years. “Yet these two have to be pulled because of the trauma inflicted June 28th, 1998, in a match that’s gone down in lore and history as Hell in a Cell. I lost my ear along the way in Munich, Germany. I’ve had six different surgeries on my knees and a complete hip and knee replacement and 350 stitches.” Then came the part that was a whole lot harder to brush off as another crazy Mick Foley war story. After listing all that damage, Foley said he fears the head injuries he suffered could eventually lead to dementia and affect him for whatever remains of his life. “And a high likelihood that my life is going to come to an end because of dementia, because of the things that I did, head injuries that will affect me for the rest of my life.” Foley wasn’t saying he currently has dementia or revealing a diagnosis. He was talking about what he believes could happen down the road after decades of taking brutal bumps and repeated shots to the head. And after dropping that pretty grim admission, Foley went right back to the political point he was making. This time, he singled out Eric Trump while comparing what he claims the Trump children have made to what Foley earned throughout his entire wrestling career. “I say that because I want you to know the Trump children have enriched themselves by about $250 million, which meant that that guy, let’s see a picture of Eric Trump. Eric Trump has made as much in 30 days as I have in 42 years. If that’s not wrong, I don’t know what else is.” Foley has told plenty of wild stories about losing teeth, losing his ear and getting thrown off Hell

title: On the Record: Latest On Why Stephanie Vaquer Missed WWE Raw
raw_title: Update On Why Stephanie Vaquer Missed WWE Raw
body: Stephanie Vaquer missed this week’s WWE Raw, forcing the company to change its plans for the Women’s World Championship picture. Her scheduled main-event match against Becky Lynch was modified. According to Dave Meltzer on Wrestling Observer Radio , Vaquer couldn’t compete because of an illness. She was scheduled to face Lynch in a number-one contender’s match to determine the next challenger for Women’s World Champion Liv Morgan. He said Vaquer’s illness was not considered particularly serious, but her return timeline remains uncertain. Meltzer stated (via WrestlingInc ), “She’s ill. I was told it’s nothing terribly serious or anything, but she’s ill, and she’s out [indefinitely]. Indefinitely in the sense that it’s not like it’s a week; it’s something more serious. He continued, “I shouldn’t even say that; it’s something that’s indeterminate yet as far as when she’ll be back. But that’s why they didn’t do that match.” Meltzer also ruled out the possibility of Vaquer’s absence being part of a storyline . Her illness is reportedly unrelated to the ankle injury she suffered at Money in the Bank on October 10. He explained, “It wasn’t about an injury, and it wasn’t a worked storyline. They were going to do the match on Monday night; she got sick and could not come. That’s why they did the Becky Lynch-Liv Morgan, and that’s why they did the DQ [finish] because they didn’t want to beat Becky Lynch.” With Stephanie Vaquer unavailable, Raw General Manager Adam Pearce announced that Lynch would challenge Morgan directly for the championship instead of facing another No. 1 contender.
