title: Pat McAfee joins Friday Night SmackDown announce team
raw_title: Pat McAfee joins Friday Night SmackDown announce team - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE today announced that Pat McAfee will debut as the new analyst for Friday Night SmackDown tonight at 8 pm ET live on FOX. McAfee dropped the news on the WWE Universe with a huge social media announcement on Friday morning. “For as long as I can remember WWE has been a company that I have admired, both for its incredible staying power of creating riveting entertainment and for its ability to connect people all over the globe,” said McAfee. “I’ve been fortunate to try a lot of cool professions but working for WWE was the one I looked forward to most. I am incredibly honored and grateful for the chance to give back to the business that has given me and many others so much and having the opportunity to sit at the same table that legends have graced is truly a dream come true. Now let’s go get it.” McAfee will be joined at ringside every week by Michael Cole, VP of WWE’s on air announce talent and voice of Friday Night SmackDown on FOX. Known for his candid, relatable, and refreshing opinions, McAfee’s insight and sense of humor have built him a large, loyal and active fan base. In addition to being a philanthropist, social media influencer, stand-up comedian and former All-Pro punter for the Indianapolis Colts, McAfee is also the host of the #1 international daily streaming sports show The Pat McAfee Show, which is simulcast both on YouTube and on Sirius XM Channel 82 Mad Dog Sports Radio. Additionally, McAfee is the host of the popular podcast The Pat McAfee Show 2.0 and has performed both inside the ring and behind the microphone on WWE’s NXT.

title: Stephanie McMahon Recalls Writing UK-Burying Promos For Vince
raw_title: Stephanie McMahon Recalls Writing Promos For Her Dad, Vince McMahon, To Take Shots At The UK
summary_src: Stephanie McMahon recalls shadowing her father. The WWE has made plenty of trips to the United Kingdom over the years, and more recently, there has been talk of bringing a WrestleMania to the UK. Being Australian, Grayson Waller is no stranger to taking shots at the UK.
body: The WWE has made plenty of trips to the United Kingdom over the years, and more recently, there has been talk of bringing a WrestleMania to the UK. Being Australian, Grayson Waller is no stranger to taking shots at the UK. Speaking with Stephanie McMahon on What’s Your Story , Waller stated that no one wants WrestleMania in the rain. This led to Stephanie recalling working with her dad, Vince McMahon, on promos. “I remember when I first started, I was shadowing my dad. I would get to work on his promos. I remember being in the UK and getting to work on some of his promos that were along those lines (of burying the UK). It was so fun. It’s always so much more fun to do that,” she said. Waller believed the UK fans enjoyed it and were in on it, and Stephanie agreed. John Cena has continued to advocate for WrestleMania in the UK. You can find his comments here. If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Stephanie McMahon appeared on Grayson Waller's What's Your Story podcast and discussed her early days shadowing her father Vince McMahon. She remembered working on his promos while in the UK that took shots at the country, describing the process as fun. Waller, an Australian, had joked about not wanting WrestleMania in the rain, prompting the conversation, and both agreed that UK fans were in on the joke.

title: No WWE Talent Declining Saudi Arabia Trip For Crown Jewel
raw_title: Report: No WWE Stars Have Declined To Travel To Saudi Arabia For Crown Jewel
summary_src: According to a new report, no WWE stars have declined to travel to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia ahead of WWE Crown Jewel 2026 next weekend.
body: WWE Plenty of questions remain surrounding WWE Crown Jewel 2026 as the company and its stars gear up to travel into Riyadh, Saudi Arabia in a little over a week, amidst ongoing tensions, missile strikes, and travel advisories in the Middle East. According to a new report, no WWE talent have asked to stay behind, however. An unnamed top star told Meltzer that WWE told them that declining to travel to Riyadh for Crown Jewel "is something very much not being encouraged." There have been minimal changes surrounding the event, which, just eight days out, appears to be going on as planned. Meltzer previously explained the incentives for the company going through with the show in the kingdom. One change surrounding Crown Jewel, however, is its venue. Though the event will remain in Riyadh, it will now emanate from The Venue , an indoor location in the city 35 minutes from the King Khalid International Airport, which recently underwent a missile strike that killed 12 and injured hundreds . Previously, the premium live event was set to take place in an outdoor temporary venue. More information regarding travel for WWE and its crew and stars has not been reported. Meltzer noted earlier in the week, as originally reported by Ariel Helwani , that athletes fighting on the Zuffa Boxing card featuring Canelo Álvarez on Saturday flew into the Bahrain airport, then drove hours into Riyadh.
summary: According to Dave Meltzer, no WWE performers have asked to sit out the upcoming Crown Jewel premium live event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. An unnamed top star said the company has made it clear that opting out of the trip is strongly discouraged. The show remains scheduled with one adjustment, moving from an outdoor setup to the indoor Venue in Riyadh, located 35 minutes from the recently struck King Khalid International Airport.

summary_src: WWE has a packed SmackDown planned for October 30, and now we know who is expected to kick things off. With Crown Jewel getting closer, the company apparently wants to get things started with one of its biggest stars.
body: According to Viper Reports, Cody Rhodes is currently listed to open tonight’s episode of Friday Night SmackDown. The information comes from the early rundown for the show, which has Rhodes scheduled for the opening segment. Of course, this is only the early rundown, and WWE can always change its plans before the show goes live. There’s also no word yet on exactly what Rhodes will be doing during the segment or who might be involved. The update comes ahead of a loaded episode of SmackDown from the Charleston Coliseum in Charleston, West Virginia. WWE has three championship matches advertised, including Sami Zayn defending the Undisputed WWE Championship against Trick Williams. Zayn has been trying to prove Roman Reigns wrong ahead of their Champion vs. Champion showdown at Crown Jewel, but he’s also putting his championship at risk by accepting challenges before the event. A loss to Williams tonight would throw those plans into question. Chelsea Green is also scheduled to defend the WWE Women’s Championship against Nikki Bella, while Rey Fenix will put the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship on the line against Ricky Saints. On top of that, Danhausen will present his Halloween-themed “Very Nice, Very Evil SmackDown,” adding another element to the final build toward Crown Jewel. As for Rhodes, WWE hasn’t revealed what his opening segment will involve. But with his name currently sitting at the top of the rundown, fans can expect to see him early in the broadcast unless something changes before showtime. body: Bryan Alvarez of F4W wrote that the candidate most likely taking HBK’s seat is none other than fellow Hall of Famer AJ Styles, who retired from in-ring competition in January of this year. Styles is currently helping out at the WWE Performance Center in one of the classes, replacing Terry Taylor who had to undergo surgery. NXT could also get an injection of new blood running it, with Alvarez mentioning CM Punk as someone who could step up and add more to his plate by spending additional time in Orlando. The former WWE champion has often mentioned that he would like to be more involved in the development of future stars. title: LJ Cleary Out 9-12 Months With Injury
raw_title: Top indie star sidelined 9-12 months due to injury
summary_src: LJ Cleary, one of the top stars on the indies, could be sidelined for the next year due to an undisclosed injury. On his social media accounts today, Cleary shared a statement announcing that he will be out of action for 9-12 months due to an injury that requires surgery.
body: LJ Cleary, one of the top stars on the indies, could be sidelined for the next year due to an undisclosed injury. On his social media accounts today, Cleary shared a statement announcing that he will be out of action for 9-12 months due to an injury that requires surgery. The timing is especially hard for Cleary, who feels like the past year is the best he’s ever had in his career. He’s had matches for both ROH and TNA in 2026, including recently appearing as an entrant in the Call Your Shot gauntlet match at Bound for Glory. The 27-year-old Cleary is originally from Ireland and now lives in the United States. He has experience in Japan for Pro Wrestling NOAH, along with working one show for NJPW in 2024. 2025 saw Cleary participate in a WWE tryout. His fiancee, Lyra Valkyria, is part of the WWE Raw women’s division. Per his timeline, summer 2027 is the earliest Cleary could return to the ring. The full 12 months would be October or November 2027. Joseph Currier Joseph Currier is a graduate of the University of Massachusetts, obtaining a journalism degree in 2016. Joseph joined F4W during his time at UMass and has now been writing about the industry for nearly a decade. In addition to his work with F4W, Joseph has previously contributed to Sports Illustrated's wrestling coverage. He lives in Massachusetts and is a diehard fan of the Boston sports teams and Liverpool Football Club.
summary: Top independent wrestler LJ Cleary announced he will undergo surgery and miss 9-12 months of action. The 27-year-old from Ireland had been enjoying the strongest year of his career with recent appearances for ROH and TNA, including the Call Your Shot gauntlet at Bound for Glory, plus prior work for NJPW, Pro Wrestling NOAH and a 2025 WWE tryout. His earliest possible return is summer 2027, per the Wrestling Observer.

title: Paul Heyman Reveals How He Violated WCW Contract For Undertaker
raw_title: Paul Heyman Explains Why He ‘Violated’ His Contract With WCW To Sneak The Undertaker Into A Meeting With Vince McMahon
body: Paul Heyman talks about betraying WCW to get The Undertaker signed by WWE. The Undertaker signed with WWE in October 1990, after finishing his one-year stint with WCW. Over the next few years, he would become one of wrestling’s biggest supernatural gimmicks of all time. Speaking on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Heyman recalled his initial meeting with Undertaker in WCW. “I met Mark in May 1990, when I went back to WCW after being fired by WCW. The person that I was paired with was Mark Calloway. The person who was in charge of the creative of WCW was an old-timer who used to own the Georgia territory when it was run on Ted Turner Superstation, TBS, named Ole Anderson, who was a notorious asshole and had fallen several years behind the times, and called Mark Calloway just some big red-headed stepchild son of a bitch that’s never going to draw any money. I could not have disagreed with him any more.” Heyman said that he snuck Undertaker to a meeting with Vince McMahon when the latter’s contract with WWE came up in September 1990. Heyman said that he “violated” his WCW contract to do this. “Ole didn’t believe in Mark to the point where, when Mark’s contract came up in September 1990 and they tried to lowball him, there was someone in WCW that violated their contract with Turner Broadcasting and WCW and snuck Mark into a meeting through a mutual friend, or a friend that I had in WWE that snuck him into the meeting with Vince McMahon. That meeting led to Mark being signed by WWE and becoming The Undertaker. Because he was snuck through a conduit into a meeting with Vince McMahon while he was wrapping up his WCW contract. It was a WCW person that betrayed the company to do that.” When asked what he thought of this at that time, Heyman said, “I thought it was great because I was that person.” “Because WCW did not see any talent in him and I saw an enormous talent that was about to be wasted. It would have been squandering one of the greatest talents in the history of this business, let alone of that era.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.
summary: Paul Heyman met Mark Calloway in WCW in May 1990 and was paired with him while Ole Anderson dismissed the wrestler as someone who would never draw money. Heyman strongly disagreed with that assessment and later sneaked Calloway to a meeting with Vince McMahon in September 1990 when his WCW contract was expiring. The Undertaker signed with WWE the following month after completing his one-year stint with WCW.

llm_long: Paul Heyman revealed he was the person who violated his WCW contract to help The Undertaker sign with WWE. The Undertaker, whose real name is Mark Calaway, had completed a one-year stint with WCW and signed with WWE in October 1990.

Heyman first met Calaway in May 1990 when he returned to WCW after being fired. He was paired with Calaway while Ole Anderson served as the head of creative for WCW. Heyman strongly disagreed with Anderson's assessment of Calaway's potential.

When Calaway's WCW contract came up for renewal in September 1990, the company attempted to lowball him. Heyman then snuck Calaway into a meeting with Vince McMahon through a mutual friend at WWE. This action violated Heyman's contract with Turner Broadcasting and WCW.
The meeting resulted in Calaway signing with WWE and debuting as The Undertaker. Heyman explained that he took the risk because WCW failed to recognize Calaway's talent.

summary_src: The Bloodline has been involved in some of WWE’s biggest angles for years now, and recently the faction has been in a heated rivalry with The 946. Last month, Jaida Parker debuted with The 946 on Raw during an attack that saw her take out Jacob Fatu via motor vehicle.
body: Link Nia Jax’s Instagram The Bloodline has been involved in some of WWE’s biggest angles for years now, and recently the faction has been in a heated rivalry with The 946 . Last month, Jaida Parker debuted with The 946 on Raw during an attack that saw her take out Jacob Fatu via motor vehicle. While Parker miraculously avoided police charges for attempted vehicular manslaughter, her presence front-and-center in the feud has resulted in wrestling fans to speculate about The Bloodline calling in a female member. Given the large presence of the Anoa’i family in WWE’s ranks, Roman Reigns has a lot of options for backups, and fans have pointed to Naomi , who has been on maternity leave since giving birth to a baby she shares with husband Jimmy Uso. Other people have brought up Roman’s distant cousin Nia Jax . Jax herself has now officially opened up about whether she is a member of The Bloodline, and if she could ever share a ring with the other members of the wrestling dynasty. “Well, technically, I am in The Bloodline,” Nia said during a recent appearance on Keep It Aloha Podcast when asked about her status with the stable. “I don’t know if you saw the chart that Dwayne [Johnson] put up. I’m up there,” the former WWE Women’s Champion said. Jax continued, “But, you know, it all just depends on storyline for wrestling, right? Everybody wants like, ‘Oh, why isn’t she just automatic be in there?’ But I actually appreciate the fact that I can carve out my own name by myself that I don’t have to.” However, she made it clear that if the other members needed her, she would be more than willing to step up. She also noted that Tamina Snuka is also a member of the family, in addition to Naomi. “If the boys ever needed me, you know, they’ve got Naomi, they got me, they got Tamina, they can always call us whenever is needed. But technically, I am in The Bloodline, just not on TV,” Jax said. What do you think, Cagesiders? Would you be down for Nia Jax working as a member of The Bloodline on WWE TV? title: Closing Match for October 30, 2026 WWE SmackDown Revealed — Spoiler
raw_title: Spoiler: Closing Match for October 30, 2026 WWE SmackDown Revealed
summary_src: WWE isn’t messing around with tonight’s SmackDown main event, as the company apparently has a major championship match lined up to close the October 30 show. And with Crown Jewel right around the corner, the outcome could have some serious consequences.
body: According to Viper Reports, Sami Zayn’s Undisputed WWE Championship defense against Trick Williams is currently scheduled to be the closing match for tonight’s episode of Friday Night SmackDown. The match is listed in the show’s early plans, although WWE can always make changes before the broadcast goes live. For now, Zayn and Williams are expected to get the final match of the night. That’s a pretty big spot for Williams, who has been looking to get himself back into the championship picture. He’s now getting a chance to challenge for WWE’s biggest prize while also closing out SmackDown just days before Crown Jewel. Zayn, meanwhile, has been making things a lot harder for himself. Roman Reigns already questioned whether he’d even make it to Crown Jewel with the Undisputed WWE Championship, but Zayn hasn’t exactly been interested in playing it safe. Instead, he’s been accepting challenges from anyone willing to step up. That nearly backfired when Je’Von Evans pushed him to the limit on Raw, but Zayn managed to escape with his championship intact. Now Williams gets his shot, and WWE apparently believes the match deserves the main event spot. If Williams manages to pull off the upset, it would completely change the championship situation heading into Crown Jewel, where Zayn is scheduled to face Reigns in a Champion vs. Champion match. The rest of tonight’s show is also stacked. Chelsea Green will defend the WWE Women’s Championship against Nikki Bella, while Rey Fenix puts the AAA World Cruiserweight Championship on the line against Ricky Saints. Danhausen is also presenting his Halloween-themed “Very Nice, Very Evil SmackDown.” Cody Rhodes is currently scheduled to open tonight’s broadcast, meaning WWE’s early plans have Rhodes starting the show and Zayn vs. Williams closing it. Nothing is final until the show actually airs, but WWE’s current lineup puts the Undisputed WWE Championship front and center for the closing match. With Crown Jewel approaching, Zayn has another opportunity to prove he can survive as champion — assuming Williams doesn’t ruin everything. title: On the Record: Additional What We Know About Shawn Michaels' Rumored WWE Promotion, Other Candidates
raw_title: Additional Details On Shawn Michaels' Rumored WWE Promotion, Other Candidates
summary_src: New details surrounding Shawn Michaels' rumored WWE promotion, as well as other candidates for the job, were reported on Friday.
body: Bruce Prichard is reportedly set to retire, or at least step back from his current role as WWE executive director of creative writing and talent , following WWE WrestleMania 43, and on Thursday, it was also reported that Hall of Famer, and current creative head of "WWE NXT," Shawn Michaels would take his place . While the initial report from PWInsider claimed Michaels is expected to "essentially" step into Prichard's shoes, Dave Meltzer offered new details on Friday. The reports of Michaels departing "NXT" for the main roster creative team are entirely "overblown at this point," according to Meltzer, and those within the WWE Performance Center haven't heard anything official. Prichard's role also includes administrative work that Michaels hasn't done before, but Koskey has done for years. Koskey has also reportedly picked up some of Prichard's work already. Michaels joined "NXT" as a writer and producer back in November 2018, when the brand was still run by his D-Generation X stablemate Paul "Triple H" Levesque. He took over "NXT" creative entirely in September 2021 following Levesque's health issues. Meltzer noted that names such as AJ Styles, Bayley, and CM Punk have been thrown around in regards to the future of WWE's developmental system. As for Roode, who has been working as a backstage producer since August 2023, Michael PS Hayes recently told Stephanie McMahon on an episode of "What's Your Story?" that he is training the former TNA star to be his replacement . Hayes said Roode is "really, really good" and he sees "great things for him."

body: Bliss took to Instagram and uploaded a video of herself alongside Paxley, with both women dressed up as characters from the 2004 comedy. body: It looks like UFC star Michael Chandler will be playing a role on WWE NXT next week. Chandler, in an Instagram video today, sent a message to NXT General Manager Robert Stone and offered to help keep order in the Cruz Montana vs. Dion Lennox unsanctioned match that’s booked for the November 4 episode of NXT. The show is taking place on Wednesday (instead of NXT’s normal Tuesday night slot) to avoid going against coverage of the United States midterm elections. Stone responded to Chandler and appeared to accept his offer: “Your making this too easy for me @MikeChandlerMMA” This summer, Chandler visited the WWE Performance Center and worked out in the ring. He previously appeared on an episode of Raw in 2024 and has been open about his desire to cross over into WWE someday, with both WWE and UFC being under the TKO umbrella. In his MMA career, Chandler competes in the UFC lightweight division and is a former champion for Bellator. NXT will be going up against AEW Dynamite’s Blood & Guts special next Wednesday. Along with Chandler appearing, John Cena and Cody Rhodes will be on the show . Cena will likely have more information about the upcoming John Cena Classic, while Rhodes will present the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic trophy to the tournament winners. title: Paul Heyman Says Roman Reigns Was The Only Choice After Brock Lesnar
raw_title: Paul Heyman: 'There Is No One Else I Could Have Followed Up My Run With Brock Lesnar With Than Roman Reigns'
summary_src: Paul Heyman says there’s no one else he could’ve followed up his run in WWE after Brock Lesnar with other than Roman Reigns. Heyman was first paired with Reigns back in August 2020, when the latter began his run as The Tribal Chief. They worked with each other for 5 years before splitting up.
body: Paul Heyman says there’s no one else he could’ve followed up his run in WWE after Brock Lesnar with other than Roman Reigns. Heyman was first paired with Reigns back in August 2020, when the latter began his run as The Tribal Chief. They worked with each other for 5 years before splitting up. Speaking on In Depth with Graham Bensinger , Heyman was asked why he believed Reigns to be the most transformative talent in his career. “Because there is no one else I could have followed up my run with Brock Lesnar with than Roman Reigns. As an athlete, top tier, 100%. Top tier. Great athlete. As a performer, his knowledge of being inside that ring is second to none. I’ve learned more from Roman Reigns than Roman Reigns has learned from his Wise Man. He knows what to say. I think I added when to say it. But I’ve learned more from him than he has ever learned from me. He is the Tribal Chief. It was the easiest name I’ve ever come up with. He is a Tribal Chief and the WWE Universe is his tribe. He has created an island of relevancy that, when you are with him, you are relevant because you are in the presence of Roman Reigns.” Elsewhere in the interview, Heyman talked about trying to lure Ric Flair into fighting him. Fans can read his full comments here . If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

body: October 30 is a lot slower of a day than those we’ve seen earlier this week. According to wrestlingdata.com , there have been around 274 major/notable title changes on this date historically. Some of the bigger changes include Vader winning the AJPW Unified Triple Crown Heavyweight Title in 1999, Greg Valentine & Ric Flair winning the NWA World Tag Team Titles (Mid-Atlantic Version) in 1977, and Charlotte Flair winning the WWE RAW Women’s Title in 2016. The earliest October 30th entry is from 1967, when Henry Pulasco won the Mexican National Heavyweight Title. Antonio Inoki and Michiaki Yoshimura won the All Asia Tag Team Titles in 1969. Flama Azul won the Mexican National Lightweight Title in 1976. Greg Valentine and Ric Flair won the NWA World Tag Team Titles (Mid-Atlantic Version) in 1977. Ashura Hara and Super Strong Machine won the All Asia Tag Team Titles in 1986. Vader won the AJPW Unified Triple Crown Heavyweight Title in 1999. In 2001, Booker T and Test won the WWF Tag Team Titles and Christian won the WWF European Title. Hiroyoshi Tenzan and Masahiro Chono won the IWGP Tag Team Titles in 2005. The GHC Junior Heavyweight Title was vacated in 2009. In 2012, Atlantis, Delta, and Guerrero Maya Jr. won the Mexican National Trios Titles and the AJPW World Tag Team Titles were vacated. In 2016, Brian Kendrick won the WWE Cruiserweight Title and Charlotte Flair won the WWE RAW Women’s Title. Kotaro Suzuki won the GHC Junior Heavyweight Title in 2018. Six title situations were recorded in 2022: the WWE 24/7 Title changed hands three times, held by Tamina, Dana Brooke, and Nikki Cross; Ninja Mack won the GHC Junior Heavyweight Title; Micro Gemelo Diablo #1 won the CMLL World Micro-Estrellas Title; and TAJIRI and Yoshitatsu won the All Asia Tag Team Titles. title: Rusev Feeling Good, Awaiting WWE TV Return
raw_title: Update On Rusev Injury Recovery
body: Rusev says that he is feeling good after being off TV due to injury and is now just waiting to get back on TV. The WWE star been off television since he got hurt during a match with Je’Von Evans on the July 27th episode of WWE Raw. He recently appeared on TMZ Inside the Ring and confirmed what happened with the injury, noting that he is ready to return when WWE needs him. “[I’m feeling good, good,” Rusev said ( per F4W Online ). “I’ve been out for what — two, three months or whatnot. But yes, I did get kicked in the head, my hands went numb, felt better, finished the match. Then, I got a little sick after that. Not related, I don’t believe it was related.” He continued, “So I was out for that. But then, I’ve been ready. I’ve been good for about two months. I’m just waiting to go back to TV.” Rusev noted that he has been training at his wrestling school in Nashville, Tennessee and has also spent time at the WWE Performance Center. There is currently no word on when he may come back to TV. Rusev and CJ Perry announced in an interview with People on Tuesday that they are expecting their first child.
summary: Rusev has been sidelined since suffering an injury during his July 27 match against Je’Von Evans on Raw. He told TMZ Inside the Ring that he felt good enough to finish the bout after getting kicked in the head but later dealt with an unrelated illness, and has been cleared and ready for about two months while training at his Nashville wrestling school and the WWE Performance Center. No return date has been announced.

title: Jeff Hardy Written Off TNA TV
raw_title: Update On Jeff Hardy After Injury Angle On TNA Impact
body: Jeff Hardy was written off TV following an injury angle on last night’s TNA Impact, with a new report giving an update on his status. The main event of Thursday night’s episode was the syX Slaughterhouse match between syX and The Hardys, which ended with Samuel Shaw and Joseph Sawyer putting a trash can over Jeff and then smashing it from either side with pipes. Fightful Select has the news and, as you may have guessed, it is in part to write Jeff off as the company is heading to Canada for their next tapings. Jeff Hardy has difficulty entering Canada due to his past legal issues with substance abuse and as has been the case many times before, TNA is writing him off so they they can account for his absence at the next few weeks of TNA TV. There is another reason though, as Matt Hardy said on The Extreme Life of Matt Hardy last week that Jeff is likely to take some time off to deal with the lingering neck injury that has been troubling him since last October. A source in TNA told the outlet that it ended up being a “perfect storm” to write Jeff off and not only not have to worry about his entering Canada, but also allow him to heal up in the coming months. Obviously, TNA can film content for him in the US to include on Impact, but Jeff will not be at the Canada shows. Sources expect that he will be back at the December tapings set to take place in Houston, Texas. In the meantime, Jeff (and Matt) will be on the Chris Jericho Rock n’ Wrestling Rager at Sea, with Jeff also set to appear at WrestleCade.
summary: Jeff Hardy was removed from television during the main event of Thursday's TNA Impact in a syX Slaughterhouse match against syX when Samuel Shaw and Joseph Sawyer used pipes to smash a trash can placed over him. Per Fightful Select, the angle was done to explain his absence as TNA heads to Canada for upcoming tapings, where Hardy faces entry issues due to past substance abuse legal matters. The situation also allows him time to address a lingering neck injury that has bothered him since last October, with Matt Hardy having discussed the planned time off on his podcast the previous week.

title: Queen Aminata Wins AEW TBS Title on Dynamite
raw_title: Recapping Queen Aminata’s path to the AEW TBS Championship | Big Vinny V
summary_src: Queen Aminata won her first AEW title on Dynamite, defeating Persephone to win the TBS Championship. It was an unexpected title change, but it hardly came out of nowhere. In fact, it was the culmination of a journey that lasted for several years.
body: Queen Aminata won her first AEW title on Dynamite, defeating Persephone to win the TBS Championship. It was an unexpected title change, but it hardly came out of nowhere. In fact, it was the culmination of a journey that lasted for several years. Let’s start with a quick bullet-point recap of Aminata’s AEW career, from her debut in 2021 to her neck injury last year: April 7, 2021: Aminata debuts on AEW Dark, teaming with Amber Nova in a losing effort against Big Swole & Red Velvet. November 23, 2022: Aminata debuts on television, losing to Hikaru Shida on Rampage. She debuted in Ring of Honor shortly thereafter, but today we’re focusing on her AEW career. January 3, 2024: Aminata debuts on Dynamite losing to Mariah May. February 16, 2024: Aminata defeats Anna Jay on Rampage, her first singles victory in AEW. She officially signs with the company shortly thereafter. October 16, 2024: Aminata’s first championship match, a loss to Mercedes with the TBS Championship on the line. She proceeded to spend the next year-plus bouncing around the midcard. In November of 2025, Aminata announced she had suffered a neck injury that would eventually sideline her for more than five months. She returned to the ring in early April of this year, unsuccessfully challenging Willow Nightingale for the TBS Championship. Following that title shot, Aminata disappeared from AEW for two months. It seemed odd at the time, but in hindsight it looks intentional, like they wanted to move her out of the spotlight so she could have a fresh start after that title loss. Aminata returned to TV on June 24, beating Velvet to qualify for a Survival of the Fittest match to fill the now-vacant TBS Championship. Hikaru Shida would win that match, and then defeat Aminata in a title defense on July 16. That still was not the end for Aminata. She spent most of September and October either teaming with Mina Shirakawa, or competing against her. Either way, she almost always came out on top. Her only defeat in this stretch was a tag team match against the Sisters of Sin, and Aminata promptly avenged that loss by beating Julia Hart in singles action. That hot streak put Aminata back into title contention, but she still couldn’t finish the job, losing an AEW Women’s World Championship match against Mercedes Mone, then a four-way match for the TBS Championship against Persephone. It felt like Aminata was running out of chances when she faced Maya World on Dynamite last week. The winner of that match would go on to challenge Persephone the following week. Obviously, Aminata beat World, then went on to defeat Persephone to finally—finally—win the TBS Championship. The story of Aminata is of an athlete who had a lot of wins, but could never win the quote-unquote “big one.” Her title win came in her sixth challenge for the TBS Championship, and that’s not even counting eliminator or qualifying matches. It’s a story of persistence and determination, as Aminata never gave up in the face of injury and f

Per the Wrestling Observer, she had been working in the midcard until her neck injury last year before this unexpected but earned title change.

HBK Replacement Pros/Cons 📝 Bleacher Report 8h Triple H Shouts Out Christian Watson Bleacher Report 3h Halloween Havoc's 10 Greatest Moments Bleacher Report 6h With WWE Hall of Famer Shawn Michaels potentially moving into a bigger role within WWE, several big names reportedly may be in line to pick up the slack in NXT. According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t Steve Carrier Ringside News), the "most likely scenario" will see WWE Hall of Famer AJ Styles replace Michaels as the head of NXT. Alvarez added that current WWE Superstars CM Punk and Bayley may have input and roles in NXT as well. On Thursday, PWInsider.com's Mike Johnson reported that WWE is planning to promote Michaels from NXT head to executive director of creative writing and talent as the replacement for Bruce Prichard. Per Johnson, Prichard is expected to transition into a different role that will allow him to work from home rather than being on location in Stamford, Connecticut. Meltzer noted that Prichard's job includes "administrative work," which Michaels has never done before, plus he is considered a valuable commodity in NXT. Nothing is certain yet, though, as Meltzer added that things could change multiple times between now and when the final decision has to be made in April. If Michaels does move into Prichard's position and leave NXT behind, the developmental brand still figures to be in great hands since Styles, Punk and Bayley are among the all-time greats and widely regarded for their ability to work with younger talent. There is reportedly some uncertainty regarding whether Gunther and Finn Balor will clash at Crown Jewel next weekend. body: The premium live event was moved from a temporary outdoor arena to The Venue, an indoor location, as of this week, and Meltzer cited photos and posters from the workers' building around the temporary venue. One poster showed Finn Balor next to one of GUNTHER, which Meltzer noted could be a singles match added to the show, as "WWE SmackDown" airs live on Friday, and next week's episode will be taped on Monday. He noted Crown Jewel's original lineup featured Balor vs. "The Ring General." Meltzer also noted that the World Tag Team Championship match , which will be the first defense for The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory since the stable won the gold on July 6, against Je'Von Evans and Mr. Money in the Bank, Penta, was originally meant to be a six-man tag. The match was meant to involve Bronson Reed and Oba Femi, but was changed due to the feeling that it made no sense to do the six-man before the title bout. World Heavyweight Champion Roman Reigns is set to take on Undisputed WWE Champion Sami Zayn for the men's Crown Jewel Championship, and WWE Women's Champion Chelsea Green will face off against Women's World Champion Liv Morgan for the women's title elsewhere on the card. Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton are also set for a Last Man Standing match .

body: Jeff Hardy was temporarily written out of TNA Wrestling programming on Impact this week — but he should be back relatively soon. The October 29 episode of TNA Impact saw The Hardys lose to Joseph Sawyer & Samuel Shaw in a Slaughterhouse Syx match. At the conclusion of the show, Hardy had a trash can wrapped around his head as Sawyer and Shaw struck it with a pair of axes . Fightful reports that Hardy will be absent from TNA in November , with the promotion set to run three events in Canada from November 15-19. Hardy, due to his past legal issues for DUI, has difficulty working shows in Canada. His brother Matt is advertised for the November dates despite Jeff missing the shows. Fightful adds that, while Jeff Hardy is also dealing with two bulging discs in his neck , he is not expected to require surgery. Jeff could be back for TNA’s tapings in Texas this December. He is advertised for those December 18-19 shows in El Paso. Plus, Jeff & Matt will have one of their “Hardy Party” events in the city on December 16 ahead of the tapings. TNA’s final pay-per-view of 2026 will be Destination X in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada on November 15. The promotion then heads to Calgary on November 18-19 for tapings. body: Samoa Joe is one of the rarest beasts in professional wrestling, in that he seems to be universally loved wherever he has worked. Popular backstage and with fans everywhere, Joe bucks the trend of burning bridges with the people that matter behind the scenes and in the stands. The word around the campfire is that his AEW contract expires in 2027, which raises some interesting questions. There is every chance that Joe calls time on his wrestling career next year. He has won world titles wherever he has gone, has a legacy with fans that will last a lifetime, and realistically, he could retire next year and receive the applause of several different generations of fans. One final run in a Vinceless WWE could be interesting for Joe, though. He had a fun run in NXT , but it came at a point in time when the audience most in tune with his work was being wowed by the first years of AEW's existence. Samoa Joe is exactly the kind of nuke that WWE's main roster could do with, especially if everyone was in the know that it was going to be his farewell run. Terry Bezer hasn't written a bio just yet, but if they had... it would appear here.

AEW feels like a more natural fit for the British high-flyer, but WWE cannot let that happen. title: TKO's Shapiro Addresses WWE Crown Jewel Safety Concerns
raw_title: TKO President Mark Shapiro Discussed Safety And Business Of WWE Crown Jewel At Town Hall
summary_src: On Wednesday, TKO held a town hall with TKO President Mark Shapiro addressing employees. A big topic of conversation was WWE Crown Jewel, which is set to take place in Riyadh on Saturday, November 7.
body: On Wednesday, TKO held a town hall with TKO President Mark Shapiro addressing employees. A big topic of conversation was WWE Crown Jewel, which is set to take place in Riyadh on Saturday, November 7. There are safety concerns in Riyadh after the airport was attacked earlier this month, which left 13 dead. The US Embassy has issued multiple warnings to citizens not to travel to Saudi Arabia. Speaking at the Town Hall (via POST Wrestling ), Shapiro noted that shareholders were keeping an eye on the situation as TKO looks to hit its target goal for 2026. “We have a lot of investors and analysts out there across the Wall Street community that are nervous that we’ll be able to pull off the year without any of our events being canceled. We’ve had investors dubious that we could close out this year without any hiccups, meaning events being canceled. You saw F1 and many events canceled given the global nature of our business. Well, so far, we’ve been lucky enough to not have any interruption. [I] [c]an’t guarantee that [we won’t have to cancel any events], but there’s not much we can do about that,” he said. He stated that if the event had to be canceled, “it will certainly have an impact on our year in a very negative way.” Though he noted the financial ramifications of the event, whether it goes forward or is canceled, he did address the safety concerns. “I don’t want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. We want to have the year we all envision we’ve all worked hard for. But if there is danger or further escalation of any of these conflicts that are going on, we will not hesitate to cancel those events, damned be our budget. So it’s certainly a balancing act. But the people part of it does come first in that. I know we’ve got a lot of big events coming up in the Middle East. We’re never putting anybody in harm’s way,” he said. UFC has a Fight Night event set for December 5 in Riyadh. Zuffa Boxing has an event on November 14 in Riyadh. Canelo Alvarez, whom TKO isn’t involved with, is scheduled to fight Saturday night at the same venue as Crown Jewel.
summary: During a TKO town hall on Wednesday, President Mark Shapiro discussed the upcoming WWE Crown Jewel event scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh. He highlighted investor and analyst worries about potential event cancellations amid safety issues in Saudi Arabia, including a recent airport attack and U.S. Embassy travel warnings. Shapiro noted TKO's strong performance so far this year without interruptions, though he could not guarantee future events would proceed uninterrupted.

title: Former WBD Executive Doesn’t Expect Skydance to Pick Up AEW Option Year
raw_title: Former WBD Executive Doesn’t Expect Skydance to Pick Up AEW Option Year
summary_src: Tony Khan’s recent meetings with Paramount Skydance may have left him feeling pretty damn good, but a new report suggests AEW shouldn’t start celebrating just yet. One former Warner Bros. Discovery executive apparently believes AEW could be in for a rude awakening when its option year comes up.
body: According to Blake Avignon , a former WBD executive told him they don’t expect Skydance’s new leadership to pick up AEW’s option year if the company keeps offering nothing beyond traditional wrestling programming. And apparently, the wrestling itself isn’t the issue here. The concern is that AEW hasn’t done enough to expand what it brings to the table beyond its regular shows. “A former @WBD executive told me they don’t expect the new @Skydance leadership to pick up @AEW’s option year if the company continues offering nothing beyond wrestling programming.” That would obviously be a pretty big deal for AEW, especially with Tony Khan recently sounding extremely optimistic about the company’s relationship with Skydance. But according to Avignon’s source, simply continuing with the same kind of content might not be enough to keep the relationship going. “Their concern is that AEW hasn’t diversified its content offering. If Tony Khan expects a renewal by simply delivering more of the same, he might be in for a rude awakening.” That’s a much different picture from what was being painted only days ago. Dave Meltzer reported on October 25 that Khan had flown from Florida to Los Angeles for another round of meetings with Skydance before heading to North Carolina for Collision. Meltzer didn’t know exactly what was discussed, but said Khan came out of those meetings happier than he had been at any point during the relationship. “He came out of the meetings extremely happy, much happier than he has been about this. He’s always been happy about this relationship. He’s always been beaming about it from day one. But he definitely came out of these meetings the happiest he’s been.” Khan himself has also been pretty upbeat about everything. During the October 17 WrestleDream post-show press conference, he confirmed he had already spoken with David Ellison several times about AEW’s future and said Ellison was excited about working with the company. “Yes, I’ve had a conversation with David Ellison about the future of AEW. I’ve had a few great conversations with David Ellison about AEW. He is very excited to be partnering with AEW.” There’s also no word yet on exactly what “diversified” content Skydance would potentially want from AEW, or whether this former executive has direct knowledge of the current leadership’s plans. Nothing has been announced regarding AEW’s option year either, so right now this is one former WBD executive’s expectation rather than a confirmed decision from Skydance. Still, it gives Khan’s recent Los Angeles meetings a whole lot more intrigue. If AEW really is being pushed to offer more than its usual wrestling programming, whatever had Khan leaving those meetings so happy could eventually tell us whether he already has something else cooking. What kind of additional content do you think AEW could offer beyond its regular wrestling shows if Skydance really wants something different? Let us know what you think in the comments. summary: Per Blake Avignon , a former WBD executive told him they don’t expect Skydance’s new leadership to pick up AEW’s option year if the company keeps offering nothing beyond traditional. Nothing has been revealed regarding AEW’s option year either, so right now this is one former WBD executive’s expectation rather than a made official decision from Skydance.

title: Rusev Feels Good, Awaiting WWE TV Return
raw_title: Update On Rusev Injury Recovery | 411MANIA | Wrestling News, WWE & AEW Results
body: Rusev says that he is feeling good after being off TV due to injury and is now just waiting to get back on TV. The WWE star been off television since he got hurt during a match with Je’Von Evans on the July 27th episode of WWE Raw. He recently appeared on TMZ Inside the Ring and confirmed what happened with the injury, noting that he is ready to return when WWE needs him. “[I’m feeling good, good,” Rusev said ( per F4W Online ). “I’ve been out for what — two, three months or whatnot. But yes, I did get kicked in the head, my hands went numb, felt better, finished the match. Then, I got a little sick after that. Not related, I don’t believe it was related.” He continued, “So I was out for that. But then, I’ve been ready. I’ve been good for about two months. I’m just waiting to go back to TV.” Rusev noted that he has been training at his wrestling school in Nashville, Tennessee and has also spent time at the WWE Performance Center. There is currently no word on when he may come back to TV. Rusev and CJ Perry announced in an interview with People on Tuesday that they are expecting their first child.

title: Singapore's first WWE wrestler Dante Chen on his journey and what comes next — 'Making history is a huge honour'
raw_title: 'Making history is a huge honour': Singapore's first WWE wrestler Dante Chen on his journey and what comes next
body: Nearly 14 years after beginning his wrestling career in Singapore, Dante Chen is returning to where it all started. He tells CNA about his five years with WWE, his departure from the company and the next chapter of his career. Chen, whose real name is Sean Tan, made history in 2021 when he became the first Singaporean to wrestle for the American professional wrestling giant, which counts Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson and John Cena among its former stars. Speaking to CNA in an email interview, the 30-year-old said he had already suspected his time with WWE was up. "The night before the phone call happened, I knew it was going to happen the following day," he said. "The way it happened was amusing to me, and I was even surprised I managed to fall asleep that night," said Chen, who now competes under the ring name CHEN. He had been scheduled to compete at a live event the following day, only to be told the night before that he was no longer required. Shortly after his match was cancelled, WWE sent a company-wide message instructing wrestlers who were not booked for the upcoming NXT event to stay away from both the show and WWE's performance centre. That struck Chen as unusual, as wrestlers were ordinarily expected to attend NXT Live! events regardless of whether they were competing. "As I expected, I got the phone call in the evening," he said. Chen announced his departure from the company in April , bringing an end to a five-year stint during which he competed primarily on NXT, WWE's developmental brand, without securing a full-time move to its main roster. Since leaving WWE, Chen has competed in a tournament organised by Japan's Pro Wrestling NOAH, taking on some of the promotion's top wrestlers. In November, he will return to the ring in Singapore at the promotion where his career began almost 14 years ago. Chen began wrestling in 2012 under the ring name Trexxus at Singapore Pro Wrestling (SPW), when the local scene was still developing. Chen described those early years as a process of "constant trial-and-error" to figure out what worked in the ring. "What made it more difficult was that I still wouldn't be able to know what was effective and what wasn't," he told CNA. His big break came in 2019, when he was scouted by WWE officials at a tryout in Shanghai. Two years later, he reported for training at WWE's Performance Center in Orlando, Florida, where he found himself learning from experienced coaches and wrestling veterans. He singled out former wrestler and WWE coach Terry Taylor as having the biggest influence on his development. "My approach towards wrestling now is heavily inspired by what he has taught me," Chen said. title: TKO Prioritizes Safety Over Saudi Events
raw_title: TKO president Mark Shapiro says company will not hesitate to cancel Saudi Arabia events
summary_src: TKO president Mark Shapiro says the company will not hesitate to cancel its upcoming events in Saudi Arabia if there is further escalation of conflicts in the region. Shapiro addressed the situation during a company town hall on Wednesday.
body: TKO president Mark Shapiro says the company will not hesitate to cancel its upcoming events in Saudi Arabia if there is further escalation of conflicts in the region. Shapiro addressed the situation during a company town hall on Wednesday. On Friday, POST Wrestling published audio of the meeting, which features Shapiro discussing the financial implications of potentially canceling the events. “Of course, business is important, but humanity is most important. So this is more about keeping people safe and comfortable. The business is secondary. So, you know, I don’t want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. We want to have the year we all envisioned. We’ve all worked hard for that year. 26 is shaping up to be that year. “But if there is danger or further escalation of any of these conflicts that are going on, we will not hesitate to cancel those events. Damned be our budget, because our people come first. You have that commitment from us.” “We have a lot of investors and analysts out there across the Wall Street community that are nervous that we’ll be able to pull off the year without any of our events being canceled.” “Well, so far we’ve been lucky enough to not have any interruption. Can’t guarantee that. And again, if it happens, it will certainly have an impact on our year in a very negative way. But there’s not much we can do about that.” WWE Crown Jewel remains scheduled for November 7 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The event was recently moved indoors to The Venue (ANB Arena). TKO also has two other events scheduled in Riyadh before the end of the year, with Zuffa Boxing on November 14 and UFC Fight Night on December 5. title: Match Made: Austin Aries vs. Matt Riddle Title Match Set for MLW Saturday Night SuperFight
raw_title: Austin Aries vs. Matt Riddle Title Match Set for MLW Saturday Night SuperFight
body: CHICAGO — Austin Aries will defend the MLW National Openweight Championship against Matt Riddle at Saturday Night SuperFight on Saturday, November 7, 2026, Major League Wrestling announced. The event streams live exclusively on VEEPS at 8 p.m. ET / 5 p.m. PT from Cicero Stadium in Cicero, Illinois, in the Chicago area. MLW says the venue is sold out. The announcement follows weeks of confrontations on Fusion, with Riddle repeatedly demanding a meeting and Aries insisting that the challenger had not earned a title opportunity. During an earlier exchange, Aries threatened to knock Riddle out “any time, any day,” before adding: “Just not today.” The champion later told MLW Insider Rich Bocchini that he controlled the terms of his title defenses and could not be pressured into giving Riddle a shot. The latest encounter began with Aries, the self-proclaimed Phantom of the Opera Cup, dismissing the remaining tournament competitors as fighting for second place. Riddle interrupted and reminded the champion that they could still meet in the tournament. Aries responded by mocking Riddle’s MMA background and making claims about his own training and connections to fight promoters. Riddle then challenged him to defend the National Openweight Championship before the Opera Cup could resolve their dispute. A final insult as Aries tried to leave brought the champion back to accept. What began as a series of verbal exchanges now gives Riddle an opportunity to leave SuperFight with a championship. Riddle brings a combination of strikes and submissions, while Aries’ technical offense and brainbuster remain threats to the challenger. The match will test whether Riddle’s persistence has forced an opening or given Aries the opportunity to settle the rivalry on his own terms. The incident prompted questions about how Flair continues to survive given his advanced age and history.
In response on social media, Flair highlighted statistics from his career along with multiple brushes with death.
He referenced competing in over 5,000 matches, including 2,400 one-hour draws and five 90-minute bouts.

He expressed disbelief that people would worry about his recent fall in light of those past experiences.

title: If WWE is a parody of pro wrestling, NXT is a bad parody of WWE
raw_title: If WWE is a parody of pro wrestling, NXT is a bad parody of WWE | Opinion
summary_src: There’s a line I keep thinking about when it comes to my thoughts on the current NXT product. Bryan Danielson once said that he saw WWE as a parody of professional wrestling.
body: There’s a line I keep thinking about when it comes to my thoughts on the current NXT product. Bryan Danielson once said that he saw WWE as a parody of professional wrestling. Not that he viewed that as a bad thing, per se, but rather he pointed out how much WWE emphasizes the entertainment aspects of its storylines over the actual matches that take place. These days I watch NXT and view it as a parody of WWE. The product often tries to emulate WWE’s storylines but in such a silly, stupid, and nonsensical way that it turns WWE’s tropes into parody, executing them in the most bizarre way possible. The build for this weekend’s Halloween Havoc was terrible, as if it tried to do everything in its power to convince me not to watch. The top match will see Tony D’Angelo taking on Grayson Waller for the NXT Championship. There was a show-long storyline on this past Tuesday’s show that saw Waller outside D’Angelo’s home, a WWE trope that has never worked, even for WWE. When D’Angelo went there, Waller was already gone, making D’Angelo look like a dope. The next two hours had D’Angelo running around trying to look for Waller, only for both of them to wind up back at the PC. This excellent show-long storyline was paid off by having them brawl into some shrubbery to end the show. Whoop-de-doo. I feel that the goal of a weekly television show is to make me, the viewer, invested in storylines so when it’s time for the promotion’s big show, I should be interested in what goes down. These days, NXT produces and airs content that is so weird it actively undermines what they’re trying to accomplish. Another nonsensical story heading into Saturday is whatever is going on between Izzi Dame and Zaria. Dame has decided to pick on Zaria for reasons unknown to anyone despite both of them clearly being heels. She has mocked Zaria for being a theatre girl. Or something. It’s never been fully explained beyond Dame wanting to “expose” Zaria, which is a line constantly uttered on WWE television. There have been plenty of words exchanged, but none of them seem to make sense to anyone outside the brain trust writing this show. And after weeks of weird promos and nonsensical gobbledygook, their feud has led to…a non-title match. Why? That isn’t part of Izzi Dame’s plan, you see. Because not only are they going to wrestle at Halloween Havoc, they are already telling you this brilliant storyline is going to continue. Definitely something I am looking forward to! The writing and storytelling in NXT right now is abysmal and detrimental to a lot of promising young talent. And the examples I’ve given so far are just the tip of the iceberg. Wren Sinclair getting suspended for attacking a referee when most weeks there’s nothing but nonstop violence backstage? Kendal Grey being sent to psychological counseling over an ear injury (?) while being forced to deliver some of the worst dialogue imaginable? body: AEW AEW star Komander hasn't been seen on AEW programming since the beginning of September, and his most recent match was for CMLL a few weeks after that. For fans missing the star, Dave Meltzer offered an update on Friday. Komander last performed at Relevos Increibles on September 20, in a loss alongside ROH World Champion Bandido in a match against Mascara Dorada and Soberano Jr. He also recently faced Titan for the CMLL World Welterweight Championship, a match he also lost, the day before. His most recent bout in AEW was a loss to Nick Wayne on an episode of "AEW Collision." Before that, he competed at AEW All In London in the Casino Gauntlet match , ultimately won by Andrade El Idolo, to determine who earned a contracted shot at the AEW World Championship. Komander made his AEW debut , wrestling without a contract, in the Face of the Revolution ladder match in March 2023. He officially signed with the company the following month , after being released from his contract by Kaoz Lucha Libre. Prior to his signing with Tony Khan's company, WWE also reportedly had interest in the luchador.

raw_title: TKO exec admits running WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh is a ‘balancing act’ between money and safety

body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. WWE is moving ahead with running its Crown Jewel PLE next weekend (Nov. 7) in a war zone in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main reason why the event isn’t being canceled is because the Saudi government typically pays WWE around 55 to 60 million dollars to run a show like this, which WWE does at least twice a year. Most wrestling fans can see this situation for what it is, which is corporate greed and stock price taking precedence over the safety of wrestlers, workers, and company employees. Shapiro expresses concern for TKO’s financial performance for 2026 if any of their Middle East events are canceled. You see, TKO has to keep shareholders happy, and those shareholders won’t be happy if WWE doesn’t bring in that Saudi money. “We of course stand with a lot of obstacles in our way in these last two months, [including] Iran and the impact that has on the entire Middle East. And I’ll remind you that we still have three events left for the remainder of the year. So, several goals we still need to accomplish, and events that we need to be successful for us to close out 2026 in the way that we hope it will close out. And that all gets wiped away to a certain degree if those events get canceled. We are a public company, of course…we have a lot of investors and analysts out there across the Wall Street community that are nervous that we’ll be able to pull off the year without any of our events being canceled…So far, we’ve been lucky enough to not have any interruption. Can’t guarantee that, and again if it happens, it will certainly have an impact on our year in a very negative way. But there’s not much we can do about that.” Shapiro praises TKO’s workers for heroically putting themselves in “potential danger” to make sure these Middle East events run as planned. The decision-makers at TKO are “praying” that everything works out okay. “At the same time, we have courageous employees, full-time and part-time, that are working across our events, going into these territories in the Middle East, and standing behind our events so that we can stage them properly, at the high quality level we’re accustomed to doing so, in the face of potential danger, and/or certainly anxiety, and nervousness. So, a big thank you to all of you that are working across these events, and you’re able to bring them in as planned. It’s really been nothing short of astonishing…it’s really miraculous, and heroic what we’re able to do. So thank you for standing in there. Thank you for making the commitments and delivering on the commitment as you always have. And we’re all hoping and praying everything goes off without a hitch.” He closes out the topic by saying humanity is more important than business, and TKO “will not hesitate” to cancel the events if necessary, even if it screws up the company’s budget. title: TKO calls Crown Jewel Saudi Arabia run a balancing act
raw_title: TKO admits running WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh is a ‘balancing act’ between money and safety
body: Link WWE Cain A. Knight is a hardcore number-cruncher who has analyzed and covered pro wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2014, and followed the sport as a fan going back to the 1980’s. WWE is moving ahead with running its Crown Jewel PLE next weekend (Nov. 7) in a war zone in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The main reason why the event isn’t being canceled is because the Saudi government typically pays WWE around 55 to 60 million dollars to run a show like this, which WWE does at least twice a year. Most wrestling fans can see this situation for what it is, which is corporate greed and stock price taking precedence over the safety of wrestlers, workers, and company employees. Shapiro expresses concern for TKO’s financial performance for 2026 if any of their Middle East events are canceled. You see, TKO has to keep shareholders happy, and those shareholders won’t be happy if WWE doesn’t bring in that Saudi money. “We of course stand with a lot of obstacles in our way in these last two months, [including] Iran and the impact that has on the entire Middle East. And I’ll remind you that we still have three events left for the remainder of the year. So, several goals we still need to accomplish, and events that we need to be successful for us to close out 2026 in the way that we hope it will close out. And that all gets wiped away to a certain degree if those events get canceled. We are a public company, of course…we have a lot of investors and analysts out there across the Wall Street community that are nervous that we’ll be able to pull off the year without any of our events being canceled…So far, we’ve been lucky enough to not have any interruption. Can’t guarantee that, and again if it happens, it will certainly have an impact on our year in a very negative way. But there’s not much we can do about that.” Shapiro praises TKO’s workers for heroically putting themselves in “potential danger” to make sure these Middle East events run as planned. The decision-makers at TKO are “praying” that everything works out okay. “At the same time, we have courageous employees, full-time and part-time, that are working across our events, going into these territories in the Middle East, and standing behind our events so that we can stage them properly, at the high quality level we’re accustomed to doing so, in the face of potential danger, and/or certainly anxiety, and nervousness. So, a big thank you to all of you that are working across these events, and you’re able to bring them in as planned. It’s really been nothing short of astonishing…it’s really miraculous, and heroic what we’re able to do. So thank you for standing in there. Thank you for making the commitments and delivering on the commitment as you always have. And we’re all hoping and praying everything goes off without a hitch.” He closes out the topic by saying humanity is more important than business, and TKO “will not hesitate” to cancel the events if necessary, even if it screws up the company’s budget. title: Cody Rhodes Shuts Down Rumor He Pitched Losing the WWE Championship
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Shuts Down Rumor He Pitched Losing the WWE Championship
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has seen the claim that he once pitched losing the WWE Championship, and he wants everyone to know that’s complete nonsense. In fact, Cody says there’s one pretty easy reason fans should be suspicious anytime they hear about a wrestler volunteering to give up their biggest meal ticket.
body: Speaking on the Double Coverage podcast , Cody addressed the rumor after noticing people were still bringing up an older report from around eight months ago claiming he personally suggested dropping the title. What bothered him was seeing the story repeated like it had eventually become an established fact. According to Cody, that’s not how wrestlers think when they’re sitting at the top of the company. Outside of someone nearing the end of their career and figuring out their final opponent, he doesn’t buy the idea of a champion walking into creative and asking to lose. “Here’s how I knew it had gotten crazy. There was a story that I had pitched to lose the title, and now I saw somebody referencing this, like eight months ago, like, ‘Well, don’t forget when he, remember he pitched it.’” Cody then flat-out denied that mentality and explained why the championship means way too much for a wrestler to casually volunteer to give it away. As far as he’s concerned, if you’re champion, somebody should have to come and take it from you. “If you ever hear a story of a wrestler pitching to lose the title, you should know right out of the gate they’re lying. No wrestler has ever said, you know what, there’s a difference between an old man figuring out who his last opponent is, but no wrestler has ever said, ‘Yeah, I want to, I need to lose the title.’” He didn’t stop there either. Cody called the championship a wrestler’s “meal ticket” and made it pretty clear that willingly pitching away that position makes absolutely no sense to him. “My gosh, that’s the meal ticket. You never—you want somebody to take it from you. Don’t pitch it.” The bigger frustration for Cody seems to be how quickly something online can go from being a report to something people start treating like evidence months later. Seeing that happen with the championship story apparently gave him a pretty good example of how disconnected wrestling conversations online can become from what he experiences in WWE arenas. “And I saw that being talked about as if it was actual evidence. And I thought, ‘Oh man, I wish you knew.’ You know, I wish you guys knew that these conversations are just here. They’re just here.” Cody’s advice for anyone getting caught up in those conversations was pretty simple: actually go to a WWE show. From his perspective, the atmosphere inside the building tells a much different story from what someone might assume after spending all day reading wrestling discourse online. “Come to a show. Come to a show and you will see. Oh, people are having a great time. They love all of it.” So Cody isn’t just denying that he ever pitched losing the WWE Championship. He’s also clearly tired of seeing an old claim get repeated enough times that people eventually start treating it like something he actually did. title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out Negative Wrestling Discourse for Ruining His Viewing Experience
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Calls Out Negative Wrestling Discourse for Ruining His Viewing Experience
summary_src: Cody Rhodes knows exactly what it’s like to fall down the wrestling internet rabbit hole, because he used to be right there with everyone else. Eventually, though, Cody realized all that negativity was starting to mess with how much he actually enjoyed watching wrestling.
body: Speaking on the Double Coverage podcast , Cody explained that when he first discovered wrestling forums, he loved finding other people who were just as obsessed with the business as he was. He started hanging around different forums, but the fun eventually wore off once the constant negativity started affecting his own viewing experience. “No, you know, you get caught in the rabbit hole. Like, we were speaking about AI earlier. You were like, I had a kick. So, I had that same kick when I discovered that there were like-minded wrestling fans online, and I was on all the forums, and then I was like, ‘This is too negative.’” At that point, Cody decided he was better off getting away from those discussions. It wasn’t about avoiding criticism of himself either — he simply didn’t want online wrestling talk changing how he personally watched the product. “This is really affecting my viewing experience, so I’m not going to frequent this anymore.” That doesn’t mean Cody thinks negative opinions from wrestling fans somehow don’t count. He was actually pretty careful about that, explaining that he never wants to dismiss someone simply because their opinion comes from a smaller group online. “You never want to say anything. You never want to say, ‘Well, that’s not real.’ You never want to say, ‘Oh, that’s a small percentage,’ because I don’t want to dismiss a fan and their opinion.” And Cody seems perfectly fine with people thinking whatever the hell they want about him. Whether someone hates his wrestling, thinks he sucks or just wants to insult how he looks, he believes being a fan doesn’t come with some mandatory set of opinions. “If they hate you, they hate you. If they think you’re fat, they think you’re fat. If they think you suck, they think you suck. There’s no wrong way to be a fan.” His bigger issue is X specifically. Cody believes conversations that feel absolutely massive on the platform can actually exist almost entirely inside that bubble rather than representing how the broader wrestling audience feels. “But what I can say is the conversations that take place on, say, X specifically, they only take place there.” And apparently wrestling isn’t the only fandom where Cody has noticed it. After paying more attention to online conversations surrounding movies, he’s found plenty of the same darkness and arguments over what people are apparently allowed to enjoy. Cody’s solution is pretty simple: maybe everybody needs more puppy videos. “It’s just dark out there, huh? And I don’t know if cinema—I’ve been, you know, now that I’m watching, you know, with a movie, what some of its chats and discussions look like. Just, it’s a little dark, you know? Like, don’t be afraid to put up a little puppy video every now and then.” Cody even knows exactly what kind of content he’d rather see. title: Chris Jericho’s first book is being developed as a TV series
raw_title: Chris Jericho’s first book is being developed as a TV series
body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) Chris Jericho’s life story could become a television series. Jericho appeared on the Skratch N’ Sniff YouTube show and said that his first book, A Lion’s Tale, is being developed as a television series. “We’ve kinda moved it up the food chain, and it’s close to filming a pilot,” Jericho said. “And we do have an actor that is very similar to me when he was first starting out that was from the Letterkenny series if you ever watched that show. “So, yeah, I mean, there might be something very, very soon, not just an autobiography because that’s not enough, because I’m Chris Jericho, right? I always have to push the envelope. We might have a whole actual TV series about kind of the early days of my career, which would be a lot of fun. So that’s something we’re working on, and we’re moving to the pilot stage very, very soon.” Check out the full interview via the Skratch N’ Sniff YouTube Channel . Powell’s POV: Jericho declined to name the Letterkenny actor, but did say there is “a real facial similarity.” It has to be the guy who plays Roald, right? Kidding. Actually, I’m guessing that it’s Dylan Playfair, who plays Reilly. Jericho and Playfair both had parts in the Dead at 27 film that just wrapped. I thought A Lion’s Tale was a great read, and I got a big kick out of the But I’m Chris Jericho web series , so I’ll definitely check out the TV series if it comes to fruition.

title: WrestleMania 37 goes Hollywood in 2021
raw_title: WrestleMania 37 goes Hollywood in 2021 - WWE
body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WrestleMania is going Hollywood. Los Angeles Mayor Eric Garcetti, Inglewood Mayor James T. Butts Jr. and WWE are proud to announce that SoFi Stadium and Hollywood Park in Los Angeles will host WWE’s pop-culture extravaganza, WrestleMania, on Sunday, March 28, 2021. “There is nothing quite like WrestleMania Week,” Garcetti said. “It is a one-of-a-kind event that provides an economic boost to the region — and fans from around the world will find a city that is ready to host them and welcomes the spectacle.” “The city of Inglewood is thrilled to say that WrestleMania will add to the growing number of national and internationally followed events that will be hosted in our city over the next eight years,” Butts said. “WrestleMania brings excitement and is followed by almost every age demographic. With the scheduling of this marquee event, we can say without contradiction, the only thing that has changed in Inglewood is…everything.” “WrestleMania is one of the world’s most-watched events, and we are proud to welcome WWE to the Inglewood community,” said Jason Gannon, Managing Director, SoFi Stadium and Hollywood Park. “WWE’s commitment to community is consistent with our mission to provide a lasting positive impact in the community. We look forward to making a difference with WWE.” This will mark the first WrestleMania in Los Angeles since WrestleMania 21. “On behalf of everyone at WWE, we are excited to bring WrestleMania back to Los Angeles,” WWE Chairman & CEO Vince McMahon said. “WrestleMania will set the bar for future sports and entertainment events held at SoFi Stadium as we add this facility to the list of iconic venues that have hosted our pop-culture extravaganza.” WrestleMania is more than just a one-day event; it’s a week-long celebration. In addition to WrestleMania 37, other events include Friday Night SmackDown, NXT TakeOver and Monday Night Raw at Staples Center, WrestleMania Axxess — WWE’s interactive fan festival at the Los Angeles Convention Center — as well as the 2021 WWE Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony. WWE will also host more than a dozen community outreach events, including hospital visits and Be a STAR bullying prevention rallies, designed to give back to the local region. Over the past 13 years, WrestleMania has generated more than $1.3 billion in cumulative economic impact for the cities that have hosted the event. This year, WrestleMania 36 takes place Sunday, April 5, from Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Fla., and streams live around the world on WWE Network.

title: TNA Adds Another Major Title Match to Destination X Card
raw_title: TNA Adds Another Major Title Match to Destination X Card
body: 0 TNA is adding another championship contest to its upcoming Destination X event, with the Knockouts division set for a major showdown on November 15. The announcement came during the October 29 episode of iMPACT , when a new challenger made her intentions impossible to ignore. Indi Hartwell’s championship reign now faces another difficult test, and this time, her challenger comes with plenty of experience and a formidable tag team partner. The segment began when Shayna Baszler and Zoey Serrano entered the ring following a video package highlighting Hartwell’s journey. Serrano attacked a security guard, while Baszler took possession of commentator Tom Hannifan’s headset to address the champion. Baszler revealed that TNA authority figure Daria Rae hired her to challenge Hartwell for the Knockouts World Championship at Destination X. She also issued a direct warning to the reigning champion. “I’m letting everybody know Daria hired me to face Indi Hartwell at Destination X, one-on-one for the TNA Knockouts Championship,” Baszler announced. She continued by addressing Hartwell’s championship journey, making it clear that she intended to turn the champion’s feel-good story into a nightmare. The match was subsequently made official, giving Baszler an opportunity to add singles gold to her current championship collection. Hartwell captured the Knockouts World Championship by defeating Xia Brookside at Bound For Glory. Baszler also enjoyed success at the same event, teaming with Serrano to defeat Allie and Kiera Hogan for the Knockouts World Tag Team Championships. The upcoming contest will mark their first singles meeting under the TNA banner, adding another interesting chapter to the Knockouts title picture. TNA Destination X takes place on November 15 at the Edmonton EXPO Centre in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and will stream live on TNA+. The updated card also features Leon Slater defending the TNA World Championship against Trey Miguel, alongside men’s and women’s Ultimate X matches and the World X-Cup tournament. With Baszler now targeting Hartwell’s gold, the champion has another serious obstacle standing between her and a successful title defence.
