title: Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles Primed For Major WWE Promotions
raw_title: Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles Primed For Major WWE Promotions
body: Michaels became the head of NXT in 2021 when Paul “Triple H” Levesque underwent a cardiac procedure. He was later promoted to Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative. Now, it appears the Heartbreak Kid is moving up the corporate ladder once again. Mike Johnson of PWInsider reported on Monday that WWE’s Executive Director – Creative Writing & Talent, Bruce Prichard, is expected to retire after WrestleMania 43 next year. Prichard is expected to remain connected with WWE as a consultant and work from home in Texas, according to the outlet. A new report indicates that Shawn Michaels will be promoted to the position in 2027 . On paper, Michaels new role seems like a match made in Heaven. Few people know more about pro wrestling and what makes it thrive than Michaels. Plus, his decades-long friendship with Triple H should bode well for the duo as they lead WWE into a new era. The prophecy has been fulfilled https://t.co/n0tYWQzrmz pic.twitter.com/izi4GQ4xza — Brandon Carney (@BenchwarmerBran) October 29, 2026 PWInsider added that Michaels will prepare for his new role in the months ahead. With Shawn Michaels stepping into a major role with WWE, he will soon have to relinquish his NXT duties. Just as WWE orchestrated Prichard’s succession plan, the company apparently has a legendary candidate in mind to replace Shawn Michaels at NXT. False Finish reported that WWE brass expect AJ Styles to be more “hands-on” within NXT following Michaels’ promotion. Earlier this year, Triple H shared that AJ Styles wants to be more involved with WWE’s development team. More specifically, the Phenomenal One wanted to help mold the next generation of WWE stars at NXT. Shortly after Styles’ in-ring retirement, Triple H appeared on Cody Rhodes’ podcast to discuss Styles’ post-retirement role in WWE. “Towards the end, AJ was like, ‘I don’t want to just be done with the business. I want to be done wrestling,” Triple H began. “Being an agent or producer is a different world than being in what we do. There are different fits for different people. AJ came in, he sat in on some creative meetings , he sat in on some production meetings, and I think he realized the writing thing’s not for him , the producer thing isn’t for him. What he really likes is getting to these young kids, spotting talent , and trying to help fan the flames of that little spark and turn it into something more—the developmental side.” AJ Styles is certainly a worthy mentor for rising wrestling stars. Styles is one of just nine wrestlers to hold the WWE and TNA World Championships . He is one of just 22 Grand Slam champions in WWE history. body: When Cora Jade stepped away from WWE in May 2025 due to mental health issues, it felt like a great shame. She seemed to revel in playing a villain on NXT, the feuds she had with Roxanna Perez were some of the best of her generation, and her character seemed to connect with fans in a way that suggested she had a real future on the company's main roster. Since taking some time away, she's rediscovered herself and continued to thrive in TNA. She's been active in the TV Title scene and even challenged for the Knockouts title, where she came up short to Xia Brookside in a bloody steel cage match at Lockdown. Whether she'd return to NXT or head straight to the main roster, Cora Jade feels like she has unfinished business in WWE. She also has the talent to have a real future there. She didn't ever win a singles title in NXT , and if she were to come face-to-face with Roxanne Perez (or even join The Judgment Day as her wingman again), a second stint for Cora Jade could reap major rewards for all involved. Terry Bezer hasn't written a bio just yet, but if they had... it would appear here.

title: Chelsea Green Retains WWE Women's Title vs Nikki Bella
raw_title: Chelsea Green Defeats Nikki Bella, Retains WWE Women's Title On SmackDown
summary_src: Chelsea Green is still WWE Women's Champion after a victory over Nikki Bella on "WWE SmackDown," and she once again faced-off with Liv Morgan.
body: WWE Chelsea Green is still WWE Women's Champion after a successful title defense against Nikki Bella on " WWE SmackDown ," but she faced off once again with Crown Jewel opponent Women's World Champion Liv Morgan after the match. Bella and Green dodged one another's finishers early on and Green tried for a quick roll-up. Bella dumped her off the rope and hit a Bella Buster, but Green kicked out. Green got Bella on the ropes, where she hit a pair of knees to the back of her neck, followed by a Rough Rider. The WWE Hall of Famer dodged Green's Unprettier and locked in the Fearless Lock, but Green fought out of the hold. Bella hit a Rack Attack 2.0, but Green got her feet on the bottom rope, and was able to win off another roll-up. Morgan came out after the match to talk trash and told Green their journeys in WWE were more alike than she originally thought, but the one distinction between them is that Morgan is a "real champion." She continued to run down Green and promised to "eat her alive" at Crown Jewel. Tiffany Stratton's music hit, and she came out with the Money in the Bank briefcase, only to be taken out from behind by Raquel Rodriguez and Roxanne Perez. Green downed Morgan with an Unprettier inside the ring, and Stratton teased a cash-in once again. She motioned for a referee to come out, then hit a Prettiest Moonsault Ever, but as she passed the briefcase to the official, Rodriguez took her out. Judgment Day beat down the babyfaces, until IYO SKY came out to run them off.

Green overcame several near-falls including a Bella Buster and Rack Attack 2.0 before securing the win with a roll-up. title: Cody Rhodes Shares The Rock's Advice On Storytelling
raw_title: WWE's Cody Rhodes Details Lesson He Learned From The Rock About Wrestling & Hollywood
summary_src: WWE star Cody Rhodes was given advice by Dwayne Johnson that he's since applied to his own career, as he continues to expand into Hollywood.
body: WWE In 2003, Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson leaned into criticism of his attempts at a Hollywood career, creating his "Hollywood Rock" persona. However, despite finding success on the silver screen, the criticism never fully subsided. According to Cody Rhodes during an interview on "Insight with Chris Van Vliet," it irks Johnson when wrestlers look down on acting. "One time, Rock told me he doesn't like when wrestlers would say, 'Oh, I don't want to be an actor, I always want to be a wrestler.' And he had good reasons; he said, 'Of course you love wrestling.' ... But also, wrestling is storytelling. And that's what he said: 'What I wish people would say is that they just want to grow as a storyteller." Rhodes later applied Johnson's logic during a general meeting with studio executives in Los Angeles, literally repeating Johnson's advice. "The lesson for me was: I want to grow as a storyteller. That's what it is, and I think coming from wrestling it's perfect, because that's what we do." Not too long ago, Rhodes commented on his complicated relationship with Johnson following their heated rivalry leading up to WWE WrestleMania 42. title: Rey Fenix Retains AAA Cruiserweight Title Against Ricky Saints
raw_title: Rey Fenix Defeats Ricky Saints, Retains AAA Cruiserweight Title On WWE SmackDown
summary_src: Rey Fenix looks to have finally settled the score with Ricky Saints as he once again retained his AAA Cruiserweight Title on "WWE SmackDown."
body: After Ricky Saints got himself disqualified in his quest to dethrone Rey Fenix as the AAA Cruiserweight Champion two weeks ago on "WWE SmackDown," he was hoping that the third time would be the charm as the two men met for a third time on the October 30 episode of "SmackDown." However, the champion still had Saints' number as Fenix was able to retain his title. Fenix got off to a hot start as he used his speed to take Saints off his game, hitting a Tope Con Hilo to the outside, but as the match entered the commercial break, Saints took advantage by sending Fenix to the outside and sending the champion over the announce table. When the action returned from the break, Saints attempted to rip Fenix's mask off which forced the champion to retreat to the corner. Saints would take the action to the top and hit a Superplex that earned a near fall, but Fenix would rally back with a near fall of his own after landing a Roundhouse Kick. Saints got his foot on the bottom rope to break up a pin after being planted face first by Fenix, who quickly followed up with a Moonsault but still couldn't put the challenger away. Fenix went for a Rolling Cutter but was stopped mid-move, with Saints following up with a Tornado DDT. Saints then hit a Death Valley Driver that only earned a two-count, but when he again took the action to the corner, Fenix countered with a Powerbomb. The champion quickly hit two Rolling Cutters which still couldn't put Saints away, which led to Fenix going for a Mexican Muscle Buster but Saints fought out of it first time around, but couldn't escape a second time as Fenix hit the move to gain the win and retain his title.
summary: Rey Fenix defeated Ricky Saints in their third meeting on the October 30 episode of WWE SmackDown. Fenix retained the AAA Cruiserweight Championship after a back-and-forth bout that featured high-flying offense from both competitors including a Tope Con Hilo, a Superplex and a Moonsault. Saints had been disqualified in their previous encounter two weeks earlier on the same show.

Fenix started the contest strongly by using his speed advantage and connected with a Tope Con Hilo to the outside. Saints gained control before the commercial break by sending Fenix to the floor and driving him over the announce table.

After the break Saints tried to remove Fenix's mask which caused the champion to retreat to the corner. Saints delivered a Superplex from the top rope that resulted in a near fall before Fenix answered with a Roundhouse Kick for a near fall of his own.

title: Mark Shapiro Says TKO Will Cancel Saudi Arabia Events if Necessary as Crown Jewel Nears
raw_title: Mark Shapiro Says TKO Will Cancel Saudi Arabia Events if Necessary as Crown Jewel Nears
body: 0 TKO President Mark Shapiro has assured employees that the company will not hesitate to cancel its upcoming events in Saudi Arabia if the conflict in Saudi Arabia gets worse and puts its people at risk. With WWE Crown Jewel just days away, there are growing questions about whether the event and other shows in the region will go ahead as planned. WWE is scheduled to host Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Saturday, November 7. However, rising security concerns have grown following reports of an attack on an airport earlier this month that reportedly killed 13 people. The US Embassy has also issued several security warnings. They advised American citizens against traveling to Saudi Arabia because of the growing tensions. On Wednesday, TKO held a town hall meeting with employees. Shapiro discussed the company’s upcoming events in the Middle East as one talking point. The conversation covered the safety concerns surrounding Crown Jewel and the possible financial impact of canceling major shows. On Friday, POST Wrestling released audio from the meeting, giving more details about Shapiro’s comments. The TKO president said investors and financial analysts were closely watching to see whether the company could finish the year without canceling any events. “We have a lot of investors and analysts out there across the Wall Street community that are nervous that we’ll be able to pull off the year without any of our events being canceled,” Shapiro said. Shapiro added that TKO had managed to avoid major disruptions so far. However, he admitted that canceling an event would hurt the company’s financial results for the year. As TKO is a publicly traded company, any such decision could have a major financial impact. However, despite the financial pressure, Shapiro stressed that TKO would never put people in danger just to protect its business. “I don’t want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. We want to have the year we all envision we’ve all worked hard for. But if there is danger or further escalation of any of these conflicts that are going on, we will not hesitate to cancel those events, damned be our budget,” he stated. Shapiro also said that the company would never knowingly put its employees or talent in harm’s way. He described the situation as a difficult balance between business interests and personal safety. title: Huge UFC Star Eyes WWE NXT Role, Robert Stone Takes Notice

body: 0 WWE NXT could have another major crossover appearance on its upcoming show, as UFC star Michael Chandler wants to get involved. The former Bellator champion has reached out to NXT General Manager Robert Stone and offered to help with a match next week. This isn’t the first time Chandler has shown interest in joining WWE. He has often spoken about his love for pro wrestling and his desire to make the move from MMA to WWE at some point. Chandler even visited the WWE Performance Center this summer, where he got the chance to train inside the ring. The UFC star also showed up on an episode of WWE RAW in 2024. Chandler recently shared an Instagram video addressing Stone ahead of the November 4 episode of NXT. The show will feature an unsanctioned match between Cruz Montana and Dion Lennox, and Chandler suggested that he could help keep things under control. The UFC star told Stone he could call on him if he needed someone to maintain order during the match. He captioned the video, “No one more unsanctioned than me. @mrstonewwe your call.” His offer caught Stone’s attention, and the NXT GM seemed interested in discussing the idea. Stone responded to Chandler’s message on X , writing, “You’re making this too easy for me. Let’s jump on a call and talk… @MikeChandlerMMA.” Neither side has confirmed that Chandler will appear on NXT. However, Stone’s response has fuelled speculation. It remains to be seen whether Chandler would serve as a special guest referee or take on another role during the show. WWE and UFC also operate under the same parent company, TKO Group Holdings. So, a potential appearance from Chandler wouldn’t come with any roadblocks. Since the merger, both companies have explored ways to work together, with athletes and personalities occasionally appearing on each other’s shows. Chandler currently competes in the UFC lightweight and welterweight divisions. His potential appearance would bring massive attention to NXT. The November 4 edition of NXT will air on Wednesday instead of its usual Tuesday night slot. WWE moved the show to avoid going up against coverage of the United States midterm elections. However, the change means NXT will now compete directly with AEW Dynamite ‘s Blood & Guts special. The post Huge UFC Star Eyes WWE NXT Role, Robert Stone Takes Notice appeared first on Wrestlezone .

title: Former WWE Star CJ Perry Says Her Book Is Being Made Into a Movie
raw_title: Former WWE Star CJ Perry Says Her Book Is Being Made Into a Movie
body: CJ Perry isn't stopping at becoming an author ... she's taking her new book to the big screen, revealing to TMZ a movie adaptation of "Bulletproof Angel" is already in the works. The former WWE Superstar joined TMZ's "Inside the Ring" Podcast alongside her husband, WWE Superstar Rusev ... and dropped the major news while discussing her new spy thriller, which hits shelves November 10. "It is going to be made into a movie," Perry told us. "We're already in the works." Perry says the team has already started working on packaging the project ... describing the story as a "James Bond spy thriller" centered around female leads. The book follows a Russian undercover spy who poses as a model while dating a Russian mafia boss ... before things go sideways and her mother is forced to step in and help save her. Getty Despite her acting experience, Perry says she plans to cast a bigger-name actress in the lead while serving as a producer -- though she may sneak in a cameo. Rusev could also appear, with Perry revealing her husband has an offer to play one of the movie’s villains. Perry says they’ve already landed a director she’s excited about, but isn’t revealing much more just yet. Before "Bulletproof Angel" hits Hollywood, it'll hit bookstores November 10 ... with Perry holding a release-day signing at Barnes & Noble at The Grove in Los Angeles. The full interview with Perry and Rusev is available now on TMZ's "Inside the Ring."

That’s when an army of miniature Danhausens came rushing toward the ring. The mini-Hausens attempted to fight back, with one delivering a headscissors and a springboard headbutt, but Gunther quickly took control. Gunther even threw a pumpkin at the miniature attackers before chopping another one down. He then placed one mini-Hausen on a table and powerbombed another directly onto him, breaking the table in the process. Things only got worse for Danhausen when Gunther positioned another table against the turnbuckles and locked him in a sleeper hold. However, the lights suddenly went out, and everything changed. Finn Balor’s Demon persona emerged, making his way toward the ring as Gunther stood frozen in disbelief. Gunther initially tried to talk his way out of the confrontation, insisting they didn’t need to take things any further. The Demon wasn’t interested in negotiating. Gunther missed a clothesline, allowing Balor to unload with flying forearms and kicks. Gunther managed to fight back with a chop and even struck Balor with his championship belt, but The Demon barely reacted. Balor responded with a Sling Blade before delivering a running dropkick that sent Gunther crashing through the table positioned in the corner. And he still wasn’t finished. With Gunther retreating to the outside, Balor grabbed a ladder and used it to knock The Ring General onto the announce table. He then climbed to the top of the ladder and delivered a massive Coup de Grace onto Gunther. The segment ended with The Demon standing tall after taking out Gunther, turning Danhausen’s bizarre experiment into one of the night’s biggest surprises. Finn Balor bringing back The Demon adds a completely different dimension to his issues with Gunther, especially after the brutal punishment The Ring General dished out during the segment. body: 0 CM Punk and Bayley are heading back to WWE NXT. Both main roster stars have been announced for the developmental brand’s upcoming Holiday Live Tour in November. However, their appearances have also brought renewed attention to reports suggesting that their involvement with NXT could eventually extend beyond the ring. WWE confirmed that Punk will appear in Detroit on November 14 and Chicago on November 15. Bayley is scheduled for Cleveland on November 13 and will also join Punk in Detroit the following evening. Both stars have previously contributed to NXT beyond their regular main roster appearances. Punk competed at an NXT live event in Virginia in August, teaming with Myles Borne and Tavion Heights to defeat The Vanity Project. He has also visited the Performance Center in Orlando for rehabilitation and to offer guidance to developing talent. Even Grayson Waller, who previously questioned Punk’s visits to NXT, has acknowledged that the former WWE Champion has been helpful to performers at the Performance Center. According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer , WWE could be considering a greater backstage presence for both Punk and Bayley as part of potential structural changes in 2027. Alvarez suggested Bayley could become involved depending on her career plans, while Punk might also receive additional creative input. Shawn Michaels is reportedly the leading candidate to replace Bruce Prichard as Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent after WrestleMania 43. AJ Styles could potentially take on a larger NXT role. The report also suggested that WWE’s ID program could receive a fresh direction early next year. However, no official appointments or changes involving Punk and Bayley have been announced. Meanwhile, Punk has plenty to handle on the main roster. A grudge match against Kevin Owens beckons in the November 7 episode of SmackDown. Their upcoming NXT appearances will give fans another chance to see two established WWE stars alongside developmental talent. body: WWE Danhausen unveiled "The Demon" Finn Balor as his experiment and unleashed him upon Gunther during " WWE SmackDown ." It's the first time Balor has donned the war-paint since WrestleMania 42. Danhausen was out in the ring as this week's Halloween host of the show, finally looking to unveil the 'experiment' he has been teasing in recent months. Gunther came out to beat down Danhausen once again, putting him through a table before a group of Minihausens ran down to the ring to try and make the save. They wound up beaten down all the same, having pumpkins hurled at them before one was powerbombed through the other and the table they were set upon. Gunther set up another table, cinching a rear choke on Danhausen before presumably looking to put him through it. Danhausen struggled to no avail but then Cursed Gunther, preceding the lights to go out and a heartbeat to play out over the venue. That heartbeat gradually got faster before "Demon" Balor arose from a gurney, revealing his alter-ego to have been Danhausen's experiment. Balor slowly approached and confronted a fearful Gunther, ending up whipped with a belt but no-selling it completely. Balor went on to dropkick Gunther through the table that he had set up, then setting him up on the announcer's desk on the outside. He then climbed a ladder and delivered Coup de Grace to put Gunther through the desk, before returning to the ring to pose with Danhausen and close the segment.

body: Halloween eve saw the “Demon” version of Finn Balor make its return ahead of a potential WWE Crown Jewel showdown against Gunther. A confrontation between Gunther and Danhausen went down on tonight’s Halloween-themed edition of SmackDown, and it was Gunther who had the advantage until Balor made the save. All show long, Danhausen teased that he had an experiment he was going to unveil. Just as Gunther was about to choke him out. Danhausen revealed the experiment to be the return of The Demon . Balor then took Gunther out, ending with a Coup de Grace off a ladder through the announce table. Gunther had promised that he was going to ruin Danhausen’s Halloween, and he was well on his way to doing so until Balor emerged. Gunther attacked Danhausen and took out a group of Minihausens. But as Gunther then locked Danhausen in a sleeper, Danhausen cursed Gunther and brought Balor down to the ring. A feud between Gunther and Balor has been ongoing, with our Dave Meltzer reporting that a Gunther vs. Balor match was planned for Crown Jewel at least at one point. We’ll see if that ends up being made official for the November 7 PLE in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia following their interaction tonight. Gunther and Balor have been featured on advertising material for Crown Jewel, further indicating that a match between the two could be added to the PLE. Balor competed as The Demon at WrestleMania 42 earlier this year, where he defeated Dominik Mysterio in a street fight. title: Sami Zayn Retains Undisputed WWE Championship Against Trick Williams After Controversial Finish on SmackDown
raw_title: Sami Zayn Retains Undisputed WWE Championship Against Trick Williams After Controversial Finish on SmackDown
summary_src: Sami Zayn is still the Undisputed WWE Champion, but the way he retained his title against Trick Williams on the October 30, 2026 episode of SmackDown is definitely going to get people talking.
body: The championship match took place under No Disqualification rules, meaning both competitors had the freedom to use weapons without worrying about getting disqualified. Lil Yachty wasted little time getting involved, handing Trick Williams a kendo stick that he immediately used to attack Zayn and score an early near fall. The fight eventually spilled into the crowd, where Zayn unloaded with punches before both men made their way back toward the ring. Williams grabbed the kendo stick again, but Zayn managed to turn things around and deliver several shots of his own. Williams eventually avoided another swing and connected with a jumping neckbreaker. He followed up with more kendo stick shots and a cyclone kick, but Zayn managed to kick out. Things got even more physical when Williams brought steel chairs into the ring and attempted to deliver a uranage onto them. Zayn countered the move with a Blue Thunder Bomb, nearly putting Williams away. The championship belt then became the center of attention. Zayn initially grabbed the title and attempted to strike Williams, but missed. Williams responded with a jumping knee that earned another close two-count. With the championship within reach, Williams grabbed the belt himself and waited for Zayn to get back to his feet. However, the closing moments took a bizarre turn when Williams pushed the referee into the action. Zayn shoved the official away and delivered a low blow to Williams while the referee wasn’t looking. Despite the match already being contested under No Disqualification rules, Zayn still made sure the official didn’t see what happened. Zayn then blasted Williams with the championship belt and covered him for the three-count, successfully retaining the Undisputed WWE Championship. The victory means Zayn leaves SmackDown with his championship intact, but his actions once again raise questions about the lengths he’s willing to go to remain on top. With Roman Reigns already questioning whether Zayn could make it to Crown Jewel as champion, the titleholder has managed to survive another major challenge, even if his methods weren’t exactly honorable. The October 30 episode of SmackDown went off the air immediately after Zayn’s victory, leaving fans with another controversial championship finish heading into Crown Jewel. title: Sami Zayn Retains Undisputed Title vs Trick Williams
raw_title: Sami Zayn Still Undisputed WWE Champion After Defeating Trick Williams On SmackDown
summary_src: Sami Zayn is still Undisputed WWE Champion after defeating United States Champion Trick Williams in the main event of "WWE SmackDown."
body: WWE Sami Zayn is still Undisputed WWE Champion after a victory over United States Champion Trick Williams on " WWE SmackDown ." Lil Yachty, Johnny Gargano, and Candice LeRae all interfered in the match, which got them ejected, and the bout restarted as a no disqualifications match. The competitors were out of the ring quickly during the first half of the match, but Williams took control even after Zayn sent him into the ring steps. Back in the ring, he looked for a Book End, but Zayn countered and hit an exploder suplex into the corner. Zayn looked for the Helluva Kick, but Williams countered. Gargano distracted the referee and LeRae threw Zayn the title, and Yachty took down Gargano at ringside. Zayn missed the belt shot and Williams hit the Book End, but Gargano drug the referee out of the ring. Williams was announced as the winner by DQ, but Zayn remained champion. "SmackDown" General Manager Nick Aldis came out and told everyone they were banned from ringside and demanded the match be restarted with no disqualifications. Williams got the kendo stick and hit Zayn. The men brawled out of the ring, where Williams smacked the champion with a garbage can. Zayn took control of the kendo stick back in the ring, but Williams hit a neck breaker and took the weapon back, breaking it off Zayn's body. He threw chairs into the ring and looked for a Book End to Zayn on top of them, but Zayn countered and hit a Blue Thunder Bomb. After Williams kicked out, Zayn went to hit him with the title, but Williams dodged and hit the Trick Shot. Zayn dodged a belt shot by using the referee as a shield, then hit a low blow, followed by a shot to Williams with the title for the win.
summary: Sami Zayn defeated Trick Williams on WWE SmackDown to remain Undisputed WWE Champion. Lil Yachty, Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae interfered and were ejected from ringside, after which the bout was restarted under no disqualification rules. General Manager Nick Aldis banned all outside parties and ordered the match restarted as a no DQ contest, with the two men brawling after Williams struck Zayn with a kendo stick.

body: Although Nick Aldis had to restart the match after some shenanigans, Sami Zayn did end up retaining the WWE Championship over Trick Williams on Friday following a low blow and a belt shot. With that win, WWE confirmed that Zayn would be facing Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel next weekend. The two were wrestling for the title on Friday when Williams went for a cover. Johnny Gargano at ringside dragged the referee out of the ring, causing a disqualification. Nick Aldis immediately arrived and said Gargano, Candice LeRae, and Lil Yachty would all be barred from ringside, and the match would restart under no disqualification rules. Williams had the advantage until Zayn dragged the referee in between then, giving him the distraction for the low blow. He then struck Williams with the title to win the match. On last week’s show, the match was set up after Williams interrupted a Zayn promo. The two exchanged words until they faced off in a six-man tag match. Williams, Penta, and Rey Fenix ended up defeating Zayn, Gargano, and Ricky Saints. BREAKING: Result of Sami Zayn vs. Trick Williams Undisputed WWE Title Match on SmackDown Discuss Now This week's episode of SmackDown featured a massive Undisputed WWE Championship match. Sami Zayn defended the gold against Trick Williams after some heated interactions between the duo in recent weeks. The winner of the contest was promised a Men's Crown Jewel Championship bout against Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel 2026. Sami Zayn and Trick Williams went to war in the main event of WWE SmackDown. Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae were at ringside to support Zayn. Meanwhile, Williams had rapper Lil Yachty in his corner. At one point in the match, The Anointed One prevented Zayn from using the championship belt to gain an unfair advantage. Williams hit the Last Real Good Guy with the Book End and attempted to pin him. However, Johnny Wrestling pulled referee Charles Robinson out of the ring. As a result, Robinson called for the bell and awarded the win to Williams via disqualification. SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis wasn't pleased with the outcome. He came out and ordered the referee to restart the bout with the No Disqualification stipulation. Amid the chaos, Trick Williams capitalized on the opening and hit Zayn in the head with a kendo stick. Despite suffering significant damage, the Undisputed WWE Champion managed to kick out. In response, Sami Zayn punished Williams with several stiff kendo stick shots. The Anointed One made a miraculous recovery and broke the weapon while assaulting Zayn. Williams then introduced steel chairs to the match. He attempted to deliver a Book End to the champion on the chairs, but Zayn countered it with a Blue Thunder Bomb. Zayn ultimately hit a massive low blow to Williams and took him out with the title belt. He successfully defended his championship via pinfall to book his date with Reigns in Riyadh next month.

In conclusion to what appeared to be a farcical segment with Danhausen, he was left frozen in fear as things went too far. The former World Champion interrupted Danhausen tonight on SmackDown , when he was set to reveal his experiment. However, what no one saw coming was what the experiment actually was. That was it, with the Ring General laid out as Balor posed with Danhausen. It seems to indicate that the Demon is back for good, and when Gunther faces him, it's going to be the Demon that he has to wrestle in the ring. Paul Heyman has opened up about the complex and polarizing legacy of former WWE Chairman Vince McMahon. Rather than measuring himself by conventional moral standards, McMahon focused entirely on his immense professional achievements and industry-shaping ambitions. Heyman portrayed Vince as a deeply intricate figure whose self-assessment was completely detached from traditional virtue, emphasizing instead his massive historical footprint on the professional wrestling landscape.

title: Sami Zayn’s Controversial Win Sets Up Roman Reigns Showdown at Crown Jewel
raw_title: Sami Zayn’s Controversial Win Sets Up Roman Reigns Showdown at Crown Jewel
body: 0 Sami Zayn is heading to WWE Crown Jewel as the Undisputed WWE Champion after he survived Trick Williams on the October 30 episode of SmackDown , using some controversial tactics. The victory also officially set up a huge champion vs. champion match between Zayn and Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel. This week’s SmackDown saw Zayn defend his Undisputed WWE Championship against Williams. The challenger had Lil Yachty in his corner, while Johnny Gargano and Candice LeRae accompanied Sami Zayn. Trick Williams started strong, hitting the champion with a series of strikes and sending him crashing to the mat. However, Zayn slowly took control. Williams eventually fought back with clotheslines. He came close to winning with a Bookend and later hit his finishing move, but Zayn kicked out. The match ended in chaos when Gargano distracted the referee, allowing LeRae to slide the championship belt into the ring. Williams tried to take advantage, but Gargano pulled the referee out of the ring before he could complete the three-count. Referee Charles Robinson then called for the bell and awarded Williams the victory by disqualification. However, since a championship cannot change hands through a disqualification, Zayn remained champion. Just then, SmackDown General Manager Nick Aldis stepped in to settle the situation. He banned everyone from ringside and ordered the match to restart under No Disqualification rules. The restarted match saw both wrestlers become even more aggressive. Both stars used the kendo stick to hit each other. Williams hit his signature moves, but Zayn kept finding ways to stay in the fight. Williams eventually brought steel chairs into the match. Zayn hit a Blue Thunder Bomb onto the chairs, but Williams somehow kicked out just before the three-count. The challenger looked close to becoming the new champion after hitting a Trick Shot. However, Zayn once again managed to get his shoulder up before Robinson could count to three. With the title within reach, the US Champion tried to use the championship belt as a weapon. Zayn responded by pulling Robinson in front of him and using him as a human shield. Robinson then got rid of Zayn’s hold, and as he was distracted, the champion hit Williams with a low blow and hit him with the WWE Championship belt to get the three-count. The self-proclaimed “last real good guy” will now officially face Roman Reigns at Crown Jewel on November 7. title: MLW stars to face NJPW's Yota Tsuji at Saturday Night Superfight: Who will step up to collide with the IWGP Heavyweight Champion?

body: Major League Wrestling recently made a huge announcement when they revealed that NJPW star and current IWGP Heavyweight Champion Yota Tsuji will compete at the upcoming Saturday Night Superfight event on November 7. It was then revealed that Tsuji will hold an open challenge against someone from the MLW roster. With this major match announced, it should be interesting to see who will step up to face “The Gene Blast.” Here are four MLW stars to potentially face NJPW’s Yota Tsuji at Saturday Night Superfight. Since leaving WWE in 2023, Matt Riddle has made his home back in Major League Wrestling over the past two years. In that time, Riddle became the MLW World Heavyweight Champion and cemented himself as a top star. “The King of Bros” has been showcased as a featured act and could shine against Yota Tsuji at Superfight. Giving Tsuji a different kind of opponent, Riddle will use his MMA background and years of experience inside the squared circle to take down the current IWGP Heavyweight Champion. One of the up-and-coming names on the MLW roster today is Brick Savage. Standing at six foot, two inches and weighing over 330 pounds, Savage has solidified himself as a rising star. Yota Tsuji has excelled against other heavyweights and would feel right at home against someone like Savage. Getting what could be the biggest bout of his career, Savage will be able to display his skills and garner the spotlight against someone the stature of Tsuji at MLW Saturday Night Superfight. After being released from WWE in 2024, many fans did not know what would be next for Cameron Grimes . Returning to his original and real life name Trevor Lee, the former WWE star has since signed with Major League Wrestling. Recently, Lee became the inaugural MLW Southern Crown Champion and might want another significant role. With Yota Tsuji coming into MLW for Saturday Night Superfight, Lee feels like the perfect opponent to give him a show-stealing bout on the November 7 card. There is no denying that one of MLW’s biggest stars on the roster right now is Donovan Dijak . Since leaving WWE, Dijak has traveled all over the world, but made his home in Major League Wrestling. Just based on his experience and size, Dijak could match up extremely well against Yota Tsuji in every way. title: SmackDown Recap: Chelsea Green Retains Women's Title
raw_title: SmackDown recap & reactions (Oct. 30, 2026): Chelsea Green’s meek ambitions
summary_src: Sigh. this championship run is doing Chelsea Green no favors. She retained against Nikki Bella because of course she did.
body: Link Marcus Benjamin has loved wrestling since his early days on the planet. He once Superkicked a tooth out of a friend’s mouth. Sweet Chin Music indeed. He’s analyzed and covered wrestling for Cageside Seats since 2021. Sigh. this championship run is doing Chelsea Green no favors. She retained against Nikki Bella because of course she did. I have no issue with the result. I even liked Chelsea’s surprise look that she got the win thanks to a roll-up. I do, however, think this match made Nikki look kinda dumb. She’s a vet in this game. She’s in the Hall of Fame and a former champion. So why on earth does she lack the ring awareness to know how close she was to the ropes during her pin attempt after hitting the Rack Attack? If she wants to get a little arrogant with the pin, cool. She’s a heel and that’s what heels do. But that arrogance shouldn’t make her look like a rookie. And now let’s get back to the champ. Liv Morgan got a microphone in hand and disrespected Chelsea like the Canadian stole her man. And Chelsea looked shook. The same woman who stood toe-to-toe with GUNTHER of all people looked like a shrinking violet in front of Liv. She had no response to Liv’s insults nor did she stand up for herself. The wildest part? She didn’t look happy the whole segment until Tiffany Stratton showed up. So the Women’s Champion can’t defend herself and can’t wait for backup? I don’t like that. This is the same Chelsea who rushed the ring on the most recent Raw . She aggressively attacked Liv and Judgment Day but looked outclassed here. How does she just let Liv say Chelsea will get fired for a third time and no one will care?That doesn’t make Chelsea sympathetic; it makes her look like a chump. It also makes her look like she needed her big sister to step in and fight for her. Speaking of Tiffany… Once again, she saw the opportunity to cash-in. Once again, she had Liv dead to rights. And once again, she hesitated like someone who has no idea how this works. All that led to Judgment Day continuing a beatdown and IYO SKY making the save. The champ needing backup is fine when she’s outnumbered like this but she feels like the one person without agency. At least consistently. As my boy Sean pointed out, the territory doesn’t seem interested in using this championship reign to further Chelsea’s character. At times she looks out of her depth and that’s a bad look for the champ. SmackDown was fine. It was a mixed show that did some things well and some not so well. summary_src: On the night of Danhausen's Halloween special, here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/30/26 episode of "WWE SmackDown!"
body: WWE Welcome to Wrestling Inc.'s weekly review of "WWE SmackDown," in this case, Danhausen's "Very Nice, Very Evil" Halloween special! We have some things to say about Danhausen, the Halloween theme, and the return of "The Demon" Finn Balor here in the column this week. We also have thoughts on Sami Zayn's Undisputed WWE title defense , Chelsea Green's WWE women's title defense , Rey Fenix's AAA Cruiserweight title defense , and more! If you missed the show, as always, you can turn to our "WWE SmackDown" 10/30/26 live blog , which contains all the objective information you could possibly want about what went down Friday night. If you're interested in the WINC staff's opinions on what went down — at least the matches and segments that grabbed our attention the most, for better or worse — you're in the right place. Here are three things we hated and three things we loved about the 10/30/26 episode of "WWE SmackDown!" WWE We are edging closer to WWE Crown Jewel 2026, a show where the two champions from each of WWE's brands will go one-on-one in special interpromotional matches, but when it comes to the women's division, it really has been a slog of a build up. The opening match of the October 30 episode of "WWE SmackDown" saw Chelsea Green defend the WWE Women's Championship against Nikki Bella in a match that was not very good. We could all kind of see this coming as the feud between Green and Bella has been dull to say the least — we get it ladies, you want to bring some of that "Divas" flare back to WWE, but for the love of everything that is good and pure, don't bring the Divas Era wrestling back, it stunk. That is what this match did, it stunk. It was slow, it was boring, it was sloppy in all the wrong ways. Sometimes wrestling can actually look better when it's rough around the edges, but when it's between two women who have little to no chemistry together it just becomes rough to watch. It almost looked AI-generated at times and the world rejoiced when it was over. However, this portion of the show wasn't over as Liv Morgan came out to run down her Crown Jewel opponent, and it all just kept going downhill. Morgan, who isn't exactly the most popular champion in WWE right now, repeatedly beat the drum of Green being a fluke champion, which is an angle that is just so played out right now that if you had a hearing aid while Morgan was talking, I wouldn't be surprised if you just turned it off. Then Tiffany Stratton showed up, and I'm not even kidding when I say this, teased cashing in her Money in the Bank contract for a third consecutive show and still didn't do it. We talked about this on Monday after "WWE Raw" — it's okay to tease it every once in a while, but doing it on back-to-back shows just feels weird. title: Kris Statlander Replaces Marina Shafir, Teams With Jon Moxley
raw_title: AEW wrestler replaces Marina Shafir, teams with Jon Moxley at Warrior Wrestling event
summary_src: Jon Moxley got a different tag team partner at Warrior Wrestling on Friday. Originally, Moxley was set to team with Marina Shafir against Lance Archer and Tootie Lynn.
body: Jon Moxley got a different tag team partner at Warrior Wrestling on Friday. Originally, Moxley was set to team with Marina Shafir against Lance Archer and Tootie Lynn. But after it was announced that Shafir was unable to make it to the show, Moxley revealed that he had a backup plan: Kris Statlander, who entered the ring as the two teams squared off. At one point in the match, the duo did the Death Riders lariats into the corner, a staple of the group. Recent days have seen a new group focus their attention on the Death Riders: The Cut , a fusion between members of the Dogs and the Bang Bang Gang. Jay White has made it clear that he not only wants Moxley, but also his AEW Continental Championship. After a brawl on Wednesday’s Dynamite, Moxley threw out the challenge for an Anarchy in the Arena match at Full Gear on November 14. Shafir, meanwhile, has set her sights on the AEW Women’s Championship, challenging Mercedes Mone after a series of confrontations. title: Jey Uso Net Worth

body: Jey Uso is an American professional wrestler who has a net worth of $4 million. Jey Uso, whose real name is Joshua Samuel Fatu, is best known for his long career in WWE, first as one-half of the successful tag team The Usos and later as a singles star known as "Main Event" Jey Uso. Together with his twin brother Jimmy, he became one of the most decorated tag-team wrestlers in WWE history, including a record-setting 622-day reign as SmackDown Tag Team Champions. His involvement in The Bloodline storyline alongside cousin Roman Reigns helped transform him from a popular tag-team performer into one of the company's leading attractions. In 2025, he won the men's Royal Rumble match and defeated Gunther at WrestleMania 41 to capture the World Heavyweight Championship. His entrance through the crowd and the audience chant "YEET" became defining parts of his solo persona, creating merchandising opportunities alongside his increasingly prominent television and arena appearances. Joshua Samuel Fatu was born on August 22, 1985, in San Francisco, California. He is the younger twin brother of Jonathan Fatu, better known as Jimmy Uso, and the son of professional wrestler Rikishi , whose real name is Solofa Fatu. The brothers grew up surrounded by professional wrestling because their extended Anoa'i family included numerous performers who worked for WWE and other promotions. The family also includes their younger brother Solo Sikoa and relatives such as Roman Reigns . Jey and Jimmy attended Escambia High School in Pensacola, Florida, where they played football, and Jey subsequently attended the University of West Alabama. Although both brothers initially pursued athletics outside the wrestling ring, their family history provided a natural connection to the business. Jey began wrestling professionally in 2007, working alongside his twin brother on the independent circuit and eventually entering WWE's developmental system. They competed in Florida Championship Wrestling, where they refined their teamwork, in-ring style, and characters. Their success in developmental wrestling prepared them for a move to the company's televised roster. The Usos made their WWE main-roster debut in 2010, initially appearing as a young Samoan tag team with strong family connections. They gradually evolved beyond their introductory characters, developing a high-energy style based on double-team maneuvers, athletic offense, and coordinated performances. Their matches against established teams helped them gain credibility with WWE's audiences. The brothers' first major breakthrough came when they captured the WWE Tag Team Championship in 2014. Their popularity grew as they developed a series of prominent rivalries and eventually adopted a tougher image built around black clothing and their "Uso Penitentiary" catchphrase. title: AJ Styles’ Rumored WWE NXT Takeover May Have Already Begun With PC Duties — Report
raw_title: AJ Styles’ Rumored WWE NXT Takeover May Have Already Begun With PC Duties — Report
body: 0 AJ Styles could be preparing for a significant backstage position in WWE NXT, and his involvement with the developmental brand may already be greater than fans realize. A new report has revealed details about the former WWE Champion’s activities at the Performance Center as speculation continues about changes to the company’s creative structure after WrestleMania 43. According to Andrew Baydala, Styles has quietly been overseeing operations at the WWE Performance Center for several months. The development adds another layer to reports suggesting he could eventually replace Shawn Michaels in a major NXT position. Baydala addressed the speculation on X , writing, “Styles has been quietly running things in the WWE PC for months.” He added that a move into Michaels’ current position following WrestleMania 43 “wouldn’t shock” him. Styles’ growing backstage involvement isn’t entirely new. He previously revealed that he had been filling in for a coach, producing matches, and working with younger performers at the Performance Center. The former WWE star retired from in-ring competition in January 2026 and was subsequently inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame. He has since taken on production and talent scouting responsibilities, making a larger developmental role a potential next chapter in his career. The speculation also connects the dots to reports that Michaels could replace Bruce Prichard as Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent after WrestleMania 43. According to Bryan Alvarez of the Wrestling Observer , Michaels is currently the most likely candidate for that position, which could leave his existing NXT responsibilities open. False Finish has also reported that people at the Performance Center expect Styles to become more involved in NXT following Michaels’ potential promotion. However, WWE hasn’t officially announced any appointments or confirmed that Styles will succeed Michaels. For now, his reported Performance Center responsibilities provide an interesting indication of where things could be heading. Styles may have traded the ring for the backstage area, but his next challenge could be helping shape NXT’s future rather than competing in it. title: WWE succession plan emerges as Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles eye new roles
raw_title: WWE succession plan emerges as Shawn Michaels and AJ Styles eye new roles
body: Bruce Prichard, WWE’s Executive Director of Creative Writing and Talent, is expected to retire after WrestleMania 43, although he could remain involved with the company as a consultant. Michaels is reportedly being lined up to replace Prichard in 2027, while Styles could take on a more hands-on role with WWE’s developmental brand, NXT. According to reports from PWInsider , Michaels is expected to move into Prichard’s position, with preparations for the transition already expected to begin in the coming months. The former WWE champion has led NXT since 2021, when Paul ‘Triple H’ Levesque underwent a cardiac procedure. Michaels was subsequently promoted to Senior Vice President of Talent Development and Creative. His experience with developing young wrestlers makes him a natural candidate for a more prominent position within WWE’s creative structure. Michaels also shares a longstanding friendship with Triple H, which could prove valuable as the pair continue shaping the company’s future. However, his potential promotion would leave a significant opening at NXT, with AJ Styles reportedly emerging as a candidate to take on greater responsibilities. According to False Finish, WWE officials expect Styles to become more involved with the developmental brand following Michaels’ departure from the role. Styles has previously expressed a desire to help prepare the next generation of WWE superstars, particularly after stepping away from in-ring competition. Triple H discussed the former champion’s plans during an appearance on Cody Rhodes’ podcast, explaining that Styles had explored several backstage positions before identifying the area that suited him best. “He really likes is getting to these young kids, spotting talent, and trying to help fan the flames of that little spark and turn it into something more, the developmental side,” Triple H said. Styles’ interest in mentoring young wrestlers could make him a strong fit for NXT, where emerging talent is prepared for the main roster. The Phenomenal One brings plenty of experience to the role, having won both WWE and TNA World Championships and becoming one of just 22 Grand Slam champions in WWE history. Styles was also inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame during WrestleMania 42 week. body: Hello Folx! We are at the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida, for the seventh annual NXT Halloween Havoc, and the 19th overall! The NXT version of Halloween Havoc has provided some fun matches and moments over the last seven years. And with the return of Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal it adds even more fun and chaos into the mix. Even with just the top two titles being defended, we have a pretty stacked card for tonight. So, let’s get into it! Shiloh Hill looks to get some revenge on Naraku! Zaria is out to make Izzi Dame pay for all she has done! Tavion Heights and Myles Borne look to settle their grudge in a Weapons Wild match! In a Spin the Wheel, Make the Deal match, Zilla Fatu will take on Charlie Dempsey! Wren Sinclair is looking to get her title back as she takes on NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan! And in our main event, Tony D’Angelo is also looking to get his title back as he takes on NXT Champion Grayson Waller! Shiloh Hill’s goofy menace works well for him. He is a big guy who has a bit of an edge, but overall he is a sweet goofball. I feel like his character work is going to translate well on the main roster. Is he ever going to be a World Champion? Maybe not, but not everyone needs to be. I’m not sure what they are doing with Naraku; he came in hot and feuded with D’Angelo for the NXT Championship, and now he is working to help build up a new star. I feel like the EVIL Naraku could be used differently. Set him up as a big bad, give him wins and maybe the North American Championship, and then when someone beats him, it means something. But this is the reality we are in, and with all the videos Hill made figuring out the secret of the mist, I don’t see him losing here. A win over a recent NXT Championship contender will help Hill get further up the card, and hopefully Naraku can regain some momentum soon. This feud bothers me a bit, not because it hasn’t been good. But because Zaria was fresh off a huge feud with former friend Sol Ruca. A feud that set Zaria up as a monster heel. But now she is the default face in this feud. She has been embarrassed and humiliated by Dame, and we are supposed to be sympathetic towards this person who just betrayed her best friend. It just doesn’t feel great to me. Hopefully Zaria can put Dame away soon and move on to being a monster heel. But I don’t think this will be a one-and-done. Dame refused the title shot, so she wins here and gets another shot when Zaria wants revenge. These two have had issues for a while now, and hopefully this ends the feud so they can both move on to better things. I know a lot of people say Borne is boring, and while I get it, I enjoy his work. Heights has a lot of potential, and since Borne has already had a run with the North American Championship, I could see Heights getting the win here, getting his revenge, and moving into a number one contender spot. title: 7 Wrestling Grudges That NEVER Really Ended – Page 3
raw_title: 7 Wrestling Grudges That NEVER Really Ended – Page 3
body: This rivalry could have an entire list of its own. Two men at total odds with one another on every conceivable level, New Yorker Vince Russo and wrestling royalty Jim Cornette go together like bread and concrete. Forced to work together as part of Vince McMahon's creative team in the Attitude Era , these are two men with completely different principles who were completely incompatible from the start. Vince Russo had worked his way up from running WWE Magazine to being part of the decision making for Monday Night Raw and, eventually, SmackDown. He was a big proponent of the car crash TV of the time, citing the brawling chaos on the Jerry Springer show and the toilet humor of South Park as his key influences. Cornette is a wrestling booker who believes in the sanctity of the wrestling business. The two's relationship started in the gutter and has descended below sea level. Russo pretends to be unbothered by Cornette, while Jim revels in despising his "big city" counterpart. Cornette insists he will be alive to " piss on Vince Russo's grave " and will say as much in every interview he can. Their isn't a word strong enough to describe the dislike these two opposites have for one another. Terry Bezer hasn't written a bio just yet, but if they had... it would appear here.

body: By Jason Powell , ProWrestling.net Editor ( @prowrestlingnet ) The Wednesday, October 28, AEW Dynamite television show averaged 620,000 viewers for TBS, according to Brandon Thurston of Wrestlenomics.com . The viewership was down from the prior week’s average of 661,000 viewers. Dynamite finished with a 0.14 rating in the 18-49 demo, down from the previous week’s 0.15 rating. Powell’s POV: The HBO Max streaming numbers are not included in the rating or viewership count for AEW programming. Dynamite ran against the fifth, final, and most-watched World Series game, which averaged a combined 14.22 million viewers on Fox and Fox Deportes. Given the stiff competition, I expected the Dynamite numbers to be worse. One year earlier, the October 29, 2025, Dynamite on TBS delivered 495,000 viewers and a 0.08 rating in the 18-49 demographic.

llm_long: World Series Wrestling streamed its MegaMania Adelaide event live on YouTube from the Adelaide Entertainment Centre in Hindmarsh, Australia on October 31, 2026. The small arena featured top-notch lighting and production quality with ample ringside space that placed the front row at a noticeable distance from the ring.

Lights were turned on during the fourth match when action spilled into the crowd, revealing an attendance of 2,000 or more in a packed venue. Killer Kross and Scarlett Bordeaux entered first, with Kross expressing hope that the main event would be a one-on-one contest.

Tetsuya Naito then appeared but was accompanied by Bushi and Ryusei, prompting Kross to deliver clotheslines to the accompanying wrestlers as they attempted to enter the ring. Naito spat toward Kross without entering the ring and subsequently returned to the back.

The opening match pitted Ricky Sosa, in his WSW debut, against Matt Riddle, and the competitors shook hands prior to the bell. Riddle attempted an RKO within the first few seconds, but Sosa blocked the move and responded with a shoulder tackle.

Riddle landed a spin kick that took Sosa down, after which Sosa delivered a dropkick at the 1:30 mark and followed with a Northern Lights Suplex that earned a nearfall. Riddle executed a running Penalty Kick on the apron, and Sosa answered with a running European Uppercut inside the ring.
Riddle scored with a gutwrench suplex at 3:30 and attempted a senton that Sosa blocked by raising his knees. Sosa followed up with a flying splash in the corner and an enzuigiri.

Finn Balor Breaks Silence After Bringing Back The Demon on WWE SmackDown Discuss Now Finn Balor made an unexpected move on the Halloween-themed edition of WWE SmackDown last night. He brought back his Demon King gimmick to destroy Gunther . Danhausen was the special host of this week's episode of SmackDown. He was featured in various segments on the program. At one point, he appeared on the entrance ramp to disclose his most "evil" science experiment. Before the former AEW star could make the reveal, Gunther attacked him from behind. Finn Balor is among the most experienced superstars on the WWE roster. He has wrestled against several top names of the company, including Roman Reigns, Seth Rollins, and CM Punk. However, WWE added a blockbuster stipulation to their upcoming match this week on SmackDown . The two superstars will now face off in a No Holds Barred match in Brooklyn, New York, next week. This addition of this stipulation has raised a lot of eyebrows, with many fans wondering the reason behind the move. Kevin Owens and CM Punk still seem to have a lot of unfinished business. However, the two stars getting a stipulation match this early raises many questions. Here are three reasons why WWE added a stipulation to Owens vs. Punk on SmackDown: The tension between CM Punk and Kevin Owens has escalated far beyond the standard competition or a basic fight over a championship. Both superstars despise each other to their core. They took many bitter shots at each other over the past two months, digging out one another's vulnerable past. Well, a standard singles match with strict rules, countouts and disqualifications would feel inadequate to contain the two rivals who genuinely hate one another. By adding a No Holds Barred stipulation, WWE seemingly wants to highlight the deep animosity between Punk and Owens. Triple H intends to show that this hatred cannot be governed by traditional ring-officiated boundaries. title: Legal Watch: Why Cody Rhodes Never Pursued an MMA Career Despite Considering It
raw_title: Why Cody Rhodes Never Pursued an MMA Career Despite Considering It
summary_src: Cody Rhodes apparently gave some real thought to stepping into MMA at one point, but that idea didn’t exactly make it very far at home. The moment he brought it up to Brandi Rhodes, he got one of the rare hard no’s of their relationship.
body: Speaking on the Double Coverage podcast , Cody was asked whether he had ever seriously considered MMA. Long before UFC became the monster it is today, Cody had already gotten a small taste of another combat sport through Brazilian jiu-jitsu. Cody trained in BJJ while he was still involved in amateur wrestling, although he wasn’t about to pretend he was some secret submission wizard. By his own assessment, he was simply “okay” at it, and the training mainly helped keep him active during wrestling’s offseason. “At the time, you know, UFC was moving, but nothing like it is now in terms of the juggernaut it’s become. But it hadn’t fully, at the time I was in high school, hadn’t fully taken. So, I would go do Brazilian jiu-jitsu, and this is before there was Brazilian jiu-jitsu everywhere. And I was okay. I was okay.” His amateur wrestling background obviously gave Cody something to work with, but he also pointed out the differences between folkstyle wrestling and other disciplines. Ultimately, he feels he stopped at pretty much the right time. “But also, folkstyle wrestling, you don’t slam a guy. You don’t get to the manipulation. Freestyle, you get points for how high they might go. But I was just okay. And it helped me in the offseason. And I ended it right where I needed to end it.” And if WWE ever needed somebody with a wrestling background to lead the charge into legitimate combat sports, Cody doesn’t think he’d be the first choice anyway. He immediately pointed across the WWE locker room at Chad Gable and his much stronger amateur credentials. “Whenever people bring that up, I’m always of the thought, yep, that was—I was good. But Chad Gable, he was an Olympic alternate. If we’re looking for someone who’s going to lead the fight, it’d be Chad over there. You know what I mean?” Still, Cody did wonder what might happen if he actually committed himself to MMA training. Apparently, he even floated the idea to Brandi once to see what she thought about him giving it a shot. That conversation ended pretty damn quickly. “But I thought about it. I mentioned it one time to Brandi. I was like, ‘I wonder if I trained and could do it.’ And that was a rare time where she was, like, hard no.” That reaction actually caught Cody off guard because Brandi apparently doesn’t usually shut down his more unusual ambitions. Cody joked that maybe his wife simply knew exactly what would happen if he ever stepped inside the cage. “And I thought, man, she never really says no about my wacky ambitions, but maybe she just knew I’d get decimated or something. But that was a hard no.” So while Cody at least entertained the idea of seeing how far his wrestling background could take him in MMA, Brandi apparently saved everyone from ever finding out. And judging by Cody’s own assessment of his BJJ skills, he doesn’t seem too upset that she did. title: On the Record: Cody Rhodes Says Hardcore Wrestling Fans Are Missing the Point About WWE’s NIL System
raw_title: Cody Rhodes Says Hardcore Wrestling Fans Are Missing the Point About WWE’s NIL System
summary_src: Cody Rhodes has heard the complaints about WWE’s NIL system, but he thinks some hardcore wrestling fans are missing the bigger picture.
body: Speaking on Double Coverage , Cody was discussing the old territorial days and his father Dusty Rhodes’ time in Florida when the conversation turned to wrestlers who came from other sports. Ernie Ladd, who played professional football before becoming a wrestling star, helped Cody make his point. According to Cody, promoters back then were constantly looking for athletes who had the physical tools to become wrestlers. The NIL system might have a modern name and structure, but he believes the basic idea is nothing new. “You know, today, hardcore wrestling fans don’t always love the NIL system, and I don’t think they realize, or maybe they do, that’s how we used to do it. You were out there looking for, ‘Hey, this guy, this baseball player out here, I think he’d be great. He’s got a great look.’” Cody even brought up the kind of old-school recruiting that could happen just from somebody catching a promoter’s eye. If someone looked like an athlete and had the right background, that could be enough to get them through the door. “Or, you know, Bill Watts seeing somebody go through the airport. ‘What do you do?’ ‘Oh, I play offensive line.’ ‘Hey, try this.’ They were looking for the athlete.” And Cody doesn’t think WWE needs to spend as much time searching for the people who already live and breathe professional wrestling. In his mind, those people are going to chase wrestling whether WWE finds them first or not. “And the reason they were looking for the athlete is because the wrestler is always going to find wrestling. Like, the hardcore wrestlers, the types that love it and it’s true to them, they’re going to find it.” Johnny Gargano was Cody’s example of exactly that kind of wrestler. Cody believes Gargano was always going to fight his way toward WWE because getting there meant too much to him. “You know, Johnny Gargano was always going to find WWE. He was going to do everything in his power to make sure he was in the biggest wrestling company there is, and will it.” The NIL system gives WWE a shot at finding the other kind of prospect — someone who might never have thought about becoming a wrestler at all. And Cody thinks Oba Femi could be one of the best examples of what happens when one of those athletes actually starts falling in love with wrestling. “But these others that are from the sports world, if you put it in front of them, they might fall in love with it. I think Oba, I don’t know, I just kind of keep a distance, watch him, think he’s falling in love with it.” Before WWE, Oba competed in track and field at the University of Alabama, and Cody clearly thinks WWE found something special there. He believes Oba has already given fans somebody they can get behind for a long time. “And that again, you know, he’s out there shot putting or whatever the heck it was for Alabama, like setting records. Another one I’m giving you a list here. Another one would be good for the pod. Articulate, lovely, and something that wrestling fans can attach to righ

title: On the Record: Vince McMahon Accused of Putting WWE Writers in a ‘Hostage Situation’
raw_title: Vince McMahon Accused of Putting WWE Writers in a ‘Hostage Situation’
summary_src: Mansoor has heard WWE’s old creative team get blamed for some of the bizarre stuff that made television during the Vince McMahon era, but he says fans were blaming the wrong people.
body: Speaking on Self-Made Sitdown , Mansoor described working in WWE during that period as anything but boring. Even when he wasn’t booked on the show, he said there was usually some kind of backstage drama going on, and the writers were often stuck right in the middle of it. “It was never boring. It was never boring. Even if you weren’t on the show, there was always drama and something happening. Those poor writers, man. Yeah, it was like they were in a hostage situation.” Mansoor joked that writers sometimes just wanted wrestlers to accept whatever was on the page rather than sending them back to Vince with complaints. From his perspective, keeping things moving was sometimes more important than arguing over the material. “‘Don’t make me go back saying that you didn’t like it. Please just nod your head, take this f****** paper, and let’s just all move on from this.’” And Mansoor thinks those writers took way too much heat from fans, particularly around 2019 when WWE creative was getting hammered online. He argued that people assumed the writers themselves were coming up with everything they saw on television when that wasn’t necessarily the case. “I think writers get a lot of heat, or at least they did in like 2019 during the real low point in WWE under Vince. And it was always like, ‘These writers don’t know what they’re doing.’ Can we, like, be so for real? They’re not coming up with this s***, bro.” According to Mansoor, writers could pitch ideas, but their main job was essentially putting together dialogue Vince didn’t want to write himself. And if keeping your job meant not fighting certain creative decisions, Mansoor understood why writers weren’t exactly lining up to challenge the boss. “Like, their job is to write dialogue that Vince doesn’t want to write himself. That was their only job. They can pitch stuff, but they’d rather keep their jobs.” Mansoor then revealed one pretty simple way wrestlers could apparently tell when something came directly from Vince. If part of the script was highlighted, Mansoor says you weren’t changing it. “It was so funny. So anything in your script that is highlighted is from Vince, so you can’t change it. It would be certain s*** that he would just feel on the day.” And his best example involved Sami Zayn. Mansoor recalled Vince speaking with somebody backstage when Zayn suddenly came through the door because he wanted to discuss a match. Vince apparently wasn’t thrilled about being interrupted and immediately sent him away. “Like, for example, I f****** love Sami. Here’s something he did. Vince was talking to somebody, and Sami burst through the door to talk about a match, and Vince was like, ‘I’m talking to somebody.’” Zayn apparently tried to squeeze in whatever he needed to say anyway, but Vince wasn’t having it. According to Mansoor, Vince simply told him to get out. “And Sami was like, ‘Can I just—can I have it really quickly?’ Vince was like, ‘Get out.’” That backstage interaction apparently didn’t st

summary_src: Nikki Bella’s shot at the WWE Women’s Championship didn’t end the way a lot of fans wanted, and they wasted absolutely no time letting WWE know about it.
body: After months of building Nikki back up, seeing the Hall of Famer lose to Chelsea Green with a roll-up on the October 30 episode of SmackDown left a pretty angry section of the fanbase wondering what the hell all that build was for. One fan was absolutely furious over WWE keeping the championship on Green. They argued that Nikki brings additional attention whenever she appears and accused the company of wasting that by having her lose again. “NO F*** YOU. THIS IS A F*** *** JOKE. NOBODY WANNA SEE MAGA CANADIAN AS A CHAMP ANYMORE. UNACCEPTABLE. NIKKI BRINGS SM RATINGS AND EXPOSURE EVERYTIME AND YALL KEEP PLAYING ON HER FACE. A F*** *** JOKE OF A COMPANY. BE ASHAMED. NO WONDER NO1 WATCHES ANYMORE.” Another fan didn’t need nearly as many words to make their feelings clear. For them, WWE simply picked the wrong winner, saying, “Nikki should’ve won.” Not everybody was only upset about the result either. One fan ripped into the match itself , claiming Nikki and Chelsea had no chemistry and hoping WWE doesn’t run it back. “No heat from the fans in the building. No chemistry in the ring. I hope we never see Nikki Bella against Chelsea Green again. This match was terrible.” The finish seemed to annoy people even more because of how much time WWE had spent building Nikki ahead of the title opportunity. One fan questioned why all of that ended with a roll-up and also criticized Nikki for failing to notice Green getting her feet onto the ropes. Another frustrated viewer turned their attention toward Triple H and WWE’s treatment of returning legends. They argued that WWE hypes those names up only to repeatedly make them look weak once they’re actually back on television. “Bull crap.!! I remember the time @TripleH was the best. I’m 34..the company give legends a shit show.!! Hall of famers… make them weak… bring people back and hype them but make them lose every match,!! Same people win…” And one fan was especially brutal about Green’s actual in-ring work. They compared the match to something kids would put together at a family party and dismissed it as “Disney Channel wrestling.” “Might be the worst woman wrestler I’ve ever seen ngl. Her matches are so boring bro my lil cousins could have a crazier wrestling match in my grandmas room during a party. Disney Channel wrestling.” All of that backlash came after Nikki came painfully close to leaving SmackDown with the championship. She hit Chelsea with the Rack Attack 2.0 late in the match, but Green managed to get her feet onto the bottom rope before eventually catching Nikki with a roll-up for the three-count. The interesting part now is where WWE actually takes Nikki from here. She got the big return, spent months getting built back up and finally received a championship opportunity, only for Chelsea to sneak past her rather than putting her away decisively. title: Former WWE Star Tammy Lynn “Sunny” Sytch Attempts to Overturn Conviction, But Judge Issues Warning About Longer Prison Sentence
raw_title: Former WWE Star Tammy Lynn “Sunny” Sytch Attempts to Overturn Conviction, But Judge Issues Warning About Longer Prison Sentence
body: Former WWE personality and Hall of Famer Tammy “Sunny” Sytch is making another attempt to challenge the conviction that sent her to prison for more than 17 years. However, her latest legal effort has already encountered a setback, and a Florida judge has warned that successfully reopening her case could potentially result in an even longer prison sentence. According to a report by PWInsider on October 30, 2026 , Sytch recently filed a post-conviction motion seeking to have her judgment and sentence overturned. The motion argues that her original defense attorney provided ineffective assistance by failing to investigate several issues surrounding the March 2022 automobile crash that resulted in the death of 75-year-old Julian Lasseter. Sytch’s legal filing raises questions about Lasseter’s medical history, toxicology findings and the circumstances surrounding his death. She argues that additional investigation into those matters could have affected the outcome of her case. Among the issues raised was Lasseter’s reported history of coronary artery disease, stenosis and other cardiovascular conditions. Sytch also pointed to toxicology records indicating that Lasseter had Adderall and Cialis in his system. Additionally, the motion questioned whether injuries associated with CPR performed at the scene could have contributed to the medical findings. Sytch maintains that her defense attorney failed to adequately investigate whether the collision legally caused Lasseter’s death and whether alternative medical circumstances played a role. The former wrestling star also raised a potential conflict-of-interest issue involving the prosecution. According to the filing, lead Assistant State Attorney Ashley Terwilliger was married to physician Zachary Terwilliger, who declared Lasseter’s death. Sytch argues that her defense failed to investigate the relationship or determine whether it presented a conflict that should have been disclosed. She is seeking an evidentiary hearing, additional discovery, and ultimately the opportunity to have her conviction vacated and potentially receive a new trial. Despite the arguments presented in her filing, Sytch’s latest legal attempt suffered an immediate setback. On October 21, Volusia County Circuit Court Judge Christian Miller dismissed the motion, ruling that it was “facially insufficient.” Importantly, the dismissal was based on procedural requirements rather than a determination of whether Sytch’s allegations about her defense attorney or the medical evidence have merit. According to the court’s order, the filing failed to include required sworn statements under Florida’s criminal procedure rules. Those requirements include certifying that the defendant has read and understands the motion and that the facts presented are true and correct. That explained, her latest legal effort has already encountered a setback, and a Florida judge has warned that successfully reopening her case could potentially result in an even longer prison.
