title: Shawn Michaels Replacing Bruce Prichard in WWE Now Being Called Overblown
raw_title: Shawn Michaels Replacing Bruce Prichard in WWE Now Being Called Overblown
summary_src: Shawn Michaels taking over Bruce Prichard’s WWE job after WrestleMania 43 was starting to look like a done deal, but now there’s a major update that could change everything.
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Meltzer addressed the speculation surrounding Prichard’s expected departure from his full-time WWE position. When Garrett Gonzales asked who could take over the role, Meltzer revealed that several people within WWE had told him the talk about Michaels stepping into the position had gotten out of hand. And according to Meltzer, Michaels wasn’t even the first name he heard when he started asking questions. Instead, Robert Roode and Ed Koskey were initially brought up as potential replacements. “We don’t know. I think that this, I was, I’ve been told by many people the Shawn stuff is way overblown. You know, I mean, when I first asked, it was, it was, I go like, who’s, who’s replacing him? And it was Robert Roode and Ed Koskey. And then everything started coming up with Shawn and it’s like, well, you know, it’s an administrative job in a lot of ways, what Bruce did. And Shawn is not suited for that.” That doesn’t mean Michaels is completely out of the picture. Meltzer acknowledged that the WWE Hall of Famer could be interested in the position, especially considering his close relationship with Triple H. However, he questioned whether Michaels would actually want the demanding travel schedule that comes with Prichard’s current responsibilities. At 61 years old, Michaels already has a major position overseeing WWE NXT in Orlando, Florida. Taking over Prichard’s job could mean traveling around the country multiple times a week for WWE television tapings, something Meltzer believes could factor into the decision. “Now, does Shawn want to do this? Yeah. You know, and again, and him and Levesque are best friends and all that. I mean, it’s, in a sense, it surprises me because, you know, Shawn’s 61, and at 61, do you, you know, you’ve got this job in Orlando, which is one of the better places to live in the world, certainly as far as weather goes and everything. Do you really, at 61, want to fly all over the country twice a week to do television? And look, it’s his call. I mean, so maybe he does. Maybe he just wants to change. It would be for more money, you know, so there’s that.” Meltzer then made another important distinction. Even if Michaels does receive a promotion, that doesn’t necessarily mean he’ll be doing everything Prichard currently handles. In fact, Meltzer said he’d been told that much of Prichard’s workload wouldn’t be transferred to Michaels. He also brought up an interesting possibility involving AJ Styles. If Michaels becomes more involved with WWE’s main roster creative direction, it could create an opening in NXT for Styles to take on a larger behind-the-scenes role. “So we’ll have to see how it plays out. body: This week’s episode of AEW Dynamite saw small drops in its rating and total viewership from the previous week. Wednesday’s show brought in a 0.14 rating in the 18 – 49 demographic and 620,000 viewers per Wrestlenomics . As always, these numbers do not include HBO Max viewing. Those numbers are down 6.7% and 6.2% respectively from the previous week’s 0.15 demo rating and 661,000 viewers. The demo rating matches the number from two weeks ago, while the total audience was the lowest since the October 7th show drew 495,000 airing on a Tuesday opposite WWE NXT. As a reminder, Nielsen made an adjustment to its Big Data + Panel numbers in late January, and even the original Big Data + Panel ratings make things difficult to compare to pre-change weeks. That said. AEW Dynamite is currently averaging a 0.121 demo rating and 656,000 viewers in 2026 compared to a 0.152 and 598,000 for the same time period in 2025.

raw_title: Bayley’s WWE Contract Status Revealed Amid Talk of Possible NXT Role
summary_src: Bayley’s future in WWE is getting some attention, and with her contract situation now part of the conversation, there’s a question about what the company has planned for her moving forward.
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer discussed Bayley’s status while talking about possible changes to WWE NXT’s leadership. With Shawn Michaels being linked to Bruce Prichard’s position after WrestleMania 43, Garrett Gonzales brought up Bayley as someone who could potentially take on a role helping develop younger talent. And according to Meltzer, that’s not such a crazy idea. He explained that several WWE veterans have expressed interest in working with younger wrestlers, including CM Punk. “I think that they’re all interested in helping younger wrestlers. You know, Punk’s made it very clear he’s interested in that.” But Bayley’s situation is a little different. Meltzer suggested that she might actually be open to making that kind of move, although nothing has been decided. “From all I hear, Bayley, you know, it’s a different story. You know, maybe that’s something that she wants to do. So it’s — that one’s possible.” The conversation then shifted to Bayley’s WWE contract, and Meltzer made it clear that there’s some uncertainty surrounding her next move. However, he doesn’t expect her to leave WWE for AEW. “Her deal’s up. I’m pretty much sure she’s not going to AEW. Not 100 sure, but pretty sure, and we’ll see what happens.” That doesn’t mean Bayley is preparing to leave wrestling or that WWE has offered her a position in NXT. But Meltzer believes there’s another factor worth considering — where WWE currently sees her in its women’s division. Despite Bayley being one of the most accomplished women on the roster, Meltzer doesn’t believe the company intends to position her among its top four female stars. “They’re not gonna put her in the top four women’s spot. Whether, you know, you could argue she deserves it. She’s really good all around and all that.” Instead, Meltzer believes WWE has established a particular role for Bayley, and that role involves helping younger stars get over rather than consistently being featured at the top of the championship picture. “They’ve got her at a certain slot, and really her slot is to be one of the women to get the younger women over.” That’s an interesting assessment considering Bayley’s history with the company. She’s a former multi-time Women’s Champion, one of WWE’s original Four Horsewomen, and someone who helped establish NXT’s women’s division long before it became the developmental brand fans know today. She’s also spent years working with rising talent on the main roster, so the idea of Bayley eventually becoming more involved with NXT wouldn’t exactly come out of nowhere. Still, there’s no indication that WWE has officially offered Bayley a developmental position or that she’s planning to stop wrestling. Meltzer’s comments were about what could happen rather than anything that’s already been finalized. For now, Bayley’s contract status remains an interesting situation to watch. Meltzer doesn’t expect her to jump to AEW, but he also doesn’t see WWE pushing her back

title: On the Record: Charlotte Flair Rocks Princess Diana’s Iconic ‘Revenge Dress’ for Halloween
raw_title: Charlotte Flair Rocks Princess Diana’s Iconic ‘Revenge Dress’ for Halloween
summary_src: Charlotte Flair went all-out for Halloween this year, and she didn’t exactly pick a random costume. The WWE star transformed herself into Princess Diana, recreating one of the late royal’s most famous looks down to the dress, wig and accessories.
body: Flair took to Instagram to share several photos from the shoot, where she recreated Diana’s iconic black “revenge dress.” Charlotte completed the transformation with a short blonde wig, sunglasses and white accessories around her arms, making the Princess Diana inspiration pretty damn hard to miss. Charlotte also had a little fun combining Diana’s famous nickname with her own Queen persona in the caption. But Charlotte wasn’t just recreating the look. She also included several Princess Diana quotes throughout the post, including one about people feeling unloved. “The biggest disease this day and age is that of people feeling unloved.” Another slide featured Diana’s famous words about following her heart rather than living by somebody else’s rules. “I don’t go by the rule book… I lead from the heart, not the head.” The final slide gave some extra context for anyone who didn’t immediately recognize the outfit. Charlotte was recreating the black off-the-shoulder dress Diana famously wore in 1994 on the same night a television interview aired in which Prince Charles admitted to infidelity during their marriage. That history made the costume a little more interesting than Charlotte simply dressing up as another famous blonde for Halloween. Between “The People’s Princess,” “The Queen” and one of Diana’s most defiant fashion moments, Flair clearly knew exactly which version of Princess Diana fit her own WWE persona. title: JBL Praises 30-Year Friendship With Savio Vega
raw_title: WWE HOFer JBL Reflects On Friendship With Savio Vega
summary_src: WWE Hall of Famer John "Bradshaw" Layfield describes his long-term friendship with Savio Vega.
body: WWE Reflecting on his first program with Savio Vega at WWE SummerSlam 1996, John "Bradshaw" Layfield may have been his enemy on-screen, but in real life, the Hall of Famer is delighted by their 30-year long friendship. JBL spoke highly of his friend, and even recounted Vega's prominent nickname that carried with him throughout his WWE career. "I had a great relationship with Savio," JBL said enthusiastically on "Something to Wrestle." "Savio was my trial match, just happened by happenstance...You couldn't ask for a better person to wrestle with then Savio. Savio was an incredible worker. I don't know anybody who's ever had anything bad to say about Savio...Hunter [Triple H] used to call him 'bumblebee' because bumblebees aren't supposed to be able to fly. And Savio would get up at the top rope...Savio could actually fly, and he's like the bumblebee. He could do things that physics said that he shouldn't do." Today, JBL and Vega work close at hand with one another, as both of them are part of WWE's sister promotion, Lucha Libre AAA Worldwide. Vega acts as one of its producers , while also serving as one of its color commentators and translators alongside JBL.

title: Jeff Hardy Written Off TNA TV Due To Neck Injury
raw_title: Backstage Report On Jeff Hardy's Upcoming TNA Absence
summary_src: Jeff Hardy has been written off of TNA television, and there are two big reasons why that has happened.
body: The October 29 episode of "TNA Impact" wasn't a good night at the office for Matt and Jeff Hardy as they were defeated by syX in a Slaughterhouse syX match, with both Samuel Shaw and Joseph Sawyer going the extra mile to take out Jeff in particular. Towards the end of the match, Jeff had a trash can placed over his head and both Shaw and Sawyer hack into it with axes to incapacitate him, but this was a move to not only give syX a big win over the former TNA World Tag Team Champions, but it was to also write Jeff off of television. According to Fightful Select , there are two main reasons why Jeff has been written off of television. The first is a nagging injury he has been dealing with in his neck, with Matt even detailing on a recent episode of his " Extreme Life of Matt Hardy " podcast that Jeff has had bulging disks in his neck which requires him to take time off. TNA sources noted that Jeff won't need surgery right now, though that could change if things don't improve for him during his stint away. The second reason, and one that is much more prominent for TNA's upcoming schedule is that the company will be holding its TNA Destination X 2026 Premium Live Event in Canada (Edmonton, Alberta to be specific) on November 14, which will be followed up with two "Impact" tapings in Calgary on November 18 and 19 respectively. Due to Jeff's previous legal issues, he is not allowed into Canada as the country is very strict when it comes to people with criminal records, and so the company wrote him off of television as a way to explain why he won't be on the next set of shows. However, TNA could still keep Jeff in the loop with pre-tapes and vignettes, with one source within the company calling it a "perfect storm" as Jeff will have no choice but to rest up and rehab his neck problems. Jeff is expected back in December for the "Impact" tapings in Texas, but he will be active while TNA is in Canada as he set to appear at the WrestleCade convention in North Carolina, and on Chris Jericho's "Rock N Wrestling Rager at Sea."

title: Why CM Punk Isn’t Likely to Take Over WWE NXT Anytime Soon
raw_title: Why CM Punk Isn’t Likely to Take Over WWE NXT Anytime Soon
summary_src: CM Punk has made it pretty clear that he wants to help WWE’s next generation of wrestlers, but anyone expecting him to take over NXT in the near future might want to pump the brakes. There’s apparently one big reason why that kind of move isn’t happening anytime soon — and it comes down to ...
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer discussed Punk’s potential future behind the scenes while talking about possible changes to WWE NXT’s leadership. With Shawn Michaels being linked to Bruce Prichard’s position following WrestleMania 43, the conversation turned to who could eventually step in and help run WWE’s developmental brand. And Punk’s name certainly makes sense. He’s spent considerable time around NXT talent since returning to WWE, and he’s been open about wanting to help younger wrestlers develop. Meltzer acknowledged that interest but made it clear he doesn’t expect Punk to walk away from competing anytime soon. “Punk’s made it very clear he’s interested in that. But, you know, like, with Punk, I don’t see him stopping wrestling for a couple of years.” The biggest issue isn’t whether Punk wants to help NXT. According to Meltzer, it’s the financial difference between being one of WWE’s top active performers and taking on a full-time role running the developmental brand. Punk is still a major attraction for WWE, and Meltzer doesn’t believe it makes sense for him to give up that kind of earning power just to move into a backstage position. “He’s making, you know, way too much money than he could make, you know, running NXT.” That doesn’t mean Punk will never end up working behind the scenes. In fact, Meltzer believes the possibility becomes much more realistic once Punk gets closer to the end of his in-ring career. The discussion comes as WWE faces questions about its future creative structure. Bruce Prichard is expected to step away from his full-time position after WrestleMania 43, while Michaels has been mentioned as a potential replacement. However, Meltzer has also pushed back on the idea that Michaels taking over Prichard’s entire role is a done deal . That leaves questions about whether Michaels will continue running NXT and who might eventually assume those responsibilities if he moves into a larger position. Punk’s experience and willingness to mentor younger wrestlers would certainly make him an interesting candidate. But there’s a major difference between helping talent backstage and being responsible for running an entire television brand every week. For now, Punk appears to have plenty left to accomplish inside the ring, and Meltzer doesn’t see him trading that career for an office job just yet. A future running NXT isn’t being ruled out, but anyone hoping to see Punk take charge of WWE’s developmental system may have to wait until he’s ready to hang up his boots. title: Comeback Watch: Why Big Cass’ WWE Return as a Heel Has Been So Difficult
raw_title: Why Big Cass’ WWE Return as a Heel Has Been So Difficult
summary_src: Big Cass admits coming back to WWE after eight years away came with one pretty big problem — fans already knew exactly who he was.
body: Speaking on The Sal Licata Show , Cass was asked whether his previous success with Enzo made establishing himself as a singles star more difficult this time around. Cass didn’t hesitate, admitting that returning as a heel meant he was immediately fighting against years of nostalgia. “It definitely does, yes, because I’m coming back into WWE as a heel, right? I think we can talk about heels and faces on your show, I’m pretty sure. I’m coming back as a heel, and the last time anybody in that viewing audience saw me, that they recognized me from, I was in one of the hottest babyface acts in the company.” And Cass isn’t underselling how popular he believes he and Enzo were during that run. In his mind, they weren’t just over — they were comfortably among WWE’s three biggest babyface acts at the time, and he’s not particularly interested in debating it. “Top three, I would say, at that time. And argue with a wall if you don’t agree with that. I would say at that point, we were a top-three babyface act in the entire company.” That history followed Cass right back through the door when he returned to WWE on the August 3 episode of RAW. Instead of Enzo standing beside him and the crowd repeating their old catchphrases, Cass returned alone as a heel and immediately attacked Je’Von Evans . Cass has since been teaming with Ethan Page, but fans clearly haven’t forgotten his old partner. He revealed that people still shout the Enzo and Cass-era catchphrases at him during matches, although he suspects they’re now doing it specifically because they know it’ll annoy him. “And now I’m coming back by myself as a heel. It makes things a lot harder. You go out there as a heel and people are booing you, but you do hear people in the crowds saying the old catchphrases at me.” Funny enough, Cass actually sees some upside in that. If fans are deliberately bringing up his old babyface run because they think it’ll piss him off, then at least they’re treating him exactly how a heel wants to be treated. “And I think they’re doing that to get under my skin. And I think that’s their true intention, which as a heel is a good thing.” Still, Cass knows things probably would have been much simpler if WWE audiences didn’t already have such a strong memory of him alongside Enzo. Instead of introducing an entirely new character, he’s trying to convince fans who once loved yelling along with him that this version of Big Cass deserves their boos. “But yes, to answer your question, it makes it way more difficult than having a clean slate.” That also makes Cass’ current pairing with Ethan Page an interesting test of whether he can finally build a WWE identity that doesn’t immediately lead back to Enzo. The old catchphrases clearly aren’t disappearing anytime soon, but Cass now has a completely different partner, role and attitude to give fans something new to associate with him. title: Reason for WWE Bringing in John Cena to NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
raw_title: Reason for WWE Bringing in John Cena to NXT Against AEW Blood & Guts
summary_src: WWE isn’t taking any chances when NXT goes head-to-head with AEW Dynamite’s Blood & Guts special, and bringing in John Cena might be the company’s biggest move to make sure the ratings battle doesn’t turn into an embarrassment.
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer discussed the upcoming Wednesday night showdown between WWE NXT and AEW Dynamite. While the scheduling conflict wasn’t originally designed to put the two promotions against each other, WWE apparently wasn’t about to let AEW walk away with an easy victory. “Nick said, you know, I mean, I heard, you know, he was like, Nick says, we got to — we can’t go in, you know, they don’t want to go in there and get killed.” Meltzer explained that AEW already has a significant advantage going into the showdown. Dynamite is airing in its normal Wednesday night slot, and Blood & Guts is traditionally one of the company’s biggest television attractions. “In a sense, AEW has the advantage. It’s their night and it’s Blood and Guts. So it’s going to be one of their highest rated shows.” That put WWE in a difficult position. NXT wasn’t moving to Wednesday because the company necessarily wanted another ratings war, but once the two shows were scheduled against each other, WWE had to figure out how to compete. And according to Meltzer, the company wasn’t interested in watching NXT get crushed in the ratings. “They didn’t want to go in there and get humiliated or anything. So what do we do?” The answer? John Cena. Meltzer pointed out that Cena remains one of the biggest television attractions WWE can bring in, making him an obvious choice to generate additional attention for NXT against such a major AEW event. “The biggest drawing card on TV is John Cena, except for Dwayne.” Cena’s involvement gives NXT a major name to promote at a time when casual wrestling fans might otherwise be more interested in watching AEW’s Blood & Guts match. Whether his appearance will actually make enough of a difference in the ratings remains to be seen. The situation is also different from some of WWE and AEW’s previous scheduling battles. Meltzer explained that NXT’s move to Wednesday was driven by The CW’s election coverage rather than an intentional effort to disrupt Dynamite. However, WWE’s apparent response shows that the company still cares about how its programming performs when the two promotions go directly against each other. And with Nick Khan’s name coming up in the discussion, it’s clear that Meltzer believes this is about more than simply putting together another episode of NXT. WWE doesn’t want to suffer a lopsided ratings defeat, and Cena gives the company one of its strongest possible attractions to help prevent that. body: Kelani Jordan discusses who have inspired her in the pro wrestling industry, noting that she loves and still looks up to Bianca Belair. When talent comes into the world of professional wrestling, even if they were not a fan of the industry beforehand, they usually have inspirations for their style in the ring, and Kelani Jordan, a former gymnast, is no different. So at the time when I grew up, when I was like, ‘oh, when I grow up,’ I wanted to be an Olympic gymnast. summary_src: Big Cass knows the Enzo Amore reunion rumors made his WWE return more complicated than it needed to be. According to Cass, the speculation got so loud before his comeback that plenty of fans apparently started believing Enzo was definitely coming back with him.
body: Speaking on The Sal Licata Show , Cass explained that the problem started almost immediately after news broke that he had signed with WWE again. Instead of his return being treated as a fresh start, his name was instantly linked with his former tag team partner. “But yes, it makes it way more difficult than having a clean slate. Especially because when news came out of me signing with WWE, it immediately got linked to him.” Cass recalled seeing the idea of an Enzo and Cass reunion spreading across wrestling podcasts. Before long, he believes speculation had turned into expectation, with fans convinced they were about to see the old team running it back in WWE. “‘They’re coming back together. They’re going to be running it back together.’ A lot of podcasts ran with that story, and people believed it.” Then Cass actually returned on the August 3 episode of RAW — and there was no Enzo. Instead, Cass showed up alone after eight years away and attacked Je’Von Evans, immediately establishing himself as a heel. Cass admits that after everything people had heard beforehand, seeing him walk out there by himself left some fans confused. “So then I come back on my own, and some people are like, ‘Wait, what?’ And it kind of made it a little difficult.” But Cass doesn’t think those expectations have stopped him from making this run work. He believes he’s done a pretty damn good job getting fans to boo the version of Big Cass they’re seeing now, which is exactly what he wants as a heel. “But I think so far I’ve done a pretty damn good job with the situation I’m in, getting booed out of buildings, which is really the goal.” Interestingly enough, Cass’s comments line up with something that was being discussed inside WWE earlier this month. WrestleVotes via Fightful Select reported that some members of WWE creative felt fans were too busy expecting Enzo to show up , making it harder to establish Cass as his own character. And the Enzo talk wasn’t completely coming out of nowhere. Dave Meltzer previously reported that Enzo returning to WWE had been discussed and at one point appeared pretty close, but the idea was reportedly to keep him separated from Cass because WWE saw more potential in Cass as a singles star. “There was talk of Enzo in NXT. It was talked to me like it was pretty much a done deal, but they were gonna keep Enzo and Cass apart because of the idea that if they put them together, Cass’s upside is very limited in that tag team based on how WWE does tag teams.” Now Cass is teaming with Ethan Page, getting booed and building something completely separate from the act that originally made him famous. Fans may still have Enzo in the back of their minds, but Cass clearly thinks he’s finally giving them something else to associate with his name. body: WWE Forget trick-or-treating. "WWE NXT" is preparing for a Halloween Havoc filled with title fights, brutal battles, and plenty of frightening surprises. Hosted by the "very nice, very evil" Danhausen, Halloween Havoc will emanate from the WWE Performance Center in Orlando, Florida on October 31, with six matches on the lineup. Two championships will be at stake during this premium live event: the NXT Women's and NXT Championship. Kelani Jordan will defend the former against Wren Sinclair, who won a number one contender's battle royal while disguised AAA's Lady Shani. The move initially left "NXT" General Manager Robert Stone conflicted, but ultimately, he awarded the title shot to Sinclair. NXT Champion Grayson Waller will put his title on the line against his predecessor Tony D'Angelo. Waller pinned D'Angelo to capture the title at "NXT" Heatwave. Weeks later, the former D'Angelo family leader secured a rematch by defeating Myles Borne in a number one contender's bout. Borne will also be in action at Halloween Havoc when he takes on his former No Quarter Catch Crew partner Tavion Heights. He turned on Heights after losing both the NXT North American and NXT Tag Team Championships at Heatwave. Now, they'll clash in a stipulation that promises to bring the intensity: Weapons Wild. Zilla Fatu and Charlie Dempsey are also slated to meet under a special stipulation. Theirs will likely be determined the night of, courtesy of the famous Halloween Havoc wheel. Elsewhere in non-title action, Izzi Dame will take on NXT Women's North American Champion Zaria. Dame has made it clear that she's eyeing the title, but for right now, she's more interested in making the red-haired Aussie face the "demons" lying inside. Rounding out Halloween Havoc is a match pitting Naraku against Shiloh Hill. The former EVIL marked his return to "NXT" programming by blinding Hill with mist, and in turn, costing him an NXT North American Title opportunity. Hill has made it his mission to find a cure for the powerful vapors ever since.

title: Samoa Joe Praises Modern Wrestlers' Adaptability
raw_title: AEW's Samoa Joe Identifies Ways Modern Wrestling Has Improved On The Past
summary_src: AEW star Samoa Joe identified some ways modern wrestling has improved compared to previous generations.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Samoa Joe has had a nearly three-decade long career in professional wrestling, and with his recent return to AEW following his latest filming schedule for "Twisted Metal," it doesn't look as though he's slowing down anytime soon . In February 2025, Joe formed The Opps faction within AEW, and in storyline, he has taken wrestlers like Hook and Katsuyori Shibata under his wing in order to elevate them. Joe spoke about the next generation of wrestlers, like Hook and Action Andretti, on an episode of " SHAK Wrestling ." He said there are two things this current generation of stars does better than his generation, and others of the past. "I think adaptability and coordination are way better than they've probably been in years," Joe explained. "I think that you get a lot of people who maybe have more of a natural aptitude, but maybe less physical potential. I think that's kind of the best way to put it. But, you're finding people who are definitely, and I think you kind of see the same trend in MMA, where it's like you know in the lighter weight classes, you're going to see a lot more technicality. You're going to see a lot more skill." Joe said you're likely to see closer matchups between more technical guys, ones who can take more punishment being in a lighter weight class. He said in the past, the scene was dominated by a more heavyweight style. On the podcast, Joe also named the opponent who hit him the hardest in his career , fellow heavyweight, Brock Lesnar. The star has worked with plenty of more technical wrestlers, such as Bryan Danielson, throughout his lengthy career, however.

summary_src: Rusev has high praise for Penta. Since returning to WWE in 2025, Rusev has frequently shared the ring with Penta. As it turns out, he's been a big fan of the luchador since their time in AEW.
body: Since returning to WWE in 2025, Rusev has frequently shared the ring with Penta. As it turns out, he’s been a big fan of the luchador since their time in AEW. “I’ve been a fan of Penta since the other company we worked for before.” Rusev said in a new interview with TMZ Inside The Ring. “CJ can tell you that as soon as I came back after the first or second show I was there, I bragged to her about these two guys, the Lucha Bros. They were just so unbelievable, they’re like live action figures. Penta is just so cool, he looks like a Mortal Kombat character. Rusev praised Penta’s recent Money In The Bank win, saying that him being a world champion is good for business. “I think he deserves it 100%. I love working with Penta, I love kicking his ass. I know how entertaining he is and how cool he is. I’m a big fan of him. If he’s becoming a champion, I will be more than happy for him and for the business in general, it’s good for the business.” “Also, he’s a great guy. He’s got so many — he’s helping so many kids in Mexico. You guys have no idea because he doesn’t talk about it, but in private conversations, [he’s told me] he’s helped like tons of orphans, people with no homes. He buys them truckloads of toys and clothes and helps these kids. He’s a tremendous guy. If people get to know him, they’d love him as a person.” Elsewhere in the interview, CJ Perry revealed that Rusev will portray a villian in the film adaption of her ‘Bulletproof Angel’ novel. title: Backstage Buzz: WWE’s Original Match Plans for Oba Femi at Saudi Arabia Event Revealed
raw_title: WWE’s Original Match Plans for Oba Femi at Saudi Arabia Event Revealed
summary_src: Oba Femi was originally supposed to have a much different role at WWE’s upcoming Saudi Arabia Crown Jewel event, but the company ended up changing the plans and leaving him out of the advertised match altogether.
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio, Dave Meltzer revealed that WWE initially planned to have Femi compete in a six-man tag team match alongside Penta and Je’Von Evans against Bron Breakker, Bronson Reed, and Austin Theory. That would’ve given Femi a prominent spot on the Saudi Arabia card, putting him directly opposite Breakker and Reed in a match featuring some of WWE’s biggest rising stars. But somewhere along the way, WWE decided to scrap that lineup. Meltzer revealed the original plans while discussing changes to the event’s match card. “The tag team title match was originally a six man with Oba Femi and Bronson Reed, you know, Oba, Penta, Je’Von against Breakker, Reed, Austin Theory.” Instead of moving forward with the six-man tag, WWE changed the bout into a tag team championship match. That decision meant Femi and Reed were no longer part of the advertised lineup. “That was the original lineup match and they changed it to a tag title match leaving Oba and Bronson Reed off.” That’s a pretty significant adjustment for Femi, especially considering the original match would’ve given him an opportunity to share the ring with Breakker, Reed, and Theory on a major international show. But just because Femi was removed from the original lineup doesn’t necessarily mean WWE is finished with the idea. Meltzer suggested that Femi and Reed could still become involved in the tag team championship match, potentially setting up the six-man encounter for a later date. “It wouldn’t shock me at all to see those two involved in that match to lead to the six man.” Of course, that’s only speculation at this point. Meltzer didn’t confirm that WWE has plans for Femi to interfere or that the original six-man match has been rescheduled. The only confirmed change from his account is that WWE originally had Femi booked for the match before switching to a tag team title bout. For now, Femi’s involvement in the Saudi Arabia event remains uncertain. WWE clearly had a spot in mind for him when the card was first being put together, but the decision to change the match has left questions about what comes next. And with Meltzer suggesting the original six-man match could still happen, there’s a chance WWE hasn’t completely abandoned the idea. title: Analyzing Randy Orton's Disappointing 2026 WWE Run
raw_title: The Disappointing 2026 WWE Run of Randy Orton (And How it Can Be Salvaged)
body: 2024 and 2025 were banner years for Randy Orton. We saw him in compelling feuds against the likes of Kevin Owens, Drew McIntyre, Logan Paul, and even running it back one last time with his best friend and arch-rival John Cena. That match with Cena was the turning point for Orton, or it should've been, as he made his intentions clear that he wanted to go for world title number 15 right here, right now. Fast forward to early 2026, in a match literally decades in the making, as Orton challenged Cody Rhodes for the Undisputed WWE Championship at WrestleMania 42. WWE's first mistake with this is pulling the trigger too early. Sure, it was teased several times since Rhodes came back to WWE in 2022. However, they needed a definitive build-up to this, which it didn't have. It only started to roll in February. But okay, fine, we're still getting Rhodes vs. Orton, Mentor vs. Student; it still sounded fun. Then, Pat McAfee happened, derailing this whole thing to oblivion weeks before WrestleMania 42, and the McAfee/Orton partnership went absolutely nowhere. To add insult to injury, Orton punt-kicked Rhodes after losing his Undisputed WWE Championship Match at the "Grandest Stage of them All." Literally a week or two later, Rhodes was on SmackDown like he never got hit with one of the most devastating wrestling moves ever. For us, that killed Orton's character in a huge way. Then, there was a lull period in between that match at 'Mania 42, and Orton came back in August 2026, a full four months later, when all the heat was gone, and they had another match at WWE Sunday Night's Main Event in September that was a bit of a dud. This whole debacle could've been avoided if they either A. built up to it, maybe resulting in a SummerSlam 2026 match instead, or B. Having Orton win at WrestleMania 42, becoming one of the biggest villains in wrestling again with the title in hand. Unfortunately, we're getting the payoff at WWE Crown Jewel 2026 of all PLEs . An event that most don't necessarily look forward to, instead of a Big 5 like Survivor Series or Royal Rumble. The feud started disastrous; now it's ending with a whimper. What was supposed to be literally generational is just another match on a B-level pay-per-view. While we can't do anything about the feud with Rhodes, with it ending a week from today, at the time of writing, WWE can still sharpen the knife that is Randy Orton to end 2026 and as he heads into 2027. First things first, have him win at WWE Crown Jewel 2026 against Rhodes to finally put the nail in this coffin, simple as that. Why? Sure, Rhodes has pulled the trigger after punt-kicking Baron Corbin . title: Comeback Watch: WWE Women’s Division Legend Rules Out In-Ring Return Despite Fan Demand
raw_title: WWE Women’s Division Legend Rules Out In-Ring Return Despite Fan Demand
body: Multi-time champion Melina held a Q&A session on TikTok, and a fan asked about returning to the ring. The former five-time Women’s Champion said that while she loves to watch wrestling and be around it, she does not have the hunger to get back in the ring. Melina noted that wrestling on television was spectacular because today’s in-ring competitors have that hunger. Therefore, she did not want to return half-heartedly and disappoint her fans. “Everyone keeps asking me this and I say no, no. I love to watch, I love to … just be around it. Now, I think those days is just different. I don’t have the hunger and you need the hunger. You need that because you see it. So, when you watch your favorite wrestlers wrestling, if they don’t, they have that hunger. That’s what makes it even better to watch. So, I don’t have that. So, I disappoint you guys and I don’t wanna do that.” Melina debuted in WWE in the early 2000s. She was the manager of the MnM tag team (Johnny Nitro and Joey Mercury) and then transitioned into a singles performer. Melina attained incredible success, winning both the WWE Women’s and Divas titles and competing against top stars like Beth Phoenix, Mickie James, and more. However, her spectacular run came to an end in 2011 when WWE released her. Following that, Melina competed on the independent circuit for a few years and continues to make non-wrestling appearances. Meanwhile, she made a few WWE appearances, including being the second participant in the 2022 Women’s Royal Rumble match and having a moment with Sasha Banks.
summary: Multi-time champion Melina held a Q&A session on TikTok, and a fan asked about returning to the ring. The former five-time Women’s Champion explained that while she loves to watch wrestling and be around it, she does not have the hunger to get back in the ring.

title: AEW Dynamite Fright Night Draws 620K Viewers
raw_title: AEW Dynamite Viewership & Ratings Report, 10/28/2026
summary_src: It was a spooky night in St. Louis this week on "AEW Dynamite," but the company saw a slight dip in the television ratings.
body: AEW/Speedy Ruiz The stars of All Elite Wrestling were in the Halloween spirit on October 28 as the company presented the Fright Night edition of "AEW Dynamite" in St. Louis, Missouri. Queen Aminata won her first piece of gold in AEW by beating Persephone to become the new AEW TBS Champion. Darby Allin successfully defended his AEW TNT Championship against Josh Alexander, and the main event of AEW Full Gear 2026 looks to be set as Kyle Fletcher challenged Will Ospreay to a match for the AEW World Championship. As far as the television ratings are concerned, AEW did receive a small fright for this week's show, as Wrestlenomics have confirmed that the Fright Night edition of "Dynamite" averaged 620,000 viewers. This is a 6% drop from the previous week's 661,000 viewers , and 18% below the trailing four week average of 758,000 viewers, with the show garnering the lowest ratings since the Grand Slam France special that was preempted to air on a Tuesday night, and the lowest in its regular Wednesday night slot since the Rebel Heart special on September 9. With all that said the current average for both the month of October and the fourth quarter of 2026 sits at 665,000 viewers, 38% above the October 2025 average and 34% above the average for the fourth quarter of last year. In the 18-49 demographic, there was also a drop as the show posted a 0.14 number, 7% lower than the 0.15 number posted seven days ago. The Fright Night special was also 18% lower than the trailing four week average of 0.17, but was enough to finish second for the night in its timeslot behind the NBA according to Dave Meltzer of the Wrestling Observer , who also reported that the show posted a 0.21 number in the 25-54 demographic.
summary: The October 28 episode of AEW Dynamite from St. Louis featured Queen Aminata defeating Persephone to win the TBS Championship, Darby Allin retaining the TNT Championship against Josh Alexander, and Kyle Fletcher challenging Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship to set up the Full Gear 2026 main event. The show averaged 620,000 viewers according to Wrestlenomics, marking a 6 percent decline from the prior week and an 18 percent drop from the trailing four-week average.

llm.headline: AEW Dynamite Fright Night Draws 620K Viewers
llm.summary: The October 28 episode of AEW Dynamite from St. Louis featured Queen Aminata defeating Persephone to win the TBS Championship, Darby Allin retaining the TNT Championship against Josh Alexander, and Kyle Fletcher challenging Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship to set up the Full Gear 2026 main event. The show averaged 620,000 viewers according to Wrestlenomics, marking a 6 percent decline from the prior week and an 18 percent drop from the trailing four-week average.

llm_long: AEW presented its Fright Night edition of Dynamite on October 28 from St. Louis, Missouri. Queen Aminata defeated Persephone to win the AEW TBS Championship and claim her first title in the promotion. Darby Allin retained the AEW TNT Championship against Josh Alexander.

Kyle Fletcher challenged Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship, setting up the main event for AEW Full Gear 2026. The episode averaged 620,000 viewers, marking a 6 percent decline from the prior week's 661,000 viewers. It represented an 18 percent drop from the trailing four-week average of 758,000 viewers and was the lowest figure for a Wednesday night broadcast since the Rebel Heart special on September 9.

In the 18-49 demographic the show posted a 0.14 rating, which was 7 percent lower than the previous week's 0.15 and 18 percent below the trailing four-week average of 0.17. The Fright Night special placed second in its timeslot behind NBA programming and third overall for the night on cable according to Dave Meltzer.

It also aired opposite the deciding game of the World Series on Fox that drew more than 14 million viewers. Compared to the same week in 2025 that also featured the World Series, Dynamite's viewership rose 35.1 percent and its 18-49 rating increased 75 percent.
The current October and fourth-quarter 2026 averages stand at 665,000 viewers, up 38 percent from October 2025 and 34 percent from the fourth quarter of the previous year.

title: Xelina Credits Rhodes And Cena For Longer Title Match
raw_title: Former WWE Star Says She Got Longer Title Match Because Of Cody Rhodes And John Cena
summary_src: A former WWE star said that she got a longer championship match thanks to Cody Rhodes and John Cena leaving the women some extra time.
body: WWE A former WWE star gave major props to Cody Rhodes and John Cena for allowing her to get some extra time in a WWE championship match that she called one of her favorite bouts of her career. Xelina, the former Zelina Vega in WWE, told the "Ring the Belle" podcast that her August 1, 2025 "WWE SmackDown" match against Giulia for the Women's United States Championship only got the time it received thanks to the stars. She explained the first 30 minutes of the show were meant for Rhodes and Cena, which ended up being Cena's face turn ahead of WWE SummerSlam . Xelina said that when WWE officials texted her about the match beforehand, the women were only going to have around seven or eight minutes total, around a commercial break. "Then when we got there, they were like, 'Yeah, it might be 30 seconds, actually. Then the break, and then three minutes,'" Xelina said. "I was like, 'Okay, so, why are we even doing this? Like, what's the point of this?' They were like, 'Well it really depends on how long Cody and John are going to go.' I was like, 'Okay...' I asked Cody, I'm like, 'Hey, so how long do you think you and John are going to go? Do you think you're going to go a little bit longer?' ...He's like, 'Uh, why? Do you guys have to base it on us?' I'm like, 'Basically. I'm just trying to ease Giulia's mind as far as how much we actually might have.' He's like, 'Oh, I think either we'll probably go right on time.'" Xelina said that she planned for the shorter time in her head after speaking to Rhodes and was ready to go. Things changed when they were standing in gorilla, however. WWE Xelina said that as she and Giulia were waiting to go out for their match, Rhodes came back through the curtain and said he and Cena saved them an extra 10 minutes. She said that she and the "Beautiful Madness" immediately panicked. "First of all, amazing for him to do that," Xelina said. "We wouldn't have had that time if it wasn't for Cody and John. He's thinking we're going to be excited and I'm like, 'No, bro... We didn't really plan it that way.' And he's like, 'Oh. Sorry...' Giulia's like panicking, I'm like, 'Look at me. Look at me. It's going to be fine. We'll just do the longer version.' We kind of talked about it. I'm like, 'I'll talk to you out there, just listen to me and we'll do it.'" The former WWE star explained that Giulia is one of her close friends, and the pair worked together in Xelina's ring at her home to figure out the match before the episode of "SmackDown." She said that they planned out some things that they could possibly do, and they ended up calling those spots in the match. Xelina said that outside of her match at Backlash 2023 in Puerto Rico , her Women's US title bout against Giulia is her favorite match of her career.
summary: Former WWE performer Xelina revealed on the Ring the Belle podcast that her August 1 2025 SmackDown Women's United States Championship match against Giulia became one of her favorite career bouts after receiving extra time. The opening segment featuring Cody Rhodes and John Cena's face turn ran long, which shortened the women's match to around three minutes initially. WWE officials told Xelina the bout length ultimately depended on how much time Rhodes and Cena used.

title: Kelani Jordan Says TNA Title Run Improved Her WWE Promos
raw_title: Kelani Jordan reveals how TNA Wrestling changed her WWE promos
summary_src: WWE NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan says her run as TNA Knockouts Champion helped her stop overthinking her promos. Speaking on The Wrestling Classic, Jordan opened up about her TNA Knockouts title run and shared that it helped her improve her promo skills.
body: WWE NXT Women’s Champion Kelani Jordan says her run as TNA Knockouts Champion helped her stop overthinking her promos. Speaking on The Wrestling Classic , Jordan opened up about her TNA Knockouts title run and shared that it helped her improve her promo skills. “ I definitely would say when I went to TNA. And the reason why I say when I went to TNA and when I was champion for TNA is because TNA, we would film lots of shows in one day at times ,” she said. “ So I honestly didn’t have time to really think about what I was going to say. So sometimes I would just go out there and talk, and whatever just came off the dome or on the fly, or maybe react to what the fans are saying. When I was in the ring doing the contract signing with Indi, I just talked. It was literally just me ,” she added. “ I think then is when it really turned for me. And I think I got in my head a lot when I first started, just trying to be so prim and proper and perfect. I did come from a broadcasting background, and the way that we were trained to talk in school was like how you would see a newscaster project and say stuff ,” Jordan further shared. She also said that when she was with TNA, she was getting way more reps because she was working with both the promotions, and it became a huge turning point for her promo skills. Jordan is now scheduled to face Wren Sinclair at WWE NXT Halloween Havoc with her NXT Women’s title on the line. body: The surprising result took place during WWE’s Road to Survivor Series: WarGames live event on October 29 at the Covelli Centre in Youngstown, Ohio. title: AEW Dynamite Will Not Go Head-to-Head With WWE SmackDown on January 1 After All
raw_title: AEW Dynamite Will Not Go Head-to-Head With WWE SmackDown on January 1 After All
summary_src: AEW Dynamite and WWE SmackDown won’t be going head-to-head on January 1 after all, despite earlier information suggesting the two shows were headed for a Friday night ratings battle.
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , Dave Meltzer clarified AEW’s television schedule for New Year’s Day 2027, revealing that Dynamite will air much earlier than initially believed. That means AEW and WWE won’t be competing directly against each other that night. Meltzer acknowledged that his original information about the scheduling conflict was incorrect and explained that he had since learned the actual plans for Dynamite. Instead of going up against SmackDown in its usual Friday night time slot, AEW Dynamite will air following a college football game. That gives the company a potentially valuable television audience without having to compete directly against WWE. “I’ve since found out that the Dynamite show on January 1st, Friday now is going to be after the football game.” And Meltzer provided a clearer picture of when fans can expect the show to air. According to his latest information, Dynamite is scheduled to begin sometime between 3:30 PM and 4 PM Eastern, meaning the entire broadcast should wrap up before SmackDown gets underway. “It’s going to start from — be around between 3:30 and 4 Eastern, and it’ll be over before SmackDown starts.” That changes the situation considerably for AEW. Instead of trying to pull viewers away from WWE on Friday night, Dynamite will have the opportunity to attract fans who were already watching college football. Meltzer pointed out that the football lead-in could give AEW a chance to reach viewers who don’t normally tune into professional wrestling. However, he also noted that the company will need to make an immediate impression if it wants those viewers to stick around. “They have 15, 30 minutes to really deliver something in front of an audience that normally will not be watching the show.” Meltzer also admitted that his original understanding of the schedule would’ve put AEW in a much tougher position. Going directly against SmackDown could have created a difficult ratings situation, especially with Dynamite airing outside its regular Wednesday night slot. “I thought they were going head to head with SmackDown, which would have been really bad.” The clarification is important because AEW moving Dynamite to Friday had initially raised questions about whether Tony Khan’s company was preparing to challenge WWE directly. Now, that won’t be the case. Instead, AEW will have a college football lead-in and a separate afternoon window to draw viewers before WWE takes over Friday night with SmackDown. body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , MLW founder Court Bauer revealed that his company had been deep into negotiations with Paramount in 2025. The talks began before Paramount’s acquisition by Skydance was finalized, and according to Bauer, MLW was the wrestling company involved in those negotiations. “And I’ll tell you a little story. You reported this and you guys will get the exclusive. The company they were talking with last year at Paramount prior to the Skydance acquisition was MLW. And the deal was going to be on the other side of the Skydance acquisition. It was being kind of going through the government to get cleared and get blessed. And we were told, you’re on standby, this deal is going to go. But we just got to wait.” And this wasn’t just a situation where MLW had a few meetings and hoped something would come together. Bauer explained that negotiations started around April 2025 during the company’s trip to Los Angeles, and things moved quickly enough that MLW was preparing to bring in additional staff and significantly increase production. “So those talks started right around the time of our LA show. We actually met with them when we were out there in, was like April-ish of 2025. Moved fast and we were just, we had deal pretty much laid out. We were just waiting on standby through June, July, and we had our people ready to go out there and make this thing happen.” The plan was ambitious. MLW wouldn’t simply be producing another taped wrestling series. title: Injury Update: Piper Niven Makes Major Breakthrough in Recovery Following Neck Surgery
raw_title: Piper Niven Makes Major Breakthrough in Recovery Following Neck Surgery
summary_src: Piper Niven just gave fans another encouraging sign that her recovery is moving in the right direction. Months after neck surgery left her wrestling future uncertain, Niven is back working out in the gym — and her latest photos show a noticeably slimmer look as she continues putting in the work.
body: Niven shared the latest look at her recovery on Twitter , showing herself training again after spending months healing from surgery. Getting back into the gym marks another major step after she previously revealed that her 12-week scans showed her neck was “healing beautifully.” One fan eventually asked Niven how she had been doing, and she made it clear that the recovery process still isn’t exactly easy. But whatever problems she’s dealing with, she isn’t letting them stop her. Niven also made it clear that she still prefers keeping much of her recovery private. After occasionally popping back up online with updates, she joked that “Mother” needs the darkness while she continues healing. It’s another positive development after a pretty scary stretch for Niven. She previously admitted there was a possibility she might never wrestle again following her neck issues, before eventually undergoing surgery and beginning the long recovery process. Her 12-week scans finally brought some much- needed good news when doctors told her everything was healing well . At the time, Niven shared the update with fans while making it clear she still wasn’t planning on becoming particularly active on social media. “Howdy cowpokes 🤠 got my 12 week scans and everything is ‘healing beautifully’.” Niven hasn’t wrestled since facing Charlotte Flair on SmackDown in Dublin in August 2025, and there still isn’t a confirmed timetable for her WWE return. But going from worrying about whether she could ever wrestle again to healing well and getting back into the gym is certainly a hell of a lot better direction for things to be heading. And Piper doesn’t seem interested in putting pressure on herself by promising a return date just yet. For now, she’s training, recovering and apparently disappearing back into the shadows whenever she feels like it — but each little update is showing more progress than the last. Are you excited to see Piper Niven making progress after her neck surgery, and who would you like to see her face when she’s eventually cleared to return? Let us know what you think in the comments. body: Nikki Bella discusses the possibility of facing off with her twin sister Brie one more time before they both retire from wrestling. While speaking to Justin Dorazio in a new interview, Nikki Bella was asked about potentially facing off with her sister Brie one last time before they both retire. “I mean, now, like, after our injuries, I don’t think so. I just don’t think… We’re so, like, at the end of our in ring careers that I feel like it just has to be together at this point. I would have loved that though before, because I really loved that match with Brie. It’s a lot like when I have my matches with Paige, there’s certain people you work with and you have great chemistry with and you give a lot to each other, and I remember that match. We just are timing, like, you know, you just have chemistry and I would have loved to have one more match, especially how I am now. I would love for Brie to, like, if it was still Paige and I in a story, for her to come in and call me out and be like, what? But, like, by the time she heals and comes back, I don’t think it’ll happen, unfortunately.” On last night’s edition of WWE Friday Night SmackDown, Nikki challenged Chelsea Green for the WWE Women’s Championship. title: Excalibur Names Omega vs Ospreay His Best Called Match
raw_title: AEW's Excalibur Pinpoints The Best Match He's Ever Called
summary_src: Before Excalibur was in AEW, he was the "Voice of PWG". He has called numerous matches, but there is one that he picked as the best he's ever called.
body: YouTube/Ballast Point Brewing Company Wrestling fans know Excalibur as a wealth of knowledge and human dictionary when it comes to the names of wrestling moves. Long before AEW existed, Excalibur was the voice of PWG. He was also an in-ring competitor from 2000 to 2007. In his time, he has been the voice associated with a variety of matches that's only grown in AEW. His trademark "Un-BEE-LEEV-able" can be heard during "Dynamite" and sprinkled throughout pay-per-views. During an interview with the Ballast Point Brewing Company , Excalibur reflected on Kenny Omega versus Will Ospreay at All In. He pointed out that the broadcast team was quiet for the first 10 minutes because of Ospreay's video package and walk to the ring. "Then he comes out to Wembley Stadium to 50,000 of his countrymen who are just screaming their heads off. They are cheering. They are singing along with his song. The fireworks are going off. What could we say as broadcasters that carried more weight than what was happening in that stadium at that moment?" Excalibur explained that once the match started, the broadcast team began the storytelling by telling the stats and explaining their rivalry. "But now it's a battle for the best and who is the top dog. And it was the best professional wrestling match that I have ever called as a broadcaster and maybe the best professional wrestling match that I've ever seen," Excalibur declared.
summary: AEW announcer Excalibur identified Kenny Omega versus Will Ospreay from All In as the greatest match he has ever called. He noted the broadcast team stayed silent for the opening 10 minutes to let Ospreay's video package, entrance at Wembley Stadium before 50,000 fans, and the crowd's reaction speak for itself. Excalibur previously served as the voice of PWG and competed in the ring from 2000 to 2007.

Ospreay entered Wembley Stadium to a crowd of 50,000 fans cheering and singing along with his theme as fireworks went off. Excalibur explained that the live atmosphere carried more impact than anything the broadcasters could add at that point.
Once the match began, the team shifted to providing statistics and background on the wrestlers' rivalry. The contest evolved into a battle to determine the top performer in professional wrestling.
Excalibur described the match as the best professional wrestling bout he has called in his career and possibly the best he has ever witnessed.

body: More Share Options More Share Options Share close facebook x threads email WWE and Blockchain Creative Labs, the new non-fungible token (NFT) business and creative studio formed by FOX Entertainment and Bento Box Entertainment, today announced an exclusive multi-year agreement to launch an NFT marketplace for licensed digital WWE tokens and collectibles. The partnership marks Blockchain Creative Labs’ first-ever content alliance with an external property beyond FOX. In collaboration with Blockchain Creative Labs, WWE will create authentic NFTs that celebrate the company’s entire catalog of digital assets, including its most iconic moments, past and present WWE Superstars and premier events, such as WrestleMania and SummerSlam. Powered by Eluvio’s eco-friendly blockchain technology, the marketplace will serve as a hub for consumers to purchase, trade, sell and store digital tokens that will be authenticated through Eluvio’s blockchain and will be interoperable across Ethereum and other blockchains. The marketplace’s name and launch date will be announced in the coming weeks. “Blockchain Creative Labs has quickly become a leader in the space with an incredible executive team that truly understands the NFT arena and its tremendous potential,” said Scott Zanghellini, WWE Senior Vice President, Revenue Strategy & Development. “This new partnership allows us to deepen our relationship with FOX, as we continue to explore new and creative ways to engage our passionate fanbase.” “Blockchain Creative Labs is excited to partner with WWE in launching its official NFT ecosystem. We know WWE’s passionate fan community will love owning authentic digital goods across the organization’s creative universe -- from past and present stars to classic, culture-defining moments,” said Scott Greenberg, CEO of Blockchain Creative Labs and Co-Founder/CEO of Bento Box Entertainment. “Our NFT studio is all about enabling fans to own NFTs and tokens that carry utility and social clout directly from the creators and brands they are passionate about, spanning animation, sports, shows and movies to music, books, art, pop culture and every other Web3-powered media asset you can possibly imagine.” To participate in the WWE NFT marketplace, fans create a secure and easy-to-use WWE digital wallet through Eluvio that acts as a vault and enables consumers to purchase collectibles using traditional currency or cryptocurrency. body: Nikki Bella speaks about several wrestlers in WWE she still would like to share the ring with before she retires, including Blake Monroe. Bella has had several different tag team partners over her wrestling career, although the most notable by far has been her tag team with her twin sister Brie, who is currently out with an injury. However, there is one talent that she still would like to have a run as a tag team with. While speaking to Justin Dorazio in a new interview, Nikki Bella spoke about the talent on WWE’s roster she still wants to share a ring with. “Oh, gosh. There’s so many. Like, love Chelsea Green. So happy. I didn’t know if I’d get to Chelsea Green. She’s just so entertaining and funny, and then I just love that. I would love to have something with Maxxine (Dupri) before I call it a day. There’s just, I look at Maxxine and she just… She’s been crushing it. I’d love to do entertaining stuff with her. I love when there’s something personal I could bring into the story. It’s always how I am, and so there’s a lot of like how Chelsea and Paige, I’ve been able to bring in so much personal stuff. I see that I could do that with Maxine. I want to revisit Liv. It was such a tease, and I think to go back to Liv would be great. Shoot, let me think. You know, I see Lola Vice would be so fun. Rhea Ripley has always been a dream.” Nikki also briefly spoke about potentially getting in the ring and teaming with Blake Monroe. “Blake Monroe. I mean, there’s so much there for Blake and I, but we’re both heels. So like, we’ve always talked like we need to be a tag team right now. It’d be so fun.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: Former WWE star praises TNA partnership but says "there's still room to improve that relationship"
raw_title: Former WWE star praises TNA partnership but says "there's still room to improve that relationship"
body: While speaking to Medd in the Morning , former WWE star Cedric Alexander commented on his ongoing run with TNA Wrestling. Alexander stated the following in regards to WWE’s partnership with TNA… “I think it’s been working very well. I think there’s still room to improve that relationship, but also, you know, it’s one of those things where it’s just good for the business. You know what I mean? I feel like the business itself progresses faster when everyone works together. There’s no need for tribalism. We all find a place to work. I remember I was in NXT when the partnership was announced, and I remember being excited because I thought, “Ooh, I could probably go to TNA and do some things in TNA.” That was my exact thought. It was one of those bucket-list things. I didn’t know how long I was going to be at WWE, and if the opportunity came to TNA in any way, shape, or form, I would love to do that. Then, when the opportunity came up, it was even better that it was with Ali and debuting there. Man, I feel like the last year and a half, two years, has been a journey of ups and downs, but it’s been a journey that helps me appreciate wrestling more and gives me better insight into what I need as a professional wrestler. I think TNA has given me exactly what I need as a professional wrestler, and that’s something that I don’t want to take away from anyone.”

title: Drew McIntyre Nearly Recalls Signing With NJPW Before 2017 WWE Return
raw_title: Drew McIntyre Says He Considered Not Returning To WWE In 2017, Had Talks With NJPW
summary_src: Drew McIntyre has said he wasn't keen on rejoining WWE in 2017 and was close to signing with NJPW, but a conversation with a WWE executive changed his mind.
body: ComposedPix/Shutterstock Drew McIntyre has disclosed that he was close to signing with NJPW before re-signing with WWE in 2017. McIntyre returned to WWE after a few years of rebuilding his character in various promotions, and his success outside WWE almost convinced him he didn't need to return. He recently said in an interview with " The Joe Vulpis Podcast " that he wanted to sign with New Japan after his time with TNA came to an end. "I realized as the success was coming, maybe I don't want to go back [to WWE]," said McIntyre. "So, when the time came with TNA, where I was working and I was champion, to not re-sign, I was okay. New management ain't feeling that for the future. I think I want to go to Japan. So, I started having initial conversations to go to Japan, like, towards New Japan. A couple of the guys who worked over there were going to speak to the bosses for me." The Scotsman's mind, though, switched after having a conversation with Triple H, who convinced him that the best decision for him was to return to WWE. "In my head, I was like, 'Ah, I feel like I'm going to go to Japan first and then see what happens there.' And within two minutes of the conversation with Hunter, it was like, 'Damn it. It's time to come back.' I'm like, 'You knew and I knew.' It was like, 'Okay, it's now time.' I'd been gone for three years. Was 32 at the time, felt very comfortable in myself. He'd been watching what's going on, could see I've kind of grown up, not just as a performer but as a man as well." McIntyre revealed that William Regal reached out to him after reading an article about him being a free agent and asked him to speak to Triple H. He added that he was keen to begin in "NXT" in his second spell in WWE and try to trick Vince McMahon into thinking he was a different, new person, eventually earning a spot on the main roster, which seems to have worked out as planned.

His success on the independent scene made him question going back until a conversation with Triple H persuaded him to re-sign with WWE in 2017. McIntyre shared the story in an interview on The Joe Vulpis Podcast.

body: Nikki Bella discusses Chelsea Green dressing up as her at a WWE live event prior to their WWE Women’s Title match on SmackDown. On this past Friday’s edition of WWE SmackDown, the WWE Women’s Championship would be on the line as Nikki would challenge Chelsea Green for the title, with Green impersonating Nikki following a live event appearance where she would dress up as the former Divas Champion. So when I got to the airport, I saw it, and honestly, I always get so flattered. It’s like… Like, I don’t even know how to put it into words, but it makes me feel very, very good.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

title: John Cena Hands Out King-Sized Candy For Halloween
raw_title: John Cena Hands Out King-Sized Candy Bars On Halloween
summary_src: John Cena gives his take on Halloween. In a new interview with The Romesh Ranganathan Show, Cena and Jessica Biel were asked about costume parties and if they'll be dressing up for Halloween this year.
body: In a new interview with The Romesh Ranganathan Show , Cena and Jessica Biel were asked about costume parties and if they’ll be dressing up for Halloween this year. Whenever he needs a last second costume for a party, Cena will just go as his wrestling personality. “So, the trope or the easy one is the John Cena costume. The jorts, the knee pads, the sneakers, the ball cap, the t-shirt, the double wristbands, the rally towel. I promise, it is a one-to-one replica. So that’s like if I need an emergency costume. It’s fail safe.” As it turns out, Cena uses his wrestling gear as a crutch, admitting that he lacks motivation to dress up. “To add to that, I think I keep that fail safe costume as a crutch for not being motivated to dress up. I don’t know.” Cena also went on to note that he hands out king-sized candy on Halloween. “I’m not anti-Halloween. He hands out oversized candy bars that he compared to diabetes in a wrapper, recalling how as a child he would repeatedly visit the one house that gave full-size bars. The performer noted that his community now has new neighbors with children, resulting in good numbers of trick-or-treaters each year.

His wife initially thought he was giving away too much candy when she first learned of his approach, but Cena insisted it was not enough. Cena stated that what he lacks in costume enthusiasm he compensates for by rewarding those who do dress up, emphasizing that both sides are necessary for the holiday.

title: Ishimori & Robbie X Win NJPW Super Junior Tag League A Block
raw_title: Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X reach NJPW Super Junior Tag League final
summary_src: Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X won the A Block of the NJPW Super Junior Tag League on Saturday, securing a place in Tuesday’s tournament final at Power Struggle.
body: Taiji Ishimori & Robbie X won the A Block of the NJPW Super Junior Tag League on Saturday, securing a place in Tuesday’s tournament final at Power Struggle. The pair defeated AEW’s Nick Wayne & KUSHIDA in the main event at Nishiyama Park Gymnasium in Nagaokakyo, Kyoto, finishing the round-robin stage at 4-1 with eight points. Wayne & KUSHIDA had entered Saturday with a slim chance of advancing, but they were mathematically eliminated before reaching the main event. DOUKI & Yoshinobu Kanemaru defeated Master Wato & KUUKAI in the preceding match, moving to eight points. Kanemaru sprayed KUUKAI with whisky from ringside before DOUKI finished him with a bridging suplex. That result meant Wayne & KUSHIDA, who began the night on four points, could no longer catch the leaders. They nevertheless had an opportunity to determine who won the block. A victory over Ishimori & Robbie X would have sent DOUKI & Kanemaru through, but Ishimori pinned KUSHIDA following a lifting double-knee gutbuster to move level on eight points. Ishimori & Robbie X advanced because they held the head-to-head victory over DOUKI & Kanemaru from earlier in the tournament. It is their second consecutive appearance in the Super Junior Tag League final after finishing as runners-up in 2025. Wayne & KUSHIDA ended their campaign at 2-3 with four points. They had earned their first victory against Místico & Masatora Yasuda before later defeating Master Wato & KUUKAI. Ryusuke Taguchi & DDT’s Kazuma Sumi finished A Block in third place after defeating Místico & Yasuda. Taguchi submitted Yasuda with an ankle lock to end their campaign at 3-2. AEW’s Blake Christian & Lee Johnson remain one of three teams tied on six points at the top of the B Block alongside Robbie Eagles & Kosei Fujita and YOH & Hyo. The B Block concludes on Sunday in Okayama. Christian & Johnson face Akira & Young, while Eagles & Fujita meet YOH & Hyo in the main event. The block winner will face Ishimori & Robbie X in the Super Junior Tag League final at Power Struggle in Hiroshima on November 3.
summary: Taiji Ishimori and Robbie X defeated Nick Wayne and KUSHIDA in the main event at Nishiyama Park Gymnasium in Nagaokakyo, Kyoto on Saturday. The win gave them an 4-1 record and eight points to top A Block and advance to the Super Junior Tag League final at Power Struggle on Tuesday. DOUKI and Yoshinobu Kanemaru also reached eight points by beating Master Wato and KUUKAI earlier in the show, but Ishimori and Robbie X progressed on the strength of their head-to-head victory.

title: JBL Doubts Vince Russo Joining WWE Creative
raw_title: JBL Doesn’t See Vince Russo Joining WWE’s Creative Team
body: “Zero. Now look, when you have creative, you bring in guys with all kinds of different ideas. So if they brought him in, I think something like that could make sense. Because when you’re doing creative you want every type of input you can get, and if Vince Russo had input, he would be able to bring all kinds of stuff. Maybe the ideas worked, maybe they didn’t work. But when you’re pitching ideas to creative people, sometimes you pitch something and they end up somewhere else — but they got there because of what you pitched. So to bring Russo in or something like that, I don’t think it’s out of the realm of possibility. Would he be the head of creative? No, I don’t think so. My opinion is that Triple H and Nick Khan are doing a great job.” “I don’t think it will happen. I think they’ve got to be happy. I know creative is subjective, but they’re selling out big-ass arenas. They’re making a ton of money. What more do you want? I understand you can always get something better. And these guys have got 50 hours of television a week. I’m exaggerating, but you get the point. They’ve got so many things that they’ve got to try, and some things are definitely not going to work. The same with Vince, the same with Jim Crockett, the same with Eddie Graham, the same with Fritz. But what you have to look at is the overall trend, and the overall trend for WWE is absolutely fantastic. So I think Nick Khan and Hunter are doing a terrific job. I think Jeremy Borash and Undertaker are lighting it on fire down at AAA.” “It makes perfect sense. Vince used to call guys all the time, and he’s the one that helped train Hunter. I’m sure Hunter and Nick Khan do the same thing. There are no wrong answers out there. When we talk about creative, you check a million different things to see what works. So I think it makes sense that they called Vince Russo.” “I would think I would have a better chance. I don’t think there’s any chance I will, but I think I’d have a better chance than Vince.”
summary: JBL believes it is possible for WWE to bring in Vince Russo for creative input to generate ideas that could help the team even if they are not used directly. However JBL does not see Russo being made head of creative and feels Triple H and Nick Khan are already doing an excellent job with the product. JBL added that with arenas selling out and strong financial success there is little reason for major changes to the creative structure.

title: Excalibur Recalls Chemistry Test With Jim Ross
raw_title: Excalibur Recalls Chemistry Test With Jim Ross Before Starting With AEW
summary_src: AEW play-by-play announcer Excalibur recalls having to do a chemistry test with the Hall of Famer Jim Ross before AEW launched at Double or Nothing in 2019
body: Since day one of AEW, Excalibur has been the most consistent voice at the promotion's commentary desk. But that may not have been the case if he hadn't impressed colleague Jim Ross in the weeks leading up to AEW's first event, Double or Nothing. In an interview with "Ballast Point Brewing Company," Excalibur revealed he and Ross were tested together to see if they were compatible, and that Ross may have been a bit uneasy about Excalibur's professionalism due to him wearing a mask . "Before we even called a show together, they brought us in for a chemistry test," Excalibur said. "We all sit down behind the microphones, but I see there's cameras there, so I put on the mask. And JR looks at me and says 'You know, this isn't about you, right?' And I'm like 'Sir, please, I know. Just give me a chance.'" Ross and Excalibur have worked together since, save for Ross' prolonged absences due to health issues , and the WWE Hall of Famer has since gone on to call Excalibur "a great friend" and "a great asset to me." Part of that may be because, at least in Excalibur's mind, he does try to put the wrestlers first and his own performance second. "The thing that I like to do most is keep the focus on the action in the ring," Excalibur said. "Because really, it's not about me. I'm just the voice, the narrator that's describing the action. The meat and potatoes of it is what's going on in the ring. And the effort being given by these guys and girls who are, quite frankly, they're risking their lives in some cases. Their future, future health, future prospects, future ability to interact with their kids, things like that. Me being respectful of that is paramount to me. It's the most important thing to be respectful of the effort being put forth by these people."

Excalibur explained that he wore his mask during the session which prompted Ross to question if he understood the focus was not on him. The two have called shows together since with Ross later praising Excalibur as a great friend and asset.
