title: Mark Henry’s Son Jacob’s Timeline for WWE Arrival
raw_title: Mark Henry’s Son Jacob’s Timeline for WWE Arrival
summary_src: Mark Henry just dropped a pretty big update on his son Jacob Henry’s WWE future — and it sounds like the second-generation prospect could finally be getting much closer to actually starting his wrestling career with the company.
body: Speaking on Busted Open Radio , Henry revealed that Jacob is expected to come into WWE in about a year. The update comes after Jacob recently went through a WWE tryout, despite already having an NIL deal with the company dating back to 2024 . While discussing WWE’s future talent, Mark casually let it slip that he already knows someone who will be part of that next wave. “I find it interesting as hell, and some of that is because I know that I have a kid that’s coming in, in a year.” Charlie Dempsey immediately realized Mark was talking about Jacob and brought up meeting him when he came in for his WWE tryout. Mark confirmed it was Jacob before revealing just how obsessed his son has become with wrestling. In fact, their relationship has apparently flipped around to the point where Jacob is now the one calling his Hall of Fame father to talk about what’s happening in WWE. “Yeah, Jacob. Jacob is ate up with wrestling. He calls me, ‘Hey Dad, what’s up? What’s going on? Hey, did you watch SmackDown last night?’ It’s all about wrestling. Our relationship used to be mentoring him and telling him, and now it’s him telling me.” The plan at the time was for Jacob to continue his college athletics career. He joined the University of Oklahoma’s wrestling program as a heavyweight and was also looking at football, so WWE was essentially investing in him for the future rather than immediately sending him into the ring. Now that future suddenly feels a hell of a lot closer, and apparently Mark won’t have to convince his son to fall in love with the business when that day arrives. Judging by all those phone calls about SmackDown, Jacob is already wrestling-obsessed enough that the mentoring is starting to go in the other direction. What do you think Jacob Henry’s ceiling could be in WWE once he finally makes the jump into professional wrestling? Let us know what you think in the comments. title: Backstage Buzz: WWE RAW’s Creative Format Has Apparently Barely Changed in Over 20 Years
raw_title: WWE RAW’s Creative Format Has Apparently Barely Changed in Over 20 Years
summary_src: WWE Raw has gone through different creative teams, major roster changes, and an entirely new era under Triple H, but there’s apparently one thing that hasn’t changed much in over 20 years — the way the show is actually put together behind the scenes.
body: During the October 31 edition of Wrestling Observer Radio , former WWE writer and current MLW owner Court Bauer discussed how professional wrestling television has evolved over the years. And while the presentation might look different today, Bauer claims the actual production format being used for Raw is practically identical to what WWE was doing when he worked there more than two decades ago. The conversation started when Dave Meltzer brought up Eric Bischoff’s influence on modern wrestling television. Meltzer argued that Bischoff helped establish the format that wrestling companies still follow today, moving away from television shows built primarily around squash matches and toward weekly programming featuring major storylines and competitive matches. Bauer agreed, pointing out that the basic structure of wrestling television hasn’t really evolved as much as fans might think. “That’s the thing I bring up a lot is the format has not changed.” But Bauer wasn’t just talking about the way wrestling looks on television. He claimed to have seen a leaked modern WWE Raw script, and what caught his attention was how familiar everything looked. According to Bauer, the show’s production rundown was essentially the same as the format WWE used when he worked for the company in the mid-2000s. “I’ve seen like a leaked, you know, modern day script from say WWE Raw or something. That format, that run sheet is identical to when I was there.” And considering how much WWE has changed since then, Bauer couldn’t believe how little the actual structure had evolved. Meltzer immediately pointed out just how long ago Bauer’s WWE tenure was, making the comparison even more interesting. That’s a pretty surprising revelation considering everything WWE has gone through since the mid-2000s. The company has moved from Vince McMahon overseeing creative to Triple H running the process, transitioned into the streaming era, and completely changed how it distributes its programming. Yet according to Bauer, the internal structure used to organize Raw’s segments and production remains almost exactly the same. The discussion also raised a bigger point about Eric Bischoff’s lasting influence on professional wrestling. Meltzer argued that the television format Bischoff helped establish during WCW’s Monday Nitro era became the blueprint that WWE and other wrestling promotions have continued using for decades. Bauer suggested that while companies have made adjustments to storytelling and presentation, the fundamental structure has stayed largely untouched. title: Results Recap: WWE Coliseum Collection Demolition Ax & Smash review (2026)
raw_title: WWE Coliseum Collection Demolition Ax & Smash review (2026)
body: October 31, 2026 Jeffrey Lyles Ax , Demolition , Mattel , Mr. Fuji , Smash , WWE Coliseum Collection , WWE Ultimate Edition When Mattel regained the rights to make Demolition figures it seemed inevitable for one of the most decorated tag teams in WWF history to get slotted into the premium WWE Coliseum Collection line. Fortunately, I was able to get the original Elite versions of Ax and Smash, but my preferred wrestling figure format is by far the Ultimate Edition takes so I was ecstatic to see them get released in that style relatively quickly. Let’s see if these ultimate versions of Demolition deliver the definitive versions of Ax and Smash or if they’re just walking disasters. Packaging: The WWE Coliseum Collection line has now shifted over to being exclusive to Ringside Collectibles so there’s no longer one box for the two individually carded figures. Now we get the same packaging style for each figure as we did the set. Ax and Smash get two full-size portraits with the silver foil side showing them in their ring gear. The back features them in their wrestling attire with the variant face paint. Instead of sharing the side portrait, now Ax and Smash have their own, which feels wrong for a tag team. The top features the lines of the iconic Demolition theme song with “Here Comes the Ax” and “Here Comes the Smasher.” The interior packaging retains the same presentation as the other CC figures. I still appreciate the different signs for every figure. Sadly, we no longer get the thick insert with the WWF interview backdrop. Ax is posed like his LJN figure and for reasons above my paygrade, Smash never got one so he’s posed to mirror Ax. As always, the plastic section pops off so you don’t have to damage the card, and the accessories are packaged in the stage stand with the figures’ names. The bios are mostly the same save switching up Ax and Smash’s names on the respective cards. It’s cool seeing how the line has progressed with this wave as the cross sell shows all of the Coliseum Collection figures made so far. Likeness: At the start (or second start once Moondog Rex got swapped out) at least, Demolition looked fairly similar with the same kind of stocky build. The main difference of course centered around their hair. While both of their hairlines were receding, Smash had a serious mullet going and it went down to the back of his neck. Smash also wore a longer knee pad on his right leg with blue or white. That’s been absent on most of the Smash figures, but it would have been a welcome touch for the high-end Smash to have it included. Mattel did include Smash’s left elbow pad, which was missing on the first Elite figure. Demolition wore a unique harness with a center ring clasping the straps together and boots with straps and studs. Mattel gave Ax and Smash thicker torsos, which I’m pretty sure are new molds. These are by far the best options for beefy guys like Demolition who weren’t big guys like Big Boss Man or Dusty Rhodes. Both head sculpts

title: Bully Ray Predicts The Rock Has One Retirement Match Left
raw_title: Bully Ray Thinks The Rock Has One More WWE Match In Him
summary_src: According to Bully Ray, WWE fans could see The Rock take part in a retirement match before it's all said and done, with one obvious opponent waiting for him.
body: WWE At WWE WrestleMania 40, The Rock stepped back into the ring to main event night one of the major event, teaming up with Roman Reigns to face Cody Rhodes and Seth Rollins. Considering "The Brahma Bull" was able to keep up with everyone else in the ring, could he have one more match left in him to tie up loose ends? Bully Ray believes so. "With all of that muscle that he's taken off, it'd be a lot less strain on him in the ring. Do I think he could get back into the ring in the shape that he is now? Yes I do," Bully Ray said during an episode of " Busted Open Radio ." Bully noted that The Rock has notably shed a lot of muscle compared to his peak in the ring, but the lighter build could end up helping his performance. "I do think there is a Rock retirement match, in front of like a hundred and fifty-thousand people." The Rock hasn't been involved in any storyline since coaxing John Cena to turn heel, as the storyline was heavily altered thereafter. While The Rock has almost completely transitioned into Hollywood, he's yet to officially retire and be inducted into the WWE Hall of Fame, which is why Bully believes a final match could make sense. Assessing a potential match pitting The Rock against Reigns, Bully believes that a failure to do so would be a missed opportunity on the level of The Undertaker vs. Sting never taking place.
summary: Bully Ray believes The Rock could return for one final WWE match now that he has shed significant muscle mass, making it easier on his body. Speaking on Busted Open Radio, he suggested a retirement bout in front of 150,000 fans would be fitting. The Rock last competed at WrestleMania 40 and has not been part of any storylines since attempting to turn John Cena heel.

body: Tony D’Angelo says that he ‘isn’t too focused’ on being considered one of the all-time greats in WWE NXT. D’Angelo has been a part of NXT for several years now, breaking out onto the brand during the 2.0 era of the developmental brand. Now in 2026, he is set to challenge for the WWE NXT Championship at Halloween Havoc and is currently a WWE NXT Grand Slam Champion. While speaking to Love Wrestling in a new interview , Tony D’Angelo was asked about how he feels about being looked at as a potential all-time great in NXT. “I try not to think of it, honestly. I’m just trying to keep my nose to the grindstone, and you know what? At the end of the day, if people want to say I’m one of the pillars or people held of high standard when it comes to NXT and championships and all that, then that would be awesome, and more power to me and my family and what I’ve done. But honestly, I’m not too focused on that.” If you use any of the quotes above, please credit and link to the original source with a h/t and link back to Fightful for the transcription.

body: The focus was on the A Block as the NJPW Super Jr. Tag League rolled into its fifth night of action. Only three matches were on tap and it was the final night of action for A Block. At the end of yesterday’s competition only three teams were left in contention in B Block. Yoh and Hyo, Robbie Eagles and Kosei Fujita, Blake Christian and Lee Johnson are all tied at six points each. You have to feel bad for Mistico. He was supposed to be teaming with El Desperado which would have made for an unstoppable team but with Despie’s injury, Mistico was teamed with Young Lion Yuto Yasuda. They have only one match of the tournament. Tonight was no different as Taguchi made Yasuda submit to the Ankle Lock. Mistico helped Yasuda to the back. House of Torture (DOUKI and Yoshinobu Kanemaru) had to win tonight’s match and hope that Taiji Ishimori and Robbie X would lose so they could continue on in the tournament. They faced Master Wato and KUUKAI who only had two points. The House jumped their competition before the bell even rang. Surprised? Not in the least. Wato and KUUKAI leapt at Douki and Kanemaru on the floor at exactly the same time wiping them out. Back in the ring, Wato splashed Douki in a corner, went down on all fours to allow KUUKAI to his a running drop kick. Wato hit the TTD as KUUKAI landed a moonsault from the top rope. Kanumaru broke the pinfall up though. Kanemaru drags Wato to the floor. KUUKAI escapes Douki’s Darkness Stretch. KUUKAI is kicked off into the ropes. Kanemaru spits whiskey in his face. Douki pins him with Suplex De La Luna to keep their tournament dreams alive. In the final match, KUSHIDA and Nick Wayne were playing the role of spoilers as they took on Unbound Company’s Taiji Ishimori and Robbie X. In the final moments of their match, Wayne hit a stunner and as X flew backwards Kushida put him in a Hoverboard Lock. Great exchange there. Ishimori isn’t the legal man but that doesn’t stop him from putting Kushida in a Bone Lock. Wayne super kicked Ishimori in the face. Ishimori springboards off the ropes. Kushida catches him with a kick. X takes out Wayne with a cutter off the ropes. He then splashes him on the floor. Kushida puts Ishimori in a standing Hoverboard Lock. title: Billy Gunn Discusses His Sons Austin And Colten
raw_title: AEW's Billy Gunn Shares Thoughts On His Children Following In His Footsteps
summary_src: Billy Gunn's sons Austin and Colten have followed in his footsteps as pro wrestlers, with the AEW coach offering his thoughts on their decision.
body: AEW/Ricky Havlik Billy Gunn has had the unique privilege of not just seeing both of his sons, Austin and Colten Gunn, follow in his footsteps and become full-time pro wrestlers, but he's even tagged alongside them and feuded against them in AEW . Gunn recently commented on his sons' wrestling careers during an interview with Inside The Ropes. "Austin is my youngest, he is me amped up to about a thousand. Colten is not anywhere near me, but he is very [much] the opposite of me and Austin, in that he is very analytic," the veteran explained about his two sons personalities. Following this, he recounted how the betrayal angle from his sons that led to their rivalry came into play, with the boys attacking him with a chair, leading to Gunn joining The Acclaimed. In spite of the chair shot, Gunn still expressed how proud he is of his sons and claimed that he legitimately thinks they're good wrestlers, and that he'd be honest if they were bad. "I wanted my kids to actually suck so they didn't do this job, but unfortunately..." Even though he's happy with Austin and Colten in AEW, Gunn had prerequisites for them before giving his blessing to begin training, claiming his sons had to go study first. "Austin, the day he graduated, walked from the stage, up the balcony where I was sitting, handed me [his diploma], and goes, 'When do we start?' And I went, 'F***!'" he recalled. "Colten, on the other hand, he was more put together, because he had his life planned out until he was 60, when he was gonna retire, and then it all went haywire for him, which was a total shock for me and Paula — Paula is my wife," Gunn added. "[Colten] came and said that he wanted to do it, and didn't want to have regrets, and then, f***, he was good at it, too."
summary: AEW star Billy Gunn described his youngest son Austin as an amplified version of himself while noting that Colten has a more analytical approach that differs from both. Gunn recalled the storyline in which his sons attacked him with a chair, which led to him aligning with The Acclaimed, and stated he is genuinely proud of their work as wrestlers. He admitted he had hoped his children would be bad at wrestling so they would avoid the profession, but acknowledged that unfortunately they are skilled enough to succeed in it.

title: TKO's Mark Shapiro Prioritizes Safety Over Budget For Saudi Events
raw_title: TKO President Mark Shapiro Talks Saudi Arabia Safety In Company Town Hall Meeting
summary_src: TKO (WWE's parent company) President Mark Shapiro remains aware of the escalations within Saudi Arabia and is prepared to make changes to upcoming shows if necessary.
body: "We will not hesitate to cancel those events, damned be our budget," said TKO President and Chief Operating Officer Mark Shapiro, regarding alternative measures he and others might have to take regarding its upcoming WWE and UFC events. Following the first town hall meeting held earlier this week, Shapiro has his eyes wide open on the safety of his employees ahead of their travels to Saudi Arabia, starting next weekend. That said, Shapiro is prepared to make changes to any and all upcoming events, should the danger over there continue to escalate. On Friday, POST Wrestling published audio recordings from its newest company town hall meeting, which Shapiro held to discuss financial implications that could occur should they cancel near and future plans for its events in the Middle East. Shapiro told employees that TKO "will not hesitate" to cancel them if there is "danger or a further escalation" of the region's conflicts. Additionally, in their hour long Zoom call, Shapiro mentioned that should they pull these events, it will have an impact in a "very negative way." However, his employees and their safety come first, and business comes second. "Of course, business is important, but humanity is most important," Shapiro explained. "So, this is more about keeping people safe and comfortable. The business is secondary. So, you know, I don't want to talk out of both sides of my mouth here. We want to have the year we all envisioned. We've all worked so hard for that year. [20]26 is shaping up to be that year." At this time, WWE's upcoming PLE, Crown Jewel, is still scheduled for next Saturday, November 7, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. On Wednesday, it was announced that the show will now be held at The Venue (ANB Arena). Saudi Arabia remains at a level three "reconsider travel" advisory through the US Department of State.
summary: TKO President and COO Mark Shapiro stated during a company town hall meeting that the organization will not hesitate to cancel upcoming WWE and UFC events in Saudi Arabia if regional dangers or conflicts escalate further. Shapiro emphasized employee safety as the top priority ahead of the first scheduled trip next weekend, while acknowledging that any cancellations would carry significant negative financial implications. The comments were made during an hour-long Zoom call whose audio was later published by POST Wrestling.

title: Tony D'Angelo Details Pressure of Being NXT Champion
raw_title: Tony D’Angelo says WWE NXT champion faces pressure over television ratings
summary_src: Former champion Tony D’Angelo recently revealed the amount of responsibility that the WWE NXT Champion has regarding TV ratings. Recently, speaking on the Battleground Podcast, D’Angelo opened up about the responsibilities of a WWE NXT Champion. “A lot comes with it.
body: Former champion Tony D’Angelo recently revealed the amount of responsibility that the WWE NXT Champion has regarding TV ratings. Recently, speaking on the Battleground Podcast , D’Angelo opened up about the responsibilities of a WWE NXT Champion . “ A lot comes with it. You’re the guy. The brand is on your shoulders. You’re at the forefront of everything, commercials, media, all this stuff. And it’s a lot more stressful because, I’m trying to be PC here, but crap rolls downhill ,” he said. D’Angelo further claimed that if the show doesn’t yield proper numbers or isn’t doing well in ratings, the promotion tends to look directly at the champion. “ Which is fine, and I appreciate Sean and everybody telling me that my shoulders are strong enough to carry it and that’s why they did that and that’s why I won. So, I’m okay with that. But, for sure, there’s a lot that goes on that you don’t really know until you’re champion ,” he finished. D’Angelo is a former WWE NXT and NXT North American Champion. He is now set to face Grayson Waller at NXT Halloween Havoc for the title.
